structured_extraction.program_description: Grants to strengthen existing cultural arts organizations and emerging arts groups in Baltimore, with a focus on capital projects that enhance programming in underserved communities. Also supports arts initiatives that drive economic development, attract and support artists, stabilize neighborhoods, and use the arts to improve academic achievement.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are available in small and regular grant sizes. Specific amounts are not stated on this page. Funds support capital projects and arts programming in underserved Baltimore communities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Cultural arts organizations and emerging arts groups in Baltimore City, particularly those serving underserved communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital projects that enhance arts programming; economic development; supporting artists to live and work in Baltimore; neighborhood stabilization and revitalization; using arts to improve academic achievement.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review eligibility and grant criteria on the Abell Foundation grants page (https://abell.org/grants/), then apply through the small or regular grants process.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Abell Foundation makes direct equity investments in innovative for-profit companies operating in or willing to relocate to Baltimore City. The Foundation invests in promising startup companies with proprietary innovations as well as mature companies creating jobs and expanding employment in Baltimore City. Investments target above-market financial returns while generating significant social and economic community benefits, expanding the Foundation's capacity to improve quality of life in Baltimore. Initial investments typically range from $150,000 to $500,000, and the Foundation prefers to invest alongside other sophisticated investors at closing. In addition to capital, the Foundation provides value-added support through its experience, knowledge base, and network of local and national connections. Returns from investments are reinvested in local businesses or applied to grantmaking. Sectors of focus include medical devices and diagnostics, materials, green energy, aerospace, and healthcare technologies. The Foundation's Board of Trustees reviews investment requests five times per year on a rolling submission basis.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Foundation provides equity investment capital to for-profit companies — startups with proprietary innovations and mature companies expanding operations — in Baltimore City. Initial investments typically range from $150,000 to $500,000. The Foundation prefers to invest alongside other sophisticated investors at closing. In addition to capital, the Foundation provides value-added support through its experience, knowledge base, and network of local and national connections. Returns from investments are reinvested in local businesses or applied to grantmaking. Investments target above-market financial returns while generating social or economic benefit. Sectors of focus include medical devices and diagnostics, materials, green energy, aerospace, and healthcare technologies. The Board of Trustees meets five times per year to review proposals.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis; Board meets five times per year (specific annual deadlines posted on the program page)
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit companies — startups with proprietary innovations or mature companies creating jobs and expanding employment — operating in or willing to relocate to Baltimore City, that deliver social and economic community benefits and offer above-market financial returns.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business startup capital or growth capital for operations and expansion that create jobs and social/economic benefits in Baltimore City, aligned with the Foundation's mission.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Company must be located in Baltimore City or willing to relocate its headquarters and principal place of operations there. Companies must create jobs in Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Must be a for-profit company
Must operate in or be willing to relocate headquarters and principal place of operations to Baltimore City
Must create jobs in Baltimore, particularly low-skill or semi-skilled jobs
Must offer significant social and economic benefits to the community
Must provide above-market financial returns
Must have a competitive advantage and/or proprietary innovation
Startups must have proprietary innovations
Mature companies must be creating employment through business expansion in Baltimore City
There must be a substantial commercial market for the innovation with potential for above-market returns
Company should leverage local strengths and resources such as manufacturing, laboratories, universities, or state biotech tax credits
Preference for investments made alongside other sophisticated investors at closing
Submit a Company Introduction with a pitch deck or executive summary
Only one submission per company will typically be reviewed within a one-year period
Must meet the Foundation's eligibility criteria
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review the Foundation's eligibility and review criteria at abell.org/direct-investment-eligibility-and-review-criteria/. Submit a Company Introduction with a pitch deck or executive summary using the online application portal at abell.org/direct-investment-application-process/. Upon submission, you receive a confirmation email. A member of the finance team may contact you with follow-up questions or schedule a pitch meeting. The Board of Trustees meets five times per year to make funding decisions, and applicants are notified in a timely manner. The Foundation encourages prospective applicants to reach out to their team before applying.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Abell Foundation funds programs aimed at achieving a cleaner, healthier environment and protecting the natural resources of Baltimore and Maryland. Grants focus on improving air and water quality, mitigating climate change, increasing low-income individuals' access to clean energy, advancing environmental health and justice, and creating local jobs in emerging green industries.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are available through small and regular grant processes. Specific award amounts and terms are not listed on this page; applicants are directed to the grants process page for eligibility and review criteria.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations working on environmental health, clean energy access, air and water quality, climate change mitigation, and green jobs in Baltimore and Maryland — with a focus on equity for Black neighborhoods and low-income residents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Improving air and water quality, mitigating climate change, increasing low-income individuals' access to clean energy, creating local jobs in emerging green industries, and advancing environmental health and justice.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Primarily Baltimore City and Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants are directed to review eligibility and review criteria on the grants process page (https://abell.org/grants/) before applying. Both small and regular grant processes are available.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Abell Foundation awards grants to nonprofit community partners in Baltimore City to improve quality of life, create more equitable opportunities, and advocate for systemic changes that support communities most affected by structural racism and disinvestment. Funding includes seed money for innovative pilot programs, support for ongoing community programs and services, and capital project funding. Grantmaking focuses on seven core program areas: Health & Human Services, Education, Community Development, Workforce Development, Criminal Justice & Addiction, Environment, and Arts. In 2025, 233 grants totaling $11,037,839 were awarded, with an average grant size of $48,633.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging from $500 to $500,000 are awarded to nonprofit community partners. Funding types include seed money for innovative pilot programs, support for ongoing community programs and services, and capital project funding aimed at improving life outcomes and reducing racial disparities in Baltimore. In 2025, 233 grants totaling $11,037,839 were awarded, with an average grant size of $48,633.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations operating in Baltimore City that address community challenges related to health and human services, education, community development, workforce development, criminal justice and addiction, environment, and arts.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Seed funding for innovative pilot programs, support for ongoing community programs and services, capital projects, creating equitable opportunities, and advocating for systemic changes in Baltimore communities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City
requirements_list: Applicant must be a nonprofit organization
Programs or services must benefit Baltimore City residents
Work should align with one or more of the Foundation's seven core program areas
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The Foundation encourages prospective applicants to reach out to their team and start a conversation before applying. Visit abell.org/grants/ for more details on the application process.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Abell Foundation awards regular grants greater than $10,000 to nonprofit organizations working to improve quality of life in Baltimore. Grants support innovative pilots, ongoing community programs and services, and capital projects. The Board of Trustees reviews proposals five times per year on a set schedule, with past grants ranging from $20,000 to $350,000 or more.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants greater than $10,000 (past grants have ranged from $20,000 to $350,000 or more), reviewed at one of the Foundation's five annual Board meetings. Applicants are notified of decisions within one week of each Board meeting. Organizations may submit multiple proposals for different projects within the same calendar year, but only one proposal per project is reviewed per year.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Five deadlines per year; reviewed at one of the Foundation's five annual Board meetings — see current schedule on the program page
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations working to improve quality of life in Baltimore
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Seed funding for innovative pilots, support for ongoing community programs and services, capital projects, and other project-based work to enhance quality of life in Baltimore
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Primarily serves Baltimore City, Maryland
requirements_list: Grant requests must be greater than $10,000
Must be a nonprofit organization
First-time applicants must submit a letter of inquiry (LOI) before a full application
Only one proposal per project is reviewed within a calendar year
Grant recipients must submit interim and post-grant reports including narrative descriptions and accounting of funds expended
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First-time applicants should submit a short letter of inquiry (LOI) to grants@abell.org describing the project and proposed budget. If invited, submit a full application through the online grant portal (abell.org/apply) by one of the five annual deadlines. Returning applicants or those who have met eligibility criteria can apply directly through the online portal.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Abell Foundation awards small grants of $10,000 or less to nonprofit organizations working to improve quality of life in Baltimore. Grants support innovative pilots, ongoing community programs and services, and capital projects. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis with no deadline. First-time applicants must attend an information session before submitting; returning applicants may access the online portal directly. Decisions are communicated within 60 days of submission. Recipients must submit a post-grant report with a narrative of project outcomes and an accounting of funds expended.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of $10,000 or less awarded on a rolling basis throughout the year with no application deadline. First-time applicants must attend an information session before applying. Decisions are made within 60 days of submission. Recipients must submit a post-grant report with a narrative of project outcomes and an accounting of funds expended.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations working to improve quality of life in Baltimore, including first-time or returning applicants seeking small grants of $10,000 or less that align with the Abell Foundation's eligibility criteria and funding priorities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Seed funding for innovative pilots, support for ongoing community programs and services, capital projects, and other project-based activities aligned with the Foundation's funding priorities
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Primarily serves Baltimore City
requirements_list: Must be a nonprofit organization
Grant request must be $10,000 or less
First-time applicants must attend an information session before submitting to confirm fit with eligibility criteria and funding priorities
Organizations may submit multiple proposals for different projects within the same calendar year
Only one proposal per project will be reviewed within a calendar year
Project must meet the Foundation's eligibility criteria and priorities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First-time applicants must sign up for and attend an information session before submitting. Once eligibility is confirmed, submit a grant application through the online portal at abell.org/apply. Returning applicants can start or return to an online application at the grant portal directly. After submission, an Abell staff member may follow up with questions or request a site visit. Decisions are made within 60 days.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Abell Foundation funds programs that train low-income, unemployed, and underemployed job seekers in Baltimore and help them find and keep jobs that pay family-sustaining wages. Priority areas include employment for people with criminal records, industry-recognized certifications, paid work experience, workplace skills training, digital and literacy skills, job retention, and policy advocacy to remove barriers to employment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are available in small and regular grant categories. Specific dollar amounts are not stated on this page. Applicants should review the grants process page for eligibility and review criteria.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations serving low-income, unemployed, and underemployed Baltimore residents, including those with criminal records or barriers to employment
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Job training programs, paid work experience, workplace skills development, digital and literacy skills, job retention and career advancement services, employer engagement, supportive services (e.g. transportation, tax prep), and policy advocacy
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Programs must serve Baltimore City residents
requirements_list: Programs must serve Baltimore City residents
Priority given to programs linking residents with criminal records to employment
Priority given to programs helping trainees earn industry-recognized certifications in high-growth industries
Priority given to programs providing paid work experience such as internships or on-the-job training
Priority given to programs providing essential workplace skills training
Priority given to programs improving digital, math, and reading skills
Priority given to programs promoting job retention and career advancement
Priority given to programs engaging employers committed to family-sustaining wages and benefits
Priority given to programs connecting participants to services like free tax preparation and transportation
Priority given to programs advocating for policies that remove barriers to employment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review the grants process page at abell.org/grants/ to learn about eligibility and review criteria and the small and regular grants processes before applying.

structured_extraction.program_description: A coalition of non-profit organizations, local government, businesses, foundations, and the IRS that promotes and provides free income tax preparation to help low-income families claim the Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) and save hundreds of dollars in fees charged by paid tax preparers. The campaign's philosophy is 'making work pay' by using the tax code as a gateway to financial services for working families.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free income tax preparation services at 13 sites throughout Baltimore City. Helps low-income families claim the federal and state Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC), saving clients hundreds of dollars in tax preparation fees and refund anticipation loan costs. A Maryland family earning $11,000 can increase their income by 48% through the federal EITC ($4,400) and state EITC ($880).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income working families in Baltimore City who are eligible for the Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC)
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free tax preparation assistance to help claim EITC refunds and avoid fees from commercial tax preparers and refund anticipation loans
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City — 13 free tax preparation sites throughout the city
requirements_list: Must be a low-income working family
Must be eligible for the Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Residents can access free tax preparation at one of 13 sites throughout Baltimore City. Outreach is conducted through business, faith, and community partners.

structured_extraction.program_description: Banner Neighborhoods provides free minor home repair and maintenance services to elderly homeowners on fixed incomes in Southeast Baltimore. Services include faucet replacement, gutter cleaning, window air conditioner installation and removal, light bulb changes, smoke detector testing, and other handyman tasks. The goal is to help aging residents remain in their homes independently by addressing household tasks that require tools, ladders, specialized knowledge, or heavy lifting.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free home maintenance and minor repair services provided by part-time crew members. Cost to the program is less than $1,000 per household per year. Participants pay no fee and re-enroll annually. Services include minor repairs, gutter cleaning, air conditioner installation/removal, light bulb changes, smoke and carbon monoxide detector testing, and referrals to city weatherization programs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Elderly homeowners on fixed incomes in Southeast Baltimore, particularly single female homeowners. Average participant age is 77 with an average annual income of $12,400.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Minor home repairs and maintenance tasks including faucet replacement, gutter cleaning, window air conditioner installation/removal, light bulb changes, smoke and carbon monoxide detector testing, and energy efficiency outreach.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Southeast Baltimore, in the area extending from Monument Street to Eastern Avenue and from Washington Street to Haven Street.
requirements_list: Must be an elderly homeowner
Must live in the Banner Neighborhoods target area in Southeast Baltimore
Must be on a fixed/limited income
Annual re-enrollment required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Banner Neighborhoods by phone. Staff will come out to assess and address maintenance needs.

structured_extraction.program_description: CollegeBound Foundation encourages and enables Baltimore City public high school students to attend college by providing full-time college advisors in Baltimore City public high schools, helping students take the SAT, choose colleges, and complete financial aid forms. The program delivers need-based and last-dollar grants to cover remaining tuition costs after other aid is exhausted. It works with mixed-status families to identify financial aid and scholarships, and also provides assistance with SAT fee coverage, financial aid application fees, and college application guidance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Last-dollar grants to cover remaining college tuition costs after other financial aid is applied. Also provides need-based funding, SAT exam fee coverage, financial aid application fee assistance, and college application guidance. In 1991-92, CollegeBound awarded $186,170 in grants to students; more recently it awarded $72,000 in last-dollar grants to 59 freshmen and more than $100,000 to 120 sophomores and juniors.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City public high school students who are academically qualified but lack the financial resources and family support needed to attend college, including mixed-status families.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: College tuition (last-dollar gap funding), SAT exam fees, financial aid application fees, college application fees, and college access advising.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to students attending Baltimore City public high schools.
requirements_list: Must be a Baltimore City public high school student
Must demonstrate financial need (average family per capita income of ~$6,435)
Must be academically qualified for college admission
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: CollegeBound Foundation advisors work directly with students to secure financial aid and then provide supplemental grant funding to cover remaining costs. Students are assisted through SAT preparation, college selection, and financial aid form completion.

structured_extraction.program_description: The CollegeBound Foundation's College Retention Program combines Last Dollar Scholarship funding with personalized support from a retention counselor to help Baltimore City public high school graduates stay enrolled and graduate from college. Retention specialists visit campuses monthly, conduct phone and email check-ins, and operate a 24-hour student hotline. The program runs from the summer after high school graduation through college graduation at participating Maryland colleges and universities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides a Last Dollar Scholarship of up to $3,000 annually, combined with ongoing personal support from a retention counselor through college graduation. Counseling includes monthly campus visits, individual and group meetings, email and phone check-ins, and a 24-hour hotline.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City public high school graduates who are enrolled or planning to enroll in college and are recipients of CollegeBound Last Dollar Grants.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: College tuition and expenses (Last Dollar Scholarship); personal academic advising, counseling, and retention support services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Baltimore City public high school students attending nine Maryland colleges and universities.
requirements_list: Must be a Baltimore City public high school graduate
Must be a recipient of a CollegeBound Last Dollar Grant
Must be enrolled at one of the nine participating Maryland colleges or universities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: CollegeBound meets with incoming students beginning in June after high school graduation to ensure they are prepared for college enrollment in the fall. Students already receiving Last Dollar Grants are enrolled into the program.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Abell Foundation funds programs and initiatives focused on reducing violence, improving re-entry and reintegration for people with criminal records, reforming pre-trial detention, expanding harm reduction services, supporting substance use disorder recovery, and providing supportive housing for people released from incarceration or in recovery.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Abell Foundation awards small and regular grants to organizations working on criminal justice reform and addiction-related programs in Baltimore. Specific grant amounts and terms are not stated on this page; applicants should review the grants process page for eligibility criteria and application details.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofits, research organizations, and service providers working to reduce violence, support re-entry, reform pre-trial detention, and improve harm reduction and substance use treatment in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Violence reduction programs, re-entry and reintegration services, pre-trial detention reform, harm reduction and substance use treatment, recovery support, and supportive housing for people leaving incarceration or recovering from substance use disorder.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Programs must serve Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Focus on one or more of the foundation's priority areas: gun violence reduction, reducing incarceration and recidivism, re-entry and reintegration, pre-trial detention reform, harm reduction, substance use treatment, recovery support, or supportive housing
Must meet the foundation's eligibility and review criteria outlined in its grants process
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review eligibility and grant process details on the Abell Foundation's grants page (https://abell.org/grants/), then submit an inquiry or application. Contact Program Officer Amanda Owens for questions.

structured_extraction.program_description: Jericho is a workforce development and reentry program for ex-offenders returning to the community. It offers a two-week job training, orientation, and job placement program, and provides transitional housing to homeless clients in partnership with The Abell Foundation. The program helps participants rebuild faith in themselves and find stable employment and housing.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive a two-week job training, orientation, and job placement program, with a reported 60% job placement rate. Transitional housing is also provided to homeless clients in partnership with The Abell Foundation to give them stability while pursuing employment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Ex-offenders re-entering the community, particularly those who are homeless or lacking stable housing and employment.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Job training, job placement assistance, and transitional housing for homeless ex-offenders.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is centered at 901 N. Milton Ave. in East Baltimore, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be an ex-offender re-entering the community
Must be willing to participate in a two-week job training and orientation program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individuals enter the Jericho program to participate in a two-week job training, orientation, and job placement process. Contact Episcopal Community Services of Maryland for details.

structured_extraction.program_description: A 13-week hands-on construction trades training program run by the Job Opportunities Task Force (JOTF) that helps low-income Baltimore City residents obtain entry-level construction jobs and gain the skills needed to enter apprenticeship programs. Graduates also receive free driver's education and assistance obtaining a driver's license and vehicle.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 13-week hands-on construction trades training program costing $4,000 per trainee. Graduates receive free driver's education, help getting a driver's license, and assistance obtaining a car through Vehicles for Change upon employment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income Baltimore City residents seeking entry-level construction jobs and apprenticeship opportunities, including individuals with prior incarceration history.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction trades skills training, safety certification, first aid and CPR certification, driver's education, and vehicle assistance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only to Baltimore City residents.
requirements_list: Must be a Baltimore City resident
Must have a high school diploma or GED
Must pass a math test prior to enrollment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested individuals can contact JOTF directly. The page mentions Our Daily Bread at 725 Fallsway as a point of contact.

structured_extraction.program_name: MAGNA Baltimore Technical Training Center (MBTTC) Technical Training Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A job training program that teaches unemployed high school graduates the tool and die trade in a simulated factory environment. Students learn to use lathes, drill presses, surface grinders, welding equipment, vertical mills, and computers. Those without a high school diploma can earn a GED on site. Social services and recreational facilities are also available.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MAGNA pays 100 percent of the $7,000 tuition for each student enrolled in the tool and die training program. Training takes place in 48,000 square feet of simulated factory space equipped with industrial machinery and computers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Unemployed young adults, including high school graduates and those working toward a GED, seeking careers in the tool and die trade.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition for tool and die trade training, GED preparation, social services support.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Located in the Pimlico neighborhood of Baltimore City; draws students from the surrounding area.
requirements_list: High school diploma or working toward GED
Must be seeking employment in the tool and die trade
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Students can apply by contacting the Baltimore Technical Training Center. When the program first opened, a banner was displayed outside the building to advertise the opportunity.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maritime Transportation and Logistics Training Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A 90-hour workforce training program that prepares unemployed and underemployed Baltimore residents for entry-level jobs in the Port-related transportation and logistics industry. The program covers freight forwarding, logistics, material handling, stevedoring, customer service, and shipping and receiving, as well as soft skills development.
eligible_industries: Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive a 90-hour training course including 60 hours of soft skills and 30 hours of maritime industry content. The program costs $3,000 per student and includes forklift certification and assistance obtaining a Transportation Worker Identification Credential (TWIC) card. Funded in part by a Maryland Department of Labor, Licensing and Regulation EARN grant and $120,000 in matching funds from the Abell Foundation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Unemployed or underemployed Baltimore residents who are 18 or older, have a high school diploma, and can pass a background check.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Job training and certification to prepare participants for employment in port-related transportation and logistics industries.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Serves Baltimore City residents.
requirements_list: Must be 18 years of age or older
Must have a high school diploma
Must be unemployed or underemployed
Must pass a background check
Must demonstrate determination and motivation to complete training and find employment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants go through a rigorous screening process conducted by Maryland New Directions to assess motivation and likelihood of completing the program and securing employment.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Abell Foundation provides mission-related investments (MRIs) to for-profit companies, non-profits, and impact funds that advance important social priorities, including innovative ideas for social and economic change aligned with the Foundation's mission and strategic goals. MRIs take the form of loans, guarantees, equity investments, and limited partnership investments, typically offered at below-market returns to help attract additional catalytic capital. The Foundation accepts reduced financial returns in exchange for meaningful mission benefits and low risk of capital loss. The Foundation considers investment requests from for-profit companies or funds located in Baltimore City or that offer substantial benefits to Baltimore City businesses or residents, particularly those that create jobs or support diversity, equity, and inclusion. The Board of Trustees reviews investment requests five times per year. In addition to capital, the Foundation serves as a value-added partner, offering experience, knowledge, and networks to support portfolio investments.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Investments typically range from $1 million to $4 million per investment. Assistance is provided at below-market investment returns as loans, guarantees, equity investments, or limited partnership interests. The Foundation accepts below-market investment returns but expects substantial mission benefits and limited risk of capital loss in exchange. The Foundation prefers to co-invest alongside experienced financial professionals and supports strategies that mitigate risk of capital loss. In addition to capital, the Foundation offers non-financial support through its network and expertise. The Board of Trustees makes funding decisions five times per year.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis; reviewed at one of the Foundation's five annual Board meetings, with deadlines listed for 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit companies, non-profits, and impact funds located in Baltimore City or offering substantial benefits to Baltimore City businesses or residents, seeking mission-aligned investment capital to address important social challenges and drive social and economic change — particularly those that create jobs (especially low-skill or semi-skilled jobs) or support diversity, equity, and inclusion.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Advancing mission priorities such as community development, education, affordable housing, support for underserved communities, social and economic change initiatives aligned with the Foundation's mission, job creation (especially low-skill or semi-skilled jobs), and strengthening the local innovation and small business ecosystem.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Organization or impact fund must be located in Baltimore City or address a substantial unmet need of Baltimore City businesses or residents.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a for-profit company, non-profit, or impact fund
Must be located in Baltimore City or offer substantial benefits to Baltimore City businesses or residents
Must advance the Foundation's mission priorities and strategic goals
Must have innovative ideas for social and economic change
Must be willing to accept below-market investment returns
Product or solution must benefit the local community and align with Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion principles
Should create jobs, particularly low-skill or semi-skilled jobs
Must have a competitive advantage or unique innovative offering
Must have assessed investment risk, particularly loss of capital, and identified strategies to reduce risk to the Foundation
Should have experienced financial professionals involved
Must thoughtfully mitigate risks of capital losses
Should leverage local strengths and resources or bring new mission-aligned resources to the innovation and small business ecosystem
Submit a Company Introduction with a pitch deck or executive summary
Foundation typically reviews only one submission per company per calendar year
Must meet the Foundation's eligibility criteria
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review the MRI eligibility and review criteria at abell.org, then submit a Company Introduction with a pitch deck or executive summary via the online application portal on the MRI Application Process page. A member of the finance team may follow up with questions or schedule a pitch meeting. The Board of Trustees reviews requests at one of five annual meetings and notifies applicants of funding decisions.

structured_extraction.program_description: NCP targets vacant and abandoned houses in Baltimore neighborhoods with healthy real estate markets. It coordinates code enforcement, community organizing, property acquisition, rehabilitation loans, land banking, selective demolition, and disposition to either rehabilitate abandoned properties or clear title for future site development. The goal is to reduce blight, restore housing values, and return properties to productive use.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: NCP uses City Bond Funds as capital and provides acquisition and rehabilitation loan programs, land banking (intervention buying, stabilization, interim maintenance), selective demolition, and disposition of abandoned properties. It coordinates public and private tools such as homeowner rehabilitation and rehab loans with community organizations and prospective homebuyers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community organizations, prospective homebuyers, and neighbors in Baltimore's Stabilization and Reinvestment areas seeking to address vacant and abandoned properties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition, rehabilitation, stabilization, demolition, and disposition of vacant and abandoned residential properties in targeted Baltimore neighborhoods.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Stabilization and Reinvestment areas within Baltimore City, including neighborhoods from Brooklyn in the southwest to St. Helena in the southeast.
requirements_list: Properties must be located in Stabilization and Reinvestment areas as classified by Baltimore's housing market study
Targeted neighborhoods must have higher household incomes and higher homeownership rates compared to citywide averages
Federal housing programs are generally not available in these areas due to income restrictions
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: HCD's land resources department and community law center undertake property acquisition through municipal eminent domain, receivership actions, or negotiated sale. The acquisition process takes a minimum of six months.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Abell Foundation provides flexible, below-market-rate financing to nonprofit organizations and government partners in Baltimore City through low- or no-cost loans and loan guarantees. PRIs are one-time, catalytic investments designed to help eligible organizations meet non-recurring funding needs or unique capital challenges within Abell's program areas. Because PRIs must be repaid, the Foundation can recycle the funds to support additional nonprofit partners. The Board of Trustees reviews PRI requests at five scheduled Board meetings each year. Applications begin with a short letter of inquiry, and invited applicants then submit a full online application by one of the annual deadlines.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A limited number of low- or no-cost loans and loan guarantees (below-market-rate financing) are offered as one-time, catalytic investments to meet unique, non-recurring capital challenges for eligible nonprofit and government partners. Loan guarantees can also strengthen credit provided by outside lenders. Because PRIs must be repaid, the Foundation can reuse funds to support additional partners. The Foundation considers PRI requests five times per year on a set schedule. Specific amounts and terms vary by investment and are determined based on the applicant's proposal and budget.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Multiple deadlines per year; reviewed at one of five Board meetings each year — see schedule on page
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations (501c3 or 509a), government agencies, and fiscally sponsored projects operating in Baltimore City within Abell's program areas, seeking below-market financing for non-recurring capital needs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Non-recurring funding needs or unique capital challenges where a one-time, catalytic investment could make a significant impact, aligned with the Foundation's mission and program areas; project-specific costs as described in the applicant's proposal and budget.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Programs or projects must focus on Baltimore City and the Baltimore, Maryland area based on the Foundation's mission.
requirements_list: Must have 501c3 or 509a nonprofit tax status, be a government agency, or be a fiscally sponsored project
Must submit a copy of IRS determination letter, federal tax identification number (EIN), or proof of fiscal sponsorship
Must operate programs or projects within one of Abell's program areas
Must have a non-recurring funding need or unique capital challenge
Must have identified and secured a source of repayment
Must focus on Baltimore City
Individuals are not eligible
Cannot fund against fundraising campaigns
Must meet the Foundation's eligibility criteria
Submit a short letter of inquiry (LOI) describing the project and proposed budget
Receive a positive response to the LOI before submitting a full application
Proposals for the same project cannot be resubmitted within the same calendar year
Organizations may submit multiple proposals for different projects within the same calendar year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Review the Foundation's criteria and confirm eligibility at abell.org/program-related-investments/pri-eligibility-and-review-criteria. 2. Submit a short letter of inquiry (LOI) to grants@abell.org describing your project and proposed budget. 3. If the Foundation wants to learn more, they will invite you to complete a full online application via the portal at abell.org/apply. 4. Submit the full application by one of the five annual Board meeting deadlines (see schedule at abell.org/pri-application-process). 5. An Abell staff member may follow up with questions or request a site visit. 6. Applicants are notified of decisions within one week of each Board meeting. Contact grants@abell.org with any questions.

structured_extraction.program_description: Project Light Bulb is an energy-efficiency program run by Civic Works that sends trained AmeriCorps workers to low- and moderate-income homes to install energy-saving improvements at no cost to residents. Improvements include replacing incandescent bulbs with compact fluorescent light bulbs (CFLs), installing faucet aerators and low-flow showerheads, adjusting thermostat and appliance settings, insulating water heaters, and providing education on additional energy conservation measures.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free installation of energy-saving devices in the home valued at approximately $205 per household. Participants receive up to 15 CFL bulbs, kitchen and bathroom faucet aerators, a low-flow showerhead, a carbon monoxide detector, hot water heater insulation, thermostat adjustment, and energy conservation education — all at no cost. Households save an estimated average of $8 per month (about 10% of monthly electricity costs) and 3.2 million gallons of water annually across participating homes.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low- and moderate-income homeowners and residents in Baltimore City neighborhoods
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of energy-efficiency improvements in the home, including CFL bulbs, aerators, low-flow showerheads, carbon monoxide detectors, water heater insulation, and thermostat optimization
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Originally piloted in the Belair Edison and Coldstream-Homestead-Montebello neighborhoods of Baltimore City
requirements_list: Must be a resident of a participating Baltimore City neighborhood
Household should be low or moderate income
Home should be a two-story rowhouse (predominant housing type in target areas)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Civic Works AmeriCorps workers visit homes in teams of two. Residents are approached directly by program staff in the target neighborhoods.

structured_extraction.program_name: Allegany County Local Development Council Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program distributes a portion of Rocky Gap Casino's slots revenue to eligible non-profits and municipalities in Allegany County for capital projects. Allegany County receives 5.5% of slots revenues from Rocky Gap Casino, and 20% of that amount is set aside for capital funding requests from local non-profits and municipalities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant awards are made from Rocky Gap Casino slots revenue shared with Allegany County. Funds may only be used for capital-related items and cannot be used for operating expenses. Award amounts are not specified on the page. Awards are announced and disbursed within approximately six weeks of the application deadline.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations and municipalities located in Allegany County, Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital-related items only; operating expenses are not eligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be non-profits or municipalities within Allegany County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a non-profit organization or municipality in Allegany County
Request must be for capital needs, not operating expenses
Must provide information on non-profit or municipality status, mission or purpose, description of capital needs, and total amount requested
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online using the Municipal & Non-Profit Grant Request Form on the county website. If needed, submit a letter of request by email or mail to Jason Bennett, CPA, Allegany County Administrator & Chairperson of the Local Development Council. The letter must include non-profit or municipality status, mission/purpose, description of capital needs, and total amount requested. All requests are reviewed by the council and awards are announced and disbursed within approximately six weeks.

It is funded using a portion (2.25%) of Allegany County Government's share of annual gross revenue from video lottery machines at Rocky Gap Casino Resort.

structured_extraction.program_description: Curb-to-curb demand response transportation service for senior citizens and people with disabilities who are unable to use fixed-route public bus service. Medical trips are prioritized for seniors; ADA Paratransit trips are unrestricted in purpose. Service is available within ¾ mile of Allegany County Transit fixed routes.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Demand response transportation at a $3.00 flat rate each way. Punch cards are available for $27.50 each, good for $30.00 worth of rides. Personal Care Attendants ride free. Reservations accepted up to 14 days in advance by calling 301-724-1255.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Senior citizens and people with disabilities who are unable to use Allegany County Transit's accessible fixed-route bus service due to their disability or age.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Transportation for medical appointments, personal trips, and any purpose within the service area.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Service is available within ¾ mile of ACT fixed bus routes in Allegany County. Origins and destinations outside this area will not be served, unless the passenger is picked up at a location inside the service area.
requirements_list: Must be a senior citizen or a person with a disability that prevents use of accessible fixed-route transit
Persons with disabilities must be certified as ADA Paratransit eligible before service can be scheduled (visitors may use service up to 21 days per calendar year without re-certification)
Must be within ¾ mile of an ACT fixed bus route
Reservations must be made at least one business day in advance
Trips must be cancelled by close of business the day before, or at least 1 hour before scheduled pick-up for emergencies
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete an Alltrans application (available as a PDF or online). Call Alltrans at 301-724-1255 between 7:30 a.m. and close of business, Monday through Friday, at least one business day before your trip. Provide your name, phone numbers, trip date, pick-up and drop-off locations, and any special assistance needs. Hearing-impaired customers may use Maryland Relay System (711).

structured_extraction.program_name: City of Cumberland Community Development Block Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) Program provides federal funding to the City of Cumberland to support community development activities. Funds are used for projects that benefit low- and moderate-income residents, including infrastructure improvements, community facilities, housing, economic development, and services for special populations. Includes a 2025-2029 Five Year Consolidated Plan with annual action plans, Citizen Participation Plan, and Analysis of Impediments to Fair Housing Updates.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal CDBG funds are allocated to the City of Cumberland through a consolidated planning process. Estimated $750,000 in CDBG funds available for the 2025-26 fiscal year. Grants support acquisition, blight removal, housing projects, neighborhood improvements, recreation, beautification, job creation, public facilities, public services, infrastructure improvements, economic development initiatives, and services for special populations. Projects must meet one of three national objectives: benefit low-income persons, address an urgent/non-fundable need, or address slum/blight. Applicants submit project proposals via the annual application packet.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations, public housing agencies, homeless service providers, economic development organizations, community groups, and other entities seeking funding for community development projects benefiting low- and moderate-income residents in Cumberland, Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition, blight removal, housing projects, neighborhood improvements, recreation, beautification, job creation, public facilities, public services, infrastructure improvements, economic development initiatives, and services for special populations benefiting low- and moderate-income persons.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Cumberland, Allegany County, Maryland
requirements_list: Projects must benefit low- and moderate-income residents
Must meet one of three national objectives: benefit low-income persons, address urgent/non-fundable need, or address slum/blight
Must address at least one priority goal in the draft Consolidated Plan
Attendance at one mandatory technical assistance meeting (January 22-23, 2025)
Must demonstrate agency capacity and experience
Must address project complexity and matching funds availability
Must submit a completed application packet by February 25, 2025
Projects subject to internal review (February 25 - March 27, 2025)
Projects reviewed through the consolidated planning process
Must comply with Fair Housing Analysis requirements
Citizen Participation Plan compliance required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Non-profit technical assistance meetings held January 22-23, 2025. Focus group meetings held January 27-28, 2025. Project requests submitted by February 25, 2025. Projects undergo internal review (February 25 - March 27, 2025). Public hearings held for needs assessment, impediments analysis, and draft plans. A proposed project list is published and public notices are issued for plan review and release of funds. Application packet available through Allegany County government website.

structured_extraction.program_name: Frostburg Main Street Structural Stabilization Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that provides financial support to help property owners on Frostburg's historic Main Street stabilize and repair the structural elements of their buildings. The program aims to remove the most critical and expensive barriers to redevelopment — such as foundation repairs, framing issues, and roof support — so that historic and commercial buildings can be brought back into active use.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants funded through $250,000 in state funding from the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) Strategic Demolition Fund (SDF). Funds cover structural repairs including foundation work, framing, roof support beams, and roofing. Funding is expected to be competitive. Specific grant amounts per applicant are not yet stated.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit property owners of commercial or mixed-use buildings located within Frostburg's Main Street district who need structural stabilization work done before they can begin broader renovations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Structural repairs to eligible buildings, including foundation repairs, framing, roof support beams, and roofing — anything that constitutes the structural integrity of the building.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties must be located within Frostburg's Main Street district in Frostburg, Maryland.
requirements_list: Property must be located within Frostburg's Main Street district
Property must be commercial or mixed-use (e.g., first-floor storefront with residential units above)
Property must be owned by a for-profit, tax-paying entity in good standing with the city, county, and state
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications will be managed by City of Frostburg staff. County staff will oversee fund distribution and compliance. A review committee will evaluate applications based on a project rubric currently under final development. Interested property owners are encouraged to begin gathering information about their properties' structural needs and project timelines before applications open.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program administered by Allegany County that makes funds available to property owners and developers undertaking adaptive reuse, building renovation, and redevelopment of vacant or underutilized buildings in the downtowns and main streets across Allegany County. The program emphasizes mixed-use development, upper story residential living, and revitalization of the county's architectural and economic landscape. The program has included a $2 million funding round, with individual awards such as $250,000 for the McMullen Building renovation by CG Enterprises.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant awards to property owners and developers for redevelopment, adaptive reuse, and renovation of vacant or underutilized buildings in Allegany County downtowns and main street areas. The program has included a $2 million funding pool, with individual project awards (e.g., $250,000 for the McMullen Building renovation). Emphasis is placed on mixed-use and upper story residential projects.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Redevelopment and renovation of vacant or underutilized buildings, adaptive reuse and conversion of legacy commercial buildings into residential or mixed-use properties, and upper story living projects in downtown and main street areas of Allegany County.

Project must be located in a downtown or main street area in Allegany County
Emphasis on mixed-use and upper story living projects

structured_extraction.program_name: SBA Disaster Loan Program – Physical Damage and Economic Injury
structured_extraction.program_description: The U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) offers low-interest disaster loans to homeowners, renters, businesses, and private non-profits in Allegany County affected by the May 2025 flooding. Loans can cover repair or replacement of real estate, personal property, machinery, equipment, inventory, and business assets not fully covered by insurance. Separate Economic Injury Disaster Loans (EIDL) are available for small businesses that suffered economic losses.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Homeowners can borrow up to $500,000 to repair or replace their primary residence and up to $100,000 for personal property. Businesses and most private non-profits can borrow up to $2 million for disaster losses not fully covered by insurance. Economic Injury Disaster Loans (EIDL) are also available for eligible small businesses and non-profits. Repayment terms up to 30 years determined case by case.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Physical damage deadline: July 21, 2025; EIDL deadline: February 23, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners, renters, businesses, and private non-profits in Allegany County affected by flooding
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Repair or replacement of primary residence, personal property, business assets, and economic injury losses from flooding
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to those in Allegany County, MD (disaster declared county contiguous to Somerset County, PA under PA-20019)
requirements_list: Located in a disaster-declared county
Sustained damages from flooding
Physical damage: deadline July 21, 2025
EIDL: deadline February 23, 2026
Damages not fully covered by insurance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call SBA's Customer Service Center at 1-800-659-2955, email DisasterCustomerService@sba.gov referencing Pennsylvania Disaster Number PA-20019, or apply online.

structured_extraction.program_description: A forgivable loan program that provides low-interest funding to small for-profit businesses looking to expand or establish operations in Allegany County. The program helps new companies establish themselves in the county and helps existing companies grow to create more jobs, increase their ability to sell products outside the area, or improve their local community presence. Up to half of the loan can be forgiven based on performance metrics like job creation and increased export capacity.
structured_extraction.agency: Allegany County Economic and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans range from $10,000 to $50,000 at interest rates more favorable than traditional lenders. Loans of $10,000 or less require no match. Loans over $40,000 require a 1:1 funding match. Payments may be deferred for up to 6 months after loan draw. Up to 50% of the loan may be forgiven based on performance conditions defined in the applicant's project narrative (e.g., number of new jobs created). Funds must be appropriated within 12 months and spent within 24 months of conditional loan approval.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis, subject to funding availability
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small for-profit businesses with fewer than 15 full-time employees that are physically located in Allegany County or plan to expand to a commercial location there.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Costs that expand the productive capacity of the business and lead to long-term sustainable growth, including equipment and furniture. Cannot be used for staff costs, salaries, acquisition or capital improvements of an existing building, or construction of a new building.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be physically present in Allegany County through ownership or long-term commercial lease of a physical asset, or operating from a personal residence with plans to move to a commercial location.
requirements_list: Must be a for-profit, tax-paying entity in good standing with Allegany County and the State of Maryland
Must have fewer than 15 full-time employees
Must be physically present in Allegany County or intend to expand to a commercial location
Must demonstrate ability to offer a tangible product or service (via patents, sales figures, taxes paid, assets, or available capital)
Must apply via formal invitation from a qualified member of Allegany County ECD
Business plan must be developed in conjunction with or approved by the local Small Business Development Center (SBDC) representative
Business plan must include a line-item budget with estimates from reputable vendors
Projects previously funded by the Invest Allegany program are ineligible
Loans over $40,000 require a 1:1 funding match
Funds must be appropriated within 12 months and spent within 24 months of conditional loan approval
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Allegany County ECD team using the contact form on the program page to express interest. The fund is capitalized at $100,000 at the start of each fiscal year.

structured_extraction.program_description: A real property tax credit for Anne Arundel County employees who work full-time as 9-1-1 specialists, including those who receive and process emergency assistance requests, perform support functions related to 9-1-1, or dispatch public safety services. The credit reduces the amount of real property tax owed on a dwelling owned by eligible 9-1-1 specialists, up to the lesser of $2,500 or total County taxes due on the dwelling. Eligibility criteria, calculation methods, duration of the credit, an application deadline, application form requirements, and an administrative fee are established by county ordinance (Bill 17-20). Bill No. 82-25, effective December 12, 2025, increased the maximum duration of this credit from 5 to 10 taxable years.

The credit is the lesser of $2,500 or the total County taxes due on the dwelling, minus a 1% administrative fee. Originally available for up to 5 taxable years with annual renewal; Bill No. 82-25 (effective December 12, 2025) extended the maximum duration to 10 taxable years (1 initial year plus up to 9 renewal years).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: On or before April 1 immediately before the taxable year for which the tax credit is sought (e.g., April 1, 2026 for tax year July 1, 2026 – June 30, 2027)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Full-time Anne Arundel County employees who work as 9-1-1 specialists as defined in §9-262 of the Maryland Tax–Property Article, who own a residential dwelling in Anne Arundel County used as their principal residence.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of Anne Arundel County real property tax liability on a principal residence dwelling for eligible 9-1-1 specialists.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must own a residential dwelling in Anne Arundel County, Maryland, used as principal residence and occupied for more than six months of the tax year.

structured_extraction.program_description: The VOLT Fund (also referred to as the VOLT Growth Fund) is a loan program administered by the Anne Arundel County Economic Development Corporation (AAEDC) on behalf of the Maryland Department of Commerce. The fund is supported by Video Lottery Terminal (VLT) casino revenue from Maryland casinos. It provides loans ranging from $25,000 to $500,000 to small, minority-owned, woman-owned, and veteran-owned businesses to help them start, grow, and expand operations. Half of the fund is targeted to small, minority, women, and veteran-owned businesses within a 10-mile radius of Maryland's six casinos; the other half is available to small businesses throughout Maryland. Loans are priced at or below current market interest rates and can be used for business and commercial real estate acquisition and expansion, leasehold improvements, equipment, working capital, renovations, loan payoff, and hiring or retaining employees. Standard underwriting considers repayment capacity, financial strength of the company and guarantors, industry and management experience, and collateral. A minimum 10% equity injection is required for start-up businesses. AAEDC is one of nine regional fund managers in the state.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans from $25,000 to $500,000 at a 5% fixed interest rate with a 1% loan fee at commitment. Normal term is 5 years (1st year interest-only, remaining 4 years principal and interest); longer terms up to 30 years available based on collateral and purpose. Funded by Video Lottery Terminal (VLT) casino revenue. Funds can be used for business and commercial real estate acquisition and expansion, leasehold improvements, equipment, working capital, renovations, loan payoff, startup costs, and hiring or retaining employees. Standard underwriting considers repayment capacity, financial strength of the company and guarantors, industry and management experience, and collateral. A minimum 10-30% equity injection is required for start-up businesses. Half of the fund is prioritized for small, minority, women, and veteran-owned businesses within 10 miles of Maryland's six casinos.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small, minority-owned, woman-owned, and veteran-owned businesses in Maryland, including start-ups and existing businesses. Half of the fund is prioritized for businesses within a 10-mile radius of Maryland's six casinos.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business and commercial real estate acquisition and expansion, leasehold improvements, equipment, working capital, renovations, loan payoff, startup costs, and hiring or retaining employees.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to small businesses throughout Maryland. Half of the fund is prioritized for small, minority, women, and veteran-owned businesses within a 10-mile radius of Maryland's six casinos (Maryland Live in Anne Arundel County, Hollywood Park in Cecil County, Rocky Gap Casino in Allegany County, Ocean Downs in Worcester County, MGM in Prince George's County, and Horseshoe Casino in Baltimore City). Note: Montgomery, Howard, and Baltimore County have local fund managers. AAEDC is one of nine regional fund managers in the state and administers the fund on behalf of the Maryland Department of Commerce.
requirements_list: Business must be a small business as defined by SBA size standards
Minority-owned, woman-owned, or veteran-owned businesses are prioritized within 10-mile casino radius
Personal credit score of 640 or above

Ineligible businesses include: adult bookstores, adult video shops, adult entertainment facilities, gambling facilities, gun shops, liquor stores, unlicensed massage parlors, pawn shops, tanning salons, tattoo parlors, and residential/transient living facilities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply on a rolling basis through the AAEDC Submittable portal if funding is available. Processing time is typically 30-90 days. Standard underwriting practices apply; evaluation based on repayment capacity, financial strength, industry and management experience, and collateral. Settlement is facilitated with outside attorneys. Post-closing servicing, loan monitoring, billing, and collections are handled by AAEDC financial services staff. Visit the VOLT Fund page on the AAEDC website for additional details.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides free financial and counseling assistance to Anne Arundel County and Annapolis residents facing eviction, including rental assistance to help renters stay current on rent payments and avoid eviction. Up to $4.5 million in financial assistance is available to tenants who have experienced a loss of income or been impacted by COVID-19. Additional support includes legal representation during court or mediation proceedings, foreclosure prevention counseling, first-time homebuyer counseling, and property rehabilitation assistance for low-income homeowners. The program is administered by Arundel Community Development Services (ACDS). Applications are accepted Monday, Wednesday, and Friday from 9am to 1pm.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Agricultural Business Improvement Grant (ABIG) Program provides matching grants to help farm-based businesses and commercial watermen in Anne Arundel County expand their operations. Administered jointly by AAEDC and MARBIDCO, the program offers grants of up to $10,000 to fund approved projects such as fencing, livestock, plant stock, equipment, construction, and infrastructure upgrades. In 2025, the program was expanded to include commercial watermen. In 2024, the program funded over $38,000 in projects supporting livestock producers, equine operations, produce production, and product marketing. Applicants must provide a one-to-one match (50% of total project cost), and proof of project completion is due within one year of the grant award. Applications are scored numerically based on their ability to increase revenue, retain or increase employees, expand operations, increase efficiency, increase local-grown food supply, and/or provide agricultural education opportunities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Matching grants of up to $10,000 per recipient. Applicants must provide a one-to-one matching contribution equal to the grant amount requested (50% of total project cost). For example, a $5,000 grant requires the applicant to contribute $5,000 of their own funds. Matching funds may not include in-kind labor or state and federal grants or cost share. Funds are awarded to the highest-ranked applications based on potential to boost revenue, create or retain jobs, expand operations, improve efficiency, increase locally grown food supply, or offer agricultural education. In 2024, the program funded over $38,000 in projects in partnership with MARBIDCO, supporting livestock producers, equine operations, produce production, and product marketing. Proof of project completion is due within the year of the grant award.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eligible projects include fencing, livestock, plant stock, equipment, construction of buildings, expanding production, upgrading shelter, and other infrastructure upgrades that boost revenue or efficiency.
