structured_extraction.program_name: Anne Arundel County Agricultural and Woodland Preservation Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary program established in 1990 that preserves agricultural and woodland land in Anne Arundel County by offering two forms of financial incentive for landowners to keep their property as working farms and forests. The first option is the purchase of development rights through a permanent Agricultural Conservation Easement: the County pays approximately 60% of the appraised Fair Market Value of development rights (recent offers ranging from approximately $8,000 to $11,000 per acre, paid as cash at settlement), the land remains in private ownership, and the easement is permanent and transfers with the deed. The second option is a Tax District Agreement (Agricultural or Woodland District), in which property owners commit to keeping land in agricultural or woodland use and not subdividing for 10 years in exchange for a credit on the County portion of their Real Property Tax Bill — meaning the County Real Estate Tax is credited away for the term of the agreement; the agreement must be renewed every 10 years to maintain the benefit. Agricultural District requires at least 50 contiguous acres devoted to agriculture and an active Soil and Water Conservation Plan; Woodland District requires at least 10 contiguous acres of woodlands and a Forest Management Plan. Both require Rural Agricultural (RA) or Residential Low Density (RLD) zoning and property outside planned Water and Sewer categories 1, 2, and 3. Over $57.5 million has been paid to preserve nearly 10,000 acres of farmland through permanent conservation easements. Funds for easement purchases are approved annually through the County Capital Budget cycle.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two forms of assistance are available: (1) Agricultural Conservation Easement — the County purchases development rights from the landowner at approximately 60% of the appraised Fair Market Value, with recent offers ranging from approximately $8,000 to $11,000 per acre paid as cash at settlement. The easement is permanent, transfers with the deed, and the land remains in private ownership as farm or forest. Funds are approved annually through the County Capital Budget cycle. Payment options include lump sum or installment. (2) Tax District Agreement (Agricultural or Woodland District) — the property owner commits to keep land in agricultural or woodland use and not subdivide for 10 years in exchange for a credit on the County Real Estate Tax portion of their Real Property Tax Bill; participating landowners are invoiced only for State property taxes and County fees and charges. The agreement must be renewed every 10 years to maintain the benefit. Early termination results in liability for all back taxes plus interest. Over $57.5 million has been paid to preserve nearly 10,000 acres of farmland through permanent conservation easements.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Easement applications: November 1 and April 1 (applications accepted 30 days prior to each date); District Agreement applications accepted anytime (March 31 recommended to receive a credit on the following fiscal year tax bill); Tax credit applications: October 1 (for tax year beginning July 1; late applications treated as applications for next tax year)
structured_extraction.contact_name: Michael Stringer, Agricultural and Woodland Program Manager
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers and landowners with qualifying agricultural or woodland parcels in Anne Arundel County who are willing to voluntarily keep their property as working farms and forests, whether through a permanent easement sale or a 10-year Tax District Agreement. Agricultural District applicants must have at least 50 contiguous acres in RA or RLD zoning; Woodland District applicants must have at least 10 contiguous acres of woodlands.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Compensation to landowners for permanently giving up development rights on agricultural or woodland land through permanent conservation easements (paid as cash at settlement); also supports enrollment in Tax District Agreements (Agricultural or Woodland) providing a credit on the County Real Estate Tax portion of the Real Property Tax bill in exchange for a 10-year commitment to agricultural or woodland use and no subdivision.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to landowners in Anne Arundel County, Maryland only. Property must be located outside Water and Sewer Categories 1, 2, and 3 (as shown in Anne Arundel County Master Plan for Water and Sewer Systems). For Tax District Agreements, property must be located within Rural Agricultural (RA), Residential Low Density (RLD), R1, or OS zoning districts. Priority factors for easement purchase include proximity to agricultural zone boundaries, proximity to developed/developing areas, proximity to other easements, and agricultural/open space designations.
requirements_list: Must own agricultural or woodland land in Anne Arundel County

For easement sale: parcel must have 50 or more acres of agricultural land and meet certain soils criteria and have an active Soil and Water Quality Conservation Plan, OR have a minimum of 25 acres of contiguous woodland with an active Forest Stewardship Plan
Current minimum size requirement for easement is 50 acres of agricultural land (proposed to be reduced to 30 acres) and 25 acres for woodland
Must have an up-to-date Soil and Water Quality Plan and/or Forest Management Plan approved/updated within the last 10 years (for easement)

Must agree to maintain property as working farm or forest and forgo future development (for easement) or commit to agricultural/woodland use and no subdivision for 10 years (for Tax District Agreement)
Participation is voluntary
Conservation easements are permanent (in perpetuity) and transfer with the deed

Agricultural District: land must consist of at least 50 contiguous acres devoted to agriculture (multiple contiguous properties under different ownership accepted if each is at least 10 acres and the total is at least 50 acres)
Property must meet USDA Soil Capability Classes criteria (for Agricultural District)
An active Soil and Water Conservation Plan must be in place (for Agricultural District)
Property must be zoned Rural Agricultural (RA), Residential Low Density (RLD), R1, or OS (for Tax District Agreement)
Property must be outside existing or planned Water and Sewer categories 1, 2, and 3 (for Tax District Agreement)
Woodland District: area must consist of at least 10 contiguous acres of woodlands (10-acre minimum per landowner when adding woodland to an existing district)
Woodland District requires a Forest Management Plan
Tax District Agreements must be renewed every 10 years to maintain the tax credit benefit
Upon approval, District Agreement is recorded in the County Land Records
Land must be in fee simple ownership (for easement)
Land must be located within an established County Agricultural District (for easement purchase)
Must maintain land according to sound agricultural soil and water conservation practices
No surface or subsurface mineral extraction may occur
Must allow right-of-entry for compliance inspections
Property must be in a State or County Agricultural/Woodland District OR have a County/State easement purchased on property (for tax credit)
Separate tax credit application required for each property tax account number
Early termination of Tax District Agreement results in liability for all back taxes plus interest

Complete petition form with owner information, farm/woodland description, tax account numbers, property identification, land use capability assessment, copies of all deeds from 1952 to present, list of adjacent property owners, and disclosure of third-party mineral extraction interests
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Anne Arundel County Agricultural and Woodland Program Manager (Michael Stringer at agpres@aacounty.org or 410-222-7432) for information on applying. For easement sales, applications are accepted 30 days prior to deadlines of November 1 and April 1 each year; submit completed application form to Office of Planning and Zoning with all required documentation; County conducts on-site investigations and appraisals. For Tax District Agreements, the landowner requests establishment of a County Agricultural District; the Planning and Zoning Officer approves establishment; the landowner executes the County Agricultural District Agreement, which is notarized and recorded in Land Records. District Agreement applications may be submitted at any time; March 31 is recommended to receive a credit on the following fiscal year tax bill. For the tax credit, applications are due by October 1 for the tax year beginning July 1; late applications are treated as applications for the next tax year. Tax credit applications are submitted to Anne Arundel County Department of Planning and Zoning at 2664 Riva Road, Mail Stop 6401, Annapolis, MD 21401 and reviewed by the Office of Finance and Program Administrator. County staff review applications in collaboration with the Agricultural Preservation Advisory Board, and the County Council has final authority over program requirements.

structured_extraction.program_name: Anne Arundel County Childcare Providers Support Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: Grants of up to $50,000 to licensed childcare businesses in Anne Arundel County that experienced significant decreases in enrollment due to COVID-19. The program provides working capital to help small childcare businesses stay open and continue serving families.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $50,000 to cover operating expenses such as rent, payroll, utilities, personal protective equipment (PPE), costs to maintain sanitary spaces, and online communications and learning tools. Grant amount depends on business size and funding availability. Grants cannot be used for expenses already covered by another government COVID-19 program, insurance-covered losses, or capital improvements.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed family childcare homes and childcare centers in Anne Arundel County that experienced enrollment declines due to COVID-19. Priority given to providers serving low-income communities, childcare desert communities, or children with special needs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating expenses including rent, payroll, utilities, PPE, sanitation costs, and online communications and learning tools.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must have been open and operating prior to March 13, 2020
Must be in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
Must submit a copy of the license issued through the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) and a signed W-9 form
Must upload a voided company check
Grant funds cannot be used for expenses previously covered by another federal, state, or local government COVID-19 program, losses covered by insurance, or capital improvements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: AAEDC is developing an online portal where businesses can create an account and complete the entire application process. The application period was expected to open in early October 2020.

structured_extraction.program_name: Anne Arundel County Community Tree Planting Mini Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A mini grant program through the Chesapeake Bay Trust that funds community tree planting projects in Anne Arundel County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Mini grants for community tree planting projects in Anne Arundel County. Specific amounts and terms are available on the Chesapeake Bay Trust website.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community organizations and local governments in Anne Arundel County interested in planting trees.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Community tree planting activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County, Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Chesapeake Bay Trust website.

structured_extraction.program_name: Anne Arundel County Emergent Grasses (Marsh Grasses) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A multi-departmental Anne Arundel County program (Department of Inspections and Permits and Department of Recreation and Parks) that provides free emergent marsh grasses (Spartina alterniflora/smooth cordgrass and Spartina patens/saltmarsh hay) to county residents and community associations with qualifying living shoreline or other tidal projects for planting in marsh areas. The program is administered in coordination with the Maryland Department of the Environment. County personnel visit the site to evaluate conditions, provide guidance on plant types and spacing, and assist with permit applications before providing plants.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free emergent marsh grasses (Spartina alterniflora/smooth cordgrass and Spartina patens/saltmarsh hay) provided at no cost to eligible county residents and community associations for planting in intertidal zones and areas above intertidal zones. County personnel also provide field site evaluations, project planning assistance, guidance on plant types and spacing based on tidal position and salinity, and support in obtaining necessary permits for associated shoreline work.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Anne Arundel County private property owners, waterfront property holders, and community associations with qualifying living shoreline or other tidal projects
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planting emergent marsh grasses in intertidal zones (between normal low and high tides) and areas above intertidal zones along living shorelines or other tidal project sites
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County properties adjacent to tidal waters (creeks and rivers), including intertidal zones and areas above intertidal zones
requirements_list: Must be an Anne Arundel County resident, private property owner, or community association
Must have a qualifying living shoreline or other tidal project
Site must pass a field evaluation by county personnel
Completed application form required
For part of extensive projects: copies of relevant permit applications required
For standalone projects: description of project required
Private property requires owner authorization
Property owner/community association contact information required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the application form (available as a PDF) and contact the Forestry Section at (410) 222-7441 or forestry@aacounty.org for additional information. County personnel will conduct a field visit to evaluate site conditions, provide guidance on plant types and spacing, and assist with obtaining necessary permits.

structured_extraction.program_name: Anne Arundel County Excluded Worker Humanitarian Relief Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: A financial assistance fund for Anne Arundel County residents who lost their jobs due to COVID-19, were not receiving unemployment benefits, and earned $25 per hour or less before the pandemic.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance (humanitarian relief funds) for eligible excluded workers in Anne Arundel County.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Anne Arundel County residents who earned $25/hour or less before COVID-19, lost their job on or after March 1, 2020, are not currently receiving unemployment benefits, and are not currently working.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: General financial relief for excluded workers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County residents only.
requirements_list: Must be an Anne Arundel County resident
Must have been earning $25/hour or less before COVID-19
Must have lost job on or after March 1, 2020
Must not be currently receiving unemployment benefits
Must not be currently working
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call (410) 987-3890 or visit aawdc.org/relief for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Anne Arundel County False Alarm Reduction Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A program requiring alarm system owners to register their alarms with Anne Arundel County to reduce the number of false alarm calls that firefighters and paramedics must respond to each year. Unnecessary false alarm responses drain emergency resources and reduce the availability of units to handle real emergencies.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Alarm owners register their alarm systems online through the county's alarm registration portal. Registration helps the county track and manage false alarm responses and may be required following receipt of a false alarm notice or invoice.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Anne Arundel County residents and businesses that have installed alarm systems or have received a false alarm notification or invoice from the county.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable — this is a registration and compliance program, not a funding program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must have an alarm system installed
Must register if you received a false alarm letter, invoice, or notification
Must register if you have a new alarm system and have never previously registered with the program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the online registration portal at crywolfservices.com/annearundelmd to register your alarm system.

structured_extraction.program_name: Anne Arundel County Geothermal Energy Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A one-time tax credit on Anne Arundel County real property taxes for residential dwellings that install geothermal energy devices (ground loop heating or cooling systems) on or after January 1, 2009. The credit is equal to the lesser of 50% of installation cost or $2,500, credited against taxes levied on the dwelling (not the land). The credit is available to owners of real property located within Anne Arundel County who install qualifying geothermal systems.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time tax credit credited against Anne Arundel County real property taxes levied on the residential dwelling (not the land). Amount is the lesser of 50% of installation cost or $2,500. Federal and state grants or state geothermal energy tax credits are excluded from the cost calculation. Device must use ground loop technology to heat or cool the dwelling and must have been installed on or after January 1, 2009.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: June 1 immediately before the taxable year for which credit is sought. If filed after June 1, treated as application for next succeeding taxable year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of residential dwellings in Anne Arundel County that install geothermal energy devices.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of Anne Arundel County real property tax liability (one-time credit) for installation of geothermal energy devices using ground loop technology for heating or cooling residential dwellings.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Residential property must be located in Anne Arundel County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Property must be located in Anne Arundel County
Property must be a residential dwelling
Geothermal energy device must be installed on or after January 1, 2009
Device must use ground loop technology to heat or cool the dwelling
Documented receipts required for materials, supplies, and installation costs
Final inspection sticker required
Application filed once only during duration of tax credit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and submit the Geothermal Energy Tax Credit Application to the Anne Arundel County Office of Finance by June 1 immediately before the taxable year for which the credit is sought. Applications filed after June 1 will be treated as applications for the next succeeding taxable year. Visit the Anne Arundel County website for additional application details.

structured_extraction.program_name: Anne Arundel County Literacy Council (AACLC) Adult Education Services
structured_extraction.program_description: AACLC provides free literacy, math, English language, and high school diploma preparation services to adults in Anne Arundel County. Trained volunteers offer one-on-one tutoring to help adults reach personal education goals such as employment readiness, GED attainment, and supporting their children's learning.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free assessments, one-on-one tutoring (at least one hour per week), and books and materials at no cost to eligible adult students.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults in Anne Arundel County seeking to improve literacy, math, English language skills, or earn a high school diploma or GED.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Literacy tutoring, math instruction, English language learning, and high school diploma/GED preparation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to adults in Anne Arundel County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be an adult residing in Anne Arundel County
Must be seeking assistance with literacy, math, English language, or high school diploma preparation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the AACLC contact page at icanread.org/contact-us to get started, or use the 'Refer a Student' page at icanread.org/refer-a-student-to-aaclc.

structured_extraction.program_name: Anne Arundel County Police Student Internship Program
structured_extraction.program_description: An unpaid internship program for current college students, preferably majoring in criminal justice, to learn about law enforcement by experiencing various aspects and responsibilities of police work while completing a project for their studies.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Unpaid internship placement with the Anne Arundel County Police Department. Students gain hands-on experience in various aspects of law enforcement while completing an academic project as part of their college coursework.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Current college students, preferably majoring in criminal justice, who are enrolled in an internship or independent study course at their college or university.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Gaining law enforcement experience and completing a required academic project.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is administered by Anne Arundel County Police Department.
requirements_list: Must be 18 years of age or older
Must be currently enrolled in college
Must be enrolled in an internship or independent study class at their college or university
Must have a 2.5 or higher grade point average on a 4.0 scale
Must pass a criminal background check
No felony arrests
Misdemeanor arrests considered on a case-by-case basis
No felony or serious misdemeanor convictions
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application online. Applicants are subject to criminal records and background checks.

structured_extraction.program_name: Anne Arundel County Solar Energy Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A one-time tax credit on County real property taxes for residential dwellings in Anne Arundel County that install solar energy equipment (including solar panels, photovoltaic arrays, collectors, storage tanks, and related hardware) on or after January 1, 2007. The credit amount is the lesser of 50% of the solar equipment cost (minus federal/state grants) or $2,500. The credit is applied against Anne Arundel County real property taxes levied on the eligible residential dwelling.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time tax credit from Anne Arundel County real property taxes levied on residential dwellings. The credit amount is the lesser of 50% of the solar equipment cost (minus any federal or state grants received) or $2,500. Applies to solar energy equipment (solar panels, photovoltaic arrays, collectors, storage tanks, and related hardware) installed on or after January 1, 2007. Equipment must be purchased (leased equipment is not eligible).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: June 1 immediately before the taxable year for which the tax credit is sought
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of residential dwellings in Anne Arundel County that install solar energy equipment on or after January 1, 2007.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of Anne Arundel County real property tax liability via a one-time tax credit for the purchase and installation of solar energy devices (collectors, photovoltaic arrays, solar panels, storage tanks, and related hardware for heating/cooling, electricity generation, or hot water) on residential dwellings.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Residential property must be located in Anne Arundel County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Property must be a residential dwelling in Anne Arundel County
Solar energy equipment must be installed on or after January 1, 2007
Equipment must collect, store, generate, or distribute solar energy
Equipment must be purchased (leased equipment is not eligible)
Must provide paid receipts, invoices, or documentation of purchase and installation costs
Must provide final inspection sticker for equipment
Application is filed only once for the duration of the credit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and submit the Solar Tax Credit Application to the Anne Arundel County Office of Finance by June 1 immediately before the taxable year for which the credit is sought. Provide paid receipts, invoices, or other documentation of purchase and installation costs, as well as a final inspection sticker for the equipment. If the solar system is leased, note that leased equipment is not eligible for the credit.

structured_extraction.program_name: Anne Arundel County Stormwater Management Property Tax Credit Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Residential and commercial property owners in Anne Arundel County can receive a tax credit on their County real property taxes for the installation of qualified permanent stormwater management practices, such as living shorelines, living roofs, permeable pavers, rain gardens, bioretention installations, cisterns, or other approved devices that reduce stormwater runoff. The credit equals 10% of the cost of materials and installation of qualifying improvements, not to exceed $10,000 over the five-year life of the credit. The credit applies to County real property taxes only and takes effect in the taxable year following submission of the approved application.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A tax credit equal to 10% of the cost of materials and installation for qualified permanent stormwater management improvements, up to a maximum of $10,000 over the five-year life of the credit. The credit applies to County real property taxes only and takes effect in the taxable year following submission of the approved application. Qualifying improvements include living shorelines, living roofs, permeable pavers, rain gardens, bioretention installations, cisterns, rain barrels, constructed wetlands, wet ponds, sidewalk infiltration planters, and other approved permanent stormwater management practices.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Application must be submitted within 45 days of completion of qualifying improvements
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential and commercial property owners in Anne Arundel County who have recently installed or plan to install permanent stormwater management practices approved by the Department of Public Works, including living shoreline projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of Anne Arundel County real property tax liability to offset the cost of installing qualified permanent stormwater management devices or practices on private property, including living shorelines, living roofs, permeable pavers, rain gardens, bioretention installations, cisterns, and other approved stormwater management practices.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to property owners within Anne Arundel County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a residential or commercial property owner in Anne Arundel County
Must install qualified stormwater management improvements approved by the Department of Public Works
Department of Public Works must certify property as qualified
Improvements must permanently reduce and change drainage patterns of stormwater runoff

Qualifying projects include living shorelines, living roofs, permeable pavers, rain gardens, bioretention installations, cisterns, rain barrels, constructed wetlands, wet ponds, and other approved methods
Application must be submitted within 45 days of completion of qualifying improvements
The credit cannot be combined with other tax credits
The qualified improvements cannot be installed as a requirement under any State or local law
The qualified improvements must be included on the Department of Public Works' list of approved devices for this program
Installed practices must pass an inspection by County staff before the credit is approved
The County retains the right to inspect the practice during the life of the credit
Taxpayer must be current on all taxes owed to the County
Improvements must be in working condition and regularly maintained for the duration of the credit period
Application must include cost documentation, sworn statement about maintenance, and acknowledgment of inspection rights
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete the Stormwater Management Tax Credit Application Form. Submit it within 45 days of completing improvements by email to taxcredits@aacounty.org or by mail to Anne Arundel County, Office of Finance, Attn: Tax Credits, PO Box 427, Annapolis, MD 21404-0427. The application must include cost documentation, a sworn statement about maintenance, and acknowledgment of inspection rights. Applications are reviewed by Department of Public Works staff, who must certify the property as qualified. The property will be inspected before the credit is approved. The property owner receives written notification of approval or denial.

structured_extraction.program_name: Anne Arundel County Watershed Restoration Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Anne Arundel County annually funds projects that reduce pollutants through on-the-ground watershed restoration practices. The program awards grants to 501(c) nonprofit organizations to implement watershed restoration projects on community or public property. Projects must reduce stormwater flowing into local waterways, treat and filter pollutants from impervious surfaces, and engage residents in the restoration and protection of local rivers and streams. Eligible practices include stormwater management, stream restoration, and related improvements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual grant funding for on-the-ground watershed restoration projects on community or public property. Grants are awarded to implement practices that reduce stormwater runoff, treat and filter pollutants from impervious surfaces, and engage residents in restoration activities. Specific award amounts and terms are not described on the program page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: 501(c) nonprofit organizations and other eligible entities seeking funding to implement watershed restoration and pollution reduction projects in Anne Arundel County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: On-the-ground watershed restoration projects that reduce stormwater flowing into local waterways, treat and filter pollutants from impervious surfaces, and engage residents in the restoration and protection of local rivers and streams. Eligible practices include stormwater management and stream restoration.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Community or public property in Anne Arundel County, Maryland
requirements_list: Applicant must be a 501(c) nonprofit organization
Projects must be on community or public property
Projects must reduce stormwater flowing into local waterways, treat pollutants from impervious surfaces, and engage residents
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Chesapeake Bay Trust grant portal. Visit the grant program page at the link provided for application details.

structured_extraction.program_name: Anne Arundel County Watershed Restoration and Forestry Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program administered through the Chesapeake Bay Trust that funds projects supporting the reduction of pollutants flowing into local waterways, cost-effective reforestation and greening efforts, and increases in protected forested land throughout Anne Arundel County and the City of Annapolis. Funding supports stormwater facility design and project implementation, including engineering, public outreach, and long-term maintenance agreements, to improve watershed health and water quality.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants awarded annually to support stormwater and forestry goals, including reducing water pollutants, reforestation, increasing tree cover, reducing flooding and erosion, habitat protection, and increasing protected forested land throughout Anne Arundel County and the City of Annapolis. Grants may fund stormwater project design (engineering, public outreach, maintenance agreements) or construction/implementation of stormwater facilities. Publicly bid construction work is typically required. Applications are typically due in the spring.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners, organizations, individuals, non-profits, and local governments in Anne Arundel County and the City of Annapolis seeking to restore watersheds, expand forest cover, support stormwater management improvements, and improve water quality.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Watershed restoration, reforestation, greening efforts, stormwater management, habitat protection, increasing protected forested land, design of stormwater treatment facilities (engineering, public outreach, maintenance agreements), and construction/implementation of stormwater facilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County, Maryland, including the City of Annapolis.
requirements_list: Projects must improve water quality
Publicly bid construction work is typically required
Long-term maintenance agreements may be required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Chesapeake Bay Trust website. Applications are typically due in the spring. See the Chesapeake Bay Trust website for current details and deadlines.

structured_extraction.program_name: Anne Arundel Ready (AAR) Community Resilience Program

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Preparedness education, emergency continuity planning, and community outreach activities
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to organizations located in Anne Arundel County, Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Fill out the online application form available on the county website.

structured_extraction.program_name: Anne Arundel Women Giving Together (AAWGT) Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: AAWGT awards grants to local nonprofits that improve the quality of life for women and families in Anne Arundel County. Funded areas include education, literacy, housing, access to healthy food, affordable health care, and curbing violence.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants awarded to local nonprofits. AAWGT has awarded over $1.7 million in grants to 52 local nonprofits since its founding in 2006. Specific grant amounts are not stated on this page.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Education, literacy, housing, access to healthy food, affordable health care, reducing violence, and other initiatives improving lives of women and children

Programs must benefit women and/or families in Anne Arundel County

Assistance includes answering questions, providing literature, offering staff and resident presentations, and helping property owners set up compliant recycling programs.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free technical assistance including answering questions, providing informational literature, in-person presentations to staff and residents, and step-by-step guidance for setting up a recycling program. Also provides a brochure on getting started and a registration form for properties.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners and managers of apartment buildings or condominium councils with ten or more dwelling units in Anne Arundel County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Setting up and operating a resident recycling program that collects metal, plastic, glass containers, and paper

structured_extraction.program_name: Arundel Community Reinvestment (ACR) Revitalization Tandem Grant Initiative
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that complements the Arundel Community Reinvestment (ACR) loan program. Business and property owners in Anne Arundel County's 11 Commercial Revitalization Districts, the inner West Street corridor in Annapolis (Church Circle to Chinquapin Round Road), and the Brooklyn Park Enterprise Zone who are approved for an ACR loan can receive a grant equal to 25 percent of their loan amount to fund façade improvements, up to a maximum of $25,000. Applicants must first apply and be approved for an ACR loan of up to $100,000 to qualify for the grant. Total grant funding is supported by $544,350 in American Rescue Plan (ARP) funds.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant equal to 25% of the approved ACR loan amount, up to a maximum of $25,000. Funds must be used for façade improvements. The accompanying ACR loan offers up to $100,000 at 0% interest, repaid over 3 to 7 years, and is limited to 90% of total project costs. Total grant funding is supported by $544,350 in American Rescue Plan (ARP) funds.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses and commercial property owners located in Anne Arundel County's 11 Commercial Revitalization Districts, the inner West Street corridor in Annapolis (Church Circle to Chinquapin Round Road), and the Brooklyn Park Enterprise Zone.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Façade improvements including renovation and upgrades to building exteriors, site improvements, and landscaping on commercial properties in eligible revitalization districts.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Anne Arundel County's 11 Commercial Revitalization Districts, the inner West Street corridor in Annapolis (Church Circle to Chinquapin Round Road), and the state-designated Enterprise Zone in Brooklyn Park.
requirements_list: Must be a business or property owner located in one of the county's 11 Commercial Revitalization Districts, the inner West Street area in Annapolis (Church Circle to Chinquapin Round Road), or the Brooklyn Park Enterprise Zone
Must apply for and be approved for an ACR loan of up to $100,000
Grant is limited to 25% of the loan amount, up to $25,000
Funds must be used for eligible exterior/façade improvements or site improvements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply for an ACR loan through AAEDC. If approved for the loan, you may receive the tandem grant equal to 25% of the loan amount for façade improvements. More information is available on the Arundel Community Reinvestment Fund page on the AAEDC website at https://www.aaedc.org/business/financing-and-tax-credits/acr-fund/

structured_extraction.program_description: A free certification and marketing program administered by Anne Arundel County that connects local farmers, agricultural businesses, restaurants, and food businesses to consumers. The program certifies Anne Arundel County farmers and agricultural businesses to increase awareness of local farming and food sourcing, helping farms get their products in front of buyers at local farm stands, farmers markets, wineries, and grocery stores. It also certifies restaurants and food businesses that source at least 25% of ingredients from in-season Maryland farms and at least 10% from Anne Arundel County farms. Certified businesses are listed in the Arundel Agriculture Grown Guide and promoted through local buy-local initiatives.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free certification and marketing support for Anne Arundel County farmers, agricultural businesses, restaurants, and food businesses. Farmers and agricultural businesses are listed in the Arundel Agriculture Grown Guide and promoted through local buy-local initiatives. Restaurants and food businesses that meet local sourcing thresholds receive certification and promotion to consumers to increase awareness of their local sourcing practices.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Anne Arundel County farmers, agricultural businesses, restaurants, chefs, and food businesses seeking free certification and marketing to reach local consumers and increase awareness of local food sourcing.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Certification and marketing to increase visibility and sales of locally grown products and to promote local food sourcing practices among restaurants and food businesses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be located in or sourcing from Anne Arundel County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a farmer or agricultural business in Anne Arundel County
Source at least 25% of ingredients from in-season products from a Maryland farm
Source at least 10% of ingredients from an Anne Arundel County farm
Percentages are based on total purchases
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Farmers and agricultural businesses should contact Shelley Garrett, Agricultural Business Development Director, by phone at 410-222-7410 or by email to become an Arundel Grown Certified business. Restaurants and chefs currently meeting the sourcing requirements are encouraged to apply through AAEDC.

structured_extraction.program_name: Bill 13-22 – Qualified Data Center Personal Property Tax Reduction
structured_extraction.program_description: Establishes a reduction in the assessed value of qualified data center personal property used in qualified data centers for the purpose of calculating Anne Arundel County personal property tax. Provides tax incentives to encourage data center development and operation in Anne Arundel County. Defines eligibility terms, sets the amount of the reduction, outlines the application process, and specifies when the reduction begins and ends.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reduction in the assessed value of qualified data center personal property for the purpose of calculating Anne Arundel County personal property tax. 100% reduction in assessment for the first five taxable years, followed by a 50% reduction for years 6–15, for a total 15-year reduction period.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 15 immediately before the taxable year for which the reduction is sought
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners or operators of qualified data centers in Anne Arundel County that hold qualifying personal property used in those data centers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of Anne Arundel County personal property tax liability on qualified data center equipment and property.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only within Anne Arundel County, Maryland, including multiple locations within the county owned or operated by the same entity.
requirements_list: Property must be qualified data center personal property as defined in the ordinance
Property must be used in a qualified data center
Minimum $10 million total investment in the qualified data center
Creation of at least 10 qualified positions
Must file a personal property tax return with the State Department of Assessments and Taxation
Certification of investment amount and number of qualified positions required
Application must be filed by April 15 deadline (immediately before the taxable year for which the reduction is sought)
Must maintain the required investment level and qualified positions to retain the reduction
Must continue doing business in Anne Arundel County to retain the reduction
An annual report is required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Application form developed by the Office of Finance and Anne Arundel County Economic Development Corporation. Submit application no later than April 15 immediately before the taxable year for which the reduction is sought. See the full bill text for complete details.

structured_extraction.program_description: A county loan program that helps property owners finance clean energy improvements, water efficiency projects, environmental remediation projects, renewable energy projects, and resiliency projects through property tax assessments. structured_extraction.program_name: Commercial Revitalization District Program Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit for property owners in Anne Arundel County who renovate, rehabilitate, construct, demolish, or redevelop a commercially or industrially zoned property located in one of the county's 11 designated Commercial Revitalization districts, including the Glen Burnie Sustainable Community Overlay Area. The credit offsets the incremental increase in real property tax assessment resulting from qualifying improvements for up to five years, extendable to 10 years for projects with $10 million or more in private funding. Improvements must include new building construction, rehabilitation of an existing building, or demolition and subsequent construction, and must result in at least $100,000 of assessed value increase. The property must be certified by the Office of Planning and Zoning as a qualified property, and owners must apply to the County Office of Finance within 120 days after receiving the notice of assessment from the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A property tax credit equal to the incremental increase in real property tax assessment resulting from qualifying improvements. The credit lasts up to five years, with an extended five-year period (years 6-10) available for projects funded by at least $10,000,000 in private funds. Qualifying improvements include new building construction, rehabilitation of an existing building, or demolition and subsequent construction of a commercial property. Improvements must result in at least $100,000 of assessed value increase. The property must be located in one of the eleven designated Commercial Revitalization Areas and certified by the Office of Planning and Zoning. The owner must apply to the County Office of Finance within 120 days after receiving the notice of assessment from the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation. Reduces Anne Arundel County real property tax liability for properties in designated commercial revitalization areas.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Within 120 days after the issuance of the Notice of Assessment by the State Department of Assessments and Taxation
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners with commercially or industrially zoned properties in one of Anne Arundel County's 11 designated Commercial Revitalization districts, including the Glen Burnie Sustainable Community Overlay Area, who invest at least $100,000 in improvements to their property.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Renovation, rehabilitation, new building construction, demolition and subsequent construction, or redevelopment of an existing building or building site; property adaptive reuse or redevelopment improvements of at least $100,000 in assessed value in a designated Commercial Revitalization Area; reduction of Anne Arundel County real property tax liability.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Property must be commercially or industrially zoned and located totally or partially within one of Anne Arundel County's 11 designated Commercial Revitalization districts, including: Area 1 - Brooklyn Park (Ritchie Highway), Area 2 - Glen Burnie Town Center North, Area 3 - Glen Burnie Town Center Core (B&A Blvd), Area 4 - Glen Burnie Town Center South (Crain Highway), Area 5 - Pasadena (Mountain Road), Area 6 - Riviera Beach (Fort Smallwood Road), Area 7 - North Odenton (MD175), Area 8 - Maryland City/Russett (MD198), Area 9 - Ferndale (B&A Boulevard), Area 10 - Glen Burnie/Harundale (Ritchie Highway), Area 11, and the Glen Burnie Sustainable Community Overlay Area. Property cannot be in a tax increment development district (except Odenton Town Center Development District).
requirements_list: Property must be located in a commercial revitalization area designated by County Council ordinance
Property must be commercially or industrially zoned
Property must be located totally or partially within one of Anne Arundel County's 11 designated Commercial Revitalization districts
Improvements must result in at least $100,000 of assessed value increase (full cash value)
Property must be certified by the Office of Planning and Zoning as a qualified property
Improvements must be constructed per building permit issued by the County
Application must be submitted to the County Office of Finance within 120 days of receiving the notice of assessment from the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation
Property cannot be located in a tax increment development district (except Odenton Town Center Development District)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Office of Planning and Zoning for certification as a qualified property. Then complete and submit the Commercial Revitalization District Program Property Tax Credit Application to the Anne Arundel County Office of Finance within 120 days of receiving the notice of assessment from the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation. Contact AAEDC for additional information.

structured_extraction.program_description: Communities of Hope is a place-based model designed by Casey Family Programs to engage local communities and bring wrap-around services and support to families in high-need areas of Anne Arundel County. The goal is to reduce poverty and lower the number of children placed in out-of-home care. Four communities are served: Brooklyn Park, West County (Severn/Meade), Annapolis, and South County. A diverse group of stakeholders — including local agencies, community organizations, residents, faith leaders, business owners, and service providers — work together to build supports that strengthen family wellness and stability. Each community focuses on core results including children entering school ready to learn, safe communities, and economically stable families, using trauma-informed and evidence-based approaches.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Wrap-around community services and supports are coordinated and delivered to families in high-need communities. Services include: mobile outreach, bilingual services, job training and vocational programs, affordable childcare, mental health and behavioral health services, housing resources, mentorship programs, home visiting programs, case management and universal intake, leadership capacity development for youth, food distribution programs, safe transportation, and community health ambassador programs. Partners collaborate to create a network of supports addressing family wellness, stability, and poverty reduction.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families, youth, and residents living in high-need communities in Anne Arundel County (Brooklyn Park, West County/Severn/Meade, Annapolis, and South County), as well as local agencies, community organizations, faith leaders, business owners, and service providers interested in partnering. Includes bilingual and Spanish-speaking populations, people experiencing poverty, and those seeking healthcare, employment, or basic needs assistance.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding and resources support wrap-around services addressing family wellness, stability, and poverty reduction including: program development and implementation, service coordination, leadership development, resource development, community awareness initiatives, healthcare and food access, job training and employment pathways, early childhood education, youth development, housing assistance, and data collection and evaluation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Limited to four communities in Anne Arundel County: Brooklyn Park (North County), West County (Severn/Meade), Annapolis (ZIP codes 21401 and 21403 prioritized), and South County.
requirements_list: Must be located in or serve one of the four designated Communities of Hope areas in Anne Arundel County
Commitment to trauma-informed approach
Focus on evidence-based practices
Willingness to address systemic barriers, racism, and inequality
Bilingual capacity preferred
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Tracey Cherry, Community of Hope Director, at SRCher88@aacounty.org to learn more or to become a partner in any COH.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grants funded by a portion of the sales tax from adult-use recreational cannabis sales in Anne Arundel County, administered by Arundel Community Development Services (ACDS). The grants support community-based initiatives intended to benefit low-income communities, with priority given to organizations serving residents in Disproportionately Impacted Areas (DIAs) — zip codes that had cannabis possession charge rates above 150% of Maryland's 10-year average. Projects must address at least one of four strategic priorities: Mental Health and Substance Abuse Services; Education, Youth Enrichment, and After School Activities; Housing and Homelessness Prevention Services; or Workforce Development and Employment Training.

Project-based grants ranging from $25,000 to $180,000, with a total allocation of $1,691,200 across four program categories for FY2026. Funds must address one or more of the following priorities: Mental Health and Substance Abuse Services; Education, Youth Enrichment, and After School Activities; Housing and Homelessness Prevention Services; or Workforce Development and Employment Training.

Priority given to organizations serving residents in Disproportionately Impacted Areas (DIAs).

structured_extraction.program_description: The County Executive's Community Support Grant provides funding to non-profit organizations in Anne Arundel County to operate or expand existing programs, pilot new programs, or fund one-time projects and small equipment purchases that improve the lives of Anne Arundel County residents. The program is administered by Arundel Community Development Services (ACDS) in partnership with the county. Priority is given to projects serving underserved populations, addressing community health and well-being, promoting equity and inclusion, or eliminating the Opportunity Gap in education. The program awards grants on a recurring basis, with award lists publicly available for fiscal years FY2021 through FY2026. Approximately $2 million is anticipated to be available for FY2027.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Approximately $2 million is anticipated to be available for FY2027 (funding period July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027). Two grant types are available: (1) Program/Project Support covering staff costs, supplies, travel, equipment, and a proportional share of administrative overhead; and (2) Capacity Building Support for one-time funds for strategic planning, governance, professional development, technology improvements, and systems innovation. Administrative overhead and fringe costs not to exceed 5% of total award. Individual awards range from $15,000 to $50,000 per organization. Collaborative projects are preferred but not required. Faith-based organizations may apply but must serve the broader community and keep inherently religious activities separate from funded programs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations serving Anne Arundel County residents, particularly those addressing underserved populations, community health and well-being, equity and inclusion, and education opportunity gaps. Populations served include people with disabilities, disaster victims, youth, immigrants, LGBTQ+ communities, incarcerated individuals, low-income adults, foster youth, children, seniors, people in recovery, unaccompanied immigrant children, and teen parents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Program/project staff costs, supplies, travel, equipment, administrative overhead proportional to program budget (not to exceed 5% of total award); one-time equipment purchases; capacity building activities including strategic planning, governance, professional development, technology improvements, and systems innovation; services to underserved populations, community health and well-being initiatives, equity and inclusion programs, and efforts to eliminate the opportunity gap in education.

Programs or projects must benefit Anne Arundel County residents

Proposals should focus on at least one County Executive priority: serving underserved populations, addressing community health and well-being, promoting equity and inclusion, or eliminating the Opportunity Gap in education

Procurement policies compliance required: cost-effective, competitive, conflict-of-interest free, with tiered competitive bidding based on purchase cost
Minority/women-owned business utilization efforts required
Faith-based organizations must serve the broader community; inherently religious activities must be separate from funded programs

structured_extraction.program_name: Conservation Land Real Property Tax Credit

structured_extraction.program_name: Diabetes Self-Management Program (Living Well with Diabetes)
structured_extraction.program_description: A free six-week workshop series for people diagnosed with prediabetes, Type 1 or Type 2 Diabetes, and their caregivers or family and friends. Participants meet for 2.5 hours once a week to learn self-management tools including goal setting, action planning, healthy eating, exercise, medication use, stress management, and communication with healthcare providers. Classes are led by trained volunteer leaders, many of whom live with diabetes themselves, and are held in community settings such as churches, libraries, and hospitals. Available virtually for Maryland residents and in-person in specific counties including Anne Arundel, Cecil, and Calvert. Each participant receives a copy of the companion book 'Living a Healthy Life with Chronic Conditions' and an audio relaxation tape at no cost. Registration is required.

Available virtually for Maryland residents and in-person in Anne Arundel County, Cecil County, and Calvert County.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Digital Services Grant Program helps small brick-and-mortar businesses and nonprofits in Anne Arundel County compete in a digital economy and recover from COVID-19 pandemic impacts. The program was launched to support businesses harmed by COVID-19 pandemic restrictions by helping them attract new customers through digital tools and services. Funded with $500,000 in federal ARPA (American Rescue Plan Act) funds designated by the Maryland Department of Commerce under the state RELIEF Act, the program targeted small businesses that had not yet received COVID-19 relief grants. Eligible organizations—small businesses with 1 to 20 employees established before March 9, 2020, and nonprofits—operating in qualifying sectors (retail, beauty and personal wellness, adult and children's activity centers, and nonprofits) could use the funds to purchase or subscribe to digital platforms and services such as email and mobile marketing, customer relationship management (CRM) software, customer loyalty programs, e-commerce solutions (online ordering and sales), and website or social media advertising. Individual grants of up to $10,000 were available; ultimately $460,800 was awarded to 144 businesses, with an average award of approximately $3,200. Applications were accepted from September 20, 2021 through October 1, 2021. The program particularly supported woman-owned, minority-owned, and veteran-owned businesses, with businesses fewer than 10 employees receiving 77% of awards.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time grants of up to $10,000 per eligible applicant (average award approximately $3,200) for the purchase of or subscription to digital platforms and services, including email and mobile marketing, customer relationship management (CRM), customer rewards/loyalty programs, e-commerce (online ordering and sales), and website and social media advertising. Total program funding was $500,000 from federal ARPA funds designated by the Maryland Department of Commerce; $460,800 was awarded to 144 businesses. Applications are closed and funds have been fully awarded.

Includes woman-owned, minority-owned, veteran-owned businesses, and businesses that had not previously received COVID-19 relief grants.

structured_extraction.program_name: Disabled Law Enforcement Officers and Rescue Workers Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit of 100% on County real property taxes levied on a dwelling owned by a disabled law enforcement officer, rescue worker, or surviving spouse of a fallen officer/worker who meets specific eligibility criteria and owns/resides in a qualifying property in Anne Arundel County.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of Anne Arundel County real property tax liability on primary residential dwelling.

Applicant must have been domiciled in Maryland within the required timeframe before adjudication of disability or death. If property was not in Anne Arundel County at time of disability adjudication, applicant must have established Maryland residency within 5 years before adjudication.

Dwelling must have been owned at the time of disability determination or death

Dwelling must have been acquired within the required timeframe before disability/death, or after qualifying for credit on a previous dwelling

Credit ceases upon remarriage of a surviving spouse

structured_extraction.program_description: A micro grant program to help Anne Arundel County businesses recover from damage and disruptions caused by Tropical Storm Ida and the accompanying tornado that struck the region on September 1, 2021. Businesses can use the grants to cover costs such as physical property repairs, replacement of business equipment or inventory, lease or rental support, vendor bill support, or moving expenses. The program is funded with $25,000 from the TD Charitable Foundation, the charitable giving arm of TD Bank, providing grants of up to $5,000 per eligible business. Eligible businesses must have a brick-and-mortar location in Anne Arundel County and be in good standing with the State of Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_name: EMS Fee for Service Transport Program – Financial Hardship Waiver
structured_extraction.program_description: A compassionate billing program that provides financial hardship waivers for patients unable to pay EMS transport fees. Anne Arundel County Fire Department seeks reimbursement from insurance carriers (Medicaid, Medicare, private insurance) to supplement operational expenses. County residents' taxes are considered as payment; non-residents and uninsured/underinsured individuals may apply for waivers or payment plans based on financial hardship.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Waiver or reduction of EMS transport charges for qualifying individuals who demonstrate financial hardship. County residents are not billed (taxes considered as payment). Annapolis residents are treated as County residents for billing purposes. Non-residents may apply for waivers if income is at or below 250% of federal poverty guidelines or if they can document catastrophic financial hardship (severe extended illness, loss of all income, homelessness). Payment plan arrangements are also available.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Waiver or reduction of EMS ambulance transport charges; payment plan arrangements for transport fees.

structured_extraction.program_name: Easy Travel Access (ETA) Program (Taxi Voucher & Rides-On-Demand)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Easy Travel Access (ETA) program provides transportation assistance to older adults aged 55 and older and individuals aged 18 and older with disabilities in Anne Arundel County. The program has two components: (1) the ETA Taxi Voucher Program, which offers discounted taxi voucher books sold at $5 each with a face value of $10 in taxi fares, allowing residents to purchase up to 15 books per month with a county match of up to $75 per month, usable with participating cab companies for errands, grocery shopping, polling places, and other trips within the county; and (2) the ETA Rides-On-Demand Program, which provides door-to-door on-demand transportation by professional drivers at approximately 50% of the normal cost, with same-day service available with at least two hours' notice, covering trips within Anne Arundel County and up to 20 miles outside the county line (excluding airport trips). Both components share a county match of up to $75 per month.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two components: (1) Taxi Voucher Program — voucher books sold at $5 each with a face value of $10; residents may purchase up to 15 books per month. (2) Rides-On-Demand — rides provided at approximately 50% of normal cost with same-day service available (minimum 2 hours' notice); door-to-door service within Anne Arundel County and up to 20 miles outside the county line (airport trips excluded). The county provides a combined match of up to $75 per month across both components. Participants may purchase up to $150/month in vouchers total.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Anne Arundel County residents who are 55 years of age or older, or 18 years of age or older with a disability. Individuals aged 18–54 must have a verifiable transportation disability that precludes use of public transportation. Income limits apply: at or below $1,255/month (single) or $1,703/month (with spouse).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Taxi fares with participating cab companies within Anne Arundel County for errands, grocery shopping, polling places, and other trips; and on-demand door-to-door transportation within Anne Arundel County and up to 20 miles outside the county line (excluding airport trips).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be an Anne Arundel County resident. Rides-On-Demand service area covers Anne Arundel County and up to 20 miles outside the county line.
requirements_list: Must be an Anne Arundel County resident
Must be 55 years of age or older, OR 18 years of age or older with a disability
Must meet income requirements: at or below $1,255/month (single) or $1,703/month (with spouse)
Must provide a Maryland State driver's license or ID with an Anne Arundel County address

Persons aged 18–54 with a disability must provide SSI/SSDI award letter or completed Disability Verification Form signed by a physician, psychiatrist, psychologist, or program director of a qualified social agency
Disability verification must document how the disability prevents use of public transportation and specify whether the disability is permanent or temporary
Participant must voluntarily enroll in the program
Participant is responsible for scheduling own trips and paying for all scheduled trips
Must adhere to requirements set by Rides-On-Demand service providers and Anne Arundel County Department of Aging and Disabilities
Must sign liability/indemnification form
Must submit a completed ETA Application, Liability Form, and applicable Order Form (Taxi Voucher or Rides-On-Demand) with payment by check or money order
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit one of two office locations in person (2666 Riva Rd, Annapolis or 7320 Ritchie Hwy, Glen Burnie, walk-in hours 8:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m.), or mail the completed ETA Application, Liability Form, Order Form, required ID, and payment (check or money order payable to Anne Arundel County) to Easy Travel Access Program, Department of Aging and Disabilities, 2666 Riva Road, Suite 400, Annapolis, MD 21401. An online ETA application form is also available at https://www.aacounty.org/aging-and-disabilities/services/transportation-assistance/eta-form. Persons with a disability must also submit a completed Disability Verification Form signed by a qualified health care provider. After enrollment in Rides-On-Demand, call the reservations number to schedule rides.
