structured_extraction.program_description: Anne Arundel County inclusionary zoning law (also called Moderately Priced Dwelling Unit or Inclusionary Zoning law) that requires developers of new residential subdivisions to offer a percentage of units at affordable prices for essential workers. Developers must make 15% of rental units available to households earning up to 75% of area median income and 10% of for-sale units available to households earning up to 100% of area median income. Modeled after Inclusionary Housing programs existing in over 700 jurisdictions across the USA.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Developers of new residential subdivisions must offer 15% of rental units at prices affordable to households earning up to 75% of area median income ($62,156 for a single person) and 10% of for-sale units affordable to households earning up to 100% of area median income ($82,875 for a single person). Over 200 new homes and apartments are expected to be available annually. Developer incentives include density bonuses, waived impact fees for MPDUs, and a 50% reduction in Capital Facility Connection Charges for water and wastewater. Developers who do not provide moderately priced units may pay a fee in lieu (1% for certain single-family detached developments, 3% of purchase price for others).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Essential workers such as teachers and teacher aides, firefighters, police officers, nurses, construction workers, public service workers, and service industry workers in Anne Arundel County or City of Annapolis who meet income eligibility thresholds. Also includes first-time homebuyers and county/city employees including Anne Arundel County Public Schools employees.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchasing or renting a moderately priced dwelling unit in Anne Arundel County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County and City of Annapolis. Eligible households must include at least one member who is a resident of the county or City of Annapolis, employed in the county or city for the last 12 months, or currently employed by Anne Arundel County, City of Annapolis, or Anne Arundel County Public Schools.
requirements_list: At least one household member must be a resident of Anne Arundel County or City of Annapolis, or employed in the county/city for the last 12 months, or currently employed by Anne Arundel County, City of Annapolis, or Anne Arundel County Public Schools
Rental applicants must earn at or below 75% of area median income ($62,156 for a single person, higher for families)
Ownership applicants must earn at or below 100% of area median income ($82,875 for a single person, higher for families)
Have not owned a home in the last 3 years (for homeownership units)
Must qualify for a first mortgage loan (for homeownership)
Must meet credit standards and rental application standards
Income limits are adjustable up to 2 times per year
Applications qualified by Anne Arundel County Department of Social Services / ACDS
AACPS employees are explicitly eligible and may receive income requirement adjustments
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The bill established a Moderately Priced Dwelling Unit Program Administrator (administered by Arundel Community Development Services Inc. / ACDS) to oversee applications. Eligible workers apply to purchase or rent qualifying units as they become available through new residential developments subject to the ordinance. Applications are qualified by ACDS.

structured_extraction.program_name: FY 2027 Video Lottery Terminal (VLT) Community Grants (Local Development Council Grants)
structured_extraction.program_description: Competitive grants for nonprofit and community organizations serving residents within a three-mile radius of Live! Casino at Arundel Mills. Administered by Arundel Community Development Services (ACDS) through the Anne Arundel County Local Development Council, and funded by a share of video lottery terminal revenues from Maryland Live! Casino, the grants support human services, community beautification and revitalization, educational outcomes, workforce development, transportation, and social services in communities near the casino. Two grant types are available: Community Grants ($1,000 to $40,000) awarded competitively, and Invitation-Only Grants (over $40,000) for organizations invited by the LDC to address a specific identified need or priority. Past award lists and grant guidelines are available on the program page.
eligible_municipalities: Arundel Mills area (within 3 miles of Live! Casino)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Community grants range from $1,000 to $40,000 and are awarded on a competitive basis. Invitation-only grants may exceed $40,000 for organizations invited by the Local Development Council to address a specific identified need or priority. Funding is limited to three consecutive cycles; organizations become ineligible for one cycle afterward (waiverable). Two grant types exist: Non-Capital Grants (capacity building, operational efficiency) and Capital Grants (equipment, supplies, renovation, remodeling, restoration, new construction). Funds must be used primarily in communities in immediate proximity to Maryland Live! Casino. Permitted uses include infrastructure improvements, facilities, public safety, sanitation, economic and community development (including housing), workforce development, and other public services and improvements. The FY28 application process is expected to begin in November 2026. Specific award amounts vary by cycle; past award lists are available on the program page.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Wednesday, December 3, 2025 at 12:00pm (FY27); FY28 process will begin in November 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations, community associations, and government entities serving residents within a three-mile radius of Live! Casino at Arundel Mills in Anne Arundel County, particularly low- and moderate-income communities and those serving large numbers of residents or special needs populations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Community beautification and neighborhood revitalization (capital improvements, property repair); schools and educational institutions (beyond Board of Education funding); human services including transportation, childcare, recreation and youth development, food/nutrition assistance, employability/job skills training, case management and support, and affordable housing development; regional facilities for seniors services, job training, and wellness programs; workforce and skills development; non-capital capacity building and operational improvements; and capital improvements including equipment, supplies, renovation, remodeling, restoration, and new construction.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Organizations must serve communities and residents within a three-mile radius of Live! Casino at Arundel Mills in Anne Arundel County. Priority is given to casino-impacted communities and low-to-moderate income communities.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a nonprofit organization, community association, or government entity
Must serve residents within a three-mile radius of Live! Casino at Arundel Mills
Community grants are capped at $40,000 (minimum $1,000); larger capital grants require an invitation from the LDC

Must meet insurance requirements for grant awardees (Non-Capital Grants over $15,000 and all Capital Grants require Commercial General Liability ($1M), Business Automobile Liability ($1M), Workers' Compensation ($500K), and Directors and Officers Liability ($1M))
County must be named as additional insured
Must be in Good Standing Status
Must be located in or serve the Anne Arundel County community
Important community need without service duplication
Population served involves large number of residents or targets special needs
Project designed to meet identified need
Organization has appropriate experience, capabilities, and financial viability
Evidence of community support and collaboration
Reasonable budget that leverages other funding
Funding limited to three consecutive cycles; organization becomes ineligible for one cycle afterward (waiverable)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application through the Neighborly Software online portal at portal.neighborlysoftware.com/acds/Participant by the posted deadline. Review the Community Grant Guidelines and Tips for a Successful Grant Proposal before applying. Proposals must include: Cover Letter, Executive Summary, Need Statement, Project Description, Objectives, Methodology, Budget with justification, and Evaluation. Use SMART objectives (Specific, Measurable, Attainable, Relevant, Time Bound). Selected applicants present to the LDC board (10-minute presentation plus 5-minute Q&A). Training videos and slides are available to guide applicants through the process. Applications for FY27 are closed; the FY28 process will begin in November 2026. Contact excasa01@aacounty.org or eHarig-Blaine@acdsinc.org for special accommodations or language interpretation.

structured_extraction.program_name: Fall 2025 Professional Development Cohort Program – Fundraising & Sustainability 2.0
structured_extraction.program_description: A professional development cohort program for 501(c)(3) nonprofit leaders and staff in Anne Arundel County focused on diversifying funding sources and building organizational sustainability. The program covers advanced fundraising strategies, organizational storytelling, strategic prospecting, grant development, annual giving, major gifts, digital campaigns, and designing a diverse fundraising plan. Delivered in partnership with Maryland Nonprofits, participants receive expert facilitation, peer learning, networking, one-on-one consulting, and lifetime access to resource materials. The program is offered in multiple cohort cycles: a fall cohort (five sessions, 2.5 hours each, held every other week from October 8 to December 3, 2025, limited to 12 organizations) and a free virtual spring cohort (six bi-weekly sessions via Zoom from March 25 to June 3, 2026, 12:00–1:30 p.m., instruction provided by Dr. Lili Leonard, Founder of Black Dog Philanthropic Consulting, open to all eligible nonprofits). Prior cohort cycles have also been offered as free 3-month programs combining in-person sessions and online coaching for teams of 2–3 people from up to 10 organizations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Training is offered in multiple formats: (1) A fall cohort of five group sessions (2.5 hours each, every other week, October 8 – December 3, 2025) for up to three staff per organization, plus one-on-one consulting and lifetime access to resource materials. Cost is $75 for organizations with budgets under $500K and $150 for those with budgets over $500K; limited to 12 organizations on a first-come, first-served basis. (2) A free virtual spring cohort of six bi-weekly Zoom sessions (March 25 – June 3, 2026, 12:00–1:30 p.m.) covering fundraising foundations, donor storytelling, annual giving and digital campaigns, major gifts, grants strategy, and fundraising planning, facilitated by Dr. Lili Leonard of Black Dog Philanthropic Consulting. Participants may attend one or all sessions at no cost. Prior cohort cycles have been offered as free 3-month programs including in-person group training and virtual coaching sessions for teams of 2–3 staff from up to 10 organizations, focused on building or updating a resource development and financial sustainability plan.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit leaders and staff at 501(c)(3) organizations located in and serving Anne Arundel County, especially those serving underserved populations or focused on health and well-being with annual budgets under $750K. The advanced fall cohort requires a basic understanding of fundraising principles or prior completion of a Fundraising & Sustainability cohort. The spring cohort is open to all eligible 501(c)(3) nonprofits serving Anne Arundel County residents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Professional development training on diversifying nonprofit funding sources, including advanced fundraising strategies, grant development, donor storytelling, annual giving, major gifts, digital campaigns, sustainability planning, and developing or updating a resource development and financial sustainability plan.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Organizations must serve Anne Arundel County residents. For the fall cohort, administrative offices must be located in Anne Arundel County and at least 75% of the population served must reside in Anne Arundel County. The spring cohort is open to all eligible nonprofits serving Anne Arundel County residents.

Must have 501(c)(3) status for at least one year
In good standing with the State of Maryland
Must provide services to Anne Arundel County residents
Administrative offices must be located in Anne Arundel County (fall cohort)
At least 75% of population served must reside in Anne Arundel County (fall cohort)
Must agree to participate in all training and coaching sessions
Must agree to share outcome data with the Nonprofit Center
Participants should have completed a previous Fundraising & Sustainability cohort OR have a baseline knowledge of fundraising concepts (fall cohort)
Registration required via Google Form (spring cohort)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For the fall cohort: Register on a first-come, first-served basis. The Nonprofit Center will contact registered organizations regarding payment once the cohort is full. Organizations should only register if they can attend all listed session dates. For the spring cohort: Register online using the provided Google Form registration link; a Zoom link will be sent upon registration. Prior cohort cycles required completing an online application via SurveyMonkey by the stated deadline; apply only if your team can attend all required in-person and virtual sessions.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program gives current and aspiring farmers access to a wide variety of modern, well-maintained farm equipment to support planting, fencing, livestock handling, and poultry processing. Equipment is available at low daily rental rates ranging from $10 to $200 per day, reducing the need for farmers to purchase expensive machinery they only use occasionally. Available equipment includes no-till drills, a turbo till, post driver, manure spreader, spinner spreader, utility baler, seeders, a mulch layer, a cattle squeeze chute with scale, and a mobile poultry processing unit.

Available equipment includes no-till drills, a turbo till, post driver, manure spreader, spinner spreader, utility baler, seeders, a mulch layer, a cattle squeeze chute with scale, and a mobile poultry processing unit.

Normal retirement is available at age 50 with at least 5 years of service, or after 20 years of service regardless of age. The plan also supports early retirement options, joint & survivor options, social security adjustment options, military service credit, and transferred service.

structured_extraction.program_name: Foreign Trade Zone Personal Property Tax Credit

Does not apply to operating personal property of a public utility

structured_extraction.program_description: Private landowners can set up off-site mitigation banks by planting native trees on their property and selling reforestation 'credits' to developers and other landowners who need to meet forest mitigation requirements due to development projects. The bank owner plants trees, posts a security deposit to ensure survival, and places the planted area under a perpetual protective agreement such as a conservation easement. The program includes two categories: Critical Area Offsite Reforestation Banks and Non-Critical Area Offsite Reforestation Banks.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Private landowners plant native trees on their property and sell reforestation credits for profit to developers and landowners who have mitigation requirements. The bank owner posts a security to ensure tree survival and places the planted area under a perpetual protective agreement such as a conservation easement. Income is generated through the sale of credits. Two categories exist: Critical Area Offsite Reforestation Banks and Non-Critical Area Offsite Reforestation Banks.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private landowners in Anne Arundel County interested in earning income by planting forests and selling reforestation credits to developers with mitigation requirements, as well as entities requiring forest mitigation in Anne Arundel County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planting native trees on private property, posting security to ensure survival, and placing planted areas under a perpetual protective agreement such as a conservation easement. Offsite reforestation banking in both critical and non-critical areas.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County, Maryland, with critical and non-critical area distinctions.
requirements_list: Plant native trees on private property
Post a security to ensure tree survival
Place the planted area under a perpetual protective agreement such as a conservation easement
In some cases, preserve existing forested areas to satisfy portions of off-site planting requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Anne Arundel County Forestry Division at ipmailbox@aacounty.org or (410) 222-7442 for details. For questions about individual mitigation banks, use the Off-site Reforestation Bank Contact List. Two categories of banks are available: Critical Area Offsite Reforestation Banks and Non-Critical Area Offsite Reforestation Banks.

structured_extraction.program_name: Free Spay and Neuter Services for Qualified Low-Income Pet Owners
structured_extraction.program_description: Anne Arundel County Animal Services offers free or low-cost spay and neuter services to help control the pet population and support animal welfare. Free spay and neuter surgery is available for qualifying low-income pet owners in the county, and reduced-rate or free services are also available for animals adopted from or impounded by the agency.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free spay and neuter surgery for pets owned by qualifying low-income residents. Reduced-rate or free services are also available for animals adopted from or impounded by Anne Arundel County Animal Services.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income pet owners in Anne Arundel County, owners of animals adopted from or impounded by Animal Services, and general county residents seeking affordable spay/neuter options.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Spay and neuter veterinary procedures for pets.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County residents, particularly those who meet low-income qualifications.
requirements_list: Must be a qualifying low-income pet owner
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Animal Services at (410) 222-8900 to ask about eligibility and available services. For impounded animals, ask an Animal Services representative directly.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Anne Arundel County Department of Aging & Disabilities and the Anne Arundel County Foodbank provide free fresh produce boxes on Fridays to eligible residents age 60 and older, or age 18 and older with a disability.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free fresh produce boxes distributed on Fridays to eligible individuals who are age 60 or older, or age 18 or older with a disability.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Fresh produce boxes for personal consumption.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the Anne Arundel County Department of Aging & Disabilities website for current information and distribution details.

structured_extraction.program_name: Full Delivery of "Turnkey" Water Quality Improvements Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Anne Arundel County's Bureau of Watershed Protection and Restoration (BWPR) funds design-build-maintain contracts with private firms to construct cost-effective stormwater Best Management Practices (BMPs) on privately owned properties. Contractors work with landowners to select a site, pay the upfront construction costs, and then the County reimburses them after construction is complete and the project is verified to be generating water quality credits. The program helps the County meet its stormwater permit (NPDES MS4) and Chesapeake Bay water quality (TMDL) requirements. Bid opportunities are typically announced each fall via an annual Request for Proposals (RFP).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The County reimburses the full project cost after construction is complete and water quality benefits are verified, typically within one year of construction. Ongoing maintenance payments are released on an annual basis for 5 years after project completion. Recent annual awards have ranged from roughly $363,000 to $3,000,000. Only sites on private property within Anne Arundel County's MS4 geography are eligible. Proposals are evaluated on technical merit, implementation likelihood, and cost-effectiveness (cost per equivalent impervious acre treated).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Solicitations open annually in late September to early October
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private firms (contractors) who partner with private landowners to design, build, and maintain stormwater Best Management Practices on privately owned properties in Anne Arundel County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Design, construction, and maintenance of stormwater Best Management Practices (BMPs) such as living shorelines, stream restoration, wetland enhancement, and stormwater conveyance systems on private property
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Only sites on private property within Anne Arundel County's Municipal Separate Storm Sewer System (MS4) geography that do not conflict with existing projects are eligible.
requirements_list: Property must be located in Anne Arundel County
Project must be located on private property within Anne Arundel County's MS4 geography
Site must not conflict with existing projects underway
Private firms submit bids on behalf of property owners
Proposals are evaluated on technical merit including implementation likelihood (construction-ready projects are prioritized)
Proposals are evaluated on cost-effectiveness measured by the County's cost per equivalent impervious acre treated
Full reimbursement is paid only after project construction is complete and water quality benefits are verified by the County
Outside funding sources may be used to reduce project cost to the County, provided they do not diminish or encumber the water quality credits offered
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Find the annual Request for Proposals (RFP) on the Anne Arundel County Purchasing Office's Bid Opportunities webpage by searching 'full delivery of turnkey water quality improvements'. Solicitations typically open in late September to early October each year. Private firms submit competitive bids on behalf of a site or property owner.

Open to both new and established organizations

Property owners submit an application with supporting documents to request reclassification under state Critical Area regulations.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners in Anne Arundel County's Critical Area seeking to reclassify land from RCA or LDA to LDA or IDA.

structured_extraction.program_description: A plan approval process that allows non-profits, HOAs, and private landowners to enhance the habitat and ecological balance of natural areas in the Chesapeake Bay Critical Area, Forest Conservation Easements, or Bog Protection Areas. Eligible activities include pruning for plant health and safety, non-commercial timber stand improvement, and removal of non-native invasive vegetation with replanting of native species. The program also covers sediment and erosion control compliance and provides a two-year approval period for invasive species removal and native vegetation restoration. This is not for clearing vegetation related to development.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Plan review and approval allowing property owners and organizations to remove more than 5,000 square feet of existing natural vegetation in protected areas, subject to an on-site proposal review and plan approval by the Forestry Division. Allows site grading without a separate grading permit; requires compliance with Standard Sediment and Erosion Control Plan; provides a two-year approval period for invasive species removal and native vegetation restoration.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profits, homeowners associations (HOAs), and private landowners in Anne Arundel County seeking to remove more than 5,000 square feet of natural vegetation in the Chesapeake Bay Critical Area, Forest Conservation Easements, or Bog Protection Areas, as well as property owners with habitat enhancement and invasive species management needs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Habitat enhancement activities such as pruning for health and safety, non-commercial timber stand improvement, and removal of non-native invasive vegetation with replanting of native species.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Anne Arundel County, Maryland, specifically within the Chesapeake Bay Critical Area, Forest Conservation Easements, or Bog Protection Areas.
requirements_list: Must involve removal of greater than 5,000 square feet of existing natural vegetation
Work must be located in the Chesapeake Bay Critical Area, Forest Conservation Easements, or Bog Protection Areas
Activities must not include clearing for development or preparation for a development application
All required State and Federal permits must be obtained before Forestry approval
Approved Habitat Enhancement Plan must be posted on-site during work for inspection purposes
Completed application with tax account number
Scaled site plan (1"=20-50' ratio) with Limit of Disturbance
Description of existing conditions and proposed work
Eradication methods and timeline
Replanting/enhancement specifications (number and species of plants)
Erosion and sediment control documentation
Management plan for short-term and long-term maintenance
Owner certification of authority and accuracy
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Contact the Forestry Office at 410-222-7741 or forestry@aacounty.org to schedule an on-site proposal review. 2. Complete the Habitat Enhancement Plan application and submit a cover letter, completed application, scaled site plan, work description, and management plan to the Permit Center Reception Desk (1st Floor) or to the Anne Arundel County Department of Inspections and Permits, Forestry Program by email, fax, mail, or in person. 3. Obtain all required State and Federal permits. 4. Await plan approval before beginning work.

structured_extraction.program_name: High Performance Building Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit on County real property taxes for high performance buildings (both residential and commercial) in Anne Arundel County. Residential buildings must meet or exceed Silver rating in LEED Green Building Rating System for homes or International Code Council's 700 National Green Building Standard (NGBS). Commercial buildings must meet or exceed Silver rating in LEED or NGBS. Authorized under Maryland Tax-Property Article §9-242.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reduces Anne Arundel County real property taxes on the building (not land) for qualifying high performance buildings. Residential credits: LEED/NGBS Silver = 40% (max $1,000); LEED/NGBS Gold = 60% (max $2,000); LEED Platinum/NGBS Emerald = 80% (max $3,000). Commercial credits: Silver = 40% (max $20,000); Gold = 60% (max $40,000); Platinum/Emerald = 80% (max $60,000). Credit applies for five consecutive taxable years beginning the year of approval.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: On or before June 1 immediately before the taxable year for which the tax credit is first sought
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of high performance residential or commercial buildings in Anne Arundel County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of Anne Arundel County real property tax liability on the building (not land) for qualifying high performance buildings.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Property must be located in Anne Arundel County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Building must meet or exceed Silver rating in LEED Green Building Rating System or ICC 700 National Green Building Standard (NGBS)
Must include copy of LEED/NGBS rating certificate with application
Must include LEED workbook or NGBS signature page from verification report
Building and systems must be regularly maintained to comply with the applicable standard
Application must be filed on or before June 1 immediately before the taxable year for which the credit is first sought
Cannot be combined with other optional property tax credits
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and submit the appropriate High Performance Building Property Tax Credit Application (Residential or Commercial) to the Anne Arundel County Office of Finance by June 1 before the taxable year for which the credit is first sought.

structured_extraction.program_description: Anne Arundel County's Historic Preservation Tax Credit Program helps property owners offset the cost of rehabilitating historic landmark buildings in the county. Property owners can receive a county real property tax credit of 25% of qualified rehabilitation expenses (or 5% for new compatible construction in a Landmark Historic District), up to a maximum of $50,000 claimed over five years. The program establishes eligibility criteria, an application procedure, and a method for calculating the credit amount, with provisions for termination under certain circumstances. The program is available to owners of properties designated as County Historic Landmarks or contributing resources within a Landmark Historic District.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A county real property tax credit equal to 25% of qualified rehabilitation expenses for historic residential or income-producing properties, or 5% for new compatible construction within a Landmark Historic District. The total credit is capped at $50,000 and may be spread over up to five tax years. The credit is applied to county real property taxes only and cannot be combined with certain other local property tax credits under Title 9 of the State Code. Unused credit may be carried forward for up to five years.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Part 3 due March 1; Part 4 (Tax Credit Application) due April 1 immediately before the taxable year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners of historic landmark buildings or contributing resources within Landmark Historic Districts in Anne Arundel County who are undertaking qualifying rehabilitation or compatible new construction work.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Qualifying interior and exterior preservation, restoration, and rehabilitation work on historic landmark structures that meets the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation, including in-kind repairs and replacements of original features, structural repairs, roof work, chimney repairs, life-safety and ADA-required improvements, plumbing, electrical, and mechanical work to meet code, reversing modern treatments to restore historic character, and architectural/engineering/archaeological fees. Ineligible work includes remodeling, modernization, replacing historic features with modern materials, appliances, landscaping, tool purchases, non-residential outbuildings, décor, and permit fees.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only in Anne Arundel County, Maryland. The property must meet criteria to be designated a County Historic Landmark or be a contributing resource within a Landmark Historic District. Properties must be listed on Anne Arundel County's Inventory of Historic Properties.
requirements_list: The historic resource must meet the criteria for designation as a County Historic Landmark (age, historic significance, integrity, and historic association)
Structure must be at least 65 years old
Structure must have high significance in history, architecture, archeology, engineering, and/or culture
Structure must retain integrity in location, design, setting, materials, workmanship, feeling, and association

Property must meet at least one criterion: National Register listing/eligibility, significant historical events, association with significant persons, distinctive design/construction characteristics, or information potential
Property must be a 'landmark' historic property or contribute to a Historic District
All rehabilitation work must comply with the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for the Treatment of Historic Properties
A historic preservation easement must be conveyed to and recorded with the County prior to Part 3 approval
Certificate of Eligibility (Part 1) and Certification of Proposed Work (Part 2) must be approved before rehabilitation work begins
Expenses must be qualified rehabilitation expenses
The tax credit cannot be combined with certain other local property tax credits under Title 9 of the State Code
Applicants must provide detailed work descriptions, existing condition information, proposed colors/materials/dimensions
Color photos required: principal facade, proposed work areas, environmental setting/viewsheds/streetscape
Sketch site plan required
Architectural or shop drawings required as needed
Owner authorization and certification required
Modified scope of work must be approved by Cultural Resources Division
Itemized records and proof of payment required for Part 3
All applicable permits must be completed
Annual Part 4 application required by April 1 to receive credit each year
Property owner must maintain buildings in same or better structural condition
Property owner must obtain Cultural Resources Section approval before any permitted construction work
Property owner must allow County inspection on reasonable notice
Property owner must notify County within 14 days of damage/destruction
Property owner must maintain insurance satisfactory to County naming County as additional insured
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The process has four parts: (1) Submit a Part 1 Certificate of Eligibility form to confirm the property qualifies as a County Landmark — OPZ responds within 30 days. (2) Hold a pre-submittal meeting with Cultural Resources staff, then submit a Part 2 Certification of Proposed Work form with supporting materials including photos, site plan, and architectural drawings — OPZ responds within 30 days; do not begin work until approved. Any modifications to approved scope require a Part 2 Addendum. (3) After completing approved work, submit a Part 3 Certification of Completed Work with itemized expenses and proof of payment by March 1 before the taxable year — execute and record the historic preservation easement. (4) Submit the Part 4 Tax Credit Application to the Office of Finance by April 1 before the taxable year; Office of Planning and Zoning certifies eligibility and Office of Finance approves/disapproves the credit. Years 2–5 require annual renewal applications by April 1. Hard copies may be mailed or digital copies emailed to the Cultural Resources Division. See also the enabling ordinance (Bill 118-15) for full legislative details.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program to help hotels, motels, inns, and bed-and-breakfast establishments in Anne Arundel County that experienced revenue losses due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Funds cannot be used for equipment and soft goods, infrastructure improvements, or technology upgrades. Grants are disbursed via ACH deposit.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Normal operating costs (rent, payroll, job training, taxes, debt service) or COVID-19 related costs (PPE, sanitization services). Cannot be used for equipment, soft goods, infrastructure improvements, or technology upgrades.

Short-term residential rentals do not qualify

Must submit a completed and signed W-9 form
Must upload a voided company check for ACH deposit

structured_extraction.program_description: Multiple housing options for older adults and individuals with disabilities in Anne Arundel County, Maryland, including subsidized apartments, congregate housing, apartments for older adults, 55+ retirement communities, and continuing care retirement communities (CCRCs).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Staff provide a referral list of independent and subsidized housing options for older adults, including properties managed by the Housing Commission of Anne Arundel County, the City of Annapolis Housing Authority, subsidized apartments, congregate housing, retirement communities, and continuing care retirement communities. Renters typically pay 30-40% of adjusted income toward rent and utilities. Congregate housing includes meals, housekeeping, personal care, and monitoring. Senior apartments offer multipurpose rooms, dining, activities, and lounges. CCRC options range from independent housing to assisted living and nursing home care.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Finding and securing appropriate housing, including subsidized and independent living options such as congregate housing, senior apartments, 55+ retirement communities, and continuing care retirement communities.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Department of Aging and Disabilities by phone or email to request the housing options list or get information and assistance.

structured_extraction.program_description: A business accelerator program designed to support the growth and success of small, minority-owned, woman-owned, and veteran-owned businesses in Anne Arundel County. The program provides tools, resources, and one-on-one assistance to help business owners succeed and grow, including business education through a multi-week virtual entrepreneurship cohort (formats have included six-week, seven-week, and eight-week online cohorts), mentorship, and expert consultations with legal, HR, and accounting professionals. Participants must complete all sessions, assignments, and required meetings to receive an operating grant for working capital upon cohort completion. Additional funding opportunities include the VOLT loan fund and VOLT Microloan Fund (low-interest loans from $25,000 to $500,000) and a Workforce Training Reimbursement grant covering 50% of employee training costs up to $1,000. Each cohort is limited to 10–13 participants. The program is offered in English and Spanish, with three cohorts planned for 2025, one of which may be offered in Spanish based on demand. Businesses must have been operating for at least two years and have employees to be eligible.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants who complete all sessions, assignments, and required meetings receive an operating grant (approximately $5,000) usable for working capital. They also receive complimentary consultations with legal, HR, and accounting experts and one-on-one business assistance. Graduates may apply for additional funding through the VOLT Fund or VOLT Microloan Fund (loans from $25,000 to $500,000) and a Workforce Training Reimbursement grant covering 50% of employee training costs up to $1,000. The program is offered in English and Spanish.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small, minority-owned, woman-owned, and veteran-owned businesses in Anne Arundel County that have been in operation for at least two years and have employees, including early-stage entrepreneurs and Spanish-speaking business owners. Applicants with a business in a commercial space are preferred.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Working capital (operating grant); employee training costs (workforce training reimbursement); general business expenses (VOLT loan/microloan); business growth and development; expert consultations in legal, HR, and accounting at no cost.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Business must be located in Anne Arundel County, Maryland. Applicants with a business in a commercial space are preferred.

Business must be located in Anne Arundel County
Business must have been operating for at least two years
Business must have employees
Must complete an application and participate in an interview
Applicants with commercial space are preferred
Each cohort is limited to 10–13 participants
Must complete all sessions, assignments, and required meetings to receive the operating grant
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the Inclusive Ventures Program page on the AAEDC website (https://www.aaedc.org/inclusive-ventures-program/) or contact the IVP Manager to request the application. Applicants must complete the application and participate in an interview to be considered for admission. Three cohorts are planned for 2025, with one potentially offered in Spanish based on demand.

structured_extraction.program_description: Recreational and legal library services offered at JRDC/ORCC (Anne Arundel County detention facilities). Includes a recreational library with various book types (mysteries, westerns, romance, biographies, etc.), a legal library for inmate research with photocopy services, and access to typewriters and computers for legal documents and correspondence.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Access to recreational library resources, legal research materials, photocopies, typewriters, and computers for legal documents and correspondence.

Legal library access on request-only basis
Fee charged for photocopies exceeding 10 pages per request

structured_extraction.program_description: Work Release allows sentenced inmates at Anne Arundel County Department of Detention Facilities to maintain regular employment while serving their sentence. Participants can pay family support, fines, court costs, taxes, and restitution from their earnings. Sentences are reduced one day for every day of successful participation. The program also offers qualifying inmates the opportunity to hold various jobs, providing extra diminution of confinement credits and other rewards. Pretrial inmates at minimum custody may also participate, earning additional 5 days per month and receiving a letter for court stating work service.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants are allowed to work outside the facility while serving their sentence. They receive job readiness and placement assistance if unemployed. A Case Manager monitors work schedules, communicates with employers, develops a fee collection agreement, and conducts counseling sessions. Sentenced inmates earn one day off their sentence for every day of successful participation. Pretrial inmates earn an additional 5 days per month and receive a letter for court stating work service. A daily fee of $15 per day worked is charged; court-ordered obligations such as fines and restitution are deducted from pay.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Sentenced inmates (priority) and pretrial inmates at minimum custody at Anne Arundel County Department of Detention Facilities who meet medical clearance and other eligibility criteria.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Maintaining employment while incarcerated; paying family support, fines, court costs, taxes, and restitution; earning diminution of confinement credits.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to inmates held at Anne Arundel County Department of Detention Facilities (JRDC, ORCC).
requirements_list: Current offense is not Escape
No escape from Work Release, House Arrest, or Weekender status in the past 3 years
Not precluded by the courts
No detainers
No pretrial commitments
No pending charge or current commitment for designated offenses
Minimum security rating
No pending 8-505 or 8-507 evaluations
Negative baseline urinalysis at intake
Approval of State's Attorney and Victim Advocate when Victim Notification request is filed
Medical clearance required
Not on probation for designated crimes if violation is pending
Custody level consideration required
Sentenced inmates receive priority consideration; medium custody with short sentences eligible for internal jobs; maximum custody eligible after custody decrease
Pretrial inmates must be minimum custody, not on segregation, and typically must be in custody for 2+ weeks
No infractions (removal/ineligibility if infractions occur)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Upon intake, eligible inmates are screened and assigned to jobs based on custody level and commitment status. Sentenced inmates are placed on active Work Release status if approved. Pretrial inmates are typically hired after 2 weeks in custody. Inmates receive comprehensive orientation including a review of Program Rules. Employment information is verified by phone or fax. Job assistance is provided to unemployed participants.

structured_extraction.program_name: Juvenile Justice Therapeutic Crisis Intervention Project
structured_extraction.program_description: A counseling and intervention program for Anne Arundel County students at risk of school suspension or involvement with the juvenile justice system. It delivers therapeutic services in school and community settings to keep youth in school, reduce suspensions and juvenile detentions, and decrease juvenile crime.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A Licensed Certified Clinical Social Worker provides therapeutic interventions using evidence-based approaches including DBT (Dialectical Behavior Therapy), CBT (Cognitive Behavioral Therapy), Motivational Interviewing, and Problem-Solving Therapy. Services are delivered in school and community settings. Parents may self-refer their child. The program is funded through the Edward J. Byrne Memorial Justice Assistance Grant (BJAG) Program via Maryland's Governor's Office of Crime Control and Policy (State Fiscal Year 2026).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Anne Arundel County students at risk of suspension, expulsion, or juvenile justice involvement, and their parents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Therapeutic counseling and crisis intervention services for at-risk youth to improve school attendance, self-regulation, interpersonal skills, and emotional well-being.

Student must be at risk of suspension, expulsion, or juvenile justice involvement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Referrals can be made through the online referral form on the program page, or by contacting Maxine Smith directly by phone or email. Parents may also self-refer their child.

structured_extraction.program_description: Anne Arundel County's Department of Public Works offers a Leak Adjustment (also referred to as the Leak Adjustment Policy) to help property owners and utility customers who receive unusually high utility bills caused by plumbing leaks on their side of the water meter. The adjustment reduces, but does not eliminate, excess water consumption charges on the utility (water/wastewater) bill resulting from an on-property leak. It is a courtesy benefit available no more than once every five years per customer.

The adjustment reduces but does not eliminate the excess charges associated with the qualifying leak. It is a courtesy benefit and may not be granted more than once every five years per customer.

structured_extraction.program_name: Legal Assistance (Referral Assistance for Legal Counseling, Advice, and Representation)

Persons with issues not handled by the Law Project are referred to other free or low-cost legal resources.

structured_extraction.program_description: Free, evidence-based workshops that help older adults and people with chronic conditions manage their own health. Topics include self-management of chronic conditions such as diabetes, high blood pressure, heart disease, chronic pain, and arthritis; falls prevention; healthy eating; exercise and fitness; stress management; and caregiver support. Workshops are offered in-person at Senior Activity Centers throughout Anne Arundel County and virtually online via platforms such as Zoom and mdlivingwell.org/hub.

Programs are available both in-person at Senior Activity Centers and virtually online. Individual workshops range from 6 to 16 weeks depending on the program, and are delivered using evidence-based curriculum.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participation in free educational workshops on chronic disease self-management, falls prevention, physical activity, healthy eating, stress management, and caregiver skills.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register for free virtual workshops at mdlivingwell.org/hub. In-person sessions are held at various Senior Activity Centers around Anne Arundel County.
