structured_extraction.program_name: National Family Caregiver Support Program (NFCSP) – Anne Arundel County Caregiver Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants and support services to family members and informal caregivers who care for older adults or individuals with disabilities at home in Anne Arundel County. The program recognizes the demands of caregiving and offers financial grants to eligible caregivers for respite (temporary relief) care and supplies or devices that make caregiving easier. Grant awards are based on availability of funds. The program also provides information, resource referrals, support groups, educational workshops, a quarterly newsletter, and an annual caregiver appreciation event. Recipients must submit a W-9 form and a Funds Acknowledgement form before payment is processed; payment is issued approximately 4–6 weeks after approval.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are available to eligible caregivers for respite (temporary relief) care and supplies or devices that make caregiving easier. Grant award is based on availability of funds. Recipients must submit a W-9 form and a Funds Acknowledgement form before payment is processed; payment is issued approximately 4–6 weeks after approval. The program also provides information, resource referrals, support groups, educational workshops, a quarterly newsletter, and an annual caregiver appreciation event.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adult family members and informal caregivers age 18 or older caring for older relatives, spouses, older adults age 60 or older, or individuals with Alzheimer's disease or related disorders. Also includes older relatives age 55+ (not parents) caring for grandchildren under 18, and older relatives including parents age 55+ caring for adults ages 18–59 with disabilities. The care recipient must live in Anne Arundel County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Respite (temporary relief) care, supplies or devices that make caregiving easier, and other support services including information, referrals, support groups, and educational workshops.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The care recipient must live in Anne Arundel County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Caregiver must be age 18 or older (or age 55+ for grandparent/older relative caregivers)

Must be caring for an individual aged 60 or older, OR any age with Alzheimer's disease or related disorders, OR a child under 18 (caregiver must be 55+ and not a parent), OR an adult aged 18–59 with a disability (caregiver must be 55+)
Older relatives (not parents) age 55 or older may apply if caring for a child under age 18
Older relatives including parents age 55 or older may apply if caring for an adult ages 18–59 with a disability
Must be caring for an older relative or spouse, or have primary responsibility for raising a grandchild
The person receiving care must live in Anne Arundel County
Must submit a W-9 form and a Funds Acknowledgement form before respite care payment can be processed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: If the person you care for has a case manager through another program, request assistance through that case manager. Otherwise, contact the Family Caregiver Program staff directly by phone at (410) 222-4375 or (410) 222-4339, or by email at caregiver_support@aacounty.org. Once approved, submit a W-9 form and a Funds Acknowledgement form; payment is issued approximately 4–6 weeks after approval.

structured_extraction.program_name: Next Stage Tech Fund (Arundel Defense Tech Toolbox)
structured_extraction.program_description: A financing and business development program administered by Anne Arundel County's AAEDC for small technology and cybersecurity companies supporting national defense, cybersecurity, and related industries. The program provides zero percent interest loans ranging from $50,000 to $250,000 with flexible repayment terms of 1 to 5 years based on the company's cash flow, workforce training reimbursable grants of up to $1,000 per employee, and complimentary consultations with experts in federal contracting, commercial technology marketing, and intellectual property. The program targets small tech businesses located in Anne Arundel County with gross revenues under $5 million and fewer than 100 employees, helping them expand their workforce, scale up operations, or bridge gaps while awaiting payment on federal contracts.
eligible_industries: Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program has three components: (1) Next Stage Tech Fund — zero percent interest loans from $50,000 to $250,000 with flexible repayment terms of 1 to 5 years based on the company's cash flow; eligible uses include leasehold improvements, equipment, working capital, hiring additional staff, expanding operations, and maintaining cash flow while awaiting federal contract payments; all owners with more than 20% stake must sign a personal guaranty; collateral may be required; standard underwriting applies. (2) Workforce training reimbursable grant of up to $1,000 per employee. (3) Complimentary consultations with experts in commercial technology marketing, federal contracting, and intellectual property.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small technology and cybersecurity companies in Anne Arundel County with gross revenues under $5 million and fewer than 100 employees that support national defense, cybersecurity, logistics, technical support, or related industries, including small government contractors and entrepreneurs seeking to expand.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Leasehold improvements, equipment purchases, working capital, hiring additional staff, expanding operations, maintaining cash flow while awaiting federal contract payments, workforce training, and expert guidance on federal contracting, commercial technology marketing, and intellectual property.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must be located in Anne Arundel County, Maryland, or have a signed lease showing intent to relocate into the county.
requirements_list: Gross revenues less than $5 million
Fewer than 100 employees
Located in Anne Arundel County or have a signed lease to move into the county

Must be a technology company supporting national defense (e.g., logistics, cybersecurity, technical support), employ designers/developers/producers of defense-related materials, or provide products/services ancillary to the cyber and defense industry
Financing must help create new full-time jobs within the first year
All owners with more than 20% stake must sign a personal guaranty
Collateral may be required
Startup companies must have a business plan and contracts in place to cover debt service
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online through the AAEDC Submittable portal at www.aaedc.org. Standard underwriting will be used, reviewing repayment capacity, financial strength, industry and management experience, and collateral protection. For more information, contact Sarah Purdum at AAEDC by phone at (410) 222-7410.

structured_extraction.program_name: Non-Profit Economic Development Recovery Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides financial grants to non-profit organizations in Anne Arundel County that serve the community with a mission focused on economic development, economic recovery, health and human services, and housing. The grants help non-profits maintain staffing and operations after being impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic economy.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Individual grant amounts are calculated after the application round closes. The total pool is approximately $1.9 million funded by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development. Grants support workforce costs and operations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations based in Anne Arundel County that serve the community in areas of economic development, economic recovery, health and human services, and housing, and that have been adversely impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic economy.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Staffing (workforce) costs and organizational operations for non-profit organizations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be based in Anne Arundel County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be based in Anne Arundel County
Must have at least one W-2 employee
Must demonstrate mission focus on economic development, economic recovery, health and human services, or housing
Must provide information on the adverse economic impact resulting from the pandemic economy
Must disclose any COVID-19 relief funds already received and the remaining funding gap
Must submit 2019 IRS Form 990
Must submit a completed and signed IRS W-9 form
Must submit a voided organization check or official bank letter confirming routing and account numbers matching the organization name on the Form 990
Priority given to organizations that have not already received a State of Maryland NORI program award in 2020 or other state/federal COVID-19 relief funds
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application online through the program page at www.ArundelBiz.org during the application window (May 10–May 21, 2021). Applicants must include required documents: 2019 IRS Form 990, signed W-9, and voided check or bank letter. Send inquiries by email to the program contact.

structured_extraction.program_name: Nonprofit Center Office and Work Spaces Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Anne Arundel County Nonprofit Center, located at 41 Community Place in Crownsville, offers flexible, below-market office and work spaces to local 501(c)(3) nonprofits. The facility opened for occupancy on May 1, 2025 and provides a collaborative work environment designed to help nonprofits build capacity and fulfill their missions. Space options include private dedicated offices (48–255 sq ft), open-space cubicles, shared offices, shared cubicles, and hot desks. The goal is to support nonprofits that address social determinants of health and improve the well-being of Anne Arundel County residents by providing affordable, collaborative workspace and amenities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Below-market office and workspace rentals ranging from $1.10 to $3.00 per square foot per month. Options range from private dedicated offices (48–255 sq ft) to shared cubicles (35–72 sq ft) and hot desks. Furnished and unfurnished options available. Rates vary by space type. Amenities include utilities, maintenance, Wi-Fi, copy machines, kitchenette, parking, meeting rooms, resource library, wellness room, mailing address, storage, and networking/learning opportunities. Organizations sign a one-year license agreement with the County's Office of Real Estate. Building hours are 7AM–7PM with potential for after-hours access.
structured_extraction.program_audience: 501(c)(3) nonprofits in good standing with the State of Maryland that are located in Anne Arundel County, especially those serving vulnerable or under-resourced populations and addressing health or social determinants of health. Priority given to small, minority-led, veteran-led organizations, and organizations with a connection to the former Crownsville State Hospital.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Office and workspace for administrative operations, virtual service delivery, or in-person service delivery. Space cannot be used for administrative services like payroll, accounting, or legal services provided by the NPC.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Organization must be located in Anne Arundel County, Maryland. Priority given to organizations where 75% or more of clients served are Anne Arundel County residents. Facility is at 41 Community Place in Crownsville, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must have 501(c)(3) status
Must provide IRS Determination Letter
Must be in good standing with the State of Maryland (proof from Maryland Secretary of State and Department of Assessments and Taxation required)
Must be located in Anne Arundel County
Priority given to organizations where 75% or more of clients served are Anne Arundel County residents

Priority given to organizations whose services address local health, wellness, or social determinants of health issues, or that offer training and economic opportunities to low- and very low-income persons
Priority given to small, minority-led, and veteran-led organizations
Priority given to organizations with a connection to the former Crownsville State Hospital
Must provide evidence of insurance upon signing the license agreement (Commercial General Liability, Workers Compensation, Business Auto Liability, and Property Insurance)
Must submit current operating budget, most recent financial statement, most recent IRS Form 990, most recent annual report, and list of Board of Directors
Strategic Plan submission optional
Dedicated space users must use the space at least three days per week; shared space users 1–2 days per week
Must agree to participate in NPC evaluation process
Organizations must follow NPC Facility Regulations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Review information on the webpage and watch the narrated slide presentation. 2. Contact NPC staff at 410-222-6999 to schedule a building tour (must be scheduled at least one week in advance). 3. After the tour, NPC staff provides a link to the Application for Office Space via Google Form. 4. Applications are reviewed by committee within 14 days. 5. Applicants are notified in writing. 6. If approved, NPC staff facilitates the licensing agreement process with Anne Arundel County's Real Estate Office. Signed licensing agreement is due 30–60 days after the decision date.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Anne Arundel County Nonprofit Center offers local 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations free, all-access membership to the Nonprofit Learning Lab (NLL), an online training service. Up to 18 slots are available, covering up to two staff members or volunteers per organization. NLL provides daily live-facilitated training on topics such as fundraising, strategic planning, communications, volunteer management, and board development, along with a resource library, Ask the Expert access, free job board postings, and discounted Grant Station membership. Priority is given to nonprofits with operating budgets under $1 million that address one or more social determinants of health and have not previously received NLL access through the Nonprofit Center. In exchange, members must complete surveys and notify the Nonprofit Center if the service is not being used regularly.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free all-access NLL membership for up to two staff members or volunteers per organization. Only 18 slots are available. Membership includes daily live-facilitated training sessions, a resource library, Ask the Expert access, free job board postings, and discounted Grant Station membership. Members must complete surveys and abide by NLL Terms of Service — membership is not transferable; member discount codes must not be shared; only up to two individuals per organization may access the courses.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Open until all 18 slots are filled
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations in Anne Arundel County, with priority given to organizations with operating budgets under $1 million that address one or more social determinants of health and have not previously received NLL access through the Nonprofit Center.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Professional development and online training for nonprofit staff or volunteers, covering topics such as fundraising, strategic planning, communications, volunteer management, and board development.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Organizations must be located in Anne Arundel County.
requirements_list: Must be a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization located in Anne Arundel County
Priority given to organizations with operating budgets under $1 million
Priority given to organizations that address one or more social determinants of health
Priority given to organizations that have not previously received NLL access through the Nonprofit Center
Must complete surveys as required by the Nonprofit Center
Must notify the Nonprofit Center if the service is not being used regularly
Must abide by NLL Terms of Service — membership is not transferable outside registered members; discount codes must not be shared
Membership covers up to two staff members or volunteers only
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the interest form or application form linked on the program page. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis until all 18 slots are filled. Organizations will be notified of their status within one week of submitting the form.

structured_extraction.program_name: Nonprofit Veterans and Military Service Organizations Exemption from Capital Facility Connection Charges
structured_extraction.program_description: This exemption removes the termination date for nonprofit veterans and military service organizations to be exempt from paying capital facility connection charges for public water and sewer connections in Anne Arundel County. Originally created by Bill 109-15, this bill makes the exemption permanent.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Nonprofit veterans and military service organizations are exempt from paying capital facility connection charges (fees for connecting to public water and sewer infrastructure) in Anne Arundel County. The exemption applies to new structures and has no expiration date, having been made permanent by Bill No. 71-19, effective August 29, 2019.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit veterans and military service organizations in Anne Arundel County seeking to connect to public water or sewer systems.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital facility connection charges waived for eligible structures connected to public water or sewer systems.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a nonprofit organization
Must be a veterans and/or military service organization

structured_extraction.program_description: The Family Protection Initiative (FPI) is a public-private partnership that helps vulnerable residents in Anne Arundel County who face family separation due to immigration or legal issues. It provides grants to nonprofit organizations for legal assistance and crisis support services through a partnership with the Community Foundation of Anne Arundel County (CFAAC). The initiative bridges the gap between due process ideals and the realities local families face when dealing with these threats alone.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: In FY2026, the program received $300,000 in public funding. The Community Foundation of Anne Arundel County (CFAAC) distributes these funds as grants to nonprofit organizations in two areas: legal assistance and crisis support services.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations providing legal assistance or crisis support services to vulnerable Anne Arundel County residents facing family separation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Legal assistance services and crisis support services for vulnerable residents facing family separation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County, Maryland
requirements_list: Applicant must be a nonprofit organization
Must focus on legal assistance or crisis support services
Must serve vulnerable Anne Arundel County residents
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Grants are distributed by the Community Foundation of Anne Arundel County (CFAAC). Contact the Office of Multicultural Affairs for more information. Additional details available at aacounty.org/county-executive/multicultural-affairs/family-protection-initiative.

structured_extraction.program_name: One-Day Class C Special Alcoholic Beverage License
structured_extraction.program_description: Allows non-profit organizations, clubs, associations, societies, and groups of people to hold one-time events where alcoholic beverages are served and/or consumed in Anne Arundel County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A one-day license (Class C Beer/Wine for $25 or Class C Beer/Wine/Liquor for $50) issued to three people attending the event, all over 21 years old. Applications must be submitted at least 10 days before the event. License fees are non-refundable.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: At least 10 days prior to the event
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations, clubs, associations, societies, and groups of people hosting one-time events with alcohol in Anne Arundel County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Permit for serving and/or consuming alcoholic beverages at a one-time event
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County only
requirements_list: Application must be submitted at least 10 days before the event
Three people attending the event must sign the application, all over 21 years old
All three applicants must attend the event
Each applicant must provide a government-issued photo ID (front only)
Upload proof of the event (invitation, e-vite, announcement, ticket, or flyer)
Non-profit organizations must upload proof of nonprofit status including EIN
Upload a contract with property owner, rental agreement, or documentation showing permission to hold the event at the location and date/time
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the online application at least 10 days before the event. The primary applicant submits the application online, then the other two applicants receive an email with a link to complete their portion. Required documents must be uploaded with the application.

structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive strategy to provide legal assistance, information, and referrals for Anne Arundel County renters facing eviction due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The program complements the existing Eviction Prevention Program by connecting residents to legal resources.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Legal assistance, information, and referrals for county renters facing eviction. Complements a separate rental assistance program for income-eligible renters who cannot pay rent due to COVID-related loss of income.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Anne Arundel County renters facing eviction, particularly those affected by COVID-19.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Legal assistance and referrals to help renters avoid eviction.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County residents only.

structured_extraction.program_description: A collaboration with Anne Arundel County Public Schools that helps eligible families access Section 8 housing vouchers. Staff help families assemble and submit voucher applications and then provide ongoing case management to support housing stability and self-sufficiency if the voucher is approved.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Assistance with applying for Section 8 housing vouchers plus case management support if a voucher is approved, helping families obtain housing and build self-sufficiency.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Elma Jones, Acting Family Stability Deputy Director
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families referred by Anne Arundel County Public Schools staff who may be eligible for Section 8 housing vouchers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Section 8 housing voucher application assistance and case management to obtain and maintain stable housing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be referred by Anne Arundel County Public Schools staff
Must be assessed as eligible for Section 8 housing vouchers
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Families are referred by Anne Arundel County Public Schools staff. Call the Resource Line at 1-800-485-0041 to speak to an Intake Coordinator and be assessed for eligibility.

structured_extraction.program_description: Helps Anne Arundel County residents living in neighborhoods near the Chesapeake Bay convert from private septic tanks to the County's public sewer system. The program reduces the cost of connection and aims to improve water quality and public health by converting up to 6,000 private septic systems over 30 years.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance to reduce the costs of converting from private septic systems to the County's public sewer system. The program targets approximately 200 conversions per year over 30 years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Anne Arundel County residents in neighborhoods near the Chesapeake Bay who have private septic systems and are eligible to connect to the County sewer system.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Covering or reducing the costs of converting a private septic system to a public sewer connection.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents in eligible neighborhoods in Anne Arundel County, particularly in densely located subdivisions near the water.
requirements_list: Must be a resident of Anne Arundel County
Property must be located in an eligible neighborhood near the Chesapeake Bay
Property must currently use a private on-site septic system
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the Septic-to-Sewer Connection page at www.ourwaater.com and enter your address into the search bar to determine eligibility. Contact the team by email at info@ourwaater.org or by phone at (410) 222-7500 for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program administered by the Maryland Department of Health and Mental Hygiene, Behavioral Health Administration to support overdose and misuse prevention efforts.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding for overdose and misuse prevention activities. Specific amounts and terms are not stated on this page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Government entities applying for overdose and misuse prevention funding through the Maryland Department of Health and Mental Hygiene, Behavioral Health Administration.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Overdose and misuse prevention activities.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit an application to the Maryland Department of Health and Mental Hygiene, Behavioral Health Administration.

structured_extraction.program_name: Paratransit for Older Adults and Individuals with Disabilities (door-to-door/shared-ride service)
structured_extraction.program_description: Anne Arundel County provides door-to-door shared-ride transportation for older adults and people with disabilities who cannot use regular fixed-route bus service. The program includes two service types: Complementary ADA Paratransit (operates near fixed bus routes) and General Paratransit (available throughout the county for any trip purpose). A subscription service option is also available for recurring trips.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Subsidized shared-ride, origin-to-destination transportation using lift-equipped vehicles or accessible taxis. Service available Monday-Sunday except holidays. Reservations can be made 1 to 7 days in advance; reservation line open 8:00 AM - 4:00 PM Monday-Friday. Vehicles arrive within a 15-minute Ready Window before/after scheduled time. Subscription service available for recurring trips. Donations are accepted by check or money order. An accessible taxi option is also available through the Taxi Voucher program. Temporary approval granted for up to 21 days while application is reviewed; eligibility valid for 3 years with recertification required upon expiration.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Anne Arundel County residents who are age 55 or older (65+ in some eligibility criteria), or age 18 or older with a disability that prevents them from using fixed-route bus service. Also eligible: children 6 years of age and under (with accompanying adult), individuals with temporary disabilities, and visitors with ADA paratransit eligibility from other transit agencies (up to 21 days/year).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Transportation for any trip purpose including shopping, medical appointments, and other destinations within or throughout Anne Arundel County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Anne Arundel County, Maryland. Complementary ADA service is limited to areas within 3/4 mile of existing fixed bus routes; General Paratransit covers the entire county.
requirements_list: Must be a resident of Anne Arundel County
Age 55 or older; OR age 18 or older with a qualifying disability
Disability must prevent use of fixed-route bus service (for General Paratransit)
Acceptable documentation or SSI award letter required for disability verification
Current and valid photo ID (Maryland Driver's License or DMV Identification Card) required
Applicant must complete ALL sections of application and provide emergency contact information
Must demonstrate functional/physical mobility limitations
Must be able to reach curb without assistance or qualify for personal care attendant
Reservations must be made 1 to 7 days in advance for General Paratransit
ADA Complementary service reservations can be made up to the close of business the day before travel and up to 7 days in advance
Must be ready to board within the 30-minute Ready Window
Must cancel unwanted trips to avoid no-show penalties
Eligibility valid for 3 years; recertification required upon expiration
Visitors must provide documentation of ADA eligibility from another transit agency or health condition documentation
Gate codes required for gated communities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Paratransit Application (Mobility Certification form) and submit by mail to Anne Arundel County Office of Transportation, 7060 Aviation Blvd., Glen Burnie, MD 21061, or by email to paratransitapplications@aacounty.org. A Spanish-language application is also available. Temporary approval granted for up to 21 days while application is reviewed; written notification of eligibility determination provided upon completion of review. Contact (410) 222-0022 to confirm service availability for your trip.

structured_extraction.program_name: Partial Deferral of Residential Wastewater System Connection Charges and Assessments
structured_extraction.program_description: Allows partial deferral of payment for residential wastewater connection charges for properties on septic systems being connected to the County's wastewater system through petition projects or County extensions. Enables up to 50% deferral of Capital Facility Connection Charges (CFCC), User Connection Charges (UCC), and front foot assessments. Deferred amounts accrue annual interest at the bond rate established by the Controller.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to 50% of CFCC, UCC, and front foot assessments can be deferred separately or in total. Remaining portion paid according to standard Code provisions. Deferred amounts financed over up to 40 annual installments with annual interest at the bond rate established by the Controller.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Kelly Phillips Kenney, Supervising County Attorney
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of residential properties with existing improvements on septic systems in eligible areas of Anne Arundel County being connected to the County wastewater system
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Defrays costs of connection to County wastewater system extensions through partial deferral of connection charges and assessments
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Eligible areas include critical areas as defined in § 18-1-101, onsite wastewater management problem areas, areas designated in the County's Master Plan for Water Supply and Sewerage Systems as septic-to-sewer conversion areas, and areas adjacent to these within wastewater extension project boundaries
requirements_list: Must be a residential property with existing improvements
Property must be on a septic system being connected to the County's wastewater system

Property must be located in an eligible area: critical areas, onsite wastewater management problem areas, designated septic-to-sewer conversion areas, or adjacent areas within wastewater extension project boundaries
Must meet eligibility criteria as defined in Bill 90-19
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Anne Arundel County Public Works – Utilities for application details.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that lets approved volunteers and fosters take shelter dogs out for a day trip or overnight stay to give them enrichment and real-world experience outside the shelter. Participation helps dogs build confidence and improves their chances of being adopted.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Approved Anne Arundel County residents who are registered fosters or volunteers can take a shelter dog that has been in the shelter for seven days or more out for a day trip or overnight stay. The shelter provides a leash and harness, and can supply bowls, treats, and toys upon request.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Anne Arundel County residents who are approved fosters or volunteers with the Anne Arundel County Animal Services shelter
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Taking shelter dogs on day trips or overnight stays to provide enrichment and behavioral socialization outside the shelter environment
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Anne Arundel County residents only
requirements_list: Must be an Anne Arundel County resident
Must be an approved foster or volunteer with the shelter (submit foster application with copy of ID, current pet information including rabies vaccination records, and home information)
Dogs taken must have been in the shelter for seven days or more
Dogs must remain on leash at all times during the outing
Must only go to dog-friendly locations
Dogs cannot interact with resident pets or other animals
Dogs on stray hold are not eligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: If not already a foster or volunteer, complete a foster application and submit it to foster@aacounty.org or bring it to the shelter in person. The application requires a copy of your ID, current pet vaccination information (including rabies), and home information. Once approved, you will receive the Paws Around Town Handbook and can participate immediately.

structured_extraction.program_description: Anne Arundel County provides a list of financial assistance resources to help property owners who are having trouble paying their property taxes.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance resources to help property owners pay their property taxes.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Anne Arundel County property owners having difficulty paying property taxes.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment of property taxes
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County

structured_extraction.program_name: Pet Food Assistance in Anne Arundel County
structured_extraction.program_description: A directory of organizations in Anne Arundel County that provide free pet food assistance to residents who need help feeding their pets. The page lists local animal welfare organizations and pet food pantries where people can get pet food at no cost.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free pet food provided through a network of local organizations including the SPCA of Anne Arundel County, Senior Dog Sanctuary, Anne Arundel County Animal Services, Happy Tails Pet Pantry, The Pet Food Pantry, Peyton's Promise, Feeding Pets in Need, and Sunshine & Friends Cats & Dog Rescue. Recipients can visit participating locations to receive pet food at no cost.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Anne Arundel County residents who need help affording food for their pets
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Pet food for cats and dogs
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County, Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact one of the listed organizations directly by phone, email, or Facebook, or visit their location to receive pet food assistance. The SPCA of Anne Arundel County can be reached at (410) 268-4388 or at aacspca.org/pet-food-bank. Anne Arundel County Animal Care can be reached at 410-222-3919 or ACCFrontDesk@aacounty.org. The Pet Food Pantry can be reached by calling or texting (410) 858-5846. Sunshine & Friends Cats & Dog Rescue can be reached at 410-796-7327 or info@sunshinesfriends.org.

structured_extraction.program_description: Anne Arundel County Animal Services provides pet food and supplies to pet owners facing financial hardship to help keep pets in their homes. Assistance is funded by donations from county residents and provided as resources allow.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Pet food and supplies are provided to owners in need, as resources allow, funded by donations from county residents.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Anne Arundel County pet owners facing financial hardship who need help affording pet food or supplies to keep their pets in the home.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Pet food and supplies to keep pets in the home.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Anne Arundel County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be facing financial hardship
Must need assistance with pet food or supplies to keep a pet in the home
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Email ACCFrontDesk@aacounty.org or call (410) 222-3919 to request assistance.

structured_extraction.program_description: A defined-benefit pension plan for Anne Arundel County police employees. It provides retirement benefits based on years of service and age. Normal retirement is available at age 50 with at least 5 years of service, or after 20 years of service regardless of age. The plan does not offer early retirement.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Defined-benefit pension payments to eligible retiring county police employees. Benefits are calculated based on years of service and age at retirement. Normal retirement requires age 50 with at least 5 years of service, or 20 years of service regardless of age. No early retirement option is available. Retirement benefit calculations are provided as estimates only, based on currently available information and subject to change at time of retirement.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Anne Arundel County police service employees and retirees
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Retirement income and pension benefit projections for eligible county police personnel
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Anne Arundel County police department employees
requirements_list: Age 50 with at least 5 years of service, OR 20 years of service regardless of age
Must be an Anne Arundel County police employee
Active Duty Military Credit (with DD214 copy) may apply
Transferred Service may apply
Completed Past Service Purchase may apply
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Retirement System by telephone, letter, or email to request a Benefit Projection form, or download it directly from the county website. Submit the completed form with employee information, retirement date request, and applicable options to the Retirement System for an official benefit estimate.

structured_extraction.program_description: Anne Arundel County utility customers can apply for a reduction in sewer charges for water used to fill a swimming pool or hot tub, as long as that water did not enter the sanitary sewer system.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A credit applied to sewer charges on an Anne Arundel County utility account for water used to fill a swimming pool or hot tub. The applicant must certify that the water did not enter the sanitary sewer system. Applications must be submitted within 6 months of filling the pool.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Within 6 months of filling the pool
structured_extraction.program_audience: Anne Arundel County property owners and utility customers with swimming pools or hot tubs
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Credit applied toward sewer charges on a utility account for water used to fill a swimming pool or hot tub
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to utility account holders in Anne Arundel County
requirements_list: Must be an Anne Arundel County utility account customer
Must certify that the water used to fill the pool or hot tub did not enter the sanitary sewer system
Must complete and submit the Pool Verification Form
New in-ground and above-ground pools over 24" require a building permit
Cannot receive both excess sewer use credit (for lawn watering/outdoor water use) and pool credit in the same quarter
Form must be submitted within 6 months of pool filling date

The form is available in English or Spanish.

structured_extraction.program_description: Pool Rewards encourages commuters who currently drive alone to start or join a vanpool. Newly formed van or car pools can receive a monthly subsidy to help offset commuting costs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $200 per month subsidy for newly formed van or car pools registered with Commuter Connections.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Commuters who currently drive alone and want to start or join a vanpool or carpool in the Washington Metropolitan region.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Monthly subsidy to offset vanpool or carpool commuting costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Origin must be in Maryland, West Virginia, Pennsylvania, New Jersey, or the District of Columbia, with a destination in the Washington 8-hour Ozone Non-Attainment area as defined by the EPA.
requirements_list: Must have an origin in Maryland, West Virginia, Pennsylvania, New Jersey, or the District of Columbia and a destination in the Washington 8-hour Ozone Non-Attainment area
Must be a newly-forming vanpool (not previously in operation within 30 days prior to application submission)
Must be registered with Commuter Connections
Must have a 7 to 15 passenger capacity including the driver
Must submit an application through a qualified vanpool provider: VPSI Inc. or Enterprise Rideshare
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application through one of the qualified vanpool providers (VPSI Inc. or Enterprise Rideshare) and register with Commuter Connections at CommuterConnections.org.

structured_extraction.program_description: The PAVE program helps increase wealth in minority-owned, women-owned, veteran-owned, and small business communities by connecting them with government contracting opportunities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides access to government contracting opportunities for minority-owned, women-owned, veteran-owned, and small businesses.

The program provides curriculum and expert-led training to help participants grow their businesses and create jobs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free entrepreneurship training program with expert-led curriculum for Veterans who want to start or expand a small business.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Veterans (Active Duty, Guard/Reserve Personnel, and Veterans) who want to start or grow a small business
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business startup or expansion training
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout Maryland
