structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary public campaign financing program established by Anne Arundel County in 2023 for the 2026 election cycle. Provides matching public funds to qualified candidates running for County Executive and County Council in Anne Arundel County, Maryland. Funded by County appropriations, unspent campaign funds from participants, returned contributions, interest earned, and voluntary donations. FY 2025 budget appropriation: $1 million.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Certified candidates receive matching public funds from the Public Campaign Financing Fund. For County Executive: $6 per dollar on the first $50 of each qualifying contribution, $4 per dollar on the second $50, and $2 per dollar on the third $50, up to a maximum of $750,000 per election cycle. For County Council: $4 per dollar on the first $50, $3 per dollar on the second $50, and $2 per dollar on the third $50, up to a maximum of $125,000 per election cycle. Qualifying contributions must be between $5 and $250 from county residents. Committees can request publicly matched funding on optional reports filed on the first and third Tuesday of each month after the distribution period is set by the State Board of Elections.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Notice of Intent must be filed on or before April 15 of the year of the election; qualifying period runs from January 1 following the last election through 45 days before the primary election; application for certification must be submitted at least 45 days before the primary election
structured_extraction.program_audience: Candidates running for Anne Arundel County Executive or County Council who are county residents and willing to follow public financing rules
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Campaign expenditures in accordance with Anne Arundel County Code § 1-12-101 et seq, including expenses incurred for primary or general election campaigns only. Specific allowable and impermissible uses are detailed in Section F of the Summary Guide.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to candidates who are Anne Arundel County residents running for covered county offices (County Executive or County Council); qualifying contributions must be from Anne Arundel County residents
requirements_list: Must be an Anne Arundel County resident running for County Executive or County Council
File a Notice of Intent with the State Board of Elections on or before April 15 of the election year
Establish a publicly funded campaign account before raising contributions
Register the Public Finance Committee via MDCRIS (electronic filing system) prior to April 15
Close or make inactive any existing candidate committee while seeking public funds
For County Executive: collect at least 500 qualifying contributions totaling at least $40,000 from county residents
For County Council: collect at least 75 qualifying contributions totaling at least $50 from county residents (aggregate at least $7,500)
May not accept contributions from organizations, PACs, corporations, labor organizations, or party committees
Qualifying contributions must be between $5 and $250 from county residents
Submit receipts for each qualifying contribution to the State Board of Elections
Contributions must be from personal funds, not reimbursed, and not loans
All campaign material must include an authority line with treasurer name and campaign finance entity name
Must retain copies of campaign materials for one year after the general election
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Candidates review the Summary Guide, file a Notice of Intent with the State Board of Elections by April 15, register their public finance committee via MDCRIS, open a publicly funded campaign account, collect the required number and dollar amount of qualifying contributions during the qualifying period (January 1 following the last election through 45 days before the primary election), then submit an application for certification (including a campaign finance report, declaration, and receipts) to the State Board of Elections. Once certified, the County Controller disburses matching public funds during the disbursement period. Committees may request publicly matched funding by filing optional reports on the first and third Tuesday of each month after the distribution period begins.

structured_extraction.program_name: Public Safety Officer Real Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A real property tax credit on Anne Arundel County real property taxes for eligible public safety officers (full-time employees, retired employees, and volunteer or retired volunteer members) who own and occupy a dwelling as their principal residence in Anne Arundel County. The credit equals the lesser of $3,500 or total County taxes due on the dwelling per taxable year (for taxable years beginning July 1, 2025 or later; $3,000 for taxable year beginning July 1, 2024). The governing ordinance (Bill 81-17) establishes eligibility criteria, how the credit is calculated, its duration, application deadlines and forms, an administrative fee, and conditions under which the credit ends. Bill 86-21 extended the duration from 5 to 10 years. Bill 91-23, passed in January 2024, further expands eligibility to retired public safety officers, updates the definition of 'Public Safety Officer,' and increases the maximum credit amount. Bill 96-25 extends the maximum duration from 10 to 25 taxable years.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A real property tax credit applied to the County property tax bill of eligible public safety officers (including active full-time, retired, and volunteer officers) who own and occupy a dwelling as their principal residence in Anne Arundel County. Credit amount equals the lesser of $3,500 or total County taxes due on the dwelling per taxable year (for taxable years beginning July 1, 2025 or later; $3,000 for the taxable year beginning July 1, 2024). Under Bill 96-25, the credit is available for up to 25 taxable years (1 initial year, renewable upon application for up to 24 additional years). Separate applications are available for full-time, retired, and volunteer officers.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: On or before April 1, 2026 to be considered for the taxable year beginning July 1, 2026 and ending June 30, 2027; applications filed after April 1 are treated as applications for the following taxable year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Active full-time employees (firefighters, emergency medical technicians, detention officers, police officers, deputy sheriffs), retired public safety officers, and volunteer or retired volunteer members of Anne Arundel County volunteer fire companies or the Anne Arundel Alarmers Association who own and occupy a dwelling as their principal residence in Anne Arundel County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of Anne Arundel County real property tax liability on a principal residence dwelling for eligible public safety officers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicant must own and occupy property as their principal residence in Anne Arundel County, Maryland. Dwelling must be located in Anne Arundel County.
requirements_list: Must be a public safety officer (firefighter, EMT, detention officer, police officer, or deputy sheriff) employed full-time by or retired from Anne Arundel County, or a volunteer member of an Anne Arundel County volunteer fire company or the Anne Arundel Alarmers Association
Must have completed at least one year of full-time employment with Anne Arundel County
Must own and occupy the property as their principal residence for more than 6 months of the tax year
Must be eligible for the state homeowner tax credit under § 9-105 of the Tax-Property Article
Volunteers must earn at least 50 service points in the preceding calendar year
Must file an application by April 1 of the year before the taxable year for which credit is sought
Must pay an administrative fee
Cannot be combined with other optional property tax credits
Must not have previously received the credit on another Anne Arundel County property during the same period
Maximum credit: $3,000 for taxable year beginning July 1, 2024; $3,500 for taxable years beginning July 1, 2025 or later (not to exceed total County tax due on dwelling)
Credit available for up to 25 taxable years total (per Bill 96-25); must reapply annually
Credit terminates upon no longer meeting eligibility requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and submit the appropriate Public Safety Officer Tax Credit Application (full-time, retired, or volunteer) to the Anne Arundel County Office of Finance by April 1 of the year before the taxable year for which credit is sought. Applications are available at the Finance Department website. An administrative fee is required. The credit must be renewed annually upon application for up to 25 total taxable years.

structured_extraction.program_description: Low-cost rabies vaccinations and microchip implantations for dogs, cats, and ferrets to help Anne Arundel County residents comply with Maryland State Law requiring rabies vaccination for pets four months of age and older. The clinic is held approximately twice per month on specific Thursdays at Anne Arundel County Animal Care & Control (411 Maxwell Frye Road, Millersville, MD 21108) and is available only to Anne Arundel County residents. Each session runs for 3 hours, with times varying by season. The clinic is held outdoors and is weather permitting, and may be canceled.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rabies vaccination at $5.00 per pet and microchip implantation at $20.00 per pet. Payment accepted by cash or check only. Clinics are held approximately twice per month for 3-hour sessions at 411 Maxwell Frye Road, Millersville, MD 21108. The veterinarian leaves promptly at the end time and the line may be concluded early to ensure all individuals in line receive service. Clinics are weather permitting and may be canceled.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Anne Arundel County residents who own dogs, cats, or ferrets four months of age or older needing low-cost rabies vaccinations or microchip implantations
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rabies vaccination and microchip implantation for pets
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only to Anne Arundel County residents
requirements_list: Must be an Anne Arundel County resident
Pets must be 4 months of age or older
Dogs must be on a leash
Cats must be in a carrier
Payment by cash or check only
Clinics are weather permitting and may be canceled
The veterinarian leaves promptly at the end time; the line may be concluded early to ensure all individuals in line receive service
Attendees must wear a mask over mouth and nose to enter the building
Pets under 3 months, pregnant/nursing mothers, quarantined pets, and sick/injured pets should see a veterinarian first
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Attend a scheduled clinic at 411 Maxwell Frye Road, Millersville, MD 21108 during posted hours. Clinics are held on specific Thursdays, approximately twice per month, running for 3-hour sessions with times varying by season. Walk-in during clinic hours — no advance appointment needed. Services are provided on a first-come, first-served basis while the line remains open. Bring cash or check for payment.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program helps formerly incarcerated Anne Arundel County residents and people at risk of becoming justice-involved re-integrate into the community. It connects participants to vocational training (automotive repair, CDL, HVAC, culinary arts), workforce development, GED preparation, mental health counseling, housing and legal assistance, and other support services. The program also serves veterans and their families.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive vocational training in automotive repair, Commercial Driver's License (CDL), HVAC, and culinary arts and hospitality, leading to industry-recognized credentials. Additional support includes anger management, food assistance, health and wellness services, GED preparation, drug and alcohol treatment, mental health counseling, mentoring, veterans services, transportation assistance, legal assistance, housing assistance, life skills coaching, and help obtaining identification documents. The program provides daily transportation to training sites and assists with obtaining required documents such as driver's licenses and social security cards.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Formerly incarcerated Anne Arundel County residents, individuals at risk of becoming justice-involved, and veterans and their families seeking community reintegration support.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Vocational training, workforce development, GED preparation, mental health counseling, housing assistance, legal assistance, transportation, food assistance, and other reintegration services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Anne Arundel County residents.
requirements_list: Must be a formerly incarcerated Anne Arundel County resident, at risk of justice involvement, or a veteran or family member seeking community support
Must complete the Re-Entry & Community Collaboration interest form to apply
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested individuals fill out the Re-Entry & Community Collaboration interest form available on the program's webpage.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Anne Arundel County Department of Detention Facilities Re-Entry Program helps inmates prepare for successful reintegration into the community. Case managers meet with sentenced inmates within 7 days of entry to create an Individual Program Agreement (IPA) that assesses psychosocial, medical, and public safety risks and sets program expectations. As inmates near release, case managers conduct Exit Conferences to review post-release requirements, make community referrals, and identify potential barriers to successful reintegration.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides case management, individual program agreements, exit conferences, community referrals, and connections to outside service providers including parole and probation officers and drug rehabilitation programs. Successful participants may access work details, work release, and house arrest opportunities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Sentenced inmates at the Anne Arundel County Department of Detention Facilities preparing for community reintegration
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Developing life skills, post-release planning, and connecting to community services to reduce recidivism
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to inmates at Anne Arundel County detention facilities
requirements_list: Must be a sentenced inmate at the Anne Arundel County Department of Detention Facilities
Must complete an Individual Program Agreement (IPA) within 7 days of entry
Must meet IPA requirements to progress to additional programming and work details
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: A case manager meets with each sentenced inmate within 7 days of arrival to complete an Individual Program Agreement. Progress is reviewed at regular intervals. As release approaches, an Exit Conference is held to finalize post-release planning.

structured_extraction.program_name: Real Property County Tax Exemption for Community or Civic Associations
structured_extraction.program_description: Tax exemption from Anne Arundel County real estate taxes for properties held by nonprofit community or civic associations that meet specific criteria.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: County real estate tax exemption for properties dedicated to use by community lot owners. The property must be held by a nonprofit community or civic association and dedicated to use of lot owners within the community.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit community or civic associations that own real property in Anne Arundel County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property must be dedicated to use of lot owners within the community; assessments may only cover improvement or maintenance of roads, property, or other community facilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Property must be located in Anne Arundel County only.
requirements_list: Title must be held by a nonprofit community civic association or corporation
Must have 501(c)(3) determination letter or equivalent proof of not-for-profit status
Property must be dedicated by appropriate record plat or deed restrictions to use of lot owners within the community
Use of property must not be contingent on dues or fees except for assessments solely for improvement or maintenance of community roads, property, or facilities
Association must be current with all taxes and fees due to Anne Arundel County
Must submit completed application with supporting documentation
Must meet requirements under §4-2-201(b) of the Anne Arundel County Code
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Real Property County Tax Exemption Community or Civic Association application form with all required sections. Submit with supporting documentation including 501(c)(3) letter, property records, record plat or deed, and a narrative describing use. Mail or email to the Anne Arundel County Office of Finance.

structured_extraction.program_name: Real Property Tax Credit for Day Care Centers (Bill No. 19-26)
structured_extraction.program_description: Establishes a real property tax credit for improvements to property used as licensed child care or day care facilities in Anne Arundel County. Applies to licensed child care centers, day care centers for adults, day care centers for the elderly, family child care homes, and large family child care homes. Credit is against county real property taxes levied on the portion of property containing an area dedicated exclusively for these uses.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual real property tax credit calculated as the lesser of $4,000 or the general county real property tax attributable to the improvement. Credit applies to that portion of real property set aside and dedicated exclusively for licensed day care use (child care, adult day care, or elder day care). Property must be owned and operated by the real property owner. Estimated average credit ranges from $1,937 to $3,100 based on benchmarking.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 1 to receive the credit in the next taxable year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Real property owners operating licensed child care or day care facilities (child care centers, adult day care centers, elder day care centers, family child care homes, or large family child care homes) in Anne Arundel County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of county real property tax liability for areas of property used exclusively as licensed day care or child care facilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County, Maryland only.
requirements_list: Property must have areas set aside and dedicated exclusively for licensed day care use (child care, adult day care, or elder day care).
Facility must be licensed or registered under applicable Maryland statutes (Education Article or Health-General Article).
Property must be owned and operated by the real property owner.
Application must be filed by April 1 to receive the credit in the next taxable year.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: An application must be filed by April 1 to receive the credit in the next taxable year. The bill was introduced on 03/02/2026, amended on 04/06/2026, and had a hearing on 04/20/2026. Final enactment status is not confirmed on this page.

structured_extraction.program_name: Real Property Tax Credit for Disabled Veterans and Their Surviving Spouses
structured_extraction.program_description: A real property tax credit on Anne Arundel County real property taxes for disabled veterans and their surviving spouses who own property in Anne Arundel County. The credit is 50% of county property tax for a service-connected disability rating of 75% or higher, or 25% for a disability rating of 50–74%. The credit applies only to county real property taxes (not state taxes or other assessments) on a dwelling house used as the primary residence. Bill 105-20 establishes eligibility criteria, calculation method, duration, and the filing deadline.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax credit against Anne Arundel County real property taxes on a dwelling house (primary residence). Credit is 50% of county property tax if service-connected disability rating is ≥75%, or 25% if disability rating is 50–74%. For surviving spouses, the credit is calculated based on the disabled veteran's disability rating at time of death. Applied after mandatory property tax credits, supplements, and deferrals. Does not apply to state taxes or other assessments. Applicant must have a federal adjusted gross income not exceeding $100,000 for the immediately preceding taxable year.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: On or before April 1 immediately before the taxable year for which the tax credit is sought (e.g., April 1, 2026 for FY 2027)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Disabled veterans (honorably discharged with a permanent service-connected disability of at least 50%, or a nonpermanent 100% service-connected disability) and surviving spouses of deceased disabled veterans who have not remarried.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of Anne Arundel County real property tax liability on a qualifying primary residence dwelling house.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Property must be located in Anne Arundel County, Maryland and used as the applicant's legal primary residence. Property must not be occupied by more than two families.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a disabled veteran or the surviving spouse of a deceased disabled veteran
Honorable discharge or release under honorable circumstances from active military/naval/air service
Permanent service-connected disability of at least 50% declared by the Veterans Administration, or a nonpermanent service-connected disability of 100%
Disability must result from blindness or other disabling cause reasonably certain to continue for life (for permanent disability)
Disability must not be caused by misconduct
Applicant must own the dwelling house and use it as their primary legal residence
Property must be located in Anne Arundel County and not occupied by more than two families
Federal adjusted gross income not exceeding $100,000 for the immediately preceding taxable year
For surviving spouses: the deceased disabled veteran must have qualified for and received the credit at time of death
Surviving spouse must not have remarried since the veteran's death
Application must be filed on or before April 1 immediately before the taxable year for which credit is sought
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and submit the appropriate Disabled Veterans Property Tax Credit Application (Year 1 for Disabled Veteran, Year 1 for Surviving Spouse, Re-Application for Disabled Veteran, or Re-Application for Surviving Spouse) to the Anne Arundel County Office of Finance by April 1 immediately before the taxable year for which the credit is sought.

structured_extraction.program_name: Real Property Tax Credit for Disabled Veterans, Surviving Spouses, and Retired Veterans (Bill 50-23)
structured_extraction.program_description: Tax credit program that provides real property tax relief to disabled veterans, surviving spouses of disabled veterans, and retired veterans in Anne Arundel County, Maryland. Bill 50-23 amended the duration of this tax credit.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Real property tax credit equal to 15% of county property tax imposed on a dwelling after mandatory credits, supplements, and deferrals are applied. Disabled veterans receive the credit for each taxable year they remain eligible. Surviving spouses receive the credit until remarriage. Retired veterans receive the credit for up to 50 years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Disabled veterans, surviving spouses of disabled veterans, and retired veterans who own and occupy real property as their primary residence in Anne Arundel County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of real property tax liability on the owner's primary residence.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Property must be located in Anne Arundel County, Maryland, and occupied as the owner's primary/principal residence.
requirements_list: Must be a disabled veteran, surviving spouse of a disabled veteran, or retired veteran
Must own and occupy the dwelling as primary residence
Surviving spouse must not have remarried
Property must be located in Anne Arundel County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Not described on this page. Contact the Anne Arundel County Council at (410) 222-1401 for details.

structured_extraction.program_name: Real Property Tax Credit for Veterans (Bill 76-18)
structured_extraction.program_description: A real property tax credit for veterans in Anne Arundel County. The ordinance defines eligibility terms, establishes the credit calculation and duration, sets a filing deadline and application form, and provides for termination of the credit.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A real property tax credit available to qualifying veterans in Anne Arundel County. Specific credit amounts, calculation methods, and duration are established in the ordinance but are not detailed on this page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Veterans who own real property in Anne Arundel County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of real property tax liability for eligible veterans.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to property owners in Anne Arundel County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a veteran meeting eligibility criteria defined in the ordinance
Must own real property in Anne Arundel County
Must file an application by the established deadline
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application form as established by the ordinance. Specific filing instructions are detailed in the bill text.

structured_extraction.program_name: Real Property Tax Payment Deferral (Bill 85-15) (Anne Arundel County)
structured_extraction.program_description: A deferral of Anne Arundel County real property taxes on residential property for eligible homeowners who are age 62 or older, permanently and totally disabled, or meet income eligibility requirements, and have lived in their home for at least 5 consecutive years. Originally proposed as an ordinance (Bill 85-15), this program allows qualifying elderly or disabled homeowners in Anne Arundel County to defer payment of their real property taxes.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Defers Anne Arundel County real property tax payments for eligible homeowners who meet age, disability, and income requirements. Eligible homeowners must be age 62 or older, permanently and totally disabled with qualifying benefits, or found permanently and totally disabled by a County Health Officer or Baltimore City Commissioner of Health, and must have resided in their home for at least 5 consecutive years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners in Anne Arundel County who are age 62 or older, permanently and totally disabled with qualifying federal benefits (Social Security, Railroad Retirement, federal military, or federal retirement system), or found permanently and totally disabled by a County Health Officer or Baltimore City Commissioner of Health, who have lived in their home for at least 5 consecutive years and meet income requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Deferral of Anne Arundel County real property tax payments.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Residential property must be located in Anne Arundel County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be elderly (age 62 or older) or disabled
Must be a homeowner in Anne Arundel County
Owner or at least one owner must have resided in the dwelling for at least 5 consecutive years

Must meet at least one condition: age 62 or older; permanently and totally disabled with qualifying federal benefits (Social Security, Railroad Retirement, federal military, or federal retirement system); or found permanently and totally disabled by a County Health Officer or Baltimore City Commissioner of Health
Must meet income eligibility requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and submit the Real Property Tax Payment Deferral Application to the Anne Arundel County Office of Finance.

structured_extraction.program_description: Anne Arundel County processes refunds of real property tax overpayments, erroneous payments, and credit balances resulting from adjustments such as abatements, homeowner tax credits, or tax exemptions. Property owners can request a refund or the county may proactively notify owners of detected overpayments of $250 or more.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Refunds are issued for overpaid real property taxes or erroneous tax payments made directly or through mortgage company escrow accounts. Credit balances of $250 or more trigger a notification letter from the county. Refunds resulting from assessment appeals may also include interest, provided a completed IRS Form W-9 is submitted. Credit balances not refunded are applied to the next tax bill or transferred to the Maryland Comptroller as unclaimed property.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Anne Arundel County real property owners who have overpaid or erroneously paid real estate taxes, or whose tax bills were adjusted resulting in a credit balance.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Refund of overpaid or erroneously paid real property taxes, including interest in cases of successful assessment appeals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to real property owners in Anne Arundel County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Submit completed refund request form with personal and property information, including the reason and amount of refund requested.
Provide verification of payments made (validated receipts, HUD-1 settlement statement, canceled checks, bank statements, or Form 1098).
Sign declaration under penalties of perjury.
Respond to county notification letters within the requested timeframe and provide required documentation.
For refunds involving interest on appealed assessments, submit a completed and signed IRS Form W-9 along with a W-9 Information Request Form.
W-9 information must match IRS records before any interest refund is processed.
Acknowledge mortgage company payment responsibility and accrual of interest/penalties if payment delayed.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Real Property Tax Refund Request form with property and personal information, specify the refund reason and amount, provide payment verification documentation (validated receipts, HUD-1 settlement statement, canceled checks, bank statements, or Form 1098), sign and date the perjury declaration, and submit to the Office of Finance. The county will review within 7 business days and issue a decision. For proactive county notifications, respond to the mailed letter with required documentation. For assessment appeal refunds, submit a completed W-9 and W-9 Information Request Form to receive any interest refund.

structured_extraction.program_name: Religious Leased Real Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: Tax credit from County real property taxes for property located in commercial zoning districts that is leased, occupied, and used by religious organizations exclusively for public religious worship, educational purposes, or office space to support/maintain these activities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Credit calculated at 100% of total taxable assessment for the portion of property used by the religious organization; cannot exceed taxes for which the organization is contractually liable. Reduces Anne Arundel County real property taxes on the portion of a commercial-zoned property leased, occupied, and used by a religious organization for worship, education, or related office space.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: on or before April 1 (prior to tax year sought)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners leasing to religious organizations; religious organizations using the property for public religious worship, educational purposes, or supporting office space in Anne Arundel County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credit applied to County real property taxes on the leased portion of qualifying commercial property.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Property must be located in a commercial zoning district in Anne Arundel County.
requirements_list: Property must be located in a commercial zoning district in Anne Arundel County
Must be leased to a religious group or organization certified under IRC §501(c)(3) or (d) of the Internal Revenue Code
Religious organization must qualify for exemption under Tax-Property Article §7-204 of Maryland Annotated Code
Religious organization must use the property exclusively for public religious worship, educational purposes, or necessary support office space
Religious organization must be contractually liable for the lease
Property cannot be leased, occupied, or used for profit-making purposes
Credit does not apply if the religious organization no longer occupies the property
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and submit the Religious Leased Real Property Tax Credit Application to the Anne Arundel County Office of Finance on or before April 1 prior to the tax year sought.

structured_extraction.program_name: Residential Rehabilitation Tax Credit and Fee Exemptions
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides a property tax credit and exemptions from grading and building permit fees for certain types of residential rehabilitation in Anne Arundel County.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Offers a real property tax credit calculated based on residential rehabilitation activity, plus exemptions from fees for grading permits and building permits related to residential rehabilitation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners undertaking residential rehabilitation in Anne Arundel County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Residential rehabilitation projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Property must undergo qualifying residential rehabilitation as defined by the ordinance.
Applicant must follow the established application procedure for the tax credit.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the procedure established by the ordinance for the residential rehabilitation tax credit.

structured_extraction.program_description: Residential property owners can finance all or part of their Capital Facility Connection charge for water and/or sewer service by spreading payments over 30 or 40 years at a 4.8289% annual bond rate. The charge covers repayment of bonds used to build public water and wastewater infrastructure such as treatment plants, force mains, and pumping stations. The current charge is $11,340 for both water and sewer connections.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property owners can finance the full $11,340 Capital Facility Connection charge (water or sewer) or make a partial payment and finance the remainder over 30 or 40 annual installments at 4.8289% annual interest. Payments begin in January of the calendar year following agreement execution and are billed annually along with the Front Foot Benefit Assessment. Any remaining balance must be paid in full when the property is transferred (sold). Current agreements are effective July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential property owners in Anne Arundel County who owe a Capital Facility Connection charge for water and/or sewer service
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Financing of the Capital Facility Connection charge ($11,340) for public water or sewer service connections
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residential property owners within Anne Arundel County, Maryland. Bureau of Utility Operations is located at 445 Maxwell Frye Road, MS 4266, Millersville, MD 21108.
requirements_list: Must be a residential property owner with a Capital Facility Connection charge for water and/or sewer service
Tax account number required
Property address and mailing address required
Phone number and email address required
Signed agreement by all property owner(s)
Property owner name and address verified against SDAT records
Any remaining balance must be paid off at time of property title transfer
Payments begin in January of the calendar year following agreement execution
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the applicable installment agreement application form (30-year or 40-year, water or sewer) with property and owner information; select financing option (full charge or partial payment with financed remainder); sign and date the form; submit to the Anne Arundel County Department of Public Works, Bureau of Utility Operations.

structured_extraction.program_description: A relief fund created to provide financial assistance to restaurant workers in Anne Arundel County who suffered economically during the COVID-19 pandemic. The program expands an existing debit card distribution program managed by Anne Arundel County Workforce Development.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Debit card distribution to restaurant workers in financial distress. The County Executive requested $2 million in supplemental funding from the County Council to support this program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Restaurant workers in Anne Arundel County who are experiencing financial hardship due to COVID-19 restrictions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Direct financial assistance via debit cards for restaurant workers in need.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to restaurant workers in Anne Arundel County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a restaurant worker in Anne Arundel County
Must be in financial distress
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 410-222-FOOD to learn about available programs and get help signing up.

structured_extraction.program_name: Restaurant and Food Service Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Anne Arundel Economic Development Corporation (AAEDC) provides grants to restaurants and food service businesses in Anne Arundel County that experienced reduced revenue due to COVID-19 restrictions and loss of consumer confidence. Funded by federal CARES Act money, supplemented by state funding through the Maryland Department of Commerce. The application period was reopened after receiving additional funds from Maryland Commerce.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of $10,000 for catering businesses, bed and breakfast establishments, and dine-in non-drive-through restaurants; $5,000 for food trucks. Total program funding is up to $10 million. Grants are disbursed via ACH deposit.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Application period expected to open in mid November (2020); reopened after receiving additional funds
structured_extraction.program_audience: Food trucks, catering businesses, bed and breakfast establishments, and dine-in non-drive-through restaurants in Anne Arundel County affected by COVID-19.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating expenses such as rent, payroll, and utilities; personal protective equipment; costs to ensure sanitary physical spaces; and implementing online customer engagement and transactions. Cannot be used for expenses covered by other government COVID-19 programs, insurance-covered losses, or capital improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be located in Anne Arundel County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Be located in Anne Arundel County
Have been open and operating prior to March 13, 2020
Be in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
Submit a copy of an active food service license issued by Anne Arundel County Department of Health
Submit a signed W-9 form
Upload a voided company check to facilitate ACH deposit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: AAEDC developed an online portal where businesses can create an account and complete the entire application process. Applications initially opened in mid-November 2020 and were later reopened after receiving additional funds. Inquiries can be directed to grants@aaedc.org.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit on County real property taxes for eligible retired veterans who own and occupy a principal residence in Anne Arundel County. Applicants must be age 65 or older and have retired from military service (including uniformed services, military reserves, or National Guard). The credit is 15% of County property tax imposed on up to $500,000 of assessed dwelling value, applied after mandatory credits, supplements, and deferrals, and is available for up to 50 taxable years. Bill No. 82-24 amended the program by removing the assessed value cap on the principal residence for eligibility purposes and adjusting the credit calculation to apply to a portion of the total assessed value.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 15% credit on Anne Arundel County property tax imposed on up to $500,000 of the assessed value of the principal residence, applied after mandatory property tax credits, supplements, and deferrals. The credit may not be combined with other optional property tax credits. Available for up to 50 taxable years. The previously applicable $800,000 assessed value cap for eligibility has been removed under Bill No. 82-24 (effective January 11, 2025).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: On or before April 1 immediately before the taxable year for which credit is sought; applications received after April 1 are treated as an application for the next succeeding taxable year. Apply on or before April 1, 2026 to be considered for the taxable year beginning July 1, 2026 and ending June 30, 2027.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Retired veterans age 65 or older who are retired members of U.S. uniformed services, military reserves, or National Guard, and who own and occupy a principal residence in Anne Arundel County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of Anne Arundel County real property tax liability on a principal residence (does not apply to State taxes or fees).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Principal residence must be located in Anne Arundel County, Maryland. Applicant must occupy the property as their principal residence for more than six months of the tax year.
requirements_list: Must be age 65 or older prior to the start of the fiscal year
Must be a retired member of U.S. uniformed services, military reserves, or National Guard
Must own the property and use it as principal residence
Must occupy the property for more than six months of the tax year
Dwelling assessed value must be $800,000 or less (note: assessed value cap for eligibility has been removed under Bill No. 82-24, effective January 11, 2025)
Must meet requirements under Maryland Tax-Property Article §9-258(A)(3)(II)
Cannot combine credit with other optional property tax credits permitted under State Code or County code
Must provide valid Maryland government identification with date of birth
Must provide DD Form 214
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and submit the appropriate Retired Veterans Property Tax Credit Application (Year 1 for first-time applicants, or Years 2-50 re-application form for subsequent years) to the Anne Arundel County Office of Finance on or before April 1 immediately before the taxable year for which the credit is sought. Applications received after April 1 will be treated as an application for the next succeeding taxable year. Contact the Office of Finance at taxcredits@aacounty.org or (410) 222-1748 for additional information.

structured_extraction.program_description: Returns an improved public road to private ownership for use as a private road.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program returns an improved public road to private ownership so it can be used as a private road.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners or communities seeking to convert a public road to private ownership.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Converting a public road to private use.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County, Maryland

structured_extraction.program_description: Allows a community to petition Anne Arundel County to accept an established private roadway into the County's road maintenance system. Once accepted, the County takes over ownership and maintenance of the road.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The County assumes ownership of the private roadbed and responsibility for maintenance. Petitioners must deed the right of way and any necessary easements to the County at no cost. All construction must meet County standards before acceptance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners abutting a private roadway in Anne Arundel County who wish to have that road accepted into the County's public road maintenance system.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Transfer of private road ownership and maintenance responsibility to Anne Arundel County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County, Maryland. The road must connect to a State or County owned road.
requirements_list: The roadway must meet all applicable laws, regulations, and the County's Standard Specification and Details for Construction.
All owners of property abutting the private roadway, including both spouses listed on deeds, must sign the petition.
The roadbed owner (if different from abutting property owners) must also sign and agree.
Each abutting property owner must dedicate the road and any necessary rights of way and slope easements to public use by deed without cost to Anne Arundel County.
Petitioners waive claims for damages to improvements within the dedicated right of way.
The road must serve a public convenience — at least five dwellings or commercial units must exist per mile petitioned (1 per 1,056 feet).
The road must connect to a State or County owned road.
The road must not be a private or developer responsibility.
Complete and legible petition information is required.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete a Road Acceptance Petition for each road requested and submit to the Department of Public Works, 2662 Riva Road, 3rd Floor, Annapolis, MD 21401. After the petition is received and validated, within six months petitioners are advised whether the petition is valid. The County then inspects the roadway for compliance with construction standards. If the road fails inspection, petitioners may need to fund improvements. Once all construction is complete and right-of-way is transferred, the County begins the process to accept ownership.

structured_extraction.program_description: A collaborative substance abuse treatment and support program for sentenced inmates at Anne Arundel County detention facilities. The program provides methadone maintenance treatment, substance abuse assessments, counseling, case management, release planning, family support services, and referrals to community resources to help inmates transition successfully back into the community.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Program provides methadone maintenance treatment, daily medication, individual assessments and counseling, release planning, family reunification support, gender-specific support groups, internal program referrals (Narcotics Anonymous, Alcoholics Anonymous, mental health services, education, job training), peer support specialist services, and state care coordination. Post-release case management is available for up to 30-60 days for Anne Arundel County residents requiring substance abuse treatment as a condition of probation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Sentenced inmates at Anne Arundel County detention facilities who have substance abuse issues, particularly those who were on a community methadone program prior to incarceration or who meet eligibility criteria while incarcerated.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Methadone treatment, substance abuse counseling and assessment, case management, release planning, family support, peer support services, referrals to community treatment and resources.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to sentenced inmates at Anne Arundel County detention facilities (Ordnance Road Detention Center and JRDC). Post-release case management available to inmates who reside in Anne Arundel County after release.
requirements_list: Must be a sentenced inmate at an Anne Arundel County detention facility
Must have been on a community methadone treatment program prior to incarceration OR meet eligibility criteria and protocols while incarcerated
Correctional Unit Counselors screen and refer inmates during the intake process (Inmate Program Agreement)
Post-release case management requires residency in Anne Arundel County and substance abuse treatment as a condition of probation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Correctional Unit Counselors screen and refer inmates for Addiction Services during the intake process when developing the Inmate Program Agreement (IPA). The Department of Health Addictions Counselor reviews referrals and determines appropriate services. An addictions counselor then meets individually with each participant to complete an assessment and develop a release plan.

structured_extraction.program_name: Runway to Success Program Powered by Southwest Airlines
structured_extraction.program_description: A travel award program powered by Southwest Airlines, administered by the Anne Arundel Economic Development Corporation (AAEDC), that provides Anne Arundel County small businesses with Southwest Airlines travel certificates to attend out-of-state conferences, meetings, and training workshops to enhance marketing, sales, or workforce development. Ten total travel awards are available, distributed to qualified local businesses, providing up to two travel awards per company. Applicants are notified within two weeks of submitting an application whether they have been approved or if additional information is needed.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Businesses receive up to two Southwest Airlines travel reward certificates per company, to be used for travel to out-of-state conferences, sales meetings, or workforce training events. Ten total travel awards are available, distributed to qualified local businesses through an application process managed by AAEDC. Applicants are notified within two weeks of submitting an application whether they have been approved or if additional information is needed.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: AAEDC plans to award all ten travel awards by the end of 2017
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses in Anne Arundel County with fewer than 100 employees and annual revenue under $10 million.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Travel to out-of-state conferences, sales and marketing meetings, or workforce training events.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to businesses located in Anne Arundel County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Business must be located in Anne Arundel County
Fewer than 100 employees
Annual revenue less than $10 million
Must detail marketing goals, travel plans, and staff assignments in application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Companies apply through AAEDC online, detailing their marketing goals, travel plans, and staff assignments. Approved companies receive travel awards for up to two employees per company. Applicants are notified within two weeks of submitting an application whether they have been approved or if additional information is needed.

structured_extraction.program_description: Safe Stations allows anyone struggling with addiction or substance abuse to walk into any Annapolis or Anne Arundel County police or fire station at any time, day or night, and ask for help. A public safety officer will assess immediate medical needs upon arrival. A Mobile Crisis Response Team (MCRT) will evaluate the person and determine an appropriate treatment path. No arrest is made for voluntarily surrendering drugs or weapons. The Office of the State's Attorney also reviews cases where warrants might block access to treatment, and can recommend release to Crisis Response for non-violent offenders so they can begin recovery before addressing legal issues.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free, walk-in access to addiction and substance abuse medical evaluation and referral to treatment through the Mobile Crisis Response Team (MCRT). Available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week at any Annapolis or Anne Arundel County police or fire station. Non-violent offenders with active warrants may be recommended for release to Crisis Response so they can enter recovery programs before addressing legal matters. No arrest is made for voluntarily surrendering drugs or weapons.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local residents suffering from any form of addiction or substance abuse, including those who may have outstanding arrest warrants, in the City of Annapolis and Anne Arundel County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Access to addiction and substance abuse evaluation, medical assessment, and referral to appropriate treatment services through the Crisis Response Team.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at any police or fire station in the City of Annapolis and Anne Arundel County, Maryland, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
requirements_list: Must be seeking help for addiction or substance abuse
Can visit any Annapolis or Anne Arundel County police or fire station at any time
Must disclose any possession of weapons or drugs upon arrival (items will be taken into custody by law enforcement)
Must be evaluated by the Mobile Crisis Response Team to determine appropriate treatment path
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Go to any Annapolis or Anne Arundel County police or fire station at any time. Ring the doorbell and ask for a Safe Station. A public safety officer will assess whether you need hospital transport or can be seen on-site. If no immediate medical need, the Mobile Crisis Response Team (MCRT) will arrive to evaluate and help identify the best treatment destination.

structured_extraction.program_description: A 6-week group education and skills-training program for family caregivers of people living with dementia. The program helps caregivers understand the course of dementia, develop coping strategies, and learn how to involve their family member in daily activities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free 6-week virtual class running at the same day and time each week. Each session uses instruction, interactive exercises, and home assignments. Covers understanding Alzheimer's and related dementias, self-care strategies, daily activity skills, and identifying family and community support resources.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Family caregivers of persons living with dementia (Alzheimer's disease and related dementias).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training covers understanding dementia, caregiver self-care strategies, skills for supporting daily activities, and identifying care resources.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Maryland; delivered virtually through Anne Arundel County.
requirements_list: Participant must be a caregiver of a person living with dementia.
Must be available every Tuesday from 10:30 AM to 1:00 PM for 6 weeks.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register using the link provided on the page (Constant Contact registration form).

structured_extraction.program_name: School Age Child Care (SACC) - Anne Arundel County
structured_extraction.program_description: A state-licensed child care program operated by Anne Arundel County Department of Recreation and Parks. It provides before-school (AM, starting at 6:30am) and after-school (PM, until 6:00pm) care for school-age children in kindergarten through 5th grade (and up to 8th grade at some locations) at elementary school locations across Anne Arundel County. The program offers structured activities including homework time, outdoor play, crafts, organized games, activity stations, and community service projects. A PM snack is included in the monthly fee. The program runs annually for each school year and is organized by region across the county. A summer care option is also available for children entering 1st-6th grades (SACC) and children ages 3-5 years old (PRE-K).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Licensed before-school care from 6:30am until school starts and after-school care from school dismissal until 6:00pm. A PM snack is included in the monthly fee. Monthly fees are paid in ten equal installments throughout the school year. There is a $25 non-refundable registration fee per child per session. A drop-in fee of $10 per child per day is available for children already registered in AM or PM care. Summer sessions (weekly): $152-$210/session for SACC; $92-$115/session for PRE-K. For the 2025-2026 school year, registration is open with first payment due August 10, 2025. For the 2026-2027 school year, wait list registration opens to the public by region April 7–14, 2026, with first payment due August 10, 2026. Fees for 2026-2027 will be finalized by July 2026. Locations are organized by region: Southern AA County, Central AA County, Crofton/Davidsonville, Pasadena, North & West County, and Western AA County. All programs follow the Anne Arundel County Board of Education school calendar and emergency closings schedule.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Wait list registration for 2026-2027 opens to the public by region April 7–14, 2026; first payment due August 10, 2026. Registration for 2025-2026 is open with first payment due August 10, 2025.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with children who are at least 5 years old by the first day of school and entering kindergarten through 5th grade (or up to 8th grade at some locations) in Anne Arundel County public schools. Also available for children ages 3-5 (PRE-K) and children entering 1st-6th grades for summer care.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Before- and after-school child care, including structured activities, snack, homework time, outdoor play, crafts, organized games, activity stations, and community service projects. Meals (breakfast, lunch, AM snack, PM snack, evening snack) provided through CACFP enrollment. Summer care sessions also available.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at elementary school locations throughout Anne Arundel County, organized by region: Southern AA County, Central AA County, Crofton/Davidsonville, Pasadena, North & West County, and Western AA County. Anne Arundel County residents only.
requirements_list: Child must be at least 5 years old by the first day of school and entering kindergarten through 5th grade (or up to 8th grade at some locations)
Child must be toilet trained and self-sufficient in restroom hygiene

State-mandated required forms for admission must be on file at the site on the child's first day, including: Emergency Form (updated annually), Health Inventory (completed by parent/guardian and physician), Blood Lead Testing Certificate, Immunization Certificate (for Pre-K or school-age children not in regular school location), Acknowledgment of Policies form, Custody Orders (as needed), and medical authorization forms for medications/allergies/asthma/anaphylaxis/seizures/topical products (renewed annually)
Registration is first-come, first-served with minimum and maximum enrollment per center
A $25 non-refundable registration fee per child per session is required at registration
Children with medical conditions, disabilities, or special needs plans must note this on the registration form
Child must be registered in AM or PM care to request drop-in services
All programs follow Anne Arundel County Board of Education school calendar and emergency closings schedule
Emergency Form must be completed annually with all required information, signed and dated
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Create an account at the Child Care Registration Portal, add your child(ren) to the account, select a location and session (AM and/or PM), and complete registration by paying the $25 non-refundable registration fee by credit card online. For the 2026-2027 school year, wait list registration opens to the public by region from April 7–14, 2026. Once a space is offered, submit required state-mandated health and admission forms (including Emergency Form, Health Inventory, Blood Lead Testing Certificate, Immunization Certificate if applicable, and Acknowledgment of Policies form) before the child's first day. First payment is due August 10 of the applicable school year.

structured_extraction.program_description: An intensive case management program for families with school-aged children who are currently experiencing homelessness, including those living in non-traditional settings, shelters, hotels, or doubled up with other families.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Intensive case management services to help homeless families find and maintain stable housing.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Elma Jones, Acting Family Stability Deputy Director
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with school-aged children who are currently experiencing homelessness in Anne Arundel County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Case management to help families experiencing homelessness obtain stable housing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a family with school-aged children
Must be currently experiencing homelessness (including living in a car, tent, shelter, hotel, or doubled up with others)
Must call the Resource Line to be assessed for eligibility
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call the Resource Line at 1-800-485-0041 to speak to an Intake Coordinator and be assessed for eligibility.

structured_extraction.program_description: A senior nutrition program that provided support for older adults with food access. The program is coming to a close, with current enrollees covered through the end of December 2024. A new health-focused nutritional strategy program is being developed as a replacement.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Nutritional support for older adults. Current FY25 enrollees are covered through December 2024. The program is ending and a new program is being developed.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Older adults in Anne Arundel County facing food insecurity
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Food and nutrition support
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County, Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Program is closing. Current FY25 enrollees continue coverage through December 2024. For food assistance, visit the Food Resources web page or call 410-222-4257.

structured_extraction.program_description: SBA grants to help theaters, concert venues, and other live entertainment facilities recover from losses caused by the COVID-19 pandemic shutdown. Grants are based on average monthly gross revenue multiplied by six, up to a maximum of $10 million.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants capped at $10 million, calculated as the average monthly gross revenue for each full month the business was operational, multiplied by six. Businesses that received a PPP loan on or after December 27, 2020 will have their grant reduced by the PPP loan amount.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Live venue operators, promoters, theatrical producers, live performing arts organization operators, museum operators, motion picture theater operators, and talent representatives impacted by COVID-19.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payroll, rent, utility payments, scheduled mortgage and debt payments, personal protective equipment, independent contractor payments, administrative costs, state and local taxes and fees, insurance, and capital expenditures.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available nationwide, including Maryland. About 141 Maryland attractions had received grant awards as of July 2021.
requirements_list: Must have been in operation as of February 29, 2020
Must be a live venue operator or promoter, theatrical producer, live performing arts organization operator, museum operator, motion picture theater operator, or talent representative
Venue or promoter who received a PPP loan on or after December 27, 2020 will have the SVOG reduced by the PPP loan amount
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply directly on the SBA's website. Businesses needing help with the application can contact SCORE or the Maryland Small Business Development Center Network (MDSBDC).

structured_extraction.program_name: Small Business Customer and Employee Protection Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that helps Anne Arundel County and City of Annapolis small businesses cover the cost of personal protective equipment (PPE), sanitation products and services, signage, technology for e-commerce and customer communications, mobile or delivery operations equipment, and compliance training during the COVID-19 pandemic. Funded by $5 million from Anne Arundel County's CARES Act allocation, the program awarded 788 grants averaging approximately $6,370 each, with a maximum of $10,000 per business. The program gives priority to minority-, women-, and veteran-owned businesses and to industries most directly affected by COVID-19 quarantine rules. Grants reimburse eligible purchases made after March 29, 2020.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $10,000 per eligible entity (averaging approximately $6,370 each) funded by $5 million from Anne Arundel County's CARES Act allocation. A total of 788 grants were approved. Grants cover or reimburse costs of PPE for employees, protective shields and dividers, sanitation products and services, digital signage and graphics, technology hardware and software (including wellness scans, virtual meetings, website upgrades, e-commerce, and customer communications tools), delivery vehicles and equipment, and professional consultation or workforce training. Eligible purchases must have been made after March 29, 2020. Applicants must submit invoices as proof of purchase. Past-due bills for ongoing expenses such as rent, utilities, and inventory do not qualify.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit small businesses and non-profits with 50 or fewer employees located in Anne Arundel County or the City of Annapolis, Maryland, with preference given to minority-, women-, and veteran-owned businesses and industries most directly affected by COVID-19 quarantine rules.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: PPE for employees; protective shields and dividers; sanitation products and services; digital signage and graphics; technology for wellness scans, virtual meetings, website upgrades, e-commerce, and customer communications; delivery vehicles and equipment; professional consultation services; and workforce training related to COVID-19 compliance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be located in Anne Arundel County or the City of Annapolis, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a for-profit business or non-profit based in Anne Arundel County or the City of Annapolis
Must have 50 or fewer employees
Must be in good standing with the State of Maryland
Must submit a detailed budget listing all vendors, amounts, and products/services
Must submit financial documents such as business tax returns, Schedule C, profit and loss statement, or Form 990
Eligible purchases must have been made after March 29, 2020
Must submit invoices as proof of purchases
Past-due bills for ongoing expenses such as rent, utilities, and inventory do not qualify
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Create an account on the online application portal on the AAEDC website, complete the application, upload a detailed budget listing all vendors and purchases, and submit required financial documents. Review all criteria and FAQs before applying. Interested businesses can join a notification list by emailing [email protected] to be alerted when the application opens.

structured_extraction.program_name: Small Business Development Center (SBDC) – Business Accelerator Development Program (BDAP) for Construction
structured_extraction.program_description: The Business Accelerator Development Program (BDAP) is a State Highway Administration program administered through the Small Business Development Center (SBDC). It provides expert, tailored, and personalized business consulting, coaching, and guidance specifically for construction-related businesses. Participants can meet with subject matter experts, attend training classes, and access resources such as software procurement support to help grow their business. A dedicated SBDC counselor meets with clients on a monthly basis and is housed at the AAEDC office in Annapolis.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides personalized business consulting, coaching, and guidance tailored to each business. Participants can meet with subject matter experts, attend training classes, and access resources such as software procurement support. A dedicated SBDC counselor meets with clients on a monthly basis to accelerate business growth and competitiveness.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Construction-related small and mid-size businesses in Anne Arundel County, particularly those seeking to accelerate growth and competitiveness.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business consulting, coaching, training classes, software purchases, and guidance to support business growth in the construction industry.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County, Maryland (SBDC counselor housed at AAEDC office in Annapolis)
requirements_list: Business must be construction-related
Must be accepted into the BDAP program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the SBDC counselor at the AAEDC office in Annapolis to inquire about eligibility and acceptance into the BDAP program.

structured_extraction.program_name: Small Business Infrastructure Improvement Pilot Program (SBIIPP)
structured_extraction.program_description: A pilot grant program that helps small businesses, nonprofits, and community and business organizations in Anne Arundel County complete water, sewer, and other infrastructure improvements needed to start or expand business operations. Eligible projects must benefit multiple businesses, not just a single entity. Grant funding is directed toward construction costs only, after applicants complete required steps including obtaining letters of community support and approval from the Anne Arundel County Department of Inspections and Permits. The program is funded by $850,000 in American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) federal stimulus funds.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants funded by $850,000 in American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funds to cover infrastructure improvement construction costs such as water and sewer improvements. Projects must benefit multiple businesses. Applicants must be able to cover soft costs and associated fees during the regulatory approval process. Final funding is contingent on Anne Arundel County Department of Inspections and Permits approval.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses, nonprofits, and community and business organizations in Anne Arundel County that are registered and in good standing with the State of Maryland, seeking to complete water, sewer, or other infrastructure improvements that benefit multiple businesses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction costs for water, sewer, and other infrastructure improvements that benefit multiple businesses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to small businesses, nonprofits, and community and business organizations located in Anne Arundel County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Submit a completed application
Applicant must be a for-profit business, nonprofit entity, or community/business organization
Must be properly registered and in good standing with the State of Maryland
Project must benefit multiple businesses, not just a single entity
Letters from neighboring organizations (e.g. chambers of commerce, business associations, commercial condominium, homeowners or community associations) required to demonstrate community support
Obtain letters of community support
Receive approval from the Anne Arundel County Department of Inspections and Permits
Have architectural documents ready
Complete required inspections before award is finalized
