Project is subject to final approval by Anne Arundel County Department of Inspections and Permits
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Application period opened December 13, 2021 and closed January 28, 2022 at 5:00 pm. Applications were submitted through the AAEDC website at www.aaedc.org. Applicants must submit letters of community support and obtain county inspection and permit approvals. Awards are conditional on completing all pre-approval requirements before funds are disbursed.

structured_extraction.program_description: Anne Arundel County's program that helps small businesses recycle by providing curbside recycling-only collection for businesses that generate a lower volume of recyclable materials.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Curbside recycling-only collection service for small businesses that generate lower volumes of recyclable materials. Businesses must meet program guidelines to enroll.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses in Anne Arundel County that generate lower volumes of recyclable materials
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Curbside recycling collection service
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County businesses only
requirements_list: Business must be located in Anne Arundel County
Business must generate a lower volume of recyclables
Must meet program guidelines prior to enrollment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Recycling Division at 410-222-7951 to discuss collection options and program details. Businesses must meet program guidelines before enrolling.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Anne Arundel County Fire Department, in partnership with the Anne Arundel Fire Safety Foundation, provides free smoke alarms and installs them for residents who cannot afford to purchase one. Visual smoke alarms for people with hearing impairments are also available when state and federal grant funding allows.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free smoke alarms provided and installed by Fire Department personnel. Visual smoke alarms for the hearing impaired are available when state and federal grant funds are available.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Anne Arundel County residents who cannot afford to purchase a smoke alarm or need help installing one, including hearing-impaired residents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Smoke alarm purchase and installation for eligible residents.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Anne Arundel County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Resident must be unable to afford a smoke alarm or need help installing one
Contact the nearest fire station to request assistance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your closest fire station or the Public Education Office by phone or email to request assistance.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state-licensed Pre-K childcare program for children ages 3, 4, and 5 at the South County Recreation Center in Harwood, Maryland. The program runs Monday through Friday on all days that Anne Arundel County Public Schools are open, with part-time (Mon/Wed/Fri) and full-time (Mon-Fri) options, and a summer session available. Activities include educational curriculum, outdoor play, story and craft time, STEM learning, cooking, music, arts & crafts, organized games, and daily rest periods. The Summer 2026 theme is 'Worlds of Wonder.'
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State-licensed Pre-K childcare program providing educational, recreational, and social activities for children ages 3-5. Part-time option (Mon/Wed/Fri, 9am-3pm): $350/month; full-time option (Mon-Fri, 9am-3pm): $460/month for the 2025-2026 school year. A $25 non-refundable registration fee per child per session applies. Drop-in fee: $10 per child per day (must be registered in AM or PM care). Registration is on a first-come, first-served basis with a maximum enrollment per session.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Summer 2026 Early Bird: February 6, 2026 (8am-11:59pm) for current school year families; General Public: February 9, 2026 (8am onward). 2025-2026 School Year rollover registration timeline temporarily on hold; new timeline to be announced.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with children ages 3, 4, and 5 (as of June 22, 2026 for summer session) residing in or near Harwood, Maryland (Anne Arundel County)
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Enrollment in a state-licensed Pre-K program offering educational curriculum, outdoor play, STEM activities, cooking, music, arts & crafts, organized games, AM snack, and daily rest periods.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is located at 4510 Owensville Sudley Road, Harwood, MD 20776 and serves children enrolled in Anne Arundel County.
requirements_list: Child must be ages 3, 4, or 5 (as of June 22, 2026 for summer session)
Child must be toilet trained and self-sufficient in restroom/hygiene
Registration must be completed online, in person, or by mail
All required state-mandated forms for admission must be submitted, including physician-signed Health Inventory
$25 non-refundable registration fee per child per session must be paid before child's first day
Enrollment is first-come, first-served up to center capacity
Payment must be made by specified due dates for child to continue attending
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Create an online account at the Child Care portal (https://www.aacounty.org/departments/recreation-parks/child-care/), add your child and an adult over 18 to the account, complete the registration, pay the $25 non-refundable registration fee, and submit all required forms for admission. Registration can also be done in person or by mail at the Child Care Administrative Office. Note: the online system may periodically be unavailable; contact the office for alternative arrangements.

structured_extraction.program_name: Southern Maryland Agricultural Equity Incentive Matching Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: A joint partnership program designed to incentivize loan requests from Southern Maryland farmers and help them meet certain down-payment (equity) requirements, in order to improve the credit quality of their loan applications.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Matching fund that helps farmers meet down-payment (equity) requirements for loan applications, improving credit quality.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Southern Maryland farmers seeking loans
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Meeting down-payment or equity requirements for loan applications
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Southern Maryland farmers only

structured_extraction.program_name: Southern Maryland Farm Mini Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A program designed to assist new and beginning farmers with small start-up projects, and to help existing farmers diversify or expand a current agriculture project. Projects must be simple in scope and completed within one year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $2,000 per applicant on a one-to-one match basis (the farmer must match the award dollar for dollar). Projects must be completed within one year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: New, beginning, and existing farmers in Southern Maryland looking to start or expand agricultural projects
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Small start-up projects, diversification or expansion of existing agricultural projects
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Southern Maryland farmers only
requirements_list: Projects must be simple in scope
Projects must be completed within one year
One-to-one match by the farmer is required

structured_extraction.program_name: Southern Maryland Revolving Loan Fund for Agricultural & Shellfish Aquaculture Producers
structured_extraction.program_description: A loan program designed exclusively for Southern Maryland agricultural and shellfish aquaculture producers. It provides financing for livestock, shellfish aquaculture, small fruits, hops, and produce safety upgrades.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans ranging from $10,000 to $20,000 for purchasing livestock and enhancing herds and flocks, shellfish aquaculture, small fruit and hops production, or upgrading facilities for Good Agricultural Practices (GAP) compliance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Southern Maryland agricultural and shellfish aquaculture producers
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of livestock, shellfish aquaculture foundation and expansion, small fruit and hops production, produce safety upgrades in line with Good Agricultural Practices (GAP)
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Exclusively for Southern Maryland applicants
requirements_list: Applicant must be located in Southern Maryland

structured_extraction.program_description: Anne Arundel County can create a Special Taxing District to help finance, refinance, or reimburse the cost of public infrastructure improvements — such as roads, sewers, water systems, sidewalks, parks, and transit facilities — that support economic development, quality growth management, or redevelopment within a defined area of the county. The county issues special obligation bonds to fund the improvements, then levies an annual special tax on properties within the district to repay the debt.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The county issues special obligation bonds to cover costs of public infrastructure improvements, issuance costs, interest during and after construction, and a reserve fund. Bonds are repaid through an annual special tax levied on properties within the district. The bonds are not a direct or indirect liability to the county. Outstanding debt must not exceed 33% of appraised property value at bond issuance and must not exceed 10% once development is complete.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property developers and property owners seeking to finance public infrastructure improvements within a defined geographic area of Anne Arundel County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Design, construction, extension, or alteration of public infrastructure including storm drainage, sewers, water systems, roads, bridges, streets, sidewalks, lighting, parking, parks, libraries, schools, transit facilities, solid waste facilities, and other necessary infrastructure.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available within defined geographic areas of Anne Arundel County, Maryland.
requirements_list: At least two-thirds of real property owners in the proposed district (by parcel count and assessed valuation) must request creation of the district.
Proposed public improvements must meet all requirements of the Special Taxing District Act (Sections 21-501 to 21-523 of the Local Government Article, Annotated Code of Maryland).
Proposed infrastructure must further the goals and policies of the County's General Development Plan and other adopted plans.
Proposed private development must be consistent with the County's Comprehensive Zoning Plan and Anne Arundel County zoning and subdivision regulations.
Developer must have a significant investment at risk relative to the bond amount.
Proposed development and business plan must be economically feasible with a high likelihood of success.
Development must be economically viable throughout the term of the bonds.
Outstanding debt must not exceed 33% of appraised property value at bond issuance and must not exceed 10% once development is complete.
Bond issuance must not adversely impact the County's credit rating.
Project must pose no direct or indirect liability to the County; developer and/or district must provide acceptable surety.
All project documents must reflect that the County has no financial liability for present or future improvements.
Applicant must complete the official application form in its entirety.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a completed application (form provided by the Controller's office) for review by the District review committee, which includes the Chief Administrative Officer, Budget Officer, Controller, Planning and Zoning Officer, Director of Public Works, Director of Programming (President/CEO of Economic Development), and County Attorney. The committee conducts due diligence and recommends approval, denial, or revised terms to the County Executive and County Council. The County Council must hold a public hearing with at least 10 days' notice before creating a district.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free entrepreneurship training program specifically for spouses or dependents of Veterans who want to start or grow a small business. It is an offshoot of Project Opportunity and includes a structured curriculum led by experts.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free entrepreneurship training course held on Wednesday evenings at the Anne Arundel Workforce Development Career Center in Linthicum, Maryland. The Fall 2022 class ran from September 14 to November 9, 2022.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Spouses or dependents of Veterans who want to start or grow a small business
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business startup or expansion training
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Classes held at the Anne Arundel Workforce Development Career Center in Linthicum, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a spouse or dependent of a Veteran

structured_extraction.program_name: Spouses of Fallen Law Enforcement Officers and Rescue Workers Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit on County real property taxes for the surviving spouses of fallen law enforcement officers and rescue workers who own and reside in residential property in Anne Arundel County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 100% County real property tax credit applied to a dwelling owned and occupied as primary residence by an eligible surviving spouse of a fallen law enforcement officer or rescue worker. Credit is applied after mandatory property tax credits, supplements, and deferrals; does not apply to state real property taxes or other assessments.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Surviving spouses of fallen law enforcement officers and rescue workers who own and reside in residential property in Anne Arundel County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: County real property tax credit on residential property owned and occupied as primary residence.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Property must be located in Anne Arundel County, Maryland. Fallen officer/worker or surviving spouse must have established Maryland residency within 5 years before death. Applicant must be domiciled in Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be the surviving spouse of a fallen law enforcement officer or rescue worker
Death must have arisen from employment; not result of willful misconduct, abuse of alcohol/drugs, or occupational disease
Fallen officer/worker must meet specific definitions under Maryland state law (Public Safety §1-101(c), Correctional Services §8-201(e), Public Safety §7-101(b), or Public Safety §7-203(a))
Applicant must be current owner and resident of property as primary residence
Dwelling owned at time of death of officer/worker
Maryland state domicile within specified timeframe per § 9-210
Dwelling acquired within specified timeframe per § 9-210
Verification of eligibility required
Credit ceases upon remarriage of surviving spouse
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and submit the Spouses of Fallen Law Enforcement Officers & Rescue Workers Property Tax Credit Application on the form provided by the Anne Arundel County Controller's office, including verification of eligibility. Renewal applications are also available for ongoing eligibility.

structured_extraction.program_description: STAIR matches second-grade students who read below grade level with volunteer tutors. Tutors work with students twice a week to improve reading skills and build self-confidence. Students are selected by school reading specialists and improve an average of 5.3 reading levels by year's end.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Volunteer tutoring provided to second-grade students reading below grade level. Tutors meet with students twice a week for 2.5 hours. Each student who completes the program receives at least 25 books of their own.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Second-grade students in Anne Arundel County Schools who are reading below grade level, the majority of whom are low income.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reading tutoring, literacy improvement, and books for participating students.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County schools, including schools in Severn and the Annapolis area.
requirements_list: Student must be in second grade
Student must be identified by Anne Arundel County Schools as reading below grade level
Students are selected by school reading specialists
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Students are identified and selected by school reading specialists. Volunteers interested in tutoring can visit stairannapolis.org/volunteer/ to learn about opportunities.

structured_extraction.program_name: Stormwater Fee Substantial Financial Hardship Exemption
structured_extraction.program_description: Reduces or waives the Watershed Protection and Restoration Fee (WPRF) — also referred to as the stormwater remediation fee — for Anne Arundel County residential property owners who demonstrate financial hardship. Applicants must meet at least two qualifying conditions related to income, disability benefits, or participation in public assistance programs. The exemption must be applied for each year. Mobile home park tenants are eligible for a 40% reduction in the base rate fee.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reduces or fully waives the annual stormwater remediation fee (WPRF) for qualifying residential property owners. Mobile home park tenants receive a 40% reduction of the base stormwater fee. Applicants must meet at least two of four qualifying conditions: (1) combined gross income at or below federal poverty guidelines; (2) receiving energy assistance subsidy; (3) receiving SSI or SNAP/food stamps; (4) receiving veterans or Social Security disability benefits. Must be applied for each year.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Anne Arundel County Office of Finance - Tax Credits
structured_extraction.program_audience: Anne Arundel County residential property owners experiencing substantial financial hardship; mobile home park tenants with valid leases.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction or waiver of the annual stormwater remediation fee (WPRF).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County, Maryland — property must contain a detached single-family dwelling or dwelling unit in an attached or multifamily residential property.
requirements_list: Property must contain a detached single-family dwelling or dwelling unit in an attached or multifamily residential property
At least one property owner must be an occupant of the property
Must demonstrate substantial financial hardship

Must meet at least two of the following four criteria: (1) combined gross income at or below federal poverty guidelines; (2) receives energy assistance subsidy; (3) receives SSI or SNAP/food stamps; (4) receives veterans or Social Security disability benefits
Mobile home park tenants must have a valid lease/contract and meet the same criteria
Must apply annually
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Stormwater Fee Substantial Financial Hardship Exemption Application with property and income information, and affirm eligibility by checking at least two applicable criteria. Mail the completed application to Anne Arundel County, Office of Finance, Attn: Tax Credits, 44 Calvert Street, Room 110, Annapolis, MD 21401, or email it to taxcredits@aacounty.org.

structured_extraction.program_description: A multi-month cohort training program for nonprofit organizations in Anne Arundel County focused on strategic planning. Participants attend seven sessions (3 in-person, 4 online) held on Wednesdays from 3–5pm, running January through April. The cohort of up to 10 groups share their organizations' strengths, identify common challenges, and work together over approximately three months. Members leave with a draft work plan and are prepared to complete their full strategic planning process on their own timeline. Offered in partnership with the Maryland Association of Nonprofits.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A cohort-based training and technical assistance program spanning approximately three months. Participants attend seven sessions (3 in-person, 4 online) covering strategic planning concepts and practices, with peer learning and facilitated group discussions. Participants leave with a draft work plan and are prepared to complete their full strategic planning process.
structured_extraction.program_audience: 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations in Anne Arundel County, particularly younger organizations that may not yet have a strategic plan.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Strategic planning training, technical assistance, and development of a draft work plan to support capacity building for nonprofit organizations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations located in Anne Arundel County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization
Must be located in Anne Arundel County
Cohort is especially suited for younger organizations without an existing strategic plan
Not all applicants are accepted into the cohort
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted online. Not all applicants are accepted. See the program page for the application link or contact the Nonprofit Center for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Subsidies for Wastewater Extension Project Costs (Bill 95-19)
structured_extraction.program_description: An Anne Arundel County ordinance that allows the Department of Public Works to provide partial subsidies (up to 25% of total project costs) to cover a portion of the costs for wastewater extension projects in specified eligible areas of the county. The program is discretionary and administered by the DPW Director.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Partial cost subsidy for wastewater extension projects, capped at a maximum of 25% of entire project costs. The Director of DPW has discretion in awarding subsidies based on factors including proximity to existing wastewater infrastructure, environmental and health benefits, engineering considerations, fund availability, financial viability, and federal/state aid availability.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners and developers in eligible areas of Anne Arundel County seeking assistance with wastewater extension project costs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Covering a portion (up to 25%) of wastewater extension project costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Four defined eligible area types within Anne Arundel County: (1) critical areas as defined in County code § 18-1-101, (2) onsite wastewater management problem areas, (3) areas designated in the County's Master Plan for Water Supply and Sewerage Systems as septic to sewer conversion areas, and (4) areas adjacent to the above three types within wastewater extension project boundaries.
requirements_list: Project must be a wastewater extension project
Project must be located in one of the four eligible area types within Anne Arundel County
Director considers proximity to existing wastewater infrastructure
Director considers environmental and health benefits
Director considers engineering considerations
Director considers fund availability and financial viability
Director considers availability of federal/state aid
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The Director of DPW has discretionary authority to approve subsidies. Contact the Anne Arundel County Department of Public Works for details on the application process.

structured_extraction.program_description: SAS helps incarcerated individuals at the Ordnance Road Correctional Center gain the motivation to seek community treatment and social support services so they can lead a substance-free, pro-social lifestyle after release. The program includes substance abuse education, relapse prevention groups, individual counseling, release planning, family strengthening services, and post-release case management.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Multi-phase program providing: (1) 8 hours of relapse prevention group sessions through the ADEPT program; (2) individual psycho-social assessment and release planning for inmates on probation for substance abuse; (3) family services including a 12-hour Male/Female Resource Group, a 15-week/50-hour Strengthening Families Program, and Moral Recognition Therapy; and (4) post-release case management for 30–60 days following release to support compliance with treatment-related probation conditions.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Inmates at the Ordnance Road Correctional Center, particularly those with substance abuse conditions of probation who will reside in Anne Arundel County after release.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Substance abuse education, relapse prevention, individual counseling, release planning, family relationship improvement, and post-release case management services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to inmates who will reside in Anne Arundel County after release.
requirements_list: Must be an inmate at Ordnance Road Correctional Center
Must be screened and referred by a correctional case manager during intake
Phase 2 is mandatory for Phase 1 graduates who have probation conditions for substance abuse treatment and will reside in Anne Arundel County after release
Strengthening Families Program requires eligible inmates to have children between ages 6 and 15
Post-release case management requires substance abuse treatment as a condition of probation and residency in Anne Arundel County after release
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Correctional case managers screen and refer inmates for SAS as part of developing their Inmate Program Agreement (IPA) during intake. Health Department Addictions Counselors then schedule referred inmates for the substance abuse education component on a first-come, first-served basis, with priority given to inmates with shorter sentences.

structured_extraction.program_description: STEP offers sentenced inmates at the Ordnance Road Correctional Center (ORCC) and inmates at JRDC educational instruction including GED preparation, Pre-GED, Adult Basic Education, Adult Literacy, and Advanced Life Skills courses. Literacy training is also offered by volunteers at JRDC. The program is run in partnership with Anne Arundel Community College (AACC).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides educational instruction to sentenced inmates including GED preparation, Pre-GED, Adult Basic Education, Adult Literacy, and Advanced Life Skills courses. Literacy training is also offered by volunteers at JRDC. All inmates at ORCC are assessed upon intake using the Test of Adult Basic Education (TABE) and other tools. Based on results, inmates are placed on a Candidate's List for the next session and assigned to the appropriate class. Each enrolled inmate receives an Individual Learning Plan (ILP) developed and monitored by STEP staff. JRDC inmates are referred to the program through their Individual Program Assessments (IPAs).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Sentenced inmates at the Ordnance Road Correctional Center (ORCC) and inmates at JRDC in Anne Arundel County, Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: GED preparation, Pre-GED, Adult Basic Education, Adult Literacy, and Advanced Life Skills instruction; literacy training delivery
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to inmates housed at the Ordnance Road Correctional Center (ORCC) and JRDC in Anne Arundel County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a sentenced inmate at ORCC or an inmate at JRDC
Must be eligible for GED programming
Must complete education assessment (TABE, Maryland Adult Performance Program Competency-Based Assessment, and computer competency interview) as part of intake
JRDC inmates must qualify for progression to ORCC
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: All inmates at ORCC are automatically referred for education assessment during intake. Based on assessment results, inmates are placed on a Candidate's List for the next session. A Class Selection Meeting is held between Education staff and Unit staff to finalize placement. Once placed on the Final Class List and attending classes, an Individual Learning Plan (ILP) is developed. JRDC inmates are referred through their Individual Program Assessments (IPAs).

structured_extraction.program_description: Anne Arundel County Recreation & Parks offers licensed full-day summer child care programs at elementary school locations across the county. The 2026 theme is 'Worlds of Wonder.' School Age Child Care (SACC) serves children entering grades 1–6 and includes arts and crafts, games, STEM, literacy activities, field trips, and on-site enrichments. A Pre-K program is also available for children ages 3–5 at South County Recreation Center. Six one-week sessions are offered throughout summer 2026.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Full-day (7:00am–6:00pm) summer child care for children entering grades 1–6 at 13 elementary school locations. Weekly fees range from $160 to $230 depending on session, with a $25 non-refundable deposit per child per session due at registration. A Pre-K half-day program (9:00am–3:00pm) is available for children ages 3–5 at South County Recreation Center (4510 Owensville Sudley Rd., Harwood, MD) for $500/month with a $25 deposit. Sessions run from June 29 through August 7, 2026. Children participating in Summer Academy may be eligible for a reduced fee.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Priority/Early Bird registration: February 6, 2026 (8am–11:59pm) for current school year families; General public registration: February 9, 2026 at 8am; fees due on rolling schedule through July 10, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with children entering grades 1–6 (SACC) or children ages 3–5 as of June 22, 2026 (Pre-K) residing in Anne Arundel County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Summer child care and enrichment activities including arts and crafts, STEM, literacy, outdoor play, field trips, and on-site visiting enrichments
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Programs are located at 13 elementary schools and recreation centers across Anne Arundel County, Maryland. Pre-K program located at South County Recreation Center, 4510 Owensville Sudley Rd., Harwood, Maryland.
requirements_list: Children in SACC must be entering grades 1–6 for the 2026–2027 school year
Children in Pre-K program must be 3–5 years old as of June 22, 2026
Children must be toilet trained and self-sufficient in restroom care
State-mandated forms (including Health Inventory with physician signature) must be completed and on file before attendance
$25 non-refundable deposit per child per session required at registration
Registration is first-come, first-served subject to minimum and maximum enrollment at each center
Priority registration available February 6, 2026 for current school year families
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Create an account at the Child Care Registration Portal, add your child(ren) to the account, then register for the desired location and session(s). Priority/Early Bird registration opens February 6, 2026 (8am–11:59pm) for current school year families; general public registration opens February 9, 2026 at 8am. Pay the $25 deposit per session at registration, with remaining balances due on the dates listed in the fee schedule. New participants are encouraged to create an account before registration day.

structured_extraction.program_description: A multi-tiered program that connects children, youth, and their families in Anne Arundel County to community resources including mental health services, food, housing, utilities, crisis or emergency services, mentoring, and parent training. An Intake Coordinator serves as a single point of entry, screening callers for eligibility and referring them to appropriate services.

structured_extraction.program_name: Trauma, Addictions, Mental Health and Recovery (TAMAR)
structured_extraction.program_description: The TAMAR Project provides individual and group trauma treatment, mental health assessment, and post-release case management to female inmates at the Ordnance Road Correctional Center (ORCC). It uses trauma-informed treatment combined with motivational counseling to help women break cycles of trauma, depression, and re-offending. The program also includes a 32-hour substance abuse education workshop with open-enrollment substance abuse education and counseling for inmates who abuse drugs or alcohol, and referral to appropriate treatment upon completion of sentence.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides individual and group therapy, mental health assessment, and post-release case management services to eligible female inmates. Also includes a 32-hour substance abuse education workshop with referral to appropriate treatment upon sentence completion. Participation is voluntary. Services are delivered by licensed clinicians. Open enrollment available for JRDC inmates; referral process through IPA for eligible ORCC inmates.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Thomas Laue, Assistant Correctional Facility Administrator, ORCC
structured_extraction.program_audience: Female inmates at the Ordnance Road Correctional Center and qualifying inmates at ORCC and JRDC who are identified as possible victims of abuse or trauma or who abuse drugs or alcohol, including both pretrial and sentenced individuals.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Individual and group therapy, mental health case management, post-release support services, substance abuse education, counseling, and treatment referral services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to inmates housed at the Ordnance Road Correctional Center (ORCC) and JRDC in Anne Arundel County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a female inmate at the Ordnance Road Correctional Center
Must be identified (through initial screening or staff referral) as a possible victim of abuse or trauma
Participation is completely voluntary
Inmate status at ORCC or JRDC
Substance abuse history for substance abuse education component
Qualification criteria for ORCC progression (for JRDC inmates)
May be part of IPA (Individualized Program Assignment)

For substance abuse education, open enrollment is available for JRDC inmates; referral process through IPA for eligible ORCC inmates.

structured_extraction.program_description: A process that allows property owners to register a land use that was not permitted, conditional, or a special exception under the zoning law when it began, but for which no enforcement action was taken within 20 years of the date the use commenced. Approval establishes the legal status of the use going forward.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Applicants apply online through the Land Use Navigator (LUN). The application itself has no fee; however, there is a $35 fee per posted sign required on the property. For properties with frontage on more than one road or on the water, additional signs are required. The Research & GIS Section provides the required signs, and applicants must post them for a minimum of 14 days. Required submission materials include a letter of explanation, an administrative site plan at engineering scale, floor plans, proof of ownership, a list of nearby property owners within 175 feet, evidence of the use's history, and Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation records.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners in Anne Arundel County whose land use has been in operation for at least 20 years without enforcement action, but was not originally permitted under the applicable zoning law.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Registering and obtaining legal status for a non-conforming land use that has existed for at least 20 years without enforcement action.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Anne Arundel County, Maryland.
requirements_list: The use must not have been permitted, conditional, or a special exception use under the zoning law when it commenced
No enforcement action may have been initiated within 20 years of the date the use commenced
Submit a Letter of Explanation describing each use on the property, when it began, its character and extent, and any enforcement actions and outcomes
Provide an administrative site plan drawn at engineering scale no smaller than 1"=40' showing all existing improvements, dimensions, setbacks, heights, and floor areas
Provide floor plans to scale for all structures with notation of use of floor area
Provide proof of ownership (deed copy from mdlandrec.net); include recorded subdivision plat or signed and sealed survey if deed lacks metes and bounds description
Provide a list of names and mailing addresses of all property owners within 175 feet of the subject property lines in all directions including across roads
Provide evidence of the use's history (sales receipts, bills, rental leases, licenses, building permits, certificates of occupancy, or other records; affidavits alone are not sufficient)
Provide records from the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation
Post required sign(s) on the subject property for a minimum of 14 days
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online using the Land Use Navigator (LUN) at the Anne Arundel County portal. Gather and submit required documents including a letter of explanation, site plan, floor plans, proof of ownership, nearby property owner list, historical evidence, and tax records. Post the required sign(s) provided by the Research & GIS Section on the property for at least 14 days. Pay the $35 sign fee (per sign required).

structured_extraction.program_description: The VOLT Disaster Recovery Relief Program (DRRP) is a disaster recovery grant program administered by Anne Arundel County and AAEDC to help nonprofits and small, minority-owned, woman-owned, and Veteran-owned businesses recover from property damage and business interruptions caused by flooding events and natural disasters that trigger a local or statewide state of emergency. The program has supported recovery from the October 29-30, 2021 storm and coastal flooding across Anne Arundel County, as well as the January 9-10, 2024 flooding event affecting businesses within Annapolis City limits. Grants of up to $50,000 are reimbursable and funded through Maryland's Video Lottery Terminal (VOLT/VLT) fund, which is supported by casino slot machine taxes, with $1,000,000 in total funding available. Eligible businesses may use funds for any legitimate business expense, including physical property repairs, equipment replacement, loss of income from closure, damaged inventory replacement, and working capital to resume operations. Recipients must provide receipts, projected sales data, tax returns, a damage statement, a budget, pictures/videos of damage, and a completed W-9 to document losses, and must be available for a site visit to review property and business damages.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursable grants of up to $50,000 per eligible business, funded through Maryland's Video Lottery Terminal (VOLT/VLT) fund (supported by casino slot machine taxes), with $1,000,000 in total funding available, awarded on a rolling basis. Eligible uses include physical property repairs, replacement of equipment, loss of income from business closure, replacement of damaged inventory, working capital to resume operations, and other legitimate business expenses. Recipients must provide receipts, projected sales data, tax returns or Schedule C, a damage statement, a budget, pictures/videos of damage, and a completed W-9 to document losses.

Businesses must qualify as small businesses under SBA size standards.

structured_extraction.program_description: The VOLT Growth Fund (VGF) provides loans to Maryland-based high-growth, innovative technology product companies to help them launch a go-to-market strategy and accelerate sales. It features flexible underwriting standards and payment terms designed to help companies grow revenue and workforce and attract future equity investment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans of up to $100,000 with a term of up to 10 years. No interest or closing costs. A 10% interest recollection amount is due at the time of a recapture event, defined as when the company raises equity investment equal to 5 times the original loan amount or after 5 years, whichever comes first. After the recapture event, the loan is repaid over 5 years in equal monthly principal payments. Collateral is a blanket UCC lien on business assets; personal guaranty required from all active owners with more than 20% ownership.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Implementing a go-to-market strategy and accelerating sales growth.

Must have a strong management team with a proven track record
Product must be created/completed and ready to bring to market
Pre-revenue and minimal revenue companies may apply
Must provide realistic financial projections showing cash flow positive within 12 months
Must provide a business plan or investor deck showing a pathway to growth and profitability
Personal guaranty required from all active owners with more than 20% ownership
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online through AAEDC's Submittable portal at https://aaedc.submittable.com/submit/211934/volt-growth-fund.

structured_extraction.program_description: The VOLT Microloan Fund provides loans of up to $50,000 to small, minority-owned, women-owned, and veteran-owned businesses in Maryland. The fund is designed to help businesses that have graduated from a business accelerator program access working capital and other business financing, especially those facing credit challenges who cannot access traditional financing. Loans can be used for working capital, vehicle purchases, equipment, leasehold improvements, and other business expenses that help increase revenue and profit. The fund is part of Maryland's Small, Minority, and Women-Owned Business (SMWOB) loan fund, which uses 1.5% of proceeds from video lottery terminals to assist businesses in targeted areas near Maryland's six casinos and throughout the state.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans up to $50,000 at a fixed 2.00% interest rate. 5-year term: first year is interest-only payments, followed by 4 years of monthly principal and interest payments. No loan fees or closing costs. Features flexible underwriting standards for businesses facing credit challenges. The fund uses 1.5% of proceeds from video lottery terminals to assist businesses in targeted areas near Maryland's six casinos (within a 10-mile radius) and throughout the state. Note: borrowers in Montgomery, Howard, Prince George's, Baltimore County, and Baltimore City should contact their local fund managers first. Excluded industries include adult entertainment, gambling facilities, gun shops, liquor stores, unlicensed massage parlors, pawn shops, tanning salons, tattoo parlors, and residential/transient living facilities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses with under $500,000 in revenue and fewer than 10 employees that are minority-owned, women-owned, or veteran-owned and have graduated from a business accelerator program (such as IVP), especially those facing credit challenges or unable to access traditional financing.

Borrowers in Montgomery, Howard, Prince George's, Baltimore County, and Baltimore City should contact their local fund managers first.
