structured_extraction.program_name: Watershed Protection and Restoration Fee Appeal, Credit Application, and Stormwater Remediation Fee Credit Agreement
structured_extraction.program_description: Allows property owners in Anne Arundel County to appeal their Watershed Protection and Restoration Fee (WPRF, also known as the stormwater fee) or apply for a credit toward their property's fee. Property owners can reduce their annual fee by up to 50% by proactively implementing stormwater runoff controls on their property. The credit amount depends on how much of the property's impervious surface area is treated and how much rainfall the stormwater practices handle (minimum 1 inch for full credit). Credits are issued initially for a 3-year period and in 3-year intervals thereafter in perpetuity if practices are maintained. Non-residential properties with a full NPDES permit may receive 50% credit. Marina properties can receive up to 50% credit (25% for NPDES permit coverage plus 25% for Clean Marina certification). Partial credits are available when only part of the property is covered. The credit renews automatically each year as long as practices remain in good condition. Grounds for appeal include incorrect residential tier placement, incorrect zoning or property classification, errors in impervious area calculation, unapplied homeowners association fee cap, mathematical or calculation errors, exempt property status, incorrect billing of the payer, property not subject to the charge, or unapplied financial hardship exemption. If an appeal is upheld, the county adjusts the billed fee and mails a refund check; refunds can go back no more than three years, and the county issues a written decision within 45 days of receiving a completed appeal. Credits are available for qualifying stormwater management practices on a property and must be applied for by October 1st of the taxable year to apply that year. For property owners who have installed small-scale stormwater management practices (such as rain gardens, dry wells, permeable pavement, or rain barrels) without a grading permit, a formal WPRF Stormwater Remediation Fee Credit Agreement is required. This agreement establishes maintenance responsibilities and allows County inspection, enabling the property owner to qualify for the WPRF Credit. Full credit requires the practice to treat a minimum of 1 inch of rainfall; partial credit is available for practices that treat less. The credit is contingent on passing a County inspection and maintaining the practice in accordance with County and state stormwater standards. Properties within the City of Annapolis are exempt from the WPRF. A separate property tax credit is also available through County Code § 4-2-316.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property owners can appeal their stormwater fee bill or apply for a credit to reduce their Watershed Protection and Restoration Fee by up to 50% by implementing proactive and sustainable stormwater runoff controls. The credit amount depends on how much of the property's impervious surface area is treated and how much rainfall the stormwater practices handle (minimum 1 inch for full credit). Credits are calculated as: (Treated Impervious ÷ Total Impervious) × Treatment Value × 50% maximum. Credits are issued initially for a 3-year period and in 3-year intervals thereafter in perpetuity if practices are maintained. Non-residential properties with a full NPDES permit may receive 50% credit. Marina properties can receive up to 50% credit (25% for NPDES permit coverage plus 25% for Clean Marina certification). Partial credits are available when only part of the property is covered. If an appeal is upheld, the county adjusts the billed fee and mails a refund check; refunds can go back no more than three years, and a written decision is issued within 45 days. Credit applications must be submitted by October 1st of the taxable year for the credit to apply that year; applications received after October 1st will be considered for the following taxable year. For small-scale stormwater practices installed without a grading permit, a formal Credit Agreement must be executed; all deed-listed owners must sign and return the Agreement by mail, after which the County inspects the practice and issues a credit decision within 90 days of a completed application. Full credit requires treating a minimum of 1 inch of rainfall; partial credit is available for less. Appeal applications are accepted on an ongoing basis. A separate property tax credit is also available under County Code § 4-2-316.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: October 1st of the taxable year (for credits); appeals accepted on an ongoing basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Anne Arundel County property owners — including residential, multi-family, and non-residential properties — who believe their stormwater fee was incorrectly calculated or issued in error, or who qualify for a credit or exemption, including those who implement stormwater runoff controls or who have installed small-scale stormwater management practices without a grading permit. Eligible property types include residential, multi-family, non-residential, agricultural, NPDES-permitted, and marina properties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction, correction, or exemption of the Watershed Protection and Restoration Fee billed to a property, including refunds for overbilled amounts and credits of up to 50% for qualifying on-site stormwater management practices. A separate property tax credit is also available.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only to property owners in Anne Arundel County, Maryland. Properties within the City of Annapolis are exempt from the WPRF.
requirements_list: Must own or be billed for property in Anne Arundel County subject to the WPRF
Must implement proactive and sustainable stormwater runoff controls (for credit applications)

Appeal must be based on an accepted ground: incorrect residential tier placement, incorrect zoning or property classification, errors in impervious area calculation for non-residential property, unapplied homeowners association fee cap, mathematical or calculation errors, exempt property status, incorrect identification of property owner, property not subject to the charge, or unapplied financial hardship exemption
Credit applications must be submitted by October 1st of the taxable year to apply that year
Refunds for upheld appeals cannot be issued going back more than three years
Stormwater management practices must be privately owned and maintained
Practices must be located on land owned by the same person or entity as the parcel seeking credit
Practices must pass a recent inspection by County staff to verify proper design, construction, and maintenance
Practices must provide water quality treatment (minimum 1 inch of rainfall treated for full credit; partial credit available for less)

Practices must be designed, approved, constructed, and maintained in accordance with County Standards, Stormwater Management Practices and Procedures Manual and/or the 2000 Maryland Stormwater Design Manual (Volumes I and II)
Property must be covered under an Inspection and Maintenance Agreement for Private Stormwater Management or a Stormwater Remediation Fee Credit Agreement

For NPDES or Clean Marina credits: property must be regulated under a National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) permit with stormwater controls and/or certified by Maryland DNR as a Clean Marina
Application must be received or postmarked by October 1 of the taxable year for credit to apply in that year
Applicant must submit photographs, a site plan/sketch, and copies of grading permit plans, stormwater management report, and installation documentation (if available)
For the Stormwater Remediation Fee Credit Agreement: the stormwater practice must not already be covered under an Inspection and Maintenance Agreement for Private Stormwater Management
If the property is transferred to a new owner, the Agreement automatically terminates and the new owner must enter into a new Agreement to continue the credit
All owners listed on the property deed must sign the Agreement and return a hard copy by mail to the County
Owner must submit inspection and maintenance records every 3 years and upon request
Owner must obtain Department approval before altering stormwater management practice
For HOA cap appeals: must provide total WPRF charged for all HOA properties and number of property tax accounts within HOA boundaries, along with documentation showing HOA boundaries

For exemption appeals: eligible exempt entities include State of Maryland, county government, municipalities, regularly organized volunteer fire departments used for public purpose, and veterans organizations exempt under IRC 501(c)(4) or 501(c)(19)
Tax Account Number and property address required for all appeal forms
Perjury declaration required on appeal forms
Authorization for DPW property inspection/entry required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For appeals or standard credit applications: complete the online web form selecting either an appeal or credit application type, provide required property and contact information, and submit via the electronic application at www.aarivers.org. Alternatively, complete the appropriate paper form (Form 13-1 through 13-5 depending on the reason for appeal) and mail to WPRF Appeals, Anne Arundel County DPW, MS 7409, 2662 Riva Road, Annapolis, MD 21401. Include photographs of the stormwater practices, a site plan, and any available grading permits, stormwater management reports, and installation documentation. Credit applications are due by October 1st of the taxable year. The county will review and issue a written decision within 45 days for appeals, and within 90 days for credit applications. For financial hardship exemptions, use the separate Financial Hardship Exemption Application form. For the Stormwater Remediation Fee Credit Agreement (small-scale practices installed without a grading permit): submit a WPRF Credit application to the County; the County will provide an unsigned draft Agreement specific to the property; all deed-listed owners must sign and return the draft Agreement by mail; the County will inspect the stormwater practice(s); if the credit is approved, the County signs the Agreement and issues a credit decision; if not approved, the Agreement becomes void. Contact the office at 410-222-7536 or wprf@aacounty.org with questions.

structured_extraction.program_name: Watershed Stewards Academy Short Course: Stormwater Success
structured_extraction.program_description: A short course for property managers and HOA leaders in Anne Arundel County that provides information and resources to help reduce stormwater pollution from their properties. The course covers flooding concerns, maintenance of stormwater management devices, reducing management costs, and ways to engage residents to reduce pollution from pet waste, litter, and other sources.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free training program consisting of three in-person sessions and three webinars, plus a toolbox of print and web-based resources. The course is free for Anne Arundel County employees.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property managers and HOA (homeowners association) representatives who live or work in Anne Arundel County, as well as Anne Arundel County employees.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and technical assistance to reduce stormwater pollution, manage stormwater devices, reduce flooding, and engage residents in pollution reduction.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to property managers and HOA representatives who live or work in Anne Arundel County.
requirements_list: Must be a property manager or HOA representative who lives or works in Anne Arundel County, or an Anne Arundel County employee
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register through the link at aawsa.org/stormwater-success-event. Contact Josh Clark at jyetterclark@aacps.org with questions.

structured_extraction.program_name: Workshop: Dealing with Trauma and Stress
structured_extraction.program_description: A free workshop hosted by the Anne Arundel County Nonprofit Center in partnership with the United Way of Central Maryland. The workshop helps nonprofit leaders and staff recognize and manage stress and trauma, covering types of stress and trauma, how they affect health, practical coping tools, ways to support others who have experienced trauma, and strategies for building organizational resilience. Two free sessions are offered in April 2026: a virtual session on April 14, 2026 (12:00–1:00 p.m.) and an in-person session on April 16, 2026 (6:00–8:00 p.m.) at the Nonprofit Center with a light dinner included. Facilitated by the United Way of Central Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two free sessions offered in April 2026: a virtual session on April 14, 2026 (12:00–1:00 p.m.) and an in-person session on April 16, 2026 (6:00–8:00 p.m.) at the Nonprofit Center with a light dinner included. Topics include types of stress and trauma, health effects, practical coping tools, and how to support others who have experienced trauma.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit leaders and staff, particularly those serving Anne Arundel County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training on recognizing and managing stress and trauma in the workplace, supporting colleagues, and building organizational resilience
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Hosted by Anne Arundel County Nonprofit Center; open to nonprofits serving Anne Arundel County
requirements_list: Registration required at https://bit.ly/NPC-Workshop-Stress
Special accommodations must be requested at least seven days in advance by contacting Amber Barnett at 410-222-2606 or exbarn24@aacounty.org
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register online at https://bit.ly/NPC-Workshop-Stress. Contact Mary Woods at exwood25@aacounty.org with questions.

structured_extraction.program_description: An after-school program for at-risk youth experiencing academic or attendance issues at Brooklyn Park Middle, Lindale Middle, and Meade Middle School, particularly youth impacted by incarceration. The program addresses current academic needs and helps youth develop personal goals and plans for future success.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: After-school academic support, goal setting, and personal development planning for at-risk middle school youth.
structured_extraction.program_audience: At-risk youth experiencing academic or attendance issues at Brooklyn Park Middle, Lindale Middle, and Meade Middle School, particularly those impacted by incarceration.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Academic support, personal goal development, and building a path toward future success.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County, serving students at specific middle schools.
requirements_list: Must be a youth at Brooklyn Park Middle, Lindale Middle, or Meade Middle School
Must be experiencing academic and/or attendance issues
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Euphemia Griffin at niecyg2@gmail.com for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: In partnership with the Anne Arundel County Mental Health Agency, this program provides one-on-one mentoring for youth aged 11 to 21 who have a mental health diagnosis. Enrolled youth also have the opportunity to meet monthly in a group setting to build peer connections and learn skills to manage their mental well-being.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-on-one mentoring and monthly group sessions for youth aged 11 to 21 with a mental health diagnosis, focused on building skills and peer connections to support mental well-being.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Youth aged 11 to 21 with a mental health diagnosis in Anne Arundel County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: One-on-one mentoring and group skill-building sessions to support youth mental health.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County
requirements_list: Must be aged 11 to 21
Must have a mental health diagnosis
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact TyJuan Thompson, Youth Programs Manager, at SRThom99@aacounty.org or 410-934-8380 for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: Anne Arundel County partnered with the Anne Arundel Workforce Development Corporation (AAWDC) to implement youth workforce development services using federal Congressional funding.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Direct workforce development services for youth funded by $500,000 in FY23 federal Congressional funding subgranted to AAWDC.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Youth in Anne Arundel County seeking workforce development services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Youth workforce development direct services
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County

structured_extraction.program_name: Property Assessed Clean Energy (PACE) / Clean Energy Loan Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A lending program that helps commercial and industrial property owners in Anne Arundel County (including the City of Annapolis) save money and energy by providing upfront capital to improve their buildings. Property owners can finance energy efficiency upgrades and renewable energy production equipment with no money down (or loans between $2,500 and $10,000 for Annapolis-based properties), with repayment made as a benefit assessment or surcharge on the property tax bill over terms up to 20 years. The assessment transfers with the property on sale and can be passed through to tenants where appropriate. The program is administered countywide through AAEDC/Maryland Clean Energy Center, with the City of Annapolis also directly facilitating loans for qualifying commercial property owners within city limits.
structured_extraction.agency: Anne Arundel County / City of Annapolis
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financing for energy efficiency upgrades and renewable energy production equipment with no money down or loans between $2,500 and $10,000, repaid as a property tax benefit assessment or surcharge over up to 20 years (10–15 years for City of Annapolis loans). Loans bear interest at a preferred rate based on market conditions and the borrower's credit. The assessment/lien transfers to new owners on sale and can be passed through to tenants.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Commercial and industrial property owners in Anne Arundel County, including the City of Annapolis, looking to make energy efficiency building upgrades or install renewable energy production equipment.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency improvements and renewable energy production equipment installed on qualifying non-residential, multifamily (5+ unit), or commercial properties.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Property must be located within a PACE-enabled area in Anne Arundel County. For City of Annapolis loans, applicant must own real property located within the City of Annapolis.
requirements_list: Applicant must be the legal owner of the building
Building must be a non-residential property or a property with 5 or more units
Property must be located within a PACE-enabled area
Mortgage must not be held in a commercial mortgage-backed security (CMBS)
Must have 100% ownership interest in real property located within the City of Annapolis (for Annapolis program)
Must obtain an energy audit showing annual energy savings equal to or exceeding annual loan repayment amount
Must agree to repay the loan through a surcharge on the property's real estate tax bill
Must provide signed statement and documentation including income statement, IRS form W-2, payroll statement, and rental report
Must provide most recent federal tax return, IRS form 1098, mortgage statement, and homeowner's insurance policy
Must have a debt-to-income ratio of not greater than 40%
Must have a title-to-income ratio of not greater than 40%
Must obtain written consent of all holders of prior recorded liens or encumbrances on the property
Must sign a lien or surcharge statement in favor of the City, to be recorded in Anne Arundel County land records
Must notify any existing lenders of the loan and obtain their written consent
Must notify all prospective purchasers of the property of the loan's existence and terms
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For county-level PACE financing, contact the AAEDC Financing & Tax Credit Representatives using the contact form on the AAEDC page, or visit the Maryland Clean Energy Center website for more information. For City of Annapolis loans, apply directly through the City of Annapolis. The City facilitates the loan directly with the property owner, who enters into a contract with the City containing the loan terms and repayment conditions.

structured_extraction.program_name: Arthritis Foundation's Walk with Ease Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Walk With Ease is a free 6-week community-based physical activity and self-management education program centered on walking. Group sessions include health education, stretching and strengthening exercises, and motivational strategies to help participants reduce arthritis pain, improve balance and strength, and build confidence in physical activity. The program is offered in a hybrid format with in-person group sessions and self-guided walks. It is partially funded under Title III-D of the Older Americans Act and is available in multiple Maryland counties including Anne Arundel and Baltimore County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free or low-cost 6-week group program. In Anne Arundel County, sessions are offered at no cost with two in-person group sessions and one self-guided walk per week. In Baltimore County, one-hour group workshops meet three times a week for six weeks; individuals 60 and over are encouraged to make a suggested donation of $15 at registration. Participants receive a guidebook. Partially funded under Title III-D of the Older Americans Act.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Older adults, particularly those 60 and over or those with arthritis or related conditions. In Anne Arundel County, adults who are able to stand on their feet without pain for at least 10 minutes.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participation in a structured walking and arthritis self-management program including health education, stretching, and strengthening exercises.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is offered at the Brooklyn Park Senior Activity Center in Anne Arundel County and at senior centers in Baltimore County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be able to stand on their feet without pain for at least 10 minutes (Anne Arundel County)
Targeted at individuals 60 and over (Baltimore County)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: In Anne Arundel County, register by calling the Brooklyn Park Senior Activity Center at 410-222-6847 or sign up in person at the center. In Baltimore County, contact Donna Bilz by email at dbilz@baltimorecountymd.gov or by phone at 410-887-3423 for more information and registration.

structured_extraction.program_description: Senior Center Plus is a structured, supervised socialization day program for older adults who need more support than a typical senior center provides but do not require medical adult day care. Experienced staff lead sessions focused on each participant's strengths and interests, offering cognitive, social, and physical recreational activities adapted for those who need extra support. The program also provides meals, health screenings, and respite care support for family caregivers. It is available in both Anne Arundel County and Charles County, Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants attend supervised day programs at select senior activity centers, with a nutritionist-approved lunch, snacks, project supplies, health screenings, and structured activities provided. Anne Arundel County charges $20 per day (10am–2pm); Charles County's daily fee varies (call 301-609-5710 for current rate). Scholarships or financial assistance may be available to offset costs. A free evaluation by a Registered Nurse or Licensed Social Worker is required to determine eligibility. In Charles County, a free in-home assessment is conducted by the Charles County Health Department's Adult Evaluation & Review Services (AERS) team.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Frail or support-needing adults (age 55+ in Anne Arundel County; age 60+ in Charles County) who are county residents and need more support than a standard senior center provides but do not require medical adult day care. Also provides respite care support for family caregivers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participation in structured socialization, cognitive, physical, and recreational activities; meals; health screenings; and supervised group programming tailored for older adults who need extra support.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Anne Arundel County (at select senior activity centers) and Charles County (at the Richard R. Clark Senior Center in La Plata, Maryland).
requirements_list: Be a current resident of Anne Arundel County (for Anne Arundel program) or Charles County (for Charles County program)
Be at least 55 years of age (Anne Arundel) or 60 years of age (Charles County)
Be assessed as a frail senior or someone who cannot participate independently in a standard senior center setting
Be able to independently use the restroom (Anne Arundel)
Be able to independently feed yourself (Anne Arundel)
Be able to communicate needs to staff (Anne Arundel)
Complete an in-home assessment by the Charles County Health Department's Adult Evaluation & Review Services (AERS) team (Charles County)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: In Anne Arundel County, call the Department of Aging and Disabilities at (410) 222-4257 to schedule a free evaluation by a Registered Nurse or Licensed Social Worker to determine eligibility. In Charles County, a free in-home assessment is conducted by the Charles County Health Department's Adult Evaluation & Review Services (AERS) team, who then makes a recommendation for the program; call 301-609-5710 for information on fees and financial assistance.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free daily telephone check-in service for older adults and adults with disabilities who live alone, are homebound, or have medical conditions but wish to maintain their independence. Trained volunteers call each participant at a set time every day, seven days a week including holidays, to confirm their well-being. If a call goes unanswered or in an emergency, a designated contact (such as a 'Good Neighbor') and local police are notified to check on the participant. Participants may also receive birthday cards from volunteers. The program is offered at no cost and is supported by public funding as well as civic, private, and individual donations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free daily person-to-person telephone check-in calls made by trained volunteers, seven days a week including holidays, between 8:00–10:00 a.m. at a time chosen by the participant. In an emergency or if a call goes unanswered, a designated contact (Good Neighbor) and local police are notified for a wellness check. Participants may also receive birthday cards from volunteers. Provided at no cost to participants. Program is funded through state and federal grants.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults age 55 or older, adults with disabilities, veterans, and family caregivers who live alone, are homebound, or lack immediate support at home — including those recently discharged from the hospital — and do not have family or friends available to regularly check on them. Income guidelines may apply (single participants ≤$1,304/month; with spouse ≤$1,762.50/month).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Daily wellness and safety telephone check-in calls to participants, with emergency coordination for isolated or at-risk individuals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available countywide in Anne Arundel County and Harford County, Maryland. Participants must be residents of the county they are enrolling in.
requirements_list: Must be age 55 or older, or an adult with a disability
Must be a resident of Anne Arundel County (for the AAC program)
Must be homebound, live alone, have a medical condition, or lack someone nearby who can handle an emergency
Must not have family or friends available to regularly check on them
Must meet income guidelines (single ≤$1,304/month; with spouse ≤$1,762.50/month)
Must have telephone access
Must provide a medical history and designate an emergency contact or Good Neighbor upon enrollment
Must provide consent for wellness checks
Good Neighbor must consent to being available as a backup contact
Volunteers must be Anne Arundel County residents, pass a background check, complete required training, and provide two non-family supervisor references
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: In Anne Arundel County, complete the participant application form and submit via email or mail to the Department of Aging & Disabilities, or call (410) 222-4257 or email caregiver_support@aacounty.org. Demographic information is requested for grant reporting purposes. In Harford County, referrals come from the Office on Aging, community outreach, or personal referrals; contact the Volunteer Office at Citizens Care and Rehabilitation Center at 410-939-5500, ext. 243 for enrollment or volunteer information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free 6-week training program that gives family caregivers practical tools and skills to manage their caregiving role. Participants learn self-care strategies to reduce stress, manage emotions, communicate needs effectively, and access community resources. The program is available for caregivers of adults with chronic conditions, older adults, individuals with disabilities, and parents of children with special needs. Sessions are offered virtually via Zoom as six 90-minute weekly workshops.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free 6-week virtual workshop (via Zoom) consisting of six 90-minute sessions. Participants gain self-care tools, caregiving skills, stress management techniques, and access to community resources.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Family caregivers of older adults, adults with chronic conditions, individuals with disabilities, and parents of children with special needs
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and education in self-care, stress reduction, emotional management, communication skills, caregiving decision-making, and building overall caregiver confidence
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County and Howard County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a caregiver for a friend, relative, or family member
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register online at mdlivingwell.org/hub or sign up directly at the provided registration link, or contact Jennifer Jackson by phone or email. Howard County residents may also visit the Howard County Office on Aging and Independence for program details.

structured_extraction.program_description: The ACR Fund provides grants and zero-interest loans to spur economic activity, investment, and improvement in Anne Arundel County's 11 Commercial Revitalization Districts, parts of the City of Annapolis, the Anne Arundel County Enterprise Zone in Brooklyn Park, and designated commercial corridors in South County, including the Glen Burnie Town Center. The program also includes professional architectural services through a full-service architectural firm with commercial revitalization experience to support commercial revitalization projects.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant up to 50% of project costs (maximum $50,000) for renovation and upgrades to building exteriors and site improvements, including landscaping. Zero-interest loans up to $100,000 repaid over three to seven years, limited to 90% of total project costs. Professional architectural services provided by a full-service architectural firm with commercial revitalization experience. ACR Fund recipients may also be offered a companion VOLT Loan of up to $500,000 for tenant improvements, equipment purchases, and working capital. A property tax credit is available for up to 10 years equal to the incremental increase in real property tax assessment for improvements of at least $100,000.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: For a limited time (no specific date provided)
structured_extraction.contact_name: Kayleigh De La Puente, Town Center/Revitalization Manager
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners or business owners with a lease located within Anne Arundel County's 11 Commercial Revitalization Districts (including Glen Burnie Town Center), parts of the City of Annapolis, the Enterprise Zone in Brooklyn Park, or designated commercial corridors in South County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Renovation and upgrades to building exteriors, site improvements including landscaping, tenant improvements, equipment purchases, and working capital. A companion loan through the VOLT Fund can also fund tenant improvements, equipment purchases, and working capital.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Anne Arundel County's eleven Commercial Revitalization Districts (including Glen Burnie Town Center and South County districts such as Mayo Rd, Galesville, Churchton, and Deale), parts of the City of Annapolis, the Anne Arundel County Enterprise Zone in Brooklyn Park, and designated commercial corridors in South County.
requirements_list: Must be located in one of the 11 designated Commercial Revitalization Districts
Applicant must be a property owner or a business owner with a lease
Property must be located within an eligible area (Commercial Revitalization District, City of Annapolis revitalization area, Enterprise Zone in Brooklyn Park, or South County commercial corridor)
Contact AAEDC to verify property eligibility before applying
Grant covers up to 50% of total project costs (max $50,000)
Loan is limited to 90% of total project costs, requiring a 10% match from the applicant
For property tax credit: improvements must be at least $100,000 and certified by Office of Planning and Zoning as qualified property
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact AAEDC to discuss the process and verify that the property is eligible, then submit an application through the online ACR application portal.

structured_extraction.program_description: A matching grant program administered through Anne Arundel Economic Development Corporation (AAEDC) in partnership with Anne Arundel County and the City of Annapolis that reimburses businesses for the cost of training new and existing employees. Eligible activities include on-the-job training, classroom or offsite training, training software purchases, and train-the-trainer programs. Businesses are reimbursed up to 50% of the cost per employee, up to a maximum of $1,000 per employee.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A matching grant reimbursing businesses up to 50% of the cost per employee for eligible training activities, up to a maximum of $1,000 per employee. Eligible uses include on-the-job training, classroom or offsite training, training software purchases, and train-the-trainer programs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses located in Annapolis and Anne Arundel County, including maritime businesses, seeking to train new or current employees.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: On-the-job training, classroom or offsite training, training software purchases, and train-the-trainer programs for new and incumbent workers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to qualified businesses located in Annapolis and Anne Arundel County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Business must be located in Anne Arundel County
Applicant must provide matching funds
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact AAEDC to learn more about training opportunities and to apply.

structured_extraction.program_name: Key Bridge Small Business Direct Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides direct cash grants ranging from $10,000 to $50,000 to small businesses severely impacted by the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse in March 2024. Launched by the Baltimore Community Foundation through the Maryland Tough Baltimore Strong Key Bridge Fund, the program helps businesses recover from lost revenue, increased costs, and operational disruptions caused by the bridge collapse. The program is administered through three designated small business grant partners: AAEDC, Baltimore Community Lending, and the Latino Economic Development Center (LEDC). Priority is given to businesses located in Southeastern Baltimore City, Southeastern Baltimore County, and Northern Anne Arundel County, though businesses in other Maryland areas demonstrating a compelling and provable case of severe impact may also be eligible. Grant amounts are based on the revenues of the small business.
structured_extraction.agency: Anne Arundel Economic Development Corporation (AAEDC) / Latino Economic Development Center (LEDC) / Baltimore Community Lending
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Direct cash grants ranging from $10,000 to $50,000 based on the revenues of the small business. Funds can be used to improve or adjust business operations following the Key Bridge collapse, including compensating for loss of revenue and covering increased costs. Grants cannot cover expenses already reimbursed by other disaster relief programs such as the Port of Baltimore Business Assistance Program, the Francis Scott Key Business Recovery Program, or the SBA EIDL Loan Program. Priority is given to businesses in Southeastern Baltimore City, Southeastern Baltimore County, and Northern Anne Arundel County.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses in the Baltimore region (Southeastern Baltimore County, Southeastern Baltimore City, Northern Anne Arundel County, or other Maryland communities) severely impacted by the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Compensating for loss of revenue, covering increased costs, and adjusting or improving business operations related to the Key Bridge collapse. Cannot be used for expenses already reimbursed by other federal, state, or local disaster relief programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses in Anne Arundel County, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, or other areas in Maryland impacted by the Key Bridge collapse. Priority given to businesses in Southeastern Baltimore City, Southeastern Baltimore County, and Northern Anne Arundel County. Businesses in other Maryland areas must demonstrate a compelling and provable case that they were severely affected by the Key Bridge collapse.
requirements_list: Business must have been in existence (operating) for at least two years as of March 26, 2024
Must demonstrate ongoing viability and sustainability
Must provide evidence of financial impact (loss of revenue or increased expenses) related to the Key Bridge collapse
Must have had revenue of at least $50,000 in at least one of the two years prior to March 26, 2024
Must have two or more employees, which may include the owner(s)
Must be in good standing (active or compliant status) with the State of Maryland, registered with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
Must provide a 2023 profit and loss statement, a 2024 year-end balance sheet, and a 2024 profit and loss statement
Must submit 2023 business tax returns or Schedule C
Must submit 2024 business tax returns or Schedule C
Must complete, sign, and date an IRS W-9 form signed by authorized signer and upload it during the application process
Must provide valid identification (driver's license or passport)
Bank account must be a business bank account matching the name of the applying business
Must explain how grant funds will be used
Grant funds cannot duplicate reimbursement from other federal, state, or local disaster relief programs
Business must be severely impacted by the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse
Business must be located in or demonstrate impact from the Key Bridge collapse affecting operations in the eligible area
All submitted documents must be clear, legible, and complete (no selfies, partial screenshots, redactions, or cut-offs)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Businesses applied through one of three designated small business grant partners: AAEDC (for businesses in Northern Anne Arundel County), Baltimore Community Lending, or the Latino Economic Development Center (LEDC). Applications were accepted from February 18, 2025 through March 20, 2025. Applicants submitted required financial documents including tax returns, profit and loss statements, a W-9 form, and valid identification online through each partner's portal (AAEDC applications submitted via the AAEDC Submittable portal). Applicants may be asked for additional information during review. Free assistance completing the application was available in English and Spanish from all partners. Contact AAEDC at 410-222-7410 or LEDC at 202-759-8397 for additional help.

structured_extraction.program_description: An annual grant program administered by BGE that provides up to $10,000 to local nonprofit organizations for environmental stewardship projects within BGE's service area in Maryland. Now in its 13th year, the program has awarded more than $2.6 million since 2013. Eligible projects must address at least one of BGE's environmental focus areas: clean air and water, climate change, alternative energy, conservation, education, energy efficiency, pollution prevention, or community engagement. Grants are funded with shareholder dollars, not customer bills.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $10,000 per eligible organization for environmental stewardship projects in BGE's service territory. Projects must address at least one focus area: clean air and water, climate change, alternative energy, conservation, education, energy efficiency, pollution prevention, or community engagement. Funded with shareholder dollars, not customer bills.
structured_extraction.program_audience: 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations and other eligible community organizations located within BGE's geographic service area in Maryland that want to carry out environmental stewardship projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Environmental stewardship projects in the areas of clean air and water, climate change, alternative energy, conservation, education, energy efficiency, pollution prevention, and community engagement.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be located within BGE's geographic service area in Maryland, covering Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Carroll, Frederick, Howard, Harford, Montgomery, Prince George's, Calvert, Charles, and Queen Anne's counties.
requirements_list: Must be a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization (primary eligibility) or other eligible community organization within the BGE service territory
Must have a board of directors
Must be located in BGE's geographic service area

Proposed project must fall into at least one of BGE's environmental focus areas: clean air and water, climate change, alternative energy, conservation, education, energy efficiency, pollution prevention, or community engagement
Must meet additional eligibility criteria listed on BGE's website
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit applications online through BGE's website during the open application window. The application period has historically opened in early March and closed in March or May depending on the cycle. Additional details and a link to the application are available at the BGE Green Grants page.

structured_extraction.program_description: BGE (Baltimore Gas and Electric), in partnership with Hello Alice and the Global Entrepreneurship Network (GEN), offers grants of up to $20,000 to eligible small businesses located in BGE's Maryland service area. Originally launched as part of BGE's Customer Relief and Energy Infrastructure Investment Plan in response to COVID-19, the program has continued as an ongoing initiative to help Maryland small businesses succeed and thrive. Funded entirely by BGE shareholder dollars (not reflected in customer bills), grants are awarded to for-profit businesses that are existing BGE electric and/or gas customers in good standing, have been operating for at least one year, have no more than 25 full-time employees, and have annual gross revenues of less than $7 million USD. Priority has historically been given to historically underrepresented minority- and women-owned businesses.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time grant of $20,000 awarded to eligible small businesses. Funded by BGE shareholder dollars (not reflected in customer bills). Total program commitment was originally $15 million over multiple years. Applicants must be existing BGE electric and/or gas customers in good standing, have been operating for at least one year, have no more than 25 full-time employees, and have had annual gross revenues of less than $7 million USD. Funds are intended to support business operations and serve customers. Priority given to minority- and women-owned businesses.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: June 13, 2025 at 6 p.m. ET (prior windows: July 18–August 26, 2022; January 20–March 3, 2021)
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit small businesses in BGE's Maryland service area that are existing BGE electric and/or gas customers, have been operating for at least one year, have up to 25 full-time employees, and have annual gross revenues under $7 million. Priority given to historically underrepresented minority- and women-owned businesses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Support business operations and serve customers during economic recovery; demonstrated need for funding required. Originally focused on COVID-19 relief and recovery, including businesses pivoting in response to the pandemic.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be an existing BGE electric and/or gas customer located in BGE's Maryland service area (primarily central Maryland), and in good standing with the State of Maryland.

Be an existing BGE electric and/or gas customer in good standing with BGE
Be in good standing (or on the way to) with the State of Maryland

Have annual gross revenues of less than $7 million USD
Demonstrate need for funding to support business and serve customers
Business must be located in BGE's Maryland electric and/or gas service area
Preference given to minority-owned and woman-owned businesses
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application online at bge.com (or previously through the Hello Alice platform at helloalice.com/partners/bge/) during one of the available application windows. The most recent deadline was June 13, 2025 at 6 p.m. ET. Previous applicants who were not selected may submit a new application and will be evaluated on new information against a new pool of applicants.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore City Fire Department provides and installs free smoke alarms to residents of Baltimore City. Firefighters install 10-year lithium, tamper-resistant smoke alarms on each level of the home, typically within two hours of a request by calling 311. Specialized alarms for residents who are deaf or hard of hearing are also available through the Office of the Fire Marshal.

Specialized alarms for residents who are deaf or hard of hearing are also available through the Office of the Fire Marshal at (410) 396-5752.

structured_extraction.program_description: A 12-week, unpaid internship offered by the Mayor's Office of Immigrant Affairs (MIMA) in Baltimore City. Interns gain professional experience, build skills through hands-on work, and earn academic credits at their college or university. The program is focused on social-impact projects and is designed to give students interested in public service exposure to local government and the immigrant affairs field.

The program runs three cycles per year: Spring (January–May), Summer (June–August), and Fall (September–December).

Must have interest in working with or learning about immigrant communities

Candidates select their preferred focus area when applying. Applications are reviewed for each semester cycle based on the posted deadlines.

structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore City's Adopt-A-Lot program allows residents, businesses, families, and neighborhood groups to steward city-owned vacant lots near them. Participants can use these lots to create community gardens, clean and green spaces, or passive recreational spaces — without paying taxes or other ownership costs. The program encourages community beautification and civic responsibility by transforming vacant lots into vibrant green spaces.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible participants receive a free license to use and maintain a city-owned vacant lot. There is no cost to adopt a lot. The adoption is finalized within 60 days of application approval. Participants can also apply for water access (accepted seasonally) with online payment now available.

structured_extraction.contact_name: Teresa Stephens (Director, Neighborhood Development & Community Outreach)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City residents, families, civic or non-profit organizations, school groups, businesses, and neighborhood groups committed to caring for a vacant lot in their neighborhood.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Maintaining and improving city-owned vacant lots as community gardens, clean and green spaces, or passive recreational spaces such as chess parks, horseshoe pits, or meditation spaces; transforming vacant lots into green spaces and community beautification projects.

Must be committed to caring for and stewarding the vacant lot
Cannot use the lot for parking, carwashes, dog parks, playgrounds, or for-profit businesses

structured_extraction.program_name: Affordable Housing Trust Fund (AHTF) – New Construction and/or Rehabilitation of Existing Affordable Rental Housing
structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore City Department of Housing & Community Development (DHCD) administers the Affordable Housing Trust Fund (AHTF), a City-funded trust fund that supports the creation and preservation of affordable rental and for-sale housing for very-low and low-income households in Baltimore City. All funds must serve households earning at or below 50% of the Area Median Income (AMI), and at least half of the funds must serve households earning at or below 30% AMI. A 30-year minimum affordability restriction is required on all funded units. The City allocates annual funds to the Trust Fund (e.g., $7 million per year starting FY2023, approximately $14.6 million in FY26). Funds are allocated across multiple spending categories including community land trusts, new rental construction, preservation of existing rental housing, senior homeownership repair, choice neighborhood initiatives, rent supplements, inclusionary housing, and administrative costs. Round 4 (closed March 17, 2023) provided up to $10,750,000, including $2 million set aside for Community Land Trusts and emerging developers. Round 7 provides funding specifically for new construction of affordable rental housing and rehabilitation of existing rental projects, with up to $7,500,000 total available. Set-asides include up to $1,000,000 for Community Land Trusts and up to $1,000,000 for emerging developers (defined as those who have completed at least three and no more than five projects). Prior rounds have included up to $2 million (Round 1), $1.7 million (Round 2), $6 million (Round 3), up to $10,750,000 (Round 4), and up to $7,000,000 (2024 NOFA, closed March 18, 2024), with supplemental funding of up to $200,000 per project made available in 2022 to address increased construction costs for prior awardees. The fund is administered by DHCD with oversight from the Affordable Housing Trust Fund Commission, which makes recommendations on policies, rules, and expenditures. Mixed-income developments are permitted (units up to 80% AMI), and long-term transitional housing is eligible.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $7,500,000 total available for Round 7, with individual project awards up to $1,000,000 or 50% of Total Development Cost, whichever is less. Per-unit maximums: up to $75,000 per unit for 50% AMI households; up to $120,000 per unit (fewer than 10 units) or $150,000 per unit (10+ units) for 30% AMI households. Set-asides include up to $1,000,000 for Community Land Trusts and up to $1,000,000 for emerging developers (at least three and no more than five completed projects). Up to 25% of award for predevelopment/acquisition costs combined; up to 10% of award for operating costs directly related to project implementation; up to 25% of award can be advanced for predevelopment/acquisition (grants only). Round 4 offered up to $10,750,000 with $2 million set aside for Community Land Trusts and emerging developers. In FY26, approximately $14.6 million is allocated across spending categories: community land trusts ($804,000), new rental construction ($4,500,000), preservation of existing rental ($4,000,000), senior homeownership repair ($1,033,000), choice neighborhood ($1,000,000), rent supplements ($1,533,000), flexible funds ($1,000,000), and administrative costs ($730,000). Funding supports new construction and rehabilitation of affordable rental housing for households earning at or below 50% AMI, with at least half targeting households at or below 30% AMI. A 30-year minimum affordability restriction is required on all funded units. Funds dispersal typically takes 6-8 weeks once capital stack is in place. Prior rounds included up to $2 million (Round 1), $1.7 million (Round 2), $6 million (Round 3), up to $10,750,000 (Round 4), and up to $7,000,000 (2024 NOFA), with supplemental funding of up to $200,000 per project made available in 2022 for increased construction costs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Very-low and low-income households (at or below 50% AMI, with priority for those at or below 30% AMI), as well as for-profit and non-profit developers, Community Land Trusts, joint ventures, emerging developers, and experienced developers working to create or preserve affordable rental housing in Baltimore City. First-time investors are advised to team with experienced developers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: New construction of affordable rental housing; rehabilitation and preservation of existing rental projects to create or preserve units affordable at 30% and 50% of Area Median Income; acquisition of non-City-owned properties (up to 25% of award); predevelopment costs (up to 25% of award, with up to 25% advanceable for grants); operating costs directly related to project implementation (up to 10% of award); construction costs including prevailing wages, builder's profit, overhead, and construction management; architecture and engineering fees; personnel and consultants; community land trusts; senior homeownership repair; choice neighborhood initiatives; rent supplements; and inclusionary housing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Baltimore City only. Projects are encouraged in Communities of Opportunity (as defined by Maryland State QAP for Low-Income Housing Tax Credits), Impact Investment Areas (as defined in DHCD Community Development Framework), Markets of Strength neighborhoods (Categories A-D per Baltimore City Housing Market Typology 2023), and other major revitalization areas. Round 7 applicants have proposed projects in neighborhoods including Broadway East, Westport, Ednor Gardens, Wilson Park, Park Heights, Rosemont/Dukeland, Hollins Market, Howard Park, Harlem Park, Mount Clare, Hillen, Forest Park, Frankfort, Mount Holly, Hampden, Madison Park, Hamilton Hills, Marble Hill, and Sandtown-Winchester.

Review and scoring runs January 20 through March 17, 2026, with award notifications the week of April 13, 2026. For Round 4, applications were submitted via the Neighborly Portal and closed on March 17, 2023; a Pre-Proposal Conference was held prior to close. The most recent prior NOFA (2024) closed on March 18, 2024, with awards pending Board of Estimates approval. The fund is administered by DHCD with oversight from the Affordable Housing Trust Fund Commission. Spending plan priorities and allocations are published separately. Visit the Trust Fund page for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Affordable Housing Trust Fund – Community Land Trust Homeownership NOFA
structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore City Department of Housing & Community Development (DHCD) provides grants from the Affordable Housing Trust Fund to Community Land Trust (CLT) organizations to promote affordable single-family homeownership in Baltimore City. The program directs funds to communities experiencing long-term and historical disinvestment and supports a broader mixed-income housing strategy. The program operates on a rolling basis across multiple rounds. Round 1 made $2.25 million available (awards of $750,000 each to three CLTs). Round 2 made up to $4 million available (awards of $750,000 each to five CLTs). Round 5 (current) has up to $8,000,000 available, with individual projects eligible to request up to $2,000,000. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis through June 30, 2026 or until all funds are allocated, with award notifications issued within 90 days of submission. Projects must serve households at or below 50% AMI, with at least half of funds targeting households at or below 30% AMI.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants to Community Land Trust organizations. Round 1 made $2.25 million available (awards of $750,000 each to three CLTs). Round 2 made up to $4 million available (awards of $750,000 each to five CLTs). Round 5 (current) offers up to $2,000,000 per project from a total pool of up to $8,000,000. Applications for Round 5 are accepted on a rolling basis through June 30, 2026 or until all funds are allocated; award notifications are issued within 90 days of submission. Grants are reimbursable; grantees must submit invoices or payment receipts with payment requests. Funds can support up to 50% of Total Development Cost (TDC) for units at or below 50% AMI, or up to 66% of TDC for units at or below 30% AMI. Up to 25% of total award for predevelopment/acquisition costs; up to 20% of award for operating costs directly related to project implementation. Projects must serve households at or below 50% AMI, with at least half of funds targeting households at or below 30% AMI.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: June 30, 2026 or until all funds are allocated (Round 5; prior rounds closed)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community Land Trust (CLT) organizations sponsoring affordable single-family homeownership projects in Baltimore City, particularly in communities with long-term or historical disinvestment. Serves low and very-low income households, including returning residents, at or below 30% and 50% AMI.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Development of affordable single-family homeownership housing through Community Land Trust models, serving low-income households (at or below 50% AMI, with at least half of funds targeting households at or below 30% AMI) in communities with historical disinvestment. Eligible uses include property acquisition, rehabilitation and construction, personnel and consultants, builder's profit and overhead, construction management, architecture and engineering fees, development fees, permits, surveys, legal fees, environmental assessment, market/financial feasibility analysis, carrying costs, financing fees, project management staff, infrastructure/utilities, and direct subsidy for Buyer's Choice projects. Closing costs (if not yet closed) and predevelopment expenses incurred after award date and before Board of Estimates approval are also eligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only. Projects must be located in Baltimore City neighborhoods and show consistency with community revitalization plans. Projects should serve communities with long-term or historical disinvestment.

structured_extraction.program_description: A subsidy program that gives SNAP (Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program) users in Baltimore City $30 in free produce digital deals each month when they spend at least $5 using their SNAP EBT card at a Baltimore City Safeway store. Participants also receive one free grocery delivery per month.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible participants receive three $10 digital deals (totaling $30) loaded to their Safeway for U account on the first of each month following a qualifying purchase. Deals apply to fresh or frozen produce with no added salt, sugar, or fat. Participants also get one free grocery delivery per month. To keep receiving benefits, participants must spend at least $5 via SNAP EBT at a Baltimore City Safeway each month.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City residents who use SNAP EBT benefits and shop at a Baltimore City Safeway location.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of fresh or frozen produce with no added salt, sugar, or fat at Safeway (in-store, online, or in-app). One free grocery delivery per month is also included.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only at Safeway locations in Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Must have a Safeway for U account (free to create online or in-app)
Must use a SNAP EBT card to spend $5 or more at a Baltimore City Safeway location each month
Must enter phone number at the pin pad at checkout (in-store) or place an online order linked to your Safeway for U account
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Sign up for a free Safeway for U account at Safeway.com or via the Safeway app. Shop at a Baltimore City Safeway and spend $5 or more with your SNAP EBT card. Enter your phone number at the pin pad or shop online. On the first of the following month, $30 in digital produce deals will be loaded to your account automatically.

structured_extraction.program_name: B'more Fresh: Online SNAP Produce Incentive
structured_extraction.program_description: B'more Fresh is an online SNAP incentive program that gives Baltimore City residents who receive SNAP (Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program) benefits a monthly $30 electronic incentive to buy fresh and frozen fruits and vegetables online. Funded by $3.6 million in ARPA funds, the program addresses inequitable access to home-delivered groceries and digital equity. After spending at least $5 on SNAP-eligible items at a participating retailer (Amazon Fresh, Giant, or Safeway), participants receive the e-incentive (produce benefit coupon) to use for online produce purchases. At Amazon Fresh specifically, participants also receive a $20 delivery promotion coupon each month. The $30 produce benefit coupon is valid for 60 days and covers SNAP/EBT eligible fresh or frozen fruits and vegetables with no added salt, sugar, or fat. Orders may be placed for curbside pickup or delivery in Baltimore City. The program is funded through 2026.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive a $30 e-incentive (produce benefit coupon) each month after spending a minimum of $5 on SNAP-eligible items at a participating online retailer (Amazon Fresh, Giant, or Safeway). The coupon is valid for 60 days and can be used to purchase fresh or frozen fruits and vegetables with no added salt, sugar, or fat. At Amazon Fresh, participants also receive a $20 delivery promotion coupon applied toward the delivery fee. Orders can be placed for curbside pickup or delivery in Baltimore City. The program is funded through December 2026 via $3.6 million in ARPA funding.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City residents enrolled in SNAP/EBT benefits who shop online at participating retailers (Amazon Fresh, Giant, or Safeway)
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Online purchases of fresh and frozen fruits and vegetables with no added salt, sugar, or fat from participating retailers (Amazon Fresh, Giant, or Safeway), via curbside pickup or delivery in Baltimore City

structured_extraction.program_description: An initiative to reduce infant mortality in Baltimore City through programs emphasizing policy change, service improvements, community mobilization, and behavior change. Also supports policy development and community mobilization.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore Development Corporation (BDC) offers a business loan program with different loan types designed to create jobs and support sustainable business growth in Baltimore City. The program provides flexible lending terms that are more affordable than traditional lenders, helping small and growing businesses access working capital, equipment financing, and leasehold improvements. The program especially aims to support minority-owned and women-owned businesses to ensure equitable access to capital.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Business loans with flexible terms including working capital, equipment financing, and leasehold improvements. A Micro Loan option is available for businesses with maximum revenue of $5 million. Borrowers must have a minimum personal credit score of 680, a minimum debt service coverage ratio of 1.20x, and must operate (or be relocating to) within Baltimore City. Personal guarantees may be required for owners with 20% or more ownership. Collateral may be required depending on loan type. All federal, state, and local taxes must be current with no outstanding judgments or liens.

structured_extraction.program_description: BMORE Beautiful is a City-led, grassroots peer-to-peer beautification program run by Baltimore City that works with neighborhoods to change attitudes and behaviors around cleanliness. The program engages residents, businesses, and organizations in beautification projects and provides educational materials, outreach resources, and direct City support. Participants who take the pledge receive a free clean kit containing a reusable bag, trash grabber, gloves, a safety vest, and educational materials. Volunteer block captains are recruited to organize beautification activities, lead behavior change efforts, and educate neighbors on City Code requirements. The program also offers three seasonal grant opportunities to support community beautification projects: (1) Care-A-Lot Grant — supports organizations that mow and maintain up to 25 vacant lots during the Grow Season (April–October); (2) Say YES (Youth Environmental Stewards) — supports organizations engaging youth in neighborhood cleaning and beautification (Spring and Fall); (3) Love Your Block — supports small block-level beautification projects (Summer).

The City also provides educational literature, outreach materials, and other resources to participating neighborhoods. structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore City Department of Public Works (DPW) provides free weekly recycling collection services to public and private schools in Baltimore City that register for the program. Each participating school is assigned a weekly collection day based on its location in the city. The program helps schools divert recyclable materials from landfill, teaches students about environmental responsibility, and conserves resources. Schools must supply their own recycling receptacles; DPW provides collection only. Registration for the regular school year is open August through October 30, and separately for summer school programs from May through June.

DPW provides collection only; schools must supply their own recycling receptacles (bins, carts, or dumpsters). If a school misses three consecutive weeks of placing recycling at its pickup location, participation may be forfeited and a new registration form must be submitted. Summer school programs must register separately even if they participated during the regular school year.

structured_extraction.program_name: Baltimore City Family Caregivers Support Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore City Family Caregivers Support Program provides federally funded support services to family caregivers through the National Family Caregiver Support Program (Title III-E of the Older Americans Act). The program offers five core service areas: (1) Information on local resources; (2) Personal assistance connecting caregivers to specific programs; (3) Counseling and education including individual counseling, support groups, and caregiver training workshops; (4) Respite care guidance and referrals covering in-home, adult day care, overnight, weekend, emergency, and recreational respite; and (5) Supplemental financial grants of $300–$600 per person per year (from date of processing, subject to fund availability) for in-home services, respite care, caregiving supplies, and other caregiving costs. Additional supplemental services include home repairs, medical supplies, and legal aid. The program serves family and informal caregivers of older adults (age 60+), individuals with Alzheimer's or related dementias, grandparents or relatives (age 55+) caring for children 18 and under, and parents or relatives (age 55+) caring for disabled adults ages 19–59. Baltimore City employees who balance work and caregiving responsibilities are also eligible. The care recipient must be a Baltimore City resident. Applications are processed on a first-come, first-served basis subject to fund availability.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial grants of $300–$600 per person per year (from date of processing, subject to fund availability) to cover respite services, in-home services, consumable caregiving supplies, medical supplies, prescription medications, nutritional supplements, household repairs and bills, clothing, bedding, household appliances, housing costs (rent/mortgage), school supplies, cleaning supplies, adult/child day care, summer camp, after school programs, and other out-of-pocket caregiving costs. Funds may be paid directly to the caregiver, care recipient, or an outside agency for respite or in-home services. Additional services include individual counseling, support groups, caregiver training workshops (e.g., Powerful Tools for Caregivers), respite care (in-home, adult day care, overnight, weekend, emergency, and recreational), legal aid, guidance and referral support to connect caregivers with local services, FMLA/leave rights guidance, work-life balance options (telework, flexible schedules), digital skills training, and technology resources for caregiving management. Applications are processed on a first-come, first-served basis.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Family and informal caregivers in Baltimore City, including those caring for older adults (age 60+) or individuals with Alzheimer's or related dementias, grandparents or relatives (age 55+) caring for children 18 and under, parents or relatives (age 55+) caring for disabled adults ages 19–59, anyone providing unpaid family care to an individual with a disability, and Baltimore City employees who balance work and caregiving responsibilities. The care recipient must be a Baltimore City resident.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Respite care (in-home, adult day care, overnight, weekend, emergency, and recreational); out-of-pocket caregiving expenses; in-home services; consumable caregiving supplies; medical supplies and prescription medications; nutritional supplements; household repairs and bills; clothing, bedding, and household appliances; housing costs (rent/mortgage); school supplies and cleaning supplies; adult/child day care, summer camp, and after school programs; individual counseling and support groups; caregiver training workshops; guidance and referrals to local caregiving resources; legal aid; FMLA/leave rights guidance; work-life balance resources; digital skills training and technology resources for caregiving management.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Care recipient must be a Baltimore City resident. Caregiver and care recipient do not need to live in the same household, but if living separately, the distance between them cannot exceed 25 miles.
requirements_list: Must be an unpaid family or informal caregiver age 18 or older
Care recipient must be a Baltimore City resident
For caregivers of adults 60+: care recipient must need help with at least 2 Activities of Daily Living (ADLs) and a Medical Status Verification Form completed by a doctor is required
For grandparent/relative caregivers of children 18 and under: caregiver must be 55+ and demonstrate guardianship, custody, or kinship care as sole responsible caregiver
For caregivers of disabled adults ages 19–59: caregiver must be 55+, care recipient must be disabled, and medical verification indicating condition and ADLs is required
Baltimore City employees who balance work and caregiving responsibilities are also eligible
If caregiver and care recipient do not live together, a notarized letter naming the primary caregiver must be provided
Distance between caregiver and care recipient cannot exceed 25 miles if not in the same household
Must complete all forms in the application packet
Applications processed on a first-come, first-served basis
Subject to availability of funds
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Call NFCSP at 410-396-1337 or 443-615-6233, or email jazmine.adams@baltimorecity.gov to request an application package or receive guidance and referral support. 2. Download the Family Caregiver Application (available at the program website) and complete all forms in the application packet. 3. Include supporting documents such as receipts, invoices, or bills. 4. Have the care recipient's doctor complete the Medical Status Verification Form (where required). 5. Complete a W-9 form for payment processing. 6. Provide a Maryland State ID or photo ID verifying age, plus unaltered Social Security cards for both caregiver and care recipient. 7. Return completed application to the office as soon as possible. Processing may take up to 90 days. Contact Jazmine Adams at 410-396-1337 or 443-615-6233 for assistance.
