structured_extraction.program_name: Expedited Reimbursement Program for Sewage Backups
structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore City's Department of Public Works offers reimbursement to residential customers (homeowners or tenants) for cleanup, disinfection, and disposal costs caused by sewage backups during capacity-related wet weather events. Eligible residents can receive up to $5,000 per dwelling unit per event. The program covers backups resulting from surcharging in the city's sanitary sewer collection system and applies to events occurring on or after April 6, 2018. The program was established under a Modified Consent Decree between Baltimore City and the EPA/State of Maryland. For insured applicants, a final written determination from their insurance company must be obtained before the application is processed, and insurance deductibles tied to cleanup or disinfection costs may also be eligible for reimbursement.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement of up to $5,000 per dwelling unit per qualifying sewage backup event for documented cleanup, disinfection, and disposal costs. For insured applicants, insurance deductibles demonstrably linked to cleanup or disinfection may also be reimbursable. Applications are processed within 60 days of receiving all required documentation. Once approved, applicants receive a release form to sign before a reimbursement check is issued. Commercial properties are excluded; only homeowners, renters, non-commercial occupants and residents are eligible.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications must be received within 90 days after the backup.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City residential customers (homeowners, renters, non-commercial occupants, or tenants) who experienced sewage backup caused by a capacity-related wet weather event on or after April 6, 2018. Commercial properties are excluded.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cleanup, disinfection, and disposal services costs resulting from a sewage backup event, including any insurance deductible paid that is demonstrably linked to cleanup or disinfection costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only to Baltimore City residential customers (homeowners or tenants) for properties located within Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Backup must be caused by a capacity-related wet weather event (at least ¼ inch of precipitation within a 24-hour period causing sewer lines to surcharge or overflow).
Backup must be the result of surcharging in the sanitary sewer collection system caused by a wet weather event.
Applicant must be a Baltimore City residential customer (homeowner, renter, non-commercial occupant, or tenant) — commercial properties are excluded.
Backup event must have occurred on or after April 6, 2018.
Notify the City through the 311 system within 24 hours of discovering the backup.
Application must be submitted within 90 days after the backup.

If property is insured against backups, applicant must obtain a final written determination from their insurance company before expenses are considered eligible; insurance must be used to its limit if available.
Must provide documentation of all cleanup, disinfection, and disposal expenses.
Must provide documentation provided to and received from insurance company, including proof of any deductible paid (may be submitted up to 30 days after receipt from insurer).
Tenants must provide a copy of their lease signed by the owner of record.
Anyone filing on behalf of an owner or tenant must include written proof of power of attorney.
Signed release form required before a reimbursement check is issued.
Eligibility is limited to either this program or the SOS Cleanup Program — not both.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Notify the City through 311 within 24 hours of discovering the backup. Apply online at the Baltimore City website, or submit a completed application by email, certified U.S. Mail, or equivalent commercial delivery to the DPW Bureau of Water and Wastewater. Residents can call 410-396-3500 to request a mailed application. Include all required documentation with the application. Insured applicants may provide insurance documentation up to 30 days after receiving it from their insurer. Applications are reviewed within 60 days of receiving complete documentation. If approved, a release form is sent for signature, and a reimbursement check is issued after the signed release is received.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Mayor's Office of Homeless Services (MOHS) requests project proposals from qualified non-profit organizations to operate non-congregate (individual room/unit, not shared sleeping space) emergency shelters and provide supportive services at City of Baltimore-owned facilities. The program targets adult individuals experiencing homelessness in Baltimore City, specifically 135 single adult men at one facility and 145 single adult women at a separate facility. Shelters operate 24/7 and provide supportive services including meals, hygiene products, care coordination, and mental health/substance use services, with a focus on Housing First principles to quickly move residents to permanent housing.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-year contracts (July 1, 2022 – June 30, 2023) funded through City General Funds, ESG, HSP, and DSS funding sources. Two shelter types: 135-bed shelter for single adult men and 145-bed shelter for single adult women. Covers shelter operations, meals (three meals and snacks daily), hygiene products, care coordination, mental health and substance use services, transportation, and staffing. Providers may apply for more than one program and be considered for multiple eligible funding sources administered by MOHS.

structured_extraction.program_name: FY 2024 Continuum of Care (CoC) NOFO Program Competition
structured_extraction.program_description: The Continuum of Care (CoC) program promotes a community-wide commitment to ending homelessness. It provides funding to nonprofit providers and state and local governments to quickly rehouse individuals and families experiencing homelessness while minimizing the impacts of trauma and dislocation. HUD releases an annual CoC Program NOFO providing over $29 million in homeless services funding to Baltimore, supporting permanent supportive housing, rapid re-housing, transitional housing, supportive services, and CoC infrastructure projects (HMIS, planning). The program also promotes self-sufficiency and access to mainstream programs for people experiencing homelessness. Funding covers new, expansion, and renewal projects including Youth Homelessness Demonstration Program (YHDP) projects. Includes scoring mechanisms for homeless assistance projects, focuses on racial equity, coordinated entry systems, and requires CoCs to demonstrate system performance improvements and involvement of individuals with lived experience. Uses Housing First approach as foundational methodology to provide permanent, affordable housing as quickly as possible for individuals and families experiencing homelessness, including supportive services and connections to community-based supports.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: HUD-funded grants distributed through the local CoC competition process to nonprofit providers and state and local governments. Supports Permanent Supportive Housing (PSH), Rapid Re-Housing (RRH), Joint Transitional Housing and Rapid Re-Housing (TH-RRH), Supportive Services Only – Coordinated Entry (SSO-CE), street outreach, safe haven, and HMIS/CoC infrastructure projects. Also includes DV Bonus funding for new PH-RRH and Joint TH and PH-RRH projects serving domestic violence survivors. Assistance includes rental assistance, leasing, move-in assistance, security deposits (max 2 months rent), utility assistance, case management, mental health services, employment assistance, and substance abuse treatment. Administrative costs capped at 10% (split 50/50 with MOHS). A 25% cash or in-kind match of the awarded grant amount (minus leasing funds) is required. Funding covers new, expansion, and renewal projects including Youth Homelessness Demonstration Program (YHDP) projects. Housing rehabilitation and new construction projects must meet a minimum $200,000 threshold. Section 3 employment and training opportunities for low/very-low-income persons are supported. Emergency Housing Vouchers (288 set-aside), Section 8 tenant-based and project-based vouchers (919 homeless set-aside), and Public Housing units (50 dedicated to Medicaid Pilot project) are also part of the broader housing toolkit. Projects scored and ranked by the Resource Allocation Committee (RAC) according to approved rubric.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Local CoC competition deadline: September 25, 2024 at 5:00 pm EST; HUD submission deadline: October 30, 2024 (unless HUD extends the deadline)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit service providers, government agencies, and organizations serving persons experiencing homelessness (including veterans, youth, families, chronically homeless individuals, people with disabilities, LGBTQ+ individuals, domestic violence survivors, and unaccompanied youth) applying for renewal or new project funding to address homelessness in Baltimore City. Also serves individuals and families experiencing homelessness, persons fleeing domestic violence, unaccompanied youth, Black and Brown communities overrepresented in homelessness, and those at risk of homelessness.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Permanent housing provision (PSH, RRH, TH-RRH), supportive services (case management, mental health, employment, food, transportation), leasing and rental assistance, move-in assistance, security deposits, utility assistance, HMIS and CoC infrastructure, street outreach, safe haven operations, coordinated entry systems, DV Bonus projects for domestic violence survivors (housing placement, stabilization, trauma-informed services, safety planning, legal services, childcare, parenting classes, housing navigation, crisis services), CoC Planning activities, Unified Funding Agency costs. Includes new projects, renewal projects, expansion projects, and Youth Homelessness Demonstration Program (YHDP) projects. Additional uses include approximately $15 million in HOME-ARP funding for permanent supportive housing and affordable housing development, $17 million in CARES funding for housing, $90.4 million in American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funding for interventions addressing racial disparities, landlord engagement and incentive funds, employment navigation and job training support, legal services (eviction prevention, landlord-tenant mediation), healthcare services coordination, and diversion and prevention services.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants create an account on the Neighborly portal, upload all required application materials, and have an authorized individual certify and submit the application before the deadline. HUD Direct Grantees must also submit in e-snaps. Expansion projects must also submit renewal applications for existing CoC renewal projects. structured_extraction.program_description: Annual HUD competitive funding opportunity for homeless services in Baltimore City. Supports permanent supportive housing (PSH), rapid re-housing (RRH), transitional housing (TH), supportive services only (SSO), coordinated entry, and HMIS projects. Approximately 2,024 individuals experience homelessness in Baltimore City on any given night. The program aims to make homelessness rare, brief, and nonrecurring through a person-centered, data-driven approach, minimizing trauma and dislocation, and promoting self-sufficiency and access to mainstream programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: FY 2025 total available funding: $42,797,644, including Annual Renewal Demand (ARD): $31,796,073; CoC Bonus Project Funding: $6,359,215; Domestic Violence Bonus Project Funding: $3,142,356; CoC Planning Grant Funds: $1,500,000. Tier 1 projects capped at $9,538,822 (30% of ARD). Permanent housing projects capped at $9,538,822 (30% of ARD). Funding supports: Permanent Supportive Housing (PSH), Rapid Rehousing (RRH, up to 24 months rental assistance), Transitional Housing (TH, up to 24 months), Joint TH-RRH, Supportive Services Only (SSO) including street outreach and coordinated entry, HMIS, and YHDP renewal/replacement projects. Eligible costs include leasing, rental assistance, supportive services (case management, mental health, substance abuse treatment, employment assistance, legal services, childcare, transportation, etc.), operations, HMIS participation, and project administration (up to 10%). A 25% match requirement applies (of awarded grant amount minus leasing funds).

structured_extraction.program_description: Helps first-time homebuyers with low to moderate incomes buy a home in Baltimore City by providing down payment assistance, gap funding to reduce the loan balance, and an interest rate buydown. Makes homeownership more affordable by lowering closing costs and boosting down payments.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible first-time homebuyers at or below 80% of the area median income (AMI) may receive: 50% of the required down payment; GAP funding (the difference between 30% of annual household income and the annual mortgage payment) to reduce the mortgage loan balance; an interest rate buydown of up to 2.5% of the sales price; and up to 50% of closing costs. An additional $5,000 bonus is available for buyers purchasing a previously rented/occupied property (6+ months) or for a buyer or household member with a disability. Assistance is provided as a five-year forgivable loan — no repayment required if the buyer stays in the home for five years. Funds cannot be used for realtor fees or cash disbursements at settlement.

structured_extraction.program_name: Housing Opportunities for Persons with HIV/AIDS (HOPWA) Program – Baltimore Eligible Metropolitan Statistical Area
structured_extraction.program_description: HOPWA is the only federal program dedicated to the housing needs of people living with HIV/AIDS and their families. The City of Baltimore's Mayor's Office of Homeless Services (MOHS) administers HOPWA funds for the Baltimore-Towson Eligible Metropolitan Statistical Area (EMSA), both directly serving low-income individuals with HIV/AIDS and their families, and by awarding competitive sub-grants to nonprofit project sponsors and city agencies through an annual application process. The program provides safe and sanitary housing, supportive services to maintain housing stability, better access to care, and improved quality of life for low-income persons diagnosed with HIV/AIDS. Supportive services help people living with HIV/AIDS (PLWHA) maintain housing stability, gain better access to health care, and enhance their quality of life. The program includes Tenant-Based Rental Assistance (TBRA), HOPWA CARES Act (HOPWA-CV) funds for short-term rental, mortgage, and utility (STRMU) assistance, and periodic amendments to Annual Action Plans as needed. Specific funded amounts have included $103,117.30 in 2018 formula TBRA funds to assist approximately 460 HOPWA-eligible households in Baltimore City, and a proposed 2019 amendment reallocating $299,069 to assist 415 households in Baltimore City and $143,305 to assist 143 households in Baltimore County through TBRA. The City of Baltimore annually contracts with localities within the EMSA to address housing needs, and all counties in the EMSA except Carroll County provide tenant-based rental assistance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides two tracks of assistance: (1) Direct assistance to eligible individuals and families, including tenant-based rental assistance (TBRA), project-based rental assistance, conversion/lease/repair of facilities, new construction, short-term rent/mortgage/utility (STRMU) payments to prevent homelessness, permanent housing placement, employment and education services, personal assistance, help accessing government benefits, and referrals for drug/alcohol treatment, daycare, nutritional services, physical and mental health care. Specific funding has included $103,117.30 in 2018 formula TBRA funds to assist approximately 460 HOPWA-eligible households in Baltimore City, $195,176.72 in HOPWA CARES Act (HOPWA-CV) funds for supportive services and STRMU assistance in the Baltimore EMSA, and a proposed 2019 amendment reallocating $299,069 to assist 415 households in Baltimore City and $143,305 to assist 143 households in Baltimore County through TBRA. (2) Competitive sub-grants awarded annually to nonprofit 501(c)(3) organizations and city agencies for housing assistance and supportive services for people with HIV/AIDS. Grant amounts depend on community need, priorities, and available funding, and are awarded for the upcoming City Fiscal Year. All counties and cities in the Baltimore-Towson EMSA except Carroll County provide housing assistance in the form of tenant-based rental assistance.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Every January (for sub-grant applicants); public comment deadlines vary by amendment (e.g., May 20, 2022 for 2019 AAP amendment)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Two audiences: (1) Low-income persons (at or below 80% of area median income) who are medically diagnosed with HIV/AIDS and their families, residing in the Baltimore-Towson Eligible Metropolitan Statistical Area (EMSA); (2) Nonprofit 501(c)(3) organizations and city agencies seeking to provide housing and services to low-income individuals living with HIV/AIDS and their families in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental assistance (tenant-based and project-based), facility conversion/lease/repair, new construction, short-term rent/mortgage/utility payments, permanent housing placement, employment and education services, personal assistance, access to benefits, referrals for health and social services, and sub-grants to project sponsors for housing assistance and supportive services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in the Baltimore-Towson Eligible Metropolitan Statistical Area (EMSA), which includes Baltimore City, Anne Arundel, Baltimore County, Carroll, Harford, Howard, and Queen Anne's counties. Baltimore City (Mayor's Office of Homeless Services) is the HOPWA grantee for this area. All areas except Carroll County provide tenant-based rental assistance.
requirements_list: Must be medically diagnosed with HIV/AIDS (for individuals)
Must be living with HIV/AIDS
Must be low-income (at or below 80% of area median income) (for individuals)
Applicants may include eligible person's family members
Must reside in Baltimore City or the Baltimore-Towson EMSA
Must be a HOPWA-eligible household (member living with HIV/AIDS)
Must reside or seek housing within the Baltimore Eligible Metropolitan Statistical Area
Must be a nonprofit 501(c)(3) tax-exempt organization or another city agency (for sub-grant applicants)
Must be in good standing with the State of Maryland (requires certificate of Good Standing from Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation) (for sub-grant applicants)
Must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) with an active DUNS number (for sub-grant applicants)

Must provide two years of the most recent A-133 financial audits (renewal projects without audits may submit two most recent years of accountant-prepared financial statements) (for sub-grant applicants)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For individuals: Contact a Coordinated Access Navigator to complete an intake packet or make an appointment with a provider, or contact the HOPWA Program through Coordinated Access via the Baltimore City website or by calling 410-935-9862 or 410-545-1511. A list of providers is also available on the Baltimore City website. For sub-grant applicants: Every January, MOHS announces the release of a Consolidated Funding Application for the upcoming City Fiscal Year. New and renewing applicants submit project proposals for funding. Projects are selected based on community needs, priorities, and availability of funding. Amendments to Annual Action Plans (such as fund reallocations) are subject to a public comment process managed by the Mayor's Office of Homeless Services; written comments may be submitted to D'Andra Pollard at MOHS by the stated deadline.

structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore City's Inclusionary Housing Program requires market-rate rental housing developers who receive public subsidies or significant land use approvals to make a portion of their units affordable. Developers of qualifying projects must set aside 10% of units as Inclusionary Units for 30 years — 5% for households earning up to 50% of area median income (AMI) and 5% for households earning up to 60% AMI. Tenants pay the maximum affordable rent set by HUD, and developers may use the High-Performance Inclusionary Housing Tax Credit to cover the difference between market and affordable rents. Staff review residential development projects to assess whether inclusionary housing requirements apply, considering factors such as total unit count, bedroom mix, rents, public subsidies, and rezoning. Projects that already support affordable housing (at least 20% affordable units or receiving affordability subsidies) are automatically exempt. Qualifying projects receive either a waiver letter or a requirements letter within approximately 45 days of initial submission.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Qualifying rental housing projects (20+ units, receiving a major public subsidy or significant land use authorization, newly constructed or substantially rehabilitated, costing more than $60,000 per unit) must set aside 10% of units as affordable Inclusionary Units for 30 years (5% at 50% AMI for very low-income households and 5% at 60% AMI for low-income households). The difference between market rent and affordable rent may be offset by the High-Performance Inclusionary Housing Tax Credit (City Code Art. 28 § 10-18.2) administered by the City's Finance Department. Staff review development projects to assess inclusionary housing requirements and projects receive either a waiver letter or a requirements letter within approximately 45 days of initial submission, following Advisory Board review if applicable. Developers must submit an Inclusionary Housing Plan that is reviewed and approved by DHCD and the Inclusionary Housing Board before building permits are released. A Declaration of Applicability/Affordability (30-year affordability covenant) must be recorded in land records. Annual developer reports are due by January 31 for the preceding calendar year. Vacated inclusionary units must be re-leased within 30 days.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Market-rate rental housing developers and residential real estate developers and property owners in Baltimore City who receive public subsidies or significant land use authorizations for projects of 20 or more units; low-income, very low-income, and extremely low-income households seeking affordable rental housing
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Creation and operation of affordable rental units within market-rate housing developments; determination of whether a development project must meet inclusionary housing requirements (affordable unit set-asides); inclusionary housing plan development and submission; tenant selection and lease requirements compliance
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only; applies to market rental projects submitting building permit applications on or after July 21, 2024

Developer must submit an approved Inclusionary Housing Plan before building permits are released

Project review considers total number of units, bedroom mix, rents, public subsidies, and significant rezoning

Inclusionary units must be on-site, dispersed throughout project, and match market-rate unit design and quality
30-year affordability covenant (Declaration of Applicability) must be recorded in land records
Tenant income certification and annual recertification required

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Developers submit a Pre-Development Information Form at their required pre-development meeting with the Planning Department. Complete the Inclusionary Housing Eligibility Form; after submission, receive an introductory email from staff and information on whether a Project Information Form is required. After review, receive preliminary findings and, if applicable, an Advisory Board meeting date. Following the Advisory Board meeting, receive either a waiver letter or a requirements letter within 45 days of initial submission. When applying for a building permit, developers submit an Inclusionary Housing Plan to inclusionaryhousingsubmission@baltimorecity.gov. DHCD staff reviews the plan and presents it to the Inclusionary Housing Board with a recommendation. Building permits are not released until the Inclusionary Housing Plan is approved. Developer signs Declaration of Applicability with the City, notarized by both parties and approved by the Chief Solicitor. Upon plan approval, notification is sent to the Permits and Plans Review Office.

Since inception, the fund has loaned $4,876,950 across 11 projects.

structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore City's Department of Housing & Community Development (DHCD) uses Judicial In Rem Foreclosure to take ownership of vacant lots and abandoned buildings where unpaid liens (property taxes, environmental citations, water bills, etc.) exceed the property's assessed value. Once the City acquires title through the Circuit Court, DHCD works with communities to make these properties available for redevelopment by homeowners, small developers, community development organizations, and others. The program aims to improve the pace of addressing blighting properties in neighborhoods block by block.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: DHCD acquires vacant lots and abandoned buildings through a court-supervised foreclosure process, clearing title, and then makes them available for redevelopment to homeowners, small developers, community development organizations, larger developers, and other parties aligned with community goals. No auction is required — DHCD works directly with communities to determine the best use for the properties.

DHCD will analyze whether the property qualifies. If a vacant property does not have high liens, residents should call 311 to request a Vacant Building Inspection instead.

structured_extraction.program_name: Legacy Homeowners Pilot Program (Support Package for Legacy Homeowners)
structured_extraction.program_description: An anti-displacement pilot program launched by Mayor Scott that clears property tax debt for long-time Baltimore City homeowners aged 65 or older. Qualifying residents who have owned their home for at least 10 years, earn $73,000 or less annually, and have a primary residence assessed at $250,000 or less can have their outstanding property tax bills eliminated. Recipients must enroll in the Tax Sale Deferral Program by April 15, 2026, complete financial literacy courses, and set up payment plans for future tax bills. Approved homeowners have their tax bills cleared the year after they apply. City staff assist eligible residents through in-person enrollment events and outreach conducted by the Mayor's Office of Older Adult Affairs and Advocacy. Funding is available on a first-come, first-served basis while the $2 million pilot fund (budgeted in Fiscal Year 2027) lasts.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A $2 million pilot program (budgeted in Fiscal Year 2027) that forgives/eliminates outstanding property tax debt for qualifying legacy homeowners. Each applicant's tax lien amount is subtracted from the total until funds are exhausted. Funded on a first-come, first-served basis while funds last. Recipients must enroll in the Tax Sale Deferral Program by April 15, 2026, complete financial literacy courses, and enroll in payment plans for future tax bills. Approved homeowners have their tax bills cleared the year after they apply.

The Mayor's Office of Older Adult Affairs and Advocacy conducts in-person and phone outreach to older adults who may qualify. Bring required documents including a government-issued ID, two utility bills showing name and property address, and proof of 2025 income.

structured_extraction.program_name: Levels of Care for Baltimore City Hospitals Responding to the Opioid Epidemic
structured_extraction.program_description: A shared, evidence-based certification framework for Baltimore City acute-care hospitals and emergency departments to implement best practices in addressing the opioid crisis. Hospitals apply for certification at Level 1, 2, or 3 based on their capacity to screen patients for substance use disorder, provide medication-assisted treatment, distribute naloxone, offer peer recovery support, and follow responsible opioid prescribing guidelines. The Baltimore City Health Department expects every emergency department in Baltimore City to earn at least a Level 3 designation. Applicants must describe how they meet each criterion and provide supporting documentation. Applications are reviewed by a leadership team led by the Baltimore City Health Department and Behavioral Health System Baltimore.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Hospitals receive a tiered certification (Level 1, 2, or 3) recognizing their commitment to opioid crisis response. Level 1 is the most comprehensive designation. Applicants complete a form indicating how their organization meets each criterion for the selected certification level, supported by documentation. The Baltimore City Health Department expects all emergency departments to achieve at least a Level 3 designation. BCHD provides site visits, detailed feedback, and technical assistance to support hospitals in achieving certification. The program provides a shared framework and best-practice guidelines rather than direct financial assistance.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Implementing evidence-based opioid response practices including screening, medication-assisted treatment, naloxone distribution, peer recovery support, and responsible prescribing; demonstrating organizational compliance with standards for treating overdose and opioid use disorder

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides career advice, job help, and other employment services for people in Baltimore who are recovering from substance use disorder. Services include peer support from recovery specialists, supported employment, and job development assistance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Offers four services: (1) Peer Program — peer recovery specialists share their own recovery experiences, provide career advice, and connect people to MOED training and job workshops; (2) Supported Employment Program — weekly meetings with a specialist using the Individual Placement and Support (IPS) model to help set and reach job goals; (3) Job Development — job developers match people in recovery with job opportunities; (4) Recovery-Friendly Workplace — training for local businesses on substance use disorder to help them build supportive work environments.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals in Baltimore City who are recovering from substance use disorder, and local businesses interested in becoming recovery-friendly workplaces.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Career counseling, peer support, job placement assistance, and workplace training related to substance use disorder recovery.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Must be in recovery from substance use disorder (for individual services)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the online interest form at baltimorecity.gov/recovery-friendly-programs. The MOED team will contact you within two business days.

structured_extraction.program_name: MOED Support for Former Federal Employees and Impacted Workers
structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore City Mayor's Office of Employment Development (MOED) provides free career services to former federal employees and workers affected by the federal government transition. Services include job search support, resume writing, interview preparation, no-cost career training, and connections to City of Baltimore job opportunities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: No-cost services including unemployment insurance assistance, job search support and referrals, resume writing, interview preparation, career training programs, and connections to City of Baltimore job openings. Assistance is available in person at Baltimore City Career Centers or virtually online.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Former federal employees and workers impacted by the federal government transition who are seeking employment support in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Career services are not monetary — assistance covers job search, resume writing, interview prep, training, and referrals to job opportunities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Services are available through Baltimore City Career Centers or virtually online.
requirements_list: Must be a former federal employee or worker impacted by the federal government transition
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit a Baltimore City Career Center, request virtual assistance online at baltimorecity.gov/job-seeker-assistance-request, or attend the free virtual workshop by emailing FedWorker.Transition@maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: City-funded outreach teams provide daily support to people experiencing unsheltered homelessness across all 14 Baltimore City council districts. Teams connect individuals with shelter, housing, medical or addiction treatment, food, transportation, and advocacy services. Teams also identify and work to resolve outdoor encampment sites by offering housing and shelter options before any site is closed.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Outreach workers visit people living outside daily across all 14 city council districts. They offer connections to shelter, housing, medical care, addiction treatment, food, rides, and advocacy. If a community member reports a person living outdoors, outreach staff will follow up. Encampments are only closed after residents are offered housing, shelter, and other resources.
structured_extraction.program_audience: People experiencing unsheltered homelessness in Baltimore City, and community members concerned about neighbors living outdoors.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services include shelter placement, housing connections, medical and addiction treatment referrals, food access, transportation, and advocacy for people experiencing homelessness.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in all 14 Baltimore City council districts.
requirements_list: Must be experiencing or at risk of unsheltered homelessness in Baltimore City
Participation in shelter and services is voluntary
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: No formal application needed. Outreach workers conduct daily field visits. Community members can report an encampment or concern via the online form, by calling 410-545-1862, by emailing HomelessOutreach@baltimorecity.gov, or by submitting a Baltimore City 311 ticket. For immediate danger, call 911; for mental health crises, call 988.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program aimed at spurring reinvestment in Baltimore City by growing the market for locally-produced goods. It supports local makers and manufacturers through a brand certification program, promotion and marketing events, and business development services to create economic opportunity through living-wage manufacturing jobs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides brand certification, promotion and marketing events, and business development services to local makers and manufacturers in Baltimore City.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Brand development, marketing, and business growth for locally-produced goods

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit MadeInBaltimore.org for more information on the brand certification program and how to participate.

eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Commercial real estate development and redevelopment in Baltimore City.

Project must be located in Baltimore City

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Access Point of Baltimore City
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Access Point (MAP) is a single entry point for older adults, adults with disabilities, their families, caregivers, and professionals to get information, referrals, and options counseling. MAP connects people to local, state, and federal programs and services—including assisted living support, legal aid, Medicare enrollment, caregiver support, meals, medication management, transportation, and help with Alzheimer's, dementia, and chronic diseases. MAP helps individuals plan for long-term care and provides community outreach and educational resources. Over 20 MAP sites exist across Maryland, with the Baltimore City site serving local residents directly.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MAP provides four main services: (1) Benefits CheckUp — a free, confidential questionnaire to identify programs and benefits for individuals 55 and older; (2) Options Counseling — one-on-one sessions with qualified staff to set long-term care goals and create a written, person-centered support plan; (3) Community Outreach and Presentations — education about available services; (4) Resource Requests — printed materials such as community resource guides, housing lists, and applications for utility assistance, water discounts, and taxi cards. Additionally, MAP provides information, screening, and referrals to federal and state benefits and community services through a single phone call or in-person visit.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Older adults (55+), adults with disabilities, their families, caregivers, and professionals in Baltimore City and statewide Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Information, referrals, options counseling, and connection to benefits and community support services including assisted living support, legal aid, Medicare enrollment, caregiver support, meals, medication management, and transportation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Primarily serves Baltimore City residents; callers outside Baltimore City can contact the statewide Maryland MAP at 1-844-627-5465. Available statewide in Maryland with over 20 in-person MAP sites across the state.
requirements_list: Must be an older adult (55+ for Benefits CheckUp), adult with a disability, family member, caregiver, or professional seeking services in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 410-396-CARE (2273) Monday–Friday, 8:30 a.m.–4:30 p.m. to speak with a Certified Information and Referral Specialist. You can also complete the Benefits CheckUp questionnaire and email it to map.bchd@baltimorecity.gov or mail it to 417 East Fayette Street, 6th floor, Baltimore, MD 21202. The website is also available 24 hours a day. In-person counseling is available at over 20 MAP sites across Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Business Works (Incumbent Worker Training - Baltimore City)
structured_extraction.program_description: A training program that helps Baltimore City businesses upgrade the skills of their current workers. Administered through a partnership between MOED and the Maryland Department of Labor, Licensing and Regulation (DLLR), the program supports employee retention, business growth, and layoff prevention by funding skill upgrades for existing employees.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Training funds provided on a dollar-for-dollar match basis. Maximum funding per trainee is $4,500 per project or series of projects. Maximum request per year is $40,000. Funds cover classroom-based training, in-house staff training, apprenticeships, and other training opportunities. Primarily targets small businesses with 250 or fewer employees.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City businesses — especially small businesses with 250 or fewer employees — that want to upgrade the skills of current workers or avoid potential layoffs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Classroom-based training, in-house staff training, apprenticeships, and other skill-upgrade opportunities for current employees.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to local and regional businesses operating in Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Dollar-to-dollar match required from the employer
Maximum $4,500 in funding per trainee per project or series of projects
Maximum request of $40,000 per year
Primarily targets small businesses with 250 or fewer employees
Businesses must provide in-demand products or services or be facing potential layoffs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact MOED Employer Services at 443-984-3014 for more information. A program overview document is available at https://www.baltimorecity.gov/media/document/mdbizworkspdf.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Tough Baltimore Strong Fund — Port Worker Assistance
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides one-time direct financial payments to port workers impacted by the Key Bridge collapse and the resulting closure of the Port of Baltimore.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible port workers can receive a one-time payment of $1,000. Funded through philanthropic organizations, corporations, and individual donors. Applications processed through the CASH Campaign of Maryland.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Port workers impacted by the Key Bridge collapse and Port of Baltimore closure.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Direct financial assistance to port workers affected by the closure.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Serves port workers across the Baltimore region.
requirements_list: Must be a port worker impacted by the Key Bridge collapse
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit https://cashmd.org/maryland-tough-baltimore-strong-key-bridge-relief-resources to apply.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Works for Wind (MWW) is a workforce development program that prepares Maryland residents for jobs in the offshore wind industry and related fields. Participants gain free job training, apprenticeships, and industry certifications in trades such as welding, electrical, manufacturing, and maritime/transportation/distribution/logistics. The program serves both Baltimore City and Baltimore County residents, connecting them with training opportunities through partnerships with local companies and training organizations. Career Navigators help match participants with partner organizations based on their career interests. The program also provides a range of supportive services to help remove barriers to employment, including child-care aid, criminal record expungement, financial aid, tools and work attire, and transportation assistance. The program is background-friendly and open to returning citizens.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides free job training, apprenticeships, and industry certifications in offshore wind-related trades (welding, electrical, manufacturing, maritime/transportation/distribution/logistics). Supportive services include child-care aid, criminal record expungement, financial aid, tools and work attire, and transportation assistance. Career Navigators help match participants with partner training organizations. Training is available through multiple partner companies in the area.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City and Baltimore County residents aged 18 or older, including youth and returning citizens (people with criminal backgrounds), seeking careers in the offshore wind industry and related construction, manufacturing, and transportation/warehousing fields.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Workforce training, apprenticeships, and certifications in offshore wind industry trades; supportive services including child care, transportation, financial aid, tools, work attire, and criminal record expungement.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Baltimore City and Baltimore County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be 18 years of age or older
Must be a Maryland resident
Program is background-friendly (open to returning citizens)
Must have a high school diploma or GED (Baltimore County)
Must be able to pass a drug test (Baltimore County)
Must be authorized to work in the United States (Baltimore County)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Fill out the online interest form at bit.ly/applywind or the registration form on the Baltimore City website. For Baltimore County residents, complete the inquiry form on the Baltimore County program webpage. Career Navigators will contact you and match you with a partner organization based on your career interests. Email marylandworks.forwind@baltimorecity.gov with questions for Baltimore City, or contact the Career Navigator at careernavigator@baltimorecountymd.gov or 410-887-6472 for Baltimore County.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Blueprint Career Coach Initiative connects Baltimore City middle and high school students with career coaches who help them explore interests, set goals, discover career options, build skills, and plan pathways after graduation — including college, training, or the workforce.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Dedicated career coaches work with students to explore career interests, set goals, and plan for life after graduation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City middle and high school students
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Career exploration, goal-setting, and post-graduation planning
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City
requirements_list: Enrolled in a Baltimore City middle or high school

Program staff help with scheduling prenatal and pediatric appointments, offer parenting guidance, family planning education, and connect participants with other needed services.

structured_extraction.program_audience: High-risk pregnant women and new mothers in Baltimore City
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Care coordination, prenatal and infant health support, parenting guidance, family planning, and referrals to additional services
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City, Maryland

Referral from a doctor or other provider, or self-referral through Health Care Access of Maryland

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Prize money awarded to winning screenwriters

Submissions accepted in episodic, feature, or short film formats

structured_extraction.program_name: Mayor Scott's 2026 Spring Cleanup & Day of Service - Stormwater Fee Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore City residents who volunteer in a registered community cleanup can earn a credit on their stormwater fee bill. Volunteers register their cleanup activity with 311 and receive certificates they can redeem for a $10 credit each, up to three certificates per year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Volunteers earn a $10 stormwater fee credit for each certificate returned with their application. Up to three certificates per year, for a maximum annual credit of $30.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City residents who participate in a registered volunteer community cleanup
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Credit applied to the resident's stormwater fee bill
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only
requirements_list: Must register volunteer cleanup with 311
Must be a Baltimore City resident
Must participate in a registered Volunteer Community Cleanup
Must return the Stormwater Fee Credit certificate with the application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register your cleanup activity with 311. After participating, you will receive a Stormwater Fee Credit application and certificate by email or mail. Return the certificate with the application to receive the credit.

structured_extraction.program_name: Mayor's HBCU Emerging Leaders Fellowship Initiative
structured_extraction.program_description: A one-year fellowship that connects recent graduates from Baltimore City Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs) with careers in local government. Fellows work full-time within Baltimore City government agencies, receiving on-the-job training, mentorship, professional development, and coaching from Baltimore Corps. After completing the fellowship, participants may earn permanent full-time positions with the city.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Fellows receive a salary of $51,500 annually (Bachelor's degree holders) or $65,000 annually (graduate degree holders), plus benefits and transportation stipends, for a one-year fellowship placement within a Baltimore City government agency. The program also includes monthly convenings, professional coaching, skill-building sessions, and immersive experiences through Baltimore Corps.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Cohort II applications are now closed.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Recent graduates from Baltimore City HBCUs (within the last two years) with backgrounds in Public Policy, Social and Human Services, Engineering, Data Sciences, Information Technology, Communications and Writing, Finance, or Architecture and Urban Planning.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable — fellows receive a salary and stipends in exchange for working within Baltimore City government agencies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Graduates must be from Baltimore City HBCUs.
requirements_list: Must be a recent graduate (within the last two years) of a Baltimore City HBCU

Degree backgrounds of interest include: Public Policy, Social and Human Services, Engineering, Data Sciences, Information Technology and Sciences, Communications and Writing, Finance, and Architecture and Urban Planning
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants go through a rigorous application and interview process. Fellows are matched with city government agencies based on their interests, skill set, and the needs of the agency. Cohort II applications are currently closed.

structured_extraction.program_name: Mayor's Office of Employment Development (MOED) - Job Seeker Services
structured_extraction.program_description: The Mayor's Office of Employment Development (MOED) operates one-stop career centers on the east and west sides of Baltimore City, providing comprehensive employment services to residents who are unemployed, underemployed, or seeking better opportunities. Centers are open to the public with no appointment needed, and virtual assistance is also available. Services include job search assistance, resume creation and review, ID and documentation assistance, basic education and GED prep, career skills training, digital literacy labs, internet and technology access, expungement services, legal aid access, and re-entry support at the Northwest Career Center for people returning from incarceration. MOED also offers recovery-friendly job programs for people overcoming substance use disorder, recruitment events, and targeted assistance for veterans, disabled persons, senior citizens, and youth. Baltimore City residents can request services at a career center, virtually, or at a community location convenient to them, such as a church, community center, or restaurant. Language access services are also available to ensure Limited English Proficient (LEP) individuals have meaningful access to MOED employment services, including telephonic interpretation (24/7 via Language Line Solutions, 170+ languages), in-person interpretation through bilingual staff, and translation of vital documents into Spanish, French, Chinese, Arabic, and Korean.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free services including job placement assistance, job search assistance, resume creation and review, ID and documentation assistance, basic education and GED prep, career skills training, digital literacy training, internet and technology access, expungement services, legal aid access, and specialized re-entry support at the Northwest Career Center for people returning from incarceration. Also includes recovery-friendly job programs for people overcoming substance use disorder, targeted employment services for veterans, disabled persons, seniors, and youth. Language access services are available including telephonic interpretation (24/7, 170+ languages via Language Line Solutions), in-person interpretation through bilingual staff, and translation of vital documents into Spanish, French, Chinese, Arabic, and Korean. Services are provided at one-stop career centers (east and west Baltimore locations), virtually, or at community locations convenient for the resident. No appointment is needed to walk in; virtual assistance is available by submitting an online request form.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City residents who are unemployed, underemployed, or employed and seeking better opportunities, including people in recovery from substance use disorder, people with prior justice system involvement, veterans, disabled persons, senior citizens, youth, and Limited English Proficient (LEP) individuals.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable — services provided directly to individuals at no cost, including job search assistance, resume development, job placement, career training programs, GED preparation, digital literacy training, criminal record expungement assistance, and specialized support services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents and job seekers in Baltimore City through MOED one-stop career centers (east and west side locations), virtually, and at community locations (churches, community centers, restaurants, etc.) and MOED Access Points.
requirements_list: Must be a Baltimore City resident to access services at community locations
Language access plan implemented as of 9/30/2024
Staff training required for employees with direct public contact
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Walk in to one of the One-Stop Career Centers (no appointment needed), fill out the online form on the MOED website to request an appointment for job search assistance or job training programs, or request virtual assistance at baltimorecity.gov/job-seeker-assistance-request. Someone will contact you within two business days. Services can be provided at a career center or at a community location. For recovery-friendly programs, fill out the interest form on the MOED website. For re-entry services, fill out the Northwest Baltimore Career Center contact form. LEP individuals may request interpretation or translation services at any point of contact.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that protects Baltimore City water customers from having their water shut off if they or someone they care for would be harmed by a water shutoff.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Exemption from water shutoff for customers or their dependents who would be medically harmed by loss of water service.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City water customers or their caregivers where the customer or dependent would be harmed by water shutoff.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Protection from water service shutoff due to medical necessity.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City residents only.
requirements_list: Applicant or person in their care would be harmed if water is turned off
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the Medical Exemption Program page to get started and apply.

structured_extraction.program_description: Homeowners who believe their water meter is larger than needed can request a smaller meter to reduce the infrastructure fee on their monthly water bill. The infrastructure fee is based on meter size, so downsizing the meter can lower monthly water bills. A certified professional must review and approve the request before the city will downsize the meter.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reduction of the monthly water bill infrastructure fee by downsizing the water meter to a smaller size. The fee is based on meter size, so a smaller meter results in lower monthly charges.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City homeowners or property owners who believe their water meter is larger than necessary for their property's needs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction in monthly water bill infrastructure fees through downsizing the property's water meter.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to properties located within Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Must demonstrate that the smaller meter size will still meet the property's water needs, including any fire sprinkler system requirements.
For meters 2 inches or smaller: a Registered Master Plumber must review and sign off on the request.
For meters 3 inches or larger: a Licensed Professional Engineer must review and approve the request.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review the Water Meter Reduction Information Sheet to understand the process. Complete the appropriate Water Meter Downsize Request Form (one form for meters 2 inches and smaller, a separate form for meters larger than 2 inches). Have a certified professional (Registered Master Plumber or Licensed Professional Engineer depending on meter size) review and sign off on the request. Submit the completed form.

structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore City certifies businesses owned and controlled by minority group members (MBE) or women (WBE) with at least 51% ownership. Certification confirms a business's status as minority- or women-owned, which can help it qualify for city contracting opportunities that include MBE/WBE participation goals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: SMBA&D reviews and certifies businesses as MBE or WBE. Certification is valid for two years and can be renewed. Applications are completed online and the review typically takes up to 60 days. Certification gives businesses recognized status when bidding on city contracts that include MBE/WBE goals.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Minority-owned and women-owned businesses located in the Baltimore City Market Area (Baltimore City and surrounding counties) that have been in operation and minority- or women-owned for at least 12 months.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Certification status used to qualify as MBE or WBE subcontractor or prime contractor on Baltimore City contracts.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Business must have an operating office within the Baltimore City Market Area, which includes Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Anne Arundel County, Howard County, Carroll County, Queen Anne's County, and Harford County.
requirements_list: Business must be independently owned and operated
Must have been in operation for at least 12 months before applying
Must have been minority- or women-owned for at least 12 months before applying
Must have an operating office with employees in the Baltimore City Market Area
Minority ownership must be at least 51% by African American, Hispanic American, Asian American, or Native American individuals (MBE); or at least 51% owned by women (WBE)
Must select applicable NAICS codes on the application
Must provide required Maryland State-issued licenses if applicable to the business type
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application online at https://baltimorecity.diversitycompliance.com/. Include required documents, applicable NAICS codes, and any required state licenses. SMBA&D reviews the application within approximately 60 days and sends a decision by email. If denied, you may reapply three months after the denial date.

structured_extraction.program_description: Mobile Career Navigators travel into Baltimore City neighborhoods to help residents connect with jobs and free training programs. Navigators meet people at locations they choose, such as libraries or coffee shops. Services include help applying for jobs at any experience level, enrolling in over 30 free training programs (such as CDL and CNA), resume writing, adult education and GED information, and connections to support services like healthcare, childcare, housing, and food assistance. Spanish language services are also available. Businesses and community organizations can also invite a navigator to their events.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free in-person career navigation services delivered where residents choose to meet. Includes help applying for jobs, enrollment in over 30 free training programs (such as CDL and CNA), resume creation, adult education and GED information, and referrals to support services including healthcare, childcare, housing, and food assistance. Spanish language services are also available.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City residents seeking employment or training, and businesses and community organizations wishing to host a navigator at events
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Career navigation, job application assistance, training enrollment, resume help, adult education referrals, and connections to support services including healthcare, childcare, housing, and food assistance
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Baltimore City; special form available for Park Heights residents
requirements_list: Must live in Baltimore City
Submit a job seeker assistance request form or call to schedule a meeting
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Residents complete the MCN Job Seeker Assistance Request Form online or call 410-746-8663 to schedule a meeting at a location of their choice. Spanish speakers can switch the form language before submitting. Park Heights residents use a separate request form. Businesses and organizations email moed.outreach@baltimorecity.gov to invite a navigator to their event.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore City Health Department (BCHD) offers free Mpox JYNNEOS vaccine at its sexual health clinics. Eligible residents can walk in or schedule an appointment by phone at clinic locations in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free Mpox JYNNEOS vaccine provided at no cost to eligible individuals at BCHD sexual health clinics. Walk-in or scheduled appointments available at two clinic locations: Druid Sexual Health Clinic (1515 W. North Ave.) and Eastern Sexual Health Clinic (1200 E. Fayette St.).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City residents who meet CDC eligibility criteria for Mpox vaccination, including people with known or suspected Mpox exposure, gay or bisexual men and transgender or gender-diverse people with recent STD diagnoses or multiple sex partners, and others at elevated risk of Mpox exposure.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free Mpox JYNNEOS vaccine for eligible individuals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at clinic locations within Baltimore City, Maryland.
requirements_list: Known or suspected exposure to someone with Mpox
Sex partner diagnosed with Mpox in the past 2 weeks
Gay, bisexual, or other man who has sex with men or transgender/nonbinary/gender-diverse person with a new STD diagnosis or more than one sex partner in the past 6 months
Sex at a commercial sex venue, at a large commercial event, or in an area with active Mpox transmission in the past 6 months
Sex in exchange for money or other items in the past 6 months
Sex partner with any of the above risks
Anticipation of any of the above scenarios
HIV or other immune suppression with recent or anticipated Mpox exposure risk
Work with Orthopoxviruses in a laboratory
Must NOT have had a severe allergic reaction (anaphylaxis) after a prior JYNNEOS dose

structured_extraction.program_description: A community-driven grant program that provides funding to support community-led projects, including operating expenses and physical improvements, in neighborhoods near Pimlico Racecourse in Baltimore City. The program is funded through Pimlico Local Impact Aid, which is state revenue from video lottery terminals allocated for community development near Pimlico Racecourse. Projects must be completed within two years.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging from $500 up to $25,000 (in 2025) to support projects that create meaningful and measurable change. Prior cycles offered up to $30,000. Funding supports both operating funds and physical improvement projects, including youth education, arts programs, gardens/urban agriculture, neighborhood events, and community services.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible non-profit organizations (including faith-based organizations proposing non-religious projects, mission-based organizations with a fiscal sponsor, and public schools proposing community-based projects) serving residents in the Park Heights Master Plan Area, One Mile Radius around Pimlico Racetrack, Liberty-Wabash, Northwest Community Planning Forum, and Coldspring-Newtown areas of Northwest Baltimore City. Beneficiaries include youth, families, communities of color, and aging community members.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Community-led projects including operating funds and physical improvements that create meaningful and measurable change. Eligible uses include youth education and mentorship programs, arts and media production equipment and classes, community garden development and improvements, landscaping and streetscaping projects, equipment purchases, community events and festivals, career awareness programming, back-to-school events, and public safety and neighborhood improvement initiatives.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to projects serving residents in designated Northwest Baltimore neighborhoods near Pimlico Racecourse, including the Park Heights Master Plan Area, One Mile Radius around Pimlico Racetrack, Liberty-Wabash, Northwest Community Planning Forum, and Coldspring-Newtown areas in Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Projects must be located within the eligible geographic area near Pimlico Racecourse
Projects must create meaningful and measurable change

Applicants must be non-profit organizations with 501(c)(3) tax-exempt status recognized by the IRS, OR mission-based organizations without 501(c)(3) status but with a tax-exempt fiscal sponsor, OR faith-based organizations proposing non-religious projects that benefit the public, OR public schools proposing community-based projects benefiting students
Projects must be completed within two years
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted during the open application window. Eligibility guidelines are available on the program's request for applications document.

structured_extraction.program_name: Office of Boards and Commissions Prequalification Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program reviews and certifies contractors and consultants who want to work on Baltimore City public works projects. Applicants go through a process that includes reference checks, affirmative action plan review, and financial analysis to determine a work capacity rating. The Board of Estimates must approve all certifications.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program issues Prequalification Certificates to contractors and consultants, allowing them to bid on Baltimore City public works projects. Contractors receive a work capacity rating that determines the maximum dollar value of projects they can pursue. Work capacity ratings range up to $1.5M for internally compiled financial statements, up to $8M for reviewed CPA statements, and higher for audited CPA statements. Processing takes a minimum of 35 days.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Contractors and consultants seeking to work on Baltimore City public works projects
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Prequalification certificate required to bid on Baltimore City public works contracts
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to contractors and consultants seeking to do business with Baltimore City
requirements_list: Submit a complete application with all required documents
Provide current project references with contact names and numbers for each prequalification category requested
References are checked before certification is forwarded to the Board of Estimates
Contractors must have an approved Affirmative Action Plan
Contractors must submit a financial statement — internally compiled (up to $1.5M work capacity), reviewed by CPA (up to $8M), or audited by CPA (above $8M)
Board of Estimates must approve the certification
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a contractor or consultant application to the Office of Boards and Commissions. Staff check the application for completeness, verify references, confirm Affirmative Action Plan approval (contractors), and conduct a financial analysis to assign a work capacity rating. The application is then forwarded to the Board of Estimates for a recommendation and final approval. The minimum processing time is 35 days.

The goal is to help organizations better understand and respond to the impact of trauma on the people they serve.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: No-cost training and technical assistance is provided through in-person organizational technical assistance, virtual learning networks, technical assistance materials, and links to federal resources. An OYTSTTAC member conducts an agency-wide Organizational Trauma-Informed Self-Assessment and then works with staff and stakeholders to build a trauma-informed approach. Note: availability is subject to change.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations and service providers in Baltimore City seeking to adopt a trauma-informed approach to their work
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable — program provides training and technical assistance rather than funding
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to organizations operating throughout Baltimore City
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations can engage OYTSTTAC to begin the process with an agency-wide Organizational Trauma-Informed Self-Assessment, after which an OYTSTTAC member provides feedback and works with staff and stakeholders.

The permit costs $175 per permit and is valid for a fiscal year (July 1 through June 30). Official Business Permits allow designated vehicles to park in specified areas.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Parking at metered spaces while conducting official Baltimore City government business.

Payment required via Credit Card, Check/Money Order, or Journal Entry

structured_extraction.program_description: The Open Bid Program lets homeowners and small developers purchase and redevelop individual or small bundles of city-owned vacant and abandoned properties in Baltimore City. The goal is to clean up vacant properties, raise neighborhood property values, create community amenities, increase local tax revenue, and attract new residents and businesses.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible applicants can purchase city-owned vacant or abandoned properties individually or in small bundles at a bid price. Applicants must have at least $90,000 available per property for rehabilitation costs. Properties go through a competitive bid process with a 2-week window for competing offers before award.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners and small developers interested in purchasing and redeveloping city-owned vacant and abandoned properties in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and rehabilitation of city-owned vacant or abandoned properties.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only within Baltimore City. Properties must be city-owned vacant or abandoned buildings.
requirements_list: Must have $90,000 available for rehabilitation per property applied for
Applicant must not own vacant building inventory older than two years
If applicant owns vacant building inventory less than two years, must have a recent open/active permit
Applicant must not have open or pending criminal cases that could prevent project completion
Applicant must not have any open federal or state liens
Applicant must not have any open federal or state judgments
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Search and apply for available properties through the BuyIntoBmore site. After submission: (1) Application is reviewed for completeness and assigned to a Neighborhood Development Officer within 7 days; (2) A 2-week competing bid period is announced; (3) A background check and feasibility review are completed within 21 days, and applicants are notified of award or rejection; (4) A Land Disposition Agreement is routed for signatures and submitted to the Board of Estimates for approval within 45 days; (5) Lien abatement and title company selection occur within 60 days; (6) Settlement takes place; (7) Compliance is monitored by an LDA Compliance Officer until a Use and Occupancy Permit is obtained.

structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore City's Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) is seeking qualified developers to rehabilitate vacant residential buildings on blocks surrounding the new Parkview Recreation Center in the Penn North neighborhood. Selected developers will convert vacant properties into homeownership opportunities for the community. The RFQ is part of an effort to leverage a $12 million recreation center and green space capital investment, with 38 properties currently in inventory or projected acquisitions.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: DHCD is acquiring vacant properties surrounding the new Parkview Recreation Center and transferring them to selected developers via land disposition agreements and exclusive negotiation privileges for rehabilitation into homeownership units. There are 38 properties currently in inventory or projected acquisitions, all zoned R-8 Rowhouse Residential District. Properties are located within the Baltimore National Heritage Area and are eligible for the CHAP Historic Tax Credit.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Mission-oriented developers and development teams with significant experience in urban construction and residential development, including demonstrated experience rehabilitating vacant buildings for homeownership opportunities in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rehabilitation of vacant residential buildings on the 2600 block of Woodbrook Avenue, 1500 block of Clifton Avenue, and 2600 block of Francis Street, facing the new Parkview Recreation Center, for homeownership. requirements_list: Developer must be mission-oriented

Must demonstrate understanding of State economic development resources
Must demonstrate financial capacity and viability
Must respond to RFQ submission requirements by the deadline
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete the RFQ (available in English and Spanish). structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore City water customers with past-due water and sewer bill balances can set up flexible, interest-free payment plans through PromisePay, a third-party provider partnered with the Baltimore City Department of Public Works. The program gives residents more time to pay their water bills while keeping water service active, allowing customers to pay off overdue charges in manageable installments. Commercial businesses with past-due balances may also apply by contacting a water customer service analyst directly.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Interest-free payment plans for past-due water and sewer bill balances. Residential customers with balances between $250 and $5,000 can enroll online or by phone through PromisePay. Customers with balances of $50 or more may qualify for payment plans. Plans keep water service active and allow customers to pay off overdue charges in manageable installments. Commercial businesses with past-due balances may also apply by contacting a water customer service analyst.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City water and sewer customers with past-due balances, including residential customers with balances between $250 and $5,000 and commercial businesses with past-due balances.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Paying off past-due Baltimore City water and sewer bill balances through structured installment repayment.
