structured_extraction.program_name: Permanent Supportive Housing Hotel Conversion - Request For Proposals (RFP)
structured_extraction.program_description: This program uses American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funding to convert three adjacent City-owned hotel properties in Baltimore into permanent supportive housing (PSH). The Mayor's Office of Homeless Services (MOHS) seeks qualified non-profit or for-profit developers to rehabilitate and operate a minimum of 100 PSH units across the properties, with a preference for a mix of 1- and 2-bedroom units at affordability levels up to 60% of area median income (AMI) with a 55-year binding affordability covenant. Proposals must include comprehensive onsite supportive services such as individualized service plans, case management, medical screenings, mental health assistance, and life skills training for residents experiencing homelessness. The selected respondent will serve as developer, property manager, and service provider.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MOHS has committed $45,015,988 in ARPA funding to support the rehabilitation and operation of permanent supportive housing at three adjacent City-owned sites (Sleep Inn and Suites at 300 N. Front Street, Holiday Inn Express at 221 N. Gay Street, and a parking lot at 320 N. Front Street). The selected respondent receives an Exclusive Negotiating Privilege (ENP) with 120 days to negotiate a Land Disposition Agreement. The City transfers ownership of the properties for a nominal amount. The selected respondent is responsible for financing onsite development, rehabilitation, supportive services, and property management. Operating subsidies may be available through Housing Authority of Baltimore City (HABC) Project Based Voucher (PBV) assistance. An affordable housing PILOT (Payments in Lieu of Taxes) agreement may also be available.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations, for-profit developers, and joint ventures capable of rehabilitating and operating permanent supportive housing with onsite services for individuals and families currently experiencing homelessness.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rehabilitation and operation of permanent supportive housing units at three City-owned hotel properties, including hotel conversion, property development and construction, provision of onsite supportive services such as individualized service plans, case management, medical screenings, mental health assistance, and life management skills, and ongoing operating costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Three adjacent City-owned properties in downtown Baltimore City (Council District 12): Sleep Inn and Suites (300 N. Front Street), Holiday Inn Express (221 N. Gay Street), and a parking lot (320 N. Front Street).
requirements_list: Applicant must be a qualified non-profit, for-profit, or joint venture
Proposal must include plans to rehabilitate and operate permanent supportive housing at the three designated City-owned sites
Minimum 100 PSH units required across both hotel buildings
Proposed unit mix of one- and two-bedroom units preferred
Affordability levels up to 60% of area median income (AMI) with 55-year binding affordability covenant
Proposal must include comprehensive onsite supportive services: individualized service plans, case management, medical screenings, mental health assistance, and life management skills
501(c)(3) status required for non-profit applicants
Previous 2 years audited financial statements required
Minimum 60 points required to be eligible (out of 100)
At least 3 qualified multifamily PSH developments in past 10 years for developer, property manager, and service provider
Low-Income Housing Tax Credit (LIHTC) financing structure
Developer responsible for securing all rehabilitation funding and operating subsidies
Compliance with historic preservation requirements
Surface parking lot management between hotels must be addressed
Proposed development timeline must be included
Compliance with Fair Housing Act and all federal, state, and local housing laws
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit one PDF electronic copy of the proposal and all required supporting documents by email to BaltimorePSH@lesardevelopment.com by August 30, 2024 at 3:00 PM EST. The City is providing site information including floor plans and environmental assessments in Addendum A. Standard performance outcomes to be provided in a forthcoming Addendum. Proposals are reviewed and scored, followed by conditional award notices. Selected respondent will negotiate a Land Disposition Agreement within 120 days under Exclusive Negotiating Privilege.

structured_extraction.program_name: Pimlico Community Development Authority (PCDA) Local Impact Aid
structured_extraction.program_description: The Pimlico Community Development Authority (PCDA) advises the Mayor on how to allocate Local Impact Aid — revenue from video lottery terminals (slots) at the nearby casino — for economic and community development projects in the Park Heights Master Plan area and surrounding neighborhoods in Northwest Baltimore City. Funded by 5.5% of gross Video Lottery Terminal (VLT) revenue per Maryland SB 3 (2007), the program prioritizes investments in new construction housing, rehabilitation of vacant homes, workforce development, and revitalization of commercial corridors in Park Heights and the One-Mile Radius. Each year, the PCDA works with the Baltimore City Department of Planning to develop an annual spending plan, reviews community applications, and submits funding recommendations to the Mayor. Final funding decisions are made by the Mayor and City Council through the City budget process. Funds are then appropriated to city agencies or community partners to carry out approved projects. Eligible uses include infrastructure improvements, facilities, public safety, sanitation, economic and community development (including housing), capital improvements, and other public services and community programs. 85% of available funds must go to the Park Heights Master Plan area; 15% goes to surrounding neighborhoods within a one-mile radius. The funding is authorized through fiscal year 2032. For FY2027, the estimated allocation is $3,290,000 for the Park Heights Master Plan area and $581,000 for the One-Mile Radius. Active grantees must submit quarterly reports on spending and project progress, and final reports when all funding has been spent and the project is closed.
eligible_municipalities: Baltimore City - Northwest Baltimore / Park Heights area
Baltimore City - Park Heights, Northwest Community Planning Forum SNAP, Liberty-Wabash, Coldspring Newton (1-mile radius around Pimlico Race Track)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Slots revenue in the form of Local Impact Aid is distributed through an annual spending plan process. 85% of available funds must go to the Park Heights Master Plan area (1,500 acres from Park Circle to Northern Parkway, Greenspring to Wabash); 15% goes to surrounding neighborhoods within a one-mile radius of Pimlico Race Track. Grants and allocations support capital projects (housing development including homeowner preservation, vacancy elimination, new construction, single- and multifamily housing; parks and recreation; community facilities; blight elimination; infrastructure improvements) and operating grants (health and social services, employment programs, youth programs, community organizing, business development, workforce training, arts and culture, food security). Home repair grants are available for critical health and safety repairs (up to $10K–$25K per property). Development incentive grants up to $50K for vacant parcel development. Appraisal gap grants up to $50K per property for homeownership rehab. Minimum award: $25,000; projects must be completed within two years from contract start. For FY27, the estimated Park Heights Master Plan area allocation is $3,290,000 and the One Mile Radius allocation is $581,000 (with a $120,000 administrative fee). Funding is authorized through fiscal year 2032.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: September 29, 2025 at midnight (FY27 round); application window August 18 – September 29, 2025; program authorized through fiscal year 2032 with annual spending plan cycles
structured_extraction.contact_name: Chris Ryer (PCDA Chair, Department of Planning)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community organizations, nonprofits, faith-based organizations, public schools, city agencies, and community partners located in or serving the Park Heights Master Plan area and surrounding neighborhoods within a 1-mile radius of Pimlico Race Track in Northwest Baltimore City. Also includes residents of Park Heights and surrounding neighborhoods, youth, seniors, immigrant and working-class families, low- and moderate-income households, and developers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital projects and community programs benefitting economic and community development, including: housing rehabilitation and new construction (single-family and multifamily), vacancy elimination and property acquisition, infrastructure improvements, parks and recreation, community facilities, public safety, sanitation, workforce development and career training, youth education and enrichment, arts and culture, food security and urban agriculture, community organizing, health and social services, neighborhood beautification, recreation center renovations, health center capital expansion, urban farm development, commercial corridor revitalization, and other public services in the Park Heights area and surrounding neighborhoods.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Northwest Baltimore, including the Park Heights Master Plan area (85% of funds; 1,500 acres encompassing 12 Neighborhood Statistical Areas from Park Circle to Northern Parkway, Greenspring to Wabash), and surrounding neighborhoods within a 1-mile radius of Pimlico Race Track (15% of funds), including the Northwest Community Planning Forum SNAP area, Liberty-Wabash area, Coldspring Newton, and neighborhoods such as Cross Country, Cheswolde, Fallstaff, Glen, and Mount Washington. The One-Mile Radius is defined as census block groups at least partially within one mile of Pimlico Racetrack plus additional areas bounded by Liberty Heights Avenue, Northern Parkway, Druid Park Drive, and Wabash Avenue.
requirements_list: Projects must be located in or benefit Northwest Baltimore / Pimlico area communities
Projects must benefit the Park Heights Master Plan area or the surrounding 1-mile radius neighborhoods
85% of funds must be allocated to the Park Heights Master Plan area
15% of funds may be allocated to the surrounding one-mile radius neighborhoods
Applicants must be community partners, nonprofits, faith-based organizations, public schools, or city agencies
Nonprofit organizations must have IRS tax-exempt status (501(c)3) or a tax-exempt fiscal sponsor
Faith-based organizations must propose non-religious public benefit projects
Public schools must propose community-based projects benefiting students
Minimum award request: $25,000
Projects must be completed within two years from contract start
Funding is allocated through an annual spending plan approved by the Mayor and City Council
PCDA reviews proposals and makes recommendations to the Mayor
Funds are administered through city agencies or appropriate agencies contracting with community partners
Active grantees must submit quarterly reports on spending and project progress
Final reports are required when all funding has been spent and the project is closed
Applicants must formalize partnership through Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) where applicable
Active participation and designated organizational members required
Project scope, objectives, and goals must be clearly defined and aligned with measurable outcomes
Demonstrated applicant capacity and resources required
Applications must include a comprehensive budget with narrative and justification
Projects must address equity components and connect to community strategic priorities
Sustainability plan beyond the grant period required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application using the online form during the open application window (e.g., August 18 – September 29, 2025 for the FY27 round). Review guidelines and scoring rubric before applying. A cure period follows eligibility review (September 29 – October 6, 2025 for FY27). Each year, a proposed spending plan is developed and released for public comment (public comment period for FY27 closed December 30, 2025). The PCDA reviews applications and community feedback, publishes recommendations, and submits a letter of recommendations to the Mayor. The Mayor and City Council make final funding decisions as part of the City budget process. Once approved, funds are appropriated to designated city agencies or administered as grants or contracts with community partners. Recipients submit quarterly reports on their projects.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides a dumpster to support large-scale community cleanups in Baltimore City. Neighborhoods can request up to four dumpsters per year to collect debris from community cleanup events with 20 or more participants.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: DPW provides a dumpster for collected debris at community cleanup events. Each neighborhood may request up to four dumpsters per year, distributed in two periods: up to two dumpsters from January through June (requests open December 1), and up to two dumpsters from July through December (requests open June 1).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling; requests accepted starting December 1 for January–June events and June 1 for July–December events
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community groups and neighborhood organizations in Baltimore City with 20 or more volunteers planning a large-scale cleanup event
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Dumpster provided for debris collection during community cleanup events
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City residents and community groups only
requirements_list: Cleanup event must include at least 20 volunteers
A designated community organizer must lead and coordinate the event
An event flyer or official posting must be provided as proof of the cleanup event
Email event flyer to dpwpitchin@baltimorecity.gov after the event is confirmed
Submit request by calling 311
Dumpsters must be staffed at all times to prevent prohibited items from being placed inside
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 311 to submit a dumpster request during the appropriate request window (December 1 for January–June events; June 1 for July–December events). Provide an event flyer and confirm event date and location. The 311 team reviews the request to ensure the neighborhood has not exceeded the annual limit, then DPW finalizes approval and places the dumpster at the designated location.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free, voluntary, and confidential mediation program that helps resolve complaints between Baltimore City Police Officers and residents. Trained community mediators facilitate face-to-face dialogue to build understanding and improve police-community relations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free mediation sessions conducted by two trained mediators from Community Mediation Baltimore. Sessions are held in the resident's neighborhood, last no more than two hours, and may include multiple sessions if needed. No formal agreement is required as an outcome.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City residents who have filed a complaint with the Civilian Review Board involving abusive language, false arrest, false imprisonment, or harassment by a Baltimore City Police Officer
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Resolving complaints between residents and police officers through facilitated dialogue
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Baltimore City
requirements_list: Complaint must involve abusive language, false arrest, false imprisonment, or harassment filed with the Civilian Review Board
Complaint must be deemed eligible for mediation
Both the resident and the officer must voluntarily agree to participate
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: If a complaint is suitable for mediation, Community Mediation Baltimore contacts both the officer and the resident to ask if they are interested. If both agree, a session is scheduled at a time and location convenient for both parties.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Development, expansion, or revitalization of urban gardens in food priority areas.

Complete application required; incomplete applications may not be accepted

structured_extraction.program_name: Rapid COVID-19 Test Kit Distribution for Residential Behavioral Health Providers
structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore City Health Department (BCHD), in partnership with Behavioral Health System Baltimore (BHSB), distributes over-the-counter rapid COVID-19 antigen test kits to residential behavioral health providers in Baltimore City. The kits are intended to help providers quickly identify and isolate residents or staff who may have COVID-19.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: BCHD provides a limited supply of free over-the-counter rapid COVID-19 antigen test kits to eligible residential behavioral health providers. Providers can request kits by completing an online form. Additional supplies may become available but are not guaranteed.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed and/or accredited residential behavioral health providers located in Baltimore City, or behavioral health residential facilities that have coordinated COVID-19 care with BCHD's Outbreak Investigation Team. Intended to support residents and staff within those facilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rapid COVID-19 antigen test kits for testing symptomatic residents or staff, close contacts of COVID-positive individuals, and individuals in quarantine after an exposure within residential behavioral health programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a residential behavioral health provider located in Baltimore City, or a behavioral health residential facility that has coordinated COVID-19 care with BCHD's Outbreak Investigation Team.
requirements_list: Must be a licensed and/or accredited residential behavioral health provider located in Baltimore City, OR a behavioral health residential facility that has coordinated COVID-19 care with BCHD's Outbreak Investigation Team
Residents must self-administer tests; staff may proctor but cannot conduct, process, or interpret results without a CLIA waiver for COVID-19 testing
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the online request form linked on the page to request at-home COVID-19 test kits.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Rat Rubout program provides free rat inspection and baiting services to Baltimore City residents who have a rat problem. Pest control workers inspect the property and apply poisonous bait inside rat burrows to help eliminate rats.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free on-site rat inspection and baiting service. Pest control workers place poisonous bait deep inside rat burrows and mark treated burrows with yellow flags. Pesticides may also be used. Residents must submit a right-of-entry/release of liability form before workers can access private property.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City residential property occupants with rat infestations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rat inspection, extermination, and baiting on private property to eliminate rat infestations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only within Baltimore City, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a Baltimore City resident or residential property occupant
Property occupant must have yard control
Must complete and submit a right-of-entry/release of liability form before workers can enter private property
A rat burrow must be present for bait to be applied
Must clean yard and remove bulk items
Must not feed pets outside
Must obtain and use durable garbage cans with tight-fitting lids
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 311 or submit an online service request through the Baltimore 311 portal. Complete the permission/release of liability form with name, address, signature, and date; mail or fax to the Bureau of Solid Waste to allow workers onto private property.

It focuses on strengths-based case management, workforce development, housing, family reunification, and access to healthcare services including mental health, substance use, and co-occurring disorders.

Members help establish and implement evidence-based re-entry practices in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with lived experience as justice-involved persons, supporters of justice-involved persons, re-entry subject matter experts, and practitioners serving the re-entry population in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Establishing and implementing evidence-based re-entry practices including case management, workforce development, housing support, family reunification, and healthcare connectivity.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City
requirements_list: Lived experience as a justice-involved person and/or experience supporting a justice-involved person, OR subject matter expertise in re-entry best practices, OR current/previous experience serving the re-entry population, OR current/previous experience with the Second Chance Act
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online through the Mayor's Office of Government Relations' boards and commissions portal at https://www.baltimorecity.gov/boards-and-commissions-application.

structured_extraction.program_description: Monthly payment plans for past-due property taxes from 2025 and earlier, designed to help Baltimore City residents stay in good standing and avoid the annual tax sale. Homeowners can enroll online and choose monthly payments that fit their budget.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible homeowners can enroll in monthly payment plans to address past-due real property taxes from 2025 and earlier. Payments are broken into manageable monthly amounts chosen by the homeowner (for example, a $3,000 balance could be paid at $250 per month). Enrollment provides protection from the 2026 tax sale. Plans are administered through Promise, a secure payment plan provider.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City homeowners with past-due real property taxes from 2025 and earlier who want to avoid the 2026 tax sale.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment of past-due real property taxes owed to Baltimore City from 2025 and earlier.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only to property owners in Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Must be a Baltimore City homeowner
Must have past-due real property taxes from 2025 or earlier
Subject to pending legislation

structured_extraction.program_name: Request for Proposals & Request for Qualifications (RFP & RFQ) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore City's Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) uses RFP and RFQ processes to select developers or development teams for large urban revitalization projects. Developers are evaluated on their experience with urban revitalization, community engagement history, and financial and organizational capacity to complete complex projects. The program includes property disposition, negotiation, and development oversight processes for city-owned vacant buildings and land.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: DHCD solicits developers through competitive RFP and RFQ processes to redevelop city-owned vacant buildings and land. Selected developers receive the opportunity to purchase or lease city properties for rehabilitation and neighborhood revitalization projects through Exclusive Negotiating Privilege (ENP) and Land Disposition Agreements (LDA). Developer incentives may be provided (e.g., minimum $15,000 per property) to subsidize rehabilitation costs. Properties are generally offered in as-is condition with no city cash subsidies anticipated in standard RFPs, though specific solicitations may include incentive budgets. Selected respondents typically receive a 90-day ENP period followed by a formal developer agreement.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Varies by solicitation; past deadlines include November 22, 2024 (Vine Street RFQ), December 17, 2021 (Fall 2021 RFP), and November 11, 2020 (Fall 2020 RFP).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualified developers and development teams with significant experience in urban housing rehabilitation and revitalization, including minority- and women-owned business enterprises (MBE/WBE), seeking to redevelop vacant city-owned properties in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rehabilitation and redevelopment of vacant buildings and land for neighborhood improvement, affordable homeownership, and community revitalization. Eligible costs include hard and soft costs, pre-development financing, construction management, site/building design, permit approvals, exterior renovations, and marketing and community engagement.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only. Specific properties and neighborhoods vary by solicitation, including areas such as the 2100 Block of Vine Street in the Fayette Street Outreach (FSO) neighborhood in Southwest Baltimore.
requirements_list: Strong experience with urban revitalization
History of working effectively with communities
Financial capacity to complete large, complex projects
Organizational capacity to complete projects on time
Must be in good standing with State of Maryland, City of Baltimore, and U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD)
Letter of Interest signed by authorized principal; proposal valid for minimum 180 days
Project Description with preliminary conceptual vision
$250 application fee (certified mail, varies by solicitation)
$1,000 non-refundable fee upon ENP selection (certified check)
Evidence of insurance coverage required upon Right-of-Entry
Compliance with all Federal, State, and City laws, rules, and regulations
MBE/WBE participation requirements must be met
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Respond to individual RFP or RFQ solicitations posted by DHCD. Solicitations are issued periodically (e.g., fall cycles) for specific city-owned properties. Developers submit proposals with required fees and documentation. Selected respondents receive an Exclusive Negotiating Privilege (ENP) for 90 days, followed by a Land Disposition Agreement (LDA). Contact developmentinfo@baltimorecity.gov for current opportunities.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides a designated on-street parking space in front of or near the home of Baltimore City residents with permanent disabilities who have no accessible off-street parking and rely on a personal vehicle as their sole means of transportation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A reserved on-street parking space is assigned near the permit holder's residence. The Department of Transportation installs a sign marking the space within 4–6 weeks of approval. The permit must be renewed annually.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City residents with permanent disabilities that severely limit mobility, who have no accessible off-street parking and cannot use public transportation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Designated on-street residential parking space near the permit holder's home.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only to residents of Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Must have a permanent disability that severely limits mobility
Must not have accessible off-street parking (driveway, garage, or parking pad) on their property
Must be unable to use any form of public transportation or rely solely on a personal vehicle for transportation
Must obtain six signatures from homeowners on the same block
Must submit supporting medical documentation
Must complete a telephone interview after application review
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete the application form, then mail it to the Parking Authority at 211 N. Paca Street, Baltimore, MD 21201 (Attention: Reserved Residential Handicap Parking). A Parking Authority team member will contact you to request additional paperwork, including six neighbor signatures. After all documents are reviewed, a telephone interview will be scheduled. If approved, a parking space will be assigned and a sign installed within 4–6 weeks.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Resident Food Equity Advisors program brings together cohorts of Baltimore City residents to help shape equitable food policies. Each cohort focuses on a specific food equity issue, such as food access in public housing or small food retail. Residents apply, are selected based on passion and personal experience, attend six or more meetings, and are compensated for their time. Advisors provide input that is translated into policy recommendations presented to city officials and partners.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Selected advisors are compensated for their time attending six or more meetings. They receive briefings from subject matter experts, participate in facilitated discussions, and contribute to policy recommendations. After the cohort ends, advisors remain connected through the Food Policy Advisory Committee (Food PAC) and can seek ongoing support from City staff.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City residents with personal experience related to food equity issues, particularly those living in affected communities such as public housing.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Compensation for time spent attending cohort meetings and participating in food policy discussions and activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Baltimore City only.
requirements_list: Must be a Baltimore City resident
Must have passion for the food equity issue
Must have personal experience related to the cohort topic
Must be able to commit to attending 6+ meetings
Must be willing to engage in deep, continual dialogue
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Residents apply to participate in a cohort. Applicants are selected based on passion for the issue, personal experience, ability to commit, and willingness to engage in ongoing dialogue.

structured_extraction.program_description: RSVP matches retired older adults age 55 and over with volunteer opportunities at schools, science centers, aquariums, and other community organizations in Baltimore City. Volunteers share their knowledge, skills, and life experience with the community.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Year-round volunteer placement matching older adults with community organizations based on their interests and skills. No financial stipend is mentioned for this program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Retired adults age 55 and older in Baltimore City
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Volunteer placement at community organizations including schools, science centers, and aquariums
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City
requirements_list: Must be 55 years of age or older
Must pass a background check
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online through the volunteer portal or call (410) 361-9400 to learn more.

structured_extraction.program_name: Ryan White Part A HIV/AIDS Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore Ryan White Part A Program provides HIV-related medical and support services to people living with HIV who lack sufficient health care coverage or financial resources. The program fills gaps in care not covered by insurance, serving more than 10,000 people each year in Baltimore City and six surrounding counties.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides core medical services (outpatient and ambulatory care, oral health, health insurance premium and cost-sharing assistance, medical nutrition therapy, hospice, mental health, substance abuse outpatient care, and medical case management) and support services (outreach, medical transportation, substance abuse residential, legal, housing, psychosocial, child care, and food bank services) to eligible individuals living with HIV.
structured_extraction.program_audience: People living with HIV who do not have sufficient health care coverage or financial resources to cope with HIV disease, residing in Baltimore City and six surrounding counties (Baltimore County, Harford, Howard, Carroll, Anne Arundel, and Queen Anne's).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Core medical and support services for people living with HIV, including medical care, oral health, mental health, substance abuse treatment, case management, housing, legal services, transportation, and food bank services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City and six surrounding counties: Baltimore County, Harford, Howard, Carroll, Anne Arundel, and Queen Anne's.
requirements_list: Must be living with HIV
Must lack sufficient health care coverage or financial resources to cope with HIV disease
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Baltimore City Health Department or access services through funded agencies in the Baltimore Eligible Metropolitan Area (EMA).

structured_extraction.program_name: Safe City Baltimore: Immigrant Education and Defense Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: Safe City Baltimore provides education, legal assistance, and deportation defense services to immigrant communities in Baltimore. It funds Know Your Rights sessions, family safety planning, immigration screenings, coordination with pro bono lawyers, and deportation defense including rapid response services and bond assistance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides three levels of support: (1) Know Your Rights sessions, family safety plan preparation, and guidance on ICE arrests; (2) immigration screening clinics, coordination with pro bono legal providers, DOJ accreditation expansion, and help with immigration applications; (3) rapid response deportation defense, legal representation coordination, case management for families, and immigration bond assistance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Immigrant individuals and families in Baltimore City, particularly those at risk of deportation or in need of legal guidance on immigration rights.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Know Your Rights education, family safety planning, immigration legal screenings, pro bono legal coordination, deportation defense, case management, and immigration bond assistance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Mayor's Office of Immigrant Affairs at mima@baltimorecity.gov to request help through the program.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: MOED and MONSE case managers coordinate plans with participants, including going behind the wall monthly to meet with individuals returning to Baltimore City.

structured_extraction.program_name: Senior Assisted Living Group Home Subsidy Program (Baltimore City)
structured_extraction.program_description: This community-based housing subsidy program helps medically and financially eligible older adults over the age of 62 pay for assisted living in facilities that have a contract with the City of Baltimore.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Housing subsidy for eligible older adults residing in assisted living facilities that have a contract with the City of Baltimore.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Medically and financially eligible older adults over age 62 in Baltimore City who reside in contracted assisted living facilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Subsidized assisted living costs in contracted group home facilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City residents only; must reside in an assisted living facility with a City of Baltimore contract.
requirements_list: Must be over 62 years of age
Must meet medical eligibility criteria
Must meet financial eligibility criteria
Must reside in an assisted living facility that has a contract with the City of Baltimore
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 410-396-2273 for more information.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Access to health, fitness, and social activities at 13 senior center locations across Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Older adults in Baltimore City
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Health and fitness programs and social activities at senior centers
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 410-396-1337 to learn more.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Senior Companion Program (SCP) places older adult volunteers in the homes of homebound seniors to provide companionship and help them remain independent in the community. Volunteers provide regularly scheduled in-home social visits to homebound older adults who are unable to participate in community-based social activities. Volunteers receive a small hourly stipend and a monthly bus pass for their service; the stipend does not affect Social Security benefits. Volunteers may choose their own hours.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Volunteers receive a small hourly stipend and a monthly bus pass for providing in-home companionship visits to homebound seniors. The stipend does not affect Social Security benefits. Volunteers may choose their own hours. Homebound seniors receive regularly scheduled in-home social visits from older adult volunteers to provide companionship and socialization.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Retired adults age 55 and older in Baltimore City who want to volunteer in a one-on-one home setting, and homebound older adults in Baltimore City who are unable to participate in community-based social opportunities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Stipend and bus pass provided to volunteers visiting homebound seniors; in-home social companionship visits and socialization provided to homebound older adults.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City residents only.
requirements_list: Must be 55 years of age or older (for volunteers)
Must pass a background check (for volunteers)
Must be an older adult
Must be homebound and unable to participate in community-based social activities (for recipients)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online through the volunteer portal or call (410) 396-2273 to learn more. Homebound seniors seeking visits should also call 410-396-2273 for more information.

Attorneys advise and represent clients on a wide range of civil legal matters including estate planning, consumer and debt collection issues, landlord/tenant disputes, housing matters, foreclosure prevention, probate, and guardianship.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free (pro-bono) civil legal advice and representation for older adults over age 60 in Baltimore City, covering estate planning, housing, foreclosure prevention, probate, guardianship, and consumer issues.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults over the age of 60 in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Civil legal services including estate planning, consumer and debt issues, landlord/tenant disputes, housing, foreclosure prevention, probate, and guardianship.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City
requirements_list: Must be over age 60
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 410-396-1322 or visit the Senior Legal Services website at baltimoreseniorlegalservices.org for more information.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Details about the type or amount of assistance provided through the Service Line Partnership are not described on this page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City residents or property owners with service line needs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available within Baltimore City.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore City Department of Public Works (DPW) provides free professional cleaning, disinfection, and disposal services to residential customers whose homes are damaged by sewage backups caused by capacity-related wet-weather events (heavy or sustained rain). DPW-contracted cleaning professionals remove sewage, disinfect and clean affected areas, dispose of damaged materials (including soiled carpet, flooring, and furniture), deodorize, and dehumidify/dry affected areas at no cost to eligible Baltimore City residential customers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free on-site sewage cleanup services provided by DPW-contracted professional cleaning vendors at no cost to eligible residential customers. Services include removal of sewage, cleaning and disinfection of affected areas, removal and disposal of soiled carpet, flooring, and furniture, deodorization, and dehumidification/drying. Available for both single-family and multi-family residential properties.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners, residents, and tenants of residential properties (single-family or multi-family) in Baltimore City whose homes have been damaged by sewage backups caused by capacity-related wet-weather events.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Professional cleaning, disinfection, disposal of damaged materials (including soiled carpet, flooring, and furniture), deodorization, and dehumidification/drying of residential property damaged by a sewage backup from a capacity-related wet-weather event.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only to residential properties located within Baltimore City. Commercial properties are explicitly excluded.
requirements_list: Must be an owner, resident, or tenant of a residential property (single-family or multi-family) in Baltimore City.

Damage must be caused by a backup that occurred during a capacity-related wet-weather event (at least ¼ inch of precipitation recorded within a 24-hour period causing sewer lines to surcharge or overflow).
The residential property owner, tenant, or property manager must call 311 or visit the Baltimore City 311-services page to report the damage to DPW as soon as it is discovered.
DPW must send an inspector to confirm the backup was caused by a capacity-related wet-weather event.
Eligibility is limited to either the SOS Cleanup Program or the Expedited Reimbursement Program for Sewage Backups — not both.
Does not apply to non-wet weather backups (e.g., dry weather blockages, clogs from wet wipes, roots, fats, oil, and grease, water main breaks, or maintenance-related issues).
Commercial properties are not eligible.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Call 311 or visit 311.baltimorecity.gov to report the sewage backup to DPW as soon as it is discovered. Step 2: DPW sends an inspector to determine the cause of the backup. Step 3: Inspector confirms the backup is due to a capacity-related wet-weather event. Step 4: DPW dispatches contracted cleaning professionals to the property; contractor contacts resident within approximately one hour to schedule and complete services.

structured_extraction.program_description: Allows property owners adjacent to city-owned vacant lots in Baltimore City to purchase those lots at a fixed price. Buyers can transform the lot into a garden, parking pad, deck, or expanded yard, helping to improve their property and beautify their neighborhood.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible property owners can purchase adjacent city-owned vacant lots at a fixed price for lots up to 1,500 square feet. Lots larger than 1,500 square feet are subject to additional cost per square foot and additional review. The maximum lot size is 5,000 square feet. Payment must be made by certified check, money order, or cashier's check. Some properties carry an annual ground rent that becomes the buyer's responsibility after settlement.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners whose principal residence is physically adjacent to a city-owned vacant lot in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of an adjacent vacant city-owned lot for use as a garden, landscaping, fencing, driveway, or expansion of existing property.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only within Baltimore City for lots that are city-owned and adjacent to the applicant's principal residence.
requirements_list: The side yard property must be vacant and unimproved.
The side yard property must be physically contiguous to the applicant's principal residence; priority given to owner-occupants.
The side yard property must consist of no more than two lots incapable of independent development as determined by local zoning and code enforcement.
Fixed pricing applies only to lots up to 1,500 square feet; lots over 1,500 SF require additional cost per square foot and review; maximum size is 5,000 SF.
The applicant must have a record of responsible property ownership and management.
Intended use must comply with Baltimore City laws and regulations.
Some uses may require Zoning approval.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a completed application including a disclosure of intended uses. DHCD reviews the application and makes an award decision within approximately 30 days. If approved, Board of Estimates approval takes approximately 45 days, followed by settlement within approximately 45 days (total estimated 120 days). Upon approval, submit a certified check, money order, or cashier's check for the full purchase amount. Settlement must occur within 60 days of an executed Land Disposition Agreement.

structured_extraction.program_description: Side-Step was a pre-arrest youth diversion program providing an alternative to formal justice system involvement for youth ages 10-17. The program focused on community outreach, violence prevention, and educational opportunities as proactive strategies to address risk factors such as poverty, exposure to violence, and unstable family or housing situations. It connected youth to supportive services promoting positive development and community engagement.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Pre-arrest diversion and wraparound support services for youth ages 10-17, including community outreach, violence prevention programming, educational opportunities, and connections to supportive services. The pilot launched in January 2022 in Baltimore Police Department's Western District and ended in 2024.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Youth ages 10-17 at risk of justice system involvement in Baltimore City
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Diversion from formal justice system involvement; access to community support services, educational opportunities, and conflict resolution resources
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City (piloted in BPD's Western District)
requirements_list: Youth must be ages 10-17
Must be eligible for pre-arrest diversion from the formal juvenile justice system
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: MONSE accepts referrals for young people who may have a history of engagement with the juvenile justice system.

structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to businesses within Baltimore City.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides free technical assistance, training, counseling, and resources to small businesses and entrepreneurs in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free workshops and counseling on business planning, accounting, minority business development, cash flow planning, and business operations.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business planning, marketplace strategy, cash flow management, operations planning

Services include tax credit assistance, permit assistance, facade improvement grants for vacant small commercial properties, assistance for locally-owned businesses seeking a commercial storefront, and small business loans and micro-loans.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: BDC provides tax credit assistance, permit assistance, city agency coordination, facade improvement grants for vacant small commercial properties needing total redevelopment, assistance for locally-owned businesses seeking a commercial storefront, and small business loans and micro-loans for new, expanding, or relocating businesses.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rehabilitation and development of commercial spaces in Baltimore City neighborhood commercial areas; facade improvements; business startup, expansion, or relocation costs.

Facade improvement grants are for vacant small commercial properties in need of total redevelopment
Loans available for new, expanding, or relocating businesses

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides Baltimore City residents with a legal and affordable way to dispose of waste at the Quarantine Road Landfill, helping to reduce illegal dumping across the city. Residents must obtain a permit through the Health Department.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Flat fee of $20 for vehicles up to 7,000 pounds gross weight, with an additional charge of $3.38 per 100 pounds beyond 7,000 pounds, for waste disposal at the Quarantine Road Landfill.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City residents who need to dispose of household or bulk waste legally and affordably.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Disposal of household trash, furniture, appliances, scrap metal, glass, plastics, paper, cardboard, electronics, used oil, yard waste, limited tires, and building materials at the Quarantine Road Landfill.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Baltimore City residents only.
requirements_list: Must be a Baltimore City resident
Must obtain a permit through the Baltimore City Health Department
Vehicle must be used for personal, non-commercial waste disposal
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Obtain a permit through the Baltimore City Health Department, then bring waste to the Quarantine Road Landfill during operating hours (Monday–Saturday, 7:30 AM–3:30 PM).

structured_extraction.program_name: Solicitation for Housing Quality Standard (HQS) Inspection Services
structured_extraction.program_description: The Mayor's Office of Homeless Services (MOHS) awards grants to organizations that provide Housing Quality Standard (HQS) inspection services for housing units occupied by homeless and HIV/AIDS-affected clients receiving rental assistance through the Continuum of Care (CoC) and Housing Opportunities for Persons with AIDS (HOPWA) programs. Inspectors conduct initial, annual, complaint, quality control, and re-inspections on behalf of MOHS. Expected 2,475 housing inspections annually across CoC and HOPWA projects covering traditional apartments, attached and detached homes, single occupancy, studio, and 1-5 bedroom units across Baltimore City.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Selected applicants may receive an award between $100,000 and $400,000 depending on project type (CoC or HOPWA). Each project is considered a separate award, but applicants may submit a combined application and budget for both. Contract term is one year: July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2023. Reimbursement is provided monthly for approved expenses including salary/fringe for HQS inspection staff, transportation costs, administrative costs, and other financial resources needed for project implementation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations that provide housing inspection services, including nonprofits and for-profit firms with current housing inspection and lead-based paint inspection licenses, with demonstrated experience managing federal funding and serving individuals experiencing homelessness.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Providing HQS inspection services including initial, annual, client complaint, quality control, and failed unit re-inspections for housing units occupied by CoC and HOPWA program clients. Allowable costs include salary/fringe for HQS inspection staff, transportation costs, stationery, necessary equipment, administrative costs, and other related expenses for service delivery.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Services are provided in Baltimore City on behalf of MOHS.
requirements_list: Submit Housing Quality Standard Inspection Services Application
Submit project budget (6-month and 1-year; template provided) with detailed line items
Provide Articles of Incorporation and Bylaws
Provide current Certificate of Good Standing from the State of Maryland
Provide Federal Tax Exemption Determination Letter (if applicable)
Provide copy of current housing inspection and lead-based paint housing inspection licenses
Provide Professional Liability/Errors and Omissions Insurance documentation
Provide list of Board of Directors/Project Organizational Chart with name, title, email, and phone for each staff position
Provide most recent single audit or independent financial audit
Demonstrated experience managing federal funding
Experience providing HQS inspection services
Qualified staff with HQS certifications and cultural competency training
Adequate financial accounting system
Ability to submit monthly cost reimbursement invoices
Ability to meet program expenses in advance of reimbursement
Work plan and staffing plan documentation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit all required documents including the completed application, project budget using the provided template, organizational documents, licenses, and financial audit. Applications were due by March 11, 2022 at 5:00 pm. A Bidder's Conference was held on February 8, 2022.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tools, gloves, bags, and pickers provided for litter cleanup; debris collection by DPW after the event

requirements_list: Cleanup event must have fewer than 20 participants
Residents must register for the program

structured_extraction.program_name: Staying Alive Overdose Response Program (Naloxone Training and Distribution)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Staying Alive Program is an Overdose Response Program (ORP) administered by Baltimore City Health Department (BCHD) and its partners. It trains individuals to recognize the signs and symptoms of opioid overdose and respond appropriately, and distributes free naloxone (Narcan) kits to people at high risk of opioid overdose. The program operates through the Syringe Exchange Program and offers training at treatment centers, syringe exchange sites, the Baltimore City Detention Center, and via live virtual community sessions and video. Between 2015 and 2023, the program trained more than 155,000 residents and helped save more than 18,000 lives. Between 2023 and 2025, nearly 26,000 naloxone kits were distributed, with over 38,000 kits and 43,000 residents trained since 2015. Training is available to individuals with substance use disorders, inmates, drug treatment clients, healthcare providers, correctional staff, and third-party community members. Naloxone is also accessible at various treatment centers and facilities throughout Baltimore City, and can be purchased at a Maryland pharmacy without a prescription.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free naloxone (Narcan) kits and overdose prevention education and training are provided at no cost to Baltimore City residents. Nearly 26,000 naloxone kits were distributed between 2023 and 2025, with over 38,000 kits distributed and over 43,000 residents trained since 2015. Training covers recognition of signs and symptoms of opioid overdose and appropriate response. Training is available via live virtual community sessions, video, and in-person request through a Naloxone Training Request Form. Naloxone is also accessible at various treatment centers and Syringe Exchange Program (SEP) sites throughout Baltimore City, and can be purchased at a Maryland pharmacy without a prescription.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City residents at high risk of opioid overdose, people with substance use disorders, their families and bystanders, individuals recently released from jail, prison, rehab, detox, or hospital, healthcare providers, correctional staff, inmates, drug treatment clients, and community members who want to be prepared to respond to opioid overdoses
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Naloxone (Narcan) kits provided free of charge for use in reversing opioid overdoses, and overdose response education and training to enable residents to recognize and respond to opioid overdoses
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Baltimore City only.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Request a naloxone kit using the online Naloxone Kit Request Form, call 443-615-7792 to request free Narcan kits, or attend a live virtual community naloxone training by registering through Eventbrite. In-person training can also be requested via the Naloxone Training Request Form through Google Forms. Training is also offered at various treatment centers, Syringe Exchange Program (SEP) sites, and the Baltimore City Detention Center throughout Baltimore City. Naloxone is also available at treatment centers and other facilities throughout Baltimore City, or can be purchased at a Maryland pharmacy without a prescription. For substance use disorder treatment referrals, call the Crisis Information and Referral Line at 410-433-5175. To report naloxone use, contact the Poison Center at 1-888-222-1222.

structured_extraction.program_name: Stormwater Fee Credit for Non-Single-Family Properties
structured_extraction.program_description: Businesses, churches, non-profits, industries, and other non-single-family property owners in Baltimore City can earn credits or reductions on their stormwater remediation fee by installing stormwater best management practices (BMPs), qualifying for green space or small development credits, holding an NPDES industrial stormwater permit, maintaining private storm drains, or meeting other qualifying conditions related to impervious area or property characteristics.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Credits or reductions applied to the stormwater remediation fee. Multiple credit types are available: Participation credit (up to $10/4hrs/year), Treatment Practice credit (up to 45%), Green Space credit (up to 45%) for lots with less than 50 sq ft of impervious area, Small Development credit (up to 33%) for lots up to 820 sq ft of impervious area, NPDES Industrial Stormwater Discharge Permit credit (55%), Harbor Discharge credit (up to 30%) for owners of private storm drains discharging directly to Baltimore Harbor, Activity-Based BMPs credit (up to 45%), Religious Structure special fee ($1/ERU/month), and property tax cap (20% of real property taxes). Credit renewal applications must be received within 30 days before the end of the credit period.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Credit renewal applications must be received within 30 days before end of credit period
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses, churches, non-profits, industries, and other non-single-family property owners in Baltimore City seeking to reduce their stormwater remediation fee.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of the stormwater remediation fee charged on the property by qualifying through stormwater management practices, property characteristics, or other eligible criteria.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only within Baltimore City. Off-site treatment practices must be located within 8-digit watersheds in Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Must own a non-single-family property in Baltimore City

Must meet one of the qualifying criteria: BMP installation and maintenance, green space (less than 50 sq ft of impervious area), small development (up to 820 sq ft of impervious area), NPDES Industrial Stormwater Discharge Permit, private storm drains discharging to Baltimore Harbor, or privately maintained cemetery streets open to the public
Must submit a stormwater fee credit application with supporting documentation
BMPs must be installed and application approved before credit is issued
For religious structure special fee: proof of tax-exempt religious status and property map required
For property tax cap: copy of recent City and State real property tax bills required
For green space credit: photo documentation of vacant parcel required
Credit renewal applications must be received within 30 days before end of credit period
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete the Non-Single Family Property Guidance Document, which includes the credit application form and instructions, then submit the completed application with required supporting documentation to the Baltimore City Department of Public Works, Bureau of Water and Wastewater.

structured_extraction.program_name: Stormwater Fee Credit for Single-Family Properties
structured_extraction.program_description: Single-family property owners in Baltimore City can reduce their stormwater fee by volunteering for community water quality activities (such as tree planting and trash clean-ups) or by installing and maintaining stormwater best management practices (BMPs) such as rain gardens, rain barrels, and trees. Credits are applied to the property's stormwater fee based on the type and scale of practices installed or volunteer hours earned.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A credit applied to the property's stormwater fee in exchange for installing qualifying stormwater treatment practices or volunteering in organized community water quality activities. Credit amounts: Participation in certified public projects ($10 per 4 hours, max $30/year); Tree planting ($5/tree/year, minimum 2 trees); Rain barrels ($25, one-time); Small rain garden ($8/year); Large rain garden ($16/year); Other BMPs (up to 45% of fee). Certificates can be gifted to other Baltimore City residents. Credits can be combined for households.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Single-family property owners in Baltimore City who want to reduce their stormwater fee.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of the stormwater remediation fee charged on the property by installing stormwater management practices (trees, rain gardens, rain barrels) or participating in volunteer water quality/stormwater clean-up activities to reduce stormwater runoff and improve water quality.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only within Baltimore City. Must own a single-family property in Baltimore City or pay a Baltimore City water bill.
requirements_list: Must be a single-family property owner in Baltimore City
Must install qualifying stormwater treatment practices (e.g., trees, rain gardens, rain barrels) or volunteer in organized water quality/stormwater events

Must complete and submit the Stormwater Fee Credit Single-Family Application with required attachments (photo of BMP, sketch showing BMP location, executed right-of-entry agreement if applicable, maintenance documentation for renewals, certificates of event participation)
For participation credits: minimum 4 hours of volunteering at City-certified events
For rain gardens: minimum size requirements (50-100 sq ft) and drainage area requirements (500-1,000 sq ft)
For tree planting: minimum 2 trees, planted after 2010, 1+ inch diameter, conforming to City guidelines
For rain barrels: minimum 50 gallons storage capacity
Must execute right-of-entry agreement for BMPs
Photo documentation and maintenance documentation required
Must maintain BMPs properly; improper maintenance may result in credit rescission
Full stormwater fee must be paid during application review period
To register a volunteer community cleanup event, call 311
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and submit the Stormwater Fee Credit Single-Family Application with supporting documentation to the Bureau of Water and Wastewater, Abel Wolman Municipal Building, 200 Holliday Street, Room 404, or email to publicworks@baltimorecity.gov. For volunteer credits, call 311 to register a Stormwater Participation Event, participate in the cleanup, receive a certificate via email/mail, and include the certificate with the application. Applications are reviewed within 30 days of receipt of a complete package. Download the Single Family Property Guidance Document for detailed instructions.

structured_extraction.program_name: Stormwater Fee Hardship Exemption and Alternative Compliance Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Tax-exempt organizations in Baltimore City that face financial hardship can apply for an exemption from the stormwater fee by submitting an alternative compliance plan. The plan outlines how organizations will reduce stormwater runoff and pollution in ways that work for them, protecting the environment and lessening the burden on the City's storm sewer system. Faith organizations may also qualify for a stormwater fee reduction for places of worship and schools. The program was established in 2012 by the Maryland Legislature mandating stormwater fees in the 10 largest jurisdictions including Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A full or partial exemption from the stormwater remediation fee for eligible tax-exempt organizations that submit and implement an approved alternative compliance plan demonstrating stormwater runoff reduction and pollution prevention practices. To qualify for hardship exemption, the annual stormwater fee must exceed 0.75% of the organization's total annual revenue, and total annual revenue must not exceed $1,000,000. Faith organizations can also receive a stormwater fee reduction for places of worship and schools, with religious structures capped at $1/ERU/month. Multiple credit types are available: green space (45%), small development (33%), treatment practices (up to 45%), participation, NPDES industrial permit (55%), and harbor discharger (30%). Maximum fee cap is 20% of annual real property taxes.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Renewal required 30 days before exemption period ends; no specific application deadline
structured_extraction.program_audience: Tax-exempt nonprofits, religious organizations, and non-single family property owners in Baltimore City with stormwater fees exceeding 0.75% of annual revenue.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Exemption from the stormwater remediation fee in exchange for implementing stormwater runoff reduction and pollution control practices as part of an alternative compliance plan, including BMP installation/maintenance, outreach/education activities, green care practices, and lawn management.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only within Baltimore City. Off-site BMPs must be in the same 8-digit watershed.
requirements_list: Must be a tax-exempt organization located in Baltimore City
Must demonstrate financial hardship
Annual stormwater fee must exceed 0.75% of total annual revenue
Organization's total annual revenue must not exceed $1,000,000
Must have current IRS tax-exempt status under IRC § 501(c)(3), (d), (4), or (19)
Must own property or have a current lease indicating responsibility for water/sewer charges
Must submit and implement an approved Alternative Compliance Plan demonstrating stormwater runoff reduction and pollution prevention/control measures
Faith organizations may qualify for a reduction for places of worship and schools
Submit completed application with supporting documentation
Execute inspection and maintenance agreement for BMP credits
Provide proof of eligibility (tax bills, permits, surveys, engineering drawings as applicable)
Maintain credit status through renewals every 5 years
Allow Department inspection at least once every 3 years
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete the Hardship Exemption and Alternative Compliance Program Plan form and submit it to the Department of Public Works. Refer to the Non-Single Family Property Guidance Document for more information and the application. Applications undergo a 30-day review period. Renewals must be submitted 30 days before the exemption period ends.

structured_extraction.program_name: Stormwater Fee Reduction for Faith Organizations
structured_extraction.program_description: Fee reduction program for religious non-profits in Baltimore City, capping stormwater fees at $1/ERU/month for structures used exclusively for places of worship or K-12 education. Part of the broader Maryland Stormwater Fee Reduction program for Non-Single Family Properties.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reduces stormwater fee from standard rate to $1/ERU/month for qualifying religious structures used exclusively for places of worship or K-12 education. Religious Structure Fee Reduction is capped at 20% of property tax. Credits can be combined up to 100% of base fee. Additional credits available for treatment practices (up to 45%), green space (up to 45%), direct harbor discharge (up to 30%), and NPDES industrial permit (up to 55%).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Faith-based organizations and religious non-profits operating in Baltimore City
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of stormwater management fees for eligible religious structures
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City; for off-site treatment credits, property must be in the same 8-digit watershed
requirements_list: Organization must be a religious non-profit exempt from State or City property tax
Must be located in Baltimore City
Structures must be used exclusively for places of worship or K-12 education
Must submit a property map identifying structures eligible for discounted rate

structured_extraction.program_description: The Supporting Our Students (SOS) Project is a school-based violence prevention initiative targeting 9th graders in Baltimore City schools located in or near Safe Streets Outposts. The project also includes school-wide awareness events, after-school clubs, and a multi-sector advisory committee of school, community, youth, and parent partners to guide and sustain the effort. A resource list of dating violence prevention and support services is also available for teens and young people, including 24/7 hotlines, crisis intervention, counseling, legal resources, and peer advocacy.

Additional dating violence resources include 24/7 hotline support, crisis intervention, counseling, legal resources, and peer advocacy for teens in unhealthy or unsafe relationships.

structured_extraction.program_description: Tax Increment Financing (TIF) bonds are financial tools used by Baltimore City to fund development projects within designated TIF districts. When a developer invests in a TIF district, property values are expected to rise. The increase in property tax revenue generated by that development is set aside to repay the bonds. Once the debt is repaid, the TIF district is dissolved and the increased tax revenue flows into the City's general fund. The program is also used to finance infrastructure improvements, mixed-income housing redevelopment, and neighborhood revitalization efforts, including public improvements such as roads, utilities, parks, and schools within designated development districts. A key application is the Vacancy Reduction and Affordable Housing TIF, part of Mayor Scott's $3 billion Vacancy Reduction Initiative (VRI) announced December 2023, targeting Baltimore's ~13,000 vacant buildings. This sub-program issues up to $150 million in TIF bonds (four series: A, B, C, D) to finance rehabilitation of vacant residential properties and affordable housing development (up to 115% AMI) across 4,285 properties in 126 neighborhoods. Specific focus areas include the Perkins Somerset Oldtown (PSO) Neighborhoods, supporting multi-phase mixed-use development including residential apartments, commercial retail/office space, parking, and institutional improvements such as school renovations. A fiscal impact analysis projects revenues, expenses, and net fiscal impact to the City of Baltimore over a 35-year period (2018-2052) for the PSO district, and a projected net fiscal impact of $732.7 million through bond term (2066) for the Vacancy Reduction TIF, assuming 3,560 total residential units rehabilitated at 200 units annually (2025-2040).
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The City issues TIF bonds to fund development projects within a designated TIF district. The bonds are repaid using the incremental increase in property tax revenue generated by rising property values within the district. For the Vacancy Reduction and Affordable Housing TIF: up to $150 million in bonds issued in four series (A, B, C, D) to finance rehabilitation of vacant residential properties and affordable housing development. Average TIF subsidy: approximately $16,758 for rehabilitation of a vacant unit and $44,758 for infill construction of a vacant lot. Developer profit capped at 12% of total development costs. Recommended funding ratio for developer-sponsored projects: 8:1 to 12:1 (non-City to City funding). Up to $50,000 per property (average award) through the Developer Incentive Program. Park Heights Phase 2 infrastructure: $11.37 million. Total projected revenues: $1,334,662,504; total projected expenses: $1,073,942,357; projected net fiscal impact to City: $732,742,756. For the PSO TIF: total bond proceeds across multiple series approximately $101.6 million (Series A: $13,372,000; Series B: $73,012,000; Series C: $15,225,000 at 5.50% interest, 30-year maturity). TIF proceeds fund public infrastructure improvements including roads, streetlighting, water/sewer systems, parks, streetscaping, school construction/renovation, and other community facilities. Special taxes on Development District parcels are available in the event of a shortfall. Enterprise Zone Tax Credits are also available for qualifying commercial/office properties within the district: 80% credit on increased assessment for first 5 years, declining by 10% annually in years 6-10. Developers must submit a TIF bond application to the Board of Finance detailing the proposed district and projected property value increases. Leveraged with State Project C.O.R.E. Funds ($50 million annually) and other private/public funds.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Alice Kennedy, Housing Commissioner; Stacy Freed
structured_extraction.program_audience: Developers seeking financing for development projects within designated Baltimore City TIF districts, including mixed-income housing developers, commercial real estate developers, community development corporations (CDCs), non-profits, minority and women-owned businesses, and individual primary homebuyers. Also serves low-to-moderate income households (30% AMI, 60% AMI, 80% AMI, up to 115% AMI, and market-rate), public housing residents, first-time homebuyers, renters, and workforce development participants within targeted neighborhoods. Additionally serves City of Baltimore departments and fiscal planning officials. Special focus on seniors, legacy Baltimore residents, Black middle-income families, and immigrant families in formerly redlined neighborhoods.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding development projects within a designated TIF district area, including: rehabilitation and new construction of vacant residential properties; hard construction costs for rental and for-sale housing (up to 115% AMI); appraisal gap and affordability gap financing; public infrastructure improvements (roads, sidewalks, utilities, streetlighting, water/sewer systems, stormwater upgrades, street trees, bus stops); school construction and renovation (e.g., City Springs School, Dunbar Middle School renovation); parks and recreation centers; streetscape enhancements; façade improvements; mixed-income housing construction (deeply affordable at 30% AMI, workforce/affordable at 60% and 80% AMI, and market-rate units); commercial and retail space development; office space development; parking facilities; adaptive reuse/facility expansions; site demolition and clearance; design and engineering fees; project management; contingency reserves; property acquisition and disposition; homebuyer down-payment grants/loans; developer incentives; vacancy prevention support; and municipal service delivery costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available within designated TIF districts in Baltimore City. The Vacancy Reduction and Affordable Housing TIF District consists of 4,285 properties across 126 Baltimore City neighborhoods, including Impact Investment Areas (IIAs) concentrated in East Baltimore, West Baltimore, and Park Heights (87% of vacant buildings). Specific Impact Investment Areas include: East (Broadway East, Coldstream Homestead Montebello, East Baltimore Midway, Johnston Square), Park Heights, Southwest, and West. Specific neighborhoods include Sandtown-Winchester, Midtown-Edmondson, Oliver, Mondawmin, Penn North, Walbrook, Upton, Pigtown/Washington Village, Brooklyn, and 100+ additional neighborhoods. Also includes the Perkins Somerset Oldtown (PSO) Development District (~200-acre area combining Perkins, Pleasant View Gardens, Somerset, and Oldtown/McElderry neighborhoods, bounded by Monument Street to the north, Eastern Avenue to the south, Little Italy/Jonestown to the west, and Broadway to the east). Enterprise Zone Tax Credit eligibility applies to commercial properties within designated Enterprise Zone or Empowerment Zone boundaries within the district.
