structured_extraction.program_name: TreeBaltimore (Yard Tree Adoption Program & Free Tree Giveaways)
structured_extraction.program_description: TreeBaltimore is a Baltimore City program that grows and cares for the urban tree canopy, working toward a citywide goal of 40% tree canopy cover. It offers free 1-gallon trees to residents, businesses, and institutions at seasonal giveaway events each spring and fall at farmer's markets, parks, and local events. TreeBaltimore also orders and delivers trees to large private and public properties such as schools, apartment buildings, hospitals, and places of worship. Neighborhood groups can order a minimum of 10 trees (free for Healthy Neighborhoods, $10/tree otherwise) for yard placement through the TreeNeighborhood Group Order Form. Discount tree coupons are available ($10 from the Growing Home Campaign or $25 from the Marylanders Plant Trees campaign). The Forestry Division also plants street trees on the street right-of-way at the request of property owners. Tree Steward training classes are offered through Recreation and Parks, along with volunteer planting and care workdays. Residents and community groups can also arrange to host a tree giveaway at their own event.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free 1-gallon trees are distributed at seasonal giveaway events (spring and fall) at farmer's markets, parks, and local events throughout Baltimore City. Neighborhood groups can order a minimum of 10 trees (free for Healthy Neighborhoods participants, $10/tree for others) in flowering or shade varieties for front or back yards. TreeBaltimore also orders and delivers trees to large private and public properties such as schools, apartment buildings, hospitals, industrial areas, colleges, places of worship, vacant lots, and public housing. The Forestry Division plants street trees in existing or new tree pits on the street right-of-way at no cost; applicants may pay for new pit creation and must water trees 20 gallons once or twice weekly from May through October for a minimum of 2 years. Trees must meet specific caliper requirements (1½-inch minimum for street/pedestrian areas; ½-inch minimum for parks). Discount tree coupons are available ($10 from the Growing Home Campaign or $25 from the Marylanders Plant Trees campaign). Tree Steward training classes are offered through Recreation and Parks, along with volunteer planting and care workdays.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property acquisition and renovation/rehabilitation of a formerly vacant home in Baltimore City

structured_extraction.program_description: The Virtual Supermarket Program works with communities and grocery stores to help residents, especially older adults in senior and disabled housing, access healthy foods through online grocery shopping. Trained community members called Neighborhood Food Advocates teach Baltimore residents online grocery ordering skills and community organizing to improve local food access and encourage healthy eating.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Program staff and trained Neighborhood Food Advocates teach participants online grocery shopping skills and community organizing to improve access to healthy foods. The program currently focuses on older adults living in senior and disabled housing in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Older adults and residents in Baltimore City who lack sufficient access to healthy foods, particularly those living in senior or disabled housing.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Access to online grocery shopping assistance and food access community organizing training.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City residents only.
requirements_list: Must be a Baltimore City resident
Primarily targets older adults living in senior/disabled housing

structured_extraction.program_description: Vision for Baltimore provides free vision screenings, eye exams, and eyeglasses to pre-kindergarten through 8th-grade students in Baltimore City Public Schools. The Baltimore City Health Department screens all students, and those who fail are offered a full eye exam in a mobile vision clinic operated by Vision To Learn. Students who need glasses receive them at no cost, delivered directly to their school.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free vision screenings, eye exams in a mobile clinic, and eyeglasses are provided to eligible students at no out-of-pocket cost to families. If a student is enrolled in Medicaid, the Medicaid provider may be billed. Eyeglasses are donated by Warby Parker.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Pre-kindergarten through 8th-grade students enrolled in Baltimore City Public Schools
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Vision screenings, eye exams, and eyeglasses for eligible students
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only at select Baltimore City Public Schools elementary and middle schools; approximately 45 schools served per year
requirements_list: Student must be enrolled in Baltimore City Public Schools in pre-K through 8th grade
Parent or guardian must sign and return a consent form for the student to receive an eye exam and glasses
No insurance required; all students served regardless of ability to pay
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: No registration is required. Parents receive a universal consent form at the start of the school year and must sign it to allow their child to receive an eye exam. Once the form is returned, the child participates when the mobile clinic visits their school.

structured_extraction.program_name: Wage Subsidy Program for Port-Impacted Small Businesses
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides wage subsidies to help Port-impacted small businesses keep their employees on payroll, maintain health benefits, and stay attached to their employers following the Key Bridge collapse.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible businesses receive $7,500 per worker in subsidy payments, up to $22,500 or 3 months of assistance per worker (up to 3 workers) per business. The City has committed an initial $1 million, with an additional $1 million under consideration. Apply at: https://airtable.com/applWOF2isbilP7sE/shrduwi9MC8r8buZh
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses impacted by the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse and Port of Baltimore closure, and their affected workers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Keeping employees on payroll, retaining or rehiring workers, and maintaining employee health benefits.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to port-impacted small businesses in Baltimore City, Baltimore County, and Anne Arundel County.
requirements_list: Business must be impacted by the Key Bridge collapse and Port of Baltimore closure
Business must be classified as a small business
Employees must be port-impacted workers
Employer must maintain affected workers on payroll
Maximum of 3 workers per business eligible for subsidy
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at https://airtable.com/applWOF2isbilP7sE/shrduwi9MC8r8buZh

structured_extraction.program_description: Gives site stewards of City-owned and privately owned community open spaces access to water for their site at a flat seasonal rate. A device is installed that allows a hose connection for the growing season (March 1 through November 1).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Site stewards pay a flat fee of $120 per growing season (March 1 through November 1) for water access at a community open space lot. If water is not available at the requested site, the $120 payment is refunded within 90 days. The fee is not prorated.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: First week of October (last week to submit applications each season)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Site stewards managing City-owned or privately owned community open spaces in Baltimore City
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Accessing water (hose connection) at a community open space lot during the growing season
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only
requirements_list: Must be a site steward of a City-owned or privately owned community open space
Must submit a completed Water Access Application via the BuyIntoBmore site
Must pay the $120 flat-rate seasonal fee at time of application
Must return a signed Water Access Agreement before a service request is submitted
Applications must be submitted by the first week of October
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online through the BuyIntoBmore site (baltimore-md-publicity.tolemi.com) by searching for a property address or selecting Water Access under Programs. Add the lot(s) to your cart, complete the application, and submit the $120 payment. Once reviewed, a Water Access Agreement is emailed to you. Return the signed agreement and, if water is available, an inspector will install a hose connection device.

structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore City water customers who used more water than usual due to a leak, equipment problem (such as a toilet or appliance), or other situational issue may request a reduction in their water or sewer bill for the affected billing period. The Baltimore Department of Public Works (DPW) reviews requests and, if approved, adjusts the bill to remove or reduce charges caused by the unplanned water loss. For interior or situational leaks, DPW reduces the water-use portion of the bill by 50% of the excess water consumed above the customer's daily average; seniors or customers facing hardship may receive a 100% reduction. For underground leaks, all extra water and sewer charges caused by the leak are removed from the bill upon submission of proof of repair by a licensed plumber. Adjustments apply to up to three consecutive months of highest usage. Approved credits appear on the customer's bill approximately four weeks after the request is received.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: For interior or situational leaks, DPW reduces the water-use portion of the bill by 50% of the excess water consumed above the customer's daily average. Customers identified as seniors or facing hardship may receive a 100% reduction of the excess. For underground leaks, all extra water and sewer charges caused by the leak are removed from the bill, provided the customer submits proof of repair by a licensed plumber. Adjustments apply to up to three consecutive months of highest usage. Approved adjustments appear on the bill approximately four weeks after DPW receives the form. Customers may receive one Situational/Interior Adjustment and one Underground Leak Adjustment per eligible period (interior/situational once per three years per property; underground once per two years per property).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Within 60 days of the bill being issued
structured_extraction.contact_name: DPW Customer Support and Services Division
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City property owners or their authorized representatives, as well as other Baltimore City water customers, who received an unusually high water or sewer bill due to a leak, appliance malfunction, or situational water loss event.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction or credit applied to the customer's water and/or sewer bill to offset charges from qualifying leaks, situational water loss, or equipment malfunctions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only to customers served by Baltimore City water and sewer service within Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Must be a Baltimore City water customer or property owner (or authorized designee); only the legal property owner or an authorized designee may request an adjustment.
Request must be submitted within 60 days of the bill being issued.
Water loss due to theft or vandalism is not eligible.
No leak adjustments will be granted if the property has an active leak or the known leak has not been repaired.
Repairs must be completed before submitting request.
Underground leak adjustments are available only once every two years per property.
Interior/situational usage adjustments are available only once every three years per property.
One adjustment per type (interior/situational or underground) is allowed per 12-month period.
For underground leaks, the leak must be repaired by a licensed plumber, and proof of repair (including date of repair, type of repair, and confirmation the repair was completed) must be submitted.
For underground leak adjustments, water consumption data must support the repair receipts if available.
Approval is not guaranteed; customer will be notified if the request is denied or if additional information is needed.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Water and Sewer Adjustment Request form (available online or as a downloadable PDF at the Baltimore City website) and submit it by mail to DPW Customer Support and Services Division, 200 Holliday St., Room 404, Baltimore, MD 21202, or in person at 200 Holliday Street, First Floor, Room 8, Baltimore, MD 21202. Include proof of repair for underground leaks. The customer will be notified by phone or letter if the request cannot be granted or if additional information is needed. Approved adjustments appear on the bill approximately four weeks after DPW receives the form.

Participants receive lower water and sewer charges through the city's affordability portal or program page.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of monthly water and sewer bill costs.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Water4All program page on the Baltimore City website or visit the Affordability Portal to explore the plan and apply.

structured_extraction.program_name: Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act (WIOA) Job Training for Youth
structured_extraction.program_description: Federally funded job training and career development programs for young people in Baltimore City. Partner organizations offer in-school programs for high school juniors and seniors and out-of-school programs for individuals ages 18–24. Programs teach life skills, job skills, and industry-specific training, including internships, certifications, and professional development. Funded through the federal Department of Labor Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act (WIOA) youth grant.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Program partners provide free job training, certifications, internships, and career development to eligible Baltimore City youth ages 17–24. Training options include CNA/GNA certification, pharmacy technician, automotive technician, HVAC-R, CDL-B license, forklift certification, IT certifications, customer service, childcare certification, and healthcare support roles. Programs offer career pathway exploration, occupational skills training, and industry-recognized credentials through partnerships with training providers and community organizations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City residents ages 17–24, including current high school juniors/seniors (in-school programs) and out-of-school youth ages 18–24 (out-of-school programs)
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Job training, certification programs, internships, career pathway exploration, industry-recognized credentials, and career development for youth
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City residents only
requirements_list: Must be a Baltimore City resident
Ages 17–24 (in-school) or 18–24 (out-of-school) depending on program
Out-of-school individuals ages 18–24 OR in-school high school seniors
Some programs require a high school diploma or GED
Some programs require drug/alcohol screening and background check
CDL-B program requires ages 21–24, 3 years driving experience, criminal background check, no points or moving violations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the individual program partner directly using the contact information listed, or reach out to Joe Smith, Program Manager at MOED, at jsmith@oedworks.com or 410-396-6727 for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: YH2O is a pre-apprenticeship and mentoring program that prepares Baltimore City residents ages 18–24 for entry-level employment in the public works industry. The program provides hands-on training, mentorship, and workplace readiness skills, and introduces participants to careers in water, wastewater, solid waste, and information technology sectors through a partnership with the Baltimore City Department of Public Works. Past graduates have gone on to work as Laborers, Community Aides, Operations Technician Apprentices, and Customer Care Analysts.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free pre-apprenticeship training program providing hands-on training, mentorship, and workplace readiness skills development focused on careers in public works, water, wastewater, solid waste, and information technology sectors. Includes career mentoring and support for entry-level employment pathways.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City residents ages 18–24 who have a high school diploma or GED, are unemployed or underemployed, and are not currently enrolled in a job training program or post-secondary education, seeking careers in public works.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Job training, career preparation, and mentoring for entry-level positions in the public works, water, and wastewater industries.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Baltimore City residents only.
requirements_list: Must be a Baltimore City resident
Ages 18–24
Must have a high school diploma or GED
Must be unemployed or underemployed
Must not be currently enrolled in a job training program or post-secondary education
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the YH2O program page at https://dpw-volunteer-initiative-baltimore.hub.arcgis.com/pages/yh2o-pre-apprenticeship-program to get more information or submit an application. You can also contact Curtis Landen at MOED directly.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides crisis bridge housing (transitional housing) for youth and young adults (ages 18–24, and unaccompanied minors under 18) who are at risk of or experiencing homelessness in Baltimore City. The program offers short-term (1–3 months) safe and stable housing while participants are connected to a permanent housing solution.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two-year grants totaling $488,084 ($244,042 per year) to fund crisis bridge housing projects serving 7–8 units for unaccompanied minors and youth experiencing homelessness.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public or private nonprofit organizations that provide shelter or supportive services to youth and young adults (ages 18–24 and unaccompanied minors under 18) experiencing or at risk of homelessness in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Crisis bridge transitional housing for homeless and at-risk youth and young adults, including housing operations and supportive services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a public or private nonprofit organization
Must serve youth and young adults (ages 18–24) and/or unaccompanied minors (under 18) experiencing or at risk of homelessness
Organizations serving unaccompanied minors must register with the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) as required by HB 206 (effective July 1, 2020)
Must run background checks on employees working with minors
Must provide mandatory reporting training for employees

Must follow protocols for attempting parental contact for unaccompanied minors

Services are available through community centers on the east and west sides of Baltimore City, including the Westside Youth Opportunity Center at 1510 W. Lafayette Ave. and the Eastside Career Center hub.

structured_extraction.program_description: YSAP provides therapeutic interventions, case management, and social supports to young people in Baltimore City who are victims of multiple forms of violence. Services include housing, transportation, educational assistance, and peer support. The program uses a trauma-informed approach to reduce risk factors related to violence exposure and help young victims heal. It serves an average of 120 victims ages 11–24 per year.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Youth ages 11–24 in Baltimore City who are primary or secondary victims of conventional crime, child maltreatment, peer/sibling victimization, sexual victimization, school violence, domestic violence, dating violence, or witnessed/indirect violence including community and family violence.

Must be located in or served through Baltimore City
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Both direct services and referral services are available. Contact the Baltimore City Health Department Office of Youth and Trauma Services for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: YouthWorks is Baltimore City's nationally recognized summer jobs program that places young people ages 14 to 21 in summer work experiences throughout Baltimore City. It connects Baltimore employers with job-ready youth and young adults for summer and year-round positions. Employers can interview and hire motivated young workers across private, nonprofit, and government sectors to help shape the future workforce, with Baltimore City serving as the employer-of-record to reduce administrative burden for participating employers. Participants learn career readiness skills and build work experience.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Employers can hire pre-screened, job-ready youth and young adults (ages 14-21) for summer and year-round positions. Baltimore City can serve as the employer-of-record, reducing administrative burden for participating employers. Youth participants are placed in summer work experiences throughout Baltimore City and receive career readiness skills development.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Hiring youth and young adults for summer and year-round positions; summer work experience and career skills development for participants

requirements_list: Must be between 14 and 21 years old (for youth participants)
Must be a Baltimore City resident (for youth participants)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the YouthWorks website at youthworks.oedworks.com for more information on how to participate as an employer or youth participant.

structured_extraction.program_name: Buy Into Bmore Fixed Pricing Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A Baltimore City program that sells specific City-owned vacant buildings and lots at fixed, transparent, below-market prices to homeowners, developers, nonprofits, and community land trusts. The goal is to streamline the transfer of vacant properties into productive use, reducing vacancy and promoting sustainable, affordable development in Baltimore neighborhoods. Priority is given to Baltimore City residents who want to restore and occupy a home as their primary residence. Properties are located within the E-J Housing Market Typology areas of Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore City Department of Housing & Community Development
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: City-owned vacant buildings and lots are sold at fixed, below-market prices depending on buyer type. Homeowners and Community Land Trusts pay $1 for a vacant building or lot. Small nonprofits (50 or fewer employees) pay $1,000 for a vacant building and $500 for a vacant lot. Large nonprofits and for-profit developers (51 or more employees) pay $3,000 for a vacant building and $1,000 for a vacant lot. A $100 application fee is required, which is credited at settlement if approved or refunded if rejected. Homeowner applicants must demonstrate at least $90,000 in available funds for rehabilitation. Properties fall within the E-J Housing Market Typology areas. Approved sales are reviewed and authorized through the Board of Estimates (BOE). Property is conveyed 'as is' and the City retains title reversion rights if obligations are not met.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis; Phase 1 Homeowner Priority Period: April 1 – June 30, 2024; Phase 2 (Charm City Roots): begins April 15, 2024; Phase 3 (All Fixed Pricing Applicants): begins July 1, 2024; ongoing thereafter on a first-come, first-served basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City residents who want to become homeowners, for-profit developers, nonprofit organizations, and community land trusts seeking to acquire and rehabilitate City-owned vacant buildings and lots
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and rehabilitation of City-owned vacant buildings and lots for residential, mixed-use, new construction, side yard expansion, or green space development. Minimum $90,000 in available assets or pre-approved financing required per property for rehabilitation. Properties must be brought to code compliance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties must be located in Baltimore City within the E-J Housing Market Typology area (with exceptions for side yard uses in A-J typologies)
requirements_list: Must have at least $90,000 available per property for rehabilitation (homeowner applicants)
Must not own vacant properties that have been vacant for more than two years without recent work
Must have no legal issues that would prevent project completion
Must have no unpaid federal or state liens or court-ordered money judgments
Homeowners must maintain the property as a primary residence for at least 5 years after obtaining a use and occupancy permit
Use and occupancy permit must be obtained within 12 months from date of settlement
Community Land Trusts must be registered as an Affordable Housing Land Trust with Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation
Applications subject to a $100 fee (refunded if rejected; credited at settlement if approved)
During the initial phase (April 1 – June 30, 2024), priority was given to Baltimore City residents who plan to restore and reside in the homes as their primary residence
Applicants must fall into one of the eligible categories: homeowner, community land trust, nonprofit, or developer
Executed construction contract required before settlement
Evidence of equity capital and/or mortgage financing commitment required
501(c)(3) status must be maintained until Certificate of Completion (nonprofit track)
Commercial General Liability insurance: minimum $1,000,000 per occurrence
Contractors Environmental Liability: minimum $2,000,000
Workers' Compensation insurance as required by law
Obtain all permits within 90 days of conveyance
No assignment or transfer without Department approval
Comply with Urban Renewal Plan requirements
Comply with Minority and Women's Business Enterprise Program (if applicable)
Pay all recordation costs, documentary stamps, and transfer taxes
Submit Preliminary and Construction Plans by specified dates
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications began being accepted on March 20, 2024. Use the Buy Into Bmore interactive map at buyintobmore.baltimorecity.gov to find a property and submit an application online. DHCD reviews applications on a rolling basis and issues award or rejection decisions within two weeks of receipt. If an applicant does not pass vetting, they have five business days to remedy the issue before the next eligible applicant is considered. If multiple qualified applicants apply for the same property, the agency reviews them in the order they were submitted. Approved sales are reviewed and authorized through the Board of Estimates (BOE). The Commissioner of DHCD is authorized to execute ancillary documents and grant approvals.

Also assists with Homeowner's Tax Credit and Renter's Tax Credit applications. Services are offered in collaboration with the Baltimore County Department of Aging and are available by appointment on a first come, first serve basis during tax season.

Emphasis on individuals aged 60 and above

structured_extraction.program_description: Specialized substance use services for adolescents in Baltimore County, including assessment, referral, education, and the Adolescent Education Program (AEP), a six-hour class series on substance use effects, legal consequences, and decision-making skills.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Adolescents receive a counselor assessment and, if needed, referral to an appropriate treatment center. The Adolescent Education Program (AEP) is a six-hour class series covering short- and long-term effects of substance use, legal consequences, and decision-making skills. Classes are held in early evenings in Arbutus, Rosedale, and Towson, and in Baltimore County alternative schools. Designed for first-time drug or alcohol offenders or youth in early experimentation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adolescents in Baltimore County with substance use concerns, including first-time offenders
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Assessment, referral to treatment, and substance use education for youth
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County
requirements_list: Must be an adolescent
AEP is designed for first-time drug or alcohol offenders or youth in the experimentation phase
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 410-887-6465 for more information and to access services.

structured_extraction.program_name: American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds (SLFRF)
structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore County received $160,706,923 in federal State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds (SLFRF) through the American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) to help the county respond to the COVID-19 public health emergency and its negative economic impacts. The funds support various grant programs and recovery initiatives in the county.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Baltimore County was awarded $160,706,923 in SLFRF funds. The county must commit all funds by December 31, 2024. Funds are distributed through various grant programs to eligible recipients.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore County residents, businesses, non-profits, and government entities affected by the COVID-19 pandemic
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: COVID-19 public health emergency response and recovery, and addressing negative economic impacts of the pandemic
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County, Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: More detailed information on grant programs is available at the ARPA Baltimore County hub (arp-bc-gis.hub.arcgis.com).

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides funding to community-based nonprofits to produce and present arts, science, history, and humanities programs and activities in Baltimore County. Supports specific projects such as performances, exhibits, lectures, classes, and workshops, improving the cultural quality of life in the area. General operating support is not available through this program. Grants are awarded for specific projects that take place in Baltimore County, with a maximum award of $9,500.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Project grants of up to $9,500 that fund specific arts, science, history, and humanities activities such as performances, exhibits, lectures, classes, and workshops. General operating support is not available. All funded activities must take place in Baltimore County.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community-based nonprofit organizations in Maryland that serve Baltimore County residents, including arts organizations, museums, drama groups, and music groups, as well as higher education institutions and government entities conducting specific cultural projects in Baltimore County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Specific projects such as performances, exhibits, lectures, classes, and workshops. All activities must take place in Baltimore County. Virtual events require the applying organization to be located in Baltimore County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Activities must take place in Baltimore County. Virtual events require the organization to be located in Baltimore County.
requirements_list: Must be a community-based, not-for-profit organization, higher education institution, or government entity
Must be located in Maryland
Activities must serve Baltimore County residents
All funded activities must take place in Baltimore County (for virtual events, the organization must be located in Baltimore County)
Project must improve the cultural quality of life in the area
General operating support is not eligible — funding is for specific projects only
Maximum grant amount is $9,500
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted during the open application window (typically posted August 1 with an October 1 deadline). Grants are awarded in January and fully funded by April. A final report is due August 1 of the grant year.

structured_extraction.program_name: BCAUSE (Baltimore County Age-Friendly Upgrades for Seniors)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides essential home repairs and safety modifications for homeowners aged 65 and older to help them age safely in their homes. Financial assistance is available with an income limit of $3,800/month (one person) or $4,345/month (two people), with no asset test.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance for home repairs and safety modifications to support aging in place. Income limit: $3,800/month (one person), $4,345/month (two people). No asset test.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners aged 65 and older in Baltimore County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home repairs and safety modifications to support aging in place
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County
requirements_list: Must be a homeowner
Must be aged 65 or older
Income under $3,800/month (one person) or $4,345/month (two people)
No asset test
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Baltimore County Department of Aging for details.

structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore County Department of Aging (BCDA) offers membership to fitness centers at Baltimore County senior centers for adults age 60 and older. Members can work out on their own schedule using quality fitness equipment specifically chosen to meet the fitness needs and abilities of seniors, including treadmills, free weights, recumbent bikes, strength training circuits, and flexibility stations. Drop-in centers are monitored by trained volunteers. Free equipment orientations are included for all members. Personal training packages and fitness assessments are also available for an additional fee. A scholarship program is available to ensure membership fees are not a barrier for qualifying older adults.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual membership costs $80 for access to all fitness centers, or $50 for a six-month membership. Free equipment orientations are included for all members. Scholarships are available for older adults who cannot afford the fee — eligibility requires gross monthly household income under 150% of the 2025 Federal Poverty Level ($1,995 for 1 person; $2,704 for 2; $3,414 for 3; $4,125 for 4). Personal training packages include: Fitness Assessment and Individualized Exercise Program ($60), one-hour session with a certified trainer ($55), and the 'Get Ready! Get Set! Get Fit!' Special package ($150, valued at $170).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults age 60 and older who are members in good standing of a Baltimore County Senior Center. Scholarship available to Baltimore County residents age 60 and older with income under 150% of the 2025 Federal Poverty Level.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Access to fitness center equipment and personal training services at senior centers; membership fees may be subsidized via scholarship
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County, Maryland. Scholarship applicants must be Baltimore County residents.
requirements_list: Must be age 60 or older
Must be a member in good standing of a Baltimore County Senior Center
Complete and sign Fitness Center Application prior to first visit
Complete and sign Consent and Release Form
Read Fitness Center Rules
Pay membership fee ($50 for 6 months or $80 for 1 year)
Wear athletic shoes with rubber soles enclosing entire foot
Scan BC-PASS membership key tag each visit
Trained Fitness Monitor must be onsite to use facility
Must be a current BCDA fitness center member to sign up for personal training
Scholarship applicants must be Baltimore County residents age 60 or older with gross monthly household income under 150% of 2025 FPL
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Fitness Center Application and Consent and Release Form before your first visit. To apply for a scholarship, complete the scholarship application and submit to the Wellness Specialist at 611 Central Ave., Room 324, Towson, MD 21204; applicants will be notified of eligibility within two weeks. To sign up for personal training, visit your local senior center.

structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore County plants native deciduous trees (20–145 trees per property) on the properties of county residents as a cost-effective best management practice to manage urban stormwater runoff. Trees are spaced 15' apart in staggered rows and equipped with deer protection (5' tube and 2" x 2" x 6' stake). Part of the County's federally mandated Chesapeake Bay Restoration Program, intended to extend and create wooded areas throughout the County. Property owners are responsible for maintaining the trees and reporting survival to the county triannually for 9 years.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: County-funded planting of 20 to 145 native deciduous trees with deer protection equipment (5' tube and stake) on eligible residential properties, paid for through the County's Waterway Improvement Fund. Trees are planted by county-selected contractors at no cost to the property owner. Property owner is responsible for all tree maintenance and triennial survival reporting for 9 years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore County residents who own residential property with space for at least 20 trees (less than one acre).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planting native deciduous trees and providing tree materials (stakes, shelters) on residential properties to increase forest canopy, manage urban stormwater runoff, and support Chesapeake Bay restoration. Funded by the County's Waterway Improvement Fund.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County residential properties. Trees cannot be used as screens or to line property. Minimum 20 trees per planting site required.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Baltimore County resident
Property must have space for at least 20 trees (minimum one-tenth of an acre); maximum 145 trees (three-fourths of an acre)
Property must be less than one acre
Trees cannot be used as screens or to line property boundaries
Property owners are responsible for all tree maintenance including removing stakes and shelters
Property owners must report tree survival to EPS triennially for 9 years
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the Backyard Trees Program application by email to forestmanagement@baltimorecountymd.gov or by mail to Baltimore County EPS Forest Management, 111 West Chesapeake Avenue, Room 305, Towson, Maryland 21204.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Baltimore County anti-litter cleanup campaign where community groups register online to conduct volunteer litter cleanups of any size during a specified timeframe. Participants can put their cleanup on a map and receive free cleanup supplies.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free cleanup supplies and an online hub to register cleanups, map them, and coordinate volunteer litter removal efforts.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Fall 2026 dates to be announced soon
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community groups and residents in Baltimore County who want to organize volunteer litter cleanups
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Conducting community litter cleanup events
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must register online during the Litter Blitz timeframe
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the BaltCo Litter Blitz Hub website to register your cleanup and learn how to participate.

structured_extraction.program_name: Baltimore County Career Centers – Services for Job Seekers
structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore County's Career Centers (also known as American Job Centers) provide free education, training, and career services to County residents and eligible workers. Services include career counseling, résumé development, job placement referrals, interview practice, occupational training scholarships for in-demand fields, and walk-in access to computers, internet, fax and copy machines, labor market information, and career assessment tools. Centers are located in Eastpoint (Baltimore), Hunt Valley, and Randallstown (Liberty). Monthly career development workshops are also offered on topics such as resume writing, interviewing strategies, LinkedIn, federal job search, and digital literacy (Microsoft Word, Excel, and technology basics). Programs are funded by the Baltimore County Department of Economic and Workforce Development (DEWD).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free career services including one-on-one career coaching, résumé development, job placement assistance, interview practice, computer and internet access, fax and copy machines, job search help, career assessments, career planning, and occupational training scholarships for eligible individuals. Training scholarships are assessed on a case-by-case basis as funds are available. Monthly career development workshops are offered on topics such as resume writing, interviewing strategies, LinkedIn, federal job search, and digital literacy. Center use requires signing a Customer Activity Sheet and adherence to center policies (dress code, no children, restrict computer use to job search).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore County residents (youth and adults) who are unemployed, economically disadvantaged, or dislocated workers, as well as non-residents recently laid off from or currently underemployed at a Baltimore County employer. Also serves general job seekers looking for employment support, career planning, and skills training.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Career counseling, résumé writing, job search support, interview practice, occupational training scholarships in high-demand fields, GED and ESOL courses, computer skills training, and access to career center resources for job search and career planning.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Primary eligibility is for Baltimore County residents. Non-residents who were recently laid off from a Baltimore County employer, or who currently work for a Baltimore County employer but are underemployed, may also qualify. Services are available at three locations in Baltimore County: Eastpoint (Baltimore, MD), Hunt Valley, and Liberty (Randallstown, MD). The American Job Center also serves individuals in the broader Baltimore metropolitan region.
requirements_list: Age 18 or older
Valid Social Security Number
U.S. citizenship or authorization to work in the U.S.
Males born on or after January 1, 1960 must be registered with the Selective Service
Must be a Baltimore County resident, OR a non-resident recently laid off from a Baltimore County employer, OR a non-resident currently underemployed at a Baltimore County employer
May need to provide documentation of Unemployment Insurance records, public assistance benefits, veteran status, residency, or income
No appointment needed at Eastpoint; appointments required after noon at Hunt Valley and Liberty
Participants must follow grievance procedures for complaints and acknowledge receipt of equal opportunity policies and civil rights notice
Information authorization required for participation; photo/statement release authorization may be requested
Sign Customer Activity Sheet with name, MWE User ID, arrival time, and services planned upon arrival
Restrict computer and phone usage to job search efforts only
Dress professionally (dress code policy enforced)
Keep cell phones on vibrate during seminars and workshops
No children allowed in Center
No food or drink near computer or electronic equipment
Arrive promptly for appointments; call by noon the day before to reschedule or cancel
Report employment upon job acceptance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Walk in during business hours (8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday through Friday) or schedule an appointment online for Hunt Valley and Liberty Career Centers. Sign the Customer Activity Sheet upon arrival. For WIOA-funded services, visit a Career Center and complete enrollment paperwork including the Receipt of Grievance Procedures and Authorization to Release Form and the Center and Computer Use Agreement. Career Consultant staff will assess eligibility, provide orientation, and develop a personalized employment plan. Training scholarship applications are processed by Career Consultant staff on a case-by-case basis.

structured_extraction.program_name: Baltimore County Energy Conservation Devices Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides a property tax credit to single and multi-family residential property owners in Baltimore County who install solar or geothermal devices that meet national safety and performance standards to heat, cool, supply electricity, or provide hot water for their home. The credit equals 50% of eligible installation and equipment costs or $5,000, whichever is less; for a hot water supply system, the credit is $1,500. The credit applies only to the Baltimore County Real Property Tax, cannot exceed property taxes owed in a given year, and any excess can be carried forward for up to two additional tax years. An annual budget cap of $1.5 million applies, and approved applications are placed on a waiting list in the order received.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Credit equals 50% of eligible installation and equipment costs or $5,000, whichever is less. For a hot water supply system, the credit is capped at $1,500. Eligible costs include component parts, accessories, and reasonable installation labor for solar or geothermal energy devices. The credit applies only to the Baltimore County Real Property Tax. It cannot exceed the property taxes owed in a given year, and any excess can be carried forward for up to two additional tax years. An annual budget cap of $1.5 million applies; approved applications are placed on a waiting list in the order received.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: June 1 of the year immediately preceding the first taxable year for which the credit is sought
structured_extraction.program_audience: Single and multi-family residential property owners in Baltimore County who install qualifying solar or geothermal energy conservation devices
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of Baltimore County real property tax obligation for costs associated with installing solar or geothermal heating, cooling, electricity, or hot water systems, including component parts, accessories, and reasonable installation labor
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only to property owners within Baltimore County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a single or multi-family residential property owner in Baltimore County
Device must use solar or geothermal energy for heating, cooling, hot water, or electricity generation
Device must meet national safety and performance standards set by a nationally recognized testing laboratory
Evidence required that device meets national safety and performance standards
Eligible costs must have been incurred within the 12 months before the initial application
Must submit detailed receipts listing amounts and dates of payment
Must submit the Permit Number for the electrical inspection completed by the Baltimore County Electrical Inspection Office
Energy conservation devices exclude household appliances
Credit does not transfer with the property; a change of ownership terminates the credit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Gather required documentation including detailed receipts listing amounts and dates of payment, evidence of national standards compliance, and the electrical inspection permit number from the Baltimore County Electrical Inspection Office. Step 2: Complete the application form with property and owner information, and list all items of cost with amounts and dates expended. Step 3: Submit to the Director of the Office of Budget & Finance (OBF) for approval or denial. Applications may be submitted online at the provided link or printed and mailed or brought to the Office of Budget and Finance, Property Tax Credit Administration, 400 Washington Avenue, Room 150, Towson, Maryland 21204.

structured_extraction.program_name: Baltimore County Optical Network (BCON) Dark Fiber Leasing Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore County leases dark fiber infrastructure to private sector businesses and other organizations at competitive rates to encourage economic development in and around the county. The network spans more than 250 miles and provides connectivity across Baltimore County and into neighboring counties. The county licenses unused dark fiber optic capacity, providing limited, exclusive use of unlit, point-to-point single-mode fiber optic strands located in overhead and underground installations, typically within public rights-of-way.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Baltimore County leases dark fiber at extremely competitive rates. The county provides access to unlit dark fiber strands; the licensee is responsible for obtaining electronic equipment and transmission services. Fiber may not be resold or sub-licensed to unaffiliated third parties. A 'Build to Suit' option is also available where the county may absorb the cost of additional fiber infrastructure construction to extend facilities to or into a customer's location, in exchange for a minimum-term lease commitment. A connection fee is required for construction to connect to specified demarcation points, and monthly license fees are payable in advance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private sector businesses, government agencies, schools, and other organizations seeking access to dark fiber network infrastructure in Baltimore County and surrounding areas, including communications service providers and authorized network operators.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Access to dark fiber telecommunications infrastructure for connectivity and communications needs. Lease fees for accessing dark fiber optic strands for telecommunications/broadband purposes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout Baltimore County with interconnect points to Anne Arundel County, Baltimore City, Carroll County, Harford County, and Howard County. Fiber routes specified in Exhibit A; subject to rights-of-way availability.
requirements_list: Must be willing to commit to a minimum lease term if requesting Build to Suit construction
Must complete and sign the Dark Fiber License Agreement
Licensee must obtain all necessary federal, state, and local permits and approvals
Licensee responsible for securing access rights and easements for private property locations
Licensee must provide 14 days' advance notice for interconnection work
Licensee cannot enter or modify County Facilities on licensor side of Demarcation Point
$5,000,000 combined single limit comprehensive general liability insurance required
Must not be in arrears on payments to County or State of Maryland
Compliance with Maryland Election Law Article §14-101 through 14-108 for contracts $100,000+
Connection fee payment required for construction to connect to specified demarcation points
Monthly license fees payable in advance
Cannot resell, sub-license, or convey fiber to unaffiliated third parties
Non-discrimination in employment compliance required
Must remove equipment and restore right-of-way upon termination
Must comply with all federal, state, and local laws
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Email BCON@baltimorecountymd.gov to inquire about dark fiber availability. Download and complete the Dark Fiber License Agreement.

structured_extraction.program_description: A membership organization providing death benefits to members and their beneficiaries. Upon the death of a PBA member, all other members contribute $4.00 per announced death, and the collected funds are paid as a one-time death benefit to the deceased member's designated beneficiary.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Upon the death of a PBA member, the remaining membership each contributes $4.00 through automatic payroll deduction. The total collected is paid as a one-time death benefit to the member's designated beneficiary, calculated at $4.00 multiplied by the total number of members at the time of death. Payment is issued by check via certified mail within 30 days of the initial claim.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Active and retired Baltimore County Police Department employees (sworn and non-sworn) who are members of the PBA in good standing.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: One-time death benefit paid to the designated beneficiary of a deceased PBA member.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Baltimore County Police Department employees and retirees in Baltimore County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a current or retired Baltimore County Police Department employee (sworn or non-sworn)
Must have joined the PBA upon hire
Must maintain active or retired status
Must remain in good standing with the PBA
Must keep membership records up-to-date
Must designate a beneficiary
Must have proper direct deposit configuration with county office
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Employees may join the PBA upon their date of hire. To update membership or beneficiary details, complete the Membership Update Form and submit via U.S. Mail, intradepartmental mail, or email to the PBA Coordinator. Upon a member's death, beneficiaries must contact the PBA Coordinator to file a claim and provide proof of death. Payment is issued within 30 days of the initial claim. For membership questions or benefit verification, contact Alaina DeLucia at 410-887-2881 or adelucia@baltimorecountymd.gov, Monday through Friday 6 a.m. to 2 p.m.

structured_extraction.program_name: Baltimore County SHIP (State Health Insurance Assistance Program)
structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore County's State Health Insurance Assistance Program (SHIP) provides free, unbiased, and confidential one-on-one Medicare counseling to Baltimore County residents. Trained volunteer counselors help Medicare beneficiaries understand Medicare options (Parts A, B, C, and D), compare Medicare Advantage and Prescription Drug plans, explore Medigap options, avoid penalties, resolve billing disputes and appeals, and identify programs that can lower costs. During the annual Open Enrollment period (October 15 to December 7), in-person counseling is available at senior centers throughout Baltimore County, with appointments available starting in September. Phone counseling is available year-round, Monday through Friday, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. Counselors also screen beneficiaries for financial assistance programs such as Medicare Savings Programs, Extra Help, the Maryland Senior Prescription Drug Assistance Program (SPDAP), and Medical Assistance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free one-on-one counseling by certified SHIP volunteer counselors, available by phone year-round and in-person during the fall Open Enrollment period (October 15–December 7). Counselors help with Medicare Parts A, B, C, and D; Medicare Advantage and Prescription Drug plan comparisons; Medigap options; billing disputes and appeals; and screening for financial assistance programs such as Medicare Savings Programs, Extra Help, SPDAP, and Medical Assistance.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Open Enrollment runs October 15 to December 7 annually; appointments available starting September annually; phone counseling available year-round
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore County residents age 65 and older, and those under 65 receiving Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI), who need help understanding or navigating Medicare coverage, comparing plans, or identifying cost-saving programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable — this is a counseling and technical assistance program, not a funding program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Baltimore County residents only. In-person appointments held at senior centers in Baltimore County during Open Enrollment; phone counseling available year-round.
requirements_list: Must be a Baltimore County resident
Must be a Medicare beneficiary
Must be age 65 or older, OR under 65 and receiving SSDI
Must bring Medicare card and any other health insurance cards (for in-person appointments)
Must bring a complete list of all medications including dosage and frequency (for Part D plan comparisons)
Must provide financial information (income and assets) to check eligibility for financial assistance programs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact SHIP by phone at 410-887-2059 or email medicareinformation@baltimorecountymd.gov to schedule counseling. Phone counseling is available year-round, Monday through Friday, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. In-person appointments at senior centers are available during the fall Open Enrollment period, with scheduling opening in September each year. Appointments can also be scheduled online through the booking portal. Bring required documents to your in-person appointment. Educational presentations are also available by contacting SHIP to register.

structured_extraction.program_description: A hardship exemption that removes the Maryland State Bay Restoration Fee from a property owner's real property tax bill for the current fiscal year. To qualify, the property must be the applicant's primary residence and the applicant must already receive one of three specific tax credits or exemptions related to homeownership hardship, disabled veteran status, or disabled law enforcement/rescue worker status.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: An approved exemption removes the Bay Restoration Fee from the applicant's current real property tax account for that fiscal year only. The exemption is not automatically renewed — applicants must reapply each year.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: September 30 of the fiscal tax year, by 4 p.m.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore County homeowners who live at the property as their primary residence and currently receive the Homeowners Tax Credit Baltimore County Supplement, Real Property Tax Exemption for Disabled American Veterans or Surviving Spouse, or Real Property Tax Credit for Disabled Law Enforcement Officers or Rescue Workers or Surviving Spouses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Removal of the Bay Restoration Fee from the applicant's real property tax bill.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to property owners in Baltimore County, Maryland.
requirements_list: The property must be the applicant's primary residence.

The applicant must currently receive one of the following: (1) Homeowners Tax Credit Baltimore County Supplement, (2) Real Property Tax Exemption for Disabled American Veterans or Surviving Spouse of Disabled American Veterans, or (3) Real Property Tax Credit for Disabled Law Enforcement Officers or Rescue Workers or Surviving Spouses of Fallen Law Enforcement Officers or Rescue Workers.
Applications must be received by 4 p.m. on September 30 of the fiscal tax year for which the exemption is sought.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and submit the online application form on the Baltimore County website. The form asks for the fiscal tax year, property owner name, parcel number, property address, and confirmation of primary residency and qualifying credit/exemption status. Submit before the September 30 deadline.

structured_extraction.program_name: Blind Individual and Surviving Spouse Tax Exemption or Refund
structured_extraction.program_description: A state law exemption that reduces the assessed value of a blind person's property — or their surviving spouse's property — by $15,000 for purposes of calculating Baltimore County real property taxes. Blind individuals or their surviving spouses may also receive a refund of property taxes paid in taxable years when the exemption was authorized but not granted, retroactive for up to three years. Individuals receiving this relief cannot also receive the Disabled Veteran or Surviving Spouse Tax Exemption.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Exempts $15,000 of a qualifying blind person's or their surviving spouse's property assessed value from real property taxes. Eligible individuals may also receive a retroactive refund of property taxes paid for up to three years when an exemption was authorized but not previously granted. Individuals receiving this relief cannot also receive the Disabled Veteran or Surviving Spouse Tax Exemption.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Blind individuals and surviving spouses of blind individuals who own real property in Baltimore County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of real property tax liability through an assessed value exemption, with a possible retroactive refund of previously paid property taxes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to blind individuals and their surviving spouses who own real property in Baltimore County, Maryland. The SDAT application form is available statewide; property must be the applicant's principal residence.
requirements_list: Must be a blind individual as defined in Section 11-2-106 of the Baltimore County Code, or the surviving spouse of a qualifying blind individual
Must own real property in Baltimore County
Property must be applicant's principal residence
Must be a Maryland resident (proof required: Driver's License, ID, voter registration, or prior year tax returns)
Medical certification of blindness: central visual acuity of 20/200 or less in better eye with corrective glasses, OR visual field defect with peripheral field contracted to 20 degrees or less
Blindness must be certified by a licensed medical doctor or optometrist, with effective date of blindness documentation
Must obtain and file an exemption application with the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
For a refund, must first receive an approved exemption from SDAT
Cannot also receive the Disabled Veteran or Surviving Spouse Tax Exemption for the same property
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For the exemption: obtain an application from SDAT and file it with SDAT (call 410-512-4900 for more information). Complete the application form with required documentation including proof of Maryland residency and medical certification of blindness. For the retroactive refund: first receive an approved exemption from SDAT, then send a copy of the approved exemption and a letter requesting a refund to the Baltimore County Council, 400 Washington Avenue, Room 205, Towson, Maryland 21204.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Community College of Baltimore County (CCBC) Learn, Earn, Achieve and Progress (LEAP) Program provides out-of-school young adults with free holistic training and support services. It helps participants earn a GED or Maryland high school diploma, gain industry-recognized certifications, and build employment and work-based learning experiences to launch a career.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free program offering GED classes, industry-recognized certifications (e.g. CNA/GNA, medical assistant, pharmacy technician, IT), leadership development, financial literacy, job development, mentoring, and life skills training. Available at multiple CCBC campus locations in Baltimore County.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Out-of-school young adults ages 18 to 24 who are Baltimore County residents and meet income requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Education, career training, certifications, GED preparation, job placement support, and life skills development.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County residents only.
requirements_list: Ages 18 to 24
Baltimore County resident
Must meet income requirements
High school diploma required for training programs only (not for GED classes)
Must be out of school
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call the LEAP information line at 443-840-4292 or email jmoon@ccbcmd.edu. Participants attend one of five CCBC campus locations.

structured_extraction.program_description: A series of in-person and virtual workshops offered through Baltimore County Career Centers to help adults build job-search skills, digital literacy, resume writing, interview preparation, and LinkedIn proficiency. Topics include Microsoft Word and Excel, federal job search strategies, and career services orientation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free workshops offered in-person at Liberty, Hunt Valley, and Eastpoint Career Centers, as well as virtually. Topics include digital literacy (computers, internet, email, Google Drive, virtual platforms), Microsoft Word and Excel, senior computer basics, resume writing, interviewing strategies, federal job search, and LinkedIn. Some workshops require prerequisites such as computer access or full attendance commitment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adult job seekers in Baltimore County, including seniors with little to no computer experience
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Developing job readiness, digital literacy, resume writing, interviewing, and LinkedIn skills
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at Career Centers in Baltimore County (Liberty, Hunt Valley, and Eastpoint locations) and virtually
requirements_list: Federal Job Search workshop: must commit to all prep and in-class assignments, attend entire class, and independently navigate a computer
LinkedIn workshop: must have access to a computer, tablet, or smartphone
Digital literacy courses require attendance at all four workshops
Microsoft Word/Excel courses require attendance at both introduction and intermediate levels
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Career Center you wish to attend to register for in-person workshops. For virtual workshops and online learning resources, email talentworks@baltimorecountymd.gov or call 410-887-8000.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides free family support, case management, information, referral, and advocacy services to Baltimore County residents aged birth through 21 years who have a developmental disability.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free family support, case management, information, referral, and advocacy services provided at no cost to eligible residents.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore County residents aged birth to 21 years with a developmental disability.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Family support, case management, information, referral, and advocacy services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Baltimore County resident.
requirements_list: Must be a Baltimore County resident
Must be between birth and 21 years of age
Must have a developmental disability
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Children with Special Healthcare Needs program by phone at 410-887-2720.

structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore County offers grant funding to help neighborhood patrol groups cover startup and operating costs. Citizens on Patrol groups are organized volunteers who patrol their neighborhoods to deter crime and report suspicious activity to police.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding is available to supplement COP groups for startup and operation costs. Grants typically open for applications around April each year.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Grants usually open around April of each year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community and neighborhood groups in Baltimore County interested in organizing citizen patrol groups
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Startup and operation costs for citizen patrol groups
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to communities and neighborhoods within Baltimore County
requirements_list: Must be a community or neighborhood group
Patrol group can have as few as two members
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact a Community Outreach Officer from your local precinct. Set up a community meeting, recruit volunteers, and coordinate a training session. Contact Detective B. Dietsch at 410-887-8599 for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A community litter cleanup initiative where groups spend 15 minutes picking up litter in their local area. Participation earns credit toward an environmental project grant for a Baltimore County public school.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Baltimore County public schools can earn credit toward an environmental project grant based on community litter cleanup participation. No specific grant amount is stated.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community groups, residents, and organizations in Baltimore County who want to support local schools in earning environmental project grants through litter cleanup activities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Environmental projects at Baltimore County public schools.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County, Maryland
requirements_list: Pick up litter for 15 minutes as a group in any messy area near you
Submit your cleanup results on the program website
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organize a group litter cleanup for 15 minutes in your local area, then submit your results using the online form on the program's hub site.

structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore County provides funding for dumpster rentals to qualifying residential communities for one cleanup per year, helping neighborhoods dispose of bulk and accumulated waste.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: County-funded dumpster rental for one cleanup event per year for eligible communities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential communities of 50 or more homes in Baltimore County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Dumpster rental for community cleanup events
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County, Maryland
requirements_list: Community must have 50 or more homes
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the Bureau of Solid Waste Management's Community Cleanup Program page or call 410-887-8693 for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore County's centralized intake and referral system for people experiencing homelessness or at risk of becoming homeless. Connects individuals and families to emergency shelter, rapid rehousing, eviction prevention, and other community support services. Also includes an in-patient facility discharge referral process with medical screening and approval for shelter admission.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Centralized hotline (410-887-8463, option 1) that screens individuals for emergency shelter, rapid rehousing, eviction prevention, shelter diversion and placement, and other community supports. Available Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 7 p.m. Also provides coordinated entry into the homeless shelter system for in-patients being discharged from medical facilities, including medical evaluation and 30-day medication supply provision. Referrals from in-patient facilities accepted Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. via fax to 410-494-2777.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Referrals accepted Monday through Friday 8:30 am to 4:30 pm
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and families in Baltimore County who are experiencing homelessness or are at risk of becoming homeless, including in-patients being discharged from medical facilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Access to emergency shelter, rapid rehousing, eviction prevention, and other community support services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to persons in Baltimore County.
requirements_list: Must be located in Baltimore County
Must be able to independently complete all activities of daily living to access emergency shelter
Referral through Coordinated Entry required for most shelter and housing programs
For in-patient facility referrals: completion of all form sections or notation of 'not applicable'
Physical health ADL assessment
Behavioral health evaluation and clearance for independent shelter living
Supporting medical documentation (H&P, progress notes, discharge summary, etc.)
COVID-19 test result
30-day medication supply ordered by physician upon approval
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For individuals: Call the Coordinated Entry hotline at 410-887-8463 and select option 1, Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 7 p.m. If no operator is available, leave a voicemail with your full name and phone number for a return call within 24 to 48 hours. For in-patient facility referrals: Referring facility completes the discharge referral form with patient and medical information, then faxes completed referral and supporting documents to 410-494-2777. Baltimore County Nurse reviews for medical approval and patient is approved or denied.

structured_extraction.program_description: Offers low- and no-cost resources to correct hazardous conditions, eliminate safety hazards, repair or replace major systems, correct interior and exterior deficiencies, make energy improvements, modify homes for persons with disabilities, and eliminate lead-based paint.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low- and no-cost loan resources for housing rehabilitation, including hazard correction, major system repair or replacement, energy improvements, disability modifications, and lead paint elimination.
structured_extraction.program_audience: County residents needing home rehabilitation assistance
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Correcting hazardous conditions, eliminating safety hazards, repairing or replacing major systems, energy improvements, disability modifications, and lead-based paint elimination
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County

structured_extraction.program_description: CountyRide provides specialized transportation services for general-purpose trips to eligible Baltimore County residents, including seniors, people with disabilities, and rural residents. Buses run Monday through Friday, 7 a.m. to 5 p.m., with wheelchair accommodations, low-step entrances, and escorts for riders who need extra assistance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Subsidized specialized demand-response transportation service for eligible residents. Wheelchair-accessible buses with trained drivers provide transportation to medical and non-medical appointments. Trips are scheduled in advance — medical trips up to two weeks ahead, non-medical trips up to one week ahead. All trips are based on availability. Escorts accompany riders who need special assistance at no additional cost. Riders must be ready 10 minutes prior to pick-up; drivers wait no longer than 5 minutes after arrival.
structured_extraction.contact_phone: 410-887-2080 (Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m.–4:00 p.m.); 711 (hearing impaired or speech disability); 410-887-4565 (cancellations, 24/7)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore County residents who are 60 years of age or older, adults with disabilities ages 18 to 59 (pending certification), or rural residents ages 18 and older within rural boundaries determined by Baltimore County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Specialized transportation for general-purpose trips, including medical and non-medical appointments.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Baltimore County, Maryland only. CountyRide vehicle must be able to safely access the applicant's residence.
requirements_list: Must be a Baltimore County resident
Seniors must be 60 years of age or older
Persons with disabilities must be ages 18 to 59 and provide required documentation verified by a physician confirming inability to use public transportation
Rural residents must be 18 years of age or older and reside within rural boundaries as determined by Baltimore County
Children under 12 must be accompanied by an adult
Child safety seats must be provided for children under age 8 unless the child is 4 feet 9 inches or taller and weighs more than 65 pounds
Must register prior to use; registration takes approximately 30 days to process
Emergency contact information required on registration form
Mobility device specifications (weight, dimensions) must be provided if applicable
Must have an accessible pickup location
Must be ready 10 minutes prior to scheduled pick-up time
Driver can wait no longer than 5 minutes after arrival
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete the CountyRide Registration Form (also available by phone, at senior centers, or at the CountyRide office). Persons with disabilities under age 60 must also have a physician complete a physician statement certifying the applicant requires specialized paratransit services. Submit the completed form (and physician statement if applicable) by mail to CountyRide, 611 Central Avenue, Towson, Maryland 21204, or by email to countyride@baltimorecountymd.gov. Processing takes approximately 30 days. Once approved, call the CountyRide Office to request a client identification number and to schedule rides.

structured_extraction.program_description: Free technology training classes for older adults, offered in partnership with the University of Maryland Extension. Young people trained as technology mentors teach seniors how to use smartphones, tablets, and computers for activities such as online games, photography, genealogy, online banking, and buying and selling online.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free in-person or online classes taught by youth technology mentors covering smartphone, tablet, and computer use for a variety of everyday tasks.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Older adults in Baltimore County who want to learn technology skills.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: N/A — training program, not a funding program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County residents.
