structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register for a session online at the provided registration link. View available session dates on the Baltimore County meetings and events calendar.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free educational support program for caregivers of people living with dementia. Includes a four-hour workshop covering topics such as understanding dementia, managing problem behaviors, handling stress, and self-care, along with a 300-page guidebook.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free four-hour workshop (offered in-person and virtually) plus a free 300-page Dealing with Dementia Guidebook. Seating limited to 20 participants.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Family and professional caregivers of people living with dementia
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Education and support for caregivers of people with dementia
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County
requirements_list: Internet access and technology required for virtual sessions
Seating limited to 20 participants
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Email caregivers@baltimorecountymd.gov or call 410-887-4724 for more information and registration.

structured_extraction.program_name: Disabled Law Enforcement Officers or Rescue Workers Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A Baltimore County real property tax credit for law enforcement officers, firefighters, and rescue workers (including volunteers) who became permanently and totally disabled while serving the citizens of Baltimore County. Eligible disabled public safety officers — including those forced to retire on a medical disability pension due to a line-of-duty injury — who reside in Baltimore County can receive a credit equal to 100% of the Baltimore County real property tax on their qualifying dwelling. The credit renews automatically each year for the lifetime of the disabled person. It applies only to the Baltimore County Real Property Tax — other charges on the tax bill are not included — and does not extend to a surviving spouse or other resident. The credit was established by Baltimore County Council Bill 109-08 on November 3, 2008, and became available starting July 2009.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The credit equals 100% of the Baltimore County real property tax on the qualifying dwelling and renews automatically each year for the lifetime of the disabled person. It applies only to the Baltimore County Real Property Tax — other charges on the tax bill are not included. The credit does not extend to a surviving spouse or other resident. Available starting July 2009, established by Baltimore County Council Bill 109-08.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: September 30 of the tax year for which the credit is requested to begin
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore County law enforcement officers, fire personnel, and rescue workers (including volunteers and retired public safety officers) who have been permanently and totally disabled or forced to retire on a medical disability pension due to a line-of-duty injury, and who currently reside in Baltimore County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of the Baltimore County real property tax on the disabled worker's primary dwelling
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to disabled workers whose qualifying dwelling is their legal residence located in Baltimore County, Maryland. This credit applies to Baltimore County only.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a law enforcement officer, fire personnel, or rescue worker (including volunteer) who suffered permanent and total disability during service to Baltimore County, or a public safety retiree disabled due to a line-of-duty injury retired on a medical disability pension
Applicant must conform to the requirements established within his or her agency to be deemed disabled

The dwelling must meet one of these criteria: (1) owned by the disabled worker at the time he or she was adjudged disabled; (2) the worker was domiciled in Maryland as of the date adjudged disabled and acquired the dwelling within two years of that date; or (3) the dwelling was acquired after qualifying for a credit on a former dwelling under one of the previous methods
The dwelling must be occupied by not more than two families
The dwelling must not be receiving any other Baltimore County real property tax credit
Credit is awarded only during the lifetime of the disabled person — it does not extend to a surviving spouse or other resident
Must submit a verifying Court Order or Administrative Notice along with the completed application
Must currently reside in Baltimore County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application to the Baltimore County Employee Retirement Office (if employed by Baltimore County) or the Baltimore County Fire Department (if a volunteer rescue worker). An agency official certifies the line-of-duty disability. The application is reviewed and approved or denied by the Office of Budget and Finance (OBF) Director or designee. The credit continues year to year without reapplication unless the Director requests evidence of continued eligibility. Applications must be submitted on or before September 30 of the tax year for which the credit is requested to begin. You may also contact the Office of Budget and Finance Tax Payer Services by emailing financeinfo@baltimorecountymd.gov or calling 410-887-2404 with your name, address, and telephone number to verify eligibility and request the necessary paperwork.

structured_extraction.program_name: Disabled Veteran and Surviving Spouse Property Tax Exemption or Refund
structured_extraction.program_description: A Baltimore County property tax exemption that removes all Baltimore County real property tax obligations for the home of a disabled veteran or their surviving spouse. Eligible veterans must have a 100% permanent and total or 100% permanently unemployable service-connected disability rating. A refund of taxes paid for up to three years before receiving the exemption is also available upon request to the Baltimore County Council. Eligible individuals cannot also receive relief under the Blind Individual or Surviving Spouse Tax Exemption.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Full exemption from all Baltimore County real property tax obligations for the home of a qualifying disabled veteran or their surviving spouse. Eligible individuals may also receive a retroactive refund for county property taxes paid in up to the three years before the exemption was granted, upon request to the Baltimore County Council. Individuals receiving this relief cannot also receive the Blind Individual or Surviving Spouse Tax Exemption.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Disabled veterans with a 100% permanent and total or 100% permanently unemployable service-connected disability rating, and surviving spouses of such disabled veterans, who own real property (a home) in Baltimore County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Full exemption from Baltimore County real property taxes on the applicant's home; retroactive refund of county property taxes paid for up to three years prior to receiving the exemption.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only to disabled veterans and their surviving spouses owning real property in Baltimore County, Maryland. Applicant must be a Maryland resident.
requirements_list: Must be a disabled veteran with a 100% permanent and total or 100% permanently unemployable service-connected disability rating, or the surviving spouse of such a disabled veteran
Must own real property (home) in Baltimore County
Must be a Maryland resident
Copy of Honorable Discharge or DD-Form 214 required
Current VA rating notification showing 100% permanent and total or 100% permanently unemployable rating required
Proof of Maryland residency (driver's license, voter registration, or previous year tax returns)
Must obtain an approved exemption from the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) before applying for a refund
For a refund, must first file for and receive an exemption from SDAT
Cannot also receive relief under the Blind Individual or Surviving Spouse Tax Exemption
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For the exemption: obtain and file an application with the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) by calling 410-512-4900 or downloading the form from their website. Submit along with copy of Honorable Discharge or DD-Form 214, current VA rating notification, and proof of Maryland residency. For the refund: after receiving SDAT approval, send a copy of the approved exemption and a written refund request letter to the Baltimore County Council at 400 Washington Avenue, Room 205, Towson, MD 21204.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grants awarded to arts and sciences organizations for capital and special projects.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Endowment grants of varying amounts awarded to arts and sciences organizations for capital and special projects. Past awards have ranged from $10,000 to $250,000.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Arts and sciences organizations in Baltimore County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital improvements and special projects
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must serve Baltimore County

structured_extraction.program_description: A fitness program led by a certified instructor that guides older adults through dynamic exercises including aerobics or walking, strength training, stretching, and balance exercises. Progress is tracked with fitness checks at enrollment and throughout the program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Partially funded under Title III-D of the Older Americans Act. One-hour classes meet three times a week for 12 weeks. Individuals 60 and over are encouraged to make a suggested donation of $35 at registration. Available at Bykota, Essex, Parkville, Rosedale, and Seven Oaks Senior Centers (hybrid format).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Older adults 60 and over of all fitness levels, from frail to fit
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participation in structured fitness classes
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County — available at Bykota, Essex, Parkville, Rosedale, and Seven Oaks Senior Centers
requirements_list: Targeted at individuals 60 and over
Classes limited to 25 participants
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Kathleen Young by email or phone for more information and registration.

structured_extraction.program_description: A court-supervised program that helps non-custodial parents who are behind on child support payments find full-time employment. Participants submit job applications and meet weekly with court coordinators for job referrals and employment support.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive weekly meetings with employment coordinators, job referrals to companies in the Greater Baltimore area, job search strategy development, drug screenings, background checks, and retention follow-up for at least one year after placement. Employers who hire FESP clients may also receive assistance obtaining tax incentives.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-custodial parents who are behind on child support payments, typically men ages 25–40, who are motivated to find employment and support their families.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Employment placement, job readiness training, and support services to help participants find and keep full-time jobs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County residents participating in the court system.
requirements_list: Must be a non-custodial parent behind on child support payments
Must be highly motivated to support their family
Must be committed to learning new job skills
Must not have been convicted of a violent crime or criminal child abuse (implied from FRSP criteria; not explicitly stated for FESP)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 410-887-0152 for more information on how to participate.

structured_extraction.program_name: Family Recovery Support Program (FRSP) — A Passport to Progress
structured_extraction.program_description: A court-supervised program that helps parents with substance abuse problems by providing intensive treatment, holistic support services, and frequent monitoring to preserve families and protect children involved in Child in Need of Assistance (CINA) cases.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive access to an intensive structured substance abuse treatment program, a holistic strength-based support network, and frequent monitoring with court reviews.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Parents who are Baltimore County residents involved in CINA cases and have a substance abuse problem affecting their ability to parent.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Substance abuse treatment, family preservation services, and child protection support.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Baltimore County resident.
requirements_list: Must be a Baltimore County resident
Must be a party in a CINA (Child in Need of Assistance) case
Must have a substance abuse problem that affects their ability to parent
Must not have been convicted of a violent crime or criminal child abuse
Must not have been diagnosed with severe mental illness, mental retardation, or any cognitive impairment that would prevent them from understanding or completing the program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 410-887-6159 for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: Each fall, Baltimore County Department of Health offers free flu shots to individuals six months of age and older at county Health Centers during regular business hours throughout the cold and flu season. Walk-ins are welcome.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free injectable trivalent flu vaccine provided at Baltimore County Health Centers. Walk-ins welcomed during regular business hours (Monday–Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.). Note: this is not the high-dose vaccine recommended for people 65 and older.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore County residents six months of age and older
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Flu vaccination
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be six months of age or older

Consult your doctor before getting vaccinated if you have had a life-threatening allergic reaction to a flu vaccine or any component of the vaccine, have had Guillain-Barré Syndrome, or are not feeling well
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Walk in to any Baltimore County Health Center during regular business hours (Monday–Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.) throughout the flu season. No appointment needed.

structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore County offers a free, drive-thru tree giveaway for county residents. Residents may choose up to two trees per household from a selection of native tree species.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to two free native trees per household, available for drive-thru pickup at the Baltimore County Agricultural Center. Species available include Eastern Redbud, Northern Red Oak, Red Maple, Serviceberry, Sweetbay Magnolia, and White Oak.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Saturday, April 25, from noon to 3 p.m. (first-come, first-served); preorders have closed
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore County residents
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free native trees for planting on residential property
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Baltimore County residents only
requirements_list: Must be a Baltimore County resident
Limited to two trees per household
Must pick up trees in person at the Baltimore County Agricultural Center in Cockeysville, Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Preordering has closed. Remaining trees are available on a first-come, first-served basis on Saturday, April 25, from noon to 3 p.m. at the Baltimore County Agricultural Center, 1114 Shawan Road, Cockeysville, MD 21030. Drive to the pickup lane, pull to the right, and a County employee will load trees into your car.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free workout class using DVD videos that accommodates all fitness levels. Modifications are demonstrated so everyone can participate. Participants bring their own weights and stretch band to class.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free and partially funded under Title III-D of the Older Americans Act. One-hour classes meet twice a week on an ongoing basis. Offered at most Baltimore County Department of Aging senior centers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Older adults of all fitness levels seeking ongoing fitness classes
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participation in ongoing fitness classes
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County — offered at most BCDA senior centers
requirements_list: Participants bring their own weights and stretch band
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Kathleen Young by email or phone for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: Allows residential property taxpayers in Baltimore County who have experienced a temporary financial hardship to pay their property taxes in installments over additional time, rather than in a lump sum, to avoid tax sale of their property.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Approved applicants can pay their property tax liability in installments over additional time instead of a single payment. Eligibility is based on demonstrated hardship, repayment ability, and financial disclosure. Approval covers only the fiscal tax year in which the application is filed. All future taxes must be kept current to maintain eligibility.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential property taxpayers in Baltimore County who have experienced a temporary financial hardship and need additional time to pay their property tax liability.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment of outstanding property tax liability in installments to avoid tax sale.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residential taxpayers in Baltimore County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a residential taxpayer in Baltimore County
Must have experienced a temporary financial hardship
Must demonstrate repayment ability
Must submit a financial disclosure
Application must be filed by the end of February to avoid property tax sale in June
All future taxes must be kept current once enrolled
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: File an application by the end of February. Contact the Baltimore County Office of Budget and Finance at 410-887-2404 or financeinfo@baltimorecountymd.gov, or visit in person at 400 Washington Avenue, Room 150, Towson, Maryland 21204.

structured_extraction.program_name: Healthcare Enhancement for Local Public Safety (HELPS) Retirees Act
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal tax benefit that allows retired public safety officers to use up to $3,000 per year from their pension funds on a pretax basis to pay premiums for health care and long-term care insurance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Retired public safety officers may use up to $3,000 annually from their pension funds (defined benefit or defined contribution plans) on a pretax basis to pay premiums for health care and long-term care insurance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Retired public safety officers seeking to pay for health care or long-term care insurance premiums using pretax pension funds.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment of health care and long-term care insurance premiums.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Federal program available nationwide, including Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a retired public safety officer
Must have a qualifying pension fund (defined benefit or defined contribution plan)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individuals should work with their personal tax professional to determine how the HELPS Retirees Act applies to their situation. Visit the IRS website or the Grand Lodge FOP website for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Baltimore County property tax credit for commercial buildings that achieve at least a silver rating under the LEED (Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design) or NGBS (National Green Building Standard) rating systems. The credit reduces the owner's Baltimore County real property tax obligation for a set number of years based on the building's energy efficiency rating level. Eligible buildings include commercial properties and income-producing residential buildings with at least 50 units.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A credit against Baltimore County real property taxes only. The credit percentage and duration depend on the rating system and level: LEED New Construction (LEED-NC): silver = 50%, gold = 60%, platinum = 70%, duration 5 years. LEED Core and Shell (LEED-CS): silver = 40%, gold = 50%, platinum = 80%, duration 5 years. LEED Existing Buildings (LEED-EB): silver = 10%, gold = 25%, platinum = 50%, duration 3 years. NGBS: silver = 50%, gold = 60%, emerald = 80%, duration 5 years. Only one credit is allowed per building, and the credit runs with the property through ownership changes.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: On or before June 1 immediately preceding the first taxable year for which the credit is sought
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of commercial buildings in Baltimore County that have achieved at least a silver rating under the LEED or NGBS green building rating systems. Commercial buildings may include income-producing residential buildings with at least 50 units.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of Baltimore County real property tax obligation for eligible high-performance commercial buildings.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only for properties located in Baltimore County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Building must be a commercial property (including income-producing residential buildings with at least 50 units)
Building must achieve at least a silver rating under either the LEED Green Building rating system (LEED-NC, LEED-CS, or LEED-EB) or the American National Standards Institute's NGBS rating system
Applicant must provide documentation from an energy systems professional confirming the building meets the High Performance Building definition
Professional LEED or NGBS Rater certification documentation required
Only one credit allowed per building
Application must be filed under oath with sufficient supporting documentation
Application must be submitted on or before June 1 preceding the first taxable year for the credit (except when filed in conjunction with a Revitalization Property Tax Credit)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the completed Application for High Performance Building Tax Credit form along with documentation from an energy systems professional (including required professional LEED or NGBS Rater certification documentation) to the Office of Budget and Finance, Property Tax Credit Administration, 400 Washington Avenue, Room 150, Towson, MD 21204, on or before June 1.

structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore County offers a property tax credit to residential property owners whose homes meet certain energy efficiency standards. The credit reduces the owner's Baltimore County real property tax bill by a percentage equal to the energy efficiency level achieved, and it lasts for three consecutive years from the first year it is awarded (five years if the home is carbon neutral). The credit applies only to the Baltimore County real property tax obligation; other charges or fees on the tax bill are not included.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A reduction in Baltimore County real property taxes equal to the percentage of energy efficiency achieved. Under the LEED or National Green Building Standard (NGBS) systems: Silver certification = 40% property tax reduction; Gold = 60%; Platinum or Emerald = 100%. Under the Home Energy Rating System (HERS) Index, the credit percentage corresponds to the efficiency level achieved. The credit runs for three consecutive years (or five years if the home is carbon neutral) and stays with the property even if ownership changes. Granting the credit is subject to funding availability. Other charges or fees on the tax bill are not included in the calculation.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: June 1 immediately preceding the first taxable year for which the credit is sought
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential property owners in Baltimore County whose homes meet approved energy efficiency standards through HERS, LEED, or NGBS rating systems, including new construction and renovated structures
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credit applied to Baltimore County real property tax account for energy-efficient new or renovated residential structures based on the energy efficiency percentage achieved
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residential properties located in Baltimore County, Maryland only
requirements_list: Property must be a residential structure (new construction or renovated)

For HERS Index: newly constructed residence must receive a HERS Rating of 70 or lower; renovated structures must achieve at least 30% increase in energy efficiency with HERS ratings submitted before and after renovation
For LEED: property must be certified Silver, Gold, or Platinum by the U.S. Green Building Council
For NGBS: property must be certified Silver, Gold, or Emerald under the ANSI-approved National Green Building Standard
Certification must be provided by a Certified LEED Rater, Certified HERS Rater, Certified ASHRAE Professional, or Certified Passive House Consultant
Application must be submitted by June 1 immediately preceding the first taxable year for which the credit is sought
Must submit a copy of the certificate indicating efficiency level provided by builder, contractor, or rater
Renovated structures must include HERS ratings completed before and after renovation
Credit is subject to funding availability
Must be a residential property owner in Baltimore County
Applicant must sign oath/affirmation of accuracy on application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Gather required documentation, including the energy efficiency certificate from your builder, contractor, or rater (and pre- and post-renovation HERS ratings if applicable). 2. Complete the application form with property details. 3. Apply online (requires valid email and documentation) or apply by mail/in person using the printed application form. 4. Mail or deliver the completed application and documentation to the Office of Budget and Finance, Property Tax Credit Administration, 400 Washington Avenue, Room 150, Towson, MD 21204. Application must be received by June 1 before the first taxable year for which credit is sought. The Director of Budget and Finance will approve or deny the application.

structured_extraction.program_description: An early intervention program that serves Baltimore County families with children under age three who have developmental delays or disabilities. Research-based services are coordinated based on the needs and priorities identified by each family, at no cost.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free early intervention services coordinated through an Individual Family Service Plan (IFSP), including supports to help children develop social, emotional, and functional skills and to help families advocate for their child.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with children under three years of age who have developmental delays or disabilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Early intervention services to promote child development and family capacity to support their child.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Baltimore County resident.
requirements_list: Child must be under three years of age
Child must demonstrate a 25 percent delay in one or more areas of development, atypical development in one or more areas, or a diagnosed condition placing them at risk for developmental delays
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Make a referral online at https://referral.mditp.org/ or call 443-809-2169. Referrals can be made by parents, healthcare providers, child care providers, social workers, family members, or others familiar with the child's development. The local Infants and Toddlers site will contact the family to schedule an evaluation. If eligible, an Individual Family Service Plan (IFSP) is developed.

structured_extraction.program_name: Lead Poisoning Prevention and Asthma Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary home visiting program that provides one to six home visits to families to reduce or eliminate lead hazards, asthma triggers, and other environmental hazards in the home. Community health workers and nurses provide education and resources. A separate case management service provides telephone support for families of children with lead poisoning.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free home visits and/or telephone case management services including education on reducing lead and asthma hazards, cleaning tips, and nutrition guidance. Home visit program requires Medicaid enrollment. Case management requires a blood lead level (BLL) of 3.5 µg/dL or greater for children age 6 or younger.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore County resident children under 19 with moderate to severe asthma or elevated blood lead levels (home visits); children age 6 or younger with elevated blood lead levels (case management).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction and elimination of lead, asthma triggers, and other environmental hazards in the home; education, cleaning tips, and nutrition guidance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Baltimore County resident.
requirements_list: Home visit program: enrolled in or eligible for Medicaid; Baltimore County resident; under age 19 and diagnosed with moderate to severe asthma or blood lead level (BLL) of 3.5 µg/dL or greater
Case management: Baltimore County resident; BLL equal to or greater than 3.5 µg/dL; age 6 or younger
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Lead Poisoning Prevention and Asthma Program by phone at 410-887-4410 or email leadasthma@baltimorecountymd.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Access Point (MAP) is Baltimore County's information and referral gateway for older adults, people with disabilities, families, caregivers, and professionals. It screens for benefits and services, connects people to county and community resources, provides options counseling for long-term care decisions, and distributes information about available services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MAP provides free information and referral services including benefit screening, connections to county and outside agency services, options counseling for long-term care decisions, distribution of brochures, and community outreach. A durable medical equipment loan closet lends items such as walkers, wheelchairs, and shower seats (some requiring a $25 refundable deposit). Staff also demonstrate small assistive devices and can recommend vendors and programs to obtain equipment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Older adults age 60 and over, people with disabilities, families, caregivers, and professionals who are Baltimore County residents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Connecting individuals to benefits, services, long-term care options, assistive devices, and community resources.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Baltimore County residents. Individuals outside Baltimore County can call the state MAP at 1-844-627-5465.
requirements_list: Must be a Baltimore County resident
Older adults must be age 60 or older
People with disabilities and caregivers also eligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call MAP at 410-887-2594 or email aginginfo@baltimorecountymd.gov. Office hours are Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Equipment loan closet pickups and drop-offs are by appointment only at Bykota Senior Center, 611 Central Avenue, Towson, MD 21204.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides perinatal services to pregnant and postpartum Baltimore County residents through the Healthy Outcomes in Pregnancy and Early Childhood (HOPE), Healthy Families, and Babies Born Healthy programs. A team of public health nurses, community health workers, and social workers offers services to promote a healthy pregnancy and delivery, plus postpartum and newborn support for infants up to 18 months.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: In-person and virtual home visits, referral, and linkage to community resources for pregnant and postpartum individuals and infants up to 18 months of age.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Pregnant and postpartum Baltimore County residents, and infants up to 18 months of age.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home visits, referrals, and linkage to community resources to support healthy pregnancy, delivery, and postpartum outcomes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Baltimore County resident.
requirements_list: Must be a Baltimore County resident
Must be pregnant, postpartum, or the parent/guardian of an infant up to 18 months of age
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the referral form online at https://baltimorecountymd.jotform.com/232846003085048 or contact Maternal Child Health by phone or email.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that helps older women build the skills and confidence they need to avoid and improve symptoms of incontinence.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Partially funded under Title III-D of the Older Americans Act. Classes are two hours, once a week for three weeks. Individuals 60 and over are encouraged to make a suggested donation of $15 at registration.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Older women, particularly those 60 and over, experiencing incontinence symptoms
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participation in skill-building classes to manage and prevent incontinence symptoms
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County
requirements_list: Targeted at women 60 and over
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Donna Bilz by email or phone for more information and registration.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Mobile Career Center (MCC) is a traveling career services unit that brings workforce support directly to job seekers in Baltimore County neighborhoods. It provides career consultations, résumé and cover letter tips, interview practice, job development assistance, and connections to training and skills-development opportunities at no cost to participants.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free, on-site career services including career consultation, résumé and cover letter tips, interview techniques and practice, job development assistance, access to a reference and resource library, and information on support services. The MCC is a mobile unit with 16 computer stations, high-speed internet, Wi-Fi hotspot, printer, and an ADA-accessible workstation that travels to neighborhoods, community events, and partner locations across Baltimore County.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Job seekers in Baltimore County, including those looking to re-enter the workforce, start a new career, or advance their current career. Also available to community partners such as employers, government agencies, and community and faith-based organizations for recruitment events and professional development workshops.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Career consultation, résumé and cover letter assistance, interview preparation, job development support, and connections to training and workforce resources.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents and organizations throughout Baltimore County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Participants must be located in or near Baltimore County.
Community partners requesting the MCC for an event must provide at least four weeks advance notice (exceptions considered case-by-case).
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Job seekers can attend MCC events in their neighborhood. Community partners who want to request the MCC at their event can email bcoworks@baltimorecountymd.gov or complete the online request form on the Baltimore County website.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program featuring activities and exercises focused on improving balance and brain function to increase coordination, sharpen cognitive skills, improve vision, and enhance self-confidence. Offered virtually with limited class size.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Partially funded under Title III-D of the Older Americans Act. One-hour workshops meet twice a week for 12 weeks. Individuals 60 and over are encouraged to make a suggested donation of $15 at registration. Held virtually; internet access and technology required.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Older adults 60 and over seeking to improve balance and cognitive function
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participation in balance and brain function exercises
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County
requirements_list: Internet access and technology required
Registration required
Class size limited
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Donna Bilz by email or phone for more information and registration.

structured_extraction.program_description: A temporary one-day liquor license for bona fide nonprofit organizations raising money for charitable purposes in Baltimore County. The license is not available to individuals or for-profit businesses.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A temporary one-day license permitting eligible nonprofit organizations to sell alcoholic beverages at a single charitable fundraising event in Baltimore County.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications must be submitted no later than 15 days prior to the event day.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Bona fide nonprofit organizations holding charitable fundraising events in Baltimore County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Authorizes the sale of alcoholic beverages at a single charitable fundraising event.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Baltimore County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a bona fide nonprofit organization
Purpose must be raising money for charitable reasons
Application must be submitted at least 15 days before the event
Application must include a signature
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Print, complete, and sign the one-day application and checklist. 2. Submit the application at least 15 days before the event by mail or in person to the Board of Liquor License Commissioners, County Office Building, 111 West Chesapeake Avenue, Room G9, Towson, Maryland 21204.

structured_extraction.program_description: General operating support grants awarded to arts and sciences non-profit organizations whose programs demonstrate significant impact on the quality of life of Baltimore County residents. Grants support visual and performing arts, science, and humanities programs, performances, exhibitions, and lectures benefiting Baltimore County residents. Grants are funded through the Baltimore County Commission on Arts and Sciences, which does not serve as the sole funding source for any applicant.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: General operating support grants of varying amounts awarded annually to eligible arts and sciences organizations. Grant amounts have ranged from a few thousand dollars to hundreds of thousands of dollars depending on the organization. Grants are funded through the Baltimore County Commission on Arts and Sciences, which does not serve as the sole funding source for any applicant. Grants are awarded approximately August of the fiscal year and fully funded by January.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: November 14 (FY27); application period for FY27 closed on November 14
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations and higher education institutions in Baltimore County, Baltimore City, Anne Arundel, Carroll, Howard, and Harford Counties that provide arts, science, or humanities programs serving Baltimore County residents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: General operating support for arts, science, and humanities programs, performances, exhibitions, and lectures.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Organizations located in Baltimore County, Baltimore City, Anne Arundel, Carroll, Howard, or Harford Counties are eligible, provided their funded activities take place in their jurisdictions and serve Baltimore County residents and demonstrate significant impact on the quality of life of Baltimore County residents.
requirements_list: Must be a not-for-profit organization or higher education institution
Must be located in Baltimore County, Baltimore City, Anne Arundel, Carroll, Howard, or Harford County
Activities must take place in the applicant's jurisdiction and serve Baltimore County residents
Commission will not be the sole source of funding for the applicant
Must submit all required attachments
Budget must be complete and accurate
Must answer all application questions completely
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application during the open application period. Applications are reviewed based on criteria including community impact, outreach to Baltimore County residents, program quality, organizational stability, and completeness of the application. Grants are awarded approximately August of the fiscal year and fully funded by January.

structured_extraction.program_description: Free two-hour online training sessions that teach participants how to recognize, respond to, and prevent opioid overdoses, and how to use intranasal naloxone (Narcan) to reverse an overdose. Attendees receive a completion certificate, a naloxone prescription, and a free naloxone kit.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free online training sessions held via Webex. Participants receive a completion certificate, a naloxone prescription, and a free naloxone kit (distributed one to three days after the training). Sessions are scheduled twice monthly throughout 2026.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Preregistration required for each session; sessions scheduled through June 17, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals concerned that a loved one is at risk for opioid overdose, and those whose naloxone training certificates are expiring within the next three months.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training on opioid overdose recognition and response; receipt of naloxone medication kit for use in an overdose emergency.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Baltimore County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Preregistration is required before attending a session
Participants concerned about a loved one's overdose risk or those with certificates expiring within three months are encouraged to attend
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register online at the provided registration link. A link to the training application will be sent prior to the start of each session. Special accommodations can be requested by calling 410-887-3072 or emailing hhs@baltimorecountymd.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore County requires contractors and developers to submit a performance bond for any development or improvement project. The bond guarantees performance and fulfillment of all undertakings, covenants, terms, conditions, and agreements under Environmental Agreements (EA), Public Works Agreements (PWA), Right-of-Way/Road Agreements (RA), Utility Agreements (UA), Installment Agreements, or Solar Agreements with Baltimore County. For projects exceeding $25,000 in contract value, the bond must equal 100 percent of the contract price.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Contractors and developers submit a performance bond to assure completion and fulfillment of obligations under development agreements with Baltimore County. The bond amount (penal sum) is determined by the County based on the estimated cost to complete obligations under the agreement, and must equal 100 percent of the contract price for projects exceeding $25,000. Acceptable security types include a bond from a bonding company or financial institution acceptable to the county, a letter of credit, a cashier's check, or cash. Applications are processed first-come, first-served and will not take more than 60 days to process. Funds are disbursed only upon non-compliance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Developers and contractors entering into development agreements with Baltimore County, including Public Works Agreements, Utility Agreements, Road Agreements, Erosion and Sediment Control Agreements, Installment Agreements, or Solar Agreements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Performance security to assure completion and fulfillment of public or private improvements required under Environmental Agreements, Public Works Agreements, Right-of-Way/Road Agreements, Utility Agreements, Installment Agreements, or Solar Agreements. Bond funds are disbursed only upon non-compliance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County, Maryland
requirements_list: Project contract value must exceed $25,000
Bond amount must equal 100 percent of the contract price (penal sum determined by County based on estimated cost to complete obligations)
Bond must be from a bonding company or financial institution acceptable to the county
Surety must be licensed in Maryland
Surety must be rated 'B' or better by A.M. Best Company
For federal projects: surety must be authorized by U.S. Department of Treasury Circular 570
Surety must be in good standing with the County
Identify the applicable agreement type: Environmental Agreement (EA), Public Works Agreement (PWA), Right-of-Way Agreement (RA), Utility Agreement (UA), Installment Agreement, or Solar Agreement
Fully executed bond must be delivered to Department of Permits, Approvals, and Inspections / Environmental Protection and Sustainability
Bond must be accepted by the County prior to permit issuance
To change the bond type on an existing project, submit a request to the agency at least 60 days before the original bond expires
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete the Performance Bond Application form, then print and submit it along with the application for any new project. The fully executed bond must be delivered to the Department of Permits, Approvals, and Inspections / Environmental Protection and Sustainability. Applications are processed on a first-come, first-served basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: Project ReTree is an urban reforestation initiative that plants large numbers of canopy trees in Baltimore County public rights-of-way each spring and fall. It also provides free front yard trees to homeowners on request. The program targets specific neighborhoods and combines two earlier programs, Operation ReTree and Street Tree Replacement, into a community-based approach.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free canopy trees planted in Baltimore County rights-of-way and free front yard trees provided to homeowners upon request. Planting occurs each spring and fall in targeted neighborhoods.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore County homeowners and neighborhoods seeking free canopy trees for front yards or public rights-of-way.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planting canopy trees in public rights-of-way and homeowner front yards to increase urban tree canopy.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County, Maryland — focuses on specific neighborhoods each spring and fall.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the Project ReTree page to learn more. Homeowners can request a free front yard tree through the program.

structured_extraction.program_name: Property Tax Credit for Historical Restorations and Rehabilitations (County Historic Tax Credit)
structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore County offers a property tax credit to encourage owners of historic properties to restore and rehabilitate their buildings. Eligible properties include contributing structures in a County or National Register Historic District, and properties individually listed on the National Register of Historic Places or the Baltimore County Final Landmarks List. Residential owner-occupied properties receive a 20 percent county property tax credit for eligible rehabilitation work for up to 10 years. Commercial and income-producing properties receive a 10-year property tax freeze on any increased assessment resulting from qualified rehabilitation work.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Residential owner-occupied properties receive a 20% county real property tax credit for eligible rehabilitation work, extendable for up to 10 years. Commercial and income-producing properties receive a 10-year property tax freeze on increased assessments attributable to qualifying rehabilitation work. The total cost of residential rehabilitation must exceed $1,000 and must conform to the Secretary of the Interior's Standards. All projects require pre-approval by the Baltimore County Landmarks Preservation Commission (LPC) before work begins. Both residential and commercial applications are available.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of historic properties in Baltimore County — including residential owner-occupants, rental property owners, commercial property owners, and non-profit organizations — whose properties are designated as contributing structures in a County or National Register Historic District, or individually listed on the National Register of Historic Places or the Baltimore County Final Landmarks List.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eligible rehabilitation work including exterior repairs (roof, windows, painting, stucco) and interior work (painting, electrical and plumbing upgrades, heating and air conditioning) on qualifying historic properties, resulting in a reduction of Baltimore County property taxes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to owners of historic properties located in Baltimore County, Maryland only. The credit applies to the Baltimore County Real Property Tax obligation only.
requirements_list: Property must be designated as historic: either a contributing structure in a County Historic District, a contributing structure in a National Register Historic District, or individually listed on the National Register of Historic Places or the Final Landmarks List
For residential properties: property must be an owner-occupied dwelling
Total cost of rehabilitation work must exceed $1,000 (residential)
Rehabilitation work must conform to the Secretary of the Interior's Standards (materials repaired or replaced in kind)
For commercial properties: rehabilitation work must result in an increased assessment attributable to the work performed
Owners of residential rental or investment properties must complete a commercial application
Pre-approval by the Baltimore County Landmarks Preservation Commission (LPC) is required before any work begins
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review the Department of Planning's County Historic Tax Credit frequently asked questions. Contact Preservation Services at planning@baltimorecountymd.gov or 410-887-3495 for more information and to apply. Owners of residential rental or investment properties must complete a commercial application. All projects require LPC pre-approval before work begins.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Office of Law provides free legal services to qualifying individuals and organizations of limited means. Baltimore County lawyers volunteer their personal time to help clients with divorce, custody, child support, bankruptcy, simple wills, and general powers of attorney.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free legal services provided by Baltimore County Office of Law attorneys on a volunteer basis. Services cover divorce, custody, child support, bankruptcy, simple wills, and general powers of attorney. Clients must be referred by Maryland Volunteer Lawyers Service or Legal Aid Bureau, Incorporated.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and organizations of limited financial means in Baltimore County who are referred by Maryland Volunteer Lawyers Service or Legal Aid Bureau, Incorporated.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Legal representation and advice in areas including divorce, custody, child support, bankruptcy, simple wills, and general powers of attorney.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be of limited financial means
Must be referred by Maryland Volunteer Lawyers Service (410-547-6537) or Legal Aid Bureau, Incorporated (410-296-6705)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Maryland Volunteer Lawyers Service or Legal Aid Bureau, Incorporated to request a referral to the Office of Law's pro bono program.

structured_extraction.program_description: A national nonprofit program managed by active law enforcement officers that prepares young adults ages 13.5 to 20 for careers and leadership in public safety. Locally sponsored by the Baltimore County Police Department (BCoPD), it provides training in law enforcement topics, builds character and leadership, and offers scholarship and travel opportunities for full members.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive instruction in law enforcement topics (criminal law, investigation, crime prevention, traffic control, community policing), practical field experiences, and leadership development. Full members can earn scholarships and travel nationally for a leadership academy and training opportunities. Service learning hours are available for high school graduation requirements.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Young adults ages 13.5 to 20 who are in junior high school and interested in public safety careers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Career preparation, leadership development, and community service training in the public safety profession.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Baltimore County through local BCoPD-sponsored units.
requirements_list: Be between 13.5 and 20 years of age and in junior high school
Maintain a minimum grade C average in school
Be a responsible citizen with good reputation and moral character
Be able to safely perform duties without posing a health or safety threat
Have full approval and support of parents or guardian
Be a United States citizen
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the online application at baltimorecountymd.gov. Once accepted, participants serve a three-month probationary period. Successful completion leads to full membership privileges.

structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore County Department of Health provides reproductive and sexual health services including family planning, birth control, pregnancy testing, STI testing and treatment, GYN checkups, immunizations, and related education and counseling. Fees are based on income and family size, and no one is denied services for inability to pay.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Sliding-scale fee health services including birth control, emergency contraception, STI testing and treatment, GYN exams, immunizations, and pregnancy testing. No one is denied services due to inability to pay. Services are available at multiple clinic locations across Baltimore County.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Women, men, and teenagers in Baltimore County seeking sexual or reproductive health services
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Family planning, birth control, STI testing and treatment, GYN checkups, pregnancy testing, immunizations, and related counseling and education
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at seven clinic locations throughout Baltimore County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Walk in or make an appointment at one of the seven Baltimore County health center locations. Call the individual clinic or the main office at 410-887-2705 for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Baltimore County property tax credit for owners of mobile home parks, senior housing developments, or commercially zoned properties in Baltimore County who make qualified physical improvements of $100,000 or more in full cash value as assessed by SDAT. The credit reduces the County real property tax obligation based on the type of property and its location within or outside a designated commercial revitalization district. For senior housing in a designated commercial revitalization district: 100% of the increase in County taxes from improvements. For senior housing outside a revitalization district: 50% of the increase. For other commercial property in a designated district: 100% of County property taxes charged against the property. For mobile home parks: 100% of the increase in County taxes from improvements. The credit runs for 5 years, or 10 years if improvement costs exceed $10 million.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property tax credit applied only to Baltimore County real property taxes. For senior housing in a designated commercial revitalization district: 100% of the increase in County taxes from improvements. For senior housing outside a revitalization district: 50% of the increase. For other commercial property in a designated district: 100% of County property taxes charged against the property. For mobile home parks: 100% of the increase in County taxes from improvements. The credit runs for 5 years, or 10 years if improvement costs exceed $10 million. A transferable credit option is also available. Qualified improvements must have a full cash value of $100,000 or more as recorded by SDAT.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Within 120 days after issuance of a SDAT assessment notice that includes the improvements
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of mobile home parks, senior housing developments, or commercially zoned properties in Baltimore County who make qualified physical improvements of $100,000 or more in full cash value as assessed by SDAT
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credit applied to Baltimore County real property taxes following qualified physical improvements to eligible properties; eligible costs include hard costs documented with receipts, invoices, and building permits
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Property must be located in Baltimore County; properties in designated commercial revitalization districts qualify for the higher (100%) credit rate, while senior housing outside such districts qualifies for a 50% credit
requirements_list: Property must be a mobile home park, senior housing development, or commercially zoned property
Owner must make qualified improvements with a full cash value of $100,000 or more as reflected in SDAT records
Property must be located in Baltimore County; properties in designated commercial revitalization districts qualify for the higher credit rate
Properties used for a railroad or public utility are not eligible
Properties covered by the Maryland Condominium Act are not eligible
Application must be filed with the Director of Budget and Finance within 120 days after SDAT assessment notice
Detailed receipts, invoices, and itemized expense sheet for all related expenses must be submitted with the application
Building permits for the project must be submitted
Certification of completed work required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Application for Revitalization Tax Credit and submit it along with detailed receipts, itemized expenses, building permits, and certification of completed work to the Office of Budget and Finance, Property Tax Credit Administration, 400 Washington Avenue, Room 149, Towson, Maryland 21204, within 120 days of the SDAT assessment notice. The application is routed for approval by Planning, SDAT, and the Office of Budget & Finance. For commercially zoned properties in revitalization districts, call the Department of Planning Neighborhood Response Team at 410-887-3480.

structured_extraction.program_description: A County-owned residential drug treatment facility in Owings Mills providing medium- and high-intensity inpatient treatment for adults 18 and older struggling with substance use disorders, with a focus on combating opioid overdose deaths.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 24-hour medium- and high-intensity residential drug treatment. Services include family counseling, transition planning, and after-care referral. Average stay is 90 to 120 days. About 300 individuals and families are served annually. Treatment is provided by Gaudenzia under a County service agreement. Costs are covered through private insurance, commercial insurance, or Medicaid.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults 18 and older with substance use disorders, particularly those at risk of opioid overdose
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Residential substance use treatment, family counseling, transition planning, and after-care referral
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Located at 10225 Jensen Lane, Owings Mills, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be 18 years of age or older
Patients must have private, commercial, or Medicaid insurance to cover costs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the facility or the Department of Health for information on admission. Call 443-425-8285 with questions or concerns.

structured_extraction.program_description: Supportive housing units available throughout Baltimore County for individuals with a history of homelessness and a disability. Provides stable housing with support services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A limited number of supportive housing units distributed throughout Baltimore County. Specific rental terms not stated on this page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals in Baltimore County who have a history of homelessness and a disability.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Stable housing with supportive services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to persons in Baltimore County.
requirements_list: History of homelessness required
Disability required
Must be referred through Coordinated Entry
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call Coordinated Entry at 410-887-8463 to be placed on a waitlist for referral.

structured_extraction.program_name: Senior Assisted Living Group Home Subsidy (SALS)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides monthly financial assistance to eligible Baltimore County residents age 62 and older who are low or moderate income seniors. Helps seniors access assisted living in small group homes licensed by the Department of Health and Mental Hygiene for four to 16 residents. Available to a limited number of eligible residents. Income limit: $4,358/month (one person). Asset limits: $20,064 (one person), $26,400 (two people — only applicant's income considered).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Monthly financial assistance paying up to $1,000 toward the cost of assisted living in small licensed group homes (4 to 16 residents, licensed by the Department of Health and Mental Hygiene). Available to a limited number of eligible residents. Income limit: $4,358/month (one person). Asset limits: $20,064 (one person), $26,400 (two people — only applicant's income considered).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low and moderate income Baltimore County residents age 62 and older residing in or seeking assisted living group homes.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cost of assisted living in small licensed group homes (4 to 16 residents).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County residents only.
requirements_list: Must be a Baltimore County resident
Age 62 or older
Must be a low or moderate income senior
Residing in or seeking placement in an assisted living group home licensed by the Department of Health and Mental Hygiene housing 4 to 16 residents
Income under $4,358/month (one person)
Assets under $20,064 (one person) or $26,400 (two people)
Limited number of slots available
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Baltimore County Department of Aging for details.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides low-income Baltimore County seniors with an electronic card worth $50 to purchase fresh, locally grown fruits, vegetables, honey, and herbs at farmers' markets across Maryland. The program also supports the growth and development of farmers' markets.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Qualified participants receive a one-time electronic card worth $50 to use at farmers' markets across Maryland from July 1 through November 30. Benefits are provided on a first-come, first-served basis.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income Baltimore County seniors
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase fresh, locally grown fruits, vegetables, honey, and herbs at farmers' markets
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Baltimore County resident
requirements_list: Must be a Baltimore County resident
Annual income below $28,953 for an individual or $39,128 for a two-person household
Must provide name, address, cell phone number or email address, date of birth, ethnicity, and race when applying
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 410-887-0311 or complete the online form. Applications are no longer being accepted for 2025.

Topics include smartphone use, photography, internet of things, online health resources, video chat, online shopping, and protecting personal information online. Multi-week foundational courses in computer and iPad essentials are also available.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free workshops and multi-week courses covering a range of technology topics. A five-week Computer Essentials course and a five-week iPad Essentials course (with iPads provided in class) are among the offerings.

structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore County's public spay and neuter program offers low-cost spay and neuter surgery for cats and dogs owned by Baltimore County residents. Each package includes surgery, rabies vaccine, other vaccines, deworming, a County animal license, and a microchip — all for $20.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A complete spay or neuter surgery package for cats and dogs, including rabies vaccine, additional vaccines (distemper and Bordetella for dogs), deworming, a County animal license, a microchip, pain medication (Onsior or Carprofen), flea treatment (Capstar), and an identification tattoo — all for a total cost of $20 per pet. Appointments are required and payment is due at the time of scheduling.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore County residents who own cats or dogs living within Baltimore County. Rescue and foster groups are not eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Spay or neuter surgery and associated preventive veterinary services (vaccines, deworming, microchip, animal license, pain medication, flea treatment, and identification tattoo) for owned pets.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only to Baltimore County residents with pets that reside in Baltimore County. Surgery is performed at the Dundalk Spay and Neuter Surgical Center (7702 Dunmanway, Dundalk, MD 21222). Not available to residents outside Baltimore County.
requirements_list: Pet must be owned and reside in Baltimore County
Dogs must be between 4 months and 6 years of age
Cats must be between 5 months and 6 years of age
Pet must weigh at least 5 pounds
Female dogs must weigh no more than 60 pounds; male dogs no more than 80 pounds
Pet must not have a known illness, injury, or medical condition
Certain dog breeds (boxers, bulldogs, pugs, Shih Tzus) and cat breeds (hairless, Himalayan, Persian) are restricted
Rescue and foster groups are not eligible
Appointment required; walk-ins not accepted
Payment required at time of scheduling
Follow post-operative home care instructions for 7-10 days after surgery
Keep pet confined and quiet during recovery
Monitor incision site daily
Administer prescribed medications as directed
Schedule booster Distemper vaccine with regular veterinarian in 2-4 weeks after surgery
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the online appointment request form on the program page. If eligible, you will receive a confirmation email. Payment by credit card is required at the time of scheduling. On the day of surgery, arrive at the Dundalk Spay and Neuter Surgical Center (7702 Dunmanway, Dundalk, MD 21222) by 8 a.m. with your pet, any available medical records, and a carrier (cats) or non-retractable leash (dogs). Pets are discharged the same day, not before 3 p.m. Contact hours are Monday–Saturday, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.

structured_extraction.program_name: Surviving Spouses of Fallen Law Enforcement Officers or Rescue Workers Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore County offers a 100% property tax credit on the Baltimore County Real Property Tax for the surviving spouse of a law enforcement officer or rescue worker (including volunteers) who died in the line of duty in Maryland while employed by Baltimore County. The credit continues each year without requiring additional applications after the initial one. The credit does not apply to other charges on the tax bill and cannot be combined with any other credit or tax relief program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A credit equal to 100% of the Baltimore County Real Property Tax obligation. The credit does not apply to other charges on the tax bill and cannot be combined with any other credit or tax relief program. Once granted, the credit continues from year to year without the need to reapply.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: September 30 of the taxable year for which the credit is desired to begin
structured_extraction.program_audience: Surviving spouses of Baltimore County law enforcement officers or rescue workers (including volunteers) who died in the line of duty in Maryland while employed by Baltimore County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of Baltimore County real property tax obligation for qualifying surviving spouses
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applies only to property located in Baltimore County, Maryland. The dwelling must be the legal residence of the applicant in Maryland. The fallen hero or surviving spouse must have been domiciled in Maryland at the time of death. The death must have occurred in the State of Maryland while the officer or worker was employed by Baltimore County.
requirements_list: The deceased must have been a law enforcement officer or rescue worker (including volunteers) employed by Baltimore County
The death must have occurred in Maryland in the course of or as a result of employment with Baltimore County
Death must be certified as line-of-duty

The dwelling must have been owned by the decedent at time of death, OR the decedent or surviving spouse was domiciled in Maryland at time of death and the dwelling was acquired by the spouse within two years of death, OR the dwelling was acquired after the surviving spouse qualified for a credit for a former dwelling under either prior method
The dwelling must be the legal residence of the applicant and occupied by no more than two families
Surviving spouse must not have remarried
Death certificate or other evidence of eligibility required
The credit cannot be combined with any other credit or tax relief program
Application must be submitted on or before September 30 in the taxable year for which the credit is desired to begin
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Application for Surviving Spouse of a Fallen Law Enforcement Officer or Rescue Worker and submit with a death certificate or other eligibility evidence on or before September 30 of the taxable year in which you want the credit to begin. Mail to: Office of Budget and Finance, Property Tax Credit Administration, 400 Washington Avenue, Room 150, Towson, Maryland 21204. The application is reviewed and approved or denied by the Retirement Section Supervisor and Director of the Office of Budget and Finance.

structured_extraction.program_name: Tai Chi Quan: Move for Better Balance
structured_extraction.program_description: A program that empowers adults 60 and older to reduce their risk of falls through highly interactive Tai Chi classes. Classes improve balance, strength, postural stability, self-management, and quality of life.

Individuals 60 and over are encouraged to make a suggested donation of $25 at registration. Available at Arbutus, Cockeysville, Edgemere, Liberty, Overlea-Fullerton, Reisterstown, Rosedale, and Victory Villa senior centers.

requirements_list: Must be 60 or older
Pre-registration required
Space is limited

Recipients are scheduled for a training or pick-up event, assessed for the Affordable Connectivity Program for reduced or free WiFi, and connected with additional BCDA technology support programs. Recipients are scheduled for a training or pick-up event, assessed for the Affordable Connectivity Program for reduced or free WiFi, and connected with additional BCDA technology support programs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income adults age 60 or older who reside in Baltimore County or are members of a Baltimore County Senior Center.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Receiving a free tablet device (iPad or Chromebook) and related technology training and connectivity assistance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must reside in Baltimore County or be a member of a Baltimore County Senior Center.
requirements_list: Age 60 or older
Reside in Baltimore County or be a member of a Baltimore County Senior Center
Qualify as low-income (200% or less of federal poverty level: single $27,180, couple $36,620)
Have the ability to learn the device
Availability subject to supply of donated/distributed devices
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and submit the application form. Upon receipt of an eligible application, BCDA Office of Communications will contact the applicant to schedule a training or pick-up event and assess WiFi assistance needs.
