structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore County businesses that provide short-term lodging (fewer than 90 consecutive days) can apply for exemptions from the county's Transient Occupancy Tax. Eligible exemptions include stays paid by federal, state, or county government employees on official business, and stays lasting 90 or more consecutive days (non-transient occupancy).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible lodging businesses may claim exemptions that reduce the net room rental revenue subject to Baltimore County's 9.5% Transient Occupancy Tax. Exemptions apply to: (1) room rentals for guests staying 90 or more consecutive days (non-transient occupancy), and (2) rooms paid for by federal, state, or county government officials or employees on official business.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Monthly returns due May 31, 2026; Quarterly returns due July 31, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore County lodging businesses that collect transient occupancy tax and seek exemptions for qualifying stays
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction in transient occupancy tax liability for qualifying room rentals
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to businesses operating in Baltimore County, Maryland
requirements_list: Business must collect transient occupancy tax in Baltimore County
Exemptions apply only to stays of 90+ consecutive days (non-transient) or to rooms paid by government officials on official business
Exemption certificate must be filed with the tax return
Returns filed monthly or quarterly depending on selected payment interval
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the online tax return form by entering gross occupancy revenue, deducting applicable exemptions, and calculating net tax owed at 9.5%. Submit the exemption certificate along with business identification. Returns and payments are due by the stated due date; late payments incur 1% monthly interest and a 10% penalty after one month past the due date.

structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore County offers a free program to humanely reduce the number of community cats living outdoors. The program provides spay or neuter surgery, vaccines, ear-tipping, microchipping, and a vet exam for unowned outdoor cats. It also offers free trap loans to eligible property owners so they can bring cats to the clinic. The program aims to maintain healthy and lawful community cat colonies and reduce populations over time, in compliance with Baltimore County Code Article 12, Section 12-1-115.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free spay or neuter surgery, rabies vaccine, FVRCP vaccine, left ear-tipping, abdominal tattoo, microchipping, topical flea treatment, and a vet exam for community cats. Free trap loans (replacement value $90 per trap, $25 per divider) are also available for eligible property owners who will bring cats to and from TNR clinics. Humane trapping instructions, educational materials, and access to a mediation program for complaint resolution are also provided.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Feral cat caregivers, trappers, transporters, and residents caring for unowned outdoor community cats living in Baltimore County, including those who trap or transport cats on behalf of others.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Spay or neuter surgery, vaccinations, microchipping, ear-tipping, flea treatment, and vet exam for outdoor community cats. Trap loan equipment for trapping cats to bring to the clinic. Cats must be returned outdoors to their original trapping location after surgery.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Cats must live outdoors at an address within Baltimore County. Traps must be placed on property owned by the borrower within Baltimore County.
requirements_list: Complete the Feral Cat Caregiver registration form before scheduling a surgery appointment
Adhere to the TNR Program guidelines and Baltimore County Code Article 12
Must be in good standing with Baltimore County Animal Services
Retrieve the cat within 24 hours of surgery (lactating mothers retrieved same day)
Return the cat outdoors to where it came from after surgery
Cat must be unowned and living outdoors at a Baltimore County address
Cat must arrive in a cat trap or transfer cage, one cat per cage (no carriers or crates)
Cat must be over three months of age and over three pounds in weight and appear healthy
Must obtain property owner permission prior to trapping if not property owner
Must ensure all cats are sterilized, ear-tipped, microchipped, and vaccinated
Must keep rabies vaccines current and maintain veterinary records
Must notify BCAS of cat colonies
Must report bites or scratches to authorities and comply with rabies confinement/observation measures
Must work to abate nuisances or public health/safety threats
For trap loan: must own the property where trapping will take place
For trap loan: must be able to bring cats to and from TNR clinics
For trap loan: must have an approved application on file
For trap loan: must schedule surgery appointments prior to trapping
For trap loan: must monitor trap when set and never leave unattended
For trap loan: must keep cats in humane conditions with covered trap in temperature-controlled area
For trap loan: must provide fresh newspaper, food, and water
For trap loan: must never transport cats in trunks or truck beds

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Feral Cat Caregiver registration form (available in English and Spanish), provide colony location and details, identify role(s) as caregiver/trapper/transporter/participant/organizer, and sign agreement to comply with TNR Program Guidelines. Submit the form before scheduling a surgery appointment. To request a trap loan, email the TNR Coordinator and submit the required forms including the registration form, permission to enter property, and trap loan agreement. Surgery appointments and trap loan pick-up and return dates are all scheduled at the same time.

structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore County plants trees on private or public land to convert open lawn areas (one acre or more) into forested areas. This reduces stormwater runoff and supports the Chesapeake Bay Watershed Improvement Program. About 200 trees are planted per acre, spaced 15 feet apart, with stakes and shelters to protect them from deer and pests. Large reforestations come with three years of maintenance and a 90% survival guarantee. The program provides native deciduous trees suitable for Piedmont and Coastal Plain regions of Maryland, including canopy trees, canopy/midstory trees, and understory trees.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: County-funded tree planting of approximately 200 trees per acre on eligible properties. Includes free or subsidized native tree species for urban tree canopy and reforestation plantings under the County's TMDL program. Includes three years of maintenance and a 90% survival guarantee. Maintenance covers seasonal mowing, vine and invasive species management, and shelter upkeep. Final species list is determined by EPS Forest Management based on availability at local nurseries.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore County landowners with one or more acres of open lawn space away from utility easements, Forest Conservation Easements, septic and septic reserves. Also open to property owners, municipalities, and organizations conducting tree planting projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Converting open lawn into forested land to reduce stormwater runoff and support watershed improvement goals. Tree species provided for reforestation and urban tree canopy plantings.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County, Maryland
requirements_list: Property must have at least one acre of open space (lawn or grass)
Area must be away from utility easements, Forest Conservation Easements, septic and septic reserves
EPS Forest Management determines final species list based on availability at local nurseries
Species requests are considered but not guaranteed
Program focuses on native deciduous trees suitable for local soil and climate conditions
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a Reforestation Property Form via the Turf to Trees page to determine eligibility. Requests for specific tree species are considered by Forest Management staff, with final determination made based on availability.

structured_extraction.program_name: Watershed Association Restoration, Planning and Implementation Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore County awards annual grants to locally-based watershed associations and nonprofit organizations to support environmental restoration activities, watershed education and outreach, and community engagement. Funded work must help implement Small Watershed Action Plans (SWAPs) and Total Maximum Daily Load (TMDL) Implementation Plans, increase resident participation in watershed restoration, and help meet water quality requirements for local streams, rivers, reservoirs, and the Chesapeake Bay.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $30,000 are available to cover staff salaries for environmental restoration activities and public education. Fringe benefits up to 30% of salary and indirect/overhead costs up to 10% of combined salary and fringe are also eligible. In exceptional cases, grants exceeding $30,000 may be awarded to established, high-performing organizations that have been funded for at least three consecutive years. Award amounts depend on organizational capacity, application strength, total funding requested, and available funds. Funded activities include tree planting, stormwater BMPs, invasive species removal, stream cleanups, rain gardens, downspout disconnections, and education/outreach.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Locally-based watershed associations and nonprofit organizations with active membership in Baltimore County that have a track record of community-based environmental restoration work.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Staff salaries and fringe benefits for conducting environmental restoration planning and implementation, and watershed education and outreach. Indirect/overhead costs up to 10% of salary and fringe are also allowable. Eligible restoration activities include tree planting, stormwater BMPs, invasive species removal, stream cleanups, rain gardens, and downspout disconnections. Materials and equipment are not funded.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All grant-funded activities must be implemented within Baltimore County, Maryland watersheds (Back River, Gwynns Falls, Jones Falls, Baltimore Harbor, Liberty Reservoir, Gunpowder Falls, Loch Raven Reservoir, Patapsco River, Prettyboy WRAS). Projects in the Deer Creek watershed may extend into Harford County. Projects must address TMDL requirements and restoration plans within eligible watersheds.
requirements_list: Must be a locally-based watershed association or community group with active membership in Baltimore County
Must be a registered 501(c)(3), 501(c)(4), or 501(c)(6) organization in good standing with the State of Maryland
Must have a demonstrated history of successfully identifying and conducting resident-based and community restoration projects
Must have fulfilled all requirements on past grants if previously funded through this program
Ratio of staff hours to grant dollars must be at least one hour per $30 requested (e.g., 1,000 hours for a $30,000 request)
Must submit latest financial statements (audited, Form 990, unaudited, or treasurer's report)
Must provide list of county, federal, state, and other grants/loans from current and last two fiscal years
Must provide officer and board member names
Projects must link to specific watershed plans and TMDL requirements (bacteria, phosphorus, nutrients, sediment, mercury, PCBs, chlordane, trash)
Must track and report quarterly restoration metrics
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application materials via email to ewatts@baltimorecountymd.gov by February 6, 2026. The application package must include: (1) completed DEPS Watershed Grant Application Questions, (2) signed Baltimore County Application for Financial Assistance (AFA form), and (3) required supporting documents (proof of good standing, budget proposal, financial statements). Submit documentation linking proposed actions to watershed plans using provided tables. Include detailed budget with salary/labor costs, benefits, and in-kind contributions. Volunteer hours must be matched to other funding sources on the AFA form. All files must be submitted as separate PDFs following the specified file naming conventions. Use the email subject line format: '[Organization Initials] – FY XX Grant Application'. Incomplete or incorrect applications will be rejected.

structured_extraction.program_name: Youth Mentoring, JOINS Program, and Children In Need of Supervision (CINS) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore County's Youth and Community Services Unit operates three related programs for youth up to age 18 and their families. The Youth Mentoring Program pairs young people with a team of professionals to prevent crime and build positive relationships and life skills through conflict resolution, referrals to outside agencies, and education on topics like substance abuse, truancy, and decision-making. The JOINS Program (Juvenile Offenders In Need of Supervision) is a diversion program for first-time, nonviolent juvenile offenders or juveniles showing early signs of delinquency. Instead of entering the juvenile justice system, eligible youth participate in community restitution projects and receive mentorship grounded in restorative justice principles to develop personal growth and rebuild their connection to the community. The award-winning CINS Program (Children In Need of Supervision) provides free support, mentoring, education, and referrals to Baltimore County families with youth who run away, behave uncontrollably, or are truant from school. Staff listens to families, helps them work together to resolve issues, and connects them with therapists and other professional services when needed.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free mentoring, conflict resolution support, referrals to external agencies, and educational workshops for Baltimore County youth up to age 18 and their families. For eligible first-time, nonviolent juvenile offenders, the JOINS program provides diversion from the juvenile justice system through community restitution projects and mentorship by JOINS officers and youth mentors based on restorative justice principles. The CINS program provides free mentoring, family support, education, and referrals to professional therapists and programs for families dealing with youth who run away, are truant, or behave uncontrollably.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore County youth up to age 18 and their families who are willing and motivated to change, including first-time, nonviolent juvenile offenders or juveniles at the beginning of a pattern of delinquency, as well as families with youth who run away, act uncontrollably, or are truant from school.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Crime prevention, conflict resolution, truancy reduction, substance abuse education, life skills development, community restitution, mentorship, personal development activities to reduce recidivism and build self-esteem, family support, and referrals to professional therapists and programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Baltimore County residents only.
requirements_list: Youth must be up to 18 years of age
Must be a Baltimore County resident
Youth and family must be willing and motivated to change
For JOINS: must be a juvenile who is a first-time, nonviolent offender or at the beginning of a delinquency pattern
For JOINS: screened for eligibility at time of arrest
Services are free of charge
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For Youth Mentoring: contact the Youth and Community Services Unit at 410-887-5823 or email policepartnerships@baltimorecountymd.gov, or find your precinct officer. For JOINS: every juvenile arrest is automatically screened for eligibility; contact Officer K. Young at 410-887-5901 or kjyoung@baltimorecountymd.gov for more information. For CINS: contact Stan Lacienski at 410-887-5824 or slacienski@baltimorecountymd.gov, or call Youth and Community Services at 410-887-5823.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program helps businesses in designated Baltimore County areas. It encourages companies to stay and grow. The program also promotes the use of empty or underused properties and the creation of new, high-paying jobs. It supports the county's efforts to improve older office and industrial areas.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore County Department of Economic Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers two main tax credits. The Real Property Tax Credit applies to companies that improve their property. This credit lasts for 10 years. For the first five years, it covers 80% of the property tax increase from the new investment. The credit amount decreases by 10% each year for the next five years. The State Income Tax Credit is for hiring new, full-time employees. Companies can get a one-time credit of up to $1,000 for each new employee. The credit can increase to $3,000 for hiring a worker who meets certain 'disadvantaged' criteria, with more credits available if the employee stays for a second and third year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses that invest in property or hire new employees within specific Enterprise Zones in Baltimore County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: This program provides tax credits, not direct funds. Businesses can earn credits for making improvements to their property or for creating new, full-time jobs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The business must be in one of three designated Enterprise Zones in Baltimore County: the Chesapeake Zone, the Southwest Enterprise Zone, or the Federal Center at Woodlawn.
requirements_list: Must be located within a designated Enterprise Zone in Baltimore County.
Must make a new investment in real property or hire new employees working in the zone.
Most businesses are eligible, but retail businesses are generally excluded.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Complete the application and send it to the Baltimore County Department of Economic Development by December 31 to receive a property tax credit on the next tax bill. 2. After the department reviews your application, you will get a letter confirming if you are eligible. 3. For the property tax credit, the county will automatically notify the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation. 4. To claim the income tax credit, you must submit Maryland Tax Form 500CR with your annual tax return. 5. If you hire a 'disadvantaged' employee to receive a higher credit, you must get that employee certified.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides loans to technology-based businesses and businesses acquiring technology equipment to finance land, buildings, plant and equipment, including new construction or facility expansion.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore County Department of Economic and Workforce Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans up to $250,000 for technology-based businesses or businesses acquiring technology equipment. Funds may be used for acquisition and improvement of land, buildings, plant and equipment, including new construction or facility expansion.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Technology-based businesses or businesses acquiring technology equipment in Baltimore County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition and improvement of land, buildings, plant and equipment, including new construction or facility expansion.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the inquiry form on the Baltimore County financing page. The Business Services team will reach out to eligible applicants.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Boost Fund provides business loans to small, minority-owned, women-owned, and veteran-owned businesses in Baltimore County. Funded through revenue from Maryland's video lottery terminals, loans range from $50,000 to $250,000 and can be used for start-up costs, equipment, building improvements, working capital, and more. The program fills the gap when a bank cannot fund the full cost of a project, requiring businesses to first seek a bank loan before applying for County gap financing.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore County Department of Economic and Workforce Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans ranging from $50,000 to $250,000 with reduced down payments and interest rates at or below current market rates. Maximum loan term is 20 years with customized payment plans. Loans serve as gap financing after a bank loan is sought first. Collateral and personal guarantees are required. The business must operate in commercially-zoned leased space.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses (as defined by SBA standards), minority-owned businesses, women-owned businesses, and veteran-owned businesses operating in Baltimore County in commercially zoned leased space.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Start-up funding, gap funding, building improvements, equipment acquisition, lease improvements, business acquisition, working capital, and commercial real estate acquisition.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Business must operate in leased space zoned Commercial within Baltimore County.
requirements_list: Must be classified as a small business by SBA standards
Must have a personal credit score of 625 or higher
Must provide collateral as security for the loan
Must provide personal guarantees
Must first apply for a bank loan; County will consider funding the shortfall if the bank cannot cover the full project cost
Business must operate in commercially zoned leased space
Bank must be unable to fund the entire project cost
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the inquiry form on the Boost Fund webpage. Before applying, confirm you meet the SBA small business definition, have a credit score of 625 or higher, and can provide collateral and personal guarantees. You must first apply for a bank loan; if the bank cannot fund the full amount, the County will consider funding the shortfall.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides interest-free loans to businesses in Baltimore County's Commercial Revitalization Districts to fund exterior and some interior improvements, such as awnings, landscaping, and signage. Businesses can combine this loan with other economic development incentives for larger projects. Eligible businesses must be in one of the designated Commercial Revitalization Districts, which can be verified using the county's 'My Neighborhood' online tool.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore County Department of Economic and Workforce Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Interest-free loans up to $60,000 for exterior improvements (awnings, landscaping, signage) and potentially some minor interior and equipment improvements. Businesses must be located in one of the designated Commercial Revitalization Districts in Baltimore County. Can be combined with other economic development incentives for larger projects.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses located in one of Baltimore County's designated Commercial Revitalization Districts.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Exterior improvements including awnings, landscaping, and signage. Some minor interior and equipment improvements may also be financed.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be located in one of Baltimore County's designated Commercial Revitalization Districts. Businesses can verify eligibility using the county's 'My Neighborhood' online tool.
requirements_list: Business must be located in a designated Commercial Revitalization District in Baltimore County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Use the county's 'My Neighborhood' tool to confirm your business is in a Commercial Revitalization District. Contact Baltimore County Economic Development (Business Services team) for more information and to download an application, or complete the online interest form. All applicants must meet with staff prior to submitting.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides direct loans or loan guarantees to new or expanding industrial or commercial businesses in Baltimore County. Funds may be used to finance the acquisition and improvement of land, buildings, plant and equipment, including new construction or facility expansion.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore County Department of Economic and Workforce Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Direct loans or loan guarantees up to $250,000 for new or expanding industrial or commercial businesses. Funds may be used to finance the acquisition and improvement of land, buildings, plant and equipment, including new construction or facility expansion.
structured_extraction.program_audience: New or expanding industrial or commercial businesses in Baltimore County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition and improvement of land, buildings, plant and equipment, including new construction or facility expansion.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the inquiry form on the Baltimore County financing page and select the finance program you are interested in. The Business Services team will reach out to eligible applicants.

structured_extraction.program_description: A one-time grant for eligible businesses signing their first commercial lease in Baltimore County. The grant helps offset initial leasing expenses at a rate of $8 per square foot, up to a maximum of $80,000. Funds are awarded on a first-come, first-served basis until available funds are exhausted. Retail, restaurant, independent financial, or insurance agent/broker businesses are not eligible.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore County Department of Economic and Workforce Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time grant of $8 per square foot, up to a maximum of $80,000, to offset initial leasing expenses for a first commercial lease in Baltimore County. Retail, restaurant, independent financial, or insurance agent/broker businesses are not eligible. Awards are subject to available funds and distributed on a first-come, first-served basis.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling, within 180 days of lease execution
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses signing their first commercial lease in Baltimore County, excluding retail, restaurant, independent financial, or insurance agent/broker establishments.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Offsetting initial leasing expenses for commercial office space (Class A or Class B office or flex space).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Business must lease Class A or Class B office or flex space within Baltimore County.
requirements_list: Must execute a direct lease with a landlord for a minimum 36-month term
Eligible properties include Class A and Class B Office space
Class A and Class B Flex space considered for businesses with demonstrated need for laboratory space
Leased property must be a minimum of 500 square feet
Maximum award of $80,000 per business
Application must be received within 180 days of lease execution
Lease must be signed after February 14, 2025
Applicant must have a minimum personal credit score of 625
Retail, restaurant, independent financial, or insurance agent or broker establishments are not eligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, complete and submit the online Program and Tax Credit Interest form on the Baltimore County financing page. After submission, the county's Business Services team will contact you if you are eligible.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides tax-exempt bond financing for manufacturers and 501(c)(3) non-profit organizations to fund acquisition and improvement of land, buildings, plant and equipment, including new construction or facility expansion. Bond financing ranges from $2.5 million to a maximum of $10 million.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore County Department of Economic and Workforce Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax-exempt bond financing ranging from $2.5 million to a maximum of $10 million. Available to manufacturers and 501(c)(3) non-profit organizations. Proceeds may be used to finance acquisition and improvement of land, buildings, plant and equipment, including new construction or facility expansion.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Manufacturers and 501(c)(3) non-profit organizations in Baltimore County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition and improvement of land, buildings, plant and equipment, including new construction or facility expansion.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County
requirements_list: Applicant must be a manufacturer or 501(c)(3) non-profit organization
Financing amount must be between $2.5 million and $10 million
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the inquiry form on the Baltimore County financing page. The Business Services team will reach out to eligible applicants.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides low-interest loans to qualifying waterfront businesses in Baltimore County for exterior improvements such as bulkhead repair, slip renovations, signage, landscaping, and facade improvements. Businesses can borrow up to $75,000 or 90% of the project cost, whichever is less, at zero percent interest over a seven-year term.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore County Department of Economic and Workforce Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans for the lesser of 90 percent of project cost or $75,000. Loan term is seven years at zero percent interest. Funds are for exterior improvements including bulkhead repair, slip renovations, signage, landscaping, and facade improvements.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualifying waterfront businesses in Baltimore County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Exterior improvements including bulkhead repair, slip renovations, signage, landscaping, and facade improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The business must be a waterfront business located in Baltimore County.
requirements_list: Business must be a qualifying waterfront business in Baltimore County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the online inquiry form on the Baltimore County financing page, selecting the finance program you want to apply for. The Business Services team will reach out to eligible applicants.

structured_extraction.program_description: A time-limited, flexible housing subsidy program that helps homeless individuals and families identify and quickly secure stable rental housing. The program provides short-term rental assistance (up to 24 months), case management, and support services. The subsidy decreases every three months as tenant income increases. Subsidy payments are made directly to the landlord, and participants are expected to pay full rent upon leaving the program. Available in both Baltimore County and Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Time-limited flexible housing subsidy for up to 24 months, with rental assistance payments made directly to the landlord. The subsidy decreases every three months as tenant income increases. Also includes security deposit coverage (up to double the monthly rental amount), housing search assistance, case management/support services, and income recertification support. Participants are expected to pay the full rent upon discharge from the program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and families experiencing homelessness or housing instability in Baltimore County and Montgomery County who need time-limited rental assistance and support services to quickly obtain and maintain stable housing. Also relevant to landlords/property owners interested in partnering with the program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Identifying and securing rental housing, time-limited rental subsidy payments (up to 24 months paid directly to landlord), security deposit coverage, case management, support services, and income recertification support for tenants.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Baltimore County and Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be referred through Baltimore County's Coordinated Entry system (for Baltimore County applicants)
Must qualify based on program criteria
Tenant must undergo income recertification
Tenant contribution must remain affordable based on current net income
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For Baltimore County: Call Coordinated Entry at 410-887-8463 to be placed on a waitlist for referral to the Rapid Re-Housing program. For Montgomery County: Interested landlords should contact Elizabeth.Driggers@montgomerycountymd.gov to express interest in partnership; tenants should contact the Department of Health and Human Services.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federally designated area near Baltimore where companies can import and export goods while deferring or reducing U.S. customs duties and fees. The zone is considered outside of U.S. Customs territory, allowing businesses to delay paying import duties, pay lower processing fees, and simplify their supply chain. Companies can use the zone for warehouse, distribution, and manufacturing operations, enabling activities that would otherwise be more cost-effective to conduct abroad to be performed on U.S. soil within the zone.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Companies operating within FTZ #74 can defer import duties, reduce customs processing fees, and benefit from streamlined logistics. Activities that would otherwise be more cost-effective to conduct abroad can be performed on U.S. soil within the zone. Benefits include deferred duties, reduced processing fees, and simplified supply chain operations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Companies importing or exporting international goods, including those using warehouse, distribution, and manufacturing facilities near Baltimore.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Warehouse, distribution, and manufacturing operations involving international goods.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Service area covers nearly 1,000 acres of designated industrial and distribution space across Baltimore City, Anne Arundel County, Baltimore County, Harford County, Cecil County, Howard County, and Queen Anne's County. A company can be located at any property within this designated service area.
requirements_list: Company must be located within the FTZ #74 designated service area
Must be involved in importing or exporting international goods
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact FTZ Director Will Cawthern at wcawthern@BaltimoreDevelopment.com to begin the activation process. Activation can be completed within a few weeks under the Alternative Site Framework (ASF).

structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore Development Corporation (BDC) provides matching grants to business owners and property owners in Baltimore City to help pay for exterior building upgrades that improve the look and feel of Baltimore's commercial and industrial areas. Eligible improvements include storefronts, signage, awnings, and other facade work on commercial buildings, vacant and corner commercial properties, industrial properties, and shopping centers. Grants are reimbursement-based and paid after the project is complete. Work must be approved before it begins.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Multiple FIG options with different maximum awards: Citywide FIG: up to $7,500 (50% match); Corner Property FIG: up to $15,000 (50% match, $50,000 minimum investment); Vacant Building FIG: up to $15,000 (50% match, $50,000 minimum investment); Industrial FIG: up to $15,000 (50% match); Shopping Center FIG: up to $50,000 (10% of total project costs, $100,000 minimum investment). All grants are reimbursement-based and paid after the project is complete. Awards depend on available funding and are made at BDC's sole discretion.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Business owners and property owners of commercial and industrial properties in Baltimore City, including businesses with signed leases, commercial property owners, vacant property owners (with conditions), and non-profit entities that sell goods or services to the general public
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Exterior building upgrades including: business signage (building-mounted, blade, hand-painted), exterior painting, storefront windows/doors and carpentry, exterior lighting, awnings, masonry and cornice work, upper floor building facade improvements, semi-permanent landscaping features, murals (max 25% of project cost), custom/specialty construction elements (max 25% of project cost), and architectural/design services (max 15% of project cost)
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only. Additional requirements for properties in CHAP historic districts (Authorization to Proceed required) and Main Street Districts (Belair-Edison, Federal Hill, Fells Point, Hamilton-Lauraville, Highlandtown, Pennsylvania Avenue, Pigtown, Waverly), where Main Streets Design Review Committee approval may also be required.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a business owner or property owner
Applicant must provide matching funds (1:1 match, except Shopping Center FIG which requires 10% of total project costs)
Grant must be approved before work begins
Applicant must meet with a BDC representative at the project site before submitting an application
Work completed before application approval is not eligible for reimbursement
Work cannot begin until the grant is awarded and an agreement letter is signed
Grants are reimbursed after the project is complete
Two contractor estimates for all work required
Conceptual drawings, renderings, or plans required
CHAP Authorization to Proceed required for properties in Historic Districts
Main Streets Design Review Committee approval may be required for specified districts
Building must have full Certificate of Occupancy
First-floor commercial tenant must be occupied
Permanent, clearly visible commercial signage required before reimbursement
Original architectural features must be preserved or restored
Project design must harmonize with surrounding area character
Closeout requires: 2+ after photos, all contractor payment receipts, signed Reimbursement Request Form
W-9 form from applicant
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Request an application by filling out the contact form on the BDC website. A BDC representative will meet with you at the project site before you submit the application. Submit application with two contractor estimates, conceptual drawings/renderings, and any required approvals (e.g., CHAP Authorization to Proceed for historic districts). Work cannot begin until the grant is approved and an agreement letter is signed. Reimbursement is paid after the project is complete upon submission of after photos, contractor payment receipts, and a signed Reimbursement Request Form.

structured_extraction.program_name: Grocery Store Personal Property Tax Credit – Food Desert Incentive Areas
structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore City offers an 80% personal property tax credit for 10 years to grocery stores and supermarkets that locate in or make significant renovations within designated grocery store incentive areas (formerly called Food Desert Retail Incentive Areas) in the city. The program aims to improve access to healthy food and spur economic development in underserved neighborhoods. Created by city legislation that went into effect January 31, 2016 and amended in 2018, the program is administered by the Baltimore Development Corporation.
eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A 10-year, 80% credit against personal property tax (covering furniture, fixtures, and equipment) for supermarkets locating in or making significant improvements in targeted grocery store incentive areas. New construction requires expenditure of at least $150,000 or $25 per square foot on new personal property. Renovated stores must meet per-square-foot spending thresholds based on total floor space: at least $5/sq ft for stores up to 20,000 sq ft; at least $8/sq ft for stores between 20,001 and 45,000 sq ft; and at least $10/sq ft for stores over 45,000 sq ft.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Initial application must be received by October 1 to be considered for the credit in the next tax year. Annual continuing eligibility form must be submitted by November 30 of the prior year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Grocery store operators and developers locating in or renovating within designated grocery store incentive areas in Baltimore City
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Personal property such as furniture, fixtures, and equipment for a new or renovated grocery store in a designated incentive area
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be located within a designated grocery store incentive area in Baltimore City. Use CityView (cityview.baltimorecity.gov) to check if a specific address qualifies.
requirements_list: Must be a supermarket or grocery store
Must be located in a designated grocery store incentive area
Must have produce, meat, seafood, and dairy departments
Must have a canned and packaged goods department
Must derive more than 50% of sales from food
Must have more than 50% of total sales floor space dedicated to food sales
For new stores: must spend at least $150,000 or $25 per square foot on new personal property
For renovated stores up to 20,000 sq ft: must spend at least $5 per square foot on new personal property
For renovated stores between 20,001 and 45,000 sq ft: must spend at least $8 per square foot on new personal property
For renovated stores over 45,000 sq ft: must spend at least $10 per square foot on new personal property
Must have at least 500 square feet dedicated to the sale of fruits and vegetables
Must have at least 500 square feet dedicated to the sale of other perishable goods including meat, seafood, and dairy products
Must meet requirements for the amount of healthy food provided
Must comply with Baltimore City Health Article requirements
Must comply with Baltimore City Building, Fire and Related Codes Article
Must remain current on all other taxes and fees owed to Baltimore
Annual continuing eligibility must be demonstrated each year for the 10-year credit period
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Submit the pre-qualification form (with store concept, rendering, and for existing stores recent sales data) to confirm the location is in an eligible incentive area; allow 30 days for processing. 2. Once pre-qualified, proceed with construction or renovation. After completion, obtain a pre-qualification letter, complete the initial application form, document expenditures with invoices/receipts, sign in blue ink, scan and email to tax.credits@baltimorecity.gov by October 1 to be considered for the credit starting January 1 of the following year; allow 60 days for processing. 3. Submit an annual continuing eligibility form each year by November 30 of the prior year to maintain the credit for the full 10-year period; complete electronically, print, sign in blue ink, scan, and email to info@baltimoredevelopment.com. Administered by the Baltimore Development Corporation.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Outdoor Spaces Grant (OSG), administered by the Baltimore Development Corporation (BDC), helps business owners, non-profits, community groups, and property owners offset the cost of installing outdoor seating, parklets, landscaping, lighting, and other features that expand a business's use of outdoor space. Projects are intended to meet demand for public space along retail corridors, activate public areas, encourage community interaction, and contribute to vibrant street life in Baltimore neighborhoods. Eligible improvements include cafe tables and chairs, benches, curbside facilities like parklets and patios, shade structures, outdoor lighting, planters, plants, landscaping, and mobile vending structures. Grants are reimbursement-based and paid after the project is complete.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement-based grant of up to $5,000 in matching funds paid after the project is complete. Applicants must contract, complete, and pay for all improvements upfront. BDC reimburses eligible expenses following proof of completion and payment. Award amounts and matching requirements depend on available funding and are made at BDC's sole discretion. Specific award maximums are detailed in the OSG Terms & Conditions.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Business owners (with signed leases), non-profit organizations (with or without commercial leases), community groups, commercial property owners, and vacant property owners in Baltimore City
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installing outdoor seating and space improvements including cafe tables and chairs, benches, curbside facilities (parklets, patios), shade structures (sails, pergolas, umbrellas), outdoor lighting (string lights, lighted trees), pots, planters, planter boxes, trellises, plants and landscaping (limited to 25% of total grant amount), mobile vending structures, and architectural/design services (limited to 25% of total project cost)
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Citywide in Baltimore City. Eligible locations include the public right-of-way (sidewalk and parking spaces immediately adjacent to the business), private outdoor seating areas and courtyards, and community spaces open to the public.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a business owner, property owner, non-profit, or community group
Businesses and non-profits must have a signed lease or be a commercial property owner
Community groups and non-profits without commercial leases must provide a signed Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) from the property owner
Vacant property owners may be eligible with conditions, including lease execution, occupancy permit, and occupancy
Grant must be approved before work begins
Applicant must meet with a BDC representative at the project site before submitting an application
Work completed before application approval is not eligible for reimbursement
Grants are reimbursed after the project is complete
Applicant must provide matching funds
Applicant must pay for all project costs before receiving reimbursement
Project construction must be completed within 120 days of the award letter
Applicant must be in good legal standing with federal, state, and local authorities
For projects in the public right-of-way, a Curbside Commercial Permit or Minor Privilege Permit is required
Applicants must obtain two quotes for work done by third-party contractors
The cost of architectural or design services cannot exceed 25% of the total project cost
The cost of plants and landscaping is limited to 25% of the total grant amount
The grant recipient must maintain the improvements for three years
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Request an application by filling out the contact form on the BDC website. A BDC representative will meet with you at the project site before you submit the application. Gather required documents including a W-9 form, a sketch of your project, cost estimates, and any necessary permits or agreements. Submit the complete application package to BDC. Work cannot begin until the grant is approved in writing. Reimbursement is paid after the project is complete and payment is documented.

structured_extraction.program_description: Calvert County offers coupons for up to $50 off the purchase of native trees at participating local nurseries. Residents can use the coupon on up to six trees and are encouraged to stack it with the State of Maryland's tree coupon. The program tracks plantings on an online watershed map and runs annually from March 1 through November 20. Trees must be planted outside the Critical Area (a separate program, CARE, serves Critical Area property owners).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Coupon worth up to $50 off the purchase of each native tree, usable for up to six trees per participant, redeemable at participating nurseries. Coupons are not redeemable for cash and cannot be used for forest conservation mitigation or other development requirements.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: November 20 (annual program runs March 1 through Nov. 20)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Calvert County residents planting native trees outside the Critical Area
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of native trees at participating nurseries in Calvert County
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to properties in Calvert County located outside the Critical Area. Properties within the Critical Area are served by the separate CARE program.
requirements_list: Tree planting must occur outside the Critical Area
Coupon is valid for up to six native trees per participant
Must register name, address, and tree species at checkout at a participating nursery
Coupons cannot be used for forest conservation mitigation or development requirements under Calvert County Zoning Ordinance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Bring or show the coupon at a participating nursery, register your name, address, and tree species at checkout, then plant your trees. Photos can be submitted by tagging #CalvertSpreadYourLeaves on social media or emailing NativeTree@calvertcountymd.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: A judicially supervised program that provides treatment and supervision to individuals with substance use disorders who are involved in the criminal justice system, offering an alternative to incarceration and helping participants achieve sobriety and become productive citizens.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides court-supervised substance abuse treatment, case management, and comprehensive support services as an alternative to incarceration. Participants receive ongoing judicial oversight, coordination with health and social services, and structured supervision aimed at breaking the cycle of substance abuse.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with substance use disorders who are involved in the criminal justice system in Calvert County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Substance abuse treatment, supervision, and case management services
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Calvert County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a substance-abusing offender involved in the Calvert County criminal justice system
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Adult Treatment Court Program Coordinator for information on eligibility and enrollment.

structured_extraction.program_description: A monthly grant program for women-owned businesses that has been awarding funding since 1998.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $10,000 per award. Rolling applications with an application fee required.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Women-owned businesses (at least 50% women-owned) that have been in existence for at least one year.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: General business use.
requirements_list: Business must be at least 50% women-owned
Business must be in existence for at least one year
Application fee required

structured_extraction.program_name: American Red Cross Basic Swim Instructor Course
structured_extraction.program_description: A training course that certifies candidates to teach foundational swimming lessons including Parent and Child Aquatics, Preschool Aquatics, Learn-to-Swim Levels 1-3, and private swim lessons. Candidates are not required to perform advanced strokes such as butterfly or diving.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Instructor certification training for teaching foundational swim courses. Participants who complete the course receive an American Red Cross Basic Swim Instructor (BSI) certification.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals at least 16 years of age who want to become certified swim instructors for beginner-level courses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Becoming a certified basic swim instructor.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available through the Calvert County Aquatic Center.
requirements_list: Must be at least 16 years of age prior to the last day of the course.
Must demonstrate Level 3 strokes: Front Crawl (25 yards), Breaststroke (25 yards), Elementary Backstroke (25 yards), Sidestroke (25 yards).

Must complete the Water Competency Sequence: step into water and fully submerge, float or tread water for 1 minute, rotate one full circle and orient to exit, swim 25 yards without stopping, and exit the water without using steps or a ladder.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call the Aquatic Center at 410-414-8350 for course schedules and to register.

structured_extraction.program_name: American Red Cross Lifeguard Certification Course
structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive certification program that teaches individuals water rescue techniques, first aid, CPR, and AED use through hands-on training and simulations. Graduates are prepared to ensure swimmer safety at aquatic facilities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Hands-on lifeguard certification training covering water rescue, first aid, CPR, and AED use. Upon successful completion, participants receive an American Red Cross Lifeguard Certification.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals at least 15 years of age who want to become certified lifeguards.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquiring lifeguard certification skills and credentials.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available through the Calvert County Aquatic Center.
requirements_list: Must be at least 15 years of age prior to the end of the course.
Must complete a 150-yard swim, followed immediately by a 2-minute tread without arms, followed immediately by a 50-yard swim.

Must complete the brick test: swim half the pool length, fully submerge and retrieve a 10lb brick from approximately 7 feet deep, and swim back holding the brick on chest — all within 1 minute and 45 seconds.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call the Aquatic Center at 410-414-8350 for course schedules and to register.

structured_extraction.program_name: American Red Cross Lifeguard Instructor Course
structured_extraction.program_description: A course that trains individuals to become certified instructors for Lifeguarding, First Aid, and CPR/AED programs. Participants learn to plan, conduct, and evaluate lifeguard training sessions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Instructor-level certification training covering how to plan, conduct, and evaluate lifeguard training courses.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals at least 17 years of age who hold a current American Red Cross Lifeguard certification and want to become certified lifeguard instructors.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Becoming a certified lifeguard instructor.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available through the Calvert County Aquatic Center.
requirements_list: Must be at least 17 years of age prior to the last day of the course.
Must possess a current basic-level American Red Cross Lifeguarding certification (including Deep Water) with CPR/AED for Professional Rescuers and First Aid.
Must obtain instructor and participant course materials before starting the course.
Must successfully complete the online session of the Lifeguarding Instructor course prior to the pre-course session.

Must successfully complete the prerequisite skill assessment scenario covering: entry, swimming approach, surface dive in deep water (7-10 feet), passive submerged rescue, rapid extrication with assisting rescuer, rapid assessment, and single-rescuer CPR for 3 minutes.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call the Aquatic Center at 410-414-8350 for course schedules and to register.

structured_extraction.program_description: A recertification course for currently certified lifeguards whose American Red Cross Lifeguard certification is nearing expiration or has expired within a 30-day grace period.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Recertification training for lifeguards with expiring or recently expired certifications (within 30-day grace period).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Currently certified lifeguards whose certification is expiring or has expired within the past 30 days.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Maintaining lifeguard certification.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available through the Calvert County Aquatic Center.
requirements_list: Must hold a current American Red Cross Lifeguard certification that is nearing expiration or expired within a 30-day grace period.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call the Aquatic Center at 410-414-8350 for course schedules and to register.

structured_extraction.program_name: American Red Cross Water Safety Instructor Course
structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive swim instructor certification course (WSI) that trains candidates to teach all swimming and water safety courses for all age groups, including Learn-to-Swim Levels 1-6, Adult Swim, and advanced aquatic programs. This is the gold-standard certification for swim instructors.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Full-scope swim instructor certification training covering all American Red Cross swimming and water safety courses for all age groups. Participants receive the Water Safety Instructor (WSI) certification upon completion.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals at least 16 years of age who want to become fully certified swim instructors for all age groups and skill levels.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Becoming a certified Water Safety Instructor for all swim courses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available through the Calvert County Aquatic Center.
requirements_list: Must be at least 16 years of age prior to the last day of the course.
Must demonstrate Level 4 strokes: Front Crawl (25 yards), Backstroke (25 yards), Breaststroke (25 yards), Sidestroke (25 yards), Elementary Backstroke (25 yards), Butterfly (15 yards).
Must be able to maintain position on back for 1 minute in deep water (floating or sculling).
Must be able to tread water for 1 minute.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call the Aquatic Center at 410-414-8350 for course schedules and to register.

structured_extraction.program_description: A court-referred anger management program that helps participants develop skills and challenge aggressive behavior patterns. The program runs for 26 weekly sessions and is provided by the Crisis Intervention Center.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 26 weekly group sessions focused on developing anger management skills and reducing aggressive behavior. A fee waiver is available. Referral is made by the court.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals referred by the Calvert County Circuit Court to an anger management program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participation in 26 weekly anger management sessions to develop coping skills and reduce aggressive behavior.

requirements_list: Court referral required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Participants are referred to the program by the Calvert County Circuit Court. Contact Family Services at 410-535-1600 ext. 2516 for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A micro-grant program open to anyone for awesome projects and ideas.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $1,000 per award. Rolling applications.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Anyone with an awesome idea or project.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: General use.
requirements_list: Anyone can apply
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at the program website.

structured_extraction.program_name: Bay Restoration Fund (BRF) Financial Hardship Exemption Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Grants a waiver (exemption) from paying the Bay Restoration Fee to qualifying residential property owners or leaseholders in Calvert County who demonstrate substantial financial hardship.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual one-year exemption from paying the Bay Restoration Fee. Applicants must reapply each year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential property owners or leaseholders in Calvert County experiencing substantial financial hardship.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Waiver of the Bay Restoration Fee charged on residential dwellings.

Contact the office at 410-535-1600 ext. 2277 to check application status.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Beginning Farmer Success Program by the University of Maryland Extension helps new farmers explore enterprise options, refine ideas, develop plans and strategies, and implement their farming practices by connecting them with resources and contacts.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides resources, contacts, and guidance to help new farmers explore farm enterprise options, develop business plans and strategies, and put their farming ideas into practice.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Farm enterprise planning, business strategy development, and implementation support
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland
