structured_extraction.program_description: Birthright provides free, confidential, and non-judgmental support for women and their unborn children, including pregnancy information, referrals to medical and financial resources, and free practical items like maternity and baby supplies.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free pregnancy tests, maternity and baby items, referrals to medical, financial, housing, legal, and social assistance, and professional counseling. Services are available for as long as needed with a 24/7 helpline.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Women experiencing unplanned or crisis pregnancies
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Pregnancy tests, maternity and baby items, referrals, and support services
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Located in Prince Frederick, Calvert County, MD
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the organization by phone or email, or call the free 24-hour helpline at 1-800-550-4900 for immediate assistance.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Calvert Alliance Against Substance Abuse (CAASA) provides mini grants to community organizations to encourage and promote prevention education and outreach related to substance abuse.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: CAASA awards $4,000 total in mini grants distributed among community organizations for substance abuse prevention education and outreach programs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community organizations in Calvert County focused on substance abuse prevention education and outreach.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Substance abuse prevention education and outreach activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Calvert County, Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the CAASA office by phone at 410-535-3733 or email CAASA@calvertcountymd.gov to request an application. The 2026-2027 application is available starting May 1, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_name: CCPR Therapeutic Recreation Scholarship Fee Assistance Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides financial assistance (scholarship) to help eligible Calvert County residents participate in recreational and leisure programs offered by Calvert County Parks and Recreation (CCPR). The program is administered through the Therapeutic Recreation division and is designed to offset or eliminate the cost of program and activity fees, making recreation accessible to individuals and families who need additional financial support, with a particular focus on those with disabilities or therapeutic recreation needs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance (scholarship) that reduces or eliminates the cost of participating in Calvert County Parks and Recreation programs and activities. The program focuses on residents with disabilities or therapeutic recreation needs, though it is open to any resident needing financial support to participate in recreational and leisure programs. Specific dollar amounts and terms are described in the application form.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Calvert County residents, particularly those with disabilities or therapeutic recreation needs, or who require financial assistance to participate in Parks and Recreation programs and activities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reducing or covering fees for Parks and Recreation recreational and leisure programs and activities, including therapeutic recreation activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Calvert County, Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete the CCPR TR Scholarship Fee Assistance application form (PDF) available on the Calvert County website and submit it to Parks & Recreation staff. The application form is available at: https://www.calvertcountymd.gov/DocumentCenter/View/46590/CCPR-TR-Scholarship-Fee-Assistance-Application-v2

structured_extraction.program_description: A program at Calvert Pines Senior Center that supports seniors with developmental disabilities in participating in senior center activities. It provides structured weekday activities and helps participants independently access the same programs and services available to all seniors at the center.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides structured weekday activities and support for seniors with developmental disabilities at Calvert Pines Senior Center. A professional knowledgeable about the needs of seniors with developmental disabilities supports participants in accessing senior center programs and services.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Persons aged 55 and older who have a developmental disability and can participate in senior center activities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participation in structured weekday activities and senior center programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Calvert County, Maryland — located at Calvert Pines Senior Center in Prince Frederick.
requirements_list: Must be aged 55 or older
Must have a developmental disability
Must be able to participate in senior center activities
Must be accepted by the Maryland Developmental Disabilities Administration for daytime funding (or contact the office if funding is not in place)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Calvert County Office on Aging at 410-535-4606 or ooamailbox@calvertcountymd.gov for information about enrollment and funding requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: Calvert County offers a property tax credit to new or expanding businesses that make significant investments and create new jobs in target industries. The credit applies to county property taxes on real property, and in some cases personal property.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax credit of up to 50% of county property taxes due in any taxable year. If the business generates electricity, the credit may also apply to personal property taxes. Eligibility requires hiring at least 25 new full-time employees in target industries, paying above-average salaries, and spending at least $2.5 million on land, building improvements, or equipment in Calvert County.
structured_extraction.program_audience: New or expanding businesses in Calvert County target industries that own real property
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of county property tax liability
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Calvert County, Maryland
requirements_list: Business must be new or expanding
Must own the land, building, and personal property, or be responsible for paying real property taxes
Must employ at least 25 new additional full-time employees in county target industries
Individual compensation for new positions must exceed the annual average salary in Calvert County for similar positions
Must spend at least $2.5 million on land, improvements, or equipment in Calvert County
Credit shall not exceed 50% of property tax due in any taxable year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Calvert County Department of Economic Development for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Calvert County Commerce Zone Tax Credits
structured_extraction.program_description: A Calvert County designation that extends tax credits to qualifying new and expanding businesses located within the Patuxent Business Park Commerce Zone area.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax credits are available to qualifying new and expanding businesses that locate within the Calvert County Commerce Zone at Patuxent Business Park. Specific credit amounts and terms are detailed in the program incentives document.
structured_extraction.program_audience: New and expanding businesses relocating to or growing within the Patuxent Business Park Commerce Zone in Calvert County, MD.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credits to offset costs for qualifying businesses operating within the Commerce Zone.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to businesses located within the Patuxent Business Park, which is also a federal Opportunity Zone, in Calvert County, MD.
requirements_list: Business must be new or expanding
Business must be located within the Calvert County Commerce Zone at Patuxent Business Park
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Fill out the online inquiry form on the Patuxent Business Park page and a representative will contact you. Additional details available in the PBP Incentives PDF.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Calvert County Diaper Bank distributes diapers and diaper supplies to families in need on a monthly and emergency basis through partner organizations in Calvert County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free diapers and diaper essentials provided monthly and in emergency situations to families in Calvert County through partner distribution organizations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with young children in need of diaper supplies in Calvert County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Diapers and diaper essentials for infants and toddlers
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to families in Calvert County, MD
requirements_list: Must be a resident of Calvert County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the online request form available on the Calvert County Baby Supplies & Furniture page to request diapers.

structured_extraction.program_name: Calvert County Economic Development Incentive Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: Calvert County offers the Economic Development Incentive Fund to companies that want to expand or locate in Calvert County. The fund is available to businesses that can demonstrate significant economic impact and operate in the county's target industries.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Discretionary financial incentive provided by the Calvert County Board of County Commissioners. Terms and conditions vary. Requires the company to create at least 10 new full-time jobs, make a capital investment of at least $1 million, and remain in Calvert County for at least five years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Companies looking to expand or relocate to Calvert County in target industries
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business expansion or new operations/facilities in Calvert County
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Calvert County, Maryland
requirements_list: Establish new operations or facilities in Calvert County or significantly expand existing operations
Create at least 10 new full-time or full-time equivalent jobs
Make a capital investment of at least $1 million
Remain in Calvert County for at least five years
Request must be consistent with the county's Comprehensive Plan
Must be in the county's target industries
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Calvert County Department of Economic Development for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Calvert County Economic Development Loan Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: A revolving loan fund offered by Calvert County that provides an alternative funding source for business expansion and economic growth in the county. The fund is designed to finance new capital expansion projects, grow the commercial tax base, and increase business and employment opportunities. It is available to well-qualified businesses in manufacturing, wholesale trade, retail trade, and professional/business services sectors, and selected start-ups may also be eligible.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Revolving loans ranging from $2,500 to $150,000. Funds may be used for purchasing fixed assets, equipment, inventory, financing contracts, and business expansion in Calvert County. The fund may not be used for debt refinancing. Selected start-ups may also be eligible in addition to established businesses.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Well-qualified businesses in manufacturing, wholesale trade, retail trade, or professional/business services looking to expand or operate in Calvert County; selected start-ups may also be eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of fixed assets, equipment, inventory, financing contracts, and business expansion in Calvert County. Cannot be used for debt refinancing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Calvert County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Primary sales or activities must be in manufacturing, wholesale trade, retail trade, and/or business services
Must be a legal entity qualified to do business in Maryland
Must have a minimum 2-year operating history with a completed business plan (selected start-ups may be eligible)
Maximum loan request is $150,000; minimum is $2,500
Cannot be used for debt refinancing
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Email Kathy MacAdams, Business Retention Specialist, at kathy.macadams@calvertcountymd.gov to apply or ask questions. You may also call 410-535-4583 for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Calvert County Mosquito Control Spray Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Calvert County offers Ultra Low Volume (ULV) truck spraying to control adult mosquitoes in qualifying communities. The county splits the cost with participating communities and operates the program under Maryland Department of Agriculture guidelines.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The county charges $62 per hour for ULV truck spraying. If a community qualifies (at least 10 homes, with 8 requesting service), the county covers half the cost. The actual cost to the community varies by season, mosquito population, and weather conditions.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annual — communities must request service every year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential communities in Calvert County with at least 10 homes, 8 of which request mosquito control spraying service.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: ULV truck spraying to control adult mosquito populations in residential communities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to qualifying communities within Calvert County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Community must have at least 10 homes
At least 8 homes must request service
Community must submit a Request for Service form annually
Spraying is only performed on assigned days (two days per week)
Spraying cannot occur during rain, unfavorable winds, extreme temperatures, or RED air quality days
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Communities submit a Request for Service form each year. Forms are available online or upon request from Mosquito Control. Individuals who want to be excluded from spraying must submit an Exemption from Adult Mosquito Control Spraying form.

structured_extraction.program_name: Calvert County Parks & Recreation Mobile Food Vending Permit
structured_extraction.program_description: A permit that allows mobile food vendors to provide food service in Calvert County parks and facilities for private and public events. All food vendors must be approved and permitted before serving at any county park or facility.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Calvert County Parks & Recreation issues a Mobile Food Vendor permit that allows approved vendors to operate at county parks and facilities. Once approved, the agreement is valid for one year and kept on file. After initial approval, vendors only need to notify Parks & Recreation at least 48 hours before each future service date.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: All documents must be received a minimum of 10 days prior to the date of first service.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Mobile food vendors seeking to operate at Calvert County parks and facilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Permit to provide food vending services at Calvert County Parks & Recreation parks and facilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Calvert County, Maryland
requirements_list: Copy of valid Calvert County Health Department Mobile Food Vendor Permit
Copy of State of Maryland Business License and proof of good standing through Maryland SDAT
Proof of General Liability Insurance listing Calvert County, Maryland as additionally insured ($1,000,000 per occurrence)
Proof of motor vehicle insurance and copy of valid driver's license of vehicle operator
Proposed complete menu to be served at the location
Photograph or detailed drawing of vending unit and/or vehicle
Proof of background check clearance for all employees who will work at the location
All documents must be received at least 10 days before the first date of service
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a completed Mobile Food Vendor Agreement, completed Mobile Food Vendor Application, and all required supporting documents to Parks & Recreation by email at patricia.ballute@calvertcountymd.gov or by U.S. Mail to 175 Main Street, Prince Frederick, MD 20678. All employees must also complete a background check through the Calvert County Parks & Recreation application site.

structured_extraction.program_name: Calvert County Property Tax Credit for Disabled Law Enforcement Officers, Rescue Workers, and Surviving Spouses
structured_extraction.program_description: A Calvert County property tax credit for totally and permanently disabled law enforcement officers, rescue workers, or their surviving spouses. The credit applies to the applicant's principal residence and reduces county property tax liability. Eligible applicants include disabled law enforcement officers or rescue workers who became disabled in the line of duty, as well as surviving spouses of such individuals.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of county property taxes on a principal residence
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to qualifying residents in Calvert County, Maryland

Property must be the applicant's principal residence
Property must be located in Calvert County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the application form provided in the county ordinance or download the PDF application from the Calvert County Treasurer's Office forms page. Submit the completed application to the Calvert County Treasurer's Office.

structured_extraction.program_name: Calvert County Property Tax Credit for Volunteer Fire, Rescue & EMS Company Members
structured_extraction.program_description: A Calvert County property tax credit for members of Calvert County volunteer fire, rescue, and EMS companies who own real property and meet the qualifications set out in the county resolution.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A property tax credit against the Calvert County property tax on real property owned by qualifying members of Calvert County volunteer fire, rescue, and EMS companies.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of county property taxes on real property owned by qualifying volunteer emergency service members
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to qualifying volunteers serving in Calvert County, Maryland

Must meet qualifications specified in the resolution
Must own real property in Calvert County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Calvert County Fire, Rescue & EMS Office at (410) 535-1600 ext. 2368 for application details.

structured_extraction.program_name: Calvert County Property Tax Refund for Disabled Veterans
structured_extraction.program_description: Calvert County issues refunds of property taxes paid by veterans after they are officially deemed disabled by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Refund of property taxes previously paid by veterans who are determined to be disabled by the Veterans Administration. The refund amount is not specified on the page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Veterans in Calvert County who have been deemed disabled by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Refund of county property taxes already paid by qualifying disabled veterans
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to qualifying veterans in Calvert County, Maryland

structured_extraction.program_name: Calvert County Public Schools Free and Reduced Price Meals
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides free or reduced-price breakfast and lunch meals to eligible students in Calvert County Public Schools. Eligibility is based on household size and income. As of July 1, 2025, reduced-price meals are converted to free meals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free breakfast and lunch meals for eligible students. Reduced-price meals converted to free meals as of July 1, 2025. Normal meal costs: Breakfast $1.65; Elementary Lunch $2.80; Secondary Lunch $3.00. Benefit period: July 1, 2025 – June 30, 2026.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted year-round; no stated deadline
structured_extraction.program_audience: School-age children enrolled in Calvert County Public Schools whose households meet income eligibility requirements
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free or reduced-price breakfast and lunch meals for eligible students
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Calvert County Public Schools students, Calvert County, Maryland
requirements_list: Household gross income at or below Federal Income Eligibility Guidelines, OR
Household receives SNAP or TCA benefits, OR
Student is a foster child, homeless, runaway, migrant, or enrolled in Head Start/Early Head Start/Even Start, OR
Student certified through Maryland Direct Certification System or Medicaid matched
U.S. citizenship required
One application per household required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Parents or guardians submit the Meal Benefit Application. The application is available on the school district website and is accepted year-round.

structured_extraction.program_name: Calvert County Supplement to State Homeowners Property Tax Credit Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Calvert County supplements the State of Maryland's Homeowners Property Tax Credit Program to help lower-income homeowners reduce their property tax burden. The county has offered this additional credit since July 1, 2006. Homeowners with gross household income under $60,000 can apply using a single application (Form HTC-60) to receive both state and county credits.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A county-level property tax credit that supplements the State of Maryland Homeowners Property Tax Credit. Eligible homeowners with gross household income under $60,000 may receive credits against their county property taxes. One application (Form HTC-60) covers both the state and county credits.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: September 1 each year (often extended to October 31)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Calvert County homeowners with gross household income under $60,000
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of county property taxes on a principal residence
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to homeowners in Calvert County, Maryland
requirements_list: Gross household income must be less than $60,000
Must be a homeowner in Calvert County
Must submit Form HTC-60 along with a copy of your federal income tax return
Application must be filed by September 1 each year (often extended to October 31)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete Form HTC-60 (available from the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation or the Calvert County Treasurer's Office). structured_extraction.program_name: Hazard Mitigation Assistance Grants for Residents
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides grant funding to homeowners with high-hazard properties in Calvert County to reduce risk from floods and other natural hazards. Grants cover up to 75% of project costs for eligible mitigation projects such as property acquisition and demolition or structure elevation. The homeowner is responsible for the remaining 25% and any cost overruns.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants cover up to 75% of eligible project costs. The homeowner pays the remaining 25% plus any cost overruns. Two main project types are funded: (1) Acquisition and Demolition — voluntary purchase of the property, demolition of the structure, and return to natural state; available for high-risk cliff properties and National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) Repetitive Loss/Severe Repetitive Loss flood properties. (2) Elevation — lifting a flood-plain structure onto a new foundation above the Base Flood Elevation; available for NFIP-insured flood-plain properties, with priority for Repetitive Loss/Severe Repetitive Loss properties. Note: As of April 4, 2025, FEMA ended the Building Resilient Infrastructure and Communities (BRIC) program, so cliff house mitigation funding is currently unavailable. Flood mitigation funding through the Flood Mitigation Assistance (FMA) program remains available.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: NLT July 1st for pre-screening questionnaire; August 31st final deadline for application materials
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners in Calvert County with high-hazard properties, including flood-plain properties and (when funding is available) cliff-side properties
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property acquisition and demolition to return land to natural state, or elevation of flood-plain structures above Base Flood Elevation
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Calvert County, Maryland. Properties must be in a high-hazard area such as a flood plain or along cliffs.
requirements_list: Property must be a high-hazard property (flood plain or cliff-side)
For Acquisition & Demolition (Flood): copy of NFIP insurance and documentation of past flood events
For Acquisition & Demolition (Cliff): certified imminent threat letter from an engineer (note: cliff funding currently unavailable)
For Acquisition & Demolition (all): property appraisal, plat survey, color photos of the house, itemized cost estimate for demolition

For Elevation (Flood only): plat survey, color photos, NFIP insurance policy documentation, documentation of past flood events, elevation certificate, certified structural stability letter from engineer, itemized cost estimate for elevation
Repetitive Loss and Severe Repetitive Loss NFIP properties are most competitive
Pre-Screening Questionnaire must be submitted by July 1st
Final application materials must be submitted to CCDEM by August 31st
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Submit the Pre-Screening Questionnaire by July 1st. CCDEM will contact you with additional information. 2. Gather and submit all required application materials to CCDEM by August 31st. 3. CCDEM develops and submits a subapplication to FEMA by mid-November (initial review) and late January (final submission). 4. FEMA releases funding decisions in late summer. 5. Funding is allocated to states and projects kick off in mid-spring the following year. The full process from initiation to funding award takes up to two years.

structured_extraction.program_name: Housing Authority of Calvert County - Housing Choice Voucher Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Housing Authority of Calvert County (HACC) administers federal Housing Choice Vouchers (HCV), funded by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD), that allow low-income families to rent quality housing from private landlords throughout Calvert County. HACC pays a portion of eligible families' monthly rent directly to the property owner each month. Families can use their vouchers to rent a house or apartment from private property owners throughout Calvert County. The program is intended to help families develop personal, economic, and social skills to transition from subsidized to non-subsidized housing. Note: as of September 2024, there is currently a 5-year waitlist for this program.

structured_extraction.program_description: Calvert County provides free mosquito fish to residents to stock in ornamental ponds and stormwater ponds. These fish eat mosquito larvae and help reduce the adult mosquito population without the need for chemical treatments.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Stocking ponds with mosquito fish to control mosquito larvae naturally.

Must have an ornamental pond or know of a nearby stormwater pond suitable for stocking

structured_extraction.program_name: Motion for Waiver of Family Services Fees
structured_extraction.program_description: Calvert County Circuit Court's Family Services Office may fully or partially waive fees for eligible family law services. Parties who qualify based on significantly limited income can request a fee waiver within 14 days of the Order date. If the court approves the motion, the Family Services Office pays a portion of the fee for each approved waiver, subject to documented need and available funds.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Full or partial waiver of Family Services fees for eligible parties. The Family Services Office pays a portion of each approved waiver based on documented financial need and available funds.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Within 14 days of the Order date
structured_extraction.program_audience: Self-represented parties or those with legal representation who have received a Family Services Order and have significantly limited income.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Covers court-ordered Family Services fees that parties cannot afford to pay.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to parties in cases heard by the Circuit Court for Calvert County in Prince Frederick, MD.
requirements_list: Must file within 14 days of the Order date
Must demonstrate significantly limited income
Must complete the Motion for Waiver of Family Services Fees Form including the Affidavit (pages 2–4)
No blanks may be left on the form
Affidavit must be notarized by a Notary Public
Must submit supporting verification documents (incomplete applications will not be processed)
Must send a copy of the motion and affidavit to the opposing party (Certificate of Service)
Determination is subject to funds availability
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Motion for Waiver of Family Services Fees Form and fill out the Affidavit section (pages 2–4). Have the Affidavit notarized. Submit the completed Motion and Affidavit to the Family Services Coordinator at the Circuit Court for Calvert County, 175 Main Street, Prince Frederick, MD 20678. Send a copy to the opposing party. If represented by an attorney, complete only the Affidavit portion, have it notarized, and give it to your attorney to file the motion on your behalf.

structured_extraction.program_description: A prescription drug discount card program administered through the National Association of Counties (NACo) and CVS Caremark that helps Calvert County residents reduce the cost of prescription medications at more than 59,000 pharmacies nationwide, including major chains and many independent pharmacies. The card also includes a safety feature that alerts pharmacists to potential drug interactions when multiple prescriptions are filled using the NACo card, and can be used to cover drugs not covered by Medicare Part D.

The card includes a safety feature that alerts pharmacists to potential drug interactions when multiple prescriptions are filled using the NACo card, and can be used to cover drugs not covered by Medicare Part D.

No enrollment forms required

structured_extraction.program_description: Operation Second Chance provides financial assistance to post-9/11 combat-wounded veterans and their families who are receiving care at a military healthcare facility. Assistance covers essential expenses such as rent or mortgage, utility bills, childcare during illness or surgery, and housing or airfare for a family member supporting an injured or recovering service member. The program also offers scholarships for dependent high school seniors of qualifying service members.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants covering rent/mortgage, utility bills (electric, gas, water, sewer), childcare during illness or surgery, and housing or airfare for a family member assisting an injured or recovering service member. Scholarships are also available for dependent high school seniors of qualifying service members.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Post-9/11 combat-wounded veterans currently receiving care at a military healthcare facility with an expected VA/military rating of at least 70%
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rent/mortgage, utility bills, childcare during illness or surgery, housing/airfare for a family member assisting an injured or recovering service member
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: National program; available to eligible veterans regardless of location
requirements_list: Must be a post-9/11 combat-wounded veteran currently receiving care at a military healthcare facility
Must have an expected military or VA rating of at least 70%, or be active duty with a Purple Heart
Priority given to combat-related injuries
Must have at least 6 months of active duty status
Total family income must not exceed $4,000 per month (exceptions for families larger than 6)
Must have an honorable discharge listed on DD214
Completed applications must be submitted through a caseworker or VA representative
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Have your service liaison, chain of command, or care provider request an application by emailing assistance@operationsecondchance.org. Completed applications must be submitted through a caseworker or VA representative.

structured_extraction.program_description: Calvert County Public Transportation provides curb-to-curb paratransit service for elderly residents and people with disabilities who cannot use the standard fixed-route bus service. The service runs Monday through Friday on four demand-response routes within the county. Riders are assisted beyond the curb on a case-by-case basis when needed.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Curb-to-curb paratransit transportation provided on four demand-response routes operating Monday through Friday within Calvert County. Service is available during the same days and hours as fixed bus routes. Case-by-case assistance beyond the curb is available when needed.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Elderly residents and individuals with disabilities who are unable to use the fixed-route bus system in Calvert County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Transportation to and from destinations within Calvert County for qualifying individuals with disabilities or elderly riders.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available within Calvert County, Maryland. Visiting ADA-certified individuals from other jurisdictions are also served for eligible trips.
requirements_list: Must be elderly or have a disability that prevents use of the fixed-route bus service
Must complete an ADA Application Form or Senior Application
Must demonstrate inability to use the fixed-route bus system where available
Applications reviewed and processed within 21 business days
Visitors staying more than 21 days must formally apply for eligibility certification
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete an ADA Application Form or Senior Application and mail it to Calvert County Public Transportation, 175 Main Street, Prince Frederick, MD 20678. Applications are reviewed within 21 business days. Applicants are notified in writing of their eligibility. If not notified within 21 business days, contact the office — service will be provided until the application is processed. Incomplete applications are returned for completion and resubmission. Denied applicants have 60 days to file a written appeal.

structured_extraction.program_description: Calvert County residents who pump out their septic tank or upgrade to a nitrogen-removing tank can enter a drawing to win cash reimbursement or other prizes. The contest is run by the Calvert County Environmental Commission to reduce pollution flowing into the Chesapeake Bay and protect local groundwater.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Winners receive a cash reimbursement or other prizes awarded by drawing. To enter, residents must either upgrade to a nitrogen-removing septic tank (using a Bay Restoration Fund Grant) or hire a company to pump out their septic tank, then submit their paid receipt. The drawing is held at the Environmental Commission's January meeting and winners are notified by letter.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: First Wednesday of January by 4 p.m.

structured_extraction.program_description: Allows eligible Agricultural Preservation District landowners to sell TDRs to Calvert County, which then retires (permanently removes) those development rights rather than reselling them. This reduces overall development density in the county. Applications are ranked and offers are made until funding runs out.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible Agricultural Preservation District owners can sell TDRs to the county at $6,230 per TDR (FY2026 approved price). Unlike the TDR Reserve, the county retires these rights permanently, reducing density rather than moving it elsewhere. Applications are ranked by the APAB and offers are made until funding is exhausted.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of Agricultural Preservation Districts in Calvert County who want to sell and permanently retire TDRs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Sale proceeds go to the APD landowner. The county retires the TDRs, permanently reducing development density.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only in Calvert County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must own an Agricultural Preservation District in Calvert County
Applications accepted September through December
Applications are ranked by the Agricultural Preservation Advisory Board (APAB)
Offers made until annual funding is exhausted
Transactions conclude by June
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application September through December. APAB reviews and ranks applications December through January. Offer letters are sent January through February. Transactions conclude by June.

structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available nationally where military installations exist, including in Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_description: A local preference program that gives Calvert County-based businesses a competitive advantage when bidding on county procurement contracts. Authorized by Maryland law, it allows qualifying resident businesses to be awarded contracts even if their bids exceed the lowest responsive bid by a specified percentage. Eligible resident businesses receive a 5% deduction on their bid price compared to non-resident competitors, helping local businesses win more county contracts and supporting economic growth in the county.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Qualifying resident businesses (those with a principal office in Calvert County) that submit responsive bids exceeding the lowest responsive bid by a nonresident business by not more than a specified percentage may be awarded the contract. For informal solicitations valued between $10,000 and $29,999.99, the preference is a 5% deduction on the bid price. For formal solicitations of $30,000 or more, the preference is 5% up to a maximum of $25,000. The preference applies to both goods and services procured through formal and informal solicitations. The program was authorized by state law effective October 1, 2024, with the County Commissioners required to comply with MD Local Government Article §§ 9–105 and 9–106 when enacting the ordinance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Resident businesses with their principal office located in Calvert County, Maryland that are bidding on county government procurement contracts.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The preference reduces a resident business's effective bid price when competing for county procurement contracts for goods and services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Business must have its principal office located in Calvert County, Maryland. A P.O. box cannot be used to establish a local address.
requirements_list: Principal office must be located in Calvert County
Must submit a responsive bid
Bid may exceed lowest responsive nonresident bid by not more than a specified percentage
A P.O. box cannot be used to establish a local or principal address
County Commissioners must comply with MD Local Government Article §§ 9–105 and 9–106 when enacting ordinance
Does not apply where federal or state law prohibits local preferences
Does not apply to contracts awarded through cooperative agreements or piggybacking other jurisdictions' contracts
Does not apply to emergency purchases
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible businesses participate in the normal county procurement bidding process. If a resident business submits a bid that is not the lowest, the Procurement Office applies the 5% preference. If the resident business declines the preference award, the contract is awarded to the lowest non-resident business. The specific application process is defined in the Calvert County ordinance enacted under authority of the state statute.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Sustainable Communities designation, established by Maryland's Sustainable Communities Act of 2010, provides a locally designated geographic focus area to target public and private resources for state agency investments and revitalization efforts. Local governments can apply for designation and renewal every five years to access technical assistance and prioritized state funding for community reinvestment and revitalization projects.

Designation enables local governments to receive technical assistance and access targeted state funding for reinvestment and revitalization within the designated area.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments seeking to designate or renew a Sustainable Communities area to access state resources for community revitalization.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Community reinvestment and revitalization activities within the designated Sustainable Communities area.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Calvert County, Maryland. The county received its first designation on August 21, 2013, and was seeking renewal by August 21, 2023.
requirements_list: Must be a local government
Designation must be renewed every five years

Must report on accomplishments made over the past five years
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Local government submits a renewal application to update the existing Sustainable Communities action plan, report on accomplishments from the past five years, request additional technical assistance, and highlight areas where progress is still needed.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that provides replacement capital to help Calvert County businesses and nonprofits offset county support service charges required to host a special event. The goal is to encourage events that create destination awareness, increase overnight stays, and generate visitor spending in Calvert County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $25,000 per organization per fiscal year (July–June), or up to 5 grant applications per fiscal year, whichever comes first. Grant funds are paid directly from the county to the appropriate county departments — no money passes through the applicant organization.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: At least 30 days prior to the special event
structured_extraction.program_audience: Calvert County businesses and nonprofits that are hosting a special event requiring county support services
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Offsetting county support service charges required for a special event, such as fees paid to county departments and offices
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be located in Calvert County, Maryland, and the special event must take place in Calvert County.
requirements_list: Applicant must be an adult (18+)
Application must be submitted at least 30 days before the special event
Must have completed and submitted a Special Events Permit application for the current fiscal year
Must have received an estimate of Calvert County support services costs from the Calvert County Events and Marketing Coordinator
Business or nonprofit must be in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
Must have no outstanding Calvert County violations (e.g. zoning violations), overdue taxes, or assessments
The special event must demonstrate the ability to create destination awareness for Calvert County
The special event must have the ability to increase overnight stays in Calvert County
The special event must have the potential to increase visitor spending in-market
The special event must have a measurable positive economic impact
After the event, the permittee must report attendance numbers and success measures to the Department of Economic Development
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Review the Special Events Permit policy and process. 2. Complete and submit a Special Events Application. 3. Receive an estimate of county support services costs from the Calvert County Events and Marketing Coordinator. 4. Submit the Tourism Development Incentive Fund Grant application online at least 30 days before the event. 5. Receive a confirmation or denial email within 10 business days.

structured_extraction.program_description: Allows landowners in Agricultural Preservation Districts to sell TDRs directly to Calvert County government instead of finding a private buyer. The county then resells those TDRs to developers. This revolving fund helps preserve farmland and forests while giving landowners a guaranteed buyer for their development rights.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The county buys TDRs from Agricultural Preservation District owners at $6,230 per TDR on a first-come, first-served basis, subject to available funding. There is a 1% administrative fee. The county resells TDRs to developers at the same price paid plus the 1% administrative fee. Owners of record of TDRs previously conveyed from the original APD are also eligible to sell.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of Agricultural Preservation Districts or holders of TDRs conveyed from an APD who want to sell TDRs to the county; developers who want to purchase TDRs from the county to increase density on receiving area properties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Sale proceeds go to the TDR holder. Purchased TDRs are used by developers to increase permitted density in designated residential growth areas.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only in Calvert County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be the owner of record of an Agricultural Preservation District or of TDRs previously conveyed from an APD
Subject to available funding and TDR supply (first-come, first-served)
1% administrative fee applies to all transactions
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the application to sell or purchase TDRs to the Department of Planning & Zoning. Applications are processed on a first-come, first-served basis as funding and supply allow. Fillable application forms are available for both selling and purchasing TDRs.

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary incentive program that recognizes and encourages community floodplain management activities that go beyond the minimum requirements of the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP). Communities that participate receive discounted flood insurance premium rates for their residents, reflecting the reduced flood risk from local actions. Premium discounts range from 5% to 45% for properties in the Special Flood Hazard Area (SFHA) and 0% to 10% for non-SFHA properties, based on the community's CRS classification (Classes 1-10). Calvert County participates in the CRS Program, requiring the county to protect the 100-year floodplain, educate the public, and provide floodplain information and data resources. In return, county residents who own property with structures in the 100-year floodplain receive a 10% discount on their flood insurance premiums when they start or renew their policies. The City of Annapolis also participates, offering similar discounts to property owners who benefit from the city's floodplain management activities that exceed minimum NFIP requirements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Flood insurance premium discounts for property owners in participating communities. Premium discounts range from 5% to 45% for properties in the Special Flood Hazard Area (SFHA) and 0% to 10% for non-SFHA properties, based on the community's CRS classification (Classes 1-10). In Calvert County, eligible residents receive a 10% discount on their National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) flood insurance premiums when they initiate or renew their policies, applicable to properties with structures located within the 100-year floodplain. Discounts reflect the reduced flood risk resulting from community floodplain management activities that exceed minimum NFIP requirements. Technical guidance and resources are also provided to participating communities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments and their residents seeking reduced flood insurance premiums through community floodplain management activities, including Calvert County residents who own property with structures located within the 100-year floodplain and Annapolis residents in participating communities. Also applicable to local government officials and property owners in any community participating in the NFIP.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction in flood insurance premiums; reducing flood damage to insurable property, strengthening the insurance aspects of the NFIP, and encouraging a comprehensive approach to floodplain management.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to property owners within the 100-year floodplain in Calvert County, Maryland, and to communities in Annapolis, MD that participate in the NFIP and exceed minimum floodplain management requirements. Nationally available to all municipalities and local jurisdictions in full compliance with NFIP rules and regulations.

Community (incorporated or unincorporated) must be in full compliance with NFIP rules and regulations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: In Calvert County, the discount is automatically applied when residents initiate or renew their flood insurance policies through the NFIP, effective May 1, 2015. structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Investment Note® is a fixed income debt security issued by Calvert Impact Capital, Inc. (Calvert Social Investment Foundation) that channels investor capital — starting at just $20 — to a diversified portfolio of organizations creating measurable social and environmental impact in communities across the U.S. and around the world. The portfolio covers affordable housing, renewable energy, small business finance, sustainable agriculture, microfinance, education, health, gender equity, and other community development sectors, focusing on areas underserved by traditional capital markets. Since 1995, Calvert Impact has made over 1,000 loans and investments to more than 550 organizations across 100+ countries. The current portfolio balance is approximately $577.7 million across ~92–100 active loans and investments in 111 countries, with a cumulative investor repayment rate of 100% and a portfolio repayment rate of over 99%. Capital is deployed as loans and investments to recipient organizations, with fixed income returns paid to investors depending on the issuer's financial condition at the time payment is due. The Note is not FDIC or SIPC insured and is subject to risk of loss of principal. Calvert Impact is headquartered in Bethesda, Maryland.

The portfolio currently holds approximately $577.7 million across 92–100 active loans and investments in 111 countries. Since 1995, Calvert Impact has made over 1,000 loans and investments to more than 550 organizations across 100+ countries. structured_extraction.program_description: The Cut Carbon Note® is an asset-backed, investment-grade rated, fixed-income debt security offered by Calvert Impact Climate, Inc. that finances energy efficiency improvements and sustainability upgrades for a portfolio of green commercial, industrial, multifamily, and non-profit buildings across the United States, with the goal of reducing carbon emissions. Investors purchase notes and the proceeds fund building efficiency projects such as HVAC, building envelope improvements, electrical and lighting, plumbing, solar PV installation, insulation, windows, elevators, water conservation, seismic retrofit, hurricane protection, and other sustainability measures. Notes are backed by Commercial Property Assessed Clean Energy (CPACE) instruments and are available to retail and institutional investors with a minimum investment of $1,000. The program incentivizes developers to meet rigorous low-carbon and zero-carbon building standards (CIRRUS™ Low Carbon Standard) and provides investors with semi-annual impact reporting. The program is designated a Green Bond by Calvert Impact, Inc. and aligns with Green Bond Principles published by the International Capital Market Association.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Investors can purchase fixed-income notes through brokerage accounts with a minimum investment of $1,000. Notes are asset-backed by Commercial Property Assessed Clean Energy (CPACE) instruments and are secured investment-grade rated. Notes are available in three classes: Class A, B, and C with fixed interest rates set at issuance. The most recent offering (Series 2025-1) included Class A notes at 6.30% interest ($44,296,000; AAA rated), Class B at 6.55% ($452,000; AA rated), and Class C at 6.85% ($452,000; BBB rated), with a total offering of $400 million across all series. The expected weighted-average life is 8.6 years, with a final legal maturity of 12/15/2053. The total portfolio balance is $100,796,100 across 20 projects in 11 states nationwide. Notes are purchased through brokerage accounts using CUSIPs. The offering periods for the first three series have closed; future series availability can be requested by contacting Calvert Impact. Notes are not FDIC or SIPC insured. Underlying CPACE financing terms average 27.56-year loan terms at a weighted-average annual interest rate of 7.40%, with financing amounts up to 95% of property value and semi-annual payment installments.

structured_extraction.program_name: Partner Community Capital (formerly Natural Capital Investment Fund) Lending and Technical Assistance
structured_extraction.program_description: Partner Community Capital (PCAP) is a certified community development financial institution (CDFI) that provides loans and technical assistance to small businesses and enterprises in Central Appalachia and the Southeast. PCAP focuses on triple-bottom-line enterprises that promote equity, protect the environment, and grow the economy, including healthy local food, specialty agriculture, renewable energy, energy efficiency, eco- and heritage tourism, child and adult day care, primary healthcare, and small town main street redevelopment. In 2024, PCAP lent more than $26 million and provided over 13,000 hours of technical assistance to 5,058 small businesses, prospective borrowers, and clients of its West Virginia Women's Business Center.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: PCAP provides loans to eligible enterprises promoting a healthy environment and healthy families. In 2024, PCAP lent more than $26 million, primarily serving low- and moderate-income individuals. PCAP also delivers technical assistance — in 2024, it provided over 13,000 hours of technical assistance to 5,058 small businesses, prospective borrowers, and clients of its West Virginia Women's Business Center.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses, enterprises, and entrepreneurs in Central Appalachia and the Southeast, particularly those serving low- and moderate-income individuals and communities, with a focus on environmental and natural-resource-based businesses and vital community services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business operations, renewable energy projects, facility acquisition and development, and other capital needs supporting environmental sustainability, healthy food systems, community services, and economic development for triple-bottom-line enterprises.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Primarily serves West Virginia and North Carolina; also serves Appalachian regions of surrounding states including Maryland, Georgia, Kentucky, Ohio, South Carolina, Tennessee, and Virginia.
requirements_list: Must be an enterprise that promotes a healthy environment and/or healthy families
Must operate in Central Appalachia or the Southeast United States

Preference for enterprises in sectors such as healthy local food, specialty agriculture, renewable energy, energy efficiency, eco- and heritage tourism, child and adult day care, primary healthcare, or small town main street redevelopment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Partner Community Capital directly through their website at partnercap.org to inquire about lending and technical assistance opportunities.

structured_extraction.program_description: A multi-million dollar fund that provides flexible, affordable loans and free business support services to small businesses and nonprofits recovering from economic hardship across 15 southern states, including Maryland. The fund works through local Community Development Financial Institutions (CDFIs) to reach small and historically underbanked businesses.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans of up to $100,000 for small businesses and nonprofits with fewer than 50 full-time employees. Loans are flexible and affordable. Free business support and advisory services are also provided through CDFI lenders.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses and nonprofits with fewer than 50 full-time employees, particularly those that are historically underbanked, located in 15 southern states including Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business recovery and economic resilience support.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Alabama, Arkansas, Delaware, Florida, Georgia, Louisiana, Maryland, Mississippi, North Carolina, Oklahoma, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Virginia, West Virginia, and the District of Columbia.
requirements_list: Fewer than 50 full-time employees
Located in one of the 15 covered southern states or DC
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants register interest at www.TheSoarFund.org and are notified when the application portal opens. Once open, applicants sign up online and are matched with a CDFI lender who assists with the application and provides advisory support.

structured_extraction.program_description: Calvert Impact originates, facilitates, and administers private debt transactions for institutional lenders seeking high-impact exposure in private credit. The service helps mission-driven organizations raise and manage capital more efficiently while giving lenders unique access to impact deals across sectors including affordable housing, community development, renewable energy, environmental sustainability, microfinance, and small business. Calvert Impact has syndicated 22 facilities totaling more than $300 million, engaging more than 30 institutional lenders including financial institutions, philanthropic foundations, and family offices across domestic and international markets.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Calvert Impact syndicates private debt facilities ranging from $15 million to $50 million in size. Institutional lenders can participate with a minimum commitment of $1 million per deal. Calvert Impact has syndicated 22 facilities totaling more than $300 million, engaging more than 30 institutional lenders (financial institutions, philanthropic foundations, and family offices) across domestic and international markets.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital deployment and capital raised through syndicated debt facilities can be used by mission-driven borrowers and community-focused intermediaries for affordable housing, community development, small business lending, renewable energy, environmental sustainability, microfinance, and other impact sectors.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Domestic and international markets served; Calvert Impact is headquartered in Bethesda, Maryland. No specific geographic restriction stated.

structured_extraction.program_description: AMP connects Caroline County high school students with local manufacturers and technical employers. Students nominated by teachers tour local manufacturing facilities, learn about career opportunities, and can apply for internships with participating companies during the school year or summer.

structured_extraction.program_name: Caroline County EMS Ambulance Subscription Plan
structured_extraction.program_description: Caroline County's Ambulance Subscription Plan protects enrolled residents and businesses from unexpected out-of-pocket costs for emergency ambulance transportation to the hospital. Enrolled members will not be billed for emergency ambulance transport by Caroline County providers. Membership fees also support local volunteer fire companies and county paramedics.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Enrolled individuals and businesses are protected from emergency ambulance transportation charges. Individual plans start at $25/year; family of two at $45/year; family of three or more at $75/year. Business plans cost $100 for up to 10 employees, $150 for 11–25 employees, and $200 for more than 25 employees. Membership fees support county paramedics and volunteer fire/EMS companies.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Caroline County residents, families, and businesses seeking protection from unexpected out-of-pocket emergency ambulance transportation costs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Coverage of emergency ambulance transportation costs from home to hospital; funds also support volunteer fire companies and county paramedics.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents and businesses located in Caroline County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a Caroline County resident or business
Number of family members or employees listed must match the selected plan level
Business plan applicants must upload a current employee roster
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the online enrollment form on the program page, including personal or business information, plan type selection, and authorization agreement. After submitting, you are directed to a payment processing page.

structured_extraction.program_description: A local real property tax credit offered by Caroline County to incentivize new and/or expanding manufacturing businesses to invest in the county. The credit offsets property taxes on the increased assessed value resulting from facility expansion or new construction, helping manufacturing companies reduce costs associated with growth investments. Companies receive a 100% credit on the real property tax tied to the increased assessed value of their expansion or new construction for five consecutive years. The program applies only to Caroline County real property taxes, not municipal taxes. The business must recertify its eligibility each year between May 1 and October 1. The program is available to businesses relocating to or expanding in Caroline County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A real property tax credit equal to 100% of the real property tax attributable to the increased assessable value of facility expansion or new construction. The credit may be claimed for up to five consecutive years. Requires a minimum investment increase in assessed value of more than $50,000 and at least 15 new full-time jobs related to the expansion. Relocated employees cannot be counted as additional employees. The business must annually recertify eligibility between May 1 and October 1 each year. The credit applies only to Caroline County real property taxes, not municipal or state taxes.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling, must be filed within one year of the expanded or newly constructed facility's placement on the tax roll.
structured_extraction.program_audience: New and expanding manufacturing businesses (manufacturers, fabricators, and assemblers) in Caroline County investing in expansion or new construction projects, including businesses relocating to the county
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Facility expansion or new construction by manufacturing businesses; offsets real property tax costs associated with capital investment in Caroline County based on the increased assessed value of the property
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to manufacturing businesses located in or relocating to Caroline County, Maryland. The tax credit applies only to Caroline County real property taxes, not municipal or state taxes.
requirements_list: Must be a new or expanding manufacturing company (manufacturer, fabricator, or assembler)
The expansion or new construction must increase the property's assessed value by more than $50,000
Must create and hire at least 15 new full-time jobs related to the expansion at the facility location
Relocated employees cannot be counted as additional employees
New employees must receive at least the federal minimum wage
The employer must provide a basic employee benefit plan that includes medical insurance, leave, and a pension for all full-time employees
The business must annually certify that it continues to meet the program requirements between May 1 and October 1 each year
Applicants must not be in default on any Caroline County or Maryland state taxes
No unpaid real property or business personal property taxes
Current year business personal property tax return must be filed with Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
Application must be filed within one year of the new or expanded facility being added to the county tax roll
For leased property, both lessor and lessee must execute the application with proof of lessee's tax liability
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: An owner or their authorized representative must file an application with the County Commissioners within one year of the new or expanded facility being added to the county tax roll. The application must be submitted under oath and include all requested information and supporting documentation, including a copy of the Caroline County real property tax bill. For leased property, both lessor and lessee must execute the application with proof of lessee's tax liability. Applicants use an official form provided by the County Commissioners. The Commissioners will expeditiously approve or deny the application. The application form and Article II are available for download from the Caroline County Economic Development website at: https://www.carolinebusiness.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/11/Caroline-Manufacturing-Tax-Credit-Application.pdf. Contact CCED for guidance.

When adult mosquitoes become a nuisance and public health threat, fogging trucks are deployed to affected areas.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: County-provided mosquito control services including property inspections and fogging. Fee is $165 for the first acre and $4 for each additional acre for residential properties. Towns and larger properties receive an estimated cost per application. Payment is due at the time the application is received.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Mosquito breeding area inspections, removal or control of breeding areas, and fogging of adult mosquitoes on enrolled properties.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a subscription/registration form and payment in early spring. County staff will personally visit the property, inspect for breeding areas, and provide recommendations. Contact Public Works at 410-479-0520 for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Caroline County Public Schools Youth Apprenticeship Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A work-based learning program run by Caroline County Public Schools in partnership with Maryland's Apprenticeship Maryland Program that connects local businesses with qualified high school students for real-world job training. Students split their time between classroom instruction and hands-on work experience at the Caroline Career & Technology Center, building workplace skills, professional networks, and exploring career paths. Students work alongside employers in a variety of industries, gain practical experience, may earn professional certifications, and earn school credits — all while receiving a paycheck. Businesses that participate gain early access to motivated young talent, can mentor students in specific skills and work habits, and receive quality work at an affordable wage. The program is distinct from traditional apprenticeships and internships; students are paid employees providing real value to the business.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Businesses receive motivated student workers who split time between school and the workplace. Students earn school credits and may earn professional certifications while developing technical and professional skills under the guidance of employee mentors. Fields include human resources, carpentry, engineering, horticulture, marketing, logistics, mechanics, technical roles, and more. Students are hired as paid employees — not unpaid interns — providing quality work at an affordable wage. Students receive parallel education at Caroline County Public Schools and the Caroline Career & Technology Center. The program aligns with students' educational and career goals as well as CTE center programs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Caroline County high school students seeking real-world career experience and school credits, and local businesses interested in hiring, mentoring, and developing young talent to build a workforce pipeline.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Provides businesses with access to trained, motivated student workers at an affordable wage; provides students with paid, hands-on career training, school credits, and potential professional certification.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to students and businesses in Caroline County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Students must be currently enrolled in a Caroline County high school
Students are hired as paid workers — not as unpaid interns
Students sign a Youth Apprenticeship contract with a participating business
Businesses provide a mentor to guide and support the student
Positions should align with CTE center programs or careers offering a livable wage and growth potential
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Eric Cook, Coordinator of College Career & CTE, at cook.eric@ccpsstaff.org or 410-479-1460, or visit the CCPS Youth Apprenticeship page at https://www.carolineschools.org/page/youth-apprenticeship for more information.

Applicants who qualify pay only 50% of the regular program fee, with the option to use a payment plan for the remaining balance.

Submit the registration form along with 50% of the program cost by mail, fax, email, or in person. Applications without payment are considered incomplete.

Homeowners who already receive the State Homeowners Credit automatically receive this credit without filing a separate county form. Once the county form is filed, it does not need to be resubmitted in future years.

Seniors who already receive the State Homeowners Credit will automatically receive this credit without filing the county form. A one-time application is required for those who do not receive the State Homeowners Credit. Once the county form is filed, no further filings are required in future years.

structured_extraction.program_name: Caroline County Small Business Loan Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Caroline County Economic Development administers a revolving small business loan fund to help small and agriculture-based businesses start up or expand in Caroline County. The program provides gap financing and working capital that cannot be obtained through traditional lenders, as well as funding for equipment purchases and inventory, including processing and packaging equipment for agritourism and agriculture-based businesses. Most loans are under $10,000, with a maximum of $20,000. Loan applicants must have already arranged or attempted traditional financing. The program has been used by restaurants and agritourism businesses for startup and expansion. Loan funds must be repaid under terms agreed upon with the County Commissioners of Caroline County, and repayment is required regardless of business standing or if the business relocates outside of Caroline County. Funds cannot be used to pay off existing debt, reimburse owners, or pay delinquent taxes.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Revolving loan fund providing gap financing and working capital to small businesses. Most loans are under $10,000, with a maximum of $20,000. Funds can be used for commercial real estate acquisition, new construction, building improvements, equipment purchases (including processing and packaging equipment), inventory purchases, business start-up costs, and up to 12 months of operating capital that cannot be financed through traditional lenders. Loan funds must be repaid under terms agreed upon with the County Commissioners; applicants sign a promissory note. A $25 application fee applies for resubmitted applications. Funds cannot be used to finance existing debt, reimburse owners or equity partners, buy out partners, pay personal expenses, invest in non-owner occupied real estate, or pay delinquent federal, state, or local taxes. Repayment is required if the business relocates outside of Caroline County.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small business owners and agriculture-based businesses in Caroline County, Maryland seeking financing to start up or expand, particularly those that have already arranged or attempted traditional financing and need additional gap funding, including restaurants and agritourism businesses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Commercial real estate acquisition, new construction, building improvements, equipment purchases (including processing and packaging equipment), inventory purchases, business start-up costs, and up to 12 months of operating capital. Cannot be used to finance existing debt, reimburse owners or equity partners, buy out partners, pay personal expenses, invest in non-owner occupied real estate, or pay delinquent federal, state, or local taxes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Business must be physically located or expanding in Caroline County, Maryland. Property must be in good standing with Town and County planning and codes regulations. Loan repayment is required if the business moves outside of Caroline County.

Must not have been subject to judgment or bankruptcy within the last ten years
No pending litigation
All taxes for the business or individual must be current
Project must benefit Caroline County (develop vacant/underutilized property, eliminate blight, or create new permanent full-time jobs)
Minimum 10% personal investment into the project
One active loan per business owner
Must submit a completed application

Must provide a personal financial statement for each owner
Must provide a credit report for each owner

Must provide current balance sheet and profit/loss statements for the preceding two years
Must provide business financial projections for three years
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the online application form or download and print the PDF version and mail to Caroline County Economic Development, c/o Debbie Bowden, 425 Colonial Drive, Denton, MD 21629. Submit all required attachments including business plan, credit report, personal financial statements, tax returns, balance sheet, profit/loss statements, and three-year financial projections. Incomplete applications will be returned. A $25 application fee applies for resubmitted applications. Staff review submissions and make recommendations to the County Commissioners, who make final loan approval decisions.

structured_extraction.program_description: Caroline County residents can purchase an annual permit that allows them to drop off solid waste at three county courtesy drop-off sites. The program is designed to make solid waste services self-funding, with permit fees directly supporting the courtesy sites.

Replacement permits are available free of charge in limited circumstances (sale of vehicle, theft of vehicle, or loss of windshield).
