structured_extraction.program_name: Economic Edge: The Caroline County Business Academy
structured_extraction.program_description: A free 8-week cohort-based business training and education program for small business owners and entrepreneurs in Caroline County, Maryland. The program covers topics such as building sustainable business infrastructure, leading people, marketing, accounting, human resources, legal issues, taxes, insurance, and preparing to access capital. Classes are held via Zoom on Tuesday evenings (approximately 6–9 p.m.) and are led by Will Holmes Consulting. Participants engage in one-on-one mentor sessions, submit weekly assignments, and deliver a final 15-minute PowerPoint presentation. Graduates who complete all requirements receive a Certificate of Completion. Space is limited to 15 participants per cohort. The program is funded through a partnership with the Mid-Shore Regional Council (MSRC) using a grant from the Rural Maryland Prosperity Investment Fund (RMPIF), administered by the Rural Maryland Council (RMC).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free 8-week business training program (no cost to participants) consisting of 8 Zoom sessions held Tuesdays from approximately 6–9 p.m. Covers organizational infrastructure, leadership and growth planning, marketing, accounting, human resources, legal structure, taxes, insurance, and capital preparation. Includes one-on-one mentor sessions and a final 15-minute PowerPoint presentation. Space is limited to 15 participants per cohort. Participants who complete all requirements — attending all classes, submitting weekly assignments, meeting with mentors, presenting cash flow projections, and delivering a final presentation — receive a Certificate of Completion. Funded through the Rural Maryland Prosperity Investment Fund (RMPIF) via the Mid-Shore Regional Council (MSRC) and the Rural Maryland Council (RMC).

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business training and technical assistance covering organizational infrastructure, leadership and growth planning, marketing, accounting, human resources, legal issues, taxes, insurance, and preparation to access capital. Not a cash grant to participants.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to businesses and entrepreneurs located in Caroline County, Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_description: A credit against state, county, and municipal property taxes for owner-occupied properties. It limits how much a property's taxable assessment can increase each year, protecting homeowners from large tax increases due to rapidly rising assessments. The credit caps the state-taxable assessment increase at 10% per year and the county-taxable assessment increase at 5% per year, reducing property tax liability growth for eligible owner-occupied principal residences.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Caps the increase in the state-taxable assessment at 10% per year and the county-taxable assessment at 5% per year for eligible owner-occupied properties. Requires a one-time application to the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of property tax liability by capping taxable assessment increases year over year
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Property must be owner-occupied (principal residence)

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a one-time application to the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation. More information available at https://dat.maryland.gov/Pages/Tax-Credit-Programs.aspx.

structured_extraction.program_description: Caroline County's Transferable Development Rights (TDR) Program allows landowners to identify, sell, purchase, and use development rights. The program designates Receiving Areas where rural-residential development is allowed (up to 50 lots) and Sending Areas (rural and farming zones) where development rights can be transferred off a property. The goal is to manage county-wide growth planning while preserving farmland, woodland, and the rural landscape.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program assigns Receiving Areas (maximum 50 lots) in R-Rural zoning districts suited for residential growth and Sending Areas where development rights can be transferred off properties in rural/farming zones. Landowners in Sending Areas can sell their development rights, while buyers in Receiving Areas can purchase rights to enable additional development.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners in Caroline County's R-Rural zoning district, including those in designated Sending Areas (who wish to transfer development rights) and Receiving Areas (who wish to purchase development rights).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Transfer of development rights from rural/farming Sending Areas to designated Receiving Areas to allow rural-residential development while preserving farmland and rural landscape.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Caroline County, Maryland, specifically in R-Rural zoning districts designated as Sending Areas or Receiving Areas.
requirements_list: Property must be located in Caroline County's R-Rural zoning district
Properties in Sending Areas may transfer development rights off the property
Properties in Receiving Areas may receive transferred development rights for rural-residential development (maximum 50 lots)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Matt Kaczynski, Development Review Coordinator, at 410-479-8100 for detailed information. The Planning Commission reviews the program yearly to determine boundary line adjustments to the Receiving Area.

structured_extraction.program_description: Carroll County Workforce Development (BERC) places local youth ages 16–18 with local Carroll County businesses for summer paid work experience at no cost to the employer. Carroll County Government hires the participants, handles all paperwork, and covers all wages, taxes, and insurance through dedicated grant/county funding, removing all financial risk for participating businesses. The program runs for approximately six weeks (July through August) and aims to employ approximately 25 youths per cycle. Youth participants must have never worked before or have one or more barriers to employment. In addition to job placement, the program includes on-site job skills training, virtual soft skills instruction, and career readiness programming such as mock interviews, job fairs, career assessments, and professional skills enrichment days. Eligible host businesses include those in recreation, retail, childcare, restaurant, office, farm, and other sectors. Youth participants earn approximately $12.50/hour, paid through county workforce grants.

Carroll County covers all wages, taxes, and insurance for youth participants through dedicated grant/county funding. Businesses receive no-cost temporary labor and mentoring support at zero financial risk. Youth also receive career readiness training including mock interviews, job fairs, career assessments, and professional skills enrichment days.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Wages, taxes, and insurance for youth participants during the six-week summer work experience program; career readiness and professional skills training for youth participants. Businesses receive no-cost temporary labor (in areas such as recreation, retail, childcare, restaurant, office, and farms) and mentoring support.

Businesses and youth may also contact youth program coordinator Eileen Vozzella at 410-386-2807 or evozzella@carrollcountymd.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Carroll County Government grant program funded through the Fiber Network Enterprise Fund that helps businesses (including home-based businesses) and Internet Service Providers (ISPs) connect to high-speed internet in unserved or underserved areas of Carroll County. The program funds 'last-mile' broadband connections by leasing county-owned fiber optic infrastructure, and also helps cover the cost of obtaining internet service for eligible Carroll County businesses. It operates as a matching grant program, reimbursing up to 50% of qualified project expenses for constructing, acquiring, or leasing facilities, wireless spectrum, land, towers, or buildings used to deploy broadband service for businesses and residentially based businesses in Carroll County. Unserved areas are defined as those with no fixed internet access at 25 Mbps download/3 Mbps upload; underserved areas are defined as those with fewer than two providers offering 100 Mbps download/20 Mbps upload.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to 50% matching reimbursement of qualified project expenses, capped at $25,000 per approved project and $100,000 per entity or service provider per fiscal year, subject to allocations approved by the Carroll County Board of Commissioners. Total grant funding available is up to $200,000. Funds are disbursed as reimbursement after eligible expenses are incurred. Eligible expenses include construction, acquisition, or leasing of facilities, wireless spectrum, land, towers, or buildings used to deploy broadband service for businesses and residentially based businesses in Carroll County.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Carroll County businesses (including home-based businesses) with unmet broadband needs or requiring internet redundancy for business continuity, and Internet Service Providers (ISPs) or service providers planning to provide service in unserved or underserved areas of Carroll County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Last-mile broadband infrastructure connections to bring high-speed internet service to commercial, industrial, and residentially-based businesses in underserved or unserved areas of Carroll County; construction, acquisition, or leasing of facilities, wireless spectrum, land, towers, or buildings used to deploy broadband service; capital investment in broadband infrastructure including equipment, construction, and fiber laterals; and general costs of providing internet service to eligible businesses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to businesses (including home-based businesses) and ISPs/service providers operating in unserved or underserved areas of Carroll County, Maryland. Unserved means no fixed internet access at 25 Mbps download/3 Mbps upload. Underserved means fewer than two providers offering 100 Mbps download/20 Mbps upload.

structured_extraction.program_name: Carroll County Restaurant Relief (Phase 1 and Phase 2)
structured_extraction.program_description: A COVID-19 relief grant program providing financial assistance to restaurants, breweries, distilleries, wineries, food trucks, and service organizations with commercial kitchens in Carroll County impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic. Funded through Maryland's 'Maryland Strong: Economic Recovery Initiative,' the program operated in two phases. Phase 1 (launched November 23, 2020) offered grants of $5,000 for businesses with 9 or fewer FTE employees or $10,000 for businesses with 10–50 FTE employees, with total program funding of $1.2 million and funds disbursed by December 31, 2020. Phase 2 offered grants of $3,000 for businesses with 9 or fewer FTE employees or food trucks (regardless of employee count), or $8,000 for businesses with 10–50 FTE employees, with applications accepted January 11–February 1, 2021. The program expanded in November 2020 to include service organizations with commercial kitchens. National/regional chains, franchises, and publicly traded companies are not eligible. Previous grant recipients were eligible to apply in Phase 2. The program ran from approximately April 2020 through June 2021 and is no longer available.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Phase 1: Grants of $5,000 for businesses with 9 or fewer FTE employees, or $10,000 for businesses with 10–50 FTE employees; total program funding of $1.2 million, with funds disbursed by December 31, 2020. Phase 2: Grants of $3,000 for businesses with 9 or fewer FTE employees or food trucks (regardless of employee count), or $8,000 for businesses with 10–50 FTE employees. FTE employees are counted as working 30 or more hours per week. Payroll is not an eligible expense. A grant agreement must be executed with each awardee and all grant documents kept for five years.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Phase 1: December 8, 2020 at 12:00 noon; Phase 2: February 1, 2021 at 4:00 PM
structured_extraction.program_audience: Carroll County restaurants, food trucks, breweries, distilleries, wineries, and service organizations with commercial kitchens established by March 1, 2020 and open and operating as of January 1, 2021. Must have 50 or fewer FTE employees. National/regional chains, franchises, and publicly traded companies are not eligible.

structured_extraction.program_name: Carroll County Workforce Development (Business/Employment Resource Center)
structured_extraction.program_description: Carroll County Workforce Development, formerly known as the Business/Employment Resource Center (BERC), is a workforce development center that helps job seekers and businesses in Carroll County. It is part of America's Job Network and aims to develop a highly trained workforce for new and existing businesses, help individuals find employment, and encourage lifelong learning. Services include job search assistance, résumé development, career counseling, skills assessment and training, apprenticeships, youth employment programs, veteran employment programs, and customized business training. Individuals who lost a job or are underemployed may also be eligible for additional training support. Federal funding for Program Year 2021 totaled $2,909,562.68 (representing 87% of available funds).

Services are available Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Federal funding for Program Year 2021 totaled $2,909,562.68 (representing 87% of available funds).

structured_extraction.program_name: Carroll Long Driveway – Hard to Connect Program (Difficult to Serve – Long Driveway Grant Program)
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program to help Carroll County homeowners connect to broadband internet when they have long driveways that internet service providers will not connect for free as part of a standard installation. The county received a state grant to help unserved residents pay for the extra cost of running a connection from existing broadband infrastructure to their home. The grant provides up to $14,000 to eligible homeowners to cover the cost of connecting their home to a nearby provider's network. Costs above $14,000 must be paid by the homeowner, and the grant does not cover equipment or ongoing service fees.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time grant of up to $14,000 per eligible home to cover the cost of extending a broadband connection from existing infrastructure to the home along a long driveway. Costs above $14,000 must be paid by the homeowner. The grant does not cover equipment or ongoing service fees. A provider must currently pass the home with its service for the property to be eligible.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Carroll County homeowners with driveways longer than what an internet service provider will connect for free during a standard installation, located in currently unserved areas where a broadband provider currently passes the home with its service.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cost of extending a broadband connection from existing infrastructure to the home along a long driveway. Does not cover equipment or monthly service fees.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a home in Carroll County, Maryland. Homes in areas already scheduled for future broadband installation are not eligible.
requirements_list: Must be a homeowner in Carroll County
Home must have existing broadband, internet, or cable TV infrastructure passing by it
Driveway must be longer than what the internet service provider will connect for free
Maximum grant is $14,000; amounts above that must be paid by the homeowner
Homes scheduled for future broadband installation are not eligible
Only one grant per house or address (apartments or businesses sharing the address cannot apply for a second grant)
Grants are not retroactive — homeowners who have already paid to connect are not eligible for reimbursement
Grant does not cover equipment or services
Must complete the Carroll County Broadband Survey and answer 'yes' to the long driveway question
Must provide name, full address, phone number, and email address in the survey
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Carroll County Broadband Survey at https://carrollcountymd.jotform.com/form/230754830587059 and answer 'yes' to the long driveway question. Once submitted, the county checks the address for eligibility with the service provider. If the grant is awarded, all respondents who answered yes will be notified by email about their eligibility status.

structured_extraction.program_description: A COVID-19 recovery grant program providing financial assistance to small businesses, home-based businesses, nonprofits, sole proprietors, and farmers/agribusiness operations in Carroll County, administered by the Carroll County Department of Economic Development from April 2020 through June 2021. Awards were based on financial need and the pandemic's impact on the applicant. Grant tiers included up to $2,000 for home-based and small businesses not in commercial or industrial zones, a matching grant for restaurants doubling their initial award, and a $5,000 grant for farmers and agricultural producers to offset COVID-19-related losses. The program is no longer available.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants awarded based on financial need and the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. Grant tiers: up to $2,000 for home-based and small businesses not in commercial or industrial zones; restaurants receive a matching grant doubling their initial award; farmers and agricultural producers are eligible for a $5,000 grant to offset COVID-19-related losses. Grants range from $2,000 to $8,000 depending on business size and location. Funds may be used for IT upgrades and e-commerce programs, marketing, employee training, commercial cleaning, professional services, equipment or vehicle expenses, COVID-19 health-related expenses (PPE, supplies, plexiglass shields, masks), and agricultural revenue loss offsets. Ineligible uses include wages, lease or mortgage payments, utilities, insurance, and non-COVID-19 expenses. Program ran from April 2020 through June 2021 and is now closed.

structured_extraction.program_name: Coronavirus State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds (SLFRF) / American Rescue Plan – Carroll County Projects
structured_extraction.program_description: Federal relief funds provided to Carroll County under the American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) Coronavirus State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds (SLFRF) program. Funds help address the COVID-19 pandemic's public health and economic impacts, including COVID-19 response efforts, replacement of lost public sector revenue, stabilization of households and businesses, premium pay for essential workers, investments in water, sewer, stormwater, and broadband infrastructure, and support for Carroll County citizens seeking access to work and learning opportunities, occupational training, and apprenticeships. $1,236,750 was awarded to Carroll County for employment and training initiatives through the Business/Employment Resource Center (BERC). Total allocation across all projects: $32,718,855.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal SLFRF funding allocated by Carroll County for eligible projects including COVID-19 response, economic stabilization, revenue replacement, premium pay for essential workers, and infrastructure investments in water, stormwater, sewer, and broadband. Specific allocations include: HVAC system upgrades ($3.5M), broadband/fiber infrastructure ($17.8M), wastewater treatment facility ($3.5M), behavioral healthcare non-profits ($3.4M), water treatment ($500K), technology/emergency equipment, family shelter design, and facilities improvements. Additionally, $1,236,750 was awarded to provide Carroll County citizens access to work and learning opportunities, occupational training, and apprenticeships through the BERC. Funding obligated by 12/31/24; Period of Performance: 3/11/21–12/31/26.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Funding obligated by 12/31/24; Period of Performance: 3/11/21–12/31/26
structured_extraction.program_audience: Carroll County government entities and departments, municipal governments, local non-profits (behavioral healthcare), Internet Service Providers, community recipients eligible under federal SLFRF guidelines (including households, businesses, and public services affected by COVID-19), and Carroll County citizens seeking employment, training, or career advancement.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: COVID-19 response; economic stabilization for households and businesses; replacement of lost public sector revenue; premium pay for essential workers; water/stormwater/sewer infrastructure; broadband infrastructure; HVAC and facility upgrades; wastewater treatment; emergency services equipment; behavioral health services; family shelter design and construction; technology systems; work and learning opportunities; occupational training; and apprenticeships.

requirements_list: Projects must fall within one of the eligible SLFRF project categories: COVID-19 response, negative economic impact relief, hardest-hit community support, revenue replacement, premium pay, water/sewer/stormwater infrastructure, or broadband infrastructure.

structured_extraction.program_name: Industrial Development Authority of Carroll County (IDA)

The IDA Board of Directors, made up of five volunteer members appointed by the Board of County Commissioners, works to benefit Carroll County residents and businesses.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Economic development, job retention, industry attraction, and promoting a balanced economy in Carroll County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Carroll County, Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Paige Sunderland at 410-386-2314 for more information. The IDA holds monthly meetings generally on the last Tuesday of each month at 8:30 AM.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that helps Maryland employers and Registered Apprenticeship sponsors offset the cost of training Registered Apprentices. Employers can receive up to $3,000 per newly registered adult apprentice or up to $7,500 per newly registered high school level apprentice to cover eligible training expenses. Designed to strengthen Registered Apprenticeships across Maryland by supporting workforce development goals and incentivizing high-quality apprenticeship opportunities leading to sustainable employment and career advancement.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Employers or sponsors of Registered Apprentices may receive up to $3,000 per newly registered adult apprentice or up to $7,500 per newly registered high school level apprentice (HSLRA) to reimburse eligible training expenses such as tuition, fees, books, materials, mentorship costs, recruitment expenses, disability accommodations, and supportive services (including driver's licenses, transportation, uniforms, tools, childcare, union fees, and application fees).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications must be submitted within 30 days of an apprentice's initial registration with MD Labor. MD Labor encourages submission 30 days prior to registration but accepts applications up to 30 days after registration. One-time exception for FY 2026: applicants may apply for apprentices registered since July 1, 2025.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Tayaabah Qazi (Grant Program Manager, Office of Strategic Initiatives)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland employers and Registered Apprenticeship sponsors who hire and register new apprentices with MD Labor; any size company, any industry
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Instructional expenses (tuition, fees, books, materials), mentorship and on-the-job learning expenses, apprentice recruitment expenses, costs associated with disability accommodations, and supportive services for apprentices (driver's licenses, transportation, uniforms, tools, childcare, union fees, application fees)
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to Maryland-based employers and Registered Apprenticeship sponsors
requirements_list: Applications must be submitted within 30 days of an apprentice's initial registration with the MD Labor Office of Apprenticeship
MD Labor encourages submission 30 days prior to registration but accepts applications up to 30 days after registration
Apprentices must be within their first year of employment as a Registered Apprentice
Apprentices must remain employed and registered for at least seven months following application submission

A one-time exception to the 30-day deadline is available for employers who hired a new Registered Apprentice between March 1, 2025 and January 28, 2026, registered the apprentice within 30 days of hire, and the apprentice completed or will complete seven months in the program on or after October 1, 2025
FY 2026 exception: applicants may apply for apprentices registered since July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a funding application (Excel form) within 30 days of an apprentice's initial registration with MD Labor. Review the program policy and invoice for reimbursement (PDF) for full terms and requirements. Contact marylandapprenticeship.incentiveprogram@maryland.gov for additional information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Heritage Areas Authority Emergency Grants

The grants help organizations continue to steward heritage resources and remain ready to reopen to the public after the crisis. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis with deadlines on the first of each month until funds are exhausted.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Heritage tourism nonprofit organizations located within one of Maryland's 13 Certified Heritage Areas
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Emergency operating expenditures for heritage tourism nonprofits impacted by COVID-19, including lost revenue from event admissions, tour groups, memberships, and donations, to keep organizations operational during the pandemic.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be located within the boundaries of one of Maryland's 13 Certified Heritage Areas in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a nonprofit organization

Must have been impacted by the COVID-19 public health emergency
Must provide matching funds

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Recovery Now! – Carroll County Nonprofit Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A COVID-19 recovery grant program under the Maryland Recovery Now! initiative providing grant funding to Carroll County 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations, veterans' organizations, and volunteer fire departments to help offset the financial impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. Administered by the Carroll County Department of Economic Development in partnership with the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD). The program ran from April 2020 through June 2021 and is closed and no longer accepting applications.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding totaling over $500,000 available for Carroll County 501(c)(3) nonprofits, veterans' organizations (501(c)(19) and 501(c)(23)), and Carroll County Volunteer Fire Departments. Awards are tiered: $10,000 for nonprofits with 0–9 FTE employees (30+ hours/week) and $15,000 for nonprofits with 10+ FTE employees (30+ hours/week). Awards are based on demonstrated need. Priority is given to nonprofits that did not receive Nonprofit Recovery Initiative (NORI) funding from DHCD in 2020. Reimbursable expenses cover March 1, 2020 – December 31, 2021.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Carroll County 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations, veterans' organizations (501(c)(19) and 501(c)(23)), and Carroll County Volunteer Fire Departments affected by COVID-19
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Offsetting financial impacts and recovery costs from COVID-19 pandemic, including payroll, inventory, utilities, rent, marketing, technology, professional services, insurance, and COVID-related items such as PPE. Reimbursable expenses for March 1, 2020 – December 31, 2021.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Carroll County, Maryland — applicants must be physically located in and serving Carroll County
requirements_list: Must be an independent 501(c)(3) organization, veterans' organization (501(c)(19) or 501(c)(23)), or Carroll County Volunteer Fire Department
Must not be under an umbrella organization
Must have a physical location in and be serving Carroll County
Must have been established prior to September 1, 2019
Must be in good standing with the IRS
Priority given to nonprofits that did not receive NORI funding in 2020
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Program is closed. Applications were accepted beginning April 12, 2021 at noon through April 23, 2021 at 4pm via carrollbiz.org. Reference materials available via linked PDF at https://carrollbiz.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/CarrollRebound_nonprofits.pdf.

structured_extraction.program_name: Online Sales and Telework Assistance COVID Relief Grant Program (MD Relief Act 2021) – Round II
structured_extraction.program_description: A COVID-19 relief grant program under the Maryland Relief Act of 2021, funded through the Maryland Economic Development Assistance Authority and Fund (MEDAAF) and administered by the Carroll County Department of Economic Development. The program provided reimbursement grants to Carroll County for-profit businesses to help cover costs related to implementing online sales platforms or enabling employee telework due to the financial impacts of COVID-19. The program ran in two rounds: the first round opened April 7, 2021 (up to $1,000 per business, running through April 20, 2021 or until funds exhausted, totaling $13,915.48 in awards), and a second round (Round II) opened August 24, 2021 (up to $5,000 per business, running through September 7, 2021 or until funds exhausted). Both rounds are now closed. Priority was given to businesses that had not previously received a COVID-19 Business Relief Grant or Loan from the Maryland Department of Commerce or Labor, and to businesses with fewer than 20 employees. Ineligible entities included non-profits, faith-based organizations, independent contractors (e.g., realtors, hair stylists, MLM), national/regional chains, publicly traded companies, franchises, and real estate holding companies.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Round I: Reimbursement grants of up to $1,000 per business (total pool: $13,915.48). Round II: Reimbursement grants of up to $5,000 per business. Both rounds covered eligible expenses incurred after March 2020 and not previously reimbursed by other federal, state, or county grant programs. Funds cover IT upgrades supporting online sales infrastructure and hardware, software, or subscriptions enabling employee telework.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Round I: April 7, 2021 at 12 noon through April 20, 2021 at 4pm or when funds exhausted. Round II: August 24, 2021 at 12 noon through September 7, 2021 at 4pm or when funds exhausted. Both rounds are now closed.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Jack Lyburn, Director, Department of Economic Development
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit businesses located and operating in Carroll County that expanded online sales or teleworking capabilities due to COVID-19, with priority given to businesses that have not received prior COVID-19 relief grants or loans from the Maryland Department of Commerce or Labor, and those with fewer than 20 employees (excluding owner).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: IT upgrades to support online sales infrastructure; hardware, software, and subscriptions to facilitate employee telework; costs incurred after March 2020 not previously reimbursed by other programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Business must be located in Carroll County (in a Commercial/Industrial Zone for Round I) and currently open and operating in Carroll County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a for-profit entity
Established and operating prior to March 9, 2020
Located and currently open and operating in Carroll County
Expanded online sales or teleworking capabilities due to COVID-19
Currently registered in good standing with the State of Maryland and Carroll County
Current on all taxes owed to the State of Maryland and Carroll County
Priority given to businesses that have not received a COVID-19 Business Relief Grant or Loan from the Maryland Department of Commerce or Labor
Priority given to businesses with fewer than 20 employees (excluding owner)

Ineligible: non-profits, faith-based organizations, independent contractors (realtors, hair stylists, MLM), national/regional chains, publicly traded companies, franchises, real estate holding companies
Fully completed application
Completed and signed IRS Form W-9
MD SDAT Certificate of Good Standing
Recent payroll summary showing number of employees
Copies of paid invoices for eligible reimbursement expenses
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Program is closed. Round I opened April 7, 2021 at noon and accepted applications through April 20, 2021 at 4pm or until funds were exhausted. Round II opened August 24, 2021 at noon and accepted applications through September 7, 2021 at 4pm or until funds were exhausted. Applicants submitted a fully completed online application with required documentation (W-9, SDAT Certificate of Good Standing, payroll summary, and paid invoices) via the online portal at carrollbiz.org. Upon award, businesses were required to enter into a formal Carroll County grant agreement and retain documentation for five years. Reference materials also available via linked PDF at https://carrollbiz.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/CarrollCountyOnlineSales_TeleworkGrant.pdf.

structured_extraction.program_name: SBA Economic Injury Disaster Loan (EIDL) Program – Maryland Drought 2023
structured_extraction.program_description: Federal low-interest disaster loans for small businesses, small agricultural cooperatives, small businesses engaged in aquaculture, and most private nonprofit organizations that suffered economic losses due to the drought that began September 5, 2023 in designated Maryland counties.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal Economic Injury Disaster Loans (EIDLs) are available under SBA declaration #20069 to cover economic losses caused by the 2023 drought. Applicants apply online or by mail.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses, small agricultural cooperatives, small businesses engaged in aquaculture, and most private nonprofit organizations in designated Maryland counties with economic losses due to drought conditions beginning September 5, 2023.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Covering economic losses caused by the 2023 drought conditions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Frederick and Washington counties and the contiguous counties of Allegany, Carroll, Howard, and Montgomery in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a small business, small agricultural cooperative, small business engaged in aquaculture, or a private nonprofit organization
Must have suffered economic losses due to drought conditions that began on September 5, 2023
Must be located in or have losses tied to the designated counties: Frederick, Washington, Allegany, Carroll, Howard, or Montgomery
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at sba.gov/disaster under SBA declaration #20069, call the SBA Customer Service Center at 800-659-2955, or email DisasterCustomerService@sba.gov. structured_extraction.program_name: SBA Economic Injury Disaster Loan (EIDL) – Maryland Drought 2025
structured_extraction.program_description: The SBA offers low-interest federal disaster loans to small businesses and private nonprofit organizations that suffered economic losses due to the drought that began March 15, 2025. Loans help cover working capital needs even if the business had no physical damage.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans up to $2 million at interest rates as low as 4% for small businesses and 3.625% for private nonprofits, with repayment terms up to 30 years. Interest does not accrue and payments are not due until 12 months after the first loan disbursement. Loans may be used to pay fixed debts, payroll, accounts payable, and other bills not paid due to the disaster.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses, small agricultural cooperatives, and private nonprofit organizations in eligible Maryland counties that experienced economic losses due to the March 2025 drought. Agricultural producers, farmers, and ranchers are not eligible (except small aquaculture enterprises).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Working capital needs including fixed debts, payroll, accounts payable, and other bills left unpaid due to the disaster.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Eligible Maryland counties: Baltimore, Carroll, Cecil, Frederick, Harford, Howard, Kent, Montgomery, and Washington. Also covers counties in Pennsylvania and Virginia.
requirements_list: Must be a small business, small agricultural cooperative, or private nonprofit organization
Must have financial losses directly related to the March 15, 2025 drought
Agricultural producers, farmers, and ranchers are not eligible except for small aquaculture enterprises
Must be located in a covered disaster declaration county
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at sba.gov/disaster. Alternatively, call SBA's Customer Service Center at (800) 659-2955 or email disastercustomerservice@sba.gov. Applicants with hearing or speech disabilities can dial 7-1-1 for relay services. A 60-day grace period applies after the February 2, 2026 deadline.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest federal disaster loans are available for physical property damage and economic injury. Applications for physical property damage were due February 5, 2019, and economic injury applications were due September 9, 2019.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Physical property damage: February 5, 2019; Economic injury: September 9, 2019
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses and residents in Carroll County, Baltimore County, Frederick County, Howard County (Maryland), and York and Adams counties (Pennsylvania) affected by the November 2, 2018 severe storms and tornado.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Repair or replace physical property damaged by the disaster, or cover economic injury (operating costs) resulting from the disaster.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Carroll County and contiguous counties of Baltimore, Frederick, and Howard in Maryland, as well as York and Adams counties in Pennsylvania.
requirements_list: Must be located in a declared disaster area (Carroll County or contiguous counties)
Must have suffered losses due to the November 2, 2018 severe storms and tornado
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants can: (1) visit the Disaster Loan Outreach Center at the Carroll County Public Library – Mount Airy Branch during posted hours (December 11–18, 2018); (2) call SBA's Customer Service Center at 1-800-659-2955; (3) email disastercustomerservice@sba.gov; or (4) apply online at DisasterLoan.sba.gov.

structured_extraction.program_name: Small Business Development Center (SBDC) – Carroll County
structured_extraction.program_description: The Small Business Development Center (SBDC), operated through the Carroll County Department of Economic Development with support from the U.S. Small Business Administration, provides free one-on-one consulting and technical assistance to small business owners and entrepreneurs at any stage—from start-up to established enterprises. SBDC advisors help with business concept evaluation, business plan and marketing plan development, financial planning, startup costs, funding connections, workforce and human resources guidance, and strategies for growth. Sessions are conducted in a confidential setting at no cost to the business owner.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free confidential one-on-one consulting and advising sessions provided by SBDC counselors. Services include business concept evaluation, business plan and marketing plan development, financial planning, funding connections, workforce and HR guidance, and ongoing support for growth. Low-cost consulting services are also available.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Entrepreneurs with a new business idea and owners of established small businesses in Carroll County seeking guidance to start, grow, or improve their operations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Technical assistance only — no direct funding provided. Sessions address business planning, marketing plan development, financial planning, and connecting to funding sources.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to all business owners and entrepreneurs in Carroll County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a small business or aspiring entrepreneur
Services are free of charge
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the SBDC office at 225 N. Center Street, Suite 101, Westminster, MD by phone at 443-356-2918 or email scolella@harford.edu to schedule a counseling session. Counselors guide clients through discovery, planning, and deployment phases to address business needs.

structured_extraction.program_name: Storm Damage Reporting for Recovery Loans
structured_extraction.program_description: Carroll County Emergency Management asks businesses and residents affected by recent severe storms and flooding to report details on their losses. This information helps the county assess damage and determine if those affected could qualify for recovery loans.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reporting storm damage is the first step to potentially qualify for recovery loans. Submitting information does not guarantee assistance but helps demonstrate need and begin the recovery process.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Carroll County businesses and residents affected by severe storms and flooding in 2018
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Recovery from storm damage including business revenue losses and damage to physical property
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Carroll County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a Carroll County resident or business owner
Must have experienced losses due to recent severe storms and flooding
Must provide date and type of damage, estimate of loss, and insurance coverage information
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit damage information electronically via the online form, or contact the office at 410-386-2455 to request a form by fax or mail. Deadline was August 24, 2018.

structured_extraction.program_description: A 280-hour certificate training program that prepares students to operate commercial trucks and tractor-trailers and qualify for a CDL-A (Commercial Driver's License Class A) license. No prior trucking experience is required. Financial assistance may be available for qualified individuals through Carroll County Workforce Development.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 280-hour truck driver CDL-A certificate training program. Financial assistance may be available for qualified individuals through Carroll County Workforce Development.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals seeking a Commercial Driver's License (CDL-A) to operate commercial trucks and tractor-trailers. No prior trucking experience required.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training to obtain a CDL-A commercial driver's license; financial assistance for qualified individuals to cover program costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Carroll County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must meet driver qualifications set forth by the Bureau of Motor Carrier Safety
Must pass the physical examination requirements established by the Department of Transportation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit Carroll Community College's program page at https://www.carrollcc.edu/programs/professional-skills-job-training/truck-driver-cdl-ab-certificate/ for enrollment information. For financial assistance, contact Carroll County Workforce Development at 410-386-2820.

structured_extraction.program_name: USDA Farm Service Agency Emergency Loan and Drought Assistance Programs – Maryland Natural Disaster Designation (Drought 2025)
structured_extraction.program_description: The USDA Farm Service Agency (FSA) offers emergency loans and disaster assistance programs for agricultural producers in Maryland counties designated as natural disaster areas due to severe drought conditions. Multiple FSA programs are available to help farmers recover from drought-related crop and livestock losses, including low-interest emergency loans and several disaster assistance grant programs. Carroll County, Maryland received a natural disaster designation due to severe drought, making it and contiguous counties eligible for emergency loan assistance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest emergency loans and disaster assistance grants may be used for recovery needs including replacing essential items such as equipment or livestock, reorganizing a farming operation, or refinancing certain debts. Available programs include the Livestock Forage Disaster Program, Emergency Assistance for Livestock Program, Livestock Indemnity Program, Honeybees and Farm Raised Fish Program, Noninsured Crop Disaster Assistance, Emergency Conservation Program, and Tree Assistance Program. Loans are reviewed based on extent of losses, available security, and repayment ability.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural producers in Maryland's central and western counties (Allegany, Carroll, Frederick, Garrett, Howard, Montgomery, Washington) and contiguous counties (including Baltimore County in Maryland; Adams and York in Pennsylvania) affected by drought conditions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Replacement of essential items such as equipment or livestock, reorganization of a farming operation, or refinancing certain debts caused by drought-related crop and livestock losses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Primary designated county: Carroll, Maryland. Also available in Allegany, Frederick, Garrett, Howard, Montgomery, and Washington counties in Maryland. Contiguous counties also eligible for emergency loans: Baltimore County, Maryland; Adams and York counties in Pennsylvania.
requirements_list: Must be an agricultural producer or farmer with crops or livestock experiencing drought conditions
Must be located in one of the eligible Maryland counties: Allegany, Carroll, Frederick, Garrett, Howard, Montgomery, or Washington, or a contiguous county
County must be designated as a natural disaster area
Drought intensity of D2 Severe for 8+ consecutive weeks during growing season, or D3 Extreme or D4 Exceptional drought
Loans reviewed based on extent of losses, available security, and repayment ability
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: File a Notice of Loss or ask questions about available programs by contacting your local USDA Service Center. Carroll County service center is located at 698 Corporate Center Ct., Suite K, Westminster, MD 21157, phone (410) 848-2780. A full list of service centers is available at offices.usda.gov. Use the Disaster Assistance Discovery Tool or Loan Assistance Tool on farmers.gov to determine program or loan options.

structured_extraction.program_name: Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act (WIOA) Formula Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: Federal formula grants that fund workforce development services for job seekers and businesses in Carroll County, including job placement assistance, training, and career advancement resources.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: $861,119 in WIOA formula grants awarded for Program Year 2021 and Fiscal Year 2022 to fund workforce development services including job search assistance, occupational training, and career resources.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Carroll County job seekers, workers seeking career advancement, and businesses seeking workforce assistance
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Job placement support, training options, career advancement resources, and occupational training
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Carroll County, Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit or contact the Carroll County Business/Employment Resource Center (BERC), open Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., or visit www.carrollworks.com.

structured_extraction.program_description: Carroll County offers a tax credit against county property taxes to encourage businesses to create new jobs. Businesses that construct or expand their facilities and hire new full-time employees can receive a credit based on increased employment. The credit applies to county property taxes on the business's real estate and personal property, and decreases over a six-year period: 52% of the increased property tax in years one and two, 39% in years three and four, and 26% in years five and six. The Carroll County Department of Economic Development helps eligible businesses understand program requirements and complete the application process.
structured_extraction.agency: Carroll County Department of Economic Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A tax credit against the county property tax on real property and personal property owned by the business, based on increased employment. The credit decreases over six years: 52% of the increased property tax in years one and two, 39% in years three and four, and 26% in years five and six. To qualify, a business must construct or expand its facility by at least 5,000 square feet and hire 25 new full-time employees within the first 24 months. New positions must be new to the state of Maryland, at least 50% must pay 125% or more of the Average Weekly Wage as determined by the Maryland Department of Labor, the business must not have moved its operations from another Maryland county or Baltimore City, and must not owe any delinquent taxes to Carroll County.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit businesses that construct or expand facilities and create new full-time jobs in Carroll County, Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credit applied against county property taxes on real estate and personal property for businesses that expand their facilities and create new jobs in Carroll County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Carroll County, Maryland. The business must be located in a designated Priority Funding Area within Carroll County.
requirements_list: Must construct or expand facility by at least 5,000 square feet
Must employ at least 25 persons in new permanent full-time positions within the first 24 months
Positions must be new to the state of Maryland
At least 50% of the new positions must pay 125% or more of the county's average weekly wage as determined by the Maryland Department of Labor
Must not have moved its operations from another Maryland county or Baltimore City
Must not owe any delinquent taxes to Carroll County
Must be a qualifying business as determined by program requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: A business must declare its intent to apply for the tax credit on a form provided by the County Comptroller. Once the business meets all eligibility requirements, it can apply for certification. Apply online at the Carroll County JotForm application link provided on the program page. Contact the Carroll County economic development team for guidance on program requirements and assistance with the application process.

structured_extraction.program_description: Carroll County offers a tax credit to encourage property owners along the Finksburg MD 140 commercial corridor to visually enhance and redevelop their properties. The credit is designed to act as a catalyst for revitalization of the area. The program provides tiered property tax credits based on improvement costs relative to assessed property value, available for up to five years.
structured_extraction.agency: Carroll County Department of Economic Development, Department of Management and Budget, and Department of the Comptroller
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers a property tax credit for up to five years based on the percentage of improvement cost compared to the current assessed value of the property. For existing buildings, the credit is 75% if improvement costs exceed 25% of the assessed property value, or 50% if costs are 25% or less. For new construction, the credit is 50% if improvement costs for the building's exterior exceed 50% of the property's assessed value. The total credit cannot exceed the total cost of improvements. Credits are only granted for improvements that significantly improve the overall appearance of the property.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: on or before May 1 immediately before the first taxable year for which the tax credit is sought
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of commercial or industrial properties along the MD 140 corridor in Finksburg, Carroll County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Exterior improvements including facade upgrades (e.g., new windows, paint, roof), landscaping, signage, lighting, sidewalks, and pedestrian plazas
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties zoned for commercial or industrial use located on or adjacent to the MD 140 corridor in the Finksburg area, from the Baltimore County line to Sandymount Road, fronting MD 140 or directly adjacent to a property that does.
requirements_list: Property must be used for business, commercial, or industrial purposes.
Property must be zoned commercial or industrial (C-1, C-2, C-3, I-1, or I-2).
Property must be located on or adjacent to the MD 140 corridor from the Baltimore County line to Sandymount Road.
Improvements must significantly improve the overall appearance of the property.
Qualified improvements include exterior facade work (windows, paint, roof), landscaping, signage, lighting, sidewalks, and pedestrian plazas.
You must apply before starting the improvement project and by the May 1 deadline.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, obtain the application form from the Department of the Comptroller. Complete and sign the application, including a tax map, property photos, a detailed description of planned improvements with drawings, and a summary of costs. Submit the complete application before beginning any work and on or before May 1 immediately before the first taxable year for which the tax credit is sought. Contact Paige Sunderland, Deputy Director / Business Development, for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: Landowners establish an Agricultural Preservation District by agreeing not to develop their property for a minimum 5-year period. In return, they receive a 50% tax credit on the land value. This is the first formal step toward obtaining an agricultural easement.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Landowners receive a 50% tax credit on the land value in exchange for agreeing not to develop their property for at least 5 years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural landowners in Cecil County who want to protect their land from development.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credit applied to land value in exchange for a commitment not to develop.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Cecil County, Maryland
requirements_list: Valid Soil Conservation and Water Quality Plan (SCWQP) on file with Cecil Soil Conservation District
Agreement not to develop property for a minimum 5-year period
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Agricultural Preservation District Application and submit to the Cecil County Planning & Zoning Division. A valid Soil Conservation and Water Quality Plan must be on file with Cecil Soil Conservation District.

structured_extraction.program_name: America's Small Business Development Center (SBDC) - Cecil County
structured_extraction.program_description: The Cecil County office of America's Small Business Development Center (SBDC) provides counseling, training, and technical assistance to emerging and small businesses in Cecil County. Services cover financial management, marketing, production, organization, engineering, technical problems, and feasibility studies. The SBDC also offers affordable educational seminars throughout the year and makes special efforts to reach socially and economically disadvantaged groups, veterans, women, and people with disabilities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free or affordable one-on-one business counseling and educational seminars covering all aspects of small business management, including finance, marketing, production, organization, engineering, technical issues, and feasibility studies.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Emerging and small business owners, potential entrepreneurs, veterans, women, socially and economically disadvantaged individuals, and people with disabilities in Cecil County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Counseling and training in business management, finance, marketing, production, organization, engineering, technical problem-solving, and feasibility studies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to small businesses and entrepreneurs located in Cecil County, Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Cecil County SBDC office to schedule counseling or register for educational seminars.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides legally blind persons a $15,000 reduction in the assessed value of their dwelling house and surrounding yard for property tax purposes, upon certification by a doctor.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: $15,000 reduction in the taxable assessed value of the qualifying dwelling, lowering property taxes for legally blind persons.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No general September 1 deadline; apply at any time
structured_extraction.program_audience: Persons with central visual acuity of 20/200 or less in the better eye
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction in property tax liability
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide
requirements_list: Central visual acuity of 20/200 or less in the better eye
Must provide doctor's certification
May apply at any time; not subject to September 1 filing deadline
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Maryland Application for Exemption for Blind Persons form and submit to the State Department of Assessments and Taxation.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free six-week workshop series for people affected by cancer, including survivors, caregivers, family members, and friends. Held once a week in community settings, the workshops teach techniques for managing fatigue, pain, and stress; appropriate exercise; nutrition; communication with healthcare providers; and setting priorities. Workshops are led by trained volunteer leaders, at least one of whom is a cancer survivor.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free six-week workshops meeting once per week for 2.5 hours. Each participant receives a copy of 'Living a Healthy Life with Chronic Conditions' and an audio relaxation CD. No cost to attend.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults aged 18 and older who have been affected by cancer — including newly diagnosed patients, survivors, caregivers, family members, and friends — who have good mental functioning and can attend workshops.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Workshop participation to build self-management skills for living with cancer, including exercise, nutrition, communication, and coping techniques.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at various locations throughout Cecil County, Maryland.
requirements_list: At least 18 years old
Good mental functioning
Able to travel to workshop locations
Affected by cancer in some way (patient, survivor, caregiver, family member, or friend)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Registration is encouraged. Call Karly Lakavitch at 410-996-8170 or Holly Loss at 410-996-5168 to register or to refer someone for a free workshop.

structured_extraction.program_name: Cecil County Healthy Options Program - Seniors (H.O.P.S.)
structured_extraction.program_description: Free fitness and wellness workshops for seniors in Cecil County, including in-person, livestream, hybrid, and pre-recorded classes such as SAIL, yoga, strength training, and Rock Steady Boxing for Parkinson's disease.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: No-cost fitness and wellness workshops offered in-person, hybrid, and online. Classes include SAIL, yoga, strength training, 20/20/20, and Rock Steady Boxing for Parkinson's. Participants must register in advance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Senior residents of Cecil County, MD
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participation in free fitness and wellness classes
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must live in Cecil County, MD
requirements_list: Must register for all classes prior to attendance
Registration is open for current spring 2026 classes
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register online via SurveyMonkey links provided for each class, or call the listed contact number for phone registration.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Local Care Team connects families, caregivers, and parents with behavioral health and wellness resources for their children. The team meets with families to understand their challenges, helps brainstorm strategies, advocates on their behalf, and links children and parents to services. Ongoing support is available through alternative resource exploration.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The team provides care coordination, outreach, referrals, and ongoing support to connect families with behavioral health and wellness services. Assistance includes meeting with families, developing strategies, and linking them to community resources at no stated cost.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Caregivers, parents, and community members in Cecil County who need help finding and accessing resources for their children, particularly related to behavioral health and wellness.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Connecting families to behavioral health and wellness services, outreach coordination, and navigating community resources.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Cecil County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a family, caregiver, or parent in need of assistance finding resources for a child
A referral form can be submitted to initiate contact
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a referral by completing the Local Care Team Referral Form (available as a PDF download), emailing localcareteam@cecilcountymd.gov, or calling 443-941-7066.

structured_extraction.program_name: Cecil County Neighborhood Youth Panel, Inc. (NYP)
structured_extraction.program_description: A community-based juvenile diversion program that provides early intervention, diversion, and referral services for first-time and low-risk juvenile misdemeanor offenders and their families throughout Cecil County. The program diverts youth from the formal juvenile justice system through community panels, community conferencing, and referrals for mental health, trauma, or other needed services. Community volunteers serve as panelists who meet with youth and their families, help determine individualized sanctions, monitor compliance, and serve as positive role models. Successful completion allows charges to be removed from the youth's record.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Youth participants receive an individualized action plan that may include community service, life skills classes, drug and alcohol education, shoplifting abatement, career aptitude testing and advising, tobacco/vape intervention, anger management classes, mentoring, community conferencing/mediation, financial literacy classes, research projects or essays, apology letters, restitution, court observation, and interactive journaling. Referrals for mental health, trauma, or other needed services are also available. Services are delivered by the Department of Community Services. Successful completion allows charges to be removed from the youth's record.
structured_extraction.program_audience: First-time and low-risk juvenile misdemeanor offenders under 18 years of age and their families who are Cecil County residents and admit involvement in the offense.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Sanctions and interventions to divert youth from the formal juvenile justice system, support positive behavioral change, and provide early intervention and referrals for mental health and other needed services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Cecil County, Maryland resident.
requirements_list: Cecil County resident
Under 18 years of age
First-time or low-risk juvenile misdemeanor offender
Admission of involvement in the offense
Consent to have case handled by NYP
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Youth are referred to the program instead of entering the juvenile justice system. Contact the Department of Community Services or the Local Management Board for information on accessing services. The panel meets with the youth and their family to discuss circumstances and develop an individualized action plan. Participants must consent to have their case handled by NYP.

structured_extraction.program_name: Cecil County Purchase of Development Rights (PDR) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Established in 2005, the Cecil County PDR Program preserves agricultural land within Cecil County by purchasing development rights from willing landowners. It supplements existing federal, state, and local preservation programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Cecil County purchases development rights from agricultural landowners to permanently protect farmland from development. Landowners receive payment for the value of the development rights.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural landowners in Cecil County who want to voluntarily sell development rights on their farmland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment to landowners for permanently giving up development rights on agricultural land.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Cecil County, Maryland
requirements_list: Valid Soil Conservation and Water Quality Plan (SCWQP) on file with Cecil Soil Conservation District
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Purchase of Development Rights Application and review the instructions. Submit to the Cecil County Planning & Zoning Division.

structured_extraction.program_name: Cecil County Transfer of Development Rights (TDR) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Effective January 1, 2007, Cecil County's TDR program allows landowners in designated sending areas (agricultural zones) to sell their development rights to owners of receiving areas (growth zones near towns). The program encourages preservation of natural resources and directs growth to suitable areas near towns.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Landowners in sending areas (NAR and SAR zoned properties meeting minimum criteria) can sell development rights to landowners in receiving areas (SR and DR zoned properties). The program is incentive-based and voluntary.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural landowners in sending zones who want to sell development rights, and developers in receiving zones who want to increase density.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Proceeds from the sale of development rights for sending area landowners; increased development density for receiving area landowners.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Cecil County, Maryland — sending areas are properties zoned NAR and SAR; receiving areas are properties zoned SR and DR.
requirements_list: Sending areas must be properties zoned NAR or SAR meeting minimum criteria
Receiving areas must be properties zoned SR or DR meeting minimum criteria
Adequate water and sewer facilities must be available in receiving areas
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Cecil County Planning & Zoning Division for guidance. Review TDR Regulations (Cecil County Zoning Ordinance Article XI, Part V, Section 246) and County Code Chapter A386.

structured_extraction.program_name: Cecil County Workforce Training Partnership Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Cecil County Office of Economic Development provides workforce training assistance to new and existing Cecil County businesses through matching grants. The program partners with eligible companies to help them build critical skills, upgrade capabilities, or gain technical training that improves production and competitiveness. Preference is given to businesses that use Cecil College for training.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Matching grants to support workforce training initiatives that advance employee technical skills and create workforce stability.
structured_extraction.program_audience: New and existing businesses located in Cecil County seeking to train or upskill their workforce
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Workforce training including skills upgrades and technical training
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Cecil County, Maryland
requirements_list: Business must be located in Cecil County
Program requires a matching contribution from the business
Preference given to businesses that utilize Cecil College for training
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review eligibility criteria in the program overview PDF, then download and complete the fillable application PDF.

structured_extraction.program_name: Cecil Grown Micro Ag Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides small grants to support the growth, diversification, and long-term sustainability of existing agricultural businesses physically located in Cecil County, Maryland. Funding supports capital improvements, value-added production, agritourism infrastructure, marketing, technology adoption, research, and other investments that strengthen Cecil County's agricultural economy.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are offered in three tiers: Seed Grants up to $2,500 for small-scale or pilot projects; Growth Grants up to $5,000 for operational upgrades or market expansion; Impact Grants from $7,500 to $10,000 for high-impact projects. Total available funding is $74,666. All awards are cost-reimbursable — awardees pay project costs upfront and submit receipts for reimbursement. All projects must be completed by May 30, 2026, and reimbursement requests must be submitted by June 15, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Existing agricultural businesses (farms, producers, and agricultural enterprises) physically located in Cecil County, Maryland, including agricultural operators and micro-agriculture businesses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital improvements, value-added processing and product development, agritourism infrastructure, strategic marketing, technology adoption, research and pilot projects, climate resiliency and conservation improvements, animal welfare improvements, and business diversification.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be physically located in Cecil County, Maryland. Projects operating outside of Cecil County are not eligible.
requirements_list: Operate an existing agricultural business (not a conceptual or idea-stage project)
Be physically located in Cecil County, Maryland
Be actively producing agricultural goods or services
Be able to cover project costs upfront and request reimbursement
Be in good standing with the State of Maryland
Submit a complete application through the County's OpenGov portal by the stated deadline
Describe existing agricultural operations including what is produced, how long in operation, and current sales channels
Submit a detailed project budget with vendor information, cost estimates, and quotes or screenshots for all major purchases
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a complete application through Cecil County's OpenGov portal (procurement.opengov.com/portal/cecil) by February 27, 2026 at 12 p.m. Applications are reviewed by Cecil County Office of Economic Development staff and external reviewers using a standardized scoring rubric. If awarded, pay project expenses upfront, then submit receipts and required documentation using the Reimbursement Request Form by June 15, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: A marketing program that provides Cecil County agricultural producers with branded materials — including a logo, banner, and price signs — to help them promote and distinguish their locally grown products to consumers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive a high-resolution Cecil Grown logo for use on marketing and packaging, a banner for display at market stands or on-farm markets, price signs for Cecil Grown products, and potentially other marketing materials upon request.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farms and agricultural businesses operating in Cecil County, MD, including those growing raw crops or producing value-added agricultural products.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Marketing and promotional materials (logo, banner, price signs) to identify and promote locally grown products.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Farm or agricultural business must be located in Cecil County, MD. Raw crops using the Cecil Grown logo must be grown in Cecil County. Value-added products must use at least 75% inputs grown in Cecil County.
requirements_list: Operate a farm or agricultural business in Cecil County, MD
Raw agricultural crops using the Cecil Grown logo must be grown in Cecil County
If producing a value-added product without growing your own inputs, 75% of inputs must be grown in Cecil County
If growing crops in Cecil County and offering a value-added product made outside the county, 75% of product inputs must be grown in Cecil County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Certified Cecil Grown Registration Form (PDF) and email it to Malik Grace at mgrace@cecilcountymd.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: A two-generation program that supports children ages 5-17 who are affected by parental incarceration and inmates held at the Cecil County Detention Center. It uses case management, Life Skills training, mediation, and an evidence-based parenting program to strengthen families and educate incarcerated parents.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Case management, Life Skills training, mediation, and parenting education services provided to eligible families. Services delivered by Youth Empowerment Source, Inc.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Children ages 5-17 affected by parental incarceration and inmates at the Cecil County Detention Center
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Case management, life skills training, mediation, and parenting education
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Cecil County, Maryland
requirements_list: Children must be ages 5-17 experiencing effects of parental incarceration
Parents must be incarcerated in the Cecil County Detention Center
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Local Management Board or Cecil County Department of Community Services for information on accessing services.

structured_extraction.program_description: Federal grants awarded by the State of Maryland to smaller local governments like Cecil County. Funds support community development activities including affordable housing, services for vulnerable residents, and job creation and retention. Non-profit organizations may have Cecil County apply on their behalf.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal block grant funds awarded annually on a competitive basis by the State of Maryland to local governments. Cecil County may apply on behalf of non-profit organizations. Funds can be used for infrastructure, economic development, public facilities, community centers, housing rehabilitation, public services, clearance/acquisition, microenterprise assistance, code enforcement, and homeowner assistance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments and non-profit organizations seeking community development funding in Cecil County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Infrastructure, economic development, public facilities, community centers, housing rehabilitation, public services, clearance/acquisition, microenterprise assistance, code enforcement, homeowner assistance
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Cecil County, Maryland
requirements_list: Only local governments may apply directly
Non-profits must have Cecil County apply on their behalf
Must submit a preliminary proposal for consideration
