structured_extraction.program_description: Cecil County's tax deferral program allows eligible elderly or permanently disabled residential property owners to postpone paying a portion of their county property taxes each year. The deferred amount is the increase in county taxes over the prior year's bill (calculated after any Homestead or Homeowner's Tax Credits), up to a lifetime maximum of 50% of the property's assessed value at the time of the first application. No interest is charged on the deferred amount. The deferral applies only to the county portion of property taxes, not state or town/municipal portions. Deferred taxes are recorded as a lien on the property in Cecil County land records and must be repaid when the owner sells, moves out, no longer qualifies, or upon death (by the estate or co-owners), or when the owner's income exceeds $60,000. The program helps eligible residents stay in their homes without facing large annual tax increases. Deferred taxes are postponed — not forgiven — and repayment is required upon a triggering event. The program requires annual reapplication. The program is authorized under The Annotated Code of Maryland, Tax-Property Article Section 10-204.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Defers the year-over-year increase in Cecil County property taxes for eligible homeowners. The deferred amount equals this year's county taxes minus last year's county taxes (calculated after any Homestead or Homeowner's Tax Credits). The total deferred balance cannot exceed 50% of the property's assessed value at the time of the first application. No interest is charged on deferred amounts. The deferral applies only to the county portion of property taxes, not state or town/municipal portions. Deferred taxes become a lien on the property and must be repaid upon sale, loss of eligibility, moving out, or death (by the estate or co-owners), or when the owner's income exceeds $60,000. Any fees associated with recording the lien in land records must also be paid.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: September 1 for first-time applicants; May 1 (application) and June 1 (signed Deferral Agreement) for consecutive-year renewals to appear on July tax bill
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential property owners in Cecil County who are at least 65 years old or permanently disabled, have lived at the property as their principal residence for at least 5 years, and have a combined household gross income of $60,000 or less.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Postpones payment of the annual increase in Cecil County property taxes for eligible homeowners. Does not reduce the tax owed; deferred amounts must be repaid upon a triggering event such as sale, moving out, loss of eligibility, or death.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only for residential properties in Cecil County, Maryland. Applies only to the county portion of property taxes, not state or town/municipal portions.
requirements_list: Must own and occupy the property as a principal residence for at least 5 years
Must have lived at the property for at least 5 years

Must be at least 65 years old OR be permanently disabled receiving benefits from Social Security, Railroad Retirement, Armed Forces, or another federal retirement program OR be certified permanently disabled by a physician
Combined gross income of all persons living in the home must not exceed $60,000
Must provide proof of age and/or disability and proof of income
All co-owners must sign the application even if not living in the home
Must reapply each year; application must be received by September 1 for first-time applicants; returning applicants should submit by May 1 with signed Deferral Agreement by June 1
Must pay the base (non-deferred) amount of taxes on time to avoid Tax Sale
Must pay any fees associated with recording the lien in land records
Must be a residential property owner
Must continue to occupy the property as principal residence
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download the application form (PDF) from the Cecil County website (also available at https://www.cecilcountymd.gov/DocumentCenter/View/744/Tax-Deferral-Application-and-Instruction-Sheet-PDF), pick up an application at the Cecil County Finance Office at 200 Chesapeake Boulevard, Suite 1100, Elkton, MD 21921, or call 410-996-5385 to request a mailed application. Submit the completed application with proof of age and/or disability and proof of income. First-time applicants must submit by September 1. Returning applicants should submit by May 1 and return the signed Deferral Agreement by June 1 to have the deferral reflected on the July tax bill.

The program provides individualized exercise sessions to help increase range of motion, improve posture, build strength, reduce fatigue, combat negative side effects of cancer treatments, and improve overall well-being. Adults 55 and older may also join the Healthy Lifestyles Fitness Center at a low monthly rate.

Participants receive free fitness training and health education regardless of age. Adults 55 and older may also join the Healthy Lifestyles Fitness Center at a low monthly rate.

requirements_list: Must be a cancer survivor
Must be a Cecil County resident
Must be currently experiencing effects of cancer surgery or treatment
Must provide a signed LBC Doctor Consent form completed and signed by a physician
Must complete a Membership Packet
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download or pick up the LBC Doctor Consent form, have your physician fill it out and sign it, complete a Membership Packet, and submit both to the Healthy Lifestyles Fitness Center at 200 Chesapeake Blvd., Suite 2500, Elkton, MD 21921. structured_extraction.program_name: Opioid Restitution Fund (ORF) Community Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Cecil County provides annual grants from opioid restitution funds — proceeds from legal settlements with manufacturers and distributors of prescription opioid products distributed through the State of Maryland — to local nonprofits, not-for-profit organizations, and government agencies located in or serving Cecil County. Grants support substance use prevention, overdose response, treatment, and recovery support services, in alignment with specific legislative provisions outlined in the Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA). For FY2027, the total funding pool is $1 million, with individual grants up to $100,000 per application.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $100,000 per application, funded by opioid litigation settlement proceeds distributed through the State of Maryland. Organizations may submit no more than two applications, each addressing a different legislative provision. Total funding pool for FY2027 is $1 million. Awards support substance use prevention, overdose response, treatment, and recovery support services.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit, not-for-profit, and government agencies located in or serving Cecil County residents working on substance use prevention, treatment, overdose response, and recovery support.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Substance use prevention, overdose response, treatment, and recovery support services, as detailed in the Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) legislative provisions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Organizations must be located within or serving Cecil County, Maryland

Organization must be located within or serving Cecil County, Maryland
Applications must align with legislative provisions prescribed by the State of Maryland as outlined in the Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA)
Maximum request of $100,000 per application
No more than two applications per organization, each addressing a different legislative provision

structured_extraction.program_description: This grant helps businesses and organizations along the Route 40/Pulaski Highway corridor in Cecil County improve their exterior appearance and function. The goal is to revitalize the Route 40 business corridor, support economic growth, and enhance the visual appearance of properties visible from Route 40. A special 'blight removal' category is available for properties with vacant or dilapidated structures that pose safety or health concerns.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive reimbursement grants up to $25,000 for exterior revitalization projects, or up to $50,000 for blight removal. Standard grants require a 1:1 match (applicant must match the grant amount from their own funds). Blight removal grants require no matching funds. Funds are disbursed on a reimbursement basis after project completion. One application per address is allowed.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit businesses and non-profit organizations located along the Route 40/Pulaski Highway corridor in Cecil County, MD, including both property owners and tenants.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Exterior improvements visible from Route 40, including signage, lighting, siding, painting, entrances, porches/decks, fencing, landscaping, sidewalks, driveways, parking, ADA ramps, demolition, and blight/eyesore removal. Up to 20% of grant funds may be used for related interior improvements with prior approval.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Property must be located along the Route 40/Pulaski Highway corridor in Cecil County, MD, with a Route 40/Pulaski Highway mailing address. Improvements must be visible from Route 40.
requirements_list: Property must have a Route 40/Pulaski Highway address and improvements must be visible from Route 40
Applicant must be a for-profit business or non-profit organization (not a primary residence)
Applicant must be in good standing with the IRS, State of Maryland, and Cecil County
Standard grants require matching funds equal to the amount requested (1:1 match); blight removal grants have no match requirement
Only one application per address is permitted
Project designs must be approved by Cecil County Government
If applicant is a tenant, written authorization from the property owner is required
Grant funds may not be used to pay off debt from prior projects
Projects must be completed by June 30, 2026 (extensions with prior approval)
Funds are disbursed on a reimbursement basis only — project must be completed before reimbursement is requested
Non-profits must provide an IRS exemption determination letter
Two years of tax returns required (if applicable)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Read the Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO). Submit a completed application with all required documents either online via OpenGov (requires account creation), by downloading and submitting a PDF application, or by requesting a mailed paper application. Required documents include tax returns, proof of good standing, property photos, project designs and cost estimates, proof of matching funds, proof of insurance, and site control documentation. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis by the Grant Review Committee until funds are expended. Applicants are notified by email of the committee's decision.

structured_extraction.program_description: Cecil Catalyst is a low-interest loan program administered by Cecil County's Office of Economic Development that provides funding to creditworthy small businesses and individuals who have difficulty obtaining financing through traditional lenders due to limited equity, collateral, or marginal cash flow. The program aims to promote job growth, new investment, business retention, and job creation in Cecil County, with a focus on small and start-up businesses.
structured_extraction.agency: Cecil County Office of Economic Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest loans ranging from $5,000 to $75,000 (higher amounts possible with Loan Review Committee and County Executive approval). Interest rate is the Wall Street Journal Prime Rate (as published on the application date) plus 2%, fixed for up to 5 years; rate resets at month 61 for longer loans. Repayment terms vary by use: real estate up to 10 years with a 20-year amortization and balloon payment at month 120; equipment 3–10 years depending on useful life; working capital 1 year interest-only with balloon at month 12 (extendable up to two additional 1-year periods); physical improvements to real property up to 5 years. Loans may be secured or unsecured at the Loan Review Committee's discretion. All loans require a personal guaranty from all business principals/owners (except limited partners in a limited liability partnership). A one-time, non-refundable $100 application fee is required at submission, plus customary closing costs including title and lien searches, recordation fees, taxes, and legal fees.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses (including startups), new investors, existing businesses seeking to retain or create jobs, and individuals in Cecil County who cannot obtain traditional financing due to limited equity, collateral requirements, or marginal cash flow.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Leasehold improvements, acquisition of real property (applicant must occupy at least 51% of improvements on the subject parcel), construction, renovation and rehabilitation, machinery and equipment, and working capital (including third-party lender/loan fees). Also supports general business investment, retention, and job creation activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to businesses and individuals located in Cecil County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must demonstrate creditworthiness
Acceptable debt-to-income ratio showing ability to repay the loan in full
Personal guaranty of all business principal(s)/owner(s) required (except limited partners in a limited liability partnership)
Application reviewed by a qualified underwriter selected by the Loan Review Committee
Loans may be secured or unsecured at the Loan Review Committee's discretion
For real property acquisition, applicant must occupy at least 51% of the improvements on the subject parcel
Loan requests exceeding $75,000 must demonstrate a level of capitalization meeting loan underwriting standards for the loan type
A non-refundable application fee of $100 is required
The borrower pays for all closing costs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Contact the Office of Economic Development at 410-996-6292 or by email to discuss your project. Step 2: Complete the application form (PDF) and submit it with required supporting documents by email to the Economic Development Manager. Step 3: The Loan Review Committee reviews the application and underwriting decision, then approves or denies the loan. If approved, settlement is scheduled and repayment terms are set based on the use of funds.

structured_extraction.program_name: ARPA State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds (SLFRF) for Surface Transportation Projects
structured_extraction.program_description: Charles County can use American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds to pay for surface transportation projects. Eligible projects include highways, bridges, road maintenance, and related infrastructure. Funds must supplement — not replace — other government funding already available for these projects. Under the Pathway 2 Streamlined Framework, the county can use funds for projects not receiving U.S. Department of Transportation funding without needing prior Treasury approval.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal ARPA SLFRF dollars allocated to surface transportation projects. Costs must have been incurred on or after December 29, 2022, obligated by December 31, 2024, and fully expended by September 30, 2026. Eligible uses include highway, bridge, and road projects eligible under Title 23 of the United States Code, including full highway maintenance (surface, shoulders, roadsides, structures, and traffic-control devices).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Obligated by December 31, 2024; expended by September 30, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Charles County government for surface transportation infrastructure projects
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Highway, bridge, road, and maintenance projects eligible under Title 23 of the U.S. Code, including surface, shoulders, roadsides, structures, and traffic-control devices.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Charles County, Maryland only
requirements_list: Funds must supplement, not supplant, other federal, state, territorial, Tribal, and local government funds available for the same projects
Costs must be incurred on or after December 29, 2022
Funds must be obligated by December 31, 2024
Funds must be expended by September 30, 2026
Under Pathway 2 (Streamlined Framework), projects must NOT be receiving funding from the U.S. Department of Transportation
Projects must be eligible under Title 23, United States Code
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Under Pathway 2 (Streamlined Framework), recipients are not required to obtain Treasury approval prior to using funds. Charles County can proceed with eligible surface transportation projects and draw down SLFRF funds accordingly.

structured_extraction.program_description: A community volunteer program that lets groups, businesses, or organizations adopt and regularly clean a specific section of road or public space in Charles County to reduce litter and improve the appearance of local areas. The county supports volunteers with supplies such as bags, gloves, vests, and grabbers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Volunteers receive free cleanup supplies (bags, gloves, vests, and grabbers) provided by the county's Litter Control division. The county can also pick up collected trash upon request. Adopted spots and roads must be cleaned at least 3 times per calendar year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Groups, businesses, organizations, and individuals in Charles County who want to voluntarily maintain a section of road or public space.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Litter cleanup supplies and trash removal support for adopted road sections or public spots.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Charles County, Maryland only.
requirements_list: Adopted spots and roads must be cleaned at least 3 times per calendar year.
Adopt-A-Road volunteers must be at least 12 years of age; those aged 12–17 must be supervised by an adult.
Adopt-A-Spot volunteers can be any age, with adult supervision required for those 17 and younger.

Roads that are house-front are not available for adoption.

After completing a cleanup, report it using the online reporting form, which also includes an option to request trash disposal and note where collected trash is located.

structured_extraction.program_name: American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) of 2021 - Charles County Funds

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Charles County received $31,710,758 in Coronavirus Local Fiscal Recovery Funds (50% in May 2021, 50% twelve months later). Funds are allocated across: Businesses ($3,670,000), Non-Profits ($2,901,700), Stormwater ($16,324,099), Housing ($447,053), Surface Transportation ($2,013,044), Broadband ($1,350,769), Public Health ($3,413,051), and Public Safety ($1,591,042). structured_extraction.program_description: A state-supported grant program locally administered by the Charles County Department of Health in partnership with Charles County. It provides grant funding from the Bay Restoration Fund to help residents replace conventional septic tanks with nitrogen-reducing units, fund sewer connections for existing homes where public sewer is available, or replace failing septic systems for low-income households. The goal is to reduce harmful nutrients such as nitrogen entering the Chesapeake Bay and its tributaries.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding covers the cost of replacing conventional septic systems with nitrogen-reducing units, connecting existing homes to public sewer, or replacing failing septic systems for low-income households. Funding comes from the Bay Restoration Fund. Specific grant amounts are not publicly stated.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Charles County homeowners with conventional on-site septic systems, especially low-income households with failing systems, who want to install nitrogen removal units or connect to public sewer.

structured_extraction.program_name: Charles County Adult Drug Court Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary program for adults in Charles County with substance use disorders who have an active criminal case in Charles County Circuit Court. Using a four-phase structure, a team including the court and service providers work together to support each participant through treatment, counseling, job training, and court supervision over 12 to 18 months. Successful graduates may have their charges reduced, dismissed, or expunged.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive structured support across four program phases including substance use and mental health treatment, individual and group counseling, family counseling, physical health support, drug testing, probation supervision, educational opportunities, job training, pro-social activities, and life skills training. Upon successful completion of the 12- to 18-month program, criminal charges may be reduced, dismissed, or expunged.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults 18 and older living in Charles County who have a diagnosed substance use disorder, are involved in Circuit Court, have entered a plea, and are identified as higher risk for reoffending with higher treatment needs and at risk of incarceration.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Substance use and mental health treatment, physical health support, individual and group counseling, family counseling, drug testing, educational and job training support, pro-social activities, life skills training, and court supervision.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must live in Charles County and have an active criminal case in the Charles County Circuit Court.
requirements_list: Be at least 18 years old
Live in Charles County
Have a diagnosed substance use disorder using ASAM criteria
Have an active criminal case in the Charles County Circuit Court and have already entered a plea
Be at risk of reoffending (determined by a risk/needs assessment)
Be identified as having a higher risk of reoffending and higher treatment needs
Be facing jail or prison due to your case or violation of probation
Be willing to participate in treatment
Sign an agreement to follow program rules
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Participation is voluntary. Referrals can come from judges, public defenders, the State's Attorney's Office, the Sheriff's Office, the Detention Center, the Probation Office, or anyone can submit a referral by completing the Adult Drug Court Program Referral form. structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary, court-supervised, four-phase program for parents with substance use and mental health disorders who are involved in child welfare proceedings in Charles County Circuit Court. The program provides intensive treatment, accountability, and support—including substance abuse treatment (inpatient or outpatient), drug and alcohol testing, individual and group counseling, 12-step support, peer recovery coaching, case management, physical health support, education and vocational services, job placement, life skills classes, mental health support, transportation assistance, parenting skills training, and referrals for public assistance and Medicaid—to help parents achieve sobriety, address mental health needs, develop parenting skills, and safely reunite with or maintain custody of their children. The program runs a minimum of 12 months across four phases.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive a personalized Recovery Service Plan that may include substance use disorder and mental health treatment (inpatient or outpatient), frequent court monitoring sessions, random drug and alcohol testing, individual and group counseling, 12-step support, peer recovery coaching, case management, physical health support, educational and vocational services, job placement, life skills classes, mental health support, transportation assistance, parenting skills training, pro-social activities, recovery support services, and referrals to ancillary services including public assistance and Medicaid. The program runs a minimum of 12 months across four phases.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Parents aged 18 and older with a substance use disorder diagnosis who are involved in child welfare cases in Charles County Circuit Court, including those with an active Child In Need of Assistance (CINA) case with a reunification permanency plan, a child under a DSS Order of Protective Supervision, or a custody/visitation/child access matter with a court order mandating substance use disorder treatment, who want to regain custody of or maintain a relationship with their children.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Substance use disorder and mental health treatment, counseling, drug and alcohol testing, case management, physical health support, educational and vocational training, job placement, life skills classes, recovery support services, parenting skills training, transportation assistance, and referrals for public assistance and Medicaid to help parents safely care for their children.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Charles County, Maryland — cases must be in Charles County Circuit Court.
requirements_list: Must be at least 18 years of age
Must have a substance use disorder diagnosis

Must have an active Child In Need of Assistance (CINA) case with a permanency plan that includes reunification, OR have a child under an Order of Protective Supervision by the Department of Social Services, OR have a custody, visitation, or child access matter with a court order or pending petition in Charles County Circuit Court mandating substance use disorder treatment
Must be willing to engage in substance use disorder treatment
Must sign a written agreement to participate upon entry into the program
Must follow a Recovery Service Plan
Must attend all hearings, appointments, and treatment sessions
Must submit to frequent and random drug and alcohol testing
Must report all drug and alcohol use at each court appearance
Must report any prescribed or over-the-counter medications to the FRC team before use
Must report any changes in address or contact information immediately
Must download and install the Reconnect testing and appointment app
Must dress appropriately for all court appearances
Must not use drugs, alcohol, or non-prescribed medications
Must follow the rules of all referred service providers
Program lasts a minimum of 12 months across four phases
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Referrals can be made using the fillable referral form available on the program website. Participation is voluntary and requires signing a written agreement upon entry. Participants complete a full needs assessment and then follow a personalized Recovery Service Plan, meeting the requirements of each of the four program phases before advancing toward graduation. Contact the Charles County Circuit Court Family Resource Specialist at 301-932-3286 for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Charles County Government Summer Internship Program

Interns are placed in various county departments to gain practical skills and contribute to county operations during the summer. The program is divided into two sessions: a 10-week session starting June 3 (running through August) and a 6-week session starting July 1 (running through August). Participants may be placed in paid or unpaid roles depending on the department and position.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Paid or unpaid internship placements within Charles County Government departments, offered in two sessions over the summer: a 10-week session starting June 3 (June–August) and a 6-week session starting July 1 (July–August).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Charles County residents who are rising high school juniors or seniors, current college or graduate students, or recent college graduates.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Work experience within Charles County Government departments through a summer internship placement.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Charles County resident.
requirements_list: Must be a Charles County resident
Must be a rising high school junior or senior, current college or graduate student, or recent college graduate
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted from April 1 through April 22. Applicants apply online through the Charles County Government job portal at GovernmentJobs.com.

structured_extraction.program_description: A team of professionals from child-serving agencies in Charles County who meet together to identify needs, make connections, advise, and assist families with children who have intensive emotional and behavioral needs. The team provides a forum for interagency problem-solving, makes referrals to community resources, and offers training and technical assistance to local agency and community partners.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Families with children who have intensive emotional and behavioral needs can submit a referral to have their case reviewed by a team of professionals from multiple child-serving agencies. The team provides assistance identifying needs and resources, interagency problem-solving, and referrals to local community resources. Meetings are held weekly on Thursdays from 9:00am to 10:00am.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with children experiencing emotional or behavioral challenges that place them or their family at risk; parents, guardians, or local agencies in Charles County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Identifying individual needs and resources, interagency coordination, referrals to care management entities and community resources, training and technical assistance
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Charles County, Maryland
requirements_list: Child must be experiencing emotional or behavioral challenges that place them or the family at risk
Referral must be submitted by a parent, guardian, or local agency
All required parts of the online referral form must be completed

Complete Part One (Youth's Information), Part Two (Youth's Background Information), and Part Three (Parent/Guardian Consent Form, for parents and guardians only). The Local Care Team Coordinator will then contact you to complete the referral process and schedule an LCT meeting. If unsure, email CCACCYF-LMB@charlescountymd.gov for guidance.

structured_extraction.program_description: A defined benefit retirement plan for Charles County government employees. Eligible employees make mandatory payroll contributions and receive a retirement annuity based on years of service and final average earnings. The plan covers both non-public safety and public safety employees, including emergency services and animal control workers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Defined benefit pension providing a retirement annuity calculated as: Final Average Earnings × Benefit Level × Credited Years of Service. Non-public safety benefit levels range from 1.5% to 2.5% of final average earnings per year depending on years of service. Public safety employees receive 2.5% of final average earnings for all years. Employee contributions are 4% of basic earnings for non-public safety and 8% for public safety employees, deducted pretax from payroll. Employees may also receive up to 3 years of military service credit toward their retirement benefit.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Open enrollment in November each year to enroll as of December 1; mandatory for employees hired on or after July 1, 1991
structured_extraction.program_audience: Charles County government employees, including non-public safety and public safety (emergency services and animal control) employees
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Retirement income in the form of an annuity upon reaching retirement eligibility
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to employees of Charles County, Maryland
requirements_list: Participation is mandatory for employees hired on or after July 1, 1991
Non-public safety employees may retire at age 62 with at least 5 years of service, or age 60 with at least 20 years of service
Public safety employees may retire after 25 years of service or upon reaching age 60
Non-public safety employees vest 100% after 5 years of service (for hire dates after July 1, 1997)
Public safety employees hired after July 1, 1997 with termination on or after July 1, 2018 vest 100% after 5 years of service
Military service credit requires 10 years of county employment prior to receiving credit
Employee must have been hired prior to July 1, 1991 to voluntarily opt in during open enrollment in November
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Participation is automatic (mandatory) for employees hired on or after July 1, 1991. Employees not currently enrolled may join during the open enrollment period held each November, with enrollment effective December 1. Account information is available online at www.empowermyretirement.com or by calling Empower at 800-338-4015.

structured_extraction.program_name: Charles County Sheriff's Office Retirement Plan
structured_extraction.program_description: A defined benefit pension plan for Charles County Sheriff's Office employees, including sworn officers, correctional officers, and communications/dispatchers. The plan provides retirement income based on years of service and final average earnings, with mandatory participation for all Sheriff's Office employees.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Defined benefit pension plan with mandatory employee contributions (8% for sworn officers, 7% for correctional officers and dispatchers) made on a pretax basis. Retirement benefit is calculated as Final Average Earnings (FAE, based on highest 3 consecutive salaries in the final 5 years) times a benefit level percentage times credited years of service. Sworn officers earn 3% of FAE per year for years 1-20 and 2% for years beyond 20. Correctional officers earn 2.25% of FAE per year. Dispatchers earn 2.00%-2.15% of FAE depending on years of service. Disability benefits range from 15% to 66 2/3% of FAE. A Deferred Retirement Option Program (DROP) is available, allowing eligible employees to retire without terminating employment for up to 5 years (sworn) or 3 years (corrections/dispatchers) while accumulating retirement benefits. Under DROP, monthly retirement benefit is calculated as of a DROP entry date and added to an account; accrued sick leave (between 580-2,580 hours) may be counted toward monthly addition to DROP account. Upon termination, participant receives monthly retirement income plus distribution of DROP account. Election to participate in DROP is irrevocable once participation begins.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Law enforcement personnel employed by the Charles County Sheriff's Office, including sworn officers, correctional officers, and communications/dispatchers
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Retirement/pension benefits for eligible participants; disability income; survivor benefits; DROP account accumulation and distribution
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Charles County, Maryland

structured_extraction.program_name: Charles County Small Local Business Enterprise (SLBE) and Minority Women Business Enterprise (MWBE) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Charles County established the SLBE and MWBE programs to encourage participation of small, local, minority-owned, and woman-owned businesses in county government procurement. The SLBE Program certifies small, locally-based businesses in Charles County, granting them exclusive access to all informal county procurements under $50,000 (when at least three SLBE firms are qualified) and bid preferences on formal solicitations valued between $50,000 and $500,000. For Invitations to Bid (ITB) and Requests for Quotation (RFQ), certified SLBE firms receive up to a 10% cost advantage over the lowest bidder; for Requests for Proposals (RFP), they receive up to 10 additional points prorated based on documented SLBE participation. Firms graduate from the SLBE program after receiving more than $3 million in SLBE awards within any 60-month period, exceeding Maryland Small Business Reserve size thresholds, or relocating out of Charles County. Together, the programs help qualifying businesses compete for county contracts and expand access to public sector procurement opportunities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Certified SLBE vendors receive exclusive access to all informal county procurements (under $50,000) as long as at least three SLBE firms are qualified. For formal solicitations between $50,000 and $500,000, SLBE firms receive bid preferences: up to 10% cost advantage over the lowest bidder on ITBs and RFQs, and up to 10 additional points on RFPs, prorated based on documented SLBE participation. The MWBE program encourages participation of minority-owned and woman-owned businesses in county procurement. Certified businesses may receive preference or participation goals on county contracts.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small, for-profit businesses headquartered or with a qualifying branch office in Charles County, Maryland, including minority-owned and woman-owned businesses, that meet Maryland Small Business Reserve size thresholds and seek to participate in Charles County government procurement.

structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Business must be headquartered in Charles County, or have a branch or satellite office in Charles County that generates at least 50% of annual gross sales or has 50% of full-time equivalent employees residing in Charles County.

Must be a small, local, minority-owned, or woman-owned business as applicable

Must have headquarters in Charles County, or a branch/satellite office in Charles County generating at least 50% of annual gross sales OR with at least 50% of full-time equivalent employees residing in Charles County
Must meet Maryland Small Business Reserve (SBR) industry-specific thresholds for gross sales and employees
Must be certified in Maryland's Small Business Reserve (SBR) Program
Must be registered with eMaryland Marketplace Advantage (eMMA)
Must meet eligibility criteria administered by the Charles County Economic Development Department
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download the SLBE application from the Charles County Economic Development website and submit it. For questions and assistance, contact slbe@MeetCharlesCounty.com or call 301-885-1334 or 301-885-1340.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides support services to family caregivers of older adults and other qualifying individuals in Charles County. structured_extraction.program_description: Long-term disability insurance coverage provided to eligible county government employees. Charles County automatically provides LTD insurance at no cost to all eligible employees; if an employee becomes unable to perform their job duties for more than 120 days due to injury or illness, the plan pays 60% of their base monthly salary until age 65 (for employees age 60 or under at the time of disability). Montgomery County offers LTD1 coverage providing 60% of basic monthly earnings (up to $2,500/month) after a 5-month waiting period, continuing for up to 12 months of occupation-specific disability and potentially longer based on age at disability onset; LTD2 is available for RSP/GRIP members and Elected Officials and provides monthly disability benefit payments replacing a percentage of final earnings (52.5%-70%+ for service-connected; minimum 33.33% up to 60% for non-service-connected).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Charles County: The plan pays 60% of the employee's base monthly salary if they are disabled for more than 120 days. Coverage continues until age 65 for employees age 60 or younger at the time of disability. For employees age 61 or older, preexisting conditions (conditions for which the employee sought or received medical treatment in the three months before coverage began) are not covered during the first 12 months after coverage takes effect. Montgomery County LTD1: Monthly income benefit of 60% of basic monthly earnings (lesser of 60% of first $4,167 or 70% of first $3,571 of predisability earnings), up to a maximum of $2,500 per month, beginning after a 5-month waiting period and continuing for up to 12 months of occupation-specific disability. If still disabled after 12 months and unable to work in any qualified occupation, benefits continue based on age at disability onset (up to age 65 or 36 payments). Benefits integrate with Social Security, Workers' Compensation, and State Disability payments. Includes rehabilitation incentives, portability options, and return-to-work support. LTD2 is available for RSP, GRIP members, and Elected Officials; provides monthly disability benefit payments replacing a percentage of final earnings (52.5%-70%+ for service-connected disability; minimum 33.33% up to 60% for non-service-connected disability). Employer contributions to retirement plans may also be included for eligible non-public safety employees.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible county government employees (Charles County and Montgomery County) who suffer an injury or illness preventing them from performing job duties for an extended period. Montgomery County LTD1 coverage is primarily for full-time ERS members enrolled in Montgomery County Employees' Retirement System (minimum 40 hours/week). LTD2 is for RSP/GRIP members, Elected Officials, and employees of participating agencies budgeted to work at least 20 hours per week.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Replacement of lost income during long-term disability — 60% of base monthly salary or basic monthly earnings. Also covers rehabilitation and vocational services, job modifications/accommodations, clinical specialist services, and Social Security disability application assistance (Montgomery County).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to eligible employees of Charles County and Montgomery County, Maryland. Montgomery County benefits continue while living in the US or Canada; benefits end after 12 consecutive months living outside these countries.
requirements_list: Employee must be unable to perform the essential functions of their position for at least 120 days following the date of injury or illness (Charles County).
For employees age 61 or older at the time of disability, preexisting conditions are excluded from coverage during the first 12 months after the effective date of coverage (Charles County).
A preexisting condition is defined as one for which the employee sought or received medical treatment in the three months prior to the effective date of the insurance (Charles County).
Must be a full-time county employee and member of the optional or integrated plan under the ERS (for Montgomery County LTD1).
Must work minimum 40 hours per week (Montgomery County LTD1).
Coverage becomes effective after 6 months of continuous active service (Montgomery County).
Not eligible after age 70 (Montgomery County LTD1).
Part-time employees are not eligible for LTD1 coverage (Montgomery County).
RSP, GRIP members, and Elected Officials are eligible for LTD2 (Montgomery County).
For LTD2: must be employed by County or participating agency at least 20 hours per week and employed for at least 6 months before disability.
Disability must be due to accident, illness, or injury (not willful misconduct or negligence) (LTD2).
Must apply for Federal Social Security disability benefits within 6 months of disability onset (Montgomery County).
Must provide medical documentation and proof of disability.
Must participate in required rehabilitation programs if capable (Montgomery County).
Must submit to medical exams as requested by insurer.
Must notify insurer of other income sources (Social Security awards, third-party settlements, Workers' Compensation, etc.).
Complete all required claim forms including Employee's Statement, Authorization to Obtain Information, Attending Physician's Statement, and Employer's Statement.
Must provide continuing proof of disability.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Charles County: Employees who suffer an injury or illness with a foreseeable long-term duration should contact the Benefits Department at (301)645-0585 as soon as possible to begin the application process. Montgomery County LTD1: Contact MetLife/benefits representative within 14 days of inability to work; obtain claim form from policyholder; submit completed LTD1 Claim Form (MetLife, form EES LTD 5323) with required proof within 90 days after elimination period ends. Employer completes job description section. Fax or mail form to MetLife (PO Box 14590, Lexington, KY 40512-4590; Fax: 1-800-230-9531). For claims prior to January 1, 2019, Standard Insurance Company administered claims (submit Standard LTD Claim Form to Standard Benefit Administrators at PO Box 5031, White Plains NY 10602-5031; Tel: 800-426-4332; Fax: 800-378-8361). Montgomery County LTD2: Submit claim using LTD2 claim form (ERS LTD 5317) through the Montgomery County Employee Retirement Plans office.

structured_extraction.program_description: Charles County Water & Sewer Billing offers qualifying customers extra time to pay their water/sewer bill. A Deferred Payment Plan lets customers spread payments over a schedule ending one week before their next quarterly bill. Both options are for customers facing unusual circumstances who need more time to pay.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A Payment Extension extends the disconnect date by one week. A Deferred Payment Plan schedules payments up to one week before the next quarterly bill, with a minimum first payment of $50, monthly payments of at least $50 for invoices over $250, and no payments more than one month apart. Late payment charges of 10% and 3% interest on arrears still apply if the full balance is not paid by the original due date.

requirements_list: Request must be submitted before the scheduled disconnect date, preferably before the due date on the bill
Eligibility is based on payment history, age of past-due amount, tenant status, and timeliness of prior payments
Customers may choose either an extension or a deferred payment plan — not both
Tenants must have a renter's form on file from their landlord; landlord must provide written approval to wsbilling@charlescountymd.gov for each deferred payment plan request
For a Deferred Payment Plan: first payment of at least $50 must be made before or immediately after the request
For a Deferred Payment Plan: last payment must be received one week before the next billing date
For a Deferred Payment Plan: payments cannot be more than one month apart
For a Deferred Payment Plan: monthly payments must be at least $50 for invoices over $250
If water is disconnected, payment in full is required before reconnection
Defaulting or late payments may result in denial of future arrangements for up to one year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a Payment Extension request or Deferred Payment Plan request online using the links provided on the page. An email confirmation will be sent within 24 business hours indicating approval, denial, or required changes.

structured_extraction.program_name: Perpetual Conservation Easement Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: Offers a property tax credit in Charles County for property owners who have placed a perpetual conservation easement on their land. The credit is applied to real property subject to a qualifying perpetual conservation easement, reducing the property tax liability for conserved land.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A property tax credit applied to real property in Charles County that is subject to a perpetual conservation easement, reducing the property tax liability for conserved land.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners in Charles County who have placed a perpetual conservation easement on their land
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of property tax liability for conserved land
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Charles County, Maryland
requirements_list: Property must be subject to a perpetual conservation easement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Perpetual Conservation Easement Property Tax Credit Application and submit to the Charles County Treasury office.

structured_extraction.program_description: Charles County's Purchase of Development Rights (PDR) program allows the county to directly purchase development rights from property owners. Unlike the TDR program, development rights are extinguished rather than transferred. The county runs periodic competitive application cycles as funding is available.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Charles County purchases development rights directly from property owners. Rights are extinguished (not transferred). Applications are evaluated using the same ranking criteria as the MALPF program. Funding cycles are periodic and subject to availability.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Periodic competitive cycles as funding is available
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners in Charles County who wish to sell their development rights directly to the county.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Landowners receive payment from the county for development rights; development rights are permanently extinguished.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Charles County, MD only.
requirements_list: Property must be located in Charles County
Applications evaluated using MALPF ranking criteria
Funding subject to availability
Participation is voluntary
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Charles County Planning Staff to learn more. Submit an application during a competitive funding cycle.

structured_extraction.program_name: Rain Barrel Watershed Protection and Restoration Fee Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: Charles County residents, businesses, and schools that harvest rainwater using a rain barrel can receive a credit on their property tax bill for the Watershed Protection and Restoration Fee. Rain barrels help reduce stormwater runoff that carries pollutants into local streams.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A credit on the property tax bill for the Watershed Protection and Restoration Fee is available to property owners who install and use a rain barrel to harvest rainwater.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Charles County homeowners, business owners, and schools who install rain barrels to harvest rainwater and reduce stormwater runoff.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable — this is a property tax fee credit, not direct funding.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to property owners in Charles County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must install a rain barrel to harvest rainwater from a downspout
Property must be located in Charles County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register for a Rain Barrel Workshop to learn how to get started and qualify for the credit.

structured_extraction.program_description: Hands-on workshops that teach residents how to use rain barrels to reduce stormwater runoff, conserve water, and protect local watersheds in Charles County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: In-person workshops with limited spaces available. Participants learn how to use rain barrels effectively to manage stormwater runoff and conserve water.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Charles County residents interested in rain barrel use, installation, maintenance, and stormwater management
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational instruction on rain barrel construction, installation, and maintenance for water conservation
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Charles County, Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register for an upcoming workshop online. Spaces are limited.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance to help eligible residents afford recreation program registration fees.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Charles County residents who need financial assistance to participate in recreation programs
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Recreation program registration fees

structured_extraction.program_description: The Resilience Authority of Charles County is a public entity that provides financial and technical assistance to support community resilience and economic development projects in Charles County, Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Resilience Authority provides financial and technical assistance to support resilience and economic development initiatives in Charles County. Specific amounts and terms are not detailed on this page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses, nonprofits, individuals, and government entities in Charles County, Maryland seeking support for resilience and economic development projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Community resilience and economic development projects in Charles County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Charles County, Maryland

structured_extraction.program_name: Rural Housing Initiative and Indoor Plumbing Assistance
structured_extraction.program_description: Helps low-income homeowners in Charles County obtain indoor plumbing and/or safe drinking water (potable water) installed in their principal residence. The program provides financial assistance to qualifying households that lack indoor plumbing or a potable water supply. Residents can determine eligibility by completing a pre-qualification form online or by contacting the Housing Authority directly.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance to cover the cost of installing indoor plumbing and/or potable water systems for qualifying low-income homeowners. Income limits vary by household size, ranging from $74,800 for a 1-person household to $141,000 for an 8-person household. Specific amounts and terms depend on applicant circumstances.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income homeowners in rural Charles County whose principal residence lacks indoor plumbing or potable water.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of indoor plumbing and/or potable water supply for a primary residence.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to homeowners residing in rural areas of Charles County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a homeowner using the property as a principal residence
Must lack indoor plumbing or potable water
Household income must be at or below the program income limits (e.g., $74,800 for 1 person, up to $141,000 for 8 persons)
Must complete and submit a Pre-application form to the Housing Authority
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Indoor Plumbing Assistance Pre-Qualification Form available on the county website (or submit via the online pre-qualification form), or contact the Housing Authority to obtain an application package. Provide your email address to receive a copy of your submission. Once a complete pre-application is submitted, the Housing Authority will follow up with the applicant.

structured_extraction.program_name: Rural Legacy Program – Zekiah Watershed and Nanjemoy-Mattawoman Rural Legacy Areas (Charles County)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Rural Legacy Program purchases conservation easements from willing landowners to permanently protect environmental, agricultural, and cultural resources in designated Rural Legacy Areas in Charles County. Charles County has two Rural Legacy Areas: the Zekiah Watershed (60,000 acres) and the Nanjemoy-Mattawoman Forest (65,000+ acres).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Voluntary purchase of conservation easements from landowners to permanently protect land. Over $18 million in easements have been purchased in the Zekiah Watershed area alone.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Rural landowners in Charles County's designated Rural Legacy Areas who wish to voluntarily preserve their land.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of conservation easements to permanently restrict development on eligible land.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be located within the Zekiah Watershed Rural Legacy Area or the Nanjemoy-Mattawoman Forest Rural Legacy Area in Charles County, MD.
requirements_list: Property must be located within a designated Rural Legacy Area in Charles County
Participation is voluntary
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Charles County Planning Staff to learn more and complete an application.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides access and coordination of services to frail, health-impaired elderly residents to help them remain in their homes. Financial assistance may be available for services such as in-home care (bathing, light housekeeping, meal preparation), medications, personal care supplies, and home monitoring.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance may be available to eligible clients for in-home care services including bathing, light housekeeping, meal preparation, medications, personal care supplies, and home monitoring.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Frail, health-impaired elderly residents of Charles County who need assistance to remain in their homes.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: In-home care services (bathing, light housekeeping, meal preparation), medications, personal care supplies, and home monitoring.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Charles County, Maryland residents.
requirements_list: Must be elderly
Must be frail or health-impaired
Financial eligibility may be required

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides seniors age 60 and older and their families with information and referrals to programs, services, and benefits through the Aging and Human Services Division and other agencies, covering areas such as benefits, housing, transportation, and frail elderly support.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Information and referral services connecting seniors and their families to benefit programs (Social Security, Medicare/Medicaid, food stamps, pharmacy assistance, veterans benefits), frail elderly services (adult day care, meals on wheels, in-home services, respite care), housing assistance (subsidized housing, weatherization, energy assistance), transportation, senior centers, and other programs such as legal assistance and health insurance counseling.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Seniors age 60 and older and their families in Charles County, MD
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Connecting seniors to programs and services covering benefits, housing, transportation, in-home care, and other support services
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Charles County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be age 60 or older (or a family member of an eligible senior)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 301-609-5712 or 301-870-3388 ext. 5118, or email MDAccessPoint@charlescountymd.gov for information on available programs and services.

structured_extraction.program_name: Senior Nutrition Program (Home Delivered Meals / Meals on Wheels)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides a variety of nutrition services to residents of Charles County aged 60 and older, including congregate meals at senior centers, home-delivered meals (Meals on Wheels) for homebound seniors, nutrition education, and one-on-one nutrition counseling and assessment. Home-delivered meals are provided through a cooperative effort between the Charles County Department of Community Services and local Meals-on-Wheels providers. All menus are written by a Registered Dietitian and meet at least one-third of the Recommended Daily Allowances for older adults. Contributions toward the cost of meals are requested and may be based on a sliding scale.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Program provides nutritious luncheon meals at senior centers (contributions requested), home-delivered meals for homebound seniors (contributions requested on a sliding scale), nutrition education through speakers and demonstrations, and one-on-one nutrition counseling and assessment at no cost to the recipient (referral from a healthcare professional required).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Charles County residents aged 60 and older, their spouses, and disabled children of eligible seniors (with approval). Home-delivered meals are specifically for those who are homebound due to illness or disability and unable to shop for food or prepare meals.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Meals and nutrition services for eligible older adults, including congregate dining at senior centers, home-delivered meals, nutrition education, and one-on-one nutrition counseling and assessment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to senior residents of Charles County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be aged 60 or older
Spouses and disabled children of eligible seniors may participate with approval
Home-delivered meals require the participant to be homebound due to illness or disability and unable to shop for food or prepare meals
Nutrition counseling requires a referral from a healthcare professional
Reservations are required for congregate meals at senior centers
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 301-934-0138 or 301-870-3388 ext. 5138 for more information or to apply. Reservations are required for congregate meals at senior centers. For home-delivered meals, call to inquire about eligibility and submit a request.

structured_extraction.program_description: Encourages Charles County property owners to install tank risers on their septic systems when having them pumped out. Risers improve access to the septic tank for future maintenance. Reimbursement is limited to one per property.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time reimbursement of $100 per property for the installation of septic tank risers. Can be applied for at the same time as the Septic System Pump Out Reimbursement. Applicants must provide proof of purchase and installation.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications must be received within six (6) months of riser installation
structured_extraction.program_audience: Charles County property owners with existing septic systems
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reimbursement for the purchase and installation of septic tank risers
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to property owners in Charles County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a property owner in Charles County with an existing septic system
Limited to one reimbursement per property
Must provide proof of purchase and installation by a hauler or contractor, or proof of purchase for independently installed risers
Application must be received within six months of riser installation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply using the online application on the Charles County website, providing proof of purchase and installation. Can be submitted at the same time as the Septic System Pump Out Reimbursement application.

structured_extraction.program_description: Reimburses Charles County residents for the cost of pumping out their septic system. The program helps meet nutrient pollution reduction goals by encouraging regular pump-outs, which reduce nutrient leaching into local waterways. Residents can apply once every three years using the online application and must provide a contractor receipt.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Maximum reimbursement of $100 per septic system, issued as a check mailed to the applicant. Applications must be submitted within six months of the pump-out and are processed within 12 weeks. Effective January 1, 2026, only pump-outs performed by septage haulers approved by the Charles County Health Department are eligible.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications must be received within six (6) months of the pump-out
structured_extraction.program_audience: Charles County residents with a septic system
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reimbursement for the cost of septic system pump-out by a licensed and county-approved septage hauler
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Charles County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a Charles County resident with a septic system
Eligible once every three years per system
Pump-out must be performed by a septage hauler approved by the Charles County Health Department (effective January 1, 2026)
Must submit online application with a copy of the contractor's receipt
Application must be received within six months of the pump-out
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the online application on the Charles County website and attach a copy of the contractor's receipt. Applications are verified and processed within 12 weeks, and a reimbursement check is mailed to the address provided.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides $14,000 in down payment assistance to eligible first-time homebuyers in Charles County. Funds help reduce the purchase price of an existing home and convert to a grant if the buyer lives in the home as their primary residence for at least five years.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: $14,000 in down payment assistance applied to reduce the purchase cost of an existing home. Funds are a grant if the homebuyer lives in the home as their principal residence for at least five years. Applicants must first be approved for the county's Settlement Expense Loan Program (SELP). Program ends when ARPA funds run out.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: When ARPA funds are no longer available
structured_extraction.program_audience: First-time homebuyers in Charles County with household income at or below 100% of Area Median Income (AMI) who have lived or worked full-time in the county for the past three years.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment assistance for the purchase of existing housing units (new construction is excluded).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must have lived or worked full-time in Charles County continuously for the last three years.
requirements_list: Must be a first-time homebuyer
Must be approved for the county's Settlement Expense Loan Program (SELP)
Household income must not exceed 100% of Area Median Income (AMI)
Must have lived or worked full-time in Charles County continuously for the last three years
Funds may only be used to purchase existing housing units — new construction is excluded
Must reside in the home as principal residence for at least five years for the assistance to convert to a grant
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested applicants must work with a SELP-approved lender to complete an application. Application details coming soon.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides low-interest or deferred loans to low- and moderate-income families to improve the basic livability of their single-family homes. Eligible work includes new roofs, windows, doors, and similar improvements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest or deferred loans to fund home improvement work such as new roofs, windows, and doors for low- and moderate-income homeowners.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low- and moderate-income single-family homeowners in Charles County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Basic home livability improvements such as roofs, windows, and doors
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Charles County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be low- or moderate-income
Must own a single-family home
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Charles County Housing Authority for details.

structured_extraction.program_description: A summer employment program that places young Charles County residents ages 16–24 who face academic or employment challenges with local businesses or non-profits, with support from Charles County Government.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Youth ages 16–24 are placed with area businesses or non-profits for summer employment. Host employers receive support from Charles County Government.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Charles County residents ages 16–24 who face academic or employment challenges; area businesses and non-profits seeking to host youth interns
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Summer employment experience for eligible youth; host businesses/non-profits receive support to employ participants
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Charles County resident (for youth participants)
requirements_list: Must be a Charles County resident
Must be between ages 16 and 24
Must face academic or employment challenges
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: See the program document linked on the page for details on how to apply or become a host employer.

structured_extraction.program_name: Surviving Spouse of Fallen EMS Officer Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides a property tax credit in Charles County to the surviving spouse of an emergency medical services (EMS) officer who died or was killed in the line of duty, reducing property tax liability on their primary residence.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A property tax credit for the surviving spouse of a fallen EMS officer who died in the line of duty in Charles County, reducing property tax liability on their primary residence.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Surviving spouses of EMS officers who died or were killed in the line of duty in Charles County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of property tax liability
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Charles County, Maryland
requirements_list: Applicant must be the surviving spouse of a fallen EMS officer who died in the line of duty
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Application for Surviving Spouse of Fallen EMS Officer Credit and submit to the Charles County Treasury office.

structured_extraction.program_description: A loan fund offering gap financing to businesses relocating to or expanding within target industries in Charles County. The fund is intended to supplement other financing and offers below-prime-rate loans with long repayment terms.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Gap financing loans up to $100,000 with a 15-year repayment period at a below-prime interest rate. Available to companies relocating to or expanding within Charles County target industries.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses in target industries that are relocating to or expanding within Charles County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business relocation or expansion costs for companies in target industries.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Charles County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be in a target industry
Must be relocating to or expanding within Charles County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download an application from the Charles County Economic Development website and submit to the department.

structured_extraction.program_description: Charles County's Transfer of Development Rights (TDR) program allows rural landowners to sell their development rights to private developers, who can then build at higher density in designated growth areas. Established in 1992, the program permanently restricts the seller's property to agricultural, forestry, and open space uses.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Landowners sell their development rights at a price negotiated between buyer and seller. The county certifies the number of TDRs associated with a property and tracks certified TDRs. A list of available TDRs can be obtained from the county.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Rural landowners in Charles County who wish to sell their development rights while keeping ownership of their land.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Landowners receive payment for their development rights; land is restricted to agricultural, forestry, and open space uses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Charles County, MD only.
requirements_list: Property must be eligible for TDR certification by Charles County
Participation is voluntary
Price negotiated between willing buyer and willing seller
Transfer recorded in Charles County Land Records
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Charles County Planning Staff to learn more. Work with the county to certify the number of TDRs for your property. Negotiate sale with a willing buyer.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides tuition reimbursement to eligible Charles County Government employees to support continued professional development through credit courses related to their current job or career progression within the County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimburses 100% of authorized tuition and textbook costs for up to 12 credit hours per year (maximum reimbursement amount set annually through the County budget process). Courses must be job-related or part of a degree related to the employee's current or expected County position. Undergraduates must earn a grade of C or better; graduate students must earn a B or better. Employees who leave County employment within one year of completing a reimbursed course must repay the benefit on a pro-rata basis.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Full-time and full-time reduced hour (grandfathered) Charles County Government employees who have worked for the County for at least one year and are not in a probationary period.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition and textbook costs for credit courses that are job-related or part of a degree related to the employee's current or expected County position.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to employees of Charles County Government.
requirements_list: Must be a full-time or full-time reduced hour (grandfathered) employee
Must have been employed with Charles County for at least 1 year
Must not be a probationary employee
Courses must be credit courses and job-related or part of a degree related to the employee's current job or a County position the employee may reasonably expect to progress into
Undergraduate students must earn a grade of C or better; graduate students must earn a grade of B or better
Employees must submit a final grade report showing successful course completion to receive reimbursement
Textbook receipts must be submitted for reimbursement
Employees who leave County employment within one year of course completion must reimburse the County on a pro-rata basis
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Employees must submit receipts for textbooks and a final grade report reflecting successful completion of the course. Additional details are in Chapter 21 of the Charles County Government Personnel Policies and Procedures Manual.

structured_extraction.program_description: VanGO Specialized Services provides door-to-door and paratransit transportation for people with disabilities and seniors in Charles County. It includes three service types: ADA Transportation (for people with disabilities near fixed routes), Demand Response (door-to-door service for seniors 60+ and people with disabilities), and Subscription Services (for trips to dialysis centers and senior centers). All rides are free.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free transportation services provided to eligible riders. ADA Transportation is available Monday–Saturday 6:00 a.m.–10:00 p.m. Demand Response is available Monday–Friday 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m. Subscription Services run Monday–Saturday 5:30 a.m.–5:30 p.m. All one-way trips and day passes are free. Personal care attendants may ride free if certified in advance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: People with disabilities who cannot use fixed-route public transit, and seniors age 60 and older who are unable to use fixed-route services due to a mental or physical impairment.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Transportation to medical appointments (including dialysis), senior centers, and other destinations within Charles County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Service is limited to Charles County, Maryland. ADA Transportation is available up to 3/4 mile around existing VanGO public routes. Demand Response destinations must be within Charles County.
requirements_list: Must complete a Specialized Services Application
Applications are reviewed weekly by the Specialized Services Review Committee
Applicants receive eligibility notification within two weeks
For ADA Transportation: must have a disability that prevents use of fixed-route transit
For Demand Response: must be age 60 or older, or have a disability; must live near a VanGO route and be unable to use fixed-route service
For Subscription Services: trips are to dialysis centers or Charles County Senior Centers
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Specialized Services Application and submit it by email to VanGO@CharlesCountyMD.Gov or by fax to 301-934-0107. The Specialized Services Review Committee reviews applications each week and notifies applicants of eligibility within two weeks.

structured_extraction.program_name: Volunteer Emergency Responders Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides a property tax credit in Charles County for active volunteer emergency responders such as firefighters and rescue/EMS personnel, recognizing their service to the community. Passed as Bill 2023-08 and effective October 4, 2023, the credit is applied to the real property of qualifying volunteer emergency responders who own property in Charles County, reducing their property tax liability.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A property tax credit applied to the real property of qualifying active volunteer emergency responders in Charles County, reducing their property tax liability.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Active volunteer emergency responders (e.g., firefighters, EMS/rescue personnel) in Charles County who own real property
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of property tax liability for volunteer emergency responders
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Charles County, Maryland only
requirements_list: Applicant must be an active volunteer emergency responder
Applicant must own real property in Charles County
Must be a volunteer emergency responder meeting eligibility requirements
