structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Volunteer Emergency Responders Tax Credit Application along with the required Affidavit and submit to the Charles County Treasury office.

structured_extraction.program_name: Waldorf Urban Redevelopment Corridor (WURC) Façade Improvement Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The WURC Façade Improvement Program provides matching grant funding to owners of existing commercial buildings within the Waldorf Urban Redevelopment Corridor (WURC) in Charles County to upgrade the visible, corridor-facing exterior components of their properties. Priority is given to projects fronting Old Washington Road.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a 50% matching grant reimbursement. The applicant pays 100% of approved façade improvement costs upfront, then receives 50% back from Charles County within 30 days of providing proof of payment. For example, a $10,000 project would result in a $5,000 grant reimbursement. Incremental draws may be possible depending on the award amount. Construction must be completed within 90 days of the award letter.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of commercial buildings and businesses located within the Waldorf Urban Redevelopment Corridor (WURC) in Charles County, MD.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eligible exterior façade improvements including: exterior wall building materials, façade color, balconies, roof treatments, roof utilities, building base and storefront, entries and doorways, windows, awnings and canopies, upper façade, lighting, cornice and fascia, porches, door hoods and stoops, roofs, chimneys, permits for eligible improvements, and signage.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Only commercial buildings located within the Waldorf Urban Redevelopment Corridor (WURC) in Charles County, Maryland are eligible. Priority is given to projects fronting Old Washington Road.
requirements_list: Application must be for a commercial building within the WURC boundary.
Application must be received by the designated deadline.
Projects must be for external building façade improvements only.
Work cannot begin prior to receiving a commitment letter from Charles County.
All scope-of-work changes must be approved by staff before work is done.
Applicant must agree to maintain all improvements in their finished state per the approved plans.
All project improvements must be paid in full by the awardee before reimbursement is issued.
Construction must be completed within 90 days of the award letter unless an extension is granted in writing.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Fill out the online application form on this page before the deadline. If selected, applicants will receive a commitment letter before starting work. After completing the project and paying all costs, submit canceled checks or other payment verification to receive the 50% reimbursement grant within 30 days. Extension requests must be submitted in writing to the Grant Administrator at least one week before the project expiration date.

structured_extraction.program_name: Senior Nutrition Program – Congregate Meals at Senior Centers
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides nutritious meals meeting one-third of the recommended dietary allowance to seniors in congregate (group) settings at senior centers. Meals offer opportunities for socialization. Menus may be provided in advance and reservations are required. Contributions toward the cost of meals are requested but not required. Spouses of any age and, in some locations, disabled children of eligible seniors (with approval) are also welcome.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Nutritious luncheon meals provided at senior centers at a subsidized cost. In Queen Anne's County, members age 60 and over (and spouses accompanying them) pay a suggested contribution of $3.00 per meal; staff, guests, and members under 60 pay the full cost of $6.79 per meal. In Charles County, contributions toward the cost of meals are requested but not required. Menus may be provided a month in advance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Seniors age 55 and older and their spouses of any age. In Charles County, residents aged 60 and older are eligible, along with spouses and disabled children of eligible seniors (with approval). In Queen Anne's County, seniors age 55 and over and their spouses of any age are eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Access to nutritious congregate meals and socialization opportunities at senior centers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to senior residents of Charles County and Queen Anne's County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be aged 55 or older (age 60 or older in Charles County)
Spouses of any age are welcome
Disabled children of eligible seniors may participate with approval (Charles County)
Reservations required (at least 2 weeks in advance in Queen Anne's County)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the senior center nearest you for days and hours of operation and to make a reservation. In Charles County, call 301-934-0138 or 301-870-3388 ext. 5138. In Queen Anne's County, contact Stacy Voorhees at 410-758-0848 x 2708 or svoorhees@qac.org.

structured_extraction.program_description: A facility development program for charter schools that provides leasing arrangements with a pathway to ownership. The program handles facility planning, financing, construction, and development so school leaders can focus on education. Schools lease facilities tailored to their educational model, student population, and budget, with the option to eventually purchase the building.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 22Beacon acquires, renovates, or constructs school facilities and leases them to charter schools with a purchase option. The program covers facility acquisition, renovation, and new construction. Schools receive comprehensive support from planning through construction, with 47 schools having exercised their purchase option to date.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Charter schools seeking to secure, develop, or finance school facilities with a pathway to ownership.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition, renovation, or new construction of charter school facilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: National program; 22Beacon is headquartered in Hanover, MD.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Schools can reach out to 22Beacon by phone, email, or through the contact form at 22beacon.org/contact, providing details about current facility challenges, future growth plans, and specific needs.

structured_extraction.program_name: Building Block Fund — Lease and Loan Guarantee and Direct Lending Programs
structured_extraction.program_description: A credit enhancement program offered by 22Beacon (Charter Schools Development Corporation) that helps charter schools secure facility loans or leases. It provides partial and limited guarantees, additional collateral, loan loss reserves, debt service reserve funds, and direct loans to enable schools to obtain fully financed, affordable facilities for acquisition, renovation, or construction. The program aims for 100% financed facilities at an affordable cost and is available in 30 states and Washington D.C., including Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides credit enhancement support including partial and limited lease and loan guarantees, additional collateral, loan loss reserves, debt service reserve funds, and direct loans to charter schools seeking to finance facility loans or leases. Enables access to funding under more favorable terms, aiming for 100% financed facilities at an affordable cost.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Charter schools seeking facility loans or leases, especially those needing credit enhancement to qualify for financing or secure more favorable terms.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition, renovation, or construction of charter school facilities; securing facility loans or leases for safe, modern, economical, and efficient school facilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in 30 states and Washington D.C.; 22Beacon is headquartered in Hanover, MD and serves Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact 22Beacon via phone, email at info@22beacon.org, or complete an application through the 22Beacon/CSDC website at 22beacon.org/contact or csdc.org to begin the application process.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Catapult Fund is a flexible, affordable loan fund created by 22Beacon (formerly Charter Schools Development Corporation/CSDC) and EFF for high-impact public charter schools that are traditionally underserved by conventional lenders. It provides customized loan products for pre-development, construction, renovations, tenant improvements, and working capital, with interest rates significantly below comparable market offerings. The fund prioritizes single-site schools where more than 65% of students qualify for free and reduced-price lunch, breaking down financial barriers for schools serving economically disadvantaged students. The program is available in 30 states and Washington D.C., including Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The fund offers four loan products: (1) Bridge/Pre-Development loans averaging $750K (max $3M) with 12-month average terms (max 24 months); (2) Working Capital loans averaging $250K (max $750K) with 12-month average terms (max 36 months); (3) Tenant Improvement loans averaging $1M (max $3M) with 36-month average terms (max 60 months); (4) Term Loans averaging $2M (max $3M) with 36-month average terms (max 60 months). Interest rates are significantly below comparable market offerings, providing low-cost capital to support facility acquisition, construction, renovation, and general school growth and sustainability needs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: High-impact public charter schools, particularly single-site schools where more than 65% of students qualify for free and reduced-price lunch, that are traditionally underserved by conventional lenders.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Pre-development costs, construction, renovations, tenant improvements, facility acquisition, working capital, and general school growth and sustainability needs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in 30 states and Washington D.C., including Maryland. Administered by 22Beacon (formerly CSDC), a Maryland-based organization.
requirements_list: Must be a public charter school
Priority given to single-site schools where more than 65% of students qualify for free and reduced-price lunch
Must be high-impact and traditionally underserved by conventional lenders
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online through the application form (https://www.tfaforms.com/5159722) or contact 22Beacon/CSDC directly to determine if Catapult is the right fit for your project.

structured_extraction.program_name: Charters RISE (Renovating for Innovative Sustainable Education)
structured_extraction.program_description: Charters RISE is a program run by 22Beacon (formerly Charter Schools Development Corporation) in partnership with Ameresco and LISC. It uses federal grant funding from the U.S. Department of Energy's Renew America's Schools Program to implement clean energy improvements in charter school facilities. The program aims to reduce facilities operating costs, support workforce development, and expand access to climate education in underserved communities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 22Beacon received an initial $300,000 prize and is part of a $15 million grant award from the U.S. Department of Energy's Renew America's Schools Program. Funds are invested in 13 Local Education Agencies (LEAs) across 10 states to implement clean energy and sustainability improvements in K-12 charter school facilities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Charter school Local Education Agencies (LEAs) seeking funding for clean energy facility improvements, particularly in underserved communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Clean energy improvements and renovations to K-12 charter school facilities, energy efficiency upgrades, workforce development, and climate education.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available across multiple states; 22Beacon is investing in 13 LEAs across 10 states. Program serves schools nationwide.
requirements_list: Must be a K-12 public charter school or Local Education Agency (LEA)
Must be in an underserved or under-resourced community
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact 22Beacon at info@22beacon.org or visit https://www.22beacon.org for more information about how to access funding through Charters RISE.

structured_extraction.program_description: City First Bank provides commercial loan products for affordable housing developers, including acquisition, construction-to-permanent, bridge, and unitranche financing for affordable housing development and preservation of Naturally Occurring Affordable Housing (NOAH). The program ensures long-term affordability for households earning up to 120% of Median Family Income (MFI). The bank partners with minority-led developers and community-based investors to expand housing access in underserved neighborhoods.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loan products for acquisition, construction-to-permanent, bridge, and unitranche financing for affordable housing development. Acquisition: up to $21,000,000, up to 10 years, up to 80% LTV. Construction-to-Permanent: up to 7 years for rehabilitation/construction, monthly interest-only during construction. Bridge: up to 24 months (longer for LIHTC) for short-term financing with identified takeout. Unitranche: up to 7 years for acquisition/construction financing, up to 90% LTV in coordination with City First Enterprises. LTV ranges 50%-80% depending on property type; LTC up to 85%. Origination fee: 1%-2%.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit and non-profit affordable housing developers and investors developing or preserving affordable housing for households earning up to 120% of MFI.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition of land or properties, rehabilitation or construction, short-term bridge financing with identified takeout, and acquisition/construction financing for affordable housing projects including NOAH properties.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City First Bank operates in the District of Columbia, Maryland, Virginia, Delaware, Pennsylvania, and California.
requirements_list: Projects must serve households at or below 120% of Median Family Income (MFI)
Units at or below 80% of AMI
DSCR of 1.20x at stabilization
LTV: 50%-80% depending on property type
LTC: up to 85%
Personal guarantees required from owners with 20% or more ownership interest
Monthly principal and interest payments (or interest-only for bridge loans)
Origination fee: 1%-2%
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact City First Bank by phone to discuss loan terms and application, or speak with a banker or schedule an appointment at the Washington DC branch via the bank's website to arrange a tailored funding strategy.

structured_extraction.program_name: City First Bank Financing for Businesses
structured_extraction.program_description: City First Bank provides customized financing solutions for small businesses and minority-owned enterprises to help them build, grow, and serve local communities. This includes working capital lines of credit, term loans for equipment, vehicles, supplies, leasehold improvements, and business expansion, owner-occupied commercial real estate financing, SBA 504 loans, SBA 7(a), Express, and Veterans Advantage loan products. The bank focuses on helping companies with revenues under $25 million become or remain owner-occupants of their business properties, primarily serving the Washington, DC metropolitan area and surrounding Maryland communities, as well as Virginia, Delaware, Pennsylvania, and California.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Multiple loan products including: Working Capital Lines of Credit, Term Loans (equipment, vehicles, supplies, leasehold improvements, business expansion), Owner-Occupied Real Estate Loans, SBA 504 Loans, SBA 7(a)/Express/Veterans Advantage loans. Primarily available to businesses with revenues under $25 million. DSCR requirements of 1.2x-1.3x depending on product. SBA products require tangible net worth less than $15 million and income less than $5 million.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit businesses with a minimum of 3 years of operations (varies by product), particularly small businesses and minority-owned enterprises with revenues under $25 million seeking financing for commercial real estate, equipment, working capital, or other business needs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cash flow needs, receivables financing, operating expenses, equipment/vehicle/supply purchase, leasehold improvements, business expansion, real estate purchase/refinance, construction, land/building purchase, and SBA-guaranteed loan purposes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City First Bank primarily serves the Washington, DC metropolitan area and surrounding Maryland communities, including Montgomery County, Prince George's County, Baltimore City, and Baltimore County, as well as Virginia, Delaware, Pennsylvania, and California.
requirements_list: Business revenues must be under $25 million
Minimum 3 years of operations (most products)
Tangible net worth less than $15 million and income less than $5 million (SBA products)
DSCR of 1.2x-1.3x (varies by product)
Owner-occupied for 51% of existing or 60% of new construction (SBA 504)
Any owner with 20%+ ownership must guarantee
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Speak with a City First Bank banker or call 888.351.3280 to schedule an appointment and discuss a tailored funding strategy.

structured_extraction.program_description: City First Bank's Commercial Impact Business Savings Account lets businesses and nonprofits grow their reserves while supporting community-focused banking. The account earns a competitive interest rate and is designed for organizations that want their savings to serve both their mission and their financial goals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Interest-bearing savings account with a $250 minimum to open. Earns a competitive interest rate on balances of $100 or more. A $5 monthly service charge applies if the monthly average balance falls below $2,500.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses and nonprofits seeking an interest-bearing savings account that supports community-first banking.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Growing organizational reserves while earning interest.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City First Bank serves Washington, DC and surrounding areas.
requirements_list: Minimum $250 to open the account
Minimum $100 deposit to earn the competitive interest rate
Minimum monthly average balance of $2,500 to avoid the $5 monthly service charge
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Speak with a banker or schedule an appointment at the Washington DC branch. Enroll online via the Digital One Business portal.

structured_extraction.program_description: City First Bank provides customized financing for community-based nonprofits to support the development and expansion of owner-occupied facilities in minority-majority and low-income urban communities, as well as broader operational and capital project needs. Eligible projects include health care centers, charter schools, arts organizations, and social service facilities. Financing options include working capital lines of credit, term loans, commercial real estate loans, lines of credit for working capital, standby letters of credit, and leverage source loans.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: City First Bank offers working capital lines of credit (up to $5M, up to 3 years, monthly interest-only payments) and term loans (up to $21M, up to 10 years, fully amortizing) to nonprofits. For charter schools, term loans cover facility acquisition, finance, and refinance, and leasehold improvements. Uses include working capital, receivables financing, general operating expenses, equipment, vehicles, supplies, leasehold improvements, organizational expansion, and property acquisition. Origination fee of 1-2%; personal guaranty typically not required.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community-based nonprofits and charter schools with a minimum of 3 years of operations, operating or developing owner-occupied facilities in minority-majority and low-income urban communities in DC, MD, VA, DE, PA, and CA
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Working capital; receivables financing; general operating expenses; purchase of vehicles, equipment, or supplies; leasehold improvements; facility acquisition, finance, and refinance; organizational expansion and growth; property acquisition
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: District of Columbia, Maryland, Virginia, Delaware, Pennsylvania, and California; focused on minority-majority and low-income urban communities
requirements_list: Must be a nonprofit organization
Minimum 3 years of operations
Debt Service Coverage Ratio (DSCR) of 1.2x
Up to $21,000,000 available for term loans; up to $5,000,000 for lines of credit
Loan terms up to 10 years (amortization up to 25 years for real estate)
1-2% origination fee
Typically no personal guaranty required
Project must involve owner-occupied commercial real estate or a qualifying facility (for real estate loans)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact City First Bank at 888.351.3280 or speak with a City First Bank banker to arrange a tailored funding strategy. Appointments can also be scheduled via the City First Bank website.

structured_extraction.program_description: City First Bank offers Property Assessed Clean Energy (PACE) financing, a green lending product that helps nonprofits and property owners finance energy efficiency, renewable energy, and other eligible improvements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: PACE financing allows borrowers to fund clean energy and energy efficiency improvements, with repayment tied to a property assessment rather than a traditional loan structure.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofits and property owners seeking to finance energy efficiency or clean energy improvements
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency upgrades, renewable energy installations, and other eligible green property improvements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Speak with a City First Bank banker to arrange a tailored funding strategy.

structured_extraction.program_description: Free evening workshops held at the Brooklyn Park Library covering personal finance topics including debt management, budgeting, credit understanding, identity theft prevention, and insurance basics.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free evening workshops on personal finance topics including debt management, budgeting, credit, identity theft prevention, and insurance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents of Anne Arundel County seeking financial education.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable — educational workshops with no direct funding component.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Classes held at the Brooklyn Park Library in Anne Arundel County (Annapolis area).
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Check the ACDS website at acdsinc.org/housing-resources/financial-empowerment for current class schedules.

structured_extraction.program_description: A shared-ride public transportation service for people with disabilities who are functionally unable to independently use Annapolis Transit fixed-route buses, as required by the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990. Eligible riders can reserve door-to-curb transportation within three-quarters of a mile of any Annapolis Transit fixed-route bus stop. Service is available Monday–Friday 5:30 AM–11:00 PM, Saturday 7:15 AM–11:00 PM, and Sunday 7:00 AM–8:00 PM. A reduced fare program and subscription (standing ride) service are also available.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Shared-ride curb-to-curb transportation service at a one-way cash fare of $4.00 (twice the fixed-route fare). Personal Care Attendants ride free of charge. One companion may accompany an eligible rider at the same fare. Subscription (standing ride) service is available for regular recurring trips. Service hours are Monday–Friday 5:30 AM–11:00 PM, Saturday 7:15 AM–11:00 PM, and Sunday 7:00 AM–8:00 PM. A reduced fare program is also available for qualifying riders.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Markus G. Moore, Director of Transportation
structured_extraction.program_audience: People with disabilities who are functionally unable to independently use Annapolis Transit fixed-route bus services, as determined by their physician, including visitors who are already ADA-eligible through another transit agency.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Accessible shared-ride transportation for eligible riders with disabilities within the Annapolis Transit service area.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Service area consists of any location within three-quarters (3/4) of a mile of any fixed-route service operated by Annapolis Transit in Annapolis, MD.
requirements_list: Must have a disability that prevents independent use of Annapolis Transit fixed-route buses
Eligibility determined by the individual's physician based on inability to use fixed-route buses
Must complete an ADA Paratransit certification application and submit it to ADOT (Annapolis Department of Transportation, 308 Chinquapin Round Road, Annapolis, MD 21401)
Must obtain a valid Annapolis Transit Disability photo identification card upon approval
Visitors already certified ADA eligible by another transit agency may use service up to 21 days within a 365-day period without local certification
Reservations must be made at least one day in advance by calling 410-263-7964 between 8:30 AM and 4:00 PM; same-day service is not available
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the ADA Paratransit certification application (PDF available online) and mail or deliver it to ADA Paratransit Certification, Annapolis Department of Transportation, 308 Chinquapin Round Road, Annapolis, MD 21401. The application is reviewed and the applicant is notified by mail within approximately 21 days. If approved, visit ADOT to obtain a photo identification card, then call 410-263-7964 to reserve rides at least one day before the trip is needed. A separate reduced fare application form is also available for qualifying riders seeking discounted fares.

structured_extraction.program_name: Adopt a Community FY 2024 Building Resilient Communities Together: Boots on the Ground Community Engagement Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: This grant funds community-based nonprofit organizations to do hands-on outreach and engagement work in specific at-risk neighborhoods in Annapolis. Grantees build long-term relationships with residents, connect them to resources, and apply a public health approach to violence prevention and community resilience.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time grants of up to $20,000 per organization, with a total funding pool of up to $200,000. Only one organization will be funded per neighborhood. A maximum of 10% of funds may be used for overhead costs. The funding period is September 2023 through June 30, 2024.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis until funds are used
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit (501c3) community-based organizations serving at-risk neighborhoods in Annapolis, MD
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Community engagement and relationship-building activities including mentorship programs, mental health services, trauma-informed programming, neighborhood outreach, and resident empowerment initiatives in one specific Annapolis neighborhood.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must operate within the City of Annapolis limits in one of the designated at-risk neighborhoods: Bay Ridge Gardens, Harbour House/Eastport Terrace, Madison Apartments, Bywater, Robinwood, Annapolis Gardens, Admiral Oaks, Clay Street/Obery Court/College Creek Apartments, Woodside, Parole, Allen Apartments, Admiral Farragut, Quiet Waters, or Watergate Village.
requirements_list: Must have 501(c)(3) nonprofit status
Must focus on one specific Annapolis neighborhood
Must include hands-on, one-on-one community engagement strategies
Must submit an itemized budget proposal
Must submit progress reports twice during the grant period
Must attend quarterly meetings with the Office of Community Services
Must not fund one-time pop-up events or projects outside Annapolis
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a complete application through the online application portal at https://arcg.is/1XSnbT. Include a work plan with timeline, SMARTIE goals, performance measures, and an itemized budget. Organizations unable to use the portal may contact communityservices@annapolis.gov to submit by paper at City Hall or by email.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free GED preparation class offered at the Stanton Community Center in partnership with Anne Arundel Community College (AACC). The class helps adults 18 and older without a high school diploma prepare for the GED exam, covering all four required subjects: math, science, social studies, and language arts. Successfully passing the GED earns participants a Maryland High School diploma.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free GED preparation classes meeting every Saturday from 9 am to 1 pm. The class covers math, science, social studies, and language arts. Participants must attend an orientation before registering.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults 18 or older who do not have a high school diploma and need to prepare for the GED exam.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: GED exam preparation leading to a Maryland High School diploma.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Classes are held at the Stanton Community Center in Annapolis, MD.
requirements_list: Must be 18 years of age or older
Must not have a high school diploma
Must attend an orientation with AACC before registering
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact AACC at gedprogram@aacc.edu or 410-777-1823 to schedule an orientation. Attend the orientation prior to registering for the class.

structured_extraction.program_name: Annapolis Conservancy Board Conservation Easement Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Annapolis Conservancy Board accepts donations of conservation easements and property on private land within the City of Annapolis to preserve open space, provide recreational opportunities, and improve water quality in the Chesapeake Bay and its tributaries. Landowners donate a legal agreement to restrict development on their land while retaining ownership, preserving it in its natural state or enhancing its environmental potential. Landowners retain the ability to sell or pass on the land. In return, landowners may receive tax benefits including a 15-year real property tax credit on the unimproved land, a reduction of federal estate taxes, and a reduction of federal income taxes for up to 6 years. The monetary value of the easement is determined by appraising the land at fair market value with and without the easement, and the difference may be used for tax deduction purposes. The Conservancy Board manages the easement on behalf of the City, monitors compliance annually, and assists landowners throughout the entire process at no cost. Easement terms can be customized to fit landowner and community needs, and may be granted in perpetuity or for a limited time. The easement is recorded as a deed in county land records and binds all present and future owners.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Landowners who donate a conservation easement may receive: (1) a 15-year real property tax credit on the unimproved land; (2) a reduction of federal estate taxes; and (3) a reduction of federal income taxes for up to 6 years. The monetary value of the easement is determined by appraising the land at fair market value with and without the easement, and the difference may be used for tax deduction purposes. The Conservancy Board also manages and monitors the easement on behalf of the City, providing ongoing technical assistance to landowners at no cost. Easement terms can be customized to fit landowner and community needs, and may be granted in perpetuity or for a limited time.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private landowners in the City of Annapolis whose land has definite conservation, scenic, or recreational value and who wish to preserve it from unwanted development in its natural or near-natural state for conservation, recreation, or environmental purposes.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Preservation of open space, natural habitats, scenic areas, and recreational land; protection of land from unwanted development; conservation of land that improves water quality in the Chesapeake Bay and its tributaries. Tax benefits derived from the easement donation can offset property taxes, federal income taxes, and federal estate taxes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Limited to land located within the City of Annapolis, Maryland. Land must have definite conservation or recreational value.
requirements_list: Land must be located within the City of Annapolis
Land must have definite conservation or recreation value
Landowner must agree to restrict development in accordance with easement terms, including terms restricting development inconsistent with environmental preservation
Easement deed must be executed and recorded in the county land records and binds all present and future owners
Easement may be granted in perpetuity or for a limited time, as agreed
Specific terms of the easement are agreed upon between the landowner and the Conservancy Board
Terms can be customized to fit landowner and community needs
Conservancy Board monitors easements annually to ensure compliance
Land is appraised to determine easement value
No formal application required; contact Planning and Zoning Department to initiate evaluation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Annapolis Department of Planning and Zoning and leave a message for the Conservancy Board. A staff member will follow up to evaluate the land for a possible easement donation. There are no formal applications to complete; the Board assists landowners through every step of the process at no cost.

structured_extraction.program_description: A pilot program that allows restaurants in Annapolis to use private parking lots and public sidewalks or streets for outdoor dining. Participating restaurants receive a permit to operate outdoor dining spaces after a city review process. The program aims to inform future city policy on outdoor dining.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Restaurants receive a city permit to operate outdoor dining in private parking lots, on public sidewalks, or on public streets. The permit fee is $4,228, payable in full or in two installments of $2,114 each. The permit is valid for a seasonal period. Restaurants in the Historic District must follow Historic Preservation Commission guidelines.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Restaurants in Annapolis seeking to expand dining into private parking lots, public sidewalks, or public streets.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Permit to operate outdoor dining spaces adjacent to a restaurant, including seasonal parking lot dining, sidewalk cafes, and street cafes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only to restaurants located within the City of Annapolis, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a restaurant operating in Annapolis
Submit a completed application identifying the outdoor dining type
Provide a letter from the parking lot property owner authorizing its use for outdoor dining if the lot is not owned by the applicant
Provide the restaurant street address, a photo of the space, and a site plan with measurements
Identify proposed barricades and provide safety information
Identify the number of impacted parking spaces
Pay the $4,228 permit processing fee (or two installments of $2,114)
Provide survey information to the City for the duration of the pilot study
Adhere to Historic Preservation Commission guidelines if operating within the Historic District
Obtain a tent/temporary structure permit if operating outside the Historic District
Obtain an updated Alcohol Beverage Control Board license if serving alcohol outdoors
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Parking Lot Dining Pilot Program Application online. The application is reviewed by Public Works, the Fire Marshal's Office, Planning & Zoning Code Enforcement, and the Historic Preservation Office (for Historic District restaurants). After review, if no significant objections are raised, the Department of Planning and Zoning issues a Parking Lot Dining Permit. Payment of the permit fee is requested upon receipt of the application.

structured_extraction.program_description: An honorary position for a poet who promotes literary arts and literacy within the Annapolis community. The Poet Laureate serves as the poetic voice of the City, participates in public events, performs and speaks about poetry and literary arts, and reaches out to children and adults through schools, community centers, and libraries.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: $1,000 annual honorarium plus up to $500 reimbursement for expenses incurred while fulfilling duties of the position. Term is one year beginning Fall 2024, renewable for a second year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Poets who live, work, or attend an academic institution within a Ward of the City of Annapolis, are at least 21 years old, and have experience in poetry through a body of work (published or unpublished).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Honorarium for serving as Poet Laureate; reimbursement for expenses related to fulfilling duties of the position.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicant or nominee must live, work, or attend an academic institution within a Ward of the City of Annapolis.
requirements_list: Must live, work, or attend an academic institution within a Ward of the City of Annapolis
Must be at least 21 years old
Must have experience in the field of poetry demonstrated through a body of work, published or unpublished
Must be able to fulfill a one-year term in residence
Must attend and participate in selected ceremonial/civic engagement events
Must participate in poetry advocacy events including Poetry Month in April
Must undertake a community outreach project
Must report on work as Poet Laureate to the AIPPC as needed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a completed application/nomination form, five poems (published or unpublished), at least one recommendation letter, a 250-word narrative about the applicant's life/career/poetry, and a 500-word statement on how a Poet Laureate can benefit Annapolis. Submit in person at Pip Moyer Recreation Center, by email, or by postal mail postmarked by July 26, 2024. A selection panel will review applications, select finalists for interviews in August, and recommend the best candidate to the Mayor for appointment in Fall 2024.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Annapolis Police Athletic League (PAL) provides youth programs focused on athletics, educational development, and social development. Programs include boxing, chess club, volleyball, and field hockey. The goal is to prevent juvenile crime and violence by building positive relationships between young people and police officers, and by fostering self-worth, community, and character.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free youth programming including boxing, chess club (free, ages 6-18, held on the fourth Saturday of every month), volleyball for middle school students, and field hockey for girls in middle school. No financial assistance is provided; the program offers structured recreational and educational activities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Youth of Annapolis, particularly children and middle school students (ages 6-18)
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participation in athletic, educational, and social development programs including boxing, chess, volleyball, and field hockey.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to youth in Annapolis, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a youth residing in or attending school in Annapolis
Chess Club open to children ages 6-18
Volleyball open to Annapolis middle school students
Field hockey for middle school girls
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Cpl. Jamal Davis at jedavis@annapolis.gov to sign up youth, volunteer, explore sponsorship opportunities, or discuss partnerships.

structured_extraction.program_description: A two-pronged program run by the Annapolis Police Department to address substance use disorder (SUD) in the city. One focus is education and prevention for at-risk youth in identified high-risk areas. The second focus is harm reduction, treatment, and recovery, with officers following up with overdose survivors and connecting them to support services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Prevention education for at-risk youth in high-risk areas, and follow-up support for overdose survivors connecting them to harm reduction, treatment, and recovery resources.
structured_extraction.program_audience: At-risk youth in identified hotspot areas and overdose survivors in Annapolis.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Substance use prevention education and connection to harm reduction and recovery resources.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Annapolis, Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Officer Amanda Benson by email or phone to learn more about the program.

structured_extraction.program_name: Around Each Corner Youth Poetry Book
structured_extraction.program_description: A youth poetry contest and publication program run by the City of Annapolis. Young people submit original poems sharing their stories, backgrounds, cultures, and experiences. Selected poems are published in a youth poetry book called 'Around Each Corner.'
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Selected young poets have their poems published in the City of Annapolis youth poetry book 'Around Each Corner.' There is no monetary award described — the benefit is publication and public recognition.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Youth enrolled in an Annapolis educational institution, home school, or pursuing a degree at Anne Arundel Community College.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Publication of poetry in a youth poetry book.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be enrolled in an Annapolis educational institution, home school, or pursuing a degree at Anne Arundel Community College.
requirements_list: Must be enrolled in an Annapolis educational institution, home school, or pursuing a degree at Anne Arundel Community College
Must submit poem by August 17, 2026 via the online application form or by email
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit poem via the online application form at the provided survey link, or email poems to rjsmith@annapolis.gov. Applications accepted from March 5, 2026 to August 17, 2026. The poetry book presentation is scheduled for October 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit available to arts and entertainment businesses, property owners, or individuals in the City of Annapolis, administered by the Department of Planning and Zoning. The credit applies to qualifying arts and entertainment activities within the city, with specific amounts and eligibility criteria detailed in the application form.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax credit for arts and entertainment activities in the City of Annapolis. Specific amounts and terms are detailed in the application form, available from the Department of Planning and Zoning or the Finance Forms page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Arts and entertainment businesses, property owners, and individuals involved in arts and entertainment activities in Annapolis.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credit applied to City of Annapolis taxes for qualifying arts and entertainment activities, providing tax relief related to arts and entertainment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Annapolis, Anne Arundel County, Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and submit the Arts and Entertainment Tax Credit Application (PDF) available on the Finance Forms page or from the Department of Planning and Zoning.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Case Management program connects residents with Social Work Care Coordinators who assess individual and family needs, then arrange, coordinate, monitor, evaluate, and advocate for services to meet those needs. Services include resource coordination, application assistance for rental, food, and utilities programs, and case management and service coordination.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Social Work Care Coordinators assess client needs and then arrange, coordinate, monitor, evaluate, and advocate for a package of services including rental assistance applications, food assistance, and utility assistance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Annapolis residents who need help accessing social services, including assistance with rental, food, and utility applications.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Connecting clients with rental, food, and utility assistance resources and coordinating supportive services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Annapolis, Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Social Work Care Coordinators directly by phone or email to get started.

structured_extraction.program_name: Chesapeake Bay Stewardship Fund Small Watershed Grants (National Fish and Wildlife Foundation)
structured_extraction.program_description: Small watershed grants through the Chesapeake Bay Stewardship Fund that support stormwater project design and implementation to improve water quality in the Chesapeake Bay watershed.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Small watershed grants for both stormwater design and project implementation. Applications are typically due in the spring.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations and entities seeking funding for stormwater and watershed improvement projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Design and implementation of stormwater and watershed restoration projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Chesapeake Bay watershed region.
requirements_list: Projects must benefit Chesapeake Bay water quality
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are typically due in the spring. See the linked website for details.

structured_extraction.program_name: Chesapeake Bay Trust - Chesapeake Conservation Climate Corps
structured_extraction.program_description: A year-long stipend-supported service program placing young adults (ages 18-25) at host organizations across Maryland to support environmental and climate-related projects. The City of Annapolis Resilience and Sustainability Division hosts a Climate Coordinator position to help implement the City's Climate Action Plan, conduct research on climate legislation and policy, and support community engagement activities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A stipend of $33,280 annually, disbursed bimonthly, for a year of service from August 19, 2026 to August 19, 2027. Benefits include health care coverage (for those without private coverage), 15 professional development trainings, 4 all-cohort project days, 4-10 networking visits to fellow Corps Members and host organizations, 1 capstone project, 1 grant opportunity, and funding to attend a regional professional conference.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Young adults ages 18-25 who are U.S. citizens or authorized to work in the U.S., interested in climate, environment, and sustainability work across Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Stipend to support a year of service working on environmental and climate resilience projects at host organizations across Maryland.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available across the state of Maryland; approximately 50 Corps Members are placed at host organizations statewide.
requirements_list: Age 18-25 at the start of the program
Must be a U.S. citizen, permanent resident alien, or have documentation confirming permission to work in the U.S. during the year-long term of service
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Chesapeake Bay Trust website. Applicants interested in working with the City of Annapolis should indicate that preference during the application process.

structured_extraction.program_name: City of Annapolis Before and After School Child Care Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Annapolis Recreation and Parks Department offers before and after school child care at select elementary schools in Annapolis. Families can register for supervised care at Annapolis Elementary, Germantown Elementary, Hillsmere Elementary, Mills-Parole Elementary, and West Annapolis Elementary schools. Child care vouchers (scholarships) are accepted. Registration for the 2026-2027 school year begins April 13, 2026 for returning families and April 15, 2026 for new families, and is first-come, first-served based on available space.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Before-school (AM) care is available for $120 per month and after-school (PM) care for $300 per month for the 2026-2027 school year. There is a $35 non-refundable registration fee. Child care vouchers (scholarships) are accepted. Care is provided at Annapolis Elementary, Germantown Elementary, Hillsmere Elementary, Mills-Parole Elementary, and West Annapolis Elementary. Registration is first-come, first-served based on available space.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Registration for 2026-2027 school year begins April 13, 2026 for returning families and April 15, 2026 for new families.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with school-age children attending participating Annapolis elementary schools
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supervised child care before and after the school day at participating elementary schools in Annapolis
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at select elementary schools in Annapolis, Maryland: Annapolis Elementary, Germantown Elementary, Hillsmere Elementary, Mills-Parole Elementary, and West Annapolis Elementary.
requirements_list: Child must attend one of the five participating Annapolis elementary schools
$35 non-refundable registration fee required
Child Care Registration Form 2026-2027 due at time of registration
Emergency Form (MSDE OCC) due at time of registration
Health Inventory (MSDE OCC) due by first day of school
MD Immunization Form required
Medication Administration Authorization Form required if applicable
Families using child care vouchers must complete required paperwork through the Child Care Scholarship Program
Registration is first-come, first-served as space allows
Registration forms must be submitted online or in person at the 'Pip' Moyer Recreation Center
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register online at the provided link or in person at the 'Pip' Moyer Recreation Center. Complete and submit the Child Care Registration Form 2026-2027 along with required documents. Pay the $35 non-refundable registration fee at time of registration. Families using child care vouchers must separately apply through the Maryland Child Care Scholarship Program.

structured_extraction.program_name: City of Annapolis Commercial Recycling Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Annapolis offers a commercial recycling collection service to businesses located within city limits. The City provides 32-gallon containers for recyclable materials and collects them once a week. Businesses may also purchase their own wheeled cart up to 96 gallons for recycling use.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The City provides 32-gallon recycling containers at no stated additional cost and offers once-a-week curbside recycling collection for businesses. Pricing is listed on a separate fee schedule page. Businesses may also purchase a commercial-grade wheeled cart up to 96 gallons.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses located within the City of Annapolis limits that can accommodate once-a-week recycling collection.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Curbside collection of recyclable materials including paper, plastic, metal, and glass.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only to businesses within the City of Annapolis city limits.
requirements_list: Business must be located within City of Annapolis limits
Must be able to handle one-day-a-week collection schedule
Recycling must be placed at the curb by 6:00 am but not before 11:00 pm the night before collection
Containers must be removed immediately after collection
All material must be placed loose in the recycling container
Cardboard not fitting in the container must be tied in bundles not exceeding 35 pounds and one foot in thickness
Avoid contamination of recycling materials
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Sign up through the online portal at the City of Annapolis recycling sign-up page (annrec123.portal.iworq.net).

structured_extraction.program_name: City of Annapolis Owner Occupied Housing Rehabilitation Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Eligible Annapolis homeowners can receive forgiveness loans for home improvements performed by a licensed contractor. No cash is given directly — a contractor does the work at no upfront cost. Improvements may include roof replacement, plumbing and electrical upgrades, furnace replacement, and kitchen and bathroom remodeling. Funding comes from the federal Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) program and is administered locally by Arundel Community Development Services (ACDS).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Forgiveness loan — home improvement work is performed at no cost to the homeowner. If the home is sold, rented, or transferred within 15 years, the full amount must be repaid. After year 11, the loan balance is reduced by 20% per year for the remaining five years. Maximum assistance is $30,000 per household.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low- to moderate-income Annapolis homeowners who use the property as their primary residence
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home repairs and improvements including roof replacement, plumbing and electrical upgrades, furnace replacement, and kitchen and bathroom remodeling
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a homeowner in Annapolis, MD
requirements_list: Must be a homeowner in Annapolis, MD
Property must be the applicant's sole and principal residence
Combined household income must be less than 60% of Area Median Income
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Property Rehabilitation Program pre-application with proof of income for all household members, proof of homeownership, proof of homeowners insurance, and proof that mortgage payments are current. Mail the completed application to Arundel Community Development Services, Inc., 2666 Riva Road, Suite 210, Annapolis, MD 21401. Or visit the ACDS website at acdsinc.org.

structured_extraction.program_name: City of Annapolis Rental Assistance Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Annapolis provides short-term rental assistance to low- and moderate-income residents facing financial hardship, including risk of eviction or housing instability. The program helps eligible households pay rent, security deposits, and/or unpaid utility bills. Approved funds are paid directly to the landlord, property manager, or utility company on the applicant's behalf. Assistance is limited to once per fiscal year and approvals are not guaranteed. Application processing can take up to 4–6 weeks.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance for rent, security deposits, and/or unpaid utility bills, paid directly to the landlord, property manager, or utility company by check. The approved amount is based on the applicant's qualifications. Assistance is limited to once per fiscal year. Processing takes up to 3 business days for approval/denial notification, and up to 4–6 weeks for the check to be received. A promissory letter is provided during processing. Account balances must not be more than 60 days past due. Approvals are not guaranteed.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low- and moderate-income renters living in the City of Annapolis who are at risk of homelessness or housing instability, including those who are employed, have been employed in the last 90 days, or are receiving retirement benefits.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rent payments, security deposits, and unpaid utility bills paid directly to the landlord, property manager, or utility company.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be renting within the City of Annapolis in a unit with a current and valid City of Annapolis rental license.
requirements_list: Must live in and rent within the City of Annapolis
Household income must be at or below 80% of Area Median Income (AMI) as defined by HUD
One or more household members must demonstrate risk of homelessness or housing instability (e.g., past-due rent or utility notice, eviction notice)
Must hold a lease or sublease in the applicant's name (or demonstrate they will in the case of security deposit assistance)
Must be currently employed, have been employed in the last 90 days, or be retired/receiving retirement benefits (offer letter acceptable if not yet started)
Unemployment benefits are not accepted as qualifying income
Must be renting in a unit with a current and valid City of Annapolis rental license
Account balances must not be more than 60 days past due
Assistance is limited to once per fiscal year
Must provide proof of current residency (official letter on company letterhead from property manager confirming residency and all individuals on the lease)
Payments can only be made to rental properties
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the online application at https://www.annapolis.gov/1980/Rental-Assistance-Program-Programa-de-As or walk in to the Robinwood Community Services office at 1453 Tyler Avenue, Annapolis, MD 21403. Submit supporting documents including proof of household income, rental/lease agreement, photo ID for all adult household members, and at least one of: eviction notice, court judgment, landlord correspondence showing arrears, or unpaid/shut-off utility notice. Allow up to 3 business days to receive an approval or denial notice via email. If approved, the finance department mails the check directly to the property manager or utility company, which can take 4–6 weeks; a promissory letter is provided during processing. If denied, the city provides information on other resources and connects applicants with a social worker. For in-person assistance, call Erin Lee at 410-562-0169 to schedule an appointment. Spanish-language support is available at (443) 875-3684.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Annapolis offers low-interest loans to property owners in the downtown Historic District to help cover the cost of installing a fire sprinkler retrofit. Loans are available at 1% annual percentage rate (APR) over 5 years, with amounts up to $25,000. Priority is given to applicants proposing residential use on upper floors and/or using a certified minority contractor.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 5-year loans at 1% APR, up to $25,000 per applicant. Funds are available until the annual allocation is exhausted. Proceeds are disbursed as a check to the applicant after a contract is executed and building permits are issued. Priority is given to those proposing residential use on upper floors and/or using a certified minority contractor.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Available until the annual allocation of the fund is exhausted
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners of residential and commercial structures on Main Street and Francis Street in the Annapolis Historic District who are required to install an automatic fire sprinkler system.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of a fire sprinkler retrofit in buildings located in the Annapolis downtown Historic District.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to property owners on Main Street and Francis Street in the Annapolis Historic District with a dedicated City water line for sprinkler system connection.
requirements_list: Property must be located on Main Street or Francis Street in the Annapolis Historic District
Property must have a dedicated City water line for sprinkler system connection
Applicant must use a licensed contractor to create a sprinkler retrofit plan
Building permits must be issued before funds are disbursed
Priority given to residential use on upper floors and/or certified minority contractors
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Have a licensed contractor create a plan for your building's sprinkler retrofit. 2. Complete the online loan application at www.annapolis.gov (use keyword 'sprinkler loan'). 3. The Finance Office reviews the completed application and shares it with the Fire Marshal, who checks with the permit office and signs off, then sends to the City of Annapolis Office of Law to draw up a contract. 4. Once the contract is complete and building permits are issued, payment is disbursed as a check to the applicant.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Annapolis partners with the Arbor Day Foundation to give away free trees each fall. The program includes an online mapping tool that helps residents identify the best location to plant trees in their yard for the greatest cooling, energy, and money-saving benefits.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free trees distributed each fall through the Arbor Day Foundation partnership. Includes access to a research-based online mapping tool to identify the best planting location for cooling, energy, and financial savings.
structured_extraction.program_audience: City of Annapolis residents interested in planting trees in their yard.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planting free trees in a resident's yard to maximize cooling, energy, and money-saving benefits.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be located within the City of Annapolis.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register through the Arbor Day Foundation website starting September 15. Use the online mapping tool to identify the best planting location.

structured_extraction.program_name: Deferral of Property Tax for Elderly or Disabled Homeowners
structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Annapolis allows eligible elderly or permanently disabled homeowners to defer payment of City real property taxes for up to 50 years, with interest accruing at 4% per year on the deferred amount.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Defers payment of City real property taxes on a residential property for up to 50 years. The amount deferred may not exceed the increase in City property tax from the date the homeowner elects to defer. Interest accrues at 4% per year on the deferred amount. The total deferred amount plus interest becomes due when the homeowner no longer meets eligibility requirements, sells or transfers the property, or at the end of 50 years. A lien attaches to the property for the deferred amount and interest.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Election to defer must be made before June 1st of a taxable year to receive deferral for the succeeding taxable year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Elderly (age 65+) or permanently disabled homeowners who have lived in their Annapolis home as their principal residence for at least 5 consecutive years and meet income eligibility requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Deferral of City real property tax payments on qualifying residential property.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Property must be located in the City of Annapolis.
requirements_list: Owner or at least one owner must have resided in the dwelling as a principal residence for at least 5 consecutive years

Owner or at least one owner must be at least 65 years of age OR be permanently and totally disabled and qualified for benefits under the Social Security Act, Railroad Retirement Act, a Federal act for U.S. Armed Forces members, or a Federal retirement system
Combined gross income must not exceed $50,000 per year
Eligible property is limited to the minimum lot size required by the applicable zoning district (but not less than the dwelling and curtilage)
Election to defer must be made before June 1st of the taxable year to receive deferral for the following taxable year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Homeowner must elect to defer taxes by submitting a written agreement before June 1st of the taxable year. The agreement is recorded in the land records of Anne Arundel County. A lien attaches to the property.

structured_extraction.program_name: Electric Leaf Blower Rebate Program (City of Annapolis)
structured_extraction.program_description: This program offers rebates to Annapolis residents and lawn care or landscape businesses to help them switch from gas-powered leaf blowers to electric models. Residents can get up to $100 and businesses can get up to $1,500.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rebates up to $100 for residents and up to $1,500 for lawn care and landscape businesses to purchase electric leaf blowers to replace gas-powered models.
structured_extraction.program_audience: City of Annapolis residents and lawn care or landscape businesses operating within city limits
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of electric leaf blowers to replace gas-powered models
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only within the City of Annapolis, MD
requirements_list: Must be an Annapolis resident or lawn care/landscape business
Proof of residency required (for residents)
Proof of purchase required
Must be transitioning from gas-powered to electric leaf blower
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Fill out the online application at the Chesapeake Bay Trust website, and provide proof of residency and proof of purchase.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides temporary rental and utility assistance for eligible renters whose employment income has been impacted by the COVID-19 public health crisis. This emergency assistance is designed to prevent evictions and utility shut-offs, and is subject to funding availability.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Temporary rental and utility assistance for eligible renters who have lost employment income due to COVID-19. Subject to funding availability.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Renters in Anne Arundel County and City of Annapolis whose employment income has been impacted by COVID-19
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental and utility payments to prevent eviction and utility shut-off
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County and City of Annapolis
requirements_list: Must be a renter
Employment income must have been impacted by COVID-19 public health crisis
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the ACDS Inc. Eviction Prevention Program page at the linked URL to apply.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Annapolis awards operating and capital grants to nonprofit organizations that provide services benefiting Annapolis residents. Operating grants support day-to-day costs of running a nonprofit organization. Capital grants support property purchases, facility construction, remodeling, expansion, or equipment purchases. Grants support programs that empower youth, families, and individuals; preserve community character; contribute to a vibrant economy; or advance community revitalization, economic development, and environmental sustainability. Grant amounts are subject to availability of funds and are reviewed as part of the annual budget process.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Operating grants cover day-to-day costs of running a nonprofit organization. Capital grants support property purchase, facility construction, remodeling, expansion, or equipment purchase. Grant amounts are not specified and are determined through the annual budget process based on committee recommendations, subject to availability of funds.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations (501(c)(3)) in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation whose programs primarily benefit City of Annapolis residents, including services related to youth and family support, community character preservation, economic vitality, and community revitalization.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating costs (day-to-day expenses) or capital costs (property purchase, facility construction/remodeling/expansion, or equipment purchase).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: At least 75% of the organization's programming must benefit and engage City of Annapolis residents. Services must benefit the Annapolis community.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a nonprofit organization in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
Must hold a current IRS 501(c)(3) tax-exempt status
Must demonstrate administrative and financial capacity to carry out the project

Project must align with at least one of the four program priorities: (1) sustain and empower youth, families, and individuals; (2) preserve and enhance community character; (3) contribute to a vibrant economy; or (4) promote community revitalization, economic development, and environmental sustainability
Must demonstrate maximum public benefit in relation to cost
Must demonstrate ability to leverage additional funds outside city funding
At least 75% of programming must benefit and engage City residents
Must show diverse funding sources such as in-kind donations, fundraising, and federal grants

Must submit required documents: last audit or financial statements (or IRS Form 990), current year organizational budget, Board of Directors list with contact information, IRS determination letter, Certificate of Good Standing, most recent annual report (if applicable), MOU or support letters for partner organizations (if applicable), and summary of City support over the previous year
Non-profits receiving funding must submit quarterly reports to the Finance Department within 30 days of each quarter's close
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and submit the online FY 2027 Community Grant Application via the ArcGIS Survey123 link on the program page. Include all required supporting documents. Applications must be received by April 1, 2026 at 4:30 PM. Late applications will not be considered. A review committee — consisting of the Mayor's designated staff person, the Director of Finance's designated staff person, and two at-large staff persons — evaluates applications based on stated criteria and makes recommendations to the Finance Committee as part of the annual budget process.

structured_extraction.program_name: FY26 Annapolis Children and Families Success Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Annapolis Office of Community Services funds community-based organizations to open, expand, or enhance child care and youth development programs. Grants support structured activities for youth with adult oversight at a physical location in Annapolis, including recreation, sports, arts, science and technology, life skills, and enrichment programs that prevent adverse childhood experiences and improve access for youth from low-income families.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $10,000 per proposal. At least five organizations will be funded. The first 75% of funds are disbursed during the week of August 25th after a signed contract is returned. Grantees must submit a mid-program and final report and participate in three meetings with OCS staff.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations and businesses that provide child care, youth development, and enrichment programs for youth in Annapolis, especially those serving low-income families.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Program costs necessary for the successful implementation and evaluation of child care and youth enrichment activities for Annapolis youth. Not intended to cover general organizational operating expenses beyond what is needed for the proposed project.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Programs must be located at a physical location within the City of Annapolis and serve Annapolis youth, especially those in low-income neighborhoods.
requirements_list: Organization must have 501(c)(3) status or be a business that will use funds to provide scholarships or develop activities at no cost to participants
Programs must be provided at a physical location within Annapolis
Programs must show how they prevent adverse childhood experiences and provide access for youth from low-income Annapolis families
Grantees must submit a mid-program and final report
Grantees must participate in three meetings with OCS staff
Applications must be submitted through the online portal or, with approval, in paper or by email
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a complete application through the online portal at https://arcg.is/1H0TTj1. Applications open June 16 and close July 25 at 4:30pm. If unable to submit online, contact Iesha Young for approval to submit by paper at City Hall or via email. Grants are reviewed after the portal closes, decisions made by August 8, and award letters sent by August 13.

structured_extraction.program_description: An educational initiative that supports limited-income families in stabilizing and improving their financial well-being. Counselors provide in-depth, personalized educational counseling to help with repairing credit, setting financial goals, building a budget, and improving income.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free one-on-one personalized educational counseling sessions covering credit repair, goal setting, budgeting, and income improvement.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Limited-income families seeking to stabilize and improve their financial situation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable — this is a counseling and education program, not a funding program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available through the City of Annapolis Office of Community Services in Annapolis, Maryland, in partnership with organizations in Anne Arundel County.
requirements_list: Limited income household

structured_extraction.program_description: Food Friday provides weekly boxes of fresh produce, fruits, vegetables, frozen meat, and non-perishable foods to food-insecure individuals and families living in the City of Annapolis. Boxes can be customized for vegan or vegetarian needs. The program also connects participants with local resources and support networks to promote long-term food security.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible residents receive a weekly box filled with fresh and canned fruits and vegetables, frozen meat, rice, pasta, and other non-perishable foods at no cost. Boxes can be customized for vegan or vegetarian dietary needs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: City of Annapolis residents currently facing financial hardship and in need of food assistance.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Weekly food boxes containing fresh produce, canned fruits and vegetables, frozen meat, rice, pasta, and other non-perishable foods.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must live within the City of Annapolis.
requirements_list: Must reside in the City of Annapolis
Must currently be facing a hardship and need assistance with food
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Sign up online using the Food Friday box application form on the City of Annapolis website.

structured_extraction.program_description: Free English language classes for adults who are beginning to learn English. Classes cover listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills for everyday life and work, hosted at the Pip Moyer Recreation Center in Annapolis.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free English Basic Skills classes for adults, held Mondays and Wednesdays, 9:30 to 11:30 a.m. at the Pip Moyer Recreation Center. No cost to eligible students.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults who are beginning to study English
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: English language learning for everyday life and work
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Hosted at the Pip Moyer Recreation Center in Annapolis, MD
requirements_list: Must be an adult beginning to study English
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact esloffice@aacc.edu or call AACC at 410-777-2901 to get started.

structured_extraction.program_description: Free class to help adults without a high school diploma prepare for the GED exam. Covers all four GED subjects: math, science, social studies, and reasoning through language arts. Hosted at the Pip Moyer Recreation Center in Annapolis.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free GED preparation class for adults 18 or older without a high school diploma. Classes held Mondays and Wednesdays, 6 to 8:30 p.m. at the Pip Moyer Recreation Center.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults 18 or older who do not have a high school diploma and want to prepare for the GED exam
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: GED exam preparation covering math, science, social studies, and language arts
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Hosted at the Pip Moyer Recreation Center in Annapolis, MD
requirements_list: Must be 18 years of age or older
Must not have a high school diploma
Must attend an orientation prior to registering
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Schedule an orientation by calling 410-777-1823 or emailing gedprogram@aacc.edu before registering for the class.

structured_extraction.program_name: Front Yard and Street Tree Program
