structured_extraction.program_description: City of Annapolis offers free trees to residents and property owners to plant in the public right-of-way or front yard. City contractors plant the tree at no cost, helping grow the urban forest, improve air quality, provide shade, reduce stormwater runoff, and make streets more livable.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free tree planting by City contractors at no cost to the resident or property owner. Recipient must water and care for the tree for the first 3 years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: City of Annapolis residents and property owners with a suitable planting location in the public right-of-way or front yard.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planting a tree in the public right-of-way or front yard of a City of Annapolis property.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be located within the City of Annapolis.
requirements_list: Must be a City of Annapolis resident or property owner
Must have a suitable planting location in the public right-of-way (typically the strip between the sidewalk and the curb) or in the front yard
Must agree to water and care for the tree for the first 3 years
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the online web form at the City of Annapolis website to request a tree.

structured_extraction.program_description: A partnership between Stanton Community Center and St. Anne's Episcopal Church that helps students strengthen academic skills. Volunteers provide homework assistance and school project help. Low-performing students receive tutoring in math and reading, with access to computers, a Smart Board, and the IXL math interactive website for practice in language arts and math. The program ends with a banquet recognizing student accomplishments. Runs Monday through Thursday, 3–6 pm during the school year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free homework help, tutoring in math and reading, access to 12 computers, Smart Board, and IXL math website. Students are recognized at an end-of-year banquet.
structured_extraction.program_audience: School-age students, particularly low-performing students needing academic support in math and reading.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Homework assistance, school project help, math and reading tutoring, and access to educational technology.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at Stanton Community Center in Annapolis, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a school-age student
Program runs during the school year

structured_extraction.program_description: GreenScape is a City of Annapolis program that partners with community volunteers to plant and maintain flower and vegetable gardens in public spaces throughout the city. The City provides plant materials, mulch, trash bags, and gloves. Volunteers of all ages plant, clean up, and care for gardens year-round. Projects can include creating new garden areas, sprucing up existing ones, litter pick-up, or planting trees.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The City supplies plant materials, trees, mulch, trash bags, and gloves to participants. Volunteer landscape architects, designers, and master gardeners also provide free garden design assistance. Plant materials are available for pick-up at Truxtun Park Pool.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals, community groups, and neighborhood associations in the City of Annapolis who want to plant and maintain gardens in public spaces.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Plant materials, trees, and supplies for planting, cleaning up, and maintaining gardens in public spaces on city property.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located on public property within the City of Annapolis.
requirements_list: Project site must be on public property within the City of Annapolis
Must obtain permission from the property owner
Must complete and submit the plant material order form by March 4
Must recruit volunteers for material pick-up, site preparation, planting, and year-round watering and weeding
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Attend the organizational meeting at the 'Pip' Moyer Recreation Center (February 4 or March 4). Select a project site on public property and get owner permission. Complete and submit the plant material order form by March 4 to mdwittlinger@annapolis.gov. Pick up plant materials at Truxtun Park Pool on April 24. Planting day is April 25, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Annapolis offers a property tax credit to owners of designated landmark properties and properties within the Annapolis Historic District who spend money on preservation, restoration, or rehabilitation of structures with historic or architectural value. The program is administered by the Historic Preservation Division within the Planning & Zoning Department. Credit rates vary based on property type and scope of work, with total annual credits capped at $150,000 citywide and $50,000 per individual credit. Unused credits may be carried forward up to five years.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property tax credit applied to City real property taxes based on qualified preservation, restoration, or rehabilitation expenses. Credit rates are: 10% for residential property exterior work; 25% for income-producing property (including life/safety and hazard mitigation); 25% for residential interior improvements required for life/safety or hazard mitigation; 25% for exterior restoration replacing non-historic features with historically appropriate ones on any property. Total qualified expenses must exceed $5,000 per application. The total credits approved by the Director of Finance may not exceed $150,000 in any fiscal year, and no single credit may exceed $50,000. If the tax credit exceeds the tax bill, the balance may be carried forward up to five years.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Work must commence within 6 months of certificate of approval; documentation must be submitted within 2 years of certification.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of properties designated as City of Annapolis landmarks pursuant to Chapter 21.56 of the City of Annapolis Historic District Zoning Ordinance, as well as property owners within the Annapolis Historic District seeking tax credits for exterior improvements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Exterior preservation, restoration, and rehabilitation of landmark structures and properties in the Historic District; interior improvements required for life/safety or hazard mitigation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Property must be located within the City of Annapolis and either designated as a City landmark or located within the Annapolis Historic District.
requirements_list: Property must be designated a landmark under Chapter 21.56 of the Annapolis City Code, or be located within the Annapolis Historic District
Total eligible expenses must exceed $5,000 per application
Must obtain a Historic Preservation Commission Certificate of Approval prior to preliminary certification of the tax credit (or submit concurrently)
Qualified work must comply with the Historic Preservation Commission Design Manual and the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation
Work must involve exterior changes subject to Historic Preservation Commission review
Certified work must commence within 6 months of issuance of the associated certificate of approval
Within 2 years of certification, property owner must submit documentation including photographs and an affidavit for final certification
If landmark status is lost due to owner's actions within 5 years of receiving the credit, the full credit amount must be refunded
Submit applications for review and approval before signing a contract or starting work
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application for the historic preservation tax credit to the Historic Preservation Division (Chief of Historic Preservation) along with required documentation and affidavit. Concurrently or previously, obtain a Certificate of Approval from the Historic Preservation Commission. The Historic Preservation Commission may authorize the Chief of Historic Preservation to certify the application. After completing the work, submit final documentation to the Chief of Historic Preservation for final certification. The Director of Finance then authorizes the approved credit to be applied to the property tax bill.

structured_extraction.program_name: Home Repair – Rebuilding Together Anne Arundel County
structured_extraction.program_description: Rebuilding Together Anne Arundel County provides free home repairs for qualifying Annapolis homeowners. The program is funded with Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) dollars and can assist with most types of repair needs. Eligible homeowners may receive up to $10,000 in home repairs at no cost.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $10,000 in home repairs provided at no cost to the homeowner. Repairs are performed by contractors — no cash is disbursed directly to the homeowner.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income Annapolis homeowners who need home repairs and cannot perform the work themselves
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Most types of home repair needs
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a homeowner in Annapolis, MD
requirements_list: Must be a homeowner in Annapolis, MD
All persons on the deed must reside in the home needing repair
Combined household income must be less than 50% of Area Median Income
Must demonstrate a legitimate need for repairs
Must be unable to perform the work themselves
Must have owned the home for more than 2 years and plan to reside there for at least 2 years after repairs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Application for Home Repairs with information about all household members, proof of income, and proof of homeownership. Mail the completed application to Rebuilding Together Anne Arundel County, 819 Ritchie Hwy, Suite 2000, Severna Park, MD 21146.

structured_extraction.program_description: Helps homebuyers cover down payment and closing costs when purchasing a Moderately Priced Dwelling Unit (MPDU) in the City of Annapolis. The program provides a zero-interest loan of up to $10,000 that does not require monthly payments and is only repaid when the property is sold, transferred, or at the end of 10 years, whichever comes first.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Zero-percent interest loan of up to $10,000 to cover down payment and closing costs. No monthly payments required. Repayment is due upon sale or transfer of the property or at the end of 10 years, whichever comes first. A lien is placed on the property via a Deed of Trust. Borrower must contribute a minimum of 1% of the sales price from their own funds.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homebuyers purchasing a Moderately Priced Dwelling Unit (MPDU) in the City of Annapolis who need help with down payment and closing costs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment and closing costs associated with the purchase of an MPDU home in the City of Annapolis.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is limited to the purchase of MPDU homes within the City of Annapolis, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must hold an MPDU Certificate of Eligibility
Must be a graduate of a HUD-certified Homeownership Counseling Program
Must be prequalified by a participating lender or a lender of your choice
Must contribute a minimum of 1% of the sales price from their own funds
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: MPDU Certificate of Eligibility holders receive application information in their Home Buyer Packet when the city notifies them of MPDUs available for sale. Applicants may also call 410-263-7961 ext. 7727 for information. MPDU staff works with the applicant's lender to determine the loan amount.

structured_extraction.program_name: Moderately Priced Dwelling Units (MPDU) Sales, Rental & Developer Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Annapolis requires that 15% of homes for sale and 15% of rental units in new subdivisions of 10 or more units be priced affordably for moderate-income households. The MPDU program operates on two tracks: (1) For income-eligible households, the program makes homes available for sale or rent at below-market prices. Applicants must obtain a Certificate of Eligibility before purchasing or renting an MPDU. The City's Planning and Zoning (P&Z) office certifies eligible buyers and renters, then connects them with available units during a 180-day priority marketing period. Rental prices are set at 80–100% of HUD Fair Market Rents depending on utility arrangements; for-sale prices are set by the Department of Planning and Zoning. The city also offers up to $10,000 in settlement expense assistance (down payment and closing costs) to income-eligible MPDU buyers at 100% or below Median Household Income. Participants may also use federal, state, or local assistance such as Section 8 vouchers. (2) For developers and builders constructing new residential developments of 10 or more units in Annapolis, the program establishes mandatory affordable housing requirements. Developers must execute an Agreement to Build MPDUs and a Declaration of Covenants with P&Z, follow construction phasing rules, and submit Offering Agreements before marketing units. City staff provides guidance on pricing methodology, marketing processes, and required agreements, and certifies eligible buyers/renters and provides lists of qualified certificate holders to sales agents.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: For income-eligible households: eligible households can purchase or rent housing units priced below market rate. Eligible applicants receive a Certificate of Eligibility to purchase or rent a Moderately Priced Dwelling Unit (MPDU) at below-market rates. Rental prices are set at 80–100% of HUD Fair Market Rents depending on utility arrangements. For-sale prices are set by the Department of Planning and Zoning. The city also offers up to $10,000 in settlement expense assistance (down payment and closing costs) to income-eligible MPDU buyers at 100% or below Median Household Income. Eligible buyers must qualify for mortgage financing; eligible renters must meet standard credit and income checks. A 180-day priority marketing period gives certificate holders first access to available units. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis in person or by mail. For developers and builders: the program sets requirements to provide 15% of total units as MPDUs. Developers receive guidance from city staff on pricing methodology, marketing processes, and required agreements. The city certifies eligible buyers/renters and provides lists of qualified certificate holders to sales agents.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Income-eligible individuals and households earning at or below 100% of the Baltimore Metropolitan Statistical Area (MSA) family median income (adjusted for household size) who do not currently own a home and are city residents, City of Annapolis employees, local school staff, Naval Academy/Naval Base employees, or Anne Arundel County residents with a qualifying disability; and developers and builders constructing new residential developments of 10 or more units in the City of Annapolis.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase or rent of a moderately priced dwelling unit in an eligible Annapolis development; down payment and closing costs (up to $10,000 in settlement expense assistance) for MPDU purchase; compliance with affordable housing requirements and guidance on MPDU offering, pricing, and marketing processes for developers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be City of Annapolis residents, City of Annapolis employees (beyond probationary period), employed within city limits for at least 12 months, full-time teachers or staff in schools within city limits or the Annapolis Senior High School district, employed at the U.S. Naval Academy or Annapolis Naval Base for at least 12 months, or Anne Arundel County residents with a qualifying disability as defined by the Social Security Administration. Developer requirements apply only within the City of Annapolis, Maryland.
requirements_list: Household income at or below 100% of the Baltimore MSA family median income, adjusted for household size (e.g., $118,313 for a household of 4 as of FY 2023)
Must not currently own a home
Must have sufficient income to make mortgage or rent payments (at least $40,000/year for rental)

Must meet one of the geographic/employment residency criteria: city resident, employed within the city for at least 12 months, City of Annapolis employee beyond probationary period, teacher/staff at a school within the city or Annapolis Senior High School district, employed at the U.S. Naval Academy or Annapolis Naval Base for at least 12 months, or an Anne Arundel County resident with a qualifying disability as defined by the Social Security Administration
Hold a valid MPDU Certificate of Eligibility
Buyers must qualify for and secure mortgage financing
Buyers must complete a HUD-certified homebuyer education/homeownership counseling course before signing a sales contract
Renters must meet standard credit checks and income tests and have the resources to pay monthly rent
Must provide credit report, income documentation, tax returns, photo ID, and asset account statements with application
Evidence of current gross household income for a one-month period (pay stubs, child support, alimony, SSI/SSA or retirement statements)
Copies of last two statements from all asset accounts (checking, savings, investments, etc.)
Copies of last two federal tax returns with all schedules, including W2s for each applicant and co-applicant
Copy of a photo ID for each applicant and co-applicant
If a dependent is 18 or older, verification of work or student status
Credit report with credit score for each applicant, no more than 6 months old
For purchase with settlement assistance: must have MPDU Certificate of Eligibility, be a graduate of a HUD-certified Homeownership Counseling Program, and be pre-qualified by a lender
Must purchase or rent an MPDU-designated unit within Annapolis
Development must include 10 or more residential units in the City of Annapolis
15% of total units must be designated as MPDUs for both rental and for-sale developments
Applicant (developer) must execute an Agreement to Build MPDUs with the Department of Planning and Zoning before final record plats are recorded
Applicant (developer) must execute a Declaration of Covenants at the same time as the Agreement to Build
MPDUs must be built along with or before other dwelling units
In single-family subdivisions, each MPDU must have two or more bedrooms
In multi-family subdivisions, the ratio of efficiency and one-bedroom MPDUs must not exceed the same ratio among market-rate units
Applicant (developer) must submit an Offering Agreement to P&Z before making MPDUs available for sale or rent
For-sale Offering Agreement may be submitted no more than 365 days from expected delivery date
For rental Offering Agreement may be submitted up to 120 days before units are available for occupancy
Self-employed applicants must submit alternative income documentation in place of pay stubs
Completion of renter certification form required for rental applicants
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For households: Download and complete the MPDU application form (available online or by calling the P&Z office). Submit the completed application with all required documents in person, by mail, or electronically to the Department of Planning and Zoning, 145 Gorman Street, 3rd floor, Annapolis MD 21401. Applications without required documentation will be returned. The city processes applications on a rolling basis and mails Certificates of Eligibility within 4 weeks. Certificates are valid for one year and may be renewed. When a developer submits an Offering Agreement, P&Z mails interest forms to certificate holders. P&Z generates a ranked list of names (2 to 2.5 times the number of available units) and forwards it to the developer's sales agent. The sales agent contacts certificate holders in order to arrange a sales or rental meeting. This process repeats as needed during the 180-day priority marketing period. Buyers may also submit an MPDU Settlement Expense Assistance Request Form for closing cost help. For developers: 1. Developer submits development plans to P&Z, which sets the MPDU requirement. 2. Developer executes an Agreement to Build MPDUs and a Declaration of Covenants with P&Z. 3. When ready to market units, developer notifies P&Z and submits an Offering Agreement with required documentation. 4. P&Z mails interest forms to MPDU certificate holders and provides a list of qualified names to the sales agent. 5. Sales agent contacts certificate holders in order and arranges sales or rental meetings. 6. Required forms are submitted to P&Z at contract signing, lease ratification, and after settlement. You may also contact the Office of Community Development for information on available MPDU units.

structured_extraction.program_description: A community-focused initiative led by the Mayor's Office that works to reduce substance use and overdoses in Annapolis. The program prioritizes outreach in communities most impacted by substance use, with a focus on equity and access to resources through community events, multimedia prevention campaigns, and education on harm reduction and treatment options.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Community engagement events, multimedia prevention campaigns, and connection to harm reduction and treatment resources.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents and families in Annapolis, especially those in communities most impacted by substance use.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Outreach, prevention campaigns, and connecting individuals and families to substance use support and resources.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Annapolis, Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact NAM by email or phone to learn about upcoming events and available resources.

structured_extraction.program_description: Organizations with 501(c)(3) nonprofit status can apply for free dockage at City of Annapolis docks. When free docking is granted, the group may not collect fees, sell merchandise, or fundraise during their stay.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free dock space at City of Annapolis docks. Each vessel is permitted to book up to four reservations per year, with a maximum of 7 days per reservation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations with 501(c)(3) status that operate vessels and need dockage in Annapolis.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free dockage at City of Annapolis docks for qualifying nonprofit vessels.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is administered by the City of Annapolis Harbormaster. Dock space is located in Annapolis, MD.
requirements_list: Must have 501(c)(3) nonprofit status
Dock reservation must be requested by the captain or authorized agent of the group, not a third party
Must provide proof of insurance with the City of Annapolis named as an alternate insured
Must provide 501(c)(3) proof
Must provide a valid credit card
Must submit a signed reservation form
Each vessel is limited to four reservations per year, each up to 7 days
When docking, the group may not collect fees, sell merchandise, or fundraise
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a dock reservation request directly to the Harbormaster's office. Requests must come from the captain or an authorized agent. Provide insurance documentation (with City of Annapolis as alternate insured), 501(c)(3) proof, a valid credit card, and a signed reservation form.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Annapolis provides shared rack storage space for paddle craft at the Truxtun Park Boat Ramp. Residents and visitors can obtain a permit to store their kayak, canoe, or similar paddle craft at one of 12 available spaces, supporting safe and environmentally responsible access to City waters.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Permits grant access to one of 12 shared rack storage spaces for paddle craft at Truxtun Park Boat Ramp. City residents pay $150 and non-city residents pay $350 for a permit.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals aged 18 or older who have reached their turn on the City Paddle Craft Waiting List and wish to store a personal paddle craft at Truxtun Park Boat Ramp.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Storage of manually propelled paddle craft (8–14 ft. long, no more than 3 ft. wide, no more than 20 in. deep) at the City rack. Personal use only — no commercial activity permitted.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to City of Annapolis residents and non-residents, but fees differ. Permits are issued only to individuals on the City Paddle Craft Waiting List.
requirements_list: Must be at least 18 years old
Must have reached their turn on the City Paddle Craft Waiting List
Paddle craft must be 8–14 ft. long, no more than 3 ft. wide, and no more than 20 in. deep
Paddle craft must be manually propelled — no engines, motors, or batteries allowed
Paddle boats may not be stored on City-owned racks
Permits are for personal use only — no commercial use (rentals, lessons, programs, tours, etc.)
Permits cannot be transferred to another person, household, group, or entity
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the 2026 Paddle Craft Rack Permit Application (available as a downloadable form on the program page). Applicants must already be on the City Paddle Craft Waiting List and have reached their turn.

structured_extraction.program_name: Property Tax Credit for Fire Sprinkler System Installation
structured_extraction.program_description: A one-time City property tax credit is available to property owners in Annapolis who install an approved fire sprinkler system in an existing residential structure where a sprinkler system is legally required. The credit equals the lesser of the total City general property tax due for the year of installation or the actual cost of the sprinkler system installation, and must be applied for during the year the system is installed to receive the credit in the current or following tax year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time credit against City general property taxes in the year the fire sprinkler system is installed. The credit equals the lesser of the total property tax due for that year or the actual cost of the sprinkler system installation. Must be applied for during the year the system is installed to receive the credit in the current or following tax year.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Must apply during the year the sprinkler system is installed.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners in the City of Annapolis who install an approved fire sprinkler system in an existing residential structure where a fire sprinkler system is legally required.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Credit applied to City general property taxes in the year a required fire sprinkler system is installed, offsetting the cost of the installation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Property must be an existing residential structure located in the City of Annapolis, Anne Arundel County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must install a fire sprinkler system in a property located in the City of Annapolis
Sprinkler system must be installed on or after July 1, 2009
A fire sprinkler system must be legally required for the structure
Installed sprinkler system must comply with standards established by the State Fire Prevention Commission and applicable City and County building and fire safety codes
Taxpayer must provide documentation of the cost of installation
Application must be submitted during the year the sprinkler system is installed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and submit the Installation of Fire Sprinkler System Tax Credit Application (available on the Finance Forms page) to the Department of Finance during the year the sprinkler system is installed. Provide documentation showing the sprinkler system complies with applicable codes and standards and documentation of the installation cost. The credit is applied to the current or following year's property tax bill.

structured_extraction.program_description: A city-funded tree planting program in Annapolis focused on restoring the city's forest canopy and achieving 50% urban tree canopy by 2050. Now in its fourth year, the program funds tree planting projects at homes, congregations, businesses, and schools across the City of Annapolis. Community volunteers trained as Tree Troopers help identify planting sites and oversee planting projects. From September 2023 to December 2025, the program planted 380 trees across the city.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: City-funded program providing free trees, planting support, and volunteer training to communities in Annapolis. Includes 4 virtual training sessions and one in-person planting event. Participants learn how trees grow, which trees suit their property, and how to engage their community. Community volunteers can become trained Tree Troopers to help identify planting sites and oversee projects. Some communities qualify for free trees based on the Chesapeake Bay Foundation's Urban Tree Grant Eligibility Map.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners, congregations, businesses, schools, and residents in the City of Annapolis who want to plant trees and restore the city's forest canopy.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tree planting at residential, religious, commercial, and school properties within Annapolis to expand urban tree canopy and create a greener future.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available within the City of Annapolis only. Some communities qualify for free trees based on the Chesapeake Bay Foundation's Urban Tree Grant Eligibility Map.
requirements_list: Must complete interest form at aawsa.org/tree-trooper to apply
Must be located within the City of Annapolis
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit aawsa.org/tree-trooper and complete the interest form under 'Become a Tree Trooper'. Alternatively, visit aawsa.org/replant to fill out an interest form.

structured_extraction.program_name: Reduced Transit Fare Program for Persons With Disabilities, Seniors and Students
structured_extraction.program_description: The Annapolis Department of Transportation offers reduced transit fares for eligible riders on Annapolis Transit fixed route buses, including persons with disabilities, seniors aged 60 and over, students (K-12 and higher education including private schools, colleges, and the Naval Academy in the service area), and Medicare cardholders. Eligible riders pay one-half of the regular fare or pass price with a valid photo ID. K-12 students who live within the City of Annapolis ride free during school months. Reduced fare does not apply to curb-to-curb ADA Complementary Paratransit service.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible riders pay $1 for a one-way cash fare (half the regular $2 fare) and half price on all regular transit passes, including day, weekly, monthly, and annual passes, with a valid photo ID. K-12 students who live within the City of Annapolis ride free during school months. Reduced fare does not apply to curb-to-curb ADA Complementary Paratransit service.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Persons with disabilities, seniors age 60 and over, Medicare cardholders, and students (K-12 and higher education including private schools, colleges, and the Naval Academy) in the Annapolis Transit service area.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduced-cost public transit fares on Annapolis Transit fixed route bus service within Annapolis and its service area.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to riders on Annapolis Transit fixed route bus service within the Annapolis Transit service area.
requirements_list: Must board at a bus stop on a regularly scheduled fixed route

Persons with disabilities must show an Annapolis Transit Reduced Fare Photo ID card, an ADA Complementary Paratransit photo ID card, or a disability ID from another transit agency plus government-issued photo ID
Seniors must be age 60 or older and show a government-issued photo ID showing age 60 and over
Medicare cardholders under age 60 must show their Medicare card and a government-issued photo ID
Students must present a valid school-issued photo ID with name, address, gender, school name, and issue date
K-12 students riding free must live within the City of Annapolis
Not valid for paratransit (ADA curb-to-curb) service
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Persons with disabilities who need an Annapolis Transit Reduced Fare Photo ID card can apply using the Application for Reduced Transit Fare Identification Card for Persons with Disabilities. Those needing an ADA Paratransit Service ID can apply using the ADA Paratransit Service Application. Seniors 60 and over may obtain a no-cost Maryland Photo ID at any Maryland MVA office. Complete and submit the Application for Reduced Fare; passes and reduced fares can also be obtained at the Annapolis Department of Transportation office during regular business hours. Present valid qualifying ID when boarding.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides rehabilitation assistance to low- and moderate-income homeowners in the City of Annapolis to address major system deficiencies and correct conditions that are hazardous or may endanger the health and welfare of occupants, ensuring homes are safe, healthy, and habitable. The program is administered by the Community Development Division and funded through the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD). Various loans and grants are available for eligible homeowners.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rehabilitation assistance funded through the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) is made available to eligible low- and moderate-income homeowners through the Community Development Division to address major system deficiencies and correct conditions that are hazardous or may endanger the health and welfare of occupants, ensuring homes are safe, healthy, and habitable. Various loans and grants are available for rehabilitation of single-family homes. Specific funding amounts and terms vary by case.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low- and moderate-income homeowners in the City of Annapolis
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home repairs to address major system deficiencies and correct hazardous conditions that may endanger the health and welfare of occupants, ensuring homes are safe, healthy, and habitable.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to homeowners within the City of Annapolis, Maryland. Administered by the Community Development Division; contact the Office of Community Development or Arundel Community Development Services, Inc. at 410-222-7600 to determine eligibility.
requirements_list: Must be a low- or moderate-income homeowner in the City of Annapolis
Property must have major system deficiencies or conditions hazardous to health and welfare
Must be an eligible homeowner
Must contact Arundel Community Development Services, Inc. to determine eligibility
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Office of Community Development or Arundel Community Development Services, Inc. at 410-222-7600 to determine eligibility and obtain application details.

structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive federal grant program that encourages small businesses to engage in research and development (R&D) with the potential for commercialization.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive federal grants awarded to small businesses engaged in federal research and R&D with commercialization potential.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses engaged in federal research and development
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Federal research and research and development activities with commercialization potential
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Nationwide, including Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a domestic small business

structured_extraction.program_description: The Annapolis City Fire Department installs free smoke alarms and carbon monoxide alarms in the homes of city residents who need them or cannot afford them. The program has been running for over 15 years and aims to protect families from fire deaths.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free installation of smoke alarms and carbon monoxide alarms for city residents who need them or cannot afford to purchase their own.
structured_extraction.program_audience: City of Annapolis residents who need a smoke alarm or carbon monoxide alarm or cannot afford one.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of smoke alarms and carbon monoxide alarms in the home.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only to residents within the City of Annapolis, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a resident of the City of Annapolis
Must need a smoke or carbon monoxide alarm or be unable to afford one
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Fill out the Smoke Alarm Assessment Form on the city's website at https://www.annapolis.gov/FormCenter/Fire-Department-5/Smoke-Alarm-Assessment-51. Fire department staff will then arrange installation.

structured_extraction.program_name: Sprinkler and Electrical Cost Assistance Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A City of Annapolis financial assistance program that helps property owners and businesses offset the cost of installing sprinkler and electrical systems, likely to support code compliance or safety upgrades. The program provides financial assistance covering or offsetting installation costs, with specific amounts and terms available from the Finance Department or the Department of Planning and Zoning.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance to help cover the cost of sprinkler and electrical system installations for property owners and businesses in Annapolis. Specific amounts and terms are detailed in the program document, available from the Finance Department or the Department of Planning and Zoning.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners and businesses in the City of Annapolis seeking financial assistance for sprinkler and electrical system installation costs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Covers or offsets the costs of installing sprinkler and electrical systems.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Annapolis, Anne Arundel County, Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review the Sprinkler and Electrical Cost Assistance Program document (PDF available from the department), contact the Finance Department or Department of Planning and Zoning, and submit the program application form.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free computer lab at Stanton Community Center in Annapolis for city residents. Residents can learn computer skills, access the internet, use Microsoft Suite, and apply for jobs online. The lab also supports after-school homework, and hosts Adult Basic Skills and GED Prep classes on Saturdays in partnership with Anne Arundel Community College.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free access to 12 computers for internet use, Microsoft Suite, job applications, homework support, and GED prep classes. Adult Basic Skills and GED Prep classes are offered Saturdays from 9 am to 1 pm in partnership with Anne Arundel Community College.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Annapolis city residents, including after-school students and adults seeking basic skills or GED preparation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Computer access for job searching, learning computer skills, homework research, and GED/adult education classes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to City of Annapolis residents.
requirements_list: Must be a City of Annapolis resident
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Walk-in access to the computer lab is available free of charge. GED Prep and Adult Basic Skills classes are held Saturdays 9 am to 1 pm.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Annapolis Water Service Line Program asks residents to self-report the material of their water service line through an online survey. This helps the city verify service line materials as required by federal regulation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Residents use an online map-based survey tool to self-report the material of their water service line. The program guides users through locating their address on a map, identifying their service line material, and submitting the required information to the city.
structured_extraction.program_audience: City of Annapolis water customers/residents required to report their water service line material under federal regulation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Completion of a self-reporting survey to identify water service line materials at residential addresses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents within the City of Annapolis water service area.
requirements_list: Must have a service address within the City of Annapolis water service area
Must have a magnet, penny or key, smartphone or digital camera, and internet access to complete the material identification
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Click the survey link. 2. Read and accept the disclaimer. 3. Search for your address on the map. 4. Click the blue dot at your address to open the survey link. 5. Follow survey instructions to identify and report your service line material.

structured_extraction.program_description: A community outreach program led by the Annapolis Fire Department that provides free training and resources to help prevent overdose deaths and respond to emergencies. It offers hands-only CPR and naloxone (Narcan) training for residents, businesses, and community organizations, and includes education on the Good Samaritan Law.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free hands-only CPR training, naloxone (Narcan) training, and education on the Good Samaritan Law. Naloxone is also distributed to participants.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents, businesses, and community organizations in Annapolis seeking overdose prevention training and resources.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: CPR training, naloxone training, and Good Samaritan Law education to prepare community members to respond to overdose emergencies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Annapolis, Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the program by email or phone to schedule a training session.

structured_extraction.program_description: The AU Scholarship Fund offsets the cost of program registration fees for eligible participants in the Abilities Unlimited Adaptive and Inclusive Recreation program. Scholarships cover either 50% or 100% of program costs based on income level.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Scholarships cover 100% of program registration costs for participants whose Adjusted Gross Income (AGI) is 300% or less of the federal poverty line, or 50% of costs for participants whose AGI is between 301% and 600% of the federal poverty line. Funds are distributed as available and are not guaranteed for all programs at all times.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with disabilities or special needs participating in Abilities Unlimited Adaptive and Inclusive Recreation programs who meet income eligibility requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Offset the cost of program registration fees for Abilities Unlimited Adaptive and Inclusive Recreation programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents participating in City of Frederick Abilities Unlimited programs.
requirements_list: Must have a RecTrac account (create at www.playfrederick.com)
Must complete the Participant Questionnaire including accommodation information
Must provide AGI information showing income at or below the applicable federal poverty line threshold (300% for 100% scholarship; 301%-600% for 50% scholarship)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Create a RecTrac account at www.playfrederick.com by clicking 'register for programs' and creating a new account. Then complete the Participant Questionnaire and provide AGI documentation to demonstrate eligibility.

structured_extraction.program_description: A rotating exhibition series hosted by the City of Frederick showcasing artwork from local artists through collaborations with nonprofits, arts organizations, schools, libraries, and community groups. Exhibitions are free and open to the public and run for one to three months. The program emphasizes inclusivity, highlighting historically underrepresented communities. Only group proposals are accepted — no solo artist exhibitions. The 2026 theme focuses on Frederick's shared future in celebration of the U.S. 250th anniversary, with priority given to proposals highlighting historically underserved and underrecognized communities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Selected groups receive exhibition space in Frederick City Hall for one to three months. Exhibitions are free and open to the public. The program also provides promotional support, including use of submitted images for marketing.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Proposals Due on a Rolling Basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofits, arts organizations, schools, libraries, and community groups in Frederick, MD that want to showcase group artwork exhibitions at City Hall.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Exhibition space in Frederick City Hall to display group artwork for one to three months.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Open to organizations and groups based in or serving the City of Frederick, Maryland.
requirements_list: Proposals must be submitted by an organization, group, school, library, or other entity — not an individual artist.
Solo artist exhibition proposals are not accepted.
Must be a local artist or organization based in or serving Frederick.
Proposal must include an exhibition title, idea, types of work to be displayed, and rationale (500 words or less).
Must attach a checklist of artwork including artist name, images, medium, size, and other relevant information.
Must attach at least three high-resolution .jpg images of artwork representing the exhibition for promotional use.
Proposals must be submitted via the RFP process.

2026 theme: proposals should focus on Frederick's shared future in celebration of the U.S. 250th anniversary; priority given to proposals highlighting historically underserved and underrecognized communities.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a proposal using the online application form at the bottom of the program page or via the RFP (PDF). Include organizational information, an exhibition proposal narrative (500 words or less), a checklist of artwork, and at least three high-resolution images. Proposals are reviewed on a rolling basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: City of Frederick residents can purchase compost bins at a subsidized price throughout the year. Bins are approximately 3 feet wide and 3 feet tall with a screw-top lid and a slider door at the bottom to extract finished compost. Staff delivers the bin after payment is received.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Residents can purchase compost bins through the city's online store and have them delivered. The program is available year-round.
structured_extraction.program_audience: City of Frederick residents who want to compost yard waste or kitchen scraps at home.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of a backyard compost bin for composting yard waste or kitchen scraps.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a City of Frederick resident. Address can be verified through the City's GIS tool.
requirements_list: Must be a City of Frederick resident
Must verify address using the City's GIS tool before purchasing
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Verify your address in the City's GIS tool, then purchase a bin through the City's online store. Staff will deliver the bin after payment is received.

structured_extraction.program_name: City of Frederick Historic Preservation Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit program for owners of historic properties in the City of Frederick who make qualifying rehabilitation or preservation improvements. Property owners can apply to receive a reduction in their city property taxes based on eligible work done to historic buildings within the City's historic districts. Applicants apply online through the City's OpenGov portal, submitting required documents such as plans, photographs, and scope of work.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A city property tax credit applied to eligible historic properties in the City of Frederick. Credit is based on qualifying rehabilitation or preservation improvements to historic buildings. Details on credit amounts and terms are provided in the City Historic Preservation Property Tax Credit Guide. Application is submitted online through the OpenGov portal with supporting documents such as plans, photographs, and scope of work.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of historic properties in the City of Frederick seeking a property tax credit for qualifying preservation or rehabilitation work, including individuals, for-profit entities, and non-profits.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax reduction for qualifying rehabilitation or preservation work on historic properties within the City of Frederick's historic districts.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only to properties located within the City of Frederick, Maryland historic districts.
requirements_list: Property must be a historic property located in the City of Frederick
Property must be designated as historic or located in a historic district
Eligible improvements must meet historic preservation standards
Applicant must submit a Historic Preservation Tax Credit Application through the Planning Department's online portal (OpenGov)
Must submit complete application with required documents including plans, photographs, and scope of work
May need to post a public notice sign for 7 days if required
May need to attend a hearing if required
Must obtain a Certificate of Approval before applying for building/zoning permits
Agent authorization form required if applying through an agent
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review design guidelines and contact a historic preservation planner. Create an account through the City's OpenGov portal and submit a complete Historic Preservation Tax Credit Application online with required supporting documents. If applying through an agent, complete an Agent Authorization Form. Post a public notice sign if required. Attend a hearing if required. Obtain a Certificate of Approval and apply for building/zoning permits. Contact the Planning Department at hpcdigital@cityoffrederickmd.gov or 301-600-1499 with questions.

structured_extraction.program_name: City of Frederick Housing Council – Housing Counseling (Landlord/Tenant Rental Counseling)
structured_extraction.program_description: A free housing counseling service provided by the City of Frederick that helps landlords and tenants understand their rights and responsibilities under Maryland law. Counselors can review leases, explain security deposit requirements, walk through rent court procedures, and clarify the eviction process. No legal advice is provided, but referrals to legal professionals are made when appropriate. No income limits apply.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free one-on-one housing counseling for landlords and tenants including lease review, explanation of security deposit requirements, rent court procedure guidance, and eviction process clarification. Counselors do not provide legal advice but will refer clients to legal professionals when appropriate. No cost and no income limits apply.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landlords and tenants in Frederick County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Information and guidance on tenant/landlord rights, lease review, security deposit requirements, rent court procedures, and eviction process. This is a counseling and advisory service, not a funding program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to landlords and tenants in Frederick County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a landlord or tenant in Frederick County
No income limits apply
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Housing Counseling Office for assistance or visit the Housing Counseling page for more information on how to access services.

structured_extraction.program_name: City of Frederick Senior Tax Credit Supplement
structured_extraction.program_description: A local property tax credit supplement for eligible senior homeowners in the City of Frederick. Administered by the State of Maryland as part of the State Homeowners' Property Tax Credit Program, the supplement provides additional tax relief to qualifying seniors on top of the state credit.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A supplemental property tax credit applied on top of the Maryland State Homeowners' Property Tax Credit. The credit amount is determined by the State when processing the applicant's state credit application. No separate application is needed for the city supplement — if the taxpayer qualifies, the State processes both credits together.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Senior homeowners aged 70 or older living in the City of Frederick with a combined gross income of $40,000 or less who qualify for the Maryland State Homeowners' Property Tax Credit.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of property tax liability on the applicant's primary residence.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only to homeowners whose principal residence is within the City of Frederick, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be qualified for the Maryland State Homeowners' Property Tax Credit
Must be at least 70 years old as of the end of the calendar year preceding the taxable year for which the credit is sought
Must have a combined gross household income of $40,000 or less
Must own or have a legal interest in the property
The property must be the applicant's principal residence for at least six months of the year, including July 1 (exceptions for recent purchasers or health/care needs)
Net worth (excluding the value of the credited property and qualified retirement savings/IRAs) must be less than $200,000
Combined gross household income cannot exceed $60,000 (State requirement)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: File for the Maryland State Homeowners' Property Tax Credit with the State. The State will automatically determine eligibility for the City supplement and, if eligible, process both the state and city credits together.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) Annual Action Plan
structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Frederick uses federal Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) funds to support community development activities. Each year, the city prepares an Annual Action Plan describing how CDBG funds will be used to benefit low- and moderate-income residents. The plan is open for public comment before final approval by the City Council.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal CDBG funds are allocated annually through the City of Frederick's Annual Action Plan to support eligible community development activities benefiting low- and moderate-income residents. Specific funding amounts and project activities are detailed in the Draft PY 2026 Annual Action Plan.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: 5 p.m. on Friday, May 15, 2026 (written comments deadline)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low- and moderate-income residents and organizations serving them in the City of Frederick
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Community development activities benefiting low- and moderate-income residents as described in the Annual Action Plan
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Frederick, Maryland
requirements_list: Projects and activities must benefit low- and moderate-income residents
Must align with eligible CDBG activity categories
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The Draft PY 2026 Annual Action Plan is on public display from April 16 to May 15, 2026. Written comments can be submitted by mail or email to the CDBG Program Manager. The City Council receives public comment at a work group session on April 28, 2026, with final plan approval scheduled for May 7, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Frederick Parks and Recreation Department offers seasonal community garden plots at Willow Brook Park for city residents. Residents can apply to use a plot to grow fruits and vegetables for personal use from March to November each year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Seasonal garden plots approximately 25 feet by 50 feet each are available for $60 per plot per season (March through November). A maximum of two plots per City household is allowed. Plots are non-transferable and must be renewed each season.
structured_extraction.program_audience: City of Frederick residents who want to grow fruits and vegetables for personal use
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Seasonal use of a garden plot to grow fruits and/or vegetables for personal use only; not for commercial sales
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a City of Frederick resident. Plots are located at Willow Brook Park, 350 McClellan Drive, Frederick, MD.
requirements_list: Must be a City of Frederick resident
Maximum of two plots per City household
Plots are for growing fruits and/or vegetables for personal use only — not for commercial sales
Plot holder is responsible for weekly maintenance, weeding, and watering of their plot and adjacent walkways
No invasive plants permitted
No littering or dumping of garbage
No unauthorized expansion of plot into surrounding paths or other plots
Plots are subject to inspection by City staff at any time
No gardening equipment provided by the City
No vehicles may be driven over the bridge at Willow Brook Park
Park all vehicles in designated parking areas only
No alcohol allowed in any City park
Abide by park hours of dawn to 10 p.m.
No open burning allowed
Applicant must keep current contact information on file with the Parks Department
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply and pay for a plot online via Visa or MasterCard following the sign-up instructions on the City's website. Each year, plots are offered for renewals first; then any available plots are opened to new plot holders. Sign up for Garden Plot notifications on the City's website for updates.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program administered by the City of Frederick that provides funding to nonprofit charitable and civic organizations to supplement existing funds that create or enhance services benefiting City of Frederick residents. Applicants can submit applications online through the Foundant portal. The city may award full or partial grant amounts, with individual awards ranging from approximately $2,000 to $28,000 in recent cycles. Funds are distributed after July 1 each year, following completion of a letter of agreement between the City and the recipient organization. A scorecard is used to evaluate applications. Separate applications are recommended for each specific type of promotion activity. FY2026 total grants distributed: $365,250.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants awarded annually to supplement nonprofit funding. Individual awards have ranged from approximately $2,000 to $28,000 in recent cycles. Partial funding may be awarded in lieu of a full award. FY2026 total grants distributed: $365,250. Funds are distributed after July 1 of the grant year, following completion of a letter of agreement between the City and the recipient organization. Separate applications are recommended for each specific type of community promotion activity.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit charitable and civic organizations serving City of Frederick residents
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Creating or enhancing services that positively impact City of Frederick residents, including community promotion activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must serve residents of the City of Frederick, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a nonprofit charitable or civic organization
Must attend one of two required virtual information sessions
All previous grant reporting must be up to date before applying
Must complete the online application via Foundant
Separate applications are recommended for each specific type of community promotion activity
A letter of agreement between the City and the organization must be completed before funds are distributed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Review the Program Overview PDF. 2. Ensure all prior grant reporting is current. 3. Attend one of two required virtual information sessions (December 15, 2025 or January 15, 2026). 4. Complete the online application through the Foundant portal. A scorecard used for evaluation is available for review. Funds are distributed after a letter of agreement between the City and the organization is completed.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Frederick excuses up to two expired parking session tickets per person per year, provided the person visits the Court Street Parking Garage Office within 30 minutes of receiving the ticket.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to two expired parking tickets per person per year can be excused at no cost if the person reports to the Court Street Parking Garage Office within 30 minutes of receiving the ticket.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Within 30 minutes of receiving a ticket
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals who receive an expired parking session ticket in Frederick, MD.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Excusing an expired parking ticket fine.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Frederick, MD
requirements_list: Must have received an expired parking session ticket
Must arrive at the Court Street Parking Garage Office within 30 minutes of obtaining the ticket
Limited to two excused tickets per person per year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Go to the Court Street Parking Garage Office within 30 minutes of receiving an expired parking session ticket to have the ticket excused.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free service that supports homeowners facing foreclosure by helping them navigate the mediation process, gather required documents, and apply for mortgage assistance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free counseling that includes help filing the Request for Mediation form, preparing documents for mediation, attending mediation with the client, and assisting with mortgage assistance applications. Services are delivered via a mortgage default intake and foreclosure prevention counseling process.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners facing mortgage default or foreclosure in the City of Frederick, MD
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Counseling to prevent foreclosure; support through foreclosure mediation and mortgage assistance application process
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Frederick, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a homeowner in default seeking assistance with the mediation process
Residents of Frederick, Maryland
Applicants must be experiencing mortgage default or facing foreclosure
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Mortgage Default/Client Intake Packet and contact the Housing Counseling Office with questions.

structured_extraction.program_name: Frederick's Festival of the Arts – Call for Artists
structured_extraction.program_description: Every June, the Frederick Arts Council hosts Frederick's Festival of the Arts along Carroll Creek. Artists selected by an independent jury can share and sell their work at this annual outdoor festival. All artists are encouraged to apply.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Selected artists are given the opportunity to exhibit and sell their work at the annual Frederick's Festival of the Arts along Carroll Creek on June 13–14, 2026.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: June 1, 2026 & annually on a rolling basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Artists seeking to exhibit and sell their work at an annual outdoor arts festival in Frederick
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Exhibition and sale of artwork at the festival
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Open to all artists; festival held in Frederick, Maryland
requirements_list: Artists must apply via ZAPplication
Selection is made by an independent jury
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through ZAPplication at the link provided. Deadline is June 1, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program launched by the Office of Opportunity and Transformation to support City of Frederick apprentices, fellows, and interns through social events and professional development workshops, building skills and networks as a pipeline for public service careers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Social events and personal and professional development workshops for City apprentices, fellows, and interns to build skills, networks, and readiness for public service.
structured_extraction.program_audience: City of Frederick apprentices, fellows, and interns.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Frederick, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a City of Frederick apprentice, fellow, or intern

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Frederick offers free curbside food scrap composting pickup to households that receive City trash collection. Residents sign up through Compost Crew, which collects food waste and turns it into compost. The program aims to reduce landfill waste, cut greenhouse gas emissions, and support a more sustainable city.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free curbside composting pickup service provided at no cost to eligible residents. The City funds the service through Compost Crew. Participants receive compostable liners annually. Apartment residents can also request a free 5-gallon bucket with lid and liners for drop-off composting at the community site.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Funded through end of June 2026; rolling sign-ups accepted as long as funding is available
structured_extraction.program_audience: City of Frederick residents whose trash is collected by the City
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free curbside pickup of food scraps and organic waste for composting
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to households with City of Frederick trash collection service. Apartment residents without curbside service can use the community drop-off site at Willowtree Plaza (5 Willowdale Dr, Frederick, MD 21702).
requirements_list: Must be a City of Frederick resident whose trash is hauled by the City
Sign up through Compost Crew at the program link
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Sign up online at the Compost Crew registration link (https://bit.ly/4eFT85N). For questions about sign-up or service, contact Compost Crew at (301) 202-4450 or info@compostcrew.com. For general program questions, email sustainability@cityoffrederickmd.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Health Care for the Homeless program provides primary health care, case management, and supportive services to people experiencing homelessness. It serves about 1,200 people each year through a clinic staffed by nurse practitioners, physician assistants, physicians, medical assistants, and case managers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Primary health care, case management, and supportive services provided at no cost to people experiencing homelessness, serving approximately 1,200 people annually.
structured_extraction.program_audience: People experiencing homelessness in Frederick City.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Primary health care visits, case management, and supportive services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Frederick, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be experiencing homelessness
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Health Center or complete a client intake form to access services.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Frederick offers free parking on streets and in garages during the holiday season, from Thanksgiving Day through New Year's Day on weekends.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free weekend parking on streets and in all city garages from 8 a.m. Saturday to 6 a.m. Monday, starting Thanksgiving Day through New Year's Day.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Visitors and residents parking in downtown Frederick during the holiday season.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free parking on streets and in garages during the holiday season.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Downtown Frederick, MD
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: No application required. Free parking is automatically available on eligible weekends.

structured_extraction.program_description: A workshop that teaches first-time homebuyers about the home-buying process. Participants who complete both sessions and an individual credit and budgeting consultation earn a certificate required for most down-payment assistance programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free monthly workshops held on Tuesday and Thursday. Participants must attend both sessions plus an individual credit and budgeting consultation to earn a completion certificate. Class size is limited to 40 participants.
structured_extraction.program_audience: First-time homebuyers across all of Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Homebuyer education and counseling; certificate earned can be used toward down-payment assistance programs
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All of Maryland
requirements_list: Must attend both Tuesday and Thursday sessions
Must complete an individual credit and budgeting consultation
Must submit a completed budget worksheet at individual consultation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the online application at https://frederickmd.gov/homebuyers. Contact the Housing Counseling Office with questions.

structured_extraction.program_description: A one-time reduction to water and sewer charges for residential customers who received an unusually high bill due to an interior or exterior leak. After the leak is repaired and normal usage confirmed, the bill is adjusted back to normal levels.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A one-time reduction (credit) applied to an excessive water and sewer bill. The bill is adjusted from the first service day of the high-usage billing period to the first normal reading. The customer continues paying based on the average of the last three billing cycles while the adjustment is processed.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential water and sewer customers of the City of Frederick who received an unusually high bill caused by an interior or exterior leak. Not available to apartments, condominiums, or multi-family structures served by one meter.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of an excessive water and sewer bill resulting from a leak.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only to residential customers within the City of Frederick, MD.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a residential customer (not an apartment, condominium, or multi-family structure served by one meter).
The water and sewer bill must reflect at least 2 times normal usage based on the average of the last three billing cycles.
The leak must be repaired and/or the property inspected by the Water Department.
The Water Department must perform two readings confirming usage has returned to normal.
The program may only be used once (one-time benefit).
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Utility Billing at 301-600-1421 to report the high bill. The Water and Sewer Finance Team will instruct the resident to repair the leak and/or coordinate a property inspection. Once the leak is fixed, the Water Department performs two readings to confirm normal usage. After confirmation, the bill is adjusted.

structured_extraction.program_name: Minority and Women-Owned Business Enterprise (MWBE) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Encourages minority-owned and women-owned businesses to participate in City of Frederick contracts through annual participation goals and subcontracting requirements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The City sets annual goals and subcontracting requirements to increase participation by minority- and women-owned businesses in City contracts. Eligible businesses must be at least 51% owned and controlled by socially and economically disadvantaged individuals, including minorities and women. Certification is obtained through the Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT) or an approved certifying agency.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Minority-owned and women-owned businesses seeking to participate in City of Frederick procurement contracts.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Access to City procurement contracts and subcontracting opportunities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to businesses seeking City of Frederick contracts.
requirements_list: Business must be at least 51% owned and controlled by socially and economically disadvantaged individuals, including minorities and women
Must obtain certification through MDOT or an approved certifying agency
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Obtain MWBE certification through MDOT or an approved certifying agency. Attend free MDOT workshops for guidance. Register as a vendor and search the City Supplier Portal for contract opportunities. Email businessdiversity@cityoffrederickmd.gov or call 301-600-1804 for help.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free counseling service that helps homeowners who are behind on their mortgage payments understand their options and protect their credit standing and home investment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free individual counseling sessions for homeowners delinquent on mortgage payments. Housing Counselors help determine the best course of action based on the homeowner's situation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners who are delinquent on their mortgage payments
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Guidance on options for resolving mortgage delinquency and protecting credit
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Frederick, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a homeowner currently delinquent on mortgage payments
Completion of Mortgage Default/Client Intake Packet required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Mortgage Default/Client Intake Packet and contact the Housing Counseling Office with questions.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Frederick allocates funds to Neighborhood Advisory Councils (NACs) for community projects such as park beautification, food drives, and donations to neighborhood projects. Any funds not committed or used by the end of April are returned to the general NAC fund for reallocation to other NACs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The City of Frederick allocates funds to NACs for neighborhood improvement projects. Funds not committed or used by the end of April are returned to the general NAC fund. All funds must be used in compliance with city procurement policies. Funding is not guaranteed and may be terminated by the city.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Neighborhood Advisory Councils (NACs) in the City of Frederick
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Park beautification, food drives, and donations to neighborhood projects
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to NACs within the City of Frederick, MD
requirements_list: Funds must be utilized in compliance with city procurement policies
Unused funds at the end of April are returned to the general NAC fund
Funding is not guaranteed and may be terminated by the city
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a funding request using the online form at the provided link.

structured_extraction.program_description: Next Steps is a drop-in reengagement and support program for youth and young adults ages 14–24 who feel stuck, disconnected, or unsure about their next steps in education, career, or life planning. Held at the C. Burr Artz Library in Frederick, MD, the program offers one-on-one support, career exploration, resume help, GED and graduation planning, and connections to jobs, training, and mentors — with no registration or paperwork required.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free drop-in support sessions held Tuesdays and Thursdays from 1:30pm to 4:30pm at the STEM Lab at C. Burr Artz Library. Participants receive individualized guidance on education re-enrollment, GED and graduation planning, career exploration, resume writing, job readiness skills, and referrals to jobs, training programs, and mentors.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Youth and young adults ages 14–24 who may be feeling stuck, disconnected, or uncertain about their next steps in education, career, or life.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable — this is a training and technical assistance program, not a funding program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is hosted at the STEM Lab at C. Burr Artz Library in Frederick, MD.
requirements_list: Ages 14–24
No registration or paperwork required
Drop-in format — no prior sign-up needed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: No sign-up required. Simply show up to the STEM Lab at C. Burr Artz Library on Tuesdays or Thursdays between 1:30pm and 4:30pm starting January 6, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: Downtown Frederick businesses can buy coupons to offer their customers free or reduced-cost parking in city garages.
