structured_extraction.assistance_description: Businesses purchase Park and Shop coupons that customers can use for hourly parking at any of the 5 city garages.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Downtown Frederick businesses that want to offer free or reduced parking to their customers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Providing free or reduced-cost garage parking to business customers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Downtown Frederick, MD
requirements_list: Business must be located in downtown Frederick
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Businesses purchase coupons to provide to their customers for use at any of the 5 city garages.

structured_extraction.program_description: Reimbursable grants to support the LGBTQ+ community in Frederick during Pride Month. Funding is available to community organizations and civic groups organizing LGBTQ+ pride events in June 2026.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursable grants distributed after July 1, 2026. Partial funding may be awarded in lieu of a full award. All awards are subject to availability and approval of FY27 funding.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community organizations and civic groups organizing LGBTQ+ pride events in the City of Frederick in June 2026.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Organizing and hosting LGBTQ+ pride events in June 2026 that promote visibility, inclusivity, and support for the LGBTQ+ community in the City of Frederick.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Events must be held in the City of Frederick.
requirements_list: Host an event in June 2026 that promotes visibility, inclusivity, and support for the LGBTQ+ community in the City of Frederick.
Submit an event budget and project budget.
Submit a Final Report by December 31, 2026.
Applications must be submitted through the online portal.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply via the online portal at grantinterface.com. Applications close May 1, 2026. Requests received via email, phone, or direct mail will not be reviewed.

structured_extraction.program_description: Prime Fitness provides free fitness center memberships to individuals through their employer or health plan partners. Qualifying members receive free access to the Talley Fitness Center.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free membership to the Talley Fitness Center, including fitness classes and open gyms, provided through employer or health plan partners.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals whose employer or health plan partners with Prime Fitness
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free access to fitness center, fitness classes, and open gyms
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at the Talley Fitness Center in Frederick, MD
requirements_list: Must be eligible through an employer or health plan that partners with Prime Fitness
Must obtain a Prime Health ID number
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Check eligibility at the Prime Fitness website (primemember.com). Then visit the Talley Fitness Center in person or email registrationdesk@cityoffrederickmd.gov with your Prime Health ID number to activate your free membership.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Frederick Parks and Recreation Department offers 50% off all youth recreation programs for eligible youth under age 18 who meet income or housing criteria.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible youth under age 18 receive 50% off all youth recreation programs offered by the City of Frederick Parks and Recreation Department.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Youth under age 18 who are City of Frederick residents and meet income or housing eligibility criteria.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Discount applied to registration fees for youth recreation programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a resident of the City of Frederick, Maryland.
requirements_list: Youth must be under age 18
Must be a City of Frederick resident (proof required: driver's license, MVA-issued ID, water bill, or electric bill)

Must meet one of the following: (A) eligible for free or reduced-price lunch through Frederick County Public Schools with a letter from FCPS; (B) live in a household receiving Food Supplement Program (FSP) or Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) benefits with an orange Independence Card from Frederick County Department of Social Services; or (C) reside in Carver, Lincoln, or Lucas Village public housing communities owned by the Housing Authority of the City of Frederick
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the Wm. Talley Recreation Center Registration Desk at 121 North Bentz Street, Monday through Friday 8:30 am to 6:30 pm, and provide proof of eligibility. Once approved, households may register at any time online, in person, or by phone. The RRP fee reduction will apply automatically.

structured_extraction.program_description: A coordinated network of services and partners that supports people returning to the community — for example, after incarceration — by connecting them to employment, education, housing, health, and community resources.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Coordination of services and partner organizations to support successful reentry through employment, education, housing, health, and community connections.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents returning to the community and workforce, including those returning from incarceration.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Frederick, Maryland

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides parking permits to residents living on designated streets in downtown Frederick so they can park on permitted streets without being subject to the standard 2-hour parking limit.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Residential parking permits are sold at $50 for the first permit and $100 for the second permit per household. Permits are valid January 1 through December 31 and allow parking on all designated residential permit streets for up to 48 continuous hours, exempt from the standard 2-hour parking limit.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Valid for calendar year January 1 – December 31
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents living on designated streets in downtown Frederick, MD who need on-street parking permits.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of a residential parking permit allowing on-street parking on designated streets.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only to residents living on specific streets in Frederick, MD as listed in the permit program.
requirements_list: Must live on an eligible designated street in the City of Frederick
Must provide proof of residency: driver's license plus vehicle registration with matching address
Renters must also provide a copy of their lease
Homeowners must also provide a property tax bill, mortgage statement, or water bill
Must apply in person at the Parking Office at 2 South Court Street, Frederick, MD 21701
Permits are subject to street sweeping, trash night, and special event restrictions
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply in person at the Parking Office, 2 South Court Street, Frederick, MD 21701. Bring required proof of residency documents. An application form is also available at https://www.cityoffrederickmd.gov/DocumentCenter/View/1109/Resident-Parking-Permit-Application. Visitor hang-tag permits for guests may also be picked up in advance by providing the parking address, license plate number, make and model, and length of stay.

structured_extraction.program_description: A paid returnship program for experienced professionals returning to the workforce. Offers paid pathways back to work along with mentorship, training, and structured support.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Paid work pathways with mentorship, training, and structured support for experienced professionals returning to employment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Experienced professionals returning to the workforce after a career break.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Frederick, Maryland

structured_extraction.program_description: A HUD-required counseling service for senior homeowners (age 62+) exploring whether a Home Equity Conversion Mortgage (HECM), also known as a reverse mortgage, is right for them. Counselors explain how reverse mortgages work and explore alternatives.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Individual appointment-based HUD-required HECM counseling. Cost is $100 (fee may be waived based on income). Counselors explain reverse mortgage terms, explore other options, and answer questions.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners age 62 or older in the City of Frederick interested in reverse mortgages
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Counseling to evaluate reverse mortgage options and understand HECM terms
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Frederick, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a homeowner
Typically age 62 or older
Must complete HECM intake packet prior to counseling
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the HECM/Client Intake Packet and contact the Housing Counseling Office to schedule an individual appointment.

structured_extraction.program_name: SECURE Initiative (Supporting Emergency Capacity, Urgency, Resiliency, and Equity)
structured_extraction.program_description: An emergency relief grant program launched by the City of Frederick to provide one-time, flexible bridge funding to local nonprofits that deliver critical services to vulnerable residents and have experienced disruptions in state or federal funding.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time, flexible bridge grants of up to $50,000 per award. Total program funding is $700,000. Grants are non-renewable. Funds can be used flexibly to support continuity of critical services.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local nonprofit organizations in Frederick County that serve City of Frederick residents and have experienced state or federal funding disruptions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Bridge funding to maintain continuity of programs and essential services affected by loss or reduction of state or federal grants.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must operate in Frederick County and provide services to City of Frederick residents.
requirements_list: Must be a nonprofit in good standing, including 501(c)(3), other nonprofit classifications, or fiscally sponsored projects
Must operate in Frederick County and serve City of Frederick residents
Must deliver programs that support community needs or essential services
Must have experienced a loss in state or federally funded grants and/or subgrants that disrupted program timelines or operations
Must have lost a previously reliable funding source due to non-renewal, reduced awards, or policy changes
Must demonstrate increased demand for services compared to the same time last year due to specific federal cuts in a similar or adjacent service area
Priority given to applicants with documented loss of state or federally funded grants disrupting operations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Log in or create an account on the City's online application portal at grantinterface.com. Ensure all reporting is up to date if prior City funding was received. Beginning October 15, 2025, eligible organizations can apply through the portal on a rolling basis until March 31, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: SilverSneakers is a fitness program for adults 65 and older who are eligible for Medicare. Qualifying members receive a free membership to the Talley Fitness Center at no additional cost to their health plan.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free membership to the Talley Fitness Center, including fitness classes and open gyms, at no additional cost to the member's health plan.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults 65 and older who are eligible for Medicare
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free access to fitness center, fitness classes, and open gyms
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at the Talley Fitness Center in Frederick, MD
requirements_list: Must be 65 or older
Must be eligible for Medicare
Must register and obtain a Silver Sneakers ID number
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Check eligibility at the Silver Sneakers website. Then visit the Talley Fitness Center in person or email registrationdesk@cityoffrederickmd.gov with your Silver Sneakers ID number to activate your free membership.

structured_extraction.program_name: Small Business Reserve (SBR) Program (City of Frederick)
structured_extraction.program_description: Reserves City contracts over $10,000 for certified Small Business Enterprises (SBEs), ensuring small businesses have dedicated opportunities in City procurement.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Contracts over $10,000 are reserved exclusively for certified Small Business Enterprises. SBEs must perform at least 50% of the contracted work. Businesses can qualify by providing proof of SBA certification or self-certifying with the City.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses meeting U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) size standards that want to participate in City of Frederick procurement contracts.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Access to reserved City procurement contracts over $10,000.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to businesses seeking City of Frederick contracts.
requirements_list: Must meet U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) size standards
Must perform at least 50% of the contracted work
Must provide proof of SBA certification or self-certify with the City
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Provide proof of SBA certification or self-certify with the City. Register as a vendor and search the City Supplier Portal for opportunities.

structured_extraction.program_description: A down payment and closing cost assistance program for people who want to purchase a home in the City of Frederick. Borrowers can get up to $25,000 interest-free, with no payments required until the home is sold, refinanced, or is no longer their primary residence.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Interest-free loans of up to $25,000 for down payment and closing costs. No repayment is required until the property is sold, refinanced, or is no longer the borrower's primary residence. Funded through HUD's Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents interested in purchasing a home in the City of Frederick
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment and closing cost assistance for home purchase in the City of Frederick
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Frederick, Maryland
requirements_list: Property must be located in the City of Frederick
Property must be used as the borrower's primary residence
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Housing Counseling Office for details on how to apply.

structured_extraction.program_name: Tax Credit for High Performance Buildings
structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit available to property owners in Frederick who construct or renovate buildings to high-performance energy efficiency standards.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax credit for buildings that meet high-performance standards. Application form available as a PDF.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners and building developers in the City of Frederick constructing or renovating high-performance buildings
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credit applied to high-performance building construction or renovation
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Frederick, MD
requirements_list: Buildings must meet high performance standards
Building location must be within City of Frederick
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and submit the Tax Credit for High Performance Buildings application form (PDF).

structured_extraction.program_description: Tree Frederick is a cost-share program that helps City of Frederick residents plant trees on their residential property. The city covers half the cost of containerized trees, encouraging residents to increase tree canopy, improve air and water quality, and reduce home energy costs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The city provides a 50/50 cost share on containerized trees. Residents pay only half the price of their selected trees, with the discount already applied at checkout. Each resident may purchase up to 5 trees per year in a single transaction.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Open from February 1st until all trees sell out
structured_extraction.program_audience: City of Frederick residents who want to plant trees on their residential property, including renters with landlord permission.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of containerized trees for planting in the resident's front or back yard.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to City of Frederick residents only. Participants must live within city limits.
requirements_list: Must be a City of Frederick resident
Renters must have landlord permission
Maximum of 5 trees per resident per year
All trees must be ordered and purchased together in one transaction
Trees must be planted in the resident's front or back yard
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Visit the Tree Frederick online store and enter your address to verify eligibility. 2. Select your trees (up to 5). 3. Pay for your trees at the discounted price reflecting the city's cost share. 4. Pick up your trees at the scheduled pickup event at Harry Grove Stadium.

structured_extraction.program_name: Weatherization Assistance Program – Whole Home Energy Efficiency
structured_extraction.program_description: Free home energy efficiency upgrades for low- to moderate-income homeowners and renters in Frederick, Carroll, and Washington Counties. A qualified professional audits the home and completes improvements such as air sealing, insulation, lighting upgrades, appliance replacements, and ventilation upgrades to reduce energy bills.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free grant-funded home weatherization services including air sealing, insulation, heating and cooling system upgrades, LED lighting, appliance replacement, and ventilation improvements. No cost to eligible homeowners or renters. Average savings of $372 or more per year on energy bills.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low- to moderate-income homeowners and renters in Frederick, Carroll, and Washington Counties
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Air sealing, insulation (attic, wall, ductwork), heating and cooling system upgrades, LED lighting installation, appliance replacement, mechanical ventilation, thermostat installation, and health and safety improvements
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Frederick, Carroll, and Washington Counties in Maryland
requirements_list: Must meet income limits based on household size (e.g., $68,500 for a 1-person household, up to $129,100 for an 8-person household)
Renters must have landlord sign a building owner agreement
Landlord-owned apartment buildings must have 4 or fewer units to qualify for State weatherization funds; buildings with more than 4 units reviewed case-by-case
Applications reviewed and approved by Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an online application through the City of Frederick website. Once approved, a qualified professional will audit the home to determine what energy-saving work can be completed.

structured_extraction.program_description: Emergency assistance for low- to moderate-income homeowners and renters in Frederick, Carroll, and Washington Counties who currently have a broken heating or cooling system. Provides free HVAC upgrades and tune-ups to restore working heat in winter or cooling in summer.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free grant-funded emergency HVAC repair or replacement for eligible households without a working heating or cooling system. Heating assistance is available in winter months; cooling assistance is available in summer months.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Heating funding available in winter months; cooling funding available in summer months
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low- to moderate-income homeowners and renters in Frederick, Carroll, and Washington Counties who lack a working heating or cooling system
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: HVAC system upgrades and tune-ups to restore heating or cooling
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Frederick, Carroll, and Washington Counties in Maryland
requirements_list: Must currently be without a working heating or cooling system
Must meet income eligibility requirements
Renters must have landlord permission to proceed with work
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an online crisis application through the City of Frederick website.

structured_extraction.program_name: Winning That Government Contracting Award Series
structured_extraction.program_description: A four-session training series from the Maryland Small Business Development Center (SBDC) that teaches entrepreneurs and small business owners how to navigate the federal government procurement process. Topics include the business development lifecycle, team roles and responsibilities, how to read a Request for Proposal (RFP), and the basics of proposal writing.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Four online training sessions covering government contracting topics, offered as a multi-session course for $98 total. Sessions are held April 28 through May 1, 2026, from 10:00 AM to 12:00 PM EDT each day. Payment is accepted by check, money order, or credit card and must be received to guarantee a spot. A login link is sent to registrants the day before each session.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Entrepreneurs and small business owners seeking to win federal government contracts
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training in federal procurement, proposal writing, and government contracting strategy
requirements_list: Registration and payment must be received prior to the training
Special accommodation requests must be submitted in advance and registration must be paid first
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register first through the event registration system; a payment link will be sent after registration. Pay the $98 fee by check, money order, or credit card. A login link for each session will be sent the day or evening before the training.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Hagerstown is allocating $600,000 in American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funds to eligible nonprofit organizations for projects in categories such as children and families, seniors, education, economic recovery, mental health, health/health disparities, and transportation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $50,000 per category are available to eligible nonprofit organizations. Total funding pool is $600,000.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations with 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(19) status serving the City of Hagerstown.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects related to children and families, seniors, education, economic recovery, mental health, health/health disparities, or transportation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to nonprofit organizations operating in or serving the City of Hagerstown, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a nonprofit organization with 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(19) status
Provide IRS Nonprofit Designation Letter
Provide Certificate of Good Standing from Maryland SDAT dated within 30 days or a dated screenshot showing current status
Provide a project budget including all current and anticipated funding sources
Provide evidence of active SAM.gov registration showing the Unique Entity Identifier (UEI)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the completed application and all required supporting documents by 4:00 p.m. on September 1, 2023 via email to grantsmail@hagerstownmd.org. Questions must be submitted by 4:00 p.m. on August 25, 2023.

structured_extraction.program_description: Helps Maryland low-income families pay off past-due utility bill balances (arrearages) to avoid disconnection.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance to pay overdue utility bill balances for low-income households.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income Maryland families with past-due utility bills
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment of past-due (arrearage) utility bill balances
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at https://www.wccac.org/our-services/energy-assistance or schedule an appointment at Washington County Community Action Council, 117 Summit Avenue, Hagerstown, MD 21740.

structured_extraction.program_name: Arts & Entertainment District Admissions & Amusement Tax Exemption Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Enterprises dedicated to visual or performing arts within Hagerstown's Arts & Entertainment District are exempt from Maryland's Admissions and Amusement Tax.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Full exemption from Maryland's Admissions and Amusement Tax for qualifying visual or performing arts enterprises located within the Hagerstown Arts & Entertainment District. Businesses must register with the Maryland State Comptroller's Office using the Combined Registration Application (CRA) to become eligible.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Visual and performing arts enterprises located within Hagerstown's Arts & Entertainment District.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Exemption from collecting and remitting Maryland's Admissions and Amusement Tax.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Only available within Hagerstown's designated Arts & Entertainment District.
requirements_list: Enterprise must be dedicated to visual or performing arts
Must be located within Hagerstown's designated Arts & Entertainment District
Must register with the Maryland State Comptroller's Office using Form CRA
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register with the Maryland State Comptroller's Office using the Combined Registration Application (CRA) to notify the state of eligibility and claim the exemption.

structured_extraction.program_name: Arts & Entertainment District Income Tax Subtraction Modification Program (Hagerstown)
structured_extraction.program_description: Qualified artists who live in Maryland and sell artistic work in any of Maryland's designated Arts & Entertainment Districts can subtract income earned from those in-district sales from their Maryland state income tax.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Qualifying resident artists may subtract income derived from sales of artistic work made within any Maryland Arts & Entertainment District — including internet sales originating in a district and, for performing artists, income from performances in a district — from their Maryland state income tax. Eligible artists submit Maryland State Tax Form 502AE with their state income tax return.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualified resident artists who live in Maryland and sell artistic work in any of Maryland's designated Arts & Entertainment Districts.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of Maryland state income tax liability on income earned from in-district artistic sales or performances.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in all Maryland designated Arts & Entertainment Districts statewide; artist must be a Maryland resident.
requirements_list: Artist must be a qualified residing artist living in Maryland
Must sell artistic work within a Maryland designated Arts & Entertainment District
For performing artists, income from performances in a district qualifies
Internet sales originating in a district also qualify
Must file Maryland State Tax Form 502AE with state income tax return
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit Maryland State Tax Form 502AE when filing your Maryland state income tax return to claim the subtraction modification.

structured_extraction.program_name: Arts & Entertainment District Real Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A 10-year property tax credit for owners who renovate buildings in Hagerstown's Arts & Entertainment District to create artist housing or space for arts and entertainment businesses. The credit covers 50% of the increase in assessed value resulting from the renovation.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 50% property tax credit for 10 years on the increase in assessed value resulting from a renovation project that creates artist housing or space for arts and entertainment enterprises. The credit applies only to the portion of the building occupied by a qualifying artist or arts and entertainment enterprise. Properties using the Enterprise Zone property tax credit are not eligible.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners in Hagerstown's Arts & Entertainment District who renovate buildings for artist housing or arts and entertainment businesses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of property taxes on increased assessed value from qualifying renovation projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Only available within Hagerstown's designated Arts & Entertainment District in Washington County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Property must be located within Hagerstown's designated Arts & Entertainment District
Renovation must create artist housing or space for arts and entertainment enterprises
Credit applies only to the portion of the building occupied by the qualifying artist or enterprise
Properties using the Enterprise Zone property tax credit are not eligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the City of Hagerstown Planning & Economic Development department to apply for the property tax credit.

structured_extraction.program_description: A scheduled pickup service that gives City of Hagerstown residents an affordable and convenient way to dispose of large or bulky items that are not accepted by regular trash service. Collections are held on the first and third Wednesday of every month.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Residents pay $25.00 per large item or per scoop of miscellaneous items (a scoop equals approximately 2 ft wide x 2 ft high x 7 ft long). Accepted items include furniture, appliances, scrap metal, small amounts of wood, paneling, drywall, water heaters, and tires. Mattresses must be wrapped in plastic. Items not accepted include batteries, paint, pesticides, automotive parts, and items containing gasoline, oil, or propane.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling; collections held first and third Wednesday of every month
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents within City of Hagerstown limits who need to dispose of bulky items not accepted by regular trash service
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Disposal of large or bulky household items such as furniture, appliances, scrap metal, and water heaters
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only to residents within the City of Hagerstown limits
requirements_list: Must be a resident within the City of Hagerstown limits
Items must be placed by the sidewalk no later than 7:00 am on the scheduled collection day
Items may be placed out no earlier than 4:00 pm the evening before collection
Mattresses must be wrapped in plastic
Payment must be completed online before collection
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Schedule and pay for a collection online using the link on the program page. A confirmation is sent to the provided email address.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Hagerstown Fire Department and Fire Marshall's Office offer free in-service safety training to businesses and industries located in the City of Hagerstown. Training topics include fire extinguisher safety and crowd management.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: In-person safety training provided to businesses and industry by the Hagerstown Fire Department. Examples include fire extinguisher safety and crowd management training.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses and industries in the City of Hagerstown
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Fire and safety training for workplace employees
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a business or industry located within the City of Hagerstown
requirements_list: Must be a business or industry located in the City of Hagerstown
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an online in-service training request form on the Hagerstown Fire Department website or call (301) 790-2476.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program helps income-qualified homeowners in Hagerstown pay for emergency home repairs. An emergency repair is defined as a situation that is life-threatening or prevents someone from living in decent, safe, and sanitary conditions. Eligible homeowners can receive a grant and/or a low-interest loan to fix these problems.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible homeowners may receive a grant of up to $15,000 for emergency repairs and/or a low-interest loan to complete comprehensive property improvements. Federal Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) income requirements apply.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Income-qualified homeowners in Hagerstown, MD who need emergency repairs to maintain safe and sanitary living conditions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Emergency home repairs that are life-threatening or prevent the homeowner from living in decent, safe, and sanitary conditions, as well as comprehensive property improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to homeowners within the City of Hagerstown, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be an owner-occupant homeowner
Must meet federal CDBG income requirements
Repair must qualify as an emergency (life-threatening or prevents decent, safe, sanitary living conditions)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Department of Housing & Community Development by phone before applying. Applicants are strongly encouraged to call first. A homeowner application form is available for download on the program page.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Hagerstown offers grants to small, for-profit businesses with five or fewer employees. The program helps low-to-moderate income business owners stabilize or expand their businesses, create or retain jobs, and revitalize commercial spaces in Hagerstown. Funding is administered as a reimbursement after the applicant submits approved receipts.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants range from a minimum of $2,500 to a maximum of $5,000. No private match is required. Funding is paid as a reimbursement after the applicant submits approved receipts for eligible expenses.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit microenterprise business owners (5 or fewer employees) located in Hagerstown whose household income is at or below HUD income limits
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business equipment, inventory, fixed assets (machinery, IT equipment, vehicles), professional services including marketing, technology infrastructure and upgrades, entrepreneurial training, and operational expenses such as payroll, utilities, and commercial rent or mortgage payments.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Business must be located within the corporate boundaries of the City of Hagerstown. Mobile 'roving' businesses must show that at least two-thirds of their work occurs within city boundaries and must have been operating for at least six months.
requirements_list: Business must be located in or primarily operate within the City of Hagerstown
Business must have five or fewer total employees including owner(s)
Business must be a private, for-profit entity
Business and owner(s) must be in good standing with the City of Hagerstown and State of Maryland
Business must comply with all applicable City regulations including the Land Management Code

Business must have been operating for at least 12 months at time of application (businesses under 12 months may still apply but must submit a business plan and proof of consultation with a business counseling service)
Business owner's household income must be at or below HUD income limits (e.g., $52,500 for a single-person household up to $98,950 for an 8-person household)
Ineligible businesses: those that restrict access to minors (18+), rental/property investment businesses, and cannabis-based businesses
Priority given to first-time applicants; previous awardees must wait 3 years before reapplying; no more than two grants per household
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the online pre-screening questionnaire. City staff will confirm receipt and provide a full application. Submit the completed application with all required documents including tax returns, bank statements, lease agreement or home business permit, and income verification documents. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: The HUD Choice Neighborhoods Initiative (CNI) is a community-based neighborhood revitalization program. The Hagerstown Housing Authority (HHA), in partnership with the City of Hagerstown, received a HUD Choice Neighborhoods Planning Grant to develop a community-driven plan to revitalize neighborhoods including Frederick Manor, Parkside Homes, Douglass Court, and the downtown area. The planning process includes needs assessment, visioning sessions, and strategy development to create an inclusive and equitable mixed-income neighborhood with real and meaningful community-driven change.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: HUD Choice Neighborhoods Planning Grant awarded to the Hagerstown Housing Authority in partnership with the City of Hagerstown to fund community-based neighborhood revitalization planning. Includes Early Action Activities (EAA) funding for projects such as safer streets (traffic calming, sidewalk repair, crosswalks, landscaping), public space improvements (art, lighting, street design), park/playground enhancements, mobile grocery/food delivery services, and community gathering spaces on vacant lots.
structured_extraction.program_audience: HHA residents (Parkside Homes, Douglass Court, Frederick Manor), neighborhood residents, downtown business owners, and youth and children in the Hagerstown Choice Neighborhoods area.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Community needs assessment and planning; Early Action Activities including street safety improvements, park/recreational space enhancement, food access programs, and public space beautification; workforce/job training programs; youth programming; healthcare facility improvements; housing development and renovation; and community identity and public art initiatives.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available within the Choice Neighborhoods boundary in Hagerstown, MD, including HHA sites Frederick Manor, Parkside Homes, and Douglass Court, and the city's downtown.
requirements_list: Must be a public housing authority or local government entity
Must focus on designated Choice Neighborhoods areas
Projects must promote community connection
Projects must meet a community need
Projects must support economic growth or opportunity
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: HHA and the City of Hagerstown applied to HUD for the planning grant. Community members participate through needs assessment surveys and community meetings to help shape the neighborhood transformation plan.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants to support redevelopment projects in Hagerstown's city center. Grants range from $150,000 to $250,000 and require a minimum 2:1 match from the developer, making total project budgets range from $450,000 to $750,000 or more. This program is part of the City's Invest Hagerstown initiative.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging from $150,000 to $250,000. Applicants must provide a minimum 2:1 match, meaning for every $1 in grant funds, the developer contributes at least $2. Total project costs typically range from $450,000 to $750,000 or more. Full program guidelines apply.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Developers and property owners undertaking redevelopment projects in Hagerstown's city center.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Redevelopment projects in the city center area of Hagerstown.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City center area of Hagerstown, Maryland.
requirements_list: Minimum 2:1 developer match required
Projects must meet complete program guidelines
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete the Guidelines and Application Form available on the program page, then submit according to the instructions in the guidelines.

structured_extraction.program_name: City Center Vacant Storefront Incentive Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Hagerstown offers grants to revitalize vacant storefronts in the Downtown City-Center Mixed-Use (CC-MU) Zoning District. The program brings first-floor commercial spaces up to current code standards to reduce blight, preserve buildings, and create jobs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants with no minimum amount and a maximum of $50,000. Funds are disbursed only after all renovation work is completed to code, required inspections are approved, and final receipts are submitted. Approved applicants receive a Letter of Commitment from the City that can help secure project financing.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners and businesses seeking to renovate vacant first-floor commercial storefronts in Hagerstown's Downtown City-Center Mixed-Use Zoning District.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Renovation of vacant storefronts to bring first-floor commercial spaces up to current code standards, including rectifying code violations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located within the Downtown City-Center Mixed-Use (CC-MU) Zoning District in Hagerstown, MD, which is part of the City's Sustainable Communities Area.
requirements_list: Project must be located in the Downtown City-Center Mixed-Use (CC-MU) Zoning District
Application must include a development plan outlining the renovation schedule and major project components
All work must comply with federal, state, and local codes, laws, and ordinances
All upgrades must be performed to City Code and regulated through the City's Planning and Code Administration Department
Funds disbursed only after staff verify all work is completed to code, inspections are approved, and final receipts are provided
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application form along with a development plan that outlines the renovation schedule and major components. The cross-department Review Committee evaluates applications based on economic impact, proximity to Public Square, renovation budget, square footage being revitalized, building condition and code violations, and length of prior vacancy. Approved applicants receive a Letter of Commitment from the City.

structured_extraction.program_name: City of Hagerstown Incentive and Business Support Programs
structured_extraction.program_description: A collection of incentive and business support programs offered by the City of Hagerstown to encourage business development, redevelopment, and investment within the city. Programs include enterprise zone benefits, grants, loans, and other assistance for businesses operating in or relocating to Hagerstown.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Multiple forms of assistance are available including enterprise zone tax credits, revolving loans, down payment and rehabilitation grants, commercial sign and façade grants, life safety infrastructure grants, microenterprise grants, spring sprouts grants, and arts and entertainment district benefits. Full details are in the program packet linked on the page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses and entrepreneurs interested in operating, relocating to, or investing in the City of Hagerstown, Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business development, commercial rehabilitation, façade improvements, life safety infrastructure, down payment assistance, microenterprise support, and other business investment activities within Hagerstown.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available within the City of Hagerstown, Maryland, with some programs limited to specific incentive districts such as the Enterprise Zone, Opportunity Zone, Arts & Entertainment District, and City Center.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the City of Hagerstown Community and Economic Development team for more information and to apply. A fillable Business Interest Form is available on the page.

Grants range from $5,000 to $25,000 and require a minimum 2:1 match from the developer, making total project budgets range from $15,000 to $75,000 or more. This program is part of the City's Invest Hagerstown initiative.

Full program guidelines apply.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Developers and property owners undertaking redevelopment projects anywhere in the City of Hagerstown.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Redevelopment projects city-wide in Hagerstown.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Hagerstown, Maryland (city-wide).
requirements_list: Minimum 2:1 developer match required
Projects must meet complete program guidelines
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete the Guidelines and Application Form available on the program page, then submit according to the instructions in the guidelines.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program gives businesses and property owners in Hagerstown's City Center a matching grant to improve their building's storefront appearance, signage, and other façade elements. The goal is to enhance the look of commercial and mixed-use buildings, increase brand visibility, and attract customers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A 50% matching (1:1) reimbursement grant for approved projects. Commercial Sign grants range from $250 minimum to $1,500 maximum (requiring a matching $250–$1,500 from the applicant, for a total project of $500–$3,000). Façade grants range from $2,500 minimum to $7,500 maximum (requiring a matching $2,500–$7,500 from the applicant, for a total project of $5,000–$15,000). Funding is subject to availability on a first-come, first-served basis.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses and property owners of commercial or mixed-use buildings in Hagerstown's City Center
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Improving storefront designs, façade elements, and commercial signage on commercial or mixed-use buildings
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be located in Hagerstown's City Center and pertain to commercial or mixed-use buildings
requirements_list: Project must involve a commercial or mixed-use building
Applicant must provide a 1:1 matching investment
Projects are approved prior to reimbursement
Subject to funding availability on a first-come, first-served basis
Must follow full program guidelines
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review the full program guidelines and application form available on the program page, then submit an application to the DCED team. Grants are awarded on a first-come, first-served basis subject to funding availability.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free, voluntary crime-prevention training and certification program for landlords, property owners, and managers of rental properties—particularly larger apartment complexes and multiple housing units—in Hagerstown, MD. The program trains participants in crime prevention, physical security, and community awareness to keep drugs, gangs, and other illegal activity off their properties, improving neighborhood livability. It is delivered in three phases: Phase I is an 8-hour management training class covering crime prevention best practices, lease agreements, and eviction issues; Phase II is a physical security survey (CPTED inspection) of doors, windows, locks, lighting, and landscaping; and Phase III is an annual community awareness social co-taught by property management and police. Successfully certified properties earn a gold certificate and the right to display the Crime-Free Multi-Housing logo. Participation is voluntary but may be required for property owners whose properties receive a certain number of city notices. Certified properties have reported up to 70% reductions in police calls for service.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free, police-led training and property certification program delivered in three phases: Phase I is an 8-hour management training class covering crime prevention, lease agreements, and eviction issues; Phase II is a physical security survey (CPTED inspection) of doors, windows, locks, lighting, and landscaping; Phase III is an annual community awareness social co-taught by property management and police. Successfully certified properties earn a gold certificate and the right to display the Crime-Free Multi-Housing logo. Some property owners/managers may be required to attend if their property receives a certain number of notices from the city. All classes are held at the Washington County Free Library, Room #334. Certified properties have reported up to 70% reductions in police calls for service.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Crime prevention training, physical security inspections (CPTED), and community awareness activities to reduce crime and illegal activity on rental properties

Open to landlords, property owners, and property managers
Participation is voluntary and targeted toward larger apartment complexes and owners of multiple housing units
Some property owners/managers may be required to attend if their property receives a certain number of notices from the city
Must complete all three phases under police department supervision to achieve full property certification
Annual renewal requires compliance with Phases I and II
Must register at least 48 hours before class to avoid cancellation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register for the next Crime-Free Multi-Housing Training Class using the registration link on the program page, or download the registration form and contact Lt. John Lehman at 301-797-6408 or jlehman@hagerstownpd.org. Then complete all three phases under police supervision to certify the property.

structured_extraction.program_description: An employer-paid, confidential benefit program for City of Hagerstown employees and their dependents that provides counseling, financial guidance, legal support, and work-life resources to help manage personal, family, and work-related issues.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides up to 6 free face-to-face counseling visits per year, financial information from Certified Public Accountants and Certified Financial Planners, a free 30-minute legal consultation per year with a 25% discount on legal fees thereafter, work-life solutions, and online resources including self-assessments and provider search tools. The program is employer-paid and confidential, available at no cost to employees and their dependents. Accessible 24/7 by phone or online through ComPsych Guidance Resources.
structured_extraction.program_audience: City of Hagerstown employees and their dependents
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Personal counseling, financial guidance, legal consultations, and work-life support services
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to City of Hagerstown employees
requirements_list: Must be a City of Hagerstown employee or dependent of an employee
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Access ComPsych Guidance Resources 24/7 by phone or online. Contact the Human Resources Department for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Enterprise Zone program offers tax credits to businesses located within the Hagerstown Enterprise Zone. Eligible businesses can receive real property tax credits on improvements, income tax credits for wages paid to new employees, and personal property tax credits for new machinery and equipment in Focus Areas. The program aims to encourage investment and job creation in designated areas of Hagerstown and Washington County, Maryland. Approximately 5,500 acres in Washington County are within three state-designated Enterprise Zones, each approved by the State of Maryland for a 10-year period.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Three tax credit/exemption components: (1) Real Property Tax Credit — a 10-year credit against local real property taxes on the increased assessed value of improvements, starting at 80% in years 1–5 and declining to 30% in year 10. (2) Income Tax Credit — a credit for wages paid to new eligible employees. General credit is $1,000 per new non-disadvantaged worker (one-time). For economically disadvantaged employees, the credit is up to $3,000 in year 1, $2,000 in year 2, and $1,000 in year 3. Minimum investment requirements: $5,000 or 1 new job in the City Center; $50,000 or 5 new jobs outside the City Center. (3) Personal Property Tax Credit — available in Focus Areas for new machinery and equipment. (4) Exemption from commercial building excise tax.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Property tax credit applications must be submitted prior to project completion and issuance of User/Occupancy Permits.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses relocating to or establishing in the Enterprise Zone, new start-up businesses, existing businesses expanding through capital investments or job creation, and property developers. Eligible business types include manufacturing, warehousing, R&D, corporate/regional offices, service industries, and (in the City Center) retail/mercantile businesses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Real property acquisition and improvements, new construction, rehabilitation projects, new machinery and equipment purchases (in Focus Areas), and creation of new full-time permanent jobs within the Enterprise Zone.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Business must be located within the Hagerstown Enterprise Zone or the Hancock Enterprise Zone in Washington County, Maryland. Personal property tax credits are limited to Focus Areas within the Enterprise Zone.
requirements_list: Business must be located within the Enterprise Zone
Must meet minimum investment or job creation thresholds: $5,000 investment or 1 new job in City Center (CC-MU Zoning Area); $50,000 investment or 5 new jobs outside City Center
Machinery and equipment purchases are not eligible for the real property investment threshold
New job must be full-time and permanent (35+ hours/week)
New job must pay at least 150% of the federal minimum wage
Employee must be employed for at least 6 months before claiming the credit
Job must not have previously existed in Washington County before the business located or expanded in the Enterprise Zone
Business must be an eligible type: manufacturing, warehousing, R&D, corporate/regional offices, service industries, or retail/mercantile if in City Center
Property tax credit application must be submitted prior to project completion and issuance of User/Occupancy Permits
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Washington County Department of Business Development. Property tax credit applications must be submitted before project completion and issuance of User/Occupancy Permits. Full program guidelines and application are available at the link provided.

structured_extraction.program_description: This grant helps property owners install or upgrade fire suppression systems that meet National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) standards. It lowers the financial barrier of adding water service lines, meter vaults, water meters, and other utility infrastructure needed for NFPA-compliant fire suppression systems in residential, commercial, or mixed-use buildings.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants range from $7,500 to $50,000 and require a 1:1 match from the applicant. For example, a $25,000 grant requires an additional $25,000 from the applicant, for a total project cost of $50,000. The maximum total project cost supported is $100,000. Grants are awarded on a first-come, first-served basis subject to funding availability.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners and developers with residential, commercial, professional office, retail, or mixed-use buildings within Hagerstown's Sustainable Communities Area who want to install or upgrade NFPA-compliant fire suppression systems.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of automatic sprinkler systems; costs related to increasing water service or fire lines; installation or upgrade of meter vaults; installing new or upgrading/replacing outdated sprinkler heads or piping; replacing mains or backflow devices.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located within the City of Hagerstown's Sustainable Communities Area.
requirements_list: Project must involve a fully residential, commercial, professional office, retail, or mixed-use building.
Project must be located within the City of Hagerstown's Sustainable Communities Area.
Applicant must be in good standing with the City of Hagerstown.
Total project cost must demonstrate a minimum 1:1 match (applicant match equals grant amount).
Fire suppression projects related to water service installations associated with bricks-and-mortar renovation projects must involve service meters that are four (4) inches or larger.
Application must align with the City of Hagerstown's overall vision for the city.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review the program guidelines and complete the application form available on the program page. Submit to dped@hagerstownmd.org. Applications are reviewed on a first-come, first-served basis, subject to funding availability.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Hagerstown Fire Department provides and installs free smoke detectors for residents of homes with 1 to 3 units. Each eligible home receives one free smoke detector per living level, provided and installed at no cost to the resident, to help protect families from fire.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One free smoke detector per living level of a 1 to 3 unit dwelling, provided and installed at no charge by the Hagerstown Fire Department.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Provision and installation of smoke detectors in residential homes

requirements_list: Must reside in a home with 1 to 3 units
Must be a resident within the City of Hagerstown
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an online smoke alarm request form at the Hagerstown city website or call (301) 790-2476. The Hagerstown Fire Department will provide and install the detector at no cost.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Hagerstown Community Garden offers City of Hagerstown residents the chance to rent an individual garden plot at low cost on public land. Gardeners can grow vegetables, herbs, and flowers in an organic community setting, with water access provided on site. The program also offers a 50% fee reduction for qualifying applicants.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Garden plots are rented annually at $20 (128 sq ft) or $30 (192 sq ft). A 50% reduction in plot fees is available to qualifying applicants upon approval by the Operating Committee. Water access is provided on site from early April through October each year.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Returning gardeners: December 31, 2025; New gardeners: January 1, 2026 to February 15, 2026

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Renting a garden plot to grow vegetables, herbs, and flowers

requirements_list: Must be a City of Hagerstown resident
Pay annual plot rental fee ($20 or $30 depending on plot size)
Observe Garden Rules governing the garden
Participate in community work days
Keep communal areas weeded
Perform maintenance tasks as directed by the Operating Committee and Plot Coordinators
Fee reduction applicants must complete a separate application form and receive approval from the Operating Committee
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Returning gardeners submit applications by December 31, 2025. New gardeners submit applications between January 1 and February 15, 2026. A separate application form is required for the 50% fee reduction, subject to Operating Committee approval.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Hagerstown Homeownership Initiative (HHI) provides up to $7,500 in down payment and closing cost assistance to help people buy homes in the City of Hagerstown. The assistance is structured as a forgivable loan that converts to a grant if the recipient meets the program conditions. The goal is to reduce vacant homes and increase homeownership across city neighborhoods. Priority is given to first-time home buyers, current renters, and those purchasing vacant properties. Eligible property types include single-family homes, townhomes, and condos.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $7,500 provided as a forgivable loan-to-grant for down payment and closing costs. No repayment is required if the recipient meets the program conditions. Priority is given to first-time home buyers, current renters, and those purchasing vacant properties. Applications must be submitted at least 30 days before settlement.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Funding has been exhausted for FY2026.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment and closing costs for purchasing a home in the City of Hagerstown.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Hagerstown Revolving Loan Fund (HRLF) provides low-interest loans to small businesses and developers in Hagerstown, MD to support growth, expansion, rehabilitation, code compliance, façade enhancement, and other eligible business activities including land improvements, building purchase or renovation, machinery and equipment purchase, building construction, leasehold improvements, micro-enterprise activities, and working capital.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Fixed-rate loans at PRIME plus 1% (minimum 3%). Maximum loan amount is $200,000 or 80% of total project cost, whichever is less. Working capital loans are capped at $30,000. Micro-enterprise loans are available up to $5,000. Minimum loan amount is $5,000. Loan term may not exceed 7 years (5 years for working capital). Borrowers must provide at least 20% cash equity investment of total project costs (40% for new restaurants open 3 years or less). Repayment begins within one month of project completion or taking possession of purchased equipment. A non-refundable application fee based on loan amount is required.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses and developers organized as a proprietorship, partnership, limited liability company, or corporation with annual sales under $5,000,000 for each of the last two years.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Growth and expansion, rehabilitation, code compliance, façade enhancement, land improvements, purchase or renovation of buildings, machinery or equipment with a useful life of at least 5 years, building construction, leasehold improvements, micro-enterprise activities, and working capital.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to businesses operating within the City of Hagerstown, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a small business or developer organized as a proprietorship, partnership, LLC, or corporation.
Annual business sales must be less than $5,000,000 for each of the last two years.
Minimum 20% cash equity investment of total project costs (40% for new restaurants open 3 years or less).
Credit check required.
Non-refundable application fee required based on requested loan amount.
For leasehold improvements, lease term must be equal to or greater than the loan term and the City must secure a lien on the land, building, and improvements.
Funds may not be used for non-profits, gambling organizations, lending or investment organizations, land speculation, or illegal activities.
Ineligible costs include management fees, financing costs, franchise fees, debt repayment, debt consolidation, moving costs, and refinancing.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review the Program Guidelines and Application document linked on the program page. Complete the application and submit it with all required documentation and the non-refundable application fee. A credit check will be conducted.

structured_extraction.program_name: Historic District and Landmark Designation — County Real Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: Property owners in locally designated Historic Districts or Landmarks in Hagerstown may receive a county real property tax credit for restoration or new construction attached to historic structures. Projects must meet the National Park Service's Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A property tax credit equal to 10% of the owner's expense for restoration of a historic structure, or 5% of the expense for new construction attached to an existing historic structure. Projects must meet the National Park Service's Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of properties in locally designated Historic Districts or Landmarks in Hagerstown, MD
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Restoration of historic structures or new construction attached to existing historic structures
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties must be located within a locally designated Historic District or be a designated Landmark in Hagerstown, MD
requirements_list: Property must be in a locally designated Historic District or be a designated Landmark
Projects must meet the National Park Service's Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the City of Hagerstown Planning Office for more information. Exterior improvements must be reviewed by the Historic District Commission.

structured_extraction.program_name: Historic District and Landmark Designation — Federal Income Tax Credit (Certified Heritage Resource Rehabilitation)
structured_extraction.program_description: Owners of income-producing historic properties in Hagerstown's locally designated Historic Districts or Landmarks may be eligible for a federal income tax credit equal to 20% of approved rehabilitation costs for a certified heritage resource.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal income tax credit equal to 20% of the costs of an approved rehabilitation of an income-producing certified heritage resource. Also includes a charitable donation deduction for conveying a perpetual easement to a qualified preservation organization.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of income-producing properties in locally designated Historic Districts or Landmarks in Hagerstown, MD
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rehabilitation of income-producing certified heritage resource properties
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties must be located within a locally designated Historic District or be a designated Landmark in Hagerstown, MD
requirements_list: Property must be income-producing
Property must be a certified heritage resource
Rehabilitation must be approved
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the City of Hagerstown Planning Office for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Historic District and Landmark Designation — Maryland Income Tax Credit (Certified Heritage Structure Rehabilitation)
structured_extraction.program_description: Owners of properties in Hagerstown's locally designated Historic Districts or Landmarks may qualify for a Maryland state income tax credit equal to 20% of the costs of an approved rehabilitation of a certified heritage structure.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Maryland income tax credit equal to 20% of the costs of an approved rehabilitation of a certified heritage structure.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of properties in locally designated Historic Districts or Landmarks in Hagerstown, MD
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rehabilitation of certified heritage structures
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties must be located within a locally designated Historic District or be a designated Landmark in Hagerstown, MD
requirements_list: Property must be a certified heritage structure
Rehabilitation must be approved
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the City of Hagerstown Planning Office for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Hagerstown buys vacant properties, renovates them, and sells them at appraised value to income-qualified individuals and families who want to purchase a home in the city. The program is funded by the Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) and can be combined with other mortgage assistance programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Renovated homes are sold at current appraised value to qualified buyers. The program may be combined with other mortgage assistance programs. The city also pays a 2.5% realtor commission if the buyer uses a realtor and successfully completes the purchase.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Income-qualified individuals and families seeking to purchase a home in the City of Hagerstown
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of a renovated home within the City of Hagerstown
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must purchase within the City of Hagerstown city limits
requirements_list: Annual household income must be below the program income limits (e.g., $52,500 for 1 person, up to $98,950 for 8 persons)
Must be pre-qualified for a mortgage loan
Must submit proof of mortgage loan pre-qualification with application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact a local mortgage company or bank to get pre-qualified for a mortgage loan. Ask about the Maryland Mortgage Program and any first-time homebuyer incentives. Once you have a pre-qualification letter, schedule a tour of available homes and submit a completed Homeownership Program Application to the Department of Housing & Community Development.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides guidance and education to juvenile fire setters and their families. It screens children and families to understand why fire setting occurred, then recommends fire safety education, professional counseling, or both to redirect dangerous behavior.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free screening interview, fire safety education, and referral to professional counseling for juvenile fire setters and their families.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families of juvenile fire setters and professionals (fire marshals, schools, Department of Juvenile Justice) who work with children involved in fire setting.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Fire safety education and referral to professional counseling for children who set fires.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Hagerstown, Maryland
requirements_list: Child must be a juvenile involved in fire setting
Referrals accepted from fire marshals, Department of Juvenile Justice, parents or relatives, schools, or other agencies
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Hagerstown Fire Department by phone, mail, or by filling out the Juvenile Fire Setter intake form online. A screening interview with the child and family will be conducted to determine next steps.

structured_extraction.program_description: A one-time refund authorized by the Next Generation Energy Act that distributes electric utility bill credits to residential electric customers of the Hagerstown Light Department. Customers can also choose to donate their credit to a local energy relief fund.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A one-time credit identified as 'Legislative Energy Relief' on the billing statement, distributed during February 2026 to all residential electric customers. Customers may also donate their credit to the Washington County Community Action Council energy relief fund.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential electric customers of the City of Hagerstown Light Department
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Electric bill credit or donation to local energy relief fund
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residential customers within the corporate limits of Hagerstown, MD served by the Hagerstown Light Department
requirements_list: Must be a residential electric customer of the Hagerstown Light Department
Credit applied during February 2026 billing period
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Credits are automatically applied to eligible residential customer bills during February 2026. Customers who wish to donate their credit to the Washington County Community Action Council energy relief fund should contact customerservice@hagerstownmd.org.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Hagerstown Department of Parks & Engineering lets residents and organizations honor a special person or life event by donating a memorial tree or bench in one of the City's parks. Donors can commemorate births, deaths, weddings, anniversaries, and other milestones with a lasting tribute in a public green space.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: For a $500 donation, the City supplies and plants a 6-foot conifer or 2-inch caliper deciduous tree, with an engraved tag (up to four lines, 20 characters per line), a letter to the donor, a listing on the Parks and Recreation webpage, and recognition at the annual Arbor Day ceremony. The tree is replaced if it dies within the first three years. For a $1,500 donation, the City provides and installs a 6-foot powder-coated metal bench (green or black) with an engraved plaque (up to four lines, 20 characters per line). All donations are tax deductible.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals, organizations, and businesses wishing to memorialize a person or life event with a tree or bench in a Hagerstown city park.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding a memorial tree planting or bench installation in a City of Hagerstown park.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in City of Hagerstown parks only. Donors may suggest a location but the City makes the final determination.
requirements_list: Complete and submit the application to the City of Hagerstown Department of Parks & Engineering, 1 East Franklin Street, Hagerstown, MD 21740
Payment is required prior to scheduling installation
Plaque or bench wording must be city-approved (up to four lines, 20 characters per line)
Decorating or adorning memorial trees is not permitted
Any plaque or bench installed without City approval may be removed at the installer's expense
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Download and complete the application form. 2. Return the application to the City of Hagerstown Department of Parks & Engineering. 3. City staff will contact you to finalize the memorial location and details. 4. Payment is required before installation is scheduled. 5. A letter of acknowledgement is sent and plaque/tag wording is finalized. 6. The tree or bench is installed.

structured_extraction.program_name: Middle Neighborhoods Emergency Repair Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants to homeowners to cover 75% of the cost of emergency home repairs, up to $15,000. An emergency repair is defined as a situation that prevents a homeowner from living in safe, decent, and sanitary conditions. Homeowners pay the remaining 25% of the project cost, plus any amount over the $15,000 grant limit. Income limits apply.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant covers 75% of emergency repair costs, up to a maximum of $15,000. Homeowners contribute the remaining 25% and any costs above the $15,000 cap. Income limits apply based on household size, ranging from $78,750 for a 1-person household to $148,425 for an 8-person household.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners in Hagerstown, MD who need emergency home repairs and meet income eligibility requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Emergency home repairs needed to maintain safe, decent, and sanitary living conditions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to homeowners in the Middle Neighborhoods area of Hagerstown, MD (Washington County).
requirements_list: Must be a homeowner
Property must be located in Hagerstown, MD
Must meet household income limits (e.g., $78,750 for 1 person, up to $148,425 for 8 persons)
Income determination includes all household members age 18 and over
Repair must qualify as an emergency — a situation preventing safe, decent, and sanitary living conditions
Homeowner must contribute 25% of project cost plus any amount exceeding the $15,000 grant maximum
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Department of Housing & Community Development by phone before applying. The department strongly encourages applicants to call first. Submit a homeowner application (available on the program page).

structured_extraction.program_description: The PEP Program offers incentives to building owners in the PEP Zone in Hagerstown's City Center to renovate commercial, residential, and mixed-use buildings, and provides rent assistance to attract new and expanding businesses to those renovated buildings.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible building owners receive: (1) an annual grant equal to City property tax for 5 years; (2) 2 free equivalent dwelling units (EDUs) for utilities valued at $13,800; (3) 1 year free parking plus 50% discount for 4 years; (4) waiver of development fees such as building permits, plan review, occupancy, and zoning fees; (5) fast-track expedited review through Planning Department and Historic District Commission; (6) flexibility under the Maryland Building Rehabilitation Code; and (7) 2 hours of free consultation on historic tax credits.
