Eligible businesses can receive rent assistance of up to $30,000 total paid to the property owner for the first 2–3 years of operation, provided the business commits to a minimum 4-year lease.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Building owners renovating commercial, residential, or mixed-use properties within the PEP Zone in Hagerstown's City Center, and businesses looking to lease space in PEP-eligible buildings.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Renovation and upgrade of commercial, residential, or mixed-use buildings; business rent assistance for new or expanding tenants in PEP-eligible buildings.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects and businesses must be located within the PEP Zone in the City Center of Hagerstown, Maryland.
requirements_list: Project must be located within the PEP Zone in the City Center
Minimum investment of $250,000 for commercial, $100,000 for residential, or $200,000 for mixed-use projects (excluding property acquisition costs)
Commercial projects must participate in the Enterprise Zone Program
Applicant must not be delinquent on any City or County taxes or other financial obligations to the City
Building and all core systems must meet all City of Hagerstown Code requirements
For residential and artist live-work spaces, minimum square footage requirements apply
Prior renovations completed after January 1, 2007 are eligible
For rent assistance: business must be new or existing and looking to move into or expand within the PEP Zone
Business must occupy first-floor retail or restaurant space, or non-storefront commercial space in PEP-approved buildings
Business must maintain a lease and operate for a minimum of 4 years
Applicants must receive building permits and implement the approved development plan and schedule
Progress reports due every six months; annual Enterprise Zone Tax Credit reports required if applicable
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a PEP Application to the City of Hagerstown. The PEP Committee reviews the application for compliance with eligibility criteria, including receipt of building permits and an approved development plan and schedule. Any changes to the approved plan must be resubmitted for committee review. Full program guidelines and a zone map are available via the links on the program page.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides a 50% reduction in plot fees for community garden plot holders in Hagerstown. Applicants must submit a separate Plot Fee Assistance application form along with their Garden Application form, and the fee reduction must be approved by the Operating Committee of the Association.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A 50% reduction in community garden plot fees. Applicants must send full payment with the application; the reduction is approved and applied by the Operating Committee of the Association.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community garden plot holders in Hagerstown, MD
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of community garden plot fees
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to community garden plot holders in Hagerstown, MD
requirements_list: Submit a Plot Fee Assistance application form along with the Garden Application form
Fee reduction must be approved by the Operating Committee of the Association
Send full payment with application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and submit a Plot Fee Assistance application form together with the Garden Application form. Include full payment with the application. The Operating Committee of the Association reviews and approves the fee reduction.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Hagerstown Police Department offers signing bonuses to experienced or recently trained police officers who join as lateral hires. Officers with Maryland certification or comparable out-of-state training are eligible for bonuses paid out over their first several years of service.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $40,000 signing bonus for current Maryland police officers, former Maryland officers eligible for immediate recertification, and applicants who completed a Maryland-approved entry-level police training program eligible for immediate certification — paid as $10,000 at end of field training, then $10,000 at completion of years 2, 3, and 4. Up to $30,000 for applicants with comparable out-of-state training or former Maryland officers eligible for recertification after comparative compliance training — paid as $10,000 at end of field training, then $10,000 at completion of years 2 and 3.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Experienced or recently trained police officers, including those certified in Maryland or with comparable out-of-state certification, seeking to join the Hagerstown Police Department as lateral hires.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Signing bonus paid to eligible lateral police officer hires over their first years of service with the Hagerstown Police Department.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to applicants from Maryland or any other state who meet certification or training requirements.
requirements_list: Possess current Maryland certification as a police officer, OR
Have been certified in Maryland within 5 years prior to selection, OR
Have successfully completed an approved Maryland Police and Correctional Training Commission (MPTSC) entry-level training program within 2 years prior to selection, OR

Have been employed as a police officer within the last 5 years in another state and completed a basic police officer entrance-level training program deemed comparable to Maryland requirements by MPTSC, OR
Have completed a basic police officer entrance-level training program meeting MPTSC requirements within the last 2 years
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Click the 'Join HPD' button on the page and complete the inquiry form to be contacted by a recruiter.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants to developers to rehabilitate rental properties to market rate. Grants range from $7,500 to $20,000 and require a minimum 2:1 match from the developer. Projects receiving more than $7,500 must renovate two or more units within a single property or parcel, with total project costs ranging from $22,500 to $60,000 or more.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants from a minimum of $7,500 to a maximum of $20,000 for rehabilitation of rental properties to market rate. Developers must provide a minimum 2:1 match. Projects receiving more than $7,500 must renovate two or more units within a single property or parcel. Total project costs range from $22,500 to $60,000 or more.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Developers rehabilitating rental properties in Hagerstown to market rate
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rehabilitation of rental properties to bring them to market rate
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Hagerstown, Maryland
requirements_list: Minimum 2:1 developer match required
Projects receiving grants greater than $7,500 must renovate two or more units within a single property or parcel
Complete program guidelines apply
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete the Guidelines and Application Form available on the program page and submit per the instructions in the guidelines.

structured_extraction.program_name: Sale of City Owned Properties – Competitive Negotiated Sale Process
structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Hagerstown makes city-owned real estate available for purchase through a Competitive Negotiated Sale Process. Applications are evaluated based on the applicant's vision and plan for the property combined with the offered purchase price. The goal is to return properties to the private sector for their highest and best use.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: City-owned properties are sold to qualified buyers through a competitive negotiated process. The sale price is considered alongside the buyer's proposed use and development plan for the property.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses, developers, and individuals interested in purchasing city-owned properties in Hagerstown for redevelopment or reuse.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and redevelopment of city-owned real estate for its highest and best use.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties are located within the City of Hagerstown, Maryland.
requirements_list: Submit a vision and plan for the property
Provide an offer price
Complete the Competitive Negotiated Sale Application Form
Participation in competitive negotiated sale process
Compliance with city property sale policies and procedures
Financial capability demonstration
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the Competitive Negotiated Sale Application Form along with a vision/plan for the property and an offer price. Contact the Department of Community and Economic Development for a full list of available properties and application materials.

structured_extraction.program_name: Single Family Rehabilitation Loans and Residential Rehabilitation Loans
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides low-interest loans and grants to help homeowners and property owners make comprehensive renovations to single-family or multi-family structures. Single-family homeowners may also qualify for a grant to cover eligible emergency repairs. Funding is subject to approval by the Hagerstown Loan Review Authority and available funds. Federal Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) income requirements apply.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest rehabilitation loans for comprehensive renovations to single-family or multi-family structures, and grants for eligible emergency repairs for single-family homeowners. Loan approval is subject to Hagerstown Loan Review Authority review and funding availability. Federal CDBG income limits apply.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Single-family homeowners and multi-family property owners in Hagerstown, MD who meet federal CDBG income requirements and need comprehensive renovations or emergency repairs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Comprehensive renovations to single-family or multi-family structures; eligible emergency repairs for single-family homeowners.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Hagerstown, Maryland
requirements_list: Must meet federal CDBG income requirements
Project must involve a single-family or multi-family structure
Loan funding subject to Hagerstown Loan Review Authority approval
Subject to funding availability
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Department of Housing & Community Development before applying. Call 301-739-8577 ext. 134 or ext. 103 for full program information. Applicants are strongly encouraged to call before submitting a homeowner application.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Hagerstown's Department of Community and Economic Development offers small grants to for-profit businesses located in the City Center Mixed-Use (CC-MU) zone. The grants help businesses improve efficiency, gain a competitive advantage, and beautify their storefronts. Eligible uses include storefront merchandising displays, planters and flowers, new office equipment, software or hardware, marketing, and professional services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement grants of up to $750 per business. If approved, the applicant purchases the product or service, submits the receipt, and the City disburses the approved amount.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: May 22, 2026, or until all allocated program funds have been distributed
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit businesses located in the City Center Mixed-Use (CC-MU) zone in Hagerstown, MD
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Storefront merchandising displays, planters and flowers, new office equipment, software or hardware, marketing, and professional services
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must be located within the City Center Mixed-Use (CC-MU) zone in Hagerstown, MD
requirements_list: Business must be located in the City Center Mixed-Use (CC-MU) zone
Must be a for-profit business
Must apply by May 22, 2026, or until funds are exhausted
Must submit receipt of approved purchase by June 5, 2026
Must provide a copy of the company's Business Status from Maryland Business Express
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Complete the Spring Sprout Grant Application and vendor forms. 2. Print a copy of your company's Business Status from Maryland Business Express. 3. Submit the application by May 22, 2026. 4. If approved, purchase the product or services. 5. Submit the receipt by June 5, 2026. 6. The City disburses the approved amount.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Hagerstown Engineering Division plants and maintains street trees in the public right-of-way at no cost to residents. The program restores forest canopy in the urban landscape and improves the appeal of city streetscapes. Funding sources include the Forest Conservation Fund and various grants. Residents can request a street tree be planted at their property by contacting the Engineering Division for a site inspection. The city averages about 200 street trees planted per year, and scheduling depends on project funding and planting season weather conditions. The city also assesses trees, obtains necessary permits from the Department of Natural Resources, and arranges a contracted arborist to complete the work.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Residents can receive street trees planted by the city at no cost. Trees must be selected from the City's Approved Street Tree List and are planted in the right-of-way or between the curb and sidewalk, or in a tree well within the sidewalk. The city averages about 200 street trees planted per year. The city assesses trees, obtains permits from the Department of Natural Resources, and arranges a contracted arborist to complete the work. Scheduling depends on project funding and planting season weather conditions.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Hagerstown residents and property owners who want a street tree planted in the public right-of-way adjacent to their property
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planting and maintenance of street trees along public streets and rights-of-way
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents within the City of Hagerstown, Maryland
requirements_list: Resident must contact the Engineering Division to request a street tree
A site inspection is required to determine if a suitable planting location exists
Trees must be from the City's Approved Street Tree List if planted in the right-of-way or between the curb and sidewalk
Tree must be located or requested in the public right-of-way between the curb and sidewalk, or in a tree well within the sidewalk
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Engineering Division at (301) 739-8577 ext. 125 to discuss a tree planting request, or submit a Street Tree Maintenance Request form online or call 301-739-8577 x. 178. A site inspection will likely be required before a tree is scheduled for planting. The city will assess the tree, apply for necessary permits from the Department of Natural Resources, and schedule a contracted arborist to complete the work.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides free information and direct assistance to Maryland renters on landlord-tenant issues, including lease reviews, eviction procedures, code enforcement, substandard housing, security deposits, rent escrow, and lead paint concerns. Also offers referrals to legal service providers and other organizations. Educational resource covering tenant rights, lease agreements, security deposits, maintenance issues, fair housing laws, and dispute resolution.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free tenant advocacy services including lease reviews, information on eviction notification and procedure, illegal eviction, nonpayment of rent, code enforcement, substandard or unsafe housing, security deposits, rent escrow, and lead paint. Also provides legal guidance on tenant rights, assistance with landlord-tenant disputes, fair housing support, and information on application fees and reusable screening reports. Referrals to legal service providers are also available. Does not provide financial assistance.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Michael Donnelly (Tenant Advocacy Coordinator); Carol Ott (Tenant Advocacy Director); Marceline White (Executive Director)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland renters (tenants), working families, low-income communities, communities of color, and vulnerable Marylanders with housing questions, rental issues, or facing housing discrimination
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational guidance and direct assistance to prevent housing loss. Not a financial assistance program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in all Maryland counties and Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Must be a tenant or landlord in Maryland with a housing or rental issue
Documentation of lease violations, harassment, or discrimination may be required
Compliance with notice requirements for various tenancy types
Adherence to fair housing laws
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an intake form at https://econaction.org/tenant-advocacy-intake-form/ to connect with a tenant advocate. Call the tenant hotline at 443-447-7336 (Tuesday-Friday, 10 AM-2 PM). Self-help resources including one-page fact sheets and a comprehensive Tenant Guide are also available for download.

structured_extraction.program_description: A community education program run by the Rockville City Police Department that teaches residents about police operations and community-police partnerships. Classes meet weekly on Wednesday evenings from June through July 2026.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free educational program running 7–9 p.m. on Wednesdays, June 3 – July 22, 2026. Participants learn about police department operations and community engagement.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Rockville residents interested in learning about local police operations
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Education and training on police operations and community-police partnerships
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Rockville, Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online via the provided DocuSign link before the deadline.

structured_extraction.program_description: A school-based group mentoring program for middle school students in Rockville that uses sports to build confidence and life skills. Students are self-referred or referred by a school counselor or administrator. The program runs during the school year from October to June and includes a five-week summer camp.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free group mentoring through sports for middle school students, designed to build confidence that carries over into other areas of life. Sessions run weekly during the school year with a five-week summer camp also included.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Middle school students in Rockville, especially those who may lack confidence in sports.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Sports-based group mentoring to build student confidence and life skills.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in the City of Rockville, Maryland.
requirements_list: Students must be at the middle school level
Students may self-refer or be referred by a school counselor or administrator
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Students can self-refer or be referred by a school counselor or administrator. Contact Cecil Rucker at crucker@rockvillemd.gov for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: Program encouraging local organizations to adopt local streams for managing litter along stream banks, shorelines, and waterways. Groups volunteer to commit to at least two self-led stream cleanups per year to remove litter and other pollutants from local waterways. Benefits include enhancing aesthetics, removing pollutants from drinking water supply, removing mosquito breeding habitat, and improving aquatic plant and animal habitat. The city provides safety information, gloves, safety vests (if requested), trash bags, and trash collection.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The city supplies safety information, gloves, safety vests (if requested), trash bags for participants, and other support as needed. Filled trash bags are collected by the city after cleanups. Groups must commit to at least two self-led cleanups per year along an adopted stream and to the adoption for at least one year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community volunteers, local businesses, civic and watershed organizations, academic institutions, scout groups, neighborhood groups, and community groups of all ages (with adult supervision for those under 18) in Rockville interested in maintaining local streams.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supplies (gloves, safety vests, trash bags) and trash collection for stream cleanup events; stream cleanup and litter removal; pollution monitoring and reporting.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available for streams located within the City of Rockville, Maryland.
requirements_list: Designate a Representative (point of contact, age 18+)
Include at least one participating adult (18+ years); one adult per six youth
Walk stream section before applying to assess appropriateness
Commit to hosting at least two self-led stream cleanups per year (recommended late spring/summer and fall)
Cleanups typically last 2-4 hours
Commit to adoption for at least one year
Submit an Adopt-A-Stream Application
Have each volunteer sign a release form and return it to Shannon Philbin
Submit a Scheduling and Supply Request Form at least two weeks before each cleanup (notify City at least one week before cleanup)
Submit a report form after each cleanup
Do not trespass on private property without permission
Stockpile collected litter in City-designated location
Separate and recycle materials where practical
All participants must wear gloves or hand protection
Work in groups of two or more
Avoid steep slopes and confined stream stretches
Cleanups during daylight hours and fair weather only
Do not pick up hazardous materials
Participants under 18 must have parent/guardian consent and sign liability waiver
Must sign liability waiver and informed consent form
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review program and safety guidelines, view the Adopt-A-Stream Map to find an available stream, survey intended stream section to assess appropriateness, submit the Adopt-A-Stream Application, have volunteers sign the release form and return it to Shannon Philbin, submit a supply request form at least two weeks before a cleanup, and submit a report form after each cleanup.

structured_extraction.program_description: Commissions site-specific public art to be installed on City of Rockville-owned property. Established in 1978, the program funds artworks that reflect historical, cultural, and socially relevant themes, helping define Rockville's cultural identity and beautify public spaces.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program is funded by an annual appropriation based on the city's prior-year budget. Funds are used to commission works of public art installed on city-owned property. Artists or organizations are commissioned to create site-specific works.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Artists and organizations who can create site-specific public art for installation on City of Rockville property
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Creation and installation of site-specific public art on city-owned property
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Rockville, Maryland
requirements_list: Art must be site-specific and installed on city-owned property
Works should reference historical, cultural, or socially relevant themes of the surrounding site
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: No application process described on this page. Contact Anne O'Dell at the Office of the City Manager for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Rockville provides free bicycle racks to businesses and property owners in Rockville. The city purchases and installs inverted-U style bike racks either in public rights-of-way or on private property, giving businesses a convenient way to offer bicycle parking for customers and visitors. Business owners or property managers who lack bicycle parking near their shop or office can apply to receive a bike rack provided and installed at no cost.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The city provides and installs inverted-U style bike racks at no cost to the applicant. Racks are for public use and can be used by anyone at any time. Racks may be placed in public rights-of-way or on private property (with a signed agreement). Each rack requires a 72" x 24" parking space, and sidewalk installations must maintain at least a five-foot clear walkway. Applications are processed on a first come, first served basis.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Business owners or property managers in Rockville who want to provide bicycle parking near their shop or office.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and installation of inverted-U style bicycle racks on or near the applicant's business property.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to businesses located in the City of Rockville, Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a business owner or property manager
Business or property must lack adequate bicycle parking nearby
Location must accommodate a 72" x 24" parking space per rack
If installed along a sidewalk or pedestrian path, at least a five-foot clear walkway must remain after installation
Private property installations require a signed agreement with the City
If applicant is not the property owner, property owner permission is required for private property installation
Applicant serves as liaison between the City and property owner
Installation must meet City's Bicycle Parking Guidelines
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download the application form, complete it with business details and location description, and include a photo of the proposed location if possible. Submit by email to bikeways@rockvillemd.gov or by mail to City of Rockville Bike Rack Grant Program, c/o Bryan Barnett-Woods, Rockville City Hall, 111 Maryland Ave., Rockville, MD 20850. The application is also available online at rockvillemd.gov/apply-for-a-bike-rack-grant/.

structured_extraction.program_name: Capital Area Solar Switch Together Co-op (City of Rockville)
structured_extraction.program_description: A cooperative purchase program that makes installing rooftop solar easier and more affordable for homeowners and small businesses. By joining together as a group, participants get a price roughly 20% lower than the standard market rate. Battery storage and electric vehicle charger options are also available. Joining the contact list does not commit you to a purchase — after roof evaluations, you receive an individual proposal and decide whether to sign a contract.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Group buying power typically secures solar installation prices about 20% below the going rate. Leasing and financing options are available for all income levels. Low- to moderate-income households may also qualify for the Maryland Solar Access Grant Program, which offers up to $7,500 per system.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Rockville homeowners and small business owners interested in installing rooftop solar
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of rooftop solar panels; optional battery storage and EV charger add-ons
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents and small businesses in the Rockville, Maryland area (Capital Area region)
requirements_list: Must have a suitable roof for solar installation
Sign up for contact list to begin the process
Roof evaluation required before receiving an individual proposal
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Sign up for the contact list at solarswitch.com. A roof evaluation is conducted to determine suitability. Members then receive an individual proposal and choose whether to sign a contract with the selected installer. The decision due date is Aug. 19.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal grant program providing funding for capital and physical improvements in low- and moderate-income communities in the City of Rockville. FY 2027 (Year 52) prioritizes capital and physical improvements, excluding public services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal CDBG funds are awarded as grants to eligible organizations for housing and community development projects. FY 2025 total allocation was $263,000. FY 2027 grants will fund projects running July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027. Eligible activities include homeowner rehabilitation and reconstruction, land acquisition and clearance for housing development, rental housing acquisition and rehabilitation, direct homeownership assistance (down payment and closing costs), housing for homeless/formerly homeless individuals, public facility improvements (neighborhood/community facilities, accessibility improvements), economic development, and historic preservation. Public services (social services) activities are NOT funded in FY 2027.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations (with 501(c)(3) designation, or that have applied and must receive it by July 1, 2026) and government/quasi-governmental agencies proposing housing and community development projects that benefit low- and moderate-income households or neighborhoods in Rockville, MD. For-profit entities are not eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital and physical improvements benefiting low- and moderate-income households or neighborhoods, including homeowner rehabilitation and reconstruction, land acquisition and clearance for housing development, rental housing acquisition and rehabilitation, direct homeownership assistance, housing for homeless/formerly homeless individuals, public facility improvements, economic development activities, and historic preservation. Public services are excluded in FY 2027.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in or serve residents of the City of Rockville, Maryland.
requirements_list: Project must benefit low- and moderate-income households or neighborhoods
Organization must be a non-profit with 501(c)(3) IRS designation, or have applied and receive designation by July 1, 2026
Government and quasi-governmental agencies are eligible, preferably in partnership with local nonprofits
For-profit entities are NOT eligible
Organization must meet HUD eligibility requirements as outlined in the FY 2027 guidelines
Complete Eligibility Form through the online grant portal to confirm qualification
Applications must be submitted by October 17, 2025 at 5:00 PM
Public services (social services) activities are not funded in FY 2027
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Download and review the FY 2027 guidelines. 2. Attend one of the virtual technical sessions (Aug. 21 or Sept. 16, 2025). 3. Create an account on the online grant portal, complete the Eligibility Form, and submit the full application by Oct. 17, 2025 at 5:00 PM. 4. Optionally attend the public hearing at Rockville City Hall on Sept. 8, 2025.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program helps neighbors and community groups work together on projects that support the health, vitality, and inclusivity of Rockville neighborhoods. The City of Rockville provides competitive matching grants to groups willing to contribute cash, in-kind donations, or volunteer hours toward community-building, improvement, or livability projects. Eligible projects include building community (neighborhood association development, inclusion and diversity activities), community improvement (enhancing shared spaces, strengthening community identity), and livability initiatives (education and outreach to increase safety, address neighborhood challenges, serve low-income residents, or welcome newcomers).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive matching grants typically ranging from $500 to $1,000. Applicants must match the grant amount through cash, in-kind donations, or volunteer hours. In-kind donations can include volunteer hours (valued at $29.95/hour), donated professional services, and donated materials. Total Cash Matching Funds plus In-Kind Donations must equal or exceed the Empowerment Funds requested. All grant funds are subject to taxes and must be used by December 14, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Neighborhood associations, civic associations, homeowners associations, community groups, groups of neighbors, and student groups who live within Rockville city limits.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Building community (neighborhood association development, inclusion and diversity activities); community improvement projects (enhancing shared spaces, strengthening community identity); and livability initiatives (education and outreach to increase safety, address neighborhood challenges, serve low-income residents, or welcome newcomers).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must benefit people who live within Rockville city limits.
requirements_list: Group must have at least three members
One individual must be designated to manage grant contracts and funds
If applying on behalf of an established organization, applicants must provide documentation of authorization
Applicant must match funding through cash, in-kind donations, or volunteer hours
Total Cash Matching Funds plus In-Kind Donations must equal or exceed Empowerment Funds requested
Volunteer hours must be detailed with specific contributor information
Volunteer labor valued at $29.95 per hour
All funds are subject to taxes
Unused funds must be returned to the City of Rockville by Dec. 18, 2026
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Download and complete the budget worksheet (PDF). 2. Create an account on the online grant portal at grantinterface.com. 3. Complete the Eligibility Form and full application; submit by 11:59 p.m. on Dec. 5, 2025. 4. Award notifications sent by Feb. 13, 2026. 5. After project completion, submit receipts, at least two visual items, and a brief project report through the online grant portal by Dec. 18, 2026. 6. Return any unused funds to the City of Rockville by Dec. 18, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides personalized services to Rockville seniors in need, including resource referrals, emergency financial information, home and hospital visits, counseling resources, notary services, and financial aid for qualified residents to access recreational classes and membership.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial aid to qualified candidates for recreational classes and membership, plus resource referrals, emergency financial information, counseling resources, and notary services.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Rockville senior residents in need of financial or community resource assistance.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Recreational classes and membership fees; emergency financial needs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Rockville, MD.
requirements_list: Must be a Rockville resident
Must qualify based on need
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 240-314-8816 or 240-314-8817 for more information. A Spanish speaker is available if needed.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Services and Enrichment Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Rockville provides annual grants to local nonprofit organizations that partner with the city to deliver community services and enrichment programs benefiting Rockville residents and visitors. This program combines the former Human Services Nonprofit Grant and Community Organization Grant Programs into a single, streamlined grant program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual grants totaling approximately $1.5 million distributed across roughly 40 recipient organizations. Grants are reimbursed quarterly based on submitted invoices and documentation. Eligible expenses include personnel (salaries, wages, benefits, payroll taxes), consultants/contract services, occupancy (rent, utilities, maintenance), consumable supplies, transportation/travel, liability insurance, equipment rental/lease, and direct program costs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit 501(c)(3) organizations that provide human services or community enrichment programs to individuals residing within the corporate city limits of Rockville, MD, including low-income residents, elderly/disabled individuals, homeless/at-risk populations, non-English speakers, families, youth, and mental health clients.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supporting community services and enrichment programs that benefit Rockville residents and visitors. Eligible expenses include personnel costs, consultants/contract services, occupancy, consumable supplies, transportation/travel, liability insurance, equipment rental/lease, and direct program costs across service areas including home care, food distribution, health clinics, ESL/citizenship classes, mental health counseling, parenting education, emergency and permanent shelter services, youth development, and therapeutic recreation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must serve individuals residing within the corporate city limits of Rockville, Maryland. Applicants can verify addresses using the Rockville Address and Residency Check map. Services may also be available to Montgomery County residents in some program areas.
requirements_list: Must be a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization
Must provide human services or community enrichment programs
Programs must serve individuals residing within the corporate city limits of Rockville
Staff member must attend mandatory technical assistance session
Must submit audit, financial statement, or compilation for most recent completed operating year
Must submit IRS Form 990 for most recent completed operating year
Must submit board roster identifying officers, term limits, addresses, and phone numbers
Must submit report from the last formal and/or informal evaluation of the program (if applicable)
Must submit document of application submission authority signed by executive director and board president
Must submit Budget, Outputs, and Outcomes Worksheet
Must provide supporting documentation with invoices for quarterly reimbursements
Must meet quarterly reporting deadlines
Must reply to City communications within 10 weekdays
Must comply with HIPAA regulations (if healthcare provider) or obtain client consent for address disclosure
Must track and report specific outputs and outcomes by service area
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review eligibility requirements and take the eligibility quiz. Register for and attend one of the four virtual technical sessions. Create an account in the online grant portal at grantinterface.com, complete the Eligibility Form to confirm eligibility, fill out the application, and submit by 11:59 p.m. on October 17, 2025. Upload all required supporting documents through the portal.

structured_extraction.program_description: Community solar allows anyone with an electric bill to access the benefits of solar energy without installing panels on their own property. Photovoltaic systems are located elsewhere in the community (fields, buildings, parking lots, etc.) and subscribers receive the benefits of that solar electricity on their electric bill. Discounted income-eligible programs are available.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Subscribers receive credits on their electric bill from shared solar installations located in the community. Discounted income-eligible programs are available in the Pepco service territory.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Renters, apartment dwellers, or anyone who cannot install solar panels at their location but wants to access solar energy
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of electric bills through subscription to offsite solar energy
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to subscribers within the Pepco electric service territory in Maryland
requirements_list: Must have an active electric bill
No roof required — open to renters and apartment residents
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit Maryland Solar United Neighbors website for information on community solar opportunities in the Pepco service territory and sign up for a subscription.

structured_extraction.program_name: Eat Fresh Rockville SNAP/EBT FMNP-WIC Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides a weekly matching benefit of up to $15 for shoppers who use federal nutrition benefits (SNAP/EBT, P-EBT, or FMNP-WIC checks) at the Rockville Farmers Market. Shoppers receive free matching Maryland Market Money tokens to spend on locally grown fruits, vegetables, meat, cheese, and dairy at the market.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Shoppers receive a 1-to-1 match of up to $15 in free Maryland Market Money tokens when they use SNAP/EBT or P-EBT cards at the market information tent. FMNP-WIC check users can bring their purchase receipt to the information tent to receive free matching tokens. Matching funds are provided once per customer per market day, while funds last.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents who receive SNAP/EBT, P-EBT, or FMNP-WIC nutrition benefits and shop at the Rockville Farmers Market.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase locally grown fruits, vegetables, meat, cheese, and dairy at the Rockville Farmers Market.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at the Rockville Farmers Market, located at the corner of Route 28 and Monroe Street, Rockville, MD 20850, on Saturdays from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m.
requirements_list: Must hold a SNAP/EBT, P-EBT, or FMNP-WIC benefit
Must visit the Rockville Farmers Market during the 2025 season
Matching funds are given once per customer per market day
Subject to fund availability
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Bring your SNAP/EBT or P-EBT card (or FMNP-WIC checks) to the Rockville Farmers Market and visit the Maryland Market Money information tent near the market entrance, open Saturdays from 8:45 a.m. to 12:15 p.m. Staff will process your card or receipt and provide matching tokens.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Rockville gives away trees to residents as part of an annual fall event to support environmental sustainability and tree canopy goals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free trees are given away to participants at an annual fall event held in Rockville, MD.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Rockville residents interested in receiving free trees
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planting trees on residential or eligible properties
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Rockville, Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Sign up for the Environment and Sustainability Newsletter to receive updates on the next event.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Flood Mitigation Assistance Program (FMAP) provides matching reimbursement funds to residents and property owners in Rockville who have made or plan to make improvements to their properties to reduce future flood damage. The City of Rockville partners with the Chesapeake Bay Trust to administer the program. Funds are distributed on a first-come, first-served basis.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program reimburses up to 50% of the total cost of approved flood mitigation improvements, with a maximum reimbursement of $5,000 per property. Approved measures include gutter maintenance, downspout redirection, drainage improvements (French drains, surface grading), flood stoppage equipment, protective flood walls, window/door flood protection, basement protection, sump pumps, utility protection, and other approved Best Management Practices (BMPs). Itemized receipts or invoices are required. Funds are distributed on a first-come, first-served basis.
structured_extraction.program_audience: City of Rockville homeowners and residential property owners seeking to reduce future flood damage on their properties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Flood-proofing and stormwater management improvements including: gutter/downspout maintenance, drainage systems, French drains, surface grading, protective flood walls, window/door flood protection, basement protection, foundation waterproofing, sump pumps, flood alert systems, utility protection, and other approved flood mitigation Best Management Practices (BMPs).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents and property owners within the City of Rockville, Maryland. Properties within locally designated historic districts may have additional requirements.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a City of Rockville resident or property owner
Only approved flood mitigation measures will be reimbursed
Itemized receipts or invoices required for reimbursement
Projects must be completed before reimbursement is issued
Obtain proper permits as applicable (Sediment Control Permit, PWK permit, Forest Conservation Easement compliance, Historic District Commission approval)
Use licensed and insured contractors
Follow Best Management Practices guidelines
Check local building codes before starting
Hire licensed professionals for electrical and plumbing work
Funds distributed on a first-come, first-served basis
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online through the Chesapeake Bay Trust application portal at cbtrust.org. The Chesapeake Bay Trust reviews and processes all applications and is available to answer questions. Additional details are available at rockvillemd.gov/apply-for-flood-mitigation-assistance/.

structured_extraction.program_description: An amendment to the Montgomery County Heritage Area Management Plan allowing City of Rockville participation in the Maryland Heritage Areas Authority program. Focuses on heritage tourism through preservation and interpretation of historic, cultural, and natural resources, based on three heritage themes: Farming, Underground Railroad and Quaker culture, and Technological advances. Offers grants, tax incentives, and capital improvement support for historic preservation, heritage tourism, and cultural programming activities in the city.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Capital grants up to 50% of project cost (up to $100,000); non-capital grants for exhibits and educational products (up to $50,000); grant match can include 25% in-kind contributions. Bonding authority of $5,000,000 minimum. Sustainable Communities Rehabilitation Tax Credit eligibility for rehabilitation of historic buildings. Funding supports acquisition, development, preservation, restoration, educational and interpretive programming, ADA accessibility improvements, streetscape enhancements, trail systems, historic structure rehabilitation, signage/wayfinding, cemetery restoration, and tourism amenities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners, businesses, non-profit organizations, government entities, educational institutions, and community groups in Rockville interested in historic preservation, heritage tourism, and cultural programming. Also serves local residents, heritage travelers, and visitors.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Preservation and adaptive reuse of historic buildings; conservation of natural areas; heritage education and interpretive programming; tourism amenities (hotels, restaurants, transportation); public exhibits and educational products; ADA accessibility improvements; sidewalks and pathways; park signage; historic structure repairs; trail system development; streetscape improvements; unified wayfinding signage; cemetery restoration; capital projects for historic sites and parks; marketing and promotional materials; community engagement activities; festivals and events; historic walking/cycling/driving tours; museum exhibits.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available within the City of Rockville, which participates in the Montgomery County Heritage Area (Certified Heritage Area). Designated historic districts include Courthouse Square, South Washington Street, W. Montgomery, Rockville Heights, Rockville Park, King Farm Farmstead Park, Glenview Farm, Rose Hill Farm, and Dawson Farmhouses.
requirements_list: Must be located within the City of Rockville (part of the Montgomery County Heritage Area)
Projects must relate to acquisition, development, public interpretation, programming, or rehabilitation of eligible buildings
Certified Local Government status required for certain funding
Multi-year programming planning for historic districts
Community and business support for projects
Grant match requirement (up to 25% may be in-kind contributions)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications through the Maryland Heritage Areas Authority, Montgomery County Heritage Area, or City of Rockville Historic Preservation Division. Contact the Historic Preservation Division for information on applying.

structured_extraction.program_description: Rockville's Historic District Designation program allows property owners and community members to nominate properties for recognition as local historic districts. Designation preserves a property's historic character, places higher standards on maintenance and alterations, and can provide financial benefits to the owner. Designated properties may also become eligible for historic preservation tax credits.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides official historic district designation and zoning recognition (HD zone), which can offer financial benefits to property owners including potential eligibility for historic preservation tax credits administered by the Maryland Historical Trust. The designation also provides regulatory protections for the historic character of the property. Properties can be nominated by owners or third parties with certified notification to the owner.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications must be submitted five weeks preceding a regularly scheduled HDC meeting; meeting schedule available online.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners and third parties interested in historic preservation who wish to nominate properties in Rockville for local historic district designation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable — this is a designation process rather than a direct funding program. Designation may unlock eligibility for historic preservation tax credits.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only for properties located within the City of Rockville, Maryland.
requirements_list: Property must be located within the City of Rockville.
Property must meet at least one of nine adopted criteria related to historic or architectural significance.
Property must have sufficient integrity to convey its historic significance (location, design, setting, materials, workmanship, feeling, and/or association).
Nomination must be submitted using the Historic District Designation Nomination Form.
Applications must be submitted online.
Property inspection access must be granted to staff.
Applicant or representative must attend the public hearing.
For third-party nominations: certified letter notification to owner required with USPS receipt.
Public notice yard sign must be posted 2 weeks prior to the HDC meeting.
Compliance with City of Rockville Zoning Ordinance Section 25.14.01.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Consult with historic preservation staff. 2. Submit a complete Historic District Designation Nomination Form online at least five weeks before a scheduled HDC meeting. 3. Staff analyzes the property for eligibility, inspects the property, and makes a recommendation; the Historic District Commission (HDC) holds a public hearing on the third Thursday of the month at 7:00 p.m. 4. Applicant presents and responds to HDC questions; HDC makes a decision. 5. If eligible, the HDC authorizes filing a Sectional Map Amendment and recommends it to the Planning Commission. 6. The Planning Commission reviews and makes a recommendation to the Mayor and Council. 7. The Mayor and Council hold a public hearing and vote on an ordinance to adopt the map amendment. 8. If adopted, the Zoning Map is updated to reflect the HD (Historic District) designation. HDC decisions may be appealed to Circuit Court.

structured_extraction.program_description: HEAP provides one-time financial assistance up to $1,000 to eligible Rockville residents who live in housing with documented energy inefficiencies. The program helps residents access weatherization services, home energy assessments, and energy audits, and covers costs for energy-efficient upgrades like insulation, lighting retrofits, and health and safety repairs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time financial assistance of up to $1,000 to cover energy-efficient upgrades such as insulation, hot water system improvements, lighting retrofits, furnace repairs, and health and safety items including mold remediation, radon mitigation, and roof repair. May also cover appliance replacement and addressing electrical hazards. Funds cannot be used for past-due utility bills or non-energy-efficient household repairs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income Rockville residents, including seniors (60+) and households with children, who meet 60% of Area Median Income (AMI) guidelines, are current or past Emergency Assistance Program recipients, use electricity or natural gas for energy and heating, and have already been approved for a qualifying energy assistance program such as MEAP, EmPOWER Maryland LIEEP, or the Weatherization Assistance Program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy-efficient home upgrades including insulation, air infiltration reduction, hot water system improvements, lighting retrofits, furnace cleaning and repairs, refrigerator retrofit, appliance repairs and replacement, and health and safety items such as mold remediation, asbestos abatement, smoke and carbon monoxide detector installation, radon mitigation, roof repair, plumbing and electrical repair, structural repair, removal of lead hazards, and approved electrical repairs. Also covers utility bill assistance and home energy audits.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must reside within Rockville city limits at the time of application and for at least six months (180 days) prior. Applicants may own their home or rent.
requirements_list: Must reside within Rockville city limits at time of application and for at least six months (180 days) prior
Must meet 60% AMI income guidelines (maximum annual household income: $24,280 for 1-person up to $58,840 for 5-person household, based on 2018 rates)
Must be a current or previous Emergency Assistance Program recipient
Must use electricity or natural gas for energy and heating
Must be a PEPCO, BGE, or Potomac Edison customer
Must have already been approved for MEAP, EmPOWER Maryland LIEEP, WAP, or Enhanced Weatherization Program
Must provide photo ID and proof of residency
Must provide Social Security documentation
Must provide income verification (paystubs, tax returns, or affidavit)
Must provide proof of home ownership or lease
Must provide documentation of three months of utility bills
Must provide documentation of a comprehensive home energy audit
Renters must provide landlord or property manager approval for energy-efficient retrofits
Must agree to reside at the property for one year after retrofits are completed
Must provide documentation of three months of utility bills post-retrofit
Property must be applicant's primary residence
Must demonstrate previous rent payments have been made for the property
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Initial intake with staff member; referral to HEAP counselor; submission of required documentation including income verification, proof of residency, utility bills, and completed home energy audit; application approval or denial; payment issued to contractor or payee. Download and complete the application form from the program page and return to the Community Services Division at hcd@rockvillemd.gov.

structured_extraction.program_name: Homeowners' Property Tax Credit Program (City of Rockville Supplemental Credit)
structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Rockville offers a supplemental property tax credit on top of the State of Maryland's Homeowners' Property Tax Credit Program. It provides real property tax relief to low- and moderate-income Rockville residents on their principal residence.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Households with gross incomes up to $91,000 per year and a net worth under $200,000 (excluding the home's value and qualified retirement savings) may qualify for a tax credit on the first $495,000 of their home's assessed value. For low-income households, the credit can be several hundred dollars, up to a maximum equal to the total city tax due on the first $495,000 of assessed value.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low- and moderate-income Rockville homeowners who use the property as their principal residence
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of city real property taxes on the homeowner's principal residence
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only to residents of the City of Rockville, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a resident of the City of Rockville
Property must be the applicant's principal residence
Household gross income must be $91,000 or less per year
Household net worth must be less than $200,000, not including the value of the home or qualified retirement savings
Must qualify under the State of Maryland's Homeowners' Property Tax Credit Program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation for more information on how to apply.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program promotes positive activities, physical exercise, and academic support for Latino male students in middle and high school in Rockville. Students can participate in soccer leagues, field trips, life skills workshops, and earn Student Service Learning (SSL) hours. Case management is also available for students' families.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides youth development services including soccer league participation, academic guidance, life skills workshops, SSL opportunities, field trips, and college tour visits. Transportation is provided to stops within the City of Rockville. Case management is available for families.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Latino male students in grades 6–12 who attend Earle B. Wood or Julius West middle schools, or Richard Montgomery or Rockville high schools, and are enrolled in the Free and Reduced-price Meals (FARMS) program for low-income families.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Youth development services including soccer leagues, academic tutoring, life skills workshops, field trips, college tours, SSL hours, and family case management.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Students must attend schools within the City of Rockville, MD. Transportation provided to stops within the City of Rockville.
requirements_list: Must be a Latino male student in grades 6–12
Must be enrolled in the Free and Reduced-price Meals (FARMS) Program
Must attend Earle B. Wood or Julius West middle school, or Richard Montgomery or Rockville High School
Must attend weekly meetings after school
Must attend weekly practices
Must attend all weekend games
Must attend all field trips
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Students may be referred by a school counselor or administrator, or may self-refer by submitting the Student Referral Form available on the program page.

structured_extraction.program_description: A school-based program that provides accessible services to at-risk children and their families to improve school adjustment and performance. Services include health care, mental health counseling, social services, educational support, after-school and summer programming, parenting workshops, and assistance with food, utility, and housing problems.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: School-based services delivered at Maryvale Elementary School in partnership with Sheppard Pratt. Services include mental health counseling, after-school and summer programming, academic mentoring, therapeutic recreation, parenting and nutrition workshops, and help with food, utility, and housing problems as well as assistance completing financial and medical assistance forms.
structured_extraction.program_audience: At-risk children and their families, particularly those attending Maryvale Elementary School in Rockville, MD
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Support for school adjustment, individual and family counseling, after-school and summer programming, parenting and nutrition workshops, and assistance with food, utility, housing, and financial aid forms
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is located at Maryvale Elementary School, 1010 First St., Rockville, MD 20850
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Fadeke Adepoju at the Housing and Community Development Department, Community Services Division, Monday–Friday 8:30 a.m.–5 p.m.

structured_extraction.program_name: Moderately Priced Dwelling Unit (MPDU) Homeownership Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Rockville requires some for-sale properties to be made available to eligible residents at below-market prices through its Moderately Priced Dwelling Unit (MPDU) Program. First-time homebuyers who meet income and eligibility requirements can purchase these income-restricted homes at affordable prices set by the city, based on area median income (AMI) levels of 50%, 60%, or 80%. Eligible households are placed on a waiting list until a unit becomes available. Non-U.S. citizens may apply. Buyers must commit to owning the home as a primary residence for 30 years, and any sale before that period must follow city resale guidelines.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible first-time homebuyers can purchase a moderately priced dwelling unit (MPDU) at a below-market price. Homes are offered at prices set by the city, based on area median income (AMI) levels of 50%, 60%, or 80%. Buyers must commit to owning the home as a primary residence for 30 years. If selling before 30 years, the resale price is determined by the city and the home is first offered to Rockville Housing Enterprises, then to others on the waiting list. Improvement credits of up to 10% of the original MPDU purchase price may be applied toward the resale price calculation for permanent improvements made during the control period.
structured_extraction.program_audience: First-time homebuyers who live or work in Rockville, MD, who meet income limits and can qualify for bank financing of at least $150,000. Non-U.S. citizens may apply. Priority is given to current Rockville residents or workers, households with members over 55, and larger households. Also relevant to MPDU owners planning to resell or refinance during the 30-year control period.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of a moderately priced for-sale home in the City of Rockville as a primary residence. May also be used in connection with resale or refinance of an MPDU during the 30-year control period.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents and workers in the City of Rockville, Maryland. Priority is given to current Rockville residents or workers, households with members over 55, and larger households. Properties must use public water and sewerage.
requirements_list: Must be a first-time homebuyer with no home ownership in past 5 years
Must qualify for a minimum mortgage of $150,000
Must qualify for bank financing
Home must be primary residence for the full 30-year MPDU period
Must commit to owning the home for 30 years; any sale before that must follow city resale guidelines
Cannot own a second home while owning an MPDU
All household members over 18 must submit proof of income
Household gross income must be within the applicable AMI limits at the time of contract signing
Must complete a HUD-approved First-Time Homebuyer Class and obtain a completion certificate
Must obtain a mortgage pre-approval letter (on company letterhead, notarized, valid for one year, with 30-year loan term)
Pre-qualification letter must disclose all household income sources (no exceptions) and include credit approval and income verification
Must apply for and receive a Certificate of Eligibility (renewed every two years)
Non-U.S. citizens may apply
For resale during control period: maximum improvement credit is 10% of original purchase price; improvements must be permanent and add market value
Required documentation for improvement credits: store receipts, cancelled checks, ratified contracts, signed invoices, detailed credit card statements, and building permits where applicable
Owner labor not credited for improvements; materials and contractor costs only
Physical deterioration or neglect may reduce improvement value
For resale/refinance requests: HUD-1 settlement sheet and original documentation for improvements required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Attend a six-hour First-Time Homebuyer Class through the Housing Initiative Partnership or a HUD-approved counseling agency and get a completion certificate. 2. Obtain a mortgage pre-approval letter from your bank lender (must be on company letterhead, notarized, and valid for one year). 3. Submit the MPDU Homeownership Program Application online or request a paper copy by emailing rockvillempdu@rockvillemd.gov. 4. If eligible, a certificate is emailed within 3–4 weeks and the household is placed on the city's MPDU waiting list. 5. When an MPDU becomes available, the seller or developer contacts households on the waiting list. For resale or refinance requests: submit a written request letter indicating the purpose (resale or refinance) with supporting documentation to the MPDU Office.

structured_extraction.program_name: Moderately Priced Dwelling Unit (MPDU) Rental Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Rockville offers affordable rental housing through its Moderately Priced Dwelling Unit (MPDU) Program, enacted by ordinance in 1990. New for-sale or rental developments in Rockville with 20 or more units are required to contain a certain percentage of affordable units. Designated rental units must remain MPDUs for 30 or 99 years depending on the date of first rental. Income-eligible households can rent units at below-market, capped monthly rates at participating properties throughout the city. Units are available to households earning within established income thresholds (generally up to 60% AMI), with specific FY 2026 maximum annual income limits ranging from $68,840 (one person) to $106,210 (five people). Minimum income must be at least 2.5x the applicable MPDU monthly rent. Non-U.S. citizens may apply. Renters apply directly through the rental properties on a first come, first served basis. No Department waiting list is maintained.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible households can rent units at capped monthly rates. As of July 1, 2025, rates for buildings initially leased before 2024 range from $1,322 (studio) to $1,890 (three bedroom). For buildings initially leased in 2024 or later, rates range from $1,400 (studio) to $1,999 (three bedroom). Rates are recalculated each June. Housing Choice Vouchers issued by Rockville Housing Enterprises (or ported in from other agencies) may also be applied toward rent. Eligibility is based on household income as a percentage of the area median income (AMI), generally up to 60% AMI. Renting is a private transaction on a first come, first served basis; no Department waiting list is maintained.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Income-eligible individuals and households seeking affordable rental housing in Rockville, MD, including non-U.S. citizens. Maximum annual household income limits for FY 2026 range from $68,840 (one person) to $106,210 (five people). Minimum income is 2.5x the applicable MPDU rent. Priority is given during a 90-day offering period to persons living or working within Rockville corporate boundaries or over age 55.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment of monthly rent on an MPDU-designated rental unit in Rockville at below-market, capped rates.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only within the City of Rockville, Maryland corporate boundaries, at participating MPDU properties.
requirements_list: Household gross annual income must be below current maximum rental income limits based on household size (e.g., $68,840 for one person, $98,340 for four people, $106,210 for five people)
Minimum household income must be at least 2.5x the applicable MPDU monthly rent (adjusted for bedroom count)
Unit must be household's primary place of residence; no subletting without written permission from HCD
No current residential property ownership and no residential property ownership within past 5 years
Annual income and household composition re-certification required within 30 days
Must vacate within 180 days if household income exceeds MPDU eligibility limits
Failure to re-certify results in 60-day notice to vacate
Family/household size determined by dependents claimed on submitted federal tax forms; legal custody documentation required for dependents
Student income counts toward household income
Appropriate bedroom size based on household size
Submit most recent federal tax returns and W-2s for all adults
Submit most recent pay stubs for all adults
Submit six-month bank statement
Complete MPDU Rental Application Form
Complete MPDU Renter's Agreement and MPDU Lease Addendum
Housing Choice Vouchers must be issued by or ported into Rockville Housing Enterprises to be used in Rockville
Non-U.S. citizens may apply
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must apply directly through the rental properties that have available MPDU units on a first come, first served basis. A list and map of available units is provided on the City of Rockville website. To apply, complete the MPDU Rental Application Form, sign the MPDU Renter's Agreement (renter completes Section 1; leasing agent completes Sections 2-3; copy sent to MPDU Office), and sign the MPDU Lease Addendum. Submit income documentation including federal tax returns, recent pay stubs, six-month bank statement, and household composition documentation. Annual re-certification is required. Contact individual MPDU properties directly for availability, eligibility, and application information.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Chesapeake Bay Trust, in partnership with the City of Rockville, provides grants to nonprofit organizations for projects within Rockville city limits that reduce stormwater pollution and protect natural resources. Eligible projects include permeable pavers and pavements, native landscaping, large-scale tree plantings, community outreach and engagement to reduce pollution, and environmental and sustainability projects that benefit underserved communities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants for stormwater pollution reduction and natural resource protection projects within Rockville city limits.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations with projects located within the City of Rockville.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Permeable pavers and pavements, native landscaping, large-scale tree plantings, community outreach and engagement to reduce pollution, and environmental and sustainability projects that assist or benefit underserved communities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located within the City of Rockville, Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a nonprofit organization
Project must be located within Rockville city limits
Project must reduce stormwater pollution or protect natural resources
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Chesapeake Bay Trust website at cbtrust.org/grants/outreach-and-restoration/.

structured_extraction.program_name: Publicly Accessible Art in Private Development Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Requires most private development projects in the City of Rockville to include an expenditure for a publicly accessible art project. Developers must choose from multiple compliance options: contribute to the Art in Public Places Program, install or present art on-site, provide arts space, provide arts-based infrastructure, or donate to eligible arts organizations. The goal is to incorporate public art into private development to preserve community character, improve quality of life, and support economic vitality.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Developers must fulfill public art requirements through one or more of the following compliance options: (1) Install or present art on-site, (2) Contribute to the City's Art in Public Places Program, (3) Provide arts space or arts-based infrastructure, or (4) Make a monetary donation to the Friends of the Arts Fund or an eligible arts organization. Required contributions are calculated based on project type, dwelling units, or square footage per an annually adjusted fee schedule. MPDU (Moderately Priced Dwelling Units) are excluded from the calculation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private developers undertaking residential, commercial, or industrial development projects within the City of Rockville that are subject to the AIPD Ordinance and seeking land use approvals
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Artist and consultant fees, freight, shipping, fabrication, installation of publicly accessible art, purchase and installation of arts-based infrastructure, construction costs associated with arts space, arts commissioning, and art presentation programs
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located within the City of Rockville, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a private development project located within the City of Rockville
Project must include residential units (single-family, townhouse, or multi-family), commercial space, or industrial construction
Project must meet the criteria outlined in the ordinance (some projects are exempt)
MPDU (Moderately Priced Dwelling Units) are excluded from the contribution calculation
Mandatory contribution based on tiered fee schedule per dwelling unit or square footage
Developers must attend meetings with Arts and Culture Program staff at specific project milestones
Artwork must be permanently installed and lasting at least 30 years with regular maintenance
Artist contract must comply with the Visual Arts Act of 1990
Artist must provide comprehensive documentation
Eligible arts organizations must have 501(c)3 status, primary office in City of Rockville, and offer more than half of programs/services in the city
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review the ordinance, implementation manual, and guidelines to determine eligibility and compliance options. Submit completed application with site plan reference, project details, unit/footage counts, calculated fees, selected compliance options, and required attachments per the AIPD Implementation Manual.

structured_extraction.program_description: A youth mentoring program in Rockville that pairs trained adult mentors and student volunteers with school-aged children for one-on-one academic and recreational support. Mentors meet with students weekly after school (Monday–Thursday) to help with homework, build math and reading skills, and provide social and emotional support. The program runs during the school year from October to June and includes a five-week summer camp.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free mentoring services for children, including one-on-one academic tutoring, homework help, recreational activities, healthy snacks, and social-emotional support during weekly one-hour sessions. Mentors (adult volunteers and student volunteers aged 16+) meet with mentees after school Monday–Thursday. A five-week summer camp with enrichment and recreation is also included.
structured_extraction.program_audience: School-aged children in Rockville schools and adult or student volunteers (minimum age 16) who want to serve as mentors.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Mentoring services for children: academic support, skill building, recreational activities, and social-emotional development.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in the City of Rockville, Maryland, at designated Rockville school locations.
requirements_list: Mentors must be at least 16 years old
Mentors must like children and be patient, kind, responsible, consistent, and respectful
Mentors must commit to weekly one-hour sessions from October to June, meeting after school Monday–Thursday
Mentors must undergo a criminal background check
Mentors must undergo a child welfare check
Mentors must provide fingerprints
Adult mentors must provide three character references (one must be from an employer/supervisor if employed)
Student volunteer mentors must provide two character references (one must be a teacher or counselor)
Mentors must complete Montgomery County Public Schools child neglect and abuse online training (for those 18 and older)
Mentors must meet with students at a set location at the same day and time each week
Mentors must observe established program boundaries and model positive behaviors
Criminal history disclosure required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the appropriate mentor application form (Adult Volunteer or Student Volunteer). Submit the completed application with references by email to Cecil Rucker at crucker@rockvillemd.gov. Applicants must also undergo background checks (criminal and child welfare), fingerprinting, and character reference verification. The program coordinator reviews the application and references before approval.
