structured_extraction.program_description: Through a partnership with the Chesapeake Bay Trust, the RainScapes Rebate Program provides funds to eligible properties in Rockville for installing small-scale stormwater management projects — such as rain gardens, rain barrels, conservation landscaping, and permeable pavers — to reduce polluted runoff, prevent flooding, and improve local waterways and the Chesapeake Bay. The program also covers pavement removal, cisterns, tree canopy planting, and green roofs, with rebates available up to a lifetime maximum of $5,000 per property.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible applicants can receive up to a lifetime maximum of $5,000 in rebates per property. Rebate amounts vary by project type: Conservation Landscaping — $6/sq ft with soil improvement, $5/sq ft without; Rain Garden — $10/sq ft; Pavement Removal — $6/sq ft (replacing with conservation landscaping) or $3/sq ft (replacing with sod); Rain Barrel — $1/gallon; Cistern — $1/gallon; Tree Canopy — $150/tree; Permeable Paver Retrofit — $14/sq ft; Green Roof — $9/sq ft.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Detached homes, townhomes, homeowners associations, condominium associations, religious institutions/places of worship, private schools, nonprofits, and multifamily properties in the City of Rockville.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installing stormwater management projects including conservation landscaping, native plantings, rain gardens, pavement removal, rain barrels, cisterns, tree canopy planting, permeable paver retrofits, green roofs, swales, cross drains, retaining walls, and terracing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a property located within the City of Rockville, Maryland. Specific watersheds within city limits include Rock Creek Watershed, Watts Branch Watershed, Twinbrook area, King Farm, and West End.
requirements_list: Property must be located within the City of Rockville

Eligible property types include detached homes, townhomes, homeowners associations, condominium associations, religious institutions/places of worship, private schools, nonprofits, and multifamily properties
Lifetime maximum rebate of $5,000 per property
Must replace lawn area or install qualifying stormwater management improvements
Seek technical assistance from licensed professional engineer or landscape architect before implementation
Check with City to determine if permits are necessary before beginning work
Some techniques require permits or permission when working in right-of-way or on City easement
Must comply with applicable federal, state, and local regulations
Call 811 or 1-800-257-7777 before digging
Conduct infiltration testing for rain gardens (48-hour drainage requirement)
Maintain minimum 10 feet distance from house; 40 feet from septic systems for rain gardens
Consult professionals for certain installations (underground tanks, large cisterns, retaining walls, terraces)
Use licensed qualified professionals for retaining walls and terraces
Obtain necessary permits and follow manufacturer maintenance recommendations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online through the City of Rockville website (rockvillemd.gov/apply-for-a-rainscapes-rebate) or through the Chesapeake Bay Trust portal at cbtrust.org/grants/rockville-rainscapes-rebate. The Chesapeake Bay Trust reviews and processes applications and performs site visits. Free educational workshops are also available — contact the City of Rockville for more information and permitting assistance.

structured_extraction.program_description: Financial assistance is available to qualified candidates for reduced rates and other discounts on City of Rockville recreation programs, including after school programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Qualified candidates receive reduced rates and other discounts on recreation program fees.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualified individuals seeking financial assistance for City of Rockville recreation programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduced fees for after school and other recreation programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in the City of Rockville, Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_name: Reduced Price Memberships at Rockville Swim and Fitness Center
structured_extraction.program_description: Discounted annual membership program providing reduced-rate daily admission to the swim and fitness center for eligible low-income residents of the City of Rockville.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Individual membership $15/year with $1.00 adult daily admission and $0.50 child daily admission; Family membership $25/year with same daily rates. Eligible low-income Rockville residents receive reduced-price memberships to the Rockville Swim and Fitness Center. Membership cannot be purchased until the application is approved.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduced-price memberships providing access to swim and fitness center facilities

Must meet prescribed income guidelines
Proof of residency required (water bill, tax bill, or state-issued photo ID)
Eligibility verification documentation required (TCA, SNAP, Medical Assistance, TEMHA, rental assistance, SSI, or shelter residency documentation)
Must submit an Application for Reduced Price Membership in person at the Rockville Swim and Fitness Center
State-issued ID verification for address confirmation
Must sign waiver and release form
Must be approved before purchasing a membership
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit completed Application for Reduced Price Membership in person at the Rockville Swim and Fitness Center along with required proof of residency and income eligibility documentation. Sign waiver and release form. Use the address finder at rockvillemd.gov/services to confirm Rockville residency. Applicants must be approved before purchasing a membership.

structured_extraction.program_name: Resources for Federal Employees and Contractors
structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Rockville offers delayed payment options and other assistance for federal employees and contractors who live in Rockville and are affected by the federal government shutdown. Eligible residents may defer payments with no penalties on city services including child care, water and sewer bills, rent, pet licenses, and parking permits. Food assistance is also available through local nonprofits, and a wellness and retraining program called Rise and Renew II is offered for affected residents.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Delayed payment with no penalties on city child care, water and sewer utilities, pet licenses, and rent payments. A residential parking permit fee waiver is also available. Food assistance is available through nonprofit partners. The Rise and Renew II program offers courses and resources for residents to recharge and move forward. Applicants must provide proof of Rockville residency and federal employment or contractor status.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Federal employees and contractors who live in the City of Rockville and are impacted by the federal government shutdown.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Deferred payments on child care, water and sewer bills, pet licenses, and parking permits; rent negotiation assistance; food assistance; and wellness/retraining resources.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must reside within the City of Rockville, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must reside within the City of Rockville
Must be a federal employee or federal contractor impacted by the government shutdown
Must provide proof of Rockville residency
Must provide proof of federal employment or federal contractor status (e.g., federal employee/contractor ID badge or employer letter)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the relevant city department for the specific service (child care, utility billing, REAP for rent, pet licenses, or parking permits). Provide proof of Rockville residency and federal employment or contractor status.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Rockville offers emergency financial assistance to eligible Rockville residents who need temporary help with evictions, utility shut-offs, prescription medications, medical and dental expenses, food, and other basic needs. Referrals for emergency food, clothing, financial counseling, and employment assistance are also available. The program helps families maintain stability through one-time emergency financial aid.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time emergency financial assistance for rent (eviction prevention), utility shut-offs, prescription medications, medical and dental expenses, and food. Referrals for food, clothing, financial counseling, and employment assistance are also provided. For residents over 60 needing prescription cost help under $200, a separate contact is available.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Rockville city residents in financial need, including those facing eviction, utility shut-offs, high medical costs, or other financial emergencies. Furloughed federal employees are also encouraged to apply.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rent/eviction prevention, utility bills, prescription medications, medical and dental expenses, food, and other basic needs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a current resident of the City of Rockville for at least six months.
requirements_list: Must be a current resident of the City of Rockville for at least six months

Rent assistance applicants must have a current court eviction notice (Summons to Appear for Failure to Pay Rent, Writ or Warrant of Restitution, or Final Eviction Notice from the Montgomery County Sheriff's Office)
Utility assistance applicants must have a current utility shut-off notice or already have had service disconnected
Must demonstrate financial need due to job loss, ongoing financial difficulty, loss of a family wage earner, unexpected medical bills, or another financial emergency
Must first apply for emergency assistance through Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) before receiving City of Rockville assistance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Apply for emergency assistance through Montgomery County DHHS first. 2. Montgomery County DHHS will submit a referral to the City of Rockville on behalf of eligible residents. 3. Once a referral is received, call the Housing and Community Development Department at 240-314-8300 to schedule an appointment.

structured_extraction.program_name: Rockville Housing Enterprises (RHE) Housing Voucher Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Rockville Housing Enterprises (RHE), the city's independent public housing authority, administers housing voucher programs that allow eligible residents to rent market-rate apartments at more affordable prices. As of February 28, 2025, the waitlist is closed to new applicants.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Housing vouchers that can be used to rent market-rate apartments at more affordable prices. RHE also operates several affordable rental properties throughout Rockville.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Waitlist currently closed as of Feb. 28, 2025
structured_extraction.program_audience: Income-eligible individuals and households seeking affordable rental housing in Rockville.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental housing assistance
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Rockville, Maryland
requirements_list: Must meet income eligibility requirements
Waitlist is currently closed to new applicants as of February 28, 2025
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit rockvillehe.org for more information. The waitlist is currently closed.

structured_extraction.program_name: Rockville Safe Waters: Swim Scholarship Program for Youth with Autism
structured_extraction.program_description: A scholarship program that provides financial support for inclusive swim lessons at the Rockville Swim and Fitness Center for children ages 3–10 with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) who are Rockville residents. The program honors the memory of Ace Alexander and aims to create a safe, inclusive environment for water safety instruction. Up to 10 children can receive scholarship funding per program cycle, with applications accepted on a rolling basis until all 10 scholarships are awarded.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Scholarship for one child for one class season of inclusive swim lessons at the Rockville Swim and Fitness Center. Up to 10 scholarships are available per program cycle, awarded on a rolling basis until all 10 are filled.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis until 10 scholarships are awarded
structured_extraction.program_audience: Children ages 3–10 with a confirmed ASD diagnosis who are residents of the City of Rockville and meet financial eligibility requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Inclusive swim lessons at the Rockville Swim and Fitness Center.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a resident of the City of Rockville.
requirements_list: Child must be ages 3–10 with a confirmed Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) diagnosis
Must be a resident of the City of Rockville
Must commit to attending in-person swim lessons at Rockville Swim and Fitness Center
Child must have established readiness to engage in group swim lessons
An adult must be present at the facility during lessons
Must provide proof of residency (water/sewage bill, property tax bill, or state-issued ID with Rockville address)

Must meet at least one financial requirement: award letter from MD Dept of Human Resources/Montgomery County DSS for TCA, SNAP, TEMHA, or WPA; proof of medical assistance from Montgomery County DSS; proof of rental assistance (public housing, HUD Section 8, or HOC); proof of residing in a shelter; SSI documentation; MCPS FARMS eligibility; Care for Kids; Maryland Energy Assistance Program (MEAP); Montgomery County HHS Rental Assistance Program; Maryland unemployment benefits; or WIC
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Scholarship Application form with personal information, disability description, water comfort assessment, and desired course number. Submit application by email to programaccess@rockvillemd.gov on a rolling basis. Selection is done by the Rockville Safe Waters Committee. Applications are accepted until all 10 scholarships are awarded.

structured_extraction.program_description: A financial assistance program that helps Rockville residents ages 60 and older afford senior classes, day trips, and Rockville Senior Center memberships by subsidizing half the cost. Administered by the City of Rockville Department of Recreation and Parks Senior Social Services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The participant pays half the actual cost (50% of actual cost). The program provides a maximum subsidy of $50 per quarter.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Rockville residents ages 60 and older who need financial help to participate in senior recreation programs including trips, classes, and memberships.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Senior classes, day trips, and Rockville Senior Center memberships.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a resident of the City of Rockville, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a Rockville resident
Must be age 60 or older
Proof of income required (W-2, benefit letters, pay stubs, tax forms, or family support letter)
Applicant must provide name, address, phone number, and date of birth
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Senior Assistance Fund Application (PDF available on the program page), submit with proof of income (W-2, benefit letters, pay stubs, tax forms, or family support letter); staff signature required. Contact 240-314-8810 for additional information.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides free bus-shuttle service and bus and taxi subsidies to senior residents of Rockville to help them get around the city.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free bus-shuttle service for all City of Rockville residents age 60 and older. Bus and taxi subsidies are also available to seniors living within Rockville city limits.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Rockville residents age 60 and older.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Transportation costs (bus and taxi).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must live within Rockville city limits.
requirements_list: Must be a City of Rockville resident
Must be age 60 or older
Reservation required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 240-314-8810 for more information. Reservation is required.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides no-interest, forgivable loans to low-to-moderate income homeowners in Rockville for necessary home repairs to correct code deficiencies. A lien is placed on the property and forgiven over a five-year period at 20% per year. Typical repairs include roof replacement, plumbing and electrical upgrades, furnace replacement, and kitchen and bathroom rehabilitation. Funded through the federal Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: No-interest forgivable loans up to $25,000 for home repairs. A lien is placed on the property and forgiven over five years at 20% per year. If the home is sold, rented, or transferred within five years of work completion, the homeowner must repay a percentage of the contract price, decreasing by 20% per year. Emergency repairs (heating/cooling, roof leaks, plumbing) are prioritized.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-to-moderate income homeowners residing within the City of Rockville, Maryland whose homes need code-related repairs
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Necessary home repairs to correct code deficiencies, including roof replacement, plumbing and electrical upgrades, furnace replacement, kitchen and bathroom rehabilitation, lead-based paint remediation, and emergency repairs such as heating/cooling, roof leaks, and plumbing issues
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicant must own and occupy a home within the City of Rockville, Maryland as their primary residence
requirements_list: Home must be the owner's sole and principal residence within City of Rockville limits
Owner must currently reside at the property
Owner must not own another home or condominium
Owner must not owe more than the home's assessed value (cannot be underwater on mortgage)
Total assets must not exceed $150,000 (excluding home value, retirement accounts, rental property, stocks, and bonds)
Personal and property taxes must be current
Ownership verified through property tax records and deed
Must meet HUD maximum gross income limits based on household size (e.g., $68,500 for one person, up to $129,100 for eight persons, effective May 2024)
Lead paint risk assessment required if home was built before 1978
Must provide proof of income, employment, mortgage information, homeowner's insurance documentation, and asset verification
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Complete and mail the eligibility assessment application form with personal and financial information to the City of Rockville Department of Housing and Community Development. 2. Provide supporting documents including three recent pay stubs, tax returns, mortgage statements, insurance documentation, and asset verification; sign oath/affidavit. 3. After the assessment is accepted, a rehabilitation specialist contacts the applicant to complete the eligibility review. 4. Application materials are reviewed and work is prioritized by the rehabilitation specialist; the review process takes approximately 7–10 business days.

structured_extraction.program_description: Property owners with private stormwater management facilities can apply for a credit to reduce their annual Stormwater Management Utility Fee. Credits reduce the mapped impervious surface area measurement for properties with private SWM facilities that are structurally maintained and operated by the owner, thereby reducing the number of ERUs and the fee amount. The credit is intended to offset owner's ongoing inspection and maintenance costs. Credits are available based on facility type and standards met.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: SWM Utility Fee credits reduce impervious surface area calculations and resulting fee amounts based on facility type and standards met: Quality Control (25% reduction), Quantity Control (50% reduction), and Groundwater Recharge (10% reduction). The annual fee is $159 per 2,330 square feet of impervious area (1 ERU). Credits reduce the square feet of impervious area counted, lowering the number of ERUs and the total fee charged.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Complete application must be submitted before January 1 and approved by March 1 for credit on July billing
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of private stormwater management facilities in Rockville, typically commercial property owners with significant impervious surfaces.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Fee credits reduce the annual Stormwater Management Utility Fee by offsetting inspection and maintenance costs for private SWM facilities. Credits reduce the impervious surface area calculation, lowering the number of ERUs and the total fee amount.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to property owners within the City of Rockville, Maryland, whose properties have private stormwater management facilities.
requirements_list: Must own a private stormwater management facility
Property must have impervious surfaces
SWM facility must be structurally maintained and operational
Facility must function in accordance with original design specifications
Owner must have legal ownership and maintenance responsibility for the private SWM facility
Complete application must be submitted before January 1 for credit on current year's July billing
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete the Stormwater Management Utility Fee Credit Application and submit it to the Environmental Management Division. The complete application must be submitted before January 1 and approved by March 1 for the credit to appear on the July billing cycle.

structured_extraction.program_description: A character-building program for Rockville students in grades 1–5. Children complete 6 out of 16 good deeds — such as volunteering, helping neighbors, or keeping a clean school environment — to earn a free refurbished bicycle and helmet. Participants are recognized by the Mayor and City Council.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible children receive a free refurbished bicycle and helmet upon completing the program requirements.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students in grades 1–5 who live or attend school in Rockville, Maryland. Limited to 80 participants per cycle.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free refurbished bicycle and helmet awarded to children who complete the required good deeds.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to students in Rockville, Maryland.
requirements_list: Child must be in grades 1–5
Must complete 6 out of 16 designated good deeds by April 30, 2026
Must mail completed form postmarked by April 30, 2026
Must register during the open registration window (Jan. 20 – Feb. 14, 2026)
Program is limited to 80 participants; selection notification sent in late February 2026
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register online at the City of Rockville recreation portal between January 20 and February 14, 2026. Participants are notified of selection in late February. Good deeds begin March 1, 2026, and must be completed by April 30, 2026. Awardees receive bikes at a special event on May 16, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: A scholarship program that helps Rockville youth ages 18 and younger pay for city recreation and childcare program fees by covering a portion of the cost beyond a $15 participant co-pay.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants pay $15 per program. The fund covers the remaining balance up to $100 per person per session (fall, winter, spring, summer) and $1,000 per family. For summer camp, the fund covers up to $175 per youth per camp session and up to $1,000 per child.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Rockville residents ages 18 and younger who need financial help paying for recreation programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Recreation and childcare program fees offered by the City of Rockville Recreation and Parks Department.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a resident of the City of Rockville.
requirements_list: Must be a Rockville resident
Must be age 18 or younger
Participant must pay $15 toward each program fee
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 240-314-8620 or email registration@rockvillemd.gov to apply or get more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Rockville provides school- and community-based mental health counseling for Rockville residents who are uninsured or unable to access counseling on their own. The program focuses on early intervention and prevention for school-age children using a short-term model of up to 12 sessions. Services include individual and group counseling covering topics like anger management, social skills, and school transitions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to 12 counseling sessions provided by a licensed professional counselor, licensed master's-level social worker, or supervised clinical intern. Sessions are available by appointment only and include individual and group formats, with guardian participation strongly encouraged.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Uninsured or underserved Rockville residents aged 4–18 who live in or attend school in Rockville and cannot access mental health services on their own.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Mental health counseling services including anger management, managing emotions, social skills development, and transition support for middle and high school.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must live in or attend school within Rockville city limits.
requirements_list: Must be school-age (4–18 years old)
Must live in or attend school in Rockville
Must be uninsured or unable to access mental health services
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Community Services Division by phone at 240-314-8306 or email at counseling@rockvillemd.gov to schedule an eligibility screening. Services are provided by appointment only.

structured_extraction.program_description: Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) program action plan for the City of Salisbury for the 2021 program year, outlining how federal CDBG funds will be used to support community development activities including housing, public services, and infrastructure improvements. The plan covers both the draft and final versions of the annual action plan.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) funds allocated to the City of Salisbury for the 2021 program year. Specific activities, amounts, and recipients are detailed in the Action Plan document, typically including housing, public services, and infrastructure improvements.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents, businesses, non-profits, and government entities in the City of Salisbury eligible to receive CDBG-funded community development assistance.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Community development activities as outlined in the 2021 Action Plan, including housing, public services, and infrastructure improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Salisbury, Wicomico County, Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Refer to the attached 2021 Action Plan PDF for specific application and funding details.

structured_extraction.program_description: A volunteer program that allows groups to 'adopt' a city park in Salisbury, Maryland, and commit to picking up litter and recyclables at least four times per year. The program enhances community pride, protects the environment, and improves the appearance of City parks. The City recognizes participants with a sign displaying the group's name and provides safety vests, gloves, and trash bags.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The City provides safety vests, disposable work gloves, trash bags, safety information, and an installed recognition sign displaying the adopter's name at the adopted park. The City will also replace signs damaged by normal wear and tear, and up to two signs per adopter if stolen or defaced.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Civic and non-profit organizations, school groups, commercial and private businesses, and families who want to volunteer to keep Salisbury city parks clean.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Volunteer litter and recyclables cleanup in designated Salisbury city parks.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in parks within the City of Salisbury, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must have an approved application on file and sign an Adopt-A-Park agreement (MOU) with the City.
Must pick up litter and recyclables from adopted park at least four times per year.
Adoption period is one year, renewable upon mutual consent.
Must designate one member as the Adopt-A-Park Coordinator to serve as point of contact with the City.
All participants under 18 must have written parental or guardian permission.
Participants under 16 must be supervised by at least one adult for every five participants.
Local chapters of national organizations must provide written authorization from the national organization.
Coordinator must ensure all participants sign the volunteer waiver before participating.
Coordinator must complete a clean-up report after each activity and submit it to the City.
Alcoholic beverages are prohibited at all times.
Adopter is responsible for replacing lost or damaged safety vests, signs, and other City-provided items.
Clean-up activity must be confined to the adopted park only; no trespassing on private property.
Must comply with safety instructions and traffic laws.
Notify Field Operations of any incidents or injuries immediately.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and submit the online Adopt-A-Park application form on the program webpage, including contact information, estimated number of volunteers, preferred cleanup location, cleanup event date and time, and agreement to the rules and waiver. Sign the MOU with the City. The City reviews applications and, after the initial cleanup event, installs a recognition sign at the adopted park.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit program for businesses in Salisbury related to advanced technology, including high-speed fiber infrastructure.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax credit available to qualifying businesses investing in advanced technology. Specific amounts and terms are not detailed on this page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses in Salisbury investing in advanced technology or high-speed fiber infrastructure.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax relief for qualifying advanced technology investments.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be located within the City of Salisbury.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the Advanced Technology Tax Credit Application through the City of Salisbury Business Development Office.

structured_extraction.program_description: A compiled list of affordable housing resources available to residents in the Salisbury, MD area, including 25+ affordable housing communities, apartment complexes, townhouses, private landlords, and additional housing resources. Provided by the City of Salisbury's Housing and Community Development department.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A resource list of affordable housing programs and services including: affordable rental apartments and townhouses with income-based rent scales, Section 8 subsidized housing, tax credit communities, Habitat for Humanity home building program, SNHS home purchase loans and rehabilitation services, Maryland Mortgage Program for first-time homebuyers, down payment assistance, tax abatement, foreclosure prevention counseling, and housing rehabilitation/renovation loans. Last updated December 20, 2023.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Seniors (62+ or 55+), elderly and disabled populations, deaf and hard of hearing individuals, low to moderate income families, very low to extremely low income households, farm workers, first-time homebuyers, and veterans seeking affordable housing resources in the Salisbury, MD area.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Housing assistance including rental housing, homeownership programs, down payment assistance, tax abatement, foreclosure prevention counseling, and housing rehabilitation/renovation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Salisbury, Fruitland, and Delmar, Wicomico County, Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_description: Anne Street Village is a housing program operated by the City of Salisbury that provides affordable or supportive housing for eligible residents. Applicants can apply through the city's online portal.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Supportive or affordable housing placement for eligible individuals through the Anne Street Village program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals seeking affordable or supportive housing in Salisbury, MD.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Housing placement and support services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Salisbury, Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online through the Salisbury city portal at https://salisburymd.portal.opengov.com/categories/1084/record-types/6470.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program offered by the City of Salisbury that allows residents or customers to defer payment of their utility bills.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Allows eligible utility customers to defer (delay) payment of their utility bills. Specific terms, amounts, and deferment periods are not described on this page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Utility customers of the City of Salisbury seeking to defer payment of their utility bills.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Deferment of utility bill payments.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to utility customers within the City of Salisbury, Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: An application form is referenced by the page title, but specific steps are not described on this page.

structured_extraction.program_description: Tax benefits available to qualifying artists and arts and entertainment enterprises located within the Salisbury Arts and Entertainment (A&E) District. Benefits include a real property tax credit for building renovation or new construction, an income tax subtraction for income earned by qualifying resident artists from artistic work created and sold in the district, and an exemption from the Admission and Amusement Tax for qualifying arts and entertainment enterprises and resident artists.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Three tax benefits are available: (1) Real Property Tax Credit — a credit on the increased assessed value of renovated or newly constructed buildings used by qualifying resident artists or arts and entertainment enterprises, offered by the City of Salisbury for up to 6 years per the enabling legislation. (2) Income Tax Subtraction Modification — qualifying resident artists pay no Maryland state or local income tax on income derived from artistic work created and sold within the district. (3) Admission and Amusement Tax Exemption — qualifying arts and entertainment enterprises and resident artists are exempt from the state Admission and Amusement Tax on gross receipts from admissions or amusement charges levied within the district.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Bob Young, Department of Assessments and Taxation
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualifying resident artists and arts and entertainment enterprises (for-profit and nonprofit entities dedicated to visual or performing arts) located within the Salisbury Arts and Entertainment District.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax relief on property taxes for renovated or new buildings used for arts purposes, income tax relief on artistic income, and exemption from admission and amusement taxes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only within the designated Salisbury Arts and Entertainment District in Salisbury, Maryland (Wicomico County).
requirements_list: Must be located within the designated Salisbury Arts and Entertainment District

For property tax credit: property must be a manufacturing, commercial, or industrial building wholly or partially renovated or newly constructed for use by a qualifying resident artist or arts and entertainment enterprise
For income tax subtraction: must be a qualifying resident artist who derives income from artistic work created and sold within the district
For admission and amusement tax exemption: must be a qualifying arts and entertainment enterprise or qualifying resident artist charging admissions or amusement fees within the district
Arts and entertainment enterprise must be a for-profit or nonprofit entity dedicated to visual or performing arts
A building permit must be obtained for renovations in order for the Department of Assessments and Taxation to be aware of them
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Office of the Maryland Comptroller for income tax subtraction and admission and amusement tax exemption. Contact the local office of the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (DAT) for property tax credit eligibility — DAT determines eligibility on a case-by-case basis. Use Maryland tax form 502AE for the income tax subtraction.

structured_extraction.program_name: Buy A Home, Build A Business
structured_extraction.program_description: A City of Salisbury program that helps young entrepreneurs realize business ideas while enabling home ownership in Salisbury. Provides tools to get a business off the ground and puts home ownership within reach, with participating local businesses offering additional incentives to qualifying participants.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $5,000 in down payment/closing cost assistance grants for home purchase; up to $500 toward business expenses; in-person mentoring and advisory time with Salisbury's mayor, business development specialist, and city legal services. Qualifying participants may also receive a $1,000 gift certificate towards new furniture from Outten Brothers of Salisbury as an additional incentive. A 5-year forgivable lien is recorded against the property.
structured_extraction.program_audience: College juniors, seniors, and recent graduates (within past 5 years) who are young entrepreneurs looking to buy a home and start a business in Salisbury, Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home down payment and closing costs; business startup expenses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Property must be located within the City Limits of Salisbury, Maryland. Business must operate within the City Limits of Salisbury.
requirements_list: Must be a college junior, senior, or recent graduate (within past 5 years)
Must have a business plan
Home must be owner-occupied
5-year forgivable lien recorded against property
Must complete SNHS Homebuyer Education class prior to settlement
Income restrictions apply
Can be used with FHA loans
Borrower(s) must contribute $1,000

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program offered by the City of Salisbury to help businesses located within the designated Main Street District recover from the negative impacts of COVID-19. Eligible businesses can receive up to $20,000 as a one-time, no-repayment grant.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time grant of up to $20,000 per business entity. No repayment required. Due to funding constraints, not all eligible applications may be fully funded.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit and non-profit businesses with a physical location in the designated Main Street area of Salisbury, MD that have been negatively impacted by COVID-19.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Paid sick leave for employees affected by COVID-19; maintaining payroll and retaining employees; covering increased costs from supply chain disruptions; past-due or upcoming rent or mortgage payments; repaying past-due or upcoming obligations; purchasing PPE or safety measures; building improvements to reduce COVID-19 spread; business equipment to expand services in response to COVID-19; other COVID-related recovery uses with narrative justification.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Business must have a physical location within the designated Main Street area of the City of Salisbury, Maryland. Funds must be used for property or business at that physical location.
requirements_list: Must have a physical location in the designated Main Street area of Salisbury
Must be a registered business entity in good standing with the State of Maryland and City of Salisbury
Must have no pre-existing tax liens or legal judgments prior to March 5
Home-based businesses are not eligible
Churches are not eligible
Banks and financial institutions are not eligible
Investment real estate entities are not eligible unless applying for payments for a business in the Main Street area or COVID-related investments on a Main Street property
Food trucks are not eligible
Government agencies are not eligible
Contractors, construction, and service repair-based businesses are not eligible unless applying for COVID-related investments on a Main Street property
Employees receiving sick leave or payroll support must spend over 50% of their time working in the Main Street area
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application during the open application period. Applications are reviewed and scored by a committee based on: the degree the business was negatively impacted by COVID-19, how the funds would help the business recover, and the business's contribution to the vitality of the Main Street area. Applicants are notified of award decisions by March 5. Funded businesses must later submit proof of receipts and a use-of-funds narrative.

structured_extraction.program_description: A one-time micro-grant program that provides $2,300 to small businesses in Salisbury, Maryland that were impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic and related State Executive Orders. The program is funded by donations from Delmarva Power and the City's Revolving Loan Fund.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time grant award of $2,300 with no repayment required. Awards are distributed through a lottery system. Tier 1 applicants (mandated to fully close) receive first priority; Tier 2 applicants (mandated to partially close) are considered if funds remain. Grant checks are mailed to awardees.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small for-profit businesses with a physical location in Salisbury, MD that were mandated to fully or partially close due to COVID-19 State Executive Orders, have 25 or fewer full-time employees, and were in good standing with the State of Maryland and City of Salisbury as of March 5, 2020.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Paid sick leave for employees unable to work due to COVID-19; maintaining payroll or retaining employees during business disruptions; meeting increased costs for materials due to supply chain interruptions; rent or mortgage payments; repaying obligations that cannot be met due to revenue losses; purchasing personal protective equipment (PPE) or spending on safety measures.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Business must have a physical establishment within the City of Salisbury. Businesses within the Revolving Loan Boundary area are eligible for both funding pools; businesses outside that boundary but meeting all other criteria are eligible for the lottery funded by Delmarva Power.
requirements_list: Must be a registered business entity in good standing with the State of Maryland and City of Salisbury
Must have a physical establishment in the City of Salisbury
Must have no more than 25 full-time employees as of March 5, 2020

Must be engaged in activities regulated or impacted by COVID-19 Maryland's State of Emergency with a license or permit associated to that regulation (proof that business was forced to partially or fully close is required)
Must have no pre-existing tax liens or legal judgements prior to March 5, 2020

Home-based businesses, churches, medical service providers, non-profit organizations, banks and financial institutions, investment real-estate entities, food trucks, national franchises, government agencies, and contractors/construction/service repair businesses are NOT eligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online or by email to [email protected]. Applications are reviewed by the Director of Business Development, a Finance Department officer, and the Deputy City Administrator for completeness. Applicants must demonstrate a tangible and immediate need for funding and certify intended use of funds. Approved applicants are classified as Tier 1 (mandated full closure) or Tier 2 (mandated partial closure) and entered into a lottery. Awardees receive a grant check by mail and must complete a disbursement form and provide receipts within 60 days of City approval.

structured_extraction.program_name: City of Salisbury Human Rights Award
structured_extraction.program_description: An annual award sponsored by the Human Rights Advisory Committee (HRAC) that recognizes an individual, group, business, or organization that has taken a leadership role in advocating for human rights and civil rights within the City of Salisbury. The award celebrates those who work to prevent prejudice and discrimination and advance equity and inclusivity in the community.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: An annual award (recognition) presented to one recipient selected by a judging panel comprising the Mayor, a City Council member, and a Salisbury community leader, based on top recommendations from the Human Rights Advisory Committee.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Last day of October each year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals, groups, businesses, or organizations based in or employed within the City of Salisbury that have taken a leadership role in advocating for human rights and social justice.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Recognition award — no monetary assistance described.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Nominees must reside or be employed within the City of Salisbury, or be a Salisbury-based group, business, or organization.
requirements_list: Nominee is an individual, group, business, or organization holding a leadership role in human rights advocacy within the City of Salisbury.
Individual nominees must reside or be employed within the City of Salisbury; groups, businesses, or organizations must be Salisbury-based.
Nominees may not self-nominate.
Nominees must not be part of a government institution or hold an official role within a political party (though affiliation with a political party is permitted).
Nomination must be received by the last day of October each year.
Nomination form must be complete; incomplete forms will not be considered.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete a nomination form via the City of Salisbury website or request one by emailing hrac@salisbury.md. Submit by the last day of October. The Human Rights Advisory Committee screens and judges nominations for merit, content, quality, and focus. The top three recommendations are forwarded to a judging panel (Mayor, a City Council member, and a community leader) who vote to confirm one recipient.

structured_extraction.program_name: City of Salisbury Owner-Occupied Housing Repair Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants to low-income homeowners in Salisbury to fund critical repairs that bring their homes into compliance with city codes. The program is administered by two nonprofit partners — Habitat for Humanity of Wicomico County and Salisbury Neighborhood Housing Services — using Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) federal funding.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $20,000 per property for eligible repairs, unless extenuating circumstances apply. A 5-year lien is placed on the property after the grant is received. Recipients are not eligible again until the 5-year lien term expires.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income owner-occupants of single-family homes within the City of Salisbury corporate limits whose total gross household income is below 80% of Area Median Income.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Repairs to bring homes into compliance with city codes, including repair or replacement of mechanical, electrical, and plumbing systems; building components such as roofs, foundations, doors, and windows; energy conservation improvements; lead paint hazard reduction; and accessibility modifications for disabled persons.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Property must be located within the City of Salisbury corporate limits.
requirements_list: Total gross household income before taxes must be below 80% of Area Median Income (limits vary by household size, e.g. $52,500 for 1 person, $74,950 for 4 persons).
Applicant must own the property in fee simple, as joint tenants, or tenants by their entireties — tenants in common ownership is not acceptable.
At least one owner on the deed of record must reside in the property to be rehabilitated.
Applicant must have legal capacity to incur obligations under the program.
All mortgage payments must be current for the previous three months.
Applicant must be free of any tax lien or judgment.
Bankruptcies must have been discharged for a minimum of 2 years.
All property taxes and City-issued invoices attached to the parcel must be current.
The applicant must have clear title to the property.
The applicant must insure the property for the entire lien term; flood insurance required for properties in the 100-year floodplain; properties in a floodway are not eligible.
Owner-occupants must not own any other house and must not have substantial assets that would enable them to secure rehabilitation funds from other sources.
A 5-year Notice of Lien must be signed and recorded in Land Records.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review the eligibility requirements on the program page. If you believe you qualify, contact one of the two subrecipient agencies: Habitat for Humanity of Wicomico County at 410-546-1551 or Salisbury Neighborhood Housing Services at 410-543-4626 for further information and to apply.

structured_extraction.program_name: City of Salisbury Summer Youth Employment Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A paid 8-week summer employment program for local high school students in the City of Salisbury. Participants work in various City of Salisbury departments to gain workforce readiness and career-specific skills. The program includes structured learning, mentoring, resume writing coaching, and soft skills development provided in partnership with Junior Achievement of the Eastern Shore and the Wicomico County Board of Education. Participants gain job skills, resume writing, soft skills development, and access to local business resources. Applications for each cycle are submitted through the City of Salisbury website, with applications for each summer hosted at a dedicated application page.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Paid employment for up to 28 hours per week over an 8-week period (June 22 – August 14, 2026). Participants also receive workforce readiness training, mentoring, resume writing assistance, and soft skills development through Junior Achievement of the Eastern Shore.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications for Summer 2026 are now closed; Applications for Summer 2027 will open in January
structured_extraction.program_audience: High school students entering 10th–12th grade for the 2026/2027 academic year who are enrolled in the Wicomico County school district. Residency in the City of Salisbury is preferred but not required.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Paid work experience in City of Salisbury departments; workforce readiness and career skills training, resume development, and access to business resources.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Residency in the City of Salisbury is preferred but not required. Students must be enrolled in the Wicomico County school district.
requirements_list: Must be entering 10th–12th grade for the 2026/2027 academic year
Must be currently enrolled in the Wicomico County school district
Must provide a work permit no later than June 22, 2026
Must provide 2 forms of updated identification (birth certificate, social security card, current student ID, or state-issued ID)
Must have consistent, reliable transportation to and from work
Must be able to work up to 28 hours per week for the 8-week period (June 22 – August 14, 2026)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications open in January each year. Submit an application through the City of Salisbury website (including via the dedicated application page for the current summer cycle). For questions, contact the Community Relations Division at 410-341-9550.

structured_extraction.program_name: City of Salisbury Tax Abatement Program (Conversion from Rental to Homeowner-Occupied Dwelling Incentive)
structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Salisbury offers a property tax abatement incentive program for property owners who purchase a formerly rented single-family home and convert it into their primary owner-occupied residence within Salisbury city limits. City property taxes are fully waived for the first five years of participation, then gradually phased in at 20% per year over the following four years (years 6–9), with full property taxes due in year ten. The program encourages homeownership by incentivizing the conversion of rental properties back to owner-occupied dwellings. Eligibility depends on the specific property; contact Housing and Community Development to determine if your property qualifies.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: City property taxes are fully abated (waived) for the first five years of participation. Taxes are then phased in at 20%, 40%, 60%, and 80% of the prevailing rate over years 6–9, with full property taxes due in year ten. Total benefit period is ten years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners converting a rental property to an owner-occupied single-family residence within the City of Salisbury
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of City property taxes on a qualifying owner-occupied single-family home previously used as a rental property; supports conversion of rental properties to owner-occupied dwellings
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Property must be located within the corporate limits of the City of Salisbury, Maryland
requirements_list: Property must be located within the corporate limits of the City of Salisbury

Property must have been used exclusively as a rental property for at least three consecutive years immediately prior to conversion, or owned by a person/entity that rehabilitated it after rental use for 3 consecutive years
Property must be converted to an owner-occupied family residence
Owner must intend to occupy the home within one year of the closing date
Property must be a single-family detached dwelling
Property must serve as the principal residence of the homeowner
Applicant agrees to maintain owner-occupied status for the full 9 years, or if sold, must sell to an owner-occupant only, or repay all abated taxes
Owner must submit an annual confirmation of family use and continued owner-occupancy for nine years
Property must qualify as determined by Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Pick up and submit an application at the City Finance Office, 125 N Division St., Room 103, Salisbury, MD 21801, or download the application from the City of Salisbury website. A Participation Form is also available on the program page. You may also contact the Housing and Community Development department to find out if your property qualifies. Annual certification is due by April 1 each year.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) 2022 Action Plan
structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) program provides federal funding to the City of Salisbury to support community development activities. The 2022 Action Plan outlines how the city plans to use its CDBG funds during the program year.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents, businesses, and organizations in Salisbury, MD eligible for community development assistance.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) – Entitlement Communities Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The CDBG program provides annual federal grants to the City of Salisbury to fund a wide range of community and economic development activities. These include neighborhood revitalization, economic development, improved community facilities, public services, housing rehabilitation, and assistance to low- and moderate-income residents. Local priorities guide how funds are used, as long as activities benefit low- and moderate-income persons, help prevent or eliminate slums and blight, or address urgent community development needs. Local nonprofit organizations, for-profit entities, and government agencies can apply as subrecipients for public service or capital project funding.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual formula-based federal grants administered by the City of Salisbury. For program year 2021 (July 1, 2021 – June 30, 2022), total CDBG funds are $399,903: $70,000 for administration, $329,903 for program/project activities, and up to $59,985 for public service projects. No more than 20% of the grant can be used for planning and administration, and no more than 15% for public service activities. The maximum any single applicant may request in a competitive funding round is $150,000. Funds are awarded on a reimbursement basis only — subrecipients must spend their own money first, then submit paid invoices and documentation to be reimbursed.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Citizens, registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations, for-profit entities, and government agencies in Salisbury seeking funding for public services or capital projects that benefit low- and moderate-income persons, prevent slums and blight, or address urgent community development needs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition and clearance of real property; public improvements and facilities (e.g., senior centers, recreation centers, day care centers); public services (e.g., child care, health care, job training, drug abuse counseling, services for homeless); relocation assistance; rehabilitation of residential, commercial, industrial, or nonprofit-owned buildings; historic preservation; lead-based paint hazard reduction; code enforcement; assistance to micro-enterprises; homeownership assistance; technical assistance to nonprofits; assistance to higher education institutions; neighborhood revitalization; economic development; and program administration.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to subrecipients operating within the City of Salisbury, Maryland.
requirements_list: Each funded activity must be eligible under Title I of the Housing and Community Development Act of 1974

All funded activities must meet at least one national objective: benefit to low- and moderate-income persons, prevention or elimination of slums and blight, or meeting an urgent community development need
Subrecipients must be a registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization and provide documentation confirming this status
Any capital project on property not owned by the subrecipient must include written approval from the property owner
Subrecipients requesting community service funds must be developing a new public service or proposing a quantifiable increase in service for an existing program
Funds are awarded on a reimbursement basis only; subrecipients must have sufficient operating funds to cover expenses before being reimbursed
Maximum request per competitive funding round is $150,000
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Prospective subrecipients should review the CDBG Program Guidelines document for details on how the program is administered and how to apply. Eligible nonprofit organizations apply as subrecipients during competitive funding rounds. Applicants must submit documentation of 501(c)(3) status and, for capital projects on property they do not own, written approval from the property owner. After award, subrecipients expend their own funds, then submit paid invoices, cancelled checks, and other documentation to the City for reimbursement.
