structured_extraction.program_name: Here is Home Residential Fee Waiver
structured_extraction.program_description: A graduated fee waiver program (Housing Expansion Incentive Program) designed to accelerate residential development construction throughout Salisbury. Provides full or partial waivers of annexation fees, permitting fees, comprehensive connection charges, and/or development assessment fees for eligible housing projects.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Graduated fee waiver program offering up to 100% waiver of annexation fees, permitting fees, comprehensive connection charges (excluding water/sewer infrastructure reimbursement fees), and development assessment fees. Waivers are tiered: 25% upon site/building plan approval, additional 25% upon construction commencement, and additional 50% upon certificate of occupancy. Fees covered include building plan review, permits, demolition, utility connection, development review, subdivision review, critical area fees, water meter setting, and fire prevention/permit fees. Prorated based on residential proportion of mixed-use projects.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Director of the Department of Infrastructure & Development
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential developers and property owners planning residential construction projects (single-family, multi-family, duplexes, townhouses, apartments, assisted living, condominiums, senior housing, group domiciliary care facilities) in Salisbury.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Waiver of permit and development fees related to residential construction or improvement, including building plan review, permits, demolition, utility connection, development review, subdivision review, critical area fees, water meter setting, and fire prevention/permit fees.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Within City of Salisbury limits OR outside city limits with signed Annexation Petition. Projects must comply with City zoning, building codes, and Historic District Commission requirements.
requirements_list: Minimum 50% residential EDUs required
Projects outside city limits must submit Annexation Petition
Must adhere to development timeline and benchmarks
Program Agreement must be executed within 15 days of receipt
Applicants must sign and submit documents within 30 days
Submit and approve site plans and building permit application by February 28, 2023
Commence construction by October 31, 2023
Obtain certificates of occupancy by June 30, 2025 (multifamily) or June 30, 2027 (single-family)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application with project narrative and EDU information. Department of Infrastructure & Development (DID) staff reviews and forwards to Mayor for pre-approval. DID staff finalizes Program Agreement. Applicant executes agreement within 15 days. Agreement presented to Mayor for final approval. Applications can be submitted to Room 202 at 125 N. Division Street or emailed to the Infrastructure & Development department.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides grants to property owners and tenants in Downtown Salisbury to help cover the cost of connecting their buildings to Maryland Broadband's high-speed fiber optic internet that runs along Main Street.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $2,500 are available on a reimbursement basis only. Funds are awarded on a first-come, first-served basis until the fiscal year budget runs out. Applicants must pay for the work first and then submit receipts or paid invoices for reimbursement. Construction costs cannot be passed on to end users of the fiber service.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Funds available until exhausted for the Fiscal Year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners and tenants located within Downtown Salisbury who want to connect their building to the high-speed fiber optic line along Main Street.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction costs to bring fiber from the existing conduit into the private property, ending at the termination point where the modem will be located.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Property must be located within Downtown Salisbury and must have access to existing conduits abutted to buildings as part of the Main Street project. The Historic District of Salisbury boundaries are shown in the Historic District map.
requirements_list: Property must be located within Downtown Salisbury using existing conduits abutted to buildings as part of the Main Street project.
Application must be made by the legal property owner or by a tenant with written approval from the property owner.
Applicant must use a licensed contractor to perform the work.
If the property is in the Historic District, approval from the Historic District is required.
The City will not approve digging up sidewalks or work that alters improvements made during the Main Street Construction project (completed November 2020).
Construction costs must not be passed on to end users of the fiber service.
Grants are made on a reimbursement basis only — work must be paid for before reimbursement is requested.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the online application form with your contact information, property address, property tax number, a detailed description of how fiber will be brought into the building, a photograph of the building façade showing the planned entry point, and the anticipated cost. If the project is already complete, include copies of all receipts or paid invoices. Tenants must include a letter of approval from the property owner. Applications are reviewed on a first-come, first-served basis.

structured_extraction.program_name: Manufacturing and Research & Development Equipment Tax Exemption
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides a personal property tax exemption on machinery and equipment used for manufacturing or research and development activities in the City of Salisbury. Eligible businesses can receive an exemption for up to 5 years on qualifying equipment purchases.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Personal property tax exemption on machinery and equipment used in manufacturing or research and development. The exemption applies to the specific year in which the equipment was purchased and can last up to 5 years. To qualify for the maximum 5-year term, the application must be submitted within 2 years from December 31st of the calendar year in which the equipment was purchased. A separate application is required for each equipment year. Each year of the exemption requires submission of a copy of the personal property tax return.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Application must be received within two (2) years from December 31st of the calendar year in which the equipment was purchased
structured_extraction.contact_name: Sandra Green (Director of Finance); Phillip Menzel (Assistant Director Finance - Accounting)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses that own and operate manufacturing or research and development facilities in Salisbury that have recently located, expanded operations, or developed a new product or industrial process in the city.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax exemption on personal property (tools, machinery, and equipment) used in manufacturing or research and development operations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be located within the City of Salisbury, Maryland.
requirements_list: Equipment must be owned and operated by a facility that (1) locates in Salisbury, (2) expands operations in Salisbury, or (3) develops a new product or industrial process in Salisbury
Application must be submitted within 2 years from December 31st of the calendar year in which the equipment was purchased to qualify for the maximum 5-year exemption term
A separate application must be made for each equipment year
Must attach a detailed equipment schedule including description, original cost, and date of acquisition for each item (general descriptions are not acceptable)
Must attach a copy of the State of Maryland Personal Property Return for the year of acquisition
Exemption must be approved by the City of Salisbury Council (receipt of exemption from Wicomico County does not guarantee City approval)
A copy of the personal property tax return must be submitted each year during the exemption period
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the online application form or download and fill out the PDF version. Attach the equipment schedule and Maryland Personal Property Return. Submit online or mail to Finance Department, 125 North Division St., Salisbury, MD 21801-4940. All exemptions require approval by the City of Salisbury Council.

structured_extraction.program_name: Newton Community Center Youth After School and Summer Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Newton Community Center offers free after-school and summer activities for youth ages 8–18 in Salisbury, MD. Participants can join enrichment clubs focused on hobbies and interests such as arts and crafts, gaming, and cooking. The center also provides a drop-in space with a music studio, gaming room, computer lab, and more.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free after-school programming available Monday through Friday from 3pm–6pm throughout the school year, with adjusted schedules during summer and occasional weekends. Includes enrichment clubs, drop-in access to a music studio, gaming room, computer lab, arts and crafts materials, homework help, and light snacks. All programs are free of charge.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Youth ages 8–18 in Salisbury, MD
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: After-school and summer enrichment activities including arts and crafts, gaming, cooking, music recording, homework assistance, and community drop-in.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at the Newton Community Center in Salisbury, Maryland.
requirements_list: Participants must be ages 8–18
Registration is required before attending
Children under age 8 must be accompanied by an adult
Participants must be registered; unregistered guests are not permitted
Participants must follow all NCC and City of Salisbury rules and guidelines
Program is not licensed childcare; participants must be mature enough for a less-structured environment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Youth After School Program Registration Form on the webpage. An NCC staff member will follow up after submission.

structured_extraction.program_description: Salisbury's Meadow Program allows residents to register a planned, intentional planting of native grasses and wildflowers on their property. Registered participants are exempt from property code violations related to tall vegetation, as long as they follow the program rules for managing their meadow. Meadows must consist mainly of plants native to Maryland and be maintained to prevent weed infestation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Registered participants receive an exemption from property code violations related to tall vegetation and unmaintained plant growth, allowing them to maintain a native wildflower and grass meadow on their property without penalty.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Salisbury residents and property owners who want to establish a native plant meadow on their property.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable — this program provides a regulatory exemption, not direct financial assistance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to properties located within the City of Salisbury, Maryland.
requirements_list: Meadow must be registered with the City of Salisbury Housing and Community Development Department
Meadow must be managed to prevent weed infestation and stagnant or foul-smelling conditions
Meadow must not contain noxious weeds as defined by the Maryland Department of Agriculture
Meadow must consist of a majority of plants native to Maryland
Meadow must be set back at least 10 feet from the front property line
Meadow must be set back at least 5 feet from side and/or rear property lines, unless a fully opaque fence at least 5 feet tall is installed between the meadow and the neighboring property
Meadow must be cut to no more than 8 inches in height at least once annually between September 15 and March 15
Renters must provide proof of property owner approval
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the registration form on the City's website. Provide your name, contact information, property address, meadow location, and approximate square footage. Renters must upload proof of property owner approval. Agree to the program rules and conditions before submitting.

structured_extraction.program_description: A real property tax credit for public safety officers — including full-time and volunteer firefighters, EMTs, paramedics, and police officers employed by the City of Salisbury — that reduces the amount of city real property tax owed on their primary residence. The credit must be renewed each year by April 1.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A tax credit of up to $2,500 applied to the City of Salisbury real property tax on the applicant's primary residence. The credit may not exceed the total real property tax imposed on the dwelling. The credit is valid for one taxable year and must be renewed annually by April 1.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 1 immediately before the taxable year for which the credit is sought
structured_extraction.program_audience: Full-time firefighters/EMTs, firefighters/paramedics, and police officers employed by the City of Salisbury with at least one year of full-time employment; active volunteer firefighters meeting service requirements; officers who retired in good standing or received a service-related disability; and volunteer firefighters with 20+ years of active service who have become Lifetime members.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of City of Salisbury real property taxes on the public safety officer's primary residence.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicant must own and reside in residential property within the City of Salisbury, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be currently employed full-time or serving as an active volunteer with the City of Salisbury Fire Department or Police Department, or have retired in good standing, received a service-related disability, or achieved Lifetime volunteer member status
Full-time employees must have completed at least one year of full-time employment
Volunteer members must meet service requirements outlined in Section 3.24.030(B) of the Salisbury Municipal Code
Must own the property to which the credit will be applied
Property must be the applicant's primary residence
Applicant must not have received a conflicting real property tax credit under Title 9 of the Tax-Property Article of the Annotated Code of Maryland
Application must be filed on or before April 1 of the year immediately before the taxable year for which the credit is sought
Must provide supporting documentation (e.g. current paystub, letter of retirement or separation, letter evidencing volunteer status)
Must notify the City of Salisbury Finance Department if eligibility requirements are no longer met
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the online application at salisbury.md/public-safety-tax-credit-application. Provide your property parcel number, personal and property information, select the applicable public safety officer designation, and attach supporting documentation. Sign the application electronically. Applications must be submitted by April 1 each year.

structured_extraction.program_name: Public Sculpture at Salisbury City Park – Request for Qualifications (RFQ)
structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Salisbury invites individual artists, artist teams, and emerging artists to submit qualifications to design and install a permanent public sculpture at the northwest corner of Salisbury City Park. The selected work should reflect themes of community engagement, accessibility, and interactivity. Five semi-finalists each receive a $1,000 stipend to develop detailed proposals, and the winning artist receives a $30,000 implementation grant to cover design, materials, fabrication, installation, and artist fees.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Five semi-finalists each receive a $1,000 stipend to develop detailed proposals (physical model, material samples, renderings, artist statement, and installation plan). The winning artist or team receives a $30,000 Maryland State Arts Council (MSAC) Implementation Grant to cover all design, materials, fabrication, installation, and artist fees. The City may also assist with site preparation and basic infrastructure such as electrical service.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individual artists, artist teams, students, and emerging artists who are Maryland residents aged 18 or older.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Design, materials, fabrication, installation, and artist fees for a permanent public sculpture at Salisbury City Park.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be Maryland residents (owning or renting residential property in Maryland for at least six months before the application deadline and throughout the funded project). The sculpture will be installed in Salisbury City Park, Salisbury, Maryland.
requirements_list: Open to individual artists, artist teams, students, and emerging artists
Must be a Maryland resident (own or rent residential property in Maryland for at least six months before submission and throughout the funded project)
Must be 18 years of age or older
Submit a resume or CV (for each artist if applying as a team)
Submit up to 3 images of previous work with descriptions (title, year, materials, dimensions, location)
Submit a letter of interest (1–2 pages) describing approach to public art, community interaction, and interest in this project
Provide contact information (email, phone, website/social media if applicable)
Semi-finalists must develop a physical model, material samples, detailed renderings, artist statement, and installation plan
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit qualifications through the online application form on the City of Salisbury website by September 30, 2025. Five semi-finalists will be selected by October 3, 2025 and notified to develop full proposals. Semi-finalist presentations take place November 7, 2025, with community input informing the final selection. The final artist/team is selected and contracted by November 10, 2025.

structured_extraction.program_description: A temporary permit program that allows Salisbury restaurants to set up outdoor dining areas during the COVID-19 reopening period, in line with Maryland Governor Hogan's guidelines. There is no application fee. Approval is temporary and expires 30 days after Maryland opens full dine-in capacity, unless a renewal is filed.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A no-fee temporary outdoor dining permit allowing restaurants to extend seating into outdoor areas. The permit is temporary and expires 30 days after Maryland opens full dine-in restaurant capacity, unless a renewal application is filed and approved.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Salisbury restaurant owners who plan to offer outdoor dining service under the State of Maryland's COVID-19 reopening guidelines.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Setting up a temporary outdoor dining area adjacent to an existing restaurant.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only to restaurants located within the City of Salisbury, Maryland.
requirements_list: No application fee is required
The State of Maryland must allow dine-in service before permits take effect
Do not set up the extended area until express written City approval is received
All outdoor facilities must be removed at permit expiration
Obtain separate approvals from the Health Department and Liquor Board as needed for food/alcohol service
Show an access path for emergency services (unimpeded by parking) to all dining area points
Plan must not impede any walkways or sidewalks; pedestrian traffic must be maintained
Safe social distancing of six feet must be maintained in all areas
Fencing/barriers must be temporary (not drilled into roadways or sidewalks) but sturdy enough to prevent being blown away or vehicle access
Plans for serving over 50 people must include two separate ingress/egress points and ADA accessibility
If indoor restrooms are not accessible, show port-a-pot locations with handwashing stations and ADA accessibility
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit your restaurant information and outdoor dining plan through this page. The City will review the application and provide express written approval before any outdoor area may be set up.

structured_extraction.program_description: A revolving loan fund administered by the City of Salisbury that provides financing to new and existing businesses and property owners located within designated loan boundary areas of Salisbury, including Downtown Salisbury. The program aims to aid in the revitalization of the Downtown area by fostering growth of new businesses and assisting expanding businesses, improving the physical appearance of interiors and exteriors of commercial and mixed-use buildings, increasing the City's tax base, providing needed goods and services to local residents, and preserving historically and architecturally significant structures. The Revolving Loan Advisory Committee reviews and advises on applications, meeting as needed when applications are received. Revised guidelines were adopted under Resolution No. 2776.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans of up to $100,000 per project available through a revolving loan fund. Interest rate is set at the U.S. Treasury less than 10-year long-term composite rate plus 1% (fixed for the loan term). Loan terms of 3, 5, or 7 years are available. Funds may be used for professional engineering and architectural assistance, renovation of building exteriors and interiors, and purchase or renovation of equipment or machinery within designated loan boundary areas of Salisbury, including Downtown Salisbury. Funds cannot be used for start-up costs, working capital, refinancing fees, access streets/roads, parking areas, or utility/service extensions. Applicants must demonstrate personal financial investment in the project and secure any other committed financing before applying. Applications are reviewed by the Revolving Loan Advisory Committee on an as-needed basis, with a goal of 45 days to take action after receipt of all required information.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis; goal of 45 days to take action after receipt of all required information
structured_extraction.program_audience: New and existing businesses and property owners, including commercial tenants (with written landlord approval), located within the Revolving Loan Fund boundary area in Salisbury, Maryland (including Downtown Salisbury) seeking financing for expansion, renovation, or redevelopment projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Professional engineering and architectural assistance, renovation of building exteriors and interiors, and purchase or renovation of equipment or machinery within the designated loan boundary area in Salisbury. Funds cannot be used for start-up costs, working capital, refinancing fees, access streets/roads, parking areas, or utility/service extensions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Business or property must be located within the designated Revolving Loan Fund boundary area in the City of Salisbury, Maryland, including Downtown Salisbury. A boundary map is available from the program. Projects involving historic buildings must have concept plan approval from the Salisbury Historic District Commission.
requirements_list: Business or property must be located within the Revolving Loan Fund boundary area in Salisbury, Maryland
Startup business plan with three-year pro forma projections
Personal and company tax returns for the past two years
Evidence of personal financial investment in the project
Conceptual design illustration and detailed project description
Project timeline with specific milestones
Three written cost estimates for proposed project costs
Copy of lease and written landlord approval (if applicable)
Evidence of Historic District Commission approval of concept plan (if applicable)
Articles of Incorporation (if applicable)
Credit report dated no more than one month before application submission
Loan request may not exceed $100,000
Must complete the Revolving Loan Fund Application
Must submit a Personal Financial Statement (including assets, liabilities, and income information)
Authorize credit report review by City of Salisbury
Disclosure of bankruptcy history
Disclosure of pending legal actions
Disclosure of criminal record history
Disclosure of tax delinquency status
Commercial tenants must provide written landlord approval
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review the application checklist and program guidelines, gather all required documents, complete the online application form (including applicant information, business information, property information, project information, and personal financial statement), upload the completed Personal Financial Statement, and submit the application to the City of Salisbury at 110 N Division Street, Salisbury, MD 21801. The Revolving Loan Advisory Committee will schedule a meeting as needed to review the application and advise City officials, with a goal of taking action within 45 days of receipt of all required information. Applicants may also contact the Business Development Specialist or Assistant City Administrator for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary certification program that recognizes businesses in Salisbury, Maryland for adopting environmentally friendly practices. Businesses earn points across a three-tier checklist of sustainable actions — such as going strawless, using reusable cups, recycling, purchasing local foods, using energy-efficient lighting, clean energy, and managing stormwater — and receive a bronze, silver, or gold certification depending on their total score. The program is administered by the City of Salisbury and is designed to publicly recognize businesses committed to sustainability.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Businesses earn a Green Business Certification by completing a point-based checklist of sustainable practices. Points are awarded for actions in three tiers: 1-point actions (e.g., going strawless, using reusable cups), 2-point actions (e.g., recycling, purchasing local foods, using efficient lighting), and 3-point actions (e.g., using clean energy, stormwater management). Certification levels are bronze (10–14 points), silver (15–19 points), and gold (20+ points). Certified businesses receive a window sticker to display at their entrance, a photo opportunity with the Mayor for social media promotion, and their logo listed on the City of Salisbury's website under a green business highlight section.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses located in Salisbury, Maryland seeking recognition for environmentally sustainable practices.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable — this is a certification program, not a financial assistance program. Recognition and promotional benefits are awarded to qualifying businesses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to businesses operating within the City of Salisbury, Maryland.
requirements_list: Business must be located in Salisbury, MD
Business must earn at least 10 points from the green criteria checklist to qualify for bronze certification
Points are earned by adopting specific environmentally friendly practices (e.g., using non-plastic straws, LED lighting, recycling, clean energy, native plants)
Bronze: 10–14 points; Silver: 15–19 points; Gold: 20+ points
Applicant must complete the point-based green practices checklist
All information provided must be accurate (attested by digital signature)
A designated 'Green Advocate' must attend the City's Sustainability Advisory Committee (Green Team) at least once per year if claiming that criterion
All BPI-certified compostable product requirements must be met for compostable items
Certifications granted before 2022 have been extended to 3 years total from initial date due to COVID-19
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the online application form at salisbury.md/green-business-certification-application with business information and social media presence, indicate which green practices your business currently follows using the three-tier checklist, total your points, and submit with a digital signature attesting to the accuracy of the information. The Green Team will verify the checklist and confirm the point total and certification level.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Enterprise Zone Program offers tax credits and tax benefits to businesses, property owners, and developers that locate, expand, or improve commercial properties within the designated Salisbury Wicomico Enterprise Zone in Wicomico County. The program provides three types of tax credits: a real property tax credit against local property taxes on qualifying commercial property improvements, a state income tax credit based on the number and type of new employees hired, and a personal property tax credit available in Focus Area Zones only. The program is designed to encourage economic development and job creation within the designated enterprise zone.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Three types of tax credits are available: (1) Real Property Tax Credit — a ten-year credit against local property taxes equal to 80% of the increase in assessed value for five years, then declining 10% per year (70%, 60%, 50%, 40%, 30%) over the remaining five years. Requires a capital investment of $50,000 or more in commercial property. (2) State Income Tax Credit — a credit based on new employees hired. For employees who are not economically disadvantaged: a one-time credit of $1,000 per qualifying employee. For employees who are economically disadvantaged: up to $3,000 in year one, $2,000 in year two, and $1,000 in year three of employment. (3) Personal Property Tax Credit — available only in designated Focus Area Zones within the Enterprise Zone.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: For the real property credit, the Zone Administrator must certify eligibility by December 31 of the preceding calendar year to receive the credit starting July 1 of the next fiscal year. Application must be submitted before project completion and before issuance of Use/Occupancy Permits.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses, property owners, and developers located within or planning to locate, expand, or substantially improve commercial property within the Salisbury Wicomico Enterprise Zone.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Real property tax credit applied to property tax bills for qualifying commercial property improvements. State income tax credits claimed on business entity tax returns for qualifying new hires. Personal property tax credit available in Focus Area Zones only.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The business or property must be located within the designated Salisbury Wicomico Enterprise Zone in Salisbury, Maryland. The personal property tax credit is available only within designated Focus Area Zones within the Enterprise Zone.
requirements_list: Property must be located within the Salisbury Wicomico Enterprise Zone
Only commercial properties are eligible for the real property tax credit; residential use (including multifamily and single family) is excluded
Applicant must plan to make a capital investment of $50,000 or more for the real property credit
Application for real property credit must be submitted before project completion and before issuance of Use/Occupancy Permits
Zone Administrator must certify eligibility by December 31 to receive the credit beginning the following July 1
For the state income tax credit, the business must have hired two or more qualifying new employees
New employees must have been hired after the Enterprise Zone designation date or after the business relocated into the zone
New employees must fill a new position or replace a previously certified economically disadvantaged employee
New employees must have worked at least 35 hours per week for at least six months
New employees must be paid at least 150% of the federal minimum wage
New employees must have spent at least half of working hours in the Enterprise Zone or on activities directly resulting from the business location in the zone
New employees must be new hires or employees rehired after being laid off for more than one year
Workers must be eligible workers to qualify for the income tax credit
Personal property tax credit is only available to businesses located in designated Focus Area Zones
Must complete the Enterprise Zone Application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Complete the application (available online or as a printable PDF) and submit it to the Business Development Specialist. 2. The Zone Administrator reviews the application and forwards it to the appropriate state entities for approval. 3. If eligible, the applicant receives a certification letter from the City of Salisbury — keep this letter as proof of Enterprise Zone certification. 4. For the real property tax credit, it is automatically reflected in the property tax bill. For state income tax credits, the business or its accountant claims them when filing business entity tax returns. 5. For the personal property tax credit (Focus Area Zones only), follow the same certification process.

structured_extraction.program_description: Tree City USA is a nationwide program that helps cities and towns manage and expand their public urban tree canopy. Communities earn Tree City USA status by meeting four core standards: maintaining a tree board or department, having a community tree ordinance, spending at least $2 per capita on urban forestry, and celebrating Arbor Day. The program has been operating since 1976 and has more than 3,400 participating communities. The City of Salisbury also issues an annual Arbor Day proclamation urging citizens to plant trees to promote environmental benefits, civic pride, and community well-being.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Communities receive a framework and recognition for managing and expanding public trees. Participation requires meeting four core standards of urban forestry management. The City of Salisbury also encourages citizens to plant trees through an annual Arbor Day proclamation. No direct financial assistance amount is specified on this page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Cities and towns seeking to improve urban forestry management and earn Tree City USA recognition; citizens of Salisbury encouraged to plant trees.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Urban forestry management, tree planting, and related community greening activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: This page is specific to Salisbury, Maryland's participation in the nationwide Tree City USA program.
requirements_list: Maintain a tree board or department
Have a community tree ordinance
Spend at least $2 per capita on urban forestry
Celebrate Arbor Day
Plant trees (voluntary participation for citizens)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Communities must meet four core standards of sound urban forestry management to achieve Tree City USA status. See the Arbor Day Foundation website for details. Citizens are encouraged to voluntarily participate in tree planting as promoted through the annual Arbor Day proclamation.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Water Incentive Program (WIN) helps eligible low-income households in Salisbury, MD pay their water and/or sewer bills. Qualifying households can receive up to $2,000 per year (if no leaks) applied toward their water and/or wastewater bill issued by the City of Salisbury, or up to $1,000 if the property has a leak. Applicants must live at the property for which assistance is being provided and meet income thresholds (at or below 60% of State Median Income) or be enrolled in qualifying assistance programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible households receive one payment per year of up to $2,000 (if no leaks) or up to $1,000 (if property has a leak) applied toward their water and/or sewer (wastewater) bills issued by the City of Salisbury. Assistance is limited to actual charges on the water and/or sewer bill.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income Maryland residents (both tenants and homeowners) who are responsible for paying a water and/or wastewater bill issued by the City of Salisbury and who live at the property for which assistance is being provided. Total household income must not exceed 60% of State Median Income, or applicant must be enrolled in a qualifying assistance program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment toward water and/or sewer (wastewater) utility bills issued by the City of Salisbury.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be Maryland residents responsible for a water and/or wastewater bill issued by the City of Salisbury, MD, and must live at the property receiving the assistance.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident
Must be responsible for payment of a water and/or sewer bill issued by the City of Salisbury
Must live at the property for which assistance is being provided

Total household gross income must not exceed 60% of State Median Income (varies by household size), OR applicant must be receiving qualifying assistance (LIHEAP, TCA, TDAP, SNAP, SSI, ERAP, or Means Tested Veteran Benefits)

Must provide government-issued photo ID, proof of residence (including most recent water/sewer bill), Social Security cards for all household members, and proof of all gross income for the last 30 days
If household had no income in the prior 30 days, must sign a Declaration of Zero Income
Both tenant and property owner must apply if applicable
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at salisbury.md/win or download and submit a printable application. Sign and date the application before submitting. The office is open 9:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Translation services available at 1-800-332-6347.

structured_extraction.program_description: Internet Essentials is a Comcast program that provides low-cost, high-speed, reliable home internet service to low-income households who qualify for certain public assistance programs, such as the National School Lunch Program, SNAP, Housing Assistance, Medicaid, and SSI. Two tiers are available: Internet Essentials at 50/5 Mbps for $9.95 per month, or Internet Essentials Plus at 100/10 Mbps for $29.95 per month. New customers receive 60 days of complimentary Internet Essentials service to help them get connected. The program is available to new and existing Comcast customers who meet eligibility requirements within Comcast service areas statewide, including Calvert County.

structured_extraction.program_description: A scholarship fund administered by the Community Foundation of Howard County providing up to $25,000 (approximately $350 per week of camp per applicant) to African American, Latino, or Native American males enrolled in a Howard County public middle school. The scholarship covers 100 percent of tuition and related expenses, including lunch, snacks, and transportation if needed, for four-week summer enrichment programs through the Howard County Public School System. Programs include morning academic courses and afternoon enrichment activities focused on leadership, academic achievement, character development, problem-solving skills, and a sense of community. In 2023, a total of $19,500 was distributed among selected recipients; in 2024, 33 students received scholarships. Previous recipients who continue to meet eligibility criteria are encouraged to reapply.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Foundation of Howard County Annual Scholarships
structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Foundation of Howard County (CFHC) awards dozens of financial scholarships annually to support Howard County students pursuing post-secondary education and extracurricular programs. Most scholarships are named in tribute of a loved one and are funded through endowed, permanent funds established by Howard County residents and local philanthropists. In 2024, the Foundation awarded 35 scholarships totaling $57,000 to 32 graduating high school seniors. In 2021, 87 scholarships totaling approximately $79,500 were awarded to 78 students, including high school seniors and middle school students. In 2020, 61 scholarships totaling approximately $68,100 were awarded to 56 students, including awards for high school seniors pursuing college and scholarships for minority middle school males to attend extracurricular camps. Scholarships recognize outstanding academic achievement, dedication to community service, and participation in extracurricular activities. Applications typically open in mid-to-late February through an online portal, with a late-March to mid-April deadline depending on the cycle. The 2026 cycle opened February 25, 2026 and closes April 13, 2026.
structured_extraction.agency: Community Foundation of Howard County / Frederick / Anne Arundel / Eastern Shore
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial scholarship awards ranging from $500 to $20,000 (some multi-year) are awarded to eligible Howard County students for post-secondary education costs and extracurricular program participation. Individual scholarships have varying eligibility requirements based on the donor's criteria, including specific high schools, fields of study, community involvement, and athletic participation. Awards are designated for post-secondary tuition and related educational expenses at eligible two- or four-year colleges, universities, or trade schools, or for qualified extracurricular camp programs. Total 2024 awards were $57,000 across 35 scholarships. The 2026 cycle opened February 25, 2026 and closes April 13, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: Endow Maryland is a Maryland state tax credit program administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) that rewards donors (businesses and individuals) who make new contributions of $500 or more to qualified permanent endowment funds (QPEFs) at eligible, accredited community foundations in Maryland. Donors receive a 25% state tax credit on their contribution, up to a maximum credit of $50,000 per year (representing a maximum $200,000 donation per year). The credit can be applied against Maryland corporate income tax, personal income tax, insurance premiums tax, or public service company franchise tax. Credits are limited and awarded on a first-come, first-served basis each calendar year. Contributions must be new gifts made by personal check, cash, or publicly traded securities — grants from donor advised funds or IRA charitable rollovers are not eligible. Five-year pledges are eligible for annual credits for each year of the pledge. The program helps build lasting charitable resources for local communities across Maryland, including funds such as the Next 50 Campaign and the Fund for the Common Good at the Community Foundation of Howard County.

Maximum credit is $50,000 per year (representing a maximum $200,000 donation per year). The credit can be applied against Maryland corporate income tax, personal income tax, insurance premiums tax, or public service company franchise tax (only one type per application). Credits are limited and available on a first-come, first-served basis each calendar year. Contributions must be new gifts made by personal check, cash, or publicly traded securities — grants from donor advised funds or IRA charitable rollovers are not eligible. Must apply to DHCD for certification; certification must be attached to Form 502CR

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Dan Flynn, Director of Development, at dflynn@cfhoco.org or 410-730-7840 to verify that credits are still available for the current calendar year and to learn which funds qualify. Download, print, and complete the Endow Maryland Certification of Contribution Form (Section I, required for each contribution) and the Donor and Foundation Acknowledgment/Waiver of Information Form (required annually, signed by both donor and foundation). The community foundation verifies the contribution in Section II of the Certification form and provides required documentation (Waiver of Information, Thank You Letter, and Proof of Donation). The foundation submits the completed forms to DHCD. DHCD reviews documentation and issues an approval letter with the tax credit amount to the donor (Section III). Donors then claim the 25% state tax credit on their Maryland tax return by attaching the DHCD certification to Form 502CR. Forms may be returned by email, drop off, or mail to Apple Ford Center at Athol Manor, 6680 Martin Road, Columbia, MD 21044 (or 10440 Little Patuxent Parkway, Suite 230, Columbia, MD 21044), or fax to 410.997.6021.

structured_extraction.program_name: Fund for Howard County Community Grants Program
structured_extraction.program_description: An annual competitive grant program through which the Community Foundation of Howard County (CFHC), in partnership with the Columbia Association, distributes funds to eligible 501(c)3 nonprofit organizations serving Howard County residents and workers. The program supports nonprofits working to strengthen quality of life in Howard County through essential services, education, arts and culture, health and wellness, human services, environment, civic programs, community engagement, mental health services, financial stability, and food security. Nonprofits may apply for either operational support or support for a specific program. Columbia Association contributes $125,000, which is combined with additional CFHC funds to create a grant pool of more than $200,000. The fund is guided by local knowledge, community partnerships, and a 13-member volunteer-led grant review committee made up of CFHC board members and community volunteers, including a representative from Columbia Association. In the 2025 cycle, $225,000 was distributed among 32 organizations, with individual awards ranging from $1,000 to $30,000, focusing on mental health services, financial stability, and food security. In the 2024 cycle, $185,500 was distributed across 50 organizations, with individual awards ranging from $1,000 to $5,000. In 2020, CFHC distributed $208,000 across 35 nonprofit organizations. Applications are reviewed based on future community impact, sustainability, and alignment with the Foundation's mission. The foundation connects donors with critical community needs through grantmaking, with each grant program having unique eligibility and application requirements.

In the 2025 cycle: up to $37,500 for organizations with budgets above $100,000 and up to $10,000 for organizations with budgets below $100,000; $225,000 was distributed among 32 organizations with individual awards ranging from $1,000 to $30,000. In the 2024 cycle: up to $10,000 for organizations with budgets above $100,000 and up to $5,000 for organizations with budgets below $100,000; $185,500 was distributed across 50 organizations with individual awards ranging from $1,000 to $5,000. In 2020, CFHC distributed $208,000 across 35 nonprofit organizations. Grant amounts vary and are determined through an annual volunteer-led grant review process. Applications are reviewed based on future community impact, sustainability, and alignment with the Foundation's mission.

structured_extraction.program_description: A permanent, flexible philanthropic fund established by the Community Foundation of Howard County to mobilize donations, coordinate grants, and support recovery and resilience during local crises and emergencies in Howard County. Originally activated to address the COVID-19 pandemic with a focus on food security, housing, childcare, and healthcare, the fund serves as a central repository for donations during any local emergency, allowing the Foundation to aggregate gifts, vet needs, and distribute grants to nonprofit partners and direct relief programs. For example, during the November 2025 'Neighbors in Need' campaign, over $12,000 was raised and distributed evenly between Columbia Community Care and the Howard County Food Bank (administered by Community Action Council of Howard County).

structured_extraction.program_name: Real Estate Charitable Foundation of Maryland (RECFM) (Real Estate Donation Facilitation)
structured_extraction.program_description: RECFM helps donors make gifts of real estate to charity. Donors transfer real property to RECFM, which handles the sale and transfers the net proceeds into a donor-advised fund at the Community Foundation of Howard County. Donors can then recommend grants from their fund to the causes they care about.
structured_extraction.agency: Community Foundation of Howard County / Frederick / Anne Arundel / Eastern Shore
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Donors gift residential, commercial, industrial, rural/agricultural, or undeveloped real estate (or a partnership interest in a real estate project) to RECFM. RECFM manages the sale, covers carrying and transfer costs, and places the net proceeds into a donor-advised fund in the donor's name at the Community Foundation of Howard County. Donors can then make grant recommendations from the fund. Benefits include maximizing tax deductions, potentially receiving income for life, avoiding capital gains on a 1031 exchange exit, and eliminating property management burdens.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals who own real estate they no longer want to maintain and wish to use it to support charitable causes, including those looking to maximize tax deductions or exit a 1031 exchange.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Proceeds from the sale of gifted real estate are placed in a donor-advised fund and used to make grants to charitable causes chosen by the donor.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Donors in Maryland or elsewhere who own real property that is environmentally clean and free (or can be freed) from mortgage liability.
requirements_list: Property must be environmentally clean
Property must be free or able to be freed from mortgage liability
Property should be income-generating or readily saleable after gifting
Eligible property types include residential, commercial, industrial, rural/agricultural, and undeveloped real estate, as well as partnership interests in real estate projects
If donor holds a controlling corporate interest, property must have been held more than one year to deduct a percentage of net profit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Email Beverly White-Seals at info@cfhoco.org or call (410) 730-7840 to initiate consideration of a gift through RECFM.

structured_extraction.program_description: A student-led grantmaking program run by the Community Foundation of Howard County's Youth in Philanthropy (YIP) program. A committee of Howard County high school sophomores and juniors (10th & 11th grade) solicits, evaluates, and awards grants to nonprofit organizations in Howard County each year. Students work in the community to raise money, build endowment funds, and make grants to nonprofit organizations with missions to improve and enhance lives in Howard County. Students learn about local community issues such as homelessness, hunger, domestic violence, arts, environment, and culture, then review grant proposals from local nonprofits and award grants to selected organizations. Students gain hands-on experience in philanthropy and community engagement by working directly with grant-seeking organizations, meeting with nonprofit leaders, observing operations, and evaluating proposals throughout the grant cycle. The program aims to prepare young people to be active, lifelong community citizens. The program has also conducted special grant rounds, including COVID-19 relief rounds in which student panels awarded larger totals to multiple Howard County nonprofits, funded through student fundraising and corporate/organizational matching gifts. The total amount available for grantmaking grows as the YIP fund receives more donations.
structured_extraction.agency: Community Foundation of Howard County / Frederick / Anne Arundel / Eastern Shore
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging from $500 to $10,000 per award in standard cycles (individual grants typically $500–$5,000, with total grantmaking of approximately $10,000 per standard cycle), distributed by a student committee to selected nonprofit applicants each year. Special grant rounds (e.g., COVID-19 relief) have awarded larger totals such as $20,000, with individual grants ranging from $2,000 to $5,000 per recipient. The total amount available for grantmaking grows as the YIP fund receives more donations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations in Howard County seeking grant funding, including organizations focused on homelessness, hunger, domestic violence, arts, environment, and culture; also targets Howard County high school sophomores and juniors (10th and 11th grade) with demonstrated interest in the welfare of others in Howard County who are interested in joining the student grantmaking committee.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: General support for nonprofit organizations and programs addressing local community needs in Howard County, including homelessness, hunger, domestic violence, educational and legal services, food access, meal delivery, senior transportation, school supplies, COVID-19 relief, general economic hardship relief, arts, environment, and culture.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to nonprofit organizations located in or serving Howard County, Maryland. Student applicants must reside in or attend high school in Howard County.
requirements_list: Must be a nonprofit organization
Must serve Howard County communities
Must submit a grant proposal for review by the YIP student committee
Grant proposals are evaluated based on community need and organizational effectiveness
Grant amounts range from $500 to $5,000 in standard cycles
Grants of $2,000 to $5,000 awarded in special rounds such as COVID-19 relief
Student committee members review and award all grants
Student applicants must attend Wednesday meetings 6PM-8PM
Student applicants must demonstrate interest in the welfare of others in Howard County
Student applicants must be responsible students
Student applicants must commit to meeting dates: January 27, February 24, March 31, April 28, 2021
Student applicants must complete application and participate in interview
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Nonprofits submit grant proposals which are reviewed by YIP student committee members. Students meet with nonprofit leaders, observe operations, evaluate proposals and organizational goals, then select grant recipients through virtual group discussions and nomination processes. The Community Foundation of Howard County solicits grant proposals from nonprofits each cycle. Students interested in joining the Youth in Philanthropy committee must complete and print the application form, submit via regular mail (not online), and participate in an interview. Students can also email yip@cfhoco.org with questions.

Funds can be used for leasehold improvements, equipment purchases, working capital, hiring (human capital increases), business expansion (including opening new locations), and business acquisition and start-up costs. The program supports business growth and job creation in Bowie, including areas designated as Maryland Priority Funding Areas. Loans may be used in combination with other loan funds as part of a larger aggregate financing package.

May be used in combination with other loan funds as part of a larger aggregate financing package (e.g., a $165,000 aggregate financing package).

Eligible projects include energy efficiency improvements, renewable energy measures (solar, fuel cells, geothermal, wind, waste-to-energy), energy conservation, energy storage, community solar, distributed energy generation, microgrids, clean transportation upgrades including EV charging stations, and resiliency measures. The program is part of the Prince George's County Green Bank, sponsored by Pepco/Exelon, and is administered by FSC First — a U.S. Treasury-certified Community Development Financial Institution (CDFI) — in partnership with the Maryland Energy Administration. structured_extraction.program_name: SBA 504 Commercial Real Estate Loan Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The SBA 504 Loan Program provides long-term, fixed-rate financing to small businesses for major fixed assets such as commercial real estate and equipment. FSC First, a Certified Development Company (CDC) designated by the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA), finances up to 40% of eligible project costs through 20-year to 25-year fixed-rate SBA 504 mortgages (or 10 years for machinery and equipment), while a third-party lender covers up to 50% and the business owner provides at least 10% equity. The program allows businesses to obtain up to 90% financing for expansion projects while retaining capital for cash flow. FSC First is authorized to serve as the CDC in any commercial real estate or equipment loan transaction in the State of Maryland. Examples include a $979,000 SBA 504 mortgage on a $2,400,000 project, a $4.7 million SBA 504 mortgage as part of a capital stack of over $15 million combining private bank funds, a partner interim lender, the Prince George's County EDI Fund, and the State of Maryland, a $1,260,000 loan covering real estate acquisition, improvement costs, and soft costs, and assistance to one borrower in acquiring a 35,560 square-foot warehouse on 3.38 acres in Frederick, MD.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Direct loans up to $5.5 million (or 40% of eligible project costs, whichever is less) for the CDC portion of the project. Fixed-rate, below-market financing with loan terms of 20–25 years for commercial real estate and 10 years for machinery and equipment with straight amortization. A minimum 10% cash down payment is typically required; start-ups or businesses with less than 3 years of profitable operating history, or limited-use facilities, may need at least 15% equity. Interest rates are determined at the time of underwriting. A private lender typically covers 50% of the project cost and the borrower contributes the remaining 10%. In one example, FSC First provided a $979,000 SBA 504 mortgage on a $2,400,000 project; in another, a $4.7 million SBA 504 mortgage as part of a capital stack of over $15 million; in a third, $1,260,000 covering real estate acquisition ($936,000), improvement costs ($385,000), and soft costs ($79,000); and in a fourth, a borrower acquired a 35,560 square-foot warehouse on 3.38 acres in Frederick, MD.
