structured_extraction.program_description: A federally-backed flood insurance program created by Congress in 1968 and administered by FEMA that makes flood insurance available to homeowners, renters, and business owners in communities that adopt and enforce floodplain management ordinances. Backed by the federal government through approximately 90 private insurance companies, the program provides an insurance alternative to disaster assistance for escalating costs of repairing flood damage to buildings and contents. Standard homeowners insurance typically does not cover flood damage; this program fills that gap by providing federally-backed flood insurance policies requiring a premium payment. Coverage extends to losses from storms, melting snow, hurricanes, water backup, broken water mains, and new construction-related flooding. Multiple Maryland counties participate in the NFIP voluntarily, including Washington County, Prince George's County, St. Mary's County (participating since February 19, 1987), and Montgomery County, enabling their residents to purchase federally-backed flood insurance. The program aims to reduce flood damage through community floodplain management and protect property owners from flood losses.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federally-backed flood insurance policies for property owners, renters, and business owners sold through approximately 90 private insurance companies and nearly 60,000 independent insurance agents. Coverage for homes includes up to $250,000 for the building and $100,000 for contents; non-residential buildings are covered up to $500,000 for the building and $500,000 for contents. A low-cost Preferred Risk Policy for low-to-moderate risk areas starts at $119/year for homeowners, $550/year for businesses, and $39/year for renters. A $100,000 flood insurance policy costs approximately $400 per year. Insurance costs vary depending on how much coverage is purchased, what it covers, and the property's flood risk. Prince George's County residents receive a 25% reduction in flood insurance premiums due to the county's Class 5 Community Rating System (CRS) designation. There is typically a 30-day waiting period before coverage takes effect from the date of purchase (waived if purchased with a mortgage loan). Applicants must pay a premium for flood insurance coverage. Not available in Coastal Barrier Resources System (CBRS) areas, Otherwise Protected Areas (OPAs), buildings principally below ground, or buildings entirely over water.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners, condo owners, apartment owners, renters, and business owners in communities that participate in the NFIP, including residents of Washington County, Prince George's County, St. Mary's County, Montgomery County, and other participating Maryland communities. Mandatory for residents with federally regulated mortgages on properties in high-risk Special Flood Hazard Areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Flood insurance coverage for physical damage to buildings and personal property/contents directly caused by flooding, including debris removal. Covers losses from storms, melting snow, hurricanes, water backup, broken water mains, and new construction-related flooding. Also provides flood insurance coverage for renters' personal property and liability protection.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in more than 20,200 communities across the United States and its territories that participate in the NFIP. In Maryland, participating communities include Washington County, Prince George's County, St. Mary's County, Montgomery County, and others. Any property located in a participating community is eligible for federally-backed flood insurance. Not available in Coastal Barrier Resources System (CBRS) areas or Otherwise Protected Areas (OPAs).
requirements_list: Must live or own property in a community that participates in the NFIP
Property must be located in a participating community such as Washington County, Prince George's County, St. Mary's County, or Montgomery County, Maryland
The participating community must adopt and enforce a floodplain management ordinance
Applicant must pay a premium for flood insurance coverage
Mandatory purchase required for properties in Special Flood Hazard Areas (A or V flood zones on FEMA FIRMs) when receiving federal or federally related financial assistance
Mandatory purchase also required for loans from federally regulated financial institutions on properties in Special Flood Hazard Areas
Montgomery County participates in the NFIP, making all properties in the County eligible
30-day waiting period before coverage takes effect (waived if purchased with a mortgage loan)
Not eligible: buildings principally below ground, buildings entirely over water, or properties in CBRS areas or Otherwise Protected Areas (OPAs)
Policy can be purchased with a credit card
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit FloodSmart.gov to find out what types of flood insurance are available, how to buy a policy, and how to find a provider. You may also speak with your insurance agent to purchase flood insurance through one of approximately 90 private insurance companies or nearly 60,000 independent agents. You may be able to purchase flood insurance with a credit card. Find flood insurance providers available for Maryland at floodsmart.gov. Call 1-800-427-4661 for more information, 1-888-435-6637 for agent referral, or TDD 1-800-427-5593. Contact an insurance agent for details on building and contents coverage options. Washington County Engineering can be reached at 240-313-2460 for local floodplain management questions.

structured_extraction.program_description: The foundation's largest funding area, covering K-12 public education, out-of-school time programs, independent private school scholarships and capital projects, and higher education. Priorities include improving literacy, socio-emotional learning, career readiness, post-secondary student success (especially for low-income, first-generation, and underrepresented students), and leveraging college and university anchor institutions to benefit surrounding communities in the Greater Baltimore area.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants for K-12 public and private education programs, out-of-school time initiatives, scholarships, capital projects, and higher education student success initiatives. Sample grants range from $45,000 to $120,000. The foundation has provided over $9 million to 19 universities supporting approximately 160 students per year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations, schools, colleges, and universities focused on K-12 education, out-of-school time programs, and higher education access and completion in the Greater Baltimore area, with emphasis on low-income, first-generation, and underrepresented students.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Improving literacy, socio-emotional learning and trauma interventions, career readiness education, scholarships for private schools and colleges, capital projects at independent schools, post-secondary student success initiatives, and community engagement by higher education anchor institutions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Primarily Baltimore City and the Greater Baltimore area.
requirements_list: Focus on K-12 public education, out-of-school time, independent private schools, or higher education
Projects should serve Baltimore City or Greater Baltimore area
Higher education grants should support low-income, first-generation, or underrepresented students
Scholarship support should increase diversity and inclusion
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: View sample grant descriptions on the foundation's website. See the 'Apply for a Grant' section for application details.

structured_extraction.program_description: The France-Merrick Foundation provides one-time, project-oriented grants to nonprofit organizations primarily within the greater Baltimore area and the State of Maryland. The Foundation focuses on capital projects, equipment, and technology that support its long-term priority areas in Baltimore, prioritizing shovel-ready projects rather than pre-development or early-stage capital work. Approximately 60% of funds support 'brick and mortar' capital projects, 30% equipment, and 20% nonprofit capacity building or other one-time needs. Annual giving and ongoing operational support are not favored. For 2025-2026, the Foundation has also launched the Meet the Moment Fund, a one-year grantmaking strategy responding to the impacts of recent public policy changes on Baltimore residents, neighborhoods, and nonprofits. Projects involving new construction or building renovation must incorporate sustainable building practices and energy conservation measures.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time grants for capital projects, equipment, and technology. Approximately 60% funds 'brick and mortar' capital projects, 30% equipment, and 20% nonprofit capacity building or other one-time needs. Requests under $50,000 are reviewed on a rolling monthly basis. Requests over $50,000 follow quarterly LOI closing dates with proposal and decision timelines. Overall review process takes 3-5 months depending on submission timing and grant size. Payments are made within one month of signed grant agreements. Specific award amounts vary by project. The Foundation does not fund individuals, special events, advertising, deficit financing, political activities, or general operating/annual giving. Projects involving new construction or building renovation must incorporate sustainable building practices and energy conservation measures.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling for requests under $50,000; quarterly closing dates for requests over $50,000 (next: May 29, 2026)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit 501(c)(3) organizations in the greater Baltimore area and Maryland seeking one-time capital funding for projects, equipment, or technology aligned with the Foundation's areas of focus.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital projects, equipment, and technology purchases; nonprofit capacity building; specific, time-limited projects with defined beginnings and endings. New construction or renovation projects must incorporate sustainable building and energy conservation practices.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Primarily Baltimore-focused; nearly 90% of grants in recent years have supported Baltimore City and/or Baltimore County. Anne Arundel, Howard, and Carroll counties are occasionally funded depending on connection to priorities, need, and competitive proposals. Environmental and historic preservation projects are considered throughout the State of Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a nonprofit organization holding 501(c)(3) status or have a fiscal sponsor with 501(c)(3) status in good standing
Must have at least three officers on the Board of Directors: president, secretary, and treasurer (per Maryland law)
Board must have at least 51% 'unrelated' voting board members (not related by family or business partnerships per U.S. law)
Submit a project-oriented request with a defined beginning and end
Annual giving and ongoing operational support requests are not favored
Submit a 1-3 page Letter of Inquiry (LOI) on official letterhead signed by the CEO/Executive Director
LOI must include legal name, address, tax ID, contact information, mission description, project description, total cost, funds committed, fundraising gap, amount requested, and project timeline
Must not have an outstanding prior grant (new requests require a two-year waiting period from the final payment date of a previous grant)
Do not submit more than one LOI at a time
Foundation prioritizes shovel-ready projects rather than pre-development or early-stage capital work
Must demonstrate financial stability to sustain the project
Must demonstrate adequate administrative capacity
Must demonstrate program effectiveness
Must be able to describe evaluation criteria, methods, and expected outcomes
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Review basic eligibility requirements and Application FAQs on the Foundation's website. 2. Submit a 1-3 page Letter of Inquiry (LOI) online via the Foundation's grant portal. 3. Foundation staff acknowledge receipt within 24 hours. 4. If invited, prepare and submit a full proposal within approximately one month, including project budget, organizational budget, board list, and audit. 5. A program officer reviews the proposal, often conducting a site visit. 6. Requests are presented to the Grants Committee; those over $50,000 go to the Board of Directors. 7. Sign a grant agreement and receive payment within one month. Overall review process takes 3-5 months depending on submission timing and grant size.

structured_extraction.program_description: The France-Merrick Foundation provides grants in health and human services to assist people facing multiple disadvantages. Funding focuses on improving health and wellness, increasing access to care for disadvantaged populations, strengthening community-based health care, food access and nutrition, housing and homelessness solutions, and capacity building for programs serving people with disabilities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of varying sizes (sample grants range from $45,000 to $500,000) for programs that improve health and wellness, increase access to care, support food banks and nutrition, address homelessness through housing placement and supportive services, and provide capital or one-time capacity building for disability services.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations and institutions serving disadvantaged populations in the Baltimore area, including those focused on health care, food access, housing, and disability services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Health and wellness programs, community-based health care, food distribution and nutrition education, rapid re-housing and permanent supportive housing, affordable housing creation, and capacity building for disability services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Primarily focused on East Baltimore and the greater Baltimore area.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: See the foundation's apply for a grant page at https://www.france-merrickfdn.org/apply-for-a-grant/ for application details.

structured_extraction.program_description: The France-Merrick Foundation funds projects that restore and maintain sites and properties of historical and architectural significance in the Baltimore region and Maryland. Grants support economic development through historic assets, community education about local history, and efforts to strengthen the regional preservation movement. The Foundation prioritizes projects that impact community development and environmental sustainability.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of varying amounts awarded to support restoration and maintenance of historically and architecturally significant sites in the Baltimore region and Maryland. Sample grants range from $48,000 to $200,000.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profits, organizations, and entities working to restore, maintain, and promote historically and architecturally significant sites and properties in the Baltimore region and Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Restoring and maintaining sites and properties of historical and architectural significance; education about community history; strengthening regional preservation capacity; community development and environmental sustainability projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Primary focus on the Baltimore region and Maryland statewide.
requirements_list: Projects must focus on restoring or maintaining historically or architecturally significant sites
Projects should be located in the Baltimore region or Maryland
Priority given to projects that positively impact community development
Priority given to projects that contribute to environmental sustainability
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the Foundation's grant application page for details on how to apply.

structured_extraction.program_description: A one-year grantmaking initiative providing short-term financial support to Baltimore-area nonprofits responding to disruptions caused by recent public policy and funding changes. The fund helps organizations prevent service disruptions, support strategic sustainability responses, and build collaborative structures to meet community needs with reduced resources. It offers one-time operating grants on a rolling basis for bridge funding, service transitions, organizational restructuring, mergers, and collaborative or capacity-building responses to major funding or policy changes. Up to 40% of the Foundation's annual distribution is allocated to this fund, which runs through the fiscal year July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time operating grants (short-term gap support and strategic response grants) provided on a rolling basis with decisions made once a month via an expedited review process. Grants can cover bridge funding while awaiting withheld or restructured resources; costs related to service discontinuation, workforce reductions, or client transitions; organizational restructuring, mergers, or consolidations; capacity building, pooled funds, cohorts for planning, and shared services. Collaborative grants for groups of nonprofits jointly addressing sector-wide changes are also available. Up to 40% of the Foundation's annual distribution is allocated to this fund.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis, decided once a month; expedited rolling review during fiscal year July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Prior France-Merrick Foundation grantees (including current grantees) and nonprofits or groups of nonprofits in Baltimore collaboratively responding to public policy changes that affect housing, health, education, safety, environmental protection, arts, historic preservation, or community development, whose organizations face risks or losses due to changes in public policy or funding.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Bridge funding while awaiting withheld or restructured resources; costs related to service discontinuation, workforce reductions, or client transitions; organizational restructuring, mergers, or consolidations; capacity building, pooled funds, cohorts for planning, and shared services; gap support for operational sustainability and strategic collaborative responses to disruptions caused by public funding cuts or policy changes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must serve the Baltimore area.
requirements_list: Must be a prior France-Merrick Foundation grantee or collaborating with other nonprofits in Baltimore
Must serve the Baltimore area
Must advance one or more of the Foundation's Areas of Focus
Organization or work must face risks and losses due to changes in public policy or funding
Must have a plan for future operational sustainability (fund is not intended to sustain programs without such a plan)
Must be responding to impacts of recent public policy changes
Must be a 501(c)(3) nonprofit or have a fiscal sponsor
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Reach out to a Foundation program officer to discuss your idea before applying. Then submit a 2-3 page request on official letterhead, signed by the CEO or Executive Director, through the Foundation's online portal. The request must include the organization's legal name, address, tax ID, contact information, mission and program description, description of the proposed project, narrative of funding loss or policy change impact and pathway to sustainability, and timeline. Attach a list of board of directors, current operating budget, latest audit (if applicable), and IRS 501(c)(3) determination letter. An expedited review process is used to accelerate grant decisions, with decisions made once a month on a rolling basis.

Scholarships help seniors participate in classes such as strength training, yoga, Zumba, and line dance regardless of their ability to pay.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Paying for fitness class fees at 50+ Community Centers.

Must be a participant at a Frederick County 50+ Community Center
Must complete a scholarship application form

structured_extraction.program_description: This grant helps Frederick County agricultural producers expand or diversify their business operations to improve economic viability. Eligible applicants can receive funding for research and development, production buildings, major fixtures, and processing facilities. The program supports innovation in farming and agribusiness through a competitive scoring process.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are awarded to eligible agricultural producers through a competitive scoring process based on a 100-point rubric that evaluates project description, budget, innovation, economic impact, and business plan quality. Funds can be used for research and development, production buildings, major fixtures, and processing facilities. Monthly expense substantiation reports are required until grant funds are fully expended.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: The next cycle will open October 1, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Crop or livestock producers, value-added producers, agricultural cooperatives, seafood processors, and primary or secondary timber products processors operating in Frederick County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Research and development, production buildings, major fixtures, and processing facilities. Eligible expense categories include materials, advertising, travel, and other project-related costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be currently operating in Frederick County for at least one year.
requirements_list: Must be currently operating in Frederick County for at least one year
Must have recorded at least $2,500 in annual sales OR include an outline of investment and its impact on future sales in the business plan
Must provide documented evidence of outreach to Planning & Zoning (tdesa@frederickcountymd.gov) discussing requirements of the proposed project for the current cycle
Must fall into one of these categories: crop or livestock producer, value-added producer, agricultural cooperative, seafood processor, or primary or secondary timber products processor
If property owner or immediate family member is not the applicant, must submit a signed rental agreement with terms
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Develop a business plan using available resources (University of Minnesota, Maryland SBDC, Maryland Women's Business Center). 2. Contact the Frederick County Zoning Office to confirm the project is an allowed use. 3. If the project involves additional waste discharge, contact the Frederick County Health Department. 4. If the property is under a Land Preservation Easement, contact Shannon O'Neil to verify allowed use. 5. Prepare a detailed budget broken down by expense category. 6. Prepare a 'Capital Needed' description. 7. Write an Economic Impact Description. 8. Submit the completed application during the open grant cycle.

structured_extraction.program_description: Frederick County residents can join the Ambulance Transport Subscription Club to reduce out-of-pocket costs for ambulance transport services. Insurance reimbursement is accepted as complete payment; no additional balance is billed to the member for covered BLS and ALS transports by Frederick County EMS.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Covers cost of BLS and ALS ambulance transports by Frederick County EMS for covered emergency calls resulting in transport

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides affordable rental housing for low-income elderly residents aged 62 or older in Woodsboro, Maryland. Tenants must have an annual income at or below 50% of the Area Median Income (AMI), with priority for those at or below 30% AMI. Tenants must have an annual income at or below 50% of the Area Median Income (AMI). There are typically no more than 1-2 vacancies per year.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Affordable rental housing

Annual income must be at or below 50% of the Area Median Income (AMI)

Participants get hands-on work experience with mentorship from experienced professionals, skill-building opportunities, and exposure to diverse roles across Frederick County Government departments.

structured_extraction.program_name: Commercial Property Assessed Clean Energy Loans (C-PACE)
structured_extraction.program_description: C-PACE provides commercial property owners with up to 100% up-front financing to make energy efficiency, renewable energy, water conservation, environmental remediation, and resiliency building upgrades. Loans are repaid over up to 20 years through a surcharge on the property's state tax bill, which transfers with the property if it is sold. Projects can be cash flow positive from day one. The program is administered through Frederick County and is available to commercial property owners throughout Maryland.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans of up to 100% financing for eligible clean energy and resiliency projects on commercial properties. Repaid over up to 20 years through a surcharge on the property's state tax bill. The repayment obligation transfers with the property upon sale. Projects can be cash flow positive from day one.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Commercial property owners, businesses, and nonprofits in Maryland seeking to finance energy efficiency, renewable energy, water conservation, environmental remediation, or resiliency improvements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Building energy efficiency upgrades, renewable energy systems (solar, geothermal, wind), water conservation projects, environmental remediation (indoor air/water quality, asbestos, lead paint, mold), resiliency projects (flood mitigation, stormwater management, fire/wind resistance, EV charging, energy storage), and all associated project costs including audits, design, installation, and loan closing costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to commercial property owners throughout Maryland. Program is administered by Frederick County.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a commercial property owner.
Project must fall within eligible categories: energy efficiency, renewable energy, water conservation, environmental remediation, or resiliency.
Upgrades must save energy and lower operating costs.

Review the C-PACE program details using the linked PDF at https://www.discoverfrederickmd.com/DocumentCenter/View/96/Commercial-Property-Assessed-Clean-Energy-Loans-PDF. Additional information is available at https://www.mdcleanenergy.org/programs/commercial-property-financing/ or by contacting Frederick County Economic Development at fcoed@frederickcountymd.gov.

structured_extraction.program_name: Food Equity and Emergency Distribution Grant Program (FEED)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Frederick County FEED Grant Program provides grant funding to local nonprofits, food banks, pantries, religious organizations, and other groups that supply food and essential services to Frederick County residents facing food insecurity. It was created in response to federal government shutdown impacts and SNAP benefit delays. The program is administered by the Community Foundation of Frederick County with funding from Frederick County, Maryland. Total available funding is $1,000,000 split across two rounds ($500,000 per round), with a grant period of June 1, 2026 – December 31, 2026.

Total available funding is $1,000,000 split across two rounds ($500,000 per round). Funds may be used for food distribution and meal programs, general operating support for food-related initiatives, administrative overhead directly tied to food service delivery, and capital purchases such as refrigerators, freezers, and food storage equipment. Vehicles are not eligible.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Food distribution and meal programs, general operating support for food-related initiatives, administrative overhead directly tied to food service delivery, and capital purchases (e.g., refrigerators, freezers, food storage). Vehicles are not eligible.

structured_extraction.program_description: Frederick County residents can earn money by serving as election judges (poll workers) during early voting and on Election Day. Election judges greet voters, manage check-in, issue ballots, assist with voting equipment, or oversee polling place operations. Responsibilities include setting up and breaking down the polling place, checking in and assisting voters, and overseeing election procedures to uphold the integrity of the electoral process. All judges must attend mandatory training and work their assigned days.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Voting Operations Judges and Provisional Judges receive $250 per day worked during early voting and on Election Day, plus a one-time $50 payment for attending mandatory training. Chief Judges receive $300 per day worked, plus a one-time $50 training payment. Judges must work all assigned days to receive the training pay. Mandatory training is provided, and reasonable accommodations are available.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Registered Maryland voters (including 16- and 17-year-olds with parental consent) who are reliable, civic-minded individuals able to commit to working election days in Frederick County. No prior experience is needed.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Compensation for time worked as an election judge during early voting and/or Election Day, plus mandatory training attendance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a registered voter in the State of Maryland and be able to work at an assigned polling place in Frederick County.
requirements_list: Must be a registered voter in the State of Maryland
16- and 17-year-olds may serve but must have parental or guardian consent
Must be able to speak, read, and write in English
Must be able to work at least 15 hours
Must be able to stand (some positions require standing for long periods)
Must be able to lift items weighing up to 25 pounds
Must have own transportation and arrive at polling place by 5:45 AM on assigned days
Must stay until the polling place is closed, cleaned, and dismissed by the Chief Judge
Must not leave the polling place except for medical emergencies
Must be able to help set up the evening before Election Day (Election Day only, not Early Voting)
Must attend a three to three-and-a-half hour mandatory training class
Must be courteous to voters and team members
Must not engage in partisan or political activity or discussions while at the polling place
Cannot be a candidate, chair, campaign manager, or treasurer for a candidate or political committee
Must not be a public or political office holder
Must be available for election dates (Primary: June 23, 2026; General: November 3, 2026)
Willing to work outside home precinct (flexibility preferred)
Must be able to work at the assigned polling place
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online or download and return a printable form by fax, mail, or email. Applicants aged 16 or 17 must also submit a parental permission form. All new and returning election judges must reapply each election year they wish to serve. Applicants will be notified by the local election office if selected.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free resource for businesses in Frederick County that helps improve employee commutes. The program provides expert guidance on commuter benefits, carpool and vanpool coordination, telework program development, bicycle commuting incentives, compressed work week arrangements, personalized commute plans for employees, onboarding and educational materials, workplace events and surveys, and connections to regional incentive programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free commuter program development and technical assistance for employers, including help launching transit subsidies, carpool and vanpool coordination, telework policies, bicycle commuting incentives, and compressed work week arrangements. Also connects employees and employers to financial incentives such as the Vanpool Incentive Program, CommuterCash, and Guaranteed Ride Home.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses and employers located in Frederick County seeking to improve employee commutes and reduce traffic congestion and parking challenges.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Developing and supporting commuter benefit programs, including transit subsidies, vanpool coordination, telework policies, bicycle commuting incentives, employee onboarding materials, and workplace commute events and surveys.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Employer Connection at support@frederickcountyec.com or the Transit Rideshare Coordinator at mdennis1@frederickcountymd.gov to learn more or request support.

structured_extraction.program_name: Frederick County Green Homes Appliance Rebate Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A county program that provides rebates to help low- to moderate-income homeowners in Frederick County make their homes more energy-efficient by upgrading to ENERGY STAR certified electric appliances. Rebates cover up to 65% of the cost of qualifying new ENERGY STAR certified electric appliances purchased from a licensed retail establishment, as part of efforts to make sustainability accessible and affordable for all residents. The program is currently paused pending new funding; interested applicants may sign up to be notified when rebates become available again.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rebates covering up to 65% of the cost of new ENERGY STAR certified electric appliances for eligible low- to moderate-income households to help lower energy costs. The program is currently paused pending new funding; interested applicants may sign up to be notified when rebates become available again.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low- to moderate-income homeowners in Frederick County looking to upgrade to energy-efficient appliances and lower energy costs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of new ENERGY STAR certified electric or qualifying green home appliances.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Frederick County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Household must be low- to moderate-income
Must be a Frederick County household
Appliances must be ENERGY STAR certified electric appliances
Appliances must be purchased from a licensed retail establishment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The program is currently paused pending new funding. Interested applicants can email GreenHomes@FrederickCountyMD.gov to be notified when rebates become available again. More information is available at frederickcountymd.gov/8741/Green-Homes-Appliance-Rebate-Program.

structured_extraction.program_name: Frederick County Historic District Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A five-year decreasing property tax credit on improvements made to existing structures within the Frederick County historic district, supporting preservation and redevelopment of residential and commercial properties. Enacted in 1975 and revised in 1990, the credit encourages preservation and rehabilitation of historically significant properties in Frederick County.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A five-year decreasing property tax credit on improvements made to existing structures within the Frederick County historic district. Enacted in 1975 and revised in 1990, the credit reduces property tax liability for eligible historically significant properties.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners making improvements to existing structures within the Frederick County historic district.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of property tax liability on improvements to historic district structures.

requirements_list: Property must be located within the historic district
Improvements must be made to existing structures
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Application form submission required. Refer to the Historic District Tax Credit document available on the Frederick County website or download the information sheet from the Frederick County Economic Development website.

structured_extraction.program_description: Helps local families with limited resources purchase their first home by providing up to $12,000 in down payment and closing cost assistance. The application is submitted on behalf of the homebuyer by the first lender.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides up to $12,000 in down payment and/or closing cost assistance. Other homebuyer assistance programs may be used alongside this program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: First-time homebuyers in Frederick County with limited financial resources.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment and closing costs for a home purchase.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Frederick County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a first-time homebuyer
Must meet income limits
Property must meet lead paint requirements
Must complete homebuyer education training
Application submitted by first lender on behalf of homebuyer
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Application is submitted by the first (mortgage) lender on behalf of the homebuyer. Homebuyer must complete required homebuyer education training through the City of Frederick (call 301-600-2077 or 301-600-3974 for schedule information).

structured_extraction.program_name: Frederick County Innovative Technology Center, Inc. (FITCI)
structured_extraction.program_description: FITCI is a business incubator that supports early-stage life science and technology companies in Frederick County. It offers office and wet lab space, business services, coaching, and strategic support to help startups in biomedicine, agricultural technology, and renewable energy grow into commercially viable businesses.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: FITCI provides early-stage companies with physical space (office and wet lab), business services, coaching, and connections to capital and resources. The incubator has two locations in Frederick, MD: 4359 Metropolitan Court and 321 Ballenger Center Drive (The EDGE @ 321).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Early-stage life science and technology startups, including companies in biomedicine, agricultural technology, and renewable energy, located in or near Frederick County, MD.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Office and wet lab space, business services, coaching, and access to capital and strategic resources.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Frederick County, Maryland. Two locations in the City of Frederick.
requirements_list: Must be an early-stage life science or technology company
Focus areas include biomedicine, agricultural technology, and renewable energy
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the FITCI website at www.fitci.org for information on how to apply to the incubator program.

structured_extraction.program_name: Frederick County No Business Personal Property Tax
structured_extraction.program_description: Frederick County does not assess or impose a local business personal property tax, meaning businesses pay a 0% rate on furniture, fixtures, equipment, machinery, and computers used in operations. This provides considerable savings compared to neighboring jurisdictions and significantly reduces ongoing operating costs for all businesses, including data centers and life sciences/biotech companies.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A 0% business personal property tax rate applies county-wide. No local business personal property tax is levied on furniture, fixtures, equipment, machinery, and computers used in business operations in Frederick County, reducing ongoing operating costs. Businesses pay no personal property tax on business assets in Frederick County, with considerable savings compared to neighboring jurisdictions.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses operating in Frederick County, Maryland, particularly data centers, life sciences, and biotech companies.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Ongoing reduction of tax burden and operating costs through elimination of local personal property tax on business equipment and other business assets.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Frederick County, Maryland only
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Automatic benefit for businesses located in Frederick County; no separate application required.

structured_extraction.program_name: Frederick County Power Saver Retrofits Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Power Saver Retrofits (PSR) program provides free home energy assessments and energy-saving improvements at no cost to low- to moderate-income households in Frederick County. A certified contractor audits the home, then performs approved upgrades to reduce energy use and lower energy bills. Eligible improvements include air sealing, insulation, duct sealing, weatherstripping, lighting upgrades, heat pump water heater replacements, HVAC tune-ups or upgrades to Energy Star models, and up to $1,500 for health and safety repairs related to energy improvements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free home energy audit and no-cost energy-saving improvements including air sealing, insulation, duct sealing, weatherstripping, lighting upgrades, heat pump water heater replacements, HVAC tune-ups or upgrades to Energy Star models, and up to $1,500 for health and safety repairs related to energy improvements.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low- to moderate-income Frederick County homeowners with gross household income below 85% of Frederick County median income based on family size.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home energy improvements: air sealing, insulation, window and door caulking, weatherstripping, duct sealing, energy-efficient lighting, heat pump water heaters, HVAC upgrades, and health/safety repairs up to $1,500.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Frederick County resident.
requirements_list: Must be a low- to moderate-income household
Must be a Frederick County resident
Must be a registered participant in Frederick County's Green Homes Challenge
Gross household income must be less than 85% of Frederick County median income based on family size (e.g., $68,500 for 1 person, $97,800 for 4 people)
Condo, mobile home, and rental property residents should contact the PSR Coordinator to discuss eligibility
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at the county website (preferred) or request a print application by calling 301-600-1416 or emailing PSR@FrederickCountyMD.gov. Applications are reviewed for eligibility. If approved, a certified contractor schedules an energy audit. A list of projects is reviewed and approved by County staff and the homeowner before work begins.

structured_extraction.program_name: Frederick County Senior Tax Credit (Elderly Individuals Tax Credit)
structured_extraction.program_description: A supplemental property tax credit for qualifying senior/elderly homeowners in Frederick County, enacted on January 3, 2012. It supplements the State Homeowner Tax Credit and the existing Frederick County Homeowner Tax Credit supplement to reduce property tax burdens for eligible older residents. The credit equals 20% of net county real property taxes, reducing the amount owed down to zero. It does not apply to the lighting district tax, community development authority tax, or fees such as the System Benefit Charge, Bay Restoration Fee, or Stormwater Remediation Fee.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A county-level supplemental tax credit equal to 20% of net Frederick County real property taxes, reducing the amount owed down to zero. Supplements the State Homeowner Tax Credit Program. Does not apply to the lighting district tax, community development authority tax, or fees such as the System Benefit Charge, Bay Restoration Fee, or Stormwater Remediation Fee. Application may be made through the Maryland Homeowners' Property Tax Credit Program or by completing the Elderly Individuals Tax Credit Application available on the Frederick County website.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Senior/elderly homeowners in Frederick County, Maryland who are at least 65 years old and meet income eligibility requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of real property tax liability for eligible senior/elderly homeowners in Frederick County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to homeowners in Frederick County, Maryland.
requirements_list: At least 65 years of age
Meet income eligibility requirements
Must be a senior homeowner meeting state and county eligibility criteria
Apply using the State Homeowner Tax Credit form
Application is administered through the State Homeowner Tax Credit Program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply using the State Homeowner Tax Credit form, administered by the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) at dat.maryland.gov, which covers state, county, and municipal credits. Alternatively, complete and submit the Elderly Individuals Tax Credit Application available on the Frederick County website. For more information, contact the Frederick County Treasury Department at 301-600-1111.

structured_extraction.program_description: Free classes that teach residents how to compost at home. Classes cover the science of composting and help participants set up a simple system that works for their household. Classes are held at the DSWM Reichs Ford Road facility and include a facility tour.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Composting education and training
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Frederick County, Maryland
requirements_list: Advance registration is required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Email or call 301-600-2960 to inquire about future class dates or to set up a custom program for your community group.

structured_extraction.program_name: Getting Ahead Workshop – United Way of Frederick County
structured_extraction.program_description: An immersive 16-session workshop that helps participants create individual plans toward self-sufficiency. The program helps people identify their own strengths and establish a strong support network.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 16-session immersive workshop helping participants build individual self-sufficiency plans and support networks.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Self-sufficiency planning and support network development
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Frederick County, Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the program by phone or visit the program website.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state-designated enterprise zone program designed to promote business growth along Route 40 west in the City of Frederick, offering property tax credits and income tax credits for job creation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Local and real property tax credits for up to 10 years on capital investment, plus state income tax credits for creating new jobs. The income tax credit is a one-time maximum of $1,000 per newly created position.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses locating or expanding along Route 40 west in the City of Frederick.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax relief on capital investment and income tax credits for new job creation.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the City of Frederick Department of Economic Development for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Golden Mile Tax Credit and Arts and Entertainment Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: State/county and City of Frederick tax credits that encourage property owners to rehabilitate commercial buildings along the Golden Mile (Route 40 West corridor) in Frederick, Maryland, and within the Downtown Frederick Arts and Entertainment District. The program provides decreasing tax abatement on building improvements over 7 years for rehabilitation of existing structures.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A decreasing tax abatement on building improvements over 7 years for rehabilitation of existing structures located along Route 40 West (Golden Mile corridor) and within the Downtown Frederick Arts and Entertainment District. The credit is administered jointly by Frederick County and the City of Frederick.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax relief on building improvements for rehabilitation of existing commercial structures along the Golden Mile corridor and in the Downtown Frederick Arts and Entertainment District.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Route 40 West (Golden Mile) corridor and Downtown Frederick Arts and Entertainment District within the City of Frederick, Maryland.

Property must be a commercial building
Project must involve rehabilitation of an existing structure
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download the Golden Mile Tax Credit and Arts and Entertainment Tax Credit information sheet from the Frederick County Economic Development website, and submit a Golden Mile Tax Credit Application (PDF available on the City of Frederick website).

structured_extraction.program_description: Green Compass provides Community Navigators who help Frederick County residents find, understand, and benefit from local, state, and federal programs and incentives to improve their home environment, lower energy costs, and live more sustainably. Navigators assess residents' needs, connect them to available programs and incentives, help complete applications, and provide referrals to partner organizations. Navigators also offer outreach to community groups to teach sustainable practices, with special attention to underserved communities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free one-on-one navigation support to help residents identify and apply for programs related to energy-efficient appliances, solar panels, electric vehicles and chargers, home energy improvements, and sustainability resources. Community Navigators provide personalized guidance to access local, state, and federal programs and incentives for home energy efficiency and sustainable living.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Frederick County residents, especially those in underserved communities, seeking guidance on sustainability and energy efficiency programs and incentives
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Navigator assistance to identify and apply for programs covering energy-efficient appliances, renewable energy (solar), electric vehicles and chargers, home energy improvements, and sustainability resources to improve home environment, lower energy costs, and support sustainable living
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Frederick County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a Frederick County resident
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact a Navigator by email at GreenHomes@FrederickCountyMD.gov or by phone at 301-600-1416, or visit the Green Compass program page at frederickcountymd.gov/8662/Green-Compass to learn more and connect with a Community Navigator.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free program that helps households in Frederick County learn eco-friendly actions, track progress toward sustainability goals, and earn certifications. Participants can reduce energy use, conserve resources, and adopt renewable energy through three challenge tracks: Power Saver, Green Leader, and Renewable Star.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free interactive program providing tips, action tracking, and certifications for households. No direct financial payment — participants earn points toward three certifications (Power Saver, Green Leader, Renewable Star) and may achieve utility bill savings by following recommended energy-efficiency and sustainability actions.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners and renters in Frederick County who want to reduce their environmental impact and save money on utility bills.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Guidance and certification for energy efficiency, resource conservation, and renewable energy adoption at the household level.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to households in Frederick County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Open to any household — renters or homeowners, urban or rural
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit FrederickGreenChallenge.org to register, choose actions, earn points, and work toward certification.

structured_extraction.program_description: A county program that helps Frederick County households live more sustainably by connecting residents with local, state, and federal programs, offering incentives, and providing community navigator support. The program especially focuses on low- to moderate-income households, elderly, minority, and disabled residents who face greater challenges adapting to climate change.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program has multiple components: (1) Green Compass provides Community Navigators to help residents find and use programs and incentives to improve home energy efficiency; (2) Green Homes Challenge offers incentives for sustainable actions; (3) Green Incentives offer financial help, including Power Saver Retrofits for low- to moderate-income households and Septic Rebates open to any household with a septic system; (4) Green Partnerships connects underserved communities with sustainability resources.
structured_extraction.program_audience: All Frederick County residents, with a focus on low- to moderate-income households, elderly, minority, and disabled individuals who may need extra support to reduce energy use and adapt to climate risks.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home energy improvements, renewable energy adoption, sustainable living actions, and septic system upgrades.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Frederick County, Maryland residents.
requirements_list: Must be a Frederick County resident
Power Saver Retrofits are limited to low- to moderate-income households
Septic Rebates require the household to have a septic system
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact GreenHomes@FrederickCountyMD.gov to connect with staff or attend an info session. Follow @SustainableFCMD on Facebook and Instagram for event updates.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free monthly distribution of seasonal produce, canned goods, and shelf-stable products for eligible Frederick County seniors. The event is held in a farmers market style setting and includes additional resources and information.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free monthly food distribution including seasonal produce, canned goods, and shelf-stable products. Participants receive food at no cost on the 3rd Friday of each month at noon (continuing until all food is distributed) at the Frederick Senior Center, 1440 Taney Avenue, Frederick, MD 21702.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Frederick County residents age 60 or older with a monthly income at or below $1,600.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Food — seasonal produce, canned goods, and shelf-stable grocery items.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Frederick County, Maryland only.

Must be age 60 or older
Must have a monthly income at or below $1,600
Must bring a photo ID to register the first time

structured_extraction.program_description: A home visiting program for first-time expectant parents or parents with a child under 3 months old. Based on the national Healthy Families America model, the program provides strength-based home visiting services to help families become self-sufficient and prepare children to enter school healthy, nurtured, and ready to learn.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home visiting support, family self-sufficiency, and early childhood development
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Frederick County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a first-time expectant parent or have a child under 3 months old
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the program by phone or visit the program website.

structured_extraction.program_name: Helping Empower Area Resources Together (HEART) Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The HEART Grant Program provides one-time emergency grants of up to $50,000 to eligible nonprofit 501(c)(3) organizations in Frederick County that were impacted by the federal government shutdown. Grants support organizations that deliver direct services and resources to Frederick County residents by covering operational expenses, addressing revenue gaps, or expanding essential services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time lump-sum grants ranging up to 10% of the nonprofit's approved annual operating budget, but not to exceed $50,000. Total program funding is approximately $1,500,000. Funds must be expended by June 30, 2026 and used for operational expenses resulting from revenue shortfalls, increased demand for services, or expansion of essential direct services to Frederick County residents.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit 501(c)(3) organizations physically located in Frederick County that serve a majority of Frederick County residents and were impacted by the federal government shutdown.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operational expenses resulting from revenue gaps or shortfalls; operational expenses from increased demand for services; or expansion of essential direct services to Frederick County residents.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Organization must have a physical location in Frederick County and serve more than 51% Frederick County residents.
requirements_list: Must be a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization
Must have a physical location/address in Frederick County and serve a majority (over 51%) of Frederick County residents
Must be in good standing with the IRS, Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation's Personal Property Tax Division, and Frederick County Government
Must have been established prior to July 1, 2022, and plan to continue operating through at least June 30, 2026
Must demonstrate impact from the federal government shutdown (e.g., decreased revenue, increased costs, financial insecurity)

Churches and religious organizations, fraternal and/or civic organizations, homeowner's associations, labor unions, private/political/public foundations, cemeteries, and volunteer fire departments are not eligible
Nonprofit organizations operating under an umbrella or fiscal sponsor are not eligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Frederick County online grant portal (Foundant). New users must create an account. Applications require: a finalized budget with actuals for the last two fiscal years and year-to-date current fiscal year; proof of good standing with Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation; IRS Nonprofit Designation Letter; financial statements for the most recent past year; and the most recent IRS Form 990 or E-Postcard. Applications are reviewed by staff from the Grant Management Department, who recommend award amounts to the County Executive for final approval.

structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit that limits how much a homeowner's taxable property assessment can increase each year. Frederick County limits annual increases to 5% for owner-occupied residential properties, helping homeowners avoid large tax increases from rising assessments.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Limits the annual taxable assessment increase for owner-occupied residential properties to 5% for county taxes and 10% for state taxes. Applied automatically to eligible properties.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owner-occupied residential property owners in Frederick County who have lived in the residence for at least 12 months prior to the issuance of the tax bill.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction in taxable property assessment increases to limit property tax bills.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland, including Frederick County.
requirements_list: Property must be listed as 'Principal Residence'
Property owner must have lived in the residence for 12 months prior to the bill issuance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Automatically applied to eligible properties. If eligible but did not receive the credit, contact SDAT at 301-815-5350 or visit the SDAT website.

structured_extraction.program_description: Helps full-time regular employees who are using a Maryland Mortgage Program (MMP) 1st Time Advantage or Flex 6000 loan product by matching the MMP $8,500 zero percent deferred loan with an equal $8,500 deferred loan, for a total of $17,000 in down payment and/or closing cost assistance. No monthly payments are required; the loan is deferred until the home is sold or refinanced.

No monthly payments required; repayment deferred until the home is sold or refinanced.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment and/or closing costs for a home purchase.

Must meet eligibility and income limit requirements
Property must meet lead paint requirements
Must complete required homebuyer education training
Application submitted by first lender on behalf of homebuyer

structured_extraction.program_description: The Housing Choice Voucher (HCV) Program, also known as Section 8, provides rental assistance to eligible low-income households so they can afford housing in the private rental market. Qualified tenants pay approximately 30%–40% of their income toward rent and utilities, and the housing agency pays the remaining monthly subsidy directly to the landlord on the tenant's behalf.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Variable monthly rent subsidies paid directly to landlords on behalf of eligible tenants. Tenants pay approximately 30%–40% of their income toward rent and utilities; the agency covers the remainder up to the applicable payment standard. Units are inspected and families are recertified annually.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental assistance for housing in the private rental market.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Frederick County, Maryland.

Must qualify based on family income (pays approximately 30%–40% of income toward rent and utilities)
Units must pass inspection
Families must be recertified annually
Must keep contact information (especially mailing address) updated on the waiting list
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The waiting list is currently closed. Address and contact changes must be submitted in writing using the Change Form to the Frederick County Department of Housing at 401 Sagner Avenue, Frederick, MD 21701.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides long-term individual vouchers for federally funded rental housing assistance, allowing qualified families to rent private market properties.

structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Frederick County, Maryland
