structured_extraction.program_description: Frederick County exempts 100% of commercial and research and development (R&D) inventory from personal property tax.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 100% exemption from personal property tax on commercial and R&D inventory held in Frederick County.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Commercial businesses and R&D organizations with inventory located in Frederick County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduces personal property tax liability on commercial and R&D inventory.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Frederick County, Maryland
requirements_list: Inventory must be commercial or research and development inventory
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Automatic benefit for qualifying businesses in Frederick County; no separate application described.

structured_extraction.program_name: Lead Hazard Reduction Grant and Loan Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides funds to help homeowners and landlords reduce or eliminate lead-based paint hazards in their homes. Eligible activities include door and window treatment, floor treatments, paint removal, stabilization and repainting, encapsulation, enclosure, and specialized cleaning. Funding is provided as a grant or loan depending on the applicant's ability to repay.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Funding is provided as a grant or loan based on the applicant's ability to repay. The maximum loan term is 20 years. There are no income limits for the program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners and landlords in Frederick County, Maryland, including owners of rental properties and licensed childcare facilities, seeking to reduce lead-based paint hazards.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Door and window treatment, floor treatments, paint removal, stabilization and repainting, encapsulation, enclosure, and specialized cleaning to reduce or eliminate lead-based paint hazards.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties must be located in Frederick County, Maryland. Grant-eligible units must be in a targeted census tract.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Maryland resident living in an owner-occupied property used as the principal residence; rental properties and licensed childcare facilities are also eligible
Units must be in need of lead hazard reduction activity
Units must be structurally sound upon completion of lead reduction work
Units seeking a grant must be in a targeted census tract
Rental properties built prior to 1950 must be registered with the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) Lead Poisoning Prevention Program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Frederick County Housing Division to apply. The applicant's ability to repay will determine whether funds are issued as a grant or a loan.

structured_extraction.program_description: Frederick County's Division of Aging and Independence contracts with a local legal services provider to offer free legal advice and representation to Frederick County residents aged 60 and older. Services are funded through the Older Americans Act and cover a range of elder law issues including consumer complaints, housing, health insurance, Social Security, and more.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free legal advice and, when necessary, legal representation. Services include community education, outreach to homebound individuals and those in long-term care facilities, and advice on elder law and legal rights topics such as consumer complaints, debt collection, evictions, food stamps, foreclosures, garnishments, health insurance, medical assistance, Medicare, Social Security, and SSI.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Frederick County residents aged 60 and older, including homebound individuals and those in long-term care facilities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Legal advice and representation on elder law issues including housing, benefits, consumer protection, and more.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Frederick County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a Frederick County resident
Must be aged 60 or older
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Frederick County Division of Aging and Independence at 301-600-1234 for a referral to the contracted legal services provider.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Local Care Team (LCT) is a roundtable support program that connects children and families with community resources and services. Parents and service providers meet to discuss individual child and family needs, and the LCT provides recommendations for services and supports based on a cultural and whole-person approach. Each family is assigned a lead agency worker to help connect them to recommended services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Families attend a 30-minute virtual roundtable meeting where a multi-agency team reviews their needs and provides written recommendations for community services within 24 hours. A lead agency worker is assigned to help connect the family to recommended services.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Children and families in Frederick County who need help accessing community supports and services. Referrals can be made by parents through self-referral or by service providers such as school counselors and therapists.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Connecting families to community services and supports based on individual child and family needs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Frederick County, Maryland
requirements_list: Contact LCT Coordinator to confirm referral is appropriate
Obtain signed LCT Release of Information from parent or guardian
Complete the LCT Referral Form
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the LCT Coordinator at 301-600-1077 or LCT@frederickcountymd.gov to begin a self-referral or confirm a provider referral. Obtain a signed Release of Information form and complete the LCT Referral Form.

structured_extraction.program_name: MAP: Maryland Access Point of Frederick County
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Access Point (MAP) is a free information and assistance service for Frederick County residents. It helps adults aged 50 and older, adults 18 and older with a disability, caregivers, and professionals find and access public and private benefit programs, community services, and long-term care options. Staff provide eligibility screening, referrals, care planning, and help with decision-making to support people in remaining in their community.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free information, eligibility screening, referrals to local/state/federal programs, care planning, and service navigation. Monthly virtual presentations on specific programs and services are also offered through the Virtual Senior Center.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Frederick County adults aged 50 and older, adults 18 and older with a disability, family members and other caregivers, and health or business professionals
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable — this is a free information, referral, and care navigation service, not a funding program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Frederick County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a Frederick County resident
Adults aged 50 and older, or adults aged 18 and older with a disability are the primary target population; caregivers and professionals may also use the service
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Division of Aging and Independence by phone at 301-600-1234 during business hours (Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m.–4:00 p.m.) or visit 1440 Taney Ave., Frederick, MD 21702. No formal application is required.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland EV Income Tax Credit for Businesses (New EVs)
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland offers a state income tax credit of up to $3,000 per new electric vehicle purchased by a business. The credit is claimed on the business's state tax return for the year the vehicle is placed in service. The credit is limited to 10 vehicles per business and is nonrefundable — unused credits cannot be carried forward.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State income tax credit of up to $3,000 per new EV, capped at 10 vehicles per business. Vehicle sale price cannot exceed $50,000 and must have a battery capacity of at least 5 kWh. The credit is nonrefundable and cannot be carried forward.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland businesses purchasing new electric vehicles
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Offset the cost of purchasing new electric vehicles
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Vehicle sale price cannot exceed $50,000
Vehicle must have a battery capacity of at least 5 kWh
Limited to 10 vehicles per business
Credit is nonrefundable; unused credit cannot be applied to future years
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Claim the credit on the Maryland state business tax return for the year the vehicle is placed in service. See the MVA website for vehicle qualifications and instructions.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland EV Income Tax Credit for Individuals (New EVs)
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland offers an income tax credit of up to $3,000 for individuals who purchase a new electric vehicle. The credit is claimed on the individual's state tax return for the year the vehicle is placed in service. The full credit is only available if the individual's tax bill is at least $3,000.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State income tax credit of up to $3,000 for the purchase of a new EV. The vehicle's sale price cannot exceed $50,000 and must have a battery capacity of at least 5 kWh. The credit is not applied at the point of purchase.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland individuals purchasing a new electric vehicle
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Offset the cost of purchasing a new electric vehicle
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Vehicle sale price cannot exceed $50,000
Vehicle must have a battery capacity of at least 5 kWh
Credit is limited to the individual's tax liability (nonrefundable)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Claim the credit on your Maryland state income tax return for the year the vehicle is placed in service. See the MVA website for vehicle qualifications and instructions.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Women's Business Center (MWBC) helps women and men start, sustain, and grow their businesses. It offers workshops, individual counseling, peer group support, networking events, and access to capital to build entrepreneurial skills and confidence.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides workshops, one-on-one business counseling, facilitated peer group support, and a monthly networking event (Coffee and Connections) for entrepreneurs in Frederick County.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Women (and men) entrepreneurs looking to start, grow, or sustain a business in Frederick County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business counseling, training workshops, peer networking, and access to capital resources.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Primarily serves entrepreneurs in Frederick County, Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the MWBC through their website or email to schedule counseling or register for workshops and events.

structured_extraction.program_name: Meals on Wheels / Home Delivered Meals
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides home-delivered meals to homebound adults in Frederick County who are unable to prepare their own meals. Eligible recipients include adults age 60 or older, or adults of any age with a chronic health condition or disability, who reside in Frederick County and cannot prepare meals for themselves. Meals are delivered within the service areas of senior centers in Brunswick, Emmitsburg, Frederick, and Urbana. Two meals per day are provided — one hot midday meal and one cold meal for later — meeting Recommended Dietary Allowances for older adults, with special diet options including regular, diabetic/low carbohydrate, low sodium, and mechanical soft menus. The program also provides wellness checks and referrals to other services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two meals per day delivered to eligible homebound participants — one hot meal at midday and one cold meal to be refrigerated for later. Meals meet Recommended Dietary Allowances for older adults. Special diet options include regular, diabetic/low carbohydrate, low sodium, and mechanical soft menus. The program also provides regular wellness checks and coordination of referrals for other services.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homebound adults age 60 or older, or adults of any age with a chronic health condition or disability, who live in Frederick County (particularly within the service areas of senior centers in Brunswick, Emmitsburg, Frederick, and Urbana) and are unable to prepare meals for themselves or attend congregate dining programs due to health problems.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home-delivered meals and wellness checks for eligible homebound adults, along with referrals to other services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must reside in Frederick County, Maryland, within the service areas of senior centers in Brunswick, Emmitsburg, Frederick, or Urbana.
requirements_list: Must be age 60 or older, OR have a chronic health condition or disability at any age
Must be homebound due to illness or physical limitations
Must be unable to prepare meals
Must have no caregiver to assist with food shopping and preparation, or cannot safely prepare food due to physical, mental, or emotional impairment
Must be unable to participate in congregate dining due to health problems
Must live within Frederick County, within service areas of senior centers in Brunswick, Emmitsburg, Frederick, or Urbana
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review the Eligibility Guidelines and then call 301-600-1234 to begin the screening process.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Mobile Community Healthcare program sends specially trained community paramedics into the community to support Frederick County residents with ongoing health needs. Paramedics work alongside primary care providers and social workers to help individuals manage chronic conditions, understand medications, address home safety concerns, and connect to social services — all at no cost to eligible residents.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free in-home and community-based health support services including chronic disease management education, care plan follow-up, medication guidance, home safety assessments, and connections to transportation, food access, housing, and other social services. No cost to eligible Frederick County residents.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Frederick County residents with ongoing health needs who may benefit from additional monitoring, education, and care coordination outside of traditional clinical settings
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Health support, care coordination, and connection to community resources for eligible residents
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to eligible Frederick County residents
requirements_list: Must be a Frederick County resident
Must have ongoing health needs appropriate for community-based support
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 301-600-HELP (4357) or email DFRSMCH@FrederickCountyMD.gov to contact the program.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federally funded program that provides support, education, training, and respite services to unpaid caregivers of older adults and people with dementia. Caregivers can receive up to $800 per year toward respite care, along with referrals, resource materials, and training.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $800 once per year toward respite care costs. Also provides education and training, information and referrals to local agencies, resource materials, and monthly caregiver updates by email or mail. No income requirements to participate.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Caregivers of adults age 60 or older; caregivers of people of any age with Alzheimer's disease or related disorders; grandparents and relative caregivers age 55 or older caring for children age 18 or under or adult children with a disability ages 19-59. Caregivers do not need to be family members.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Respite care (temporary relief care for caregivers). Also includes education, training, and referral services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to caregivers in Frederick County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Caregiver must be providing care to someone age 60 or older, OR to a person of any age with Alzheimer's disease or a related disorder
OR: Caregiver must be a grandparent or relative age 55 or older caring for a child age 18 or under, or an adult child with a disability ages 19-59
Caregivers seeking the grandparent/relative respite benefit cannot be the child's natural or adoptive parent
No income requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the appropriate respite application (Caregiver Respite Application for those caring for someone 60 or older or with early onset dementia, or the Grandparent/Relative Respite Application) and submit with required W-9 form. Contact Caregiver Program Coordinators at 301-600-6022 or caregiversupport@frederickcountymd.gov for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit for partially disabled veterans in Frederick County to help reduce their property tax burden.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A county property tax credit for eligible partially disabled veterans that reduces property tax liability. Applicants must be partially disabled veterans residing in Frederick County, Maryland.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Partially disabled veterans in Frederick County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of property tax liability
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Frederick County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a partially disabled veteran
Must reside in Frederick County, Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and submit the Partially Disabled Veteran Tax Credit Application available on the Frederick County website.

structured_extraction.program_name: Payments In Lieu of Tax Policy (PILOT)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides reduced tax payments in lieu of full property taxes for low and moderate income rental housing projects in Frederick County.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Payments in lieu of taxes (PILOT) for qualifying low and moderate income rental housing projects, reducing the property tax burden for eligible developments.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Developers and owners of low and moderate income rental housing projects in Frederick County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction in property tax obligations for qualifying rental housing projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Frederick County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Project must provide low and moderate income rental housing
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Susan Brown for information on applying.

structured_extraction.program_description: An internship offered by the Frederick County Division of Planning and Permitting that gives students professional public sector planning experience. Interns work on special projects, research, and analysis related to historic preservation under the direction of Historic Preservation Planners. Hours are flexible to fit the student's school schedule.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Hands-on internship experience in public sector planning, including historic preservation projects, research, and analysis. Flexible hours to accommodate the student's school schedule.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students seeking professional planning and historic preservation experience in the public sector.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable — this is an internship/training opportunity, not a funding program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Frederick County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a student (internship hours are flexible to accommodate school schedule)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Internship opportunities are announced on the Government Jobs platform at governmentjobs.com/careers/frederickmd. Availability varies by the division's current needs.

structured_extraction.program_name: Prescription Discount Drug Program / Live Healthy Health & Dental Discounts
structured_extraction.program_description: Frederick County residents can access discounted health and dental services through the National Association of Counties' Live Healthy program. The discount programs are not insurance but provide reduced costs for services and supplies, including savings of 15%–50% on most dental procedures through a national network of dentists and specialists.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants pay $6.95/month or $69/year for an individual, or $8.95/month or $79/year for a family. The program provides access to discounted health and dental services — not insurance — with average savings of 15%–50% on dental procedures. No waiting periods apply.
structured_extraction.program_audience: All Frederick County residents regardless of age, income, or existing health coverage.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduced-cost dental and health services and supplies through a national provider network.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to all Frederick County, Maryland residents.
requirements_list: Must be a Frederick County resident
Open to all ages and income levels
No requirement to lack existing health coverage
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the National Association of Counties Live Healthy page (https://www.naco.org/page/live-healthy-us-counties) to learn more and sign up.

structured_extraction.program_description: When no suitable family member is available to serve as guardian, the Area Agency on Aging (AAA) Director or her designee may be appointed by the Circuit Court as a Public Guardian for adults age 65 and older who have been declared unable to make their own decisions. The Public Guardian may determine appropriate living arrangements, oversee services, and consent to medical treatment on behalf of the person under guardianship. Guardianship may cover the person (health care, food, clothing, shelter) and/or property (money, income, stocks, bonds, and other financial matters).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A court-appointed Public Guardian (the AAA Director or designee) manages living arrangements, oversees services, and consents to medical treatment for eligible adults who cannot make their own decisions. Guardianship may cover the person and/or property of the alleged disabled person.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults age 65 and older in Frederick County who have been declared by the Circuit Court to be incapable of making their own decisions and have no suitable family guardian available. Interested persons such as relatives, friends, healthcare providers, social workers, or local department directors may also initiate the petition process.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Guardianship services including determining living arrangements, overseeing provision of services, and consenting to medical treatment. Guardian of person makes decisions about health care, food, clothing, and shelter; guardian of property makes decisions about money, income, stocks, bonds, and other financial matters.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Frederick County, Maryland. The alleged disabled person must reside in or be physically present in Maryland, or have property in Maryland; the petition is filed in the county where the alleged disabled person lives or has property.
requirements_list: Must be age 65 or older
Must be declared by the Circuit Court to be incapable of making their own decisions
No suitable family member available to serve as guardian
Verified certificates of competency from two physicians OR one physician plus one licensed psychologist/certified social worker-clinical/nurse practitioner
At least one health care professional evaluation must occur within 21 days of petition filing
Less restrictive alternatives must be attempted and documented as failed
Disclosure of criminal convictions (if applicable) with good cause explanation
Complete list of all interested persons and their contact information
Description of alleged disability and its functional impact
List of all property (if seeking guardianship of property)
Clear and convincing evidence of disability and inability to make responsible decisions
Guardian orientation program completion before appointment
Guardian training program completion within 120 days (person) or 60 days (property) of appointment
Prospective guardian must not have disqualifying criminal convictions
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Guardianship is initiated through the Circuit Court. Step 1: Complete the Petition for Guardianship (CC-GN-002) with required exhibits. A petition for guardianship may be filed using Maryland court forms. Contact the Division of Aging and Independence for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: R Info 4 Kids! Recycling Education Kits
structured_extraction.program_description: A loan program that provides recycling education kits to K-5 classroom teachers in Frederick County at no charge. Kits include DVDs, books, show-and-tell items, lesson plans, and hands-on activities to help students in grades K-2 and grades 3-5 learn about waste and recycling.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free loan of recycling education kits for up to 4 weeks per classroom. Each kit contains age-appropriate materials including DVDs, books, lesson plans, and hands-on activities. Classes may also receive a limited number of coloring books, pencils, or other take-home items.
structured_extraction.program_audience: K-5 classroom teachers in Frederick County schools
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Classroom-based recycling and waste education for students in grades K-5
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to classroom teachers in Frederick County, Maryland
requirements_list: Kits must be reserved at least two weeks in advance
Kits may be borrowed for up to 4 weeks
Request by calling 301-600-2960
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 301-600-2960 to reserve a kit at least two weeks before you need it.

structured_extraction.program_name: Reduced Capacity Fees for Properties with LEED Certification for Water Efficiency
structured_extraction.program_description: Frederick County offers reduced water and sewer capacity fees for buildings or properties that obtain LEED certification for water efficiency. The program assumes that LEED-certified buildings require less capacity and place less demand on the county's water and sewer system than comparable non-certified buildings.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reduced capacity fees for water and sewer connections for buildings or properties that obtain LEED certification for water efficiency. A Notice of Intent must be filed before the building permit is issued. Applies to building permits issued on or after August 16, 2012.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners and developers seeking LEED certification for water efficiency in Frederick County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction in water and sewer capacity fees for eligible LEED-certified buildings
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Frederick County, Maryland
requirements_list: Building permit issued on or after August 16, 2012
Property must obtain LEED certification for water efficiency
Notice of Intent must be on file prior to issuance of building permit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: File a Notice of Intent prior to issuance of the building permit. Execute a LEED Reduced Capacity Fee Agreement. See Section 11.G of the Frederick County Water and Sewer Rules and Regulations for full details.

structured_extraction.program_name: Rehabilitated Vacant Commercial Structures Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit that encourages rehabilitation and reuse of vacant commercial structures in Frederick County, promoting capital investment in existing infrastructure. The credit applies to properties that have been vacant for at least 18 of the last 24 months, are used for non-residential purposes in commercial or industrial zones, and were constructed prior to the year 2000.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A county property tax credit for owners of vacant commercial structures that have been vacant for at least 18 of the last 24 months, are used for non-residential purposes in an area permitting commercial or industrial use, and were constructed prior to the year 2000. The credit provides a tax exemption on the increased assessment value attributable to reconstruction and improvements to vacant commercial properties, reducing property tax liability to encourage reoccupancy or redevelopment of vacant commercial structures.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 30th (for tax credit to be applied to following fiscal year tax bill mailed July 1)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners and commercial real estate brokers rehabilitating or redeveloping vacant commercial structures in Frederick County or the City of Frederick.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of property tax liability on rehabilitated or reoccupied vacant commercial structures; tax exemption on increased assessment value attributable to reconstruction and improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Frederick County, Maryland, including the City of Frederick.
requirements_list: Property must have been vacant for at least 18 of the last 24 months prior to lease or sale
Property must have been actively listed for sale or lease
Property must be used for non-residential purposes in an area permitting commercial or industrial use
Structure must have been constructed prior to the year 2000
Rehabilitation must be completed
Pedestrian and vehicular connections to adjacent commercial properties must be provided (or documented as not feasible by Planning Department)
Applicant must be current property owner
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit completed application form and backup documentation to State Department of Assessment & Taxation. Include broker certification of vacancy period and listing status, supervisory assessment confirmation of improvements and increased assessment value, and City/County calculations of tax exemption. Download the Vacant Commercial Tax Credit Application or the program information sheet from the Frederick County Economic Development website. Refer to the Vacant Commercial Structures Tax Credit document available at https://www.frederickcountymd.gov/DocumentCenter/View/280232.

structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit available through Frederick County for retired service members to help reduce their real property tax burden.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A county-level real property tax credit for retired military service members in Frederick County.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Retired military service members who own property in Frederick County, Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of real property tax liability for eligible retired service members.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to homeowners in Frederick County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a retired military service member meeting county eligibility criteria
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Frederick County Tax Credits page on the official website.

structured_extraction.program_name: Revitalization Area Rehabilitated Structures Tax Credit – Town of Middletown
structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit for rehabilitated structures in the revitalization area of the Town of Middletown, Frederick County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A property tax credit for eligible rehabilitated structures located in the revitalization area of the Town of Middletown.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners with rehabilitated structures in the Town of Middletown revitalization area
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of property tax liability for rehabilitated structures in Middletown's revitalization area
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Town of Middletown revitalization area, Frederick County, Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Refer to the Revitalization Area Rehabilitated Structures Tax Credit document available on the Frederick County website.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program helps fund the rehabilitation, restoration, and preservation of historic properties located in the unincorporated areas of Frederick County. Grants are designed to preserve, protect, and enhance rural historic properties and support the identification and preservation of historic and cultural resources in rural, unincorporated areas of the county.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants fund rehabilitation, restoration, and preservation work on historic properties in unincorporated Frederick County. Specific grant amounts and terms are not stated on the program pages.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners or stewards of historic properties located in unincorporated areas of Frederick County seeking funding for preservation, rehabilitation, or restoration work.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rehabilitation, restoration, and preservation of rural historic properties and cultural resources.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties must be located in the rural, unincorporated areas of Frederick County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Property must be historic and located in the unincorporated areas of Frederick County
Applicants are encouraged to attend a grant workshop before applying
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted during the open grant cycle (September 1 through November 30, 2025). Applicants are encouraged to attend a virtual workshop before applying. Complete and submit the grant application and follow the provided instructions. Contact staff with any questions if unable to attend a workshop.

structured_extraction.program_name: Safe Streets for All Municipal Technical Assistance Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Frederick County offers grant funding to eligible municipalities for projects that improve roadway safety. The program supports the county's goal of eliminating traffic-related deaths and serious injuries and building a long-term safety culture.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Approximately $200,000 in total funding is available to support eligible municipalities with roadway safety improvement projects. Funding comes from a US Department of Transportation Safe Streets for All (SS4A) grant awarded to Frederick County.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted as long as funding is available
structured_extraction.program_audience: Municipalities in Frederick County seeking to improve roadway safety
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects that improve roadway safety within eligible municipalities
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Municipalities within Frederick County, Maryland
requirements_list: Applicant must be an eligible municipality within Frederick County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application; applications are accepted on a rolling basis while funding remains available.

structured_extraction.program_name: Scott Key Center Employment Training and Placement
structured_extraction.program_description: Scott Key Center provides employment training and job placement for adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities in Frederick County. Services include individual (competitive) job placements, supported employment with job coaching, and vocational training. Clients are placed with local employers and supported through ongoing job coaching.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Job placement, supported employment, and vocational training for adults with developmental disabilities. Includes initial job coaching support and ongoing drop-in support as needed. No financial assistance amount specified.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults age 21 and over with intellectual and developmental disabilities who are residents of Frederick County, Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Employment training, job coaching, and supported employment placement.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Frederick County, Maryland residents only.
requirements_list: Must be a resident of Frederick County, Maryland
Must be age 21 or older
Must have an intellectual or developmental disability
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Executive Director Sean M. Lore by calling 301-600-1600. A job development specialist will meet with the prospective client or employer to develop a plan for job coaching and ongoing communication.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides free legal assistance to income-eligible individuals representing themselves in court. Offers one-on-one consultations, tools for case organization and trial preparation, and legal advice on family law matters including custody, divorce, and trial preparation.

structured_extraction.program_description: Frederick County Transit Services offers the Vanpool Incentive Program (VIP) to help new vanpools get started during their first year of operation. The program provides monthly financial subsidies to cover the cost of empty seats while a vanpool is filling up, helping new vanpools become financially viable. For months 1–6, the maximum monthly subsidy ranges from $263 (7-passenger van) to $500 (15-passenger van). For months 7–12, the maximum ranges from $158 to $300 depending on vehicle size. The per-seat subsidy is calculated by dividing total eligible operating expenses (lease cost and gasoline) by the number of available seats (excluding the driver), then multiplied by the number of unfilled seats. As more riders join, the subsidy decreases.

The per-seat subsidy is calculated by dividing total eligible operating expenses (lease cost and gasoline) by the number of available seats (excluding the driver), then multiplied by the number of unfilled seats. The subsidy decreases as more riders join the vanpool.

structured_extraction.program_name: Frederick County Commercial & Industrial Business Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A 10-year real property tax credit for businesses conducting manufacturing, fabricating, or assembling operations in Frederick County. The program supports business investment and growth by providing a county property tax credit to eligible commercial and industrial businesses that build new facilities or expand existing ones. To qualify, businesses must make a total new investment of at least $5 million and create at least 25 new full-time jobs paying at least 150% of the federal minimum wage. The credit reduces the amount of property tax owed on the value of new improvements. If the average credit over the 10 years exceeds 60% of the new tax amount, County Council approval is required.

structured_extraction.program_name: Frederick County New Jobs Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit for businesses in Frederick County that construct or expand their facilities in a Priority Funding Area and create new full-time jobs. Businesses must expand by at least 5,000 square feet and create at least 25 full-time jobs within the first two years of occupying the new or expanded premises. The standard credit applies over six years on the increased assessed value of real property: 52% in years one and two, 39% in years three and four, and 26% in years five and six. An Enhanced New Jobs Tax Credit is also available for larger expansions of at least 250,000 square feet, providing a 12-year credit equal to 58.5% of property tax imposed on the increase in assessment of new or expanded premises and substantially renovated adjoining property. To qualify for the Enhanced credit, businesses must create at least 1,250 full-time permanent jobs paying at least 150% of the federal minimum wage, or at least 2,500 full-time jobs with 500 additional positions also paying at least 150% of the federal minimum wage. The program encourages employment growth and economic development in Frederick County and is available to businesses new to the county, already located there, or relocating from outside Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_name: Frederick County Small Business Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit for small businesses in Frederick County to support local business retention and growth. Eligible businesses must obtain at least 2,500 square feet of new or expanded premises and employ at least five full-time people within a 24-month period of occupying the new or expanded space. The business must be located in a Frederick County priority funding area. The credit is structured as a decreasing property tax exemption over six years: 40% in years 1 and 2, 30% in years 3 and 4, 20% in years 5 and 6, and 0% thereafter. structured_extraction.program_name: Red Folder / File of Life Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A free program providing red magnetic packets or folders to county residents to store important medical documents such as advance directives, medication lists, allergies, emergency contacts, caregiver information, doctor contact info, and insurance information. First responders and paramedics are trained to look for the red folder or packet during emergencies, enabling them to quickly access a resident's medical history and care wishes even when the person cannot communicate. The program is available in both Frederick County (Red Folder Program) and Montgomery County (File of Life).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free red magnetic folders or packets (one per household where possible) are provided to eligible residents to store copies of important medical documents. The folder/packet is durable, portable, and brightly colored for easy identification by first responders. In Frederick County, residents can request a folder online or by phone. In Montgomery County, residents can call 311 to receive a packet by mail or download and print the insert from the county website. The Montgomery County File of Life card documents personal details, allergies, medical conditions, medications, vaccination dates, emergency contacts, healthcare decisions (DNR/MOLST status), and health insurance information, stored in a red magnetic pouch placed on the refrigerator door.
structured_extraction.contact_phone: 301-600-4357; Aging and Disability Services: 240-777-3000; Fire & Rescue Safety Education: 240-777-2430
structured_extraction.program_audience: Older adults, people with multiple medical diagnoses, extensive medication needs, or complex care requirements living in Frederick County or Montgomery County, Maryland, especially those who may need emergency responders to quickly access their medical history. Particularly seniors and individuals with disabilities. Spanish-language materials are available for Frederick County residents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Storing copies of medical documents including advance directives, medication lists, allergies, emergency contacts, caregiver information, doctor contact info, and insurance information for use by first responders during emergencies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Frederick County and Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must reside in Frederick County or Montgomery County, Maryland
One folder/packet per household is requested where possible
In Montgomery County: complete the card using pencil, place in red magnetic pouch on refrigerator door, and update information as changes occur
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: In Frederick County: request a folder online through the online form or by calling the Mobile Community Healthcare Program at 301-600-4357. In Montgomery County: call 311 to request a free packet by mail, or download and print the insert from the Montgomery County website. To use the File of Life card: fill out the card, fold it, insert in the red magnetic pouch, and place on the refrigerator door.

structured_extraction.program_name: FREE Friendsville Renewable Energy Effort Solar Co-Op
structured_extraction.program_description: The Friendsville Renewable Energy Effort (FREE) is a volunteer-run solar co-op that helps local residents, businesses, and landowners in Garrett and Allegany counties sign up for solar photovoltaic (PV) panel installations. By organizing a group of interested participants, FREE works with NABCEP-certified local solar installers from the mountaintop area to offer lower prices through bulk purchasing. The program also aims to create local jobs by including Garrett County electricians and contractors in installations, and facilitates hands-on solar installation training for local electricians and contractors. There is no charge to the contractor or buyer for FREE's services, and estimates are free.

structured_extraction.program_name: Garrett County Agricultural Land Preservation District Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary program to preserve productive local farmland and woodland in Garrett County. Enrolled properties receive a 100% rebate on real estate property taxes for all agricultural lands and woodlands under the county's Tax Credit Ordinance. The program also helps screen and pre-qualify landowners for selling perpetual conservation easements to the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation. The District Agreement provides a minimum 3-year protection from development. If the district is terminated, the landowner must repay all back property taxes plus interest.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Properties approved for the Agricultural Land Preservation District receive a 100% rebate on property taxes for all agricultural lands and woodlands. Taxes on residential and agricultural structures continue to be assessed. The District Agreement provides a minimum 3-year protection from development. Landowners may subsequently apply to sell perpetual conservation easements to the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation or the County, with development rights purchased and land use restricted to agricultural purposes perpetually.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners with productive agricultural or woodland property in Garrett County, including individual landowners and business entities (corporations, partnerships, etc.)
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax relief for enrolled agricultural and woodland properties; preservation of farmland and woodland through easement purchases and tax incentives
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Garrett County, Maryland. Land must be outside the 10-year water and sewer service area (unless extraordinary agricultural capability). Minimum 50 contiguous acres required (smaller parcels may qualify if adjacent to an existing district or with extraordinary capability). Includes the Bear Creek Rural Legacy Area for Rural Legacy Funding opportunities.
requirements_list: Minimum 50 contiguous acres (exceptions for smaller parcels with extraordinary agricultural capability or adjacent to existing district)
Property must be located outside the planned 10-year water/sewer service district boundaries (unless extraordinary agricultural capability)
Property must meet soil productivity standards (qualifying soils: Class I, II, III or Group 1, 2)
Current Soil and Water Conservation Plan (revised within last 10 years)
Nutrient Management Plan (if applicable)
Forestry Stewardship Plan (if applicable)
Tax map with property boundaries and withheld acreage clearly marked
Landowner must keep property in agricultural use for a minimum of 3 years
No commercial, industrial, or residential use except as permitted by Maryland Agriculture Article Section 2-513
No property division/subdivision without County written approval
No non-agricultural buildings or structures without County approval
No more than one tenant house per 100 acres
Landowner must sign and notarize the Garrett County Agricultural Land Preservation District Agreement
Agreement must be recorded in Land Records by the County
Approval from Agricultural Land Preservation Advisory Board, Planning Commission, and Board of Garrett County Commissioners
Consistency with county plans (Master Plan, Comprehensive Land-Use Plan, Growth Management Plan, etc.)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the District Property Description form with required documentation (including Soil and Water Conservation Plan, Nutrient Management Plan if applicable, Forestry Stewardship Plan if applicable, and tax map) with assistance from the Garrett Soil Conservation District (301-334-6951) to verify soil productivity requirements. Submit completed form to the Department of Planning & Land Development or Soil Conservation. Obtain approval from the Agricultural Land Preservation Advisory Board, Planning Commission, and Board of County Commissioners. Sign and notarize the Garrett County Agricultural Land Preservation District Agreement. The County records the agreement in Land Records. After a minimum of 3 years, landowner may request to sell an agricultural preservation easement to the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation or the County.

structured_extraction.program_description: A regional business attraction and support initiative for Western Maryland that encourages entrepreneurs in the outdoor recreation and lifestyle manufacturing industries to start or relocate businesses to Allegany and Garrett Counties. The program is part of a three-report marketing plan (Manufacturing Business Attraction Analysis, Tourism Business Expansion Analysis, and Strategic Marketing Plan) aimed at developing Allegany and Garrett counties as an outdoor recreation and lifestyle manufacturing hub. It connects businesses with local economic development teams, tax credits from the State of Maryland, and resources to help find cost-effective locations, while also using digital and traditional advertising campaigns to attract businesses and workers to the region.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The State of Maryland offers tax credits to businesses that open in the Western Maryland region, including the One Maryland Tax Credit ($1–5 million based on employees and investment size) and the More Jobs for Marylanders Incentive Program (refundable income tax credit for a 10-year consecutive benefit period). Garrett County has a Small Business Administration HubZone designation. Local economic development teams in Allegany and Garrett Counties help businesses find cost-effective locations, including industrial parks, incubator spaces, and workforce training programs. The program also includes digital and traditional advertising campaigns (videos, digital ads, print ads, billboards, brochures), a landing page at MakeItInTheMountains.com, and potential relocation program incentives (cash incentives, outdoor recreation access, coworking space, social programming, professional development) and ambassador programs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Entrepreneurs, manufacturers, and businesses in outdoor recreation and lifestyle manufacturing (including apparel, outdoor vehicles/boats/parts/accessories, timber/wood products, specialty foods, accommodations, dining, and retail) looking to start, relocate, or expand a business in Western Maryland (Allegany or Garrett County). Also targets remote workers and job seekers considering relocating to the region.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business startup, relocation, and site selection in Western Maryland; development of lodging, dining, retail, and recreation businesses; infrastructure improvements along trails and recreation areas.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to businesses locating in Allegany County or Garrett County, Maryland. Communities along county borders or on major transportation routes (Interstate 68, Old National Road, Amtrak access) are highlighted. The broader five-county Appalachian region analysis includes Mineral County (WV) and Bedford and Somerset counties (PA).
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the MITM Resources page at makeitinthemountains.com/resources/ or contact the local economic development team in Allegany or Garrett County for assistance. Prospective applicants can also use the landing page call-to-action form at MakeItInTheMountains.com to contact appropriate county economic development representatives.

structured_extraction.program_name: Garrett County Property Tax Incentive Program for New or Expanding Businesses
structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit program for new and expanding businesses in Garrett County, implemented by the Board of County Commissioners to encourage business growth. Businesses that increase their property tax assessment by at least $100,000 through new improvements to business property can receive a credit against the county's portion of real property tax on those improvements for five years. The credit starts at 50% of the assessed value of new improvements in year one and decreases by 10 percentage points each year (40%, 30%, 20%), reaching 10% in the fifth and final year. Eligible projects include expanding, renovating, or making capital improvements to a commercial or industrial business property. After five years, the improved property returns to full tax rolls at full-assessed value.
structured_extraction.agency: Garrett County Department of Business Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A five-year tax credit against the county's portion of real property tax on new improvements to business property. The credit starts at 50% of the increase in County real estate tax for the first year, then decreases by 10 percentage points each year (40%, 30%, 20%), reaching 10% in the fifth and final year. The new improvement must increase the tax assessment on property improvements by at least $100,000 to qualify. Improvements must be reflected on tax bills after June 30, 2007. After five years, the improved property returns to full tax rolls at full-assessed value. Businesses in enterprise zones may be eligible for combined credits.
structured_extraction.program_audience: New and expanding for-profit and non-profit commercial or industrial businesses in Garrett County making property improvements that increase the tax assessment by at least $100,000. Includes businesses locating in enterprise zones within the county.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credit applied against county real property taxes on qualifying new improvements to business property. Eligible projects include new construction, expanding, renovating, or making capital improvements to a business property, reducing county business property tax obligations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to businesses located anywhere in Garrett County, Maryland, including enterprise zones within the county. Improvements must be reflected on tax bills after June 30, 2007.
requirements_list: Business must be located in Garrett County, Maryland
Must be a new or expanding commercial or industrial business
New improvement must increase the tax assessment on property improvements by at least $100,000
Improvements must be reflected on tax bills after June 30, 2007

Employee residency and demographics (full-time, part-time, female, minority) are tracked as part of the application

structured_extraction.program_name: Goldseker Fellows Program at Morgan State University
structured_extraction.program_description: The Goldseker Foundation provides grants to Morgan State University to support the Goldseker Fellows Program, which offers need-based graduate fellowships to students pursuing master's and doctoral degrees, as well as activities designed to enhance the university's relationships and visibility in the Baltimore metropolitan community. The Goldseker Foundation has supported this program since 1976, awarding $5.5 million toward 2,273 graduate fellowships across multiple grant cycles. Early support included a five-year commitment of $1,153,000 starting in 2006, and subsequent grants of $175,000 (2011), $157,500 (2012), $165,000 (2013), $185,000 (2014), $205,000 (November 2015), $200,000 (November 2017), $210,000 (November 2020), $230,000, $285,000, $300,000 (November 2022), and $300,000 (December 2023). Up to $20,000 of each grant may be used at the discretion of the University President to improve the University's relationships and visibility in the Baltimore metropolitan community. Fellows are selected by Morgan State University.

structured_extraction.program_description: Project JumpStart (PJS) is an 87-hour (approximately 14-week) pre-apprenticeship construction job training and placement program that prepares Baltimore City residents for careers in the construction trades through hands-on training and connects them with job opportunities in the industry. structured_extraction.program_description: Invest York Road (IYR) is a standalone entity created from the York Road Partnership to address the lack of control over commercial real estate along the York Road corridor in Baltimore. It uses innovative approaches to organize local financial capital — through accessible small-dollar investments — to purchase and manage commercial properties, empowering residents to drive community change and creating a healthier, safer, and more economically vibrant community. The Goldseker Foundation has awarded multiple grants to support this initiative, including a $25,000 operating support grant in September 2021, a $30,000 grant in December 2023, and a $40,000 grant in February 2024 (the latter administered through Loyola University fbo Invest York Road Initiative).
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Operating support grants awarded by the Goldseker Foundation to support the Invest York Road initiative's work organizing local financial capital to purchase and manage commercial properties along the York Road corridor. Known grants include $25,000 in September 2021, $30,000 in December 2023, and $40,000 in February 2024.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations and community initiatives working on community economic development and commercial real estate control along the York Road corridor in Baltimore, particularly the Invest York Road (IYR) entity and the York Road Partnership and its related community development entities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating support for the Invest York Road initiative, which focuses on organizing local financial capital to purchase and manage commercial properties along the York Road corridor, giving community members control over commercial real estate and driving neighborhood economic development.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: York Road corridor in Baltimore City, Maryland

Staff help organizations complete grant applications, solve post-award problems like payment delays, and find relevant funding opportunities from federal, state, local, and private sources.

Access by filling out an intake form to request a meeting.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Governor's Family Violence Council certifies Abuse Intervention Programs (AIPs) for inclusion in the Administrative Office of the Courts Bench Book for Maryland Judges. This certification allows judges to refer abusers to approved abuse intervention programs. Programs must meet operational standards including victim confidentiality, intake processes, victim safety, program format, discharge criteria, staffing requirements, and community collaboration. Certification is valid for three years and programs are subject to on-site audits during the certification period.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Certification recognizes compliance with state guidelines for abuse intervention programs. Certified programs are listed in the Administrative Office of the Courts Bench Book for Maryland Judges, enabling judicial referrals and referrals from the Department of Parole and Probation. Certification is valid for three years from date of issuance and is subject to on-site audits during the certification period.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations operating abuse intervention programs in Maryland seeking certification for judicial and probation/parole referrals
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: N/A – this is a certification program, not a direct funding program
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide – available to abuse intervention programs operating anywhere in Maryland, serving one of Maryland's designated counties with COMAR Domestic Violence Programs

Applications and supporting documents are available on the program page.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides grants to local government agencies in Maryland to establish and operate Day Reporting Centers. These centers offer community-based services and treatment to adults under parole, probation, or pretrial supervision as an alternative to incarceration, with the goal of reducing recidivism, jail and prison populations, and corrections-related costs. Participants live at home and report to the center regularly to receive counseling, cognitive behavioral therapy, drug treatment, job training, educational support, and intensive supervision.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants to local government agencies to fund Day Reporting Center operations. Eligible cost categories include personnel, contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, travel, and other expenses. A training and technical assistance session was offered on March 17, 2026.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Personnel, contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, travel, and other costs related to operating a Day Reporting Center providing supervision and treatment services to non-violent adult offenders.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to local government agencies throughout Maryland.

Services must target non-violent adult offenders under parole, probation, or pretrial supervision
Program must address criminogenic needs such as antisocial thoughts, substance abuse, anger, employment, education, and life skills

structured_extraction.program_name: Body Armor for Local Law Enforcement (BARM)
structured_extraction.program_description: A state-funded reimbursement grant that helps local law enforcement agencies cover the cost of purchasing bullet-resistant body armor and stab-resistant vests for sworn officers. The program reimburses 50% of the cost of each body armor vest purchased for non-state local law enforcement agencies in any Maryland county, incorporated city or town, including Baltimore City. Supports purchasing new body armor and replacing existing armor if testing or age indicates replacement need. Aligns with the objective of disrupting criminal organizations involved in guns, gangs, drugs, and human trafficking.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimburses non-state local law enforcement agencies 50% of the cost of bullet-resistant body armor and stab-resistant vests purchased for sworn officers. Eligible equipment includes protective body armor, stab-resistant vests conforming to NIJ Standard 0101.07 and V-50 ballistic testing requirements, ballistic and trauma plates, tactical carriers, undershirt carriers, and vest-mounted accessories (MOLLE or similar systems). Total anticipated funding: $49,088; 5-15 awards anticipated; maximum award per applicant: $5,000. Requires 50% cash or in-kind cost share match. Reimbursement is based on actual quarterly expenditures. State agencies are not eligible.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of bullet-resistant body armor and stab-resistant vests for sworn law enforcement officers, including ballistic and trauma plates, tactical carriers, undershirt carriers, and vest-mounted accessories (MOLLE or similar systems).

Applicants partnering with ENOUGH Grant Program initiative in 27 ENOUGH-eligible communities with high levels of concentrated child poverty receive bonus points. State agencies are not eligible.

structured_extraction.program_name: Byrne State Crisis Intervention Program (Byrne SCIP/BSCI)
structured_extraction.program_description: Authorized by the Bipartisan Safer Communities Act of 2022 (Pub. L. No. 117-159, 136 Stat. 1313, 1339), this program provides states with funding to implement firearm violence reduction strategies at the intersections of behavioral health and domestic violence. This includes funding for extreme risk protection order (ERPO) programs, mental health courts, drug courts, veteran treatment courts, behavioral health deflection programs, and law enforcement efforts to safely store relinquished firearms.

structured_extraction.program_name: Child Advocacy Center Services (CACS) Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This grant program supports Child Advocacy Centers (CACs) across Maryland, which bring together professionals from law enforcement, child protective services, social work, and other disciplines as a multi-disciplinary team to handle child abuse cases, including sexual crimes against children. The primary purpose is to coordinate investigation of child abuse and neglect and provide services to children and non-offending family members without causing further trauma, approaching victims in a sensitive, respectful manner and restoring lives of abused children through partnerships with local communities and agencies. The goal is to ensure children are not traumatized by the investigative and intervention process and to help centers meet accreditation standards under the Maryland Statewide Organization for Child Advocacy Centers. Funding supports the coordination of investigative and intervention services by designated Child Advocacy Centers and the Maryland Children's Alliance.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding provided to Child Advocacy Centers and the Maryland Children's Alliance to support services related to child abuse and sexual crimes against children investigations, including meeting national and statewide accreditation standards per Criminal Procedure 11-928(e). Grants may fund contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, personnel, travel, and other related costs. Funding is reimbursed quarterly unless otherwise noted. Funding must supplement, not supplant, money received from other sources.

structured_extraction.program_name: Child Sex Trafficking Screening and Services Act Regional Navigator Program (RGNV)
structured_extraction.program_description: This program funds organizations to provide regional navigator services for child sex trafficking victims. Regional navigators help law enforcement and local Departments of Social Services connect child victims of sex trafficking with needed services, support self-sufficiency, improve victim safety, and ensure victims know their rights and available resources. The program requires law enforcement and local Departments of Social Services to notify a Regional Navigator when they have reason to believe a child is a victim of sex or labor trafficking. Grantees must coordinate and/or provide services for suspected child sex or labor trafficking victims until the child reaches age 24. The program expanded statewide to cover all 24 Maryland jurisdictions as of FY2023. Grant funding is provided under the ARPA (American Rescue Plan Act) State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds (SLFRF), CFDA/ALN 21.027.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding covers contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, personnel, travel, and other costs to support regional navigator programs for child sex trafficking victims. For SFY2024, up to $1,750,000 in total funding was available with up to 8 awards ranging from $50,000 to $200,000 (single jurisdiction) or up to $500,000 (multiple jurisdictions). For SFY2026, 14 continuation awards are available at SFY2024 levels. Funding is provided under ARPA (American Rescue Plan Act) State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds (SLFRF), CFDA/ALN 21.027.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, personnel, travel, and other costs related to providing regional navigator services for child sex trafficking victims. structured_extraction.program_description: An intensive 5-day course designed to give child abuse professionals the skills to conduct legally sufficient forensic interviews of child sexual abuse victims. Topics include effective interviewing techniques, child development, how children experience sexual abuse and disclosure, age-appropriate questioning, team communication, and building stronger cases for prosecution.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free 5-day forensic interviewing training fully funded through a federal Children's Justice Act grant. Maryland has been a certified ChildFirst® state since 2004. The Maryland Police and Correctional Training Commission has coordinated the program since 2007.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training to conduct forensic interviews of child sexual abuse victims
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a child abuse professional

structured_extraction.program_name: Children's Justice Act Committee (CJAC) Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Federal grant program under the Child Abuse Prevention and Treatment Act (CAPTA) that funds efforts to improve the investigative, administrative, and judicial handling of child abuse, neglect, and maltreatment cases — particularly child sexual abuse and exploitation — in ways that limit additional trauma to child victims. Focuses on front-end, intake, and investigative stages of child welfare through innovative programming, including support for multidisciplinary teams (MDTs) and collaborative efforts using evidence-informed, developmentally appropriate, legally sound, culturally responsive, and trauma-informed techniques. Direct services are not permitted. Federal Children's Justice Act funds are awarded to eligible organizations in Maryland to develop, establish, and operate programs addressing child abuse and neglect cases.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Approximately $282,000 total funding available for FFY 2026, with 5–7 sub-awards ranging from $50,000 to $75,000 each. Funds are reimbursed on a quarterly basis based on actual expenditures. Allowable budget categories include personnel (salaries, fringe benefits), operating expenses (rent, communications, postage), travel (per state/federal rates), contractual services (consultant services up to $81.25/hour or $650/day), equipment (unit cost $10,000 or more), supplies and equipment under $10,000, training and technical assistance, and other eligible costs. Federal funds cannot supplant state or local funds.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Developing, establishing, and operating programs that improve investigation, prosecution, and judicial handling of child abuse and neglect cases while minimizing trauma to child victims. Allowable costs include: personnel (salary and fringe benefits for MDT members and child abuse investigators), operating expenses (rent, communication, postage, printing), travel (per state/federal rates), contractual services (consultant services up to $81.25/hour or $650/day), equipment (unit cost $10,000 or more), supplies and equipment under $10,000, training and technical assistance, and other eligible expenses. structured_extraction.program_description: Established in 2016 by §4–701 through 4–703 of the Public Safety Article, this program provides grants to local law enforcement agencies to establish community programs and to local government agencies to establish violence intervention programs. Funded programs must offer recreational or athletic opportunities, improve relations between citizens and law enforcement, otherwise benefit the community, or support violence intervention efforts. The program seeks to develop criminal justice strategies coordinated at local, state, and federal levels and aims to enhance relationships between law enforcement and youth.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging from $5,000 to $50,000, with up to $500,000 in total available funding and 15–25 anticipated awards. The award period is July 1, 2026 – June 30, 2027. Funds are disbursed on a quarterly reimbursable basis following submission of quarterly fiscal and programmatic reports. Eligible budget categories include personnel, operating expenses, travel, contractual services, equipment, and other allowable costs.

Eligible program activities include recreational or athletic opportunities, police/community events (e.g., National Night Out), violence intervention programs, School Resource Officer programs in public schools, and partnerships with community groups such as food pantries, recreational leagues, athletic events, and local health departments.

structured_extraction.program_description: COAP provides states, tribes, territories, and local governments with funding to develop or expand comprehensive programs in response to the overdose crisis and impacts of illicit opioids, stimulants, or other substances. It supports efforts to respond to illicit substance use and misuse, reduce overdose deaths, promote public safety, and support access to prevention, harm reduction, treatment, and recovery services. In Maryland, it supports the Law Enforcement Assisted Diversion (LEAD) program, which connects law enforcement with service providers to divert people with mental illness or substance use disorders away from the criminal justice system. Priority is given to expanding access to Medication for Opioid Use Disorder (MOUD) and Medication-Assisted Treatment (MAT) for individuals involved in the justice system. Funds also support racial equity efforts, harm reduction, youth prevention, workforce expansion, and recovery support services. Funded through the Office of Justice Programs, Bureau of Justice Assistance (AL# 16.838).
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding issued on a quarterly reimbursement basis for actual expenditures in approved budget categories: personnel (salaries, wages, fringe benefits; max 30%), operating expenses (rent, communications, printing), travel (per Maryland rates), contractual services (consultant rates max $81.25/hour or $650/day), equipment ($10,000+ per unit with useful life >1 year), supplies, and indirect costs (negotiated rate or 15% de minimis). Subawards up to $50K per subaward are allowed. Specific award amounts are not stated on the program page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: County, local, and state government agencies, non-profits, for-profit entities, medical institutions, educational institutions, and community-based organizations in Maryland responding to opioid and substance use crises
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Implementing and expanding substance use diversion programs (e.g. LEAD), medication-assisted treatment (MOUD/MAT), harm reduction efforts, youth prevention programs, addiction workforce development, and recovery support services. Eligible cost categories include personnel, contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, travel, supplies, indirect costs, and other approved costs. Also includes case management, peer recovery services, housing coordination, behavioral health care, and connections to employment, education, and benefits.

Service sites may be local (specific county), multijurisdictional, or statewide. Applicant must have active SAM.gov registration with valid expiration date.
