Applicants should draft narratives in a word processor first, then transfer to the state Grant Management System (GMS). Multiple narrative sections with specific word limits are required. Submit signed Certified Assurances and other required documents in the GMS document section by the NOFA due date.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides funding to domestic violence centers to respond to incidents of family violence, intimate partner stalking, domestic violence, and dating violence, and to develop and strengthen victim services in cases involving such crimes. Grants support comprehensive domestic violence programs, county and local government agencies, direct victim services providers, local and state law enforcement, state domestic violence coalitions, and faith-based and community organizations.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants fund contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, personnel, travel, training, and other costs for eligible domestic violence programs and government agencies responding to family violence, domestic violence, and dating violence and strengthening victim services. Funds are reimbursed quarterly. For FY2023: $3,000,000 total available — Category A (COMAR programs): $1,500,000, up to 19 awards of $78,947 each; Category B (Other DVC programs): $1,500,000, up to 30 awards ranging from $50,000–$100,000 each. Funds must supplement, not supplant, existing state or local funds.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Projected application month: August; FY2023 deadline was Monday, September 19, 2022 by 3:00 PM
structured_extraction.program_audience: Comprehensive domestic violence programs, county and local government agencies, direct victim services providers, local and state law enforcement, state domestic violence coalitions, faith-based organizations, community organizations, and state government agencies serving domestic violence victims and survivors.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Personnel salaries and fringe benefits, equipment, training, operating expenses, travel, contractual services, program supplies, registration fees, and other approved costs related to responding to family violence, domestic violence, and dating violence and strengthening victim services. Fringe benefits cannot exceed 30% of salary costs; equipment over $5,000 requires inventory records.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland; applicants must specify their service area (county-specific, multi-jurisdictional, or statewide).

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through the Grant Management System (GMS). Applicants must complete the online application, submit a detailed budget with justifications for all line items prioritized by funding priority, and generate and sign required certifications. The NOFA is projected to be released in September and applications are projected to be due in August.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program certifies nonprofit and government victim services providers to get online access to shielded peace order and protective order court records. Certified organizations can view these shielded records to help victims of abuse. Certification is granted for a three-year period under COMAR 01.04.04.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Approved organizations receive online access to shielded peace order and protective order court records to assist victims of abuse. Certification lasts three years (current period: March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2029).
structured_extraction.program_audience: State-designated domestic violence shelters, certified rape crisis centers, and Maryland Legal Services Corporation grantees identified by the Maryland Network Against Domestic Violence or the Maryland Coalition Against Sexual Assault as entities that provide services to victims. Other organizations may also be considered at the agency's discretion.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Online access to shielded court records to assist victims of abuse.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland-based victim services providers.
requirements_list: Must be a State-designated domestic violence shelter, a certified rape crisis center, or a Maryland Legal Services Corporation grantee identified by MNADV or MCASA as providing services to victims
Organizations not in these categories may be deemed eligible at the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy's discretion

Full cooperation with inquiries regarding misuse

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the completed 2026 DVCR Certification Application along with any questions to Rebecca Allyn at rebecca.allyn@maryland.gov by January 30, 2026. Applications must include an attachment describing confidential information policies and procedures; Category 4 organizations must submit additional supporting materials.

structured_extraction.program_description: This grant program provides funding to local and state law enforcement agencies to meet District and Circuit Court guidelines for serving protective orders efficiently and on time. It reduces the delay between the issuance of ex parte orders and protective orders and their entry into the MILES/NCIC law enforcement database, and supports the establishment or operation of domestic violence units within law enforcement agencies.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State-funded grants to local and state law enforcement agencies to support personnel costs related to serving protective orders and entering them into the MILES/NCIC database in a timely manner, as well as establishing or supporting domestic violence units.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local and state law enforcement agencies in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Personnel costs related to serving protective orders and entering them into the MILES/NCIC database, and meeting District and Circuit Court guidelines for domestic violence case handling
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to local and state law enforcement agencies
requirements_list: Must be a local or state law enforcement agency
Must be a registered user of the Grants Management System to apply
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download the Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) from the program page, register in the Grants Management System, and submit an application online by the deadline.

structured_extraction.program_name: Edward J. Byrne Memorial Justice Assistance Grant (JAG) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Bureau of Justice Assistance (BJA) of the U.S. Department of Justice allocates funding each year to states and local governments based on population and crime statistics. Administered in Maryland by the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy, the program supports a broad range of state and local criminal justice initiatives to help Maryland achieve safer communities. Funds are intended to fill gaps in services related to violent crime, crime victims, law enforcement, prosecution, adjudication, detention, and rehabilitation. Local governments such as Anne Arundel County apply under annual Local Solicitations. A Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) is projected to be released in August each year, with applications accepted in September via the Grant Management System (GMS).
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual formula-based grant funding allocated to eligible state and local governments and organizations for criminal justice purposes. Funds may be used for personnel, training, equipment, contractual services, operating expenses, travel, and other costs supporting criminal justice programs. Amounts are determined by BJA formulas based on population and crime statistics. Three funding allocations available under SFY 2026: General BJAG Formula Funds ($911,378 available, up to 18 awards, $20,000-$100,000 each). Funds are reimbursed on a quarterly basis based on actual expenditures. Local governments such as Anne Arundel County apply under annual Local Solicitations with authorization from their governing bodies. Applications are submitted through the Grant Management System (GMS). No matching funds required.
structured_extraction.program_audience: State and local government agencies, law enforcement agencies, nonprofit organizations, faith-based organizations, institutions of higher learning, and units of local government working on criminal justice issues in Maryland, including those listed on the BJA JAG Allocations List such as the City of Annapolis and Anne Arundel County. Individuals and for-profit entities are not eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Personnel salaries and fringe benefits, training, equipment, contractual services, operating expenses, travel, technology, supplies, and other costs supporting criminal justice programs addressing violent crime, victim services, law enforcement, prosecution, adjudication, detention, and rehabilitation. Funds must supplement, not supplant, existing state or local funds. Excluded uses include alcoholic beverages, bonuses, construction, fundraising, lobbying, meals, and trinkets.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland; units of local government listed on the BJAG Allocations List are eligible, including the City of Annapolis and Anne Arundel County. Projects must serve specific Maryland jurisdictions and identify geographic coverage areas with city and 9-digit zip codes.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a faith-based organization, institute of higher learning, local government agency, local law enforcement, nonprofit organization, state government agency, or state law enforcement agency
Individuals and for-profit entities are not eligible
Applicant must be a unit of local government listed on the BJAG Allocations List (for local solicitations)
Program must address gaps in service related to violent crime, crime victims, enforcement, prosecution, adjudication, detention, or rehabilitation
Project must support at least one Federal Purpose Area and one State Priority Area
Must submit an application and appendices per BJA guidance
Applications reviewed based on eligibility, relevance, and merit
Application must be submitted through the Grant Management System (GMS)
Must comply with applicable fiscal year Local Solicitation requirements
Local governments may require governing body authorization (e.g., county council resolution) before submitting application
Application must be made public with opportunity for citizen and community-based organization comment
No supplanting of state or local funds with federal grant funds
Single audit required if organization expends $1,000,000 or more in federal awards during fiscal year
Property Inventory Report Forms (PIRFs) required for equipment costing $10,000 or more per unit
No sensitive personally identifiable information (PII) allowed in applications
Non-profit applicants must provide 501(c)(3) documentation
Contracts existing at application time must be uploaded to GMS; post-award contracts must be uploaded before reimbursement
Project summary limited to 100 words or less
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: A Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) is released each year (projected in August). Applications for SFY 2026 are due September 10, 2025 at 11:59 PM. Applicants submit through the Grant Management System (GMS). A draft application is posted for public comment before submission; comments should be directed to the program manager. For local solicitations, local governments such as Anne Arundel County may require governing body authorization and a public comment period before submitting to the U.S. Department of Justice, Office of Justice Programs. Funds are reimbursed quarterly based on actual expenditures.

structured_extraction.program_description: This grant program funds local domestic violence services programs to provide temporary shelter and supportive services to victims of family violence, domestic violence, and dating violence and their dependents. It supports program establishment, maintenance, and expansion, including specialized services for children exposed to domestic violence, underserved populations, and racial and ethnic minority victims. These programs provide comprehensive services to meet the specific needs of domestic violence victims and their families, increasing the likelihood that victims will benefit from services and that appropriate linkages to other community-based services are made. Provision of services fosters a coordinated community approach that includes partnerships with law enforcement, courts, hospitals, local departments of social services, and other related support agencies. Grants are made through a network of local domestic violence services programs statewide.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants fund direct victim services including 24-hour hotline services, safe accommodations and emergency shelter, therapeutic counseling, legal counseling and advocacy, court accompaniment, case management, employment services, transportation, childcare, health and behavioral health services, prevention services, and specialized services for underserved populations (tribal communities, LGBTQ individuals, persons with disabilities, culturally and linguistically specific populations, and individuals with Limited English Proficiency). Funding is provided on a quarterly reimbursement of expenditures basis and covers personnel, equipment, operating expenses, contractual services, and travel.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adult victims of family, domestic, and dating violence; youth victims; dependent children of victims; non-abusing parents; children exposed to violence; and underserved populations. Served through rape crisis centers and local domestic violence services programs statewide.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Temporary shelter and emergency housing, supportive services, safety planning, individual and group counseling, peer support, legal advocacy, medical advocacy and referrals, case management, employment services, transportation, childcare, health and behavioral health services, housing assistance and homelessness prevention, prevention services, training and technical assistance, outreach and awareness activities, and culturally and linguistically appropriate services for domestic violence victims and their dependents.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — available to eligible organizations across Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a rape crisis center or local domestic violence services program
Applicant must be a non-profit 501(c)(3) organization or faith-based organization (grant funds cannot support inherently religious activities)
Comprehensive domestic violence service providers must be designated by COMAR
Sub-recipients must have organizational capacity to provide direct victim services
Non-profit entities with awards over $50,000 must comply with monthly reporting requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: A Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) is projected to be released in June, with applications due in July. Applications are submitted through the state Grant Management System (GMS).

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grant funds to law enforcement agencies and prosecutors that have a demonstrated need and a viable plan to reduce firearms-related violence in their jurisdictions. Supports removal of illegal firearms from Maryland communities and reinforces prevention, disruption, and prosecution strategies. Funds support contractual services, equipment, personnel, travel, and other costs related to reducing gun violence across Maryland. Administered in collaboration with the Maryland CeaseFire Council.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to 25 awards ranging from $15,000 to $100,000, with total anticipated funding of $926,940. Award amounts are based on jurisdictional needs and impact levels. Funds support personnel (salaries/overtime for law enforcement, prosecutors, crime analysts), travel, contractual services, equipment (ballistic technology, gunshot detection systems, case management systems), covert investigations, firearm tracing, and other costs related to reducing firearms-related crime. Grants are reimbursed on a quarterly basis.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Matika Palmer (Grant Monitor); Tabitha Wilson (Fund Manager); Courtney Thomas (Fiscal Specialist); Richard Alban (Assistant Director, Public Safety Strategies)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local law enforcement agencies, state law enforcement agencies, and State's Attorney's Offices (SAOs) in Maryland. Note: Maryland Criminal Intelligence Network (MCIN) lead sites are NOT eligible; however, allied MCIN partners are encouraged to apply.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Personnel salaries and overtime for law enforcement officers, prosecutors, and crime analysts dedicated to gun violence reduction; travel to conferences, workshops, and training on gun violence prevention; contractual services for expert consultants and research organizations; equipment including ballistic technology, gunshot detection systems, and case management systems; covert investigations; firearm tracing; educational materials and public awareness campaigns; and other allowable costs related to addressing firearms-related violence.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to eligible Maryland law enforcement and prosecution agencies.

structured_extraction.program_name: Internet Crimes Against Children (ICAC) Task Force Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: Supports investigations and prosecutions of internet crimes against children, and the ongoing operations of the Maryland Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force. Aims to reduce victimization of Maryland's children by protecting them from abuse or neglect, addressing Adverse Childhood Experiences (ACEs) and childhood trauma, and developing coordinated criminal justice strategies at state and local levels. Funds can be used for salaries, training, equipment, travel, operating expenses, and contractual services. The governor must include at least $2 million for local law enforcement and the ICAC Task Force, and up to 25% of funds may support child advocacy centers.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants disbursed on a quarterly reimbursable basis for: salaries/fringe benefits for law enforcement, forensic interviewers, victim advocates, and digital forensic analysts; training for law enforcement; equipment ($10,000+ unit cost); supplies, software, and training (<$10,000); operating expenses (rent, communication, postage for ICAC Task Force only); travel for ICAC-related conferences and training; contractual services for investigation/prosecution support. The governor must include at least $2 million for local law enforcement and the ICAC Task Force. Up to 25% of funds may support child advocacy centers. Fringe benefits may not exceed 30% of salary costs without prior approval. Consultant rates capped at $81.25/hour or $650/day.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local law enforcement agencies, state law enforcement agencies (including Maryland State Police), designated child advocacy centers (accredited or on path to accreditation by National Children's Alliance), prosecutorial offices, victim advocacy organizations, and digital forensic analysts in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Investigation and prosecution of internet crimes against children; personnel support (salaries, overtime, fringe benefits) for sworn officers, forensic interviewers, victim advocates, and digital forensic analysts; equipment for investigation and prosecution; training; operating expenses; travel; contractual services. Federal funds cannot supplant state or local funds and cannot be used for explicitly religious activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — available to eligible agencies and centers throughout Maryland. Projects must serve specific geographic areas (county-wide, statewide, or multijurisdictional).

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide initiative that provides technical assistance, training, and grant funding to support police-led diversion programs for individuals with substance use disorders. The program connects law enforcement directly to service providers and supports communities in developing diversion and deflection programs to reduce opioid overdose deaths and increase access to care and treatment. Part of the Comprehensive Opioid, Stimulant, and Substance Abuse Program (COSSAP), developed under the Comprehensive Addiction and Recovery Act (CARA), aimed at identifying, responding to, treating, and supporting those impacted by illicit opioids, stimulants, and other drugs of abuse.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy awards federal COSSUP (Comprehensive Opioid, Stimulant, and Substance Use Program) funds to local sites. In 2019, a $6.5 million federal grant was received to support nine communities over four years. In 2022, an additional $6 million federal grant was received to continue diversion and deflection programming. Funding is designed to be flexible, allowing each community to address unique needs and respond to emerging threats. Funded sites also receive ongoing training and technical assistance materials.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local health departments, law enforcement agencies, public defender offices, and other government and non-profit stakeholders working on substance use diversion programs in Maryland. Also serves people referred for arrest diversion or social contact referral, particularly those impacted by substance abuse.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supporting police-led diversion programs, detention-based referrals, treatment access, and community partnerships to address substance use disorders and reduce opioid overdose deaths. Funds may be used for development, implementation, or expansion of comprehensive efforts to identify, respond to, treat, and support those impacted by illicit opioids, stimulants, and other drugs of abuse.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; current awarded sites include Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Calvert, Carroll, Garrett, Howard, Harford, St. Mary's, and Washington counties.
requirements_list: Must be a local government agency or qualified partner organization in Maryland
Must be focused on substance use disorder diversion, deflection, or treatment
Must comply with data collection and reporting requirements outlined in the LEAD Data Definitions and Reporting Guide
Submission of quarterly data by January 15, April 15, July 15, and October 15
Tracking of referrals, enrollments, demographics, service referrals, and outcomes
Regular meetings with key decision makers
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy's Criminal Justice Programs Division for information on COSSUP funding. More information is available at the COAP grants page linked from the main program page.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Law Enforcement Training Scholarship Program provides scholarships of up to $5,000 per person per course to support specialized law enforcement training for eligible state and local law enforcement agencies in Maryland. Designed to support access to specialized investigative and law enforcement training for criminal justice professionals, it provides funding for specialized training courses and seminars in investigation, crime prevention, crime analysis, and related topics. Funds cover non-degree courses and related expenses such as travel, lodging, registration fees, and training materials. Funds may also be used to bring trainers directly to a law enforcement agency. No matching funds are required.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Scholarships of up to $5,000 per individual per course; agency fiscal year LETS request cannot exceed $5,000; minimum application amount $1,000. No matching funds required. Funds may be used for non-degree training courses and related expenses including travel, lodging, registration fees, and training materials, or to bring trainers directly to the agency. Funds are distributed on a quarterly reimbursement basis following submission of fiscal and programmatic reports.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Continuous/Ongoing; subject to funding availability; applications must be received at least 30 business days before training begins; projects must end on or before September 30, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Criminal justice professionals including law enforcement officers, deputies, lab technicians, and attorney's office staff at state and local law enforcement agencies, local State's Attorney's Offices, and the Maryland Attorney General's Office.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Registration fees, training materials, travel expenses (airfare, mileage, parking, ground transportation), lodging, and per diem. May also fund bringing trainers directly to a law enforcement agency.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All eligible state and local law enforcement agencies in Maryland, including prosecuting agencies.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a state or local law enforcement agency, prosecutorial office, or qualifying Maryland government office.
Applications must be submitted at least 30 business days prior to the start of the training.
Applicant must be a registered user of the Grants Management System to apply.
Training must be a non-degree course.
No cost-share required.
Funds must supplement existing budget, not replace previously appropriated funds (no supplanting).
SAM.gov registration with valid UEI required.
Consultant rates capped at $81.25/hour or $650/day; higher rates require prior approval.
Quarterly programmatic reports due within 15 calendar days of quarter end.
Quarterly financial reports due within 30 calendar days of quarter end.

Submit Certified Assurances and Federal Anti-Lobbying Certification signed by Authorized Representative.
Single audit requirement if expending $1,000,000 or more in federal awards annually.
Subrecipient Organizational Capacity Questionnaire (SOCQ) required with supporting policy/procedure attachments.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register as a user in the Grants Management System (GMS), download the Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA), and submit an application online through the GMS. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis but must be submitted at least 30 business days before the training start date. Include project narrative, budget details, letters of support, sustainability plan, and disclosure of pending applications. Funds are reimbursed on a quarterly basis following submission of fiscal and programmatic reports.

structured_extraction.program_name: Legal Services for Crime Victims Fund (LSCV)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides annual grants to ensure that Maryland crime victims have legal representation in court. Funded through unclaimed restitution collected by the Division of Parole and Probation (DPP) and Department of Juvenile Services (DJS) under Maryland Criminal Procedure Article §11-919, the program distributes grants to organizations that provide legal counsel (advice, consultation, or representation by licensed attorneys) to victims of crime and delinquent acts to protect victims' rights as provided by law. Created by the Maryland General Assembly in 2007.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual grants funded by unclaimed restitution collected under Maryland Criminal Procedure Article §11-919. Total anticipated funding is $150,000 for SFY 2027, with a maximum award of $75,000 per recipient (2 awards anticipated). Grant funds are reimbursed on a quarterly basis. Funded categories include personnel (staff attorneys, directors of legal services), contractual services, equipment (useful life >1 year, cost ≥$10,000/unit), operating expenses, travel (within State of Maryland reimbursement rates), and other costs. Consultant rates capped at $81.25/hour or $650/day; fringe benefits capped at 30% of salary unless prior approval received.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local government agencies, state government agencies, and nonprofit organizations (including faith-based and community organizations) that provide statewide legal services to crime victims in Maryland, including primary and secondary victims and Limited English Proficient (LEP) individuals.

Allowable budget categories include: personnel (salaries and fringe benefits for staff attorneys, directors of legal services); operating expenses (rent, communication, postage, printing); travel (mileage, transportation, meals, lodging within State of Maryland reimbursement rates); contractual services (consultant contracts for training/evaluation); equipment; supplies; other (registration fees, indirect costs). structured_extraction.program_name: Local Warrant Apprehension & Absconding Grant Program (WAAG)
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides grants to local law enforcement agencies and local government agencies across Maryland to help reduce the number of open warrants — especially for violent crimes — and to apprehend individuals who have absconded from court-ordered drug or alcohol treatment facilities without administrator permission. The program aims to improve quality of life and create safer communities through reduction in violent crime, and supports coordinated criminal justice strategies and data-driven decision making.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $1,000,000 total available for SFY 2026 with up to 30 awards anticipated. Award amounts vary by agency size: Small Agencies (up to 50 sworn officers) up to $30,000; Medium Agencies (51–300 sworn officers) up to $50,000; Large Agencies (300+ sworn officers) up to $75,000. Individual award range: $10,000 to $75,000. Funds are reimbursed on a quarterly basis and may cover personnel overtime, data analysis, clerical data entry, communication/postage, extradition travel, consultant services, equipment, and supplies for safe warrant execution. Contractual services, operating expenses, and other allowable costs are also covered.

structured_extraction.program_name: Markell Hendricks Youth Crime Prevention and Diversion Parole Grant Program (YCPD)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grant funding to local law enforcement agencies and eligible organizations to support diversion programs or youth engagement programs in high-crime areas. Focuses on creating outreach and programming to divert youth who committed threshold offenses (including school-based offenses) from formal juvenile justice system processing. Goal is to reduce youth entering the juvenile justice system by providing supportive services within communities. Created by Maryland law (HB1348, 2019) and administered by the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: $50,000 available for one award for SFY 2026, with intent of two additional years of level funding for SFY 2027 and SFY 2028 (contingent on good standing and positive outcomes). Grant funds are reimbursed quarterly based on actual expenditures. Allowable costs include personnel, operating expenses, travel, contractual services (consultants capped at $81.25/hour or $650/day), equipment ($10,000+ per unit), and other costs. Priority jurisdictions include Anne Arundel County, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Prince George's County, and Montgomery County (which account for 51.1% of statewide youth intake complaints per FY24 data).

structured_extraction.program_description: The Criminal Injuries Compensation Board (CICB) provides financial compensation to innocent victims of crime in Maryland to help remedy the harm caused by criminal activity. It reimburses eligible victims and their families for medical expenses, lost wages, funeral costs, crime scene cleanup, and other crime-related losses not covered by other sources. It covers medical/dental expenses and lost wages for physical injuries, psychological injury expenses (including counseling) for certain offenses, lost wages for psychological injuries, bereavement leave, disability compensation, funeral expenses for homicide victims, loss of support for dependents of homicide victims, and crime scene cleanup costs. Emergency and supplemental awards are also available. CICB is the payer of last resort — all other available reimbursement sources must be used first. The board's authority is construed to remedy harm to victims and in favor of eligibility for the victim or claimant.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial compensation for crime victims covering: medical/dental expenses related to physical injury; psychological injury expenses (including counseling) for certain offenses; lost earnings directly related to inability to work after the crime; bereavement leave up to 2 weeks or $2,000; disability (total or partial, permanent or temporary); funeral expenses for homicide victims; loss of support or dependency when a homicide victim was providing support; crime scene cleanup costs; up to 30 days in lost wages for a parent or guardian caring for a child injured by crime; and other expenses approved by the Board. Emergency and supplemental awards are also available. Minimum of $100 in unreimbursed costs required. Lost wages require at least two continuous weeks of lost earnings, or less if combined with other eligible costs over $100. CICB is the payer of last resort — all other available reimbursement sources must be exhausted before CICB pays.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Within 3 years from the date of the crime or the death of the victim; in child abuse cases, within 3 years of when the claimant knew or should have known of the abuse.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Innocent victims of crime who have suffered physical or psychological injuries, surviving spouses or children of homicide victims, persons who assumed funeral expenses for a homicide victim, dependents of homicide victims, persons injured while preventing a crime or assisting a police officer, persons injured or killed by a drunk driver, certain family members of incarcerated abusers, parents/guardians of minor victims, secondary victims, persons responsible for crime-related expenses, and other eligible claimants throughout Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Medical/dental expenses, psychological injury expenses (including counseling), mental health treatment costs, lost wages, bereavement leave, disability compensation, funeral/burial expenses, crime scene cleanup, loss of financial support for dependents of homicide victims, lost wages for caregivers of injured children, and other crime-related expenses approved by the Board.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Crime must have occurred in Maryland (exceptions may apply). CICB office is located at 6776 Reisterstown Rd, Suite 209, Baltimore, MD 21215.
requirements_list: Must be an innocent victim of crime in Maryland who suffered physical or psychological injury as a result of a crime or delinquent act, a surviving spouse or child of a homicide victim, a person who assumed funeral expenses for a homicide victim, or a dependent of a homicide victim
Unless good cause is shown, must report the crime to appropriate authorities within 48 hours of the crime occurring
Must have incurred at least $100 in unreimbursed reimbursable expenses or lost wages
To receive lost wages, must have lost at least two continuous weeks of earnings or support (this period can be less if combined with more than $100 in other unreimbursed eligible costs)
Victim must not have caused, provoked, or substantially contributed to the crime that caused the injury
Victim was not engaged in criminal activity when injured
Must cooperate with law enforcement and CICB unless good cause is shown for not doing so
Claims must be filed within 3 years of the date of the crime or the victim's death
For child abuse cases, claim must be filed within 3 years of when the claimant knew or should have known of the abuse
Claimants must be at least 18 years old; parents or guardians may apply on behalf of minor victims
Physical injury or death must be directly related to the crime
All other available reimbursement sources must be exhausted before CICB pays
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Application for Crime Victim Compensation (available in English and Spanish with instructions). Forms can be obtained by calling 410-697-9338 or 1-888-679-9347, or by downloading them online from the CICB website. Submit the completed application to the Criminal Injuries Compensation Board at 6776 Reisterstown Rd, Suite 209, Baltimore, MD 21215. Victim advocates are available to assist with applications and provide status updates.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Criminal Intelligence Network (MCIN) program brings together criminal justice agencies to collaborate on tactics, resources, and intelligence through data sharing, cross-jurisdictional partnerships, and supporting technologies. It focuses on identifying, disrupting, and dismantling gangs and violent criminal networks involved in illegal drug distribution, firearms violence, human trafficking, and other violent criminal enterprises through enforcement, prevention, intervention, and information sharing. At the local level, the grant funds agencies such as the Frederick Police Department, covering personnel costs including a Crime Analyst and a Heroin Coordinator who helps overdose victims connect to resources, as well as overtime pay for larger investigations involving regional law enforcement partners such as the Frederick County Sheriff's Office, Thurmont Police Department, and Brunswick Police Department.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding to support a coalition of criminal justice agencies sharing criminal intelligence and improving intelligence infrastructure. Funds may cover contractual services, equipment, personnel costs (e.g., Crime Analyst, Heroin Coordinator), travel, overtime pay for regional law enforcement investigations, and other costs. Eligible applicants include local law enforcement, state law enforcement, and State's Attorney's Offices.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local law enforcement agencies, state law enforcement agencies, and State's Attorney's Offices in Maryland targeting gangs and violent criminal networks, as well as regional law enforcement partners.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Improving intelligence infrastructure; collecting information to support investigations identifying and dismantling criminal networks; employing subject matter experts trained to investigate such networks; paying for expert prosecutors to prosecute cases at the federal and state levels; personnel costs (Crime Analyst, Heroin Coordinator); and overtime funding for larger regional law enforcement investigations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — available to eligible law enforcement and prosecutorial agencies throughout Maryland. structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide program that funds local domestic violence service organizations to prevent incidents of family violence, domestic violence, and dating violence and to meet the needs of all victims and their dependents, including those in underserved communities. The program makes temporary shelter environments and supportive services available through a network of local domestic violence services programs, including 24-hour hotlines, safe accommodations, therapeutic counseling, legal counseling, court accompaniment, community awareness activities, and abuse intervention programs. It aims to increase access to services locally and foster coordinated community responses, including partnerships with law enforcement, courts, hospitals, and social service agencies.

Maximum award per jurisdiction: $116,099. Grants are reimbursable on a quarterly basis with no match required.

Created to implement the Declaration of Crime Victims' Rights Amendment to the Maryland Constitution and federal guidelines for treating and assisting crime victims and witnesses, the fund is administered by the State Board of Victim Services under the Governor's authority through the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Entertainment District Security Grant (EDSG) helps community organizations, nonprofits, and local governments fund security operations during high-pedestrian-traffic times in entertainment districts that generate above-average calls for police assistance. Established in 2024 under §§4–1701 through §4–1703 of the Public Safety Article of the Maryland Code, the program supports security and law enforcement overtime, purchase of surveillance cameras and other equipment, hiring of security administrators, and public safety awareness initiatives. It aims to reduce crime and improve public safety in entertainment districts across Maryland.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding distributed on a quarterly reimbursable basis to cover personnel (including law enforcement overtime and security administrator hiring), equipment (surveillance cameras, enhanced lighting, communication tools), operating expenses, travel, contractual services, emergency response training, lighting improvements, public safety signage, and other allowable costs related to security operations in entertainment districts. Equipment costing $10,000 or more requires a Property Inventory Report Form (PIRF). Consultant rates are capped at $81.25/hour or $650/day without prior approval, and fringe benefits may not exceed 30% of salary costs without prior approval.

structured_extraction.program_name: Opioid Use Disorder Examinations and Treatment Program (HB 116)
structured_extraction.program_description: This statewide program requires local correctional facilities and the Baltimore Pretrial Complex to screen, evaluate, and treat incarcerated individuals for opioid use disorder, specifically using medications to treat opioid use disorder (MOUD). The program was phased in beginning with four counties (Howard, Montgomery, Prince George's, St. Mary's) by January 2020, six additional counties by October 2021, and all counties by January 2023. The Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services partnered with HealthCare Access Maryland and Health Management Associates to support implementation and provide technical assistance to local correctional facilities, including virtual learning sessions, individualized coaching, site visits, and a learning collaborative.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Technical assistance is provided to local correctional facilities to help implement opioid use disorder screening, evaluation, and treatment programs. This includes 14 virtual learning sessions, 21 site visits to 18 correctional facilities, individualized 1:1 coaching to correctional and healthcare teams, and an all-day in-person learning collaborative (133 participants). Program resources, data reporting tools, and curriculum aligned to HB 116 requirements were developed in partnership with HealthCare Access Maryland and Health Management Associates. Facilities are also supported in providing all three FDA-approved MAT medications (methadone, buprenorphine, naltrexone), reentry coordination, Medicaid enrollment assistance, peer recovery specialist integration, and harm reduction strategies.

structured_extraction.program_name: Paul Coverdell National Forensic Sciences Improvement Program (CFSI)
structured_extraction.program_description: This federal grant program provides funding to crime laboratories and medical examiner's offices to improve the quality and timeliness of forensic science and medical examiner/coroner services. Funds can be used to eliminate evidence analysis backlogs, purchase equipment, train forensic staff on new techniques, pursue accreditation, and buy supplies. The program supports law enforcement goals of disrupting criminal organizations and addresses bottlenecks in evidentiary forensic sample examination. It is administered by the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services and distributed to certified state and local forensic science laboratories across Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Performance Incentive Grant Fund (PIGF) provides grants funded by savings from Maryland's Justice Reinvestment Act (JRA) reforms. The program supports evidence-based initiatives to safely reduce Maryland's prison population, improve reentry outcomes, reduce recidivism, support crime victims, and connect nonviolent offenders with behavioral health treatment and community support services. It provides for county-led innovations and state expansions of programming prioritized by Maryland's Justice Reinvestment Coordinating Council (JRCC). Eligible applicants include community-based nonprofit organizations, local government agencies, state government agencies, local detention centers, local health departments, faith-based organizations, and state and local courts. Program outcomes are monitored by the Justice Reinvestment Oversight Board.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants funded by savings from Maryland's Justice Reinvestment Act reforms. Category A (JRA Funding Initiatives): up to $450,000 for state agencies; up to $200,000 for nonprofits. Category B (Local Funding Initiatives): up to $350,000 for local government; up to $200,000 for nonprofits. Minimum award: $50,000; Maximum award: $450,000. Funds are issued on a quarterly, reimbursable basis and can cover personnel, operating expenses, travel, contractual services (consultants capped at $81.25/hour or $650/day), equipment (under $10,000), and other approved costs. The SFY 2027 funding opportunity had an application deadline of April 3, 2026 at 11:59 p.m.

structured_extraction.program_name: Police Accountability, Community, and Transparency Grant (PACT)
structured_extraction.program_description: The PACT grant helps law enforcement agencies across Maryland develop effective accountability procedures, improve training, enhance community relations, and promote transparency. The program was created to help law enforcement departments comply with the Maryland Police Accountability Act of 2021 by funding personnel, equipment, contractual services, operating expenses, travel, and other related costs. It supports three main categories: (1) Core Priorities—Accountability, Training, and Transparency; (2) High Impact Support Initiatives—Officer Wellness and Community Engagement; (3) Innovation and Research Initiatives—Emerging Needs and Best Practices. Grantees must track and measure outputs and outcomes on a quarterly basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: Supports Maryland law enforcement agencies in developing, implementing, and sustaining evidence-informed strategies to address recruitment and retention challenges. Emphasis on hard-to-fill positions and underserved communities. Funding can be used for hiring bonuses, retention incentives, tuition reimbursement, health incentives, personnel costs, equipment, travel, contractual services, and other related costs.

structured_extraction.program_name: Program for Preventing Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) Infection for Rape Victims
structured_extraction.program_description: This program reimburses physicians, healthcare providers, hospitals, and pharmacies for providing a full course of non-occupational post-exposure prophylaxis (nPEP) treatment and follow-up care to prevent HIV infection in rape and sexual assault victims. The medication must begin within 72 hours of the assault, and follow-up care is covered up to 180 days after the assault. The program also covers sexual assault forensic medical examinations (SAFE), medical evaluation, forensic evidence collection, laboratory testing, STI testing, toxicology screening, medications, and vaccines.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement from the Criminal Injuries Compensation Fund for the full cost of nPEP treatment, medication, HIV exposure assessment, laboratory services (HIV testing, pregnancy tests, blood panels), SAFE exams, forensic evidence collection, STI testing, toxicology screening, medications, vaccines, and related follow-up care for sexual assault victims. Total annual reimbursements may not exceed $750,000. Claims must be submitted within 90 days from the date of service using the nPEP Reimbursement Form or SARU SAFE Reimbursement Form.

structured_extraction.program_description: Project Safe Neighborhoods grants support anti-gang prevention and violent crime enforcement strategies in Maryland. The program funds dedicated partnerships that form a PSN task force to create safer neighborhoods by reducing violent crime—particularly felonious firearm offenses and gang-related violence—through a research-driven, strategic, and collaborative approach. It includes enforcement, prosecution, deterrence, community engagement, and prevention/intervention strategies, bringing together federal, state, local, and community partners to identify and address specific crime problems at the local level. Grants develop, implement, and support anti-gang prevention and violent crime enforcement strategies through dedicated funding, emphasizing four core elements: Community Engagement/Partnerships, Prevention and Intervention, Focused and Strategic Enforcement, and Accountability.

Funds support contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, personnel, travel, and other allowable costs related to developing, implementing, and supporting anti-gang and violent crime reduction strategies through PSN task forces.

structured_extraction.program_description: Established in 2020, this grant program provides funding to nonprofit and faith-based organizations with facilities and members that may be targeted for hate crimes. Grants support physical security enhancements, community engagement and education, and emergency preparedness at those facilities, and help coordinate collaboration between law enforcement, victim services, and communities targeted by hate crimes. The program addresses documented and recent risks of hate crime victimization for organizations serving protected classes including religion, race, color, sexual orientation, gender, disability, national origin, and homelessness.

structured_extraction.program_description: The RSAT program helps state, local, and tribal governments develop and run substance abuse treatment programs inside correctional and detention facilities. It also funds community reintegration services for people after they are released from incarceration. The goal is to break the cycle of drugs and violence by reducing illegal drug use and trafficking. Funds can support three types of programs: residential treatment, jail-based treatment, and aftercare services. Funding is provided to local detention centers, the Maryland Department of Juvenile Services (DJS), and the Maryland Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services (DPSCS). Programs provide substance use treatment services lasting at least 6 months in residential treatment facilities set apart from the general prison/jail population, and include integrated treatment for co-occurring substance use disorder (SUD) and mental health disorders, trauma-informed services, medication-assisted treatment (MAT), and phased programming based on behavioral/recovery milestones.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funds may be used for personnel, contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, travel, and other costs related to residential, jail-based, or aftercare substance abuse treatment programs within correctional and detention facilities. Funds also support medication-assisted treatment (MAT) for opioid use disorders, community-based aftercare services including case management, recovery support, housing, job training, and peer support, and reentry planning and reintegration services. Funds are distributed on a quarterly reimbursement basis. Applications involving partnerships with community-based substance abuse treatment programs receive priority consideration. Consultant rates are capped at $650/day. Fringe benefits may not exceed 30% of salary unless pre-approved.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local detention centers, Maryland Department of Juvenile Services (DJS), and Maryland Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services (DPSCS); pre-trial defendants; individuals detained or incarcerated in jail or prison with substance use disorders or co-occurring SUD and mental health disorders; individuals in recovery post-release
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Developing and implementing residential, jail-based, and aftercare substance abuse treatment programs within correctional facilities; community reintegration and reentry services for released offenders; medication-assisted treatment (MAT) for opioid use disorders; case management, recovery support, housing, job training, and peer support services; personnel/salaries, fringe benefits, operating expenses, travel, contractual services, equipment, and other approved expenses. Unallowable uses include UAS/UAV, vehicles, facility construction/renovation, prizes, entertainment, lobbying, food/beverage, and supplanting state/local funds.

structured_extraction.program_name: STOP (Services * Training * Officers * Prosecutors) Violence Against Women Formula Grant Program (STOP VAWA)
structured_extraction.program_description: The STOP VAWA Program is a federal grant program providing formula grant funding to develop and strengthen effective responses to domestic violence, dating violence, sexual assault, and stalking. It supports victim-centered law enforcement, prosecution, court strategies, and nonprofit victim services to combat violent crimes against women in Maryland. Administered by the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy, funds are distributed among law enforcement, prosecutors, courts, and nonprofit victim service providers. The program also supports criminal justice entities in holding offenders accountable and requires set-asides for underserved populations and sexual assault services. At least 10% of the victim services allocation must go to linguistically and culturally specific community-based organizations, and at least 20% of total funds must meaningfully address sexual assault.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Formula grant funds distributed across four categories: 25% to law enforcement, 25% to prosecution, 30% to nonprofit non-governmental victim services, and 5% to courts, with up to 15% at the State's discretion. At least 10% of the victim services allocation must go to linguistically and culturally specific community-based organizations. At least 20% of total funds must meaningfully address sexual assault. The FFY 2024 cycle offered $3,018,680 in continuation funding with an award period of October 1, 2024 – September 30, 2025. Eligible expenses include contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, personnel, travel, and other related costs. The program also supports specialized training, technical assistance, coordinated community response teams, bilingual and culturally competent staffing, trauma-informed response training, hospital-based victim advocacy, court-based victim representation, and technology infrastructure for victim safety.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides reimbursement to physicians, hospitals, pharmacies, and laboratories for the cost of forensic medical examinations, evidence collection, and emergency treatment of victims of alleged rape, sexual assault, or child sexual abuse. The program also reimburses on behalf of individuals and their families affected by sexual assault. It covers SAFE exams, medical-only exams, follow-up care, nPEP (non-occupational post-exposure prophylaxis), drug-facilitated sexual assault (DFSA) toxicology testing, and related medical services. It aims to prevent financial re-victimization by handling medical-forensic claims so victims and families can focus on healing, under Code of Maryland Regulations 10.12.02.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement paid directly to physicians, hospitals, pharmacies, and laboratories on behalf of sexual assault victims for forensic medical examinations (SAFE exams), medical-only exams, evidence collection, and emergency treatment. Covers follow-up care within 90 days, pregnancy and STI screening, diagnostic tests, toxicology screening (including drug-facilitated sexual assault testing), and related medications including emergency contraception, antibiotics, vaccines, and HIV prophylaxis (nPEP). Physician reimbursement is capped at $80 for examination and evidence collection, or up to $80/hour for up to 5 hours for child sexual abuse cases. Hospital, laboratory, and pharmacy reimbursements are based on rates set by the Health Services Cost Review Commission. DFSA testing reimbursement covers blood and urine sample analysis by qualified forensic toxicology laboratories. Claims must be submitted within 90 days of the date of service.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Claims must be submitted within 90 days from the date of service

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reimbursement for forensic medical exams (SAFE), medical-only exams, evidence collection, emergency and follow-up treatment, pregnancy and STI screening, diagnostic and toxicology testing (including DFSA testing), nPEP follow-up care, and related medications provided to sexual assault victims
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — available throughout Maryland. Services must be provided within the state of Maryland by providers licensed in Maryland. Victims assaulted in another state may still receive reimbursement for care provided in Maryland.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the SARU SAFE Reimbursement Form (SSRF) along with a payment sheet (UB-04, CMS-1450, or OMB-0938-1197 1500 form) and itemized bill. For DFSA testing, submit an invoice and completed SSRF with required documentation including signed informed consent forms. For CAC services, use Form 4456. Submit all documentation to the SARU within 90 days of the date of service. Individuals and families may also submit claims through the Sexual Assault Reimbursement Unit's claims processing process. Contact saru.claims@maryland.gov for billing questions or call 410-697-9338.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Sexual Assault Services Program provides intervention, advocacy, accompaniment (such as accompanying victims to court, medical facilities, and police departments), support services, and related assistance for adult, youth, and child victims of sexual assault, family and household members of victims, and others collaterally affected by sexual assault. Created by the Violence Against Women and Department of Justice Reauthorization Act of 2005 (42 U.S.C. §14043g), it is the first federal funding stream solely dedicated to the provision of direct intervention and related assistance for victims of sexual assault. Federal grant funding is awarded to rape crisis centers and qualifying organizations to cover costs related to providing direct services to sexual assault victims. The program supports the establishment, maintenance, and expansion of rape crisis centers throughout Maryland.

Funds may cover personnel, contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, travel, training, and other costs related to providing direct services to sexual assault victims, including intervention, advocacy, and accompaniment services.

The Office anticipates having up to $50,000 available and making one award per cycle, with intent of two additional years of level funding for SFY 2028 and SFY 2029 contingent on good standing and positive outcomes.

structured_extraction.program_name: Title II Juvenile Justice Delinquency Prevention Formula Grant (JJAC)
structured_extraction.program_description: This federal formula grant program funds reform initiatives in Maryland's juvenile justice system. Authorized under Sections 221–223 of the Juvenile Justice and Delinquency Prevention Act of 1974 (as amended), it supports strategies aligned with a Developmental Approach to Juvenile Justice Reform, including accountability without criminalization, alternatives to justice system involvement, individualized responses based on needs and risk assessments, limiting confinement to public safety needs, fairness, addressing disparate treatment, and family engagement. The program aims to improve outcomes for children and youth by strengthening programs in aftercare and reentry, alternatives to detention, diversion, and probation. It also increases and strengthens community-based programs and services, expands community-based alternatives to confinement, and brings the state into compliance with federal limitations on holding youth in adult jails or lock-ups. Funded through U.S. Department of Justice, Office of Justice Programs, Office of Juvenile Justice and Delinquency Prevention Title II Formula Grant Program (ALN# 16.540).

structured_extraction.program_description: The Victims of Crime Act (VOCA) program provides competitive grants to improve the treatment of crime victims by funding services that help them recover after violent crimes and navigate the criminal justice process. The primary purpose is to support the most critical crime victims' needs statewide by funding victim service providers with a proven track record of service, including assuring that victims receive information about and assistance in filing for Crime Victim Compensation. Funded services include crisis intervention, counseling, emergency transportation to court, temporary housing, criminal justice support and advocacy, hotline support, safety planning, emergency shelter, mental health counseling, legal assistance, and forensic medical examinations. The program is funded by the federal Crime Victims Fund, which is financed by fines, forfeited bail bonds, penalty fees, and special assessments from federal offenders — not taxpayers. The SFY 2027 funding period covers July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027, with approximately $60 million in total anticipated funding and approximately 150 awards anticipated.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's MBE Certification Program is a socioeconomic procurement program that certifies small, minority- and women-owned businesses so they can compete for Maryland State procurement and contracting opportunities as prime contractors or subcontractors on State contracts that have MBE participation goals. The program aims to provide greater economic opportunities to these businesses by increasing their participation in state government contracts and ensuring that socially and economically disadvantaged small business owners are included in state procurement and contracting. It sets a statewide aspirational goal of 29% MBE participation across 70 participating state agencies and departments—meaning state agencies must make every effort to award at least 29% of the total dollar value of their procurement contracts to certified MBE firms. Certified firms are listed in an official online MBE directory (DoSEM's online directory) used by government procurement officials statewide—in counties, cities, and municipalities—as well as private sector companies seeking diverse suppliers. Certification allows firms to fulfill minority participation goals on state-funded contracts and contracts funded by Maryland counties and cities, which non-certified businesses cannot do. Applicants are evaluated for both MBE and DBE (Disadvantaged Business Enterprise) certification simultaneously using a single application. Certified firms are reassessed annually and may seek an Expansion of Services when they add new products or services. Support includes MBE Liaisons at each participating agency who advocate for MBEs on active contracts, a free T.I.P.S. Small Business Webinar Series (two classes per month) to help small, minority, women, and veteran-owned firms compete in state contracting, and monthly application assistance workshops on the first Tuesday of every month to help prospective applicants prepare their certification application. DoSEM certification is also accepted by most local county governments. The program also incorporates nondiscrimination requirements from 49 CFR Part 26 and operates as the uniform certification office for the entire State of Maryland, with certification effective since 1978. Optional components include a Mentor-Protégé Program and DBE Business Development Program.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Small, Minority and Women Business Affairs
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free certification as a Minority Business Enterprise (MBE), which qualifies the certified firm to count toward minority business participation goals on state-funded contracts and contracts funded by Maryland counties and cities. Certified firms are listed in the state's official MBE directory (DoSEM's online directory) used by government agencies, local governments, and private companies. There is no cost to apply or maintain certification; the process takes several months once a full application package is received. The program sets a 29% aspirational MBE participation goal across 70 state agencies. MBE Liaisons at each participating agency advocate for MBEs on active contracts. A free T.I.P.S. Small Business Webinar Series (two classes per month) helps small, minority, women, and veteran-owned firms compete in state contracting. OMBE offers a free Application Assistance Workshop on the first Tuesday of every month to help applicants prepare. An MBE Fraud Hotline is available at 410-697-9611 to report violations. Certified firms are reassessed annually and may seek an Expansion of Services when they add new products or services. MBE participation credit on contracts is calculated based on firm role: suppliers/wholesalers/regular dealers (60% credit), manufacturers and furnish-and-install/service providers (100% credit), and brokers (reasonable fee/commission only). MBE primes may self-perform up to 50% of the overall goal with their own forces, or up to 100% of one subgoal. Additional technical assistance includes referral services to federal, state, municipal and private agencies providing bid/proposal preparation, bonding assistance, and project financing. Business development support includes Operation Guaranteed Help consulting services, Mega Success Conferences, outreach meetings, and training courses in business plan writing, small business management, construction estimating and bidding, computer applications, and other technical areas. Contract financing and surety bonding support available through Maryland Small Business Development Financing Authority (MSBDFA).

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Certification enables firms to be listed in the state MBE directory, fulfill minority business participation requirements on state and local government contracts, and access state-funded contract opportunities as a certified MBE subcontractor or prime contractor. Certified businesses may also participate in state procurement opportunities listed on eMaryland Marketplace Advantage (eMMA). For trucking firms, certification enables participation in hauling and material distribution on MDOT contracts. Certified firms may also access contract financing and surety bonding support for working capital on MDOT contract work.

Out-of-state applicants with home-state certification are eligible; out-of-state firms must have new work areas included in home state certification before requesting expansion in Maryland. The MBE directory is used by government procurement officials in counties, cities, municipalities, and the state, as well as private sector companies. DoSEM certification is also accepted by most local county governments.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Small Business Reserve (SBR) Program is a state procurement initiative that gives Certified Small Businesses (CSBs) the exclusive opportunity to compete as prime contractors on designated Maryland state government contracts. Under a 2021 executive order, all executive branch procurement units under the governor's authority must set aside contracts between $50,000 and $500,000 for small business prime contractors. Over 20% of all open state-funded solicitations on Maryland's eProcurement platform (eMaryland Marketplace Advantage, or eMMA) are designated as SBR, giving small businesses access to nearly $500 million in state-funded contracting opportunities where only CSBs can win those contracts. Additionally, 74 participating state agencies, including all Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT) modal administrations, are required to spend at least 15% of their total procurement dollars with qualified small businesses. When a solicitation is designated as an SBR procurement, only certified small businesses can bid or submit proposals, allowing small businesses to compete among peers of similar size. CSBs also benefit from the Small Business Preference (SBP) Program, which provides a price preference of up to 5% of total contract value (up to 7% for veteran-owned small businesses and up to 8% for disabled-veteran-owned small businesses). The state also encourages procurement officers to consider small businesses for higher-dollar contracts above the $500,000 ceiling.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Certified Small Businesses (CSBs) gain exclusive access to state procurement contracts designated as SBR (over 20% of all open state-funded solicitations, representing nearly $500 million in contracting opportunities). State procurement contracts valued between $50,000 and $500,000 are reserved for small businesses as prime contractors, and participating state agencies set aside at least 15% of their total procurement spending for CSBs. CSBs only compete against other small businesses rather than larger companies, and receive direct payments from the state as a prime contractor on reserved solicitations. Vendors already registered in eMaryland Marketplace Advantage may qualify for same-day certification. There is no cost to become a CSB, and certification is valid for three years. CSBs also benefit from the Small Business Preference (SBP) Program, which provides a price preference of up to 5% of total contract value (up to 7% for veteran-owned small businesses and up to 8% for disabled-veteran-owned small businesses). The state encourages procurement officers to consider small businesses for higher-dollar contracts above the $500,000 ceiling as well.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's VSBE Program, enacted in 2010, certifies veteran-owned small businesses so they can compete for set-aside contracting opportunities on state-funded procurements. Designated state agencies are directed to spend at least 3% of their procurement contract dollars with certified VSBE firms, with a 1% statewide goal minimum. Certified firms can participate as prime contractors or subcontractors to help meet agency VSBE goals. The program offers certification that helps veteran-owned small businesses access greater economic opportunities through state government contracting, including set-asides and procurement goals. There is no cost to apply, and certification must be renewed every three years (effective September 1, 2025). Certified vendors receive email notices of procurement opportunities valued over $15,000 through the eMaryland Marketplace Advantage (eMMA) platform. As of FY2020, $31M was paid to VSBEs across 52 participating agencies and departments.

Goals are evaluated on a contract-by-contract basis and may be applied to IFBs and RFPs, as well as individual task orders competitively procured under master contracts. Certification is free and valid for three years (renewable, effective September 1, 2025). Certified vendors receive email notices of procurement opportunities valued over $15,000 through the eMaryland Marketplace Advantage (eMMA) platform. Certified businesses may participate as prime contractors or subcontractors on state-funded procurements across 52–70 participating state agencies and departments.

structured_extraction.program_name: CDBG/HOME Nonprofit Subrecipient Grants (Community Development Block Grant & HOME Investment Partnerships Program)
structured_extraction.program_description: Harford County administers federal Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) and HOME Investment Partnerships Program entitlement funds to support a wide range of community development activities throughout Harford County. The County subgrants money to partner organizations serving low- to moderate-income residents. Eligible projects include public facility improvements (community centers, parks, infrastructure), housing rehabilitation, homeowner assistance, nonprofit services, tenant-based rental assistance, affordable housing construction, first-time homebuyer support, critical home repairs, economic development, and slum and blight reduction. Funds are distributed annually to eligible nonprofit and, in some cases, for-profit or government organizations. Activities must meet one of the CDBG national objectives and align with the HUD-approved Consolidated Plan and Annual Action Plan. Community members are also invited to provide input on how funds should be prioritized. Harford County reserves the right to approve, reject, or reduce funding requests.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual subgrants from federal CDBG and HOME entitlement funds awarded by Harford County to eligible partner organizations. Funds support capital projects and services benefiting low- to moderate-income persons, including community centers, housing rehabilitation, homeowner assistance, public services, infrastructure improvements, public facilities, affordable housing construction, tenant-based rental assistance, first-time homebuyer support, critical home repairs, economic development, slum and blight reduction, and urgent community needs. Funding amounts vary by project; the typical application period runs during January/February each year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private nonprofit organizations with 501(c)(3) status, government partners, for-profit entities, and community groups seeking to serve low- to moderate-income residents of Harford County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Public facility improvements, community centers, housing rehabilitation, homeowner assistance, nonprofit services, tenant-based rental assistance, affordable/low-to-moderate income housing construction, first-time homebuyer support, critical home repairs, infrastructure improvements, public facilities including parks, economic development, slum and blight reduction, and urgent community needs

requirements_list: Must serve low- to moderate-income citizens of Harford County

All proposed projects must meet applicable federal regulations
Activities must meet one of the CDBG national objectives: benefit low-to-moderate income persons, eliminate slum and blight, or address urgent need
Projects and activities must align with the HUD-approved Consolidated Plan and Annual Action Plan
Subject to availability of funding and Harford County budget review
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Community members are invited to complete an online survey to provide input on how CDBG/HOME funds should be spent. Eligible organizations may submit a formal application through the Harford County Grants Portal (https://gn.ecivis.com/GO/gn_redir/T/4n3o1tuzxrh8) during the typical January/February application period each year.
