structured_extraction.program_description: Harford Transit LINK provides two shared-ride transportation services for residents who cannot use fixed-route buses on their own. Demand Response serves anyone over age 60 or anyone under 60 with a qualifying disability who lives outside the ADA Paratransit service area, with trips within Harford County from 9:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. ADA Paratransit serves people with mobility disabilities who are functionally unable to use fixed-route buses, with trips to and from locations within 3/4 mile of a bus route during normal operating hours (4:30 a.m. to 8:30 p.m.).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Riders pay $2.00 each way (cash or Token Transit app). ADA Paratransit eligibility also grants reduced fares on fixed-route service. An approved aide may ride free with an ADA Paratransit-eligible rider when notified in advance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Harford County residents aged 60 or older, or individuals with a qualifying mobility disability who are unable to independently use fixed-route bus service.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Shared-ride transportation within Harford County (Demand Response) or to/from locations within 3/4 mile of a fixed bus route (ADA Paratransit).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Demand Response trips must be within Harford County. ADA Paratransit trips must originate and end within 3/4 mile of a Harford Transit LINK fixed route.
requirements_list: Must be age 60 or older (Demand Response), OR have a qualifying disability (both services)
For ADA Paratransit: must complete a four-part application (Parts I–III filled by rider or legal guardian; Part IV filled and signed by a certified medical professional currently treating the rider)
For ADA Paratransit: both pick-up and drop-off must be within 3/4 mile of a fixed route
ADA Paratransit eligibility card is issued and typically valid for five years before reapplication is required
Demand Response riders over 60 may register by phone; riders under 60 with a qualifying disability must complete Parts I and II of the application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For Demand Response (over 60): call Dispatch at 410-612-1620 (option 1) between 8:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m., Monday–Friday, to register by phone. For ADA Paratransit (disability): download and complete the application (Parts I–IV), have a certified medical professional complete Part IV, then submit the full application. Applications are also available online. Once approved, you receive an eligibility card. Schedule trips by calling Dispatch; Demand Response trips should be scheduled one week in advance (not more than 90 days out).

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary program that helps Harford County households participating in the Housing Choice Voucher (HCV) program become economically independent. Participants work with an FSS specialist to set career and financial goals, access support services, and build savings through an interest-bearing escrow account over up to five years.

The escrow account grows as the household's earned income increases (reducing their rental subsidy share). The full escrow balance plus interest is paid out upon successful contract completion. Escrow funds are non-taxable and do not affect HCV subsidy status.

Must have employment goals and wish to achieve financial independence
Must complete and sign an FSS contract and maintain a current signed training plan
Must complete all goals and activities within five years
Must be free of welfare benefits (Maryland Temporary Cash Assistance) and employed at time of graduation to access escrow account
Must maintain regular contact with FSS specialist and follow through on contract commitments

structured_extraction.program_description: Harford County's Agricultural Land Preservation Program (HALPP) is a competitive easement purchase program that permanently preserves productive agricultural land and woodland in Harford County to support continued production of food and fiber and agriculture's role in the local economy. Landowners voluntarily sell their development rights (via a permanent conservation easement) to the county or state in exchange for cash payment, with the goal of keeping agricultural land in farming and preventing future commercial or residential subdivision. The farm is subject to a deed of easement that extinguishes all pre-existing development potential and prohibits future non-agricultural development, while the owner retains title; the restriction binds the original owner and all future owners. Properties are ranked using an Easement Priority Ranking System, and the Agricultural Preservation Advisory Board reviews applications and makes recommendations to the Department of Planning and Zoning. Selected applicants enter into a Deed of Easement Purchase Agreement. The program also includes a voluntary Agricultural Preservation District component: landowners commit to limiting subdivision of their agricultural parcel for a minimum of five years in exchange for a property tax credit of $50 per acre, up to 50% of the county real property tax bill (whichever is less). After the initial five-year term, the agreement and tax credit continue until the owner requests termination, at which point all accrued tax credits must be repaid to the county. A minimum of 50 acres is required for district enrollment. The program is administered by Harford County in coordination with the state.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The county purchases permanent conservation easements on qualifying farmland on a competitive basis, providing landowners a cash payment for permanently extinguishing all development rights (purchase of development rights) on their agricultural property through a recorded deed of easement. The landowner retains full ownership of the land but no further commercial or residential subdivision is permitted, and the restriction binds all future owners. Properties are ranked using an Easement Priority Ranking System. Additionally, through the Agricultural Preservation District component, landowners can receive a tax credit of $50 per acre, up to 50% of the county real property tax bill (whichever is less), in exchange for a minimum five-year commitment not to subdivide the land. After the initial term, the agreement and tax credit continue until the owner requests termination, at which point all accrued tax credits must be refunded to the county. A minimum parcel size of 50 acres is required for district enrollment. Property owners can request a district agreement at any time.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Property owners can request a district agreement at any time; easement purchases are competitive and ongoing.

Participants who successfully complete the program may receive a probation before judgment or a not guilty finding.

Successful graduates receive a probation before judgment; those meeting additional criteria may receive a not guilty finding.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Drug education classes, individual and group counseling, family counseling, vocational and educational services, and probation support.

structured_extraction.program_name: Harford County Economic Development Opportunity Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: A loan program offered by Harford County Economic Development that provides funding to small businesses in Harford County to support growth through capital investment, job creation, and job retention. Loans up to $200,000 are available with flexible terms depending on the project and business, and can be used for building and land purchases, renovations, technology upgrades, or equipment purchases. Financing can be combined with other lenders through gap financing. Collateral is required, with exceptions possible for loans under $10,000. Loans over $75,000 require Harford County Council approval, and settlement occurs within 90 days of approval.

structured_extraction.program_name: Harford County Enterprise Zone Tax Credit Program
structured_extraction.program_description: State-designated Enterprise Zones in Harford County offer real property tax credits and state income/job creation tax credits to businesses locating, retaining, or expanding in one of the county's two enterprise zones — one in the Aberdeen/Havre de Grace area and one in the Edgewood/Joppa area. The program aims to encourage new job creation, retain and expand existing businesses, and promote development of vacant or underutilized land and buildings in older industrial areas. Two types of tax credits are available: local real property tax credits of up to 10 years on capital investments (80% credit on increases in assessed value for the first five years, decreasing by 10% annually for the remaining five years), and state income/job tax credits including a one-time $1,000 credit per new job created and up to $6,000 total per eligible economically-disadvantaged employee distributed over three years.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two types of tax credits are available: (1) Local Real Property Tax Credits — up to 10 years on capital investments, with an 80% credit on increases in assessed value for the first five years, decreasing by 10% annually for the remaining five years. (2) State Income/Job Tax Credits — a one-time $1,000 tax credit per new job created, filed with annual taxes using Form 500CR; an additional credit of up to $6,000 total per eligible economically-disadvantaged employee distributed over three years. Credits apply to businesses in the Aberdeen/Havre de Grace and Edgewood/Joppa enterprise zones.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses locating, retaining, or expanding within Harford County's designated enterprise zones (Aberdeen/Havre de Grace and Edgewood/Joppa) that meet minimum job creation or capital investment requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital investment in construction or rehabilitation of real property within the Enterprise Zone; job creation including hiring economically-disadvantaged employees; business retention and expansion within enterprise zones.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available within the Aberdeen/Havre de Grace and Edgewood/Joppa enterprise zones in Harford County, Maryland. The Aberdeen/Havre de Grace zone covers properties along U.S. Route 40 and in Aberdeen and Havre de Grace municipalities, extending east to portions of Aberdeen Proving Ground, south to Belcamp and Perryman, and west to CONVERGE (formerly the HEAT Center).

Minimum job creation of two new jobs for businesses with 10 or fewer employees, or five new jobs for businesses with 11 or more employees
New jobs must be at least 35 hours per week; if hourly, pay must be at least 150% of minimum wage
At least half of work time must be within the Enterprise Zone
Enterprise Zone Administrator must be contacted prior to construction to align real property tax credit timing with July 1st
Building must be occupied to receive real property tax credit
Submit itemized cost breakdown for construction/renovation and site plan with application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Enterprise Zone Administrator Karen Holt before starting construction. Visit https://www.harfordcountymd.gov/1280/Enterprise-Zones for maps, incentive details, and requirements, or call 410-638-3059.

structured_extraction.program_name: Harford County Grant-in-Aid Program (Outside Agency Request Fund)
structured_extraction.program_description: Harford County's Department of Housing & Community Services allocates more than $1 million each year to support local nonprofits and community organizations through the Grant-in-Aid Program and the Outside Agency Request Fund (ORF). These competitive grant programs provide funding to non-profit organizations to enhance their ability to deliver human services, housing, homeless prevention, and affordable housing services, addressing resource needs for low- to moderate-income residents of Harford County. The program supports a wide range of supportive services and community improvement goals. New applicants can receive up to $5,000 in starter funds to help growing service providers get financial and technical support. Organizations must meet eligibility criteria, be incorporated as a 501(c)(3) non-profit, and submit applications by a predetermined deadline using county-provided forms. All grantees enter into a formal agreement with Harford County and must comply with financial and programmatic procedures. A list of past ORF and Grant-in-Aid awardees is available on the county website.

Grant funds are awarded to eligible non-profit organizations under a formal agreement with Harford County; grantees must comply with financial and programmatic procedures and submit required forms. New applicants are eligible for up to $5,000 in starter funds providing financial and technical support. Competitive grant funds are available to eligible organizations that meet certain criteria and apply by a predetermined deadline using county-provided application forms. Lists of past Grant-in-Aid and Outside Agency Request Fund awardees are available via the county document portal.

structured_extraction.program_name: Harford County Historic Landmark Designation and Technical Assistance
structured_extraction.program_description: Harford County formally recognizes properties that are significant in American or Harford County history, architecture, archaeology, engineering, or culture through its Historic Landmark Designation program. Designated landmarks receive eligibility for county, state, and federal historic preservation tax credits, grants, and free technical assistance from the county historic preservation planner and members of the Historic Preservation Commission (HPC). Technical assistance covers preservation, rehabilitation, and exterior alteration projects for designated historic landmark properties, and is provided in compliance with the Secretary of the Interior's Standards. Properties must be surveyed in the Maryland Inventory of Historic Properties, be at least 50 years old, and have sufficient integrity of location, design, materials, and workmanship, as well as meet at least one criterion of historical/cultural or architectural/design significance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Designated landmarks become eligible for county, state, and federal historic preservation tax credits and grant funding opportunities. Owners also receive free technical assistance from the county historic preservation planner and Historic Preservation Commission members, covering preservation, rehabilitation, and exterior alteration projects in compliance with the Secretary of the Interior's Standards.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a completed Historic Landmark Nomination Form to the Historic Preservation Commission (HPC). The HPC reviews the nomination at a public meeting and votes to recommend it to the Harford County Council. The Department of Planning and Zoning then forwards the nomination to the county council, which holds a public hearing and votes to place the property on the Harford County Historic Landmarks list. Once designated, owners may contact Joel Gallihue at 410-638-3136 or jagallihue@harfordcountymd.gov for free technical assistance.

structured_extraction.program_name: Harford County Historic Preservation Tax Credits
structured_extraction.program_description: Harford County offers property tax credits to owners of structures designated as Harford County Historic Landmarks who rehabilitate or restore their historic properties. Owners can reduce their county real property tax bill based on: (1) the increase in their property assessment due to the rehabilitation or restoration, and (2) a credit equal to 10% of qualified restoration and rehabilitation expenses (QREs), up to $7,500 (based on QREs of $75,000; QREs may exceed $75,000 but the 10% credit is capped at $7,500). There is no limit on the number of tax credits granted, but a previous tax credit must be exhausted before another can be granted. Applicants submit a two-part application covering the proposed work and the completed work to receive the county tax credit.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Owners may reduce their county real property tax by: (1) a credit based on the amount their assessment increased due to rehabilitation or restoration, and (2) a credit equal to 10% of qualified restoration and rehabilitation expenses (QREs) up to $7,500 (based on QREs of $75,000; QREs may exceed $75,000 but the 10% credit is capped at $7,500). There is no limit on the number of tax credits granted, but a previous tax credit must be exhausted before another can be granted. The credit is applied following a two-part process: first a Certificate of Appropriateness is obtained for the proposed work, then a Certification of Completed Work is submitted after the rehabilitation is finished.

structured_extraction.program_name: Harford County Solar/Geothermal Energy and Senior Citizens & Veterans Real Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: Harford County provides real property tax credits to qualifying residents and property owners. Available credits include: (1) a solar/geothermal energy credit for taxpayers who install qualifying energy conservation devices (solar or geothermal energy systems); (2) a senior citizens and veterans credit for qualifying seniors, veterans, and surviving spouses; (3) historic property credits; (4) homeowner credits; and (5) landfill credits. Eligible homeowners may receive a 20% credit on county property taxes for up to 20 years. The solar/geothermal credit is available to individuals, for-profit entities, and non-profits that install qualifying devices. The senior citizens and veterans credit is available to individuals over 65 who have owned and lived in their dwelling for at least 35 years, retirees or surviving spouses (not remarried) of U.S. Uniformed Services retirees, and veterans or surviving spouses (not remarried) of U.S. Uniformed Services veterans with a permanent service-connected disability with a combined evaluation of 50% or higher that substantially limits one or more major life activities. Eligible properties must have an assessed value of $600,000 or less for the senior/veterans credit.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A 20% real property tax credit on county property taxes for up to 20 years. For solar/geothermal: applies to properties with qualifying energy conservation devices (solar or geothermal systems). For seniors/veterans: applies to qualifying homeowners over 65 who have owned and lived in the dwelling for at least 35 years or are U.S. Uniformed Services retirees or surviving spouses, and to veterans or surviving spouses with a permanent service-connected disability with a combined service-connected evaluation of 50% or higher that substantially limits one or more major life activities; eligible properties must have an assessed value of $600,000 or less. Additional credits are available for historic properties, homeowners, and landfills.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Opioid Restitution Fund (ORF) distributes money awarded to Maryland through prescription opioid-related lawsuits against pharmaceutical companies and distributors. The framework was collaboratively developed at the Opioid Restitution Fund Stakeholder Summit (4.18.24) in partnership with The Leadership Institute for Compassionate Changemaking, focusing on Prevention and Education and Centralized Treatment to contribute to a healthy, thriving, and supportive community in Harford County.

Centralized Treatment initiatives include safe spaces for available resources, information for services, increased access to transportation, inclusive services for the county's diversity, and comprehensive post-treatment care for sustained recovery, including 24-hour coordinated care.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Harford County Tourism Funding Program supports nonprofits, municipalities, and partnerships in creating, expanding, or enhancing tourism-related events and programs that drive economic growth in Harford County. It operates through two funding tracks: the Partnership Fund, which supports collaborative festivals, events, exhibits, and programming that bring together two or more organizations to attract visitors from outside Harford County and drive overnight hotel stays; and the Community Impact Fund, which supports individual nonprofits or municipalities in creating or enhancing tourism-related events and programs that attract both overnight visitors and day-trippers. Eligible activities include cultural attractions, outdoor recreation, arts, heritage, and sports tourism. The total FY26 budget was $770,000 across both funds, drawn from Harford County's 6% hotel tax revenue. The Partnership Fund receives top funding priority; the Community Impact Fund receives remaining funds after the Partnership Fund is fully allocated.
structured_extraction.agency: Harford County Department of Economic Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants funded by Harford County's 6% hotel tax revenue. The program has two tracks: (1) Partnership Fund — receives top funding priority; the lead applicant receives the full grant award and is responsible for distributing funds to partner organizations; marketing costs receive highest priority within the budget. (2) Community Impact Fund — receives remaining funds after the Partnership Fund is fully allocated; may cover direct tourism marketing costs, non-marketing event expenses, and limited operational costs including staff salaries (capped at 75% in year 1, 50% in year 2, 25% in year 3, 0% in subsequent years). Across both funds, funds may not be used for daily operating costs, capital improvements, property acquisition, or equipment for daily office functions. Total FY26 budget was $770,000 across both funds.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations (501(c)(3) or 501(c)(6)) registered in Harford County, MD, Harford County municipalities, and partnerships between two or more such organizations. The Partnership Fund requires involvement of two or more organizations; the Community Impact Fund is open to individual nonprofits and municipalities. Priority is given to applicants driving out-of-county visitors and overnight hotel stays. For-profit organizations may serve as partners in the Partnership Fund but not as lead grant recipients.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tourism-related festivals, events, exhibits, and programming. Partnership Fund prioritizes direct tourism-related marketing costs. Community Impact Fund may also cover non-marketing event expenses and limited staff salaries (with declining coverage over consecutive years). Neither fund may be used for daily operating costs, capital improvements, property acquisition, or equipment for daily office functions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Only organizations registered in Harford County, Maryland are eligible to apply.
requirements_list: Must be a 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(6) organization or a Harford County municipality
Must be registered in Harford County, Maryland
Must be in good standing with the Maryland State Department of Assessment and Taxation at time of application
Must be in good standing with the Maryland Office of the Secretary of State, Charitable Organization Division
Must submit most recently filed Form 990
Must submit Balance Sheets and Income Statements for fiscal years 2023 and 2024
Must submit list of board members, partners, and key staff for all organizations
Partnership Fund: Must involve a partnership between two or more organizations
Partnership Fund: Must demonstrate how the event/program drives overnight hotel stays in Harford County
Partnership Fund: Must provide letters of commitment from all partnering organizations
The organization's mission must be tourism-related, meaning its activities primarily attract visitors from outside Harford County for overnight stays
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications open February 23, 2026. Apply through the online portal linked on the program page. For the Partnership Fund, the lead applicant organization submits the application. A review committee comprised of Economic Development Advisory Board members evaluates applications for both funds and submits funding recommendations to the County Executive, who makes final award decisions. Quarterly budget and activity reporting with receipts is required after award.

structured_extraction.program_name: Healthy Neighborhoods, Inc. Home Loans and Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: Healthy Neighborhoods, Inc. (HNI) offers below-market interest rate financing, grants, and professional advice to current and prospective homeowners in select Baltimore City neighborhoods. The program provides multiple loan products: (1) Purchase/Rehab Mortgages up to $375,000 with a fixed interest rate 1% below market rate, no private mortgage insurance (PMI), and design advice from an architectural firm — borrowers contribute 3% of the purchase price from their own funds and may borrow up to 110% of the after-rehabilitation appraised value; (2) Refinance/Rehab Mortgages up to $375,000 for existing homeowners to refinance their current mortgage and borrow up to 110% of the after-rehabilitation appraised value to update and renovate their home (no PMI required, design assistance included); and (3) Home Improvement Loans between $5,000 and $20,000 at 1% below the current market interest rate with a 10-year repayment term, for renovations such as kitchen upgrades, bathroom updates, window replacements, exterior improvements like porches, energy-efficient appliances, or mechanical system improvements. Funds must be used for improvements made after the loan closes — not for prior work or debt repayment. Eligible borrowers with household income below program limits (e.g., $102,672 for a household of 1, up to $193,572 for a household of 8) may qualify for a matching grant of up to $10,000 when paired with a loan, awarded on a first-come, first-served basis. Grants are also available to community organizations for resident engagement, block projects, and neighborhood marketing. HNI develops market-driven strategies to benefit Baltimore's middle neighborhoods — areas with significant assets but stagnant or undervalued real estate — and invests in properties, provides loans to homebuyers and homeowners, markets neighborhood assets, and strengthens resident capacity. Eligible neighborhoods include the Greenmount Corridor cluster (Abell, Better Waverly, Charles Village, Ednor Gardens-Lakeside, Harwood, Remington, and Waverly) as well as other HNI target neighborhoods in Baltimore City. Since inception, more than 380 loans totaling $57 million have been made across 41 Baltimore neighborhoods. The program is supported by a $35 million private loan fund. The Goldseker Foundation has provided core operating support grants to HNI, including a $70,000 grant awarded in September 2020 and a $75,000 grant awarded in September 2019 for general operating costs and strategic planning. Loans are underwritten and approved by M&T Bank.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Purchase/Rehab Mortgages up to $375,000: fixed rate 1% below market (minimum 3%), no PMI, design advice from an architectural firm; borrowers contribute 3% of the purchase price from personal funds and may borrow up to 110% of the after-rehabilitation appraised value; 12+ month construction term, up to 30-year permanent term; 'two close' structure (short-term construction loan refinanced into long-term permanent loan upon completion). Refinance/Rehab Mortgages up to $375,000 for existing homeowners: allows borrowing up to 110% of the after-rehabilitation appraised value to renovate; no PMI required; architectural design assistance included; interest-only payments during construction, then principal + interest + escrow after completion; 'two close' structure. Home Improvement Loans of $5,000–$20,000 at 1% below market rate with a 10-year repayment term for renovations (kitchens, bathrooms, windows, exterior improvements, energy-efficient appliances, mechanical systems); recorded as second mortgage; funds must be used for improvements made after loan closing and cannot repay existing debt; minimum credit score 700 (some exceptions); no down payment required; no PMI required; total long-term debt payments ≤43% of borrower income; cannot own rental properties; cannot have previously borrowed from Healthy Neighborhoods Loan Pools; maximum aggregate loan amounts ≤105% of after-renovation value. Matching grants of up to $10,000 available for borrowers with household income below program limits by household size (e.g., $102,672 for household of 1, up to $193,572 for household of 8); must be paired with a loan; no stand-alone grants; first-come, first-served. Grants also provided to community organizations for resident engagement, block projects, and neighborhood marketing. The Goldseker Foundation awarded a $70,000 core operating support grant to HNI in September 2020 and a $75,000 grant in September 2019. The program is supported by a $35 million private loan fund; since inception, more than 380 loans totaling $57 million have been made across 41 Baltimore neighborhoods.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review the borrower process guide at https://healthyneighborhoods.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/Borrower-Guide-vF.pdf and complete the online eligibility quiz (approximately 3–5 minutes) at healthyneighborhoods.org, or visit the loan eligibility portal at https://healthyneighborhoods.org/loan-eligibility-portal/ to get started. Those without an offer on a property can request a pre-qualification letter by contacting Healthy Neighborhoods directly. The full process includes: Complete Loan Eligibility Quiz; review loan terms; decide scope of work; find licensed contractor; submit contractor estimate; HNI architect visit; introduction to M&T Bank loan servicer; finalize draw schedule; provide financial info; finalize loan application; M&T orders appraisal; review and sign final loan docs; advance paid to contractor; construction begins. The process takes at least 45 days; a 60-day contract of sale is recommended for complex renovation work. The quiz is not a loan application; actual loan application is subject to additional information and underwriting review by M&T Bank. structured_extraction.program_description: NSP2 is a federal competitive grant program established by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) under the Housing and Economic Recovery Act (HERA) and funded through the Recovery Act to stabilize communities suffering from foreclosures and abandonment. It is a component of the Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) program. In Baltimore, Healthy Neighborhoods, Inc. used a $26 million NSP2 grant—combined with $19 million in private financing—to acquire, rehabilitate, and sell foreclosed and vacant properties in seven targeted neighborhoods. Homes were sold to households earning at or below 120% of the Area Median Income, with total neighborhood investment reaching approximately $45 million. Up to $1.93 billion was available nationally, with a separate up to $50 million for technical assistance and capacity building.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A $26,092,880 NSP2 federal grant was awarded to Healthy Neighborhoods and leveraged with $19 million in private financing for a total $45 million neighborhood investment. Up to $1.93 billion was available nationally through a competitive Notice of Fund Availability (NOFA) process, with a separate up to $50 million for technical assistance and capacity building. Funds support acquisition, rehabilitation, demolition, land banking, homebuyer assistance, housing counseling, and redevelopment of foreclosed and abandoned properties. A minimum 25% of funds must serve households at or below 50% of area median income. All beneficiaries must have incomes at or below 120% of area median income. Properties must be purchased at a minimum 1% discount per property and 5% average discount across all purchases. Grantees must expend 50% of funds within 2 years and 100% within 3 years. Down payment assistance to homebuyers and operating/investment capital are also eligible uses.

structured_extraction.program_audience: States, local governments, nonprofit organizations, consortia of nonprofits, and for-profit partners addressing neighborhood decline from foreclosures and abandonment, as well as low- and moderate-income homebuyers and renters with incomes at or below 120% of area median income (with at least 25% of funds targeting those at or below 50% AMI).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition, rehabilitation, and redevelopment of foreclosed, abandoned, and vacant properties in targeted Baltimore neighborhoods, including resale to income-qualified households. Eligible uses include: establishing financing mechanisms (soft-seconds, loan loss reserves, shared-equity loans); purchase and rehabilitation of foreclosed/abandoned homes; land banking; demolition of blighted structures (limited to 10% of grant unless waiver approved); redevelopment of demolished or vacant properties as housing; general administration and planning (up to 10%); homebuyer counseling and homeownership assistance; energy efficiency and green building improvements; affordable housing for households at or below 50% AMI (minimum 25% of funds); and relocation assistance for displaced tenants.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Seven designated NSP2 target areas in Baltimore City, Maryland, including specific census tracts in Barclay (CT 1204), Belair-Edison (CTs 80101, 260202, 260301, 260302), Ednor Gardens/Better Waverly/Coldstream Homestead Montebello (CTs 903, 905, 906), Patterson Park/Patterson Place/McElderry Park (CTs 601, 602), and Reservoir Hill (CTs 1301, 1302). Nationally, target geography must have an average foreclosure needs index score of 18 or greater, or demonstrate average foreclosures with vacancy risk.

structured_extraction.program_name: Special Purchase Program (SPP) with Interest Rate Reduction (IRR) Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: A purchase-only mortgage loan program for homebuyers interested in purchasing formerly vacant, fully renovated, move-in ready homes from HNI-approved developers in designated 'Healthy Neighborhood' or other authorized areas in Baltimore City. The program offers a below-market fixed interest rate (1% below current market rate), a 30-year term, no private mortgage insurance (PMI), and a minimum 3% down payment requirement. First mortgage financing is available up to $375,000. Healthy Neighborhoods partners with local community development organizations to support homeownership in historic communities including Edmondson Village, Rognel Heights, Edgewood, and Allendale in the Edmondson Avenue corridor. For select properties, the program also offers an Interest Rate Reduction (IRR) Grant that buys down mortgage discount points on behalf of the borrower to reduce the interest rate to 3.5%. The IRR Grant is available for properties located in Vacancy Reduction Priority Geography zones within Baltimore City.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Fixed-rate first mortgage loan up to $375,000 at approximately 1% below the current market interest rate (minimum 3%), with a 30-year term, no private mortgage insurance (PMI), maximum 97% LTV, and a minimum 3% down payment required from the borrower's own funds (gifts allowed, but not grants or settlement loans). The loan is available to owner-occupant homebuyers purchasing formerly vacant, fully renovated, move-in ready homes (1-4 units) from HNI-approved developers in designated Healthy Neighborhoods areas. For select properties located in Vacancy Reduction Priority Geography zones, an Interest Rate Reduction (IRR) Grant is also available, where Healthy Neighborhoods Inc. buys mortgage discount points on behalf of the borrower to reduce the interest rate to 3.5%. The program is offered in partnership with M&T Bank as lender.

structured_extraction.program_description: Howard County's Agricultural Land Preservation Program, overseen by the Agricultural Preservation Board, protects farmland from development by purchasing permanent conservation easements (development rights) from willing landowners. Landowners voluntarily sell the right to develop their land to the county, which pays them the difference between the land's unrestricted fair market value and its agricultural use value. The land remains privately owned, can still be farmed, sold, or passed down, and is permanently restricted from non-agricultural development in perpetuity. The program helps keep Howard County agricultural land in active use for future generations.

The easement permanently restricts non-agricultural development rights on the property while the landowner retains ownership and may continue farming, selling, or passing down the land.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Moderate Income Housing Unit (MIHU) program operates on two levels in Howard County. First, it requires residential developers to set aside a percentage of units in new developments as affordable housing for moderate-income households, offering density bonuses and other incentives in exchange for including these units. Second, during open enrollment periods, income-eligible households can apply to rent or purchase these below-market, moderately priced units—including homeownership opportunities—at rates established by the county as part of its inclusionary zoning requirements. For-sale units are subject to resale restrictions to maintain long-term affordability, allowing moderate-income buyers and renters to access housing at prices below what the open market would charge. Renters must meet income eligibility requirements and must reside or seek to reside in Howard County.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Residential developers who include affordable moderate-income units receive density bonuses and other incentives as part of the county's inclusionary zoning requirements. Income-eligible households may rent or purchase housing units—including below-market-rate homeownership units—at prices below the open market rate as established by Howard County. For-sale units are sold with resale restrictions to maintain long-term affordability. Rental units are also made available to income-eligible households at below-market rates in qualifying residential developments.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential developers and builders in Howard County, as well as income-eligible moderate-income households seeking affordable rental or for-sale (homeownership) housing at below-market prices.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Inclusion of affordable housing units in new residential developments (for developers); renting or purchasing a moderately priced home at below-market rates in Howard County (for households).

Must reside or seek to reside in Howard County

structured_extraction.program_description: The Youth Engagement Programming (YEP!) Grant, launched by Howard County Executive Calvin Ball, provides funding to nonprofit and community organizations that offer underserved youth opportunities for engagement, growth, and career exploration outside of traditional school hours. The program also helps parents in Howard County enroll their children in out-of-school activities offered through the Howard County Center of African American Culture. The program promotes free, accessible, and supportive programming for young people in Howard County, including school clubs, youth writing programs, career readiness training, mentorship, social-emotional learning, mental health, and wellness activities. Programming includes structured activities for educational, social, and emotional wellbeing during non-school times, with a focus on social engagement, positive peer interaction, positive self-expression, artistic creativity, realistic life aspirations and goals, field trips to significant cultural and historic venues throughout Howard County and the Baltimore-Washington corridor, and creative workshop projects (art, spoken word, drama). Grants support programming for youth (particularly ages 14-25) that is free or low-cost and developed specifically for Howard County youth outside of traditional school hours.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding provided to nonprofit and community organizations to develop free or low-cost youth engagement programming and activities in Howard County, and to parents/guardians to help cover participation costs for children in out-of-school youth programming. Programs must be offered outside of traditional school hours and focus on career readiness, mentorship, social-emotional learning, mental health, wellness, seminars/workshops, bus trips for field trips, and other youth engagement activities. Grant monies come from the County Executive. Specific award amounts and terms are not publicly detailed.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit and community organizations serving underserved youth in Howard County, as well as parents and guardians of children in Howard County seeking to enroll their children in out-of-school youth programming. The specific program offered through the Howard County Center of African American Culture targets youth ages 14-17 years old in grades 9-10, with enrollment limited to 12 students.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supporting youth career readiness training, mentorship, job development, social-emotional learning, mental health, wellness programming, school clubs, youth writing programs, seminars/workshops, bus trips for field trips to cultural and historic venues throughout Howard County and the Baltimore-Washington corridor, creative workshop projects (art, spoken word, drama), and other youth engagement activities offered outside of traditional school hours that are free and accessible to Howard County youth; also covers participation costs for children in out-of-school activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to organizations and individuals serving youth in Howard County, Maryland, including Columbia. Field trips may extend to the Baltimore-Washington corridor.
requirements_list: Must be a nonprofit, community organization, or parent/guardian of a child in Howard County
Programming must be free or low-cost and accessible to youth
Programming must be developed for Howard County youth
Programming must be offered outside of traditional school hours
Priority focus on underserved youth, including career exploration, mentorship, and development programming
For the HCCAAC program: participant must be age 14-17 years old and in grades 9-10
Enrollment limited to 12 students for the HCCAAC program
Parent/guardian consent required
Release of liability signature required
Applicant parents or guardians must complete the YEP Grant application form and submit by email or mail
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download the YEP Grant application form, complete it, and submit by email to hccaac@gmail.com or mail to the Howard County Center of African American Culture at 5434 Vantage Point Road, Columbia, Maryland 21044. For the HCCAAC program, complete the Registration and Consent Form and submit via the same channels.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Howard County property tax credit program for owners of commercial and industrial properties located along the US Route 1 corridor. The program encourages investment, revitalization, and economic development in the Route 1 area by offering credits on county property taxes for visible improvements to properties. Applications open each July and are reviewed on a rolling basis until the annual allocation is used.
structured_extraction.agency: Howard County Department of Planning & Zoning
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a property tax credit up to a maximum of $100,000 per property against county property taxes. Applicants may be eligible for up to 125% of approved expenses if costs exceed the initial estimate, not to exceed the $100,000 cap. The full credit is available over five years if the property's taxes are high enough. The credit stays with the property, not the owner, if it is sold. The program has a total annual allocation of $250,000.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications open each July and are reviewed on a rolling basis until the annual allocation is used.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of commercial and industrial properties along the US Route 1 corridor in Howard County, Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eligible uses include: exterior renovations or cleaning; structural improvements to the facade; replacing false facades; restoring architectural features; adding streetscape items like landscaping, walkways, or lighting; repairing doors and windows; new signs, canopies, or awnings; visible roof repairs; screening for utility or trash areas; enhanced exterior lighting; fencing that does not hide the building; sidewalks; new construction that improves the property's appearance; and necessary interior structural work.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Limited to properties and businesses along the US Route 1 corridor in Howard County, Maryland.
requirements_list: You must be current on property taxes.
The property must have no outstanding violations for zoning, licensing, permits, or fire codes.
Proposed improvements must comply with the Route 1 Manual and county development standards.
Approval for the tax credit does not replace the need for any required building or sign permits.
The program has a total annual allocation of $250,000.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, contact the agency to discuss your proposed project. If you decide to apply, submit an application with contractor cost estimates and photos of the property's current condition. County staff review the application to ensure you meet all requirements. An inter-departmental committee then votes to approve or deny the project. You must not begin any work until you receive a Certificate of Eligibility. After completing the work, submit a final application with a maintenance agreement and invoices by April 1st. A county representative will inspect the site to verify the work was completed as approved.

structured_extraction.program_name: Coordinated Entry System of Homeless Services (CES)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Coordinated Entry System (CES) is a unified, HUD-required system for connecting individuals and families experiencing homelessness or housing crisis to housing resources and supportive services. It provides a standardized process to assess needs and prioritize individuals and families for available housing resources, including permanent supportive housing, rapid re-housing, transitional housing, emergency shelter, diversion, and prevention services. The system uses real-time data and standardized assessments (VI-SPDAT and Full SPDAT) to prioritize placements based on level of need and vulnerability. Operated at the county level, CES connects people through multiple access points including outreach workers, emergency shelters, libraries, hospitals, and jails. The system implements a Housing First approach with low-barrier access and no clinical prerequisites. It tracks clients entering and exiting the homeless response system and identifies patterns and trends in homelessness.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: CES connects individuals and families experiencing homelessness or housing crisis to appropriate housing support through multiple access points. The system uses standardized assessments (VI-SPDAT, Full SPDAT) to prioritize housing placements based on level of need and vulnerability. Housing interventions include: Rapid Rehousing (time-limited financial and housing assistance with supportive services), Permanent Supportive Housing (permanent housing subsidy with long-term wraparound services for persons with disabilities), Transitional Housing (up to 24 months temporary housing with supportive services), SHaRP (short-term rental assistance, quarterly payments up to 100% of base rent for up to 12 months), Emergency Shelter (low-barrier access with meals, basic necessities, laundry, case management), Safe Haven services, Street Outreach, HUD Veterans Affairs Supportive Housing (HUD-VASH), and diversion and prevention services. CES meetings are held on the 2nd and 4th Thursday of each month, where a Program Manager matches clients to vacancies based on prioritization scores.
structured_extraction.contact_name: CES Program Manager; CoC/ICH Coordinator: Rozina Adhanom; Social Worker II (PACS): Sarah Moore
structured_extraction.contact_phone: DHHS Rockville: 240-777-4550; DHHS Germantown: 240-777-4448; DHHS Silver Spring: 240-777-3075; Crisis Center: 240-777-4000
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and families experiencing homelessness or at imminent risk of homelessness in Montgomery County, Maryland, including: literally homeless individuals (Category 1), those at imminent risk of homelessness (Category 2), those fleeing domestic violence (Category 4), veterans, young adults (ages 18-24), families with minor children, adult-only households, domestic violence survivors, returning citizens, and older adults (55+).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Access to permanent supportive housing, rapid re-housing, transitional housing, emergency shelter, safe haven services, street outreach, diversion, prevention, and supportive services including case management, primary medical care, mental health crisis services, behavioral health navigation, employment assistance, and benefits assistance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to individuals and families in Howard County and Montgomery County, Maryland. Within Montgomery County, services are available county-wide including Upcounty, Midcounty, and East County areas.
requirements_list: Must be experiencing homelessness or a housing crisis, or at imminent risk of homelessness
Must meet HUD definition of homelessness (Categories 1, 2, or 4)
Must complete standardized assessment tools (VI-SPDAT or Full SPDAT) to determine level of need and appropriate housing placement
Residency eligibility for homeless services programs required
HMIS enrollment and documentation required
Updated Release of Information (ROI) required
Identity and asset documentation required
Disability documentation required (for certain programs)
Non-discrimination policy compliance
Data and privacy compliance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individuals can access the system through multiple designated entry points including outreach workers, emergency shelters, libraries, hospitals, and jails. Standardized assessments (VI-SPDAT or Full SPDAT) are conducted to determine acuity and prioritization scores. CES meetings are held on the 2nd and 4th Thursday of each month, where the Program Manager matches clients to vacancies based on prioritization. Housing providers then meet with consumers and provide written program descriptions. Clients may complete a decline form if choosing not to accept a housing offer.

Turnkey solutions enable startups to focus on core business value drivers. Tenants get access to private offices, co-working desks, BSL2 wet labs, shared scientific instruments, and the broader Johns Hopkins innovation community including investors, industry experts, and academic researchers.

Access to Johns Hopkins core facilities and exclusive access to the innovation district are also included.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Johns Hopkins University President's Innovation Award is given each year to one early-to-mid career faculty member who is committed to translating research into real-world products or services and solving societal problems. The $250,000 award supports the recipient's translational and commercialization goals broadly during crucial early career years, without requiring a specific business idea or technology proposal, helping advance their innovations toward the marketplace.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A one-time $250,000 non-dilutive grant awarded annually to one faculty member to advance their translational research and commercialization activities. Funds can be used for key or exploratory experiments, lab support, conference attendance, contract research organization (CRO) work, publication of findings, or other activities most likely to advance their innovations toward the marketplace.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Full-time tenure-track (or equivalent) faculty members at Johns Hopkins University, especially those at the Assistant or Associate Professor stage (early-to-mid career), who have demonstrated a commitment to translating science into real-world products or services and solving societal problems.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Key or exploratory experiments, lab support, conference attendance, contract research organization (CRO) work, publication of findings, or any activities most likely to advance the recipient's innovations toward the marketplace during crucial early career years.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Johns Hopkins University faculty members.
requirements_list: Must be a full-time tenure-track (or equivalent) JHU faculty member
Must be an early-to-mid career faculty member (Assistant or Associate Professor stage preferred)
Must have demonstrated a commitment to translating science into real-world products or services
Must be focused on solving problems in society and translating research beyond academia
Nomination must be submitted by a full-time JHU faculty member

Submission must include nominator and nominee contact information, nominee's CV, a letter of nomination (up to 3 pages), a one-page summary of research and proposed use of award, and a sample work product
Finalists must submit a letter of support from a Dean or Department Chair
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: A full-time JHU faculty member nominates an eligible colleague by the January 19, 2026 deadline. The selection committee conducts a two-tier review: the first tier identifies finalists from initial nominations; finalists are then asked to submit a letter of support from a Dean or Department Chair. Finalist packages are forwarded to the JHU president and provost for final selection. Winners are announced in late March.

structured_extraction.program_name: Translational Funding at JHTV (Cohen, Thalheimer, and Zizic Funds)
structured_extraction.program_description: Johns Hopkins Technology Ventures (JHTV) offers non-dilutive translational funding to help Johns Hopkins faculty advance early-stage innovations and formally disclosed technologies toward commercialization. A single application provides access to three separate philanthropic funds — the Cohen Translational Engineering Fund, the Louis B. Thalheimer Fund for Translational Research, and the Zizic Translational Fund — which support proof-of-concept work, prototype development, validation studies, and commercialization readiness efforts. Awards are flexible and typically capped at $50,000, right-sized to help each project reach its next critical milestone. Recipients are encouraged to apply at multiple stages using a phased development approach. When funded technologies are successfully licensed, a portion of Johns Hopkins' license revenue (twice the award amount) is repaid to the Thalheimer/Zizic Fund before revenues are distributed to Johns Hopkins or inventors. Funding cycles occur twice per year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Non-dilutive grants provided twice per year through one streamlined application covering three translational funding programs (Cohen, Thalheimer, and Zizic). Awards are flexible and typically capped at $50,000, right-sized to help each project reach its next critical milestone. Funding supports proof-of-concept studies, prototype development, validation studies, regulatory pathway planning, and commercialization readiness activities including in vivo studies, formulation optimization, animal studies, analytical services, materials, reagents, and characterization. Faculty salary and indirect costs are excluded. Funding does not require equity ownership, though it may include participation rights or a payback component. When funded technologies are successfully licensed, a portion of Johns Hopkins' license revenue (twice the award amount) is repaid to the Thalheimer/Zizic Fund before revenues are distributed to Johns Hopkins or inventors.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Johns Hopkins University faculty and principal investigators with formally disclosed early-stage technologies seeking funding to advance innovations toward commercialization. At least one investigator must hold a full, joint, or courtesy faculty appointment at Johns Hopkins University.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Proof-of-concept studies, prototype development, validation studies, in vivo studies and validation, formulation optimization, regulatory consulting and IND pathway planning, animal studies and analytical services, materials, reagents, and characterization to de-risk technologies, reach key milestones, and enhance their commercial value. Excluded uses: faculty salary and indirect costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Johns Hopkins University faculty with a full, joint, or courtesy faculty appointment at Johns Hopkins University (Baltimore, MD campus community).
requirements_list: Applicant must be affiliated with Johns Hopkins University with a full, joint, or courtesy faculty appointment.
Technology must be formally disclosed to JHTV and assigned a case number.
The invention must not be subject to any pre-existing exclusive licenses, non-exclusive licenses, or options.
Technology must be at an early stage suitable for translational research support.
Only one application per Lead Principal Investigator per application cycle.
Must be seeking to commercialize a technology or innovation.
Application deck must be non-confidential and suitable for sharing with industry experts.

Application must use the provided template and include all relevant sections (executive summary, team, problem statement, solution, technology status, competitive landscape, commercialization pathway, project plan, budget, and risk assessment).
No confidential information permitted in application materials.
Letters of Support from industry partners are optional but valued.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Prepare a non-confidential pitch deck using the provided template and submit it through the online application portal. The deck must include an executive summary, team, problem statement, solution, technology status, competitive landscape, commercialization pathway, project plan, budget, and risk assessment. Use graphics, charts, and tables; write for a business professional audience. Letters of Support from industry partners are optional but valued. A single application is reviewed for all three funds (Cohen, Thalheimer, and Zizic). Applications open March 23, 2026 and close April 14, 2026; the next cycle opens in September 2026. Finalists will be notified and invited to refine their presentation for an in-person pitch. The JHTV Technology Development team is available to help strengthen applications before submission. An information session recording is available on the program page. Contact Stewart Neifert for questions.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Venture Mentorship Program (VMP) provides business-focused group mentorship to Johns Hopkins faculty, students, and innovators from all nine Johns Hopkins schools to help advance emerging technologies through the commercialization process. Groups of two to four volunteer mentors guide assigned ventures over multiple months using a structured model adapted from MIT's mentorship program, meeting roughly once a month with a commitment of 2-4 hours per month. The VMP office manages all administrative work including applications and scheduling.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free group mentorship from two to four volunteer mentors who guide ventures through the commercialization and business development process over multiple months. Mentors handle the business aspects of startup development, meeting roughly once a month with a commitment of 2-4 hours per month. The VMP office manages all administrative work including applications and scheduling.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Johns Hopkins faculty, students, innovators, and startups (including early-stage) from all nine Johns Hopkins schools seeking business mentorship for emerging technologies.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business development, mentorship, and guidance through the commercialization process for emerging technologies and startups.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Open to Johns Hopkins faculty, students, and startups affiliated with any of the nine Johns Hopkins schools in Baltimore.
requirements_list: Must be a Johns Hopkins faculty member, student, startup, or affiliated innovator
Must be accepted into the program
Both mentors and mentees must apply to participate
Mentors must sign a statement of guiding principles/code of ethics
Focused on business aspects of startup development
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application through the VMP office. Contact Justin Berger, Network Program Specialist, at JHTV or email vmp@jh.edu for more information or to apply as a mentor or mentee. The VMP office handles all administrative work including applications and scheduling mentor sessions.

structured_extraction.program_name: Innovation Fund for Community-Academic Partnerships – Community-Based Project and Research Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: Grants of up to $30,000 or $80,000 for JHU faculty and their community partners to collaborate on community-based projects and/or research. The grants support the bidirectional exchange of community-based and university-based knowledge, values, and expertise to address specific community needs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two funding tiers are available: (1) up to $30,000 for established partnerships that have existed at least one year, over a term of up to two years; and (2) up to $80,000 for firmly established partnerships that have existed at least two years, over a term of up to two years. Funds should be split between JHU and community partners, with the majority going to community partners in most cases. Eligible uses include salary (including fringe), graduate and undergraduate students, postdoctoral fellows, technicians, equipment, travel, and events.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications for the 2026-2027 cycle have closed. Applications for the 2027-2028 cycle will open in Fall 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: JHU tenure-track and tenured faculty (or equivalent in non-tenure divisions) at any rank, applying on behalf of a community-academic partnership. Must have 1–3 named community partners. Applications from multiple faculty spanning more than one school or division are especially encouraged.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Salary (including fringe), graduate and undergraduate students, postdoctoral fellows or technicians, equipment, travel, and events. Majority of funds should go to the community partner or directly benefit the community.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Work should take place in a geographic area local to the applicant. Most awardees are expected to work in Greater Baltimore or Washington, D.C., but proposals from any geographic location are welcome.
requirements_list: Lead applicant must be tenure-track or tenured JHU faculty (or equivalent in non-tenure divisions).
Must have at least 1 and no more than 3 named community partners who participated in the proposal process.
Only one Project/Research proposal per lead PI is accepted.
Staff, students, postdoctoral fellows, and non-tenure-track faculty are not eligible to serve as PIs or co-PIs.
Partnerships must have existed for at least one year to be eligible for the $30,000 tier.
Partnerships must have existed for at least two years to be eligible for the $80,000 tier.
Applications must be led by faculty from an eligible JHU school or division (APL, BSPH, CBS, KSAS, Peabody, SAIS, SOE, SOGP, SOM, SON, or WSE).
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application with seven elements: (1) title; (2) ~250-word abstract; (3) proposal of up to three pages covering goal, partnership history, approach, expected impact, dissemination plan, and sustainability; (4) budget with justification; (5) CV/resume/biosketch for all leads and co-applicants; (6) one letter of affirmation per community partner; and (7) up to five keywords. All documents are uploaded as a combined PDF. Award decisions are announced in Spring; funds are available starting late Spring.

structured_extraction.program_name: Innovation Fund for Community-Academic Partnerships – Institute, Center, and Program Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: Grants of up to $100,000 to enhance the work of Johns Hopkins University institutes, centers, and programs that have historically supported community-academic partnerships. The grants aim to sustain and enhance current programming and test innovative new projects and approaches in community-based academic engagement.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Awards of up to $100,000 with a term of up to two years. Funds may support salary (including fringe), graduate and undergraduate students, postdoctoral fellows, technicians, supplies, equipment, travel, events, and activities or services of a community partner. For coursework support, no more than $10,000 per semester in grant funds is allowed.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications for the 2026-2027 cycle have closed. Applications for the 2027-2028 cycle will open in Fall 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Staff and faculty in leadership positions at JHU institutes, centers, or programs that have historically supported community-based academic engagement as a significant part of their mission.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Salary (including fringe), graduate and undergraduate students, postdoctoral fellows or technicians, supplies, equipment, travel, events, and activities or services of a community partner.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Work should take place in a geographic area local to the institute, center, or program. Most awardees are expected to work in Greater Baltimore or Washington, D.C., but proposals from any geographic location are welcome.
requirements_list: Applicant must be staff or faculty in a leadership position at a JHU institute, center, or program.
The institute, center, or program must have historically supported community-based academic engagement as a significant part of its mission.
Each institute, center, or program may only submit a single application.
The institute, center, or program must employ at least one FTE (not including the applicant) who dedicates at least 75% of their effort to the applying entity.
All staff/faculty leads must be full time at JHU.
Proposed work should take place locally to the institute, center, or program.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application consisting of three elements: (1) title; (2) a proposal of up to three pages covering mission, proposed use of funds, qualifications, innovation, expected impact, and sustainability plan; and (3) a budget with justification. Applications are reviewed on a cycle basis (e.g., 2027-2028 cycle opens Fall 2026).

structured_extraction.program_name: U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) Support Programs
structured_extraction.program_description: The SBA is a federal agency that helps small businesses start, grow, and thrive through three main areas: Capital (loans and grants), Contracts (federal contracting certifications and set-asides), and Counseling (free or low-cost mentorship, training, and technical assistance through resource partners like SCORE and SBDCs).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: SBA offers multiple forms of assistance: (1) SBA-guaranteed loans including 7(a), 504, microloan, and Community Advantage programs for entrepreneurs who cannot access traditional financing; (2) SBIR and STTR grants for R&D and commercialization; (3) surety bonds and disaster relief loans; (4) federal contracting certifications such as 8(a), HUBZone, WOSB, Veteran-Owned, and Small Disadvantaged Business; and (5) free or low-cost counseling, mentorship, and training through SCORE, SBDCs, Women's Business Centers, and Veterans Business Outreach Centers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses seeking capital, federal contracts, or business counseling and training.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Starting or growing a business, R&D, disaster recovery, pursuing federal contracts, or accessing mentorship and training.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available nationwide including Maryland.
requirements_list: Must qualify as a small business under SBA size standards

structured_extraction.program_name: First-Time Homebuyer Education and Counseling (Spanish / En Español and English)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Latino Economic Development Center (LEDC), a HUD-approved housing counseling agency, provides first-time homebuyer education and counseling services in the DC, Maryland, and Northern Virginia area. Services include one-on-one counseling sessions, group seminars, and full-day workshops offered in both Spanish and English. Spanish-language workshops are held at locations in Wheaton/Silver Spring (Montgomery County) and Baltimore, MD; English-language workshops are held in Wheaton, MD. Workshop options include a 2-hour virtual introduction to homebuying (covering resources in Montgomery and Prince George's counties or Baltimore), an 8-hour in-person homebuyer education seminar held at WorkSource Montgomery in Wheaton (certificate awarded), and a 6-hour homebuyer education seminar delivered in two 3-hour virtual sessions via Zoom for first-time homebuyers in Montgomery and Prince George's counties. LEDC housing counselors cover each step of the home-buying process, mortgage basics, credit history, budgeting, and personal finances, and help clients apply for down payment assistance programs. All workshops feature guest experts including a loan officer, home inspector, real estate agent, and insurance agent, and provide information about first-time homebuyer assistance programs in MD and DC. Workshop sessions cost $50 per person or $75 per couple; the 6-hour virtual seminar is free; reimbursement is available through the My Home (MD) program; scholarships are available for HPAP clients; NeighborhoodLIFT recipients and Citibank pre-approved clients can have their fee waived by calling ahead; and some lenders/banks may cover the registration fee. A free individual counseling session with a HUD-certified LEDC housing counselor is available after the workshop to receive a completion certificate. All sessions fulfill first-time homebuyer training requirements for lenders and government programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: LEDC housing counselors offer one-on-one sessions, group seminars, and full-day courses in both Spanish and English covering the home-buying process, mortgage loans, credit, budgeting, and personal finances, as well as assistance applying for down payment assistance programs. Course options include a 2-hour virtual introduction to homebuying, an 8-hour in-person homebuyer education seminar (certificate awarded) at WorkSource Montgomery in Wheaton, and a free 6-hour homebuyer education seminar delivered in two 3-hour virtual sessions via Zoom. Workshops are held in Wheaton/Silver Spring and Baltimore (Spanish) and Wheaton (English). In-person workshops cost $50 per person or $75 per couple, with reimbursement available through the My Home (MD) program, scholarships for HPAP clients, fee waivers for NeighborhoodLIFT recipients and Citibank pre-approved clients, and potential lender coverage of fees. A free individual counseling session with a HUD-certified counselor is offered after the workshop to receive a completion certificate or HUD certificate required for special first-time homebuyer programs.

structured_extraction.program_name: LEDC Small Business Loans (Growth, Startup, and SEED Loans / InBusiness Microloan Program)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Latino Economic Development Center (LEDC), a certified Community Development Financial Institution (CDFI), provides alternative microloan and small business loan options to startups and existing small businesses that have difficulty obtaining credit from traditional banks. Three loan tiers are available: the Growth Loan for established businesses (2+ years in operation), the Startup Loan for newer ventures (under 2 years), and the SEED Loan for pre-launch or very early-stage businesses (under 1 year or planning to launch within 3 months). Loans range from $500 to $250,000 depending on business stage and can be used for a variety of business purposes including vehicles and equipment, working capital, inventory, renovation or business expansion, hiring additional personnel, bridge financing for government grants and contracts, expansion to new locations, and business acquisition. Loan officers assess each transaction beyond traditional credit underwriting guidelines, and business advice is provided at no cost.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans from $500 to $250,000 depending on business stage, all carrying a fixed APR starting at 6.5%. Growth Loan: up to $250,000 for established businesses (2+ years), terms up to 120 months (10 years), 3% closing fee, collateral required, requires last 2 years of business and personal tax returns and last 6 months of personal and business bank statements. Startup Loan: up to $20,000 for businesses under 2 years old, terms up to 60 months, 3% closing fee, collateral required, requires last 2 years of business and personal tax returns and last 6 months of personal and business bank statements. SEED Loan: up to $5,000 for businesses under 1 year or planning to launch within 3 months, terms up to 36 months, 1% closing fee, no collateral required, requires last 2 years of personal tax returns and last 6 months of personal bank statements. Eligible uses include vehicles and equipment, working capital, inventory, renovation or business expansion, hiring additional personnel, bridge financing for government grants and contracts, expansion to new locations, and business acquisition. Business advice provided at no cost.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Startups and existing small businesses, including those that have difficulty obtaining credit from mainstream financial institutions, seeking affordable alternative financing. The Growth Loan targets established small businesses with at least two years of operations; the Startup Loan targets businesses under two years old seeking capital to launch or consolidate; the SEED Loan targets pre-launch or very early-stage businesses with less than one year of operations or entrepreneurs planning to launch within 3 months.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Vehicles and equipment, working capital, inventory, renovation or business expansion, hiring additional personnel, bridge financing for government grants and contracts, expansion to new locations, and business acquisition.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Serves the Washington DC metro area including Maryland suburbs (Montgomery and Prince George's counties). LEDC also serves the broader metro region including DC and Virginia.
requirements_list: At least two years in business operations (Growth Loan); under 2 years (Startup Loan); under 1 year or planning to launch within 3 months (SEED Loan)
Last 2 years of business and personal tax returns (Growth and Startup Loans); last 2 years of personal tax returns only (SEED Loan)
Last 6 months of personal and business bank statements (Growth and Startup Loans); last 6 months of personal bank statements only (SEED Loan)

structured_extraction.program_name: Agribusiness Equipment and Working Capital Loan Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides low-interest loans to help Maryland agribusinesses and rural businesses innovate, diversify, and pursue new market opportunities. The program targets rural businesses and agribusinesses that cannot obtain commercial financing for working capital and equipment purchases from traditional lenders such as banks or farm credit associations. Offered by MARBIDCO, the program supports equipment purchases and working capital needs to help businesses take advantage of emerging market opportunities. The program complements financial services of other public sector lending agencies through joint funding.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans ranging from $15,000 to $100,000. Equipment loans have terms of 3 to 8 years (with up to 12 months interest-only). Operating loans have terms of 1 to 2 years (with up to 6 months interest-only). Interest rate is 4.75% when a partnering public-sector lender is involved, or 6.75% without one. A Home Town Hero Veteran rate reduction of an additional 0.25% (25 basis points) is available. A 1% loan origination fee applies. Typically requires 10% equity contribution from the borrower. Personal guarantee required for all business-entity loans.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland agribusinesses and rural businesses — including agricultural businesses, resource-based businesses, food or fiber production and processing businesses, farm businesses, and rural businesses — that cannot obtain commercial financing for working capital or equipment purchases from traditional lenders such as banks or farm credit associations.
