Grants support activities such as on-farm and value-added food processing, smaller-scale secondary wood products manufacturing, and business-related technology enhancements.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: See individual programs for application deadlines
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers, agribusiness owners, resource-based industry businesses (forestry, seafood, on-farm processors), and local governments in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: On-farm and value-added food processing, smaller-scale secondary wood products manufacturing, business-related technology enhancements (especially energy efficiency), agricultural entrepreneurship, and emerging food and fiber markets
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a qualified farmer, agribusiness owner, or local government
Must be an agricultural or resource-based business (e.g. forestry, seafood, on-farm processors)
Grants are awarded on a competitive basis
Ranking factors include economic significance and business economic viability
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact MARBIDCO staff for consultation to determine program fit. See individual programs for specific application requirements and deadlines. Applications are reviewed by MARBIDCO's Grant Review Committee.

structured_extraction.program_name: Forestry Equipment and Working Capital Loan Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: Low-interest loans for Maryland's forest products businesses for working capital and equipment purchases. Aims to help forest products-related businesses innovate and exploit emerging market opportunities. Complements financial services offered by private commercial lenders to make rural business financing available and affordable.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans ranging from $15,000 to $150,000. Equipment loans have 3- to 6-year terms; operating loans have 1- to 2-year terms. Interest rate is set case-by-case with a minimum fixed rate of 6.25%. A 1% loan origination fee applies. Borrowers typically contribute 5–10% equity toward total project cost. A commercial lender must participate by providing a letter of referral. The total outstanding portfolio balance under this program cannot exceed $400,000.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland forest products businesses including corporations, partnerships, proprietorships, and LLCs needing working capital or equipment financing
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Working capital and equipment purchases for forest products businesses, including value-added secondary wood processing, timber growing or harvesting, environmental/water quality projects, and biomass/energy products
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Applicant must be a forest products-related business in Maryland
Commercial lender must participate and provide a letter of referral
Equity contribution of typically 5–10% of total project cost required
Personal guarantee by business owners required
Farm/business income documentation required
Debt repayment schedule required
Financial statements required (expenses, income calculations)
Contact MARBIDCO office before completing an application due to portfolio cap of $400,000
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants originate and submit their own applications. Submit financial documentation including income statements, expense schedules, and debt repayment schedules. Cooperative Extension agents, Maryland Forest Service, county agricultural marketing officials, and other business professionals may help prepare the application. Applications are processed as received. Submit completed applications by mail to MARBIDCO Forestry Loan Program, 1410 Forest Drive, Suite 21, Annapolis, MD 21403, or by email to bcadden@marbidco.org.

structured_extraction.program_description: MARBIDCO offers U.S. military service members and veterans a 0.25% (25 basis points) interest rate reduction on select MARBIDCO rural business loan programs. This reduction is available to eligible applicants who are currently serving or have honorably served in any branch of the U.S. military and have at least 50% veteran ownership and management in their agribusiness or farming operation.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A 0.25% (25 basis points) interest rate reduction applied to eligible MARBIDCO rural business loans, including the Maryland Resource-Based Industry Financing Fund (MRBIFF), Maryland Vineyard/Hopyard/Orchard Planting Loan Fund, Agribusiness Equipment and Working Capital Loan Fund, Forestry Equipment and Working Capital Loan Fund, and Maryland Large Animal Veterinarian Assistance Loan Program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Current U.S. military service members and veterans with at least 50% veteran ownership and management control in an agribusiness or farming operation in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Interest rate reduction on qualifying MARBIDCO rural business loans.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland
requirements_list: Must be currently serving in any branch of the U.S. military (with a letter of support from commanding officer) OR have served and received an 'Honorable' or 'General (Under Honorable Conditions)' discharge (proven by DD-214 form)
Must have at least 50% veteran ownership in the agribusiness or farming operation
Must have at least 50% veteran management control in the agribusiness or farming operation
Must notify MARBIDCO at the time of loan application of intent to seek Hometown Hero interest rate reduction eligibility
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Notify MARBIDCO at the time of loan application about intent to seek the Hometown Hero interest rate reduction. Provide required documentation: a letter of support from commanding officer (if currently serving) or DD-214 form (if veteran). Submit a business plan and borrower financial information as required by the underlying loan program.

structured_extraction.program_name: Local Government Agriculture & Resource-Based Industry Project Cost Share Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that matches rural business development investments made by local governments and rural regional development councils. It supports retention and growth of Maryland's existing and emerging agricultural and resource-based businesses by partnering with local economic development offices on cost-share projects in farming, forestry, seafood, agritourism, value-added processing, and water/air quality improvement.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Matching grants up to $10,000 per project. Food Safety Modernization Act (FSMA) matching grants are capped at $5,000. Deer fences, farm solar systems, or generators providing commercial business energy are capped at $3,000. A single government jurisdiction may receive no more than $25,000 in total grants per fiscal year. Individual farmers or business owners (called 'Designees') have a $15,000 lifetime maximum. MARBIDCO grant cannot exceed the local government's own investment. Projects must benefit Maryland's farming, forestry, or seafood industries. Individual business owners must contribute their own equity if they directly benefit from the project.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local and regional economic development offices and rural regional development councils acting on behalf of Maryland agricultural, forestry, seafood, and resource-based businesses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cost-share projects that support farming, forestry, seafood, agritourism, value-added food processing and marketing, food safety compliance (FSMA), deer fences, farm solar/generator systems for commercial energy, water/air quality improvements that contribute to business sustainability, biomass/energy production, equipment and facilities, and industry feasibility studies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland, with a focus on rural areas. Past partners have included Anne Arundel, Cecil, Howard, Kent, Montgomery, Queen Anne's, Salisbury-Wicomico Economic Development Inc., Town of Mount Airy, and Worcester.
requirements_list: Application must be submitted by a local or regional economic development office — individual businesses cannot apply directly.
The governmental entity's funds must be own-source (not pass-through funds).
MARBIDCO grant cannot exceed the local government's own investment in the project.
The project must fit within MARBIDCO's economic development profile and benefit Maryland's farming, forestry, or seafood industries.
If the project directly benefits an individual farmer or business owner, that person must make a financial (equity) contribution to the project.
Projects not directly involving individual business owners (e.g. industry feasibility studies) may not require private equity contributions.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download the application form from MARBIDCO's website. Submit the completed application through a local or regional economic development office by mail to MARBIDCO, Local Government Grant Program, Attn. Daniela Merkle, 1410 Forest Drive, Suite 21, Annapolis, MD 21403, or electronically to dmerkle@marbidco.org.

structured_extraction.program_name: MARBIDCO Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Financing Programs
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation (MARBIDCO) is a quasi-state agency that offers more than 20 targeted low and moderate-cost loan and grant programs for Maryland's commercial farming, forestry, and seafood industries. Programs serve new and existing businesses, young and beginning farmers, watermen, aquaculture operators, seafood processors, wood processors, vineyard owners, veterinarians, and rural entrepreneurs. MARBIDCO helps businesses secure affordable capital for equipment, facilities, and real estate, with a special focus on innovative and start-up operations that face higher risk profiles that commercial lenders are reluctant to finance alone. Programs foster sustainability, profitability, rural economic growth, and preservation of working farmland.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MARBIDCO offers a wide range of low and moderate-cost loan and grant programs including: Maryland Resource-Based Financing Fund (MRBIFF), Next Generation Farmland Acquisition Program (Next Gen), Small Acreage Next Generation Farmland Acquisition Program (SANG), Maryland Watermen's Microloan Program, Maryland Shellfish Aquaculture Financing Fund, Maryland Remote Setting Shellfish Aquaculture Loan Fund, Maryland Oyster Shucking House Loan Program, Maryland Large Animal Veterinarian Assistance Loan Program, Agribusiness Equipment and Working Capital Loan Fund, Maryland Livestock Processing Loan Program, Maryland Vineyard/Hops/Orchard Fruit Planting Loan Fund, Forestry Equipment and Working Capital Loan Fund, Rural Business Energy Efficiency Improvement Loan Fund, Maryland Value-Added Producer Matching Grant (USDA Option), Certified Local Farm and Fish Food Aggregation Grant Program, Future Harvest Beginner Farmer Training Graduate Grant, Maryland Wood Products Industry Equity Investment Program (WPIEI), Maryland Urban Agriculture Commercial Lending Incentive Grant Program, Maryland Livestock Processing Equipment Grant Program, Southern Maryland Agricultural Revolving Loan Fund, Local Government Agricultural & Resource-Based Industry Project Cost Share Program, and Upper Shore Regional Council Farm Incentive Fund. MARBIDCO partners cooperatively with commercial banks, Farm Credit Associations, USDA Farm Service Agency (FSA), and other federal, state, and local agencies to streamline financing for qualifying businesses and individuals.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Commercial farmers, foresters, watermen, aquaculture operators, seafood processors, wood processors, vineyard owners, veterinarians, agribusinesses, young and beginning farmers, landowners, and rural entrepreneurs in Maryland, including start-up operations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Equipment purchases, commercial facility improvements, real estate and farmland purchases, livestock processing, aquaculture, urban farming, local farm food aggregation, working capital, energy efficiency improvements, wood products industry investment, and general agribusiness development to start or grow agricultural, forestry, or seafood businesses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland.
requirements_list: Must operate in Maryland's agricultural, forestry, or seafood industries
Must be a qualifying business or individual in commercial farming, forestry, or seafood sectors
Practical farm and/or business experience required (may be supplemented by academic or hands-on training)
Submission of a business plan required
Submission of borrower financial information required
May need to be working with a mentor if experience is limited
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact MARBIDCO at 410-267-6807 to discuss which programs best fit your needs. Applicants can consult with MARBIDCO's experienced staff to identify the most appropriate programs. Applications require a business plan and borrower financial information. MARBIDCO works cooperatively with commercial banks, Farm Credit Associations, USDA offices, and other federal, state, and local agencies to streamline the borrowing process. Visit the MARBIDCO website at https://www.marbidco.org/ for additional program details.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Large Animal Veterinarian Assistance Loan Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Established by MARBIDCO to help attract and/or retain large animal veterinarians in Maryland. Addresses student loan debt burden that inhibits veterinarians' ability to obtain commercial financing for trucks and specialized equipment needed to provide large animal veterinary care services.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans between $25,000 and $100,000 at a 4.50% interest rate. Loan terms vary by amount: 3.5 years for $25,000–$39,999; 4 years for $40,000–$59,999; 4.5 years for $60,000–$79,999; 5 years for $80,000–$100,000. A 0.25% loan origination fee applies. A maximum 6-month interest-only repayment option is available. Borrowers must contribute at least 10% of the purchase cost. Collateral may not exceed 95% of fair market value. A personal guarantee is required for business entity borrowers. Minimum credit score of 620.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed large animal veterinarians with clinical experience who reside in Maryland and provide veterinary care to large animals such as cattle, horses, hogs, sheep, or goats. Particularly aimed at veterinarians carrying significant student loan debt.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of a truck or specialized equipment necessary for providing large animal veterinary care services in Maryland. May also support setup of a new veterinary practice in Maryland.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicant must reside in Maryland on the date the loan is settled and agree to have a majority of their large animal practice in Maryland during the loan term.
requirements_list: Hold a license to practice veterinary medicine in Maryland issued no earlier than January 2004
Have clinical experience providing veterinary care to large animals (e.g., cattle, horses, hogs, sheep, or goats)
Reside in Maryland on the date the loan is settled
Agree to have a majority of their large animal practice in Maryland during the loan term
Agree to pay at least 10% of the costs of any items purchased with MARBIDCO loan proceeds
Minimum credit score of 620
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must originate and submit a completed, signed application form with all required attachments. Applications are processed as received. Submit by mail to: MARBIDCO Large Animal Veterinarian Loan, Attn: Brittany Rawlings, 1410 Forest Drive, Suite 21, Annapolis, MD 21403, or by email to brawlings@marbidco.org.

structured_extraction.program_description: Established by MARBIDCO as a complement to USDA's Meat and Poultry Intermediary Lending Program, this program offers loans to help start up or expand small- and medium-sized USDA-inspected slaughter facilities in Maryland. It supports increased processing of meat, poultry, and blue catfish. Large meat and poultry processing companies are not eligible. The program can provide standalone financing or work alongside commercial lenders.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans range from $250,000 to $2,500,000 at a fixed interest rate of 4.00%. Loan proceeds can be used to purchase real estate, construct a new or expand an existing livestock processing facility, and purchase processing equipment. Loan terms correspond to the useful life of the financed assets, with an initial interest-only period of up to 12 months. A loan origination fee of 0.25% of the loan amount (up to $5,000) applies. Borrowers must contribute at least 7.5% of total project cost as equity. MARBIDCO will match the equity contribution dollar-for-dollar up to 10% of project cost, capped at $250,000 as an equity grant. Applicants building a new facility must show minimum working capital of 10% of project cost. Personal guarantees are required but waived if the borrower provides a 20% equity contribution including MARBIDCO's equity grant. Funding comes from the USDA Meat and Poultry Intermediary Lending Program Grant with matching funds from MARBIDCO. All projects must receive USDA approval before MARBIDCO can disburse funds.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small- and medium-sized USDA-inspected slaughter and livestock processing facilities in Maryland, including individual owners and guarantors in livestock/meat and poultry processing businesses. Large meat and poultry processing companies are not eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase real estate, construct a new or expand an existing livestock processing facility, and purchase livestock processing equipment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Priority given to construction of new facilities, especially in underserved parts of Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a small- or medium-sized USDA-inspected slaughter facility; large meat and poultry processing companies are not eligible
Borrower must provide at least 7.5% of total project cost as equity
Applicants constructing a new facility must demonstrate minimum working capital of at least 10% of project cost (cash or bank line of credit)
Personal guarantees required from owners of business entities (waived if 20% equity contribution including MARBIDCO equity grant is provided)
All projects must be submitted to USDA for approval before funds can be disbursed
Self-certification that recipient/business does not hold top four market share in meat and poultry processing sector
Labor standards certification: offer/maintain wages, benefits, and opportunities to workers
Environmental Assessment completion by USDA RD State Office
Drug-free Workplace Certification (USDA RD Form AD-1049)
Demographic information submission (optional but encouraged)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must originate and submit completed applications with required certifications and documentation. Applications are processed in the order received, subject to availability of funds. MARBIDCO completes intermediary certification and coordinates environmental assessment with USDA RD State Office. Send completed applications to: MARBIDCO Loan Programs, c/o Allison Roe, 1410 Forest Drive, Suite 21, Annapolis, MD 21403.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Oyster Shucking House Loan Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides low-interest loans to help finance the construction, renovation, or expansion of oyster processing facilities and the purchase of oyster processing equipment. It aims to increase oyster shell retention and return to the Chesapeake Bay. The program was created by legislation in 2022 (Senate Bill 830) and is operated by MARBIDCO using $1 million in state funding.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Fixed-rate loans at 3.25% interest with no origination fee. Minimum loan amount is $25,000 and maximum is $250,000, capped at $25,000 per full-time or seasonal full-time job created or retained. Loan terms correspond to the useful life of the financed assets, with an initial interest-only period of up to 6 months. Borrowers must contribute at least 3% equity toward total project cost. In Cecil, Kent, and Queen Anne's counties, MARBIDCO will match the borrower's equity contribution dollar-for-dollar up to 5% of project cost (capped at $12,500) using grant funds from regional councils. Applicants building a new facility must show working capital of at least 15% of project cost; all others must show at least 10%. Personal guarantees are normally required.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed Maryland Seafood Dealers and Tidal Fishing License (TFL) holders who operate oyster processing businesses
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Renovate or construct a new oyster processing facility, expand an existing facility, or purchase oyster processing equipment
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland; equity match incentive available only in Cecil, Kent, and Queen Anne's counties
requirements_list: Must have been a licensed Maryland Seafood Dealer for at least 3 years, OR be a TFL-holder for at least 5 years and agree to obtain a Seafood Dealer License if approved
Must have paid all applicable taxes and fees for the last 5 years
Must contribute at least 3% of total project cost as equity
Must demonstrate minimum working capital of 15% of project cost for new facility construction, or 10% for all other projects
Must submit a business plan including financial projections
Personal guarantee normally required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are processed on a rolling basis as received. Complete the fillable application form and include all required attachments listed in the application checklist (Page 8). Submit completed applications by email to skubofcik@marbidco.org or by mail to MARBIDCO Loan Programs, 1410 Forest Drive, Suite 21, Annapolis, MD 21403.

structured_extraction.program_description: MARBIDCO's most popular loan program that provides low-interest, below-market-rate gap financing to farmers, agricultural enterprises, and resource-based industry businesses in Maryland. The program works in partnership with commercial banks and Farm Credit lenders to help agricultural enterprises diversify or expand operations, assist young and beginning farmers buy their first farms, and support resource-based industry enterprises in purchasing land and capital equipment for production and processing activities. Available as a Direct Lending program or a Participation Loan program, both requiring collaboration with a commercial or public sector lender. MARBIDCO takes the junior collateral lien position behind the commercial lender, with the goal of reducing borrower costs, improving debt service coverage ratios, and eventually graduating borrowers to conventional commercial financing.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest direct loans and participation loans for purchasing land and capital equipment for agricultural and resource-based industry production and processing activities. MARBIDCO supplies additional loan proceeds ranging from 20% to 40% of total commercial financing required, contingent on a commercial lender providing at least an equal financial commitment. Direct loan rates: 4.75% for first 3 years, 5.25% for next 3 years, 5.75% for remaining term, plus 1% origination fee; terms of 5–7 years (land: 10–30 years with 10-year balloon). Direct loan maximums: real estate/poultry house construction $600,000; equipment/fixed assets $300,000; large-scale food/fiber processing $1,000,000 (max 25% of project cost). Participation loan rates: 4.25% (max 5.00% including lender servicing fee); MARBIDCO share 30%–49%. Participation loan maximums: real estate/poultry house construction $700,000; equipment/fixed assets $350,000; large-scale food/fiber processing $1,000,000 (max 25% of project cost). Typically requires 10% equity (less for beginning farmers). MARBIDCO takes the junior collateral lien position behind the commercial lender.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers, agricultural enterprises, and resource-based industry businesses in Maryland; young and beginning farmers seeking to buy their first farm; commercial lenders working with these borrowers
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of land, poultry house construction, capital equipment for production and processing, large-scale food/fiber processing projects, and farm or resource-based business acquisition, diversification, or expansion
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland; participation loans available through Horizon Farm Credit and Colonial Farm Credit
requirements_list: Must be a farm or resource-based industry business
Application must be submitted by a commercial bank or Farm Credit Association loan officer and/or Farm Service Agency representative
Commercial or public sector lender is required
Commercial lender must have at least an equal financial commitment to the project
Typically 10% equity of total project cost (may be less for young/beginning farmers)
Poultry projects may not exceed a combined loan-to-value of 92%
Large-scale food/fiber processing loans may not exceed 25% of total project cost
MARBIDCO may provide up to a maximum of 40% of project financing
Available as direct loan or participation loan option
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are developed and submitted to MARBIDCO by a commercial bank or Farm Credit Association loan officer, possibly in consultation with other rural business advisors and/or a Farm Service Agency representative. Loan officers can download the Direct Loan or Participation Loan guidance sheets for detailed information. Email completed applications to Brian Cadden at bcadden@marbidco.org or mail to Loan Programs, c/o Brian Cadden, 1410 Forest Drive, Suite 21, Annapolis, MD 21403. For inquiries, contact MARBIDCO at (410) 267-6807 or info@marbidco.org.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Shellfish Aquaculture Financing Fund (including Remote Setting)
structured_extraction.program_description: A subsidized loan program administered by the Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation (MARBIDCO) in partnership with the Maryland Department of Natural Resources (DNR) and the University of Maryland to provide affordable financing to commercial watermen, individuals, and entrepreneurs who want to start or expand shellfish aquaculture operations—including remote setting (nursery) shellfish aquaculture—in Maryland's Chesapeake and Coastal Bays. Loans are offered at below-market, subsidized rates with partial principal forgiveness available for first-time and existing borrowers in good standing, effectively converting a portion of the loan into a grant. Historically, $2.2 million in subsidized loans was made available from Maryland's oyster restoration budget. Training and business planning assistance is also available through the University of Maryland Extension and the Maryland Department of Agriculture. An equity incentive matching grant is also available specifically for applicants in Cecil, Kent, and Queen Anne's counties through the Upper Shore Regional Council. The program can also be coordinated with NRCS Environmental Quality Incentives Program (EQIP) grants and Chesapeake Bay Watershed Initiative Grants.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Subsidized loans ranging from $5,000 to $100,000 at an interest rate of 5.25% (as low as 3.00% during the initial interest-only period). There is no loan origination fee. Borrowers must contribute at least 10% equity. Repayment terms vary by use: up to 5 years for substrate/seed, 7 years for capital equipment, or 6 years for blended purchases, with 1–3 years interest-only followed by principal and interest payments. Quarterly repayment is required. For remote setting loans ($5,000–$30,000): loans of $5,000–$15,000 have a 5-year term; loans of $15,001–$30,000 have a 6-year term, both with interest-only payments in year one. First-time borrowers receive 40% principal forgiveness (up to $100,000). Existing borrowers in good standing receive 25% principal forgiveness on amounts between $100,001 and $300,000. For remote setting borrowers in good standing who follow their production plans, the final year of loan repayments is forgiven, amounting to an effective grant of 22%–27% of the original loan principal. Funds may be used for substrate (e.g., shell), seed or larvae, capital equipment with a 15-year life expectancy, and remote setting equipment such as tanks, pumps, blowers, valves, and tank heaters. Motor vehicles including boats and trucks are not eligible expenses. The program can be coordinated with NRCS EQIP grants; if combined, borrowers cannot receive double principal forgiveness from both MARBIDCO and NRCS for the same project activity. Historically, $2.2 million in subsidized loans was made available from Maryland's oyster restoration budget.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling — applications processed in the order received
structured_extraction.program_audience: Commercial watermen, individuals, and entrepreneurs (including individual proprietors, partnerships, LLCs, corporations, and agricultural cooperatives) holding or having applied for a state shellfish aquaculture lease or aquaculture nursery permit from DNR who want to start or expand shellfish aquaculture operations, including remote setting shellfish aquaculture, in Maryland's Chesapeake and Coastal Bays.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Starting or expanding commercial shellfish aquaculture operations, including remote setting (nursery) shellfish aquaculture and oyster and clam production, in Maryland's Chesapeake and Coastal Bays. Eligible expenses include purchase of substrate (e.g., shell), seed or larvae, capital equipment with a 15-year life expectancy, and remote setting equipment such as tanks, pumps, blowers, valves, and tank heaters. On-bottom and water column (cages or floats) aquaculture projects are eligible. Motor vehicles (boats, trucks) are not eligible. If coordinated with NRCS EQIP grants, grant funds are applied first to interest-only phase payments and then to principal reduction.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to persons holding or having applied for a State submerged land or water column aquaculture lease or aquaculture nursery permit from the Maryland Department of Natural Resources. Operations must be conducted in the Chesapeake and Coastal Bays of Maryland. State water column lease holders are also eligible. An equity incentive matching grant is also available specifically for applicants in Cecil, Kent, and Queen Anne's counties through the Upper Shore Regional Council.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a commercial waterman, individual, or business (individual proprietorship, partnership, LLC, corporation, or agricultural cooperative) seeking to start or expand shellfish aquaculture operations
Applicant must hold a shellfish aquaculture lease or aquaculture nursery permit from DNR, or have applied for such a lease or permit
Persons holding State water column leases are also eligible
Applicant must demonstrate that proposed shellfish aquaculture production will begin within 12 months of lease approval

Must have production and business plans demonstrating financial feasibility of the planned aquaculture operation, including pro forma income statements for Years 1–3, business income and expense projections, personal income and expense documentation, and business and personal debt repayment schedules
Credit bureau score of at least 620 (a qualifying co-signer is required for scores below 620)
No bankruptcy within the last seven years
At least 10% equity contribution of the loan amount (ownership of a commercial workboat may help satisfy this requirement)
Personal guarantees from principal business owners are required
Must be engaged in or seeking to start remote setting shellfish aquaculture (for the remote setting component)

If combining with NRCS EQIP grants, must complete proposed project prior to receiving grant funds and cannot receive double principal forgiveness from both MARBIDCO and NRCS for the same project activity
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete the application form from MARBIDCO's website. Submit the signed original application along with all required attachments to MARBIDCO Loan Programs Office (Attn: Brittany Rawlings, 1410 Forest Drive, Suite 21, Annapolis, MD 21403) or email to brawlings@marbidco.org. Applications are processed in the order received. Required financial documentation includes pro forma income statements, business and personal expense projections, and debt repayment schedules. Review the project financing submission checklist included at the end of the application form before submitting.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Urban Agriculture Commercial Lending Incentive Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: This grant helps beginning urban farmers get commercial lender financing to start or expand their urban farming operations. It provides a cash grant to reduce the cost of a commercial loan used for farm-related purchases such as equipment, supplies, real estate, and labor. The program is a partnership between MARBIDCO and Horizon Farm Credit, and supports commercial lending incentives for urban agriculture in Maryland.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $15,000 for equipment and working capital, or up to $35,000 for real property purchases. Grant amount cannot exceed 25% of total project cost or 33% of the approved commercial loan. Minimum grant is $1,000 (requires a commercial loan of at least $3,000). A commercial lender must approve a loan for the project before a grant is awarded. Funds are disbursed on a schedule set at the time of award. Program is administered in partnership with Horizon Farm Credit.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Beginning urban farmers — individuals or incorporated businesses whose principal operator(s) have 10 or fewer years of commercial farming experience or a net worth under $300,000, operating a commercial food or fiber growing operation in an urban area as defined by the U.S. Census Bureau or any incorporated Maryland municipality.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of real estate, agricultural inputs and supplies (seeds, fertilizer, compost, baskets), farm tools and equipment, greenhouses, high tunnels, refrigeration and irrigation systems, and hired labor (up to 20% of total eligible project cost).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The farming operation must be located in an urban area as defined by the U.S. Census Bureau or any incorporated municipality recognized by the State of Maryland.
requirements_list: Principal operator must have 10 or fewer years of commercial farming experience OR a net worth under $300,000
Operation must be a commercial food or fiber growing operation in an eligible urban area
A commercial lender or Farm Service Agency must have approved a loan for the proposed project before a grant is awarded
Grant amount cannot exceed 25% of the total project cost
Grant amount cannot exceed 33% of the approved commercial loan
Minimum commercial loan of $3,000 required
Applicants may not materially deviate from their approved business plan without MARBIDCO and lender approval
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the application form and verify that commercial lender or Farm Service Agency loan proceeds are available to help complete the proposed farming project. Mail the completed application to MARBIDCO Urban Agricultural Grant, 1410 Forest Drive, Suite 21, Annapolis, MD 21403, or email it to info@marbidco.org.

structured_extraction.program_description: MARBIDCO offers affordable loans to Maryland rural landowners who want to establish or expand vineyards, orchards, and hop yards. The program aims to increase the acreage of viable commercial vineyards, tree fruit orchards, and hop yards in Maryland by providing low-cost financing in partnership with a private commercial lender. Supported by the Maryland Wineries Association and the Maryland Grape Growers Association. Interest-only payment options are available for an initial period of up to three years.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest loans from $15,000 to $100,000 for establishing or expanding vineyards, orchards, and hop yards. Maximum loan term is 10 years. Two interest rate options are available: Option 1 offers an adjustable rate of 5.00% for the first three years, then 6.25% for the remainder; Option 2 is a fixed rate of 6.25% with the option to make interest-only payments for the first three years. A 1% loan origination fee applies. Borrowers typically need to provide 10% equity of total project cost (grant funds may qualify). A personal guarantee is required. All loans must be fully collateralized. MARBIDCO makes and services all loans.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland rural landowners seeking to establish or expand commercial vineyards, tree fruit orchards, or hop yards
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Land preparation for plant installation, purchase of vines or trees, and related equipment and supplies for vineyard/hopyard/orchard installation. Tractors, pickup trucks, and winemaking equipment are not eligible under this program (available under other MARBIDCO programs).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. An additional equity incentive is available for farmers in Cecil, Kent, and Queen Anne's counties through the Upper Shore Regional Council.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland rural landowner
Project must involve installation of a new vineyard, tree fruit orchard, or hop yard
A commercial lender must participate and provide a letter of referral
Typically 10% equity contribution of total project cost required (grant funds may qualify)
Personal guarantee required
All loans must be fully collateralized
Applicant must complete detailed financial statement including income sources and expenses
Applicant must provide farm/business debt repayment schedule
Applicant must provide personal debt repayment schedule (including car loans)
Detailed expense tracking required (labor, equipment, fertilizer, seeds, utilities, etc.)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit a completed application to MARBIDCO by mail at 1410 Forest Drive, Suite 21, Annapolis, MD 21403, or by email to info@marbidco.org. The application requires comprehensive financial disclosures including farm/business income and expense documentation and debt repayment schedules. Applications are reviewed as received and typically take 3-4 weeks to process. A panel of agricultural lenders reviews financial viability, and a viticulture committee reviews operational viability. Cooperative extension agents, Maryland Forest Service, county agricultural marketing officials, and other business professionals may help develop applications.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides low-interest, unsecured microloans to licensed commercial watermen and seafood processing businesses in Maryland. Watermen can use the loans to buy equipment or a commercial fishing boat, while seafood processors can use them to purchase processing equipment. The program offers partial loan forgiveness for borrowers who make all payments on time. It is a revolving loan fund established by MARBIDCO to provide affordable commercial capital and credit to Maryland watermen, designed to support those who harvest fish and shellfish from the Chesapeake Bay.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest (3% fixed rate), unsecured loans ranging from $7,000 to $20,000 for equipment purchases, up to $30,000 for a commercial workboat, and up to $40,000 for a workboat plus equipment. The lifetime aggregate limit per borrower is $40,000. Repayment includes at least a 6-month interest-only period followed by 4–6 years of quarterly principal-and-interest payments depending on loan size. Borrowers who make all payments on time receive partial loan forgiveness (the final 25% of payments, i.e., the final 4–6 quarterly payments, are forgiven). No collateral is required. Equipment purchased must have a useful life of at least 7 years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed commercial watermen (generational and beginner) and seafood processing businesses in Maryland. Generational Watermen must derive 50%+ of annual income from commercial seafood harvesting. Beginner Watermen must be at least 18 years old with 2–10 years of commercial seafood harvesting experience. Seafood Processors must hold a Seafood Dealer license from DNR.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of tangible equipment (boats, motors, harvesting gear) for watermen; seafood processing equipment for seafood processors. Equipment must have a useful lifespan of at least 7 years.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be residents of Maryland. Eligible license holders include those with a Tidal Fish License (TFL) from the Department of Natural Resources or a commercial license from the Potomac River Fisheries Commission.
requirements_list: Must be a licensed commercial waterman or seafood processing business
Must hold a Tidal Fish License (TFL) issued by the Department of Natural Resources OR a commercial license from the Potomac River Fisheries Commission
Generational Watermen must show that 50% or more of annual income came from commercial seafood harvesting (two most recent federal tax returns required)
Beginner Watermen must be at least 18 years old and demonstrate 2–10 years of commercial seafood harvesting experience via written narrative and reference letter
Beginner Watermen must document species harvested during the last 3 years
Seafood Processing Businesses must hold a Seafood Dealer license from DNR for at least the last two years and show commercial seafood processing income via two most recent federal tax returns
Seafood processors may only purchase seafood processing machinery
Equipment purchased must have a useful life of at least 7 years
Minimum credit score of 620
An applicant may not have more than one active microloan at a time
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the fillable application form. Submit electronically to brawlings@marbidco.org or mail to MARBIDCO c/o Brittany Rawlings, 1410 Forest Drive, Suite 21, Annapolis, MD 21403. Applications are processed in the order received. Applicants must submit two years of tax returns and complete income verification forms (Attachment A). Beginner watermen must also complete the Experience Verification Form (Attachment B) and provide a reference letter attesting to commercial fishing experience.

structured_extraction.program_name: Next Generation Farmland Acquisition Program (Next Gen)
structured_extraction.program_description: Helps beginning and first-time farmers purchase farmland by providing down payment assistance equal to up to 51% of the fair market value of the land only, capped at $500,000. MARBIDCO purchases a farmland conservation easement option on the property, allowing the new farmer to buy the property at a reduced upfront cost. After settlement, the farmer has 4-7 years to sell a permanent easement to a rural land preservation program (such as the County's Agricultural Land Preservation District program), after which they repay MARBIDCO the original option purchase amount plus a 3% administrative fee. If the farmer cannot obtain or sell a permanent easement within the specified timeframe, MARBIDCO exercises the option and places a permanent easement on the property at no additional cost, held by a designated third-party holder. This program preserves working farmland from future development while helping new and beginning farmers access land. The program operates in collaboration with commercial or farm credit lenders.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MARBIDCO pays up to 51% of the fair market value of the land only (in the 48-51% range, capped at $500,000) by purchasing a conservation easement option on the property, providing down payment assistance in collaboration with commercial or farm credit lenders. The assistance enables the farmer to meet equity requirements for commercial lender financing. After the farmer sells a permanent easement to a land preservation program (within 4-7 years depending on default easement holder), the farmer repays MARBIDCO the original option purchase amount plus a 3% administrative fee. Easement sale offers must meet minimum thresholds (100-125% of purchase amount). If the farmer cannot sell the permanent easement within the specified timeframe, MARBIDCO exercises the option and places a permanent easement on the property at no additional cost, held by a designated third-party holder. Commercial lender financing is required; applicants must subordinate their mortgage to the conservation easement.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Monthly, by 4:00 p.m. on the last business day of each month
structured_extraction.program_audience: Beginning and first-time farmers (individual farmers, partnerships, corporations, LLCs, or proprietorships) who do not own a farm or own less than 20 acres, have not operated a farm as principal operator for more than 10 years, have at least one year of farming experience or completed a qualified farm management training program, and plan to actively and substantially participate in farming the purchased property. Eligible farm types include beef cattle, sheep/goats/swine, equine, dairy, grain and row crops, greenhouse and nursery, poultry and eggs, vegetables and specialty crops, and value-added products. Applicants in Washington County must contact the County's Land Preservation Office.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment assistance for the purchase of qualifying farmland (land only), typically over 50 acres, for beginning and first-time farmers entering agriculture. The development rights of the acquired farmland are temporarily relinquished, leading to permanent land preservation. Operating expenses may also be addressed through commercial lender financing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. The subject farmland must be located in Maryland and must have qualifying soils (Class I, II, III, or Group 1, 2) and meet agricultural preservation criteria. Properties must be MALPF-eligible, Rural Legacy-eligible, or county program-eligible depending on default easement holder choice. Properties within designated Priority Preservation Areas or Rural Legacy Areas receive bonus points in application ranking. Applicants must contact the county agricultural land preservation office in the county where the farmland is located.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a beginning farmer: does not own a farm or owns less than 20 acres, has not been a principal farm operator for more than 10 years, has at least one year of farming experience or completed a qualified farm management training program, and expects to substantially participate in farming the property.
A ratified contract of sale for the subject farm property must be in place by the application deadline.
Applicant must contact the county agricultural land preservation administrator to discuss the subject farm property no later than one month before submission.
Required paperwork from the farm property seller (Form 1 - Property Seller's Information Form) must be received by the county office at least one month in advance.
Applicant must complete Form 2 (Applicant Information Form).
Applicant must have a detailed farm business plan developed (with 7 required categories).

A commercial bank or Farm Credit Association must participate in providing a portion of the farm purchase financing (firm loan commitment required after approval, not at application); applicant must subordinate mortgage to conservation easement.
Farmland is typically over 50 acres.
Property must qualify for the County's Agricultural Land Preservation District program (where applicable) or be MALPF-eligible or Rural Legacy-eligible depending on default easement holder choice.
After settlement, landowner must actively pursue and sell a permanent easement within 4-7 years (depending on default easement holder selection).
Landowner must enroll in the County's Ag District program after settlement (where applicable).
Development rights of acquired farmland must be temporarily relinquished.
Total net worth limits apply.
Property must remain in agricultural use.

Required financial documentation includes: two years tax returns, completed balance sheet, two years income statements, pro forma income statement, debt repayment schedule, and applicant experience/education statement (college transcript or farm training program certification).
Resume (if available) required.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Contact the county agricultural land preservation office in the county where the farmland is located at least one month before submission to discuss suitability. 2. Negotiate and ratify a contract of sale for the subject farm property. 3. Seller completes Form 1 (Property Seller's Information Form) and submits to county program staff at least 30 days prior to MARBIDCO application submission. 4. Develop a detailed farm business plan (with 7 required categories) and gather all required financial documentation (two years tax returns, balance sheet, income statements, pro forma income statement, debt repayment schedule). 5. Begin contact with a commercial lender to understand financing requirements. 6. Applicant completes Form 2 (Applicant Information Form) and submits a completed application with all required forms and attachments to the MARBIDCO office in Annapolis by 4:00 p.m. on the last business day of the month. 7. If approved, arrange commercial lender financing and submit a loan commitment letter to MARBIDCO within the specified window. Note: In Washington County, applicants complete the application with the County's Land Preservation Office, which then submits to MARBIDCO; the process takes approximately six months after submission.

structured_extraction.program_name: Rural Business Energy Efficiency Improvement Loan Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: A low-interest microloan program that helps rural farmers and agricultural-based businesses implement energy efficiency improvements. The program provides below-market-rate financing to purchase equipment or technology that lowers business energy consumption, with the goal of reducing energy use and increasing profitability. Targets dairy, poultry, and food/fiber processing enterprises. A small grant incentive is also included.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans range from $5,000 to $30,000 at a fixed interest rate of 4.50% with 2-7 year terms tied to the anticipated energy savings payback period. A grant incentive equal to 10% of the loan amount (up to $1,000) is also available. Loan advances may not exceed the cost of improvements minus any grant incentive funding received. A $75 loan origination fee is paid at closing. Loans are fully amortized and require at least a 1.0–1.0 debt service coverage ratio on annual energy savings. No collateral security required; personal guarantee of borrower and/or business is required.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers and agricultural-based industry business owners (including dairy farmers, poultry farmers, and food and fiber processing business owners) in rural Maryland who want to improve energy efficiency in their operations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and installation of equipment or technology to lower business-related energy consumption, as recommended by a third-party energy auditor.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. An equity incentive is also available specifically for farmers in Cecil, Kent, and Queen Anne's counties through a partnership with the Upper Shore Regional Council.
requirements_list: Borrower must have a credit score of at least 620
No bankruptcies filed within the last seven years
Loans are unsecured; only personal guarantee of borrower and/or business is required
Must submit a copy of an energy audit, an ag energy management plan report, or an energy savings confirmation letter from a qualified third-party energy auditor
Must provide a simple commercial lender referral
Debt service coverage ratio of at least 1.0–1.0 on annual energy savings payback
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: All applications must be originated by the applicant. Download and complete the application form, then send the completed application along with required documents (energy audit and lender referral) to MARBIDCO Loan Programs, 1410 Forest Drive, Suite 21, Annapolis, MD 21403, or email to info@marbidco.org. Applications are processed in the order received.

structured_extraction.program_name: Small Acreage Next Generation Farmland Acquisition Program (SANG)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Small Acreage Next Generation Farmland Acquisition Program (SANG) helps young and beginning farmers purchase small farmland properties between 10 and 49 acres in Maryland. MARBIDCO provides 30% to 60% of the Fair Market Value of the land (land only) in exchange for a permanent agricultural conservation easement, and that money is used as a down payment to buy the farmland. The program fills a gap left by the original Next Gen Program, which typically required properties of at least 50 acres. MARBIDCO serves as a conduit financing agent in conjunction with State and local government agencies and/or private land trust organizations. At the time of real estate settlement, the property is considered permanently preserved by MARBIDCO — no separate seven-year easement pursuit requirement applies. A commercial or farm credit lender must also be involved in the transaction, and most approved purchases are completed in 6 to 8 months. Applications are evaluated on a competitive basis by a Review Committee. The program is offered in partnership with the Southern Maryland Agricultural Development Commission (SMADC) for the five Southern Maryland counties.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MARBIDCO provides 30% to 60% of the Fair Market Value (land only) in exchange for a permanent agricultural conservation easement, capped at $6,000 per acre of MARBIDCO funding. That money is used as a down payment for the farmland purchase (10 to 49 acres), allowing the farmer to meet equity contribution requirements for commercial lender financing. MARBIDCO serves as a conduit financing agent in conjunction with State and local government agencies and/or private land trust organizations. The property is permanently preserved by MARBIDCO at settlement, with no requirement to pursue an additional permanent easement within seven years. A commercial or farm credit lender must also be involved. Most approved purchases are completed in 6 to 8 months. County matching funds may be available on a 50/50 basis.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Monthly, by 4:00 p.m. on the last business day of each month; sales contract must be signed before the final day of the month
structured_extraction.program_audience: Beginning and first-time farmers who do not currently own a farm or own less than 9 acres, have not operated a farm as a principal operator for more than 10 years, have at least one year of farming experience, and plan to substantially participate in farming the subject property. Legally incorporated farm businesses (corporation, partnership, proprietorship, LLC) are also eligible. The program addresses barriers such as high farmland costs and limited access to financial capital. Available statewide, including Washington County and the five Southern Maryland counties served through SMADC.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment to purchase farmland between 10 and 49 acres, in exchange for a permanent agricultural conservation easement. Includes a land preservation component. Funds help farmer meet equity contribution requirements for commercial lender financing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Prospective property must be eligible for the program — applicants must contact the county agricultural preservation program office in the county where the farmland is located at least one month before submitting an application to confirm eligibility. Preference given to properties in Priority Preservation Areas and Rural Legacy Areas. Property must meet county planning/zoning consistency requirements and tier map considerations under Senate Bill 236.

At least 90% of acres must be cropland or forage land

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the county agricultural preservation program office in the county where the farmland is located at least one month before the application deadline to confirm property eligibility. Ensure required seller paperwork (Form 1 - Property Seller's Information Form) reaches the county office at least 30 days in advance. Submit a competitive application (multi-form submission including seller application, property information, county submission, and commercial lender form) including a business plan and borrower financial information to the MARBIDCO office in Annapolis by 4:00 p.m. on the last business day of each month. The county Program Administrator reviews and affirms completeness. MARBIDCO's Review Committee ranks applications and makes recommendations to the MARBIDCO Board of Directors. Work with a commercial or farm credit lender for down payment funding. Contact Allison Roe (aroe@marbidco.org, 410-267-6807) for further information. Washington County applicants may also contact the County's Department of Planning & Zoning at planningzoning@washco-md.net or 240-313-2430.

structured_extraction.program_name: Southern Maryland Revolving Loan Fund for Agriculture
structured_extraction.program_description: A subsidized low-cost loan program for farmers in Southern Maryland who need financing for agricultural projects that may not qualify for traditional commercial loans. Loan amounts range from $10,000 to $20,000 at a 4.50% interest rate with no collateral security pledge required. Borrowers in good standing may have approximately 20-25% of their loan forgiven at the end of the loan term by foregoing the final quarter of amortizing payments.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Subsidized low-cost loans ranging from $10,000 to $20,000 at a 4.50% interest rate. No collateral security pledge required. Interest-only periods range from 3-18 months depending on commodity type, followed by amortization periods of 1-4 years. No loan origination fee (paid by SMADC on the borrower's behalf). Personal guarantee required for business entity borrowers; minimum credit score of 620. Borrowers in good standing may have approximately 20-25% of the loan forgiven at the end of the term (final quarter of amortizing payments foregone).

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase livestock or enhance herds/flocks; incubate or expand small fruits and hops production; upgrade facilities for GAP and FSMA compliance; shellfish aquaculture foundation development; purchase equipment for on-farm value-added production; equine farm industry foundation development and expansion; veterinary, medicine, and breeding costs; miscellaneous farm/business expenses.

Minimum credit score of 620

Project must be for an eligible agricultural purpose

Completed applications are processed as received and can be mailed to MARBIDCO Loan Programs, 1410 Forest Drive, Suite 21, Annapolis, MD 21403, or emailed to info@marbidco.org. Download the application from the program page.

structured_extraction.program_name: Upper Shore Regional Council Farm Incentive Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: A partnership between the Upper Shore Regional Council (USRC) and MARBIDCO that provides a 5% equity contribution toward financing projects funded by MARBIDCO loans. The fund is designed to help farmers in Cecil, Kent, and Queen Anne's counties meet down-payment (equity) requirements of lenders, improving the credit quality of their loan applications. It is an ongoing grant program available to farm residents in Maryland's Upper Shore region.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A 5% equity contribution toward the hard costs of a project financed through a MARBIDCO loan. For most MARBIDCO loan programs, the grant is the lesser of 5% of hard project costs or $5,000. For the Maryland Resource-Based Industry Financing Fund (MRBIFF), the grant is the lesser of 5% of hard project costs or $15,000.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers located in Cecil, Kent, and Queen Anne's counties on Maryland's Upper Shore who are seeking a MARBIDCO loan.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Equity contribution (down payment) toward the hard costs of an agricultural or resource-based industry project financed through a MARBIDCO loan program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only to farmers in Cecil, Kent, and Queen Anne's counties (Upper Shore region of Maryland).
requirements_list: Applicant must be a farmer located in Cecil, Kent, or Queen Anne's County
Must apply for and meet eligibility criteria for a qualifying MARBIDCO loan program
Must meet MARBIDCO's underwriting criteria for the applicable loan program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants follow the regular MARBIDCO application process for the specific loan program they are applying under. Upper Shore applicants must meet MARBIDCO's underwriting criteria for the chosen loan program.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Capital Enterprises (MCE) provides small business loans to help for-profit business owners in MCE's service area start, operate, or expand their businesses. Loans range from $500 to $5,000 and are available to for-profit micro businesses with 10 or fewer employees located in Maryland's Eastern Shore counties or in Baltimore City, Anne Arundel County, and Baltimore County. The program provides financing for equipment, supplies, working capital, and vehicles, along with mandatory business counseling and periodic site visits. structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Capital Enterprises Business Loans and Microlending Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Capital Enterprises (MCE) is a nonprofit organization that provides microloans and small business loans to entrepreneurs who cannot qualify for traditional bank financing, including people who are unemployed, have limited credit history, lack collateral, or are starting a new business. MCE serves for-profit micro businesses located on Maryland's Eastern Shore (Caroline, Dorchester, Kent, Queen Anne's, Somerset, Talbot, Wicomico, and Worcester counties) as well as Baltimore County, Baltimore City, and Anne Arundel County. The program targets businesses with 10 or fewer employees that have been unable to obtain financing through traditional lenders. Loans range from $5,000 to $35,000 for new businesses and from $35,001 to $100,000 for expansion, with terms up to 10 years and interest rates starting at 6%. MCE is certified as an SBA, USDA, and CDFI (Community Development Financial Institution) Intermediary Lender, making it a federally recognized nonprofit lender focused on underserved borrowers. In addition to lending, MCE provides counseling, support, training, and management assistance for small businesses including startups and businesses seeking to expand.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans from $5,000 to $35,000 for new businesses and from $35,001 to $100,000 for expansion. Loan terms up to 10 years. Interest rate starts at 6%, determined by loan committee based on business plan quality, credit history, and collateral. Upfront application cost is $125 ($100 application fee plus $25 credit report fee per applicant). Additional closing fees include a 1% underwriting fee and a legal reserve fee ranging from $250 to $1,500 depending on loan amount. Monthly payments are automatically debited; choosing not to use auto-debit increases the interest rate by 2%. MCE also provides counseling, training, and management support alongside loans. Program is open to startups, self-employed individuals, and expanding businesses.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit micro businesses and self-employed individuals with 10 or fewer employees located on Maryland's Eastern Shore or in Baltimore County, Baltimore City, or Anne Arundel County that have been unable to obtain traditional bank financing. Also open to startup entrepreneurs with limited credit or lack of collateral.

MCE is the only micro-enterprise organization in Maryland certified as an SBA, USDA, and CDFI Intermediary Lender.

Pay the $125 application fee ($100 application fee plus $25 credit report fee per applicant). The Loan Committee reviews the application and may approve, adjust terms, or deny the request. Upon approval, closing fees are collected and loan funds are disbursed. MCE provides counseling and training alongside the loan application process.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Capital Enterprises Women's Business Center Mentoring, Education, and Free Business Training Webinars
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Capital Enterprises (MCE) offers mentoring and education programs for entrepreneurs and small business owners through its Women's Business Center (WBC). MCE connects local entrepreneurs as mentors for aspiring business owners, providing assistance in day-to-day operations or in specific business areas. The WBC offers free online business training webinars, workshops, and educational resources on an ongoing basis through an external online portal (mced-online.org), as well as scheduled no-charge webinar series. Topics covered include SBA programs and services, starting a business in Maryland, federal contracting through SAM.gov, MBE/DBE/SBE certification, business plan writing, cash flow projections, Instagram/social media marketing, SBA financing options, crowdfunding, government contracting (including WOSB certification), networking, small business finance, financial fundamentals, and resources for women- and veteran-owned businesses. Additional educational resources include classes, guest speakers, and other learning formats. In-person one-on-one consulting sessions are also available in Easton (Talbot County) and Cambridge (Dorchester County), MD. Sessions are designed for entrepreneurs, prospective business owners, and small business owners across Maryland and surrounding regions, including those from underserved communities, women-owned businesses, veteran-owned businesses, and nonprofits. All webinars are held online and require advance registration. Sessions are offered on a recurring monthly schedule throughout the year.

In-person one-on-one consulting sessions are also available in Easton and Cambridge, MD. Additional educational offerings include classes, guest speakers, and other learning resources. All scheduled webinar sessions require advance registration; participants receive an access link upon registration. Sessions are offered on a recurring monthly schedule throughout the year.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Capital Enterprises (MCE) provides small business loans to start-up for-profit businesses in its service area. The program aims to help new businesses open their doors, grow, and succeed by providing financing along with business training and mentoring support. Funds can be used for almost anything needed to start and run a business, including machinery and equipment, furniture and fixtures, supplies, materials and inventory, working capital, and vehicle purchases for business use.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans ranging from $5,000 to $35,000 with repayment terms up to 10 years and interest rates between 6% and 12%. Fees include a 1% closing fee, a legal reserve fee of $250–$1,500, a $100 non-refundable application fee, and a $25 non-refundable credit report fee per applicant. No early repayment penalties. Security (collateral) may be required up to the full loan amount. MCE also provides business training and mentoring support.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Start-up for-profit business owners with 10 or fewer employees who have been unable to obtain financing through a traditional lender or bank, located within MCE's service area in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Machinery and equipment, furniture and fixtures, supplies, materials and inventory, working capital, and vehicle purchases for business use. Funds can be used for almost anything needed to start and operate a business.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to businesses located in Maryland's Eastern Shore counties (Wicomico, Worcester, Somerset, Dorchester, Talbot, Caroline, Queen Anne's, and Kent), Cecil County, and the Central Maryland counties of Baltimore City, Anne Arundel, Baltimore, Harford, and Calvert.
requirements_list: Start-up for-profit business with 10 or fewer employees
Has attempted to obtain a loan from a traditional lender or bank
Located within MCE's service area
Must have a clearly established business idea and business plan
Ability to create full-time and/or part-time employment for low-to-moderate income residents
Must be a U.S. citizen or legal alien
Must demonstrate ability to repay the loan
Must have reasonable credit history and payment records
Applicant must be a sole proprietor, partnership, or corporation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Schedule an appointment with an MCE Loan Officer before submitting an application. The Loan Officer will review your paperwork, help prepare the Loan Application Packet, and present it to the Loan Committee. Allow up to one or two months to gather all required documentation. The loan decision is made on the day of the Loan Committee meeting. Closing takes place 2–4 weeks after approval, once all liens and title searches are completed.
