structured_extraction.program_description: The Bridge Finance Facility (BFF) is a financing program administered by the Maryland Clean Energy Center (MCEC) in partnership with the Maryland Energy Administration (MEA). It provides short-term bridge loans to solar and solar-plus-storage developers and project owners to cover pre-construction and early-construction costs, with a particular focus on accelerating the development of Maryland-sited solar photovoltaic (PV) projects that benefit low- and moderate-income (LMI) households. Eligible projects include community solar (front of the meter, at or below 2 MW AC) and affordable multifamily housing solar installations (behind the meter). The facility fills early-stage capital gaps for costs such as interconnection studies, engineering and design, permitting, and equipment deposits that traditional commercial lenders typically will not fund. Funds come from the State's Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF) Program and are subject to Maryland law and SEIF program requirements. Borrowers must meet specific legal and contractual requirements tied to the use of public funds. Solar-plus-storage projects are eligible; battery storage is not required.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MCEC provides short-term bridge loans typically ranging from $500,000 to $1,000,000, with a maximum of $1,500,000 per developer (aggregated across all accepted projects). The maximum initial interest rate in Round 1 is 7%, with the final rate fixed at approval and determined by project risk and impact (based on the SOFR rate plus a risk/impact spread). Preferred loan term is 12 months, with an optional 6-month extension. No origination or legal fees. Repayment is interest-only during the term, with principal due at maturity. Collateral includes a first-priority UCC lien and/or guaranty. Funds are disbursed in a single draw based on approved uses, documentation, and project milestones. Goal for the first round is to disburse funds by May 2026. Financing is designed to fill pre-construction and early-construction gaps that often delay otherwise viable clean energy projects. Funds cannot be used for general operational costs.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: February 13, 2026 (Round 1); the intake period for Round 1 has ended — subscribe for updates on future application windows.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private and nonprofit solar developers, project special purpose entities (SPEs), affordable housing owners or affiliates, and mission-driven organizations developing Maryland-sited solar or solar-plus-storage projects that serve low- and moderate-income (LMI) households. Out-of-state developers are eligible if the project is located in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eligible uses include: utility interconnection applications, studies, and deposits; engineering and system design; permitting and related fees; equipment deposits and procurement; site preparation and EPC (engineering, procurement, and construction) mobilization; and initial construction and commissioning-related costs, including early construction and equipment procurement costs once construction financing is identified. Funds may not be used for long-term operating expenses or general operational costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located (sited) in Maryland. Applicants may be based outside Maryland. Funds are subject to Maryland law and SEIF program requirements.
requirements_list: Project must be a solar PV or solar-plus-storage installation sited in Maryland
Project size must be at or below 2 MW AC (for community solar front-of-meter projects)
Project must be a community solar project (front of the meter) or an affordable multifamily housing solar installation (rooftop, carport, or behind the meter)
At least 51% (more than 50%) of total project energy or financial benefits must serve LMI households (annual income at or below 150% of the applicable Area Median Income)
Projects must reduce energy burdens for LMI households by at least 20%
Solar-plus-storage is eligible; battery storage is not required
Applicants must demonstrate site control or a credible path to site control (lease, option, or letter of intent)
Applicant must demonstrate a credible plan for repaying (taking out) the BFF loan
Eligible borrower types include corporate entities, special purpose entities (SPEs), nonprofits, and multifamily housing cooperatives that own or control Maryland-sited solar PV project assets
Must qualify as a 'qualified business' under Maryland law
Must comply with all federal, Maryland, and local laws including taxation and regulatory requirements
Each project must be submitted as a separate application
Must provide closing deliveries: certificate of secretary with corporate approvals, good standing certificates for Maryland and state of formation, and sufficient insurance coverage
Must submit periodic reporting on use of financial assistance
Financial assistance may not be used for general operational costs
Must agree that MCEC does not consent to courts outside Maryland, binding arbitration, or laws of another state that would implicate sovereign immunity
Prior written consent of MCEC required before amending, waiving, or deleting Maryland-specific contractual provisions

Required documents include: site control documentation, interconnection status evidence, project site map, construction timeline, subscriber acquisition plan (community solar), affordable housing status evidence (multifamily), 2 years of business tax returns, 3 years of financial statements, preliminary EPC scope or budget, project-level pro forma, financial projections, capital stack summary, sources and uses, articles of organization, operating agreement, W-9, company bio, and employee count
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Submit a BFF Intake online application during the open application window (Round 1: February 3–13, 2026). 2. After submission, applicants receive a link to upload required supporting documents to MCEC's OneHub document platform. 3. MCEC conducts eligibility and risk/impact screening and may request additional information or invite the project to the next stage of review. 4. Selected projects undergo due diligence and underwriting. 5. Projects proceed through the review and approval pathway, including MCEC Board of Directors approval. 6. Legal documentation is finalized and executed. 7. Following closing, borrowers request funds via an agreed draw structure. 8. Borrowers repay principal and interest per agreed terms. Applicants should also review the BFF Credit Policy and Manual for full requirements. Funding is subject to underwriting, approvals, and capital availability.

structured_extraction.program_name: Charging and Fueling Infrastructure (CFI) Discretionary Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program administered by the U.S. Department of Transportation/FHWA through the Maryland Clean Energy Center (MCEC) and its partners. The program provides discretionary grant funding to install electric vehicle (EV) charging stations along Alternative Fuel Corridors and in low-to-moderate income communities across Maryland, with a goal of installing 120 EV charging stations statewide. Through CFI, public and private partners collaborate via the Maryland Equitable Charging Infrastructure Partnership (MECIP) to expand equitable charging infrastructure, with a focus on Justice40 communities. The program also invests in innovative workforce development related to EV charging infrastructure.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of electric vehicle (EV) charging stations along Alternative Fuel Corridors and in low-to-moderate income communities, as well as workforce development related to EV charging infrastructure.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland, with a focus on Alternative Fuel Corridors, low-to-moderate income communities, and Justice40 communities.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Check back soon for updates on the application process.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Climate Catalytic Capital (C3) Fund was established by the Climate Solutions Now Act of 2022 to increase implementation of clean energy measures and technologies that reduce greenhouse gas emissions and mitigate climate change across Maryland. The fund supports projects, companies, and technologies at all scales and is designed to be leveraged with additional private capital. At least 40% of the fund's investments must assist low-income households and communities across Maryland. A total of $15 million was committed over three fiscal years beginning in FY2024. The fund manages multiple investment vehicles including a Revolving Loan Fund, Block Grant Program, Equity Investment Fund, and Capacity Building Program. The fund may include state-appropriated money, private contributions, federal grants, and other sources.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The fund provides multiple forms of financing for clean energy projects, companies, and technologies, leveraged with additional private capital. A total of $15 million was committed over three fiscal years beginning in FY2024. No more than 5% may be used for administrative purposes. Specific mechanisms include: (1) Revolving Loan Fund — debt financing including rate subsidies, loss reserves, gap financing, and patient capital for programs in all sectors including low-to-moderate income households; (2) Block Grant Program — grants for eligible projects and programs, focusing on local government and community organizations, including matching and reimbursable grants for planning and development; (3) Equity Investment Fund — direct and equity-linked investments generating revenue/income/profit, supporting technology startup and advancement; (4) Capacity Building Program — training, technical assistance, and enabling activities; (5) MDPACE — tax lien collateralized loans for energy efficiency, EV charging, stormwater management, and resiliency; (6) Maryland Clean Energy Capital Program (MCAP) — bond financing for projects exceeding $5M in value. Applications are due by the 15th of each month, with awards made approximately 60 days thereafter. Funds cannot be used to install new fossil fuel equipment or improve the efficiency of existing fossil fuel equipment.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications due by the 15th of each month; awards made approximately 60 days thereafter
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland citizens, businesses, nonprofits, municipalities, institutions, and individuals seeking funding for clean energy and greenhouse gas reduction projects, with priority for low-income households and communities (census tracts with average median income at or below 80% of state average median income).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Climate mitigation and GHG reduction; renewable energy generation, transmission, and distribution; building electrification and weatherization; clean transportation adoption and fleet electrification; energy efficiency improvements in buildings; clean energy generation and storage; weatherization for low-to-moderate-income households; community-scale resilience infrastructure; advanced clean energy technology deployment; biomass energy; waste management; agriculture and forestry; job creation and workforce development; and a Maryland Green Bond Program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Low-to-moderate income communities are prioritized before September 30 of each fiscal year; other qualified projects are considered after September 30.
requirements_list: Investment must measurably reduce greenhouse gas emissions or mitigate climate change effects
At least 40% of fund investments must assist low-income households and communities
Cannot be used to install new fossil fuel equipment or improve efficiency of existing fossil fuel equipment

Projects must demonstrate: proposer eligibility and qualifications; financial feasibility; GHG/climate vulnerability reductions; cost-effectiveness; technological viability; job creation potential; alignment with C3 Fund statutory purposes
Annual certified financial statements from CFO or authorized representative required
Annual reports including construction status, financial statements of C3 Funds spent, operations summary, and other requested information
Notification of Committee if events may delay or materially impair project objectives
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are due by the 15th of each month, with awards made approximately 60 days thereafter. Low-to-moderate income communities are prioritized before September 30 of each fiscal year; other qualified projects are considered after September 30. Contact MCEC with questions.

structured_extraction.program_name: Climate Technology Founders Fund (CTFF) – MEIA Phase 3
structured_extraction.program_description: The Climate Technology Founders Fund (CTFF), established through Senate Bill 0960 and administered by the Maryland Clean Energy Center under the MEIA program, provides direct equity investment to climate tech startup teams in Maryland. The fund targets founders who have proven their technology and are ready to raise capital (Technology Readiness Level 4–7), investing $50,000 to $100,000 per team with a matching requirement — founders must raise external capital or invest personal funds alongside the MEIA investment. The fund takes a lead investor role, setting deal documents and conducting due diligence to help catalyze market growth. It supports a diverse range of founders, with priority given to small, minority-owned, women-owned, and veteran-owned businesses whose core mission is developing climate technology and emission-reducing solutions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Direct equity investment of $50,000 to $100,000 per team. A matching requirement applies — founders must raise external capital or invest personal funds alongside the MEIA investment. The fund takes a lead investor role, setting deal documents and conducting due diligence. Additional grant funding may support emission-reducing technology projects.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland-based climate tech startup teams at Technology Readiness Level (TRL) 4–7 that are ready to fundraise for a Pre-seed or Seed round. Emphasis on supporting diverse founders including small, minority-owned, women-owned, and veteran-owned businesses working on climate change and emission-reduction solutions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital to advance climate technology companies to the next stage (demonstration or deployment); funding emission-reducing technology projects; building and growing climate tech companies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available exclusively to Maryland-based ventures and teams.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland-based venture or team
Core mission must be developing climate technology or emission-reducing solutions
Technology Readiness Level (TRL) 4–7
Ready to fundraise for a Pre-seed or Seed round
Must meet matching requirement by raising external capital or investing personal funds
Must be an entrepreneur or founder focused on climate change solutions
Priority given to small, minority-owned, women-owned, and veteran-owned businesses

structured_extraction.program_name: MCEC Clean Energy Advantage (CEA) Loan Pilot Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Clean Energy Advantage (CEA) Loan Pilot Program, offered by the Maryland Clean Energy Center, provides Maryland homeowners a convenient and affordable financing option for residential energy efficiency and clean energy improvements. Borrowers receive a 0% APR for the first 24 months, after which a below-market interest rate (50% below market average) applies. Eligible improvements include air conditioning, heating systems (including heat pumps), insulation, windows, and other energy-saving upgrades. Loan amounts range from $3,000 to $50,000 with flexible terms of 3, 5, 7, or 10 years. Loans must be combined with utility rebates and used with an approved contractor. The program is available to Maryland residents served by participating utilities including BGE, SMECO, Potomac Edison, Delmarva Power, Pepco (excluding Montgomery County), or Washington Gas.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 0% APR loan for the first 24 months for residential energy efficiency and clean energy improvements. After 24 months, a below-market interest rate applies (50% below market average). Loan amounts range from $3,000 to $50,000 with flexible terms of 3, 5, 7, or 10 years. Loans must be combined with utility rebates and used with an approved contractor. Available to all Maryland homeowners regardless of income level. Visit cealoan.org for specific terms and to apply.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residential property owners and homeowners seeking financing for energy efficiency or clean energy improvements, particularly those served by BGE, SMECO, Potomac Edison, Delmarva Power, Pepco (excluding Montgomery County), or Washington Gas, at all income levels.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Residential energy efficiency and clean energy improvements including air conditioning, heating systems (including heat pumps), insulation, windows, and other energy-saving upgrades to reduce energy bills and improve home comfort.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland, with a focus on residents served by BGE, SMECO, Potomac Edison, Delmarva Power, Pepco (excluding Montgomery County), or Washington Gas.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident
Must be a homeowner in Maryland
Must be served by BGE, SMECO, Potomac Edison, Delmarva Power, Pepco (excluding Montgomery County), or Washington Gas
Must use an approved contractor
Must participate in your utility's rebate program (Home Performance with ENERGY STAR, Home Energy Improvement Program, or HVAC rebate program)
Credit score as low as 580 may qualify, subject to underwriting guidelines
Maximum of $50,000 in financing per installation address
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Find your utility, select a participating contractor from the CEA website, contact the contractor to discuss eligible energy improvements, and apply through the utility's rebate program alongside the CEA loan application at cealoan.org.

structured_extraction.program_description: MEIA's Launchpad program helps create new climate tech companies and supports them through their early startup journey. It targets technologies at Technology Readiness Levels (TRL) 3, 4, and 5, engaging founders and researchers with high-potential innovations. Over 4–6 months, startup teams conduct customer discovery, develop a business model canvas, and create a commercialization plan and investor-ready pitch deck. MEIA recruits two Energy Executives per team to lead commercialization planning.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Hands-on direct MEIA support, Energy Executive in Residence (EEIR) engagement, and services support. Provides a $10,000 budget with the opportunity to apply for an additional $5,000. Program runs over a 6-month timeline.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Founders and researchers with climate tech innovations at TRL 3–5 who want to commercialize their technology and start a company.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Commercialization activities including customer discovery, business model development, and pitch deck creation.
requirements_list: Have a working technology, potentially with prior grant funding (MEII, SBIR, or other)
Interested in commercializing technology into a new venture
Technology at TRL Level 3–4
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the online Airtable form linked on the program page.

It offers capital-raising workshops, one-on-one investment coaching, and investor engagement opportunities. The program is a collaboration with the Maryland Department of Commerce and emphasizes recruiting startups with at least 40% underrepresented founders, including women, minorities, and veterans.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: An 8-month program (October 2025 to April 2026) providing weekly capital-raising webinars and panels, personalized one-on-one coaching on pitch decks, data rooms and outreach campaigns, and facilitated introductions and pitch sessions with climate-focused investors.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland-based climate tech startups that are currently ready to raise private capital and have committed founders focused on fundraising. Priority given to startups with at least 40% underrepresented founders (women, minorities, veterans).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Technical assistance to prepare for investment fundraising — not a direct funding award.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Maryland-based climate tech startup.

Currently ready to raise private capital
Committed founders actively pursuing fundraising
Priority given to startups with at least 40% underrepresented founders (women, minorities, or veterans)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: No separate application process described on the page. Program runs October 2025 to April 2026.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland C-PACE (Commercial Property Assessed Clean Energy) Program / MDPACE
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Clean Energy Center (MCEC) administers Maryland's C-PACE program, known as MDPACE, a statewide Commercial Property Assessed Clean Energy financing tool for energy and/or water efficiency, renewable energy, resiliency, or environmental remediation measures in commercial buildings. Property owners can fund improvements repaid through a long-term property assessment (surcharge) tied to the commercial property tax bill, which transfers to new owners if the property is sold, and financing costs may be passed to tenants in some cases. The program provides low-cost, standardized financing services to property owners, contractors, capital providers, and local governments across Maryland. Repayment terms typically extend 10–35 years (capped at 35 years based on weighted average equipment useful life), with underwriting based on the underlying building value rather than the owner's credit rating, making it accessible to borrowers without investment-grade credit. Repayment is collected through annual or semi-annual surcharges added to the property's tax bill, and borrowers can be cash-flow positive from day one. Interest can be capitalized to defer initial payments. The financing does not appear on the owner's balance sheet as traditional debt and can help owners realize tax credits such as the solar Investment Tax Credit (ITC) and accelerated depreciation benefits (MACRS). Counties must opt in to participate by passing a local ordinance and signing a Locality Agreement with MCEC. The program is available in Maryland counties that have enacted C-PACE-enabling legislation (19 counties to date). Montgomery County and Prince George's County administer their own independent programs; all other participating counties are served through MDPACE managed by MCEC. Eligible property types include office, retail, hospitality, multifamily (more than 4 units), senior housing, assisted living, healthcare, faith-based, agricultural, industrial, warehouse, self-storage, nonprofit, and specialty use. Lenders and financial institutions can register as approved MDPACE Capital Providers to offer C-PACE loans. County governments can opt into the program by passing a local ordinance, after which MCEC administers the entire C-PACE program at no cost to the county government. The program provides 100% up-front capital with no upfront cost to the property owner, with a minimum project size of $50,000 and example project sizes ranging from $134,000 to $13,100,000. The program is sponsored by MCEC and administered by Abacus Property Solutions, LLC. The Maryland Energy Administration also provides resources related to C-PACE financing.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: C-PACE financing provides 100% up-front private capital (minimum project size $50,000; no maximum threshold) for commercial property owners to fund energy efficiency, water efficiency, renewable energy, resiliency, or environmental remediation improvements with no upfront cost or down payment required. Repayment is made through a long-term surcharge (property assessment) on the property tax bill — collected annually or semi-annually — that transfers with the property upon sale, with terms tied to the weighted average equipment useful life (capped at 35 years). Underwriting is based on the underlying building value rather than the owner's credit rating, making it accessible to borrowers with non-investment grade credit, and borrowers can be cash-flow positive from day one. The surcharge constitutes a first and prior lien against the property. Interest can be capitalized to defer initial payments. The financing does not appear on the owner's balance sheet as traditional debt and can help owners realize tax credits such as the solar Investment Tax Credit (ITC) and accelerated depreciation benefits (MACRS). The owner can sell the property, treat expenses as operational, and pass costs to tenants. Eligible costs include hard costs (materials, labor, overhead), ancillary costs (roof/electrical upgrades necessary for installation), and soft costs (project management, closing fees, legal services, engineering, permits, title reports, appraisals, capitalized interest). Example project sizes range from $134,000 to $13,100,000. Montgomery County and Prince George's County administer their own independent programs; all other eligible counties are served through MDPACE. Capital providers (lenders) can register to offer C-PACE loans. For county governments, MCEC and Abacus Property Solutions, LLC administer the full C-PACE program at no cost to the county, including intake, review, and approval of projects; training local contractors; registering private capital providers; providing annual program reports; establishing procedures to place C-PACE surcharges; and overseeing remittance of surcharge payments to capital providers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Commercial property owners, real estate investors, builders, contractors, capital providers, and local governments in Maryland counties that have enacted C-PACE-enabling legislation seeking to finance energy, water, resiliency, or environmental remediation improvements; building developers pursuing new construction or substantial renovation/adaptive reuse improvements; lenders and financial institutions interested in offering C-PACE financing products to commercial property owners; and county governments in Maryland that want to offer C-PACE financing to property owners in their jurisdiction. Nonprofits otherwise exempt from real estate taxation (if they have a real property tax identification number in SDAT) may also be eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency upgrades (lighting, HVAC, chillers, boilers, building envelope — windows, insulation, roofing), renewable energy (solar PV, wind, geothermal), environmental remediation (asbestos, mold, lead paint, lead pipe removal, Phase 1 and Phase 2 Environmental Site Assessments, indoor air and water quality improvements), water efficiency and conservation improvements, resiliency measures (stormwater management, flood mitigation, hurricane/wind shutters, EV charging stations, energy storage), heat recovery system upgrades, plumbing, elevators, water conservation systems, and other qualifying energy efficiency and sustainability improvements to existing commercial buildings or as part of new construction and substantial renovation/adaptive reuse projects. Eligible costs include hard costs (materials, labor, overhead for installation), ancillary costs (roof/electrical upgrades necessary for installation), and soft costs (project management, closing fees, legal services, engineering, permits, title reports, appraisals, capitalized interest, financing fees). Also includes program administration services for running a county-level C-PACE financing program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland counties that have enacted C-PACE-enabling legislation and signed a Locality Agreement with the Maryland Clean Energy Center (19 counties to date), including Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Calvert, Caroline, Carroll, Cecil, Charles, Dorchester, Frederick, Garrett, Harford, Howard, Kent, Queen Anne's, St. Mary's, Somerset, Talbot, Washington, Wicomico, and Worcester counties. Montgomery County and Prince George's County administer their own independent programs; all other eligible counties are served through MDPACE managed by MCEC. Carroll County and Dorchester County have additional requirements noted.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For Montgomery County, apply through the Montgomery County C-PACE program. For Prince George's County, apply through FSC First. For Garrett County or all other eligible counties, apply through MDPACE at the Maryland Clean Energy Center (mdcleanenergy.org) by contacting the MCEC Finance Team to discuss the project and get connected with a C-PACE lender, by emailing the MD Clean Energy finance team (building.decarbonization@maryland.gov), or by clicking the 'Apply Now' link on the program page. Property owners may also explore eligibility through the Maryland PACE website at md-pace.com. The application process involves execution of a C-PACE Surcharge Processing Agreement between parties, and a Technical Review Certificate is required. See Appendix D for the application checklist. Lenders and financial institutions seeking to become capital providers should email the MDPACE finance team to start the registration process and execute the Standard Offer agreement between the Capital Provider and MCEC. County governments should download the model ordinance from MCEC, pass it through the county's legislative body, then contact MCEC to enter into an administration agreement. Additional C-PACE financing resources are also available through the Maryland Energy Administration at http://energy.maryland.gov/business/pages/cpace-financing-resources.aspx.

structured_extraction.program_description: MCAP provides low-cost, long-term financing for large clean energy and energy efficiency projects in Maryland. It serves government agencies, educational and other institutions, nonprofit organizations, and businesses, connecting them with tax-exempt capital from private lenders and offering customized loan structures through both taxable and tax-exempt bond financing using MCEC's bond issuance capabilities. The Maryland Clean Energy Center (MCEC) structures financing arrangements, often using a Shared Energy Savings model or Energy Performance Contracts, to fund building upgrades that reduce energy use and costs. Projects are typically $5 million or more, with financing amounts in past projects ranging from approximately $3.4 million to $18.3 million, interest rates between 2.60% and 3.68%, and loan terms of 10 to 15 years. Eligible uses include energy efficiency measures, energy resiliency measures, mechanical equipment upgrades, combined heat and power systems, renewable energy production, microgrids, co-generation, building envelope updates, HVAC modernization, lighting upgrades, boiler and transformer replacement, water conservation systems, and ventilation controls.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-cost, long-term financing for clean energy and energy efficiency projects, typically $5 million or more. Past projects have ranged from approximately $3.4 million to $18.3 million, with interest rates between 2.60% and 3.68% and loan terms of 10 to 15 years. MCEC connects eligible applicants with tax-exempt financing from private lenders and may also enter into loan agreements to provide 100% of project capital. Customized finance structures are available, including Shared Energy Savings and Energy Performance Contract models to enable third-party project ownership, using MCEC's bond issuance capabilities for both taxable and tax-exempt financing.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Clean Energy Center (MCEC) Procurement and Technical Assistance
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Clean Energy Center (MCEC) offers a suite of procurement and technical assistance services to help organizations develop and execute clean energy and decarbonization projects across Maryland. Services include project design and feasibility assessments, regulatory navigation and permitting support, financing and grant funding matching (including grant writing assistance), measurement and verification of energy savings, and procurement services such as vendor identification and proposal evaluation. MCEC also supports decarbonization planning and energy performance contracting for all buildings in Maryland other than State agency facilities. MCEC acts as a neutral advisor to help clients—including commercial building owners and operators, non-profits, government entities, higher education institutions, and other organizations—at any stage of their clean energy project. Master Service Agreements are in place with multiple firms covering building efficiency, microgrids, and general clean energy services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MCEC provides procurement and technical assistance including project design and feasibility studies, regulatory guidance and permitting support, financing and grant funding matching (including grant writing assistance), measurement and verification of energy savings, decarbonization planning, energy performance contracting, and procurement services such as vendor identification and proposal evaluation. Master Service Agreements are in place with multiple firms covering building efficiency, microgrids, and general clean energy services. MCEC works with clients at any stage of their project to help plan and implement clean energy and building decarbonization projects for all non-State-agency buildings in Maryland.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations, commercial building owners and operators, non-profits, government entities, higher education institutions, universities, schools, hospitals, local governments, and private entities in Maryland seeking to develop or implement clean energy and decarbonization projects (excluding State agency facilities).

Participants work through entrepreneurial readiness, customer discovery, business model development, and commercialization planning, including identifying potential funding sources such as grants and equity investment. The program covers startup readiness and concludes with an in-person graduation. Graduates may continue into MEIA's Launchpad or Accelerator programs.

The program covers entrepreneurial readiness, customer discovery, business model development, financing, and commercialization planning. Participants receive mentorship from a chosen mentor over a 2-month, part-time commitment. It concludes with an in-person graduation. Graduates may continue into MEIA's Launchpad or Accelerator programs.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Energy Innovation Accelerator (MEIA) Energy-Executive-in-Residence (EEIR) Program (mentorship track)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Energy-Executive-in-Residence (EEIR) program connects entrepreneurs, current or retired executives, and others with early-stage clean energy technology startup teams. EEIRs are hired using each team's consulting budget to perform business activities, participate in strategic planning, and support customer discovery. The program lets EEIRs learn about startup team dynamics and work alongside inventors before a company is formally created. A separate unpaid mentor track is also available for people who want to give advice, open doors to industry connections and funding, and potentially serve on a startup's advisory board.

EEIRs perform needed business activities and participate in strategic planning; they do not receive equity. The amount of the consulting budget is not specified on this page.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Energy Innovation Accelerator (MEIA) – Pre-Accelerator, Launchpad, Climate Technology Founders Fund, and Phase 2: Prototyping & Manufacturing
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Energy Innovation Accelerator (MEIA) is a clean energy startup accelerator administered by the Maryland Clean Energy Center that supports and funds inventors, scientists, and startup founders building climate technologies. The program operates across multiple phases: a Pre-Accelerator, Launchpad, Climate Technology Founders Fund, and Phase 2 (Prototyping & Manufacturing / Manufacturing Accelerator). Together, these phases provide tailored resources and services to help innovators bring energy-reducing and greenhouse-gas-cutting technologies to market. The program accelerates the commercialization of advanced energy and climate technologies from Maryland's businesses, universities, and labs, connecting climate tech startups with experienced advisors, Energy-Executives-in-Residence, investors, and partners to help them become investible companies. The Climate Technology Founders Fund specifically targets Minority, Women, and Veteran-Owned Business (MWVOB) entrepreneurs, and a Climate Technology Fund to Support Diverse Founders was launched in early 2025. Phase 2 helps early-stage clean energy startups at Technology Readiness Level (TRL) 4-6 scale by supporting prototyping and manufacturing, with activities including customer development, introductions to investors, product development roadmapping, and manufacturing strategy. Program participation and financial support are subject to fund availability and approval by a Fund Oversight Committee. To date, the accelerator has facilitated over $90 million in funding, supported 120+ participants, and helped create more than 175 full and part-time jobs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A comprehensive multi-phase accelerator program offering tailored resources, business coaching, industry connections, co-founder and advisor matching (including Energy-Executives-in-Residence), ecosystem navigation support, and capital access. The program connects climate tech startups with experienced executives as mentors, facilitates introductions to investors and partners, and has supported 120+ participants in raising over $90 million in funding, helping create more than 175 jobs. The Climate Technology Founders Fund provides direct investments to qualifying Minority, Women, and Veteran-Owned Business (MWVOB) entrepreneurs working on clean energy and decarbonization solutions. Phase 2 provides up to $30,000 to advance prototyping and manufacturing, plus hands-on direct program support and connections to ecosystem partners, funders, and other State of Maryland startup services. Participating companies receive structured accelerator programming designed to help them create or expand Maryland-based clean energy businesses. Funding is subject to fund availability and approved by a Fund Oversight Committee.

Phase 2 specifically targets clean energy startups at Technology Readiness Level (TRL) 4-6 that are ready to develop a product for manufacturing and build initial operating facilities. Also advisors, executives, and partners who want to support clean energy startups.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Solar for All Program supports the expansion of solar programs for financially vulnerable, low-income, and underserved households across Maryland. Funded by a $62 million EPA grant award to the state as part of the federal $7 billion Solar for All initiative, it provides rebates and financing for rooftop solar on single-family homes, multifamily housing, and community solar projects. Administered by the Maryland Clean Energy Center, the program makes solar power accessible and affordable for under-resourced residents, helping them lower energy expenses and improve energy efficiency.

Backed by a $62 million EPA grant to Maryland as part of the federal $7 billion Solar for All program, funding is used to help financially vulnerable and under-resourced Maryland residents lower energy expenses and improve efficiency through expanded access to clean solar energy.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Clean Energy Center, in partnership with the Maryland Energy Administration (MEA), launched a $5 million revolving fund to accelerate the deployment of solar photovoltaic (PV) and energy storage systems across affordable housing communities in Maryland. The fund addresses financing gaps that delay or stall clean energy projects by covering early-stage development and installation costs. A $4.5 million revolving line of credit is administered through Enterprise Community Development, covering engineering and design, interconnection and commissioning, and procurement and construction costs. An additional $500,000 is dedicated to program administration and oversight. As loans are repaid, capital is recycled back into the program to support additional projects.

structured_extraction.program_name: USDA Rural Energy for America Program (REAP)
structured_extraction.program_description: The USDA Rural Energy for America Program (REAP) helps agricultural producers and rural small businesses reduce energy costs and consumption, and supports the integration of renewable energy technologies into their facilities. The program provides two types of funding: (1) Renewable Energy Systems and Energy Efficiency Improvements Assistance, and (2) Energy Audit and Renewable Energy Development Assistance Grants. Administered federally by the USDA and supported by the Maryland Clean Energy Center and Garrett County, eligible applicants can receive guaranteed loan financing and matching grants covering up to 25% of the cost of qualifying energy improvements, including renewable energy systems and energy efficiency upgrades.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Guaranteed loan financing and matching grants covering up to 25% of project costs for eligible energy improvements. Renewable energy system grants range from $2,500–$500,000; energy efficiency improvement grants from $1,500–$250,000; guaranteed loans from $5,000–$25 million; energy audit/development assistance grants up to $100,000 aggregate per recipient; maximum total grant assistance per entity is $750,000 per fiscal year. Eligible systems include wind, solar, renewable biomass (including anaerobic digesters), small hydro-electric, ocean, geothermal, or hydrogen derived from renewable resources.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: March 31, 2025 marked the final quarterly deadline for applications
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural producers who earn at least 51% of their income from farming or ranching, and privately owned for-profit small businesses located in rural areas or towns with populations of 50,000 or fewer, in Maryland. Eligible entities for energy audit and development assistance grants may also include units of State, Tribal, or local government, institutions of higher education, rural electric cooperatives, and public power entities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase or installation of renewable energy systems (wind, solar, renewable biomass, small hydro-electric, ocean, geothermal, or hydrogen derived from renewable resources), energy efficiency improvements to operations, energy audits, and renewable energy development assistance. The project's technology must be readily available for purchase.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be located in a rural area or town with a population of 50,000 people or less. Priority is given to rural areas with lowest incomes where at least 20% of the population lives in poverty per American Community Survey census tract data. Maryland farms and small businesses may also receive support through MCEC or Garrett County's community development office.
