structured_extraction.program_description: A Maryland Clean Energy Center program that helps facilities switch from fossil fuels to renewable thermal energy using locally sourced woody biomass (wood chips, pellets, and other forest byproducts). The program provides technical assistance, engineering analyses, supply chain support, and help applying for grants to install biomass heating systems. It also supports education, outreach, and advocacy for wood energy systems and economic development, raising public awareness about the benefits of biomass energy for forest health, rural economies, and clean energy goals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides technical assistance to help prospective users of wood energy apply for grants, including USFS Wood Innovations Grants. Services include USFS Wood Education and Resource Center (WERC) engineering and analysis, IMPLAN regional economic impact analyses, bid-ready system designs, wood supply chain development, connections to economic development partners and funding programs, and community education and outreach materials. Engineering analyses for thermal wood energy systems at state-owned facilities have already been completed. Additionally, grants and educational resources are provided to promote wood and biomass energy systems and support economic development in the wood energy sector.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Facilities, government entities, landowners, logging and forestry businesses, community economic leaders, and individuals interested in switching from fossil fuels to renewable thermal energy using woody biomass, as well as organizations interested in wood and biomass energy systems in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of thermal woody biomass energy systems; engineering and feasibility analyses; supply chain development; community outreach, education, and advocacy.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland, with a focus on rural counties that have large forest stands and high dependency on heating oil.
requirements_list: Facility should currently have little access to renewable energy
High dependency on heating oil preferred
Location near large forest stands with need for active forest management
Opportunity for employment within the community
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Send an email to MCEC expressing interest. MCEC will assist prospective users with grant applications and provide technical services to help facilities make the switch to woody biomass energy systems.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grants to increase resources and capacity for local Area Agencies on Aging, Senior Villages, and nonprofit organizations serving older Marylanders and their caregivers. The grants support high-quality services, social connection, and community engagement so older adults can live in their own homes and communities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MDOA awarded $261,173 to 11 organizations in FY26 grants to help older adults in Maryland live healthy, financially secure, purposeful, and socially connected lives in their own homes and communities. Individual awards in FY26 ranged from approximately $9,500 to $45,000.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local Area Agencies on Aging, Senior Villages, and nonprofit organizations serving older Marylanders and their caregivers
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Providing transportation, social programs, food delivery, care coordination, financial and housing counseling, caregiver support, accessibility improvements, and other services to help older adults age in place
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — Maryland
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local Area Agency on Aging, a Senior Village, or a nonprofit organization
Must serve older Marylanders and/or their caregivers
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the Grant Availability page at aging.maryland.gov/Pages/Grants.aspx for information on Aging-in-Place and other funding opportunities.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Housing/Healthy Aging Program (formerly Congregate Housing Services Program)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Aging contracts with housing and senior service provider organizations to operate a Community Housing/Healthy Aging program for eligible residents of designated buildings. The program provides services and supports that allow residents to live as independently as possible, including meals, housekeeping, medication management, and limited personal assistance with activities such as bathing, dressing, and laundry.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are awarded to housing and senior service provider organizations such as local housing authorities, nonprofit organizations, or housing management companies to operate Community Housing/Healthy Aging programs. In FY26, over $1.9 million was awarded to 10 organizations across Maryland, with individual awards ranging from approximately $48,000 to $527,000.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Housing and senior service provider organizations (local housing authorities, nonprofits, housing management companies) that serve low-income residents aged 62 and older who need assistance with activities of daily living.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding supports delivery of services such as meals, housekeeping, medication management, and limited personal assistance (bathing, dressing, laundry) to eligible residents in designated buildings.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Designated buildings in Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Montgomery, Prince George's, and Garrett counties are currently served.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a housing or senior service provider organization such as a local housing authority, nonprofit, or housing management company
Program must serve residents who are at least 62 years of age
Program must serve residents with low or no income
Program must serve residents who need assistance in one or more activities of daily living
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local Maryland Access Point for additional information on local housing programs by calling 1-844-MAP-LINK (1-844-627-5465).

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides nutritious meals at more than 250 community locations (meal sites) across Maryland, along with opportunities for social engagement, nutrition education, physical activity, and health screenings. The program helps older adults access free or low-cost meals through local partner sites statewide.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free or low-cost meals served at more than 250 community dining sites throughout Maryland, along with social and health-related programming including nutrition education, physical activity opportunities, and health screenings.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Older adults across Maryland seeking nutritious meals and social connection.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Access to nutritious congregate meals and participation in social, educational, and health programming at community meal sites.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at more than 250 locations statewide through local partners.
requirements_list: Must be an older adult
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Find a meal site near you using the Maryland Access Point search tool at https://search.marylandaccesspoint.211md.org/search?query=BD-5000.1500&query_type=taxonomy&query_label=Congregate%20Meals/Nutrition%20Sites&query_language=en or via the link on the program page.

structured_extraction.program_name: FY24 Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementia (ADRD) Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Aging awards grants to non-profit organizations to support home- and community-based services for people living with Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias (ADRD) and their caregivers. Funded activities include day center scholarships, dementia care training, transportation, companionship programs, intergenerational education initiatives, care coordination, and social support programs to maximize health and independence.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Nearly $134,000 in total grant funding was awarded across six non-profit organizations in FY24. Individual grants ranged from approximately $11,500 to $27,000. Funds support implementation of home- and community-based supportive services, care coordination, social support, day center scholarships, dementia care training, transportation, companionship programs, and intergenerational programming for individuals with ADRD and their caregivers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations providing services to individuals living with Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias (ADRD) and their caregivers in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home- and community-based supportive services, dementia care training, day program scholarships, transportation, companionship and home visits, intergenerational education programs, care coordination, and social support programs for people with ADRD and their caregivers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. FY24 awardees served areas including Worcester County, Kensington, Baltimore, Salisbury, Hagerstown, and Silver Spring.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a non-profit organization
Programs must support individuals experiencing ADRD and/or their caregivers
Services must be home- and community-based
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Not described on the program page. Contact Mark Tesoro at the Maryland Department of Aging for application information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Living Well Center of Excellence – Chronic Disease Self-Management Education Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: A two-year federal grant awarded to MAC Inc.'s Living Well Center of Excellence in Salisbury, Maryland to expand statewide coverage of evidence-based chronic disease self-management education and support programs. The grant supports licensing, training, technical assistance, and data management to help older adults and adults with disabilities better manage chronic conditions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A two-year grant totaling $733,698 awarded to MAC Inc. to provide statewide expansion of evidence-based self-management education programs, including licensing, training, technical assistance, and data management support.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Older adults and adults with disabilities with chronic conditions; aging network organizations and health care systems in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Licensing, training, technical assistance, and data management for evidence-based chronic disease self-management education programs; expanding statewide program capacity
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Durable Medical Equipment Re-Use Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Aging operates a statewide program that collects donated, gently used durable medical equipment (DME), sanitizes and refurbishes it, and provides it at no cost to Maryland residents who have an illness, injury, or disability, regardless of age. The program helps people maintain safety and mobility while avoiding more expensive levels of care. Equipment includes both basic items (canes, crutches, walkers, rollators, shower chairs, tub transfer benches, bedside commodes, toilet safety rails) and complex items (manual and power wheelchairs, transport wheelchairs, power scooters, home hospital beds, bed rails, mechanical lifts, knee scooters, overbed tables, and trapeze bars). Requests must be initiated by a licensed healthcare professional, and equipment is distributed by scheduled pick-up appointment at the program's Re-Use Center in Cheltenham, MD, with potential transport to satellite sites around the state for some items. Recipients keep the equipment permanently at no charge. When no longer needed, recipients are encouraged to donate it back for redistribution. Applications may be submitted online via Maryland OneStop or by hard copy mail, scanned email, or fax.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides durable medical equipment at no cost to eligible Maryland residents, subject to availability. Equipment is distributed through scheduled pick-up appointments at the program's Re-Use Center (11701 Crain Highway, Cheltenham, MD 20623), with transport to satellite sites around the state potentially available for some items. Delivery to the recipient's home is not available. Basic equipment includes canes, crutches, walkers, rollators, shower chairs, tub transfer benches, bedside commodes, and toilet safety rails. Complex equipment includes manual and power wheelchairs, transport wheelchairs, power scooters, home hospital beds, bed rails, mechanical lifts, knee scooters, overbed tables, and trapeze bars. Recipients keep the equipment permanently at no charge.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents of any age with an illness, injury, or medical condition who need durable medical equipment and have exhausted other means (insurance, Medicare, Medicaid) of obtaining it. Requests must be initiated by a licensed healthcare professional (PT, OT, MD, DO, PA, or CRNP). Requests for complex equipment such as power wheelchairs and power scooters must be completed by a Physical Therapist or Occupational Therapist only.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Obtaining free durable and home medical equipment such as canes, crutches, walkers, rollators, shower chairs, tub transfer benches, bedside commodes, toilet safety rails, manual and power wheelchairs, transport wheelchairs, power scooters, home hospital beds, bed rails, mechanical lifts, knee scooters, overbed tables, and trapeze bars for personal use by the beneficiary to support safety and mobility.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to all Maryland residents statewide. Beneficiary must be a Maryland resident. Pick-up must occur at the Re-Use Center in Cheltenham, MD (Prince George's County) or at satellite sites around the state when available, though the program serves the whole state.
requirements_list: Beneficiary must be a Maryland resident
Beneficiary must have an illness, injury, or disability requiring durable medical equipment
No age requirement
Individuals with insurance (Medicare, Medicaid, or private) must first attempt to obtain DME through their insurance provider
Request must be initiated by a licensed healthcare professional (PT, OT, MD, DO, PA, or CRNP)
Requests for power wheelchairs and power scooters must be completed by a Physical Therapist or Occupational Therapist only
A Complex Request Form (Parts A, B, and C) must be completed and submitted for complex DME items
Part A must be completed by the Requestor (the person requesting equipment — can be the user, a family member, caregiver, or trusted individual, but NOT the healthcare provider)
Parts B and C must be completed by a qualifying Healthcare Professional treating the beneficiary
The Requestor must sign the Liability Waiver and Release agreement in Part A, page 2
A formal prescription is not required — only the completed Request Form is needed
Completed Request Form must be submitted by mail, scanned email, or fax (cell phone or tablet photos of forms are not accepted — scanned documents only)
Equipment is subject to availability
Equipment must be picked up at the Re-Use Center or a satellite site; no home delivery is available
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Option 1 (Online): Visit Maryland OneStop, create an account, verify your email, and complete the online form. The healthcare provider portion (Parts B and C) can be completed online or via hard copy upload. Option 2 (Hard Copy): Download and print the applicable Request Form. Healthcare professional completes Parts B and C (with signature in black or blue ink). Patient or caregiver completes Part A and signs the Liability Waiver and Release Agreement. Submit the completed form by mail to Maryland Durable Medical Equipment Re-Use, 11701 Crain Highway, Cheltenham, MD 20623, or by scanned email to DME.MDOA@maryland.gov, or by fax. Program contacts the requestor by phone to confirm equipment availability. If equipment is in stock, a pick-up appointment is scheduled. Pick-up is by appointment only; delivery is not available. For more information, visit aging.maryland.gov/pages/DME.aspx or call 240-230-8000.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Durable Medical Equipment Re-Use Program – Basic DME
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides free, refurbished basic durable medical equipment (DME) to Maryland residents who need it. Equipment includes canes, crutches, walkers, rollators, shower chairs, tub transfer benches, bedside commodes, toilet safety rails, and bedrails. Recipients keep the equipment permanently and are encouraged to donate it back when no longer needed so it can be redistributed. Equipment is picked up by appointment at the Re-Use Center in Cheltenham, MD or at a satellite site nearest the recipient; delivery is not available.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free durable medical equipment (basic items such as canes, crutches, walkers, rollators, shower chairs, tub transfer benches, bedside commodes, toilet safety rails, and bedrails) is provided to eligible Maryland residents at no cost. Equipment is available for pickup by appointment at the Re-Use Center in Cheltenham, MD or at satellite sites around the state. Delivery is not available. Once equipment is provided, the recipient keeps it permanently.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents who need basic durable medical equipment such as mobility aids (canes, crutches, walkers, rollators), shower chairs, tub transfer benches, bedside commodes, toilet safety rails, and bedrails, and who have a healthcare professional who can complete part of the request form.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition of basic durable medical equipment including canes, crutches, walkers, rollators, shower chairs, tub transfer benches, bedside commodes, toilet safety rails, and bedrails for personal use.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Maryland residents statewide. Equipment can be picked up at the Re-Use Center in Cheltenham, MD (11701 Crain Highway, Cheltenham, MD 20623) or transported to a satellite site nearest the recipient.
requirements_list: Must complete the Basic DME Request Form (no formal prescription required)

Part C of the Request Form must be completed by a treating healthcare professional (Physician, Physical Therapist, Occupational Therapist, Physician's Assistant, or Certified Registered Nurse Practitioner)
Requestor must sign the Liability Waiver and Release agreement in Part A of the Request Form
Equipment must be picked up by appointment by the beneficiary or a designated trusted individual; delivery is not available
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Option 1 (Online): Submit the request form through Maryland OneStop at onestop.md.gov by creating an account, verifying your email, and submitting the online form. Option 2 (Mail or Email): Download the Basic DME Request Form, complete all required fields in blue or black ink, and submit by mail to Maryland Durable Medical Equipment Re-Use, 11701 Crain Highway, Cheltenham, MD 20623, or scan and email the completed form to DME.MDOA@maryland.gov. After the form is processed, staff will contact the requestor to confirm equipment availability and schedule a pickup appointment.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program helps family members and informal caregivers care for their loved ones at home for as long as possible. It provides a coordinated set of support services designed to reduce caregiver stress, depression, and anxiety, and to help caregivers provide care longer — potentially avoiding or delaying the need for costly nursing home or institutional care.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers five types of caregiver services delivered through a local network of Area Agencies on Aging. Specific service types and benefit amounts are not detailed on this page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Family members and informal caregivers (age 18+) caring for older adults (60+), individuals of any age with Alzheimer's disease or related disorders, and grandparents or relatives (55+) caring for children under 18 or adults ages 18–59 with disabilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supports caregivers in providing care at home through a coordinated array of community-based services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through local Area Agencies on Aging across Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be an adult family member or informal caregiver age 18 or older caring for someone age 60 or older
OR an adult caregiver age 18 or older caring for someone of any age with Alzheimer's disease or related disorders
OR a grandparent or other relative (not a parent) age 55 or older caring for a child under 18
OR a grandparent or other relative (not a parent) age 55 or older caring for an adult age 18–59 with a disability
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local Area Agency on Aging to access services.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland High-Tech Assistive Technology Reuse (MATR) Center
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides free high-tech assistive technology devices to Maryland residents with disabilities. Devices include speech communication tools, eye-gaze systems, video magnifiers, adapted computer accessories, and iDevices, along with training and support to help users integrate them into daily life.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free high-tech assistive technology devices provided to Maryland residents with disabilities, along with training and support to help integrate technology into daily life.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents with disabilities who need high-tech assistive technology devices.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Obtaining high-tech assistive technology such as speech communication devices, eye-gaze systems, magnifiers, adapted keyboards, and personal sound amplifiers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident
Must have a disability
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online using the MATR application form. For more information, visit the MATR Center page or contact Shawn Bateman at 410-554-9232 or MDTAP.AT-Reuse@maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland SMP is an anti-health care fraud program that increases Medicare and Medicaid beneficiary awareness of health insurance misuse and fraud. It trains senior volunteers to help Medicare and Medicaid clients recognize and report health care fraud, waste, abuse, or error. The program offers free, confidential counseling (in person or by phone), home visits for beneficiaries unable to travel, community educational meetings, and access to free My Health Care Trackers. Volunteers are matched to activities such as administering, distributing information, staffing exhibits, making presentations, counseling, and managing complex fraud-reporting interactions, with all volunteers completing Maryland SMP training before participation. The program is available statewide, including in Cecil County through the Aging & Disability Resource Center.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free, confidential assistance including individual counseling (in person or by phone), home visits for beneficiaries unable to travel, community educational meetings, and access to free My Health Care Trackers. Trained volunteers provide education and outreach to help Medicare and Medicaid beneficiaries recognize, understand, and report health insurance fraud, waste, abuse, or error, including assistance with understanding Medicare billing statements. Volunteers are matched to activities such as administering, distributing information, staffing exhibits, making presentations, counseling, and managing complex fraud-reporting interactions.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Medicare and Medicaid beneficiaries, their caregivers, families, and community members throughout Maryland; also open to volunteers who want to help fight health care fraud.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Education and counseling to help Medicare and Medicaid clients identify and report health care fraud, waste, abuse, or error, including assistance understanding Medicare bills.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in all Maryland counties, including Cecil County through the Aging & Disability Resource Center. County-specific counselors are listed with local phone numbers for each of Maryland's 24 jurisdictions.
requirements_list: Must be a Medicare or Medicaid beneficiary, caregiver, family member, or community member to receive services
Volunteers must complete Maryland SMP training
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your county's SMP counselor by phone for free and confidential assistance. Cecil County residents may also contact the Aging & Disability Resource Center. To become a volunteer or request My Health Care Trackers, call 877-808-2468.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland State Health Insurance Assistance Program (SHIP)
structured_extraction.program_description: SHIP is a free, unbiased, and confidential counseling and community education service that helps Medicare beneficiaries, their family members, and caregivers understand their healthcare options and rights. Federally funded, trained and certified staff and volunteer counselors provide one-on-one in-person and telephone guidance on Medicare enrollment, plan comparisons (including Medicare Advantage and Medigap), prescription drug coverage (Part D), long-term care insurance, financial assistance programs (including Medicare Savings Programs, Extra Help, QMB, and SLMB), billing and claims support, appeals, preventive services information, and health care fraud prevention (including through the Senior Medicare Patrol component). Available statewide in all 23 Maryland counties and Baltimore City, with dedicated county-level service points including Anne Arundel County, Howard County, and others. In Baltimore City, residents can call the Maryland Access Point (MAP) hotline at 410-396-CARE (2273) to connect with a local SHIP Counselor. In St. Mary's County, counselors are available at each senior activity center (Garvey, Northern, and Loffler). In Charles County, self-enrollment computer labs are also available at local libraries and senior centers during Open Enrollment. Howard County residents receive free one-on-one counseling from trained volunteers to understand Medicare options, compare plans, and navigate Medicare-related decisions. Community education presentations are also available. Services are offered year-round and during Open Enrollment periods.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free and confidential one-on-one counseling and education sessions available in-person or by phone. Services cover Medicare Parts A, B, C, and D; Medicare basics, enrollment, plan comparisons; prescription drug coverage (Part D); Medigap and Medicare Supplement options; Medicare Advantage; long-term care insurance; financial assistance programs (Medicare Savings Programs, Extra Help, QMB, SLMB); billing and claims support; appeals, denials, and grievances; preventive services information; health care fraud prevention (including Senior Medicare Patrol); referrals to other resources; and community education presentations. The QMB program pays full monthly Medicare premiums, co-pays, and deductibles for eligible Maryland residents. The SLMB program pays only the monthly Medicare Part B medical insurance premium for eligible individuals. In Baltimore City, call the MAP hotline at 410-396-CARE (2273). In Anne Arundel County, call (410) 222-4257 or email ship_program@aacounty.org. In St. Mary's County, appointments are available at senior activity centers (Garvey, Northern, and Loffler). In Charles County, self-enrollment computer labs are available at local libraries and senior centers during Open Enrollment. In Frederick County, contact the Division of Aging and Independence at 301-600-1234. In Prince George's County, sessions can be scheduled online via Calendly or by calling 301-265-8401 or 301-265-8450. In Charles County, contact the La Plata area at 301-609-5712, Waldorf area at 240-448-2816, or Western Charles County at 301-934-9305. In St. Mary's County, contact Melissa Craig at (301) 475-4200 ext. 1064. In Howard County, trained volunteer counselors provide free one-on-one counseling sessions. No cost to the beneficiary.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Medicare Open Enrollment: October 15 through December 7; program is available year-round
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents with Medicare or approaching Medicare eligibility, including those age 65 and older, individuals under 65 with qualifying disabilities, low-income individuals, caregivers, and family members of Medicare recipients who need help reviewing and choosing coverage options. Also available to Medicare-eligible individuals and their family members or caregivers in Baltimore City, Anne Arundel County, Howard County, and all other Maryland counties. QMB and SLMB programs are available to individuals and married couples receiving or who have applied for Medicare benefits who are Maryland residents and U.S. citizens or lawfully admitted aliens.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Counseling and education to help beneficiaries understand and enroll in Medicare, compare plans, access financial assistance programs like Medicare Savings Programs, Extra Help, QMB, and SLMB, navigate billing and appeals, address health care fraud issues, understand long-term care insurance options, resolve billing issues, denials, and grievances, and obtain referrals to other relevant resources. QMB program funds pay Medicare premiums, co-pays, and deductibles; SLMB program funds pay Medicare Part B premiums.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in all 23 Maryland counties and Baltimore City. Dedicated local SHIP offices serve Baltimore City (Maryland Access Point hotline: 410-396-2273), Anne Arundel County (410-222-4257), Frederick County (Division of Aging and Independence: 301-600-1234), Prince George's County (Aging and Disabilities Resource Center: 301-265-8401 or 301-265-8450), Charles County (La Plata area: 301-609-5712; Waldorf area: 240-448-2816; Western Charles County: 301-934-9305), Howard County (howardcountymd.gov/SHIP), and St. Mary's County (senior activity centers throughout the county), among others. QMB/SLMB applications are mailed to the local Department of Social Services in the applicant's county.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident
Must have Medicare or be approaching Medicare eligibility
Caregivers and family members of Medicare recipients are also eligible
Must be a Medicare beneficiary, family member, or caregiver
Income and asset guidelines apply for prescription drug and Medicare premium payment assistance programs (QMB/SLMB)
For QMB/SLMB: must be receiving or have applied for Medicare benefits
For QMB/SLMB: must be a U.S. citizen or lawfully admitted alien
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call (410) 767-1100 to connect with your local SHIP office, or contact the county-specific phone numbers listed in the SHIP Directory. Anne Arundel County residents may call (410) 222-4257 or email ship_program@aacounty.org to schedule a free one-on-one counseling session. Baltimore City residents may call the Maryland Access Point (MAP) hotline at 410-396-CARE (2273) to be connected with a local SHIP Counselor; SHIP staff are also available for in-person or virtual community outreach events. Frederick County residents may contact the Division of Aging and Independence by phone at 301-600-1234, Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m.–4:00 p.m. Prince George's County residents may schedule a counseling session online at the provided Calendly link or call 301-265-8401 or 301-265-8450 Monday through Friday, 8:30 am–5:00 pm. Charles County residents may call 301-609-5712 (La Plata), 240-448-2816 (Waldorf), or 301-934-9305 (Western Charles County), or attend a self-enrollment computer lab at a local library or senior center during Open Enrollment. St. Mary's County residents may contact Melissa Craig at (301) 475-4200 ext. 1064 or Melissa.Craig@stmaryscountymd.gov to schedule an appointment at a senior activity center. Howard County residents may visit howardcountymd.gov/SHIP for information on scheduling a counseling session with a trained volunteer. Applications for Medicare premium assistance programs (QMB/SLMB) are available at all senior activity centers and may be submitted to the local Department of Social Services. Cecil County residents may also contact the Aging & Disability Resource Center. Counselors provide free, confidential one-on-one assistance in-person or by phone.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grants to community-based organizations that provide programming, service coordination, and community support in neighborhoods where large numbers of low-income older adults live. The program addresses declining health, social isolation, financial hardship, and language barriers through three project types: Elder Abuse Prevention, Holocaust Survivors Program, and Traditional NORC.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MDOA awarded $1.3 million in state funds to 7 community-based organizations in FY26. Individual awards ranged from $75,000 to $325,000 to support programming, service coordination, and community support for older adults.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community-based organizations serving concentrated areas of low-income older adults in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Programming, service coordination, and community support including elder abuse prevention, support for Holocaust survivors, and aging-in-place services for low-income older adults
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — Maryland, targeting concentrated areas where low-income older adults face health, isolation, financial, or language challenges
requirements_list: Applicant must be a community-based organization
Must serve areas with concentrated populations of low-income older adults
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the Grant Availability page at aging.maryland.gov/Pages/Grants.aspx for information on funding opportunities.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal law-based program that funds a wide range of home- and community-based services for older adults across Maryland, including home-delivered and congregate meals, caregiver support, transportation, health and wellness programs, in-home personal care, long-term care ombudsman services, and protection against elder abuse.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Services funded by OAA include home-delivered and congregate meals (over 3 million meals per year), caregiver respite care and support, transportation to medical appointments and errands, in-home personal care (chores and daily living activities), senior center health promotion programs, and long-term care ombudsman visits to assisted living and nursing homes.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Older adults and people with disabilities in Maryland, as well as their caregivers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Nutrition services, caregiver support, transportation, in-home personal care, health and wellness programs, and long-term care complaint resolution.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland through local Area Agencies on Aging and community organizations.
requirements_list: Must be an older adult or person with a disability in Maryland
Services accessed through Maryland Access Point or local Area Agency on Aging
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Access services by visiting Maryland Access Point (marylandaccesspoint.211md.org) to find programs and services you may be eligible for.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free daily automated phone call or text message wellness check-in service for Maryland residents age 60 and older. Each day, an automated call or text is placed to the participant at a pre-selected time. If the participant does not answer after three attempts, a pre-selected alternate contact is called. If neither the participant nor the alternate responds, the local non-emergency service is notified. The program is designed to provide peace of mind to seniors living at home, particularly those who live alone. TTY is available, and the program operates every day of the year except six holidays.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free daily automated phone call or text message wellness check for enrolled participants. If the participant does not answer after three attempts, a pre-selected alternate contact is called. If neither responds, the local non-emergency service is contacted. TTY is available. The program operates every day of the year except six holidays.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents age 60 or older who have a landline or cell phone (TTY available), particularly those who live alone.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Daily automated wellness check-in and emergency notification service for older adults living at home.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to any Maryland resident age 60 or older, statewide.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident age 60 or older
Must have a landline or cell phone (TTY available)
Participant and alternates should not have automated call-blocking enabled, or should disable it for this program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online by clicking 'Register Now' on the program website, or call toll-free 1-866-502-0560 to request a paper application by mail. You may also contact the Maryland Department of Aging by phone at 410-767-1100 or 800-243-3425. After enrollment, information is verified through a test call to both the participant and alternate. A Welcome Packet with the start date is then mailed to the participant's home address.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Senior Care Program, administered statewide by the Maryland Department of Aging, provides case management and support services for people aged 65 and older who are frail, health-impaired, or at risk of being placed in a nursing home. The program screens and assesses older adults, conducts in-home evaluations, develops a person-centered care plan, and assigns a case manager to locate, arrange, and coordinate services to help seniors continue living at home and in their community. Gap-filling funds may be available to qualifying individuals to cover personal care, chores, medications, medical equipment and supplies, adult day care, respite care, home-delivered meals, transportation, and emergency response systems at no cost to the individual. In Frederick County, the program is also locally administered by the Frederick County Department of Aging as the Personal Care Program, which provides in-home aide services to adults aged 60 and older who need help with daily living activities such as bathing, dressing, and meal preparation, as well as chore or homemaker services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Case management services including in-home needs evaluation, screening, assessment, and ongoing care coordination delivered by local aging, health, and social services agencies. Gap-filling service dollars are available to qualifying individuals who meet financial and eligibility criteria to cover personal care, chores, medications, medical equipment and supplies, adult day care, respite care, home-delivered meals, transportation, and emergency response systems. In Frederick County, in-home aide services covering activities of daily living (bathing, dressing, meal preparation) and chore or homemaker services are also available. There is no cost to the individual.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents aged 65 or older who are frail, health-impaired, moderately or severely disabled, and at risk of nursing home or institutional placement. In Frederick County, residents aged 60 or older who need assistance with daily living activities are also eligible through the local Personal Care Program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Personal care, chores, medications, medical equipment and supplies, adult day care, respite care, home-delivered meals, transportation, emergency response systems, bathing assistance, dressing assistance, meal preparation, and other daily living support to help seniors remain at home.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through local aging, health, and social services agencies; applicants must live in the county where services are to be received. Also available locally in Frederick County through the Frederick County Department of Aging, Division of Aging and Independence.
requirements_list: Must be at least 65 years of age (60 years of age or older for Frederick County Personal Care Program)
Must be moderately or severely disabled
Must be medically at risk of institutionalization
Must need assistance with several daily activities such as bathing or meal preparation
Must live in the county where services are to be received
Must meet case management and income criteria for gap-filling funds
Assets must not exceed established resource limits for gap-filling funds
Require assistance with activities of daily living (Frederick County)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local MAP (Maryland Access Point) Information and Assistance Office or call 1-844-MAP-LINK (1-844-627-5465). A qualified staff person or team will conduct a screening and in-home evaluation to determine eligibility, followed by a face-to-face assessment and development of a person-centered care plan. A case manager is then assigned to locate, arrange, and ensure timely delivery of appropriate services. In Frederick County, contact the Division of Aging and Independence (Joy Rowe, JRowe1@frederickcountymd.gov, 301-600-1234) to inquire about eligibility and arrange an assessment.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Aging allocates funds to support innovative programs and critical operating needs for senior centers across the state. Each county receives a base allocation based on the number of Marylanders aged 60 and older, with additional competitive funds available for programs that serve historically underserved communities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: More than $750,000 in FY25 funds allocated to senior centers statewide. Base funding is distributed to each county based on the population of residents aged 60 and older. Additional competitive grants are available to counties with innovative programs serving historically underserved communities. Caroline, Cecil, Harford, and Worcester counties received additional competitive awards in FY25.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Senior centers and organizations serving older adults (age 60+) across Maryland counties
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating needs for senior centers and innovative programs serving historically underserved communities
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide; all Maryland counties receive base funding, with additional competitive funds available
requirements_list: Must operate a senior center serving Marylanders aged 60 and older
Competitive funds require innovative programs that serve historically underserved communities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Counties apply competitively for additional funds beyond the base allocation. Contact the Maryland Department of Aging or local Area Agency on Aging for details.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides free legal advice, counseling, and representation to older Marylanders. Local Area Agencies on Aging contract with local attorneys and law centers to deliver services. Priority issues include income maintenance, nutrition, public and disability benefits, health care, housing, utilities, consumer protection, employment, age discrimination, and advocacy for institutionalized persons.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free legal advice, counseling, and representation on priority issues. No cost to eligible individuals. Preference is given to older adults with the greatest economic or social need. Services are delivered through local Area Agencies on Aging contracting with local attorneys and law centers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents aged 60 and older, or caregivers of such persons.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Legal advice, counseling, and representation on issues including income maintenance, nutrition, public/disability benefits, health care, protective services, abuse, housing, utilities, consumer protection, employment, age discrimination/civil rights, and advocacy for institutionalized persons.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Maryland who are 60 years of age or older.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident
Must be 60 years of age or older, or be a caregiver of such a person
Priority given to those with greatest economic or social need
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local Area Agency on Aging's Maryland Access Point (MAP) to seek assistance.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides short-term loans of portable ramps to Marylanders with disabilities who need help getting in and out of their homes. Ramps are available through centers for independent living (CILs) across Maryland and are typically loaned for up to 120 days.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Portable ADA-compliant ramps loaned for up to 120 days (4 months) at no cost. Borrowers must arrange pickup from and return to the local center for independent living.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Marylanders with disabilities who need short-term access to a portable ramp to enter or exit their home.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Borrowing a portable ramp to improve home access for up to 120 days.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland through local centers for independent living.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident
Must need short-term portable ramp access
Borrower must arrange pickup and return of ramp at the local CIL
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local center for independent living (CIL) to inquire about borrowing a portable ramp. Find your local CIL using the ILRU directory.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Agricultural Nutrient Management Program requires farmers to develop and follow nutrient management plans when applying fertilizer, manure, or other nutrients to crops. Plans specify how much fertilizer and manure can safely be applied to achieve crop yields while preventing excess nutrients from polluting waterways. The program also trains and certifies consultants and farmers to write these plans, and ensures farms use nutrients efficiently while protecting water quality in the Chesapeake Bay and local waterways.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides technical assistance to farmers by requiring and supporting the development of nutrient management plans. It also trains and certifies consultants and farmers to prepare their own plans. Farmers applying nutrients to 10 or more acres per year must attend a two-hour nutrient applicator course once every three years. Consultants must complete continuing education hours to maintain certification. Specialized workshops are offered for different operation types (crop, poultry, pasture-based, nursery/greenhouse). Businesses providing consulting services must be licensed and file annual activity reports by September 30.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annual Implementation Report due by March 1; consultant license annual activity report due by September 30; certification exam applications must be filed at least 15 days before any announced examination
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland farmers grossing $2,500 or more per year, or livestock producers with 8,000 pounds or more of live animal weight, as well as consultants who write nutrient management plans, crop advisory service providers, fertilizer distributors, biosolids and manure handlers, and individuals seeking nutrient management certification.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Development and implementation of nutrient management plans for crop fertilization and animal manure management.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland, served through 6 regional MDA Nutrient Management offices covering all counties.
requirements_list: Farmers grossing $2,500 or more per year or livestock producers with 8,000+ lbs of live animal weight must follow nutrient management plans
Plans must be prepared by a certified University of Maryland specialist, certified private consultant, or a trained and certified farmer
Farmers must submit copies of initial nutrient management plans to the program
Plans must be updated before expiration
Soil samples must be taken at least once every three years
Manure analyses required at least every other year if using manure

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Farmers must obtain a nutrient management plan from a certified specialist, certified private consultant, or by becoming certified to prepare their own plan. Consultants can apply for certification by attending a two-day Fundamentals of Nutrient Management training course and then taking the certification exam, usually held in early summer and early August respectively. Farmers interested in self-certification can complete the interest form for the Farmer Training and Certification Program. Businesses providing consulting services must submit a license application with required fee to MDA, including license holder information, firm details, business status, employee information, and list of certified consultants. Certification exam applicants must submit a completed application with required documentation and $50 fee at least 15 days before the announced examination.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants to individuals, vendors, and businesses to showcase proven, innovative technologies for managing animal waste in Maryland. Funded technologies may reduce nutrient levels in animal waste, change its form or function, or generate energy and marketable products from waste. Projects must have the potential to enhance public health and environmental well-being, offer alternative waste management solutions, and have a positive economic development impact.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Approximately $750,000 in grant funding is available for Fiscal Year 2026 (ending June 30, 2026) to support innovative animal waste management technologies. Funding is provided through the Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays Trust Fund. Projects in the research and development stage are not eligible.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: December 23, 2025 (full proposal); Letter of Intent due October 17, 2025
structured_extraction.program_audience: Vendors, businesses, and individuals with proven, innovative technologies for managing animal waste generated by Maryland livestock or animal production processes.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Demonstration of proven, innovative animal waste management technologies, including alternative product development, manure-to-energy projects, nutrient reduction, and other beneficial uses of animal waste.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must involve Maryland livestock or animal production processes.
requirements_list: Animal waste must be generated by on-farm animals or through an animal production process involving Maryland livestock
Project must not be in research and development stage — must be a proven technology
Project must demonstrate potential to enhance public health and environmental well-being
Project must offer alternative waste management solutions for the agricultural sector
Project must have a positive economic development impact in Maryland
Additional consideration given to projects addressing climate and community benefits

Submissions are reviewed and ranked by the department in consultation with the Animal Waste Technology Evaluation Committee. High-ranking projects are invited to submit a full grant proposal due December 23, 2025.

structured_extraction.program_name: Certified Local Farm and Fish Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program encourages Maryland state agencies and public four-year universities to purchase at least 20% of their food from certified local farms and Chesapeake Invasive Species Providers. Established in 2020 by House Bill 1488 and modified in 2023 (HB 63) and 2024 (SB 290), it is designed to increase economic opportunity and participation of qualified Maryland farms and seafood processors in state government procurement. Farms and seafood dealers can apply to be certified and listed in an online directory that state agencies use when procuring food. Certification is free and requires farms to have a nutrient management plan or dealers to hold a Tidal Fish Dealer license.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Farms and seafood dealers receive free certification and listing in an online directory, making them eligible to sell to Maryland state agencies and universities that must meet a 20% local food purchasing goal. State agencies and universities must structure food procurement to achieve an overall goal of purchasing 20% of their total food dollar value from Certified Local Farm and Chesapeake Invasive Species Providers. Purchases can be made directly from certified providers or through prime vendors and subcontractors. Waivers are available for sole-source, expedited, or emergency procurements with documented good reason. There is no cost to become certified.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: September 30, 2025 (for annual reports and waiver requests)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland farms (with a nutrient management plan) and seafood dealers (licensed as Tidal Fish Dealers with DNR) seeking to sell food to state agencies and universities; Maryland state agencies, public four-year universities, food service contractors (prime and sub-contractors), and food distributors required to achieve a 20% local food purchasing goal.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Certification and directory listing to facilitate sales to state agencies; state agencies use the directory to meet their 20% local food procurement goal. Procurement of local farm and fish products by state agencies and universities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland for farms and seafood dealers operating in Maryland. Applies to all Maryland counties and municipalities.
requirements_list: Farms must have a nutrient management plan with the Maryland Department of Agriculture, or meet nutrient management requirements (e.g., apiarists or aquaculturists).
Seafood dealers must be licensed as a Tidal Fish Dealer with the Maryland Department of Natural Resources.
Applicants must register through the Maryland OneStop online application portal.
Certified participants must update their directory information once a year.
State agencies and public four-year universities must submit annual Reports and Waiver Requests to MDA by September 30 each year (COMAR 15.01.19).
State agencies and universities must achieve 20% procurement goal from Certified Local Providers.
Waiver requests must include documentation of efforts made to contact providers, including contact attempts, provider responses, and limitations encountered.
Must complete all required fields in application (marked with red asterisks).
Must have a DNR (Department of Natural Resources) license (for seafood dealers).
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Register/login to the Maryland OneStop portal and search for the Certified Local Farm and Fish Program Application. 2. Complete and submit the application form. 3. Receive confirmation upon submission. 4. MDA verifies the farm's nutrient management plan or the dealer's Tidal Fish Dealer license. 5. Upon verification, MDA certifies the applicant and lists their contact information, products, and certification number in the online directory. 6. Participants update their directory information annually (reminders sent 90 days before, 7 days before, and on the renewal deadline). 7. State agencies submit annual reports and waiver requests to MDA by September 30 each year.

structured_extraction.program_name: Conservation Equipment Tax Break (Income Tax Subtraction Modification for Conservation Equipment)
structured_extraction.program_description: A Maryland income tax benefit that helps farmers offset the cost of buying certain types of conservation equipment to control soil erosion, manage nutrients, and protect local water quality. Farmers can subtract 100% of eligible equipment costs (50% for vertical tillage equipment) from their taxable income on Maryland individual and corporate tax returns. Authority: Md. Code Ann., Tax - General, § 10-208 (2021).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible farmers may subtract 100% of the cost of qualifying conservation equipment purchases from their Maryland taxable income (50% for vertical tillage equipment). Eligible equipment includes no-till planters, manure injection equipment, manure spreading equipment, deep no-till rippers, GPS devices, optical sensing systems, and vertical tillage equipment. Equipment must have a useful life of at least 4 years and be retained for a minimum of 3 years after the tax year in which the subtraction is claimed.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Equipment must have been purchased within the last five years
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland farmers and agricultural businesses who purchase conservation equipment to control soil erosion, manage nutrients, or protect water quality
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of conservation equipment including no-till planters, manure injection equipment, manure spreading equipment, deep no-till rippers, GPS devices, optical sensing nutrient application systems, and vertical tillage equipment
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide; equipment must be used in agricultural production in Maryland
requirements_list: Equipment purchased after specified dates (varies by equipment type; earliest December 31, 1985)
No-Till Planter/Drill: purchased after December 31, 1985
Manure Injector: purchased after December 31, 1989; not used for sludge application
Equipment must have a useful life of at least 4 years
Taxpayer must maintain ownership/retain equipment for a minimum of 3 years after the tax year in which subtraction is claimed
Equipment must be used for agricultural production in Maryland
Must submit certification form and signed equipment receipt to local Soil Conservation District
Must provide serial numbers for new and trade-in equipment
Nutrient Management Plan required for manure spreaders (prepared per Agriculture Article, Title 8, Subtitle 8)
Equipment must be purchased within the last five years
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete the application/certification form and submit it along with a signed equipment receipt to the local Soil Conservation District. The certified form is then submitted with your Maryland individual or corporate tax return.

structured_extraction.program_name: Conservation Reserve Enhancement Program (CREP) and Permanent Easement Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Conservation Reserve Enhancement Program (CREP) is a federal-state partnership administered by the Maryland Department of Agriculture in coordination with USDA and the Maryland Department of Natural Resources. It pays farmers and rural landowners to temporarily remove environmentally sensitive agricultural land from production for 10–15 years and install conservation practices to protect streams, improve water quality, and create wildlife habitat. Enrolled landowners receive annual rental payments above normal rates, bonuses for planting riparian forest buffers or herbaceous buffers, retiring highly erodible land, or restoring wetlands and shallow water habitats. Specifically, benefits include a 100% rental rate bonus for planting a forest buffer, an 80% bonus for herbaceous buffers or retiring highly erodible land or restoring wetlands, a one-time state incentive payment of $100/acre, and 75–100% cost share for practices. Newly enrolled farmers who plant new riparian forest buffers next to streams also qualify for a one-time signing bonus of up to $1,000 per acre (through 2031). Cost-share assistance is also available for installing streamside buffers, watering systems, and livestock fencing. Contracts run 10–15 years. Sign-up for Maryland CREP is ongoing until acreage goals are met. After a federal CREP or CRP contract expires, landowners who have installed the required conservation practices may enroll their land in a permanent conservation easement with the State of Maryland, permanently restricting land use to approved conservation practices. The easement is recorded with county land records and applies to current and all future landowners. Compensation for the permanent easement is determined by an easement valuation system considering fair market value, buffer sizes, contract/match acres, and whole farm protection. In Washington County, the program is further enhanced by State-funded conservation easements that permanently protect existing federal CREP Contract areas; landowners can add up to ten times their CREP Contract acreage to the easement, and Washington County has paid over $4.8 million to preserve nearly 1,926 acres under this program. Enrollment is non-competitive and open. As of January 2024, all Maryland counties are eligible for the permanent easement component.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Enrolled landowners receive: a per-acre annual rental payment above normal rates; a 100% rental rate bonus for planting a riparian forest buffer; an 80% rental rate bonus for planting herbaceous buffers, retiring highly erodible land, or restoring wetlands; a one-time state incentive payment of $100/acre; and 75–100% cost share for conservation practices. Federal and state sign-up bonuses of $200 per acre (if eligible) or $100 per acre (Maryland state bonus for re-enrollment) are also available. Newly enrolled farmers who plant new riparian forest buffers next to streams also qualify for a one-time signing bonus of up to $1,000 per acre (through 2031). Cost-share assistance is also available for installing streamside buffers, watering systems, and livestock fencing. Contracts run 10–15 years. After the federal contract expires, landowners who have installed required conservation practices may enter into a permanent conservation easement with the State of Maryland, receiving compensation determined by an easement valuation system considering fair market value, buffer sizes, contract/match acres, and whole farm protection status. In Washington County, the program is further enhanced by State-funded conservation easements permanently protecting existing federal CREP Contract areas; landowners can add up to ten times their CREP Contract acreage to the easement. Washington County has paid over $4.8 million to preserve nearly 1,926 acres under this program. Enrollment is non-competitive and open.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Sign-up for Maryland CREP is ongoing until acreage goals are met. Enrollment is non-competitive and open.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers and rural landowners with environmentally sensitive cropland, streamside property, highly erodible land, or wetlands in Maryland, including cropland planted in two of the five most recent years or marginal pasture adjacent to streams suitable for riparian forest buffers. Eligible land includes properties next to a stream or waterway, highly erodible land within 1,000 feet of a stream, and marginal pastureland next to a stream. Landowners who have an existing federal CRP or CREP contract and have installed the required conservation practices may also enroll in a permanent conservation easement after their federal contract expires. Washington County landowners with existing FSA CREP Contracts may apply for permanent conservation easements with expanded acreage.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Taking environmentally sensitive agricultural land out of production and installing conservation practices such as riparian forest buffers, herbaceous buffers, retiring highly erodible lands, restoring wetlands, and creating shallow water habitat on enrolled agricultural land. Also supports installation of streamside buffers, watering systems, and livestock fencing. After the federal contract period, funds support permanent conservation easements that protect water quality and natural resources permanently, representing payment to landowners for permanently restricting land use to approved conservation practices as defined in a conservation management plan or forest stewardship plan. In Washington County, funds also support payment to landowners for permanent conservation easements on CREP Contract areas and expanded adjacent acreage.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. As of January 2024, all Maryland counties are eligible for the permanent easement component. Eligible land includes streamside property, certain highly erodible land (within 1,000 feet of a stream), and wetlands. Land must have been planted as cropland two of the five most recent years, or be marginal pasture adjacent to streams suitable for riparian forest buffers, and must be adjacent to waterways or other water bodies. Landowners apply through their local USDA Farm Service Agency office. For the permanent easement component, land must have an existing federal CREP or CRP contract with required conservation practices installed. Washington County offers an additional permanent conservation easement component for landowners with existing FSA CREP Contracts, allowing enrollment of up to ten times the CREP Contract acreage.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that pays higher incentives for enhanced cover crop implementation to encourage greater biodiversity and residue management in order to improve soil health.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Higher incentive payments for farmers who grow cover crop mixes on the same field for three consecutive years, maintain a living root system, and manage the cover crop for maximum benefits.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers interested in enhanced cover crop implementation to improve soil health
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Growing enhanced cover crop mixes to increase biodiversity, manage residue, and improve soil health
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide
requirements_list: Must grow cover crop mixes on the same field for three consecutive years
Must maintain a living root system
Must manage the cover crop for maximum benefits
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local soil conservation district for free assistance.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Cover Crop Program provides cost-share grants to help farmers plant cold-hardy cereal grains, legumes, brassicas, and other fall cover crops following the harvest of spring and summer crops. Cover crops help recycle unused plant nutrients, prevent erosion, improve soil health, remove carbon dioxide from the air, and protect farm fields from extreme weather. The program supports the health of the Chesapeake Bay and the productivity of Maryland farmland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Cost-share grants cover seed and planting costs for eligible fall cover crop species. Cost-share rates vary from year to year. Additional incentives are available for early planting (by October 10) or for using rye, triticale, or a multi-species cover crop mix. Cost-share is also available for seed testing. There is a 10-acre minimum with no acreage cap.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annual enrollment window, usually late June and early July; 2026-2027 sign-up opens June 22, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland farmers who plant fall cover crops following spring or summer crops
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Seed and planting costs for eligible fall cover crop species; seed testing costs
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland; applications submitted through local soil conservation districts
requirements_list: Must plant a minimum of 10 acres
Cover crops must be planted after corn, soybeans, sorghum, tobacco, vegetables, hemp, sunflowers, sod, or millet
Eligible planting methods: no-till, conventional till, broadcast/light tillage, broadcast/stalk chopping, or aerial seeding
Must follow Maryland Seed Law and Regulations if using homegrown seed
Must be in good standing with Conservation Grants and Nutrient Management programs
Must certify planted acres with local soil conservation district within one week of planting and after kill down or suppression

Current Nutrient Management Plan (NMP) required, compliant with COMAR 15.20.07
Seed testing: minimum 2 lbs seed sample, $30.00 fee per sample, separate form required for each sample, treated samples must state treatment name
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply in person at your local soil conservation district during the annual signup window (usually late June to early July). Bring a completed Nutrient Management Plan Certification and IRS Form W-9. After planting, certify planted acres with your local soil conservation district within one week of planting and again after kill down or suppression. For seed testing, mail seed samples to: MD Seed Lab, 50 Harry S Truman Parkway, Annapolis, MD 21401 with a completed Seed Sample Testing Form.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides a menu of conservation incentives that promote clean water, healthy soils, and climate solutions for Maryland farmers and landowners. Incentives include conservation buffer payments, tree planting incentives ($2 per tree planted as part of an approved conservation practice), CREP bonus payments, Cover Crop Plus grants, tax incentives for conservation equipment (including a 100% income tax subtraction for eligible conservation equipment purchases such as no-till planters, manure injection/spreading equipment, deep rippers, GPS devices, nutrient application systems, and vertical tillage equipment), and low-interest loans (LILAC) for agricultural conservation projects. The tree planting incentive supports Maryland's goals to capture greenhouse gas emissions and is financed through the Maryland Agricultural Water Quality Cost-Share Program. Qualifying tree planting practices include Windbreak Establishment, Silvopasture, Riparian Forest Buffer, Hedgerow Planting, and Tree and Shrub Establishment. The tax subtraction component allows farmers to subtract 100% of eligible equipment purchase costs (50% for vertical tillage equipment) from taxable income on Maryland individual and corporate tax returns.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Multiple incentives available: (1) Tree Planting Incentives — $2 per new tree planted as part of an approved conservation practice, in addition to regular cost-share rates (Windbreak Establishment: $2/tree + up to 100% cost-share; Silvopasture: $2/tree + up to 87.5% cost-share; Riparian Forest Buffer: $2/tree + up to 100% cost-share; Hedgerow Planting: $2/tree + up to 100% cost-share; Tree and Shrub Establishment: $2/tree + up to 100% cost-share); (2) Conservation buffer payments; (3) CREP bonus payments; (4) Cover Crop Plus grants; (5) Maryland Income Tax Subtraction — subtract 100% of eligible conservation equipment purchase costs from taxable income (50% for vertical tillage equipment); eligible equipment includes no-till planters, manure injection/spreading equipment, deep rippers, GPS devices, nutrient application systems, and vertical tillage equipment; excess subtraction carries over up to five succeeding tax years; (6) Low-interest LILAC loans for agricultural conservation projects.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland farmers, agricultural producers, and landowners seeking conservation incentives for clean water, healthy soils, and climate-smart practices, including those installing qualifying conservation practices under the Maryland Agricultural Water Quality Cost-Share Program and those purchasing eligible conservation equipment for tax subtraction purposes
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Conservation buffers, tree planting, cover crops, conservation equipment purchases (no-till planters, manure injection/spreading equipment, deep rippers, GPS devices, nutrient application systems, vertical tillage equipment), and agricultural conservation projects to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and improve environmental outcomes
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Must be enrolled in an approved conservation practice under the Maryland Agricultural Water Quality Cost-Share Program (for tree planting incentive)
Practice must include qualifying tree planting (Windbreak Establishment, Silvopasture, Riparian Forest Buffer, Hedgerow Planting, or Tree and Shrub Establishment) for tree planting bonus
For tax subtraction: equipment must have a useful life of at least four years
For tax subtraction: equipment must be owned for at least three years after the tax year in which the subtraction is claimed
For tax subtraction: equipment must have been purchased within the last five years (purchase dates vary by equipment type, ranging from 1985–2012 eligibility start dates)
For tax subtraction: submit certification form and signed dated receipt to local soil conservation district
For tax subtraction: provide serial numbers for new and trade-in equipment
For tax subtraction: excess subtraction carries over to succeeding tax years, not to exceed five years
For manure spreaders: compliance with Nutrient Management Plan required
Equipment must be used in agricultural production
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local soil conservation district for free assistance. For the tax subtraction: complete the certification application form with equipment information and receipts, submit to local soil conservation district for verification and eligibility certification, district forwards to Maryland Department of Agriculture for final approval, and applicant receives two copies of the certified form to submit with their tax return.

structured_extraction.program_name: FSMA Produce Safety On-Farm Readiness Reviews
structured_extraction.program_description: Free and confidential technical assistance program to help farmers understand and meet requirements of the federal Food Safety Modernization Act (FSMA) Produce Safety Rule (PSR). Teams from MDA, UMD, and UME conduct on-farm walkthroughs to observe practices, discuss compliance, and provide customized feedback. The program is educational and non-regulatory, and includes a pre-review manual, on-site walkthrough, post-review notes on compliant areas and improvement needs, and follow-up assistance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free on-farm readiness review (OFRR) including a pre-review manual, on-site walkthrough with a team from MDA/UMD/UME to observe practices and discuss compliance, customized post-review notes identifying compliant areas and areas needing improvement, and follow-up assistance as needed. This is educational and non-regulatory technical assistance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers required to comply with the FSMA Produce Safety Rule, including farms engaged in growing, harvesting, packing, or holding covered produce
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: On-site technical assistance to help farms understand and meet federal FSMA Produce Safety Rule requirements; no financial assistance provided
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to farms located in Maryland
requirements_list: Farm must grow covered produce subject to the FSMA Produce Safety Rule
Farm must potentially be required to comply with FSMA Produce Safety Rule requirements
Completion of OFRR request form with farm details, covered activities, and financial category
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the On-Farm Readiness Review Request Form with farm details, covered activities, and financial category. Submit via email, fax, or mail to MDA. MDA will contact the farm to discuss details and schedule a review date and time.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Farm to School Program connects locally produced foods with school cafeterias and supports hands-on learning activities such as farm visits, school gardening, and culinary classes. It integrates food-related education into classroom curriculum and enriches school food offerings while supporting local agriculture. The program includes all types of producers and food businesses — farmers, watermen, food processors, manufacturers, and distributors — and is jointly supported by the Maryland Department of Agriculture and the Maryland State Department of Education.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides technical assistance to help schools source locally grown Maryland foods and incorporate agriculture education into cafeterias and classrooms. Support includes connecting schools with local producers, food businesses (farmers, watermen, processors, manufacturers, and distributors), and facilitating hands-on learning activities such as farm visits, school gardening, and culinary classes.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public schools, school cafeteria managers, teachers, administrators, local farmers, watermen, food processors, manufacturers, and distributors in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Sourcing locally produced Maryland foods for school meals and incorporating agriculture and food education into school programs, including hands-on learning activities such as farm visits, school gardening, and culinary classes
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to Maryland public schools and food producers/businesses supplying Maryland schools
