structured_extraction.application_process_overview: New applicants: Download and complete the applicable application packet (Crop and Pasture, Livestock, or On-Farm Processor/Handler), develop an Organic System Plan, and submit the completed forms along with the $500 application fee to MDA. MDA reviews the application for compliance with NOP standards; if the OSP appears compliant, MDA schedules an on-site inspection. MDA reviews the application and inspection report and issues a certificate to applicants that meet all requirements. Renewal applicants: Submit the annual update packet and $500 fee by April 1. Exempt producers: Submit the Organic Exempt Application and $30 fee annually. Material inputs must be submitted to MOCP for review and approval prior to use; additional materials may be submitted for review at any time. See the Organic Producers Certification page for application forms and additional information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A volunteer corps of veterinary professionals who assist Maryland in responding to large-scale animal emergencies such as disease outbreaks, floods, fires, and other disasters. Members become temporary State employees when activated and receive liability and workers' compensation coverage.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Members receive free online training courses through FEMA's Emergency Management Institute (EMI), which count toward continuing education units (CEUs) for veterinary license renewal. When activated, members are covered by State Tort liability protection and workers' compensation. Expenses are paid if deployed to another state under the Emergency Management Assistance Compact (EMAC).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Veterinarians, veterinary students, veterinary technicians, veterinary assistants, and veterinary students willing to volunteer during animal emergencies.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training to prepare for and respond to large-scale animal emergencies; liability and workers' compensation coverage when activated.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to volunteers who will respond to emergencies within Maryland. Members may also be asked to serve in other states under the Emergency Management Assistance Compact (EMAC), with expenses paid.
requirements_list: Must be a veterinarian, veterinary student, veterinary technician, assistant, or student
Must be willing to voluntarily respond to animal emergencies
Required online FEMA courses: IS 800, IS 700, IS 100, and IS 200
Recommended additional courses: IS 10, IS 11, IS 111
Must submit course completion certificates for credentialing
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register online at the Maryland Responds portal (https://mdresponds.health.maryland.gov/index.php). Complete required FEMA online training courses and submit certificates of completion to the program coordinator and the State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Spay and Neuter Grants Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Agriculture (MDA) funds competitive grants to local governments and non-profit animal welfare organizations — including animal shelters, humane societies, animal control agencies, and rescue organizations — to provide free spay and neuter services for pets of low-income Marylanders and for free-roaming unowned community cats (where permitted by local law). The goal is to reduce pet overpopulation and lower intake and euthanasia rates in Maryland animal shelters. Organizations may apply for a Pet Focused Grant, a Feral Cat Focused Grant, or both. Surgeries may also include free rabies vaccines and other approved costs. Funding comes entirely from annual fees paid by pet food manufacturers that sell cat or dog food and treats in Maryland, not from tax dollars, and is disbursed in two allocations: the first covers 50% of surgery funding plus 100% of rabies vaccine and other approved costs; the second covers the remaining 50% once the grantee has spent 35% of their budget. This is a supplemental grant and not intended to be an organization's sole or primary funding source. The Spay and Neuter Advisory Board (SNAB) reviews applications annually, scores them, and makes funding recommendations to the Maryland Secretary of Agriculture for approval at an annual meeting typically held in August. The program has funded projects annually since at least 2015. The program does not provide funding directly to individuals — low-income residents must contact the local organization serving their area to access free spay and neuter services. Coverage may be limited to specific counties or zip codes. Queen Anne's County also administers a local component through Animal Services, which provides free spay and neuter services for cats and dogs owned by low-income county residents (households earning under $60,000 annually).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants are awarded annually to eligible organizations to fund free spay/neuter surgeries and related services. Two separate grant opportunities are offered each year: one for pet dogs and cats owned by low-income Marylanders (Pet Focused), and one for unowned or feral cats (Feral Cat Focused). Funding is disbursed in two allocations: the first covers 50% of surgery funding plus 100% of rabies vaccine and other approved costs; the second covers the remaining 50% of surgery funding once the grantee has spent 35% of their budget. This is a supplemental grant and not intended to be an organization's sole or primary funding source. Grant requests are capped at 25% of annual operating budget (maximum $75,000). Eligible costs include spay/neuter surgical procedures (all-inclusive: materials, veterinary services, pre- and post-operative care), rabies vaccines (capped at $5.00 per dose if a separate line item), transportation assistance, outreach and educational materials, HQHVSN training for veterinarians and surgical staff, equipment purchases up to $5,000 cumulative, and emergency medical expenses up to 5% of grant budget (requires case-by-case approval within 60 days). Ineligible costs include staff salaries, overhead, co-pays, and non-essential procedures. Funding comes entirely from fees paid by pet food manufacturers that sell products in Maryland, not from tax dollars. The Spay and Neuter Advisory Board reviews applications annually, scores them, and makes funding recommendations to the Maryland Secretary of Agriculture for approval. Approved applicants sign a Grant Contract typically in September-October, and first funding allocations usually arrive in mid-to-late December. For individuals, free spay and neuter surgeries for cats and dogs owned by low-income residents are provided through MDA-funded local organizations. Surgeries may also include a free rabies vaccine. Funding is limited and projects may cover specific counties or zip codes. Additionally, Queen Anne's County Animal Services administers a local Spay/Neuter Grant providing free spay and neuter services for cats and dogs owned by low-income county residents (annual household income under $60,000).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Early January to early April each year; FY27 window is now closed. FY28 window opens January 2027. Individual access to services through funded organizations is active as long as grant funds allow. County-level program active as long as grant funds allow.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments and non-profit animal welfare organizations (including animal shelters, humane societies, animal control agencies, and rescue organizations) that provide spay/neuter services for pets of low-income Marylanders or for free-roaming unowned community cats in Maryland; low-income pet owners in Maryland who own cats or dogs and need access to free spay/neuter services; and low-income residents of Queen Anne's County (annual household income under $60,000) who own cats or dogs in need of spay or neuter services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free spay and neuter surgeries for pets of low-income Maryland residents or for unowned free-roaming cats; may also cover rabies vaccines (required, capped at $5.00 per dose if separate line item), HQHVSN training for veterinarians and surgical staff, transportation assistance for recipients, outreach and educational materials, equipment purchases (up to $5,000 cumulative), and emergency medical expenses (up to 5% of grant budget, case-by-case approval). Cannot be used for shelter or rescue animals prior to placement, staff salaries, overhead, co-pays, or non-essential procedures. For feral cat projects, eligible costs also include trapping equipment and supplies, ear tipping, microchipping, and monitoring. At the county level, free spay and neuter services for cats and dogs owned by qualifying low-income Queen Anne's County residents.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across all Maryland counties. Past grantees include organizations in Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Calvert, Caroline, Carroll, Cecil, Charles, Dorchester, Frederick, Harford, Howard, Kent, Montgomery, Prince George's, Queen Anne's, Somerset, St. Mary's, Talbot, Washington, Wicomico, and Worcester counties. Applying organizations and veterinary clinics do not need to be based in Maryland, but all animals and owners receiving services must reside in Maryland. Projects may be limited to specific areas or zip codes within a county. Outdoor cat colony services must not be prohibited by local law; some municipalities may allow TNR where counties prohibit it. For feral cat projects, target areas must directly relate to sources of intake for municipal shelters and applicants must obtain signed Permission to Enter Forms from property owners/tenants. Queen Anne's County residents may access the county-level grant through Animal Services; applicants must reside in Queen Anne's County and have a household income under $60,000.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local government or non-profit animal welfare organization (including animal shelters, humane societies, animal control agencies, or rescue organizations) for the MDA statewide program
Non-profit applicants must have 501(c)(3) tax-exempt status
Organization must be in good standing with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) and the MD Secretary of State Charities Division

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For the MDA statewide program, read the Guidelines and Instructions documents for the relevant grant opportunity (Pet Focused and/or Feral Cat Focused) before applying. Gather required documentation including a signed W-9, SDAT good standing verification, charitable registration permit (if applicable), shelter statistics, a detailed work plan with timeline, and map(s) of target area(s). Submit the application during the open window (January to early April). After submission, no changes or resubmissions are allowed. Applications are reviewed by the Program Coordinator and then sent to the Spay and Neuter Advisory Board (SNAB) for scoring and funding recommendations at an annual meeting typically held in August. Recommendations go to the Maryland Secretary of Agriculture for approval. Approved applicants sign a Grant Contract typically in September-October, and first funding allocations usually arrive in mid-to-late December. Grantees must submit Quarterly Grant Progress Reports and a Final Report. Final report fact sheets for completed grant cycles are published on the MDA website. Contact the Spay and Neuter Grants Program Coordinator (Jen Swanson, jen.swanson@maryland.gov) for more details. For individuals seeking free services, check the list of active projects on the MDA website to find an organization serving your county or zip code, then contact that organization directly to confirm eligibility and schedule services. If no project covers your area, contact your local animal shelter or nonprofit animal welfare organization for other low-cost options. For the Queen Anne's County program, residents should submit the Maryland Spay/Neuter Grant Application (https://qacmd.seamlessdocs.com/f/qacasSpayandNeuterGrantApplication) along with required documents to Animal Services. After submission, applicants will be contacted to schedule the spay or neuter appointment. The county application form is also available at https://www.qac.org/1436/Forms.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Specialty Crop Block Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Agriculture awards competitive grants to enhance the competitiveness of Maryland specialty crops, including fruits and vegetables, culinary herbs and spices, honey, hops, grapes, maple syrup, Christmas trees, and nursery crops. Projects must demonstrate broader industry benefit beyond a single business or individual.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants funded through the USDA Specialty Crop Block Grant Program. Approximately $400,000 in total funding is anticipated. Individual producers may apply but must show broader benefit to a group of similar producers or an industry segment — funds will not be awarded for projects that benefit only a single organization, business, institution, or individual.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Specialty crop producers, non-profits, government entities, and other organizations working to improve the competitiveness of Maryland specialty crops such as fruits, vegetables, herbs, honey, hops, grapes, maple syrup, Christmas trees, and nursery crops.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects that enhance the competitiveness of specialty crops, such as extending growing seasons, demonstrating new production methods, and sharing results with a broader group of producers. Allowable costs include salaries/wages, contractual services, conferences, equipment rental, travel, participant support, insurance, memberships, printing/publications, supplies and materials, computing devices (under $5,000), training related to project objectives and Federal grants management, and marketing aligned with grant purpose. Funds may not be used for projects that only benefit or profit a single entity, or for unallowable costs such as sponsorships, trade show attendance/displays, meeting room reservations, or exhibits not aligned with grant program purpose.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Best is Maryland's statewide marketing program administered by the Maryland Department of Agriculture. It connects consumers to fresh and local Maryland agricultural products and helps Maryland farmers and agricultural producers find and develop profitable marketing opportunities at the local, national, and international level. The program also connects producers to federal resources and policy information relevant to the agricultural sector, while supporting them in selling locally, nationally, and internationally.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides marketing support and access to local, national, and international market opportunities for Maryland farmers and agricultural producers. It connects consumers to fresh and local Maryland products, helps farmers find new buyers, and provides information on federal resources and agricultural policies. Benefits include direct and indirect financial impact on how farmers sell products and develop new buyers. Non-financial assistance includes regulatory program support, services, technical assistance, and information.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland farmers and agricultural producers
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Marketing and connecting producers to local, national, and international buyers; accessing federal resources and policy information
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides farmers and landowners with incentive payments to plant streamside buffers on farmland to improve the health of local streams and the Chesapeake Bay. The program supports three types of buffers: forest buffers, grass buffers next to waterways or field ditches, and watercourse access control areas adjacent to pastures. It complements CREP by offering flexible site management, shorter contract terms, and options for field ditches. Payment rates range from $500 per acre for an existing grass buffer to $4,500 per acre to install a riparian forest buffer with pasture fencing. Farmers receive 75% of the project cost upfront and 25% after planting is verified. An extra one-time tree bonus payment of $1,000 per acre is available for forest buffers, plus up to $330 per acre per year for up to 5 years in annual maintenance payments for forest buffers. Contracts are for 5 or 10 years. Local soil conservation districts provide free technical assistance to help install buffers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Payment rates range from $500 per acre for an existing grass buffer to $4,500 per acre to install a riparian forest buffer with pasture fencing. Farmers receive 75% of the project cost upfront and 25% after planting is verified. An extra one-time tree bonus payment of $1,000 per acre is available for forest buffers, plus up to $330 per acre per year for up to 5 years in annual maintenance payments for forest buffers (including mowing at $160/ac, spot spraying at $150/ac, and tree shelter maintenance at $20/ac). Contracts are for 5 or 10 years. Free technical assistance is provided by local soil conservation districts.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers and landowners responsible for the management of eligible cropland or pasture adjacent to streams, ditches, or watercourses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of streamside grass buffers, riparian forest buffers, or watercourse access control areas on eligible farmland adjacent to waterways or field ditches. Eligible uses include planting trees next to streams, installing livestock exclusion fencing, and establishing grass or forest buffers. Optional annual maintenance activities include mowing, spot spraying, and tree shelter maintenance for forest buffers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to farmers and landowners with eligible cropland or pasture adjacent to waterways. Buffer width requirements vary (10-34 ft. narrow; 35-100 ft. wider options). Contact your local soil conservation district for assistance.
requirements_list: Must be a farmer or landowner responsible for the management of eligible lands.
Farmers who lease land must certify an active lease for the term of the buffer or provide an agreement from the landowner.
Farmers and landowners must be in good standing with USDA and state cost-share programs.
A current Nutrient Management Plan Certification is required and must be submitted with the application.

Eligible land must be cropland next to a stream or ditch with an established cropping history in pasture, commodity crops, or hay, or areas adjacent to watercourses with highly erodible or hydric soils.
Existing buffers or agricultural lands actively enrolled in state (MACS) or federal programs (CRP, CREP, EQIP, etc.) or mandated by an easement are not eligible.
Field ditches are not eligible for woody conservation buffers.
Plants must be installed within 1 year of the signed agreement date.
Must install qualifying streamside or field ditch buffers.
Compliance with state nutrient management requirements (MD Agric. Code Ann. §§8-801-8-806 and COMAR 15.20.06-08).
Color map of buffer area with premise address, showing acres and location for each buffer area.
Signed W-9 form matching application name/address.
All landowners on property deed must sign agreement.
Authorization documentation (Certificate of Resolution, Power of Attorney, Certificate of Sole Proprietor, or Trust Agreement) as applicable.
Funding not guaranteed; subject to ranking process if demand exceeds available funds.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local soil conservation district to apply. Download the application form and submit it along with a map showing the location and acreage of the buffer, a signed Nutrient Management Plan Certification Form, and a signed IRS Form W-9. Applications are accepted on a first-come, first-served basis. Submit completed checklist with required documentation to Soil Conservation District and DNR. Visit bit.ly/MDA_Buffer for sign-up details.

structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive grant program that supports Maryland farmers and organizations working with farmers to implement innovative soil health conservation practices. The program encourages adoption and testing of new conservation management practices to improve soil health, yield, profitability, and carbon capture. Selected applicants receive funding to support enhanced soil health practices over three years, including agroforestry practices such as alley cropping, critical area plantings, and tree planting that improve soil health and build climate resilience.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants of up to $50,000 per selected applicant to support 3 years of enhanced soil health practices. Up to 30% of funds are provided upfront, with the remainder distributed annually in spring after verification of progress (4 total payments over the grant period). Funds may be used for conservation practice implementation, equipment purchase or rental (preference for rented or used equipment and matching funds), project staff and administrative time, and research costs. Cannot be used for overhead/indirect expenses, livestock, imported livestock feed, or soil fertility inputs. Eligible practices include agroforestry practices such as alley cropping and critical area plantings.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: January 9, 2026 at 5:00 pm EST (postmark deadline for mail: January 6, 2026). The application period for the 2025-2026 Program is now closed; grant award recipients will be contacted by March 30, 2026.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Nick Miller, Healthy Soils Program Specialist
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland farmers (individual or groups), and individuals or organizations working with farmers in Maryland seeking to improve soil health and build climate resilience through enhanced soil practices and agroforestry.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Implementation of conservation practices including cover crops, conservation tillage, pasture and hay planting, conservation cover, critical area planting, conservation crop rotation, nutrient management, integrated pest management, prescribed grazing, soil carbon amendment, and agroforestry practices such as alley cropping and tree planting. Funds may also cover equipment purchase or rental (preference for rented or used equipment and matching funds), project staff and administrative time, and research costs. Cannot be used for overhead/indirect expenses, livestock, imported livestock feed, or soil fertility inputs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be farming or working with farmers in Maryland. No minimum or maximum acreage requirements. Statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be an individual farmer, group of farmers, or organization working with farmers operating in Maryland

Agricultural operation must have a gross annual income of $2,500 or more (or $2,500 or more of donated agricultural products if a non-profit) and/or manage 8 or more animal units (8,000 pounds of live animal weight)
Must provide proof of compliance with Maryland's nutrient management requirements by submitting a Current Nutrient Management Plan Certification Form at the time of application
Must apply during the open enrollment period (typically January, approximately 8 weeks)
Must implement approved soil health practices for 3 years
Proposals should focus on adopting conservation practices and soil health systems that are innovative and expand knowledge within the agricultural community
Participation with local Soil Conservation District (SCD) or NRCS office required/encouraged
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply during the open enrollment period, which typically begins in January and runs for approximately 8 weeks. Submit a completed application including project narrative (limited to 10 pages excluding images), project budget, and any applicable templates (cover crop, grazing, tree and shrub planting, grass and forb planting). Download documents to your device before completing. Submit via email as Word or PDF attachments, or print and mail to the address on page 4 of the application document. The 2025-2026 application period is now closed; grant award recipients will be contacted by March 30, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: A pilot program established by Executive Order in 2017 to test the feasibility of controlling chironomid midges (non-biting midge flies) in the Back River area using Bacillus thuringiensis israelensis (Bti), a naturally occurring soil bacterium. The program tests the most cost-effective dosage and frequency of Bti treatments applied by boat and/or helicopter. Bactimos WG (Bti strain AM65-52) biological larvicide is applied to control non-biting midge larvae in aquatic habitats.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Bactimos WG (active ingredient: Bti strain AM65-52) is applied to the Back River area (specifically a 260-acre section in Essex, Baltimore County) by boat using specialized apparatus to suppress midge populations at public expense. Five monthly treatments were scheduled: August-October 2017 and May-June 2018. This is a government-operated pilot service, not a grant or loan program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents, citizens, and businesses in the Back River area (particularly Essex, Baltimore County) affected by chironomid midge infestations. Also relevant to industrial facilities and the tourism industry impacted by midge nuisance.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Midge suppression through Bactimos WG biological larvicide (Bti) application to aquatic midge larval habitats in the Back River area, including aquatic spray contract management and treatment implementation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: 260-acre section of Back River in Essex, Baltimore County, Maryland. Targets freshwater aquatic environments with midge larval habitat (substrate/soil at bottom of water body).
requirements_list: Midge larvae must be present in water body substrates
Application targets midge larval habitat (substrate/soil at bottom of water body)
Treatments are typically not overhead sprays

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Agriculture's Mosquito Control Program provides direct mosquito control services to approximately 2,000 communities in 16 Maryland counties. The program aims to prevent mosquito-borne diseases in humans, pets, and livestock through an Integrated Mosquito Management (IMM) approach including arbovirus surveillance and disease testing, biological control, breeding ground reduction, larval mosquito control, public education, and insecticide applications by ground or aircraft (aerial applications limited to Eastern Shore only).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides direct mosquito control services under an Integrated Mosquito Management (IMM) approach, including: arbovirus surveillance and disease testing; breeding ground reduction and larval control; scheduled and unscheduled insecticide applications via ground-based ultra-low-volume (ULV) truck-mounted aerosol generators (statewide) and aerial ULV application (Eastern Shore only). Active ingredients used include Permethrin, piperonyl butoxide, and naled. Communities share costs with the state. Participation is voluntary. Property owners/lessees may request exemption from spraying on their property and up to a 300-foot buffer zone. Services are provided to approximately 2,000 communities in 16 Maryland counties.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Communities, local governments, residents, pet owners, and domestic livestock owners in participating Maryland counties seeking mosquito control services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Mosquito surveillance and arbovirus disease testing, biological control, breeding ground reduction, larviciding, adulticiding (ground and aerial spraying), and public education to prevent mosquito-borne disease.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in 16 Maryland counties that have entered into cooperative agreements with MDA. Truck-mounted ground spraying is available statewide in participating counties; aerial application is limited to the Eastern Shore. Participating counties include Anne Arundel, Baltimore County, Baltimore City, Cecil, Charles, Dorchester, Harford, Howard, Kent, Prince George's, Queen Anne's, Somerset, St. Mary's, Talbot, and Worcester.
requirements_list: Participation is voluntary
Requires local government and/or community funding (communities share costs with the state)
Communities must be within a participating county that has a cooperative agreement with MDA
Property owners/lessees seeking exemption from spraying must submit a written request to the Maryland Department of Agriculture
Exemption requests must include copies provided to appropriate community association or relevant parties
Aerial application is limited to Eastern Shore communities only
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Communities submit mosquito complaints via the Online Mosquito Complaint Form. For spray exemptions, property owners/lessees complete and submit a written Adult Mosquito Control Exemption Form to the Maryland Department of Agriculture. Contact the program office directly for information on participating in services. County-specific contacts: St. Mary's: 301-373-4264/65; Charles: 1-888-523-0256; Baltimore & Harford: 1-877-425-6485; Prince George's/Central/Western MD: 301-422-5080; Anne Arundel: 410-841-5870; Queen Anne's: 410-758-2168; Eastern Shore: 410-543-6626.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Department of Agriculture and University of Maryland Extension offer training courses, certification exams, voucher training, and continuing education for farmers, consultants, and natural resource personnel on nutrient management planning, soil science, and related regulations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: In-person seminars, workshops, online webinars, and certification exams covering nutrient management planning, soil science, and state regulations. Some sessions are free; the Maryland Nutrient Management Certification Exam has a $50 non-refundable fee (government personnel exempt). Participants earn continuing education units (CEUs) applicable to nutrient management certification and recertification requirements.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Various dates through 2026; ongoing sessions available
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers, agricultural consultants, natural resource personnel, and turfgrass/fertilizer applicators seeking nutrient management training, certification, or continuing education credits.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and certification in nutrient management planning and soil conservation practices.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland; some events held at specific county locations.
requirements_list: Farmers applying nutrients to 10 or more acres must complete a 2-hour voucher training course every three years
Certification exam candidates must pay a $50 non-refundable fee (government personnel exempt with a Government Sales and Use Tax Exempt certificate)
Participants in software update sessions must be familiar with a keyboard/computer and able to retrieve and save files
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register for specific sessions via Eventbrite, Google Forms, or University of Maryland Extension links listed on the page. For the certification exam, use the provided Google Form registration link. For online webinars, access recorded sessions and complete the associated quiz to earn CEUs.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Farm Bill-funded program that reimburses organic producers and handlers for a portion of their organic certification fees. Eligible Maryland producers submit a cost share application to the Maryland Department of Agriculture to receive reimbursement after being issued their organic certificate.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement of 75% of organic certification fees, up to a maximum of $750 per certification scope. Reimbursement cannot be issued until the producer receives their certificate. Non-MDA certified producers must be located in Maryland and submit a copy of their certification fees invoice with their application. As of August 2025, USDA had not yet announced funding for 2025.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Not stated; applications posted when USDA announces funding
structured_extraction.program_audience: USDA-accredited certified organic producers and handlers in Maryland seeking reimbursement of certification costs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reimbursement of organic certification fees paid to USDA-accredited certifiers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to producers located in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be certified by a USDA-accredited certifier
Must be located in Maryland
Must submit a Cost Share Application to MDA Organic Certification Program
Non-MDA certified producers must submit a copy of their certification fees invoice
Reimbursement cannot be issued until the producer receives a certificate
Subject to annual USDA funding availability
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the Cost Share Application to the MDA Organic Certification Program. Application forms are posted when USDA announces funding. As of August 2025, 2025 funding had not yet been announced.

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary program that provides farmers and agricultural producers with an opportunity to safely dispose of unwanted, unused, banned, or expired pesticide materials at no cost. The Maryland Department of Agriculture (MDA) arranges collection of EPA- or USDA-registered pesticides directly from the farm or storage site and transports them to an EPA-approved disposal facility.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free collection and disposal of unusable, unwanted, banned, or expired pesticides. A licensed hazardous waste hauler collects the materials and transports them to an EPA-approved incinerator or hazardous waste landfill at no cost to the participant. Commercial businesses may be allowed to participate at MDA's contract cost. Unknown or unlabeled materials will be sampled and analyzed before collection.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Current or retired farmers and agricultural producers, including orchardists, nursery operators, greenhouse operators, and Christmas tree growers. Also individuals who purchased farms with large quantities of pesticides. Pesticide dealers and commercial applicators should contact MDA for applicability. Homeowners with household pesticides are not eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Covers the cost of collecting, transporting, and disposing of unwanted, unused, banned, or expired pesticides from farm or storage sites.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to Maryland farmers and agricultural producers across all 23 counties and Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a current or retired farmer or agricultural producer (including orchardists, nurserymen, greenhouse operators, and Christmas tree growers), or an individual who purchased a farm with large quantities of pesticides
Pesticides must have an EPA or USDA registration number, or be identifiable as a pesticide
Unknown materials will be sampled and tested by MDA before collection; cropping or use information must be provided for unknown materials
Complete registration form listing grower name, address, county, telephone, contact person, site address, directions, and name and amount of each pesticide for disposal
Maintain accurate inventory of pesticides for disposal
Allow MDA staff to inspect and verify pesticide types and amounts
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete the fillable PDF registration form. Submit the completed form by email to rob.hofstetter@maryland.gov or by mail to the MDA Pesticide Regulation Section at 50 Harry S Truman Pkwy, Annapolis, MD 21401. MDA staff will contact the applicant to arrange an inspection and verify pesticide types and amounts. Once a complete inventory is compiled, MDA will arrange for a licensed hauler to collect the materials.

structured_extraction.program_name: Poultry and Rabbit On-Farm Processing Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary certification program that allows Maryland producers to slaughter and process their own poultry and rabbits on-farm and sell the products intrastate — including to restaurants, retailers, and farmers markets — without continuous USDA inspection. Certified producers are recognized as an approved source by the Maryland Department of Health and Mental Hygiene. The program covers poultry (chickens, turkeys, ducks, geese) and rabbits, and requires producers to slaughter fewer than 20,000 poultry per year of their own production.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MDA provides certification and training to on-farm poultry and rabbit producers. Certification allows producers to sell directly to consumers, restaurants, retailers, and farmers markets anywhere in Maryland. Annual certification fee is $75. An online self-paced training course (approximately 6 hours) is required; producers must score 80% or better on an open-book exam to receive a training certificate. The program requires one person per facility to attend MDA training, compliance with basic program requirements, and facility access for MDA inspections. Certified producers may also store meat from USDA inspected facilities on-farm under MDA inspection instead of requiring a separate MDH license.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland farmers and producers who raise and slaughter poultry or rabbits of their own production on their farm and want to sell those products intrastate beyond direct farm sales.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Certification to sell on-farm processed poultry and rabbit products intrastate; access to training on processing requirements. Annual certification fee: $75.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to producers operating in Maryland; intrastate sales only.
requirements_list: At least one person from each facility must complete the MDA-required training (online self-paced course, ~6 hours) and score 80% or better on open-book exam
Annual limit of 20,000 poultry under federal FSIS inspection exemption
Slaughter limited to the producer's own production
No slaughter of sick animals; biosecurity measures required
Maintain clean animal production areas with rodent control
Protected slaughter/processing area to prevent contamination
Equipment capable of cleaning and sanitization
Use only potable water; annual water testing required (unless municipal source)
Adequate lighting for processing areas (especially if processing outside at night or in an enclosure)
Access to toilet and hand washing facilities
Chill animals to 40°F within 4-8 hours depending on weight; store at 40°F or less
Calibrated thermometers with recorded calibration dates
Personnel hygiene requirements (no smoking/eating/drinking during processing; no communicable diseases/open sores)
Written GMPs, SSOPs, and HACCP plans required
Use only USDA-compliant compounds
Compliance with MDE wastewater regulations (land application exemption, discharge permit, or approved septic system)
Submit product labels for approval (if new or changed)
Must abide by USDA/FSIS inspection exempt requirements
Must comply with all applicable federal, state, and local laws
Products may not be ground
Submit certification application with $75 fee and sample product label
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register for the online self-paced training course; receive course materials; complete course and exam (score 80% or better); submit exam results; receive training certificate; complete and submit the On-Farm Rabbit/Poultry Processing Application (new or renewal) with $75 fee and sample product label for approval. Renewal applications are due June 30. Contact Molly Gillingham at molly.gillingham@maryland.gov or Felicia Holland at Felicia.Holland@maryland.gov to be notified of upcoming training sessions.

structured_extraction.program_name: Program for the Certification of County Agricultural Land Preservation Programs (CLAPP)
structured_extraction.program_description: This program allows Maryland counties to retain a larger share of locally generated Agricultural Land Transfer Tax revenue in exchange for creating, maintaining, and improving effective local agricultural land preservation programs. Certified counties retain 75% of the Agricultural Land Transfer Tax (compared to 33% for uncertified counties), and must spend or commit those funds for land preservation within six years or they revert to the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Fund. Counties voluntarily apply for certification and must meet standards set jointly by the Maryland Department of Planning and the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation (MALPF) Board. Recertification is required every five years, aligned with comprehensive plan updates. As of June 30, 2019, 16 of Maryland's 23 counties are fully or conditionally certified.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Certified counties retain 75% of locally generated Agricultural Land Transfer Tax revenue (versus 33% for uncertified counties). Retained funds must be spent or encumbered for land preservation within six years or they revert to the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Fund. Funds can be used to purchase land preservation easements, participate in MALPF's Matching Funds Program, service past debt from land preservation activities, or cover administrative expenses for the county's land preservation program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland counties that have effective local agricultural land preservation programs and wish to retain a greater share of the Agricultural Land Transfer Tax revenue.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase land preservation easements, participate in MALPF's Matching Funds Program, service past debt from land preservation activities, or pay administrative expenses for the county's land preservation program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to all Maryland counties on a voluntary basis. As of June 30, 2019, 16 of Maryland's 23 counties are fully or conditionally certified.
requirements_list: County must have an effective local agricultural land preservation program
County must apply to both the Maryland Department of Planning and MALPF
Must be approved by the MALPF Board and Maryland Department of Planning
County must establish Priority Preservation Areas (PPAs) in its comprehensive plan
County must set a farmland preservation acreage goal for the PPA
County must use other land preservation tools such as protective agricultural zoning and transfer of development rights
Retained funds must be spent or encumbered within six years or they revert to the State fund
Recertification is required every five years (aligned with comprehensive plan updates)
Participation is voluntary
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested counties apply voluntarily to both the Maryland Department of Planning and MALPF. Counties seeking renewal apply for recertification every five years, aligned with their comprehensive plan updates.

structured_extraction.program_name: Registration of Service Agencies and Service Technicians
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Agriculture registers service agencies and service technicians who install, service, or repair commercially used weighing and measuring devices such as gas pump meters and scales. Registered agencies and technicians are added to a published list that device owners can use to find qualified service providers. Requires traceable standards certification from a NIST-approved state lab.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Applicants who pass a qualifying exam and meet requirements receive a biennial registration certificate and a registration number. Service agencies pay a $250 biennial registration fee. Service technicians pay a $75 biennial registration fee (with annual renewal option). Registered status is published in a department list. In-person class and exam proctoring is available for $25. The NCWM online exam option is also accepted; NCWM member exam fee is $50, non-member is $100, with an additional $20 for virtual proctoring or $25 for in-person proctoring at MDA headquarters.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Service agencies and individual technicians who install, service, or repair commercial weighing and measuring devices in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Registration authorizes service agencies and technicians to place commercial weighing and measuring devices into service. Fees cover registration, licensing, and exam administration costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Classes held in person at 50 Harry S. Truman Pkwy, Annapolis, MD 21401.
requirements_list: Applicant must complete the appropriate application form (New Service Agency form or New Service Agency/Technician form) and email it to [email protected].
Service agency must provide a copy of their test/service report forms.

Service agency must provide a copy of ALL current certificates showing that their standards have been approved by the Maryland Weights and Measures Laboratory, NIST, or another NIST-approved state metrology laboratory.
Service technician applicant must work for a registered Service Agency.

Service technician applicant must pass the qualifying examination: either the State of Maryland in-person class/exam ($25) or the NCWM exam ($50 for members, $100 for non-members), with optional virtual proctoring ($20) or in-person proctoring at MDA headquarters ($25).
Biennial registration fee: $250 for service agencies, $75 for service technicians.
Renewal of registration is required on a biennial (every two years) basis for service agencies; annual renewal option available for service technicians.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Fill out the applicable application form (New Service Agency or New Service Technician) and email it along with required certificates and materials to [email protected]. State Weights and Measures staff review the submission and notify applicants of any deficiencies. Once the review is complete, applicants pay the biennial fee. For technicians, passing a qualifying exam is required before registration is issued. Applicants may take the in-person class at MDA headquarters or use the NCWM online exam option. Upon completion, applicants receive a registration number and certificate (or wallet-size ID card for technicians).

structured_extraction.program_description: The RFSI Program builds resilience in the middle of the food supply chain by supporting aggregation, processing, storing, transporting, wholesaling, and distribution of local and regional food products. It provides grants to help small farms and food businesses develop value-added products, access better markets, receive fair prices and wages, and create safe job opportunities. Two grant types are available: Infrastructure Grants and Simplified Equipment-Only Grants.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two grant types are available: (1) Infrastructure Grants ranging from $100,000 to $3,000,000 per project, running for three years, requiring a 50% match of total proposed project cost (reduced to 25% for historically underserved farmers/ranchers and qualifying small businesses including small disadvantaged businesses, women-owned small businesses, and veteran-owned small businesses); (2) Simplified Equipment-Only Grants ranging from $10,000 to $100,000, with no matching requirements, for equipment purchases only (fixed price grants). MDA has approximately $3.6-3.8 million total from a USDA cooperative agreement to award.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Food businesses, farms, processors, aggregators, distributors, wholesalers, cooperatives, institutions (schools, universities, hospitals), local and tribal government entities involved in local/regional food supply chains, including historically underserved farmers and ranchers and qualifying small businesses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cold storage equipment, expanding capacity for processing, aggregation, and distribution, construction or expansion of new or existing facilities, employee training, modernizing manufacturing, tracking, storage, and IT systems, worker safety improvements, food safety compliance capacity, packaging and labeling capacity. Funds support projects related to aggregation, processing, storing, transporting, wholesaling, and distribution of locally and regionally produced food products including specialty crops, dairy, grains for human consumption, aquaculture, and other food products (excluding meat and poultry, wild-caught seafood, animal feed, forage, fiber, landscaping products, tobacco, and dietary supplements).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Facilities must be physically located within Maryland. Applicants doing business along the Maryland border should only apply in one state to avoid duplication of federal funds.
requirements_list: Infrastructure Grants: minimum $100,000, maximum $3,000,000; Equipment-Only Grants: minimum $10,000, maximum $100,000
Infrastructure Grant projects must last three years

Infrastructure Grant applicants must provide a 50% match of total proposed project cost (reduced to 25% for historically underserved farmers/ranchers and qualifying small businesses under SBA definitions)
Equipment-Only Grants require no matching funds
For-profit entities must meet SBA small business size standards

Projects must relate to aggregation, processing, storing, transporting, wholesaling, or distribution of local/regional food products (excluding meat and poultry, wild-caught seafood, animal feed, forage, fiber, landscaping products, tobacco, dietary supplements)
Facilities must be physically located within Maryland
Must submit USDA Applicant Environmental Questionnaire with application
Receipts required for single purchases over $1,000
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review the RFP and informational webinar materials. Complete either the Infrastructure Equipment Grant application or Equipment Grant Only application (fillable PDF). Include the USDA Applicant Environmental Questionnaire, Match Verification Template Letter, Evidence of Critical Resources and Infrastructure Template Letter, and RFSI Budget-Match Worksheet. Submit completed application to MDA by March 15, 2024 at 11:59 pm EST.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides financial assistance to urban and small-scale producers who want to plant cover crops but do not qualify for traditional cover crop grant programs designed for larger farm operations. Growers are reimbursed for the cost of planting cover crops on less than 10 acres. The program supports soil health goals by encouraging planting of cover crop mixes during fallow periods and terminating winter cover crops in spring. Benefits include increased biological activity of soil, reduced leaching of excess crop nutrients into groundwater, immobilization of unused nitrogen from root zone, and reduced soil erosion.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement grants of up to $1,500 per grower per year. Eligible expenses include seed costs (including shipping), labor (capped at $15/hour), custom services, and equipment rental fees directly related to cover crop planting. Reimbursement is based on submitted receipts and proof of payment. Eligible species include single cereal grains or cover crop seed mixes planted in open fields, raised beds, or high tunnels.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: March 16 through April 24, 2026; documentation must be submitted by December 31, 2027
structured_extraction.program_audience: Urban and small-scale agricultural producers, including individual growers, for-profit agricultural businesses, and non-profit organizations that farm less than 10 acres of cover crops and generate at least $1,000 in annual sales or donations from farm products grown in Maryland. Farm operators must be currently farming land under consistent cropping rotation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of cover crop seeds (single cereal grains or seed mixes) for planting on less than 10 acres, including seed shipping costs; labor costs (capped at $15/hour); custom services and equipment rental fees directly related to cover crop planting.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Farm product must be grown or raised in Maryland. Operators must be farming land they currently operate.
requirements_list: Must plant less than 10 acres of cover crops
Operation must produce at least $1,000 in sales or donations annually
Farm product must be grown or raised in Maryland
Applicant may be an individual grower, for-profit agricultural business, or non-profit organization
Must comply with all local, state, and federal regulations and secure required permits
Cover crops must be planted following seed manufacturer or University of Maryland Extension recommendations
Own or lease/rent enrolled land
Current Nutrient Management Plan or Nutrient Management Conditional Exception required
Plant cover crop mix during fallow periods
Terminate winter cover crop after March 1, 2027 (or February 15, 2027 for early season vegetables with planting within 2 weeks)
Maintain control of enrolled land for agreement duration
Provide receipts and proof of payment
Maintain Soil & Water Conservation Plan (if applicable)
Plant annual cover crops on currently farmed land under consistent cropping rotation
Follow seed company recommended seeding rates (or increase by 25% for certain planting methods)
Provide aerial photograph or sketch of area to be planted
Commercial seed must be tested and labeled per Maryland Seed Law, with minimum 80% germination and no more than 16 restricted noxious weed seeds per pound
Use one of six approved planting methods
Properly maintain cover crop for duration of agreement
Submit documentation by December 31, 2027
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete the 2026 Small Acreage Cover Crop Program Application form. Submit during the enrollment period (March 16 – April 24, 2026) along with a map of cover crop location and Nutrient Management Certification or Conditional Exception form. Sign the Program Requirements and Agreement. After planting, submit paid receipts and proof of payment for reimbursement. All documentation must be submitted by December 31, 2027.

structured_extraction.program_name: Small Farm and Urban Agriculture Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides financial assistance to small-scale agricultural operations in urban, peri-urban, rural, and suburban areas of Maryland. The program helps farmers adopt Bay-friendly and climate-smart farming practices to improve natural resource management and increase community access to healthy foods.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are available through two sub-programs: Small Acreage Cover Crop Grants (offered in spring and fall) and Water and Power Grants for qualifying operations in urban areas. Other grant programs are under development. Funding comes from the Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays Trust Fund.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals, for-profit agricultural businesses, and non-profit organizations operating small-scale farms in Maryland that generate at least $1,000 in sales or donations annually from a farm product grown or raised in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Adoption of Bay-friendly and climate-smart farming practices, cover crops, and water and power infrastructure improvements for qualifying agricultural operations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Farm product must be grown or raised in the state of Maryland. Water and Power Grants are limited to operations in urban areas.
requirements_list: Must be an individual, organized for-profit agricultural business, or non-profit organization
Operation must produce a farm product generating a minimum of $1,000 in sales or donations annually
Farm product must be grown or raised in Maryland
Grantee is responsible for all local, state, and federal regulations and permits required for the agricultural operation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the program for the specific grant type (Small Acreage Cover Crop Grants or Water and Power Grants). Contact the program administrator for details.

structured_extraction.program_name: Soil Conservation Districts Technical Assistance Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Office of Resource Conservation provides Maryland's 23 soil conservation districts with operating funds and staffing support to deliver free technical and engineering assistance to landowners, farmers, and horse owners. District staff help design and install best management practices (BMPs) on farms and properties to protect natural resources and comply with environmental laws. Districts also develop Soil Conservation and Water Quality Plans required by many federal and state conservation programs. The program also provides free consultation on permit and authorization requirements for work in streams, floodplains, and wetlands, and supports farmers in navigating federal and state cost-share programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free technical and engineering assistance to design and install best management practices on farms and properties. Assistance includes developing Soil Conservation and Water Quality Plans required by federal and state conservation programs, free farm evaluation and natural resource inventory, soil mapping, best management practice recommendations, and operation and maintenance guidance. The Maryland Agricultural Water Quality Cost-Share (MACS) Program provides grants covering up to 100% of eligible BMP installation costs. Technical assistance also covers permit and authorization requirements for work in streams, floodplains, and wetlands. Services are delivered through 24 local soil conservation district offices across Maryland.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners, farmers, horse owners, and agricultural producers seeking free technical or engineering assistance to install best management practices on their land, manage soil erosion, protect water quality, and comply with environmental laws.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Design and installation of best management practices to protect natural resources, comply with environmental laws, and develop Soil Conservation and Water Quality Plans. Eligible uses include stream crossing installation, streambank stabilization, exclusion fencing, erosion and sediment control measures, buffer area establishment, rotational grazing, cover crops, manure management, nutrient management, pasture management, wildlife habitat enhancement, and other conservation practices.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through 24 local soil conservation districts across Maryland, including farms in the Chesapeake Bay watershed, coastal zone, and western regions.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a landowner, farmer, or horse owner in Maryland
Most activities in streams, floodplains, and wetlands require prior permits or authorizations before work begins
Nutrient management plan required for all Maryland agricultural land
Soil testing required at least every three years
Manure testing required every other year if used
Some livestock and poultry farms required to obtain farm plans as part of CAFO permitting process
Many federal and state programs require Soil Conservation and Water Quality Plans
Comply with federal, state, and local laws and regulations
Obtain necessary permits for certain structures or restoration activities
Work with local soil conservation district for many practices
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local soil conservation district office directly. A list of all 24 district offices with phone numbers is provided on the program page. District staff will conduct a farm evaluation and develop a personalized conservation plan. Obtain necessary federal, state, and local permits before beginning restoration or construction work.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's lawn fertilizer certification and licensing program that regulates how lawn care professionals and homeowners apply fertilizer to protect the Chesapeake Bay from excess nitrogen and phosphorus runoff. The program requires lawn care professionals to become certified and licensed under the Fertilizer Use Act of 2011, sets fertilizer application rules and blackout dates, and provides training and exams for certification. It also includes an annual reporting requirement for fertilizer applications made to turf during the calendar year, tracking nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium nutrient applications by county.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides fertilizer applicator training, certification exams offered throughout the year, and recertification classes and webinars. Professional Fertilizer Applicator Certificates are valid through December 31 each year and may be renewed for a $100 fee with verification of recertification training. Business licenses are required for individuals and companies that apply fertilizer commercially and are valid for up to one year; the application fee is $50 for private companies and no fee for government agencies. Exam locations are in Annapolis (Anne Arundel County), Derwood (Montgomery County), Boonsboro (Washington County), and Salisbury (Wicomico County).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Certificates and licenses must be renewed annually by December 31; Annual Fertilizer Application Report due no later than March 1
structured_extraction.program_audience: Lawn care professionals, turf managers at golf courses, parks, airports, athletic fields, businesses, cemeteries, and other non-agricultural properties, as well as homeowners who apply fertilizer to their own lawns. Also includes businesses and government agencies employing certified fertilizer applicators.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Certification training and exams for lawn fertilizer applicators; compliance with Maryland's lawn fertilizer law to protect the Chesapeake Bay. Certification application fee of $100; business license fee of $50 for private companies (no fee for government agencies).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Exam locations in Annapolis, Derwood, Boonsboro, and Salisbury.
requirements_list: Lawn care professionals must be certified by the Maryland Department of Agriculture or work under direct supervision of a certified individual.
Businesses and individuals that fertilize turf for hire must obtain a business license (MDA-F).
At least one Maryland Certified Professional Fertilizer Applicator must be on staff for a business license.
Employees must be registered and work under direct supervision of a certified applicator.
PFA certification application requires a $100 fee; business license application requires a $50 fee (no fee for government agencies).
A score of 70% or better is required to pass the certification exam.
Government-issued photo ID required for exam entry.
Calculator (not cell phone) and two #2 pencils required for exam; no cell phones allowed in testing room.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation (MALPF) / Agricultural Preservation Easement Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation (MALPF) is a state-level voluntary purchase of development rights (PDR) program administered by the Maryland Department of Agriculture with county participation. It acquires permanent agricultural preservation easements on qualifying agricultural and woodland parcels to prevent conversion to non-agricultural uses. Property owners sell development rights to the State, receiving payment while permanently restricting their land to agricultural use in perpetuity. Payment equals the landowner's asking price, the difference between the appraised fair market value and the agricultural value, or a maximum of 75% of the appraised fair market value — whichever is less. In recent years, payments have ranged from $600 to over $10,000 per acre. If the easement is sold for less than its full appraised value, the landowner may also qualify for certain tax benefits. Properties are ranked by soil quality, proximity to other easements, farming intensity, and proximity to growth areas. The program preserves productive agricultural land and woodland to ensure continued food and fiber production, protect farmland from urban development, preserve open space, curb urban sprawl, and support wildlife habitat and water quality in the Chesapeake and Coastal Bays. Since 1980, the program has invested over $900 million and preserved over 350,000 acres, making it one of the most successful programs of its kind in the United States. The program is administered locally by each county; Harford County's agricultural preservation coordinator serves as the local program administrator, and the easements include limited subdivision rights reserved for the original grantor and immediate family members. Washington County has paid over $49.8 million to preserve more than 17,000 acres; over 3,000 acres in Worcester County are currently permanently protected; Anne Arundel County participates with recent offers ranging from approximately $8,000 to $11,000 per acre (up to 75% of appraised Fair Market Value of development rights); Charles County has preserved more than 10,000 acres through the program; and in Caroline County, the state has paid between $2,000 and $4,000 per acre for easements in recent years. Cecil County participates through its local Planning & Zoning Division and Agricultural Preservation Advisory Board, requiring a valid Soil Conservation and Water Quality Plan on file with the Cecil Soil Conservation District. Eligible entity types include trusts, limited partnerships, LLCs, and corporations. Applicants may reserve family lots (up to 3, tied to the original owner) or unrestricted lots, or waive all rights to new building lots.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Agriculture / Washington County / Talbot County / Worcester County / Anne Arundel County / Charles County / Caroline County / Cecil County / Harford County
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MALPF purchases permanent agricultural preservation easements on eligible farmland and/or woodland from property owners. Payment equals the landowner's asking price, the difference between the appraised fair market value and the agricultural value, or a maximum of 75% of the appraised fair market value — whichever is less. In recent years, payments have ranged from $600 to over $10,000 per acre. Recent Anne Arundel County offers ranged from approximately $8,000 to $11,000 per acre. Washington County has paid over $49.8 million to preserve more than 17,000 acres. Worcester County retains 75% of the agricultural transfer tax collected for farmland protection and receives additional state funds, with over 3,000 acres currently permanently protected. Charles County has preserved more than 10,000 acres through the program. In Caroline County, the state has paid between $2,000 and $4,000 per acre for easements in recent years. Cecil County landowners receive payment for permanently retiring development rights while continuing to own and operate the farm. Harford County easements include limited subdivision rights reserved for the original grantor and immediate family members. Applicants may reserve family lots (up to 3, tied to the original owner) or unrestricted lots (subdivideable or non-subdivideable building envelope), or waive all rights to new building lots; landowners must pay back a per-acre amount if exercising the unrestricted lot option. If the easement is sold for less than its full appraised value, the landowner may also qualify for certain tax benefits. The program has invested over $900 million and preserved over 350,000 acres since 1980. Easement restrictions remain in perpetuity.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of eligible prime farmland and/or woodland in Maryland, including Washington County, Talbot County, Worcester County, Anne Arundel County, Charles County, Caroline County, Cecil County, and Harford County, who want to permanently protect their land for agricultural use in exchange for payment of an easement. Eligible applicants include individual landowners as well as entities such as trusts, limited partnerships, LLCs, limited liability limited partnerships, and corporations.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland law allows land that is actively used for farming or agriculture to be assessed at its agricultural use value rather than its full market value, significantly reducing the property tax burden for qualifying farmland owners. Qualifying farmland is assessed at $500 per acre, woodland under a Forest Conservation Management Agreement is assessed at $125 per acre, and land under a forest stewardship plan is assessed at $187.50 per acre — all instead of full market value. For example, a 100-acre parcel with a $3,000/acre market value would be taxed on $50,000 (agricultural value) instead of $300,000 (market value), saving roughly $2,780 in taxes annually. Woodland parcels enrolled in a Forest Conservation Management Agreement with the Maryland Department of Natural Resources also qualify for the $125 per acre rate. The program works in conjunction with Maryland's Agricultural Land Preservation Program, serving as a deterrent to land conversion, a penalty for removing land from preferential use, and a funding mechanism for easement purchases. Note: lands receiving this assessment may be subject to an Agricultural Transfer Tax if transferred or converted to non-agricultural use.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Qualifying farmland is assessed at a preferential agricultural use value — currently $500 per acre for farmland, $125 per acre for land in a Forest Conservation Management Agreement (woodland parcels enrolled with the Maryland Department of Natural Resources, minimum 5 acres, plan by a professional registered forester), and $187.50 per acre for land in a forest stewardship plan — instead of full market value. This reduces the property tax owed. For example, a 100-acre parcel with a $3,000/acre market value would be taxed on $50,000 (agricultural value) instead of $300,000 (market value), saving roughly $2,780 in taxes annually using a combined rate of $1.112 per $100 of assessment. Agricultural Transfer Tax revenues also fund purchase of development rights/easements on existing farms through the Agricultural Land Preservation Program. Note: lands receiving this assessment may be subject to an Agricultural Transfer Tax if transferred or converted to non-agricultural use.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of land actively devoted to farm or agricultural use, including woodland under an approved forest management plan or Forest Conservation Management Agreement, located anywhere in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of property tax liability through lower assessed value on qualifying agricultural or forested land. Agricultural Transfer Tax revenues fund purchase of development rights/easements on existing farms through the Agricultural Land Preservation Program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across all 23 Maryland counties and Baltimore City. Some counties impose an additional local agricultural transfer tax.
requirements_list: Land must be actively and primarily used for a continuing farm or agricultural use.
Parcels under 3 acres are generally not eligible unless specific exceptions apply (e.g., adjoining qualified land, 51% gross income from the parcel, or family farm unit).
Homesites are excluded from the agricultural use assessment and are valued at market value.
Land rezoned to a more intensive use at the owner's request is not eligible.
Parcels between 3 and 5 acres must meet a $2,500 average gross income test from agricultural activity.
Parcels between 5 and 20 acres may need to meet the $2,500 gross income test if the extent of agricultural activity is difficult to determine.
Woodland under a forest management plan must consist of at least 5 acres; the plan must be prepared by a professional registered forester.
No more than 5 parcels under 10 acres in the same county and no more than 2 parcels under 3 acres statewide per ownership may qualify under subdivision plat rules.

For the Forest Conservation Management Agreement rate: parcel must have a minimum of 5 acres of woodland within the forest management plan (excluding homesite); parcels may not be combined to reach the 5-acre minimum; plan must be provided by the State Department of Natural Resources pursuant to the Forest Conservation Management Agreement; property owner must submit compliance with the plan to the Department at required intervals.
Must complete agricultural use application approved by the Department of Assessments and Taxation.
For Declaration of Intent: commitment to maintain agricultural use for 5 full consecutive taxable years.
Must notify Assessment Office 7 days prior to recording deed if improvements are made.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the local Assessment Office in the county where the property is located. For woodland parcels under a Forest Conservation Management Agreement, first obtain the agreement through the Maryland Department of Natural Resources, then contact your local Assessment Office to apply the agricultural use assessment. The Department of Assessments and Taxation evaluates whether land qualifies based on the nature and extent of agricultural activity, parcel size, land use ratios, and other criteria defined in COMAR Title 18 and the Maryland Assessment Procedures Manual.

structured_extraction.program_name: Assessment Exemption for an Improvement Required for the Health or Medical Condition of a Resident
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides a property tax assessment exemption for new improvements, changes, or additions to residential buildings that are specifically required by the health or medical condition of a resident. The improvement must add value to the property and be medically necessary. The exemption amount may not exceed 10% of the total market value of the real property (land and improvement combined). The exemption applies for the current tax year in which the application is received and is removed in the next full tax year after the individual whose condition required the improvement no longer resides in the building. Based on Tax Property Article Section 8-233.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that allows Maryland homeowners and property owners to permanently buy out (redeem) their ground rent obligation, converting their leasehold property interest into full ownership. Ground rent is a recurring payment owed to a landlord when a home sits on leased land. Homeowners submit an application and a lump-sum payment to the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT), which then issues a Certificate of Redemption. The program includes separate application forms depending on whether the homeowner has or has not received a bill or communication in the past three years, and also addresses irredeemable ground rents. Both individual tenants and business entities may apply.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Homeowners and property owners submit an application and a processing fee ($70 for expedited 5-week processing, or $20 for regular 9-week processing) to SDAT's Ground Rent Department at 700 East Pratt Street, 2nd Floor, Suite 2700, Baltimore, Maryland 21202. Required documents include a recorded deed establishing property interest and a recorded document establishing existence of ground rent. After receiving approval, and no sooner than 100 days later, the homeowner submits an Affidavit of Certificate of Redemption and a lump-sum redemption payment via certified check or money order (personal or business checks not accepted) payable to 'SDAT'. SDAT then issues a Certificate of Redemption, which must be recorded with the county land records office to permanently remove the ground rent obligation. Ground rent owners/landlords may also submit a Ground Rent Owner Request for Payment form to receive redemption funds from SDAT.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Review the ground rent checklist and search for irredeemable ground rents. Gather required publicly recorded documents (deed and ground rent lease). Step 3: Notify the ground rent owner of intent to redeem via certified mail. structured_extraction.program_description: The Homeowner Protection Program (HPP) is a statewide Maryland program that helps limited income, elderly, and disabled homeowners navigate the tax sale process. If approved, the program can keep a home out of tax sale for at least three years and may also provide short-term loans and individualized assistance to help homeowners pay overdue property taxes and avoid losing their homes due to tax sale or foreclosure. Eligible homeowners must use the home as their principal residence, have a property assessed value not exceeding $300,000, combined household income no more than $60,000 annually, and total assets (excluding the dwelling) not exceeding $200,000. Priority enrollment is given to homeowners aged 60 or older, those receiving federal Social Security Disability Insurance or Supplemental Security Income benefits, or those who have lived in the home for 10 or more years. Enrollment is limited and eligibility does not guarantee enrollment. A donation portal is also available for community members to contribute to the program.
