Provides a low-interest loan to pay delinquent property taxes with affordable monthly payments based on the applicant's ability to pay. Connects homeowners with resources and support to help them remain in their home. Enrollment is limited and eligibility does not guarantee enrollment. A donation portal is also available for community members to contribute to the program.

structured_extraction.program_name: Homeowners' Property Tax Credit Program (with Local Supplement)
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Homeowners' Property Tax Credit Program, administered by the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation, limits the amount of property taxes a homeowner must pay based on their income. If a homeowner's property taxes exceed a fixed percentage of their gross household income, the state issues a credit to reduce their tax bill. Credits appear on tax bills and reduce the amount due; if a credit is issued after taxes are already paid, a refund is automatically issued. The program is available to homeowners of all ages throughout Maryland who qualify based on household income relative to their property tax obligation. Combined gross household income must be under $60,000 and net worth under $200,000 (excluding the home and qualified retirement savings). Homeowners must re-apply each year between February 1 and October 1. A single application also covers the Montgomery County Supplemental Homeowners Property Tax Credit, the Montgomery County Senior Tax Credit, and serves as the Baltimore County Local Supplement application. Anne Arundel County also offers a supplemental credit administered through the same program. Baltimore County also offers a supplemental credit that applies only to county property taxes, available to eligible homeowners experiencing a hardship on their primary dwelling on a one-time basis. Baltimore County homeowners aged 70 or older may qualify for an additional local credit. Frederick County also offers a county supplemental tax credit alongside the state credit, with a local application deadline of September 1. Worcester County homeowners whose principal residence is subject to real property tax are also eligible. In Cecil County, applications received after May 1 that are approved will be refunded by the Cecil County Finance Office if the tax bill has already been paid. St. Mary's County residents age 70 and older who receive the credit may also receive an additional credit equal to the remaining tax bill (less the Bay Restoration Fund fee). Applications are also available at senior centers in Calvert County. Low-income applicants can get help completing applications through Benefits Data Trust - Maryland Benefits Center at (855) 444-4994. Applications can also be submitted at the Caroline County Tax Office or the State Department of Assessments for Caroline County. Harford County homeowners of all ages may also apply for the credit based on gross household income, with applications and instructions available through the Harford County government website for each tax year. Queen Anne's County homeowners may also access program information and apply through the Queen Anne's County Tax Credits page.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A credit is applied against the homeowner's property tax bill for the amount by which property taxes exceed a set percentage of gross household income. The state credit formula is: 0% of the first $8,000 of household income, 4% of the next $4,000, 6.5% of the next $4,000, and 9% of income above $16,000. The credit applies only to taxes on the first $300,000 of assessed value. Homeowners who apply by April 15 receive the credit directly on their initial July tax bill; those who apply by October 1 receive a revised tax bill or refund check. If the credit is issued after taxes are paid, a refund is automatically issued. In Cecil County, applications received after May 1 that are approved will be refunded by the Cecil County Finance Office if the tax bill has already been paid. Baltimore County provides a local supplement: the credit equals the difference between actual property taxes and the tax limit shown in the income table (ranging from $160 for $12,000 household income up to $1,680 plus $90 per $1,000 above $30,000 for incomes up to $60,000); homeowners aged 70 or older may qualify for an additional local credit. The Baltimore County supplemental credit applies only to county property taxes, is available on a one-time basis for eligible homeowners experiencing a hardship on their primary dwelling, and does not require a separate application — applicants must apply for the state credit to be considered. Anne Arundel County also offers a supplemental credit administered through the same program. The Baltimore County application deadline is September 1; the statewide deadline is October 1. Frederick County also offers a county supplemental tax credit in addition to the state credit, with a local deadline of September 1. Worcester County homeowners may also receive a credit against property taxes on their principal residence based on household income and taxes levied. St. Mary's County residents age 70 and over who qualify can receive an additional credit up to the amount of their remaining tax bill (excluding the Bay Restoration Fund fee). Harford County homeowners may apply annually for the credit using the application and instructions available for each tax year. Applications are also available at senior centers in Calvert County. Homeowners must re-apply each year.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: October 1 of each year (apply by April 15 to receive credit on initial July tax bill); applications accepted between February 1 and October 1. Baltimore County and Frederick County local supplement deadline is September 1. Cecil County: file by October 1 to have credit shown on tax bill.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland homeowners of all ages whose property tax bill exceeds a set percentage of their gross household income, and who qualify based on income relative to their total property tax obligation. Combined gross household income must be under $60,000 and net worth under $200,000 (excluding the home and qualified retirement savings). Anne Arundel County homeowners may also qualify for a supplemental credit. Baltimore County homeowners aged 70 or older may qualify for an additional local credit. Frederick County homeowners may also qualify for a county supplemental credit. Worcester County homeowners with a principal residence subject to real property tax are also eligible. Cecil County homeowners must meet income requirements set by the State. St. Mary's County residents age 70 and over may receive an enhanced additional credit. Calvert County residents may obtain applications at local senior centers. Harford County homeowners of all ages who qualify based on gross household income are also eligible. Queen Anne's County homeowners may access program information through the county Tax Credits page.

The credit applies to the real property tax bill, excluding fixed metropolitan charges, excess land acreage, business portions, or rental portions. Anne Arundel County, Baltimore County, Frederick County, Worcester County, Cecil County, Harford County, and St. Mary's County each provide additional local supplement credits or refund processes for eligible homeowners.

Frederick County offers a county supplemental credit with a September 1 deadline. Worcester County homeowners in Maryland are also eligible. In Cecil County, the first application must be obtained from the Assessment Office or the Cecil County Finance Office; applications received after May 1 are refunded by the Cecil County Finance Office if taxes have already been paid. structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Homestead Property Tax Credit Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland requires all homeowners to submit a one-time application to establish eligibility for the Homestead Tax Credit. The credit limits how much a homeowner's taxable property assessment can increase each year, capping annual increases at a fixed percentage set by each county or municipality (10% or less per year for most of Maryland; 5% for the Town of Kensington in Montgomery County). State law requires counties and municipalities to set a Homestead Credit Percentage between 0% and 10%. For example, if a home's assessed value rises from $100,000 to $120,000, only $110,000 is taxable; the homeowner receives a credit on the tax owed for the $10,000 difference. Every county and municipality in Maryland is required to participate, and only one application is needed per property for the lifetime of ownership. The credit applies to owner-occupied residential properties and is based on the combined land and dwelling assessment. The credit is not applicable in the first year after purchasing a new home. A Homestead Tax Credit application on file with SDAT by May 1, 2026 is also required to receive the Montgomery County Income Tax Offset Credit (ITOC) of $692 on future tax bills beginning July 1, 2026. New purchasers will be mailed an application after their deed is recorded, and applicants must provide their Social Security number on the application. The credit applies regardless of property value or income level, and credit eligibility remains in place as long as the dwelling remains the primary residence.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A credit applied to property taxes that limits the increase in a home's taxable assessment to a cap set by each county or municipality (10% or less per year for most jurisdictions; 5% for the Town of Kensington in Montgomery County). State law requires counties and municipalities to set a Homestead Credit Percentage between 0% and 10%. Homeowners pay no property tax on the portion of any reassessment that exceeds the local cap. For example, if a home's assessed value rises from $100,000 to $120,000, only $110,000 is taxable; the homeowner receives a credit on the tax owed for the $10,000 difference. The credit is not applicable in the first year after purchasing a new home. Homeowners submit a one-time application to establish eligibility (required since 2008), after which the credit applies automatically each year for the duration of ownership. County governments set their own assessment caps, which can result in substantial credits for eligible homeowners. Additionally, a Homestead Tax Credit application on file with SDAT by May 1, 2026 is required to receive the Montgomery County Income Tax Offset Credit (ITOC) of $692 on future tax bills beginning July 1, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland homeowners who own and use their property as their principal residence and seek protection from large annual property assessment increases, including owner-occupants of residential properties throughout the state, including those in Charles County and Montgomery County. Married couples are limited to one principal residence.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduces property tax owed on assessment increases above the local annual cap on the owner's principal residence; limits taxable assessment increases on principal residence.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland; every county and municipality in Maryland is required to participate, including all 24 Maryland counties. In Montgomery County the cap is 10% for most areas and 5% for the Town of Kensington.
requirements_list: Property must be the owner's principal residence
Property must be used as the single principal residence of the homeowner(s), currently and expected to be used next calendar year
Owner must have lived in the property for at least six months of the year, including July 1 of the tax year (unless temporarily unable due to illness)
Owner can receive the credit on only one property
Property must not have been transferred to new ownership in the previous tax year
No owner-requested zoning change that increased property value
No substantial change in use of the property
Previous assessment must not have been clearly erroneous
One-time application must be filed with SDAT to establish eligibility (required beginning 2008)
Applicant must be a homeowner in Maryland
Not applicable in the first year after purchase of a new home
A Homestead Tax Credit application on file with SDAT by May 1, 2026 is required to receive the Montgomery County Income Tax Offset Credit (ITOC) of $692 on future tax bills
Must complete the Homestead Tax Credit Eligibility Application (HST) and submit to the State Department of Assessments and Taxation
Must provide Social Security number on the application
Property cannot be a vacation home or rental property; no portion of the principal residence can be rented
Assessment of principal residence must have increased more than the applicable local cap percentage over the prior year to trigger the credit
Property address must be where homeowner(s) file their federal and Maryland income tax return (if filing)
Property address must match MD driver's license or identification card address (if applicable)
Property address must match voter registration (if registered)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Check your Homestead Application status on the SDAT Real Property Search page — if it shows 'Approved' or 'Application Received,' no action is needed. Step 2: If your status shows 'No Application,' apply online through the Maryland OneStop portal at https://onestop.md.gov (browse to Department of Assessments & Taxation, then select 'Homestead Tax Credit Eligibility Application'), or through the dedicated portal at https://sdathtc.dat.maryland.gov, using your Real Property Account Number. Alternatively, download and complete the paper application (available at https://dat.maryland.gov/realproperty/Documents/Homestead_application.pdf) and mail or fax it to the Homestead Tax Credit Division in Baltimore. New purchasers will be mailed an application after their deed is recorded. Applicants can also schedule an in-person service appointment at 123 Market Place, Baltimore, MD 21202, or call 866-650-8783 for more information. Only one application is needed for the lifetime of ownership of the property. Once approved, the credit is subsequently administered automatically by SDAT each year when the assessment increase exceeds the applicable threshold. For additional assistance, contact SDAT at sdat.homestead@maryland.gov or 410-767-2165.

structured_extraction.program_name: MarylandSaves WorkLife Savings Account and Annual Report Fee Waiver
structured_extraction.program_description: MarylandSaves is a state-mandated workplace savings program that requires eligible Maryland employers to offer employees a way to save for retirement through automatic payroll contributions into a portable WorkLife Account (Roth IRA). Workers are automatically enrolled through their employer but can opt out or adjust their contribution level at any time; the account stays with the worker through job changes. The default contribution rate starts at 5% of each paycheck, increasing by 1% per year up to 10%. The first $1,000 is placed in an Emergency Savings Fund; additional funds go into a Target Retirement Date fund. Investment options include Emergency Savings Fund, Target Retirement Date funds, Bond Index, and Global Growth Stock funds. Account fees are $30 per year ($24 to administrator, $6 to MarylandSaves) plus annualized asset-based fees ranging from 0.18% to 0.87% depending on investment choices. Self-employed individuals and independent contractors can also sign up directly. Most Maryland private-sector employers are required by law to either offer a qualified retirement plan or enroll in MarylandSaves. Employer registration is free and employers are not required to make contributions themselves. Businesses enrolled in MarylandSaves may have their SDAT Annual Report filing fee waived. Employers who enroll in MarylandSaves and remain qualified participants receive a $300 waiver on their SDAT Annual Report filing fee for each year they remain enrolled. Eligible businesses are identified by MarylandSaves and a list of approved SDAT IDs is published each year. Employers must register and submit payroll contributions (or claim an exemption) before December 31 to qualify for the SDAT fee exemption the following year (note: the deadline for the 2025 Annual Report fee exemption was December 1, 2024). The program is free for employers to facilitate and helps businesses recruit and retain employees. The program is administered by Vestwell State Savings, LLC (dba Sumday Administration) with The Bank of New York Mellon as custodian, under the governance of the Maryland Small Business Retirement Savings Board.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Workers contribute a portion of their paycheck (as little as 1%, with a default of 5% increasing by 1% annually up to 10% maximum; contributions must be whole-number percentages) into a personal WorkLife savings account (Roth IRA) that can be used for emergencies and retirement. The first $1,000 is placed in an Emergency Savings Fund; additional funds go into a Target Retirement Date fund. Investment options include Emergency Savings Fund, Target Retirement Date funds (2025–2065), Bond Index Option, and Global Growth Stock Option. Contributions have the potential to grow tax-free over time, and participation is voluntary — workers can opt out and rejoin at any time. Account fees are $30 per year ($24 to administrator, $6 to MarylandSaves) plus annualized asset-based fees ranging from 0.18% to 0.87% depending on investment choices. Contributions held for 7 business days before withdrawal eligibility. Self-employed individuals can contribute directly from a bank account (must be ACH member). Qualifying businesses enrolled in MarylandSaves receive a $300 waiver (exemption) of the SDAT Annual Report filing fee for the applicable year. Employers must register and submit payroll contributions (or claim an exemption) by December 31 each year to qualify for the following year's fee exemption (the deadline for the 2025 Annual Report exemption was December 1, 2024). MarylandSaves compiles a list of approved SDAT IDs and submits it to SDAT each year. The program is free for employers to set up and administer, and employers are not required to make employer contributions to employee accounts.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Register and submit payroll contributions or claim an exemption by December 31 each year to qualify for the SDAT fee exemption the following year (deadline for 2025 Annual Report exemption was December 1, 2024)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland workers aged 18 or older who do not have access to employer-sponsored retirement savings plans, self-employed individuals and independent contractors, and other individuals who want to save easily through automatic payroll deductions or direct bank transfers; also private-sector employers in Maryland required to offer retirement savings access and seeking the SDAT Annual Report fee waiver. Employers must have at least one W-2 employee in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Emergency savings and retirement savings via Roth IRA (WorkLife Account) contributions through automatic payroll deductions or direct bank transfers; waiver of the $300 SDAT Annual Report filing fee for enrolled employers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to private-sector employers and their employees, as well as workers who perform services for work within Maryland, including self-employed individuals and independent contractors. Employees must have a permanent U.S. street address. Also available to businesses registered with SDAT statewide in Maryland.

Must perform services for work within Maryland
Must be a private-sector employer or employee in Maryland
Employers must have been in operation for at least 2 calendar years (founded January 1, 2021 or earlier)
Employer must have at least one W-2 employee over age 18 in Maryland
Employer must use an automated payroll system
Employer must enroll in the MarylandSaves retirement savings program
Must be enrolled in MarylandSaves and approved by MarylandSaves for the fee exemption
Employer must remain qualified each year to receive the $300 fee waiver for that year's Annual Report

Employers must register and submit payroll contributions or claim an exemption by December 31 to receive the SDAT filing fee exemption for the following year (deadline for 2025 Annual Report exemption was December 1, 2024)

Participation is voluntary — workers may opt out at any time
Self-employed individuals and independent contractors may enroll directly using Social Security Number or ITIN
Employers who already offer a qualified retirement plan can certify their exemption online using their EIN
Most Maryland employers are required by state law to offer employees some form of retirement savings plan
Businesses with no employees or that run manual payroll may certify an exemption
Must register and begin sending payroll contributions by the annual deadline to qualify for the $300 fee waiver
MarylandSaves compiles a list of approved SDAT IDs submitted to SDAT; check the published list to confirm eligibility

Roth IRA income eligibility requirements apply; participants responsible for determining own Roth IRA eligibility
Contributed amounts held for 7 business days before withdrawal eligibility

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Employers register at marylandsaves.vestwell.com/register/employer using their EIN and access code (received via notification from MarylandSaves), then complete a 7-step onboarding process including business setup, password creation, payroll information, bank connection, employee roster upload, and contribution setup. Workers are automatically enrolled 30 days after their employer registers and can customize their contribution amounts, investment choices, or opt out within 30 days at marylandsaves.com/gateway or online at marylandsaves.vestwell.com. Self-employed individuals or those whose employer is not registered can sign up directly at marylandsaves.com using their Social Security Number or ITIN, date of birth, and residential address, then set up automatic contributions from a bank account. Participants can customize contribution rates, investment options, and beneficiaries at any time, or opt out online, by phone, or by mail. Employers who already offer a qualified retirement plan can certify their exemption online at marylandsaves.vestwell.com/exempt. Businesses exempt from the requirement can certify their exemption online. MarylandSaves compiles a list of approved SDAT IDs and submits it to SDAT. Check the list of SDAT IDs compiled by MarylandSaves to confirm eligibility for the fee exemption on your Annual Report filing. A PDF list of entities entitled to the fee waiver is available on the SDAT website (e.g., http://www.dat.maryland.gov/businesses/Documents/MDSaves_2025.PDF and https://dat.maryland.gov/businesses/SiteAssets/Pages/default/LIST%20OF%20ENTITIES%20ENTITLED%20FOR%202026%20MARYLAND%20SAVE.pdf).

structured_extraction.program_name: Personal Property Tax Exemption for Home-based Businesses
structured_extraction.program_description: Small, home-based sole proprietor businesses may be exempt from paying personal property tax on business equipment and inventory located at their home, as long as the total original cost of all business personal property is less than $10,000.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible sole proprietors are exempt from personal property tax on business property located at their home. The total original cost of all business personal property (including average inventory value, excluding exempt vehicles) must be less than $10,000. Businesses must file an initial Personal Property Return for Sole Proprietors (Form 2). After initial approval, no further returns need to be filed as long as eligibility criteria continue to be met. Businesses may also file amended returns for prior years within 3 years of the original April 15th due date.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individual sole proprietors who run a home-based business with less than $10,000 in total business personal property.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Exemption from personal property tax on business equipment and inventory owned by the sole proprietor and used at their home-based business.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: The personal property must be owned by an individual operating as a sole proprietorship (corporations, LLCs, LPs, and LLPs are not eligible).
The personal property must be located at the individual's principal residence, which must also be the principal place of business.
The total original cost of all business personal property, including average inventory value and excluding exempt vehicles, must be less than $10,000.
Eligible businesses must initially file a Personal Property Return for Sole Proprietors (Form 2).
Businesses needing a Traders License must submit a Declaration of Inventory form to the Clerk of the Court with the license application instead of filing a personal property return.
Amended returns for prior years must be filed within 3 years from the April 15th date the original report was due.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: File an initial Personal Property Return for Sole Proprietors (Form 2). If eligibility criteria are met, the business will receive a one-time approval email near the beginning of the calendar year after the initial filing. No further returns need to be filed as long as the criteria continue to be met.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program allows eligible property owners to defer the increase in their property tax bill. It is available to property owners age 65 or older, and in Montgomery County to homeowners of all ages who meet certain residency and income requirements. Each local government must adopt the program and may set income restrictions and interest rates. Deferred taxes become a lien on the property and must be repaid when the property is transferred.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Qualifying property owners may elect to defer the increase in their annual property tax bill. Deferred amounts accrue as a lien on the property. Local governments set income restrictions and interest rates. Deferred taxes must be repaid when the property is sold or transferred.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners age 65 or older; in Montgomery County, also available to homeowners of all ages who meet residency and income requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Deferral of the annual property tax bill increase on the owner's property.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in local jurisdictions that have adopted the program statewide in Maryland.

Local government must have adopted the program
Must meet any income restrictions set by the local government
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local government to determine if the program has been adopted and to apply. Local governments set the specific terms including income restrictions and interest rates.

structured_extraction.program_name: Religious Organization Real Property Tax Exemption
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides a real property tax exemption for property owned by churches, religious organizations, and related religious institutions (including parsonages, convents, religious educational buildings, and church cemeteries) that is actually and exclusively used for religious purposes.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Full exemption from real property taxes on qualifying property. Organization must own the property before July 1 of the tax year and apply by September 1 following the start of the tax year. Applications received after September 1 will be considered for the next tax levy.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: September 1 in order to have the exemption considered for the current tax levy. Applications received after September 1 will be considered for the next tax levy.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Churches, parsonages, convents, religious educational buildings, and church cemeteries in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of real property taxes on property used exclusively for religious purposes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — property must be in Maryland. Application submitted to the local county assessment office where the property is located.
requirements_list: Organization must own the property before July 1 of the tax year (or hold a 99-year or perpetually renewable lease)
Property must be actually used and exclusively for religious purposes
Application must be filed by September 1 following the start of the taxable year; applications received after September 1 will be considered for the next tax levy
Vacant land does not qualify; construction of permanent improvements must have commenced
Caretaker houses and similar incidental uses do not qualify for the exemption
Must file with local Supervisor of Assessments
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Churches, Parsonages, Convents, Religious Educational Buildings, and Church Cemeteries exemption application and submit to the local county assessment office where the property is located by September 1 following the beginning of the taxable year.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Renters' Tax Credit Program provides property tax credits of up to $1,000 per year to eligible renters who meet certain income and rent requirements. Because renters indirectly pay property taxes as part of their rent, this program gives eligible renters financial relief similar to the Homeowners' Tax Credit (Circuit Breaker) Program. The credit is calculated based on the difference between 15% of annual rent (excluding utilities) and a tax threshold determined by the applicant's income. Utilities included in rent reduce the eligible amount (e.g., -18% if heat and electricity are included). The credit is paid as a direct check from the State of Maryland, helping offset housing cost burdens for qualifying low-income renters. Eligibility is based on total gross household income and monthly rent amount. The program is administered statewide by the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation; local applications are also available at senior activity centers in St. Mary's County and Calvert County. Applications must be submitted every year.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible renters receive a direct check from the State Treasury for the difference between 15% of their annual occupancy rent (the assumed property tax portion) and a fixed tax limit based on their income. Utilities included in rent reduce the eligible amount (e.g., -18% if heat and electricity are included). The maximum credit is $1,000 per year. The credit amount depends on the relationship between rent and income. In St. Mary's County and Calvert County, applications are also available at senior activity centers for local residents seeking the annual rent reimbursement. Applications must be filed annually.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: October 1 of the year in which the credit is sought
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland renters who are age 60 or older, 100% disabled, or under 60 with at least one dependent under 18 and income under $31,200 for a family of four, who meet income and rent thresholds and live in their principal Maryland residence at least six months per year. Also open to renters of all ages who qualify based on gross household income relative to rent charged.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Direct property tax relief payment to eligible renters to offset the portion of rent that goes toward property taxes. No restriction on how the check is spent. Also used as reimbursement of rent paid on primary residence.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicant must rent their principal residence in Maryland and live there at least six months of the year. Credits are only available for rent paid in Maryland. In Baltimore City, call 410-767-4433. Local applications also available in St. Mary's County and Calvert County through senior activity centers. Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must rent a principal residence in Maryland (apartment, house, duplex, co-op, condo, mobile home, etc.)
Must live in the dwelling at least six months of the year
Must have a bona fide leasehold interest and be legally responsible for the rent
The dwelling must not be owned by a tax-exempt or charitable organization or otherwise exempt from property taxation
Must not receive federal or state housing subsidies or reside in public housing (applies to renters under 60 with dependents)
Age 60 or older OR 100% disabled: monthly rent must exceed the threshold in Chart 1 for your income level

Under age 60: must have had at least one dependent under 18 living with you during 2023 AND combined household income must be below the Chart 2 income limits (e.g., under $31,200 for a family of four)
Income includes all combined gross household income from all sources before deductions, including Social Security and retirement benefits
Must qualify based on gross household income in relationship to fixed rent amount
Combined net worth of applicant and spouse/co-tenant must be under $200,000 as of December 31
Must rent (not own) home
Must be below certain income limits
Must have paid rent towards primary residence
Must meet income eligibility requirements
Must apply annually
First-time applicants and those who moved must submit lease, cancelled checks, or proof of rent paid
Report gross income from all sources (taxable and non-taxable)
Include Social Security benefits, worker's compensation, deferred compensation
Report full amount of inheritance as income
Report all gifts exceeding $300 as income
Report expenses paid on applicant's behalf by others as income
Household occupants not claimed as dependents and not paying reasonable fixed charges must report total gross income from previous year
If filed Federal Income Tax Return for 2024, include photocopy of completed return with all schedules and forms
If income derived from partnership or corporation, include Form 1065 (with Schedule K-1) and/or Form 1120/1120S (with Schedule K-1)
Do not send original documents
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online through the Maryland OneStop portal or download the Renters' Tax Credit Application (RTC-1 Form) as a PDF and mail the completed application and supporting documents to: State Department of Assessments & Taxation, Renters' Tax Credit Program, P.O. Box 49006, Baltimore, MD 21297. Alternatively, visit dat.maryland.gov/renters to apply. Do not email applications containing personal information such as Social Security numbers or tax returns. Applications are due by October 1 each year. For general information, call 1-800-944-7403; in Baltimore City, call 410-767-4433. Local applications are also available at senior activity centers in St. Mary's County and Calvert County. Contact sdat.renters@maryland.gov for assistance.

structured_extraction.program_name: State Property Tax Exemption for 100% Disabled Veterans and Military Families
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides a full exemption from real property taxes on the principal residence (dwelling house and surrounding yard) of a veteran whose disability has been rated 100% service-connected, permanently, and totally disabling by the Veterans' Administration, or who has been found permanently unemployable by the VA. The exemption also extends to certain disabled active duty service members and to un-remarried surviving spouses of qualifying veterans or military personnel killed in the line of duty. The exemption covers the dwelling, its lot, and structures needed to use the property as a residence. Refunds of taxes paid going back to tax year 2018-2019 are available if the exemption was authorized but not previously granted, provided the application is made within 3 years of the calendar year in which eligibility began. Property tax exemptions are also available for qualifying blind persons in Maryland. Veterans and surviving spouses may apply at any time and are not required to meet the September 1 filing deadline. Applicants must apply through their local SDAT office.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Complete exemption from state, county, and municipal real property taxes on the applicant's principal residence (dwelling house and surrounding yard). Eligible groups include veterans with a VA-determined 100% service-connected permanent and total disability or unemployable rating, certain disabled active duty service members, and un-remarried surviving spouses of qualifying veterans or military personnel killed in the line of duty. Refunds of taxes paid going back to tax year 2018-2019 are available if the exemption was authorized but not previously granted, provided the application is made within 3 years of the calendar year in which eligibility began. Property tax exemptions are also available to qualifying blind persons in Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Veterans and surviving spouses may apply at any time and do not have to meet the September 1 filing deadline.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland veterans with a 100% service-connected, permanent and total disability rating or unemployable rating from the VA, disabled active duty service members, un-remarried surviving spouses of qualifying veterans or military personnel killed in the line of duty, and qualifying blind persons who own property in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Full exemption from real property taxes on the applicant's primary dwelling and surrounding yard, covering the dwelling, its lot, and structures needed to use the property as a residence. Also available for reduction or elimination of property tax liability for qualifying blind persons.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Applicant must be a Maryland resident and property must be located in Maryland. Applications are processed through local Maryland SDAT assessment offices. In Worcester County, contact the local Assessment Office at 410-632-1196 for further information and to apply. In Charles County, contact the State Department of Assessments and Taxation at 301-932-2440.

Disability must not be due to veteran's own misconduct
Some active duty service members may qualify based on disability recognized by their branch of service

Must own property in Maryland

Must be a Maryland resident
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply at any time by completing the appropriate application form based on eligibility: 100% Disabled Veteran (https://dat.maryland.gov/SDAT%20Forms/3-2025_rp_form_revisions/Disabled-Veteran%202-25.pdf), Disabled Active-Duty Service Member (https://dat.maryland.gov/SDAT%20Forms/Active_Duty_Application.pdf), Surviving Spouse of Military Casualty (https://dat.maryland.gov/SDAT%20Forms/Surviving-Spouse-MilitaryCasualty.pdf), or Surviving Spouse of a 100% Disabled Veteran (https://dat.maryland.gov/SDAT%20Forms/Surviving-Spouse-Veteran.pdf). Submit the completed form along with required documents (VA certification or disability rating decision, DD-214, proof of Maryland residency) to the local county SDAT Supervisor of Assessments office where the property is located. Contact the DVMF service program office in Baltimore at 800-446-4926 ext. 6450 to streamline VA disability verification. In Charles County, contact the State Department of Assessments and Taxation at 301-932-2440. For blind persons and other exemptions, visit the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation website for information on how to apply. Refund applications are available under Tax Property Article 7-208.

structured_extraction.program_name: Surviving Spouse of Military Casualty Property Tax Exemption
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides a real property tax exemption on the principal residence of the surviving spouse of an individual who died in the line of active military duty. The exemption is administered statewide by the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation, with local application submitted to the county assessment office where the property is located. The exemption may apply to the dwelling owned at the time of the service member's death, a dwelling acquired by the surviving spouse within 2 years of the death (if domiciled in Maryland at the time of death), or a subsequently acquired dwelling up to the amount of the prior exemption. Calvert County also administers a local application process for eligible surviving spouses residing in that county.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Full exemption from real property taxes on the surviving spouse's principal residence. The exemption may apply to the dwelling owned at the time of the service member's death, a dwelling acquired by the surviving spouse within 2 years of the death (if domiciled in Maryland at the time of death), or a subsequently acquired dwelling up to the amount of the prior exemption. Applications are submitted to the local county assessment office (or, in Calvert County, through the County Treasurer's Office forms page).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Surviving spouses of individuals who died in the line of active military duty, residing in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction or elimination of real property tax liability on the surviving spouse's principal residence.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — property must be located in Maryland. Application submitted to the local county assessment office where the property is located. Calvert County residents may also apply through the County Treasurer's Office.
requirements_list: The dwelling must be owned by the surviving spouse
The applicant must be an unremarried surviving spouse
The individual must have died while in active service as a result of an injury or disease incurred in the line of duty

The dwelling must have been owned by the individual at time of death, OR acquired by the surviving spouse within 2 years of the death if the individual or surviving spouse was domiciled in Maryland at the time of death, OR acquired after the surviving spouse qualified for a prior dwelling exemption (up to the previous exemption amount)
Must provide documentation of military service and death from the Veterans Administration
Must file application with the local Supervisor of Assessments
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Surviving Spouse of Military Casualty Exemption Application, including certification that the individual died in the line of duty, and submit to the local county assessment office where the property is located. The application form is available on the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation website. Calvert County residents may also download and complete the application (PDF) from the Calvert County Treasurer's Office forms page at https://www.calvertcountymd.gov/1344/Forms-and-Documents.

structured_extraction.program_name: Surviving Spouse of a 100 Percent Disabled Veteran Property Tax Exemption
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides a full real property tax exemption on the principal residence (dwelling house and surrounding yard) of the un-remarried surviving spouse of a veteran who had a 100% service-connected, permanent and total (or permanently unemployable) disability rating from the VA. The exemption continues as long as the surviving spouse owns and resides in the dwelling and has not remarried. If the spouse moves to a new dwelling, the exemption on the new dwelling equals the amount allowed on the prior dwelling. Refunds back to tax year 2018-2019 are available if applied within 3 years of initial eligibility.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Full exemption from real property taxes on the surviving spouse's principal residence (dwelling house and surrounding yard). If the spouse moves to a new dwelling, the exemption on the new dwelling equals the amount allowed on the prior dwelling. Refunds back to tax year 2018-2019 are available if applied within 3 years of initial eligibility. May also include a refund of property taxes paid.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Un-remarried surviving spouses of veterans who had a 100% service-connected, permanent and total (or permanently unemployable) VA disability rating and who are Maryland residents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Full elimination of real property taxes on the surviving spouse's principal residence.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — property must be in Maryland and applicant must be a Maryland resident. The veteran must have been a Maryland resident at time of death. Application submitted to the local county assessment office where the property is located.
requirements_list: The disabled veteran must have had a 100% service-connected, permanent and total or 100% permanently unemployable disability rating
Disability rating must not have been incurred through misconduct

The disabled veteran must have owned the dwelling at the time of death, OR the surviving spouse acquired a new dwelling within 2 years of the veteran's death (if the veteran or spouse was domiciled in Maryland at time of death)
The surviving spouse must own and reside in the dwelling
Surviving spouse must be a Maryland resident
Surviving spouse must not have remarried (remarriage ends eligibility; annulment may restore it)
Copy of veteran's Honorable Discharge or DD-Form 214 required
Copy of veteran's VA rating notification packet showing 100% rating and effective date required
Proof of Maryland residency required (driver's license, voter registration, or redacted tax return)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Surviving Spouse of a 100 Percent Disabled Veteran Exemption Application and submit required documents to the local county assessment office where the property is located. See the State website for the application form.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business growth and expansion

structured_extraction.program_name: BRAC Revitalization and Incentive Zone (BRAC) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The BRAC Revitalization and Incentive Zone program provides tax incentives to businesses and employees locating or expanding near military installations affected by Base Realignment and Closure (BRAC) decisions in Maryland. It is designed to attract private sector investment and jobs to areas near impacted military bases.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax incentives for businesses and employees locating or expanding in designated BRAC Revitalization and Incentive Zones near Maryland military installations affected by BRAC decisions.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses and employees locating or expanding in BRAC zones near Maryland military installations
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business location or expansion near BRAC-affected military installations
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Designated BRAC Revitalization and Incentive Zones near Maryland military installations affected by Base Realignment and Closure decisions

structured_extraction.program_description: BIITC provides a refundable income tax credit to investors who make qualifying investments in early-stage biotechnology companies headquartered in Maryland (called Qualified Maryland Biotechnology Companies, or QMBCs). The credit equals 33% of the investment (up to $250,000 in credits), with higher rates available for companies in certain counties or located in Opportunity Zones or RISE Zones. Enhanced credits of up to 75% (up to $750,000) are available for investments in companies within designated Opportunity Zones, and a 50% credit (up to $500,000) is available for companies in Allegany, Dorchester, Garrett, or Somerset counties or in RISE Zones.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Income tax credit equal to 33% of an eligible investment in a Qualified Maryland Biotechnology Company (QMBC), up to $250,000 in credits. The credit increases to 50% (up to $500,000) if the QMBC is located in Allegany, Dorchester, Garrett, or Somerset County. For investors in Opportunity Zone funds investing in eligible QMBCs, a Level 1 enhancement provides a 65% credit (up to $575,000) and a Level 2 enhancement provides a 75% credit (up to $750,000). A RISE Zone enhancement provides a 50% credit (up to $500,000). The minimum qualifying investment is $25,000. Credits are allocated first-come, first-served up to the annual budget. The credit is refundable if the investor has no Maryland income tax liability. A single QMBC may not receive, for the benefit of investors, more than 10% of the program's fiscal year funding.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Form B QMBC applications due 03/31/2026; Form A Investor applications due 04/30/2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individual and entity investors who invest at least $25,000 in a qualifying Maryland biotechnology startup; also biotechnology companies seeking QMBC certification
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Investment in a Qualified Maryland Biotechnology Company (QMBC) in exchange for equity or convertible debt that converts to equity
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The QMBC must have its headquarters and base of operations in Maryland. Enhanced credits are available for QMBCs located in Allegany, Dorchester, Garrett, or Somerset County, in designated Opportunity Zones, or in RISE Zones.
requirements_list: Investor must invest at least $25,000 in a QMBC
Investor must be required to file an income tax return in any non-tax haven jurisdiction
Corporate investors must be registered and in good standing to do business in Maryland
Investor must submit all required documentation within two weeks of application or be rejected
QMBC must have its headquarters and base of operations in Maryland
QMBC must have fewer than 50 full-time employees
QMBC must have been in active business no longer than 12 years
QMBC must be certified by the Maryland Department of Commerce
Qualified investors in a single QMBC may not have received more than $7,000,000 in total BIITC credits
Founders and current employees of the QMBC (in business more than 5 years) are disqualified as investors
Retirement plans and their fiduciaries are disqualified as investors
QMBC must own or have useable rights in biotechnology-related intellectual property with a U.S. non-provisional patent filing or issued patent
QMBC must have at least one full-time non-executive employee engaged in qualified biotechnology research and development in Maryland
QMBC must be organized and operated as a biotechnology company primarily engaged in R&D or commercialization of innovative and proprietary technology involving biological material
Tax credit recapture provisions apply if investor sells interest or company ceases operations within 2 years
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. QMBC submits Form B application through Commerce's online portal (accepted starting August 19, 2025). 2. Investor submits Form A application through the online portal (accepted starting September 2, 2025; must be submitted by September 15, 2025 at 11:59 p.m. to be eligible for the online queue on September 16). 3. Investor receives a username and reference number by email. 4. On September 16, 2025 at 9:00 a.m. EST, investor registers in the Online Electronic Queue to establish first-come, first-served position. 5. If approved, Commerce issues an Initial Certificate of Approval. 6. Investor makes the investment within 30 days and provides proof of investment to Commerce within 10 days of investing. 7. Commerce issues a Final Certificate of Approval with the tax credit amount. 8. Investor claims the credit on a Maryland tax return with the Final Certificate attached.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Brownfields Revitalization Incentive Program (BRIP) promotes economic development and environmental improvement — especially in distressed urban areas — by helping to identify and redeploy underutilized properties that may be contaminated with hazardous substances. It supports Smart Growth efforts by providing financial incentives for organizing and assessing brownfield properties, performing environmental evaluations, and conducting remedial action cleanups. Properties that have gone through the Voluntary Cleanup Program (VCP) and received a Maryland Department of Commerce designation as a qualified brownfield site can earn a 50% property tax credit on the increase in county and/or municipal real property tax assessment resulting from remediation. The credit lasts for 5 years, or up to 10 years if the property is located in an Enterprise Zone or qualified opportunity zone. An additional 20% credit may be available for properties in an Enterprise Zone, qualified opportunity zone, or designated commercial revitalization area, and another additional 20% for cleanup or corrective action costs exceeding $1,000,000. Combined with other real property tax credits, the total credit may not exceed 100% of the tax on the increased value of the site. The credit ends if the recipient withdraws from the VCP or if MDE withdraws approval. Low-interest loans or grants may also be available through the Maryland Economic Development Assistance Authority and Fund (MEDAAF) for Phase I and Phase II environmental assessments and site remediation costs. The brownfield property must be located within a participating jurisdiction that has enacted BRIP legislation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property owners of qualifying brownfield sites receive a real property tax credit of 50% on the property tax attributable to the increase in assessed value of the site after cleanup. The credit lasts for 5 years. An additional credit of up to 20% may be granted at the jurisdiction's option, and a further 20% is available for cleanup or corrective action costs exceeding $1,000,000. In a designated Enterprise Zone or qualified opportunity zone, the credit may be extended for up to an additional 5 years (10 years total). In Baltimore County, an Enhanced Credit of 70% for 5 or 10 years is available if the site is in a Commercial Revitalization District, cleanup costs exceed $1,000,000, or the site is in an Enterprise Zone. Combined with other real property tax credits, the total credit may not exceed 100% of the tax on the increased value of the site. The credit ends if the recipient withdraws from the VCP or if MDE withdraws approval. Additionally, grants and loans through MEDAAF may be available for organizing and assessing a brownfield property, performing environmental evaluations, Phase I and Phase II environmental assessments, and site remediation costs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners, operators, developers, businesses, and local governments seeking to redevelop underutilized brownfield properties, especially in distressed urban areas. Applicants must qualify as inculpable persons under the Voluntary Cleanup Program. Particularly targets owners and developers of industrial or commercial sites in densely populated urban centers that are underutilized.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Real property tax reduction on the increase in assessed value of a remediated brownfield site; organizing and assessing a brownfield property; Phase I and Phase II environmental assessments; performing environmental evaluations; site remediation and remedial action cleanup costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in jurisdictions that have enacted local BRIP legislation. All Maryland counties and municipal corporations may elect to participate. Participating counties include Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore County, Baltimore City, Cecil, Dorchester, Frederick, Howard, Montgomery, Prince George's, Queen Anne's, Somerset, and Worcester. Participating municipalities include Baltimore City, Colmar Manor, Cumberland, Frederick, Salisbury, and Taneytown. Additional benefits apply to properties located within an Enterprise Zone, qualified opportunity zone, or designated commercial revitalization area. Properties must generally be industrial or commercial sites located in densely populated urban centers and be generally underutilized.
requirements_list: Brownfield property must be located within a participating jurisdiction that has enacted BRIP legislation.
Applicant must be an inculpable person (as determined by the Maryland Department of the Environment).
Site must be accepted into MDE's Voluntary Cleanup Program (VCP).
Applicant must obtain a closure document from MDE (Certificate of Completion or No Further Requirements Determination) once remediation is complete.
The site must have received formal designation by the Maryland Department of Commerce as a 'qualified Brownfields site'.
A copy of the building permit issued by the jurisdiction must be provided.
A completed General Application and BRIP addendum must be submitted to Commerce.
The cost of voluntary cleanup or corrective action plan must be determined by demonstrated costs incurred at the time of application.
Credit is terminated if the recipient withdraws from the VCP or if MDE withdraws approval of the Response Action Plan or Certificate of Completion.
Property must generally be an industrial or commercial site located in a densely populated urban center and be generally underutilized.
Additional 20% credit requires meeting criteria established by the participating jurisdiction.
Property must be revalued after cleanup completion.
Taxing jurisdiction must enact enabling legislation and contribute to the State Brownfields Revitalization Incentive Fund.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Voluntary Cleanup Program through the Maryland Department of the Environment, obtain a qualified brownfield site designation from the Maryland Department of Commerce, then submit a completed General Application with the BRIP addendum to the Maryland Department of Commerce along with copies of MDE letters evidencing acceptance into the Voluntary Cleanup Program, Inculpable Person status, and a closure document, plus a copy of the local building permit. Commerce will issue a qualification letter that the property owner takes to the local jurisdiction to apply for the tax credit. For Baltimore County, an application form is also available from Baltimore County Economic Development. For grants and loans, visit the Department of Commerce MEDAAF website. For additional information, contact the Maryland Department of Commerce.

structured_extraction.program_name: Build Our Future Grant Pilot Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A Maryland Department of Commerce competitive grant program, funded under Maryland's Innovation Economy Infrastructure Act of 2023, that provides funding to private companies, nonprofits, local governments, and colleges and universities to support innovation infrastructure development in eligible high-growth technology sectors including advanced manufacturing, aerospace, agriculture, artificial intelligence, biotechnology, blue technology, cybersecurity, defense, energy and sustainability, life sciences, quantum, and sensors and robotics. Grants defray the cost of acquiring, constructing, rehabilitating, installing, improving, or equipping eligible innovation infrastructure projects such as innovation centers, labs, wet laboratories, cyber ranges, specialized training spaces, and manufacturing facilities, helping organizations commercialize new technologies and create jobs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants of up to $2 million per recipient to defray the cost of acquiring, constructing, rehabilitating, installing, improving, or equipping eligible innovation infrastructure projects in qualifying technology sectors. Matching funds are required: grants up to $1 million require matching funds equal to at least 200% of the grant amount; grants between $1 million and $2 million require matching funds equal to at least 400% of the grant amount. Funds from other State grant programs do not count toward the matching requirement. Grant funds must be spent within two years of the agreement date, and the project must be fully operational within two years of the agreement date. A single organization cannot receive more than $2 million in one fiscal year. Colleges and universities cannot receive more than 50% of total funds available in a fiscal year. In a prior round, 11 grants totaling $9 million were awarded. In the June 2025 round, $6.95 million was awarded across 10 projects, with individual awards ranging from approximately $333,333 to $1 million.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications are not being accepted for the remainder of FY2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private companies, nonprofit organizations, local governments, and colleges and universities in Maryland working in eligible high-growth technology sectors including advanced manufacturing, aerospace, agriculture, AI, biotechnology, blue technology, cybersecurity, defense, energy and sustainability, life sciences, quantum, and sensors and robotics.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquire, construct, rehabilitate, install, improve, or equip eligible innovation infrastructure projects such as innovation centers, labs, wet laboratories, cyber ranges, specialized training spaces, and manufacturing facilities in qualifying technology sectors to support commercialization and job creation. Grant funds cannot be used for indirect costs such as salaries or management fees.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to companies and organizations located in Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a private company, nonprofit entity, local government, or college/university

Project must support innovation infrastructure development in an eligible technology sector: Advanced Manufacturing, Aerospace, Agriculture, AI, Biotechnology, Blue Technology, Cybersecurity, Defense, Energy and Sustainability, Life Sciences, Quantum, Sensors and Robotics
Must use funds for innovation infrastructure development to support commercialization and manufacturing of innovative products
Applicants must provide matching funds: 200% match required for grants up to $1 million; 400% match required for grants between $1 million and $2 million
Funds from other State grant programs do not count toward the matching requirement
Applicants must show they can pay for their share of the project costs
A single organization cannot receive more than $2 million in one fiscal year
Colleges and universities cannot receive more than 50% of the total funds available in a fiscal year
Projects from colleges and universities must collaborate with private industry or show a significant potential for economic impact
Grant funds must be spent within two years of the agreement date
The project must be fully operational within two years of the agreement date
Two-phase application process required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants go through a competitive two-phase application process. First, applicants submit an initial project summary. A review committee then invites a limited number of applicants to submit a more detailed second application. The process is reviewed and administered by the Maryland Department of Commerce.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides an incentive for qualified Maryland companies to purchase cybersecurity technologies and services from a Qualified Maryland Cybersecurity Seller. The credit helps small businesses protect their information and supports the state's cybersecurity industry. Companies with fewer than 50 employees that are required to file a Maryland state income tax return are eligible to receive a tax credit for qualifying purchases.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax credit equal to 50% of the net purchase price of cybersecurity technologies and services purchased from a Qualified Maryland Cybersecurity Seller. The maximum credit is $50,000 per year, covering up to $100,000 in purchases. The program has a total of $4 million available each year — $3 million for technology purchases and $1 million for service purchases. The credit must be claimed for the tax year in which the purchase is made.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland businesses with fewer than 50 employees that are required to file a state income tax return and are purchasing cybersecurity technologies and services from a Qualified Maryland Cybersecurity Seller.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of eligible cybersecurity technologies and services from a Qualified Maryland Cybersecurity Seller. Technologies must be proprietary products designed to protect information systems and data. Services must align with the most recent National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Cybersecurity Framework.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Qualified Maryland Company operating in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must have fewer than 50 employees in Maryland
Must be required to file a Maryland income tax return
Must purchase cybersecurity technologies or services from a Qualified Maryland Cybersecurity Seller
Tax credit must be claimed for the tax year of purchase
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Before applying, contact Cindy Zeng at cindy.zeng@maryland.gov to confirm eligibility, as some sellers may have reached their funding cap for the current tax year. After confirming eligibility, submit an application online through the Department of Commerce (no other formats accepted). If approved, you will receive a Certificate of Approval, which must be attached to your Maryland income tax return.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Commerce runs the Cannabis Business Assistance Fund, which provides grants and loans to small businesses entering the adult-use cannabis industry, with a focus on minority-owned and women-owned companies. The fund also offers grants to Historically Black Colleges and Universities for cannabis-related programs, and to business development organizations to train and assist licensed small cannabis businesses. Current funding is available for Social Equity Applicants who hold a conditional cannabis license.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides grants and loans to eligible cannabis businesses. A specific grant for Social Equity licensees offers funding based on license type: a standard dispensary can receive up to $131,250, a processor up to $183,750, and a grower up to $525,000. Businesses with micro-licenses receive smaller amounts. The grant is paid in four parts as the business meets specific milestones. The fund also supports HBCUs and business development organizations through separate grants.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: The application portal opened on June 3, 2025.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small, minority-owned, and women-owned businesses seeking to enter the adult-use cannabis industry, particularly Social Equity Applicants with a conditional cannabis license. Also supports HBCUs and business development organizations that train cannabis entrepreneurs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used for license applications, operating costs, capital expenses, and targeted training to support participation in the adult-use cannabis industry.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a small, minority-owned, or women-owned business
Must be entering the adult-use cannabis industry
Must meet the minimum Adequate Capital Requirement set by the Maryland Cannabis Administration (MCA).
Must be an existing business in Good Standing with the State of Maryland.
Must be a small business with 0-50 employees per license.
The business must hold a Maryland Social Equity Cannabis Business Conditional License.
The business must be at least 51% owned by individuals with a personal net worth not exceeding $1.7 million.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register for access to the application portal on the Department of Commerce website before requesting your first payment. Required documents include your lottery number, conditional license letter, personal net worth information for owners, a W-9 form, and proof that your business is in Good Standing with Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Maryland state tax credit for businesses that invest in cellulosic ethanol technology. The credit is intended to encourage investment in the production of ethanol from cellulosic (plant fiber) materials.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A tax credit available to businesses that invest in cellulosic ethanol technology in Maryland. Specific credit amounts and terms are not detailed on this page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses investing in cellulosic ethanol technology in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Investment in cellulosic ethanol technology.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.

structured_extraction.featured_description: No-interest loans for capital expenses to child care providers who participate in the Child Care Scholarship Program.
structured_extraction.program_name: Child Care Capital Support Revolving Loan Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Commerce manages this fund. It offers no-interest loans to child care providers for capital expenses. To qualify, providers must participate in the State Department of Education's Child Care Scholarship Program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides no-interest loans. There are no application fees. Borrowers must repay the loan within five years. There are no penalties for paying the loan back early.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland child care providers who are licensed and participate in the Child Care Scholarship Program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Loans pay for capital expenses like buying a building, expanding space, renovating, or new construction. Funds cannot pay for operations, working capital, or refinancing old debt.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is available statewide. It gives priority to providers in rural areas, underserved communities, and areas that lack enough child care slots.
requirements_list: Must have a valid child care license from the Maryland State Department of Education.
Must participate in the Child Care Scholarship Program.
Must repay the loan within five years.
Must provide collateral to secure the loan.
Must not use funds for refinancing existing debt or general operations.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must apply through the online portal by January 30, 2026. The application requires details on ownership, a valid license, and proof of scholarship participation. Applicants must also submit financial projections, tax returns, and collateral details.
