structured_extraction.assistance_description: No program details were available on this page.

structured_extraction.program_name: Data Center Maryland Sales and Use Tax Exemption Incentive Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Qualifying data centers that locate, operate, or expand in Maryland may receive an exemption from Maryland's 6% sales and use tax on the purchase of qualified data center personal property, including servers, equipment, and related data center infrastructure. To qualify, businesses must be certified as a Qualified Data Center by the Maryland Department of Commerce, meet investment thresholds (which vary by location tier), and create new full-time qualified positions. The exemption is available for 10 years, extendable to 20 years if the business invests at least $250 million within the first ten years.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible businesses receive an exemption from Maryland's 6% sales and use tax on qualifying data center personal property. The exemption applies for 10 years, with the ability to extend to 20 years if the business invests at least $250 million within the first ten years. Investment thresholds vary by location: at least $2 million for Tier 1 Areas (including specific counties and all Opportunity Zones) and at least $5 million for all other areas of the State.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses that operate data centers and plan to locate or expand in Maryland, including data center operators, developers, and businesses looking to meet investment and job creation requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of state sales and use tax liability on the purchase of qualified data center personal property, including servers, equipment, and related infrastructure.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Different investment thresholds apply based on location: Tier 1 areas (including specific counties and all Opportunity Zones) have a lower investment threshold of $2 million, while all other areas require at least $5 million.
requirements_list: Must be certified as a 'Qualified Data Center' by the Maryland Department of Commerce.
Must operate, locate, or expand a data center in Maryland.
Invest at least $2 million in qualified data center personal property if located in a Tier 1 Area.
Invest at least $5 million in qualified data center personal property if located in any other area of the State.
Create at least five new, full-time qualified positions within a three-year period.
Qualified positions must pay at least 150% of the State minimum wage, be filled for at least 12 months, and be new to Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, submit an Eligibility Application to the Maryland Department of Commerce. Commerce reviews the application and issues a Certificate of Eligibility. Finally, Commerce notifies the Comptroller's Office, which issues the sales and use tax exemption certificate to the business.

structured_extraction.program_name: Economic Development Opportunities Program Fund (Sunny Day)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Sunny Day fund supports extraordinary economic development opportunities that create and retain jobs and generate significant capital investments. Projects must create substantial employment, particularly in areas of high unemployment, and are evaluated on a competitive basis. Projects must align with the state's strategic economic development plan. The program provides financial assistance for large-scale economic development projects requiring significant capital investment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance for economic development projects that create and retain jobs and generate significant capital investment. Participants must provide a minimum capital investment of at least five times the amount of Sunny Day assistance received. Assistance may be provided as direct loans, project grants, or other financial assistance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses and organizations seeking to create or retain jobs in Maryland through large-scale economic development projects, particularly in areas of high unemployment, that can demonstrate creditworthiness and a strong balance sheet.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supporting economic development projects that create and retain employment and generate significant capital investment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; projects that generate significant jobs in areas of high unemployment are prioritized.
requirements_list: Must provide a minimum capital investment of at least five times the amount of Sunny Day assistance
Must have a strong balance sheet
Must be creditworthy
Projects must be consistent with the state's strategic economic development plan
Projects are evaluated on a competitive basis
Project must generate a substantial number of jobs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Program Manager, Timothy Doyle, at the Maryland Department of Commerce, Office of Finance Programs for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Employer Security Clearance Costs (ESCC) Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: The ESCC Tax Credit provides Maryland income tax credits to businesses that incur costs related to federal security clearance administration, construction or renovation of Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities (SCIFs), and first-year leasing costs for small businesses performing security-based contract work in Maryland. Three separate tax credit incentives are available covering security clearance administrative expenses, sensitive facility construction or renovation, and first-year leasing costs for qualified small businesses conducting security-related business within the state. Credits apply to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2022, and before January 1, 2028.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Three types of income tax credits are available: (1) Up to $200,000 per taxable year for qualified security clearance administrative expenses; (2) 50% of SCIF construction/renovation costs up to $200,000 for a single SCIF, or up to $500,000 for multiple SCIFs; (3) Up to $200,000 for first-year leasing costs for qualified small businesses (independently owned, not a subsidiary, not dominant in its field, and fewer than 25 employees). Total credits are capped at $2 million per calendar year across all applicants; if the cap is exceeded, credits are awarded on a pro-rata basis. Excess credits can be carried forward until fully used. Credits apply to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2022, and before January 1, 2028. Eligible expenses do not include wages and salaries.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: September 15 following the tax year in which expenses were incurred (Tax Year 2024 program is now closed)
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit businesses (including individuals, sole proprietorships, partnerships, limited partnerships, corporations, LLCs, and other for-profit entities) with 500 or fewer employees that incur federal security clearance administrative expenses, SCIF construction/renovation costs, or first-year leasing costs for security-based contracting work in Maryland. Small businesses with 25 or fewer employees that are independently owned and not dominant in their field are eligible for the First Year Leasing Costs credit.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credit applied against Maryland state income tax liability for: security clearance administrative expenses (including processing applications, maintaining/upgrading computer systems, and employee training); SCIF construction or renovation costs and equipment; and first-year rental payments for spaces used for security-based contracting. Does not include wages and salaries.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Expenses and facilities must be located in Maryland. Computer systems, employee training, SCIF construction, and leased spaces must all be in Maryland.
requirements_list: Business must apply to and be certified by the Maryland Department of Commerce
Business must employ 500 or fewer employees
Business must be doing business in the State of Maryland
Business must incur qualified security clearance administrative expenses, SCIF construction/renovation costs, or first-year leasing costs for security-based contracting

For the First Year Leasing Costs credit, the business must qualify as a small business: independently owned and operated, not a subsidiary, not dominant in its field, and employed no more than 25 individuals in its most recently completed fiscal year
A Small Business Affidavit must be completed and signed under penalties of perjury and submitted with applications claiming the First Year Leasing Costs credit
Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities (SCIFs) must be accredited by the appropriate federal agency
Application must be submitted through the web portal by September 15 following the end of the tax year for which expenses are being claimed
Eligible expenses must be for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2022, and before January 1, 2028
Businesses must retain supporting documentation including proof of service/purchase, proof of payment, and proof that work was performed in Maryland
Cash transactions are generally not eligible as they cannot be easily tracked
Eligible expenses do not include wages and salaries
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application through the Commerce web portal by September 15 following the tax year in which expenses were incurred. Include itemized accounting of qualifying expenses with invoices and proof of payment. For SCIF costs, include detailed itemized accounting of SCIF assets and equipment. For leasing costs, include a copy of the rental agreement, payment schedule, proof of payment, and a signed Small Business Affidavit. Commerce will certify the approved credit amount by December 15. The business then files an amended Maryland income tax return (Form 500CR) and attaches a copy of the Commerce certification to claim the credit.

structured_extraction.program_description: ExportMD grants help small and mid-sized Maryland companies grow their international sales by reimbursing eligible expenses associated with international marketing projects. Companies may receive reimbursement of up to 50% of eligible expenses, with a maximum reimbursement of $5,000. Eligible expenses include international travel (airfare), trade show fees, translation of brochures, website development, and other international marketing costs. Grants are awarded on a monthly basis. Applicants must be in existence for at least one year, export ready, and meet SBA small business size standards.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement of up to 50% of expenses incurred for international marketing initiatives, with a maximum reimbursement of $5,000. Eligible expenses include trade show fees, airfare, translation of brochures, website development, and other international marketing costs. Grants are awarded on a monthly basis with applications due on the 1st of each month.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications are due on the 1st of each month
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small and mid-sized Maryland companies seeking to expand into international markets through trade shows and other international marketing projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: International marketing expenses including trade show fees, airfare, brochure translation, website development, and other expenses associated with international marketing projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to small and mid-sized companies based in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland company
Must have business operations in Maryland and be in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation.
Must be in existence for at least one year.
Must be export ready.
Must not have received an ExportMD Award in the last year.
Must be a 'small business' as defined by the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA).
Must be planning an international business initiative that will start and finish within six months of the application deadline.
Expenses must be for international marketing initiatives
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, contact the program specialist to discuss your international marketing plan. A regional manager will then give you more details and the application form. You must schedule an export counseling meeting before the deadline. Contact the office at least two weeks before the application deadline to start the process. Applications are submitted on a monthly basis through the Maryland Department of Commerce ExportMD program.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides a refundable tax credit to film production companies. The credit is for certain costs a company has while making a film in Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Qualified film productions can get a refundable tax credit of up to 28% of their direct costs. A television series can get a credit of up to 30% of direct costs. The maximum credit per project is $10 million. Qualified Maryland Small Films can receive a tax credit of up to 28% of direct costs, with a maximum of $125,000 per project.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Film production companies, including Maryland-based small film companies.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The tax credit applies to direct costs for film production in Maryland. These costs must be for goods and services from qualified Maryland vendors. A detailed list of authorized direct costs is available on the program website.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is available statewide. At least 50% of the principal photography must take place in Maryland.
requirements_list: Total direct costs must be over $250,000 ($25,000 for Maryland Small Films).
At least 50% of principal photography must happen in Maryland.
Applicants must show proof of financing and national distribution.
Principal photography must start within 120 days of receiving a Letter of Qualification.
Maryland Small Films must be organized in Maryland for at least 3 months, be independently owned, and have 25 or fewer full-time employees.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, submit an Application for Qualification with all required documents before starting any work in Maryland. You can submit it by email, mail, or in person. The Department reviews complete applications in the order they are received. Within 30 days, the Department will issue a Letter of Qualification or a denial. After production is complete, you must submit an Application for Final Tax Credit Certification no later than 180 days after the completion date.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Maryland state income tax credit for small businesses that hire qualified veterans. Businesses may qualify for a credit equal to 30% of up to the first $6,000 of wages paid to a qualified veteran employee in the first year of employment, for a maximum credit of $1,800 per veteran. The credit applies to wages paid during the first year of employment for veterans hired after January 1, 2017, and was available for tax years 2017 through 2020.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State income tax credit for small businesses hiring qualified veterans. Employers may qualify for a credit equal to 30% of the first $6,000 in wages paid to a qualified veteran employee during their first year of employment, up to a maximum of $1,800 per veteran. Businesses can claim the credit for up to five veterans per tax year. The credit is non-refundable and cannot be carried forward or backward.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses with 50 or fewer full-time employees that hire qualified veterans
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credit applied to state income tax liability based on wages paid to a newly hired, qualified veteran employee during their first year of employment
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a small business with 50 or fewer full-time employees
Must hire qualified veterans after January 1, 2017
Credit available for first year of employment only
Can claim up to five veterans per tax year
Hired employee must be a qualified veteran under program guidelines
The tax credit is non-refundable and cannot be carried forward or backward
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To receive the credit, a business submitted application forms, employee self-certification, W-2s or paystubs, and military discharge forms to the Maryland Department of Commerce for certification. After receiving the certificate, the employer filed it with their state tax return using Maryland Tax Form 500CR.

structured_extraction.program_name: International Market Research (Maryland Department of Commerce)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Commerce helps Maryland businesses expand into international markets by providing free international market research through its eleven international offices worldwide. Companies can request up to 20 hours of free market research per year, with an option for up to 40 additional hours through the ExportMD program. Research scope is determined in collaboration with the Maryland Department of Commerce.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to 20 hours of free international market research per year through Maryland Department of Commerce's eleven international offices worldwide. Companies may apply for up to 40 additional hours of free assistance through the ExportMD program. Research scope is determined in collaboration with the Maryland Department of Commerce.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland companies seeking to expand into international markets
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: International market research to support global business expansion and entry into international markets
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to businesses located in Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland company
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a request through the Maryland Department of Commerce Global Expansion resources.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Job Creation Tax Credit (JCTC) provides a Maryland state income tax credit to eligible businesses that locate or expand in Maryland and create a minimum number of net new full-time positions. Businesses that establish or expand a facility primarily engaged in qualifying activities—including warehousing and distribution within a Priority Funding Area—may receive a credit for each new qualified job created. Small businesses that hire qualified veteran employees can also qualify. The credit encourages job creation and business expansion across the state, with higher credit amounts available in revitalization areas and for positions filled by qualified veterans. Credits of up to $3,000 per job are available statewide, or up to $5,000 per job in designated revitalization areas (enterprise zones, sustainable communities, federal empowerment zones, or Tier 1 Counties). Caroline County businesses must add at least 10 qualifying positions. The program is capped at $4 million in total tax credits per calendar year, awarded on a first-come, first-served basis.
eligible_industries: Mining, Quarrying, and Oil and Gas Extraction
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Income tax credit of $3,000 per new qualified full-time job created anywhere in Maryland; $5,000 per job if located in a revitalization area (state enterprise zone, federal empowerment zone, DHCD Sustainable Community, or Tier 1 County). For positions filled by a qualified veteran employee, the credit increases to $4,000 per job ($6,000 in a revitalization area). Small businesses hiring qualified veteran employees receive a credit of $2,500 per qualified veteran employee (up to five per credit year). For warehousing and distribution facilities in a Priority Funding Area, the credit equals the lesser of $1,000 or 2.5% of one year's wages for each new employee in a qualified position. The maximum credit per business per year is $1 million. The program is capped at $4 million in total tax credits per calendar year. Unused credits may be carried forward for up to five taxable years. Credits are certified on a first-come, first-served basis. The credit is taken against Maryland state income tax using Form 500CR.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Program remains in effect until Jan. 1, 2027, subject to extension by the Maryland General Assembly. Credits certified on a first-come, first-served basis.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit businesses (and some non-profits with taxable income) that are locating or expanding in Maryland and creating new full-time jobs, including companies newly locating or expanding in revitalization areas; small businesses hiring qualified veteran employees; and businesses generally seeking to create new full-time jobs across the state. Caroline County businesses must add at least 10 new qualifying full-time jobs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credit applied against Maryland state income tax liability; cannot be used for county income tax. Unused credits may be carried forward for five years. Not refundable. Supports job creation through business location or expansion.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Lower job creation thresholds apply in Priority Funding Areas (25 jobs) and in qualifying lower-income/smaller counties (10 jobs), including Caroline County. Higher credit amounts apply in revitalization areas including Tier 1 Counties (Allegany, Baltimore City, Caroline, Dorchester, Garrett, Kent, Somerset, Washington, Wicomico, Worcester). Warehousing and distribution facilities must be located within a Priority Funding Area.
requirements_list: Business must notify Maryland Department of Commerce of intent to seek certification before hiring qualified employees (except small businesses hiring veterans).
Business must apply for and receive certification as a qualified business entity.

Must create a minimum number of net new full-time positions within a 24-month period: 60 jobs anywhere in the state; 25 jobs in a Priority Funding Area; or 10 jobs in qualifying lower-income or smaller counties (including Caroline County).

Facility must be primarily engaged in a qualifying business activity (e.g., manufacturing, mining, transportation, agriculture, biotechnology, computer services, financial services, cannabis operations, warehousing and distribution, etc.).
Business expansion or establishment must be at a single location in Maryland.
Positions must be filled for at least 12 months before the business applies for final certification.

For positions filled on or after Oct. 1, 2021: position must pay the prevailing wage rate or 150% of state minimum wage; provide career advancement training; allow collective bargaining; provide paid leave; be covered employment for unemployment insurance; entitle employee to workers' compensation; offer employer health insurance with premiums not exceeding 8.5% of employee's net monthly earnings; and offer retirement benefits.
For positions filled before Oct. 1, 2021: position must pay at least 120% of state minimum wage.
Qualifying positions must be full-time and paid at least 120% of the state minimum wage.
Jobs must remain filled for at least three years following the credit year.
Maintain qualified positions within 5% of average during credit year for 3 years; recapture triggered if positions fall more than 5% below average or fall below minimum threshold.
Submit annual reports for 3 years following credit year; 3rd year report requires CPA statement.
A business may not claim both the One Maryland Tax Credit and JCTC in the same tax year.
A small business must employ 50 or fewer total full-time employees to qualify under the small business veteran hiring provision.
Qualified veteran employee must be honorably discharged from active military service and qualify as a 'qualified veteran' under the Federal Work Opportunity Tax Credit.
Veteran employee must be a 'veteran' (honorably discharged after 180+ days active duty OR discharged for service-connected disability OR active duty did not end within 60 days before hire date).

Veteran employee must meet 'qualified veteran' criteria: SNAP recipient for 3+ months in prior 15 months OR service-connected disability with discharge within prior year OR unemployed 4+ weeks in prior year.
Veteran employee must complete and sign self-certification form and provide copy of DD-214 or discharge papers.
For warehousing and distribution facilities: facility must be located within a Priority Funding Area as defined by the Job Creation Tax Credit statute.
Credits certified on a first-come, first-served basis.
Business may not claim more than $1 million in any credit year.
Program capped at $4 million total per calendar year.
Must be a newly locating or expanding company.
Business must be in good standing with Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT).
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Submit a Notice of Intent to Commerce before hiring qualified employees (not required for small businesses hiring veterans). 2. Optionally submit a Preliminary Application and Employment Affidavit to determine preliminary qualification. 3. Once positions have been filled for at least 12 months, submit a Final Application (along with the List of Qualified Employees Form) through the online portal at programs.commerce.maryland.gov/jobcredits. 4. Commerce will review the application and issue a Final Certificate of Eligibility (processing time approximately 60 days). 5. Claim the credit on Maryland Tax Form 500CR and attach the Final Certificate of Eligibility. 6. Submit annual reports for 3 consecutive years following the credit year (3rd year report requires CPA statement). Credits are certified on a first-come, first-served basis based on when the application is received and credit availability.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Capital Access Program (MD CAP) helps small businesses get financing. It creates a Loan Reserve Program to encourage banks to lend to businesses that might otherwise have trouble getting a loan.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: This program helps lenders cover losses if a small business defaults on a loan. It can cover up to 100% of losses for participating lenders. The maximum loan amount that can be enrolled is $250,000. Loans can have a term up to ten years. The lender, borrower, and the MD CAP program all contribute to a reserve account to cover potential losses.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland small businesses and non-profit organizations with fewer than 50 employees. Businesses must meet SBA size standards.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used for start-up costs, business expansion, or working capital. The program does not fund passive real estate investments, residential living facilities, certain adult entertainment businesses, or sectarian religious instruction.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is available to businesses located in Maryland.
requirements_list: Borrower must qualify as a small business under SBA size standards
Borrower must have fewer than 50 employees
Loan term may not exceed ten years
Loan amount may not exceed $250,000
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, a small business applies for a loan directly with a participating lender. The lender determines if the loan qualifies for the program. If it does, the lender enrolls the loan. The lender, the borrower, and the MD CAP program all contribute to a reserve fund. The lender submits a one-page enrollment form to the Maryland Capital Access Program.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit for businesses that invest in cybersecurity products or services in Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax credit for eligible cybersecurity investments made by businesses in Maryland. Specific credit amounts and terms were not detailed on this page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland businesses that invest in cybersecurity products or services
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cybersecurity products or services
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Department of Commerce's Partnership for Workforce Quality (PWQ)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Partnership for Workforce Quality (PWQ) program provides matching training grants to Maryland businesses, including small and mid-sized manufacturing and technology companies, to fund employee training and workforce development. It helps businesses offset the costs of eligible workforce training—including on-the-job training, classroom or offsite training, purchase of training software, and train-the-trainer programs—for new and incumbent workers, with the goals of improving skills, boosting productivity, and increasing employment stability. The program reimburses up to 50% of qualified training project costs, with a minimum grant award of $10,000 (requiring a total project cost of at least $20,000) and a maximum of $200,000 per year. Employers pay for training upfront and are reimbursed upon successful completion. At least 60% of available funds must go to employers with 150 or fewer employees in Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Matching training grants that reimburse up to 50% of qualified training project costs. Minimum grant award is $10,000 (requiring a total project cost of at least $20,000); maximum is $200,000 per year. Employers pay for training upfront, then submit certificates and invoice/PO paperwork for reimbursement after training is successfully completed. At least 60% of available funds must go to employers with 150 or fewer employees in Maryland. Eligible costs include curriculum development, course books, materials, instructor salaries and expenses, training software, and train-the-trainer scenarios.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: On-the-job training, classroom or offsite training, purchase of training software, train-the-trainer scenarios, curriculum development, course books, materials, instructor salaries and expenses, training existing workers for new technologies and production processes, improving employee productivity, and increasing employment stability
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland; applicant must be a Maryland company.

Applicant should have a minimum of ten full-time employees
Must not be in arrears with any State taxing agency
Must not be in default with any Commerce program
The total training project cost must be at least $20,000
Priority given to manufacturing and technology companies
At least 60% of funds must go to employers with 150 or fewer employees in Maryland
Small and minority-owned businesses encouraged to apply

Contact the regional representative from the Maryland Department of Commerce for your county or region to initiate the process. Finalize an agreement with the Department; employer pays for training upfront; upon successful completion, submit copies of certificates and PO/Invoice paperwork for review and reimbursement.

structured_extraction.program_description: MEAF provides loans of up to $150,000 to help small and underserved businesses upgrade or modernize operations, develop or expand commercial applications for technology, or enter new markets. Eligible uses include working capital, equipment, building renovation, real estate acquisition, and site improvements. Eligible companies must have no more than 50 employees and must demonstrate creditworthiness and an inability to qualify for loans from traditional lending sources.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans of up to $150,000 for small businesses with fewer than 50 employees. Funds can be used for working capital, equipment, building renovation, real estate acquisition, and site improvements. Applicants must demonstrate creditworthiness and an inability to qualify for loans from traditional lending sources.

You must also explain how much money you will contribute and what collateral you will provide. Contact the program via email at arp.meafloanfund@maryland.gov or call 410-767-6356 to obtain an application.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Economic Development Assistance Authority and Fund (MEDAAF)
structured_extraction.program_description: MEDAAF (also known as Advantage Maryland) is a flexible, broad-based financing program administered by the Maryland Department of Commerce that provides conditional grants, loans, and investments to support economic development in Maryland. The program helps attract and retain businesses, fund infrastructure, redevelop brownfields, support arts and entertainment districts, child care centers, revolving loan funds, and local strategic planning. It offers six types of financing capabilities: (1) Significant Strategic Economic Development Opportunities — loans up to the lesser of $10 million or 20% of current fund balance; (2) Local Economic Development Opportunity — loans up to $5 million, conditional loans and grants up to $2 million, with local jurisdiction sponsorship and 10% match; (3) Direct Assistance to Local Jurisdictions or MEDCO — up to $3 million (more for qualified distressed counties) for land, infrastructure, fixed assets, feasibility studies, and planning; (4) Regional or Local Revolving Loan Fund — grants of $250,000 annually to local jurisdictions to capitalize revolving loan funds, with matching funds required; (5) Special Purposes Loan — targets critical state economic health initiatives including Brownfield Revitalization, Seafood and Aquaculture, Animal Waste, Arts & Entertainment, and Child Care Center programs; (6) Sunny Day Fund — promotes extraordinary economic development opportunities requiring minimum capital investment of five times the assistance amount. In most cases, assistance cannot exceed 70% of total project costs. Projects must be located within Priority Funding Areas and eligible industry sectors. Awards are made on a competitive basis. Examples include a $315,000 conditional loan to Crystal Steel for job creation and capital expenditures at its new Federalsburg facility, a $400,000 conditional loan to Hahn's of Westminster, a $700,000 conditional loan to Knorr Brake Company for expansion in Carroll County, and a $320,000 conditional loan approved to assist with a business expansion in Westminster.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Six financing capabilities: (1) Significant Strategic Economic Development Opportunities — loans up to the lesser of $10 million or 20% of current fund balance; (2) Local Economic Development Opportunity — loans up to $5 million, conditional loans and grants up to $2 million, with local jurisdiction sponsorship and 10% match; (3) Direct Assistance to Local Jurisdictions or MEDCO — up to $3 million (more for qualified distressed counties) for land, infrastructure, fixed assets, feasibility studies, and planning; (4) Regional or Local Revolving Loan Fund — grants of $250,000 annually to local jurisdictions to capitalize revolving loan funds, with matching funds required; (5) Special Purposes Loan — targets critical state economic health initiatives including Brownfield Revitalization, Seafood and Aquaculture, Animal Waste, Arts & Entertainment, and Child Care Center programs; (6) Sunny Day Fund — promotes extraordinary economic development opportunities requiring minimum capital investment of five times the assistance amount. In most cases, assistance cannot exceed 70% of total project costs. Awards are made on a competitive basis.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Global Gateway Soft Landing Program for Foreign Companies
structured_extraction.program_description: This program helps international companies test the U.S. market at a low cost. It gives companies access to business facilities, resources, and advisors. The program also provides funding for costs related to entering the market.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides funding to help cover costs for entering the U.S. market. This includes physical, programmatic, and other related expenses. Companies can also use business facilities and receive mentoring and networking services for up to six months.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Foreign companies that want to explore entering the U.S. market.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding can be used for costs related to entering the U.S. market, including expenses for physical space, program participation, and other related costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is available statewide through a network of partner organizations. Companies must physically locate in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be legally registered as a business in its home country for at least one year.
Must have at least five full-time equivalent employees.
Must have at least $500,000 USD in sales revenue and/or external investment in a single year (2023 or 2024).
Must be able to locate physically in Maryland within six months of the application round.

structured_extraction.program_description: MIDFA promotes private sector investment in economic development projects by issuing taxable and tax-exempt bonds and providing credit insurance (loan guarantees) to reduce lender risk. The program improves capital access for small and medium-sized businesses, historically disadvantaged businesses, non-profit organizations, day care providers, and businesses in rural areas located in Maryland's Priority Funding Areas.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MIDFA issues private activity revenue bonds (taxable and tax-exempt) and provides credit insurance in the form of loan guarantees. Taxable bonds provide access to long-term capital markets for fixed asset financing. Tax-exempt bonds are available to 501(c)(3) nonprofits, manufacturers, and certain solid waste projects. The Conventional Credit Insurance Program insures up to 80% (or 90% for export transactions), not to exceed $2.5 million, of transactions made by a financial institution. The Bond Program insures bonds up to 100%, not to exceed $7.5 million, of taxable or tax-exempt bonds. Linked Deposits provide below-market-rate loans to eligible small businesses in rural high-unemployment areas through a certificate of deposit provided to the lender.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small and medium-sized commercial and industrial businesses in Priority Funding Areas (excluding retail), manufacturers, non-profit organizations, and day care providers seeking long-term capital for fixed assets or other economic development projects. Also supports historically disadvantaged businesses and businesses in rural areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Land acquisition, building acquisition, construction costs, machinery and equipment, furniture and fixtures, leasehold improvements, eligible soft costs, energy-related projects, working capital, and below-market-rate loans for eligible small businesses in rural high-unemployment areas.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Commercial and industrial businesses must be located in a Maryland Priority Funding Area (retail businesses are excluded). Manufacturers, nonprofits, and day care providers may also be eligible. Linked Deposits are limited to certain rural areas with qualifying high unemployment.
requirements_list: Must be a commercial or industrial business located in a Maryland Priority Funding Area (retail excluded), a manufacturer, a non-profit entity, or a day care provider
Tax-exempt bonds limited to 501(c)(3) non-profit organizations, manufacturing facilities, and certain solid waste projects
Additional Federal tax law limitations apply depending on transaction type
Credit enhancement subject to applicable program limits
Retail businesses are not eligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Bruce Alderman, Finance Specialist at the Maryland Department of Commerce, Office of Finance Programs, for more information about the program and how to apply.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Manufacturing 4.0 / Maryland MADE (Manufacturing Assets Deployed for Energy) Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program managed by the Maryland Department of Commerce that helps small and mid-sized Maryland manufacturers invest in Industry 4.0-related technologies such as robotics, artificial intelligence (AI), enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems, and digital process improvements, as well as advanced energy-efficient manufacturing technologies. Grants range from $25,000 to $500,000, covering up to 75% of eligible costs for small manufacturers (3–50 employees) and up to 50% for mid-sized manufacturers (51–250 employees). The Maryland MADE grant component provides mini-grants of up to $15,000 per recipient, awarded on a first come, first served basis, to small manufacturers with between 3 and 75 full-time employees to adopt smart manufacturing and high-performance manufacturing technologies that increase energy efficiency, reduce carbon emissions, and enable lasting improvements. The governor's proposed budget increases funding for the program to $6 million in FY2026. Education, technical, and financial assistance are also provided.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants covering up to 75% of eligible costs for small manufacturers (3–50 employees) and up to 50% for mid-sized manufacturers (51–250 employees), ranging from $25,000 to $500,000, to help manufacturers adopt advanced technologies including robotics, AI, ERP systems, and digital process improvements. The Maryland MADE component awards mini-grants of up to $15,000 per recipient on a first come, first served basis to manufacturers with between 3 and 75 full-time employees to support adoption of smart manufacturing and energy-efficient manufacturing technologies. Funding supports automation equipment, process control systems, data analytics, sensors, ERP systems, robotics, CNC machines, and digital manufacturing upgrades to modernize production facilities. Additional technical and financial assistance is provided for investment in Industry 4.0-related technologies, machinery, robotics, and digital business practices. The governor's proposed budget increases funding for the program to $6 million in FY2026. Grant applications are accepted until all funds are disbursed.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Grant application will run until all funds are disbursed.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small and mid-sized Maryland manufacturers with 3 to 250 full-time employees seeking to adopt advanced, energy-efficient, Industry 4.0, and digital manufacturing technologies.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Industry 4.0-related technologies, machinery, robotics, artificial intelligence (AI), enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems, digital process improvements, smart manufacturing, digitization, automation, advanced sensors, data analytics, cloud computing, cybersecurity, systems integration projects, CNC machines, process control systems, and adoption of advanced energy-efficient manufacturing technologies to increase energy efficiency and reduce carbon emissions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to small and mid-sized manufacturers operating in Maryland. Applicants must be an established manufacturing business in Maryland.

Must be located in Maryland
Must be a manufacturer operating in Maryland

Must invest in Industry 4.0 related technologies, machinery, robotics, or digital business practices

Applicants submit proposals through an online portal at the Maryland Department of Commerce website. Funding decisions for the standard Manufacturing 4.0 grants are competitive.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Nonprofit Development Center Program and Funds - Nonprofit, Interest-Free Micro Bridge Loan Account (NIMBL)
structured_extraction.program_description: NIMBL is an interest-free, micro bridge loan program that provides short-term financing to qualifying nonprofit organizations. The loans help cover operating costs while nonprofits wait to receive funds from a government grant or contract they have already been awarded. Nonprofits must have an existing government grant or contract in place to repay the loan.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: No-interest (0%) bridge loan of up to $25,000 to cover operating costs while a nonprofit waits for payment from an existing government grant or contract. Loans are awarded on a rolling, first-come, first-served basis.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations located in Maryland that have been awarded a government grant or contract but are waiting to receive the funds.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Loan funds can only be used for operating expenses while awaiting payment from a government grant or contract.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Applicants must be located in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a 501(c)(3), (4), or (6) nonprofit organization.
Must have an existing government grant or contract in place to repay the bridge loan.
Must provide written confirmation of funding from a government grant or contract.
Must not have received the government funds yet.
Must repay the loan by the date of the final payment from the government grant or contract.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To apply, contact Les Hall at les.hall@maryland.gov to request an application form. Submit the completed application and all required documents by email. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis as they are received. Visit the Maryland Department of Commerce website for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program offers increased tax credit benefits to businesses located in Maryland Opportunity Zones. To receive these benefits, a business must first qualify for one of several other state economic development tax credit programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: This program provides larger tax credits than what is normally available through other state programs. Businesses can apply for Level 1 or Level 2 enhancements, with Level 2 offering the highest credit amounts. The specific credit amount depends on the base program, such as the Job Creation Tax Credit, One Maryland Tax Credit, or Biotechnology Investor Incentive Tax Credit.
structured_extraction.program_audience: This program is for businesses and investors operating within designated Maryland Opportunity Zones.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: This program enhances the value of other state tax credits. Businesses receive a larger reduction in their state tax liability.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: To be eligible, a business or investment must be located within a designated Maryland Opportunity Zone.
requirements_list: Must first qualify for an underlying tax credit program, such as the Job Creation Tax Credit or One Maryland Tax Credit.
For most credits, the business must be a Qualified Opportunity Zone Business that has received an investment from a Qualified Opportunity Fund.
For investment-based credits like the BIITC or IITC, the investor must be a Qualified Opportunity Fund.
To qualify for Level 2 enhancements, the business must meet additional community engagement requirements, such as having local residents on its board or a community benefits agreement.
Level 2 enhancements also require a letter of approval from the local municipality or county government.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must attach the Opportunity Zone Enhancement program application as an addendum to their application for the specific underlying tax credit.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Small Business COVID-19 Emergency Relief Grant Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide grant program supporting Maryland small businesses and non-profits negatively impacted by COVID-19. The program includes a $50 million Emergency Relief Grant Fund offering grants up to $10,000 to cover operating expenses, as well as additional state Relief Act funding of $10 million for small businesses facing continued financial impacts from the pandemic.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $10,000, not to exceed 3 months of demonstrated cash operating expenses for the first quarter of 2020. Part of a $50 million fund, with additional $10 million in state Relief Act funding for businesses facing continued COVID-19 financial impacts.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland small businesses and non-profits with under 50 full- and part-time employees negatively impacted by COVID-19.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cash operating expenses including payroll, supplier costs, rent, fixed debt payments, and other mission-critical operating costs, as well as relief from continued financial impacts of COVID-19.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland-based businesses and non-profits only. Program is statewide.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland-based business or non-profit
Must have fewer than 50 full- and part-time employees
Must have been negatively impacted by COVID-19
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the Maryland Department of Commerce program page to apply.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Venture Fund provides equity investment to early-stage technology and life sciences companies in Maryland to help them grow and commercialize their innovations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Maryland Venture Fund makes equity investments in early-stage technology and life sciences companies based in Maryland. Specific investment amounts and terms are not detailed on this page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Early-stage technology and life sciences companies in Maryland seeking equity investment to grow and commercialize their products or services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business growth and commercialization of technology and life sciences innovations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to companies located in Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_name: Military Personnel and Veteran-Owned Small Business Loan Program (MPVSBLP)
structured_extraction.program_description: A no-interest loan program providing financing to businesses owned by military veterans, Reservists, and National Guard personnel, as well as small businesses with 50 or fewer employees that employ such persons. Eligible businesses may receive loans to cover general business expenses, equipment purchases, accessibility improvements for service-disabled veterans, and other necessary costs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: No-interest loans ranging from $1 to $50,000 with repayment terms of 1 to 8 years. Available to businesses owned by military veterans, Reservists, and National Guard personnel, or small businesses with 50 or fewer employees that employ such individuals. For businesses with owners called to active duty, funds can cover general business expenses caused by deployment. For service-disabled veteran-owned businesses, funds can help make a home, vehicle, or workplace accessible.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Veteran-owned businesses, Reservist-owned businesses, National Guard-owned businesses, and small businesses (50 or fewer employees) that employ veterans, Reservists, or National Guard personnel
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: For businesses with owners called to active duty, funds can cover general business expenses caused by the deployment. For businesses involving service-disabled veterans, funds can help make a home, vehicle, or workplace accessible. Funds may also cover equipment purchases and other necessary business costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Business must be owned by a military veteran, Reservist, or National Guard member, OR business must have 50 or fewer employees and employ a veteran, Reservist, or National Guard member
Must be a small business with fewer than 50 employees
Loan amount up to $50,000
Repayment term 1 to 8 years
Submit a Business Plan with 3-year projections
Provide a current Personal Financial Statement
Provide a list of all owners and their ownership percentages
Submit a resume for the principal owner(s)
Include personal federal tax returns with all schedules for the two most recent years
Include business federal tax returns with all schedules for the two most recent years
Explain the amount of personal or business funds contributed to the project
Explain the type of collateral provided to secure the loan
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application to the Maryland Department of Commerce. The Maryland Department of Veterans & Military Families then reviews it for basic eligibility. If eligible, the Department of Commerce conducts a financial review and underwriting.

structured_extraction.program_name: More Jobs for Marylanders – Manufacturing Tax Credit (MJM)
structured_extraction.program_description: A Maryland state program that promotes manufacturing growth by offering tax incentives for creating new manufacturing jobs, encouraging investment in new equipment through accelerated and bonus depreciation, and funding job training and apprenticeship programs. Manufacturers receive a 10-year state income tax credit equal to 5.75% of wages per new eligible full-time position, plus a $1,000 credit for each eligible apprentice hired. New businesses locating in Tier 1 counties may also receive a credit against the State's portion of real property tax, a refund of sales and use tax, and a waiver of fees charged by the State Department of Assessments and Taxation. In 2019, the program expanded to include non-manufacturers that locate or expand in Opportunity Zones. Note: The program stopped accepting new applicants on June 1, 2024; only companies enrolled before that date may continue to participate during their benefit period.
eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Manufacturers creating at least 5 new full-time jobs receive: (1) a 10-year state income tax credit equal to 5.75% of wages per eligible new full-time position; (2) a $1,000 tax credit for each eligible apprentice hired. New businesses locating in Tier 1 counties (e.g., Garrett County) may also receive: (1) a refundable credit against the State income tax; (2) a credit against the State's portion of real property tax; (3) a refund of sales and use tax; and (4) a waiver of fees charged by the State Department of Assessments and Taxation. Existing businesses may receive a refundable credit against the State income tax. New jobs must pay at least 120% of the State minimum wage and be filled for at least 12 months. Non-manufacturers that locate or expand in Opportunity Zones are also eligible. Businesses must notify the Maryland Department of Commerce of their intent prior to hiring new employees. Existing manufacturers may not relocate from one Maryland county to another to qualify. The program is closed to new applicants as of June 1, 2024; enrolled companies must submit an Initial and Final Tax Credit Application each year during their benefit period.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Program sunsetted June 1, 2024. Not accepting new applicants.
structured_extraction.program_audience: New and existing manufacturers (and non-manufacturers locating or expanding in Opportunity Zones) in Maryland that created at least 5 new qualified full-time jobs and enrolled before June 1, 2024.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax incentives for job creation including income tax credits, real property tax credits, sales and use tax refunds, fee waivers; accelerated and bonus depreciation on new equipment; job training and apprenticeship programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Tier 1 counties such as Garrett County and any designated Opportunity Zone receive a 10-year benefit period; Tier 2 areas receive a 5-year benefit period. Existing manufacturers that moved from one Maryland county to another after June 1, 2017 are not eligible.
requirements_list: Must have enrolled in the program before June 1, 2024
Must be a manufacturer (NAICS sectors 31, 32, or 33) or a non-manufacturer locating or expanding in an Opportunity Zone
Must locate or expand in Maryland
Must create at least 5 new full-time jobs (at least 10 in Tier 1 Areas; at least 20 in Tier 2 Areas)
New jobs must pay at least 120% of the State minimum wage (manufacturing) or at least $50,000 per year (non-manufacturing)
New jobs must be filled for at least 12 months
Must provide ongoing job training or education programs
Must notify Maryland Department of Commerce prior to hiring new employees
Existing manufacturers may not relocate from one Maryland county to another to qualify
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: This program is closed to new applicants as of June 1, 2024. Companies already enrolled must submit an Initial and Final Tax Credit Application each year during their benefit period to receive the tax credit. Previously, businesses would notify the Maryland Department of Commerce of their intent prior to hiring new employees and apply through commerce.maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Maryland state income tax credit for businesses that invest in an economic development project in a distressed (Tier 1) county by acquiring, constructing, rehabilitating, installing, or equipping a facility in Maryland — including costs to move a business from outside Maryland and furnish and equip a new location. The credit rewards businesses that create a minimum number of new, full-time qualified jobs in eligible industries within a 24-month period. Credit amounts scale with capital investment and number of new jobs created, up to a maximum of $5 million. The program also includes a Start-Up Tax Credit of up to $500,000 for eligible start-up costs. For example, the program has been used to incentivize businesses such as Crystal Steel Fabricators to expand to Maryland communities like Federalsburg, supporting job creation and capital investment.
eligible_industries: Mining, Quarrying, and Oil and Gas Extraction
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State income tax credit based on capital investment and new jobs created within a 24-month period: (1) At least $1 million in eligible project costs and 10–24 new qualified positions: up to $1 million in credits; (2) At least $2.5 million in eligible project costs and 25–49 new qualified positions: up to $2.5 million in credits; (3) At least $5 million in eligible project costs and at least 50 new qualified positions: up to $5 million in credits. The minimum eligible project cost is $500,000. Additionally, a Start-Up Tax Credit of up to $500,000 (the lesser of total eligible start-up costs, $10,000 × number of qualified employees, or $500,000) is available for furnishing/equipping a new location and relocation costs. Credits can be carried forward for up to 14 taxable years. Beginning in the fourth year after the credit year, the business may apply the credit against state income tax and request a refund limited to payroll withholding attributable to qualified positions. Insurance companies may claim the credit against insurance premiums tax.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses (for-profit and nonprofit) engaged in eligible industries that locate or expand in a Priority Funding Area within a Tier 1 County in Maryland and create at least 10 new full-time qualified jobs within 24 months. Insurance companies and 501(c)(3)/(c)(4) organizations are also eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Credit applied against Maryland state income tax liability (or insurance premiums tax for insurance companies). Eligible project costs include acquiring, constructing, rehabilitating, installing, or equipping a business facility; costs to relocate a business from outside Maryland; costs to furnish and equip the new location; land acquisition; bonds and insurance; architectural and engineering services; environmental mitigation; utility installation; interest costs; legal and accounting fees; fixed telecom equipment; and office furniture and equipment. Start-up tax credit covers furnishing/equipping a new location and moving/separation costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Project must be located in a Priority Funding Area (PFA) within a Tier 1 County, or in a qualified opportunity zone in Allegany, Garrett, Somerset, or Wicomico County. Tier 1 counties are those with an average unemployment rate exceeding 150% of the state average for the most recent 24-month period, exceeding the state average by at least 2 percentage points, or with median household income equal to or less than 75% of the state median. As of December 2025, Tier 1 counties are: Allegany, Baltimore City, Caroline, Dorchester, Garrett, Kent, Somerset, Washington, and Wicomico. Worcester County remains eligible under the 24-month look-back provision through September 2026.
requirements_list: Business must notify Maryland Commerce in writing of its intent to seek certification before incurring eligible costs or creating new qualified jobs.
Business must be certified as a qualified business entity eligible for the One Maryland Tax Credit.

Business must be engaged in an eligible activity such as manufacturing, mining, transportation, communications, agriculture, forestry, fishing, public utility, research and development, biotechnology, business services, warehousing, filmmaking, resort and recreation, computer-related services, or central financial/real estate/insurance/administrative services.
Business must create at least 10 new full-time qualified positions at the project within 24 months.

Positions must be full-time (at least 840 hours over at least 24 weeks in a 6-month period), pay at least 120% of State Minimum Wage ($18.00/hour as of January 1, 2024), be filled for 12 months, and be net new jobs to Maryland.
Business must incur at least $500,000 of eligible project costs.
Minimum $1 million in eligible project costs for the first credit tier (10–24 new qualified positions).
Project must be located in a Priority Funding Area (PFA) in a Tier 1 County, or in a qualified opportunity zone in an eligible Tier 1 county.
Project facility must be primarily engaged in an eligible activity as defined by statute.
Business may not claim both the One Maryland Tax Credit and the Job Creation Tax Credit in the same tax year.
Business must submit an annual report to Commerce each year it claims the credit during the carry-forward period.
Construction, acquisition, or installation must begin within 12 months of notification or application.
Project must be completed within 3 years.
Investment and job creation thresholds determine maximum credit amount.
Commitment to job creation.
Capital expenditures in Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Submit a written Notice of Intent to Maryland Commerce before incurring eligible costs or creating new jobs. 2. Register for an account at the Commerce online portal. 3. Submit a Preliminary Application and Employment Affidavit through the online system. 4. Upon acceptance, Commerce issues a Preliminary Certificate of Eligibility (processing time: 30–60 days). 5. After incurring eligible costs and filling at least 10 qualified positions for 12 months, submit a Final Application with documentation. 6. Commerce issues a Final Certificate of Eligibility (processing time: 120 days), which the business attaches to its tax return.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Research and Development Tax Credit program is designed to foster increased research activities and expenditures in Maryland. It provides state income tax credits to businesses that invest in qualified research and development activities in Maryland. Businesses can earn a credit equal to 10% of eligible R&D expenses that exceed the Maryland Base Amount for the taxable year, up to a maximum of $250,000 per applicant. The total program has a $12 million annual cap ($3.5 million set aside for small businesses, $8.5 million for other businesses). Small businesses with net book value assets under $5 million may receive a refundable credit for credits certified after December 15, 2012, to the extent they exceed the income tax liability for the taxable year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax credit equal to 10% of Maryland qualified R&D expenses incurred during the taxable year that exceed the Maryland Base Amount. Total statutory cap is $12 million annually ($3.5 million set aside for small businesses, $8.5 million for other businesses). No single applicant may receive more than $250,000. Credits may be carried forward for up to 7 years. For small businesses (net book value assets under $5 million), credits certified after December 15, 2012 are refundable to the extent they exceed the income tax liability for the taxable year.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: November 15 of the calendar year following the end of the taxable year in which expenses were incurred; Applications for Tax Year 2025 will be available June 1, 2026 through November 15, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit businesses (corporations, LLCs, partnerships, sole proprietorships, S corporations, estates and trusts, unincorporated trades or businesses) and individuals that incur qualified research and development expenses in Maryland, including small businesses (net book value assets less than $5,000,000) and large businesses
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Income tax credit to offset Maryland tax liability for businesses that invest in qualified research and development activities conducted in Maryland, as defined by IRC §41(b)
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Qualified R&D expenses must be incurred in Maryland. Research and development must be conducted in Maryland, and Maryland gross receipts must be reasonably attributable to the conduct of trade or business in the State.
requirements_list: Must incur Qualified Research and Development Expenses as defined by §41(b) of the Internal Revenue Code in Maryland
Expenses must qualify as 'qualified research' under IRC §41(d)
Must submit an application to Commerce by November 15 of the year following the taxable year in which expenses were incurred
For small business designation, net book value assets must total less than $5 million at the beginning or end of the taxable year
Small businesses must submit documentation showing net book value assets under $5 million
Only the parent company may apply when a corporation has subsidiaries in Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application through the online portal at rdtaxcredit.commerce.maryland.gov by November 15 of the calendar year following the tax year. Commerce will issue a tax credit certificate by February 15 of the following year. After receiving certification, the business may file an amended tax return for the year it is certified or claim the credit on a tax return for any of the following 7 tax years. The business must attach a copy of the Department's certification to its tax return.

structured_extraction.program_name: Small, Minority and Women-Owned Business Administration COVID-19 Relief Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A COVID-19 relief program providing $10 million in state Relief Act funding to small, minority, and women-owned businesses in Maryland facing continued financial impacts from the pandemic. Funded through bipartisan legislation, the program is administered through eight regional fund managers of the Video Lottery Terminal (VLT) program across the state.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: $10 million in COVID-19 relief grants disbursed through eight regional fund managers located across Maryland to small, minority, and women-owned businesses impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small, minority, and women-owned businesses in Maryland impacted by COVID-19.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Relief from continued financial impacts of COVID-19 for small, minority, and women-owned businesses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland; applications available through fund managers located in various regions of the state.
requirements_list: Business must be small, minority-owned, or women-owned
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through one of the eight fund managers operating across various regions of Maryland. Find a list of fund managers at the program website.

structured_extraction.program_name: Soft Landing Exchange for Maryland Companies
structured_extraction.program_description: This program helps Maryland companies test expansion into new international markets affordably. It provides access to facilities, resources, and networking through a global network of partners.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible companies can receive a grant of up to $10,000. This money helps pay for program costs and travel expenses like flights, lodging, and transportation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland companies that want to expand into new international markets.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Grant funds can cover participation costs charged by the partner program, as well as travel, lodging, and transportation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is available to companies located anywhere in Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To apply, click the 'Apply Now' button on the program webpage to access the online grant application.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides a refundable tax credit to theatrical production companies. The credit equals 25% of the production costs spent in Maryland. The credit is refundable, meaning the company can receive a payment even if it owes no state income tax.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers a refundable tax credit of 25% for qualified production costs spent in Maryland. The maximum credit is $2 million for a single production.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications must be submitted before beginning any work on the theatrical production in the State.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit theatrical production companies creating National Touring or Pre-Broadway productions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can cover direct production costs in Maryland. This includes set construction, special effects, wardrobe, makeup, sound, lighting, and staging. It also covers salaries for work in Maryland, advertising, facility and equipment rentals, vehicle leases, food, lodging, and travel to Maryland for employees.
requirements_list: Estimated total direct production costs in Maryland must exceed $100,000.
The production must be a for-profit National Touring or Pre-Broadway live stage theatrical production.
National Touring Productions must have at least two public performances in Maryland and then perform for four or more weeks in at least four cities outside the state.
Pre-Broadway Productions must have at least eight public performances in Maryland and be prepared for a Broadway presentation within twelve months of its final Maryland performance.
The applicant must demonstrate it has financing for the project.
Productions with total direct costs over $250,000 must provide an independent, third-party auditor's report.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, submit an Application for Qualification by email before starting any work in Maryland. The Department will review it and send a Letter of Qualification within 30 days if approved. Second, submit an Application Addendum before the first rehearsal. Third, after the production finishes, apply for the final Tax Credit Certificate within 180 days. You must include final documents and an auditor's report if your costs were over $250,000. Finally, file your state income tax return with the certificate to claim the credit.

structured_extraction.program_name: Winery and Vineyard Economic Development Grant Program (WVEDG)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides financial assistance to individuals and corporations to establish a new winery or vineyard in Maryland or to complete capital improvements at an existing winery or vineyard. The program supports agritourism businesses by funding eligible equipment and infrastructure upgrades, covering up to 25% of qualified capital expenses. Qualified capital expenses include buying and installing equipment or agricultural materials for producing wine or growing grapes.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a grant for 25% of qualified capital expenses. Eligible expenses include barrels, bins, canopy management machines, fermenters, fruit harvesters, irrigation equipment, presses, seeders, tanks, bottling equipment, tractors, and fruit plants. Total funding available is $1 million. The grant does not cover construction of buildings, utilities, labor, or general supplies. Awards are made by December 15 following the application deadline.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annually on September 15 (most recent deadline: January 16, 2026)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals or corporations that operate or want to establish a winery or vineyard in Maryland, including new and existing operations seeking to make capital improvements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Qualified capital expenses for buying and installing equipment or agricultural materials for producing wine or growing grapes. Examples include barrels, bins, canopy management machines, fermenters, fruit harvesters, irrigation equipment, presses, seeders, tanks, bottling equipment, tractors, and fruit plants. Funds may not be used for constructing buildings, utilities, labor, or general supplies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to wineries and vineyards located in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a new or existing winery or vineyard in Maryland
A qualified winery must hold a Class 3 or Class 4 winery license from the Comptroller of Maryland
A qualified vineyard must be at least one continuous acre of agricultural land in Maryland used only for growing grapes for a licensed Maryland winery
Expenses must be qualified capital expenses (buying and installing equipment or agricultural materials)
Grants cover up to 25% of eligible capital costs
Applicants must submit a detailed report of expenses with proof of purchase
Capital expenses must be for either establishing a new winery or vineyard, or making capital improvements to an existing one
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an online application to the Maryland Department of Commerce by the annual deadline (September 15, or as posted). The application must include a detailed report of expenses with supporting documents. Commerce will review the application and certify the grant amount. Awards are announced by December 15 following the application deadline. Apply at commerce.maryland.gov/wvedg.

structured_extraction.program_name: Small, Minority and Women-Owned Business Account - Video Lottery Terminal (VLT) Fund / VLT Small Business FLEX Fund / State Lottery Terminal (SLoT) Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: A state program financed by 1.5% of video lottery terminal (slots/gaming) proceeds from Maryland's six casinos that provides below-market-rate loans and other financial assistance to small, minority, women-owned, and veteran-owned businesses in Maryland. Authorized by Article XIX of the Maryland Constitution and established by Chapter 4, Acts of 2007 Special Session; authority transferred from the Board of Public Works to the Maryland Department of Commerce in May 2017 via Chapter 453, Acts of 2017. At least 50% of funds are directed to targeted businesses within jurisdictions and communities surrounding Maryland's six casinos (Hollywood Casino Perryville in Cecil County, Ocean Downs in Worcester County, Maryland Live! in Anne Arundel County, Rocky Gap Casino in Allegany County, Horseshoe Casino in Baltimore City, and National Harbor in Prince George's County), and the remaining 50% is available to eligible businesses statewide. The program is administered through a network of regional fund managers, including FSC First/Meridian Management Group (Prince George's County), Anne Arundel Economic Development Corporation, Maryland Capital Enterprises, Baltimore County Department of Economic and Workforce Development, Baltimore Development Corporation, Howard County Economic Development Authority, Tri-County Council for Western Maryland (Allegany, Garrett, and Washington counties), and Montgomery County Economic Development Corporation. In Western Maryland, the program is administered by the Tri-County Council for Western Maryland as the State Lottery Terminal (SLoT) Loan Fund, using State Lottery Terminal revenues to provide financing to small businesses and entrepreneurs, including women-owned and minority-owned businesses, in Allegany, Garrett, and Washington counties. Loans range from $10,000 to $1,000,000, with interest rates tied to the prime rate (currently prime plus 1%), terms up to 5 years for working capital and up to 15 years for fixed assets, and a minimum 10% equity injection generally required for start-up businesses. FSC First administers the VLT Small Business FLEX Fund as a $2 million loan fund offering loans from $25,000 to $250,000 with faster approval (approximately two weeks), flexible repayment options, loan terms up to 10 years, collateral in the form of business and personal assets, personal guarantees required, and no government guarantee or loan loss reserve required. The program supports small businesses — including Minority Business Enterprise (MBE)-certified companies — with flexible funding for growth capital, working capital, operational costs, real estate, equipment, manufacturing, packaging, distribution, capacity expansion, job creation, and business success. Businesses must qualify as a small business under SBA size standards. Businesses may be referred by partners such as the Maryland Department of Commerce, and fund managers arrange meetings to assess viability and review documentation before approving and disbursing funds. Recent legislation has also enabled grants of up to $10,000 when paired with a SMWOBA loan.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Commerce / FSC First / Tri-County Council for Western Maryland / Cecil County Office of Economic Development
