eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans ranging from $10,000 to $1,000,000 at below-current-market interest rates for eligible small, minority, women-owned, and veteran-owned businesses. Interest rates are tied to the prime rate (currently prime plus 1%). Terms of up to 5 years for working capital and up to 15 years for fixed assets. A $250 non-refundable application fee applies (or $25 for loans $10,000–$25,000); approved borrowers pay a 1% loan origination fee at closing. Collateral required includes Deeds of Trust, machinery and equipment liens, personal guaranties, and key man life insurance. A minimum 10% equity injection is generally required for start-up businesses. Personal credit score of 650 generally required (lower scores considered). Through FSC First (Prince George's County), loans range from $25,000 to $250,000 with terms up to 10 years, interest rate determined at underwriting, collateral including business and personal assets, personal guarantees required, reduced underwriting requirements, faster approval (approximately two weeks), flexible repayment options, and no government guarantee or loan loss reserve required. In Western Maryland, the Tri-County Council for Western Maryland administers the fund as the SLoT Loan Fund covering Allegany, Garrett, and Washington counties. At least 50% of allocations go to targeted businesses within a 10-mile radius of Maryland's six casinos; the remaining 50% is available to eligible businesses throughout Maryland. Grants of up to $10,000 may be available when paired with a SMWOBA loan. Funds may be used for business and commercial real estate acquisition and expansion, leasehold improvements, equipment, vehicles, furniture/fixtures, working capital, start-up costs, manufacturing, packaging, distribution, capacity expansion, job creation, professional services, marketing, personnel additions, inventory expansion, and refinancing of existing debt under certain circumstances. Technical assistance and informational services are also available through fund managers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small, minority, women-owned, and veteran-owned businesses in Maryland, with priority for those located in targeted areas within 10 miles of Maryland's six casinos. Also available to small business owners and entrepreneurs in Prince George's County through FSC First, and in Western Maryland (Allegany, Garrett, Washington counties) through the Tri-County Council for Western Maryland. MBE-certified companies are also eligible. Businesses must qualify as small businesses under SBA size standards. Non-minority owned businesses may also be eligible in some cases.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business acquisition and expansion, owner-occupied commercial real estate, leasehold improvements, equipment purchases, vehicles, furniture and fixtures, start-up costs, working capital, manufacturing, packaging, distribution, capacity expansion, business growth, job creation, operational improvements, marketing, personnel additions, inventory expansion, professional/technical assistance, and refinancing of existing debt under certain circumstances for small, minority, women-owned, and veteran-owned businesses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to small, minority-owned, and women-owned businesses located throughout Maryland. At least 50% of funds reserved for targeted businesses within a 10-mile radius of Maryland's six casinos (Maryland Live in Anne Arundel County, Hollywood Casino Perryville in Cecil County, Rocky Gap in Allegany County, Ocean Downs in Worcester County, Horseshoe Casino in Baltimore City, and National Harbor in Prince George's County); remaining funds available to eligible businesses throughout Maryland. Garrett, Allegany, and Washington counties are designated as a targeted area and overseen by the Tri-County Council for Western Maryland as the SLoT Loan Fund. Prince George's County businesses may access the program through FSC First as the VLT Small Business FLEX Fund.
requirements_list: Must be a small, minority, women-owned, or veteran-owned business
Business must qualify as a small business under SBA (Small Business Administration) size standards
Must be located in Maryland
Priority given to businesses in targeted areas within a 10-mile radius surrounding the six Maryland casinos
Must be a county-based business (for Prince George's County VLT FLEX Fund)
Loans between $10,000 and $1,000,000 (up to $250,000 through FSC First)
Loan term up to 10 years (FSC First) or up to 15 years for fixed assets (SLoT Fund)
Collateral required: Deeds of Trust, machinery/equipment liens, personal guaranties, key man life insurance
Personal guarantee required from all owners with 20% or greater interest
No government guarantee or loan loss reserve required (FSC First)
Minority Business Enterprise (MBE) certification noted as relevant
Must provide required documentation demonstrating company viability, including a business plan
Personal credit score of 650 generally required (lower scores considered)
Minimum equity injection of 10% generally required for start-up businesses
Non-refundable application fee of $250 (or $25 for loans $10,000–$25,000)
Approved borrowers must pay a 1% loan origination fee at closing
Standard underwriting applies: repayment capacity, debt service coverage, financial strength, industry/management experience, and collateral
Geographic proximity to casinos may be a factor for priority funding
Business must be a legally organized for-profit entity
Fund managers required to maintain state interest-bearing checking accounts
Other requirements apply
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the fund manager serving your area to apply. Fund managers include FSC First, Anne Arundel Economic Development Corporation, Meridian Management Group, Maryland Capital Enterprises, Baltimore County Department of Economic and Workforce Development, Baltimore Development Corporation, Howard County Economic Development Authority, Tri-County Council for Western Maryland, and Montgomery County Economic Development Corporation. In Western Maryland (Allegany, Garrett, Washington counties), the program is administered through the Tri-County Council for Western Maryland's SLoT Loan Fund; submit a completed SLoT inquiry form along with a business plan and the applicable non-refundable application fee ($250, or $25 for loans $10,000–$25,000). Download and complete the SLoT Loan Fund Inquiry Form and Application from https://www.tccwmd.org/apply-online/forms-and-applications and submit to the Tri-County Council for Western Maryland (info@tccwmd.org, (301) 689-1300). Businesses in Cecil County near Hollywood Casino Perryville may contact the Cecil County Office of Economic Development at 410-996-8465 for more information or to apply. In Prince George's County, the program is administered by FSC First as the VLT Small Business FLEX Fund, with a loan approval turnaround time of approximately two weeks; apply online at https://pgfscfirst.tfaforms.net/6. Businesses may also be referred by partners such as the Maryland Department of Commerce. Visit the Maryland Department of Commerce VLT program page at https://commerce.maryland.gov/fund/programs-for-businesses/vlt or the FSC First program detail page at https://fscfirst.com/learn/programs/small-business-flex-fund/ or the Tri-County Council for Western Maryland at https://www.tccwmd.org/programs/summit-financing-solutions for additional information.

structured_extraction.program_description: This fund provides grants to promote Maryland's breweries, distilleries, and wineries. The program supports research, promotion, and business development to establish the state as a top producer of craft beverages and a destination for tourists.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Commerce, Office of Tourism
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The fund provides grants to eligible organizations. The specific grant amounts are not detailed.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible applicants include nonprofit organizations with 501(c)(3) or (6) status, as well as state and local government units.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Grant funds can be used for several activities. These include expanding state breweries, distilleries, or wineries. Funds can also attract new visitors, create special promotional events, and educate the public about the industry's history. Other uses include researching local agricultural products for beverages and supporting minority ownership in these businesses.
requirements_list: Grant awardees must submit a Final Report within 60 days after the grant term ends.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, applicants should review the program's tips and hints document. Then, they must submit the application online by the deadline. The Advisory Commission on Maryland Alcohol Manufacturing and Promotion reviews applications. The commission then makes recommendations to the Secretary of Commerce, who gives final approval.

structured_extraction.program_description: Access Maryland provides capital funding to state-owned facilities, University System of Maryland campuses, and state-owned parks to make accessibility upgrades consistent with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) and Section 504, removing physical barriers to achieve programmatic accessibility for persons with disabilities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State capital funds are provided to cover design and construction phases of accessibility modification projects at state-owned facilities. Projects must cost more than $2,500. University System of Maryland and higher education campuses are required to contribute a minimum of 30% institutional funding.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications due March 1st annually; solicitation sent in January with 4-6 weeks to submit. If no solicitation received by February 1st, contact Access Maryland staff.
structured_extraction.program_audience: State agencies, University System of Maryland campuses, and state-owned parks seeking to make accessibility upgrades to their facilities for persons with disabilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Physical accessibility improvements and barrier removal at state-owned facilities, parks, and university campuses, consistent with ADA Accessible Design Standards of 2010. Covers design phase costs and construction costs for barrier-removal modifications. Projects must cost more than $2,500.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland for state-owned facilities, parks, and university campuses.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Maryland state agency, University System of Maryland campus, or state-owned park
Facility must be state-owned
Projects must address physical accessibility barriers consistent with ADA Accessible Design Standards of 2010
Current ADA Transition Plan on file (within 3 years)
Project costs must exceed $2,500
Minimum 30% institutional funding contribution required (USM/higher education campuses)
Project cannot be part of a larger renovation or 5-year CIP
Project not located in auxiliary facilities
Not for employee reasonable accommodations
Design must be completed and approved within one year of funding
Construction contract must be awarded within 6 months of design approval
Projects cannot exceed anticipated costs by more than 25%
Must focus on programmatic access
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: A solicitation is sent in January; state agencies and USM campuses have 4-6 weeks to submit applications, with a deadline of March 1st. If no solicitation is received by February 1st, contact Access Maryland staff. The Maryland Department of Disabilities prioritizes requests, recommends projects for funding, and provides oversight through design and construction phases. See the Policies and Procedures document for full application and review process details.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides financial reimbursement to help adults with severe chronic or permanent physical disabilities pay for attendant care services. Participants choose their own care providers and can receive services at home, school, work, or other community locations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial reimbursement for attendant care services provided in the home, school, workplace, or other community locations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults age 18 to 64 with severe chronic or permanent physical disabilities who need attendant care services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment for attendant care services in home, school, workplace, or other community settings.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be an adult age 18 to 64
Must have a severe chronic or severe physical disability

Must meet at least one of: be self-employed or competitively employed with compensation; be actively seeking employment; be attending a postsecondary, higher education, or apprenticeship training program; be a resident of a nursing facility seeking to transition into the community; or be at risk of nursing home placement as certified by a physician if attendant care services are not received in the community
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register a OneStop account at onestop.md.gov. Provide your first and last name and a verifiable email address. Once registered, return to the home screen and select 'Maryland Department of Disabilities' to complete a short application to be placed on the registry. As space becomes available on the waiting list, you will receive an email link to complete the full application.

structured_extraction.program_name: Centers for Independent Living Technical Assistance (CIL-TA) Project
structured_extraction.program_description: A technical assistance project to benefit Maryland's seven Centers for Independent Living (CILs). The project provides technical assistance and training to CILs on enhancing operational infrastructure and program sustainability, in support of the state's Aging and Disability Resource Centers (ADRCs).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Technical assistance and training on enhancing operational infrastructure and program sustainability, delivered by the Maryland Center for Developmental Disabilities at Kennedy Krieger Institute.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland's seven Centers for Independent Living (CILs) that serve as ADRC disability partners.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Enhancing operational infrastructure and program sustainability of Centers for Independent Living.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Centers for Independent Living operating in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be one of Maryland's seven designated Centers for Independent Living

structured_extraction.program_description: The Communication Facilitator (CF) service provides DeafBlind Marylanders with equal access to communication during video calls. A skilled signer — the Communication Facilitator — copies sign language from a video caller and relays it to the DeafBlind person through close-vision, tactile sign language, tracking, or another method. The service supports calls over any video platform, including videophone, Video Relay Services, FaceTime, Zoom, Skype, Google Hangouts, and Google Meet, and can be used at home or in public spaces.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free communication facilitation service for DeafBlind individuals. A Communication Facilitator assists during video calls and in-person settings by relaying sign language and visual information through close-vision, tactile sign language, ProTactile, tracking, or spoken English. Available at home or in other locations of the consumer's choice.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Marylanders who are DeafBlind (combined hearing and vision loss)
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Communication facilitation during video calls and in-person interactions with friends, family, coworkers, and others
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Must be DeafBlind (combined hearing and vision loss)
Must complete the Communication Facilitator Service DeafBlind Consumer Application (available at MDRelay.org)
Must be approved by the MAT program before receiving CF services
Must complete Communication Facilitator Service Request Form to schedule services
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Communication Facilitator Service DeafBlind Consumer Application (available at MDRelay.org) and submit it to the MAT program for approval. Once approved, submit a Communication Facilitator Service Request Form to CF.Scheduler@Maryland.gov to schedule the service.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Auto Program (CAP) is a state pilot program that facilitates the donation of working, adapted vehicles to eligible individuals with disabilities who cannot qualify for other programs or financing to purchase adapted vehicles. The program also facilitates vehicle modifications and adaptations for eligible individuals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides donated, working, adapted vehicles to eligible recipients at no cost. Vehicles are donated by others and redistributed to qualified individuals with disabilities. The program also facilitates vehicle modifications and adaptation services for eligible individuals. Priority is given to individuals residing in areas with limited access to public transportation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with disabilities who use a mobility aid and cannot qualify for other programs or financing to purchase adapted vehicles. Priority is given to those residing in areas with limited access to public transportation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Receiving a donated, working, adapted vehicle for personal transportation, as well as vehicle modification and adaptation services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Individuals residing in areas with limited access to public transportation are prioritized.
requirements_list: Must be an individual with a disability who uses a mobility aid
Must be the vehicle's primary driver
Must possess a valid driver's license with appropriate adaptation restrictions, OR possess a current (last 12 months) prescription for vehicle modifications

Must have been turned down for a financial loan through the AT Financial Loan Program within the MD Department of Disabilities, OR voluntarily self-disqualify by not applying to the AT Financial Loan Program
Must not qualify for other Department programs providing adapted vehicle access
Residency in areas with limited public transportation access is prioritized
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Email mdtap.general@maryland.gov for information on the qualification process and to join the driver-eligibility list. Individuals who want to donate a working, adapted vehicle may also contact via email.

structured_extraction.program_description: Community Choice Homes provides affordable rental housing in Montgomery County for adults with disabilities who have extremely low income. Participants pay 30% of their monthly adjusted household income for rent and utilities while living in one of 30 Housing Opportunities Commission (HOC)-owned rental units. The program is a partnership between the Housing Opportunities Commission of Montgomery County and the Maryland Department of Disabilities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants pay only 30% of their monthly adjusted household income for rent and utilities in one of 30 HOC-owned units. This is a project-based affordable housing subsidy tied to specific units for a period of 15 years. The subsidy does not transfer if the participant leaves the unit.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults with disabilities aged 18–62 at time of leasing who have extremely low income (at or below 30% of area median income), receive SSI or SSDI, and live or work in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Affordable rental housing — subsidized rent and utilities in HOC-owned units in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Montgomery County, Maryland. Applicants must live or work in Montgomery County at the time of referral, or have lived or worked in Montgomery County within the past 5 years and currently live in an institution or group living setting.
requirements_list: Household income at or below 30% of area median income (AMI), with priority for income between 10–30% AMI
Income must include cash payment from SSI or SSDI at the time of initial eligibility determination (applicants with suspended SSI eligibility also qualify)
Adults aged 18–62 at time of leasing (may continue in the program after age 62)
Must be registered on the HOC Housing Path Waitlist
Must live or work in Montgomery County at time of referral, or have done so within the past 5 years and currently reside in an institution or group living setting

Criminal background must not include a requirement to register on a lifetime sex offender registry or a conviction for production of methamphetamine on federally assisted housing, and must meet other HOC eligibility requirements

Must comply with program requirements including maintaining housing assistance eligibility, applying for rent subsidies as offered by HOC, completing tenant training, making timely rent and utility payments, and adhering to all lease terms
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Persons with disabilities should contact their case manager, support planner, resource coordinator, coordinator of community service, or community health worker to complete the pre-screening and application. Case managers add interested applicants to the MDOD Weinberg Apartment waitlist via www.Socialserve.com. Priority for referral goes to applicants on the Weinberg Apartment waitlist who want to live in Montgomery County, have a Montgomery County address, and meet CCH eligibility criteria. HOC verifies eligibility including income and criminal background.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community First Choice Self-Direction (CFC SD) Training Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A training program for Community First Choice (CFC) participants who want to self-direct their personal assistance services. The program offers individual and small group training at the participant's home or an accessible community location. Topics include how to recruit, interview, hire, supervise, and dismiss personal assistance providers, as well as emergency preparedness and creating a back-up plan.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Individual and small group training sessions held at the participant's home or an accessible community location. Participants are referred through their Supports Planner.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community First Choice (CFC) participants who are interested in or want more information about self-directing their personal assistance services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training on how to manage personal assistance providers and serve as an effective employer.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a Community First Choice (CFC) participant
Must be referred through a Supports Planner
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Participants are referred to the program through their Supports Planner.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides individual and family supports to people with developmental disabilities who are on the DDA Waiting List.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides individual and family supports to up to 400 people with developmental disabilities on the DDA Waiting List, with an overall budget cap of $25,000 per year per participant.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with developmental disabilities on the DDA Waiting List.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Individual and family support services for people with developmental disabilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must have a developmental disability
Must be on the DDA Waiting List
Annual budget cap of $25,000 per person
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: See DDA's website for more information on how to access this waiver.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides expedited and accountable energy and energy efficiency assistance to medically vulnerable households. The program is intended to continue or restore utility service for people with critical medical needs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Expedited energy and efficiency program assistance to continue or restore utility service for medically vulnerable households. Case managers must complete navigator training through the Office of the People's Counsel before helping clients apply.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Medically vulnerable households at risk of losing or already without utility service. Case managers who support these clients must become trained navigators.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Continuing or restoring utility service for medically vulnerable households.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Household must be medically vulnerable
Case managers must attend navigator training through the Office of the People's Counsel before assisting clients
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Case managers attend training to become a navigator, then assist their client in applying for program assistance.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides individual and family supports for children from birth to age 21 with developmental disabilities who are on the Developmental Disabilities Administration (DDA) Waiting List.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Individual and family supports provided through a Medicaid waiver approved by the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services, administered by the DDA.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Children from birth to age 21 with developmental disabilities who are on the DDA Waiting List
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Individual and family supports for children with developmental disabilities
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Must have a developmental disability
Age birth to 21
Must be on the DDA Waiting List
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: See DDA's website for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: Hearing Carry-Over (HCO) is a Maryland Relay telephone service for people who can hear clearly but have difficulty speaking or being understood over the phone. A Maryland Relay Operator voices the user's typed words to the other person, while the user listens directly to the other person's spoken response.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free relay telephone service that allows users to type their side of a conversation while a Maryland Relay Operator voices the typed words to the other party. The user listens directly to the other person's spoken response. HCO-to-HCO and HCO-to-TTY options are also available. Users can request HCO with Privacy so the Operator cannot hear the other person's response. HCO phones and assistive devices may also be available through the Maryland Accessible Telecommunications (MAT) program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents who can hear clearly but have difficulty speaking or being understood over the telephone.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Access to relay telephone communication services for people with speech disabilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Maryland residents statewide.
requirements_list: User must be able to hear clearly but have difficulty speaking or being understood over the telephone
User must have a TTY or HCO phone to type their side of the conversation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Dial 7-1-1 or 800-735-2258 to connect to a Maryland Relay Operator. Type 'HCO PLS GA' to indicate an HCO call, or set up a Customer Profile to automatically connect with the appropriate Operator. Enter the number you wish to call and begin your conversation. For HCO phones provided by the state, apply through the Maryland Accessible Telecommunications (MAT) program.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Assistive Technology Program (MDTAP) operates a small 3D printing lab that fabricates low-tech assistive devices for Marylanders with disabilities at no cost. Eligible individuals can request devices through an online catalogue and request form, choosing from available models. MDTAP also works with requesters on device customization to best meet individual needs, including printing custom devices not in the standard catalogue.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free 3D-printed low-tech assistive devices fabricated on request. Applicants choose from a catalogue of available models and can request customization to meet individual needs. Devices are provided at no charge to Marylanders with disabilities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Marylanders with disabilities who need low-tech assistive devices
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Receiving free 3D-printed assistive devices tailored to individual needs to support daily living and independence
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Maryland statewide
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident with a disability
Must submit a request through the 3D AT Catalogue and Request Form or contact MDTAP directly
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review the 3D AT Catalogue and Request Form online and submit a request, or contact MDTAP directly by phone at 1-800-832-4827 or by email with questions or customization needs.

structured_extraction.program_name: MDTAP Consultations, Demonstrations, and Device Loans
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Assistive Technology Program (MDTAP) offers free consultations, device demonstrations, and short-term device loans to help people with disabilities find assistive technology (AT) that supports independent living, working, and learning. Staff meet with consumers in person or virtually to discuss needs and explore AT options. Consumers can try devices hands-on and borrow AT free of charge for up to 4 weeks at a time, with shipping and virtual setup support available.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free consultations (in-person or virtual), hands-on or virtual device demonstrations, and device loans for up to 4 weeks at a time. Devices can be picked up in person or shipped directly to the consumer, with virtual setup and instructional support provided at no charge.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with disabilities who need assistive technology to live, work, or learn more independently
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Accessing assistive technology through consultations, demonstrations, and device loans
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a service request online at https://forms.gle/xRG1DY6q3AqU7UyN6 or contact MDTAP directly by phone or email.

structured_extraction.program_description: Origin-to-destination transportation service for people with disabilities who cannot ride fixed-route public transit. Registered users can use paratransit services across all Maryland cities and throughout the U.S., though pre-registration is required with each system.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Door-to-door paratransit transportation for eligible individuals with disabilities who cannot use fixed-route public transit. Riders must apply and be certified by the MTA Certification Division. Trip planning assistance is also available Monday through Friday, 6:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m.
structured_extraction.program_audience: People with disabilities who are unable to ride fixed-route public transportation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Transportation to and from destinations for individuals with disabilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland; registered users are also eligible to use paratransit services in other U.S. cities.
requirements_list: Must have a disability that prevents use of fixed-route public transportation
Must complete a certification application through the MTA Certification Division
Must pre-register with each paratransit system you wish to use
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Obtain a certification application from the MTA Mobility website or the MTA Certification Division. Complete and mail the form to: Maryland Transit Administration, Certification Division, 4201 Patterson Avenue - 2nd Floor, Baltimore, MD 21215.

structured_extraction.program_description: The MAT program provides free or reduced-cost assistive telecommunications equipment to qualified Maryland residents who have difficulty using a standard telephone due to a disability. Equipment options include amplified phones, captioned telephones, tablets, text telephones (TTYs), Braille TTY devices, picture phones, hands-free phones, large-button phones, ring signalers, and other adaptive phone devices to help people independently make or receive phone calls. Braille TTY devices allow DeafBlind users to type their side of a phone conversation and read the other person's responses on a Braille display using the Maryland Relay service. Captioned telephones display word-for-word captions of what the other person says during a call, working like a standard phone with added captioning technology. The program also provides free personalized one-on-one evaluations at statewide MAT evaluation centers — located in Baltimore, Cumberland, Easton, Glen Burnie, Hagerstown, Mechanicsville, Salisbury, Silver Spring, and Towson — along with personalized setup instructions and training from a MAT evaluator. Specialists can even create custom equipment solutions. During the evaluation, a trained evaluator works one-on-one with the participant to assess their needs, demonstrate equipment options, and place an order for state-provided equipment. After approval, equipment is loaned by the State and mailed within 4–6 weeks of the completed evaluation. Captioned phones may also be purchased directly from Weitbrecht Communications for $75 with a 90-day money-back guarantee. Free Braille TTY training is also available upon request. Equipment must be returned if the participant moves out of state.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Qualified Maryland residents can receive a no-cost loan of telecommunications equipment through the MAT program, including amplified phones, captioned telephones, TTYs, Braille TTY devices, tablets, picture phones, hands-free phones, large-button phones, ring signalers, and other adaptive phone devices. Equipment options also include Voice Captioned Telephone, HCO, STS, Video Phone, and Augmentative and Alternative Communication (AAC) devices. Covered repair/maintenance for normal wear and tear is included. Specialists can create custom solutions as needed. The program also provides a free personalized one-on-one evaluation at one of the statewide MAT evaluation centers (located in Baltimore, Cumberland, Easton, Glen Burnie, Hagerstown, Mechanicsville, Salisbury, Silver Spring, and Towson) and personalized setup instructions and additional training from a MAT evaluator. After approval, equipment is mailed within 4–6 weeks of the completed evaluation. Captioned phones may also be purchased directly from Weitbrecht Communications for $75 with a 90-day money-back guarantee. Free Braille TTY training is available by calling 800-552-7724, 410-767-6960 (Voice/TTY), or 443-453-5970 (Video Phone).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents age 3 or older who have difficulty using a standard telephone due to a disability, including being Deaf, hard of hearing, DeafBlind, blind, low vision, or having cognitive, mobility, speech, or physical disabilities, and who are on a fixed income or receive qualifying benefits.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: No-cost loan or acquisition of accessible telecommunications equipment such as amplified phones, captioned telephones, TTYs, Braille TTY devices, tablets, picture phones, hands-free phones, large-button phones, ring signalers, and other adaptive phone devices for personal home communication use. Equipment evaluations and Braille TTY training are also provided free of charge to help participants select and use the most appropriate device.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to qualified Maryland residents statewide through evaluation centers located throughout the state in Baltimore, Cumberland, Easton, Glen Burnie, Hagerstown, Mechanicsville, Salisbury, Silver Spring, and Towson. Applicants must have a mailing address in Maryland (not a PO box) and must have landline or Internet service (or have applied for such service). Equipment must be returned if the participant moves out of state.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident
Must be at least 3 years old (applicants 18 and under need a parent or legal guardian signature)
Must have difficulty using a standard telephone due to a disability
Must be certified as Deaf, hard of hearing, DeafBlind, blind, low vision, or having cognitive, mobility, or speech-related difficulties

Must be on a fixed income or receive at least one of: Social Security (SSA) benefits, Veterans (VA) benefits, Supplemental Security Income (SSI), Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI), Temporary Disability Assistance Program (TDAP), Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF), or pharmacy/medical/housing assistance
Must have hearing loss or difficulty hearing over the phone (for captioned telephone)
Must be DeafBlind or otherwise eligible under the MAT program criteria (for Braille TTY)

Must complete a Disability Certification form signed by a qualified medical or rehabilitation professional (e.g., doctor, audiologist, rehabilitation counselor, speech pathologist, social worker, psychologist, mental health counselor, registered nurse, licensed practical nurse, or physical therapist)
Must provide required eligibility documents with application, including proof of benefits or fixed income, a copy of a photo ID, and a copy of a telephone or utility bill
Must have home phone service, high-speed internet/WiFi, or be applying for phone or internet service
Must have a mailing address in Maryland (not a PO box)
Must complete an application signed by the applicant or their power of attorney
Must complete a free one-on-one evaluation after approval (mandatory for all participants approved to receive state-provided equipment)
Federal law prohibits use of IP Captioned Telephone with captions turned on by anyone other than registered users with hearing loss
Equipment must be returned if the participant moves out of state
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Review qualification criteria. 2. Complete the application online at mat-apply.org, download and print the application, request by mail, or email the completed application. 3. Have a licensed physician, audiologist, speech pathologist, or rehabilitation counselor complete and sign the Disability Certification Form (Part 4). 4. Include required documentation: proof of benefits or fixed income, a copy of a photo ID, and a copy of a telephone or utility bill. 5. Mail all completed forms to: State of Maryland – MAT Program, 301 W. Preston St., Suite 1008A, Baltimore, MD 21201. A notification letter is mailed approximately two weeks after the completed application is received. If approved, the letter includes instructions for scheduling a free one-on-one evaluation (in-person or virtual) at one of the evaluation centers throughout Maryland. A MAT specialist helps you select the right equipment (including custom solutions if needed), which is then ordered and mailed within 4–6 weeks. For Braille TTY training, call 800-552-7724 or 410-767-6960 (Voice/TTY) or 443-453-5970 (Video Phone). For more information, call 800-552-7724 or 410-767-7253 (Voice/TTY) or 410-801-9618 (Video Phone), or email [email protected].

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Assistive Technology Loan Program (also known as the Assistive Technology Financial Loan Program, ATLP), administered by the Maryland Assistive Technology Program (MDTAP) under the Maryland Department of Disabilities, helps Maryland residents with disabilities, older Marylanders, and their families qualify for low-interest loans to purchase assistive technology equipment and devices to live, work, and learn more independently. Loans can be used for a wide range of assistive technology including home modifications, adapted and non-adapted vehicles and vehicle modifications, scooters and wheelchairs, braille equipment, hearing and vision aids, augmentative communication devices, environmental control units, computers and adaptive peripherals, and other devices that support independent living, work, and employment goals. Lending criteria are more lenient than traditional bank loans, with below-market fixed interest rates and extended repayment terms. In 2021, 25 loans were approved with a total value of $644,719.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest loans ranging from $500 to $70,000 with below-market, fixed interest rates and extended repayment terms. Unsecured AT loans up to $10,000; unsecured vehicle and home modification loans up to $20,000; non-adapted vehicles up to $40,000; adapted vehicles up to $70,000. Rates vary by creditworthiness and are disclosed at application processing. Lending criteria are more lenient than traditional bank loans. A loan guarantee program is also available for applicants declined by lenders, where the ATLP Board may guarantee loans and make partial or full payments on the applicant's behalf. In 2021, 25 loans were approved with a total value of $644,719.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents with disabilities, older Marylanders, and their families, as well as family members, friends, or others intending to purchase assistive technology for a Maryland resident with a disability, who need equipment, home accessibility modifications, or vehicle purchases to live, work, and learn more independently. U.S. military veterans receive preferred consideration.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of assistive technology devices and services including home modifications, adapted and non-adapted vehicles and vehicle modifications, scooters and wheelchairs, braille equipment, hearing and vision aids, augmentative communication devices, environmental control units, computers and adaptive peripherals, smart home technology, and other devices that help people with disabilities live, work, and learn more independently.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland; loan must be for the benefit of a Maryland resident with a disability.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident with a disability, or the loan must be used to purchase assistive technology for a Maryland resident with a disability
Approval based on income compared to debt, stability in residence and employment, payment history with existing creditors, and financial ability to repay the loan
Some applicants may be declined based on creditworthiness; loan guarantee available if declined by lender
Photo ID required (passport, driver's license, or state-issued ID)
Income documentation required (pay stubs within 30 days, SSI/SSDI award letters, pension statements, or tax forms 1099/1040/W-2)
Credit authorization and background check required
Must affirm legal statements and confession of judgment
Can apply as independent borrower or with a co-applicant; co-applicant must provide information and signature before processing
Must create a OneStop account to apply online
Loan amounts and terms subject to restrictions and qualifications
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Create a OneStop account and upload a photo ID. Complete and submit the ATLP application online at the Maryland OneStop portal (https://onestop.md.gov/forms/mdod-assistive-technology-loan-program-application-6322337acffd140001989667), or download the fillable PDF application and email it with supporting documents to mdtap.atlp@maryland.gov. MDOD reviews the application for completeness, then forwards to the lender for review. If declined by the lender, the ATLP Board reviews for a possible loan guarantee. An appeal option is available if the Board declines. For more information, call 1-800-832-4827 or email mdtap.atlp@maryland.gov. Financial counseling and coaching is available through a partnership with the CASH Campaign of Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Homeownership Program for Individuals with Disabilities (HomeAbility)
structured_extraction.program_description: A home loan program for individuals with disabilities and their caregivers who meet eligibility criteria, administered through the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A home loan available to individuals with disabilities and their caregivers who meet the program's eligibility criteria.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with disabilities and their caregivers seeking to purchase a home in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home purchase financing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be an individual with a disability or a caregiver of an individual with a disability
Must meet the program's eligibility criteria
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the Maryland Mortgage Program website for details on how to apply.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Relay offers free presentations for schools, groups, and organizations on topics such as relay services, assistive telecommunications equipment, and how to apply for free equipment through the Maryland Accessible Telecommunications (MAT) program. Presentations are led by outreach coordinators who tailor content to each audience.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free in-person or arranged presentations by Maryland Relay outreach coordinators covering relay services, assistive telecommunications equipment, and the MAT program. Topics are customized to the requesting group's needs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Schools, groups, and organizations seeking information about Maryland Relay services and assistive telecommunications equipment.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Presentations covering relay services, assistive equipment options, and MAT program eligibility — no funds disbursed.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must submit an online inquiry form or call to schedule a presentation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the online inquiry form or call 800-552-7724, 410-767-6960 (Voice/TTY), or 443-453-5970 (Video Phone) and ask to speak to an outreach coordinator.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free program that trains Maryland businesses on how to identify, receive, and place Relay calls — phone calls made by people who are deaf, hard of hearing, or have speech disabilities through Maryland Relay. Businesses get free on-site training, promotional materials, and a listing in the Relay Partner directory.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free on-site training with a Maryland Relay outreach coordinator on how to place and receive Relay calls. Also includes free promotional materials (window decal, digital website badge), ongoing promotion of the business to Relay users, a listing in the Relay Partner online directory, and access to a digital library of training and promotional materials.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland-based businesses that want to better serve customers who use Maryland Relay (people who are deaf, hard of hearing, or have speech disabilities).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and promotional support to help businesses communicate with Relay users.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Open to all Maryland-based businesses.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland-based business
Must have a telephone — no other special equipment required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 800-552-7724 or 410-767-6960 (Voice/TTY) or 443-453-5970 (Video Phone) and ask to speak to an outreach coordinator about becoming a Maryland Relay Partner. You can also complete the online registration form at https://doit.maryland.gov/mdrelay/Pages/relay-partner-registration.aspx.

structured_extraction.program_name: Model Waiver for Medically Fragile Children
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides medically necessary home and community-based services for children with complex medical needs, from birth through age 21, so they can live with their families in their own homes instead of a hospital, nursing facility, or other long-term care facility. The program is limited to a maximum of 200 enrolled individuals. Parents' income and assets are waived during the financial eligibility process, and services must be cost-neutral compared to institutional care costs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides medically necessary community-based services to enable medically fragile children to live at home rather than in institutional settings. The program is limited to a maximum of 200 enrolled individuals. Parents' income and assets are waived during the financial eligibility process. Services must be cost-neutral compared to institutional care costs.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Coordinator Center for Home and Community Care
structured_extraction.program_audience: Medically fragile children from birth through age 21 who are chronically ill or severely impaired and need hospital or nursing facility level of care, and their families.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home-based medical and support services as an alternative to hospital or nursing facility care, enabling medically fragile children to live at home with their families.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland for Maryland residents.
requirements_list: Must be admitted before turning 22 years old
Must have complex medical needs (chronically ill or severely impaired)
Must need hospital or nursing facility level of care as determined by a state-contracted reviewer
Medically necessary community-based services must be cost-neutral compared to institutional care costs
Parents' income and assets are waived during financial eligibility process
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: A state-contracted reviewer assesses the level of care needed based on information provided by the referring physician. Contact the Coordinator Center for Home and Community Care at 410-987-1048 (Baltimore), 301-621-7830 (Washington), or 1-877-463-3464 (Maryland Department of Health). TTY: 1-800-735-2258.

structured_extraction.program_name: Money Follows the Person (MFP) Peer Outreach and Support Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A peer outreach and support program that connects individuals living in nursing facilities with peers who have personal experience transitioning to community living. Peers visit nursing facilities, participate in group activities, and educate residents about their options for long-term services and supports in the community.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Peer outreach and support visits to nursing facility residents who want information about transitioning to community living. Peers are individuals with disabilities who have personal experience with the transition process or are currently receiving community supports.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals residing in nursing facilities who want more information about living in the community.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Education and support related to transitioning from nursing facilities to community living.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be residing in a nursing facility
Must be interested in learning about community living options
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Peers visit nursing facilities regularly to connect with residents.

structured_extraction.program_description: Remote Conference Captioning (RCC) is a free service that provides real-time text captioning of conference calls for people with hearing loss. A captionist listens to the call and types everything said, so users can read the text on any internet-connected device during the call.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free real-time captioning service for conference calls. No special software is required. Users must submit a scheduling request at least 24 hours before the call. After scheduling, the user receives an email with a link to view captions on a computer or mobile device.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents, businesses, and organizations where participants have hearing loss, are Deaf, hard of hearing, late-deafened, DeafBlind, or have difficulty speaking.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Real-time captioning of conference calls to enable effective communication for people with hearing loss.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available exclusively to Maryland residents, businesses, and organizations.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident, business, or organization
Must have access to a conference bridge or high-quality audio (telephone, webcast, or VoIP)
Must submit the RCC Scheduling Request Form at least 24 hours before the call to guarantee service
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the RCC Scheduling Request Form at https://hamiltonrelay.com/maryland/services/rcc-remote-conference-captioning/ at least 24 hours before the scheduled conference call. After scheduling, the user receives an email with a link to view captions on their device during the call.

structured_extraction.program_description: Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) provides monthly cash benefits to blind or disabled workers, widow(er)s, adults disabled since childhood, and qualifying family members. Eligibility is based on the worker's earnings record and Social Security tax (FICA) contributions, or those of a spouse or parent. The program is authorized under Title II of the Social Security Act and is funded through worker contributions to the Social Security trust fund. Three pathways exist: (1) SSDI based on own work history; (2) Adult Child with Disability benefits based on parent's work history; (3) Surviving Spouse with Disability benefits based on deceased spouse's work history. Includes Medicare eligibility after 2 years of benefits receipt.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Monthly cash benefits paid to eligible blind or disabled workers, widow(er)s, adults disabled since childhood, and certain qualifying family members who have worked long enough and paid Social Security taxes. Benefit amounts are based on the recipient's Social Security earnings record and prior FICA contributions. Disability must be medically determinable and expected to last 12+ continuous months or result in death. Medicare eligibility is granted after 2 years of receiving SSDI benefits. Work incentives allow beneficiaries to work while maintaining partial cash benefits up to the Substantial Gainful Activity (SGA) threshold.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Blind or disabled workers, widow(er)s, adults who have been disabled since childhood, and qualifying family members who have paid Social Security taxes (FICA) through their own work history or that of a spouse or parent, including Marylanders meeting eligibility requirements. Also includes dependents of eligible insured workers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: General living expenses and income support for eligible disabled or blind individuals and their families. Also covers healthcare through Medicare (after 2 years on SSDI) and Medicaid/Medical Assistance through the EID program for working individuals with disabilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available nationwide, including all Maryland residents.
requirements_list: Must be blind or have a disability that meets Social Security's definition
Impairment must be medically determinable (physical or mental)
Disability must be expected to last 12+ continuous months or result in death
Condition must be severe
Condition must be found on the Social Security list of disabling conditions or be equivalent
Must be unable to engage in substantial gainful work activity
Must be insured — meaning you worked long enough and paid Social Security taxes (FICA), or are eligible through a spouse's or parent's earnings record
Work credits (insured worker status) must be met for SSDI eligibility
For Adult Child with Disability benefits: must have a parent with qualifying work history
Complete and return periodic paperwork verifying timely progress requirements when assigned to Ticket to Work program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at www.SSA.gov, by phone at 1-800-772-1213, or in person at a local Social Security field office. If work credit criteria are met, the case is sent to Maryland Disability Determination Services (DDS), which develops medical evidence and makes a disability determination through a team of physician/psychologist and disability examiner. You may also call DDS at 1-833-877-3084 or contact the Medical Relations Office at 410-308-4335. If denied, applicants may appeal the decision online or by mail based on instructions in the denial letter. DORS can provide benefits counseling services to help understand the impact of earnings on benefits.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Relay's Speech-to-Speech (STS) service helps people with mild to moderate speaking difficulties make and receive phone calls. A Maryland Relay Operator listens to the STS user and re-voices what they say to the other person on the call, making phone communication accessible for people with conditions such as cerebral palsy, Parkinson's disease, stuttering, or stroke.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free relay operator service available by dialing 7-1-1 or 800-785-5630. A Maryland Relay Operator re-voices the STS user's speech as needed during phone calls. A Visually Assisted STS option is also available using live video. Users can set up a Customer Profile to customize their calling preferences.
structured_extraction.contact_phone: 866-269-9006 (English) or 866-744-7471 (Spanish) for STS User Training Line
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents with mild to moderate speaking difficulties who can hear clearly on the phone, including those with cerebral palsy, multiple sclerosis, muscular dystrophy, Parkinson's disease, stroke, stuttering, traumatic brain injury, or laryngectomy.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Telephone relay communication assistance for people with speaking difficulties.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must have mild to moderate speaking difficulties
Must be able to hear clearly on the phone
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Dial 7-1-1 or 800-785-5630 to reach a Maryland Relay Operator. Tell the operator you want an STS call and provide the number you wish to call. Optionally set up a Customer Profile for automatic connection to the appropriate operator.

structured_extraction.program_description: Supplemental Security Income (SSI) provides monthly cash assistance payments to people who are elderly (age 65 or older), blind, or disabled (including children) who have limited income and resources. The federal government funds SSI from general tax revenues. Eligibility depends on income and resources (things you own). Recipients are also automatically eligible for Medicaid (Medical Assistance). Work incentive programs are available to protect benefits while working. Disability determinations for Maryland applicants are evaluated by the Disability Determination Services (DDS) as part of the Social Security Administration's disability determination process.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Monthly cash payments to eligible individuals who have low income and limited resources and meet age (65 or older), blindness, or disability criteria, including children with disabilities. Benefits are based on financial need. Recipients are also automatically eligible for Medicaid/Medical Assistance. Work incentive programs are available to help protect benefits while working. Asset limits apply ($2,000 for individuals; $3,000 for married couples).
structured_extraction.program_audience: People with low income and limited resources who are age 65 or older, blind, or disabled (including children under age 18 and adults), including Maryland residents with disabilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Monthly income support for general living expenses and basic needs for eligible recipients based on financial need. Also covers automatic Medicaid/healthcare coverage and supports employment through work incentive programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available nationwide, including statewide in Maryland. Program is federally administered with state-level implementation by Maryland DDS.
requirements_list: Must be age 65 or older, blind, or disabled (including children)

Must meet Social Security's definition of disability (inability to engage in substantial gainful work activity due to medically determinable impairment lasting 12+ continuous months or resulting in death)
For children under 18: medically determinable impairment causing marked and severe functional limitations, lasting 12+ months or resulting in death
Must have low income
Must have limited resources (assets below $2,000 for individuals; $3,000 for married couples)
Must demonstrate financial need
Medical documentation must be sufficiently complete to evaluate severity, functional restrictions, and duration
For 1619-B work incentive: earnings below $41,740/year; continued need for Medicaid; no other reasons for SSI loss
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at the Social Security website (www.SSA.gov), by calling SSA at 1-800-772-1213, or by visiting a local Social Security office. A large part of the application can be completed online. Maryland residents may call DDS at 1-833-877-3084 for more information. DDS assigns an examiner who requests medical and non-medical evidence, reviews evidence, consults with a physician or psychologist, and determines eligibility. DORS counselors and Benefits Counselors are also available to assist with employment services.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Relay provides a telephone relay service for people who are Deaf, hard of hearing, or have difficulty speaking. Users type on a TTY (text telephone) and a Maryland Relay Operator voices the typed text to the other party, then types back the spoken responses so the TTY user can read them. This allows two-way telephone communication between TTY users and standard phone users, including direct TTY-to-TTY calls, relay operator assistance for calls to non-TTY users, call answering procedures, and emergency 9-1-1 access.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free telephone relay service connecting TTY users with standard phone users through a trained Relay Operator. Users dial 7-1-1 or 800-735-2258 to initiate a call. The Operator voices the TTY user's typed text and types back the spoken responses. Supports direct TTY-to-TTY calls, relay operator assistance for calls to non-TTY users, and emergency 9-1-1 access. All conversations are kept confidential by law.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Deaf and hard of hearing individuals, as well as people who have difficulty speaking, who need to make or receive telephone calls.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Telephone relay service for communication between TTY users and standard phone users.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Maryland residents statewide. Agency located at 301 W. Preston Street, Suite 1008A, Baltimore, MD 21201.
requirements_list: Must be Deaf, hard of hearing, or have difficulty speaking
Must have access to a TTY device for direct user calls
Knowledge of TTY abbreviations and protocols (GA, SK, etc.) recommended
Proper placement of phone receiver on TTY cups with curly cord to the left
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: No application required. Dial 7-1-1 or 800-735-2258 to begin using the relay service. User training is available by calling 800-552-7724, 410-767-6960 (Voice/TTY), or 443-453-5970 (Video Phone).

structured_extraction.program_name: The Harry and Jeanette Weinberg Foundation's Affordable Rental Housing Opportunities Initiative for Persons with Disabilities
structured_extraction.program_description: A partnership between The Harry and Jeanette Weinberg Foundation and the State of Maryland, co-administered by the Maryland Department of Disabilities (MDOD), that provides affordable rental housing options for people with disabilities. The initiative increases accessible, affordable, and independent community housing by designating units in rental housing developments specifically for very low-income people with disabilities, commonly called 'Weinberg Apartments.' Capital grants from the Foundation are used to create designated units, and tenants pay rent based on 30 percent of their income.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Capital grants totaling $7 million from The Harry and Jeanette Weinberg Foundation are available to owners of eligible rental housing developments with non-profit involvement to designate units for very low-income people with disabilities. Tenants in 'Weinberg Apartments' pay 30 percent of their income toward rent and utilities, with units serving non-elderly, disabled persons earning 10-30 percent of Area Gross Median Income (AGMI).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-elderly individuals with disabilities between the ages of 18-62 who receive SSI or SSDI and have a gross household income at 10-30 percent of Area Gross Median Income (AGMI).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Affordable rental housing — units are rented to eligible tenants at below-market rents based on 30 percent of the tenant's income.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. As of February 2020, units are available in Dorchester, Harford, Montgomery, Prince George's, Somerset, and Wicomico counties, with additional units under construction or in the pipeline in Anne Arundel, Baltimore County, Howard, and Baltimore City. More units will be added over time.
requirements_list: Must verify disability and receipt of SSI and/or SSDI income
Must be between the ages of 18 and 62
Must be disabled and receiving SSI or SSDI
Must have a gross household income at or between 10-30 percent of AGMI in the Maryland county where they wish to reside
Must not have a criminal background that includes a lifetime sex offense registry requirement
Must not have a criminal background that includes a conviction for the production of methamphetamines in federally-assisted property
Must be referred by a case manager, support planner, resource coordinator, coordinator of community service, or community health worker to complete the pre-screening and application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested applicants must be referred by their case manager, support planner, resource coordinator, coordinator of community service, or community health worker to complete the pre-screening and application. MDOD qualifies eligible households and refers potential tenants to property managers. Applicants are drawn from a waiting list as units meeting their needs become available. Waiting lists may be long; apply as soon as possible.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Universal Service Trust Fund collects surcharges from Maryland communications companies to fund telecommunications access programs for people with disabilities, including the Maryland Accessible Telecommunications (MAT) Program, the Newsline Reading Service, and the Maryland Relay Service.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Communications companies that collect the surcharge may retain 1.5% of the total surcharge collected to offset administrative expenses related to billing, collecting, and remitting the surcharge. The surcharge rate is $0.09 per month per active account for communications services billed within Maryland. Proceeds are remitted monthly to the Maryland Comptroller by the 15th of each month for the previous month's service.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland landline, wireless/cellular, and VoIP communications service providers required by state law to collect and remit a surcharge on behalf of the state.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds the operational and maintenance costs of the MAT Program, Newsline Reading Service, and Maryland Relay Service.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All active accounts billed for communications services within the State of Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a communications company providing landline, wireless/cellular, or VoIP service in Maryland
Must apply the $0.09 per month per account surcharge to all active Maryland accounts
Must label the surcharge as 'UNIVERSAL SERVICE FEE' on subscriber bills
Must remit proceeds monthly to the Maryland Comptroller by the 15th of each month for the previous month's service
Must submit the remittance form monthly regardless of whether there is a surcharge to remit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and submit the 2025–2026 remittance worksheet monthly. Mail the completed worksheet and remittance check to the Comptroller of the Treasury, P.O. Box 207, Annapolis, MD 21404-0207. The worksheet is available online at www.mdrelay.maryland.gov or upon request.

structured_extraction.program_name: iCanConnect: The National DeafBlind Equipment Distribution Program
structured_extraction.program_description: iCanConnect provides free telecommunications equipment, assessments, and training to people who are DeafBlind so they can access modern communication tools and participate fully in society. The program is managed at the state level in Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free telecommunications equipment, assessments, and training for eligible DeafBlind individuals who meet federal eligibility guidelines.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals who are DeafBlind and meet federal eligibility guidelines
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Telecommunications technology and training to enable DeafBlind individuals to communicate and interact with the world
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland; managed at the state level
requirements_list: Must be DeafBlind
Must meet federal eligibility guidelines
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit www.icanconnect.org/maryland to learn more and download an application.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Nonprofit Security Grant Program (NSGP) is a federal grant program administered by FEMA and managed in Maryland by the Maryland Department of Emergency Management (MDEM). It provides funding for physical security improvements and other security-related activities to nonprofit organizations that are at high risk of a terrorist or extremist attack. The program also works to connect nonprofit preparedness activities with broader state and local emergency preparedness efforts.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants providing up to $200,000 per location for physical security enhancements. An organization may apply for up to six locations total, with no more than three in either the Urban Area (NSGP-UA) or State (NSGP-S) funding category, and a maximum of $600,000 total per state. The FY2025 program allocates $274,500,000 nationwide. The grant operates on a reimbursement basis — organizations must spend funds first and then request reimbursement. There is no cost-share requirement for FY2025.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Application period is currently closed; program recurs annually
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations (501(c)(3)) in Maryland, including private colleges and universities, that are at high risk of terrorist or extremist attack. Organizations in Montgomery County and Prince George's County must apply through the National Capital Region via the District of Columbia.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Physical security enhancements and other security-related activities at eligible nonprofit facilities, such as equipment installation and facility hardening. Funds may also support contracted security services, planning, training, and exercises as allowed by FEMA guidelines.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Organizations in Montgomery County and Prince George's County must apply through the National Capital Region (DC). Maryland counties are divided into three funding categories: State Area, Baltimore Urban Area, and National Capital Region Urban Area.
requirements_list: Must be a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization
Must be at high risk of a terrorist or other extremist attack
Must submit an Investment Justification form
Must submit a vulnerability assessment conducted at the facility within the last two years (by a law enforcement agency or security company; houses of worship may do a self-assessment)
Must submit the organization's mission statement on letterhead
Must submit short bios and resumes for organizational leadership and board members including names and addresses
Must have or obtain a Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) through SAM.gov prior to receiving an award
Must comply with FEMA National Priority Areas including Border Crisis Response and Enforcement Support
Must declare whether the organization's work involves supporting aliens or has DEI practices
Must not include foreign nationals or noncitizens unless properly vetted
Must adopt NIMS (National Incident Management System) as applicable
Must attend mandatory Subrecipient Grant Award Briefing if awarded
Must submit quarterly status reports during the period of performance
Montgomery and Prince George's County organizations must apply through the DC National Capital Region, not MDEM
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a single email to nsgp.mdem@maryland.gov with a complete application packet as PDFs. The packet must include: (1) a completed Investment Justification form downloaded and opened from your computer, (2) a vulnerability or risk assessment of the facility conducted within the last two years, (3) the organization's mission statement on letterhead, and (4) short bios and resumes for organizational leadership and board members. Do not submit applications directly to FEMA or grants.gov — MDEM is the State Administrative Agency and handles all submissions to FEMA.

structured_extraction.program_name: ACCESS Harm Reduction Grants (Advancing Cross-Cutting Engagement and Service Strategies for People Who Use Drugs)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Health Behavioral Health Administration Office of Harm Reduction (OHR) awards grants to nonprofits and Local Health Departments to support local harm reduction programs statewide. ACCESS stands for 'Advancing Cross-Cutting Engagement and Service Strategies for People Who Use Drugs.' The grants aim to reduce substance-related illness and death by optimizing services for people who use drugs, including ensuring access to naloxone. OHR currently funds 50 organizations — 28 nonprofits and 22 Local Health Departments — to conduct harm reduction activities statewide.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding is provided to nonprofits and Local Health Departments (currently 50 organizations total — 28 nonprofits and 22 Local Health Departments) to conduct harm reduction activities, including naloxone distribution and services for people who use drugs, aimed at reducing substance-related illness and death.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications for new funding are closed at this time.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations and Local Health Departments that provide or implement harm reduction programs for people who use drugs in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Implementing harm reduction programs including naloxone distribution and other activities to reduce substance-related morbidity and mortality among people who use drugs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — available to organizations operating across Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a nonprofit organization or a Local Health Department
Must conduct harm reduction activities for people who use drugs
Must conduct activities aligned with OHR strategic goals for harm reduction
