structured_extraction.program_description: The Governor's Transitioning Youth Initiative (GTYI) provides funding for supported employment and other day services to eligible students with developmental disabilities who are leaving the school system. It creates a special eligibility category within the Maryland Developmental Disabilities Administration (DDA) that allows qualifying youth turning 21 or graduating from high school to access adult services without being placed on a lengthy waiting list. The initiative is a collaboration between Maryland's Developmental Disabilities Administration (DDA) and Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS). Services are coordinated through a Coordinator of Community Services (CCS) agency, which develops a person-centered plan based on the individual's goals and support needs, regardless of severity of need. Available supports include adult vocational training, day habilitation, supported employment services, career discovery and exploration, and skills training aligned with Employment First principles prioritizing community employment. There are no fees.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The initiative earmarks funds in the DDA budget to cover supported employment and other day services for eligible students leaving school, funded through federal waiver programs (Community Pathways, Family Supports, Community Supports). Services are provided through person-centered planning and coordinated case management, regardless of severity of need. A Coordinator of Community Services (CCS) agency is assigned to provide targeted case management and develop a person-centered plan based on the individual's goals and support needs. Available supports include adult vocational training, day habilitation, supported employment services, career discovery, exploration, skills training, and planning assistance aligned with Employment First principles prioritizing community-based employment. There are no fees.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Beryl Parker (Central MD); Jim Sullivan (Eastern Shore); Nicole Sheppard (Southern MD); Brenda Sperow (Western MD)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals ages 21 through 22 with developmental disabilities who are transitioning out of the public school system after receiving special education services, and their families. Youth should make contact at age 14 to begin transition planning.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supported employment services, adult vocational training, day habilitation, career discovery and exploration, skills training, and other day services for eligible students transitioning out of school. Services are aligned with Employment First principles prioritizing community-based employment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland through four regional offices: Central Maryland (Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Harford, Howard), Eastern Shore (Caroline, Cecil, Dorchester, Kent, Queen Anne's, Somerset, Talbot, Wicomico, Worcester), Southern Maryland (Calvert, Charles, Montgomery, Prince George's, St. Mary's), and Western Maryland (Allegany, Carroll, Frederick, Garrett, Washington).
requirements_list: Must be found fully eligible as developmentally disabled under DDA criteria
Must have a severe chronic disability attributable to a physical or mental impairment (other than sole diagnosis of mental illness), or combination of mental and physical impairments
Disability must be manifested before age 22
Disability is likely to continue indefinitely
Disability results in inability to live independently without external support or continuing and regular assistance
Reflects the need for a combination and sequence of special, interdisciplinary, or generic care, treatment, or other services that are individually planned and coordinated
Must be between 21st and 22nd birthday to join DDA services under the Transitioning Youth category; if graduation is after 21st birthday, eligible for one year after date of graduation
Must be a student with a developmental disability preparing to graduate from the school system at age 21
Application must be submitted by June 30 of the eligibility year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply for DDA services through the DDA eligibility process. Coordinators of Community Services (CCS) assist with accessing services. Once found eligible, a CCS agency is assigned to provide targeted case management and develop a person-centered plan. Applications must be submitted by June 30 of the eligibility year. For more information, visit https://health.maryland.gov/dda/Pages/TY.aspx or contact the appropriate regional DDA office.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Health Equity Resource Communities (HERC) program provides grant funding and state resources to local communities across Maryland to address health disparities, improve health outcomes, expand access to primary care and prevention services, and help reduce health care costs. Five awards went to Pathways grantees expanding pilot program work. Free clinical and social services are provided, including transportation, food assistance, housing support, and more — no one will be turned away.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Healthiest Maryland Businesses (HMB) program is a collaborative network of Maryland businesses and employers with a shared mission to build and promote a culture of health in the workplace. Three recognition levels are offered: Wellness Exemplar, Wellness Pacesetter, and Wellness Standout. Businesses in good standing may display the HMB logo on their website, email signatures, or in their workplace to show their commitment to employee wellbeing.

structured_extraction.program_name: Home & Community Based Options Waiver Program (Community Options Waiver)
structured_extraction.program_description: A Medicaid waiver program that enables adults 18 and older whose care needs meet the requirements for nursing home placement to remain in a community setting rather than a long-term care facility. Medicaid-covered services that would normally only be available in nursing facilities can instead be provided in a person's own home or in an assisted living facility. Services include support planning, personal care, respite care, medical adult day care, home-delivered meals, environmental assessments and adaptations, personal emergency response systems, assistive devices, behavior consultations, nutritional consultations, and home accessibility modifications. The program also includes nurse monitoring, assistive technology, and transition services. It may also include Community First Choice services and eligibility for other Medicaid services such as prescription assistance, family and consumer training, and senior center plus services. Additional covered services include assisted living (excluding room and board), case management, dietitian and nutritionist services, and all other standard Medicaid services. Qualified individuals must meet medical, technical, and financial eligibility criteria. A statewide registry is managed by the Maryland Department of Health; individuals in nursing facilities should contact their social worker, while community-based individuals may contact Maryland Access Point (MAP) to be screened and added to the registry. The program is available statewide, including in Cecil County where residents may contact the Cecil County Aging & Disability Services office for local assistance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The State pays for covered Medicaid services to help eligible clients remain in the community through a federal Medicaid waiver. Financial assistance covers community-based care including assisted living (excluding room and board) or in-home care services. Specific services include support planning, personal care, respite care, medical adult day care, home-delivered meals, environmental assessments and adaptations, personal emergency response systems, assistive devices, behavior consultations, nutritional/dietitian services, home accessibility modifications, case management, nurse monitoring, assistive technology, family and consumer training, senior center plus services, medical equipment, Community First Choice services, and help with transitional costs. The program may also provide eligibility for other Medicaid services such as prescription assistance. These services are provided in participants' own homes or in assisted living facilities rather than nursing facilities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents age 18 and older whose advanced age or disability would warrant long-term care facility placement but who wish to remain in the community, and who meet Medicaid's long-term care admission criteria (medically, technically, and financially eligible). Includes older adults and individuals with physical disabilities at risk of requiring nursing home level of care.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home and community-based services including support planning, personal care, respite care, medical adult day care, home-delivered meals, environmental adaptations, personal emergency response systems, assistive devices, behavior and nutritional/dietitian consultations, home accessibility modifications, nurse monitoring, assistive technology, assisted living (excluding room and board), case management, family and consumer training, senior center plus services, medical equipment, Community First Choice services, and transitional costs — enabling eligible adults to live in their own homes or assisted living facilities instead of nursing facilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to eligible Maryland residents statewide, including residents of Anne Arundel County, Calvert County, Cecil County, Charles County, Frederick County, and St. Mary's County. Statewide registry managed by Maryland Department of Health.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Hospital Preparedness Program (HPP) supports hospitals and health care systems so they can provide effective care and save lives during emergencies and disasters that exceed normal day-to-day capacity. The Maryland Department of Health receives federal funding each year and awards it as grants to health care system partners across the state, including hospitals, free-standing emergency departments, community health centers, state-managed facilities, poison control centers, emergency medical services agencies, home care and hospice agencies, and regional health care preparedness coalitions. Funded partners use these funds to prepare for, respond to, and recover from disasters and other public health emergencies that threaten community health and safety. Maryland is divided into four HPP-funded regional coalitions covering all 23 counties and Baltimore City: Western Maryland (Garrett, Allegany, Washington, Frederick), Central Maryland (Anne Arundel, Baltimore County, Carroll, Harford, Howard, Baltimore City), the Eastern Shore (Caroline, Cecil, Dorchester, Kent, Queen Anne's, Somerset, Talbot, Wicomico, Worcester), and Southern Maryland/National Capital Region (Calvert, Charles, Montgomery, Prince George's, St. Mary's).

structured_extraction.program_name: Increasing Access to Integrated Behavioral Health Services (CHRC Grants)

structured_extraction.program_name: Low Intensity Support Services (LISS) Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The LISS Program provides up to $1,000 in grant funding to children living at home with their family and adults with developmental and/or intellectual disabilities living independently in the community who are not currently receiving support services from the Developmental Disabilities Administration (DDA), as well as those on the DDA waiting list. The program helps eligible individuals purchase services and items that improve quality of life, promote independence, and support community integration across their lifespan. Approved services and items include adaptive items, assistive technology, attendant/personal care, childcare, community integration and recreational services, educational services, home modification/barrier removal, identification services, respite care, summer camps and therapeutic programs, transportation, and wellness services. Funding is distributed by random selection among eligible applicants each fiscal year round. Funds are administered through two regional LISS Program Providers: Maryland Community Connection and Penn-Mar Human Services, which cover different counties across Maryland. If selected, recipients must provide documentation verifying identity, disability, residency, and an identified eligible service or item delivered by an eligible vendor, and must also complete a Services Eligibility Application.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides up to $1,000 per eligible individual (decreased from $2,000 due to budget constraints) to purchase approved services and/or items including adaptive items, assistive technology, attendant/personal care, childcare, community integration and recreational services, educational services, home modification/barrier removal, identification services, respite care, summer camps and therapeutic programs, transportation, and wellness services that address their needs, enhance quality of life, promote independence, and support community integration. Funding is awarded through a random selection process conducted each fiscal year round and is not an entitlement. If selected, the recipient must provide documentation verifying identity, disability, residency, and the eligible service or item from an eligible vendor. The program is administered through two regional providers: Maryland Community Connection (serving Calvert, Charles, Montgomery, Prince George's, St. Mary's, Caroline, Cecil, Dorchester, Kent, Queen Anne's, Somerset, Talbot, Wicomico, and Worcester counties) and Penn-Mar Human Services (serving Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Carroll, Frederick, Garrett, Harford, Howard, and Washington counties).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: FY 2026 Round 1: application window open July 14, 2025 – September 15, 2025; random selection September 30, 2025
structured_extraction.contact_name: Maryland Department of Health, Developmental Disabilities Administration (DDA)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Children living at home with their family and adults with developmental and/or intellectual disabilities living in their own home in the community who are not currently receiving any DDA support services, as well as those on the DDA waiting list. Applicants must have an eligible developmental disability diagnosis and need low-intensity supports not covered by other funding sources.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Adaptive items, assistive technology, attendant/personal care, childcare, community integration and recreational services, educational services and items, home modification and barrier removal, identification services, respite care, summer camps and therapeutic summer programs, transportation, and wellness services and medical/therapeutic items to address the individual's needs, enhance quality of life, promote independence, and support community integration, as listed on the LISS website and delivered by an eligible vendor. Funds cannot be used for experimental treatments, cash, gift cards, housing assistance, vehicles, vacations, toys (unless therapeutic), or items purchased with cash/gift cards.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland through two program providers: Maryland Community Connection (serving Calvert, Charles, Montgomery, Prince George's, St. Mary's, Caroline, Cecil, Dorchester, Kent, Queen Anne's, Somerset, Talbot, Wicomico, and Worcester counties) and Penn-Mar Human Services (serving Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Carroll, Frederick, Garrett, Harford, Howard, and Washington counties). Applicants must be Maryland residents. Proof of residency required (utility bill, lease, mortgage statement, or two alternative documents dated within last 12 months).
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident
Must have a developmental and/or intellectual disability (eligible developmental disability diagnosis)
Must not be currently receiving any support services from the DDA (or must be on the DDA waiting list)
Children must be living at home with their family; adults must be living in their own home in the community
Must identify an eligible service or item from an eligible vendor
Application must be submitted online during an open Round window
Children under 21 without a court-ordered legal guardian require a natural or adoptive parent to complete the application using the child's demographic information
Individuals with a court-ordered legal guardian must have the legal guardian complete the application using the individual's demographic information

Individuals over 21 without a legal guardian may receive assistance completing the application but must use their own demographic information; if only needing physical assistance, a parent, relative, friend, or case manager may help under the individual's direction
Applicant's own demographic information (not parent/guardian) must be entered on the application
Funding distributed based on random selection among eligible applicants; funding is not an entitlement
Must meet eligibility requirements set by DDA
If selected, must provide documentation verifying identity, disability, residency, and the eligible service or item
If selected, a Services Eligibility Application must also be completed
If selected, must provide proof of payment (bank/credit card statement or canceled check)
If selected, must complete W-9 for account owner
Proof of identity required (Social Security card, birth certificate, passport, green card, military ID, or Maryland driver's license)
Proof of Maryland residency required (utility bill, lease, mortgage statement, or alternative documents dated within last 12 months)
Proof of developmental disability required (medical letter, approved IEP, or DDA eligibility determination letter)
Documentation of home ownership required for home modification requests
Quotes/invoices with state license numbers required for applicable services
W-9 forms required for service providers/vendors
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the online Random Selection Application during an open Round window using the access link found on the DDA website under Resources. The link is only open during each Round's submission window. Enter the demographic information of the child or adult applicant (not the parent/guardian). Upon submission, a confirmation email with a confirmation number will be sent. After the random selection date (September 30, 2025 for FY 2026), the LISS Program Provider will notify applicants by letter within 20 business days. If selected, a representative of the LISS agency serving the applicant's county will contact the applicant to assist with the LISS process, and a Services Eligibility Application must also be completed along with required documentation for the specific service or item. If unable to apply online, contact the LISS Program Provider for assistance. Visit the DDA website or review the current LISS Applicant and Reference Guide for full application details.

The program uses evidence-based practices from existing programs including Healthy Families and Helping Families Recover.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant award of $275,000 to Harford County Health Department to support the MEGAN Place project, using evidence-based practices from existing programs including Healthy Families and Helping Families Recover.
structured_extraction.program_audience: At-risk pregnant and postpartum women and their families, particularly those with substance use disorders in Harford County; administered through the Harford County Health Department
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Program operations to provide a supportive perinatal health and family resiliency center, including services to support at-risk pregnant and postpartum women
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Harford County, Maryland

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide initiative launched by Governor Wes Moore and the Maryland Department of Health to expand immunization access for uninsured and underinsured adults aged 19 and older. The program provides free recommended vaccines at no cost to eligible adults through local health departments across Maryland, funded by $2.8 million allocated in partnership with the Maryland General Assembly. The program aims to reduce barriers and help prevent the spread of vaccine-preventable diseases such as COVID-19, influenza, measles, pneumonia, RSV, and shingles. 'Underinsured' means health insurance does not cover recommended vaccines, or the person has high deductibles that create a financial burden.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free recommended vaccines provided to eligible adults at local health departments across Maryland, funded by $2.8 million allocated in partnership with the Maryland General Assembly. All vaccines are provided at no cost to eligible uninsured and underinsured adults age 19 and older. No one will be turned away due to inability to pay. Currently available in Baltimore County, Garrett, Montgomery, and Somerset counties, with expansion to other counties planned. Local access is also available at the Queen Anne's County Health Department, 206 N. Commerce St., Centreville, MD 21617 (call 410-758-0720 to schedule an appointment).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Uninsured and underinsured adults age 19 and older in Maryland. 'Underinsured' means health insurance does not cover recommended vaccines, or the person has high deductibles that create a financial burden.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free vaccines for eligible uninsured and underinsured adults to protect against and prevent vaccine-preventable diseases, including COVID-19, influenza, measles, pneumonia, RSV, and shingles.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide initiative available across all of Maryland. Currently available in Baltimore County, Garrett, Montgomery, and Somerset counties, with availability expanding to other counties. Local access point also at the Queen Anne's County Health Department, 206 N. Commerce St., Centreville, MD 21617.
requirements_list: Must be age 19 or older
Must be uninsured or underinsured
Underinsured means health insurance does not cover recommended vaccines, or you have high deductibles creating a financial burden
Appointment required at some locations (call 410-758-0720 for Queen Anne's County Health Department)
You may be asked to confirm your insurance status
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local health department to check vaccine availability, or visit health.maryland.gov for more information. To schedule an appointment at the Queen Anne's County Health Department, call 410-758-0720. You may be asked to confirm your insurance status.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Breast and Cervical Cancer Program (BCCP) on the Eastern Shore
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides free breast and cervical cancer screenings to eligible women on Maryland's Eastern Shore who face financial barriers to care. The program removes financial barriers to early cancer detection by offering no-cost clinical breast exams, mammograms, Pap tests, HPV tests, and follow-up testing and support through local doctors, clinics, and hospitals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: No-cost breast and cervical cancer screenings including clinical breast exams, mammograms, Pap tests, HPV tests, and follow-up testing and support, provided through local doctors, clinics, and hospitals.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Women ages 40–64 (or over 65 without Medicare Part B) with limited income and no or insufficient health insurance coverage, living in Eastern Shore Maryland counties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: No-cost breast and cervical cancer screenings: clinical breast exams, mammograms, Pap tests, HPV tests, and follow-up care and testing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only to residents of Eastern Shore Maryland counties: Kent, Queen Anne's, Cecil, Caroline, Dorchester, Talbot, Wicomico, Somerset, and Worcester.
requirements_list: Must live in a Maryland Eastern Shore county
Must be between ages 40 and 64, or over 65 without Medicare Part B
Must have a limited income
Must have no health insurance or insurance that does not fully cover breast exams, mammograms, or Pap/HPV tests
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the local program office serving your county by phone. Upper Shore (Kent, Queen Anne's, Cecil): 410-778-7970. Mid-Shore (Caroline, Dorchester, Talbot): 410-479-8080. Lower Shore (Wicomico, Somerset, Worcester): 410-548-5175.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Breast and Cervical Cancer Screening Program (BCCP)
structured_extraction.program_description: Funded by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and the Maryland Cigarette Restitution Fund, this program provides free or low-cost breast and cervical cancer screening, diagnostic services, and patient navigation to eligible women across Maryland who are uninsured, underinsured, or have limited income. The program also provides grants to local health departments, health systems, and hospitals to offer no-cost education, screening, diagnosis, and treatment services for breast and cervical cancer. It connects eligible residents to needed care, follow-up, and treatment, while supporting the local organizations that deliver these services. At the local level, the program offers free or low-cost mammograms, Pap tests, and pelvic exams to eligible women with limited or no health insurance. Grant funds may also support outreach, community health outreach workers, and contracts with private physicians, radiologists, surgeons, and medical laboratories.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: For eligible individuals: covers breast and cervical cancer screening and diagnostic services including clinical breast exams, mammograms, breast ultrasound, surgical consultations, breast biopsies, Pap tests, HPV tests, pelvic exams, colposcopies, and cervical biopsies. Also provides patient navigation services such as appointment scheduling and follow-up, finding transportation, interpretation services, and linkage to treatment. For eligible organizations: project grants are administered to local health departments, health systems, and hospitals to provide education and no-cost cancer screening, diagnosis, and treatment services to eligible residents. Funds can also support outreach, community health outreach workers, and contracts with private physicians, radiologists, surgeons, and medical laboratories.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Center for Cancer Prevention and Control
structured_extraction.program_audience: Women in Maryland ages 18–64 (or 65+ without Medicare Part B) with limited income at or below 250% of the Federal Poverty Level who are uninsured, underinsured, or need help accessing cancer screening services; as well as local health departments, health systems, and hospitals serving low-income, uninsured, and underinsured Maryland residents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Breast and cervical cancer education, screening (including mammograms, Pap tests, and pelvic exams), diagnostic testing, patient navigation services, outreach, and treatment for eligible residents. Grant funds may also support hiring community health outreach workers and contracting with private physicians, radiologists, surgeons, and medical laboratories.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Individuals must live in Maryland. Local delivery available in all counties including Howard County.

Age 65 or older without Medicare Part B

No health insurance, or health insurance that does not fully cover needed services, or insured but needing help getting screened or receiving follow-up testing

Serves low-income, uninsured, or underinsured Maryland residents (for organizational applicants)

Organizations: Contact the Center for Cancer Prevention and Control at [email protected] or 410-767-5281 for information on participation.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Center for Global Migration and Immigrant Health (CGMIH)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Center for Global Migration and Immigrant Health coordinates and provides culturally-informed, language-accessible public health services for newly arrived humanitarian immigrants (including refugees, asylees, humanitarian parolees, Cuban/Haitian Entrants, Special Immigrant Visa holders, and Victims of Trafficking) and agricultural/seasonal migrant workers in Maryland. The Center partners with Federally-Qualified Health Centers, local health departments, healthcare providers, and community organizations to ensure these populations receive comprehensive health assessments, follow-up care, care coordination, referrals, immunizations, and community-based health education. It also provides technical assistance, resources, training, and culturally appropriate, language-accessible educational materials to healthcare providers and community organizations serving limited English proficient populations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides comprehensive health assessments, follow-up care, care coordination, referrals, and health education for humanitarian immigrants and migrant/seasonal agricultural workers. Also offers technical assistance, resources, and training to healthcare providers and community organizations working with these populations. Develops and distributes culturally appropriate, language-accessible educational materials for limited English proficient populations. May also provide project grants to eligible organizations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Federally-Qualified Health Centers, local health departments, healthcare providers, community-based organizations, and newly arrived humanitarian immigrants (refugees, asylees, humanitarian parolees, Cuban/Haitian Entrants, Special Immigrant Visa holders, Victims of Trafficking) and agricultural/seasonal migrant workers in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Health assessments, follow-up care, care coordination, referrals, immunizations, community health education, technical assistance, training, and development of culturally and linguistically appropriate educational materials for immigrant and migrant worker populations. Also includes connecting immigrants to culturally-informed healthcare and providing education about the U.S. healthcare system.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must serve or be a newly arrived ORR-eligible humanitarian immigrant (refugee, asylee, humanitarian parolee, Cuban/Haitian Entrant, Special Immigrant Visa holder, or Victim of Trafficking) or an agricultural/seasonal migrant worker in Maryland
Must be a Federally Qualified Health Center, health provider, local health department, community-based organization, or an eligible individual immigrant/migrant worker
Organizations must work with these immigrant or migrant worker populations
Eligible populations include refugees, asylees, humanitarian parolees, Cuban-Haitian Entrants (CHEs), Special Immigrant Visa (SIV) holders, and Victims of Trafficking (VoTs)
Eligible organization types include county government, non-profit, and state government
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: No formal application process is described on the program page. Organizations or individuals seeking technical assistance, training, or services should contact the Center directly. Grant opportunities are available on an annual basis.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Certified Community Health Worker (CCHW) Certificate Renewal
structured_extraction.program_description: This program allows Maryland Certified Community Health Workers (CCHWs) to renew their professional certification every two years at no cost. Renewal requires completing 20 hours of professional development activities (such as courses, webinars, conferences, workshops, trainings, lectures, or readings) and submitting a renewal application through the Maryland OneStop portal. Applications can be submitted up to 120 days before expiration or up to two years after expiration. The Department reviews applications within 30 calendar days for completeness and makes a final determination within 1–90 calendar days. There is no renewal fee. A renewal webinar is offered periodically to guide applicants through the process. Spanish-language resources are also available.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free certificate renewal for Certified Community Health Workers. Certificates are valid for two years and authorize individuals to represent themselves publicly as a Certified Community Health Worker (CCHW). Renewal requires completing 20 hours of professional development activities (courses, webinars, conferences, workshops, trainings, lectures, or readings) and submitting a renewal application through the Maryland OneStop portal or via paper application. Professional development activities must include: activity title, date, hours, sponsor, location, written explanation of acquired knowledge/skill application, and the associated CHW core competency or health principle. Only educational/instructional hours count (exclude travel, breaks, meals, networking, social media time). Applications can be submitted up to 120 days before and up to two years after the certificate expiration date. The Department reviews applications within 30 calendar days for completeness and makes a final determination within 1–90 calendar days. There is no renewal fee. If more than 2 years have passed since expiration, the individual must reapply as a new applicant meeting original certification requirements.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling — applications accepted up to 120 days before and up to two years after certificate expiration date; recommended to submit at least 30 days before expiration
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland Certified Community Health Workers (CCHWs) seeking to renew their professional certificate, including those whose certificates have expired or are approaching expiration. Also relevant to CHW supervisors, trainers, and health and social service agencies.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Certificate renewal and maintaining active CCHW certification in Maryland; professional development activities required for renewal (training, seminars, workshops, conferences). No funding is disbursed — this is a professional certification renewal program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Certified Community Health Workers throughout Maryland statewide, including Maryland residents and professionals working as CHWs in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a current or recently expired Maryland Certified Community Health Worker (CCHW)

Complete 20 hours of professional development activities (e.g., courses, webinars, conferences, workshops, trainings, lectures, readings, employer-sponsored trainings, Maryland CHW Association meetings, community meetings/committees with educational components)
Only instructional/educational hours count toward the 20-hour requirement (exclude travel time, breaks, meals, networking, social media time, and non-educational components)
Document each activity with: title, date, hours, sponsor, location, a written explanation of knowledge/skills gained, and the CHW core competency or health principle associated with the activity

Activities must be associated with at least one of Maryland's nine CHW Core Competencies (advocacy/community capacity building, communication, cultural competency, ethics/confidentiality, local resource knowledge, care coordination support, health behavior change teaching, outreach methods, public health concepts) or a health principle
Submit a Certificate Renewal Application through the Maryland OneStop portal or request a paper application
Apply no earlier than 120 days before and no later than two years after the certificate expiration date; it is recommended to submit at least 30 days before expiration
If more than 2 years past expiration, must reapply as a new applicant meeting original certification requirements
Notify the Department of any name or contact information changes
Personal report/attestation required
All required fields for each professional development activity must be completed for activity acceptance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the Certificate Renewal Application online through the Maryland OneStop portal at https://onestop.md.gov. Enter professional development activities directly into the application and upload required documents, or upload a completed Professional Development Activities Tracking Sheet. The application remains in Draft mode until submitted. Alternatively, contact the CHW Team at 410-767-5971 or MDH.CHWApplications@maryland.gov to request a paper application. A Professional Development Activities Tracking Sheet is available to help document activities before submission. Use Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, or Safari for best results. MDH sends renewal notifications at least 90 days before expiration. Processing takes up to 90 calendar days after submission. A renewal webinar is offered periodically in both English and Spanish to guide applicants through the process.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Children's Health Insurance Program (MCHP) uses federal and state funds to provide free or low-cost health insurance coverage to eligible uninsured children in Maryland and other qualifying individuals. The program covers children under age 19 whose family income is too high for Medicaid but too low to afford private health insurance, pregnant women of any age, families with children under age 21, and childless adults up to age 64 who meet income guidelines. Full health benefits include doctor visits, hospitalizations, lab work, vaccines, prescriptions, dental care (free for children, pregnant women, and adults enrolled in Medicaid or MCHP), vision care, mental health services, substance abuse treatment, and transportation to medical care. Coverage is delivered through one of Maryland's nine HealthChoice Managed Care Organizations (MCOs) or a Qualified Health Plan via Maryland Medicaid or the Maryland Health Connection. Children of employed parents whose employer does not offer family health insurance may also qualify, even if the family has some existing coverage. Income must be at or below 200% of the federal poverty level (or up to 300% with a premium). Local case workers at county health departments and local departments of social services help residents determine eligibility, understand MCO options, and enroll in coverage. The program is available statewide, including local enrollment support in Howard County, Montgomery County, and Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free or low-cost health insurance coverage through Medicaid and MCHP, including full health benefits such as doctor visits, check-ups, immunizations, hospitalizations, lab work/X-ray services, vaccines, prescriptions, urgent care, emergency services, prenatal/postpartum care, family planning, home health, dental care (free for children, pregnant women, and adults enrolled in Medicaid or MCHP), vision care and glasses (children under 21), behavioral health services, substance abuse treatment, and transportation to medical care. No fees or payments required for eligible children. Coverage is delivered through one of Maryland's HealthChoice Managed Care Organizations (MCOs) or a Qualified Health Plan. Income must be at or below 200% of the federal poverty level (or up to 300% with a premium). Applications can be completed online, by phone, or in person at a local health department or department of social services.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Apply any time — no deadline, applications accepted on a rolling basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low- to average-income uninsured children under age 19, pregnant women of any age, families with children under age 21, and childless adults up to age 64 who meet income and eligibility requirements. Primarily targets uninsured children whose family income is too high for Medicaid but too low to afford private health insurance. Available statewide, with local enrollment support including in Howard County, Montgomery County, and Prince George's County through local health departments and DHHS offices.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Medical insurance and full health care coverage including doctor visits, check-ups, immunizations, hospitalizations, lab work, X-ray services, vaccines, prescriptions, urgent care, emergency services, prenatal/postpartum care, family planning, home health, dental care, vision care and glasses (children under 21), behavioral health services, substance abuse treatment, and transportation to medical care for children, pregnant women, families, and qualifying adults.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must live in Maryland. Available statewide. MCO service areas vary by county; eligible counties include Baltimore City, Anne Arundel, Baltimore, Calvert, Caroline, Carroll, Cecil, Charles, Dorchester, Frederick, Harford, Howard, Kent, Montgomery, Prince George's, Queen Anne's, Somerset, St. Mary's, Talbot, Washington, Wicomico, and Worcester counties. Local enrollment assistance is available through county health departments and local departments of social services. Howard County residents may visit the Howard County Health Department for local enrollment assistance. Montgomery County residents may apply at Office of Eligibility and Support Services locations in Silver Spring, Rockville, or Germantown, or call 240-777-0311. Prince George's County residents may visit the Prince George's County Health Department at 9187 Central Avenue, Suite 254, Capitol Heights, MD 20743 (no appointment necessary; Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m.).
requirements_list: Must live in Maryland
Must be a child under age 19, pregnant woman of any age, family with children under age 21, or childless adult up to age 64
Must be uninsured or lack access to employer-sponsored family health insurance
Child must not have other health coverage
Must meet income eligibility guidelines (countable income at or below 200% of the federal poverty level, or up to 300% with a premium)
Children must not be eligible for Medicaid
Children of employed parents whose employer does not offer family health insurance may also qualify
Must be a U.S. Citizen or qualified non-citizen
Must provide government-issued photo ID
Must provide most recent income documents from all sources
Must provide citizenship documents (passport, birth certificate, or naturalization certificate)
Must provide immigration documents if applicable (I-94 form, work authorization, or permanent resident card)
Must provide or apply for a Social Security number
Must meet household income limits
Family income must meet the program's income limit for household size
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply at any time online at https://www.marylandhealthconnection.gov/, by phone at (855) 642-8572 or TTY (855) 642-8573, or in person at a local health department or local department of social services. Provide general family information (names, birth dates, social security numbers), proof of income, citizenship or immigration documents, government-issued photo ID, and Social Security card. If pregnant, provide expected delivery date signed by a doctor or nurse. Montgomery County residents may apply in person at one of four Office of Eligibility and Support Services locations in Silver Spring, Rockville, or Germantown; processing takes approximately 10 days, after which families select a HealthChoice MCO and primary care doctor. Prince George's County residents may also visit the Prince George's County Health Department in person at 9187 Central Avenue, Suite 254, Capitol Heights, MD 20743 (no appointment necessary; Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m.) where case workers will help determine eligibility, explain MCO options, and assist with enrollment. Howard County residents may contact the Howard County Health Department for local enrollment assistance.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Climate Change Health Adaptation Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program is part of Maryland's statewide strategy to reduce public health vulnerability to climate change. It provides tools, resources, and technical assistance to help citizens, communities, non-governmental organizations, schools, local governments, planners, and state agencies incorporate health considerations and health data into their climate change plans.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Developing climate change plans that incorporate health data and health considerations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — available to Marylanders and Maryland organizations.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Colorectal cancer screening and control activities.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Community Health Resources Commission (CHRC) Grants – Baltimore City Grantees
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Community Health Resources Commission awards grants to organizations in Baltimore City and surrounding areas to address health disparities, expand access to primary care, behavioral health, dental services, food security, infant mortality reduction, and other community health needs. The program supports nonprofits, health systems, hospitals, health departments, academic institutions, and community-based organizations serving low-income, uninsured, underinsured, and otherwise underserved populations. The page lists past and current grantees with their grant amounts and project descriptions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging from approximately $20,570 to $2,400,000 awarded to health care organizations, nonprofits, hospitals, health departments, and academic institutions to expand community health services and reduce health disparities in Baltimore City and surrounding counties. Funds support staff salaries, clinical services, equipment, health education, care coordination, community health worker programs, outreach, and other direct health service delivery costs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations, health care providers, hospitals, health departments, academic institutions, and community-based organizations serving low-income, uninsured, underinsured, or otherwise underserved populations in Baltimore City and surrounding areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Staff salaries, clinical services, equipment, health education, care coordination, community health worker programs, outreach, and other program costs to expand health care access and reduce health disparities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Primarily Baltimore City; some grants also extend to Baltimore County, Howard County, Anne Arundel County, Harford County, Carroll County, and Wicomico County.
requirements_list: Must serve low-income, uninsured, underinsured, or otherwise underserved populations
Must address health disparities or safety net capacity needs in underserved populations
Must provide direct health services or expand access to care
Grantee organizations include nonprofits, health systems, health departments, and academic institutions
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations apply to the Maryland Community Health Resources Commission for grant funding. Specific application rounds and processes are managed by the Commission. The grantee listing page shows past and current grantees and their project descriptions; detailed application instructions are available through the Commission directly.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Community Health Resources Commission Grant 08-004 – Dental Program Expansion at Choptank (Caroline County / Goldsboro)
structured_extraction.program_description: This three-year grant supported the expansion of Choptank Community Health System's dental program, including the construction and enhancement of a new seven-chair dental facility in Goldsboro, Maryland. The facility provided care to 6,374 patients over the grant period, serving underserved rural communities in Caroline County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Three-year grant of $300,000 (Grant 08-004) awarded to Choptank Community Health System to expand and enhance a seven-chair dental facility in Goldsboro, Maryland, increasing dental care capacity for underserved rural patients in Caroline County.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community health organizations expanding dental care capacity in underserved rural areas of Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction and enhancement of a dental facility, including infrastructure and equipment for a seven-chair dental clinic; expansion of dental care services
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Caroline County, Maryland (Goldsboro)

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Community Health Resources Commission Grant 08-010 – Electronic Health Record Deployment at Choptank Community Health System (Caroline County)
structured_extraction.program_description: This two-year grant supported Choptank Community Health System's deployment of an electronic health record (EHR) system across all its health center sites and locations, including planning, testing, infrastructure development, software acquisition, and staff IT training. The grant was awarded under the Maryland Community Health Resources Commission to improve health information technology capabilities at community health centers in Caroline County.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Electronic health record software, IT infrastructure development, planning and testing, and staff IT training across all health center sites
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Caroline County, Maryland

structured_extraction.program_description: A two-year grant that supported the operations of a school-based health center in Dorchester County. Funds were used to pay staff salaries and to support administrative work aimed at improving billing and maximizing reimbursement to make the program more sustainable. The grantee, the Dorchester Health Department, served more than 860 students and provided more than 2,700 clinical and mental health services over the grant period.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A two-year grant totaling $220,000 (grant number 09-005) awarded to the Dorchester Health Department to support a school-based health center, covering staff salaries and administrative costs to improve billing and reimbursement sustainability.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local health departments operating school-based health centers in Dorchester County, Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Staff salaries at the school-based health center and administrative support to improve billing practices and maximize reimbursement for long-term program sustainability.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Dorchester County, Maryland

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Community Health Resources Commission Grant 18-001 – Pediatric Dental Access Expansion in Rural Caroline County
structured_extraction.program_description: This grant addresses dental workforce shortages in rural Caroline and Dorchester counties by expanding access to pediatric dental services through a new dental practice in Denton and a partnership with the University of Maryland School of Dentistry to recruit a dental fellow to provide pediatric dental care at existing clinics including locations in Denton, Federalsburg, Goldsboro, and Cambridge. The grant was awarded to Choptank Community Health System.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant award of $240,000 (Grant 18-001) awarded to Choptank Community Health System to expand pediatric dental services in rural Caroline and Dorchester counties through a dental fellowship program in partnership with the University of Maryland School of Dentistry.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community health organizations addressing pediatric dental care shortages in rural Maryland, particularly those serving underserved communities with dental workforce shortages
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Recruitment of a dental fellow to provide pediatric dental services; expansion of pediatric dental clinic capacity in Denton, Federalsburg, Goldsboro, and Cambridge

Must partner with a dental education institution to recruit a dental fellow

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Community Health Resources Commission Grant 20-011 – Behavioral Health Integration at Choptank Denton
structured_extraction.program_description: This grant funds the start of mental health and substance use disorder (SUD) treatment services for vulnerable adults and children at the Choptank Community Health System dental practice in Denton, Caroline County. It supports integrating behavioral health care on-site with existing somatic and dental services, including medication-assisted treatment (MAT) for SUD, rather than relying on contracted outside providers. The program targets underserved populations in Caroline County.

structured_extraction.program_description: A professional certification program administered by the Maryland Department of Health for Community Health Workers (CHWs) who have completed an accredited CHW training program. The certification is valid for two years from the date of issue and is free to obtain and renew at no cost. The program is available statewide and applications can be submitted in English or Spanish. Applicants must be at least 18 years old, hold a high school diploma or GED equivalent, and provide official documentation of completing a Maryland Department of Health-accredited CHW training program. Applications are processed through the Maryland OneStop portal, and a determination is made within 1–90 calendar days of submitting a complete application.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A free two-year professional certification issued to qualifying Community Health Workers, valid from the date of issue, with no fee charged for initial certification or renewal. Applicants submit through the Maryland OneStop portal (onestop.md.gov) or may request a paper application in English or Spanish by contacting the CHW Team. Applications take approximately 30–60 minutes to complete. Applications are reviewed within 30 calendar days for completeness and a determination is made within 1–90 calendar days of submitting a complete application. The certification confirms the holder has completed an accredited training program and meets state standards to work as a Community Health Worker in Maryland. Renewal is required within 30 days of expiration.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals aged 18 or older who hold a high school diploma or GED equivalent and have successfully completed a CHW training program accredited by the Maryland Department of Health. The program is available in English and Spanish.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Professional certification for Community Health Workers to demonstrate completion of an accredited training program and to work as a Community Health Worker in Maryland.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to residents who meet the eligibility requirements.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Consortium on Coordinated Community Supports Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Created by the Maryland General Assembly as part of the Blueprint for Maryland's Future, the Maryland Consortium on Coordinated Community Supports funds new and expanded behavioral health programming for students pre-K through grade 12 in all 24 Maryland jurisdictions. Grants support community behavioral health service providers, local coordinating hubs, and Community Support Partnerships that connect schools with mental health and wraparound services. The program fosters collaboration between providers, schools, and families, and provides training and technical assistance in evidence-based approaches for clinicians and educators through the National Center for School Mental Health. Year two (2025-2026) programs are projected to serve approximately 157,000 students.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Consortium awards grants through three tracks: Track 1 - Community Supports Partnerships (seven partnerships covering 12 jurisdictions); Track 2 - Hub Capacity-Building (nine new hubs); Track 3 - Service Providers (grants to support behavioral health services in areas without full partnerships). Currently 108 programs totaling $96 million are under implementation statewide. The FY 2027 funding round (RFA #4) was released in December 2025 and received 58 applications requesting $152 million (Track 1: $109,523,126 across 14 proposals; Track 2: $456,884 across 2 proposals; Track 3: $41,667,452 across 42 proposals); awards are expected in spring 2026. Grantees also receive training and technical assistance in evidence-based behavioral health programs from the National Center for School Mental Health, available to both clinicians and school staff.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications submitted; awards to be made later in spring 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community behavioral health service providers, local coordinating hubs (Community Support Partnerships), schools and school staff, families, and communities serving Maryland students pre-K through grade 12
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Expanding access to comprehensive behavioral health services for Maryland students, including: individual, group, and family therapy; psychiatric and medication management services; crisis intervention and stabilization; suicide prevention education and training; care coordination and navigation; case management; substance use disorder prevention and treatment; trauma-informed care; school-based mental health services; parent and family education and support; staff training and professional development; telehealth/virtual services; after-school programs and summer camps; mentoring programs; community health worker support; and transportation vouchers
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in all 24 Maryland jurisdictions. Agency address: 45 Calvert Street, Room 336, Annapolis, MD 21401.

Applications reviewed through the Consortium's Request for Applications (RFA) process
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through a Request for Applications (RFA) process. The FY 2027 RFA #4 was released in December 2025. Applicants submit applications during the open window across three tracks: Track 1 (Community Supports Partnerships), Track 2 (Hub Capacity-Building), and Track 3 (Service Providers). The Consortium reviews applications and awards are announced in the spring. The FY 2027 round received 58 applications requesting $152 million, with awards expected in spring 2026.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Dent-Care Loan Assistance Repayment Program (MDC-LARP) (Dentists & Hygienists)
structured_extraction.program_description: MDC-LARP is a student loan repayment program for licensed dentists and dental hygienists who treat Maryland Medical Assistance Program (MMAP/Medicaid) recipients. The program aims to increase access to oral health care for Maryland's most vulnerable populations by incentivizing providers to serve Medicaid patients in underserved communities. Full-time dentists can receive up to $50,000 per year for a three-year commitment (total up to $150,000), while part-time dentists (20–39 hours/week with at least 80% clinical hours) can receive up to $25,000 per year for a three-year commitment. Full-time dental hygienists can receive up to $10,000 per year for a two-year commitment (total up to $20,000), and part-time dental hygienists can receive up to $5,000 per year for a two-year commitment. Participants must maintain a patient population of at least 30% MMAP recipients. The program is administered by the Maryland Department of Health, Office of Oral Health, with loan repayment checks distributed through the Maryland Higher Education Commission's Office of Student Financial Assistance. The University of Maryland School of Dentistry is not an eligible worksite.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Student loan repayment assistance paid directly to recipients. Full-time dentists receive up to $50,000 per year for a three-year commitment (total up to $150,000). Part-time dentists (20–39 hours/week with at least 80% clinical hours) receive up to $25,000 per year for a three-year commitment. Full-time dental hygienists receive up to $10,000 per year for a two-year commitment (total up to $20,000). Part-time dental hygienists receive up to $5,000 per year for a two-year commitment. In exchange, participants must maintain a patient population of at least 30% MMAP (Medicaid) recipients. Number of awards per cycle depends on available funding. The University of Maryland School of Dentistry is not an eligible worksite.

structured_extraction.contact_name: Stacy Costello, MPH, CHES, Program Manager

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Repayment of higher education (student) loan debt for participating dentists and dental hygienists in exchange for service to underserved populations.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Early Hearing Detection and Intervention (MD EHDI) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The MD EHDI Program works to make sure every baby born in Maryland gets a newborn hearing screening and that any hearing loss is identified as early as possible, preferably by 3 months of age. The program coordinates with providers across the state to help babies identified as deaf or hard of hearing receive early intervention services, preferably by 6 months of age. It also connects families of children diagnosed as deaf or hard of hearing with experienced parent support contacts. The program promotes best communication outcomes for children with hearing status that could affect language acquisition, tracks and monitors newborn hearing screen status, follows babies who pass screening if they have risk factors for late-onset or progressive hearing status, and ensures referral to early intervention services for infants identified with permanent hearing status affecting language acquisition.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides universal newborn hearing screening prior to hospital discharge, rescreening services using AABR or OAE, diagnostic auditory brainstem response (ABR) testing, risk factor identification and monitoring, referral to early intervention services (at no cost to families), family education and support in preferred language, coordination with birthing hospitals, alternative birthing sites, diagnostic centers, primary care physician offices, and other healthcare facilities, and family navigation support for children who are deaf or hard of hearing from birth to 36 months.
structured_extraction.program_audience: All newborns and infants from birth to 36 months born or residing in Maryland, parents and families of children who are Deaf or hard of hearing, and healthcare professionals and early intervention specialists.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Hearing screening and diagnostic services, early intervention services (at no cost to families), family education and support, and language development services for children who are deaf or hard of hearing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Referrals made to Local Infants and Toddlers Program in the infant's jurisdiction of residence.
requirements_list: Child must be born in Maryland or reside in Maryland
Child must be identified as deaf or hard of hearing (for family support services)
Infants who do not pass newborn hearing screen receive rescreening prior to one month of age
Children with risk factors for late-onset or progressive hearing loss are followed even if they pass initial screening
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Families seeking peer parent support can complete the request form linked on the program page and will be contacted as soon as possible. Healthcare providers coordinate referrals to early intervention services through the Local Infants and Toddlers Program in the infant's jurisdiction of residence.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Family Planning Program (MFPP) makes sexual and reproductive health services accessible and affordable for all Marylanders, including teenagers and minors. Operating through a statewide network of 60+ health care sites (including some school-based locations) in 22 of Maryland's 24 jurisdictions, the program partners with local health departments, non-profit health organizations, and federally-qualified health centers to provide comprehensive family planning, sexual and reproductive health, pregnancy-related, and related preventive health services. Services include pregnancy testing, pregnancy options counseling, prenatal care, contraception and birth control counseling and access to contraceptive methods, cancer screening, STI and HIV testing, treatment and prevention, preconception counseling, reproductive life planning, fertility awareness education, folic acid supplementation, immunizations, infection and disease testing, counseling on tobacco/alcohol/substance use, blood pressure management, mental health support, vaccines, health education, telehealth, and general preventive health screenings and referrals. The program has a welcoming environment specifically noted for the LGBTQ+ community. Minors (ages 13–19 and under 18) may access confidential services without parental knowledge, as permitted under Maryland law. Services are free or low-cost and available to individuals of all ages, races, ethnicities, genders, sexual orientations, income levels, and residency statuses. Medicaid and other insurance are accepted but not required. Medicaid coverage is available for eligible pregnant individuals and extends 12 months postpartum. No one is denied services because of inability to pay.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free or low-cost sexual and reproductive health care services provided through 60+ clinic sites (including some school-based sites and telehealth) across Maryland. Services include pregnancy testing, pregnancy options counseling, prenatal care (folic acid supplementation, immunizations, infection and disease testing, tobacco/alcohol/substance use counseling, blood pressure management, mental health support), contraception and birth control counseling and access to contraceptive methods, cancer screening, STI and HIV testing, treatment and prevention, preconception counseling, reproductive life planning, fertility awareness education, vaccines, health education, and general preventive health screenings and referrals. Services are provided on a sliding-scale basis. Minors may access confidential services without parental consent. Medicaid and other insurance are accepted but not required; no one is turned away based on inability to pay. Medicaid coverage is available for qualifying pregnant individuals and extends 12 months postpartum. A welcoming environment is specifically noted for the LGBTQ+ community.

This includes women, men, and people across the gender spectrum (with a welcoming environment specifically noted for the LGBTQ+ community) seeking to prevent or delay pregnancy, teenagers (ages 13–19) and minors (under 18) who may access confidential services without parental consent, as well as pregnant individuals seeking pregnancy testing, pregnancy options counseling, prenatal care, preconception care, reproductive life planning, and related preventive health services, regardless of insurance status or ability to pay.

structured_extraction.program_description: A dental benefits program administered by the Maryland Department of Health for Medicaid recipients. The program provides dental care to eligible Medicaid members at no cost, covering a wide range of services including checkups, cleanings, fillings, crowns, root canals, extractions, fluoride treatments, anesthesia, and x-rays. Children under 21 also receive orthodontics, sealants, and fluoride varnish. Adults receive denture adjustments. There are no premiums, deductibles, copays, or annual benefit limits. The program connects eligible patients with enrolled dental providers across Maryland and is administered through a Dental Administrative Service Organization (currently SKYGEN USA, transitioning to DentaQuest in early 2026). Dental providers who enroll in the program can submit claims for reimbursement for dental services provided to Medicaid-eligible patients at rates set by the Maryland Healthy Smiles Dental Fee Schedule. A provider manual, fee schedule, and enrollment resources are available through the ePREP portal. Eligible populations include children under age 21, former foster care members through age 25, pregnant and postpartum adults over age 21, and adults over age 21 receiving full Medicaid benefits.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Medicaid-funded dental benefits with no premiums, deductibles, copays, or annual benefit maximum. Covered services include checkups, cleanings, fillings, crowns, root canals, extractions, fluoride treatments, anesthesia, and x-rays. Children under 21 also receive orthodontics, sealants, and fluoride varnish. Adults receive denture adjustments. Cosmetic procedures, dentures for adults 21 and older, and experimental procedures are not covered. Dental providers who enroll in the program can submit claims for reimbursement for dental services provided to Medicaid-eligible patients at rates set by the Maryland Healthy Smiles Dental Fee Schedule. Providers access credentialing, demographic updates, and claims processing through the ePREP portal and SKYGEN USA (transitioning to DentaQuest in early 2026). A provider manual and fee schedule are available. Preauthorization is required for certain procedures including comprehensive orthodontic treatment (HLD Index score of 15+ required). Claims must be submitted within 12 months of date of service; corrected claims within 18 months. Transportation assistance is available at select locations.

Also includes dental providers seeking to enroll in Maryland Medicaid's dental program and serve Medicaid-eligible patients.

For providers, reimbursement for dental services provided to Medicaid-eligible patients, as well as enrollment, credentialing, and participation in delivering dental services to Medicaid recipients. Transportation assistance available at select locations.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Loan Repayment Program (MLRP) - Nurses and Nursing Support Staff
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Loan Repayment Program (MLRP) helps nurses and nursing support staff repay their education loans in exchange for working at eligible healthcare practice sites in Maryland that serve underserved populations. The program pays qualifying education loan debt directly to verified loan holders on behalf of participants who fulfill a service obligation. Award amounts depend on whether the participant works part-time (20–39 hours per week) or full-time (40+ hours per week) and on funding availability. Service obligations begin July 1 following the application cycle.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MLRP pays qualifying education loan debt directly to the loan holder on behalf of program participants. Participants must fulfill a service obligation by working part-time (20–39 hours per week) or full-time (40+ hours per week) at an approved eligible practice site in Maryland. Award amounts depend on work schedule and funding availability. Funds are applied to loans obtained for undergraduate or graduate study leading to practice as an advanced practice registered nurse, nurse, or nursing support staff.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: July 1 following the application cycle (service obligation start date)
structured_extraction.contact_name: Office of Health Care Access and Workforce Development

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Repayment of education loans (tuition, educational expenses, or living expenses) obtained for undergraduate or graduate study leading to licensure or certification as an advanced practice registered nurse, nurse, or nursing support staff.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Practice site must be physically located in Maryland. Participants must have a valid employment contract to work at an eligible Maryland practice site and must hold an active, valid Maryland license.
