Practice site must provide services to all patients regardless of ability to pay, with no or nominal charge for patients at or below 100% of federal poverty guidelines and a sliding fee scale for patients between 100–200% of federal poverty guidelines
Practice site must accept Medicare, Maryland Medical Assistance, and Maryland Children's Health Insurance Program reimbursements where applicable
Practice site must agree to ongoing reporting requirements including employment verification, patient population data, health care quality outcomes, and CLAS standards assessment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must verify discipline eligibility (active Maryland license in an eligible nursing discipline), participant eligibility (citizenship, loan debt, employment contract), and practice site eligibility during the application process. The practice site must be approved by MLRP at the time of application. Service obligations begin July 1 following the application cycle. Contact the Office of Health Care Access and Workforce Development at mdh.loanrepaymentprograms@maryland.gov or 410-767-6123 for specific application steps and cycle dates.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Loan Repayment Program (MLRP) - Physicians and Physician Assistants
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Loan Repayment Program (MLRP) helps physicians, osteopathic physicians, and physician assistants repay their education loans in exchange for working at an eligible practice site in Maryland that serves patients regardless of their ability to pay. Participants must fulfill a service obligation at an approved site, and MLRP funds are paid directly to the verified education loan holder on the participant's behalf. The amount and terms depend on whether the participant works part-time (20–39 hours per week) or full-time (40+ hours per week), and the length of the service obligation. Final-year medical residents may apply for a three-year service obligation (final year of residency plus two years at an eligible practice site). Eligibility criteria can change year to year based on legislation and funding availability.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MLRP pays qualifying education loan debt directly to the verified loan holder on behalf of the participant. Awards are tied to a service obligation at an approved practice site in Maryland. Full-time participants (40+ hours per week) and part-time participants (20–39 hours per week) are eligible, with part-time participants automatically classified as part-time program participants. Final-year medical residents may apply for a three-year service obligation (final year of residency plus two years at an eligible practice site). Specific award amounts are not publicly stated; eligibility criteria and funding availability may change year to year based on legislation.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Office of Health Care Access and Workforce Development
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland-licensed physicians (MD/DO), physician assistants (PA), and final-year medical residents (MD or DO) specializing in primary care who have outstanding education loan debt and are willing to practice at an approved site in Maryland that serves patients regardless of ability to pay.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Repayment of education loans (tuition, educational expenses, or living expenses) obtained for undergraduate or graduate study leading to licensure as a physician or physician assistant. Funds are paid directly to the loan holder.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Participants must work at a practice site physically located in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must have completed training in an accredited program and hold an active, unrestricted Maryland license as an MD, DO, or PA, or be enrolled in the final year of a primary care medical residency (as of July 1 following the application cycle).
Must be a U.S. citizen or national.
Must personally owe eligible education loan debt obtained for undergraduate or graduate study leading to practice as a physician or physician assistant.
Must have a valid employment contract to work at an eligible Maryland practice site beginning July 1 following the application cycle.
Must dedicate at least 80% of work hours to direct patient care (OB/GYN physicians: at least 50% in ambulatory care setting).
Must work part-time (20–39 hours/week) or full-time (40+ hours/week); on-call time does not count toward practice hours.
Must fulfill service obligation at an approved eligible practice site.
Must not have federal or state judgment liens.
Must not have defaulted on any payment obligations (even if currently in good standing).
Must not have breached a prior service obligation to any government or other entity.
Must not have had debt written off as uncollectible or received a waiver of service/payment obligations.

Must not have outstanding contractual obligations for health care professional service (e.g., employer sign-on bonuses) unless fully satisfied before the MLRP service obligation begins (exception: Reserve Component of U.S. Armed Forces or National Guard members are eligible).

Practice site must be located in Maryland, serve all patients regardless of ability to pay using a sliding fee scale or discounts for low-income patients, accept Medicare and Maryland Medical Assistance (Medicaid) and CHIP reimbursement where applicable, and agree to participate in required reporting.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must verify discipline, participant, and practice site eligibility during the application process. The practice site must be approved by MLRP at the time of application. Applications are submitted on an annual cycle, with service obligations beginning July 1 following the application cycle. Monitoring and compliance requirements must be met throughout the service obligation. Contact the Office of Health Care Access and Workforce Development for specific application instructions and deadlines.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Loan Repayment Programs (MLRP) / State Loan Repayment Program (SLRP) / Maryland Loan Assistance Repayment Program for Physicians (MLARP)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Health administers the Maryland Loan Repayment Programs (MLRP), which include three sub-programs: the federally funded State Loan Repayment Program (SLRP), the state-funded Maryland Loan Assistance Repayment Program for Physicians and Physician Assistants (MLARP PPA), and the Maryland Loan Assistance Repayment Program for Nurses and Nursing Support Staff (MLARP NNSS). Together, these programs provide educational loan repayment assistance to health professionals — including physicians (MD/DO), physician assistants, final-year medical residents, APRNs, RNs, LPNs, and nursing support staff — in exchange for a service obligation at an eligible practice site in a health professional shortage area (HPSA), medically underserved area (MUA), or state-designated shortage area in Maryland. The SLRP requires a 1:1 match with MLARP; MLARP is administered in coordination with the Maryland Higher Education Commission. The programs aim to improve recruitment and retention of healthcare workers across the state. Award amounts vary by credential and work schedule. Recipients may reapply after completing the first obligation, with a lifetime maximum of $200,000. As part of program requirements, MLRP participants and practice sites must also complete cultural competency and implicit bias training using approved resources including federal HHS training tools, TRAIN Maryland courses, and the MDH Office of Minority Health and Health Disparities catalog.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loan repayment awards are provided in exchange for a service obligation at an eligible practice site in a health professional shortage area or medically underserved area. The Maryland Department of Health pays awarded funds directly to verified education loan holders to repay qualifying education loans obtained for tuition, educational expenses, or living expenses for undergraduate or graduate study. Award amounts vary by credential and work schedule: Physicians (MD/DO) and Physician Assistants can receive up to $100,000 (full time, ≥40 hrs/week) or $50,000 (part time, 20–39 hrs/week) for a 2-year service obligation. Final-year medical residents can receive up to $100,000 (full time) or $50,000 (part time) for a 3-year obligation (1 year during residency + 2 years post-residency). APRNs (CRNP, CNM, CRNA, CNS) can receive up to $100,000 (full time) or $50,000 (part time) for 2 years. RNs and LPNs can receive up to $50,000 (full time) or $25,000 (part time) for 2 years. Nursing support staff (CMT, CMA, CNA, GNA) can receive up to $5,000 (full time) or $2,500 (part time) for 1 year. Recipients may reapply after completing the first obligation, with a lifetime maximum of $200,000. Award is not based on financial need. Funding comes from the federal HRSA State Loan Repayment Program (SLRP) and state-level resources (MLARP). Participants must also complete required cultural competency and implicit bias training using approved resources (HHS online tools, TRAIN Maryland, and the MDH Office of Minority Health and Health Disparities catalog). Recipients must sign a promissory note and service obligation agreement. Not-for-profit and public practice sites are prioritized over for-profit sites; for nurses/nursing support staff, for-profit sites must be in areas with identified healthcare workforce shortage or public health need.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Application Enrollment Opens: March 1; Application Deadline: April 15 (annual cycle)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Health professionals including physicians, physician assistants, final-year medical residents, APRNs, RNs, LPNs, and nursing support staff who are licensed in Maryland and willing to serve at eligible practice sites in health professional shortage areas or medically underserved areas in Maryland. Also applicable to MLRP practice sites required to complete cultural competency and implicit bias training.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Repayment of qualifying higher education (student) loans obtained for tuition, educational expenses, or living expenses for undergraduate or graduate study leading to practice as a physician, PA, APRN, nurse, or nursing support staff; cultural competency and implicit bias training for participating health care providers and practice sites.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland; participants must practice at eligible sites in health professional shortage areas (HPSAs), medically underserved areas (MUAs), rural areas, or state-designated health professional shortage areas in Maryland. Priority given to rural areas and underserved communities; areas federally designated as HPSAs receive priority technical scoring. Service areas defined by zip codes served.
requirements_list: Must be a United States citizen or U.S. National
Must be a licensed health professional (physician, physician assistant, medical resident, APRN, RN, LPN, or nursing support staff)
Must hold a medical degree and a valid unrestricted license to practice medicine in Maryland at the time the service obligation begins (for physician/PA track)
Must commit to a service obligation at an eligible practice site in a health professional shortage area or medically underserved area
Service obligation length varies by credential (1–3 years)
Full-time participation requires ≥40 hours per week; part-time requires 20–39 hours per week
At least 80% of time worked must be direct patient care
Participant must work at least 45 weeks at the practice site (less than 35 days away for holidays, vacation, professional education, illness, or other reasons)
Workweek may be compressed into less than 4 days per week (max 12 hours per 24-hour period)
Must have existing higher education loan debt and must not be in default on any eligible higher education loan
Eligible loans must have been obtained for undergraduate or graduate study leading to practice; loans obtained beyond licensure/certification are ineligible
Must have no existing or un-served service obligation with any other loan repayment program
Must never have violated court-ordered child support or been delinquent in child support payments
Must complete required documentation including promissory note, service obligation agreement, and lender verification
Participant must authorize lender information sharing; lender must complete verification form and loans must have outstanding balance
Lobbying certification required — no Federal appropriated funds may be used for lobbying activities
Must submit debarment affirmation affirming no suspension or debarment by any public entity and no knowingly entered contracts with debarred/suspended persons
Year 2 renewal requires employment verification, impact data collection, cultural competency training and assessment, and updated lender verification
Participant must complete impact data collection form documenting patient services, payer types, and quality improvement outcomes; attestation of information accuracy required
Participants must complete 6 hours of continuing education in cultural, linguistic, and health literacy competency and submit proof of training completion

Practice sites must complete organizational assessment related to National Standards for Culturally and Linguistically Appropriate Services (CLAS) using HHS CLAS tool, SurveyMonkey link, or other approved means
Annual cultural competency and implicit bias training compliance required (completion period: July 1 – June 30)
Eligibility criteria and number of awards may change year-to-year based on legislation and funding availability
Application enrollment opens March 1
Application deadline is April 15 (11:59 p.m., EST)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted during the annual cycle from March 1 through April 15 (11:59 p.m., EST). Applicants complete and file an application available from the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) at https://health.maryland.gov/pophealth/Pages/State-Loan-Repayment-Program.aspx. Awarded participants must then complete offer acceptance documentation including: promissory note, service obligation agreement, lender verification form, lobbying certification, debarment affirmation, and ACH/direct deposit authorization. For lender verification, participants complete authorization, provide lender information, lender completes the verification form and returns to participant, and the form is submitted to MDH. Year 2 renewal documentation is required to receive the second year of funds, including employment verification (employer completes form certifying employment details and compliance), impact data collection form (documenting patient services, payer types, and quality improvement outcomes), cultural competency training and assessment form, and updated lender verification. Participants must also complete required cultural competency and implicit bias training using approved resources (HHS online tools, TRAIN Maryland, and the MDH Office of Minority Health and Health Disparities catalog) and submit proof of training completion and organizational assessment results. For questions, call (410) 767-6123 or email [email protected]. See the MLRP Program Guidelines for full details.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Medicaid (also called Medical Assistance or MA) is a public health insurance program that provides free or low-cost comprehensive health care coverage to eligible low-income adults, children, pregnant individuals, parents, primary caretakers, former foster care youth, elderly adults, and people who are blind or disabled. It pays medical bills for needy and low-income individuals and families using federal and state funds, administered by the State of Maryland through the Maryland Department of Health, with applications also processed through the Maryland Department of Human Services and local departments of social services statewide — including Anne Arundel County's Department of Social Services. The program also provides coverage for individuals who are aged, blind, disabled, living in a nursing home, or medically needy. Coverage includes doctor's visits, exams, prescriptions, inpatient and outpatient hospital care, x-ray and lab services, pharmacy, basic physician care, nursing home costs, medical day care, personal care, mental health and substance abuse treatment, Medicare premiums, emergency dental care, family planning, limited transportation to providers, home health services, and physical therapy. As of June 30, 2025, the program covers 1,508,710 Marylanders — roughly one in four residents — including 331,577 adults under ACA expansion. Eligibility is based on income limits, residency, citizenship or immigration status, and for some programs, age, disability, or medical need. A spend-down option is available for those over the income limit. Emergency Medicaid is also available for emergency services and pregnant women regardless of immigration status. Coverage can start right away if the applicant is eligible, and retroactive coverage for up to 3 months prior to application may be available for those with outstanding medical expenses. People who receive SSI are automatically eligible and do not need to apply. Applications are accepted year-round online, by phone, in person at local health departments or departments of social services, or through the Maryland Benefits portal.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free or low-cost health insurance coverage for eligible Maryland residents. Coverage is provided through managed care plans (HealthChoice) or fee-for-service arrangements and pays for medical expenses including doctor's visits, exams, prescriptions, inpatient and outpatient hospital care, x-ray and lab services, pharmacy, basic physician care, nursing home costs, medical day care, personal care, mental health and substance abuse treatment, Medicare premiums, emergency dental care, family planning, limited transportation to providers, home health services, and physical therapy. Coverage also includes dental care for all populations, vision care for children, and immunizations for children. Coverage amount may vary by income and assets. There are no fees or payments required from enrollees. Emergency Medicaid is available for emergency services and pregnant women regardless of immigration status. A spend-down option is available for those over the income limit. Retroactive coverage for up to 3 months prior to application may be available for those with outstanding medical expenses. Applications are accepted year-round. In Anne Arundel County, residents can apply through the Anne Arundel County Department of Social Services (410-269-4500).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No deadline — you can apply at any time
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents who are low-income adults aged 20–64, children aged 0–19, pregnant individuals, parents or primary caretakers, former foster care youth, individuals aged 65 and older, individuals who are blind or disabled, low-income families with children under 21, people with disabilities during the 24-month Medicare waiting period, SSI/SSDI recipients, Medicare recipients, individuals living in a nursing home, and medically needy individuals. Also includes ACA expansion adults ages 19–65, refugees and asylees, and legal permanent residents. Pregnant women and emergency care patients may qualify regardless of immigration status. Anne Arundel County residents can apply through the county's Department of Social Services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Health care coverage including medical, dental, vision, and specialty services; payment of medical bills and health care costs including doctor's visits, exams, prescriptions, inpatient and outpatient hospital care, x-ray and lab services, pharmacy, physician care, nursing home costs, medical day care, personal care, mental health and substance abuse treatment, Medicare premiums, emergency dental care, family planning, limited transportation to providers, home health services, and physical therapy. Emergency services for those who may not otherwise qualify.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Applicant must be a Maryland resident and a U.S. citizen or meet alien status requirements. Applications can be submitted online at marylandbenefits.gov or mymdthink.maryland.gov, or in person at one of DHS's 24 local departments of social services. In Anne Arundel County, residents may apply through the Anne Arundel County Department of Social Services (410-269-4500) or via marylandbenefits.gov. In Prince George's County, residents may apply through the Prince George's County Department of Social Services or via Maryland Health Connection (marylandhealthconnection.gov) or MyMDTHINK Benefits (mymdthink.maryland.gov). In Montgomery County, residents can apply with assistance from the Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services, or in person at regional Office of Eligibility and Support Services locations in Silver Spring, Rockville, and Germantown (contact: 240-777-1815). In Howard County, apply at the Howard County DSS office at 9780 Patuxent Woods Drive, Columbia, MD 21046 (410-872-8700).
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident
Must be a U.S. citizen or qualifying immigrant who meets immigration status requirements
Must meet income limits for your coverage group
Must be a needy or low-income individual

Must be in an eligible category: low-income adult, child, pregnant individual, parent or primary caretaker, former foster care youth, elderly adult, person who is blind or disabled, individual living in a nursing home, or medically needy individual
For certain programs: meet technical eligibility (e.g., specific age or disability)
For certain programs: meet financial eligibility including income and asset limits (applies if age 65+, blind, disabled, or needing long-term care)
For certain programs: meet medical eligibility (need a certain level of care)
People who receive SSI are automatically eligible without applying
People with disabilities may be eligible during the 24-month Medicare waiting period
Individuals under 65 apply through Maryland Health Connection; individuals 65+ or disabled or on Medicare apply through Maryland Benefits Programs & Services Portal
Emergency Medicaid is available for emergency services and pregnant women regardless of immigration status
U.S. citizens or individuals lawfully present in the U.S. for at least 5 years generally qualify (with exceptions for emergency services and pregnant women)
Must provide proof of income such as a tax return or two recent pay stubs
Must provide proof of identity such as a driver's license or photo ID
Must provide proof of citizenship such as a birth certificate or passport
Must provide Social Security number
Pregnant women may qualify under the Healthy Babies Equity Act (regardless of immigration status) or Full Medicaid (U.S. citizens and lawfully present immigrants)
Families and children must be under age 21 and meet specific income levels

Children under 19, families with unmarried children under 21, pregnant women, SSI/TCA/foster care recipients, aged 65+, verified blind or disabled, Medicare recipients, or adults aged 19-64 not disabled (effective January 2014)

Spend-down provision available if income is over the limit
May apply even if you have private insurance or third-party coverage

Must keep contact information up to date and renew coverage when renewal notice is received
Must select a Managed Care Organization (MCO) upon enrollment

Proposed future changes under H.R. 1 (One Big Beautiful Bill Act): work requirements of 80 hours/month for ACA expansion adults ages 19-65 (effective Dec. 31, 2026); eligibility renewals every 6 months for ACA expansion adults (effective Jan. 1, 2027); cost-sharing not to exceed 5% of total income for ACA expansion adults (effective Oct. 1, 2028)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at marylandhealthconnection.gov, through the Maryland Health Connection mobile app 'Enroll MHC' (Apple or Android), by calling 1-855-642-8572 (toll-free; TTY: 855-642-8573), online at marylandbenefits.gov or mymdthink.maryland.gov, or in person at a local health department or one of DHS's 24 local departments of social services. In Anne Arundel County, residents may apply through the Anne Arundel County Department of Social Services (410-269-4500) or via marylandbenefits.gov. In Prince George's County, residents may apply through the Prince George's County Department of Social Services or via Maryland Health Connection (marylandhealthconnection.gov) or MyMDTHINK Benefits (mymdthink.maryland.gov). In Montgomery County, residents may apply with assistance from the Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services, or in person at regional Office of Eligibility and Support Services locations in Silver Spring, Rockville, or Germantown (240-777-1815). In Howard County, apply at the Howard County DSS office at 9780 Patuxent Woods Drive, Columbia, MD 21046 (410-872-8700); bring proof of identity, Social Security numbers for all household members, proof of address, proof of income for everyone in household, and proof of household expenses. Once enrolled, select from available MCOs for managed care coverage. Most applications are processed within 30 days (90+ days if disability determination is required). Applications can also be mailed to a local department of social services. For questions about benefits or services, contact your managed care organization or the HealthChoice Helpline at 800-284-4510. There is no application deadline — applications are accepted on a rolling basis at any time throughout the year.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Medicaid Cell and Gene Therapy Coverage
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Medicaid covers two approved cell and gene therapies (Casgevy and Lyfgenia) for eligible members with sickle cell disease. These treatments modify stem cells so the body produces healthy red blood cells, which can reduce pain episodes and hospital visits. The program includes comprehensive evaluation, stem cell collection, optional fertility preservation, gene therapy infusion, and 15-year follow-up care, offering coordinated, whole-person care addressing physical health, behavioral health, and social needs. Treatment is only covered at two approved centers: University of Maryland Medical Center in Baltimore, MD, and Children's National Medical Center in Washington, D.C.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Medicaid covers the cost of two FDA-approved cell and gene therapies — Casgevy and Lyfgenia — for eligible members with sickle cell disease. Treatment must be received at one of two approved centers: University of Maryland Medical Center in Baltimore, MD, or Children's National Medical Center in Washington, D.C. The program also provides comprehensive supportive services including transportation assistance, housing assistance, childcare services, fertility preservation services, behavioral health support, and peer support. A case manager is assigned to coordinate care throughout the process.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland Medicaid members aged 12 or older with a sickle cell disease diagnosis who meet the medical requirements for one of the two covered therapies (Casgevy or Lyfgenia).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Coverage of cell and gene therapy treatment (Casgevy or Lyfgenia) for sickle cell disease at an approved treatment center, as well as comprehensive supportive services including transportation, housing, childcare, and fertility preservation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Maryland Medicaid members statewide. Treatment must be received at one of two approved centers: University of Maryland Medical Center in Baltimore, MD, or Children's National Medical Center in Washington, D.C.
requirements_list: Must have Maryland Medicaid
Must be at least 12 years old
Must have a sickle cell disease diagnosis
Must meet the medical requirements for one of the two covered therapies (Casgevy or Lyfgenia)
Treatment must be received at an approved treatment center
Comprehensive evaluation at treatment center (physical, behavioral health, and social needs assessment)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Talk to your health care provider to discuss eligibility and next steps. A referral from a hematologist to a treatment center initiates the process; a case manager is then assigned to schedule appointments and coordinate care. HealthChoice members may also contact their HealthChoice plan. For other questions, email [email protected].

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Medicaid covers doula (birth worker) services for eligible Medicaid members. A doula is a trained, non-clinical professional who provides physical, emotional, and informational support to birthing parents before, during, and after birth. Services are free for eligible members and include prenatal and postpartum home visits and attendance at the birth. The program allows doulas to enroll as Medicaid providers and receive reimbursement for services provided to eligible Medicaid members. Organizations that train doulas can also apply to become Maryland Department of Health (MDH)-approved certification organizations, allowing their trained doulas to qualify for Medicaid enrollment and reimbursement.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Doula services are free of charge to eligible Maryland Medicaid members, including prenatal visits, attendance at birth, and postpartum visits such as breastfeeding assistance and connection to community resources. Members connect to a doula through their HealthChoice Managed Care Organization (MCO). Maryland Medicaid reimburses enrolled doula providers for services provided to eligible Medicaid members during pregnancy and birth. Certification organizations can apply for MDH approval, allowing their trained doulas to qualify for Medicaid enrollment and reimbursement. The program provides resources on enrollment, billing, and reimbursement for providers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland Medicaid members who are pregnant or have been pregnant within the last 180 days; doulas seeking to become enrolled Medicaid providers; and organizations that train doulas seeking to become MDH-approved certification organizations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Physical, emotional, and informational support before, during, and after birth, including prenatal education, birth attendance, postpartum support, breastfeeding assistance, and connection to community resources. For providers: reimbursement for doula services provided to Medicaid-eligible individuals during pregnancy and birth. For certification organizations: MDH approval enabling their trained doulas to qualify for Medicaid enrollment and reimbursement.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland for Medicaid members and Medicaid-enrolled doula providers.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland Medicaid member (for recipients)
Must be pregnant or have been pregnant within the last 180 days (for recipients)
Doulas must obtain certification through an MDH-approved certification organization
Doulas must enroll as a Medicaid provider
Certification organizations must apply for and receive MDH approval to qualify their doulas for Medicaid enrollment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For Medicaid members: Contact your HealthChoice Managed Care Organization (MCO) to be connected with a doula. You can also talk to your health care provider or call your health insurance provider for more information. For doulas: Get certified through an MDH-approved certification organization, then complete the Medicaid provider enrollment process. Organizations seeking to become an approved certification organization can apply during open application periods by contacting MDH at mdh.medicaidmch@maryland.gov to be notified of future application periods.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Medicaid covers medically necessary gender-affirming care for transgender and gender-expansive people. This includes services to help individuals align their body with their lived gender identity, such as hormone therapy, surgeries, voice surgery and therapy, hair removal and transplants, fertility preservation, facial surgery, top surgery, preventative care after transition, and revision or reversal of prior gender-affirming procedures. Benefits may be provided through Medicaid directly or through HealthChoice managed care organizations (MCOs).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Maryland Medicaid covers medically necessary gender-affirming services including hormone therapy and lab testing, voice surgery and therapy, hair removal and transplants, fertility preservation, facial surgery, top surgery, gender-affirming surgery, preventative care after transition, and revision or reversal of prior gender-affirming procedures. Services may be delivered through Medicaid directly or through HealthChoice managed care organizations (MCOs).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Transgender and gender-expansive individuals enrolled in Maryland Medicaid who need medically necessary care to align their body with their lived gender identity.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Covers the cost of medically necessary gender-affirming health care services including hormone therapy and lab testing, surgeries, voice therapy, hair removal and transplants, fertility preservation, and related preventative and follow-up care.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Maryland Medicaid enrollees statewide.
requirements_list: Must be enrolled in Maryland Medicaid
Must have a diagnosis from a health care provider supporting the need for care
Must be able to make fully informed decisions and consent to treatment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Enroll in Medicaid if not already enrolled. Talk to your health care provider about a diagnosis for gender-affirming care. If you receive benefits through a HealthChoice managed care organization (MCO), contact them for more information about covered services.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Medicaid Home Visiting Services Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Medicaid covers home visiting services for HealthChoice and Medicaid fee-for-service enrollees statewide. The program supports eligible organizations, including local health departments and other providers, to deliver evidence-based home visiting services to Medicaid members. Home Visiting Services provide support and parenting skills training to pregnant people and new parents before and after birth. A specially trained professional or nurse visits the home to help families have a healthy pregnancy and raise healthy children. Services include three types: prenatal home visits, postpartum home visits, and infant home visits. Services continue after birth until the child reaches age two or three, depending on the program selected. Maryland offers two evidence-based models: Healthy Families America (HFA) and Nurse-Family Partnership (NFP). Services cover child development, parenting skills, self-care, nutrition, mental health, stress management, future planning, and connecting families to community resources. Regulations effective January 13, 2022 define qualifications, scope, and billing requirements for enrolled Home Visiting Organizations. Reimbursement is $188 per home visit (in-person or telehealth), limited to once per calendar week per beneficiary.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Maryland Medicaid reimburses enrolled Home Visiting Organizations $188 per home visit (in-person or via telehealth) for covered home visiting services provided to HealthChoice and Medicaid fee-for-service enrollees. MCOs must reimburse at a rate no lower than the fee-for-service rate. Services are billable on a calendar week basis (Sunday–Saturday), limited to once per calendar week per beneficiary using CPT code 99600. Home visits typically last 60 minutes. Providers must enroll through the Maryland Medicaid provider enrollment system (e-PREP) at the organizational level using a Type 2 NPI to receive reimbursement. For eligible Medicaid members, free in-home visits are provided covering education on child development, parenting skills, self-care, nutrition, mental health, stress management, future planning, and connecting families to community resources. Maryland offers two evidence-based models: Healthy Families America (HFA) and Nurse-Family Partnership (NFP). Services continue from pregnancy until the child's second or third birthday depending on the program. Reimbursement covers direct service costs only; it does NOT cover administrative overhead, lactation consulting, program start-up costs, or non-medically necessary services. Regulations effective January 13, 2022 define qualifications, scope, and billing requirements for providers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Home visiting organizations (including local health departments, HFA accredited programs, NFP fidelity programs, FQHCs operating HFA or NFP programs, and non-LHD organizations) seeking to enroll as Maryland Medicaid providers to deliver home visiting services, as well as pregnant Maryland Medicaid members or those with infants younger than 90 days old at enrollment. For NFP specifically, enrollment is limited to individuals with no previous live births.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Delivery of and reimbursement for evidence-based home visiting services to eligible Medicaid enrollees, including prenatal home visits, postpartum home visits, and infant home visits. Covers parenting education, child development guidance, nutrition, mental health support, stress management, future planning, and community resource referrals. Does NOT cover administrative overhead, lactation consulting, program start-up costs, or non-medically necessary services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to enrolled Medicaid providers and eligible Medicaid and HealthChoice members. Service area must be defined by each site.
requirements_list: Must meet qualifications defined in Maryland home visiting services regulations effective January 13, 2022 (COMAR 10.09.78.00-09)
Must enroll as a Maryland Medicaid provider through the e-PREP (Electronic Provider Revalidation and Enrollment Portal) system at the organizational level with a Type 2 NPI
Must follow the Home Visiting Services Program Manual guidelines
Must implement an evidence-based home visiting model (Healthy Families America or Nurse-Family Partnership) and meet fidelity/accreditation standards
Must be fully enrolled with Maryland Medicaid before billing
Must be contracted with an MCO
Must sign attestation that providers are in good standing

Must provide Tax Identification Number (TIN/EIN)

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For providers: interested organizations must obtain a National Provider Identifier (NPI) through the National Plan and Provider Enumeration System (NPPES) website. Organizations then complete provider enrollment through Maryland Medicaid's e-PREP system at the organizational level using a Type 2 NPI. Steps include: create user profile with username, password, and 6-digit authentication code verification; log in and create a business profile with NPI verification; answer security questions; navigate to 'My Applications' tab and generate a new application selecting the appropriate organization type (e.g., 'Other Healthcare Organization'); complete required sections including business information, service address, cultural competency training, FFS Medicaid participation, language services, adverse action disclosure, ownership/control interests, and attach the Medical Assistance Program Application Facility/Organization PT Home Visiting Services Addendum. Separate enrollment guidance and recorded webinars are available for Local Health Departments (LHDs) and non-LHD organizations. For recipients: contact your Managed Care Organization (MCO) or health care provider to request Home Visiting Services. Your health plan can help determine which program is the right fit for you.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Medicaid Maternal Opioid Misuse (MOM) Case Management Services
structured_extraction.program_description: The MOM program improves care for pregnant and postpartum Medicaid participants diagnosed with opioid use disorder (OUD). It provides free, enhanced case management services through Maryland's nine Medicaid managed care organizations (MCOs). A case manager meets with participants at least monthly to create a person-centered care plan covering mental and physical health, opioid use disorder treatment, overdose prevention, and connection to local resources. Services are available during pregnancy and for up to one year after birth, with a focus on prenatal and postpartum health care utilization, behavioral health treatment, and screenings for depression, anxiety, and social determinants of health. Care plans are shared through CRISP, Maryland's statewide health information exchange. Partners can identify and refer potential participants, and enrollment is available online.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free, enhanced case management services for eligible Maryland Medicaid members. A case manager meets with participants at least monthly to coordinate prenatal and postpartum care, opioid use disorder treatment, and support services. Includes person-centered care planning and goal-setting, screenings for depression, anxiety, and social determinants of health, linkage to community resources, overdose prevention, and coordination with health care providers through the CRISP health information exchange. Services cover prenatal and postpartum care visits, connection to opioid treatment medications, and linkage to local support resources during pregnancy and up to one year postpartum. Provided at no cost to eligible members.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Pregnant and postpartum individuals covered by Maryland Medicaid who use or have a history of using opioids, including those diagnosed with opioid use disorder (OUD).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Case management services to coordinate prenatal and postpartum care, opioid use disorder treatment, mental and physical health needs, overdose prevention, behavioral health treatment access, and connection to local community resources during pregnancy and up to one year after birth.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to Medicaid participants.
requirements_list: Must have health insurance through Maryland Medicaid
Must be pregnant or postpartum
Must use or have used opioids, or be diagnosed with opioid use disorder (OUD)
Must be diagnosed with opioid use disorder (OUD)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Enroll online at http://health.maryland.gov/EnrollMOM or contact your Medicaid managed care organization (MCO). Partners can identify and refer potential participants. For questions, email MDH.MOMModel@maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Medical Assistance (Medicaid) pays for nursing facility care for eligible participants who meet both financial and medical requirements. The program covers full-time nursing care in a licensed facility when a person's health condition requires round-the-clock supervision by a licensed nurse. Maryland serves over 20,000 participants each year in nursing facilities statewide. Administered by the State using Federal and State funds through Local Departments of Social Services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Maryland Medical Assistance pays nursing facilities on behalf of eligible Medicaid participants using a case-mix system. Payment rates are calculated separately for each facility based on the facility's operating costs, the amount and type of care each resident needs, and other factors. There is no fixed dollar amount per participant. The program covers nursing facility services for over 20,000 participants per year. Also offers community-based alternatives through Community First Choice/Community Options Waiver and the MFP Nursing Facility Transition Program, enabling nursing home residents to receive care in their own community homes.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland Medicaid participants who need full-time nursing facility care and meet financial and medical eligibility requirements, including individuals with serious mental illness or intellectual disabilities screened through PASRR. Must be U.S. citizens or eligible aliens, Maryland residents, age 65 or older or disabled, and low-income. Also includes nursing home residents currently receiving Medical Assistance who prefer to transition to community-based services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment for nursing facility services, including full-time care under licensed nursing supervision. May also fund long-term care services and supports in community settings through transition programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland for individuals residing in or being admitted to a participating Medicaid nursing facility. Must be a Maryland resident. Applications are made through the local Department of Social Services in the county where the applicant resides, or in the county where the nursing facility is located.
requirements_list: Must apply for Medical Assistance through the local Department of Social Services in the county where the applicant lives (or where the facility is located if already in a facility)
Must be a U.S. citizen or eligible alien and a Maryland resident
Must be age 65 or older, or disabled
Must meet financial eligibility requirements (documentation of income and resources required)
Must be certified as medically eligible — condition must require full-time care under licensed nursing supervision ('medically necessary')
Applicant's physician must complete Medical Eligibility Review Form DHMH 3871 if not already in a nursing facility or hospital
Must pass PASRR (Pre-Admission Screening and Resident Review) if suspected of having a serious mental illness, intellectual disability, or related condition
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply for Medical Assistance at the local Department of Social Services (in person or by mail), providing documentation of income and resources. A physician must complete the Medical Eligibility Review Form (DHMH 3871) and mail it to Delmarva Foundation if the applicant is not already in a nursing facility or hospital. If the applicant is already in a nursing facility or hospital, the facility or hospital handles the medical eligibility application. Complete PASRR screening if required. The physician must also complete the MR/MI Screen Form as required under PASRR. Individuals interested in transitioning from a nursing home to community-based care may contact the MFP Nursing Facility Transition Program.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Medicaid Pharmacy Program provides pharmacy services to Maryland Medicaid members across several coverage programs. Services vary by enrollment type: full pharmacy coverage for standard Medicaid members, contraceptives and STI treatments for Family Planning members, mental health and substance use disorder medications for HealthChoice managed care enrollees (with most other drugs covered by their MCOs), and coverage for drugs excluded from Medicare Part D for fully dual-eligible Medicare/Medicaid beneficiaries. Mental health medications are carved out of MCO pharmacy benefits and payable as Fee-for-Service (FFS) through Maryland Medical Assistance, subject to prior authorization requirements and clinical criteria from the Preferred Drug List (PDL). Substance Use Disorder (SUD) medications are similarly carved out and payable as fee-for-service, subject to PDL prior authorization, clinical criteria, and quantity limits; treatment should be part of a comprehensive management program including psychosocial support.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Covers prescription drug costs for eligible Maryland Medicaid enrollees. Medicaid members receive complete pharmacy services. HealthChoice members receive mental health and substance use disorder medications through Medicaid as Fee-for-Service (with all other drugs provided by their Managed Care Organizations). Mental health medications covered include anticonvulsants, antidepressants, antipsychotics, stimulants, benzodiazepines, and other psychiatric medications. SUD medications covered include buprenorphine, naltrexone, naloxone, acamprosate, disulfiram, lofexidine, nalmefene, bupropion SR, varenicline, and nicotine replacement therapies. Family Planning members receive contraceptives and STI treatments. Fully dual-eligible Medicare Part D beneficiaries receive most drugs excluded from Medicare coverage, with all other drugs provided by Medicare Prescription Drug Programs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland Medicaid members, HealthChoice managed care enrollees, Family Planning program members, fully dual-eligible Medicare/Medicaid beneficiaries, and Maryland Medicaid beneficiaries with substance use disorders
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Prescription medications and pharmacy services, including mental health drugs (antidepressants, antipsychotics, anticonvulsants, benzodiazepines, stimulants), substance use disorder medications (buprenorphine, naltrexone, naloxone, acamprosate, disulfiram, varenicline, nicotine replacement therapies), contraceptives, STI treatments, and drugs excluded from Medicare Part D coverage
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to eligible Medicaid enrollees and Medicare dual-eligible beneficiaries
requirements_list: Must be enrolled in Maryland Medicaid, HealthChoice, Family Planning, or Medicare Part D dual-eligible program
Must be a fully dual eligible Medicare/Medicaid beneficiary to receive coverage for drugs excluded from Medicare Part D
Prescription from healthcare provider required
Prior authorization may be required for certain medications per the Preferred Drug List (PDL) and clinical criteria
Medications subject to quantity limits
Age-specific coverage for certain medications (e.g., clonidine ER and guanfacine ER covered for ages 6-17)
Preauthorization required through CAMP program for leuprolide acetate or medroxyprogesterone for adult males with certain behavioral disorders
SUD treatment should be part of a comprehensive management program including psychosocial support
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligibility and enrollment is determined through Maryland Medicaid or the applicable managed care organization (MCO). HealthChoice members receive most drug coverage through their MCO; mental health and substance use disorder medications are carved out and covered as Fee-for-Service through Maryland Medical Assistance following specific formularies and PDL requirements. Prior authorization may be required for certain medications. No separate application for pharmacy benefits is required beyond enrollment in the appropriate program. Contact the Maryland Department of Health for enrollment information.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Medicaid reimburses healthcare providers for medically necessary services delivered via telehealth, including synchronous audio-visual and audio-only visits, asynchronous telehealth, remote patient monitoring (RPM), and store-and-forward technologies used in dermatology, ophthalmology, or radiology. The program aims to increase access to services, reduce preventable hospitalization, improve health outcomes through timely disease detection, and expand capacity in underserved areas. There are no geographic restrictions, and all distant site provider types are eligible for reimbursement. All telehealth platforms and transmissions must be HIPAA compliant. Outpatient Mental Health Centers (OMHCs) may now bill at clinic rates for telehealth services when both practitioner and patient are offsite, effective June 1, 2025.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Maryland Medicaid reimburses enrolled providers for covered services delivered via telehealth, including synchronous (audio-video and audio-only) visits, asynchronous telehealth, remote patient monitoring, and store-and-forward technologies for dermatology, ophthalmology, and radiology. Reimbursement rates are the same as in-person services. Providers must include the 'GT' modifier for audio-visual telehealth or 'UB' modifier for audio-only services. Reimbursement covers professional fees only; facility/room/board charges are not reimbursed unless the professional fee cannot be billed separately. Services are subject to the same program restrictions, pre-authorizations, and limitations as in-person services. Reimbursement rates and covered services are defined in provider-specific COMAR chapters and manuals. Providers must meet requirements under COMAR 10.09.49 and any provider-specific COMAR chapters and manuals incorporated by reference. Outpatient Mental Health Centers (OMHCs) may bill at clinic rates for telehealth services when both practitioner and patient are offsite, effective June 1, 2025.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland Medicaid-enrolled healthcare providers delivering medically necessary services via telehealth to Medicaid participants, including fee-for-service and HealthChoice MCO enrolled participants.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reimbursement for covered telehealth services including synchronous (audio-video and audio-only) visits, asynchronous telehealth, remote patient monitoring, and store-and-forward technologies for specific specialties such as dermatology, ophthalmology, and radiology. Also covers behavioral health and acute care services delivered via telehealth.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: No geographic restrictions for telehealth services within Maryland Medicaid. Originating site (patient location) may be the participant's home or any secure location approved by the patient and provider. Out-of-state participants may be eligible depending on provider licensing board regulations.
requirements_list: Provider must be enrolled in Maryland Medicaid
Provider must consult their professional licensing board for telehealth governing scope of practice and licensure requirements
Services must be medically necessary
Services must comply with COMAR 10.09.49 Telehealth Services
Provider-specific COMAR chapters establish which services may be delivered via telehealth
All telehealth platforms and transmissions must be HIPAA compliant
Providers are responsible for establishing reasonable safeguards for patient confidentiality

Freestanding clinics (PT 33, PT 35, PT 38) are subject to the federal four walls rule — neither practitioner nor patient may be offsite at the clinic (with exceptions for FQHCs and FQHC-sponsored School-Based Health Centers)
Outpatient Mental Health Centers (OMHCs) may submit claims for telehealth services when both practitioner and patient are offsite, effective June 1, 2025 (CMS approval received May 19, 2025)
This exception does not apply to FQHCs or FQHC-sponsored School-Based Health Centers for other four walls provisions
Services must meet 42 C.F.R. §440.90(a) requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Providers must be enrolled in Maryland Medicaid. Reimbursement is obtained by submitting claims per fee-for-service billing guidelines through the standard billing process, using the appropriate modifier ('GT' for audio-visual or 'UB' for audio-only). Consult the Maryland Medicaid Telehealth Program Policy Guide and provider-specific COMAR chapters for coverage details. Contact the telehealth team for questions: mdh.mabehavioralhealth@maryland.gov (behavioral health), mdh.professionalservicespolicy@maryland.gov (acute care), or mdh.medicaidtelehealth@maryland.gov (telehealth billing and policies).

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Overdose Response Program (ORP) – Free Naloxone, Fentanyl Test Strips, and Xylazine Test Strips
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) Center for Harm Reduction Services authorizes governmental agencies and community-based organizations as Overdose Response Programs (ORPs). Once authorized, organizations can provide overdose education and dispense naloxone (Narcan®), fentanyl test strips, xylazine test strips, benzodiazepine test strips, and medetomidine test strips to people at risk of opioid overdose, through a partnership with a licensed prescriber (Licensed Health Care Provider, LHCP). Approved organizations receive an ORP certificate, a ship point setup, access to naloxone supplies through MMCAP (a purchasing cooperative), and an online orientation, allowing staff without prescribing authority to distribute naloxone under the LHCP's standing order. Non-profits that are 501(c)(3) certified may also ship naloxone directly to residential addresses. Supplies are distributed in person at local ORPs located across the state through fixed sites, vending machines, and mobile outreach, or by mail in select counties. Additional harm reduction services vary by location and may include HCV and HIV testing, HIV PrEP and PEP, medication for opioid use disorder (MOUD), syringe services and disposal, wound care, personal care kits, housing and food access referrals, substance use disorder counseling and treatment, reproductive health services, RAD (Rapid Analysis of Drugs) testing, and telehealth. Naloxone is also available at pharmacies under a statewide standing order without a prescription, though it is not free at pharmacies. No prescription or proof of certification or training is required for individuals to receive supplies from an ORP. Maryland residents can find a local ORP through an interactive map or PDF list on the program page.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MDH grants organizational authorization to dispense naloxone and provides free naloxone (Narcan®/opioid overdose reversal medication), fentanyl test strips, xylazine test strips, benzodiazepine test strips, and medetomidine test strips at no cost through local Overdose Response Programs, either in person (at fixed sites, vending machines, or mobile outreach) or by mail in certain counties. Naloxone is dispensed in two doses per kit, available in intranasal spray (3mg, 4mg, or 8mg) or intramuscular injection (0.4mg/mL) formulations, with ancillary supplies including gloves, rescue breathing shields, alcohol swabs, syringes, and needles where available. Approved organizations receive an ORP certificate, a ship point setup, access to naloxone supplies through MMCAP (a purchasing cooperative), and an online orientation. This allows staff without prescribing authority to distribute naloxone under a Licensed Health Care Provider's standing order. Non-profits that are 501(c)(3) certified may also ship naloxone directly to residential addresses. Additional harm reduction services vary by location and may include overdose education, HCV and HIV testing, HIV PrEP and PEP, medication for opioid use disorder (MOUD), syringe services and disposal, wound care, personal care kits, housing and food access referrals, substance use disorder counseling and treatment, reproductive health services, RAD (Rapid Analysis of Drugs) testing, case management, and telehealth. Naloxone is additionally available at pharmacies without a prescription under a statewide standing order, though it is not free at pharmacies. No prescription or proof of certification or training is required for individuals to receive supplies from an ORP.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents seeking free naloxone, fentanyl test strips, xylazine test strips, or other harm reduction supplies for overdose prevention and response; and governmental agencies and community-based organizations seeking to provide overdose education and distribute naloxone to the public in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Obtaining free naloxone for opioid overdose reversal; fentanyl test strips, xylazine test strips, benzodiazepine test strips, and medetomidine test strips for drug supply testing and overdose prevention; overdose education and free naloxone distribution to community members; dispensing naloxone (Narcan) to individuals at risk of opioid overdose; additional harm reduction services including HCV/HIV testing, wound care, syringe services, housing and food access referrals, and substance use disorder counseling and treatment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland through local Overdose Response Programs at fixed sites, vending machines, and mobile outreach; mail delivery of naloxone is available only in certain Maryland counties.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident (for individuals seeking supplies)
No prescription required (for individuals)
No proof of certification or training required (for individuals)
Mail delivery limited to residents in certain Maryland counties
Must be a governmental agency or community-based organization (to become an authorized ORP)
Must partner with a nurse practitioner or doctor (Licensed Health Care Provider, LHCP) with prescribing authority
Must complete and submit an ORP application
Must prepare a Standing Order signed by the LHCP (valid for two years from date of signing)
Must prepare an LHCP Agreement signed by the LHCP
Must prepare a Dispensing Protocol
To ship naloxone to a residential address: must also provide 501(c)(3) documentation and an MMCAP waiver
Must attend an online ORP orientation before ordering naloxone
Must set up a ship point before ordering naloxone
Organizations must apply to be authorized as an Overdose Response Program by the MDH BHA Office of Harm Reduction
Must designate personnel responsible for ordering, receiving, and monitoring naloxone inventory
Naloxone must be stored in original packaging at room temperature (59-86°F)
Each naloxone kit must contain two doses
Dispensing records must be maintained for a minimum of five (5) years
Monthly reporting required via ORP Training Report webform
Naloxone must be labeled with: ORP name/address, date dispensed, prescriber name, and standing order prescription date
Organizations must report naloxone administration incidents via Naloxone Use Report form
Written agreement between authorized entity and licensed health care provider with prescribing authority required
Training protocols for employees and/or volunteers required
Supervision procedures by licensed health care provider required
MMCAP Infuse members must provide Tennessen Warning to affected individuals before submitting private data
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individuals: Find a local Overdose Response Program using the interactive map or PDF list on the program page (http://health.maryland.gov/pha/NALOXONE/Documents/Maryland-ORPs.pdf). Visit in person or contact the ORP to ask about mail delivery if available in your county. For pharmacy access, no prescription is needed under the statewide standing order. Organizations: 1. Complete the online ORP Application at the CognitoForms link provided. 2. Identify a Licensed Health Care Provider (LHCP) — a nurse practitioner or doctor with prescribing authority — who will sign the Standing Order and LHCP Agreement. 3. Prepare and attach supporting documents (Standing Order, LHCP Agreement, Dispensing Protocol, and if applicable, 501(c)(3) documentation and MMCAP waiver). 4. Enter into a written agreement with the LHCP, designate an ORP Training Director, and establish dispensing protocols and training procedures. 5. Submit the application; MDH will review and email your ORP certificate upon approval. 6. MDH will contact you to set up a ship point and schedule an online ORP orientation before naloxone can be ordered. For more information on becoming an ORP, visit http://health.maryland.gov/pha/NALOXONE.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides competitive grants for pediatric cancer research to physicians, hospitals, laboratories, educational institutions, and other organizations and individuals. The Maryland Pediatric Cancer Research Commission oversees the award of grants from the Fund, developing criteria, standards, and requirements for applicants, and reviewing, evaluating, ranking, and rating proposals according to established procedures and guidelines. Grant recipients are subject to oversight standards and progress reviews.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Physicians, hospitals, laboratories, educational institutions, and other organizations and individuals conducting pediatric cancer research.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Pediatric cancer research.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — program is administered by the Maryland Department of Health.
requirements_list: Applicants must submit a complete application that satisfies the criteria, standards, and requirements developed by the Commission.
Applications are subject to review, evaluation, ranking, and rating under Commission-established procedures.
Grant recipients are subject to oversight standards and progress reviews.

The Commission reviews applications for completeness and compliance with eligibility criteria. Contact Sadie Peters at sadie.peters@maryland.gov at the Maryland Department of Health for more information.

Many of these individuals have experienced trauma such as war, torture, or prolonged family separation.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Mental health counseling and support services.
