structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland STOP Act (Statewide Targeted Overdose Prevention Act) of 2022 — Naloxone Distribution Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The STOP Act encourages certain types of providers to offer naloxone/Opioid Overdose Reversal Drugs (OORDs) to people likely to witness or experience an overdose. Goals include placing more naloxone in the hands of people at highest risk, supporting organizational change for providers to routinely offer naloxone, and sustaining funding for naloxone. Covered organizations include homeless services programs, correctional facilities, parole and probation offices, opioid treatment programs, intensive outpatient programs, EMS providers, and hospitals. The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) purchases and provides naloxone to these identified organizations to support compliance. EMS providers are also authorized to dispense take-home naloxone to patients treated for nonfatal overdose or evaluated by a crisis evaluation team. Businesses also receive improved liability protections when they make naloxone available to employees or patrons. Over 200,000 naloxone doses have been distributed statewide in a single year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MDH purchases and provides naloxone (Narcan) or another FDA-approved opioid overdose reversal drug (OORD) free of charge to identified organizations, including homeless services programs, correctional facilities, the Division of Parole and Probation, intensive outpatient programs, opioid treatment programs, hospitals, and EMS providers. Free naloxone/OORDs are offered directly to eligible individuals at no cost, including paraphernalia needed for administration. Over 200,000 doses have been distributed annually statewide. Organizations must have a protocol to offer the drug free of charge to eligible individuals they serve. EMS providers are also authorized to dispense take-home naloxone to patients treated for nonfatal overdose or evaluated by a crisis team. Businesses also receive improved liability protections when they make naloxone available to employees or patrons.
structured_extraction.program_audience: People at highest risk of overdose, people who use drugs, family members of people who use drugs, and patients treated for substance use disorder, opioid use disorder, or nonfatal drug overdose. Served through homeless services programs, state and local correctional facilities, the Division of Parole and Probation, intensive outpatient treatment programs (IOPs), opioid treatment programs (OTPs), hospitals, EMS providers, and businesses in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Distribution of free naloxone and opioid overdose reversal drugs (including paraphernalia needed for administration) to individuals at risk of overdose, including those with opioid use disorder, substance use disorder, or a history of nonfatal drug overdose.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to all identified organizations under the STOP Act.
requirements_list: Homeless services programs must offer free naloxone to individuals with opioid use disorder or at risk of drug overdose (protocol required by June 30, 2024).
State and local correctional facilities must offer free naloxone to sentenced individuals before release who have opioid use disorder or are at risk of overdose (protocol required by June 30, 2024).
Division of Parole and Probation must offer free naloxone to individuals under supervision with opioid use disorder or at risk of overdose (protocol required by June 30, 2024).
Intensive outpatient programs must offer free naloxone to all individuals receiving services (protocol required by June 30, 2023).
Opioid treatment programs must offer free naloxone to all individuals receiving services (protocol required by June 30, 2023).
Hospitals must directly offer free naloxone before discharge to patients treated for substance use disorder, opioid use disorder, or nonfatal drug overdose (protocol required by June 30, 2023).
EMS providers are authorized to dispense take-home naloxone to patients treated for nonfatal overdose or evaluated by a crisis team (effective July 1, 2022).
Organizations must become an Overdose Response Program (ORP) authorized by MDH to dispense naloxone to the community.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations must become an Overdose Response Program (ORP) authorized by MDH. Visit the 'How to Become an ORP' page on the MDH website to learn the steps. MDH will then purchase and provide naloxone to the organization.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland School-Based Health Center Program supports clinics physically located on school campuses that provide comprehensive primary, acute, and preventive health services — including chronic condition management — to students, families, and communities. There are currently 91 active school-based health centers across 16 jurisdictions in Maryland. The program aims to increase access to health services in underserved communities and improve student health and educational outcomes. Organizations interested in opening new school-based health centers can apply to join the program, receiving tailored support and guidance through the application process. Applications for new centers are typically accepted in July and November.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Organizations interested in opening a new school-based health center can apply to join the Maryland School-Based Health Center Program. Applications for new centers are typically accepted in July and November. The program provides support and tailored guidance to help eligible organizations establish and operate school-based health centers. Specific financial assistance amounts are not stated on the program page.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications are typically accepted in July and November
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations interested in opening or operating a new school-based health center on a school campus in Maryland, serving students, families, and communities — especially in underserved areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Establishing and operating school-based health centers that provide primary, acute, and preventive health services — including chronic condition management — to students, families, and communities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland; currently 91 active centers across 16 jurisdictions.
requirements_list: Center must be physically located on a school campus
Applicant must be an organization interested in opening a new school-based health center on a school campus (type may vary — non-profit, for-profit, government, or other)
Applicants should collaborate with local stakeholders
Building structure of the desired site is a factor
Type of organization applying is a factor
Application must be submitted during open application windows (typically July and November)
Contact program before applying for tailored guidance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Email [email protected] for further information and tailored support before or during the application process. Applications for new school-based health centers are typically accepted in July and November. The process varies depending on the type of organization applying, the extent of local stakeholder collaboration, and the building structure of the desired site.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free phone, text, and web-based tobacco cessation program that helps Maryland residents age 13 and older quit any form of tobacco, including cigarettes and vaping. Trained quit coaches provide confidential one-on-one counseling, personalized quit plans, follow-up support, and free nicotine replacement therapy (NRT) such as patches or gum while supplies last. Available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. Teens aged 13–17 can also access the Live Vape Free program for additional vaping cessation support via text or online, including podcasts, videos, and live coach chats, as well as five free, private counseling calls delivered by specially trained youth coaches who discuss triggers, stressors, peer influences, and secondhand smoke exposure. Intensive multi-call coaching programs are also available for pregnant women. Healthcare providers can refer patients via Fax to Assist or email, and free training is available for healthcare providers. Educational materials can be mailed to participants upon request. The Quitline may also refer participants to local health departments for in-person cessation classes or counseling.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free, confidential tobacco cessation coaching delivered 24/7 by phone, text message, or online enrollment. Services include one-on-one counseling from trained coaches, a personalized quit plan with a quit date, follow-up support, printed and web-based self-help materials, text messaging support, and a free supply of nicotine replacement therapy (patches, gum, lozenges, inhalers, etc.) while supplies last. Teens aged 13–17 can enroll in the Live Vape Free program via text or online for podcasts, videos, and live coach chats focused on quitting vaping, as well as five free, private counseling calls with specially trained youth coaches who discuss triggers, stressors, peer influences, and secondhand smoke exposure. Intensive multi-call coaching programs are also available for pregnant women. Healthcare providers can refer patients via Fax to Assist or email, and free training is available for healthcare providers. Educational materials can be mailed to the participant's home upon request. The Quitline may also refer participants to local health departments for in-person cessation classes or counseling.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents age 13 and older who want to quit tobacco use, including cigarettes, vaping, or other tobacco products. Adults 18 and older, including those in recovery from substance use disorders, are eligible for the full suite of services including NRT. A separate track (Live Vape Free) and youth counseling track are available for teens aged 13–17. Specialized support is also available for pregnant women. Non-smokers who want to help someone else quit may also access the program. Healthcare providers can refer patients or access free provider training.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable as a traditional grant or loan. Assistance consists of free coaching, counseling, quit planning, nicotine replacement therapy (patches, gum, lozenges, inhalers), educational materials, and support services to help participants quit tobacco, as well as referrals to local resources.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to all Maryland residents age 13 and older, statewide. The Quitline may also refer participants to local health departments for in-person cessation classes or counseling.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident
Must be age 13 or older
Must want to quit tobacco use (any form)
Adults 18 and older are eligible for nicotine replacement therapy (while supplies last)
Teen and young adult track specifically serves those aged 13 to 17
Specialized intensive multi-call programs available for pregnant women
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 1-800-QUIT-NOW (1-800-784-8669), text 'READY' to 34191, or enroll online at smokingstopshere.com or quitnow.net/maryland. Coaches are available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. Teens and young adults can text VAPEFREE to 873-373 or enroll online at livevapefree.com. Healthcare providers can refer patients via the Fax to Assist program or by email.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Tobacco Quitline – New and Expectant Parents Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A free tobacco cessation service for pregnant and newly postpartum Marylanders. Trained quit coaches help participants create a personalized quit plan, discuss medication options, and provide ongoing support 24 hours a day, 7 days a week by phone, web, or text message. Pregnant participants can enroll in a specialized incentive program to receive gift cards for completing program activities while supplies last. Free informational booklets are also provided.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free quit-coaching sessions (typically 15–25 minutes) delivered by phone, web, or text message, available 24/7 in English, Spanish, and other languages. Also includes web and text message support, free informational booklets, and gift cards for participation in the specialized incentive program for pregnant participants (while supplies last).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Pregnant and newly postpartum Marylanders who use tobacco and want help quitting
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tobacco cessation support including coaching sessions, educational materials, and incentive gift cards for pregnant participants
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to all Maryland residents
requirements_list: Must be pregnant or a new/expectant parent
Must be a Maryland resident
Must enroll in the Maryland Tobacco Quitline to access coaching and support
Pregnant participants must register for the specialized incentive program during Quitline enrollment to receive gift cards
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Enroll in the Maryland Tobacco Quitline by phone, online, or text message. Pregnant participants should register for the specialized incentive program at the time of enrollment. Coaches are available 24/7 and will guide participants through a personalized quit plan.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Vaccines for Children (VFC) Program is a federally funded entitlement program administered by the Maryland Department of Health and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). It provides free vaccines to eligible children 18 years old and younger through enrolled physicians and clinics. The program is designed to remove cost as a barrier to vaccination by supplying all routinely recommended ACIP childhood vaccines (including influenza vaccine during influenza season) at no cost to enrolled providers, who then administer them to qualifying children. Eligible children include those who are Maryland Medicaid eligible, uninsured, Native American or Alaskan Native, or underinsured (health insurance does not cover immunization). The program operates a contact center with phone numbers assigned by county for providers or families to reach program staff. Participating providers also receive training on safe vaccine storage and handling, as well as updates on immunization issues and the VFC Program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Enrolled physicians and clinics receive all routinely recommended ACIP childhood vaccines (including influenza vaccine during influenza season) free of cost to administer to eligible children 18 years old and younger. There is no charge to the provider for the vaccines. Providers must offer all medically appropriate ACIP-recommended vaccines to all VFC-eligible patients. Providers also receive training on safe vaccine storage and handling, as well as updates on immunization issues and the VFC Program. Eligible children receive vaccines at no cost through these enrolled providers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Physicians, clinics, and healthcare providers (medical practices/offices with enrolled/responsible physicians) seeking to provide free vaccines to eligible children 18 years old and younger who are Maryland Medicaid eligible, uninsured, Native American or Alaskan Native, or underinsured (health insurance does not cover immunization), as well as families of eligible children across Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free childhood vaccines for eligible children 18 years old and younger, administered through enrolled provider practices and clinics. Covers vaccine procurement and distribution of all ACIP-recommended routine childhood vaccines.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland through public and private vaccine delivery sites. Contact numbers are assigned by county.
requirements_list: Provider must be a physician or clinic (medical practice/office with enrolled/responsible physician)
Provider must enroll in the VFC program by submitting a letter of interest on business letterhead to mdh.izinfo@maryland.gov
After enrollment, provider will be contacted by an assigned VFC Site Reviewer who will verify compliance before vaccine shipment
Annual educational training required for enrolled physician, practice/office contact, and backup contact
EHR/EMR system required for newly enrolled providers; vaccine administration data must be submitted to ImmuNet within 7 days
Digital data logger (DDL) with valid calibration certificate required for each vaccine storage unit plus at least one backup
Stand-alone or pharmaceutical-grade vaccine storage units required
Provider must offer all medically appropriate ACIP-recommended vaccines to all VFC-eligible patients
Provider must comply with federal law regarding vaccine documentation
Children served must be 18 years old or younger and meet at least one eligibility criterion: Maryland Medicaid eligible, uninsured, Native American or Alaskan Native, or underinsured
Site review and compliance verification required before initial vaccine shipment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested providers submit a letter of interest on business letterhead via email to mdh.izinfo@maryland.gov. The VFC program then sends completion documents via email. A site reviewer visits the practice to verify compliance with storage, training, and reporting requirements. After compliance is confirmed, an initial vaccine order is placed by VFC; subsequent orders are placed bi-monthly through the ImmuNet system. Providers or families may also contact the VFC Contact Center by phone based on county, or email the Center for Immunization for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland WIC (Women, Infants, and Children) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland WIC is a federally funded nutrition assistance program administered by the Maryland Department of Health that provides healthy supplemental foods, nutrition education, breastfeeding promotion and support, health screenings, and referrals to health and social services for eligible low-income pregnant women, postpartum women, breastfeeding women, infants, and young children under age five who live in Maryland and meet income and nutritional need guidelines. The program helps over 150,000 babies each year statewide. Participants receive supplemental nutritious foods (milk, cheese, eggs, cereal, infant formula, fruits, vegetables, dairy, and whole grains) delivered via an electronic benefits (eWIC) card, along with nutrition counseling, growth and weight health screenings, breastfeeding support from lactation specialists, and referrals to health and social services. An authorized foods list (available in Spanish, effective February 1, 2026) specifies all approved items purchasable with WIC benefits and is available at health.maryland.gov/phpa/wic/Pages/authorized_foods_list.aspx. Participants also have access to the annual WIC Farmers' Market Program. Fathers, grandparents, and guardians can also apply on behalf of a child. Benefits can be accessed through the Maryland WIC app (available on iOS and Android) or at authorized retailers through local county clinics. Participants who already receive Medicaid, Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA), or SNAP/Food Stamps are automatically income-eligible. There are no fees to participate. Program information and services are available in multiple languages including Spanish, with bilingual staff and translators available at Baltimore City WIC clinics.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: WIC provides eligible participants with supplemental nutritious foods (milk, cheese, eggs, cereal, infant formula, fruits, vegetables, dairy, and whole grains) loaded onto an electronic benefits (eWIC) card for purchase at authorized retailers, based on an authorized foods list (effective February 1, 2026, also available in Spanish; full list at health.maryland.gov/phpa/wic/Pages/authorized_foods_list.aspx). Approved foods include fruits and vegetables, dairy products, protein sources, whole grains (including whole grain bread, pita bread, oats, whole wheat pasta), 100% juices (limited to 4 oz/day), and cereals (cold cereal minimum 12 oz, hot cereal minimum 9.5 oz, low in sugar and high in iron, at least 75% whole grain; up to 36 oz of cereal can be purchased in various combinations). The program feeds more than 150,000 babies annually across Maryland. Benefits are accompanied by nutrition education and counseling, growth and weight health screenings, breastfeeding education and support from lactation specialists, referrals to healthcare providers, health departments, and community organizations, and access to the annual WIC Farmers' Market Program. Eligibility is based on income at or below 185% of the Federal Poverty Income Guidelines (ranging from $28,953 annually for a family of 1 to $100,178 for a family of 8, plus $10,175 per additional member, effective April 4, 2025); participants who already receive Medicaid, Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA), or SNAP/Food Stamps are automatically income-eligible. Foster children are also automatically income-eligible. The amount of benefits varies based on the participant's category (pregnant woman, breastfeeding mother, postpartum mother, infant, or child under age 5). Benefits can be accessed through the Maryland WIC app (available on iOS and Android) or at authorized retailers. Fathers, grandparents, and guardians can apply on behalf of a child. There are no fees to participate.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Pregnant women, postpartum women (up to 6 months after delivery), breastfeeding mothers (up to 1 year after delivery), infants, and children under age five residing in Maryland who meet income and nutritional risk requirements. Fathers, grandparents, foster parents, and other guardians can apply on behalf of a child. Those receiving Medicaid, TCA, or SNAP are automatically income-eligible. Foster children are also automatically income-eligible. Spanish-language resources and bilingual staff are also available.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of approved supplemental nutritious foods through the eWIC electronic benefits card (per the authorized foods list effective February 1, 2026), including fruits and vegetables, dairy products, protein sources, whole grains, 100% juices, and approved cereals. Nutrition education and counseling, growth and weight health screenings, breastfeeding promotion and support from lactation specialists, access to the annual WIC Farmers' Market Program, and referrals to health and social services and community organizations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must reside in Maryland. Program is available statewide in all Maryland counties and Baltimore City through local WIC agencies. In Baltimore City, services are delivered through Baltimore City WIC clinic locations. In Prince George's County, six WIC clinic locations are available: Andrews AFB, Cheverly, Central Ave (Landover), Clinton, Hyattsville, and Laurel.
requirements_list: Must live in Maryland

Must be a pregnant woman, postpartum woman (up to 6 months after delivery), breastfeeding mother (up to 1 year after delivery), infant, or child under age 5, or a caregiver applying on behalf of such a child
Fathers, grandparents, and guardians can apply on behalf of a child

Must meet income eligibility requirements (at or below 185% of the Federal Poverty Income Guidelines based on family size, ranging from $28,953 annually for a family of 1 to $100,178 for a family of 8, plus $10,175 per additional member, effective April 4, 2025), or participate in Medicaid, Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA), or SNAP/Food Stamps (automatic income eligibility)
Foster children are automatically income-eligible
Must be determined to be at nutritional risk by a health professional or trained WIC staff
Must have a nutritional need

Must bring proof of household income (pay stubs, benefit letter, Medical Assistance card, Independence Card with receipt, or tax return; also accepted: SSI/Social Security/unemployment benefit letter, SNAP/EBT card with recent receipt, or prior year W-2)
Must bring proof of identity for each person applying (birth certificate, driver's license, Social Security card, or government/school/employment photo ID)
Must bring proof of address (driver's license, official bill or statement, or rental/lease agreement)
Must bring all persons applying for benefits to the first appointment
If applicable: proof of pregnancy, immunization record for infant or child, WIC referral form
Must provide required documentation at time of application
Participants must purchase only WIC-approved foods and may not sell, trade, or give away WIC benefits or food
Participants may not return WIC foods to stores for refunds or store credit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the local WIC agency in your county by calling 1-800-242-4942 or through the online Client Portal (wicclientportal.health.maryland.gov) to discuss eligibility, find the closest WIC office, and schedule a certification appointment. You may also email [email protected] or download the Maryland WIC app (available on iOS and Android) to begin the application process. Existing MD WIC Mobile App users can log in with existing credentials. In Baltimore City, call the WIC appointment line at (410) 396-9427 to schedule an appointment at a Baltimore City WIC clinic location near you; bilingual staff and translators are available. In Prince George's County, visit one of six WIC locations (Andrews AFB, Cheverly, Central Ave/Landover, Clinton, Hyattsville, or Laurel) during business hours (Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.). WIC staff will determine nutritional risk during the certification visit. Bring all persons applying for benefits to the first appointment along with required documents: proof of household income, proof of identity for each person, and proof of address. Additional documents such as proof of pregnancy, vaccination records, or a WIC referral form may also be required. Program information is available in multiple languages including Spanish and alternative formats for persons with disabilities.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland WIC (Women, Infants, and Children) Program offers interactive training classes for authorized WIC vendors and their staff. Classes are designed to help stores, pharmacies, and other retailers successfully participate in the WIC Program by covering WIC program policies and procedures, authorized foods, transaction requirements, and updates including changes to the Authorized Foods List. Vendors are required to attend at least one state or local interactive training session each calendar year, and must designate a WIC trainer to train all staff involved in WIC transactions on program policies and procedures.
eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free interactive training sessions offered at the state or local agency level to authorized WIC vendors. Training covers WIC program policies, procedures, authorized foods, transaction requirements, and updates including changes to the Authorized Foods List. Vendors must attend at least one interactive training session per calendar year. Each vendor must designate at least one person as the WIC trainer, who is responsible for training all cashiers, pharmacy cashiers, and other staff involved in WIC transactions, and for promptly informing employees of any program changes.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Authorized WIC vendors, including grocery stores, pharmacies, and other retailers that accept WIC benefits in Maryland, and their staff involved in WIC transactions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training on WIC program policies, procedures, authorized food lists, transaction requirements, and updates including changes to the Authorized Foods List.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to authorized WIC vendors operating throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be an authorized WIC vendor
At least one representative must attend and participate in at least one state or local agency interactive training session each calendar year
Must designate at least one person to serve as the designated WIC trainer
Designated WIC trainer must train all cashiers, pharmacy cashiers, and other staff involved in WIC transactions
Vendor or designated trainer must promptly inform employees of changes to the WIC Program, including the Authorized Foods List
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Authorized vendors must attend at least one state or local agency interactive training session per calendar year. Designated trainers then train store staff on WIC policies and procedures. Vendors should contact the Maryland WIC Program to register for available training classes. A variety of training classes are offered for vendors.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Commitment to Veterans (MCV) provides care coordination, peer support, and referral services for US uniformed service members, veterans, and their families in Maryland. The program also offers educational opportunities and fosters collaboration with behavioral health and medical providers, peers, first responders, and community partners. Services include suicide prevention initiatives, lethal means safety and safety planning, housing stability support for veterans experiencing or at risk of homelessness, and Supportive Services for Veteran Families (SSVF). Services are available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, and are accessible regardless of discharge status. The program coordinates with national, state, and local organizations to help service members, veterans, and their families access wellness and recovery support at no cost.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides care coordination, peer support, and referral services at no cost. Services are available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week by calling 1-877-770-4801. Connects service members, veterans, and their families to behavioral health, medical, and other wellness services regardless of discharge status. Additional services include suicide prevention programs (Lethal Means Safety and Safety Planning, Governor's Challenge to Prevent Suicide), Supportive Services for Veteran Families (SSVF), Psychiatric Rehabilitation Programs (PRPs), and housing stability support. The program coordinates with national, state, and local organizations to help eligible individuals access wellness and recovery support, as well as educational opportunities.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Jeff Nash (Program Manager); Hannah Rodriguez (SMVF Suicide Prevention Administrator)
structured_extraction.program_audience: US uniformed service members (Active Duty, Guard, and Reserve), veterans, and their families seeking behavioral health and wellness services in Maryland, regardless of discharge status. Also serves veterans experiencing or at risk of homelessness and transitioning service members.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Access to care coordination, peer support, referrals to behavioral health and medical services, connection to behavioral health and wellness resources, educational opportunities, recovery support, suicide prevention services, lethal means safety education, safety planning, housing stability support, and Supportive Services for Veteran Families (SSVF) for service members, veterans, and their families.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to all eligible service members, veterans, and their families regardless of discharge status. Regional coordinators serve the Eastern Shore, Southern, Central, and Western regions of Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a current or former US uniformed service member (Active Duty, Guard, or Reserve), or a family member of such a person
Must be seeking wellness or behavioral health services in Maryland
No restriction based on discharge status
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 1-877-770-4801 (available 24/7) or email bha.mcv@maryland.gov to connect to services. No formal application required.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maternal, Infant and Early Childhood Home Visiting Program (MIECHV)
structured_extraction.program_description: A federally funded grant program administered by the Maryland Department of Health that supports evidence-based home visiting services for pregnant women, infants, and young children. Home visitors—trained professionals or nurses—provide free, voluntary, in-home visits offering education and support tailored to each family's needs, covering child growth and development, parenting skills, self-care, community resources, nutrition, future planning, and mental health and stress management. The program helps families strengthen attachment, promote optimal child development, ensure child safety, and reduce the risk of child maltreatment. MIECHV funds evidence-based home visiting models delivered by local organizations, and also produces newsletters and continuous quality improvement resources for home visiting practitioners. Services are free and available statewide to pregnant people and new parents, with prioritization for communities identified as having the highest need based on a statewide needs assessment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal MIECHV grant funding (formula grant and other financial assistance) distributed to states, territories, and tribal entities to support evidence-based home visiting programs and services for eligible families across Maryland. Up to 25% of funding can be allocated for 'promising' home visiting models that are rigorously evaluated. Direct services include free home visits by trained professionals or nurses covering child development, parenting skills, self-care, community resources, diet and nutrition, future planning, and mental health and stress management. The program also provides technical assistance, services, and continuous quality improvement resources for home visiting practitioners. Specific award amounts and terms vary.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Pregnant individuals and people who recently gave birth in Maryland who need support for a healthy pregnancy and healthy child development, as well as county governments, non-profits, and other organizations delivering home visiting services to pregnant women, infants, and young children in Maryland, particularly those in at-risk communities, and home visiting program providers and practitioners.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supporting evidence-based home visiting services to improve maternal and child health, child development, and family well-being for pregnant women, infants, and early childhood populations, including in-home education and support covering child growth and development, parenting skills, self-care, community resources, diet and nutrition, future planning, and mental health and stress management. Funds also support strengthening family bonds, promoting child safety, and reducing the risk of child maltreatment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland, but prioritizes funding for communities identified as having the highest risk based on a statewide needs assessment.
requirements_list: Must be pregnant or have recently given birth (for families seeking direct services)
Services are free and voluntary
Referral through a Maryland Family Planning Program clinic or other health provider may be an entry point
Grants may only support evidence-based home visiting programs that meet specific federal criteria
Up to 25% of funding can be allocated for 'promising' home visiting models, which must be rigorously evaluated
Must be eligible based on program criteria (specific eligibility details available on the home visiting program page)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations interested in MIECHV grant funding should contact the MIECHV team by email at [email protected] for more information. Families seeking direct home visiting services should visit the Maryland Home Visiting Services page on the Maryland Department of Health website for eligibility information and how to connect with services. Referral through a Maryland Family Planning Program clinic or other health provider may also be an entry point. Grant funding is awarded annually on a varying schedule.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Medicaid offers an enhanced payment to qualified CenteringPregnancy practices that provide group prenatal care services to Medicaid members. CenteringPregnancy is an evidence-based, patient-centered framework that replaces individual prenatal appointments with group appointments of 8-10 participants of similar gestational age, consisting of ten 90-120 minute interactive group perinatal care visits covering medical and non-medical aspects of pregnancy including nutrition, common discomforts, stress management, labor and birth, breastfeeding, and infant care. Eligible practices must complete provider enrollment steps before billing for the enhanced payment, which became effective January 1, 2023. Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs) are also eligible for enhanced payments under a separate transmittal issued in November 2023. Guidance is published in the Professional Services Provider Manual.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Qualified CenteringPregnancy practices receive an enhanced (higher) payment rate of an additional $50 per participant per visit for up to ten group prenatal care visits (billed using CPT code 99078 with modifier -TH) when billing for group prenatal care services through Maryland Medicaid, effective January 1, 2023. Individual care codes (99212, 99213) can be billed in addition to the group care code. FQHCs are eligible to implement CenteringPregnancy and HealthySteps models but are not eligible to bill for enhanced payments due to Prospective Payment System constraints. A HealthySteps enhanced payment of $15 per participant per visit up to age four (code H0025) is also available for pediatric primary care practices.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Healthcare providers and practices that offer CenteringPregnancy group prenatal care services and are enrolled in Maryland Medicaid, including OBGYN, Pediatric, and Family Medicine practices, nurse practitioners, nurse midwives, Managed Care Organizations, and FQHCs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Enhanced reimbursement payments for providing CenteringPregnancy group prenatal care services to Medicaid-enrolled patients, and HealthySteps pediatric primary care services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to Maryland Medicaid-enrolled providers.
requirements_list: Practice must be a qualified CenteringPregnancy provider accredited or pending accreditation by Centering Healthcare Institute (CHI)
Must complete provider enrollment steps before billing for the enhanced payment
Must upload a supplemental application through the ePREP portal for both group and each rendering provider
Must submit CHI approval letter attesting to accreditation status
Must submit CenteringPregnancy Addendum
Must follow guidance in the Maryland Medical Assistance Program Professional Services Provider Manual
FQHCs must enroll through the Maryland Medicaid Maternal Child Health Programs webpage; no ePREP action required for billing purposes
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible practices must complete provider enrollment by uploading supplemental applications through the ePREP portal for both the group and each rendering provider, including a CHI approval letter and CenteringPregnancy Addendum. Once enrolled, providers can bill for the enhanced payment per guidance in the Professional Services Provider Manual and published transmittals. FQHCs should refer to the Maryland Medicaid Maternal Child Health Programs webpage for enrollment information. Detailed guidance is available through the Provider Enrollment page and ePREP materials provided on the program page.

structured_extraction.program_description: CenteringPregnancy is a group-based prenatal and postpartum/postnatal care program for Maryland Medicaid members. Pregnant members meet regularly in groups of 8 to 10 people who share similar due dates. Each session lasts 90 minutes to two hours and includes a one-on-one exam with a provider along with group education and peer support. Sessions cover topics such as labor and delivery, breastfeeding, baby care, stress management, and healthy eating. The program is provided at no cost to eligible participants.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free group prenatal and postnatal care sessions for eligible Maryland Medicaid members. Each visit lasts 90 minutes to two hours and includes a provider exam and group sessions covering pregnancy health topics such as labor and delivery preparation, breastfeeding, baby care, stress management, and nutrition. The program is provided at no cost to eligible participants.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Pregnant individuals who are enrolled in Maryland Medicaid (HealthChoice managed care)
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Group-based prenatal and postnatal care including provider exams, health education, and peer support covering pregnancy health, labor and delivery preparation, breastfeeding, baby care, stress management, and nutrition before and after birth
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to Maryland Medicaid members through their Medicaid Managed Care Organization (MCO)
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland Medicaid member
Must be pregnant
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call your Medicaid Managed Care Organization (MCO) using the number on your insurance card. They will help you find a CenteringPregnancy provider near you.

structured_extraction.program_name: Medicaid Family Planning Program (Income-Based Limited Benefits)
structured_extraction.program_description: A free, income-based, limited-benefits health plan for Maryland residents who do not qualify for full Medicaid coverage. The program covers family planning services including birth control, STI screening, cervical and breast cancer screening, HPV vaccine, and sterilization procedures for eligible individuals. It is not full health care coverage and has no premiums, deductibles, or copays. The program does not cover prenatal care, infertility services, or non-emergency medical transportation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free family planning services with no premiums, deductibles, or copays. Covers exams and birth control counseling, prescription and over-the-counter birth control, IUDs, implants, emergency contraception, STI/hepatitis/HIV screening, cervical and breast cancer screening and diagnosis, and HPV vaccine. Sterilization (tubal ligation or vasectomy) is available for those 21 and older. Does not cover prenatal care, infertility services, or non-emergency medical transportation. Eligible members can use any Medicaid Family Planning Program provider.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents of all ages who are not eligible for full Medicaid, Medicare, or other Medicaid programs, meet income limits, are U.S. citizens or qualified non-citizens, and have not been sterilized or are not currently pregnant.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Family planning services including birth control (prescription, over-the-counter, IUD, implant, emergency contraception), STI and HIV screening, cervical and breast cancer screening and diagnosis, HPV vaccine, and sterilization procedures for eligible individuals aged 21 and older.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Maryland resident.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident
Must be a U.S. citizen or a qualified non-citizen
Must meet the income limit for the Family Planning program
Must not have or be eligible for full Medicaid coverage or another Medicaid program
Must not have Medicare
Must not have previously been sterilized (tubes tied or vasectomy)
Must not be currently pregnant
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply at any time online or by contacting Maryland Health Connection. If eligible, coverage can start right away. Call Maryland Health Connection at 1-855-642-8572 for questions about eligibility or your application.

structured_extraction.program_description: HealthySteps adds a child development specialist to a child's pediatric care team to support healthy growth and development during the first three years of life. The program provides developmental screenings, parenting resources, breastfeeding support, mental health and stress guidance, and connections to additional services such as housing and transportation. Available at no cost to eligible Maryland Medicaid members with children from birth to their 4th birthday.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free child development support services provided through a HealthySteps Specialist embedded in a child's pediatric care team. Services include developmental tracking and screenings, parenting resources, breastfeeding support, mental health and stress guidance, and referrals to community resources such as housing and transportation. There is no cost to eligible Medicaid members with children from newborn up to (but not including) their 4th birthday.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland Medicaid members with children from newborn to age 3 (before their 4th birthday)
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Child development screenings, parenting support, breastfeeding guidance, mental health and stress resources, and referrals to housing, transportation, and other community and family services
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to Medicaid members
requirements_list: Child must be a Maryland Medicaid member
Child must be newborn up to (but not including) their 4th birthday
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call your Medicaid Managed Care Organization (MCO) using the number on your insurance card and ask about finding a HealthySteps provider. Your MCO will help you locate a participating pediatrician. You can also speak directly with your child's pediatrician about the program.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Medicaid's HealthySteps program provides an enhanced payment to qualified pediatric practices that integrate developmental and behavioral health support into primary care visits for young children enrolled in Medicaid. Eligible practices can bill for enhanced billing code H0025 on pediatric E&M or well-child visit encounters that include HealthySteps services in clinic or outpatient settings. Practices must complete provider enrollment steps through the ePREP portal before billing. Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs) are also eligible to implement the program, though they cannot bill for enhanced payments due to Prospective Payment System restrictions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Enhanced billing code H0025 applied to pediatric E&M or well-child visit encounters that include HealthySteps services in clinic or outpatient settings. Provides a flat rate payment to cover all tiers of HealthySteps care. Practices must complete provider enrollment steps through the ePREP portal by submitting the ePREP Supplemental Application before billing. Eligible provider types include physician groups (PT 20), nurse practitioner groups (PT 23), and physician assistant groups (PT 80), as well as individual rendering providers. FQHCs administering HealthySteps do not need to take action in the ePREP system but cannot bill for the enhanced payment due to Prospective Payment System restrictions.

structured_extraction.program_description: Medicare Savings Programs (also called Medicare Buy-In Programs) help protect low-income Medicare beneficiaries from the costs of Medicare coverage by paying Medicare Part A (Hospital Insurance) and Part B (Medical Insurance) premiums, as well as out-of-pocket expenses such as deductibles, coinsurance, and copayments, depending on the specific program. The four programs are: Qualified Medicare Beneficiary (QMB), which pays full Medicare Part B premiums and cost-sharing amounts (co-pays and deductibles) for individuals with income at or below 100% of the federal poverty level; Specified Low-Income Medicare Beneficiary (SLMB), which pays only the Medicare Part B premium for those with income between 100% and 120% of the federal poverty level; Qualifying Individual (QI/SLMB II); and Qualifying Disabled & Working Individuals (QDWI). Asset limits apply: up to $9,090 per individual or $13,630 per couple for QMB, SLMB, and QI; $4,000 per individual or $6,000 per couple for QDWI. Applications can be submitted at a local Department of Social Services office, local health department, or by downloading the QMB/SLMB/MSP application form. When you apply, eligibility workers determine which of the four programs you qualify for based on income and assets.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Depending on the program: QMB pays full Medicare Part B premiums and cost-sharing amounts (deductibles and co-payments) for individuals with income at or below 100% of the federal poverty level and assets up to $9,090 (individual) or $13,630 (couple). SLMB pays only the Medicare Part B premium for those with income between 100% and 120% of the federal poverty level and the same asset limits. QI/SLMB II provides additional premium assistance. QDWI provides premium assistance with lower asset limits ($4,000 individual/$6,000 couple). All programs pay at minimum the Medicare Part A and/or Part B premiums for qualifying individuals. When you apply, the program determines which of the four sub-programs you qualify for based on income and assets.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents who are Medicare beneficiaries with limited income and modest assets, including low-income individuals and married couples enrolled in Medicare Part A and/or Part B who need help covering Medicare premiums and cost-sharing expenses. Eligible populations include aged, blind, and disabled individuals, refugees, and U.S. citizens or lawfully admitted aliens who are Maryland residents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment of Medicare Part A and/or Part B premiums, and potentially Part A and Part B deductibles, coinsurance, and copayments depending on the specific sub-program for which the applicant qualifies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland; applicants must be Maryland residents and apply through their local department of social services or local health department in their county of residence.
requirements_list: Must be a Medicare beneficiary (enrolled in Medicare Part A and/or Part B)
Must be a Maryland resident
Must be a U.S. citizen or lawfully admitted alien
Income must be below the applicable program income limits (limits vary by program tier)
Assets must be below the program's limits
QMB: combined income must not exceed 100% of the federal poverty level; assets up to $9,090 per individual or $13,630 per couple
SLMB: income between 100% and 120% of the federal poverty level; assets up to $9,090 per individual or $13,630 per couple
QDWI: asset limits of $4,000 per individual or $6,000 per couple
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply in person or by mail at your local Department of Social Services office or local health department. Download the current application form (QMB/SLMB/MSP Application) from the Maryland Department of Human Services website at https://dhs.maryland.gov/documents/Public Assistance/9705-DHS-QMB-SLMB-MSP-Application-Revised-February-2022-1.pdf. When you apply, eligibility workers determine which of the four Medicare Savings Programs you qualify for based on your income and assets. State Health Insurance Assistance Program (SHIP) Coordinators are also available to assist applicants.

structured_extraction.program_description: MOTA is a chronic disease prevention program that funds organizations to provide community-based education and health promotion interventions to reduce health inequity. It targets racial and ethnic minority communities and other underserved populations through community engagement, partnerships, outreach, technical assistance, and ongoing intervention. Focus areas include asthma, cardiovascular disease, cancer, obesity, diabetes/prediabetes, pregnancy and birth outcomes, and mental health and substance use disorders. Awards range from $25,000 to $75,000, with up to 18 awards anticipated for the one-year funding period (July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027). FY27 grantees may be considered for optional non-competitive continuation funding in FY28 based on satisfactory Year 1 performance, with MHHD monitoring through narrative reports, performance measures, and data collection.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant funding (cooperative agreement model) for organizations providing chronic disease prevention, education, outreach, and linkage-to-care services. Awards range from $25,000 to $75,000, with up to 18 awards anticipated. Funding covers a one-year period (July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027) with an optional non-competitive one-year renewal contingent on satisfactory performance. Grants are reimbursement-based with quarterly invoicing. Eligible costs include personnel (salary and fringe), consultants, travel, contractual services, supplies, and operating costs. MHHD monitors grantees through narrative reports, performance measures, and data collection throughout the funding period.

structured_extraction.program_description: Money Follows the Person (MFP) is a Medicaid program that helps eligible individuals who live in nursing homes or intermediate care facilities move into the community — such as a home, apartment, or small group home with four or fewer people. The program enhances outreach efforts and increases public awareness through options counseling for individuals who want to return to or remain in the community. A support team, including a peer mentor, helps participants find housing, care, and services needed to live independently and transition successfully from institutional settings to community-based living. The program also supports nursing home residents who want to transition to assisted living facilities by providing access to community-based services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Medicaid long-term care services and supports follow the individual from a nursing home or intermediate care facility for individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities into the community. A team with a peer mentor helps the person find housing, care, and services needed to transition to and live independently in a home, apartment, or group home of four or fewer people. Options counseling and transition assistance are provided to help individuals move from institutional or nursing facility settings back to community living, including apartments, private homes, or small group settings. Transition support and access to community-based services are also provided for nursing home residents moving back into the community or an assisted living facility.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Medicaid-eligible individuals who have lived at least 60 consecutive days in a nursing home or intermediate care facility for individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities and wish to move into the community, as well as nursing home residents who want to transition back to community living or assisted living. Also serves individuals residing in a Maryland institutional or nursing facility setting who wish to transition back to community living.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Long-term care services and supports to help individuals transition from institutional settings to community-based housing such as homes, apartments, or small group homes, including help finding housing and needed care services. Also provides options counseling and transition support to community living, including transitions to assisted living facilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland, including Baltimore City. Must reside in Maryland in an institutional setting receiving long-term care.

Meet the income and asset guidelines for the waiver programs

structured_extraction.program_description: The Pay-For-Performance (P4P) program awards Maryland Medicaid nursing facilities that perform highly on specific quality indicators. Each year, one percent of the program's total nursing facility Medicaid budget is distributed to eligible facilities — 85 percent goes to top-scoring facilities and 15 percent to facilities showing the most improvement over the prior year that did not qualify for the top tier. Scores are based on staffing levels (up to 20 points), staff stability (up to 15 points), MDS quality indicators for long-stay residents (up to 30 points), family satisfaction survey results (up to 30 points), and staff immunization rates (up to 5 points).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual performance-based award equal to one percent of the program's nursing facility Medicaid budget, calculated as a per diem rate ($/MA Day) multiplied by total Medicaid days based on facility performance and improvement scores. Facilities with the highest scores receive 85 percent of the total award pool (Pay-for-Performance/P4P); facilities that did not qualify for the top tier but showed the greatest improvement from the prior year receive the remaining 15 percent (Pay-for-Improvement/P4I). Award amounts vary based on facility scores across staffing levels (up to 20 points), staff stability (up to 15 points), MDS quality indicators for long-stay residents (up to 30 points), family satisfaction survey results (up to 30 points), and staff immunization rates (up to 5 points). No specific restriction on use of funds is stated.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland Medicaid-participating nursing facilities with 45 or more beds that are not continuing care retirement centers (CCRCs) and meet baseline quality standards, having not been cited for certain federal quality or payment violations in the prior year.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Performance-based awards to qualifying nursing facilities; funds may be used for quality improvement initiatives, staffing enhancements, and resident care improvements. No specific restriction on use of funds is stated.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to qualifying Medicaid-participating nursing facilities located throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Must have 45 or more beds
Must not be a continuing care retirement center (CCRC)
In the previous year ending March 31, must not have been identified as a federally-designated 'special focus facility'
Must not have had a denial of payment for new admissions (DPNA) issued by CMS in the prior year
Must not have been determined to have provided 'substandard quality of care' as defined in federal Medicaid regulations in the prior year
Staffing levels must meet acuity-adjusted goals
Staffing stability benchmark of more than 2 years tenure
Must participate in resident satisfaction survey (MHCC survey)
Must submit MDS outcome measures data
Staff immunization rates must exceed 95% for full points
Must submit minimum cost report
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible facilities are evaluated automatically based on data already reported to state and federal agencies, including federal staffing records (payroll data), MDS quality indicator reports, the Staffing Stability Survey, the Maryland Health Care Commission Family Satisfaction Survey, staff immunization data, and cost reports. No separate application process is required. Facilities receive a scoresheet and can review it using the Scoresheet Guide provided by the program.

structured_extraction.program_name: Opioid-Associated Disease Prevention and Outreach Program (OADPOP)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Health authorizes organizations as OADPOPs to provide a wide range of services to people who use drugs, including infectious disease prevention, overdose prevention, sterile injection supplies, syringe distribution and collection, substance use disorder counseling, treatment and recovery services, HIV/HCV/STD testing, naloxone distribution, wound care, and reproductive health services. The program reviews new applications, manages reporting, issues guidance, and provides ongoing technical assistance and support to approved programs through MDH's Office of Overdose Prevention & Education (OPE). There are currently 30 authorized OADPOPs operating in 21 Maryland counties. The program is also known as the Syringe Services Program (SSP) and is authorized under Maryland Health-General §24-901 and COMAR 10.52.01.05–10.52.01.06.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MDH authorizes eligible organizations to operate as OADPOPs, providing program approval, reporting management, guidance documents, and ongoing technical assistance and support from MDH's Office of Overdose Prevention & Education (OPE). Approved programs receive authorization to legally operate syringe services and related harm-reduction activities under Maryland law, including distributing and collecting syringes at no cost, providing overdose prevention education and naloxone, offering HIV/HCV/STD testing and substance use disorder counseling, connecting clients to treatment and recovery services, and providing wound care and reproductive health services to people who use drugs. Authorization requires joint approval from MDH and the local health officer in each county of operation. Programs may operate in a single county or across multiple counties.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications may be submitted at any time (rolling)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local health departments and community-based organizations seeking to operate an authorized Opioid-Associated Disease Prevention and Outreach Program in Maryland, serving individuals who inject drugs and community members at risk of opioid-associated diseases.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Providing sterile injection supplies, syringe distribution and collection at no cost, overdose prevention education, naloxone distribution, HIV/HCV/STD testing, substance use disorder counseling, treatment and recovery referrals, wound care, and reproductive health services to people who use drugs; operating syringe services and harm-reduction programs under Maryland law.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland; programs may operate in a single county or across multiple counties with approval from the local health officer in each county where operations are proposed. There are currently 30 authorized OADPOPs operating in 21 Maryland counties.
requirements_list: Must apply using the official online Cognito Forms web application
Must read the OADPOP Application Guidance document thoroughly before submitting
Must be a local health department or community-based organization
Must agree to provide required services either on-site or by referral
Must obtain joint authorization from MDH and the local health officer in each county of proposed operation
Must comply with Maryland Health-General Article, Title 24, Subtitle 9 (§24-901 et seq.)
Must comply with COMAR 10.52.01.05 and 10.52.01.06
Must comply with 42 CFR Part 2 (confidentiality of substance use disorder records)
Must maintain participant confidentiality per Health-General Article §24-906(b)
Must have program operating procedures for needle/syringe distribution, collection, and disposal
Must have a community outreach and education plan (including needle litter cleanups)
Must implement a unique participant identification card system (non-cross-indexed to personal data)
Staff must have expertise in working with individuals who inject drugs and in harm reduction strategies
Staff must be trained in community referrals, counseling, and preventive education
Must implement program security procedures
Must collect required data and maintain confidential records
Must incorporate technical assistance from the Standing Advisory Committee
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Read the OADPOP Application Guidance document thoroughly, then submit an application using the online Cognito Forms application portal (cognitoforms.com). Applications are accepted on a rolling basis. MDH and the local health officer jointly review and approve applications. MDH manages program reporting, issues program guidance, and provides technical assistance to approved programs. Approved programs must operate in accordance with applicable statute and regulations. Programs whose approval is revoked may appeal in writing to the Deputy Secretary for Public Health Services within 30 calendar days of the revocation notice postmark date; the Deputy Secretary must respond within 60 days. For questions, email mdh.syringeservices@maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_name: Providing Dental Care for Low-income Children and Adults (CHRC Dental Grants)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Community Health Resources Commission (CHRC) awards grants to organizations across Maryland to expand access to dental services for low-income, uninsured, and underserved children and adults. Grantees include federally qualified health centers, county health departments, hospitals, and nonprofits that deliver preventive, restorative, and emergency dental care, often in underserved or rural areas. The program supports a wide range of activities including hiring staff, purchasing supplies and equipment, providing subsidized dental services, supporting community health workers, and funding partnerships with dental schools and hospitals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging from approximately $10,000 to $745,000 are awarded to organizations to expand dental programs, hire staff, purchase dental supplies and equipment, provide subsidized dental services to patients, support community health workers, fund transportation and patient navigation, and support partnerships with dental schools and hospitals. Grants are typically multi-year, ranging from one to three years.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Staff salaries, dental supplies and equipment, subsidized dental services for patients, community health worker costs, transportation assistance, patient navigation, oral health education, case management, and capital costs for dental clinic expansion or opening.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; grants have been awarded to organizations serving Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Anne Arundel, Allegany, Carroll, Caroline, Cecil, Charles, Dorchester, Frederick, Garrett, Harford, Howard, Kent, Montgomery, Prince George's, St. Mary's, Washington, Wicomico, and other Maryland counties.

The program strengthens the public health workforce by providing practical, hands-on experience to complement academic studies and prepare students for careers in public health. Subject areas include behavioral science, biostatistics, community health, epidemiology, health education, health informatics, health policy, healthcare administration, infectious disease, preparedness and response, public health accreditation, and public health communications.

Undergraduate interns earn $17.15 per hour and graduate interns earn $20.15 per hour. Interns gain hands-on experience across public health subject areas including behavioral science, biostatistics, community health, epidemiology, health education, health informatics, health policy, healthcare administration, infectious disease, preparedness and response, public health accreditation, and public health communications. Worksites include locations across Maryland including Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Carroll County, and Prince George's County.

structured_extraction.program_description: RAD is a statewide drug checking program that tests used drug paraphernalia voluntarily submitted by participants of Maryland Opioid-Associated Disease Prevention and Outreach Programs (OADPOPs). A trained OADPOP staff member wipes the paraphernalia and sends the sample to the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) for testing using Direct Analysis in Real Time Mass Spectrometry (DART-MS) technology. Results are shared back with the OADPOP and the participant who submitted the sample within approximately 24-28 hours of receipt. The program aims to improve understanding of the drug supply, empower people who use drugs with information to reduce risk, identify new and emerging drug trends, and support overdose prevention efforts across Maryland. As of Q4 CY2025, 21 OADPOPs in 14 jurisdictions participate statewide. Piloted in 8 OADPOPs from October 2021 through September 2022; expanded to ongoing service for interested OADPOPs. Total of 5,853 samples collected since October 2021.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free drug composition testing service for used paraphernalia submitted through participating OADPOPs. A trace amount from used paraphernalia is wiped by a trained OADPOP staff member and mailed to NIST for DART-MS analysis. Results are reported back to the OADPOP and the submitting participant within approximately 24-28 hours of receipt. No personal identifying information is collected or shared. Participating OADPOPs also provide additional harm reduction services including drug test strips (fentanyl, xylazine, benzodiazepine, medetomidine), naloxone/overdose education, HCV/HIV testing, syringe services, wound care, medication for opioid use disorder, housing referrals, food access, and telehealth services.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Participants of Maryland Opioid-Associated Disease Prevention and Outreach Programs (OADPOPs) who use drugs and want to know the composition of their drug supply, as well as OADPOP organizations seeking to participate in the program. Also serves people at risk of overdose, individuals with opioid use disorder, and unhoused populations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Drug composition testing to identify substances present in the illicit drug supply, inform harm reduction decisions, and support overdose prevention efforts. Also supports drug sample analysis, supply provision, and overnight/rush shipping for priority samples.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through participating OADPOPs across Maryland. As of Q4 CY2025, 21 OADPOPs in 14 jurisdictions participate, including Allegany, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Calvert, Caroline, Cecil, Frederick, Harford, Howard, St. Mary's, Washington, Wicomico, and additional counties.
requirements_list: Must be a participant of a Maryland OADPOP that participates in the RAD program
Testing must be conducted through an authorized OADPOP (required for legal exemption from Maryland drug paraphernalia laws)
Paraphernalia is wiped by a trained OADPOP staff member
Participant completes a webform (Cognito webform) with staff — no personal identifiers are collected
No personal health information or personal private information is collected
Participation is completely voluntary for OADPOPs and participants
Do not mail equipment; avoid swabbing blood or biohazards
Cognito webform must be completed for every sample before mailing
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Find a participating RAD site using the interactive map on the program page. Visit the OADPOP site, mobile unit, or street outreach location (walk-in/drop-in access at most locations; some by appointment). A trained OADPOP staff member wipes the paraphernalia and completes a Cognito webform with the participant (no personal identifiers collected). The wipe is mailed to NIST for DART-MS analysis. Results are shared back to the OADPOP and then to the participant within approximately 24-28 hours of receipt.

structured_extraction.program_name: Rare and Expensive Case Management (REM) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The REM program provides medical case management and other services for Medicaid-eligible individuals who have a rare and expensive medical condition. It is a voluntary program that assigns a personal case manager to help participants develop a care plan, find needed services, apply for benefits, and coordinate their care. Participants receive all standard Medicaid-covered services plus additional REM-specific services beyond standard coverage. Services must be medically necessary and ordered by a health care provider; some require preauthorization.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive a personal REM case manager who conducts a needs assessment, develops a care plan, helps apply for services, monitors care, and provides education. Additional covered services beyond standard Medicaid include Certified Nursing Assistant (CNA) and CNA Certified Medication Technician (CMT) services, chiropractic services, Home Health Aide (HHA) and HHA CMT services, nutrition counseling and supplements, occupational therapy, speech-language pathology, and private duty nursing and shift nursing services. Services must be medically necessary and ordered by a health care provider; some require preauthorization. Eligibility is based on qualifying ICD-10 diagnoses including genetic disorders, metabolic disorders, hematologic conditions, neurological conditions, kidney disease, and other rare conditions, with age-specific eligibility (typically 0-20 or 0-64 depending on diagnosis).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland Medicaid HealthChoice enrollees who have at least one qualifying rare and expensive medical condition and choose to voluntarily participate in the program. Age limits vary by diagnosis (typically 0-20 or 0-64 years depending on condition).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Medical case management, care planning, service coordination, and additional clinical services such as nursing, therapy, nutrition counseling, and home health aide services for individuals with rare and expensive conditions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to eligible Maryland Medicaid HealthChoice enrollees. Maryland Department of Health, REM Intake Unit, 201 W. Preston Street, Room 208, Baltimore, Maryland 21201.
requirements_list: Must be eligible for and enrolled in the Maryland HealthChoice managed care program (Medicaid)
Must have at least one qualifying rare and expensive condition for your age group (as defined in COMAR 10.09.69.17)
Must voluntarily choose to participate in the REM program
Patient must have a Medical Assistance (MA) number
Must have a qualifying ICD-10 diagnosis from the REM Disease List
History and Physical completed within past 12 months
Specialist consultation note or report confirming diagnosis (varies by condition)
Laboratory values confirming diagnosis (where applicable)
Supporting imaging studies for certain diagnoses
Physician/licensed health care provider signature on referral form
Services must be medically necessary and ordered by a licensed health care provider
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Anyone can refer an individual to the program. A licensed health care provider must complete, sign, and date the REM Intake and Referral Form. The completed form can be faxed to 410-333-5426 or emailed to mdh.remreferralfax@maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_name: Refugee Medical Screening for Cuban/Haitian Entrants
structured_extraction.program_description: Cuban and Haitian Entrants (CHEs) and other eligible humanitarian immigrants (refugees, asylees, humanitarian parolees, and victims of trafficking) are eligible for a no-cost comprehensive domestic medical screening examination (Refugee Health Assessment/RHA) starting from the date of their humanitarian parole. The screening is more thorough than overseas medical examinations and identifies health conditions that could affect school attendance or employment, provides required vaccinations, conducts infectious disease screening (including Hepatitis B, TB, HIV/AIDS), emotional well-being assessment, and refers clients to primary care, public health, and/or specialty care providers for ongoing healthcare. Services are culturally informed and language accessible, provided by appointment only through local health partners. At least two clinic visits (1-3 hours each) are required, to be completed within 90 days of arrival.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A no-cost comprehensive domestic medical screening and health assessment (Refugee Health Assessment/RHA). Services include physical exams, medical tests (blood, urine, stool), immunization review, infectious disease screening (Hepatitis B, TB, HIV/AIDS), parasitic infection testing, emotional well-being/mental health screening, specialist referrals, medications, and ongoing TB treatment if needed. At least 2 clinic visits (1-3 hours each) required. Services are culturally informed and language accessible. Provided by appointment only through local Federally Qualified Health Center (FQHC) partners: Baltimore Medical System (serving Baltimore City and Anne Arundel, Baltimore, Frederick, Harford, and Howard Counties) and CCI Health and Wellness Services (serving Prince George's and Montgomery Counties).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Within 90 days after date of arrival, entry into community, or asylum is granted
structured_extraction.program_audience: Cuban and Haitian Entrants (CHEs), refugees, asylees, humanitarian parolees, and victims of trafficking arriving in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Medical screening, health assessment, vaccinations, infectious disease screening, emotional well-being assessment, and referrals to healthcare providers
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore Medical System serves clients in Baltimore City and Anne Arundel, Baltimore, Frederick, Harford, and Howard Counties (email RefugeeHealth@bmsi.org or call 443-703-3404). CCI Health and Wellness Services serves clients in Prince George's and Montgomery Counties (email Lesvia.Velasquez@cciweb.org or call 667-770-6760).

Must complete screening within 90 days of arrival, entry into community, or grant of asylum
At least 2 clinic visits required (1-3 hours each)

Must bring required documentation: identification card or photo ID, I-94 form, and IOM (International Organization for Migration) documentation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Center for Global Migration and Immigrant Health at mdh.immigranthealth@maryland.gov or 410-767-6698.
