structured_extraction.program_name: EmPOWER Maryland Limited Income Energy Efficiency Program (LIEEP)
structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide program administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) that helps limited-income households reduce energy use by providing free energy efficiency upgrades and weatherization services at no cost. The program includes five components: Whole Home Efficiency, MEEHA (Multifamily Energy Efficiency and Housing Affordability), Base Efficiency, MEET (Maryland Energy Efficiency Tune-up), and Energy Kits. Uses a whole-house approach with sophisticated analysis and modeling to maximize energy and dollar savings. Improvements include insulation, hot water system improvements, lighting retrofits, furnace repairs, refrigerator retrofits, HVAC replacements, air sealing, appliance replacements, and other health and safety improvements. Materials and equipment are installed at no charge to eligible households within EmPOWER utility service territories to reduce energy costs, lower monthly utility bills, improve comfort, and may improve air quality and family health. Services are provided in each of Maryland's 23 counties and Baltimore City. As of March 31, 2023, the program has delivered benefits to over 53,900 limited-income families. The program also operates a network of local service providers — including nonprofits, local governments, and for-profit home improvement contractors — who deliver these services and are selected through competitive procurement rounds (RFA/RFP) held at least every 3 years. Operates on a three-year cycle with DHCD submitting three-year program plans. Funded and regulated through the EmPOWER Maryland Act and overseen by the Maryland Public Service Commission (PSC).
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: For eligible households: free installation of energy efficiency improvements and weatherization services at no or low cost, including attic, floor and wall insulation, hot water system upgrades, lighting retrofits (LED lighting), furnace cleaning and repairs, refrigerator retrofits and replacements, HVAC replacements, air sealing, duct sealing and insulation, appliance replacements (refrigerators, freezers, dishwashers, clothes washer/dryer, dehumidifiers), heat pump water heaters, solar thermal systems, smart thermostats, window replacements, advanced power strips, occupancy sensors, faucet aerators, showerheads, water pipe insulation, recovery ventilators, and health and safety items. Funding covers mandatory and optional energy efficiency measures including: health & safety work, LED lighting, air sealing, duct sealing/insulation, attic/ceiling/wall/floor insulation, window replacements, HVAC system replacements, water heating measures, smart thermostats, refrigerator replacements, and recovery ventilators. Whole Home Efficiency program provides comprehensive energy retrofits up to $16,000 per job, health and safety repairs capped at $1,000 per job, and incidental repairs up to 30% of total job cost. Weatherization Readiness Funds available up to $15,000 average per unit for addressing deferral conditions. Energy kits containing direct-install measures (low-flow showerhead, smart power strip, outlet gaskets, pipe insulation, faucet aerators) are available for hard-to-reach households. MEET program provides personalized home visits (1-2 hours) with HVAC maintenance, equipment tune-up, direct install of approved measures, and energy education for previous LIEEP clients. MEEHA program provides improvements to multifamily properties including grants and loans, with HVAC equipment funding up to 85% of project cost (15% landlord contribution required for multi-unit properties). An energy audit is conducted first to prioritize the most effective upgrades. Services are provided to eligible households within EmPOWER utility service territories (BGE, Delmarva Power, FirstEnergy, Pepco, SMECO, or Washington Gas). For service providers: nonprofits, local governments, and for-profit contractors are selected through competitive rounds (RFA/RFP) held at least every 3 years to deliver these services to low-income households.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Limited-income households in Maryland (at or below 250% Federal Poverty Level or 80% Area Median Income, whichever is higher, or at or below 200% of poverty level for some program components) who are customers of participating EmPOWER utility companies (BGE, Delmarva Power, FirstEnergy, Pepco, SMECO, or Washington Gas), including homeowners, renters, mobile home owners, group home and shelter residents, and seniors (over 60), disabled persons, and households with children; multifamily property owners and managers (for MEEHA program); as well as nonprofits, local governments, and for-profit home improvement contractors interested in becoming network service providers. Priority given to elderly, households with children under 5, persons with disabilities, and households with high energy cost burden.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home energy efficiency improvements and weatherization improvements for residential properties (single-family, manufactured homes, low-rise multifamily) including attic, floor, ceiling and wall insulation; hot water system improvements; lighting retrofits (LED bulbs, ceiling fans with LED); furnace cleaning, tuning and safety repairs; refrigerator retrofit and replacement; HVAC replacements and tune-ups (forced air heating, heat pumps, central AC, ductless mini-splits, hydronic boilers, window AC); air sealing; duct sealing and insulation; windows and doors; appliance replacement (refrigerators, freezers, dishwashers, laundry, induction cooktops, dehumidifiers); heat pump water heaters; solar thermal systems; building certifications; smart thermostats; advanced power strips; recovery ventilators; occupancy sensors; faucet aerators; showerheads; water pipe and tank insulation; and health and safety items including smoke/CO detectors, electrical repairs, fuel leak repairs, mold/moisture remediation, radon precautions, pest removal. Also covers critical home repairs (structural, electrical, water leaks, lead, asbestos encapsulation, biological hazard remediation), incidental repairs necessary for preservation of weatherization measures, and roof repairs when necessary for measure installation. Weatherization Readiness Funds available for addressing deferral conditions. Service providers use funding to deliver these energy efficiency services to low-income households, including administrative costs, program operations, energy audits, inspections, customer outreach, permits, training and technical assistance, and transportation costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland, with services provided in each of Maryland's 23 counties and Baltimore City, to customers of six participating EmPOWER utility companies (BGE, Delmarva Power, FirstEnergy, Pepco, SMECO, or Washington Gas). Additional categorical eligibility for areas with Final EJ Score Percentile at or above 90 on the MDEE J Map. Properties listed in or eligible for listing in the National Register of Historic Places require additional review by the Maryland Historical Trust. DHCD mailing address: 7800 Harkins Road, Lanham, MD 20706.
requirements_list: Must be a low-income or limited-income household

Household income must be at or below 250% of Federal Poverty Level or 80% Area Median Income, whichever is higher (e.g., $72,950 for a 1-person household, up to $137,550 for an 8-person household); some program components require income at or below 200% of Federal Poverty Level.
Must have a utility account with one of six participating EmPOWER utility companies: BGE, Delmarva Power, FirstEnergy, Pepco, SMECO, or Washington Gas.
Must be located in an EmPOWER utility service territory.
Power must be available to home (contact office if no electrical service).
Income documentation from last 30 days required.
Recent utility bill copy required.
Social Security card copies for all household members required.
Photo ID of applicant required.
Zero income affidavit (if applicable).
Income certification valid for 12 months from certification date.
Documented medical condition (with physician's letter, not older than 180 days) may prioritize application; required for air conditioning as a health and safety measure for at-risk occupants.

Automatic income eligibility if currently participating in SNAP, TANF, SSI, Medicaid, OHEP Utility Bill Pay Assistance, HUD housing assistance, Fuel Fund Assistance, DHCD Rehab Programs, Baltimore Lead Hazard Control Program, MEA Energy Equity Grant, or MEEHA.
Energy audit required before work begins; Signed Energy Assessment Agreement required before work starts.

Building type eligibility: single-family homes, duplexes, townhomes, manufactured housing, and walk-up buildings with 4 or fewer units; group homes and shelters eligible with specific unit counting methodology.
Building Owner Agreement required for rental properties.
Health & Safety measures mandatory before energy measures proceed.
Combustion appliance testing required when combustion appliances present.
Manual J required for heating/cooling appliance installation.
AHRA certification required for asbestos testing.
State and local code compliance mandatory.
No fuel switching with EmPOWER Whole Home or Base Efficiency.
DOE priority categories must be considered for scheduling; DOE priority lists and mandatory measures vary by housing type (single-family site-built, manufactured homes, low-rise multifamily).
Energy modeling may be required for non-standard HVAC systems.
Specific R-values and efficiency ratings required for insulation and equipment.
Service providers must respond to an active Request for Applications (RFA) or Request for Proposals (RFP).
For-profit contractors must respond to an RFP.
Nonprofits and local governments must respond to an RFA in conjunction with the DOE WAP program.
Register on the eMaryland Marketplace Advantage (eMMA) website to receive notifications of open procurements.
Network partners must maintain complete, accurate, organized client files; records retention: 3 years following grant close.
Separate accounting required for fee-for-service activities.
Annual re-verification of eligibility required.
Properties must comply with Maryland Historical Trust Act requirements if listed or eligible for listing in the National Register of Historic Places.
Materials and installation must meet DOE WAP standards and Standard Work Specifications (SWS).
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For households: Complete an online pre-application through the DHCD website (dhcd.maryland.gov) or submit a paper application with required documents to the DHCD office. Applicants may also apply for Energy Assistance through the Maryland Department of Human Services (OHEP, 1-800-332-6347) to be screened for the program. If already approved for Energy Assistance payments, call the intake line at 1-855-583-8976. Once eligibility is confirmed, a local agency will schedule a home energy audit, discuss results, and arrange for a contractor to complete the recommended upgrades. For service providers: Register on the eMaryland Marketplace Advantage (eMMA) website to be notified of open procurements. Contact Seth Fawcett to be added to the vendor email list. Respond to an active RFA or RFP when posted. For MHRP (home repair): Submit completed application with all required documentation including property ownership documents, income verification, and licensed Maryland contractor quotes (not more than 60 days old) with contractor documentation (MHIC or specialty license, Certificate of Insurance of $1M minimum, good standing letter, W-9 form). Incomplete applications will not be processed.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides loans to new or growing developers. The loans support projects that revitalize communities and increase quality affordable housing. The program also aims to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and expand opportunities for Maryland residents and businesses. The fund supports talented developers who have a commitment to their communities but lack the necessary capital for their projects.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides loans to support development projects.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Emerging and undercapitalized real estate developers with a demonstrated commitment to community revitalization.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support projects that revitalize communities, increase quality affordable housing, and reduce greenhouse gas emissions.
requirements_list: Applicant must be an undercapitalized developer.
Applicant must demonstrate a commitment to communities.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, download the necessary forms from the program website. Second, complete the files as instructed. Third, save the completed files to your computer. Fourth, upload the saved files. Finally, complete the online submission form and click submit.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing

structured_extraction.program_description: An interest form that allows residents to request information, start an application, or visit the Department of Human Services (DHS) energy assistance website. Responses help the agency understand community needs and plan future energy assistance programs.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: This is an interest form — not a direct assistance program itself. Applicants can use it to request information or start an application for energy assistance programs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland homeowners seeking energy assistance or efficiency programs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Fill out the online form at https://dhcd.wufoo.com/forms/k2lirta0kk1ok2 to request information, start an application, or be directed to DHS energy assistance resources.

structured_extraction.program_name: FY24 Home Stretch – Difficult to Serve Properties Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A state grant program administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) that provides funding to county jurisdictions to help cover capital construction costs for installing broadband internet service at premises that are hard to reach due to remoteness, distance from existing broadband infrastructure, long driveways, or other geographic issues that discourage ISPs from delivering service. In FY24, $19.6 million was awarded to 18 jurisdictions in the first round, providing internet access to approximately 2,400 unserved households — every jurisdiction that applied received funds. County jurisdictions develop a sub-grant program with ISP partner(s) and may pass funding through to homeowners and businesses in difficult-to-serve locations, including a 'long driveway' subsidy component. Garrett County, Somerset County, Montgomery County, and other participating counties administer this program locally for eligible residents and businesses. Funded by the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021 (U.S. Treasury Coronavirus Capital Projects Fund), with some counties supplementing with ARC POWER funding.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $1,100,000 total available at the state level per county award; maximum of $8,000 per location. In FY24, $19.6 million was distributed statewide to 18 jurisdictions in the first round. County jurisdictions develop a sub-grant program with one or more ISP partners to fund installation of broadband service at difficult-to-serve properties (e.g., properties with long driveways or set far back from the road), including a subsidy component for connecting homes with high connection costs. A 25% match of eligible project costs is required from the county. End beneficiaries (homeowners and businesses) may receive grant funding to cover the cost of connecting properties that are expensive to serve due to distance from existing infrastructure. Funded by the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021, Capital Projects Fund.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Limited-time opportunity; no specific deadline stated. First-round applications have already been awarded. Future rounds may be announced.
structured_extraction.program_audience: County jurisdictions in Maryland with geographically difficult-to-serve properties; homeowners and business owners in hard-to-reach areas (e.g., Garrett County, Somerset County, Montgomery County) who lack reliable high-speed internet access due to long driveways, remote locations, or distance from existing broadband infrastructure. Also local governments and internet service providers seeking to extend broadband access to unserved Maryland households.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital construction costs for installing broadband internet service to remote or hard-to-reach premises, including properties with long driveways, set far back from the road, or otherwise expensive to connect due to distance from existing infrastructure. Includes subsidizing the cost to connect homes with long driveways or properties with high connection costs. Extends broadband to unserved households facing geographic barriers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland; county jurisdictions apply at the state level through the Office of Statewide Broadband and administer sub-grant programs locally. Participating counties include Garrett County, Somerset County, and Montgomery County, among others, for eligible properties in hard-to-reach areas.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a county jurisdiction or local Maryland jurisdiction (for state-level grant)
County must develop a sub-grant program with one or more ISP partners
Maximum funding of $8,000 per location
25% match of eligible project costs required
All federal rules of the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021, Capital Projects Fund apply
Property must be difficult or expensive to serve with broadband (e.g., set far back from the road, long driveway, or remote location)
Must be located in an area where standard broadband installation is cost-prohibitive
Households served must be currently unserved by broadband internet
Geographic or distance challenges must make service delivery difficult for providers
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Application package, form, and notice of funding opportunity available for download from the DHCD Broadband page (see also FY24-Application-Package.pdf). Local jurisdictions apply to the Office of Statewide Broadband (dhcd.maryland.gov/Broadband). First-round applications have already been awarded. Future rounds may be announced. For local applicants, contact the relevant county administrator (e.g., Garrett County at broadband@garrettcountymd.gov or 301-914-1543, Somerset County, or Montgomery County Rural Broadband page) for information on how to apply through the county's sub-grant program.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Family Self-Sufficiency (FSS) Program is a voluntary program that helps Housing Choice Voucher (Section 8) participants achieve higher education, improve their employment status, and move toward financial independence. The program evaluates skills and determines needs of families and individuals, providing guidance in financial literacy, job training, childcare, and workforce success. Participants build interest-bearing escrow savings accounts as employment wages increase, with tax-free disbursement upon contract completion. The program is administered through the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development Eastern Shore Regional Office, with a dedicated community engagement center in Cambridge, Maryland serving local Housing Voucher participants.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Program coordinators guide Housing Choice Voucher participants through steps to reach self-sufficiency. Assistance includes financial literacy training, job training and job retention support, childcare assistance, education support, employment counseling, health services referral, homeownership guidance, and transportation assistance. An interest-bearing escrow account is established for participants, with monthly deposits based on employment wage increases. Escrow funds are disbursed tax-free upon successful program completion and can be used for employment wages, down payment on a home, vehicle repair, testing fees, or other goal-related expenses. Participants also receive workshops, classes, and community support referrals. The Cambridge Community Engagement Center provides in-person support for Cambridge-area participants.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families and individuals receiving Housing Choice Voucher (Section 8) rental assistance in Maryland, including heads of household, all family members, and disabled individuals with a working household member, seeking to improve their education, employment, and financial self-sufficiency.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Escrow account funds (plus interest) provided upon successful program completion for use toward employment wages, down payment on a home, vehicle repair, testing fees, or other goal-related expenses. Payments are IRS-ruled nontaxable. Also supports higher education, employment improvement, and achieving financial self-sufficiency.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Housing Choice Voucher participants receiving rental assistance in Maryland, served by the Maryland DHCD Eastern Shore Regional Office and Cambridge Community Engagement Center, located in Cambridge, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a Housing Choice Voucher (Section 8) participant
Complete application submitted by head of household
Sign Contract of Participation
Complete Needs Assessment with case manager
Set realistic and achievable goals toward economic independence
Maintain suitable employment
Successfully complete contract tasks and goals (5-year contract, extendable 2 years)
Two required long-term goals: obtain employment and be free of TANF benefits
Complete individual family plan with FSS coordinator
Achieve 12 months TANF-free status to receive escrow funds
Quarterly communication/check-ins with coordinator
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact DHCD at 410-901-4080 or fss.dhcd@maryland.gov, or complete the online FSS Inquiry Form to have a program coordinator reach out and begin the application process. Meet with an FSS coordinator to review family strengths and complete a needs assessment. Cambridge-area participants may also contact the Cambridge Community Engagement Center directly for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: Program created by the Maryland General Assembly in 2007 to provide loans to homeowners to buy out (redeem) ground leases. A ground lease is a long-term lease (usually 99 years, renewable forever) that requires the homeowner to pay periodic 'ground rent' to the lease holder. The program helps homeowners end this obligation by purchasing the ground lease outright. It cannot provide grants for this purpose.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans are provided to homeowners to redeem (buy out) ground leases. Maximum loan amount is $3,500 including transactional costs up to $1,000. Interest rates vary by income level: 4.5%–6.0% for households at 80% AMI; 0%–4.5% for households at 60% AMI; deferred principal and interest possible for households at 50% and 30% AMI with no repayment capability. Transactional costs such as title search and loan closing are also covered.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners who own and occupy their leasehold property as a principal residence and meet household income limits (cannot exceed 80% of statewide median income, based on household size).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Redeeming (buying out) ground leases on residential leasehold properties, including transactional costs such as title search and loan closing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Ground rents are most prevalent in Baltimore City but exist in some other Maryland counties as well. The program is available statewide. Income limits vary by geography: Washington DC PMSA (Calvert, Charles, Frederick, Montgomery, Prince George's Counties) vs. Rest of State.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a homeowner on a property subject to a ground rent obligation
Property must be the applicant's primary/principal residence
Must have homeowners insurance
Household income cannot exceed 80% of the statewide median income (limits vary by household size and geography)
Must complete the DHCD Ground Rent Redemption Loan application
Must provide evidence of ownership and ground rent documentation
Must provide documentation of household income and debts
Anyone on the deed but not occupying the property must provide proof of residence elsewhere
Applicants behind on ground rent payments may still apply
Personal debt history documentation required (judgments, bankruptcy, foreclosure)
Credit check authorized
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the DHCD Ground Rent Redemption Loan Application (available as a PDF on the program page) and submit it with required documentation to the local administrator or DHCD Special Loan Programs office. Information will be verified with employers and financial institutions. A credit check will be authorized and an underwriter will review the application. An inquiry form is also available online.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Group Home Program provides loans to help individuals, qualified limited partnerships, and nonprofit organizations construct, acquire, or modify housing to serve as group homes or assisted living units for people with special housing needs. It can also refinance existing group home mortgages. Funding comes from state funds and tax-exempt mortgage revenue bonds. The program targets low-income elderly, disabled, juveniles, homeless, victims of sex trafficking, and other individuals with special housing needs.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Mortgage loans for acquisition, construction, and modification/rehabilitation of group home buildings. Interest rates range from 0% to 7% (target 4%) depending on the funding source and project cash flow. Maximum term is generally 30 years (up to 40 years); construction term maximum is 1 year. Maximum loan amount is $125,000 per bedroom (including caretaker's bedroom), with a 15% increase available in high-cost areas (Montgomery, Prince George's, and Howard Counties). Loans may be up to 100% of appraised/after-rehabilitation value for first lien; 95% for subordinate liens. Loan deferral provisions available (typically not exceeding 2 years). Nonprofit sponsors must contribute 5% toward the project; individual sponsors must make a 10% equity contribution. Upon sale or disposition, sponsors must share net equity with the Department (minimum 25%) at a rate the Department determines. Emergency Shelter and Transitional Housing Grants also available as secondary assistance.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications will reopen at a later date.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Special Loans Program, Community Development Administration
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals, nonprofit organizations, and limited partnerships that provide group homes or assisted living units for people with special housing needs, including the developmentally or physically disabled, elderly, juveniles, homeless persons, victims of sex trafficking, and others with special housing needs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Refinancing existing group home mortgages; acquisition of property; construction of new buildings; rehabilitation of existing residential buildings; professional fees (architect, legal, appraisal, survey, soil boring); closing costs; appraisal and inspection fees; reserve for replacement deposits; modification costs including repair or replacement of major systems (heating, roofing, electrical, plumbing), accessibility modifications (ramps, grab bars), lead paint abatement, general repairs, and code compliance improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland across all 24 counties and Baltimore City. For Special Housing Opportunities Program financing, property must be located in a Priority Funding Area unless a waiver is granted for existing construction. When using federal HOME Investment Partnerships Program (HOME) funds, eligible counties exclude entitlement jurisdictions (Baltimore City, Anne Arundel, Baltimore County, Harford, Howard, Montgomery, and Prince George's Counties), which receive their own HOME fund allocations. Higher loan limits (15% increase in bedroom allotment) apply in high-cost areas: Montgomery, Prince George's, and Howard Counties.
requirements_list: Applicants must be licensed by the appropriate Maryland licensing authority.
Nonprofit applicants seeking Special Housing Opportunities Program funding must have a 501(c)(3) IRS designation.
Property must be in good repair and compliant with applicable state and local housing and occupancy codes, or able to be made so with loan proceeds.
Appraisal must be completed by an appraiser on the department's approved list and must not be more than 90 days old at the time of approval.
Property must have a home inspection acceptable to the department.
Properties built before 1978 require a lead paint risk assessment by a certified and accredited lead paint testing company.
At least 51 percent of all beds must be available for residents with incomes at or below 60 percent of the area median income.
A Federal Funds Notice must be completed by the borrower and executed by the seller before entering into a binding sales contract for all Group Home Program loan requests.
The Federal Funds Notice must disclose: federal assistance, no eminent domain use, and fair market value estimate with reasonable evidence.
Occupancy status must be confirmed at time of sales contract signing.
Commitment letter executed by both parties required.
Financial statements (certified) required.
Evidence of land control (purchase agreement, option, or letter of intent) required.
Title commitment and title policy required.
Survey with surveyor's certificate required.
Zoning compliance evidence required.
Construction documents (permits, plans, specifications, contracts) required.
Insurance policies (liability, builder's risk, hazard) required.
Minority Business Enterprise Plan required for projects over $250,000 in construction costs.
Certificate of Completion signed by Sponsor, contractor, and Housing Rehabilitation Officer required upon project completion.
Certificate of use and occupancy required for new construction.
Executed mechanic lien waivers from all contractors and subcontractors required.
10% retainage held until substantial completion.
Prior written CDA approval required for all change orders.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Special Loans Program at the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development to confirm fund availability before submitting an application. Complete the required Federal Funds Notice with the seller prior to a binding sales contract; seller must sign and date the notice. Submit application with appraisal, home inspection, and other required documentation. Payment requests for construction are processed on an agreed schedule; inspection of completed work is required before payment requests are submitted. GHFP Manager reviews and approves inspection reports; Assistant Director signs approved payment request packages.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Healthy Homes Production Grant Program (HHPG) provides financial assistance to low-income homeowners to create safer and healthier living environments. It funds comprehensive home inspections and remediation of health and safety hazards such as mold, lead, radon, asbestos, structural issues, and more in owner-occupied single-family homes. Eligible homeowners receive a free, in-home comprehensive assessment to identify improvements and enroll in appropriate programs. The program follows the 'Eight Principles of a Healthy Home' to ensure homes are dry, clean, safe, well-ventilated, well-maintained, pest- and contaminant-free, and thermally controlled.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $15,474 per property for the actual cost of critical home repair and hazard remediation work on owner-occupied single-family homes. Total program funding is $2,000,000. Funds cover comprehensive assessments by a Healthy Homes Evaluator and remediation of identified hazards including mold, gas leaks, roof repair, asbestos, electrical, plumbing, radon, and structural issues. Maximum bid total cannot exceed $50,000.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 18, 2026 (for public comments on Environmental Review Record)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income homeowners (at or below 80% of Area Median Income) in eight Maryland counties, with priority given to households with children under six years old, seniors (60+), disabled persons, critically ill members, and households receiving certain benefits (SNAP, TANF, SSI, HUD housing assistance, Medicaid, OHEP, Maryland Fuel Fund)
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Critical home repairs and hazard remediation including mold remediation, gas leak repair, roof repair and replacement, asbestos abatement, combustion appliance repair/replacement, chimney repair, foundation waterproofing, radon mitigation, electrical hazard remediation, plumbing repairs, water/well/septic/sewer issues, window and door repairs, structural repair, building shell stabilization, and pest treatments
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Allegany, Calvert, Charles, Garrett, Montgomery, Prince George's, Saint Mary's, and Washington counties in Maryland
requirements_list: Household income must be at or below 80% of the Area Median Income (AMI), adjusted for household size
Property must be an owner-occupied single-family residence
Property must be located in one of the eight eligible counties: Allegany, Calvert, Charles, Garrett, Montgomery, Prince George's, Saint Mary's, or Washington
Priority given to households with children under six years old
Income verification required (2 months paystubs or employer letter, 2 years tax returns, 2 months bank statements, benefit award letters if applicable)
Home ownership documentation required (photo ID, deed, current mortgage statement, property tax bill, homeowners insurance declaration page)
Bids from licensed Maryland contractors required (not older than 60 days, with photos, contact info, MHIC license, Certificate of Liability Insurance, Letter of Good Standing, W-9)
Bid total cannot exceed $50,000
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Start with a free, in-home comprehensive assessment to identify improvements and enroll in appropriate programs. 2. Complete the Combined Energy Rehabilitation Application; DHCD reviews for eligibility. 3. Select one or more licensed contractors to provide bids for the repair work. 4. Submit a work proposal with photos from a licensed and insured Maryland Home Improvement contractor; DHCD's Healthy Homes Evaluator reviews and may inspect the property. 5. Contractor provides required documents (MHIC license, certificate of liability insurance, letter of good standing, W-9). 6. Sign the Grant Agreement, Rehabilitation Grant Agreement, and other closing documents via DocuSign; contractor and owner sign the Rehabilitation Agreement; Order to Proceed issued after funds are encumbered and permits submitted. 7. Contractor performs the work; Healthy Homes Evaluator conducts on-site inspections; owner signs Certificate of Completion before final contractor payment. Submit complete application with all required documentation; incomplete applications will not be processed.

structured_extraction.program_name: Healthy Homes for Healthy Kids Lead Initiative (DHCD Program)
structured_extraction.program_description: This initiative helps families reduce lead exposure in homes and childcare locations built before 1978 where a child under 18 has elevated blood lead levels. It covers lead removal and minor home repairs necessary to keep lead paint properly sealed. The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) in partnership with the Maryland Department of Health pays for lead removal from houses or apartments where children live or spend time, at no cost to property owners or tenants.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Covers lead removal and minor home repairs necessary to ensure lead paint remains properly sealed. Available at no cost to property owners or tenants. Available to families of children with elevated blood lead levels enrolled in or eligible for Medicaid/MCHP.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with children under 19 years old who live in Maryland, have a blood lead level of 3.5 micrograms per deciliter or higher, are enrolled in or eligible for Medicaid/MCHP, and spend 10+ hours per week in the location where exposure occurred
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Lead removal and minor home repairs necessary to ensure lead paint remains properly sealed in residential properties where children live or spend time
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland; child must reside in or visit the home or apartment with a lead problem for 10 or more hours per week
requirements_list: Child must be under 19 years old and live in Maryland
Child must have a recent blood lead test of 3.5 micrograms per deciliter or higher
Child must be enrolled in or eligible for Medicaid/Maryland Children's Health Insurance Program (MCHP)
Child must spend 10 hours or more per week in the location where lead exposure occurred (home, apartment, or day care)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call the Environmental Health Help Line at 1-866-703-3266 (toll-free) or contact your local health department for more information and to apply. You may also email mdh.healthyhomes@maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_name: Home Stretch - FY24 Affordable Housing Grant (Expanded Round)
structured_extraction.program_description: An expanded round of the Home Stretch program providing grants to municipal and nonprofit owners of public housing and internet service providers to install broadband-capable wiring to individual dwelling units in affordable housing. The program is funded by $26.9 million allocated from the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021, Capital Projects Fund, to support the Office of Statewide Broadband's mission to bridge the digital accessibility gap. Grants range from $250,000 to $5,000,000, covering up to 95% of eligible project costs with a required 5% match.

structured_extraction.program_name: Homebuyer Education for First Time Homebuyers
structured_extraction.program_description: Homebuyer education, also called housing or pre-purchase counseling, helps first-time homebuyers prepare for purchasing a home and the responsibilities of homeownership. The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development recommends this education for all prospective homebuyers and requires it for participants in the Maryland Mortgage Program.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Homebuyer education and pre-purchase counseling is provided through HUD-approved counseling agencies, National Industry Standards agencies, and several online course options. Some courses may have a registration fee.
structured_extraction.program_audience: First-time homebuyers in Maryland preparing to purchase a home
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Education and counseling to prepare for homeownership

If securing financing, check with your lender, insurer, or servicer for any specific homebuyer education requirements

structured_extraction.program_description: The Homelessness Solutions Program (HSP) helps communities across Maryland prevent and end homelessness by providing over $15 million in annual funding to Continuums of Care (CoCs) and Local Homeless Coalitions (LHCs). Administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD), Division of Homeless Solutions, it leads the state's strategy, policy, and coordinated response effort to prevent and end homelessness. The program provides federal and state funding, technical support, and grant funding to lead agencies of CoCs and LHCs, which coordinate homeless services and connect people to housing programs, shelters, and other services. The program consolidates several prior funding streams including the Emergency Solutions Grant, Rental Allowance Program, Emergency and Transitional Housing and Services, Homeless Women's Crisis Shelter Homes, Service-Linked Housing, and the Housing Navigator and Aftercare Program. It also includes the Emergency Assistance Program (EAP), formerly known as the Homelessness Prevention Program.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: HSP provides grant funding and technical support to eligible lead agencies on behalf of homeless services providers. Funded activities include street outreach, emergency shelter, rapid rehousing, homeless prevention/diversion, permanent supportive housing (PSH) case management, Homeless Management Information System (HMIS) costs, rental assistance, transitional housing, service-linked housing, housing navigation/aftercare services, flex funds for landlord incentives and barrier removal, direct cash transfer programs for vulnerable subpopulations, host homes, Coordinated Entry systems, and administrative costs (capped at 10% of grant request).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Organization Profile Review: Friday, March 21st, 2025; Application Narrative, Budget, Performance Tool: Friday, April 25th, 2025 – 5pm
structured_extraction.program_audience: Lead agencies for Maryland's 16 Continuums of Care (CoCs) and Local Homeless Coalitions (LHCs), including HUD-approved Collaborative Applicants and DHCD-approved lead agencies for Balance of State CoC LHCs, applying on behalf of homeless services providers in their community. Lead agencies may subgrant to government agencies and nonprofit organizations. Minority, women, and youth-led organizations are encouraged to apply.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Street outreach, emergency shelter, rapid rehousing, homeless prevention/diversion, permanent supportive housing (PSH) case management, HMIS data entry and system administration, rental assistance, transitional housing, shelter operations, service-linked housing, housing navigation/aftercare services, host homes, Coordinated Entry systems, flex funds for landlord incentives and barrier removal, direct cash transfer programs for vulnerable subpopulations, and administrative costs (up to 10% cap).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland through the 16 Continuums of Care and Local Homeless Coalitions. Applicants must be part of a local Continuum of Care.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a HUD-approved Collaborative Applicant/lead agency of a Maryland Continuum of Care (CoC) or a DHCD-approved lead agency for a Balance of State CoC Local Homeless Coalition (LHC)
Applications must be submitted on behalf of homeless services providers in the community
Only eligible lead agencies may submit applications — independent or non-affiliated organizations will not be accepted
Must enroll in HMIS or comparable database for victim services providers
Must comply with HUD standards on participation, data collection, and reporting
Current/previously funded grantees must be in full compliance with HMIS implementation guidelines at application
New subgrantees must be in full compliance with HMIS at grant agreement signing
Must participate in Maryland State Homelessness Data Warehouse (MSHDW)
Must meet all data quality standards
Matching funds required (cash or non-cash contributions)
Administrative costs cannot exceed 10% cap
Victim services providers must establish comparable database and document confidentiality procedures
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Complete Organization Profile Review by Friday, March 21st, 2025. 2. Read the Application Guidance carefully before downloading and completing the forms. 3. Submit Application Narrative, Budget, and Performance Tool by Friday, April 25th, 2025 at 5pm via the Project Portal at https://projectportal.dhcd.state.md.us/. 4. Review the application training slides for guidance. 5. Contact your project manager with any questions.

structured_extraction.program_name: Homeowner Assistance Fund (HAF) WholeHome Critical Home Repairs Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: This grant helps eligible Maryland homeowners who experienced financial hardship due to the COVID-19 pandemic pay for critical repairs to their primary residence that could otherwise cause displacement. It covers repairs such as heating and cooling systems, water heaters, roofs, plumbing, electrical systems, septic systems, and mold, lead paint, or asbestos remediation. The program is funded through the federal Homeowner Assistance Fund and administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Standard grant of up to $10,000 per project. Up to $15,000 may be approved in extenuating circumstances with documentation. Payment options include 33% deposit with 67% at completion, or 0% deposit with 100% at completion. Funds are paid directly to licensed and insured Maryland Home Improvement Contractors for critical home repairs. Applications were submitted on a first-come, first-served basis and are now closed as all funding has been used.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 2, 2026 (closed early because funds ran out)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland homeowners who experienced financial hardship after January 21, 2020 due to the COVID-19 pandemic, have household income at or below 150% of County Area Median Income (AMI), and own and reside in their primary residence as named on the deed of trust.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Critical health and safety home repairs including heating and cooling systems, water heaters, electrical and plumbing/septic repairs, well repairs, roof repair or replacement, mold and mildew remediation, lead paint and asbestos removal, structural and maintenance issues, and trip/slip hazards that could cause involuntary displacement.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Maryland homeowner residing in the property as their primary residence. Program is available statewide across Maryland.
requirements_list: Experienced financial hardship after January 21, 2020 due to COVID-19
Household income at or below 150% of County Area Median Income (AMI)
Must be a Maryland homeowner and occupy the property as principal residence
Must reside in the primary residence
Must be named on the deed of trust
Must have critical repair(s) causing risk of involuntary displacement
Must provide the lowest qualifying bid/work proposal from a licensed and insured Maryland Home Improvement Contractor, dated within the last 60 days and including photos or drawings
Total repairs not to exceed $10,000
Contractor must provide: MHIC/trade license, Certificate of Liability Insurance ($1M+ per occurrence), Letter of Good Standing, and completed W-9
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications were submitted on a first-come, first-served basis. Applicants needed to submit a completed application with all required documentation via email or mail, including the lowest qualifying bid estimate from a licensed and insured Maryland Home Improvement Contractor, dated within the last 60 days and including photos. A free, in-home comprehensive assessment may be conducted to identify improvements and enroll applicants in appropriate programs. Applications are now closed as all funding has been used.

structured_extraction.program_description: The federal Housing Choice Voucher Program provides rental subsidies in the form of vouchers to eligible low-income, very low-income, and extremely low-income families or individuals to help pay for housing. Federally funded and enacted as part of the Housing and Community Development Act of 1974, the program provides housing assistance payments to help low- and very-low income families afford rental housing in neighborhoods of their choice. HUD funds local public housing agencies — typically the participant's county or municipality — to run the program, including setting eligibility criteria, processing applications, managing waitlists, and verifying requirements. Includes specialized programs: Veterans Affairs Supportive Housing (VASH), Family Unification Program (FUP), Mainstream Vouchers, and Non-Elderly Disabled (NED2) vouchers. Offers both project-based and tenant-based voucher options, a Section 8 Voucher Homeownership option, as well as the Family Self-Sufficiency (FSS) program to help families enhance economic stability. Currently administers 2,583 HCVs statewide through DHCD.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rental vouchers that eligible families or individuals can use toward housing payments. Families receive Housing Assistance Payment (HAP) contracts; DHCD pays portion of rent directly to landlord and family pays the Total Tenant Payment (TTP) based on income. Family share of rent may not exceed 40% of monthly adjusted income. Payment standards are based on family size and local Fair Market Rent. Utility reimbursement payments are provided when calculation results in payment due to family. Monthly housing assistance payments also support homeownership expenses including mortgage principal/interest, property taxes, insurance, maintenance, repairs, and utilities. Maximum assistance period of 15 years for non-elderly/disabled families; no time limit for elderly/disabled families. Maryland DHCD directly administers the program for Caroline, Dorchester, Kent, Somerset, Talbot, Wicomico, and Worcester Counties, and the City of Elkton. Other counties and municipalities operate their own programs. Includes specialized vouchers for veterans (VASH), families involved with child welfare (FUP), people with disabilities (NED2), and homeless populations. A homeownership option is also available for participants who have been assisted for at least three years, limited to five families during the first year, for purchase of single-family homes, condominiums, or manufactured homes. Mobility counseling services and access to MDhousingsearch.org database for unit matching are also provided. Portability is available for families moving outside the jurisdiction.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 30, 2026, at 5:00 PM (for Eastern Shore and Town of Elkton waitlist opening April 1, 2026)
structured_extraction.contact_name: Jacob R Day (Secretary), Julia Glanz (Deputy Secretary)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible low-income, very low-income, and extremely low-income families and individuals seeking rental assistance, including elderly families (62+), families with disabilities, veterans, homeless individuals and families, chronically homeless populations, youth aging out of foster care, domestic violence victims, displaced persons, persons at least 18 years of age or emancipated minors, and racial/ethnic groups with disproportionate housing needs. Specifically targets families at or below 30% AMI (extremely low-income), families >30% but ≤50% AMI (very low-income), and families >50% but <80% AMI (low-income). At least 75% of new admissions must be extremely low-income families. Families must meet minimum income requirements (federal minimum wage × 2,000 hours for homeownership option).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental housing payments to landlords; utility costs; childcare expenses (when enabling employment or education); medical expenses (for elderly or disabled households); disability-related expenses; Family Self-Sufficiency program support; housing accessibility modifications; landlord engagement and outreach; mobility counseling services; supportive services for employment assistance; homeownership purchase assistance for qualified participants including mortgage principal/interest, property taxes, insurance, maintenance, repairs, and utilities; homeownership counseling programs (pre- and post-purchase)
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through local public housing agencies. DHCD directly administers vouchers for Caroline, Dorchester, Kent, Somerset, Talbot, Wicomico, and Worcester Counties, and the City of Elkton, with an Eastern Shore Regional Office serving these counties. Western Maryland counties (Allegany, Frederick, Garrett) are also served. All other jurisdictions have their own local programs. Residency preference for families living or working within the jurisdiction where they applied. Families may lease units outside PHA jurisdiction under portability procedures. Families may also purchase homes in other jurisdictions with qualifying homeownership programs. Program encourages housing selection outside areas of poverty and minority concentration. Families must have domicile or legal residence in Maryland at date of initial application (with exceptions for reasonable accommodations). Portability available to families moving within United States and its territories.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local public housing agency to apply. For state-administered areas (Eastern Shore counties and City of Elkton), submit a preliminary application online at waitlistcheck.com/MD1645 or check waitlist status at waitlistcheck.com. Application process includes: intake and recertification interviews, income verification and documentation, citizenship/eligible immigration status verification at initial application and first annual reexamination, Request for Tenancy Approval submission, HQS unit inspection, and lease execution with owner. If you have a disability or need extra support, contact dhcd.hcv@maryland.gov or 410-901-4081 for assistance. Maryland Relay Service: (800) 735-2258 (for hearing impaired). Note: some county waiting lists may be closed for up to 24 months; check with the relevant PHA for current status. FSS program enrollment is encouraged for eligible participants.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Housing Innovation Pilot Program (HIPP) is a competitive funding program administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) that supports innovative approaches to multifamily affordable housing development. The program provides low- or no-interest loans through the Housing Innovation Fund to local housing authorities or county governments partnering with housing developers to increase housing production. Funds can also be used by a county, together with a local housing authority or housing developer, to purchase existing privately owned housing. The program rewards counties pursuing innovative solutions to housing scarcity and supports new construction, acquisition, or rehabilitation of mixed-income rental housing.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low- or no-interest loans provided through the Housing Innovation Fund. Short-term loans (3-5 years) at approximately 3% interest, or longer-term loans (7-10 years) at approximately 5.5% interest. Maximum award: $2.5 million per project. Total available funding: $5 million for FY 2026. Supports new construction, acquisition, or rehabilitation of mixed-income rental housing (including apartments, townhouses, single-family homes, single room occupancy buildings, and shared housing facilities), as well as purchase of existing privately owned housing. Maximum one award per jurisdiction.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public housing authorities, county governments partnering with housing developers, counties working with local housing authorities or housing developers to purchase existing privately owned housing, and developers proposing innovative approaches to affordable multifamily housing in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: New construction of multifamily rental housing, acquisition of existing private-sector housing, renovation/rehabilitation of existing housing (including major renovations), and development of innovative affordable multifamily housing. Projects must support mixed-income, cross-subsidized housing and achieve minimum 15% energy savings for rehabilitated buildings.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. New construction projects must be located in Priority Funding Areas (PFAs); rehabilitation projects are not subject to the PFA requirement. Bonus scoring for projects within 3/4 mile of planned or existing transit rail stops/stations, in ENOUGH Initiative eligible census tracts, with Just Communities designation, or in Communities of Opportunity.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a Pre-Application Meeting Request Form, then download the HIPP Application Submission Package from the DHCD document library and complete the required forms (Form 202, Form 203, Form 209, Form 212). Submit documentation for Developer, Sponsor/Owner, General Contractor, Architect, and Management Agent. Applications are evaluated on experience level (scoring: 10 points for extensive experience, 7 points for adequate experience, 4 points for limited experience, 1 point for little/no experience). Submit through the DHCD portal (Procorem) no later than 12:00 p.m. on May 18, 2026. A Waiver Request Form is also available. Refer to the Request for Proposals and Information Session Presentation/Slides for full details.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit program administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) for Maryland residents who make their homes more accessible for people with disabilities. Applicants can receive up to 50% of eligible renovation costs back, up to $5,000, for accessibility improvements made to their own home, a family member's home, or a rental property. Applicants submit an application and supporting documents by June 1st each year; DHCD reviews applications by August 31st and, if approved, issues a tax credit certificate that applicants use to file an amended Maryland tax return (Form 502X).
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax credit equal to up to 50% of eligible renovation costs, capped at $5,000 per applicant. DHCD can approve up to $1,000,000 in total credits per year; if demand exceeds this cap, individual credits may be reduced. The credit applies to renovations completed during the previous tax year. If approved, DHCD issues a tax credit certificate and applicants file an amended Maryland tax return (Form 502X) with the certification attached.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: June 1st of the current calendar year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents who have made accessibility renovations to their own home, a family member's home, or a rental property
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reimbursement of costs for home accessibility renovations such as no-step entrances, grab bars, handrails, widened doorways, chairlifts, elevators, roll-in showers, slip-resistant floors, visual alarms, accessible kitchen/bathroom features, and other modifications that improve accessibility for people with disabilities or mobility limitations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Maryland residents statewide. Renovations must be to Maryland properties only.
