Must file taxes in Maryland for the same calendar year the renovations were completed
Applicant must own home with accessibility renovations completed in applicable tax year
Applicant must have paid for renovations themselves
Must provide detailed invoices and proof of payment (receipts, invoices, before-and-after photos) for eligible accessibility renovations
Must provide pre- and post-renovation pictures
Cannot have received funds from other sources for the same renovations
Only one application per household
Must certify all information is true and correct
Must keep documentation for verification
Must submit a completed application to DHCD with supporting documentation by June 1st of the current calendar year
Renovations must have been completed during the previous tax year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Complete eligible accessibility renovations. 2. File your Maryland taxes for the tax year the renovation was completed. 3. Submit your completed application and supporting documentation (receipts, invoices, before-and-after photos) to DHCD by June 1st — either online (via the WUFOO link on the application page) or via the paper application by email or mail. 4. DHCD reviews applications by August 31st. 5. If approved, file an amended Maryland tax return (Form 502X) with the DHCD tax credit certification attached.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Indoor Plumbing Program (IPP) provides loans to fund the installation or repair of indoor plumbing in residential properties, including single-family owner-occupied homes and rental properties with one to twenty units. Eligible improvements include septic systems, wells, plumbing fixtures, piping, connections to public water or sewer systems, lead pipe replacement, and related infrastructure. The program is administered statewide by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) through a network of local administering agencies, including county housing offices.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest loans with interest rates ranging from 0% to 6% based on the applicant's income and ability to repay. The maximum loan amount is 95% of the property value (accounting for any existing mortgage) for a maximum term of 20–30 years. Deferred loans are available for health, safety, or accessibility improvements for owner-occupants at or below 50% of the applicable statewide or Washington, D.C. MSA median income. Deferred amounts may be forgiven annually for households with incomes below 30% of the applicable median income. Landlords are not eligible for deferred loans.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owner-occupants of single-family homes and owners/landlords of rental residential properties (1–20 units) who are income-eligible (at or below 80% of the statewide or Washington, D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income), as well as homeowners needing to replace or repair indoor plumbing including lead pipes.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Wells, septic tanks and drain fields, piping, connections to public water or sewer systems, plumbing fixtures and equipment including handicapped fixtures, replacement or repair of lead pipes inside the home, additions and modifications required for toilet and bath facilities, sand mound systems, purification systems, percolation tests, alternative and innovative septic and water systems, connection fees and assessments.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Loans are processed by local governments and administering agencies for properties within their jurisdiction. Income limits are based on the statewide or Washington, D.C. MSA median income depending on property location. Washington, D.C. PMSA counties include Calvert, Charles, Frederick, Montgomery, and Prince George's; all other Maryland counties use Rest of State income limits. Income limits are updated annually (effective July 1, 2025).
requirements_list: Applicant must be an owner-occupant of a single-family home or owner/landlord of a rental residential property (1–20 units)
Property must have inoperative or unsafe plumbing and be structurally sound
Owner-occupants and all residents of assisted rental housing must have income at or below 80% of the statewide or Washington, D.C. MSA median income
Loan amount may not exceed 95% of the property value accounting for any superior mortgage
Deferred payments available only for owner-occupants at or below 50% of the applicable MSA median income
Deferred amounts may be forgiven annually for households with incomes below 30% of the applicable median income
Landlords are not eligible for deferred loans
Must be an individual with limited income
Household income must not exceed specified limits based on household size and location (DC PMSA vs. Rest of State)
Income limits effective July 1, 2025
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local housing office (see the list of local contacts by county on the DHCD website) or call DHCD Special Loan Programs at 301-429-7409 or toll-free 877-218-8101. Loans are originated, packaged, and closed through DHCD's network of local administering agencies, including county housing offices, nonprofits, and local banks.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide designation program that identifies 419 Maryland communities historically harmed by exclusionary and disinvestment policies. Designated communities receive prioritized access to Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) funding programs, helping to counteract past government policies that limited wealth-building through homeownership and disinvested in minoritized neighborhoods. Based on HB 241 and SB 308 (2024 legislative session), the program provides a five-year designation to prioritize state investments and advance economic, racial, and health equity. Areas are identified through a data-driven scoring process using 14 legislatively mandated criteria including homeownership rates, housing cost burden, historical redlining, environmental contamination, imprisonment rates, lead paint exposure, and asthma rates.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Applicants located in a designated Just Community are prioritized for state investment when applying for eligible DHCD funding programs, including energy efficiency grants, housing repair loans, business loans, tax credits, and community revitalization grants. Designated areas receive concentrated state investment to advance equity, create opportunities, and repair past harms. Areas are identified through data-driven analysis; census tracts must score ≥13.5 on the Just Communities Score and be within Maryland Priority Funding Areas.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals, businesses, non-profits, and governments located within one of the 419 designated Just Communities in Maryland that have been historically affected by exclusionary policies and disinvestment. Communities that have borne the brunt of segregation, discrimination, and place-based harm, including socioeconomically marginalized and minoritized communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Prioritization for existing DHCD funding programs covering energy efficiency, home repair, business development, housing counseling, neighborhood revitalization, and tax credits. State investment prioritization in designated Just Communities to support development, infrastructure, and community well-being.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in 419 designated Just Communities throughout the State of Maryland. Areas are census tracts within Maryland Priority Funding Areas scoring 13.5 or greater on the Just Communities Score, identified through a data-driven scoring process based on factors such as homeownership rates, property values, redlining history, vacancy rates, proximity to Superfund sites, lead-based paint exposure, asthma rates, imprisonment rates, and other indicators of disinvestment.
requirements_list: Applicant or project must be located in one of the 419 designated Just Communities
Must be applying for an eligible DHCD funding program
Just Community status is verified at time of application to eligible programs
Census tracts must score ≥13.5 on the Just Communities Score
Must be within Maryland Priority Funding Areas

Score based on weighted quartile analysis of criteria including homeownership rates, housing cost burden, historical redlining, environmental contamination, imprisonment rates, lead paint exposure, and asthma rates
Evidence of legal racial segregation, mass incarceration impacts, or unequal environmental/health hazard exposure
Past and current economic and housing trends demonstrating reinvestment need
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: When applying for eligible DHCD funding programs, applicants are asked whether they are located in a designated Just Community. If yes, their application is prioritized for state investment. Use the Just Communities Geographic Viewer map to check if a location is designated. Areas are identified through data-driven analysis; the DHCD Secretary recommends communities to the Governor for designation based on mapping exercise and criteria analysis.

structured_extraction.program_description: DHCD received $4 million from HUD's Office of Lead Hazard Control and Healthy Homes to help Maryland homeowners and landlords remove lead hazards from their properties. Grants of up to $25,000 per eligible property owner are available for lead abatement work performed by licensed and accredited contractors. The program also offers amortizing loans (0%-7%, 20-year term) and deferred loans (0%, 20-year term) for lead hazard reduction treatment in residential properties. Funding is available statewide except in Baltimore City, until April 1, 2029.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $25,000 per unit (annual sponsor maximum $100,000) for lead hazard reduction treatment in residential properties. Also offers amortizing loans at 0%-7% for 20-year terms and deferred loans at 0% for 20-year terms. Match requirements vary by applicant type: 20% for for-profit sponsors, 10% for nonprofit sponsors, and 10% for owner-occupants with income above 80% AMI. Clearance testing required. Available statewide except in Baltimore City. Funding is available until April 1, 2029.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland homeowners, landlords, for-profit and nonprofit sponsors, and licensed day care centers seeking to remove lead hazards from their properties, excluding properties located in Baltimore City. Households must meet income limits (up to 80% AMI).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Lead hazard reduction treatment, lead abatement in pre-1978 homes, lead testing costs, risk reduction treatments, rehabilitation and construction costs, site/exterior work, professional fees (architect, legal, testing), and administrative costs
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland, except in the City of Baltimore. Income limits vary by location (Washington DC PMSA counties: Calvert, Charles, Frederick, Montgomery, Prince George's vs. Rest of State).
requirements_list: Must be a homeowner, landlord, for-profit or nonprofit sponsor, or licensed day care center in Maryland
Property must not be located in the City of Baltimore
Lead abatement work must be performed by a licensed and accredited lead abatement contractor
Clearance testing required after lead hazard reduction work
Match requirement: 20% for for-profit sponsors; 10% for nonprofit sponsors; 10% for owner-occupants with income above 80% AMI
Household income must not exceed specified limits based on household size, location (Washington DC PMSA vs. Rest of State), and income tier (up to 80% AMI)
Property must be properly zoned for proposed use
For rental properties (1-4 units), all units must be occupied by families of limited or lower income upon completion
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application using the Application Form or Sponsor Application Form available on the DHCD website. Contact Special Loan Programs at 301-429-7409 or DHCD.SpecialLoans@maryland.gov for more information, or contact a local county contact for assistance. Toll-free: 877-218-8101.

structured_extraction.program_name: Lead Hazard Reduction Grant and Loan Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This state-funded program helps make Maryland homes safer by removing or reducing lead-based paint hazards in residential buildings and daycare centers. It provides grants, amortizing loans, and deferred loans to owner-occupants of single-family homes, landlords of rental properties (including multi-family), and licensed residential childcare facilities. Financial assistance is based on the applicant's ability to repay and location. Grants are available up to $25,000 per unit; amortizing loans at 0%-7% interest for up to 20 years; deferred loans at 0% interest for up to 20 years, which may be forgiven if no equity is available after 20 years or upon property resale/transfer.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $25,000 per unit. Amortizing loans at 0%-7% interest, 20-year term, up to $25,000 per unit. Deferred loans at 0% interest, 20-year term, up to $25,000 per unit; may be forgiven if no equity available after 20 years or upon property resale/transfer. For the broader Maryland Home Rehabilitation Program, maximum loan is $50,000 with up to 30-year term and interest rates from 0%-6%. Deferred payment options available for families at or below 50% AMI. Grants require a 20% match for for-profit sponsors, 10% for nonprofits/owner-occupants above 80% AMI. No income limits in targeted areas; elsewhere the limit is 80% of Area Median Income (AMI). Eligible costs include door and window treatments and replacement, floor treatments, paint removal, stabilization and repainting, encapsulation, enclosure, specialized cleaning, lead testing, and other approved lead hazard reduction methods.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland homeowner-occupants, landlords of residential rental properties (single-family and multi-family), licensed residential childcare facilities, and sponsors/developers of 1-4 unit residential rental housing for limited-income families seeking to reduce lead hazards
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Lead hazard reduction activities including door and window treatments and replacement, floor treatments, paint removal, stabilization and repainting, encapsulation, enclosure, specialized cleaning, lead testing, rehabilitation and construction costs, site/exterior work, architect/legal fees, and other approved lead hazard reduction methods. Acquisition costs cannot be financed with MHRP funds.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland across all 23 counties; grants available in certain target areas; income limits vary by household size and geography (Washington DC PMSA counties vs. Rest of State)
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Maryland resident if an owner-occupant, and must own and occupy the dwelling as a principal residence
Rental properties must be registered with the Maryland Department of the Environment Lead Poisoning Prevention Program
Property must be in need of lead hazard reduction activity
Property must be structurally sound upon completion of lead hazard reduction activity
Income must be at or below 80% of Area Median Income (AMI) outside of targeted areas; no income limit in targeted areas
Licensed residential childcare facilities may also be eligible
Sponsor properties must be 1-4 units
Lead testing required and results must be submitted
For-profit sponsors require a 20% match for grants; nonprofits/owner-occupants above 80% AMI require a 10% match
Non-profit sponsors must provide 501(c)(3) verification
Deferred payment loans available for families at or below 50% AMI
Income limits vary by household size and county/region (Washington DC PMSA vs. Rest of State)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an Application Form or Sponsor Application Form available on the DHCD website. Contact Special Loan Programs by phone (301-429-7409 or toll-free 877-218-8101) or email (DHCD.SpecialLoans@maryland.gov). Local county contacts (Special Loan Program Partners) can also provide program and application information.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development's Community Development Administration (CDA) issues tax-exempt bonds on behalf of Maryland counties, municipalities, and their agencies to finance public infrastructure projects. Bond proceeds are loaned to local governments at rates based on market conditions at the time of the pooled bond sale. The program pools local demand to reduce issuance costs and provides bond counsel, a financial advisor, and expertise to help local governments navigate tax-exempt bond financing without having to initiate the process entirely on their own.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Community Development Administration issues tax-exempt bonds and loans the proceeds to local governments. Loan amounts can range from $150,000 to $10 million or more. The interest rate is based on market conditions at the time the pooled bonds are sold. The loan term is set by the local government but cannot exceed the useful life of the project or 30 years, whichever is less. Local governments must repay the debt and pay their pro-rata share of bond issuance costs, pledging full faith and credit as security.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland counties, municipalities, and their agencies that need long-term capital financing for public infrastructure projects but do not routinely issue bonds or have limited resources to initiate financing on their own.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eligible projects include streetscape improvements, street lighting, landscaping, sidewalks, public space improvements, public safety vehicles and equipment, water production and treatment systems, stormwater control and sewer facilities, government office and meeting facilities, police, fire, transportation, education, health, recreation, and maintenance facilities, and refinancing of existing eligible project debt.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to all Maryland counties, municipalities, and their instrumentalities with the legal authority to construct, operate, and maintain the proposed project, pledge security, and repay the loan.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Maryland county, municipality, or their agency
Applicant must have legal authority to construct, operate, and maintain the proposed project
Applicant must have legal authority to pledge security for and repay the proposed loan

Project must support an essential physical element of a municipality's public service system
Project must meet federal tax law requirements
Project must be undertaken by or on behalf of a local government or its agencies
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Local governments must complete an application that collects information similar to what a bond rating agency would require to evaluate creditworthiness. Those seeking technical assistance before applying may submit an Expression of Interest form outlining the proposed project or specific questions. An online form is available at https://dhcd.wufoo.com/forms/r5qnekm1sfg0sf. The CDA provides bond counsel and a financial advisor to assist throughout the process. Bond issuance timing depends on the volume and frequency of participation by local governments.

structured_extraction.program_name: Low Income Housing Tax Credit (LIHTC) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Federal Low-Income Housing Tax Credit (LIHTC) program was created by the Tax Reform Act of 1986 to encourage private sector investment in the construction and rehabilitation of rental housing for low- and moderate-income families. Maryland receives an annual tax credit allocation based on population, administered in accordance with Section 42 of the Internal Revenue Code by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development. Tax credits are awarded competitively to nonprofit and for-profit sponsors of eligible housing projects based on criteria in the State's Qualified Allocation Plan (QAP). Projects financed with tax-exempt bonds may also be eligible outside the competitive process. Credits are typically claimed over a 10-year period and can be sold to investors to raise equity financing for housing projects. Sponsors or their investor partners claim the credit on their federal income tax returns. Ten percent of Maryland's annual allocation is set aside solely for nonprofit sponsors, and buildings must remain in compliance with income, rent, and occupancy requirements for a minimum of 40 years under a recorded covenant. Enterprise Community Partners also helps developers access and use these credits to finance affordable housing projects.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax credits equal to an applicable percentage (determined by the IRS) of the qualified basis of each qualified low-income rental housing building. Credits are typically claimed over a 10-year period and can be sold to investors to raise equity financing for housing projects. Ten percent of Maryland's annual allocation is set aside solely for nonprofit sponsors. Credits are claimed on the sponsor's or investor partner's federal income tax return. Projects must remain in compliance with income, rent, and occupancy requirements for a minimum of 40 years under a recorded covenant. Awards are made competitively based on the State's Qualified Allocation Plan (QAP). Annual income and rent limits are updated (effective April 1, 2025 for properties with Placed in Service date of May 15, 2023 or later; Hold Harmless provisions apply to earlier PIS properties).

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction and rehabilitation of residential rental housing for low- and moderate-income families; utility allowance calculations and compliance documentation; ongoing compliance with income, rent, and occupancy requirements

Projects financed with tax-exempt bonds may be eligible outside the competitive process. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis. Owners must complete annual Owner's Certificate of Continuing Program Compliance and certify compliance with federal tax code requirements and state regulations. For more information, visit the Multifamily Document Library on the DHCD website or contact the program directly.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Digital Inclusion Grant Program (MD-DIG) provides competitive grant funding to expand digital inclusion across Maryland. Funded by the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021 with $2 million total available, it supports access to high-speed internet and digital literacy by funding digital inclusion planning, program implementation, workforce training, and public access computing centers for underserved populations including low-income households, aging individuals, individuals with disabilities, individuals with language barriers, racial and ethnic minorities, and rural residents.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two types of competitive grants: (1) Digital Inclusion Planning — up to 50% of planning costs, grants between $5,000 and $30,000. (2) Digital Inclusion Program Implementation — up to 100% of implementation costs, grants between $10,000 and $75,000. $2 million total available, funded by the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021. Individual grant amounts may be reduced based on the impact of the applicant's intended population and ability to deploy funds.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications for funding will be accepted through March 31, 2022
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments (counties and municipalities), 501(c) nonprofit organizations providing services in Maryland, and community-based anchor institutions serving underserved populations including low-income households, aging individuals, individuals with disabilities, individuals with language barriers, racial and ethnic minorities, and rural residents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Developing a digital inclusion plan; implementing, expanding, or continuing digital inclusion activities; facilitating broadband adoption for covered populations; providing training programs covering basic, advanced, and applied skills or other workforce development programs; constructing, upgrading, expanding, or operating public access computing centers through community anchor institutions.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD), through its Office of Statewide Broadband (OSB), administers the Connected Communities Grant Program (MD-GAPS). The program assists local governments, non-profits, community-based organizations, and anchor institutions in building, expanding, or operating gap networks and community networks that provide low-cost or no-cost broadband internet access to low- and moderate-income households and other underserved populations. The program is funded by the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021 with $5 million total available.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of between $25,000 and $250,000, covering up to 100% of costs for the construction, deployment, expansion, or continued operation of community-based gap networks and community networks. $5 million total available, funded by the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021. Funding is competitive and individual award amounts may be reduced based on the applicant's intended population impact and ability to deploy funds promptly. Award types include network infrastructure grants for broadband expansion, neighborhood connectivity grants for community access to broadband, emergency education relief grants for broadband access at key facilities, and project-based awards for specific road/area broadband extensions.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications for funding will be accepted through March 31, 2022
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments (counties and municipalities), non-profit 501(c) organizations providing services in Maryland, community-based anchor institutions, other community-based organizations serving low- to moderate-income households and other covered populations, Internet Service Providers (ISPs), public schools and school systems, libraries, churches and religious institutions, housing authorities and housing partnerships, YMCAs, and educational institutions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Equipment, networking hardware and software, digital network technology, and infrastructure needed to provide broadband internet service at low or no cost to covered populations. This includes building new gap/community networks, upgrading or expanding existing networks, operating and maintaining networks, and purchasing end-user equipment such as routers, switches, antennas, modems, and access points. Also includes fiber optic installation, broadband access equipment and connectivity at community facilities, and rural broadband extensions. Eligible projects must provide a minimum of 100 Mbps download and 100 Mbps upload speeds.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be providing services within the State of Maryland and must be registered with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation. Awards have been made across a wide range of Maryland counties including Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Caroline, Carroll, Cecil, Charles, Dorchester, Frederick, Harford, Howard, Kent, Montgomery, Prince George's, Queen Anne's, Somerset, St. Mary's, Talbot, Washington, Wicomico, and Worcester counties.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local government (county or municipality), a non-profit 501(c) organization providing services in Maryland, a community-based anchor institution, or another community-based organization.
Applicant must be registered and in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation.
Project must be designed to reliably provide a minimum of 100 Mbps download and 100 Mbps upload internet connectivity.
Only fully complete applications at the time of submission will be considered for funding.

Eligible projects must serve covered populations: households at or below 150% of the federal poverty level, aging individuals, individuals with disabilities, individuals with language barriers, and racial or ethnic minority group members.
Project must address internet affordability for low- to moderate-income households.
All federal rules of the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021 apply.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a completed application and all required supporting documents via email to OSB.MD@Maryland.gov by March 31, 2022. The application must include a project summary (executive summary, statement of experience, network design, community profile, subscriber cost, potential barriers, partners and local engagement, intended outcomes and metrics, schedule, and funding scope and budget), a signed application form, IRS Determination Letter (if non-profit), Certificate of Good Standing from the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation, IRS W-9 form, and a DUNS number. Application guide and form are available for download.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Main Street Improvement Program (MIP) Grant provides operating assistance funding to designated and affiliate Main Street Maryland communities and Baltimore City's designated Main Street neighborhoods. The goal is to help these communities build capacity for revitalization and economic development in designated Sustainable Community areas across Maryland.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Operating assistance grants are awarded in three tiers: $33,000 for designated Main Street Maryland communities with full accreditation, $25,000 for designated communities with affiliate accreditation, and $12,000 for Main Street Maryland Aspiring Communities. Final amounts are contingent on approval by the General Assembly during the FY2027 legislative session. Grants cover operating expenses only — no capital project costs. Eligible uses include staff and consultant services, general operating expenses, market and business recruitment strategies, marketing and advertising, placemaking initiatives, and other activities identified in the applicant's annual work plan. No funding match is required. Projects must be completed within one year.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Main Street Maryland Program is a statewide effort coordinated by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development that supports the revitalization, preservation, and economic development of historic downtown business districts and traditional commercial districts. It operates as Maryland's coordinating program for the National Main Street Center and connects designated communities to resources, a statewide network of professionals, training, and technical assistance. The program is based on the National Main Street Center approach and emphasizes historic preservation, adaptive reuse, and quality of place. The program operates through a tiered designation framework (Designated, Aspiring, and Connected Main Streets), with Aspiring Main Streets completing a two-year training program to build a strong foundation and work toward national accreditation. An annual Main Street Maryland Conference provides keynote speakers, workshops, and networking sessions to strengthen local main streets.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers a tiered designation framework (Designated, Aspiring, and Connected Main Streets) with training programs, technical assistance, and coordination support to help communities pursue revitalization of historic downtowns and commercial districts. Assistance includes designated community status, a variety of training opportunities (classroom, virtual, and recorded presentations), topical resource documents and manuals, support for organizing volunteer committees, and facilitation of downtown revitalization efforts. Aspiring Main Streets complete a two-year training program to build a strong foundation and work toward national accreditation. Designated communities receive connection to a statewide network of professionals, access to training and resources, participation in the annual Main Street Maryland Conference (including keynote speakers, workshops, and networking sessions), and funding support for downtown revitalization and economic development in traditional main street areas.

structured_extraction.program_audience: City/town officials and leaders, local nonprofit organizations, community volunteers, business owners, and downtown stakeholders seeking economic revitalization, preservation, and strengthening of their main streets and traditional commercial districts in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Revitalization, preservation, and economic development of historic downtown business districts and traditional commercial districts, including economic development activities, historic and cultural preservation, volunteer and partnership development, and improvements to the physical appearance of commercial districts.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program helps make housing more affordable for Maryland households with low incomes. It provides funding for various housing-related costs. These costs include construction, nonprofit developer support, resident services, and operating expenses. A Board of Trustees governs the program, which the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development manages.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides funding as grants for capacity building, operating costs, and support services. It offers deferred-payment loans or recoverable grants for capital costs. These are repayable if the project is sold or no longer serves low-income residents. Pre-development awards are typically loans that must be repaid.
structured_extraction.program_audience: This program is for nonprofit organizations, public housing authorities, government agencies, and for-profit companies that develop affordable housing.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used for: capital costs for rental and homeownership housing; financial help for nonprofit developers to build their capacity; supportive services for residents of affordable housing; and operating costs for affordable housing projects.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Capital Access Program (MCAP) is a credit enhancement program that helps small businesses in Priority Funding Areas across Maryland access financing. The program establishes a Loan Reserve Program to encourage lenders to make loans to businesses that might otherwise have difficulty obtaining financing. The program enables private lenders to set up a loan loss reserve fund using fees paid by lenders, borrowers, and the State of Maryland, making it easier for small businesses to get loans that fall slightly outside a lender's normal credit guidelines. State funds of $1 million leverage approximately $33 million in small business loans. Note: There are currently no lenders participating in the program; contact DHCD to learn about other lending programs.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Credit enhancement program where enrolled loan amounts may range from $10,000 to $1,000,000 (maximum enrolled loan amount of $250,000 per the existing DB record). The lender, borrower, and the program each contribute to a loan loss reserve account. Typically the borrower and lender each contribute 1.5% (totaling 3%) and the program matches that with a 3% contribution, for a total reserve of 6% of the original loan amount. The program can cover up to 100% of losses for participating lenders. Loans can have a term up to ten years. Can be used for both lines of credit and term loans. State funds of $1 million leverage approximately $33 million in small business loans.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on rolling basis; contact for additional information
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland small businesses and nonprofit organizations located in Priority Funding Areas, with fewer than 50 employees and meeting SBA size standards
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business financing through lines of credit and term loans, including start-up costs, business expansion, or working capital. Cannot be used for passive real estate ownership, residential or transient living facilities, certain community facilities (community halls, fire stations, hospitals, colleges, universities), adult entertainment businesses, check cashing, gambling, liquor stores, massage parlors, pawn or gun shops, tanning salons, tattoo parlors, or sectarian religious instruction.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be located in a Maryland Priority Funding Area approved by the Maryland Department of Planning under the Smart Growth Act of 1997. The program is available to businesses located throughout Maryland within designated Priority Funding Areas.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: A small business applies to a participating lender. The lender submits a one-page enrollment form with summary information to the Maryland Capital Access Program. The lender, borrower, and the MD CAP program all contribute to a reserve fund to cover potential losses. If a loan defaults, the lender files a claim using a one-page form.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Connected Devices Program (MD-CDP) is a statewide digital equity and inclusion initiative administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD). It provides new, internet-enabled devices (HP Chromebook 14 G7 or similar) to counties and municipal governments for distribution to eligible low-income households who cannot afford a device. The program addresses the digital divide by giving families access to the technology needed to connect to the internet, particularly those who struggled during the COVID pandemic without adequate technology. Eligible households are those with income at or below 200% of the Federal Poverty Guidelines. One device per address is allowed. A stipend of $6 per device is available to the distributing government to help with distribution costs. Round one awarded 91,300 devices; round two awarded the remaining allotment with priority for new eligible applicants. For example, St. Mary's County was approved for 4,500 devices valued at $894,375 plus $27,000 in distribution support, and Carroll County distributed up to 5,000 free HP Chromebook laptops to eligible residents through distribution events and partner organizations, with devices including setup instructions and information for internet access.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of internet-enabled devices (HP Chromebook 14 G7 or similar, with 13" screen, Chrome OS, SD card reader, dual-band Wi-Fi, 2 USB ports, headphone and video output jacks, and a one-year manufacturer's warranty) to counties and municipal governments for distribution to eligible low-income households. Eligible households must have income at or below 200% of the Federal Poverty Guidelines, with one device per address. A stipend of $6 per device is available to the distributing government to help with distribution costs. Round one awarded 91,300 devices; round two awarded the remaining allotment with priority for new eligible applicants. Carroll County distributed up to 5,000 free Chromebooks to eligible residents while supplies last through distribution events or partner organizations. St. Mary's County received 4,500 devices valued at $894,375 plus $27,000 in distribution support.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides capital funding to local governments and community development organizations to improve the exterior facades of commercial buildings and facilities located in designated Maryland Sustainable Communities — geographic areas targeted for revitalization. Approximately $5 million in capital funding is available for FY2025. Funds are used to capitalize a local grants fund that local governments or community development organizations administer, allowing businesses in eligible Sustainable Communities to apply for capital costs related to improving the exterior facades of their buildings. The program supports community revitalization and downtown improvement efforts statewide, bolstering economic vitality and stimulating private investment through consistent, attractive designs for commercial corridors. Eligible exterior improvements include painting, siding, windows, shingles, rain gutters, porch repair, storefront reconstruction, exterior lighting, masonry, murals, signage, and related work. Minimum award is $1,000 and maximum is $50,000 per business per award cycle. Technical assistance and information are also available to applicants.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Approximately $5 million in capital funding available for FY2025. Funds are used to capitalize a local grants fund that local governments or community development organizations administer. Businesses in eligible Sustainable Communities can then apply to that fund for capital costs related to improving the exterior facades of their buildings and facilities. Minimum award is $1,000 and maximum is $50,000 per business per award cycle. Eligible exterior improvements include painting, siding, shingles, windows, rain gutters, porch repair, storefront reconstruction, exterior lighting, masonry, murals, signage, ADA accessibility upgrades, energy efficiency upgrades, and related work. Properties over 50 years old are subject to the Federal Secretary of Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation. Technical assistance and information are also provided to applicants.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, groups of local governments, community development organizations (such as community development corporations, main street organizations, and downtown partnerships), nonprofits, for-profit entities, and property owners seeking to support façade improvements for businesses in Sustainable Communities and commercial areas. End beneficiaries include business owners and operators of commercial properties, property owners/landlords, businesses serving important community needs, and legacy and minority businesses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital costs related to improving the exterior facades of business buildings and facilities located in designated Maryland Sustainable Communities, including painting, siding, shingles, windows, rain gutters, porch repair, storefront reconstruction, exterior lighting, masonry, murals, signage, ADA accessibility upgrades, energy efficiency upgrades, restoration of historical features, and related exterior work. Improvements should prioritize aesthetic improvements over routine maintenance and focus on primary elevations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located within designated Maryland Sustainable Communities. Eligibility can be checked using the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper. Available statewide in Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Foreclosure Mediation Program allows homeowners facing foreclosure on their primary residence to request a mediation session with their lender. A neutral administrative law judge from the Maryland Office of Administrative Hearings facilitates the session to help both parties explore options and reach a voluntary agreement to avoid foreclosure, such as a loan modification, short sale, deed in lieu of foreclosure, or other loss mitigation arrangement. Homeowners must request mediation within 25 days of receiving the required form from their lender after foreclosure proceedings begin. Free or reduced-fee legal services are also available through partner organizations for low- and moderate-income households.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Homeowners pay a non-refundable $50 filing fee to the Circuit Court to request mediation. A trained administrative law judge from the Maryland Office of Administrative Hearings mediates between the homeowner and lender to help reach a voluntary agreement, such as a loan modification, short sale, deed in lieu of foreclosure, or other arrangement to avoid foreclosure sale. Mediation must occur within 60 days of the Office of Administrative Hearings receiving the request. Free or reduced-fee legal services are also available through partner organizations for low- and moderate-income households.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Within 25 days of receiving the Final Loss Mitigation Affidavit and Request for Foreclosure Mediation form from the lender
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland homeowners who have received a foreclosure action filed on or after July 1, 2010 on their primary residence and are currently living in the property as their principal residence
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Mediation sessions to explore options and negotiate with the lender to reach a voluntary agreement to avoid or manage foreclosure, such as a loan modification or other loss mitigation option

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Once the lender initiates foreclosure proceedings, they must send the homeowner a Request for Foreclosure Mediation form along with the Final Loss Mitigation Affidavit. The homeowner has 25 days to complete the form, attach the $50 non-refundable fee, and file both with the Circuit Court in the county or city where the foreclosure action was filed. A copy must also be sent to the lender's attorney using the preprinted envelopes provided. The court then refers the request to the Office of Administrative Hearings, which schedules and conducts the mediation session within 60 days of receiving the request.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide program providing financial assistance to Maryland homeowners who experienced financial hardship due to the COVID-19 pandemic after January 21, 2021, helping them with mortgage payments and other housing costs. The program was funded with approximately $250 million and scheduled to run through September 2026 or until funds are exhausted. As of the most recent review, the program is no longer accepting applications, and homeowners are directed to contact a HUD-certified housing counseling agency or the State Tax Sale Ombudsman for assistance. Homeowners at risk of tax sale may also qualify for the Homeowner Protection Program, which can keep a home out of tax sale for at least 3 years and help pay delinquent property taxes.

The program was scheduled to end September 2026 or when funds are exhausted, whichever came first. Specific per-household assistance amounts were not publicly stated. The Homeowner Protection Program component can also help pay delinquent property taxes and keep a home out of tax sale for at least 3 years. The program is no longer accepting applications.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Housing Counseling Fund Program / Maryland HOPE Counseling Network
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Housing Counseling Fund (MHCF) provides competitive grants awarded annually to non-profit organizations and local government agencies to support housing counseling services and free or low-cost legal assistance statewide. Funded activities include homebuyer education, pre-purchase counseling, foreclosure counseling, rental counseling, financial capability coaching, and legal services for homeowners facing foreclosure and renters facing eviction. HUD-approved housing counseling agencies with HUD-certified counselors on staff receive priority funding consideration. The program also operates the Maryland HOPE Counseling Network, a statewide network of more than 30 nonprofit housing counselors that connects distressed homeowners with safe, reliable information about alternatives to foreclosure. Counselors help individuals facing foreclosure by negotiating with mortgage servicers and advising homeowners on the best actions to save their homes.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants awarded annually to support operating costs of housing counseling programs and legal services providers; grantees must submit quarterly progress reports by the 15th of the month following the end of each quarter. Priority funding consideration is given to HUD-approved housing counseling agencies with HUD-certified counselors on staff. Additionally, free housing counseling and foreclosure prevention assistance is available through the Maryland HOPE Counseling Network. Homeowners can connect with a counselor by calling the Maryland Hope Hotline at 877-462-7555.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations and local government agencies that provide housing counseling or free/low-cost legal assistance to homeowners and renters in Maryland, as well as Maryland homeowners who are delinquent on their mortgage, at risk of becoming delinquent, or at some stage in the foreclosure process.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating support for housing counseling programs (homebuyer education, pre-purchase counseling, foreclosure counseling, rental counseling, financial capability coaching) and legal services for homeowners at risk of foreclosure and renters at risk of eviction. The counseling network also provides free foreclosure prevention assistance directly to distressed homeowners.

For counseling services: Call the Maryland Hope Hotline at 877-462-7555 to be connected with a housing counselor in the network.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Housing Fund Mortgage Insurance Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Housing Fund (MHF) provides credit enhancements and loan insurance to make loans financed by DHCD and other lenders safer and more available to people and developers in Maryland. It promotes the development of affordable single-family and multifamily housing across the state and supports economic development in priority funding areas. The program insures mortgage loans to protect lenders against monetary losses in the event of default. It covers construction and permanent loans for multifamily housing (apartments, senior housing, housing for people with disabilities), supports nonprofits financing group homes through the Special Housing Opportunities Program (SHOP), and helps lenders offer mortgages in areas with declining homeownership through its Revitalization Program. MHF also supports a loan program to protect and strengthen property values in targeted areas of Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MHF provides credit enhancements and loan insurance for: (1) Construction and permanent loans for building or rehabilitating multifamily housing (apartments, senior housing, housing for people with disabilities), including federally subsidized projects; (2) Special Housing Opportunities Program (SHOP) — helps nonprofits finance or refinance group homes and shared living facilities for people with special needs; (3) Revitalization Program — makes it safer for lenders to offer mortgages in areas with declining homeownership, helping buyers who cannot afford repairs or closing costs. MHF also supports a loan program to protect and strengthen property values in targeted areas of Baltimore City. The program insures mortgage loans, protecting lenders against financial losses if a borrower defaults.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Housing Rehabilitation Program (MHRP) provides affordable rehabilitation loans to owner-occupants of single-family homes and landlords of one-to-four unit rental properties to address critical health and safety issues and bring properties into compliance with applicable building codes and standards. Eligible repairs include mold remediation, roof repair, lead abatement, electrical and plumbing issues, structural repairs, accessibility improvements for seniors and people with disabilities, energy conservation measures, and elimination of lead-based paint hazards. The program is administered statewide by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development through local governments and their partner nonprofit organizations. In Frederick County, the program is administered locally by the Frederick County Division of Housing. In Hagerstown, the program is administered locally by the City of Hagerstown Department of Housing & Community Development. Eligible applicants include low- and moderate-income homeowners and sponsors of small rental properties. Programs address rehabilitation, energy conservation, lead paint abatement, accessibility, and installation of indoor plumbing. Up to 40% of amortizing MHRP loans may be used for general property improvements. Household income may not exceed 80% of the Adjusted Median Income published annually by DHCD.

eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans up to $50,000 (or up to 110% of the property's value accounting for any existing mortgage) with interest rates from 0% to 6% based on the applicant's ability to repay and household income. Maximum loan term is 30 years (20 years for some local programs). Loans over $5,000 or with deferred payments are secured by a mortgage. Households with incomes at or below 50% of the statewide or Washington D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income may qualify for deferred payments if needed for project feasibility; in exceptional cases, deferred loans may be considered for borrowers up to 80% of median income. Landlords are not eligible for deferred loans. Up to 40% of amortizing MHRP loans may be used for general property improvements. Funds may be used for home rehabilitation, remodeling, energy conservation, accessibility, plumbing, wells, sewer, lead hazard reduction, or meeting building code requirements. Maximum initial deposit is 33% of total project cost.

Available statewide, including Frederick County residents served through the Frederick County Division of Housing, and Hagerstown residents served through the City of Hagerstown Department of Housing & Community Development.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Microenterprise Loan Program (MLP) provides flexible financing to help entrepreneurs start and expand microenterprises (businesses with 5 or fewer employees and under $500,000 in annual revenue). Loans are delivered through community-based microlenders (called Intermediaries) operating in designated Sustainable Communities and Priority Funding Areas across Maryland. The program also connects borrowers with training and technical assistance. Funds can be used for leasehold improvements, equipment purchases, working capital, real estate acquisition down payments, minor renovations, marketing/planning/feasibility studies, and human capital increases to expand an established business or fund a feasible start-up. Intermediary partners include Baltimore Community Lending (Baltimore City), Enterprise Development Group, Latino Economic Development Center, Maryland Capital Enterprises, Inc., FSC First, Prince George's Financial Service Corporation, and Eastern Shore Entrepreneurship Center (Venture Ahead). In Caroline County, loans are administered by Maryland Capital Enterprises, Inc. and the Eastern Shore Entrepreneurship Center.

Interest rates up to 12% (determined at underwriting). Loan term of 2 to 5 years (cannot exceed 5 years). Collateral is required (personal guarantees, liens on business assets, pledges of accounts). No prepayment penalties. Loans may be used as part of larger aggregate financing packages for eligible businesses. FSC First applicants may apply online through the FSC First application portal.

structured_extraction.program_description: Opportunity Zones are a federal tax incentive created by the 2017 Tax Cuts and Jobs Act to encourage long-term private investment in low-income census tracts. Investors who reinvest unrealized capital gains into a Qualified Opportunity Fund can temporarily defer taxes on those gains, reduce the amount owed, or permanently exclude gains earned from long-term Opportunity Zone investments. The program aims to spur business creation, affordable housing development, infrastructure investment, and economic growth in designated low-income areas. Maryland has 149 designated Opportunity Zones statewide, with at least one in every county, including areas in Denton and Federalsburg in Caroline County, Salisbury in Wicomico County, four tracts in Anne Arundel County (one in Odenton and three in Brooklyn Park), designated tracts in Garrett County near Keyser's Ridge Business Park, Southern Garrett Business & Technology Park, and commercial sites along Francis Sanders Drive in Mountain Lake Park, and designated Opportunity Zone areas within the City of Hagerstown and Washington County. The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) administers the program in the state with support from the Maryland Department of Commerce. There is no cap on the amount of capital that can be invested. The program provides preferential treatment on capital gains taxes to encourage economic growth through 2027.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Investors receive three federal tax incentives: (1) Temporary Deferral — capital gains reinvested in a Qualified Opportunity Fund are deferred from taxable income until the investment is sold or December 31, 2026, whichever comes first. (2) Step-Up in Basis — the taxable basis of the reinvested gain increases by 10% if the fund investment is held at least 5 years, and by an additional 5% (total 15%) if held at least 7 years, excluding up to 15% of the original gain from taxes. (3) Permanent Exclusion — capital gains accrued within a Qualified Opportunity Fund investment are permanently excluded from taxable income if the investment is held for at least 10 years. There is no authorized cap on the amount of capital that can flow through Opportunity Zone investments. The program runs through 2027. Designated Opportunity Zone tracts exist throughout Maryland, including four tracts in Anne Arundel County (Odenton and Brooklyn Park), areas in Caroline County (Denton and Federalsburg), Wicomico County (Salisbury), Garrett County (near Keyser's Ridge Business Park, Southern Garrett Business & Technology Park, and Mountain Lake Park), and designated areas within the City of Hagerstown and Washington County.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private investors and businesses with capital gains or unrealized capital gains who want to invest in distressed communities designated as Opportunity Zones in Maryland, including areas in Denton and Federalsburg in Caroline County, Salisbury in Wicomico County, Odenton and Brooklyn Park in Anne Arundel County, designated tracts in Garrett County, designated Opportunity Zone areas within the City of Hagerstown, and other designated zones throughout Washington County and statewide, seeking to invest in qualifying business, residential, and infrastructure projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Investment in eligible Opportunity Zone property and businesses located within designated Opportunity Zones through a Qualified Opportunity Fund, including business stock, partnership interests, business property, startup businesses, workforce and affordable housing development, new infrastructure, capital improvements to underutilized assets, and new capital investments in business and residential projects in designated Opportunity Zone areas statewide, including small businesses and real estate within Washington County and Hagerstown's designated Opportunity Zones.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in 149 designated Opportunity Zone census tracts throughout Maryland, with at least one in every county, including designated areas in Denton and Federalsburg (Caroline County), Salisbury (Wicomico County), four tracts in Anne Arundel County (one in Odenton and three in Brooklyn Park), Garrett County tracts near Keyser's Ridge Business Park, Southern Garrett Business & Technology Park, and commercial sites along Francis Sanders Drive in Mountain Lake Park, and designated Opportunity Zone areas within the City of Hagerstown and Washington County.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Small Business Development Financing Authority (MSBDFA) - Contract Financing Program (CFP), Guaranty Fund Program (GFP), Surety Bond Program (SBP), and Equity Participation Investment Program (EPIP)
structured_extraction.program_description:
The Maryland Small Business Development Financing Authority (MSBDFA), administered by Meridian Management Group (MMG Capital Group) on behalf of the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (with oversight also from the Maryland Department of Commerce), promotes the viability and expansion of businesses owned by economically or socially disadvantaged entrepreneurs, as well as small businesses that cannot meet the credit criteria of financial institutions. Since 1995, MSBDFA has provided over $239 million in financing to over 761 small businesses in Maryland. It operates four key programs for eligible small and disadvantaged businesses in Maryland, offering affordable financing through loans, equity investments, loan guarantees, surety bonds, and professional/technical assistance.

The Contract Financing Program (CFP) provides direct loans and lines of credit to eligible Maryland-based small and disadvantaged businesses, including minority-owned, women-owned, and veteran-owned enterprises, to help them start, continue, or complete work on government or regulated utility contracts. Lines of credit offer advances up to 80% of invoices less than 90 days old (or up to 50% of a purchase order), funded within 24–48 hours, with terms of 12–24 months at prime rate plus 2%. Mobilization funding is also available as a short-term loan repayable within 10 months for new contract startup costs. Loans are used for working capital and equipment needed to fulfill the contract. Loans are limited to $2,000,000 at generally Prime Rate plus 2% interest, with repayment made as contract proceeds are received; loan term equals the duration of the contract(s). Revolving lines of credit are renewable annually, and all payments must be assigned to MSBDFA. Applicants may qualify for financing prior to contract award. Additional SSBCI components offer loans of $25,000 to $1,000,000 for working capital, equipment, or contract financing (requiring the lender to have 20% at risk), and equity investment of $25,000 to $1,000,000 in forms including preferred stock, common stock, warrants, partnership interests, and other equity-like structures to support business expansion and growth. Both SSBCI loan and equity components require a minimum 1:1 private capital match.

The Guaranty Fund Program (GFP) provides loan guaranties and interest rate subsidies to help eligible small businesses secure loans from financial institutions when they cannot obtain adequate financing through normal channels. The GFP provides a loan guaranty of up to the lesser of 80% of the loan or $2,000,000, with guaranties not to exceed 10 years. The interest rate charged by the financial institution is limited to prime plus 2%. GFP can also subsidize up to 4 percentage points of the interest charged by the lending institution, subject to annual review, with repayment terms for the subsidy negotiated directly with the borrower. Guarantee fees range from 0.75%–1.5% of the maximum loan amount for lines of credit and 0.75%–1.5% annually on the loan balance for term loans.

The Surety Bond Program (SBP) helps eligible small businesses obtain bid, performance, or payment bonds needed to perform on government, public utility, or private contracts. MMG acts as the surety (guarantor) and provides direct issuance of surety bonds or guarantees of surety bonds. MSBDFA either directly issues bonds (up to $2,500,000) or guarantees a surety company's losses (up to 90% of the face value of the bond, or $2,250,000, whichever is less) if a contractor fails to fulfill a bond. Bond premiums generally range from 2 to 3 percent for directly issued bonds. Fees for guaranteed bonds are 10%–20% of the surety's premium plus 0.5% of the bond amount, payable by the contractor. A surety bond revolving line of credit may also be established to issue or guaranty multiple bonds within pre-approved terms. Businesses must not subcontract more than 75% of the dollar value of the bonded contract and must not have defaulted on a bond, loan, loan guarantee, or equity investment from MSBDFA within two years of the application date.

The Equity Participation Investment Program (EPIP) expands business ownership for socially and economically disadvantaged entrepreneurs and small businesses that cannot obtain adequate financing through normal channels. It provides loans, loan guaranties, and equity investments to purchase franchises, acquire existing businesses, develop technology businesses, or start and expand other small businesses. Financial assistance of up to $2,000,000 is provided in the form of subordinated term loans, lines of credit, demand loans, letters of credit, and equity investments. Equity investments may take the form of qualified securities, convertible debt, interests in limited partnerships or LLCs, simple agreements for future equity (SAFE), or other debt and equity instruments. Interest rates for loans generally range from 7%–12%; equity returns generally range from 15%–22%. EPIP is supported in part by federal State Small Business Credit Initiative (SSBCI) funds and will receive $45 million in SSBCI funding over 7 years (Maryland received up to $198 million in federal SSBCI funds total). All loans and equity investments must be recaptured by the end of the seventh year. The company must have identified a probable investment exit. Collateral for loans can consist of business and personal assets.

Overall loan amounts range from $25,000 to $2,000,000; term loan rates are fixed at 5%–8%; lines of credit 4%–8%; technical assistance loans at 2%; SSBCI-funded loans may carry rates as low as 2%. Professional/technical assistance loans are available up to $25,000. A non-refundable application fee of $250 is required for debt or equity applications. All programs target businesses that have been unable to obtain financing through normal channels due to social, economic, or physical barriers. Applications over $350,000 go to the MCBIF Board; those $350,000 or less go to the MMG Internal Loan Committee.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Use the online Application Questionnaire/Tool on the MMG Capital Group website (mmgcapitalgroup.com/application-form) to find the right program and assess qualification. Review the Funds Under Management, Application Process, Program Guidelines, and FAQs before applying. Based on responses, MMG will recommend which program application to submit. Register and complete the application form on the MMG Capital Group online platform, pay the applicable non-refundable $250 application fee at the time of submission (the application will not be processed until the fee is received), and upload all required documents. A Loan/Investment Officer (LIO) will be assigned to review the application (typically 2–4 weeks), may request additional information, and will submit qualifying applications for approval. The approving body typically meets on the 2nd and 4th Thursday of each month. Applications over $350,000 go to the MCBIF Board; those $350,000 or less go to the MMG Internal Loan Committee. If approved, a commitment letter and term sheet are issued within approximately 3 business days. Sign and return the commitment letter with a non-refundable commitment fee ($500–$3,500) within 14 days. An attorney will then prepare closing documents and schedule closing. Closing generally occurs 3–6 weeks after acceptance of the Commitment Letter. Loan proceeds are disbursed by check or ACH within 1–3 business days after closing. Applicants must provide a turndown letter from a financial institution demonstrating inability to obtain conventional financing. For GFP, SBP, or EPIP inquiries, contact MMG Capital Group to discuss eligibility and the application process. Application portal: https://www.mmgcapitalgroup.com/apply. New users must register for an account before applying; after registration, you will receive an email with further instructions. Existing account holders can log in or use 'Forgot Password' if needed.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland State Small Business Credit Initiative (SSBCI) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's SSBCI program provides loans and equity investments to support small businesses with limited growth opportunities, administered through the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) in partnership with the Maryland Department of Commerce and the Maryland Technology Development Corporation (TEDCO). DHCD allocates funds through lending partners (Lendistry, City First Enterprises, FSC First, Community Development Fund) to serve small, micro, and Socially and Economically Disadvantaged Individual (SEDI) businesses statewide, with a focus on communities with high concentrations of such businesses. Financing options include capital access programs, loan participations, loan guarantees, collateral support, and venture equity programs, as well as direct loans ranging from $500,000 to $5 million with terms up to 30 years. Technical assistance is available through the MD Business Opportunity Center (financial advisory consulting, webinars, workshops, and loan packaging assistance) and F3Tech's SEDI Program (mentorship and network connections). Additionally, TEDCO allocates up to $50 million in federal SSBCI funds across four existing programs — the Venture Equity Fund, Venture Capital Limited Partnership Equity program, Seed Funds Equity program, and Social Impact Funds — to support technology-based small businesses and entrepreneurs in Maryland, including those from disadvantaged communities. No grant funds are available under either program; all assistance is in the form of loans or equity investments.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Assistance is provided in two tracks. Through DHCD: direct loans ($500,000 minimum to $5 million maximum, terms up to 30 years, senior or subordinate positions, interest rates determined by underwriting, requires 1:1 private capital match) and equity investments via lending partners (Lendistry, City First Enterprises, FSC First, Community Development Fund), plus technical assistance including financial advisory consulting, financial webinars and workshops, loan packaging assistance, and mentorship through the MD Business Opportunity Center and F3Tech's SEDI Program. Financing options include capital access programs, loan participations, loan guarantees, collateral support, and venture equity programs. Through TEDCO: up to $50 million in equity investment across four sub-programs (Venture Equity Fund, Venture Capital Limited Partnership Equity program, Seed Funds Equity program, and Social Impact Funds), targeting technology and life sciences startups including entrepreneurs from disadvantaged communities. No grants are available under either track.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small, micro, and Socially and Economically Disadvantaged Individual (SEDI) businesses in Maryland with limited opportunities for growth; also technology and life sciences businesses and entrepreneurs in Maryland, including those from disadvantaged communities. Small business owners with fewer than 500 employees seeking capital for expansion or maintenance.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business growth and credit support via loans or equity investments, including capital access programs, loan participations, loan guarantees, collateral support, and venture equity programs. Direct loan funds may be used for: machinery or equipment purchase, working capital, owner-occupied real estate acquisition or renovation (minimum 51% owner-occupied for renovations; 60% for new construction), passive real estate acquisition and maintenance, debt refinancing (not with the same lender), and tax payments (with limitations). TEDCO funds support equity investment into technology-based Maryland businesses and startups. Technical assistance is available for loan packaging, financial advising, and mentorship. No grant funding is available.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland, with a focus on communities with high concentrations of small, micro, and SEDI businesses. Businesses must be Maryland-based and private capital lenders must be licensed in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a small, micro, or SEDI business (DHCD track)
Must have limited opportunities for growth (DHCD track)
Must have fewer than 500 employees
Must not be a 100% residential business (mixed-use projects may qualify)
Requires minimum 1:1 private capital match (direct loan program)
Loan amounts between $500,000 and $5 million (direct loan program)
Must be a technology or life sciences business or entrepreneur based in Maryland (TEDCO track)
Social Impact Funds component specifically supports entrepreneurs who demonstrate several disadvantages (TEDCO track)
Funds are loans or equity investments only — no grants available

Ineligible business types: adult entertainment facilities, check cashing facilities, gambling facilities, gun shops, liquor stores, massage parlors, pawn shops, tanning salons, tattoo parlors, cannabis businesses
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants can apply through two channels. For DHCD: apply directly through the SSBCI Application Portal at apps.dhcd.state.md.us/nbwapplication, or apply directly with lending partners (Lendistry, City First Enterprises, FSC First, or Community Development Fund). For TEDCO: apply through one of four sub-programs (Social Impact Funds, Seed Funds, or Venture Funds) via the MyTEDCO portal at TEDCO's website (tedcomd.com/funding/state-small-business-credit-initiative-ssbci).
