structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Weatherization Assistance Program (WAP) is a federally funded program administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development that helps income-eligible low-income and limited-income homeowners and renters reduce their heating and cooling costs through energy-conservation improvements, while also addressing health and safety issues in their homes. The program installs energy conservation materials and makes weatherization improvements at no cost to eligible households to reduce energy costs and improve health and safety. Services may include blower door air infiltration reduction, attic/floor/wall insulation, hot water system improvements, lighting retrofits, furnace cleaning/tune-up/repair/replacement, health and safety repairs, solar readiness evaluation, emergency heating/cooling system repairs and replacements, and maintenance and education services (MEET). The program includes a mandatory Health and Safety (H/S) component ensuring worker and occupant safety during weatherization activities, covering combustion gases, electrical hazards, formaldehyde/VOCs, fuel leaks, gas appliances, hazardous materials disposal, lead-based paint, mold/moisture, pests, and radon. Priority is given to elderly residents (over age 60), people with disabilities, and families with children, as well as households with high energy usage or energy burden. Eligible OHEP applicants are automatically referred to WAP unless they opt out on the OHEP application. The program is delivered through a statewide network of local weatherization agencies (subgrantees), including Community Action Agencies, nonprofits, and local governments, which are selected through Requests for Applications (RFA) conducted at least every 3 years. For-profit contractors can also bid on weatherization work through local subgrantee procurement processes. The program is funded through multiple sources including DOE grants, the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law (BIL), the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF), and the Maryland Energy Assistance Program/Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (MEAP/LIHEAP). The BIL-funded component covers the program period 07/01/2022 - 06/30/2027 with total federal funding of $45,708,416.00 and plans to weatherize 4,284 units at an average cost of $6,000.23 per unit. The program also includes sub-programs such as EmPOWER, LIEE, Base Efficiency, Whole Home Efficiency, and MEET (Maryland Energy Efficiency Tune-up), which provides follow-up energy efficiency services to clients who previously received weatherization services. Serves single-family site-built homes, manufactured/mobile homes, duplexes, townhomes, walk-up buildings with 4 or fewer units, low-rise multifamily buildings, group homes, shelters, and multi-unit affordable housing projects.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: For eligible households: free home energy improvements delivered through local weatherization agencies at no cost. Services may include blower door air infiltration reduction, attic/floor/wall insulation, hot water system improvements, lighting retrofit, furnace cleaning/tune-up/repair/replacement, health and safety repairs, solar readiness evaluation, emergency heating/cooling system repairs and replacements (November 1/October 1–March 31 for heating; June 1–September 30 for cooling), water heater repair/replacement (April 1–September 30), window replacements, appliances (up to $250 per home in DOE WAP funds for general heat waste measures), and follow-up maintenance through the MEET program. Health and Safety measures are mandatory and must be completed before energy measures proceed; they are funded separately and excluded from SIR calculations. An energy audit inspection using DOE-approved tools (HEAT energy modeling tool) is conducted first to identify needed services. Eligible OHEP applicants are automatically referred to WAP when submitting an OHEP application unless they opt out, and qualified applicants will be contacted by the WAP office prior to receiving benefits. Average cost per dwelling unit: $7,496.27 (DOE WAP) or $6,000.23 (BIL WAP). Resolution of deferral conditions (roof repair, plumbing, electrical, mold remediation, etc.) is supported through the Weatherization Readiness Fund (WRF), with up to $15,000 average per unit for addressing deferral conditions. Energy conservation measures (ECMs) include appliances and baseload improvements, lighting upgrades, domestic hot water systems, heating and cooling systems, distribution systems, air sealing and insulation, and mobile home measures. Health and safety measures include combustion analysis, asbestos testing and encapsulation, biological/unsanitary condition remediation, structural assessments, code compliance reviews (capped at $1,000 per job for WAP; 20% average of job cost for MEAP-Wx; 50% of HVAC replacement cost for MEAP-C), radon hazard education, smoke and CO alarm installation, fire extinguishers (when solid fuels present), and ventilation systems. For subgrantees and contractors: subgrantees are selected through Requests for Applications (RFA) conducted at least every 3 years. For-profit contractors can bid on weatherization work through local subgrantee procurement processes following OMB regulations to ensure free and open competition. Funds are allocated to subgrantees by county, with Year 1 allocation based on coverage area and production capacity and subsequent years based on production capacity and prior performance. Training and technical assistance (T&TA) reimbursement is also available for pre-approved activities.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: September 5, 2024, 5:00 p.m. Local Time (for subgrantee RFA)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Income-eligible Maryland homeowners and renters statewide, with priority given to those over age 60, people with disabilities, households with children under 5, households with high energy usage, and households with high energy cost burden (21%+ of income). At-risk clients with valid medical documentation receive highest priority. Also includes low-income Maryland households who apply for OHEP energy assistance and meet WAP eligibility criteria. Additionally, Community Action Agencies, nonprofits, local governments, housing authorities, and contractors interested in providing weatherization services to low-income Maryland households. Disadvantaged communities per Climate and Economic Justice Screening Tool are also prioritized. Serves residents of single-family site-built homes, manufactured/mobile homes, low-rise multifamily buildings, group homes, and shelters. Electrically heated or cooled clients of BGE, PE, Pepco, Delmarva, SMECO, and WGL are also eligible for EmPOWER-funded services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency improvements to the home including insulation (attic, wall, floor, duct, rim/band areas), air sealing, hot water system upgrades, lighting retrofits (LED), furnace repairs or replacement, HVAC replacements, window replacements, door replacement, appliances (up to $250 per home in DOE WAP funds for general heat waste measures), health and safety fixes, solar readiness evaluation, and emergency HVAC and water heater repairs or replacements to reduce energy costs and improve household health and safety. Health and Safety measures (mandatory) include combustion analysis, asbestos testing and encapsulation, biological/unsanitary condition remediation, structural assessments, code compliance reviews, radon hazard education, smoke and CO alarm installation, fire extinguishers (when solid fuels present), ventilation systems (ASHRAE 62.2 compliance), and client education materials. Resolution of deferral conditions through Weatherization Readiness Fund (WRF) up to $15,000 average per unit. Funds also support weatherization services delivered by subgrantees and contractors to low-income households, including program administration (at least 7.5% of state grant, up to 12.5% for smaller subgrantees), training and technical assistance (T&TA), quality assurance and monitoring activities, and labor for audits, inspections, and installation. Specific fund categories include: Weatherization Readiness ($2,083,964.00), Health & Safety ($415,000.00), Program Operations ($387,185.00), T&TA ($260,531.00), and Subgrantee Administration ($310,000.00). Additional allowable costs include vehicle maintenance (capped at $2,000/vehicle/year), liability insurance, financial audits, and transportation costs. Minimum 80% of Program Income funds must be used for labor, materials, and program support; up to 10% may be used for technical assistance and training.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland across all 23 counties and Baltimore City. Services are delivered through local weatherization agencies designated by county, with primary and secondary agency designations where sufficient applicants are available. Dwellings must have a physical address in Maryland. Applicants should contact their county/city's designated Local Weatherization Agency. The program recognizes two distinct climate zones: Western Maryland and Eastern Maryland. Western Allegany and Garrett County have higher attic insulation requirements (R-60 vs R-49). Certain measures are restricted by utility territory (e.g., gas system replacements limited to BGE or WGL territories; electric systems available in all EmPOWER territories). Health and safety code compliance requirements may vary by local jurisdiction.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For household applicants: contact your Local Weatherization Agency (LWA) or submit an interest form or application through DHCD. Once eligibility is confirmed, the agency will schedule a home energy audit inspection using DOE-approved tools. Based on the audit, eligible energy improvements will be identified and installed at no cost. Health and Safety assessments are conducted and mandatory measures completed before energy conservation measures proceed. Alternatively, eligible OHEP applicants are automatically referred to WAP when submitting an OHEP application unless they opt out, and qualified applicants will be contacted by the WAP office. For subgrantee applicants: respond to a Request for Applications (RFA) when posted on the web page; contact Kiahnna Burney to be added to the vendor email list for notifications. Subgrantees must specify which county or counties they are submitting an application for. Network Partners enter data in Hancock database certifying eligibility and completion; one job per invoice with each funding source billed separately; invoices are pre-screened by Hancock then reviewed by DHCD. For contractors seeking to bid on weatherization work: contact your local weatherization agency directly to bid on work in the counties you want to serve. For T&TA reimbursement: submit pre-approval requests at least one week before the activity; submit reimbursement requests with certificates of completion after activity completion.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland WholeHome Program, financed by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD), helps homeowners make repairs and improvements that lower monthly utility bills and improve quality of life. It offers low-interest loans and grants for energy efficiency upgrades (Energy Star appliances, insulation, air sealing, HVAC upgrades, lighting), accessibility improvements for seniors and those with special needs, lead paint removal, plumbing repairs, roof work, septic repairs, and other structural and maintenance issues. Loan terms are based on the type of work needed, household income, and ability to repay, with a maximum interest rate of 4% (as low as 0%), and payments may be deferred. There is no application fee.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans and grants based on the type of work needed, household income, and ability to repay. Maximum interest rate is 4% and may be as low as 0%. Payments may be deferred. There is no application fee. Covers energy-efficient appliances, heating and cooling systems, insulation, accessibility features, lead paint removal, plumbing upgrades, roof work, septic repairs, and structural/maintenance repairs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland homeowners seeking affordable home repairs, energy efficiency improvements, or accessibility upgrades.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home repairs (roof, plumbing, septic, structural, code violations, lead paint, porches, accessibility aids); energy efficiency improvements (Energy Star appliances, insulation, air sealing, HVAC upgrades, lighting); heating and cooling system repairs; and other structural and maintenance issues.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call toll-free 1-844-369-4150 or 1-855-583-8976 to start your application, or complete the Maryland Home Rehabilitation Program Application.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides flexible financing to small businesses and nonprofits to start up, rehabilitate, or expand operations that offer healthy food options in underserved areas (food deserts). Emphasizes businesses that source fresh food from Maryland farmers and are located in designated Food Desert Areas or Sustainable Communities.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Flexible loans originated and administered through community-based lending intermediaries (Community Development Financial Institutions, local governments, or quasi-public agencies). Intermediaries also provide technical assistance to borrowers. Financing supports start-up, rehabilitation, or expansion of food-related businesses and nonprofits in designated Food Desert Areas and Sustainable Communities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses and nonprofits located in Maryland designated Food Desert Areas or Sustainable Communities that offer or will offer healthy food options, especially those sourcing fresh food from Maryland farmers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Start-up, rehabilitation, or expansion of food-related businesses and nonprofits offering healthy food options in food desert areas and Sustainable Communities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be located in a designated Food Desert Area or Sustainable Community in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be located in a designated Food Desert Area or Sustainable Community
Businesses and nonprofits must offer healthy food options to residents
Priority given to businesses sourcing fresh food from Maryland farmers
Financing is accessed through approved community-based lending intermediaries (CDFIs, local governments, or quasi-public agencies)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants apply through approved intermediary lenders/partners. Intermediaries originate and administer loans and provide technical assistance to borrowers. To become an intermediary, entities currently working in Maryland communities that are CDFIs, local governments, or quasi-public agencies must submit a separate application; intermediaries must renew partnership status every five years or when awarded funds are fully committed.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Multifamily Bond Program increases the construction and rehabilitation of multifamily rental housing for families with limited incomes. It provides tax-exempt bonds and notes for construction and permanent financing, and leverages federal Low-Income Housing Tax Credits (LIHTCs). The program supports new construction, acquisition, and rehabilitation of existing multifamily rental housing, and allows refinancing of existing high-interest-rate private loans when combined with rehabilitation. Multiple financing structures are available with different credit enhancements (FHA Risk Sharing, GNMA MBS, Freddie Mac TEL, FNMA MBS, Cash Collateral) and varying debt structures (17-40 year maturities, 35-40 year amortization).
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax-exempt bonds and notes provide construction and permanent financing for multifamily rental housing. Multiple financing structures are available with different credit enhancements (FHA Risk Sharing, GNMA MBS, Freddie Mac TEL, FNMA MBS, Cash Collateral). Financing supports new construction and substantial rehabilitation with 20-24 month construction periods. Debt structures have varying terms with 17-40 year maturities and 35-40 year amortization. Loans are also available to refinance existing high-interest-rate private loans when combined with rehabilitation. Interest rates are based on the Community Development Administration's bond rate. Loan terms are generally 30 to 40 years. A first lien position is generally required. All loans must be insured or have other acceptable credit enhancement. Projects must comply with federal requirements for tax-exempt revenue bonds and the Maryland Qualified Allocation Plan to access 4% Low-Income Housing Tax Credits.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on rolling basis; contact for additional information
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit and nonprofit developers of multifamily rental housing serving low-income households.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: New construction, acquisition, and substantial rehabilitation of existing multifamily rental housing with a minimum of five units. Refinancing of existing high-interest-rate private loans when combined with rehabilitation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Projects must contain a minimum of five units
Projects must contain complete independent dwelling units
Either 20% of units must be available to households earning 50% or less of area median income, OR 40% of units must be available to households earning 60% or less of area median income
Projects must comply with the Maryland Qualified Allocation Plan to receive 4% Low-Income Housing Tax Credits
Projects must comply with the Multifamily Rental Financing Program Guide
All loans must be insured or have other acceptable credit enhancement
A first lien position is generally required for all bond loans
All loans must comply with federal requirements for tax-exempt revenue bonds
Housing must be for families with limited incomes
Projects must have 20-24 month construction periods
Completion of TEFRA Public Hearing Notice Information Sheet form required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The program accepts applications on a rolling basis. Contact Housing Development Programs by email at dhcd.rentalhousing@maryland.gov or by phone at 301-429-7854 for information on applying. A variety of financing structures are accepted; current options, indicative interest rates, fees, and costs are summarized in the Multifamily Program Financing Option Comparison document. TEFRA Public Hearing Notice Information Sheet form must be submitted by email to benedict.durant@maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_name: Multifamily Energy Efficiency and Housing Affordability (MEEHA) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The MEEHA program promotes energy efficiency and housing affordability in affordable multifamily rental housing developments. It provides grants and loans to fund energy efficiency measures, greenhouse gas reduction measures, electric panel upgrades, building electrification, solar photovoltaic systems, EV charging stations, and related improvements in both rehabilitation and new construction projects. Eligible projects must be above minimum code and performance standards and achieve at least 20% energy savings. The program operates through two sub-programs: EmPOWER (grants or loans at 0% interest with deferred payments to reduce electric or gas consumption) and the Greenhouse Gas Reduction Program (GHGRP, grants to replace fossil fuel equipment with electric equipment and support building energy conservation).
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Funding is provided through two sub-programs: (1) EmPOWER — grants or loans (0% interest, deferred payments) to reduce electric or gas consumption, with $134.9 million allocated for 2024–2026; gas-reducing measures are only funded in BGE or WGL utility territories. (2) Greenhouse Gas Reduction Program (GHGRP) — grants only to replace fossil fuel equipment with electric equipment, support building energy conservation, and fund electric panel upgrades; up to $15,000 per dwelling unit (project cap of $1.25 million); $8.75 million in FY2024 and $5 million each in FY2025 and FY2026. Funds are released after equipment is installed and inspected, through a requisition process. Projects must be above minimum code and performance standards and achieve at least 20% energy savings. Eligible measures include energy efficiency and weatherization upgrades (HVAC, insulation, lighting, appliances, fenestration), electrification/decarbonization, solar photovoltaic installation, and EV charging station installation.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications are accepted on an ongoing basis.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners and operators of affordable multifamily rental housing developments in Maryland seeking to improve energy efficiency and reduce greenhouse gas emissions. Properties must have a minimum percentage of units designated for households at or below 80% AMI.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency measures (reducing electric or gas consumption), greenhouse gas reduction measures (replacing fossil fuel equipment with electric equipment), electric panel upgrades, building energy conservation, alternative energy generating systems (solar photovoltaics), EV charging station installation, HVAC and domestic hot water system upgrades, insulation, lighting, duct sealing, smart thermostats, air sealing, fenestration, and limited health and safety or incidental repairs related to eligible measures. Funds may also be used for energy efficiency and conservation upgrades for existing, major renovation, and new construction projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Gas-reducing measures under EmPOWER are only eligible in the Baltimore Gas and Electric Company (BGE) or Washington Gas Light Company (WGL) utility service territories. GHGRP requires existing buildings to have 35,000 gross square feet of floor area or more (excluding parking garages), or two or more buildings with combined 35,000+ sf served by the same meters/systems.
requirements_list: EmPOWER: Minimum 20% of households must be at or below 80% Area Median Income (AMI) for at least 5 years.
GHGRP: Minimum 51% of households must be at or below 80% AMI for at least 15 years.
EmPOWER: Open to all building sizes and configurations, including single-family units as a group project, individually metered, or master metered buildings.
GHGRP: Existing buildings must have 35,000 gross square feet of floor area or more, excluding parking garages, or two or more buildings with combined 35,000+ sf served by same meters/systems.
A Qualified Energy Professional must perform an energy audit (rehabilitation) or energy certification review (new construction) and submit the Funding Request to DHCD on behalf of the project owner.
Projects applying for DHCD Rental Lending programs may submit the 202 application form instead of the standard MEEHA application.
Projects must be above minimum code and performance standards.
Must achieve at least 20% energy savings.
Must be an affordable multifamily rental housing development.
Project must reduce direct greenhouse gas emissions.
All energy conservation measures (ECMs) must adhere to MEEHA Measure Specifications Parameters.
ECMs must meet existing and recommended criteria per Program Guidance.
Total Measure Cost must be identified using actual contractor bids.
Photos required for all measures, organized by category and meeting specific quality standards.
Diagnostic testing results required for ventilation recommendations.
Account holder authorization/consent for energy use information release required (covering 24 months before project start through 24 months after project completion).

Insulation requirements vary by location (e.g., R-49 minimum for gabled attics, R-30 for crawlspace).
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Owner submits the MEEHA Application to MultifamilyEnergy.dhcd@maryland.gov (or submits the 202 Application if also applying for Rental Lending programs). 2. A Qualified Energy Professional completes an energy audit (rehabilitation) or energy certification review (new construction) and submits a Funding Request to DHCD on behalf of the owner. 3. DHCD reviews the Funding Request and sends a scope confirmation. 4. Owner accepts the scope and signs the funding agreement. 5. Construction proceeds; the project team submits requisitions with supporting documentation. 6. DHCD inspects installed measures and processes payment (typically 4–5 weeks). 7. Project enters the affordability period after construction is complete. Applications may also be submitted through DHCD's One-Stop Shop Application at dhcd.maryland.gov. Starting in 2026, funding requests are planned to be submitted through DHCD's MINT tool.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides capital exclusively to Community Development Financial Institutions (CDFIs) for re-lending to small businesses. It targets businesses owned and operated by Socially and Economically Disadvantaged Individuals (SEDI), Very Small Businesses (VSB) with fewer than 10 employees, and businesses in CDFI Investment Areas. DHCD issues SSBCI Loans to CDFIs at 0%-2% interest for up to 7 years, which are matched with private capital and re-lent to small businesses. SSBCI Loans to CDFIs range from $2,000,000 to $15,000,000, with individual Small Business Loans (SBLs) to end-use borrowers capped at $250,000 (unless DHCD approves higher). CDFIs must have 20% at risk and provide a required private capital match (4:1 for non-SEDI businesses with 10 or more employees; 2.3:1 for SEDI businesses or those with fewer than 10 employees). Applications are processed on a first-come, first-served basis. The program is designed to provide flexible financing for start-ups and business expansions with a focus on CDFI investment areas.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: SSBCI Loans to CDFIs range from $2,000,000 to $15,000,000 at 0%-2% interest with terms up to 7 years (with annual renewal options). Individual Small Business Loans (SBLs) to end-use borrowers are capped at $250,000 unless DHCD approves a higher amount, at a maximum interest rate of 18%, with terms up to 5 years (longer if financing assets with longer useful lives). Combined origination fees and points maximum: 1%; Application fee maximum: $100 for SBLs. CDFIs must have 20% at risk. Required private capital match: 4:1 for non-SEDI businesses with 10 or more employees; 2.3:1 for SEDI businesses or those with fewer than 10 employees. Applications are processed on a first-come, first-served basis.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Re-lending to eligible small businesses as Small Business Loans (SBLs), particularly SEDI-owned businesses and very small businesses (fewer than 10 employees), with individual SBLs up to $250,000 per business. Funds may support business loans, investments, and other credit or equity support for establishing and sustaining small businesses including start-ups and expansions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. CDFIs must be operating in Maryland and serving businesses in CDFI Investment Areas (as defined in 12 C.F.R. § 1805.201(b)(3)(ii)). Priority given to businesses in rural communities, communities undergoing economic transitions, and underserved communities.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and submit the SSBCI NBW Loan to Lender Application (PDF) available at the program website. Applications are processed on a first-come, first-served basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: A venture debt program that provides bridge financing to early-stage businesses in Maryland with high job growth potential. It supports companies that have already raised equity from early-stage investors and need funding to reach their next equity milestone. Typical bridge rounds are greater than $2,000,000.

structured_extraction.program_name: National Capital Strategic Economic Development Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: The National Capital Strategic Economic Development Fund (NED) provides competitive capital and operating funding to support commercial and residential revitalization and economic development activities in targeted Sustainable Communities within Prince George's County and Montgomery County in the Maryland National Capital region. The program focuses on areas where modest investment and a coordinated strategy will have a meaningful neighborhood revitalization impact. For FY2025, approximately $19 million in capital funding and $1.2 million in operating funding are available.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive capital and operating funds awarded to support eligible commercial and residential development and economic development projects in targeted Sustainable Communities within defined geographic boundaries in Prince George's County and Montgomery County. For FY2025, $19 million in capital funding and $1.2 million in operating funding are available. Projects in Prince George's County must be in a Sustainable Community at least partly within the boundary of Interstate 495 and the District of Columbia. Projects in Montgomery County must be within an Enterprise Zone or the boundary defined by Prince George's County, Maryland Route 200, Interstate 270, Interstate 495, and the District of Columbia.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, nonprofits, and community development organizations in eligible areas of Prince George's County and Montgomery County seeking to support economic development and neighborhood revitalization in Sustainable Communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment assistance for homebuyers, acquisition or rehabilitation of vacant or dilapidated properties, improvement of residential and business properties, energy efficiency weatherization and retrofits, affordable housing development, mixed-use project development, community open space or public infrastructure improvements, strategic demolition, and broader economic development capital and operating costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: In Prince George's County: Sustainable Communities located at least in part within the boundary of Interstate 495 and the District of Columbia. In Montgomery County: Sustainable Communities within an Enterprise Zone or the boundary defined by Prince George's County, Maryland Route 200, Interstate 270, Interstate 495 to the Maryland state line, and the District of Columbia.

Project must be located in a designated Sustainable Community
Project must support goals and objectives outlined in the targeted area's Sustainable Communities Action Plan
Project must be within the defined NED geographic boundary in Prince George's County or Montgomery County
Prince George's County projects must be at least partly within the boundary created by I-495 and the District of Columbia
Montgomery County projects must be within an Enterprise Zone or a specific geographic boundary defined by Prince George's County, MD Route 200, I-270, I-495, and the DC state line
Projects should help achieve strategies outlined in the local government's Sustainable Communities plan
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register for the application training webinar and view program information at the DHCD State Revitalization Programs website. First-time applicants should contact a regional project manager for eligibility determination. Use the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper to verify whether a specific address falls within the NED boundary. Submit application by June 26 at 3 p.m.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program administered by Maryland's Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) that helps create and preserve affordable rental housing for households with the lowest incomes. DHCD uses these funds to support extremely low-income (ELI) households earning 30% or less of the Area Median Income (AMI). Funds may be used for acquisition, new construction, reconstruction, or rehabilitation of non-luxury housing with suitable amenities. The federal fiscal year 2025 allocation is $3,000,000. Funds are often combined with other federal, state, and local housing resources to make affordable housing projects financially feasible. Projects must maintain affordability requirements for 40 years from project completion.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: HTF funds may be used for development hard costs, acquisition costs, related soft costs, relocation costs, operating/rental assistance (limited to one-third of annual allocation; must be fully utilized within 5 years of award), and operating costs including insurance, utilities, real property taxes, maintenance, and scheduled reserve payments for major system replacement. Operating reserves of 3-6 months of underwritten operating expenses and replacement reserves of $300+ per unit annually are supported. Maximum per-unit development subsidy limits range from $181,488 (0 BR) to $359,263 (4 BR). Construction cost limits range from $227-$271/sq ft for new construction and $173-$277/sq ft for rehabilitation. Funds cannot be used for refinancing existing debt. Assistance may be structured as equity investments, interest-bearing or non-interest-bearing loans, deferred payment loans, grants, or other forms approved by HUD. DHCD awards funds on a competitive and non-competitive, first-ready first-served basis depending on fund availability. If selected, applicants receive a Notice of Award stating DHCD's intent to provide HTF funds.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations, for-profit developers, and other qualified housing development entities seeking to create or preserve affordable rental housing for extremely low-income households (at or below 30% of Area Median Income), including low-income families and individuals, homeless families, persons with disabilities, and populations with special needs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: New construction or rehabilitation of affordable rental housing, property acquisition, development hard costs, related soft costs, resident relocation costs, operating reserves (3-6 months of underwritten operating expenses), replacement reserves ($300+ per unit annually), limited operating costs or operating reserves for HTF-assisted units, developer fees (may be deferred), and project betterments. Maximum rents are set by the Department annually.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. New construction projects must be located in Priority Funding Areas (PFAs). Projects must be located in: Qualified Census Tracts (QCT) or Difficult Development Areas (DDA) contributing to concerted community revitalization plans, OR family projects in 'Communities of Opportunity' as designated on Maryland QAP Comprehensive Opportunity Maps, OR communities designated by court order. Rural areas (as defined by USDA Rural Development eligibility) receive preferential scoring. Special consideration given to projects in Allegany, Caroline, Dorchester, Garrett, Kent, Somerset, Washington, Wicomico, and Worcester Counties.
requirements_list: Must be a nonprofit organization, for-profit developer, or other qualified housing development entity
Must demonstrate financial capacity to complete the project
Must have experience developing or managing affordable multifamily rental housing
Primary Development Team must include: Developer/Owner, general contractor, architect, and property manager
Must be able to comply with HTF program requirements and reporting
Must be familiar with other housing funding programs used in the project
Must meet minimum threshold requirements
Recipients must certify compliance with HTF requirements for the full period of the project
Projects must maintain affordability requirements for 40 years from project completion
New construction projects must be located in Priority Funding Areas
Projects must meet accessibility, energy efficiency, and health/safety standards
Operating assistance limited to one-third of annual HTF allocation and must be fully utilized within 5 years of award
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: A sponsor can request HTF funds as part of a project application, or DHCD staff may recommend using HTF funds during project review in consultation with the sponsor. DHCD awards funds on a competitive and non-competitive, first-ready first-served basis depending on fund availability. If selected, the applicant receives a Notice of Award.

structured_extraction.program_description: A loan participation program that helps small businesses in Maryland acquire or renovate owner-occupied real estate and cover working capital needs through the SSBCI program. Offers below-market interest rates and loans up to $5 million for businesses located in CDFI Investment Areas. Priority is given to very small businesses (fewer than 10 employees) and businesses owned or operated by Socially and Economically Disadvantaged Individuals (SEDI).
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Senior or junior debt with an SSBCI portion of $350,000 to $5,000,000. Loans cover up to 30% of total project cost. Interest rate is determined by underwriting analysis. Loan terms up to 30 years depending on use and amount. Requires personal guarantees, collateral, and a private capital match (minimum 1:1; target 4:1 for non-SEDI/VSB and 2.3:1 for SEDI/VSB). Application fee of $250 and closing fee of $250. Priority given to very small businesses (fewer than 10 employees) and Socially and Economically Disadvantaged Individuals (SEDI).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses with fewer than 500 employees operating in Maryland, especially very small businesses (fewer than 10 employees) and businesses owned or operated by Socially and Economically Disadvantaged Individuals (SEDI). Local governments are not eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Owner-occupied real estate acquisition or renovation, mixed-use projects combining residential and commercial uses, working capital, machinery and equipment, and other costs associated with sustaining or expanding a small business.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Business must be located or planning to locate in a CDFI Investment Area. Local governments are not eligible.

Fewer than 500 employees
Local governments are not eligible applicants
Private capital match required (minimum 1:1; target 4:1 for non-SEDI/VSB; 2.3:1 for SEDI/VSB)
Business must be located or planning to locate in a CDFI Investment Area
Must demonstrate business viability and cash flow

Flexible applicant cash contribution required

structured_extraction.program_description: The Neighborhood BusinessWorks (NBW) loan program offers flexible financing to new or expanding small businesses and nonprofit organizations to help improve and revitalize existing commercial districts and town centers. Loans support a wide range of commercial projects located in Sustainable Communities, Priority Funding Areas, Opportunity Zones in select counties, Transit-Oriented Development areas, or BRAC Revitalization and Incentive Zones across Maryland. The department partners with banks, CDFIs, and mixed-use developers to help entrepreneurs turn business plans into brick-and-mortar businesses. In Frederick County, the program specifically provides gap financing to businesses and projects located in one of seven Sustainable Communities targeted for redevelopment in older neighborhoods. Eligible uses include acquisition and permanent financing of commercial and mixed-use real estate, refinancing of stabilized commercial and mixed-use projects, nonprofit facility loans for acquisition, rehabilitation, and new construction, machinery and equipment, working capital, and other costs associated with opening, operating, or expanding a Maryland small business. The program has a 20+ year history and currently manages 158 loans with $20+ million in outstanding principal. It can function as a senior or subordinate lender, or a combination of both.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Bond-funded direct business loans up to $5 million with flexible terms up to 30 years. Interest rate is set through underwriting analysis based on market conditions. A 10% applicant cash contribution is required. Personal guarantees and collateral are required. Minimum debt service coverage ratio of 1.50 for CDA loans and 1.25 for senior loans. Fees include a $250 application fee, $250 closing fee, and 1% commitment fee. Can function as senior loans (up to 70% LTV), subordinate loans (state-appropriated capital), or combined financing structures up to 100% CLTV (for-profit: 90% max; nonprofit: 95% max). Top loss/deficiency guaranty coverage up to 30% by CDA/MHF. Lending partners including banks and CDFIs also participate in the program. In Frederick County, the program provides gap financing to businesses in designated Sustainable Communities. Eligible uses include acquisition and permanent financing of commercial and mixed-use real estate, refinancing of stabilized commercial and mixed-use projects, nonprofit facility loans for acquisition, rehabilitation, and new construction, machinery and equipment, working capital, leasehold improvements, market/planning/feasibility studies, and real estate acquisition. Excluded industries include adult entertainment, casinos, check-cashing services, gun stores, liquor stores, massage salons, pawn shops, tanning salons, tattoo studios, and cannabis businesses.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Partnership Rental Housing Program (also known as the Rental Housing Program) expands the supply of affordable rental housing for low-income households. It provides low-interest and deferred loans to developers, local governments, housing authorities, and eligible non-governmental entities to finance new construction, acquisition, or rehabilitation of rental housing. Residents must have incomes at or below 60% of area median income (or 50% of statewide median income for Partnership program units, or 30% of Area Median Income for disability/special needs units). Funds can be combined with federal HOME money, low-income housing tax credits, and other public or private financing sources.

Any profits from sale must be used for other low-income housing purposes.

structured_extraction.program_name: Project C.O.R.E. (Creating Opportunities for Revitalization and Equity) – Strategic Demolition Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: Project C.O.R.E. is a multi-year partnership between the State of Maryland and Baltimore City to demolish thousands of vacant and blighted buildings and catalyze redevelopment, reinvestment, and neighborhood stabilization in Baltimore City. The program operates in two phases: Phase I uses state and city funds—$75 million from the state and $18.5 million from Baltimore City—to demolish blighted properties, including half- and whole-blocks of blight, with the Maryland Stadium Authority managing demolition, grading, seeding, and fencing of cleared sites. Selected properties are also stabilized for future rehabilitation and redevelopment. Phase II leverages Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development programs to encourage new investment and redevelopment in cleared communities, with an estimated $600 million in leveraged resources. The Strategic Demolition Fund component provides capital funding (including $50 million available for FY2025) to accelerate the elimination of vacant properties in Baltimore City. The initiative aims to improve economic opportunity and quality of life by creating safer neighborhoods, more green space, affordable and mixed-use housing, small business opportunities, employment opportunities, and workforce development programs. The workforce development component focuses on connecting local Baltimore residents to jobs created by demolition, deconstruction, building stabilization, rehabilitation, and site redevelopment activities. Contractors working on Project C.O.R.E.-funded projects must develop Workforce Projection Plans. In Fiscal Year 2017, nearly $16 million was awarded to 30 projects, expected to catalyze an additional $285 million from public, private, and nonprofit partners. As of October 1, 2024, Project C.O.R.E. has been succeeded by Reinvest Baltimore, a new unified state-city approach to address Baltimore's vacancy crisis.

In Fiscal Year 2017, nearly $16 million was awarded to 30 projects, expected to catalyze an additional $285 million from public, private, and nonprofit partners. Phase II leverages an estimated $600 million through DHCD programs for revitalization and redevelopment. The initiative also provides attractive financing and other incentives to encourage investment in Project C.O.R.E. communities. structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a completed Application Submission Package (available in the Multifamily Housing Development Document Library), including completed CDA Form 202 with RHW funds clearly identified, along with required threshold documentation including projected Full Time Equivalent jobs and certification of competitive funding awards. Separate applications for other DHCD funding (MBP, LIHTC) must be completed concurrently or in advance. Applications are tracked by date of receipt and reviewed alongside Multifamily Bond Program applications. Projects passing threshold are scored using the Guide's evaluation criteria. Kick-off meetings are scheduled after scoring, and projects are funded on a first-ready, first-served basis.

structured_extraction.program_name: Request for Interest: Federal Funding Application Assistance
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides 100% grants to local jurisdictions or their internet service provider (ISP) partners to cover costs associated with preparing federal broadband funding applications. OSB partners with applicants to assist in preparing and reviewing federal funding applications for broadband deployment to unserved rural residents and businesses. Eligible costs include market studies, engineering, legal, financial, and other consulting services needed to prepare a federal funding application. OSB will coordinate with other State Agencies on use of State assets where feasible.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 100% grants covering costs of outside consultants (market studies, engineering, legal, financial, and other approved services) needed to prepare a federal broadband funding application. Maximum funding of $125,000 for properly contracted services. Reimbursement only for projects submitting completed federal applications meeting federal program requirements. OSB also assists with preparing and reviewing federal funding applications to ensure completeness and competitiveness, and coordinates with other State Agencies on use of State assets where feasible.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Costs of outside consultants for federal broadband funding application preparation, including engineering consultant services, financial consultant services, marketing studies, legal consultant services, and other contracted services approved on a case-by-case basis
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — available to local jurisdictions across Maryland, targeting unserved rural areas lacking internet service at 25 Mbps down/3 Mbps up (or per federal program definition) and areas without prior federal broadband investment

Funds cover costs of federal funding application preparation only

Areas must lack existing federal broadband investments
Minimum network capability required

structured_extraction.program_description: The Section 811 Project Rental Assistance Program expands affordable housing for low-income adults with disabilities by making community housing affordable through project-based rental assistance. Funded by HUD and authorized under the Frank Melville Supportive Housing Investment Act of 2010, the program is administered in Maryland by the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) in partnership with the Maryland Department of Disabilities (MDOD) and the Maryland Department of Health (MDH). DHCD awards project-based rental assistance tied to specific units in approved rental housing projects that receive federal Low-Income Housing Tax Credits or State Rental Housing Funds and are financed by DHCD. Eligible tenants pay 30% of their income for rent and utilities combined, and the program pays the remaining rent directly to the landlord. The initial lease term is 1 year, and rent does not change unless the tenant's income changes. The program also provides tenant training, transition planning, money management assistance, and access to voluntary support services including waivers, case management, and community-based services. Eligible low-income adults with disabilities are referred to available units by MDOD. The program provides approximately 150 integrated and affordable rental units in vibrant and choice communities throughout Maryland, including LIHTC and other federally/state-financed developments, with no more than 25% of units in each development set aside for the 811 PRA program. The program serves a cross-disability population including persons with mental health, physical, developmental, and intellectual disabilities.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Project-based rental assistance subsidizes the contract rent for eligible units in approved rental housing projects. Tenants pay 30% of their income for rent and utilities combined; the program pays the remaining rent directly to the landlord. The initial lease term is 1 year, and rent does not change unless the tenant's income changes. Assistance is awarded to housing projects (not individuals directly). Projects must receive federal Low-Income Housing Tax Credits or State Rental Housing Funds and be financed by DHCD. DHCD issues a Reservation Award Letter to selected developers confirming eligibility for funding. Eligible residents pay reduced rent based on their income (at or below 30% of Area Median Income). Contract rents cannot exceed Section 8 Fair Market Rent unless substantiated by a market study, and annual rent adjustments are based on HUD's Operating Cost Adjustment Factor (OCAF). Vacancy payments of up to 80% of contract rent for up to 60 days are available under specified conditions. Utility reimbursements are available where applicable. The minimum rental assistance contract term is 20 years with a 30-year use restriction. Administrative costs are limited to up to 8% of the annual Section 811 PRA award (and up to 5% of awarded amount for planning, program development, infrastructure, technology, and energy/water conservation improvements where applicable). Prior funding rounds targeted the Baltimore and Washington D.C. metropolitan areas (approximately 75%) and the Eastern Shore and Western Maryland (approximately 25%). Additional case management services are provided including move-in assistance and security deposit support, tenant training (lease understanding, safety, housekeeping, rent payment), financial management and budgeting support, mental health and behavioral health services coordination, crisis intervention and emergency financial assistance, vocational services, and community inclusion activities. No more than 25% of units in each development may be set aside for 811 PRA program participants.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Waitlist Registry opened November 17, 2014; may be closed at MDOD discretion; contact for additional information
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-elderly adults age 18 to under 62 with disabilities who are Maryland Medicaid recipients with household income at or below 30% of Area Median Income, referred by the Maryland Department of Disabilities. Also includes victims of domestic violence, dating violence, sexual assault, or stalking. Eligible disability types include mental health, physical, developmental, intellectual, learning, psychiatric, sensory, and traumatic brain injury disabilities. Priority populations include persons living in nursing homes with Medicaid HCBS access, persons at risk of institutionalization, persons desiring to move from group homes to independent living, and homeless individuals who are Medicaid recipients. Housing developers and property owners with DHCD-financed rental projects are the applicants for program funds.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Subsidizing rent for eligible units in approved rental housing projects serving adults with disabilities; also covers tenant training, transition planning, money management assistance, and access to voluntary support services including waivers, case management, and community-based services. Vacancy payments for vacant assisted units and utility reimbursements where applicable. Administrative costs for program operation including outreach, referrals, waiting list management, and service coordination are also eligible. Planning and program development costs, infrastructure and technology costs, and energy and water conservation improvements may also be covered. Additional eligible uses include move-in assistance, security deposits (not to exceed $50), application fees (typically $25-35 per adult), pet deposits (not to exceed $300), moving expenses, financial counseling, crisis intervention, and community resource referrals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland in participating housing units. Applicants indicate up to 5 preferred counties in which they are willing to live. Projects must be located in priority funding areas. Properties cannot be located in 100-year floodplains, airport clear zones, wetlands, or Coastal Barrier Resource System units. Prior funding rounds targeted the Baltimore and Washington D.C. metropolitan areas (approximately 75%) and the Eastern Shore and Western Maryland (approximately 25%). All Maryland counties and Baltimore City are included in the program. Program office located at 217 East Redwood Street, Baltimore, MD 21202.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For housing developers: DHCD meets with an Interagency Committee (including representatives from MDOD and MDH) to review projects aligned with program goals. Once a project is selected, DHCD issues a Reservation Award Letter to the developer confirming eligibility for funding. For prospective residents: (1) Outreach and identification of eligible persons; (2) Housing assessment through face-to-face meeting; (3) Contact case manager, support planner, resource coordinator, coordinator of community service, or community health worker to complete pre-screening and application on your behalf; (4) Referral to 811 PRA Program via MDOD website/Maryland Partnership for Affordable Housing; (5) Name placed on waiting list (Waitlist Registry); (6) Obtain housing documents and resources while on waitlist; (7) Upon reaching top of list, case manager assists with eligibility packet completion; (8) Background check (criminal and credit history review); (9) Submission of completed eligibility packet to property manager; (10) Property manager reviews for eligibility and compliance with federal regulations; (11) Unit matching based on needs and county preferences (applicants indicate up to 5 preferred counties); (12) 5 business day acceptance/decline window; (13) Re-application possible after 6 months if lease terminated. For assistance, contact Social Serve, Inc. (811 PRA Referral System): 1-877-496-4954 (8:30 a.m.-5:00 p.m. EDT, Monday-Friday). Three main process stages: Unit Identification and Turnover Process; PRA Tenant Issue Process; Applicant Process. Waiting lists may be long; prospective residents should apply as soon as possible.

structured_extraction.program_name: Seed Community Development Anchor Institution Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides competitive grants and loans to anchor institutions — colleges, universities, and hospitals — for capital improvement and neighborhood improvement projects in Sustainable Communities or underinvested/blighted areas of Maryland. Projects must generate jobs, strengthen partnerships between anchor institutions and the state, and lead to safer, healthier, and more attractive communities. Approximately $10 million in capital funding is available for FY2025. Recipients must provide matching funds equal to the amount of financial assistance received (1:1 match). For example, Washington College received $500,000 toward construction of its Innovation Plant for workforce training and entrepreneurship.

Approximately $10 million in capital funding available for FY2025. Recipients must provide matching funds equal to the amount of financial assistance received (1:1 match). Projects must be located in a Sustainable Community and/or an area of blight or underinvestment. Washington College, for example, received $500,000 toward construction of its Innovation Plant for workforce training and entrepreneurship.

structured_extraction.program_name: Shelter and Transitional Housing Facilities Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides capital financing for emergency shelters and transitional housing facilities that provide housing and support services to prevent homelessness and assist households to live independently. Uses a 'Harm Reduction' approach for supportive services. Funds eligible project types including new construction, acquisition, alteration, conversion, relocation, renovation, replacement, restoration, site development, utilities, and equipment/furnishings.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants fund new construction, acquisition, rehabilitation of housing, and purchase of capital equipment for transitional housing and emergency shelters. Total capital assistance cannot exceed 50% of total development costs, but under certain conditions may cover up to 75%. Sponsors must maintain the project as transitional housing or an emergency shelter for 15 years; if the use is discontinued before 15 years, the grant must be repaid. Applications are accepted any time of year on a first-come, first-served basis.

Cannot fund: refinancing existing debt, portions not providing homeless housing, financial transaction costs, replacement furnishings in existing facilities, operating assistance, feasibility studies, existing debt/interest, fundraising, employee salaries, or administrative/legal costs.

structured_extraction.program_description: The STAR Program provides zero-interest, fully deferred loans to low-income owner-occupants of single-family homes to rehabilitate their properties to meet applicable building codes, standards, or minimum housing quality standards. In some cases, STAR loans can also fund replacement houses. The program is funded with federal HOME funds and follows U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) requirements. It is administered statewide by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, with loan requests processed directly by local governments such as Frederick County.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Zero percent interest, fully deferred loans secured by a mortgage or Deed of Trust. The maximum loan is generally up to $50,000 or up to 100–110 percent of the after-rehabilitation value of the property; exceptions to the debt-to-value limit are considered on a case-by-case basis. Interest rates range from 0% to 6% based on ability to pay; maximum term of 30 years; deferred payments available for households at or below 50% of median income. Grants may also be considered on a case-by-case basis. Eligible for households with incomes at or below 50% of HUD Area Median Income (AMI), or at or below 30% of the Washington, D.C. MSA median income in some jurisdictions; up to 55% of statewide median income with a poor credit rating; or up to 80% AMI in exceptional cases or if the household is ineligible for other DHCD financing. The property must meet HUD's definition of 'modest housing.' Loans are processed directly by local governments.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rehabilitation of owner-occupied single-family homes to bring them up to applicable building codes, standards, or minimum housing quality standards; eligible repairs include mold remediation, roof repair, asbestos/lead abatement, electrical hazards, plumbing issues, foundation waterproofing, radon mitigation, structural repair, accessibility modifications, and pest treatment; in some cases, construction of replacement houses

Contact Special Loan Programs for more information or use the online inquiry form. Documentation can be submitted to DHCD.SLP_documentation@maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: The State Revitalization Programs offer a range of funding — including grants, loans, and technical assistance — to support community revitalization goals across Maryland. Funds are primarily used for capital projects with at least a 15-year useful life, such as upper-story residential redevelopment, commercial façade improvements, adaptive reuse of vacant buildings, neighborhood parks, arts and cultural amenities, small business incubators, and acquisition or rehabilitation of vacant properties. The program works with local partners to bring new investment and vitality to Maryland's core communities, addressing priorities such as increasing housing, creating lovable places, and righting the wrongs of the past. Projects must be located within a designated Sustainable Community and align with that community's Sustainable Communities Action Plan. Sub-programs include: Baltimore Regional Neighborhood Initiative, Community Legacy, Maryland Façade Improvement Program, National Capital Strategic Economic Development Fund, Seed Community Development Anchor Institution Fund, Strategic Demolition Fund – Statewide, and Baltimore Vacants Reinvestment Initiative.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant and loan funding for capital revitalization projects. Capital activities include: property acquisition, construction, architectural and engineering drawings, site development, demolition, deconstruction, and rehabilitation (approximately 15-year useful life). Some programs also allow operating activities such as staff salaries, feasibility/planning studies, marketing, and maintenance. Capital-only programs include Community Legacy, Strategic Demolition Fund, SEED, and Maryland Façade Improvement Program. Programs allowing both capital and operating funding include Baltimore Regional Neighborhood Initiative and National Capital Strategic Economic Development Fund. Specific award amounts vary by sub-program. Applications are reviewed during a summer review period and awards are announced in the fall.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: July 2, 2025 at 2:59 PM (FY26 round — now closed)
structured_extraction.contact_name: Larry Brown, Jr. (Assistant Director); Garland Thomas (Assistant Director)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, non-profit community development organizations, anchor institutions (hospitals and higher education institutions), and other eligible organizations seeking funding for community revitalization capital projects within Maryland Sustainable Communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital projects such as upper-story residential redevelopment, commercial façade improvements, adaptive reuse of vacant buildings, neighborhood parks, arts and cultural amenities, small business incubators, acquisition or rehabilitation of vacant residential properties, demolition of derelict structures, site assembly, infrastructure improvements, historic preservation, affordable housing development, and workforce development. Operating support (staff salaries, planning studies) is permitted under select sub-programs.

Certain sub-programs have additional geographic requirements: BRNI is limited to Baltimore City, Baltimore County (inner-beltway communities), and Anne Arundel County (inner-beltway communities); the National Capital Strategic Economic Development Fund targets Prince George's County and Montgomery County; Community Legacy and Strategic Demolition Fund have Opportunity Zone eligibility in Allegany, Garrett, Somerset, and Wicomico Counties.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Strategic Demolition Fund provides capital funding to accelerate economic development and job creation in existing Maryland communities. It focuses on making 'grey field development' (redeveloping already-built areas) more economically viable by supporting demolition of blighted and derelict non-contributing structures, land assembly, and site preparation for new development. Administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, the program awards competitive grants to local governments and nonprofit community development organizations for projects in Sustainable Communities or qualifying Opportunity Zones. Approximately $10 million in capital funding was available for FY2025. Since funds are limited, awards focus on projects that can have a high economic and revitalization impact in their existing communities.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants from a pool of approximately $10 million (FY2025) to fund demolition of derelict non-contributing structures, site acquisition and assembly, site development, and construction-level architectural and engineering designs. Projects must be located in Sustainable Communities outside Baltimore City, or in Opportunity Zones in Allegany, Garrett, Somerset, and Wicomico Counties. For example, Main Street Historic Chestertown received $250,000 to demolish deteriorating structures at 107 North Cross Street to enable redevelopment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, Main Street organizations, and nonprofit community development organizations working outside of Baltimore City whose projects are in Sustainable Communities or qualifying Opportunity Zones.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Demolition of derelict non-contributing and deteriorating structures, site acquisition and assembly to create redevelopment-sized parcels, site development, and construction-level architectural and engineering designs to prepare sites for redevelopment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available for projects located in Sustainable Communities outside Baltimore City, or in Opportunity Zones in Allegany, Garrett, Somerset, and Wicomico Counties. Available statewide in Maryland.

Project must be located outside Baltimore City

Projects should help achieve strategies outlined in the local government's Sustainable Communities plan

First-time applicants should contact a regional project manager for eligibility determination. Submit application by the posted deadline (most recently June 26 at 3 p.m.).

structured_extraction.program_description: The Sustainable Communities Program provides an official geographic designation to local areas in Maryland to support community development, revitalization, and sustainability. Administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD), the designation helps local governments access state resources to improve older communities and promote growth that is environmentally, economically, and socially responsible. The program encourages cross-governmental collaboration by providing designated Sustainable Communities with access to an interagency revitalization toolbox of financing programs and tax credit incentives, with partners including the Department of Commerce, Maryland Economic Development Corporation, Department of Planning, Department of Environment, State Highway Administration, and Department of Transportation. Areas must be within a Priority Funding Area and demonstrate a need for revitalization. The designation is required to apply for certain state funding programs such as Community Legacy, Strategic Demolition and Smart Growth Impact Funds, the Sustainable Communities Tax Credit, Neighborhood BusinessWorks loans, Sidewalk Retrofit funding, Community Safety and Enhancement funding, Job Creation Tax Credits, and Enhanced Local Tax Increment Financing. Once designated, organizations, residents, and jurisdictions within the area gain priority or enhanced access to state grants, loans, and tax credits. Designations are valid for five years. Designated areas located within a state-designated Transit Oriented Development (TOD) area approved after 2023 can also benefit from State Revitalization Program (SRP) funding. Boundary amendments can be submitted on a rolling basis and are reviewed by DHCD twice per year. The program is available statewide including in Howard County and Prince George's County, where designated Sustainable Communities gain access to state resources, grants, and technical assistance to improve neighborhood quality of life, economic development, and environmental sustainability.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Local governments receive a Sustainable Communities designation valid for five years that unlocks eligibility for various state revitalization funding programs. The program provides an interagency revitalization toolbox including: Community Legacy Program (capital funding for business retention/attraction, homeownership, commercial revitalization); Neighborhood BusinessWorks (gap/subordinate financing for new/expanding small businesses with first-floor retail); Strategic Demolition and Smart Growth Impact Fund (grants for predevelopment, demolition, land assembly); Operating Assistance Grants (support for operating and technical assistance costs); National Capital Strategic Economic Development Fund (greyfield development financing for areas between Washington D.C. and Interstate 495); Seed Community Development Anchor Institution Program (grants/loans for community development); Sustainable Communities Tax Credit; Sidewalk Retrofit funding; Community Safety and Enhancement funding; Job Creation Tax Credits; Enhanced Local Tax Increment Financing; Main Street Maryland (technical assistance, training, planning, architectural design, historic preservation assistance); Maryland Façade Improvement Program (funds for commercial property exterior improvements); LIHTC (support for multi-family affordable housing); and Water Quality Financing (below-market loans and grants for wastewater treatment and green projects). Designated areas located within a state-designated Transit Oriented Development (TOD) area approved after 2023 can also benefit from State Revitalization Program (SRP) funding. Baltimore Regional Neighborhood Initiative (BRNI) funding is available to inner beltway Sustainable Communities within and surrounding Baltimore City. Organizations and residents in designated areas gain eligibility to apply for state grants, loans, tax credits, training services, planning assistance, below-market interest rate loans, and loan forgiveness programs. The designation itself does not directly provide financial assistance but is a prerequisite for accessing these programs. Boundary amendments may be submitted on a rolling basis and are reviewed by DHCD twice per year.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis; reviewed by DHCD twice per year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Municipal and county governments in Maryland seeking a Sustainable Communities designation to support local revitalization and access state funding programs, as well as property owners, developers, businesses, organizations, residents, and jurisdictions located within or seeking inclusion in designated Sustainable Community areas, including Howard County, Anne Arundel County's designated communities of Brooklyn Park, Glen Burnie, and Odenton/Severn, Baltimore City, and communities in Prince George's County. Also includes local development agencies, local development corporations, anchor institutions (institutions of higher education or hospitals), and eligible businesses seeking tax credits. Program also serves low to moderate income households, displaced workers, seniors, persons with disabilities, and diverse community stakeholders.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supports community revitalization, historic preservation, housing, transportation, economic development, neighborhood revitalization, workforce development, infrastructure improvements, multimodal transportation, green development, affordable and sustainable housing, employment options, and development that strengthens existing communities, aligned with the Sustainable Communities Action Plan. Also supports reinvestment and revitalization of older communities and eligibility for state incentive programs including Community Legacy, Neighborhood BusinessWorks, and the Strategic Demolition and Smart Growth Impact Fund. Specific uses include capital projects (parks, community centers, athletic facilities), infrastructure improvements (pedestrian/bicycle paths, trails, bus stop improvements, street extensions, bicycle/pedestrian crossing upgrades, sidewalk improvements, streetscape retrofits), community services (senior programs, child care, food assistance), housing rehabilitation and affordable housing development, planning and feasibility studies, design services, business facade and retail improvements, green infrastructure and stormwater management, commercial revitalization, library expansion, recreational facility improvements, town center placemaking, wayfinding signage, workforce training, transit operations, and property rehabilitation and redevelopment of underutilized properties.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The proposed community area must be within a Priority Funding Area, and within or near a town center or transportation center. The area must show a financial need for local revitalization. In Baltimore City, eligible areas include Main Streets corridors, Healthy Neighborhoods areas, transit-oriented development zones, arts and entertainment districts, anchor institution areas, and emerging market neighborhoods within the designated Sustainable Community boundary. In Anne Arundel County, designated areas include Brooklyn Park, Glen Burnie (both approved 2013), and Odenton/Severn (approved 2014). Prince George's County and Howard County communities are also eligible within their designated Sustainable Community areas. The National Capital Strategic Economic Development Fund applies to areas between Washington D.C. and Interstate 495. The Baltimore Regional Neighborhood Initiative (BRNI) applies to inner beltway Sustainable Communities within and surrounding Baltimore City.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For new designations: 1. Email Tynan Stevenson at tynan.stevenson@maryland.gov to request an application template. Include 'Sustainable Communities [New Designation or Renewal] Application – [Community Name] - [Sponsoring Jurisdiction]' in the subject line. New designation applicants must schedule a meeting with program staff before applying. 2. Submit an application including a defined geographic area, a Sustainable Community Action Plan, and a local government resolution. 3. An interagency panel led by DHCD reviews the application. 4. The panel presents the application to the Governor's Smart Growth Subcabinet for final approval. 5. Once approved, the designation is valid for five years. For renewals: Submit a comprehensive renewal application including sections on Applicant Information, Qualitative Assessment, Competitive Funding, Action Plan Update, Workgroup Roster, and Signature Letter, along with CAO signature and County Attorney approval. For boundary amendments (e.g., Baltimore City): Submit a request to the Baltimore City Planning Department at plan@baltimorecity.gov with the address of boundaries to be included and bullet points showing alignment with the SC Action Plan strategies. The Planning Department reviews the request in collaboration with other city agencies and forwards it to DHCD's internal review committee. The requester receives a letter with the decision. For Anne Arundel County information, contact Lynn Miller at the Office of Planning and Zoning (410-222-7431 or pzmill03@aacounty.org) or visit the Maryland DHCD website for individual state financing and tax credit programs. For Howard County information, visit https://www.howardcountymd.gov/planning-zoning/resource/sustainable-communities. For Prince George's County, contact the Economic Development Corporation at 301-583-4650 and ask to speak with a Business Development Specialist, or visit the Maryland Department of Planning website for more information.
