structured_extraction.program_description: The Technical Assistance Grant (TAG) program helps local governments and nonprofit organizations cover operating costs related to local housing and community revitalization efforts. Grants can pay for salaries, professional services, technology, and other administrative expenses tied to community and economic revitalization activities. The program also supports capacity building, housing studies, professional design and planning services, homeownership preparation, and home repair programs. Projects must be located in or serve designated Priority Funding Areas or Sustainable Community areas. Part of the Operating Assistance Grant Program under DHCD's Division of Neighborhood Revitalization.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $50,000 to cover operating costs including staff and consultant services, general operating expenses, professional services contracts, and technology costs. No funding match is required. Projects must be completed within one year. Grant funds may not be used for capital project costs. Upon award execution, organizations may request a 25% advance of funds. Past Kent County recipients received awards ranging from $20,000 to $30,000 for housing studies, professional design services, nonprofit capacity building, and home repair programs.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating costs related to administering community revitalization efforts, including salaries, professional services contracts, technology costs, and other related administrative expenses. Also supports capacity building, housing studies, professional services for design and planning, homeownership preparation, and home repair programs. Eligible expenses include contracts, consultant services, payroll, and other documented operational costs. Capital project costs are not eligible. Cannot fund alcohol, controlled substances, entertainment, personal items, fines, parking tickets, or travel companions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in or serve residents of a Priority Funding Area (verified using the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper tool). Additional consideration for projects in designated ENOUGH Act, Just Communities, and Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) areas. Available statewide in Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_name: UPLIFT (Utilizing Progressive Lending Investments to Finance Transformation)
structured_extraction.program_description: UPLIFT helps close the appraisal gap in historically redlined communities by funding the difference between the cost to build or renovate affordable housing and the price the property can sell for on the market. The program aims to increase property values and create wealth-building homeownership opportunities by accelerating the development, construction, and sale of quality affordable housing in low-income census tracts and designated Sustainable Communities. It also couples development loans to build new housing with a commitment from DHCD to offer grants and loans to nearby Legacy Homeowners, often living in energy-inefficient and deteriorated housing. The program focuses on reversing disinvestment patterns in low-property-value areas through new construction or substantial rehabilitation of formerly vacant structures, and encourages meaningful involvement of nonprofits, public housing authorities, and local small businesses.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: UPLIFT covers the appraisal gap — the difference between the total eligible cost to develop a property and the price it can sell for on the market. Selected development teams receive a combination of public and private financing. The State provides 2nd lien development loans up to $75,000 per unit. Homebuyers receive a promissory note for the appraisal gap amount at 0% interest, with the balance declining 20% annually and fully forgiven after 5 years. At least 25% of units must be sold to households at or below 80% AMI. There is a $1,000 non-refundable application fee per project and a 1% origination fee due at initial closing.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis, as long as funding is available
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit and for-profit developers and builders, community-based organizations, Public Housing Authorities, and local small businesses working to develop, build, and sell quality affordable housing in low-income census tracts and designated Sustainable Communities in Maryland. Homebuyers earning up to 80% Area Median Income (AMI) are the intended end beneficiaries.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition, development, construction, and sale of quality affordable housing in targeted neighborhoods to close the appraisal gap. Eligible costs include: property acquisition, hard construction costs (new construction and substantial rehabilitation of formerly vacant structures), soft costs (legal, title, engineering, environmental, architectural fees), off-site infrastructure improvements, developer fees (maximum $50,000/DU or 12.5% of total development costs), marketing and sales, neighborhood engagement activities, and homebuyer assistance through down payments, down payment assistance, mortgages, or UPLIFT subsidy loans.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in both a low-income census tract (where 50% of households have incomes below 60% AMI or poverty rate ≥25%) AND a designated Maryland Sustainable Community. New construction projects cannot be in FEMA Flood Zone A or V; Zone C and X require waivers with flood documentation. Projects must be within a defined project area (a single municipality, jurisdiction, or targeted area). A UPLIFT Qualified Areas Map is available to determine eligibility.

25% of units must be sold to households at or below 80% AMI

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 0: Review the program guide and prepare project details, then schedule a pre-application meeting. Step 1: After the meeting, submit the Electronic Application Submission Request Form to receive a private Dropbox link. Step 2: Download the Application Documents Package, complete all sections, and prepare narratives, certifications, financials, and other required documentation. Step 3: Pay the $1,000 non-refundable fee and upload proof of payment. Step 4: Upload all files to Dropbox and deliver a hard copy to DHCD's Lanham, MD office. Steps 5–6: DHCD reviews and scores eligible projects; if approved, applicants receive a commitment letter. Note: Waiver requests must be submitted in writing to the Director of the Community Development Administration in advance of application submission; DHCD provides a response within 15 calendar days of receipt.

structured_extraction.program_description: The NourishMD Grant Program provides direct grants to eligible food retailers to expand access to healthy and fresh foods in Maryland communities experiencing food insecurity. It is a strategic and targeted investment by Maryland DHCD to support development, stabilization, and expansion of retail outlets providing fresh food in areas with limited or no access to nutritious food options. Retailers can use funds for equipment, facility upgrades, inventory expansion, and infrastructure to support SNAP/EBT acceptance. The program targets areas with limited healthy food access as measured by the Maryland Community Business Compass Fresh Food Gap Score, aiming to build stronger, healthier, and more economically resilient communities across Maryland.

eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Direct grants ranging from $25,000 to $150,000 for capital-related needs supporting business stabilization or expansion. Total funding available is up to $2 million. A $250 processing fee is deducted from the award amount. No application fee. Supplemental loan funding is also available through DHCD's Neighborhood BusinessWorks (NBW) program.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Equipment purchases (refrigeration, shelving, etc.), buildout and facility upgrades, capital costs for inventory expansion, initial inventory costs, working capital tied to expansion or construction, and infrastructure and technology for SNAP/EBT acceptance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must serve a community with a Maryland Community Business Compass (MCBC) Fresh Food Gap Score of 60% or higher. Your business does not need to be listed on the Maryland Community Business Compass to be eligible for the NourishMD grant program.

structured_extraction.program_description: Project Restore provides grant funding to new or expanding businesses that move into previously vacant retail or commercial spaces in Maryland. It offers two types of grants: a Rental Assistance Grant of up to $30,000 for small businesses with 50 or fewer employees, and a Business Operations Grant of up to $250,000 per year for businesses that generate sales and use tax. The program incentivizes commercial investment in vacant retail and commercial properties across Maryland, helping businesses cover rent payments and operating costs.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two grant options are available: (1) Rental Assistance Grant — up to $30,000 total (up to $2,500/month for 12 months) for qualifying small businesses with 50 or fewer full-time equivalent employees; (2) Business Operations Grant — up to $250,000 per year for 1 or 2 years, paid quarterly based on sales and use tax submitted to the state. Businesses in Tier 1 areas (including Baltimore City, Allegany, Baltimore County, Caroline, Cecil, Dorchester, Garrett, Kent, Prince George's, Somerset, Washington, Wicomico, and Worcester Counties, plus any Opportunity Zone or state-designated Main Street) are eligible for 2-year awards; all other counties are eligible for 1-year awards. Business Operations Grant funds may be used for staff costs, capital improvements, marketing, inventory and supplies, utilities, and similar operating expenses — not for executive salaries or bonuses. Total program funding is $25 million.

All other counties are Tier 2 (1-year award).

structured_extraction.program_name: Administration Of The Maryland Energy Assistance Program (MEAP) And The Electronic Universal Service Program (EUSP) (RFP)
structured_extraction.program_description: This is a Request for Proposals (RFP) issued by the Maryland Department of Human Services, Family Investment Administration, Office of Home Energy Programs (OHEP) for organizations to administer the Maryland Energy Assistance Program (MEAP) and the Electronic Universal Service Program (EUSP). MEAP provides assistance once per year to eligible households and shelters to help with heating and cooling bills for gas, electric, and fossil fuels, as well as emergency assistance to prevent or mitigate energy crises. EUSP provides assistance once per year to eligible applicants with ongoing electric expenses through bill payment assistance. The RFP seeks contractors to manage and deliver energy and utility assistance to eligible Maryland residents, including application intake, eligibility determination, payment processing, outreach, and crisis intervention services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: This is a procurement RFP — not a direct assistance program. The Maryland Department of Human Services is seeking proposals from organizations to administer the MEAP and EUSP programs statewide. Selected contractors would manage intake, outreach, eligibility determination, and benefit delivery for energy assistance to low-income Maryland residents. MEAP provides monetary benefits for heating/cooling bills and emergency energy crisis assistance. EUSP provides electric bill payment assistance. Crisis assistance is provided within 18 hours for life-threatening situations and within 48 hours for energy crisis situations. Direct payments are made to bulk fuel providers, landlords, and applicants. Arrearage assistance is available for past due bills 21+ days overdue.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations seeking to administer the Maryland Energy Assistance Program (MEAP) and Electronic Universal Service Program (EUSP) on behalf of the state. The programs ultimately serve low-income households, including households with members 67+ years old, households with disabled members, and households with high home energy burdens.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Administration of energy assistance and electronic universal service benefit programs for eligible Maryland residents. Includes outreach activities, application intake, certification for benefits, payments processing, eligibility determination notifications, benefit appeals administration, crisis assistance, and home heating equipment repair or replacement. Energy assistance covers heating fuel (gas, electric, oil, kerosene, propane, wood, coal), cooling assistance, utility bill arrearages, and emergency energy crises prevention.
