structured_extraction.program_name: Adoption Search Contact and Reunion Services (ASCARS)
structured_extraction.program_description: ASCARS helps people separated from birth relatives reconnect. The program includes a voluntary registry (MCVAR) that matches adult adoptees, birth parents, and birth siblings, as well as active search services that use trained Confidential Intermediaries (CIs) to identify, locate, and engage sought individuals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free search, contact, and reunion services for eligible individuals. The Department of Human Services does not charge fees for registry enrollment or search services provided by Local Departments of Social Services. Private agencies may charge fees according to their own fee schedule, but fee waivers or reductions may be available upon request with a Fee Waiver Form and supporting documentation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adult adoptees (age 21+), birth parents, and birth siblings (age 21+) involved in adoptions finalized or initiated in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services are used to identify, locate, and facilitate contact between adoptees and birth relatives; access to voluntary adoption registry; non-identifying and medical information requests.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available for adoptions that were finalized or initiated in Maryland.
requirements_list: Adoption must have been finalized or initiated in Maryland
Applicants must be adult adoptees (at least 21 years old), birth parents, or birth siblings (at least 21 years old)
Search services are only available to adult adoptees, birth parents, and birth siblings who were themselves adopted
Parental rights must have been voluntarily terminated for birth parents to request search services
Third-party agencies, relatives, spouses, friends, or affiliates of adoptees may not request services
Complete application packet required (application form, notarized consent form, copy of photo ID, statistical survey)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a completed application packet via the online Google/Smartsheet form or mail a paper application to the Department of Human Services. The Department reviews the information, contacts the relevant jurisdiction or agency to verify adoption records, and assigns a Confidential Intermediary (CI). Both the registrant and CI receive an email identifying the CI. The registrant must contact the CI to initiate the search and enter into a service agreement.

structured_extraction.program_description: Children with special needs who are adopted or placed under guardianship from Maryland's out-of-home (foster) care system may qualify for a financial subsidy and medical assistance coverage to help their adoptive or guardianship families meet the children's needs. Specific subsidy amounts and terms are determined through the local department of social services. Post-adoption support services including clinical services, counseling, support groups, and educational resources are also available for adoptive, foster, kinship, and guardianship families.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible children with special needs may qualify for an adoption or guardianship subsidy and medical assistance coverage after being adopted or placed under guardianship from out-of-home care. Specific subsidy amounts and terms are determined through the local department of social services. Additionally, free post-adoption services are available through partnerships with Adoptions Together/FamilyWorks Together and Center for Adoption Support and Education (C.A.S.E.), including individual and family therapy, interracial adoption support groups, parent advocates, adoption-competent counseling, crisis intervention, and educational training and webinars.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families who adopt or obtain guardianship of children with special needs from Maryland's out-of-home (foster) care system, including adoptive parents, guardians, kinship families, transracial/transcultural families, adult adoptees, and birth parents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Financial support for the care of children with special needs following adoption or guardianship, along with medical assistance coverage. Post-adoption services include counseling and therapy, support groups, case management, crisis intervention, training and webinars, and search and reunion services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through local departments of social services in Maryland.
requirements_list: Child must have special needs
Child must be unable to reunify with birth parents or guardians
Child must be in or have been in Maryland's out-of-home (foster) care system
Adoption or guardianship must be finalized through a local department of social services
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local department of social services for information on eligibility and how to apply. A link to find local contacts is provided on the DHS website. Post-adoption services can be accessed by contacting Adoptions Together/FamilyWorks Together at MD_DHHS_Referrals@familyworkstogether.org or (410) 402-1121, or C.A.S.E. at appts@adoptionsupport.org or 866-217-8534.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants to help low-income households pay off past-due (arrearage) electric and gas utility bills. Eligible customers can receive a grant of up to $2,000 toward their overdue balance. Applicants must have a past-due balance of at least $300 and must already qualify for the Electric Universal Service Program (EUSP). Customers may only receive an arrearage grant once every five years, with certain exceptions. Arrearage grants received between January 1, 2020 and December 31, 2021 do not count toward the five-year limit. The grant is sent directly to the utility company. The program is administered statewide by the Maryland Department of Human Services through local Offices of Home Energy Programs (OHEP), including the Prince George's County Department of Social Services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $2,000 toward past-due electric or gas utility bills, paid directly to the utility company. Customers must have a past-due balance of $300 or more and must qualify for the EUSP. Customers may only receive an arrearage grant once every five years, with certain exceptions. Arrearage grants received between January 1, 2020 and December 31, 2021 do not count toward the five-year limit. Applications may be submitted on a rolling basis, once per fiscal year (July–June).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling; apply at any time during the year, once per fiscal year (July–June)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income Maryland households with past-due electric or gas utility bills of at least $300 who also qualify for the Electric Universal Service Program (EUSP), including residents of Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment toward past-due electric and gas utility bill arrearages, sent directly to the utility company.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. In Prince George's County, applications may also be submitted to the Prince George's County Department of Social Services at 805 Brightseat Road, Landover, MD 20785, or in person at 425 Brightseat Road, Landover, MD 20785.
requirements_list: Must have a past-due electric or gas utility bill of $300 or more
Must be eligible to receive an EUSP grant
Income-based eligibility
May only receive an arrearage grant once every five years (with certain exceptions)
Arrearage grants received between January 1, 2020 and December 31, 2021 do not count toward the five-year limit
Grant amount is based on the outstanding arrearage amount
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Maryland Benefits portal or the local Office of Home Energy Programs (OHEP) as part of the OHEP application process. Applications can be submitted online at dhs.maryland.gov/office-of-home-energy-programs, by email to pgcdss.energy@maryland.gov with completed application and supporting documents, by fax to 301-909-6331, by mail, or in person at a local OHEP office. In Prince George's County, apply at 425 Brightseat Road, Landover, MD 20785 or mail to 805 Brightseat Road, Landover, MD 20785. A fillable application is available at https://dhs.maryland.gov/documents/DHS%20Forms/FIA%20Forms/English/OHEP/OHEP2024Application%20Fillable.pdf.

structured_extraction.program_description: Connects new asylees across Maryland to services and benefits they may be eligible for, while providing case management and support. Staff lead outreach activities statewide to ensure new and existing asylees know about programs funded by MORA and others.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Case management, outreach, and support to connect asylees to services and benefits they may be eligible for.
structured_extraction.program_audience: New and existing asylees in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Case management and support services to help asylees access eligible benefits and programs
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Must be an asylee
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact HIAS Inc. for more information at asyleeoutreach.org

structured_extraction.program_description: This program funds services for families. These services include mediation, counseling, and parent education. It also helps develop parenting plans, enforce visitation, and create guidelines for visitation and custody.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides grant funding to organizations. These organizations then offer services like mediation, counseling, parent education, and help with creating parenting plans.
structured_extraction.program_audience: County governments and non-profit organizations that provide family services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support services for families, including: mediation, counseling, parent education, developing parenting plans, enforcing visitation, and creating visitation guidelines.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must respond to a Request for Proposals (RFP) through the eMMA system.

structured_extraction.program_name: Center for Excellence in Resource Family Development (CfE)
structured_extraction.program_description: A federally-funded, four-year grant program (approximately $8 million over four federal fiscal years beginning October 1, 2019) that develops and implements a model to recruit, prepare, and support foster and kinship resource parents in Maryland. The program provides evidence-based training (KEEP/KEEP SAFE for resource parents; PTC-R for families of origin), mobile crisis response, respite care, peer support, stipends, and technical assistance to help resource parents work closely with birth families to support timely reunification and reduce unnecessary congregate care placements. The program aims to improve child and family well-being through increased timely reunification or guardianship, prevention of re-entry after reunification, and maintaining essential connections. Local departments of social services receive technical assistance from model developers, a robust foster parent training program, and participation in a Quality Improvement Collaborative (QIC). Implemented in five pilot sites across Maryland: Baltimore County, Carroll County, Frederick County, Montgomery County, and Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Resource parents receive an enhanced board rate (CfE Differential) plus a bed retainer rate to reserve space for CfE-eligible youth. They also receive $25 gift card per completed training module, stipends for weekly KEEP/KEEP SAFE attendance, and compensation for participation in support activities. Training includes a 16-week KEEP/KEEP SAFE evidence-based parenting support and skill-building program, a four-module (8-hour) Parent Partnership curriculum, and virtual training modules on co-parenting and implicit bias. Birth/families of origin receive 16-week Parenting Through Change for Reunification (PTC-R) program (10 weeks of group sessions plus 6-week post-reunification follow-up), with childcare, snacks, peer support, and stipends provided. Mobile Response and Stabilization Services (MRSS) dispatch a therapist to the home within 1 hour during mental health or behavioral crises, and planned and emergency respite care is available. Local departments of social services (LDSS) receive technical assistance from model developers, workforce training on parent partnership practices, and participation in a Quality Improvement Collaborative (QIC).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Resource (foster and kinship) parents selected by their local department of social services, birth families of children in foster care working toward reunification or guardianship, child welfare workers and LDSS staff and supervisors, and local departments of social services participating as implementation sites seeking to improve resource family recruitment, retention, and support. Children and youth ages 4–18 in out-of-home care are the ultimate beneficiaries.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training resource and birth parents (KEEP/KEEP SAFE, PTC-R, Parent Partnership curriculum), providing stipends and enhanced board rates for resource parents, mobile response and stabilization services, respite care, peer support groups, case management, workforce training and capacity building, technical assistance to improve foster family recruitment, retention, and reunification outcomes for children in foster care, and quality improvement activities and evaluation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program implemented in five pilot LDSS sites in Maryland: Baltimore County, Carroll County, Frederick County, Montgomery County, and Prince George's County. Local departments of social services applied through a competitive process to be selected as CfE implementation sites. Resource parents are selected by their local department from among existing or newly recruited resource families in the community.
requirements_list: Resource parents must be selected by their local department of social services to participate
Resource parents must sign a commitment form outlining training and practice expectations
Resource parents must commit to the values of the CfE, including prioritizing reunification and shared parenting
Resource parents must be willing to engage authentically and respectfully with birth families
Resource parents must be trauma-responsive and practice cultural humility
Resource parents must participate in prerequisite training in addition to Maryland's standard pre-service training
Resource parents must participate in KEEP/KEEP SAFE sessions and support groups
Resource parents must actively work to build and maintain positive relationships with birth parents and extended family members
Resource parents must invite birth parents into their home regularly and stay in regular communication with the birth parent
Children must be age 4+ for KEEP; age 13+ for KEEP SAFE
Families of origin must have a permanency goal of reunification or guardianship to be eligible for PTC-R
Resource parents must have an eligible child currently placed in their home
KEEP/KEEP SAFE requires attendance of at least 12 of 16 sessions for completion
Local sites must have sufficient staff and resources to implement the interventions and participate in the QIC
Local sites must commit to collecting data on process and outcome measures
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Local departments of social services (LDSS) applied through a standardized application assessed on a rubric for readiness and capacity, followed by phone interviews. Five LDSS sites were selected (Baltimore County, Carroll County, Frederick County, Montgomery County, and Prince George's County). LDSS then select resource parents within their jurisdiction to participate. Resource parents are not selected through an open public application — they are chosen by their local department from among existing or newly recruited resource families in the community.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides comprehensive assistance to refugees and other eligible populations on Maryland's Eastern Shore, helping them connect with available resources, federal and state benefits, and support to become self-sufficient.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Services include case management, application support for financial/medical/nutritional assistance, employment and job placement assistance, career counseling, training and skill-building, English language instruction, youth programming, psycho-social support, and immigration-related legal assistance. All services are culturally informed, linguistically appropriate, and trauma sensitive.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Haitian Development Center of Delmarva (HDCD); Rebirth, Inc.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Refugees and eligible populations on Maryland's Eastern Shore
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Case management, employment assistance, language instruction, youth programming, psycho-social support, and legal assistance to achieve self-sufficiency
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Eastern Shore of Maryland, based in Salisbury (Wicomico County)
requirements_list: Must be a refugee or other eligible population
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Haitian Development Center of Delmarva (hdcd.org) or Rebirth, Inc. (rebirth4hope.org) for more information

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Child Support Administration helps parents and caregivers establish, collect, and manage child support payments. The program assists custodial parents, non-custodial parents, and caregivers with opening child support cases, establishing paternity, setting up payment arrangements, and enforcing court orders for child support. Services include paternity establishment, support order establishment and modification, payment collection and distribution, and enforcement of existing orders. The program also supports modification of existing child support orders due to material changes in circumstances such as changes in employment, custody, childcare expenses, or health care costs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program helps custodial parents and caregivers collect child support payments from non-custodial parents. Services include paternity establishment, support order establishment and modification, payment collection and distribution, and enforcement of existing orders. There is a one-time $15 application fee (waived for current or former Temporary Cash Assistance or Medical Assistance recipients). An additional annual $15 fee applies to cases where more than $3,500 in payments are distributed in a given year. Modification of existing child support orders is also available through the Child Support Administration based on material changes in circumstances, or through Circuit Court using form CC-DR-006. Financial statements (form CCDR-030) are used to document income and expenses for child support calculation in court proceedings.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Parents and caregivers seeking to establish, modify, or collect child support, and non-custodial parents making child support payments in Maryland. Also includes parents/guardians involved in child support modification proceedings in Circuit Court.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Child support payments are distributed to custodial parents and caregivers to help cover the costs of raising children. Financial documentation supports child support calculation in court proceedings.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Out-of-state applicants are encouraged to apply through their state of residence using the Uniform Interstate Family Support Act (UIFSA) process. Modification requests must be filed with the county office or Circuit Court where the case originated.
requirements_list: Must be a parent or caregiver involved in a child support case
Applicant must be a parent or caregiver seeking child support services
A separate application is required for each case
A $15 one-time application fee is required (waived if you currently or previously received Temporary Cash Assistance or Medical Assistance)
For modification requests: completion of Modification Review Questionnaire, Notice of Legal Representation form, and two-page Financial Statement
For modification requests: submission of current child support order and guidelines worksheet
For modification requests: four recent paystubs or income verification documents
For modification requests: W-2s, 1099s, tax forms, or tax returns for previous year
For modification requests: documentation of material change in circumstances (employment, custody, childcare, or medical expenses)
For modification requests: photo ID or driver's license copy
For court modification (CC-DR-006): must attach completed financial statement (CC-DR-030 or CC-DR-031 depending on income)
For court modification (CC-DR-006): must serve opposing party and local child support office if applicable
For court modification (CC-DR-006): must wait at least 30 days since entry of original child support order before filing
For financial statement (CCDR-030): must file Notice Regarding Restricted Information (form MDJ-008)

For financial statement (CCDR-030): report total monthly income from all sources (excluding means-tested benefits), existing support obligations, alimony, health insurance premiums, child care expenses, extraordinary medical expenses, and school/transportation costs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online through MarylandBenefits.gov (recommended), by mail using a paper application downloaded from the website or picked up at a local Child Support office, or in person at a local Child Support office, or by calling 800-332-6347. If seeking establishment or modification of a court order, include a Financial Statement with your application. Online applications have a $1.50 convenience fee if the $15 application fee applies. Paper applications can also be mailed, faxed, or hand-delivered to a local Child Support office. For administrative modification requests, submit the completed modification packet to the county-specific child support office via email. For court modification, complete form CC-DR-006, attach the appropriate financial statement, file with the Circuit Court clerk, and serve the opposing party.

structured_extraction.program_name: Commodity Supplemental Food Program (CSFP) / My Groceries To Go!
structured_extraction.program_description: My Groceries To Go! (also known as CSFP) reduces food insecurity for low-income seniors by providing monthly food packages valued at approximately $50. The program helps seniors avoid choosing between healthy food and other necessities like medicine or rent. Participants can pick up their package at a local food bank or sponsor, have someone pick it up for them, or in some areas receive home delivery. The program also utilizes food distribution as an avenue for seniors to access information about nutrition, programs, and services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Monthly supplemental food packages containing USDA Foods distributed according to approved food package guide rates. Packages are distributed on a monthly basis via self pick-up, group pick-up, or home delivery. Includes nutrition education materials and activities. Distributed through local agencies including the Salvation Army Central Maryland Area Command, Capital Area Food Bank, and Allegany County Human Resources Development Commission (AHRDC).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Seniors age 60 or older with incomes at or below 150% of the Federal Poverty Level (based on household size) residing in Maryland, particularly in Allegany County, Anne Arundel County, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Carroll County, Garrett County, Harford County, Howard County, Montgomery County, Prince George's County, or Queen Anne's County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Monthly USDA food packages to supplement the diets of eligible low-income seniors.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland, with distribution sites in Allegany County, Anne Arundel County, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Carroll County, Garrett County, Harford County, Howard County, Montgomery County, Prince George's County, and Queen Anne's County.
requirements_list: Must be 60 years of age or older
Must have household income at or below 150% of the Federal Poverty Level (based on household size)
Must verify name, age, and address using a government-issued ID (may be past original expiration date)
Must provide proof of identification at time of food package collection
Must live in an area served by a CSFP local agency in Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete a certification form developed by the State agency and approved by FNSRO. Provide verification of name, age, and address using acceptable government-issued ID. Report income to be certified within eligibility guidelines. Contact one of Maryland's CSFP providers directly to apply: The Salvation Army Central Maryland Area Command, Capital Area Food Bank, or the Allegany County Human Resources Development Commission. Waiting lists may be maintained if capacity is reached.

structured_extraction.program_description: CAAP allows private attorneys across Maryland to provide legal representation in child and adult protective proceedings when a conflict of interest arises with a Maryland Legal Services Program (MLSP) Provider. The program ensures that children involved in Child in Need of Assistance (CINA) and Termination of Parental Rights (TPR) cases, and low-income alleged vulnerable adults in Adult Protective Services (APS) and Adult Public Guardianship Review Board (APGRB) proceedings, receive quality legal representation throughout the court process.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Private attorneys are paid to provide legal representation in conflict cases for children and indigent alleged vulnerable adults in court proceedings statewide.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private attorneys statewide who can provide legal representation in CINA, TPR, APS, and APGRB proceedings when a conflict of interest arises with an MLSP Provider.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Legal representation of children and indigent alleged vulnerable adults in court proceedings.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across all of Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a private attorney
Must be available to handle cases where a conflict of interest arises with an MLSP Provider
Cases must involve CINA, TPR, APS, or APGRB proceedings

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that promotes the safety and well-being of children and their families by strengthening parents' ability to create a safe and stable home environment while keeping families together. Caseworkers from the Local Department of Social Services work closely with each family member to develop a plan.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Caseworkers provide personalized support plans including help for families affected by substance use, parenting resources, therapy and behavior support referrals, education plans, healthcare assistance, and connections to community providers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with children who need support to maintain a safe and stable home environment
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Support for substance use issues, parenting skills, therapy and behavior referrals, education planning, and healthcare assistance
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through local departments of social services
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local department of social services for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland replaces food and cash benefits that have been stolen from EBT cards. This program reimburses Maryland residents whose Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT) benefits — including SNAP food assistance, cash assistance (TCA, TDAP, PAA, RCA, TSS), SUN Bucks, or Pandemic EBT (P-EBT) benefits — were stolen without their permission. Eligible households can receive 100% replacement of confirmed stolen benefits dating back to January 1, 2021. Since March 2023, the state has operated the reimbursement program using both federal and state funds. Maryland was the first state to use federal funds to replace stolen SNAP benefits. As of April 2026, over $50 million in benefits have been replaced across more than 97,000 approved claims.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: DHS replaces 100% of EBT and P-EBT benefits confirmed to be stolen, including SNAP food benefits, cash assistance (TCA, TDAP, PAA, RCA, TSS), SUN Bucks, and Pandemic EBT benefits. Replacement benefits are loaded directly onto the recipient's EBT card within 10 business days of claim submission. Claims submitted more than 45 days after the applicant became aware of the theft are not eligible (for benefits stolen on or after March 1, 2023). Benefits stolen January 1, 2021 – September 30, 2022 have no deadline; benefits stolen October 1, 2022 – February 28, 2023 had a deadline of May 31, 2023. Willingly sharing an EBT card and PIN with someone who then steals benefits is also not eligible for reimbursement. As of April 2026, over $50 million in benefits have been replaced across more than 97,000 approved claims.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Benefits stolen Jan. 1, 2021 – Sept. 30, 2022: No deadline; Benefits stolen Oct. 1, 2022 – Feb. 28, 2023: May 31, 2023; Benefits stolen on or after March 1, 2023: within 45 days of discovering the theft
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland EBT cardholders (SNAP, cash assistance, SUN Bucks, or P-EBT recipients) whose benefits were stolen without their permission
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Replacement of stolen EBT food assistance (SNAP), cash assistance benefits (TCA, TDAP, PAA, RCA, TSS), SUN Bucks, and Pandemic EBT benefits
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Must be an EBT cardholder (SNAP, cash assistance, SUN Bucks, or P-EBT recipient)
Must have had EBT benefits stolen without permission
Must complete and submit an EBT Stolen Benefits Attestation Claim Form (EBT Fraud Claim Attestation form)
For benefits stolen on or after March 1, 2023, claim must be submitted within 45 days of becoming aware of the theft
For benefits stolen January 1, 2021 – September 30, 2022, there is no filing deadline
For benefits stolen October 1, 2022 – February 28, 2023, the deadline was May 31, 2023
Benefits cannot be replaced if the cardholder willingly shared their EBT card and PIN with the person who stole benefits
Stolen benefits must have occurred on or after January 1, 2021
Must file a claim to receive reimbursement
Type name on signature line and submit form
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the EBT Stolen Benefits Attestation Claim Form (EBT Fraud Claim Attestation form) online at marylandbenefits.gov or through the DHS reimbursement portal at dhs.maryland.gov/ebt-reimbursement/, by scanning the QR code on outreach materials, by phone with help from a SNAP Community Partner Organization, or in person at a Local Department of Social Services office. Type name on signature line and submit form. DHS will make a decision within 10 business days. If denied, you may request a Fair Hearing by completing DHS/FIA 334 form and submitting to your local office or the Office of Administrative Hearings within 90 days of the notice date (within 10 days to maintain benefit continuity).

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland ETV program provides annual vouchers on a first-come, first-served basis to current and former foster care youth to help pay for college, university, or vocational school tuition and related educational costs. Youth enrolled full-time may receive up to $5,000 annually; part-time enrollment may receive up to $2,500. Administered in partnership with the nonprofit Foster Care to Success and the Maryland Department of Human Services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $5,000 annually for full-time enrollment, or up to $2,500 for part-time enrollment in college or vocational school. Funds are distributed on a first-come, first-served basis. Foster youth must submit the FAFSA by Maryland's March 1st deadline to be eligible.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: March 1st each year (FAFSA deadline for Maryland state financial aid)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Current foster care youth in out-of-home placement and former foster care youth who were placed into guardianship or adopted after age 16, seeking to attend college, university, or vocational programs in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Education-related expenses including college or vocational school tuition, fees, and other costs associated with attending a postsecondary or vocational program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to eligible foster care youth.
requirements_list: Must be currently in out-of-home placement, OR placed into guardianship or adopted after age 16, OR a former foster care youth
Must be enrolled full-time or part-time in a college, university, or vocational school
Must submit the FAFSA by the March 1st Maryland deadline
Funds awarded on a first-come, first-served basis
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the FAFSA online at studentaid.gov by the March 1st Maryland deadline. Contact your caseworker or Independent Living Coordinator for additional details and to initiate the voucher application process.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Electric Universal Service Program (EUSP) is the Office of Home Energy Programs (OHEP) electric assistance program administered by the Maryland Department of Human Services for low-income, elderly, or disabled households statewide. It provides an annual grant applied directly to the recipient's electric company to help cover current or past-due electric costs. Enrolled customers are placed on a budget billing plan with their utility company to spread annual utility costs into even monthly payments. The grant amount is determined by household income and electric use over the past 12 months, and benefits are available once per program year (July through June). Eligible populations include low-income households, elderly or disabled individuals on a limited income, and those receiving veterans or Social Security disability benefits. In Washington County, applications may be submitted online or in person at the Washington County Community Action Council. In Prince George's County, applications may be submitted online, by email, fax, mail, or in person. In St. Mary's County, applications are accepted July through May each year through the Tri-County Community Action Committee at senior activity centers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One grant per program year (July–June) applied directly to the recipient's electric company to assist low-income, elderly, or disabled households with current or past-due electric charges. Grant amount is determined by household income and electric use over the past 12 months. Enrolled customers are placed on a budget billing plan with their utility company to spread annual costs into even monthly payments. No turn-off notice is required to qualify, and benefits can be received once per fiscal year.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling; applications accepted July through May each year (program year July–June)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income, elderly, or disabled electric customers and households in Maryland who need help paying current or past-due electric bills, including those receiving veterans or Social Security disability benefits. In Washington County, serves low-income families struggling to pay electric bills.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment of current or past-due electric utility bills, paid directly to the applicant's electric company.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. In Washington County, apply online at wccac.org or in person at Washington County Community Action Council, 117 Summit Avenue, Hagerstown, MD 21740. In Prince George's County, apply at 425 Brightseat Road, Landover, MD 20785 or online. In St. Mary's County, applications may be submitted at any senior activity center through the Tri-County Community Action Committee between July and May each year.
requirements_list: Must be a low-income household or electric customer in Maryland
Elderly or disabled and living on a limited income, and/or receiving veterans or Social Security disability benefits
Must meet income-based eligibility criteria
Must reapply each fiscal year (July–June)
Can only receive benefits once per program year
No turn-off notice required to qualify
Must participate in utility company's budget billing plan
Grant amount based on household income and electric use over the past 12 months
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Maryland Benefits portal at dhs.maryland.gov/office-of-home-energy-programs, contact your local Home Energy Program (OHEP) office, or call 1-800-332-6347. In Washington County, apply online at https://www.wccac.org/our-services/energy-assistance or schedule an appointment at Washington County Community Action Council, 117 Summit Avenue, Hagerstown, MD 21740. In Prince George's County, apply online, by email to pgcdss.energy@maryland.gov with completed application and supporting documents, by fax to 301-909-6331, by mail to Prince George's County Department of Social Services, 805 Brightseat Road, Landover, MD 20785, or in person at 425 Brightseat Road, Landover, MD 20785. In St. Mary's County, apply at any senior activity center through the Tri-County Community Action Committee between July and May each year. Upon approval, the grant is sent directly to the electric company.

structured_extraction.program_name: Emergency Assistance to Families with Children (EAFC)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides emergency financial assistance to families with dependent children under age 21 who are facing an immediate crisis. Eligible crises include eviction notices, mortgage foreclosures, gas and electric shut-off notices, delinquent water bills, emergency fuel and heating shortages, and burial assistance. Funds are available through the local Department of Social Services once every 24 months per household, subject to fund availability. The program is administered statewide by the Maryland Department of Human Services, with county-level administration including Anne Arundel County DSS, Prince George's County DSS, and Howard County DSS.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time emergency cash assistance available once every 24 months per household, subject to fund availability. Covers rent (eviction prevention), mortgage foreclosure prevention, emergency fuel or heating costs, gas and electric utility shut-offs, delinquent water bills, burial assistance, and other urgent emergency expenses. Apply through your local DHS/DSS office or online at MarylandBenefits.gov.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with one or more dependent children under age 21 (or who are pregnant) who are facing an immediate financial crisis such as eviction, mortgage foreclosure, utility shutoff, delinquent water bill, emergency fuel or heating shortage, or burial need. Available to Maryland residents statewide, including Anne Arundel County, Prince George's County, and Howard County residents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rent (eviction prevention), mortgage foreclosure prevention, emergency fuel or heating costs, gas and electric utility shut-off notices, delinquent water bills, burial assistance, and other urgent emergency expenses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Maryland resident. Available statewide through local Departments of Social Services, including Anne Arundel County DSS (410-269-4500), Howard County DSS at 9780 Patuxent Woods Drive, Columbia, MD 21046, and Prince George's County DSS offices.
requirements_list: Must have at least one related dependent child under 21 living in the household, or be pregnant
Must be related to the child by blood, marriage, or adoption
Must be a Maryland resident
Household members must be U.S. citizens, lawful permanent resident aliens, refugees, or asylees
Must be facing an immediate crisis such as eviction, foreclosure, utility shutoff, delinquent water bill, emergency fuel/heating shortage, or burial need
Must demonstrate an emergency not caused by a family member voluntarily quitting a job without good cause
Must not have refused to accept employment
Must be actively engaged in job search or employed
Must provide proof that household can maintain ongoing monthly rent and utilities
Must have evidence of a stable source of income to prevent recurrence of the emergency
Must provide an eviction notice, utility shutoff notice, or other proof of emergency
Must provide identification
Must provide proof of address/residency
Must provide proof of income for the past 30 days (wage stubs, benefit letters from SSA, Veterans Assistance, or Unemployment Insurance)
Must provide current bank account statement and balance
Must provide proof of other cash or non-cash resources
Must provide Social Security Number for everyone receiving services
Must provide proof of household expenses
Available only once in a 24-month period per household
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply in person at your local Department of Social Services, or submit an application by mail, fax, or other electronic means. You can also apply online at MarylandBenefits.gov (mydhrbenefits.dhr.state.md.us). Bring required documents including valid ID, proof of residency, proof of income (wage stubs for past 30 days, benefit letters), court order or summons, utility shut-off notice, record of monthly expenses and bills for at least 30 days, current bank account statement and balance, and Social Security numbers for all household members. In Anne Arundel County, contact the local DSS office at 410-269-4500. In Howard County, apply at Howard County DSS at 9780 Patuxent Woods Drive, Columbia, MD 21046. In Prince George's County, visit one of the local Prince George's County DSS offices. Interpretation services are available free of charge for limited English proficiency customers.

structured_extraction.program_description: Free English language classes for refugees to help them learn English, integrate socially, and become economically self-sufficient. Classes are offered online with in-person testing at locations in Baltimore City, Montgomery County, and Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free English language classes offered online, with in-person testing available. Classes are provided through three community college partners: Baltimore City Community College (serving Baltimore City and surrounding counties), Montgomery College (serving Montgomery County), and Prince George's Community College (serving Prince George's County).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Newly arrived refugees living in Baltimore City and surrounding counties, Montgomery County, or Prince George's County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: English language instruction to support social integration and economic self-sufficiency
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Montgomery County, Prince George's County, and the Baltimore Metropolitan Area
requirements_list: Must be a refugee
Must be newly arrived (inquire through assigned caseworker)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Newly arrived refugees should inquire about enrollment with their assigned caseworker. Classes are available through three community college partners depending on location.

structured_extraction.program_description: Allows former Maryland foster youth to voluntarily re-enter foster care so they can continue learning and practicing independent living skills and access all services available to youth in out-of-home placement.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: All services provided to youth in out-of-home placement, including housing, health care, education, employment, and financial literacy support.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Independent Living Coordinator at local Department of Social Services
structured_extraction.program_audience: Former Maryland foster youth who left foster care before age 21 and are not older than 20 years and 6 months at time of application.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: All services available to youth in out-of-home foster care placement.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through local departments of social services.
requirements_list: Youth was in care, custody, or guardianship of a Maryland local department of social services on their 18th birthday
Youth left foster care prior to age 21
Youth is not older than 20 years and 6 months at time of application
Youth did not exit foster care due to reunification, adoption, guardianship, marriage, or military duty

Within 30 days of signing the agreement, youth must agree to complete secondary education or equivalent, enroll in post-secondary or vocational training, participate in a program promoting employment, work at least 80 hours per month, or have a documented medical condition preventing these activities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local department of social services for more information and to apply.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides ongoing and intensive support to eligible refugees and similar populations who are not already receiving such help from other programs. Helps clients overcome barriers to self-sufficiency, social integration, and access to benefits and community resources in the U.S.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Case management support to address barriers such as lack of childcare, limited transportation, language illiteracy, financial illiteracy, food insecurity, lack of healthcare, inability to obtain or maintain housing, unfamiliarity with U.S. work culture, and need for legal/immigration assistance.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Ethiopian Community Development Council (ECDC) African Community Center DC Metro; International Rescue Committee (IRC) in Baltimore or Silver Spring; Lutheran Social Services of the National Capital Area (LSSNCA) in Arbutus, Greenbelt, or Frederick
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible refugees and similar populations not already receiving intensive case management from other programs
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Case management to help clients and families overcome barriers to self-sufficiency and achieve their goals in the U.S.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland, with service providers in Baltimore, Silver Spring, Arbutus, Greenbelt, and Frederick
requirements_list: Must be an eligible refugee or similar population
Must not already be receiving intensive case management from another program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact ECDC African Community Center DC Metro (acc-dc.org), IRC Baltimore or Silver Spring (rescue.org), or LSSNCA (lssnca.org) for more information

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program administered through FEMA that provides financial assistance for funeral expenses specifically related to COVID-19 deaths under the Other Needs Assistance (ONA) provision of the Individuals and Households Program (IHP), provided at 100 percent federal cost share under the Coronavirus Response and Relief Supplemental Appropriations Act, 2021, and the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021. Eligible applicants can apply by phone to receive reimbursement for costs such as transportation to identify the deceased, transfer of remains, casket or urn, burial plot, marker or headstone, clergy services, funeral home staff and equipment, cremation or interment, and death certificate costs. Applicants must provide documentation including a death certificate that lists COVID-19 as a cause of death or contributing factor. FEMA awards assistance on a single application per deceased individual; if multiple people contributed to funeral expenses, they may register together as applicant and co-applicant.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement of up to $9,000 per COVID-19-related funeral for actual funeral costs incurred on or after January 20, 2020. Eligible costs include transportation to identify the deceased, transfer of remains, casket or urn, burial plot or cremation niche, marker or headstone, clergy or officiant services, funeral ceremony arrangement, funeral home equipment or staff, cremation or interment costs, death certificate production and certification, and any additional expenses required by local or state law. FEMA awards assistance on a single application per deceased individual; multiple contributors may register as applicant and co-applicant.
structured_extraction.program_audience: U.S. citizens, non-citizen nationals, or qualified aliens (legal residents, asylees, refugees) who paid for funeral expenses for someone who died from COVID-19 on or after January 20, 2020 in the United States, U.S. territories, or District of Columbia.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funeral and burial expenses including transportation to identify the deceased, transfer of remains, casket or urn, burial plot or cremation niche, marker or headstone, clergy or officiant services, funeral ceremony arrangement, funeral home equipment or staff, cremation or interment costs, death certificate production and certification, and any additional expenses required by local or state law.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available nationwide including U.S. territories and the District of Columbia where COVID-19 disaster declarations have been issued, including Maryland residents. Death must have occurred in the United States, U.S. territories, or District of Columbia within an area covered by a COVID-19 disaster declaration.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a U.S. citizen, non-citizen national, or qualified alien (legal resident, asylee, or refugee).
Applicant or co-applicant must have incurred the funeral expenses.
Death certificate must indicate the decedent died from COVID-19, or that COVID-19 was probable, presumed, suspected, or that the death was likely a result of COVID-19 or COVID-19-like symptoms.
A photocopied or scanned copy of the death certificate is acceptable; an original certified copy is not required.
If COVID-19 is not listed on the death certificate, the medical certifier listed on the death certificate must amend the record before applying.
Funeral expenses must have been incurred after January 20, 2020.
Death must have occurred in the United States, U.S. territories, or District of Columbia within an area covered by a COVID-19 disaster declaration.
Documentation of expenses must include the applicant's name as responsible party, the decedent's name, the amount of expenses, and the date incurred.
Expenses already reimbursed by government agencies, voluntary agencies, non-profits, burial or funeral insurance cannot be resubmitted.
If outside assistance was received, documentation of that assistance must be included in the application.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call the COVID-19 Funeral Assistance Line at 844-684-6333 (TTY: 800-462-7585), Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. CT. Before calling, gather required documents including the death certificate and proof of funeral expenses. Multiple individuals who contributed to expenses should register under a single application as applicant and co-applicant. You may also apply through the FEMA website at https://www.fema.gov/disasters/coronavirus/economic/funeral-assistance.

structured_extraction.program_description: A nonprofit that provides one-time financial assistance to low-income households facing an energy crisis, such as a utility shut-off notice or a need for bulk fuel. The fund combines resources from the client, local charitable organizations, and the Fuel Fund to resolve outstanding energy bills. Households may still qualify even if they exceed Energy Assistance income limits and are eligible for assistance once every 12 months.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time financial assistance to resolve outstanding energy bills or cover a bulk fuel purchase. Households are eligible once every 12 months.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income households facing an energy crisis, including those who may exceed Energy Assistance income limits and those needing help paying utility bills
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Paying outstanding energy bills or purchasing bulk fuel
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland, available to households meeting eligibility requirements
requirements_list: Must have a utility shut-off notice
Must have completed an application for Energy Assistance through the Office of Home Energy Programs
Households may still qualify even if they exceed Energy Assistance income limits
Eligible once every 12 months
Must be a low-income household
Must meet Fuel Fund of Maryland eligibility requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at https://fuelfundmaryland.org/apply on Tuesdays and Wednesdays from 9:00 am to 12:00 pm. The application link is only available during open hours and based on availability.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Homelessness Prevention Program (HPP) helps individuals and families facing a housing crisis by providing small, one-time emergency grants to prevent eviction and keep people safely housed. The program also offers case management, counseling, budgeting and life skills training, tenant rights education, and mediation between landlords and tenants.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time direct grants are paid to landlords to prevent eviction. Case management, counseling, budgeting and life skills training, tenant rights education, and landlord-tenant mediation are also provided.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and families facing eviction or a housing crisis who have a lease in their name and can demonstrate the ability to pay rent going forward.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rent payments to landlords to prevent eviction; budgeting and life skills training; tenant rights education; landlord-tenant mediation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through local Departments of Social Services (DSS) offices.
requirements_list: Must have a lease in their name
Must demonstrate the ability to pay rent going forward
Local DSS or service provider must determine the household can remain in permanent housing or move to other permanent housing
Must comply with a documented case plan
All policies applied consistently and in accordance with COMAR
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local Department of Social Services office to apply. Find your local office at https://dhs.maryland.gov/local-offices.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides aide services in the home to help adults with disabilities with personal care (dressing, bathing, grooming, eating), household chores (cooking, laundry, cleaning, shopping), and other daily living activities. The goal is to help adults remain living at home and avoid unnecessary placement in nursing homes or other facilities. Ongoing case management is also provided.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: In-home aide services are provided on a sliding-scale fee basis depending on the applicant's income and family size. The applicant may need to contribute toward the hourly cost of the aide service, with fees paid to the local Department of Social Services. The number of individuals served depends on available funding, and a ranking scale is used to prioritize those with the greatest need.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults aged 18 and older residing in Maryland who have functional disabilities and need help with personal care, chores, or daily living activities to remain in their own homes. Priority is given to vulnerable adults with no willing or capable caregiver, those at risk of institutional placement, and those at risk of abuse or neglect.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Personal care assistance (dressing, bathing, transferring, grooming, eating), household chores (cooking, laundry, light cleaning, shopping), and other activities of daily living to help adults remain in their homes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Applicants must reside in Maryland and apply through their local Department of Social Services.
requirements_list: Must be at least 18 years old
Must reside in Maryland
Must have a functional disability
Must need assistance with personal care, chores, and/or activities of daily living to remain at home
Priority given to those with no willing or capable caregiver, those at risk of institutional placement, and those at risk of abuse or neglect
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The individual or their caregiver should call the local Department of Social Services in the county or city where they live. A local department representative will arrange a home visit to interview the applicant and assess their specific needs. A ranking scale is used to prioritize those with the greatest need based on available funding.

structured_extraction.program_description: Voluntary aftercare services for former foster youth ages 18-21 that provide financial assistance for room and board, referrals, and support to help them achieve self-sufficiency after leaving foster care. Services are time-limited and include financial assistance to purchase goods and services, as well as referrals for counseling, employment, education, and medical assistance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Time-limited financial assistance for room and board and to purchase goods and services, provided through the local Department of Social Services. Also includes referrals for counseling, employment, education, and medical assistance.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Independent Living Coordinator at local Department of Social Services
structured_extraction.program_audience: Former foster youth ages 18-21 who need help transitioning to self-sufficiency after leaving foster care.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Room and board expenses; purchase of goods and services; counseling, employment, education, and medical assistance referrals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through local departments of social services where the youth resides.
requirements_list: Was in foster care until age 18
Currently under 21 years old
Exited out-of-home placement after their 18th birthday but have not attained age 21, OR exited via adoption or relative guardianship after their 16th birthday
Need continued help making the transition to self-sufficiency
Participate in developing a service agreement and sign and comply with its terms
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local Department of Social Services or your caseworker to apply for Aftercare Services. Contact the Independent Living Coordinator at your local department for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides financial and support benefits to informal kinship caregivers — relatives or family by choice who are voluntarily caring for a child full time without state involvement. Benefits include cash assistance, medical coverage, food assistance, energy assistance, and childcare support.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible caregivers can apply for multiple benefits on behalf of the child: (1) Temporary Cash Assistance 'Child Only Grant' — not income-dependent but requires applying for child support; (2) Medical Assistance/Insurance including Maryland Children's Health Program (MCHP) for uninsured children up to age 19 and Medicaid for aged, blind, disabled, or medically needy individuals; (3) SNAP/Supplemental Food Program food assistance — income-dependent; (4) Maryland Energy Assistance Program (MEAP); (5) Office of Home Energy Programs (OHEP); (6) Child Care Scholarship Program through the Maryland State Department of Education; (7) Social Security Survivor Benefits or SSI if parents are deceased or disabled. Additional non-financial supports include health care and education affidavits, kinship navigator services, training, and referrals to community partners.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Informal kinship caregivers who are relatives (within five degrees of blood or marriage) caring for a child full time (24/7) due to serious family hardship, without state custody involvement. Non-relative caregivers may also qualify for certain support services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cash assistance for the child, medical coverage, food assistance, energy assistance, and childcare costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Maryland resident. Program is available statewide through local Departments of Social Services.
requirements_list: Must be an informal kinship caregiver related by blood or marriage within five degrees of consanguinity to the child
Child must be in your physical care full time (24 hours a day, 7 days a week)
Non-relative caregivers may be eligible for certain support services
For Temporary Cash Assistance, must apply for child support
SNAP benefit is income-dependent
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at marylandbenefits.gov, in person at your local Department of Social Services, by phone at 1-833-373-5867, or request a mailed application from your local DSS. For Child Care Scholarship, apply separately through the Maryland State Department of Education portal. For healthcare and education affidavits, contact your local health department, school, or DSS.

structured_extraction.program_description: Job Network is an employment and training program run by the Community College of Baltimore County (CCBC) that helps noncustodial parents who owe child support find jobs. It links employers with unemployed or underemployed noncustodial parents in Baltimore County, providing career counseling, employment support services, and unsubsidized job placement. The program is referred through the Baltimore County Office of Child Support, and part-time case managers and Benefit Eligibility Specialists help connect participants with courts, the Department of Social Services, and American Job Centers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: CCBC provides career counseling, employment support services, and unsubsidized job placement to eligible noncustodial parents. Job matching and networking services connect employers with unemployed or underemployed noncustodial parents. Part-time case managers and Benefit Eligibility Specialists help connect participants with courts, the Department of Social Services, and American Job Centers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Unemployed or underemployed noncustodial parents who owe child support, can commit to working upon program completion, and have a Baltimore County child support case.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Job training, employment support, placement services, and job matching to help noncustodial parents find and maintain employment and pay child support.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must have a Baltimore County child support case. Career and employment support services are available to noncustodial parties statewide through the Baltimore County program.
requirements_list: Must be a noncustodial party with a Baltimore County child support case
Must be unemployed or underemployed
Must be able to commit to working upon program completion
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The Baltimore County Office of Child Support refers eligible noncustodial parties to Job Network at CCBC. Contact jobnetworkmd@ccbcmd.edu for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Commission for Women Internship Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Commission for Women offers paid internships to undergraduate and graduate students to support the commission's work advancing social, political, and economic opportunities for women in Maryland. Interns work with staff and volunteer Commissioners on policy research, communications, legislative monitoring, event coordination, newsletter development, social media management, outreach, and administrative projects related to advancing opportunities for women in Maryland. Internships are available in fall, spring, and summer terms on a rolling admissions basis in a hybrid format (remote and in-office at the Commission for Women office in Rockville, MD).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Paid hybrid internship at $16.85 per hour for approximately 20 hours per week. Interns work remotely and at the Commission for Women office in Rockville, MD. Internships are available during fall, spring, and summer terms on a rolling admissions basis. Interns receive hourly wages for their work on policy research, communications, legislative monitoring, event coordination, newsletter content development, social media management, and outreach activities related to women's issues in Maryland.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Undergraduate and graduate students with a demonstrated interest in women's issues, social justice, and civic engagement.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Interns receive hourly pay ($16.85/hr) as wages for internship activities including policy research, communications, legislative monitoring, event coordination, outreach activities, newsletter content development, and social media management related to women's issues in Maryland.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Hybrid program based at the Commission for Women office in Rockville, MD; open to eligible students statewide.
requirements_list: Must be enrolled as an undergraduate or graduate student
Demonstrated interest in women's issues, social justice, and civic engagement
Strong writing and research skills
Comfort with social media
Experience with community or student organizations
Availability of at least 20 hours per week
Submit a résumé and cover letter addressing topics of interest within the commission
Provide dates and hours of availability
Provide a list of goals to achieve during the internship
Submit a writing sample of no more than 2-3 paragraphs
Participate in an in-person interview
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Email a résumé, cover letter, dates and hours of availability, a list of internship goals, and a writing sample (2–3 paragraphs) to Ariana Kelly at Ariana.Kelly@Maryland.Gov. Qualified applicants will be invited to participate in an in-person interview. Admission is on a rolling basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: The State of Maryland offers an Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) for working people with low to moderate income. If you qualify for the federal Earned Income Tax Credit and claim it on your federal return, you may be entitled to a Maryland EITC on your state return. The credit matches 50% of the federal EITC for filers claiming dependents, and 100% of the federal EITC for single filers without dependents. ITIN filers may also be eligible. The credit reduces or eliminates the amount of state and local income tax owed and may result in a refund for eligible workers. Free tax preparation and filing services are also available through IRS-certified volunteers (VITA program) for individuals who earned less than $67,000 in 2024, including e-filing, direct deposit refunds, and free tax software via cashmd.org and the Direct File tool.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A Maryland state income tax credit equal to 50% of the federal Earned Income Tax Credit for filers claiming dependents, or 100% of the federal EITC for single filers without dependents. ITIN filers may be eligible. The credit reduces or eliminates state and local income tax liability and may result in a refund for eligible low- and moderate-income workers. Additionally, free tax preparation services are available through IRS-certified volunteers who e-file taxes and deposit refunds directly to bank accounts (up to three separate accounts). Free tax software is available at cashmd.org, and a Direct File tool supports streamlined federal and state filing with no hidden fees.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Working individuals and families with low to moderate income who qualify for the federal EITC and file a Maryland state income tax return, including ITIN filers. Free tax preparation services available to individuals who earned less than $67,000 in 2024.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduces or eliminates state and local income tax liability; may result in a refund for eligible workers. Free tax preparation and filing assistance, including direct deposit of refunds and access to free tax software.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to residents who qualify for the federal EITC and file a Maryland state income tax return. Free tax preparation sites available across Maryland including Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore County, Baltimore City, Calvert, Carroll, Charles, Dorchester, Frederick, Garrett, Harford, Howard, Montgomery, Prince George's, Somerset, St. Mary's, and Wicomico counties.
requirements_list: Must qualify for the federal Earned Income Tax Credit
Must claim the federal EITC on your federal tax return
Must file a Maryland state income tax return
ITIN filers are eligible
Must be a limited-income worker
Income less than $67,000 in 2024 to qualify for free tax preparation services
Social Security card or ITIN proof for each family member and photo ID for each taxpayer
W-2 and/or 1099 forms for all 2024 jobs
Form 1099-G (if applicable)
Child care provider letter including address, tax ID, child name, and amount paid (if applicable)
Banking account information (routing and account numbers) for direct deposit
Previous year tax return copy
Form 1095-A (health insurance form, if received)
All adults on return must appear in person
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Claim the Maryland EITC on your Maryland state income tax return after claiming the federal EITC on your federal return. Free tax preparation assistance is available through the VITA program at locations across Maryland for those earning $67,000 or less. Visit cashmd.org or call 800-492-0618 for free tax preparation services. Free tax software and the Direct File tool for federal and state filing are also available at cashmd.org. For additional information, contact the IRS at 1-800-829-1040 or the Maryland Taxpayer Service at 1-800-638-2937.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Emergency Food Program (MEFP) provides annual grants to non-profit feeding organizations and local government-run programs so they can purchase food and distribute groceries and meals at no charge to families and individuals in emergency need. Eligible organizations include soup kitchens, food banks, food pantries, shelters, residential treatment programs, and after-school programs. Funds are allocated across all 24 Maryland jurisdictions based on population size, unemployment rates, poverty levels, and SNAP benefit recipients. Currently, 104 programs statewide receive MEFP funding.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual grants are awarded to eligible non-profit feeding organizations and local government-run programs to purchase food for distribution. Total FY26 allocation is $1,241,661. Maximum grant award is $50,000; minimum grant award is $2,000. First-time grantees are capped at $2,000. Funds are distributed to all 24 Maryland jurisdictions based on poverty, unemployment, and SNAP benefit recipients. Currently, 104 programs statewide receive MEFP funding.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Tax-exempt non-profit feeding organizations (IRS 501(c)(3)) and local government-run programs such as soup kitchens, food banks, food pantries, shelters, residential treatment programs, and after-school programs that distribute food at no charge to individuals and families in emergency need across Maryland. Served populations include disabled individuals, unemployed persons, veterans, homeless individuals, seniors (60+), adults (18+), and children (0-17).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and distribution of food at no charge to provide groceries and meals to people in emergency need; food preparation and serving of meals; funding for food pantry operations, meal delivery, and weekend backpack programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Funds are allocated to all 24 jurisdictions in Maryland.

Must be an Emergency Food Provider for at least three years

Designated person to submit reports
