structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations apply through the MEFP application process. Eligible feeding organizations receive grants based on available funding and need indicators. The FY 2026 application cycle closed at 5:00 PM on May 9, 2025. Refer to the MEFP FY26 Grant Guidelines for detailed application instructions. Site visits are conducted to review food storage areas and program records; staff reviews financial statements, audit reports, and purchase receipts. Quarterly reporting is required via designated online link, including activity log and receipt documentation. For questions, contact Judith Potter-Brown at judith.potterbrown1@maryland.gov or call 1-800-332-6347.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Energy Assistance Program (MEAP) / Office of Home Energy Programs (OHEP) / Electric Universal Service Program (EUSP)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Office of Home Energy Programs (OHEP), administered by the Maryland Department of Human Services, provides grants and utility bill assistance to low-income Maryland households to help pay their heating fuel, electric, and cooling utility bills, and to prevent utility service shut-offs. The program covers costs for electricity, natural gas, heating oil, propane, wood, wood pellets, and kerosene. Eligible households can receive financial assistance toward their energy costs and, if they have large past-due balances, may also qualify for Arrearage Retirement Assistance (ARA) to pay off overdue electric bills (up to $2,000) and Gas Arrearage Retirement Assistance (GARA) to pay off overdue gas bills (up to $1,000). Arrearage assistance can only be received once every five years unless the household includes a member aged 60+, under age 2, or medically fragile. The Low-Income Water Assistance Program (LIHWAP) helps eligible households with past-due water and wastewater utility bills. MEAP provides a one-time grant each heating season paid directly to the applicant's heating supplier; grant amounts depend on fuel type, household income, and area of the state. For the Electric Universal Service Program (EUSP), the grant is also based on prior 12-month kilowatt usage and average kilowatt-hour cost. The Utility Service Protection Program (USPP) protects low-income families from utility shut-offs by allowing eligible households to enter a year-round even monthly payment plan, and a 55-day hold on utility termination can be placed while an application is being processed. MEAP (administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development) also helps limited income households achieve more comfortable homes through the repair or replacement of heating, cooling, and water heating systems. The program is especially beneficial for elderly, disabled, and low-income individuals, including those receiving veterans or Social Security disability benefits. Payments are made directly to fuel suppliers and utility companies on behalf of eligible customers. The program is income-based — no turn-off notice is required to apply. Households must reapply each fiscal year (July–June). Grants received January 1, 2020–December 31, 2021 do not count toward the five-year arrearage limit. Grant amounts vary by income level and fuel type and do not need to be repaid. Receiving energy assistance does not reduce other public assistance benefits such as TCA, Food Stamps, or Social Security. Local program offices in every county connect residents with specialists who guide them through the application process and answer questions. In Washington County, the program is administered locally by the Washington County Community Action Council (WCCAC). A Critical Medical Needs Program is also processed through OHEP. During crisis season (November 1 – March 31), applicants may self-declare income using the Crisis Season Declaration Form if complete documentation is unavailable, with additional documentation due within 15 days.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants and subsidies are provided directly to utility and heating fuel providers on behalf of eligible households to help pay home heating and electric utility bills, as well as to prevent utility shut-offs for electric, gas, and water services. The benefit covers electricity, natural gas, heating oil, propane, wood, wood pellets, and kerosene. MEAP provides a one-time grant per heating season paid directly to the heating supplier; the grant amount depends on the type of fuel used, household income, and the area of the state where the applicant lives. For the Electric Universal Service Program (EUSP), the grant amount is also based on prior 12-month kilowatt usage and average kilowatt-hour cost. If heat is included in rent, the landlord may receive the grant and deduct it from the rent owed; landlord must reduce tenant's rent/utility charge by the full benefit amount received and cannot apply benefits toward security deposits or dwelling damage costs. The Low-Income Water Assistance Program (LIHWAP) helps with past-due water and wastewater utility bills (up to $2,000 for reconnection of water/wastewater services and reduction of arrear balances). Grant amounts vary based on income level and fuel type and do not need to be repaid. MEAP (DHCD) also covers repair or replacement of heating, cooling, and water heating systems at no cost to eligible households. For Arrearage Retirement Assistance (ARA), eligible customers may receive up to $2,000 toward a past-due electric bill; for Gas Arrearage Retirement Assistance (GARA), eligible customers may receive up to $1,000 toward a past-due natural gas bill. Customers must have a past-due balance of $300 or more to qualify for arrearage assistance, and may only receive an arrearage grant once every five years (with exceptions: grants received January 1, 2020–December 31, 2021 do not count toward the five-year limit, and households with a member aged 60+, under age 2, or medically fragile are also excepted). Income limits for FY26 range from $2,608/month for a household of 1 to $10,859/month for a household of 10; households at or below 200% of the federal poverty level or receiving SNAP or TCA are eligible. The Utility Service Protection Program (USPP) allows eligible households to enter a year-round even monthly payment plan with their utility company. A 55-day hold on utility termination can be placed while an application is being processed. Households must reapply each fiscal year (July–June) and may only receive benefits once per year. Receiving energy assistance does not reduce other public assistance benefits such as TCA, Food Stamps, or Social Security. Weatherization and energy efficiency improvements are also available through the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (call 1-855-583-8976 for information).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Year-round program; applications accepted July through May each year; must reapply each fiscal year (July–June); effective July 1, 2025 – June 30, 2026; crisis season: November 1 – March 31
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income Maryland residents including renters, homeowners, public housing residents, sub-metered home residents, and roomers/boarders who are responsible for paying energy and heating costs. Households at or below 200% of the federal poverty level, or receiving SNAP or Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA), are eligible, as are those receiving veterans or Social Security disability benefits. The program assists with home heating bills, electric utility bills, arrearage retirement, shut-off prevention, past-due water/wastewater bills (LIHWAP), and repair or replacement of heating, cooling, and water heating systems. Available statewide, including Washington County, Frederick County/City of Frederick, and Montgomery County residents. Also available to applicants with personal safety concerns (domestic violence survivors) and those who cannot apply in person (proxy application available). Households experiencing energy crisis during crisis season (November 1 – March 31) may self-declare income. Utility customers with serious illness or life support equipment needs may obtain physician certification for shut-off protection.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment toward home heating fuel bills (electricity, natural gas, heating oil, propane, wood, wood pellets, and kerosene), electric utility bills, water and wastewater utility bills (LIHWAP), shut-off prevention, and past-due utility balances (arrearage retirement via ARA and GARA); repair or replacement of heating, cooling, and water heating systems (MEAP via DHCD); energy crisis assistance and making heating and cooling expenses more affordable; prevention of energy service loss and restoration of service. Heating costs paid directly to the heating supplier. Landlord-received grants must be applied to reduce tenant's rent or utility charge for heating/electricity costs only and cannot be used for security deposits or dwelling damage costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland through local Home Energy Program offices in each county and Baltimore City, including through county departments of social services. Grant amount varies by area within Maryland. In Washington County, applications are handled by the Washington County Community Action Council (WCCAC) at 117 Summit Avenue, Hagerstown, MD 21740; apply online at https://www.wccac.org/our-services/energy-assistance or call (301) 797-4161 or email WashingtonCountyOHEP@wccac.org. In Frederick County/City of Frederick, applications may be mailed to PO Box 3929 Frederick, MD 21705, emailed to ohep@cityoffrederickmd.gov, or dropped off at 420 East Patrick Street. In St. Mary's County, applications may be submitted at any senior activity center through the Tri-County Community Action Committee. In Montgomery County, applications can be submitted online at MyDHR, by phone appointment at 240-777-4450, by email to OHEP@montgomerycountymd.gov, by mail to 1301 Piccard Drive, Suite 4200, Rockville MD 20852, or dropped off at the document drop box at 1301 Piccard Drive. Applicants apply through their local Home Energy Program office.
requirements_list: Must be a low-income, limited income, elderly, or disabled household (homeowner, renter, public housing resident, sub-metered home resident, or boarder)

Household income must be at or below 200% of the federal poverty level, based on gross income of all household members over 18 in the prior 30 days; FY26 monthly income limits range from $2,608/month for 1 person, $3,525 for 2, $4,441 for 3, up to $10,859 for 10
Households receiving SNAP or TCA in Maryland are categorically eligible and do not need to apply separately
Must be a Maryland resident
Does not require a turn-off notice to apply
Completed and signed application listing everyone in the household
Valid government-issued photo identification for applicant
Proof of primary residency (lease or mortgage statement)
Social Security cards or federal documents with name and Social Security number for all household members including children
Proof of household gross income for the last 30 days (pay stubs, Social Security award letters, pension statements, unemployment documentation, etc.)
Copy of most recent utility bill (and termination notice if applicable)
Copy of most recent heating fuel bill or receipt if applicable
Grant amount is based on fuel type, household income, and location within the state
For Arrearage Retirement Assistance (ARA/GARA): past-due balance of $300 or more required

Arrearage grant may only be received once every five years (exceptions apply: households with a member aged 60+, under age 2, or medically fragile; grants received January 1, 2020–December 31, 2021 do not count toward the five-year limit)
Households must reapply each fiscal year (July–June) and may only receive benefits once per year
Full-time students' income is not counted if full-time status is documented

Self-employed applicants must complete income verification form (DHS-FIA-808) and attach documentation of income from last 30 days; if taxes filed, IRS Schedule SE required; if taxes not filed, must submit weekly/monthly/quarterly books, statements, ledgers, or bank records
Household members 18+ with zero income must complete a Declaration of Zero Income form (DHS-FIA-806)
Elderly or disabled individuals and/or those receiving veterans or Social Security disability benefits may also qualify
Receiving energy assistance does not reduce other public assistance benefits such as TCA, Food Stamps, or Social Security
Must submit a completed application to the local OHEP office

Applicants with personal safety concerns (e.g., domestic violence survivors) who cannot provide a delivery address must submit DHS FIA 804 form with third-party verification of safety concerns; verification may be provided by domestic violence service providers, legal representatives, medical/psychological/social service providers, law enforcement professionals, county children and youth representatives, or an acquaintance/friend/relative/neighbor
Applicants who cannot apply in person may designate a proxy (age 18+) using DHS-FIA-811 Proxy Authorization Form; proxy form must be witnessed and signed (does not need to be notarized)

If applying with zero household income, must document basic needs (shelter, food, utilities) and may need a Resource Provider Statement (DHS-FIA-813) if receiving non-government assistance; may be required to have applied for Unemployment Insurance or public assistance
TTY users may call 1-800-735-2258

For LIHWAP: must be responsible for payment of water and/or wastewater bill from a public water system; must live at the property receiving assistance; gross household income cannot exceed 60% of state median income (thresholds range from $3,121/month for 1 person to $8,283/month for 8 people); only one water/wastewater account per service address is eligible

For landlord/sub-metered utility situations: heating or electricity costs must be included in tenant rent or billed through a sub-metering company; landlord must complete DHS-FIA-809 Landlord Agreement and DHS-FIA-812 Rent/Living Arrangements Form

For utility shut-off protection due to serious illness or life support equipment needs: must submit Form PSC-801 (Physician Certification) completed by a licensed physician, certified nurse practitioner, or physician assistant; must enter into payment agreement with utility within 30 days of certification

During crisis season (November 1 – March 31), applicants may self-declare income using the Crisis Season Declaration Form (DHS-FIA-805) if complete documentation is unavailable; additional documentation must be provided within 15 days or benefits must be repaid
Verification of alimony or child support payments required if applicable (DHS-FIA-803 form); payor must complete form and payee must sign authorization
Navigators processing Critical Medical Needs Program applications must sign a confidentiality certification and agree not to disclose Personally Identifiable Information without written consent
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through one of the following methods: (1) Online — apply at MarylandBenefits.gov, myohepstatus.mymdthink.maryland.gov, or mydhrbenefits.dhr.state.md.us; (2) Drop box — download and print the application form, complete it with required documents, and drop at local office drop box (Baltimore City residents use nearest CAP Center); (3) Mail — mail completed application and documents to your local OHEP office; (4) Phone — call 1-800-332-6347 (Spanish available; TTY: 1-800-735-2258) to apply by phone or request a paper application, then mail or email documents; (5) In person — visit a local office. Submit all required documents with the application to avoid delays. Applications are reviewed within 14 days of receiving a complete packet; final determination is made within 45 days. Categorically eligible households (SNAP/TCA recipients) are automatically issued benefits after redetermination. For Washington County: apply online at https://www.wccac.org/our-services/energy-assistance or schedule an appointment at Washington County Community Action Council, 117 Summit Avenue, Hagerstown, MD 21740; call (301) 797-4161 or email WashingtonCountyOHEP@wccac.org. For Frederick County/City of Frederick: apply online at myohepstatus.mymdthink.maryland.gov, or download a paper application from dhs.maryland.gov/office-of-home-energy-programs or cityoffrederickmd.gov/187/Programs-Information (available in English and Spanish). Paper applications can be mailed to PO Box 3929 Frederick, MD 21705, emailed to ohep@cityoffrederickmd.gov, or dropped off in the lobby at 420 East Patrick Street; call 301-600-2410 for local assistance. For Prince George's County: apply by email to pgcdss.energy@maryland.gov with completed application and supporting documents, by fax to 301-909-6331, by mail to Prince George's County Department of Social Services, 805 Brightseat Road, Landover, MD 20785, or in person at 425 Brightseat Road, Landover, MD 20785. For Montgomery County: apply online at MyDHR (mydhrbenefits.dhr.state.md.us), call 240-777-4450 to request a phone appointment, or download and complete a paper application (English or Spanish). Submit completed applications by email to OHEP@montgomerycountymd.gov, by mail to 1301 Piccard Drive, Suite 4200, Rockville MD 20852, or drop off at the document drop box at 1301 Piccard Drive. For St. Mary's County: apply at any senior activity center through the Tri-County Community Action Committee between July and May each year. For Calvert County, the local office can be reached at (301) 274-4474, Extension 1. For MEAP (DHCD): Submit an interest form or application through DHCD; after eligibility is confirmed, a contractor is assigned to conduct an in-home energy assessment and complete recommended work at no cost. For utility shut-off protection (serious illness/life support): submit Form PSC-801 to the utility company. Applicants unable to apply in person may designate a proxy using DHS-FIA-811. You must reapply each fiscal year.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides free legal representation in Maryland Circuit Courts to children involved in Child in Need of Assistance (CINA) and Termination of Parental Rights (TPR) cases, and to indigent adults in Adult Guardianship cases, when the local department of social services or the Office of Aging is a party to the case. In FY 2023, over 6,279 clients received legal representation through this program. Services are delivered by attorneys with experience in child welfare, child disability, family law, and related fields, selected through a Request for Proposals (RFP) process. The program monitors attorney-client contact ratios, hours per case, and service quality through audits and training sessions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free legal representation in Maryland Circuit Courts provided through contracted attorneys selected via a Request for Proposals (RFP) process. Attorneys must have extensive experience in child welfare, child disability, family law, or related fields. In FY 2023, over 6,279 clients received legal representation through this program. The program monitors attorney-client contact ratios, hours per case, and service quality through audits and training sessions.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Children involved in CINA and TPR cases, and indigent adults in Adult Guardianship cases, where the local department of social services or the Office of Aging is a party to the proceedings.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Legal representation in Circuit Court proceedings for eligible children and adults.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland through local departments of social services.
requirements_list: Must be a child involved in a CINA or TPR case, or an indigent adult in an Adult Guardianship case
Local department of social services or the Office of Aging must be a party to the case
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Legal representation is arranged through contracted attorneys selected via a Request for Proposals (RFP) process. Eligible clients are referred through the courts and local departments of social services. Contact DHS or your local department of social services for referral.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Legal Services Program – Adult Representation
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Legal Services Program (MLSP) provides legal representation to low-income (indigent) alleged vulnerable adults involved in Adult Protective Services (APS) and Adult Public Guardianship Review Board (APGRB) proceedings across Maryland. State-contracted attorneys represent these adults for the full duration of their need.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free legal representation is provided to indigent alleged vulnerable adults in APS and Adult Public Guardianship proceedings. Attorneys are compensated through state contracts on a fee-based structure. Representation continues for the duration of the client's need.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Indigent alleged vulnerable adults involved in Adult Protective Services or Adult Public Guardianship Review Board proceedings in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Legal representation in Adult Protective Services and Adult Public Guardianship Review Board proceedings.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Multiple law firms serve different counties across the state.
requirements_list: Must be an alleged vulnerable adult involved in APS or APGRB proceedings
Must be indigent (unable to afford legal representation)
Local Department of Social Services or Office on Aging must be a party to the case
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact MLSP by email at askmlsp@maryland.gov or by phone at (410) 767-7858. Include your name, telephone number, and county or city if possible.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Legal Services Program – Child in Need of Assistance (CINA) Legal Representation
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Legal Services Program (MLSP) oversees contracts for legal representation of children involved in Child in Need of Assistance (CINA), Termination of Parental Rights (TPR), Voluntary Placement, Guardianship, and related Adoption proceedings in Maryland. The program ensures that abused and neglected children in the foster care system receive quality legal representation for the duration of their time in need, using a fee-based payment structure through state contracts.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program awards state contracts to law firms and legal service providers to compensate attorneys for legal representation of children in CINA, TPR, Voluntary Placement, Guardianship, and related Adoption proceedings. Contracts are secured through a competitive and confidential procurement process. Attorneys are compensated on a fee basis for services rendered.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Law firms and attorneys who provide legal representation to children in the Maryland child welfare system (CINA, TPR, Guardianship, and related Adoption proceedings).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Compensation for attorneys providing legal representation to children involved in Maryland child welfare proceedings.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide – providers serve specific jurisdictions across all Maryland counties and Baltimore City as assigned under contract.
requirements_list: Must provide legal representation to children in CINA, TPR, Voluntary Placement, Guardianship, or related Adoption proceedings
Must participate in a competitive and confidential procurement process
Must meet quality standards for legal representation set by MLSP
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Legal services contracts are secured through a highly competitive and confidential procurement process administered by MLSP. Interested firms must participate in the procurement process to be considered for a contract.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland SUN Bucks is a summer grocery benefit program that provides $120 per eligible school-aged child ($40 per month for June, July, and August) to help families buy food during summer break when school meals are not available. The program covers all 24 Maryland jurisdictions and aims to serve up to 540,000 children, putting $60 million directly into families' hands. Benefits are loaded onto an EBT card (either an existing SNAP Independence Card or a new white Maryland SUN Bucks card mailed to the household) and can be used at grocery stores, some farmers' markets, and authorized online retailers that accept EBT. Benefits expire 122 days after the date they are issued.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible families receive $40 per eligible school-aged child per month for June, July, and August (a total of $120 per child per summer). Benefits are loaded onto the household's existing SNAP Independence Card or a new white Maryland SUN Bucks card is mailed if the household has never had an EBT card. Benefits can be used to purchase eligible food items including fruits, vegetables, meats, protein sources, whole grains, dairy, and other food products at grocery stores, some farmers' markets, and authorized online retailers that accept EBT. Benefits expire 122 days after the date they are issued and cannot be used for alcohol, tobacco, non-food items, or hot/prepared food.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted year-round; eligibility for summer benefits determined before August 31, 2025
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with school-aged children (ages 5–18) enrolled in a Maryland school that participates in the National School Lunch Program (NSLP) / Free and Reduced-Price School Meals (FARMS) who qualify for free or reduced-price meals, or whose household receives SNAP, Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA), or Medicaid, or who are in foster care, homeless, migrant, or runaway. All children who meet income eligibility requirements are eligible regardless of immigration status.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchasing eligible food items including fruits, vegetables, meats, protein sources, whole grains, dairy, and other food products at grocery stores, farmers' markets, and authorized online retailers that accept EBT. Cannot be used for alcohol, tobacco, non-food items, or hot/prepared food.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in all 24 Maryland local jurisdictions. Child must be enrolled in a Maryland school participating in the National School Lunch Program (NSLP) / Free and Reduced-Price School Meals (FARMS) program. Virtual schools and homeschools do not qualify.
requirements_list: Child must be enrolled in a Maryland school that participates in the National School Lunch Program (NSLP) / Free and Reduced-Price School Meals (FARMS) program
Child must be age 5–18

Child must meet one of the following: applied for and received free or reduced-price meals (FARMS or School Breakfast Program) during the current school year; household receives SNAP, TCA, or Medicaid; child is in foster care; child is homeless, migrant, or runaway; or child applies and is determined eligible for FARMS before August 31
Household must meet income guidelines for the NSLP (if not automatically enrolled)
All children who meet income eligibility requirements are eligible regardless of immigration status
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Most eligible children are automatically enrolled — no application needed if the child received free or reduced-price meals last school year, is in a SNAP/TCA/Medicaid household, or is in foster care. Families not automatically enrolled (e.g., children at Community Eligibility Provision schools not receiving SNAP/TCA/Medicaid) must apply online at marylandbenefits.gov, in person at a local Department of Social Services office, by calling 1-800-332-6347, or by submitting a paper application (available in English and Spanish). Applications are accepted year-round. Once enrolled, benefits are issued in the last week of June, July, and August and loaded to the household's existing SNAP Independence Card or a new white SUN Bucks card mailed to the household. Recipients of a new Maryland SUN Bucks card must activate it and create a 4-digit PIN by calling 800-997-2222.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program helps Maryland residents living in a nursing home pay for their nursing home care costs if they meet financial, technical, and medical criteria. It also helps pay for doctor, hospital, and other medical services. The program determines initial and ongoing eligibility for nursing home Medicaid and includes a review of financial history (five-year look-back) from the 60 months prior to application. Coverage also extends to long-term care facility services, waiver-based community care, and medical bills incurred in the past 3 months. Administered statewide by the Maryland Department of Human Services, with county-level administration (e.g., Montgomery County DHHS) handling local applications.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Pays for nursing home care costs and other Medicaid-eligible medical services (doctor, hospital, etc.) for eligible low-income residents. Coverage includes long-term care facility services, waiver-based community care, and medical bills incurred in the past 3 months. The applicant may be required to pay a portion of their income to the nursing home as determined by the program. Eligibility includes a five-year (60-month) look-back at financial resources for initial applications; redeterminations require reporting asset transfers within the past 12 months. Income and asset limits vary by program category based on Federal Poverty Level percentages and family size. Specific dollar amounts vary based on individual circumstances.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income Maryland residents living in a nursing home or requiring long-term care services (nursing facility, state institution, or community-based care) who meet financial, technical, and medical eligibility criteria. Includes U.S. citizens and lawfully admitted immigrants, aged/blind/disabled individuals, and their authorized representatives. Montgomery County residents may call 240-777-1003 for eligibility questions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Nursing home care costs, long-term care facility services, waiver-based community care, medical bills incurred in the past 3 months, and other Medicaid-eligible medical services such as doctor and hospital visits.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. The Office of Long Term Care at 746 Frederick Road, Catonsville, MD 21228 covers applications from Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Anne Arundel County, and Prince George's County. Montgomery County residents are served by Montgomery County DHHS at 401 Hungerford Drive, 4th Floor, Rockville, MD 20850. Applications may also be submitted to the Local Department of Social Services or Bureau of Long-Term Care Eligibility.
requirements_list: Must be a U.S. citizen or lawfully admitted immigrant with eligible immigration status
Must be a Maryland resident
Must be a low-income individual requiring nursing home or long-term care level of care
Must meet disability criteria if under age 65
Must meet income and asset eligibility requirements (income and asset limits vary by program category and family size based on Federal Poverty Level)
Financial history over the past 60 months (five-year look-back) will be reviewed for initial applications; redeterminations require reporting asset transfers within the past 12 months

Must provide documentation of citizenship and personal identification, Social Security number, health insurance/Medicare information, income, and assets (including bank statements, tax returns, and asset statements)
Must provide complete and truthful disclosure of all financial information, income, assets, and transfers
Must report changes within 10 days
If an annuity is held, the Department must be named as primary remainder beneficiary
Must comply with program laws and regulations; non-compliance may result in benefit denial, repayment requirement, or fraud investigation
Applicant must sign application form; witness signature required if applicant signs with X; spouse and/or authorized representative signature required if applicable
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at https://marylandbenefits.gov (benefits.maryland.gov), or submit completed application form (DHS/FIA 9709) with required supporting documentation to your local department of social services or the Bureau of Long-Term Care Eligibility. Applicants should not delay submission if documents are incomplete — additional time will be provided to submit missing documents. Applications for Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Anne Arundel County, and Prince George's County are handled by the Office of Long Term Care, 746 Frederick Road, Catonsville, MD 21228. Montgomery County residents may call 240-777-1003 for eligibility questions, request an application packet by mail, or pick up the packet at 401 Hungerford Drive, 4th Floor, Rockville, MD 20850, and submit by mail, in person, or fax (240-777-1330). Existing recipients must complete a redetermination application (DHS/FIA 9709R) with current income and asset verification. Recipients have the right to appeal within 90 days of notice by calling 1-800-332-6347.
