structured_extraction.program_description: Re-Engaging Individuals through Successful Employment (RISE) helps noncustodial parents who owe child support get back on their feet economically. The program assists unemployed and underemployed noncustodial parties in the Mid-Shore Region of Maryland find and keep jobs. It partners with local businesses and temporary employment agencies to connect participants with employers and provides job training, certification, and support services at no cost, helping participants make regular child support payments.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free employment training and placement services, including hard skills training in in-demand industries (healthcare, construction, welding, hospitality, warehousing, biotechnology, and more), soft skills training, job readiness coaching, industry-recognized certifications, work experience, transportation assistance, referrals to community services, help resolving barriers to employment (e.g. criminal record, driver's license suspension), access to work clothing and tools, and support from a personal career navigator.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Damien Ransome (Cecil, Kent, Queen Anne's); Louis Nichols (Caroline, Dorchester, Talbot); Kameka Sampson / Jada Johnson (Wicomico, Worcester, Somerset)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Noncustodial parents who have a Mid-Shore child support case, are unemployed or underemployed, and can commit to working upon program completion.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Employment training, certification, job placement, and support services to help participants obtain and retain employment and make regular child support payments.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in the Mid-Shore Region of Maryland: Cecil, Kent, Queen Anne's, Caroline, Dorchester, Talbot, Wicomico, Worcester, and Somerset counties.
requirements_list: Must have a Mid-Shore child support case
Must be unemployed or underemployed
Must be able to commit to working upon program completion
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the program coordinator for your county to enroll. At the enrollment session, inform the intake coordinator if you are interested in a specific training program. For general assistance, call the DHS help-line at 800-332-6347.

structured_extraction.program_name: Mobile Point of Sale Equipment Program (MPOSEP)
structured_extraction.program_description: MPOSEP provides grants to farmers markets and individual farmers or vendors to buy mobile point-of-sale (mPOS) equipment used to process Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) / SNAP transactions at farmers markets. The program aims to increase SNAP redemption at farmers markets and provide low-income consumers access to fresh, locally produced food.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $600 per market or vendor for the purchase of one SNAP-compatible mobile point-of-sale (mPOS) device or system that allows farmers markets and vendors to accept SNAP/EBT payments.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Open application until all grant funds have been exhausted
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers markets and individual farmers or vendors (including farmer vendors, value-added vendors, and prepared food vendors) who participate in Maryland farmers markets and want to accept SNAP/EBT payments.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of one SNAP-compatible mobile point-of-sale (mPOS) device, system, or application to process EBT/SNAP transactions (maximum $600 per award). Cannot be used for credit/debit card readers that do not accept SNAP.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to farmers markets and vendors operating in Maryland farmers markets listed in the annual Maryland Farmers Market Directory. Vendor must operate at farmers market(s) within Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a farmers market or a dedicated vendor in at least one Maryland farmers market that meets the state definition and can accept SNAP.
Must complete the USDA eAuthentication Account Registration.
Must apply for and become authorized as a SNAP-authorized retailer (receive a USDA FNS number).
Must provide proof of farmers market vendor membership and authorized FNS number.
Vendor applicants must indicate their vendor category (Farmer Vendor, Value Added Vendor, or Prepared Food Vendor) and provide applicable permits or certifications.
Must have a valid Tax ID (EIN) number.
Must provide copies of farmers market vendor agreement or letter from market manager.
Must choose an mPOS device/application service.
Must submit the MPOSEP grant application with all required documentation.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete USDA eAuthentication registration, obtain SNAP retailer authorization (FNS number), gather proof of farmers market participation and USDA authorization letter, provide valid Tax ID (EIN), select an mPOS device/app service, then submit the MPOSEP grant application with all required documentation to the Bureau of Special Grants. Application is open on a rolling basis until all grant funds are exhausted.

structured_extraction.program_description: The NETWorks Program helps noncustodial parents who owe child support overcome barriers to employment so they can better support themselves and their families. It provides a network of resources including one-time financial support for items like identification, work boots, glasses, uniforms, interview clothes, and transportation to job interviews. Case managers also help participants address issues such as criminal records. The program supplements the Tri Pep Program, which serves Somerset, Wicomico, and Worcester counties.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time financial support to cover costs such as identification documents, work boots, glasses, uniforms, interview attire, and transportation to and from job interviews. Training options include GED and Driver Improvement courses, regional flagger certifications, work experience, and CDL (Commercial Driver's License) courses. Case managers may also assist with expunging criminal records. The program provides an overall employment and support resource network to help unemployed or underemployed noncustodial parents find and keep jobs and pay child support.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Noncustodial parents who owe child support and are unemployed or underemployed, living in Somerset, Wicomico, or Worcester counties in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Identification documents, work boots, glasses, uniforms, interview attire, transportation costs, GED courses, Driver Improvement courses, flagger certifications, CDL training, work experience, and criminal record expungement assistance; employment and resource support to help noncustodial parents find and keep jobs and pay child support
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to noncustodial parties served by the Somerset County, Wicomico County, or Worcester County Office of Child Support
requirements_list: Must be a noncustodial party owing child support
Must agree to the stipulations set by program administrators
Must live in Somerset, Wicomico, or Worcester County
Must have a direct connection to IVA (public assistance) services or a court-ordered referral for employment services through the Tri Pep Program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are reviewed on the merits and financial aid dependencies. Contact Diana Columna at 410-713-3147 or diana.columna@maryland.gov, or Torrez Wise at 410-219-5712 or torrez.wise@maryland.gov for more information. You can also call DHS's helpline at 1-800-332-6347.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Office of Community Grants (OCG), under the Maryland Department of Human Services Family Investment Administration, contracts with emergency food providers throughout the state to distribute funds and commodities to meet the needs of hungry Marylanders. It supports over 1,100 local programs including food banks, food pantries, soup kitchens, and shelters.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides programmatic and fiscal funding guidelines, policy oversight, contract compliance monitoring, and technical assistance to emergency food provider programs in all 24 Maryland jurisdictions.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Emergency food providers including food banks, food pantries, soup kitchens, and shelters throughout Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Distribution of funds and commodities to meet the needs of hungry Marylanders through local emergency food programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in all 24 Maryland jurisdictions.

structured_extraction.program_description: A family-focused employment and support program run by the Caroline County Department of Social Services under the Maryland Department of Human Services. It helps non-custodial parents (mothers and fathers) gain job skills, find and keep employment, improve relationships with co-parents and children, and increase child support payments. The program provides free job readiness training, life skills counseling, and connections to local staffing agencies, enabling both parents to work together to support their children financially.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: No-cost job readiness training, employment development, life skills counseling, job placement and retention assistance, relationship and parenting skill development, and mediation. Program partners include local staffing agencies whose recruiters help participants develop an action plan for employment, enabling noncustodial parents to find and keep jobs and pay child support.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-custodial parents who have a Caroline County child support case, are unemployed or underemployed, and can commit to working upon program completion.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Job readiness training, employment development, life skills counseling, parenting skill development, and job placement and retention support to help noncustodial parents find and keep jobs and pay child support.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must have a Caroline County child support case. Caroline County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Have a Caroline County child support case
Be unemployed or underemployed
Commit to working upon program completion
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Program Coordinator Loge Knight at 410-819-4593 or elouzia.knight@maryland.gov, or call DHS's helpline at 1-800-332-6347 for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Payment Incentive Program encourages noncustodial parents (NCPs) to make consistent child support payments by reducing or eliminating state-owed child support arrears. If an NCP makes full child support payments for 12 consecutive months, their state-owed arrears are reduced by 50%. If they make full payments for 24 consecutive months, the remaining balance owed to the state is eliminated entirely. Credit is given for uninterrupted court-ordered payments made before joining the program, and periods of unemployment due to seasonal work or no-fault job loss are also considered. Note: Arrears owed directly to the family are not reduced.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants who make full child support payments for 12 consecutive months receive a 50% reduction in state-owed arrears. Participants who make full payments for 24 consecutive months have the remaining state-owed arrears eliminated entirely. Credit is given for uninterrupted court-ordered payments made before joining the program. Periods of unemployment due to seasonal work or no-fault job loss are also considered. Eligibility requires gross income below 225% of the Federal Poverty Level (household size considered). Arrears owed directly to the family are not reduced.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Noncustodial parents who have a Maryland court order with arrears owed to the state (because the custodial party received public assistance) and whose gross income is below 225% of the federal poverty level.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction or elimination of state-owed child support arrears.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Applicant must have a Maryland court order.
requirements_list: Applicant must have a Maryland court order with an arrears balance owed to the state because the custodial party received public assistance.
Applicant's gross income must be less than 225% of the federal poverty level (household size is considered).
Applicant must pay child support as ordered for 12 or 24 consecutive months to receive the corresponding reduction.
Applicant must not have been terminated from this program three or more times.
A separate application must be completed for each case.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and print the Payment Incentive Program application from the DHS website, or submit an application online through the program's online portal. Submit completed application and recent pay stubs to the local child support office. A separate application must be completed for each child support case. Contact the Maryland Department of Human Services Child Support Administration for additional details.

structured_extraction.program_description: Project Home, also called the C.A.R.E. (Certified Adult Residential Environment) Program, provides housing to adults who need supervision and assistance with activities of daily living and who are unable to live by themselves. Providers offer care in their own homes to one to four residents who have a disability. It provides an adult foster family model of care that offers a stable, family-like living arrangement in the community as a less costly alternative to nursing homes, psychiatric hospitals, and other institutional settings. Residents receive case management, daily living support, and opportunities to develop independent living skills.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible residents may receive financial assistance through Public Assistance to Adults and Medical Assistance programs for room and board in a certified adult foster home. Care providers are reimbursed based on the resident's needs and level of care system; reimbursements are not considered taxable income. Case management services link residents to appropriate community activities and supports.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults age 18 or older with mental, developmental, or physical disability, or elderly individuals unable to live alone. Also recruits and certifies individuals age 21 or older willing to open their homes as care providers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Room, board, supervision, assistance with daily living activities, recreational and social activities, medication supervision, and transportation to medical appointments. Provider reimbursement is based on the resident's level of care.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland across all 24 counties; administered through local Departments of Social Services.
requirements_list: Residents must be age 18 or older
Residents must have a documented mental, developmental, or physical disability, or be an elderly individual unable to live alone
Residents must be willing and able to live in a family setting
Documentation of disability, income, and functional capability required
Residents who take medication must be able to self-medicate or learn to self-medicate with cuing and coaching
Care providers must be age 21 or older
Care providers must live in the home where care will be provided
Care providers must have willingness to assist an adult
Care providers must be recruited, screened, and certified by local DSS
Care providers must demonstrate other income to meet their own needs
Care providers must participate in training provided by the local Department of Social Services
Care providers must work with the local DSS case manager and resident to develop a treatment plan
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local Department of Social Services office. Care providers are recruited, screened, and certified by the local DSS. Residents apply through the local DSS office.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Public Assistance to Adults (PAA) program supplements Supplemental Security Income (SSI) benefits and pays for the cost of care and a personal needs allowance for eligible adults in Maryland. Specifically, PAA covers the cost of care and a personal needs allowance for individuals living in assisted living facilities licensed by the Maryland Department of Health or in Certified Adult Residential Environmental homes (Project Home). For people residing in Maryland Department of Health Rehabilitative Residences, PAA pays only the personal needs allowance. Recipients are also eligible for Medical Assistance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: PAA covers the cost of care and a personal needs allowance for eligible individuals in licensed assisted living facilities or Certified Adult Residential Environmental homes (Project Home). For residents of Maryland Department of Health Rehabilitative Residences, PAA provides only the personal needs allowance. Recipients also qualify for Medical Assistance. The program also serves as a cash supplement to SSI benefits for eligible adults.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults living in licensed assisted living facilities, Certified Adult Residential Environmental homes (Project Home), or Maryland Department of Health Rehabilitative Residences who receive or are eligible for SSI and need additional financial support, and who meet technical and financial eligibility criteria.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cost of care in licensed assisted living or Project Home facilities, and a personal needs allowance to supplement SSI benefits. For residents of MDH Rehabilitative Residences, funds cover only the personal needs allowance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Must be a Maryland resident.
requirements_list: Must meet technical and financial eligibility criteria
Must apply for Social Security Administration (SSA) benefits as a condition of eligibility
Cost of care must be greater than the applicant's countable income
Assets must not exceed the allowable limit
Assistance unit is always one person
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at MarylandBenefits.gov (https://MarylandBenefits.gov/home/#/) or visit a local DHS office.

structured_extraction.program_description: PA2E is a workforce development program that gives people receiving public assistance the resources and training they need to start and grow a small business. The program runs approximately 6 weeks and consists of 8 courses held 1-2 times per week (approximately 2 hours each), covering topics such as Entrepreneurship 101, Marketing Research, Financial Statements, Business Plan Creation, Credit Restoration, Loan Process, Social Media Marketing, and Business Plan Presentation. Participants also receive ongoing consulting and support through a partnership with the Maryland Small Business Development Center (SBDC), including access to SBDC business consultants and peer group learning. Classes are offered in Spring and Fall semesters, available both virtually and in person through regional SBDC partnerships. The program is delivered statewide in partnership with local Departments of Social Services, including Washington County Department of Social Services and local offices on the Eastern Shore and in Western Maryland. In Howard County, the program is administered locally through Howard County Department of Social Services. In Anne Arundel County, the program is available to DHS customers through a local partnership.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A free approximately 6-week entrepreneurship training program consisting of 8 courses held 1-2 times per week (approximately 2 hours each). Courses cover Entrepreneurship 101, Marketing Research, Financial Statements, Business Plan Creation, Credit Restoration, Loan Process, Social Media Marketing, and Business Plan Presentation. Participants must attend all eight sessions. Participants also receive access to SBDC business consultants, ongoing consulting support, workforce development training credits, and peer group learning. Courses are offered in Spring and Fall semesters, available both virtually and in a classroom setting. In Howard County, contact howco.dss@maryland.gov or 410-872-8700 for local enrollment details.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents currently receiving public assistance from their local Department of Social Services — including SNAP recipients, Temporary Cash Assistance recipients, non-custodial parents, foster youth, and veterans on assistance — who want to start or grow a small business. In Howard County, open to current Department of Human Services customers interested in starting a business. Also available to DHS customers in Anne Arundel County interested in starting a business.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Entrepreneurship and workforce development training, business education, and ongoing consulting to help participants start or sustain a small business.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland through regional SBDC partnerships and local Departments of Social Services, including locally in Howard County through Howard County Department of Social Services, in Anne Arundel County through the local DHS office, and in 12 jurisdictions on the Eastern Shore and in Western Maryland through Washington County Department of Social Services and partner SBDCs.
requirements_list: Must be currently receiving public assistance from a local Maryland Department of Social Services
Must be a current DHS customer (e.g. SNAP recipient, Temporary Cash Assistance recipient, non-custodial parent, foster youth, or veteran on assistance)
Must have an idea or interest in starting or growing a small business
Must attend all eight training sessions
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online using the Google Form linked on the program page at dhs.maryland.gov/PA2E. Howard County residents may also visit howardcountymd.gov/workforce-development/public-assistance-entrepreneurship-pa2e/ for local enrollment details, or contact howco.dss@maryland.gov or 410-872-8700. Anne Arundel County residents may visit aacounty.org/workforce-development/public-assistance-entrepreneurship-pa2e/. For information on classes in Western Maryland or Eastern Shore jurisdictions, contact family investment specialists Steve Chapman at 240-420-2507 or Jarena Griffin at 240-420-2559.

structured_extraction.program_description: Ready By 21 is a statewide initiative by the Maryland Department of Human Services to prepare youth in foster care for successful adulthood. It provides individualized, strengths-based transition plans covering education, employment, financial empowerment, housing, and well-being for youth ages 14 to 21 who are involved in the foster care system.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Individualized transition planning and support services across five domains: education and employment, financial empowerment, permanent and supportive connections, safe and stable housing, and well-being and civic engagement. Plans are developed with the youth, their foster care worker, and their support team, and are continually monitored and updated.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Youth ages 14 to 21 in the Maryland foster care system who are transitioning to independent living
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Transition planning and support for education, employment, financial skills, housing stability, and well-being
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland for youth involved in the state foster care system
requirements_list: Must be between ages 14 and 21
Must be involved with the Maryland foster care system
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Youth work with their Local Department of Social Services (LDSS) foster care worker and support team to develop and monitor an individualized transition plan.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides employment assistance to refugees and asylees in Maryland to help them achieve economic self-sufficiency quickly after arriving in the U.S. Services are delivered through a network of provider organizations in the Baltimore, Suburban Washington, and Frederick areas.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Employment services are provided at no cost to eligible refugees and asylees through local resettlement organizations. Services include job readiness training, resume writing, case management, job search assistance, vocational training, interview preparation, transportation assistance, interpretation during job interviews, and post-placement support.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Refugees and asylees who have recently arrived in the United States and are located in the Baltimore Metropolitan Area, Suburban Washington Area, or Frederick Area of Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Job readiness training, vocational training, job search and placement support, transportation assistance, interpretation services, and case management to address employment barriers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Services are available in the Baltimore Metropolitan Area, Suburban Washington Area (Silver Spring and Greenbelt), and Frederick Area of Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a refugee or asylee
Must be located in the Baltimore Metropolitan Area, Suburban Washington Area, or Frederick Area of Maryland
Must be an employable member of the refugee population
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact one of the participating provider organizations directly: International Rescue Committee Baltimore, Lutheran Social Services of the National Capital Area, or Ethiopian Community Development Council African Community Center DC Metro. Locations and contact information are listed on the program page.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides programming for refugee parents and their young children (ages 0-5) at the same time. Parents get English classes, tutoring, and employment skills support, while children participate in enrichment courses and playgroups. The program removes childcare barriers for refugee parents attending English classes.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Multi-generational programming delivered simultaneously for refugee parents and children ages 0-5. Services include English classes and tutoring for parents, childhood enrichment courses and playgroups for children, and support services.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Refugee parents attending ESOL courses and their children ages 0-5 in Prince George's County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: English language instruction, childcare, childhood enrichment, and employment skills development
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Prince George's County through Solutions in Hometown Connections
requirements_list: Must be an ORR-eligible refugee parent with children ages 0-5
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Solutions in Hometown Connections directly by email or phone for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: MORA partners with the Center for Global Migration and Immigrant Health (CGMIH) at the Maryland Department of Health to provide health education services for eligible refugee clients. Services aim to increase health literacy, support navigation of the health care system, and organize wellness and peer support groups, including for mental wellness.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Health education services including health literacy support, health care navigation assistance, and wellness groups (including mental wellness and peer support). Services are provided in coordination with medical screenings.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible refugee clients receiving medical screenings
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Health education, health care navigation, and wellness group participation
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Must be an eligible refugee client
Services are provided in coordination with medical screenings — clients interested must inquire during their screening
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Clients interested in Refugee Health Promotion Program services should inquire during their medical screening appointment.

structured_extraction.program_description: Refugee Medical Assistance provides short-term medical coverage to refugee populations who are not eligible for Medicaid. It covers eligible individuals for up to 12 months after arriving in the U.S. or being granted asylum, eligible humanitarian parole status, or victim of trafficking certification.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Short-term medical coverage similar to Medicaid benefits for up to 12 months after U.S. arrival or grant of asylum. Applicants must first apply for Medicaid through Maryland Health Connection; if found ineligible, they may apply for RMA through the MarylandBenefits portal.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Refugee populations ineligible for Medicaid, including refugees, asylees, humanitarian parolees, and trafficking victims who arrived in the U.S. within the past 12 months
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Medical coverage and healthcare access
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a refugee, asylee, humanitarian parolee, or trafficking victim
Must be ineligible for Medicaid
Must apply within 12 months of U.S. arrival or grant of asylum
Individuals under age 65 with no disabilities must first complete Medicaid application requirements and be screened ineligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through Maryland Health Connection (marylandhealthconnection.gov) for Medicaid first. If found ineligible, apply for RMA through the MarylandBenefits portal (MarylandBenefits.gov).

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Refugee Health Program provides comprehensive health assessments for newly arrived refugees, asylees, parolees, and other eligible immigrants within 90 to 180 days of U.S. arrival or granted asylum date. Screenings include physical and mental health assessments, immunizations for children, and referrals to primary care.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free comprehensive health assessment exam including physical and mental health screening, immunizations for school-age children, referral to primary care, and treatment or referral for communicable diseases. Provided at local health departments and federally-qualified health clinics, including Baltimore Medical Systems (Baltimore metro area) and CCI Health Services (Montgomery and Prince George's Counties).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Newly arrived refugees, asylees, parolees, and other eligible immigrants
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Health assessments, immunizations, treatment, and referrals to primary care
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland; services provided in Baltimore metropolitan area and Suburban Washington area (Montgomery and Prince George's Counties)
requirements_list: Must be a newly arrived refugee, asylee, parolee, or other eligible immigrant
Health assessment must be initiated within 90 days of U.S. arrival or granted asylum date
Health assessment must be completed within 180 days of U.S. arrival or granted asylum date
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local health department or one of the federally-qualified health clinics: Baltimore Medical Systems (Baltimore metro area, email RefugeeHealth@bmsi.org, phone 443-703-3404) or CCI Health Services (Montgomery and Prince George's Counties, email RHA@cciweb.org, phone 301-979-7656). Resettlement agencies are responsible for ensuring newly arrived refugees receive a screening appointment.

structured_extraction.program_description: Supports school-aged refugee youth (primarily ages 0-18) in achieving academic success and helps public schools serve refugee students. The program provides academic support outside the classroom, engages parents in their children's education, and builds cultural competence among school staff.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Academic support outside the classroom, parent engagement in school activities, and cultural competency training for school staff. Delivered through local resettlement agencies including IRC Silver Spring, IRC Baltimore, and Baltimore City Community College.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Refugee youth ages 0-18, their parents, and public school systems serving refugee populations
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Academic support, English language acquisition, parent engagement in school activities, and cultural competency training for school staff
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide, administered through IRC Silver Spring, IRC Baltimore, and Baltimore City Community College
requirements_list: Must be an ORR-eligible refugee youth of school age (primarily ages 0-18)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact International Rescue Committee (IRC) Silver Spring, IRC Baltimore, or Baltimore City Community College (BCCC) for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: Refugee Transitional Cash Assistance (RTCA or RCA) is a state-administered, federally funded temporary financial assistance program. It provides cash support to eligible refugees and asylees until they can find employment and become financially independent.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Temporary cash assistance payments provided to eligible refugees and asylees. Benefits last for up to 4 months after arrival in the U.S. or after an asylum grant, as long as the recipient remains ineligible for other cash assistance programs and meets income guidelines.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Refugees and asylees who have held an eligible immigration status in the U.S. for less than 4 months, are not eligible for other cash assistance programs (such as TANF, SSI, OAA, AB, APTD, or AABD), are not full-time students in higher education, and meet income eligibility guidelines.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: General living expenses and financial support while recipients seek employment and work toward economic independence.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across all Maryland counties through local resettlement agencies in the Baltimore metro area, suburban Washington area, and Frederick area. Remote access is available for individuals in all counties.
requirements_list: Must hold an eligible and documented immigration status in the U.S. for less than the established RTCA eligibility period (currently 4 months after arrival or after an asylum grant)
Must be ineligible for other cash assistance programs including TANF, SSI, OAA, AB, APTD, and AABD
Must not be a full-time student in an institution of higher education
Must meet income eligibility guidelines
Must complete all required paperwork including proof of eligible immigration status
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact one of the local resettlement agencies partnering with MORA — International Rescue Committee (IRC) Baltimore, Lutheran Social Services of the National Capital Area (LSSNCA), or Ethiopian Community Development Council (ECDC) African Community Center DC Metro — in the Baltimore metro, suburban Washington, or Frederick areas. Applications can be completed in person or remotely.

structured_extraction.program_description: Promotes positive civic and social engagement and supports academic and career achievement for refugee youth ages 15-24. Local resettlement agencies match eligible youth with mentors who provide personalized guidance and support to help youth integrate socially and become economically self-sufficient.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant-funded mentoring program that matches refugee youth with mentors who provide personalized guidance, academic support, vocational and career advancement assistance, and social inclusion support.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Refugee youth ages 15-24 who are ORR-eligible
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Academic achievement, vocational and career advancement, social inclusion, and mentoring support
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide, administered through ECDC, IRC Baltimore, IRC Silver Spring, and Lutheran Social Services of the National Capital Area (LSSNCA)
requirements_list: Must be an ORR-eligible refugee youth ages 15-24
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Ethiopian Community Development Council (ECDC), IRC Baltimore, IRC Silver Spring, or Lutheran Social Services of the National Capital Area (LSSNCA) for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: Engages, empowers, and supports noncustodial parents in Anne Arundel County to obtain and maintain employment so they can make regular child support payments.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Employment assistance for unemployed or underemployed noncustodial parents to help them obtain and maintain unsubsidized, competitive employment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Unemployed or underemployed noncustodial parents in Anne Arundel County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Employment support services to help noncustodial parents find and keep jobs
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County, Maryland

structured_extraction.program_description: The Restaurant Meals Program (RMP) allows elderly (age 60+), homeless, and disabled SNAP (Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program) recipients to use their EBT (Electronic Benefit Transfer) card to purchase prepared or hot food (breakfast, lunch, or dinner) at participating restaurants and delis. Eligible SNAP households experiencing homelessness can also purchase meals at a discounted price from restaurants contracted with the federal government. Eligible recipients include people experiencing homelessness, adults age 60 or older (and their spouses), and disabled individuals (and their spouses if they are the only two on the SNAP case). The program is currently being piloted in select Maryland counties with plans to expand statewide.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible SNAP recipients can use their existing EBT card benefits to buy prepared or hot meals (breakfast, lunch, or dinner) at participating restaurants and delis. Using this program does not change the recipient's benefit amount — it simply expands where they can spend their existing SNAP benefits. No tax is charged on purchases made through the program. Participants can use a combination of SNAP EBT and EBT cash in a single transaction. Eligible Maryland RMP participants may also use their benefits at restaurants in other states that participate in the RMP. For restaurants, participation means becoming authorized to accept SNAP EBT cards as payment for prepared meals.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland SNAP recipients who are homeless, age 60 or older (including qualifying spouse), or disabled (including spouse if only two people on the SNAP case). Also open to for-profit restaurants and other meal service providers interested in participating as authorized vendors accepting SNAP EBT payments for prepared meals.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of prepared or hot meals (breakfast, lunch, or dinner) at participating restaurants and delis using existing SNAP EBT benefits.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is piloting in select Maryland counties with plans to expand to additional jurisdictions statewide. Eligible Maryland RMP participants may use their benefits at participating restaurants in other states that also run the Restaurant Meals Program.
requirements_list: Must be an active Maryland SNAP recipient
Must meet at least one eligibility criterion: experiencing homelessness, age 60 or older (including qualifying spouse), or disabled (including spouse if they are the only two on the SNAP case)
Eligibility is reviewed at every SNAP recertification/redetermination
Must use EBT card at a participating, authorized restaurant
Cannot use benefits to purchase alcohol or non-food items
For restaurants: must apply to USDA and sign a Memorandum of Understanding with MD DHS
For restaurants: must be a private, for-profit establishment with 50% or more of gross sales in prepared foods
For restaurants: must submit FNS 252-2 form with required documentation (photo ID, Social Security verification, valid business license)
For restaurants: must prevent workers from trading cash for SNAP benefits
For restaurants: must prevent unauthorized use of SNAP benefits
For restaurants: must not use SNAP benefits for credit accounts or loans
For restaurants: must not use SNAP benefits for non-eligible items
For restaurants: must treat SNAP customers the same as other customers
For restaurants: cannot be both a restaurant and traditional retailer simultaneously
Restaurant applicant must be principal administrator, executive director, or owner
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Recipients do not need to submit a separate application — eligibility is determined during the normal SNAP enrollment and recertification/redetermination process. Eligible recipients can locate participating restaurants on the DHS website or by asking their Eligibility Worker. They can check their EBT balance by calling 1-800-997-2222 or visiting www.connectebt.com, then use their EBT card at a participating restaurant. Restaurants wishing to participate must apply to USDA by submitting a completed FNS 252-2 form and a signed Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with MD DHS, along with required documentation (photo ID, Social Security verification, valid business license). MD DHS collects and submits the application package on behalf of the restaurant to USDA Food and Nutrition Service. USDA has 45 days to make an authorization decision after receiving a complete application.

structured_extraction.program_name: SNAP Outreach Community Based Organizations Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) Outreach Program funds and coordinates community-based organizations (CBOs) to inform and educate the public about SNAP food benefits, helping eligible individuals and families who may qualify but are unaware of the program. The Maryland Department of Human Services authorizes CBOs across the state to provide free information and application assistance to people who may qualify for SNAP. The program aims to reduce stigma associated with receiving food assistance and builds a statewide outreach network to help Maryland residents access food benefits and reduce hunger. Services are free and available through local organizations in most Maryland counties, as well as statewide organizations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal funds and private contributions from program partners are used to fund and coordinate SNAP outreach services through authorized community-based organizations across Maryland. Authorized CBOs provide free information and application assistance to help individuals apply for SNAP food benefits. The program provides funding to support outreach activities that connect eligible residents with SNAP benefits. Services are available in person through local CBOs located throughout Maryland, including statewide organizations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents who may be eligible for SNAP food benefits and need assistance applying, as well as community-based organizations and local departments of social services that help connect Maryland residents with SNAP food benefits.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Outreach and education activities to inform eligible individuals and families about SNAP benefits, reduce stigma, and help residents apply for food assistance. Includes application assistance and information about SNAP food benefits.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — authorized organizations serve specific counties and regions across Maryland, with some organizations serving statewide.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individuals seeking help: Contact any authorized community-based organization listed on the DHS website that serves your area. If no organization is listed in your area or county, contact any organization listed as serving statewide. The service is free. Organizations interested in participating: Connect through the SNAP Outreach Community Based Organizations directory on the DHS website.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Safe Haven Program reduces newborn mortality and promotes healthy beginnings for newborns by offering a safe and legal way for a parent or responsible adult who is unable or unwilling to care for their child to surrender the newborn. A mother or responsible adult can surrender a newborn (60 days old or younger and unharmed) at a designated facility — such as a hospital, licensed medical provider, police department, state police barracks, or insured fire company — without risk of arrest or prosecution. The newborn receives necessary medical care and is then placed with the Local Department of Social Services for placement with a permanent, stable family through adoption. Parents who change their mind may contact the Local Department of Social Services at 1-800-917-7383.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Parents or responsible adults may surrender a newborn (60 days old or younger and unharmed) at a designated facility — including hospitals, licensed medical providers, police departments, state police barracks, and insured fire companies — without fear of arrest or prosecution. The newborn receives necessary medical care and is then placed with the Local Department of Social Services (LDSS) for placement with a permanent, stable family through adoption. Parents who change their mind may contact LDSS at 1-800-917-7383.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Parents or responsible adults (18 years or older) who are unable or unwilling to care for a newborn infant (60 days old or younger) and wish to surrender the child safely and legally; also includes pregnant individuals seeking options.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Safe, legal surrender of a newborn at a designated facility to ensure the child's health and well-being; newborn receives medical care and is placed with a permanent family through the Local Department of Social Services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland at designated hospitals, licensed medical providers, police departments, state police barracks, and insured fire companies in all 24 counties and Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Newborn must be 60 days old or younger
Newborn must be unharmed — no evidence of physical injury or failure to provide proper care as determined by a licensed health care practitioner
Surrender must occur at a designated facility (hospital, licensed medical provider, police department, state police barracks, or insured fire company)
Direct handover must occur with a designated facility staff member — newborn cannot be left unattended
Responsible adult must be 18 years or older
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Bring the newborn to any designated Safe Haven facility in Maryland, including hospitals, licensed medical providers, police departments, state police barracks, or insured fire companies. Present the newborn directly to a staff member and state 'This is a Safe Haven baby.' Optional medical and family health history questions may be asked. Call 2-1-1 to locate the nearest Safe Haven facility, or call the DHS toll-free hotline at 1-800-917-7383 to make a Safe Haven notification. After surrender, the facility will notify DHS and the newborn will receive medical attention before being placed with LDSS for adoption. If the parent changes their mind, contact the Local Department of Social Services at 1-800-917-7383.

structured_extraction.program_description: The SILA program provides foster youth ages 16 to 21 the opportunity to learn and practice independent living skills while receiving support from the local department of social services and a provider agency. Youth can live semi-independently in a rented room, their own apartment, or a college dorm while working toward self-sufficiency. Each month, SILA youth receive financial assistance from the local Department of Social Services to help cover living expenses including rent, food, and other costs. Support services include housing, health care, education, employment, financial literacy, and social and emotional well-being assistance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Monthly financial assistance check to help cover living expenses such as rent, food, and other costs while living semi-independently, plus support services including housing, health care, education, employment, financial literacy, and social and emotional well-being assistance provided through the local department of social services.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Foster youth ages 16 to 21 who are enrolled in school or vocational training or working at least 80 hours per month, are sufficiently mature, and need help transitioning to self-sufficiency.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Living expenses including rent, food, and other costs of semi-independent living; housing, health care, education, employment, financial literacy, and social and emotional well-being support.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through Maryland's 24 local departments of social services, including Baltimore City.

structured_extraction.program_name: Services Helping the Involvement of Non-Custodial Parents and Employment (SHINE)
structured_extraction.program_description: SHINE is a free, 12-month case management program for noncustodial parents in Allegany County who are obligated to pay child support. The program helps participants overcome barriers to employment, gain financial stability, and strengthen their relationships with their children. It offers job readiness support, skills training, legal aid, documentation help, parenting resources, and referrals for housing, transportation, and other basic needs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free 12-month case management including employment and job readiness support, skills training, occupational/vocational training access, GED classes, resume and interview prep, legal aid (expungement, mediation, pro bono services), help obtaining vital documents (birth certificates, IDs, Social Security cards), parenting resources, mental health and substance abuse referrals, housing referrals, transportation assistance, and help applying for state benefits. Successful participation can also help participants avoid driver's license suspension and contempt charges for child support nonpayment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Noncustodial parents in Allegany County who are seeking stable employment and need support to comply with a child support order, typically referred by a Magistrate during a contempt hearing or by the Child Support Administration.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Employment services, job training, legal assistance, documentation support, parenting skills, mental health and substance abuse referrals, housing and transportation resources, and basic needs support.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to noncustodial parents in Allegany County, Maryland. Services are provided through the Allegany County Department of Social Services office at 1 Frederick Street, Cumberland, MD 21502.

Must be seeking stable employment
Must be referred by a Magistrate during a contempt hearing or by the Child Support Administration
Must not have known physical or mental disabilities that prevent working
Must report weekly job search activities, current employment status and income, child support payment history, and any changes to address, phone, or employment status
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Once referred by a court or the Child Support Administration, the local DSS office schedules an intake appointment. The applicant meets with a Noncustodial Parent Employment Program (NPEP) Specialist at the Allegany County DSS office for an assessment of strengths and needs. The specialist then develops a personalized plan to address barriers and reviews all program compliance policies. After intake, ongoing monthly meetings with the NPEP Specialist take place throughout the 12-month program.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Social Services to Adults (SSTA) program is the Maryland Department of Human Services' core case management program for vulnerable adults, administered locally through county departments of social services. It helps adults with limited abilities stay self-supporting and self-sufficient, prevents abuse, neglect, self-neglect, or exploitation, and reduces unnecessary institutionalization or arranges appropriate care when needed. The program provides three types of services at no cost: (1) Information and Referral — connects adults to other agencies best suited to meet their needs; (2) Crisis Intervention — up to 60 days of intensive help and guidance for adults facing a crisis or major life change; and (3) Case Management — a social worker conducts a comprehensive needs assessment and develops an individualized plan of service to help the adult live as independently as possible in the community or arrange institutional care when appropriate. Information and Referral and Crisis Intervention are available regardless of income. Continuing Case Management requires income below 80% of State Median Income and, in some counties, liquid assets below $19,999 for one person ($3,000 more per additional family member).

Information and Referral and Crisis Intervention are available regardless of income. Continuing Case Management requires income not exceeding 80% of State Median Income and liquid assets not exceeding $19,999 for one individual (plus $3,000 per additional family member).

Available statewide through local departments of social services, including Montgomery County residents who may also contact the Aging and Disability Resource Unit.

structured_extraction.program_name: Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) / Maryland Food Supplement Program
structured_extraction.program_description: SNAP, also known as the Food Supplement Program in Maryland, is the largest federal nutrition assistance program in the nation. It helps low-income households buy food they need for good health by providing monthly food assistance benefits to eligible individuals and families in Maryland, including U.S. citizens and certain eligible immigrants. More than 680,000 Marylanders receive SNAP each month, including nearly 270,000 children, with an average monthly benefit of $180. Benefits are loaded onto an Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) card called the Independence Card, which works like an ATM/debit card and can be used to purchase eligible food items at authorized retailers, including online grocery shopping. The benefit amount is calculated based on household size and monthly income after allowable deductions (standard deduction, 20% of earned income, dependent care costs, child support payments, shelter and utility expenses, and medical expenses over $35/month for members age 60+ or with disabilities), following the USDA Thrifty Food Plan, which is updated annually to reflect food prices. Households must also spend some of their own cash in addition to benefits. Benefits are available within 30 days of application approval, or within 7 days for households that qualify for expedited (emergency) benefits. Some people with little or no money may qualify for Expedited SNAP benefits right away with only an interview and identity verification. Able-Bodied Adults Without Dependents (ABAWDs) between ages 18 and 64 must meet work requirements — working, joining a work program, or volunteering for at least 80 hours per month starting November 1, 2025 — to continue receiving benefits. ABAWDs receive a 3-month grace period of benefits between July 1, 2023, and June 30, 2026, while they find work or join a work program. The program is currently undergoing major changes due to federal law H.R. 1 (2025), signed into law on July 4, 2025, which affects who qualifies, reduces benefit amounts for some households, and increases the state's share of program costs. Starting October 1, 2027, Maryland may be required to cover up to 15% of benefit costs depending on the state's payment error rate. Non-citizen eligibility is now limited to lawful permanent residents, Cuban or Haitian immigrants, and individuals from the Federated States of Micronesia and the Republic of the Marshall Islands; refugees and asylees must have a green card and meet the 5-year waiting period. Under H.R. 1 (2025), households without a member aged 60+ or with a disability must provide proof of utility payments (a utility bill from the last 30 days) to claim the $572 Standard Utility Allowance (SUA). Maximum monthly benefit amounts vary by household size (1 person: $339; 8 people: $1,421; additional person: +$136), effective October 2025. Income eligibility is based on 130% of the Federal Poverty Level (gross monthly income), with maximum net income under 100% of FPL; categorical eligibility available at 200% FPL. The program is administered by the Maryland Department of Human Services, Family Investment Administration (DHS/FIA). SNAP Employment and Training (E&T) services are also available through partner organizations statewide, providing job readiness training, vocational training, job placement, and supportive services for SNAP recipients. SNAP benefits can also be used for online grocery shopping at participating retailers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Monthly food purchasing assistance provided based on the USDA Thrifty Food Plan (Maximum Allotment), adjusted annually for food prices. The average monthly benefit is $180 per client. Maximum monthly benefit amounts vary by household size: 1 person: $339; 8 people: $1,421; each additional person: +$136 (effective October 2025). Benefits are loaded onto an EBT card (the Independence Card) and can be used to purchase eligible food items at authorized retailers, including online grocery shopping at participating retailers (e.g., Amazon, Walmart, ShopRite). Shipping/delivery fees cannot be paid with SNAP benefits. The benefit amount depends on household size and net monthly income after allowable deductions (standard deduction, 20% of earned income, dependent care costs, child support payments, shelter and utility expenses, and medical expenses over $35/month for members age 60+ or with disabilities). Income eligibility is based on gross monthly income under 130% of the Federal Poverty Level, with maximum net income under 100% FPL; categorical eligibility available at 200% FPL. Households must also spend some of their own cash in addition to benefits. Under H.R. 1 (2025), households without a member aged 60+ or with a disability must submit a utility bill from the last 30 days to claim the $572 Standard Utility Allowance (SUA). Benefits cannot be used to purchase alcohol, tobacco, guns, bullets, explosives, or illegal drugs, and EBT cards cannot be used in liquor stores, adult entertainment venues, or gambling establishments. Benefits are available within 30 days of application approval. Some people with little or no money may qualify for Expedited SNAP benefits within 7 days with only an interview and identity verification; expedited eligibility applies if household monthly income is under $150 AND cash/savings are $100 or less, OR shelter costs exceed income and liquid resources, OR the household includes a migrant/seasonal farm worker. ABAWDs receive a 3-month grace period of benefits between July 1, 2023, and June 30, 2026, while they find work or join a work program. After the grace period, benefits may stop unless the recipient meets work requirements or qualifies for an exemption. Starting October 1, 2027, Maryland may be required to cover up to 15% of benefit costs depending on the state's payment error rate. SNAP Employment and Training (E&T) services are also available through partner organizations, providing vocational training, job placement, job retention, and supportive services for SNAP recipients.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low- and no-income individuals and households in Maryland, including U.S. citizens and certain eligible immigrants, those who work for low wages, are unemployed or part-time workers, receive public assistance (including SSI or medical assistance), are elderly or disabled with small incomes, are homeless or unhoused, families with children, seniors, veterans, people experiencing homelessness, young adults who aged out of out-of-home care, migrant/seasonal farm workers, and qualifying immigrants such as permanent residents, Cuban/Haitian entrants, and citizens of Micronesia and the Marshall Islands. Also includes Able-Bodied Adults Without Dependents (ABAWDs) ages 18–64 who must meet work requirements starting November 1, 2025. Income eligibility based on household income under 130% of the Federal Poverty Level.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchasing eligible food items and groceries for household meals and nutrition needs at authorized retailers, including online grocery shopping, using an EBT card. Benefits cannot be used for alcohol, tobacco, guns, bullets, explosives, illegal drugs, or non-food items. Shipping/delivery fees for online orders cannot be paid with SNAP benefits.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland through local departments of Social Services. Must be a Maryland resident. Applications can be filed online at MarylandBenefits.gov, in person, by mail, by phone, or by fax at local Social Services offices. In Anne Arundel County, contact the Department of Social Services at 410-269-4500 or visit aacounty.org/social-services. In Calvert County, contact the Department of Social Services at 443-550-6900 or visit 200 Duke Street, Prince Frederick. In Howard County, apply at 9780 Patuxent Woods Drive, Columbia, MD 21046 (drop-off 8am–4:30pm, face-to-face interviews Monday–Thursday). In Montgomery County, applications may also be submitted via fax, email to OESS.MoCo@montgomerycountymd.gov, or mail to any OESS office. In Prince George's County, apply through the Department of Social Services. Interpretation services are available free of charge for limited English proficiency customers. TTY users dial 800-735-2258.
