structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at MarylandBenefits.gov (benefits.maryland.gov) or at https://mydhrbenefits.dhr.state.md.us using a smartphone, tablet, or computer, in person at a local department of Social Services, by phone, by mail, by fax, or by downloading and submitting the PDF application. The office accepts a signed application the same day it is received even if an interview cannot be conducted that day. A caseworker will schedule an interview (in-person or by phone) to review the application, verify information, and screen applicants for eligibility and work requirement exceptions. Bring proof of income, immigration status (if applicable), child support payments, and medical expenses. Applications must be signed by the head of household or authorized representative. After the interview, the local department will send a notice explaining your eligibility and benefit amount. For online grocery shopping with SNAP benefits, register your EBT card on participating retailer websites (e.g., Amazon.com/SNAP-EBT, walmart.com/grocery, ShopRite.com), add items labeled 'SNAP EBT eligible,' and select EBT as payment method at checkout. In Anne Arundel County, contact the local DSS office at 410-269-4500 or visit aacounty.org/social-services. In Calvert County, contact the Calvert County Department of Social Services at 443-550-6900 or visit 200 Duke Street, Prince Frederick. In Howard County, apply at 9780 Patuxent Woods Drive, Columbia, MD 21046; applications can be dropped off at the front desk (8am–4:30pm) any day of the week and face-to-face interviews are held Monday–Thursday. In Montgomery County, you may also fax your application to the appropriate OESS office, email OESS.MoCo@montgomerycountymd.gov, or mail to any OESS office. In Prince George's County, apply through the Department of Social Services. Walk-ins and appointments are accepted at regional offices. Interpretation services are available free of charge for limited English proficiency customers. Call 1-800-332-6347 for help. TTY users dial 800-735-2258. Existing recipients will have updated rules applied at their next recertification.

structured_extraction.program_name: Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program Employment and Training (SNAP E&T)
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's SNAP E&T program connects people who receive SNAP food benefits to free, job-driven training programs across the state. Training typically runs 12 to 16 weeks and covers in-demand industries such as welding, construction, machining, manufacturing, healthcare, hospitality, and IT. The program provides job placement, retention support, and comprehensive services to help participants overcome barriers to employment such as criminal backgrounds, limited work experience, or transportation issues. Participants receive support from a personal career navigator and success coach throughout the program. Participation is voluntary for most SNAP recipients, though Able-Bodied Adults Without Dependents (ABAWDs) face a 3-month SNAP time limit unless working or enrolled in E&T. Programs are delivered statewide through local Departments of Social Services and third-party training providers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free job-driven training programs averaging 12 to 16 weeks at no cost to participants in industries such as welding, construction, machining, manufacturing, healthcare, hospitality, and IT. Services include hard skills training, soft skills training, job readiness, job search and placement assistance, industry-recognized certifications, work experience, transportation assistance, legal services, referrals to community services, help resolving employment barriers (such as criminal records, driver's license issues, or licensing problems), and access to work clothing, tools, or textbooks. A personal career navigator and success coach provide ongoing support throughout the program. No application is required — participation is voluntary for most SNAP recipients.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents age 16 and older who currently receive SNAP food benefits, do not receive Cash Assistance (TANF), and are able to work upon completing the program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Job-driven workforce training, job placement and retention services, industry-recognized certifications, work experience, transportation, work clothing and tools, textbooks, legal services, and other employment barrier removal support services in fields including welding, construction, machine operation, manufacturing, healthcare, hospitality, and IT.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide throughout Maryland through local Departments of Social Services and third-party training providers.
requirements_list: Must be age 16 or older
Must currently receive SNAP (food assistance/food supplement) benefits
Must not receive Cash Assistance/TANF
Must be able to work upon completion of the program
Participation is voluntary for most SNAP recipients
Able-Bodied Adults Without Dependents (ABAWDs) face a 3-month SNAP time limit unless working or enrolled in E&T
Individual training programs may have additional eligibility requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: No separate application is required for SNAP E&T. SNAP recipients can contact their local Department of Social Services (DSS) or call the DHS helpline at 1-800-332-6347 to learn about available programs and enroll. Those who do not yet receive SNAP can apply online at marylandbenefits.gov or in person at a local DSS office.

structured_extraction.program_description: When a family receives Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) and child support payments are also being made, the Maryland Department of Human Services (DHS) passes through a portion of those child support payments directly to the custodial party. Child support payments collected from the non-custodial parent (NCP) are assigned to the state, and if the NCP pays current child support in a given month, DHS passes a portion of that payment directly to the custodial party. Eligible custodial parties receive a monthly pass-through payment of up to $100 for families with one child or $200 for families with two or more children, or the court-ordered current support amount — whichever is less. Payments are based on current child support paid in the prior calendar month and are disbursed the following month. Payments on support arrears are not eligible. Once the TCA case closes, child support transfers fully to the custodial party and pass-through payments end, though one final payment may arrive in the month after closure if the NCP paid during the last month the case was open.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Custodial parties with an active Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) case receive a monthly pass-through payment based on current child support paid by the NCP in the prior calendar month. Maximum monthly payments are: $100 for families with 1 child, $200 for families with 2 or more children. The actual payment is whichever is less — the applicable maximum amount or the court-ordered child support amount. Payments are based on current child support paid — not arrears — and are disbursed the month after the noncustodial parent makes payment. Payments on arrears (back-owed support) are not eligible.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Custodial parents and caregivers (including other custodial parties) who have an active Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) case and are receiving child support payments through the Child Support Administration, where the noncustodial parent pays current child support.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supplemental cash income passed directly to custodial families receiving TCA when current child support is paid by the noncustodial parent. Payments can be used for general household or child-related needs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to families with an active TCA cash assistance case enrolled in the Maryland Temporary Cash Assistance program.
requirements_list: Must have an active Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) case to receive pass-through payments.
Must have an active child support case.
An active SNAP (food assistance) case alone does not qualify — a TCA case is required.
Non-custodial parent must have made current support payments in the prior calendar month.
Payments on support arrears (past-due support) are not eligible.

Once the TCA case closes, child support transfers fully to the custodial party and pass-through payments end (though one final payment may arrive in the month after closure if the NCP paid during the last month the case was open).
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: No separate application is required. Enrollment is automatic for families with an active TCA case who also have child support payments coming in. Payments are automatically calculated and issued to eligible custodial parties based on an active TCA case and child support payments received. Contact the customer service center at 1-800-332-6347 for questions.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Human Services Office of Community Grants funds a set of nonprofit organizations to deliver support services including home-delivered meals, nutritional counseling, after-school programming, grief counseling, and fresh produce distribution to low-income and vulnerable residents across Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are awarded to nonprofit organizations to fund direct community services such as home-delivered meals and nutritional counseling for people with life-threatening illnesses, after-school programs, grief counseling, and fresh produce distribution to food deserts. Specific grant amounts are not stated on this page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations that provide support services such as meals, counseling, after-school programming, and food access to vulnerable and low-income Marylanders.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home-delivered meals and nutritional counseling, after-school programming, grief counseling, and fresh produce distribution to food deserts.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Services are provided in all 24 Maryland jurisdictions.
requirements_list: Must be a nonprofit organization
Must provide qualifying support services to vulnerable or low-income populations in Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Application process is not described on this page. Contact the Maryland Department of Human Services Office of Community Grants for details.

structured_extraction.program_name: Supporting, Training, and Employing Parents Program (STEP Up)
structured_extraction.program_description: STEP Up is a free, job-driven pilot program that offers job training and comprehensive support services to unemployed or underemployed noncustodial parents who have a Baltimore City child support case. Participants can train for careers in welding, green construction, machining, healthcare, hospitality, warehousing, biotechnology, and other in-demand industries. Support services include hard skills training, soft skills training, job readiness, job search and placement, industry-recognized certifications, work experience, transportation assistance, referrals to community services, help resolving barriers to employment (criminal record, legal issues, driver's license suspension), access to work clothing and tools, and a personal career navigator. Participants who successfully complete the program may earn forgiveness of child support arrears owed to the State of Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free job training in in-demand industries (healthcare, construction, welding, green construction, machining, hospitality, warehousing, biotechnology, and more). Support services include hard skills training, soft skills training, job readiness, job search and placement, industry-recognized certifications, work experience, transportation assistance, referrals to community services, help resolving barriers to employment (criminal record, legal issues, driver's license suspension), access to work clothing and tools, and a personal career navigator. Participants who successfully complete the program may earn forgiveness of child support arrears owed to the State of Maryland.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Unemployed or underemployed noncustodial parents (parents who do not have primary custody of their child) who have a Baltimore City child support case and can commit to working upon program completion.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Job training, soft skills development, job placement, industry-recognized certifications, transportation assistance, access to work clothing and tools, and support services to overcome barriers to employment (criminal record, legal issues, driver's license suspension), as well as potential forgiveness of child support arrears owed to the State of Maryland.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must have an active Baltimore City child support case. Initial enrollment takes place at the Baltimore City Office of Child Support Services at Mondawmin Mall, 2401 Liberty Heights Ave., Baltimore, MD 21215, Suite 4645.
requirements_list: Must be a noncustodial parent with a Baltimore City child support case
Must be unemployed or underemployed
Must be able to commit to working upon program completion
Must reside in Baltimore City
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call (410) 844-7001 x 7144 to schedule an enrollment session at the Baltimore City Office of Child Support Services at Mondawmin Mall, 2401 Liberty Heights Ave., Baltimore, MD 21215, Suite 4645. Inform the intake coordinator of any specific training program interest. Once enrolled, participants join a training program with one of the STEP Up employment partners. You may also visit the STEP Up program page or contact your local Department of Social Services for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) / Maryland's Temporary Assistance to Needy Families (TANF)
structured_extraction.program_description: Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) is Maryland's Temporary Assistance to Needy Families (TANF) program. It provides time-limited cash assistance and employment resources to low-income families with dependent children under age 18 (or age 19 if graduating in the same calendar year) when other resources do not fully meet the family's needs. The program's primary goal is to assist clients in becoming financially independent through employment, offering job readiness classes, job search assistance, and work programs. It may also provide childcare and transportation support. Benefits are delivered via an Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) card (the Independence Card) or direct deposit, with cash benefits made available from the 2nd to the 4th of every month based on the first letter of the recipient's last name. Recipients may withdraw money from ATMs or use the card at participating stores. The program also supports adults in finding employment through work readiness activities including job readiness programs, volunteer work experience, and vocational education and training. Recipients are required to participate in a work program as a condition of receiving benefits. The program is administered statewide by the Maryland Department of Human Services, with local access available through county offices including Anne Arundel County Social Services and Montgomery County DHHS offices in Rockville, Silver Spring, and Germantown.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Cash assistance payments are provided to eligible families with dependent children under 18 years of age (or age 19 if graduating in the same calendar year). Benefit amounts vary based on assistance unit size and family income, ranging from $328 for a family of 1 to $1,372 for a family of 8. Benefits are loaded onto an EBT card (Independence Card) or provided via direct deposit, with funds available from the 2nd to the 4th of each month based on the first letter of the recipient's last name. Recipients can use the card at ATMs or participating stores. The program also includes work readiness activities such as job readiness programs, volunteer work experience, and vocational education and training. A Welfare Avoidance Grant (WAG) may also be available to cover employment-related expenses such as transportation, temporary childcare, tools, and uniforms. Montgomery County residents may access the program at three local DHHS locations in Rockville, Silver Spring, and Germantown. Anne Arundel County residents may apply through the local DSS office or contact 410-269-4500.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income families with dependent children under 18 (or age 19 if graduating in the same calendar year) who have limited income and resources and need temporary financial support while working toward self-sufficiency. Includes U.S. citizens or qualified immigrants who meet income guidelines. Also includes individuals with disabilities who may require medical evaluation for work capacity determination. Available statewide, including Anne Arundel County residents who may apply through the local DSS office, and Montgomery County residents who may also apply through DHHS/OESS offices in Rockville, Silver Spring, and Germantown.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: General living expenses and household needs via EBT card or direct deposit; recipients can withdraw cash from ATMs or purchase goods at participating stores. Program also supports employment preparation through work readiness activities. A Welfare Avoidance Grant (WAG) may cover transportation, temporary childcare, tools, uniforms, and other employment-related expenses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Maryland resident. Available statewide. Apply online or at a local Department of Social Services office. Anne Arundel County residents may contact the local DSS office at 410-269-4500. Montgomery County residents may apply at three DHHS locations: Mid-County DHHS Building in Rockville, DHHS Silver Spring Center in Silver Spring, and Up-County Regional Services Center in Germantown.
requirements_list: Must have at least one child under 18 (or age 19 if graduating in the same calendar year) in the household
Must have dependent children
Must meet income guidelines based on household size — earned and unearned income cannot exceed the benefit level for the assistance unit size
Other resources and services must not fully meet the family's needs
Must have insufficient resources to meet family needs
Must meet financial and technical eligibility requirements
Must be a U.S. citizen or a non-citizen with 'qualified immigrant' status
Must have a face-to-face interview
Must pursue child support — provide information on non-custodial parents and cooperate with Child Support Enforcement; must apply for Child Support within 30 calendar days of application date
Must cooperate with substance abuse screening within 30 calendar days of application date
Must comply with substance abuse provisions
Must participate in work activities (job readiness, work experience, or vocational training) before case is approved
Participants must prepare for employment/independence through work
Must complete assigned work activity hours each week and provide weekly attendance verification
If previously received TCA for more than 6 months, must complete DHHS and Equus TCA Orientations and submit packets within 30 days of case approval
Proof of identity, Social Security number, proof of residence, proof of income, and proof of citizenship or immigration status required
If a 12-month disability is indicated, must apply for Social Security benefits, SSI, and/or Medicare and sign Interim Reimbursement Form 340 and Authorization to Represent Form (SSA-1696)
Medical evaluation (Form 500) may be required to assess work capacity and determine eligibility for individuals with disabilities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at MarylandBenefits.gov (benefits.maryland.gov), in person at a local Department of Social Services or DHS/OESS office, or by mail, fax, or other electronic means. Someone else may also drop off an application on your behalf. Applications must be signed by the head of household or authorized representative. Applicants must complete a face-to-face interview and begin work activities before the case is approved. A medical report (Form 500) completed by a health care provider may be required for applicants with disabilities. Anne Arundel County residents may apply through marylandbenefits.gov or contact the local DSS office at 410-269-4500. For Montgomery County: 1. View the DHHS Orientation video online and download the DHHS Orientation Packet. 2. Submit the completed packet by email to Employment.Services@MontgomeryCountyMD.gov or fax to 240-777-4166. 3. Apply for Child Support Enforcement Services through the DHS online portal at benefits.maryland.gov. 4. After DHHS orientation, register with Equus for the Work Program by emailing MDMontCoTANF@equusworks.com or calling 301-740-7700.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Temporary Disability Assistance Program (TDAP) provides short-term cash assistance to low-income, disabled Maryland residents between ages 18 and 64 who have no dependent children (or no children under 18 in the home) and no other resources. It helps individuals through a short-term disability or while awaiting approval of federal disability support such as Supplemental Security Income (SSI) or Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI). Spouse income in the household (except SSI benefits) is used to determine eligibility, and recipients must agree to reimburse the program from any SSI payment received. Benefits are limited to 12 months out of any 36-month period unless the recipient is actively pursuing SSI. The program is administered statewide by the Maryland Department of Human Services through Local Departments of Social Services, including in Anne Arundel County, Prince George's County, and Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Time-limited cash assistance provided to disabled, low-income adults ages 18–64 with no dependent children and no other resources while awaiting SSI/SSDI determination or managing a short-term disability. Benefits are limited to 12 months out of any 36-month period unless the recipient is actively pursuing SSI. Spouse's income (except SSI) is counted in eligibility determination, and recipients must agree to reimburse the program from any SSI payment received. Applications can be submitted online at MarylandBenefits.gov, by mail, fax, email, or in person at local DSS offices (e.g., Howard County DSS at 9780 Patuxent Woods Drive, Columbia, MD 21046, 8am–4:30pm, with interviews held Monday–Thursday; Anne Arundel County DSS at 410-269-4500). In Montgomery County, applications may also be faxed or emailed to the OESS office.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income, disabled Maryland residents ages 18–64 without dependent children and no other resources who are experiencing a short-term disability or awaiting federal disability (SSI/SSDI) approval, including individuals in Anne Arundel County, Prince George's County, and Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cash assistance for general living expenses and basic needs during a period of short-term disability or while the SSI/SSDI determination process is ongoing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland through Local Departments of Social Services, including Anne Arundel County, Prince George's County, and Montgomery County. Must be a Maryland resident and a U.S. citizen or legally admitted alien for permanent residency.
requirements_list: Must be a low-income Maryland resident
Must be a disabled adult between ages 18 and 64
Must have a disability (physical or mental) verified by a licensed medical practitioner (medical report required)
Must have no dependent children (no children under age 18 living in the home)
Must have no other resources
Cannot be working
Cannot have the capacity to work for at least 3 months
Cannot be receiving unemployment benefits
Applicants disabled for 12 months or more must file an application for Supplemental Security Income (SSI)
Must have a pending Supplemental Security Income (SSI) application if awaiting SSI determination
May be required to apply for SSI and SSDI
Must agree to reimbursement from any SSI payment received
Benefits limited to 12 months out of every 36-month period unless actively pursuing SSI
Must be a U.S. citizen or legally admitted alien for permanent residency
Spouse income is considered for eligibility (except SSI benefits)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at MarylandBenefits.gov (benefits.maryland.gov) or at mydhrbenefits.dhr.state.md.us, or submit an application in person, by mail, fax, email, or other electronic means at your Local Department of Social Services. In Howard County, apply at the DSS office at 9780 Patuxent Woods Drive, Columbia, MD 21046; applications can be dropped off at the front desk (8am–4:30pm) any day of the week, with interviews held Monday–Thursday. In Montgomery County, applications may be faxed or emailed to the OESS office, or mailed to any OESS office; applications must be signed by the head of household or authorized representative. Anne Arundel County residents may contact the local DSS office at 410-269-4500. Prince George's County residents may also contact their local DSS office for assistance.

structured_extraction.program_name: The County Alliance Program for Employment (CAPE)
structured_extraction.program_description: CAPE is a free job training and support program for non-custodial parents who owe child support in Washington County, Maryland. It helps unemployed or underemployed parents overcome barriers to employment and start careers in fields like welding, green construction, machining, healthcare, and hospitality. Participants who complete the program may earn forgiveness for child support arrears owed to the State of Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free job training in in-demand industries (welding, green construction, machining, healthcare, hospitality), soft skills training, job readiness and placement, industry-recognized certifications, work experience, transportation assistance, referrals to community services, help resolving barriers to employment (criminal record, legal services, driver's license suspension), access to work clothing and tools, and support from a personal career navigator and success coach. Participants who complete the program may earn forgiveness for child support arrears owed to the State of Maryland.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-custodial parents who have a child support case in Washington County and are unemployed or underemployed
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Job training, career development, and support services to help participants gain employment and make consistent child support payments
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must have a child support case in Washington County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a non-custodial party with a child support case in Washington County
Must complete an employability assessment covering employment status, skills, abilities, employment history, education, literacy, communication skills, and career interests
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Program Coordinator Bobbie Nave at 301-302-2404 or washington.cape@maryland.gov to start the enrollment process. Once enrolled, participants join a training program offered by one of the CAPE participating partners.

structured_extraction.program_description: TEFAP is a federal-state partnership that provides USDA-purchased foods and federal funds to eligible soup kitchens, food pantries, and shelters across all 24 Maryland jurisdictions. The Maryland Department of Human Services (DHS) administers the program in Maryland by contracting with the Maryland Food Bank and the Capital Area Food Bank to receive, store, and distribute food to eligible agencies and low-income individuals. Residents can find their nearest TEFAP distribution site by entering their zip code on the Maryland Food Bank or Capital Area Food Bank websites.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: USDA-purchased foods (such as canned fruits and vegetables, meat, dairy, grains, and dried beans) and federal administrative funds are distributed to eligible food pantries, soup kitchens, and shelters. Each state receives an allocation based on population, poverty, and unemployment rates. Eligible Recipient Agencies (ERAs) receive food at no cost, including delivery. Low-income individuals and families can also receive free food directly through local distribution sites. Individual eligibility is based on participation in SNAP, Medical Assistance, TANF, Unemployment Assistance, or Energy Assistance, OR household income at or below 185% of Federal Poverty Guidelines (e.g., $29,526 annually for a 1-person household; $103,082 for an 8-person household in FFY26). Residents outside Montgomery and Prince George's counties use mdfoodbank.org; those in Montgomery or Prince George's counties use capitalareafoodbank.org.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible food distribution agencies such as soup kitchens, food pantries, and shelters (including faith-based organizations, community development centers, senior living facilities, and other charitable institutions with tax-exempt status), as well as low-income individuals and families at or below 185% of Federal Poverty Guidelines, SNAP recipients, Medical Assistance recipients, TANF recipients, Unemployment recipients, Energy Assistance recipients, homeless populations, and homebound or disabled individuals.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Distribution of USDA foods (Entitlement and Bonus foods) to low-income individuals through eligible agencies for household consumption and prepared meals; administrative funds support ordering, receiving, tracking, storing, and distributing TEFAP foods; equipment purchases and facility operations for pantries, soup kitchens, and shelters.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in all 24 Maryland jurisdictions. Montgomery and Prince George's counties are served by the Capital Area Food Bank; all other 22 jurisdictions (including Baltimore City) are served by the Maryland Food Bank. Allocation to jurisdictions is based on poverty and unemployment rates.
requirements_list: Must be an eligible agency such as a soup kitchen, food pantry, or shelter (Eligible Recipient Agency or Emergency Feeding Organization)
Must maintain current, verified tax-exempt status (501(c)(3) or equivalent)
Must operate in one of Maryland's 24 jurisdictions
Must contract with either the Maryland Food Bank or the Capital Area Food Bank via a Memorandum of Agreement
Must comply with nondiscrimination policies and procedures and display nondiscrimination statement
Must attend annual Civil Rights training
Must maintain inventory management registers (FNS-155 form) and submit monthly inventory reports
Must use FIFO (First In, First Out) inventory system
Must store food at proper temperatures
Food cannot be sold, traded, bartered, or exchanged for cash
Must complete eligibility determinations prior to or at time of food distribution using the Maryland Self-Disclosure Form
Individual recipients must be Maryland residents

Individual recipients must meet one eligibility category: SNAP recipient, Medical Assistance recipient, TANF recipient, Unemployment recipient, or Energy Assistance recipient; OR household income at or below 185% of Federal Poverty Guidelines
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible agencies should contact the Maryland Food Bank (for most of Maryland) or the Capital Area Food Bank (for Montgomery and Prince George's counties) to participate and sign a Memorandum of Agreement. Agencies must complete required compliance documentation including Civil Rights training and monitoring forms. Individuals seeking food complete a Self-Disclosure Form indicating household size, location, and eligibility category at the point of food distribution. Individuals can find their nearest TEFAP provider at mdfoodbank.org/need-food/ or capitalareafoodbank.org/get-help/ by entering their zip code and the distance they can travel to get a list of nearby food programs including hours and contact information.

structured_extraction.program_description: Scholarship program covering 100% of tuition and mandatory fees for students pursuing credentials or degrees in targeted human services positions within the Maryland Department of Human Services. Includes an employment opportunity upon completion with state benefits such as pension, generous time off, and career advancement opportunities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Covers 100% of tuition and mandatory fees at eligible public Maryland higher education institutions. Recipients must fulfill a service obligation by working in targeted DHS positions (Child Support Series, Family Investment Specialist Series, Family Support Worker Series, Family Services Caseworker Series, Social Worker Series) for 15 months per academic year of scholarship receipt within 8 years. Targeted positions have salary ranges from $37,271 to $112,044 annually. Employment opportunity with #TeamDHS and state benefits included.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents or Maryland high school graduates; rising high school seniors and current higher education students accepted into or enrolled at public Maryland higher education institutions and seeking careers in human services positions with the Maryland Department of Human Services
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition and mandatory fees at eligible public higher education institutions in Maryland
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be Maryland residents or graduates of Maryland high schools enrolled at public Maryland higher education institutions. Employment must occur in Baltimore City, Baltimore County, or Prince George's County. Applicants should contact the Local Department of Social Services in their desired jurisdiction.
requirements_list: Maryland resident or Maryland high school graduate
Accepted into or enrolled at eligible public Maryland higher education institution
Pursuing credential or degree for targeted positions (Child Support Series, Family Investment Specialist Series, Family Support Worker Series, Family Services Caseworker Series, Social Worker Series)
Maintain minimum 2.5 cumulative GPA (4.0 scale)
Sign service obligation agreement with DHS to work in targeted positions for 15 months per academic year of scholarship receipt within 8 years
Educational requirements vary by position (high school diploma, AA, BA in related fields, or MSW with license)
Experience requirements vary by position level (ranging from no experience to 6+ years)
Interest in working for DHS in high-demand positions
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review eligibility requirements and scholarship flyer documents linked on the DHS initiatives page. Contact the Local Department of Social Services in your desired jurisdiction. Contact dhs.hscscholarship@maryland.gov or call (410) 767-3300 / (800) 974-0203 for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Transportation Assistance Program (TAP) provides reliable used vehicles to eligible low-income families and individuals across Maryland, especially those receiving Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) funds. The program aims to remove transportation barriers to employment and financial independence by giving families access to a car for two years or 24,000 miles, whichever comes first. Vehicles are provided through a network of partners across the state and can be used for commuting to work, accessing higher-paying jobs or shifts, shortening commutes, and other essential activities such as medical appointments, grocery shopping, and children's activities, ultimately improving overall quality of life.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides a reliable used vehicle to eligible low-income individuals and families for two years or 24,000 miles, whichever comes first, through a network of partners across the state, increasing mobility and access to employment opportunities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income individuals and families across Maryland, particularly recipients of Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) funds, who face transportation barriers to employment and financial independence.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Access to a reliable used vehicle for commuting to work, accessing higher-paying jobs or shifts, shortening commutes, and other essential activities such as medical appointments, grocery shopping, and children's activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through local departments of social services and the statewide TAP partner, Vehicles for Change.
requirements_list: Must be a low-income individual or family
Must be a recipient of or eligible for Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) funds or similar low-income assistance; TANF recipients are prioritized
Must need transportation assistance to get to work
Must face transportation barriers to employment
Must inquire through a local department of social services TAP Coordinator or contact Vehicles for Change
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local Department of Social Services TAP Coordinator to find out if you qualify for TAP, or reach out to the statewide TAP partner, Vehicles for Change, at vehiclesforchange.org/need-a-car/. You may also call 1-800-332-6347 or visit the program website for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: Protects low-income families in Maryland from having their utility service shut off during the heating season. All customers eligible for the Maryland Energy Assistance Program (MEAP) may participate. Participation requires year-round even monthly budget billing, which spreads annual utility costs into equal monthly payments. Missing consecutive payments may result in removal from the program. In Prince George's County, applications can be submitted online, by email, fax, mail, or in person at the local Department of Social Services office.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Prevents utility disconnection during the heating season for eligible low-income customers. Participants must enroll in year-round even monthly budget billing to spread annual utility costs into equal monthly payments. Missing consecutive payments may result in removal from the program. Applications accepted on a rolling basis, once per fiscal year (July–June).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling; apply at any time during the year, once per fiscal year (July–June)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income households in Maryland who are eligible for MEAP and at risk of utility shut-off during the heating season.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Protection from utility service disconnection/termination during the heating season.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be eligible for the Maryland Energy Assistance Program (MEAP)
Must participate in year-round even monthly budget billing
Must enroll in year-round even monthly budget billing
Must make consecutive monthly payments to remain enrolled
Consecutive missed payments may result in removal from the program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Office of Home Energy Programs via the Maryland Benefits portal at dhs.maryland.gov/office-of-home-energy-programs, online, or at a local OHEP office. Alternatively, contact your utility provider at the number on your bill, or visit the PSC website at www.psc.state.md.us for utility contact information. In Prince George's County, applications may also be submitted by email to pgcdss.energy@maryland.gov with completed application and supporting documents, by fax to 301-909-6331, by mail to Prince George's County Department of Social Services, 805 Brightseat Road, Landover, MD 20785, or in person at 425 Brightseat Road, Landover, MD 20785.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Winning Fathers Program helps noncustodial and incarcerated fathers in Baltimore County prepare for employment and re-enter the workforce so they can support their children financially. The program provides job readiness classes, soft skills development, and connections to employment and community resources. It serves both unemployed or underemployed noncustodial fathers and incarcerated fathers at the Baltimore County Men's Detention Center, helping participants obtain and maintain jobs, pay child support, and build a more stable future for their families.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive job readiness workshops, resume writing assistance, cover letter writing, interview techniques, background and credit check guidance, employment law education, legal resources, federal bonding information, expungement help, and soft skills training (communication, time management, problem solving, anger management). A full-time Job Developer and two full-time Social Workers support participants as they transition from incarceration back into the community or from unemployment into stable employment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Unemployed or underemployed noncustodial fathers in Baltimore County, as well as incarcerated fathers at the Baltimore County Men's Detention Center who have at least 120 days remaining on their sentence and have a court-ordered child support obligation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Employment preparation, job readiness training, soft skills development, employment connections, and transition support services to help fathers obtain and maintain jobs and pay child support.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County, Maryland. Incarcerated participants must be held at the Baltimore County Men's Detention Center in Towson, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a noncustodial father in Baltimore County who is unemployed or underemployed, OR an incarcerated father held at the Baltimore County Men's Detention Center
Must have a minimum of 120 days remaining on sentence (for incarcerated participants)
Must have a court-ordered child support obligation
Must possess a positive attitude and eagerness to improve
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact one of the Program Coordinators — Jan Uehlinger at 410-853-3868 or Aimee Bollinger at 410-853-3591 — or call the DHS helpline at 1-800-332-6347 for enrollment information.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Young Fathers Employment Program helps noncustodial parents in Baltimore County, Caroline County, and Talbot County become more financially, emotionally, and physically supportive of their children. The program provides job readiness training, employment development, life skills counseling, and job placement assistance. It also offers parenting skill development, relationship mediation, and connects participants with legal and social services through community partners, helping them obtain and maintain employment so they can pay child support and support their families.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: No-cost employment training and career preparation, job placement and retention assistance, life skills counseling, parenting classes, case management, and referrals to legal services (housing, foreclosure assistance, family law, debt assistance) through program partners. Serves noncustodial parents in Baltimore County, Caroline County, and Talbot County.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Young unemployed or underemployed noncustodial parents in Baltimore County, Caroline County, and Talbot County who have a child support case and can commit to working upon program completion.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Job training, employment development, life skills counseling, parenting classes, and legal services referrals to help noncustodial parents support their families and pay child support.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County, Caroline County, and Talbot County, Maryland. Participants must have a child support case in one of these counties.
requirements_list: Must have a Talbot County child support case
Must be unemployed or underemployed
Must be able to commit to working upon program completion
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the program coordinator Isaiah Greene at 410-819-4471 or isaiah.green@maryland.gov, or Lori Keel at lori.keel@maryland.gov to start the enrollment process.

structured_extraction.program_name: Active Duty Military Servicemember or Spouse License Recognition Application
structured_extraction.program_description: Active duty military servicemembers or their spouses who hold an occupational license in good standing in another state can have that license recognized as valid in Maryland at a similar scope of practice. This allows them to practice their licensed profession in Maryland without obtaining a permanent Maryland license, for as long as their military orders require them to be stationed in Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Applicants receive an official letter of recognition allowing them to practice their licensed profession in Maryland without obtaining a full Maryland license. There is no fee for this application. The recognition is valid for the duration of the military placement in Maryland.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Active duty military servicemembers and their spouses who hold an occupational license in good standing in another U.S. state or territory and have been ordered to be stationed in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Allows the holder to practice their licensed occupation in Maryland without obtaining a permanent Maryland license for the duration of their military orders.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicant must reside in Maryland as their primary residence as a result of military orders assigning duty station in Maryland.
requirements_list: You or your spouse is an active duty military servicemember (Army, Navy, Air Force, Marine Corps, Space Force, Coast Guard, NOAA commissioned corps, or Public Health Service commissioned corps)
You reside in Maryland as your primary residence due to military orders
You hold an occupational license in good standing issued by a U.S. state or territorial licensing authority in a similar scope of practice
Your license must be maintained in good standing in its original jurisdiction for the duration of the military orders
You have used your occupational license in the two years immediately preceding the order to relocate to Maryland
License must be for one of the recognized boards or programs under the Maryland Division of Occupational and Professional Licensing
Comply with Maryland laws, regulations, and discipline guidelines
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete the application form from the Division's website. Save the PDF to your computer before filling it out. Submit the completed application along with: verification of active licenses from original licensing authority, military orders assigning duty station in Maryland, marriage certificate (if military spouse), and proof of residence in Maryland. If additional documents are required for your specific license type, a board representative will contact you. Review Maryland laws and regulations before submitting, as you will be subject to Maryland standards of practice, ethics, and continuing education requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides adult Maryland residents aged 18 and older with instruction in basic reading, math, and writing skills, English language acquisition, GED test preparation, workforce readiness, career pathways, and family literacy. Adults can also earn a Maryland High School Diploma through three pathways: GED testing, the National External Diploma Program (NEDP), or the Adult High School Program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free classes and instruction available in all Maryland counties and Baltimore City. Services include basic academic skills, adult secondary education, English language acquisition, integrated English literacy and civics, workforce preparation, career pathways, integrated education and training, and family literacy. Adults can pursue a Maryland High School Diploma through GED testing, the National External Diploma Program, or the Adult High School Program. Funding is provided through the federal Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act (WIOA) in partnership with the state.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adult Maryland residents aged 18 and older who are not currently enrolled in high school and want to improve basic skills, learn English, prepare for the GED, or earn a high school diploma.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Instruction in basic academic skills, English language learning, GED preparation, and workforce readiness; high school diploma attainment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in all Maryland counties and Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Must be 18 years of age or older
Must not be currently enrolled in high school
Must be a Maryland resident
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the classes page on the Maryland Department of Labor website to find classes in your area, then enroll directly.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that allows adults 21 and older who did not graduate from high school to earn a Maryland High School Diploma. Participants complete coursework aligned with Maryland graduation requirements and may also earn industry-recognized credentials or post-secondary credit.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free adult high school education leading to a Maryland High School Diploma. Program provides academic coursework, postsecondary education and training opportunities, industry-recognized credentialing, and wraparound support services. Currently offered at two locations in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults 21 years of age or older who reside in Maryland and have not earned a high school diploma or equivalent (GED or National External Diploma Program).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable — program provides direct educational services, not funds.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must reside in the State of Maryland. Current school locations are in Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Must be 21 years of age or older
Must reside in the State of Maryland
Cannot already have a Maryland High School Diploma
Cannot have completed high school graduation requirements through the GED Test or the National External Diploma Program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact one of the two adult high schools directly to get more information or to enroll: South Baltimore Adult High School (contact Sharée Turner at 443-682-9403) or The Excel Center (contact Sherry DeFrancisci at 443-870-5050).

structured_extraction.program_name: Continuation Grant for Consolidated Adult Education & Family Literacy Services
structured_extraction.program_description: A continuation grant that funds adult education and family literacy services across Maryland. Recipients use the funds to deliver adult education and literacy programs to residents.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Continuation grant funding for organizations that provide consolidated adult education and family literacy services.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: FY 27 grant will be released in April 2027
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations that provide adult education and family literacy services in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Delivery of adult education and family literacy programs and services
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Email [email protected] for information and documents related to the FY 26 grant. The FY 27 grant will be released in April 2027.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides academic and workforce development education to incarcerated individuals in Maryland state correctional institutions. Offers instruction in reading, math, social studies, and science from basic literacy through adult secondary levels, as well as occupational training programs and library services, to help inmates successfully re-enter the workforce and community upon release.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free academic instruction (reading, math, social studies, science), occupational/career training, and library services provided to eligible incarcerated individuals in Maryland state correctional facilities. Inmates without a GED or high school diploma who have at least 18 months remaining on their sentence are required by law to participate unless exempt due to a medical, developmental, or learning disability. After earning a high school diploma, participants may pursue occupational programs or college courses through partnering institutions.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Incarcerated individuals in Maryland Division of Public Safety and Correctional Services (DPSCS) state institutions, Patuxent Institution, Metropolitan Transition Center, and pre-release units
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Academic education (literacy through adult secondary), occupational/career training, and library services to support workforce re-entry upon release
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at all DPSCS state institutions, Patuxent Institution, Metropolitan Transition Center, and all pre-release units in Maryland
requirements_list: Must be incarcerated in a Maryland DPSCS state institution, Patuxent Institution, Metropolitan Transition Center, or pre-release unit
Mandatory participation if individual lacks a GED or high school diploma, has at least 18 months remaining on their sentence, and is not exempt due to a medical, developmental, or learning disability
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Enrollment is administered through the correctional institution; eligible inmates are mandated to participate or may enroll voluntarily in available programs.

structured_extraction.program_description: EARN Maryland (Employment Advancement Right Now) is a statewide workforce training initiative that funds industry-led partnerships to provide job training and career advancement opportunities for workers and job seekers in Maryland. The program connects employers, educational institutions, and community organizations to develop and deliver sector-based training programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State grants fund industry-led workforce training partnerships. For every $1 of state funding invested, an additional $18.16 in economic impact is created. As of October 2024, more than 25,000 Marylanders have been positively impacted, more than 15,000 incumbent workers have received training and credentials, and nearly 11,000 individuals have obtained employment through the program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Industry-led partnerships including employers, educational institutions, and community organizations seeking to provide workforce training; also job seekers and incumbent workers in Maryland seeking training and employment.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Workforce training programs that help workers gain new credentials, certifications, and skills, and help job seekers obtain employment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be an industry-led partnership
Partners may include employers, educational institutions, non-profits, and government entities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the EARN Maryland website to find job training programs near you or learn about partnership grant opportunities.

structured_extraction.program_name: Expedited Occupational and Professional Licensing for Military Veterans and Families (Veterans Full Employment Act of 2013)
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland law (Veterans Full Employment Act of 2013) requires licensing boards and units to help veterans, active duty service members, and their spouses and surviving spouses obtain occupational and professional licenses in Maryland faster. Eligible applicants who hold a valid license in good standing in another state can receive their Maryland license within 60 days of submitting a completed application with all required supporting documents (or within 15 business days for certain health occupation boards). The program also authorizes temporary expedited licenses valid up to 6 months, grants credit for relevant military training, education, and experience toward licensure requirements, waives continuing education requirements for deployed service members, and assigns advisors to assist applicants through the process. It applies across multiple sectors including health occupations, business regulation, education, and financial institutions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Expedited processing of occupational and professional license applications. Eligible applicants receive a Maryland license within 60 days of submitting a completed application with all required supporting documents (certain health occupation boards must issue licenses within 15 business days). Temporary licenses are available, valid until the earlier of 6 months after issuance or the date a permanent license is granted or denied. Additional benefits include: credit for all relevant military experience toward years-of-practice requirements; credit for military training and education toward training/education requirements if substantially equivalent; assignment of board advisors to assist with the application process; assistance identifying education/training programs if requirements are not yet met; waiver of penalties and reinstatement fees for late renewals due to deployment; and expedited educator certification and academic credit for military training at higher education institutions.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Veterans must apply within one year of discharge or separation. Surviving spouses of service members must apply within one year of the service member's death. Surviving spouses of veterans must apply within one year of the veteran's honorable discharge or separation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Military veterans (honorably or otherwise non-dishonorably discharged), active duty service members (including Reserve Components and National Guard) assigned to a Maryland duty station or with established legal residence in Maryland, spouses of active duty service members, spouses of veterans or service members, and surviving spouses of deceased service members — who hold a valid occupational or professional license in good standing in another state.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Obtaining an occupational or professional license in Maryland through expedited processing, including temporary licenses, credit for military training and experience, and waiver of certain requirements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Active duty service members and their spouses must be assigned to a duty station located in Maryland or have established legal residence in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must hold a valid license, certificate, or registration in good standing from another state with substantially equivalent or exceeding requirements

Must be a veteran honorably or otherwise non-dishonorably discharged from the U.S. Armed Forces, an active duty service member or reservist/National Guard member assigned to a Maryland duty station or with established legal residence in Maryland, a spouse of such a service member or veteran, or a surviving spouse of a deceased service member
Veterans must apply within one year of discharge or separation
Surviving spouses of service members must apply within one year of the service member's death
Surviving spouses of veterans must apply within one year of the veteran's honorable discharge or separation

Must submit supporting documents: DD Form 214 (veterans and surviving spouses), military orders (active duty and their spouses), marriage certificate (spouses and surviving spouses), death certificate (surviving spouses), and proof of residence (all applicants)
Must alert the board/commission at time of application that you qualify as a service member, veteran, or military spouse
Criminal background check application (if required by the licensing unit)
Submission of full permanent license application (when seeking temporary license)
Payment of any required application fees
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the relevant licensing board or commission through its website or visit its licensing applications page. Submit an application for the specific license needed. Notify the board that you qualify as a veteran, active service member, or military spouse. Include all required supporting documents (e.g., DD Form 214, military orders, marriage certificate, death certificate, proof of residence as applicable). For a temporary license, also submit a full permanent license application and any required criminal background check. Veterans must apply within one year of discharge; current service members and military spouses may apply when assigned to a Maryland duty station or upon establishing legal residence in Maryland. Board advisors may be assigned to assist with the process. Direct follow-up inquiries to the board/commission or call 410-230-6221.

structured_extraction.program_description: ARPA-funded initiative providing up to $15 million to support employers working on infrastructure projects throughout Maryland. Designed to help employers attract and retain workers by addressing barriers to workforce participation and retention. Employers can use funds to create Employee Support Programs (such as transportation, housing, and child care assistance) and Payroll Incentives (such as signing bonuses, retention bonuses, and wages during training) to improve employee recruitment, training, and retention. Maximum total benefit per employee is $10,000.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants to employers to fund Employee Support Programs (e.g., transportation assistance, housing/rental assistance, child and dependent care) and Payroll Incentives (e.g., signing bonuses, retention bonuses, wages during training). Maximum total benefit per employee is $10,000. The grant gives employers flexibility to design programs that best meet their employees' needs.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis until funds exhausted; all funds must be spent by December 1, 2024
structured_extraction.contact_name: Erin Roth (Deputy Assistant Secretary); Heather Evans (Jobs that Build Project Manager)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland-based employers with difficulty hiring/retaining employees for construction and infrastructure maintenance work
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Employee support programs (transportation assistance, housing/rental assistance, child and dependent care) and payroll incentives (signing bonuses, retention bonuses, wages during training)
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland-based businesses with employees working on Maryland infrastructure projects
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Maryland-based employer negatively impacted by COVID-19
Must have employees currently working or beginning work on an infrastructure contract by 01/01/2024
Employees must be full-time, Maryland-based, and working on infrastructure projects
Ineligible positions include executive-level, superintendent, foreman, site supervisor, and controller
Must be in good standing with MD Comptroller
Must not owe outstanding unemployment or other taxes
Must have Certificate of Good Standing from State Department of Assessments and Taxation
Proposed program must include elements of Employee Support Programs, Payroll Incentives, or both
Application must identify benefits provided, how employees will access and be approved for benefits, and benefit amounts per employee
Program design should involve human resources, payroll, and accounting staff
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Employers submitted a grant application identifying the proposed program, benefit types, employee eligibility criteria, and benefit amounts. Applications were accepted on a rolling basis until funds were exhausted. Check the program website for updates.

structured_extraction.program_name: Living Wage for State Service Contracts
structured_extraction.program_description: This program requires contractors and subcontractors to pay a living wage to employees who perform work on certain state service contracts worth more than $100,000. It ensures workers doing direct, measurable work under qualifying state contracts receive at least the required living wage rate set by Maryland law. General contractors must also certify and post notices informing covered employees about wage requirements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Contractors and subcontractors with state service contracts over $100,000 are required to pay employees a minimum living wage rate. The program sets wage floors and enforces compliance. General contractors must post a 'Notice to Employees' at the worksite in English, Spanish, and any other language commonly used by employees, and certify this posting prior to contract execution. Employees who believe their employer is not paying the required amount can file a confidential complaint.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Employees working under state service contracts over $100,000 and the contractors/subcontractors who employ them.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Wage payments to employees performing direct, measurable work on qualifying state service contracts.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — applies to all state service contracts in Maryland over $100,000.
requirements_list: Contractor or subcontractor must have a state service contract in excess of $100,000
Employee must perform direct, measurable work under the covered contract
Worker must provide personal and employment information including rate of pay and employment dates
Claim must be made under penalties of perjury
Full-time employment status and consecutive weeks of work on project may be required
General contractors must certify that 'Notice to Employees' will be posted conspicuously at worksite
Posting must be in English, Spanish, and any other language commonly used by employees
Signed certification must be returned to Commissioner prior to contract execution
Certain exemptions apply as defined in the Living Wage Law
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Employees who believe their employer is not paying the required living wage can file a confidential complaint using the Living Wage Complaint Form available on the program page or by calling 410-767-2232. The form requires worker details, employment dates, employer information, contract value, and wage information, submitted under penalties of perjury. General contractors must sign a certification form and return it to the Department of Labor prior to contract execution.

structured_extraction.program_name: MOSH Free Safety and Health Seminars
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Occupational Safety and Health (MOSH) offers free educational seminars for Maryland employers and employees. The program is designed to reduce occupational injuries and illnesses through education. Participants can enroll in half-day, full-day, and two-day seminars at no cost.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free half-day, full-day, and two-day safety and health seminars available to Maryland employers and employees at no cost.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland employers and employees seeking safety and health education to reduce workplace injuries and illnesses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Safety and health education and training to reduce occupational injuries and illnesses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to employers and employees across Maryland.
requirements_list: Registration required through the MOSH online registration system
Not available to meet formal training requirements mandated by MOSH safety and health standards
Not available to comply with training time requirements of specific MOSH standards
Not available for specific work processes or equipment operations such as scaffolds and cranes
Not available as part of an informal conference or for abatement of a citation
Not available to employees of fee-charging consultants
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register online at https://ezregister.com/promoters/5674/

structured_extraction.program_description: A program from the Maryland Department of Labor that helps learners who have passed three of their four GED® tests finish their Maryland High School Diploma. It provides short-term financial assistance to cover the costs of preparation classes, tutoring, practice tests, and the fourth and final GED® exam.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Short-term financial assistance to cover costs of GED® preparation classes, tutoring, practice tests, and the fourth and final GED® exam module for eligible learners who have already passed three of the four GED® tests.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults in Maryland who have passed three of the four GED® test modules and need help with costs to complete their Maryland High School Diploma.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: GED® preparation classes, tutoring, practice tests, and the fourth and final GED® exam fee.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to Maryland residents.
requirements_list: Must have passed exactly three of the four GED® test modules
Must need assistance with costs of practice tests and/or exam fees
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online through the Maryland Department of Labor Adult Education website. A link to apply is available on the program page.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Access to Banking Act – Assessment Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: Offers an annual assessment credit to Maryland state-chartered banks and credit unions that open new branches or maintain existing branches in low-to-moderate income (LMI) communities. The credit reduces the annual regulatory assessment fee paid by these depository institutions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A credit against the annual regulatory assessment fee charged to Maryland state-chartered banks and credit unions. The credit is earned by establishing new (de novo) branches or retaining existing branches in LMI communities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland state-chartered banks and credit unions operating or planning to operate branches in low-to-moderate income communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of annual regulatory assessment fees for depository institutions in LMI communities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to Maryland state-chartered banks and credit unions with branches in low-to-moderate income communities.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland state-chartered bank or credit union
Must operate a new (de novo) branch or retain an existing branch in a low-to-moderate income (LMI) community
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Subscribe to OFR emails for updates on how to apply for and earn the assessment credit. Applications should be sent via email to finreg.licensing@maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state-seeded venture fund that invests in financial technology (fintech) firms developing innovative products to expand access to capital, funding, and financial services for small businesses in low-to-moderate income (LMI) communities. The fund also makes these innovations available to Maryland state-chartered banks and credit unions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The MCIV Fund is seeded with up to $2,500,000 in initial equity capital from OFR's Banking Institution and Credit Union Regulation Fund. Through June 30, 2028, the Commissioner may match investments made by Maryland state-chartered banks or credit unions in an amount equal to the assessment credit earned by that institution. The fund invests in and partners with fintech firms and makes resulting innovations available to Maryland state-chartered depository institutions.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Fintech firms developing financial products and innovations to serve LMI communities, and Maryland state-chartered banks and credit unions interested in participating in the fund.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Investment in fintech tools and innovations that enhance access to capital, funding, and financial services for small businesses in low-to-moderate income communities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to Maryland state-chartered depository institutions and fintech firms serving LMI communities in Maryland.
requirements_list: Fintech firms must be developing financial products and innovations that enhance access to capital, funding, and financial services for small businesses in LMI communities
Maryland state-chartered banks and credit unions may participate by investing in the MCIV Fund
Matching investment by the Commissioner available through June 30, 2028
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Subscribe to OFR emails for updates regarding next steps, eligibility criteria, and the application process. Applications should be sent via email to finreg.licensing@maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Maryland state subsidy that reduces the cost of GED® test modules for Maryland residents. Test takers apply a discount code at registration to lower the per-module test fee for their first attempt at each module.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A discount code (MDGED2175) reduces the cost of each GED® module from $36.00 to $14.25 per module for the first attempt, applicable to both in-person and Online Proctored (OP) testing.
structured_extraction.program_audience: All Maryland residents taking the GED® test for the first time on each module.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of GED® test module registration fees.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to all Maryland GED® test takers statewide.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident
Discount applies to the first attempt of each module only
Must apply the discount code MDGED2175 at registration
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply the Maryland Subsidy Discount Code (MDGED2175) when registering for GED® test modules through the GED Testing Service website.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Healthy Working Families Act (Sick and Safe Leave)
structured_extraction.program_description: Requires all employers with employees whose primary work location is in Maryland to provide earned sick and safe leave. Employers with 15 or more employees must provide paid leave; employers with fewer than 15 employees must provide unpaid leave. Leave accrues at one hour for every 30 hours worked.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Employees accrue sick and safe leave at a rate of one hour per every 30 hours worked. Employers with 15 or more employees must provide paid leave; those with fewer than 15 employees must provide unpaid leave. Leave is the minimum entitlement — employers may provide more.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Employees whose primary work location is in Maryland, and employers subject to Maryland law
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Earned sick and safe leave for qualifying employees
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to all employees whose primary work location is in Maryland, regardless of where the employer is located
requirements_list: Employee's primary work location must be in Maryland
Leave accrues at one hour per 30 hours worked

Employees are not entitled to accrue leave during a 2-week pay period in which fewer than 24 total hours were worked; a 1-week pay period if fewer than a combined 24 hours were worked in the current and immediately preceding pay period; or a twice-monthly pay period in which fewer than 26 hours were worked
Certain employees are exempt from coverage under the law
Employers with 15 or more employees must provide paid leave; employers with fewer than 15 employees must provide unpaid leave
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: This is a statutory requirement, not an application-based program. Employers must comply automatically; employees accrue leave based on hours worked.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Home Improvement Commission (MHIC) Guaranty Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: The MHIC Guaranty Fund compensates homeowners for actual monetary losses caused by poor workmanship or a licensed contractor's failure to perform a home improvement contract. The Fund is supported by assessments paid by licensed home improvement contractors when they obtain or renew their license.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Homeowners can recover up to $30,000 (the amount paid to the contractor) for losses due to poor workmanship or contractor failure to perform. If total claims against a single contractor exceed $250,000, each homeowner's award is pro-rated. The Fund only applies to work done by MHIC-licensed contractors.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland homeowners who suffered financial losses due to poor workmanship or non-performance by a licensed home improvement contractor
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Compensation for actual monetary losses resulting from a licensed contractor's poor workmanship or failure to complete a home improvement contract
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — available to homeowners throughout Maryland where work was performed by an MHIC-licensed contractor
requirements_list: Work must have been performed by an MHIC-licensed contractor
Claim must be filed with the Commission within the applicable deadline
Loss must result from poor workmanship or contractor's failure to perform the home improvement contract
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a claim form to the MHIC. Obtain a claim form by emailing [email protected], calling 410-230-6231, or writing to MHIC, 100 S. Charles Street, Tower I, Baltimore, MD 21201.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Unemployment Insurance program provides temporary financial assistance to eligible workers and residents who are unemployed through no fault of their own while they search for new work.
