Eligible claimants can receive weekly benefit payments ranging from $50 to $430 for up to 26 weeks (6 months). The exact amount depends on prior wages and other factors such as severance received. Benefits are administered through the BEACON online portal and require weekly certification and documented job search activities. The program also establishes rates and collects taxes from Maryland employers to finance benefits, and conducts appeals for claimants and employers when disputes arise.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Weekly payments ranging from $50 to $430 for up to 26 weeks (6 months). The exact amount depends on prior wages and other factors such as severance received. Claimants must certify their eligibility each week and document at least 3 job search activities per week to continue receiving benefits.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applicant must file as soon as possible upon separation from employment
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland workers and residents who are unemployed through no fault of their own, including laid-off employees, former federal civilian employees, military members, and federal workers on furlough.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Temporary income support while unemployed and actively seeking new work. Funds provide financial assistance for living expenses during unemployment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Federal employees whose last duty station was in Maryland, or Maryland residents whose last duty station was outside the US, may also apply.
requirements_list: Must be unemployed through no fault of your own
Must be ready and available to work normal hours without restrictions
Must have earned at least $1,176.01 in one quarter and a minimum of $1,800 over at least two quarters during the 18-month base period
Must actively seek work and document at least 3 job search activities per week
Must register with the Maryland Workforce Exchange System
Must complete a weekly certification each week to continue receiving benefits
Must meet eligibility criteria for qualifying for benefits
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Check if you qualify. Step 2: Gather required documents including Social Security number, 18-month employment history, and any separation documents. Step 3: File a claim online at the Maryland Unemployment Insurance Portal (BEACON) at beacon.labor.maryland.gov or by calling 667-207-6520 Monday through Friday 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. Step 4: Register with the Maryland Workforce Exchange and document weekly job search activities (at least 3 per week). Step 5: Complete a weekly certification each Sunday online or by phone to continue receiving benefits.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's American Job Centers (AJCs) are located in every Maryland county and Baltimore City. They provide free employment-related services to job seekers and businesses, including career exploration, résumé preparation, job placement, training referrals, workshops, and business recruitment and retention support.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free services for job seekers include career exploration assistance, referrals to training programs, placement services, résumé preparation, and job-seeking workshops. Computers, printers, copiers, fax machines, and phones are available. Free services for businesses include recruitment support, retention strategies, and access to state workforce resources.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Job seekers and businesses throughout Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Career exploration, job placement, training referrals, résumé preparation, and business workforce development
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in all 24 Maryland jurisdictions (23 counties and Baltimore City)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the American Job Center nearest you by selecting your county from the directory on the page. No application required — services are free and open to job seekers and businesses.

structured_extraction.program_description: POAC provides free career and job search support to professionals, executives, technical workers, managers, and scientists who are looking for work. Services include access to a computer lab, written resources and publications, individualized career guidance, free copying, networking events, job postings, and career management information and program announcements. Staff are experienced in helping job seekers from a wide range of professional fields navigate career transitions and find new employment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free career guidance, computer lab access, written publications and resource materials, copying services, networking events, job postings, and career management information. All services are provided at no cost to Maryland residents.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Professionals, executives, technical workers, managers, and scientists seeking employment and career transition support.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Career transition support, networking, job placement assistance, career guidance, and access to job search resources.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Located at 1306 Concourse Drive, Suite 340, Linthicum, MD 21090; available to Maryland residents statewide.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident
Must be in professional, executive, technical, managerial, or scientific occupations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the center at 1306 Concourse Drive, Suite 340, Linthicum, MD 21090, contact via email or phone, or subscribe to the mailing list to receive information on events and programs.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grant funding to eligible organizations to help cover the costs of butchering and processing deer that hunters donate to food assistance programs serving low-income individuals and the homeless in Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $25,000 are available on a first-come, first-served basis and may be split among applicants. Funds may only be used to pay for butchering and processing donated deer, at a maximum rate of $60 per deer when grant funds are used. Administrative costs are not eligible for reimbursement.
structured_extraction.program_audience: County governments, municipal corporations, and 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations that operate or administer programs providing food or nutritional support to low-income individuals or the homeless in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Butchering and processing costs for donated deer. Administrative costs are not eligible. Maximum reimbursement is $60 per deer.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Applicants indicate specific county or counties where their venison donation program will be active. Deer must be hunted in compliance with Maryland State hunting laws and regulations.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a county government, municipal corporation, or a 501(c)(3) tax-exempt organization
Deer must be hunted in compliance with State hunting laws and regulations
Deer must be donated to a program that provides nutritional support or food for low-income individuals or the homeless
Deer must have a dressed weight of at least 50 pounds
Maximum reimbursement of $60 per deer for butchering and processing
Grantees must identify and contract with processors and coordinate venison distribution
Quarterly reports required including DNR hunting confirmation numbers, processor names and deer counts, amounts paid per deer, pounds of venison distributed, and list of recipient organizations
Maximum grant amount of $25,000; funds available on first-come, first-served basis
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the application form and submit it electronically to Brian Eyler at brian.eyler@maryland.gov by 11:59 pm on June 16, 2025.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide poster contest for 5th grade classes in Maryland, sponsored by the Maryland Forest Service and the Maryland Forest Conservancy District Boards. Students create posters on the theme 'Trees Are Terrific…and Color Our World!' and compete at the county and statewide level. Winners receive tree plantings at their school along with Smokey Bear prize packs. All participating classrooms receive Smokey Bear prize packs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Statewide winners receive tree plantings at their school: 1st place receives 15 trees and a Smokey Bear Prize Pack, 2nd place receives 10 trees and a Smokey Bear Prize Pack, and 3rd place receives 5 trees and a Smokey Bear Prize Pack. All participating classrooms receive a Smokey Bear prize pack.
structured_extraction.program_audience: 5th grade students and classes (public and private schools) and their teachers throughout Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tree plantings at winning schools.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Open to 5th grade classes statewide throughout Maryland, in all 24 Maryland counties.
requirements_list: Open to 5th grade classes only
Poster theme must be 'Trees Are Terrific…and Color Our World!' and must appear on the poster spelled correctly
Original artwork only; student may enter only once
Acceptable media: marker, crayon, paint pens, watercolor, ink, acrylic, colored/regular pencil, tempera paint
Computer or photo-generated art not acceptable
No commercial product, company, or organization names displayed
Poster size: minimum 8.5" x 11", maximum 22" x 28"
No matting
A signed Release Form must be filled out and attached to the back of every poster entry using scotch tape only
All information on the release form is required and must be printed clearly
Parent/guardian signature required on release form
Student signature required on release form
Posters must be submitted to the local county MD Forest Service Office by 12:00 p.m. on April 1, 2026
Posters are judged at the county level; county winners advance to statewide competition judged by the Maryland Urban and Community Forestry Committee (MUCFC)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Students create an original poster following the contest rules. The completed poster with a signed Release Form attached to the back with scotch tape must be dropped off at the local county MD Forest Service office by 12:00 p.m. on April 1, 2026. Staff may arrange pickup if needed. County-level winners are submitted to the statewide competition judged by the Maryland Urban and Community Forestry Committee. Winners' teachers are notified directly in late April 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: An annual grant of up to $5,000 awarded to a local Maryland land trust on behalf of an individual who has demonstrated outstanding leadership, partnership, and/or innovation in a conservation project or organizational development. The grant honors the late Aileen Hughes, a leader in the conservation movement. Funding is directed to the land trust, not the individual.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual grant of up to $5,000 awarded to a local Maryland land trust on behalf of an individual who has demonstrated outstanding leadership, partnership, and/or innovation in a conservation project or organizational development. Funding is directed to the land trust, not the individual.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland land trusts and land conservation organizations nominating an individual who has shown outstanding leadership, partnership, or innovation in conservation or organizational development.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Support local land trust programming, conservation projects, or land trust organizational development on behalf of the recognized individual.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to local land trusts in Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local land trust in Maryland
Grant is awarded to the land trust on behalf of an individual, not directly to the individual
Individual must have demonstrated outstanding leadership, partnership, and/or innovation in a conservation project or organizational development
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Keep Maryland Beautiful grant portal at cbtrust.org/grants/keep-maryland-beautiful/.

structured_extraction.program_name: American Tree Farm System (ATFS) in Maryland
structured_extraction.program_description: The American Tree Farm System (ATFS) is a national certification program for private forest landowners who sustainably manage their woodlands. It recognizes and certifies landowners who protect wildlife habitat, watersheds, and soil while producing wood products and committing to sustainable forest management. Landowners with 10 or more acres of forested land and a written forest management plan can become certified Tree Farmers at no cost, gaining professional recognition, free periodic consultations with a certified professional forester on a five-year cycle, access to forestry resources, and updates on legislative issues affecting forest landowners. Currently, 964 Tree Farmers (757 certified) with nearly 110,000 acres are enrolled in Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free certification as a sustainably managed Tree Farm with no cost to join. Benefits include: free periodic land inspections and consultations with a certified professional forester on a five-year cycle; information on legislative issues affecting forest landowners; participation in national and state Tree Farmer of the Year contests; the right to display the Tree Farm sign and certificate; and access to woodland resources and management tools.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private forest landowners in Maryland who own 10 or more acres of forested land and have, or are willing to develop, a written forest management plan and are committed to sustainable forestry practices.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Program provides certification, technical assistance, and professional forester consultations for sustainable forest management — not a grant or loan program. No funds are disbursed.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to private forest landowners throughout Maryland. Currently 964 Tree Farmers (757 certified) with nearly 110,000 acres enrolled in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must own 10 or more acres of forested land
Must have a written and implemented forest management plan covering forest products, water quality, wildlife habitat, soil conservation, biodiversity, and recreation

Must meet the ATFS Standards of Sustainability, including commitment to sustainable forestry, legal compliance, reforestation, air/water/soil protection, fish/wildlife/biodiversity conservation, forest aesthetics, protection of special sites, and harvests conducted per a management plan
Must participate in inspections with an ATFS-certified volunteer tree farm inspector on a five-year cycle
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local Maryland Forest Service office to determine if your property qualifies. If eligible, a free inspection of your land can be arranged by contacting a certified inspecting forester in your area. You can also visit the American Tree Farm System website for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: Free fishing education program that teaches new and existing anglers fishing skills and techniques. Offers events ranging from beginner to advanced levels for both youth and adults, including learn-to-fish workshops, lure crafting, fly fishing instruction, and fishing demonstrations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free in-person fishing education events and workshops held at libraries, parks, and community venues across Maryland. Topics include learn-to-fish basics, lure crafting, fly fishing, and fish filleting demonstrations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: New and existing anglers of all ages, including youth and adults
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Learning fishing skills and techniques
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Events held at various locations across Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register for individual events through the links provided in the event schedule. Check the program page for updated event listings.

structured_extraction.program_description: Allows shellfish aquaculture leaseholders to transfer their lease to a new party, add a co-leaseholder, or remove an existing co-leaseholder. This process is used to end lease operations by transferring to another party, ensure lease continuity, or adjust business partnerships.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The department reviews the transfer request, verifies lease eligibility, and processes a personalized lease transfer packet — including required forms, instructions, and applicable permit applications — to legally transfer a shellfish aquaculture lease to a new or additional leaseholder. Processing takes up to 4 weeks after a complete request is submitted.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Requests received after October 1st may be held until annual invoicing and reporting concludes
structured_extraction.program_audience: Current shellfish aquaculture leaseholders who wish to transfer their lease to another party, add a co-leaseholder, or remove an existing co-leaseholder; prospective new leaseholders
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Transferring or modifying shellfish aquaculture lease ownership or co-leaseholder status
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland state waters and submerged lands with existing shellfish aquaculture leases
requirements_list: Applicant must hold a current shellfish aquaculture lease in good standing
Primary leaseholder must hold a Shellfish Aquaculture Harvester Permit (SAHP)
Completed and signed Request to Transfer Form must be submitted
Full legal names with middle initials and suffixes required
New leaseholder must be at least 18 years old
Personalized transfer form must be returned in hard copy with all original signatures and notarization
All parties must sign and date the notarized transfer form before a Notary Public on the same day
Assignee must provide any applicable supporting business documents
If business entity: must be active and in good standing with SDAT; provide SDAT ID, Articles of Organization, Operating Agreement/Bylaws
For corporations: must be organized under Maryland law with more than 50% stock owned by Maryland residents
Assignee submits Shellfish Aquaculture Harvester Permit (SAHP) Application
U.S. Army Corps of Engineers permit transfer required if applicable
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Print, complete, and return the Request to Transfer Form to the Aquaculture Division by email (aquaculture.dnr@maryland.gov), fax (410-260-8310), or mail. Department staff review the form for accuracy and verify lease eligibility. If valid, the department sends a personalized transfer packet to the current primary leaseholder. Assignor ensures all documents are completed and returned; the notarized transfer form must be returned in hard copy with all original signatures.

structured_extraction.program_description: This permit allows researchers, educators, and organizations to sample, remove, or possess aquatic organisms from Maryland waters for purposes not covered by commercial or recreational fishing licenses. Eligible uses include scientific research, educational projects, collecting display animals, ecological monitoring, and in-stream surveys. It cannot be used to collect animals for sale or personal use.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual permit issued for a $10 fee (payable by check, money order, or online). The permit authorizes the holder to sample, remove, or possess aquatic organisms from Maryland waters for scientific, educational, or monitoring purposes. Permit holders must submit a summary report of activities annually.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Researchers, educators, and organizations conducting scientific research, educational projects, ecological monitoring, or in-stream surveys involving aquatic organisms in Maryland waters.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Permit authorizes collection of aquatic organisms for scientific research, educational projects, display animal collections, ecological monitoring, and in-stream surveys.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — applies to all Maryland waters. Collections must occur within Maryland; applicant must specify county of collections on application.
requirements_list: Must be conducting scientific research, educational projects, display animal collection, ecological monitoring, or in-stream surveys
Cannot use permit to collect animals for sale or personal use
Must submit maps of intended sampling locations to the department when applying
Must pay $10 annual permit fee
Must submit an annual summary report of activities
Complete all application information
Provide project proposal (reason for study, objectives, justification, species, numbers)
List sampling gear to be used
List all collectors in addition to principal officer
Certification statement signed and dated
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Aquatic Scientific Collection Permit Application (available as a PDF or online via Google Forms). Email maps of intended sampling locations to fishcollection.dnr@maryland.gov. Pay the $10 fee by check, money order, or through the online payment system. Permits are issued annually.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal grant program administered by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources, funded through the U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service Sport Fish Restoration Program, that provides grant funds to public and private schools (pre-K through 12) and environmental education centers that are part of the public school system. The program aims to increase public understanding of water resources and aquatic life through angler education, outdoor ethics, stewardship, and conservation activities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funds from the U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service Sport Fish Restoration Program provided to eligible public and private schools (pre-K through 12) and environmental education centers that are part of the public school system for aquatic-based education projects, including angler education, outdoor ethics, stewardship, and conservation programs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public and private schools (pre-K through 12) and environmental education centers that are part of the public school system in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Aquatic-based education projects including angler education, outdoor ethics, stewardship, and conservation activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland, statewide.
requirements_list: Applicants must be public or private schools (pre-K through 12) or environmental education centers that are part of the public school system.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Available through the DNR Grants Gateway; see the program page for more information on available funds for partners outside of DNR.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Natural Resources Forest Service's Backyard Buffers program helps homeowners and property owners who have a waterway on or near their property create a streamside riparian forest buffer of native trees and shrubs. The program provides free native seedlings to stabilize streambanks, reduce erosion, improve water quality, filter sediment and pollutants, and create wildlife habitat. A 'buffer in a bag' containing 20 to 30 native tree and shrub bare-root seedlings (approximately 1 to 2 feet tall) is provided along with fact sheets on species, planting techniques, and maintenance. Reservations are taken in March on a first-come, first-served basis through county coordinators, and bags are available for pickup at local sites during the spring planting season. A limited number of bags are available each year. Landowners eligible for agricultural cost-share programs are not eligible.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides a free 'buffer in a bag' containing 20 to 30 native tree and shrub bare-root seedlings (approximately 1 to 2 feet tall), along with fact sheets on species, planting techniques, and maintenance. Native trees and shrubs are provided at no cost on a first-come, first-served basis while supplies last. A limited number of bags are available each year. Reservations are taken during March and bags are available for pickup at a designated local site in time for the spring planting season.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Reservations typically taken during March each year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland homeowners and property owners with a drainage ditch, stream, creek, or river on or adjacent to their property who are interested in planting native trees and shrubs to create riparian forest buffers. Homeowners with 5 acres of land or less are particularly targeted. Landowners eligible for agricultural cost-share programs are not eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planting native trees and shrubs to create a streamside riparian forest buffer that stabilizes streambanks, reduces erosion, filters sediment and pollutants, reduces water pollution, improves water quality, and provides wildlife habitat.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland through county coordinators, though availability in select counties may depend on funding. Listed counties include Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore County, Calvert, Carroll, Caroline, Cecil, Charles, Dorchester, Frederick, Garrett, Harford, Howard, Kent, Montgomery, Queen Anne's, St. Mary's, Somerset, Talbot, Washington, Wicomico, and Worcester. Not available in all counties in every year due to limited funding.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland homeowner or property owner
Must have a drainage ditch, stream, creek, or river flowing through or adjacent to their property
Must have 5 acres of land or less (per county program guidelines)
Must not be eligible for agricultural cost-share programs
Must contact county coordinator to reserve a bag during March
Reservations taken on a first-come, first-served basis
Limited quantities available each year
Bags picked up at a designated local site during spring planting season
Program availability may vary by county due to limited funding
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local Backyard Buffers County Coordinator by phone or email during March to reserve a bag. Packet reservations are typically accepted in March, with bags available for pickup at a designated local site in time for spring planting. Bags are distributed on a first-come, first-served basis while supplies last. Contact the Maryland DNR Forest Service for availability.

structured_extraction.program_description: Becoming an Outdoors-Woman (BOW) offers outdoor skills workshops for women 18 and older. Participants learn about a wide variety of outdoor recreational activities — including firearm safety, fly fishing, preserving the harvest, hunting, hiking, and boating — in a casual, hands-on environment. The program includes weekend workshops with over 30 classes plus evening programs, as well as focused Beyond BOW workshops lasting one to three days on specific activities such as fishing, backpacking, goose hunting, field-to-table game processing, or outdoor survival skills. Over 80 different class offerings span archery, fishing, hunting, camping, kayaking, gardening, beekeeping, blacksmithing, photography, outdoor cooking, survival skills, and crafts, ranging from beginner to advanced levels.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Hands-on outdoor skills training workshops for women 18 and older. The Weekend Workshop runs August 7–9, 2026, and includes over 30 classes plus evening activities. Beyond BOW workshops are one to three days and focus on specific outdoor activities such as fishing, backpacking, goose hunting, field-to-table game processing, or outdoor survival skills. Over 80 different class offerings include archery, fishing, hunting, camping, kayaking, gardening, beekeeping, blacksmithing, photography, outdoor cooking, survival skills, and crafts. Many classes include hands-on field experience and take-home projects. Some classes require prerequisites. Registration details for the 2026 weekend workshop are forthcoming.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Registration for the 2026 Weekend Workshop (August 7-9, 2026) coming soon
structured_extraction.program_audience: Women 18 years of age and older interested in learning outdoor recreational skills and activities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participation in outdoor skills workshops covering hunting, fishing, hiking, boating, firearm safety, gardening, crafts, survival skills, and related activities; training and instruction in outdoor skills with equipment provision for courses
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; workshops held at various locations in Maryland; Maryland residents
requirements_list: Must be 18 years of age or older
Must be female
Some courses require prerequisites (e.g., Basic Firearms Safety before advanced shooting courses; Outdoor Photography before Advanced Outdoor Photography)
Hunter Education Certification requires completion of online course before workshop
Maryland Nontidal Sport Fishing license required for fishing courses
Some courses require specific attire and footwear (e.g., blacksmithing, hiking)
Participants must bring own digital cameras for photography courses
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Registration details for the 2026 Weekend Workshop (August 7–9, 2026) are coming soon. Contact mollie.kemp@maryland.gov with registration questions. Join the mailing list to stay updated on upcoming workshops.

structured_extraction.program_description: Uses dredged sand and sediment as fill material for natural resource restoration projects such as living shorelines, marsh enhancement, and island restoration. This approach reduces fill and transportation costs while delivering environmental benefits to coastal and shoreline ecosystems in Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Dredged material is placed directly at restoration sites, reducing fill and transportation costs and providing environmental benefits for projects such as living shorelines, marsh enhancement, or island restoration.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations or entities undertaking coastal, shoreline, marsh, or island restoration projects in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Fill material for habitat restoration sites including living shorelines, marsh enhancement, and island restoration
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Catherine McCall by email or phone for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A public donation fund that collects contributions to support largemouth bass and smallmouth bass conservation in Maryland. Donated money funds projects such as enhancing aquatic habitat, supplies awarded to directors of black bass tournaments, hatchery improvements to raise and stock more bass, and similar conservation efforts. Projects are reviewed each year by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources and its Black Bass Advisory Committee.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The fund accepts donations of any amount from the public. Donations of $1,000 or less can be made by check payable to the Maryland Department of Natural Resources with 'Black Bass Conservation Fund' in the memo, or online through the Maryland Outdoors licensing portal (mdoutdoors.maryland.gov) under the Merchandise section. Donations greater than $1,000 require contacting martha.bruder@maryland.gov directly. Note: donations are not tax-deductible. Funds are used for habitat enhancement, tournament supplies, hatchery equipment, and fish stocking projects.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Members of the general public who wish to support black bass (largemouth and smallmouth) conservation in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Enhancing aquatic habitat, supplies for black bass tournament directors, purchasing hatchery equipment to raise more largemouth bass for stocking, and similar bass conservation efforts.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — funds support bass conservation projects throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Donations are not tax-deductible
Donations of $1,000 or less should be made by check payable to the Maryland Department of Natural Resources with 'Black Bass Conservation Fund' in the memo
Donations greater than $1,000 require direct contact with Martha Bruder at martha.bruder@maryland.gov
Donations can also be made online through the Maryland Outdoors licensing portal under the Merchandise section
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Donate online through the Maryland Outdoors licensing portal (mdoutdoors.maryland.gov) under the Merchandise section, or send a check to Martha Bruder, 580 Taylor Avenue, B-2, Annapolis, MD 21401. For donations over $1,000, contact martha.bruder@maryland.gov directly.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Maryland DNR program funded through Black Bear Conservation Stamp sales and donations that reimburses landowners for damages caused by black bears, while also providing technical assistance and educational materials to help the public cope with nuisance bear problems.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimburses landowners for property or livestock damage caused by black bears. Also provides technical assistance and educational materials to help landowners deal with nuisance bear problems.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners in Western Maryland who have experienced damage caused by black bears.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reimbursement for damages caused by black bears.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Western Maryland, primarily Allegany, Garrett, and Washington counties where black bear populations are present.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a landowner who has experienced damage caused by black bears
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Karina Stonesifer at MD DNR Wildlife and Heritage Service for information on filing a claim.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's sewage pumpout program installs sewage disposal stations for boats at marinas so boaters can properly dispose of waste from holding tanks and portable toilets, helping reduce nutrient pollution and bacteria in the Chesapeake Bay.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program installs sewage disposal (pumpout) stations at marinas and provides information to boaters on how to properly dispose of boat sewage.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Boaters using Maryland waterways who need to dispose of sewage from boat holding tanks or portable toilets.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of sewage pumpout stations at marinas statewide.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland's waterways and lakes.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Boaters can find a list of pumpout station locations on the DNR website and are encouraged to call ahead to verify availability of services.

structured_extraction.program_description: Volunteers serve as Camp Hosts at Maryland state parks and forests. In exchange for working a set number of hours per week on campground-related tasks — such as welcoming campers, keeping sites clean, and answering questions — Camp Hosts receive a free campsite for the duration of their stay. Many parks also include Camp Hosts in general park operations based on their skills and interests.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Volunteers receive a free campsite for the duration of their stay while participating in the program. Some parks provide additional amenities such as electric hook-ups, water hook-ups, sewer hook-ups, and access to dump stations depending on the location. Volunteers typically work 20–30 hours per week with a minimum stay ranging from 1 month to 1 year depending on the park.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals interested in volunteering at Maryland state parks and forests in exchange for a free campsite and, at some locations, utility hook-ups.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free campsite accommodations (and in some cases electric hook-ups, water hook-ups, sewer hook-ups, and dump station access) provided to volunteers in exchange for campground-related work and park operations support.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at multiple Maryland state parks and forests statewide, including Elk Neck, Patapsco Valley, Susquehanna, Assateague, Janes Island, Martinak, Pocomoke River, Tuckahoe, Cedarville State Forest, Greenwell, Point Lookout, Smallwood, Cunningham Falls, Deep Creek Lake, Gambrill, Greenbrier, Rocky Gap, Swallow Falls, and Washington Monument State Parks.
requirements_list: Must be available to work a stipulated number of hours per week (typically 20–30 hours; some parks require 28–30 hours)
Must commit to a minimum stay (typically 1–2 months depending on the park, some parks up to 1 year)
Generally required to be on site on weekends (Friday–Sunday) and holidays
Must contact the specific park to discuss dates and availability
Some parks may have additional or different guidelines
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Review the park listing on the DNR website to choose a location. 2. Contact the specific park directly by email, phone, or mail to discuss available dates and confirm there is an opening. 3. Finalize arrangements with the park directly. A list of Volunteer Coordinator contacts by park is available on the DNR website.

structured_extraction.program_description: This permit allows individuals to legally possess, breed, sell, trade, or barter native Maryland reptiles and amphibians beyond personal possession limits. The program is designed to protect and conserve native reptiles and amphibians while allowing educational and economic benefits derived from them. A single permit covers all three activities: breeding, possessing, and/or commercially trading captive reptiles and amphibians.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A permit is issued for a $10.00 annual fee (check payable to Department of Natural Resources), valid from the date of issuance through December 31 of the same year. The permit authorizes the holder to possess, breed, sell, offer for sale, trade, or barter native Maryland reptiles and amphibians subject to specific species lists and conditions. Permit holders may possess an unlimited number of captively produced or legally out-of-state obtained animals from Lists A and B with proper documentation. Compliance with Maryland's Workmen Compensation Act (Article 1-401) may be required, along with a Certificate of Insurance or Insurance Binder Number.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals, businesses, and organizations wishing to possess, breed, sell, trade, or barter native Maryland reptiles and amphibians beyond standard possession limits.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Permit authorizes legal possession, breeding, and commercial trade of native Maryland reptiles and amphibians within regulated limits.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Pay a $10.00 annual permit fee (check payable to Department of Natural Resources)
Compliance with Maryland's Workmen Compensation Act (Article 1-401)
May require Certificate of Insurance or Insurance Binder Number
Submit completed application with all pages
Maintain records of all transactions involving each individual reptile and amphibian in possession
Keep certificates of origin, bills of sale, or other documentation proving legal acquisition
Submit a summary of reporting forms at time of renewal or by January 31 following permit expiration
House animals under humane, safe, and healthy conditions meeting all specified housing requirements
Meet all shipping and transportation standards for live reptiles and amphibians

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal grant program funded by the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) that enables Maryland to achieve the goals of the 2014 Chesapeake Bay Watershed Agreement. Funds support state programs and partner projects that improve water quality in the Chesapeake Bay Watershed by reducing nonpoint source nutrient and sediment pollution. The program also supports broader Bay restoration goals including sustainable fisheries, vital habitats, toxic contaminant reduction, and climate resiliency, as established under the 2014 Chesapeake Watershed Agreement's 10 goals and 31 outcomes.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding provided to partners to support projects that restore and protect the Chesapeake Bay. Applicants must provide a 1:1 non-federal match for the funds. Assistance also includes services and technical assistance. Funded through the EPA to support Maryland state programs and partners working to reduce nonpoint source nutrient and sediment pollution and meet the goals of the 2014 Chesapeake Bay Watershed Agreement.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible applicants include state agencies, the University of Maryland system, local governments (county government and municipalities/towns), and non-profit organizations working on water quality improvement and Bay restoration in the Chesapeake Bay Watershed.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support projects that help restore and protect the Chesapeake Bay, including efforts to reduce water pollution (nonpoint source nutrient and sediment), improve fisheries and habitats, address toxic contaminants, and enhance climate resiliency.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland, Chesapeake Bay Watershed.
requirements_list: Requires a 1:1 non-federal match
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Available through the DNR Grants Gateway; see program page for details.

structured_extraction.program_name: Chesapeake Bay Implementation Grant – Environmental Education and Stewardship (Outcome 4)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grant funding to support environmental education and stewardship projects within Maryland's portion of the Chesapeake Bay Watershed. Funded through the U.S. EPA's Chesapeake Bay Implementation Grant (CBIG), Outcome 4 aims to improve the ability of students and communities to take action benefiting Chesapeake and coastal ecosystems. Projects may include professional development and training for educators, curriculum expansion, outdoor learning experiences, and community environmental education programs. Two tracks are available: Track 1 for formal K-12 education systems (connecting to NGSS, Maryland Environmental Literacy Standards, or Maryland Service-Learning Graduation Requirements) and Track 2 for community or public education. Projects must focus on environmental issue exploration and stewardship action, including hands-on learning and community engagement, addressing local watershed and land-use issues based on sound environmental education principles. Project sites may include public lands, schoolyards, community property, or private property within Maryland's Chesapeake Bay Watershed.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $75,000 per proposal are available, with up to $100,000 in total CBIG funds for Outcome 4. Applicants requesting above $100,000 should contact the outcome manager directly. Funds are allocated annually through a federal EPA appropriation and can vary year to year. Funding becomes available September 1, 2026 for the current cycle. Projects may be located on public lands, schoolyards, community property, or private property within Maryland's Chesapeake Bay Watershed.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local non-governmental organizations, non-profits, local and state agencies, schools and school systems including higher education institutions working on environmental education and stewardship within Maryland's Chesapeake Bay Watershed.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Transportation and facility fees for student or community access to natural areas; environmental engagement or stewardship activities; educator professional development and training; community environmental education programs; supplies for environmental investigations, field equipment, and stewardship projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located within Maryland's portion of the Chesapeake Bay Watershed. Project sites may include public lands, schoolyards, community property, or private property.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local non-governmental organization, non-profit, local or state agency, school, school system, or higher education institution.
Project must be located within Maryland's portion of the Chesapeake Bay Watershed.
Projects must focus on environmental issue exploration and investigation leading to stewardship action.
Projects should involve collaborative student or community-stakeholder planning focused on capacity building and civic engagement.
Both tracks must address local watershed and land-use issues based on sound environmental education principles.

Track 1 proposals must serve formal K-12 education systems and connect to curriculum standards such as Next Generation Science Standards (NGSS), Maryland Environmental Literacy Standards, or Maryland Service-Learning Graduation Requirements.

Track 1 applicants must submit a transmittal letter on official letterhead signed by an authorized executive, letters of support from school system leadership, letters of support from partners or impacted community members, and an Environmental Literacy Plan or similar evidence.
Track 2 proposals must serve communities or public education and connect to environmental or stewardship best practices.

Track 2 applicants must submit a transmittal letter with signature of authority, letters of support from partnering school administration or other partners, and an outline or documentation of environmental education curriculum or programming plan.
Applications must be submitted through DNR's Grants Gateway under Outcome 4.
Proposals are reviewed and scored on demographics/need, education and stewardship connections, program development, and budget.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Maryland DNR Grants Gateway portal under Outcome 4. Contact Jen Wolfe at jen.wolfe@maryland.gov to discuss project ideas or confirm eligibility before submitting. Submit all required attachments based on the applicable track (K-12 school system or community organization) by the deadline of December 12, 2025. Proposals are reviewed and scored on demographics and need, education and stewardship connections, program development, and budget.

structured_extraction.program_name: Chesapeake Bay National Estuarine Research Reserve (CBNERR-MD)

structured_extraction.program_name: Chesapeake Bay and Endangered Species Fund

Projects funded include stream cleanups, tree plantings, habitat research and protection, and monitoring and conservation of threatened plants and animals such as bog turtles, rare butterflies, sandplain gerardia, and Important Bird Areas.

structured_extraction.program_name: Chesapeake Forest Lands Hunting Tract Lottery
structured_extraction.program_description: A lottery program that allows hunt clubs to obtain hunting lease agreements on Chesapeake Forest Lands managed by the Maryland Forest Service. Winners must sign a notarized lease and provide proof of insurance before hunting begins.

The lease agreement covers ten hunting seasons (2025–2026 through 2034–2035). There is no fee to enter the lottery. The lease is mailed to the winner, who must sign and notarize it and return it with payment. Proof of insurance is required before hunting begins. Lessees obtain exclusive hunting rights on designated forest land premises for legal wild game species, subject to property maintenance obligations and insurance requirements.

structured_extraction.program_name: Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays Trust Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: A Maryland state program that provides financial resources to accelerate Chesapeake Bay and Atlantic Coastal Bays restoration by funding the most effective and cost-effective non-point source (runoff) pollution control projects identified in Maryland's Tributary Strategies and 2-Year Milestones. The fund supports restored streams and floodplains, riparian buffers and forests, wetland ecosystems, and stormwater management, while also providing technical assistance to local governments and nonprofits to help them meet local water quality goals. The program incorporates co-benefits into project selection to promote holistic projects, including restoration of aquatic resources, climate resilience, carbon sequestration, wildlife habitat creation, local employment opportunities, recreational opportunities, and environmental justice benefits. It also supports beneficial use projects such as marsh enhancement, beach nourishment, island restoration, and shoreline stabilization, and incorporates updated science from the Comprehensive Evaluation of System Response (CSER) report. State agencies work with local and federal partners to administer funding through new and innovative approaches that leverage funds, target cost-effective locations using the Trust Fund Targeting Map, and engage the community. Funds are geographically targeted to maximize pollution reduction to the Chesapeake Bay and Atlantic Coastal Bays.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are awarded to local partners for non-point source pollution control and habitat restoration projects, including stream and floodplain restoration, riparian buffer and forest enhancement, wetland ecosystem improvement, stormwater management, and innovative non-point source pollution control technologies. Projects must provide cost-effective, measurable nonpoint source pollution reductions along with co-benefits such as restoration of aquatic resources (submerged aquatic vegetation, oyster reefs), climate resilience, carbon sequestration, wildlife habitat creation, local employment opportunities, recreational opportunities, and environmental justice benefits. The program also funds beneficial use projects including marsh enhancement, beach nourishment, island restoration, and shoreline stabilization, as well as cover crop programs, agricultural best management practices, tree planting, and conservation reserve enhancement. Technical assistance is provided to local governments and non-governmental organizations to help them meet local water quality goals. Funds are leveraged with local and federal partners and geographically targeted using the Trust Fund Targeting Map to maximize impact and cost-effectiveness.
structured_extraction.program_audience: State agencies, local governments, Soil Conservation Districts, non-governmental organizations, state colleges and universities (including University of Maryland), non-profit organizations, and other partners working on Bay restoration, water quality improvement, and non-point source pollution control in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Non-point source pollution control projects identified in the State's Tributary Strategies and 2-Year Milestones, including stream and floodplain restoration, riparian buffer and forest enhancement, wetland ecosystem improvement, stormwater management, and innovative non-point source pollution control technologies. Additional eligible uses include habitat restoration (submerged aquatic vegetation, oyster reefs), climate resilience projects, carbon sequestration initiatives, wildlife habitat creation, recreational opportunity projects, environmental justice benefit projects, marsh enhancement, beach nourishment, island restoration, shoreline stabilization, cover crop programs, agricultural best management practices, tree planting, and dredged material placement for beneficial use.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland across all 24 counties, focused on the Chesapeake Bay and Atlantic Coastal Bays watershed, with geographic targeting toward areas where projects will most effectively and efficiently reduce nonpoint source pollution entering the Chesapeake Bay and Atlantic Coastal Bays, as identified by the Trust Fund Targeting Map. Projects should align with targeting map layers identifying priority areas for coastal resiliency, habitat, recreation, and environmental justice.

The program encourages citizens to care for their local environment through education, outreach, and hands-on stewardship activities.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's CoastSmart Communities Initiative helps coastal communities prepare for and respond to short- and long-term coastal hazards such as high tide flooding, storm surge, and sea level rise. It connects local government staff and partners to information, tools, training, and financial and technical assistance to build resilience along Maryland's shorelines. The program provides financial assistance through the Chesapeake & Coastal Grants Gateway (Outcome 2), technical assistance to local communities, and training opportunities for local practitioners. It also links communities to federal and state resources, tools, visualizations, and networks. The CoastSmart Council adopts siting and design criteria for future capital projects to address sea level rise and coastal flooding impacts. The program also includes guidance for incorporating probabilistic Relative Sea Level Rise (RSLR) projections into planning, regulatory, and site-specific projects, and requires coastal jurisdictions to develop and update Nuisance Flood Plans every five years. A key component is the Nuisance Flood Plan (NFP) requirement — a five-year plan executed by jurisdictions to understand, plan, and implement programs to reduce flood risk and increase resilience to nuisance flooding, addressing high-tide flooding, sea level rise, land subsidence, storm surge, precipitation, and wind-driven flooding impacts.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides financial assistance through the Chesapeake & Coastal Grants Gateway (Outcome 2), technical assistance to local communities, and training opportunities for local practitioners. Also connects local planners to essential information, tools, people, visualizations, and networks to address coastal hazards. The CoastSmart Council also adopts siting and design criteria for future capital projects to address sea level rise and coastal flooding impacts. Provides step-by-step guidance for incorporating sea level rise projections into planning, regulatory, and site-specific projects, including a six/seven-step planning framework. Requires coastal jurisdictions to develop and update Nuisance Flood Plans every five years, with technical and financial assistance available through MDNR. The six-step NFP planning process includes: (1) Organize resources, (2) Review existing plans, (3) Assess current/future flooding, (4) Develop plan with recommendations, (5) Submit plan, (6) Implement plan. Guidance includes tools and resources for flood documentation, mapping, adaptation strategies, and access to funding opportunities.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Initial Nuisance Flood Plans due on or before October 1, 2020; updated every five years thereafter (second phase due October 2025; third phase due October 2030)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local government staff, coastal community partners, local practitioners, planning professionals, decision-makers in private, local, state, and federal sectors involved in coastal planning and resilience, counties and municipalities in Maryland's Coastal Zone, and communities facing coastal hazards such as high tide flooding, storm surge, and sea level rise. Also includes county emergency management agencies, planning departments, public works departments, and residents and businesses in flood-prone areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects that foster healthy ecosystems, communities, and economies resilient to coastal hazards including flooding and sea level rise; planning, information, tools, training, and siting/design criteria for coastal hazard mitigation; flood planning, resilience projects, stormwater management, nature-based solutions, and infrastructure adaptation. Also supports infrastructure assessment and documentation, flood mitigation planning, and road and bridge vulnerability identification.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Maryland's coastal communities along the Chesapeake Bay, Coastal Bays, and Atlantic Ocean. Maryland's Coastal Zone extends three miles into the Atlantic Ocean to inland boundaries of 16 counties and Baltimore City bordering the Atlantic Ocean, Chesapeake Bay, and Potomac River up to the District of Columbia, covering two-thirds of Maryland's land area and home to approximately 70% of Maryland's residents.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Chesapeake & Coastal Grants Gateway, which provides a one-stop location for communities seeking financial assistance. Technical assistance and training opportunities are also available through the program. For Nuisance Flood Plans, follow the six-step planning process: (1) Organize resources, (2) Review existing plans, (3) Assess current/future flooding, (4) Develop plan with recommendations, (5) Submit plan to Maryland Department of Planning, (6) Implement plan. For sea level rise planning, follow the seven-step methodology: (1) Define project type, goal, and area; (2) Determine timeframe; (3) Select tide gauge; (4) Determine flood risk tolerance; (5) Select RSLR estimate; (6) Assess flood impacts; (7) Consider adaptation options.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Forestry Catalyst Fund (CF2) provides grants to support tree planting projects and build the capacity of organizations to expand tree planting and maintenance in overburdened and underserved communities across Maryland. Designed in accordance with the 2020-2025 Maryland Forest Action Plan, the program aims to reduce barriers to tree planting and gives local partners flexible access to funding that can be leveraged to secure additional resources, with no matching funds required. Funding is available under three tracks: Site Readiness (Track A), Implementation (Track B), and Capacity Building (Track C).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are available under three tracks: Track A (Site Readiness) – $5,000 to $50,000 for site preparation activities (stump removal, hazardous tree removal, vegetation removal, concrete removal leading to replacement tree planting); Track B (Implementation/tree planting) – $5,000 to $50,000 for tree planting projects with a 2-year post-planting maintenance plan; Track C (Capacity Building) – $50,000 to $250,000 per year for organizational capacity enhancement. No match is required. All work must take place in or benefit disadvantaged communities as identified in the Inflation Reduction Act Disadvantaged Communities Map. Track B projects require pre-application technical assistance from the Maryland Forest Service or an authorized representative. 90% of award released after contingencies; 10% held until final report approval.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local government entities, federally recognized tribes and tribal organizations, non-profit organizations, public and state-controlled institutions of higher education, and community-based organizations working in overburdened and underserved communities across Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Track A (Site Readiness): stump removal, hazardous tree removal, vegetation removal, concrete removal leading to replacement tree planting. Track B (Implementation): tree planting projects with two-year maintenance planning including watering, mulching, pruning, pest/disease monitoring, and invasive management. Track C (Capacity Building): staff or contractual support, workforce development, expansion or creation of new pilot programming. Funds may also cover personnel time, supplies, and subcontractor/contractor services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must take place in or benefit disadvantaged communities identified in the Inflation Reduction Act Disadvantaged Communities Map (archived Climate and Economic Justice Screening Tool). 100% of work must take place in or benefit disadvantaged communities. Projects must identify watershed, county, and legislative district location.
requirements_list: Projects must directly or indirectly result in trees being planted in overburdened, underserved communities
Projects must be located in or serve disadvantaged communities identified in the IRA Disadvantaged Communities Map
100% of work must take place in or benefit disadvantaged communities
Match is waived; this waiver must be passed on to any sub-awardees
Track B applicants must obtain pre-application technical assistance from the Maryland Forest Service or an authorized representative from one of the 5 Million Trees for Maryland partnership agencies
Track C applications may not be combined with Track A or Track B applications
Track C minimum grant amount is $50,000 per year
Executive Officer and Project Leader must be two separate individuals, not contractors, able to make decisions on behalf of organization
Project Leader email must match submission email address

Two-year maintenance plan required addressing: watering (20 gallons per tree every 2 weeks first season), mulching, pruning, pest/disease monitoring, climbing invasive management (3x/year for 50+ tree sites), leaf removal strategy, mowing/care integration
Final reports required with receipts, invoices, and timesheets (with date and name)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through an online system at cbtrust.org/grants/community-forestry/. Contact the CBT Program Officer, Samara Pyfrom, at 410-974-2941 ext. 147 or spyfrom@cbtrust.org with questions about the application process.

structured_extraction.program_description: The CPP program provides competitive grant funding to restore existing park and green space systems and create new park and green space systems in municipal corporations across Maryland and Baltimore City. Eligible projects include rehabilitating, expanding, or improving existing parks; creating new parks; developing environmentally oriented parks and recreation projects; purchasing and installing playground equipment in older neighborhoods and intensely developed areas; building trails; creating water access points; and acquiring land for new parks. The program invests in established communities across Maryland, addressing unmet need for park and playground improvements and revitalization statewide, supported by the Governor and the Maryland General Assembly. Annual funding has ranged from $2.5 million to $5 million, supporting dozens of projects per year; the Governor's Fiscal Year 2026 budget includes $5 million to fund 26 new parks and playgrounds projects. A total of $97.4 million has been approved for 908 projects since the program began.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive reimbursable grants that can fund up to 100% of eligible capital project costs. There is no established minimum or maximum grant amount. Funds can cover land acquisition (up to the average of two independent appraisals plus incidental closing costs), development of new parks, rehabilitation of existing parks, playground equipment, trails, and water recreation access. Local matching funds are welcome but not required. Since CPP is a reimbursable grant program, the recipient must pay costs upfront and then request reimbursement. Partial project reimbursements are permitted to assist with cash flow, and advance payments may be considered in limited circumstances. Selected projects must be completed as proposed; remaining funds cannot be redirected to other projects. The Governor's Fiscal Year 2026 budget includes $5 million to fund 26 new parks and playgrounds projects. A total of $97.4 million has been approved for 908 projects statewide since the program began. Projects are presented to the Board of Public Works for final approval.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications are due in August of each calendar year; the application period for the Fiscal Year 2027 grant is now closed. The FY2027 application deadline was Wednesday, August 20, 2025 by 3:00 p.m.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Tiffany DePaoli (Allegany, Baltimore, Calvert, Carroll, Charles, Garrett, Harford, St. Mary's Counties); Katelyn Mayberry (Anne Arundel, Cecil, Frederick, Howard, Kent, Washington Counties, Baltimore City); Michael McQuarrie (Caroline, Dorchester, Montgomery, Prince George's, Queen Anne's, Somerset, Talbot, Wicomico, Worcester Counties)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Governing bodies of municipal corporations in Maryland and Baltimore City seeking to develop, revitalize, or improve parks and playgrounds.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital projects to develop new parks; rehabilitate, expand, or improve existing parks; purchase and install playground equipment in older neighborhoods and intensely developed areas; develop environmentally oriented parks and recreation areas; develop new or extend existing trails; create water recreation access points; or acquire land to create new parks. Eligible expenditures include contract costs, direct purchases of supplies/materials/services/equipment rental, and in-house labor and equipment. Funds cannot be used for operating or maintenance costs or contingency reserves. Projects must remain open to all users and capital improvements must last at least 20 years.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to municipal corporations and Baltimore City throughout Maryland, statewide. Project location must be within designated eligible areas on DNR eligibility map and within the applicant's jurisdiction.
requirements_list: Only governing bodies of municipal corporations and Baltimore City are eligible to apply

Applicant must hold a deed to the property or have a joint use agreement, easement, or long-term lease (with more than 20 years remaining and no termination for convenience clause) signed by the property owner
Applicant must demonstrate capacity to plan, implement, and maintain the project (qualified staff or contractor, effective administrative procedures, evidence of past success)
HOAs and nonprofits are not directly eligible but may partner with an eligible municipality
Projects must be open and available to all users
Grant funds may only be used for prospective projects — the project cannot have already started before funds are awarded
Replacement of facilities previously funded by POS Local or CPP is only eligible after 20 years (or 15 years for Local Parks and Playgrounds Infrastructure grants) have passed
Development projects must have a minimum 20-year lifespan; acquired land must be maintained for public use in perpetuity
No contingency costs or similar reserves may be included in project estimates
Land acquisitions must be supported by two independent appraisals; property may not be purchased before grant award
Grant funds must be used for the project as approved by the Board of Public Works
Compliance with all Local, State, and Federal statutes and regulations
Non-discriminatory access required (Title VII Civil Rights Act, ADA compliance)
Consistent with National Playground Safety Standards and ADA standards
No lead (>90 ppm) or PFAS chemicals in playground surfacing materials
Project must be retained for public outdoor recreation or open space purposes
Subject to Department inspection for compliance
Retain support documents for three years after final reimbursement
Submit photos of completed project and grant acknowledgement sign for final reimbursement
Facility must be maintained in attractive, safe, sanitary condition
Local Government responsible for operation and maintenance
Conversion to other uses requires written approval from three state secretaries and replacement with equivalent facilities
Local Government must indemnify Department from claims/liability
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: DNR Program Open Space Local staff prepare and distribute application materials to local governments and may conduct grant writing workshops (a workshop was held via Google Meet on June 24, 2025). Applicants submit applications by August of each calendar year (FY2027 deadline was August 20, 2025 by 3:00 p.m.). Applicants download and complete the fillable PDF application (Community Parks and Playgrounds Application and Project Agreement), save it, fill in all required fields, and submit with all necessary attachments (including deed or joint use agreement). Program staff review complete submissions and evaluate projects based on consistency with CPP's purpose, eligibility requirements, and criteria. Staff recommendations are provided to the DNR Secretary for possible inclusion in the Governor's budget. After a State Clearinghouse review, selected grants are submitted to the Board of Public Works (BPW) for approval. Applicants are notified by May of the following calendar year whether their project was included in the upcoming fiscal year's budget. After project completion, submit a Reimbursement Request form with required documentation (invoices, proof of payment, labor and equipment records) detailing project costs for state reimbursement up to the BPW-approved amount.

structured_extraction.program_description: Strengthens public outreach and engagement in on-the-ground restoration and increases locally led restoration projects. Staff help local governments, watershed groups, and community organizations align their restoration efforts with Chesapeake Bay water quality goals and Watershed Implementation Plan targets, supporting community engagement and outreach alongside on-the-ground implementation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Technical assistance and staff support to local governments, watershed groups, and community organizations for restoration planning and implementation aligned with the Chesapeake Bay Total Maximum Daily Load (TMDL) and Watershed Implementation Plan goals, plus support for community engagement and outreach.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, watershed groups, and community organizations in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: On-the-ground habitat and water quality restoration projects and community engagement aligned with Chesapeake Bay water quality goals and Watershed Implementation Plan targets
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Carrie Decker by email or phone for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A fund established through a Memorandum of Understanding between Maryland DNR and offshore wind developer US Wind Inc. to compensate commercial and for-hire (charter) fishing vessel owners, operators, and crew who experience direct economic losses and/or impacts from the construction, operation, or decommissioning of US Wind's offshore wind energy project. Includes a Navigational Enhancement and Training Program (NETP) and a Multi-Use Fishing Community Resilience Fund.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: $5.46 million total fund divided across three project periods: Construction ($1,546,864), Operations/5 years post-COD ($1,893,510), and Decommissioning ($2,014,757). Compensation is claims-based for demonstrated direct economic losses. Also includes vouchers for navigation equipment via the Navigational Enhancement and Training Program (NETP) and a Multi-Use Fishing Community Resilience Fund for community projects supporting Maryland fishing interests. The amount available to an individual or company depends in part on past landings from the affected area, based on historical and current federal and state fishery landings data. Claims must be made no later than two calendar years after the end of the applicable Project Period, extendable to five years for good cause or data unavailability.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: on or before May 13, 2025 (MOU development deadline); claims due no later than two calendar years after end of applicable Project Period (extendable to five years)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Commercial and for-hire (charter) fishing vessel owners, operators, and crew (regardless of home port) who have fished in or near Lease Area OCS-A 0490 approximately 11.5 miles east of Ocean City, Maryland, and experience impacts from wind farm construction, operation, or decommissioning.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Direct compensation for economic losses attributable to construction, operation, and decommissioning of the offshore wind farm; vouchers for navigation equipment (NETP); harbor maintenance, gear development, business development, and community resilience funding.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to commercial and for-hire fishing vessel operators regardless of home port who have fished in the US Wind offshore project area (Lease Area OCS-A 0490) in federal waters approximately 11.5 miles east of Ocean City, Maryland, off the Delmarva Peninsula. Interconnection point at Indian River Substation, Dagsboro, Delaware.
requirements_list: Must be a commercial vessel owner, operator, or crew member, or a for-hire/charter fishing operator
Must have a documented history of fishing in or near Lease Area OCS-A 0490
Must have been impacted by the construction, operation, or decommissioning of the wind energy project
Must be able to document and demonstrate the direct economic impact
Amount based on past landings from the affected area using historical and current federal and state fishery landings data
Claims must be filed no later than two calendar years after the end of the applicable Project Period (extendable to five years for good cause or data unavailability)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Direct compensation becomes available once offshore project construction begins for fishermen who experience and can document an impact. Claims are submitted through a claims-based process. Visit the Fisheries Compensation Program for Atlantic Coast Offshore Wind page (rfainfo.com) for the most up-to-date information. Option election deadline is July 1, 2026 for certain program components.

structured_extraction.program_name: Complimentary Lifetime Fishing License for DAV/POW
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland residents who are 100% service-connected disabled veterans (DAV), former prisoners of war (POW), or deemed unemployable by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs can receive a free lifetime fishing license. The license incorporates the non-tidal angler's license, trout stamp, Bay & Coastal sport fishing license, and recreational oyster license for fishing in Maryland's fresh waters, Chesapeake Bay, tributaries, and Atlantic coastal waters.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A free lifetime fishing license at no cost that incorporates the non-tidal angler's license, trout stamp, Bay & Coastal sport fishing license, and recreational oyster license. Applicants must submit a completed DNR F-3 fishing license application form along with a letter of disability or VA certification with the initial application.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland resident veterans who are 100% service-connected disabled (permanent and total), former prisoners of war, or deemed unemployable by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free lifetime fishing license covering recreational fishing in Maryland's fresh waters, Chesapeake Bay and tributaries, Atlantic Ocean and coastal bays, including non-tidal angling, trout fishing, Bay & Coastal sport fishing, and recreational oyster fishing
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Maryland residents statewide
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident
Must be a 100% permanent and total service-connected disabled veteran, former POW, or deemed unemployable by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs
Must provide a letter of disability or certification from the Veterans Administration with the initial application
Must submit a completed and signed DNR F-3 Fishing License Application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a completed DNR F-3 fishing license application form along with a letter of disability or VA certification to one of seven DNR Licensing and Registration Service Centers (Annapolis, Centreville, Salisbury, Bel Air, Frederick, Solomons, or Cumberland). Additional details are available on the Maryland DNR Military One-Stop Shop page.

structured_extraction.program_name: Complimentary Lifetime Hunting License for POW/DAV
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides a free lifetime hunting license to eligible Maryland residents (and non-residents from reciprocal states) who are former prisoners of war, 100% service-connected disabled veterans (permanent and total), or deemed unemployable by the US Department of Veterans Affairs. The license includes the bow stamp, muzzleloader stamp, sika deer stamp, and furbearer permit. The Maryland Migratory Game Bird Stamp is not included and must be purchased separately each year, along with other annual items such as the Federal Migratory Bird Hunting and Conservation Stamp and Big Game Harvest Record.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A complimentary (free) lifetime hunting license that includes the bow stamp, muzzleloader stamp, sika deer stamp, and furbearer permit, allowing recipients to hunt all legal game in season. The Maryland Migratory Game Bird Stamp, Federal Migratory Bird Hunting and Conservation Stamp, and Big Game Harvest Record are not included and must be obtained separately each year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents (and non-residents from states offering reciprocal privileges to Maryland residents) who are former prisoners of war, 100% permanent and total service-connected disabled veterans, or deemed unemployable by the US Department of Veterans Affairs
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Lifetime hunting license including bow stamp, muzzleloader stamp, sika deer stamp, and furbearer permit, allowing hunting of all legal game in Maryland
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Maryland residents statewide and non-residents from states that offer the same privilege to Maryland residents. License must be obtained at a DNR Licensing and Registration Service Center by appointment only.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident or a non-resident from a state that offers the same privilege to Maryland residents
