Must be a former prisoner of war, 100% permanent and total service-connected disabled veteran, or deemed unemployable by the US Department of Veterans Affairs
Must furnish a letter of disability or certification from the Veterans Administration with the initial application
Must submit a completed and signed Hunting License Application
Must obtain license at a DNR Licensing and Registration Service Center (by appointment only)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply in person at a DNR Licensing and Registration Service Center (by appointment only, Monday–Friday 8:30 AM–4:30 PM) with a completed Hunting License Application and supporting documentation (letter of disability or VA certification letter). Documents can be scanned or faxed. Additional details are available at the Maryland DNR Military One-Stop Shop page.

structured_extraction.program_description: A DNR wildlife biologist provides information on available deer management techniques and helps corporations identify the most appropriate methods for managing deer on company properties.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A DNR wildlife biologist consults with corporation representatives to explain deer management techniques and help identify the most suitable methods for the company.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Corporation representatives seeking assistance with deer management on company properties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Technical guidance on deer management techniques.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Request must come from a corporation representative.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Kevin Lamp, Deer Project Leader, to request assistance.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Natural Resources (DNR) offers paid and volunteer internships to high school and college students across a wide range of environmental and natural resources fields. Interns gain hands-on experience working within a state agency, apply classroom knowledge to real-world projects, and build professional skills and networks. Interns receive mentorship, professional development, and may earn academic credit. Enrichment activities such as career panels, hikes, and park visits are also included.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Paid and volunteer internships lasting approximately 10–12 weeks, offered in summer (June–August) and fall (October–December). Interns work in-person at DNR locations across Maryland, primarily in Annapolis. Academic credit is available. Enrichment activities such as career panels, hikes, and park visits are included. Compensation depends on the specific position.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Summer internships open for applications in February; fall internships open in July.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Currently enrolled high school and college students, or individuals who have graduated within one year of the internship start date, interested in environmental and natural resources fields.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Internship placements provide work experience, mentorship, and professional development — not direct financial assistance to recipients. Interns may receive pay depending on the position and may earn academic credit.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Internships are primarily based in Annapolis, MD, but positions may be located across the state of Maryland depending on agency needs.
requirements_list: Currently enrolled in high school or college, OR graduated within one year of the internship start date
Completed state application
Resume
Two letters of recommendation (not from relatives)
Unofficial transcript with a minimum 2.5 GPA
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: When available, internships are posted on the State of Maryland Job Openings webpage at jobapscloud.com/MD. Applicants submit a state application, resume, two letters of recommendation, and an unofficial transcript. An Internship Interest Form is also available to receive notifications when future internship positions open.

structured_extraction.program_name: Day-Use Area Admission Fee Waiver for Active Duty Military and Maryland National Guard
structured_extraction.program_description: Active duty military personnel and members of the Maryland National Guard can enter Maryland State Park day-use areas at no charge by presenting their active duty military identification card to the gate attendant. The day-use entrance service charge is waived for the ID card holder only, or the per-vehicle fee if a per-vehicle charge is in effect. No other facility service charges are waived.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Day-use entrance service charges at Maryland State Park day-use areas are waived for the active duty military ID card holder or Maryland National Guard member. The waiver covers the ID card holder only, or the per-vehicle fee if a per-vehicle charge is in effect. No other facility service charges are waived.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Active duty military personnel and members of the Maryland National Guard with a valid active duty military ID card.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Covers day-use entrance fees at Maryland State Park day-use areas statewide.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at all Maryland State Park day-use areas statewide.
requirements_list: Must be a member of the Maryland National Guard or active duty military personnel
Must display a valid active duty military identification card to the gate attendant
Waiver applies to the ID card holder only (or per-vehicle fee if a per-vehicle charge is in effect)
No other facility service charges are waived
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Display your active duty military identification card to the gate attendant at any Maryland State Park day-use area to have the entrance fee waived.

structured_extraction.program_name: Day-Use Area Admission Fee Waiver for Veterans
structured_extraction.program_description: Waives all applicable day-use entrance fees at Maryland State Park day-use areas for veterans of the United States Armed Forces (uniformed services), including both Maryland residents and out-of-state veterans, year-round. The waiver applies to the veteran only, not to others in the same vehicle, unless a per-vehicle charge is in effect, in which case the per-vehicle fee is also waived. No other facility use or service charges are waived.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: All applicable day-use entrance fees at Maryland State Park day-use areas are waived for the veteran year-round. If a per-vehicle charge is in effect, the per-vehicle fee is also waived. The waiver applies to the veteran only, not to others in the vehicle (unless a per-vehicle fee applies). No other facility use or service charges are waived.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Veterans of the United States Armed Forces (uniformed services), including both Maryland residents and out-of-state veterans.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Waiver of day-use entrance fees at Maryland State Park day-use areas.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at all Maryland State Park day-use areas statewide; open to both Maryland resident and out-of-state veterans.
requirements_list: Must be a veteran of the United States Armed Forces (uniformed services)
Waiver applies to the veteran only, not other occupants of the vehicle (unless a per-vehicle charge is in effect)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Present veteran identification or proof of veteran status at the gate attendant upon arrival at any Maryland State Park day-use area to have the entrance fee waived.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Deer Cooperators Program licenses businesses to provide deer control assistance in areas where hunting is not a viable option. Licensed cooperators use non-lethal and lethal deer management techniques to help resolve deer-related problems at locations such as airports, test tracks, and agricultural areas.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: DNR issues permits to licensed Deer Cooperator businesses authorizing them to use non-lethal and lethal deer management techniques. Permits for human safety concerns (e.g., airports, test tracks) can be issued for year-round operations. Permits for agricultural or other areas without human safety concerns are valid from January 15 to April 15. Community consensus and annual DNR approval are required.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses seeking to become licensed deer control cooperators in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Deer damage management using non-lethal and lethal techniques at locations where hunting is not viable
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a licensed Deer Cooperator
Community consensus required
Annual DNR approval required
Permits for non-human-safety areas limited to January 15 – April 15
Permits for human safety concerns (airports, test tracks, etc.) may be issued for year-round operations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Kevin Lamp, Deer Project Leader at the Wildlife & Heritage Service, for more information on obtaining a Deer Cooperator permit.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Wildlife and Heritage Service issues Deer Management Permits to help landowners, agricultural lessees, and designated employees resolve legitimate damage to commercial farm crops, orchards, nurseries, and certain managed forests caused by deer. DNR investigates severe deer damage and, if warranted, authorizes population reduction through permits allowing the taking of specified numbers of antlerless deer. County-specific staff contacts are assigned to process and oversee these permits during normal business hours.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: DNR investigates severe deer damage to eligible properties; if warranted, permits are issued authorizing landowners, agricultural lessees, or designated employees to take a specified number of antlerless deer (with limited exceptions for antlered deer) to reduce the local deer population. Harvested deer must be utilized by permittees/agents or donated to others. County-specific Wildlife and Heritage Service staff process and oversee these permits.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Master Confirmation Number Log Sheet due no later than March 15 following permit expiration
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners, agricultural lessees, and designated employees of farms, orchards, or nurseries experiencing severe deer damage to commercial farm crops, orchards, nurseries, or managed forests in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Deer population reduction through authorized shooting by permittees and agents on properties with documented severe deer damage. Harvested deer must be utilized by permittees/agents or donated to charitable food programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland; county-specific staff contacts are assigned across all Maryland counties. Specific county and zone restrictions apply regarding firearm types (e.g., shotgun-only counties/zones, Deer Management Region A) and archery distance requirements in certain counties including Calvert, Carroll, Frederick, Harford, Montgomery, St. Mary's, and Anne Arundel.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a landowner, agricultural lessee, or designated employee (W2 form recipient) of a farm, orchard, or nursery experiencing severe deer damage.

Eligible damage areas include commercial farm crops (row crops, truck crops, pasture), orchards, nurseries (including Christmas trees), and woodland areas with DNR or licensed private consulting forester management or planting plans.
DNR must investigate and determine that severe deer damage is present before a permit is issued.
Permittees are authorized to take a specified number of antlerless deer; antlered deer may be taken only in limited circumstances.
Master Confirmation Number Log Sheet must be submitted no later than March 15 following permit expiration.
Appointments required to visit the Tawes State Office Building; walk-in customers not accepted without a confirmed appointment.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the county-specific Wildlife and Heritage Service staff member by email or phone during normal business hours. DNR will investigate the reported deer damage and, if warranted, issue a Deer Management Permit. To schedule a wildlife permit appointment, email wildlifepermits.dnr@maryland.gov or call 410-260-8540.

structured_extraction.program_description: A deer cooperator permit that allows the holder to conduct deer carcass removal and handling operations on private land in Maryland. The permit is valid for one year from the date it is issued.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The permit costs $100 (check payable to Department of Natural Resources) and is valid for one year (expiring December 31st following issuance). It authorizes the holder to remove and handle deer carcasses on private land. Applicants must describe how they plan to dispose of deer carcasses and specify the location where activity will be conducted when applying.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and businesses/organizations seeking to conduct deer carcass removal and handling on private land in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Authorizes deer carcass removal and handling operations on private land.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Applicant must specify the county and location where activity will be conducted.
requirements_list: Applicant must describe the method they will use to dispose of deer carcasses at the time of application.
Permit fee of $100 required (check payable to Department of Natural Resources).
Operations must be conducted on private land.
Valid workers' compensation insurance or certificate/binder, or qualification as self-employed/family-only employer.
Complete application with all required personal/business information including date of birth and SSN/Tax ID/FID.
Applicant must specify the county and location where activity will be conducted.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the written Deer Salvage Permit Application Form and submit to the Permits Coordinator at Tawes State Office Building, 580 Taylor Ave E-1, Annapolis, MD 21401. The form may also be submitted by email to wildlifepermits.dnr@maryland.gov or georgia.johnson@maryland.gov, or by phone at 301-501-0202 or 410-260-8540. In-person appointments must be scheduled in advance.

structured_extraction.program_description: Annual recognition program for tournament organizers who protect black bass resources and include youth participants in sportfishing tournaments. Supports youth-focused bass fishing tournaments by providing supplies that promote black bass conservation and watercraft safety. Tournament directors or co-directors can apply to receive equipment such as aerators, rubber nets, live-well accessories, and other conservation supplies to improve fish survival during competitive tournaments.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Award-winning organizers receive supplies up to $500 in value (such as scales, cull clips, barbless tackle, life jackets, aerators, weigh-in systems, and other conservation-related equipment), a small plaque, and certificates of recognition. Up to two awards are given per year. The department purchases supplies on behalf of the winning director or co-director. Participants who complete the online Bass Class receive a Certificate of Completion.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Tournament directors or co-directors who are Maryland residents and run youth-oriented bass fishing tournaments where at least 50% of participants are between 16 and 25 years old.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of tournament supplies and equipment that support bass conservation and fish survival, such as aerators, rubber nets, mesh bags, bump tanks, release chutes, ice, thermometers, life jackets, non-piercing cull clips, barbless tackle, shade canopies, scales, and weigh-in systems.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: At least one organizer/co-organizer must be a Maryland resident. Tournament participants must hold a valid Maryland fishing license if required by law.
requirements_list: Director or co-director applicant must be a Maryland resident
Tournament participants must have a Maryland fishing license if required by law
Tournament must have at most 49 boats
At least 50% of angler participants must be between 16 and 25 years old (inclusive)
Director or co-director must identify at least one best management practice when obtaining a tournament permit from Fishing and Boating Services
All tournament participants must complete Fishing and Boating Services' online Bass Class
Director or co-director must submit a brief narrative (100 words or less) describing the tournament's supply needs and reasons for those needs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application electronically by May 1, 2025 to Ryan Gary at ryan.gary@maryland.gov. Applicants will be notified of their standing by June 1, 2025. If selected, the department will purchase supplies on behalf of the winner beginning July 1, 2025.

structured_extraction.program_name: Discounted Fishing and Hunting Licenses for Purple Heart Recipients
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland veterans who have received a Purple Heart for injuries sustained in service qualify for a 50% discount on Maryland hunting and fishing licenses.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 50% discount on Maryland hunting and fishing licenses for qualifying Purple Heart recipients.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland veterans who have received a Purple Heart
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Discounted hunting and fishing licenses in Maryland
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Maryland veterans statewide
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland veteran
Must have received a Purple Heart for injuries sustained in service

structured_extraction.program_name: Elk Neck State Forest Fuelwood Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program allows members of the public to obtain permits to collect and remove firewood (fuelwood) from down, damaged, or standing dead trees along designated driving trails at Elk Neck State Forest. Permittees may collect up to five standard pickup-truck loads per calendar year for personal use only. Re-sale of collected wood is not permitted. Daily permits cost $10.00 and are required before collecting wood.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Permitted individuals may collect firewood from designated areas of Elk Neck State Forest at a cost of $10.00 per daily permit. Each permittee is limited to one standard pickup-truck load per day (not exceeding one cord, and not exceeding the cab height of a standard pickup truck) and no more than five standard loads per calendar year. Operations are not permitted between September 1 and January 31, or on weekends or after hours. No more than three permittees are allowed per day. Resale of collected material is prohibited. Dump trucks and other heavy service vehicles are prohibited. Splitting of material on-site is prohibited.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Members of the public seeking firewood for personal use from Elk Neck State Forest in Cecil County, Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Personal use firewood collection from down, damaged, or standing dead trees along designated forest driving trails. Collected wood is for personal use only; resale is prohibited.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only at Elk Neck State Forest in Cecil County, Maryland. Operations are limited to the Trails Area, defined as within 200 linear feet of main driving trails, excluding Trail 2 south of Plum Creek and areas near Irishtown Road. Permittees must remain within the ENSF boundary and use designated Main Trails for firewood collection.
requirements_list: Permit required — obtained by submitting a Google Form application
Operations permitted only between February 1 and August 31 (no operations September 1 through January 31)
No weekend or after-hours operations
No more than three permittees per day
Maximum of five standard loads per permittee per calendar year
Maximum of one standard load per permittee per day
Standard load must not exceed cab height of pickup truck and must not exceed one cord
Collected wood is for personal use only — re-sale is prohibited
Standard pickups only — dump trucks and heavy service vehicles are prohibited
Splitting of material on-site is prohibited
Permittee must contact forest staff for load inspection before departing
Must be within ENSF boundary
Must use designated Main Trails for firewood collection
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Fill out the Google Form application at the link provided on the program page. 2. The forest will contact the applicant to schedule a payment date and start date. 3. After payment and permit issuance, the permittee will be escorted to the designated collection area. 4. Upon reaching the daily load limit, the permittee contacts forest staff for a load inspection before departing.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Forest Service offers a 50/50 cost-share program to help public land managers treat ash trees against the Emerald Ash Borer (EAB), an invasive beetle that kills ash trees. The most effective treatment is trunk injection with emamectin benzoate, which must be performed by a licensed pesticide applicator. The program is available statewide to local governments and conservation land managers. Educational guidance is also available for homeowners on identifying ash trees and protecting them from EAB through various insecticide treatment options.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 50/50 cost share for Emerald Ash Borer treatments on public land. The program covers trunk injection treatments with emamectin benzoate conducted by licensed pesticide applicators. Additionally, educational guidance is provided on insecticide treatment options (soil drenches, basal sprays, trunk injections), application methods, timing, costs, tree identification, and environmental protection measures.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public land managers including local governments and managers of conservation lands with ash trees threatened by Emerald Ash Borer, as well as Maryland homeowners with ash trees.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Trunk injection treatments with emamectin benzoate to protect ash trees from Emerald Ash Borer infestation on public lands. For homeowners, funds support insecticide treatment options to protect ash trees.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland, available to public land managers and homeowners.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a public land manager (e.g. local government or conservation land manager)
Treatments must be conducted by a licensed pesticide applicator
Trees must have less than 30% canopy loss for treatment to be effective
Treatments should be applied while trees are transpiring (after leaf-out/before leaf drop)
Avoid application within 25 feet of water bodies
Do not apply when heavy rainfall expected within 24 hours
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Emerald Ash Borer Treatment Program application (linked as a PDF on the page). For homeowners, report infested trees to extension.umd.edu/hgic and consult with an arborist or licensed pesticide applicator for professional treatment.

structured_extraction.program_description: This permit allows properly accredited scientists and public educational institutions to collect, capture, mark, release, salvage, or maintain rare, threatened, or endangered (RTE) animal and plant species in Maryland for scientific or educational purposes. The permit is required before anyone can work with state-listed RTE animal or plant species in the wild. It is valid through December 31 of the issuing year and requires an annual report by the same date.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A one-year permit (valid through December 31 of the issuing year) that authorizes the holder to collect, capture, mark, release, salvage, or maintain rare, threatened, or endangered species in Maryland for scientific or educational purposes. The permit costs $10, payable by check or money order to the Department of Natural Resources. An annual report must be submitted by December 31 of the issuing year.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Valid through December 31 of the issuing year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Accredited scientists, researchers, and public educational institutions seeking to collect or work with rare, threatened, or endangered species in Maryland for scientific or educational purposes.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Authorizes collection, capture, marking, release, salvage, and maintenance of rare, threatened, or endangered animal and plant species for scientific or educational purposes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland for activities involving state-listed rare, threatened, or endangered species.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a properly accredited person of known scientific attainment, or a public educational institution.
Purpose must be scientific or educational.
Must complete the Endangered Species permit application and submit it with a $10 fee (check or money order payable to Department of Natural Resources).
Complete all pages of application.
Provide project proposal with reason for study, objective, and justification.
List species to be collected with common and scientific names, numbers, age classes, and sex.
Specify methods of collection.
Specify final disposition of specimens.
List collectors in addition to applicant.
Specify specific areas and time period for collection.
Certification under penalty of perjury.
Annual report must be filed by December 31 of the issuing year.
May also need a Scientific Collection permit and/or an Aquatic (Fisheries) Scientific Collection permit depending on target species and methodology.
A federal permit from USFWS and/or USDA may also be required for migratory birds or federally listed species.
Compliance with Nongame and Endangered Species Conservation Act (Annotated Code of Maryland 10-2A-01) and COMAR 08.03.08 regulations.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Endangered Species permit application (available as a PDF on the program page) and mail it with a $10 check or money order to the Permits Coordinator at Wildlife and Heritage Service, Tawes State Office Building, 580 Taylor Ave., E-1, Annapolis MD 21401. You can also request the application by email at wildlifepermits.dnr@maryland.gov or by phone at (410) 260-8540. Office visits require a confirmed appointment.

structured_extraction.program_name: Exemption to Maryland Hunter Education Field Day Workshops for Military, Law Enforcement and Certain Handgun Permit Holders
structured_extraction.program_description: This program allows qualifying individuals who have completed Maryland's online hunter education course to skip the in-person field day workshop and still receive their hunter education certification card. Eligible groups include active-duty and honorably discharged military members, current and retired Maryland law enforcement officers, and holders of a current Maryland Permit to Carry a Handgun.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Qualifying individuals who complete the online hunter education course can request an exemption from the required in-person field day workshop. Upon approval, they receive their hunter education certification card by email. Processing takes up to four weeks after all required documents are submitted.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Active-duty or honorably discharged U.S. military members stationed in or residing in Maryland, current or retired Maryland law enforcement officers, and current holders of a Maryland Permit to Carry a Handgun who have completed the online hunter education course.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Exemption from the in-person field day workshop requirement for hunter education certification.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a permanent Maryland resident or, for active-duty military, stationed in Maryland. Retired law enforcement must have been employed by a Maryland law enforcement agency.
requirements_list: Must have completed Maryland's online hunter education course

Must qualify under one of the eligible professions/certifications: active-duty or honorably discharged U.S. military stationed in or residing in Maryland; current or retired Maryland law enforcement officer with Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission Police Officer Certification; or holder of a current State of Maryland Permit to Carry a Handgun (HQL does not qualify)
Must submit supporting documents including a copy of driver's license or state ID and online course completion document
Active law enforcement must provide current Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission compliance card and agency ID
Retired law enforcement must provide a letter on agency letterhead signed by agency head confirming prior employment as a police officer
Active-duty military must provide most recent Leave and Earnings Statement (with SSN redacted) and duty orders if a non-resident
Honorably discharged military must provide Member 4 DD-214 (with SSN redacted)
Handgun permit holders must provide front and back copy of current Maryland Permit to Carry a Handgun
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the online hunter education course, then submit an exemption request through the provided Google Form along with all required supporting documents. Allow up to four weeks for processing. Once approved, the certification card will be sent by email.

structured_extraction.program_name: Explore the Patuxent Teen Leadership Paddle
structured_extraction.program_description: A week-long canoeing expedition for high school students on the Patuxent River. Participants practice leadership and teamwork, conduct water quality tests, study plant communities, help with a stewardship project, camp by the riverside, and prepare meals together. The program builds environmental stewardship skills and ends with a presentation to local leaders and family. Scholarships are available for participants who need financial assistance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tiered pricing for participation: Tier III (reduced rate) is $200, Tier II (partially subsidized) is $250, and Tier I (closest to full cost) is $300. Scholarships are available through Friends of Jug Bay for participants who need additional financial assistance beyond Tier III. The program provides outdoor education, leadership training, and environmental science experience including camping, meals, water quality testing, and stewardship activities.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling, first come, first served basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: High school students interested in outdoor adventure, leadership, and environmental education along the Patuxent River.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participation in a week-long canoeing and environmental education expedition on the Patuxent River, including camping, meals, water quality testing, stewardship projects, and leadership skill building.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program takes place along the Patuxent River in Maryland, beginning at Patuxent River Park.
requirements_list: Must be a high school student
Must apply via the online application form
Applications accepted on a rolling, first come, first served basis
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the online application form available at the program page or through teenpaddle.com. Applications are accepted on a rolling, first come, first served basis. Contact Olivia Wisner at olivia.wisner1@maryland.gov with questions or to request a scholarship.

structured_extraction.program_name: Farmers and Hunters Feeding the Hungry (FHFH)
structured_extraction.program_description: A program administered by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources that pays the full processing fees for hunters and farmers who donate deer to feed hungry people in Maryland. Hunters field dress and bring legally tagged deer to participating meat processors, and FHFH covers the full processing cost using cash donations from churches, foundations, businesses, and individuals. The processed venison is then distributed through food banks, church pantries, and other community organizations serving people in need across Maryland. The average deer yields about 40 pounds of meat at an effective processing cost of approximately $1.64 per pound.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: FHFH pays the full discounted processing fee for donated deer brought to approved participating meat processors. Processors charge a special reduced rate and FHFH covers that cost entirely on behalf of the donor. The average deer yields about 40 pounds of meat at an effective processing cost of approximately $1.64 per pound.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Hunters and farmers in Maryland who want to donate harvested deer to feed people in need
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Covers the cost of processing donated deer at participating approved meat processors so that venison can be distributed to food banks, church pantries, and community organizations
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland during bow, muzzleloader, and firearms deer seasons
requirements_list: Deer must be legally tagged
Hunter or farmer must field dress the deer
Deer must be brought to a participating approved meat processor
Farmers may also donate deer taken under a Deer Damage Permit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Field dress your legally tagged deer and bring it to the nearest participating FHFH meat processor. Visit feedingthehungry.org to find a list of donation locations.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Boating Access Program is a federally funded program administered by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources' Waterway Improvement and Infrastructure Program, as part of the federal Wildlife and Sport Fish Restoration (WSFR) Program administered by the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service. It provides federal funding for the construction and renovation of publicly owned boat ramps and associated amenities used by recreational, trailered motorboat owners. Funding comes from excise taxes on fishing equipment and motorboat/small engine fuels, apportioned to states by formula. Maryland receives approximately $500,000 in Sport Fish Restoration funding per year for boating access, with at least 15% of each state's federal apportionment required to go toward boating access. The program offers up to 75% federal funding with a minimum 25% local/state match required, and is open year round on a reimbursement basis.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal grant funding (reimbursement-based) covering up to 75% of eligible project costs, with a minimum 25% local/state match required. Funds design and construction of public boat ramps, parking lots, access roads, bulkheads, breakwaters, piers, and associated amenities for recreational trailered motorboats. Maryland receives approximately $500,000 per year in Sport Fish Restoration funding for boating access. Funding is derived from excise taxes on fishing equipment and motorboat/small engine fuels, apportioned to states by formula, with at least 15% of each state's federal apportionment directed to boating access.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local jurisdictions interested in constructing or renovating publicly owned boat ramps and associated recreational boating access infrastructure in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction and renovation of public boat ramps, trailer parking areas, access roads, bulkheads, breakwaters, piers, and associated amenities for recreational trailered motorboats. Includes design and construction services; expenses are reimbursable after Land Control Agreement execution.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across all Maryland counties.
requirements_list: Applicants must be local jurisdictions (public entities)
Projects must involve publicly owned boat ramps
Ramps must be used by recreational, trailered motorboats
Local jurisdiction must obtain all necessary permits
Submit project plans and specifications to the Department for review and approval
Advertise project for bid; submit bid tabulations and recommended award for Department approval before contract award
Facility must be reasonably available to the public (physical access, equitable fees, open periods)
ADA accessibility guidelines must be applied and appropriate signage must be posted
Any fees must be Department-approved and non-discriminatory (same rates for all users including out-of-state boaters)
Minimum 25% local/state match required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Program is open year round on a rolling basis. Contact the Federal Boating Access Program Projects Lead, Jennifer Jackson, for information on how to apply. Process involves submitting project plans and specifications for Department review and approval, advertising for bid, and submitting bid tabulations for approval prior to contract award. Reimbursement is made after a Land Control Agreement is executed.

structured_extraction.program_name: Federal Estate Tax Exclusion for Conservation Easements
structured_extraction.program_description: Landowners who donate a conservation easement on their property can reduce its taxable estate value for federal estate tax purposes. A conservation easement limits development potential, lowering the appraised land value of the property. An additional estate tax exclusion of up to 40% of land value (capped at $500,000 per owner) is available for land subject to a donated easement, as governed by 26 U.S.C. § 2031(c). Because an easement limits development potential, it lowers the appraised value of land, reducing the overall taxable estate beyond the standard deduction. This exclusion is available to federal taxpayers nationwide, including Maryland landowners. Also referenced as 'The American Farm and Ranch Protection Act,' the program combines IRC Section 2055(f) and 2031(c) benefits and provides a post-mortem option for heirs to donate easements after the landowner's death and still receive estate tax benefits.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Conservation easements reduce the taxable value of an estate by limiting development potential through a donated conservation easement. An additional partial exclusion of up to 40% of land value (maximum $500,000 per owner) is available under 26 U.S.C. § 2031(c) for land subject to a donated easement, reduced 2% for each percentage point the easement value is below 30% of land value. An additional deduction is available under IRC 2055(f), and income tax deductions are available under IRC 170(h) for pre-mortem donations. The easement also lowers the appraised value of the land by limiting its development potential, further reducing the overall taxable estate.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Due date for filing estate tax return (generally nine months from decedent's death)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners with property having public value for open space, agriculture, wildlife habitat, or recreation; estate executors and heirs; landowners seeking to preserve family lands; and estate planners seeking to reduce federal estate tax liability.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of federal estate tax liability on land subject to a donated conservation easement.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to federal taxpayers nationwide, including Maryland landowners statewide with qualifying donated conservation easements. Property anywhere in the United States is eligible as of the 2001 tax law changes. Maryland Environmental Trust is a qualifying donee organization for conservation easement donations.
requirements_list: Land must be subject to a donated conservation easement
Governed by 26 United States Code section 2031(c) and IRC 2055(f)
Easement must meet IRS requirements for qualified conservation contributions under 26 U.S.C. § 2031(c)
Exclusion is reduced 2% for each percentage point the easement value is below 30% of land value
Post-mortem election must be made by the due date for the estate tax return, generally nine months from the decedent's death
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Consult a tax advisor or estate planning attorney. Donate a qualifying conservation easement to Maryland Environmental Trust or another qualified organization (public charity or governmental entity). Heirs may also elect to donate an easement post-mortem. The reduced appraised value and exclusion are applied when calculating federal estate taxes, and the exclusion is claimed when filing the federal estate tax return.

structured_extraction.program_name: Federal Income Tax Deduction for Conservation Easement Donations
structured_extraction.program_description: Landowners who donate a conservation easement to a qualified organization or government unit, such as the Maryland Environmental Trust (MET), can claim a federal income tax deduction equal to the appraised value of the easement. The deduction is capped at 50% of adjusted gross income per year (or 100% for IRS-qualified farmers and ranchers), with any remaining amount carried forward for up to 15 years. The easement must be perpetual and donated exclusively for conservation purposes as defined by the IRS. The deduction value equals the appraised property value before the easement minus the value after restrictions are imposed.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal income tax deduction equal to the appraised value of the donated conservation easement. Deduction is capped at 50% of adjusted gross income (100% for IRS-qualified farmers/ranchers) in the year of donation, with carry-forward for up to 15 years. The deduction value equals the appraised property value before the easement minus the value after restrictions are imposed. A qualified appraiser must establish the easement value. IRS Form 8283 must be attached to the federal tax return. If the donation value exceeds $500,000, a copy of the appraisal must also be submitted to the IRS. Deduction amount may be reduced if the easement increases the value of other property owned by the donor or a related person.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners who donate a perpetual conservation easement to Maryland Environmental Trust or another qualified governmental unit or §501(c)(3) charitable organization.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of federal income tax liability through a charitable deduction for the donated conservation easement value. Qualifying conservation purposes include: preservation of land areas for outdoor recreation or education, protection of natural habitats and ecosystems, preservation of open space (farmland, forest land), and preservation of historically important land areas or certified historic structures.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to federal taxpayers nationwide, including Maryland landowners donating easements statewide; administered through the Maryland Environmental Trust. Property must be located within United States jurisdiction and subject to state and local recording requirements.
requirements_list: Easement must be perpetual and donated exclusively for conservation purposes as defined by the IRS
Easement must be conveyed to a qualified governmental unit or §501(c)(3) charitable organization
A qualified appraiser must determine the value of the donated easement
IRS Form 8283 must be attached to the federal tax return
If donation value exceeds $500,000, a copy of the appraisal must be submitted with the form to the IRS
Donor must attach a statement identifying conservation purposes, before/after valuation, and any related interests in nearby property
Property must be a qualified real property interest
Donation must further a clearly delineated federal, state, or local conservation policy
Must meet one of four conservation purpose categories: scenic enjoyment, protection of open space, historic preservation, or other qualified purposes
Significant public benefit must be demonstrated
Appropriate public access must be provided (requirements vary by conservation purpose)
No inconsistent uses permitted unless necessary for conservation protection
If mortgaged property (post-Feb. 13, 1986): mortgagee must subordinate mortgage
Deduction amount reduced if easement increases value of other property owned by donor or related person
Donor/related person must not receive greater financial benefits than general public
Substantiation requirements per § 1.170A-13(c) must be met
Property restrictions must be binding in perpetuity and legally enforceable, recorded in land records
Qualified appraisal required for noncash contributions exceeding $5,000 deduction
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Obtain a qualified appraiser to determine easement value. Complete IRS Form 8283 and the required statement identifying conservation purposes, before/after valuation, and any related interests in nearby property. Send to Maryland Environmental Trust for donee acknowledgment signature (allow at least 10 business days). Attach the completed form and statement to your federal income tax return. Governed by Internal Revenue Code § 170(h) and Treasury Regulations § 1.170A–14.

structured_extraction.program_description: This permit allows private landowners or operators to offer pay-to-fish opportunities on privately-controlled ponds or lakes. Paying customers can catch and keep fish without needing a Maryland Recreational Fishing License.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: An annual permit is issued for a $25 fee (payable by check, money order, or online). The permit authorizes the holder to operate a fee-fishing lake or pond where paying customers can fish without a Maryland Recreational Fishing License. Fish stocked must come from approved commercial hatcheries or licensed sellers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private landowners or operators who own, lease, or control a pond or lake and want to offer fishing for a fee to the public.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Permit authorizes operation of a pay-fishing facility on private land; not a grant or loan.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — available to eligible operators anywhere in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must own, lease, or control the pond or lake where fishing will occur
Fish stocked must be from an approved supplier (commercially propagated or purchased from licensed sellers)
Must obtain a fish stocking permit before stocking additional fish
Must maintain shipping and receiving records by species at the facility
Must notify DNR immediately upon discovery of any fish disease
Any invasive or nonnative species found must be euthanized on-site and not returned to Maryland waters
Must include a map showing facility location with directions from nearest major roadway with the initial application
Must provide a description of the fee fishing operation and sketch of facility, ponds, inflow/effluent
Must provide workmen's compensation insurance certificate if employing staff
Annual $25 permit fee must be paid
Must submit annual activity report
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Fee Fishing Lake Permit Application (PDF or online form at the Google Forms link). Include a map of the fishing location with your initial application. Pay the $25 annual fee by check, money order, or through the online payment system. Submit application and inquiries to paylakes.dnr@maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free outreach and technical assistance program run by the Maryland Forest Service that helps homeowners and communities in wildland-urban interface (WUI) areas reduce their wildfire risk. Services include community wildfire protection planning, home risk assessments, brush chipping clean-up days, hazard fuel reduction projects, and education on defensible space and fire-resistant landscaping.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free services provided to qualifying Maryland residents and communities, including: community outreach and education, HOA meeting presentations, community wildfire protection planning, wildfire risk assessments, wildfire home risk assessments and Home Ignition Zone analysis, community clean-up days with brush chipping services, hazard fuel reduction projects, and assistance becoming a nationally recognized Firewise Community.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners, homeowner associations, and communities located in wildland-urban interface areas throughout Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reducing wildfire risk through education, planning, home risk assessments, brush chipping, and hazard fuel reduction.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to qualifying Maryland residents and communities statewide, with a focus on wildland-urban interface areas.
requirements_list: Must be a qualifying Maryland resident or community in a wildland-urban interface area
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Firewise Maryland program by calling 410-742-6520 or emailing lance.carroll@maryland.gov to request services.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free recreational fishing award program that recognizes anglers who catch trophy-sized fish in Maryland. Anglers can report catches of more than 60 eligible species across five categories (Atlantic Coast, Chesapeake Bay, Nontidal, Catch and Release, and Invasive) at or above a minimum size to receive recognition.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free recreational fishing award program that showcases Maryland as a fishing destination. Participants catch and report trophy-sized fish in eligible species categories to earn awards and recognition.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Any angler fishing legally in Maryland, including residents and visitors of all ages.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Award recognition for catching and reporting trophy-sized fish in Maryland waters.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to anyone fishing legally in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must fish legally in Maryland
Must catch and report a fish at or above the minimum size threshold
Fish must be one of more than 60 eligible species in five categories
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Catch an eligible trophy-sized fish, then submit a report through the FishMaryland program page.

structured_extraction.program_description: A training program that gives participants the skills and knowledge to run beginner fishing lessons through their own organization. Completing the training qualifies participants to borrow fishing gear from the state for free and for extended use in their fishing lessons.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free instructor training sessions available Tuesday through Thursday, 8am–4pm, November through April. At least 10 participants are required per training session. Upon completion, participants may borrow fishing gear from the state at no cost for an extended period to use in their beginner fishing lessons.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Youth organizations, schools, scout troops, parks, nature centers, 4-H clubs, libraries, summer camps, community groups, and individuals age 18 or older who want to teach beginner fishing lessons.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training to run beginner fishing lessons and borrowing fishing equipment from the state for use in those lessons.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must have at least 10 participants to request training
Participants must be 18 years of age or older
Must have or acquire a fishing license prior to the training
Must report on use of borrowed equipment after training
Must maintain all borrowed equipment
Must return any borrowed equipment upon completion of fishing lessons
Schedule training in advance — limited availability, may need to book up to a year ahead
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Chelsea Kenworthy to schedule a training session. Training is available Tuesday through Thursday, 8am–4pm, from November through April. Scheduling well in advance is strongly recommended as availability is limited and may require booking up to a year ahead.

structured_extraction.program_description: Flying WILD is a bird education and conservation program for educators. Participants attend a 3-6 hour workshop led by certified trainers and receive an activity guide called 'Flying WILD: An Educator's Guide to Celebrating Birds.' The workshops give educators hands-on experience with a variety of bird-focused activities they can use in their classrooms or programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Educators attend a 3-6 hour workshop with certified trainers and receive a free copy of 'Flying WILD: An Educator's Guide to Celebrating Birds.' Alternatively, the guide can be purchased directly from the Association of Fish and Wildlife Agencies online store.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Educators interested in bird education and conservation
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educator training in bird education and conservation activities
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Two training partners are available in Maryland: one at the Ward Museum of Wildfowl Art in Salisbury and one at Black Hill Nature Programs in Boyds (Montgomery County).
requirements_list: Must attend a 3-6 hour workshop with certified trainers to receive the free activity guide
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the training partner nearest you to inquire about upcoming workshop opportunities, or check the Maryland DNR professional development page for scheduled events.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Forest Conservation Act (FCA) requires that any land development project of 40,000 square feet or more that needs a subdivision, grading, or sediment control permit must assess and protect existing forests as part of the planning process. Developers must submit a Forest Stand Delineation and a Forest Conservation Plan before proceeding. The program integrates forest protection into the earliest stages of land planning and development, prioritizing conservation of forests near streams, wetlands, steep slopes, and wildlife corridors. When clearing is unavoidable, developers must replant trees on-site or at approved off-site locations. As of 2022, the program shifted from a 'no net loss' benchmark to a net gain goal for forest cover.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The FCA provides a regulatory framework with technical guidance for protecting forests during land development. Qualified Professionals (QPs) trained and certified by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources help landowners and developers prepare Forest Stand Delineations and Forest Conservation Plans. Local county and municipal forest conservation programs implement the requirements, providing project-level oversight and review. Three types of Forest Stand Delineations (Simplified, Intermediate, Full) are available based on project complexity. When on-site or off-site planting cannot be accomplished, developers may contribute to the Forest Conservation Fund as a fee-in-lieu option. Long-term protection instruments include conservation easements, deed restrictions, covenants, Forest Management Plans, and Forest Conservation and Management Agreements.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners, developers, planners, licensed foresters, landscape architects, engineers, surveyors, and others undertaking development projects of 40,000 square feet or more requiring subdivision, grading, or sediment control permits in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Forest conservation planning, forest stand delineation, reforestation, and afforestation as part of land development projects; optional fee-in-lieu contributions to the Forest Conservation Fund when on-site or off-site planting cannot be accomplished; tree protection and maintenance during construction
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland; implemented locally by counties and municipalities with approved forest conservation programs. Applies to all Maryland counties and municipalities. Priority areas include stream buffers, floodplains, wetlands, steep slopes, wildlife corridors, and urban forests.
requirements_list: Project must involve 40,000 square feet (approximately one acre) or more
Project must require a subdivision, grading, or sediment control permit
Must submit a Forest Stand Delineation (FSD) prior to approval; approved FSD valid for five years
Must submit a Forest Conservation Plan (FCP) for approval before proceeding
FSD and FCP must be prepared by a Maryland Licensed Forester, Licensed Landscape Architect, or Qualified Professional certified by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources
Environmental features mapping required (floodplains, streams, wetlands, steep slopes, sensitive habitats)
Priority forest identification required per §5-1607
Forest Retention Areas must be a minimum of 10,000 square feet continuous cover
No construction activities permitted in retention areas
Critical Root Zone (CRZ) protection required (minimum 1 foot radius per inch of DBH for stand edges; 1.5 feet per inch for isolated trees)
Minimum forest cover thresholds must be met based on land-use category and zoning (Conservation Threshold)
Reforestation/afforestation must be completed within one year or two growing seasons after project completion
Minimum two-year maintenance and monitoring agreement required for afforested/reforested areas
Financial security required for monitoring agreements as approved by approving authority
Species must be native to physiographic region unless approved alternatives are specified
Reforestation minimum: 100 live trees per acre with 50% reaching 2-inch diameter within 7 years
Logging operations must file a Declaration of Intent stating no development for at least 5 years post-logging
Exemptions may apply based on determination by the State or local Forest Conservation Program Coordinator
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants work with a Qualified Professional to prepare a Forest Stand Delineation (FSD), which is submitted to the local authority for review (30 days for approval). A Preliminary Forest Conservation Plan is then submitted (45 days for approval), followed by a Final Forest Conservation Plan. Once both are approved, other required permits are issued. Reforestation or afforestation must occur within one year of project completion, with a minimum 2-year maintenance and monitoring agreement established. Where no local program exists, submit to DNR directly. Check with the local program for specific submission requirements.

structured_extraction.program_name: Forest Conservation Act Qualified Professional Certification
structured_extraction.program_description: Certification program for qualified professionals approved by DNR Forest Service to submit forest stand delineations and forest conservation plans under Maryland's Forest Conservation Act. Qualified Professionals help ensure that development projects identify and protect priority forest areas, comply with state and local requirements, and support Maryland's smart growth and forest stewardship goals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Applicants who meet education and experience requirements and complete a DNR Forest Service-approved forest conservation training program may apply for Qualified Professional status. Once approved by the State Forest Conservation Manager, they are authorized to submit forest stand delineations and forest conservation plans under the Forest Conservation Act. Applicants designate the county or counties where they will accept work, or may select all counties.
structured_extraction.contact_phone: 410-260-8DNR or toll-free 877-620-8DNR; TTY via Maryland Relay
structured_extraction.program_audience: Natural resource professionals, licensed foresters, licensed landscape architects, and other professionals with relevant degrees and experience in natural resource sciences, natural resource management, landscape planning, or environmental planning who wish to submit forest stand delineations and forest conservation plans in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Professional certification to submit forest stand delineations and forest conservation plans for development projects subject to Maryland's Forest Conservation Act.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — applicant designates the county or counties where they will accept work; may select all counties in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must hold a four-year degree in natural resource sciences, natural resource management, landscape planning, or environmental planning; OR have 4 years of appropriate professional experience; OR hold a graduate degree in natural resources plus at least 1 year of professional experience
Must successfully complete a MD DNR Forest Service approved forest conservation training program (e.g., offered through Anne Arundel Community College or Carroll Community College)
Must submit transcripts
Must submit a resume
Must submit a certificate of completion of forest conservation training
Must provide supervisor verification of competence under penalty of perjury
Must submit a completed Qualified Professional Application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download the Qualified Professional Application from the DNR website. Submit the completed application along with proof of course completion, transcripts, resume, certificate of training completion, and supervisor verification by email to FCA.DNR@maryland.gov or by mail to the address listed on the application form. The State Forest Conservation Manager reviews and grants final approval.

structured_extraction.program_name: Forest Conservation and Management Agreement Income Tax Subtraction
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland private landowners who get approved to enter into a Forest Conservation and Management Plan with the Maryland Department of Natural Resources can subtract up to $500 in qualified conservation program expenses from their Maryland state income taxes. Landowners report this subtraction on Maryland Form 502SU, Line 13, using code letter kk.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible landowners can subtract up to $500 in qualified conservation program expenses from their Maryland state taxable income on Form 502SU, Line 13, using code letter kk, once approved by the Department of Natural Resources to enter into a Forest Conservation and Management Plan.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private landowners in Maryland who have an approved Forest Conservation and Management Plan with the Maryland Department of Natural Resources
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax subtraction for qualified conservation program expenses related to a Forest Conservation and Management Plan, subtracted from Maryland state taxable income
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to residents filing Maryland state taxes
requirements_list: Must have an application approved by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources to enter into a Forest Conservation and Management Plan
Must enter into a Forest Conservation and Management Plan
Must file Maryland state taxes using Maryland Form 502SU
Qualified conservation program expenses must be up to $500
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply for the Forest Conservation and Management Program through the Maryland Department of Natural Resources. Once approved, report qualified conservation program expenses on Maryland Form 502SU, Line 13, code letter kk when filing state taxes. Consult a tax professional for details.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Forest Conservation and Management Program (FCMP), established in 1957, provides landowners with a financial incentive to conserve and responsibly manage their forestland by minimizing the loss of Maryland's forest resources during land development. Participants sign a legally binding Forest Conservation and Management Agreement (FCMA) with the Maryland Department of Natural Resources and receive a reduced, stabilized property tax assessment — generally at the agricultural rate — for the life of the agreement (minimum 15 years). The assessed value of enrolled forest land is frozen (for example, from $5,000/acre to $125/acre). Enrolled landowners must develop a forest stewardship plan that includes a schedule of stewardship practices covering fish and wildlife support, natural heritage, recreation, soil and water management, and forest products. The program identifies and protects forests and other sensitive areas, and provides free forest management plans drawn up by a forester for eligible Maryland landowners. Private forests provide broad public benefits including water quality protection, wildlife habitat, carbon storage, flood control, erosion control, open space for beauty and recreation, and support for rural economies. If the agreement is terminated early, back taxes are assessed retroactively to the start of the agreement.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A forester draws up a free forest management plan for eligible landowners at no cost. Enrolled forestland receives a reduced property tax assessment — generally at the agricultural rate — with the assessed value frozen for the life of the agreement (minimum 15 years); for example, assessed value may drop from $5,000/acre to $125/acre. The landowner enters a legally binding Forest Conservation and Management Agreement (FCMA) recorded in county land records. Enrollment requires the development of a forest stewardship plan that includes a schedule of stewardship practices related to fish and wildlife, natural heritage, recreation, soil and water, and forest products. Annual inspection and entry fees apply. If the agreement is terminated early, back taxes are assessed retroactively to the start of the agreement. Open land recently planted with tree seedlings can be included after one growing season, as can Christmas tree plantations harvested at maturity. House sites, cropland, and other non-forest open spaces are not eligible.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland property owners with five or more contiguous acres of forestland, including individuals and landowners who are developing or managing forested land in Maryland, who want to conserve and manage their forest in exchange for reduced property taxes.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Forest management planning, identification and protection of forests and sensitive areas during land development, forest stewardship and conservation practices on enrolled forested land, and reduction and stabilization of property tax assessments on enrolled forestland in exchange for responsible forest management under an approved forest management plan. Funds are not distributed to landowners but represent foregone tax liability.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to any landowner with five or more contiguous acres of forestland, including forested tracts, newly reforested land (after one growing season), and Christmas tree plantations harvested at maturity.
requirements_list: Must own five or more contiguous acres of forestland
Must be a Maryland resident or property owner
Eligible land must be forested, newly reforested (after one growing season), or a Christmas tree plantation harvested at maturity
Non-forest land such as house sites, crop fields, and open land is not eligible
Must enter into a Forest Conservation and Management Agreement (FCMA) with the Maryland Department of Natural Resources
Agreement must be guided by a forest management plan prepared specifically for the property
Must develop a forest stewardship plan for the property
Plan must include a schedule of stewardship practices related to fish and wildlife, natural heritage, recreation, soil and water, and forest products
Minimum agreement term is fifteen years
Must comply with the forest management plan throughout the agreement period
If the agreement is terminated early, back taxes are assessed retroactively to the start of the agreement
Landowner must agree to manage forest land according to a department-prepared management plan
Annual inspection and entry fees apply
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local Maryland Forest Service office. Forestry staff will answer questions, explain requirements, prepare or review a forest management plan, and guide you through enrollment. The FCMA is recorded in county land records. You may also apply through the Maryland Forest Service's Forest Conservation and Management Program page on the DNR website.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Natural Resources Forest Service (MDNR-FS) and the USDA Farm Services Agency (USDA-FSA) offer cost share assistance to landowners to help cover the cost of recommended forest improvement practices. A county forester provides technical assistance, helps find vendors, and reports completion of the work. Assistance typically covers 50% to 75% of the total cost of an approved forestry practice. Three specific programs are available: the Environmental Quality Incentive Program (EQIP), the Woodland Incentive Program (WIP), and the Conservation Reserve Enhancement Program (CREP). Eligibility depends on property size and fund availability, and a forest stewardship management plan is typically required before receiving assistance. Funding must be allocated before any work begins.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Cost share assistance reimburses landowners for 50% to 75% of the total cost of recommended forestry practices. Three programs are available: Environmental Quality Incentive Program (EQIP), Woodland Incentive Program (WIP), and Conservation Reserve Enhancement Program (CREP). Eligibility depends on property size and fund availability. A forest stewardship management plan is typically required before receiving assistance. Funding must be allocated before any work begins.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Forest landowners in Maryland seeking to offset the cost of forest improvement practices on their private forest land
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Implementing recommended forestry practices on private forest land as outlined in a forest stewardship management plan, including defraying costs of forest improvement practices
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland; eligibility depends on property size and availability of funds. Contact your county forester for local details.
requirements_list: Must be a landowner
Must have a forest stewardship management plan written for the property (in most cases)
Property size requirements apply
Eligibility depends on property size and availability of funds
Funding must be allocated prior to beginning any work
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your county forester to get started. The forester can provide technical specifications, set up recommended practices, help identify contract crews to perform the work, and report on completed work.

structured_extraction.program_name: Forest Incentives Program (FIP) and Environmental Quality Incentives Program (EQIP) Cost Share
structured_extraction.program_description: A nationwide federal cost-share program administered by the USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service (NRCS) for private non-industrial forest landowners to implement approved forest management and conservation practices. Eligible practices include tree planting, stand improvement, and site preparation for natural regeneration. Federal cost-share money is available with a limit of $10,000 per person per year, with cost-share limited to no more than 65% of the cost of implementing an approved forestry practice. The program is available statewide in Maryland through local USDA-NRCS offices and is often referenced as a complementary resource alongside state forestry programs such as the Maryland Tree Farm program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal cost-share financial assistance for private non-industrial forest landowners implementing eligible forest management and conservation practices. Cost-share is available up to a limit of $10,000 per person per year, with cost-share limited to no more than 65% of the cost of implementing an approved forestry practice. Available in counties designated based on a Forest Service survey of eligible private timber acreage. Specific amounts and terms are determined by the local USDA-NRCS office.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private non-industrial forest landowners in Maryland, including individuals, groups, associations, or corporations with non-publicly traded stock not primarily engaged in manufacturing forest products or public utility services
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tree planting; improving a stand of forest trees; site preparation for natural regeneration; implementation of eligible forest management and conservation practices.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland through local USDA-NRCS offices; available in counties designated based on a Forest Service survey of eligible private timber acreage. Contact local USDA office to confirm county participation in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must own no more than 1,000 acres of eligible forest land (exceptions possible in public interest)
Must be a private landowner of non-industrial forest land
Individuals, groups, associations, or corporations with non-publicly traded stock may be eligible if not primarily engaged in manufacturing forest products or public utility services
Land must be suitable for afforestation, reforestation, or improved forest management
Land must be capable of producing marketable timber crops and meet minimum productivity standards
At least 10 acres of eligible forest land required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the USDA Service Center in your county or the NRCS Annapolis Service Center for information on which counties participate and to apply. Visit the USDA-NRCS office locator to find your local office.

structured_extraction.program_description: Suite of programs providing technical and financial assistance for establishment, protection, planning, and management of forests on private non-industrial forest lands. Includes Forest Stewardship Plans, cost-share programs, tax incentives, equipment rental, tree seedlings, and various forestry services. Available statewide across all Maryland counties, organized into four regional offices.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Forest Stewardship Plans (long-range management plans incorporating landowner objectives); Timber Stand Improvement Marking ($12/acre); Forestry Services Coordination ($4/acre); Planting Site Examinations ($40 flat fee); Equipment Rental; Tree seedlings from State Nursery (at cost, orders taken first-come first-served basis beginning in fall for spring shipment); Cost-share programs: WIP (65% funding, 5-1,000 acres), EQIP (variable cost-share), CRP/CREP (financial incentives for vegetative buffers and erosion control); Tax incentives: FCMA, Woodland Assessment, MD Income Tax Modification, Public Law 96-451. Services and fees vary by region.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Tree seedling orders taken on first-come, first-served basis beginning in fall for spring shipment; no specific deadline for other services
structured_extraction.contact_phone: 410-260-8531 (Forest Service main); 1-877-620-8DNR ext. 8531 (toll-free); TTY: 711 (MD) or 800-735-2258 (out of state); 1-800-TREES-MD (John S. Ayton Tree Nursery)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private non-industrial forest landowners in Maryland seeking help managing, establishing, or protecting forested land
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reforestation, site preparation, wildlife enhancement, timber stand improvement, forest management and stewardship activities, tree planting, equipment rental, forestry services coordination on private non-industrial forest lands
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across all Maryland counties, organized into four regions: Central (Baltimore City, Baltimore, Carroll, Cecil, Harford, Howard, Montgomery), Eastern (Caroline, Dorchester, Kent, Queen Anne's, Somerset, Talbot, Wicomico, Worcester), Southern (Anne Arundel, Calvert, Charles, Prince George's, St. Mary's), and Western (Allegany, Frederick, Garrett, Washington). Priority Areas apply for certain programs; 10-500 acres for Forest Stewardship Plan assistance; 5-1,000 acres for cost-share programs.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a private non-industrial forest landowner in Maryland
Forest Stewardship Plan required for State and Federal cost-share programs and FCMA participation
Minimum woodland acreage varies by program: 10-500 acres for Forest Stewardship Plans, 5-1,000 acres for cost-share programs
Property must be located in a Priority Area for certain programs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Maryland DNR Forest Service regional office corresponding to your county. Regional brochures outlining services and fees are available for download. Tree seedling orders are taken on a first-come, first-served basis beginning in fall for spring shipment. Main contact: 410-260-8531 or 1-877-620-8DNR ext. 8531.

structured_extraction.program_description: A required license for any person who wants to buy, sell, acquire, transport, ship, or store the fur or pelt of any wild quadruped (four-legged animal) taken within or outside Maryland. Both resident and non-resident options are available.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A Fur Dealer's License authorizes the holder to legally buy, sell, acquire, transport, ship, or store fur or pelts of wild quadrupeds. Resident license fee is $50.00; non-resident fee is $100.00. Licenses expire on June 30 following the date of issuance. Renewal requires submission of a ledger documenting all transactions. Out-of-state fur shipments require a completed Fur Shipping Record form with one copy retained with the pelts and one copy returned to DNR.
