structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Licenses expire June 30; renewal applications submitted June 1–10 each year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and businesses who buy, sell, acquire, transport, ship, or store wild animal fur or pelts in Maryland, including resident and non-resident fur dealers and fur trappers
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: License authorizes fur dealing activities; not a funding program
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Maryland residents (with 6-month residency requirement for resident license) and non-residents who wish to deal in fur or pelts in Maryland
requirements_list: Resident applicants must have lived in Maryland for at least 6 months before applying
Must complete the application form provided by Wildlife and Heritage Service
Must pay applicable fee ($50.00 for residents; $100.00 for non-residents)
Must provide date of birth and SSN/Tax ID/FID
Must provide workers' compensation insurance compliance documentation, or certify self-employed/family-only employment
Must provide insurance binder number or certificate of insurance if applicable
Must provide information on related state and federal licenses/permits
Non-resident applicants must provide a copy of current Maryland non-resident hunting license
Must maintain a ledger recording all fur transactions including seller name, address, DNR ID or license number, date, species, quantity, origin location, and final disposition
Must submit ledger and renewal application between June 1 and June 10 each year
Must allow Natural Resources Police or other law enforcement to inspect premises and records
Must carry license and show it on demand

Out-of-state fur shipments must have special shipping tags/Fur Shipping Record forms attached to the outside of each package, including trapper name and address, date shipped, type of furbearer, county of capture, and recipient name, address, and license number
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the completed resident or non-resident fur dealer permit application with fee and supporting documentation by mail, email, or phone to the Permits Coordinator at Maryland DNR Wildlife and Heritage Service (Tawes State Office Building). Walk-in appointments require prior scheduling by email or phone. Permit expires June 30th following issuance date; annual renewal requires submission of transaction ledger between June 1 and June 10.

structured_extraction.program_description: A lifetime pass that gives Maryland residents aged 62 and older free day-use entry to all state parks that charge service fees (per-vehicle fee waived for everyone in the vehicle when the cardholder is present), half-price camping at campsites and mini-cabins (Sunday through Thursday, excluding holidays, for one site), and waived boat launching fees at Maryland State Parks. A $10 processing fee applies, and the pass is non-transferable.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A non-transferable lifetime pass available for a $10 processing fee. Pass holders receive free day-use entry to all state parks that charge service fees (per-vehicle fee waived for everyone in the vehicle when the cardholder is present), half-price camping on campsites and mini-cabins (Sunday through Thursday, excluding holidays) for one site, and waived boat launch fees at Maryland State Parks. If lost or stolen, a new pass must be purchased.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents who are 62 years of age or older.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free day-use entry to state parks, half-price camping at campsites and mini-cabins (Sunday through Thursday, excluding holidays), and waived boat launching fees at Maryland State Parks.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at all Maryland State Parks statewide that charge service fees.
requirements_list: Must be 62 years of age or older
Must provide valid proof of age (U.S. Passport, Birth Certificate, Driver's License, or State-Issued ID)
$10 processing fee required
Pass is non-transferable and for cardholders only (unless a per-vehicle fee is in effect)
Passholder must be present and part of the camping party for the entire stay when using the camping discount
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Purchase the pass online at shopdnr.com and upload a valid age-verification document (U.S. Passport, Birth Certificate, Driver's License, or State Issued ID). Alternatively, purchase in person at designated state parks (call ahead to verify availability). If unable to upload proof of age online, mail a copy of the document along with the purchase confirmation to Maryland Park Service, 580 Taylor Avenue, E-3, Annapolis, MD 21401. The physical pass will be mailed within 7–10 days and is not valid until the physical pass is received.

structured_extraction.program_description: A DNR wildlife biologist consults with government agencies to identify appropriate deer management techniques and helps design a plan to manage deer on government-controlled properties.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A DNR wildlife biologist consults with government agency representatives to recommend deer management techniques and assists in designing a deer management plan for government-controlled properties.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Government agency representatives seeking assistance with deer management on properties they control.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Technical guidance and planning assistance for deer management.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Request must come from a government agency representative.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Kevin Lamp, Deer Project Leader, to request assistance.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Greenspace Equity Program is a competitive grant program that provides funding to eligible applicants to improve public health and livability in overburdened and underserved communities by preserving, creating, and enhancing public greenspace. Eligible projects include land acquisition (fee simple or perpetual conservation easement) and stewardship activities such as community gardens, parks, trails, urban farms, woodland areas, green networks, and community gathering spaces. The program is funded from the state share of Program Open Space, subject to annual budget actions; the FY 2025 grant round awarded $4.3 million. Geographic diversity across the state is a selection consideration.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursable competitive grants up to 100% of project cost with no established minimum or maximum amount. The FY 2025 grant round awarded $4.3 million. Funds can cover land acquisition costs (up to the average of two independent appraisals), site clearing and development costs, playground installation (surfacing must meet safety standards: ≤90 ppm lead, no added PFAs), administrative costs (up to 3% of the grant amount), and program compliance costs for easement monitoring (up to 1.5% of the grant amount). Maintenance and operating costs are not eligible. Partial reimbursements are permitted to help with cash flow, and advance payments may be considered on a case-by-case basis after Board of Public Works approval.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Land trusts, nongovernmental organizations (NGOs), county governments, and municipal governments located in or working in overburdened or underserved communities in Maryland, as well as other eligible applicants seeking to preserve, create, or improve public greenspace in those communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquiring land in fee simple or a perpetual conservation easement; developing or improving community greenspace (community gardens, parks, trails, urban farms, woodland areas, green networks, community gathering spaces, community woodlands); playground installation (surfacing must meet safety standards); related due diligence costs (appraisals, environmental assessments, surveys, title work); administrative costs up to 3% of grant; easement monitoring program compliance costs up to 1.5% of grant. Maintenance and operating costs are not eligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in or adjacent to a census tract designated as an overburdened or underserved community as defined under Maryland Environment Article §1-701, as determined using the MDEnviroScreen tool. Project location must be verified on the DNR eligibility map before applying. Eligible census tracts span across the state of Maryland. Geographic diversity across the state is a selection consideration.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a land trust, nongovernmental organization (NGO), county government, or municipal government.

Land trusts must be a qualified organization under IRC §170(H)(3), have a cooperative agreement with Maryland Environmental Trust, or be an Affordable Housing Land Trust under Real Property Article §14-501.
NGOs that are not land trusts are not eligible for acquisition projects.
Land trusts and NGOs must be in good standing.
Project must be located in, or adjacent to, a census tract designated as an overburdened or underserved community as determined by the MDEnviroScreen tool.
Must serve overburdened and underserved communities.
Land acquisition must be supported by two independent appraisals; purchase price funded up to the average of the two appraisals.
Land acquired must be maintained for public use in perpetuity.
Land developed or improved must be operated and maintained for public use for at least 15 years from project completion.

Applicant must have rights to develop the property (ownership, easement, long-term lease with more than 15 years remaining and no termination for convenience clause, or a project-specific Joint Use Agreement).
Contingency costs are not eligible and must not be included in cost estimates; applicants must submit realistic cost estimates.
Administrative costs must be documented and related to the approved project.
Program compliance funds for easement monitoring must be placed in an endowment or long-term managed investment account; principal cannot be withdrawn without DNR approval.
Projects must be completed as proposed; substantive scope changes will not be approved.
Applicants must meet eligibility requirements outlined in the Grant Proposal Guide.
Incomplete or late applications may not be considered for funding.
Community involvement is required in project development.
Demonstrated partnerships with county/municipal governments, land trusts, or NGOs are required.
Playground surfacing must meet safety standards (≤90 ppm lead, no added PFAs).
Project location must be verified on the DNR eligibility map prior to applying.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete the Grant Application and Project Agreement, then submit with all required attachments including an itemized cost estimate and all supporting documentation listed on the Accompanying Document Checklist (including evidence of local government support, community support, and collaboration among partners). Additional detail may be submitted as an attached narrative. The Greenspace Equity Program Administrator prepares and distributes application materials to local governments and interested parties. Grant writing workshops may be held to assist applicants. Selected projects go through State Clearinghouse review and must be approved by the Maryland Board of Public Works before funds are encumbered. Since this is a reimbursable grant, recipients pay costs upfront and are reimbursed after project completion, with partial reimbursements permitted. Applications for FY 2027 are due Wednesday, January 14, 2026, by 3:00 p.m. Application materials for FY 2028 will be posted when available. Questions can be directed to Stephanie Benavides at stephanie.benavides1@maryland.gov or 443-510-4572, or submit general questions/project submissions to laplocalgrants.dnr@maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grant funding to obtain independent appraisals for greenspace acquisition projects in overburdened and underserved communities in advance of FY 2028 acquisition applications. Supports preservation, creation, and enhancement of community greenspace in overburdened and underserved communities in Maryland, as determined using the MDEnviroScreen tool.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant funding to cover costs for up to two independent appraisals from certified general real estate appraisers for properties proposed for acquisition under the Greenspace Equity Program. Appraisals must meet Uniform Standards of Professional Appraisal Practice (USPAP) narrative report requirements. Up to $100,000 total available for this appraisal grant round. Eligible applicants include land trusts, county governments, and municipal governments serving overburdened and underserved communities, as determined using the MDEnviroScreen tool.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Land trusts (qualified organizations under IRC §170(H)(3), with MET cooperative agreement, or affordable housing land trusts), county governments, and municipal governments seeking to acquire greenspace in overburdened or underserved communities who need funding to obtain independent appraisals before submitting an acquisition application for the FY 2028 Greenspace Equity Program Grant round.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Independent appraisals from certified general real estate appraisers only. Narrative reports must meet Uniform Standards of Professional Appraisal Practice (USPAP) standards. Unused funds must be returned.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties must be located in overburdened or underserved communities in Maryland, or in adjacent census tracts (for conservation easement or fee simple property), as determined using the MDEnviroScreen tool. Property location must have a Maryland Legislative District designation (1-47).
requirements_list: Property proposed for acquisition must meet the general requirements of the Greenspace Equity Program
Property must be located in an overburdened or underserved community (or adjacent census tract for conservation easement or fee simple property), verified through MDEnviroScreen tool

Applicant must be an eligible organization: land trust (qualified under IRC §170(H)(3), with MET cooperative agreement, or affordable housing land trust as defined in Real Property Article section 14-501), county government, or municipal government
Land trusts must be located or working in overburdened or underserved communities
Appraisals must be completed by certified general real estate appraisers and meet USPAP narrative report standards
Applicants selected for appraisal funding must procure and complete appraisals in time to submit an application for the FY 2028 Greenspace Equity Program Grant round
Complete application and project agreement with all necessary accompanying documents must be submitted by the deadline
Incomplete or late applications may not be considered for funding
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the FY 2027 Greenspace Equity Program Appraisal Funding Grant Application and Project Agreement with all required accompanying documents and email it to laplocalgrants.dnr@maryland.gov by 3:00 p.m. on May 13, 2026. Use the Appraisal Funding Grant Proposal Guide for instructions. Incomplete or late applications may not be considered.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Natural Resources Wildlife and Heritage Service offers five free educator kits designed to supplement Growing Up WILD activities. The kits contain hands-on materials such as puppets, books, magnifying glasses, replicas, laminated cards, DVDs, and activity guides to teach children aged 3–7 about nature topics including ocean life, fish, recycling, leaves, and trees. Kits can be borrowed for up to two weeks at a time from loaner facilities across Maryland, and must be picked up and dropped off at the loaner facility. There is no charge for use.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free loan of five educator kits for up to two weeks at a time. The program includes all supplies, labor, and at least three years of maintenance and technical advice, along with ongoing technical support from the Maryland Forest Service and partner organizations.

structured_extraction.program_description: A partnership program that encourages physical activity by connecting community members to Maryland State Parks. Healthcare providers refer patients to the program, which offers recreational opportunities and outdoor exercise programs in outdoor settings to improve health and reduce chronic conditions such as obesity, hypertension, diabetes, and depression. DNR staff work with local health departments and healthcare providers to refer patients to free outdoor physical activity programs at participating state parks, where Local Health Departments provide health tips, health-related messages, and diverse recreational opportunities for all fitness levels.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive a prescription from their healthcare provider to increase physical activity and take part in programs offered at nearby State parks. DNR staff work with local health departments and healthcare providers to refer patients to free outdoor physical activity programs at state parks. Local Health Departments provide health tips, health-related messages, and diverse recreational opportunities for all fitness levels.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participation in recreational and physical activity programs at Maryland State Parks in western Maryland and Caroline County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at Rocky Gap, Herrington Manor, New Germany, and Deep Creek Lake state parks in western Maryland, and at Tuckahoe and Martinak state parks in Caroline County.

Healthcare provider must determine the patient is physically able to increase their level of physical activity
Participation must be deemed beneficial to the patient's health and well-being

Patients receive a prescription to increase physical activity and then participate in programs offered at nearby State parks.

Events include classroom instruction, live-fire range time, and equipment provided at no cost for most participants. Some events target specific groups such as youth (ages 14-17), women, active military, and veterans.

Some events may have a participation fee (e.g., $100 for the BEYOND BOW x Precision Point Frederick women's rifle workshop). structured_extraction.program_name: Income Tax Modification for Reforestation and Timber Stand Improvement
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides a financial incentive for forest landowners in Maryland to manage their forest land. Eligible participants may deduct double the cost of reforestation and timber stand improvement practices — minus any cost-share assistance received through other programs such as WIP or EQIP — as a subtraction from federal adjusted gross income when calculating Maryland state income taxes. Only practices installed on 3 to 1,000 acres are eligible for the modification in any one year. Practices must remain in effect for at least 15 years; if not maintained, tax savings must be repaid. Christmas tree and ornamental tree operations are not eligible.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants may deduct double the cost of reforestation and timber stand improvement practices — minus any cost-share assistance received through other programs such as WIP or EQIP — as a subtraction from federal adjusted gross income on their Maryland state tax return. Only practices installed on 3 to 1,000 acres are eligible for the modification in any one year. Practices must remain in effect for at least 15 years; if not maintained, tax savings must be repaid.

structured_extraction.program_name: Innovative Technology Fund – Research and Development and Seed Capital Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: Administered by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources in partnership with the University of Maryland and EPA, the Innovative Technology Fund supports two complementary tracks: (1) a Research and Development track, in partnership with the University of Maryland's Maryland Industrial Partnership Program (MIPS), that funds university researchers and businesses to develop new technologies reducing nutrient and sediment pollution and accelerating Chesapeake Bay restoration, with awards ranging from $30,000 to $100,000; and (2) a Seed Capital Fund track, administered by Mtech Ventures at the University of Maryland, that invests $250,000 annually over a three-year period (with grants of $50,000 to $450,000) in Maryland-based startup companies with innovative technologies that may help improve air and water quality in the Chesapeake Bay area, supporting commercialization of innovative environmental technologies that support Chesapeake Bay restoration. The program provides $1 million total per year ($500,000 for grants, $500,000 for investments) and supports green job creation and business development in Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two funding tracks are available: the R&D track offers awards from $30,000 to $100,000 for research and development of technologies that reduce nutrient and sediment pollution in the Chesapeake Bay, administered with the University of Maryland's MIPS program; the Seed Capital track invests $250,000 per year over a three-year period (awards ranging from $50,000 to $450,000) in Maryland-based startup companies commercializing innovative Bay restoration and environmental quality technologies, administered by Mtech Ventures at the University of Maryland. Total annual funding is $1 million ($500,000 in grants and $500,000 in investments).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students, faculty, staff, and researchers from the University of Maryland System, businesses developing technologies to reduce Chesapeake Bay pollution, and Maryland-based startup companies seeking to commercialize innovative environmental technologies related to Bay restoration and improving air and water quality in the Chesapeake Bay area.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Research and development of new technologies to reduce non-point source nutrients, sediment, and other pollutants affecting the Chesapeake Bay; commercialization of innovative environmental technologies supporting Bay restoration; demonstration-scale projects and pilot programs for environmental solutions; business development and green job creation in Maryland.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For the R&D track, contact Sarah Lane at sarah.lane@maryland.gov or 410-260-8788, or visit www.mips.umd.edu. For the Seed Capital track, contact Scott Christensen at schris14@umd.edu or visit http://mtech.umd.edu/ventures/chesapeake-bay-seed-capital-fund.html. structured_extraction.program_description: Grants through the Keep Maryland Beautiful program and related initiatives administered by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources (Maryland Environmental Trust) and the Chesapeake Bay Trust that support volunteer-based nonprofit groups, communities, land trusts, school groups, and youth organizations in Maryland. Programs include: Community Stewardship grant (up to $5,000 for nonprofits, schools, municipalities, community/homeowners associations, and service/civic groups for roadside enhancement, environmental education, and community green space development); Land Trust Capacity Building grant (up to $10,000 for Maryland local land trusts with a current Cooperative Agreement with MET for organizational capacity building, strategic land conservation, and stewardship); Tree Planting on Agricultural Lands grant (small-scale projects under 2 acres up to $10,000; large-scale projects over 2 acres up to $50,000; for private, community, nonprofit, and government-owned agricultural properties); and the Bill James Environmental Grant (up to $1,000 for school groups, science and ecology clubs, and nonprofit youth groups for environmental education projects). The Aileen Hughes Award (up to $5,000) recognizes an individual representing a Maryland land trust for outstanding leadership, partnership, and innovation. In 2026, 20 grants totaling $205,134 were awarded to community organizations. The program has been presented annually since 1986 and has provided over $1 million over the past three decades. Funds must be used between March 30, 2026 and February 28, 2027, with grant money received by April 15, 2026. Projects support environmental education, stewardship, litter removal, tree planting, and protection of natural resources in urban and rural areas statewide.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are awarded to eligible organizations for environmental projects across four tracks: (1) Community Stewardship (up to $5,000) for community/youth engagement projects including roadside enhancement, environmental education, and community green space development; (2) Land Trust Capacity Building (up to $10,000) for organizational capacity building, strategic land conservation, and land trust strengthening; (3) Small-Scale Tree Planting on Agricultural Lands (under 2 acres, up to $10,000) and Large-Scale Tree Planting on Agricultural Lands (over 2 acres, up to $50,000) for reforestation/afforestation on qualifying agricultural land; and (4) Bill James Environmental Grant (up to $1,000) for school groups, science and ecology clubs, and nonprofit youth groups. The Aileen Hughes Award provides up to $5,000 to an individual representing a Maryland land trust for outstanding leadership and innovation. In 2026, 20 grants totaling $205,134 were awarded: Community Stewardship $47,000; Land Trusts Assistance $55,000; Aileen Hughes $5,000; Tree Planting on Agricultural Lands $98,134. Funds must be used between March 30, 2026 and February 28, 2027, with grant money received by April 15, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_name: Land and Water Conservation Fund Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: The Land and Water Conservation Fund (LWCF) is a federal program that provides matching acquisition and development grants to state and local governments for outdoor recreation projects, including land acquisition, wetlands protection, and facility development. Established by the Land and Water Conservation Fund Act of 1965 and administered nationally by the U.S. Department of the Interior, National Parks Service, the program is funded primarily by federal revenues from offshore oil and gas leases. It aims to create and maintain quality public outdoor recreational resources and stimulate non-federal investment in protecting these areas. Eligible projects include picnic areas, inner city parks, campgrounds, tennis courts, boat ramps, bike trails, outdoor swimming pools, support facilities, and other outdoor recreation amenities, as well as wetlands acquisition and recreational land preservation. States must develop a Statewide Comprehensive Outdoor Recreation Plan (SCORP) — including a wetlands component — updated every five years, to be eligible to receive funds. In Maryland, the Department of Natural Resources, Land Acquisition and Planning Unit manages the program and coordinates grant rounds for project funding. Over 400 projects have been funded in Maryland since inception. Grants are reimbursement-based and require a 1:1 match with non-federal funds, with a minimum grant request of $50,000 (for a $100,000 total project) and a maximum of $3,000,000 (for a $6,000,000 total project). Projects must be completed within 3 years of the award date, with the possibility of a 2-year extension. Funds are not available for operation and maintenance of facilities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement-based 50/50 matching grants requiring a 1:1 match with non-federal funds. The minimum grant request is $50,000 (for a $100,000 total project) and the maximum is $3,000,000 (for a $6,000,000 total project). Applicants must incur 100% of project costs upfront and request reimbursement after completion and NPS grant closure. Projects must be completed within 3 years of the award date, with the possibility of a 2-year extension. Grants are also available for revising and updating existing SCORPs and for statewide surveys, technical studies, data collection, and planning, as well as for acquisition of wetlands and natural areas. Matching funds can come from Program Open Space Local funds, Community Parks and Playground grant funds, Recreational Trails Fund, Community Development Block Grants, and Readiness and Environmental Protection Integration. Fund monies are not available for operation and maintenance of facilities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: State agencies, counties, municipalities, and local government entities seeking funding for public outdoor recreation land acquisition (including wetlands) or facility development and renovation in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition of land (including wetlands and natural areas) and development or renovation of public outdoor recreation amenities, including picnic areas, inner city parks, campgrounds, tennis courts, boat ramps, bike trails, outdoor swimming pools, trails, swimming and boating facilities, fishing and hunting facilities, nature study facilities, athletic fields (soccer, tennis, basketball, softball), and support structures (comfort stations, roads). Also available for revising and updating existing SCORPs and for statewide surveys, technical studies, data collection, and planning. The entire park must be permanently protected and dedicated exclusively to recreational use. Cannot fund structures not supporting outdoor recreation, agriculture, indoor recreation, or luxury facilities. Fund monies are not available for operation and maintenance of facilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to eligible government entities. States must have a current SCORP on file to be eligible. Counties must have submitted a timely 2022 County Land Preservation, Parks, and Recreation Plan (LPPRP) for full scoring consideration. Municipalities are eligible but scored out of 90 points rather than 100 in the selection criteria. Projects must align with the Maryland Land Preservation and Recreation Plan (LPRP). Preference for Targeted Ecological Areas and climate change adaptation areas.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a government entity (state agency, county, municipality, or local government).
State must develop a Statewide Comprehensive Outdoor Recreation Plan (SCORP) before receiving funds; SCORP must be updated every five years.
SCORP must include a wetlands component identifying agencies, evaluating protection mechanisms, assessing resources, identifying loss factors, and establishing protection priorities.

LWCF funding must be matched 1:1 (50/50) with non-federal funds. Acceptable federal sources for matching include Recreational Trails Fund, Community Development Block Grants, and Readiness and Environmental Protection Integration.
Program Open Space and Community Parks and Playground grants may be used as matching funds.
The entire park must be permanently protected and dedicated exclusively to recreational use.
Facilities must be open to the general public and not limited to special groups.
Development of basic rather than elaborate facilities is favored.
Projects must be completed within 3 years of award date (with possibility of a 2-year extension).
Projects must reflect the policies and priorities of Maryland's current Land Preservation and Recreation Plan (LPRP/SCORP).
No property acquired or developed with LWCF assistance may be converted to non-public outdoor recreation use without approval of the Secretary of the Interior.
Fund monies are not available for operation and maintenance of facilities.
Land must be protected and maintained for public outdoor recreation in perpetuity.
No agricultural leases or agricultural profit permitted on assisted property.
Structures must be in direct support of public outdoor recreation only.
Applicant must own property (fee simple or equivalent).
Applicant must incur 100% of project costs upfront; reimbursement provided after completion and NPS grant closure.
For acquisition projects: appraisal, purchase agreement, and demonstrated readiness required.
Projects must comply with Forest Conservation Act of 1991 (Natural Resources Article, Sections 5-1601 through 5-1613).
Must consult with Maryland Historical Trust (Project Review and Compliance Program Division) to determine adverse effects on historic properties.
Applications for federal/state funds for development subject to Maryland Department of Planning State Clearinghouse review.
Projects must not adversely affect properties listed in or eligible for the Maryland Register of Historic Properties.
Counties must have submitted a timely 2022 County Land Preservation, Parks, and Recreation Plan (LPPRP) for full scoring consideration.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The LWCF grant uses a 2-step application process. First, applicants submit preliminary project proposals to the Maryland DNR during the Open Project Selection Process (OPSP). Optional individual meetings to review proposals may be scheduled May 1–29. Preliminary applications are due to molly.pickel@maryland.gov by 5 p.m. on June 24, 2026. DNR notifies selected applicants by September 15. Successful applicants are then invited to prepare a full federal application for submission to the National Park Service. Local applicants (counties and municipalities) use 'Local' application materials; state agencies use 'State' application materials. For development projects, applicants must submit a site development plan and ownership documentation. Applicants should review the LWCF Competitive Grant Announcement and Open Project Selection Process Criteria before applying. Local Program Open Space projects must be reviewed for Forest Conservation Act conformance prior to state submission. Applicants must also consult with the Maryland Historical Trust before applying. Applications subject to federal/state fund review and State Clearinghouse process approval. States must develop a SCORP addressing required issues as a prerequisite for applying. For federal-level inquiries, contact the SCORP Program Manager at the National Park Service Recreation Resources Assistance Division in Washington, DC.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Department of Natural Resources Licensed Tree Expert (LTE) program licenses individuals who work in the business of tree care, treatment, and removal. The program protects consumers, promotes responsible natural resource management, and supports industry safety by requiring tree experts to meet education and experience standards, pass a written exam, carry liability insurance, and follow a code of ethics. Licensed Tree Experts must also complete continuing education units to maintain their license. The exam covers 10 domains, consists of 140 multiple-choice questions, and is administered in person at the Tawes State Office Building in Annapolis, offered up to ten times per year (typically the second Wednesday of each month, except June and August).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Department issues a state tree expert license to qualified applicants who meet education or experience requirements, pay the required fee ($30 application fee; $20 per domain for exam retake; $20 for renewal), and pass a written examination. The exam covers 10 domains, consists of 140 multiple-choice questions, and requires a passing score of at least 70% in each domain and overall. Licenses must be renewed every two years; renewal requires completion of 8 continuing education units (CEUs). The exam is administered in person at the Tawes State Office Building in Annapolis, offered up to ten times per year (typically the second Wednesday of each month, except June and August). The license allows individuals to legally engage in the business or work of a tree expert in Maryland. Licensed Tree Experts must display their license number on trucks, proposals, contracts, and advertisements, and must comply with COMAR 08.07.07 and ANSI A300 standards for tree care.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: License renewals are due January 1 and must be received no later than January 31st. 2026 renewals will begin after November.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Licensing authorizes the holder to legally engage in the business or work of a tree expert in Maryland, including diagnosis, treatment, pruning, cabling, and removal of trees.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Applicants must have experience with a licensed tree expert in Maryland or an acceptable tree expert company in another state.

Must pass the Department's written licensing examination with a score of at least 70% in each of the 10 domains and overall
Must carry and show proof of liability and property damage insurance in the form and amount required by the Department, listing DNR as Certificate Holder
Must maintain Workers' Compensation insurance if employing staff
Must complete 8 continuing education units (CEUs) during each two-year renewal period
Must display license number on trucks, proposals, contracts, and advertisements
Must comply with COMAR 08.07.07 standards and ANSI A300 standards for tree care
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application online at the Maryland Forest Service Submittable portal or via printable PDF (also available in Spanish). Provide qualification certification including employer names, dates, and signatures from supervising licensed tree experts. Submit proof of insurance with DNR listed as Certificate Holder. Once the application and all required verification are approved, the Department will schedule an exam date. The in-person exam is held at the Tawes State Office Building in Annapolis, offered up to ten times per year (typically the second Wednesday of each month, except June and August). Contact Veronica Guerra at lte.dnr@maryland.gov for exam dates and registration. For license renewal, submit the renewal application beginning after November each year; renewals are due January 1 and must be received by January 31. CEUs can be completed via approved online courses and submitted by mail, fax, or email to Maryland Forest Service; CEU pre-approval for events must be submitted at least 30 days prior to the event.

structured_extraction.program_name: Local Parks and Playgrounds Infrastructure Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program funded through the FY 2022 and FY 2023 state capital budgets that provides funds primarily to local governments for park and recreation acquisition and development projects. Administered similarly to Program Open Space local grants, but with no matching requirement. Projects must be accessible to the general public and cannot require memberships, exclude the public due to high fees, or include residential or elaborate lodging facilities. Includes funding for acquisition of land for new parks or additions to existing parks, as well as design, construction, and capital equipment for indoor and outdoor park infrastructure projects that enhance recreational amenities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Capital budget grants (reimbursement-based) for local park and recreation acquisition and development projects. Administered similarly to Program Open Space local grants with the matching requirement waived. For acquisition projects: funds cover land acquisition costs, improvement costs, and incidental costs (appraisals, title work, surveys, legal fees, settlement fees). For development projects: funds cover design, construction, and capital equipment for indoor and outdoor park infrastructure. Funds cannot be used for projects inaccessible to the general public, requiring memberships, excluding the public because of higher use fees, or including residential or elaborate lodging facilities. Projects with costs ≥$500,000 that include a structure and are located within a Coast Smart Climate Ready Action Boundary must comply with Coast Smart Siting and Design Criteria.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments (counties, municipalities, and political subdivisions) and certain nonprofit organizations seeking funding for park and recreation acquisition or development projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition: land acquisition costs, improvement costs, and incidental costs (appraisals, surveys, title searches, legal fees, settlement fees). Development: design, construction, and capital equipment for indoor and outdoor park and playground infrastructure that enhances recreational amenities. Projects must be accessible to the general public.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — available to local governments across Maryland, including all counties, Baltimore City, and municipalities. Preference noted for Priority Funding Areas for acquisition projects. Coast Smart Climate Ready Action Boundary considerations apply for certain development projects.

Projects cannot include residential or elaborate lodging facilities
No matching requirement

For acquisition: must be consistent with County Land Preservation, Parks and Recreation Plan (LPPRP)

For development: itemized detailed cost estimate required

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Submit the applicable LPPI Acquisition or Development Project Application and Project Agreement to the Maryland Department of Natural Resources, along with the Funding Authorization Form signed by the County Liaison Officer. Acquisition applications require project information, location, land description, cost breakdown, two independent appraisals, and funding sources. Development applications require project description, eligibility justification, detailed cost estimates, project timeline, and Coast Smart screening forms if applicable. Acquisition projects require Board of Public Works approval. 2. After project completion, submit the appropriate Request for Reimbursement form with supporting documentation (invoices, contractor requisitions, canceled checks, cost summaries, and for in-house labor/equipment: worker lists with job functions, dates, hours, and rates). Submit completed reimbursement forms to the county program administrator.

structured_extraction.program_name: MUCFC Community Tree Planting and Education Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Urban and Community Forestry Council (MUCFC) provides grants to organizations, communities, and schools for community-based tree planting, street tree maintenance, and urban forestry education projects on public lands across Maryland. The program strives to unite and encourage citizens to protect and enhance Maryland's community trees and forest ecosystems, promoting plant diversity, wildlife habitat restoration, and long-term environmental stewardship. Grants are awarded and distributed through local County Forestry Boards with funding from the USDA Forest Service. Projects must strengthen the urban tree canopy, engage citizens, and occur on public lands such as parks, school campuses, streetscapes, and municipal properties. Projects with matching funds or in-kind support receive priority.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $1,000 are awarded to organizations, communities, and schools for tree planting, street tree maintenance, and urban forestry education projects on public lands. Grants are distributed through local County Forestry Boards with funding from the USDA Forest Service. Eligible uses include tree purchase and planting, tree planting supplies, site preparation, native/shade trees, maintenance planning, signage (with MUCFC acknowledgement), equipment (with detailed future use plan required), mulch, tools, and educational workshops and publications. Educational projects must include draft content, target audience description, distribution plan, and explanation of unmet informational need. Projects with matching funds or in-kind support receive priority. Invasive species planting is not funded. Unused funds must be returned with the final report.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: by 11:59 p.m. on January 15 and July 15
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations (not individuals) statewide seeking to plant and maintain urban street trees or conduct urban forestry education on public lands in Maryland, including municipalities, non-profits, civic groups, communities, schools, volunteer groups, Master Gardeners, and youth groups.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tree planting and maintenance on public lands (schools, parks, town centers, municipal properties, streetscapes) including tree purchase and planting, site preparation, native/shade trees, maintenance planning, mulch, tools, and equipment (with detailed future use plan); and educational/outreach projects that raise public awareness about the value of urban trees, including signage, publications, distribution materials, and educational workshops and training. Invasive species planting is not funded.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland through local County Forestry Boards. All funded projects must occur on public lands (school grounds, parks, town centers, municipal properties, or land owned by local, state, or federal government).

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides reimbursement grants to public and private marinas for the purchase, installation, upgrade, replacement, and maintenance of marine sewage pumpout facilities. The program gives boaters a proper method of sewage disposal to help clean up Maryland waters. Funded 75% by the Federal Clean Vessel Act (Sport Fish Restoration and Boating Trust Fund) and 25% by the Maryland Waterway Improvement Fund, marinas pay costs upfront and submit invoices for reimbursement after DNR conducts a final inspection. Grant funding is also available for reimbursements of pumpout operations and maintenance, pumpout replacements and upgrades.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement grants of up to $20,000 for the purchase and installation of new marine sewage pumpout facilities, and up to $18,000 for upgrades or replacements. Additional grant funding is available for pumpout operations, maintenance, upgrades, and replacement. Funded 75% by the Federal Clean Vessel Act (Sport Fish Restoration and Boating Trust Fund) and 25% by the Maryland Waterway Improvement Fund. Marinas must pay costs upfront and then submit invoices for reimbursement after DNR conducts a final inspection. Eligible costs include equipment purchase, installation labor (contractor or in-house), plumbing and electrical work, local permits, and waste holding tanks if applicable. Facilities must serve the general public during reasonable business hours and may not charge more than $5.00 per pumpout for the first 50 gallons plus $0.10 per gallon above 50 gallons. Technical assistance and information is also available.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public and private marina owners and operators in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and installation of marine sewage pumpout facilities; pumpout operations and maintenance; pumpout upgrades and replacement; local permit fees for first-time installations; plumbing and electrical work; waste holding tanks (if applicable).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to marinas located within the state.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Abandoned Boat and Debris Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Natural Resources (DNR) provides reimbursable grants and technical expertise to help public agencies remove abandoned boats and hazardous debris from Maryland state waterways. The program aims to reduce navigation hazards and environmental harm in state waters. Funding comes from the state Waterway Improvement Fund, which is generated from a one-time 5% excise tax on boats purchased and titled in Maryland. Grants of up to $25,000 per project are available on a 100% reimbursable basis, and funds are obligated immediately upon approval.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 100% reimbursable grants of up to $25,000 per project for the removal of abandoned vessels and hazardous debris (such as fuel or propane tanks) from Maryland state waters, plus technical expertise to assist public agencies. Reimbursement covers contractor costs, supplies, materials, equipment rental, and in-house labor and equipment. Reimbursement is paid after the work is completed and all grant terms and conditions are met, including submission of invoices, canceled checks or EFT documentation, and before/after photos. Applications are accepted in July and funds are obligated immediately upon approval. Funding comes from the state Waterway Improvement Fund, generated from a one-time 5% excise tax paid when a boat is purchased and titled in Maryland.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Removal and disposal of abandoned vessels and hazardous debris (such as fuel or propane tanks) from Maryland state waters. Eligible costs include contractor services, supplies, materials, equipment rental, and in-house labor and equipment costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. The vessel or debris must be located on aquatic lands under the jurisdiction of the applying public entity.

Before and after photos of removal required.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the grant application (available in MS Word or Adobe PDF at https://dnr.maryland.gov/Boating/Pages/abandonedboats.aspx) to the Department of Natural Resources, Boating Services Unit, Abandoned Boat and Debris Program in July. After removal work is completed, submit the reimbursement request form with required documentation (invoices, canceled checks or EFT printouts, before and after photos, and proof of contractor selection process) to the DNR Boating Services Unit. Allow approximately one month for processing.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Archery in the Schools Program (MD NASP)
structured_extraction.program_description: MD NASP promotes student education through participation in archery for students in grades 4–12. The program delivers International-style target archery training through classroom instruction, hands-on shooting activities, and a written curriculum covering archery history, safety, shooting techniques, equipment use, and mental concentration. All activities are conducted indoors. The program meets national physical education standards and is accessible to students with disabilities, including most wheelchair-bound and visually impaired students. Teachers and school administrators are supported in setting up an indoor archery range and delivering the program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides schools with a ready-made archery curriculum, instructor training, and guidance on setting up an indoor archery range. It includes a written curriculum covering archery history, safety, shooting techniques, equipment, and mental concentration. Equipment needs and funding resources are covered through the program's supporting web pages.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Delivering archery instruction, physical education curriculum, and training to students in grades 4–12.

Delivered in school settings (indoors)

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Archery in the Schools Program (MD NASP) Equipment Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: Grants may be available to Maryland schools to help reduce the cost of purchasing a NASP archery starter kit, which includes bows, arrows, targets, quivers, bow rack, arrow curtain, maintenance kit, and other equipment needed to run an archery program. A starter kit normally valued at approximately $7,000 can be purchased at a special price of around $3,700, and grants can bring that cost down even further.

The kit normally costs approximately $7,000 but is available to schools at a special price of around $3,700. Grants may reduce the cost further. The starter kit includes bows, arrows, targets, quivers, bow rack, arrow curtain, and maintenance kit. Contact the Maryland NASP State Coordinator for current grant availability.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Archery in the Schools Program (MD NASP) — Basic Archery Instructor Training
structured_extraction.program_description: A one-day teacher training course that certifies school educators to teach basic archery safely to students as part of the National Archery in the Schools Program (NASP). Teachers learn safe range setup, archery techniques, equipment use and maintenance, coaching skills, and how to run a school archery program. Upon passing a test, teachers receive a Basic Archery Instructor (BAI) certification and a starter kit. Certified instructors must report teaching hours annually by July 31 to maintain certification.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Teachers attend a one-day (4–8 hour) training session covering safe range set-up, archery techniques, equipment use and maintenance, and coaching skills. Upon passing a test, teachers become certified Basic Archery Instructors (BAIs). Each certified teacher receives a BAI kit including a pocket reference guide, string bow material, and a NASP whistle. Training cost ranges from $0 to $80 depending on the instructor. Certified BAIs must report teaching hours annually by July 31 to maintain certification.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Teacher certification in basic archery instruction for use in school curricula, enabling safe and standards-based archery programs in schools

Must attend and pass the one-day Basic Archery Instructor training course

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Biological Stream Survey (MBSS) Training & Certification
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Natural Resources offers training and professional certifications in stream sampling protocols and taxonomic standards used by the Maryland Biological Stream Survey (MBSS). Training covers field and laboratory methods for stream biomonitoring, including benthic macroinvertebrate sampling, fish identification and crew leadership, mussel taxonomy, and physical habitat assessment. Certifications are required by some counties and state agencies for stream sampling work to be considered consistent with MBSS standards. Summer training runs May 26–29, 2026 at Bowie State University, mixing classroom/laboratory instruction with field protocol demonstrations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Summer training is 4 days in-person at Bowie State University (May 26–29, 2026), with classroom/laboratory instruction and field protocol demonstrations. Participants may register for 1–2 days at $75 per day, or 3 or more days for a total of $200. Six certifications are available: benthic macroinvertebrate sampling, benthic macroinvertebrate laboratory processing and subsampling, fish crew leader, fish taxonomy, mussel taxonomy, and physical habitat assessment. Certification validity periods vary: benthic macroinvertebrate sampling, lab processing/subsampling, fish crew leader, and fish taxonomy are valid for 3 years; physical habitat assessment is valid for 1 year; mussel taxonomy is valid indefinitely with annual documentation. Certification fees are charged after passing written tests. Fish certifications are $300 per certification or $400 combined; mussel taxonomy certification fee is $50. Field audits for benthic macroinvertebrate sampling must be scheduled before March 15; field audits for fish certifications must be scheduled before June 15.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals, consultants, and organizations (non-profit and for-profit) who conduct stream biomonitoring and need MBSS-consistent stream sampling certifications required by Maryland counties or state agencies. Open to professionals and non-professionals including students, interns, seasonal employees, volunteers, and researchers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training in stream biological sampling protocols and obtaining professional certifications in MBSS stream sampling methods including fish, macroinvertebrate, mussel, and habitat protocols, recognized by Maryland counties and state agencies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland; summer 2026 training held at Bowie State University in Prince George's County. Certifications are recognized statewide. Mussel taxonomy certification also applicable to surveys in other states using similar protocols to Maryland protocol.
requirements_list: Attendance at MBSS spring or summer training is required for five of the six certifications
Passing written tests and field audits is required for most certifications

Benthic macroinvertebrate laboratory processing and subsampling certification requires passing a laboratory audit and a written test; taxonomy requires SFS Group 2 (EPT) and Group 3 (Chironomidae) certification
Benthic macroinvertebrate sampling field audit must be scheduled before March 15; BIBI score difference must be ≤1.0 from QC Officer (first season only)

Mussel taxonomy certification requires scoring ≥90% on the mussel taxonomy test and 100% on threatened and endangered mussel species identification, and documentation of adequate prior experience (minimum 20 surveys within last 10 years OR 10 surveys within last 5 years) and two letters of reference
Fish Crew Leader certification requires annual MBSS summer training attendance; passing written test; and completing a field audit in the first year (scheduled before June 15)

Fish Taxonomy certification requires scoring ≥90% on the Fish Taxonomy test (minimum 36/40); and in the first year, passing a field audit identifying all fish from at least one electrofishing pass with ≥15 species richness with ≤1 misidentification
To maintain benthic macroinvertebrate sampling certification, individuals must attend spring training each year during the three-year term
To maintain fish crew leader certification, individuals must attend the fish sampling protocol portion of summer training each year during the three-year term

To maintain mussel taxonomy certification, individuals must provide annual documentation of minimum experience (handle 5 individuals of each threatened and endangered mussel species per year in field OR 0.5 hours per species in natural history museum) by February 15 annually
Payment of certification fees for benthic macroinvertebrate sampling, fish crew leader, fish taxonomy, or mussel taxonomy is not accepted until after the written test is passed
Physical habitat assessment certification requires pre-registration and advance payment via credit card; no walk-in registrants accepted
All certifications are issued to individuals only; organizations, firms, and agencies cannot be certified as entities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register for summer training using the registration link provided on the program page. Pay training fees ($75–$200) through the DNR Outdoor Store using a credit card; pre-registration required (no walk-ins). Attend training sessions in person. After passing required written tests at training, submit certification fees and complete field or laboratory audits as required for each certification type. For benthic macroinvertebrate sampling, schedule field audit before March 15. For fish certifications, schedule field audit before June 15. Submit certification payment within one week of audit completion.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide voluntary certification program administered by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources that recognizes and promotes marinas, boatyards, yacht clubs, and other boating facilities that meet legal requirements and voluntarily adopt pollution prevention practices to protect Maryland's waterways by reducing harmful chemicals, excess nutrients, and debris. Facilities can earn certification as a Clean Marina or a Clean Marina Partner designation. The Clean Marina Partner designation specifically recognizes smaller boating facilities — such as public boat ramps, private community piers, charter boat liveries, and maritime museums — that minimize boating-related pollution and promote clean boating habits. Certified facilities receive an Award Certificate signed by the Governor, a burgee and flag, a large aluminum sign, a free online business listing on the Clean Marina website, inclusion in Clean Marina publications and public displays, and advertising in regional boating publications. The program also provides a guidebook with best management practices, checklists for self-evaluation, free educational materials including clean boating tip sheets and posters, staff assistance with certification, informal site visits, mentorship from existing Clean Marina operators, and introductory workshops. Certification requires achieving minimum scores across eight key areas: vessel maintenance/repair, petroleum control, emergency planning, sewage handling, waste containment, marina management, stormwater management, and marina design/maintenance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Certified marinas and boating facilities receive an Award Certificate signed by the Governor, a burgee and flag to fly at their facility, a large aluminum sign, a free online business listing on the Clean Marina website, inclusion in Clean Marina publications and public displays, and advertising in regional boating publications. Technical assistance includes a guidebook with best management practices, checklists for self-evaluation, free educational materials (clean boating tip sheets and posters) at no cost, informal site visits, staff recommendations, mentorship from existing Clean Marina operators, and introductory workshops. Certified facilities may use the official Clean Marina logo and receive recognition as a Clean Marina or Clean Marina Partner. Certification requires meeting minimum scores across eight assessment areas: Area 1 (85%), Area 2 (80%), Area 3 (80%), Area 4 (80%), Area 5 (85%), Area 6 (80%), Area 7 (75%), Area 8 (70%), verified during a confirmation visit.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Within one year of pledge signing date
structured_extraction.program_audience: Marinas, boatyards, and yacht clubs of any size operating in Maryland, as well as operators of smaller boating facilities including public boat ramps, private community piers, charter boat liveries, and maritime museums.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Pollution prevention practices, compliance with environmental regulations at marine facilities, and free educational materials to promote clean and environmentally responsible boating practices. Certified facilities also receive marketing and recognition benefits including signage, logo use, and online listings.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to marine and boating facilities throughout Maryland statewide.
requirements_list: Must be a marina, boatyard, yacht club, or other boating facility (e.g., public boat ramp, private community pier, charter boat livery, maritime museum)
Must meet legal requirements and comply with applicable federal and state laws and regulations
Must voluntarily adopt pollution prevention practices
Sign and submit the Clean Marina Pledge
