Obtain program materials (Guidebook, Pledge form, Award Checklist)
Conduct a self-assessment using the Clean Marina Award Checklist
Achieve minimum scores across all eight assessment areas: Area 1 (85%), Area 2 (80%), Area 3 (80%), Area 4 (80%), Area 5 (85%), Area 6 (80%), Area 7 (75%), Area 8 (70%)

Implement best management practices across vessel maintenance/repair, petroleum control, emergency planning, sewage handling, waste management, staff training, stormwater management, and facility design/maintenance
Call upon a mentor for assistance if needed
Pass a confirmation visit by Clean Marina staff and a certified Clean Marina operator
Receive approval from the Clean Marina advisory committee
Apply to Maryland DNR for certification within one year of pledge signing
Annually sign and return the Affirmation of Good Standing
Schedule a reaffirmation visit at least every three years
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Obtain program materials (Guidebook, Pledge form, Award Checklist) by attending a workshop, downloading from the website, or contacting the Clean Marina office. 2. Sign and submit the Clean Marina Pledge and display it in a public area at your facility. 3. Conduct a self-assessment using the Clean Marina Award Checklist; optionally request an informal site visit from Clean Marina staff. 4. Implement recommended changes and pollution prevention practices across all eight assessment areas at your own pace with help from staff or mentor marinas. 5. Contact Donna Morrow at donna.morrow@maryland.gov or 410-260-8773 to schedule a confirmation visit when minimum scores are met in all areas. 6. Receive certification if the advisory committee approves. 7. Apply for certification within one year of signing the pledge. 8. Maintain Clean Marina or Clean Marina Partner status by annually signing the Affirmation of Good Standing and scheduling a reaffirmation visit at least every three years.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Conservation Corps (MCC) is an AmeriCorps program administered by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources that engages young adults ages 17–25 in a year of service dedicated to natural resource conservation and environmental protection. Members are placed on crews at state parks and natural resource management areas across Maryland to perform hands-on conservation and park improvement work, including trail construction and maintenance, wildland fire fighting, invasive species removal, environmental education, chainsaw operations, canoe trip leading, wildlife management, animal care, carpentry, and other outdoor conservation and park operations tasks. Members gain diverse skills and experience in natural resource conservation while receiving a living stipend, health care benefits (medical, prescription, AD&D, vision, and dental through Cigna Healthcare), low-cost park housing (averaging $150/month including utilities), gear reimbursements (boot and pant reimbursements), uniforms, personal protective gear, and a $6,000 completion award upon finishing the program. Crew positions are located throughout Maryland including Western Maryland (Garrett County), Central Maryland (Cecil and Harford/Baltimore Counties), Southern Maryland (Prince George's and Calvert Counties), and the Eastern Shore (Worcester County). Shadow opportunities are available from October through early June each year for those considering joining. The program runs from mid-September to late June.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Members receive a $6,000 completion award and a Conservation Steward Apprenticeship Certificate upon finishing the program. Additional benefits include health care coverage (medical, prescription, AD&D, vision, and dental) with premiums paid by the program through Cigna Healthcare; low-cost park housing at most crew locations (averaging $150/month including utilities); a $200 boot reimbursement; a $150 pant reimbursement; uniforms (work shirts and sweatshirts); and all personal protective gear. Extensive skills training is provided including Basic First Aid and CPR/AED, 40-hour Wildland Fire Fighting certification, chainsaw safety, trail construction and maintenance, invasive species removal, canoe trip leading, animal care, carpentry, and environmental education. Shadow opportunities (one-day volunteer crew experiences) are available from October through early June for prospective members. Participants serve a full year of service focused on natural resource conservation at state parks and other public lands statewide. Applicants may participate via the Service Year pathway, which involves creating an account on the BuildWithin portal and submitting a Service Year application specifying outdoor interests and preferred geographic location(s) within Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Program begins mid-September and ends late-June; virtual interviews scheduled beginning in May
structured_extraction.program_audience: Young adults ages 17–25 who are U.S. citizens and Maryland residents seeking hands-on experience and training in natural resource conservation, park operations, and management careers in Maryland. Members must have or be willing to obtain a high school diploma or GED and be committed to community and conservation service.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Completion award of $6,000 provided to members upon finishing the program. Living support provided during service includes low-cost housing, health insurance, gear reimbursements, and uniforms. Members participate in conservation crews performing work on Maryland public lands including trail construction and maintenance, invasive species removal, environmental education, animal care, facility improvement projects, carpentry, and other park improvement activities at state parks, public lands, watersheds, classrooms, and natural resource management areas statewide.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — applicants must be Maryland residents at the time of application. Members work across Maryland's public lands and state parks. Applicants can specify their preferred geographical location(s) within Maryland. Crew positions are located throughout Maryland including Western Maryland (Garrett County), Central Maryland (Cecil and Harford/Baltimore Counties), Southern Maryland (Prince George's and Calvert Counties), and the Eastern Shore (Worcester County). Preference for state housing is given to out-of-area members.
requirements_list: Be 17 to 25 years of age
Must be a Maryland resident at the time of application
Be a United States citizen
Have a high school diploma or be willing to work toward a GED
Have a desire to work in conservation
Be willing to work in all kinds of outdoor conditions
Be willing to camp for up to a week at a time
Be a team player
Have a positive attitude
Must provide personal or public transportation to a designated job site
Dedication and commitment to service
Must submit an online application through the Department of Service and Civic Innovation website (dsci.maryland.gov)
Create account on BuildWithin portal (for Service Year applicants)
Specify preferred geographical location(s) within Maryland
Explain specific interest in MCC program
Complete AI pre-screening questionnaire
Pass virtual interview with MCC staff
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application online through the Department of Service and Civic Innovation website at https://dsci.maryland.gov/, or contact the park manager or download an application from the Maryland DNR Maryland Conservation Corps website at https://www.dnr.maryland.gov/publiclands/pages/mcc.aspx. Alternatively, applicants may apply via the Service Year pathway by: (1) creating an account on the BuildWithin portal, (2) submitting a Service Year application specifying outdoor interests and preferred geographic location(s), (3) completing an AI pre-screening questionnaire, (4) submitting the MCC application, and (5) participating in a virtual interview with MCC staff (interviews scheduled beginning in May). Once submitted, the application is reviewed by Annalyn O'Grady, Conservation Corps Program Officer, at 580 Taylor Avenue, E-3, Annapolis MD 21401 (phone: 443-883-6514). Housing is first-come, first-served with preference for out-of-area members. Crew supervisors may connect members before the program begins. Visit the MCC How to Apply page on the DNR website at https://dnr.maryland.gov/publiclands/Pages/mcc_application.aspx for additional application details, or download the application guide at https://www.dnr.maryland.gov/publiclands/Documents/MCC-How-to-apply.pdf.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Conservation Jobs Corps (CJC) is a summer employment program run by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources (Maryland Park Service) in partnership with community youth organizations and the Student Conservation Association (SCA). Established in 2008 on the 75th anniversary of the Civilian Conservation Corps, the program provides disadvantaged youth ages 14-19 with paid conservation work experience, job and life skills training, and workforce preparation. Participants work in crews of 4-7 members Monday through Thursday on hands-on conservation service projects at Maryland State Parks and public lands—including trail building and maintenance, invasive species removal, native plant restoration, bridge and retaining wall construction, entry-level carpentry and construction, and historic site maintenance—while Fridays are dedicated to enrichment activities such as environmental education, archery, kayaking, canoeing, fishing, and camping. Participants receive paid wages, daily meals (breakfast, morning snack, lunch, and afternoon snack), transportation to and from park locations, work uniforms, and certificates of achievement upon completion. The program combines outdoor experiential activities and the power of nature to challenge and enrich the lives of youth while preparing them for future success in the workforce. Peer Leader and Crew Leader opportunities are also available for additional leadership development.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants join a crew for five to six weeks during the summer to complete hands-on outdoor conservation projects at Maryland State Parks and other public lands, including trail building and maintenance, invasive species removal, native plant restoration, bridge and retaining wall construction, carpentry, landscaping, and park facility improvements. Work is conducted Monday through Thursday, with Fridays dedicated to enrichment activities (environmental education, archery, kayaking, canoeing, fishing, camping, and a 3-day, 2-night camping experience). Additional benefits include paid wages, daily meals (breakfast, morning snack, lunch, and afternoon snack), transportation to and from park locations, work uniforms and safety equipment, skills training (power tools, woodworking, knot tying, problem-solving, leadership), professional networking and mentorship, and certificates of achievement upon completion. Crew Leader and Peer Leader opportunities are available for those seeking additional leadership development and skills.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Disadvantaged and underserved youth ages 14-19 in Maryland, particularly those from Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Harford County, Montgomery County, Prince George's County, Worcester County, and Anne Arundel County, seeking paid summer employment, job and life skills training, and workforce preparation through hands-on outdoor conservation service work in Maryland State Parks and public lands. Primarily first-time job seekers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participants are paid for performing conservation and park maintenance work at Maryland State Parks and other public lands, including trail building and maintenance, invasive species removal, native plant restoration, native tree planting, bridge and retaining wall construction, entry-level carpentry and construction, and historic site maintenance. Funds also cover youth and staff wages, meals, transportation, uniforms and safety equipment, project supplies, tools and equipment, and enrichment activities including camping, archery, kayaking, canoeing, and fishing, supporting career preparation and outdoor recreation skill-building.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide — program operates at Maryland State Parks and other public lands across the state, including Patapsco Valley State Park, Gunpowder Falls State Park, Seneca Creek State Park, Assateague State Park, Susquehanna State Park, Pocomoke River State Park, and parks in Baltimore City, Harford County, Montgomery County, Prince George's County, Worcester County, Anne Arundel County, and Baltimore County. Youth participants are primarily drawn from Baltimore City and surrounding Maryland communities.
requirements_list: Must be a youth ages 14-19
Classified as disadvantaged/underserved youth
Must reside in an eligible area (primarily Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Harford County, Montgomery County, Prince George's County, Worcester County, or Anne Arundel County)
Must be able to work Monday through Thursday during the summer program period
Commitment to strict attendance and performance standards
Staff must meet background investigation and driving record requirements
Crew Chiefs/Leaders must complete mandatory training with minimum 75% average score
First Aid and CPR certification required for Crew Chiefs/Leaders
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are handled through partner organizations including local departments of social services and the Mayor's Office for Employment Development (Youthworks). Visit the CJC Home Page or Program page for application details and check the program website for updates on future opportunities to join the program.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that provided funding to volunteer fire departments to install dry fire hydrants — non-pressurized pipe systems permanently installed into lakes, streams, or ponds to permit water withdrawal by drafting for fire suppression with all-weather access. The program ran from 2003 to 2007 and funded the installation of 114 new dry hydrants across Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants paid for 100% of the cost of materials and installation of dry fire hydrants. The program ran from 2003 to 2007 and funded the installation of 114 new dry hydrants across Maryland. Funding was provided through the USDA Forest Service as a partner.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Volunteer fire departments in rural areas of Maryland lacking pressurized fire hydrant systems; fire departments, emergency management centers, and state and federal partners.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of dry fire hydrants — materials and installation costs — in lakes, streams, or ponds to provide reliable rural water sources for fire suppression.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — all 24 Maryland counties, with specific installations in communities at risk from wildfire as identified in the state fire assessment. Regions include Western (Allegany, Frederick, Garrett, Washington), Central & Southern (Baltimore, Carroll, Cecil, Harford, Howard, Montgomery, Anne Arundel, Calvert, Charles, Prince George's, St. Mary's), and Eastern (Caroline, Dorchester, Kent, Queen Anne's, Somerset, Talbot, Wicomico, Worcester).
requirements_list: Applicant must be a volunteer fire department
Dry hydrant must be installed in a suitable water source such as a lake, stream, or pond
Community must be at risk from wildfire as identified in the state fire assessment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Program has concluded. Sub-grants were awarded to volunteer fire departments for installation costs. No current application process is described.

structured_extraction.program_description: Conserves, improves, stimulates, and perpetuates the aesthetic, natural, scenic, and cultural aspects of Maryland's environment. MET was formed in 1967 and promotes conservation of open space and appreciation of the environment. Programs include Land Conservation, Monitoring and Stewardship, Local Land Trust Assistance, and the Keep Maryland Beautiful Grants Program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Multiple programs including land conservation easements, stewardship monitoring, local land trust capacity building assistance, and Keep Maryland Beautiful grants.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners, local land trusts, and organizations promoting conservation and environmental stewardship in Maryland, as well as communities seeking to conserve Maryland's natural, scenic, and cultural resources
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Land conservation, open space preservation, environmental stewardship, local land trust capacity building, and community beautification
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide across Maryland

structured_extraction.program_description: An environmental science competition for high school students that covers soils, forestry, wildlife, aquatics, and a current environmental issue topic. Students can compete at the county, regional, state, and North American levels and have the opportunity to win college scholarships. Hands-on learning experiences are offered with teachers, community members, and natural resource personnel.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Students participate in an annual environmental science competition with training resources in aquatics, soils, forestry, wildlife, and a current environmental issue topic. Winners have the opportunity to compete for college scholarships at county, regional, state, and North American levels. Hands-on learning experiences are offered with teachers, community members, and natural resource personnel.
structured_extraction.program_audience: High school students interested in natural resources and environmental science
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: College scholarships for winning competitors
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland; each county and Baltimore City participates
requirements_list: Must be a high school student
Must contact local Soil Conservation District to participate
Participants should contact their local Soil Conservation District to get involved
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local Soil Conservation District for information on how to join the Maryland Envirothon competition. Visit the official Maryland Envirothon website at mdenvirothon.org for more details.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Chesapeake Bay Foundation initiative that provides free plant material, installation, and three years of maintenance for streamside forest buffers and upland tree plantings on farms. Also supports livestock producers interested in converting row crop fields to pasture for rotational grazing, and connects them with grazing mentors and technical assistance on farm economics and marketing through the CBF-led Maryland Grazers Network.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free plant material, implementation, and three years of maintenance for streamside forest buffers and upland tree plantings. Livestock producers can receive funding for converting row crop fields to pasture for rotational grazing, plus grazing mentors and technical assistance on farm economics and marketing.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland farmers and landowners, particularly those with streamside land, seeking forest buffers, upland tree plantings, or rotational grazing conversion
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Streamside forest buffers, upland tree plantings, conversion of row crop fields to pasture for rotational grazing, grazing mentorship, and technical assistance for farm economics and marketing
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Rob Schnabel at rschnabel@cbf.org or 443-482-2175 for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal-state partnership program established under the 1990 Farm Bill that protects environmentally important private forests from being converted to non-forest uses. It does this by purchasing perpetual conservation easements (or full title) from willing landowners at market value, preserving the land's wildlife, water quality, timber, watershed, recreational, scenic, cultural, historical, and ecological values. Properties must be located within a designated Forest Legacy Area in Maryland (as identified in the Forest Legacy Program Assessment of Need) and be at least 75% forested. Federal funding covers up to 75% of the easement purchase price, with the remaining 25% coming from state, local, or NGO funds, or donated by the landowner. The number of parcels accepted depends on available funding and the estimated value of parcels selected.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program purchases perpetual conservation easements (or full title) at market value from willing landowners. Landowners can sell development rights, public access rights, grazing rights, and/or farming rights. Up to 75% of funding comes from the federal government; at least 25% must come from state, local, or NGO funds, or can be donated by the landowner (at least 50% of easement value may be donated or paid by other sources). The easement permanently restricts development on the land while the landowner retains ownership, protecting environmentally and commercially important forests long-term. A forest management plan approved by the State is required and must be updated every 15 years. The number of parcels accepted depends on available funding and the estimated value of parcels selected.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications are evaluated and ranked on an annual basis.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private forest landowners (including individuals, family trusts, and multiple landowners with consensus) within designated Forest Legacy Areas in Maryland who are willing to sell their development rights, seeking to protect viable working forestland from conversion to non-forest uses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of perpetual conservation easements or full title to private forest land to prevent conversion to non-forest uses, protecting wildlife, water quality, and timber values. Funds may also cover property appraisals and surveys, title searches, and forest management planning.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Only available for private forest land located within areas identified as Forest Legacy Areas in Maryland's Forest Legacy Program Assessment of Need. At least 75% of the area placed under easement must be forested; the remaining 25% must be in a compatible land use such as agriculture. Priority given to parcels near protected lands, in priority watersheds, and with multiple conservation values. Scoring considers proximity to public lands, water bodies, and infrastructure.
requirements_list: Land must be private forest located within a designated Forest Legacy Area in Maryland (as identified in the Forest Legacy Program Assessment of Need).
At least 75% of the area put under easement must be forested.
The remaining 25% must be in a compatible land use such as agriculture.
Landowner must be a willing seller.
Projects are ranked on forest importance, threat of development, and strategic value to nearby protected lands or conservation initiatives.
25% non-federal match required (from state, local, NGO funds, or landowner donation).
Properties are ranked at the state and national level for funding.
Completed application (incomplete applications not considered); four copies of application package (one original, three copies) for each non-contiguous parcel.
Signed consent/approval and release form allowing inspection and appraisal.
Map showing property location relative to roads, protected open space, and ecological features.
Legal description and/or deed copy.
List of encumbrances and liens.
Plan-map with scale, north arrow, date, and title showing forested/non-forested areas, wetlands, and structures.
Parcel must convey development and mineral rights (minimum requirement); additional rights such as public access may also be conveyed.
Approved forest management plan required, updated every 15 years.

Scoring criteria includes: forest percentage coverage, building site reservations, community support, adjacency to other Forest Legacy parcels, complement to federal investments, donated/other-funded portions of easement value, and conveyance of additional rights.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Landowners complete and submit a landowner application (with four copies per non-contiguous parcel). All applications are evaluated and ranked annually using a scoring system based on forest importance, threat of development, strategic value to other protected lands or conservation initiatives, and other qualifying criteria including bonus points for factors such as 100% forest coverage and not reserving building sites. Highest-ranked applications enter the national ranking process for federal funding. Funded projects proceed to the negotiation and acquisition phase to finalize easement terms. If funding is not received or negotiations do not produce acceptable terms, landowners may reapply in future years.

structured_extraction.program_description: Awards scholarships of $500 and $1,000 to college and graduate students pursuing careers in natural resources. Scholarships are administered by the Maryland Association of Forest Conservancy District Boards. Specific scholarships and requirements are listed on the program website.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Scholarships of $500 or $1,000 awarded to college and graduate students pursuing careers in natural resources. Specific scholarships and requirements are listed on the program website.
structured_extraction.program_audience: College and graduate students pursuing careers in natural resources.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational expenses for students pursuing natural resource careers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a college or graduate student pursuing a career in natural resources.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review specific scholarships and requirements at http://www.marylandforestryboards.org/scholarship.cfm and apply accordingly.

structured_extraction.program_description: A mapping, targeting, and planning tool developed by Maryland DNR Forest Service to identify forested watersheds most important for protecting water quality. The tool scores forests based on attributes like stream buffers, steep slopes, wetlands, and nutrient filtering efficiency, and provides guidance for zoning and land use planning to balance economy and ecology through forest conservation, restoration, and sustainable management.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides a prioritization map, scoring model, and planning guidance to direct forestry actions where most effective for protecting water quality and watershed health. Includes guidance for zoning and land use planning in rural resource areas, large lot development areas, and established/targeted growth areas. References land conservation programs such as Program Open Space, Rural Legacy, and land trusts.
structured_extraction.contact_phone: 410-260-8531; Toll Free: 1-877-620-8DNR ext 8531; TTY via Maryland Relay: 711
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, communities and jurisdictions, forest landowners, developers, planners, conservation practitioners, and government agencies seeking to identify priority areas for forest conservation and watershed protection in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Forest conservation and land protection, forest restoration projects, mitigation banking in priority areas, urban tree canopy expansion, and targeting and prioritizing areas for forest retention, restoration, and management to protect water quality.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland, with emphasis on rural resource areas, watersheds, and targeted ecological areas (TEAs).
requirements_list: Maintain low-density zoning (1 house per 20 acres or less in rural areas)
Maintain more than 50% watershed forest cover
Maintain more than 75% riparian zone forest

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's mandatory hunter safety education program trains first-time hunters in safe and responsible hunting practices. The program is required for anyone purchasing a first Maryland hunting license. It offers traditional in-person classroom courses (12–16 hours, multi-day), hybrid online/field-day courses, trapper education, and advanced specialty courses in bow hunting, muzzleloader hunting, waterfowl hunting, and tree-stand safety. Training is provided by state-certified volunteer instructors at no cost to participants (except the online component of the hybrid option). Students who pass the course receive a Certificate of Competency required to purchase a Maryland hunting license. The course covers firearm safety, hunting skills, wildlife conservation, ethics, and survival skills, and is available statewide.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free, multi-day in-person hunter safety education courses taught by state-certified volunteer instructors. The traditional classroom course runs 12–16 hours and includes classroom instruction, a 50-question multiple choice written test (80% passing score required), a Trail Walk scenario exercise, and a live-fire range session. A hybrid option is also available for participants age 13 and older, combining an online component (fee charged through Hunter-Ed.com) with a free in-person Field Day Workshop. Specialty courses in bow hunting, muzzleloader hunting, waterfowl hunting, trapper education, and tree-stand safety are also offered. Participants who pass all required components receive a Certificate of Competency needed to purchase a first Maryland hunting license. Pre-registration is required.
structured_extraction.program_audience: First-time hunters in Maryland, including youth and adults, who need to satisfy the state's hunter safety education requirement to purchase a hunting license. Especially applicable to new and young hunters wishing to hunt in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participation in hunter safety education and certification training required for first-time hunting license purchase in Maryland; no monetary funds are disbursed.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland. Classes are scheduled and held throughout the year at various locations across the state by independent training teams.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident or person seeking a Maryland hunting license for the first time
Pre-registration is required
Persons under age 13 must attend the traditional fully in-person course and must be accompanied by an adult (18+) during all sessions
Persons at least 13 years old may use the hybrid online/field day option
Must pass a 50-question multiple choice written test with a score of at least 80%
Must pass a Trail Walk scenario exercise
Must demonstrate safe firearm handling to an instructor
Must participate in a live-fire range event (some classes may have a waiver for this requirement)
Students must demonstrate safe and mature behavior throughout the course
Proper clothing for outdoor sessions is required
Students with special needs must contact the Chief Instructor immediately upon registration
Some facilities may have special requirements noted at registration
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register for a class on the DNR website. For the traditional in-person classroom course, register through the DNR registration portal at https://register-ed.com/programs/maryland/88-maryland-hunter-education-classroom-course. For the hybrid option, complete the online training through Hunter-Ed.com first (fee applies), then register for and attend a free one-day Field Day Workshop. Classes fill quickly, so check the schedule frequently. Select an available class near you and follow any special instructions listed for that class. Contact the Chief Instructor for the specific class with any questions.

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary training program for logging professionals in Maryland that provides comprehensive instruction in best management practices, logging aesthetics, forest management, field practicum, logging safety and OSHA, first aid/CPR, and other topics. Loggers who complete the full training agenda earn Master Logger designation and must complete continuing education courses each year to maintain their status. Landowners, foresters, and other interested parties may also attend.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A series of training courses covering best management practices, logging aesthetics, forest management, field practicum, logging safety and OSHA, and first aid/CPR. Most courses cost $20–$40. After completing the initial training, Master Loggers must attend at least one continuing education course per year. Periodic job site visits may also be required to maintain Master Logger status.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Professional loggers, landowners, foresters, and other interested individuals in Maryland involved in forest management and timber harvesting.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training in forest management principles, best management practices, harvest design, logging safety, first aid/CPR, and continuing education to maintain Master Logger certification.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Voluntary program attendance
Complete all initial training courses (best management practices, logging aesthetics, forest management, field practicum, logging safety/OSHA, first aid/CPR)
Attend at least one continuing education course per year to maintain Master Logger status
Periodic job site visits may be required to maintain designation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Attend the required training courses to earn Master Logger designation. Contact John Hooven at the University of Maryland Extension for information on upcoming course schedules and enrollment.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide natural history training program developed in partnership with the University of Maryland Extension and the Maryland Department of Natural Resources Natural Heritage Program. The program provides 60 hours of classroom and field experience covering ecology, flora and fauna identification, environmental interpretation, and citizen science skills, including topics such as forestry management, birds, wetlands, Chesapeake Bay, insects, plants, and interpretation/teaching. Trainees pass content knowledge tests throughout the program, complete a final interpretation project, and earn the title 'Master Naturalist.' Graduates then volunteer 40 hours annually to support community science, habitat restoration, public outreach, education, and field trips. Classes are held at Maryland DNR Natural Heritage Program headquarters in Annapolis (580 Taylor Ave, Annapolis, MD 21401), Anne Arundel County, focusing on the natural history of Maryland's Coastal Plain. The program runs every even year and accepts approximately 20 participants per cohort.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive 60 hours of in-depth classroom and field-based natural history training including instruction in ecology, species identification, environmental interpretation, and citizen science skills covering topics such as forestry management, birds, wetlands, Chesapeake Bay, insects, plants, and interpretation/teaching. Training includes hands-on field days, expert instructors, and content-knowledge testing. Participants must pass content knowledge tests, complete a final interpretation project demonstrating interpretation skills, and donate 40 volunteer hours within one year of training completion to the host organization to earn the 'Master Naturalist' title. Graduates must continue volunteering 40 hours per year to maintain certification and join a network of volunteers supporting the Natural Heritage Program. Applicants must provide three references, pass a background check, and have internet access or arrange assistance for online materials. Fees apply (see University of Maryland Extension for details).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Registration for spring 2026 is now closed; contact paula.becker@maryland.gov for 2028 waitlist
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults and ecologically interested individuals who want to deepen their natural history knowledge in ecology, flora, fauna, and environmental interpretation, and who are willing to volunteer time to support Maryland's natural areas, wildlife, community science, and environmental stewardship.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and education in natural history, ecology, species identification, environmental interpretation, and citizen science skills; volunteer service in habitat restoration, public outreach, environmental education, and community science. No direct financial assistance provided.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide program open to Maryland residents; classes are held at Maryland DNR Natural Heritage Program headquarters at 580 Taylor Ave, Annapolis, MD 21401 (Anne Arundel County), focusing on the natural history of Maryland's Coastal Plain.
requirements_list: Complete 60 hours of classroom and field training
Pass content knowledge tests throughout the program
Complete a final project demonstrating interpretation skills
Donate 40 volunteer hours within one year of training completion to the host organization
Continue volunteering 40 hours per year to maintain certification
Attend training sessions (Wednesdays 6-9pm and Saturdays)
Pass a background check (no criminal convictions more serious than parking/speeding violations)
Provide three references (non-family members) with complete addresses
Have internet access or arrange assistance for accessing online materials
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a completed volunteer application form including personal information, experience, references, and background check authorization. The Program Facilitator reviews the application, contacts references for verification, and conducts a background check. The program is hosted every even year at the Natural Heritage Program's Annapolis headquarters and accepts approximately 20 participants per cohort. For the spring 2026 class, registration is closed. To be placed on a waitlist for the 2028 class, contact Paula Becker at paula.becker@maryland.gov or call 410-260-8568. For policies, fees, and class details, visit the University of Maryland Extension website.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Mentored Hunt Program – National Deer Association Mentored Deer Hunt
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Mentored Hunt Program pairs first-time or lapsed hunters (mentees) with experienced mentor hunters to teach hunting skills. Mentees go through technical lectures covering firearm safety, hunting tips, techniques, and strategies, plus range time to build skills and confidence before heading out to hunt. The program provides ongoing support from the mentor throughout the program at no cost to participants. As part of this broader program, the National Deer Association Mentored Deer Hunt is a specific free 2.5-day mentored muzzleloader deer hunting event held in Accident, MD (Garrett County) that introduces new and lapsed hunters to deer hunting. Selected hunters attend an orientation day including a processing facility tour, range time, and meals provided throughout the event. Most equipment is also provided. Space for the deer hunt is limited and all applications are reviewed for acceptance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free mentorship pairing new or lapsed hunters with experienced mentors statewide. Program includes technical lectures on firearm safety and hunting techniques, range time, and ongoing support from the mentor throughout the program at no cost. Additionally, a specific free 2.5-day mentored muzzleloader deer hunt is held in Accident, MD (Garrett County), including an orientation day, processing facility tour, range time, all meals, and most equipment at no cost to participants. Space for the deer hunt is limited and all applications are reviewed for acceptance.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: December 15, 2025 (for the National Deer Association Mentored Deer Hunt event)

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participation in mentored hunting activities, training, and events at no cost, including a free guided mentored muzzleloader deer hunt with meals and most equipment provided.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The broader mentored hunt program is available statewide in Maryland. The National Deer Association Mentored Deer Hunt event takes place in Accident, MD (Garrett County), January 1–3, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: A fund established through a Memorandum of Understanding between Maryland DNR and offshore wind developer US Wind Inc. to mitigate impacts to commercial and charter fishers from offshore wind energy project construction, operation, and decommissioning. The fund supports fish landing facilities in West Ocean City Harbor, harbor maintenance, and associated fishing businesses affected by the construction of offshore wind turbines. It includes three components: Facility Displacement Component, West Ocean City Harbor Maintenance Component, and Programmatic Funds Component.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: $13.5 million fund with three components: (1) Facility Displacement Component providing financial support to displaced fishing facilities/operators including coastal zoning analysis, capital funds, bulkhead stabilization, and shoreside services; (2) West Ocean City Harbor Maintenance Component covering dredging, dock and shore stabilization support; (3) Programmatic Funds covering gear development, business development/marketing, vessel resilience fund, new entrant incentives, and charter fisher marketing support. Funding based on displacement options: full displacement, partial displacement, or no displacement of existing fishing operations. Funds cannot be used for litigation, regulatory work, or petitioning activities.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: MOU development period extended to May 13, 2025 for stakeholder consultation
structured_extraction.contact_name: Katherine Charbonneau, Assistant Secretary for Aquatic Resources; Catherine McCall, Director, Maryland Coastal Zone Management Program
structured_extraction.program_audience: Commercial fishers (registered Maryland commercial vessels using West Ocean City Harbor), charter/for-hire recreational fishing vessel operators and crews, fishing facilities and operators, new fishing industry entrants, and local fishing industry representatives affected by US Wind's operations and maintenance facility construction.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Bulkhead stabilization, temporary ice service support, business development, harbor maintenance, support for new entrants to the local fishing industry, dredging, dock and shore stabilization, gear development, vessel resilience, charter fisher marketing support, and offsetting unquantifiable impacts to fisheries-dependent businesses and working waterfront. Cannot be used for litigation, regulatory work, or petitioning activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Specific to West Ocean City Harbor area (including 12929 and 12933 South Harbor Road) in Worcester County, Maryland. Related to US Wind OCS-A-0490 lease area impacts approximately 11.5 miles east of Ocean City, Maryland.

Projects must support Maryland's fishing interests

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Funds become available on varying timelines. MOU development period was extended to May 13, 2025 for stakeholder consultation. Visit the Fisheries Compensation Program for Atlantic Coast Offshore Wind page (rfainfo.com) for the most up-to-date information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Natural Resources Police Cadet Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A paid training program for men and women ages 18-20 to learn about becoming a Maryland Natural Resources Police Officer through hands-on field and classroom experience. Cadets complete training including boater and hunter safety courses, self-defense, and specialized units, and then enroll in the Maryland Natural Resources Police Academy to become certified police officers. The program provides a paid salary and full state employee benefits while participants train and prepare for a career in law enforcement with the Maryland Department of Natural Resources.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Cadets receive a paid salary between $36,093 and $55,376 (Grade 7, Step 3 on the State of Maryland Standard Salary Schedule, effective Fiscal Year 2025) while participating in the training program. Officer Candidates receive a base salary of $51,000 during academy training. Benefits include health insurance, retirement (LEOPS pension — a defined benefit plan requiring 7% member contributions, with service retirement at age 50 or after 25 years of eligibility service), annual/sick/personal leave, and other state employee benefits. Additional compensation includes shift differential ($2.00/hour for qualifying shifts), clothing allowance ($1,500 per fiscal year), fitness bonus ($1,000 annual upon passing fitness test), education compensation ($125–$500 based on degree level), and student loan repayment plan (up to $20,000 over a 10-year service commitment, with service on or after January 1, 2019 counting toward eligibility). Cost of living adjustments: 7% July 2022; 5% July 2023 and 2024.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Program provides paid employment and training leading to police academy enrollment and certification as a Maryland Natural Resources Police Officer. Salary and benefits are provided to participants throughout the cadet training program, including retirement pension (LEOPS — a defined benefit pension with member contributions of 7% of earnable compensation), health insurance, student loan repayment assistance (up to $20,000 over a 10-year service commitment), fitness bonuses, education compensation, and clothing allowance.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides small grants to support equitable access to outdoor recreation for communities that have been historically underserved. It funds community-based projects that help Marylanders overcome social, geographic, cultural, physical, and economic barriers to outdoor recreation — such as transportation costs, equipment costs, entry fees, lack of exposure, and not feeling welcome outdoors.

Funds may be used for program staff, materials, transportation, outreach, gear, event costs, or other eligible expenses that directly support project goals related to outdoor equity and access. Approximately 5 awards are made per cycle. Projects must be completed by September 30, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Park Service Youth Group Pass

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Property Tax Credit for Conservation Easement Donations (Maryland Environmental Trust Easement Program)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Environmental Trust (MET) Easement Program allows landowners to voluntarily protect their land through a conservation easement — a legal agreement that permanently restricts future development and subdivision of the property while keeping it in private ownership. The easement is recorded in county land records and runs with the land in perpetuity, protecting agricultural, historic, natural, scenic, scientific, open space, or recreational values. MET monitors the property over time to ensure the terms are upheld. Landowners can continue to live on, farm, and sell their property while potentially receiving significant federal and state tax benefits. The program provides a 15-year property tax credit on unimproved land under easement: during the 15-year period, no property tax is owed on the land subject to the easement. After 15 years, unimproved land is assessed at the highest agricultural rate, even if not actively farmed. The credit does not apply to residential improvements or a minimum of one acre surrounding those improvements. Conservation easements also generate credits directly against state income tax liability. The State Income Tax Credit may be up to $5,000 per year for 15 years (maximum $80,000 total, cannot exceed donation value). No cash payment is made to the landowner; instead, donors may also be eligible for state and federal income, estate, and capital gains tax benefits based on the difference in the property's appraised value before and after the easement. Donors receive federal income tax deductions of up to 50% of adjusted gross income for 16 years (up to 100% for farming/ranching/forestry income earners) based on the appraised value of the easement. Estate tax benefits may also apply, making it easier to pass land to heirs. MET staff are available to visit potential easement sites, meet with landowners, and guide the donation process. Conservation easements are individually negotiated with landowners to protect a property's environmental features. Credits directly offset tax due rather than reducing taxable income. The program accepts both full gifts (no money changes hands) and partial gifts (bargain sales). The program is based on Tax-Property Article Title 9-107 and Md. Code Ann., Tax-Gen. §10–723.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Landowners who donate a conservation easement may receive: (1) a federal income tax deduction of up to 50% of adjusted gross income for 16 years (up to 100% for farming/ranching/forestry income earners) for the appraised value of the easement as a charitable gift; (2) a Maryland state income tax credit of up to $5,000 per year for 15 years (maximum $80,000 total, cannot exceed donation value) generated directly against state income tax liability (Md. Code Ann., Tax-Gen. §10–723); (3) possible federal estate tax exemptions; (4) a 15-year full property tax credit (100% of assessment — no property tax owed) on unimproved, non-commercial land subject to the donated conservation easement (Maryland Tax-Property Article, Section 9-107); and (5) reduced estate and inheritance taxes due to the lowered development potential of the property. The credit does not apply to residential improvements or a minimum of one acre surrounding those improvements. After 15 years, unimproved easement land is assessed at the highest agricultural rate, even if not actively farmed. Credits directly offset tax due rather than reducing taxable income. A qualified appraiser must establish the easement's value to calculate tax benefits; full appraisals mandatory for donations exceeding $500,000. Application filed using the Conservation Property Tax Credit Application with the County Office of the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation on or before October 1 of the taxable year for which relief is sought; subsequent years by June 1. Easement must be donated prior to July 1 of the taxable year to qualify for that year's credit. MET staff are available to visit potential easement sites, meet with landowners, and guide the donation process. Easements are perpetual and run with the land. The program accepts both full gifts and partial gifts (bargain sales). There is no fixed dollar amount — the tax benefit depends on the individual easement's appraised value. MET works with landowners on a case-by-case basis to tailor easement terms to the property's unique features and the owner's goals.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No yearly deadline for easement donation; applications for the property tax credit must be filed on or before October 1 of the taxable year for which credit is sought. Subsequent years' credits to be computed and submitted by June 1. To donate within a particular calendar year, contact MET no later than June of that year. Easement must be donated prior to July 1 of taxable year to qualify for that year's credit. Form 8283 must be submitted to MET at least 10 working days before tax return is due.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners in Maryland who have donated or wish to donate a perpetual conservation easement to the Maryland Environmental Trust or the Maryland Department of Natural Resources, including private landowners with rural properties containing agricultural, historic, natural, scenic, scientific, open space, or recreational values, as well as exceptional urban properties — especially those providing public access. Also includes landowners seeking to permanently protect woodland, wetlands, farmland, scenic areas, historic areas, wild and scenic rivers, or natural areas from development and other harmful uses, or those wishing to pass land to heirs with reduced estate tax burdens. Individuals, institutions, and other legal entities (corporations, LLCs, limited partnerships, trusts) may participate. Conservation organizations, government agencies, and land trusts may also cooperate with MET in the program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eliminates property tax on easement-encumbered unimproved, non-commercial land for 15 years (100% property tax credit); after 15 years, agricultural assessment rate applies. Also provides potential state and federal income, estate, and capital gains tax benefits from donating a conservation easement, including a state income tax credit of up to $5,000/year for 15 years and federal income tax deductions. Conservation easements restrict future development and subdivision of land, permanently protecting natural areas, farmland, forest, open space, and historic properties. The benefit is tax deductions and credits for the landowner in exchange for permanently restricting development rights on qualifying land. Protected conservation purposes include: preservation of land for outdoor recreation/education, protection of natural habitat for fish/wildlife/plants, preservation of open space for scenic enjoyment, preservation of historically important land areas, protection of rare/endangered species habitat, wildlife corridors, and archeological sites.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland, from Garrett County to the Chesapeake Bay shoreline. Any land in Maryland whose conservation would confer a significant public benefit may be considered. Significant rural properties (25+ acres preferred; smaller parcels considered if meeting specific criteria) and exceptional urban properties of all sizes may be considered. Easements must be donated to Maryland Environmental Trust or the Maryland DNR. Application filed with the County Office of the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation. Easements are recorded in local county land records. Preference given to contiguous or clustered protected areas.
