structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Conservation Easement Program Team to determine if your property is eligible and if an MET easement matches your goals. MET staff will visit the potential easement site and meet with the landowner. MET reviews each offer on a case-by-case basis, reviewed by the Board of Trustees and staff using MET policy and the Internal Revenue Code. Typical processing steps are outlined in the Conservation Easement Processing Steps document (12-step process: initial contact with MET planner; property visit; research; easement term discussion; deed drafting; appraisal; lender subordination; board approval; deed signing). If eligible, MET and the landowner work together to finalize the terms of the Deed of Conservation Easement. MET often works with nonprofit land trust partners in this process. Once the easement is accepted, it is drafted, signed, and recorded in the local county land records. A Baseline Documentation Report (Exhibits A-G) must be prepared. Download and complete the Conservation Property Tax Credit Application (available at https://www.dnr.maryland.gov/met/Documents/Conservation_Property_Tax_Credit_Application.pdf) and file it on or before October 1 of the taxable year for which credit is sought (subsequent years by June 1) with the County Office of the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation. Easement must be donated prior to July 1 of the taxable year to qualify. Attach a copy of the recorded Deed of Conservation Easement and the Board of Public Works approval letter. For federal tax deductions, complete Form 8283 and submit to MET at least 10 working days before your tax return is due. Landowners in Harford County may contact the Harford County Department of Planning and Zoning for guidance. MET monitors the property regularly after the easement is in place.

structured_extraction.program_description: Allows Virginia-licensed charter boat operators to provide fishing guide services in Maryland's tidal waters (Chesapeake Bay) without obtaining a Maryland commercial fishing guide license. The permit is free of charge and is available to Virginia charter boat licensees who meet specific documentation requirements. It is valid only for trips originating from Virginia's tidal waters and is nontransferable.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A free, nontransferable permit that allows a Virginia-licensed charter boat operator to run fishing trips in Maryland tidal waters of the Chesapeake Bay without needing a Maryland commercial fishing guide license. The permit is valid only for trips originating from Virginia tidal waters.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Virginia-licensed charter boat operators who wish to guide fishing trips in Maryland tidal waters of the Chesapeake Bay
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Authorization to operate a charter fishing vessel in Maryland tidal waters without a Maryland commercial fishing guide license
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available for charter fishing trips in the tidal waters of the Chesapeake Bay in Maryland, but only for trips originating from the tidal waters of Virginia
requirements_list: Must be licensed by Virginia to operate a charter boat in its jurisdictional tidal waters
Must provide documentation of fishing activity for 2001 and 2002 based on Virginia Marine Resources Commission licensing and reporting requirements
Must submit a completed application form
Must provide proof of Virginia Charter Boat license for 2001 and 2002
Must provide a copy of current Coast Guard license
Must provide a copy of current Virginia Charter Boat license
Must hold all appropriate federal and state licenses while operating
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a completed Fishing Guide Reciprocity Application along with proof of Virginia Charter Boat licensure for 2001 and 2002, a copy of your current Coast Guard license, and your current Virginia Charter Boat license. Allow at least one week for processing. Permits cannot be processed at licensing service centers.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Public Access, Water Trails and Recreation Planning Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program works with local, state, and federal government partners to develop and promote water trails and public access sites across Maryland. It provides technical, mapping, and design assistance to local governments to plan, implement, and promote water trails, and it coordinates the designation of official Maryland Water Trails.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides technical, mapping, and design assistance to local governments to plan, implement, and promote water trails. It also offers official designation as a Maryland Water Trail, which includes listing on the Maryland Water Trails web page and inclusion in promotional materials.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, citizen associations, and nonprofit organizations seeking to develop or designate water trails and public water access sites in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planning, development, and promotion of water trails and public water access sites, including mapping, design, and interpretive components.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — available to partners across all of Maryland.
requirements_list: The trail route must follow an identified route along a waterway in Maryland and be reviewed and approved by the program.
There must be identified public access sites owned, managed, and maintained by a specific entity such as a municipal, local, state, or federal agency.
The trail and its access sites must be accessible and open to the general public.
The trail must have an existing map and/or guide.
The trail must have an interpretive component that educates boaters about state regulations, promotes safety, fosters natural resource stewardship, and shares historical or cultural information.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Lisa Gutierrez at Lisa.Gutierrez@Maryland.gov for more information on the designation process or to request technical assistance.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland law (Md. Natural Resources Code Ann. § 5-103) that requires replacement of forests cleared during state-funded construction projects. When construction using state funds clears 1 acre or more of forested land, the responsible agency must replant trees at a one-to-one acre ratio on public lands within two years or three growing seasons of project completion. If on-site replanting is not possible, the agency may purchase credits in a forest mitigation bank or deposit funds into the Reforestation Fund (at a rate of $0.10 per square foot or approximately $4,356 per acre), which the Maryland Department of Natural Resources uses to plant replacement trees. Applies to units of state or local government and any other person or entity using state funding for construction projects.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Requires constructing agencies to reforest equivalent acreage (1:1 ratio) when 1 acre or more of forest is cleared during state-funded construction. Reforestation must occur on public lands within two years or three growing seasons of project completion. Priority locations: (1) on-site/project right-of-way; (2) in the county and watershed of the construction activity; (3) elsewhere in the county or watershed; (4) via forest mitigation bank credits in the watershed. If on-site replacement is not feasible, the agency may purchase forest mitigation bank credits. As a last resort, the agency deposits $0.10 per square foot (approximately $4,356 per acre) into the Reforestation Fund, which DNR uses to plant replacement trees. DNR field review is completed within 20 working days of submission.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Prior to construction start (before any removal occurs)
structured_extraction.contact_name: Daniel Coy, Urban & Community Forestry Supervisor
structured_extraction.program_audience: State and local government units and private entities using state funding for construction projects that result in clearing 1 acre or more of forest.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tree planting on public lands to offset forest cleared during state-funded construction; forest mitigation bank credits; treatment of plant pest impacts on private property; forest health emergency prevention and response; limited administrative costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Reforestation is prioritized: (1) on-site or within the project right-of-way; (2) in the county and watershed where construction activity occurred; (3) elsewhere in the county or watershed in the state; (4) via mitigation bank credits in the watershed. Regional DNR Forest Service offices serve specific counties: Central (Montgomery, Howard, Baltimore, Harford, Carroll, Cecil), Eastern (Kent, Queen Anne's, Caroline, Talbot, Dorchester, Somerset, Wicomico, Worcester), Southern (Anne Arundel, Prince George's, Calvert, Charles, St. Mary's), and Western (Garrett, Allegany, Washington, Frederick).
requirements_list: Construction project must use $1 or more of state funding
Construction must have caused cutting or clearing of 1 acre or more of forested lands
Replacement must occur on an acre-for-acre (1:1) ratio on public lands
Replanting must occur within two years or three growing seasons of project completion
Submit Site Review Request form during initial design phase, prior to construction start and before any removal occurs
Provide site plans showing forest areas to be removed (highlighted) and removal amounts
Submit estimated clearing and reforestation summary
Identify on-site replacement acreage or locate alternate sites on public lands
Detailed justification required if fund transfer option is requested instead of direct planting
DNR field review is completed within 20 working days of submission
Priority is given to reforestation sites within the same county or watershed as the impacted area
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Constructing agency completes and submits a Reforestation Site Review Request form during the initial design phase, before any forest removal occurs. The submission must include site plans showing forest areas to be removed and estimated clearing and reforestation summary. Forms are submitted to the appropriate regional DNR Forest Service office based on the county where the project is located. DNR conducts a field review within 20 working days and determines reforestation requirements, including on-site planting, off-site public land planting, mitigation bank credits, or fund transfer with approved justification.

structured_extraction.program_description: A six-week program for senior citizens (age 55+) that teaches them about parks, nature, history, and conservation through weekly sessions led by rangers, historians, naturalists, and other Department of Natural Resources experts. Activities include exercise, guided talks, games, hikes, and fellowship. Sessions run approximately 1.5 to 2 hours each. Participants who complete all six sessions become certified Senior Rangers. Space is limited and registration is required at each participating park location. A program fee of $40 applies at some locations ($30 for Golden Age Passholders).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Six weekly group sessions offered at various state parks across Maryland, covering plants, animals, nature, history, conservation, and outdoor activities such as birding, yoga, kayaking/canoeing, hikes, and guided tours. Sessions run approximately 1.5 to 2 hours each (typically 10 AM–12 Noon). A program fee of $40 applies at some locations ($30 for Golden Age Passholders). Participants who complete all sessions receive a Senior Rangers certification. Space is limited; registration is required at individual parks. Session topics vary by location and may include herpetiles, knot-tying, birding, yoga, paddle trips, historic lighthouse tours, tree planting, and a statewide gathering with potluck, fishing, hiking, and boat rides.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Varies by park and session. Registration opens April 1, 2026 at Bohemia River State Park and Elk Neck State Park. Some sessions already at capacity. Check individual park websites or contacts for availability.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents aged 55 and older who want to learn about nature, parks, and the outdoors while staying active and socially engaged. Golden Age Passholders are eligible for a discounted program fee.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable as a direct financial assistance program. Participants pay a program fee ($40, or $30 for Golden Age Passholders) to receive free educational and recreational programming at state parks. No monetary assistance is provided.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at select Maryland state parks including Bohemia River State Park (Chesapeake City, Cecil County), Elk Neck State Park (North East, Cecil County), Tuckahoe Complex, Seneca Creek State Park (Montgomery County, statewide gathering), Patapsco Valley State Park, Janes Island State Park, and the Southern Maryland Recreational Complex (Calvert Cliffs & Merkle NRMA).
requirements_list: Must be age 55 or older
Must register in advance — space is limited
Must attend sessions at a participating Maryland state park
Must complete all sessions to receive Senior Ranger certification
Program fee of $40 applies at some locations ($30 for Golden Age Passholders)
Wear loose clothing for yoga sessions; bring yoga mat if available
No paddling experience required for canoe/kayak trips
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the specific park where you want to attend or use the registration link provided for that location. Some locations offer email registration (e.g., bohemiariver.statepark@maryland.gov for Bohemia River State Park; william.gibb@maryland.gov for Elk Neck State Park; contact Erin Gale for Tuckahoe Complex). Registration opens at different times depending on the park — for example, registration opens April 1, 2026 at Bohemia River and Elk Neck State Parks. Check the program page or individual park websites for current session dates and availability.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland State Income Tax Credit for Conservation Easement Donations
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland landowners who donate a perpetual conservation easement to the Maryland Environmental Trust (MET), the Maryland Department of Natural Resources, or the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation (MALPF) — with Board of Public Works approval — can claim a Maryland state income tax credit. The credit is up to $5,000 per year per individual and can be carried forward for up to 15 additional years, for a maximum total credit of $80,000. Spouses filing jointly may each claim up to $5,000 per year ($10,000 combined). Pass-through entities may also claim the credit, subject to a $200,000 aggregate annual cap per taxable year. When multiple owners jointly donate, each owner is separately entitled to up to $5,000 per year. Additional tax benefits include a federal income tax deduction up to 50% of adjusted gross income (up to 100% for farming/ranching/forestry), a property tax credit on unimproved land for 15 years from donation date, and estate tax reductions through lowered land valuation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State income tax credit worth up to $5,000 per year (or the amount of state income taxes owed, whichever is smaller), based on the appraised value of the donated easement. Credit may be carried forward for up to 15 additional years for a maximum lifetime credit of $80,000. Spouses filing jointly may each claim up to $5,000 per year ($10,000 combined). Pass-through entities may also claim the credit, subject to a $200,000 aggregate annual cap per taxable year (per Md. Ann. Code Tax-General § 10-723). When multiple owners jointly donate, each owner is separately entitled to up to $5,000 per year. Additional benefits include: federal income tax deduction up to 50% of AGI for up to 16 years (up to 100% for farming/ranching/forestry); property tax exemption on unimproved land for 15 years from donation date; estate tax reduction through lowered land valuation. Claimed using Maryland Form 502CR (individuals) or Form 500CR (pass-through entities).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland landowners and members of pass-through entities that donate a perpetual conservation easement to the Maryland Environmental Trust (MET), the Maryland Department of Natural Resources, or the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation (MALPF). Also includes farming, ranching, and forestry operators who may qualify for enhanced federal deduction rates.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of Maryland state income tax liability as an incentive for donating conservation easements to the Maryland Environmental Trust, Maryland Department of Natural Resources, or the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation. Additional benefits apply toward federal income tax liability and local property taxes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to Maryland taxpayers who donate qualifying perpetual conservation easements on property located in Maryland.
requirements_list: Easement must be perpetual
Easement must be conveyed to Maryland Environmental Trust, Maryland Department of Natural Resources, or Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation (MALPF)
Easement must be approved by the Board of Public Works
A qualified appraiser must determine the value of the donation using IRS criteria
Total credit taken cannot exceed the appraised value of the easement
Any payment received for the easement must be deducted from the credit
A taxpayer may not claim both a state income tax deduction and a state income tax credit for the same donation
Pass-through entity aggregate credits claimed by all members cannot exceed $200,000 per taxable year (Md. Ann. Code Tax-General § 10-723)
Form 502CR must be attached to the Maryland individual tax return (Form 502 or 504); pass-through entities use Form 500CR
Must be a Maryland resident (nonresidents are not eligible to claim on Form 502CR)
PTE members must use Form 500CR, not Form 502CR
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Obtain a qualified appraisal to determine the easement value. Complete Maryland Form 502CR Part F (individuals) or Form 500CR (pass-through entities) and attach to your Maryland income tax return (Form 502 or 504). Report the conveyance amount, any payments received, and calculate the credit amount. See Md. Ann. Code Tax-General § 10-723 for statutory details. Contact Maryland Environmental Trust at 410-697-9515 for additional information.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Veterans Conservation Corps (VCC) is a full-time, paid, year-round program that places U.S. military veterans in Maryland State Parks to perform conservation and natural resource management work, including trail building, habitat restoration, facilities maintenance, and environmental education. The program empowers veterans by leveraging their unique backgrounds, diverse job skills, and service ethic to address pressing conservation needs. Members gain hands-on experience, professional training, and certifications to help them pursue careers in conservation and park operations. The VCC focuses on developing veterans professionally through training and on-the-job experience within the Maryland Park Service and the Department of Natural Resources.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Members receive competitive wages, health insurance (provided through the Student Conservation Association), professional skills training and certifications (including Emergency Medical Responder, Wildland Fire Fighter, Chainsaw Use and Care, trail construction, carpentry, and more), uniforms, personal protective equipment, and a $200 boot reimbursement. Positions are one year long with the possibility of renewal. The program also provides on-the-job experience and professional development in conservation service work at Maryland State Parks and public lands.
structured_extraction.program_audience: U.S. military veterans interested in conservation, natural resource management, park operations, environmental stewardship, and outdoor recreation careers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Wages and benefits for veterans performing conservation and park operations work in Maryland State Parks and public lands, as well as professional development and training in conservation service work.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The VCC crew is based at Merkle Natural Resources Management Area in Prince George's County and works regularly in the Southern Maryland Regional Complex, which includes Calvert Cliffs State Park, Cedarville State Forest, Chapel Point State Park, Chapman State Park, Hallowing Point Waterfront Recreation Area, Rosaryville State Park, and Smallwood State Park.
requirements_list: Prior service in the U.S. Armed Forces
Education or experience in park operations, recreation, education, business, administration, forestry, social sciences, or a natural resources related field preferred
Ability to lift up to 50 lbs repeatedly and use hand tools including heavy tools like pulaskis, sledge hammers, and chainsaws
Ability to travel to and from park locations and various work sites
Willingness to serve for one year with possibility of renewal
Willingness to attend some mandatory overnight trainings and projects for up to one week at a time
Willingness to work on certain weekends
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Director of Conservation Corps, Ranger Sara Marcinak, at sara.marcinak@maryland.gov or 443-370-8246 for more information on how to apply.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax incentive program that encourages private landowners to create, develop, rehabilitate, and preserve waterfowl habitats on their land. The program provides technical assistance and enters into 10-year renewable license agreements with landowners for approved waterfowl habitat management projects. Approved project expenditures are treated as contributions to the State of Maryland for tax purposes, providing a tax benefit. The program also provides annual documentation of approved project status for tax reporting purposes.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Landowners enter into 10-year renewable license agreements and receive a Waterfowl Habitat Management Plan developed with a Wildlife and Heritage Service biologist. Approved project expenditures are treated as contributions to the State of Maryland, providing a tax benefit. The department provides annual documentation of approved project status for tax reporting purposes. The agreement is renewable at the end of the 10-year term. Program focuses on semi-permanent water or wetlands restoration projects.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private landowners in Maryland who want to develop or manage waterfowl habitat on their property
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Creating, developing, rehabilitating, and preserving waterfowl habitats on private lands, including wetland improvements, semi-permanent water features, and nesting and resting habitat to support breeding, migrating, and wintering waterfowl
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland for private landowners; project location must be in Maryland though mailing address can be anywhere
requirements_list: Project area must encompass a minimum of 10 contiguous acres of habitat that provides food and/or cover for ducks
Project must include at least 1 acre of semi-permanent water with nesting and resting habitat within or near the water
Normal agricultural practices are permitted within the project area
Private lands used for commercial hunting enterprises are not eligible
Landowner must enter into a 10-year license agreement with the Wildlife and Heritage Service
Landowner must agree to and carry out an approved Waterfowl Habitat Management Plan
License agreement is renewable at the end of the 10-year term
Landowner signature required
Map of project area required showing nearest town, access roads, and property location
Project area acreage specification required (total acres and acres of semi-permanent water/wetlands)
Current land use description required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Review project eligibility rules to confirm your property qualifies. 2. Complete the Maryland Waterfowl Restoration Program Application Form with landowner information, property details, and a map of the project area. 3. Mail the completed application to: Maryland Waterfowl Restoration Program, DNR- Wildlife & Heritage Service, PO Box 68, Wye Mills, MD 21679, or call 410-827-8612 ext. 103. 4. A Regional Habitat Biologist for your county will review your application and contact you to arrange a site inspection. Application may be referred to the Migratory Game Bird Advisory Committee. 5. After acceptance, you receive an official information kit with all program documents. 6. Contact Richard Walls at 410-827-8612 ext. 103 with questions.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free fishing club open to young people ages 5 to 15 in Maryland. Members receive two Maryland Youth Fishing Club stickers, can find information about special youth fishing events, share fishing stories and photos, and learn new things about fishing. Members also receive fishing information, opportunities, tips, and fun, with email updates available.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free membership with two Maryland Youth Fishing Club stickers upon joining. Members get access to fishing information, opportunities, tips, and fun, as well as information about special youth fishing events and educational fishing resources. Email updates are also available.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Youth ages 5 to 15 in Maryland interested in fishing.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable — this is a free membership club providing stickers and access to fishing events and educational resources.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be between the ages of 5 and 15
Membership is free
Parent/Guardian signature required
Provide name, address, and birthday
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the sign-up form with member information (name, address, birthday) and parent/guardian signature. Mail completed form to Angel Wright, 580 Taylor Ave, B-2, Annapolis, MD 21401, or fax to 410-260-8279. You may also download and print the sign-up sheet or use the online registration form at https://goo.gl/forms/cHG2TtEpqlwS1Pzv2. Option to receive email updates upon registration.

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary program that encourages Maryland residents to create backyard wildlife habitat. The program provides fact sheets, educational resources, nest box plans, landscaping guides, and identification guides to help landowners enhance their property for wildlife by creating food, water, and shelter resources. It also publishes a quarterly newsletter called HabiChat highlighting native plants, animals, and habitat-enhancing activities. Resources include identification guides for common backyard herps, bees, butterflies and skippers, feeder birds, mammals, mammal tracks, broadleaf and coniferous trees, and snakes, as well as a School Wildlife Garden Guide for creating native plant wildlife gardens in school settings to benefit songbirds, monarch butterflies, and pollinators.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free educational fact sheets, nest box plans, landscaping guides, identification guides, and a quarterly newsletter (HabiChat) to help landowners, schools, and communities create and improve wildlife habitat on their property. Resources include identification guides for wildlife species, a School Wildlife Garden Guide with design plans for songbird, monarch butterfly, and pollinator gardens, and references to funding sources and plant suppliers for school garden projects.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents, landowners, schools, educators, students, and communities interested in creating or improving backyard wildlife habitat on their property or schoolyard.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Creating and enhancing wildlife habitat by providing food, water, shelter, and space for wildlife on private lands, backyards, and schoolyards. For school gardens: garden installation and maintenance including native plants, seeds, lumber, mulch, and signage.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must respect local or county laws, homeowners' agreements, and other covenants.
For school wildlife gardens: obtain school administration and principal approval.
For school wildlife gardens: submit proposal addressing reason for installation, curricular connections, funding sources, and maintenance plan.
For school wildlife gardens: contact Department of Physical Facilities for new planting areas (6-12 months in advance).
For school wildlife gardens: call MISS UTILITY before digging.
For school wildlife gardens: establish maintenance plan before installation.
For school wildlife gardens: select appropriate site with 4-6 hours of full sun for butterfly/pollinator gardens.
For school wildlife gardens: ensure good drainage and access to a water source.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: No formal application required for individual participants. Participants voluntarily use the program's resources, fact sheets, and guides to create wildlife habitat on their property. For school wildlife gardens: develop a garden proposal, obtain administrative approval, contact Physical Facilities, prepare site, plant, and maintain the garden.

structured_extraction.program_description: A citizen science and stewardship program where waterfront property owners and community volunteers grow young oysters (called spat) in wire mesh cages suspended from their private piers. After about nine months, the grown oysters are collected and planted on local sanctuaries closed to harvesting, helping restore Maryland's native oyster population and improve Chesapeake Bay water quality and ecosystem health. The program launched in September 2008 on the Tred Avon River and has since expanded to operate in 32 rivers and creeks with approximately 7,500 cages. The program runs September through May. Participation is free of charge.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive free oyster cages (wire mesh) stocked with oyster spat at no cost, plus planning and implementation guidance, sanctuary selection by DNR, and optional data collection training and forms. DNR provides cages and oyster spat entirely free of charge and cannot provide funding for tasks to be completed by applicants. At pickup, participants receive a briefing and information package on caring for the oysters.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Waterfront property owners, citizen volunteers, community associations, non-profit organizations, RiverKeeper groups, local government entities, and public schools in Maryland with access to a suitable pier or wharf in one of the 32 participating tributaries, who are willing to tend oyster cages for up to 10 months and are interested in oyster restoration and Chesapeake Bay stewardship.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Growing and protecting young oysters in cages during their first year of life, after which they are planted on local oyster sanctuaries closed to harvesting, to restore the native oyster population and improve Chesapeake Bay water quality. DNR explicitly states it cannot provide funding for tasks to be completed by applicants.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be located on one of the 32 participating rivers, creeks, or coves in Maryland's Chesapeake Bay watershed with appropriate salinity levels supporting oyster survival and growth. The program began on the Tred Avon River in 2008 and has since expanded statewide.
requirements_list: Must have an existing pier or wharf with at least four feet of water at low tide
Must be located in one of the selected program tributaries (rivers, creeks, coves, or inlets) with appropriate salinity levels
Must be willing to maintain oyster cages for up to 10 months (program runs September through May)
Must keep cages clean by rinsing every one to two weeks and protect oysters from freezing in winter
Must not eat or harvest the oysters — all oysters are planted in sanctuaries
Do not consume oysters grown at private piers due to potential pathogenic contamination from untested waters
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Waterfront property owners and eligible organizations can register for oyster gardening online via the provided registration link or apply for their tributary to join the program using the PDF application form (submitted by March 31). After signing up, participants are contacted by a local sponsor when cages are ready for pickup. At pickup, participants receive cages, spat, and a briefing and information package on oyster care. Optional data collection training is available upon request.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide program administered by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources that encourages Maryland residents and organizations to plant native trees by offering a $25 coupon toward the purchase of a qualifying native or recommended tree at participating retail nurseries and garden centers. The program is funded through a Clean Air Act violation settlement from a major power generator, in partnership with the Office of the Attorney General and participating tree vendors.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A $25 coupon is redeemable at the time of purchase at participating retail nurseries and garden centers toward one qualifying native or recommended tree with a retail value of at least $50. The coupon must be completely filled in and signed by the customer. One coupon per tree purchased; wholesale purchases do not qualify. The $25 cost is funded through a Clean Air Act violation settlement from a major power generator, in partnership with the Office of the Attorney General and participating tree vendors. A recommended list of native and acceptable tree species (organized by small and large trees) is also provided to guide species selection; trees must be from the recommended list, cultivars of native species, or native species to Maryland.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents and organizations who want to plant native or recommended trees on their property, purchasing from participating retail nurseries and garden centers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of a qualifying native or recommended tree (retail value $50 or more) from the Marylanders Plant Trees Native and Recommended Tree List at a participating retail nursery or garden center.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland at participating retail nurseries and garden centers.
requirements_list: Tree must have a retail value of at least $50
Tree must be on the Marylanders Plant Trees Native and Recommended Tree List (including cultivars of native species or native species to Maryland)
Tree must be purchased from a participating MPT nursery or garden center
Coupon must be completely filled in and signed by the customer
One coupon per tree purchased
Only retail sales qualify; wholesale purchases do not
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Print a coupon from the DNR program website. Step 2: Find a participating nursery or garden center in your area. Step 3: Fill in the coupon completely and sign it. Step 4: Present the completed coupon at the time of purchase to receive the $25 discount toward a qualifying native or recommended tree. Contact Ryan Mayenschein (ryan.mayenschein@maryland.gov, 667-408-0000) with questions about specific tree species.

structured_extraction.program_name: Monocacy NRMA Agricultural Land Lease Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Park Service leases farmable lands at Monocacy River Natural Resources Management Area to interested farmers for short-term agricultural use. The leased lands contain prime agricultural soils and have a history of being farmed, supporting open space, wildlife habitat, and locally sourced food production. Available parcels are made accessible through a competitive bid process. Two properties are currently available for bid: the Henderson property (103.27 acres, 11 fields) and the Rock Hall Chadwick property (43.59 acres, 6 fields), located near Dickerson in Frederick County, Maryland. Leases are for approximately three years (May 1, 2024 – March 31, 2027) with conservation and best management practice requirements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Short-term leases of agricultural cropland at Monocacy NRMA. Two properties are available for bid: the Henderson property (103.27 acres across 11 fields) and the Rock Hall Chadwick property (43.59 acres across 6 fields), both located at 221 Dickerson Rd, Dickerson, MD 20842. Minimum acceptable bid is $85/acre. Lease term is approximately three years (May 1, 2024 – March 31, 2027), paid in three annual equal installments due by May 1 each year. Interested farmers submit a sealed bid using the property-specific bid packet forms provided by the Maryland Park Service.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Jacqueline Tahsuda (Supervisor, Land & Property Management); Shea Niemann (Area Manager, Monocacy NRMA)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers and agricultural operators interested in leasing cropland at Monocacy River Natural Resources Management Area in Frederick County, Maryland. Minority businesses are encouraged to participate.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Short-term agricultural crop farming on leased parkland that has prime agricultural soils and a history of cultivation. Land must be used for crop farming operations only; no subletting or sharecropping permitted.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Monocacy River Natural Resources Management Area, 221 Dickerson Rd, Dickerson, MD 20842, Frederick County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Submit a sealed bid using the property-specific bid packet form for the chosen property (Henderson or Rock Hall Chadwick)
Bid must be submitted by 12:00pm April 13, 2024 via mail or in person to Seneca Creek State Park
Minimum acceptable bid: $85/acre
Comply with all Federal, State, and Local laws
Follow good agricultural practices
Maintain soil fertility and provide soil tests upon request
Obtain written approval for all chemicals before application
Control noxious weeds per Maryland Department of Agriculture standards
Maintain 100-foot vegetative buffer from water bodies (no planting, plowing, or fertilizers within buffer)
Plant fall cover crops on applicable fields
Implement multi-species cover crop and reduced tillage/no-till practices
Obtain and comply with a Nutrient Management Plan
Obtain Soil and Water Quality Plan(s) approved by the relevant Soil Conservation District
Implement Best Management Practices (BMPs) including grassed waterways, field edge buffers, riparian buffers, and filter strips
Maintain comprehensive farming history documentation
Personal use by tenant only; no subletting or sharecropping
Allow public hunting access on premises
Surrender premises in good condition at lease termination
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and fill out the bid packet for the property of interest (Henderson or Rock Hall Chadwick). Submit a sealed bid proposal with per-acre amount and lump sum total, along with all required information. Return the completed form by mail or in person to Seneca Creek State Park, 11950 Clopper Road, Gaithersburg, MD 20878 by 12:00pm on April 13, 2024. Successful bidder must sign a Cropland Lease Agreement.

structured_extraction.program_name: NOAA Chesapeake Bay Watershed Education and Training (B-WET Chesapeake) Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Grants to support hands-on watershed education for students and teachers to foster stewardship of the Chesapeake Bay.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants to support hands-on watershed education for students and teachers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students and teachers in the Chesapeake Bay watershed
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Hands-on watershed education programs
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Chesapeake Bay watershed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the NOAA Chesapeake Bay program website.

structured_extraction.program_description: A seven-day residential summer camp for high school students interested in careers in natural resources. The camp covers traditional forestry, GIS/GPS technology, urban forestry, wildlife habitat, fisheries, and watershed ecology. Students learn from industry and natural resource professionals and can develop contacts for future employment. Local Forest Conservancy District Boards recruit two students per county, conduct interviews, and provide partial scholarships to cover camp costs. Students aged 16 or older may earn two transferable college credits from Allegany College of Maryland by attending the full week and passing an exam.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Partial scholarships are provided by local Forest Conservancy District Boards to cover the cost of attending the seven-day Natural Resources Career Camp. Students aged 16 or older who attend the full week and pass an exam may also earn two transferable college credits from Allegany College of Maryland at no additional cost.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications for NRCC 2025 are now being accepted; camp runs July 20–26, 2025
structured_extraction.program_audience: High school students interested in careers in natural resources
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Attendance at a seven-day natural resources career camp, including instruction, activities covering traditional forestry, GIS/GPS technology, urban forestry, wildlife habitat, fisheries, and watershed ecology, and potential transferable college credit from Allegany College of Maryland
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide — each of Maryland's 24 Forest Conservancy District Boards recruits students from their respective counties
requirements_list: Must be a high school student
Two students per county are recruited and interviewed by local Forest Conservancy District Boards
Must be recruited and interviewed by a local Forest Conservancy District Board
Must be at least 16 years of age by the first day of camp to be eligible for college credits
Must attend the entire week and complete an exam to earn college credits
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local Forest Conservancy District Board, which is responsible for recruiting, interviewing, and providing partial scholarships. Applications are also available through the Maryland Forestry Foundation website at https://www.marylandforestryfoundation.org/programs/students-educators/nrcc/ and the Maryland Forestry Boards website at marylandforestryboards.org/nrcc.cfm.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Maryland and Delaware-specific program established through a Memorandum of Understanding between Maryland DNR and offshore wind developer US Wind Inc. to help coastal fishing vessel operators enhance safety and navigation equipment and training for operating in and around the offshore wind energy area (Lease Area OCS-A 0490, approximately 80,000 acres in federal waters approximately 11.5 miles off the coast of Maryland). Provides vouchers for mariners to access navigational enhancement and training services, including equipment installation/upgrades and training for safe navigation and fishing activities in and around wind turbines.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: $1.04 million program for Maryland and Delaware coastal fishing industry participants to enhance safety and navigation capabilities around the wind energy area. Equipment upgrades: commercial vessels up to $10,000; for-hire charter vessels up to $5,000. Training: $1,000 per vessel for up to two participants for professional mariner or radar training, or to recover reasonable income losses during training participation. $35,000 toward experiential training development at Maryland Maritime Institute of Technology and Graduate Studies (MITAGS) facility. Eligible vessels and individuals may choose to participate in radar training or upgrade navigation equipment on their vessels via a voucher system.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland and Delaware commercial and charter vessel owners, fishers, and for-hire fishing operators who need to navigate in and around the offshore wind energy area (OCS-A 0490).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Navigation equipment installation and upgrades for vessels operating near the offshore wind energy area; radar and professional mariner training; registration fees for training; recovery of reasonable income losses during training participation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Specific to Maryland and Delaware coastal fishing industry participants operating in or around Lease Area OCS-A 0490, approximately 11.5 miles east of Ocean City, Maryland, with primary focus on the Worcester County/West Ocean City Harbor area.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland or Delaware coastal commercial fishing vessel operator or captain
Must be eligible based on vessel type and use in the offshore wind project area
Commercial fishing vessels or U.S. Coast Guard inspected for-hire/charter fishing vessels directly or reasonably expected to be impacted by wind turbines in Lease Area OCS-A 0490
MOU to be finalized by May 13, 2025
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the Fisheries Compensation Program for Atlantic Coast Offshore Wind page (rfainfo.com) for the most up-to-date information on how to participate. Parties are seeking feedback from commercial and recreational fishing industry during MOU development.

structured_extraction.program_name: New or Replacement Pumpout Installation Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: Grant for marinas to purchase and install a new or replacement boat sewage pumpout system. Funded through the federal Clean Vessel Act and the Maryland Waterway Improvement Fund.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Installation grant for the purchase and installation of a new or replacement pumpout system at a marina. Specific award amounts are not stated on the program page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Marina operators seeking to install a new or replacement boat sewage pumpout system in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and installation of a new or replacement boat sewage pumpout system.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to marinas located statewide in Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review the How to Apply for a Grant for a New Pumpout page and complete the Pumpout Grant Application and Agreement. Contact pumpouts.dnr@maryland.gov with questions.

structured_extraction.program_name: Non-Shellfish Aquaculture Technical Assistance (Fishing and Boating Services)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Natural Resources Fishing and Boating Services provides technical assistance to aquaculture permit holders and anyone engaged in non-shellfish aquaculture or related activities. Assistance covers fish and aquatic species growing methods and aquatic disease control, and is available upon request. An aquaculture permit (free of charge, valid for five years) is required before operating a facility, with an annual report summarizing activities, production techniques, and species stocked or harvested. The program covers tank culture, pond culture, and educational projects.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free technical assistance for growing methods and aquatic disease control is available upon request to anyone engaged in non-shellfish aquaculture or related activities in Maryland. The program also includes regulatory permitting, inspections, and monitoring of non-shellfish aquaculture facilities (tank culture, pond culture, educational projects). An aquaculture permit (free of charge, valid for five years) is required before operating a facility.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals, non-profits, businesses, commercial producers, hobby farmers, researchers, and educational institutions engaged in non-shellfish aquaculture or related activities in Maryland, including commercial pond rearing, commercial fish growers, private fish stocking, and private pond operators.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Technical guidance on fish and aquatic species growing methods and aquatic disease control for aquaculture operations, as well as facility development and operation (tank/pond culture systems, water sourcing, discharge treatment).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland for anyone operating or planning to operate an aquaculture facility in Maryland state waters and facilities.
requirements_list: Must obtain a free aquaculture permit before engaging in aquaculture or related activities
Aquaculture permit must be renewed every five years
Annual report required summarizing activities, production techniques, and species stocked or harvested
Failure to submit annual report or conduct planned activities may result in permit revocation
Health certification and species origin documentation
Facility location map with directions
Facility sketch including inflow/effluent systems
Identification of nearest receiving body of water
Solid waste management plan for mortalities/byproducts
Containment systems for hybrid/non-native species
Statement of operational goals and production estimates
Workers' compensation compliance certificate or insurance policy
Compliance with all applicable health and environmental laws
Quarterly shipping/receiving records by species (3-year retention)
Immediate disease notification to Department
Facility inspection access
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and submit an Aquaculture Permit Application (available from DNR). For renewals or amendments, resubmit the application noting desired changes. Technical assistance is available upon request after obtaining a permit.

structured_extraction.program_description: A lottery-based licensing process that allows Maryland hunters to reserve designated locations (blind sites) on state tidal waters to hunt waterfowl. Hunters enter an online lottery for a county of their choice, and lottery winners select up to two blind sites during a virtual meeting with a Maryland DNR representative.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Hunters can license up to two offshore waterfowl blind sites at $20 per site. Sites are reserved through a virtual appointment process with DNR staff who help the hunter select eligible locations on an electronic county map. Sites are reserved for 30 calendar days after licensing, pending electronic payment through the MD Outdoors system.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Lottery registration: July 16, 2025 through July 29, 2025 at 11:59 pm
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland resident hunters seeking to reserve offshore waterfowl blind sites on state tidal waters; also open to riparian landowners regardless of residency or hunting license status.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Licensing a designated location on state waters to hunt waterfowl from an offshore blind.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland; hunters must be Maryland residents (landowners are exempt from residency requirement).
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident (exception: riparian landowners or hunters with written landowner permission are exempt)
Must have purchased either a 2024-2025 or 2025-2026 Maryland hunting license prior to the appointment (landowners and those with written landowner permission are exempt)
Must have a valid MD Outdoors account
Must provide an email address and cell phone number when registering
Must be present in the virtual meeting to reserve sites — the lottery winner or person who made the appointment must attend
Landowners must provide a copy of property information and a tax map or legible map showing the shoreline location
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Register online through the MD Outdoors licensing system between July 16 and July 29, 2025 to enter the free lottery. 2. Lottery winners are notified by email with a date and time for a virtual meeting via Microsoft Teams. 3. During the 20-minute virtual meeting (up to 10 minutes for site selection), hunters work with a DNR representative to select up to two blind sites on an electronic county map. 4. After the meeting, hunters submit electronic payment of $20 per site through their MD Outdoors account within 30 days. 5. After the initial lottery period, remaining appointments are available by self-scheduling on a virtual calendar starting August 14 for meetings beginning August 19.

structured_extraction.program_description: Operation Campout is a free gear-lending program run by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources / Maryland Park Service for active military members, veterans, wounded warriors, and their immediate families. Participants can borrow camping gear — including a 6-person tent, ground tarp, sleeping pads, folding chairs, cook stove, lantern, and roasting sticks — at no charge at participating state parks across Maryland. The program is designed to offer an opportunity to experience Maryland's natural, cultural, historical, and recreational resources firsthand through camping. It is especially suited for military individuals and families who are new to camping or who are stationed or recovering in the area, giving families a chance to reconnect with nature in a safe and relaxing setting. Participating parks include Cunningham Falls, Swallow Falls, New Germany, Rocky Gap, Patapsco Valley, Pocomoke River, and Janes Island State Parks. Campsites include picnic tables and fire pits; restroom and shower facilities are available at some locations, and some sites offer electric hook-ups. Standard camping service charges for the campsite apply. Pets are welcome in designated loops and service animals are welcome. Importation of personal firewood is prohibited due to the Emerald Ash Borer threat; firewood is available at the park.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free loan of camping gear (6-person tent, ground tarp, sleeping pads, folding chairs, cook stove, lantern, and roasting sticks) for use at participating state parks across Maryland. Participants are responsible for bringing sleeping bags, food, personal items, cookware, dishware, cooler with ice, water containers, flashlight, first-aid kit, and other essentials. Campsites with picnic tables and fire pits are provided; restroom and shower facilities are available at some locations. Some sites have electric hook-ups. Participants pay nightly campsite reservation fees. Reservations must be made directly by phone or email with the desired park office. Campsite accommodates up to 6 people.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Active duty military members, wounded warriors, veterans, and their immediate families — including those new to camping or experienced campers stationed or recovering in Maryland. Open to all ages (no age restrictions for children); groups of up to 6 people. Pets welcome in designated loops; service animals welcome.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Borrowing camping gear at no charge and use of campsites at participating Maryland state parks, including Cunningham Falls, Swallow Falls, New Germany, Rocky Gap, Patapsco Valley, Pocomoke River, and Janes Island State Parks.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at seven participating state parks across Maryland: Cunningham Falls, Swallow Falls, New Germany, Rocky Gap, Patapsco Valley, Pocomoke River, and Janes Island State Parks. Rocky Gap State Park is located in Flintstone, Maryland (Allegany County). New Germany State Park is located in Garrett County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be an active military member, veteran, wounded warrior, or immediate family member
Must be new to camping or an experienced camper stationed or recovering in the area
Must contact the desired participating park directly by phone or email to make a reservation
Must inform park staff that the reservation is through Operation Campout
Standard camping fees apply
Participants must bring: sleeping bags, food, personal items, cookware, dishware, cooler with ice, water containers, flashlight, first-aid kit, clothing, toiletries, and other essentials
Personal firewood importation is prohibited due to the Emerald Ash Borer threat; firewood is available for purchase at the park
Campsite accommodates up to 6 people
Pets welcome in designated loops; service animals welcome
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the participating state park of your choice directly by phone or email to reserve camping gear and check available dates. Specify that the reservation is for 'Operation Campout!' gear. For Rocky Gap State Park, call 301-722-1480 or email rockygap.statepark@maryland.gov. For general inquiries, contact Christina Carlson at 443-603-6073 or Christina.Carlson@maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: A permit that allows out-of-state suppliers to sell finfish intended to be stocked in Maryland waters. Suppliers must pass annual fish health inspections and meet documentation requirements to ensure fish do not introduce disease to native or naturalized aquatic resources. Requires statistically based representative sampling of all fish lots and species-dependent pathogen testing per AFS Bluebook or OIE protocols.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Regulatory permit authorizing out-of-state finfish suppliers to sell fish for stocking in Maryland waters, subject to annual fish health inspections and documentation of fish health history. Includes annual on-site fish health inspection with statistically based representative sampling for certifiable pathogens. No financial assistance is provided; this is a compliance and authorization program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Out-of-state aquaculture facilities, fish suppliers, hatcheries, baitfish suppliers, and broodstock facilities seeking to sell finfish for stocking in Maryland waters.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Permit to sell and stock finfish in Maryland waters from out-of-state facilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to out-of-state suppliers seeking to stock fish in Maryland waters statewide.
requirements_list: Permit is limited to the sale of finfish from a facility outside Maryland.
Finfish must be evaluated by MDNR for risk of viral, bacterial, or parasitic infections.
Only finfish from approved locations and of acceptable species or genetic origin may be stocked in Maryland waters.
Sale must be accompanied by a receipt showing origin, date of sale, supplier name and address, species and amount.
Live finfish must be accompanied by a permit to stock fish in Maryland waters.
All fish must come from approved sources and be held in isolation once received.
Annual fish health inspection is required from a qualified inspector (USDA/APHIS-accredited veterinarian, AFS/FHS-certified aquatic animal health inspector, or MDNR-recognized inspector).
Inspector cannot be the facility owner or have direct supervisory authority over the facility.
Statistically based representative sampling of all fish lots is required.
Species-dependent pathogen testing per AFS Bluebook or OIE Manual protocols (including furunculosis, enteric redmouth, bacterial kidney disease, viral diseases, whirling disease, etc.).

Fish health inspection reports must include species examined, lot descriptions (lot number, species, age, number of fish sampled), pathogens tested, diagnostic methods used, inspector qualifications, and other required details.
Inspection is valid for one year from the effective date; expires upon discovery of a prohibited or regulated disease.
Brokers holding fish at alternative locations prior to stocking must submit documentation of an isolation facility.
Isolation facility must have documented water supply and biosecurity protocols (foot baths, separate equipment, restricted access, physical barriers, disinfection procedures, dead fish disposal).
Disinfection of transport and holding tanks between shipments is required.
Separate listings required for fish from multiple growing sites.
Each species must originate from source listed on permit.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and review the general information and requirements document. Gather fish health inspection reports from facility of origin and current holding facility. Submit completed application form listing fish species (scientific and common names), age in months, quantity, and place of origin for all fish at time of stocking. Brokers must also submit isolation facility documentation and property drawing. Submit either the printable application form or the online Finfish Supplier Application (https://forms.gle/PJ6AX7vAoF9WY8Mt8). Notify DNR of any population changes. For hard copy submissions or inquiries, contact Pond Stocking at pond.dnr@maryland.gov or (410) 260-2403.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides funding to help local governments, nonprofits, and higher education institutions understand and plan for coastal and precipitation-based flood impacts within Maryland's Coastal Zone. Funded projects support flood risk assessments, vulnerability analyses, adaptation planning, and the development of conceptual or engineered designs for flood adaptation strategies. Projects should improve understanding of flood vulnerabilities and result in risk-reduction strategies or higher regulatory standards that support on-the-ground adaptation projects.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Awards up to $125,000 per project, with typical requests ranging from $40,000 to $100,000 for projects up to one year in duration. Assistance may be provided as a direct financial grant or as technical assistance through a DNR-selected contractor. Funding becomes available October 1, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, non-governmental organizations, and higher education institutions with projects located within Maryland's Coastal Zone addressing flood resilience and climate adaptation planning.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Flood risk assessments of current and future flood vulnerability, incorporation of adaptation strategies into local planning processes, development of conceptual or engineered designs for identified flood adaptations, community and stakeholder engagement related to flood resilience planning, and production of risk-reduction strategies or higher regulatory standards that support on-the-ground adaptation projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located within Maryland's Coastal Zone. Project areas can encompass both public and private lands.
requirements_list: Project must be located within Maryland's Coastal Zone
Applicant must be a local jurisdiction, non-governmental organization, or institution of higher education
Projects addressing tidal flooding must reference the jurisdiction's nuisance flood plan, flood mitigation plan, or other relevant planning process

Projects addressing sea level rise are strongly encouraged to use Maryland's 2018/2023 Sea Level Rise Projections guidance; Appendix A (Guidance for Using Maryland's 2023 SLR Projections) must be completed for projects addressing sea level rise
Projects addressing precipitation-induced flooding must be consistent with trends in the Northeast chapter of the Fourth National Climate Assessment
Must submit a transmittal letter on official letterhead signed by an authorized executive
Must submit letters of support from county or town council, town administrator, county executive, or appropriate decision-making body
Must submit photographs of impacted areas
Must submit a complete Budget Table (available on Grants Gateway website)
Must submit a Communication and Engagement Strategy
Projects must demonstrate intent to advance recommended solutions and commit to achieving a program change
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Grants Gateway portal (WizeHive/webportalapp.com). Submit a complete proposal including all required attachments: transmittal letter, letters of support, photographs, budget table, Appendix A (if applicable), and a Communication and Engagement Strategy. Proposals are reviewed based on completeness, problem description and need, technical feasibility and appropriateness, use of climate tools, advancement of flood risk reduction, community engagement, partner commitment, and readiness to proceed.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Outdoor Recreation Legacy Partnership Program (ORLP) is a competitive grant initiative under the Land and Water Conservation Fund (LWCF) Act aimed at enhancing parks, recreational opportunities, and conservation areas in urban, underserved communities. It complements LWCF Stateside and Local Assistance Program formula grants and funds acquisition and development of parks and outdoor recreation areas, as well as renovation of existing facilities. Projects must be in communities with populations of 25,000 or more (per the 2020 Census) and determined to be underserved based on federal environmental justice screening tools (CEJST, EJScreen) or other documentation. The program supports public-private partnerships to leverage project support, fosters resilience and sustainable landscape development through local public greenspace investment, and enhances public health in underserved areas through active living, land conservation, water resource protection, cultural preservation, native landscape restoration, and disaster mitigation. Grants are competitive at the federal level, with applications coordinated through Maryland DNR before submission to the National Park Service.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive matching grants for park and outdoor recreation projects in underserved communities. Grants range from an estimated $300,000 to $15,000,000 per award, with 25-40 awards per calendar year. Grants are provided on a matching basis for up to 50% of total project-related allowable costs (1:1 non-federal cost share required). Funds may be used for acquisition and/or development of lands and outdoor recreation facilities, including renovation and rehabilitation. The National Park Service selects applicants based on a pre-application, then requires a final application to be submitted within one year. Applications go through Maryland DNR before being forwarded to NPS.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted any time before June 1 and November 1 each year (11:59 PM Eastern Time Zone). Spring Round: pre-applications due April 15 to DNR, full applications due June 1 to NPS. Fall Round: pre-applications due September 15 to DNR, full applications due November 1 to NPS.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments and eligible entities in underserved communities with a population of 25,000 or more seeking to develop, improve, or expand parks and outdoor recreation facilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition and development of parks and outdoor recreation areas, renovation of existing facilities, and infrastructure projects. Maximum 25% of total budget may be used for costs not directly attributable to physical development or rehabilitation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be located in a community with a population of 25,000 or more (per the 2020 Census) that is determined to be underserved using CEJST, EJScreen, or other written documentation.
requirements_list: Project must be located in a community with a population of 25,000 or more per the 2020 Census
Community must be determined to be underserved using CEJST, EJScreen, or other written documentation
Must coordinate with Maryland Department of Natural Resources (DNR)
Pre-application must be submitted to DNR before full application is submitted to NPS
Full application to NPS must be submitted within one year of pre-application selection
Projects must align with the state's Statewide Comprehensive Outdoor Recreation Plan (SCORP)
50% (1:1) non-federal cost share required
Projects typically take 1-3 years to complete from last Grant Agreement signature
Compliance with DOI Standard Terms and Conditions
American iron, steel, and manufactured products per 2 CFR 184 required for infrastructure projects
Geospatial data must meet FGDC or DOI standards
Federal Financial Report (SF-425) submission required
Post-completion inspections required within 5 years and at least once every 5 years thereafter
Property must be retained in perpetuity for public outdoor recreation use
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Molly Pickel at DNR to discuss potential projects before applying. Submit a pre-application to DNR by the applicable round deadline (April 15 for Spring, September 15 for Fall). DNR reviews materials for eligibility and completeness. Full applications are then due to NPS by June 1 (Spring) or November 1 (Fall) at 11:59 PM Eastern Time. Successful applicants are notified approximately 3 months later that they may proceed to a final application to NPS.

structured_extraction.program_name: Outreach and Engagement Program (Land Trust Assistance)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Environmental Trust (MET) Outreach and Engagement Program provides technical assistance to local non-profit land trusts and conservation partners that co-hold conservation easements with MET. The program facilitates communication and cooperation among Maryland land conservation organizations, provides educational opportunities, stewardship assistance, and supports land conservation initiatives. It helps land trusts access services and programs from state agencies, counties, and other land trusts, and offers direct support for easement monitoring and stewardship activities through resources, training, and capacity-building support.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Technical assistance includes monitoring resources and trainings, record-keeping guidance, publications and aids (including a model easement document), access to MET's online Land Trust Toolbox, and capacity-building mini-grants through the Keep Maryland Beautiful Program. Additional benefits include written certifications for property tax exemptions and credits, exemption from recordation tax, access to Maryland state funding programs (Local Land Trust Revolving Loan Program, Land Trust Grant Fund, Program Open Space, Rural Legacy Program, Greenspace Equity Program), joint conservation easement acquisition and monitoring, stewardship and enforcement support, co-grantee status as co-holders of Deeds of Conservation Easement with independent enforcement authority, and access to Terrafirma conservation defense insurance. Assistance is available to land trusts that have a Cooperative Agreement with MET.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local non-profit land trusts, regional and national land trusts, governmental entities, and conservation partners that co-hold conservation easements with or have a Cooperative Agreement with the Maryland Environmental Trust.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supporting easement and stewardship programs, monitoring, record keeping, capacity building, land conservation activities, conservation easement acquisition, and enforcement.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to Maryland land trusts with or seeking a Cooperative Agreement with MET. Land trusts must have a defined geographic area of operation within Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a local non-profit land trust, conservation partner, governmental entity, or regional/national land trust
Must be a charitable land trust incorporated in any state with 501(c)(3) tax-exempt status
Must be a 'qualified organization' under IRC Section 170(h)(3)
Must maintain good standing with Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation
Must have or seek a Cooperative Agreement with MET for full technical assistance benefits
New Cooperative Agreement requests require review and approval by the Land Trust Outreach Committee (LTOC) and MET's Board of Trustees
Requests for a Cooperative Agreement must be submitted at least 30 days in advance of an LTOC meeting
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Land Trust Assistance Manager at met.info@maryland.gov to discuss the status of your land trust's Cooperative Agreement with MET. New requests for a Cooperative Agreement require review and approval by the Land Trust Outreach Committee and MET's Board of Trustees, with submissions due at least 30 days before a committee meeting.

structured_extraction.program_name: PLANT Award Program (People Loving and Nurturing Trees)
structured_extraction.program_description: The PLANT Award Program (People Loving and Nurturing Trees) recognizes Maryland communities that plant, care for, and promote trees. Established in 1991 to serve as an accessible entry point for building urban and community forestry programs, it supports communities of all sizes — including schools, homeowners associations (HOAs), parks, local governments, government facilities, scout groups, and faith-based organizations — especially those that may not qualify for national recognition programs like Tree City USA. Awards are given at four levels (Bronze, Silver, Gold, Green) based on a community's level of tree-related activity over the past year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Award recognition at one of four levels (Bronze, Silver, Gold, Green) based on tree planting, stewardship, and urban forestry activities over the past year. Bronze is for single events or one-time efforts; Silver is for communities beginning to organize; Gold is for communities actively managing trees through policies, planning, or active tree management programs; Green is for established, sustained programs with ongoing effort. Communities recognized through Tree City USA or Tree Campus USA automatically qualify at the Green level. No monetary funds are provided — this is a recognition award only.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland communities of all types including schools, homeowners associations (HOAs), parks, local governments, government facilities, scout groups, and faith-based organizations that plant, care for, or promote trees.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Recognition award for tree planting, tree care, and community forestry activities. No monetary funds are provided.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland.
requirements_list: Community must have hosted a tree planting, organized tree care or organized around tree care, or taken steps to improve its local canopy within the past year
Select or apply at the award level that best matches the community's activity level over the past year
Submit application and supporting materials by email
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit your application and supporting materials by email to treemendous.dnr@maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: A special permit that allows falconers to capture passage peregrine falcons for falconry purposes. Maryland limits the total number of falcons that may be captured each season. Thirty permits are awarded through a random drawing of applications received by the deadline.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to 30 permits are awarded by random drawing. Permit allows the holder to trap one passage peregrine falcon during the designated season (September 20 – October 20, 2025). Application fee is $10 for Maryland residents and $50 for non-residents (non-refundable). Falconers who capture a bird must call in and report the take by 8 pm on the day of capture. The season closes immediately once the federally allocated number of falcons has been taken.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications must be postmarked by August 22, 2025
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland resident and non-resident falconers who hold a current general or master falconry permit
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Permits the capture of one passage peregrine falcon for use in falconry
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide – open to Maryland residents and non-residents with valid state and federal falconry permits
requirements_list: Must hold a current general or master falconry permit
Non-residents must provide a copy of their current state and federal falconry permit
Application must be postmarked by August 22, 2025
$10 fee for residents; $50 fee for non-residents (non-refundable)
Must call in and report any capture by 8 pm on the day the bird is taken
Completed application form with all sections filled out
