A lapsed hunter must have held a Maryland hunting license in the past but not purchased one for any three of the last five years
Must have a valid MD Outdoors account to enter the lottery
Must have the necessary hunting license or apprentice license to participate
Must supply own gear and firearms
Can only select one hunt day; cannot apply for both days
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Log in to your MD Outdoors account (or create one for free) and enter the pheasant hunt lottery between July 1 and October 3, 2025. Select your first, second, and third choice hunt area and one preferred day. Winners are selected by random drawing, listed on the DNR webpage by their DNRId by October 24, 2025, and notified by email by October 31, 2025 with hunt details.

structured_extraction.program_description: Sunfish and Students is an aquatic resources education program run by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources. Classroom teachers and nature/environmental education centers raise hatchery-bred Bluegill Sunfish in classroom aquariums from October through May, conducting lessons aligned with science and environmental literacy standards, then releasing the fish at an approved site. The Maryland DNR provides aquarium supplies (including a 20-gallon glass tank, filter system, air pump, test kits, water treatment chemicals), fish, food, teaching materials (teacher's manual, data sheets, lesson plans, and background information), and partial reimbursement for fish release trip costs. Starter and replacement aquarium kits (approximately $300 value per set) are provided free of charge, subject to annual budget and space limits on a first-come-first-served basis. The release event features outdoor educational activities including fishing, macroinvertebrate hunts, water quality testing, hikes, seining, SAV monitoring, kayaking/canoeing, crafts, and nature journaling.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The DNR provides free starter and replacement aquarium kits (approximately $300 value per set, subject to annual budget and space limits, first-come-first-served), including a 20-gallon glass tank, filter system, air pump, air stones, test kits, water treatment chemicals, thermometer, fish net, and batteries. Also provided: hatchery-raised Bluegill Sunfish, fish food, a teacher's manual, data sheets, lesson plans, and background information at no cost. Participants also receive reimbursement for fish release trip costs: 50% of total bus costs (up to 3 buses) and 100% of substitute teacher costs (up to 3 substitutes). Reimbursement requires itemized invoices with receipts, school principal certification, and submission to the ARE Program at Maryland DNR. DNR staff support is also available for release events if requested at least 2 weeks in advance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Classroom teachers, non-formal educators, Environmental Education Centers, and Nature Centers in Maryland; students participate in hands-on aquatic education activities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Aquarium supplies and equipment (20-gallon tank, filter, air pump, test kits, chemicals), live bluegill fish and fish food, educational materials (teacher's manual, data sheets, lesson plans), and reimbursement for transportation (bus costs) and substitute teacher costs related to the fish release field trip.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to eligible classroom teachers, non-formal educators, and nature/environmental education centers. Equipment returned to Maryland DNR in Annapolis if discontinuing program.
requirements_list: Must be a classroom teacher, non-formal educator, Environmental Education Center, or Nature Center
Must register every year by May 15th (both new and returning participants)
New participants and returning participants every 3 years must attend the mandatory Teacher Training Workshop in September (e.g., September 12, 2026)
Must pick up fish on one of the designated Thursday pickup dates in October (or an approved alternate option); no fish available after October 31st
Must release fish at an approved location no later than June 30th
Must submit reimbursement package (itemized invoice with receipts, school principal certification, W-9 if new vendor) by June 30th
Must complete the ARE (Aquatic Resources Education) online reporting form (demographic/Google form) by July 31st — failure to report results in unenrollment from the program
Must inventory materials upon receipt and report missing/broken items immediately
Must return all equipment to Maryland DNR in Annapolis if discontinuing the program
Daily monitoring of water quality and fish activity required; weekly fish measurements; biweekly to monthly equipment maintenance
Water quality parameters to maintain: Total Ammonia <2.5 ppm (optimum 0), Unionized Ammonia <0.12 ppm (optimum 0), Nitrite optimum 0, Nitrate optimum <40 ppm, pH 6.5–8.5, Temperature 65–80°F
Program is supported by a Federal grant requiring statistical reporting; certification that expenditures align with Federal award terms required for reimbursement
May require user agreement form, reservation fees, or entry fees for fish release event location
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the online registration form (available from January 1st each year) by May 15th. Attend the mandatory Teacher Training Workshop in September. Pick up fish and aquarium supplies at a designated location on one of the scheduled October pickup dates. Raise fish and conduct lessons October through May, maintaining daily water quality monitoring and weekly fish measurements. Release fish by June 30th at an approved site (contact DNR staff at least 2 weeks in advance if requesting staff support for the release event). Submit reimbursement package (itemized invoice on organization letterhead with receipts and school principal certification) by June 30th and complete the online ARE reporting form by July 31st. Return all equipment to Maryland DNR in Annapolis if discontinuing the program.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Natural Resources offers free fishing gear for loan at various locations throughout the state, including state parks, public libraries, and nature centers. The program helps new anglers and their families try recreational fishing by providing rods, reels, and basic tackle at no cost.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free loan of fishing gear (spincast rod and reel setup with bobber, split shot sinker, swivel, and hook) at participating sites. Loans may be on-site only or off-site depending on location. Some sites allow multi-day loans. Group programs are available at select sites by reservation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals, families, and groups interested in recreational fishing, especially new anglers and those spending time in Maryland parks.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Borrowing fishing equipment for recreational fishing at or near participating loaner sites.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide at participating locations including state parks, public libraries, and nature centers across multiple Maryland counties.
requirements_list: Borrower must complete a borrower registration form
Anglers age 16 and older must have a valid Maryland fishing license
Gear must be returned to the site on the agreed return date
Group programs require reservations
Policies may vary by site — contact the site directly to confirm procedures
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Find a nearby loaner site (state parks, libraries, nature centers). 2. Fill out the online borrower form at the DNR website. 3. Visit the chosen site to pick up gear. 4. Go fishing. 5. Return gear on the agreed return date.

structured_extraction.program_description: Tree-Mendous Maryland is a Maryland Forest Service program that helps local governments, community groups, schools, scout troops, volunteers, and other organizations plant native trees on public lands and community open spaces across Maryland. The program provides quality native trees at reduced cost through a wholesale nursery agreement, with free delivery to three statewide distribution locations each spring and fall season. Direct-to-site delivery is also available for an additional fee. A Gift of Trees program is available at $40 per tree ($400 for a grove of ten), with trees planted on public land in the recipient's county.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides native trees at reduced cost through a wholesale nursery agreement (Clear Ridge Nursery). Includes free delivery to three statewide distribution points each spring and fall. Direct-to-site delivery is available for an additional fee. Also offers a Gift of Trees program at $40 per tree ($400 for a grove of ten) where trees are planted on public land in the recipient's county. A password-protected order form is used; applicants must contact the program to verify eligibility and receive access.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, community groups, schools, scout troops, parks, volunteers, and other organizations seeking to plant trees on public land or community open spaces in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planting native trees and shrubs on public lands and community open spaces such as schools, parks, street tree locations, along creeks and streams, and other community open spaces.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland for planting on public lands and community open spaces.
requirements_list: Trees must be planted on public land or community open space
Applicants must obtain permission from land owners
Applicants must contact the program to receive the password-protected order form
Organization information and location must be submitted to determine eligibility
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations that believe they qualify should send their organization's information and location to ryan.mayenschein@maryland.gov to determine eligibility and receive access to the password-protected order form on the nursery website (Clear Ridge Nursery). Orders are then placed directly through the nursery partner.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides free technical assistance from Maryland Department of Natural Resources (DNR) Forest Service foresters to landowners interested in managing their forest lands to improve watershed health and water quality.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Foresters are available throughout Maryland to provide technical assistance to landowners interested in managing their forest lands to improve water quality in their watershed.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners interested in managing forest lands to improve watershed health and water quality
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Forest management and technical guidance to improve water quality and reduce erosion in Maryland's watersheds
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide throughout Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a landowner interested in managing forest lands
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Maryland DNR Forest Service for technical assistance. A link to the DNR mailroom is provided on the page for comments and inquiries.

structured_extraction.program_description: An environmental education program where classroom teachers, environmental education centers, and nature centers raise rainbow trout from eggs and conduct aquatic science lessons with students in grades 3-12. The Maryland Department of Natural Resources, in partnership with Trout Unlimited, provides financial aid for equipment (starter kits, chillers, replacement kits), hatchery-raised rainbow trout eggs, fish food, lesson plans and background materials, and reimbursement for fish release field trip costs. The program introduces youth to cold water conservation as a first step in becoming future protectors of and advocates for clean and healthy streams, lakes, and rivers. It is available statewide in Maryland and runs annually from October through May.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial aid is provided to participating schools as budget allows. New schools receive one starter kit (approximately $700, not including a chiller) and one chiller. Returning schools receive one replacement kit (approximately $220). The program also provides hatchery-raised rainbow trout eggs and fish food, lesson plans and background materials, and reimbursement for fish release field trip costs — covering 50% of bus costs (up to 3 buses) and 100% of substitute teacher costs (up to 3 substitutes). DNR also provides technical, training, and advisory support, including a free one-day orientation and training seminar for new teachers, and priority technical support and emergency equipment access for the first two years of participation.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Registration opens January 1st; deadline March 15th. Invoice/reimbursement packages due June 30th. Reporting form due July 31st.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Classroom teachers (grades 3-12), environmental education centers, nature centers, and learning organizations in Maryland. Program serves students in grades 3-12.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of starter kits, chillers, and replacement equipment for raising trout in the classroom; fish food; obtaining hatchery-raised trout eggs; reimbursement for transportation and substitute teacher costs for fish release field trips. Schools are expected to purchase items such as insulation board, surge power strip, bucket, measuring tools, safety glasses, and annual replacement supplies including filter media, test kits, and batteries.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a classroom teacher, environmental education center, nature center, or learning organization serving grades 3-12
Must register annually starting January 1st (deadline March 15th)
Must submit a signed Memorandum of Intent (MOI) with registration by March 15
Must obtain an Aquatic Studies Permit issued by DNR
Must attend Teacher Training Workshop in fall (hosted by Trout Unlimited); mandatory new teacher seminar on or around October 24
Must raise fish and conduct lessons from October through May
Must release fish at an approved release site in April or May

Invoice packages for reimbursement must be submitted by June 30 with invoice on organization letterhead, itemized list of approved expenses with receipts, Federal EIN number, School Principal certification and signature, and updated W-9
Certification that payment has not been previously received and that submission complies with federal award terms and conditions
Reporting form must be completed online by July 31; failure to report results in removal from the program
Minimum 2 weeks advance notice required if requesting DNR staff assistance for release event
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Complete the registration form starting January 1st (deadline March 15th) and submit a signed Memorandum of Intent (MOI). 2. Attend the mandatory fall Teacher Training Workshop/new teacher orientation seminar (late October or early November) hosted by Trout Unlimited. 3. Receive fish eggs in early December from the Albert Powell Fish Hatchery. 4. Raise fish and conduct student lessons from October through May. 5. Release fish at an approved site in April or May (contact DNR at least 2 weeks in advance if staff assistance is needed). 6. Submit reimbursement package on organization letterhead (invoice, itemized expenses with receipts, Federal EIN, School Principal signature, updated W-9) by June 30. 7. Complete the online reporting form by July 31.

structured_extraction.program_name: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Environmental Education Grants Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Grants that support projects promoting environmental awareness and stewardship, available to a wide range of organizations nationwide including those in Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants to fund projects that promote environmental awareness and stewardship.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations and educators running projects that promote environmental awareness and stewardship
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects promoting environmental awareness and stewardship
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Nationwide, including Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the EPA Environmental Education Grants program page at the EPA website.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides money to marinas and local governments. They can use the funds to build temporary boat slips for recreational boats that are longer than 26 feet.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers project grants.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Marinas and local or state government bodies.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support the construction of boat slips for temporary use by recreational boats over 26 feet long.
requirements_list: Projects must be for recreational vessels over 26 feet in length.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Universal Disability Pass (UDP) is a free lifetime pass for Maryland residents with qualifying disabilities that provides free entrance to Maryland State Parks, Forests, and other public lands managed by the Department of Natural Resources, including wildlife management areas. The pass grants the holder and one accompanying person free entrance to day-use facilities where entrance fees apply. The pass does not cover automated gate systems, camping fees, boat launches and rentals, bus parking, concessions, or other special charges. Eligibility can be documented via a Veterans Affairs disability determination (including Disabled American Veterans and Prisoners of War), an MVA Disability Parking Certification, or certification by a licensed health care professional (physician, chiropractor, optometrist, podiatrist, or nurse practitioner), and covers any physical or mental impairment that substantially limits one or more major life activities as defined under the ADA or §504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973. The pass also includes a Hunt From a Vehicle provision, which allows eligible holders with a valid Maryland hunting license and a mobility impairment (certified by a physician) to hunt from a stationary vehicle in designated accessible areas on state parks, state forests, and Wildlife Management Areas, subject to specific regulations. One non-hunting companion may accompany the permit holder inside the vehicle in posted areas. All weapons must be unloaded while the vehicle is in motion. A non-profit group version of the pass is also available for qualifying organizations serving people with disabilities. No renewal is required.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free lifetime pass (no renewal required) that grants the pass holder and one accompanying person free entrance to day-use facilities at Maryland State Parks, Forests, and public lands managed by the Department of Natural Resources where entrance fees apply. The pass does not cover automated gate systems, camping fees, boat launches and rentals, bus parking, concessions, or other special charges. The pass also includes a Hunt From a Vehicle permit for holders with mobility impairments, allowing them to hunt from a stationary vehicle in designated accessible areas on public lands including Wildlife Management Areas, State Parks, and State Forests; one non-hunting companion may be inside the vehicle beyond the entrance to posted areas. The vehicle must be at a complete stop with motor off while shooting, aiming, or firing, and all weapons must be unloaded (including no ammunition in magazine) while the vehicle is in motion. No loaded weapons are permitted on public roadways or shoulders. Non-profit groups may apply using a separate application.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents with qualifying disabilities, including Disabled American Veterans (DAV), Prisoners of War (POW), veterans with a 100% permanent and total VA service-connected disability rating, those with a Veterans Affairs disability determination, an MVA Disability Parking Certification, or certification by a licensed health care professional; hunters with mobility impairments who wish to hunt from a vehicle on Maryland public lands including State Parks, State Forests, and Wildlife Management Areas; and qualifying non-profit organizations serving people with disabilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free lifetime entrance to Maryland state parks, forests, and public lands managed by the Department of Natural Resources. Eligible holders with a mobility impairment and a valid Maryland hunting license may also hunt from a stationary vehicle in designated accessible areas on public hunting lands across Maryland.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide at all Maryland public lands managed by the Department of Natural Resources, including state parks, state forests, and Wildlife Management Areas. Passes can be obtained from any Maryland DNR Regional Service Center (locations in Annapolis, Solomons, Bel Air, Salisbury, Centreville, and Frederick) by mail, email, or in-person appointment. Applications are also available from Wildlife and Heritage Service regional offices or online. Maryland residents only.
requirements_list: Applicant must have a disability as defined by the ADA or §504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 (a physical or mental impairment that substantially limits one or more major life activities, a record of such impairment, or being regarded as having such an impairment)

Must provide one of: copy of VA disability determination letter (including DAV/POW documentation), copy of MVA Disability Parking Certification, or certification by a licensed health care professional
Licensed health care professional must be a physician, chiropractor, optometrist, podiatrist, or nurse practitioner
Licensed health care provider must include their medical license number and issuing state on the certification
Certification must identify the condition(s) and specify whether the disability is permanent or temporary (with anticipated end date if temporary)
For veterans, must have a 100% permanent and total VA service-connected disability rating to qualify under veteran eligibility
Must have a DNRid account (register at mdoutdoors.maryland.gov)
Must complete the Application for Universal Disability Pass with name, DNRid#, phone number, signature, and date
Identification may be requested when the pass is presented
Valid hunting license required to use the vehicle hunting provision
Must have a mobility impairment to use the Hunt From a Vehicle permit
Physician must certify the Hunt From a Vehicle permit application
Must have UDP in possession while hunting
Vehicle must be at a complete stop with motor off while shooting, aiming, or firing
All weapons must be unloaded (including no ammunition in magazine) while vehicle is in motion
Must not shoot or have a loaded weapon in the vehicle while on a public roadway or shoulder
Companion in vehicle may not hunt from the vehicle if they are a licensed hunter

For non-profit group pass: must provide evidence of current non-profit status and certification from a licensed health care provider documenting clients' disabilities that substantially limit major life activities
Must apply through a Maryland Service Center
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Register at mdoutdoors.maryland.gov to obtain a DNRid number. Step 2: Complete the Application for Universal Disability Pass (PDF) including name, DNRid#, phone number, signature, date, and supporting documentation (VA disability determination letter, MVA Disability Parking Certification, or licensed health care professional certification — physician, chiropractor, optometrist, podiatrist, or nurse practitioner must provide their license number and issuing state, and specify whether the condition is permanent or temporary). Step 3: Submit application and documentation to any DNR service center (Annapolis, Solomons, Bel Air, Salisbury, Centreville, or Frederick) by mail, email, or in-person appointment. Non-profit groups use a separate Non-Profit Group UDP Application form and must submit by appointment to one of six regional service centers, including evidence of non-profit status and medical certification. For the Hunt From a Vehicle permit, applications are available from Wildlife & Heritage Service regional offices or online, and a physician must certify the application before submission. Visit the Maryland DNR Universal Disability Pass FAQ page at https://dnr.maryland.gov/publiclands/Pages/udpfaq.aspx for full details.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Volunteer Fire Assistance (VFA) Grant Program provides financial, technical, and related assistance to rural volunteer fire departments and their communities in Maryland. The program enhances wildland fire suppression capabilities, improves firefighter safety, promotes the use of wildland personal protective equipment, and supports basic wildland fire training. Grants are competitive, scored using a points system, and awarded on a 50/50 cost-share basis with federal funds reimbursing up to 50% of eligible costs (maximum $3,500 per department).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Sub-grants of up to $3,500 per department awarded on a 50/50 cost-share basis. Federal funds reimburse up to 50% of eligible costs after the department has purchased and paid for approved items. In 2025, grants totaled $167,314 to 55 fire departments for $370,376 in total project costs. Grants can be used for wildland firefighting personal protective equipment (PPE), wildland power tools (chainsaws, leaf blowers), fire hose less than 2.5 inches in diameter, nozzles and fittings, bladder bags, wildland gear, chainsaw supplies, fire engine and UTV pumping units, rehabilitation of equipment from federal excess programs, fire communications equipment (pagers, radios), ATVs/UTVs and related wildland firefighting attachments, and wildland firefighting training tuition. Grants are competitive and scored using a points system. Also provides technical and related assistance to rural volunteer fire departments and their communities. Grants cannot be used for capital improvements, vehicle purchases, structural firefighting equipment, HAZMAT, rescue, EMS equipment, or fire hose larger than 2.5 inches in diameter.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Rural volunteer fire departments serving communities with a population of 10,000 or less (based on the latest Census), or area fire departments whose service area includes a rural area or rural community with a population of 10,000 or less.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Wildland firefighting personal protective equipment (PPE), wildland power tools (chainsaws, leaf blowers), fire hose less than 2.5 inches in diameter, nozzles and fittings, bladder bags, wildland gear, chainsaw supplies, wildland fire engine and UTV pumping units, rehabilitation of equipment from federal excess programs, fire communications equipment (pagers, radios), ATVs/UTVs and related wildland firefighting attachments, and wildland firefighting training tuition. Also covers fire department operations, financial needs, technical needs, and community fire protection. Cannot be used for capital improvements, vehicle purchases, structural firefighting equipment, HAZMAT, rescue, or EMS equipment, or fire hose larger than 2.5 inches in diameter.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to rural volunteer fire departments in Maryland serving communities with a population of 10,000 or less (based on the latest Census), or area fire departments whose service area includes a rural area or community of 10,000 or less. Program has served departments across approximately 18 Maryland counties.
requirements_list: Must be a rural volunteer fire department serving a rural area or rural community with a population of 10,000 or less (latest Census).
Area fire departments may serve an aggregate population greater than 10,000 if the service area includes a rural area or community of 10,000 or less.
50/50 cost-share match required; federal funds reimburse up to 50% of eligible costs (maximum $3,500 payment).
Department must pay for items first; federal funds reimburse up to 50% (maximum $3,500).
Purchases must occur between January 1, 2025 and December 31, 2025 for approved 2025 grants.
Equipment must have application to wildland firefighting; equipment solely for structural firefighting, HAZMAT, rescue, or EMS is disqualified.
Grants will not cover capital improvements, vehicle purchases, or fire hose larger than 2.5 inches in diameter.
Prior grant recipients receive a standard points deduction for each of the three years prior to the application year.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a web-based application through the online Application Form Portal before 4:00 p.m. on September 15, 2025. After submission, you will receive a confirmation email with a copy of your responses. Applicants will be notified by October 15, 2025 whether the application was approved or denied. If awarded, you will receive supporting documentation including a Memorandum of Understanding. Purchases must be completed by December 31, 2025, and supporting documentation (proof of purchase and payment) must be submitted by January 15, 2026. After documentation is received, the Maryland Forest Service will reimburse the volunteer fire department within 45 days based on the 50/50 cost-share agreement, up to the $3,500 maximum.

structured_extraction.program_name: Warrior Hike 'Walk Off The War' Program
structured_extraction.program_description: An outdoor therapy program that supports combat veterans transitioning from military service by thru-hiking America's three national scenic trails (Appalachian Trail, Pacific Crest Trail, and Continental Divide Trail). The program provides equipment and supplies needed to complete a thru-hike, coordinates trail town support (food, transportation, and lodging) with veteran and hiking organizations along the trail, and helps veterans find future employment through program partners.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides combat veterans with equipment and supplies needed to complete a thru-hike of one of America's three national scenic trails. Also coordinates trail town support (food, transportation, and lodging) with veteran and hiking organizations along the trails, and assists with employment opportunities and job placement services after completing the hike.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Combat veterans who are honorably discharged and desire to thru-hike one of America's three national scenic trails
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Equipment and supplies for thru-hiking national scenic trails; food, transportation, and lodging trail town support; employment placement services
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Three national scenic trails across the United States: Appalachian Trail (Georgia to Maine, including through Maryland), Pacific Crest Trail (California to Washington), and Continental Divide Trail (New Mexico to Montana)
requirements_list: Must have served in a combat zone
Must be honorably discharged
Must desire to thru-hike one of America's three national scenic trails
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Warrior Expeditions website at warriorexpeditions.org/apply/

structured_extraction.program_description: Free water safety education program for youngsters and adults in Maryland. Taught by the Maryland Natural Resources Police, the program covers basic water and boating safety concepts to help prevent drowning and water-related accidents. Sessions are fun, customizable, and last 15 minutes to an hour, and can be tailored for different age groups from pre-kindergarten through adult. Programs are delivered in-person to schools, community groups, and organizations statewide.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free in-person water safety education sessions lasting 15 minutes to one hour. Sessions cover basic boating and water safety concepts and are customizable by age group. Hosts need only provide a room full of interested students and possibly a TV and VCR depending on the program selected.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Schools, youth groups, community groups, and other organizations seeking water safety education for children and adults of all ages, from pre-kindergarten through adults.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Water and boating safety education — not a financial assistance program. Sessions cover basic water safety and boating safety concepts delivered to participants.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Host must provide a room full of interested students
Host may need to provide a VCR and TV depending on the program chosen
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 410-643-8502 or email Donna Seymour at donna.seymour@maryland.gov to schedule a session with the Safety Education Section of the Maryland Natural Resources Police.

structured_extraction.program_description: A license required for anyone who wants to operate a waterfowl processing business in Maryland. The license is issued by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources (DNR) Wildlife and Heritage Service at no cost. Licensees must keep detailed records of all wild waterfowl received and processed, allow inspections by law enforcement, and submit annual reports to the Department.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A free license (no fee charged) that legally permits the holder to operate a waterfowl processing operation in Maryland. The license expires on June 30 following the date of issuance and can be renewed by submitting a completed renewal application. Licensees must maintain detailed processing logs and submit annual records to the Department prior to March 1st.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annual records/log books must be returned prior to March 1st
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals or businesses seeking to operate a waterfowl processing operation in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Authorization to legally receive, process, and dispose of wild waterfowl in Maryland; tracking and documentation of processed waterfowl by species, date, location of harvest, and customer information
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — available to anyone operating a waterfowl processing operation in Maryland; operation location must be specified in Maryland
requirements_list: Must apply using the Department-provided form
Must not receive or hold wild waterfowl that is not properly tagged per state and federal law
Must keep records of species, quantity, origin location, dates received and disposed, and names/addresses of persons from whom waterfowl was received and delivered
Must submit a copy of records to the Department annually before March 1st of the permit year
Must allow Natural Resources Police or other law enforcement officers to inspect premises and records at any reasonable hour

Must maintain workers' compensation insurance or qualify for exemption (comply with Maryland Workmen's Compensation Act by providing certificate of insurance, insurance binder, or self-employment documentation)
Must complete all application pages and provide current information and identification
Must certify information under penalty of perjury
Must keep a copy of completed reports for own records
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Waterfowl Processing Operation Permit Application form (available on the DNR website). Submit by email to wildlifepermits.dnr@maryland.gov, by phone at 410-260-8538 or 410-260-8540, or by mail to Wildlife Permit Coordinator, MD DNR Wildlife and Heritage Service, 580 Taylor Ave., E-1, Annapolis MD 21401. In-person appointments are available by scheduling via email or phone. Annual processing log books must be completed and returned to the Permits Coordinator prior to March 1st; additional log books can be requested by calling 410-260-8538.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program helps local communities with watershed restoration projects. It connects them with services, technical help, and other resources to improve water quality in Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides grants for planning and designing water quality improvement projects. It also offers technical assistance, project management, help with financing strategies, and training for local governments and organizations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, non-profits, universities, and community groups in Maryland that want to work on watershed protection and restoration projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Assistance can be used for design, watershed planning, and program development. The program also provides technical help with project management, financing strategies, and stakeholder outreach.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be in the Maryland portion of the Chesapeake Bay watershed, the Youghiogheny watershed, or the Maryland Coastal Bays.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To get help, communities fill out a Request for Resources & Services Form. A separate Request for Proposals is available for the grant program.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides technical planning and design assistance for projects that protect and restore water quality in the Maryland portion of the Chesapeake Bay watershed and the Maryland Coastal Bays. Planning projects can include watershed characterization, surveys, assessments, action plans, or financing plans. Design requests are accepted for the full range of non-point source best management practices (practices that reduce pollution from diffuse sources like runoff). Design assistance is also available for non-point source best management practices.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Technical planning and design assistance grants for water quality protection and restoration projects in the Chesapeake Bay watershed and Maryland Coastal Bays. Assistance covers watershed planning projects and design of non-point source best management practices. Specific grant amounts and terms are available on the Chesapeake Bay Trust website.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments and non-profit organizations working on water quality protection and restoration in the Maryland portion of the Chesapeake Bay watershed and Maryland Coastal Bays, seeking technical assistance for watershed planning and design projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Watershed characterization, surveys, assessments, action plans, financing plans, and design of non-point source best management practices.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland portion of the Chesapeake Bay watershed and the Maryland Coastal Bays.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local government or non-profit organization
Project must be associated with protection or restoration programs that lead to improved water quality in the Maryland portion of the Chesapeake Bay watershed or Maryland Coastal Bays

structured_extraction.program_name: Watershed Assistance – Two-Year Milestone Support Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This grant program supports design assistance, watershed planning, and programmatic development for protection and restoration projects that lead to improved water quality in the Maryland portion of the Chesapeake Bay watershed, the Maryland portion of the Youghiogheny watershed, and the Maryland Coastal Bays.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants support design assistance, watershed planning, and programmatic development associated with protection and restoration projects that improve water quality in Maryland watersheds.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local jurisdictions and communities seeking to implement non-point source restoration and protection efforts in Maryland watersheds.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Design assistance, watershed planning, and programmatic development for water quality protection and restoration projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland portion of the Chesapeake Bay watershed, Maryland portion of the Youghiogheny watershed, and the Maryland Coastal Bays.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download the Request for Proposals and submit a request. Communities can also fill out the Request for Resources & Services Form or contact Carrie Decker for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A five-year pilot grant program that provides financial and technical support to project sponsors managing specific Maryland watersheds. The program takes a collaborative, science-based approach to accelerate restoration of the Chesapeake Bay and Atlantic Coastal Bays watersheds. It funds pollution reduction, habitat creation, aquatic resource improvements, equitable public access, carbon sequestration, public health enhancements, climate resilience, and outreach to overburdened and underserved communities across five selected watersheds. Agricultural support is also available through the MD Agricultural Cost Share Program and MD Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Implementation and Operating Grants provide up to 50% of project implementation costs (up to $2 million per watershed per year for FY2026, with $20,000 included for operational expenses). Water Quality Monitoring Grants total $1.25 million ($250,000 per watershed). Agricultural support is also available through the MD Agricultural Cost Share Program and MD Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation. The program requires a 1:1 match — the project sponsor must provide 50% outside funding toward implementation costs (cash match preferred; in-kind contributions also eligible). Outside funds cannot come from any of the six Whole Watershed Fund sources, and must be spent after July 1, 2025. Funds are distributed to the project sponsor on a quarterly reimbursement basis. Sub-awards to partner entities are allowed. The program also provides coordinated state permitting support and technical assistance. In FY26, total allocation was $11,248,876 (state funds) plus $11,007,788 (leveraged funds) for a total investment of $22,256,644 across 37 projects in 5 watersheds.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: The next RFP will be released by October 1, 2029; the original RFP deadline was December 3, 2024.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Municipal, county, and regional agencies; nonprofit organizations; faith-based groups; homeowners associations; soil and water conservation districts; and other organizations acting as a project sponsor for a Maryland watershed restoration project.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Watershed restoration and conservation actions including pollution reduction, habitat creation, stormwater management, stream restoration, shoreline stabilization, living shorelines, wetland restoration, riparian buffers, aquatic resource improvements, wildlife habitat improvements, community outreach, public health enhancements, and water quality monitoring within selected Maryland watersheds. Also supports conservation overlay zone development, trail and bridge design for equitable public access, and watershed planning.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland; projects must be located within an eligible 8-digit Maryland watershed. Five watersheds were selected for the first five-year pilot period (Antietam Creek, Baltimore Harbor, Upper Choptank River, Newport Bay, and Severn River). At least one watershed must adjoin a neighboring state. The next RFP cycle opens October 1, 2029.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a municipal, county, or regional agency; nonprofit organization; faith-based group; homeowners association; soil/water conservation district; or similar organization.
A single project sponsor must be identified to administer the project and is accountable for funds, partner coordination, and reporting.
The project must be located in a Maryland 8-digit watershed.
The project must be endorsed by each county and municipal corporation in which it will occur.

Project sponsor must provide 50% of project implementation costs from outside funding not associated with the six Whole Watershed Fund sources (cash match preferred; in-kind contributions also eligible).
Outside matching funds must be spent after July 1, 2025.
Project sponsor must hold at least 4 community meetings per year that include local government representation.
Project sponsor must provide opportunity for public comment on preliminary designs of each major or large-scale action.

Proposal must demonstrate plans for at least five co-benefits such as wildlife habitat, aquatic resource restoration, carbon sequestration, climate resilience, local employment, public health, and recreational access.

Selected watersheds must collectively meet these designations: one urban, one suburban, two agricultural, one with an adjoining state, and two with opportunities to engage overburdened or underserved communities.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: A Request for Proposals (RFP) is issued by the State Management Team every five years. Applicants submit a proposal through an online application form (with an upload option for additional detail) describing watershed restoration plans, partnership structure, budget, and match funding. The State Management Team evaluates proposals based on water quality improvement potential, cost-effectiveness, environmental justice, innovation, local land use support, and multi-benefit criteria. The SMT may approve up to five projects, with awardees selected by March 1 of the year following the RFP. After selection, the SMT works with each project sponsor to develop an Implementation and Financing Plan. Funds are distributed via quarterly reimbursement requests.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland requires anyone who performs wildlife damage control work to obtain a Wildlife Damage Control Permit. The state offers three permit types — Commercial, Assistant, and Public Agency — for operators conducting damage control work for others, and a free Landowner Permit for property owners doing work on their own land. Permit holders may perform wildlife damage control services, including bat exclusion work, and can be listed publicly for wildlife damage control calls. Renewals are annual and require submission of annual reports by December 31.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program issues permits (Commercial, Assistant, and Public Agency types) that authorize holders to legally conduct wildlife damage control work in Maryland. Applicants must pass an open-book online exam with an 80% passing score (retakes allowed after 45 days, up to three times per year). The exam consists of 70 questions and requires a minimum score of 56/70. Permit fees: Commercial $50, Assistant $25, Public Agency waived. Renewal is annual and requires submission of annual reports by December 31. If authorized for bat work, permit holders must also submit annual bat colony exclusion reports. A free Landowner Permit is available through USDA Wildlife Services for landowners controlling wildlife damage on their own property. Permit holders may optionally be listed on the DNR website for public wildlife damage control calls.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling; renewals sent 2 months before renewal date; annual reports due December 31
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals, businesses, and public agencies conducting wildlife damage control work in Maryland, as well as landowners seeking to control wildlife damage on their own property
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Authorization to conduct wildlife damage control activities, including bat exclusion work, in Maryland
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland

Submit annual reports with renewal or by December 31st.

structured_extraction.program_description: Free, hands-on educational lending kit program for Maryland educators that brings wildlife topics into the classroom. Each trunk contains an educator guide with lesson plans and K-12 activities, plus physical items like animal furs, skulls, track molds, books, DVDs, and prepped activity supplies. Trunks are available on topics including white-tailed deer, black bear, furbearers, wild turkey, bats, aquatic invasive species, and early childhood wildlife education. Educators may borrow trunks free of charge for 1–2 week periods from nine pickup locations across Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free loan of wildlife education trunks for 1–2 week periods depending on availability. Educators pick up and return trunks at designated locations across Maryland at no cost. Multiple trunk types are available at nine locations statewide: Annapolis, Abingdon, Flintstone, Clear Springs, Oakland, Gaithersburg, Princess Anne, La Plata, and Baltimore City. Trunks contain curriculum guides, lesson plans, hands-on materials (animal furs, skulls, track molds, jawbone specimens), books, DVDs, and activity supplies covering topics such as white-tailed deer, black bear, furbearers, wild turkey, bats, and aquatic invasive species. Curriculum materials are aligned with Maryland Environmental Literacy standards and include activities for grades PK-12 organized by grade level bands (K-4, 5-8, and 9-12). Activity types include games, crafts, simulations, tracking identification, skull examination, and population dynamics modeling.
structured_extraction.program_audience: K-12 educators and students in Maryland, including early childhood (PK) through grade 12; wildlife educators, hunters, and wildlife management professionals
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Classroom wildlife education activities and lessons for students in grades PK-12, covering Maryland wildlife topics including white-tailed deer, black bears, furbearers (beaver, bobcat, coyote, fisher, gray fox, long-tailed weasel, American mink, muskrat, nutria, Virginia opossum, Northern raccoon, red fox, river otter, Eastern striped skunk), wild turkey, bats, and aquatic invasive species; also covers wildlife management, conservation history, animal tracking and identification, skull examination, predator-prey relationships, and population dynamics
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland through nine pickup locations: Annapolis, Abingdon, Flintstone, Clear Springs, Oakland, Gaithersburg, Princess Anne, La Plata, and Baltimore City

For Project WILD workshop information, visit http://dnr.maryland.gov/wildlife/Pages/Education/ProjectWILD.aspx.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state permit required for anyone in Maryland who wants to care for and rehabilitate orphaned, sick, or injured wildlife with the goal of releasing them back to the wild. The permit is issued by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources and renewed every two years. The program includes apprentice and master rehabilitator classifications.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A two-year Wildlife Rehabilitator Permit/License authorizing the holder to possess and care for specified species and numbers of wildlife. The permit designates which species and how many animals may be held at one time. Continuing education credits are required to maintain the permit. Permit holders may also be listed in DNR referral network for public inquiries.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and organizations engaged in wildlife rehabilitation in Maryland, including apprentice and master-level rehabilitators.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Care, treatment, and rehabilitation of orphaned, sick, or injured wildlife until they can be safely released back to the wild.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_name: Woodland Incentive Program (WIP) / Environmental Quality Incentives Program (EQIP)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Woodland Incentive Program (WIP) provides cost-sharing assistance to private, non-industrial forest landowners in Maryland for tree planting, site preparation, and timber stand improvement practices. Landowners complete approved practices, pay for them, and then receive reimbursement for up to 65% of their costs, not to exceed $5,000 per calendar year or $15,000 per consecutive 3-year period. Approximately $100,000 is distributed annually to 75-100 landowners for management practices on 1,500-2,000 acres. The Environmental Quality Incentives Program (EQIP) is a federal program that provides farmers and private forest landowners with financial, technical, and educational assistance to address natural resource and environmental problems on their land. Participants must develop and implement an approved conservation plan. EQIP offers cost-share payments typically covering 50% to 75% of the total cost of recommended structural, vegetative, and management conservation practices, with payments generally limited to $10,000 per person per year and $50,000 total over a 5 to 10 year contract life. Limited resource producers and beginning farmers and ranchers may qualify for up to 90% cost-share. Both programs require a forest stewardship or management plan and are administered in coordination with the Maryland Department of Natural Resources Forest Service.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The WIP reimburses up to 65% of eligible practice costs (or flat rate allowance, whichever is lesser) for private, non-industrial forest landowners after they complete and pay for approved practices, not to exceed $5,000 per calendar year or $15,000 per consecutive 3-year period. Approximately $100,000 is distributed annually to 75-100 landowners for management practices on 1,500-2,000 acres. Eligible WIP practices include thinning, pruning, prescribed burning, crop tree release, site preparation for reforestation, herbicide treatments, planting seedlings, and Forest Stewardship Plan preparation. Under the broader EQIP framework, cost-share payments typically cover 50% to 75% of the total cost of recommended conservation and forestry practices (structural and vegetative), with limited resource producers and beginning farmers and ranchers eligible for cost-shares up to 90%. EQIP payments are generally limited to $10,000 per person per year and $50,000 total over the 5 to 10 year contract life. EQIP funding must be allocated before any work begins. Incentive payments are also available for land management practices such as nutrient management, manure management, integrated pest management, irrigation water management, wildlife habitat enhancement, and forestry management practices. Both programs also provide technical assistance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private, non-industrial woodland owners in Maryland owning at least 5 but no more than 1,000 contiguous acres of forestland with potential for harvest of forest products, as well as farmers and agricultural producers in geographic priority areas with natural resource or environmental problems on their land, including individuals, LLCs, trusts, and other entities engaged in livestock, agricultural production, or forestry management seeking to improve their land through recommended conservation practices. Note: Corporations manufacturing forest products or providing utility services are NOT eligible for WIP.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tree planting, site preparation, and timber stand improvement practices including thinning, pruning, prescribed burning, crop tree release, reforestation of open land (abandoned farm fields) and cutover woodlands, herbicide treatments, seedling planting, and Forest Stewardship Plan preparation. Also covers structural and vegetative practices such as grassed waterways and manure management facilities, as well as nutrient management, integrated pest management, irrigation water management, wildlife habitat enhancement, and other forest improvement and conservation practices as recommended in a forest stewardship or conservation management plan. Assistance is for forest improvement and growth of harvestable forest products on a long-term basis.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to eligible private, non-industrial forest landowners owning 5 to 1,000 contiguous acres capable of producing 20 cubic feet of wood per acre per year, and on eligible agricultural and private non-industrial forestland. All Maryland counties are served through four regional offices (Western, Eastern, Central, and Southern). EQIP targets geographic priority areas (GPAs) designated nationally and by each state. Eligibility depends on property size and fund availability.

DNR Forester review and sign-off required before application submission
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For WIP: Complete the fillable PDF application form with all relevant fields populated. Obtain a Licensed Forester-approved plan. Obtain landowner signature (electronic or physical). DNR Forester reviews and signs off. Submit to DNR Headquarters via email with Regional Forester copied. Application is assigned a number and entered into the system; a confirmation letter is sent to the landowner. Department notifies approval/disapproval within 30 days. Upon approval, complete the practices and pay for goods and/or services. Submit copies of invoices, receipts, and checks to the local forester for processing after the forester inspects and approves the work. A reimbursement check is then issued for up to 65% of costs (not to exceed $5,000/year or $15,000 per 3-year period). For EQIP: Contact your local USDA Service Center in your county, the Farm Service Agency Maryland State Office, or the Maryland DNR Forest Service for guidance. Local work groups convened by conservation districts help identify eligible practices. Apply through the USDA NRCS. Funding must be allocated prior to beginning any work.

structured_extraction.program_name: Wounded Warrior and Veteran Outreach Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A Maryland Park Service program that connects wounded warriors, veterans, and their families with recreational opportunities across 75 state parks. Activities include hiking, biking, boating, fishing, swimming, horseback riding, teambuilding ropes courses, hunting, and camping to support veterans' mental and physical well-being.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides recreational access and programming at Maryland state parks for wounded warriors, veterans, and their families, including opportunities to work, learn, volunteer, and recreate in natural habitats across Maryland.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Wounded warriors, veterans, and their families from nearby military installations and facilities including Fort Meade, Andrews Air Force Base, Walter Reed National Military Medical Center, and others.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Recreational activities, volunteering, and employment opportunities in Maryland state parks.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide across Maryland's 75 state parks, with particular focus on serving military installations in and around Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a wounded warrior, veteran, or family member of a service member
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Wounded Warrior & Veteran Outreach Coordinator, Christina Carlson, for information on available programs and accommodations.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Department of Natural Resources Fishing and Boating Services partners with local community organizations to host youth fishing rodeos across the state. The program introduces children ages 3–15 to fishing by providing a safe, supervised environment where kids can learn basic angling skills, develop a stewardship ethic, and have a positive outdoor experience. Events are held at ponds, lakes, and streams throughout Maryland between March and November, teaching hands-on fishing experience and encouraging stewardship of natural resources. The program supports up to 70 rodeos annually, with approximately 7,000 children participating each year. Fish are provided via U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service Wildlife and Sport Fish Restoration Program grant funds.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The department provides support and assistance to community and non-profit organizations that sponsor youth fishing rodeo events. Support includes limited fish stocking (trout or hybrid sunfish, minimum 100 trout per event at 50 per surface acre), technical advice and information, website listing of events, and assistance locating alternative commercial fish sources. A regional biologist conducts pre-event evaluation and recommendations. Not all requesting events can be supported due to limited fish supply. Organizations must submit a post-event evaluation report within 30 days of the event to receive a permit or fish for a subsequent event.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: January 15 each year; applications accepted after September 1 of prior year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community and non-profit organizations interested in sponsoring youth fishing events for children ages 3–15 in Maryland; also organizations serving individuals with physical or mental disabilities and veterans with service-connected disabilities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Support for organizing and running youth fishing rodeo events, including fish stocking (trout or hybrid sunfish), technical advice and guidance, website promotion, assistance locating alternative fish sources, and event coordination. Event organizers typically provide fishing gear/bait, fishing tips, food, and prizes for participants.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland; events held between March and November at lakes, ponds, or streams. Private property events limited to water bodies not exceeding 10 acres surface area. Stocked area must remain open to public fishing for at least 14 days after the event, minimum 8 hours per day with consistent daily hours.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted after September 1 of the prior year and must be submitted by January 15 each year. Complete the Youth Fishing Rodeo Program Application (PDF) and submit via mail, fax, or email to the Youth Fishing Rodeo Program Coordinator (Michael Anderson). Requests are prioritized by information supplied and receipt date. Review the updated program policy and information letter before applying. After each event, submit a post-event evaluation Rodeo Survey Form (via mail, fax 301-791-4672, or online) within 30 days to qualify for future support and remain eligible for a permit or fish stocking the following year.

structured_extraction.program_name: Baltimore County East Side Revitalization Community-Wide Assessment Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: A U.S. EPA-funded brownfields assessment grant administered by the Maryland Department of Planning. The grant provides free Phase I and/or Phase II Environmental Site Assessments (ESAs) for properties on Baltimore County's east side that may be contaminated by hazardous substances, pollutants, or contaminants. The 52-census-tract East Side target area includes portions of Sparrows Point, Essex, Middle River, Dundalk, Bowleys Quarters, Edgemere, Perry Hall, and White Marsh. Phase I assessments identify potential contamination concerns; Phase II assessments involve physical sampling and testing to confirm contamination. The assessments help property owners understand the condition of their land, which can make properties more marketable for sale, refinancing, redevelopment, or reuse — such as community solar, parks, new businesses, or other community benefits. The program also facilitates participation in MDE's Voluntary Cleanup Program (VCP) and Technical Review Services (TRS) at no cost to property owners. Property owners can contact the program directly to determine eligibility, and community members can also submit potential brownfield locations using the Brownfields Scout form to help identify eligible properties for assessment. The program supports brownfield revitalization and redevelopment in the region. MDP may expand the target area beyond the East Side if grant funds cannot be fully expended in the initial target area. Project completion was anticipated by September 2024.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $300,000 in EPA community-wide assessment grant funding (assistance agreement 96387501) covers free Phase I and/or Phase II Environmental Site Assessments (ESAs) for eligible brownfield properties in the 52-census-tract East Side target area of Baltimore County. The program also facilitates participation in MDE's Voluntary Cleanup Program (VCP) and Technical Review Services (TRS) at no cost to property owners. Phase I assessments identify potential contamination concerns; Phase II assessments involve physical sampling and testing to confirm contamination. The assessments can help property owners make properties more marketable for sale, refinancing, redevelopment, or reuse. Property owners must sign an access agreement with the environmental consultant and the Maryland Department of Planning to participate. Property owners may contact the program directly to inquire about eligibility, or community members may submit potential brownfield property locations via the Brownfields Scout form. Eligibility is not guaranteed and properties are reviewed by the project team before assessments are conducted.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners, residents, and community members in Baltimore County's east side — including areas such as Sparrows Point, Essex, Middle River, Dundalk, Bowleys Quarters, Edgemere, Perry Hall, and White Marsh — who own or are aware of potentially contaminated (brownfield) properties and are interested in free Phase I and/or Phase II environmental site assessments, MDE Voluntary Cleanup Program participation, and brownfield revitalization support.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding covers the cost of Phase I and/or Phase II Environmental Site Assessments on eligible brownfield properties, including former gas stations, auto repair shops, dry cleaners, metal salvage facilities, industrial sites, illegal dumping sites, and other properties that may have hazardous substances, pollutants, or contaminants present. Assessments support cleanup, redevelopment, or reuse of properties for purposes such as community solar, parks, or new businesses. Funds also support participation in MDE's Voluntary Cleanup Program (VCP) and Technical Review Services (TRS).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Limited to the 52 census tracts making up the East Side target area in Baltimore County, including portions of Sparrows Point, Bowleys Quarters, Lower Back River Neck Peninsula, North Point/Edgemere, Essex, Middle River, Perry Hall/White Marsh, and Dundalk. MDP may expand the target area beyond the East Side if grant funds cannot be fully expended in the initial target area.

Property must be a potential brownfield — meaning it may have hazardous substances, pollutants, or contaminants present
