Submission of property information via the Brownfields Scout form (for community-identified properties)
Property owners must be willing to participate in the assessment process
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Property owners interested in participating should review the eligibility criteria and may visit the Property Owner Portal on the program website to learn about the target area and eligibility criteria. Property owners may also email sylvia.mosser@maryland.gov or mdp.brownfields@maryland.gov to find out if their property is eligible for a free Environmental Site Assessment. If eligible, the owner signs an access agreement allowing the environmental consultant and MDP to conduct the assessment on the property. Community members may attend community outreach events listed on the program calendar, review the East Side Target Area Map, and submit potential brownfield property locations using the Brownfields Scout form (Google Form link provided on the program page). The project team will research submitted properties to determine eligibility for a grant-funded site assessment. Sites selected for Phase II ESAs are determined based on Phase I results.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Planning helps local governments, nonprofits, and other interested parties with brownfield (contaminated or potentially contaminated land) remediation and redevelopment. Assistance includes providing brownfields inventories, coordinating with state and federal agencies (including EPA Region III, MDE, and the NJIT Technical Assistance for Brownfields (TAB) program), helping prepare and manage EPA Brownfields grant applications, and recommending land use plan or zoning code changes to support redevelopment. The program also connects local planning jurisdictions across Maryland with funding and resources for brownfield site assessment and cleanup. Staff can provide general assistance to help determine how to focus brownfield efforts, assess which incentives and opportunities are available in a given area, and coordinate community education and training.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Planning staff provide free technical assistance including: brownfields site inventories, liaison services with MDE, EPA Region III, and the NJIT Technical Assistance for Brownfields (TAB) program, help identifying and preparing EPA Brownfields grant applications, grant management support, recommendations for comprehensive plan language or zoning/subdivision code modifications to facilitate brownfield redevelopment, coordination of training through NJIT TAB, and general guidance on available incentives and opportunities for brownfield redevelopment. The program also connects local planning jurisdictions with funding and resources for brownfield assessment and cleanup.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, nonprofits, local planning jurisdictions, and anyone interested in brownfield remediation and redevelopment in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Technical assistance for brownfield site assessment, remediation planning, grant application development and management, community education, land use planning support, zoning/planning recommendations, brownfield cleanup, and assessing available incentives and opportunities for brownfield redevelopment
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland, with an emphasis on expanding EPA Brownfields funding beyond Baltimore City to other urban and rural areas throughout the state. Available to all local planning jurisdictions statewide.
requirements_list: Must be interested in brownfield remediation or redevelopment
Submit a Request for Brownfield Assistance form to enlist Planning's help
Applicant must be a local government, nonprofit, or other interested party
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the online Request for Brownfield Assistance form available on the Maryland Department of Planning website, or contact Sylvia A. Mosser at the Maryland Department of Planning. Planning staff will then coordinate appropriate assistance.

structured_extraction.program_name: MDE Free Services (Voluntary Cleanup Program and Technical Review Service)
structured_extraction.program_description: Property owners participating in the Baltimore County East Side Revitalization Community-Wide Assessment Grant can access free Maryland Department of Environment (MDE) services, including the MDE Voluntary Cleanup Program (VCP) and the MDE Technical Review Service (TRS). These services help property owners get their properties ready for redevelopment by providing state authorization of environmental site conclusions and cleanup plans. The VCP was established via emergency legislation in February 1997 to encourage investigation, cleanup, and redevelopment of eligible properties with known or perceived controlled hazardous substance contamination, and as of October 1, 2004, properties contaminated by oil or petroleum are also eligible. The TRS provides free technical review of site-related environmental documents including work plans, environmental investigation reports, soil management plans, proposed sampling strategies, and remediation plans.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive free access to the MDE Voluntary Cleanup Program (normally a $6,000 application fee) and the MDE Technical Review Service (normally $500–$1,500 in fees), for a total value of approximately $6,500–$7,500 in waived fees. VCP provides liability releases and finality to site cleanup via No Further Requirements Determination (NFRD) or Certificate of Completion (COC). TRS provides document review, written summaries, site visits, and consultation services for site-related environmental documents.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners in the Baltimore County East Side area who are participating in the EPA-funded Community-Wide Assessment Grant and want to prepare brownfield properties for redevelopment. More broadly, the underlying MDE programs serve property owners, developers, and prospective purchasers with contaminated properties seeking environmental site status determinations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Covers the cost of MDE VCP application fees and TRS review fees for brownfield site environmental assessment and cleanup authorization, including document review, site visits, and consultation services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to property owners in the Baltimore County East Side Revitalization area participating in the EPA-funded grant program. The underlying MDE VCP and TRS programs are available statewide across Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a property owner participating in the Baltimore County East Side Revitalization Community-Wide Assessment Grant
Property must be a brownfield site eligible under the grant program
VCP requires a completed application and non-refundable $6,000 application fee (waived under this program)
VCP requires a Phase I environmental site assessment (ASTM standards, within 180 days of application)
VCP requires a Phase II environmental site assessment (within one year of application, unless Phase I shows no recognized environmental conditions)
TRS requires submission of a written request letter on site owner/representative letterhead signed by an authorized representative
TRS requires copies of site-related environmental documents
Note: Petroleum-related issues under TRS are handled by the Oil Control Program, not TRS
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Property owners participating in the EPA grant-funded program can access these free MDE services as part of their participation. For VCP, submit a complete application with required environmental site assessments. For TRS, submit a written request letter on official letterhead with copies of site-related environmental documents to MDE's State Assessment and Remediation Division. See the Property Owner Portal for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A mentorship network that pairs newly appointed planning commissioners and board of appeals members with experienced citizen planners (Peer Leaders). It helps new appointees build confidence, ask practical questions, share best practices, and strengthen their skills in local planning and zoning roles.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Experienced citizen planners (Peer Leaders) are matched with newly appointed planning commissioners or board of appeals members. Interactions can be virtual or in-person, formal or informal, on an as-needed or regular basis. Peer Leaders answer practical questions, share experiences, and offer general non-project-specific advice to help new appointees build confidence and skills.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Newly appointed planning commissioners and board of zoning appeals members (Peers), as well as experienced citizen planners willing to serve as Peer Leaders, across Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable — this is a mentorship and technical assistance program, not a funding program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to citizen planners serving on planning commissions or boards of appeals throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a newly appointed planning commissioner or board of appeals member (to join as a Peer), or an experienced citizen planner (to join as a Peer Leader)
Must complete the sign-up form to be matched with a peer or peer leader
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Fill out the online sign-up form to register as either a Peer or a Peer Leader. Someone from the MPCA or the Maryland Department of Planning will then contact you to facilitate a match.

structured_extraction.program_description: Annual awards program that recognizes individuals, businesses, organizations, and local governments for outstanding contributions to smart, sustainable growth throughout Maryland. Awards are given in three categories: Leadership, Project, and Policy.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Winners receive recognition through a Governor's Citation, elevating their contributions at the state level. There are three award categories: Leadership (for individuals or organizations championing sustainable growth), Project (for excellence in sustainable buildings, infrastructure, or places), and Policy (for impactful policies, regulations, or plans supporting sustainable land use).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals, businesses, organizations, and local governments that have made outstanding contributions to sustainable growth in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Recognition award — no direct financial assistance provided.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — open to projects, policies, and leaders from anywhere in Maryland.
requirements_list: Nominations must demonstrate alignment with at least 4 of the 8 Sustainable Growth Principles (SGP3).
Nominations are evaluated on Replicability, Impact, Collaboration, Innovation, and Endurance.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a nomination starting September 1, 2026. Nominations are evaluated by judges against the five core criteria and alignment with the Sustainable Growth Principles.

structured_extraction.program_name: Planning Commission, Planning Board and Board of Appeals Education Course
structured_extraction.program_description: An online training course developed by the Maryland Department of Planning (MDP) for members of local planning commissions, planning boards, and boards of zoning appeals. Required by the Smart and Sustainable Growth Act of 2009, the course covers topics such as the role of the comprehensive plan, zoning ordinances, subdivision ordinances, land preservation methods, adequate public facilities ordinances, and proper standards for special exceptions and variances. The course takes approximately 6 hours to complete.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free online education course for planning commission, planning board, and board of appeals members in Maryland counties and municipalities. The course is mandatory and takes approximately 6 hours to complete. Local alternatives are permitted. Participants create an account on the MDP training site and complete the course online. A recording of a virtual training session from November 13, 2025 is also available.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: By July 1, 2010 for incumbent members; within 6 months of appointment for newly appointed members
structured_extraction.program_audience: Members of local planning commissions, planning boards, and boards of appeals in Maryland non-charter counties, municipalities, and charter counties including Montgomery and Prince George's that exercise planning and zoning authority.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable — this is a training program, not a funding program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to all Maryland jurisdictions with planning and zoning authority under Article 66B, Article 25A, or Article 28 of the Annotated Code of Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a member of a planning commission, planning board, or board of appeals
Must represent a Maryland local jurisdiction (county or municipal) that exercises planning and zoning authority under the Land Use Article
Required for members of non-charter counties and municipalities, as well as charter counties including Montgomery and Prince George's
Complete education course within 6 months of appointment or by July 1, 2010 for incumbent members
One-time completion required (not required for each reappointment)
Topics must cover comprehensive plans, special exceptions/variances standards, zoning, planned development and subdivision ordinances
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Access the online course at planning.maryland.gov, create an account, log in, and complete the online course. Members of the public who are not commission or board members may view course materials without creating an account.

structured_extraction.program_name: Power Plant Research Program (PPRP) Technical Assistance for Solar Facility Siting
structured_extraction.program_description: The Power Plant Research Program (PPRP) provides free technical assistance to local governments on utility-scale solar facility siting. This includes help understanding the Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity (CPCN) approval process, conducting site visits of proposed solar facilities, answering technical questions about the utility industry, and sharing ideas for developing local solar siting ordinances. PPRP can also discuss likely licensing conditions and recommendations for proposed facilities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free technical assistance for local governments, including guidance on the CPCN review process, site visit opportunities, answers to technical questions about utility-scale solar facilities, and ideas for local solar siting ordinances. PPRP can also explain anticipated licensing conditions and likely approval or disapproval recommendations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments in Maryland seeking assistance with utility-scale solar facility siting, the CPCN process, or developing local solar ordinances.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Technical guidance on solar facility siting, CPCN process participation, and local ordinance development.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to Maryland local governments.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local government entity in Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact PPRP directly for assistance. See dnr.maryland.gov/pprp/Pages/contact.aspx for contact information.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Priority Funding Areas (PFA) program directs state funding for growth-related infrastructure to designated geographic areas called Priority Funding Areas. Local governments certify areas as PFAs with the Maryland Department of Planning, which reviews submissions within 30 days and issues a PFA concurrence letter. Once certified, projects located in these areas become eligible for many state incentives, including Maryland Economic Development Assistance Authority Fund (MEDAAF) programs, the Community Investment Tax Credit, and the Maryland Mortgage Program. Growth-related projects include highways, sewer and water construction, economic development assistance, transportation, neighborhood revitalization, housing assistance, and state leases or construction of new office facilities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Maryland Department of Planning reviews local government PFA certification submissions within 30 days and issues a PFA concurrence letter. Once a PFA is certified, projects located within designated Priority Funding Areas become eligible for state incentives including all MEDAAF programs and the Community Investment Tax Credit. The program directs state investment in growth-related infrastructure such as highways, sewer and water construction, economic development assistance, transportation, neighborhood revitalization, housing assistance, and state office facilities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments seeking to certify locally designated Priority Funding Areas to the Maryland Department of Planning, as well as businesses, non-profits, and projects located within designated Priority Funding Areas seeking state investment and incentives for growth-related development.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Transportation, highways, water and sewer infrastructure, neighborhood revitalization, housing assistance, economic development assistance, and state leases or construction of new office facilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to all Maryland local governments statewide. Projects and businesses must be located within a designated Priority Funding Area (PFA).
requirements_list: Submit an official letter from the jurisdiction stating its local certification of an area as a PFA
Include a map and parcel number(s) for the certified properties
Include applicable zoning for certified properties
Include allowable residential density
Include sewer service area designations
Include comprehensive plan designated growth area status
Include any other relevant information showing the property meets PFA criteria
Send all PFA certification materials via email to mdp.planreview@maryland.gov and all regional planners assigned to the jurisdiction
Project or business must be located within a designated Priority Funding Area (PFA)
Project must be growth-related, such as development involving highways, sewer/water construction, economic development, or state office facilities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Local governments should send all PFA certification materials via email to mdp.planreview@maryland.gov as well as all regional planners assigned to the jurisdiction. The Maryland Department of Planning will review the submission for compliance with PFA criteria and send a PFA concurrence letter within 30 days. Businesses and projects seeking to take advantage of PFA incentives may contact the Prince George's County Economic Development Corporation at 301-583-4650 and ask to speak with a Business Development Specialist for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide capital program that provides over $300 million annually in state funding for public school construction, renovation, and expansion projects. The Interagency Committee for School Construction (IAC) develops funding recommendations, linking school construction to sound land use patterns, community revitalization, and sustainable development goals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Over $300 million in state school construction funds are distributed annually. The IAC reviews and recommends projects for funding, prioritizing responsible deployment of limited capital funds for school construction, renovation, and expansion.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local government jurisdictions planning to open, close, renovate, or expand public school buildings in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction, renovation, and expansion of public school buildings.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across all Maryland jurisdictions.
requirements_list: Projects must be justified by the IAC based on development patterns, community and educational perspectives, fiscal constraints, and construction standards.
School construction growth must be linked to sound land use patterns, community revitalization, and sustainable development goals.
IAC membership includes Maryland Department of Planning, Maryland State Department of Education, and Maryland Department of General Services.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Local jurisdictions submit school construction projects for review by the Interagency Committee for School Construction (IAC), which develops funding recommendations. More details are available at the IAC website (https://iac.mdschoolconstruction.org/).

structured_extraction.program_name: Smart DG+ Solar and Wind Siting Screening Tool
structured_extraction.program_description: Smart DG+ is a free, online, map-based screening tool sponsored by PPRP and the Maryland Energy Administration (MEA). It helps solar and wind developers and government officials identify potential locations for new renewable energy projects in Maryland by displaying the location of electrical transmission lines, geographic barriers to project construction, local zoning restrictions, and other geographic data relevant to project feasibility. The tool includes a county zoning guide updated annually to keep county-level information current. The county zoning guide provides county-by-county zoning guidance for large-scale (>2 MW) solar and wind projects, identifying areas where county zoning prohibits all large-scale renewable energy projects and providing links to county zoning codes and comprehensive plans.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free online mapping tool that displays electrical transmission line locations, barriers to project construction, local zoning restrictions, and other geographic data to help developers and local governments identify financially feasible locations for utility-scale solar and wind projects in Maryland. Includes a county zoning guide updated annually with county-by-county zoning guidance for large-scale renewable energy projects, links to county zoning codes and comprehensive plans, and C-PACE program information for qualified counties.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Solar and wind energy developers, property owners, and local government officials (including county and municipal planning/zoning departments) in Maryland seeking to identify viable sites for utility-scale renewable energy projects and understand local zoning and infrastructure constraints.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Site identification and feasibility screening for utility-scale solar and wind energy projects, including understanding local zoning and infrastructure constraints. Actual application processes and permit requirements vary by county zoning authority.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across all 24 Maryland counties. Eligibility for specific projects varies by county and zoning district; additional rules may apply within municipalities beyond county zoning.
requirements_list: Large-scale projects (>2 MW) must comply with county zoning regulations
Height limitations vary by county and project type (ranging from 50–160 feet depending on county)
Capacity limitations vary by county and project type
Zoning district restrictions apply in many counties
Special exception or conditional use permit approvals often required from Board of Appeals
Minimum parcel/lot area requirements in some counties
Setback/distance requirements from residential zones in some counties
Verify eligibility with local county or municipality planning/zoning department
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Access the tool directly online at dnr.maryland.gov/pprp/Pages/SmartDG.aspx. No application required. The county zoning guide and map tool are freely available as informational resources. Actual permit applications are processed by county zoning authorities.

structured_extraction.program_description: An annual collegiate interdisciplinary competition hosted by the Maryland Sustainable Growth Commission (administered by the Maryland Department of Planning) that engages undergraduate and graduate students and faculty from Maryland's colleges and universities in planning, sustainability, and community reinvestment issues. Students analyze economic, social, and environmental aspects of sustainable growth and develop creative solutions for actual community challenges, including redevelopment of vacant lots, community charrettes, green infrastructure and public access, and coastal issues. Submissions include a completed submission form, a final student report/plan/project (or web tool), and a video or in-person presentation. Projects must address Maryland's 12 Visions for Smart Growth. Finalists participate in a Presentation Day in mid-February, and winning teams are recognized at the commission's annual spring awards ceremony. The program provides career-building, real-world learning experience and the opportunity to interact with local leaders and engage in community planning processes.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Recognition competition for student work on sustainable growth, planning, and reinvestment topics. Students participate in a competitive planning challenge, submit reports/plans/projects (or web tools), and finalists present their work on a Presentation Day in mid-February. Winners receive statewide recognition at events or publications, an invitation for their Dean or University President to the awards ceremony, and the opportunity to present at conferences (MPCA, MML, APA MD). No monetary prize amount is stated. The competition also provides students career-building, real-world learning experience and the opportunity to interact with local leaders and engage in community planning processes.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: January 17, 2020 (fall competition cycle; awards ceremony held in spring)
structured_extraction.contact_name: Joe Griffiths, Local Assistance and Training Manager
structured_extraction.program_audience: Undergraduate and graduate students at Maryland colleges and universities pursuing degrees in planning, architecture, engineering, or other sustainability-minded concentrations, as well as faculty advisors interested in community planning, sustainability, and sustainable growth issues.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participation in the competition — students submit planning projects, reports, plans, or web tools completed during a semester, addressing sustainable investment in Maryland's communities with a focus on economic opportunity, environmental protection, and social justice, and supporting at least one of Maryland's 12 Visions for Smart Growth. The program provides recognition and community engagement experience rather than direct financial assistance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Open to students enrolled at all Maryland institutions of higher education.
requirements_list: Must be a student enrolled at a Maryland college or university (professors/faculty advisors also eligible)
Student work must be completed during a semester (e.g., a 2019 semester)
Submission must include a completed submission form with faculty/student names, contact info, and explanation of how project addresses Maryland's 12 Visions
Final project must be submitted (report, plan, web tool, etc.)
250-500 word description of the project required
Video or in-person presentation required
At least one student must attend presentation day or submit a recorded video with availability to answer questions
Projects must be student-driven
Projects must support at least one of Maryland's 12 Visions for Smart Growth
Projects should focus on sustainable investment in Maryland communities addressing economic opportunity, environmental protection, and social justice
Submissions due January 17, 2020
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Summer 2019: Outreach to faculty. Fall 2019: Faculty inform students and register interested participants. Academic programs are contacted each fall to elicit interest in the competition. Students complete a submission form with project details and a 250-500 word description, then submit along with their final student report, plan, web tool, or project to Joe Griffiths at joseph.griffiths@maryland.gov by the stated deadline (January 17, 2020). If the file is too large to email, call 410-767-4553. Finalists prepare for a Presentation Day scheduled for mid-February. Winning teams are recognized at the commission's annual spring awards ceremony. A flyer, FAQs, and application form are available on the program website.

structured_extraction.program_description: An online education course on Tax Increment Financing (TIF) that teaches local government officials how TIF works, its benefits and risks, and how it can be used to fund public improvements and spur redevelopment in designated Sustainable Communities. Completion of the course is required before a local jurisdiction can use the TIF authority for Sustainable Communities established under Maryland's 2013 Sustainable Communities – Designation and Financing Law. Upon completion, the Maryland Department of Planning issues a certification. The course is currently temporarily offline; interested parties should contact Chuck Boyd directly.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free online training course covering TIF concepts, benefits, risks, and how to implement TIF in designated Sustainable Communities. Participants receive a certification from MDP upon completion. The course is currently offline due to technical issues; interested parties should contact Chuck Boyd directly at chuck.boyd@maryland.gov.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Chief administrative officers and chief financial officers of local Maryland jurisdictions who need to fulfill the mandatory TIF education requirement before using TIF authority for Sustainable Communities revitalization under the 2013 Sustainable Communities – Designation and Financing Law.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Education and certification on Tax Increment Financing practices and Maryland law — no funds disbursed; the course provides knowledge on implementing TIF financing for public improvements that promote economic development.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to Maryland local government officials.
requirements_list: Participant must be a chief administrative officer or chief financial officer of a local Maryland jurisdiction
Completion required before the local jurisdiction may use TIF authority for Sustainable Communities under the 2013 Sustainable Communities – Designation and Financing Law
Jurisdiction must intend to use TIF authority under the Sustainable Communities – Designation and Financing Law
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Chuck Boyd at chuck.boyd@maryland.gov to access the course while the online TIF training is temporarily offline. Normally completed via the online training portal. Upon completion, MDP provides a certification.

structured_extraction.program_name: Transfer of Development Rights (TDR) Technical Assistance Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Department of Planning provides outreach, education, technical assistance, and analysis support to local governments interested in Transfer of Development Rights (TDR) programs. TDR programs are a voluntary land preservation tool where developers buy development rights from owners of rural land in designated sending areas, and a perpetual conservation easement is placed on the property. Developers can then use those rights to build more intensively in receiving areas where development is planned. This helps counties limit loss of farmland and forest land by allowing development rights to be transferred from preservation areas to planned growth areas. Planning staff help communities identify what type of TDR program would be most beneficial for their needs, provide educational presentations and materials, and offer technical analysis support to establish or improve TDR program operations.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Planning staff provide outreach, education, technical assistance, and analytical support to local governments on TDR programs. This includes identifying the most beneficial type of TDR program, delivering educational presentations and materials, and providing technical analysis in support of establishing or improving a TDR program. Specific assistance includes: policy development, plan review, ordinance creation, supply and demand analysis, tax revenue analysis, infrastructure needs assessment, presentations and workshops, informational materials, data analysis, mapping expertise, and one-on-one consulting. Staff assist communities in identifying the best program type for their needs and support local TDR program operations and analysis.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments (counties and municipalities) in Maryland interested in establishing or improving Transfer of Development Rights programs to preserve rural land and direct development to planned growth areas with existing infrastructure. Also relevant to county planning departments, property owners in sending areas, and developers in receiving areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Technical assistance for planning and implementing TDR programs, including educational presentations, materials, and analytical support for local TDR program operations to preserve rural land and direct development to areas with existing infrastructure. Specific uses include policy development, plan review, ordinance creation, supply and demand analysis, tax revenue analysis, and infrastructure needs assessment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to Maryland local governments with or considering TDR programs. Counties with documented TDR programs include: Calvert, Caroline, Cecil, Charles, Frederick, Harford, Howard, Montgomery, Queen Anne's, St. Mary's, Talbot, Wicomico, and Worcester. Somerset County has a TDR program on the books but unused.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local government jurisdiction in Maryland
Must be interested in establishing or improving a Transfer of Development Rights program
Strong incentives for landowners in sending areas to sell development rights
Demand for bonus density or equivalent in receiving zones
TDRs must be the predominant option for acquiring bonus density
Program must move rights from rural to growth areas
Market demand for bonus density
Education of stakeholders
Program marketing
Economic development plan
Design guidelines for receiving area
Local administrative commitment
Program participation is voluntary
Comprehensive plan and zoning should support TDR program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Communities interested in a TDR program are encouraged to contact Maryland Department of Planning staff directly for one-on-one consulting. Staff will assist in identifying the most beneficial program type for their needs and provide educational presentations, materials, and technical analysis support. Counties may also participate in regional meetings to share updates on program activity and changes.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Service and Civic Innovation (DSCI), through the Governor's Commission on Service and Volunteerism (GCOSV), offers formula-based operational grant funding to nonprofits, public agencies, and institutions of higher education to join the AmeriCorps State and National portfolio. Grantees use the funding to recruit, deploy, and support full- or part-time AmeriCorps members serving in communities across Maryland, addressing critical local needs in education, economic opportunity, capacity building, and other community priorities. Grant award amounts are based on the number of AmeriCorps members serving with the organization. Individuals who complete a term of service can receive an educational award of up to $5,775. Subgrantees also receive compliance support, strategic guidance, and access to resources including governing documents, reporting guides, training, and professional development.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Service and Civic Innovation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Formula-based operational grants funding organizations to deploy full- or part-time AmeriCorps members in communities across Maryland. Programs must support the equivalent of at least 20 full-time AmeriCorps members in their first year. Grant amount is based on the number of members served. Matching funds may be required. Individuals who complete a term of service can receive an educational award of up to $5,775. Subgrantees also receive compliance support, strategic guidance, and access to resources including governing documents, reporting guides, training, and professional development through the GCOSV grantmaking program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofits, public agencies, and institutions of higher education seeking to engage AmeriCorps members to address critical community needs across Maryland by joining the Maryland AmeriCorps State and National portfolio.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Development and operation of programs that engage AmeriCorps members in direct community service, including addressing education, economic opportunity, capacity building, and other critical community needs across Maryland. Eligible expenses include personnel expenses, personnel fringe benefits, staff travel, member travel, equipment, supplies, contractual and consultant services, staff training, member training, data collection and validation, other operating costs, living allowance, member support costs, and administrative/indirect costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — programs must serve Maryland communities. Projects must place AmeriCorps members in service positions located only within Maryland.
requirements_list: Programs must support the equivalent of 20 full-time AmeriCorps members in their first year of operation
Matching funds may be required
Applications must be submitted through the America Learns application portal
Must be a program or nonprofit organization, public agency, or institution of higher education
Must be interested in joining the Maryland AmeriCorps State and National portfolio
Must address community needs in areas such as education, economic opportunity, or capacity building
Certificate of Status from Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation required
Maryland Business Express Entity Search registration required
Member Service Year (MSY) Requirements must be met
Data Collection and Quality Plan obligations must be fulfilled
State Support and Oversight Fee compliance required
National Performance Measures reporting required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review the NOFO and application instructions on the DSCI website at dsci.maryland.gov/americorps-md/notice-funding-opportunities. Complete application materials using the America Learns application portal at https://grants.americalearns.net/serve-maryland. Submit a cover sheet and required narratives, including National Performance Measures reporting and a detailed budget. Applications are evaluated on Program Design, Organizational Capability, and Cost Effectiveness & Budget Adequacy. Submit required documents and waivers by April 22, 2026 at 5 PM ET. Direct questions to Chelsea Scott at [email protected] or the Maryland AmeriCorps team at DSCI.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's state-level AmeriCorps program that has operated for more than three decades, managed by the Maryland Department of Service and Civic Innovation. Participants serve full- or part-time for a few weeks up to 12 months, connecting with organizations tackling challenges like education gaps and economic opportunity. Members give back to their community, gain leadership experience and professional development, and earn a living allowance/stipend and an education award usable for tuition or student loan repayment. AmeriCorps members join a national network of over one million alumni.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Service and Civic Innovation

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Corps/Service Year Option (MC/SYO) Program is a statewide workforce development and civic innovation initiative administered by the Maryland Department of Service and Civic Innovation (DSCI). Two pathways are available: the Service Year Option targets recent Maryland high school graduates (ages 18–24 with a high school diploma, GED, or Certificate of Completion) seeking to spend at least nine months with a host site partner organization earning a living wage; and Maryland Corps, open to all adults 18 and older with no education requirement, targeting those looking to change careers or re-enter the workforce. Members serve full-time (30–40 hours per week) for a minimum 9-month term (at least 41 weeks, starting Fall 2026 and ending Summer 2027) at a Host Site Partner organization — such as a school, nonprofit, government agency, or private business — earning at least $15/hour, receiving on-the-job training, mentoring, monthly in-person professional development, weekly virtual learning opportunities, dedicated Member Success coaching, networking opportunities, and a $6,000 taxable cash completion award upon successful completion. Members may also enroll in a federally recognized registered apprenticeship pathway through the U.S. Department of Labor and earn trade credentials. Host Site Partner organizations (nonprofits, for-profits, government agencies, higher education institutions, and others) hire program Members as W-2 employees and receive a cost-reimbursement grant covering approximately two-thirds of member wages — up to $20,000 per member per year out of an estimated total annual cost of $27,450 — paid quarterly after documentation is submitted. Cost-share waivers are available on a competitive basis. DSCI also provides training, coaching, and professional development directly to service members, and helps members build a lifelong alumni network.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Service and Civic Innovation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Members earn at least $15.00 per hour for 30–40 hours per week over at least 41 weeks. Upon successfully completing the service term, members receive a taxable $6,000 cash completion award (usable for any purpose). Members also receive on-the-job training, mentoring, monthly in-person professional development, weekly virtual learning opportunities, dedicated Member Success coaching, networking opportunities, and may enroll in a federally recognized registered apprenticeship and earn trade credentials. Host Site Partner organizations receive a cost-reimbursement grant covering approximately two-thirds of member wages: DSCI reimburses up to $20,000 per year per full-time member (out of an estimated total annual cost of $27,450). Host sites cover the remaining ~$7,450 per year (~$180 per week) as cost-sharing and must provide fringe benefits including healthcare. Reimbursements are paid quarterly after host sites submit documentation. A payroll provider option is available for organizations for which direct reimbursement is not a good fit. Cost-share waivers are available on a competitive basis.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents age 18 and older who want to serve full-time in their communities, gain work experience, and earn a living wage. Service Year Option targets ages 18–24 with a high school diploma, GED, or Certificate of Completion; Maryland Corps is open to all adults 18+ with no education requirement. Also includes nonprofit, for-profit, government, higher education, and other Maryland-based organizations seeking to host service members as Partners, and those who want to nominate a Member.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Living wage earnings (at least $15/hour, 30–40 hours per week) during service term, healthcare benefits provided by host site, on-the-job training, mentoring, monthly professional development, weekly virtual learning, networking, career exploration, apprenticeship/trade credential support, and a $6,000 taxable cash completion award that can be used for any purpose (debt repayment, education, savings, etc.). For host site organizations: supplemental grant funding offsets member wages, payroll taxes, and benefits (including health insurance); reimbursements offset approved member costs paid upfront by the host site. DSCI also funds the $6,000 Member completion award and professional development resources.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland, spanning all 24 Maryland jurisdictions, from Western Maryland to the Eastern Shore. Participants must reside in Maryland. Host site organizations must be Maryland-based and provide a physical location in Maryland for Members to serve. Host sites in jurisdictions with minimum wages above $15/hour should expect higher costs proportionate to the wage increase.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Complete an application on DSCI's Application and Matching Portal (BuildWithin) at dsci.maryland.gov/apply-now/mcyso as a Member, as a Partner (host employer), or submit a nomination for a Member. Reasonable accommodations available upon request. 2. DSCI reviews applications on a rolling basis and may contact you for follow-up or clarification. 3. Once conditionally accepted, use the portal to explore positions, apply, interview with Host Site Partner organizations, and accept an offer. structured_extraction.program_name: ATTAIN Grant (2022) – US Route 50 Technology Deployment
structured_extraction.program_description: Federal FHWA ATTAIN grant awarded to MDOT SHA to deploy Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) and Traffic Signal Management and Operations (TSMO) strategies on the 113-mile US Route 50 corridor in Maryland's Eastern Shore. Deploys adaptive signal control, connected vehicle systems, traffic sensors, machine learning traffic prediction, and traveler information systems to improve safety, travel time reliability, mobility, and quality of life in rural communities. structured_extraction.program_name: Commuter Choice Maryland Employer Partner Program and Maryland Commuter Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: Commuter Choice Maryland, administered by the Maryland Department of Transportation and funded by the State of Maryland, is a statewide free Transportation Demand Management (TDM) program that helps reduce traffic congestion by connecting employers and commuters with programs and resources that make commuting easier, safer, cheaper, and greener. The Employer Partner Program recognizes Maryland employers that offer transportation benefits and commuting incentives to their employees, providing free support including surveys, data, and materials to help build or expand commuter benefits programs. Participating employers receive recognition through webinars, newsletters, and social media. Employers can provide up to $270 per month in tax-free commuter benefits as a monthly transit or vanpool pass or voucher, employees can use pre-tax salary deductions to pay for transit or vanpool costs, or both options can be combined to share the monthly commute cost. Statewide, employees who participate in commuter benefits programs can set aside pre-tax money through their employer to help pay for commuting costs, saving up to 40% on qualifying commuting expenses including transit, ridesharing, biking, telework, guaranteed ride home, and cash in lieu of parking. The program also offers commuter incentives such as Ride Together Rewards (including Vanpool Incentive Program offering $500 monthly, Carpool Incentive Program offering $5 daily during a 90-day special incentive period, and Transit Incentive Programs), Guaranteed Ride Home (up to 6 free emergency rides home per year), and Commuter Cash (via the CommuterCash app, which allows users to log commute trips to earn points redeemable for cash, gift cards, or transportation credits). A pilot program (MD295 Pilot) provides free one-on-one support, monthly workshops, custom resources, and commuter survey development to employers along the MD 295 corridor between West Nursery Road and I-95. The Maryland Commuter Tax Credit allows eligible Maryland-based employers to claim a state tax credit equal to 50% of the commuter or telework subsidies they provide to employees — up to $100 per employee per month (up to $1,200 per employee per year) — for qualifying benefits such as transit passes, vanpool, carpool, telework expenses (including internet access, computer equipment, telephone service, co-working memberships, or job-related software), active transportation, guaranteed ride home, cash in lieu of parking, and multimodal last-mile connections. The credit can be applied against state personal income tax, corporate income tax, or insurance premium tax. Non-profits file MD State forms 508CR and MW508; for-profit businesses file MD State Form 500CRW; the credit can also be filed against the Insurance Premium Tax per COMAR 31.06.04.03. Registration for the Maryland Commuter Tax Credit should be completed annually.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Statewide: Employers can provide up to $270 per month in tax-free commuter benefits as a monthly transit or vanpool pass or voucher. Employers can also pay for employee transit or vanpool commuting exempt from payroll taxes, and offer parking cash-out options convertible to tax-free transit or vanpool benefits. Employees can set aside pre-tax money through their employer to pay for qualifying commuting costs, saving up to 40% on expenses such as transit, ridesharing, biking, telework, and parking-related expenses. Federal law also allows employers to offer employees up to $265 per month as a pre-tax deduction or tax-free subsidy for transit, vanpools, and eligible parking under IRS Section 132(f). Employer Partner Program: Free membership with support including surveys, data, and materials to help employers build or expand their commuter benefits programs, plus recognition through webinars, newsletters, and social media, and access to a resource library. CommuterCash App: Users can log commute trips to earn points and redeem them for cash, gift cards, or transportation credits. MD 295 Corridor Pilot: Free one-on-one support, monthly workshops, commuter survey development, and custom resources for employees. Ride Together Rewards: Vanpool Incentive Program ($500 monthly), Carpool Incentive Program ($5 daily during 90-day special incentive period), and Transit Incentive Programs including FareShare employer reimbursement program (up to $3,000). Maryland Commuter Tax Credit: Eligible employers can claim a 50% tax credit against the cost of providing commute alternative or telework subsidy programs to employees, up to $100 per employee per month (up to $1,200 per employee per year), for qualifying benefits including transit passes, vanpool (6+ seat capacity, minimum 3 employees), carpool (E-ZPass, tolls, parking), telework (internet, computer equipment, telephone service, co-working memberships, job-related software), active transportation (bicycle maintenance), guaranteed ride home, cash in lieu of parking, and multimodal last-mile connections. The credit can be applied against state personal income tax, corporate income tax, or insurance premium tax. Non-profits file MD State forms 508CR and MW508. For-profit businesses file MD State Form 500CRW. The credit can also be filed against the Insurance Premium Tax per COMAR 31.06.04.03.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Registration for the Maryland Commuter Tax Credit should be completed annually
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland employers (both for-profit businesses and 501(c)(3)/501(c)(4) non-profit organizations) of all sizes, state agencies, and public sector organizations that provide or want to provide commuter subsidies, transportation benefits, or telework subsidies to employees, including office managers, HR representatives, and benefits administrators, as well as individual commuters statewide and along the MD 295 corridor between West Nursery Road and I-95. Special focus on employers located along the MD 295 corridor between West Nursery Road and I-95 (Inner Harbor to BWI Airport area). Also applicable to Maryland employees who commute by transit or vanpool.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Qualifying commuting costs including transit passes, vanpool vouchers, ridesharing, biking, telework, and parking-related expenses; building or expanding employer commuter benefits programs including surveys, data collection, outreach materials, and monthly workshops; commuter incentives such as Ride Together Rewards, Guaranteed Ride Home, and Commuter Cash; establishing or improving employer commuter benefit programs along the MD 295 corridor; tax credit offset for costs of providing employees with qualified commuter benefits including transit, vanpool, carpool, telework expenses (internet access, computer equipment, telephone service, co-working memberships, job-related software), active transportation, guaranteed ride home, cash in lieu of parking, and multimodal last-mile connections; subsidized transit fare and Parking Cash Out benefits for employees; FareShare employer reimbursement for transit benefits; CharmPass and FareShare transit incentives; improving workforce recruitment, retention, and reliability.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to employers and commuters statewide in Maryland. The MD 295 Corridor Pilot is specifically limited to the MD 295 corridor between West Nursery Road and I-95, spanning from the Inner Harbor in Baltimore to BWI Airport in Anne Arundel County. The Maryland Commuter Tax Credit is available to all businesses and non-profits operating in Maryland. Commuter benefits must be for travel to/from a location in Maryland.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Employers can join the free Employer Partner Program by contacting the Commuter Choice Maryland Team by email at commuterchoice@mdot.maryland.gov or by completing the online application at the SurveyMonkey link provided on the program page. Commuters and employers can also learn more through the program website at commuterchoicemaryland.com, quarterly webinars, and by contacting the team by phone at (410) 865-1100 (Monday–Friday, 8:30 am–5:30 pm EST). For the MD 295 Corridor Pilot, employers can fill out the interest/participation form on the program webpage or email commuterchoice@mdot.maryland.gov to get started. Commuters can visit tinyurl.com/CCMD295 to set up a Commuter Connections account, find carpool or vanpool matches, and learn how to earn rewards. To earn cash rewards, users can download the CommuterCash mobile app and log their trips. For the Maryland Commuter Tax Credit: 1) Gather business information and details on commuter or telework subsidies provided and apply at the One Stop Maryland website (onestop.md.gov). 2) Commuter Choice Maryland reviews the application and emails an approval certificate if approved. 3) Include the certificate when filing annual state taxes using the appropriate tax forms (Form 500CRW for for-profits; forms 508CR and MW508 for non-profits). Employers must register annually to receive the tax credit. Additional guidance is available in the Maryland Commuter Tax Credit guidance document.

structured_extraction.program_description: CommuterCash is a free mobile app-based rewards program that helps commuters throughout Maryland and the Washington, DC area find and plan alternative commuting options — such as carpool, vanpool, transit, biking, and multimodal travel — and earn cash rewards for logging eligible commute trips. Commuters earn points for logging eligible weekday commute trips during peak hours (6:30–9:30am and 4:00–7:00pm), redeemable for cash, gift cards, or transportation credits. Earn up to $10 after completing 20 trips, or save points for higher-tier rewards up to $90 in value, with up to $600 earnable per calendar year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Commuters earn points for logging eligible weekday commute trips during peak hours (6:30–9:30am and 4:00–7:00pm). Points can be redeemed for cash, gift cards, or transportation credits. Earn up to $10 after completing 20 trips, or save points for higher-tier rewards up to $90 in value. Up to $600 can be earned per calendar year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Commuters traveling anywhere in Maryland or into the Washington, DC area who commute to a physical work location on weekdays during peak hours and want to earn rewards for sustainable commuting.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Points redeemable for cash, gift cards, or transportation credits to offset commuting costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to commuters traveling anywhere in Maryland or into the Washington, DC metro area.

Only one morning and one evening trip earns points per day
Telecommuting and unemployment trips are not eligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download the CommuterCash app from the Apple App Store or Google Play. Register for a Commuter Connections account, log eligible commute trips during peak hours, and redeem accumulated points for cash, gift cards, or transportation credits.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Transportation's Office of Minority Business Enterprise (OMBE) certifies small businesses as Disadvantaged Business Enterprises (DBE), Airport Concession Disadvantaged Business Enterprises (ACDBE), and/or Small Business Enterprises (SBE). Certification qualifies firms to participate in MDOT contracting and procurement programs, as well as federally-funded transportation projects. There is no cost to apply, and a single Uniform Certification Application can be used to seek all three certifications at once. The program is administered by MDOT in conjunction with U.S. Department of Transportation requirements under 49 CFR Part 26.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free certification as a DBE, ACDBE, and/or SBE, which qualifies the firm to compete for MDOT contracts, procurement opportunities, and federally-funded transportation projects. Certified firms must have at least 51% ownership and control by socially and economically disadvantaged individuals. The Personal Net Worth (PNW) cap for all three programs is $2,047,000. OMBE also offers a free monthly workshop to help applicants prepare their application, and an optional 30-minute cursory review of a complete application package upon request. Interstate certification is available under 49 CFR § 26.85 for firms already certified in another state.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Socially and economically disadvantaged business owners (including women, Black American, Hispanic American, Native American, Asian-Pacific American, and Subcontinent Asian American individuals), small business enterprises, and for-profit firms seeking to participate in MDOT and federally-funded transportation contracting and procurement opportunities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Certification enables firms to compete for MDOT transportation contracting and procurement set-asides and goals, as well as federally-funded transportation contracts and airport concession opportunities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — available to businesses operating in Maryland. Out-of-state firms seeking federal DBE/ACDBE certification may also apply. Firms must maintain their principal place of business in their home state for initial certification; interstate certification available under 49 CFR § 26.85.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at the MDOT MBE certification portal or download and print the Uniform Certification Application. Complete all sections with applicable NAICS codes, attach required supporting documents per the Document Checklist, complete the Personal Net Worth Statement with all worksheets and supporting documentation, and submit the full package online. Retain a copy for your records. Contact OMBE with questions or to request a pre-submission application review. Firms already certified in another state may seek interstate certification under 49 CFR § 26.85.

structured_extraction.program_name: Disadvantaged Business Enterprise (DBE) / Airport Concessions Disadvantaged Business Enterprise (ACDBE) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The federal DBE Program increases participation by certified disadvantaged business firms in state and local transportation procurements funded by the U.S. Department of Transportation (USDOT). In Maryland, the program is administered through MDOT SHA, MDOT MAA, MDOT MTA, and the MDOT Office of Planning. The ACDBE Program additionally allows certified firms to meet disadvantaged business participation goals on federally-funded contracts for airport concessionaires managed by MDOT MAA. MDOT serves as the Unified Certification Program (UCP) for Maryland since 1978, administering certification based on 49 CFR Part 26, Subpart D standards.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Certification as a DBE or ACDBE enables firms to participate as subcontractors or prime contractors on USDOT-assisted contracts administered by MDOT SHA, MDOT MAA, MDOT MTA, and the MDOT Office of Planning. Certified firms are listed in DoSEM's online directory. There is no cost to apply for or maintain certification. Firms are no longer eligible if annual gross receipts exceed $23,980,000. The program includes set-asides and goals for DBE participation on USDOT-assisted contracts, as well as technical assistance, bonding/financing support, business development programs, and mentor-protégé programs. Certified firms may also participate in the race-neutral Small Business Enterprise (SBE) component.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Office of Minority Business Enterprise (OMBE) and Office of Diversity and Equity (ODE)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses at least 51% owned and controlled by socially and economically disadvantaged individuals (Women, African Americans, Hispanic Americans, Native Americans, Asian Pacific Americans, Subcontinent Asian Pacific Americans). Personal Net Worth must not exceed $2,047,000. Also includes airport concessionaires seeking ACDBE certification and small businesses seeking the SBE program component.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Certification enables firms to count toward DBE/ACDBE participation goals on USDOT-assisted contracts, gaining access to subcontracting and prime contracting opportunities on federally funded transportation projects including highway, transit, and airport concessions contracts. Contract work performance includes labor and materials for project execution, professional and consulting services, and equipment rental and supplies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland for USDOT-assisted contracts administered by MDOT SHA, MDOT MAA, MDOT MTA, and MDOT Office of Planning. Out-of-state firms with home-state certification may also seek interstate certification for Maryland contracts.

U.S. citizenship proof and government-issued photo ID

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online or by calling DoSEM's OMBE at 410-865-1269 or 800-544-6056. Submit the Uniform Certification Application (can apply for both MBE and DBE simultaneously). Applications are reviewed by the OMBE Intake Unit, then assigned to an MBE Officer who conducts an office interview and job-site visits if applicable. Applicants may appear before the MBE Advisory Committee. Track application status at https://marylandmdbe.mdbecert.com/. Appeals to USDOT must be filed within 90 days; firms denied certification must wait 12 months before reapplying. Bidders on federal-aid contracts must submit DBE participation documentation including Certified DBE Utilization Affidavit, DBE Participation Schedule, and DBE Subcontractor Project Participation Affidavit.

structured_extraction.program_name: Electric Vehicle (EV) Infrastructure Accessibility and Reliability Accelerator (2023)
structured_extraction.program_description: Discretionary grant program to repair or replace inoperable EV charging stations across Maryland. A pilot program to gather lessons learned and best practices for full NEVI deployment, aimed at improving EV charger reliability and accessibility. Funded through the NEVI (National Electric Vehicle Infrastructure) program via FHWA.

Stations must be replaced with NEVI-compliant chargers. 80% federal funding with 20% matching funds required from partners. Total project cost: $5,400,219.60; federal funding: $4,360,175.68.

20% matching funds required from partners
80% federal funding provided

They can use these perks to attract and keep employees. The program also promotes partner employers in webinars and on social media. Additionally, employers can save money through tax benefits.

structured_extraction.program_description: This suite of competitive grant programs provides federal funding to support the improvement, expansion, and sustainability of public ferry services across urban and rural areas. Programs fund capital investments, planning efforts, and in rural areas, operating assistance to maintain essential service.

structured_extraction.program_description: Guaranteed Ride Home is a free program that provides registered commuters who regularly bike, walk, carpool, vanpool, or take transit to work with up to six free emergency rides home per year in the event of a personal or family emergency or unscheduled overtime. Eligible commuters can use the benefit via taxi, rental car, bus, or train. The program ensures commuters who use alternative or sustainable transportation have a reliable backup transportation option. Available statewide in Maryland and administered regionally through local county programs, including Frederick County and Prince George's County RideSmart Commuter Solutions. Advanced registration at commuterconnections.org is required before use.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to six free rides home per year (by taxi, rental car, bus, or train) for registered commuters who experience a personal or family emergency or unscheduled overtime on days they used an alternative commute mode (bike, walk, carpool, vanpool, or transit). Commuters must leave their personal vehicle at home at least twice a week and register for the program in advance at commuterconnections.org.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Commuters who regularly use alternative transportation (transit, carpool, bike, walk, vanpool, or telework) at least twice a week and need a reliable backup transportation option for personal or family emergencies or unscheduled overtime.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Emergency rides home from work (via taxi, rental car, bus, or train) when a personal or family emergency or unscheduled overtime arises on days the commuter used an alternative or sustainable commute mode.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to registered commuters throughout Maryland, including the National Capital Region, Frederick County, and all counties. Locally promoted through county programs such as Prince George's County RideSmart Commuter Solutions and Frederick County.

Must regularly use a sustainable commuting method (bike, walk, carpool, vanpool, or transit)
Must leave personal vehicle at home at least twice a week
Advanced registration required at commuterconnections.org
Can use the benefit up to six times per year
Ride home must be for an unexpected personal emergency or unscheduled overtime
Must comply with participation guidelines

Create an account and enroll in the Guaranteed Ride Home program through the Commuter Connections website. Frederick County residents may also register online via the link provided on the Frederick County program page.

Certified firms are listed in Maryland's online DBE directory and may be eligible to participate in federally funded transportation contracting opportunities.

Certification is based on existing DBE status in another state (Jurisdiction of Original Certification). Firms must submit a cover letter, proof of original certification, and a Declaration of Eligibility (DOE) in PDF format.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Certification status enabling participation in federally funded transportation contracting opportunities in Maryland
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to firms certified as DBEs or ACDBEs in other states

structured_extraction.program_description: MDOT's Joint Development Program uses state-owned land near transit stations to encourage Transit-Oriented Development (TOD). It seeks private development partners to build mixed-use communities with housing (including affordable units), jobs, retail, public amenities, and entertainment close to transit stations. The program supports Maryland's housing, transportation, and economic development goals. An active example is the Reisterstown Plaza Metro Station TOD Vision Plan, a joint effort among public agencies, private sector partners, and community to increase housing opportunities, grow ridership, and support a well-connected transit-oriented future at Reisterstown Plaza Metro Station in Northwest Baltimore City.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MDOT provides access to state-owned land near transit stations for joint development projects. Private partners enter into development agreements with MDOT to build Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) on MDOT-owned sites. The program also includes an unsolicited joint development process for interested developers. For example, the Reisterstown Plaza Metro Station TOD Vision Plan includes: Wabash Avenue redesign, transit plaza and mobility hub improvements, bus circulation and electric bus charging facility, Patterson Avenue redesign, shared parking garage, mixed-use residential and retail development (797 apartment units, 65 townhomes, 53,000 sq ft retail), and 4.8 acres of open space and community gathering areas.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private developers, non-profits, and other qualified partners interested in developing mixed-use, transit-oriented projects on MDOT-owned land near transit stations. Also includes residents, current and future transit riders, business owners, property owners, faith-based organizations, and communities in disadvantaged areas (Justice40 Initiative focus).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Development of mixed-use communities near transit stations, including housing (market-rate, workforce rental, senior housing, and ownership units), jobs, retail, public amenities, and entertainment. Also covers infrastructure improvements (streets, transit facilities, parking), open space and community gathering spaces, green infrastructure and stormwater management, and public realm improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland at MDOT-owned transit station sites. One active site is the 25.6-acre TOD site at Reisterstown Plaza Metro Station in Northwest Baltimore City, within a half-mile radius of the transit station.

Must be interested in developing on MDOT-owned land near transit stations
Must align with MDOT's Joint Development Policy goals and objectives
Minimum 250 workforce rental units required (Reisterstown Plaza site)
EV charging stations and bicycle parking in shared garage
ADA-compliant accessibility features
Coordination with City of Baltimore planning department (where applicable)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested partners should contact MDOT's Office of Real Estate and Economic Development (ORED) directly to explore potential opportunities. MDOT also accepts unsolicited joint development proposals as outlined in its Joint Development Policy. The Reisterstown Plaza TOD plan is currently under refinement with MDOT development partners and the City of Baltimore planning department.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state-funded, competitive, reimbursable grant program established in 2012 and administered by the Maryland Department of Transportation's Office of Active Transportation and Micromobility. The program supports bicycle network development activities across Maryland by offering state grant assistance to local jurisdictions and regional agencies to expedite development of bicycle infrastructure. It funds projects that maximize bicycle access and improve last-mile connections to work, school, shopping, and transit, and prioritizes projects that improve safety and access for disadvantaged communities. Three project types are funded: Design (up to $400,000 for feasibility studies and semi-final design plans up to 65% design), Minor Retrofit (up to $200,000 for low-cost treatments such as bicycle route signing, pavement markings, bicycle parking, counters, drainage grate replacement, state of good repair projects, and Complete Streets intersection treatments), and Construction (up to $500,000 for construction of bikeways infrastructure including trails, shared-use paths, protected bike lanes, cycle tracks, and bicycle and pedestrian bridges, for projects that have reached at least 65% design). Grantees must provide a minimum 20% match of total project cost in cash or in-kind contributions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursable grants for three project types: (1) Design — up to $400,000 for feasibility studies and semi-final design plans up to 65% of proposed bikeways (2-year completion); (2) Minor Retrofit — up to $200,000 for low-cost treatments such as bicycle route signing, pavement markings, bicycle parking, counters, drainage grate replacement, state of good repair projects, and Complete Streets intersection treatments (2-year completion); (3) Construction — up to $500,000 for construction of bikeways infrastructure including trails, shared-use paths, protected bike lanes, cycle tracks, and bicycle and pedestrian bridges, for projects that have reached at least 65% design (3-year completion; 5-year for TAP match projects). Reimbursable expenses include signs, pavement markings, trail/pathway construction, capital equipment (limited to 10% of project costs), contractual/consultant services, approved travel, and materials (case-by-case, limited to lesser of 10% of award or $10,000). Grantees must provide a minimum 20% match of total project cost in cash or in-kind contributions.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: FY27 applications open in April and run through May 31
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland local governments, state agencies, Metropolitan Planning Organizations (MPOs), transit entities, non-profit organizations, and federal public lands agencies operating in Maryland seeking to develop bicycle infrastructure.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Bicycle network development including: engineering design plans and feasibility assessments (up to 65% design); low-cost minor retrofit improvements (bicycle route signing, pavement markings, bicycle parking, counters, drainage grate replacement); state of good repair maintenance on existing bicycle routes; Complete Streets intersection treatments with bicycle facilities; construction or installation of bikeways infrastructure such as shared-use paths, bicycle and pedestrian bridges, protected bike lanes, cycle tracks, and trails; educational and promotional materials (up to 10% or $10,000 of award); and Federal TAP match funding.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Projects must meet at least two eligibility criteria related to proximity to transit (within 3 miles of rail station or major bus hub), county priority designation, location within a Sustainable Community or Bicycle and Pedestrian Priority Area (BPPA), proximity to a Main Street or major institution, access for low-income or disadvantaged communities, or safety intervention in a Vulnerable Roadway User Area. Projects on State right-of-way must submit a Complete Streets objective statement (required starting FY27); projects on local right-of-way may optionally submit one.
