structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a letter of intent by email to MDBikeways@mdot.maryland.gov. The letter should include project title, description, physical limits, estimated cost, anticipated funding request amount, and applicant contact information. Formal applications open in April and close May 31 for the FY27 cycle. After award, submit a work plan within 30 days of grant award notification and quarterly updates every three months until project closes. Submit final report upon project completion; final reimbursement cannot be processed until the Final Report is accepted.

structured_extraction.program_description: Federal FHWA grant awarded to MDOT to accelerate the adoption of low-carbon construction materials — including asphalt, concrete, cement, steel, and glass — on federal-aid eligible construction projects in Maryland. Supports Maryland's Climate Solutions Now Act goals to reduce GHG emissions by 60% over 2006 levels by 2031 and achieve net-zero emissions by 2045. Includes a seven-task structure aligned with three FHWA implementation pathways: Introduce, Expand, and Institutionalize LCTM. Covers identification, testing, quality assurance, specifications development, contractor incentives, EPD development, and long-term performance monitoring. Program activities run from October 2024 to August 2031.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Total program budget of $48,417,000 requested from FHWA. Funds pilot projects and full deployment of low-carbon asphalt, concrete, cement, steel, and glass materials on federal-aid eligible construction projects in Maryland. Covers equipment procurement ($1,161,000), IT services ($2,115,000), internal staff time ($3,123,356), professional services ($6,185,907), university resources ($2,605,191), construction costs ($28,200,000), travel and supplies ($500,000), and contingency ($4,401,547). Includes cost delta coverage when LCTM exceeds conventional material costs, contractor incentives, EPD development and database creation, quality assurance specifications, training and workforce development, test strip placement, and performance monitoring. All funds must be obligated before September 30, 2026.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: All funds must be obligated before September 30, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: State transportation agency personnel (MDOT, SHA, MTA, MAA, MPA, MVA), contractors, material producers (asphalt, concrete, cement, steel, glass), academic and research institutions, trade associations, regional DOTs, local and municipal agencies, Disadvantaged Business Enterprises (DBEs), minority-owned businesses, women-owned businesses, and small businesses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Procurement and use of low-carbon materials on federal-aid construction projects to reduce embodied greenhouse gas emissions; equipment purchases for laboratory analysis; IT services; internal staff time; professional services; university research resources; construction costs including test strips and pilot projects; travel and supplies; contingency; EPD development and database creation; quality assurance specifications development; training and workforce development; contractor incentives and cost delta coverage when LCTM exceeds conventional material costs; and long-term performance monitoring.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland; Title 23 federally-aided projects across four regional zones: Eastern Shore, Western MD, Central MD, and Southern MD.
requirements_list: Projects must be eligible for federal-aid (Title 23) funding
Materials must have substantially lower embodied carbon compared to industry averages
Participation aligned with FHWA implementation pathways (Introduce, Expand, Institutionalize LCTM)
All funds must be obligated before September 30, 2026
Program activities run from October 2024 to August 2031
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Program is administered by MDOT SHA Office of Materials Technology (OMT). Eligible participants coordinate with MDOT/SHA for project identification, material testing, quality assurance protocol development, and construction implementation. Contractors may receive incentives or cost delta coverage for using eligible low-carbon transportation materials on qualifying projects.

structured_extraction.program_description: MDOT's Minority Business Enterprise/Disadvantaged Business Enterprise (MBE/DBE) Compliance Program was created to address discrimination and its effects in transportation contracting markets. It provides compliance monitoring, procurement assistance, and training and outreach to support MBE and DBE participation in highway, transit, airport, and highway safety transportation contracts.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides compliance monitoring, procurement assistance, and training/outreach to help minority and disadvantaged businesses participate in transportation contracting. It assists with resolving disputes between prime contractors and MBE/DBE subcontractors, promotes MBE certification, and hosts procurement outreach events. MDOT aims to achieve 29% MBE participation in its contracting.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Minority-owned and disadvantaged businesses seeking to participate in MDOT transportation contracting, as well as prime contractors with MBE/DBE subcontracting commitments.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Procurement assistance, training, outreach, and compliance support for MBE/DBE participation in transportation contracts.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland; covers highway, transit, airport, and highway safety transportation contracting markets.
requirements_list: Must be a Minority Business Enterprise (MBE) or Disadvantaged Business Enterprise (DBE) certified firm, or a prime contractor with MBE/DBE subcontracting commitments.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact MDOT's MBE/DBE Program Manager for more information, including access to DBE and MBE program manuals and the MBE/DBE Directory.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free monthly workshop run by the Office of Small and Minority Business Policy (OSMBP) to help small, minority, and women-owned businesses apply for certification as a Minority Business Enterprise (MBE), Disadvantaged Business Enterprise (DBE), Airport Concession Disadvantaged Business Enterprise (ACDBE), and/or Small Business Enterprise (SBE). The workshop covers eligibility standards, the full application process, the Uniform Certification Application, common application questions, and tips on connecting to business opportunities with the State of Maryland. Helps businesses meet minority participation goals on government and private sector contracts.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free monthly webinar workshops held on the first Tuesday of each month, with morning (10:00 AM) and evening (5:30 PM) sessions. Additional Spanish-language sessions are also available. Participants learn about eligibility standards, the application process, and how to complete the Uniform Certification Application. Attendees can also meet with a certification expert after the presentation. Space is limited; registration via GoToWebinar is required.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small, minority, women-owned, and disadvantaged businesses interested in obtaining MBE, DBE, ACDBE, or SBE certification to work with the State of Maryland and MDOT.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Technical assistance to complete certification applications; no financial funds are distributed.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland; workshops are held at MDOT Headquarters at 7201 Corporate Center Dr., Hanover, MD 21076 and via webinar.

Register individually for each workshop session via GoToWebinar (space is limited)
Application must be at least 50% complete before scheduling a Cursory Review
Completed UCA (Uniform Certification Application) required for certification
Declaration of Eligibility with wet ink signature (for disadvantaged status claimants)

Five years of business federal tax returns
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register for a monthly workshop using the registration links on the page via GoToWebinar (space is limited). After registering, you will receive a confirmation email with instructions on how to join the webinar. Sessions are held on the first Tuesday of every month with morning and evening slots. Spanish-language sessions are also available. Attend the workshop to get guidance on completing your certification application. Submit a complete application (including the Uniform Certification Application or MBE application and all supporting documents) electronically through the online portal at https://marylandmdbe.mdbecert.com/.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal funding opportunity (Carbon Reduction Program) supporting surface transportation emissions reduction and decarbonization projects in Maryland. The portal provides a centralized location for solicitation of transportation projects that incorporate climate benefits, aligned with Maryland's Climate Solutions Now Act of 2022. Projects may also include optional resilience components for those located in vulnerable areas.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Sub-recipient federal funding (Carbon Reduction Program) for transportation projects that reduce surface transportation emissions and support decarbonization. Funding is structured as an 80% federal / 20% non-federal match split, meaning applicants must provide a minimum 20% cash match. Eligible activities include: Adaptive Traffic Control Systems, Alternative Fuel Vehicles/Infrastructure, Bicycle-Pedestrian/Micro-mobility, Carpooling/Vanpooling, Congestion Reduction, Diesel Reduction Strategies, EV Infrastructure, Freight Modal Shift, Managed Lanes, Transit Construction/Operation, Sustainable Pavements, ITS, Port electrification, and more. Technical assistance is available through weekly virtual office hours on Wednesdays from 3:00–4:00 pm during the solicitation window.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Metropolitan Planning Organizations (MPOs), local governments, WMATA, MDOT Modal Administrations (SHA, MPA, MTA, MAA, MVA), and public/private organizations and agencies implementing surface transportation emissions reduction projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Fleet electrification and zero-emission vehicle infrastructure; Transportation Systems Management and Operations (TSMO); Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS); Congestion mitigation; Vehicle Miles Travelled (VMT) reduction; Transportation mode-shift projects; Public transportation services and facilities; Bike/pedestrian facilities; Efficient street lighting; Diesel engine retrofits; Port electrification; Truck parking technology; Traffic monitoring, management, and control facilities/programs; Congestion pricing and transportation demand management; Right-of-way acquisition (if applicable).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Projects must be located within an MPO (Metropolitan Planning Organization) region. Projects within the CS-CRAB (Coast Smart-Climate Ready Action Boundary) data layer are prioritized, including CRAB Riverine and CRAB Coastal layers. Applicants must identify specific county, city, route, and mile marker for project location.

Projects must be located within an MPO region in Maryland
Minimum 20% non-federal cash match required (80/20 funding split)
Project point of contact designation required
Alignment with state/local carbon reduction goals

Equity/environmental justice considerations
Detailed cost estimate required
Must have or create a OneStop account
Must complete and sign application form
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application through the Maryland OneStop portal during the solicitation window (February 5 – March 26, 2025, at 4:30pm). Steps: Register on OneStop Portal → Verify email → Login → Access Climate Focused Funding application → Complete and submit application (drafts can be saved and resumed). Weekly virtual office hours are held on Wednesdays from 3:00–4:00 pm during the solicitation window. Contact Allison Breitenother (abreitenother@mdot.maryland.gov) for application questions and Deron Lovaas (dlovaas@mdot.maryland.gov) for program/process questions.

structured_extraction.program_description: This page tracks federal transportation discretionary grants that the Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT) and its agencies have applied for, been awarded, or are pursuing. It covers a wide range of transportation infrastructure projects including transit, aviation, port, highway, rail, scenic byway, environmental improvements, and renewable energy initiatives across Maryland. Specific projects include regional bus network asset scans, transit-oriented development financing, port infrastructure modernization, bridge reconstruction, scenic byway tourism information, culvert replacement for fish passage, solar photovoltaic array installation at airports, and electric ground service equipment charging infrastructure.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal discretionary grants awarded to MDOT and its subsidiary agencies (MAA, MPA, MTA, SHA, MDTA, TSO) for transportation infrastructure projects. Award amounts range from hundreds of thousands to billions of dollars depending on the program and project scope. Specific awards include: $2,418,000 in BUILD grant funding for truck parking expansion and safety improvements; $6.932 million for Cresaptown transportation infrastructure improvements; $15,800,000 total project cost (80% federal, 20% non-federal match) for Brunswick & Rockville Station Improvements; $1 million in IFAC Grant Program funding for Regional Bus Network Asset Scan and Innovative Finance Analysis; $1 million for Unlocking TOD through Innovative Financing on Camden & Brunswick MARC Lines; funding for Seagirt Marine Terminal Berth I and II Modernization (Port of Baltimore); $1,728 million total project cost for American Legion Bridge and I-270 Multimodal Improvements (Large BIP); funding for Maryland's Chesapeake Country All-American Road Tourist Information Project; funding for C&O Canal Scenic Byway Corridor Management Plan and Tourist Information Project; funding for culvert replacement at BWI Runway 10 Approach Road for fish passage restoration; up to $20 million FAA grant (75% of project cost) for solar photovoltaic array installation at BWI Airport (25% local match required); and approximately $16.256 million FAA grant (75% of $21.675 million total project cost) for procurement and installation of 250 electric chargers for ground service equipment at BWI Airport (25% local match required).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: October 1, 2025 (IFAC Grant for Camden & Brunswick MARC Lines TOD project); May 31, 2025 (FAA FY2023 Supplemental Discretionary Grant Program - Solar Array and eGSE projects)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland Department of Transportation and its subsidiary agencies seeking federal funding for transportation infrastructure projects, including transit-dependent populations, commercial truck drivers, freight industry stakeholders, rail commuters, airport users, pedestrians and cyclists, port operators, tourism organizations, scenic byway stakeholders, airport authorities, airlines and ground service equipment operators, and local communities across Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Transportation infrastructure improvements including transit facilities, airport improvements, port infrastructure, highway safety, rail improvements, pedestrian and bicycle access, bridge reconstruction, scenic byway tourism information, culvert replacement for fish passage, renewable energy systems, and electric ground service equipment charging infrastructure. Specific uses include: construction of pedestrian/bicycle bridges, truck parking expansion and safety improvements, rail station platform and trackwork improvements, shared-use path construction, airport terminal and control tower improvements, feasibility assessments, preliminary design plans, economic impact analyses, regional bus network asset scans, innovative financing analysis, TOD planning and implementation, port berth modernization and dredging, bridge superstructure and substructure improvements, interpretive signage and byway hub installation, corridor management plan development, culvert replacement with fish passage designs, solar PV array installation over airport parking lots and rooftops, electrical transmission and connection infrastructure upgrades, and purchase and installation of 250 electric chargers for ground support equipment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland, with specific projects in Baltimore City (Cherry Hill/Patapsco Station, Masonville Cove), Prince George's County (I-95 College Park), Howard County (I-95 NB Laurel), Frederick County (I-70 Mount Airy, Brunswick), Montgomery County (Rockville, I-495/I-270 corridor), Allegany County (Cresaptown, Little Orleans, Cumberland), Baltimore County (Port of Baltimore/Seagirt Marine Terminal, Martin State Airport), Anne Arundel County (BWI Airport/Stony Run culvert - designated EPA nonattainment/maintenance area), Eastern Shore counties (Cecil, Kent, Queen Anne's, Talbot, Caroline, Dorchester, Wicomico, Somerset, Worcester) for Chesapeake Country All-American Road, and C&O Canal corridor counties (Montgomery, Frederick, Washington, Allegany).

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: MDOT submits applications to various federal agencies (USDOT, FAA, FRA, FTA, EPA, FEMA, ARC, FHWA, etc.) through their respective discretionary grant programs. Applications include project narratives and supporting documentation. For FAA projects, applicants complete FAA Form 5100-144 and submit via email to IIJA.Airports@faa.gov. For FAA FY2023 Supplemental Discretionary Grant (solar and eGSE projects), the process includes: preliminary data collection, design engineering, procurement, bid review and grant agreement execution, delivery and enabling projects, and installation - with cost estimates to be replaced with actual bids by May 31, 2025. For rail projects, applications are coordinated through MTA with partnerships among municipalities and stakeholders. For Federal Lands Access Program projects, applications are submitted through the Eastern Federal Lands Highway Division (EFLHD). For IFAC Grant projects, applications are submitted to FTA. For scenic byway projects, applications are coordinated through MDOT's Office of Planning and Capital Programming (OPCP).

structured_extraction.program_name: MDOT Federal Discretionary Grants and Grants Roadshow Local Opportunities
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT) provides technical assistance, resources, and partnership support to help local governments, non-profits, counties, municipalities, and other community partners identify and apply for competitive federal and state transportation grants. MDOT offers guidance on grant opportunities authorized under the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law (IIJA) and other federal programs, letters of support for project applications, grant application roadshows, and connections to university partners including the Build America Center at the University of Maryland and the National Transportation Center at Morgan State University. MDOT hosts a series of Grants Roadshow regional events to help partners identify transportation projects and submit successful grant applications, covering programs such as urban tree plantings, bike and pedestrian pathways, electric vehicle charging, safety improvements, bridges, transit-oriented development, freight rail, and more. Featured federal discretionary grant programs include: Active Transportation Infrastructure Investment Program (ATIIP), Charging and Fueling Infrastructure (CFI) Grant Program, Safe Streets and Roads for All (SS4A), Reconnecting Communities Pilot (RCP) Program, Railroad Crossing Elimination, and Promoting Resilient Operations for Transformative, Efficient, and Cost-saving Transportation (PROTECT). Nearly 33% of IIJA funding is available through competitive discretionary grants. MDOT also maintains a Federal Discretionary Grants Interactive Map Application, a mailing list for grant updates, monthly newsletters and webinars on federal opportunities, and downloadable program-specific fact sheets.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MDOT provides technical assistance to help local partners identify and apply for competitive federal and state transportation grants. Assistance includes strategic guidance matching projects to federal opportunities, grant application support, letters of support, monthly newsletters and webinars on federal opportunities, connections to university partners (Build America Center at University of Maryland and National Transportation Center at Morgan State University), potential state matching funds (case-by-case basis), and access to MDOT's Federal Discretionary Grants Interactive Map Application and mailing list for grant updates. MDOT also hosts regional Grants Roadshow workshops and events with RSVP registration, offering overview materials and program-specific fact sheets for programs such as urban tree grants, bike/pedestrian infrastructure, electric vehicle charging, safe streets, recreational trails, bikeways, transit-oriented development, freight rail, and bridge grants. Featured programs include: ATIIP ($44.5M guaranteed), CFI ($1.3B guaranteed), SS4A ($461.5M guaranteed), RCP (~$200M guaranteed), Railroad Crossing Elimination ($500M+), and PROTECT. A kick-off event recording is available online.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, municipalities, counties, non-profits, locally operated transit services, and other community partners seeking federal and state transportation funding in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Transportation infrastructure projects including transit, roads, bridges, safety improvements, urban tree planting, bike/pedestrian infrastructure, electric vehicle charging, transit-oriented development, freight rail, and related facilities; active transportation facilities; EV and alternative fueling infrastructure; roadway safety projects; railroad corridor preservation; bridge replacement, rehabilitation, and preservation; resilience improvements; also supports grant application development, project planning, and access to federal and state transportation funding opportunities
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland for local partners

Projects seeking federal discretionary grants must meet program-specific eligibility requirements

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Sean Winkler at MDOT to explore partnership opportunities or express interest in partnering. Request a letter of support via the online form linked on the program page. Subscribe to the MDOT Federal Discretionary Grants mailing list for updates. Register for 2026 Grants Roadshow Regional Events using the provided registration link. Watch federal grant webinars and consult MDOT resources for guidance on specific federal and state grant programs. Contact Allison Gost at abreitenother@mdot.maryland.gov with questions about Grants Roadshow events. For individual sub-programs, consult the relevant fact sheets and program contacts.

structured_extraction.program_description: The MDOT Fellows Internship Program introduces promising college students to Maryland's integrated transportation system. Summer interns are placed in senior-level assignments within one of MDOT's agencies. The program is offered by The Shriver Center in partnership with the Office of the Secretary of Transportation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Summer internship placements in senior-level assignments within MDOT agencies. Participants gain hands-on work experience in Maryland's transportation system.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Undergraduate college students in Maryland interested in careers in transportation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Internship placement and work experience within MDOT's integrated transportation system.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the MDOT Fellows Program page at The Shriver Center (publicservicescholars.umbc.edu/mdot/) for application details.

structured_extraction.program_description: The MDOT Freight Rail Grant Program (FRGP) is a state-funded, competitive, reimbursable grant program administered by the Office of Rail and Intermodal Freight (RIF) of the Secretary's Office at MDOT. The program offers state grant assistance to local jurisdictions, railroads, businesses and commercial interests, and other key agencies to help preserve railroad corridors, support economic development, and foster sustainability and innovative technologies in Maryland's freight rail network. The program is designed to make targeted investments that allow MDOT to better leverage existing infrastructure, assets, and funding programs, and to help create a better pipeline of projects that address departmental goals of supporting a safe, secure, and resilient multimodal freight network.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursable state grants awarded on a competitive basis to support freight rail infrastructure investments. Recipients pay for costs upfront and are reimbursed by the state. A minimum 20% local cash match is required (80% grant / 20% match). Funds support design projects (feasibility assessments, design plans, economic benefits analysis, environmental impact assessment) and construction projects (rail corridor improvements including sidings/sidetracks, grade crossings, bridges/structures, drainage improvements, and innovative technology implementation). Design may be funded as a component of a construction award. Funds may not be used for routine maintenance. Specific maximum award amounts are not stated on the program page.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 1 – June 30 annually (anticipated April 1 – June 30, 2026 for current cycle)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments (counties, municipalities/towns), Maryland state agencies, Metropolitan Planning Organizations (MPOs), railroad operators and owners, railroad-served businesses, commercial and industrial entities, and non-profit organizations involved in freight rail in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Design projects: completion of design plans, feasibility assessments, economic benefits analysis, environmental impact assessment. Construction projects: rail corridor improvements including sidings/sidetracks, eligible grade crossings, bridges/structures, drainage improvements, industrial/commercial site development for rail access, safety improvements (fencing, signage, walkways), infrastructure modernization and retrofitting, freight mode shift improvements (truck to rail conversion), innovative technology implementation, system preservation, and environmental protection/carbon reduction. Also supports inactive infrastructure preservation and rehabilitation.

Application resources including a list of application questions, a guidance document, a project readiness checklist, and FAQs are available on the program page. Project ideas can be discussed with MDOT staff prior to application.

structured_extraction.program_name: MDOT Solar Program (Renewable Energy Master Contract)
structured_extraction.program_description: MDOT's Renewable Energy Master Contract allows the Maryland Department of Transportation and eligible outside entities to install solar photovoltaic (PV) systems on MDOT properties across Maryland. Six pre-selected master contractors compete through secondary bidding to install, own, operate, and maintain solar PV systems on MDOT sites for 20–25 years. MDOT purchases the generated power at a fixed rate without spending capital funds. MDOT may also receive land lease/license payments, Solar Renewable Energy Credits (SRECs), or a combination of benefits depending on the site arrangement. Early buyout is allowed after the 5th year of the task order. Maryland counties, municipalities, state instrumentalities, other government agencies, and nonprofit 501(c)(3) organizations can also use the contract to purchase solar installation services from the selected Master Contractors.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Six pre-selected Master Contractors compete through secondary bidding (Task Order Requests) to install solar PV systems on MDOT properties and eligible partner sites. The contractor constructs, owns, operates, and maintains the system for 20–25 years. MDOT and eligible partners pay only for the electricity generated at a fixed rate — no upfront capital cost. MDOT may also receive land lease/license payments, Solar Renewable Energy Credits (SRECs), or a combination of benefits depending on the site arrangement. Task orders are issued per site or bundled sites, with a 20-year term and one optional 5-year extension. Early buyout is allowed after the 5th year of the task order.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland state agencies, counties, municipalities, state instrumentalities, other government agencies, and 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations seeking to install solar photovoltaic systems on their properties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation, operation, and maintenance of solar photovoltaic systems on eligible properties; purchase of solar-generated electricity at a fixed rate below current utility prices.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to MDOT properties and eligible Maryland counties, municipalities, state instrumentalities, government agencies, and 501(c)(3) nonprofits.
requirements_list: Eligible purchasers include Maryland counties, municipalities, state instrumentalities, other non-State of Maryland governments or government agencies, and 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations within Maryland.
Purchases by non-State entities are separate agreements between the contractor and that entity, and are not binding on the State of Maryland.
Minimum site size target is one acre (approximately 250 kW capacity); four or more acres preferred.

structured_extraction.program_description: A community tree planting grant program created by Maryland statute (Transportation §2–103.8) from the 2021 legislative session, run in partnership between the Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT) and the Department of Natural Resources, with oversight from the Maryland Urban and Community Forestry Committee (MUCFC). The program funds tree replanting in communities that have lost tree canopy due to transportation infrastructure and construction projects. Priority is given to communities affected by the Purple Line construction, urban heat islands, or environmental justice concerns. The program supports the Maryland Five Million Trees initiative and MDOT's environmental goals. Replanting may occur on public or private property, subject to project approval. Applications are accepted year-round and reviewed twice a year — by February 15 for spring planting and by July 15 for fall planting. Planted tree species must be native to the area, and projects with matching funds or in-kind support receive preference.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $5,000 for tree planting projects, with additional funds available for pocket forest projects based on scope. Funds can be used for tree and plant material, supplies, signage, and project maintenance costs (watering, weeding, mulching) — up to 1 year for standard planting projects and up to 3 years for Pocket Forest projects. Up to 5% of the grant may be used for volunteer outreach, signs, or project promotion. Replanting may occur on public or private property, subject to project approval. Applications are reviewed twice a year — by February 15 for spring planting and by July 15 for fall planting (4:30 p.m. deadline). Funds cannot be used for required mitigation planting.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: February 15 (Spring Planting) and July 15 (Fall Planting) by 4:30 p.m., recurring annually
structured_extraction.program_audience: Communities, municipalities, organizations, schools, businesses, property owners, non-profits, community groups, higher education institutions, and local governments in areas where tree canopy was lost due to transportation infrastructure or construction projects, including those impacted by the Purple Line, urban heat islands, or environmental justice concerns.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchasing and planting trees on public or private property in areas impacted by transportation infrastructure projects, including standard planting projects and pocket forest projects. Funds may also cover project maintenance costs like watering, weeding, and mulching (up to 1 year for standard projects; up to 3 years for Pocket Forests). Up to 5% of the grant can pay for volunteer outreach, signs, or project promotion. Funds cannot be used for required mitigation planting.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland in communities that have lost trees due to transportation construction projects, including areas affected by the Purple Line construction, urban heat islands, or environmental justice concerns. Projects must be in communities where a state transportation project removed trees. Eligible areas must have an urban population of at least 2,500 people.

Eligible areas include communities impacted by the Purple Line construction, urban heat islands, or environmental justice concerns

Funding cannot be used for required mitigation planting

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online year-round through the MDOT UTP Application form at onestop.md.gov. First, get your project approved by your county Forestry Board. Then submit an application through the Maryland OneStop system before the deadline. Applications are reviewed twice a year — by February 15 (4:30 p.m.) for spring planting and by July 15 (4:30 p.m.) for fall planting. Your application must include a site plan, a photo of the site, a list of proposed native plants, any required permit information, and a maintenance plan. Additional application materials are available via the DNR grant application PDF (https://dnr.maryland.gov/forests/Documents/MDOTUrbanTreeprogramGrantApplication.pdf). Contact Allison Gost for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Highway Safety Office (MHSO) Safety Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: MHSO Safety Grants fund behavioral safety projects and initiatives that improve traffic safety in Maryland, including Safe Routes to School-related activities. The grants support education, engagement, and enforcement efforts targeting behaviors that cause crashes, such as impaired driving, distracted driving, speeding and aggressive driving, and lack of occupant protection. The program also supports the safety of pedestrians, bicyclists, motorcyclists, young drivers, and older drivers. Funds are aligned with the Maryland Strategic Highway Safety Plan and NHTSA proven countermeasures. All funds are 100% reimbursable.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 100% reimbursable grants for behavioral safety pilot projects, safety campaigns, educational materials, and NHTSA-proven countermeasures. Funding supports projects directly related to Safe Routes to School initiatives, the Maryland Strategic Highway Safety Plan, impaired driving prevention, distracted driving prevention, speeding and aggressive driving prevention, occupant protection, and the safety of pedestrians, bicyclists, motorcyclists, young drivers, and older drivers. Applicants must spend funds first and are then reimbursed.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Government agencies, non-profits, colleges, universities, and other organizations seeking to improve traffic safety behavior through education, engagement, and enforcement, particularly related to school-aged children, Safe Routes to School, and highway safety priorities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Behavioral safety pilot projects, safety projects related to the Maryland Strategic Highway Safety Plan, safety campaigns, educational materials, and NHTSA-proven countermeasures. Includes projects focused on preventing impaired driving, distracted driving, speeding, and aggressive driving, as well as promoting seat belt use and the safety of pedestrians, bicyclists, motorcyclists, young drivers, and older drivers.

structured_extraction.program_description: MDOT's new process for evaluating and ranking surface transportation capacity-enhancing projects that request state funding in the Consolidated Transportation Program (CTP). The process uses data-driven, performance-based scoring every two years to produce a ranked list of submitted projects for potential inclusion in the CTP. Projects are evaluated across six goal areas: Safety, Accessibility & Mobility, Climate Change & Environment, Social Equity, Economic Competitiveness, and Sustainable Land Use/Demand Management, using 11 quantitative measures. A no-funding pilot round was conducted in 2025 to test the system before full legislative implementation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State funding and state-controlled federal funding for surface transportation capacity-enhancing projects. State funding request must be at least $5 million and less than $400 million per project. Eligible project types include highway capacity projects, transit capacity projects, bike/pedestrian capacity projects, intercity passenger/commuter rail capacity projects, and intelligent transportation systems projects. Projects are scored and ranked using a Score-Cost Ratio methodology for potential inclusion in the CTP. The amount of available funding is determined by the MDOT Secretary after core needs (maintenance, operations, debt service, State of Good Repair) are funded.
structured_extraction.program_audience: County governments, municipal governments, state government agencies, independent cities, Metropolitan Planning Organizations (MPOs), and Locally Operated Transit Systems (LOTS) seeking state funding for surface transportation capacity-enhancing projects located on or providing benefits to the Maryland state transportation system.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Surface transportation capacity-enhancing projects located on or providing benefits to the state transportation system, including highway capacity projects (new roadways, bridges, interchanges, auxiliary lanes), transit capacity projects (new routes, route expansion, new stations), bike/pedestrian capacity projects, intercity passenger/commuter rail capacity projects, and intelligent transportation systems projects. State funding request must be at least $5 million and less than $400 million.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located on or operate on the Maryland state transportation system, or provide benefits to the state system. All 23 Maryland counties and Baltimore City are eligible.

Endorsement letter from proposing entity leadership (using MDOT template)

Applicant authorization attestation confirming accuracy of information

structured_extraction.program_name: RAISE Grant Program (2022) – Baltimore Penn Station Connections
structured_extraction.program_description: Federal RAISE grant awarded to MDOT MTA for construction of multi-modal transit station access improvements at Baltimore Penn Station. The project comprises four coordinated components: transit priority treatments, bus stop amenities, curbside management, and bicycle/pedestrian connectivity. Improvements include dedicated bus lanes, curb extensions, bicycle and pedestrian connectivity investments, public plaza improvements, bus stop improvements, signal adjustments, crosswalk improvements, bridge railing replacement, kiosks, and secure bicycle parking. Supports anticipated growth in transit ridership and revitalization of a federally-designated Opportunity Zone.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: $6 million in federal RAISE grant funds (50% of $12 million total project cost) for multimodal transit station access improvements. structured_extraction.program_name: Ride Together Rewards: CharmPass Free Transit Incentive (New Rider)
structured_extraction.program_description: During select promotional periods, new transit riders in the Greater Baltimore area can download the CharmPass mobile app and receive free transit passes loaded directly to their account. As part of the broader Ride Together Rewards initiative, Baltimore-area commuters can also explore sustainable commuting options including vanpools (saving approximately $500 per month) and carpools (earning a $5 daily incentive for up to 90 days). New transit riders can receive free CharmPass transit passes during select promotional periods (May 1–8, June 1–8, and July 1–8, 2026).

Additionally, as part of Ride Together Rewards, vanpool participants save approximately $500 per month, and carpoolers earn a $5 daily incentive for up to 90 days.

structured_extraction.program_description: MDOT launched this pilot program in 2024 to expand Safe Routes to School (SRTS) delivery across Maryland. Under the program, Transportation Alternatives Program (TAP) federal funds are allocated to local jurisdictions to cover 80% of the salary for a local SRTS coordinator. These coordinators lead SRTS strategies, work directly with schools, manage programming, and prioritize safety infrastructure improvements around local schools. The program implements the '5 E's' framework (Education, Encouragement, Engineering, Enforcement, Evaluation) and provides toolkit and resources for schools to develop individualized SRTS plans. It focuses on getting K-12 students to and from school safely by walking, biking, or rolling, with priority emphasis on underserved, low-income, and minority populations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: TAP federal funds cover 80% of the salary for a local SRTS coordinator hired by the local jurisdiction. The jurisdiction is responsible for the remaining 20% of the coordinator's salary. As of 2026, four counties have joined the pilot. Additional assistance includes technical assistance for walking audits, development of SRTS School Action Plans, infrastructure project support (sidewalks, crosswalks, bike lanes within ~2 miles of schools), non-infrastructure activities (education, outreach, encouragement, community engagement, policy development), and connection to resources and grant opportunities including MHSO Safety Grants (applications typically January–February annually) and TAP SRTS funding (spring annual announcement).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: TAP SRTS: Spring (yearly announcement); MHSO Safety Grants: January to February (annually)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local jurisdictions (counties and municipalities) seeking to hire a dedicated Safe Routes to School coordinator; K-12 students, parents, families, school staff and administrators, community members, transportation safety advocates, public health and planning professionals; priority emphasis on underserved, low-income, and minority populations
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Covers 80% of the salary for a local SRTS coordinator who leads SRTS strategies, works with schools, manages programming, and prioritizes infrastructure improvements. Funds may also support: walking audits and SRTS School Action Plans, infrastructure improvements (sidewalks, crosswalks, bike lanes, traffic calming within ~2 miles of schools), educational materials and safety campaigns, community events and awareness campaigns, volunteer recruitment and training, helmets and safety equipment, student ambassador programs, and stakeholder engagement.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland; local jurisdictions across the state are eligible to participate. Infrastructure projects must generally be within approximately 2 miles of a school.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local jurisdiction, school, LEA, or eligible community/non-profit organization
Local jurisdiction must provide 20% match (cash or in-kind) for TAP SRTS projects
Coordinator must lead SRTS strategies and work directly with schools
School must have an identified SRTS champion
Completion of walking audit
Participation from school staff and stakeholders
Development of a customized SRTS action plan
Complete scope of work and detailed project documentation required for grant applications
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Meg Young, Deputy Director of the Office of Active Transportation and Micromobility, at mdot.activetransportation@maryland.gov for information about joining the pilot program. TAP SRTS grant applications are announced each spring; MHSO Safety Grants applications are accepted January–February annually.

TAP covers 80% of eligible project costs and requires a 20% local match.

Eligible projects include feasibility studies, design, construction, and safety awareness and program coordination related to Safe Routes to School.

structured_extraction.program_name: Safe Streets and Roads for All (SS4A)
structured_extraction.program_description: The U.S. Department of Transportation (USDOT) Safe Streets and Roads for All (SS4A) program provides competitive grants to local, regional, and Tribal communities to support comprehensive efforts aimed at reducing roadway fatalities and serious injuries for all users, including pedestrians, bicyclists, transit riders, and motorists. The program funds three main activity types: (1) Safety Action Plan development and enhancement, (2) supplemental planning and demonstration activities, and (3) implementation of safety projects and strategies identified through approved Safety Action Plans. Implementation grants support construction of projects, operational strategies, and project feasibility/design/development. Planning grants support development or update of Safety Action Plans, road safety audits, and demonstration activities such as quick-build feasibility studies, MUTCD engineering studies, pilot behavior/operational programs, and innovative technology pilots (e.g., speed cameras, adaptive signal timing). The program emphasizes data-driven, systemwide Safe System Approaches, equitable investments, and scalable solutions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants for development and enhancement of safety action plans, supplemental planning and demonstration initiatives, and implementation of projects and strategies identified through those plans. Implementation grants fund construction of projects, operational strategies, and project design/development. Planning grants fund Safety Action Plan creation or updates, road safety audits, and demonstration activities. Emphasizes data-driven, systemwide Safe System Approach with focus on improving safety outcomes, advancing equitable investments, and supporting innovative, scalable solutions.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local, regional, and Tribal communities of varying sizes — including county governments, municipalities/towns, non-profit organizations, and state/regional entities — seeking to reduce roadway fatalities and serious injuries through comprehensive safety approaches.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Development and enhancement of safety action plans, supplemental planning and demonstration activities, and implementation of safety projects and strategies. Planning grants support Safety Action Plan development/updates, road safety audits, and demonstration activities (quick-build feasibility studies, MUTCD engineering studies, pilot safety programs, innovative technology pilots). Implementation grants fund construction projects, operational strategies, and project design/development identified in an approved Safety Action Plan.
requirements_list: Must use data-driven, systemwide approaches grounded in the Safe System Approach
Projects must focus on reducing roadway fatalities and serious injuries
Implementation grants require an approved Safety Action Plan
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply by May 26, 2026 via Grants.gov. Informational webinars offered: Action Plans on April 9, 1:30–3:00 PM ET; Supplemental Planning and Demonstration Activities on April 14, 1:30–3:00 PM ET. Additional program details available at the MDOT TSO page.

structured_extraction.program_description: A race- and gender-neutral program administered by MDOT's Office of Minority Business Enterprise (OMBE). It certifies small businesses that meet U.S. Small Business Administration size standards and U.S. Department of Transportation (USDOT) eligibility requirements, allowing them to participate in USDOT-assisted contracts and be counted toward small business participation goals on federally-aided transportation projects with MDOT State Highway Administration (SHA), MDOT Maryland Transit Administration (MTA), and MDOT Maryland Aviation Administration (MAA). Certified firms appear in the MDOT online directory. Firms currently certified as MDOT Disadvantaged Business Enterprises (DBE) are automatically certified as SBE.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free certification that qualifies small businesses to participate in USDOT-assisted contracts and be counted toward small business participation goals on federally-aided projects with MDOT SHA, MTA, and MAA. Certified firms are listed in the MDOT online directory. Firms currently certified as MDOT DBE are automatically certified as SBE. All others must apply. Certified firms must annually submit an affidavit confirming continued eligibility. MDOT also offers free Application Assistance Workshops to help applicants through the process. Firm's average gross receipts cannot exceed $30.72 million (USDOT size standard). Eligible business structures include Sole Proprietorship, LLC, LLP, Corporation, and Partnership. Firm must have a street address in Maryland (no P.O. boxes).
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit small businesses (including sole proprietorships, LLCs, LLPs, corporations, and partnerships) seeking to participate in USDOT-assisted contracts and federally-aided transportation projects in Maryland that meet SBA size standards, have average annual gross receipts below $30.72 million over the previous three fiscal years, are at least 51% owned by individuals with a personal net worth (PNW) under $2,047,000, and whose majority owner is a U.S. citizen or permanent resident. Also open to socially and economically disadvantaged owners (SEDO).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Certification to participate in USDOT-assisted contracts and federally-aided projects with MDOT SHA, MTA, and MAA as prime contractors; inclusion in the MDOT online certified firm directory; eligibility to be counted toward small business participation goals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland for federally-aided projects with MDOT SHA, MTA, and MAA. Firm must have a street address in Maryland (no P.O. boxes).
requirements_list: Must be a for-profit firm organized for profit (Sole Proprietorship, LLC, LLP, Corporation, or Partnership).
Must meet SBA small business size standards under 13 CFR Part 121 applicable to the type of work performed.
Average annual gross receipts (averaged over the previous three fiscal years) must not exceed limits set in 49 CFR 26.65 or the overall USDOT cap of $30.72 million.
At least 51% of the firm must be owned by individuals whose personal net worth (PNW) does not exceed $2,047,000 as prescribed by 49 CFR 26.67.
The 51% owner must be a U.S. citizen or lawfully admitted permanent resident.
Firm must have a street address in Maryland (no P.O. boxes).
Must submit a complete application with all required supporting documentation in PDF format, unredacted.
Must provide 6-digit NAICS codes for all requested business classifications.
Must annually submit an affidavit affirming continued eligibility.
Completed SBE certification application with all owner information and NAICS codes.
U.S. citizenship proof and photo ID.

Contact OMBE at 410-865-1269 or [email protected] with any questions.

structured_extraction.program_description: Federal NHTSA grant to Maryland State Police and MDOT to improve statewide crash data collection and reporting systems, including modernizing the Automated Crash Reporting System (ACRS), integrating multiple data sources (EMS, vehicle records, court data, drug/alcohol test results, supplemental investigation materials), establishing data quality assurance dashboards, implementing timeliness metrics, and developing training programs for law enforcement on crash data collection.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) Designation Program gives state recognition to local jurisdictions that have made deliberate plans to advance TOD at eligible sites near transit stations. Receiving a designation unlocks access to state financial support, including MDOT's TOD Capital Grant and Revolving Loan Fund, and provides other competitive advantages for housing tax credits and state office leasing decisions. The program is supported by TOD Design Guidelines developed by MDOT MTA that provide a framework for determining TOD Place Types and design standards across six primary elements: Transit Station and Infrastructure, Public Open Spaces, Land Uses, Network Connectivity, Parking for All Modes, and Wayfinding.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides state recognition (designation) to qualifying TOD sites. Designation makes a jurisdiction eligible to apply for MDOT's TOD Capital Grant and Revolving Loan Fund, earns additional points in the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development's Low Income Housing Tax Credit competitive rounds, and gives priority consideration in state office leasing evaluations. MDOT also provides planning support, design guidance, and advocacy. Technical assistance includes TOD Design Guidelines covering best practices for station infrastructure, public open spaces, land uses, network connectivity, parking for all modes, and wayfinding across four TOD Place Types: Downtown Urban, Urban Neighborhood, Town/Suburban/Employment Center, and Village Center/Rural Town.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local jurisdictions and multicounty agencies with land use and planning authority that want to advance transit-oriented development near existing or planned transit stations. Also relevant to developers, transit planners, and community stakeholders involved in TOD projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: State recognition that unlocks eligibility for TOD Capital Grants, Revolving Loan Funds, housing tax credit scoring bonuses, and state leasing preferences. Technical guidance supports land assembly, planning and feasibility studies, infrastructure design and development, public open space creation, and station area improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to local governments in Maryland with eligible sites adjacent to or within one-half mile of a planned or existing transit station. TOD Design Guidelines apply to areas near MDOT MTA transit stations throughout Maryland, with applicability varying by TOD Place Type designation.
requirements_list: Site must be adjacent to or within one-half mile of a planned or existing transit station, or adjacent to a planned or existing transit corridor
Applicant must be a local government or multicounty agency with land use and planning responsibility
Local legislative body must adopt a resolution supporting the designation

Applicant must demonstrate a deliberate TOD plan addressing eight categories: Land Use, Bike/Pedestrian/Complete Streets, Housing, Action Plan, Parking, Transportation Network, Cohesion with regional plans, Green Infrastructure, and Economic Development
Designation is awarded by the Smart Growth Subcabinet based on MDOT's recommendation
Must align with one of four TOD Place Types: Downtown Urban, Urban Neighborhood, Town/Suburban/Employment Center, or Village Center/Rural Town
Must adhere to design guidelines for station infrastructure, public spaces, land uses, connectivity, parking, and wayfinding
Mixed-use development with density appropriate to place type (e.g., 60 du/acre for Downtown Urban; 40 du/acre for Urban Neighborhood)
Pedestrian and bicycle access prioritization; block perimeters no greater than 2,400 feet
Active ground floor uses on primary streets
ADA compliance required
Kiss-and-ride placement within 800 feet of primary station entrance where applicable
Compliance with Manual of Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD) and MDOT MTA design and construction standards
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The local jurisdiction develops a deliberate TOD plan or strategy and has its legislative body adopt a resolution. The jurisdiction then submits an application to MDOT via the online TOD Designation Application Form. MDOT circulates the plan to relevant transit modes and Smart Growth Subcabinet (SGSC) members, resolves any issues with the applicant, and prepares a recommendation. The SGSC then deliberates and issues a resolution approving or denying designation.

structured_extraction.program_name: Strengthening Mobility and Revolutionizing Transportation (SMART) Stage 1 – Work Zone Speed Management (2023)
structured_extraction.program_description: Federal USDOT SMART grant awarded to MDOT State Highway Administration (SHA) to develop a real-time work zone speed management program using drone data, roadside sensors, and probe vehicles to implement Variable Speed Limits (VSLs) and improve safety and traffic efficiency near construction zones. The program investigates the integration of drone-informed data and VSLs to dynamically manage speeds in work zones, with Stage 1 focused on I-695 in Baltimore City and Stage 2 intended for statewide deployment.

Budget includes $350,000 to University of Maryland and $1,260,000 for contracted services.

structured_extraction.program_name: Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) Capital Grant and Revolving Loan Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: The Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) Capital Grant and Revolving Loan Fund provides financial assistance to local jurisdictions and development partners to support equitable and inclusive development at State-designated TOD sites in Maryland. Established under the Equitable and Inclusive Transit-Oriented Development Enhancement Act, the fund has $5 million allocated in its first year and must maintain that balance as a minimum going forward, with FY25 funding coming from the Transportation Trust Fund. Financial assistance can support design plans, public infrastructure improvements, or gap funding for development within eligible State-designated TOD areas that advance the TOD goals established in the relevant designation.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants and revolving loans are available to local jurisdictions and development partners. The fund has $5 million allocated in its first year and must maintain that balance as a minimum going forward, with FY25 funding from the Transportation Trust Fund. Local jurisdictions applying for a grant must commit a 10% match. Loan candidates must demonstrate ability to repay. Grants and loans can support design plans, public infrastructure improvements, or gap funding for development within an eligible State-designated TOD site. Specific amounts and terms are detailed in the Notice of Funding Opportunity.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Currently closed; additional rounds anticipated later this year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local jurisdictions (counties and municipalities) and development partners (with local jurisdiction as co-applicant) at State-designated TOD sites in Maryland. Private entities and nonprofits may partner with local jurisdictions for gap funding applications. Priority focus on low-income and minority residents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Design plans, public infrastructure improvements, and gap funding for equitable and inclusive development within an eligible State-designated TOD site that advances the TOD goals established in the relevant designation. Eligible uses include transit-supportive land use designations, Complete Streets improvements, design and construction enhancements to TOD, and infrastructure supporting transit access.

Refer to the MD Designated TOD Map for eligibility.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Section 5310 Program – Enhanced Mobility for Seniors and Individuals with Disabilities Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Section 5310 Program, formally known as the Enhanced Mobility of Seniors and Individuals with Disabilities Program, is funded by the Federal Transit Administration (FTA) and administered statewide by the Maryland Department of Transportation Maryland Transit Administration (MDOT MTA). In Western Maryland, the Tri-County Council for Western Maryland serves as the Regional Coordinating Body, disbursing FTA funds to eligible applicants in Garrett, Allegany, Washington, and rural Frederick Counties under both the 5310 Enhanced Mobility program and the Senior Rides program. The program is designed to improve mobility for older adults and individuals with disabilities by supporting transportation services that go beyond the scope of traditional public transit. Eligible applicants include private nonprofit organizations, state or local government authorities, and public transit agencies. Projects must be derived from the regional coordinated public transit-human services transportation plan and consistent with the regionally adopted long-range transportation plan. Federal cost share requirements apply: capital projects are funded at 80% federal and 20% local match, while operating projects are funded at 50% federal and 50% local match. The Tri-County Council also provides technical assistance to applicants and coordinates the local review committee that scores and forwards applications to MTA.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Transportation Maryland Transit Administration (MDOT MTA) / Tri-County Council for Western Maryland
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants cover 80% of the cost for capital projects (e.g., accessible vehicles, technology, wheelchair lifts, communication equipment, vehicle maintenance, computer hardware/software) and 50% of the cost for operating projects (e.g., accessible taxi, ride-sharing, vanpooling, voucher programs, volunteer driver programs). Applicants must provide a local cash match of 20% for capital and 50% for operating expenses. The Tri-County Council for Western Maryland also provides technical assistance to applicants in Western Maryland applying for transportation-related grants.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations providing transportation services to seniors and individuals with disabilities, including nonprofit organizations, government entities, and public transit agencies statewide; and specifically organizations serving seniors and individuals with disabilities in Western Maryland (Garrett, Allegany, Washington, and rural Frederick Counties).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can pay for capital and operating expenses. Capital expenses include buses, vans, communication equipment, wheelchair lifts, vehicle maintenance, and computer hardware or software, as well as mobility management programs. Operating expenses include costs for accessible taxi services, ride-sharing, vanpooling, voucher programs, volunteer driver programs, dialysis trips, medical transportation, and access to jobs for 2nd and 3rd shift workers. All projects must be consistent with the regional coordinated public transit-human services transportation plan.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; Western Maryland applicants (Garrett, Allegany, Washington Counties, and rural parts of Frederick County) apply through the Tri-County Council for Western Maryland as the Regional Coordinating Body.
requirements_list: Applicants must provide a cash match of 20% for capital projects and 50% for operating projects.
Services cannot compete with existing public transit or private for-profit providers.
Applicants must follow federal rules, including Title VI of the Civil Rights Act and the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA).
Projects must be derived from the coordinated public transit-human services transportation plan for the region.
Projects must be consistent with the regionally adopted long-range transportation plan.
Applicants must demonstrate coordination with other transportation and human service providers.
Applicants must demonstrate financial and managerial capacity to manage federal funds.
Vehicles or equipment purchased must be maintained in compliance with FTA guidelines.
In Western Maryland, applications are reviewed, scored, and forwarded to MTA by the local review committee coordinated by the Tri-County Council.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants obtain the application package from the Transportation Association of Maryland (TAM) website. Applications must be submitted electronically through the MDOT MTA Grant Application Portal; paper submissions by mail or delivery are not accepted. In Western Maryland, applicants submit the MTA 5310 Application or MTA Senior Rides Application to the Tri-County Council for Western Maryland, which coordinates a local review committee that reviews, scores, and forwards applications to MTA for final consideration.
