structured_extraction.program_description: Charlotte Hall Veterans Home provides assisted living and skilled nursing care to eligible Maryland veterans and certain non-veteran spouses. Located in St. Mary's County on 126 acres, the facility offers a 126-bed assisted living program, a 318-bed skilled nursing program, and memory care. Residents receive a wide range of on-site services including medical care, therapy, dental, pharmacy, and activities. The State of Maryland subsidizes the cost of care beyond what the veteran's income and VA per diem covers.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Veterans and Military Families
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Veterans receive a per diem subsidy from the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs: $148.71/day ($4,535.66/month) for nursing home care and $64.19/day ($1,957.80/month) for assisted living care (rates as of October 1, 2025). Veterans rated 70% or greater service-connected disability may be entitled to the full cost of nursing home care. For assisted living, veterans pay 90% of their monthly net income (up to the full monthly cost), and the balance after the VA per diem credit is subsidized by the State of Maryland. Nursing home costs are covered through personal resources, long-term care insurance, Medicare, and Medicaid where eligible.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland veterans who served on active duty and were discharged under honorable conditions, certain reserve component members, and certain non-veteran spouses of eligible veterans. Applicants must be Maryland residents, at least 62 years of age or deemed disabled by the Social Security Administration or U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Residential assisted living or skilled nursing care, including medical services, therapy, memory care, and on-site amenities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Maryland resident.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland veteran who served on full-time active duty (other than active duty for training) and was discharged or released under honorable conditions
Certain reserve component members meeting legal residence requirements are also eligible
Non-veteran spouses of eligible veterans may be admitted to assisted living (paying full cost of care)
Must be a Maryland resident
Must be at least 62 years of age or deemed disabled by the Social Security Administration or U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Call 301-884-8171 Ext. 5112 to make an appointment with the Veterans Service Officer (VSO), Nicole Watson, who assists with VA documents and benefits review. 2. Complete the application form (PDF available at charhall.org/content/admissions). 3. Email the completed application to Amanda Hanbury or mail it to Charlotte Hall Veterans Home, Attn: Admissions, 29449 Charlotte Hall Road, Charlotte Hall, Maryland 20622.

structured_extraction.program_name: Commercial Driver's License Skills Test Waiver
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA) waives the driver skills test required to obtain a Class A or B Commercial Driver's License (CDL) for recently discharged service members who qualify.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Veterans and Military Families
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible recently discharged service members can have the CDL driver skills test waived. Applicants must have 2 years of military driving experience verified by their Commanding Officer and must pass the CDL knowledge test.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Recently discharged military service members seeking a Class A or B Commercial Driver's License in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Waiver of the driver skills test required to obtain a CDL.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a recently discharged service member
Must have 2 years of military driving experience
Military driving experience must be verified by Commanding Officer
Must pass the CDL knowledge test
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Maryland Motor Vehicle Administration. See the MVA website for details.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Veterans and Military Families (DVMF) Service and Benefits Program helps veterans, service members, and their families understand and apply for benefits they have earned. VA-accredited Benefits Specialists provide free, in-person support to help people file claims with the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), the Department of Defense, the State of Maryland, and other veteran-serving programs.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Veterans and Military Families
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free in-person assistance from VA-accredited Benefits Specialists at service offices across Maryland. Specialists help with military discharge document review, VA system review (healthcare, benefits, cemeteries), DVMF program review, and disability compensation or pension claim submission. No fees are charged to veterans for this service.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Veterans, active-duty service members, dependents, and survivors seeking VA benefits, Department of Defense benefits, State of Maryland benefits, or other veteran-serving benefits.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Technical assistance to support filing benefit claims — not a direct financial award.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Service offices are located across Maryland, including Baltimore, Annapolis, Bel Air, Capitol Heights, Charlotte Hall, Cumberland, Easton, Elkton, Frederick, Gaithersburg, Glen Burnie, Hagerstown, Laurel, Rosedale, Salisbury, and Waldorf.
requirements_list: Must be a veteran, active-duty service member, dependent, or survivor
Must make an appointment at a DVMF Service Office
Offices are open Monday–Friday, 8:00am–4:00pm, by appointment only
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Find a DVMF Service Office near you and call that office directly to make an appointment. During the appointment, a VA-accredited Benefits Specialist will review your documents and assist with claim submission.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Insurance Administration reimburses veterans for the costs of approved licensing and certification tests required to become a Maryland insurance producer.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Veterans and Military Families
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement of costs for approved licensing and certification exams required to obtain a Maryland insurance producer license.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Veterans seeking to become licensed insurance producers in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reimbursement of approved licensing and certification test fees.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a veteran eligible for benefits
Must have remaining entitlement to benefits
Delimiting date must not have passed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Maryland Insurance Administration. See the MIA website for details.

structured_extraction.program_name: License Plates and Complimentary Lifetime Vehicle Registration for Disabled Veterans
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides free specialty license plates and complimentary lifetime vehicle registration to Maryland veterans with a 100% permanent and total service-connected disability rating (including those compensated at the 100% rate due to individual unemployability). Eligible veterans receive license plates (with or without the universal disability symbol), a permanent registration card, and a permanent sticker, eliminating the need for annual registration renewal.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Veterans and Military Families
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free specialty license plates (with or without the universal disability symbol) and complimentary lifetime vehicle registration for eligible Maryland veterans rated 100% disabled (permanent and total) or compensated at the 100% rate due to individual unemployability by the VA. Includes permanent registration cards and stickers, eliminating the need for annual registration renewal trips.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland resident veterans rated 100% disabled (permanent and total) or compensated at the 100% rate based on individual unemployability by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free specialty license plates and complimentary lifetime vehicle registration for qualifying disabled veteran-owned vehicles.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Maryland resident.
requirements_list: Must be a veteran who is a Maryland resident
Must be rated 100% disabled (permanent and total) or compensated at the 100% rate (individual unemployability, permanent and total) by the VA
Must have a 100% VA service-connected disability rating (permanent and total)
Eligible vehicle classes: passenger car (A), multi-purpose vehicle (M), truck with one ton or less manufacturer's rated capacity (EPO)
Must provide proof of 100% disability from the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs
If requesting plates with the universal disability symbol, must also complete the Application for Maryland Parking Placard/License Plates for Individuals with a Disability
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply in person at any full-service MVA branch, mail your application to the Specialized Tag Unit at 6601 Ritchie Highway, Glen Burnie, MD 21062, or visit an MVA-licensed tag and title service. For additional details, visit the Maryland MVA veterans page at https://mva.maryland.gov/Pages/veteran.aspx.

structured_extraction.program_name: Local Property Tax Exemptions for Veterans
structured_extraction.program_description: Some local jurisdictions in Maryland have enacted laws providing property tax exemptions for veterans. These exemptions may differ slightly from the state-level exemption. Eligibility and application requirements are set by each county. The program is available in select Maryland counties, with each county setting its own rules for amounts and eligibility criteria.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Veterans and Military Families
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property tax exemptions on real estate for qualifying veterans offered by local jurisdictions. Each county sets its own rules for amounts and eligibility, which may differ from the state-level exemption. Check your county's website to determine if you qualify.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Veterans and military families who own property in participating Maryland counties where local property tax exemption laws have been enacted.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction or exemption of local property taxes for eligible veterans.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in select Maryland counties: Anne Arundel, Baltimore County, Calvert, Cecil, Frederick, Harford, Howard, Montgomery, and Washington counties. Each county has its own eligibility criteria and application process.
requirements_list: Must be a veteran or qualifying military family member
Must own property in a participating county
Must meet each county's specific eligibility criteria — check your county's website for details
Eligibility criteria may vary by local jurisdiction
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Local property tax exemptions are regulated at the county level. Visit your county's website to learn about eligibility and how to apply. Links to each county's application information are provided on the Maryland Department of Veterans and Military Families website at https://veterans.maryland.gov/benefits-services/tax-exemptions/local-property-tax-exemptions.

structured_extraction.program_description: Older or disabled Maryland residents may subtract a portion of their taxable pension and retirement annuity income from their federal adjusted gross income before calculating Maryland state income tax.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Veterans and Military Families
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible taxpayers may subtract a portion of their taxable pension and retirement annuity income from their federal adjusted gross income. The maximum exclusion amount is described in Instruction 13 of the Maryland resident tax booklet. Traditional IRAs, Roth IRAs, SEPs, Keogh Plans, and ineligible deferred compensation plans do not qualify.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents age 65 or older, or who are totally disabled (or whose spouse is totally disabled), who receive pension or retirement annuity income from an employee retirement system.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of Maryland state income tax liability through subtraction of pension and retirement annuity income from federal adjusted gross income.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to Maryland residents.
requirements_list: Must be 65 or older or totally disabled, or spouse must be totally disabled, on the last day of the tax year
Must have included on federal return income received as a pension, annuity, or endowment from an employee retirement system
Traditional IRAs, Roth IRAs, SEPs, Keogh Plans, and ineligible deferred compensation plans do not qualify
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Follow Instruction 13 in the Maryland resident tax booklet when filing your Maryland state income tax return.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland State Veterans Cemeteries Burial Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland provides eligible veterans, National Guard members, Reservists, and their eligible dependents with burial services at one of five state veterans cemeteries located throughout Maryland. Eligible veterans and their eligible dependents receive a burial plot, grave liner, headstone, and interment services at no cost. National Guard members, reservists, and eligible dependents pay a flat fee for burial services. DVMF also assists with pre-interment planning, burial scheduling, grave assignments, and Military Funeral Honors.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Veterans and Military Families
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible veterans and their eligible dependents receive a burial plot, grave liner, headstone, and interment services at no cost. National Guard members, reservists, and eligible dependents pay a $1,002 fee that covers casketed and cremated interments, liner cost, and perpetual care. Disinterments or re-interments also cost $1,002. This fee equals the burial plot allowance provided by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs and may change annually on October 1. DVMF also assists with pre-interment planning, burial scheduling, grave assignments, and Military Funeral Honors.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Veterans, National Guard members, Reservists, and their eligible dependents who meet criteria established by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs National Cemetery Administration (NCA). National Guard members, Reservists, and their family members must also meet Maryland residency requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Burial services including plot, grave liner, headstone, and interment at a Maryland state veterans cemetery.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide at five Maryland state veterans cemeteries. National Guard members, Reservists, and their family members must meet Maryland residency requirements.
requirements_list: Must be an eligible veteran, National Guard member, reservist, or eligible dependent
Must meet eligibility criteria established by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs National Cemetery Administration (NCA)
National Guard members, Reservists, and their family members must also meet Maryland residency requirements
Veterans must have a discharge other than Dishonorable to qualify for military funeral honors
Service members who lived outside Maryland at the time of death may require additional documentation
Pre-application does not guarantee final approval; DVMF makes a final eligibility determination at time of death
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Family members or a funeral director should contact the desired Maryland State Veterans Cemetery to confirm burial eligibility and schedule a date and time. For pre-interment planning, complete the Pre-Application Interment Planning form and mail it to the desired cemetery location as indicated on the form. Contact DVMF for assistance with pre-interment planning, burial scheduling, and grave assignments.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Veterans Service Animal Program and Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides grants to Maryland-based nonprofit organizations that train service dogs or offer equine-assisted therapy for veterans, their spouses, and eligible dependents. The goal is to improve mental health and well-being, reduce suicide risk among veterans, and support outreach and education on veteran suicide prevention and military cultural competency.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Veterans and Military Families
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are awarded annually to Maryland-based 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations. Grant funds may support staff costs for veteran program services, equine care, staff development and training, equipment, supplies, and outreach and education activities. Ten organizations received grants in January 2026 for FY26.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland-based 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations that train service dogs or provide equine-assisted therapy to veterans, veteran spouses, and eligible dependents
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Staff costs for veteran program services, equine care, equine training, supplies and equipment, staff professional development and training, outreach and education on veteran suicide prevention and military cultural competency
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Organizations must be Maryland-based and serve Maryland veterans, their spouses, and eligible dependents
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland-based 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization
Must train service or support dogs for veterans OR provide equine-assisted therapy to veterans
Must serve Maryland veterans, veteran spouses, or eligible dependents
Must address the program's priority of improving mental health and reducing suicide risk in the veteran population
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations apply during the annual grant cycle. Contact the Grant Specialist for application details.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Veterans Trust Fund provides grant awards to veterans, their family members, Gold Star parents, spouses, and members of the Maryland National Guard who are in dire financial situations, as well as to private organizations that help veterans. Grants help eligible individuals overcome financial hardships such as housing, utilities, and transportation costs. The fund is supported by donations and contributions from community partners, individuals, and mandated state revenue partners.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Veterans and Military Families
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant awards funded by donations and contributions, awarded to veterans, their family members, Gold Star parents, spouses, and members of the Maryland National Guard facing dire financial hardship, as well as to private organizations that help veterans. Grants support urgent needs such as housing, utilities, and transportation. One-time grants are provided to eligible individuals to help overcome financial hardships.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Not stated; applications temporarily paused as of March 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Veterans, military families, Gold Star parents, spouses, and members of the Maryland National Guard facing financial hardship, as well as private organizations that assist veterans. Individuals outside these categories may request a waiver.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Housing, utilities, transportation, and other urgent financial needs for eligible individuals; support for private organizations that help veterans.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to Maryland veterans, their families, and organizations that assist veterans.
requirements_list: Must be a veteran, family member of a veteran, Gold Star parent, spouse, member of the Maryland National Guard, or a private organization that helps veterans
Individuals outside these categories may request a waiver during intake
Must be experiencing financial hardship or dire financial need (for individual applicants)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through the program. As of March 2026, acceptance of new applications is temporarily paused while a high volume of recent requests is processed. Updates will be posted on the program page when applications reopen.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA) offers military-related specialty license plates to eligible veterans for qualifying vehicles.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Veterans and Military Families
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Veterans can obtain military-related license plates for passenger cars, multi-purpose vehicles, motorcycles, and trucks (10,000 lbs or less) by paying a $25 application fee and submitting proof of military service.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Veterans who are Maryland residents and own eligible vehicles.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Military-themed license plates for qualifying vehicles.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Maryland resident veteran.
requirements_list: Must be a veteran
Must submit application form VR-120
Must pay $25 application fee
Must provide one of: DD-214 discharge papers, Medal Certification, or written proof from National Personnel Records Center
Eligible vehicles: passenger cars, multi-purpose vehicles, motorcycles, trucks 10,000 lbs or less
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete form VR-120 from the MVA website. Submit the form with the $25 fee and required proof of military service to the MVA.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland program that restores state veterans benefits to veterans who received other-than-honorable, General Under Honorable Conditions, or Uncharacterized discharge status due to PTSD, traumatic brain injury, military sexual trauma, sexual orientation or gender identity, or other qualifying criteria. Veterans can apply to have their discharge reviewed and state benefits restored.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Veterans and Military Families
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Restoration of state veterans benefits for veterans with other-than-honorable (OTH), General Under Honorable Conditions (GUH), or Uncharacterized (UC) discharge status who meet qualifying criteria. The DVMF Discharge Review Board reviews applications and, if approved, restores access to state veterans benefits.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland veterans with other-than-honorable, General Under Honorable Conditions, or Uncharacterized discharge status due to PTSD, traumatic brain injury, military sexual trauma, sexual orientation or gender identity, or other qualifying criteria under 38 C.F.R. § 3.12
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Restoration of state veterans benefits
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Maryland veterans statewide
requirements_list: Veteran must have an other-than-honorable (OTH), General Under Honorable Conditions (GUH), or Uncharacterized (UC) character of service
Discharge status must be due to PTSD, traumatic brain injury (TBI), military sexual trauma (MST), sexual orientation or gender identity, or other criteria established in 38 C.F.R. § 3.12
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download the fact sheet and application packet from the DVMF website, complete required documents, and mail to: Maryland Department of Veterans and Military Families, ATTN: DVMF Discharge Review Board, 16 Francis Street, 4th Floor, Annapolis, MD 21401. Free legal assistance with federal discharge upgrade applications is also available through the University of Baltimore School of Law Bob Parsons Veterans Advocacy Clinic.

structured_extraction.program_name: Retirement Pay and Pension Tax Deductions and Exclusions
structured_extraction.program_description: Veterans or spouses of military retirees who receive military retirement income may subtract a portion of that income from their federal adjusted gross income before calculating Maryland state income tax. Taxpayers age 55 or older may subtract up to $20,000 of military retirement income, while taxpayers under age 55 may subtract up to $12,500. Eligible retirement income must result from service in the U.S. Armed Forces (active or reserve), Maryland National Guard, or commissioned corps of the Public Health Service, NOAA, or Coast and Geodetic Survey.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Veterans and Military Families
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Taxpayers age 55 or older may subtract up to $20,000 of military retirement income from their federal adjusted gross income before determining Maryland tax. Taxpayers under age 55 may subtract up to $12,500. To claim the deduction, complete Maryland Form 502 and follow the instructions on line 13.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Veterans and surviving spouses of military retirees who receive military retirement income and file Maryland state income taxes.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of Maryland state income tax liability through subtraction of military retirement income from federal adjusted gross income.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to Maryland residents.
requirements_list: Must be a veteran or spouse of a military retiree receiving military retirement income

Retirement income must result from service in the U.S. Armed Forces (active or reserve), Maryland National Guard, or commissioned corps of the Public Health Service, NOAA, or Coast and Geodetic Survey
Taxpayers 55 or older on the last day of the taxable year may subtract up to $20,000
Taxpayers under 55 on the last day of the taxable year may subtract up to $12,500
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete Maryland Form 502 and follow the instructions in the Maryland resident tax booklet for line 13 when filing your Maryland state income tax return.

structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Veterans and Military Families
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants to purchase, construct, or modify a specially adapted home for veterans with a 100% (permanent and total) service-connected disability rating.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Building, purchasing, or adapting a home to accommodate a service-connected disability
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Maryland veterans; administered by the VA
requirements_list: Must have a 100% VA service-connected disability rating (permanent and total)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local Department of Veterans and Military Families (DVMF) service program office for details.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time grant for home improvements and structural alterations for eligible service-connected veterans. Requires physician referral.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home improvements and structural alterations for medical purposes

structured_extraction.program_name: VA Home Loan Funding Fee Exemption

structured_extraction.program_name: Vehicle Registration Tax Credit for Military Members
structured_extraction.program_description: An excise tax credit on vehicle titling for active duty military members and their immediate families who are new Maryland residents or returning Maryland residents.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Veterans and Military Families
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Active duty military members (or their immediate family) who are new Maryland residents must title their vehicle within 60 days. If they have not been a Maryland resident for more than one year, they receive an excise tax credit. Returning Maryland residents on active duty (or their immediate family) also receive an excise tax credit if the vehicle is titled within one year of their return. Proof of active military status is required.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Within 60 days of moving to Maryland for new residents; within one year of return for returning residents.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Active duty military members and their immediate family who are new or returning Maryland residents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of vehicle excise tax when titling a vehicle in Maryland.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be titling a vehicle in Maryland as a new or returning resident.
requirements_list: Must be an active duty military member or immediate family member
New residents must title vehicle within 60 days of moving to Maryland
Must not have been a Maryland resident for more than one year (for new residents)
Returning Maryland residents must title vehicle within one year of return
Must submit proof of active military status (military ID or equivalent)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit proof of military status along with vehicle titling paperwork at an MVA branch office within the required timeframe.

structured_extraction.program_name: Vessel Excise Tax Exemption for Active Duty Military
structured_extraction.program_description: Active duty military members stationed in Maryland are exempt from the 5% vessel excise tax for one year on vessels brought into Maryland due to a duty transfer.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Veterans and Military Families
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A one-year exemption from Maryland's 5% vessel excise tax for active duty military members serving in Maryland. The exemption applies only to vessels already registered elsewhere and brought into Maryland because of a duty transfer. New vessel purchases are not exempt.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Members of the armed forces serving on active duty in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Exemption from the 5% vessel excise tax on vessels brought into Maryland due to a military duty transfer.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be serving on active duty in Maryland. Vessel must be currently registered elsewhere and brought into Maryland due to a duty transfer.
requirements_list: Must be a member of the armed forces on active duty in Maryland
Vessel must already be registered elsewhere
Vessel must be brought into Maryland due to a duty transfer
New vessel purchases are not eligible
Exemption is valid for one year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Maryland Department of Natural Resources for information on applying for the boat registration and vessel excise tax exemption.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Veterans can have a 'veteran' designation placed on their Maryland driver's license at no stated cost by presenting qualifying discharge or status documents at a local MVA branch.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Recognition of veteran status on driver's license.

structured_extraction.program_description: Helps service-connected veterans with employment handicaps prepare for, find, and maintain suitable employment, or achieve independence in daily living.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide coordination program established in 2017 to improve services for Maryland's military-connected community. Each Maryland state government department and agency has a designated Veterans Services Specialist (VSS) or liaison who provides information on veteran-related resources and benefits to state employees with military connections and to citizens with questions about veteran benefits. Specialists connect veterans, active duty service members, National Guard and Reserve personnel, and their families to state benefits and resources across multiple agencies. When liaisons cannot resolve questions, they work with the Department of Veterans and Military Families (DVMF) Communications, Outreach, and Advocacy Program to answer questions, make referrals, and provide support for the military-connected community.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Veterans and Military Families
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Each state agency has a designated Veterans Services Specialist embedded within it who provides information, referrals, and coordination of veteran-related resources and benefits. They connect veterans, active duty service members, National Guard and Reserve personnel, and their families to state resources and benefits across multiple agencies. The DVMF Communications, Outreach, and Advocacy Program supports liaisons and handles escalated questions that cannot be resolved at the agency level, making referrals to meet the needs of the military-connected community.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Military-connected community including veterans, active duty service members, National Guard and Reserve personnel, their families and dependents, and state employees who have served or have family members who have served in the military.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Connecting military-connected individuals to veteran-related resources, benefits, information, and referrals across Maryland state government agencies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across all Maryland state government departments and agencies.

structured_extraction.program_name: Bay Restoration Fund (BRF) Financial Hardship Exemption
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides a financial hardship exemption from the Bay Restoration Fund fee (commonly called the flush tax), a state-mandated fee collected by billing authorities (water/sewer utilities and county finance offices) on behalf of the State of Maryland to fund Chesapeake Bay restoration and water quality improvement projects. At the state level, billing authorities must develop a formal exemption plan and submit it to the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) for approval. Once approved, eligible residential users who demonstrate substantial financial hardship may apply through their local billing authority to be exempt from paying the fee. The program is administered statewide by MDE, with local administration by county billing authorities. For example, Allegany County residents may apply annually through Allegany County; Talbot County taxpayers billed the Bay Restoration Fee on their real property tax bill or Talbot County Sanitary District sewer bill may apply through Talbot County's Finance Office; and Cecil County residents who meet income and benefit criteria may apply through Cecil County's Finance Department by September 1 of the applicable fiscal tax year. In Cecil County, the fee is $60 per year (billed quarterly at $15 on sewer bills or annually on property tax bills for properties with private septic systems). Exemptions are granted for up to one year, after which eligibility must be re-verified and a new application submitted.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Full exemption from the annual Bay Restoration Fee (flush tax) for eligible residential users who meet financial hardship criteria. In Cecil County, the fee is $60 per year (billed quarterly at $15 on sewer bills or annually on property tax bills for properties with private septic systems). Qualifying criteria include receiving energy assistance, public assistance (SSI, food stamps, WIC, Temporary Cash Assistance), veterans or social security disability benefits, or meeting income criteria established by the Maryland Department of Human Services. Exemptions are granted for a period not to exceed one year, after which eligibility must be re-verified. No direct funds are provided — the benefit is relief from the annual fee obligation.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: September 1 of any given fiscal tax year for Cecil County (may be extended to coincide with the Homeowners' Property Tax Credit filing deadline); varies by billing authority
structured_extraction.contact_name: Director, Maryland Water Quality Financing Administration
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential water/sewer customers and owner-occupied residential property owners experiencing substantial financial hardship, including Talbot County taxpayers billed the Bay Restoration Fee on their property tax or sewer bill, Cecil County low-income residential property owners receiving the Homeowners' Property Tax Credit, and the billing authorities (including county governments such as Allegany County, Cecil County, and Talbot County) that serve them
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Exemption from paying the Bay Restoration Fund (flush tax) fee for eligible residential users — no direct funds are provided
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland; administered locally by billing authorities. Allegany County residents may contact 301-777-5965. Talbot County taxpayers may apply through the Talbot County Finance Office. Cecil County residents may contact the Cecil County Finance Department at 410-996-5385 or tax@cecilcountymd.gov.

Must demonstrate financial hardship
Billing authority must submit a proposed financial hardship exemption plan to MDE for approval
Plan must include: proposed criteria, application procedure and forms, required supporting documentation, exemption time period and re-verification process, and estimated number of qualifying users
Individual exemptions may not exceed one year without re-verification of eligibility
Must submit a new application every year to maintain the exemption
Talbot County applicants must be billed the Bay Restoration Fee on a Real Property Tax bill or a Talbot County Sanitary District sewer bill
Must meet hardship qualifications as described in the applicable local application document
Cecil County: property owner must have applied for and received the Homeowners' Property Tax Credit for the same fiscal year
Cecil County: property owner must be receiving benefits from at least one qualifying program (energy assistance subsidy, public assistance, SSI, or Veterans Disability Benefits)
Cecil County: application must be received by September 1 of the applicable fiscal tax year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Billing authorities develop a financial hardship exemption plan and submit it to MDE (Maryland Department of the Environment, 1800 Washington Boulevard, STE 515, Baltimore, MD 21230-1718, Attn: Director, Maryland Water Quality Financing Administration) for approval. A form for preparing the proposed plan is available for download on the MDE program page. Once approved, individual residential users apply through their local billing authority. Allegany County residents may complete and submit the Bay Restoration Fund Financial Hardship Exemption Application (PDF available at https://www.alleganygov.org/201/Bay-Restoration-Flush-Tax) and must file a new application each year. Talbot County residents may download and complete the Bay Restoration Fee Hardship Application form (https://www.talbotcountymd.gov/departments/finance/uploads/File/finance/bayrestorationfeehardship2024.pdf) and submit it to the Talbot County Finance Office. structured_extraction.program_name: Bay Restoration Fund Best Available Technology (BAT) Grants for Onsite Sewage Disposal Systems
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grant funding and subsidies to upgrade conventional onsite sewage disposal (septic) systems in Maryland to Best Available Technology (BAT) for nitrogen removal, reducing nitrogen loading to the Chesapeake Bay, Atlantic Coastal Bays, and groundwater. The program approves and ranks nitrogen-removing septic system technologies in multiple classes: Class I (field-verified), Class II (currently under field verification), Class III, and Class IV combination systems. Property owners can replace or upgrade to an approved BAT system, or connect to public sewer systems. Priority is given based on whether the system is failing or non-conforming and whether it is located within the Critical Area (land within 1,000 feet of tidal waters near the Chesapeake Bay and its tributaries). The program generates an estimated $27 million per year from a $60 annual fee per onsite system user; 60% of funds go to septic upgrades and 40% go to cover crops. Over 12,000 systems have been upgraded to date. Only field-verified systems are currently funded (non-field verified systems no longer funded). Applications are currently closed and will reopen in December 2026.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants and subsidies are available through the Bay Restoration Fund to help cover the cost of installing an approved BAT nitrogen-removing onsite sewage system, the marginal cost of using BAT instead of conventional technology, or for connecting properties to public sewer systems. Grant amounts vary by applicant type and income: 100% grant for eligible homeowners with household income ≤$300,000/year; 50% grant for homeowners with household income >$300,000/year; 100% grant for non-profit entities; 75% grant for small businesses; 50% for other for-profit businesses. Low-income households may receive a 50% grant for ongoing O&M costs beyond the initial period. Maximum $25,000 per sewer connection for eligible projects. Funding covers BAT system purchase, installation, and 2 years of operations and maintenance. Upgrades are prioritized in the following order: (1) failing systems in the Critical Area, (2) failing systems outside the Critical Area, (3) non-conforming systems in the Critical Area, (4) non-conforming systems outside the Critical Area, (5) other systems in the Critical Area including new construction, (6) other systems outside the Critical Area including new construction. The fund generates approximately $27 million per year; 60% is allocated to septic system upgrades and 40% to cover crops.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland homeowners, property owners, non-profit entities, small businesses, for-profit businesses, and local governments with onsite sewage disposal (septic) systems who want to install an approved nitrogen-removing BAT system or connect to public sewer systems, with priority for failing or non-conforming systems located in Critical Areas near the Chesapeake Bay and its tributaries.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase, installation, and 2-year operation and maintenance of approved Best Available Technology (BAT) systems for removing nitrogen from onsite (septic) sewage disposal systems; connection of properties to public sewer systems for nitrogen reduction; cost difference between conventional and BAT systems for new construction; principal (but not interest) on local government debt for connections; implementation of cover crops to reduce nitrogen loading to the Chesapeake Bay and Atlantic Coastal Bays.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Properties must generally be in Priority Funding Areas or have an exception approved. Priority given to failing or non-conforming septic systems in Critical Areas (land within 1,000 feet of tidal waters near the Chesapeake Bay and its tributaries). Projects outside Priority Funding Areas require additional documentation.
requirements_list: Must be a user served by an onsite sewage disposal (septic) system in Maryland
The septic system technology must be on MDE's approved BAT list (Class I, Class II, Class III, or eligible Class IV combination)
Only field-verified systems are currently funded (non-field verified systems no longer funded)
Systems must have undergone rigorous third-party testing (e.g., NSF 245, NSF 40 Class I, CAN/BNQ 3680-600, EN 12566-3, or a peer-reviewed university field study)

Upgrades outside the Critical Area for new construction may use conventional systems under 2016 regulatory reforms, except for large systems with design flow of 5,000 gallons per day or greater which still require BAT
Properties must generally be in Priority Funding Areas or obtain an exception; septic to sewer connections must be consistent with County Water and Sewer plans
Funding covers best available technology for nitrogen removal or the marginal cost over conventional technology
RetroFast units limited to households of 1-4 occupants with 3 bedrooms or less
Program is implemented by local County Health Departments or other parties effective July 1, 2010
Applicants should contact vendors or their local County Health Department for more information about specific systems

Grant percentages vary by applicant type: 100% for homeowners (income ≤$300,000/year), 50% for homeowners (income >$300,000/year), 100% for non-profits, 75% for small businesses, 50% for other for-profit businesses

The BAT Technical Review Committee accepts applications from vendors to have systems considered as BAT and eligible for Bay Restoration Fund grants. Property owners interested in installing an approved system should contact MDE's Wastewater Permits Program / Bay Restoration Fund Program or visit the BRF Onsite Disposal Systems implementation page on the MDE website for application details.

structured_extraction.program_name: Bay Restoration Fund – Enhanced Nutrient Removal (ENR) Wastewater Treatment Plant Upgrades and Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides up to 100% grant and subsidy funding to upgrade Maryland's publicly owned wastewater treatment plants with Enhanced Nutrient Removal (ENR) technology to reduce nitrogen and phosphorus entering the Chesapeake Bay, meeting commitments under the 2000 Chesapeake Bay Agreement. The Maryland Department of the Environment uses the Bay Restoration Fund to upgrade the major wastewater treatment plants (66–67 facilities) that discharge to the Chesapeake Bay with ENR technologies, targeting effluent quality of 3 mg/l total nitrogen and 0.3 mg/l total phosphorus — achieving approximately one-third of the nutrient reduction required under the Chesapeake Bay 2000 Agreement. Eligible projects include ENR upgrades at major and minor wastewater treatment plants, combined sewer overflow (CSO) and sanitary sewer overflow (SSO) abatement, sewer rehabilitation, upgrade of existing sewerage distribution systems, incremental cost of ENR operations and maintenance, wastewater conveyance system improvements and pumping station upgrades, sewer extensions to connect homes on septic to BNR/ENR plants, nutrient-reducing shared community septic systems, MS4 stormwater projects by local governments with a stormwater or resilience enterprise fund, and flood mitigation and watershed restoration projects. The ENR Refinement Program reinvests in ENR upgrades at WWTPs that completed original upgrades 15+ years ago, encouraging comprehensive engineering evaluations to enable continued ENR operation for another 20 years and establishing a new total nitrogen goal of 2.85 mg/L to offset climate change impact. Funds are provided on a reimbursable basis after grantees submit payment requests covering planning, design, and construction costs. Non-ENR items and expansion costs may be funded through the Water Quality State Revolving Loan Fund or other federal/state grants. The program is funded by a $5.00 monthly fee ($30/year) per household or equivalent dwelling unit (EDU) collected from wastewater treatment plant users, generating approximately $100 million per year. Bonds backed by program fees may be issued to expedite implementation. The 67 major publicly owned facilities discharging to the Chesapeake Bay have funding priority; minor and other facilities may be considered on a case-by-case basis based on cost effectiveness. Starting in FY 2018, funding is first allocated to minor WWTPs for ENR upgrades after the 67 significant WWTPs complete upgrades, with remaining funds allocated by project priority ranking.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides up to 100% grant and subsidy funding for eligible wastewater and stormwater capital projects, delivered on a reimbursable basis after grantees submit payment requests for incurred eligible costs. Eligible uses include: (1) Enhanced Nutrient Removal (ENR) upgrades at major wastewater treatment plants (targeting effluent quality of 3 mg/l total nitrogen and 0.3 mg/l total phosphorus), including planning, design, and construction; (2) combined sewer overflow (CSO) and sanitary sewer overflow (SSO) abatement; (3) sewer rehabilitation; (4) upgrade of existing sewerage distribution systems (up to $5M/yr through FY 2009); (5) incremental cost of wastewater treatment plant ENR operations and maintenance (up to 10% of annual revenue or ~$6M/yr starting FY 2010); (6) wastewater conveyance system improvements and pumping station upgrades; (7) sewer extensions to connect homes on septic to BNR/ENR plants; (8) nutrient-reducing shared community septic systems; (9) MS4 stormwater projects by local governments with a stormwater or resilience enterprise fund; and (10) flood mitigation and watershed restoration projects. The ENR Refinement Program provides 100% funding for comprehensive engineering evaluations at WWTPs 15+ years post-original-upgrade, with design costs prorated based on eligibility percentage and BRF grant funding for design and construction to achieve ENR for another 20 years (new TN goal of 2.85 mg/L). For minor and other WWTPs, 100% grant funding is available for planning and design phases; construction funding is available if cost-effectiveness criteria are met (less than $150 per pound of total nitrogen reduced over 20 years). Non-ENR items and expansion costs may be funded through the Water Quality State Revolving Loan Fund or other federal/state grants. The 67 major publicly owned facilities discharging to the Chesapeake Bay have funding priority; minor and other facilities are considered on a case-by-case basis. Bonds backed by program fees may be issued to expedite implementation. Program is funded by a $30/year per equivalent dwelling unit fee, generating approximately $100 million per year.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: December 1 through January 31 annually; applications will reopen in December 2026
structured_extraction.contact_name: Zoë Goodson (drinking water projects); Gerald Gorham, Jr. (loan financing)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Publicly owned wastewater treatment plants (particularly the 66–67 major facilities with a design flow of 500,000 gallons per day or greater discharging to the Chesapeake Bay), local governments, water and sewerage authorities, community water systems, public water utilities, and wastewater treatment plant operators in Maryland seeking funding for wastewater, stormwater, and flood mitigation capital projects to benefit the Chesapeake Bay. Also includes WWTPs that completed ENR/BNR upgrades 15+ years ago seeking refinement funding.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planning, design, and construction for upgrading wastewater treatment plants with ENR technology to achieve effluent quality of 3 mg/l total nitrogen and 0.3 mg/l total phosphorus; combined sewer overflow (CSO) and sanitary sewer overflow (SSO) abatement; sewer rehabilitation; upgrade of existing sewerage distribution systems; incremental cost of ENR operations and maintenance; wastewater conveyance system improvements and pumping station upgrades; sewer extensions for septic-to-sewer connections; nutrient-reducing shared community septic systems; MS4 stormwater projects; flood mitigation and watershed restoration projects; comprehensive engineering evaluations of existing ENR systems; design and construction of ENR refinement projects to extend operational life by 20 years; drinking water system water conservation and efficiency projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland, with priority for the 67 major publicly owned facilities discharging to the Chesapeake Bay watershed. Facilities outside the Chesapeake Bay and Coastal Bay watersheds pay a lower fee. Minor and other facilities may be considered on a case-by-case basis based on cost effectiveness. Projects must be within Priority Funding Areas (PFAs) or granted PFA exceptions, or be categorically excepted/excluded.

Local government must have a system of charges through a local stormwater or resilience enterprise fund (for MS4 stormwater projects)
Projects must involve wastewater treatment plants or related sewer infrastructure in Maryland

Remaining funds are allocated by project priority ranking

The ENR Refinement Program and Cost Effectiveness Evaluation guidelines outline the process for minor and other facilities seeking funding. Contact MDE at 410-537-3908, zoe.goodson@maryland.gov (drinking water projects), or gerald.gorham@maryland.gov (loan financing) for specific application steps.

structured_extraction.program_description: BayScapes promotes environmentally sound landscaping practices that benefit people, wildlife, and the Chesapeake Bay. The program advocates a holistic approach to landscaping using principles inspired by natural environments, reducing mowing, fertilizing, and pesticide use while improving water quality and wildlife habitat.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides a series of seven homeowner's guides on BayScaping principles and access to demonstration sites. Technical guidance and outreach on low-input landscaping practices benefiting the Chesapeake Bay.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners, businesses, schools, parks, and community organizations in the Chesapeake Bay region.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Implementing low-input, wildlife-friendly landscaping to improve water quality and habitat in the Chesapeake Bay watershed.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Chesapeake Bay watershed region.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call the Chesapeake Regional Information Service at 1-800-662-CRIS for information and demonstration site locations.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides capital grant funds and low-interest loans to publicly owned wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) to help them retrofit or upgrade facilities with biological nutrient removal (BNR) technology — specifically biological nitrification and denitrification — to reduce nitrogen in treated water. The goal is to achieve an annual average effluent concentration of 8 mg/l total nitrogen. Upgrades are typically done alongside Enhanced Nutrient Removal upgrades using Bay Restoration Fund grants. Grants are provided on a 50/50 cost-share basis, with small low-income communities eligible for up to 75% grant coverage. Low-interest loans are also available to local governments to finance the local share of BNR facility implementation and other plant upgrade or expansion costs consistent with Smart Growth.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Capital grants on a 50/50 cost-share basis for eligible costs of BNR upgrades at publicly owned WWTPs. Small low-income communities may receive up to 75% grant coverage. Eligible costs include engineering and pilot studies, design, and construction. Funds are provided on a reimbursable basis after a payment request is made following incurrence of eligible costs. MDE also provides low-interest loans to local governments to finance the local share of BNR facility implementation and other plant upgrade or expansion costs consistent with Smart Growth. Other state, local, or federal funds may be used as the local match.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Funding Applications Accepted December through January Annually
structured_extraction.program_audience: Publicly owned wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) and local municipalities and agencies, including small low-income communities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Engineering and pilot studies, design, and construction costs for BNR retrofits or upgrades at publicly owned WWTPs; local governments may also use loans for other plant upgrade or expansion costs consistent with Smart Growth.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Projects must conform to Smart Growth Criteria and be consistent with the County Water and Sewer Plan.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a publicly owned wastewater treatment plant
Goal of achieving annual average effluent concentration of 8 mg/l total nitrogen
Projects must be rated and ranked through the Integrated Project Priority System (IPPS)
Projects must conform to Smart Growth Criteria
Projects must be consistent with the County Water and Sewer Plan
Costs associated with plant expansion only (not upgrade) are not eligible for grant funding
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a funding application during the December through January application window each year. Projects are evaluated and ranked using the Integrated Project Priority System (IPPS). Funds are provided on a reimbursable basis after eligible project costs are incurred and a payment request is submitted.

structured_extraction.program_description: An EPA-grant-funded initiative administered by MDE that provides free environmental site assessments to eligible property owners or prospective purchasers to help determine the type and extent of possible contamination on a brownfield property.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free Phase I and Phase II environmental site assessments conducted by MDE at no charge to the property owner or prospective purchaser. Assessments help reduce investigation costs for VCP applicants. Available on a first-come, first-served basis beginning July 1 of each calendar year.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: First-come, first-served beginning July 1 of each calendar year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners and prospective property owners of brownfield sites, including both public and private sector applicants. VCP applicants may also apply.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Environmental site assessments (Phase I and Phase II) to determine type and extent of contamination.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Properties must meet eligibility conditions.
requirements_list: Property must have perceived or known contamination
Property must be vacant or underutilized
Property must be located in a commercial or industrial area
Project must create jobs
Project must improve the local tax base following redevelopment
Eligible properties include sites on EPA CERCLIS and State Master List
Properties under active enforcement by MDE are not eligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Land Restoration Program at 410-537-3493. Applications are accepted on a first-come, first-served basis beginning July 1 of each calendar year.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides regulatory oversight for contaminated properties not in the Voluntary Cleanup Program. It uses a Technical Review Service and enforces Controlled Hazardous Substances regulations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers project grants. It also provides regulatory services and technical assistance.

requirements_list: Applicant must be responsible for a contaminated property not participating in the Voluntary Cleanup Program.

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary certification program for vehicle repair businesses that employ Master Certified Emissions Technicians (MCETs) and have equipment to repair vehicles to peak emissions performance. Part of Maryland's Vehicle Emissions Inspection Program (VEIP), it allows certified facilities to appear on the public CERF map available to motorists.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Certification status that allows vehicle repair facilities to participate in Maryland's emissions repair program. Benefits include: technical information about VEIP; free or low-cost training; access to RepairTrak data management system; newsletters and technical bulletins; online advertisement in CERF Map; official CERF signage; and quality assurance checks of diagnostic equipment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Vehicle repair facilities and Master Certified Emissions Technicians (MCETs) seeking certification to perform emissions-related repairs in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable — non-financial assistance program providing certification, training, and technical support for vehicle emissions repairs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland
requirements_list: Must employ at least one Master Certified Emissions Technician (MCET) with ASE L-1 certification
Must possess specific diagnostic equipment (OBD scan tool, multimeter, pressure gauges, vacuum gauges/pump, compression tester)
Must complete Vehicle Emissions Repair Reports for customers
Must provide detailed repair receipts on printed business invoices
Subject to periodic unannounced MDE inspections
Must post CERF and MCET certificates in repair area
Must comply with Maryland Workers' Compensation Act
Must complete and submit application form
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Application for Admission to the CERF Program and submit via email (mde.veip@maryland.gov) or fax (410-537-4435). A facility inspection will be scheduled after submission.

The Trust prioritizes education projects that promote behavior change and restoration activities that use volunteers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are awarded to nonprofit organizations, community associations, civic groups, schools, and public agencies for Bay awareness and conservation projects such as cleanup, recycling, awareness, education, and restoration. Over 1,000 groups have received grants.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations, community associations, civic groups, schools, and public agencies working to restore the Chesapeake Bay.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Bay awareness, conservation, cleanup, recycling, education, and restoration projects using volunteers. Projects uniting business, government, and citizens are encouraged.

requirements_list: Applicant must be a nonprofit organization, community association, civic group, school, or public agency
Project must contribute to restoration of the Chesapeake Bay
Priority given to education projects promoting behavior change toward the Bay and restoration activities utilizing volunteers

structured_extraction.program_audience: Parties legally responsible for cleanup of sites on the State Master List, or parties accepted into the VCP where water quality is an issue.

Water quality must be an issue at the site
Applicant must be a party legally responsible for cleanup or accepted into the VCP

structured_extraction.program_name: Climate Pollution Reduction Grants (CPRG) - Phase 1 Planning Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: The EPA's Climate Pollution Reduction Grants (CPRG) program provides funding to states, local governments, tribes, and territories to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and other harmful air pollution. Phase 1 provided $250 million in noncompetitive planning grants to develop climate action plans (Priority Climate Action Plans and Comprehensive Climate Action Plans) with a four-year performance period. Phase 2 provides approximately $4.6 billion for competitive Implementation Grants. Maryland's Department of the Environment leads the statewide planning grant, and three Metropolitan Statistical Areas received additional planning grants. Maryland's CCAP targets 60% GHG emissions reduction by 2031 and net-zero by 2045, implementing 21 GHG reduction measures across multiple sectors.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Phase 1: $250 million total noncompetitive planning grants awarded to states, local governments, tribes, and territories to develop Priority Climate Action Plans (PCAPs) and Comprehensive Climate Action Plans (CCAPs). Maryland received a statewide planning grant (EPA assistance agreement 5D-95316101-0) and three Metropolitan Statistical Areas received additional grants. Phase 2: approximately $4.6 billion for competitive Implementation Grants. Technical assistance and planning support also provided through the Local Government Climate Action Support Program for counties outside MSA planning grants.
structured_extraction.program_audience: State and local governments, regional planning organizations, and stakeholders in Maryland seeking to develop climate action plans to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, with priority focus on Low-Income and Disadvantaged Communities (LIDACs).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Development of Priority Climate Action Plans (PCAPs) and Comprehensive Climate Action Plans (CCAPs); GHG inventory development; emission reduction strategy development across electricity, transportation, buildings, industry, waste, agriculture, and forestry sectors; workforce planning analysis; stakeholder engagement and outreach; benefits analysis (health, economic, environmental); climate resilience planning; EV charging infrastructure; port decarbonization.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland. Baltimore MSA (Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Carroll, Harford, Howard, Queen Anne's counties), Philadelphia-Camden-Wilmington MSA (Cecil County), and Washington-Arlington-Alexandria MSA (Charles, Frederick, Montgomery, Prince George's counties) each received separate MSA planning grants. Counties outside MSAs (Allegany, Calvert, Caroline, Dorchester, Garrett, Kent, Somerset, St. Mary's, Talbot, Washington, Wicomico, Worcester) are eligible for the Maryland Local Government Climate Action Support Program.
requirements_list: Must be a state, local government, tribe, or territory
Must develop a Priority Climate Action Plan meeting EPA requirements
State executive branch agencies must develop Climate Implementation Plans
Counties outside MSA areas may request support by filling out the provided Google Form
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Phase 1 planning grants were noncompetitive and have already been awarded. Three MSA regional planning groups and the State of Maryland received grants. Counties outside MSA areas may request support by filling out the provided Google Form. Annual conferences held with Maryland Municipal League and Maryland Association of Counties for local government support.
