structured_extraction.program_description: The EPA's Climate Pollution Reduction Grants (CPRG) program Phase 2 provides approximately $4.6 billion in competitive grants to states, local governments, tribes, and territories to implement measures that reduce greenhouse gas emissions and other harmful air pollution.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Approximately $4.6 billion in competitive implementation grants awarded nationwide. Maryland is participating through two multi-state coalition awards: the Clean Corridor Coalition (EV charging infrastructure along I-95) and the Atlantic Conservation Coalition (natural carbon sequestration through forest management and coastal habitat restoration).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Competition winners announced July 2024; funds awarded October 2024
structured_extraction.program_audience: States, local governments, tribes, and territories seeking to implement greenhouse gas emissions reduction projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Implementation of greenhouse gas emissions reduction measures such as electric vehicle charging infrastructure and natural carbon sequestration through forest management and coastal habitat restoration.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; Maryland is included in two multi-state coalition grants.
requirements_list: Must be a state, local government, tribe, or territory
Must propose projects that implement greenhouse gas emissions reduction measures identified in a Priority Climate Action Plan
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Competition winners were announced in July 2024 and funds were awarded in October 2024. This round of competitive grants has closed.

structured_extraction.program_name: Coastal Wetlands Planning, Protection, and Restoration Act Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: This federal program authorizes the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service to make matching National Coastal Wetlands Conservation grants to coastal states for acquiring, managing, restoring, or enhancing coastal wetlands. Priority is given to projects consistent with the National Wetlands Priority Conservation Plan and states with dedicated wetlands funding programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Matching grants provided to coastal states for acquiring, managing, restoring, or enhancing coastal wetlands. Up to 75% of restoration project costs may be funded. Grants for property acquisition are provided only if land will be managed for long-term conservation. 15% of available funding is dedicated to wetlands conservation projects in coastal states through the North American Wetlands Conservation Act process.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Coastal state governments seeking to acquire, manage, restore, or enhance coastal wetlands.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquiring, managing, restoring, or enhancing coastal wetlands. Property acquisition must be for long-term conservation management.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Coastal states. Maryland is a coastal state and eligible.
requirements_list: Priority given to projects consistent with the National Wetlands Priority Conservation Plan
Priority given to states with dedicated funding programs for acquisition of coastal wetlands, natural areas, and open spaces
Priority given to projects in maritime forests on coastal barrier islands
Property acquisition grants require long-term conservation management of the land
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Division of Federal Aid, Fish and Wildlife Service, U.S. Department of the Interior.

structured_extraction.program_description: A challenge that encourages organizations to adopt commuter benefit programs and alternative transportation options for their employees. Organizations take steps to reduce single-occupancy vehicle commuting — such as offering tax credits, telework, carpooling, or biking incentives — and submit a form to enter a prize drawing with rewards like cycling gear and work-from-home accessories.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Organizations that take at least one qualifying commuter benefit step are entered into a prize drawing. One step earns one entry; two to five steps earns two entries; six or more steps earns three entries. Prizes include cycling gear, work-from-home accessories, and assistance from the Commuter Choice program with employee education.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland employers and organizations looking to support employees with commuter benefits and reduce carbon footprint
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable — prize-based recognition program for employers adopting commuter benefit steps
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland
requirements_list: Organization must take at least one qualifying commuter benefit step
Submit a form via Google Forms or email steps taken to commuterchoice@mdot.state.md.us
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Take at least one of the listed commuter benefit steps, then submit the Google Form or email the steps taken to commuterchoice@mdot.state.md.us to be entered in the prize drawing.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Comprehensive Flood Management Grant Program (CFMGP), established in 1976, provides matching grant assistance to local governments ('subdivisions') for comprehensive flood hazard mitigation projects and management planning. The program uses state bond proceeds to fund watershed studies, development of flood mitigation plans, acquisitions, elevations, and relocations of flood-prone structures, establishment of flood warning systems, construction of flood control infrastructure, infrastructure retrofits, emergency preparedness measures, and watershed restoration. Grants cover up to 75% of total project costs for projects without a federal sponsor, or up to 50% of the local match for projects with a federal sponsor (when federal agencies provide 75% of total project cost, the state covers up to 12.5% and the local government provides 12.5%). The program also helps communities establish long-term floodplain management programs to prevent future flood damage and restore natural floodplains.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Matching grants covering up to 75% of total project costs for projects without a federal sponsor, or up to 50% of the local match for projects with a federal sponsor. When federal agencies provide 75% of total project cost, the state grant covers up to 12.5% and the local government provides 12.5%. Grants support comprehensive flood management studies, flood mitigation plans, acquisitions, elevations, and relocations of flood-prone structures, establishment of flood warning systems, construction of flood control projects, infrastructure retrofits, emergency preparedness measures, watershed restoration, and establishment of long-term floodplain management programs. Applications are typically accepted December through January each year.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications will reopen in December 2026; typically accepted December 1 through January 31 each year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland local government subdivisions and communities in flood-prone areas seeking to reduce flood risks, improve flood resilience, and restore natural floodplains through studies, planning, and mitigation capital projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Comprehensive flood management studies, flood mitigation plans, acquisitions, elevations, and relocations of flood-prone structures, establishment of flood warning systems, construction of flood control projects, infrastructure retrofits, emergency preparedness measures, watershed restoration, and establishment of long-term floodplain management programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to Maryland local jurisdictions and communities.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local government subdivision
Projects must reduce risk of loss of life and property from flooding
Projects must address properties within flood-prone areas
Requires local government matching funds (amount varies based on federal involvement)
Projects must increase flood resilience and/or restore natural floodplains
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application during the open solicitation window. Applications are typically accepted December 1 through January 31 each year. Applications are currently closed and will reopen in December 2026. Contact Maryland Department of the Environment, Water and Science Administration at (410) 537-3908 for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Conservation Reserve Program (CRP), established by the 1985 Farm Bill, provides cost sharing and land rental payments to farmers for conservation practices such as establishing permanent cover on highly erodible lands, planting filter strips and riparian forest buffers, and restoring wetlands and shallow water areas for wildlife.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Landowners enter 10-15 year contracts and receive annual rental payments. No commodity crops can be grown on enrolled land during the contract. Haying, grazing, and commercial harvesting are also prohibited. A maximum of 25% of a county's eligible cropland may be enrolled. Some practices (riparian buffers, filter strips, grassed waterways, contour buffer strips, shallow water areas for wildlife) qualify for continuous sign-up without a competitive ranking process.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Sign-up periods usually occur once or twice per year; some practices qualify for continuous sign-up.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers and landowners with eligible cropland or pasture, particularly in priority conservation areas such as the Chesapeake Bay region.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Establishing permanent vegetative cover on highly erodible lands, planting filter strips and riparian forest buffers, and restoring wetlands and shallow water wildlife habitats.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Nationwide; Chesapeake Bay region is a designated national conservation priority area. Maximum 25% of a county's eligible cropland may be enrolled.
requirements_list: Land must be eligible cropland
10-15 year contract required
No commodity crops, haying, grazing, or commercial harvesting during contract period
Maximum of 25% of a county's eligible cropland may be enrolled
Offers are ranked nationally and selected based on cost and environmental benefit (except continuous sign-up practices)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local USDA Service Center. Landowners offer land for enrollment during announced sign-up periods (usually once or twice per year). Certain practices qualify for continuous sign-up at any time without competitive ranking.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides funding to Local Emergency Planning Committees (LEPCs) responsible for administering the federal Emergency Planning and Community Right-to-Know Act (EPCRA).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Funding for Local Emergency Planning Committees to support administration of the federal Emergency Planning and Community Right-to-Know Act.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local Emergency Planning Committees
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Administration of the federal Emergency Planning and Community Right-to-Know Act
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland

structured_extraction.program_description: The Drinking Water Revolving Loan Fund (DWRLF) provides below-market, low-interest loans, grants, and loan principal forgiveness to eligible public and private community water systems, local governments, and other eligible borrowers for projects that ensure safe drinking water and protect Maryland's drinking water supply in compliance with the Federal Safe Drinking Water Act. Eligible projects include water treatment plant construction and upgrades, source water protection planning, raw water intake and conveyance infrastructure, finished water storage facilities, water distribution system rehabilitation including lead service line replacement, and consolidation of water systems. The program is authorized under the Safe Drinking Water Act (SDWA) Amendments of 1996 and includes funds from the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law. The Maryland Water Infrastructure Financing Administration (MWIFA) administers the program, may issue revenue bonds to support the fund, and also offers financial advisory services to help borrowers determine water rate structures and assess the financial impact of a proposed loan. Two interest rate options are available: Standard Rate (50% of market rate) or Disadvantaged Community (DAC) Rate (25% of market rate). Additional subsidy is available through loan principal forgiveness.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Below-market, low-interest revolving loans, grants, and loan principal forgiveness funded by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and state sources for eligible drinking water infrastructure capital projects. Two interest rate options: Standard Rate (50% of market rate) or Disadvantaged Community (DAC) Rate (25% of market rate). Loan principal forgiveness up to 50% of financed amount, not to exceed $1.5 million for disadvantaged communities (DACs); up to 25% loan principal forgiveness for projects where water user rates would increase more than 20%. Up to 100% SRF loans for non-compliant systems; up to 87.5% State Water Supply Grant for small disadvantaged systems in compliance. Loan terms up to 40 years for DACs. FFY 2025 total funding allocation: $122,439,007 in loans and grants. MWIFA may issue revenue bonds to support the fund and also provides financial advisory services to help borrowers determine water rate structures and assess the financial impact of a proposed loan. Applications are typically accepted December through January each year.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications typically open December through January each year; currently closed and will reopen in December 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public and private community water systems, local governments, and eligible borrowers in Maryland seeking to finance drinking water supply improvements and infrastructure capital projects to achieve or maintain compliance with the Federal Safe Drinking Water Act. Includes small water systems serving fewer than 10,000 people, disadvantaged communities, and systems with compliance issues.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Water treatment plant construction and upgrades, source water protection plans, raw water intake and conveyance infrastructure, finished water storage facilities, water distribution system rehabilitation including lead service line replacement, consolidation of water systems, planning/design/construction of eligible drinking water projects, PFAS and emerging contaminant treatment, water audits, conservation plans, capacity management plans, feasibility studies, engineering reports, and backup power systems.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to eligible community water systems, local governments, and other eligible borrowers in Maryland. Projects must be physically located in Maryland and generally must be within a Priority Funding Area (PFA) or receive a PFA exception. Projects must also be included in the applicable County Water and Sewerage Plan.
requirements_list: Must be a community water system, nonprofit noncommunity water system, local government, or other eligible entity
Must demonstrate technical, managerial, and financial capacity to maintain the water system prior to receiving a loan, as required by the federal Safe Drinking Water Act
Projects must be consistent with the Federal Safe Drinking Water Act
Projects must be physically located within a Priority Funding Area (PFA) or receive a PFA exception
Projects must be included in the County Water and Sewerage Plan
Small System designation requires serving a population of fewer than 10,000 AND the benefitting population is responsible for the capital costs

Disadvantaged Community (DAC) designation requires: 50%+ of project serves an Environmental Justice area (EJ Score ≥75) OR at least 2 of the following: Median Household Income <80% of state MHI, poverty rate >110% of state level, unemployment rate >120% of state level
Systems in significant noncompliance may be eligible if the project addresses the cause of noncompliance or is unrelated to the noncompliance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted on an annual basis, typically opening in December and closing in January 31. Applications are currently closed and will reopen in December 2026. Applicants should prepare by reviewing eligibility requirements, ensuring the project is included in the County Water and Sewerage Plan, and confirming Priority Funding Area status. Contact MWIFA for additional information. Public comment periods are conducted on program documents; comments may be submitted to mde.wqfa_announcement@maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides financial assistance to local governments for the acquisition, construction, rehabilitation, and improvement of publicly owned water supply facilities throughout Maryland. The program helps fund projects that address water supply-related health problems and helps meet federal Safe Drinking Water Act requirements. Grant awards require a local match and are based on system size, compliance status, and affordability.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants fund up to 87.5% of total eligible project cost, not to exceed $1.5 million per project. A 12.5% local match is required, which may be funded through the Drinking Water Revolving Loan Fund (DWRLF) Program. Grants are based on median household income of the community and system size, compliance status, and affordability. Only applicants with insufficient or limited financial capability are eligible. Costs for planning, engineering, and project administration are eligible for loans only. Applicants may receive a combination of a State grant and a Drinking Water Revolving Loan.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: December 1 through January 31 annually; applications will reopen in December 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments and community water systems with publicly owned water supply facilities that have insufficient or limited financial capability, seeking assistance for water supply and infrastructure needs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Upgrading water treatment facilities, well development, water storage tanks, water distribution facilities up to private property lines, consolidation of smaller water systems, and general water supply and water infrastructure improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in a Priority Funding Area (or have a PFA exception or categorical exception/exclusion) and be consistent with the County Water and Sewer Plan. Projects must also conform to Smart Growth Criteria. Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Project must be eligible under the federal Safe Drinking Water Act
Project must conform to Smart Growth Criteria
Project must be located in a Priority Funding Area (or have a PFA exception or be categorically excepted/excluded)
Project must be consistent with the County Water and Sewer Plan
Applicant must submit a water audit
Water systems serving a population greater than 10,000 must submit a water conservation plan
Only applicants with insufficient or limited financial capability are eligible
Local match required (12.5% of total eligible project cost)
Award amount based on system size, compliance status, and affordability
Maximum award of $1.5 million per project
Community water systems must serve at least 25 persons or 15 connections year-round
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a funding application during the open solicitation window (December 1 through January 31 each year). Applications are currently closed and will reopen in December 2026. Projects are rated and ranked based on Environment Article 9-423 and COMAR 26.03.09.06 criteria, including public health benefits, regulatory compliance, safety, water system reliability, financial capability of the applicant, previous corrective efforts, and community size. Applicants are encouraged to also seek funding from USDA Rural Development Program or Maryland DHCD Small Cities Community Development Block Grant Program.

structured_extraction.program_name: EPA Wetlands Program State Development Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: Federal grants available to states for developing and enhancing their wetlands protection programs. Funds support both regulatory and nonregulatory activities including conservation planning, monitoring, and integration of wetlands into existing water and natural resource programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants provided to states starting in fiscal year 1990. Example grant amounts include $50,000, $26,970, and $44,645 for specific projects. Priority is given to innovative approaches and transferable project results.
structured_extraction.program_audience: State governments seeking to develop new wetlands protection programs or refine and enhance existing programs
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: State wetlands conservation plans; projects integrating wetlands into traditional water and natural resource programs; multi-objective river corridor management; water quality standards for wetlands; Section 401 program improvements; expanding geographic jurisdiction of existing regulatory programs; monitoring projects
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to states; Maryland falls under EPA Region 3
requirements_list: Priority given to innovative approaches
Priority given to projects with transferable results
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Regional Grant Coordinator at EPA Region 3 in Philadelphia for application guidance.

structured_extraction.program_name: Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment (EVSE) Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal tax credit for purchasing and installing home electric vehicle charging station equipment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to 30% of the cost of qualifying charging station equipment, with a maximum credit of $1,000.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and businesses purchasing electric vehicle charging equipment
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and installation of electric vehicle charging station equipment
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available nationwide including Maryland
requirements_list: Must purchase qualifying electric vehicle charging station equipment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Claim the credit using IRS Form 8911 when filing your federal income tax return.

structured_extraction.program_name: Electronic Collection and Recycling Grant Program for Counties and Municipalities
structured_extraction.program_description: Grants to Maryland counties and municipalities to support local electronics recycling (eCycling) programs for computers and video display devices. Counties that have addressed methods for separate collection and recycling of computers and video display devices in their solid waste management plans, and municipalities with local computer and video display device recycling programs, are eligible. Grants are funded partly from manufacturer registration fees. No grants are currently being offered.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants funded by a portion of manufacturer registration fees to support county and municipal eCycling programs for computers and video display devices. No specific dollar amounts are stated. No grants are currently being offered.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No eCycling grants are currently being offered.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland counties and municipalities with electronics recycling programs
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Support local collection and recycling of computers and video display devices through eCycling programs
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to all Maryland counties and municipalities
requirements_list: County must have addressed methods for separate collection and recycling of computers and video display devices in its solid waste management plan
Municipalities must have a local computer and video display device recycling program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Details and forms on eCycling grants, when available, are provided in the County Coordinator Resources section of the Department's Waste Diversion web page.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program that responds to natural disasters by helping groups of people address imminent hazards to life and property caused by floods, fires, windstorms, and other natural events. It funds emergency measures such as debris removal, bank stabilization, levee repair, and floodplain easements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: NRCS may cover up to 75% of construction costs for emergency measures. The remaining 25% must come from local sources in the form of cash or in-kind services. All work must reduce threats to life and property, be economically and environmentally defensible, and sound from an engineering standpoint. Public and private landowners are eligible but must be represented by a public agency project sponsor.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Within 10 days of the disaster for exigency situations and within 60 days for nonexigency situations
structured_extraction.program_audience: Groups of people with a common problem following a natural disaster; represented by a public agency project sponsor such as a city, county, general improvement district, or conservation district
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Removing debris from stream channels, roads, and bridges; reshaping and protecting eroded banks; correcting damaged drainage facilities; repairing levees and structures; reseeding damaged areas; purchasing floodplain easements
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available nationwide including Maryland
requirements_list: Work must be sponsored by a political subdivision of the state (city, county, general improvement district, or conservation district), except for floodplain easements
Sponsor must provide land rights, permits, local cost share, and oversee installation of work
Applications must be submitted within 10 days of disaster for exigency situations or 60 days for nonexigency situations
Funds cannot be used to solve pre-existing problems or improve protection above pre-disaster levels
Funds cannot be used for operation and maintenance or repair of private/public transportation or utilities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application to the local NRCS office within 10 days (exigency) or 60 days (nonexigency) of the disaster. A project sponsor (public agency) must represent landowners.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal tax credit for homeowners who install qualifying energy-efficient appliances, including air source heat pumps, heat pump water heaters, and biomass stoves and boilers with a thermal efficiency rating of at least 75%.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax credit of 30% of the project cost, up to $2,000 per year. Eligible costs may include labor for installation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners installing qualifying energy-efficient heating appliances
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of air source heat pumps, heat pump water heaters, and biomass stoves or boilers
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available nationwide including Maryland
requirements_list: Appliance must be an air source heat pump, heat pump water heater, or biomass stove/boiler
Biomass appliances must have a thermal efficiency rating of at least 75%
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Claim the credit when filing your federal income tax return.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant fund administered by the Maryland Department of Commerce that awards grants to producers of eligible construction materials. The fund supports the development, standardization, and transparency of environmental product declarations for construction materials and products.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are awarded to producers of eligible construction materials to support the development, standardization, and transparency of environmental product declarations. The fund consists of money appropriated in the state budget.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Producers of eligible construction materials who need to develop environmental product declarations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Development, standardization, and transparency of environmental product declarations for construction materials and products.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_name: Federal Aid in Sport Fish Restoration Act (Dingell-Johnson Act) and Federal Aid in Wildlife Restoration Act (Pittman-Robertson Act)
structured_extraction.program_description: Two federal programs that distribute funds to states for fish and wildlife conservation. The Dingell-Johnson Act supports fish restoration and management; the Pittman-Robertson Act supports wildlife conservation including wetland acquisition and restoration.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Dingell-Johnson funds cover up to 75% of the cost of fish restoration and management projects and comprehensive fish and wildlife resource management plans. Pittman-Robertson grants cover up to 75% of wildlife conservation activity costs including wetland acquisition and restoration. Since 1952, roughly $1.4 billion has been distributed under Dingell-Johnson and $2 billion under Pittman-Robertson. The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service also provides technical assistance to states.
structured_extraction.program_audience: State governments for fish and wildlife conservation activities including wetland acquisition
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Fish restoration and management projects; comprehensive fish and wildlife resource management plans; aquatic resource education; wildlife conservation including acquisition, restoration, and maintenance of wetlands
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to all states including Maryland; funds distributed by formula based on geographic area and fishing license holders (Dingell-Johnson)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service Division of Federal Aid.

structured_extraction.program_description: Allows fleet operators to perform official emissions inspections limited to their own fleet vehicles under the Vehicle Emissions Inspection Program (VEIP), eliminating the need to take vehicles out of service for testing at State inspection stations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Authorization (FIS License) for qualified fleet operators to conduct in-house vehicle emissions inspections on their own fleet vehicles, avoiding the need to visit State VEIP stations. Operators must purchase FIS testing equipment from Envirotest of Maryland and pay a $30 VEIP inspection fee plus electronic transaction fees per inspection.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Fleet operators with at least 25 vehicles seeking authorization to conduct in-house vehicle emissions inspections in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Equipment purchase fees, inspection fees, and electronic transaction fees associated with operating an in-house fleet vehicle emissions inspection station.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide
requirements_list: Own or lease a fleet of at least 25 vehicles and operate a vehicle maintenance facility
Employ a Master Certified Emissions Technician (MCET) at each location
Purchase FIS testing equipment from Envirotest of Maryland
Provide high-speed internet, 110 volt power outlet, and compressed air line
Allow access for unannounced quality assurance audits
Possess specific repair tools (multimeter, pressure gauges, vacuum pump, compression tester)
Pay $30 VEIP inspection fee plus electronic transaction fees per inspection
Provide annual list of affected vehicles with quarterly updates
Comply with Maryland Workers' Compensation Act
Pass facility inspection
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Application for Admission to the FIS Program and submit to MDE. Applicant will be contacted to schedule a facility inspection. See program fact sheet and FIS presentation for equipment and process details.

structured_extraction.program_name: Forest Stewardship Program / Stewardship Incentive Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Two linked federal programs that help private landowners protect or enhance their forest lands and associated wetlands. The Forest Stewardship Program provides technical assistance and the Stewardship Incentive Program provides cost-sharing for implementing forest stewardship plans.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Technical assistance is provided through the Forest Stewardship Program to help landowners enhance and protect timber, fish/wildlife habitat, water quality, wetlands, and recreational values. The Stewardship Incentive Program provides cost-sharing for nine eligible practice categories. The maximum amount a landowner may receive per year is $10,000. Approximately $100,000 is distributed annually to about 150 landowners covering 2,000 acres. Practices receiving cost-share must be maintained for a minimum of 10 years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private landowners who own five or more acres of forest land or non-forest land that can be planted to trees
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Management plan development; afforestation; forest improvement; windbreaks and hedgerows; streamside and wetlands protection; fisheries and aquatic habitat improvement; wildlife habitat enhancement; forest recreation habitat enhancement; soil and water protection
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Must own five or more acres of forest land or non-forest land that can be planted to trees
Practices receiving cost-share must be maintained for a minimum of 10 years
Must have an approved Forest Stewardship Program plan before receiving Stewardship Incentive Program cost-share
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the MD Department of Natural Resources Forest Service in Annapolis. Programs have open enrollment.

structured_extraction.program_name: General Permit for Discharges of Stormwater Associated with Construction Activity (Maryland General Permit No. 20-CP)
structured_extraction.program_description: This permit (No. 20-CP, NPDES No. MDRC0000) authorizes discharges of stormwater associated with construction activity to Waters of the State in Maryland. It replaces Maryland General Permit No. 14-GP (expired December 31, 2019). It covers construction sites disturbing one or more acres of land, or less than one acre if part of a common plan of development that will ultimately disturb one or more acres, including clearing, grading, and excavation activities. The permit is effective April 1, 2023 and expires March 31, 2028. Operators must obtain coverage by submitting a Notice of Intent (NOI) electronically. The permit sets requirements for erosion and sediment controls (E&SC), stormwater management (SWM) plans, stormwater pollution prevention plans (SWPPPs), turbidity monitoring, inspections, corrective actions, and reporting to protect water quality. It implements EPA's Construction and Development (C&D) Rule requirements including non-numeric effluent limitations, Environmental Site Design (ESD) to the maximum extent practicable, PCB contamination prevention, and addresses sensitive waters (Tier II). Free training opportunities and guidance documents (FAQs, decision trees, SWPPP templates, inspection forms, corrective action logs) are provided to help operators comply with permit requirements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MDE issues a general permit that authorizes stormwater discharges from construction sites. The permit covers all types of construction activity involving earth disturbance of one or more acres, including residential, commercial, industrial, highway, bridge, utility, demolition, and other construction types, as well as construction support activities (concrete/asphalt batch plants, equipment staging yards, material storage areas, excavated material disposal areas, borrow areas) and pre-active mining staging areas and access roads. Free training opportunities are available for permittees. MDE also provides guidance documents, templates (SWPPP Template, Inspection Forms, Corrective Action Log), decision trees, and FAQ resources to help operators comply with permit requirements. Quarterly turbidity monitoring and reporting is required for dewatering discharges to Tier II waters and sediment-impaired waters (benchmark: 150 NTU). Local and state government projects are exempt from permit fees. Fees for others are set per COMAR 26.08.04.09-1; the ePermits payment system accepts credit cards (plus 3% processing fee) or ACH payments ($3 flat fee).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: For existing 14-GP permittees: no later than September 30, 2023. New sites: minimum 14 days prior to commencing construction. New operator (transfer): minimum 14 days prior to transfer date. Emergency projects: no later than 7 calendar days after commencing activities. Continuation of Authorization must be submitted at least 60 days before permit expiration. Quarterly turbidity reporting deadlines: April 28, July 28, October 28, January 28.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Operators and responsible parties overseeing construction activity that discharges stormwater in Maryland, including developers, builders, general contractors, construction support activity operators, demolition contractors, and mining operators. Multiple operators on the same project must each obtain coverage; subcontractors are generally not considered operators.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable — this is a regulatory permit, not a funding program. The associated training and technical assistance help applicants comply with stormwater requirements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland, including all waters of the State (surface and underground waters, Chesapeake Bay and tributaries, streams, wetlands, and floodplains). Additional requirements apply for sites discharging to Tier II waters or sediment-impaired waters, and for sites discharging to waters impaired for PCBs.
requirements_list: Submit a Notice of Intent (NOI) electronically through the ePermits website (egov.maryland.gov/mde/npdes)
NOI must be electronically signed by the person in authority from the developer or builder
Must submit all supporting documents with the NOI; a 14-day public notification period follows submission
Existing permittees under the previous 14-GP permit must submit an NOI no later than September 30, 2023 to prevent a lapse in coverage

Prepare and implement a Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plan (SWPPP) when required (e.g., when using chemical additives, handling contaminated materials, performing dewatering, or other specified criteria); SWPPP must be developed prior to NOI submission in applicable cases
Develop and implement an Erosion and Sediment Control (E&SC) plan per ESC Handbook and a Stormwater Management (SWM) plan
Personnel responsible for implementation and maintenance of erosion and sediment controls must be properly trained per COMAR 26.17.01.06; at least one certified member must be on-site
Notify the Water and Science Administration Compliance Program at (410) 537-3510 at least 2 weeks prior to start of construction
Establish Stream Protection Zones (50 feet minimum for Tier I; average 100 feet, minimum 50 feet for Tier II)
Conduct site inspections at required frequencies (every 4 calendar days for Tier II discharges; every 4 business days OR every 7 days plus within 24 hours of a 0.25-inch rain event otherwise)
Monitor and report daily maximum turbidity values (in NTU) for dewatering discharges to Tier II or sediment-impaired waters; benchmark of 150 NTU applies
Submit quarterly turbidity monitoring reports via MDE ePermits system within 28 days following end of each quarter
Post permit coverage notice at the construction site
Maintain on-site records including NOI, approved plans, general permit copy, SWPPP, and inspection reports for three years after permit termination
Take corrective actions within specified deadlines when triggering conditions occur; complete inspection reports within 24 hours
Notify MDE of violations within 24 hours; notify National Response Center for reportable spills within 24 hours
Comply with prohibited discharge requirements (e.g., no concrete washout, paint/stucco washout to waters)
Fees apply per COMAR 26.08.04.09-1 (local and state government projects are exempt)
Design, install, and maintain effective erosion and sediment controls; complete installation prior to commencement of relevant construction phases
Minimize stormwater volume and velocity; control peak flowrates and total stormwater volume
Minimize exposed soil and disturbance of steep slopes (>3:1 grade)
Provide and maintain natural buffers around waters; direct stormwater to vegetated areas; maximize infiltration
Minimize soil compaction and preserve native topsoil where feasible

Initiate soil stabilization immediately when earth-disturbing activities cease or pause more than 14 calendar days; within 3 days for steep slopes and perimeter areas, 7 days for other disturbed areas
Install perimeter controls (filter berms, silt fences, vegetative strips) along site perimeters
Remove accumulated sediment before reaching one-half the height of perimeter controls
Restrict vehicle use to designated exit points; install and maintain stabilization at all paved road exit points
Remove tracked-out sediment by end of business day or next business day
Minimize dust through water application or other suppression techniques
Install sediment basins/traps with surface outlet structures; protect storm drain inlets with sediment control measures

If using chemical additives: pre-approval required, use only when conventional BMPs are insufficient, proper storage and documentation required; obtain Department approval 30 days prior to using cationic chemical additives
Manage stockpiles with barriers and covers (for inactive piles 14 or more days)
Prevent equipment/vehicle fueling and maintenance spills; properly manage equipment and vehicle wash water
Store hazardous chemicals in secondary containment; manage construction and domestic waste in covered containers
Comply with Threatened and Endangered Species Protection requirements
Comply with Safe Drinking Water Act UIC requirements for subsurface controls
Modify SWPPP within 7 days of specified conditions; maintain records of all SWPPP modifications
Comply with PCB minimization practices for sites discharging to waters impaired for PCBs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a Notice of Intent (NOI) electronically through the MDE ePermits website (https://egov.maryland.gov/mde/npdes/Account/Login). Agents and consultants may prepare the NOI, but the responsible party (developer or builder) must electronically sign and submit it. A Subscriber Agreement may be required to validate authorization. After submission of the NOI and all supporting documents, a 14-day public notification period begins. For sites in Tier II watersheds, complete the antidegradation checklist (Appendix C) and conduct a Tier II review if required. Pay applicable fees through the ePermits portal via credit card (plus 3% processing fee) or ACH payment ($3 flat fee).

structured_extraction.program_name: General Permit for the Discharge of Composting Toilet Wastewater to Groundwater by Land Application (Maryland General Permit No. 18-CT)
structured_extraction.program_description: This general permit allows composting toilet owners to discharge composting toilet wastewater to groundwater via land application. It regulates management of three waste streams: compost toilet liquids, compost toilet solids, and graywater. It establishes requirements for land application rates, buffer zones, fecal coliform testing, and monitoring. It replaces individual permits and offers cost savings by eliminating newspaper publication requirements. Current individual permit holders will be contacted at renewal and can apply for this general permit instead.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Issues a general discharge permit for composting toilet wastewater land application, replacing more costly individual permits and providing cost savings to permittees by eliminating newspaper publication requirements. Includes authorization to discharge composting toilet liquids to groundwater via land application, with operational oversight, monitoring requirements, and compliance standards.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners and operators of composting toilets who need to discharge composting toilet wastewater to groundwater via land application, including current individual permit holders up for renewal.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Obtaining a permit to legally discharge composting toilet wastewater to groundwater by land application.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland. Onsite, land application only within Maryland territorial boundaries. Cannot be used in critical areas unless composting toilet system is approved as Best Available Technology for nitrogen treatment.
requirements_list: Must submit a Notice of Intent (NOI) to obtain coverage under the general permit
Current individual permit holders may apply when their permit is up for renewal
Complete NOI form with all requested information and required Supplemental Information
Site map identifying Primary and Reserve Land Application Areas
Operation & Maintenance Manual
Initial wastewater analysis
MSDS for each additive
Approval of graywater onsite disposal system (if applicable)
Designated operator designation
Worker's compensation insurance information
Certification by responsible corporate officer or authorized representative
Documentation from local county Environmental Health Department of onsite sewage disposal system permit approval
Fecal coliform testing required before land application; must be less than 200 mpn/100 ml
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a completed NOI form with all required attachments (site map, Operation & Maintenance Manual, initial wastewater analysis, etc.) to the MDE Wastewater Permits Program / Groundwater Permits Division. Current individual permit holders will be contacted at renewal and given the opportunity to apply for this general permit. Annual monitoring reports are due by January 31st each year.

structured_extraction.program_description: A challenge program run by the Maryland Green Registry that encourages organizations to green their vehicle fleets by purchasing fuel-efficient or alternative-fuel vehicles, improving fleet management practices, offering EV charging, and promoting green vehicles to employees. Participants can join the challenge and be recognized publicly on the Maryland Green Registry.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Organizations that participate in the challenge are recognized on the Maryland Green Registry. Past participants were also entered into a prize drawing. While the prize drawing is now closed, organizations can still add their names to the challenge, particularly if they have an EV charging station on their property.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations (businesses, universities, nonprofits, and government entities) in Maryland that operate vehicle fleets and want to reduce emissions through cleaner, more efficient vehicles and fleet practices.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable — this is a recognition/challenge program, not a direct funding program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland Green Registry member or willing to join
Organization must operate a vehicle fleet
Participation areas include vehicle purchasing, fleet management, freight carrier efficiency, EV charging/alternative fuel refilling, employee incentives, and outreach
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations sign up using the online Google Form linked on the page to add their name to the challenge.

structured_extraction.program_description: FEMA's Hazard Mitigation Grant Program provides funding after a federally declared disaster to help reduce future flood damage and support long-term hazard mitigation projects. Eligible projects include purchasing flood-prone properties, relocating or elevating homes within the 100-year floodplain, and other measures to reduce loss of life and property in future disasters. FEMA provides states with an amount equal to 7.5% of the emergency financial assistance rendered after a declared disaster, with funds matched 75% federal and 25% state and local.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: FEMA provides states with an amount equal to 7.5% of the emergency financial assistance rendered after a declared disaster. Funds are matched 75% federal / 25% state and local. Eligible projects include property purchases, house relocations, and house elevations in the 100-year floodplain, as well as other long-term hazard mitigation measures to reduce loss of life and property in future disasters.
structured_extraction.program_audience: State and local governments, Indian tribes, non-profits, and property owners in flood-prone areas following a federally declared disaster
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property purchases, house relocations, house elevations to reduce future flood damage within the 100-year floodplain, and other long-term hazard mitigation projects to reduce loss of life and property in future disasters
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland in areas where a federal disaster has been declared
requirements_list: A federal disaster must be declared in the area
Projects must reduce future flood damage within the 100-year floodplain
Requires 25% match from state and local funds
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Maryland Department of the Environment for guidance on applying following a federally declared disaster.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Land Restoration Program (LRP) oversees cleanup and redevelopment of contaminated properties across Maryland, including brownfields and voluntary cleanup sites. It provides fact sheets for each project site, covering location, operational history, environmental actions, and current status. The program focuses on cleaning up uncontrolled hazardous waste sites throughout Maryland to protect public health and the environment at historically contaminated sites. It includes the Voluntary Cleanup Program (VCP), which provides liability assurances and financial incentives for brownfields redevelopment, as well as a Technical Review Service (TRS) for project oversight and closure.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The LRP provides technical oversight and guidance for environmental cleanup and brownfield redevelopment at contaminated sites. It includes the Voluntary Cleanup Program (VCP), brownfields redevelopment support, land use control compliance, and technical review services. The program issues fact sheets for each project site and maintains records of environmental actions and site status. The Brownfields Revitalization Incentive Program (BRIP) offers up to 70% property tax credit on increased property value for 5 years. A Certificate of Completion is issued upon satisfactory cleanup. The Technical Review Service (TRS) provides site investigation, data collection, risk evaluation, remediation oversight, and Environmental Management Plan development, billed at $50-$100 per hour for staff time.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling/ongoing; VCP public comment periods typically 30 days from public notice posting date; varies by property
structured_extraction.contact_name: Brian Dietz, Chief of the State Assessment and Remediation Division
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners, developers, prospective purchasers, businesses, lenders, local governments, and other entities seeking to clean up and redevelop contaminated or brownfield properties in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Environmental site assessment, cleanup planning, remediation oversight, brownfield redevelopment technical assistance, site cleanup and restoration activities, and property redevelopment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — available in all Maryland counties, including National Priorities List (NPL) sites and State Master List sites throughout Maryland, with emphasis on densely populated urban centers and substantially underutilized commercial/industrial areas.
requirements_list: Property must be a brownfield or historically contaminated hazardous waste site
Applicant must be an inculpable person or responsible party
Public notice required on property
Completed application submitted to MDE
Phase I environmental site assessment
Phase II environmental site assessment
$6,000 application fee
Response action plan with implementation schedule
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For the VCP: Submit completed application with Phase I and Phase II environmental site assessments and $6,000 application fee; public notice is posted on the property; public comment period (typically 30 days); MDE review and assignment of project manager. For the Technical Review Service (TRS): Mail or email completed request letter and copies of environmental reports to the Chief; a project manager is assigned; requests are processed in order received; typical response time up to 60 days; process includes document review, meetings, and investigation/remediation plan development; completion marked by a Site Status Letter.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides financial assistance to property owners for voluntary environmental enhancement projects such as wetlands restoration, streambank stabilization, tree plantings, and wildlife habitat creation on unvegetated, eroded, or degraded land.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance for voluntary environmental enhancement projects including wetlands restoration, streambank stabilization, tree plantings, and wildlife habitat creation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners with unvegetated areas adjacent to streams or wetlands, drained or eroded fields, woods, streams, or filled wetlands
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Wetlands restoration, streambank stabilization, tree plantings, wildlife habitat creation
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland
requirements_list: Must own property with unvegetated areas adjacent to streams or wetlands, drained or eroded fields, woods or streams, or filled wetlands

structured_extraction.program_name: Local Household Hazardous Materials (HHW) Collection Programs
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland counties operate local collection programs that allow residents to safely dispose of household hazardous waste (HHW) such as mercury, paint, paint thinner, pesticides, herbicides, and batteries. These programs prevent HHW from contaminating the environment, harming children and pets, or disrupting septic and wastewater systems. The programs also include collection and proper disposal of residential leftover and/or expired medications (over-the-counter and prescription); medications should never be poured down drains, on ground, into storm sewers, or flushed down toilets.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: County-run collection events and drop-off sites accept household hazardous waste items including paint, pesticides, motor oil, antifreeze, batteries, and electronics. Frequency varies by county — some offer year-round drop-off, others hold biannual or annual events. Some programs are available to residents only; Montgomery County also accepts business waste on Wednesdays. Additionally, residential leftover and/or expired medication drop-off locations are available at police stations, sheriff's offices, and select pharmacies (including some Walgreens locations); many offer 24-hour access.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents (and some businesses) seeking to safely dispose of household hazardous waste materials and/or leftover or expired medications
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Safe disposal and recycling of household hazardous waste such as paint, pesticides, motor oil, antifreeze, mercury, batteries, and electronics; also safe disposal of residential over-the-counter and prescription medications
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in most Maryland counties. Eligibility and accepted materials vary by county. Most programs serve county residents only. Medication collection is available statewide, though Dorchester, Somerset, and Worcester counties have no medication collection program.
requirements_list: Must be a resident of the county offering the program (most counties)
Must bring accepted materials — varies by county
Some counties have scheduled event days only; contact your county for dates
For medication collection: medications must be over-the-counter or prescription drugs; some counties have restrictions on controlled substances, inhalers, syringes, and chemotherapy drugs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your county's HHW program directly (phone numbers and websites listed in the county table on the MDE page) to find the next collection event date and confirm what materials are accepted. For medication disposal, drop off at local police stations, sheriff's offices, or participating pharmacies — many offer 24-hour access.

structured_extraction.program_name: MD Occupational Safety and Health Consultation Services
structured_extraction.program_description: Free on-site consultation program for small employers that identifies workplace safety hazards, helps develop safety and health programs, provides on-site education and training, and assists with occupational health and ergonomic issues.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free on-site consultation services including hazard identification, safety program development assistance, limited on-site education and training, and ergonomic/occupational health guidance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small employers in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Workplace safety improvements, hazard correction, safety program development
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a small employer

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide compensatory mitigation program administered by the Maryland Department of the Environment that collects in-lieu fee payments from permit holders who impact wetlands and aquatic resources, and uses those funds to restore, create, enhance, or preserve aquatic resources across Maryland. The program operates three special funds: the Nontidal Wetlands Compensation Fund (accepting payments since 1991), the Tidal Wetlands Compensation Fund (accepting payments since 1996), and a proposed Nontidal Waterways Fund. Funds collected are used to implement wetland mitigation projects across watershed-based service areas, providing pooled funding for larger and more ecologically viable mitigation projects than available on a permit-by-permit basis.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Permittees (those required to provide compensatory mitigation under permit conditions) can pay into the ILF program to transfer their mitigation obligation to MDE. MDE consolidates fees to fund larger mitigation projects (minimum 20 acres for nontidal projects; 0.4 acres for tidal projects; 5,000 linear feet for stream projects). MDE assumes legal responsibility for identifying, implementing, managing, and monitoring mitigation projects including site identification, acquisition, design, permitting, construction, planting, monitoring, remediation, and long-term protection. Funds are deposited in FDIC-insured accounts with interest and earnings remaining in accounts. MDE provides long-term maintenance and protection through perpetual protection mechanisms such as Conservation Easements or Declarations of Restrictive Covenants. Note: the US Army Corps of Engineers currently does not allow use of this program to satisfy federal compensatory mitigation requirements until the program is revised and approved by the Interagency Review Team (IRT).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Permit holders and project proponents who are required to provide compensatory mitigation for impacts to wetlands, waterways, and aquatic resources in Maryland, including developers, utility companies, and any entity with authorized permanent impacts to tidal or nontidal wetlands or waterways.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds must be used to restore, establish, enhance, or preserve wetlands and aquatic resources to replace lost wetland acreage, functions, and values. Eligible uses include: nontidal wetland restoration and creation, tidal wetland restoration and enhancement, stream restoration and enhancement, riparian zone restoration and enhancement, shoreline restoration, agricultural best management practices, invasive species control, floodplain connectivity enhancement, site acquisition, design and construction of mitigation projects, monitoring and remediation during initial monitoring period, and long-term management and perpetual site maintenance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland, organized by watershed-based service areas using Federal 8-digit Hydrologic Unit Codes (HUCs). Service areas include: Youghiogheny River (HUC 05020006), Potomac River (HUC 020700), Western Chesapeake Bay (HUCs 02050306, 02060003, 02060004, 02060006), Eastern Chesapeake Bay (HUCs 02040205, 02060001, 02060002, 02060005, 020801), and Coastal Bays (HUC 02040303). Covers five physiographic provinces: Coastal Plain, Piedmont, Blue Ridge, Valley and Ridge, and Appalachian Plateau.
requirements_list: Applicant must hold a permit that requires compensatory mitigation for impacts to wetlands, waterways, or aquatic resources.
Federal compensatory mitigation requirements cannot currently be satisfied through this program until MDE revises the ILF Instrument and receives IRT approval.
In-kind mitigation required: nontidal wetland impacts must be mitigated with nontidal wetland projects; tidal wetland impacts must be mitigated with tidal wetland projects.
Mitigation must occur within the same service area (watershed) as the permitted impact.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Permittees pay into the appropriate fund (Nontidal Wetlands, Tidal Wetlands, or Waterways Compensation Fund) based on the type and location of their permitted impacts. MDE manages the funds and implements mitigation projects, partnering with the Chesapeake Bay Trust for an RFP process to locate and evaluate mitigation sites. The program is currently under revision to meet federal requirements; a revised ILF Instrument must be approved by the Interagency Review Team before new federal payments are accepted.

structured_extraction.program_name: MDE State Grant Minority and Women's Business Enterprise Program (M/WBE)
structured_extraction.program_description: This program requires recipients of Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) state capital grants — including prime construction contractors and architecture/engineering (A/E) service vendors — to make good-faith efforts to use Minority Business Enterprises (MBEs) and Women's Business Enterprises (WBEs) in state grant-funded procurement contracts. It applies to contract procurement actions funded in part by MDE assistance agreements awarded after October 1, 2008, including grants from the Bay Restoration Fund, Water Pollution Control Fund (grants over $500,000), and Water Supply Financial Assistance Fund (grants over $500,000).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Guidance, checklists, and required forms to help state grant recipients and prime contractors undertake six good-faith efforts to include M/WBE firms in procurement contracts. Covers procurement of construction, equipment, services, and supplies. Applicable to Bay Restoration Fund grants, Water Pollution Control Fund state grants over $500,000 (Biological Nutrient Removal), and Water Supply Financial Assistance Fund grants over $500,000 (Water Supply Grants). All work must be performed entirely within the State of Maryland.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Recipients of MDE state capital grants and their prime contractors and subcontractors working on state grant-funded water infrastructure projects, including MBE and WBE firms seeking subcontracting opportunities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Ensuring M/WBE participation in procurement contracts funded by MDE state grants, including subcontract awards for construction, architecture/engineering, equipment, services, and supplies
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland; applicable to projects funded through Bay Restoration Fund, Water Pollution Control Fund, and Water Supply Financial Assistance Fund. All work must be performed entirely within the State of Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a recipient of MDE state grant funds or a prime contractor/subcontractor on a state grant-funded project
Must demonstrate six good-faith efforts to engage M/WBE firms
Must develop a list of qualified M/WBE firms using MDOT and other resources
Must submit required M/WBE forms and checklists with bid proposals
A/E service consultants receiving grant funds are considered prime contractors and must comply
Must also meet local M/WBE requirements
Include MDE guidance in contracts with primary contractors
Pay subcontractors within 30 days of payment receipt
Provide written notification prior to M/WBE subcontractor termination
Maintain compliance records and bidders lists
Complete MDE forms: Good Faith Efforts Checklist and Solicitation Summary and Results
Continue good faith efforts even after achieving fair share goals
Ensure M/WBEs are aware of contracting opportunities through outreach and recruitment
Solicit MBEs and WBEs whenever they are potential sources
Divide requirements into small tasks when economically feasible
Post solicitations for minimum 30 calendar days before closing date
Advertise in minority, local, and regional papers or Dodge Report
Send invitations to M/WBE trade associations
Contact US-SBA/MBDA/MDOT
Provide prime contractors and MDE with bidders lists
Ensure reasonable delivery schedules
Include 'MDE Grant Insert' in bidding documents
Submit Attachment A with bid proposals and supporting documentation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Follow the six good-faith effort steps in the guidance documents. Use the required checklists and forms (Appendices A, B, C and Recipient Forms). Complete M/WBE Participation Good Faith Efforts Checklist (Sections A-D) and submit Attachment A (Solicitation Summary and Results) with bid proposals. Maintain documentation of bidders lists and good faith efforts. Submit required M/WBE information to MDE DBE Coordinator. Contact the DBE Coordinator at MWIFA for additional guidance.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides financial assistance to replace older, higher-emission diesel school buses with newer, cleaner buses (or electric school buses). The program reduces children's exposure to in-cabin diesel emissions and improves air quality in surrounding communities and roads where buses travel. For FY2023-2024, the program updated its goal to replace older diesel buses with electric buses, providing financial assistance of up to 45% of the purchase price, with charging infrastructure also eligible for funding.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants cover up to 25% of the purchase price (up to $20,000) for replacement of older diesel school buses with new cleaner diesel buses certified to 2019 or newer EPA emissions standards. For FY2023-2024, the program updated its goal to replace older diesel buses with electric buses, providing financial assistance of up to 45% of the purchase price, with charging infrastructure also eligible for funding. The bus owner provides the remaining cost.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Counties and school districts with older diesel school buses, especially those that have previously applied unsuccessfully for federal or state grants; school bus owners and operators seeking to replace diesel buses with electric alternatives
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Replacement of older diesel school buses with new cleaner diesel or zero-emission electric school buses; charging infrastructure for electric buses
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide, with priority for areas with poor air quality such as the Baltimore and Washington DC ozone nonattainment areas
requirements_list: Buses must be replaced with a diesel bus having a 2019 or newer model year engine certified to EPA emissions standards (for earlier cycles), or with electric school buses (FY2023-2024)
Owner must provide funding for the remainder of the purchase price beyond the grant amount
Counties and school districts that previously applied unsuccessfully for federal or state grants are considered first
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants apply through MDE's DERA State Grant process. Contact Tim Shepherd for additional information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A point-of-sale rebate program that helps Marylanders purchase new or used electric vehicles (EVs). The rebate lowers the upfront cost of buying an EV and stacks on top of the federal Clean Vehicle Credit. Low and moderate income households qualify for an additional bonus rebate.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Point-of-sale rebate of $2,500 for a new EV and $1,000 for a used EV for all qualifying Marylanders who also meet the federal Clean Vehicle Credit criteria. Low and moderate income households receive an additional bonus rebate of $5,000 for a new EV and $3,000 for a used EV. Combined with the federal incentive (up to $7,500 new / $4,000 used), qualifying low-to-moderate income households can save up to $15,000 on a new EV or $8,000 on a used EV. A Superuser Bonus provides extra incentives for drivers who commute the farthest and consume roughly twice the average amount of fuel.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents, businesses, and tax-exempt organizations purchasing new or used electric vehicles; additional bonuses for low and moderate income households and high-mileage 'superuser' drivers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of new or used electric vehicles.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to Maryland residents and businesses.
requirements_list: Must meet the criteria to qualify for the federal Clean Vehicle Credit
Low and moderate income households qualify for additional bonus rebate
Superuser Bonus targets individuals and businesses/tax-exempt organizations in Maryland that drive roughly twice the average mileage
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Rebate is applied at the point of sale. Additional details were recommended by the Maryland Commission on Climate Change in 2023; final program details are contingent on funding.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Climate Teach-In is a statewide month-long event held throughout April (Earth Month) that encourages climate change education activities for educators, students, and community members. It empowers people to act to mitigate causes and adapt to impacts of climate change. Participants register, carry out a climate-related activity or discussion during April, and complete a post-event survey to receive a certificate of participation and qualify for prizes.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive educator resources, classroom-ready climate education activities, instructional strategies, and best practices through webinars and resource guides. Upon completion, participants receive a certificate of participation and qualify for prizes. Public recognition is given for contributions to environmental and climate literacy. Organizations can also sponsor the program through a tiered sponsorship package: Climate Leader ($2,000), Climate Champion ($1,000), and Climate Partner ($500 or in-kind), with benefits including logo/name recognition on website and materials, verbal acknowledgment, and funding for environmental field trips, classroom projects, and educational materials/resources.
structured_extraction.program_audience: All Marylanders including teachers and professors, students (pre-school through adulthood), community and faith-based group leaders, state and municipal agency personnel, and organization sustainability leaders interested in climate change education and literacy.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Climate change education initiatives, lesson plan development and implementation, community engagement activities, environmental field trip stipends, classroom/group environmental projects, and environmental materials/resources for educators.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to all Marylanders; activities must occur in Maryland during April (Earth Month).
requirements_list: Complete registration form via SurveyMonkey link or website
Implement proposed lesson plan or climate education activity during April (Earth Month)
Submit summary, feedback, and/or photos after implementation
Activity must have a connection to climate change education
Incorporate climate education into instruction or group activities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Register online using the provided SurveyMonkey link or QR code. Step 2: Receive a follow-up email with additional information. Step 3: Implement a climate education activity or discussion during April. Step 4: Submit follow-up summary, feedback, and/or photos. Step 5: Receive a certificate of participation and qualify for prizes. For sponsorship inquiries, contact Amy Lambert at alambert@eaest.com or 410-527-2470.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Drinking Water Laboratory Certification Program
structured_extraction.program_description: MDE's Laboratory Certification Program (LCP) is the accreditation body for all certified drinking water laboratories in Maryland. It ensures labs meet minimum standards set by the federal Safe Drinking Water Act and state regulations. Only state-certified labs are allowed to analyze compliance samples for Maryland's Public Water Systems. Covers Chemistry, Microbiology, and Radiochemistry testing methods.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides accreditation (certification) to drinking water laboratories in Maryland, authorizing them to analyze compliance samples for public water systems. Certification is required annually and applies to both in-state and out-of-state labs. Labs must submit applications, personnel qualification forms, and fees to maintain or obtain certification. Fees: $400 one-time initial certification fee for new lab applicants; $400 flat fee for out-of-state labs; $250 base fee plus $10 per test method for in-state renewals (federal, state, and local government labs are exempt from renewal fees).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Drinking water laboratories (in-state and out-of-state) seeking certification to analyze compliance samples for Maryland's Public Water Systems, including commercial laboratories, public water systems, wastewater plants, and other laboratory types.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Certification authorizes labs to perform compliance testing of drinking water samples for Maryland's public water systems. Certification fees cover the cost of laboratory certification requests for drinking water methods.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to in-state and out-of-state laboratories seeking to conduct compliance testing for Maryland public water systems. Out-of-state labs are eligible through reciprocal certification (must hold certification in home state or from EPA).

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Environmental Management System (ISO 14001) Implementation Assistance Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides free technical assistance to Maryland companies in developing and implementing Environmental Management Systems (EMSs) based on the global ISO 14001 standard. The program is offered in partnership with the University of Maryland Technology Enterprise Institute and is delivered through workshops, assignments, and on-site visits. Businesses not seeking formal ISO 14001 registration can join the related Greening Your Business Program, which uses workshops and site visits to help participants identify opportunities, set goals, and build green teams. Free sustainability opportunity assessments are also provided to Maryland businesses to identify opportunities for improving energy and water use efficiency, hazardous and non-hazardous waste reduction, wastewater reduction, and process optimization, with a focus on voluntary actions to reduce environmental impacts and costs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free technical assistance to implement an ISO 14001-compliant Environmental Management System, delivered through workshops, assignments, and on-site visits. An alternative non-registration track (Greening Your Business Program) is also available for businesses that want EMS benefits without formal certification. Additionally, facility-wide audits are conducted to identify resource efficiency opportunities and waste reduction, with a written report prioritizing opportunities based on ROI, payback period, environmental impact, feasibility, and priorities, plus in-person or online discussion with other participants to discuss best practices.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Developing and implementing an ISO 14001-based environmental management system at a facility; identifying and acting on resource efficiency and waste reduction opportunities
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to companies located in Maryland statewide

Provide facility information to consultants
