Members share at least five environmental best practices (such as reducing energy and water use or reducing waste) and report measurable results. In return, they receive technical assistance, recognition, visibility on the Maryland Green Registry website, and eligibility for annual Leadership Awards. Open to organizations of all types and sizes throughout Maryland, in both owned and leased space.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Local Government Climate Action Support Program provides free technical assistance and support to local governments in Maryland counties not covered by a CPRG Metropolitan Statistical Areas Planning Grant. The program helps local governments identify high-priority greenhouse gas emissions reduction projects, align efforts statewide, and build capacity for project planning, design, financing, implementation, and tracking. Services are delivered through MDE and the University of Maryland's Environmental Finance Center (EFC) and include project facilitation, education and training, community outreach and engagement, consultation, and direct technical assistance to navigate resources, tools, and financing mechanisms available for climate action projects.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Scrap Tire Program regulates businesses that collect, store, recycle, and process scrap tires. It funds cleanup of illegal scrap tire stockpiles using the Used Tire Cleanup and Recycling Fund, licenses haulers and businesses, enforces scrap tire laws, and supports projects that reduce, recover, and recycle scrap tires. The program is funded by a $1.00 per-tire fee on the first sale of each new tire in Maryland. It also licenses entities that transport, collect, process, recycle, dispose, incinerate, or use scrap tires as tire-derived fuel. The program works with property owners to ensure cleanup of illegal scrap tire stockpiles and issues licenses for scrap tire collection facilities, processors, incinerators, recyclers, and haulers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides regulatory oversight, licensing for scrap tire businesses and haulers, compliance assistance, cleanup of illegal scrap tire stockpiles using the Used Tire Cleanup and Recycling Fund, and public information about proper scrap tire management. The Fund is generated from a $1.00 fee per tire collected on the first sale of each new tire in Maryland. The program does not offer direct financial grants or loans to individuals or businesses. It also issues required licenses for collection facilities, processors, incinerators, recyclers, and haulers.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's statewide eCycling program requires electronics manufacturers to register with the state, pay annual fees based on sales volume, and offer free takeback programs for their covered electronic devices (CEDs). It also directs residents to recycle old electronics through manufacturer takeback programs, retail drop-off sites, and county collection programs to keep harmful materials like lead and mercury out of the environment.

Manufacturers can reduce fees by implementing an approved CED takeback program that is free to consumers and includes data destruction education. Residents can recycle electronics for free through manufacturer takeback programs, retail drop-off locations (Best Buy, Staples, Apple, and others), and county collection sites. County programs may have fees for some items.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Registration fees fund program administration; electronics recycling keeps harmful materials out of landfills, conserves natural resources, and reduces electronic waste

structured_extraction.program_description: The Voluntary Cleanup Program (VCP) allows property owners, prospective purchasers, responsible persons, lenders, and other eligible parties to voluntarily investigate and clean up contaminated properties (brownfields) in Maryland. The program provides state oversight and streamlines the cleanup process by giving applicants certainty about environmental requirements, helping them predict costs and timelines, while ensuring compliance with environmental regulations. Participants who complete the program receive liability releases from the State, including No Further Requirements Determinations (NFRD) or Certificates of Completion (COC), providing protection from future State enforcement actions related to identified contamination, as well as EPA agreement that cleaned-up sites will be considered of no federal interest. Eligible prospective purchasers may also substantially limit their liability before buying a contaminated property. The program works alongside the Brownfields Revitalization Incentive Program, which offers tax credits, loans, and grants for eligible brownfield redevelopment in participating jurisdictions. Applicants intending to use the property for clean or renewable energy may qualify for an application fee waiver.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MDE reviews applications and provides oversight of site investigation, cleanup plans, and environmental assessments throughout the voluntary cleanup process. Participants receive State liability releases (NFRD or COC) upon successful completion. Initial application fee is $10,000 (starting June 1, 2025); subsequent applications for the same property require a $2,000 fee. An expedited Inculpable Person (IP) approval option is available for a $2,000 fee, requiring submission of the Expedited IP Form and a completed Inculpable Person Affidavit. Applicants who intend to use the property for clean or renewable energy may qualify for a fee waiver. MDE notifies applicants within 45 days whether the application is incomplete, accepted, or denied, and issues final site approval letters (NFRD or COC) upon successful cleanup completion. A $2,000 fee is also required for issuance of NFRD or COC with land use controls. Department bills applicants for direct costs exceeding the application fee on a semi-annual basis. Phase II ESAs must be prepared per ASTM E1903 standard.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Environmental site assessment (Phase I and Phase II), investigation, and cleanup of properties contaminated with hazardous substances; redevelopment of brownfield sites; liability protection upon completion of cleanup under MDE oversight.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's voluntary Water Quality Trading Program allows participants to buy and sell Nitrogen, Phosphorus, and Sediment reduction credits through a State marketplace to help restore and protect the Chesapeake Bay and local waterways. Eligible entities can generate water quality credits by implementing best management practices that reduce pollutant loads below an established baseline — one credit equals one pound of pollutant reduction per year. Credit sellers — including wastewater, stormwater, septic system, oyster aquaculture, and agricultural operators — can generate and sell certified credits on Maryland's Trading Registry. Buyers, primarily holders of wastewater discharge (NPDES) permits, can purchase credits through individual bilateral agreements negotiated between buyer and seller based on market supply and demand. Agricultural credits are calculated through the Maryland Nutrient Tracking/Trading Tool (MNTT) and certified by MDA; non-agricultural credits are certified by MDE. A 5% reserve ratio is applied to each certified credit to buffer against credit losses, and all credits are adjusted using Edge of Tide (EoT) factors to account for regional differences in pollutant loads reaching the Chesapeake Bay. Practices funded with public money are not eligible for credit generation during their funded lifespan unless otherwise specified. Purchases are registered with MDE's Trading Administrator by submitting a completed Credit Purchase Form signed by both parties, or through MDA for agricultural credits. The program can also be used to meet Clean Water Act (NPDES) permit requirements, which may require a permit modification.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants can generate tradeable water quality credits (1 credit = 1 pound of pollutant reduction per year) by implementing best management practices in sectors such as stormwater, wastewater, on-site disposal systems, and oyster aquaculture. Credits are certified by MDE and listed on Maryland's Trading Registry for sale. A 5% reserve ratio is applied to each certified credit, and all credits are adjusted using Edge of Tide (EoT) factors based on regional contributions to the Chesapeake Bay. Credit buyers — primarily holders of wastewater discharge (NPDES) permits — can purchase Nitrogen, Phosphorus, and Sediment credits from sellers through individual bilateral agreements, with credit values negotiated between buyer and seller based on market supply and demand. A 2:1 uncertainty ratio is applied when credits are purchased from a non-point source to meet a wastewater permit. Purchases are registered with MDE's Trading Administrator by submitting a completed Credit Purchase Form signed by both buyer and seller. Agricultural credits are calculated through the Maryland Nutrient Tracking/Trading Tool (MNTT), certified by MDA, and registered through the Maryland Department of Agriculture. Permitted entities buying credits to meet permit requirements may need a permit modification. Credits may be purchased to meet permit compliance, WIP target load reduction, local impairment, or water quality benefit objectives.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Wastewater facilities, stormwater managers, septic system operators, oyster aquaculture operations, agricultural producers, regulated entities, NPDES permit holders, non-governmental organizations, private citizens, aggregators, brokers, and industrial wastewater dischargers seeking to generate or purchase water quality credits on Maryland's trading registry.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Generating and selling nitrogen, phosphorus, and sediment reduction credits by implementing qualifying best management practices, or purchasing credits to meet NPDES permit compliance requirements, WIP target load reduction, local impairment, or water quality benefit objectives.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland, focused on Chesapeake Bay watershed restoration. Projects must be located within the Patuxent, Potomac, Eastern Shore, Western Shore, or Maryland Susquehanna Basins. Credits are adjusted by Edge of Tide (EoT) factors based on regional contributions to the Chesapeake Bay. Trades must comply with local water quality standards and impaired waters requirements.
requirements_list: Credits must be certified by MDE (for wastewater, stormwater, septic, and oyster aquaculture) or MDA (for agricultural practices)
Agricultural credits must be calculated using the Maryland Nutrient Tracking/Trading Tool (MNTT) at www.mdnutrienttrading.com
Trading must comply with COMAR 26.08.11 regulations
Participation is voluntary
Meet baseline requirements for the sector-specific practice
Implement a best management practice that achieves a load reduction below the established baseline
Submit a Credit Certification and Registration form to MDE for credit generation
Credit Purchase Form must be completed and signed by both the buyer and the seller for credit purchases
Form must be submitted to the MDE Trading Administrator
All permits must be structured to allow purchased credits to be applied toward permit requirements, which may require permit modification
Purchases of agricultural credits must be registered with the Maryland Department of Agriculture
A 5% reserve ratio is applied to each certified credit
All credits require Edge of Tide (EoT) adjustments
Best management practices implemented with public funding are not eligible for credit generation during their funded lifespan unless otherwise specified
Legal agreement between purchaser and seller required for credit transfer
Generator and purchaser must agree to provide Department/State-approved verifiers access to BMPs during credit lifespan
A 2:1 uncertainty ratio is applied when credits are purchased from a non-point source to meet a wastewater permit
Wastewater facilities must request a minor permit modification to allow credit generation
Wastewater facilities must operate below performance-based benchmark during calendar year and submit Credit Certification and Registration Form with supporting documentation

Oyster aquaculture: valid oyster aquaculture lease required; oysters grown from less than 2 inches shell height in final grow-out location; harvested oysters must be larger than 2.0 inches shell height; oysters must be alive when removed; credits certified only for nitrogen and phosphorus loads
Stormwater BMPs must be from MDE-approved Urban Stormwater and Alternative BMP code list
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review the Frequently Asked Questions document for general program information and getting started. Use the tabs on the program website for information on generating credits, purchasing credits, and accessing the registry and marketplace. To generate credits: meet the baseline requirements for your sector (stormwater, wastewater, on-site disposal, or oyster aquaculture), implement a qualifying best management practice, and submit a Credit Certification and Registration form to MDE. MDE reviews the documentation and, if approved, certifies the credits and publishes them on Maryland's Trading Registry. To purchase credits, submit a completed and signed Credit Purchase Form to the MDE Trading Administrator; for agricultural credits, registration is handled through the Maryland Department of Agriculture. Direct general questions to MDE's Water Quality Trading Program email and agricultural credit questions to MDA's Trading Administrator.

structured_extraction.program_description: A certification program for tier 1, level 1, and level 2 Solar Renewable Energy Facilities for the Maryland Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS). Enables solar PV system owners to obtain certification numbers and trade Solar Renewable Energy Credits (SRECs) to meet the state's RPS compliance requirements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Certifies completed solar PV systems and provides certification numbers for SREC registration and trading. Processes Initial, Proposed Change/Growth, and Decertification applications. Solar system owners can register and earn Renewable Energy Credits (RECs) that can be sold or traded to utilities and other entities seeking to meet Maryland's Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS) requirements. Each credit represents the environmental benefits of 1 megawatt-hour of solar electricity generated.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Solar PV system owners who have completed system installation and are seeking to trade SRECs
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Financial return on solar investment through certification and sale of Solar Renewable Energy Credits (SRECs) representing the environmental attributes of solar energy produced
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland
requirements_list: Must own a solar energy system
Must have completed solar PV system installation
Must register with the Maryland Public Service Commission
Companies must provide Certificate of Good Standing
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register your solar system through the Maryland Public Service Commission. Submit Initial, Proposed Change/Growth, or Decertification applications as applicable. See the Solar PV process guide for registration steps.

structured_extraction.program_description: A certification program for individual vehicle emissions technicians who demonstrate advanced competency in diagnosing and repairing emissions-related vehicle problems in Maryland. Part of the Vehicle Emissions Inspection Program (VEIP), it provides certification and professional development for technicians specializing in emissions systems repair on gasoline-powered on-road motor vehicles.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Individual certification recognizing master-level competency in vehicle emissions repair. Benefits include: a distinctive MCET embroidered patch, access to RepairTrak (internet-based program for managing VEIP repair data and test results), technical assistance, free or low-cost training opportunities, and a newsletter and technical bulletins. Technicians must maintain ASE certifications to retain MCET certification.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Automotive service technicians and mechanics performing emissions-related repairs on gasoline-powered on-road motor vehicles in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Professional certification for vehicle emissions technicians.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland
requirements_list: Valid ASE A-6 (Electrical Systems) certificate
Valid ASE A-8 (Engine Performance) certificate
Valid ASE L-1 (Advanced Engine Performance) certificate
Either: 5+ years full-time emissions repair work experience OR 2+ years full-time vehicle repair education combined with 4+ years full-time emissions repair work experience
Must maintain current ASE renewal certificates to retain MCET certification
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Print and complete the MCET application from www.mde.maryland.gov/veip. Submit application via email to mde.veip@maryland.gov or fax to 410-537-4435. Attach copies of current valid ASE certificates or certification summary. There is no application fee.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal corporate depreciation program that allows businesses to recover investments in solar technologies through depreciation deductions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Allows businesses to recover investments in solar technologies through depreciation deductions on federal taxes.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses investing in solar technologies
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Recovery of costs for solar technology investments through depreciation
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available nationwide including Maryland
requirements_list: Applicant must be a business
Investment must be in solar technologies
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Claim depreciation deductions when filing federal business taxes. See details at the DSIRE program page.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal tax credit for people who buy new qualifying electric vehicles (EVs) or plug-in hybrid electric vehicles (PHEVs).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $7,500 tax credit for qualifying new electric vehicle or plug-in hybrid purchases made in 2023 or after.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals purchasing new qualifying electric or plug-in hybrid vehicles
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of new qualifying electric or plug-in hybrid vehicles
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available nationwide including Maryland
requirements_list: Must purchase a qualifying new electric vehicle or plug-in hybrid electric vehicle in 2023 or later
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Claim the credit when filing your federal income tax return.

structured_extraction.program_name: North American Wetlands Conservation Act Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: Federal matching grants available to states, private groups, and individuals for wetlands conservation projects that further the goals of the North American Waterfowl Management Plan and international migratory bird treaties. Grants support acquisition of land or water rights and restoration, management, or enhancement of wetlands.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal matching grants for acquisition of land and water rights, and for restoration, management, or enhancement of wetlands. Projects must further the North American Waterfowl Management Plan and involve public/private partnerships. Land acquired must become part of the National Wildlife Refuge System unless the Migratory Bird Conservation Commission approves conveyance to a state or private organization that can ensure long-term protection.
structured_extraction.program_audience: States, private groups, or individuals seeking to conduct wetlands conservation projects that support the North American Waterfowl Management Plan and migratory bird treaties through public/private partnerships.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition of land or water rights; restoration, management, or enhancement of wetlands.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Nationwide, including Maryland.
requirements_list: Projects must further the goals of the North American Waterfowl Management Plan and international migratory bird treaties
Projects must entail public/private partnerships
Requires biennial assessments of progress

Land acquired must become part of the National Wildlife Refuge System or be approved by the Migratory Bird Conservation Commission for conveyance to a state or private organization with long-term protection capability
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service North American Waterfowl and Wetlands Office.

structured_extraction.program_name: On-Site Pollution Prevention Technical Assistance for Maryland Businesses
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) offers free, confidential, on-site pollution prevention technical assistance to Maryland businesses, funded through U.S. EPA Pollution Prevention (P2) grants. Independent engineering consultants or engineers from the Maryland Manufacturing Extension Partnership (MD MEP) conduct assessments of business facilities, identifying opportunities to reduce energy, water, and waste usage, cut operating and disposal costs, reduce regulatory liability, and decrease worker exposure to hazardous materials. After each visit, businesses receive a written report with findings, recommendations, and implementation guidance, along with an offer for follow-up assistance. Assessments are confidential, voluntary, and non-regulatory. MDE also shares lessons learned across targeted sectors. The 2024 round targeted five manufacturing sectors: Food and Beverage Manufacturing and Processing; Chemical Manufacturing, Processing and Formulation; Automotive Manufacturing and Maintenance; Aerospace Product and Parts Manufacturing and Maintenance; and Metal Manufacturing and Fabrication. Past sector projects have also served hospitals, hotels, food processing facilities, and minor league baseball stadiums.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free on-site pollution prevention assessments conducted by engineers from the Maryland Manufacturing Extension Partnership (MD MEP) and independent consultants, funded through U.S. EPA Pollution Prevention (P2) grants. Visits typically take about one hour. Businesses receive a written report summarizing findings, recommendations, and implementation guidance, along with an offer for further follow-up assistance. Assessments are confidential, voluntary, and non-regulatory. MDE also shares sector-wide lessons learned after each project cycle. The 2024 round targeted five manufacturing sectors: Food and Beverage Manufacturing and Processing; Chemical Manufacturing, Processing and Formulation; Automotive Manufacturing and Maintenance; Aerospace Product and Parts Manufacturing and Maintenance; and Metal Manufacturing and Fabrication. Past sectors served include hospitals, hotels, food processing facilities, and minor league baseball stadiums.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland businesses in targeted industry sectors, particularly manufacturers, looking to reduce operating costs, improve environmental performance, and reduce energy, water, and waste at their facilities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: On-site facility assessment to identify pollution prevention, resource reduction, and cost-saving opportunities; businesses receive a written report with recommendations and follow-up implementation assistance; MDE shares lessons learned across the sector
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to businesses throughout Maryland
requirements_list: Business must be located in Maryland
Participation is completely voluntary
Must operate in a sector currently targeted by MDE's P2 project cycle

For the 2024 round, must be a manufacturer in one of five eligible sectors: Food and Beverage Manufacturing and Processing; Chemical Manufacturing, Processing and Formulation; Automotive Manufacturing and Maintenance; Aerospace Product and Parts Manufacturing and Maintenance; or Metal Manufacturing and Fabrication
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the online interest form to indicate interest in a free sustainability assessment, or contact MDE's Pollution Prevention Program by calling 410-537-4119, 1-800-633-6101 (ext. 4119), or MD Relay Service at 1-800-735-2258. An engineer will contact you to answer questions and schedule a site visit. Contact MDE for information on currently targeted sectors and how to participate.

structured_extraction.program_name: Onsite Systems Training – Installer Certification Courses
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) Onsite Systems Division offers free, in-person training courses that allow individuals to become certified to install sand mound systems, at-grade systems, and BAT (best available technology) sewage disposal systems in Maryland. Courses also qualify for continuing education units (CEUs). Online renewal courses are available every five years for sand mound and at-grade installer certification holders.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free, full-day, in-person certification courses held at MDE headquarters in Baltimore, offered annually (generally late winter and early spring). Courses cover design, permitting, and construction standards, and require passing a written exam. Initial courses are 4–7.5 hours. Five-year renewal courses are available online and take approximately 2 hours.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals seeking certification or certification renewal to install sand mound, at-grade, or BAT sewage disposal systems in Maryland; also open to on-site regulatory community members for education.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training to obtain or renew installer certifications for onsite sewage disposal systems.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide – available to individuals seeking to install systems in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must pass a written examination for initial certification
Sand mound and at-grade certifications valid for five years; renewal required before expiration
BAT installer certification also requires certification by respective technology manufacturers
Local installation requirements may also apply for BAT systems
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register for the course using the provided Google Forms registration links. If registration is not currently open, fill out the Course Interest List form to be notified when registration opens. For online renewal courses, access the Google Forms-based course, watch the embedded video presentation, and complete the 10 knowledge check questions.

structured_extraction.program_name: Partners for Fish and Wildlife Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A technical and financial assistance program administered by the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service that works in voluntary partnership with private (non-federal) landowners to restore wetlands, streams, river corridors, prairies, grasslands, and other important fish and wildlife habitats for federal trust species including migratory birds, threatened and endangered species, and anadromous fish.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Technical advice on restoration project design and location, and financial assistance to implement restoration projects under voluntary cooperative agreements. Landowner must agree to maintain the restoration project for a minimum of 10 years. Assistance may include wetland hydrology restoration, native planting, fencing, removal of exotic species, prescribed burning, and in-stream habitat reconstruction.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private (non-federal) landowners interested in voluntarily restoring wetlands and other fish and wildlife habitats on their land.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Restoration of wetland hydrology, planting native trees/shrubs/grasslands, fencing and off-stream watering facilities, removal of exotic species, prescribed burning, reconstruction of in-stream aquatic habitat.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Nationwide, including Maryland. Many projects are located near existing National Wildlife Refuge System lands or State Wildlife Management Areas.
requirements_list: Must be a private (non-federal) landowner
Must enter into a voluntary cooperative agreement
Must agree to maintain the restoration project for a minimum of 10 years as specified in the agreement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service Division of Habitat Conservation, Branch of Habitat Restoration. Note that in many states there is a waiting list due to high demand.

structured_extraction.program_description: A partnership between the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) and the University of Maryland Technology Enterprise Institute (MTECH) that places engineering students as summer interns at Maryland manufacturing companies. Interns work with staff to identify process and equipment improvements that save money and reduce environmental impact, including energy efficiency, waste reduction, and material use efficiency. The program has been operating since 2000.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Engineering students are placed as summer interns at participating Maryland manufacturing companies. Interns identify process and equipment improvements that reduce costs and environmental impact, including waste reduction, energy efficiency, VOC reduction, water conservation, and material use efficiency. Projects are funded by a combination of U.S. EPA, MDE, and participating company contributions. In total, interns have identified over $3.7 million in cost savings.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland manufacturing companies seeking to reduce environmental impact and improve operational efficiency through summer intern placements, as well as undergraduate and graduate engineering students
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Identifying and implementing process and equipment improvements to save money and reduce environmental impact, including energy efficiency, waste reduction, material use efficiency, water conservation, and hazardous waste reduction.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to manufacturing companies located in Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a manufacturing company located in Maryland
Willing to participate in cost-sharing funding for the internship project
Must allow student assessment of operations
Companies work with MTECH consulting engineers and university faculty
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Laura Armstrong at MDE (laura.armstrong@maryland.gov, 410-537-4119) for more information about participating as a host company.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative (RGGI) conducts quarterly regional auctions where CO2 allowances are bought and sold. Maryland participates in these multi-state auctions, which are open to corporations, individuals, non-profits, brokers, and environmental advocacy organizations. Participants submit sealed bids and all allowances are sold at a uniform clearing price.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants can purchase CO2 allowances through quarterly sealed-bid auctions. Bids are submitted in multiples of 1,000 allowances. All allowances are sold at a uniform clearing price based on the highest rejected bid. Each participant is limited to purchasing a certain percentage of the allowances offered.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Quarterly; schedule published on RGGI website
structured_extraction.program_audience: Corporations, individuals, non-profit organizations, brokers, and environmental advocacy organizations interested in purchasing CO2 allowances
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of CO2 emission allowances under the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative cap-and-trade program
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Multi-state program; Maryland participates in all quarterly auctions
requirements_list: Submit a Qualification Application
Submit an Intent to Bid
Provide financial security assurances
Disclose direct and indirect corporate associations
Comply with limits on the percentage of allowances that can be purchased
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit a Qualification Application, Intent to Bid, and financial security assurances. RGGI states review and approve qualifications. Approved participants then submit sealed bids in the quarterly auction.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Department of the Environment awards CO2 offset allowances to projects that demonstrate real, additional, verifiable, enforceable, and permanent avoidance of CO2 emissions or reduction of atmospheric CO2 levels. Eligible project types include landfill methane capture, energy efficiency improvements, agricultural manure management, sulfur hexafluoride (SF6) emission reductions, and carbon sequestration through reforestation, improved forest management, or avoided conversion.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MDE awards CO2 offset allowances (tradeable credits under the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative) to qualifying projects that reduce or avoid CO2 and other greenhouse gas emissions. Projects may be located in any participating RGGI state or other approved jurisdiction. A consistency application must be submitted within six months of commencing the project (one year for carbon sequestration projects). Eligible project types include landfill methane capture and destruction (flaring, electricity generation, or direct-use), energy efficiency improvements in commercial and residential buildings targeting natural gas, oil, or propane combustion, avoided methane emissions from agricultural manure management via anaerobic digesters, SF6 emission reductions, and carbon sequestration through reforestation, improved forest management, or avoided conversion.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Within six months of commencing the offset project (one year for carbon sequestration projects); for projects commenced before January 1, 2009: June 30, 2009
structured_extraction.program_audience: Entities operating projects that reduce or avoid greenhouse gas emissions, including landfill operators, agricultural operations, energy efficiency project owners, SF6 users, and forest managers in RGGI participating states.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: CO2 offset allowances are awarded for demonstrated emission reductions and can be used within the RGGI cap-and-trade system. Eligible uses include landfill gas collection and combustion equipment, energy conservation measures in buildings (building envelope, HVAC, combustion equipment upgrades), methane capture and destruction through anaerobic digestion at agricultural facilities, and electricity generation from biogas.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects may be located in any participating RGGI state or other approved jurisdiction. Projects in non-participating states may also be eligible with cooperating regulatory agency compliance. U.S. Forest Projects are also eligible.
requirements_list: Project must demonstrate real, additional, verifiable, enforceable, and permanent avoidance of CO2 emissions or reduction of atmospheric CO2 levels
Consistency application must be submitted to MDE within six months of commencing the project (one year for carbon sequestration projects)
Applications failing to meet deadlines will be denied and the project will remain ineligible
Project must comply with COMAR 26.09.03 regulations
Independent verifier certification required for all project types
Monitoring and Verification Plan required
Annual Monitoring and Verification Reports required
Projects must not receive funding from Strategic Energy Investment Fund or state auction proceeds
Projects must not be used for renewable energy portfolio standard compliance

For landfill methane projects: comprehensive M&V Plan, monthly landfill gas flow meter readings at 15-minute intervals minimum, daily methane concentration instrument readings, annual third-party laboratory analysis, equipment calibration per manufacturer specifications

For energy efficiency building projects: must comply with ASHRAE, RESNET, and IPMVP standards; professional engineer signature required; baseline and post-installation energy use documentation required

For agricultural methane projects: at least 50% of digester input must be manure-based; monthly influent monitoring; quarterly third-party laboratory methane concentration analysis; annual QA/QC reporting
Legal rights to offset project or authorization to act on behalf of rights holder required
For avoided conversion forest projects: forest management practice certification (ATFS, FSC, SFI, or similar) required if commercial timber harvesting occurs
Carbon stock calculations and documentation required for forest projects
Field measurement data collection and documentation required for forest projects
Quality assurance procedures documentation required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Obtain the appropriate application and technical support documents for your project type from the MDE website. Submit a consistency application to MDE within six months of commencing the offset project (one year for carbon sequestration projects). Include required documentation such as project summary, equipment specifications, building plans (for energy efficiency projects), baseline energy/emissions calculations, and Monitoring and Verification Plan. An independent verifier must review and certify the application. Submit annual Monitoring and Verification Reports with verified data. For forest avoided conversion projects, submit Monitoring and Verification Reports with forms 2.1, 2.2, and 3.1, including field data, carbon calculations, and independent verifier certification. MDE reviews applications and awards offset allowances for qualifying projects.

structured_extraction.program_name: Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative (RGGI) in Maryland
structured_extraction.program_description: RGGI is a cooperative, market-based cap-and-invest program among twelve northeast and mid-Atlantic states to reduce carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions from fossil fuel-fired power plants. States set emission budgets and sell allowances at quarterly regional auctions. Since 2005, RGGI states have reduced annual power sector emissions by 50% and raised over $10 billion for community investment. Maryland uses auction proceeds to fund state and local programs that promote energy efficiency, renewable energy, and utility bill assistance for consumers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Regulated fossil fuel-fired power plants (25 MWe or greater nameplate capacity) must acquire CO2 allowances to cover emissions — one allowance equals one short ton of CO2. Allowances are distributed primarily through quarterly regional auctions and can be held, banked, or traded on secondary markets. Offset allowances are limited to 3.3% of emissions for compliance; excess emissions are subject to a three-times penalty deduction. A minimum of 25% of allowance proceeds are allocated to consumer benefit or strategic energy purposes. Auction proceeds fund energy efficiency programs, renewable energy development, direct ratepayer impact mitigation, innovative carbon abatement technology, and utility bill assistance. Cost Containment Reserve (CCR) allowances with tiered trigger prices are available for price stability.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Fossil fuel-fired power plants (25 MWe or greater) subject to CO2 caps; consumers and communities benefiting from auction-funded energy efficiency, renewable energy, and bill assistance programs; retail electricity providers and customers participating in voluntary renewable energy markets.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency measures, renewable or non-carbon-emitting energy technology promotion, direct ratepayer impact mitigation, innovative carbon emissions abatement technology development, voluntary renewable energy market support, and program administration.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland as part of a ten-state regional initiative including Connecticut, Delaware, Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, Rhode Island, and Vermont.
requirements_list: Applies to fossil fuel-fired power plants with nameplate capacity of 25 MWe or greater (15 MWe or greater in New York)
Power plants must hold allowances equal to their CO2 emissions
Allowances are purchased at quarterly regional auctions or on secondary markets
Must maintain a CO2 budget permit
Must establish a COATS account with an authorized account representative and alternate
Must install and maintain Continuous Emissions Monitoring Systems (CEMS) for CO2 mass emissions tracking
Must submit monitoring plans per 40 CFR 75.62
Must submit compliance certification reports by March 1 annually
Must submit annual output reports by March 1 for the preceding calendar year
Must maintain records for 10 years from creation
Offset allowances limited to 3.3% of emissions for compliance
Excess emissions subject to three-times penalty deduction
Submit account certificate of representation
CO2 budget permit application required prior to commencing operation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Power plants participate in quarterly regional CO2 allowance auctions administered through RGGI Inc. Owners and operators must establish a COATS account, obtain a CO2 budget permit, install required monitoring systems, and submit compliance certification reports. Auction proceeds are reinvested by Maryland into consumer benefit programs. Refer to RGGI.org and MDE contacts for specific program participation details.

structured_extraction.program_name: School Waste Reduction and Composting Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Awards grants to schools to reduce food waste and establish composting programs, supporting waste diversion and decarbonization goals in Maryland's waste sector.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants awarded to schools to reduce food waste and establish composting programs. Specific grant amounts are not stated on this page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Schools seeking to reduce food waste and start composting programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reducing food waste and establishing composting programs at schools.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program covers two related activities: (1) issuing Sewage Sludge Utilization Permits to entities seeking to treat, compost, transport, store, distribute, land-apply, incinerate, market, or otherwise utilize sewage sludge (biosolids) in Maryland; and (2) providing formula grants to counties to conduct supplemental inspections and monitoring of sewage sludge utilization sites under contracts between the Maryland Department of the Environment and the requesting county. Permitted activities include treatment, composting, transportation, storage, distribution, land application on agricultural or marginal land, energy generation or incineration, marketing, innovative or research projects, and disposal at a municipal landfill.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MDE issues permits to authorize sewage sludge utilization activities in Maryland. Applicants must submit an application along with a permit fee (ranging from $25 to $750 depending on permit type) and a performance bond or other financial security (such as an irrevocable standby Letter of Credit), except for municipal landfills and government agencies. Bond amounts range from $10,000 for transportation or marketing up to $125,000 for in-state treatment, composting, storage, or distribution facilities. Additionally, the program provides formula grants to counties to fund supplemental inspections and monitoring of sewage sludge utilization sites through contracts with MDE. Regulatory services, technical assistance, and information are also provided. Applicants must also provide an Environmental Justice (EJ) Score from the MDEnviroScreen tool and workers' compensation coverage.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annually (for county grants); rolling for permit applications
structured_extraction.program_audience: Any person or entity seeking to treat, compost, transport, store, distribute, land-apply, incinerate, market, or otherwise utilize sewage sludge in Maryland, as well as county governments seeking funds to conduct supplemental inspections and monitoring of sewage sludge utilization sites.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Permit authorizes specific sewage sludge utilization activities as described in the application, including agricultural land application, marginal land application, energy generation or incineration, composting, treatment, storage, distribution, transportation, and disposal at municipal landfills. County grant funds may be used for supplemental inspections and monitoring of sites where sewage sludge is used.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland; out-of-state facilities may require additional requirements for distribution in Maryland
requirements_list: Must obtain a Sewage Sludge Utilization Permit before engaging in permitted activities unless an exemption under COMAR 26.04.06.09(c) applies
Must submit a completed application with required supporting information depending on the activity type (application must be dated within 6 months of submission)

Must provide a performance bond, liability insurance, irrevocable standby Letter of Credit, or other financial security in the required amount for the proposed activity (except municipal landfills and government agencies)
Must pay the permit application fee (ranging from $25 to $750 depending on permit type)
Must provide an Environmental Justice (EJ) Score from the MDEnviroScreen tool
Must provide evidence of workers' compensation coverage (Certificate of Compliance or Insurance Policy)
Required number of copies varies by permit type (4 or 6 copies plus original)
County applicants for monitoring grants must enter into a contract with the Maryland Department of the Environment

For agricultural land application: owner consent form, site information form, soil conservation plan, soil pH and CEC testing, topographic map, detailed site plan, laboratory analysis of sewage sludge, and other specified materials
For marginal land application: similar requirements to agricultural land application plus future site use description
For energy generation or incineration: air quality permit from MDE (COMAR 26.11.02), detailed operation plan, and other specified materials
For treatment by PFRP: geologic and hydrogeologic information, groundwater protection and monitoring plans, engineering plans, evidence of PFRP standards compliance
For transportation: performance bond ($10,000), detailed operation plan including transportation routes, vehicles, spill/leak procedures
Performance bond requires separate bond per sewage sludge project; 120-day cancellation notice requirement with 60-day substituted security provision
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For permits: Complete the Sewage Sludge Utilization Permit Application and gather required supporting documents based on the activity type. Provide an Environmental Justice (EJ) Score from the MDEnviroScreen tool. Submit the required number of copies (4 or 6 depending on permit type) with the permit fee. Send a photocopy of the application and the permit fee to MDE at P.O. Box 1417, Baltimore, MD 21203-1417. Send the original plus required copies to MDE at 1800 Washington Blvd., Suite 610, Baltimore, MD 21230-1719. For renewal applications: submit updated required documentation including owner's consent form, field information form, updated site maps, current nutrient management plan, and other specified materials. For county grants: Counties should contact MDE to establish a contract for supplemental inspection and monitoring services.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grant assistance primarily to small and disadvantaged communities for planning, design, and construction of wastewater and sewerage facility improvements needed to address high priority public health or water quality problems. The program supplements water quality loan programs, particularly where affordability is a concern. Grants are not to exceed $1.5 million per award, based on system size, compliance status, and affordability. A local match is required.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding not to exceed $1.5 million per award for local governments to supplement water quality loan programs for sewerage facilities, particularly where affordability is a concern or where public health or water quality issues exist. Award amounts are based on system size, compliance status, and affordability. A local match is required. Covers planning, design, and construction of wastewater and sewer infrastructure improvements, including advanced wastewater treatment, CSO/SSO correction, aging sewer rehabilitation, sewer extensions, landfill leachate treatment, and energy/water conservation. Low-interest State Revolving Fund loans are also available. Applications open December 1 through January 31 annually.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governmental entities, public water and sewerage systems, community water systems, and municipalities — especially small and disadvantaged communities — with sewerage facility or wastewater improvement needs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planning, design, and construction of wastewater and sewer infrastructure improvements to address high priority public health or water quality problems; supplementing water quality loan programs where affordability is a concern; advanced wastewater treatment, CSO/SSO correction, aging sewer rehabilitation, sewer extensions, landfill leachate treatment, and energy/water conservation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland; priority given to small and disadvantaged communities. Projects must be located within Priority Funding Areas (PFAs) or qualify for a PFA exception or categorical exemption.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local government, public water/sewerage system, or community water system
Priority given to small and disadvantaged communities
Projects must address high priority public health or water quality problems
Local match required
Award amount based on system size, compliance status, and affordability
Maximum grant award of $1.5 million
Projects must be located within Priority Funding Areas (PFAs) or qualify for a PFA exception
Applications accepted during open solicitation window (December 1 through January 31 annually)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application during the open solicitation window, which runs from December 1 through January 31 annually. Contact MWIFA at 410-537-3908 for details.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Maryland program that provides technical and financial assistance to landowners, communities, local governments, and businesses to complete structural and non-structural shoreline and streambank erosion control projects along the Chesapeake Bay and its tributaries.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance for non-structural shoreline stabilization projects is provided as: (1) 75% interest-free loans for projects on private and public lands using State special funds; or (2) 75%-25% matching grants for projects on public lands using Federal funds. Technical assistance is also provided through site evaluations, problem assessments, and recommended solutions.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners, communities, local governments, and businesses whose land abuts a body of water in Maryland and who need help addressing shoreline or streambank erosion.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Design, construction, management, and financing of streambank or shoreline erosion control projects, including vegetative buffers and structural measures.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to owners of property abutting a body of water in Maryland, primarily along the Chesapeake Bay and its tributaries.
requirements_list: Applicant must own or control property abutting a body of water in Maryland
Must file an application requesting assistance
Financial assistance for non-structural projects only
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The owner of property abutting a body of water in Maryland files an application with Shore Erosion Control requesting assistance in the design, construction, management, and financing of an erosion control project. Shore Erosion Control then provides technical assistance and, for eligible projects, financial assistance through loans or matching grants.

structured_extraction.program_name: Source Collection And Threat Reduction (SCATR) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The SCATR Program helps Maryland radioactive material licensees properly dispose of unwanted sealed radioactive sources. The program provides financial assistance to cover costs of packaging, transportation, and disposal of unused radioactive material that could otherwise pose a security risk.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance (SCATR funds combined with licensee funds) to cover costs of packaging, transportation, and disposal of unwanted radioactive material sealed sources. The program is coordinated through the Conference of Radiation Control Program Directors (CRCPD), Los Alamos National Laboratory, and the Department of Energy's National Nuclear Security Administration.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland Radioactive Material Licensees who have unwanted radioactive material sealed sources
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Packaging, transportation, and disposal of unwanted radioactive material sealed sources
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Maryland Radioactive Material Licensees statewide
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland Radioactive Material Licensee
Must have unwanted radioactive material sealed sources
Material must be identified and registered
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Identify and register radioactive material for disposal, find outlets for the material, obtain commitment for SCATR funds, enter a contract for packaging, transportation, and disposal, and move material to a collection point. Registration instructions are available on the CRCPD website at www.crcpd.org/page/SCATR.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants for water quality point source projects, non-point source pollution control, drinking water system upgrades, and septic system upgrades using best available technology for nitrogen removal on onsite sewage disposal systems.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants for water quality and septic system projects. Between FY21 and FY23, the program provided $45 million in revenues for 2,567 Best Available Technology (BAT) installations and 497 connections to public sewer.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Water and wastewater system operators, local governments, and property owners seeking funding for septic and water quality upgrades.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Best available technology (BAT) septic installations, connections to public sewer, drinking water system upgrades, and water quality improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Energy Administration (MEA) provides grants for energy efficiency and decarbonization projects at industrial facilities across Maryland. The state also plans to expand support for decarbonization activities, with priority investments in cement manufacturing decarbonization and hydrofluorocarbon (HFC) reduction.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are available for energy efficiency and decarbonization projects at industrial facilities. MDE, MEA, and the Maryland Clean Energy Center (MCEC) also provide staff capacity to help industry access grants and financing for emissions reduction projects.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Industrial facilities in Maryland seeking to reduce energy use and greenhouse gas emissions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency improvements and decarbonization projects at industrial facilities, including cement manufacturing decarbonization and HFC reduction.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be an industrial facility located in Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: MDE, MEA, and MCEC staff work with industry to streamline access to grants and financing for emissions reduction projects.

structured_extraction.program_name: State Revolving Fund Disadvantaged Business Enterprise Program (DBE)
structured_extraction.program_description: This program requires recipients of Maryland Water Quality and Drinking Water State Revolving Loan Fund (SRF) loans — including prime contractors and subcontractors — to make good-faith efforts to award a fair share of contract work to Disadvantaged Business Enterprises (DBEs), including small business enterprises (SBEs), minority business enterprises (MBEs), and women's business enterprises (WBEs). The program is a federal requirement tied to EPA funding (governed by Federal regulation Title 40, Part 33) and sets participation goals for construction, equipment, services, and supplies.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Guidance and compliance requirements for SRF loan recipients, prime contractors, and subcontractors to undertake six good-faith efforts to provide DBE firms (MBEs, WBEs, SBEs) opportunities in construction, equipment, services, and supply contracts. MDE sets negotiated DBE participation goals with EPA: Construction MBE 22%, WBE 16%; Equipment MBE 23%, WBE 11%; Services MBE 25%, WBE 18%; Supplies MBE 23%, WBE 11%. Goals are not quotas. Also provides resource referrals and directory listings connecting loan recipients and bidders with qualified MBE/WBE firms.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Recipients of Maryland Water Quality and Drinking Water State Revolving Loan Fund loans, prime contractors, and subcontractors working on SRF-funded projects; DBE/MBE/WBE firms seeking contracting opportunities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Ensuring DBE participation in procurement contracts (construction, equipment, services, and supplies) funded by Clean Water or Drinking Water Revolving Loan funds
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland; applicable to projects funded through MDE Clean Water and Drinking Water Revolving Funds; EPA Region 3 jurisdiction
requirements_list: Must be a recipient of SRF loan funds or a prime contractor/subcontractor on an SRF-funded project
Must demonstrate six good-faith efforts to engage DBE firms
Must maintain a DBE bidders list throughout the project construction period
Prime contractors must complete EPA forms 6100-2, 6100-3, and 6100-4 and submit with bid proposal
Must include MDE DBE Insert/Requirements and Contract Provisions in bidding documents
Advertise in minority, local, regional papers or Dodge Report
Contact DBE trade associations, US-SBA, MBDA, MDOT
Break down projects into smaller components where economically feasible for DBE bidding
Allow minimum 30 days for DBE bidding
Prime contractors must pay DBE subcontractors within 30 days of payment receipt
Prime contractors must provide written notice before terminating DBE subcontractors
Maintain documentation of good faith efforts and compliance records
Notify recipient prior to DBE subcontractor termination
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Follow the six good-faith effort steps outlined in the guidance documents. Use the provided checklists and EPA forms (6100-2, 6100-3, 6100-4). Submit required forms with bid proposals. Search MBE/WBE directories and contact relevant organizations from the resource listing. Contact the DBE Coordinator at MWQFA for additional guidance.

structured_extraction.program_description: The State Revolving Loan Fund provides low-interest financing to local governments, private landowners, and water system owners for capital improvements that protect or improve water quality and provide safe drinking water. Loans are available through the Drinking Water Revolving Loan Fund (DWRLF) and the Water Quality Revolving Loan Fund (WQRLF), administered by the Maryland Water Infrastructure Financing Administration (MWIFA). The program encourages infrastructure improvements to ensure safe drinking water and improved water quality across Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest loans with terms up to 30 years (up to 40 years for Disadvantaged Communities for DWRLF, not to exceed useful life of asset). Standard interest rate for FY2024 ranged from 1.60% to 2.00% (excluding admin fee). Disadvantaged Community rate ranged from 0.80% to 1.00%. An annual administrative fee of 5% of aggregate debt service divided by the loan term is collected. Rates change monthly based on the Bond Buyer 11-Bond Index (BB11-BI). Additional principal forgiveness or grants may be available for Disadvantaged Communities. Applications are accepted in December of each year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, private landowners, and water system owners seeking financing for drinking water or water quality infrastructure projects, including those serving Disadvantaged Communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital improvements to protect or improve water quality and provide safe drinking water, including drinking water and wastewater infrastructure projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local jurisdiction, government entity, private landowner, or water system owner
Disadvantaged Community designation required for reduced interest rates and potential principal forgiveness or grants
Loan term may not exceed useful life of the asset
Applications accepted in December of each year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted in December of each year. Contact MWIFA at (410) 537-3908 for additional information on applying.

structured_extraction.program_name: Technical Assistance Grants for Small Fleet Electrification
structured_extraction.program_description: Grants that provide technical assistance to owners of small vehicle fleets to help them develop fleet electrification plans, supporting the transition from gasoline and diesel vehicles to electric vehicles.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Technical assistance grants to help owners of small fleets (10–199 vehicles) develop fleet electrification plans. Fleet vehicles are typically driven more miles annually than average vehicles, so they have an outsized impact on transportation emissions.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of small vehicle fleets with 10 to 199 vehicles located in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Development of fleet electrification plans.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to Maryland-based fleet owners.
requirements_list: Must own or operate a fleet of 10–199 vehicles
Fleet must be located in Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Not specified on this page. Additional details available in the 2023 Annual Report of the Maryland Commission on Climate Change.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal tax credit for people who buy a used qualifying electric vehicle (EV) or fuel cell vehicle (FCV).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to 30% of the sale price for qualifying used electric vehicle or fuel cell vehicle purchases, with a maximum credit of $4,000.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals purchasing used qualifying electric or fuel cell vehicles
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of a qualifying used electric or fuel cell vehicle
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available nationwide including Maryland
requirements_list: Must purchase a qualifying used electric vehicle or fuel cell vehicle
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Claim the credit when filing your federal income tax return.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides financial assistance for projects that replace older diesel-powered heavy-duty vehicles with cleaner alternatives and supports installation of electric vehicle charging stations to reduce emissions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance for vehicle replacement projects targeting older diesel-powered heavy-duty vehicles and installation of electric vehicle charging stations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners and operators of older diesel-powered heavy-duty vehicles
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Replacement of older diesel vehicles with cleaner alternatives; installation of electric vehicle charging stations
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland

structured_extraction.program_name: Volkswagen Settlement Grants – EV Charging Infrastructure (Charge Ahead Grant Program)
structured_extraction.program_description: Grants funded by Maryland's share of the Volkswagen emissions settlement to support the purchase and installation of Level 2 electric vehicle (EV) charging equipment at workplaces, making EV charging more accessible across the state and reducing air pollution.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are available for the purchase and installation of Level 2 EV charging infrastructure at workplaces. This is the third and final round of funding. Specific award amounts vary by project proposal.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses, nonprofits, and government entities seeking to install Level 2 EV charging equipment at workplaces in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and installation of Level 2 electric vehicle charging equipment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must follow the updated Charge Ahead Grant Program Framework (Round 3)
Must submit a project proposal form
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Read the Charge Ahead Grant Program Framework carefully, then submit a project proposal using the provided application form before the deadline.

structured_extraction.program_name: Voluntary Cleanup Program (VCP) Clean and Renewable Energy Application Fee Waiver
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Voluntary Cleanup Program (VCP) waives the application fee for developers who plan to build clean or renewable energy projects on brownfield sites (contaminated or degraded lands). Participants also receive liability protection after cleaning up the brownfield site and, in qualifying jurisdictions, may access brownfield tax incentives. The program encourages investigation and cleanup of contaminated properties intended for clean/renewable energy use and provides predictability and finality to cleanup of eligible properties.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Waives the VCP application fee (initial $6,000 for new projects or $2,000 for a subsequent application for the same or contiguous/adjacent properties) for applicants who certify their intention to use an eligible brownfield property to generate clean or renewable energy at an anticipated yearly output of at least 2 megawatts. Participants also receive liability protection following site remediation and may qualify for brownfield tax incentives in participating jurisdictions. The fee waiver became effective January 1, 2022.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Developers, property owners, and other applicants seeking to locate clean or renewable energy projects on brownfield or contaminated sites in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Fee waiver covers the VCP application fee when redeveloping brownfield sites with clean or renewable energy projects such as solar, wind, geothermal, or biomass plants, with a minimum anticipated yearly energy output of 2 megawatts.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland for eligible brownfield sites subject to VCP application.
requirements_list: Applicant must apply to the Voluntary Cleanup Program (VCP)
Applicant must certify their intention to use the eligible property to generate clean or renewable energy
Property must qualify as a brownfield or degraded land under VCP criteria
Clean or renewable energy project as defined by COMAR 26.14.3.02B(4) and (16)
Anticipated yearly clean or renewable energy output of at least 2 megawatts
Submit completed Clean or Renewable Energy Certification form with VCP application
Form must be signed, dated, and notarized
Certification must include: energy type, anticipated yearly output, construction schedule, and anticipated energy generation start date
Applicant must be authorized representative with legal authority to execute affidavit
Site location map must be attached
Information must be accurate and complete under penalty of law
Within 5 years of receiving NFRD or COC, verify property is generating clean/renewable energy as certified, including current yearly energy output
Must meet criteria established in COMAR 26.14.03
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the VCP application on an MDE-provided form and submit a VCP Clean and Renewable Energy Fee Waiver Certification form along with the standard VCP application to MDE's Land Restoration Program. The fee waiver became available on January 1, 2022.

structured_extraction.program_name: WIIN Act Section 2107 Grant Funding for Lead Remediation in Schools
structured_extraction.program_description: This grant program provides funding to Maryland local educational agencies (LEAs) to help test for and remove sources of lead in drinking water at schools. The U.S. EPA awarded the grant to the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) under the Water Infrastructure Improvements for the Nation (WIIN) Act, Section 2107. Funds can be used for materials and labor for lead remediation projects, with priority given to schools serving lower-income children and young children, schools where at least 50% of students receive free or reduced-price meals, schools that primarily serve children 6 years old and under, and schools built before 1988.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funds cover materials and labor costs for lead remediation projects at schools, including permanently closing access to outlets, removing outlets, installing and maintaining point-of-use filters, repairing outlets/plumbing/service lines, reconfiguring outlets/plumbing/service lines, replacing outlets/plumbing/service lines, installing and maintaining automatic flushing of outlets, and checking and replacing grounding wires. Funds are available as reimbursement for projects completed between November 15, 2021 and the application date, or disbursed after completion of planned projects to be completed by September 30, 2022. Priority is given to schools where at least 50% of students receive free or reduced-price meals, schools that primarily serve children 6 years old and under, and schools built before 1988. Eligible project dates run from November 15, 2021 through September 30, 2022.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: June 22, 2022 (application period); remediation projects must be completed by September 30, 2022
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local educational agencies (LEAs) / school districts in Maryland seeking funding to test for and remove lead from drinking water in public and nonpublic schools.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Materials and labor costs for lead remediation of drinking water outlets at schools, including permanently closing access to outlets, removing outlets, installing and maintaining point-of-use filters, repairing outlets/plumbing/service lines, reconfiguring outlets/plumbing/service lines, replacing outlets/plumbing/service lines, installing and maintaining automatic flushing of outlets, and checking and replacing grounding wires. Covers both completed projects (reimbursement) and planned projects (disbursement after completion).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland school districts are eligible to apply.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local educational agency (LEA) / school district in Maryland
Remediation projects must occur between November 15, 2021 and September 30, 2022
All required documentation must be submitted to MDE no later than September 8, 2022
Application must include percentage of students receiving free or reduced-price meals, Head Start program status, grade range served, funding amount requested, and school/contact information
Must provide the year the school building was constructed
Must provide invoices (for completed projects) or estimates (for future projects) for materials and labor
Priority given to schools with at least 50% of students receiving free and reduced price meals
Priority given to schools that primarily care for children 6 years and under
Priority given to schools built before 1988
LEAs first complete a short interest poll (one required and three optional questions); each LEA designates one person to complete the poll on behalf of the entire school district
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: MDE opened an application period from June 1 through June 22, 2022. LEAs first completed a short interest poll by March 25, 2022. When the application period opened, applicants submitted the provided Excel application form to MDE including school information, meal subsidy percentages, Head Start status, grade ranges, construction year, and invoices or estimates for remediation work. Applications are evaluated after the close of the application period. Funds for completed projects are reimbursed as soon as possible after the award decision date; funds for planned projects are disbursed after work is completed and documentation is received.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Water Quality Revolving Loan Fund (WQRLF) provides below-market interest rate revolving loans to local governments and other eligible entities to finance a wide variety of projects to protect or improve the quality of Maryland's rivers, streams, lakes, the Chesapeake Bay, and other water resources, consistent with the Federal Clean Water Act. It supports both point source and nonpoint source pollution prevention projects. Funded by federal EPA and state sources, MWIFA may issue revenue bonds to support the fund. The Maryland Water Infrastructure Financing Administration (MWIFA) also offers financial advisory services to help applicants determine affordable user rate structures and model the fiscal impact of the proposed loan. The program also provides grants and loan principal forgiveness for eligible water quality capital improvement projects. Established pursuant to the Clean Water Act of 1987 and Maryland Water Quality Financing Administration Act, the program uses an Integrated Project Priority System to rate and rank projects for an annual Project Priority List (PPL).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Below-market interest rate revolving loans, project grants, and loan principal forgiveness funded by federal EPA and state sources for water quality improvement projects consistent with the Federal Clean Water Act. Current interest rates: Standard Rate = 50% of Market Rate; Disadvantaged Community (DAC) Rate = 25% of Market Rate. Loan terms up to 30-40 years (not to exceed useful life of asset); no loan origination fees; 5% annual administrative fee. Up to 50% principal forgiveness (max $1.5 million per fiscal year per applicant) for disadvantaged communities. Up to 87.5% as Bay Restoration Fund (BRF) wastewater grants. IIJA General Supplemental grants with loan principal and forgiveness; IIJA Emerging Contaminants grants. Point source pollution prevention loans are available to public entities and local governments only. Nonpoint source pollution prevention loans are available to both public and private entities through a linked deposit program. MDE/MWIFA also provides financial advisory services to help applicants assess user rate structures and fiscal impact. MWIFA may issue revenue bonds to support the fund. Applications are accepted December through January each year.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted December 1 through January 31 annually; applications will reopen in December 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public entities, local governments, for-profit businesses, individuals, and private entities seeking to fund projects that protect or improve water quality in Maryland, including wastewater treatment and nonpoint source pollution control capital projects. Also includes public small and large water/wastewater systems, communities with disadvantaged status, and entities with MS4 stormwater permits.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Wastewater treatment plant improvements and expansion, sewerage collection and conveyance systems, sewer infiltration and inflow correction, combined sewer overflow correction, sludge handling facilities, landfill leachate pretreatment, backwash facilities at drinking water treatment plants, stormwater best management practices (gray and green infrastructure), wellhead protection, landfill closure, stream corridor restoration, hazardous waste cleanup (brownfields), shoreline erosion control, agricultural nutrient management plans, forestry efforts using tools like the Maryland Forest Financing Implementation Tool (MD FFIT), nonpoint source pollution control, water quality point source projects, pump station replacements and upgrades, septic system elimination and connections to public sewers, enhanced nutrient removal (ENR), biosolids processing and PFAS reduction facilities, dam repair and rehabilitation, wetland restoration/creation, energy and water conservation, and other water quality and public health improvement capital projects consistent with the Federal Clean Water Act.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland for projects that protect or improve Maryland water resources. Projects in the Chesapeake Bay Watershed and Maryland Coastal Bays Watersheds receive priority.
