Projects for treatment works must be located within a Priority Funding Area (PFA) or have a PFA exception or categorical exemption. Projects must also comply with county Comprehensive Land Use Plans and Water & Sewerage Plans.
requirements_list: Point source pollution prevention projects are limited to public entities and local governments
Nonpoint source pollution prevention projects are open to both public and private entities (via linked deposit program)
Projects must protect or improve quality of Maryland's water resources
Projects must be consistent with the Federal Clean Water Act
Treatment works projects must be located within Priority Funding Areas (PFA) or have a PFA exception or categorical exemption
Projects evaluated on nitrogen removal cost efficiency ($/lb TN per year)
Climate resilience to disasters and extreme weather must be considered
Sustainability criteria apply (expansion <20% EDU growth or support for sustainable community development)
Environmental Justice criteria considered in project scoring
Projects must comply with county Comprehensive Land Use Plan and Water & Sewerage Plan
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application during the open solicitation window (December 1 through January 31 each year). Applications are currently closed and will reopen in December 2026. Projects are rated and ranked using the Integrated Project Priority System to develop an annual Project Priority List (PPL). For more information, call 410-537-3908.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide certification program for individuals who collect drinking water samples for public water systems in Maryland. Certification ensures that Safe Drinking Water Act compliance samples are collected properly and that samplers meet all current regulatory requirements under state law. Certification cards are valid for a maximum of three years.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Training classes and a required examination to become a certified water sampler in Maryland. Certification card is valid for a maximum of three years and assures reliability of Safe Drinking Water Act compliance samples submitted to state certified laboratories. Registration and examination are handled by the Maryland Rural Water Association (MRWA). First-time applicants must also complete a Hands-On Practicum Skills Test. As of January 1, 2025, there are new requirements for first-time samplers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Laboratory personnel, water system operators and superintendents, county and state health department staff, and other individuals who collect drinking water samples for public water systems in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and examination to obtain certification for collecting Safe Drinking Water Act compliance samples for public water systems.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be laboratory personnel, a water system operator/superintendent, county/state health department staff, or other individual collecting samples for a Public Water System
Minimum high school education required
No prior experience required
Must register for and complete the Water Sampler Class through MRWA and pass the required examination
First-time applicants must also complete a Hands-On Practicum Skills Test
Certification card is valid for a maximum of three years and must be renewed
As of January 1, 2025, first-time samplers must meet new certification requirements (see MRWA website for details)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Register for a Water Sampler Class through the Maryland Rural Water Association (MRWA) website. 2. Complete the class and pass the required examination. 3. First-time applicants must also complete a Hands-On Practicum Skills Test. 4. Receive Sampler Certification Card via email. Contact MRWA at training@md-rwa.org or (410) 489-5877 for class registration questions, or MDE at mde.labcertification@maryland.gov or (410) 537-3729 for program questions.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides state grants to local governments. The grants help pay for capital improvement projects for drinking water systems.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides project grants to support capital improvements for drinking water systems.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, including counties and municipalities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used for capital improvement projects for drinking water systems.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grant assistance to small communities for the acquisition, construction, rehabilitation, and improvement of publicly-owned water supply facilities. Priority is given to disadvantaged communities and those not meeting drinking water standards.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant assistance for acquisition, construction, rehabilitation, and improvement of publicly-owned water supply facilities throughout the state. Priority given to disadvantaged communities and/or communities non-compliant with drinking water standards. Applications are accepted December through January each year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small communities seeking to improve publicly-owned water supply facilities, particularly disadvantaged communities or those not meeting drinking water standards.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition, construction, rehabilitation, and improvement of publicly-owned water supply facilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland; priority to disadvantaged communities and/or communities non-compliant with drinking water standards.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local government or public water system
Priority given to disadvantaged communities
Priority given to communities non-compliant with drinking water standards
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications accepted December through January each year. Contact MWIFA at (410) 537-3908 for details.

structured_extraction.program_name: Watershed Protection and Flood Prevention Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A USDA program that provides technical and financial assistance to local sponsoring organizations and state and public agencies to voluntarily plan and install watershed-based projects on private lands. Projects address natural resource and economic problems on a watershed basis.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: NRCS provides both technical and financial assistance. The 1990 Farm Bill amended the program to allow federal cost sharing of 50% or more for acquiring perpetual easements on wetlands or floodplains for conservation or flood prevention. Projects must be in watersheds of 250,000 or fewer acres.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Native American tribes, state or local governments, soil or water conservation districts, flood prevention or control districts, nonprofit water users' associations, and similar organizations that can carry out and maintain improvement projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Watershed protection, flood prevention, erosion and sediment control, water supply, water quality, fish and wildlife habitat enhancement, wetland creation and restoration, and public recreation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Nationwide program available through NRCS office in Annapolis, Maryland.
requirements_list: Eligible organizations include Native American tribes, state or local governments, soil or water conservation districts, flood prevention or control districts, nonprofit water users' associations, and similar organizations
Projects must be in watersheds of 250,000 or fewer acres
Organizations must be able to carry out and maintain improvement projects
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the local NRCS office to discuss project eligibility and planning. NRCS works with local sponsoring organizations to plan and implement watershed-based projects.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Wellhead Protection Program, administered by the Maryland Department of the Environment, provides technical assistance, financial assistance, and zero percent interest loans to local governments and water supply systems to help protect public drinking water supplies. The program supports wellhead protection projects, land acquisition, and conservation easements within wellhead protection areas to manage activities that might affect source water quality. Applications are accepted in December each year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Zero percent interest loans and financial assistance are available to local governments and water supply systems for wellhead protection projects and to purchase land or conservation easements within wellhead protection areas. Technical assistance includes help delineating wellhead protection areas, providing lists of regulated activities within those areas, and connecting communities with other agencies that can assist in protection efforts. Applications are accepted in December of each year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, public water suppliers, and water supply systems seeking to protect public drinking water supplies
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of land or conservation easements within wellhead protection areas; wellhead protection projects and source water protection land acquisition
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local government, public water supplier, or water supply system
Funds must be used to purchase land or conservation easements within a designated wellhead protection area, or for wellhead protection projects
Applications are accepted in December of each year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact MDE's Water Supply Program, Source Protection and Appropriation Division at (410) 537-3714 for information on how to apply. Applications are accepted in December of each year.

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary USDA program that offers landowners the opportunity to protect, restore, and enhance wetlands on their property in exchange for financial payments and technical assistance. The program targets previously drained or converted agricultural and timber lands.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: NRCS provides technical and financial support. Payment is based on the agricultural value of the land. Three enrollment options are available: permanent easements, 30-year easements, or 10-year restoration cost-share agreements. To offer a permanent or 30-year easement, the landowner must have owned the land for at least one year prior to enrollment. The landowner retains ownership and can retain hunting, fishing, and recreational use rights.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private landowners who own wetlands that have been drained or converted to agricultural or timber production uses and want to restore and protect them.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Restoration, protection, and enhancement of wetlands and associated upland habitat on private lands.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Nationwide program; NRCS service center located in each Maryland county.
requirements_list: Land must be restorable and suitable for wildlife benefits
Must have owned land at least one year prior to enrollment for permanent or 30-year easement
Ineligible land includes wetlands converted after December 23, 1985, certain CRP contract lands with established trees, federal lands, and lands where restoration is impossible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Landowners contact their local USDA Service Center or the NRCS Annapolis Service Center to apply. NRCS provides technical assistance and works with landowners to determine eligibility and select the appropriate enrollment option (permanent easement, 30-year easement, or 10-year cost-share agreement).

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary USDA program that provides technical assistance and cost-share payments to landowners who want to develop and improve wildlife habitat primarily on private lands.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: USDA pays up to 75% of the cost of installing wildlife habitat practices. Cost-share agreements generally last 5 to 10 years. Participants prepare a wildlife habitat development plan with NRCS help. Cost-share payments may be used to establish new practices or replace practices that fail for reasons beyond the landowner's control.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private landowners and those who control land and want to develop and improve wildlife habitat.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Establishing and improving fish and wildlife habitat on private lands through practices such as planting, habitat development, and related improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Nationwide program available in Maryland through local USDA Service Centers.
requirements_list: Participants must own or control the land under consideration
Federal land is ineligible
Land enrolled in Water Bank Program, Conservation Reserve Program, Wetlands Reserve Program, or similar programs is ineligible
Land subject to Emergency Watershed Protection Program floodplain easement is ineligible
WHIP funds cannot be used for mitigation or on converted wetland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Landowners contact their local USDA Service Center or NRCS office. NRCS helps participants prepare a wildlife habitat development plan in consultation with the local conservation district. USDA and the participant then enter into a cost-share agreement.

structured_extraction.program_description: Federal grant funding administered by the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) under Section 319(h) of the Clean Water Act to reduce or eliminate water quality problems caused by nonpoint source pollution — runoff from land that carries pollutants into waterways. Funds support planning, design, construction, monitoring, and analysis of projects that implement best management practices and outreach efforts to improve water quality in impaired Maryland watersheds. This is a reimbursement-style grant, meaning recipients must spend their own funds first and then receive reimbursement.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement-style grants provided under Section 319(h) of the Clean Water Act for planning, design, construction, monitoring, and analysis of projects that reduce or eliminate water quality impairments from nonpoint source pollution, including implementation of best management practices and outreach initiatives. Grant amounts typically range from $30,000 to $400,000, with approximately $1 million total available for FY2026. No matching funds required — the State of Maryland covers the 40% federal match. Recipients must have funding capacity to pay costs upfront before receiving reimbursement. Eligible entities include county and municipal agencies, Soil Conservation Districts, state agencies, state institutions of higher learning, private firms, and nonprofit organizations. A Request for Proposals is released each spring with a summer/fall submission deadline. Specific amounts and terms are described in the RFP.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: The RFP for FFY26 funding closed September 30, 2025. The next RFP for FFY27 funding will open on July 1, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: County and municipal agencies, Soil Conservation Districts, state agencies, state institutions of higher learning, private firms, and nonprofit organizations in Maryland seeking to implement water quality improvement projects and reduce nonpoint source pollution entering Maryland's waterways.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planning, design, construction, monitoring, and analysis of projects that reduce or eliminate water quality impairments listed on Maryland's 303(d) List of Impaired Waters, particularly in watersheds with approved Total Maximum Daily Loads (TMDLs), as well as implementation of best management practices and outreach initiatives to reduce nonpoint source pollution (e.g., stormwater runoff, agricultural runoff).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Implementation projects (involving in-ground construction) typically require EPA-accepted nine-element watershed-based plans for the specific watershed. Communities without watershed-based plans may be eligible for a waiver. Specific eligible watersheds include Aaron Run, Antietam Creek, Assawoman Bay, Casselman River, Corsica River, Lower Jones Falls, Middle Gwynns Falls, Lower Monocacy River, Sassafras River, Spring Branch, Tidal Back River, Upper Back River, Upper Choptank River, and Upper Jennings Run, among others.
requirements_list: Applicants must demonstrate capacity in grant management and funding, as this is a reimbursement-style grant requiring upfront funding by the recipient.
Justification of financial and management capacity must be included in the proposal.

Implementation projects (in-the-ground construction) typically require an EPA-accepted nine-element watershed-based plan for the target watershed; communities without such plans may apply for a waiver.
Projects must target watersheds with impairments listed on Maryland's 303(d) List, especially those with approved TMDLs.
Projects must result in quantifiable or measurable improvements in water quality and habitat.
No matching funds required — the State of Maryland covers the 40% federal match.
Grant amounts typically range from $30,000 to $400,000.
Request for Proposals released each spring/summer with applications typically due in late summer or fall.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants respond to the Request for Proposals (RFP) released each spring. The FFY26 RFP closed September 30, 2025; the FFY27 RFP will open July 1, 2026. Proposals must include justification of the applicant's capacity for grant management and upfront funding. Selections for FFY26 funding are scheduled for November 2025. Early submissions are accepted and encouraged. Contact MDE's §319 Program Manager Jacey Brooks with questions at mde.nps319@maryland.gov or (410) 537-4437.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Economic Development Corporation (MEDCO) helps with public-private partnerships. MEDCO can assess if a project is workable and manage proposal requests. The agency can also issue revenue bonds and own, develop, or operate project assets.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MEDCO provides services for public-private partnership projects. This includes evaluating project viability, managing solicitations for proposals, issuing revenue bonds, and owning, developing, or operating assets.
structured_extraction.program_audience: This program assists county and state governments, municipalities, towns, for-profit businesses, and state universities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: MEDCO provides services for public-private partnership projects. These services include project evaluation, solicitation management, and asset ownership, development, or operation. MEDCO can also issue revenue bonds for projects.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Business Ready Sites Program (MBRSP) enhances Maryland's industrial and commercial infrastructure by identifying and improving potential development sites statewide. Created by Executive Order of Governor Wes Moore on December 19, 2024, and funded at $3.5 million for FY2026, it provides financial support for site characterization and site improvements to attract business relocation, expansion, and investment, and offers collaborative marketing assistance to prepare commercial and industrial sites for private sector occupancy.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Three types of support are available: (1) Site Characterization Grants provide up to $10,000 (in-kind services) to assess a site's development readiness and assign a Ready Score on a 1–5 tier scale; no local match required as of January 1, 2026, though a 1-to-1 cash match may be required from other sources per application requirements. (2) Site Improvement Grants fund infrastructure upgrades, environmental remediation, due diligence studies, design/engineering, clearing and grading, and construction to prepare sites for industrial or commercial development; FY2026 grants ranged from $125,000 to $450,000 with no stated maximum; requires a 3:1 total cash match (or 4:1 in some cases) from federal, state, local, and private-sector sources. (3) Collaborative Marketing Support includes publication in the MBRSP Sites Dashboard, site characterization reports, and access to MEDCO's services to market sites that received grants.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis with a priority cycle in May; May submissions receive notification by July 1; submissions on June 1 or later receive notification within 60 days.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public sector entities (counties, municipalities, and their authorities including economic development, redevelopment, and industrial development authorities) and private sector entities that own or hold development rights to eligible land in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Site characterization assessments (retaining a site development professional to evaluate site readiness and potential), infrastructure upgrades, environmental remediation, due diligence studies (environmental phase 1 & 2, geotechnical, threatened/endangered species, wetlands, surveys), design and engineering, clearing and grading, and other site development improvements to prepare commercial or industrial sites for private sector occupancy.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across all Maryland counties and municipalities for eligible sites of at least 5 acres intended for industrial or commercial use.
requirements_list: Site must be a greenfield, brownfield, or redevelopment site in a pre-development phase
Site must be a minimum of 5 acres
Site must be intended solely for industrial or commercial purposes (tourism and agricultural farmland are explicitly excluded)

Site must be intended for occupancy primarily by private sector companies in Maryland's growth industries (e.g., life sciences, information technology, aerospace, defense, computational biology, quantum computing, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, position/navigation/timing) or jurisdiction-specific industries of focus
Site must not be otherwise restricted from further development
Applicants must own the land or hold development rights and agree to conditions in the MBRSP Program Guidelines
Site must align with county/municipality economic development goals
Owner documentation of ownership required for approval
Private sector applicants must provide a letter of support from the relevant county or municipal government
Site Characterization Grant: 1-to-1 cash match required from any source (per application; no local match required as of January 1, 2026 per program guidelines)
Site Improvement Grant: 3:1 or 4:1 total cash match required from federal, state, local, and private-sector sources

Site Improvement Grant applications must include: letters of support from county/municipal governments (if applicable), detailed project budget with timelines and deliverables, due diligence reports (environmental phase 1 & 2, geotechnical, threatened/endangered species, wetlands, surveys), site development plans, and evidence of title or purchase option documentation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted on a rolling basis with a priority cycle in May. Download the Site Characterization Grant Application or Site Improvement Grant Application from the program page. Submit the completed application and supporting documents by email to mbrsp@medco-corp.com. Site Improvement Grant applications must include applicant and site information, transportation/connectivity details, utility provider information, economic impact alignment, scope of work, and all required attachments.

structured_extraction.program_name: Pimlico Request for Expressions of Interest (REI) – Outparcels
structured_extraction.program_description: MEDCO invites developers and other interested parties to submit expressions of interest for developing outparcels adjacent to the Pimlico Race Course redevelopment site in Baltimore City. Respondents can propose uses and development concepts for available parcels as part of the broader Pimlico redevelopment effort.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MEDCO is soliciting expressions of interest from developers and other parties for the development of outparcels at the Pimlico site. This is a solicitation process, not a direct financial assistance program; selected respondents may be offered development opportunities tied to the Pimlico redevelopment project.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Developers, investors, and other parties interested in developing outparcels at the Pimlico Race Course redevelopment site in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Development of outparcels adjacent to the Pimlico Race Course redevelopment area.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Limited to the Pimlico Race Course outparcels in Baltimore City, Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and review the REI documents, then submit an expression of interest per the instructions in the REI notice. The deadline has been extended; see the attached PDF for updated submission details.

structured_extraction.program_name: Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities (SCIF) Capital Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: Capital grants to help recipients acquire, plan, design, furnish, and refurbish Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities (SCIFs) — secure work environments for security-cleared professionals. MEDCO administers the program on behalf of the State of Maryland, leveraging its quasi-government nonprofit status to apply for funding through the Maryland Department of General Services (DGS).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Capital grants to fund acquisition, planning, design, technology, furnishings, and refurbishment of SCIF spaces. MEDCO has awarded $5 million to date across five projects. For every dollar invested in SCIF space, an additional two to three dollars of private, nonprofit, or government match is generated.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations in Maryland seeking to build or improve secure work environments (SCIFs) for security-cleared professionals.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition, planning, design, technology, furnishings, and refurbishment of SCIF spaces.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland, with a focus on regions positioned to bring talent, jobs, and opportunity to the state.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: MEDCO navigates the application process with the Maryland Department of General Services (DGS) on the state's behalf. Contact MEDCO for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A loan fund that makes targeted investments into real estate and infrastructure projects that support transformative placemaking, transit-oriented development, community development, and inclusive and equitable economic growth. MEDCO (Maryland Economic Development Corporation) serves as the fund sponsor, raising capital and building a pipeline of project investments. The fund is designed to fill financing gaps in residential, commercial, mixed-use, and light industrial projects.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Flexible-term loans intended to fill financing gaps in residential, commercial, mixed-use, and light industrial development projects. Funds may be used for property acquisition, design and development, infrastructure, and other costs associated with new construction, adaptive reuse, or extensive rehabilitation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Developers and project sponsors pursuing real estate and infrastructure projects located within a Maryland Sustainable Community, Priority Funding Area, or Transit-Oriented Development area.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition of property or vacant sites, design and development, infrastructure, and other costs associated with new construction, adaptive reuse, or extensive rehabilitation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located within a Maryland Sustainable Community, Priority Funding Area, or Transit-Oriented Development area.
requirements_list: Project must be located within a Maryland Sustainable Community, Priority Funding Area, or Transit-Oriented Development area.
Priority given to projects that activate underutilized government or institutionally owned property.
Priority given to projects with significant development or redevelopment value.
Priority given to projects that leverage private investment.
Priority given to projects with significant job creation or retention potential.
Eligible project types include residential, commercial, mixed-use, and light industrial projects.

structured_extraction.program_description: A scholarship program that provides eligible recipients with access to Cybrary online cybersecurity training accounts to support cyber preparedness education.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides access to a Cybrary online cybersecurity training account through a scholarship. Funding for this opportunity was limited; waitlisted applicants will be notified if additional opportunities become available.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Application is now closed; scholarship recipients will be announced by Friday, June 13, 2025
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals seeking cybersecurity training and education
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Access to Cybrary online cybersecurity training platform
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide - available to Maryland residents
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Application is now closed. Waitlisted applicants will be notified if additional opportunities become available.

structured_extraction.program_name: FY20 BRIC and FMA Technical Assistance
structured_extraction.program_description: Technical assistance provided by the Maryland Emergency Management Agency (MEMA) to help local governments and subapplicants prepare applications for FEMA's Building Resilient Infrastructure and Communities (BRIC) and Flood Mitigation Assistance (FMA) grant programs. The assistance includes guidance on financial considerations, pre-award costs, management costs, project scope, benefit-cost analysis (BCA), environmental and historic preservation (EHP) requirements, and the subapplication process. FMA reduces or eliminates flood risk, prioritizing repetitive and severe repetitive loss properties. BRIC supports community capability and capacity building, encourages innovation, promotes partnerships, and enables large infrastructure projects.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Technical assistance sessions covering financial considerations, subapplication process overview, project scope development, benefit-cost analysis, and environmental and historic preservation requirements for FEMA BRIC and FMA grant applications. Materials include PDF guides and recorded video sessions. Grant funding provides financial reimbursement for hazard mitigation projects, pre-award costs (NEPA data, BCA development, design specifications), management costs (up to 5% of project costs), project implementation (design, engineering, labor, materials, inspections, permits, construction), and contingency costs (up to 5-7% of project costs). Projects must achieve a Benefit-Cost Ratio (BCR) of at least 1.0 to be considered cost-effective.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Notice of Interest due to MEMA: August 31, 2020; Subapplications due to MEMA: November 20, 2020; MEMA submits State Application to FEMA: January 29, 2021
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments and state agencies in Maryland with approved Local Hazard Mitigation Plans (LHMP) seeking to apply for FEMA BRIC and FMA hazard mitigation grants. Individuals, businesses, and nonprofits are ineligible to apply directly and must be sponsored by a local government or state agency.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Pre-award costs (NEPA data, BCA development, design specifications); management costs (up to 5% of project costs); project implementation (design, engineering, labor, materials, inspections, permits, construction); contingency (up to 5-7% of project costs); mitigation planning and project scoping; building code enhancement activities; capacity building for mitigation workforce; construction/implementation of mitigation projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Local jurisdictions must have a FEMA-approved Local Hazard Mitigation Plan (LHMP). Small and Impoverished Communities (3,000 or fewer individuals; average per capita income at or below 80% of national average) may receive special consideration. Repetitive Loss and Severe Repetitive Loss areas are prioritized for FMA. Properties in Special Flood Hazard Areas (SFHA) are eligible for certain project types.
requirements_list: Must have a FEMA-approved Local Hazard Mitigation Plan (LHMP)
Local governments must have adopted the 2015 or 2018 International Building Code (IBC)
Projects must be cost-effective with a Benefit-Cost Ratio (BCR) of at least 1.0
Must include detailed BCA documentation using a 7% OMB standard discount rate
Compliance with NEPA and all applicable federal environmental and historic preservation laws and Executive Orders
Complete EHP Screening Form and attach to FEMA GO Subapplication
Project location mapping and documentation required
Color photographs of structures and surrounding areas required
Construction date information for buildings required
Consultation letters regarding threatened/endangered species, wetlands, historic properties, and archaeological resources
Scope of work documentation required
Design drawings required when applicable
Non-federal cost share required
Subapplication must be submitted to MEMA no later than November 20, 2020
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a Notice of Interest to MEMA by August 31, 2020. Complete and submit subapplication to MEMA by November 20, 2020. MEMA reviews subapplications and submits the State Application to FEMA by January 29, 2021. Subapplicants should review provided video sessions and PDF materials on the MEMA website covering financial considerations, project scoping, BCA, and EHP requirements. Complete EHP Screening Form and provide supporting documentation including maps, drawings, and photographs. Contact state/local preservation agencies as required.

structured_extraction.program_description: A MDEM program that oversees and promotes cybersecurity funding opportunities from Maryland and federal sources to help eligible entities improve their cybersecurity maturity.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The CPU Grant Manager oversees cybersecurity funding opportunities from both Maryland and federal sources intended to help eligible entities address their cybersecurity maturity. Specific funding opportunities are listed on a separate page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Entities seeking cybersecurity funding in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Addressing cybersecurity maturity needs
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — available to eligible entities in Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the funding opportunities page at https://mdem.maryland.gov/Pages/cyber-preparedness-funding.aspx for a full list of opportunities.

structured_extraction.program_name: Individual Assistance Program (Individuals and Households Program)
structured_extraction.program_description: After a Presidentially declared disaster, this federal program provides grants to eligible households who face difficulties recovering. It offers Housing Assistance (temporary housing, repair, replacement, or construction) and Other Needs Assistance (medical, dental, funeral, clothing, household items, vehicles, and other disaster-related expenses) when other sources like SBA loans or insurance are insufficient.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants to eligible households for Housing Assistance (temporary housing rental, home repair up to the IHP maximum, home replacement under rare conditions, or semi-permanent/permanent housing construction) and Other Needs Assistance (medical and dental expenses, funeral costs, clothing, household items, tools, educational materials, clean-up items, fuel, vehicle repair or replacement, moving and storage, and other necessary disaster-related expenses). Available only after a Presidentially declared disaster when SBA loans are denied and insurance does not fully cover losses.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and households in Maryland who are experiencing difficulties following a Presidentially declared disaster and whose losses are not fully covered by SBA disaster loans or homeowners/flood insurance.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Housing Assistance: temporary housing rental, home repair, home replacement, or housing construction. Other Needs Assistance: medical and dental expenses, funeral and burial costs, clothing, household items, job tools, educational materials, clean-up items, fuel, vehicle repair/replacement, moving and storage, and other necessary disaster-related expenses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland following a Presidential disaster declaration.
requirements_list: Must be in an area covered by a Presidential disaster declaration
Must have been denied a low-interest SBA disaster loan, or insurance payout must be insufficient to cover losses
Homeowners in Special Flood Hazard Areas must comply with flood insurance purchase requirements and local flood codes
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through FEMA's Individual Assistance program. See FEMA's website at https://www.fema.gov/assistance/individual for application details.

structured_extraction.program_description: A partnership program that helps Maryland K-12 school systems strengthen their cybersecurity resilience. It provides planning, implementation, and ongoing support services to protect sensitive student and staff data, respond to cyber threats, and recover from cyber incidents.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides free technical assistance to K-12 school systems in four areas: (1) Planning — cybersecurity maturity assessments, emergency plan reviews, resource allocation analysis, and training program setup; (2) Implementation — remediation recommendations, cyber incident response plan development, disaster recovery and continuity of operations (COOP) planning, and training exercises; (3) Support — funding opportunity notifications and ongoing network support for response and recovery efforts.
structured_extraction.program_audience: K-12 Local Education Agencies (LEAs) and school systems throughout Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cybersecurity assessments, incident response planning, disaster recovery planning, staff training and exercises, and access to ongoing cybersecurity support resources
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to K-12 school systems throughout Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a K-12 Local Education Agency (LEA) or school system in Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the online request form linked on the program page to request support in one or more of the available assistance areas.

structured_extraction.program_description: A MDEM program that helps local government entities — including schools and health departments — develop and exercise cyber preparedness plans tailored to their unique needs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides planning assistance, exercise support, and cyber preparedness guidance to local jurisdictions including schools and health departments. Services include helping incorporate cyber-specific annexes into Emergency Operations Plans, assisting incident response, and supporting cyber incident preparedness and response activities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local government entities, schools, and health departments in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Developing and exercising cyber preparedness plans; integrating cyber annexes into emergency operations plans
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — available to local jurisdictions across Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Email cyberpreparedness.mdem@maryland.gov for a full list of this program's functions and available support.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Public Assistance Program provides supplemental federal grant funding to state agencies, local governments, and certain private non-profit organizations (including higher education institutions) to help pay for response and recovery work after a presidentially-declared disaster. Grants cover the repair, replacement, or restoration of disaster-damaged, publicly owned, and uninsured facilities, and help alleviate the financial burden to the State and local governments following a federally-declared disaster. Funding is provided at a minimum 75% federal / 25% applicant cost-share formula. The program covers Emergency Work (debris removal, emergency protective measures) and Permanent Work (restoration of roads, bridges, water control facilities, buildings, utilities, parks and recreational facilities) across Categories A–G, as well as Section 406 Hazard Mitigation measures.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal grant assistance provided at a minimum 75% federal / 25% applicant cost-share formula for repair, replacement, or restoration of disaster-damaged publicly owned and uninsured facilities. Covers seven categories of eligible work: Category A (Debris Removal), Category B (Emergency Protective Measures), Category C (Roads & Bridges), Category D (Water Control Facilities), Category E (Buildings, Equipment & Vehicles), Category F (Utilities), and Category G (Parks, Recreational Facilities & Other Facilities). Also includes Section 406 Hazard Mitigation measures, Immediate Needs Funding (INF) for expedited emergency work, and management/administrative costs (up to 5% for subrecipients; up to 7% for State). Donated resources (labor, equipment, materials) can offset cost share. Available only following a presidential disaster declaration.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Request for Public Assistance (RPA) must be filed within 30 days from the Presidential Disaster Declaration date; damage listings due within 60 days of Recovery Scoping Meeting
structured_extraction.contact_name: Nora Lagola, State Public Assistance Officer
structured_extraction.program_audience: State agencies, local governments, and eligible private non-profit organizations (including higher education institutions) in Maryland affected by a presidentially-declared disaster. Also includes tribal governments and private non-profit organizations providing critical services (education, emergency medical, utilities, emergency services) or essential social services (community centers, libraries, homeless shelters, childcare, senior centers, etc.).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Debris removal (Category A); emergency protective measures (Category B); permanent work including restoration of roads and bridges (Category C), water control facilities (Category D), buildings and equipment (Category E), utilities (Category F), and parks and recreational facilities (Category G); Section 406 Hazard Mitigation; management and administrative costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — available to eligible applicants throughout Maryland following a presidential disaster declaration. Eligibility is limited to areas designated in the presidential disaster declaration.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a state agency, local government, tribal government, or eligible private non-profit organization (including higher education institutions)
A disaster must be officially declared by the President
Damage must result from a presidentially-declared disaster
Facilities must be publicly owned and uninsured (or underinsured)
Applicants must provide a 25% cost share (donated resources may offset this)
Applicants must complete registration on the FEMA Grants Portal
Request for Public Assistance (RPA) must be submitted within 30 days of the Presidential Disaster Declaration
Damage listings must be submitted within 60 days of the Recovery Scoping Meeting
Private nonprofit organizations must have IRS tax-exemption under Section 501(c), (d), or (e) or satisfactory evidence of nonprofit status under Maryland law
Private nonprofit organizations must provide proof of ownership or lease of damaged facility
Work must eliminate immediate threat to life, public health, safety, or prevent significant damage to improved public or private property
Insurance must be considered before providing funds; documentation of insurance and claims required
Detailed documentation required: labor hours, equipment use, debris estimates, GPS locations, contracts, permits, engineering reports
Disaster impact must meet county-specific thresholds (per FEMA FFY thresholds and indicators)
Compliance with Robert T. Stafford Disaster Relief and Emergency Assistance Act (42 USC 5121-5206)
Completion of Impact Statement Form to accompany Initial Damage Assessment Form
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants are encouraged to create an account on the FEMA Grants Portal in advance. After creating an organizational account, the main contact will receive a link to finish registration. When a presidential disaster is declared, the Public Assistance process is completed through the FEMA Grants Portal. A Request for Public Assistance (RPA) must be filed within 30 days of the disaster declaration. Applicants then have 60 days after the Recovery Scoping Meeting (RSM) to identify all disaster-related damages. An Impact Statement Form must be completed and submitted with the Initial Damage Assessment Form. Contact the MDEM Public Assistance team or the State Public Assistance Officer for guidance.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Resilient Maryland Revolving Loan Fund offers low-interest loans (at no more than 1% interest) to local governments to help finance projects and activities that reduce the effects of natural and human-caused hazards, including floods, snowstorms, tornadoes, severe storms, wildfires, extreme heat, storm surges, high water levels, shoreline erosion, drought, and earthquakes. Authorized under the federal STORM Act (42 U.S.C. § 5135) and Maryland Public Safety Article § 14-110.4(b), and funded through FEMA Safeguarding Tomorrow grants with a 10% Maryland state cost match. Local governments may take out loans on behalf of homeowners, businesses, nonprofit organizations, and communities. The program helps communities across Maryland build resilience, supports low-impact development, wildland-urban interface management, floodplain reconnection, open space projects, building code adoption, zoning and land use planning, and can also satisfy the non-federal cost share requirement for federal hazard mitigation grants such as HMGP, FMA, or BRIC. At least 40% of loans are targeted to underserved recipients. Aims to decrease loss of life and property, insurance costs, and federal disaster payments.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest revolving loans issued to local governments to finance hazard mitigation and resilience projects. Standard loans: 1% interest rate, 20-year repayment period. Loans for economically challenged areas: 0.05% interest rate, 30-year repayment period. Repayments begin one year after loan funding. Local governments may borrow on behalf of homeowners, businesses, nonprofit organizations, and communities. Loans may also cover the non-federal cost share requirement for federal hazard mitigation grants such as HMGP, FMA, or BRIC. At least 40% of loans are targeted to underserved recipients. Projects in economically challenged geographic areas receive preferential loan terms.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments in Maryland, including local government officials and emergency management, public works, transportation, sustainability, environment, and floodplain planning professionals, acting on behalf of homeowners, businesses, nonprofit organizations, and communities seeking to finance hazard mitigation and resilience projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects and activities that mitigate the effects of natural and human-caused hazards, including floods, snowstorms, tornadoes, severe storms, wildfires, extreme heat, storm surges, high water levels, shoreline erosion, drought, and earthquakes; low-impact development; wildland-urban interface management; conservation areas; floodplain reconnection and open space projects; building code adoption; zoning and land use planning; administrative and technical costs; and satisfying the non-federal cost share for hazard mitigation grants (HMGP, FMA, BRIC).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to all local governments. Projects in economically challenged geographic areas receive amplified consideration and preferential loan terms. Tie-breaking criterion: jurisdictions with the greatest burden of social vulnerabilities are prioritized.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local government
Local government must have a FEMA-approved Hazard Mitigation Plan
Legislative resolution identifying a dedicated revenue source for loan repayment
Local government must demonstrate ability to repay the loan
No presidential disaster declaration required
Participation in the National Flood Insurance Program is not required
At least 40% of loans are reserved for underserved recipients
Compliance with 42 U.S.C. §5135 (STORM Act)
Compliance with Maryland Public Safety Article §14-110.4
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested applicants should express interest by submitting the online interest form (Notice of Intent) linked on the program page, available year-round. Projects are ranked and prioritized based on federal requirements, state law, NOFO, and the state Hazard Mitigation Plan criteria; funds are disbursed accordingly. Comments on the Intended Use Plan and Project Proposal List can be sent to resilientloan.mdem@maryland.gov by May 31st. Contact MDEM for more information on the full application process.

structured_extraction.program_description: A MDEM program that helps local and state agencies assess cybersecurity risk, determine their risk appetite, and connect to available technological resources through risk assessments and operational analyses.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides assistance with risk assessments, operational analyses, risk appetite determination, implementation of security controls, privacy controls, and supply chain management controls. Also links state and local agencies to available technological resources.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland local and state government agencies
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cybersecurity risk assessments, operational analyses, security and privacy controls implementation
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — available to Maryland local and state agencies
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact cyberpreparedness.mdem@maryland.gov for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A MDEM program designed to help Maryland state agencies develop and exercise their cyber preparedness plans.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Assists state agencies with developing and exercising their cyber preparedness plans, including planning assistance, incident response support, training, and exercises tailored to state agency needs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland state agency representatives
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Developing and exercising cyber preparedness plans for state agencies
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — available to Maryland state agencies
requirements_list: Applicant must be a representative of a Maryland state agency
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: State agency representatives interested in partnering with the Cyber Preparedness Unit should email cyberpreparedness.mdem@maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_name: State and Local Cybersecurity Grant Program (SLCGP)
structured_extraction.program_description: The State and Local Cybersecurity Grant Program (SLCGP) provides federal funding to help state and local governments address cybersecurity risks and threats to their information systems. The program supports strategic investments to improve the cybersecurity posture of government agencies, protect critical infrastructure, and strengthen the resilience of essential public services. Jointly managed by CISA and FEMA at the federal level, in Maryland the Maryland Department of Emergency Management (MDEM) serves as the State Administrative Agency (SAA) and pass-through entity, with the Maryland Department of Information Technology (DoIT) providing technical guidance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement-based subgrant funding for approved cybersecurity projects. Funds support five investment priority categories: (1) Priority cybersecurity best practices adoption/enhancement, (2) General cybersecurity best practices, (3) Cybersecurity policy and governance, (4) Addressing specific jurisdictional cybersecurity needs, (5) Cybersecurity workforce development. Allowable expenses include planning, organization, equipment, training, exercises, and management/administration (up to 5% of award). Subrecipients must complete projects within the period of performance for their fiscal year, submit quarterly status reports, and meet federal and state compliance requirements. FY22 projects must be completed by September 30, 2026; FY23 projects by September 30, 2027. A second-round application for FY2023 funds is currently open on a rolling basis.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis (FY2023 second-round funding currently open; application open February 2026, project completion deadline September 30, 2027)
structured_extraction.program_audience: State agencies, local governments, school districts, special districts, councils of governments, and rural communities in Maryland seeking to improve their cybersecurity capabilities and protect government information systems.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cybersecurity improvements for government information systems including: adoption or enhancement of cybersecurity best practices (asset discovery/management, multi-factor authentication, endpoint detection and response, email gateway, security awareness training, firewalls, enhanced logging, data encryption, end-of-life software/hardware removal, password management, backup/recovery systems, migration to .gov domains); cybersecurity policy and governance; addressing jurisdictional cybersecurity gaps; operational technology (OT) cybersecurity; cybersecurity workforce development; and vendor services/contractors (with itemized quotes).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to state agencies and local governments throughout Maryland. All 24 Maryland jurisdictions are eligible. Eight counties are designated as rural under FEMA's definition (population under 50,000, not designated as urbanized area): Caroline, Dorchester, Garrett, Kent, Queen Anne's, Somerset, Talbot, and Worcester. Other entities may qualify as rural by providing evidence of local planning/zoning rural designation.
requirements_list: Must be a state agency, local government, school district, special district, council of governments, or eligible rural community
Must register for the CISA Cyber Hygiene (CyHy) service and send proof to MDEM
Must complete the Nationwide Cybersecurity Review (NCSR) annually and send certificate of completion to MDEM
Must submit Quarterly Status Reports (QSRs) until project completion
Must have a signed Subrecipient Agreement (SRA) contract before starting any project
Must obtain a Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) via SAM.gov
Must retain copies of reports and financial documentation for at least 3 years after the end of the period of performance
Do not begin project until FEMA approval notification is received from MDEM and SRA is in place
Must use provided budget narrative and project proposal templates
Must submit a detailed line-item budget with accompanying budget justification
Must accept award within 30 days via acceptance letter to slcgp.grant@maryland.gov
Rural applicants outside FEMA's 8 designated rural jurisdictions must provide evidence of rural status (planning/zoning designation or mapping evidence)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Review the FY2023 application documents and informational guides available for download on this page. 2. Download and complete the FFY2023 Subgrant Project Proposal Application, Additional Application Documents Packet (budget, Appendix A, Appendix E), and Form W-9 if applicable. 3. Submit a detailed line-item budget spreadsheet with accompanying budget justification. 4. Email completed forms to slcgp.grant@maryland.gov with subject line formatted as: FY[year] SLCGP - [Subrecipient name] - [Project title] Application Forms. 5. MDEM submits project proposals to FEMA on behalf of the State. 6. FEMA approves or rejects projects. 7. If approved, funds are awarded to MDEM as the pass-through entity upon signature of the subrecipient subaward agreement. 8. Submit a Letter of Intent to Accept or Reject Funding within 30 days.

structured_extraction.program_name: MDEMA Donald "Doc" Lumpkins Memorial Scholarship Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Emergency Management Association (MDEMA) offers annual scholarships to students pursuing degrees in emergency management or a closely related field. The program aims to nurture and develop future emergency management professionals by helping cover the cost of their education. Five $1,500 scholarships are awarded each year, one per geographic area covering all five MDEMA regions across Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MDEMA awards five $1,500 scholarships annually, one per geographic area: Area I (Western Maryland), Area II (National Capital), Area III (Central Maryland), Area IV (Eastern Shore), and Area V (Southern Maryland).
structured_extraction.program_audience: High school seniors attending an accredited Maryland high school who have been accepted to a two- or four-year college or university and plan to major in emergency management or a closely related field, or students currently enrolled in a two- or four-year college or university pursuing a degree in emergency management or a closely related field.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational expenses for students pursuing an associate or baccalaureate degree in emergency management or a closely related field.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available across all five MDEMA geographic areas covering the entire state of Maryland. Applicants must attend an accredited Maryland high school or be enrolled in a college or university. One scholarship is awarded per geographic area.
requirements_list: Must be a high school senior attending an accredited Maryland high school who has been accepted to a two- or four-year college or university and plans to major in emergency management or a closely related field, OR
Must be a student currently accepted or enrolled in a two- or four-year college or university pursuing a degree in emergency management or a closely related field.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the MDEMA website at marylandema.org/scholarship.php to obtain the application and additional information, and submit before the deadline.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program funds nonprofit and community-based organizations to conduct outreach across Maryland, educating homeowners and renters about the benefits of building electrification, energy efficiency upgrades, and renewable energy solutions. The program focuses on low- to moderate-income households and overburdened communities to help reduce energy burdens and support the state's climate goals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants totaling $250,000 are anticipated for FY26. Minimum award is $50,000 and maximum is $125,000, though MEA may increase the maximum based on applicant qualifications. MEA may also issue partial awards. Grant funding is provided directly to the 501(c)(3) nonprofit applicant, which may then issue subgrants or stipends to other organizations or community groups working within Maryland. Eligible activities include in-person outreach and education on building electrification, energy efficiency, renewable energy, and available incentives/rebates, as well as online resources, phone/email advising, print materials, community events, hands-on demonstrations, and equipment demonstrations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: 501(c)(3) nonprofit and community-based organizations conducting outreach to low- to moderate-income (LMI) households and overburdened communities across Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Outreach and education activities to inform owners and tenants of single-family and multi-family homes about the benefits of building electrification, energy efficiency upgrades, and renewable energy solutions. Eligible expenditures include: material/equipment purchase for electric appliance demonstrations, print collateral and media materials, outreach supplies, community event/meeting rentals, food and supplies, online promotions, staffing expenditures, subgrants or stipends for partner organizations, and administrative/indirect costs (10% minimum or negotiated rate for nonprofits).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is open statewide in Maryland, with an emphasis on serving low- to moderate-income households and overburdened communities. Partial awards possible for equitable regional distribution.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization
Must be registered to do business in Maryland with Evidence of Good Standing (SDAT Business Entity Search or Certificate of Status)
IRS Form W-9 with matching organization name and address
Submit narrative (max 15 pages) addressing eligibility and evaluation criteria
Submit detailed budget (Excel or PDF spreadsheet)
Grant funding is provided directly to the individual/organization identified on the application
Recipients may provide subgrants or stipends to other organizations or community groups working within Maryland
Optional: Two or more letters of support from project partners
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and submit the Application Jotform at https://form.jotform.com/marylandenergy/electrification-outreach. Review the Program Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA) for full program details before applying. Submit quarterly progress reports with invoices and a final close-out report with metrics, lessons learned, and best practices.

structured_extraction.program_description: BGE's program for facilities 35,000 square feet and larger provides building benchmarking, an ASHRAE Level 2 energy audit, and installation of low-cost energy improvements through an approved contractor.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: An approved contractor will benchmark the building using ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager, provide an ASHRAE Level 2 audit, and install low-cost energy improvements for facilities 35,000 sq ft and larger.
structured_extraction.program_audience: BGE commercial customers in facilities 35,000 square feet and larger
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Building benchmarking, ASHRAE Level 2 energy audit, and low-cost energy improvements
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: BGE service territory in Maryland

Must be a BGE customer

structured_extraction.program_description: BGE subsidizes the cost of a home energy audit for residential customers and offers incentives for follow-up energy improvements such as air sealing, insulation, and window upgrades.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: BGE subsidizes the cost of a home energy audit ($100 for a $400 value). After the audit, customers are eligible for incentives for air and duct sealing, insulation, windows and doors, and more.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential BGE customers
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home energy audit and follow-up energy improvements (air sealing, insulation, windows, doors)

This includes a free onsite energy assessment for small business and small nonprofit BGE customers to identify energy-saving opportunities, as well as a free walk-through energy assessment for commercial buildings less than 75,000 square feet under the Small Building Tune-up Program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free onsite energy assessment for small businesses and small nonprofit customers, and a free walk-through energy assessment for commercial buildings less than 75,000 square feet.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses, small nonprofits, and BGE commercial customers in buildings under 75,000 square feet within the BGE service territory
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free onsite or walk-through energy assessment to identify energy-saving opportunities

Building must be less than 75,000 square feet (for Small Building Tune-up Program)
Must be a BGE customer

structured_extraction.program_description: BGE offers rebates for customers who purchase smart thermostats and enroll in demand response programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rebate offered to customers who purchase qualifying smart thermostats and enroll in BGE's demand response program.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of smart thermostats

Must purchase a qualifying smart thermostat
