structured_extraction.program_name: Building Energy Performance Standards (BEPS) Technical Assistance Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A technical assistance program run by the Maryland Energy Administration (MEA) through its Clean Buildings Hub initiative. It provides customized, one-on-one technical assistance to building owners and managers whose properties are covered by Maryland's Building Energy Performance Standards (BEPS). Assistance focuses on compliance activities such as energy benchmarking, decarbonization planning, and multi-year retrofit planning. The program is being developed in partnership with the Maryland Environmental Service (MES) and targets buildings over 35,000 square feet subject to BEPS.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Customized, one-on-one technical assistance to building owners and managers to help with BEPS compliance activities including energy benchmarking, decarbonization planning, and multi-year retrofit planning. The program is being developed in partnership with the Maryland Environmental Service (MES) through a Request for Proposals process.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Building owners and managers with properties over 35,000 square feet covered by Maryland's Building Energy Performance Standards (BEPS)
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy benchmarking, decarbonization planning, and multi-year retrofit planning to achieve BEPS compliance
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — available to buildings in Maryland covered by BEPS
requirements_list: Must own or manage a building covered by Maryland's Building Energy Performance Standards (BEPS)
Building must be over 35,000 square feet
Building must be subject to Maryland's Building Energy Performance Standards (BEPS)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The program is in development. Stakeholders can subscribe to the Clean Buildings Hub Newsletter to receive updates on the forthcoming program.

structured_extraction.program_name: Business Energy Investment Tax Credit (ITC) / Section 48 Energy Investment Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal tax credit that reduces tax liability for investments in renewable energy properties, including solar energy systems, energy storage, and geothermal systems. The credit provides 30% of the cost of qualifying solar energy systems installed after December 31, 2019, and applies to both residential and commercial installations. Governed under Section 48 of the Internal Revenue Code.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides a 30% federal tax credit for investments in qualifying renewable energy properties, including solar energy systems installed after December 31, 2019, energy storage, and geothermal systems. Applies to both residential and commercial installations. The credit directly reduces federal tax liability.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners, businesses, non-profits, and other entities investing in or installing renewable energy properties such as solar, energy storage, and geothermal systems.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Investment in and installation of renewable energy properties, including solar energy systems, energy storage, and geothermal systems.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available nationwide, including Maryland.
requirements_list: Solar energy system must be installed after December 31, 2019
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Claim the credit when filing federal taxes. See details at the Federal Register program page or the DSIRE program page (http://programs.dsireusa.org/system/program/detail/658).

structured_extraction.program_name: Clean Burning Wood and Pellet Stove Rebate Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides rebates to Maryland homeowners who purchase and install an eligible clean-burning wood or pellet stove at their primary residence. The goal is to help homeowners invest in clean energy by replacing electric, non-natural gas fossil fuel heating systems, or old wood or pellet stoves. The program operated for nine years and is concluding after fiscal year 2024.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rebates are available for qualifying stoves: $500 for wood-burning stoves emitting no more than 3.0 grams of particulate matter per hour with an EPA efficiency rating of at least 75%; $700 for pellet-burning stoves emitting no more than 2.0 grams of particulate matter per hour with an EPA efficiency rating of at least 75%.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Stoves must be purchased by December 1, 2023; systems must be installed and applications received or postmarked by March 31, 2024
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland homeowners installing a clean-burning wood or pellet stove at their primary residence
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and installation of an eligible clean-burning wood or pellet stove at the applicant's primary residence
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — available to Maryland homeowners across all counties; property must be located in Maryland
requirements_list: Stove must be purchased by December 1, 2023 (stoves purchased after January 4, 2024 are ineligible)
Stove must be installed and application received or postmarked by March 31, 2024
Stove must meet or exceed required particulate emissions limits (wood: ≤3.0 g/hr; pellet: ≤2.0 g/hr)
Stove must have an EPA-published Higher Heating Value (HHV) efficiency rating of at least 75% (required from September 15, 2022)
Must be a Maryland homeowner installing the stove at their primary residence
Home must be owned by the applicant and be their primary residence at time of application
Home must not be owned by an irrevocable trust
Stove must be new (not used or secondhand)
Must comply with all requirements in the Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review the FY24 Funding Opportunity Announcement, purchase an eligible stove by December 1, 2023, install it, then submit an application to MEA by March 31, 2024 (received or postmarked). Applications are processed on a first-come, first-served basis until the program budget is exhausted. Applications available at https://energy.maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Energy Administration (MEA) offers competitive grants to owners of Maryland-based commercial, industrial, data center, agricultural, and non-profit facilities to invest in energy improvements that exceed current building codes or standards and achieve at least 20% energy savings. Both new construction and existing facilities are eligible. Benefits can include lower operating costs, reduced emissions, improved health and safety compliance, and increased productivity. The FY26 program has a total budget of up to $8,400,000, divided into three Areas of Interest: existing facilities serving general populations (AOI.1, $3,000,000), existing facilities serving low-income populations (AOI.2, $4,000,000, eligible for 100% cost reimbursement), and new construction (AOI.3, $1,400,000). A special provision offers 100% cost coverage for qualified non-governmental facilities that primarily serve low-income populations (over 50% of clientele at or below 80% HUD median family income). Grant awards range from a minimum of $20,000 to a maximum of $500,000 per project. The program does not support renewable energy investments. The FY27 program is expected to launch in or around September 2026.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive reimbursement-based grants for energy efficiency and conservation improvements (Energy Conservation Measures, ECMs) at commercial, industrial, data center, agricultural, and non-profit facilities. Grant awards range from a minimum of $20,000 to a maximum of $500,000 per project. The FY26 program has a total budget of $8,400,000, divided into three Areas of Interest (AOI): AOI.1 (existing facilities serving general populations, $3,000,000), AOI.2 (existing facilities serving low-income populations, $4,000,000, eligible for 100% of net total project cost), and AOI.3 (new construction/substantial rehabilitation, $1,400,000). For AOI.1 and AOI.3, coverage ranges from 30% to 85% of project cost depending on tier. Eligible equipment includes HVAC systems, chillers, lighting systems, motors/pumps/drives, and industrial process equipment. Engineering assessments and photometric design work are eligible (up to $20,000 reimbursement for pre-ratification audits/feasibility studies if recommendations are implemented). Ancillary costs (labor, installation, ductwork extension) may be included but must not exceed equipment costs. Awards are paid in arrears based on documented project expenses. Grantees may finance remaining costs through the Jane E. Lawton Conservation Loan Program.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: 3:00 P.M. ET, Friday, January 30, 2026 (FY26); FY27 program expected to launch in or around September 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses (corporations, LLPs, LLCs, GPs, etc.), non-profit entities, government entities, and higher education institutions that own or operate commercial, industrial, data center, manufacturing, warehouse, office, retail, agricultural, private school, private college, or multifamily residential (5+ units) facilities in Maryland. Also includes non-profits providing services to low-income populations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency and conservation improvements (ECMs) to commercial, industrial, data center, agricultural, and non-profit facilities, including both new construction and existing buildings, that result in energy performance exceeding current codes or standards and achieve at least 20% energy savings. Eligible uses include HVAC systems, chillers, lighting systems, motors/pumps/drives, industrial process equipment, energy audits and feasibility studies (up to $20,000 if recommendations implemented), system design costs within limits, and electrical infrastructure upgrades if recommended ECMs are installed. Does not support renewable energy investments.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland-based facilities only; available statewide in Maryland. Projects must be located within jurisdictions enforcing current building/energy codes as of MEA's application closing date.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a business entity (registered corporation, LLP, LLC, GP, etc.), non-profit, government entity, or higher education institution
Facility must be located in Maryland
Building must have commercial, industrial, data center, or non-profit use
Proposed improvements must result in energy performance exceeding current codes or standards
Project must achieve at least 20% energy savings

Eligible facility types include manufacturing/industrial, data centers, office/commercial/retail, agricultural, private schools (Pre-K through university), multifamily residential with 5+ units, and institutional human or community services

For AOI.2 (low-income populations), over 50% of the facility's clientele must be defined as low-income (at or below 80% of HUD median family income for Maryland), and the facility must be non-governmental
For AOI.3 (new construction), the facility must be newly built, substantially rehabbed with replacement of major mechanical systems, or repurposed after one year or more of vacancy
Applications must be submitted before the program deadline (3:00 P.M. ET, January 30, 2026 for FY26)
Project expenses eligible for reimbursement must be tied to procurement commitments that post-date the grant agreement's ratification
Project must involve energy efficiency upgrades in stationary facilities
All ECMs must demonstrate cost-effectiveness superior to alternatives meeting minimum codes/standards
For existing facilities: Net total project cost = gross cost minus utility rebates
For new construction/substantial rehab: Net total project cost = incremental cost of high-efficiency equipment versus code-minimum alternatives
MEA retains discretion to disallow insufficient cost-effective ECMs
Multifamily residential buildings must contain five or more units
For lighting systems: fixtures must be owned by the property owner, not the utility
Ancillary costs (labor, installation, ductwork extension) may be included but must not exceed equipment costs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a completed application (FY26 C&I APPLICATION form) before the deadline of 3:00 P.M. ET on January 30, 2026. Applications may be submitted electronically; staff will confirm receipt within one to two business days via email. MEA scores each application for quality of documentation and magnitude of environmental benefits (annual GHG reductions from baseline). Awards are issued in rank order until the program budget is exhausted. If also seeking a loan for remaining costs, applicants should submit a Jane E. Lawton Conservation Loan application at the same time. Successful applicants receive a notice of award with a Letter of Commitment requiring countersignature via DocuSign. A separate draft grant agreement follows and also requires countersignature. An informational webinar was held on November 20, 2024 to share best practices, eligibility criteria, and application tips.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Community EVSE Grant Program provides grants to increase access to affordable and reliable electric vehicle (EV) charging networks and reduce transportation greenhouse gas emissions throughout Maryland, especially in overburdened, low-and-moderate income, and underserved communities. The program has two areas of interest: (1) EV Infrastructure Planning, which funds feasibility and planning studies for future EV charging development, and (2) EVSE Installations, which funds the installation of Level 2 or Level 3 EV charging equipment, including DC Fast Charging.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MEA anticipates $10 million total available in FY 2026: $500,000 for Area of Interest 1 (EV Infrastructure Planning) and $9,000,000 for Area of Interest 2 (EVSE Installations). Actual amounts awarded may vary based on available funds and application quality. Grants are competitive and statewide. AOI 1 is limited to local governmental entities (counties and incorporated towns/cities). AOI 2 per-port incentive amounts range from $5,600–$150,000 depending on ownership structure, charger type, power level, and number of ports. Funds are disbursed as reimbursement in arrears for eligible expenses.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: February 25, 2026 at 3:00 PM Eastern Time Zone (AOI 1); February 27, 2026 at 3:00 PM EST (AOI 2)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses, nonprofits, institutions of higher education, and state and local governments in Maryland, especially those serving overburdened, low-and-moderate income, and underserved communities, seeking to plan or install EV charging infrastructure. AOI 1 is limited to local governments (counties and incorporated towns/cities).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Area of Interest 1: Community-level planning activities (feasibility studies, readiness plans across jurisdictions) and site-level planning activities (engineering analyses, site assessments, electrical diagrams, load capacity verification, permit identification, cost breakdowns, consultant and engineer hiring). Area of Interest 2: Purchase and installation of Level 2 or Level 3 (including DC Fast Charging) EV charging equipment; costs may include engineering/design, utility and electrical upgrades, construction, equipment, operations and maintenance planning, community outreach and education, and site design and preparation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland. Priority given to overburdened communities (census tracts with at least 3 environmental health indicators above the 75th percentile statewide, as identified using the MDEnviroscreen Tool) and, for AOI 2, locations over 50 miles from currently available charging stations.
requirements_list: Project must be in or accessible to low-and-moderate income, overburdened, or underserved communities.
Applicants must be eligible under the Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA) for the applicable Area of Interest.
Applications may be submitted to one or both Areas of Interest.
Area of Interest 1: Applicants are local governments (all counties including Baltimore City, and incorporated towns and cities) funding feasibility and planning studies.

Area of Interest 2: Applicants must be businesses/LLCs registered in good standing with Maryland SDAT, incorporated non-profits in good standing with SDAT, Maryland institutions of higher education accredited by Middle States Association, local education agencies, units of municipal or county governments, or Maryland-recognized Tribal governments. Residential homeowners (4 units and under), regulated energy utility companies, Maryland state government agencies, and federal or foreign government units are ineligible.
Area of Interest 2: Applicants must install Level 2 or Level 3 EV charging equipment.
Area of Interest 2: 97% uptime requirement for operations.
Projects must be completed within 24 months of executed grant agreement, including all milestones and reporting.
No reimbursement for costs incurred prior to grant agreement execution unless MEA agrees in writing.
Applicants cannot receive another MEA grant for the same project if previously funded by MEA.
Applicant must be an authorized representative with sufficient authority to complete funded activities.
Budget Workbook required with breakdown of grant and leveraged funds.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Solar Low-to-Moderate Income Power Purchase Agreement Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides competitive grants to Maryland PSC-approved Community Solar Subscriber Organizations to offset costs associated with Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs), enabling clean energy to be offered to low-income and low-to-moderate income (LMI), overburdened, and underserved Maryland households at a lower subscription rate. FY26 focuses on Low-Income households and includes two areas of interest: AOI-1 (subscribing low-income households to community solar projects with minimum 25% cost savings) and AOI-2 (solar projects on landfills/brownfields benefiting low-income residents with at least 50% of energy at no cost). Funded through approximately $17 million from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund using Solar Alternative Compliance Payment funding, with $5 million allocated for AOI-1 and $12 million for AOI-2, and a $6 million landfill incentive cap applying to AOI-2. The program aims to increase participation by low-to-moderate income households in community solar projects by maximizing value to LMI subscribers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants totaling approximately $17 million from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund using Solar Alternative Compliance Payment funding. AOI-1 ($5 million): Monetary incentives for subscribing at least 15% of energy output to low-income subscribers with minimum 25% cost savings from CSEGS credit rate. AOI-2 ($12 million): At least 50% of energy at no cost to designated low-income subscribers; remaining energy at 25% savings; projects must be on landfills, rubble-fills, or brownfields; funded at $2,000/kW-dc plus interconnection incentives (75% of wiring costs after first $1,000,000, max $3,000,000); $6 million landfill incentive cap applies. Grants are paid as milestone and completion payments and enable lower subscription rates for low-to-moderate income community solar subscribers over 20-year terms.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Offsetting costs associated with Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs) to lower the cost of clean energy for low-income and low-to-moderate income community solar subscribers, enabling reduced subscription rates. Funds may support development, construction, and installation of solar photovoltaic arrays serving eligible income households.

structured_extraction.program_name: Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment (EVSE) Rebate Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The EVSE Rebate Program, administered by the Maryland Energy Administration (MEA), provides rebate funding to help cover the costs of buying and installing qualified electric vehicle (EV) charging stations. The program aims to reduce the financial burden of acquiring and installing charging equipment and to increase EV adoption in support of Maryland's EV deployment and greenhouse gas reduction goals. Rebates cover 50% of total eligible costs for residential and commercial applicants statewide. Residential (individual) applicants can receive up to $700 per charger, while commercial applicants can receive up to $5,000 per charger (with a maximum of $125,000 aggregate per commercial applicant in FY2026). The FY26 total program budget is $2.5 million ($1.5 million residential, $1 million commercial through April 1, 2026). The program is non-competitive and awards funding on a first-come, first-served basis until funds are exhausted. Applicants must provide their own funding and apply after EVSE is acquired, installed, operational, and paid in full.

The FY26 total program budget is $2.5 million ($1.5 million residential allocation, $1 million commercial allocation through April 1, 2026). Rebates are not available for Level 1 EVSE purchased on or after October 1, 2023. The program is non-competitive and awards funding on a first-come, first-served basis until funds are exhausted. structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive grant program administered by the Maryland Energy Administration that provides Maryland community-serving buildings with funding to electrify existing building systems. Projects may include installing heat pumps, electric water heaters, upgraded panels, energy-efficient building shells, and other electric equipment to replace fossil fuel-powered systems. The program supports hospitals, medical facilities, multi-family buildings in low-and-moderate income communities, schools, houses of worship, universities, daycare centers, non-profits, arts and science centers, senior centers, museums, private libraries, grocery stores, nature centers, volunteer fire stations, performing arts centers, and other community buildings. The goal is to reduce lifecycle costs, cut onsite emissions, and help facilities shift to cleaner energy alternatives.
eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive, reimbursement-based grants from a total FY26 budget of $6.8 million. Award range: $25,000–$1.5 million, capped at 50% of total project costs after utility incentives are applied. Quarterly disbursement following grant agreement execution; reimbursement for completed work upon proof of purchase via detailed invoices. 24–27 month performance period for project completion. Funds cover heat pumps, electric water heaters, heat pump dryers, ENERGY STAR and equivalent appliances, induction stovetops and ovens, water and steam system management improvements, building envelope improvements (insulation, air sealing, doors, windows), building controls, electric panel and wiring upgrades, engineering and design services, and other energy conservation measures.

Eligible applicants include for-profit and non-profit building owners, higher education institutions, and government entities.

structured_extraction.program_description: Established by the Maryland General Assembly in 2008, EmPOWER Maryland promotes energy efficiency and conservation, aiming to reduce per capita electricity usage and peak demand, saving Marylanders money. The program requires electric companies, gas companies, and the Department of Housing and Community Development to develop energy efficiency, conservation, and greenhouse gas emissions reduction programs. Maryland's largest electric utilities offer programs to help households, businesses, and organizations save energy and money through incentives such as free or discounted energy audits, weatherization assistance, and efficient appliances. Starting in 2024, new incentives are also available to help customers switch from fossil fuel heating and appliances to efficient electric alternatives. The program includes behind-the-meter programs, front-of-meter utility/community programs, demand response, and beneficial electrification, with a focus on low- and moderate-income residential households through a whole-home retrofit approach addressing health/safety upgrades, weatherization, energy efficiency, and general maintenance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Utilities offer free or discounted energy audits, weatherization services, and rebates/incentives for energy efficiency improvements and efficient appliances. Starting in 2024, new incentives are also available to help customers switch from fossil fuel heating and appliances to efficient electric alternatives. Program also includes demand response and beneficial electrification programs, health and safety upgrades, whole-home retrofits, breaker box upgrades, portable heating and cooling equipment, and rate relief/offsets for eligible residential customers. Cost recovery occurs through surcharge line items on customer bills, with financial performance incentives and penalties for investor-owned companies and full cost recovery on current basis by January 1, 2028.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy audits, weatherization, efficient appliances, energy efficiency improvements to reduce electricity usage and peak demand, transition from fossil fuel-powered heating and appliances to electric alternatives, demand response implementation, beneficial electrification, health and safety upgrades, general home maintenance for low-income housing, breaker box upgrades, portable heating and cooling equipment, and rate relief for residential customers

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Resilient Infrastructure for Sustainable Energy (RISE) Program provides competitive grants funded through Section 40101(d) of the 2021 Bipartisan Infrastructure Law (Bipartisan Infrastructure Law) to help fund improvements to Maryland's electricity and related power infrastructure. The program aims to strengthen grid resilience and reliability against threats such as severe weather, cyberattacks, physical attacks, and aging components, supporting Maryland's goal of reaching 100% clean energy by 2035. The FY25 program has an approximately $15,000,000 budget and awards grants on a competitive basis to eligible electricity grid operators and related stakeholders, including electric utility infrastructure owners/operators, electric utility-scale generators, transmission owners/operators, distribution providers, electricity storage operators, and fuel suppliers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants from an approximately $15,000,000 program budget, federally funded through Section 40101(d) of the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (Bipartisan Infrastructure Law). Two Areas of Interest (AOIs) based on electricity sales volume: AOI 1 (Large Applicants) for entities selling >4,000,000 MWh annually to Maryland ratepayers — grants up to $3,000,000 with 100% cost-match requirement; AOI 2 (Small Applicants) for entities selling ≤4,000,000 MWh annually to Maryland ratepayers — grants up to $3,000,000 with 1/3 cost-match requirement. MEA reserves the right to determine final grant amount. Awardees must meet federal requirements in addition to Maryland requirements. Funds are encumbered upon execution of grant agreement; electronic payments via ACH/Direct Deposit required.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland electricity infrastructure operators including electricity grid operators, electricity storage operators, electricity generators, transmission owners or operators, distribution providers, fuel suppliers, and other relevant entities involved in the electric grid. Projects benefiting critical infrastructure and low-to-moderate income, overburdened, underserved (LMIOU) and Justice40 communities are prioritized.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Enhancing the resilience and reliability of the electricity grid through non-generation measures, including: weatherization technologies and equipment; fire-resistant technologies and fire prevention systems; monitoring and control technologies; undergrounding of electrical equipment; utility pole management; relocation/reconductoring of power lines with advanced conductors; vegetation and fuel-load management; microgrids and battery storage for enhancing system adaptive capacity; adaptive protection technologies; advanced modeling technologies; hardening of power lines, facilities, substations, and systems; replacement of old overhead conductors and underground cables; transmission and distribution capacity improvements; workforce development and training programs in clean energy sectors.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — available to eligible applicants operating within Maryland. All project sites must be located within the State of Maryland. Geographic diversity within the state is considered in award decisions to enhance diversity and meet federal Justice40 outcomes. Work must be performed 100% in the United States unless DOE approves otherwise.

structured_extraction.program_name: FY26 Maryland Electric School Bus Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides competitive grants to support the adoption of zero-emission electric school buses and installation of associated charging infrastructure for public and privately operated school bus fleets across Maryland. The program prioritizes overburdened communities and low-to-moderate income areas. Up to $4.9 million is available in FY2026, with grants covering up to 120% of the incremental cost of eligible electric school buses plus charging infrastructure and associated costs. Part of the Moore-Miller administration's $17 million commitment (FY25-FY26) for electric school bus grants.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $4.9 million available in FY2026. Grants cover up to 120% of the incremental cost of eligible electric school buses, plus charging infrastructure and associated costs. Charging infrastructure funding capped at up to 30% of total project funding, and up to $300,000 for EVSE/facility planning. Technician training funded up to $7,200 to certify six technicians. Project start-up expenses funded up to $200,000 for LEAs and up to $25,000 for vendors (max 4 per district). Maximum award is $2,000,000 per grantee; this cap may increase to $2,500,000 depending on income qualifications and school district size. Grants are awarded on a cost-reimbursement basis. State and federal incentives combined may not exceed the total project cost.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public Local Education Agencies (LEAs), public school districts, tribal government-operated school districts, charter schools, and private school bus vendors/fleets operating on behalf of LEAs in Maryland, with priority given to overburdened and low-to-moderate income communities, including communities with Title I schools.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase or lease of new electric school buses (Type A, C, and D); charging infrastructure equipment and installation (EVSE); facility planning for EV infrastructure (up to $300,000); technical training for technicians (up to $7,200 for six technicians); project start-up costs including staff time, fleet analysis, and EV plans; and other associated costs related to electric school bus deployment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland; strong focus on expanding access for overburdened and low-to-moderate income communities.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a public Local Education Agency (LEA), tribal government, charter school, or a fleet/private school bus vendor operating on behalf of an LEA with a contract/agreement in place.
Vehicles must be publicly-funded school buses used for routine student transportation.
Vehicles must be purchased new — retrofits or repowered vehicles are not eligible.
A vehicle that has been funded in whole or in part by another Maryland State grant may not be funded through this program.
MEA and other state incentives (including federal) may not exceed the total funding request/cost of the project.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a Jotform online application by December 26, 2025 at 3:00 PM ET. Review the Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA) and complete Attachment A (Electric School Bus Summary Table) and Attachment B (Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment Summary Table). Contact transportation.mea@maryland.gov for 1-on-1 meetings or questions about the application.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Energy Administration (MEA) Geothermal Rebate Program provides rebates to Maryland residents who install new geothermal heating and cooling (GHC) systems on residential properties. Single-family detached homes and single-family townhomes are eligible; multi-family properties are not. Rebates are awarded on a non-competitive, first-come, first-served basis for complete and eligible applications. FY26 is the final year for the program, with a total budget of $150,000.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A flat rebate of $3,000 is awarded per new geothermal heating and cooling system installation on an eligible Maryland residential property. The system must exceed 1.00 refrigerant ton (approximately 12,000 BTU/hr or 3.51 kW), must be an electrically-powered ground-source heat pump serving as the primary heating and cooling system, and must include new ground loops, pond loops, or vertically-drilled wells. Rebates are awarded on a non-competitive, first-come, first-served basis for complete and eligible applications. Total FY26 program budget is $150,000.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of a new geothermal heating and cooling system on a Maryland residential property
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to Maryland residents on Maryland residential properties. Multi-family properties are not eligible.

Property must be located in Maryland

The system must be an electrically-powered ground-source heat pump serving as the primary heating and cooling system
System must include new ground loops, pond loops, or vertically-drilled wells
Must comply with all state laws, local ordinances, permits, and inspections
Completed signature sheet and IRS W9 form required for application completion
Application must be complete and eligible
Application must be submitted by February 27, 2026 or until budget is exhausted

structured_extraction.program_name: Higher Education Clean Energy Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This competitive statewide grant program supports Maryland's accredited colleges and universities in adopting clean energy. It funds solar installations on campus, strategic sustainability and clean energy planning, clean energy curriculum development, and workforce training to create sustainable learning environments and prepare students for careers in the clean energy sector. The program also supports on-site renewable energy technologies and the integration of strategic energy planning into campus operations and academics, as well as advancement of workforce development in the renewable energy sector.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants totaling up to $8,000,000 from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF). Amount awarded may be more or less depending on quantity and quality of applications received. Per application, solar installation funding is capped at $1,000,000. Per applicant, additional caps apply: up to $145,000 for campus clean energy master planning, $145,000 for clean energy course development, and $25,000 for student internships ($5,000 per intern, maximum 5 interns). Up to 15% of total awarded grant funds can be allocated for Grant Administration Costs. Applicants may submit more than one application. Funding also supports on-site renewable energy adoption, energy planning, and renewable energy workforce development. Fossil fuel and combustion technology projects are ineligible.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Accredited two- and four-year colleges and universities in Maryland accredited by the Middle States Association of Colleges and Schools, Commission on Higher Education, including community colleges and Minority Serving Institutions (MSI) recognized by the U.S. Department of Education
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Solar system installations, strategic sustainability and clean energy campus planning (Campus Clean Energy Master Plan), clean energy curriculum development, student workforce training/internships, on-site renewable energy technologies, and strategic energy planning integration. Not eligible: fossil fuel expansion, natural gas technologies, or lifespan extensions of fossil fuel systems.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Maryland institution of higher education. For additional compliance fee-funded awards: community colleges located in census tracts with median income at or below 80% of state median income, or in overburdened or underserved communities.

Electrical schematic

structured_extraction.program_name: Inflation Reduction Act Home Energy Rebate Programs (HERO and HEAR)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Energy Administration administers two rebate programs created under the federal Inflation Reduction Act to help Maryland residents make energy-efficient home improvements. The Home Efficiency Rebates Opportunity Program (HERO) provides rebates for whole-home energy efficiency upgrades that reduce a home's energy use by at least 20%. Rebates are up to $4,000 or 50% of project costs for efficiency upgrades projected to save at least 35% of a home's energy use, or up to $2,000 or 50% of project costs for projects with modeled energy savings of 20–34%. Higher rebates are available for households with income below 80% of AMI. The program is funded by $137 million from the federal IRA. The Home Electrification and Appliance Rebates Program (HEAR) provides rebates for replacing fossil-fuel appliances (such as fuel oil or natural gas equipment) with electric alternatives, along with supporting upgrades, for income-qualifying households and multifamily building owners. HEAR rebate amounts include: heat pump HVAC systems (up to $8,000), electric panel upgrades (up to $4,000), electric wiring (up to $2,500), and heat pump water heaters (up to $1,750). The program prioritizes low-and-moderate income households, with availability to households with incomes up to 150% of AMI or multifamily buildings where at least 50% of residents have incomes at or below 150% AMI. The HERO program has received conditional DOE approval but final approval and funding receipt are still pending as of the latest update.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rebates for qualifying homeowners, landlords, and multifamily building owners for energy efficiency and electrification measures. HEAR covers: replacement of fossil-fuel appliances (e.g., fuel oil, natural gas) with electric alternatives, including heat pump air conditioning and heating systems (up to $8,000), electric panel upgrades (up to $4,000), electric wiring (up to $2,500), and heat pump water heaters (up to $1,750). Available to households with incomes up to 150% of AMI or multifamily buildings where at least 50% of residents have incomes at or below 150% AMI. HERO covers whole-home energy efficiency upgrades: rebates of up to $4,000 or 50% of project costs for efficiency upgrades projected to save at least 35% of a home's energy use, or up to $2,000 or 50% of project costs for projects with modeled energy savings of 20–34%. Higher rebates available for households with income below 80% of AMI. Final DOE approval and funding are still pending for HERO. Funded by $137 million from the federal IRA.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individual households, homeowners, landlords, and multifamily building owners with qualifying income levels (up to 150% AMI), aggregator organizations serving low-and-moderate income residents, and Maryland homeowners seeking to electrify home appliances and move away from fossil fuels or pursue whole-home energy efficiency improvements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency and electrification upgrades to homes, including replacement of fossil-fuel appliances with electric alternatives, installation of heat pump HVAC systems, electric panel upgrades, electric wiring, heat pump water heaters, and whole-home energy efficiency upgrades achieving at least 20% reduction in energy use.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Service territories vary by utility, including Potomac Edison, Southern Maryland Electric Cooperative, Baltimore Gas & Electric, Pepco, and Delmarva Power & Light (DPL).
requirements_list: Priority for low-and-moderate income households
Household income must be at or below 150% of area median income (AMI), OR multifamily building must have at least 50% of residents with incomes at or below 150% AMI
Must be a low or moderate income household (for HEAR)
Must achieve at least 20% reduction in home energy use (for HERO)
Must be replacing fossil-fuel appliances with electric alternatives (for HEAR); cannot replace electric appliances with other electric appliances
Project must be projected to save at least 20% of the home's energy use
Higher rebate amounts available for households with income less than 80% of area median income (AMI)
Projects must comply with IRA requirements and Maryland state requirements
DOE final approval required before launch
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: MEA will develop accessible rebate application processes for all Marylanders including low-income building owners and occupants. The HEAR program is available for eligible households and building owners. The HERO program has not yet launched; MEA is pursuing final DOE approval and has issued a Request for Proposals through Maryland Environmental Service to select a program delivery contractor. Education of contractors, building owners, and customers will support program uptake. Programs will be coordinated with utility and DHCD-run EmPOWER programs. Interested recipients should subscribe to email updates at irarebates.mea@maryland.gov for launch announcements. Visit the Maryland Energy Administration's website for the latest updates on program availability.

structured_extraction.program_description: The L-GEM program supports local governments in Maryland as they pursue sustainable, long-term clean energy and energy efficiency projects. It provides grant funding to help reduce energy use and greenhouse gas emissions, increase cost savings, and promote clean energy and economic development. For fiscal year 2026, the program offers $64 million in one-time funding across four areas: a non-competitive formula block grant for counties, and competitive grants for planning, energy efficiency, and electrification projects. The program incentivizes decarbonization planning, energy efficiency, clean energy, and electrification projects across Maryland's local governments, accelerating clean energy adoption at public facilities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: $64 million total in grants for FY26: $50 million for planning and renewable energy projects, $10 million for energy efficiency projects, and $4 million for electrification projects. Offered across four Areas of Interest (AOI): AOI1 is a non-competitive formula block grant available only to counties and Baltimore City, with a minimum $1 million per county plus population-based allocation and a 36-month period of performance; AOI2 is a competitive planning grant open to municipalities (grant range $50,000–$300,000, reimbursement up to 90% of total project cost); AOI3 is a competitive implementation grant for renewables and efficiency (excluding electrification) open to municipalities (grant range $50,000–$1,000,000); AOI4 is a competitive electrification grant open to counties and municipalities (grant range $50,000–$1,500,000). All grants are reimbursement-based; applicants must pay upfront and submit invoices. A 10% cost share requirement applies across all projects collectively.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Incorporated towns, cities, and counties of Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Clean energy planning (feasibility studies, energy audits, strategy development), renewable energy installation (solar PV, geothermal, landfill-gas-to-energy), building envelope improvements (weatherization, insulation), efficient equipment upgrades (heat pumps, heat pump water heaters, LEDs, building controls, retrocommissioning), electrification of fossil fuel systems (replacing fossil fuel equipment with electric alternatives), pre-electrification upgrades, and decarbonization planning projects at public facilities owned or leased by applicants.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Only incorporated towns, cities, and counties of Maryland may apply. Counties and Baltimore City are eligible for the non-competitive block grant (AOI1). Municipalities are not eligible for AOI1 but may apply for AOI2, AOI3, and AOI4. Projects must be located in the State of Maryland on eligible facilities owned or leased by the applicant.

Contact Lacey Allor or schedule a one-on-one virtual meeting for assistance.

structured_extraction.program_name: MEA's Commercial & Canopy Solar Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grant funding for the installation of solar photovoltaic (PV) systems on commercial properties, including rooftops, ground-mounts, or parking canopies. Funding is targeted toward systems that are owned by or directly benefit low-to-moderate income communities or overburdened and underserved communities in Maryland. Eligible installations must be located in a qualifying census tract with average median income at or below 80% of the state average median income, or in an overburdened/underserved community.

structured_extraction.program_name: MEA's Decarbonizing Public Schools Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Decarbonizing Public Schools Program helps Local Education Agencies (LEAs), also known as school districts, build capacity and advance strategies for clean and efficient energy use in K-12 schools and support facilities. It provides incentives for school districts to expand their capacity to manage energy data, reduce energy use and greenhouse gas emissions, and plan for future high-performance schools. The program supports energy data management, net zero energy design, solar installations, and energy efficiency upgrades. Approximately $36 million in grant funding is available from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund, Climate Action Plan, and Alternative Compliance Program, offered as both formula and competitive grants with consideration of need. Four Areas of Interest (AOIs) are available: AOI1 Capacity Building for Energy Management, AOI2 Energy Efficiency Capital, AOI3 Solar on Schools, and AOI4 Net Zero Energy Schools.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Approximately $36 million in grant funding is available from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund, Climate Action Plan, and Alternative Compliance Program. Funding is offered as both formula and competitive grants, with consideration of need. Applicants may apply for one or multiple Areas of Interest (AOIs): AOI1 Capacity Building for Energy Management (Category 1: Energy Data Management Support — base $75,000 + $3,000 × scaling factor; Category 2: Capital Planning for Energy Efficient Schools — base $70,000 + $3,000 × scaling factor; total AOI1 funding $1,500,000); AOI2 Energy Efficiency Capital (reimburses up to 75% of project costs for weatherization, electrification upgrades, HVAC, building envelope, controls, and lighting); AOI3 Solar on Schools (planning/technical studies up to $50,000; purchased solar up to $3,000/kW capped at $1,000,000; 3rd party-owned solar canopy up to $750/kW capped at $1,000,000; 3rd party-owned rooftop up to $500/kW capped at $1,000,000); AOI4 Net Zero Energy Schools (incremental costs of design, construction, and post-occupancy commissioning for NZE schools, funded over multiple fiscal years). Applications can cover an entire school district, a multi-facility subset, or individual school facilities. Partial awards are anticipated.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy data management, energy efficiency upgrades (HVAC, electrification, building envelope, controls, lighting), solar installations on schools, net zero energy school design and construction, post-occupancy commissioning, strategic capital planning, and energy policy development
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland; AOI2 and AOI3 prioritize schools located in census tracts designated as overburdened or with income at 80% or below median state income (per MDEnviroScreen Tool); schools serving qualifying census tracts but not physically located in them are eligible if at least 50% plus one of enrolled students come from qualifying tracts

structured_extraction.program_name: MEA's Jane E. Lawton Conservation Loan Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Energy Administration offers low-interest loans to Maryland nonprofit organizations, local governments, businesses, higher education institutions, and state agencies to finance cost-effective energy efficiency and conservation projects that reduce energy consumption and costs at their facilities, including commercial buildings. Funds are provided at below-market rates to nonprofits and businesses, and at zero financing cost to local governments and state agencies, resulting in significant energy savings and greenhouse gas emission reductions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest loans for energy efficiency and conservation projects. Microloans: $10,000–$50,000 at 3% interest, up to 10 years, simple payback ≤50% of project cost-effectiveness. Traditional Loans: $50,001–$500,000 at 2% interest, up to 18 years, simple payback cannot exceed project cost-effectiveness. DGS & State Agencies: Up to $2,000,000 at 0% interest plus 1% administrative fee, up to 18 years. Loans can finance up to 100% of Net Total Project Cost (facility retrofits) or Incremental Project Cost (new construction/full rehabilitation). Total available funds for FY26: $4,281,842. Program is first-come, first-served subject to funding availability.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland nonprofit organizations, local governments, businesses, higher education institutions, and state agencies seeking to fund energy efficiency and conservation improvements at their facilities, including commercial and industrial/manufacturing buildings.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy conservation measures (ECMs) and facility retrofit projects; incremental improvements projects; equipment purchase, installation, and commissioning; energy efficiency improvements. Funds can reimburse expenses incurred after Commitment Letter execution but before loan closing. Borrower must contribute minimum $250 cash plus all loan-associated fees.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Collateral must be located in Maryland (except mobile equipment and motor vehicles).

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the appropriate application online: businesses, nonprofits, and local governments use the FY26 Lawton Businesses, Nonprofits, and Local Governments Application; state agencies use the FY26 Lawton State Agency Application. Disbursement requests must include loan number, amount, project manager, contact information, tax ID, work narrative, and itemized invoices. Applications are accepted through February 27, 2026 at 3:00 P.M. EST. Contact MEA at lawton.mea@maryland.gov for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Clean Cities and Communities Coalition (MDCC&C)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Energy Administration leads a U.S. Department of Energy-designated coalition that promotes cleaner transportation solutions statewide. The coalition works with businesses, fleets, and communities to reduce dependence on fossil fuels, improve air quality, and advance alternative fuel vehicles and technologies including EVs, hydrogen, renewable fuels, and biodiesel.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Expert technical assistance and data to help fleets, fuel providers, and stakeholders adopt alternative fuels, improve fuel economy, and deploy emerging transportation technologies. Resources include coalition support, the Alternative Fuels Data Center, FuelEconomy.gov, Technical Response Service, and specialized assistance from national labs. Also includes matching fleet needs to electrification with available programs and financial support, and infrastructure development support for fueling, charging, and facilities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses, fleets, fuel providers, utilities, community leaders, and communities seeking to adopt alternative fuels and clean transportation technologies
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Shifting to affordable, efficient, and clean transportation fuels and technologies; reducing greenhouse gas emissions; evaluating new mobility options; improving equitable access to advanced transportation; infrastructure development for fueling, charging, and fleet transition planning
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Coalition Director Natalie Buscemi by email at transportation.mea@maryland.gov to become a coalition member.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's permanent Community Solar Program lets residents and businesses subscribe to a share of a local solar energy project and receive credits on their electric bills. The program replaced the earlier Community Solar Pilot Program and is managed by the Maryland Public Service Commission. Subscribers can choose projects in their electric utility service area and may qualify for special discounts if they have low or moderate income.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Subscribers sign up for a share of a community solar project in their electric utility service area (BGE, Pepco, Potomac Edison, or Delmarva Power). They receive bill credits for the solar energy their share produces. Low- and moderate-income subscribers may be eligible for special discounts. Subscription terms and pricing vary by project and subscriber management organization.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents and businesses in BGE, Pepco, Potomac Edison, and Delmarva Power utility service areas, including low- and moderate-income households
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of electricity costs through bill credits for a subscriber's share of a community solar project
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only in BGE, Pepco, Potomac Edison, and Delmarva Power utility service areas in Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a customer of an eligible electric utility (BGE, Pepco, Potomac Edison, or Delmarva Power)
Must subscribe through an approved Subscriber Management Organization
Projects must have available subscription capacity
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review the publicly available project listing spreadsheet to find a project in your utility service area. Contact the Subscriber Management Organization listed for a project that is accepting new subscribers. Low- and moderate-income applicants should ask about special discounts when contacting the Subscriber Management Organization.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Offshore Wind Supply Chain Investment Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides non-competitive grant funding to help new or existing businesses enter the offshore wind supply chain in Maryland. The program covers capital expenditures (such as relocation, construction, and equipment purchases) and costs for attending offshore wind industry events. Grants are awarded on a first-come, first-served basis.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $2,000,000 total in grant funding split across two areas of interest: AOI 1 (Capital Expenditures) has $1,750,000 available for costs like relocation, construction, and equipment purchases — grants cover up to 50% of total project costs, not to exceed $400,000, with applicants required to provide at least 50% matching funds; AOI 2 (Industry Events) has $250,000 available, with up to $5,000 one-time reimbursement per applicant (limited to one event per fiscal year) for attending eligible offshore wind or marine technology industry events. Grants are awarded on a first-come, first-served basis.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: 5:00 P.M. EST, March 15, 2025 or until all program funding has been awarded, whichever occurs first
structured_extraction.program_audience: New or existing emerging businesses (at least 51% owned by individuals with personal net worth not exceeding $6,500,000 adjusted for inflation) seeking to enter or expand into Maryland's offshore wind supply chain, including businesses willing to relocate or expand into Maryland. Minority, woman, and veteran-owned emerging businesses and members of historically disenfranchised groups are strongly encouraged to apply. Non-profit organizations and government/public institutions are also eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: AOI 1: Relocation costs, new construction or renovation of real property, purchase/installation of new or refurbished equipment, certifications (e.g., ISO certifications), and other capital expenditures for business expansion. AOI 2: Event registration fees, exhibition fees, scheduled travel costs, lodging, ground transportation, baggage fees, airfare (economy/coach only, up to 6 months in advance), meeting space audio/visual fees, and shipping sample products.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. MEA will also consider applications from businesses willing to relocate or expand into Maryland contingent upon receiving a grant award. For AOI 2, events must be located within the United States and its territories; events outside the United States are ineligible.
requirements_list: Business applicants must qualify as an 'Emerging Business' — at least 51% owned and controlled by individuals with a personal net worth not exceeding $6,500,000 (adjusted annually for inflation per Consumer Price Index)
Proposals must come from organizations interested in entering the offshore wind industry
Applicants must be able to contribute to Maryland's offshore wind supply chain and workforce
Applications must be submitted through the online Jotform portal
Applications must include all required materials as detailed in each AOI's respective Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA)
MEA will not consider administratively incomplete applications
AOI 1 applicants must provide at least 50% matching funds

AOI 1 applications must include a Project Narrative (maximum 10 pages) addressing all evaluation criteria, including: Applicant Overview, Project Scope Statement with location details and site map, Needs Assessment addressing supply chain gaps, Project Timeline with milestones and risk mitigation strategies, Project Partners list with qualifications and responsibilities, and Sustainability Statement
AOI 2 reimbursement is limited to one event per fiscal year
AOI 2 eligible events must be located within the United States and its territories
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application through the online Jotform portal specific to each Area of Interest (links provided on the program page). For AOI 1, include a Project Narrative addressing all grant scoring criteria with required sections: Applicant Overview, Project Scope Statement, Needs Assessment, Project Timeline, Project Partners, and Sustainability Statement. Include all required documents as described in each AOI's respective FOA. Questions can be directed to the program contact. Applications are reviewed on a first-come, first-served basis.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Offshore Wind Workforce Training & Education Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides competitive grant funding to nonprofit organizations, academic institutions, businesses, labor unions, and government entities to develop or expand offshore wind workforce training centers and education programs. It supports the State's offshore wind workforce training and education efforts, including general offshore wind education, technical trade skills training, and certification-based workforce training programs to prepare workers for careers in the offshore wind industry, including skilled trades, manufacturing, transportation, and logistics. The Maryland Energy Administration partners with the Maryland Department of Labor's EARN Maryland Program to fund projects for fiscal year 2026.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $3,000,000 in total competitive grant funding is available, split between two Areas of Interest (AOIs): AOI 1 (Industry Education) offers up to $1,500,000 to offset capital and operating costs for developing or expanding offshore wind education programs; individual awards are up to 75% of total project costs, not to exceed $500,000, with applicants required to provide a minimum 25% match in funds or in-kind services. AOI 2 (Workforce Training) offers up to $1,500,000 to support new or existing workforce training centers developing or expanding offshore wind certification-based training programs; individual awards are also up to 75% of total project costs, not to exceed $500,000, with a minimum 25% match required. MEA may reallocate funding between AOIs based on demand, application quality, and availability. For fiscal year 2026, MEA is working with the Maryland Department of Labor's EARN Maryland Program to fund projects.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations, academic institutions, businesses, minority-owned emerging businesses, labor unions, and state, local, and municipal governments seeking to develop or expand offshore wind education programs or workforce training centers in Maryland. Programs are intended to benefit the general public, K-12 students, graduate degree holders, members of historically marginalized and disenfranchised communities, formerly incarcerated individuals, and people with disabilities seeking careers in the offshore wind industry.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: AOI 1: Capital and operating expenditures for developing or expanding offshore wind education programs for any education level, including curriculum development and implementation, facility renovations, equipment purchase and installation, labor and personnel, permitting and inspections, administrative expenses, relocation costs, and marketing and outreach. AOI 2: Costs associated with developing or expanding offshore wind workforce certification-based training programs, including curriculum development and expansion, equipment purchase and installation, facility renovations, labor and personnel, permitting and inspections, administrative expenses, relocation costs, and supportive services for trainees. Eligible activities also include preparing people for careers in skilled trades, manufacturing, transportation, or logistics.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland; proposed projects must prepare individuals for employment within the offshore wind industry in Maryland and the larger U.S. offshore wind market.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a nonprofit organization, academic institution, business, labor union, or government entity
Proposed project must provide general offshore wind education or training for employment in the offshore wind industry
Projects must address technical trade skills and/or safety standards
Applications must be submitted through the online Jotform portal
Applications must be administratively complete with all required materials per the relevant FOA
Applicants that received funding in a previous fiscal year may apply for additional funding
Project Narrative (maximum 10 pages) addressing evaluation criteria
Applicant Overview with organizational history and mission
Project Scope Statement with goals, outputs, outcomes, and location details
Needs Assessment addressing problem/issue and anticipated impact
Detailed Project Work Plan with timeline and outreach plan
Course curricula, syllabi, and modules (or intended versions if not finalized)
Project Partners list with qualifications and responsibilities
Site map from Google Earth or mapping service showing project location(s)
Marketing/outreach plan for disadvantaged communities
List key personnel with qualifications and responsibilities
Minimum 25% matching funds or in-kind services required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For fiscal year 2026, visit the EARN Maryland Summer 2025 Solicitation for Implementation Grant Proposals webpage; the Maryland Department of Labor manages the application process. For prior cycles, review the relevant AOI Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA) for full details and submit a complete application package through the online Jotform portal linked on MEA's website. Applications must include a Project Narrative (maximum 10 pages) using the provided template addressing all scoring criteria and required sections. Questions may be submitted to the MEA Wind Team.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants to eligible individuals, nonprofit organizations, and business entities to help incentivize the installation of mechanical insulation on commercial or industrial properties in Maryland, enabling energy-saving improvements to large-scale thermal distribution networks and reducing energy waste. Focuses on energy savings through insulation of pipes, ducts, boilers, chillers, heat exchangers, tanks, valves, and related distribution hardware. Does not cover building envelope insulation or thermal system equipment repair/remediation.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are awarded on a reimbursement basis to help cover the cost of installing mechanical insulation on commercial or industrial properties to reduce energy waste in thermal distribution networks. Awards are up to 30% of qualified project expenses or $20,000 maximum per project (whichever is less). Minimum project cost is $10,000. Multiple applications per entity are allowed with a total award cap of $100,000 per entity. Funds cover project design, feasibility analysis, material acquisition, installation, and post-installation commissioning. Applications are accepted on an ongoing basis until funding is fully awarded or until December 17, 2025 at 3 P.M. EDT, whichever occurs first. Earlier applications are strongly encouraged to improve chances of receiving funding. Applicants are also encouraged to apply simultaneously for the Jane E. Lawton Conservation Loan (2% interest rate) to finance remaining eligible costs.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications are accepted on an ongoing basis until funding is fully awarded or until December 17, 2025 at 3:00 P.M. EDT, whichever occurs first.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals, nonprofit organizations, and business entities that own or operate commercial or industrial properties in Maryland with thermal heating and/or cooling systems seeking to reduce energy consumption and operating costs through mechanical insulation improvements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Project design and feasibility analysis, material acquisition for mechanical insulation, installation, and post-installation commissioning. Cannot be used for building envelope insulation, thermal system repair/remediation, or costs incurred before grant agreement execution.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — available throughout Maryland. Project must be located within the State of Maryland; funds cannot benefit facilities or offtakers outside Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be an eligible individual, nonprofit organization, or business entity
Project must involve installation of mechanical insulation on a commercial or industrial property
Applicant must own or operate an industrial or commercial facility
Total project cost must be a minimum of $10,000
Energy audit or assessment results
Insulation manufacturer cut sheets/product descriptions
Summary of leveraged funding sources
Utility rebate applications (if applicable)
12-month energy billing history
IRS Form W-9
Maryland SDAT Certificate of Good Standing (for non-governmental applicants)
Documentation of applicant organization type
Compliance with MEA General Provisions Version 3.0
Supporting documentation quantifying energy-saving potential
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application electronically in PDF format to insulation.mea@maryland.gov; electronic submission strongly encouraged. Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis. Earlier submission is strongly encouraged. Applications must be received by 3:00 P.M. EDT on December 17, 2025. Contact MEA at insulation.mea@maryland.gov or 410-537-3031 for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Medium-Duty and Heavy-Duty Zero-Emission Vehicle Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides grants to Maryland fleet companies, organizations, and communities to help cover the cost of purchasing newly manufactured zero-emission medium-duty or heavy-duty fleet vehicles and qualified heavy equipment for commercial or industrial use. It supports accelerated adoption of zero-emission vehicles (ZEVs) in medium and heavy-duty applications, covering battery electric vehicles (BEV) and hydrogen fuel cell electric vehicles (FCEV), to reduce greenhouse gas emissions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants cover up to 75% of the incremental cost difference between qualified zero-emission vehicles/equipment and equivalent conventional vehicles. AOI 1 (on-road vehicles): up to $2.5 million per applicant maximum. AOI 2 (off-road/heavy equipment): up to $375,000 per applicant maximum. Up to $10 million is available in Fiscal Year 2026, with separate funding pools for on-road vehicles and off-road equipment. Grants are paid in arrears; partial awards are possible if insufficient funds are available.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Fleet companies, organizations, and communities in Maryland seeking to purchase zero-emission medium-duty or heavy-duty vehicles or heavy equipment for commercial or industrial use, including commercial and industrial entities, agricultural operators, fleet operators, transit agencies, local government units, and manufacturers. State and federal agencies, individuals seeking funding for personal activities, public schools, and school bus operators are ineligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of newly manufactured zero-emission medium-duty or heavy-duty fleet vehicles and qualified heavy equipment property for commercial or industrial use, including industrial electrical generation equipment, industrial lift equipment, and industrial material handling equipment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to fleet companies, organizations, and communities in Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a fleet company, organization, or community located in Maryland
Vehicles and equipment must be newly manufactured and zero-emission
Must meet eligibility requirements detailed in the Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA)
Applicant must enter into a Grant Agreement with MEA if selected
IRS Form W-9 required with matching name and federal tax ID as grant agreement
State and federal agencies, individuals seeking funding for personal activities, public schools, and school bus operators are ineligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review the FY26 Application Guide and Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA) posted on the program page, then submit application materials by the deadline of November 20, 2025 at 3:00 P.M. ET. MEA offers expertise and advice to match applicant needs with available programs and financial support. Webinar recordings and slides are available to help applicants prepare.

structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive grant program administered by the Maryland Energy Administration that provides grants to nonprofit organizations and local governments to implement energy efficiency, electrification, and solar PV upgrades to single-family and multi-family homes benefiting low-to-moderate income Maryland residents. The program has two Areas of Interest: AOI 1 for energy efficiency projects (anticipated budget of $17,246,905) and AOI 2 for solar energy projects (anticipated budget of $8,000,000). AOI 1 applications are reviewed competitively within defined regional areas; AOI 2 applications are reviewed competitively statewide. Residents do not receive funds directly from MEA; rather, grants are awarded to eligible organizations serving qualifying households.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants awarded to nonprofits and local governments for energy efficiency, electrification, and solar PV upgrades that reduce residential energy usage and pass benefits to income-qualifying Maryland residents. Grants are reimbursement-based (paid in arrears for actual costs incurred). AOI 1 (energy efficiency): anticipated budget of $17,246,905; maximum $21,000 per residence. AOI 2 (solar energy): anticipated budget of $8,000,000; maximum $30,000 per home for solar PV systems (3–15 kW). 100% funding of actual installed costs up to maximums. Maximum training assistance: $6,000 per grant award. Administrative costs limited to 15% of total project costs. No charges to residents for program-funded work. Residents do not receive funds directly from MEA.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations and local government entities that serve residential buildings and Maryland residents with low-to-moderate incomes (up to 80% of state median income), including households ineligible for the Weatherization Assistance Program (WAP) or EmPOWER Maryland LIEEP.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency upgrades including weatherization, HVAC replacements, water heater replacements, appliance replacements, lighting upgrades, window repairs, and enabling repairs (AOI 1); solar PV system installations (AOI 2); grant administration costs; indirect costs; and worker training and certification assistance (up to $6,000 per grant award).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland for projects benefiting income-qualifying Maryland residents. AOI 1 applications are reviewed competitively within defined regional areas; AOI 2 applications are reviewed competitively statewide. At least 80% of worksite workers must reside in Maryland or within 50 miles of Maryland's borders.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a nonprofit organization (tax-exempt under IRC §501(c)(3), (4), or (6), incorporated and registered in Maryland) or a local government entity (city, county, and/or municipality)
Projects must benefit Maryland residents experiencing low-to-moderate incomes
Projects must generate significant reductions in residential energy usage
Non-profits must submit a Conflict of Interest Disclosure Form (with organization's Conflict of Interest Policy and board certifications) if applicable
Solar PV systems that have already received funding from the Maryland Solar Access Program (MSAP) are not eligible
Building Performance Institute (BPI) certified energy auditor must perform audit per BPI Standards 1100 and 1200 for energy efficiency measures
Energy efficiency measures must be cost-effective (Simple Payback ≤ 18 years for whole house projects)
Attic insulation upgraded to minimum R60 where possible
HVAC equipment must be ENERGY STAR certified or equivalent
Manual J heating/cooling load calculations required for HVAC replacements
Installations must meet state and local building codes and be performed by certified contractors
Execute Grant Agreement within 10 business days of electronic transmission
Comply with all Environmental Standards
Maintain comprehensive third-party legal liability insurance ($1M minimum per occurrence)
Retain all supporting documentation for 3 years from final reimbursement
Make worksite available for MEA inspection for 3 years
Grantee must not be suspended or debarred from state contracting and must not be in default on financial obligations to the State or MEA
No paid solicitors or agents retained for securing the grant (except bona fide employees)
Reimbursement requests must be received no later than 60 days after project completion
Solar systems must carry 25-year warranty on panels, 10-year warranty on inverters, and 10-year workmanship warranty
30-day cancellation right with no penalty for residents
Personal information protection and data security compliance required

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Residential and Commercial Energy Storage (RCES) Program provides grants to residential and commercial customers in Maryland to support the installation of battery energy storage systems (BESS). The program aims to improve grid reliability, increase energy resilience, and accelerate adoption of clean energy technologies statewide. It replaces the discontinued Maryland Energy Storage Income Tax Credit Program, which ended at the close of calendar year 2024.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are awarded on a first-come, first-served basis using a two-step application process. The total FY26 program budget is $2,000,000, funded from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF). Applications are accepted until June 5, 2026, or until all funding is exhausted. As of the last update (April 6, 2026), 100% of the budget has been requested and 90% reserved. The application portal is currently closed to new applications while MEA processes the existing queue; the portal may reopen if funding remains.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications must be submitted electronically through the MyMEA Portal (https://mdmea.my.site.com/MEAPrograms/rces-program-details) using a two-step process. Extensions of up to 60 days beyond the original project completion deadline may be requested no later than 30 days before the reservation expiration date.
