structured_extraction.program_description: The Resilient Maryland Program provides competitive grants for organizations to develop and install microgrids, resiliency hubs, and other distributed energy resources (DERs) for critical and community uses. Funding covers preconstruction planning and system installation, helping Maryland communities, businesses, and critical infrastructure access reliable, clean, and affordable energy. The program reduces reliance on utility-supplied power, lowers greenhouse gas emissions, and protects vital services against power outages. Grants offset the costs of planning, designing, and constructing microgrids, resilient facility power systems, resilient combined heat and power systems, solar PV systems, and battery energy storage systems for resiliency hubs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $13,000,000 in total competitive grant funding is available under three Areas of Interest (AOIs): AOI 1 (Preconstruction Planning) — $500,000 for feasibility analysis and planning activities; AOI 2 (Microgrids) — $4,500,000 for equipment and installation of microgrids, resilient facility power systems, and resilient combined heat and power (CHP) systems; AOI 3 (Resiliency Hubs) — $8,000,000 for solar photovoltaic (PV) and battery energy storage systems at community resiliency hub facilities. Funds offset costs for feasibility analysis, planning, equipment, and installation. Grant funding includes cost-sharing requirements.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations including businesses, non-profits, and government entities in Maryland seeking funding to install distributed energy resources, microgrids, or resiliency hubs for critical or community purposes. Low- and moderate-income (LMI) and vulnerable populations are especially targeted for AOI 3. Program is not open to residential applicants.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Feasibility analysis, preconstruction planning, equipment procurement, and installation of microgrids, resilient facility power systems, resilient combined heat and power systems, solar PV systems, and battery energy storage systems for resiliency hubs. Also covers renewable energy technology implementation (solar PV, microturbines, geothermal), battery energy storage systems, microgrid control systems, EV chargers, demand response systems, technical studies, and feasibility assessments.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide throughout Maryland. AOI 3 projects must be located within communities classified as Low-to-Moderate Income (LMI) or overburdened as defined in State Government Article §9-20B-05(i)(1); eligible census tracts available on MEA's website.

Funding is split across three Areas of Interest with separate eligibility and requirements detailed in the Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA)

Applicants must have an established Employer Identification Number (EIN)

For AOI 3: At least 80% of workers must reside within 50 miles of project (compliance measured by Maryland residency or within 50 miles of MD borders)
State/County/Local Government entities must comply with State Finance and Procurement Article Sections 14-416 and 17-303
Project Proposal (maximum 10 pages plus 1-page executive summary) required

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review the Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA) for detailed requirements. structured_extraction.program_description: The Solar Energy Equity (SEE) Grant Program provides grant funding to non-profit organizations and local governments to design and install solar photovoltaic (PV) energy systems on homes of low-to-moderate income Marylanders, or those in overburdened or underserved communities. Eligible homes must have previously received energy efficiency or weatherization upgrades through qualifying state programs. The program funds up to 100% of solar PV system design and installation costs, up to $25,000 per home.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants funding up to 100% of solar PV system design and installation costs, up to $25,000 per home (inclusive of all direct and indirect costs). Up to $5,000 per home may be used for roof repairs or mold remediation necessary for safe solar installation. Maximum total individual grant is $1,500,000. Total program budget is up to $10,000,000, split between two Areas of Interest (AOI 1: Direct Ownership; AOI 2: Zero-Cost Power Purchase Agreement). Reimbursement is paid in arrears after obtaining Permission to Operate (PTO) and passing all permitting inspections.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations and local governments serving low-to-moderate income households or those in overburdened/underserved communities in Maryland whose homes have already received energy efficiency or weatherization upgrades through qualifying MEA or DHCD programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Design and installation of solar photovoltaic (PV) energy-generating systems on eligible single-family homes. Eligible costs include solar PV system equipment and installation labor, energy audits (BPI-certified), and roof repairs or mold remediation (up to $5,000 per home) necessary for safe solar installation. Grant administration costs also permitted up to applicable limits.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland for homes in low-to-moderate income, overburdened, or underserved communities as defined by §1-701 of the Environmental Article, Annotated Code of Maryland. Homes must be located in eligible census tracts with average median income at or below 80% of Maryland median income.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides free-of-charge technical assistance through Maryland Environmental Service (MES) to state and local government entities for solar site surveys and preliminary development of solar projects. Focused on supporting solar energy and solar-integrated resiliency projects on existing infrastructure (buildings, parking lots, developed properties). Helps governments that want to add on-site solar power but lack the technical expertise to evaluate siting issues, so they can make informed decisions about location, use (including resiliency options), and budgeting for solar energy projects.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MEA provides technical assistance at no cost to applicants through the Maryland Environmental Service (MES). Assistance includes: solar site assessments on government-owned or controlled buildings and previously disturbed land; microgrid system sizing and rough design assistance (where resiliency is needed); detailed technical support for specific engineering problems; data analytic services (GIS mapping, energy modeling, financial analysis including ROI and NPV); solar project reviews and owner representative services. Services also include property identification and inventory, initial building evaluation via satellite imagery, on-site inspections using Solmetric SunEye 210, solar resource evaluation, vegetation assessment, roof condition coordination, proposed system sizing, energy usage estimates, and comprehensive reporting. The FY26 program budget is up to $860,000. The program is first-come, first-served and remains open until funding is expended.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications submitted before 3:00 p.m. on Friday, March 13, 2026, are likely to be funded before the end of the fiscal year. Program remains open until funding is expended (no hard deadline).
structured_extraction.program_audience: State and local government entities (counties, municipalities, state agencies and departments, public universities, community colleges, and public schools) interested in on-site solar generation but lacking the technical expertise to evaluate siting options.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Solar site surveys and preliminary development of solar projects, including evaluation of location, use (such as resiliency options), and budgeting. Also covers microgrid system sizing, GIS mapping, energy modeling, financial analysis, and solar project reviews.

requirements_list: Applicant must be a state or local government entity in Maryland (including counties, municipalities, state agencies, public universities, community colleges, and public schools)

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application through the online JotForm application portal. Applications are reviewed on a first-come, first-served basis. MEA coordinates with MES and technical service providers to deliver assistance for accepted projects.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Energy Administration (MEA) manages the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF) to make Maryland's energy more affordable, cleaner, and more reliable. SEIF funds programs that reduce energy bills, minimize energy waste, address climate change, create jobs, improve energy resilience, address energy equity, attract and retain businesses, and promote energy independence. SEIF funds are distributed through programs administered by MEA and other state agencies covering a wide range of energy-related initiatives including energy efficiency upgrades, solar energy, electric vehicles, weatherization, community solar, offshore wind, and direct bill assistance. Funding sources include RGGI (Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative) auction revenue, alternative compliance payments, and fund interest.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: SEIF funds are allocated to energy programs administered by MEA and other state agencies. Assistance types include competitive grants, rebates, direct electric utility bill assistance (including arrearage retirement up to $2,000 for past-due bills), tax credits, energy performance contracting, equipment purchase incentives (EVs, LED fixtures, charging stations), and subsidies for energy management systems. Programs cover energy efficiency upgrades (HVAC, weatherization, insulation, lighting), solar installation, electric vehicle infrastructure, microgrids, offshore wind research, and community solar. Specific program amounts and terms vary by funded sub-program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low- to moderate-income (LMI) Maryland residents, residential customers, commercial and industrial businesses, agricultural operations, local governments, public schools, nonprofits, higher education institutions, state agencies, fleet companies, and overburdened/underserved communities seeking energy affordability, reliability, clean energy programs, and energy efficiency support.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency measures and upgrades (HVAC, weatherization, insulation, lighting), solar photovoltaic installation, electric vehicle purchase incentives and charging infrastructure, energy bill assistance, arrearage retirement, offshore wind research, microgrids and energy resilience infrastructure, community solar, energy audits and analysis, state fleet EV purchases, energy policy and planning, and federal match funding for IIJA and IRA programs.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Application processes vary by sub-program administered under SEIF. Applicants should refer to the specific MEA or partner agency program page for application instructions, as programs may be competitive, first-come first-served, or ongoing.

structured_extraction.program_name: Engaging Neighborhoods, Organizations, Unions, Governments and Households (ENOUGH) Act Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Engaging Neighborhoods, Organizations, Unions, Governments and Households (ENOUGH) initiative is a first-of-its-kind, state-led, place-based, community-based strategy to fight concentrated child poverty in Maryland by directing resources into neighborhoods disproportionately impacted by systems and policies that limit wealth creation and economic mobility. Launched by Maryland Governor Wes Moore, the program provides competitive grants and technical support to eligible communities to develop and implement locally-driven solutions to deeply rooted challenges that cause child poverty. Funded communities develop Neighborhood Action Plans and Community Voice Committees to reduce childhood poverty by increasing local investments and improving economic mobility. Grant funding is available under three tracks: Track 1 (Partner Development), Track 2 (Plan Development), and Track 3 (Implementation). The Governor's Office for Children, Maryland agencies, and a network of local, state, and national organizations will partner with applicants and grantees to develop and implement community-focused solutions to end child poverty. The program represents a $20 million total investment driven by residents' lived experience and expertise, authorized under the ENOUGH Act (2024). Frederick County received one of the inaugural grants ($300,000) to work along the Route 40 / Golden Mile corridor on the west side of the City of Frederick. In Anne Arundel County, five eligible census tracts (Pumphrey/Patapsco Park, Maryland City, Clay Street, Eastport Terrace, and Bay Ridge Gardens) may apply under these tracks.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A $20 million total statewide investment providing competitive grants and technical support to eligible communities. Grant funding is available under three tracks: Track 1 (Partnership Development): ~$65,000 per award (up to 10 awards) for capacity building to address root causes of poverty; Track 2 (Plan Development): ~$300,000 per award (up to 7 awards) for community asset mapping, needs assessments, and neighborhood action plan development; Track 3 (Implementation): up to $5,000,000 per award (up to 3 awards) for implementing neighborhood action plans over 4 funding cycles. All recipients receive technical assistance, training, resource hub access, and data dashboard support. The Governor's Office for Children, Maryland agencies, and a network of local, state, and national organizations will partner with applicants and grantees to develop and implement community-focused solutions to end child poverty.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Notice of Intent to Apply Due: July 19, 2024; Full Application Deadline for Track 1: not specified; Full Application Deadline for Track 2 and Track 3: September 20, 2024
structured_extraction.program_audience: Communities and community organizations throughout Maryland most affected by concentrated child poverty, including neighborhoods, organizations, unions, governments, and households. Eligible applicants include community-based non-profit organizations, local government entities, public schools, anchor institutions, unions, philanthropic organizations, and community-led organizations serving as 'Community Quarterback.' In Anne Arundel County, eligible census tracts include Pumphrey/Patapsco Park, Maryland City, Clay Street, Eastport Terrace, and Bay Ridge Gardens. In Frederick County, the program targets neighborhoods along the Golden Mile (Route 40 corridor on the west side of the City of Frederick).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Developing and implementing community-focused solutions to end child poverty and address historic inequities and deeply rooted economic challenges, including partner development, plan development, and implementation of community-driven poverty-fighting strategies in eligible neighborhoods. Specific uses include developing Neighborhood Action Plans, establishing Community Voice Committees, increasing local investments to reduce childhood poverty and improve economic mobility, community asset mapping, needs assessments, capacity building, and implementing neighborhood action plans across funding cycles.

In Frederick County, targets neighborhoods along the Golden Mile (Route 40 corridor on the west side of the City of Frederick).

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Health and Higher Educational Facilities Authority (MHHEFA) Financing Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Health and Higher Educational Facilities Authority (MHHEFA) is a public instrumentality of the State of Maryland that provides low-cost financing to non-profit hospitals, related health care organizations, and private non-collegiate and higher educational institutions for the construction, acquisition, and refinancing of capital projects. The Authority issues bonds and provides access to capital markets through a variety of financing options tailored to meet the specific needs of each individual project.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Health and Higher Educational Facilities Authority
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MHHEFA provides least-cost financing through access to capital markets, including fixed and variable rate bonds (including commercial paper), leases and subleases, private placements, direct bank placements, public and limited public offerings, loans to participating institutions, and pooled loan programs. Financing is tailored to meet the specific needs of each individual project, covering construction, acquisition, and refinancing of approved capital projects.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit healthcare organizations (hospitals, ambulatory care centers, life plan communities, nursing homes, etc.) and non-profit educational institutions (colleges, universities, and non-collegiate schools) in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction, acquisition, and refinancing of approved capital projects including hospital facilities, parking garages, research facilities, equipment, technology improvements, campus buildings, student housing, dining halls, libraries, and utility plants.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a non-profit hospital, related health care organization, or private non-collegiate or higher educational institution

structured_extraction.program_description: The Academic Common Market (ACM) is a tuition-savings program for Maryland residents. If a degree program is not available at a public college or university in Maryland, eligible students may attend a participating out-of-state public institution offering that program and receive a waiver of out-of-state tuition charges, paying in-state tuition rates at the host institution instead of out-of-state rates.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible Maryland residents receive a waiver of out-of-state tuition charges when enrolling in an ACM-approved degree program at a participating out-of-state public college or university in a Southern Regional Education Board (SREB) member state. The student pays the in-state tuition rate at the host institution for degree programs not available at Maryland public institutions.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Three cycles per year: March 1 – June 30; September 1 – November 15; January 2 – February 28
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents who are accepted or enrolled in an ACM-approved degree program at a participating out-of-state public college or university as a degree-seeking student (undergraduate, transfer, or graduate). Undergraduate students under age 24 require a parent/legal guardian signature on the affirmation form.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of out-of-state tuition charges at participating out-of-state public institutions for approved degree programs not available at Maryland public institutions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Maryland residents statewide. Participating institutions are located in other Southern Regional Education Board (SREB) member states (note: North Carolina does not participate).
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident
Must be accepted or enrolled as a degree-seeking student (undergraduate, transfer, or graduate) in an ACM-approved program at a participating public college or university
Must be admitted to the academic program before applying (MHEC does not conduct pre-evaluations)
Must submit application through the OneStop portal within one of the three annual application cycles
Must upload two qualifying documents showing Maryland residency with matching addresses as a single PDF
Military students must also attach an earnings statement and military orders signed by their commander
Transfer students must email MHEC for special application instructions
Parent/legal guardian signature required for undergraduate students under age 24
Must maintain full-time enrollment (summers/winter breaks excluded)
Must maintain good academic standing
Cannot change major, add minor, or double major without re-certification
Authorization for MHEC to obtain information including academic standing, GPA, and enrollment status
Program must be unique (not offered in Maryland); programs with 51%+ curriculum similarity to Maryland programs may be removed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the ACM Application on the OneStop portal (https://onestop.md.gov) during one of three annual cycles. Upload a single PDF containing two residency documents verifying Maryland residency. Complete the 'Contact SREB' page with student contact and program information. Student (and parent/legal guardian if undergraduate under age 24) must sign the affirmation form under penalties of perjury. Check with your institution's ACM Coordinator for any additional requirements. Once approved, the Maryland ACM Coordinator forwards your certification to the host institution's ACM Coordinator, and it is also available in your OneStop account. Previously certified students do not need to reapply unless they change their major or have a break in enrollment.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Air Force Reserve Officer Training Corps (ROTC) Scholarship Program covers full college tuition, laboratory fees, textbook costs, and incidental fees for eligible high school graduates who commit to active duty military service after graduation. The program also provides a non-taxable $100 monthly allowance during the school year and requires a minimum four-year active duty service obligation upon graduation. It is usable at over 500 colleges and universities nationwide.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Full college tuition, laboratory fees, textbook costs, and incidental fees covered. Also provides a non-taxable $100 monthly allowance during the school year. Minimum four-year active duty service obligation required upon graduation. Available at over 500 colleges and universities nationwide.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No later than December 1 of senior year of high school
structured_extraction.program_audience: High school graduates who are U.S. citizens between the ages of 17 and 25.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: College tuition, laboratory fees, textbooks, and incidental fees.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available nationwide at over 500 participating colleges and universities.
requirements_list: Must be a U.S. citizen
Must be a high school graduate
Must be between ages 17 and 25
Awards based on SAT or ACT scores, GPA, class standing, interview, and physical aptitude test
Apply in junior year of high school or no later than December 1 of senior year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply during junior year of high school or no later than December 1 of senior year. Call 1-800-522-2091 or write to HQ AFROTC Recruiting Division, Maxwell AFB, AL 36112-6106.

structured_extraction.program_description: Recipients of career-based and occupational grant or scholarship awards from the Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC) must fulfill employment service obligations after completing their degree. They must work in Maryland in an occupation directly related to their eligible program of study. Recipients report their employment history to MHEC each year by submitting an Annual Service Questionnaire until the service obligation is fulfilled. Recipients must also submit an Employer Verification Release Form before employment history can be verified, and the employing or contracting agency must annually certify that the recipient is fulfilling the service requirement. Deferment is available for recipients enrolled in full-time or part-time undergraduate or graduate degree programs, with a Registrar Certification Form required for deferment requests. This includes recipients of phased-out programs who still have outstanding obligations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: This is a compliance and reporting process — not a direct funding program. Recipients of career-based and occupational grants or scholarships must fulfill a service obligation by working in Maryland in a field related to their program of study. Recipients verify employment annually by submitting an Annual Service Questionnaire and an Employer Verification Release Form through MHEC's MDCAPS online portal. The employing or contracting agency must certify annually that the recipient is fulfilling the service requirement. Eligible employer types include State/Local/Federal Government, 501(c)(3) or (4) nonprofits, for-profit organizations, public schools, public prekindergarten programs, licensed hospitals, nursing homes, adult day care centers, public health agencies, and home health agencies — particularly those serving low-income or underserved Maryland residents. Deferment is available for recipients enrolled full-time (12+ credits/semester undergraduate; 9+ credits/semester graduate) or part-time (6-11 credits undergraduate; 6-8 credits graduate) in a degree-granting program, with a Registrar Certification Form required. Enrollment below 6 credits may result in repayment obligations.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Employer Verification Release Form must be returned within 10 business days
structured_extraction.program_audience: Current recipients of MHEC career-based and occupational grant or scholarship awards who have completed their degree and are fulfilling their service obligation, including recipients of phased-out programs who still have outstanding obligations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable — this page describes service obligation requirements and the annual reporting process for existing grant/scholarship recipients, not a funding program open to new applicants.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Recipients must be employed within the State of Maryland in an occupation related to their eligible program of study. Employers that primarily serve low-income or underserved Maryland residents are preferred qualifying organizations.
requirements_list: Must be a recipient of a career-based or occupational grant or scholarship from MHEC
Must begin employment in Maryland after degree completion in an occupation related to the eligible program of study
Must submit an Annual Service Questionnaire each year through MDCAPS
Must complete and upload the Employer Verification Release Form when submitting the questionnaire
Recipient must authorize employer to release employment information (Section A of Employer Verification Release Form)
Employer must complete Section B verification and return form to employee within 10 business days

Employment must be with a qualifying organization type (State/Local/Federal Government, nonprofits, for-profit, public schools, public prekindergarten programs, licensed hospitals, nursing homes, adult day care centers, public health agencies, home health agencies)
Organization preferably serves low-income or underserved Maryland residents
Full documentation of employment dates, job title, hours worked, and employment status required
Employer or contracting agency must annually certify that the recipient is performing the service requirement

Deferment available if enrolled full-time (12+ credits/semester undergraduate, 9+ credits/semester graduate) or part-time (6-11 credits/semester undergraduate, 6-8 credits/semester graduate) in a degree-granting program
Enrollment below 6 credits may result in repayment obligations

Submit a Registrar Certification Form (Section A completed by student; Section B completed by college/university registrar with official seal and signature) when requesting deferment due to enrollment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Recipients log in to their MDCAPS account at https://mdcaps.mhec.state.md.us/MDCAPS/login.aspx, complete the Annual Service Questionnaire, download and upload the Employer Verification Release Form (recipient completes Section A authorization; employer completes Section B verification and returns within 10 business days). If requesting deferment, student completes Section A of the Registrar Certification Form, sends it to the college/university for Section B completion with official seal and signature, then returns the completed form to the Office of Student Financial Assistance.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Army Reserve Officer Training Corps (ROTC) Scholarship Program provides tuition, laboratory fees, and a standard textbook and supplies allowance to eligible high school graduates who commit to military service after graduation. Recipients also receive a tax-free subsistence allowance of up to $1,500 each school year of scholarship support. Recipients must fulfill a military service obligation: either 2–4 years active duty followed by Army National Guard or Army Reserve service, or 8 years in the Army National Guard or Army Reserve.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Covers tuition, laboratory fees, and a standard amount for textbooks, classroom supplies, and equipment. Also provides a tax-free subsistence allowance of up to $1,500 each school year of scholarship support. Recipients must fulfill a military service obligation (2–4 years active duty followed by National Guard or Reserve service, or 8 years in the Army National Guard or Army Reserve).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Apply during junior year in high school
structured_extraction.program_audience: High school graduates who are U.S. citizens between the ages of 17 and 21.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: College tuition, laboratory fees, textbooks, classroom supplies, and equipment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Four-year scholarship recipients must attend Army ROTC host institutions; two- and three-year recipients may attend any college offering Army ROTC.
requirements_list: Must be a U.S. citizen
Must be between ages 17 and 21
Must be a high school graduate
Awards based on SAT or ACT scores, high school academic review, interview, and physical aptitude exam
Apply during junior year in high school
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply during your junior year in high school. Write to the Department of the Army, ROTC Scholarships, Ft. Monroe, VA 23651.

structured_extraction.program_name: Brightwood College Closed School Loan Discharge
structured_extraction.program_description: Federal student loan discharge program for students who attended Brightwood College when it closed in December 2018. Eligible students can have their federal student loans discharged and receive reimbursement for amounts already paid.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Discharge of Federal Direct Loans, Federal Perkins Loans, or FFEL Loans used to attend Brightwood College, plus reimbursement of amounts already paid on those loans.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students who were actively enrolled at Brightwood College when it closed December 7, 2018, or who withdrew up to 120 days before closure and could not complete their program of study.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Discharge of federal student loans used to attend Brightwood College.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Maryland Brightwood College students statewide.
requirements_list: Must have been actively enrolled at Brightwood College at the time of closure or withdrawn within 120 days before closure
Must not have been able to complete the program of study
Must not have completed the program at another school (which would disqualify the discharge)
Must file an application with your loan servicer
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Determine your loan servicer and current federal debt at nslds.ed.gov. Download the Closed School Loan Discharge Form and submit it to your loan servicer.

structured_extraction.program_name: Brightwood College State Refund (First Report of Claim)
structured_extraction.program_description: State refund program for students affected by the closure of Brightwood College campuses in Baltimore, Beltsville, and Towson on December 7, 2018. Provides refunds of self-paid tuition, fees, and private lender monies paid to the institution. Students not pursuing a credit transfer may apply for a state-issued refund.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Refund of self-paid tuition/fees and private lender monies paid to Brightwood College. Four options available: (1) Federal loan discharge + state refund, (2) Teach-out at approved institution, (3) Maryland Registered Apprenticeship, (4) Independent transfer. Does not cover federal loans under the state refund option.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students enrolled at Brightwood College Baltimore, Beltsville, or Towson at time of closure (December 7, 2018), or on approved leave of absence, or former students who did not receive required refunds and are not pursuing a credit transfer.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: State refund of tuition and fees paid by students or private lenders to Brightwood College.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Brightwood College campuses: 1520 South Caton Avenue, Baltimore; 4600 Powder Mill Road, Beltsville; 803 Glen Eagles Court, Towson.
requirements_list: Must have been enrolled or on approved leave of absence as of December 7, 2018
Must not be pursuing a transfer of Brightwood credits to a new institution
Payments must have been made via cash or private loans (not federal loans) for state refund option
Must complete the First Report of Claim form
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and submit the First Report of Claim form available on the MHEC website.

structured_extraction.program_name: Charles W. Riley Firefighter and Ambulance and Rescue Squad Member Scholarship Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This scholarship program encourages active career and volunteer firefighters, ambulance crew members, and rescue squad members who serve Maryland communities to take credited college courses leading to a degree in fire service technology, emergency medical technology, fire service management, or public safety administration with a related concentration. It provides annual financial awards covering at least 50% of tuition and mandatory fees at eligible Maryland institutions, supporting Maryland residents who serve in fire-fighting, ambulance, and rescue organizations to pursue credited courses that lead to employment in organized fire departments, ambulance, or rescue squads in Maryland. Renewal recipients are given priority over initial applicants, and both groups are ranked by submission date of their completed application. Recipients must sign a Promissory Note and Employment Obligation Agreement before receiving payment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual award of at least 50% of the student's actual annual tuition and mandatory fees at an eligible institution. The award cannot exceed the highest annual expenses for a full-time resident undergraduate at a University System of Maryland four-year public institution (excluding UMGC/UMUC and UMB). Up to five years of total funding available. Renewal recipients are given priority over initial applicants, and both groups are ranked by submission date of their completed application. Applicants not selected are placed on a waitlist pending available funding. Recipients must sign a Promissory Note and Employment Obligation Agreement before payment is released.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: 2025-2026 academic year closing date: April 1, 2026; 2026-2027 academic year application opens January 15, 2026 and closes October 15, 2026; MHEC One App and required documentation: May 1
structured_extraction.program_audience: Active career or volunteer firefighters, ambulance crew members, and rescue squad members serving Maryland communities who are Maryland residents (and dependent students whose parents are also Maryland residents) pursuing qualifying higher education degrees in fire service technology, emergency medical technology, fire service management, or public safety administration with a fire service concentration.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition and mandatory fees at an eligible Maryland institution for degree programs in fire service technology, emergency medical technology, fire service management, or public safety administration with a fire service concentration; credited courses leading to employment in an organized fire department, ambulance, or rescue squad in Maryland.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to Maryland residents (dependent students' parents must also be Maryland residents) who are members of fire-fighting, ambulance, or rescue organizations serving Maryland communities and who attend an eligible institution in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be an actively engaged career or volunteer firefighter, ambulance, or rescue squad member
Maryland resident (dependent students' parents must also be Maryland residents)
Member of a fire-fighting, ambulance, or rescue organization serving Maryland communities

Volunteer members in a county/municipality with a Length of Service Award Program (LOSAP) must have recorded at least 50 LOSAP points in the prior tax year, earned in at least two different categories
Volunteer members in a county/municipality without LOSAP must have recorded at least 50 points under the local point system in the prior tax year, earned in at least two different categories
Career members must have worked a minimum of 1,000 hours as part of a fire, ambulance, or rescue squad in the prior tax year
Must maintain a 2.5 GPA on a 4.0 scale
Must meet Satisfactory Academic Progress (SAP) requirements
Must be accepted for admission or enrolled at an eligible Maryland institution (full-time: 12+ credits; part-time: 6-11 credits)

Initial applicants must submit the online application, Service Verification Form, Fire Official Acceptance Letter or comparable documentation, and LOSAP or points documentation (if active volunteer) through MDCAPS
If awarded, initial applicants must electronically sign a Promissory Note and Employment Obligation Agreement in MDCAPS before payment is released
Renewal recipients must submit updated Service Verification Form and LOSAP or points documentation (if active volunteer)
Must submit all required documents through MDCAPS by the closing date
Submit MHEC One-App and required documentation by May 1 (where applicable)
Enrolled in credited courses leading to employment in a fire department, ambulance, or rescue squad in Maryland
Must work at least 1 year as a volunteer or career firefighter, ambulance, or rescue squad member in Maryland after completion of study; must repay funds if service obligation is not completed
FAFSA not required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the online application and all required documents through the Maryland College Aid Processing System (MDCAPS) at https://mdcaps.mhec.state.md.us by the application closing date. Initial applicants must upload supporting documents including a Riley Application, Riley Service Verification Form, Official Acceptance Letter or comparable documentation, and LOSAP/points documentation (if active volunteer). If awarded, initial applicants must electronically sign the Riley Fire Promissory Note and Riley Fire Employment Obligation Agreement in MDCAPS before receiving payment. Renewal applicants must resubmit the Riley Service Verification Form and LOSAP or points documentation (if active volunteer) each year. Renewal recipients receive priority over initial applicants; within each group, applicants are ranked by the date their completed application is submitted. Also submit MHEC One App and required documentation by May 1. Awards are provided on a first-come, first-served basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state grant program administered by the Maryland Higher Education Commission that supports college access and completion goals by providing financial support and fostering collaboration between Maryland's high-need local education agencies (LEAs) and higher education institutions. The program funds activities that encourage disadvantaged and low-income students in grades 6-12 to aim higher, study harder, and take courses required for college admission. Recipients provide student support services, mentoring, and financial aid counseling. The program works in conjunction with the federally funded Maryland GEAR UP program and serves students in high-need areas including Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Caroline County, Prince George's County, Somerset County, and Wicomico County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State grant funding of up to $150,000 per project awarded to accredited Maryland public or independent two- or four-year higher education institutions. Partnerships between a lead higher education institution and a non-profit organization are welcome to apply. Funds support one or more of three activity types: (A) Academic Services to Students (enrichment, remediation, tutoring); (B) Student and Family Financial Aid Advising Services; (C) Student and Family Academic Planning and Career Counseling. Grant disbursement: 50% at project start, 50% upon receipt and processing of interim report. Indirect costs cannot exceed 8% of funds requested. The current project period runs August 5, 2025 through August 4, 2026.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: July 25, 2025 at 4:00 p.m. (electronic and paper submission)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Accredited Maryland public or independent two- or four-year higher education institutions, with partnerships between a lead institution and a non-profit organization welcome. Serves Maryland middle and high school students in grades 6-12 in high-need areas, particularly students eligible for Free and Reduced-price Meals Services (FARMS) and those requiring college remediation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supporting college access and completion initiatives for economically and environmentally disadvantaged students in grades 6-12, including academic services (tutoring, enrichment, remediation), financial aid advising, college and career counseling, professional development, college visits, internships, parent/family programming, salaries and wages, fringe benefits, travel (in-state), materials and supplies, consultant and contractual services, and facility rental.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must serve students in high-need LEAs meeting at least 3 of 4 eligibility criteria: ≥44.4% FARM students in feeder middle schools; ≥39.6% FARM students in feeder high schools; FARM cohort graduation rate below 77.93%; college remediation rate above 32.7%. Priority counties include Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Caroline County, Prince George's County, Somerset County, and Wicomico County. GEAR UP districts include Baltimore City, Dorchester, and Wicomico counties.
requirements_list: Must be an accredited Maryland public or independent two- or four-year institution of higher education
Partnerships between a lead higher education institution and a non-profit organization are welcome to apply
Must partner with a Local Education Authority (LEA)
Must serve students in eligible high-need LEA school sites meeting at least 3 of 4 FARM/graduation/remediation eligibility criteria
Program must serve low-income and disadvantaged students
Cooperative planning between higher education institution and local education agency required
Diagnosis of basic skill deficiencies required
Formalized agreement(s) with participating LEA(s) and collaborative partners required
Funds must supplement, not supplant, existing programs
Must comply with Title VI Civil Rights Act of 1964
Must participate in statewide assessment/evaluation programs as required by MHEC
Must provide MHEC and Legislative Auditor access to records
Records retention required for 5 years
Partner coordination required including LEA Coordinator, High School Principal, and other partners with documented signatures and roles/responsibilities
Proposal narrative maximum 15 pages, 12-point Times New Roman or Arial font, single-spaced, 8.5x11 inch pages with 1-inch margins
Submit original proposal with hard copies and electronic copy
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit both electronic and paper applications by the deadline of July 25, 2025 at 4:00 p.m. Electronic submission should include: Abstract (Word), entire proposal (PDF), and budget request (Excel). Hard copy submission: 1 original plus copies with all required components in order; original hard copy signatures preferably in blue ink. Submit to Anthony Reiner at MHEC via mail, hand delivery, or email. Refer to the FY2025 CPIP RFP and appendices for full application requirements including proposal forms, proposal checklist, and Maryland Local Education Agency information. Applications are reviewed by a CPIP review panel.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community College Tuition Waiver for Students with Disabilities Receiving SSI or SSDI
structured_extraction.program_description: This program waives tuition at Maryland community colleges for students with disabilities who receive Supplemental Security Income (SSI) or Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) benefits. The waiver covers tuition remaining after any grants and scholarships are applied, for up to 12 credits per semester in degree or certificate programs designed to lead to employment, or up to 6 credits per semester for other community college credit courses. A course must have at least 10 enrolled students for the waiver to apply. Students remain responsible for all other costs such as books.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Students are exempt from paying tuition at Maryland community colleges for up to 12 credits per semester when enrolled in degree or certificate programs designed to lead to employment, or up to 6 credits per semester for other enrollment purposes. The waiver applies to the tuition balance remaining after all grants and scholarships have been applied. A course must have at least 10 enrolled students for the waiver to apply. Students remain responsible for all other costs such as books. Students must file the FAFSA by March 1 each year (June 1 also referenced in some sources) and contact their college financial aid office to activate the waiver each time they enroll.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: March 1 each year (for State aid consideration); FAFSA by June 1 also referenced in some sources; contact your financial aid office to apply
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students receiving SSI or SSDI benefits who plan to attend a Maryland community college
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition costs at Maryland community colleges for degree, certificate, or continuing education programs designed to lead to employment, or other community college credit courses
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at community colleges throughout Maryland
requirements_list: Must be receiving Supplemental Security Income (SSI) or Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) benefits
Must provide proof from the Social Security Administration (SSA) of receiving SSI or SSDI benefits
Must complete and submit the FAFSA annually; for State aid consideration, FAFSA must be filed between January 1 and March 1 each year (June 1 also referenced in some sources)
Must contact the financial aid office at the community college to activate the waiver
Must request the waiver every time you enroll
Course must have at least 10 enrolled students for the waiver to apply
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and submit the FAFSA at www.fafsa.gov between January 1 and March 1 each year (June 1 also referenced in some sources). Then contact the financial aid office at the community college you plan to attend to have the waiver activated. The waiver must be requested each time you enroll.

structured_extraction.program_name: Complete College Maryland – One Step Away (OSA) Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive, state-funded grant program administered by the Maryland Higher Education Commission that funds accredited Maryland public and nonprofit independent two-year and four-year colleges and universities to identify, re-engage, re-enroll, and help graduate near-completer students — those who have earned 75% or more of the credits needed for an associate or bachelor's degree but have stopped out for 12 or more consecutive months without obtaining a degree. Funded institutions provide financial assistance, tutoring, customized degree plans, and dedicated One Step Away advisors to support near-completers in earning their degrees. Grants are awarded competitively, with institutions required to provide in-kind or matching funds equal to at least one-third of the total project cost.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants of up to $60,000 per institution. Institutions must provide in-kind or matching funds equal to at least one-third of the total project cost; up to 8% of total direct costs may be claimed as indirect costs for matching purposes only. The current grant period runs from August 5, 2025 through August 31, 2026. In the 2018 funding cycle, more than $311,000 was distributed among six institutions, with individual awards ranging from approximately $41,000 to $57,000. Funds support salaries and wages, fringe benefits, travel, equipment, materials and supplies, consultant and contractual services, financial assistance for students (including tuition discounts and textbook cost waivers), tutoring services, customized degree plans, and dedicated One Step Away advisors. Grants supplement new and/or existing programs and cannot be used to supplant non-grant funds.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Accredited Maryland public and nonprofit independent two-year and four-year associate and bachelor's degree-granting colleges and universities serving near-completer students — both degree-eligible and degree-potential — who have earned 75% or more of their college credits and have stopped attending for at least 12 consecutive months.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Identifying, contacting, re-engaging, re-enrolling, and graduating near-completer students who have earned 75% or more of credits toward an associate or bachelor's degree but have stopped out for 12 or more consecutive months, through: degree audit infrastructure and software enhancements; individualized or template-based degree program completion plans; enhancement/redesign of degree programs; establishment of concierge or near-completer counselor approaches; faculty and staff development; marketing and outreach; academic, financial, and social advising; prior learning assessments and competency-based testing; alternative/general studies degree programs; financial aid including tuition discounts and textbook waivers; salaries and wages for project personnel; fringe benefits; travel; equipment; materials and supplies; and consultant and contractual services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — available to eligible accredited higher education institutions located across Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be an accredited Maryland public or nonprofit independent two- or four-year college or university that grants associate or bachelor's degrees.
Must provide in-kind or matching funds equal to at least one-third of the total project cost.
Program must target near-completer students (those who have earned 75% or more of credits toward a degree but stopped out for 12 or more consecutive months).
Target students must have earned 75% or more of their college credits.
Target students must have postponed their education for at least 12 consecutive months.
Must demonstrate sustainability of initiative after grant ends.
Must report specific data metrics on degree-eligible and degree-potential near-completers.
Must complete Needs Assessment, Project Objectives and Outcomes, Management Plan, Operations Plan, and Project Evaluation.
Up to 8% indirect costs allowable as in-kind match only.

Projects must address at least two of six defined objectives (outreach strategies, student support systems, re-enrollment tracks, prior learning assessments, alternative degree programs, and sustainable financial aid options).
Must track and report demographic data (gender, race, age, degree program) on near-completers.
Must report on degree-eligible and degree-potential near-completers' contact, re-enrollment, and completion rates.
Must comply with Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964.
Must comply with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA).
Must comply with all relevant federal and state laws.
Must participate in statewide assessment/evaluation programs.
Must maintain records for 5 years.
Must obtain prior written approval for scope changes, personnel changes, or budget changes exceeding $1,000 or 10% in any category.
Must submit interim and final reports, including Final Narrative and Final Budget Summary Report.
Must acknowledge MHEC support in publications.
Funds must supplement, not supplant, non-grant funds.
Finance officer signature required on final budget summary report.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a completed application including project narrative (Needs Assessment, Project Objectives and Projected Outcomes, Management Plan, Operations Plan, and Project Evaluation), budget summary, budget narrative, and institutional assurances with authorized institutional authority signature. Applications are submitted to the Maryland Higher Education Commission by the deadline of Friday, July 25, 2025 at 4:00 p.m. During the grant period, institutions must submit interim progress reports (electronic copy of Narrative Progress Report and Budget Expenditure Report) to the MHEC contact. At grant end, institutions must submit a Final Progress Report and signed Final Budget Summary Report. Grantees are subject to monitoring visits and desk reviews. Contact Anthony Reiner at Anthony.Reiner@Maryland.gov for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: This scholarship supports Maryland students pursuing education in cybersecurity-related degree or certificate programs identified by the Secretary of Higher Education as directly relevant to cybersecurity at eligible Maryland public or private non-profit institutions. Recipients must be within three years of graduation, have at least a 3.0 cumulative GPA, and commit to working in the cybersecurity field for a Maryland government agency, local education agency, public high school, or community college after graduation. If the service obligation is not fulfilled, the award converts to a repayable loan.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual scholarship award in an amount prescribed by MHEC that may be used to pay for tuition, mandatory fees, and room and board at an eligible Maryland public or private non-profit institution. Full-time students may renew for up to two additional years; part-time students may renew for up to five additional years. If the service obligation is not met, the award converts to a repayable loan.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: The 2026-2027 application opens January 15, 2026 and closes October 15, 2026. April 1, 2026 deadline applies for the 2025-2026 academic year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students currently enrolled full-time or part-time at a public or private non-profit institution in Maryland who are within three years of graduating from an approved cybersecurity degree or certificate program, have at least a 3.0 cumulative GPA, and have completed at least 25% of their credit requirements, and who commit to Maryland public service employment after graduation. Part-time students must take at least 6 semester hours per semester.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition, mandatory fees, and room and board at an eligible Maryland institution.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicant must be enrolled at a public or private non-profit institution in Maryland in an approved cybersecurity degree or certificate program identified by the Secretary of Higher Education as directly relevant to cybersecurity. Applicant must be eligible for in-state tuition under Maryland Education Article, Title 15. Service obligation must be fulfilled in the State of Maryland.

Enrolled full-time or part-time at a public or private non-profit institution in Maryland

Within three years of graduation from an approved, credit-bearing cybersecurity degree or certificate program
Cumulative GPA of at least 3.0 at the time of application
Completed at least 25% of total credit requirements toward the approved degree or certificate
Enrolled in an MHEC-approved cybersecurity program
Must not have received a Federal Cyber Corps Scholarships for Service award
Part-time students must take at least 6 semester hours per semester and maintain in-state tuition eligibility

Must sign an agreement to work in Maryland in the cybersecurity field for an eligible employer after graduation (local education agency, public high school, community college, state/county/city government, or teach in an eligible cybersecurity education program)
Submit cybersecurity application and required documentation by the application deadline
Must submit official or unofficial college transcript
Must submit Institutional Verification Form confirming enrollment in an approved cybersecurity program
Must apply through MDCAPS (https://mdcaps.mhec.state.md.us)
For renewal: must continue to be eligible for in-state tuition, maintain satisfactory academic progress, and maintain at least a 3.0 GPA
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the online application through the Maryland College Aid Processing System (MDCAPS) at https://mdcaps.mhec.state.md.us using the MHEC One App. Upload all required documents (transcript and Institutional Verification Form) through your MDCAPS account by the closing date. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. The 2026-2027 application opens January 15, 2026 and closes October 15, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_name: Douglas J.J. Peters Veterans of Afghanistan and Iraq Conflicts Scholarship Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Douglas J.J. Peters Veterans of Afghanistan and Iraq Conflicts Scholarship (VAIC) provides financial assistance to U.S. Armed Forces personnel who served in the Afghanistan or Iraq Conflicts, as well as their children (son, daughter, stepson, stepdaughter) or spouse, who are current high school seniors or full-time or part-time degree-seeking undergraduate students enrolled at an eligible accredited Maryland postsecondary institution. Awards are renewable for up to 4 years of full-time enrollment or 8 years of part-time enrollment. Applicants must submit the MHEC One-App and all required documentation by the deadline.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual scholarship awards up to 50% of the annual tuition, mandatory fees, and room and board at the highest-cost four-year public University System of Maryland institution (excluding UMGC and UMB). Maximum award amounts for 2026-2027: up to $9,189 (on campus), up to $5,756 (off campus), or up to $5,186 (living with parents). Awards supplement federal education benefits but total aid may not exceed cost of attendance. Renewal students are given first priority; eligible veterans have priority over dependents and spouses. Renewable for up to 4 years of full-time enrollment or 8 years of part-time enrollment.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: October 15, 2026 (for 2026-2027 academic year); application window January 15, 2026 through October 15, 2026; MHEC One-App and all required documentation due by October 1; FAFSA or MHEC One-App for Undocumented Students must be submitted by March 1
structured_extraction.program_audience: U.S. Armed Forces personnel who served in Afghanistan or Iraq Conflicts (including veterans, active duty members, reserve component members, and Maryland National Guard members activated for those conflicts, on or after October 24, 2001 for Afghanistan and on or after March 19, 2003 for Iraq) and their qualifying family members (son, daughter, stepson, stepdaughter, or spouse) who are current high school seniors or undergraduate students, and who are Maryland residents (or active duty military stationed in Maryland) enrolled or accepted at an eligible Maryland postsecondary institution.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational expenses including tuition, mandatory fees, and room and board at any eligible accredited Maryland postsecondary institution. Funds are paid directly to the institution after enrollment certification.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be Maryland residents (including active military members stationed in Maryland or whose home of residency is Maryland) enrolled or accepted in an eligible undergraduate or 2-year terminal certificate program at an eligible accredited Maryland postsecondary institution.
requirements_list: Must have served in Afghanistan (on or after October 24, 2001) or Iraq (on or after March 19, 2003), including contiguous air space or waters, or be the spouse, son, daughter, stepson, or stepdaughter of such a service member
Must be a Maryland resident or an active duty military member stationed in Maryland
Must be a current high school senior or full-time or part-time degree-seeking undergraduate student
Must be accepted or enrolled in a regular undergraduate program or eligible 2-year terminal certificate program (with transferable credits) at an eligible Maryland institution
Must be enrolled at least part-time (6-11 credits per semester) or full-time (12+ credits per semester)
If filing the FAFSA or MHEC One-App for Undocumented Students, it must be completed by March 1 of the applicable award year
Must submit the MHEC One-App and all required documentation by October 1
Must submit required military service documentation (e.g., DD-214, marriage certificate, birth certificate, or military orders) through MDCAPS account
Required documentation varies by applicant type: marriage certificate, birth certificate, military orders, and/or DD-214 as applicable
Renewal recipients must maintain enrollment in an eligible program, remain a Maryland resident, and make satisfactory academic progress
Total financial assistance cannot exceed cost of attendance
Award must be accepted within six weeks of notification date
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the online application through the MHEC One-App on the Maryland College Aid Processing System (MDCAPS) at https://mdcaps.mhec.state.md.us. The application window for 2026-2027 is January 15, 2026 through October 15, 2026. Upload all required supporting documents (such as DD-214, marriage certificate, birth certificate, or military orders) through your MDCAPS account by October 1. If filing a FAFSA or MHEC One-App for Undocumented Students, complete it by March 1 of the applicable award year. Renewal students are prioritized over initial applicants; initial applicants are ranked by submission date. Accept award via MDCAPS within six weeks of notification. Renewal students do not need to reapply.

structured_extraction.program_name: Dr. Peg E. Daw Nurse Faculty Annual Recognition Award (NFAR)
structured_extraction.program_description: An annual award program administered by the Maryland Higher Education Commission that recognizes outstanding full-time Maryland nurse faculty members for their contributions to nursing education and service to nursing students. Recipients are nominated by their Dean or Director of Nursing at a Maryland School of Nursing and selected based on excellence in teaching, impact on students, engagement in the nursing program and institution, innovation in education and technology, and contributions to nursing education. Each recipient receives a $10,000 award. In 2024, 35 nurse faculty members received awards totaling $350,000.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Each award recipient receives a $10,000 grant. In 2024, 35 nurse faculty members received awards totaling $350,000. Recipients are full-time nurse faculty nominated by their Dean or Director of Nursing and selected based on excellence in teaching, impact on students, engagement in the nursing program and institution, innovation in education and technology, and contributions to nursing education.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Full-time Maryland nurse faculty members at Maryland Schools of Nursing
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Recognition award for outstanding contributions and service in nursing education; no restricted use stated
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to full-time nurse faculty at Maryland Schools of Nursing statewide
requirements_list: Must be a full-time Maryland nurse faculty member
Must be nominated by the Dean or Director of Nursing at a Maryland School of Nursing

Must demonstrate excellence in one or more of five categories: teaching, impact on students, engagement in the nursing program and institution, innovation in education and technology, or contributions to nursing education
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Candidates are nominated by their Dean or Director of Nursing at a Maryland School of Nursing. The Nurse Support Program II administers the selection process on behalf of the Maryland Higher Education Commission.

structured_extraction.program_name: Edward T. and Mary A. Conroy Memorial Scholarship Program & Jean B. Cryor Memorial Scholarship Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Two combined scholarship programs administered by the Maryland Higher Education Commission. The Conroy program provides student financial assistance to certain Maryland residents based on their eligible military or public safety service, or their family or marital relationship to such an individual. Eligible categories include veterans with service-connected disabilities of 25% or greater who have exhausted federal benefits, dependents and surviving spouses of U.S. Armed Forces members killed or 100% permanently disabled in service, dependents/spouses of September 11 victims, POW/MIA veterans of the Vietnam Conflict and their children/stepchildren, and dependents/spouses of public safety employees killed or 100% disabled in the line of duty, as well as public safety employees who were 100% disabled in the line of duty. The Jean B. Cryor component provides assistance to eligible children and surviving spouses of school employees who died or were rendered 100% disabled as a victim of violence in the line of duty. These are merit-based scholarships (not need-based); awards are determined by the institution's financial aid department. Awards are administered through the college financial aid office with an annual deadline of July 15.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Scholarship awards up to a maximum of $14,086 for the 2026-2027 academic year (up from $13,689 for the 2025-2026 academic year). The award may not exceed the equivalent annual tuition and mandatory fees of a resident undergraduate at the highest-cost four-year public institution in the University System of Maryland (excluding University of Maryland University College and University of Maryland, Baltimore). Minimum award is $3,000 or the equivalent annual tuition and mandatory fees at the institution attended, whichever is less. Awards may be held for up to five years of full-time study (12+ credits per semester) or eight years of part-time study (6–11 credits per semester), or a combination of both. Covers tuition and mandatory fees at eligible undergraduate, graduate, professional, or 2-year terminal certificate programs at an eligible institution, or enrollment in a private career school. The scholarship is administered through the college financial aid office with a deadline of July 15. FAFSA is not required (merit-based program).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents who are veterans with a service-connected disability of 25% or greater who have exhausted federal veterans' educational benefits, dependents or surviving spouses of U.S. Armed Forces members killed or 100% permanently disabled in service, dependents/spouses of September 11 terrorist attack victims, POW/MIA individuals from the Vietnam Conflict or their children/stepchildren, public safety employees who were 100% disabled in the line of duty, dependents or spouses of public safety employees killed or 100% disabled in the line of duty, and children or surviving spouses of school employees killed or 100% disabled by violence in the line of duty.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition and mandatory fees at eligible undergraduate, graduate, professional, or 2-year terminal certificate programs at an eligible institution, or enrollment in a private career school.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must generally be Maryland residents at the time of application. Certain public safety employees who were 100% disabled in the line of duty, their family members, and surviving spouses are exempt from the Maryland residency requirement. Must attend an eligible institution of higher learning within Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be at least 16 years old

Must be enrolled at least part-time in an eligible undergraduate, graduate, or professional program at an eligible institution, OR in a 2-year terminal certificate program with transfer credit to a baccalaureate program, OR in a private career school

Must qualify under at least one eligible category: child/stepchild/surviving spouse of a U.S. Armed Forces member who died or became 100% permanently disabled due to service (death after December 7, 1941, or disability after December 7, 1942); a veteran with a service-connected disability of 25% or greater who has exhausted federal veterans' educational benefits; child/stepchild/surviving spouse of a September 11, 2001 terrorist attack victim; POW/MIA of the Vietnam Conflict (on/after January 1, 1960) or their child/stepchild (born prior to or while parent was POW/MIA); child/stepchild/surviving spouse of a state or local public safety employee who died or was 100% disabled in the line of duty; a public safety employee who was 100% disabled in the line of duty; child/stepchild/surviving spouse of a school employee who died or was 100% disabled due to an act of violence in the line of duty
Must generally be a Maryland resident at time of application (with limited exceptions for certain public safety employee dependents, surviving spouses, and disabled public safety employees)
Must attend an institution of higher learning within Maryland
Total financial assistance cannot exceed cost of attendance
FAFSA not required (merit-based program)
Apply through college financial aid office by July 15
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: New and renewal applicants should contact their institution's financial aid office for application instructions. All required documentation should be submitted directly to the institution. Do not submit applications or documentation to MHEC. Institutions award eligible students and are reimbursed by the state. Renewal awardees do not need to reapply each year; initial awards are automatically renewed by the financial aid office.

structured_extraction.program_name: Employer Student Loan Repayment Assistance Tax Exclusion (CARES Act Extension)
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal tax benefit that allows employers to make tax-free contributions toward their employees' student loan repayment. The CARES Act created this benefit in 2020, and the December 2020 stimulus bill extended it through 2025. Contributions are excluded from the employee's taxable income, up to $5,250 per year per employee, and can be part of any new or existing employer educational assistance program meeting IRS § 127 requirements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Employers can contribute up to $5,250 per year per employee toward student loan repayment as a tax-free benefit. The amount is excluded from the employee's taxable income and can be part of any new or existing employer educational assistance program. The benefit was extended through 2025 under a federal stimulus bill signed December 21, 2020. Applies to undergraduate and graduate student loan debt.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland employers who want to offer student loan repayment assistance as a tax-free employee benefit
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Employee student loan repayment contributions, tax-free up to $5,250 per employee per year
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available nationwide, including Maryland
requirements_list: Employer must have a qualifying educational assistance program under § 127 of the Internal Revenue Code
Payments must be part of an employer educational assistance program meeting IRS § 127 requirements
Benefit capped at $5,250 per employee per year
Applies to undergraduate and graduate student loan debt
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Employers must establish or update an educational assistance program meeting IRS § 127 requirements. See the IRS website for eligibility details.

structured_extraction.program_description: Expanding SUCCESS is a pilot student success initiative that reduces inequities in college completion by providing coaching, financial support, and community resources to community college students. The program uses evidence-based advising models to help students — especially students of color and those from low-income families — complete postsecondary degrees or credentials and improve economic mobility. MHEC and MDRC provide training, support, and data analytics to participating institutions to track student retention and degree completion.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Each participating community college receives $125,000 in funding. MHEC and MDRC also provide training, support, and data analytics to participating colleges to track student retention and degree completion.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Donna Thomas (BCCC); Crystal Smith (PGCC); Paul Fields (Wor-Wic)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community colleges serving students of color and students from low-income families seeking to complete postsecondary degrees or credentials in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Coaching, financial support, community resources, advising services, and data analytics to improve student retention and degree completion rates.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Pilot program limited to three participating institutions: Baltimore City Community College, Prince George's Community College, and Wor-Wic Community College.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland community college
Institutions were selected based on student population composition and MHEC's commitment to serving community colleges statewide
Program eligibility requirements vary by college
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: This is a pilot program with participating institutions already identified and selected by MHEC based on student population and statewide commitment. Contact the relevant college directly for student eligibility requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Next Generation Scholars of Maryland (NGS) Program is a college access program established by the Maryland General Assembly in 2016. It supports low-income, first-generation students in high-poverty school systems by providing a cohort-based model of mentoring, guidance, and college access support. Cohorts are identified as early as 7th grade and receive support through high school graduation and into their first year of college. The program provides comprehensive services including high school graduation planning, summer work/internship opportunities, financial aid literacy assistance, career and interest assessments, mentorship and one-on-one counseling, college campus and workplace visits, intensive summer bridge programs, and support for matriculation and graduation from higher education institutions. FY 2026 grants continue funding to nonprofit organizations that were awarded grants in FY 2025, supporting postsecondary education preparation and college completion for the next generation of scholars.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $5,000,000 in total grant funding is available for FY 2026, with an estimated 11 to 15 grants to be awarded. Grants are continuation awards for nonprofit organizations that were awarded Next Generation Scholars Program grants in FY 2025. Grant period runs July 1, 2025 – June 30, 2026. Funds support guidance, mentoring, and support services to cohort students (grades 7-12) who pre-qualify for the Guaranteed Access Grant in eligible school districts. Allowable uses include salaries, stipends, paid student internships, student transportation, materials and supplies, travel, equipment, contracted services, and other costs approved by MHEC. Funds cannot be used for supplanting existing program funds, capital improvements, purchase of gift cards, or costs incurred prior to grant approval. Indirect costs are capped at 8% of direct costs.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Proposals are due no later than 5 p.m. EDT on July 1, 2025
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations that were awarded Next Generation Scholars Program grants in FY 2025 and that serve grade 7-12 students in eligible high-poverty school districts in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Providing mentoring, college guidance, and support services to cohorts of low-income, first-generation students from grades 7-12 through high school graduation and into their first year of college, including students who pre-qualify for the Guaranteed Access Grant. Allowable costs include: salaries and wages, fringe benefits, stipends, paid student internships, student transportation, materials and supplies, travel, equipment, contracted/consultant services, and other costs approved by MHEC. Indirect costs are capped at 8% of direct costs. Funds cannot be used for supplanting existing program funds, capital improvements, purchase of gift cards, or costs incurred prior to grant approval.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Nonprofits must support students in one or more of the following school systems: Allegany County Public Schools, Baltimore City Public Schools, Caroline County Public Schools, Dorchester County Public Schools, Kent County Public Schools, Prince George's County Public Schools, Somerset County Public Schools, or Wicomico County Public Schools.
requirements_list: Must be a nonprofit 501(c)(3) organization that was awarded a Next Generation Scholars grant in FY 2025
