Submit the completed application by email to Tiffany.Majors1@Maryland.gov by 5:00 p.m. EDT on July 1, 2025. Timeline: applications released June 2, 2025; applications close July 1, 2025; MHEC review July 2–9; notifications July 10–18; grant period July 1, 2025 – June 30, 2026. This funding opportunity is now closed.

structured_extraction.program_description: The GEAR UP Scholarship Award provides financial aid to students who participated in GEAR UP activities in Baltimore City, Dorchester, or Wicomico Counties during the 2014-2020 grant period. Awards are made after federal Pell Grant, state aid, and other public or private aid (excluding loans and work-study) have been applied. Students must file the FAFSA by March 1 each year and complete a GEAR UP Scholarship Application to be considered. Award amounts vary based on financial need and will not exceed the Cost of Attendance (COA).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Maximum GEAR UP Scholarship award is $15,000 for fall and spring of the 2023-2024 academic year and $10,000 for summer 2023. Award amount varies based on the student's financial need but will not exceed the Cost of Attendance (COA). Awards are made after federal Pell Grant, state aid, and other public or private aid (excluding loans and work-study) have been applied.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Undergraduate tuition and educational costs at accredited two- or four-year institutions, private career schools, or state/regional accredited trade schools/certificate programs, up to the Cost of Attendance (COA), applied after other aid sources.

Then complete and submit the GEAR UP Scholarship Application (links provided on the program page for Summer 2023 and Fall 2023/Spring 2024). The program helps students and community partners gain access to postsecondary education preparation resources, supporting college readiness activities through partnerships with public and private institutions of higher education and nonprofit organizations.

structured_extraction.program_name: Governor's Emergency Education Relief (GEER) Fund – Maryland Community College Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal COVID-19 emergency relief grant under the CARES Act that allocated $10 million to Maryland's 16 community colleges to expand workforce development courses and continuing professional education leading to government or industry certification or licensure. The program prioritized individuals who lost employment due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Funds were distributed by the Governor through the Maryland Higher Education Commission, with individual allocations ranging from $250,000 to approximately $1.48 million per institution, covering the period July 1, 2020 to December 30, 2021.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: $10,000,000 in total grant funds distributed to Maryland's 16 community colleges, with individual allocations ranging from $250,000 to approximately $1.48 million per institution. Funds may be used for direct student aid, materials and supplies and equipment, curriculum development, salaries and wages, professional development and technical training, student recruitment and marketing, and technology training or certification/licensure fees or vouchers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland's 16 community colleges, and through them, students and workers impacted by COVID-19 through loss of employment.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Workforce development courses and continuing professional education leading to government or industry certification or licensure; direct aid to students; materials, supplies, and equipment; curriculum development; salaries and wages; professional development and technical training; student recruitment, marketing, and advertising; technology training, certification, examination, and licensure fees or vouchers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — all 16 Maryland community colleges are eligible.
requirements_list: Must be one of Maryland's 16 community colleges
Funds must support workforce development courses or professional education leading to government or industry certification or licensure
Priority focus on individuals impacted by COVID-19 through loss of employment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Awards are administered by the Maryland Higher Education Commission's Office of Grants Management. Funds were allocated directly to the 16 community colleges with no public application process described. Contact Priscilla Moore at priscilla.moore@maryland.gov for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Governor's Emergency Education Relief Fund II (GEER II)
structured_extraction.program_description: The GEER II Fund provided emergency supplemental grants to Maryland community colleges and private nonprofit colleges and universities to help them recover from the financial impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic. Community colleges received funding to offer workforce development and continuing professional education courses leading to government or industry-required certification or licensure, with a focus on workers who lost jobs due to COVID-19. Private nonprofit colleges and universities received funding to cover institutional costs resulting from the pandemic. Funding was provided through the U.S. Department of Education via the Coronavirus Response and Relief Supplemental Appropriations (CRRSA) Act, 2021.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: $10 million in total GEER II grants allocated by Governor Hogan: $7.4 million to 16 community colleges (individual awards ranging from $185,000 to $1,095,645) for workforce development and continuing professional education courses, and $2.6 million to 13 private nonprofit colleges and universities ($200,000 each) to cover institutional costs related to COVID-19. Funded through the U.S. Department of Education via the Coronavirus Response and Relief Supplemental Appropriations (CRRSA) Act, 2021.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland community colleges and private nonprofit colleges and universities affected by COVID-19 seeking emergency relief funding.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Community colleges: workforce development courses and continuing professional education leading to government or industry-required certification or licensure. Private nonprofit colleges and universities: institutional costs resulting from COVID-19.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — available to eligible institutions located across Maryland.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Grants were allocated directly to specific institutions by the Governor; no open application process is described. Grants were awarded to 16 community colleges and 13 private nonprofit colleges and universities.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides need-based financial assistance to degree-seeking graduate and professional students in Maryland who demonstrate financial need. It supports students enrolled in eligible programs such as dentistry, law, medicine, nursing, pharmacy, social work, and veterinary medicine at specific Maryland institutions. Awards do not need to be repaid. Funds may not be available to award all eligible students. Application deadlines are set by each participating institution after the student files the FAFSA.

Students may receive an award for up to eight semesters if they remain enrolled in an eligible program, maintain satisfactory academic progress, file a FAFSA each year, and demonstrate financial need. Funds do not need to be repaid. Funds may not be available to award all eligible students. Application deadline is determined by the institution after filing the FAFSA.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Contact the financial aid office of the school you will attend for their deadlines
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland resident degree-seeking graduate and professional students with financial need enrolled in eligible programs at designated Maryland institutions in dentistry, law, medicine, nursing, pharmacy, social work, or veterinary medicine.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Financial assistance for graduate and professional degree programs, including postsecondary education costs in dentistry, law, medicine, nursing, pharmacy, social work, and veterinary medicine.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be Maryland residents and attend one of the following eligible institutions: University of Maryland Baltimore (UMB) Schools of Medicine, Dentistry, Law, Pharmacy, or Social Work; University of Baltimore School of Law; The Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine; The Virginia-Maryland Regional College of Veterinary Medicine; or certain Maryland institutions offering a master's degree in nursing or social work or a first professional degree in pharmacy.

Then contact the financial aid office at the institution you plan to attend and request consideration for the Graduate and Professional Scholarship. The institution determines eligibility, specific deadlines, and renewal.

structured_extraction.program_name: Howard P. Rawlings Campus-Based Educational Assistance Grant (CBEAG)
structured_extraction.program_description: A need-based, campus-based financial aid grant program designed to assist undergraduate students who were not considered for the Howard P. Rawlings Educational Assistance Grant because they did not file the FAFSA or MHEC One App (Maryland State Financial Aid Application) by the Maryland state priority deadline of March 1. State funds are allocated to participating Maryland colleges and universities, which then select and award eligible students each academic year. Students who file the FAFSA or MSFAA on March 2 or later may be considered for this grant. The grant does not need to be repaid.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Awards range from a minimum of $400 to a maximum of $3,000 per year. Students at four-year institutions receive 40% of their OSFA adjusted financial need; students at community colleges receive 60%. Total state aid cannot exceed cost of attendance or $28,000, whichever is less. Eligible for students who file the FAFSA or MSFAA on March 2 or later. Does not need to be repaid.

Rawlings Educational Assistance Grant. Students must be eligible for the federal Pell Grant.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Financial assistance toward postsecondary education costs, including cost of attendance at a Maryland two-year or four-year college or university.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants and their parents (if dependent) must be Maryland residents. Students must be enrolled full-time (12+ credits per semester) at a two-year or four-year Maryland college or university.

structured_extraction.program_name: Howard P. Rawlings Educational Excellence Awards (EEA) Program – Guaranteed Access (GA) Grant and Educational Assistance (EA) Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's largest need-based financial assistance program for higher education, administered by the Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC). The program includes two grants as part of the Delegate Howard P. Rawlings Educational Excellence Awards: the Guaranteed Access (GA) Grant and the Educational Assistance (EA) Grant. The GA Grant provides grants to low-income Maryland students enrolled full-time at eligible two-year or four-year Maryland postsecondary institutions to help pay for educational expenses, covering up to 100% of a student's calculated adjusted financial need for the first two academic years of enrollment, up to the maximum award amount. The maximum GA Grant award for 2026-2027 is $18,000 (the maximum was $22,100 for 2024-2025); the minimum award is $100 per year. GA Grant recipients must be under age 26 at time of first receiving the grant (born after July 1, 2000 for 2026-2027). The EA Grant provides up to $3,000 per year (minimum $400/year) for up to four years, calculated based on cost of attendance, living situation, and financial need using the OSFA Adjusted Financial Need formula (subtracting the Student Aid Index, certain state awards, and the Federal Pell Grant). As of May 2024, 223 renewal students received a total of $665,700 under the EA Grant. The EA Grant may be used at an out-of-state institution only for deaf or hearing-impaired students if the institution provides special services not available at Maryland institutions. Neither grant needs to be repaid, and both can be renewed for up to 3 additional years. MHEC begins awarding initial EA Grant recipients after all eligible GA Grant applicants have been awarded. Each year the program awards more than $130 million to more than 65,000 students. Students must file the FAFSA or MHEC One-App by March 1 (priority deadline) and submit required documentation by the applicable documentation deadline (e.g., August 1, 2026 for the 2026-2027 cycle; July 15, 2025 for the 2025-2026 GA/EA Grant cycle). MHEC's MDCAPS system automatically considers students who meet basic eligibility requirements. Award notifications are sent to students within 24 hours after they are awarded. All awarding is contingent on availability of funds. Cannot receive both EA and Guaranteed Access Grant simultaneously.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Need-based grants for students attending Maryland postsecondary institutions. The Guaranteed Access (GA) Grant covers up to 100% of a student's calculated adjusted financial need for the first two academic years of enrollment, or up to the maximum award amount, whichever is lower. The maximum GA Grant award for 2026-2027 is $18,000 (the maximum was $22,100 for 2024-2025); the minimum award is $100 per year. The Educational Assistance (EA) Grant provides $400 to $3,000 per year for up to four years total (renewable for up to 3 additional years). Award amounts for both grants are based on cost of attendance, living situation, and calculated financial need using the OSFA Adjusted Financial Need formula (subtracting the Student Aid Index, certain state awards, and the Federal Pell Grant). As of May 2024, 223 renewal students received a total of $665,700 under the EA Grant. Cannot receive both EA and GA Grant simultaneously. Neither grant needs to be repaid. Award notifications are sent to students within 24 hours after they are awarded. MHEC awards on a weekly basis, beginning with GA Grant applicants before awarding initial EA Grant recipients. All awarding is contingent on availability of funds.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: FAFSA or MHEC One-App filed by March 1, 2026 (priority deadline for 2026-2027 cycle); documentation deadline August 1, 2026 (for 2026-2027 cycle); July 15, 2025 for 2025-2026 GA/EA Grant cycle
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income Maryland residents, including high school seniors and full-time undergraduate students, with demonstrated financial need seeking their first undergraduate degree at an eligible Maryland two-year or four-year institution. Includes U.S. citizens, eligible non-citizens, and undocumented students eligible for in-state tuition, as well as returning (renewal) recipients. GA Grant recipients must be under age 26 at time of first receiving the grant (born after July 1, 2000 for 2026-2027). Males must be registered for Selective Service (or provide proof of ineligibility).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational expenses and postsecondary education costs at eligible Maryland two-year or four-year postsecondary institutions, including tuition, fees, room and board, and approved educational expenses. The EA Grant may be used at an out-of-state institution only for deaf or hearing-impaired students if the institution provides special services not available at Maryland institutions, or under Academic Common Market reciprocal agreements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be eligible for in-state tuition in Maryland and must list a Maryland college or university on their FAFSA or MHEC One-App. Available statewide to Maryland residents attending eligible Maryland postsecondary institutions.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: There is no specific separate application for either the GA Grant or the EA Grant. Students must submit a FAFSA (for U.S. citizens and eligible non-citizens) or MHEC One-App (for undocumented students eligible for in-state tuition) by March 1 with a Maryland institution listed. MHEC's MDCAPS system automatically considers students who meet basic eligibility requirements. If additional documentation is required, students must upload it through their MDCAPS account at https://mdcaps.mhec.state.md.us by the applicable documentation deadline (e.g., August 1, 2026 for the 2026-2027 cycle; July 15, 2025 for the 2025-2026 cycle). Documentation may also be submitted at a Document Drop-Off Event, by mail to MHEC's Office of Student Financial Assistance at 6 North Liberty Street, Baltimore, MD 21201, by email to ga.mhec@maryland.gov, or by dropping off at drop boxes at MHEC's buildings. For the GA Grant, awarding begins the first week of April (or May, depending on the cycle) and continues until funds are exhausted, with additional rounds announced during the summer months. For the EA Grant, awarding is anticipated to begin in Summer 2026. MHEC awards on a weekly basis and strongly encourages applicants to create an online account through the MHEC One-App to enable award processing and track notifications. Award notifications are sent to students within 24 hours after they are awarded.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grant funding to Maryland postsecondary institutions and nonprofit organizations to address campus hunger and food insecurity among college students. Supports eligible campuses in developing and funding programs that combat student hunger and improve food security.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding awarded to eligible postsecondary institutions and nonprofit organizations to support campus hunger and food insecurity initiatives.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public and private institutions of higher education and nonprofit organizations in Maryland addressing campus food insecurity.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Campus hunger and food insecurity programs, including initiatives to reduce food insecurity among college students.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application by the October 6, 2025 deadline. See program page for details.

structured_extraction.program_name: Inmate Training and Job Pilot Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A state grant program administered by the Maryland Higher Education Commission that provides funds to eligible institutions of higher education to offer educational and vocational training opportunities for inmates in the 12 months before their release from Maryland correctional institutions. The goal is to expand and improve higher education pathways for incarcerated individuals and support postsecondary education and job training for those who are incarcerated.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State grant funds awarded to eligible institutions of higher education to establish pilot programs providing educational and vocational training for inmates in the 12 months preceding release. Initial implementation grants are up to $25,000 for a six-month implementation period. Continuation grants are available on a pro-rata basis according to enrollment data. The grant period runs August 2025 through June 2026. Indirect costs are capped at 8% of total direct costs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible institutions of higher education in Maryland, specifically Bowie State University, Coppin State University, Morgan State University, and University of Maryland Eastern Shore, for FY 2025 funding.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Establishing pilot programs to provide educational and vocational training opportunities for inmates incarcerated at Maryland correctional institutions in the 12 months before their release. Allowable costs include: personnel compensation, fringe benefits, stipends for mentors, travel expenses, equipment and supplies, consultant and contractual services, and indirect costs (up to 8%). Funds must supplement new and/or existing programs and cannot be used to supplant non-grant funds. Unallowable uses include capital improvements or costs incurred prior to grant approval.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is available to eligible institutions of higher education in Maryland that serve inmates at Maryland correctional institutions, including 14 DPSCS correctional facilities located statewide.

Programs must target inmates in the 12 months preceding their date of release from incarceration

Applications undergo an initial review for formatting and completeness, followed by a review panel evaluation using weighted criteria. A cover sheet and abstract (250-300 words) are required along with a completed budget template (CPIP form/Appendix B) and signed Statement of Assurances (Appendix C) by an authorized official at the President or V.P. level or above. RFP documents and appendices are available on the program page. Contact Anthony Reiner for additional information. This funding opportunity is now closed.

structured_extraction.program_name: Jack F. Tolbert Memorial Student Grant Program

Awards are up to $500 per student and may be renewed once if the student continues to meet enrollment requirements, including remaining enrolled at least 18 clock hours per week and filing the FAFSA. The preferred FAFSA deadline is March 1, with a rolling deadline for the Tolbert Grant application through the institution through June 15. Funds may not be available to award all eligible students.

The preferred FAFSA deadline is March 1; the Tolbert Grant application through the institution has a rolling deadline through June 15. Funds may not be available to award all eligible students.

structured_extraction.program_name: Janet L. Hoffman Loan Assistance Repayment Program (LARP)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides state assistance in repaying educational loans to attract qualified individuals to government and nonprofit employment, particularly in fields with critical staffing shortages and lower salaries than the private sector. The program assists Maryland residents working in public service careers who have outstanding qualifying student loan debt, helping them reduce the burden of student loan obligations incurred while pursuing careers in certain eligible fields.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State assistance in repayment of educational/student loans for Maryland residents employed in government or nonprofit sectors. Applications and required documentation must be submitted by October 1 annually. Specific career eligibility requirements apply.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Janet L. Hoffman application and required documentation due October 1

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Repayment of educational/student loans for public service employees.

Must work in a qualifying career field
Submit Janet L. Hoffman LARP application and required documentation by October 1

structured_extraction.program_name: MHEC One App for Undocumented Students
structured_extraction.program_description: A single online application (MHEC One App) that allows qualified children of undocumented immigrants who are eligible for in-state tuition under §15-106.8 of the MD Education Article to apply for various State financial aid grants and scholarships through the Maryland Higher Education Commission. The application covers up to 27 scholarship and grant programs — including the Educational Assistance Grant, Guaranteed Access Grant, Campus Based Educational Assistance Grant, Part Time Grant, Maryland Community College Promise Scholarship, Near Completer Grant, Cybersecurity Public Service Scholarship Award, Legislative Scholarship Program, and the Richard W. Collins III Leadership with Honor Scholarship — all through a single MDCAPS account, replacing the previous Maryland State Financial Aid Application (MSFAA). Up to $130 million in total financial aid is available statewide. Award amounts vary by program; MHEC notifies applicants of Educational Assistance Grant and Guaranteed Access Grant awards in late April, with other program awards announced in summer. Social Security Number is not required to apply.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible undocumented students who meet the non-resident tuition exemption requirements under §15-106.8 of the MD Education Article and attend an eligible Maryland public or private institution may receive various State financial aid grants and scholarships. Up to $130 million in total financial aid is available through 27 scholarship and grant programs. Award amounts vary by program. Students apply through the Maryland College Aid Processing Portal (MDCAPS). Award notifications for the Educational Assistance Grant and Guaranteed Access Grant are sent in late April; other grant/scholarship awards are announced in the summer. Students must accept awards within 2 weeks via MDCAPS.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Deadlines vary by scholarship or grant program; March 1 is the deadline for the Educational Assistance Grant and Guaranteed Access Grant (the largest need-based programs); other programs have different deadlines. Application opens each year when the FAFSA opens (around October 1 for most award years).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Undocumented students, DACA students, and qualified children of undocumented immigrants who are eligible for in-state tuition under §15-106.8 of the Maryland Education Article and plan to attend an eligible Maryland public or private institution, college, university, or career/trade school in Maryland. Also includes students ineligible for federal financial aid (FAFSA).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition and educational expenses at eligible Maryland public or private institutions, colleges, universities, or career/trade schools. Grants and scholarships help cover the cost of attending an eligible Maryland institution.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must attend an eligible Maryland public or private institution and meet Maryland's non-resident exemption requirements under §15-106.8 of the MD Education Article; available to Maryland students statewide. Students must have Maryland state of legal residence and must have filed Maryland income tax returns for the required prior years.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Log in to or create a MDCAPS account at mdcaps.mhec.state.md.us, then click the MHEC One-App link and follow the prompts to review and apply for available scholarships. Provide dependency status information and, if applicable, parent/spouse income and tax information. Select up to 10 schools and housing plans. Review terms and conditions, then submit the application. If classified as dependent, download and submit the Parent Signature Page (parent must certify and submit). Monitor the 'Check Your Application Status' page in your MDCAPS account for any additional information requests. After submission, MHEC will review the application and notify applicants by email if awarded. Students must accept or decline their award within 2 weeks through their MDCAPS account.

structured_extraction.program_description: A need-based scholarship that financially supports Maryland community college students who transfer to a four-year public or private nonprofit institution in Maryland and complete their bachelor's degree. It provides annual awards to eligible transfer students who have demonstrated financial need, maintain a minimum 2.5 GPA, and have earned or are in the process of earning an associate degree from a Maryland community college. Higher award amounts are available to students pursuing workforce shortage fields such as teaching, STEM, engineering, computer science, mathematics, or nursing. Applicants are ranked by academic merit and financial need due to high demand, and there is a waiting list each year. The scholarship does not need to be repaid.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual scholarship award of up to $2,000 ($1,000 per term) for students in science, teaching, engineering, computer science, mathematics, or nursing programs, or up to $1,000 annually ($500 per term) for students in all other programs. Funds may be used for tuition and mandatory fees at the four-year Maryland institution the student transfers to. The scholarship is renewable for up to 3 years or six terms of study, whichever is longer, subject to availability of funds. Applications and FAFSA are due by December 31, 2025 for the 2025-2026 award year, or October 15, 2026 for the 2026-2027 award year. Required documents are due January 31, 2026 (2025-2026) or November 15, 2026 (2026-2027). Applicants are ranked based on academic merit and financial need; a waiting list exists each year due to high demand. The scholarship does not need to be repaid.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents who are community college students transferring to a four-year public or private nonprofit institution in Maryland, have demonstrated financial need, and have earned or are completing an associate degree from a Maryland community college.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition and mandatory fees at the eligible four-year Maryland institution the student has transferred to.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Maryland resident attending a Maryland community college and transferring to a Maryland public or private nonprofit four-year institution.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the MHEC One-App on MDCAPS (https://mdcaps.mhec.state.md.us) by the applicable deadline (December 31, 2025 for 2025-2026; October 15, 2026 for 2026-2027). Also submit the FAFSA and a community college transcript showing current cumulative GPA by the document deadline (January 31, 2026 for 2025-2026; November 15, 2026 for 2026-2027). Applications are reviewed and conditionally awarded on a rolling basis. After conditional award, students must provide a final community college transcript showing degree conferment date (by March 15, 2026 for 2025-2026; February 15, 2027 for 2026-2027) and proof of Selective Service registration if applicable. Applicants are ranked based on academic merit and financial need; a waiting list exists each year due to high demand.

structured_extraction.program_description: A last-dollar scholarship for eligible Maryland residents enrolling at one of Maryland's 16 community colleges. It covers up to $5,000 per academic year (or actual tuition and mandatory fees after all other federal or state financial aid has been applied, whichever is less) with a minimum award of $100 annually ($50 per semester). Eligible programs include credit-bearing vocational certificate, certificate, or associate degree programs; sequences of courses leading to licensure or certification; and registered apprenticeship programs. Non-credit continuing education programs leading to licensure or certification are also eligible. The scholarship does not need to be repaid.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $5,000 per academic year (or actual tuition and mandatory fees after federal and state aid, whichever is less) to cover remaining tuition and mandatory fees at a Maryland community college after federal and state financial aid has been applied (last-dollar scholarship). Minimum award is $100 annually ($50 per semester). Does not cover books, room, board, or other costs. Does not need to be repaid. Renewal recipients must maintain a 2.5 cumulative community college GPA and make satisfactory academic progress.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: FAFSA or MHEC One App by April 15; Submit all required documentation by April 15 (priority deadline July 15); rolling deadline for Continuing Education applicants as determined annually by MHEC
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland high school graduates or GED recipients eligible for in-state tuition who are enrolling full or part time at one of Maryland's 16 community colleges in a credit-bearing vocational certificate, certificate, or associate degree program; a sequence of courses leading to licensure or certification; or a registered apprenticeship program. Also includes currently or previously enrolled community college students, homeschooled applicants with verified GPA, undocumented students and eligible non-citizens, permanent residents, and T Visa holders. Income limits apply: adjusted gross income up to $100,000 (single or single-parent household) or up to $150,000 (married or two-parent household).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition and mandatory fees at a Maryland community college only. Does not cover books, room, board, or other costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be eligible for in-state tuition at a Maryland community college as determined by the community college per Maryland Education Article Title 15, and must attend the community college located in their county or region of residence, unless the home college does not offer the desired program. Regional community colleges include Wor-Wic Community College, Chesapeake College, and College of Southern Maryland.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the FAFSA at studentaid.gov or the MHEC One App (for students ineligible for FAFSA) by April 15, then contact your local community college to submit required documentation including transcripts, GED scores as applicable, and income documentation. The priority deadline for submitting documentation to the institution is July 15; the final deadline is April 15. Non-credit continuing education applicants must also complete the Promise Non-Credit Application online through the MHEC One App in MDCAPS. Create a Maryland College Aid Processing System (MDCAPS) account at MHEC.Maryland.gov. Documents can also be submitted via mail, drop box at MHEC offices, or at Document Drop-Off Events, and checked via MDCAPS at https://mdcaps.mhec.state.md.us/MDCAPS.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland GEAR UP Workforce Employability and Leadership Skills Program (WELSP)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Workforce Employability and Leadership Skills Program (WELSP) is a federal college access program funded by the U.S. Department of Education under Title IV of the 1998 Amendments to the Higher Education Act of 1965. It provides career exploration and educational planning for economically disadvantaged, low-income, and first-generation students. It offers in-school soft skill and leadership workshops, career exploration counseling, summer programs, workplace readiness training, and youth employment programs. The program trains students to understand their core values, build soft skills, set achievable goals, and develop leadership abilities through career and job exploration. It emphasizes the benefits of postsecondary education and connects youth to professional sectors, while also educating students and their families about postsecondary education and college financing options.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $90,000 per institution (five or more awards anticipated) fund in-school soft skill and leadership workshops, career exploration counseling, summer programs, workplace readiness training, and youth employment programs. Also supports educating students and their families about postsecondary education and college financing options. Requires a 25% matching contribution (cash and/or in-kind). Funds are disbursed in two 50% payments: 50% upon award notification and 50% after interim report approval. Indirect costs cannot exceed 8%. Funds must supplement, not supplant, existing programs. Applicants must be an accredited public or nonprofit two- or four-year institution of higher education partnered with a Local Education Agency (LEA).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Accredited public or nonprofit two- or four-year institutions of higher education partnered with Local Education Agencies (LEAs) in Maryland GEAR UP school districts (Baltimore City, Dorchester, and Wicomico counties) serving economically disadvantaged, low-income, and first-generation students and their families.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: In-school/virtual soft skills and leadership workshops, career and job exploration counseling, summer programs, workplace readiness training, and youth employment activities. Also includes educating students and families about postsecondary education and college financing options. Allowable budget categories include salaries and wages, fringe benefits, travel (in-state; out-of-state conference travel not allowed), equipment, materials and supplies, consultant and contractual services, and other approved project expenses. Funds must supplement, not supplant, existing programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only in Maryland GEAR UP school districts: Baltimore City, Dorchester County, and Wicomico County.
requirements_list: Applicant must be an accredited public or nonprofit independent two- or four-year Institution of Higher Education (IHE)
Must partner with a Local Education Agency (LEA)
Must serve economically disadvantaged students in GEAR UP school districts (Baltimore City, Dorchester, and Wicomico counties)
25% matching contribution required (cash and/or in-kind)
Quarterly time and effort reports required
Interim report due April 15, 2021
Final report due December 3, 2021 (within 90 days of closeout)

Indirect costs cannot exceed 8%
Pre- and post-assessments for evaluation required
Detailed recruitment and retention plans required

Acknowledge Maryland Higher Education Commission support in all publications

Formalized agreements required with LEAs and collaborative partners

Grant recipient records subject to MHEC and Legislative Auditor access/examination
Applicant must have legal authority to apply

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application in response to the Request for Proposals (RFP). Required forms include a Plan of Operation (with narrative and objectives/outcomes table), Budget Summary (in Excel format with detailed personnel, costs, and contributions), and Assurances and Cooperative Planning Agreement signed by required partners (College/University applicant, School District Superintendent, LEA GEAR UP Coordinator, High School Principal, and other partners as applicable). Each partner must summarize their responsibilities and duties. The Plan of Operation requires both narrative and table format for each activity. See the RFP documents linked on the program page for full instructions. Contact Kendall Cook for questions.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Gaining Early Awareness and Readiness for Undergraduate Programs (GEAR UP) Leadership Development Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A six-year federal grant program administered by the Maryland Higher Education Commission that provides grants to accredited Maryland colleges and universities partnering with local school districts (Local Education Agencies) to offer summer enrichment, skill-building, and college-preparation programming for economically disadvantaged secondary school students. The program supports leadership curricula and activities, mentoring, career exploration projects, application workshops, counseling and advising, diversity workshops, and activities to help students and their families learn about postsecondary education and college financing options. The program focuses on building students' skills in goal-setting, financial aid awareness, and postsecondary enrollment, with emphasis on English/Language Arts and mathematics. Funded activities include self-discovery and career exploration, project leadership, innovation sessions, communication workshops, and cross-cultural leadership and diversity workshops.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $45,000 per institution for the grant period of June 15, 2018 through August 15, 2019. Funded activities include application workshops, counseling and advising, mentoring, career exploration, leadership training, diversity workshops, self-discovery, innovation sessions, and cross-cultural leadership workshops. In the 2018 funding cycle, more than $80,000 was distributed in total (e.g., $44,526 to Johns Hopkins University and $43,100 to University of Maryland, College Park).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Accredited Maryland public or nonprofit two-year and four-year institutions of higher education that partner with local education agencies (school districts) to serve economically disadvantaged secondary school students in Baltimore City, Dorchester County, and Wicomico County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Summer enrichment, skill-building, and inclusive programming for secondary GEAR UP students; leadership curricula, mentoring, career exploration projects, application workshops, counseling and advising, diversity workshops, self-discovery and career exploration, project leadership, innovation sessions, communication workshops, cross-cultural leadership and diversity workshops, and activities to educate students and families about postsecondary education and college financing options.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in GEAR UP districts: Baltimore City, Dorchester County, and Wicomico County.
requirements_list: Applicant must be an accredited Maryland public or not-for-profit independent two-year or four-year institution of higher education (IHE).
Institution must partner with a Local Education Agency (LEA) in a GEAR UP district.
Districts include Baltimore City, Dorchester County, and Wicomico County.
Institution must select required funded activities.
Must include a completed and signed Cooperative Agreement by the submission deadline.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download the application at http://www.mhec.maryland.gov/institutions_training/Pages/GEARUP.aspx and submit both electronic and hard copies to Kendall E. Cook at the Maryland Higher Education Commission by May 7, 2018 at 4:00 p.m.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Higher Education Outreach and College Access Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grant funding to support college outreach and access programs that help Maryland students and residents prepare for and access postsecondary education. Grants are awarded to community partners, nonprofits, and educational institutions to support college outreach and access initiatives.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants to community partners, public and private institutions of higher education, and nonprofit organizations to support college outreach and access programs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community partners including public and private institutions of higher education and nonprofit organizations supporting college access for Maryland students and residents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: College outreach and access activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application by the October 6, 2025 deadline. See program page for details.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland John R. Justice Grant Student Loan Repayment Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A federally funded program that provides student loan repayment assistance to Maryland state and federal public defenders and prosecutors. Recipients must agree to remain employed as a public defender or prosecutor for at least three years as a condition of receiving the grant. If a recipient fails to fulfill the three-year service commitment, they must repay the full grant award.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Direct payments toward qualified education loans (Federal Stafford loans, Graduate PLUS loans, consolidation loans, and Perkins loans) made to loan servicers on behalf of eligible applicants. Maximum $10,000 per calendar year; maximum aggregate total of $60,000. Annual allocation distributed equally between appellate court districts. Award amounts determined by loan debt-to-AGI ratio and cost of living factor. Recipients must sign a three-year service obligation agreement to remain employed as a public defender or prosecutor; failure to complete the three-year obligation requires full repayment of the grant award. Repayment benefits are taxable income.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland state and federal public defenders and prosecutors who are licensed attorneys in Maryland with outstanding qualifying student loan balances. Note: the 2021-2022 cycle was specific to public defenders only.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Repayment of qualified education loans (Federal Stafford loans, Graduate PLUS loans, consolidation loans, and Perkins loans). Payments are made directly to loan servicers/holders on behalf of the beneficiary.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be employed in Maryland as full-time public defenders or prosecutors at the state, local, tribal, nonprofit contractor, or federal defender level. Funds are allocated equally among appellate court districts based on the applicant's county of employment; cost of living factor based on county of residence is also used in selection.
requirements_list: Must be a U.S. Citizen or eligible non-citizen
Must have an outstanding balance on a qualified education loan (Federal Stafford, Graduate PLUS, consolidation, or Perkins loans)
Must be an attorney continually licensed to practice law in Maryland
Must be a full-time employee working as a prosecutor or public defender at the state, local, tribal, nonprofit contractor, or federal level in Maryland

Must be a full-time employee who prosecutes criminal or juvenile delinquency cases for the state or local government, OR provides legal representation to indigent persons in criminal or juvenile delinquency cases for the state or local government, OR works for a nonprofit under contract with the state or local government providing legal representation to indigent persons, OR is employed as a full-time federal defender attorney
Must sign a three-year service obligation agreement to remain employed as a public defender or prosecutor
Must not be in default on a federal guaranteed educational loan or owe a refund on any scholarship or grant program administered by MHEC's Office of Student Financial Assistance
Must be a state or federal public defender or prosecutor in Maryland
Must maintain regular personal loan payments during the grant period
Must notify state agency of job transfers, voluntary separation, or loan default
Social Security Number required
Repayment benefits are considered taxable income
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and submit the application form (available as a PDF or Word document on the program page) to the Maryland Higher Education Commission. Applicants must sign a service obligation agreement. Applications for the 2021-2022 cycle were due Friday, April 15, 2022.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Loan Assistance Repayment Program for Foster Care Recipients (MLARP Foster Care)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides state assistance in repaying educational loans owed by foster care recipients who are employed by the state of Maryland or a county or municipality of Maryland, and who earned a graduate or undergraduate degree from a Maryland institution of higher education. Applicants must submit the MLARP application and required documentation by December 1.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State assistance in repayment of educational loans for eligible foster care recipients employed by the state of Maryland or a county or municipality. Applicants must submit the MLARP application and required documentation by December 1.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: MLARP Application and required documentation due December 1
structured_extraction.program_audience: Foster care recipients employed by the state of Maryland or a county or municipality of the state, who earned a graduate or undergraduate degree from a Maryland institution of higher education and have outstanding educational loan debt.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Repayment of educational loans incurred while earning a graduate or undergraduate degree from a Maryland institution of higher education.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Must be employed by Maryland state, county, or municipal government; degree must be from a Maryland institution of higher education.
requirements_list: Must be a foster care recipient
Must be employed by the state of Maryland or a county or municipality of the state
Must have earned a graduate or undergraduate degree from a Maryland institution of higher education
Submit MLARP application and required documentation by December 1
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the MLARP application and required documentation by December 1.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Loan Assistance Repayment Program for Police Officers and Probation Agents
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides state assistance to help repay educational loans for individuals who work as police officers or probation/parole agents serving Maryland. Recipients receive a payment toward their student loan debt based on their annual salary and total loan balance. Awards are calculated as a percentage of the applicant's total student loan debt based on annual salary, and recipients may renew for up to three years.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Awards are calculated as a percentage of the applicant's total student loan debt, based on annual salary. Debt under $15,000 receives 10% of the debt paid; $15,000–$40,000 receives 20%; $40,000–$75,000 receives 30%; over $75,000 receives 40%. For example, a salary of $64,000 with debt between $15K–$40K yields an award of $12,800 (salary × 20%). Award cannot exceed total debt. Recipients may renew for up to three years.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: March 15, 2026 for the 2025-2026 application; October 15, 2026 for the 2026-2027 application
structured_extraction.program_audience: Police officers and probation/parole agents employed at eligible Maryland law enforcement agencies who have a graduate, professional, or undergraduate degree in criminal law, criminology, or criminal justice from a public Maryland college or university and have been employed for at least 2 years. Also includes fire and explosive investigators at eligible agencies.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Repayment of student educational loans used for undergraduate or graduate/professional degrees in criminal law, criminology, or criminal justice.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be employed as a police officer, probation agent, or fire and explosive investigator at an eligible law enforcement or parole and probation agency in Maryland. The degree must be from a public college or university in the state of Maryland.
requirements_list: Must hold a graduate, professional, or undergraduate degree in criminal law, criminology, or criminal justice from a public college or university in Maryland
Must be employed as a police officer, probation agent, or fire and explosive investigator at an eligible Maryland law enforcement agency for at least 2 years
Must be employed at an eligible law enforcement or parole and probation agency in Maryland
Annual gross salary cannot exceed $85,000; if married, individual salary cannot exceed $85,000 and combined salaries cannot exceed $170,000
Must submit a signed Maryland income tax return
Must submit an employment verification form
Must submit a lender verification form documenting loan debt
Must submit documentation of degree completion
Must remain employed at an eligible agency throughout the application cycle
Renewal recipients must submit annual employment, lender, and tax documentation by the established deadline each year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the online application through the MHEC One App in MDCAPS at https://mdcaps.mhec.state.md.us. All required documents must be uploaded and submitted through the applicant's MDCAPS account by the closing date. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Police Officer and Probation Agent Scholarship Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This scholarship supports current police officers, probation agents, and individuals planning to enter law enforcement who are enrolled in an academic program that furthers their career in law enforcement at a Maryland public senior institution. Recipients must commit to working as a police officer or probation agent in Maryland after completing their studies. The scholarship is administered by the Maryland Higher Education Commission and is available statewide to eligible Maryland residents or Maryland high school graduates attending a Maryland public senior institution.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual scholarship award equal to 50% of the equivalent annual tuition and mandatory fees charged to a resident undergraduate student at the eligible Maryland public senior institution where the recipient is enrolled. The award converts to a loan if the service obligation is not met. Recipients must sign a promissory note and service obligation agreement committing to work as a police officer or probation agent in Maryland for at least five years within the eight-year period after graduation.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: 2025-2026 academic year application closed April 1, 2026; 2026-2027 academic year application opens January 15, 2026 and closes October 15, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Current police officers or probation agents, and individuals planning to become a police officer or probation agent, who are Maryland residents or Maryland high school graduates enrolled full- or part-time in an undergraduate or graduate program at a Maryland public senior institution in a course of study that furthers their career in law enforcement.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition and mandatory fees at a Maryland public senior institution for undergraduate or graduate study in a program that furthers a career in law enforcement.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicant must be a Maryland resident or have graduated from a Maryland high school. Must be enrolled at a Maryland public senior institution. Recipients must pledge to work as a police officer or probation agent in Maryland upon completion of their studies.
requirements_list: Must be a current police officer, probation agent, or individual planning to become one after graduation
Must be accepted for admission or currently enrolled in an undergraduate or graduate program at a Maryland public senior institution
Must be a Maryland resident or have graduated from a Maryland high school
Must be enrolled full-time or part-time in a course of study that furthers a career in law enforcement
Current police officers must be authorized to enforce general criminal laws of the state and be a member of one of the specified law enforcement agencies
Probation agents must be serving as a parole and probation agent, supervisor, or regional administrator for the Maryland Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services

Must submit a copy of your final high school transcript if you graduated from a Maryland high school but are not a Maryland resident
Must submit documentation from the institution confirming enrollment in a program that furthers a law enforcement career
Pledge to work as a police officer in Maryland after completing studies
Must maintain a 3.0 GPA for renewal
Must maintain satisfactory academic progress
Must remain drug-free
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online through the Maryland College Aid Processing System (MDCAPS) using the MHEC One App by the applicable deadline. Submit any required supporting documentation, including proof of current employment as a police officer (if applicable), a copy of your final high school transcript (if you graduated from a Maryland high school but are not a Maryland resident), and institutional confirmation of enrollment in a qualifying law enforcement program.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Tuition Waiver for Homeless Youth
structured_extraction.program_description: This program waives tuition and mandatory fees at Maryland public colleges and universities for homeless youth enrolled in an associate degree, bachelor's degree, or vocational certificate program. Eligibility is based on the federal McKinney-Vento Homeless Assistance Act definition of homelessness, and applicants must have been verified as homeless at any time during the 24 months immediately preceding enrollment or while enrolled. Applicants must file the FAFSA or MHEC One-App each year and apply through their college financial aid office. Undocumented applicants who cannot complete the MHEC One App should consult the institution's financial aid office directly. The waiver lasts until ten years after first enrolling as a candidate for a degree or vocational certificate, or until a bachelor's degree is awarded, whichever comes first. Scholarships or grants received may not be applied to tuition covered by this waiver. The waiver does not cover room, board, books, or transportation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Full waiver of tuition and mandatory fees (including registration fees, fees for credit-bearing and noncredit courses required as a condition of enrollment, and other required enrollment fees) at any Maryland public institution of higher education. The waiver lasts until ten years after first enrolling as a candidate for a degree or vocational certificate, or until a bachelor's degree is awarded, whichever comes first. Scholarships or grants the student receives may not be applied to tuition covered by this waiver. The waiver does not cover room, board, books, or transportation.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Contact your financial aid office to apply
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeless youth, as defined by the McKinney-Vento Homeless Assistance Act, who are enrolled or plan to enroll in a Maryland public institution of higher education, have been verified as homeless at any point during the 24 months prior to or during their enrollment, and who enroll on or before reaching age 25.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition and mandatory enrollment fees (including registration fees and other required enrollment fees) at Maryland public colleges and universities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must have had a consistent presence in Maryland for at least one year before enrolling at a public institution of higher education, documented by school, employment, or other records. Available at any Maryland public institution of higher education.
requirements_list: Must have had a consistent presence in Maryland for at least one year before enrollment, documented by school, employment, or other records
Must have been verified as a homeless child or youth under the federal McKinney-Vento Homeless Assistance Act at any time during the 24 months immediately preceding enrollment or while enrolled
Must complete and file the FAFSA or MHEC One-App (MSFAA) each year
Must enroll on or before reaching age 25

Must be enrolled full time or part time as a candidate for an associate degree, bachelor's degree, or vocational certificate (credit-bearing or non-credit-bearing) at a Maryland public institution of higher education
Eligibility is verified by the Maryland Department of Human Services
Undocumented applicants who cannot complete the MHEC One App should consult the institution's financial aid office directly
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the financial aid office at the Maryland public college or university you attend or plan to attend to apply for the waiver. Complete the FAFSA at https://studentaid.gov or the MSFAA via the MHEC One App each year to maintain eligibility. Eligibility information is provided to Maryland public colleges and universities by the Maryland Department of Human Services. Undocumented applicants who cannot complete the MHEC One App should consult the institution's financial aid office directly.

structured_extraction.program_description: The federal Montgomery GI Bill provides monthly educational benefits to help pay for education and training for veterans, reservists, and active duty military personnel. Additional benefits are available under the Survivors' and Dependents' Educational Assistance Program and the Post-Vietnam Era Veterans' Educational Assistance Program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Monthly educational benefits provided to eligible veterans, reservists, and active duty personnel to cover education and training costs. Additional benefits available under the Survivors' and Dependents' Educational Assistance Program and the Post-Vietnam Era Veterans' Educational Assistance Program.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Education and training expenses, including higher education costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available nationwide, including Maryland. VA Regional Office located at 31 Hopkins Plaza, Baltimore, MD 21201.
