structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 1-888-442-4551 or contact the VA Regional Office at 31 Hopkins Plaza, Baltimore, MD 21201.

structured_extraction.program_name: Naval ROTC Navy-Marine Corps Scholarship Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Naval Reserve Officer Training Corps (ROTC) Navy-Marine Corps Scholarship Program covers tuition, laboratory fees, books, and fees for eligible high school graduates who commit to active and reserve military service after graduation. Recipients receive $150 monthly compensation and may attend a participating college of their choice, with a four-year active duty service obligation followed by four years of reserve duty.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Covers tuition, laboratory fees, books, and fees, plus $150 monthly compensation. Requires a four-year active duty service obligation followed by four years of reserve duty. Recipients may attend a participating college of their choice.
structured_extraction.program_audience: High school graduates who are U.S. citizens, at least age 17 when enrolled, and not over age 27 when graduated and commissioned.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: College tuition, laboratory fees, books, and fees.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at participating colleges nationwide.
requirements_list: Must be a high school graduate
Must be a U.S. citizen
Must be at least age 17 when enrolled
Must not be over age 27 when graduated and commissioned
Awards based on SAT or ACT scores, high school academic review, interview, physical aptitude exam, and other processing requirements
Four-year active duty service obligation plus four-year reserve duty required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call (703)696-4581 or write to Commander, Navy Recruiting Command (CODE 314), 801 N. Randolph Street, Arlington, VA 22203.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state grant program administered by the Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC) that provides financial assistance to Maryland residents who previously enrolled in a degree program but did not complete it, and now plan to re-enroll to earn their associate or bachelor's degree at a Maryland community college or public four-year institution. The program was created by House Bill 16 signed by Governor Larry Hogan following the 2018 legislative session and went into effect for the fall 2019 semester. Awards are applied toward tuition only, after all non-loan aid has been applied, and are granted on a first-come, first-served basis. The 2023-2024 academic year was the last year of awarding.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Award is applied toward tuition only, after all non-loan aid has been applied. Near completers re-enrolling at a community college are eligible for up to one-third of the in-county tuition charge. Near completers re-enrolling at a public four-year institution are eligible for up to one-third of the in-state undergraduate tuition charge. Awards are granted on a first-come, first-served basis.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: The 2023-2024 application is now closed. 2023-2024 is the LAST year of awarding for the Near Completer Grant.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents who previously attended a community college or senior higher education institution, earned significant credits toward a degree but did not complete it, are not currently enrolled at a post-secondary institution, and plan to re-enroll to complete their associate's or bachelor's degree. Community college track requires at least 45 credit hours earned; four-year institution track requires at least 90 credit hours earned toward a bachelor's degree.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition only at Maryland community colleges or public four-year institutions of higher education.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Maryland resident eligible for in-state tuition.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident eligible for in-state tuition
Must have started but not yet completed a college degree
Must not currently be enrolled at a post-secondary institution
For community college re-enrollment: must have previously earned at least 45 credit hours with a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.0
For four-year institution re-enrollment: must have previously earned at least 90 credit hours toward a bachelor's degree with a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.0
Must submit transcripts from previous institution showing required credit hours
FAFSA or MSFAA is not required but encouraged to be completed by March 1
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Log into the Maryland College Aid Processing System (MDCAPS) to complete the online application. After completing the application, use the Electronic File Upload Tool to submit required transcripts from the previous institution. FAFSA or MSFAA is not required but encouraged to be completed by March 1.

structured_extraction.program_name: New Nursing Faculty Fellowship (NNFF) — Nurse Support Program II (NSP II)
structured_extraction.program_description: The New Nursing Faculty Fellowship is an annual program that recruits, retains, and supports the development of new nursing faculty at Maryland colleges, universities, and community colleges. New recipients receive $20,000 disbursed over three years ($10,000 in year one and $5,000 each in years two and three), while returning recipients in their second and third year receive $5,000 per year, contingent on continued full-time employment in good standing. Previously awarded faculty receiving ongoing disbursements also receive annual payments based on continued full-time employment in good standing. Nominations are submitted by Deans and Directors of Nursing Programs at eligible Maryland institutions each August. Priority consideration is given to faculty from underrepresented groups including racial and ethnic minorities and men. Nominees with doctorates are preferred to teach and conduct nursing research.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: New recipients receive $20,000 total over three years: $10,000 in year one and $5,000 each in years two and three, contingent on continued full-time employment in good standing. Returning recipients (in their second or third year) receive $5,000 per year. Previously awarded faculty receiving ongoing disbursements also receive annual payments based on continued full-time employment in good standing. Nominations are submitted by Deans and Directors of Nursing Programs at eligible Maryland institutions each August.
structured_extraction.program_audience: New and existing nursing faculty at Maryland universities and community colleges, nominated by their institution's Dean or Director of Nursing Programs. Priority is given to faculty from underrepresented groups including racial and ethnic minorities and men. Nominees with doctorates are preferred to teach and conduct nursing research.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Fellowship awards to support nursing faculty recruitment, retention, and professional development to encourage and sustain new and existing faculty in Maryland nursing education programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be employed full-time at a Maryland nursing program (university or community college).
requirements_list: Must be a newly nominated nursing faculty member at an eligible Maryland nursing program
Must be nominated by the Dean or Director of a Maryland nursing program
Must be a nurse faculty member at a Maryland college or university
Must be employed full-time at a Maryland nursing program
Must maintain continued full-time employment in good standing to receive ongoing annual disbursements
Ongoing awards require continued full-time employment in good standing
Recipients are evaluated at the 3-year and 5-year marks of employment
Nominations are due every August
Nominees with doctorates preferred to teach and conduct nursing research
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Deans and Directors of Nursing Programs at participating Maryland institutions submit nomination requests each August. MHEC and NSP II review nominations and make awards annually to eligible nominees across Maryland universities and community colleges. Nominees selected by NSP II receive the fellowship award. MHEC administers the awards with funding approved by the Maryland Health Services Cost Review Commission (HSCRC).

structured_extraction.program_name: Nurse Educator Doctoral Grants for Practice and Dissertation Research (NEDG)
structured_extraction.program_description: Annual grants awarded to Maryland nursing faculty members who are pursuing a doctoral degree to help them complete their terminal degrees and reduce existing student loan debt. The program aims to increase the number of doctorate-prepared nurse educators in Maryland, retain qualified nursing faculty at Maryland institutions, and address the projected nursing shortage by improving nursing education across the state. Awards range from $5,000 to $60,000 per recipient. The program has been in place since 2012. In FY2021, $1,470,000 was awarded to 36 nursing faculty members across 12 nursing programs; in FY2019, $470,000 was awarded to 16 nursing faculty members across eight nursing programs; and in FY2023, seven nursing faculty at five Maryland programs shared $293,914 in awards. The program is funded by the Maryland Health Services Cost Review Commission (HSCRC) and administered by the Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Individual grants ranging from $5,000 to $60,000 awarded to nursing faculty to expedite completion of a terminal (doctoral) degree and reduce existing student loan debt. Awards are nominated by Deans and Directors of Nursing Programs at Maryland universities and community colleges. In FY2021, $1,470,000 was awarded to 36 nursing faculty members across 12 nursing programs; in FY2019, $470,000 was awarded to 16 nursing faculty members across eight nursing programs; and in FY2023, seven nursing faculty at five Maryland programs shared $293,914 in awards. Nominations are due each September and awards are made annually.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Full-time nursing faculty employed at Maryland nursing programs who are pursuing a doctoral degree, nominated by the Dean or Director of their nursing program at Maryland universities and community colleges.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Expediting completion of a terminal (doctoral) degree and reducing existing student loan debt for nurse educators.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide; recipients must be employed at a nursing program in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a nursing faculty member employed at a Maryland nursing program
Must be pursuing a terminal (doctoral) degree
Must be nominated by the Dean or Director of their nursing program
Nominations are submitted annually in September
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Deans and Directors of Nursing Programs at Maryland universities and community colleges nominate eligible nursing faculty each September as part of an annual cycle. MHEC reviews nominations and approves awards. The program is funded by the Maryland Health Services Cost Review Commission (HSCRC) and administered by MHEC.

structured_extraction.program_name: Nurse Support Program II (NSP II) Competitive Institutional Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: The Nurse Support Program II (NSP II) is a broader ongoing program funded by the Maryland Health Services Cost Review Commission (HSCRC) and administered by the Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC). It expands the capacity to educate nurses by supporting nursing education programs at Maryland higher education institutions. The program funds competitive institutional grants and statewide initiatives aimed at producing more nurse faculty and undergraduate and graduate nurses. Statewide initiatives include New Nurse Faculty Fellowships (NNFF), Nurse Educator Doctoral Grants for Practice and Dissertation Research (NEDG), the Hal and Jo Cohen Graduate Nursing Faculty Scholarship (GNF), and Academic Nurse Educator Certification (ANEC). Competitive institutional grants support capacity-building through shared resources and innovative educational designs, including one-year resource/planning grants, multi-year implementation grants, and continuation grants. The program addresses the nursing shortage in Maryland and increases the number of qualified nurses and nurse educators. Funding is provided at up to $90 million over five years ($18 million per year beginning FY2021), funded at 0.1% of pooled hospital gross patient revenue. The FY 2020 cycle awarded nearly $6.2 million for 17 competitive institutional grant proposals, the FY 2023 cycle awarded $4,101,847 across 13 proposals at 12 institutions, and the FY24 cycle awarded $5.8 million to nine Maryland nursing programs. Grants support innovative projects such as expanding enrollment, creating new nursing programs, developing certificate programs, supporting nursing faculty education, and building nurse-managed health centers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $90 million over five years (approximately $18 million per year beginning FY2021), funded by 0.1% of pooled hospital gross patient revenue through the Maryland Health Services Cost Review Commission (HSCRC). Assistance is delivered through two tracks: (1) Competitive Institutional Grants to increase structural capacity of Maryland nursing schools through shared resources and innovative educational designs — grant types include one-year resource/planning grants, three-year full implementation grants, continuation grants, and nursing resource grants; nearly $6.2 million was awarded for 17 competitive institutional grant proposals in FY 2020, the FY 2023 cycle awarded $4,101,847 across 13 proposals at 12 institutions, and the FY24 cycle awarded $5.8 million to nine Maryland nursing programs; and (2) Statewide Initiatives including the New Nurse Faculty Fellowships (NNFF, up to $20,000 over three years), Nurse Educator Doctoral Grants for Practice and Dissertation Research (NEDG), the Hal and Jo Cohen Graduate Nursing Faculty Scholarship (GNF, up to $13,000/year tuition and $25,000/year living expenses), and the Academic Nurse Educator Certification (ANEC). Funds support tuition, research, course release time, faculty recruitment and retention, clinical simulation, leadership development, doctoral education support, nurse educator training, nursing workforce data infrastructure, scholarships and stipends for students, tutoring, mentoring, testing, remediation, support services, lab equipment, clinical sites, classroom and laboratory facilities, and other capacity-building initiatives across Maryland. Supports ADN, RN-BSN, BSN, and MSN programs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland higher education institutions with nursing programs (including HBCUs and community colleges), nursing schools, nursing faculty, hospital-based nurses, and nursing educators seeking to expand academic capacity, increase nursing workforce development, and address the state nursing shortage. Also includes consortia of Maryland higher education institutions and Maryland hospitals, nursing students, and individuals pursuing graduate nursing degrees to become nursing faculty.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Expanding nursing education capacity, increasing nursing program enrollment, developing new cohorts or degree programs, supporting nurse faculty, developing new nursing degree programs, funding simulation resources, improving nursing workforce data infrastructure, faculty development, doctoral education support, nurse educator training, graduate degree tuition support, doctoral degree completion support, nurse educator certification, faculty leadership development, course release time for faculty, faculty recruitment and retention, clinical simulation, establishing new nursing programs, developing certificate programs (e.g., Real-World Data & Pragmatic Research, Nurse Educator Certificate), building nurse-managed health centers, supporting clinical training, preparing students for licensure examinations, innovative approaches to address nursing workforce challenges, scholarships and stipends for students, tutoring and mentoring programs, pre-admission courses and testing, curriculum redesign, off-hours scheduling (weekends/evenings), online training, ESOL training for diverse students, lab equipment and supplies, academic advisors and support staff, clinical site coordinators, and student health insurance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland to nursing education programs at Maryland institutions of higher education; 15 community colleges and 13 universities across all geographic regions of Maryland are encouraged to participate.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland institution of higher education with a nursing education program
Must submit a competitive institutional grant proposal
Competitive Institutional Grant applicants must demonstrate plans to increase structural capacity through shared resources or innovative educational designs
Proposals evaluated on ability to impact the nursing shortage, depth and breadth of initiative, and budget feasibility
Statewide initiative applicants must meet specific program criteria (e.g., newly hired faculty for NNFF, doctoral research for NEDG)
Programs must support goals such as increasing baccalaureate and doctoral-prepared nurses and qualified nurse faculty
Must support national and state nursing workforce initiatives
Proposals are reviewed and recommended for funding by MHEC and approved by the Health Services Cost Review Commission (HSCRC)
Must be a Maryland nursing program, nursing faculty member, or hospital-based nurse
Community colleges and universities across all geographic regions of Maryland are eligible to participate
Applications considered through MHEC's Nurse Support Program II competitive application process
Proposals must be reviewed and approved by a review panel (eight or nine members depending on cycle) and the Health Services Cost Review Commission (HSCRC)
Proposal must demonstrate ability to impact the nursing shortage in a timely manner
Budget must be feasible
Must demonstrate innovative approaches to nursing education or workforce development
Institutions must provide detailed plans itemizing resources required to produce specified number of additional graduates
Compliance with Maryland Board of Nursing faculty requirements (graduate degree in nursing)
Eligible nursing programs include ADN, RN-BSN, and BSN programs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Institutions submit competitive institutional grant proposals that are reviewed by a review panel (eight or nine members depending on cycle). Recommended proposals are approved for funding by the Maryland Health Services Cost Review Commission (HSCRC). For statewide initiative programs, applicants must meet specific program criteria. Visit nursesupport.org or contact MHEC or the NSP II Program Director for details on specific grant programs and how to apply.

structured_extraction.program_name: Nurse Support Program II Academic Nurse Educator Certification (ANEC) Award
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides $5,000 financial awards to full-time nursing faculty at Maryland higher education institutions who complete or renew their Certified Nurse Educator (CNE) credential from the National League for Nursing. The program aims to increase the number of CNE-credentialed faculty and address potential nursing workforce shortages. Funds support professional development and continuing education activities that enhance faculty careers, including CNE examination fees, continuing education, professional certifications and licensing, and professional organization dues. Nominations are submitted by deans and directors of nursing at Maryland higher education institutions. In one recent award round, 34 faculty members at 15 institutions received awards totaling $170,000.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Each qualifying nurse faculty member receives a $5,000 award (one-time per award cycle) upon completing or renewing their Certified Nurse Educator (CNE) credential from the National League for Nursing. Awards are funded through the Nurse Support Program II. Funds may be used for a wide variety of professional development activities including CNE examination fees, continuing education requirements to maintain the credential, professional certifications and licensing, and dues for professional organizations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Full-time nursing faculty at Maryland community colleges and colleges/universities who have completed or renewed the National League for Nursing's Certified Nurse Educator (CNE) credential and are nominated by their dean or director of nursing.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Professional development and continuing education activities required to obtain or maintain the Certified Nurse Educator (CNE) credential, including CNE examination fees, continuing education, professional certifications and licensing, and dues for professional organizations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to nursing faculty at higher education institutions across Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be full-time nurse faculty at a Maryland higher education institution
Must have completed or renewed the National League for Nursing's Certified Nurse Educator (CNE) credential during the eligible academic year period
Must be nominated by the dean or director of nursing at their institution
Must demonstrate excellence as an academic nurse educator
Must achieve and maintain the National League for Nursing Certified Nurse Educator (CNE) credential
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Faculty are nominated by deans and directors of nursing programs at Maryland higher education institutions. Nominations are due by March 15 for the next award cycle. Recipients are selected based on demonstrated excellence in academic nursing education and achievement of the CNE credential. For more information, visit the Nurse Support Program II website.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Part-Time Grant Program provides need-based grant funds to Maryland public and independent colleges and universities based on the number of undergraduate part-time students with demonstrated financial need who are enrolled in degree-granting programs. Institutions select and award recipients. The program also supports students dually enrolled in a Maryland high school and a higher education institution. Grants do not need to be repaid. Award availability depends on available funds.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Need-based grants awarded by the institution range from a minimum of $200 to a maximum of $2,000 per year. Funds are distributed to Maryland colleges and universities, which then award eligible students. Recipients may receive the grant for up to eight years total, provided they maintain satisfactory academic progress and continue to demonstrate financial need. Requires FAFSA or MHEC One App by March 1 (suggested for renewal) or June 1 for initial application. Grants do not need to be repaid. Award availability depends on available funds.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: FAFSA or MHEC One App suggested by March 1 (renewal) or June 1 (initial); contact institution for additional deadlines
structured_extraction.program_audience: Part-time, degree-seeking undergraduate students and students dually enrolled in a Maryland high school and a higher education institution who demonstrate financial need and are Maryland residents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Financial assistance for postsecondary education expenses for part-time undergraduate degree-seeking students enrolled in degree-granting programs at Maryland two-year or four-year colleges or universities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicant and parents (if dependent) must be Maryland residents. Students must enroll at a two-year or four-year Maryland college or university.
requirements_list: Applicant and parents (if dependent) must be Maryland residents

Must be enrolled part-time (3–11 credits per semester) as a degree-seeking undergraduate at a Maryland two-year or four-year college or university, or dually enrolled in a Maryland high school and a higher education institution
Must demonstrate financial need as determined by the FAFSA or MHEC One App (Maryland State Financial Aid Application)
Must complete and file the FAFSA or MHEC One App by June 1 for initial application; March 1 suggested for renewal
For renewal: must maintain satisfactory academic progress and file FAFSA/MHEC One App each year by March 1
Award may be received for a maximum of eight years total
Eligibility determined by institution
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and file the FAFSA or the MHEC One App (available through MDCAPS for students ineligible for federal aid but eligible for in-state tuition) by March 1 (suggested for renewal) or June 1 (initial application). Then contact the financial aid office at your institution to apply and check for additional deadlines, as the institution selects and awards recipients.

structured_extraction.program_description: Scholarships for part-time undergraduate and graduate students in Maryland pursuing higher education degrees. Allows waiver of semester hour requirements for applicants with documented disabilities. A 2023 law change removed the full-time (12 credit hour) enrollment requirement for students with a documented disability, allowing them to submit a proof of disability waiver and receive a scholarship while attending school part-time at a pace that fits their needs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Scholarship awards for eligible Maryland part-time students. Part-time senatorial scholarships are available for up to 8 academic years (minimum 6 semester hours per semester). Part-time delegate scholarships are available for up to twice as many years as full-time equivalents. Up to one-half of the yearly award may be used for summer school. Recipients must maintain in-state tuition eligibility and enrollment status. Students with documented disabilities may request a waiver of semester hour requirements.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Part-time undergraduate and graduate students in Maryland, particularly students with documented disabilities who are enrolled part-time and working toward a degree at an accredited institution of higher education.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition and educational expenses at accredited institutions for students pursuing degree attainment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Applicants must be eligible for in-state tuition or be domiciled in Maryland (for active duty military) and enrolled in a Maryland institution of higher education.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland student pursuing a degree at an accredited institution of higher education
Must be enrolled part-time (minimum 6 semester hours per semester for both undergraduate and graduate students)
Must maintain in-state tuition eligibility and continued enrollment at institution
Students with documented disabilities may request a waiver of semester hour requirements from the Maryland Higher Education Commission
Previously required full-time enrollment (12 credit hours); students with disabilities are now exempt from this requirement following a 2023 law change (effective July 1, 2024)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Students with documented disabilities may request a waiver of semester hour requirements from the Maryland Higher Education Commission along with their scholarship application to be considered under the part-time enrollment exemption. Specific additional application steps beyond the waiver submission are not detailed on the program page.

structured_extraction.program_name: Richard W. Collins III Leadership with Honor Scholarship Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A scholarship program that promotes diversity in ROTC (Reserve Officer Training Corps) programs and in the student bodies at Maryland's Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs). It provides financial awards to minority students and members of groups historically underrepresented in ROTC programs who are Maryland residents enrolled at one of four eligible HBCUs — Bowie State University, Coppin State University, Morgan State University, or University of Maryland Eastern Shore — and are members of a ROTC program. The program is open to current or prospective full-time or part-time undergraduate and graduate students, including undocumented students eligible for in-state tuition.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual scholarship award of at least $500 per semester ($1,000 per academic year), up to the recipient's total education expenses. The exact amount is determined by MHEC and may be adjusted if total financial assistance received exceeds cost of attendance. Students with financial need are prioritized. Recipients may renew for up to three additional years if they continue to meet eligibility and enrollment requirements and maintain satisfactory academic progress.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: October 15, 2026 (online application); April 1, 2026 (2025-2026 application closing date)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Current or prospective undergraduate and graduate students (full-time or part-time), including undocumented students eligible for in-state tuition, who are minority students or members of groups historically underrepresented in ROTC programs, are Maryland residents, and are enrolled full-time or part-time at Bowie State University, Coppin State University, Morgan State University, or University of Maryland Eastern Shore.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Postsecondary education expenses (tuition, fees, and other eligible costs) at an eligible Maryland HBCU institution.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be enrolled at one of four eligible Maryland HBCUs: Bowie State University, Coppin State University, Morgan State University, or University of Maryland Eastern Shore. Must be eligible for Maryland in-state tuition.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident and eligible for Maryland in-state tuition
Must be a current or prospective degree-seeking undergraduate or graduate student (full-time or part-time), or an undocumented student eligible for in-state tuition
Must be enrolled full-time (12+ credits) or part-time (6-11 credits) in a certificate, undergraduate, graduate certificate, or graduate degree program
Must be identified as a minority student or member of a group historically underrepresented in ROTC programs
Must be enrolled at Bowie State University, Coppin State University, Morgan State University, or University of Maryland Eastern Shore
Must be a member of a ROTC program
Must submit FAFSA or MHEC One App (for undocumented students or those ineligible for federal aid) by established deadline
Must submit online application through MDCAPS One-App by the closing date (October 15)
Must submit Institutional Certification Form completed by the institution
Must submit documentation confirming ROTC membership
Must remain drug-free for the full term of the award
For renewal: must maintain satisfactory academic progress, reapply each year, and continue to meet all eligibility and enrollment requirements (renewable for up to three additional years)
Must accept award within established timeframe to prevent cancellation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications open January 15, 2026 through October 15, 2026. Submit FAFSA at studentaid.gov or the MHEC One App through the Maryland College Aid Processing System (MDCAPS) at mdcaps.mhec.state.md.us (for students ineligible for federal aid) by July 15. Then complete and submit the online scholarship application through the MDCAPS One-App by October 15. Upload all required documents — including the Institutional Certification Form (completed by your institution) and documentation confirming ROTC membership — through your MDCAPS account via secure upload. Check application status through 'Award Status' in MDCAPS.

structured_extraction.program_description: SARA allows participating Maryland colleges and universities to offer distance-learning programs and courses to residents of other member states without seeking separate state-by-state approval. It also provides quality assurance and consumer protection to Maryland residents taking distance-learning programs from institutions in other member states. MHEC also oversees a complaint resolution process for students enrolled in interstate distance education programs offered by participating SARA institutions, investigating allegations of dishonest or fraudulent activity, false or misleading information, and violations of C-RAC Guidelines that result in student harm.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MHEC approves Maryland institutions to participate in SARA, enabling them to offer distance-learning courses to students in other member states without obtaining individual state approvals. Annual fees range from $2,000 (fewer than 2,500 FTE students) to $4,000 (2,500–9,999 FTE) to $6,000 (10,000 or more FTE). A separate fee is also payable to NC-SARA upon approval. MHEC also investigates and resolves complaints from students enrolled in distance education programs offered by Maryland SARA-approved institutions, covering fraudulent activity, false/misleading information, and violations of C-RAC Guidelines.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland degree-granting postsecondary institutions accredited by a U.S. Department of Education-recognized accreditor that are authorized to operate in Maryland and meet financial stability requirements. Also serves students enrolled in online degree programs from Maryland-based SARA-approved institutions who have complaints about distance education programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Authorization to offer distance-learning programs to students in other SARA member states without seeking state-by-state approval.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to institutions located in Maryland and authorized to operate in Maryland as in-state institutions. The complaint process applies to distance education programs offered by Maryland SARA-approved institutions to students in other SARA member states.
requirements_list: Must be accredited as a degree-granting institution of higher education by an accrediting body recognized by the U.S. Department of Education
Must be authorized to operate in Maryland as an in-state institution
If not a public institution, must document a composite score of at least 1.5 out of 3.0 on the USDOE financial stability scale
For complaint process: student must exhaust the institutional complaint process first before submitting to MHEC
For complaint process: must submit a written complaint form with additional information and release
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the NC-SARA Application and Approval Form for Institution Participation in SARA (with required signatures of the CEO or CAO). Submit the form along with the applicable annual fee (check made payable to 'Maryland Higher Education Commission' with a reference to SARA) electronically to sara.mhec@maryland.gov or by mail to MHEC-SARA, 217 East Redwood St., Suite 2100, Baltimore, MD 21202. Processing takes two to three weeks after receipt. Upon MHEC approval, institutions receive a link to complete NC-SARA's separate payment and approval process. For student complaints: (1) Exhaust the institutional complaint process; (2) Submit a written complaint to MHEC; (3) Institution provides information and proposed resolution; (4) MHEC and institution negotiate in good faith if unresolved; (5) MHEC issues an outcome letter.

structured_extraction.program_name: State Financial Aid Grant and Scholarship Appeal Process
structured_extraction.program_description: The Office of Student Financial Assistance (OSFA) at the Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC) runs an appeal process that allows students who fail to meet certain requirements for state financial aid awards to request reconsideration when special circumstances caused them to miss eligibility requirements. Students can appeal for reasons such as significant changes in family income, late FAFSA or MHEC One-App submission, extended time to degree (5th year of award), disability, academic program structure, delayed college entrance, credit completion issues, GPA requirements, and enrollment below required credits. Appeals apply to programs including the Guaranteed Access Grant, Educational Assistance Grant, 2+2 Transfer Scholarship, Teaching Fellows for Maryland Scholarship, Senatorial Scholarship, and Delegate Scholarship.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Students may appeal for reconsideration of existing state grant and scholarship awards when they have experienced special circumstances that caused them to miss eligibility requirements. Appeal types include: Special Financial Circumstance (income reassessment), Late FAFSA/MHEC One-App, 5th Year of Award, Program of Study, Delayed College Entrance, Credit Completion (academic program or disability), 2.5 GPA, and Enrolled in Less Than Required Credits (academic program or disability). For enrollment appeals, financial aid is recalculated based on part-time status: 9-11 credits = 75% of award; 6-8 credits = 50% of award. Decisions are provided by email within 45 business days of submission. The appeal process itself does not provide new funding but allows continuation or restoration of existing awards.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Varies by appeal type: July 1, 2026 (Special Financial Circumstance and Late FAFSA/MHEC One-App); September 1, 2026 (5th Year of Award, Program of Study, Delayed College Entrance); October 15, 2026 (Credit Completion and 2.5 GPA appeals, opens May 1, 2026); December 15, 2026 / April 15, 2027 (enrollment appeals; Less Than 12 Credits Academic Program Fall opens July 1, 2026, Spring opens October 1, 2026)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland college students who currently receive or previously received state financial aid grants or scholarships and have experienced special circumstances affecting their eligibility, including students with disabilities, students experiencing financial hardship, students with academic program constraints, students entering their third or fourth year of GA or EA funding, and students enrolled in less than 12 or less than 6 credits due to disability
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Continuation or restoration of state financial aid grant and scholarship awards for higher education expenses, including reconsideration of awards for college attendance
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Maryland residents attending college in Maryland who receive or have received state financial aid awards
requirements_list: Must be a recipient or applicant for an eligible Maryland state financial aid program (Guaranteed Access Grant, Educational Assistance Grant, 2+2 Transfer Scholarship, Teaching Fellows for Maryland Scholarship, Senatorial Scholarship, or Delegate Scholarship)
Must submit appeal through the online form by the applicable deadline
Must upload all required documentation with the appeal request
Incomplete or late appeal requests will be denied
Specific eligibility reasons vary by appeal type (e.g., significant reduction in income, late FAFSA due to specific circumstances, documented disability, academic program structure)

Special Financial Circumstance allowable reasons: death of parent or student's spouse on/after January 1, 2026; separation or divorce on/after January 1, 2026; complete involuntary unemployment for 10+ consecutive weeks beginning on/after January 1, 2025; loss of child support or social security benefits due to reaching age of majority on/after January 1, 2026

Late FAFSA/MHEC One-App allowable reasons: serious injury of student, serious illness of immediate family member, serious emotional difficulties, or other extenuating circumstances (detailed timeline and professional documentation required)

5th Year of Award allowable reasons: 5-year academic program, serious illness/injury, family member serious illness, serious emotional difficulties, or extenuating financial circumstances (after January 1, 2026)

Delayed College Entrance: must have entered college 6+ years after high school/GED completion due to extenuating circumstances outside their control; cannot have previously received Educational Assistance Grant

Credit Completion (Academic Program): must be entering 3rd or 4th year of GA or EA funding; must have completed at least 18 credit hours in 2025-2026 academic year; cannot have received Part-Time Grant from MHEC in 2025-2026; appeal must be based on required course/activity or structure of academic program

Credit Completion (Disability): must have completed less than 24 credit hours due to disability; must be entering 3rd or 4th year of funding; medical documentation from licensed clinical practitioner confirming disability and impact on credit completion required; copy of most recent transcript required; cannot have received Part-Time Grant in 2025-2026; cannot appeal for GA if previously received EA

2.5 GPA (Renewal) Appeal: eligible program is 2+2 Transfer Scholarship; allowable reasons include serious illness/injury, family member illness/death, serious emotional difficulties, or other extenuating circumstances; must submit required documentation specific to reason for appeal and copy of most recent transcript

Enrollment Less Than 12 Credits (Academic Program): minimum 6 credits enrollment; cannot have received Part-Time Grant from MHEC in 2026-27; Department Chair Certification Form required; copy of program curriculum structure from institution's catalog or website required

Enrollment Less Than 12 Credits (Disability): medical documentation from licensed practitioner confirming disability and impact on full course load required; documentation of disability permanence status required (updated each term for non-permanent disabilities); class schedule/documentation of courses and credits for semester being appealed; cannot have received Part-Time Grant from MHEC in 2026-27

Enrollment Less Than 6 Credits (Disability - Senatorial/Delegate Scholarship): medical documentation confirming disability and its impact on ability to take half-time course load required; updated documentation required each term for non-permanent disabilities; documentation of courses and credits being taken required
Students with previous Educational Assistance Grant or CBEAG cannot appeal for Guaranteed Access Grant consideration
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and submit the appeal request through the online form (2026-2027 MHEC Grant and Scholarship Appeal Request Form at https://forms.gle/joSCmbMiQ5rPuwXU7) by the applicable deadline. Upload all required documentation with the submission. A decision will be provided by email within 45 business days. Each appeal type has its own open and close dates. For Credit Completion appeals requiring Department Chair certification, student must complete Parts A-C and Department Chair must complete Parts D-F of the Department Chair Certification Form. For Enrolled in Less Than 12 Credits (Academic Program) appeals, a Department Chair Certification Form is also required along with documentation of courses/credits for the semester being appealed.

structured_extraction.program_name: State Senatorial and Delegate Scholarship (Legislative Scholarships)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Senatorial Scholarship and Delegate Scholarship provide financial aid to Maryland residents pursuing postsecondary education at two-year or four-year Maryland colleges, universities, or private career schools. Maryland state legislators award scholarships directly to students in their legislative districts to help them afford college. Delegates and Senators each administer their own scholarship funds for constituents. The Senatorial Scholarship is awarded through each student's state Senate district delegation based on financial need as demonstrated by the FAFSA, with a minimum award of $400 for the 2026-2027 academic year. The Delegate Scholarship is awarded by Maryland House of Delegates members to students in their legislative district, with a minimum award of $200 for the 2026-2027 academic year and must be re-applied for each year. Both programs are administered by the Maryland Higher Education Commission and provide legislative scholarships to support postsecondary credential attainment. Scholarships are available regardless of family income, whether the student attends full-time or part-time, or which Maryland college or university they choose. Eligible students include current high school seniors, full-time and part-time degree-seeking undergraduate and graduate students, private career school enrollees, undocumented students eligible for in-state tuition, and community college certificate or licensure program students. Students apply through their elected state senator or delegate and must complete the FAFSA (or MHEC One-App if ineligible for federal aid) and may apply through the Maryland Higher Education Commission MDCAPS portal. Awards may be used at out-of-state institutions in limited circumstances including unique majors not available in Maryland, active military duty, or disability accommodations. Recipients enrolled in fewer than 6 credits due to disability may submit a waiver for reconsideration. Senatorial Scholarship awards can be renewed for up to three years, and in some cases a fifth undergraduate year is available. Delegate Scholarships are not automatically renewable — students must re-apply each year through their local State Delegate.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Senatorial Scholarship awards have a minimum of $400 for the 2026-2027 academic year (exact maximum not yet determined). Delegate Scholarship awards have a minimum of $200 for the 2026-2027 academic year up to an unspecified maximum, awarded at the Delegate's discretion. Scholarships are available regardless of family income, whether the student attends full-time or part-time, or which Maryland college or university they choose. The total of all state scholarship awards may not exceed the student's cost of attendance as determined by their Financial Aid Office. Senatorial Scholarship awards can be renewed for up to three years, and in some cases a fifth undergraduate year is available. Delegate Scholarships are not automatically renewable — students must re-apply each year through their local State Delegate. Available for full-time students (12+ credits undergraduate or 9+ credits graduate per semester) and part-time students (6-11 credits undergraduate or 6-8 credits graduate per semester). Awards may be used at out-of-state institutions in limited circumstances (unique major not available in Maryland, active military duty domiciled in Maryland, or disability accommodations not available at a Maryland institution).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Contact your local state Senator or Delegate for instructions; FAFSA or MSFAA deadline March 1 if OSFA is administering awards; Unique Major out-of-state application opens March 15 and closes July 1. Disability Appeal deadlines: Fall Appeal July 1 – December 15, 2026; Spring Appeal October 1, 2026 – April 15, 2027.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents who are current high school seniors, undergraduate or graduate students (full-time or part-time), private career school enrollees, undocumented students eligible for in-state tuition, or community college certificate/license program students pursuing postsecondary education in Maryland, residing in a state legislative district. Open to all income levels. Students with disabilities enrolled in fewer than 6 credits may appeal for reconsideration.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Postsecondary tuition and educational expenses at a two-year or four-year Maryland college, university, or private career school. Can also reimburse educational expenses for community college certificate or licensure programs. May be used at out-of-state schools in limited circumstances if the student's major is unavailable at any Maryland institution, if the student is on active military duty domiciled in Maryland, or if the student has a disability requiring special provisions not available at Maryland institutions. Total awards cannot exceed cost of attendance as determined by the institution's Financial Aid Office.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Maryland resident and eligible for in-state tuition. Senatorial Scholarship awards are issued through the student's state Senate district; Delegate Scholarship awards are issued through the student's local State Delegate's office. Out-of-state use is allowed if the student's major is unavailable at any Maryland institution, if the student is on active military duty domiciled in Maryland, or if the student has a disability requiring special provisions not available at Maryland institutions. Students must contact their elected officials in their legislative district.

structured_extraction.program_name: Student Loan Debt Relief Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A Maryland state tax credit program for residents who have significant student loan debt. Eligible Maryland taxpayers who have incurred at least $20,000 in undergraduate and/or graduate student loan debt and still owe at least $5,000 can apply for a tax credit applied against their Maryland state income taxes to help pay down their college loans. The credit is refundable — if the credit exceeds the applicant's tax liability, the applicant receives a refund for the difference. Recipients must use the full credit award amount to pay their outstanding college loan balances within the required timeframe and provide proof of payment to MHEC. Up to $18 million total in tax credits is available to eligible Maryland residents. Eligible applicants are divided into two groups: those who attended a Maryland in-state institution and those who attended an out-of-state institution. Residents who attended an in-state institution receive a higher credit amount ($1,000) than those who attended an out-of-state institution ($883). The program also encourages Maryland residents to remain in the state workforce, with awarding priority given to Maryland State employees with student loan debt. Both undergraduate and graduate student loan debt is eligible. Parent PLUS loans are not eligible.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A refundable tax credit claimed on Maryland Form 502 applied against the recipient's Maryland state income taxes to help reduce student loan debt. If the credit exceeds the applicant's tax liability, the applicant receives a refund for the difference. Up to $18 million total in tax credits is available to eligible Maryland residents. Applicants who attended in-state institutions receive $1,000 in tax credits; applicants who attended out-of-state institutions receive $883 in tax credits. Recipients must use the full credit award amount to pay their outstanding college loan balances (principal and/or interest, lump sum or installments) within three years of the close of the taxable year for which the credit applies, and must provide proof of payment to MHEC via their OneStop account. Failure to do so results in recapture of the credit by the state.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland taxpayers who maintain Maryland residency for the applicable tax year, have incurred at least $20,000 in undergraduate and/or graduate student loan debt (excluding Parent PLUS loans), and still have at least $5,000 in outstanding student loan debt at the time of application, having attended either a Maryland in-state or out-of-state institution. Awarding priority is given to Maryland State employees with student loan debt.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Must be applied toward the recipient's outstanding college/student loan balance (principal and/or interest, lump sum or installments) within three years of the close of the taxable year for which the credit applies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must maintain Maryland residency for the applicable tax year and file Maryland State Income Taxes for that year. Available to Maryland residents statewide.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Student Loan Debt Relief Tax Credit Application through the OneStop portal at onestop.md.gov or through the MHEC website before September 15th. Eligible applicants are divided into two groups: those who attended in-state institutions and those who attended out-of-state institutions. Submit acceptable lender documents and all required documentation as required. After receiving the credit, claim it on your Maryland income tax return (Form 502) when filing taxes. Log into your OneStop account to submit proof of payment to lenders within the required timeframe. Applications are reviewed and credits are awarded annually.

structured_extraction.program_name: Teacher Quality and Diversity Competitive Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides competitive grants to teacher preparation programs at Maryland institutions of higher education. The program helps students from groups historically underrepresented in the teaching profession — including African Americans, American Indians/Alaska Natives, Hispanics/Latinos, low-income individuals, first-generation college students, and people with disabilities — meet teacher preparation and certification requirements. It also helps institutions take advantage of national foundation efforts to develop highly qualified, diverse teachers and leaders. Grants support initiatives to improve the quality and diversity of teachers in Maryland through alternative accelerated pathways, consortium-based initiatives, transfer pathways from community colleges, mentoring, test preparation, and targeted interventions for underrepresented groups including male-identifying students.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants totaling $1,000,000 annually. Individual track awards range from $50,000 to $150,000. Consortium track awards range from $250,000 to $500,000. Grants run from December 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026. Up to 8% of total direct costs may be used for indirect cost recovery.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Accredited institutions of higher education in Maryland, with priority given to historically Black colleges and universities (HBCUs) and Hispanic-serving institutions with a track record of preparing diverse, high-quality teachers. Ultimately serves students from groups historically underrepresented in the teaching profession, including African Americans, American Indians/Alaska Natives, Hispanics/Latinos, low-income individuals, first-generation college students, individuals with disabilities, male-identifying students, career changers with subject-matter expertise, conditionally licensed teachers, and federal workers transitioning into teaching.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supporting students from underrepresented groups in meeting teacher preparation and certification requirements. Funds may support alternative accelerated pathways into teaching, consortium-based programs, transfer pathways from community colleges, mentoring, test preparation, and targeted interventions for male-identifying students and other underrepresented groups. Allowable costs include salaries and wages for professional and support personnel, fringe benefits, travel for essential personnel, equipment (useful life greater than 1 year), supplies and materials, consultant and contractual services, and other specified expenditures. Funds must supplement, not supplant, existing institutional investment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to accredited institutions of higher education located in Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be an accredited institution of higher education in Maryland.
Proposals must demonstrate a sustainable plan for continuation beyond the grant period (program is not intended to supplant existing institutional investment).

Priority given to proposals emphasizing alternative accelerated pathways, consortium-based approaches, transfer pathway strengthening, standards-aligned programming with mentoring, transcript analysis licensure pathways, and targeted interventions for male-identifying students and other underrepresented groups.
Consortium applications (two or more institutions, or institution plus local education agency) are strongly encouraged.

Must comply with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA).
Must participate in statewide assessment/evaluation programs as required.
Grant records must be maintained for 5 years.
Must acknowledge MHEC support in all publications and include required disclaimer.
Must submit interim and final reports.
Prior written approval required for scope changes, project director changes, staff/consultant changes, and budget changes exceeding $1,000 or 10%.
Indirect costs limited to a maximum of 8% of total direct costs.
Professional personnel must be listed by name and title in budget submission.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application by email to mhecgrants@maryland.gov and/or mhectqdp@mhec.state.md.us by 4:00 p.m. on October 30, 2025. Submit a complete proposal with all requisite forms. A qualified reviewer panel scores proposals against evaluation criteria (maximum 105 points) and convenes to discuss and recommend funding. Recommendations are submitted to the Secretary of Higher Education for final funding decisions. Award notifications will be made no later than November 28, 2025. For technical assistance, contact Elena Quiroz-Livanis at elena.quiroz@maryland.gov. For application submission questions, contact Anthony Reiner at anthony.reiner@maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Teaching Fellows for Maryland Scholarship provides financial awards to students who commit to working as a public school or public prekindergarten teacher in Maryland after completing their studies. Recipients must teach in a high-needs school (as identified by the Maryland State Department of Education, including schools where at least 50% of students are eligible for free or reduced-price meals) or in a grade level or subject area with a shortage of qualified educators. The program is open to undergraduate and graduate students, including career changers and teaching assistants with at least 2 years of experience at a Maryland public school or public prekindergarten program, who are enrolled or planning to enroll at an eligible Maryland institution in a program leading to a Maryland professional teacher's certificate. Maryland residency is not required, and GPA, GRE, or SAT scores are not required. Awards are reviewed and distributed on a weekly basis. MHEC awarded a total of $1,916,770 to 106 students in the most recent round. Undergraduate recipients must fulfill a service obligation of one year for each year they receive the scholarship; graduate recipients must fulfill two years for each year they receive the scholarship.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: At a Maryland public senior higher education institution, the award covers 100% of annual tuition, mandatory fees, and room and board for a resident undergraduate or graduate student. At a Maryland private nonprofit institution, the award equals the lesser of: (1) 100% of University of Maryland College Park resident tuition and fees plus 100% of room and board at the private institution, or (2) 50% of the private institution's resident tuition and fees plus 100% of room and board. Private nonprofit institutions must provide a matching scholarship equal to the State award for tuition and fees (but not room and board). Students living off campus or with parents receive a housing allowance. The award is renewable for up to three additional years (four renewals if enrolled in a 5-year program), provided the recipient maintains continued enrollment and satisfactory academic progress. Awards are reviewed and distributed on a weekly basis. MHEC awarded a total of $1,916,770 to 106 students in the most recent round. Undergraduate recipients must fulfill one year of service for each year of scholarship received; graduate recipients must fulfill two years for each year of scholarship received.

structured_extraction.program_name: Title IX Campus Sexual Assault Proceedings - Attorney Reimbursement Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC) maintains a list of attorneys willing to represent students in Title IX Campus Sexual Assault Proceedings at Maryland colleges and universities, and reimburses attorney fees and certain costs for that legal representation. Attorneys on the MHEC Attorney List charge no more than $120 per hour (the civil legal services rate set by the Maryland Legal Services Corporation), and those fees may be paid by MHEC upon application by the attorney. Attorneys not on the approved list may also seek fee reimbursement for up to 20 hours at $120 per hour. Travel cost reimbursement is also available. All listed attorneys have completed training on representing students in Title IX proceedings. Reimbursement is subject to availability of appropriated funds, and payment requests must be submitted within 60 days of termination of representation. Representation must be for Title IX proceedings only — not civil, criminal, or non-Title IX student disciplinary proceedings. Legal services must have been provided on or after August 1, 2019.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MHEC reimburses attorneys at $120 per hour (the civil legal services rate set by the Maryland Legal Services Corporation) for legal representation in Title IX proceedings, up to a cap of 20 hours per case. Travel cost reimbursement is also available (mileage at $0.70 per mile for FY 2025, tolls, parking, public transit) up to $200 per case with receipts required. Office expenses are not covered. Reimbursement is subject to availability of appropriated funds. Payment requests must be submitted within 60 days of termination of representation, and processing takes at least 60 days. MHEC also maintains a list of trained attorneys available to represent students; all listed attorneys have completed at least 5 hours of training on trauma-informed Title IX representation. Attorneys not on the list may also seek fee reimbursement for up to 20 hours at $120 per hour. Representation is covered for investigation, mediation, hearing, and appeal phases of Title IX proceedings.

structured_extraction.program_name: Tuition Reduction for Non-Resident Nursing Students
structured_extraction.program_description: This program reduces tuition costs for out-of-state students enrolled in a nursing program at a Maryland public two-year or four-year institution. The award covers the difference between out-of-state and in-state tuition (the tuition differential) at the student's institution, so the student effectively pays the in-state rate. The award renews automatically for up to one additional year at a two-year school or three additional years at a four-year school, provided the student maintains satisfactory academic progress and remains enrolled in an eligible nursing program. Recipients must sign a promissory note agreeing to serve as a full-time nurse in a hospital or related institution for two years (two-year school graduates) or four years (four-year school graduates) after graduation, or repay the award with interest.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The annual award equals the tuition differential — the difference between out-of-state and in-state tuition at the same institution for the same program and number of credit hours. The institution adjusts tuition charges so the student pays the in-state resident tuition rate. The award renews automatically: one additional year for two-year institution students, three additional years for four-year institution students, provided the student maintains satisfactory academic progress and stays enrolled in an eligible nursing program. Recipients must sign a promissory note agreeing to serve as a full-time nurse in a hospital or related institution after graduation (two years for two-year school graduates; four years for four-year school graduates), or repay the award with interest.

structured_extraction.program_name: Tuition Waiver for Foster Care Recipients
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Tuition Waiver for Foster Care Recipients provides free tuition and mandatory fees at Maryland public colleges and universities to eligible foster care youth and former foster care youth. It waives tuition and mandatory fees (including registration fees and other required enrollment fees) at any Maryland public institution of higher education for individuals who were placed in out-of-home care by the Maryland Department of Human Services and are enrolled in an associate degree, bachelor's degree, or vocational certificate program. The waiver does not cover room, board, books, or transportation. Scholarships or grants awarded to a recipient may not be applied to tuition since tuition is already waived. The waiver applies to fall, winter, spring, and summer terms, and youth must enroll before age 25.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The waiver exempts eligible students from paying tuition and mandatory fees (including registration fees and other required enrollment fees) at any Maryland public institution of higher education. It applies to fall, winter, spring, and summer terms. The waiver does not cover room, board, books, or transportation. Scholarships or grants awarded to a recipient may not be applied to tuition since tuition is already waived. Youth must enroll before age 25.

structured_extraction.program_description: A one-time scholarship incentive program that encouraged 12- to 17-year-olds in Maryland to get vaccinated against COVID-19. Twenty winners received a $50,000 scholarship each, covering the equivalent of full tuition and fees at a public, in-state college or university, distributed as a Maryland 529 Prepaid College Trust Account (for ages 12–14) or a Maryland College Investment Plan contribution (for ages 15–17). Winners were selected through random drawings held between July 12 and Labor Day (September 6, 2021), with two winners selected per week for eight weeks and four winners selected on Labor Day. The program was funded by federal COVID-19 relief funds.

Two winners were selected per week for eight weeks beginning July 12, 2021, and four winners were selected on Labor Day (September 6, 2021). The program was funded by federal COVID-19 relief funds.

Must be vaccinated against COVID-19 in Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Winners were selected through random drawings using a random number generator. Two winners were selected per week for eight weeks starting July 12, 2021, and four winners were selected on Labor Day (September 6, 2021). Winners may remain anonymous, but their city or county was published.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides financial assistance to Maryland resident students, Maryland high school graduates, and active duty U.S. Military members stationed in, residing in, or domiciled in Maryland who enroll in approved non-credit certificate programs at participating Maryland community colleges. Programs must lead to apprenticeships, employment, licensure, or job skill enhancement. The scholarship may be renewed for an additional developmental sequence.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Maximum award of $2,000 annually to cover tuition, mandatory fees, and associated costs of attendance at a participating Maryland community college, to the extent those costs have not already been covered by another state grant, scholarship, or employer funding. The scholarship may be combined with other state grants or scholarships as long as the total does not exceed the student's tuition, fees, and other associated costs. Award may be renewed for an additional developmental sequence. Administered through college financial aid offices; applicants must contact their college for deadlines.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applicants must contact their college financial aid office to apply and get deadlines
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland resident students, Maryland high school graduates, and active duty U.S. Military members stationed in, residing in, or domiciled in Maryland, who are enrolled in an eligible Workforce Development Sequence at a participating Maryland community college.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition, mandatory fees, and associated costs of attendance for non-credit workforce development courses at a participating Maryland community college.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Maryland resident, Maryland high school graduate, or active duty U.S. Military member stationed in, residing in, or domiciled in Maryland. Must attend a participating Maryland community college.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident, Maryland high school graduate, or active duty U.S. Military member stationed in, residing in, or domiciled in Maryland
Must be enrolled in an eligible Workforce Development Sequence at a participating community college
Must enroll in an approved non-credit certificate program
Courses must be non-credit and related to job preparation or registered apprenticeship, licensure or certification, or job skill enhancement
Program must lead to an apprenticeship, employment, licensure, or job skill enhancement
Additional eligibility criteria may apply at individual colleges
Contact college financial aid office to apply and obtain deadline
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your community college's financial aid office to apply and obtain the deadline.

structured_extraction.program_name: Workforce Shortage Student Assistance Grant Program (WSSAG)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Workforce Shortage Student Assistance Grant Program (WSSAG) provides financial assistance to Maryland resident students who plan to work in specific career fields with workforce shortages upon graduation. Eligible fields include child care, human services, teaching, nursing, physical and occupational therapy, social work, and public service. Annual grant awards are based on institution type and enrollment status, ranging from $1,000 to $4,000 per year. Recipients must sign a promissory note and fulfill a service obligation in their field within one year of completing their degree. Awards may be renewed for up to five years if eligibility is maintained.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual grant awards based on institution type and enrollment status: $2,000 per year for full-time attendance (12+ credits per semester) at a Maryland community college; $1,000 per year for part-time attendance (6–11 credits per semester) at a community college; $4,000 per year for full-time attendance at a Maryland four-year institution; $2,000 per year for part-time attendance at a four-year institution. Awards may be renewed for up to five years if eligibility is maintained. Funds are paid to the institution at the beginning of each semester after certification. Recipients must sign a promissory note agreeing to fulfill a service obligation (1–2 years per scholarship year depending on full-time/part-time work status) in their employment field within one year of degree completion.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: FAFSA by June 1 (not required but recommended); Workforce Shortage application and required documentation by July 1; April 1, 2026 (2025-2026 academic year); October 15, 2026 (2026-2027 academic year)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland resident undergraduate and graduate students enrolled at a Maryland college or university in an eligible major leading to employment in a workforce shortage field, including child care, human services, teaching, nursing, physical and occupational therapy, social work, and public service. Also open to high school students (entering freshmen) planning to enroll in eligible programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition and educational expenses for degree programs in eligible workforce shortage fields including child care, human services, teaching, nursing, physical and occupational therapy, social work, and public service at Maryland two-year or four-year colleges or universities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicant must be a Maryland resident; dependent students' parents must also be Maryland residents. Must attend a two-year or four-year Maryland college or university.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident (if a dependent student, the parent must also be a Maryland resident)
Must enroll at a two-year or four-year Maryland college or university

Must be a degree-seeking student in an eligible major leading to employment in an eligible workforce shortage field (child care, human services, teaching, nursing, physical or occupational therapy, social work, or public service)
Plans to work in the eligible field upon graduation
Full-time undergraduate enrollment: 12+ credits per semester; part-time undergraduate: 6–11 credits per semester
Full-time graduate enrollment: 9+ credits per semester; part-time graduate: 6–8 credits per semester
Must earn at least 12 credit hours per academic year (undergraduate) or 9 credit hours per academic year (graduate) including summer
Must maintain satisfactory academic progress standards of the institution

Must sign a promissory note agreeing to fulfill a service obligation (1–2 years per scholarship year depending on full-time/part-time work status) in the eligible employment field within one year of degree completion
Students who received awards under prior MHEC career/occupational programs are not eligible to also receive a WSSAG award
File FAFSA by June 1 (not required but preferred) to be considered for need-based ranking
Submit Workforce Shortage application and required documentation by July 1
Submit official or unofficial transcript(s) showing cumulative GPA (calculated by MHEC on a 4.0 scale)
For nursing, physical therapy, or occupational therapy students: submit acceptance letter from department
Submit transfer transcripts from all prior institutions if applicable
Accept award within 3 weeks of notification email
Drug-free pledge required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the online application through the Maryland College Aid Processing System (MDCAPS) using the MHEC One App. Optionally file the FAFSA at www.fafsa.gov by June 1 (recommended) to be considered for need-based ranking. Submit official or unofficial transcripts showing cumulative GPA. Certain majors (nursing, physical therapy, occupational therapy) require an acceptance letter from the department. All supporting documents must be submitted with the application (not reusable from prior years). Applicants are ranked by GPA and then by financial need within each occupational field. The Workforce Shortage application and required documentation are due by July 1 (rolling deadline). Accept the award within 3 weeks of receiving the notification email and submit the online promissory note.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Workforce and Employability Skills Program (WESP) awards grants to Maryland higher education institutions to create skills-development programs that help low-income youth prepare for college. Programs funded through WESP offer career exploration, educational planning, job skills training and workshops, communication, teamwork, self-advocacy, experiential learning, and workplace readiness training to students who may not otherwise consider college. WESP is part of a six-year federal grant program (2014–2020) administered through the Maryland GEAR UP program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants awarded to two- and four-year Maryland higher education institutions partnering with Local Education Authorities (LEAs). In the 2019 funding cycle, more than $108,000 was distributed: $80,000 to Johns Hopkins University and $28,372 to Wor-Wic Community College. This funding is part of a six-year federal GEAR UP grant program (2014–2020).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland two- and four-year higher education institutions partnering with Local Education Authorities to serve low-income and underrepresented youth in Baltimore City, Dorchester, and Wicomico counties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Creating in-school programs focused on career exploration, educational planning, job skills, communication, collaboration, teamwork, self-advocacy, experiential learning, and workplace readiness training for low-income and underrepresented students.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Programs are focused on Maryland GEAR UP districts: Baltimore City, Dorchester County, and Wicomico County.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Maryland two- or four-year higher education institution
Must partner with a Local Education Authority (LEA)
Programs must serve low-income and underrepresented students
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Maryland two- and four-year institutions applied to MHEC in conjunction with the Maryland GEAR UP program. Eligible institutions partner with Local Education Authorities (LEAs) as part of the grant application. No additional application process details are provided on this page.

structured_extraction.program_name: African American Heritage Preservation Program Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides capital grants to nonprofits, local governments, businesses, and individuals to help preserve buildings, sites, and communities of historical and cultural importance to the African American experience in Maryland. The Maryland Historical Trust and the Maryland Commission on African American History and Culture jointly administer the program. Grants can fund acquisition, restoration, rehabilitation, stabilization, new facilities for interpretation, and pre-construction planning work. The program typically has an annual budget of $5 million for grants.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Capital grants of up to $250,000 per applicant to assist in preserving buildings, sites, or communities significant to the African American experience in Maryland. The program typically has an annual budget of $5 million for grants. No matching funds required. Grants cannot be used for routine maintenance, fundraising, research, exhibits, or work already started or completed. State and federal government entities may apply as nonprofits.
