structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations, local governments, businesses, and individuals seeking to preserve properties and sites significant to African American history and culture in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Preservation or acquisition of buildings, sites, or structures significant to African American history; restoration or rehabilitation of historic sites; development of new facilities to interpret or celebrate African American history; stabilization of endangered properties; pre-construction planning including architectural, engineering, or other special services such as studies, surveys, and predevelopment costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in Maryland.
requirements_list: Project must be located in Maryland
Project must demonstrate a clear, direct connection to African American history, culture, or heritage
Property owner permission must be provided with the application
Projects must comply with the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Treatment of Historic Properties (26 CFR 68)
For religious properties, grants generally fund only structural or exterior work, not interior worship spaces or elements with religious imagery
For cemeteries, applicant must demonstrate clear property ownership
The project must provide a strong public benefit to be competitive
Work that is already underway or completed is not eligible for funding
If the property is listed or eligible for the National Register, the owner must convey a term preservation easement to the Maryland Historical Trust
Property Owner Consent Letter required for Capital Projects and Easements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Review the current grant guidelines and sample materials. 2. Confirm applicant and project eligibility. 3. Attend a pre-application workshop or webinar. 4. Prepare required attachments such as cost estimates, photographs, letters of support, and proof of ownership or site control. 5. Submit a completed application through the grants portal before July 1, 2026 at 11:59 PM. The FY27 grant round is expected to open in March 2026, with applications typically available in early April and due by July 1. The agency announces decisions by December each year.

structured_extraction.program_description: A two-weekend workshop in spring where Scouts BSA members learn about archaeology and Maryland history. One weekend covers classroom learning and one focuses on fieldwork, including hands-on activities and excavation at an active archaeological site.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants attend two weekends of instruction led by MHT archaeologists — one weekend of classroom learning and one of fieldwork at an active archaeological site. Scouts who complete all requirements and prerequisites can earn the Scouts BSA Archaeology Merit Badge.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Scouts BSA members interested in archaeology and Maryland history, whether registering individually or with a troop.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participation in archaeology workshops to earn the Scouts BSA Archaeology Merit Badge.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Open to Scouts BSA members; no explicit geographic restriction stated.
requirements_list: Must be currently registered with Scouts BSA
Must participate in both weekends of the workshop
Must complete the prerequisites for the Scouts BSA Archaeology Merit Badge
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Sign up for the interest list via the Google Form link on the page to be notified when future workshops open. Space is limited and fills quickly.

structured_extraction.program_description: Each year, the Maryland Historical Trust (MHT) provides grants to local governments that participate in the Certified Local Government (CLG) Program. These grants fund historic preservation projects and programs, including historic property surveys, National Register nominations, design guidelines, training for preservation commission members, preservation planning studies, and public education and outreach.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive project grants up to $25,000 per project, plus non-competitive education and training grants up to an amount specified in annual guidelines. No match is required, but a 15% match is encouraged. All grants are subject to available federal funding through the Historic Preservation Fund.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments certified under the Certified Local Government (CLG) Program in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Historic property surveys, National Register of Historic Places nominations, design guidelines for historic districts, training for local preservation commission members and staff, preservation plans or planning studies, and public education and outreach about preservation topics.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Certified Local Governments throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Certified Local Government (CLG) participating in the CLG Program.
Projects must be non-capital in nature (except for commissioner and staff training grants).
Applications must be submitted through the MHT grants portal before the posted deadline.
Applicants are strongly encouraged to contact MHT staff early in the planning process for guidance.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications and grant guidelines are emailed to CLG contacts when the application round opens (early February). Applicants review the guidelines, confirm eligibility, consult with MHT staff as needed, and submit a completed application through the MHT grants portal before the end of February deadline. Awards are announced in May.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Certified Local Government (CLG) Program recognizes local governments in Maryland that meet high standards for historic preservation planning and have applied for certification. It is administered by the Maryland Historical Trust (MHT) in partnership with the National Park Service. Certified local governments receive technical support, training, and access to annual grant funding to strengthen local historic preservation programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Each year, MHT awards 10% of its federal Historic Preservation Fund allocation as grants to Certified Local Governments. Grants can fund education and training for preservation commission members and staff, surveys, planning documents, design guidelines, and public outreach or interpretation projects. Technical support and training are also available. Grant applications are typically due in February.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments (counties and municipalities) in Maryland that have established or are working to establish a qualified historic preservation commission and meet state and federal preservation planning standards.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Education and training for preservation commission members and local government staff; surveys, planning documents, and design guidelines; public outreach or interpretation projects that connect residents to local history.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to local governments throughout Maryland. There are currently 24 Certified Local Governments, including 13 cities and 11 counties.
requirements_list: Enact a preservation ordinance that meets state and federal standards
Appoint a qualified historic preservation commission
Maintain a system for identifying and protecting historic properties
Complete a certification application outlining all CLG standards
Complete training and a short report annually (to maintain certification)
Participate in an evaluation every four years (to maintain certification)
Maintain public participation mechanisms
Maintain conflict of interest provisions
Satisfy annual reporting requirements
Participate in local review procedures for National Register nominations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Check whether your jurisdiction is already a Certified Local Government (CLG). 2. If not, adopt a preservation ordinance, designate a qualified commission, and set up review procedures. Review the CLG Procedures Manual and CLG application. 3. Submit a certification application to MHT. 4. Once certified, watch MHT's website each February for the annual CLG grant round and contact MHT staff early to discuss draft applications. Note: Ongoing annual monitoring and evaluation apply; non-compliance may result in decertification.

structured_extraction.program_name: Federal Historic Preservation Tax Incentive (Rehabilitation Tax Credit)
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal tax credit program for owners and developers of income-producing historic buildings who undertake qualified rehabilitation projects. Jointly administered with the National Park Service (NPS), the program provides a federal income tax credit equal to 20% of the qualified capital costs expended in the rehabilitation of eligible income-producing historic properties. There is no cap on the amount of the federal credit. The Maryland Historical Trust (MHT) serves as the State Historic Preservation Office and is the first point of contact for applicants in Maryland. MHT reviews applications, advises on rehabilitation projects, makes site visits, and sends certification recommendations to the NPS, which administers the program. The program aims to create jobs and revitalize communities.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal Rehabilitation Tax Credit (also called the historic preservation tax credit or historic tax credit) for rehabilitating income-producing historic buildings listed in the National Register of Historic Places. The credit equals 20% of the qualified capital costs expended on an approved rehabilitation. There is no cap on the credit amount. The credit offsets federal income taxes owed. Specific credit amounts and rates are set by the NPS/IRS; applicants should refer to the NPS program page for details.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners, private investors, businesses, non-profits, and individuals who own or develop income-producing historic buildings seeking to undertake qualified rehabilitation projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rehabilitation of income-producing buildings listed in or eligible for the National Register of Historic Places. The tax credit applies to qualified costs for the rehabilitation of an eligible historic property.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to historic properties throughout Maryland; MHT serves as the state point of contact for applicants.
requirements_list: Building must be listed in or eligible for the National Register of Historic Places
The property must be a certified historic structure
Project must involve a qualified rehabilitation
Building must be income-producing
The rehabilitation project must meet the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Download the application from the NPS website. 2. Complete the application. 3. Submit a Teams channel request form. 4. Submit the application and any necessary documentation to the Teams channel. MHT reviews the application and makes certification recommendations to NPS, which provides final approval.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants of up to $100,000 for the preservation of Maryland's historic properties and sites. Funds important and urgently needed capital projects that benefit the public, including acquisition, stabilization, rehabilitation, restoration, or predevelopment of historic properties. Energy projects as part of an acquisition or rehabilitation are also eligible expenditures. If a property receives grant funding, the applicant must convey a historic preservation easement on the property to MHT.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $100,000 per project for capital projects involving acquisition, stabilization, rehabilitation, restoration, or predevelopment of historic properties that provide a public benefit. Energy projects as part of a qualifying project are eligible. A 1:1 cash match is required for all applicants except nonprofits. If a property receives grant funding, the applicant must convey a historic preservation easement on the property to MHT. Total program funding is $1 million.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations, local governments, businesses, and individuals seeking to preserve historic properties listed in or eligible for the National Register of Historic Places in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquire historic properties; stabilize, rehabilitate, or restore historic properties; develop plans and specifications and architectural, engineering, or other special services directly related to pre-construction work (nonprofits and local governments only); energy efficiency improvements as part of a qualifying project. Cannot be used for routine maintenance, fundraising, research, exhibits, or work already started or completed.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Properties must be listed in or determined eligible for listing in the National Register of Historic Places.
requirements_list: Property must be listed in or determined eligible for listing in the National Register of Historic Places
Projects must provide a public benefit
Property owner permission must be provided with the application
Projects must comply with the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Treatment of Historic Properties (26 CFR 68) and Standards for Rehabilitation
A 1:1 cash match is required for all applicants except nonprofits
A historic preservation easement must be conveyed to MHT if grant funding is received
Religious properties: grants can generally only fund structural or exterior work, not interior worship spaces or elements bearing religious imagery
Cemeteries: applicant must demonstrate clear property ownership
Pre-construction planning services (architectural, engineering, etc.) are only eligible for nonprofit and local government applicants
Work that is already in progress or completed is not eligible for funding
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Review current grant guidelines and sample materials. 2. Confirm applicant and project eligibility. 3. Attend a pre-application workshop or webinar. 4. Prepare required attachments (cost estimates, photographs, letters of support, proof of ownership or site control). 5. Submit a completed application through the MHT grants portal before the posted deadline. Applications open in February and are due in March; awards are announced in June.

structured_extraction.program_description: Funds research, survey, documentation, planning, and education projects related to Maryland's historic, architectural, archaeological, and cultural resources. These grants do not support building construction or major rehabilitation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants of up to $75,000. Local governments must provide a 1:1 match (cash or in-kind). Nonprofit organizations and state/federal agencies applying as nonprofits are not subject to the match requirement.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations (including state and federal agencies applying as nonprofits) and local governments undertaking research, survey, documentation, planning, or education projects related to Maryland's historic, architectural, archaeological, and cultural resources.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Surveys and studies of historic buildings, archaeological sites, and cultural resources; reports on history and significance of historic properties; National Register nominations and historic contexts; improvements to qualifying archaeological collections; emergency planning documentation; educational materials and public programs; oral history and cultural heritage documentation; preservation plans, feasibility studies, and property assessments.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must relate to Maryland's historic, architectural, archaeological, and cultural resources.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a nonprofit organization (state and federal agencies may apply as nonprofits) or a local government
Local governments must provide a 1:1 match (cash or in-kind)
Projects must not involve building acquisition, major construction, or full rehabilitation
Work must not begin prior to grant approval
Projects focused mainly on fundraising, social or promotional events, or general administrative costs are not eligible
Submit an Intent to Apply form when the application round opens
Attend a virtual workshop is strongly encouraged
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Review the current grant guidelines and manual. 2. Attend a virtual workshop. 3. Submit an Intent to Apply form when the round opens (June). 4. Prepare a full application package including project description, budget, timeline, and explanation of significance. 5. Submit the completed application through the MHT grants portal before the August deadline. Awards are announced in November.

structured_extraction.program_description: Mobile outreach program by the Maryland Historical Trust (MHT) that offers virtual and in-person educational sessions across Maryland. Sessions cover MHT preservation programs, funding opportunities, and financial incentives for homeowners, local governments, nonprofits, and others interested in historic and cultural places — especially those with limited experience with these programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free educational sessions (virtual and in-person) covering MHT grant programs, tax credit incentives, and technical preservation resources. Sessions can be tailored to specific audiences and include Q&A with MHT staff. Organizations can also request a custom local session with a partner host.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners, local governments, nonprofits, heritage organizations, and community groups — especially those with limited experience with MHT programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable — this is a training and outreach program, not a direct funding program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland. In-person events rotate among Maryland's regions annually. Virtual sessions are open to anyone.
requirements_list: To request a local session, a partner organization must host and help market the event. Eligible hosts include local governments, planning commissions, historical societies, and nonprofit organizations.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Attend scheduled sessions listed on MHT's Upcoming Events page. To request a custom local session, identify your audience and preferred topics, then submit a request through MHT's online form or by contacting MHT staff directly.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program designates, supports, and collaborates with heritage areas and their partners to create place-based experiences for the public. It preserves and promotes Maryland's unique historic, cultural, and natural stories while contributing to local economies. The program provides technical and financial assistance to help protect and enhance heritage resources within certified heritage areas, improving quality of life for residents and maximizing economic development through heritage tourism.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers capital and non-capital project grants, mini-grants, loans, and tax credits. Non-capital grants are available up to $50,000 and capital grants up to $100,000; both require a one-to-one match. Loans can cover up to 50% of a project's cost. A tax credit of up to 20% is available for eligible rehabilitation costs of qualifying historic structures. Technical assistance and information are also provided.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: The FY26 grant round is now closed. The FY27 grant round will open in December 2025.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations, government agencies, individuals, and businesses with projects located within certified Maryland heritage areas, working to preserve and promote historic, cultural, and natural resources.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support capital and non-capital projects. Capital uses include buying property, construction, repair, and restoration. Non-capital uses include planning, creating exhibits and signs, and funding educational programs or events. Loans can cover purchase of equipment, furnishings, and inventory. Overall purpose is supporting, protecting, and interpreting Maryland's diverse heritage through tourism and community enhancement.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide within designated certified Maryland heritage areas.
requirements_list: Projects must be located within or support a designated Maryland heritage area.
All grants require a one-to-one matching contribution from the grantee.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact program staff or visit sub-pages for project grants and mini-grants for application details. The program operates on an annual grant cycle; contact the program administrator for current round information.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Heritage Areas Program provides loans to nonprofits, local governments, businesses, and individuals to support projects that create or improve place-based heritage resources within a designated heritage area.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans covering up to 50% of total project cost based on applicant's financial need. Loan amount depends on available funding. Refinancing is not eligible as part of the project cost.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofits, local governments, businesses, and individuals with projects in Maryland heritage areas
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition of property or easements; development, repair, or alteration of buildings or structures for heritage tourism; rehabilitation or restoration of properties; leasehold improvements on properties with leases at least as long as the loan term; purchasing equipment, furnishings, or inventory
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Project must be located within a designated Maryland heritage area
requirements_list: Project must create or improve place-based heritage resources within a heritage area
Loan covers up to 50% of total project cost
Refinancing is not an eligible project cost
For leasehold improvements, the lease must last at least as long as the loan term
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review the program's loan regulations and contact program staff for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: Each of Maryland's 13 heritage areas may offer mini-grants for heritage-related non-capital projects such as educational programming or planning efforts. Individual heritage area organizations administer these grants for projects under $5,000.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Mini-grants of under $5,000 for heritage-related non-capital projects such as educational programming or planning efforts. Administered by individual heritage area organizations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations, agencies, and local partners located within Maryland's 13 heritage areas
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Heritage-related non-capital projects such as educational programming or planning efforts
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be located within one of Maryland's 13 designated heritage areas
requirements_list: Project must be heritage-related and non-capital
Project cost must be under $5,000
Project must be within a designated heritage area
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the individual heritage area's website to learn about their specific mini-grant process.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Heritage Areas Program Project Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Heritage Areas Program awards grants for capital and non-capital projects within Maryland's certified heritage areas. Funded projects highlight Maryland's diverse heritage, enhance local communities, and promote tourism, sustainability, and economic development. Projects must create or improve publicly accessible, place-based experiences that preserve and promote Maryland's unique stories.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Approximately $3 million is awarded per grant round. A 1:1 match (any combination of cash or in-kind) is required. Non-capital grants range from $5,000 to $50,000. Capital grants range from $5,000 to $100,000. Capital projects may fund property acquisition, construction, repair, restoration, or construction planning. Non-capital projects may fund planning, programs, and interpretation.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: March (full application due); Intent to Apply due January; grant round opens December; awards announced July
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations, local governments, and state or federal agencies with projects located within one or more of Maryland's 13 certified heritage areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital projects: buying property, building, repairing, restoring, or planning for construction. Non-capital projects: planning, programs, and interpretation related to Maryland's heritage.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located within the boundaries of one or more of Maryland's 13 certified heritage areas.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a nonprofit organization in good standing with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation, a local government, or a state or federal agency
Project must take place within the boundaries of one or more certified Maryland heritage areas
A 1:1 match (cash or in-kind) is required
Project must create or enhance publicly accessible, place-based experiences or assets that preserve and promote Maryland's unique stories and contribute to local economic well-being
Applicants must submit an Intent to Apply form by the January deadline
Applicants must submit a full application through the grants portal by the March deadline
Proof of nonprofit status and organizational documents required
Letters of support may be submitted
Budget documentation required
Photographs required per submission requirements
Property owner consent required where applicable
Project review by Maryland Department of Natural Resources required where applicable
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Review the grant guidelines. 2. Confirm your project is located within a heritage area using the Medusa database. 3. Submit an Intent to Apply form by the January deadline. 4. Contact the appropriate local heritage area staff to discuss your project. 5. Prepare application materials including project description and timeline, budget and supporting materials, and optional letters of support. 6. Submit the full application through the grants portal by the March deadline.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Heritage Areas Program – Management Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: Annual grants to certified heritage area management organizations across Maryland for management, marketing, and mini-grants to local organizations. The grants help heritage areas promote and support historic, cultural, and natural resources while strengthening local economies.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual management grants provided to the 13 certified heritage area management entities for management activities, marketing, and mini-grants to local organizations. Matching funds are required (specific percentages detailed in grant guidelines). Specific dollar amounts are not stated on this page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Certified heritage area management organizations in Maryland's 13 designated heritage areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Management activities, marketing, and mini-grants to local organizations within each heritage area.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to the 13 certified heritage areas covering all 23 Maryland counties and Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Organization must be certified by the Maryland Heritage Areas Authority (MHAA)
Must serve as the managing entity for one of the 13 designated Maryland heritage areas
Nonprofit status and tax-exempt documentation required
Matching funds required (specific percentages detailed in Grant Amounts and Matching Fund Requirements section of guidelines)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Heritage area management entities apply through the Maryland Heritage Areas Program. Application includes selection criteria and scoring rubric (Appendix A). Guidelines and budget templates are available on the program page.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program gives homeowners a state income tax credit for restoring historic houses. The credit is 20 percent of the project costs. The maximum credit is $50,000 over a 24-month period. You must spend at least $5,000 to qualify.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Homeowners can receive a state income tax credit for 20% of qualified repair costs. The credit is capped at $50,000 in a 24-month period. Projects must have at least $5,000 in eligible expenses.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Dana Marks Halpert, Carey L. Jones, or Kate Jaffe
structured_extraction.program_audience: This program is for homeowners who live in their single-family historic home, either as a primary or secondary residence.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used for projects that repair or alter a historic home while preserving its important features. Examples include: Roof repair or replacement; Chimney repair; Window restoration; New storm doors or windows; Masonry repointing; Floor refinishing; Structural repairs; Plumbing, electrical, and mechanical systems.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The home must be a certified historic structure. This means it is either listed in the National Register of Historic Places, is a contributing resource within a National Register Historic District, or is a locally designated structure that the Maryland Historical Trust determines is eligible for the National Register.
requirements_list: Must be a single-family, owner-occupied residence.
The building must be a certified historic structure.
Projects must have a minimum of $5,000 in eligible expenses.
All work must be reviewed and approved by the Maryland Historical Trust before starting.
The project must meet the Secretary of the Interior’s Standards for Rehabilitation.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, read the application instructions and contact tax credit staff for guidance. Second, download and complete the three-part application. Part 1 certifies that your home is a historic structure. Part 2 certifies that the proposed work meets program standards. Part 3 certifies that the completed project meets the standards and documents eligible expenses.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Historic Revitalization Tax Credit (Small Commercial)
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides a state income tax credit for restoring historic, income-producing properties. The credit equals 20% of the approved rehabilitation costs for projects with total expenses under $500,000. The program has a yearly funding cap of $2 million.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers a state income tax credit equal to 20 percent of qualified rehabilitation costs. Total project expenses cannot exceed $500,000. The credit is capped at $50,000 within a 24-month period. Projects must have at least $5,000 in eligible expenses to qualify. Projects in Opportunity Zones may receive additional credits.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling, on a first-come, first-served basis until the program cap is reached for the current fiscal year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: This program is for owners of certified historic structures that are used to produce income. This includes developers who plan to sell a rehabilitated property to a homeowner.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used for projects that repair or alter a historic structure for a modern use while preserving its significant features. Eligible work includes roof and chimney repair, window restoration, structural repairs, and updating plumbing, electrical, and mechanical systems. Funds cannot be used for landscaping, new construction, appliances, or tool purchases.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: To be eligible, a building must be a certified historic structure. This means it is listed on the National Register of Historic Places, is a contributing resource in a National Register Historic District, is a designated local historic structure, or is located within a certified heritage area.
requirements_list: The building must be a certified historic structure.
The building must be primarily income-producing, rehabilitated to be sold to a homeowner, or a targeted agricultural or post-WWII building.
Total qualified rehabilitation expenses must not exceed $500,000.
Projects must have a minimum of $5,000 in eligible expenses.
All project work must meet the Secretary of the Interior’s Standards for Rehabilitation.
The Maryland Historical Trust must review and approve all aspects of the project before work begins.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should contact program staff early in the planning process. The application has three parts. Part 1 certifies that the building is a historic structure. Part 2 certifies that the proposed project meets program requirements. Part 3 certifies that the completed project meets program requirements. Applicants must submit all parts for approval before starting work.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Historic Revitalization Tax Credit Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A Maryland state tax credit program that encourages the rehabilitation of certified historic properties (also referred to as certified heritage structures) for productive use. Owners of certified historic properties may earn a state income tax credit equal to 20% of qualified capital costs spent on rehabilitation, including energy improvements. The program offers three credit tracks: one for homeowners rehabilitating historic homes (credits capped at $50,000 in a 24-month period), one for owners of small commercial buildings with total rehabilitation costs under $500,000 (offering up to $50,000 in tax credits per 24-month period, with a yearly program funding cap of $2 million, to help strengthen communities and encourage local economic growth), and one for major/competitive commercial rehabilitations offering up to $5 million for substantial rehabilitations of income-producing historic properties. Properties must be listed on the National Register of Historic Places (individually or as contributing properties within a district) or locally designated as historic properties, and rehabilitation work must meet the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation. Eligible costs include plumbing, HVAC, electrical upgrades, kitchen and bathroom rehabilitation, appliances as part of an overall rehabilitation scheme, architectural and engineering fees, restoration of historic landscape features, and interior finishes. Work must be completed within a 24-month period per phase with a minimum cost threshold of $5,000 for owner-occupied residential projects, or the greater of the adjusted basis of the structure or $25,000 for competitive commercial projects. For small commercial projects, total qualified rehabilitation expenses must not exceed $500,000 and minimum eligible expenses must be at least $5,000. Properties within a designated Maryland heritage area may qualify for the credit based on individually listed historic properties, eligible-but-not-yet-listed historic buildings, or non-historic buildings certified by the Maryland Heritage Areas Authority as contributing to a heritage area. Projects in Opportunity Zones may receive additional credits. Applicants must apply before starting any renovations. The competitive commercial track requires electronic submission and MHT review/approval before work begins; projects awarded $1 million or more in tax credits must meet state corporate diversity requirements. The program supports community revitalization, job creation, smart growth, and environmental sustainability, and is reported to return $8.53 for every state dollar invested. It helps preserve Maryland's historic properties for future generations and encourages investment in historic neighborhoods. Non-profit developers receive full refunds of tax credits since they cannot utilize them directly.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Maryland state income tax credit equal to 20% of qualified capital costs spent on the rehabilitation of certified historic properties or certified heritage structures, including energy improvements. Three credit tracks exist: homeowner (for individuals rehabilitating historic homes, credits capped at $50,000 in a 24-month period), small commercial (for owners of small commercial buildings with total rehabilitation costs under $500,000, up to $50,000 per 24-month period, with a yearly program cap of $2 million; minimum $5,000 in eligible expenses required), and competitive commercial/major rehabilitation (for large-scale income-producing commercial projects, up to $5 million). Eligible costs include plumbing, HVAC, electrical systems, kitchen and bathroom rehabilitation, appliances as part of an overall rehabilitation scheme, architectural and engineering fees, restoration of historic landscape features, and interior finishes. Work must be completed within a 24-month period per phase. Minimum rehabilitation cost threshold is $5,000 for owner-occupied residential projects, or the greater of the adjusted basis of the structure or $25,000 for competitive commercial projects. Projects awarded $1 million or more in tax credits must meet state corporate diversity requirements. Properties within a designated Maryland heritage area may also qualify for a credit of up to 20% of eligible rehabilitation costs, which may be in addition to other available state tax credits. Projects in Opportunity Zones may receive additional credits. Applicants must apply before starting any renovations. The program reportedly returns $8.53 for every state dollar invested. Non-profit developers receive full refunds of tax credits since they cannot utilize them directly.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annually; contact program administrator. Small commercial track is rolling on a first-come, first-served basis until the program cap is reached for the current fiscal year. FY2026 application deadline to be updated when posted.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of certified historic properties or certified heritage structures in Maryland, including homeowners (single-family, owner-occupied), commercial property owners, developers, non-profits, and government entities rehabilitating historic structures for residential, commercial, or other productive uses; also owners of properties listed on the National Register of Historic Places (individually or as part of a district) or locally designated historic properties undertaking qualifying rehabilitation work, and property owners and developers undertaking rehabilitation work on historic or contributing properties within a Maryland heritage area. Includes developers who plan to sell a rehabilitated property to a homeowner. Non-profit organizations that rehabilitate historic properties may receive full refunds of tax credits.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Qualified rehabilitation expenditures and capital costs including energy improvements to certified historic properties or certified heritage structures; eligible rehabilitation costs including plumbing, HVAC, electrical systems, kitchen and bathroom work, appliances as part of an overall rehabilitation scheme, architectural/engineering/consultant fees, restoration of significant historic landscape features, and interior finishes such as wainscoting, mantles, molding, and plaster. Also includes roof repair or replacement, chimney repair, window restoration, new storm doors or windows, masonry repointing, floor refinishing, and structural repairs. New construction, financing charges, building permit fees, general landscaping, and tool purchases are not eligible. Rehabilitation and renovation of historic buildings for productive residential, commercial, and office purposes, including substantial rehabilitations of income-producing commercial historic properties; eligible rehabilitation costs for qualifying properties within Maryland heritage areas. Use of funds may also include LEED certification and green building elements, energy efficiency improvements, and adaptive reuse for mixed-use development including residential lofts, office space, retail, and arts-related uses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland, including communities such as Berlin, Cumberland, Easton, Frederick, Hagerstown, Salisbury, and Baltimore. Properties must be certified historic properties or certified heritage structures listed on the National Register of Historic Places (individually or as contributing properties within a district), designated local historic structures, or locally designated as historic properties. Properties located within a designated Maryland heritage area may qualify under the heritage area provisions. The property may also qualify by being a contributing resource in a historic district or being located in a Certified Heritage Area. Historically, Baltimore City has accounted for the highest concentration of awarded projects.
requirements_list: Must apply before any renovations are started
Property must be a certified historic property, structure, or certified heritage structure

Property must be listed on the National Register of Historic Places (individually or as a contributing property within a district), be a contributing resource in a National Register Historic District, be a designated local historic structure, or be located within a certified heritage area
Projects must meet the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation
Building must be a historic structure eligible for rehabilitation
Costs must be qualified capital costs for rehabilitation
Renovation work must meet applicable standards
Work must be completed within a 24-month period (projects may be phased)
Minimum rehabilitation cost of $5,000 for owner-occupied residential projects, or the greater of the adjusted basis of the structure or $5,000 for all other projects
For competitive commercial projects, eligible expenses must exceed the greater of the structure's adjusted basis value or $25,000
For small commercial track, total qualified rehabilitation expenses must not exceed $500,000 and minimum eligible expenses must be at least $5,000
Plans should be approved by MHT before work begins
Projects completed without prior approval must meet all Standards and be documented with before and after photographs
For competitive commercial track, all forms must be submitted electronically; contact MHT Tax Credit staff to set up a Microsoft Teams channel
Projects awarded $1 million or more in tax credits must meet state corporate diversity requirements

For heritage area eligibility: property must be individually listed or contributing to a historic district on the National Register of Historic Places, eligible for but not officially listed on the National Register, OR certified by the Maryland Heritage Areas Authority as contributing to the heritage area
Work must involve rehabilitation of the qualifying property
For homeowner track: must be a single-family, owner-occupied residence (primary or secondary)
For small commercial track: building must be primarily income-producing, rehabilitated to be sold to a homeowner, or a targeted agricultural or post-WWII building
Projects must involve previously used/historic buildings; new construction is not eligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Maryland Historical Trust before starting any renovations. Applicants should contact program staff early in the planning process. Submit both the federal and state tax credit application forms — the federal form must be fully completed; only the first sheet of each part of the state form needs to be filled out (remaining pages are identical to the federal form). For phased projects, the first application should describe all projected phases; later applications may amend the initial application. The competitive commercial track is a competitive program requiring electronic submission: contact MHT Tax Credit staff to set up a Microsoft Teams channel. The application has three parts: Part 1 certifies the building is historic; Part 2 describes the proposed project to certify it meets program requirements; Part 3 certifies that the completed work meets the requirements. All parts must be submitted and approved before starting work. For heritage area properties, visit the Maryland Historic Revitalization Tax Credit Program page at mht.maryland.gov for full details.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Historical Trust Capital Loans for Historic Preservation
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Historical Trust (MHT) offers low-interest capital loans to help preserve historic properties in Maryland. Eligible borrowers include nonprofits, local governments, business entities, and individuals who cannot access private financing. Funding is available for acquisition, refinancing, rehabilitation, stabilization, restoration, and predevelopment work on properties listed in or eligible for the National Register of Historic Places. Energy projects undertaken as part of a qualifying acquisition or rehabilitation are also eligible expenditures. Additionally, certain qualified cooperating nonprofit organizations may apply for a nonrepayable transfer of funds (similar to a grant) beginning in FY 2024, which can be used to acquire properties for resale, restore properties, or provide loans to other organizations and individuals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Fixed-rate capital loans at a rate equal to the most recent general obligation bond rate plus 0.125% (1/8 percent above the most recent State general obligation bonds). Nonprofits and local governments may receive an even lower rate. Loan terms are up to two years for predevelopment projects and up to twenty years for other projects. The loan amount depends on available funds, the borrower's ability to repay, and the property's value, typically not exceeding 80% of appraised value. A fee of $1,000 or 10% of the loan amount, whichever is less, is required. Funds can be used for acquisition, stabilization, rehabilitation, restoration, refinancing, or predevelopment work (plans, specifications, architectural/engineering services) on historic properties, as well as energy projects undertaken as part of a qualifying project. Recipients must convey a historic preservation easement to MHT on the funded property. Qualified cooperating nonprofit organizations may also apply for non-repayable fund transfers (grants) to acquire properties for resale, restore properties, or provide loans to other organizations and individuals.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Loan applications accepted year-round as funds become available; transfer applications open in November and close in January each year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations, local governments, business entities (that cannot obtain private financing), and individuals (that cannot obtain private financing) seeking to preserve historic properties. Qualified cooperating nonprofit organizations may also apply for nonrepayable fund transfers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquiring historic properties; refinancing existing loans; stabilizing, rehabilitating, or restoring historic properties; predevelopment work such as plans, specifications, and architectural or engineering services; and energy projects as part of a qualifying acquisition or rehabilitation project. Transfer funds for qualified nonprofits can be used to acquire properties for resale, restore properties, or provide loans to other organizations and individuals. Cannot be used for routine maintenance, fundraising, research, exhibits, or work already started or completed. Applicants are responsible for all fees (appraisal, survey, title, attorney, processing).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Eligible properties must be listed in or determined eligible for the National Register of Historic Places.
requirements_list: Property must be listed in or determined eligible for the National Register of Historic Places, individually or as part of a historic district.
Property must have historical and/or cultural significance.
Business entities and individuals must demonstrate they cannot obtain private financing.
Projects must comply with the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Treatment of Historic Properties (26 CFR 68) and Standards for Rehabilitation for preservation incentives.
Property owner permission must be provided as part of the loan application, including a letter from property owner(s) confirming support and willingness to convey preservation easement.
If funded, a historic preservation easement on the property must be conveyed to MHT.
Identification of all less-than-fee simple interests (mortgages, leases, mineral rights, reversionary interests) required.
Corporate resolution from authorized officer required for entities.
Personal Financial Statement required for proprietors, limited/general partners, 20%+ stockholders, or loan guarantors.
Complete financial disclosure (mortgage accounts, personal property, assets, unpaid taxes, other liabilities, life insurance).
Proof of good standing with Maryland SDAT (for entities).
501(c)(3) proof (for nonprofits).
Flash drive of project photos with descriptions.
Property location map with road intersections.
Architectural/engineering drawings or specifications.
Resumes of involved professionals.
Property Tax Bill (latest).
Fire and Extended Insurance Policy.
Mortgage/Notes outstanding on property documentation.
Deed to property.
Sales Contract (if acquisition).
Payment history on current loan (if refinancing).
Construction financing commitment letter(s) (if pre-development).
Financial statements (past three years for nonprofits/businesses).
Estimated Annual Operating Expense Statement (if income-producing).
Religious properties: loans can generally only fund structural or exterior work, not interior worship spaces or elements bearing religious imagery.
Cemeteries: applicant must demonstrate clear property ownership.
Applicant must contact MHT staff as a first step to discuss eligibility and available funding.
The project must show a public benefit to be competitive.
A fee of $1,000 or 10% of the loan amount, whichever is less, is required. A $250 application fee also applies.
Homeowner-occupied homes are generally not competitive unless they are exceptionally significant historically.
Nonrepayable transfer funds are only available to qualified cooperating nonprofit organizations (new beginning FY 2024).
Grant/loan agreements required.
Insurance requirements (Commercial General Liability, Flood Insurance).
Easement conveyance/modification documentation required.
Scope of work approval required.
RFP and bid solicitation process required.
Recognition of MHT support required.
Certify financial condition as of application date; false statements subject to criminal prosecution, fines up to $50,000, and/or imprisonment up to five years.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Contact MHT staff to discuss eligibility and funding availability (required first step). 2. Review program guidelines and manual. 3. Prepare and submit the appropriate application (loan or transfer) with required attachments including project description, financial statements, cost estimates, appraisal/report, evidence of public benefit if required, organizational documents, owner confirmation letter, corporate resolution, and personal financial statements (refer to Checklist of Attachments for complete documentation requirements). 4. If approved, MHT coordinates loan settlement, including scope of work approval, RFP preparation, bid solicitation, and loan closing procedures. The full process typically takes 6 to 9 months from application to settlement. Transfer applications open in November and close in January each year.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Museum Assistance Program (MAP) offers funding and technical assistance to help Maryland museums and institutional collections strengthen everyday operations, build professional capacity, and improve long-term sustainability. Grants support activities such as paying staff, training, administrative costs, environmental monitoring, and security systems. The program also promotes tourism, supports public education, and encourages professionalism within museum practice.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $20,000, typically between $10,000 and $15,000. In FY26, $285,000 was available statewide. No matching funds are required. Technical assistance and information are also provided.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations and local governments that operate a museum open for at least three years that interprets Maryland's cultural heritage, history, natural history, or history of science and technology. Museums operated by the state or federal government are not eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Everyday museum operations including staff salaries, staff and volunteer training, administrative costs (insurance, reporting, accounting), environmental monitoring (pest management, humidity control), and security and safety systems. Also supports projects that interpret Maryland's history, promote tourism, and provide public education. Capital projects such as construction, restoration, or building repairs are not eligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Applicant museums must interpret Maryland's cultural heritage, history, natural history, or history of science and technology.
requirements_list: Must be a nonprofit organization or local government
Must operate a museum that has been open and operating for at least three years
Nonprofit applicants must be in good standing with the state
Nonprofit applicants must be tax-exempt or have applied for tax-exempt status
Museum must collect, preserve, and interpret objects and materials for the public
Museum must interpret Maryland's cultural heritage, history, natural history, or history of science and technology
Museums operated in whole or in part by the state or federal government are not eligible
Each museum seeking funding must submit a separate application if the applicant operates more than one museum
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Review the current grant guidelines. 2. Confirm project eligibility and applicant type. 3. Prepare required attachments such as cost estimates, photographs, and proof of ownership or site control. 4. Submit a completed application through the MHT grants portal before the posted October deadline.

structured_extraction.program_description: Funded by the National Park Service and administered by the Maryland Historical Trust, this competitive grant program supports projects that protect historic maritime resources and increase public awareness of the nation's maritime heritage. Projects may focus on identifying maritime resources, repairing or rehabilitating historic maritime structures and vessels, or improving public access to maritime sites. All projects must include a public education component.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants between $10,000 and $100,000 are available. Total project costs must be between $20,000 and $200,000. A 1:1 non-federal match is required. Total program funding is $380,192. Grant funds cannot support work that has already started or been completed.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Tribal governments, state governments, local governments, and nonprofit organizations with projects that protect historic maritime resources and increase public awareness of maritime heritage.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Identification of historic maritime resources including archaeological sites; repair, rehabilitation, stabilization, maintenance, or limited reconstruction of historic maritime buildings, structures, vessels, and sites; improvements that increase public access to maritime resources. All projects must include a public education component.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is administered by the Maryland Historical Trust on behalf of the National Park Service. Projects must involve historic maritime resources.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a tribal government, state government, local government, or nonprofit organization
Project must demonstrate a clear public benefit
Project must follow the Secretary of the Interior's Standards and Guidelines for Archeology and Historic Preservation
Where applicable, project must follow the Standards for Historic Vessel Preservation Projects
Project must include a public education component

Project must support at least one eligible activity: identification of maritime resources, repair/rehabilitation/stabilization/maintenance or limited reconstruction of historic maritime resources, or improvements that increase public access
Total project costs must be between $20,000 and $200,000
A 1:1 non-federal match is required
Grant funds cannot support work that has already started or been completed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review the grant guidelines and manual for detailed requirements. Confirm applicant and project eligibility. Prepare a complete application including scope of work, budget, and required documentation. Submit through the grants portal before the June 1 deadline. Applicants are strongly encouraged to contact MHT staff early in project planning.

structured_extraction.program_description: A legal agreement between a property owner and the Maryland Historical Trust (MHT) that protects a property's historic character and ensures its long-term preservation. Property owners can voluntarily donate a preservation easement to MHT, or an easement may be required as a condition of certain MHT grants or loans. Through the easement, an owner agrees to preserve the property's historic features and obtain MHT approval before making specific changes. MHT reviews eligible properties and, if accepted, records a formal easement deed in county land records specifying which features are protected and what changes require approval. Easements are tied to the property — not the owner — and apply to all future owners during the easement period. Donated easements may qualify for federal charitable contribution tax deductions. Property owners are responsible for costs such as title work, surveys, and recording fees. Most easements are completed within several months to a year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MHT reviews and accepts preservation easements at no fee to the property owner. The easement is recorded in county land records and may provide the owner with potential federal tax deductions for charitable contributions. MHT staff also provide guidance and technical assistance on appropriate repairs, maintenance, and rehabilitation methods, and help with project planning. Property owners are responsible for costs such as title work, surveys, and recording fees. Easements may also be required as a condition of certain MHT grants or loans.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of historic properties in Maryland who wish to protect a property's historic character — particularly properties individually listed in or eligible for the National Register of Historic Places, or properties significant to Maryland's history, architecture, archaeology, or culture — as well as property owners required to convey an easement as a condition of an MHT grant or loan.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Long-term protection of historic buildings, structures, archaeological sites, maritime resources, and landscapes through a perpetual easement deed; potential federal tax deductions for donated easements; guidance and technical assistance on preservation practices.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland for eligible historic properties.
requirements_list: Property must be individually listed in or eligible for individual listing on the National Register of Historic Places, OR significant in Maryland's history, architecture, archaeology, or culture
Owner must agree to limit some development rights
Owner must maintain the property and protect its historic features
Owner must provide limited public access

Owner must obtain prior MHT approval before making changes or alterations, including construction, reconstruction, improvement, enlargement, alteration, demolition, maintenance, repair, painting/changing material finishes, grading, and landscape or site changes
Owner must submit a letter expressing desire to donate an easement
Owner must provide supporting information such as property description, history, maps, and photographs for MHT review
Easement is tied to the property and binds all future owners for the duration of the easement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Property owners may donate or convey an easement to MHT voluntarily, or an easement may be required as a condition of certain MHT grants or loans. To donate voluntarily, submit a letter to MHT expressing your desire to donate an easement along with supporting information about the property (description, history, maps, photographs). MHT reviews the submission and decides whether to accept. If accepted, MHT prepares a draft easement deed for your review. After both parties approve, the easement is signed, executed, and recorded in county land records. Visit the 'Donate or Convey an Easement' page for full eligibility requirements and documentation. Contact the Easement Program staff with questions.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Excise Tax Credit for Zero-Emission Plug-In Electric and Fuel Cell Electric Vehicles
structured_extraction.program_description: A Maryland state excise tax credit that reduces the excise tax owed when purchasing a qualifying zero-emission plug-in electric or fuel cell electric vehicle. The credit is administered through the Maryland Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA) at the time of vehicle registration, and is subject to available funding.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: $3,000 excise tax credit for the purchase of a qualifying zero-emission plug-in electric or fuel cell electric vehicle, applied at the time of registration through the Maryland MVA. Subject to available funding.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents and businesses purchasing qualifying zero-emission plug-in electric or fuel cell electric vehicles
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of excise tax owed on the purchase of a qualifying zero-emission plug-in electric or fuel cell electric vehicle
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Must purchase a qualifying zero-emission plug-in electric or fuel cell electric vehicle
Subject to available funding
Administered through the Maryland MVA at vehicle registration
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Maryland Motor Vehicle Administration when registering the vehicle. For more information, contact MVA at https://mymva.maryland.gov/TAP/IND/?link=ContactMVA.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Small Business Development Center (SBDC) Business Counseling, Training, and Consulting
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Small Business Development Center (SBDC) offers free or low-cost one-on-one business counseling, consulting, and professional training programs to aspiring entrepreneurs and existing small to mid-sized business owners statewide, including farmers. Through local offices serving all Maryland counties — including three regional counselors hosted by AAEDC in Anne Arundel County (with a bilingual Spanish-speaking counselor available), a Southern Region office in Prince Frederick serving Calvert, Charles, and St. Mary's counties, and a local office in Harford County — SBDC advisors guide clients through the steps needed to start or expand a business. Counseling and advisory services cover business plan development, financing and loan packaging, financial analysis, money management, marketing plans, accounting, website and SEO review, workforce development, procurement and contracting guidance, exporting and importing support, market research, technology commercialization, strategic planning, permits and licenses, business valuation, equity funding development, feasibility studies, needs assessments, management information systems, and MBE/WBE/WOSB/DBE/SBE/8(a) certification assistance. Topics also include legal compliance and tax issues. Low-cost or no-cost workshops and professional training programs are offered, ranging from introductory start-up guidance to executive-level training in money management and marketing. Training events are listed on the SBDC online calendar. All services are confidential. Clients must be legally present in the United States.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free (no-cost), confidential, individualized business counseling and consulting covering business plan development, financial analysis and loan packaging, money management, marketing plans, accounting, website and SEO review, workforce development, procurement and contracting guidance, market research, technology commercialization, start-up guidance, strategic planning, permits and licenses, business valuation, equity funding development, feasibility studies, needs assessments, management information systems, legal compliance, tax issues, and certification assistance (MBE/WBE/WOSB/DBE/SBE/8(a)). Low-cost or no-cost professional training workshops and programs are also available, with events listed on the SBDC online calendar. Services are delivered through local SBDC offices statewide, including three regional counselors hosted at the AAEDC office in Annapolis serving Anne Arundel County (a bilingual Spanish-speaking counselor is available), a Southern Region office in Prince Frederick serving Calvert, Charles, and St. Mary's counties, and a local office serving Harford County.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Aspiring entrepreneurs, new or existing small to mid-sized business owners at any stage of development, and new farmers who are legally present in the United States and located anywhere in Maryland — from those thinking about starting a business to established business executives — including Spanish-speaking business owners. Served across all Maryland counties including Anne Arundel, Calvert, Charles, St. Mary's, Harford, and all others.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable — technical assistance, advisory services, and training, not funding. Assistance covers business counseling and guidance for starting or expanding a business, including business planning, financial analysis, money management, marketing, accounting, website review, legal compliance, tax issues, certification guidance, strategic planning, business valuation, feasibility studies, and professional training programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland. Must be an aspiring entrepreneur or existing business owner (or new farmer) in Maryland

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Residencies, workshops, assemblies, and professional development by teaching artists for students birth through grade 12
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland public schools serving PreK-12 students and early childhood sites statewide

Subsidizes 50%-80% of total costs; schools are responsible for remaining costs

structured_extraction.program_description: A one-time grant that supports fully developed and ready-to-implement public art projects in Maryland that celebrate America's 250th anniversary (Semiquincentennial). Eligible projects include conservation of existing works or creation and installation of new works such as murals, mosaics, paintings, or sculptures by Maryland-based artists.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time grant funding for public art projects aligned with America250 goals. Awarded funds may cover administrative fees (up to 15% of total request), artist fees and labor for Maryland-based artists and fabricators, materials, contracted services and equipment rental, studio or space rental, signage or plaques, and dedication event expenses.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland-based nonprofit organizations (501(c)3), units of state or local government, and colleges or universities seeking to support public art projects that celebrate America's 250th anniversary.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Administrative fees (up to 15%), artist fees and labor for Maryland-based artists and fabricators, materials (artwork, base, lighting, landscaping), contracted services and equipment rental, studio or space rental to fabricate and assemble artwork, signage or plaques, and dedication event expenses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Project must be located in Maryland and created by a Maryland-based artist, artisan, studio, or team. Applicant organization must be Maryland-based.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Maryland-based nonprofit (IRS 501(c)3), unit of state or local government, or college/university
Project must be located in Maryland
Artwork must be created by a Maryland-based artist, artisan, studio, or team
Project must be fully developed and ready for immediate implementation
Artwork concept must be finalized with all required permits and site permissions acquired
Project must be entering initial stages of implementation and able to complete and fully install by June 30, 2026
Artwork must be an architectural enhancement of artistic significance or an installation (e.g., mural, tile mosaic, painting, or sculpture)
Artwork must fit within MSAC's definition of Public Art
Clear, specific project description aligned with America250 goals
Site-responsive artwork and community engagement
Demonstrated artistic excellence and merit
Lead artist and team with proven experience delivering safe, durable public artworks
Realistic timeline for completion within required timeframe
Financially sound budget

Applications must be submitted electronically with an electronic signature. Technical support for SmartSimple is available during regular office hours. Applications are scored on a rubric across 5 criteria (each 1-10 points). All grantees must file a final report in SmartSimple by September 1, 2026.
