structured_extraction.program_description: The A&E District Designation program allows Maryland county and municipal governments to designate specific geographic areas as Arts & Entertainment Districts. Designated districts receive tax incentives and other tools to encourage arts activity and investment as part of a local economic development strategy. The designation supports coordination with local economic development plans and policies, and arts and entertainment must be a component of the area's economic development approach.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Designated districts receive tax incentives (tax credits and tax exemptions) and other tools to encourage arts activity and investment within the designated geographic area. The designation also supports coordination with local economic development plans and policies.
structured_extraction.program_audience: County and municipal governments in Maryland seeking to designate a geographic area as an Arts & Entertainment District to promote arts-based economic development.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax incentives and tools to encourage arts activity, entertainment venues, arts businesses, and investment within the designated district as part of an economic development strategy.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be located within designated Priority Funding Areas in Maryland. Applicants must be a county or municipal government in Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a county or municipal government in Maryland
The proposed district must be a geographic area with a significant level of arts activity, entertainment venues, and/or arts businesses
Arts and entertainment must be included in the area's economic development strategy
Applicant must communicate with all municipalities and counties involved and obtain agreement from all impacted governments concerning tax credits
Applicant must complete an Intent to Apply form online at least 90 days before the chosen application deadline
District must be located within a designated Priority Funding Area
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, contact MSAC staff to begin the process. Then communicate with all impacted governments and obtain agreement on tax credits. Complete the Intent to Apply form online at least 90 days before the chosen deadline (April 1 or October 1). Submit a full application as specified in the A&E District Designation Guidelines. Applications are reviewed by MSAC staff for completeness, then by the MSAC A&E Districts Advisory Committee (which includes representatives from the departments of Commerce, Housing & Community Development, Transportation, and Planning), and finally decided by the Maryland Secretary of Commerce.

structured_extraction.program_name: Arts & Entertainment (A&E) Districts - Operating Support Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: Develops, promotes, and supports diverse artistic and cultural centers in communities throughout Maryland that preserve a sense of place, provide unique local experiences, attract tourism, and spur economic revitalization and neighborhood pride. Annual operating grants from the Maryland State Arts Council (MSAC) support activities, programs, and projects in designated Arts & Entertainment (A&E) Districts throughout Maryland. Appointed management entities for these districts can apply for funds to support district priorities, including activities, programs, and projects that advance the goals of the designated A&E District.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual operating grants are awarded to appointed management entities of designated A&E Districts. Grants are $15,000. Payment is processed within 6–8 weeks of executing the grant agreement. Grantees must submit a final report at the end of the funded fiscal year. Funds may be used for operations and administration, programs or projects, and in-kind support including district promotion, event/festival production, business attraction, artist support services, public art projects, real estate promotion, partnership management, fundraising, board management, and advocacy.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Appointed management entities of designated Arts & Entertainment Districts in Maryland, including nonprofit 501(c)(3) organizations and local government entities, whose A&E District designation has been approved by the Secretary of Commerce
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Support district priorities including activities, programs, and projects within designated A&E Districts; operations and administration; programs or projects funding; in-kind support; district promotion; event/festival production; business attraction; artist support services; public art projects; real estate promotion; partnership management; fundraising; board management; advocacy
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to management entities of designated A&E Districts located throughout Maryland, where the designation has been approved by the Secretary of Commerce
requirements_list: Must be the appointed management entity of a designated A&E District in Maryland
Must complete a signed Letter of Agreement to apply
Must complete a letter of agreement between the county or municipality holding the designation and the management entity
Must have a current contract or MOU with a county or municipality to manage a designated A&E District (if management entity is a 501(c)(3) non-profit)
Must be a nonprofit 501(c)(3) organization or local government entity
Must maintain a Board of Directors or Advisory Board of at least 5 individuals representing diversity of populations and constituencies served
Must have at least one paid employee working a minimum of 15 hours per week coordinating district activities
Local government must provide financial and/or in-kind support
Must work to meet A&E Districts Program goals
Must work to meet district-specific goals from designation/redesignation/application
Adhere to MSAC grantmaking, crediting, and reporting requirements
Maintain equitable, community-responsive programs and events
Maintain website/webpage with district information and MSAC links
Maintain constituent distribution list and send regular communications promoting district and MSAC opportunities
Maintain current profile on MSAC website
Notify MSAC two months ahead of local grant opportunities for artists
Provide ongoing updates of local needs through scheduled reports
Arrange at least one annual site visit for MSAC
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The management entity submits either an On-Year application (in the fifth fiscal year post-designation, including updated goals, objectives, strategies, outcomes, management and marketing plans, and a proposed budget) or an Off-Year application (all other years, a shorter application with proposed budget and any updates). The A&E Districts Advisory Committee reviews on-year applications and recommends funding; MSAC staff reviews off-year applications. Funding recommendations are subject to approval by the Council and the Secretary of Commerce.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Arts & Entertainment (A&E) Districts program offers tax-related incentives to encourage arts activity, economic revitalization, and community development in 29 designated arts districts across Maryland's towns and cities. Incentives include a local property tax credit for property owners who renovate for use by qualifying artists or arts enterprises, an income tax subtraction modification for qualifying resident artists who sell artistic work within a district, and a local admissions and amusement tax exemption for arts and entertainment enterprises operating in a district.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Three tax incentives are available: (1) Property Tax Credit — property owners who renovate commercial, manufacturing, or industrial property for use by qualifying artists or arts enterprises may receive a local property tax credit based on the difference between pre- and post-renovation assessments; the amount, duration, and application process are set by the local government. (2) Artist Income Tax Subtraction Modification — qualifying resident artists (who live in Maryland, conduct a business in an A&E district, and earn income from selling or performing original artistic work within a district) may subtract that qualifying income from their Maryland state taxable income by filing Form 502AE with their annual state tax return; there is no cap on the amount that can be subtracted. (3) Admissions & Amusement Tax Exemption — local governments may exempt arts and entertainment enterprises and qualifying resident artists from the admissions and amusement tax on gross receipts in an A&E district.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners, qualifying resident artists (individuals who live in Maryland, conduct an arts business in an A&E district, and earn income from original artistic work created and sold within a district), and arts and entertainment enterprises (for-profit or nonprofit entities dedicated to creating, selling, or sharing artistic work) located in one of Maryland's 29 designated A&E Districts.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax relief on property renovations for arts use, reduction of state income tax on qualifying artistic income, and exemption from local admissions and amusement taxes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in any of Maryland's 29 designated Arts & Entertainment Districts located in towns and cities across the state.
requirements_list: For the property tax credit: property must be manufacturing, commercial, or industrial and wholly or partially renovated for use by a qualifying residing artist or arts and entertainment enterprise; local government sets specific requirements.

For the income tax subtraction modification: artist must own or rent residential property in Maryland; must conduct a business in an A&E district; must earn income from the sale or performance of original artistic work created and sold within an A&E district; must file Form 502AE with their Maryland individual income tax return.

Artistic work must be original and creative and fall within the defined categories (writing, plays, music, visual art, sculpture, crafts, film, dance, jewelry/clothing design, storytelling, digital/new media, etc.).
Work must be created within an A&E district and sold within an A&E district (internet sales are eligible if shipped from within the district).
Only independent individual artists and sole proprietors qualify for the income tax subtraction modification; employees of organizations do not qualify.
Royalties, licenses, and revenue from publishing or reproduction rights do not qualify for the income tax subtraction modification.
Industry-related work (produced at large volume or for commercial purposes) does not qualify.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For the income tax subtraction modification, qualifying artists file Form 502AE with their annual Maryland individual income tax return. For the property tax credit, contact the district manager for the specific A&E district to learn about the local application process. For the admissions and amusement tax exemption, contact the State Comptroller's Office.

structured_extraction.program_description: State capital project grants for eligible Maryland arts organizations to improve or build a complete, usable, and accessible arts facility. The program supports expanding, producing, renovating, or making major repairs to a facility or its infrastructure. The Maryland General Assembly allocated $3,000,000 per year for six years (FY24–FY29) for this program, with individual grants ranging from $50,000 to $500,000.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State capital funding grants ranging from $50,000 to $500,000, distributed from $3,000,000 allocated annually (FY24–FY29) for projects that improve or produce a complete, usable, and accessible arts facility.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland-based 501(c)(3) non-profit arts organizations with annual operating budgets below $3,000,000 that own or lease a physical property in Maryland, and are either open to the public and provide arts-based cultural education or experiences, or participate in MSAC's Grants for Organizations or County Arts Development programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital projects that improve or produce a complete, usable, and accessible arts facility, including expanding, producing, renovating, or making major repairs to a facility or its infrastructure.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be based in Maryland and the project facility must be located in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a 501(c)(3) non-profit organization
Must be based in Maryland
Annual operating budget must be below $3,000,000
Must operate a physical property in Maryland that is either leased or owned
Must either participate in MSAC's Grants for Organizations or County Arts Development programs, or be open to the public and provide arts-based cultural education or experiences
Must provide proof of property ownership or a lease agreement with at least five years remaining at the time of application
Previous grantees must have completed their prior projects and submitted final reports before re-applying
Cannot have received $500,000 in Arts Capital funds within a five-year period
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First-time applicants should contact program staff before applying. All organizations apply through the SmartSimple online system. A statewide panel reviews all applications. The Maryland State Arts Council (MSAC) will notify all applicants of their decision electronically.

structured_extraction.program_name: Arts in Education (AiE) Teaching Artist Roster
structured_extraction.program_description: A panel-reviewed roster of Maryland-based teaching artists who provide group or classroom arts instruction and/or performances in educational settings. Artists approved for the roster become eligible to apply for Arts in Education (AiE) grants that fund teaching artist fees at Maryland schools and community groups. The roster includes artists and organizations offering residencies, workshops, visiting performances, professional development, out-of-school time programs, online programs, and lecture/demonstrations across multiple disciplines (theater, music, dance, visual arts, literary arts, media arts, storytelling, multidisciplinary).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Approved teaching artists are listed on the MSAC Teaching Artist Roster, making them eligible to receive funding through the Arts in Education Grant program (a separate application). Benefits include connections to a statewide professional development network, individualized feedback and evaluation sessions, and visibility through the MSAC Arts Directory. Teaching artists are evaluated on a rubric covering: arts discipline background and experience, lesson plan quality with Maryland State standards connections, artistic inspirations informing instruction, commitment to diversity/equity/justice, commitment to inclusion/accessibility, and recorded live instruction/performance capability. Arts learning activity types include: Workshop (focused arts learning on specific topic or skill, 1-2 days), Residency (multi-session arts learning building knowledge and skills over time, may include culminating project), Out of School Time Program (arts learning before or after normal school hours), Lecture/Lecture Demonstration (presentation sharing deep knowledge with possible demonstrations), Visiting Performance (arts performance delivered to audience at designated location), Field Trip (audience travels to venue for arts experience), and Online Program (virtual arts learning, asynchronous, synchronous, or blended).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Currently paused for new applications; check back for updates in Spring 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland-based independent teaching artists and arts organizations (nonprofits, government units, and University System of Maryland institutions) who provide arts education programming in school and community settings, serving students, school-based and community audiences at schools, recreation centers, senior centers, theaters, and museums
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Roster membership qualifies teaching artists to apply for AiE grants that cover teaching artist fees for residencies, workshops, performances, and other arts education programming in schools and community groups.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be Maryland residents (owning or renting residential property in Maryland for at least six months prior to application). Organizations must be incorporated in Maryland or be a Maryland government unit or University System of Maryland member institution.
requirements_list: Independent artists must be Maryland residents (owning or renting residential property in Maryland six months prior to application) and at least 18 years old
Ensembles or collaborative groups must be composed of artists 18 or older, with at least 50% meeting the residency requirement
Applicants must not be enrolled in any high school, undergraduate, or graduate degree program at time of application
Artists must remain Maryland residents while active on the roster and during any funded AiE grant activities
Organizations must be a 501(c)3 incorporated in Maryland, a Maryland government unit, or a University System of Maryland member institution
Organizations must have at least one completed and documented fiscal year with ongoing arts activities at the time of application
Organizations applying on behalf of multiple teaching artists must submit a separate application for each artist
Applicants must demonstrate teaching artist experience and provide lesson plans with Maryland State standards connections
Applicants must demonstrate commitment to diversity/equity/justice and inclusion/accessibility in their arts education practice
Applicants must provide a recorded demonstration of live instruction or performance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are reviewed by a panel using a rubric covering arts discipline experience, lesson plan quality with state standards connections, artistic inspirations, diversity/equity/justice commitment, inclusion/accessibility practices, and live instruction/performance capability. Applicants must submit information on their arts training and experience, examples of arts education programs (workshops, residencies, performances, etc.), answers to questions about inspirations, values, and ability to adapt to different learning styles, and a sample recording of arts education instruction or performance. Applicants are encouraged to schedule a virtual meeting or attend office hours with AiE staff before applying. The program is currently paused for new applications.

structured_extraction.program_description: Arts in Education grants provide funds to teaching artists on the Maryland State Arts Council (MSAC) Teaching Artist Roster to support arts education engagements at Maryland-based schools, nonprofit organizations, and other government entities. The program strengthens and promotes lifelong learning in the arts by supporting teaching artists to lead educational activities in schools and communities across Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to a maximum of $6,000 (final amount depends on the applicant's request) fund teaching artists to implement arts education activities in school and community settings including schools, libraries, community centers, detention centers, and other nonprofit or government locations. Individual lead artists may receive a maximum of $21,000 in grant awards for FY 2026; teaching artist organizations may receive a maximum of $84,000 for FY 2026.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications are accepted on a rolling basis between July 2025 and January 2026. Deadlines: September 5, 2025; November 5, 2025; January 5, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Teaching artists listed on the Maryland State Arts Council's (MSAC) Teaching Artist Roster who collaborate with Maryland schools, nonprofit organizations, or government entities to lead arts education activities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supporting teaching artists to implement arts education programs in Maryland schools, libraries, community centers, detention centers, and other nonprofit or government locations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland.
requirements_list: The teaching artist must be on the MSAC Teaching Artist Roster.
The collaborating school or community site must be a 501(c)3 nonprofit, a unit of government, or a college/university in Maryland.
The collaborating site must have operated for at least one full fiscal year with ongoing arts activities.
A school or community site may participate in up to two grants per fiscal year.
Individual lead artists may receive a maximum of $21,000 in grant awards for FY 2026.
Teaching artist organizations may receive a maximum of $84,000 in grant awards for FY 2026.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, the teaching artist and the school or organization agree to collaborate on services, timelines, and fees. Second, the school or organization identifies a coordinator for the project. Third, the teaching artist or their affiliated organization starts and submits the application online using SmartSimple. A panel then reviews applications, and the applicant receives a notification the following month.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Percent-for-Art program that reserves a portion of construction budgets for new, permanent, site-specific artworks in state-owned buildings. The Maryland State Arts Council (MSAC) manages each commission project from artist selection through installation, and completed works join the State's public art collection. For capital projects, 0.05% of construction costs are set aside to acquire public artwork. Artists apply once to the roster; staff pulls groups of 60-100 artists per project for consideration. The roster is the primary method for selecting artists for projects with budgets from $50,000 to $1,500,000.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 0.05% of the estimated construction cost of each new or renovated state building is set aside to commission or purchase site-specific original artwork. Artists contract directly with the state government unit responsible for the project. Projects range from $50,000 to $1,500,000. There are currently 17 active commissions across the state with over $5.5 million in artist contracts. Works become part of the State of Maryland's Public Art Collection. Commissions typically last two to five years depending on project scale and construction timeline.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Artists and artist-led teams, studios, or collectives who are residents of the United States and its territories interested in creating permanent public art for Maryland state buildings.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Creating and installing permanent, large-scale, publicly accessible artworks integrated into the construction or renovation of eligible state buildings.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Artworks are placed in state-owned buildings across Maryland. Artists must be U.S. residents but are not required to be Maryland residents (though a Maryland-based studio label is available on the roster).
requirements_list: Must be a resident of the United States or its territories
Must be an independent artist or lead artist of an artist-led team, studio, or collective with original work
Must join the Maryland Public Artist Roster or respond to an open call (Request for Qualifications) for individual projects
Selected artists contract directly with the state government unit responsible for the building project
Must work directly with the project design team to integrate artwork into the project
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Artists apply to join the Maryland Public Artist Roster (2026-2028) when it is open. The roster application deadline is June 30, 2025. An Artist Selection Committee reviews candidates from the roster for each project, with staff pulling groups of 60-100 artists per project for consideration. MSAC may also issue open calls (Requests for Qualifications) for specific projects, which are posted on the program page.

structured_extraction.program_description: County Arts Development (CAD) grants support Maryland's county arts agencies, helping them extend the reach of the Maryland State Arts Council (MSAC) by funding and strengthening local arts activities across all 24 Maryland jurisdictions. The program supports county arts agencies in connecting with artists, arts organizations, and local communities, encourages local arts activities, and provides equitable funding for the arts at the county level.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MSAC provides formula-based grant funding and technical assistance to county arts agencies to help them meet their local arts goals, support artists and arts organizations, and promote equitable and accessible arts programming within their jurisdictions. Funds support the operations of county arts agencies, including their own grant-making activities and other programs that serve local artists, arts organizations, and audiences.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland's designated county arts agencies — government offices and non-profit organizations supporting local arts in each of Maryland's 24 jurisdictions (23 counties and Baltimore City).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supporting local arts activities, providing financial and technical support to artists and arts organizations, promoting equitable arts programming within each county jurisdiction, and funding the operations and grant-making activities of county arts agencies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to the officially designated arts agency or council for each of Maryland's 23 counties and Baltimore City — all 24 Maryland jurisdictions.
requirements_list: Must be a designated county arts agency (government office or non-profit) for one of Maryland's 24 jurisdictions
Must be a local agency or nonprofit designated by the jurisdiction's government as the official arts agency or council
Must support local arts activities and equitable funding processes
Must engage with MSAC's network of county arts agencies
Submit an application annually, which will be either a detailed three-year plan ('On-Year') or a shorter update ('Off-Year')
Grantees must submit interim and annual final reports detailing the use of funds
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Designated county arts agencies submit one of two types of applications each year. Every three years, an agency submits an 'On-Year' application with a detailed three-year plan. MSAC staff and a review panel review a draft and provide feedback. The agency revises the plan and submits it for final Council approval. In the two years between, the agency submits a simpler 'Off-Year' application noting any changes to the three-year plan and including required financial reports. See the full program page at https://www.msac.org/programs/county-arts-development/county-arts-development-grant for application details.

structured_extraction.program_description: Funds a mentor artist and an apprentice artist to work together for one year, with the mentor passing down knowledge of a living cultural tradition in Maryland.

Funding supports mentor and apprentice artist compensation, teaching materials, and travel expenses. Total project expenses must equal at least $5,000. Payment is processed within 6-8 weeks of executing the grant agreement. Grantees must submit a final report upon completion.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supporting a one-year apprenticeship in which a mentor artist teaches an apprentice artist a traditional cultural art form, covering logistical, financial, and cultural aspects of the apprenticeship. Eligible expenses include mentor artist compensation, apprentice artist compensation, teaching materials, and travel. Minimum total expenses of $5,000 required.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Apprentice artists must be Maryland residents. Mentor artists must be U.S. residents or residents of a U.S. territory and demonstrate vital contributions to a living cultural tradition in Maryland. Out-of-state mentor artists are permitted if the desired skillset is unavailable in Maryland.
requirements_list: Mentor artist must be a resident of the United States or a U.S. territory
Mentor artist must demonstrate vital contributions to a particular living cultural tradition in Maryland
Mentor artist must demonstrate extensive expertise and public/community recognition
Apprentice artist must be a Maryland resident
Apprentice artist must demonstrate some prior experience, a basic level of skill, and a commitment to long-term learning in a particular traditional art
Apprentice artist must show a clear trajectory of past accomplishments
If mentor artist resides out of state, apprentice must demonstrate the desired skillset is unavailable in Maryland
Apprentice artists younger than 18 must provide contact information and e-signature of a parent or guardian
Folklife form must demonstrate a strong connection to a cultural community over a generational period
Apprenticeship must contribute cultural, practical, and artistic value to the tradition
Work plan must be clear with specific activities, materials, dates, and locations
Total project expenses must equal at least $5,000
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application through SmartSimple including narrative answers describing the cultural history and current community practice of the traditional art, biographical information for both artists, a work plan with logistical, financial, and cultural details, and optional supplemental written or audiovisual materials. Applicants may also upload an audio or video recording answering narrative questions instead of written responses. Applications are evaluated using a scoring rubric across 5 criteria: traditional nature of the art form, mentor expertise, apprentice preparedness, impact on tradition vitality, and work plan feasibility.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides general operating support to nonprofit and tax-exempt organizations, units of government, and colleges and universities that produce or present ongoing arts programming open to the public in Maryland. GFO grants help sustain Maryland's arts infrastructure, create future audiences, uplift communities, and stimulate economic impact across the state. In FY 2025, MSAC awarded $18,136,157 to 309 arts organizations. Grant amounts are determined by a tiered funding formula based on the organization's budget size, with maximum grant caps being phased down over five years: $1.4M (FY24), $1.3M (FY25), $1.2M (FY26), $1.1M (FY27), and $1M (FY28). Cap allocations as a percentage of allowable expenses by budget tier (fully phased in by FY28): Tier 1 ($50K–$500K) = 15%, Tier 2 ($500K–$1.5M) = 10%, Tier 3 ($1.5M–$5M) = 6%, Tier 4 ($5M–$10M) = 4.5%, Tier 5 ($10M+) = 4%. Organizations that did not receive GFO funding in the previous fiscal year must first submit an Intent to Apply form by September 15 annually to determine eligibility before completing a full grant application by November 15.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: General operating support grants. Grant amounts are determined by a tiered funding formula based on the organization's budget size. In FY 2025, MSAC awarded $18,136,157 to 309 arts organizations across Maryland. Maximum grant caps are being phased down over five years: $1.4M (FY24), $1.3M (FY25), $1.2M (FY26), $1.1M (FY27), and $1M (FY28). Cap allocations as a percentage of allowable expenses by budget tier (fully phased in by FY28): Tier 1 ($50K–$500K) = 15%, Tier 2 ($500K–$1.5M) = 10%, Tier 3 ($1.5M–$5M) = 6%, Tier 4 ($5M–$10M) = 4.5%, Tier 5 ($10M+) = 4%. Grant funds are distributed in full after the Grant Agreement Form and required reports are submitted. New applicants must first submit an Intent to Apply form by September 15 annually, and if found eligible, complete a full application by November 15.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Intent to Apply form due September 15 annually; GFO application due November 15
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit arts organizations, units of local government, and colleges and universities that produce or present ongoing public arts programming in Maryland, including new applicants that did not receive GFO funding in the most recent fiscal year.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: General operating support for arts organizations and programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be incorporated in Maryland as a nonprofit or have a significant physical presence in Maryland. The majority of arts activities must take place in Maryland and most annual expenditures must be devoted to activities within Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a nonprofit, tax-exempt organization, unit of government, or college/university
Produce or present the arts to the public through ongoing arts programming
Have 501(c)3 tax-exempt status from the IRS at time of application (except units of local government and colleges and universities)
Be incorporated in Maryland as a nonprofit or have significant physical presence in Maryland
Have operated as an arts organization or arts program for one full fiscal year and be able to submit a financial statement for the most recently completed fiscal year
Majority of arts activities must take place in Maryland and most annual expenditures devoted to in-state activities
Be governed by a legally-liable board of directors acting under a mission statement and budget specific to the organization
Must obtain a Unique Entity ID (UEI) from SAM.gov
New applicants or organizations that did not receive a GFO grant in the most recent funding cycle must complete an Intent to Apply form by September 15 annually
If found eligible after Intent to Apply review, must complete a standard GFO application by November 15
Organization must not have received FY 2026 GFO funding to be considered a new applicant

Must be classified as either an Arts Organization (primary mission is producing or presenting arts through public programs/services) or an Arts Program (primary mission is other than arts, but provides ongoing arts programming/activities)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: New applicants or organizations not funded in the most recent cycle must submit an Intent to Apply form by September 15 annually to determine eligibility. After eligibility is determined, organizations complete a GFO application by November 15. All applicants need a Unique Entity ID (UEI) from SAM.gov. Applications are reviewed by a panel of diverse experts from across Maryland. Review the guidelines document and available webinar resources before applying (including the FY27 'How to Apply' Webinar). Starting FY 2027, a four-year application cycle will be implemented; organizations will have an annual conversation with a GFO program director and one site visit by a public panelist. Contact the Program Director if uncertain about Arts Organization vs. Arts Program classification.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Heritage Awards recognize long-term achievement in the traditional arts by people, places, and traditions located in Maryland, honoring individuals, places, and traditions that represent living cultural traditions and folklife connected to Maryland communities. Each year, six winners are selected across three categories: Person/People, Place, or Tradition. Each award winner receives a $10,000 grant they can use at their discretion. The program is administered by the Maryland State Arts Council as part of the Maryland Traditions program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Each award winner receives a $10,000 grant to use at their discretion. Payment is processed within 6-8 weeks after the grant agreement is signed. Grantees must submit a final report at the end of the funded project. Nominations are evaluated on: identification of a living cultural tradition connected to a community of origin, the nominee's importance to the cultural community, and the nominee's sustained engagement with folklife (scored using a rubric: Excellent 17-20 points, Good 13-16 points, Fair 9-12 points, Poor 8 or fewer points).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals, places, and traditions in Maryland representing living cultural traditions and folklife connected to Maryland communities, including performers, artists, community leaders, cultural sites, and recurring cultural practices that demonstrate long-term achievement in the traditional arts.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: At the grantee's discretion.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Nominees must be people, places, or traditions located in Maryland.
requirements_list: Nominees must be people, places, or traditions located in Maryland.
Nominees must demonstrate long-term achievement in the traditional arts.
Nomination must identify a living cultural tradition connected to a cultural community of origin.
Nominee must demonstrate importance to the current community participating in the folklife.
Nominee must show sustained engagement with the folklife over time.
Eligible categories: Person/People, Place, or Tradition.
Awards are not given posthumously.
A person, place, or tradition may receive the award only once.
Self-nominations are accepted.
Nominators may reside anywhere and must provide contact information.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a nomination through MSAC's online grants management system SmartSimple. First-time users must create a profile. Nominators complete prompts describing the nominee's long-term achievement in the traditional arts and may include optional supplemental materials. Nominations are scored on three criteria using a rubric (Excellent 17-20 points, Good 13-16 points, Fair 9-12 points, Poor 8 or fewer points). Contact State Folklorist Ryan Koons to have a draft reviewed before submission.

structured_extraction.program_description: Poetry Out Loud is a national arts education program, a partnership between the National Endowment for the Arts and the Poetry Foundation, that encourages high school students (grades 9-12) to study great poetry through recitation competitions. Students memorize and recite poems from an official online anthology of 1,200+ poems. They compete at the classroom, school, regional, state, and national levels, with winners advancing to national finals in Washington, DC. The program builds public speaking skills, self-confidence, social and emotional maturity, analytical skills, and a lifelong love of poetry. It aligns with Common Core Standards and National Core Arts Standards and is free with materials available online.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Monetary prizes are awarded to students who place 1st and 2nd at the state level: $200 for the state winner and $100 for one runner-up. Schools/organizations receive materials stipends ($500 for state winners; $200 for runners-up). State champions receive an all-expenses-paid trip to the National Finals in Washington, DC. At the national finals, a total of $50,000 in awards and school stipends is distributed annually, including $20,000 for the National Champion. Students who advance to regional and state competitions also have the opportunity to work with a Poetry Coach.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Schools and organizations must host their local competition by Friday, January 16, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: High school students (grades 9-12) across Maryland, including homeschool students
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Competition prizes and school/organization stipends for poetry recitation performance; all-expenses-paid travel to National Finals for state champions; poetry materials purchase
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland; regional competitions held in Baltimore-central, West-central, and South-central regions. Part of a national program administered in all 50 states through state arts coordinators.
requirements_list: Must be a currently enrolled high school student in grades 9-12 (8th-grade students in 9th-12th grade classes may also be eligible)
Students must memorize and recite poems from the official Poetry Out Loud anthology
Poems must be delivered entirely from memory
Students must announce the title, author, and translator (if applicable) before reciting
No editorial comments allowed before or after recitation
No props or costumes allowed
At state and national finals, three poems are required: one poem of 25 lines or fewer, and one poem written before the 20th century
Must compete in lower-level competition before advancing to state finals (independent or homeschooled students may register directly for regional competitions)
Local competition must be hosted by January 16, 2026
Winners of local competitions advance to regional competitions
Must submit IRS Form W-9 or W-8 to receive prize money
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Schools, homeschool organizations, or community organizations register with the Maryland State Arts Council and host a local competition. Winners advance to a regional competition (held in February 2026), then the top three or four students from each regional competition advance to the state finals (March 7, 2026). Independent or homeschooled students may register directly for regional competitions. State champions advance to the National Finals in Washington, DC.

structured_extraction.program_description: This grant program encourages and supports relevant professional development opportunities for artists and arts organizations throughout Maryland. The goal is to support growth and learning for long-term financial success among individual artists, arts organizations, and related entities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $2,000 to support relevant professional development opportunities for artists and arts organizations in Maryland. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis through the Smart Simple online portal.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis from September 2, 2025 through March 31, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individual artists and arts organizations throughout Maryland seeking professional development opportunities, including Maryland-incorporated 501(c)3 nonprofits, units of local government, and Maryland colleges/universities/schools.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support relevant professional development opportunities for artists and arts administrators.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicants must be either an independent artist, a Maryland-incorporated 501(c)3 nonprofit in operation for at least one year, a unit of Maryland local government, or a Maryland college/university/school.
Applicants must identify a specific professional development opportunity that will take place during the application period.
Nonprofits must meet certain grant income requirements.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted through the Smart Simple online portal on a rolling basis from September 2, 2025, through March 31, 2026. A panel reviews applications submitted by the last day of each month during the following month. The agency then sends notifications. If approved, you will receive a grant agreement to process the payment.

structured_extraction.program_name: Public Art Across Maryland Conservation Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: The Public Art Across Maryland (PAAM) Conservation Grant supports organizations in conserving and preserving existing local public artworks in Maryland. It funds conservation planning efforts — such as collection inventories, digitization of records, community outreach, research, and assessments — as well as the actual implementation of conservation and relocation efforts that maintain or improve public access to artworks.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two grant types are available: (1) Conservation Planning Grant awards a flat $10,000 to support conservation planning activities including project administration, consultant fees, community engagement, and collection management services. (2) Conservation Implementation Grant awards up to $30,000 to support the full conservation of a permanent public artwork, including cleaning, structural repairs, relocation, lighting, landscaping, and interpretive signage. Organization administration/project management fees cannot exceed 10% of the grant request. Indirect costs cannot exceed 10% of the total grant request.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland-based nonprofit organizations, units of government, colleges and universities, and schools (pre-K through grade 12) that own or manage existing public artworks and want to conserve or preserve them.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Conservation Planning Grants: project administration, consultant fees (conservator, artist, engineer, historian, etc.), community engagement activities, and collection management technology. Conservation Implementation Grants: artwork relocation, cleaning/coating/painting, structural repairs, landscape site improvements, lighting and electrical work, interpretive signage, and project management (up to 10% of grant).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The artwork being conserved must be located in Maryland. Applicants must be Maryland-based organizations (or Maryland-based fiscal sponsors).
requirements_list: Applicant must be a nonprofit 501(c)3 organization based in Maryland, a unit of government, a Maryland college or university, or a Maryland school (pre-K through grade 12)
Nonprofit fiscal sponsors must have a Model A fiscal sponsorship agreement in place with the sponsored group
Applicants may only submit one PAAM grant application per fiscal year
Organizations that received a PAAM Project Grant (New Artworks or Conservation) in FY 2024 are not eligible to apply for any PAAM Project Grant in FY 2025
The artwork must meet MSAC's definition of public art (free and accessible to the public)
The artwork's final location must be in Maryland
The artwork must be publicly accessible
The artwork must comply with local jurisdiction regulations, permissions, and permitting requirements
For Implementation grants, the conservation project must be fully developed with a project team identified and approval from the artwork and site owners
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the online grants management system SmartSimple at marylandarts.smartsimple.com. Create a free account or log in, complete the application electronically, and submit with an electronic signature. Technical support is available during regular office hours. Late or misdirected applications are the applicant's responsibility. Applicants must meet any revision deadlines after submission or the application will be withdrawn. After receiving a grant, grantees must file a final report in SmartSimple (deadline: March 30, 2026 for Planning grants; September 30, 2026 for Implementation grants).

structured_extraction.program_name: Public Art Across Maryland New Artworks Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: Grants support artists and organizations planning, creating, and installing new local public art projects in Maryland. There are two grant types: Planning grants (up to $10,000) help artists or organizations develop public art proposals with communities, and Project grants (up to $30,000) help organizations fabricate and install new public artwork that has been developed through a community engagement process.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Planning grants award up to $10,000 to support independent artists or organizations developing public art proposals with communities. Project grants award up to $30,000 to organizations to support the fabrication and installation of new public artwork. Funds may cover artist fees, materials, fabrication, transportation, community engagement, permits, consultants, and related project costs. Organization administration/project management fees cannot exceed 10% of the total grant request.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: FY2026 New Artworks grant applications will be accepted from September 8 through December 12, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Independent Maryland artists (age 18+, not currently enrolled in a degree program) and Maryland-based nonprofit organizations, fiscal sponsors, government units, colleges/universities, and schools seeking to create and install new public art projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planning grants: community outreach, artist selection, proposal design, consultant fees, equipment rentals, permit applications. Project grants: artist fees, contracted services, fabrication materials and equipment, transportation, insurance, permitting, plaque/signage, and project management (capped at 10% of grant request).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be Maryland residents (individuals) or Maryland-based organizations. Artwork must be designed by a Maryland artist and installed in a publicly accessible location.
requirements_list: Independent artists must be Maryland residents (owning or renting residential property in Maryland for at least six months before application) and at least 18 years old
Independent artists must not be enrolled in any matriculated high school, undergraduate, or graduate degree program at time of application and throughout the grant period
For collaborative groups, at least 50% of members must be Maryland residents
Organizations must be Maryland-based nonprofits with 501(c)(3) status, fiscal sponsors with a Model A agreement, units of government, colleges/universities, or schools
Artwork must be considered public art as defined by MSAC, be new and original, and be designed by a Maryland artist
Artwork must be publicly accessible and comply with local permitting and siting regulations
For Project grants, artwork must have been developed through a community engagement process and be fully designed with the artist(s) identified at time of application
Applicants may only submit one PAAM grant application per fiscal year
Organizations that received PAAM Project grants in FY2024 are ineligible to apply for PAAM Project grants in FY2025
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the secure online grants management system SmartSimple at marylandarts.smartsimple.com. Create a free account or log in, complete the application, and submit electronically including an electronic signature. Meet all revision deadlines after submission. A multi-disciplinary statewide panel reviews and scores applications.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Public Art Across Maryland Program promotes and supports the inclusion of art in everyday experiences for Marylanders. It supports those planning, making, and caring for art in public spaces across the state through direct commissions, grants, technical assistance, and professional development.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides direct commissions, grants, technical assistance, and professional development to support public art projects across Maryland.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planning, creating, and installing public art; conserving existing public artworks; professional development.

structured_extraction.program_description: A $60 million one-time COVID-19 pandemic relief grant program for licensed child care centers and registered family child care providers in Maryland. Funded through the Coronavirus Response and Relief Supplemental Appropriations Act of 2021, the program helps providers cover costs related to the pandemic, including decreased enrollment, reduced capacity, temporary closures, fixed costs, increased operating expenses, cleaning and sanitation, PPE, and increased staff wages. Grants range from $2,400 to $60,000 depending on licensed capacity.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time pandemic relief grants from a $60 million pool funded through the Coronavirus Response and Relief Supplemental Appropriations Act of 2021. Grants range from $2,400 to $60,000 depending on licensed capacity. Grants are paid to licensed child care providers to cover COVID-19-related costs such as decreased enrollment, reduced capacity, temporary closures, fixed costs, increased operating expenses, cleaning and sanitation, PPE, and increased staff wages. Payments are issued as individual checks or direct deposit. Grants above $600 are reportable on Form 1099-G. Funds must be spent by December 31, 2021.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed child care centers, registered family child care providers, certificate of registration holders, letter of compliance holders, and before and after school providers in Maryland affected by the COVID-19 pandemic
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Costs of decreased enrollment, reduced capacity limits, temporary closures, fixed costs, increased operating expenses, cleaning and sanitation, PPE, increased staff salaries or wages, facility costs (rent, mortgage, property taxes, and other eligible pandemic-related expenses) during the COVID-19 pandemic; funds must be spent by December 31, 2021
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — available to licensed child care providers operating in Maryland as of March 3, 2021
requirements_list: Must be a licensed child care center, certificate of registration holder, or letter of compliance holder issued by MSDE
License/registration issue date must be on or before March 11, 2021
Must have a valid license number
Must be open and operating as of March 3, 2021 (before and after school providers must also be operating and maintaining license as of March 3, 2021)
Program must be open and operating at time of application or, if temporarily closed, must reopen and serve children before September 6, 2021
Must have Verification of Reopening Form on file with Office of Child Care

Subject to random audit requirements
Grants above $600 are reportable as 1099-G income
Each location requires a separate application if operating under multiple licenses

Applicants must verify eligibility by answering 'yes' to all checklist questions. Visit earlychildhood.marylandpublicschools.org for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: 2022 Equipment Assistance Grants for National School Lunch Program (NSLP) Operator
structured_extraction.program_description: This grant provides funds for National School Lunch Program (NSLP) operators to purchase equipment to serve healthier school meals, improve food safety, and expand access to school meals. Equipment requests may include new equipment, renovation of existing equipment, or replacement of equipment. Each individual item requested must have a value greater than $1,000.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funds for purchasing, renovating, or replacing food service equipment. All individual items requested must cost more than $1,000. Costs incurred before grant approval are not eligible for reimbursement. Priority is given to high-needs schools where 50% or more of students qualify for free or reduced-price meals, and to schools that have not previously received an NSLP Equipment Grant. Grant structure includes Phase 1 (Oct 1, 2022–June 30, 2024) and Phase 2/reallocation (July 1, 2024–Sept 30, 2024). Awards are made within 30 days of application approval.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase, renovation, or replacement of food service equipment to serve healthier school meals, improve food safety, and expand access to school meals

Download the MSDE Grant Recipient Assurances and access the Budget Template through the Maryland Accountability Reporting System (MARS) or by contacting Sara Brandt. The grant follows a two-phase structure: Phase 1 (Oct 1, 2022–June 30, 2024) and Phase 2/reallocation (July 1, 2024–Sept 30, 2024). Awards are made within 30 days of application approval. MSDE held two virtual customer service support sessions on January 9 and January 18, 2023, to review requirements and answer questions.

structured_extraction.program_name: 21st Century Community Learning Centers (21st CCLC) Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program funds community learning centers that provide students with out-of-school time (OST) academic enrichment opportunities occurring before school, after school, during summer, and on Saturdays. Centers offer academic enrichment aligned with Maryland College and Career Readiness Standards, including instructional services in core academic subjects (language arts, mathematics, science, and social studies), as well as youth development, substance use/alcohol prevention, service-learning, violence prevention, counseling, art, music, recreation, and technology education. Centers must also offer literacy instruction and related educational development programs for families of participating students. The program targets students in grades 1-12, particularly those attending Title I schools or schools serving a high percentage of students from low-income families.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Multi-year (three-year) competitive reimbursement grants awarded to eligible organizations to operate community learning centers providing out-of-school time academic enrichment and supplemental services. Total funds for FY25 were $22.6 million. Grant amounts are funded at 100% of the original award contingent on availability of funding and satisfactory performance, and are level funded for all three years unless specified otherwise. Grantees incur costs and invoice MSDE for reimbursement (6-8 weeks processing time). Grantees also receive technical assistance through bi-monthly networking meetings with MSDE staff, peer-to-peer support, and other resources. Renewal applications are available for existing cohorts (Fiscal Year 2024 Cohort Year 3 and Fiscal Year 2025 Cohort Year 2).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local education agencies, non-profit organizations, city or county government agencies, faith-based organizations, institutions of higher education, for-profit corporations, and consortia of two or more eligible entities that serve students in grades 1-12, particularly those attending Title I schools or schools with high percentages of low-income students and their families.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Academic enrichment programming (reading/language arts, mathematics, science, social studies), enrichment activities, behavioral health supports, wraparound services, youth development programs, family literacy instruction, salaries and wages for instructional and program staff, contracted services for direct student instruction, supplies and materials (max 8% of total requested), equipment (max 3% of total requested), professional development and training, evaluation services (external evaluator max 7% of total requested), and transportation if necessary.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to eligible organizations serving students at Title I schools or schools with high concentrations of low-income students. Rural LEAs with locale codes 32, 33, 41, 42, or 43 are eligible for a competitive priority.
requirements_list: Must serve students and families who primarily attend Title I school-wide eligible schools or schools with a high percentage of students from low-income families

Eligible applicants include local education agencies, non-profits, faith-based organizations, government agencies, higher education institutions, for-profit corporations, or a consortium of two or more such entities
Must provide academic enrichment opportunities and services that complement the regular academic program
Must offer family literacy instruction and related educational development programs
Grantees must attend bi-monthly networking meetings
Grantees must undergo periodic evaluation with an external evaluator
Must submit annual and final summative evaluation reports to MSDE
Evaluation results must be used to refine and improve program
Evaluation results must be made available to public upon request
Evaluation must include both qualitative and quantitative methods
Evaluator must have background in qualitative and quantitative education evaluations and out-of-school-time programming knowledge
Evaluation reports must include executive summary, purpose, program description, evaluation questions, demographic/attendance data, methodology, data analysis, conclusions, and recommendations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a renewal grant application by the deadline of August 29, 2025. structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland provides financial assistance to licensed child care centers, registered family child care homes, and school-age only programs to help cover the costs of pursuing state or national accreditation. The fund covers required application fees for national accreditation bodies—including the National Association for Family Child Care (NAFCC)—and reimburses the cost of non-consumable instructional materials for Maryland Program Accreditation through the Maryland Excels quality rating system. Family child care providers can use the fund as a first step toward NAFCC accreditation, while licensed child care centers and school-age only programs may pursue either state or national accreditation support.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The fund provides two types of support: (1) National Accreditation Support covers required application fees (initial, renewal, and annual update) for licensed child care centers, registered family child care providers (including NAFCC accreditation), and school-age only programs. Funds are paid directly to the accrediting organization on behalf of the program. The MSDE Accreditation Manager reviews applications within 30 days and notifies applicants via email of approval status. (2) Maryland Program Accreditation Support reimburses the cost of non-consumable instructional materials (e.g., curricula, classroom technology, outdoor play equipment, science and sensory materials, books) for licensed child care centers and school-age only programs pursuing Maryland Accreditation through the Maryland Excels quality rating system. Maximum reimbursement is $2,500 per accreditation cycle for programs serving 100 or fewer children, and $3,000 per accreditation cycle for programs serving more than 100 children. Consumable items (paint, crayons, markers, glue, paper) are not reimbursable. Funds cannot be used for facility improvement, association membership fees, staff training, or costs already covered by another funding source.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed child care centers, registered family child care providers, and school-age only programs in Maryland seeking state (Maryland Accreditation) or national accreditation, including NAFCC accreditation for family child care providers
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: National accreditation application fees (initial, renewal, annual update) paid directly to accrediting organizations; and reimbursement for non-consumable instructional materials (curricula, classroom technology, outdoor play equipment, science and sensory materials, books, and other learning materials) for Maryland Accreditation through the Maryland Excels quality rating system
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to licensed child care centers, registered family child care homes, and school-age only programs in Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a licensed child care center, registered family child care home, or school-age only program
Must be pursuing state (Maryland) or national accreditation (including NAFCC accreditation)

For National Accreditation Support: must submit a copy of completed application to the accrediting organization, completed Accreditation Work Plan, copy of the accrediting organization's fee page, and copy of current accreditation certificate (if currently accredited)
For Maryland Accreditation Support: items must be purchased within 12 months before the application date; only non-consumable materials are reimbursable
Each site with an individual license number can apply separately
Costs cannot already be covered by another funding source
Costs cannot exceed the fee charged by the accrediting organization
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For National Accreditation Support: submit required documents (completed application to accrediting organization, Accreditation Work Plan, fee page, and current accreditation certificate if applicable) via the Application for National Accreditation Support on the Maryland OneStop portal. The MSDE Accreditation Manager reviews within 30 days and notifies the applicant via email; award is paid directly to the accrediting organization. For Maryland Accreditation Support: submit the Application for Maryland Accreditation Support with documentation of eligible non-consumable instructional material purchases (complete a separate form for each vendor and attach receipts/invoices). Both applications are available through the Maryland OneStop portal. A video tutorial is available to guide applicants. Additional details and FAQs are available on the MSDE Early Childhood website and the Maryland Excels website.

structured_extraction.program_name: Acquired Brain Injury (ABI) Specialized Employment Services
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS) provides specialized vocational rehabilitation services to job seekers whose primary disability is an acquired brain injury (ABI). DORS works with community rehabilitation partners to offer individualized, long-term, and ongoing support to help people with ABI get and keep a job. ABI includes injuries caused by traumatic events (e.g., motor vehicle accidents, falls, assaults, sports injuries, concussions) or non-traumatic events (e.g., brain aneurysm, tumor, stroke, infection). Specially trained ABI counselors are located throughout Maryland to help individuals achieve their employment goals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Individualized, long-term, and ongoing support services delivered through specially trained ABI counselors and community rehabilitation partners located throughout Maryland. Services include vocational rehabilitation, benefits counseling, supported and customized employment, self-employment support, rapid job retention support, work experience programs, job accommodations and assistive technology, job coaching, discovery services, and work incentive planning. Services are designed to help people with acquired brain injury find, obtain, and maintain employment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Job seekers whose primary disability is an acquired brain injury (ABI), including injuries caused by traumatic events (motor vehicle accidents, falls, assaults, sports injuries, concussions) or non-traumatic events (brain aneurysm, tumor, stroke, infection). ABI must be an injury to the brain that was not present at birth. Also includes individuals seeking to return to work or enter the workforce after brain injury, including SSDI/SSI recipients.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Employment support services to help individuals with acquired brain injury obtain and retain employment, including vocational rehabilitation, job coaching, benefits counseling, accommodations, assistive technology, and work incentive planning.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide throughout Maryland through DORS counselors and community rehabilitation partners located across the state. State and local vocational rehabilitation offices and Employment Networks also available.
requirements_list: Primary disability must be an acquired brain injury (ABI)
ABI must be an injury to the brain that was not present at birth
Must have interest in pursuing or maintaining employment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 410-554-9381 or email Derick Serra (Derick.Serra@maryland.gov), Office of Field Services Program Manager, to learn more and begin the application process. Individuals may also contact their local vocational rehabilitation office or connect with Employment Networks (for SSDI/SSI recipients).

structured_extraction.program_name: Adult High School Pilot Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that funds pilot adult high schools in Maryland authorized under House Bill 1381. The program supports non-traditional high school programs for adults operated in partnership with community colleges and community organizations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding is provided to approved pilot adult high schools operating in Maryland. The most recent funding round listed is Fiscal Year (SFY) 2025.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Susan C. Spinnato, Laurel Williams, Perketer Tucker
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations operating or seeking to operate pilot adult high schools in Maryland, such as non-profits and community colleges.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating adult high school pilot programs serving adult learners seeking a high school diploma.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be an approved pilot adult high school authorized under House Bill 1381
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: See the Adult High School Pilot Program Grant Fiscal Year 2025 page for application details.

structured_extraction.program_name: Afterschool Meals and Snacks Programs (NSLP and CACFP)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides financial reimbursement to help school-based, non-profit, and non-school-based organizations serve healthy snacks and/or suppers to children in afterschool care programs as part of the USDA National School Lunch Program (NSLP) or Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP). This includes two related programs: (1) Afterschool Snacks in the National School Lunch Program (NSLP), available to school districts already participating in the NSLP; and (2) Afterschool Meals through the Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP), available to school-based and non-school-based organizations in area-eligible locations (where a majority of children qualify for free or reduced-price meals). Both programs require that afterschool programs offer educational or enrichment activities in a supervised environment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial reimbursement for healthy snacks and/or suppers served to children in eligible afterschool programs. Under the NSLP, reimbursement is available to school districts already participating in the National School Lunch Program. Under CACFP, reimbursement covers snacks and/or suppers for programs in area-eligible locations where a majority of children qualify for free or reduced-price meals.
structured_extraction.program_audience: School districts participating in the National School Lunch Program (NSLP), as well as school-based, non-profit, for-profit, and non-school-based organizations operating afterschool care programs in area-eligible locations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Serving healthy snacks and/or suppers to children in supervised afterschool programs with educational or enrichment activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to eligible school districts and organizations, with CACFP eligibility further restricted to area-eligible locations where a majority of children qualify for free or reduced-price meals.
requirements_list: Must already participate in the National School Lunch Program (NSLP) (for NSLP Afterschool Snacks)
Program must be 'area eligible' (located in an area where a majority of children qualify for free or reduced-price meals) (for CACFP)
Afterschool program must provide educational or enrichment activities in a supervised environment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 410-767-0199 to speak with OSCNP staff to determine eligibility. Contact the Maryland State Department of Education School and Community Nutrition office to participate. Additional information is available at the USDA Afterschool website, and USDA provides CACFP Meal Patterns guidance for CACFP participants.

structured_extraction.program_description: Career and Technical Education (CTE) registered apprenticeship program that connects Maryland high school students ages 16 and older with paid, mentored on-the-job training and related technical instruction while in school. Students complete at least one year of related classroom instruction and a minimum of 450 hours of work-based training in Manufacturing, STEM, and traditional occupations. Students earn at least minimum wage, gain hands-on workforce experience, and can earn industry-recognized credentials including a State Skill Certificate upon completion. The program is approved by the Maryland Apprenticeship and Training Council and delivered in partnership with local school districts and the Maryland Department of Labor.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Students receive a minimum of 450 hours of paid on-the-job training (OJT) and at least one year of related classroom instruction (RTI). Students are paid at least minimum wage and receive instruction from skilled mentors at the worksite. Upon completion, students earn a State Skill Certificate. Placements and schedules are flexible — during the school day, after school, over the summer, or on weekends — and are set by the employer and student. Employers partner with a Maryland Department of Labor Navigator to register positions and host student apprentices.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland high school students ages 16 and older (junior year and above) and employers in manufacturing, STEM, and traditional occupations seeking to build a talent pipeline through youth apprenticeships
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Paid on-the-job training and related classroom instruction for students; employers pay student wages (minimum wage or higher) and provide mentored worksite training to build their workforce pipeline
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across all Maryland school systems; originally piloted in Frederick and Washington Counties
requirements_list: Student must be age 16 or older
Student must be in junior year of high school or above
Must be enrolled in a Maryland local education agency
Positions must be approved by the Maryland Apprenticeship and Training Council (MATC)
Minimum 450 hours of paid on-the-job training required
Minimum one year of related classroom instruction required
Employers must pay minimum wage or higher
Employers must identify required skills and knowledge and instruct apprentices in required competencies
Employers must provide safety instruction and assign a mentor and skilled trainers
Employers must allow release time for training/meetings
Employers must comply with youth apprenticeship agreement and state and federal child labor laws
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Students and families should contact their school's apprenticeship or career-connected learning coordinator to explore opportunities, eligibility, and scheduling. Employers should partner with a Maryland Department of Labor Navigator to register positions and host student apprentices.

structured_extraction.program_name: Autism Program Planning Success for Employment (APPS)
structured_extraction.program_description: APPS helps job seekers with autism build self-determination and employment readiness skills through small group, interactive learning sessions. Topics include self-advocacy, decision making, career exploration, job readiness, career interests, work expectations, employer expectations, employee responsibilities, and understanding workplace expectations. Sessions are offered in-person in the community, at the DORS Workforce & Technology Center (WTC) campus in Baltimore, and online.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Small group, interactive learning sessions covering self-determination, self-advocacy, decision making, career interests and skills, job exploration, work expectations and responsibilities, employer expectations, employee responsibilities, and job readiness. Offered in-person in the community, at the DORS Workforce & Technology Center (WTC) campus in Baltimore, and online.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Job seekers with a documented autism diagnosis who can participate in all program activities and community activities with little supervision.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Employment readiness training and self-determination skill development.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in-person at community locations or at the DORS Workforce & Technology Center (WTC) campus in Baltimore, and also available online throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Documentation of autism diagnosis
Interview with DORS Autism Services staff prior to beginning the program
Ability to participate in all APPS and community activities with little supervision
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your DORS Counselor or local DORS office for more information or to request services.

structured_extraction.program_description: A 12-week training program at the DORS Workforce & Technology Center in Baltimore that prepares individuals with disabilities for entry-level automotive detailing jobs. The program combines classroom instruction and hands-on experience covering interior and exterior cleaning, restoration of headlights, washing, waxing, polishing exteriors, use of detailing equipment, chemical safety, and quality standards required by high-end detail shops and dealerships.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 12-week automotive detailing training course including videos, lectures, product demonstrations, and extensive hands-on experience. Topics include customer service, interior and exterior cleaning techniques, equipment safety, chemical handling, clay bar use, scratch removal, compounding and waxing, and restoration of headlights.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with disabilities seeking entry-level employment in automotive detailing
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Vocational training to prepare for employment as an automotive detailer
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Open to Maryland residents. Training is provided at the DORS Workforce & Technology Center campus in Baltimore, Maryland.
requirements_list: Valid driver's license with no more than two points
3rd grade or higher reading comprehension level and basic math skills
Ability to lift 50 pounds
