Ability to squat, stoop, and kneel
Certain criminal backgrounds may disqualify an individual from the program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact a DORS Counselor or local DORS office for more information. Individuals may also request services via QR code as provided in program materials.

structured_extraction.program_description: A 16-week training course that prepares job seekers with disabilities for entry-level work in the automotive industry as General Service Technicians. The program covers automotive maintenance and repair, customer service, shop safety, and hands-on use of industry-standard equipment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 16-week vocational training program at the WTC campus in northeast Baltimore. Training covers lubrication and fluid changes, tire changing and balancing, battery replacement, tune-ups, vehicle inspections, brake repair, testing and charging starting systems, and use of shop equipment including tire balancing machines, 4-wheel alignment tools, lifts, and hand tools.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Job seekers with disabilities who want to enter the automotive industry as entry-level General Service Technicians
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Vocational training in automotive maintenance and repair skills
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland residents; training provided at the WTC campus in northeast Baltimore
requirements_list: Valid driver's license with no more than 2 points
Ability to lift 50 pounds
Ability to squat, stoop, and kneel
3rd grade reading level and basic math skills
No disqualifying criminal backgrounds
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact a DORS Counselor or local DORS office to request services. A QR code is available to request DORS services.

structured_extraction.program_description: A class provided by Occupational Therapists or Physical Therapists covering basic back anatomy, back injury facts and prevention, and proper body mechanics for material handling and job tasks. Available to WTC students in specific training programs and to individual job seekers on request.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A lecture and hands-on material handling lab covering back injury prevention, proper body mechanics, and job-specific tasks to help consumers prepare for and maintain employment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: DORS consumers participating in Auto Mechanics, Food Service, Environmental Services, Warehouse, and Work Readiness training programs, as well as other job seekers on an individual basis.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training to prevent back injuries and promote long-term employment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available through DORS's Work Technology Center (WTC) and on an individual basis.
requirements_list: Must be a DORS consumer
Participating in a designated WTC training program or referred on an individual basis
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Automatically included for students in designated WTC training programs; individual job seekers should contact DORS to request the class.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free online training course that child care providers, staff, substitutes, and adults responsible for children in licensed child care programs must complete to meet state and federal Child Care and Development Block Grant (CCDBG) requirements. The course covers health, safety, and nutrition best practices connected to Maryland Office of Child Care regulations. Delivered through the MSDE Canvas learning management system, the course includes modules and a Final Assessment, with a Certificate of Completion issued upon scoring 80% or higher.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free online training course consisting of four modules plus a final review and survey. Takes approximately 3 hours to complete. Participants must score at least 80% on all topic reviews and the Final Assessment to receive a certificate of completion. The course is offered monthly, with a 21-day window to complete it. Each account is allowed two attempts to pass the Final Assessment. An annual update (1.5 hours) is also available free of charge through the MSDE Canvas platform. New employees must complete training within 90 days of hire for compliance.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Registration opens monthly (e.g., June cohort registration opens May 13 at 9:00 am and closes May 23 at 12:00 pm); new employees must complete training within 90 days of hire
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care providers, staff, substitutes, volunteers, and adults responsible for the care and safety of children in licensed child care programs in Maryland; new employees in early childhood programs must complete within 90 days of hire
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Completion of required health and safety training for child care licensing compliance
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to all licensed child care program staff
requirements_list: Must be a child care provider, staff member, substitute, or adult responsible for children in a licensed child care program
Must have a valid email address to register; each participant must use a unique email address
Must complete all four modules and the final review and survey
Must score a minimum of 80% on all topic reviews and the Final Assessment to receive a certificate
Each account is allowed two attempts to pass the Final Assessment
Registration must be completed during the open registration window (one week per month); late registrations are not accepted
Participants who previously took the training and scored below 80% are not allowed to retake the online course and must complete it in an approved face-to-face format
Must complete the Introduction module before accessing other topics
Must use the EXIT COURSE button to properly close the training to save progress
New employees must complete training within 90 days of hire for compliance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register during the monthly open registration window using the online registration form at https://msde.instructure.com. After registration, you will receive login credentials via email before the course opens. Log in to the course platform (Instructure/Canvas) during the 21-day course window, complete the Introduction module first, then complete all remaining modules in order, and finally complete the Final Assessment and survey. The system saves progress between sessions. Print or save your certificate of completion (available in the Modules section) before the course closes.

structured_extraction.program_description: Benefits Planning Services connects people with disabilities who receive Social Security benefits with trained and certified benefits counselors (benefits planners). These counselors help individuals understand how returning to work will affect their personal Social Security benefits and work incentives.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-on-one counseling from certified benefits planners who help individuals understand the impact of work on their Social Security benefits and work incentives.
structured_extraction.program_audience: People with disabilities who receive Social Security disability benefits and are exploring returning to work.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Counseling and guidance on navigating Social Security work incentives.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland through DORS.
requirements_list: Must have begun services with DORS
Must be interested in exploring a return to work
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Once you begin services with DORS, let your counselor know you are interested and they will schedule an appointment with a benefits planner.

structured_extraction.program_name: Broadening Options and Opportunities for Students Today (BOOST) Scholarship Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The BOOST Scholarship Program provides scholarship awards to help income-eligible students (those who qualify for free or reduced-price school meals) pay tuition at participating nonpublic (private) schools in Maryland. Awards are sent directly to the school and applied to the student's tuition balance. Priority is granted to students who received BOOST scholarships in the prior year and their siblings.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Scholarship funds are deposited to the student's tuition account at the participating nonpublic school and applied toward tuition and required fees only. Approximately $9,000,000 is available with an estimated 2,500 awards. Award amounts vary based on household income, the student's academic level, and financial assistance already provided by the school. The award cannot exceed the amount of tuition owed. Funds cannot be used for transportation or meals, cannot be split, transferred, or carried over to subsequent years.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Nonpublic school applications: no later than March 6, 2026; Parent applications: no later than May 8, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. EDT
structured_extraction.contact_name: Allison Sanborn, Program Manager; James Clark, Administrative Support
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland students in grades K–12 who qualify for free or reduced-price school meals (FARMs) and are enrolled or accepted at a participating nonpublic school; families in informal kinship care arrangements; nonpublic schools seeking to participate in the program
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition and required fees at a participating nonpublic school; funds cannot be used for transportation or meals and cannot supplant other financial aid
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland; the nonpublic school must be registered to operate in Maryland and approved to participate in the program. Participating schools are located across 19 jurisdictions including Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Calvert, Carroll, Cecil, Charles, Frederick, Garrett, Harford, Howard, Montgomery, Prince George's, St. Mary's, Talbot, Washington, Wicomico, and Worcester counties.
requirements_list: Student must qualify for free and reduced-price meals (FARMs)
Student must be enrolled or accepted at a participating nonpublic school for the 2026-2027 school year
Student must be entering grades kindergarten through 12th grade (Pre-K students are not eligible)
Parents must upload their 2025 Federal 1040 tax returns to verify income and household size
Business losses cannot be used to reduce income; income from interest, dividends, IRA distributions, pensions, annuities, and social security are counted
Application must be submitted online through the BOOST Scholarship application portal
Renewal students (prior BOOST recipients with confirmed enrollment) receive priority; new applicants considered after budget bill passage (April 2026) and BOOST Advisory Board meeting (Summer 2026)
Nonpublic schools must hold a certificate of approval from or be registered with the State Board of Education
Nonpublic schools must be approved to participate in the Nonpublic Textbook Program
Nonpublic schools must provide at least a 1st grade full-day level program (pre-K only schools are not eligible)
Nonpublic schools must complete an application to the BOOST Scholarship Program by March 6, 2026
Nonpublic schools must comply with non-discrimination requirements (Title VI, Title 20 Subtitle 6; no discrimination based on race, color, national origin, sexual orientation, or gender identity)
Nonpublic schools must administer national norm-referenced standardized assessments or approved Maryland assessment (MCAP) in ELA, Mathematics, and Science
Nonpublic schools must report certified and non-certified teacher data
Nonpublic schools must report student withdrawal/expulsion data for BOOST recipients
Nonpublic schools must complete enrollment confirmation for BOOST students
Nonpublic schools must submit all required reports to MSDE by September 25, 2026
Nonpublic schools must notify MSDE within 7 business days if a student becomes ineligible
Nonpublic schools must return scholarship funds on a pro-rata basis if a student withdraws or is expelled
Nonpublic schools must maintain BOOST records for three years

For informal kinship care: relative caregiver must be over 18 years old, child must be living with relative due to serious family hardship, relative must provide 24/7 care and notify MSDE within 30 days of any changes
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Parents complete the online BOOST Scholarship application on the Submittable platform and upload their 2025 Federal 1040 tax returns. Nonpublic schools must separately apply to participate through the BOOST program by March 6, 2026. MSDE offers virtual customer service support sessions to walk applicants through the process. Schools receive the awarded student list in early September and must complete required reporting by September 25, 2026. Families in informal kinship care must complete and submit the Informal Kinship Care Affidavit form.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's USDA Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP) Meal Service Training Grant expands menu planning training to address meal pattern requirements, menu planning principles, creditable and non-creditable foods, standardized recipes, healthy food preparation methods, and culturally appropriate CACFP recipes. Also offers training on infant feeding, including breastfeeding, formula use, and safe food handling.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Training grant providing menu planning and meal service training, including infant feeding instruction (USDA's 'Feeding Infants in the CACFP'). A peer advisory team guides programming.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care agencies and staff participating in the CACFP in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Menu planning training, meal pattern compliance, healthy food preparation, standardized recipes, and infant feeding knowledge and skills.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide.
requirements_list: Must participate in the CACFP
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact OSCNP at 410-767-0199 for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: CDA Exemption for Pre-K Teaching Assistants
structured_extraction.program_description: A credential exemption pathway that allows teaching assistants in publicly funded prekindergarten classrooms to qualify for their position through documented work experience instead of holding a Child Development Associate (CDA) credential or associate degree. Eligible individuals must verify at least 5 years of experience in a publicly funded Pre-K program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Teaching assistants who lack a CDA or associate degree can qualify for Pre-K assistant positions by documenting at least 5 years of experience (minimum 20 hours per week, at least 180 days per year) in a publicly funded prekindergarten program. Employers (local education agencies or private providers) complete and submit a verification template on behalf of the assistants. All experience must be verified by June 30, 2025.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Dr. Nakeisha Savage, Director of Early Learning and Instruction
structured_extraction.program_audience: Teaching assistants or paraeducators working in publicly funded Pre-K classrooms in Maryland who do not hold a CDA credential or associate degree.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Verifying documented work experience to qualify for a teaching assistant position in a publicly funded Pre-K classroom without a CDA or associate degree.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland for teaching assistants employed in publicly funded Pre-K programs. Maryland State Department of Education, 200 W. Baltimore Street, Baltimore, MD 21201.
requirements_list: Minimum of 5 years of experience in a publicly funded Pre-K program as of July 1, 2024
At least 20 hours per week or at least 0.5 FTE
At least 180 days per year
Experience must be in classrooms funded by the Prekindergarten Expansion Grant, Maryland State Prekindergarten Grant, or Blueprint formula funding (other funding may require pre-approval)
All experience must be verified by June 30, 2025
Verification must be submitted by the employer (LEA or private provider) using the documented experience template
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Teaching assistants work with their employer (local education agency or private provider) to complete the documented experience template. The template requires the organization's letterhead, the date, and a table listing all Pre-K assistants being submitted. The completed template is then emailed to the Division of Early Childhood.

structured_extraction.program_description: A partnership between the Maryland Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS), CVS Health, and the Community College of Baltimore County that prepares job seekers with disabilities to become Certified Pharmacy Technicians. The program includes classroom instruction, hands-on practice in a mock CVS pharmacy, and an externship at CVS pharmacies across Maryland. Pharmacy Technicians assist pharmacists in hospitals or retail pharmacies, serving customers, processing insurance claims, maintaining inventory and filling prescriptions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 14 weeks of classroom instruction plus 6 weeks of clinical on-the-job training (externship) at CVS pharmacies. Training covers CVS programs and procedures, inventory management, and prescription medication measurements. Prepares participants to take the national Pharmacy Technician Certifying Board (PTCB) certification exam.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Job seekers with disabilities who are at least 18 years old with a high school diploma or GED and want to work as pharmacy technicians.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Classroom training and externship to prepare for pharmacy technician certification.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Classroom instruction is offered at the DORS Workforce and Technology Center (WTC). Externships take place at CVS pharmacies in the participant's local community throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Be at least 18 years of age with a high school diploma or GED
Have the desire to work in a retail environment and ability to provide excellent customer service
Have a 9th-grade reading comprehension level and 9th-grade math skills
Be detail oriented, able to multitask, and work accurately and quickly
Have efficient computer, telephone, and study skills
Pass a drug screen and background check before starting the program
Be able to lift up to 30 pounds and bend, stoop, and stand for long periods
Have close visual acuity
COVID-19 vaccination required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact DORS to apply. Applicants must meet program requirements including a background check and drug screen before starting.

structured_extraction.program_name: Career & Technology Training Programs at WTC (training component)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Workforce and Technology Center (WTC) offers career and technology training programs that prepare students with disabilities for entry-level employment. Programs provide individualized instruction, essential supports, and accommodations to help students with varying learning styles reach their employment goals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Career and technology training programs are offered in fields including Automotive Detailing, Automotive General Service Technician, Child Care Provider, CVS Retail Academy, CVS Pharmacy Technician, Environmental Services, and Food Service. Programs include individualized instruction and accommodations for individuals with disabilities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with disabilities seeking entry-level employment skills
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Career and vocational training to prepare for employment in fields such as automotive services, child care, retail, pharmacy, environmental services, and food service
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available through the Maryland Workforce and Technology Center
requirements_list: Must be an individual with a disability

structured_extraction.program_name: Child Care Career and Professional Development Fund (CCCPDF) Scholarship (Degree Programs)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides scholarship funding to child care providers and staff who participate in the Maryland Child Care Credentialing Program to pursue a college degree in Early Childhood Education, Child Development, Elementary Education, or Special Education. Payments are made directly to the college or university on behalf of the participant.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Scholarship funding paid directly to accredited colleges and universities on behalf of eligible participants. The fund does not reimburse participants — payments go straight to the institution. MSDE notifies applicants of fund approval.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care providers and staff who are participating in the Maryland Child Care Credentialing Program and wish to pursue an associate or bachelor's degree in early childhood-related fields.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: College tuition and fees for degree programs in Early Childhood Education, Child Development, Elementary Education, or Special Education at participating accredited institutions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to participants in the Maryland Child Care Credentialing Program.
requirements_list: Must be a child care provider or staff member
Must be participating in the Maryland Child Care Credentialing Program
Must pursue a degree in Early Childhood Education, Child Development, Elementary Education, or Special Education
Must attend an accredited college or university recognized by the U.S. Department of Education
Institution should participate in the CCCPDF (marked with asterisk on the program page)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through MSDE. MSDE will notify applicants of whether or not they have received fund approval. Payments are made directly to the college or university.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland EXCELS offers published child care programs a free one-year subscription to Child Care Exchange magazine, which includes six issues and access to Articles on Demand. This is a recognition benefit for programs committed to pursuing quality child care and early education.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A free one-year subscription to Child Care Exchange magazine (six issues plus access to Articles on Demand). Limited to one subscription per program. Subscriptions last one year and are not automatically renewed.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care and early education programs that are published (listed) in Maryland EXCELS
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Magazine subscription providing professional resources and articles for child care providers
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to programs published in Maryland EXCELS statewide
requirements_list: Program must be published in Maryland EXCELS
Limited to one subscription per program
Information provided must be accurate and complete
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Sign up using the form on the Maryland EXCELS website page.

structured_extraction.program_description: A 16-week training course that prepares job seekers with disabilities to become certified childcare providers. The program combines classroom instruction with a nine-week community-based internship at a licensed childcare facility. Offered in partnership with the Community College of Baltimore County at select locations throughout Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive 16 weeks of instruction covering child development, activity planning, communication, infant/toddler care, school-age child care, and First Aid/CPR certification, plus a nine-week community-based internship at an approved licensed childcare facility. Training is provided at select locations throughout Maryland in partnership with CCBC.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Job seekers with disabilities who are at least 18 years old and want to work as childcare providers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and internship experience to obtain childcare provider certification leading to employment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Select locations throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: At least 18 years of age
Background check and health clearance
6th grade reading comprehension level and basic math skills
High school diploma, GED, or certificate
Basic computer knowledge
Ability to lift and move children up to 30 pounds or more
Ability to see details at close range
Ability to hear and give verbal instructions in noisy conditions
Ability to change from one task to another
Ability to supervise children independently
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact a DORS Counselor or local DORS office to request services. A QR code is also available to request services.

structured_extraction.program_name: Child Care Quality Incentive Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Child Care Quality Incentive Grant Program (CCQIG) provides grants to licensed child care providers to purchase supplies, materials, and equipment that improve and enhance the quality of care for children and their school readiness. The program focuses on educational curricula and activities in literacy, math, science, social studies, and physical development for children ages 0 to 16. Grants help providers acquire resources to create stimulating learning environments after gaining additional training and education in early childhood development. Grants are awarded quarterly (January, April, July, October) based on the number of children in care, and providers are eligible once every three years.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are awarded quarterly (January, April, July, October) based on the number of children in care: up to $1,000 for facilities with fewer than 10 children; up to $1,500 for facilities with up to 29 children; up to $2,500 for facilities with more than 30 children. Child care providers are eligible for a grant award once every three years. Grant funds may be spent only on approved supplies, materials, and equipment to improve the quality of child care and implement knowledge gained through training. Eligible purchases include items for active play, arts and crafts, dramatic play, literacy, math, science, manipulatives, program planning, and special needs equipment. All materials must be age appropriate for children aged 0 through 16.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Coming soon — revised Grant Information Guide and Application are pending review and approval
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed child care centers and family child care home providers in Maryland serving children ages 0 to 16 who are working to enhance the quality of care and children's school readiness
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of supplies, materials, and equipment to create stimulating learning environments and implement knowledge gained through training, including items for literacy, math, science, social studies, physical development, dramatic play, arts and crafts, manipulatives, active play, and special needs equipment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to child care providers across Maryland.
requirements_list: Must possess a current license or letter of compliance
Must currently operate a child care center or family child care home
Must implement a curriculum that aligns with standards established by Kindergarten Readiness and Early Learning Assessment (ELA) guidelines
Must meet additional requirements specific to child care centers or family child care homes as outlined in the program's requirements chart
Funds must be used to purchase approved supplies, materials, and equipment
All materials must be age appropriate for children aged 0 through 16
Grant must improve children's developmental skills
Preference given to grants focusing on literacy, math, science, social studies, and physical development
Computers purchased must be for child care use
Curriculum guides must be MSDE-approved
Must complete a full grant application — incomplete applications will be returned
Must provide FEIN/SSN identification per site when operating multiple locations
Must itemize all proposed purchases with costs and descriptions of how each item improves care quality
Eligible for a grant award once every three years
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the grant application form, itemizing all supplies, materials, and equipment with costs and descriptions of intended use. Submit one application per child care facility (for providers with multiple sites). Forward completed application(s) to the Credentialing Branch. Applicants will be notified in writing whether their application is approved or disapproved. The revised Grant Information Guide and Application will be announced through the IMPACT and Tidbits newsletter and posted on the MSDE website when approved.

structured_extraction.program_name: Child Care Scholarship Advance Payments (provider payment mechanism)
structured_extraction.program_description: MSDE pays child care providers in advance based on enrollment rather than retroactively. Each month, MSDE issues two payments — one on the 1st and one on the 15th — based on the number of children with enrolled scholarships. Payments are calculated on daily rates and adjusted for voucher/scholarship end dates, EXCELS Tier payments, adverse action, registration fees, union dues, and recoupments. A True-Up process adjusts payments one month later to account for late enrollments, early scholarship endings, or provider ineligibility. Attendance is required but does not affect payment amounts.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Advance, enrollment-based payments issued twice monthly (on the 1st and 15th) to child care providers participating in the Child Care Scholarship program. Payment amounts are based on the number of enrolled scholarship children and calculated on daily rates. Payments are adjusted for voucher/scholarship end dates, EXCELS Tier payments, adverse action, registration fees, union dues, and recoupments. A True-Up reconciliation occurs one month after the Advance Payment to correct for any overpayments or underpayments. Attendance is required but does not impact payment amounts.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care providers participating in the Maryland Child Care Scholarship program, and families seeking affordable child care
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operational funding for child care providers serving children with Child Care Scholarships; provider reimbursement for child care services for scholarship recipients
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland
requirements_list: Provider must be licensed or regulated and in good standing with Maryland EXCELS
EXCELS participation is mandatory for CCS program participation
Children must appear on the provider's invoice by the last Saturday of the previous calendar month to be included in the Advance Payment
Provider must submit signed invoices for each monthly service period
Provider must submit attendance records (attendance does not impact payment amount)
Students with more than 60 days of absence cannot continue to receive payments
Attendance/Invoice Reports must be submitted within 60 days of service period end
Provider must pass MSDE Program Integrity Audits; failure to submit invoices results in repayment of funds
Providers may submit inquiries/appeals within 90 days of payment receipt
Provider must be enrolled in the ChildCareCentral2 system
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Providers submit invoices and attendance records through the Child Care Provider Portal at provider.childcareportals.org. Advance Payments are calculated automatically based on enrollment data. For payment disputes, providers may submit informal inquiries or appeals within 90 days of payment receipt; formal appeals are available for intentional program violations. Providers can contact CCS Central 2 at 877-227-0125, email CCS2review.msde@maryland.gov, or submit a Child Care Scholarship Provider Inquiry for questions. Escalation to MSDE is available if the vendor cannot resolve issues within 3 business days.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Child Care Scholarship (CCS) Program helps eligible Maryland families pay for high-quality child care and early education. Formerly known as the Child Care Subsidy Program (also previously called Purchase of Care or voucher), it is administered by the Maryland State Department of Education and managed by a centralized vendor called Child Care Scholarship Central 2 (CCS Central 2). Families receive a scholarship that covers a portion of their child care costs at participating Maryland EXCELS providers (licensed child care centers or registered family homes), or through informal providers (relative and non-relative care). The family is responsible for a state-assigned co-payment and any additional provider fees. Families receiving Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) or Supplemental Security Income (SSI) have a $0 co-payment. A Fast Track option provides a temporary 60-day scholarship within three business days while the full application is processed. Applications and redeterminations are submitted online through the Family Child Care Portal at family.childcareportals.org. The program serves approximately 37,000 children, 25,000 parents, and 3,500 early care and educational programs statewide. As of May 1, 2025, the program has temporarily stopped issuing scholarships to new families.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible families receive scholarships (subsidies) that cover a portion of child care costs at participating Maryland EXCELS providers or informal providers (relative and non-relative). The State pays the scholarship rate directly to the child care provider on a biweekly basis. A temporary 60-day scholarship is issued within 3 business days of a Fast Track application. If approved for a full scholarship, coverage lasts 52 weeks (two-year scholarships upon full approval), contingent on submitting additional documentation within 15 days of Fast Track approval. Families pay a state-assigned co-payment ($0–$3 per week); families receiving TCA or SSI have a $0 co-payment. Co-payment waivers are available for eligible parents through the HB1121 Program. The scholarship rate is set by state regulation. Eligible expenses include child care and early education at a licensed child care center, registered family home, or approved informal provider, including before and after school care. Scholarships cover children under age 13, or individuals ages 13–19 with a qualifying disability. Income limits vary by family size (ranging from approximately $61,222 for a family of 2 to $135,049 for a family of 12 on the Initial Income Scale; continuation limits are higher). Advance payments are processed monthly on the 1st and 15th. Applications and changes are submitted through the Family Child Care Portal at https://family.childcareportals.org. Informal providers also have access to training and learning resources beyond annual requirements through approved trainers and training organizations.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: As of May 1, 2025, the program has temporarily stopped issuing scholarships to new families.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland resident families with children under age 13 (or individuals ages 13–19 with a qualifying disability) who are working, in an approved training program, or attending school, and who meet income guidelines or receive TCA or SSI. Also includes parenting youth in out-of-home care, migrant workers, homeless individuals, emancipated minors, and families receiving SNAP, WIC, WAG, GBI, or Housing Assistance. Child care providers (licensed child care centers, registered family child care homes, large family child care homes, and informal child care providers) may also participate as approved providers and manage scholarships, attendance, and invoicing through the Provider Portal.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment for child care and early education expenses at a Maryland EXCELS-participating licensed child care center, registered family home, or approved informal provider (relative or non-relative), including before and after school care and extended hours (7pm–6am for parenting youth in out-of-home care). For providers, funds support child care services provision with attendance and invoicing documentation submitted through the Provider Portal.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Maryland residents statewide. Applicants must have a residential address within the state of Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident
Must be working, enrolled in an approved training program, or attending school (both parents in the same household must meet this requirement)
Must be a recipient of TCA or SSI, or meet CCS income guidelines (Initial Income Scale ranges from approximately $61,222 for family of 2 to $135,049 for family of 12)
Child must be under age 13, or ages 13–19 with a qualifying disability
Must agree to have child immunized to Maryland state standards or provide an exemption
Must provide proof that each child needing care is a U.S. citizen or qualified alien (parents are not required to be U.S. citizens)
Must provide proof of identity for all household members
Head of household must provide a photo ID
Proof of residency (utility bill, lease, mortgage contract, or Maryland driver's license with current address)
Proof of income (4 weeks consecutive pay stubs, tax returns, Employment Verification Statement; self-employed: Profit & Loss statements, IRS forms 1040, Schedule C or K-1)
Proof of activity/work hours and schedule (current school/training schedule for education/training activities)
Social Security Number or Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (ITIN)
Child birth certificates or proof of age
Documentation of other benefits if applicable (SNAP, TCA, WAG, GBI, Housing Assistance)
Special documentation for migrant workers, homeless individuals, and emancipated minors
For informal providers: criminal background check with fingerprinting (applicant and all household members 18+); renewed every 5 years
For informal providers: notarized Child Protective Services consent form (annually)
For informal providers: completion of Basic Health & Safety Training (3 hours, 80%+ passing score) and annual Training Update (1.5 hours)
For informal providers: Adult, Child and Baby First Aid/CPR/AED certification (in-person skills component required)
For informal providers: compliance with health and safety standards including emergency preparedness, safe sleep practices, immunizations, first aid/CPR
For informal providers: no more than 6 children in care at one time; no more than 2 children under age 2
For informal providers: Emergency Preparedness Plan and Emergency Ready-to-Go Pack completed with parent
For informal providers: Emergency Care & Medication Authorization Form signed by parent, provider, and healthcare provider
For informal providers: blood-lead level testing documentation for children under age 6
For informal providers: immunization records and physical examination documentation for children
For providers: must respond to scholarship requests within 5 business days
For providers: must submit attendance and invoicing records at end of each service period
For providers: must maintain sign-in/sign-out logs and invoices
For providers: must report when child is no longer in care, rate changes, and maintain current payment address information
For providers: must comply with program integrity audit requirements
For providers: disputes must be submitted within 90 days of receipt of payment/notification
Incident reporting within 24 hours of reportable incidents
5 working days notice required to stop caring for a child or to change providers
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Create an account on the Child Care Scholarship Family Portal at family.childcareportals.org. Step 2: Complete and submit the short Fast Track online application with three documents: proof of employment/training/school enrollment, proof of residency, and proof of income. Step 3: CCS Central 2 processes the Fast Track application within 3 business days. Step 4: If eligible, a temporary 60-day scholarship is issued. Within 15 days of Fast Track approval, submit additional documentation (4 weeks of pay stubs, proof of identity, proof of approved activity, proof of all other income, proof of address) for a full 52-week scholarship review. Redetermination must be submitted 45 days before end of current eligibility period. For licensed/registered providers, register an account at https://provider.childcareportals.org/, complete user registration with two-factor authentication, select provider type, and submit the appropriate application. For informal providers, submit the Informal Provider Initial or Renewal Application with all required documentation via the Provider Portal; a health/safety inspection is required prior to approval. Providers manage scholarship requests, submit attendance and invoice records through the portal dashboard. To find a participating program, search at https://findaprogram.marylandexcels.org/ or contact Maryland Family Network at 877-261-0060. For help completing your application, call 1-877-227-0125, press 3. Translation and interpreter services are available.

structured_extraction.program_name: Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP) reimburses child and adult care agencies for the cost of nutritionally balanced meals and snacks served to eligible children and adults at participating childcare centers, daycare homes, afterschool care programs, emergency shelters, and adult day care facilities. The program supports healthy growth and development for young children and promotes health and wellness for older adults and people with chronic disabilities enrolled in participating care facilities. Funds are used to offset meal and supplement costs to public, private nonprofit, or proprietary centers licensed to provide non-residential childcare services and eligible adult daycare centers. Over 300 agencies across Maryland participate.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participating agencies receive federally funded cash reimbursements for nutritious meals and snacks (breakfast, lunch, snack) that meet USDA nutrition standards and meal patterns. Sponsors also receive cash-in-lieu of USDA Foods with their meal reimbursements. Emergency shelters receive the highest reimbursement rates with the least paperwork requirements. Reimburses for meals served to eligible children (including infants) in childcare settings and adults over 60 or living with a disability in daycare facilities. Providers manage financial claims through the Maryland Accountability and Reporting System (MARS).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Childcare centers, daycare homes, afterschool care programs, emergency shelters, and adult day care centers serving children (including infants), older adults (60+), and adults with disabilities across Maryland. Includes public, private non-profit, and for-profit centers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reimbursement for the cost of nutritious meals and snacks served to enrolled participants that meet USDA nutrition standards and meal patterns.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across all Maryland counties. Over 300 agencies across Maryland participate.
requirements_list: Must be a childcare center, daycare home, afterschool care program, emergency shelter, or adult day care facility
Must be licensed to provide non-residential child or adult care services
Meals and snacks must comply with USDA nutrition standards and meal patterns
Family Child Care providers must participate through an approved sponsoring organization
Adults served must be age 60 or older or living with a disability and enrolled in a daycare facility
Children served must be age 18 or younger (for emergency shelters, automatically eligible for free meals)
Complete CACFP Interest Survey and Budget Worksheet
Complete CACFP Basics Training
Complete three-part online application
Pass pre-approval visit by MSDE
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call MSDE or a sponsoring organization to begin. Complete the CACFP Interest Survey and Budget Worksheet. MSDE determines eligibility. Center completes CACFP Basics Training and the three-part online application. MSDE conducts a pre-approval visit. MSDE approves participation and reimbursement begins. Family Child Care providers should contact one of the approved sponsoring agencies listed on the page for their county. Providers manage financial claims through the Maryland Accountability and Reporting System (MARS). Contact the Office of School and Community Nutrition Programs for additional information on participation.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Client Assistance Program (CAP) advocates for the rights of people with disabilities who are applying for or receiving services from Maryland's Centers for Independent Living (CILs) or the Maryland State Department of Education's Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS). CAP provides free information, advice, and advocacy to help resolve concerns about vocational rehabilitation (VR) employment services, Pre-Employment Transition Services (Pre-ETS), and independent living (IL) services. This includes explaining rights and responsibilities, helping communicate concerns to DORS or CIL staff, explaining policies and procedures, advocating for individuals denied or unhappy with a service, arranging legal services for formal appeals when necessary, and informing individuals about employment rights under the Americans with Disabilities Act. CAP also assists with mediation and the formal appeal process when concerns cannot be resolved at lower levels. CAP handles questions and complaints about vocational rehabilitation and independent living services statewide and is accessible by phone or email.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: CAP provides free information, advice, and advocacy services. This includes explaining rights and responsibilities in VR employment, Pre-ETS, and IL processes; helping communicate concerns to DORS or CIL staff; explaining policies and procedures; advocating for individuals denied or unhappy with a service; arranging legal services for formal appeals when necessary; and informing individuals about employment rights under the Americans with Disabilities Act. CAP also assists with mediation and the formal appeal process, including scheduling hearings through the Office of Administrative Hearings (OAH) within 60 days of a DORS decision or action. Accessible by phone or email.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Within 60 days of the DORS decision or action (for appeals)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Marylanders with disabilities who are applying for or receiving services from DORS or a Center for Independent Living (CIL), including students ages 14-21 seeking Pre-Employment Transition Services, legally blind individuals age 55 and over, and any individuals experiencing difficulties with or dissatisfied with vocational rehabilitation or independent living services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Advocacy, information, legal representation referrals, mediation assistance, and assistance resolving disputes with DORS or CIL regarding vocational rehabilitation, pre-employment transition, or independent living services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to Maryland residents with disabilities. Seven Centers for Independent Living located throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Must have a disability
Must be applying for or currently receiving services from DORS or a Maryland Center for Independent Living (CIL)
Must be applying for or receiving vocational rehabilitation or independent living services in Maryland

For formal appeals: written appeal request must include the action/decision being appealed, a brief statement of reasons, the requested action/response, signature of the individual or authorized representative, and contact information
Appeal request must be submitted within 60 days of the DORS decision or action
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact CAP by phone (410-554-9361 or toll-free 1-800-638-6243), fax (410-554-9362), or email (cap.dors@maryland.gov) to request assistance. For formal appeals, submit a written appeal request to the Assistant State Superintendent in Rehabilitation Services at DORS (2301 Argonne Drive, Baltimore, MD 21218) or by email to dors@maryland.gov. A written acknowledgment will be provided, and a hearing will be scheduled through the Office of Administrative Hearings (OAH) within 60 days. Mediation is available if both parties agree prior to the hearing. An Administrative Law Judge serves as the impartial hearing officer.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Eligibility Provision (CEP) is a meal service option that allows schools and school districts in low-income areas to serve free breakfast and lunch to all enrolled students without collecting household income applications. It promotes equity and access to nutritious meals during the school day.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Schools and school districts that elect CEP receive federal reimbursement to provide free breakfast and lunch to all enrolled students at no cost. No household income applications are required. Reimbursement is based on the school's Identified Student Percentage (ISP).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public schools and school districts in low-income areas with an Identified Student Percentage (ISP) of 25% or higher
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Providing free breakfast and lunch to all enrolled students without charge
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to eligible schools and school districts throughout Maryland
requirements_list: School or school district must have an Identified Student Percentage (ISP) of 25% or higher
Identified students are those directly certified for free meals through participation in programs such as SNAP and TANF
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Schools and school districts with a qualifying ISP elect to participate in CEP. Detailed Maryland CEP data and participating schools are available on the Data page.

structured_extraction.program_description: CCEIS is a federal grant program under IDEA Part B that requires local education agencies (LEAs) identified by Maryland as having significant racial or ethnic disproportionality in special education — including identification of children as disabled, placement in particular educational settings, or disciplinary actions — to reserve 15% of their IDEA Part B Section 611 and Section 619 funds for early intervening services. These reserved funds must be used to implement a comprehensive, proactive system addressing the root causes of overidentification. LEAs without significant disproportionality may also voluntarily elect to use IDEA Part B funds for CCEIS. Services target students in kindergarten through grade 12 (ages 3–21) who are not currently identified as needing special education but who need additional academic and behavioral support to succeed in general education settings, as well as students currently identified as requiring special education or related services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: LEAs identified as having significant disproportionality must reserve 15% of their IDEA Part B Section 611 and Section 619 funds (including CCEIS 611, CCEIS ARP 611, CCEIS 619, and CCEIS ARP 619 grants) to implement CCEIS. Allowable uses include educational and behavioral evaluations, services and supports (including evidence-based literacy instruction), professional development and coaching for general and special education staff, systemic planning activities, root cause analysis, implementation of equity-focused changes to address overidentification in special education, staff salaries (teachers, counselors, psychologists, social workers, coordinators), tutoring/coaching services, instructional materials, software and computing devices for struggling students, substitute teachers, and extended contracts. Not allowable: special education evaluations, student transportation, furniture, office equipment, rent, core curriculum costs, and universal screening costs. LEAs without significant disproportionality may voluntarily set aside IDEA Part B funds for early intervening services. All funds must supplement (not supplant) state, local, and other federal funds per 34 CFR §300.202(a)(3).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Interim Report #1: January 31, 2025; Interim Report #2: January 31, 2026; Grant Amendment Requests: August 15, 2026; Final Report: November 30, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local education agencies (LEAs) in Maryland, particularly those identified by the state as having significant racial or ethnic disproportionality in special education identification, placement, or disciplinary actions, as well as LEAs that voluntarily elect to use IDEA Part B funds for early intervening services. Program ultimately serves students ages 3–21, particularly from racial/ethnic groups experiencing disproportionate identification, placement, or discipline in special education.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational and behavioral evaluations, services and supports (including evidence-based literacy instruction), professional development and coaching for general and special education staff, systemic planning activities, root cause analysis, implementation of equity-focused changes to address overidentification in special education, academic and behavioral supports for students not yet identified for special education, staff salaries, tutoring/coaching services, instructional materials, software and computing devices, substitute teachers, extended contracts, tier 2 and tier 3 interventions, and review and revision of policies and procedures contributing to disproportionality.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to local education agencies across all Maryland jurisdictions, with mandatory participation for those identified as having significant disproportionality in special education.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Maryland local education agency

LEAs identified as having significant disproportionality — a risk ratio greater than 2.0 for two or more consecutive years in identification, placement, or disciplinary actions for one or more racial or ethnic subgroups — must participate; others may voluntarily elect to participate
LEA must reserve 15% of IDEA Part B Section 611 and Section 619 funds for CCEIS activities (for required participants)
Must complete and submit CCEIS Plan Template
Must submit C-1-25 Budget Forms (including C-1-25, C-1-25 A, C-1-25 B) and Budget Detail
Must document allowable costs per the CCEIS Allowable Costs Stoplight guidance
Must obtain CCEIS Plan Review and Feedback Tool from MSDE
LEA must address root cause factors contributing to significant disproportionality
LEA must address and review a policy, practice, or procedure contributing to overidentification
Must submit progress reports as required during the grant period (Interim Report #1: January 31, 2025; Interim Report #2: January 31, 2026; Final Report: November 30, 2026)
Non-supplantation compliance required per 34 CFR §300.202(a)(3)
Self-assessment using guiding questions addressing identification, placement, and disciplinary removals
Four required signatures: Local Director of Special Education, Chief Academic Officer, Finance Officer, and Superintendent
Staff must be appropriately licensed for academic instruction
Interventions must be scientifically based
Instructional materials and software must be exclusively for struggling students identified through universal screening
Proper time and effort records required for staff charged to grant
Data collection, root cause analysis, co-implementation, and co-evaluation required
Progress monitoring of Problem Resolution Activities (PRAs) required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Identified LEAs must complete the CCEIS Plan Template and required C-1-25 Budget Forms and Budget Detail, then submit them to the MSDE Division of Special Education/Division of Early Intervention and Special Education Services (DEI/SES). For a copy of the CCEIS Plan Review and Feedback Tool, contact Interagency Equity Specialist Demetria White at demetria.white@maryland.gov. Amendment templates and progress report templates are also available on the program page. Submit programmatic amendments using the CCEIS Plan Programmatic Amendment Template with required multi-signature approvals from local and state officials. Submit progress and fiscal reports per specified deadlines: Interim Report #1 by January 31, 2025; Interim Report #2 by January 31, 2026; Grant Amendment Requests by August 15, 2026; Final Report by November 30, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: CPSEO is a Pre-Employment Transition Services (Pre-ETS) program that provides counseling on post-secondary education options to students with autism. Students explore options such as apprenticeships, job training, direct job placement, and college, and participate in a college tour.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Classroom and community-based activities that expose students to post-secondary options including apprenticeships, job training, direct job placement, and college. Program also includes a college tour.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Pre-Employment Transition Services (Pre-ETS) eligible students with autism.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Counseling and exploration of post-secondary education and employment pathways.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Student with autism eligible for Pre-Employment Transition Services (Pre-ETS)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact DORS to connect with Pre-ETS services and enroll in the program.

structured_extraction.program_description: DORS Apprenticeship Services help Marylanders with disabilities explore, access, and participate in registered apprenticeship programs across Maryland. Registered apprenticeships are paid jobs combining on-the-job training from skilled craftspeople with related classroom instruction, with apprentices paid according to progressive pay scales. Services include consultations, academic assessments, exploration of apprenticeship opportunities, academic instruction, and ongoing support for individuals in pre-apprenticeship, registered apprenticeship, and youth apprenticeship programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free consultation, academic assessment, exploration services, academic instruction, and coordination support to help individuals with disabilities prepare for, apply to, and participate in registered apprenticeship programs. Services are delivered by an Apprenticeship Coordinator and Academic Instructor for Apprenticeship Services. Includes connection to existing apprenticeship programs or development of customized registered apprenticeship programs, and recruitment support through American Job Centers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Marylanders with disabilities who are interested in pursuing registered apprenticeships; individuals 18+ seeking apprenticeships
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Preparing for, applying to, and participating in registered apprenticeship programs, including academic remediation and skills assessments
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a DORS consumer (individual with a disability served by DORS)
Must be interested in exploring or pursuing a registered apprenticeship
Be 18 years of age
Have high school diploma (graduation, GED®, or NEDP)
Have transportation
Be drug free
Be physically able to perform required tasks
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Sam Grimsley at 410-554-9288 or Samantha.Grimsley@maryland.gov to learn more and get started. For apprentices: Visit occupations.mdapprenticeship.com, then call/email an apprenticeship navigator, and apply directly to the program sponsor/employer.

structured_extraction.program_description: Services to help Maryland businesses grow by connecting them with qualified job seekers with disabilities. The DORS Business Relations Team provides no-cost services to Maryland employers, including recruitment assistance, ADA consultation, worksite assessments, onsite training, and assistance with paid internships and apprenticeships for individuals with disabilities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: No-cost services including: pre-screening qualified job candidates, recruitment assistance for open positions, reimbursement of wages for on-the-job training, technical assistance for accessing tax incentives, ADA consultation and reasonable accommodation guidance, worksite assessments, onsite disability awareness and sensitivity training, retention services for employees with disabilities, and assistance with DORS-sponsored paid internships and apprenticeships.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland businesses seeking to hire and support employees with disabilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Wage reimbursement for on-the-job training; tax incentive technical assistance; staff disability and employment training; recruitment and retention services; ADA compliance assistance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland through local DORS Business Relations Representatives.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local DORS Business Relations Representative or the DORS Business Relations Team for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS) partners with private, usually non-profit, Community Rehabilitation Programs (CRPs) to provide rehabilitation and employment services to job seekers with disabilities. DORS approves CRPs to deliver services such as Supported Employment and Employment Services to DORS consumers across Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Approved CRPs receive referrals and funding from DORS to deliver rehabilitation and employment services to DORS consumers with disabilities. Services may include Supported Employment and Employment Services. Approval is based on program capacity, population served, location, cost, service quality, staff credentials, and record of success.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private non-profit organizations that provide rehabilitation and employment services to individuals with disabilities, including those who are blind, vision-impaired, deaf, deaf-blind, or have limited English proficiency.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Delivery of rehabilitation and employment services to DORS consumers with disabilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. DORS is particularly seeking partners in areas serving individuals who are blind, vision-impaired, deaf, deaf-blind, or have limited English proficiency.
requirements_list: Must be a private, usually non-profit, organization

Must be licensed by the Behavioral Health Administration (BHA) or Developmental Disabilities Administration (DDA) for Supported Employment/Employment Services, and/or hold third-party national accreditation such as CARF
Must provide current documentation of 501(c)(3) non-profit status
Must submit a description of the agency including primary clientele, geographic location, mission and values
Must submit a description of services to be provided, staff qualifications, service length, and expected outcomes
Must submit an agency annual report
Must provide copies of current licenses from accreditation organizations (CARF, DDA, BHA, etc.)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact one of the DORS Staff Specialists for CRPs (Kate Drake or Tamla McDowell-Omodho) for more information or to apply. Submit required documentation including proof of non-profit status, agency and service descriptions, annual report, and accreditation copies.

structured_extraction.program_name: DORS Office for Blindness & Vision Services (OBVS)
structured_extraction.program_description: The DORS Office for Blindness & Vision Services (OBVS) provides vocational rehabilitation, independent living, transition, and other specialized services to individuals in Maryland whose primary disability is vision loss, including those who are blind, vision impaired, or deaf-blind. Services include career guidance and exploration, assistive technology (such as screen reading software, magnifiers, and low vision aids), vocational training, academic education support, independent living skills training, orientation and mobility instruction, job placement assistance, transition services for students moving from school to post-school life, and business enterprise opportunities. Counselors, case managers, and teachers are assigned based on where the consumer lives and are located in DORS offices throughout Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: OBVS provides free vocational rehabilitation counseling, career guidance and exploration, assistive technology (such as screen reading software, magnifiers, and low vision aids), career training or academic education, independent living skills training (cooking, personal care, household management), orientation and mobility instruction, job placement services, support for reasonable workplace accommodations, and business enterprise opportunities. OBVS counselors, case managers, and teachers are located in DORS offices throughout Maryland and provide individualized services based on where the consumer lives.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals who are blind, vision impaired, or deaf-blind residing in Maryland and seeking employment, independent living support, or transition services from school to post-school life. Also includes students with disabilities (transition services), individuals aged 55+ with vision loss (ILOB program), and currently employed individuals struggling with vision loss or blindness.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Assistive technology, career training, academic education, independent living skills training, orientation and mobility instruction, job placement support, vocational rehabilitation counseling, and business enterprise program support.

OBVS operates three regional offices: Baltimore region (Baltimore City, Baltimore, Cecil, Howard, and Harford Counties), Wheaton region (Allegany, Carroll, Frederick, Garrett, Montgomery, and Washington Counties), and Annapolis region (Anne Arundel, Calvert, Caroline, Charles, Dorchester, Kent, Prince George's, Queen Anne's, St. Mary's, Somerset, Talbot, Wicomico, and Worcester Counties). OBVS counselors and case managers are assigned based on where the consumer lives.

structured_extraction.program_description: The DORS Rehabilitation Technology Services (RTS) program, operated by the Maryland State Department of Education's Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS), provides customized assistive technology (AT) assessments, training, and technical support to help people with disabilities find, keep, and succeed in employment. Services include worksite job accommodation evaluations, adaptive driving services, blind and low vision services, occupational and physical therapy services, home modification consultation, and hands-on AT training. Examples of assistive technology provided include desktop/portable video magnifiers, note-taking devices, specialized software (such as voice recognition, screen readers like JAWS™, and magnification software like ZoomText™), mobile apps for organization and time management, hand controls for cars, ramps and stair glides, alternative keyboards and mice, and specialized computer-based writing tools. Assessments and training can be conducted at the DORS Workforce & Technology Center (WTC) campus in Baltimore or in the individual's community.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides free customized AT assessments to identify the right equipment or software, along with hands-on training and technical support on AT hardware and software. Training includes specialized classes on JAWS™, ZoomText™, and other AT tools. Services also include worksite evaluations, adaptive driving services, blind and low vision services, occupational and physical therapy services, and home modification consultation. Specific equipment such as desktop/portable video magnifiers, note-taking devices, voice recognition software, screen readers, magnification software, mobile apps for organization/time management, hand controls, ramps, stair glides, alternative keyboards, and specialized writing tools may be provided. Assessments and training can be conducted at the DORS Workforce & Technology Center (WTC) in Baltimore or in the individual's community.
structured_extraction.program_audience: People with disabilities who are job seekers, students, or currently employed; DORS consumers with an employment or school goal; and businesses seeking worksite accommodation support.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Assistive technology devices and software, worksite accommodations, adaptive driving equipment, home modifications, and related assessment and training services to support employment and school goals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Assessments and training conducted at the DORS Workforce & Technology Center (WTC) campus in Baltimore or in the individual's community.
requirements_list: Must have a disability
Must be a job seeker, student, or currently employed, or a business seeking worksite accommodation support
Must be a DORS consumer with an employment or school goal (for AT assessment and training services)

Services can also be requested via QR code. Once enrolled, RTS staff can arrange an AT assessment, worksite evaluation, or other applicable services. Assessments can be conducted at the DORS Workforce & Technology Center in Baltimore or in the community.

structured_extraction.program_name: DORS Vocational Rehabilitation and Employment Services
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS), under the Maryland State Department of Education, helps people with physical, emotional, sensory, cognitive, and learning disabilities prepare for, get, keep, or advance in employment. DORS assesses eligibility and provides vocational rehabilitation services based on the severity of a person's disability, prioritizing those with 'most significant' disabilities under the Order of Selection law. Services are delivered by rehabilitation counselors through more than 20 community offices statewide, at the Workforce and Technology Center (WTC) in northeast Baltimore, and virtually. Employment services include career counseling and skills assessment, assistive technology, job training, college or career training, work-readiness training, higher education support, resume and cover letter development, interview preparation, disability disclosure and reasonable accommodations guidance, professional communication coaching, job placement, employer follow-up after hire, and job coaching referrals. Specialized counselors work with people who are deaf or hard of hearing, blind or vision impaired, or living with mental illness, as well as students with disabilities. Pre-Employment Transition Services (Pre-ETS) are free to students and their families. DORS pays for the least expensive service or product that meets an individual's needs; if a more expensive option is chosen, the individual pays the difference. Some services beyond basic counseling and placement are subject to a financial need determination; SSI/SSDI recipients receive all services at no cost. People aged 55 or older who are blind or vision impaired may also request independent living services. DORS also works with Maryland businesses to support recruitment, onboarding, job retention, disability awareness education, and internship coordination. All services are provided at no cost to eligible individuals. Spanish-language resources, telephone interpreter services, Spanish-language brochures, and Vietnamese-language resources are available. Eligibility determination is completed within 60 days of application. Services are provided based on individual strengths, resources, priorities, concerns, capabilities, aptitudes, and interests, and are subject to availability of state and federal funds and community provider vacancies. Only services pre-approved and authorized in writing by a DORS official are covered.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free vocational rehabilitation and employment support services available statewide, delivered in the community, at the Workforce and Technology Center (WTC) in northeast Baltimore, or virtually through more than 20 community offices. Services include eligibility assessment, vocational counseling and skills assessment, career assessment, assistive technology, job training, college or career training, work-readiness training, higher education support, job-seeking skills training, job search assistance, resume and cover letter development, interview practice, disability disclosure and reasonable accommodations guidance, professional communication coaching, job placement, employer follow-up after hire, and job coaching referrals. A DORS counselor works with each eligible individual to develop a personalized Individualized Employment Plan or Trial Work Plan for employment. Specialized counselors are available for people who are deaf or hard of hearing, blind or vision impaired, or living with mental illness, as well as students with disabilities. Pre-Employment Transition Services (Pre-ETS) are free to students and their families and include job search counseling, self-advocacy training, workplace readiness training, post-secondary education counseling, and work-based learning experiences. Student Employment Services for ages 14-21 include vocational counseling, skills training, job search and placement, job coaching and support, assistive technology solutions, and post-secondary training. Independent living services are available for adults aged 55 or older who are blind or vision impaired. DORS pays for the least expensive service or product meeting the individual's needs; if a costlier option is chosen, the individual pays the difference. Some services beyond basic counseling and placement are subject to a financial need determination; SSI/SSDI recipients receive all services at no cost. Services are prioritized by disability severity: individuals with 'most significant' disabilities (substantial limitations in three or more functional areas) are served first; those with 'significant' disabilities may be placed on a waiting list. SSI and SSDI recipients are presumed eligible. Businesses receive customized training, recruitment support, disability awareness education, and internship coordination assistance. Spanish-language applicants and non-English speakers can access services through telephone interpreter support, Spanish-language brochures, and Vietnamese-language resources. Benefit planning services and Work Incentives Planning and Assistance (Ticket to Work/WIPA) are available for SSI/SSDI recipients. Academic tutoring, GED preparation, behavioral health services, occupational training programs, and work readiness programs are available at the Technology and Workforce Center campus. All services must be pre-approved and authorized in writing by a DORS official and are subject to availability of state and federal funds and community provider vacancies.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents with physical, emotional, cognitive, sensory, or learning disabilities that seriously affect their ability to work, including high school and college students aged 14-21 with disabilities (including those with IEPs or 504 plans), individuals receiving SSI or SSDI who are ready to seek or maintain employment, people who are deaf/hard of hearing, blind or vision impaired, autistic individuals, or living with mental illness, adults aged 55 or older who are blind or vision impaired seeking independent living services, and Maryland businesses seeking to hire and support employees with disabilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Vocational rehabilitation and employment support services to help individuals with disabilities obtain or maintain employment, including career assessment and counseling, assistive technology, vocational training, college or career training, work-readiness training, higher education support, job placement, retention, and job coaching; Pre-Employment Transition Services (Pre-ETS) for students; Student Employment Services for students ages 14-21; independent living services for eligible adults aged 55 or older with vision impairments; benefit planning services and Work Incentives Planning and Assistance for SSI/SSDI recipients; academic tutoring, GED preparation, behavioral health services, and occupational training programs; and recruitment and disability awareness support for businesses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide throughout Maryland through more than 20 community offices, offered in the community, at the Workforce and Technology Center (WTC) in northeast Baltimore, and virtually.
