structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the online Request DORS Services form on the DORS website or contact a local DORS community office by phone to complete the form. Allow approximately 10 business days for your nearest DORS office to process your form and schedule an appointment (virtual or in person) with a DORS counselor. You will receive a written eligibility decision within 60 days. Interpreter services are available by phone for non-English speakers (call and provide your phone number and language; DORS will connect you with a phone interpreter). Spanish-language applicants can follow the process at https://dors.maryland.gov/consumers/Pages/Referral-Spanish.aspx. You may bring a support person (family member, friend, or advocate) to any DORS appointment. Bring medical records, school records (including psychological testing and IEP if applicable), job training records, and a list of previous jobs to your meeting. DORS staff will gather information to determine eligibility and connect you with appropriate services. Work with your DORS counselor to develop an Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE), Individualized Employment Plan, or Customized Employment Plan collaboratively, exploring career options and their pros and cons, job market information, and community resources. Priority is given to individuals with the most significant disabilities. More than 20 community offices are available across Maryland. Customer Assistance Program (CAP) available at 410-554-9361 or 1-800-638-6243. Videophone for Deaf/Hard of Hearing: 410-405-7054. Toll-free: 1-888-554-0334. TTY: 410-554-9411. Appeals may be submitted in writing to the Assistant State Director for Rehabilitation Services, 2301 Argonne Drive, Baltimore, MD 21218.

structured_extraction.program_name: Deaf and Hard of Hearing Unit (DHHU) Vocational Rehabilitation Services
structured_extraction.program_description: The DHHU helps Maryland job seekers who are Deaf or hard of hearing prepare for, find, and keep stable employment. Services include vocational rehabilitation (VR) employment services, student employment services, and Pre-Employment Transition Services (Pre-ETS), as well as career counseling, job coaching, supported employment, assistive technology solutions, job skills training, and job search and placement services. The unit also supports Deaf/hard of hearing students transitioning from school to post-school life and promotes self-advocacy and independence.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides vocational rehabilitation counseling, career assessment and counseling, job coaching and supported employment, job skills training, job search and placement, assistive technology solutions, interpreting services (including Video Remote Interpreting/VRI), higher education support, work-readiness training, and workplace adjustment support to Deaf and hard of hearing job seekers and students across Maryland. Rehabilitation counselors fluent in ASL are located at DORS offices statewide. Services available virtually and via video phone.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Employment preparation, job placement support, transition services, assistive technology, career counseling, job coaching, higher education support, and related vocational rehabilitation services for Deaf and hard of hearing individuals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide throughout Maryland. DHHU rehabilitation counselors are located at DORS offices throughout the state. Services also available virtually and via video phone.

Students must be ages 14-21

People who are deaf automatically qualify for Category 2 priority

structured_extraction.program_description: DORS provides specialized vocational rehabilitation services for people who are Deaf-Blind, including Braille training from Deaf-Blind instructors, Orientation and Mobility (O&M) training, job coaching from trained providers, and access to Rehabilitation Counselors for the Deaf who communicate in American Sign Language (ASL). A comprehensive resource directory connects DeafBlind individuals in Maryland to services including ASL/Pro-Tactile interpretation, assisted living, assistive technology, employment services, education, mental health, transportation, telecommunications access, and more.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides specialized support services including Braille training, Orientation and Mobility instruction, job coaching, and communication-accessible rehabilitation counseling for Deaf-Blind individuals seeking employment and community participation. Also includes a comprehensive resource directory connecting DeafBlind individuals to interpretation services, assistive technology, mental health counseling, addiction services, independent living skills training, legal aid, advocacy, housing, transportation, telecommunications devices (including large screen captioned telephones, RTT, VRS apps), and other community services.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Braille training, Orientation and Mobility instruction, job coaching, access to community and vocational rehabilitation services, telecommunications devices, interpretation services, mental health and addiction services, independent living skills training, legal aid, advocacy, housing, and transportation.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Rehabilitation Services (DORS), administered through the Maryland State Department of Education, provides driver rehabilitation and vehicle modification services for people with disabilities who need to drive or be transported independently in order to get or keep a job. Services include driving assessments, driver education classes (with two tracks: Track 1 for autism, Track 2 for all others), adapted driving training, and vehicle modification evaluations and funding. Certified driving instructors and occupational therapists evaluate and train individuals, and state-licensed evaluators determine what vehicle modifications are needed. State funding is also available to help eligible individuals cover the cost of modifying their vehicles. Services must be included in the individual's Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE). ASL interpreting services are provided.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Services include: (1) Driving Assessment – certified instructors and occupational therapists evaluate ability to drive; (2) Driver Education – a 30-hour MVA-approved curriculum plus 6-hour behind-the-wheel training, offered in person at WTC, locally in some communities, and virtually. Two tracks available: Track 1 for autism, Track 2 for all other disabilities. WTC provides 2-3 additional class sessions beyond commercial standards. ASL interpreting services provided; (3) Adapted Driving – determination of adaptive equipment needs and training on adaptive equipment needed for a driver's license; (4) Vehicle Modification – evaluation and state-funded modification of consumer-owned vehicles so individuals with disabilities can enter, exit, and operate them safely. Vehicle modifications are available only for vehicles owned (not leased) by the DORS consumer or their family. Services must be included in the individual's Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE). Exact dollar amounts for vehicle modification funding are not specified.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents with disabilities who are DORS consumers and need driving, adapted driving training, or vehicle modification services to obtain or maintain employment or drive/be transported independently.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Driver assessment, driver education, adapted driving training, and vehicle modification for employment-related transportation needs, including funding to cover the cost of modifying a vehicle to accommodate a person with a disability and enable them to drive to and from work. Also covers adaptive equipment provision and training.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to eligible DORS consumers statewide in Maryland. Services are provided at the Workforce & Technology Center (WTC), locally in some communities, and virtually.
requirements_list: Must apply for DORS services and be determined eligible
Must have a disability requiring driver rehabilitation or vehicle modification services
Driver and vehicle services must be included in the individual's Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE)
Services must be needed to help the individual get or maintain a job

A Learner's Permit is required to complete the 6-hour Behind-the-Wheel training portion of driver education (not required for the 30-hour classroom portion)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your DORS counselor or local DORS office, or complete the Request DORS Services form at dors.maryland.gov to begin the eligibility process. You may also call DORS at 410-554-9100 (TTY 410-554-9411). Once eligible, work with your counselor to include these services in your Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE). Services can also be requested via QR code on program materials.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Early Literacy Coaching Network (ELCN) is a Maryland State Department of Education initiative that strengthens K–3 literacy instruction through aligned, job-embedded coaching. It brings early literacy coaches together through regional in-person convenings and virtual Communities of Practice to deepen understanding of the Maryland Coaching Model, engage with evidence-based reading tools, and earn professional development credit toward Maryland Educator License renewal.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive in-person regional convenings (full-day, 9am–4pm) and synchronous online virtual Communities of Practice (3-hour half-day sessions). Coaches can earn 1 Professional Development Point (PDP) per clock hour of engagement, applicable toward Maryland Educator License renewal. Invitations are sent to current network participants; future cohort information will be announced.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland elementary early literacy coaches (K–3)
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Professional learning and coaching support, including applying MSDE literacy tools, deepening understanding of science of reading instruction, and engaging in collaborative learning to improve classroom literacy instruction.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to Maryland elementary literacy coaches.

Must be invited as a current network participant or join a future cohort
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Invitations are sent to current network participants. Interested coaches should stay tuned for information on the next cohort.

structured_extraction.program_name: Enhanced Child Care Support and Teacher Retention Award (ECSTRA) Retention Bonus Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The ECSTRA program provides retention bonuses to early childhood educators who remain employed in eligible child care roles. It uses American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funds to help stabilize the early childhood educator workforce and reduce high turnover rates in child care settings. Inspired by Virginia's Teacher Recognition Program, which reduced turnover by 50%, ECSTRA includes a research component to study the impact of different bonus sizes on retention outcomes. Educators apply, meet eligibility criteria, and participate in a lottery to determine their bonus amount ($0, $1,000, $2,000, or $3,000). Bonuses are paid in two equal installments: the first after at least 5 months of continued employment and the second after at least 8 months. Up to 7,500 educators are eligible to receive bonuses.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Retention bonuses ranging from $1,000 to $3,000, determined by lottery, paid in two equal installments to eligible early childhood educators who remain employed in the same program in an eligible role. The first half of the bonus is paid after at least 5 months of continued employment (by April 2024), and the second half after at least 8 months (by June 2024). Up to 7,500 educators are eligible to receive bonuses.

FAQs and customer service support sessions are available on the MSDE Grants office website.

structured_extraction.program_name: Food Is Safe Here (FISH) Initiative – Food Safety for School Programs (ServSafe)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Food Is Safe Here (FISH) Initiative is an ongoing program providing food safety training options and resources for school food service personnel in Maryland who participate in federally funded Child Nutrition Programs. A key component is the ServSafe Manager Training and Certification and ServSafe Food Handler Training for school nutrition professionals. This includes nationally recognized food safety credentials and basic food safety instruction, covering onboarding and refresher training. Certified ServSafe Instructors from local education agencies (LEAs) can teach classes and order materials at no cost, and Certified Proctors can order answer sheets and administer exams at no cost.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Ongoing food safety training options and resources for school food service personnel participating in federally funded Child Nutrition Programs. Includes ServSafe Manager Training and Certification (minimum 8 hours, meets USDA Professional Standards requirements) and ServSafe Food Handler training materials. Certified Instructors from LEAs can teach classes and order materials at no cost. Certified Proctors can order answer sheets and administer exams at no cost. Orders must be placed four weeks in advance of scheduled training.
structured_extraction.program_audience: School food service personnel, School Nutrition Managers, Supervisors, Directors, and other staff required to receive food safety training under USDA Professional Standards, as well as Certified ServSafe Instructors and Proctors from LEAs, all participating in federally funded Child Nutrition Programs in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Food safety training and resources, including food safety manager certification and food handler training for school nutrition staff.

This is followed by a seven-week paid internship at a local business for hands-on experience.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Vocational training in food handling, preparation, kitchen safety, customer service, and related skills leading to employment in food service occupations such as cafeterias, restaurants, and food stores.

Must be able to follow two-step instructions
Must be able to lift and carry 30 lb. food containers and trays
Must be able to stand for long periods of time
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact a DORS Counselor or local DORS office to apply. Applicants are assessed for eligibility and physical requirements before enrollment.

structured_extraction.program_description: General Education Development (GED) program for individuals with disabilities who need a high school diploma to pursue their employment goals. Students work individually or in small groups on a rolling admission basis.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: GED instruction offered individually or in small groups at WTC and virtually. Students are expected to take the formal GED test upon completion. GED Ready Practice Tests may also be given.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with disabilities who need a high school diploma to achieve their employment goals.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Preparation for and completion of the GED high school equivalency exam.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at WTC and virtually.
requirements_list: Must have at least 8th grade reading and math skills as recorded on the CASAS or TABE.
GED Ready Practice Tests may also be given.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Rolling admission; work with a DORS counselor to enroll.

structured_extraction.program_name: Healthy Hunger Free Kid's Act Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides funds to eligible schools and residential child care institutions. The money helps them comply with meal pattern rules established by the Healthy Hunger Free Kids Act of 2010.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides direct payments for specific uses to help schools and child care institutions comply with federal meal pattern rules.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible schools and residential child care institutions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds help schools and child care centers meet the meal pattern requirements of the Healthy Hunger Free Kids Act of 2010.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS) provides home modification services to help people with disabilities access their homes so they can achieve their employment goals. A team evaluates and improves home accessibility through construction coordination, onsite monitoring, and ADA compliance checks.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides assessment of bathroom accessibility, home entry/exit, and multi-level access; coordinates and schedules construction for modifications; conducts onsite monitoring during construction; coordinates final inspections; and confirms all modifications comply with the Americans with Disabilities Act. Services take place in the participant's home.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Current DORS consumers with disabilities who need home modifications to achieve an employment goal and who own or whose family owns the property.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home modifications to improve accessibility including bathroom access, home entry and exit, and access to different levels of the home.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to DORS consumers statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Individual must be a current DORS consumer.
Modifications must be needed to achieve an employment goal.
Modifications must be for property owned by the DORS consumer or their family.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact DORS to enroll as a consumer, then work with the WTC home modification team for evaluation and services.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Independent Living Older Blind (ILOB) Program helps people aged 55 and older who are blind or have a vision impairment to live independently in their homes and communities. Rehabilitation specialists visit participants at home to provide assessment and training in daily living skills, personal care, household tasks, safe cooking, and connections to community resources and peer support groups.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Home-based rehabilitation services including training in personal care, household tasks, labeling and organizing items (clothing, appliances, medications), safe cooking techniques, orientation and mobility training, Braille instruction, assistive technology use, and referrals to community resources and peer support groups such as NFB-NEWSLINE and Maryland State Library for the Blind and Print Disabled. Rehabilitation specialists work with ophthalmologists, low vision specialists, and community partners to provide personalized service. No employment goal is required. Services are provided at no stated cost to eligible individuals.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents aged 55 or older who are blind or have a vision impairment and wish to live independently at home and in their community. No upper age limit.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and support services to help older adults with blindness or vision impairment maintain independence in their homes and communities, including in-home rehabilitation specialist assessment, personal care and household task training, and community resource referrals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout all areas of Maryland, including rural counties. Regional offices serve: Baltimore City and Baltimore, Cecil, Howard, and Harford Counties (410-261-2954); Allegany, Carroll, Frederick, Garrett, Montgomery, and Washington Counties (301-949-3750); Anne Arundel, Calvert, Caroline, Charles, Dorchester, Kent, Prince George's, Queen Anne's, St. Mary's, Somerset, Talbot, Wicomico, and Worcester Counties (410-974-7604).
requirements_list: Must be 55 years of age or older
Must be blind or have a vision impairment
No upper age limit
Employment goal not required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Request DORS Services form online (can be submitted by the individual, a family member, medical provider, or caretaker). After submission, DORS will contact you to set up an intake appointment to gather information and determine eligibility.

structured_extraction.program_name: Infant & Early Childhood Mental Health Support Services Program Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: This grant supports positive mental and behavioral health practices for young children who have developmental, social, emotional, or behavioral issues. It funds referrals and services for children, families, teachers, and caregivers, and builds the capacity of early care and education providers and families to promote healthy social-emotional development.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding to non-profit and public agencies to provide infant and early childhood mental health services, including referrals and direct services for children, families, teachers, and caregivers.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No later than 5:00 p.m. on Wednesday, August 9, 2023
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit and public agencies licensed to do business in Maryland with proven capacity to provide Infant and Early Childhood Mental Health Services and that operate 12 months per year except for federal holidays.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Providing referrals and mental health services for young children with developmental, social, emotional, or behavioral issues, and building capacity of early care and education providers and families to promote healthy social-emotional development.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be licensed to do business within the State of Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a non-profit or public agency
Must be licensed to do business in Maryland
Must have proven capacity to provide Infant and Early Childhood Mental Health Services
Must operate 12 months per year except for federal holidays
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the application form and submit by 5:00 p.m. on August 9, 2023. Applicants may attend virtual customer service support sessions held by MSDE in June and July 2023 to learn about program requirements and the proposal process.

structured_extraction.program_name: Judy Centers (Judith P. Hoyer Early Child Care and Family Education Centers)
structured_extraction.program_description: Judy Centers, also known as Judy Center Early Learning Hubs, are grant-funded programs located in elementary schools across Maryland, typically within Title I and high-needs school catchment areas. They serve as comprehensive community hubs where families with children from prenatal through age five can access early childhood education and support services available 7–12 hours a day, year round. Services include developmental screenings, family learning activities, parenting classes and workshops, evidence-based home visiting, early intervention identification, case management, adult education connections, and referrals to community support services. The program also provides grants to child care providers for accreditation and professional development programs for staff. The program uses a multigenerational approach to prepare at-risk children for school readiness by empowering families, especially those in historically underserved communities. FY 2024 total funding was $28,380,000, sourced from American Rescue Plan Funds, MSDE General Funds, and Blueprint for Maryland's Future Funds.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant-funded programs housed in Title I and high-needs elementary schools provide families with direct services including developmental screenings, family learning activities, parenting classes and workshops, evidence-based home visiting, early intervention identification, case management, and referrals to community support services. Services are available 7–12 hours a day, year round. Includes parent and child playgroup sessions (minimum 2 per week), professional learning opportunities for partners, bilingual education options, and inclusion of children with disabilities (IEP/IFSP). Grants are also provided to child care providers for accreditation and professional development programs for staff. FY 2024 total funding was $28,380,000 with a typical per-center allocation of $330,000. An Expansion Grant Application for Fiscal Year 2026 is available for eligible applicants.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with children from prenatal through age five who reside in Title I or high-needs school districts in Maryland, within the school zone of an elementary school hosting a Judy Center; also child care providers, community partners, and school staff who serve at-risk children from birth to age five and their families.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Early childhood education and support services for young children and their families to support school readiness, including child development support, family engagement, parenting education, developmental screenings, home visiting, early intervention, adult education connections, and case management services. Funds also support accreditation and professional development programs for child care provider staff, playgroup programming, professional learning opportunities, community outreach and interpreter services, outdoor learning space development, and family support resources.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across all 24 Maryland jurisdictions in specific Title I and high-needs school districts (schools scoring 0.6 or above on the CDC's Social Vulnerability Index); services are provided to children and families living within the school zone of the elementary school where the Judy Center is located.
requirements_list: Child must be from prenatal through age five
Families must reside in a specific Title I or high-needs school district in Maryland
Child must live within the school zone of the elementary school where the Judy Center is located
High-needs schools must score 0.6 or above on the CDC's Social Vulnerability Index to qualify as a host site
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your closest Judy Center Early Learning Hub directly or visit the Maryland State Department of Education early childhood website at http://earlychildhood.marylandpublicschools.org/families/judy-centers for more details. A Judy Center Expansion Grant Application for Fiscal Year 2026 is also available for program expansion applicants. Grant applications are typically due in June annually.

structured_extraction.program_name: LEA/PA Part B Grants (IDEA Part B 611 and 619 Federal Funds) – Local Application for Federal Funds (LAFF)
structured_extraction.program_description: Federal grants under the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA) Part B that provide funding to Maryland local education agencies (LEAs) and public agencies (PAs) to support special education and related services for children and students with disabilities ages 3 through 21, ensuring a free appropriate public education (FAPE). Covered activities include early childhood intervention, secondary transition, access/equity/progress initiatives, preschool special education, family support services, and related expenditures. Each eligible LEA and PA must develop and submit a Local Application for Federal Funds (LAFF) to receive and spend IDEA Part B 611 (school-age) and 619 (preschool) funds. Applications, budgets, and supporting documents are submitted via the MSDE MOVEit Secure File Transfer site, and agencies must comply with applicable programmatic and fiscal regulations including maintenance of effort and excess cost requirements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal IDEA Part B 611 (school-age) and 619 (preschool) funds are allocated to eligible Maryland LEAs and public agencies through a formal Local Application for Federal Funds (LAFF) process. Recipients must submit a grants application, budget documents (including C-1 Budget Forms and Budget Detail and a budget workbook), Local Implementation for Results (LIR) plans, and comply with maintenance of effort and excess cost requirements. Funds support special education staffing, services, and related expenditures for students with disabilities, including preschool special education, early childhood intervention, secondary transition, family support services, and access, equity, and progress activities. Required documents include the LAFF Grant Information Guide and Application, Primary Passthrough, PPPSS Plan (if applicable), SECAC Plan (if applicable), Family Support Services Template (if applicable), CCEIS Declaration Form/Plan (if applicable), GEPA Form, LIR Plan Templates, Comparative Staffing/Funding Data Form, Preschool Special Education Budgeted Expenditures form, and C-1 Budget Forms, all uploaded to the MSDE MOVEit Secure File Transfer site.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annual submission cycle; LIR due August 15; CCEIS Plan due June 30; Maintenance of Effort and Excess Costs due January 31; see Part B Grants Calendar and Submission Timeline for specific dates
structured_extraction.contact_name: Daniele Redivo, Management Associate; Gary W. Richardson, MBA, Branch Chief; Nancy Vorobey, Fiscal Liaison
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland local education agencies (LEAs) and public agencies (PAs) responsible for providing special education and related services for children with disabilities under IDEA Part B
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Providing free appropriate public education (FAPE) for children and students with disabilities ages 3 through 21, including special education staffing, services, preschool special education and related services, early childhood intervention, secondary transition services, family support services, comprehensive coordinated early intervening services (CCEIS), and access, equity, and progress initiatives
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to all Maryland local education agencies and public agencies across all Maryland jurisdictions
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland LEA or public agency receiving federal IDEA Part B funds
Must develop and submit a Local Application for Federal Funds (LAFF) for expenditure of federal funds
Must comply with applicable programmatic and fiscal regulations
Submissions must be uploaded to the MSDE MOVEit Secure File Transfer site
Files must be correctly named and contain only one submission per file
LEAs required to address Significant Disproportionality must reserve 15% of Part B 611 and 619 funds for Comprehensive Coordinated Early Intervening Services (CCEIS)
Must submit required progress/variance reports and financial reports on schedule
All uploaded files must follow MSDE MOVEit submission procedures to be considered timely filed
Must submit completed LAFF Application and Grants Information Guide documentation
Must submit Family Support Services Plan Template if applicable
Must submit required LIR (Locally Identified Results) plan templates for applicable areas (Early Childhood, Secondary Transition, Access/Equity/Progress)
Must submit Comparative Staffing/Funding Data Form
Must submit Preschool Special Education Budgeted Expenditures form
Must submit C-1 Budget Forms and Budget Detail
Must submit grants application and budget workbook
Must submit CCEIS Plan by June 30 if required
Must demonstrate maintenance of effort compliance
Must demonstrate excess cost compliance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Attend the LAFF Information Session(s). Download the LAFF Grant Information Guide and Application from the MSDE website. Complete the application, budget, and required attachments (including Primary Passthrough, PPPSS Plan if applicable, SECAC Plan if applicable, Family Support Services Template if applicable, CCEIS Declaration Form/Plan if applicable, GEPA Form, LIR Plan Templates for applicable areas, Comparative Staffing/Funding Data Form, Preschool Special Education Budgeted Expenditures form, and C-1 Budget Forms and Budget Detail). Submit required financial compliance certifications (maintenance of effort, excess cost) on the established schedule. Upload all submissions to the MSDE MOVEit Secure File Transfer site following the naming and submission requirements in the MSDE MOVEit Secure File Transfer Website Access and Submission Procedures document.

structured_extraction.program_name: Licensing Compliance Grant for Family Child Care Providers (LCGFCCP)
structured_extraction.program_description: This grant helps registered family child care providers offset the costs of opening or maintaining their child care programs. It reimburses eligible expenses needed to achieve or maintain compliance with Maryland family child care regulations, up to $1,000 per provider.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimburses up to $1,000 in expenses a provider incurs to achieve or maintain compliance with family child care regulations. Eligible expenses include safety supplies, provider medical examination fees, criminal background check fees, small household repairs in approved child care areas, approved training course fees, costs related to local water/sewer/fire/health requirements, program materials and equipment, and other costs necessary to complete the registration process.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Registered family child care providers whose annual income does not exceed 60% of Maryland's State Median Income (SMI) for their family size.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Safety supplies, provider medical exam fees, criminal background check fees, small household repairs in child care areas, approved training course fees, water/sewer/fire/health compliance costs, program materials and equipment, and other costs needed to complete the registration process.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to registered family child care providers.
requirements_list: Must be a registered family child care provider
Annual income must not exceed 60% of Maryland's current State Median Income (SMI) for the applicant's family size
Program is operated in accordance with COMAR 13A.14.07
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligibility requirements, application procedures, and award methods are specified in COMAR 13A.14.07. A new grant opportunity is noted as coming soon; more information will be posted on the program webpage.

structured_extraction.program_description: A peer-support group for individuals who are blind or visually impaired. Members meet to discuss common concerns such as relationships, independence, advocacy, responsibility, and technology. The group meets once per week for eight weeks and is offered four times a year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Peer-support group that meets once per week for eight weeks, up to eight participants per group. Offered four times per year at the WTC, at local DORS offices on request, and virtually via Google Meet.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals who are blind or visually impaired
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participation in peer-support discussions covering relationships, independence, advocacy, responsibility, and technology
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at the Workforce & Technology Center, local DORS offices, and virtually statewide
requirements_list: Must be blind or visually impaired
Must be a DORS consumer
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact WTC or a local DORS office to request participation. Virtual sessions available via Google Meet.

structured_extraction.program_name: MSDE Science of Reading Microcredential Courses
structured_extraction.program_description: Free professional development courses for Maryland educators covering Science of Reading and literacy leadership topics. Funded through a philanthropic partnership, the courses help educators strengthen reading instruction skills and meet Maryland's reading proficiency requirement for teacher license renewal.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Five free professional development courses offered online and in-person through partnerships with AIM Institute and SUNY New Paltz. Courses include: (1) SUNY New Paltz Science of Reading Fundamentals Microcredential — 35-hour fully online introductory course for all educators; (2) AIM Pathways to Proficient Reading: Secondary — extensive online course with six synchronous one-hour virtual community sessions for secondary educators; (3) AIM Pathways to Literacy Leadership — extensive online course with two six-hour in-person community sessions for school and district leaders; (4) AIM Specialized Reading Knowledge: English Learners — 10-hour online course with three virtual communities of practice; (5) AIM Demystifying Dyslexia — three-hour online course. Funded by a $6.85M philanthropic partnership with the Ibis Group. The SUNY microcredential fulfills Maryland's reading proficiency requirement for teacher license renewal.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland public school educators including paraeducators, teachers, specialists, and school and district leaders
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Professional development in Science of Reading instructional methods and literacy leadership
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to educators in Maryland public schools
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland public school educator (paraeducator, teacher, specialist, or school/district leader)
Different courses target different levels of prior Science of Reading knowledge
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the AIM Institute or SUNY New Paltz websites to learn more about and enroll in the appropriate course.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Accreditation allows licensed child care centers and public pre-kindergarten programs to demonstrate their commitment to high-quality early learning. Programs complete a self-appraisal, create an improvement plan, and receive a validation visit. Accreditation is awarded for 5 years.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Accredited programs gain eligibility for Maryland EXCELS Quality Rating 5, higher Maryland EXCELS payments, and access to Accreditation Support Funds for purchasing instructional materials. Optional virtual or onsite technical assistance is available during the accreditation process.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed child care centers and public pre-kindergarten programs in Maryland. Family child care programs are not currently eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Accreditation Support Funds can be used to purchase instructional materials.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a licensed child care center or public pre-kindergarten program
Family child care programs are not eligible
Must complete a Self-Appraisal including input from staff and enrolled families
Must develop a Program Improvement Plan based on areas needing improvement
Must complete a Final Self-Appraisal reviewing program improvements
Must undergo a Validation Visit for observation and feedback
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Programs use Maryland Accreditation Standards, complete a Self-Appraisal, develop a Program Improvement Plan, complete a Final Self-Appraisal, and participate in a Validation Visit. Optional technical assistance (virtual or onsite) is available for support.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Accreditation offers technical assistance to early care and education programs to help them meet accreditation requirements. Support is available in two forms: virtual assistance (phone calls focused on accreditation indicators and required evidence) and onsite assistance (observation and feedback on observable required evidence).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two types of technical assistance are available: (1) Virtual Technical Assistance — a phone call focused on questions about Maryland Accreditation indicators and required evidence; (2) Onsite Technical Assistance — an in-person observation of the program with feedback on observable required evidence.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care and early education programs seeking Maryland Accreditation support.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Technical assistance to help programs understand and meet Maryland Accreditation indicators and evidence requirements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Program must be pursuing Maryland Accreditation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Refer to the Maryland Accreditation Technical Assistance FAQ PDF on the Maryland Accreditation Resources page for more information on how to access technical assistance.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Business Enterprise Program for the Blind (BEP)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Business Enterprise Program for the Blind (BEP) trains, licenses, and supports people who are legally blind to manage retail concession, food service, and vending operations in federal, military, DOD, and State of Maryland facilities. Authorized by the Federally mandated Randolph-Sheppard Act, the program prepares participants to operate successful businesses in public facilities and at business partner locations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: BEP provides a three-phase training and licensing program: (1) an eight-week New Manager Training course at DORS' Workforce & Technology Center in Northeast Baltimore; (2) formal food service training with certified instructors leading to a National Restaurant Association certification in food service sanitation; and (3) three to six months of on-the-job training at BEP facilities under an experienced manager. After completing training, participants receive licensing to operate vending and food service facilities in public buildings including federal, military, DOD, and State of Maryland properties, as well as business partner locations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Legally blind U.S. citizens, including individuals whose primary disability is vision loss (blind, vision impaired, or deaf-blind), as well as legally blind individuals over age 55 with independent living goals, who are interested in operating retail concession, food service, or vending businesses in public facilities and who are certified as eligible by DORS.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and licensing to operate retail concession, food service, and vending operations in federal, military, DOD, and State of Maryland public facilities, as well as business partner locations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland; operations are located on Federal, Military, DOD, and State of Maryland properties and at business partner locations. Training is conducted at the DORS Workforce & Technology Center in Northeast Baltimore.
requirements_list: Must be legally blind
Must be a U.S. citizen
Primary disability must be vision loss
Must have a minimum high school diploma or GED equivalent
Must have an aptitude for business management
Must have practical skills and meet legal criteria for operating a business
Must be referred by a DORS OBVS counselor
Must complete all three phases of the training program satisfactorily
Must obtain National Restaurant Association certification in food service sanitation
Must complete the on-the-job training internship
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: If you already have a DORS counselor, ask your counselor about BEP. If you are not working with DORS, complete a Request DORS Services form on the DORS website (dors.maryland.gov). You will be contacted to set up an intake appointment where DORS will gather information and determine your eligibility for services. The form can be completed by the job seeker.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Child Care Resource Network Technical Assistance
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Child Care Resource Network (MCCRN) provides technical assistance covering all aspects of starting, expanding, and operating a child care center or becoming a family child care provider. Services include help with licensing and compliance, behavioral issues, children with special needs, and support for providers working toward credentials and program accreditation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free technical assistance covering licensing and compliance, behavioral issues, special needs support, credential attainment, and program accreditation. Services are available to existing and potential child care providers, Head Start programs, nursery schools, cooperatives, drop-in centers, playgroups, community and non-profit organizations, employers, and public agencies.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Existing and potential center-based and family child care providers, Head Start programs, nursery schools, cooperatives, drop-in centers, playgroups, community and non-profit organizations, community groups, employers, and public agencies committed to expanding child care resources.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Technical assistance for starting, expanding, or operating a child care program; licensing and compliance guidance; behavioral support; serving children with special needs; credential and accreditation support.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Maryland Child Care Resource Network (MCCRN) through marylandfamilynetwork.org.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Disability Determination Services (DDS) is a state agency within the Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS) that determines eligibility for Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) and Supplemental Security Income (SSI) using SSA regulations. DDS processes applications by developing medical and non-medical evidence and making disability determinations for Maryland applicants.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides eligibility determinations for two federal disability benefit programs through medical and non-medical evidence review: SSDI pays monthly cash benefits to insured workers who have worked long enough and paid Social Security taxes and become disabled; SSI pays monthly cash benefits to low-income individuals with disabilities based on financial need.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults unable to work due to a medically determinable disability; children under 18 with marked and severe functional limitations; health practitioners, advocates, school personnel, and citizens seeking information
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Monthly disability benefit payments to eligible individuals and qualifying family members
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Maryland only
requirements_list: Medically determinable physical or mental impairment(s) expected to last 12+ continuous months or result in death
For adults: inability to engage in substantial gainful work activity
For children: marked and severe functional limitations
For SSDI: must have sufficient work credits (worked long enough and paid Social Security taxes)
For SSI: must meet income and resource guidelines demonstrating financial need
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through a local SSA office, SSA toll-free line (1-800-772-1213), or www.SSA.gov. Once initial criteria are met, the case is sent to DDS for a disability determination. Mail correspondence to PO Box 1810, Cockeysville, MD 21030-1810.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland EXCELS is a Quality Rating and Improvement System (QRIS) administered by the Maryland State Department of Education that uses nationally recognized standards and best practices to support and recognize quality improvement in early childhood programs, child care centers, school-age child care programs, family child care homes, and public prekindergarten programs across Maryland. Participating providers receive published quality ratings from 1 to 5 based on standards in areas such as developmentally-appropriate practice, professional development, and family engagement. These ratings help families make informed child care choices. The program provides a road map, training, and incentives to help providers improve their practices, along with ongoing guidance from a regional Quality Assurance Specialist and access to a community of peer providers. Participants also receive financial rewards including increased Child Care Scholarship reimbursements, quality improvement bonuses, free training, promotional tools, and vendor discounts. Participants gain access to an online system for documenting and uploading evidence of meeting standards, as well as professional development resources to help improve their rating level and overall program quality. Professional development and technical assistance support includes assigned Program Coordinators, regional Quality Assurance Specialists, virtual and in-person training sessions that award Core of Knowledge hours and certificates, Continuous Quality Improvement (CQI) observation visits every three years for programs at ratings 1–3, CLASS® assessment visits for programs at ratings 4–5, peer support through workgroups and cohorts, and access to the Maryland EXCELS Toolkit and Child Care Resource Network. Participation in Maryland EXCELS is required to accept Child Care Scholarship (Subsidy) reimbursement.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Programs receive a published quality rating (1–5), a quality improvement road map, training, and incentives to improve practices. Participants receive increased Child Care Scholarship reimbursements, bonuses for quality improvement, free training, and discounts from vendors and partner organizations. Eligibility for state grants and the Military Child Care in Your Neighborhood program (at Quality Rating 3) is also available. Providers are assigned a Program Coordinator for guidance and consultation, as well as a regional Quality Assurance Specialist (QAS) for on-site, phone, and email support. Virtual and in-person training sessions award Core of Knowledge hours and certificates. Programs at ratings 1–3 receive Continuous Quality Improvement (CQI) observation visits every three years; programs at ratings 4–5 receive CLASS® assessment visits. An online Maryland EXCELS Toolkit and system is available for documenting and uploading evidence of meeting standards. Participants also gain access to the Child Care Resource Network, local Child Care Resource Centers, peer support through workgroups and cohorts, promotional tools including quality rating badges and certificates, advertising resources, and professional development resources designed to help them increase their Maryland EXCELS rating level and improve overall program quality.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed child care centers (including school-age only and letter of compliance programs), registered family child care homes, Head Start programs, public prekindergarten programs, and other early childhood and school-age child care providers that are open and operating in Maryland who want to demonstrate and improve the quality of care they provide to children and families.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Quality improvement activities, professional development training, technical assistance, quality improvement planning, and meeting Maryland EXCELS standards in areas such as developmentally-appropriate practice and family engagement, as well as resources to achieve higher quality ratings, eligibility for child care subsidy reimbursement, and access to financial rewards including increased reimbursement rates, quality improvement bonuses, and state grants.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to all eligible licensed or registered child care and prekindergarten programs.

Must have a valid License Number, Registration Number, or School ID
Must be authorized to submit the application on behalf of the program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Log in to or create a user account at excels.marylandexcels.org, then complete the 12-step online application process: create account, verify email, log in, select application type, look up program by license/registration/school ID, confirm lead contact status, complete program details, and submit application. Step-by-step instructions are available in the 'Applying to Participate in Maryland EXCELS' tutorial (https://marylandexcels.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/05/Applying-to-Participate-in-Maryland-EXCELS-and-or-Maryland-Accreditation.pdf). Once accepted, programs are assigned a Program Coordinator and a regional Quality Assurance Specialist provides ongoing support. A Quality Assurance Specialist supports the provider in creating and uploading evidence of meeting standards into the online system. Evidence is reviewed by Maryland EXCELS staff, who then assign ratings for each standard area and an overall quality rating. Training sessions can be signed up for through monthly emails sent to Maryland EXCELS programs. Contact info@marylandexcels.org for more information about available rewards and resources. Technology support is available 24/7 at 443-872-9250.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland EXCELS recognizes child care and public prekindergarten programs that provide services above and beyond the standard Maryland EXCELS requirements. Programs that earn these additional achievements are acknowledged in the Find a Program Directory on the Maryland EXCELS website. Achievements cover areas such as accreditation, asthma and allergy safety, cultural and linguistic competency, eco-friendly practices, family engagement, health and wellness, Judy Center partnerships, military child care participation, and quality business practices.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Programs that meet specific criteria in one or more of nine achievement categories (Accredited Programs, Asthma and Allergy Friendly, Cultural and Linguistic Competency, Eco-Friendly Program, Family Engagement, Health and Wellness, Judy Center, Military Child Care in Your Neighborhood, Quality Business Practices) receive official recognition badges that can be displayed on websites, social media, newsletters, and communications with families. There is no direct financial payment; the benefit is recognition and acknowledgment in the Maryland EXCELS Find a Program Directory.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care programs and public prekindergarten programs in Maryland that want to demonstrate quality above and beyond standard Maryland EXCELS requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Recognition badges and directory listing — no funds disbursed.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to child care and public prekindergarten programs throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Program must participate in the Maryland EXCELS quality rating system

Asthma and Allergy Friendly: must complete MSDE-sponsored Asthma, Allergy and Anaphylaxis Prevention and Management Training
Cultural and Linguistic Competency: must complete the Cultural and Linguistic Competency Application and the Pathways to Cultural Competency Checklist
Eco-Friendly Program: must participate in at least one recognized eco initiative (Eco-Healthy Child Care, Nature Explore Program, Eco-Schools USA, or Maryland Green Schools)
Family Engagement: must complete a training module and the Maryland EXCELS Family Engagement Additional Achievement Application
Health and Wellness: must complete Healthy Kids, Healthy Futures modules and the Maryland EXCELS Health and Wellness Additional Achievement Application

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Log into your Maryland EXCELS profile at excels.marylandexcels.org. Navigate to the 'Achievements' section under the Program Menu, select earned Additional Achievements, and provide required documentation for each. A Program Coordinator will review documentation and recognize the achievement in your online profile if approved. Badges can be downloaded as a zip file from the Certificate and Badge section of the Program Menu. Contact your assigned Program Coordinator or email info@marylandexcels.org for specific requirements for each achievement category.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland State Department of Education distributes bonuses to child care programs that participate in Maryland EXCELS, a quality rating and improvement system. Programs earn bonuses when they publish a quality rating for the first time or re-publish a quality rating of 4 or 5. Bonus amounts range from $1,000 to $13,500 depending on the type of program, quality rating level, and enrollment capacity.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Flat bonus payments ranging from $1,000 to $13,500 per qualifying event (first-time quality rating publication or re-publication of a rating 4 or 5). Bonus amounts are determined by program type (child care center, family child care, or large family home) and, for centers, enrollment capacity. Funds can be used for staff salary increases, hiring additional qualified staff, purchasing high-quality learning materials and furniture, program quality improvements, and accreditation preparation. Payments are issued by check or direct deposit, typically within 60 days of the quality rating being published. No application is required — eligible programs receive payment automatically.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Bonuses available between July 1, 2026 and June 30, 2027
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care programs (child care centers, family child care homes, and large family homes) participating in Maryland EXCELS
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Staff salary increases; hiring additional qualified staff; purchasing high-quality learning materials; purchasing furniture; program quality improvements; accreditation preparation
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to all Maryland EXCELS-participating programs
requirements_list: Must be a participating program in Maryland EXCELS
Must be in compliance with all Maryland EXCELS regulations
Must participate in scheduled Continuous Quality Improvement visits
Must publish a quality rating for the first time OR re-publish a quality rating of 4 or 5 between July 1, 2026 and June 30, 2027
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: No application is required. Eligible programs automatically receive bonus payments by check or direct deposit, typically within 60 days of the qualifying quality rating being published. Programs can check payment status on the General Accounting Division (GAD) website after registering there. To participate in Maryland EXCELS, contact a regional Quality Assurance Specialist.

structured_extraction.program_description: A pilot mentoring program for child care providers that includes a mandatory self-paced Introduction to Mentoring training. Participants who complete the training earn 2 COK (Credential of Knowledge) hours.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Self-paced Introduction to Mentoring training that awards 2 COK (Credential of Knowledge) hours upon completion.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care providers and educators participating in the Maryland EXCELS quality rating system who are interested in becoming mentors.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Professional development training for mentoring in child care settings.

requirements_list: Must complete the self-paced Introduction to Mentoring training as a mandatory first step.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the self-paced Introduction to Mentoring online training available on the Maryland EXCELS website. Upon successful completion, 2 COK hours are awarded.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland EXCELS Payments reward licensed child care providers for delivering high-quality services to families who receive Child Care Scholarship (the state's subsidized child care program). Providers at Maryland EXCELS Quality Ratings 3, 4, and 5 receive increased reimbursement amounts on top of their standard Child Care Scholarship payments. The bonus ranges from 10% to 44% depending on the child's age, the type of care (family child care home or child care center), and the program's quality rating level. For family child care homes, increases range from 10–11% (Level 3) to 28–29% (Level 5) depending on child age. For child care centers, increases range from 10–22% (Level 3) to 26–44% (Level 5) depending on child age, with centers serving children under 2 receiving 22% (Level 3), 37% (Level 4), or 44% (Level 5) above the base rate. Payments appear as 'EXCELS' entries on the Invoice Detail Report for each eligible child.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Providers at Maryland EXCELS Quality Rating Level 3, 4, or 5 receive a percentage increase on top of their Child Care Scholarship reimbursement. For family child care: Level 3 adds 11% (under age 2) or 10% (age 2+); Level 4 adds 22% (under 2) or 21% (age 2+); Level 5 adds 29% (under 2) or 28% (age 2+). For child care centers: Level 3 adds 22% (under 2) or 10% (age 2+); Level 4 adds 37% (under 2) or 19% (age 2+); Level 5 adds 44% (under 2) or 26% (age 2+). Payments appear as 'EXCELS' on the Invoice Detail Report for each eligible child.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed family child care providers and child care centers participating in Maryland EXCELS at Quality Rating Level 3, 4, or 5 that serve children whose families receive Child Care Scholarship.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Increased reimbursement payments to child care programs for serving children who receive Child Care Scholarship subsidies, rewarding high-quality child care provision.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to licensed child care providers participating in the Maryland EXCELS quality rating system.
requirements_list: Program must be enrolled in Maryland EXCELS
Program must achieve a Maryland EXCELS Quality Rating of Level 3, 4, or 5
Program must accept and serve children whose families receive Child Care Scholarship
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Providers must participate in the Maryland EXCELS quality rating system. Once a program achieves Quality Rating Level 3, 4, or 5, the increased reimbursement payments are applied automatically to Child Care Scholarship payments and appear as 'EXCELS' on the Invoice Detail Report for each eligible child.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Hearing Aid and Language & Communication Video Loan Bank
structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide resource that loans hearing aids and educational videos to Maryland families of children who are deaf or hard of hearing. Families without insurance coverage or other means to obtain hearing aids may borrow devices for up to one year at no cost. The program also provides DVDs and other materials to help families learn about language and communication options for their child.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Infants and Toddlers Program (MITP) Consolidated Local Implementation Grant (CLIG)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Infants and Toddlers Program (MITP) provides family-centered early intervention services for children birth through age three (with an option to extend to age four) who have developmental delays or disabilities, coordinating support, information, and services in community settings through 24 local Infants and Toddlers Programs (LITPs) across Maryland. A team of professionals works with families to understand concerns, determine if a child needs special help, and create a plan to support the child's development. Services are delivered in home, child care, library, or other community locations, building on child and family strengths and addressing family goals and concerns. There is no cost to families, and eligibility is based on a child's need rather than family circumstances. The MITP Consolidated Local Implementation Grant (CLIG) is the state and federal funding mechanism through which local jurisdictions receive funds to implement these local early intervention programs in compliance with federal IDEA Part C and state regulations. The designated Local Lead Agency (LLA) of each LITP aggregates information from partner agencies to complete the grant application and required submissions throughout the grant period, and administers services. Funds must be linked to program improvement through a required chart submitted with the application, and cover program operations including staff and program improvement activities tied to the State Systemic Improvement Plan. Funds must be reported on through variance reports, financial reports, and other required submissions on a defined annual timeline. Recipients must also submit required appendices including assurances, certifications, and local interagency agreements. The program provides family-centered, capacity-building services focused on three early childhood outcomes: positive social-emotional skills, acquisition and use of functional knowledge and skills, and appropriate behavior to meet needs. Implements evidence-based practices including Routines-Based Interview, Reflective Coaching, and Pyramid Model. Supports historically underrepresented populations including minority, low-income, homeless, inner city, rural children, and children in foster care. In Queen Anne's County, families may contact the local single point of entry through the QAC Department of Health. The grant also accounts for IDEA Part C, Part B 611, Part B 619, State, and Medical Assistance funds for jurisdictions, and identifies budgetary and staff commitment of each agency participating in the local early intervention system. Includes support for effective IFSP development, Comprehensive System of Personnel Development (CSPD), family support services, and transition from Part C to Part B services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal and state funds are distributed to local jurisdictions through designated Local Lead Agencies via the Consolidated Local Implementation Grant (CLIG) to implement early intervention programs for infants and toddlers with disabilities under IDEA Part C. Funding sources include IDEA Part C Funds for Program Support, IDEA Part C Discretionary Funds, IDEA Part B 619 Funds for Family Support (Age 3 to Kindergarten Transition), Blueprint for Maryland's Future Funds, Medicaid Funds (federal reimbursement), State Incentive Grant (SIG) Funding, and State Systemic Improvement Plan (SSIP) Funding ($50,000 for selected jurisdictions). Free early intervention services are provided to eligible children from birth to age 3 (with an option to extend to age four under the Extended IFSP Option). Services provided through the MITP may include audiology, physical therapy, occupational therapy, transportation, speech-language pathology, family training, special instruction, assistive technology, health services, and home visits. Funds also support comprehensive system of personnel development (CSPD), individualized family service plans (IFSP), and family support services. Families of eligible children may also choose Maryland's Extended IFSP Option to continue services beyond the child's third birthday if the child qualifies for preschool special education. Funds must be linked to program improvement through a required chart submitted with the application, and cover program operations including staff and program improvement activities tied to the State Systemic Improvement Plan. Local Lead Agencies must submit applications, budgets, and post-application submissions via the MSDE MOVEit Secure File Transfer site. There is no cost to families and eligibility is based on the child's need, not family income. The program provides formula and project grants as well as direct payments for specified use to local jurisdictions. A fixed allocation of $5,000 is available for a Family Support Coordinator (Part C) position (parent of child with disability). Funding supports compliance indicators (timely services, 45-day timeline, transition outcomes, timely TPM) and results indicators (natural environment, child outcomes, family awareness of rights, child find). Includes support for family support services for children birth through kindergarten, early intervention family survey implementation, and Part C to Part B transition services.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families of children birth through age three (or up to age four under the Extended IFSP Option) with developmental delays or disabilities, and Designated Local Lead Agencies (LLAs) of each Local Infants & Toddlers Program (LITP) in Maryland. Local governments and non-profit organizations that provide services to infants and toddlers with disabilities. Early intervention service providers, paraprofessionals, community partners, and referral sources. In Queen Anne's County, families with infants and toddlers (birth to age 3) who have developmental delays, are at risk for delays, or have a diagnosis that may affect development may also contact the local QAC Department of Health. Also includes families transitioning from Part C to Part B services (age 3 to kindergarten).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Implement local early intervention programs for infants and toddlers with disabilities in compliance with federal and state regulations, including services such as audiology, physical therapy, occupational therapy, transportation, speech-language pathology, family training, special instruction, assistive technology, health services, and home visits. Also supports comprehensive system of personnel development (CSPD), individualized family service plans (IFSP), and family support services. Supports Child Find and public awareness activities targeting referral sources and underserved populations. Professional development and staff training in evidence-based practices and culturally responsive assessment. Implementation of Child Outcomes Summary (COS) process. Infrastructure and personnel development for service delivery. Early intervention and developmental support services for children from birth to age 3 are provided at no cost to families. Funds may also support program improvement activities tied to the State Systemic Improvement Plan. Salaries and fringe benefits for direct service positions, contracted early intervention services, administrative and early intervention supplies and equipment, staff and parent training, and Family Support Services Coordinator positions (parent of child with disability). Transition-related activities for children ages 3 to kindergarten. Professional learning on evidence-based practices (Pyramid Model, Routines-Based Interview, reflective coaching). System and content coaching. Collaboration with early childhood mental health programs and community partners. Stipends for partners and families to engage in local implementation activities. Funds designated for improving compliance indicators (timely services, 45-day timeline, transition outcomes, timely TPM) and results indicators (natural environment, child outcomes, family awareness of rights, child find). Family support services implementation, early intervention family survey administration, and strategies to improve survey response rates and demographic representativeness. IFSP review for functional, routines-based outcomes and personnel development strategies aligned with EI Personnel Standards.

Commerce St., Centreville, MD 21617). Child must live in Maryland and be under three years old.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Families may make a referral through the MITP online referral site at referral.mditp.org or contact their county's local Infants and Toddlers Program directly by phone at 1-800-535-0182. Parents, teachers, physicians, community agencies, daycare/nursery schools, other health specialists, and private schools may also refer children. After referral, the local program contacts the family to gather information and schedule a free developmental evaluation conducted in the home or preferred location. If eligible, the family joins the early intervention team to develop a service plan (IFSP). In Queen Anne's County, families may contact the single point of entry: Mary Lou Christian, R.N., QAC Department of Health, 206 N. Commerce St., Centreville, MD 21617, Phone: 410-758-0720 Ext. 4456. Local Lead Agencies should attend the CLIG Grant Information Session, then download the CLIG Grant Information Guide and current forms from the MSDE website just before completing them. Complete the CLIG application and required budget workbook (using the CLIG Grant Information Guide, CLIG Application, Budget Submissions Workbook, Linking Funds to Program Improvement Chart, and other required forms including all required appendices such as assurances, certifications, and interagency agreements), aggregating information from partner agencies. Applicants must also complete the GEPA Section 427 Form addressing four required questions (existing mission/policies ensuring equitable access, identification of barriers, steps to address barriers, and timeline with targeted milestones); may cross-reference responses to other application sections or State Plan documents. All completed submissions are uploaded to the MSDE MOVEit Secure File Transfer Website (https://msde.sftp.md.gov/) following the naming and submission procedures outlined in the MSDE MOVEit Secure File Transfer Website Access and Submission Procedures. After uploading, send email notification to the assigned fiscal grants liaison with the document name(s). Certification document required certifying compliance with lobbying, debarment, and drug-free workplace requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Meals for Achievement (MMFA) is a state-funded program that supplements federal school breakfast reimbursements, allowing participating schools to offer free breakfast in the classroom to all students. Schools must meet economically disadvantaged criteria to qualify. Currently, 581 schools participate statewide. The program increases students' access to a nutritious breakfast at the start of each school day and is credited with improving test scores, behavior, attendance, and well-being.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides state funds to supplement federal meal reimbursements so that all children in participating schools receive a free nutritious breakfast in the classroom each school day. Currently 581 schools participate across Maryland.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Providing free nutritious breakfast in the classroom to all students in participating schools
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — currently 581 schools participate across Maryland

Must meet the economically disadvantaged criteria
Meals must be consumed in the classroom
