structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Medicaid Home and Community-Based Services Waiver for Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder (Autism Waiver)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Autism Waiver provides community-based, long-term, person-centered therapeutic services and support to eligible children and youth with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD). It enables home and community living as an alternative to institutional care, using the home and community environment as a learning experience. Services include one-on-one support, respite care, family consultation/training, residential habilitation, therapeutic integration, environmental accessibility adaptations, adult life planning, and intensive individual support services (IISS). The program is administered statewide by the Maryland State Department of Education and the Maryland Department of Health, with service coordination and case management provided through local education agencies. Services are delivered in the home and community outside of school hours. Participants also receive full Medicaid benefits including health insurance, dental care, and prescription coverage. The program is currently at capacity; families may add their child's name to the Autism Waiver Registry at 866-417-3480 and slots are filled on a first-come, first-served basis through attrition at no cost to families.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Medicaid waiver services including Adult Life Planning (ALP), Environmental Accessibility Adaptations (EAA), Family Consultation/Training (FC), Intensive Individual Support Services (IISS), Residential Habilitation (regular or intensive), Respite Care, Therapeutic Integration (TI: regular or intensive), and Service Coordination through local education agencies. Participants also receive full Medicaid benefits including health insurance, dental care, prescription coverage, and other services. Financial eligibility requires monthly income not exceeding 300% of SSI benefits and countable assets not exceeding $2,000 or $2,500 depending on eligibility category. Service coordination and case management are provided at no cost to families, with slots filled on a first-come, first-served basis through the Autism Waiver Registry. The program is currently at capacity and not accepting new applications; families may join the waiting list via the Registry.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Not accepting new applications at this time; families may join the Autism Waiver Registry waitlist. Once invited to apply, applicants have 45 days to accept the invitation and complete the application process; 30 days to submit the financial assistance request and technical eligibility checklist (with a 15-day extension if needed).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Children ages 1 through the end of the school semester in which they turn 21 (or earlier upon exit from the school system), who have a current diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder, reside in Maryland, receive special education or early intervention services, and meet Medicaid financial eligibility requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Community-based therapeutic services including one-on-one support (IISS), family consultation and training, respite care, residential habilitation, therapeutic integration, home accessibility adaptations (EAA), adult life planning, intensive individual support services, targeted case management, and service coordination for children with autism outside of school hours.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must reside in Maryland. Program is available in all 24 Maryland jurisdictions including all counties and Baltimore City. Service coordination may be provided through local county agencies. Program is administered statewide by MSDE and MDH.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The program is currently at capacity and not accepting new applications. Families must contact the Autism Waiver Registry at 866-417-3480 to register and join the waiting list. Upon registration, families receive a confirmation letter. An MDH provider conducts an initial screening based on parent report. Technical, financial, and medical eligibility are evaluated. Slots are offered on a first-come, first-served basis through attrition. When a vacancy occurs, eligible families on the Registry are invited to apply and have 45 days to accept the invitation and complete the application process. structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Pathways in Technology Early College High School (P-TECH) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: P-TECH is a grade 9–14 public school program that creates clear pathways from high school to college and career for students from all academic backgrounds. Students graduate in six years or less with a high school diploma and a no-cost two-year Associate of Applied Science (AAS) degree. Each P-TECH school partners with industry and a local community college to offer rigorous, career-relevant curriculum, one-on-one mentoring, workplace visits, skills instruction, paid summer internships, and first-in-line consideration for jobs with partner companies. The program addresses workforce needs by preparing students for middle-skill employment and requires partnerships among local school systems, institutions of higher education, and local employers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive planning grants are awarded to local school systems to establish P-TECH sites. Planning grants range from $93,031–$100,000 for schools in development phase (total $600,000 in FY2016). P-TECH student grants: $520 per student annually (50% state, 50% local match beginning FY2017). Supplemental school grants: minimum $750 per student per school year; state pays 50% (or 25% for counties not receiving certain prior grants), local boards must match 100% (in-kind allowed). Supplemental college grants cover tuition and mandatory fees (state covers 25–50%, local covers remainder). Students receive no-cost associate degrees, mentoring, paid summer internships (minimum 6 weeks), and career placement support. Grants also support additional staff, instructional support, extended day programs, and student support services.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local school systems partnering with community colleges and businesses to establish P-TECH schools. Priority enrollment for high school students meeting free and reduced-price meals (FARM) income criteria (minimum 50% of enrollment capacity reserved). Open to students from all academic backgrounds interested in STEM and career pathways.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planning and establishing P-TECH school sites including: additional staff for pathway implementation, instructional support services and professional development, extended day programs, student support services (counseling, tutoring, career exploration), college tuition and mandatory fees (no cost to students), transportation, and curriculum development, mentoring, internships, and career placement.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Prior and current sites established in Baltimore City, Allegany County, Prince George's County, Baltimore County, Montgomery County, Queen Anne's County, Talbot County, and Caroline County.
requirements_list: Local school system must partner with a community college and local businesses
Schools serve students grades 9–14
Program leads to a high school diploma and a no-cost two-year Associate of Applied Science (AAS) degree within six years
Must participate in competitive grant process administered by MSDE
Minimum 50% of enrollment must be students meeting free and reduced-price meals (FARM) income criteria
Local school systems must match 100% of supplemental school grant funds (in-kind contributions allowed)
Program must demonstrate success in preparing students for workforce or postsecondary education before additional schools can be established
Partnership requirement: local school system, higher education institution, and employer all required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Local school systems apply through a competitive grant process administered by MSDE. Contact Kellise Williamson for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide prekindergarten program for 3- and 4-year-old children that provides high-quality early education through both public schools and private providers, including child care centers, family child care homes, Head Start programs, Montessori schools, and faith-based preschools. The program helps young children develop the basic skills needed to succeed in school. Grantee organizations receive Pre-K slots under two funding categories: standard state funding and Pre-Kindergarten Expansion Blueprint Funding.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Award of Pre-Kindergarten slots to grantee organizations under two funding categories: standard state funding and Pre-Kindergarten Expansion Blueprint Funding. Families can enroll eligible 3- and 4-year-olds in free Pre-K programs through their local public school system or approved private providers. Eligible families may also receive a scholarship from their local Department of Social Services for additional child care options such as before and after care.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with 3- and 4-year-old children in Maryland seeking early childhood education; and organizations (public schools, private child care centers, Head Start programs, Montessori schools, faith-based preschools, non-profit child development organizations, and family child care providers) seeking to offer Pre-K slots
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Pre-kindergarten program slots and operations, including before/after care through a child care scholarship for eligible families
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland's 24 local school systems, including Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Calvert, Caroline, Carroll, Cecil, Charles, Frederick, Garrett, Harford, Howard, Kent, Montgomery, Prince George's, Talbot, Washington, Wicomico, Worcester, Allegany, Dorchester, and Queen Anne's counties
requirements_list: Child must be 3 or 4 years old
Eligibility requirements vary by local school system
Families may need to contact their neighborhood school for enrollment details
Provider organizations must be approved grantees under state or Blueprint expansion funding
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your neighborhood school or local school system's Early Childhood office to ask questions, enroll your child, or find a program. Eligible families can contact their local Department of Social Services for child care scholarship options. Provider organizations may apply for grantee status through the Maryland State Department of Education Early Childhood division.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) grant program that uses federal funds to stabilize, strengthen, and sustain Maryland's licensed child care system following the COVID-19 pandemic. Grants are awarded under six strategies: expanding access to quality child care, early learning models of excellence, expanding mental health supports and services, growing a highly effective child care workforce, boosting family child care, and advancing a coordinated prekindergarten enrollment system.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants funded by federal dollars are awarded to eligible child care providers and early childhood organizations. Applicants must select at least one of six high-leverage strategy areas and describe how their planned activities align with that strategy, what products or services will be delivered, and the expected impact on the early childhood community. Award notices were issued in December 2022.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed child care providers, early childhood organizations, higher education institutions, and government agencies in Maryland seeking to stabilize and improve the child care system after the COVID-19 pandemic.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Helping families find and afford child care; improving program quality; providing mental health supports for children and families; supporting the early childhood workforce; increasing the resilience of family child care businesses; and advancing coordinated prekindergarten enrollment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide across Maryland
requirements_list: Must be an eligible child care provider or early childhood organization
Must select at least one of the six high-leverage strategy areas
Must describe how planned activities align with the chosen strategy
Must describe expected products, services, and impact on the early childhood community
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit applications describing their chosen strategy area(s), planned activities, deliverables, and expected outcomes. MSDE reviewed applications and issued award notices in December 2022.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Work Incentives Planning and Assistance Project (WIPA)
structured_extraction.program_description: WIPA provides benefits planning services to SSI and SSDI recipients in Maryland, helping them understand how going back to work will affect their Social Security cash benefits and medical coverage. Trained and certified benefits counselors assist individuals with understanding work incentives and their personal circumstances.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free benefits counseling and planning services provided by certified benefits counselors to help SSI/SSDI recipients understand how work affects their benefits under Social Security work incentive programs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: SSI and SSDI recipients in Maryland considering returning to work or currently working.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable — technical assistance/counseling service.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be an SSI or SSDI recipient
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Maryland Work Incentives Network (md-win.org) to access benefits planning services. DORS counselors can also assist with connecting to these services.

structured_extraction.program_name: Medication Administration Training for Child Care Providers
structured_extraction.program_description: Medication Administration Training (MAT) is a required pre-service training course for individuals seeking a Child Care Center License or Family Child Care Registration in Maryland. The six-hour classroom training (6 Hours Health, Safety, Nutrition) is conducted by licensed Maryland Registered Nurses approved by the Office of Child Care's Nurse Consultant. Optional special needs support services training (Type 1 Diabetes, Seizure management, Tube Feeding, Urinary Catheter, Oxygen support) and Spanish language instruction are also available.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A six-hour classroom training covering theory and practice of medication administration. Optional special needs support services (Type 1 Diabetes, Seizure management, Tube Feeding, Urinary Catheter, Oxygen support) and Spanish language instruction are available. Participants receive a certificate upon completing the course and passing content and skill tests. Trainers deliver classes at locations and times they specify across Maryland.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals seeking a Child Care Center License or Family Child Care Registration in Maryland; child care providers statewide
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Pre-service training requirement for child care licensing; medication administration training delivery
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across all Maryland counties; trainers serve multiple counties and are available throughout Maryland
requirements_list: Must be seeking a Child Care Center License or Family Child Care Registration
Training conducted by MSDE-approved licensed Maryland Registered Nurses
RN trainers must hold current Maryland RN licensure (MBON-RN#)
RN trainers must have experience, skills, and/or training in teaching medication administration to adults
RN trainers must complete orientation and adhere to Office of Child Care's Medication Administration Training Guidance and Standards
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Find a MAT trainer in your area using the approved trainers list and contact them directly to register for a class. To become a certified MAT instructor (RNs): complete the Medication Administration Instructor Application and Training Plan, mail both to MSDE Office of Child Care Licensing Branch, and attend mandatory orientation.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Milken Educator Awards program recognizes and rewards outstanding educators across the country with $25,000 unrestricted cash awards. The program aims to inspire excellence in education by honoring top teachers and education professionals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Recipients receive a $25,000 unrestricted cash award. The award is given to selected educators — recipients do not apply; they are identified and notified by the program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Outstanding K-12 educators in Maryland public schools
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Unrestricted — recipients may use the award funds for any purpose
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to educators in Maryland public schools; program operates nationally
requirements_list: Must be an educator in a public school
Selection is by nomination/identification — educators do not apply directly
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Educators are identified and selected by the program — there is no direct application process. Contact the Office of Communications for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: The National School Lunch Program (NSLP) provides nutritionally balanced, low-cost, or free lunches and snacks to children each school day in participating public and nonprofit private schools and residential childcare institutions across Maryland. The federal government reimburses schools for meals that meet USDA nutrition standards aligned with the Dietary Guidelines for Americans. Children may receive free or reduced-price lunches based on household income, categorical eligibility (e.g., participation in SNAP or Temporary Assistance Cash), direct certification through Medicaid, or enrollment in qualifying programs such as Head Start. Under the Maryland Cares for Kids Act, all children eligible for reduced-price meals receive free meals using state funding. The program helps ensure students have access to nutritious food to support their health, development, and academic success. Funds help offset the cost of producing meals for students.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Schools receive federal reimbursement for each meal served that meets USDA nutrition standards. Children may receive free or reduced-price lunches based on household income, categorical eligibility (e.g., participation in SNAP or Temporary Assistance Cash), direct certification through Medicaid, or enrollment in qualifying programs such as Head Start. Under the Maryland Cares for Kids Act, all children eligible for reduced-price meals receive free meals using state funding. State funding ensures students from households qualifying for reduced-price meals receive meals at no cost. Direct payments are provided to help offset the cost of producing meals for students.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public schools, nonprofit private schools, and residential childcare institutions serving children in Maryland; families seeking free or reduced-price meals for their children.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Providing nutritionally balanced lunches and snacks to students at no cost or reduced cost. Funds help offset the cost of producing meals for students.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All 24 Maryland public school systems and 22 nonprofit private schools and residential childcare institutions participate statewide.
requirements_list: Must be a public school system, nonprofit private school, or residential childcare institution
Must serve meals that meet USDA nutrition standards aligned with the Dietary Guidelines for Americans to receive federal reimbursement
Local Education Agencies (LEAs) participating in NSLP must have a local school wellness policy

Children qualify based on income (at or below 130% of federal poverty level for free meals; 130–185% for reduced-price), categorical eligibility, direct certification through Medicaid, or enrollment in qualifying programs such as Head Start
Household income at or below published Income Eligibility Guidelines (IEGs) for appropriate household size
Income verification based on frequency of income sources
Use of annualization conversion factors when household has multiple income sources at different frequencies
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Schools enroll through their Local Education Agency's school nutrition office. Families apply for free or reduced-price meals through their school by submitting an application with household income information, which is compared to Income Eligibility Guidelines (IEGs) for appropriate household size and frequency. Families may also be directly certified based on participation in federal assistance programs. Contact the Office of School and Community Nutrition Programs for additional information on participation.

structured_extraction.program_name: Nonpublic Special Education School Cost Approval (Budget and Cost Sheet Process)
structured_extraction.program_description: MSDE reviews and approves the costs of nonpublic special education schools that serve students placed at public expense by local school systems. Each nonpublic school submits an annual budget to MSDE, which uses it to set per diem and related services rates that fund the reasonable expenses necessary to provide a Free Appropriate Public Education (FAPE) to students. The process covers education, residential, related services, and extended school year services, and applies to both in-state and out-of-state providers serving Maryland students.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MSDE approves program costs by reviewing each nonpublic school's annual budget and setting per diem and related services rates. Schools submit budgets using standardized templates (Forms 1A, 1B, 2A-5B); MSDE conducts budget analysis and issues Per Diem and Related Service Rate Calculations. Upon consensus, MSDE issues final Annual Program Cost Sheet Templates with locked rates that populate into cost sheets distributed to LEAs for tuition billing. Schools may request rate reconsideration or appeal within 30-day timeframes. Out-of-state residential providers may also obtain approved rates through a separate process.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 15, 2026 (Budget Submission Due Date for All Schools); April 27, 2026 (Due Date for Budgets with MSDE-Approved Extensions)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonpublic special education schools and programs serving students placed by Maryland local school systems or public agencies at public expense; students with disabilities (ages 3-21); Local Education Agencies (LEAs); out-of-state residential providers serving Maryland students.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating expenses necessary to provide a Free Appropriate Public Education (FAPE), including personnel salaries (administrative, classroom, related services, support staff), fringe benefits/insurance, contractual professional fees, supplies, equipment, occupancy, utilities, transportation, educational materials, related services provision, and indirect costs (capped at 10% of direct costs). Also covers residential services, extended school year services, and supplementary aids and program modifications.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to nonpublic schools serving Maryland students placed at public expense; out-of-state residential providers may also apply through a separate process. Schools must operate within any of the 24 Maryland local school systems or be certified in their state of operation for out-of-state placements.
requirements_list: School must serve students placed by a local school system (LSS) or public agency at public expense.
School must comply with COMAR 13A.09.10 (Educational Programs in Nonpublic Schools and Child Care and Treatment Facilities).
Annual budget must be submitted to MSDE for review and approval using the current SFY template with all required forms and documentation.
Payment or reimbursement may not require an additional contribution from the State beyond approved costs.
Comply with GAAP accounting principles; ensure all costs are reasonable and allowable.
Provide supporting documentation for equipment, transportation, and depreciation.
Maintain teacher parity salary verification (Teacher Pay Parity Act compliance for SFY 2027).
Complete Related Services Revenue/Cost Compliance Verification Tool (new for SFY 2027).
Complete salary schedules (Forms 3/3A-3F) with FTE and costs; complete operating cost forms (Forms 4A-4N).
Complete Annual Program Cost Sheet in Microsoft Excel format with student information (name, DOB, gender, ethnicity, disability code).
Provide Medical Assistance eligibility documentation.
Submit entry/discharge dates aligned with billable days and IEP-based service specifications.
Provide signatures from Director of Education and Director of Finance.
Submit written notification of changes within 30 calendar days.
Complete SFY Cost Approval Agreement or Disagreement form; upload to MOVEit secure file transfer site.
Comply with Financial Audit, Medicaid, and related services requirements.
Calendar revisions must be submitted no later than July 5; information changes submitted within 10 business days of change.
Out-of-state providers must provide Legal Authority Name on Certificate of Approval and MSDE School Number.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Each nonpublic school submits an annual budget packet to MSDE using the provided budget template and guidelines. MSDE reviews the budget against allowable operating expense guidelines and approves program costs, which are then functionalized as per diem and related services rates. Schools complete standardized forms, provide supporting documentation, and upload materials to the MOVEit secure file transfer site. Upon receipt of Per Diem and Related Service Rate Calculations, schools complete the Cost Approval Agreement or Disagreement form within two weeks. If disagreement is filed, schools may request rate reconsideration within 30 calendar days. Upon consensus, MSDE issues final Annual Program Cost Sheets to LEAs.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Maryland State aid program that helps fund the cost of educating students with disabilities who are placed in nonpublic (private) special education schools through the Individualized Education Program (IEP) process. The State calculates its share of nonpublic special education costs under Education Article §8-415 (and §8-406) of the Annotated Code of Maryland and reimburses local school systems for these placements. Covers approved day or residential programs, individual placements, and out-of-state programs, including standard education, related services, extended school year services, and specialized services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State aid covers a share of nonpublic special education tuition costs for students placed in MSDE-approved day or residential programs, individual placements in non-approved programs, or out-of-state programs through the IEP process. Covered costs include standard education, related services (audiology, counseling, occupational therapy, physical therapy, speech-language pathology, behavioral modification, etc.), extended school year services, residential services when necessary, and supplemental aides/program modifications as outlined in IEPs. The State's share is calculated per Education Article §8-415. Local education agencies (school systems) apply for reimbursement; these students are counted in the September 30 enrollment with a code 09 designation and are excluded from standard Foundation formula calculations because they go through the tuition reimbursement process instead.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Within 30 calendar days of entry date, discharge date, or service revision date; September 30, 2022 for ESY/July-August entries; July 7, 2023 for June 3-30 entries (FY2023 cycle)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local education agencies (school systems) that place students with disabilities in nonpublic special education schools through the IEP process; students with disabilities (ages 3+) requiring day, residential, or individual nonpublic special education placements
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition costs and related educational services for students with disabilities placed in nonpublic special education day or residential programs, individual placements in non-approved programs, or out-of-state programs; includes related services, extended school year services, residential services when applicable, and supplemental aides/program modifications
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across all Maryland jurisdictions; out-of-state programs are also eligible for individual placements
requirements_list: Student must be placed in a nonpublic special education school through the IEP process
Student must be included in the September 30 enrollment count with a code 09 designation
Placement must be in an MSDE-approved day or residential program, or an individual placement (non-approved or out-of-state)
IEP developed in accordance with federal and state laws and approved by parent/guardian
Review of measurable annual goals with benchmarks/short-term objectives completed
Placement must provide appropriate educational program in least restrictive environment
Supporting documentation on file (IEP, annual review, progress reports)
Approved cost sheet for current fiscal year (individual placements)
IEP team minutes supporting placement decision
Letter from service provider confirming FAPE implementation in least restrictive environment
Mediation/due process agreement documentation (if applicable)
LSS Special Education Supervisor/Director signature and approval
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Local education agencies submit the MSDE Approved Day and Residential Program Application for approved program placements. Individual placement applications are available upon request. Applications must be submitted within 30 calendar days of entry date, discharge date, or service revision date. Directions, definitions, and examples are provided separately for approved day/residential programs and individual placements.

structured_extraction.program_name: OBVS Services at Workforce & Technology Center (WTC)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Division of Rehabilitation Services' Office for Blindness and Vision Services (OBVS) provides evaluation, training, and case management services at the Workforce & Technology Center campus to help individuals who are blind or visually impaired live and work as independently as possible. Services include orientation and mobility training, communications skills, household arts and daily living, adjustment to blindness, interview prep, disability advocacy, resume prep, and pre-employment transition services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free vocational rehabilitation and independent living services for individuals who are blind or visually impaired, delivered at the WTC campus. Services include orientation and mobility evaluation and training, communications skills (large print, Braille, keyboarding), household arts and daily living skills, the eight-week ABLE (Adjustment to Blindness for Life & Employment) program offered twice yearly, interview prep, disability advocacy, resume prep, and pre-employment transition services for students.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals who are blind or visually impaired seeking to improve independent living skills and prepare for employment.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and evaluation services to develop orientation and mobility, daily living, communication, and employment readiness skills.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Services are provided at the DORS Workforce & Technology Center campus in Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be blind or visually impaired
Must be a DORS consumer or eligible for DORS services
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact DORS or OBVS to be referred for services at the Workforce & Technology Center.

structured_extraction.program_description: An assessment available at the Work Technology Center (WTC) and in the community that provides information about an individual's functional ability to work or live independently, along with recommendations to enhance independent living skills and work activities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: An occupational therapy assessment that evaluates functional ability for work or independent living and provides recommendations for improvement.
structured_extraction.program_audience: DORS consumers who need assessment of functional ability for work or independent living.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Assessment and recommendations to improve work performance and independent living skills.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at WTC and in the community throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a DORS consumer
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact DORS to be referred for an Occupational Therapy Evaluation.

structured_extraction.program_name: Occupational-Physical Therapy Evaluation / Functional Capacity Evaluation (OT-PT/FCE)
structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive assessment provided through the Maryland Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS) that offers objective information about an individual's physical capabilities and limitations related to employment. Participants are assessed by both a Physical Therapist and an Occupational Therapist to determine their ability to perform work safely. The evaluation — which may take the form of a Functional Capacity Evaluation (FCE) — measures maximum physical work capabilities and compares them to specific job requirements, supporting the development of an individualized employment plan.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A dual assessment by both a Physical Therapist and an Occupational Therapist (and/or a Functional Capacity Evaluation) that evaluates a job seeker's employment-related physical capabilities, strengths, and limitations, and compares findings to job requirements to support employment planning.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Job seekers with disabilities who need a comprehensive, objective assessment of their physical work capabilities and limitations to support employment planning.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Assessment services to determine an individual's ability to perform specific jobs or job tasks and to identify physical strengths and limitations relevant to employment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available through DORS, which serves Maryland residents statewide.
requirements_list: Must be a DORS consumer (individual with a disability seeking employment)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact DORS to be referred for an OT-PT Evaluation or Functional Capacity Evaluation as part of an individualized employment plan.

structured_extraction.program_description: This process allows a Local School System (LSS) in Maryland to apply for State nonpublic tuition assistance when placing a student with special education needs at an out-of-state residential school. The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) partners with the LSS to review the out-of-state facility, verify it meets Maryland requirements, approve program costs, and issue a cost sheet for state funding contributions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The State provides a financial contribution (tuition assistance) toward the cost of placing a student with special education needs at an out-of-state residential nonpublic school. MSDE approves the program cost and issues a Maryland Annual Program Cost Sheet to the provider once eligibility is confirmed.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local School Systems (LSSs) in Maryland seeking to place a student with special education needs at an out-of-state residential nonpublic school
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition and program costs for out-of-state residential nonpublic school placements for students with special education needs
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to all Maryland Local School Systems
requirements_list: The LSS must consider all Maryland nonpublic school options before pursuing out-of-state placement
The LSS must partner with MSDE prior to implementing the out-of-state placement
The LSS must verify the out-of-state school can support the student's progress toward a Maryland high school diploma or the Maryland High School Certificate of Program Completion
MSDE must determine that the out-of-state provider is approved by the state in which it is located
The provider must substantially meet certain requirements established in Maryland (COMAR 13A.05.02.12)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The LSS reviews the instructional program and related services of the out-of-state facility and partners with MSDE before implementing placement. MSDE reviews the provider's approval status and compliance with Maryland standards. If approved, MSDE works with the provider to approve costs and issue a Maryland Annual Program Cost Sheet.

structured_extraction.program_description: Educational support services for job seekers with autism in collaboration with community colleges throughout Maryland. The program is a collaboration between DORS and participating community colleges, helping students adjust to college life, explore careers, and develop employment and communication skills.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Educational support including adjustment to college life, career guidance and counseling, assessment services, employment and communication skills training, and individual and group sessions. Students enroll in credit or certificate classes and register with the college's Disability Support Services.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Job seekers with a documented autism diagnosis who have an active DORS Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE) that includes college as part of a vocational/employment plan and are attending a participating community college.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Support for college enrollment, career exploration, and employment skill development.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at Anne Arundel Community College, Community College of Baltimore County, Howard Community College, Prince George's Community College, College of Southern Maryland, and Montgomery College.
requirements_list: Documented diagnosis of autism
Active DORS Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE) that supports college as part of an employment plan
Registered with the Disability Support Services (DSS) program at the college
Attend weekly group sessions and schedule classes around this standing appointment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact a DORS Counselor or local DORS office to request services (QR code available). Work with a DORS Counselor to establish an IPE that supports college, then register with the Disability Support Services at a participating community college and connect with the DORS Pathways coordinator.

structured_extraction.program_name: Perkins V (Carl D. Perkins Career and Technical Education Act) State and Local Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: Federal funding distributed to local school systems, community colleges, and other education providers in Maryland to support career and technical education (CTE) programs of study. Recipients use funds to improve CTE instruction and expand student access to high-quality career pathways aligned to high-skill, high-wage, and in-demand jobs. The program supports a continuum from secondary through postsecondary levels, including work-based learning, industry-recognized credentials, apprenticeships, dual enrollment, and P-TECH programs. Requires completion of a Comprehensive Local Needs Assessment (CLNA) every two years to identify gaps in CTE programming and align improvement efforts with the College and Career Readiness Pillar in Maryland's Blueprint for Maryland's Future.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal Perkins V formula grants allocated to eligible local education agencies (school systems), community colleges, the Juvenile Services Education System, the Adult Correctional Education System, and other affiliates. Of total funds, 15% is retained by MSDE for state administration and leadership; 85% is distributed to recipients (5% competitive reserve fund, 65% to secondary, 35% to postsecondary). Reserve fund grants are competitive and prioritize rural areas, those with high percentages or numbers of CTE completers. To qualify, applicants must complete a Comprehensive Local Needs Assessment (CLNA) every two years and submit an approved Local Application. Local applications must be fully completed, negotiated, and approved by July 1st of each year. Funds support CTE program development, equipment purchases, professional development for educators, curriculum updates, infrastructure improvements, instructor recruitment and retention, work-based learning and apprenticeship opportunities, and strategies to improve student performance outcomes.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Must be fully completed, negotiated, and approved by July 1st of each year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local school systems, community colleges, juvenile services education programs, adult correctional education programs, and other CTE affiliates in Maryland; secondary (grades 9-12) and postsecondary students including special populations, students with disabilities, English learners, homeless youth, foster youth, out-of-school youth, nontraditional students, economically disadvantaged students, single parents, migrant students, and youth with parents in active military service; CTE educators, instructors, counselors, and administrators
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Improving CTE instruction; expanding student access to quality CTE programs of study; supporting career pathways leading to industry-recognized credentials; work-based learning and apprenticeship programs; P-TECH program expansion; professional learning for teachers, faculty, counselors, and administrators; equipment and technology; dual enrollment and early college credit; student support services for special populations; CTE marketing; data system development; equity initiatives; career guidance and counseling; curriculum updates; infrastructure improvements; instructor recruitment and retention initiatives; outreach initiatives; program enhancement and new program development
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — available to eligible Maryland local education agencies and postsecondary institutions across all 24 Maryland counties
requirements_list: Must complete a Comprehensive Local Needs Assessment (CLNA) every two years to evaluate capacity to offer high-quality CTE programming
Must submit a Local Application incorporating CLNA results and outlining planned use of federal funds; must be fully completed, negotiated, and approved by July 1st of each year
Must meet State Determined Performance Levels (SDPLs) on required core indicators for secondary and postsecondary CTE programs
Must align programs to high-skill, high-wage, and/or in-demand careers
Must provide annual analysis of CTE student performance and target improvement efforts in annual applications
Reserve fund eligibility requires meeting at least one criterion: located in rural area, high percentage of CTE completers, or high number of CTE students
Must have at least 2 state-approved CTE Programs of Study, each with minimum 3 credits of coordinated coursework
Must meet Size, Scope, and Quality criteria for CTE programs
Must establish stakeholder team including required representative groups
Must establish and monitor S.M.A.R.T.I.E. goals (Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound, Inclusive, Equitable)
Must align programs with Maryland's labor market projections
Must collect and report data on accountability indicators for CTE concentrators
Performance levels must be objective, quantifiable, and measurable, and must show meaningful progress toward improving all CTE student performance
Must develop program improvement plans for underperforming indicators
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Local education agencies and postsecondary institutions assemble a diverse stakeholder team and complete the Comprehensive Local Needs Assessment (CLNA) every two years, analyzing data on program performance by student group and identifying root causes of underperformance. Applicants then establish S.M.A.R.T.I.E. goals, align goals with annual Perkins budget, and submit a Local Application (must be fully completed, negotiated, and approved by July 1st each year) describing how they will use Perkins funds to improve CTE. Approved applications receive Perkins funding through formula allocation or competitive reserve fund grants.

structured_extraction.program_description: An evaluation to identify a consumer's level of functioning and need for personal assistance with daily living activities while attending college. The evaluation also covers equipment or modifications needed for coursework and daily living in college campus housing.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: An assessment to determine the hours of personal assistance needed and any equipment or modifications required for a consumer to participate in college coursework and campus living.
structured_extraction.program_audience: DORS consumers with disabilities who are attending or planning to attend college and need personal assistance services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Assessment to determine personal assistance needs and equipment or modifications for college attendance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available through DORS, which serves Maryland residents.
requirements_list: Must be a DORS consumer
Must be attending or planning to attend college
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact DORS to be referred for a Personal Assistance Service evaluation as part of an educational plan.

structured_extraction.program_description: A physical therapy assessment available at the Work Technology Center (WTC) and in the community, provided by DORS staff and third-party vendors. It evaluates an individual's functional ability to work or live independently and provides recommendations to improve mobility, work performance, and physical tolerance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A physical therapy assessment that evaluates functional mobility and work ability, with recommendations to improve independent living skills, work performance, and physical tolerance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: DORS consumers who need assessment of functional mobility and physical work capacity.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Assessment and recommendations to improve functional mobility, independent living, and work performance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at WTC and in the community throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a DORS consumer
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact DORS to be referred for a Physical Therapy Evaluation.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides instruction in self-advocacy and social skills training to Pre-Employment Transition Services (Pre-ETS) students with Autism. Students participate in activities that develop soft skills needed to get and keep a job, including introduction to education, training and employment options after high school (apprenticeships, career training, job placement, college). Includes college tour participation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Self-advocacy instruction, social skills training, soft skills development, post-secondary education counseling, and college tours to help students with autism develop skills needed to obtain and maintain employment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Pre-ETS students with Autism Spectrum Disorder diagnosis; currently enrolled in high school, post-high school education program, or recognized trade school; ages 14-22; with documented disability via IEP, 504 plan, or medical records.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Self-advocacy training and social skills development for employment preparation, including post-secondary education counseling and college tours.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Currently enrolled in high school, post-high school education program, or recognized educational program (trade school)
At least 14 years old but less than 22
Has Individualized Education Program (IEP), 504 plan, or medical records documenting disability
Diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact a DORS Counselor or local DORS office, or request services via QR code.

structured_extraction.program_description: Pre-Employment Transition Services (Pre-ETS) are five specific services — job exploration counseling, self-advocacy instruction, counseling on post-secondary education, workplace readiness training, and work-based learning experiences — designed to help students with disabilities between ages 14 and 21 identify career interests and prepare for employment and post-secondary education. The program gives students opportunities to explore and experience the world of work through these specific Pre-ETS activities. Services are short-term, introductory, and free to students and families at no cost. Offered in partnership with students, families, school staff, approved community rehabilitation providers (CRPs), and other key stakeholders.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free services including job exploration counseling, self-advocacy instruction, counseling on post-secondary education options, workplace readiness training, and work-based learning experiences at local employers. Available to all eligible students with disabilities ages 14–21. There is no cost to students or families. Services are generally short-term and cover introductory topics. Also available virtually through DORS offices located throughout Maryland (more than 20 offices statewide).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students with disabilities aged 14 to 21 who are enrolled in secondary school, post-secondary education, homeschool, or other approved/recognized educational program (and have not graduated or withdrawn), and have documented disabilities (IEP, 504 plan, or medical documentation). Families and parents of eligible students are also served.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Career exploration and counseling, self-advocacy skill development, post-secondary education counseling, workplace readiness training, and work-based learning experiences.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through local DORS offices (more than 20 offices) across Maryland; services also available virtually. Maryland residents only.
requirements_list: Must be at least 14 years old and no more than 21 (under age 22)
Must be currently enrolled in secondary school, post-secondary education, homeschool, or other recognized/approved educational program and have not graduated or withdrawn
Must have a documented disability (IEP, 504 plan, or medical documentation/records)
All students in this age range with disabilities are currently eligible for Pre-ETS services — no additional eligibility requirements
No financial eligibility requirements — no cost to student or family
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Visit dors.maryland.gov and click 'Request DORS Services' (or call local DORS office for phone assistance). 2. Complete the Request DORS Services form (can be submitted by student, parent, medical provider, or school staff). 3. DORS contacts the student and family by email through the secure SARA system with instructions; a DORS representative responds within 10 business days to schedule a virtual or in-person meeting. 4. Student or parent/guardian submits additional documentation (Social Security Number, disability documentation, proof of school enrollment, proof of age) and signs the Pre-ETS Consent to Participate form via SARA. 5. DORS staff review documentation and forward the qualifying student's information to the local DORS office. 6. A local DORS counselor contacts the student and family to hold a Pre-ETS Service Agreement Meeting to plan services. Spanish-language applicants can follow the process at https://dors.maryland.gov/consumers/Pages/Referral-Spanish.aspx.

structured_extraction.program_description: Academic instruction program for individuals who are not yet at the skill level needed for GED® instruction but want a high school diploma to pursue their employment goals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Pre-GED instruction offered at WTC and virtually to help participants build the skills needed to enter the GED program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with disabilities who need to build academic skills before beginning GED instruction.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Academic skill building toward a high school diploma and employment goals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at WTC and virtually.
requirements_list: Must have at least 7th grade reading and math skills as recorded on the CASAS or TABE.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Work with a DORS counselor; rolling admission basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive grant program administered by the Division of Early Childhood at MSDE that funds Local Education Agencies (LEAs) and private providers to deliver high-quality, full-day prekindergarten and school readiness services for three- and four-year-old children from families with household incomes up to 300% of the Federal Poverty Level, in alignment with The Blueprint for Maryland's Future.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant funding awarded to Local Education Agencies (LEAs), qualified vendors, and private providers to expand access to high-quality prekindergarten programs. Total funding available: $26,644,000 with an estimated 50 grants at approximately $400,000 per grant. Funding is $19,950 per full-day slot for three- and four-year-old children. A 20% advance payment is available upon request with supporting receipts. Reimbursement is only for occupied slots; utilization must remain above 85%. Funds cannot be directed to tuition. Grant period: July 1, 2026 – June 30, 2027.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Wednesday, March 11, 2026. No later than 5:00 pm EDT.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Dr. Nykia Washington, Prekindergarten and Mixed Delivery Program Manager
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local Education Agencies (LEAs), qualified vendors as defined in COMAR 13a.06.02, and private providers (including Head Start, center-based, and family child care programs) that hold a valid license or registration and will deliver prekindergarten services in Maryland. Ultimately serves three- and four-year-old children from families with incomes up to 300% of the Federal Poverty Level, including children with disabilities, multilingual learners, and children experiencing homelessness.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Lead teacher and assistant teacher salaries meeting qualification requirements; curriculum and high-quality instructional materials (HQIM); professional learning, coaching, and instructional support; administrative costs; program quality improvements to reach Maryland EXCELS Level 5; contracted services (e.g., health screenings, assessments, specialized services); supplies and materials; equipment and technology; family engagement activities; child assessments; professional development (minimum 20 hours annually for teaching staff). Funds cannot be directed to tuition.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide throughout Maryland. MSDE reserves the right to consider geographic distribution when making awards, with priority given to areas with demonstrated unmet Pre-K service needs.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Local Education Agency (LEA), a qualified vendor as defined in COMAR 13a.06.02, or a private provider (Head Start, center-based, or family child care program).
Must hold a valid license or registration (if applicable), or be a Head Start program.
Must participate in the Maryland EXCELS program and maintain or achieve a quality rating of Level 5.
Services must align with The Blueprint for Maryland's Future and Maryland Early Learning Standards.
Must serve children aged three or four years old from families with household incomes up to 300% of the Federal Poverty Level.
Must use high-quality, evidence-based curriculum and implement High-Quality Instructional Materials (HQIM).
Programs must operate a minimum 180-day school year with at least 6.5 hours of instruction per day.
Must execute a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with private providers by September 30, 2026 (for mixed-delivery models).
Must maintain separate tracking of grant funds and submit a detailed budget with calculations and justifications.
Must submit a comprehensive sustainability plan with community and business partnerships.
Must report student enrollment data (demographics, enrollment, income eligibility).
Must comply with fiscal and program monitoring requirements, including annual review visits.
Must comply with GEPA Section 427 (non-discrimination and access requirements).
Must comply with Civil Rights Act (1964), CFR 34, ESEA, EDGAR, GEPA, and ADA.
Must maintain ADA-accessible facilities and ensure digital/web-based tools meet WCAG 2.1 Level AA accessibility standards.
Must retain financial records for a minimum of 5 years.
Entities expending $1,000,000 or more annually must have an annual financial and compliance audit.
Must obtain prior written approval for programmatic changes or budget realignments of $1,000 or 15% of total, whichever is greater.
Nonprofit organizations are subject to a 15% de minimis indirect cost rate (effective July 1, 2025).
Applicants must review the updated Grant Information Guide (GIG) before applying.
Application must be completed in Qualtrics; no changes can be made after submission.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review the Grant Information Guide (GIG) released January 21, 2026. Attend optional customer service support sessions or office hours hosted by MSDE. FAQ and answers will be posted to the Prekindergarten webpage following customer service support sessions. Funding opportunity documents can be downloaded from the MSDE Office of Grants Administration and Compliance website. Submit the grant application via the online Qualtrics form (four sections: Applicant Information, Slots Requested, Application, and Appendices) by March 11, 2026 at 5:00 pm EDT. Applications can be saved and returned to using the same device/browser. Download a PDF copy of responses before final submission as no changes can be made after submission.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Preschool Special Education Services provides specialized instruction and related services — such as speech-language therapy, physical therapy, and occupational therapy — to eligible children ages 3 through 5 with disabilities. Services are delivered at no cost to families through local education agencies, the Maryland School for the Blind, and the Maryland School for the Deaf, ensuring a free appropriate public education (FAPE) in the least restrictive environment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free specialized instruction and related services (including speech-language therapy, physical therapy, and occupational therapy) provided through local education agencies at no cost to families. Services are tailored through an Individualized Education Program (IEP) for each eligible child.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Children ages 3 through 5 with qualifying disabilities and their families in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Specialized instruction and related services including speech-language therapy, physical therapy, and occupational therapy for preschool children with disabilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through 24 local education agencies, the Maryland School for the Blind, and the Maryland School for the Deaf. Service availability is based on the jurisdiction where the family resides.
requirements_list: Child must be between the ages of 3 and 5

Child must have a qualifying disability under IDEA: Autism, Deafness, Deaf-Blindness, Developmental Delay (ages 3 to 7), Emotional Disability, Hearing Impairment, Intellectual Disability, Multiple Disabilities, Orthopedic Impairment, Other Health Impairment, Specific Learning Disability, Speech or Language Impairment, Traumatic Brain Injury, or Visual Impairment including blindness
Referral must be made to the local education agency's Child Find office
Parental consent required before assessments
Eligibility determined by an IEP team following comprehensive evaluation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Make a referral to the local education agency's Child Find office or call the program in your jurisdiction. Provide parental consent for assessments. Participate in an IEP team meeting where assessment results are reviewed and eligibility is determined. If eligible, an IEP is developed and services are implemented. Families may also visit referral.mditp.org for referral information.

structured_extraction.program_description: An initiative designed by a local school system to address the needs of individual students or groups of students who are at high risk of being placed in a nonpublic special education school. The program uses wrap-around supportive services within the public school setting to meet a targeted need and help school systems build local capacity to address specific, immediate needs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Wrap-around supportive services delivered within the public school setting to prevent nonpublic placement for at-risk students. Specific funding amounts are not stated on this page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local school systems with students at high risk of placement in nonpublic special education schools.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Wrap-around supportive services within the public school setting to address targeted student needs and build local capacity to serve students with intensive special education needs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to local school systems throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a Local School System (LSS) in Maryland
Must serve students at high risk of placement in a nonpublic special education school
Program must address a specific, immediate targeted need
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Preventative Service Plan is available upon request. Contact Sheila F. Philip at MSDE for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Professional Learning in Early Literacy Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: This grant funds professional learning for Pre-K teachers and early childhood educators on strategies based on the Science of Reading research. It extends the Maryland Leads initiative to support teachers of 3- and 4-year-old children, including Head Start teachers and private child care teachers and supervisors/directors.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Awards range from $40,000 to $80,000 per Local School System (LSS). A total of $1,000,000 is available, with an estimated 12–24 grants. The grant period runs September 1, 2022 through September 30, 2023, with possible extension to March 2023 pending federal approval. Funds may be used for salaries & wages, contracted services (Science of Reading vendors), supplies & materials, equipment, other charges, and indirect costs.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: October 11, 2022, no later than 5:00 p.m. EST
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local School Systems (LSSs), Head Start programs, and private child care providers in Maryland seeking to provide professional learning to Pre-K teachers, assistant teachers, coaches, specialists, special educators, Head Start teachers, and private child care teachers and supervisors/directors of 3- and 4-year-olds.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Professional learning activities and materials for early childhood educators aligned to the Science of Reading research, including salaries & wages, contracted services (Science of Reading vendors), supplies & materials, equipment, facilitator costs, program implementation, evaluation activities, and indirect costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to all Local School Systems (LSSs) and eligible early childhood providers throughout Maryland. MSDE may consider geographic distribution when making awards.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Local School System (LSS), Head Start program, or private child care provider
Proposals must be submitted by 5:00 p.m. EST on October 11, 2022
Applications must be submitted via email
Identify clearly defined literacy problem and professional learning needs
Describe alignment to science of reading research
Provide facilitator qualifications
Include project timeline with evaluation
Submit C-1-25 MSDE budget form
Submit signed recipient assurances page
Include scope of work from approved Science of Reading vendor
Include resumes of key personnel
Provide education support professionals employment data with documentation
Engagement of private child care providers and Head Start staff
Comprehensive evaluation plan
Clear management structure with qualified personnel
Reasonable budget with aligned line items
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download the Grant Information Guide and application form from the program page. Submit the completed application with cover page, C-1-25 MSDE budget form, signed recipient assurances, scope of work from approved Science of Reading vendor, resumes of key personnel, and education support professionals employment data via email by 5:00 p.m. EST on October 11, 2022. Applications are scored on a 100-point rubric across six categories: Extent of Need (10 points), Goals (20 points), Implementation Plan (30 points), Evaluation and Dissemination (10 points), Management Plan (10 points), and Budget (20 points). MSDE held customer service support sessions on September 14 and 15, 2022 for interested applicants.

structured_extraction.program_description: A funding agreement between a Local School System (LSS) and a Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE)-approved nonpublic special education program. The program places students with significant and intensive special education needs in the Least Restrictive Environment (LRE) within their community, enhancing IEP services and supporting inclusion and provision of Free Appropriate Public Education (FAPE). It is especially helpful for students with short-term needs who are in crisis or awaiting a more intensive placement, as well as students transitioning to less restrictive programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State funding for full-time equivalent (FTE) seats based on actual enrollment, paid through a funding agreement (tuition contribution) between a local school system and an MSDE-approved nonpublic special education program. Payment is reconciled based on actual enrollment days and FTE seats used during the school year. The program is cost-neutral to the State and cannot exceed traditional nonpublic tuition assistance costs. Specific dollar amounts are not stated.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: By June 1 of each school year for renewals; minimum 30 calendar days prior to requesting State funding for each fiscal year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local school systems (LSS) partnering with MSDE-approved nonpublic special education programs to serve students with significant and intensive special education needs, including students requiring short-term placements, students in crisis or awaiting intensive placement, and students transitioning to less restrictive programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding enhanced IEP services for students with significant and intensive special education needs placed in MSDE-approved nonpublic programs, including short-term placements, access to public school instruction and activities, and student transitions to less restrictive programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to local school systems throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a Local School System (LSS) in Maryland
Partner program must be an MSDE-approved nonpublic special education program
Student must have significant and intensive special education needs
Placement must be in the Least Restrictive Environment (LRE)
Signed contracts required before State funds are released
Mid-year and end-of-year enrollment and outcome data reporting required
Fiscal year reconciliation must be completed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: LSS initiate discussions with MSDE by February 1. Applications are submitted to MSDE by June 1. MSDE provides notice of intent to fund by July 15. Finalized contracts must be submitted before funds are released. Applications are available upon request from Sheila F. Philip at MSDE, along with the PPP Financial Worksheet, PPP Verification and Assurances, and other required documents.

structured_extraction.program_description: Push to Pre-K helps child care providers expand their services and access state prekindergarten funding. Pre-K Specialists guide providers through every step of meeting requirements and applying for Pre-K grants.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides access to state prekindergarten grant funding and hands-on guidance from Pre-K Specialists to help child care providers meet grant requirements and expand their services.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care providers seeking to expand their services and access state pre-K grant funding
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Expanding child care services to offer state-funded prekindergarten programs
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to child care providers in Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a licensed child care provider
Must meet requirements for Pre-K grants (guidance provided by Pre-K Specialists)
Read and understand the Grant Information Guide (GIG)
Meet eligibility criteria outlined in the GIG
Demonstrate technical expertise, personnel, and financial capacity to provide services as described in the GIG
Obtain support from all organizational stakeholders
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Grant Consideration Checklist before beginning the application process. Must answer 'yes' to all four checklist questions before proceeding. Visit PushToPreK.com for more information. Pre-K Specialists are available to walk providers through every step of the process.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Ready for Kindergarten (R4K) Grant provides funding to Local School Systems (LSSs) in Maryland to support professional learning, improve teacher practices, and increase Prekindergarten students' readiness for Kindergarten. Eligible uses include the Child Development Associate (CDA) credential for Prekindergarten Assistant Teachers, planning for a coordinated Prekindergarten mixed delivery enrollment process, and accreditation in the Maryland EXCELS program. Grant funds must support continuous improvement using the R4K comprehensive assessment system for Prekindergarten and Kindergarten.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding for professional learning initiatives, CDA credentialing for Prekindergarten Assistant Teachers, planning for coordinated Prekindergarten mixed delivery enrollment, and program accreditation through Maryland EXCELS. The grant period was June 15, 2022 – December 30, 2023.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local School Systems (LSSs) in Maryland seeking funding to improve Kindergarten readiness and support early childhood assessment practices.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Professional learning initiatives, Child Development Associate (CDA) credential for Prekindergarten Assistant Teachers, planning for a coordinated Prekindergarten mixed delivery enrollment process, and accreditation in the Maryland EXCELS program. Funds must support continuous improvement using the R4K assessment system for Prekindergarten and Kindergarten.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Local School Systems throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Local School System (LSS) in Maryland
Grant applications must be submitted by June 3, 2022 via email
Application must be saved as 'Name of LEA_R4K23 Grant Proposal'
Email subject line must read 'R4K FY23 Grant Proposal'
Funds must be used to support initiatives for continuous improvement using the R4K comprehensive assessment system
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download the R4K Application, complete it, and save as 'Name of LEA_R4K23 Grant Proposal'. Submit by email to r4kgrant@maryland.gov with 'R4K FY23 Grant Proposal' in the subject line by June 3, 2022. MSDE held two customer service support sessions on May 9 and May 11, 2022 for applicants with questions.

structured_extraction.program_description: The SEED School of Maryland is a statewide public boarding school offering a college-preparatory education for students in grades 6 through 12 from disadvantaged circumstances. Students live on campus Sunday through Friday and are expected to graduate and attend a four-year college. The school serves up to 400 students and draws from across all Maryland counties.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Students receive a publicly funded boarding school education including on-campus housing Sunday through Friday, college-preparatory curriculum, and special education services as needed. The program is funded through state and local sources at no tuition cost to students.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications due in April; lottery held in mid-May
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland students from disadvantaged circumstances who are about to enter 6th or 9th grade and are motivated to pursue a college education
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Public boarding school education including housing, college-preparatory instruction, and special education services
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to students from throughout Maryland; lottery is designed to ensure at least two eligible students from each Local Education Agency (LEA) have an opportunity to enroll
requirements_list: Must be about to enter 6th or 9th grade
Must reside in Maryland
Must be capable of being safe and healthy in a boarding school setting
Must be personally motivated to pursue and prepare for college
Prior academic performance is not a determining factor for eligibility
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted in the fall for the following school year. A lottery is held in mid-May for all eligible applicants, with applications due in April. Details are available on SEED's website at seedschoolmd.org/eligibility.

structured_extraction.program_name: SMILE (Skills to Move Towards Independence, Life & Employment)
structured_extraction.program_description: A summer program for Pre-ETS and transitioning youth who are blind or visually impaired. The program focuses on career exploration, work readiness, advocacy, independence, and social skills development. Activities include college and vocational exposure, technology instruction, guest speakers, and community resource connections.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Summer program offering in-person activities at the WTC and in the community, as well as virtual sessions. Covers career exploration, work readiness, self-advocacy, independence, social skills, interest inventories, guest speakers, and community resources.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Pre-ETS and transitioning youth who are blind or visually impaired
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Career exploration, work readiness, advocacy and independence skill development, technology training, social skills instruction
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Services offered in the community, at the WTC, and virtually statewide
requirements_list: Must be blind or visually impaired
Must be a Pre-ETS or transitioning youth DORS consumer
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact WTC or a local DORS office to enroll in the summer program.

structured_extraction.program_description: The School Breakfast Program (SBP) provides nutritious breakfasts to students in participating public and private schools and residential childcare institutions across Maryland each school day. The federal government reimburses participating schools for meals that meet USDA nutrition standards. Studies show eating breakfast is linked to higher test scores, fewer behavioral problems, reduced food insecurity, and fewer school absences. Over 898,000 students are served each day across all 24 Maryland public school districts, 17 non-profit private schools, and residential childcare institutions. Funds help offset the costs of producing meals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Schools receive federal reimbursement for each meal served that meets USDA nutrition standards. Students from families with incomes at or below 130–185% of the federal poverty level may receive meals free or at reduced price. Students in families receiving Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) or food stamp benefits qualify for free meals automatically. The program reimburses participating schools and institutions for providing nutritious breakfasts to over 898,000 students each day, helping offset the costs of producing meals.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public and nonprofit private schools and residential childcare institutions serving students in Maryland, including all 24 Maryland public school districts, 17 non-profit private schools, and residential childcare institutions serving children who qualify for free or reduced-price breakfast
