structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Providing nutritious breakfasts to students; funds help offset the costs of producing breakfast meals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — all 24 Maryland public school districts, 17 non-profit private schools, and residential childcare institutions are eligible to participate.
requirements_list: Must be a public school, nonprofit private school, or residential childcare institution
Must serve meals that comply with USDA nutrition standards and Dietary Guidelines for Americans
Students must meet family income eligibility (at or below 130–185% of the federal poverty level) for free or reduced-price meals
Students receiving Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) or food stamps qualify for free meals automatically
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Schools apply to participate through the Maryland State Department of Education's Office of School and Community Nutrition Programs. Applications are submitted annually. Contact the Office of School and Community Nutrition Programs for information on participation.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides milk to children in schools, childcare centers, and eligible camps that do not participate in other federal child nutrition meal programs. Reimburses participating institutions for the milk they serve to children. Also available to schools with half-day pre-K and kindergarten programs where children do not have access to school meal programs. Encourages the consumption of fluid milk by children in public and private nonprofit schools, summer camps, and other eligible nonprofit sites by offsetting the cost of the half-pint of milk served to children.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial reimbursement (direct payment) for milk served to children in schools, childcare institutions, and eligible camps that do not participate in other federal child nutrition meal programs. Also available to schools with half-day pre-K and kindergarten programs where children do not have access to school meal programs. Funds are used to offset the cost of the half-pint of milk served to children.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public and private nonprofit schools, childcare centers, summer camps, and other eligible nonprofit sites that serve milk to children, including schools with half-day pre-K and kindergarten programs where children do not have access to school meal programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Providing milk to children in schools, childcare institutions, and eligible camps; funds offset the cost of milk served to children.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a school, childcare center, or eligible camp
Must not participate in other federal child nutrition meal programs (or be a school with half-day pre-K/kindergarten without access to school meal programs)
Eligible entities include public and private nonprofit schools, summer camps, and other eligible nonprofit sites
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Office of School and Community Nutrition Programs for information on participation. Applications are submitted annually. A USDA program fact sheet is available for additional details.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) provides annual grants to qualified non-profit organizations that offer enriching educational programs to Maryland students. Funded programs provide learning experiences aligned with the State's curricular and educational priorities and the Blueprint for Maryland's Future that cannot be replicated in the classroom, including free or reduced admission, field trips, mentoring, tutoring, and professional development for teachers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual grants provided to qualified non-profit organizations to fund educational programs, experiential learning opportunities, mentoring, tutoring, field trips, and professional development for teachers that align with Maryland's curricular and educational priorities. Approximately $6,706,449 is available for FY 2027, with an estimated 60-65 grants to be awarded. The grant period is July 1, 2026 – June 30, 2027. Currently 57 organizations are in the program serving approximately 440,000 Maryland students and teachers. Funds cannot be used for operating costs (property repair/maintenance, property taxes, insurance, utilities, furniture, salaries for office/leadership staff, office supplies, rent); funds are intended for educational program purposes only.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: June 13, 2025, no later than 5:00 p.m. EDT
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations and State-Aided Institutions that provide enriching educational programs, experiential learning, mentoring, tutoring, and professional development to Maryland students (PreK-12) and teachers. Programs serve Local Education Agencies (LEAs) and participating schools statewide.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free or reduced admission programs, full-day and residential field trips with hands-on activities, mentoring, tutoring, pre- and post-visit classroom activities, professional development for teachers, outreach and expansion efforts, program evaluation and data collection, personnel and staffing, and other allowable cost-effective program expenses. Funds may not be used for operating costs such as property repair/maintenance, property taxes, insurance, utilities, furniture, salaries for office/leadership staff, office supplies, or rent.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Programs must serve Maryland students and align with the State's educational priorities and the Blueprint for Maryland's Future. Program is available statewide across all Maryland counties.
requirements_list: Must be a qualified 501(c)(3) non-profit organization in good standing
Must be based in Maryland, incorporated/registered under Maryland law
Must be current in payment of all tax obligations to the State
Must have an independent governing board with member list
Must maintain active liability insurance coverage
Must provide educational programs that align with Maryland's curricular and educational priorities
Programs must provide learning experiences that cannot be replicated in the classroom
Programs must emphasize experiential learning and one-on-one support services
Less than 50% of organization's budget may come from state grants (exception: Baltimore Zoo)
Must submit C-1-25 MSDE budget form signed, with all funds entered on line 214 'Community Services'
Budget totals must align between application and C-1-25 form
Must submit Fiscal Impact Statement (Appendix A)
Must submit Student Safety response (Appendix B)
Must submit GEPA Section 427 response (Appendix C)
Application must include program narrative and appendices
Compliance with COMAR 13A.05.13.00 through 13A.05.13.06
Evidence of Impact section required for new applicants only
Environmental Literacy standards alignment
Signed assurance page due July 2026
Submit interim reports and final invoices by specified deadlines
Must be registered with Maryland Secretary of State Public Registry of Charities
Submit interim progress report (C-1-25C) by January 31, 2026
Submit final reports by August 15, 2026 (C-1-25D and MFR)
Budget amendments must be requested 45 days in advance
Independent annual audit required (or internally generated financial statements until audit available)
Track students with IEP or 504 plans for disability statistics
Data collection on field trips (date, school name, school type, LEA)
Tracking of time spent on SAI-related activities for salary allocations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications open May 1, 2025. Complete the Application for Participation and submit by June 13, 2025 at 5:00 p.m. EDT. MSDE holds customer service support sessions for interested applicants to review requirements and walk through the application. MSDE review committee reviews submissions based on rubric (July); State Superintendent reviews results; State Board of Education reviews in August 2025; Governor releases draft budget bill in January; Budget subcommittees review, voted on/published around April 2026; grant period begins July 1, 2026. Contact the SAI Program Manager with questions.

structured_extraction.program_description: Student Employment Services (SES) provides a broad range of vocational rehabilitation services to students with disabilities ages 14–21 who want to participate in Pre-Employment Transition Services (Pre-ETS) activities and gain meaningful employment and a successful career. Services are individualized to each student's career goal and specific needs, helping students prepare for and find jobs in their chosen career field, earning at least minimum wage and working alongside peers without identified disabilities. Students with the most significant disabilities are served first; others may be placed on a waiting list but can still receive Pre-ETS while waiting.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Wide range of vocational rehabilitation and employment services provided at no cost to the student or family for eligible students with disabilities ages 14–21. Services are individualized to the student's career goals and disability-related needs, including: career counseling and decision making; skills and job training; disability-related skills training; post-secondary education; job search and job placement services; job coaching and supported employment services; assistive technology solutions; and Pre-Employment Transition Services (Pre-ETS). A DORS counselor helps identify funding sources and other supports.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students with disabilities ages 14–21 enrolled in secondary school, post-secondary education, or a recognized educational program, who have not yet graduated or withdrawn, and have a documented disability (IEP, 504 plan, or medical records). Also relevant to parents of eligible students, school staff, and medical providers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Vocational rehabilitation and employment preparation services individualized to each student's career goal and disability-related needs, including career counseling and decision making, skills and job training, disability-related skills training, post-secondary education, job search and job placement services, job coaching and supported employment services, assistive technology solutions, and Pre-Employment Transition Services (Pre-ETS).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through more than 20 local DORS offices throughout Maryland; services also available virtually.
requirements_list: Must be a student with a disability between ages 14 and 21
Must be enrolled in secondary school, post-secondary education, or a recognized educational program and not yet graduated or withdrawn
Must meet DORS eligibility requirements
Must provide Social Security number at intake
Must provide documentation of disability (e.g., recent medical records, IEP, or 504 Plan)
Must provide documentation confirming enrollment in school (IEP or 504 Plan)
Must have participated in Pre-ETS activities
Parental consent required for minors
Students with the most significant disabilities are served first; others may be placed on a waiting list but can still receive Pre-ETS while waiting
Specific SES eligibility criteria apply, unlike Pre-ETS which is open to all students with disabilities in that age range
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete a Request DORS Services form (available on the DORS website at dors.maryland.gov). The form can be submitted by the student, a parent, a medical provider, or school staff. After the form is received, DORS contacts the student and family by email, text, or letter and schedules an intake meeting. At the intake meeting, DORS reviews eligibility documents and may schedule assessments if needed. A letter is sent after the eligibility determination with information about next steps. Alternatively, contact a DORS counselor directly or contact a DORS community office to determine eligibility and begin services.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Summer Food Service Program (SFSP) is a federally funded, state-administered program that reimburses organizations for serving free, healthy meals to children and teens age 18 and younger in low-income or economically disadvantaged areas during summer months when school is not in session. The program combines summer activity and enrichment programs with a federal meal reimbursement program. Sites can operate the SUN Meals program (meals consumed on-site) or the SUN Meals To-Go program (multi-day meal boxes picked up by families).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participating organizations (sponsors) receive federal meal reimbursements for each free meal served to eligible children and teens age 18 and under. Sites can operate the SUN Meals program (meals consumed on-site) or the SUN Meals To-Go program (multi-day meal boxes picked up by families). Reimbursements cover the cost of providing free, nutritious meals in low-income areas during summer months.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations seeking to become SUN Meals sites and serve free meals to children and teens 18 and under in low-income or economically disadvantaged communities during the summer. Children and teens 18 and younger can receive free meals at participating sites.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reimbursement for the cost of providing free, nutritious meals to children and teens in low-income areas during summer months when school is not in session.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across all Maryland counties, targeting economically disadvantaged and low-income areas. Organizations contact their county's sponsoring organization (typically the county public school system) to apply.
requirements_list: Must be a summer food service sponsor or organization seeking to become a SUN Meals site
Must serve children and teens 18 years and younger
Sites must be located in or serve low-income or economically disadvantaged areas
Meals must meet USDA nutrition requirements and meal patterns
Organizations operate under a sponsoring organization for their county
SUN Meals To-Go sites require participant registration
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations interested in becoming a SUN Meals site should contact the sponsoring organization for their county (listed in the county contact table on the program page) to apply. Baltimore City has an online application through the Baltimore City Department of Housing; all other counties contact their county public schools office by phone. For general program information, contact the Office of School and Community Nutrition Programs.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides Deaf-Blind individuals with access to specially trained Support Service Providers (SSPs) who supply visual and environmental information, sighted guide services, and communication accessibility to help Deaf-Blind people access their community and vocational rehabilitation services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Assigns trained Support Service Providers (SSPs) to Deaf-Blind individuals. SSPs provide visual and environmental information, sighted guide services, and communication support to enable access to community and vocational rehabilitation services.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with combined vision and hearing loss (Deaf-Blind) who need assistance accessing their environment and making informed decisions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Access to community activities and vocational rehabilitation services through trained SSP support.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must have combined vision and hearing loss (Deaf-Blind)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Deaf-Blind Specialist or the Office for Blindness & Vision Services to inquire about SSP services.

structured_extraction.program_name: Supported Employment for Mental and Behavioral Health Disabilities
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides continued job support to people with mental and behavioral health disabilities after they start working. Support can include job training, supervision, and workplace adjustment help. There are two types: Evidence-Based Supported Employment (using research-proven methods to help people find jobs quickly based on their own goals) and Traditional Mental Health Supported Employment (broader support including help choosing a job goal, evaluating likelihood of success, and providing ongoing support from a provider and DORS counselor after employment begins). Participants receive ongoing support from both a trained community rehabilitation partner and a DORS counselor after starting work.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Ongoing job support services provided after a person starts working. Includes training, supervision, workplace adjustment assistance, job search support, and coordinated support from both a community rehabilitation partner and a DORS counselor. Two service tracks available: Evidence-Based Supported Employment (research-backed, goal-driven rapid job placement) and Traditional Mental Health Supported Employment (broader support including help choosing a job goal, assessing likelihood of employment success, and ongoing workplace support).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with mental and behavioral health disabilities seeking employment support
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Job placement and ongoing employment support services including job goal selection, employment readiness assessment, job search support, training, supervision, and workplace adjustment assistance
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland through DORS counselors and community rehabilitation partners
requirements_list: Must have a mental or behavioral health disability
Must be eligible for DORS services
Must be referred by or working with a DORS counselor
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact a DORS counselor to determine eligibility. If eligible, the counselor may refer you to a mental health community rehabilitation partner (CRP) to assess your qualifications for ongoing support.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Teachers of Promise program pairs promising pre-service education students from Maryland colleges and universities with veteran Teachers of the Year and other distinguished educators who serve as mentors. Students in their last year of college nominated by their schools are matched with award-winning teachers for an online mentoring partnership. The program culminates in a one-day Institute featuring keynote addresses, panel discussions, wellness workshops, and community building sessions to prepare new teachers for their careers, including content on Maryland's Blueprint for Maryland's Future initiatives.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Pre-service education students receive mentoring from veteran award-winning teachers, including online partnerships throughout the spring and summer, classroom observation opportunities, professional development at the one-day Teachers of Promise Institute (featuring panel discussions, wellness workshops, and networking), and networking that may lead to teaching job placements.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Pre-service education students in their final year at Maryland colleges and universities who plan to teach in Maryland public schools in the fall, as well as new and experienced teachers in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Mentoring, professional development, classroom observation, and support transitioning into first-year teaching positions in Maryland public schools
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Students must attend Maryland colleges and universities and plan to teach in Maryland public schools.
requirements_list: Must be a student in their last year of college or university
Must be majoring in Education
Must be nominated by a Maryland college or university (5–7 students per school)
Must intend to teach in Maryland public schools in the fall
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Students are nominated each year by their Maryland college or university. Only nominees from accredited Maryland institutions who will teach in Maryland public schools in the fall are accepted. Nominees are then matched with Maryland Teachers of the Year, Milken Educators, and other award-winning educators.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides funding to Local Education Agencies (LEAs) participating in the National School Lunch Program (NSLP) or Seamless Summer Option (SSO) during School Year 2021-2022 to take part in a USDA Team Nutrition grant project managed by the Office of School and Community Nutrition Programs. The goal is to build state capacity to create four new, high-quality, appealing standardized recipes for Maryland schools using local agricultural products, developed in partnership with chefs from Prince George's Community College's Department of Wellness, Culinary Arts, and Hospitality. Recipes will be tested and refined based on student and school nutrition staff feedback to achieve an 85% acceptance rate. Funding supports staff time for training and recipe tasting events, purchasing food and supplies for those events, and building program operator capacity through equipment, training, technical assistance, and nutrition education resources made available to school nutrition staff and teachers. Partners include Maryland SNAP-Ed, Prince George's Community College's Department of Wellness, Culinary Arts, and Hospitality, and the Maryland Department of Agriculture.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants awarded to LEAs to fund: salaries/wages for substitute school nutrition staff attending training; stipends for staff time for training outside normal work hours; food and nutrition equipment/smallware for recipe development (max 5% of total); food costs for training and tastings (max 20% of total); consumable costs for training events. USDA grant funding also supports recipe development, equipment, technical assistance, and nutrition education resources made available to school nutrition staff and teachers.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No later than 5:00 pm EST on April 22, 2022
structured_extraction.contact_name: Sara Booker, Nutrition Education and Training Coordinator
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local Education Agencies (LEAs) in Maryland participating in the National School Lunch Program (NSLP) or Seamless Summer Option (SSO) during School Year 2021-2022; school nutrition staff, students, and teachers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Salaries/wages for substitute school nutrition staff attending training; stipends for staff time for training outside normal work hours; food and nutrition equipment/smallware for recipe development; food costs for training and tastings; consumable costs for training events; contracted services; supplies and materials; equipment and furniture; grant administration and coordination.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to LEAs and eligible program operators across Maryland statewide.
requirements_list: Must be a Local Education Agency (LEA) participating in the National School Lunch Program (NSLP) or Seamless Summer Option (SSO) during School Year 2021-2022 in good standing
LEA must designate a Grant Coordinator as primary liaison
Each participating school must prepare at least one chef-designed recipe
Each participating school must host at least two student taste tests per recipe (Spring 2022 - Spring 2023)
LEA can select up to three schools to participate; if more than one school selected, at least two schools required
Goal: 85% student acceptance rate for each of four recipes
Recipes updated after first round based on feedback for second taste test
Participate in periodic virtual meetings
Manage data collection from taste testing events
Submit quarterly reports
Secure photographs, attendance records, and success stories
Menu at least one final recipe
Compliance with 1964 Civil Rights Act, CFR 34, ESEA, EDGAR, GEPA, and ADA
Compliance with Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act
ADA facility accessibility requirements
Certification of Debarment and Suspension compliance (Federal Executive Order 12549)
Establish fiscal control and fund accounting procedures per 2 CFR §200
Retain financial records for 5 years minimum
Annual financial and compliance audit if expending $750,000+ in a single fiscal year
Adherence to MSDE reporting requirements
Prior written approval for programmatic changes
Prior written approval for budget realignments of $1,000 or 15% of total expenditure (whichever is greater)
Web-based programs must comply with Section 508 of Federal Rehabilitation Act and Maryland Education Article Section 7-910
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete the Grant Application and Budget Template (available via the Maryland Accountability Reporting System or from Sara Booker). Review the Grant Information Guide for instructions, timelines, and submission requirements. Submit application materials no later than 5:00 pm EST on April 22, 2022. Questions may be emailed to the Project Director, Sara Booker, at sara.booker@maryland.gov or call 410-767-0204.

structured_extraction.program_description: Employment Networks (ENs) are public or private organizations that contract with Social Security to provide free employment support services to Social Security disability beneficiaries ages 18 through 64. Services include career planning, job leads and placement, ongoing employment support, and benefits counseling. Individual ENs may specialize in serving specific populations such as former Vocational Rehabilitation clients, Deaf/Hard of Hearing/DeafBlind individuals, or those receiving SSI/SSDI benefits.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free employment support services including career planning, job leads and placement, ongoing employment support, and benefits counseling provided through contracted Employment Networks. Individual ENs offer a range of services such as resume development, interview preparation, benefits summary and analysis, work incentives counseling, job coaching, job development and placement, career advancement planning, workplace accommodations assistance, peer support, and financial education. Services may be delivered virtually or in person depending on the EN.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Within 90 days of VR closure recommended for continuous protections (varies by EN)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Social Security disability beneficiaries ages 18 through 64, including SSI and SSDI recipients; some ENs specialize in former VR clients, Deaf/Hard of Hearing/DeafBlind individuals, or those seeking to return to work
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Employment support services including career planning, job placement, benefits counseling, work incentives guidance, workplace accommodations, and financial education
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — individual ENs may serve specific counties, regions, or the entire state. Some ENs serve multi-state areas. Anne Arundel County served by AAWDC; regional Maryland areas served by Work Opportunities Unlimited.
requirements_list: Must be a Social Security disability beneficiary (SSI or SSDI)
Must be between ages 18 and 64
Must reside in Maryland (for most ENs)
Must be currently working or interested in working
Some ENs require case closure with Maryland Vocational Rehabilitation
Some ENs require assignment of Ticket within 90 days of VR closure for continuous protections
Reliable internet access and devices needed for ENs offering virtual services
Some ENs require current earnings above $1,310 monthly or intent to earn above that threshold
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact an Employment Network directly or visit choosework.ssa.gov/findhelp for additional options. Individual ENs may require a referral from a Vocational Rehabilitation counselor, a phone inquiry, or development of an Individual Work Plan (IWP). Regional coordinators are available for some ENs.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Ticket to Work program is a Social Security Administration program that connects people with disabilities who receive Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) or Supplemental Security Income (SSI) with employment services and support. In Maryland, the Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS) within the Maryland State Department of Education serves as an Employment Network, working with participants to develop an Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE) and providing services such as training, career counseling, vocational rehabilitation, job placement, benefits counseling, and ongoing support. Locally, the Harford County Office on Mental Health also connects participants to community programs that help them find jobs, increase their income, and build independence. Participation is free and voluntary, and participants receive protection from Continuing Disability Reviews while their Ticket is 'In Use' and they meet SSA Timely Progress requirements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free and voluntary program providing individualized employment planning, training, career counseling, vocational rehabilitation, job placement, job coaching, benefits counseling/planning, and ongoing support services. Participants are connected to community programs that help them enter the workforce, increase income, and build independent lives while maintaining health insurance. Participants also receive protection from Continuing Disability Reviews as long as their Ticket is 'In Use' with DORS and they meet Social Security Administration (SSA) Timely Progress requirements.
structured_extraction.program_audience: People with disabilities aged 18-64 who receive SSDI or SSI benefits and want to enter or re-enter the workforce
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training, career counseling, vocational rehabilitation, job placement, job coaching, benefits counseling/planning, and ongoing employment support services
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to Maryland residents; local access also available through the Harford County Office on Mental Health
requirements_list: Must be between 18 and 64 years old
Must receive Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) or Supplemental Security Income (SSI)
Must have a Ticket to Work issued by the Social Security Administration
Must want to become employed
Must sign an Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE) with DORS to make Ticket 'In Use'
Ticket must not already be assigned to another Employment Network (or must be unassigned)
Must reply to letters from Social Security
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact DORS to get started. DORS will work with SSA to confirm your Ticket is available. You and your DORS counselor will then develop and sign an Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE) outlining the services and goals for your path to employment, which places your Ticket 'In Use.' No paper Ticket is required to begin services. Harford County residents may also contact the Harford County Office on Mental Health to be connected to a community program that can help them find work.

structured_extraction.program_name: Training & Technical Assistance – Office of School and Community Nutrition Programs (OSCNP)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Office of School and Community Nutrition Programs (OSCNP) provides training and technical assistance to schools and participating community agencies to help them understand and meet nutritional standards and guidelines set by the USDA. Training covers programs such as the National School Lunch Program, School Breakfast Program, Child and Adult Care Food Program, and Summer Food Service Program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Ongoing training and technical assistance including required annual and twice-annual administrative meetings, monthly one-day orientation sessions, food safety training (ServSafe), and access to online training resources. No cost information specified.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public school systems, residential child care institutions, nonprofit private schools, child care centers, adult day care centers, family child care sponsors, at-risk afterschool programs, and summer food service program agencies participating in federally funded Child Nutrition Programs in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and technical assistance to ensure compliance with USDA nutritional standards and guidelines, professional development, and food safety certification.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to agencies participating in federally funded Child Nutrition Programs.
requirements_list: Must participate in a federally funded Child Nutrition Program (e.g., NSLP, SBP, CACFP, or SFSP)
Attendance at certain administrative meetings is required for public school systems, RCCIs, NPPSs, and CACFP-participating agencies
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact OSCNP at 410-767-0199 for dates and locations of trainings.

structured_extraction.program_name: USDA Department of Defense (DOD) Fresh Fruit and Vegetable Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The USDA DOD Fresh Fruit and Vegetable Program allows Maryland schools to receive weekly deliveries of fresh fruits and vegetables by directing all or part of their USDA Foods funds to the program. Schools choose products from a Maryland-based produce company, with an emphasis on locally available items. Additionally, through the broader Fresh Fruit and Vegetable Program (FFVP), eligible Maryland elementary schools receive funding to provide free fresh fruits and vegetables to students during the school day, outside of regular meal programs. The program introduces children to new and different varieties of fresh produce and promotes nutrition education to encourage healthier eating habits. It is currently active at 196 elementary schools across Maryland. Eligible organizations include schools and residential child care institutions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Schools can allocate all or a portion of their USDA Foods funds toward weekly deliveries of fresh fruits and vegetables, sourced from a Maryland-based produce company with an emphasis on locally available products. Eligible elementary schools also receive funding (direct payments) to provide free fresh fruits and vegetables to students during the school day outside of regular meal programs. The program is currently active at 196 elementary schools across Maryland.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland schools and residential child care institutions participating in the USDA Foods program, including eligible elementary schools serving children who benefit from increased access to fresh produce and nutrition education.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and distribute fresh fruits and vegetables delivered weekly from a Maryland-based produce company; fund free fresh fruit and vegetable distribution to students during the school day outside regular meal programs; support nutrition education about the fruits and vegetables served.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to eligible schools statewide in Maryland; the FFVP component is currently active at 196 elementary schools across the state.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland school with allocated USDA Foods funds
Must be a public elementary school in Maryland to participate in the FFVP component
School must meet eligibility criteria for the FFVP
Must meet USDA nutrition guidelines and standards
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Schools order their choice of fresh fruits and vegetables to be delivered weekly from a Maryland-based produce company. Schools interested in the Fresh Fruit and Vegetable Program component should contact the Maryland State Department of Education Office of School and Community Nutrition Programs. Applications are accepted annually. View the USDA Fresh Fruit and Vegetable Program Fact Sheet for additional details.

structured_extraction.program_description: The USDA Foods in Schools program supports Maryland schools by purchasing 100% domestically grown and produced food products for use in school meal programs, primarily the National School Lunch Program, at no direct cost to schools. The program reduces overall food expenses by an average of 20% and supports both school nutrition and domestic agriculture. Maryland schools can choose from over 200 options including fruits, vegetables, grains, poultry, dairy, and meat products to incorporate into their school menus. Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP) sponsors receive cash-in-lieu of USDA Foods with their CACFP meal reimbursements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Schools receive USDA-purchased, 100% American-grown and -produced food products at no direct cost, reducing food expenses by an average of 20%. Schools select from a catalog of over 200 domestically grown choices including fruits, vegetables, grains, poultry, dairy, and meat products to incorporate into school meal preparation and menus. Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP) sponsors receive cash-in-lieu of USDA Foods with their CACFP meal reimbursements.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland public schools, school districts, and Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP) sponsors participating in federal child nutrition programs including the National School Lunch Program
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Food products (fruits, vegetables, grains, poultry, dairy, and meat) to incorporate into school meal preparation and menus
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to schools and school districts throughout Maryland statewide
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland school or school district participating in a federal child nutrition program such as the National School Lunch Program
CACFP sponsors receive cash-in-lieu of USDA Foods with meal reimbursements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Schools select food products from a catalog of over 200 domestically grown choices to incorporate into their menus. Contact the Office of School and Community Nutrition Programs at (410) 767-0199 or scnp_mailbox.msde@maryland.gov to determine eligibility and participation requirements.

structured_extraction.program_name: Ulysses Currie Head Start State Supplemental Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides supplemental state funding to Head Start and Early Head Start programs to increase access to high-quality early care and education services. Funds can be used to expand hours of service, add summer programming, and support quality improvement measures such as professional development, program improvement, and salary enhancement. Aims to enhance school readiness outcomes and support evidence-based practices.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State supplemental grant funding provided to eligible Head Start and Early Head Start programs to expand hours of service, add summer programming, and support school readiness, evidence-based practices, program improvement, and salary enhancement.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: August 22, 2023, no later than 5:00 pm EST
structured_extraction.program_audience: Existing Head Start and Early Head Start program operators seeking to expand services or improve quality, serving eligible children and families in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Expanding hours of service, adding summer programming, school readiness support, evidence-based and research-based practices, activities reinforcing and complementing the regular program year, professional learning and development, program improvement, and salary enhancement
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to eligible Head Start and Early Head Start programs operating within Maryland jurisdictions
requirements_list: Application must be submitted as a single PDF document with original signatures
Must be submitted via email by 5:00 pm EST on August 22, 2023
Must be a current federal Head Start or Early Head Start grantee or delegate in compliance status
Participation in Maryland EXCELS program required
Programs not at Maryland EXCELS level 5 must include a goal to advance at least one level
Submit evaluation reports annually and quarterly progress reports
Provide evidence of Maryland EXCELS rating level
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Head Start Grant Application and submit it as a single PDF with original signatures via email to the program contact by the deadline. MSDE held three customer service support sessions in June and July 2023 to help applicants understand the process.

structured_extraction.program_description: VCAMP is a virtual mentoring and support program for DORS consumers on the autism spectrum who are attending college but not enrolled in the Pathways program. It helps students navigate college and develop self-advocacy, social skills, time management, and organizational skills needed to succeed in a college environment. Available when in-person DORS Pathways program is not available.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Remote (virtual) mentoring and support delivered through weekly online sessions with DORS Autism Services staff and weekly VCAMP online group sessions. Instruction covers college transition, time management, organizational skills, self-advocacy, social skills, and grooming/hygiene. Available to students at in-state or out-of-state two- or four-year colleges where in-person DORS Pathways is unavailable.
structured_extraction.program_audience: DORS consumers on the autism spectrum attending two- or four-year colleges (in-state or out-of-state) who are not participating in the Pathways program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Virtual mentoring to support college transition, self-advocacy, social skill development, time management, organizational skills, and grooming/hygiene.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available remotely to students attending Maryland or out-of-state colleges where in-person DORS Pathways is unavailable.
requirements_list: Be a DORS participant on the Autism spectrum
Have an approved Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE) that includes college
Work towards an industry-recognized college degree or certification from a two-year or four-year college where in-person DORS Pathways is unavailable
Attend weekly online sessions with DORS Autism Services staff
Attend weekly VCAMP online group sessions
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your DORS Counselor or local DORS office to request services and learn about enrollment in the program.

structured_extraction.program_name: Virtual Self-Advocacy Support Group for Pre-ETS and Transitioning Youth
structured_extraction.program_description: A virtual support group that helps young people who are blind or have low vision develop self-advocacy skills to overcome everyday life challenges. Participants also connect with peers of similar age.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 10-week virtual group offered four times per year via Google Meet. Sessions meet once per week for one hour. Maximum of six participants per group. The facilitator offers additional individualized sessions after each 10-week session as needed.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Pre-ETS (Pre-Employment Transition Services) and transitioning youth who are blind or have low vision
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Self-advocacy skill development and peer engagement for youth with visual impairments
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Offered virtually statewide via Google Meet
requirements_list: Must be blind or have low vision
Must be a Pre-ETS or transitioning youth DORS consumer
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact WTC or a local DORS office to request participation in the virtual group.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides behavioral health and health support services to DORS (Division of Rehabilitation Services) consumers with mental health disabilities who have been referred by their DORS counselors. Services support a healthy recovery lifestyle as consumers work toward employment and self-sufficiency. Services include addiction assessments, behavioral health screening, counseling, consultation, and education, as well as health services related to diabetes management and general health education. Services can be delivered in person at a local DORS office, at the Workforce and Technology Center (WTC), or virtually.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Services are provided in person at a local DORS office, at the Workforce and Technology Center (WTC) campus in Baltimore, or virtually. Services include addictions assessment and drug testing, behavioral health screening for addictions and co-occurring disorders, behavioral health counseling (coping strategies, general support, referrals), behavioral health consultation (case history review, written reports), behavioral health education (stress management, work-life balance, employment drug testing), diabetic assessments, diabetic education, diabetic follow-up, health consultation, and general health education (hygiene, sleep, medication management). Supports recovery and helps consumers move toward employment and self-sufficiency.
structured_extraction.program_audience: DORS consumers with mental health disabilities who have been referred by their DORS counselors and are working toward employment and self-sufficiency while maintaining a healthy recovery lifestyle. Also includes individuals in recovery from substance use disorders and consumers with diabetes or other health concerns.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Behavioral health counseling, addiction assessment, health education, diabetes management support, and general health services to help consumers achieve employment and self-sufficiency goals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland through local DORS offices, the Workforce and Technology Center campus in Baltimore, or virtually.
requirements_list: Must be a current DORS consumer
Must have a mental health disability
Must be referred by a DORS counselor
Must demonstrate a commitment to the recovery process
No pre-determined abstinence timeframe required
Consumers experiencing withdrawal symptoms or moderate-to-severe substance use will be assessed for readiness and may receive a referral for treatment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your DORS counselor or local DORS office for a referral. Services can also be requested via QR code. If you are already working with DORS, contact Michele Pinto, RN, at 410-554-9326 or Michele.Pinto@maryland.gov for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: WTC Deaf and Hard-of-Hearing Employment Services
structured_extraction.program_description: Partners with job seekers who are Deaf or hard of hearing to help them prepare for, find, and keep stable employment. Staff fluent in American Sign Language (ASL) provide individualized support including resume help, job search skills, interview practice, job coaching, and coordination of interpreting services. Encourages job seekers towards self-advocacy and independence.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Staff provide individualized program planning, team management, coordination of ASL interpreting services (including video remote interpreting), resume building, cover letter writing, job seeking skills training, interview practice, job application support, job development, job coaching, and support at job interviews, orientations, and on-the-job training. Also includes ASL interpreting services for Driver Education for eligible consumers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Deaf and hard-of-hearing job seekers who use ASL as their primary communication and are participating in DORS programs
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Employment support services including job search, resume assistance, interpreting coordination, and on-the-job coaching
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Services offered in-person at the Workforce and Technology Center, in the community, and virtually throughout Maryland
requirements_list: Must be deaf or hard-of-hearing
Must use ASL as primary communication
Must be a DORS consumer participating in WTC programs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your DORS Counselor or local DORS office to request services. You may also contact WTC Deaf Services Coordinator Penelope Shook for more information, or request DORS services via the QR code on program materials.

structured_extraction.program_description: A 10-week retail training program for people with disabilities, offered through a partnership between DORS' Workforce and Technology Center (WTC), CVS Health, and Maryland community colleges. The program combines classroom instruction in a mock CVS store, hands-on learning at real CVS store locations, and a paid externship at CVS stores. Participants receive four weeks of classroom and mock store training at the Workforce and Technology Center, followed by six weeks of in-store work experience at Baltimore-area CVS Pharmacy stores. Training covers customer service, inventory management, cash register skills, phone etiquette, and non-verbal communication, preparing participants for competitive integrated employment in retail settings. The program is designed to run three times per calendar year, serving up to 24 individuals per year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A 10-week program combining four weeks of classroom and mock store training at the DORS Workforce and Technology Center with six weeks of in-store work experience at Baltimore-area CVS Pharmacy locations. CVS Health donated shelving, products, curriculum, training materials, and staff training. Training covers customer service, inventory management, cash register skills, phone etiquette, stock rotation, and non-verbal communication. The program runs three times per calendar year, serving up to 24 individuals per year, and includes a paid externship component at CVS stores.
structured_extraction.program_audience: People with disabilities (at least 16 years old) seeking competitive integrated employment in retail settings
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Retail job skills training and work experience, including classroom instruction, mock store practice, and paid in-store externship experience to prepare participants for employment in CVS Pharmacy stores or similar retail environments
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore-area CVS Pharmacy stores; classroom and mock store training conducted at DORS' Workforce and Technology Center in Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a person with a disability
Must be a vocational rehabilitation (VR) consumer through DORS
Must be at least 16 years old
High school diploma preferred but not required
Must have a desire to work in retail
Must have a 6th-grade reading level
Must have basic math skills and ability to use a calculator
Must be able to follow simple written and oral instructions
Must be able to lift 25 to 50 pounds and bend, stoop, and stand for long periods of time
COVID-19 vaccination is required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact a DORS Counselor or local DORS office to request services and inquire about enrollment in the next available training cohort. Services can also be requested via QR code. The program is offered at the DORS WTC location and select Baltimore-area CVS Pharmacy locations.

structured_extraction.program_description: DORS reimburses employers for wages paid during on-the-job training of individuals with disabilities, helping businesses offset the cost of training new employees.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Employers receive wage reimbursement to offset the cost of training new employees with disabilities through on-the-job training programs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland businesses and employers who hire and train individuals with disabilities; job seekers with disabilities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reimbursement of wages paid to employees with disabilities during on-the-job training
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland through local DORS Business Relations Representatives
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local DORS Business Relations Representative or the DORS Business Relations Team for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A two-part training program that helps individuals with disabilities who have little or no work experience — or who have been out of the workforce for an extended time — prepare for competitive employment. The program combines classroom sessions and community-based activities to build workplace skills. Courses are offered at the DORS Workforce & Technology Center (WTC) campus in Baltimore and can be taken together or separately.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two six-week courses (Work Readiness 1 and Work Readiness 2) that can be taken together or separately. Work Readiness 1 covers career exploration, soft skills development, financial management, organizational skills, self-determination and self-awareness, interpersonal skills and teamwork, workplace preparation and communication, and job retention through videos, lectures, guest speakers, worksite tours, and job shadowing. Work Readiness 2 focuses on soft skills and real-world work experience at community worksites, covering customer service, workplace ethics, conflict management, resume writing, mock interviews, and managing your online footprint, including guest speakers, job shadowing, and volunteer work experiences.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students and job seekers with disabilities who have little or no work experience or who have been out of the workforce for an extended period
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Workforce readiness training including soft skills development, career exploration, financial management, organizational skills, self-determination, interpersonal skills, and real-world work experience at community worksites
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland residents; courses held at the DORS Workforce & Technology Center (WTC) campus in Baltimore
requirements_list: Work Readiness 1: Must be able to function in a classroom setting
Work Readiness 1: Must be able to fully participate in all individual and group activities
Work Readiness 2: Must have the capability and desire to participate in competitive employment
Work Readiness 2: Must be able to spend half of each day volunteering at a community worksite with drop-in support only
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact a DORS Counselor or local DORS office for more information or to request services.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS) Workforce & Technology Center (WTC) provides vocational rehabilitation services to help people with disabilities prepare for and find employment. CARF-accredited program offering academic tutoring and GED preparation, behavioral health services, career training programs, apprenticeship services, autism services, services for deaf and hard-of-hearing individuals, counseling and case management, employment services, rehabilitation technology, work readiness programs, and residential dormitory accommodations. Services are available on the WTC campus in northeast Baltimore at 2301 Argonne Drive, in the community, and virtually.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free vocational rehabilitation services for eligible DORS consumers, including academic services, apprenticeship services, autism services, behavioral health services, career and technology training, counseling and case management, deaf and hard of hearing employment services, employment services, enrichment services, office for blindness and vision services, rehabilitation technology services, work readiness programs, and residential dormitory accommodations with meals, medication support, and laundry facilities. Services are available on-campus, in the community, and virtually.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Active DORS consumers — individuals with disabilities seeking vocational rehabilitation, employment, and career readiness services, including individuals who are deaf or hard of hearing, blind, on the autism spectrum, or in need of behavioral health services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Career training, academic tutoring and GED preparation, apprenticeship services, employment services, rehabilitation technology, behavioral health support, work readiness programs, counseling and case management, enrichment activities, and residential housing and daily living support services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Services available statewide in Maryland — at the WTC campus located at 2301 Argonne Drive, Baltimore, MD 21218, in the community, and virtually. Maryland residents are eligible.
requirements_list: Must be an active DORS (Maryland Division of Rehabilitation Services) consumer
Must have a disability
Must have an approved rehabilitation plan with a DORS field counselor
Must comply with WTC rules and conduct expectations
Must maintain appropriate attendance and punctuality
Must dress according to program requirements and display ID badge while on campus
Must complete assigned tasks and maintain professional behavior
Must attend medical/therapy appointments and comply with medication requirements
Prohibited: alcohol, illegal drugs, marijuana (any form including medical marijuana without prior disclosure and approval), weapons, theft, and gambling on campus
WTC campus is drug, alcohol, tobacco, smoke, and vape-free
Residential consumers must comply with 11:00 p.m. curfew and nightly room checks
Residential consumers must shower by 10:45 p.m.
Residential consumers must return home on weekends (depart by 4:30 p.m. Friday, return after 4:30 p.m. Sunday)
Residential consumers must follow dormitory rules including laundry, room cleanliness, and sign-out procedures
Room cleaning mandatory every Wednesday evening
Children must be supervised by family members
Day users cannot return for evening residential visits
All visitors must register and wear visitor badges in main lobby
Visitors must remain in main enrichment room; cannot access residential areas
No sexual activity on WTC grounds
Service animals allowed with restrictions; no emotional support animals (service animals only per ADA)
Documentation required for appointments outside WTC
Participation in service plan development required
Locked doors when leaving room
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your DORS counselor to access services and develop an individualized rehabilitation plan. To visit the WTC campus, reservations are required for tours (general public and schools). Call 410-554-9108 or 1-888-200-7117, or email wtc.dors@maryland.gov. Consumers work with a center counselor/case manager; a formal complaint process is available through the Risk Manager. Admission packet provided; orientation required for residential services. ID badge issued on admission day.

structured_extraction.program_description: Worksite Services provides assistive technology assessments and training to people who need technological help to perform essential job functions due to a disability. Rehabilitation Technologists and Occupational Therapists work with individuals and their employers to identify technology-based solutions, such as magnification software, communication devices, adaptive keyboards, and ergonomic workstation equipment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Assistive technology assessments and training are provided by Rehabilitation Technologists and Occupational Therapists. Services include evaluation and implementation of accommodations such as magnification and screen reading software, communication and assistive listening devices, physical access equipment, sit-stand workstations, adaptive keyboards and mice, and note-taking tools.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with disabilities who are experiencing difficulty performing their job duties due to disability-related limitations and are referred by a DORS Counselor.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Assistive technology assessments and workplace accommodations to help individuals with disabilities perform essential job functions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through the Maryland Department of Rehabilitation Services.
requirements_list: Individual must have disability-related limitations affecting job performance
Must be referred by a DORS Counselor
A detailed description of the difficulties experienced must be provided
Position description is required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individuals must be referred for Worksite Services by their DORS Counselor. A detailed description of the job difficulties and a position description are required to initiate services.

structured_extraction.program_description: A class provided by Occupational Therapists covering ergonomic principles, proper workstation setup, good sitting posture, position changes, workstation exercises, and low-tech ergonomic solutions. Available to Computer Skills Development students and others on an individual basis.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A class teaching ergonomic workstation setup and healthy computer use habits to promote optimal health and long-term employment for computer-based workers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: DORS consumers in the Computer Skills Development training program and other job seekers or employed individuals who work at a computer workstation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training on ergonomics and workstation comfort to support long-term employment health.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available through DORS's Work Technology Center (WTC) and on an individual basis.
requirements_list: Must be a DORS consumer
Enrolled in Computer Skills Development program or referred individually
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Automatically included for Computer Skills Development students; others should contact DORS to request the class.

structured_extraction.program_name: Independent Living (IL) Services through Centers for Independent Living
structured_extraction.program_description: Independent living services are provided through Maryland's Centers for Independent Living for individuals with disabilities who want to be more independent at home and in the community, but whose goal is not employment. Services help people with disabilities gain greater independence in daily life and are available to those who are not eligible for the ILOB program. The program also includes the Independent Living Older Blind (ILOB) Program, which helps individuals age 55 or older who are blind or have a vision impairment live independently.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education, Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Independent living services provided through Centers for Independent Living to help individuals with disabilities become more independent at home and in the community. Services include technical assistance, direct support, and access to information. The ILOB program provides specialized services for individuals 55 or older who are blind or have a vision impairment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with disabilities whose goal is increased independence at home and in the community rather than employment, and who are not eligible for the ILOB program. A specific program (ILOB) is also available for blind or vision-impaired individuals who are 55 or older.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services to support independent living at home and in the community, including access to Centers for Independent Living and specialized support for older blind individuals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must have a disability
Goal must be independent living, not employment
Must not be eligible for the ILOB program
For the Independent Living Older Blind Program (ILOB), applicant must be 55 or older and blind or have a vision impairment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Maryland Statewide Independent Living Council (MSILC) for more information about available Centers for Independent Living, or find a local Center through the MSILC website.

structured_extraction.program_description: The ARR Challenge helps Maryland's rural and agricultural businesses recover from the economic impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic. It funds technology-driven projects that help businesses recover, rebuild, or pivot, and encourages collaboration between rural businesses, research institutions, and industry partners.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $200,000 per project for a one-year period. Disbursed in two tranches: 50% at closing and 50% upon completion of a mid-term activity report. A five-year quarterly reporting requirement follows the award. Funds technology-empowered initiatives helping rural and agricultural businesses recover, rebuild, or pivot.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland rural and agricultural businesses with fewer than 100 employees impacted by COVID-19, as well as research institutions and industry partners collaborating with those businesses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Development of innovative products or novel applications of existing technology to help rural or agricultural businesses recover or pivot from the COVID-19 economic crisis.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to rural and agricultural businesses located in Maryland, excluding Baltimore County, Baltimore City, Howard County, Anne Arundel County, Prince George's County, and Montgomery County. Rural areas as defined in State Finance and Procurement Article §2-207, Annotated Code of Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a rural or agricultural business in Maryland
Must be a Maryland Qualified Business in good standing with the MD Department of Assessments & Taxation
Must have fewer than 100 workforce members
Must have been detrimentally impacted by COVID-19 and associated economic downturn
Project must be technology-empowered
Collaboration with research institutions or industry partners encouraged
Excludes retail sales, real estate development, insurance, banking, lending, and professional services (accountants, attorneys, physicians)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are now closed. Previously, applicants could review the Request for Applications (RFA) for eligibility requirements, funding structure, and review criteria, then submit through TEDCO.

structured_extraction.program_name: Amazon Web Services AI Pitch Competition-In Person
structured_extraction.program_description: A curated AI pitch competition where selected organizations present AI challenges or concepts to a panel of AWS industry experts. Participants receive real-time feedback and can win up to $50,000 in AWS and PREDICTif services to help develop their AI initiatives, from early-stage ideas to fully formed projects.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $50,000 in AWS cloud services and PREDICTif services awarded to winning teams. Up to 10 finalists compete for these prizes. Free to attend with required registration (limited to 110 attendees).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations and innovators working on AI initiatives, from early-stage ideas to fully developed AI projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: AWS cloud computing services and PREDICTif technical services to support AI development.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland
requirements_list: Must register to attend or pitch
Selected/handpicked participants present to judges
Up to 10 finalists compete
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register for the event and apply to pitch via the Maryland SBDC Corridor Region pitch competition page (https://www.marylandsbdc.org/locations/corridor-region/pitch-competition).

structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore Innovation Initiative (BII) Pilot Program supports an equitable innovation and entrepreneurial ecosystem at higher education institutions in the Baltimore-Columbia-Towson Metropolitan Statistical Area (MSA). It helps advance technology toward commercialization of products or services and supports entrepreneurs developing technology-based ventures. BII is part of Maryland's matching contribution toward the Baltimore Tech Hub.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two grant tracks are available: (1) Technology Advancement grants of up to $50,000 for faculty, students, or student principal investigators to advance commercialization of technology; joint applications from two or more qualifying universities may receive up to $75,000. Technology-based startups collaborating with faculty, students, or staff at BII-participating institutions may also apply. Duration up to 9 months. (2) Entrepreneurship Commercialization, Programming, and Infrastructure grants of up to $50,000 for staff or faculty running entrepreneurship or commercialization programs at an eligible institution. Duration up to 12 months.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Faculty, students, student principal investigators, and staff at eligible higher education institutions in the Baltimore-Columbia-Towson MSA, as well as technology-based startups collaborating with those institutions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Technology commercialization, startup creation, entrepreneurship program development, and commercialization infrastructure enhancement at eligible institutions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Open only to eligible institutions located within the Baltimore-Columbia-Towson Metropolitan Statistical Area (MSA).
requirements_list: Institution must be in the eligible institution list for the Baltimore-Columbia-Towson MSA
Institution must formally opt in to participate as a collaborator in BII
Only collaborating organizations may submit project proposals
Applicants must engage with an onsite Project Lead at least 30 days before application submission
Application must include a current, dated letter of approval signed by the onsite Project Lead
Project proposals must either advance technology commercialization and support startup creation, or foster entrepreneurship development at the eligible university
Full-time faculty at MII-Qualifying Universities are not eligible to serve as lead applicants for a BII Technology Advancement Grant
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Read the BII Request for Applications (RFA). 2. Verify eligibility and select the appropriate grant track. 3. Meet with your institution's onsite Project Lead. 4. Submit an Indication of Interest (IOI) form within 15 days of meeting with the onsite Project Lead. 5. BII staff review the IOI for eligibility (allow up to two weeks). 6. If approved, receive an invitation and link to submit a full application. 7. Obtain a Letter of Approval from the onsite Project Lead at least 30 days before submitting the full application. 8. Submit the full application by the deadline.

structured_extraction.program_description: BioHealth Innovation, Inc. (BHI), in partnership with Montgomery County, Maryland, places experienced professionals (Executives-in-Residence) to provide business counseling and technical assistance to life sciences, digital health, and medical device startups and growth-stage companies in Montgomery County. The program supports technology commercialization and market entry for local biohealth entrepreneurs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One or more Executives-in-Residence provide business counseling, technical assistance, customer discovery support, regulatory planning, market assessment, non-dilutive funding guidance, and access to specialized experts and attorneys. Services include pre-scheduled advising/office hours at incubators, accelerators, shared labs, and universities; company preparation for pitch competitions; subject matter expert presentations; and pipeline development for managers and executives. The total contract amount for all contractors does not exceed $135,000. This is a contract position (6–12 months) without benefits.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Not specified; contract ideally beginning last quarter of 2022
structured_extraction.contact_name: Sarah Miller, Vice President of Economic Development
structured_extraction.program_audience: Seasoned professionals (Executives-in-Residence) passionate about technology commercialization, and Montgomery County biohealth startups and growth-stage companies in diagnostics, medical devices, digital health, bioinformatics, AI/machine learning, and therapeutics. Entrepreneurs of color, women and non-binary founders, and LGBTQ+ community members are encouraged to apply.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business counseling and technical assistance for Montgomery County biohealth startups, including technology validation, customer discovery, regulatory planning, market assessment, non-dilutive funding assistance, pitch competition preparation, and ecosystem-building activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland only.
requirements_list: Startup experience required for Executive-in-Residence applicants
Direct investing and/or fundraising experience preferred
Relevant experience in diagnostics, digital health, therapeutics, medical devices, bioinformatics, or bioengineering
Must provide a letter of interest, proposed start/end dates, billable hours, and hourly/monthly rate
Must provide reference contacts for business or founder mentoring and coaching
Must submit a resume/CV demonstrating significant business-building experience
Contractor must maintain and submit a monthly log of all business development counseling and technical assistance appointments
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a letter of interest, proposed start/end dates, number of billable hours per month, hourly/monthly rate, reference contacts, and a resume/CV to Sarah Miller, VP of Economic Development at BHI, via email at smiller@biohealthinnovation.org.

structured_extraction.program_name: Business Resource Information, Development, and Guidance Ecosystem (BRIDGE) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: TEDCO's Business Resource Information, Development, and Guidance Ecosystem (BRIDGE) Program provides legal, accounting, and financial advisory services to businesses owned by Socially and Economically Disadvantaged Individuals (SEDI) and Very Small Businesses (VSBs) across the Mid-Atlantic region. The program offers resources and support services to help SEDI-owned businesses and very small businesses succeed.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Legal, accounting, and financial advisory services provided to SEDI-owned businesses and Very Small Businesses (VSBs), along with broader business resources and support services.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Socially and Economically Disadvantaged Individuals (SEDI) and Very Small Businesses (VSBs) in the Mid-Atlantic region.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Legal, accounting, and financial advisory services; general business resources and support services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Mid-Atlantic region.
requirements_list: Must be a Socially and Economically Disadvantaged Individual (SEDI) or a very small business
Business must be owned by a Socially and Economically Disadvantaged Individual (SEDI) or qualify as a Very Small Business (VSB)

structured_extraction.program_description: Coalition of the Willing is a program related to TEDCO's Cultivate Maryland fund. The page provides minimal detail about the program's purpose or structure.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: No assistance details are provided on this page. The program is associated with TEDCO's Cultivate Maryland fund.

structured_extraction.program_description: Concept Capital is TEDCO's initiative to bridge the early-stage funding gap for underrepresented entrepreneurs across Maryland. The program provides flexible convertible note funding and specialized support services to founders who are socially and economically disadvantaged, disabled, female, minority, or rural-based, helping them prepare for future venture opportunities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Convertible notes ranging from $25,000 to $50,000 with zero interest, zero discount, and negotiable valuation caps. Recipients may also access one-on-one mentoring and advisory services, advanced software for performance tracking and investment-readiness, and tailored guidance to achieve critical venture milestones.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Graham Dodge, Karen Zuccardi, Justin Ferguson, Sephora Saint-Armand
structured_extraction.program_audience: Underrepresented entrepreneurs in Maryland, including socially and economically disadvantaged individuals (SEDI), minority, disabled, and female founders, as well as founders located in rural communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Early-stage business development for technology-driven companies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Business must have its principal office in Maryland with 51% or more of its workforce in-state. Founder or business must be located in a rural or disadvantaged community, or the founder must be a socially and economically disadvantaged individual.
requirements_list: Maryland-based business with principal office in Maryland and 51%+ workforce in-state
Technology-driven business (non-retail focus)
Founded within the last 7 years
Founder or business located in a rural or disadvantaged community, or founder is a socially and economically disadvantaged individual (SEDI), including minority, disabled, or female founders
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are currently closed and will reopen in 2027. Apply through TEDCO's MyTEDCO portal when open.

structured_extraction.program_description: TEDCO's Equal Access Initiative is a diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) strategy that ensures all entrepreneurial communities in Maryland have access to TEDCO's programs, funding, and resources. It includes the Diversity Rider (a commitment to build diverse investor bases in deals TEDCO leads), Social Impact Funds, and the Urban Business Innovation Initiative (UBII), along with data collection through TEDCO Registration to track and improve equitable access across the organization.
