TEDCO measures and tracks DEI metrics across investment programs, collecting demographic data from founders and C-level executives to assess who TEDCO is serving and adjust strategies accordingly.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: TEDCO commits to including a Diversity Rider in all deals it leads, using best efforts to identify diverse co-investors and offer investment opportunities to underrepresented communities. The initiative also supports tech startup founders through Social Impact Funds (including the Builder Fund and Inclusion Fund), Seed Funds, MVF, and the Urban Business Innovation Initiative (UBII). Tracks investment approvals and demographic data for underrepresented founders and executives across multiple investment funds.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Tech startup founders and C-level executives, especially those from underrepresented and diverse communities in Maryland, including underrepresented racial/ethnic groups, women-led/founded companies, disabled founders, veterans, and rural entrepreneurs
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Early-stage investment capital and support for technology startup founders from underrepresented communities
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland
requirements_list: Company must register with TEDCO annually to access resources and funding
Must be a technology startup
Self-identification of demographic data (founders/C-level executives) required
Optional 'choose not to disclose' option available for demographic data
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Annual registration process through TEDCO Registration with demographic data collection. Data collected is used to understand community access and plan programs. DEI impact tracking launched 7/1/22.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Equitech Growth Fund (EGF) is an initiative under Cultivate Maryland managed by TEDCO's Venture Development division. It provides grants for infrastructure and workforce development initiatives that support Maryland's economic competitiveness, foster economic opportunity for all, and accelerate growth of emerging and advanced industries. The goal is to position Maryland as a top-ten fastest growing innovation state by 2040, while attracting and retaining businesses and encouraging participation from underrepresented communities. An informational webinar is scheduled for June 11, 2026 from 11:00 AM to 12:00 PM for prospective applicants.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Infrastructure Awards of up to $1 million per project with durations of 12–36 months (estimated $3 million total annual funding; 1–3 awards expected), and Workforce Development Awards of up to $250,000 per project with durations of 12–24 months. Priority areas include entrepreneurship development, STEM education, advanced manufacturing (bio-manufacturing, aerospace and defense, prototyping, 3D printing, semiconductors, microelectronics, robotics), cybersecurity and IT workforce development, advanced technology (quantum computing, computational biology, environment sensing, 5G/next-gen telecommunications), AR/VR learning, and advanced laboratory space. Additional consideration areas include environmental and energy technology, aerospace and defense, smart agriculture and food technology, healthcare and life sciences, bioinformatics, autonomous systems and robotics, FinTech, creative industries and digital media, and logistics and supply chain innovation. Workforce funds may not be used for scholarships or salary increases. AI technology or SaaS platform development may be funded if aligned with program goals.

Recipients also receive executive support from TEDCO as a condition of the investment. Eligible companies must be corporations or limited liability companies (not sole proprietorships) and must have received less than $15,000,000 in dilutive funding and have fewer than 251 employees. The platform helps users manage the full lifecycle of IP processes including searching, drafting, and prosecution of patents, using AI and machine learning tools. It enables startups to streamline IP processes, reduce risks, and enhance the value of their intellectual property, providing a strong foundation for future business growth. IPGen also provides up to two hours of hands-on practical support and 30 minutes of onboarding assistance per user.

structured_extraction.program_description: The DefTech Center is a joint initiative between TEDCO, the Maryland Department of Commerce, and the U.S. Department of Defense (DoD) that helps entrepreneurs, technology companies, and DoD lab personnel commercialize defense technologies developed at Department of Defense laboratories in Maryland. It connects Maryland businesses to federal labs for product development, testing, IP licensing, and commercialization. Member companies and clients receive professional services including DefTech Academy and Certification courses on technology transfer and government contracting, pre-lab engagement training, access to monthly federal funding notices, private meetings with DoD federal labs, monthly virtual office hours with DefTech Advisors, networking with lab staff and service providers, education on IP/patent law and customer discovery, and one-on-one mentoring for those seeking to license technology from DoD labs in Maryland. Monthly virtual office hours sessions are also available for businesses to learn how DefTech can support them by leveraging cutting-edge technology, facilities, equipment, and expertise found in Maryland DoD Labs. Program costs are waived for the initial 30 companies in the first program year due to DoD, Maryland Department of Commerce, and TEDCO funding.

Free monthly virtual office hours sessions are also available providing guidance on how businesses can access DoD lab resources including technology, facilities, equipment, and expertise. Core services include: navigating the Technology Transfer (T2) process with federal research laboratories, connecting with T2 staff, scientists, engineers, and service providers, market-oriented product development guidance, IP and patent law education, customer discovery, and one-on-one technical assistance for licensing, IP identification, market analysis, and commercialization planning. Program costs are waived for the initial 30 companies in the first program year due to DoD, Maryland Department of Commerce, and TEDCO funding.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Innovation Initiative (MII) Funding – Technology Validation, Market Assessment & Company Formation
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Innovation Initiative (MII), administered by TEDCO in partnership with qualifying Maryland universities, helps move promising technologies from university research labs into the commercial marketplace. It funds technology validation, market assessment, and the creation of Maryland-based startup companies built on research from qualifying universities. Participating universities include Johns Hopkins University, Morgan State University, University of Maryland Baltimore, University of Maryland Baltimore County, University of Maryland College Park, Frostburg State University, and Bowie State University. The program provides two phases of funding: (1) Technology Assessment — grants of up to $130,000 over 9 months for technology validation and market assessment (or up to $180,000 for joint applications from two or more qualifying universities); and (2) Company Formation — a commercial launch investment of up to $300,000 (provided as a convertible debt note or reimbursable grant) over 9 months for Maryland-based startups that have licensed technology from a qualifying university within the past 12 months. Total funding can reach up to $430,000 for sole applicants across both phases. If technology is licensed out of state or the company relocates outside Maryland, funds must be repaid with interest.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MII provides up to $430,000 total for sole applicants across two phases: (1) Technology Assessment — a grant of up to $130,000 over 9 months for technology validation and market assessment (up to $180,000 for joint applications from two or more qualifying universities); includes up to $15,000 for commercialization plan development, up to $5,000 for I-Corps participation, and up to $4,500 for company formation or university start-up attorney costs; at JHU, up to $12,500 can be used to pay down patent expenses; and (2) Company Formation — a commercial launch investment of up to $300,000 over 9 months for Maryland-based startups that have licensed technology from a qualifying university within the past 12 months, provided either as a Convertible Debt Note (5-year, 8% annual interest, convertible upon a qualifying investment of $500,000+, acquisition, or asset sale) or as a Reimbursable Grant (3% of quarterly revenues for 10 years or until 2x repayment); Company Formation funds support personnel, equipment, materials, supplies, and indirect costs up to 20% (capped at $60,000 for startups; up to $30,000 for patent/licensing). If technology is licensed out of state or the company leaves Maryland, all funds must be repaid with interest.

structured_extraction.program_description: TEDCO's Maryland Makerspace Initiative Program (MMIP), created through Maryland General Assembly legislation in 2022, encourages the growth and development of Makerspaces throughout Maryland by providing financial and technical assistance to local governments and nonprofit entities. A Makerspace is a community space that gives learners and entrepreneurs access to tools, technology, and knowledge; supports the prototyping or creation of physical goods; and fosters technical education and workforce training for personal growth. Technical assistance is provided by Open Works (Baltimore City). Grants can be used to establish a new Makerspace, expand an existing one, or develop programming for one. In 2025, nearly $785,000 in total awards were distributed to 14 organizations across Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are awarded in three types: Type A (Establish New Makerspace) — up to $100,000/year for 3 years (max $300,000), or $25,000 for a feasibility study; Type B (Expand Existing Makerspace) — up to $100,000 for one year; Type C (Develop Programming) — up to $25,000 for one year. All grant types require a 1:1 match (cash or in-kind contributions), except feasibility study applications may not use in-kind matches. Applicants may submit multiple applications for different grant types. Technical assistance of up to 10 hours is also available through Open Works. In 2025, nearly $785,000 in total awards were distributed to 14 organizations across Maryland.

Allowable expenses include purchase of equipment (e.g., 3D printers), design software, training, marketing, internship and community engagement programs, building partnerships with universities and makerspaces, and utility costs if aligned with project objectives.

structured_extraction.program_name: Open Institute for Black Women Entrepreneur Excellence (Howard County Pilot Program)
structured_extraction.program_description: A 10-month hybrid leadership and entrepreneurship development program for Black women business owners. TEDCO partners with Maryland's four HBCUs to build a cohort-based community of entrepreneurs, develop peer networks, and strengthen critical business skills that foster resilience. The program focuses on leadership, communication, real-world business perspectives, and end-game planning.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive a 10-month hybrid (in-person and virtual) entrepreneur leadership development program. Sessions cover leadership and communication, real-world perspectives, and development planning. Participants pay a $250 registration fee; $200 is refunded upon completing the program. In-person sessions are held at the Maryland Innovation Center in Columbia, MD.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Black women who are founders, co-founders, or CEOs of companies at pre-seed to pre-Series A stage, primarily based in Howard County, Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Leadership and entrepreneurship development training, including assessments, workshops, and peer networking sessions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Primarily designed for Howard County-based business owners; entrepreneurs outside Howard County may be considered based on available slots.
requirements_list: Must be a founder, co-founder, or CEO
Company must be at a minimum of pre-seed stage and a maximum of pre-Series A stage
Participants must pay a $250 registration fee upon acceptance
Participants may miss no more than two sessions to graduate
Primarily Howard County-based, though out-of-county applicants may be considered
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through TEDCO. If accepted, pay a $250 registration fee. Attend in-person and virtual sessions over 10 months. Complete the course to receive a $200 refund of the registration fee.

structured_extraction.program_description: TEDCO's Rural Business Innovation Initiative (RBII) helps startup and small technology-based businesses in rural Maryland grow by providing free professional mentoring, consulting, and targeted project support. Companies that receive at least 90 days of mentoring can also apply for up to $25,000 in pre-seed funding.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free mentoring and technical assistance is provided by regional RBII mentors at no cost to the company. Mentors help with business strategy, market analysis, funding opportunities, financial analysis, business plan review, intellectual property, prototype development, and manufacturing problem solving. Companies that have received mentoring for at least 90 days are eligible to apply for $25,000 in pre-seed funding.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small and early-stage technology-based companies in rural Maryland with fewer than 16 employees and annual revenues of $1 million or less.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business strategy, market analysis, competitive analysis, funding introductions, financial analysis, business plan or grant review, intellectual property, prototype development, manufacturing problem solving. Pre-seed funding of up to $25,000 for eligible companies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to companies located in rural Maryland as defined by the Rural Maryland Council. Regional mentors cover Southern Maryland (Charles, Calvert, St. Mary's), Northern Maryland (Frederick, Carroll, Northern Baltimore Counties), Allegany, Garrett, Washington, Upper Shore (Harford, Cecil, Kent), and Lower Shore (Talbot, Caroline, Dorchester, Wicomico, Queen Anne's, Somerset, Worcester) counties.
requirements_list: Must be involved in developing new technologies/products or utilizing technology to create new or expand their business
Must have fewer than 16 employees
Annual revenues of $1 million or less
Must be in good standing with the Maryland Department of Taxation and Assessments
Must be located in rural Maryland as defined by the Rural Maryland Council
Must receive at least 90 days of RBII mentoring to be eligible for pre-seed funding
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the RBII mentor assigned to your region for an initial assessment. Mentors will evaluate your company and determine eligibility for mentoring and project assistance. After at least 90 days of mentoring, companies may apply for $25,000 in pre-seed funding. Applicants are encouraged to review the applicable TEDCO investment legislation regulations before applying.

structured_extraction.program_name: Rural and Underserved Business Recovery from Impact of COVID-19 (RUBRIC)
structured_extraction.program_description: An economic relief initiative to assist Maryland's technology companies detrimentally impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic and associated economic downturn. Targets socially and economically disadvantaged companies or those in rural areas of Maryland. TEDCO administered $5 million in state emergency funds as reimbursable grants of up to $100,000 to help early-stage companies bridge the gap during the COVID-19 downturn and position them for the next phase of fundraising or sustainability.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursable grants of up to $100,000 awarded to eligible early-stage technology companies. Funds are disbursed in two 50% tranches, with the second tranche upon completion of an activity report. Recipients pay 3% of quarterly revenues for 5 years as royalty repayments, capped at 150% of the award amount. A 10% discount per year is available for early repayment. Funds can be used to defray costs of attracting/retaining jobs, attracting/retaining customers, and helping sustain companies having difficulties raising capital.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland technology companies impacted by COVID-19 that are socially or economically disadvantaged, or located in rural areas of Maryland, with fewer than 100 employees.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Address specific challenges faced by the company associated with COVID-19, including attracting/retaining jobs and customers, and helping sustain companies having difficulties raising capital. Eligible expenses as described in the application (Exhibit A).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland counties except Baltimore City, Baltimore County (excluding northern Baltimore County), Howard County, Anne Arundel County, Prince George's County, and Montgomery County. Companies must be located in rural areas of Maryland as defined in State Finance and Procurement Article, §2-207, Annotated Code of Maryland, OR be socially/economically disadvantaged.
requirements_list: Must be a technology-based company with a proprietary competitive advantage in the market
Must be socially and economically disadvantaged OR located in rural Maryland
Must have been detrimentally impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic
Must have fewer than 100 employees
Must have high barriers to traditional financing
Must be expected to scale to the next phase of fundraising or reach sustainability
Must maintain accurate financial records
Must submit Initial Activity Report within 6 months of effective date
Must submit Second Activity Report within 12 months of effective date
Must submit Quarterly Financial Reports beginning 6 months after effective date
Must make quarterly revenue-based reimbursement payments (3% of quarterly revenues)
Must comply with all applicable federal, state, and local laws
Excludes retail sales, real estate development, insurance, banking, lending, and professional services (accountants, attorneys, physicians)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are no longer being accepted. Previously, applicants could review the Request for Applications (RFA) for eligibility requirements, funding structure, and review criteria, then direct questions to Rubric@tedco.md.

structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive grant program that provides matching funds to Maryland small businesses that have received federal SBIR or STTR Phase I or Phase II awards. The program aims to boost commercialization of research, support technology transfer from universities and federal labs, and encourage small businesses — including economically disadvantaged ones — to pursue SBIR/STTR funding. It also stimulates innovation and entrepreneurship and attracts early-stage small businesses engaged in R&D to Maryland. Awards are issued on a quarterly basis, subject to availability of funds.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: For Phase I SBIR/STTR awards, TEDCO can grant an additional award equal to the lesser of 25% of the Phase I award or $25,000. For Phase II SBIR/STTR awards, TEDCO can grant an award equal to the lesser of 25% of the Phase II award or $75,000. Awards are issued on a quarterly basis, subject to availability of funds.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Four application cycles per year: January 1 - March 30, April 1 - June 30, July 1 - September 30, October 1 - December 31. All deadlines at 5:00 pm Eastern Time. If deadline falls on a weekend or Maryland State holiday, the effective deadline is the first non-holiday weekday.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland small businesses with fewer than 250 employees that have received a federal SBIR or STTR Phase I or Phase II award within six months of the application cycle. Primarily technology or life sciences companies, not primarily engaged in retail sales, real estate development, insurance, banking, lending, or professional services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Commercialization of research conducted by small businesses; technology transfer from universities and federal labs to small businesses; stimulation of innovation and entrepreneurship.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to small businesses located in Maryland with operations in-state.
requirements_list: Must have received a federal SBIR/STTR award
Company must have received an SBIR or STTR award within six months of the application cycle
Must have fewer than 250 employees
Must be a technology or life sciences company
Must not be primarily engaged in retail sales, real estate development, insurance, banking, lending, or professional services (accountants, attorneys, physicians)
Must meet all eligibility requirements listed in the Request for Applications (RFA)
Applications must be submitted online through TEDCO's application portal
Applications submitted by email, mail, or after the deadline will not be considered
Confidential business and financial information should be marked as such at the top of reports
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application online through TEDCO's application portal during an open application cycle. After submission, applicants receive a confirmation email. For additional confirmation or inquiries, email sbir-ta@tedcomd.com. Refer to the RFA document for complete program details.

structured_extraction.program_description: A training and technical assistance program run by TEDCO that helps Maryland life science and technology small businesses write and submit winning SBIR/STTR proposals. TEDCO selects up to 25 companies to participate in a two-part virtual program that provides workshops, proposal reviews, market research tools, and expert coaching to position companies for up to $305,000 in non-dilutive Phase I funding from the National Science Foundation (NSF).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A two-part virtual program (up to 25 companies selected) that provides comprehensive training and coaching to help small businesses prepare competitive SBIR/STTR proposals. Part I covers business planning, commercialization, and pitch writing through 2 live workshops. Part II provides 6 additional workshops focused on proposal quality and submission readiness. Participants also receive training materials, access to collaborative SharePoint portals, market research tools, and help with government registrations (SAM.gov and Research.gov). The goal is to position companies for up to $305,000 in NSF Phase I SBIR/STTR funding.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland life science and technology small businesses seeking federal SBIR/STTR funding, particularly from NSF
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and technical assistance to develop competitive SBIR/STTR grant proposals; program does not directly provide grant funding
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Open to small businesses across Maryland's 24 counties and Baltimore City
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland-based small business
Must be in the life science or technology sector
Part II participation typically requires an approved NSF project pitch and a refined business model
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online via the application link at https://tedco.tfaforms.net/181. Contact Julia Deng at jdeng@tedcomd.com for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that helps Maryland technology and life sciences small businesses build expertise to access federal SBIR/STTR funding. It provides workshops covering federal agency-specific SBIR/STTR program overviews, proposal writing training, commercialization planning, and budget preparation, along with two rounds of individual expert proposal reviews.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides workshops on federal SBIR/STTR program overviews (federal, DoD, NIH, DoE), proposal writing, commercialization planning, and budget preparation. It also includes two rounds of individual proposal reviews by technical and/or business experts. No financial award amount is specified.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland small businesses in technology and life sciences that have not yet been awarded an SBIR/STTR grant.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and technical assistance to prepare competitive SBIR/STTR proposals for federal funding.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to small businesses located in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland small business
Must not have previously been awarded an SBIR/STTR
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online through the TEDCO application portal at https://tedco.tfaforms.net/170.

structured_extraction.program_description: TEDCO's evergreen Venture Funds provide equity investments to early-stage, Maryland-connected companies at the pre-seed to pre-venture capital funding stage. The funds are sector-agnostic and back entrepreneurs with a track record of execution, investing between $500K and $2M per company. Funding is supplemented by Maryland's State Small Business Credit Initiative (SSBCI). TEDCO manages over $110M in assets under management and prefers to lead deals but will also co-invest alongside other investors. Pre-launch investments are considered for exceptional opportunities led by experienced entrepreneurs. The program uses taxpayer dollars and is subject to Maryland laws and regulations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Convertible note or equity investment ranging from $500,000 to $2,000,000 per company. Requires a minimum 1:1 private capital match. TEDCO manages over $110M in assets under management and prefers to lead deals but will also co-invest alongside other investors. TEDCO typically invests as the first institutional investor or in the first institutional round. Cannot invest in retail sales, real estate development, insurance, banking, lending, professional accounting, law, or medical services.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing — opportunities assessed on a rolling basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Early-stage, technology-based or life science-based Maryland companies and entrepreneurs seeking equity investment, particularly at the pre-seed to pre-venture capital funding stage.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: General business growth and development for early-stage companies, from pre-seed to the stage of attracting venture capital.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Company must be headquartered in Maryland with principal business operations in Maryland. More than 50% of the workforce must work from a physical location in Maryland. A 5-year commitment to Maryland is required via a clawback agreement. TEDCO may refer companies outside the region to co-investors.
requirements_list: Company must have a connection to Maryland
Must be headquartered in Maryland with principal business operations in Maryland
More than 50% of workforce must work from a physical location in Maryland
Started operations within 7 years of application
Received less than $30 million in prior funding (excluding TEDCO and grants)
Fewer than 250 employees
Technology-based with intellectual property protection potential
Must rely on technology for competitive advantage
Willing to sign 5-year clawback agreement
Minimum 1:1 private capital match
Must be a corporation or limited liability company (NOT a sole proprietorship)
Applications must be submitted online through the TEDCO website
Email investments@tedcomd.com after submitting to confirm receipt
Applications submitted by email or mail will not be considered
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application online at TEDCO's application portal (https://tedco.tfaforms.net/f/vftedcoapplication). After submitting, email investments@tedcomd.com to confirm your application was received. TEDCO evaluates company merits using various criteria. Opportunities are reviewed on a rolling basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: TEDCO's Seed Funds provide seed-stage equity investment to early-stage technology companies in Maryland that show promise of becoming venture-fundable or that will become sustainable through customer revenue, follow-on funding, or other forms of corporate venture capital. The fund is supported in part by Maryland's State Small Business Credit Initiative (SSBCI). Four fund types are available: Cybersecurity Investment Fund, Life Sciences Investment Fund, Technology Commercialization Fund, and Gap Investment Fund. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: TEDCO invests seed-stage equity (via convertible note or equity investment) into companies that show potential to attract venture capital or achieve sustainability through revenue or follow-on funding. Investment amounts range from $100,000 to $500,000 depending on the fund type. Four focus areas: Cybersecurity Investment Fund, Life Sciences Investment Fund, Technology Commercialization Fund, and Gap Investment Fund. Requires a minimum 1:1 private capital match. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis. Note: Technology Commercialization Fund is 100% deployed for FY25.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Early-stage technology startups in Maryland seeking seed-stage equity investment to grow toward venture fundability or revenue sustainability.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Seed-stage business development and growth toward venture fundability or revenue sustainability, including commercializing technology and reaching sustainability through customer revenue or follow-on funding. Gap Fund specifically restricted to new hires in Maryland only.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to seed-stage companies statewide in Maryland; must have a principal place of business in Maryland; headquarters must be in Maryland; more than half of workforce must work from a physical location in Maryland; principal business operations conducted from a physical location in Maryland. A 5-year claw-back/Securities Repurchase Agreement is required.
requirements_list: Company must be at seed stage
Must show promise of becoming venture-fundable or sustainable through customer revenue, follow-on funding, or corporate venture
Must have a principal place of business in Maryland
Headquarters must be in Maryland
More than half of workforce must work from physical location in Maryland
Must be a Maryland-based company
Must have at least one full-time employee
Must be an early-stage technology company
Started operations within 5 years of application (except Builder Fund)
Not more than 250 employees
Not received over $15,000,000 in prior funding (excluding TEDCO and grants)
Minimum 1:1 private capital match
Technology-based business
Must be a corporation or limited liability company (sole proprietorships not eligible)
Focus areas: cyber tech/IT, life sciences, general tech commercialization, or gap funding
Ineligible industries include: retail sales, real estate development, insurance, banking, lending, professional accounting/law/medical services
Must execute a five-year Securities Repurchase Agreement (claw-back provision)
Must maintain 'qualified business' status under Maryland law
Must grant board observation, information, and inspection rights to TEDCO
Application must be submitted online through TEDCO's application portal
Applicants should email investments@tedcomd.com after submitting to confirm receipt
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application online through TEDCO's application portal at tedcomd.com/seed-funds on a rolling basis. After submitting, email investments@tedcomd.com to confirm your application was received. Applications submitted by email or mail will not be considered. See the TEDCO Seed Funds page for additional details.

structured_extraction.program_name: TEDCO Social Impact Funds – Pre-Seed Builder Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: A TEDCO investment program providing pre-seed equity-style investments to technology startups founded by socially and economically disadvantaged individuals in Maryland. Through the SSBCI-backed Social Impact Funds, TEDCO typically invests an initial amount of $100,000 via convertible notes, with the Social Impact Funds able to invest up to $750,000 in a single deployment (with investments generally ranging from $200,000 to $500,000). Funded companies also receive Builder Fund resources including hands-on executive support, peer-to-peer mentorship and collaboration, and networking opportunities to help early-stage companies grow. Eligible organizations include corporations and limited liability companies; sole proprietorships are not eligible.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: TEDCO typically invests an initial amount of $100,000 via convertible notes, with the Social Impact Funds able to invest up to $750,000 in a single deployment (investments generally range from $200,000 to $500,000). Requires a minimum 1:1 private capital match. Funded companies also receive Builder Fund resources including hands-on and educational executive support, peer-to-peer mentorship and collaboration, and networking opportunities. Eligible entity types include corporations and limited liability companies (not sole proprietorships). Ineligible industries include retail sales, real estate development, insurance, banking, lending, and professional accounting/law/medical services.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Pre-seed technology startups where at least 50% of founders demonstrate economic and social disadvantage (Socially and Economically Disadvantaged Individuals, SEDI), with a principal place of business in Maryland and a majority of their workforce based in Maryland. Eligible entities are corporations or limited liability companies (not sole proprietorships).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Pre-seed business development and general company growth as an early-stage technology startup.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Principal place of business (headquarters) must be in Maryland; principal business operations must be conducted from Maryland; more than half of the workforce (W-2 employees and active founders) must work from a physical location in Maryland. Available statewide.

Minimum 1:1 private capital match
Fewer than 251 employees
Less than $15,000,000 in dilutive funding raised to date (excluding TEDCO)
Must be a technology-based business with competitive market advantage and protectable intellectual property
Principal place of business (headquarters) is in Maryland
Principal business operations conducted from Maryland
At least one full-time employee
More than half of the workforce (W-2 employees and active founders) based in Maryland
Must be a corporation or limited liability company (sole proprietorships not eligible)
Willing to sign a 5-year clawback agreement
Founder/officers/managers agree to receive executive support
Not engaged in retail sales, real estate development, insurance, banking, lending, or professional accounting/law/medical services
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application online through TEDCO's website at the designated application page. After submitting, email investments@tedcomd.com to confirm receipt. Applications submitted by other means (email, mail) will not be considered.

structured_extraction.program_description: A monthly virtual open forum hosted by TEDCO's Venture Development team every third Wednesday at noon. Designed to keep Maryland's entrepreneurial ecosystem informed, the forum covers tools, services, and funding available through TEDCO's Venture Development programs to help early-stage tech companies and founders succeed.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free monthly virtual sessions providing information, Q&A, and networking focused on TEDCO Venture Development programs including Prelude Pitch, Concept Capital, and Rural and Urban Business Innovation Initiatives mentorship and collaboration opportunities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: First-time founders, seasoned entrepreneurs, and support organizations interested in TEDCO's Venture Development programs for early-stage tech companies
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland entrepreneurs and ecosystem stakeholders
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register via the Zoom link provided on the event page to attend the monthly online session.

structured_extraction.program_description: TABA allows federal agencies to provide funding to small businesses that have received SBIR/STTR Phase I or Phase II awards, to help them commercialize their technology. TEDCO helps Maryland-based SBIR/STTR awardees access and navigate TABA funding by identifying needs, developing a Statement of Work, and providing ongoing expert support in areas like market analysis, IP protection, business strategy, and regulatory planning.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Phase I awards provide up to $6,500 per award. Phase II awards provide up to $50,000 per project. Funding may be in addition to or included within the SBIR/STTR award budget, depending on the federal agency. TEDCO helps applicants identify TABA-offering agencies, develop a Statement of Work, and connects them with experts for ongoing support in commercialization, market analysis, IP protection, business strategy, and regulatory planning.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland-based small businesses that are SBIR/STTR Phase I or Phase II awardees with fewer than 250 employees and a CEO and at least 50% of the company located in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business strategy, operations, product sales, IP protection, market research, market validation, regulatory planning, manufacturing plans, technology assessment, market analysis and strategy, business model development, commercialization road mapping, investment readiness, and IP/regulatory affairs support.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be a Maryland company with fewer than 250 employees, with the CEO and at least 50% of the company located in Maryland.
requirements_list: Maryland company with fewer than 250 employees
CEO and 50% of the company must be located in Maryland
Must be a current SBIR/STTR Phase I or Phase II awardee
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at the TEDCO application portal (rolling basis). TEDCO performs an initial assessment and schedules conversations with the applicant to identify technical and business needs. TEDCO then works with the applicant and an expert to develop a Statement of Work outlining specific TABA support services.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program for full-time faculty at Bowie State University and Frostburg State University that supports technology validation and commercialization. It funds proof-of-principle studies to validate a technology's commercial use and supports market analysis to develop a commercialization plan.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $50,000 total per award for full-time faculty, to be completed within a 6-month project period. Up to $40,000 for Technology Development (proof-of-principle studies) and up to $10,000 for Market Assessment (market analysis and commercialization plan).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Full-time faculty at Bowie State University and Frostburg State University
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Proof-of-principle studies to validate technology for commercial applications and advance intellectual property, plus market analysis and development of a commercialization plan.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to faculty at Bowie State University (Prince George's County) and Frostburg State University (Allegany County).
requirements_list: Must be full-time faculty at Bowie State University or Frostburg State University
Project must be completed within a 6-month period
Must complete both a Technology Development Report and a Market Assessment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a rolling application per the Technology Validation Program RFA. Applications were open from 3/15/2024 to 6/30/2024.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Urban Business Innovation Initiative (UBII) provides technical and business assistance to early-stage and small companies in key urban areas of Maryland. TEDCO's Venture Growth Advisors mentor companies, connect them to support programs, and help them commercialize technology, explore market channels, identify financing, and develop their management teams.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: TEDCO provides technical and business assistance through dedicated Venture Growth Advisors who mentor companies and connect them to support programs. Specific support includes UBII project grant funding, I-Corps participation, access to the Builder Fund, partner programs, guidance on technology commercialization, SBIR/STTR proposal writing assistance, prototype development support, and connections to local service providers.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Tammira Lucas, DBA (Baltimore City); Malcolm Tyson (Prince George's County); Claudius Taylor (Central Maryland)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Early-stage and small companies in urban Maryland, particularly in Baltimore City, Prince George's County, and Central Maryland, operating in technology and innovation sectors.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Technology commercialization, market development, prototype development, SBIR/STTR proposal writing, management team building, and general business development.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to companies in key urban areas of Maryland, specifically Baltimore City, Prince George's County, and Central Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be an early-stage or small company
Must be located in an urban Maryland area served by the program (Baltimore City, Prince George's County, or Central Maryland)
Must be evaluated by a Venture Growth Advisor
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Venture Growth Advisor for your region. Advisors evaluate potential clients and provide mentoring and connections to TEDCO support programs.

structured_extraction.program_description: Equity investments in early-stage, high-growth companies. MMG co-invests alongside other investors using instruments such as preferred stock, convertible notes, SAFE agreements, and warrants. MMG expects an exit within 3–7 years and a 2x or greater return. Investments are evaluated case by case.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Equity investments from $25,000 to $2,000,000 using preferred stock, convertible notes, SAFE agreements, warrants, or other equity instruments. Investment terms match those of other investors in the same round. Target exit within 3–7 years with a 2x or greater return. MMG is not typically the lead investor.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Early-stage companies with high growth potential located in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Working capital, inventory, equipment, construction and renovation, leasehold improvements, real property (if business occupies at least 51%)
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland-based businesses
requirements_list: Company must be an early-stage business with high growth potential
Investments considered on a case-by-case basis
MMG co-invests with other investors and is not typically the lead investor
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the online Application Questionnaire/Tool at mmgcapitalgroup.com/application-form to assess qualification and determine which program fits best. Review the Funds Under Management, Application Process, Program Guidelines, and FAQs before applying.

structured_extraction.program_description: Term loans and loan guarantees for Maryland-based businesses that need flexible financing. Loans are based on the business's ability to generate cash flow to repay the debt. Business and personal assets are used as collateral. Loan guarantees cover up to 80% of principal and interest on loans from participating banks.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Term loans from $25,000 to $2,000,000 with a 3–10 year term (amortization up to 20 years). Interest rate is WSJ prime rate +/- 3%. Minimum credit score of 550 required. Loan guarantees up to 80% of principal and interest on loans from participating banks. Collateral and personal guarantees from owners with 20% or more ownership are required in most cases.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland-based businesses, particularly those with credit challenges, collateral gaps, or limited financial resources
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Working capital, refinancing debt, machinery and equipment, improvements to leased or owned real property, acquisition of real property used in the business
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland-based businesses
requirements_list: Minimum credit score of 550 across the three main credit bureaus
Business assets must be pledged as collateral
Personal guarantee required from owners holding 20% or more
Corporate guarantees may be required depending on circumstances
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the online Application Questionnaire/Tool at mmgcapitalgroup.com/application-form to assess qualification and determine which program fits best. Review the Funds Under Management, Application Process, Program Guidelines, and FAQs before applying.

structured_extraction.program_description: MCBIF provides access to affordable, flexible capital for small, minority, women, and veteran-owned businesses in Maryland. Funded by 1.5% of proceeds from video lottery terminal (slot machine) facilities in Maryland and distributed by the Maryland Department of Commerce, at least 50% of funds must be allocated to businesses in communities surrounding a casino (Target Areas). Since 2014, MCBIF has provided over $31 million in financing to over 145 small businesses in Maryland. The program offers loans, equity investments, and surety bonds to help businesses grow, acquire equipment, purchase real estate, and more.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides loans ranging from $50,000 to $1,000,000, equity investments (convertible subordinated notes, preferred stock, common stock, warrants), and surety bonds (bid, payment, and performance). Term loans carry interest rates of 4%–8%; lines of credit 4%–7%; professional/technical assistance loans 2%–4%. Loan terms run one to ten years. Eligible uses include business acquisition, equipment, owner-occupied commercial real estate, vehicles, furniture and fixtures, leasehold improvements, working capital, marketing, personnel, inventory expansion, professional consulting, and refinancing existing debt under certain circumstances. A non-refundable application fee of $250 is required, plus a commitment fee of $500–$3,500 if approved.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses, minority-owned, women-owned, and veteran-owned businesses in Maryland, with priority for businesses in communities surrounding casino locations in Baltimore City, Cecil County, Allegany County, Anne Arundel County, Worcester County, and Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Working capital, equipment acquisition, owner-occupied commercial real estate, business acquisitions, leasehold improvements, vehicles, furniture and fixtures, marketing, personnel, inventory expansion, professional/technical consulting, and refinancing of existing debt.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Business must be located in the State of Maryland. At least 50% of investment funds must go to businesses in designated Target Areas near casino/video lottery terminal facilities; the remaining 50% may go to any Maryland business.
requirements_list: Must be a small, minority, women, or veteran-owned business

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides mental health and substance use disorder screening, assessment, and referral services for low-income, uninsured or Medicaid/Medicare-covered residents of Montgomery County. It also offers consultations to agencies and individuals, and includes Bridges Transitional Psychiatry for uninsured clients transitioning to community care.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free or sliding-scale-fee behavioral health assessments, referrals to public mental health and substance use disorder services, in-person or telephone clinical consultations, and assistance connecting to additional social service resources. Fees for assessments, counseling, and psychiatry visits are determined using the Maryland Department of Health sliding fee schedule. The program accepts Medicaid and Medicare. No one is denied services based on inability to pay.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income, uninsured or Medicaid/Medicare-insured Montgomery County residents age 18 or older who need mental health or substance use disorder services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Mental health and substance use disorder assessments, referrals to public services, clinical consultations, and transitional psychiatry and counseling.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Montgomery County, Maryland resident for assessment and referral services. Telephone consultation and information/referral services are available to all residents and professionals.

Must be age 18 or older for assessment and referral services
Must be uninsured with no or low income, or have Medicaid or Medicare insurance
Bring identification, proof of residency, and proof of insurance and/or income if applicable
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 240-777-1770 for information. Walk-in assessment and referral services are available Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., on a first-come, first-served basis. Arrive by 8:30 a.m. for morning assessments or by 12:30 p.m. for afternoon assessments. Apply in person at 27 Courthouse Square, Suite 101, Rockville, MD 20850.

structured_extraction.program_description: Individual critical illness insurance for eligible Montgomery County government employees. Pays a lump-sum benefit directly to the policyholder upon diagnosis of a covered serious illness such as heart attack, cancer, stroke, or organ transplant.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Lump-sum benefit of $10,000–$30,000 (depending on coverage level chosen) paid directly to the policyholder upon diagnosis of a covered critical illness. Premium deductions are taken from the employee's paycheck.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Unrepresented and IAFF (firefighters union) employees of Montgomery County government
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Financial support upon diagnosis of a serious illness including heart attack, sudden cardiac arrest, internal cancers, coma, end-stage renal failure, stroke, major organ transplants, or paralysis
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Montgomery County government employees

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact AFLAC directly for a quote and to apply. If approved, AFLAC notifies the County to begin payroll deductions. Eligible employees can sign up at any time.

structured_extraction.program_description: Individual short-term disability insurance coverage for eligible Montgomery County government employees. Pays benefits directly to the policyholder for off-the-job accidents or sickness, regardless of other disability coverage the employee may have.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Monthly benefit of $500–$6,000 (subject to income requirements). Benefit periods of 3, 6, or 12 months. Elimination periods of 0/7 days or 0/14 days for injury/sickness. Premium deductions are taken from the employee's paycheck.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Income replacement during off-the-job accident or sickness

structured_extraction.program_name: AGZA ServicePro Certification with Electric Leaf Blower Rebate for Landscapers
structured_extraction.program_description: A hands-on training and certification program for small to mid-sized landscaping businesses in Montgomery County to support transition to battery-electric operations, with a focus on electric leaf blowers. Includes a professional certification course, live equipment demonstrations, and equipment coupons.
eligible_industries: Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive a free AGZA Service Pro Certificate (a $359 value training course in battery operations), a $500 equipment coupon for electric blowers or batteries at Commercial Mower Depot (one per company), live equipment demos, breakfast and lunch, and raffle prizes including cleaning kits and TOWA power distribution systems.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and certification in battery-electric equipment operations; equipment coupon for electric blowers or batteries.

Not open to government agencies
Attendance may be limited to one person per business
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register online at the provided Google Form link. Location will be disclosed only to registered applicants. Event is May 13, 9am-1pm in Derwood, MD.

structured_extraction.program_name: ALERT / Alcohol Law Education Regulatory Training
structured_extraction.program_description: ALERT is a free online training program that educates Montgomery County alcohol beverage licensees — including servers, sellers, managers, and owners — on alcohol beverage regulatory compliance. The program covers alcohol's effects on the body, responsible alcohol beverage service, Maryland alcohol rules and regulations, inspections, underage alcohol use and ID checking, and Board of License Commissioners (BLC) hearings. Participants learn how to develop responsible alcohol policies, review issues identified by county and state enforcement agencies, and network with peers and county officials.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free online training sessions held twice a month (2nd and 4th Monday, 10AM–12PM). Available in English and Spanish. Registration is required as space is limited. Participants who join after 10:15am will not be admitted and will not receive a letter of attendance. Training covers alcohol's effects on the body, responsible alcohol beverage service, Maryland alcohol rules and regulations, inspections, underage alcohol use and ID checking, and Board of License Commissioners (BLC) hearings. Completion certificate provided upon finishing the training.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Registration required before each session; sessions held throughout 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County alcohol beverage servers, sellers, managers, owners, license holders and applicants for alcohol licenses
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Alcohol beverage regulatory compliance education, including responsible service practices, ID verification, inspection preparation, and Board of License Commissioners hearing procedures
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must register in advance as space is limited
Must join the online session by 10:15am or will not be admitted
Completion of ALERT training required for alcohol service employees and license holders
Training must be completed within 60 days of Board of License Commissioners violation decision
Minimum age 21 to purchase alcohol; 18 to serve/sell
Valid ID required for alcohol purchases
Employee records must be retained for 1 year after employment ends
Alcohol sales receipts must be retained for 2+ years
Must purchase alcohol only from ABS/county liquor stores
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register online via the Zoom registration link for English or Spanish sessions. Sessions are held on the 2nd and 4th Monday of each month (with some Spanish sessions on Wednesdays). Sign in 10 minutes early to allow time for troubleshooting. For licensing, submit online at montgomerycountymd.gov/ABS, pay $100 processing fee with application, attend hearing with Board, receive resolution letter within 10 days, schedule final inspection, and pay license fee.

structured_extraction.program_description: A structured hybrid program lasting 24 to 30 weeks for individuals who have shown a pattern of abusive or controlling behaviors in intimate partner relationships. The program uses a specialized curriculum with cognitive-behavioral therapy techniques to build accountability, empathy, and healthier relationship skills, with the goal of breaking the cycle of violence and creating lasting behavior change.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Weekly group sessions over 24 to 30 weeks using cognitive-behavioral therapy and structured curriculum. Fees are $50 for intake/registration, $20 per class session, and $40 for individual counseling. A sliding-scale fee reduction is available for those who cannot afford full payment — no one is turned away due to inability to pay.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents (male or female) involved in intimate partner violence, or non-residents whose incident occurred in Montgomery County, referred by Maryland Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services agents, caseworkers, Montgomery County courts, or attorneys.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participation in a structured behavior-change and counseling program focused on ending abusive and controlling behaviors in intimate partner relationships.

Must provide participant ID and court documents including Statement of Charges (SOC), court documents, and probation contracts
Must sign an enrollment agreement outlining rules and behavior change requirements
Must attend weekly group sessions and complete the program consecutively (one credit per week)

Submit required documents (participant ID, Statement of Charges, court documents, probation contracts) to schedule an intake.

Services include a 24-hour crisis hotline, individual and group counseling, legal advocacy, emergency shelter, children's counseling, counseling for abusive partners, and community education.

No fees for emergency services; all other fees are on an ability-to-pay basis. No one is denied services due to lack of funds.

structured_extraction.program_name: Academia Hispana para la Comunidad (Hispanic Community Academy)
structured_extraction.program_description: A free, Spanish-language community education program run by the Montgomery County Police Department. The program teaches Hispanic community members about local laws, police operations, and resources available to them in Montgomery County. Topics include criminal law, Maryland traffic laws, investigations, safety drills, and resources for abuse victims. Graduates use what they learn to build trust and cooperation between the Hispanic community and local police.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free 13-week training program held one night per week (Wednesdays, 6:00 PM – 8:30 PM). Classes are held at the Public Safety Training Academy in Gaithersburg. Three sessions are offered per year. Class size is limited to 40 students, first come first served. Extra services include CPR classes and a ride-along with police officers. Immigration status does not affect eligibility.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Community education and training — no funds are distributed to participants

Must live or work in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register online through the provided registration form link. Enrollment is first come, first served, limited to 40 students per session. Registration for Session 24 (starting August 26, 2026) opens in June 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: An unpaid internship program at Montgomery County's Pre-Release and Reentry Services (PRRS) offered in conjunction with a college or university. The program provides supervised field experience for students in human services-related degree programs, including training in resident supervision, community release verification, recreational programming, case management, adjustment hearings, on-site verifications, home visitations, and administrative support. The program is structured as an 8-week cycle with formal and on-the-job training components. Time commitment and responsibilities vary based on school requirements and staff availability.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Unpaid supervised internship experience in community corrections and reentry services, tailored to the academic requirements of the student's college or university program. The 8-week structured program includes formal and on-the-job training in resident supervision, community release verification, recreational programming, case management, adjustment hearings, on-site verifications, home visitations, and administrative support. Hours and responsibilities vary based on school requirements and staff availability. Generally requires approximately 24 hours per week including part of a weekend shift (Friday-Saturday or Sunday-Monday).

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Unpaid supervised work experience in community corrections and reentry services to fulfill academic internship requirements, including resident supervision, community release coordination, recreational programming, administrative assistance, and participation in adjustment hearings and home visitations.

All buses are low-floor with ramps, and include automated stop announcement systems for passengers who are blind, low vision, deaf, or hard of hearing.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Accessible transportation to travel around Montgomery County, including commuting to work and general transit trips.

Those unable to use fixed-route transit due to disability may apply for MetroAccess paratransit services through WMATA.

structured_extraction.program_description: A licensing program that allows property owners to register an accessory dwelling unit (ADU) — a secondary living space either within or added to an existing single-family home, or in a separate structure on the same lot — with Montgomery County's Department of Housing and Community Affairs. Owners without a Special Exception approved before May 20, 2013 must apply for this Class 3 license.

Applicants submit an application (online or paper), an affidavit, and arrange a sign pickup. The county reviews the application, may produce a Director's Finding Report, and neighbors may file objections.

structured_extraction.program_description: An outpatient behavioral health program that provides individual and group psychotherapy, office-based case management, psychiatric evaluations, and medication monitoring to low-income Montgomery County residents with serious mental illness who cannot access the public mental health system due to lack of public benefits, immigration status, or income.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides outpatient behavioral health services including individual and group psychotherapy, psychiatric evaluations, medication monitoring, office-based case management, and psychoeducation for co-occurring disorders. Fees are determined by a sliding scale based on income. Maryland Medical Assistance (Medicaid), PAC, and Medicare are accepted. No private insurance accepted. Clients are not turned away due to inability to pay or immigration status.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income Montgomery County adults age 18 and older with serious mental illness who lack private insurance and have been unable to find services in the public mental health system, including individuals regardless of immigration status.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Outpatient behavioral health services including therapy, psychiatric care, medication management, and case management.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County residents only.
requirements_list: Must be a Montgomery County resident
Must be age 18 or older
Must have a serious mental illness
Must not have private insurance
Must be low income
Must not have been able to find services elsewhere in the public mental health system
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call Access to Behavioral Health Services at 240-777-1323. Walk-ins and direct referrals are not accepted. Bring proof of residency, proof of income, and Medicaid/Medicare card if applicable.

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary, court-supervised treatment program for adult offenders in Montgomery County whose criminal conduct is driven by substance use disorders. The program lasts a minimum of 20–22 months and is divided into multiple phases plus aftercare, combining intensive substance abuse treatment (group and individual sessions), recovery meeting attendance (AA/NA), case management, frequent court status hearings, urinalysis testing, graduated sanctions, and positive reinforcement — all as an alternative to traditional incarceration or criminal case processing. A separate Intervention Track is available for lower-level offenders with 18 months or less of incarcerable time and a high risk/high need assessment, including those with severe opiate addiction or multiple DUI cases; the Intervention Track is a minimum 12-month program with four phases (minimum 4 months each) and cases originate in District Court. Participants may be required to reside in court-approved sober housing within Montgomery County, including Pre-Release and Re-entry Services (PRC) facilities, Miracle House (transitional housing), or other approved sober housing. Medication-assisted treatment options (Antabuse/Vivitrol/Naltrexone) are available. Fees are charged on a sliding scale based on income for uninsured individuals; Maryland Medicaid (MA) and Pharmacy Adult Care (PAC) are accepted, and no one is refused services due to inability to pay. The goal is to help participants achieve sobriety, reduce reoffending, and become productive community members.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive an alternative to traditional criminal case processing through a minimum 20–22 month (or minimum 12-month Intervention Track), multi-phase program that includes collaborative treatment planning, case management, substance abuse treatment (group and individual sessions including IOP/OP), recovery meeting attendance (AA/NA, minimum 3 per week), urinalysis testing, SCRAM alcohol monitoring (if ordered), frequent court status hearings, peer support, drug and alcohol monitoring, graduated sanctions and positive reinforcement, medication-assisted treatment options (Antabuse, Vivitrol, Naltrexone), housing support (PRC facility, Miracle House transitional housing at no cost for 60 days then $50/week, or court-approved sober housing at $600–$800/month), GED program and education support, career resource specialist support, and employment assistance (minimum 35 hours/week employment, school, or volunteer work required). Fees are charged on a sliding scale based on income for uninsured individuals; Maryland Medicaid (MA) and Pharmacy Adult Care (PAC) are accepted, and no one is refused services due to inability to pay. Upon successful completion of all phases, participants are released from probation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adult residents of Montgomery County (18 and older) who are non-violent offenders with a substance use disorder, including repeat criminal offenders whose criminal behavior is motivated by drug-seeking behavior or committed under the influence of drugs or alcohol. The Intervention Track is available for lower-level offenders with 18 months or less of incarcerable time, fewer than seven prior convictions, and a high risk/high need assessment (DWI offenders must have four or fewer convictions). Participants are referred through a plea agreement or as a condition of a probation violation before the Circuit Court or District Court of Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Substance use treatment services, case management, court supervision, drug and alcohol monitoring (including SCRAM bracelet), recovery support, housing support (PRC, Miracle House, sober housing), GED and education services, employment assistance, medication-assisted treatment, and supervised alternatives to traditional criminal prosecution to help participants overcome addiction and avoid incarceration.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Montgomery County, Maryland. Cases originate in both Circuit Court and District Court. The Intervention Track specifically serves cases originating in District Court. Participants must reside in court-approved sober housing within Montgomery County throughout enrollment.
requirements_list: Adult resident of Montgomery County, Maryland, 18 years of age or older
Non-violent offender
Criminal conduct must be motivated by drug-seeking behavior or committed under the influence of drugs or alcohol
Assessed as suffering from a substance use disorder

Sanctioned and approved by the Office of the State's Attorney for referral as part of a binding plea agreement, OR referred as a condition of a violation of probation before the Circuit Court of Montgomery County
Fully capable of participating in Drug Court activities and programs

Applicant must meet with a therapist to determine clinical eligibility

Must complete all phases to graduate
Must be employed and demonstrate maintained sobriety to graduate

Must permit home visits without advance notice

Intervention Track additional requirements: 18 months or less of incarcerable time; high risk/high need assessment; fewer than seven prior convictions; DWI offenders must have four or fewer convictions; must enter guilty plea or admit to violation of probation; must reside in sober house or court-approved residence
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Referrals can come from police, family members, defense attorneys, the State's Attorney's Office's own case review, or any other party by contacting the Problem Solving Courts Coordinator at 240-777-9141 or jenna.davis@mdcourts.gov. For the Intervention Track, referral forms can also be submitted via email to Jenna Davis or fax to (240) 773-3913. A Problem-Solving Court Referral Form is available online. The State's Attorney's Office evaluates each case individually, reviewing criminal history, crime facts, and public safety concerns. Eligible applicants then meet with a therapist for clinical assessment. When contacting the program directly, bring photo identification, a copy of any insurance cards, and proof of residence. Readmission to the program (following termination) is via a Motion for Reconsideration.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides supervised housing and support to disabled adults in family homes and small assisted living homes in the community. It includes case management services and a subsidy for eligible applicants when funds are available.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Case management is provided at no cost regardless of income or assets. Eligible applicants receive a placement subsidy when funds are available. Each resident contributes to the cost of care based on their individual income, but is allowed to keep a monthly personal allowance ranging from $60 to $139 depending on income and subsidy source.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents age 18 and older who cannot live independently due to mental, physical, and/or developmental disabilities. For assisted living placements, applicants must be Montgomery County residents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supervised residential placement in a family home or assisted living home, plus case management support.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: For certified residential environments: Maryland residents. For assisted living: Montgomery County residents only.
requirements_list: Must be age 18 or older
Must be unable to live independently due to mental, physical, and/or developmental disabilities
Must be a Maryland resident (for certified residential environments)
Must be a Montgomery County resident (for assisted living placements)
Must undergo a clinical assessment including review of income and asset documentation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 240-777-3000 to determine eligibility. A clinical assessment is conducted, usually at the applicant's current residence, and includes a review of income and asset documentation.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state-mandated program that investigates allegations of abuse, neglect, self-neglect, and financial exploitation of vulnerable adults. It provides professional services to reduce risk factors and promote the health, safety, and welfare of vulnerable adults who lack the physical or mental capacity to provide for their daily needs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Professional investigation and assessment services are provided to vulnerable adults at risk of abuse, neglect, self-neglect, or financial exploitation. A staff person conducts a risk assessment of the person's safety and health needs and makes recommendations for prevention and protection. Services can be delivered in the client's home.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Vulnerable adults age 18 and over in Montgomery County who are at risk of abuse, neglect, financial exploitation, or self-neglect.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable — program provides investigative and protective services, not financial assistance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a vulnerable adult age 18 or older
Must be at risk of abuse, neglect, financial exploitation, or self-neglect
Must lack the physical or mental capacity to provide for daily needs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call the Aging and Disability Resource Unit (ADRU) at 240-777-3000 or 1-800-91-PREVENT to report a concern. If the case is accepted, a worker will visit within five business days.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides short-term loans to developers to acquire properties at risk of losing affordability, allowing current renters to remain in their community at affordable rents. The fund combines $14 million in revolving County funds with private lending matched at least 3:1. The fund is managed by the National Housing Trust for Community Development Fund (NHTCDF), which coordinates applications and arranges private capital.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Short-term loans from a $14 million revolving fund, matched at least 3:1 with private lending. Loans help developers bid competitively to acquire and preserve affordable housing properties. Initial funding has been distributed; applications are reviewed on a rolling basis as loans are repaid and the fund is replenished.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis as initial loans are repaid and the fund is replenished
structured_extraction.program_audience: Developers seeking to acquire and preserve affordable housing properties at risk of losing affordability in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquiring properties at risk of losing affordability so that current renters can remain in their community at affordable rents.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are coordinated by NHTCDF on a rolling basis. NHTCDF arranges private capital to combine with Montgomery County funds.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides matching grant cost-share assistance to qualified Montgomery County-based agricultural entrepreneurs for business projects essential to the improvement or expansion of their agricultural enterprises. MARBIDCO and the Office of Agriculture (OAG) contribute up to half of the total project cost, not to exceed $6,000 (with an additional $1,000 available for projects over $20,000). Eligible projects include deer fencing, agricultural wells, vertical racks for microgreens, farm equipment and tools, hydroponics equipment, aquaponics equipment, and refrigeration.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Matching cost-share grant that reimburses up to half of the total project cost, not to exceed $6,000 per project (with an additional $1,000 available for projects over $20,000). MARBIDCO matches up to $3,000 per project. The farmer/agricultural business must pay at least 50% of the total project cost. Up to 2 applications per fiscal year are allowed. The lifetime maximum per farm, farmer, or agricultural operation is $15,000. Applicants must receive approval before making any purchases or starting any phase of the project.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural entrepreneurs and businesses (including table crop farmers, vineyards, commodity farmers, vertical farmers, horticulture businesses, and non-traditional agricultural enterprises) headquartered in Montgomery County, Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Infrastructure projects, equipment purchases, and other agricultural business projects (such as deer fencing, agricultural wells, farm equipment and tools, hydroponics equipment, aquaponics equipment, vertical racks for microgreens, refrigeration) that enhance the agricultural economy, enable startup or expansion, or support revenue and employment growth.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Agricultural enterprise must be headquartered in Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be registered as a business and in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessment and Taxation
Agricultural enterprise must be headquartered in Montgomery County
Farmer/business must pay at least half of the total project cost
Maximum lifetime benefit is $15,000 per farm, farmer, or agricultural operation
Up to 2 applications per fiscal year allowed
Must apply and receive approval from the Office of Agriculture before making any purchases or beginning any phase of the project
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through MARBIDCO's online application portal before making any purchases or starting the project. For assistance, contact Jacqueline Arnold at 301-590-2859 or Jacqueline.Arnold@montgomerycountymd.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: A criminal justice diversion program for adult offenders in Montgomery County who have committed offenses or infractions.
