Participants perform community service as an alternative sanction to dispose of their criminal case, providing an alternative to prosecution for first-time offenders charged with misdemeanors. The program assists eligible offenders in getting cases expunged and reduces financial impact to courts and the community.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Offenders perform a minimum of 24 hours of community service instead of prosecution as an alternative sanction to resolve their criminal case. Participants work with approved governmental, charitable, or non-profit organizations. Three community service work crews are available performing indoor/outdoor work, with flexible hours to allow continued employment. The program also includes a 2.5-hour alcohol education class for certain participants covering alcohol laws, penalties, abuse, addiction, and treatment options. A program fee is collected to offset program costs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adult offenders aged 18+ in Montgomery County, including first-time offenders charged with misdemeanors, persons on probation, and defendants with prior PBJ or STET dispositions (case-by-case basis)
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Community service work performance as an alternative sanction to resolve a criminal case; program fee collection offsets program costs
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland (located at 11651 Nebel Street, Rockville, Maryland 20852)
requirements_list: Must be an adult offender (aged 18+)
Must have committed an offense or infraction against an individual or the community
Complete a minimum of 24 hours of community service
Call/meet with assigned ACS Caseworker as instructed
Refrain from behavior leading to new charges
Offender signature required on referral form
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Referrals are made through the court or probation. A Probation Referral Form is available for submission, requiring agent and manager team review and processing. The agent must print and retain a copy of the completed form.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free volunteer program for adults age 55 and older that connects seniors with local volunteer opportunities. The program helps participants find the right volunteer placement based on their skills, interests, and availability, and provides liability and injury insurance while volunteering, plus volunteer recognition.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free program that matches volunteers age 55+ with screened local volunteer opportunities. Includes complimentary liability and injury insurance while volunteering, personalized placement advice from an RSVP advisor, and volunteer recognition through a Service Rewards Program (SRP) that provides gifts for logged volunteer hours.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults age 55 and older who want to volunteer in Montgomery County, Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Volunteer placement, insurance coverage, and recognition for senior volunteers
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be age 55 or older
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact an RSVP advisor at the Volunteer Center to discuss your skills, interests, and availability. The advisor suggests relevant volunteer opportunities and you choose the one you wish to pursue, then work directly with the organization to tailor the arrangement.

structured_extraction.program_description: Part of Montgomery County's Pedestrian Safety Program, this program installs minor sidewalk projects each year to fill missing links in existing sidewalk networks. The main goals are improving access for people with disabilities and improving pedestrian access to schools, public transportation, and public facilities. Projects come from resident and community association requests, which are then evaluated and prioritized based on feasibility and equity.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The county installs sidewalk infrastructure (new sidewalks and ADA-compliant curb ramps) at no direct cost to requestors. Projects are selected through a prioritization process based on feasibility and equity. Residents and associations can submit requests through an online portal.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents and community associations seeking new sidewalk installation or ADA accessibility improvements in their neighborhoods
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of new sidewalk segments that fill missing links in existing networks, and ADA-compliant infrastructure improvements near schools, public transportation stops, and public facilities
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a resident or association in Montgomery County
Request must be feasible for a minor sidewalk project (as determined by field investigation)
Projects are prioritized based on budget availability and equity criteria
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a sidewalk installation or ADA request through the online ArcGIS portal. The county performs a field investigation to assess feasibility. Requests are then prioritized for project selection. Residents can also check the status of existing requests through the same portal.

structured_extraction.program_name: Annual Speak Up, Save a Life Video Contest
structured_extraction.program_description: A video contest that challenges 6th–12th grade students living in or attending school in Montgomery County to create an original video raising awareness about the dangers of illicit opioids, fentanyl, and overdose risk. Winners receive cash prizes, and MCPS students earn 10 SSL (Student Service Learning) hours for participating.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Cash prizes awarded to winning entries: 1st place receives $5,000; 2nd place receives $3,000; 3rd place and Fan Favorite winners each receive $1,000; and an additional $5,000 is split among Honorable Mention winners.
structured_extraction.program_audience: 6th–12th grade students living in or attending school in Montgomery County, Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cash prizes for student video creators; not restricted to a specific use.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Open to students living in or attending school in Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a 6th–12th grade student
Must live in or attend school in Montgomery County
Must create an original video promoting awareness about illicit opioids, fentanyl, and overdose risk
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register via the Video Contest Registration Page and submit your entry by the deadline of December 7, 2025.

structured_extraction.program_name: Apprentice Training, Inc. – Demolition & Environmental Worker Apprenticeship
structured_extraction.program_description: An apprenticeship program that trains workers in all aspects of demolition, including environmental remediation, saw-cutting, and operating mini excavators.
eligible_industries: Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Paid apprenticeship at $19 per hour, 40 hours per week, until 8,000 hours are completed.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals age 18 or older with a GED or high school diploma seeking to work in demolition and environmental remediation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Earn wages while training in demolition and environmental work.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Sponsor located in Landover, Maryland.
requirements_list: Age 18 or older
GED or high school diploma
$19 per hour pay
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact info@apprenticetrain.org or 240-764-0400 for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Arts and Entertainment District Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A real property tax credit for owners of manufacturing, commercial, or industrial buildings located in a designated Arts and Entertainment District in Montgomery County that are wholly or partially renovated for use by a qualifying resident artist or arts and entertainment enterprise. The credit is applied over 10 years based on the increased property assessment resulting from renovation, with rates of 80% in years 1–5, 70% in year 6, 60% in year 7, 50% in year 8, 40% in year 9, and 30% in year 10. For properties that also receive an Enterprise Zone Tax Credit, the Arts and Entertainment credit provides an additional 20% on top of the Enterprise Zone credit.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A 10-year county real property tax credit based on the increased property assessment from renovation. Credit rates: Years 1–5: 80%; Year 6: 70%; Year 7: 60%; Year 8: 50%; Year 9: 40%; Year 10: 30%. For properties that also receive an Enterprise Zone Tax Credit, the Arts and Entertainment credit is an additional 20% on top of the Enterprise Zone credit.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of manufacturing, commercial, or industrial buildings in designated Arts and Entertainment Districts in Montgomery County that are renovated for use by qualifying resident artists or arts and entertainment enterprises.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of county real property tax liability based on assessment growth from renovation of buildings for use by qualifying resident artists or arts and entertainment enterprises.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Buildings located in designated Arts and Entertainment Districts in Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Building must be manufacturing, commercial, or industrial
Located in a designated Arts and Entertainment District
Building must be wholly or partially renovated for use by a qualifying resident artist or arts and entertainment enterprise
Credit applies as long as the building continues to be used for qualifying purposes
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: No application process described; contact the Department of Finance for details.

structured_extraction.program_name: Autism, Intellectual, Developmental Disabilities (IDD) and Alzheimer's Outreach Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A program by the Montgomery County Police Department that provides education, outreach, resources, and support to individuals with Alzheimer's disease, Autism, intellectual disabilities, and Down Syndrome, as well as their caregivers. The program uses a layered approach including education, follow-up, empowerment, and coordinated response to address the needs of these individuals, including those who may wander.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Education, outreach, and community resources for individuals with Alzheimer's, Autism, intellectual disabilities, and Down Syndrome, and their caregivers. Includes a coordinated police response for wandering individuals.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with Alzheimer's disease, Autism, intellectual disabilities, and Down Syndrome, and their caregivers in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable — this is an outreach and education program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a resident of Montgomery County or have a loved one with Alzheimer's, Autism, intellectual disability, or Down Syndrome
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Autism, IDD and Alzheimer's Outreach Unit by calling 240-773-6525 or emailing Laurie.Reyes@montgomerycountymd.gov for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A youth ambassador program run by the BTheOne.org campaign that recruits students to help spread awareness about suicide prevention, mental health, and substance misuse among teenagers. Ambassadors can participate at two levels: sharing digital awareness content on social media, or organizing in-person activities and campaigns at their schools.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Ambassadors receive access to advertising resources (digital and physical posters and flyers), connections to professional speakers, ready-made education and presentation materials, and expert guidance from experienced mental health professionals affiliated with BTheOne.org.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students and student organizations in Montgomery County, Maryland who want to raise awareness about suicide prevention, mental health, and substance misuse among their peers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable — this is a technical assistance and training program, not a funding program. Resources provided include campaign materials, speaker connections, and expert guidance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to students in Montgomery County, Maryland (specifically mentions Montgomery County Public Schools).
requirements_list: Must be a student or student organization
Open to individuals or groups of any size
No specific club membership required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Students or student organizations can email info@collaborationcouncil.org to get involved or request help connecting with professional speakers or obtaining guidance.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Babies Born Healthy program provides care coordination services to help at-risk pregnant women connect with resources and stay healthy through their pregnancies. Services include prenatal education, screening for depression, substance abuse, intimate partner violence, and environmental safety. The program also provides intense education on preterm labor prevention, effects of smoking, drugs, and alcohol, parental nutrition, safe sleep for newborns, breastfeeding, and family planning. Additional supports include transportation to prenatal appointments, safe sleep equipment, diapers, car seats, and other incentives.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free care coordination services including prenatal education, health screenings, transportation to prenatal appointments, safe sleep equipment (Pack-n-Play portable crib), diapers, car seats, and other incentives for newborns. No fees or payments required.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Black/African American pregnant women who are Maryland Medicaid recipients and live in the Downcounty region of Montgomery County (zip codes 20903, 20904, and 20906).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Care coordination, prenatal education, health screenings, transportation to prenatal appointments, baby supplies (safe sleep equipment, diapers, car seats), and other supports to promote healthy pregnancies and birth outcomes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Participants must live in the Downcounty region of Montgomery County, specifically zip codes 20903, 20904, and 20906 (Silver Spring area).
requirements_list: Must be Black/African American
Must be a Maryland Medicaid recipient
Must live in the Downcounty region of Montgomery County (zip codes 20903, 20904, or 20906)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 240-777-3118 to apply. Self-referrals are encouraged. Referrals are also accepted from doctors, nurses, social service providers, and other community members. Bring a Maryland Medicaid insurance card if available.

structured_extraction.program_description: Bethesda Transportation Solutions (BTS), operated by the Bethesda Urban Partnership, provides free commuter services to employers, employees, residents, and visitors in downtown Bethesda. BTS helps employers create Transportation Demand Management (TDM) Plans, runs commuter information fairs, conducts biennial commuter surveys, offers green business certification, and recognizes employers who support alternative commuting. The program also provides transit subsidies and tax credit information, carpool/vanpool formation assistance, parking information and discounts, biking/walking amenities support, guaranteed ride home program, teleworking/alternative work schedule design, car sharing program information, and customized seminars and presentations. The goal is to reduce traffic congestion by encouraging employees to use transit, carpools, vanpools, biking, walking, and telework instead of driving alone.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free services including commuter information fairs, biennial commuter surveys, green business certification, employer recognition, and help designing and carrying out a Transportation Benefits Program for the worksite. Services also include transit subsidies and tax credit information, public transportation route/fare information, carpool/vanpool formation assistance, parking information and discounts, biking/walking amenities support, guaranteed ride home program, teleworking/alternative work schedule design, car sharing program information, HOV lane access information, and customized seminars and presentations. Employers with 25 or more employees in the TMD are required by county law to submit a TDM Plan. Residential building owners with 100+ dwelling units and new development/construction project applicants must also submit TDM Plans. Three levels of TDM Plans are available: Level 1 (Basic), Level 2 (Action), and Level 3 (Results).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: 90 days after written notice from Director (for TDM Plan submission)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Employers, employees, residents, and visitors in the Bethesda Transportation Management District; specifically employers with 25+ employees, building owners of residential complexes with 100+ dwelling units, and new development/construction project applicants
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reducing solo driving by helping employees and residents learn about and use transit, carpool, vanpool, biking, walking, and telework options; development and implementation of transportation demand management strategies; employer-selected strategies from approved menu or Director-approved proposals
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be located within the Bethesda Transportation Management District in Montgomery County, MD
requirements_list: Employers with 25 or more employees in the TMD must submit a TDM Plan within 90 days of written notice from the Director
Must participate in the TMD's biennial commuter survey
Must submit an annual report of employer actions to assist with reducing traffic congestion
Residential building owners with 100+ dwelling units must submit a TDM Plan
New development or construction project applicants (excluding single-family detached housing and townhouses) must submit a TDM Plan
TDM Plans must address 20 compliance questions covering parking subsidies, transit benefits, carpool/vanpool programs, telework policies, employee education, bike benefits, and commuter services
Must report on commuting/travel patterns, auto occupancy rates, parking supply/demand, transit use, carpool/vanpool use, bicycle use, and EV charging stations
Must distribute employee information on transit and alternative commuting options
Must promote the Guaranteed Ride Home Program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact BTS office at 301-656-0868 or visit www.bethesdatransit.org. TDM Plans can be submitted online. Employer submits completed TDM plan form; TMD Representative reviews; Committee reviews; Final approval granted.

structured_extraction.program_description: Bone Builders is a free, volunteer-led community-based osteoporosis prevention program for adults 55 and older that combines weight training, balance exercises, and education to increase bone density, improve balance, reduce fall risk, and enhance overall well-being. One-hour classes are held twice per week at more than 30 recreation and senior centers throughout Montgomery County. Studies show participants can gain an average of one percent bone density after one year of consistent attendance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free twice-weekly, one-hour fitness classes led by volunteers at over 30 community locations. Participants use ankle weights and hand weights and engage in warm-up, cool-down, and balance exercises designed to increase muscle strength and bone density, improve balance, and reduce fall risk. Participants bring their own weights. Classes are available at multiple recreation and senior center locations throughout Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Registration takes place each program season
structured_extraction.program_audience: County residents aged 55 and older who want to prevent osteoporosis, improve bone density, balance, and overall well-being, and reduce fall risk
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participation in twice-weekly weight training, balance, and education exercise classes
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Participants must be Montgomery County, Maryland residents. They may register for only one Bone Builders class.
requirements_list: Must be a Montgomery County resident
Must attend classes twice per week consistently to maintain place in class
May only register for one Bone Builders class at a time
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register through ActiveMONTGOMERY online. Registration opens each program season. Contact the specific center location for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free service that mails library materials to the homes of Montgomery County residents who cannot visit the library due to a physical disability, health issue, or frailty. Materials are sent and returned through the U.S. Postal Service using postage-prepaid reusable bags.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible residents can receive up to 5 library items per week by mail with a 6-week checkout period, up to 20 total items checked out at a time. Excludes Lucky Day, technology, and special collections items; items cannot be renewed. Materials are mailed to and from the customer's home at no cost.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents who cannot visit the library due to a physical disability, health issue, mobility or frailty limitations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Borrowing library materials (print books, books on CD, DVDs) delivered by mail.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Montgomery County, Maryland residents only.
requirements_list: Must be a Montgomery County resident
Must be unable to visit the library due to a physical disability, health issue, or frailty
Must have or apply for a library card
Applicant signature required
Certification from a healthcare provider, social services provider, or clergy member required certifying the applicant cannot come to the library
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete the Books @ Home application form. Have a healthcare provider, social services provider, or clergy person sign the form certifying your inability to visit the library. Mail the completed form to the Books@Home address or email it to elizabeth.lang@montgomerycountymd.gov. The applicant will be contacted by email, phone, or postal mail.

structured_extraction.program_name: Bridges to Behavioral Health Services Transitional Psychiatry Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A short-term, intensive psychiatric support program that bridges the gap between acute psychiatric care and long-term outpatient treatment. It serves individuals stepping down from inpatient hospitalization or crisis stabilization, or those unable to connect with a community provider. The program provides psychiatric evaluation, medication management, individual therapy, case management, and care coordination to reduce the risk of relapse and re-hospitalization.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Short-term, team-based psychiatric care including psychiatric evaluation and treatment, medication management, individual therapy, psychoeducation, case management, care coordination, and discharge planning. Services are available via telehealth and at two Rockville locations. Fees are charged on a sliding scale for uninsured clients using the Maryland Department of Health fee schedule. The program accepts Maryland Medicaid and Medicare. No one is denied services based on ability to pay or immigration status.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents age 18 or older who are uninsured with no or low income, or who have Medicaid or Medicare insurance, and need transitional psychiatric support after inpatient hospitalization or crisis stabilization. Telephone consultation and referral services are available to all residents and professionals.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Psychiatric evaluation and treatment, medication management, individual therapy, psychoeducation on mental health and medications, case management, care coordination, connection to community resources, and discharge and step-down planning.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Montgomery County, Maryland resident age 18 or older for assessment and referral services. Telephone consultation and information and referral services are available to all residents and professionals regardless of residency.
requirements_list: Must be a Montgomery County resident
Must be age 18 or older
Must be uninsured with no or low income, or have Medicaid or Medicare insurance
Telephone consultation and referral services are available to all residents and professionals
No denial of services based on ability to pay or immigration status
Documents required: identification, proof of residency, proof of insurance and/or income if applicable
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Referrals can be made by hospital staff, primary care providers, community mental health agencies, or by self-referral. Contact ACCESS to Behavioral Health Services at 240-777-1770 to schedule an intake assessment. The team will conduct an intake assessment to determine eligibility and develop a personalized treatment plan.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Montgomery County property tax credit for owners of qualified brownfield sites that complete a voluntary cleanup or corrective action plan, encouraging environmental remediation of contaminated properties.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A 5-year credit equal to 50% of the increase in property tax resulting from assessment increases after completing a voluntary cleanup or corrective action plan. An additional 20% credit is available if the site is in an Enterprise Zone or a county-designated Neighborhood Business Development Program area. Eligibility ends if the recipient withdraws from the voluntary cleanup program or approval is withdrawn by the Maryland Department of the Environment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of qualified brownfield sites in Montgomery County that are completing or have completed a voluntary cleanup or corrective action plan.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of county property tax liability attributable to increased assessment after brownfield remediation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. Enhanced credit available for sites in Enterprise Zones or designated Neighborhood Business Development Program areas.
requirements_list: Property must be a qualified brownfield site
Must complete a voluntary cleanup or corrective action plan
Credit applies for 5 tax years following the first revaluation after cleanup
Recipient must remain in the voluntary cleanup program
Maryland Department of the Environment must not withdraw approval
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: No application process described; contact the Department of Finance for details.

structured_extraction.program_description: BEPS establishes energy efficiency requirements for covered commercial and multifamily buildings in Montgomery County. Buildings must achieve interim (2028-2032) and final (2033-2036) energy performance standards by set deadlines or file a Building Performance Improvement Plan (BPIP). Compliance is measured using each building's normalized net site energy use intensity (NN EUI) compared to standards based on building type. Standards apply to covered buildings 25,000+ gross square feet, including county-owned buildings, privately owned nonresidential buildings, and multifamily residential/mixed-use buildings.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program sets energy performance standards and offers compliance pathways including a Building Performance Improvement Plan (BPIP) pathway for buildings where meeting the standard is not cost effective. Buildings must achieve normalized net site EUI at or below interim and final performance standards by specified deadlines, with standards accounting for weather normalization, renewable energy allowance, parking, and EV charging adjustments. DEP provides free onsite engineering consultations conducted by a DEP engineer to help building owners understand requirements and develop improvement plans. BPIPs require ASHRAE Standard 211 Level 2 energy audits, electrification readiness assessments, renewable energy feasibility assessments, and a Retrofit Plan with defined implementation timing for cost-effective energy improvement measures.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: First BPIP deadline in 2029; interim compliance deadlines 2028-2032; final compliance deadlines 2033-2036
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of covered commercial and multifamily buildings 25,000+ gross square feet in Montgomery County, including county-owned buildings, privately owned nonresidential buildings (grouped by size), and multifamily residential/mixed-use buildings, subject to county building energy performance requirements
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Implementation of energy improvement measures including operational upgrades, equipment replacement, control system optimization, electrification projects, renewable energy integration, and other building energy performance upgrades to meet interim and final EUI standards
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland only. Buildings in Montgomery County are exempt from the State's BEPS requirements and are subject only to County requirements.
requirements_list: Building must be a covered building under Montgomery County law (25,000+ gross square feet)
Buildings must benchmark energy use annually using ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager and report to DEP by June 1 each year
Buildings must benchmark for at least 3 years to establish a baseline; performance baseline calculated from highest two years of normalized net site EUI over 3-year baseline period
Buildings must meet interim performance standard by their interim deadline (2028-2032, depending on group)
Buildings must meet final performance standard based on building type by their final deadline (2033-2036, depending on group)
Buildings not meeting standards must file a Building Performance Improvement Plan (BPIP) no later than 90 days before the compliance documentation deadline; first BPIP deadline in 2029
BPIP requires a comprehensive energy audit per ASHRAE Standard 211 Level 2 covering full building scope including all tenant-controlled systems

BPIP audit must include system inventory and condition assessment, operational review and controls assessment, building operations staff engagement, and equipment replacement planning (10-year horizon)
BPIP must include electrification readiness assessment and onsite renewable energy feasibility assessment
BPIP Retrofit Plan must document all cost-effective energy improvement measures with defined implementation timing and cost-effectiveness analysis using simple payback method
Annual benchmarking data must be reported to DEP each year by June 1
Buildings on BPIP pathway must report annually by June 1 that committed retrofit measures were installed as planned
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Building owners must annually submit energy benchmarking data to DEP by June 1. If a building's energy use is above the interim or final standard, the owner may either reduce energy use to meet the standard or file a Building Performance Improvement Plan (BPIP). To file a BPIP, the owner must complete an ASHRAE Standard 211 Level 2 energy audit, assess electrification readiness and renewable energy feasibility, and submit a Retrofit Plan with defined implementation timing for all cost-effective energy improvement measures to DEP no later than 90 days before the compliance documentation deadline. DEP reviews the submission, may request clarifications, and approves based on demonstration of cost-effective measures and a complete, actionable plan. A standardized reporting format will be issued in advance of the 2029 deadline. Book a free engineering consultation via the DEP booking link or email Energy@MontgomeryCountyMD.gov for assistance.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Building Lot Termination (BLT) Easement program permanently retires an approved on-site waste disposal system (septic system) associated with a buildable lot on agricultural land. Because the lot has already proven it can support a residence, the easement payment for eliminating the development potential is higher than a standard TDR. BLTs can be purchased by the County (retiring the development rights) or sold directly by landowners to developers for use in designated receiving areas.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The County purchases BLT easements, paying landowners to permanently retire a buildable lot's development potential. Easement values are set annually on July 1 by the County Executive, who considers recent agricultural easement prices, TDR prices, and fair market value for agricultural land. BLTs may also be sold privately to developers for use in Life Science (LS), Transit Mixed-Use (TMX), or Commercial/Residential (CR) receiving zones.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of agricultural land in Montgomery County's Agricultural Reserve that has an approved septic system site plan for a buildable lot
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Compensation to landowners in exchange for permanently retiring a buildable lot and its associated development rights
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Land must be located in the Agricultural Reserve (AR) Zone in Montgomery County. Land must lie outside water and sewer categories 1, 2, and 3.
requirements_list: Land must be located in the Agricultural Reserve (AR) Zone
Property must be at least 50 acres; smaller properties may qualify if contiguous to other protected lands
At least 50 percent of the land must meet USDA Soil Classification Standards I–III or Woodland Classifications 1 and 2
Land must lie outside water and sewer categories 1, 2, and 3
Land must not be encumbered by Federal/State/County agricultural or conservation easements (except TDR easements)

Land must be able to achieve a percolation rate sufficient to support an individual on-site waste disposal system, as evidenced by a septic system site plan approved by the Department of Permitting Services
Any TDRs retained above the threshold of 1 TDR per 25 acres must be created/severed from the land prior to or simultaneously with BLT easement settlement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Mike Weyand at michael.weyand@montgomerycountymd.gov with questions about BLT easements or to explore options for your property.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants to help low-income households pay for burial and funeral costs. Administered through Housing Stabilization Services, the program is available to Montgomery County residents whose household income is below 60% of the Area Median Income.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $650 to help cover burial and funeral costs. Household income must be below 60% of the Area Median Income (e.g., $65,520 for a family of three). Additional eligibility criteria apply as determined by Housing Stabilization Services.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income individuals and families in Montgomery County needing help with burial and funeral costs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment of burial and funeral expenses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland residents.
requirements_list: Household income must be below 60% of the Area Median Income (e.g., $65,520 for a family of three)
Must meet additional eligibility criteria as determined by Housing Stabilization Services
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete an online service request at the Montgomery County 311 portal, or call 311 (or 240-777-0311 from outside Montgomery County) to request assistance.

structured_extraction.program_name: Burtonsville Enterprise Zone Property Tax Credits
structured_extraction.program_description: This regulation (Executive Regulation 6-14) establishes policies, procedures, and eligibility criteria for administering the Burtonsville Enterprise Zone in Montgomery County, including property tax credits available to businesses and property owners located within the zone.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property tax credits available to eligible businesses and property owners within the Burtonsville Enterprise Zone, administered under the policies and procedures set by Executive Regulation 6-14.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses and property owners within the Burtonsville Enterprise Zone in Montgomery County, Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax credits for eligible participants in the Burtonsville Enterprise Zone
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Burtonsville Enterprise Zone in Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Property or business must be located within the Burtonsville Enterprise Zone
Must meet eligibility criteria established in Executive Regulation 6-14
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Montgomery County Department of Economic Development for a copy of the regulation and application procedures.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Burtonsville Facade Improvement Program provides county funding to help property owners and locally owned businesses revitalize and improve the exterior appearance of commercial buildings in the Burtonsville area of Montgomery County. Improvements can include new facade structures, exterior siding and painting, LED lighting, parking lot repairs and resurfacing, ADA-compliant sidewalks, energy-efficient windows and doors, new signage, landscaping, and outdoor seating. The program aims to revitalize the Burtonsville commercial corridor, leveraging county investment to spur additional private investment — for example, a $240,000 county investment at 15420 Old Columbia Pike spurred nearly $296,000 in privately funded improvements, a separate $240,000 county investment spurred $250,000 in privately funded improvements at one site, a $180,000 county investment leveraged $223,000 in private/owner-funded improvements at another, a $227,500 county investment at 15440 Old Columbia Pike spurred nearly $240,000 in privately funded improvements, and a $155,000 county investment at 15530 Old Columbia Pike spurred $168,400 in additional private improvements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: County investment of up to $240,000 in facade improvement funds per project to support facade and exterior improvements to commercial properties. The program co-invests with property owners to fund exterior building upgrades, and is designed to leverage additional private investment — for example, a $240,000 county investment at 15420 Old Columbia Pike spurred nearly $296,000 in privately funded improvements, a $240,000 county investment spurred $250,000 in privately funded improvements at another site, a $180,000 county investment leveraged $223,000 in private/owner-funded improvements at a third site, a $227,500 county investment at 15440 Old Columbia Pike spurred nearly $240,000 in privately funded improvements, and a $155,000 county investment at 15530 Old Columbia Pike spurred $168,400 in additional private improvements.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Commercial property owners and locally owned businesses in the Burtonsville area of Montgomery County seeking to revitalize and improve building exteriors.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Facade structure upgrades, exterior siding, wall repairs, cleaning and painting, LED lighting for parking lots and buildings, new business and shopping center signage (including backlit and monument signs), ADA-compliant sidewalks, energy-efficient windows and doors, landscaping, outdoor seating, and parking lot repair and resurfacing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Burtonsville area of Montgomery County, Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County operates four Business Innovation Centers that provide incubator space and support services to help businesses grow. Facilities offer business consulting, legal and accounting resources, intellectual property and commercialization assistance, and access to state and county funding programs. Centers are located near federal, academic, and nonprofit research agencies and are part of the Maryland Global Gateway Soft Landing Program for international companies. The program offers virtual and lab workspace options for businesses in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Businesses receive access to incubator/office space (virtual or lab), business consulting, legal and accounting resources, intellectual property and commercialization assistance, and connections to state and county funding programs. Four centers focus on life sciences (Germantown), MedTech (Rockville), general office/all-industry (Silver Spring), and AI-enhanced technologies (North Bethesda) respectively.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Business owners, entrepreneurs, and established companies — including international companies — seeking to grow in Montgomery County, MD, especially those in life sciences, MedTech, high-tech, and AI-related industries.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Incubator office space (virtual or lab facilities), business consulting, legal and accounting resources, intellectual property and commercialization support, and access to funding programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. Must be located in or planning to relocate to Montgomery County. Facilities located in Germantown, Rockville, Silver Spring, and North Bethesda.
requirements_list: Copy of articles of incorporation or similar company structure documentation
Business plan or business proposal
Current financial information (revenues, grants, funds raised)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Innovation Center Intake Form (PDF available on the page) with company information, financial data, and supporting documents, or request a tour through the county website. Contact the Business Center at BusinessCenter@MontgomeryCountyMD.gov for questions.

structured_extraction.program_name: COC Common Area Assistance Loan Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: A loan fund administered by Montgomery County's Department of Housing and Community Affairs (DHCA) that provides interest-free financial assistance to common ownership communities (COCs) — including homeowner associations, residential condominiums, and cooperative housing projects — in Montgomery County that are experiencing financial hardship and need help funding urgent health or safety repairs in common areas. Eligible projects include repairs to water supply lines, elevators, fire suppression systems, stormwater drainage, facades, balconies, sidewalks, pathways, and parking lots, as well as general common area improvements. The program also supports predevelopment construction-related services.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Interest-free loans of up to $500,000, repaid over up to 15 years, secured by a pledge of current and future COC assets. A 1% loan commitment fee on the total approved loan amount is required. DHCA loans are subordinate to other loans. The COC must contribute at least 20% of total project costs. Funds are released as progress payments based on invoices. Montgomery County approved $1.23 million for FY2025 and $1.85 million for FY2026 (July 1, 2025–June 30, 2026). Applications are accepted on a rolling basis beginning November 20, 2024.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis beginning November 20, 2024; applications accepted until available loan funds are committed
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowner associations, residential condominiums, and cooperative housing projects (Common Ownership Communities) in Montgomery County that are at least 51% owner-occupied, fully compliant with all County regulatory requirements, and in need of funding for critical common area health or safety repairs or general common area improvements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Critical repairs or replacements in common areas to address health, safety, or occupancy risks — such as failing water supply lines, elevators, fire suppression systems, stormwater drainage, facades, balconies, sidewalks, pathways, and parking lots — as well as general common area improvements and predevelopment construction-related services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to County-regulated Common Ownership Communities (COCs) located in Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a common ownership community (homeowner association, condominium, or cooperative)
Must demonstrate financial hardship
Repairs must be for immediate health or safety issues documented by professional assessments or government citations
At least 51% of the COC's total units must be owner-occupied
The governing board must be fully compliant with all County regulatory requirements
COC governing board or agent must complete annual Commission on Common Ownership Communities registration

Must provide a certified engineering or contractor analysis/inspection of physical issues; a reserve study; a professional capital needs assessment; an engineering analysis defining the scope of work; and contractor cost estimates

Must submit a complete financial documentation package including audited financials, current reserve fund budget reports, HOA/condo fee delinquency assessment, existing loan details, and documented efforts to raise special assessments or other funding
The COC must have the financial capacity to contribute 20% of total project costs and pay a 1% loan commitment fee on the total loan amount
The COC must maintain its operating budget, adhere to the maintenance schedule, and stay current on all existing loan repayments
Application must include a scope of work, cost estimates, and expected funding sources
AIA Forms required for construction loans
Construction/rehabilitation schedule and cost estimate required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Contact the Office of Common Ownership Communities (OCOC) at 240-777-0311 to discuss needs, eligibility requirements, and procedures. 2. Download and review the document checklist. 3. Prepare all required documents. 4. Fill out the online loan application (Wufoo online form linked on the program page) and upload all required documents. DHCA reviews the application and makes lending decisions based on eligibility, priority of need, and available funds. The process involves multiple phases: Loan Commitment Review, Loan Closing, and Construction Loans phases with documented requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Montgomery County and State subsidized transportation program providing curb-to-curb taxicab service, designed as a supplement to Montgomery County's local transportation services. Helps transport low-income seniors (age 65 or older) and low-income individuals with disabilities (ages 18-64) who are county residents to medical and/or personal appointments. Subsidy assistance is provided on a sliding fee scale based on total household income. Travel is allowed for any purpose within Montgomery County, and for medical reasons to approved facilities in Designated Service Areas outside the county.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Subsidized curb-to-curb taxi trips on a sliding fee scale based on household income. Participants receive a CNR swipe card with monthly subsidy applied. For a household of one, participants pay between $5.25 and $30.00 per $60 of value loaded onto a swipe card, depending on annual income. All trips must begin and end in Montgomery County, with special exceptions for approved medical facilities in Designated Service Areas outside the county, including Baltimore, Prince George's County, Northern Virginia, and Washington, DC.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income adults age 65 or older, or low-income adults ages 18-64 with a disability who are Montgomery County residents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Transportation to medical and/or personal appointments via participating taxi companies; any-purpose travel within Montgomery County, and medical transportation to approved facilities in Designated Service Areas outside the county (Baltimore, Prince George's County, Northern Virginia, and Washington, DC).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a current Montgomery County resident (PO Box not acceptable; proof of residency within last 6 months required). All trips must begin and end in Montgomery County. Special exceptions allow transportation to approved medical facilities in Designated Service Areas outside the county, including Baltimore, Prince George's County, Northern Virginia, and Washington, DC.
requirements_list: Must be low income and at least 65 years of age, OR
Must be low income and 18-64 years of age with a disability
Must be a Montgomery County resident (PO Box not acceptable)
Proof of current Montgomery County residency (within last 6 months)
Proof of age (government-issued ID, birth certificate, etc.)
Household income documentation for all family members
Ages 18-64 must have documented disability certified by a Licensed Physician, PA, CRNP, or psychologist
Completed Disability Certification Form required for ages 18-64
Passport-size or recent photograph (recommended for swipe card)
Re-certification required every two years
Must have valid CNR swipe card in possession during trips
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 301-948-5409, Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. for information on how to apply. Complete the CNR Application Form and submit with required documentation (proof of age, residency, income, and disability certification if applicable) via fax, email (cnrorder@montgomerycountymd.gov), or mail/hand-delivery to Montgomery County, 101 Monroe Street, 5th Floor, Rockville, MD 20850. A disability certification form must be completed by a licensed healthcare provider for applicants ages 18-64. Re-certification is required every two years; recertification forms must be submitted within 30 days of the recertification letter.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides free Capital Bikeshare memberships and a free helmet to income-eligible residents or workers in Montgomery County who are already receiving assistance through federal, state, or Montgomery County social services programs. Qualifying low-income residents in the Washington DC metro area, including Montgomery County, may also access an annual Capital Bikeshare membership for $5, significantly discounted from the standard price. The program gives access to over 4,500 bikes and 500+ stations across the Washington, D.C. metropolitan area.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Qualified individuals receive a free Capital Bikeshare membership and a free helmet, giving access to over 4,500 bikes and 500+ stations across the Washington, D.C. metropolitan area. Alternatively, qualifying low-income residents may access an annual membership for $5, significantly discounted from the standard price.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Income-eligible individuals living or working in Montgomery County who receive assistance through programs such as TANF, SSI/SSDI, SNAP, WIC, LIHEAP, Medicaid, or partner programs, as well as low-income residents in the Capital Bikeshare service area including Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free bikeshare membership and helmet, or discounted annual bike-share membership, for personal transportation use.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must live or work in Montgomery County, Maryland. Program is part of the broader Capital Bikeshare service area in the Washington, D.C. metropolitan region.
requirements_list: Must live or work in Montgomery County
Must currently receive assistance through a qualifying federal, state, or Montgomery County social services program (e.g., TANF, SSI/SSDI, SNAP, WIC, LIHEAP, Medicaid, or approved partner programs)
Must meet qualifying criteria (income-based eligibility)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register online at the Capital Bikeshare for All registration page, or contact Montgomery County Commuter Services by email at Commuter.Services@montgomerycountymd.gov or by phone at 240-777-8380.

structured_extraction.program_description: Allows landlords of rent-stabilized properties in Montgomery County to request a temporary rent surcharge to recover the cost of major permanent structural improvements made to a property. Routine maintenance and repairs do not qualify.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Landlords may add a temporary surcharge to monthly rent to recover capital improvement costs. For building-wide improvements, the surcharge is divided equally among all units, prorated over at least 96 months, and cannot exceed 20% of base rent. For unit-specific improvements, the surcharge is shared among affected units, prorated over at least 60 months, and cannot exceed 15% of base rent. The surcharge is separate from base rent and annual rent increases, does not change over time, and cannot be applied mid-lease. Landlords may request an extension by submitting a Certificate of Continuation at least 90 days before the surcharge expires.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landlords of rent-stabilized (regulated) rental properties in Montgomery County who have completed or plan to complete major permanent structural improvements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Recovery of costs for permanent structural capital improvements that enhance or rehabilitate housing units.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland only.
requirements_list: Property must be a regulated rental property
Improvements must be permanent structural alterations that enhance or rehabilitate the housing unit
Routine maintenance and repairs do not qualify
For retroactive CIPs (health and safety emergencies), landlord must file within 30 days of completion of work
Applications and required documentation must be submitted via the Rental Housing Portal
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application and all required documentation through the Montgomery County Rental Housing Portal. Sample application forms are available on the Applications and Forms page.

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County Fire and Rescue Service accepts donated used vehicles for firefighter training. Donors receive a tax deduction based on the Kelly Blue Book value of their vehicle, and free local towing is available for Montgomery County residents.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Donors receive a tax deduction up to the Kelly Blue Book value of the donated vehicle. Free local towing is available for Montgomery County residents.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents who want to donate a used vehicle to support firefighter training
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Donated vehicles are used for firefighter training exercises
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Montgomery County residents; free towing limited to local/Montgomery County area
requirements_list: Clear title required
Tags required
Vehicle must be available for donation to firefighter training
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Captain Jaymie Birney by email or call the Fire & Rescue Training Academy at 240-773-8218 to coordinate the donation. Arrange drop-off or free local towing if needed.

structured_extraction.program_description: Care for Kids provides a medical home for uninsured children in Montgomery County who are not eligible for Medicaid or other health insurance programs. Regardless of immigration status, eligible children can receive well and sick care, prescriptions, and limited specialty care through partnerships with Kaiser Permanente, Community Clinic Inc, Spanish Catholic Center, school-based health centers, private doctors, hospitals, and other providers. There are no fees or costs associated with the program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free medical care including well and sick visits, prescriptions, and limited specialty care for eligible uninsured children in Montgomery County. There are no fees or costs associated with the program. Coverage is provided regardless of immigration status.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Uninsured, low-income children in Montgomery County who are not eligible for Medicaid or other health insurance programs, regardless of immigration status.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Medical care including well and sick visits, prescription drugs, and limited specialty care.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County residents only.
requirements_list: Must be a Montgomery County resident
Must be a child
Must be uninsured
Must not be eligible for Medicaid (Medical Assistance) or other health insurance
Must meet financial eligibility requirements
No immigration status requirement
Must provide proof of income, proof of identity, and proof of Montgomery County residence
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the fillable application form, print it, and return it to the Office of Eligibility and Support Services (OESS). OESS will confirm eligibility. For more information, call 301-628-3450.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides dental care to uninsured children in Montgomery County who are not eligible for Maryland Children's Health Program (MCHP) or MCHP Premium and whose family income is at or below 250% of the Federal Poverty Level.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Dental care coverage for eligible uninsured children. Benefits can be applied for online through the Community Connect Portal starting January 1, 2025.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Uninsured children from birth through age 18 who are Montgomery County residents with family income no greater than 250% of the Federal Poverty Level and who are not eligible for MCHP or MCHP Premium.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Dental care services for eligible children.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Montgomery County resident.
requirements_list: Montgomery County resident
Ages newborn through 18
Child must be uninsured and not eligible for MCHP or MCHP Premium
Family income no greater than 250% of the Federal Poverty Level
Documents verifying parentage or legal guardianship (driver's license, passport, or other legal picture ID)

Documents verifying identity of the minor (active Care for Kids card or eligibility letter, plus one of: MCPS ID, MCPS enrollment form, birth certificate, passport, physician's certificate, baptismal/church certification, hospital certificate, parent's notarized affidavit, birth registration, or other legal/notarized ID)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online through the Community Connect Portal at communityconnect.montgomerycountymd.gov. Bring required documents to the initial appointment.

structured_extraction.program_name: Care for Kids and Senior Dental Programs (COVID-19 relief aggregation)
structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County safety-net programs that provide access to medical and dental services for low-income, uninsured families and individuals who do not qualify for State and Federal health programs. Includes three programs: Montgomery Cares, Care for Kids, and Senior Dental.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Access to medical and dental services for uninsured, low-income residents who are not eligible for State or Federal health programs. Programs include: Care for Kids (dental care for children), Senior Dental (dental care for seniors), and Montgomery Cares (general health coverage). Specific benefit amounts not stated on this page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income, uninsured families and individuals in Montgomery County who are not eligible for State or Federal programs, including children (Care for Kids), seniors (Senior Dental), pregnant individuals, and other uninsured adults (Montgomery Cares).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Medical and dental services, including dental care for children and seniors, and general health coverage assistance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must reside in Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be low-income
Must be uninsured (no active health insurance coverage — self-declaration under penalty of perjury)
Must not be eligible for State or Federal health programs
Household income documentation required
Employment/earned income information required
Unearned income documentation (child support, Social Security, pensions, unemployment, etc.) required
Social Security numbers for household members required
Valid proof of residence in Montgomery County required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download the fillable application (English or Spanish) from the Montgomery County website. Complete the application with household member information, income and employment documentation, health insurance status verification, and all required disclosures. Sign the attestation under penalty of perjury. Email the completed application to the Office of Eligibility and Support Services at OESS.MoCo@montgomerycountymd.gov. For eligibility questions, call 240-777-1003.

structured_extraction.program_name: Caregiver Support Program - U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (Veterans Only)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Program of General Caregiver Support Services (PGCSS) provides resources, education, and support to caregivers of veterans. The veteran does not need a service-connected condition and may have served during any era. Enrolled caregivers get access to education and training (including courses at local VA medical centers), support services, and VA home and community-based care.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides education, training (including courses at local VA medical centers), support services, and access to VA home and community-based care for caregivers of veterans.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Caregivers of veterans, regardless of the veteran's era of service or whether the condition requiring care is service-connected.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Education and training, support services, VA home and community-based care.
requirements_list: Caregiver of a veteran
Veteran may have served during any era
Veteran does not need a service-connected condition for which the caregiver is needed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Enroll in PGCSS through the VA. Contact the DC VA Medical Center at 202-745-8000 x 57797 for local assistance.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free program that helps applicants navigate complex commercial permit processes in Montgomery County. A case facilitator acts as a liaison between the applicant and the Department of Permitting Services (DPS), helping to coordinate plan reviews, schedule inspections, resolve code compliance issues, and keep projects on track from application through final inspection.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free case facilitation services for complex commercial projects. A case facilitator is assigned to guide the applicant through design consultation meetings, permit applications, plan reviews, inspections, and project finalization. The facilitator coordinates communication between all DPS divisions and keeps stakeholders informed of project status.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Applicants with complex commercial projects, new or major renovations of places of worship, and county-wide strategic economic development projects in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable — program provides process facilitation and technical assistance, not direct funding.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available for projects located within Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Project must be a complex commercial project, a new or major renovation of a place of worship, or a county-wide strategic economic development project (other projects may be admitted at DPS discretion or by written request).
Applicant must schedule and attend a design consultation meeting.

Applicant must bring a detailed project description, architectural and/or civil plans, construction phasing plans, project timeline(s), professional design team, and a list of code compliance concerns or questions.
Applicant must provide an agenda for the design consultation meeting.
Applicant must keep meeting minutes and submit them to DPS within 5 business days after the meeting.
All permit applications and plans must be submitted electronically through DPS eServices.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Submit a written request (if not automatically eligible) with a detailed project description, construction phasing, current/planned uses, code compliance obstacles, point of contact, and estimated timeline. 2. Schedule a design consultation meeting — a case facilitator will be assigned. 3. Attend the design consultation meeting with required documents and your design team. 4. Submit permit applications and plans electronically through DPS eServices with assistance from your case facilitator. 5. The facilitator monitors the project through inspections and final permit approval.

structured_extraction.program_description: A service that guides entrepreneurs through opening and operating a home or center-based child care program in Montgomery County, including help with business plans, marketing, record keeping, and budgeting.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-on-one business counseling to help entrepreneurs start and run a child care program. Staff provide guidance on business plans, marketing, record keeping, and budgeting.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Entrepreneurs looking to open or operate a home or center-based child care program in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business planning, marketing, record keeping, and budgeting for child care programs
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Email Kenia Almendarez at Kenia.Almendarez@MontgomeryCountyMD.gov for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Child Care Support Services - Coaching and Consultation
structured_extraction.program_description: Free coaching and consultation services for early childhood educators in Montgomery County. Services include one-on-one coaching, infant and early childhood mental health consultation, and health consultation from a registered nurse. Coaches and consultants work onsite to help educators improve classroom practices, routines, and children's social-emotional development.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free onsite consultation, teacher coaching, classroom modeling, and reflection sessions. Services include: one-on-one coaching, strength-based assessments, action plan creation, modeling and discussing teaching strategies, identifying resources and referrals, infant and early childhood mental health consultation, and health and safety consultation from a registered nurse.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Early childhood educators and child care programs in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Improving classroom environments, teaching practices, daily routines, lesson plans, social-emotional development support, and health and safety practices in child care settings
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 240-777-GROW (4769) to schedule a consultation.

structured_extraction.program_name: Child Care Support Services - Family Support
structured_extraction.program_description: Free, personalized consultations from bilingual Family Resource Specialists who help Montgomery County families find licensed child care, learn about play-based programs, navigate tuition assistance applications, and connect with parenting workshops and community resources.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Families receive free one-on-one consultations (in person, virtual, or by phone) with trained bilingual counselors who help identify licensed child care, apply for tuition assistance programs (Child Care Scholarship, Working Parents Assistance, EquiCare Grant), and connect to parenting workshops, Family Involvement Center sessions, and community resources.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Jennifer Ferreira, Kim Choi (Family Resource Specialists)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with young children in Montgomery County seeking child care options, tuition assistance, or parenting support
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Consultations, referrals, and application assistance for child care and tuition assistance; free parenting workshops and family learning sessions
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to families in Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a family residing in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the program to schedule a one-on-one consultation in person, virtually, or by phone. Counselors then guide families through locating child care and applying for relevant assistance programs.

structured_extraction.program_name: Child Care Support Services - Professional Development
structured_extraction.program_description: Free or low-cost professional development program for early childhood workers in Montgomery County. Offers training, career counseling, mentoring, and financial reimbursements to help child care providers advance their skills, fulfill licensing requirements, and pursue credentials such as the Maryland Child Care Credential, CDA, and higher education.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides free or low-cost MSDE-approved training (in English and Spanish, in-person, virtual, and hybrid), career pathway counseling, peer-to-peer mentoring, reimbursements and scholarships for CDA credentials and renewals, accreditation material reimbursements, and reimbursement for translation of foreign credentials. No-cost live interpretation of classes is available upon request.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care providers and early childhood workers in Montgomery County, MD seeking professional development and career advancement.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training costs, CDA credential and renewal expenses, accreditation materials, and translation of foreign credentials.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to child care providers and early childhood workers in Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a child care provider or early childhood workforce member
Must be located in or serve Montgomery County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Request onsite presentations via a request form; register for MSDE Core of Knowledge training through the registration portal; complete reimbursement forms for CDA expenses, accreditation materials, or foreign credential translation; request or sign up to be a peer mentor via online forms.

structured_extraction.program_name: Child Care Support Services - Quality Enhancement
structured_extraction.program_description: Free quality enhancement support for licensed child care centers, letter of compliance programs, and registered family child care programs in Montgomery County. The program provides expert coaching, peer mentoring, group sessions, and multilingual support to help providers improve child care quality, reach higher Maryland EXCELS levels, obtain accreditation, and strengthen business operations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free supports include: expert quality enhancement coaches who help develop and implement individualized action plans; a business coach for owners and administrators; peer mentors; group sessions; multilingual support; and reimbursement for accreditation materials. Services are available onsite and virtually.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed child care centers, letter of compliance programs, and registered family child care programs in Montgomery County seeking to improve quality and/or obtain accreditation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Quality improvement activities, reaching Maryland EXCELS levels 3–5, obtaining or renewing national and state accreditation (NAEYC, NAFCC, MSDE), leadership development, business coaching, and reimbursement for accreditation materials.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a licensed child care center, letter of compliance program, or registered family child care program in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Child Care Support Services Quality Enhancement team to get started. Consultants will guide providers through developing an action plan. Accreditation materials reimbursement requires submitting a reimbursement form (available on the program page).

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides 29 dedicated spaces in public county facilities to expand affordable, high-quality child care in underserved communities. Programs are county-subsidized and must meet high-quality standards including accreditation and Maryland EXCELS levels 3–5.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: County-subsidized space in public facilities for child care providers, accessible through a competitive bid process. Programs receive ongoing monitoring and support to maintain quality benchmarks. Providers must achieve accreditation and reach levels 3–5 in the Maryland EXCELS quality rating system.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care providers seeking subsidized space in public facilities to serve underserved communities in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating a child care program in county-provided public space
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland — underserved communities
requirements_list: Must meet accreditation requirements
Must achieve levels 3–5 in Maryland EXCELS quality rating system
Must participate in ongoing monitoring to ensure quality benchmarks are maintained
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Programs are selected through a competitive bid process. Email Tamieka Thomasson at Tamieka.Thomasson@MontgomeryCountyMD.gov for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program helps parents involved in separation, divorce, and child custody cases resolve disputes about their children — such as where the children will live, how decisions will be made, and visitation arrangements — through a free, structured mediation process rather than going to trial.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A single free three-hour mediation session conducted by a Maryland-certified mediator. The session takes place within Family Division Services, and the outcome is immediately reported to a Family Magistrate at a Status Hearing. If the parties reach an agreement, it is drawn up as a consent custody/access order.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Parents with open cases in the Montgomery County Circuit Court seeking court decisions about child custody and access.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Mediation services to help parents create a parenting plan covering living arrangements, visitation, holiday and vacation scheduling, communication, transportation of children, and emergency planning.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to parents with cases filed in the Montgomery County Circuit Court.
requirements_list: Must have an open case filed in the Montgomery County Circuit Court involving child custody or access.
Cases with active protective orders due to domestic violence are not eligible.
Each party must complete a comprehensive intake interview before mediation begins.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The court orders parties to participate in the program. A comprehensive intake interview is conducted with each party. Parties then attend a single three-hour mediation session at Family Division Services (South Tower, First Floor, Room 1500). Immediately after the session, the parties report the outcome to a Family Magistrate at a Status Hearing.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Child Investment Fund allocates money each year based on the number of babies born in Montgomery County. Funds grow in an interest-bearing account over time. When a child turns 18 and is a county resident, they can withdraw from the fund to pay for vocational or educational expenses, invest in a county business, purchase property in the county, or save for retirement. Payments are made progressively based on wealth and income at the time of application.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A direct financial benefit paid out of an interest-bearing fund to eligible residents when they turn 18. The amount is based on accumulated county allocations over time. Funds can be used for education, vocational training, business investment in the county, property purchase in the county, or retirement savings. Payments are scaled progressively by income and wealth at the time of application.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents of Montgomery County who were born in the county and turn 18 years old
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Vocational or educational expenses, investment in a business in Montgomery County, purchasing property in Montgomery County, or retirement investments
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a resident of Montgomery County at the time of application and age 18
requirements_list: Must be 18 years old
Must be a resident of Montgomery County at time of application
Payments made progressively based on wealth and income
