structured_extraction.program_description: The Child Tax Credit (CTC) provides families with a tax credit of up to $2,000 per qualifying child under age 17. Up to $1,700 is refundable, meaning eligible families can receive money back even if they owe little or no federal taxes. The credit phases out at higher income levels.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $2,000 per qualifying child under age 17 as a tax credit. Up to $1,700 is refundable (returned as a tax refund if the credit exceeds taxes owed). The credit phases out by $50 for every $1,000 of income above $200,000 (head of household) or $400,000 (married filing jointly). A separate $500 non-refundable credit is available for qualifying dependents who do not meet the CTC requirements, including children with an Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (ITIN).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and families with qualifying children under age 17 who have earned income above $2,500 and a valid Social Security number (SSN) or Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (ITIN).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduces federal income tax owed; excess refundable portion (up to $1,700) is returned to the filer as a tax refund.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Federal tax credit available to eligible taxpayers nationwide, including Maryland residents.
requirements_list: Must have earned income greater than $2,500
You and your spouse must have a Social Security number (SSN) or Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (ITIN)
Qualifying child must be under age 17 on December 31, 2024
Qualifying child must live with you in the U.S. for more than half the year
Qualifying child must have a valid SSN (ITIN not accepted for the CTC)
Qualifying child must be considered your dependent for tax filing purposes

Qualifying child must meet the relationship test: son, daughter, grandchild, stepchild, adopted child, sibling, step-sibling, half-sibling or their descendant, or foster child placed by a government agency
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: File a 2024 federal tax return and include Schedule 8812 'Additional Child Tax Credit.' Free tax filing assistance is available through the Volunteer Income Tax Assistance (VITA) program.

structured_extraction.program_name: Child and Adolescent Behavioral Health Services
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides family-focused outpatient mental health services to children, adolescents, and their families to help address trauma, emotional, behavioral, and substance use issues. Services include behavioral health assessment, diagnostic evaluation, individual and family and group psychotherapy, psychiatric evaluation, medication management, substance use screening, clinical case management, and some school-based services in Montgomery County Public Schools (MCPS).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Outpatient mental health and substance use services provided on a sliding-scale fee basis. No one is denied services based on ability to pay. Clients with Care For Kids are charged $5 per session. Services include therapy, psychiatric evaluation, medication management, and case management.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents aged 5 to 18 who have Medicaid or no health insurance, and youth ages 18 to 20 enrolled in MCPS.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Mental health assessment, therapy, psychiatric evaluation, medication management, substance use screening, and clinical case management services for children and adolescents.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Montgomery County, Maryland resident.
requirements_list: Must be a Montgomery County resident
Must be between 5 and 18 years of age (or 18–20 if enrolled in MCPS)
Must have Medicaid or no health insurance
Must provide proof of residency and proof of income or Medicaid card
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 240-777-1450 or 240-777-1432 to schedule an appointment. Bring proof of residency and proof of income or Medicaid card to the appointment.

structured_extraction.program_description: A pre-tax benefit account that lets Montgomery County employees set aside money from each paycheck before taxes to pay for eligible dependent care expenses that allow the employee (and their spouse) to work. Qualifying individuals include children under 13 and dependents or spouses who are incapable of self-care. Administered by Voya.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Employees elect an annual contribution amount that is deducted from each paycheck before taxes. After incurring eligible dependent care expenses, employees submit a claim with supporting documentation to Voya for reimbursement. Employees have until April 30 of the following year to submit claims, and until March 15 following the end of the calendar year to incur expenses. Unused funds are forfeited. The account is separate from the Health Care FSA and contributions cannot be transferred between accounts. Maximum contribution is $7,500/year (single or married filing jointly) or $3,750 (married filing separately).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Must enroll each year during open enrollment
structured_extraction.program_audience: Benefit-eligible Montgomery County Government employees with qualifying dependent care expenses
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eligible dependent care expenses such as day care, elder care, before/after school care, babysitter fees, and nanny or au pair costs for children under age 13 or incapacitated adults, that enable the employee (and spouse) to work.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Montgomery County government employees.
requirements_list: Must be a benefit-eligible Montgomery County Government (MCG) employee
Must enroll each year to participate
Dependent care expenses must enable the employee to work
Child must be under age 13, OR adult dependent/spouse must reside with employee more than 6 months per year and be mentally or physically incapable of self-care
Must incur expenses by March 15 following the end of the plan year
Must submit claims by April 30 following the end of the plan year
Keep receipts for IRS substantiation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Enroll each year during the open enrollment period. Elect a contribution amount to be deducted pre-tax from each paycheck. After incurring eligible expenses, submit a claim with supporting documentation to Voya for reimbursement.

structured_extraction.program_name: Childhood Lead Poisoning Prevention and Environmental Case Management Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides home-based case management services to families of children with elevated blood lead levels or moderate to severe asthma. Services include environmental health education, help identifying and reducing lead and asthma hazards in the home, care coordination, referrals for free lead abatement, cleaning supplies, pest management items, and connections to community resources.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Home visits with environmental health education, case management, referrals for free lead abatement services at no cost to the family or property owner, cleaning supplies, and pest management items provided throughout enrollment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families of children age 19 or younger who are Montgomery County residents with elevated blood lead levels (3.5 µg/dL or greater) or a diagnosis of moderate to severe asthma, and who are enrolled in or eligible for Medicaid/CHIP.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Environmental case management, home education, lead abatement referrals, cleaning supplies, and pest management support.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Montgomery County, Maryland resident.
requirements_list: Child must be 19 years old or younger
Must be a Montgomery County resident
Must have a diagnosis of moderate to severe asthma or an elevated blood lead level of 3.5 µg/dL or greater
Must be enrolled in or eligible for Medicaid/CHIP
For lead program: child must spend 10 or more hours per week in the location where lead exposure occurred
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the program at 240-777-3380 or submit a referral from the Maryland Department of Environment, a medical provider, community organization, school, or local daycare facility. The Environmental Case Manager (Nurse) will provide information on any documentation needed.

structured_extraction.program_name: Children with Special Health Needs Care Coordination Program (Children's Medical Services)
structured_extraction.program_description: Helps low-income, uninsured families get special medical care for children with chronic medical conditions or disabilities. A care coordinator links families to needed services and helps manage the child's care needs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: No-cost care coordination that covers specialist visits, hospitalizations, surgeries, medications, therapies, lab work, x-rays, and medical equipment for eligible children. There are no fees for this service.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income, uninsured families with children (birth to 21 years old) who have chronic illnesses or disabilities and live in Montgomery County or Prince George's County, MD.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Specialist visits, hospitalizations, surgeries, medications, therapies, lab work, x-rays, and medical equipment for children with special health needs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a resident of Montgomery County or Prince George's County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Child must be between birth and 21 years of age
Child must have a diagnosed or suspected chronic illness or disability requiring evaluation and/or treatment
Child must be a resident of Montgomery County or Prince George's County
Family income must be no greater than 200% of the federal poverty level
Child must not qualify for any other health insurance, or have insurance that does not meet the child's special medical needs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The child's medical provider may make a referral to the program. Families can also call the Care Coordinator at 301-628-3487 with questions about next steps. The Care Coordinator will provide information about required documents.

structured_extraction.program_description: Free classes that help permanent residents prepare for the U.S. naturalization (citizenship) test and interview. Classes cover U.S. history, civics, and English reading, writing, and speaking skills needed to pass the citizenship exam. Offered in-person and online formats in Montgomery County, MD, and accessible on smartphones, tablets, or computers. Winter 2026 session ran from late January through early April; a Spring session is expected.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free citizenship preparation classes offered in two formats: online (Tuesdays 7:00–9:00 pm) and in-person at the Gaithersburg Library (Saturdays 10:15 am–1:15 pm). Classes cover U.S. history, civics, and English language skills. Available online via phone, tablet, or computer. Winter 2026 session ran from late January through early April. Students may register for only one class.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Registration for WINTER 2026 classes is now closed. Check again later for information about our Spring session.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents aged 18 or older who are lawful permanent residents (green card holders) interested in applying for U.S. citizenship and wanting to prepare for the naturalization test and interview.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Preparation for the U.S. naturalization test and interview, including U.S. history, civics, and English reading, writing, and speaking skills.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Montgomery County, Maryland resident.
requirements_list: Must be a permanent resident for at least four years (or two years if married to a U.S. citizen)
Must be a Montgomery County, MD resident
Must be 18 years of age or older
All classes are taught in English; at least basic English required
Students may only register for one class
Interested in applying for U.S. citizenship
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register online using the registration form linked on the program page. Classes fill up quickly; if full, applicants are directed to classes offered by other providers in Montgomery County.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Montgomery County program that provides financial incentives to buyers and providers of electricity produced by clean, renewable sources. The Director of Environmental Protection administers the program, and the Director of Finance may make payments to buyers or providers of qualifying electricity. The program rewards residents and businesses in Montgomery County for using clean energy, established by Bill 39-04, effective June 17, 2005.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial incentives (payments) to buyers or providers of electricity generated by clean renewable energy sources. The Director of Finance may make payments to qualifying buyers or providers. Specific reward amounts are not detailed in available sources.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents, businesses, and providers of clean renewable electricity in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rewards for purchasing or providing electricity generated by clean renewable sources; supporting clean energy adoption
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must purchase electricity produced by clean renewable sources
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Montgomery County Council Office or Department of Environmental Protection for details. Established by Bill 39-04, effective June 17, 2005.

structured_extraction.program_name: Clean Water Montgomery Watershed Restoration and Outreach Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This grant program funds public outreach, stewardship, and community-based water quality restoration projects in Montgomery County. Projects should educate and engage residents in watershed improvement while achieving measurable water quality impacts and sustainable behavior change. The program is administered by the Chesapeake Bay Trust on behalf of Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant awards fund community-based restoration projects, litter reduction efforts, public outreach and stewardship, and water quality monitoring. Award amounts are set each year based on available funds. Match is encouraged but not required; projects with match or in-kind services are given preference.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Typically, the fall of each year
structured_extraction.program_audience: 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations such as local watershed groups, community associations, service and civic groups, and faith-based organizations that include at least one partner representing a stakeholder group based in Montgomery County, Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Community-based restoration design and construction on nonprofit-owned property, litter reduction, public outreach and stewardship to educate residents on water quality improvement, and community-based water quality monitoring.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must include at least one partner representing a stakeholder group based in Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization
Must include at least one partner representing a stakeholder group based in Montgomery County, Maryland
Projects should achieve measurable water quality impacts and sustainable behavior change
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through an online system managed by the Chesapeake Bay Trust. Visit the CBT website at cbtrust.org/grants/cleanwatermontgomery for current program status and to apply.

structured_extraction.program_description: CATS provides inmates at Montgomery County detention facilities with behavioral health screening, assessment, suicide prevention, post-booking diversion opportunities, and linkage to community or in-house service providers. It also helps inmates returning to the community develop a comprehensive transition plan that addresses their behavioral health needs, including mental health, substance abuse, housing, vocational, family reintegration, and education support. Some services are billable while others are provided at no cost.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: No-cost behavioral health screening, clinical assessment, suicide risk evaluation, post-booking diversion opportunities, service planning, and discharge/transition planning for inmates at Montgomery County detention facilities. Includes linkage to community or in-house service providers. Transition services are provided for inmates within 30–60 days of release. Some services may be billable.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Incoming inmates and individuals preparing for release from the Montgomery County Detention Center or Correctional Facility who have behavioral health, mental health, substance abuse, or co-occurring disorders.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Behavioral health screening, clinical assessment, suicide prevention, diversion referrals, in-custody treatment linkage, and reentry transition planning including mental health, substance abuse, housing, vocational, family reintegration, and education support.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County residents or individuals who are homeless with service connections to Montgomery County, held at the Montgomery County Detention Center or Correctional Facility.
requirements_list: Must be an inmate at the Montgomery County Detention Center or Correctional Facility
For transition services: must be a documented Montgomery County resident or homeless with service connections to Montgomery County
For transition services: must be receiving behavioral health or substance abuse treatment while incarcerated
For transition services: must be within 30–60 days of release date
For transition services: must not be involved with other case management programs such as Drug Court, Pre-Release, DOCR Reentry Services, or community-based case management
For reentry services: must be a Montgomery County resident, over 18, recidivist, with chronic mental health and/or co-occurring disorders, and no outstanding detainers or lengthy state sentences
Must not have any outstanding detainers or lengthy state sentences
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: There is no formal application. Inmates are screened upon intake. Referrals come from a correctional officer, case manager, or nurse. Those identified with behavioral health needs, self-harm risk factors, or referred by staff, family, or other providers are assessed by CATS staff for service needs.

structured_extraction.program_name: Co-Parenting Program (Parent Education and Custody Effectiveness, or PEACE)
structured_extraction.program_description: An online parent education program for families going through separation or divorce. It teaches parents skills to keep children out of family conflicts, helps them understand the effects of divorce on adults and children, and promotes effective communication between parents.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Online parenting education classes offered for $25 per class. Available to parents with a court order from the Montgomery County Circuit Court, as well as Montgomery County residents ordered by another Circuit Court to attend a parenting class.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Parents going through separation or divorce who have been court-ordered to attend a parenting class, particularly Montgomery County Circuit Court participants and Montgomery County residents ordered by any Circuit Court.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participation in online parenting education classes focused on the effects of divorce on adults and children, and promoting effective communication between co-parents.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to parents with a Montgomery County Circuit Court order, or Montgomery County residents ordered by another Circuit Court to attend a parenting class.
requirements_list: Must have a court order to attend a parenting class
Must be a Montgomery County Circuit Court participant OR a Montgomery County resident ordered by another Circuit Court
Must arrive on time to be admitted to class
Program costs $25 per class
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Classes are offered online. Contact the program at 240-777-9342 for enrollment information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A facade improvement program for commercial properties at 10210-10222 New Hampshire Avenue in Silver Spring, MD. The program involves purchasing facade easements and improving the exterior appearance of buildings in the Hillandale Center area of Colesville.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides facade improvements to commercial properties. Specific financial terms and amounts are not stated on this page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Commercial property owners at 10210-10222 New Hampshire Avenue, Silver Spring, MD 20903
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Exterior facade improvements and signage upgrades to commercial buildings
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Limited to properties at 10210-10222 New Hampshire Avenue, Silver Spring, MD 20903 (Hillandale Center area)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Email comments to the Chief, Neighborhood Revitalization Section. A public notice has been issued for review.

structured_extraction.program_description: A reentry case management program for sentenced inmates at Montgomery County Correctional Facility (MCCF) and Detention Center (MCDC). Reentry staff conduct needs screenings and assessments, develop individualized Reentry Service Plans, and coordinate with community supervision agents, family members, and service providers to help incarcerated individuals prepare for release and successfully reintegrate into the community.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reentry staff provide a comprehensive, clinically oriented case management process including an initial needs screening, a full psycho-social assessment, coordination with community supervision agents and family members, and development of a personalized Reentry Service Plan. The plan outlines action steps to address each person's identified needs before and after release. A Release Information Summary is also provided, listing follow-up appointments and referral contacts. Services are most intensive for sentenced inmates rated at High or Medium service levels; pretrial inmates receive limited services such as a Reentry Resource Guide and workshops.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Sentenced inmates (and some pretrial detainees on a limited basis) held at Montgomery County correctional facilities who are preparing for release and community reintegration.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reentry planning services, psycho-social needs assessment, individualized service plan development, referrals to community resources, and coordination with supervision agents and service providers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to inmates incarcerated at Montgomery County Correctional Facility (MCCF) and Montgomery County Detention Center (MCDC) in Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a sentenced inmate with a projected release date to receive full Reentry Case Management services
Pretrial detainees may receive limited services based on risk and need levels
Sentenced inmates with active detainers are generally deferred from full Reentry Case Management but may receive Reentry Transition Planning on a case-by-case basis
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Reentry staff review all sentenced inmates for eligibility. An initial Reentry Needs Screening is completed, followed by a full Reentry Needs Assessment. A Reentry Service Plan is developed with the inmate's direct input and finalized in the final days or weeks before release.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides free colorectal cancer screenings, including colonoscopies and follow-up care, to eligible Montgomery County residents who are uninsured or under-insured. A nurse case manager supports patients through follow-up care if results require further attention. The program also offers care coordination to connect patients to further diagnosis and treatment if needed, along with health education to promote cancer awareness and the importance of screenings. Limited funding is also available for treatment if cancer is detected. Funded by the Maryland Department of Health (MDH), Center for Cancer Prevention and Control, and/or CDC.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free colorectal cancer screenings (including colonoscopies) and nurse case management for follow-up care at no cost to eligible residents. Limited funding is also available for treatment if cancer is detected. The program provides care coordination, patient navigation, and links patients to community and healthcare partners for treatment services. Referrals to payment assistance programs such as Maryland Medical Assistance and Maryland Health Benefit Exchange are also available.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Uninsured or under-insured Montgomery County residents age 45 or older (or younger with higher risk for colorectal cancer) with household income at or below 250% of the Federal Poverty Level and no current diagnosis of colorectal cancer.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free colorectal cancer screenings (colonoscopy), nurse case management, patient navigation, and follow-up care coordination; limited funding for treatment if cancer is detected.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Montgomery County, Maryland resident.
requirements_list: Must be a Montgomery County resident
Must be uninsured or underinsured
Household income at or below 250% of the Federal Poverty Level
Age 45 or older, or younger with higher risk for colorectal cancer
No current cancer diagnosis
Proof of residency (lease, mortgage, or utility bill in applicant's name)
Proof of earned income or family income documentation (tax return, W-2, pay stubs, or notarized letter stating no income)
Photo identification (MD driver's license, MD ID card, Green Card, passport, or work authorization)
Recent healthcare facility/provider clinic or progress notes
Completed application form and all supporting documentation
Maryland Department of Health Authorization to Release/Receive Information Form
Acknowledgement of Notice of Privacy Practices required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at the Colorectal Cancer Screening Application portal, or download and complete the application (available in English and Spanish) and submit by mail, fax, or email. You may also call 240-777-1750 Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. for assistance with scheduling and coordination. After submission, a team member will contact you within 7 to 10 business days. You will need to provide proof of residency, proof of income, and a photo ID.

structured_extraction.program_name: Commercial Property Assessed Clean Energy (C-PACE) Financing
structured_extraction.program_description: The Commercial Property Assessed Clean Energy (C-PACE) program helps qualifying commercial property owners in Montgomery County finance energy efficiency, renewable energy, resiliency, climate adaptation, water conservation, and environmental health and safety upgrades. A private lender or capital provider offers long-term, fixed-rate financing, which is repaid through annual or semi-annual surcharges added to the property's tax bill. The loan stays with the property, so any future owner continues paying the surcharge until the loan is fully repaid. Retroactive financing is available up to 12 months following final inspection. The program is administered in partnership between Montgomery County and the Montgomery County Green Bank.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Long-term, fixed-rate financing from private capital providers or lenders for qualifying commercial property improvements including energy efficiency, renewable energy, climate resiliency, climate adaptation, water conservation, and environmental health and safety upgrades. Loan terms up to 20 years. The loan is repaid through annual or semi-annual surcharges on the property tax bill and transfers to any subsequent property owner until fully paid off. Higher loan-to-value ratios are available through a 5-year pilot program. Retroactive financing available up to 12 months following final inspection.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Commercial property owners, developers, capital providers, energy service contractors, non-profit and faith-based organizations, minority-owned businesses, and low-income and disadvantaged community (LIDAC) property owners and developers in Montgomery County seeking financing for clean energy, energy efficiency, resiliency, and related improvements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency improvements (e.g., LED lighting, insulation, window replacements, heat pumps), renewable energy installations (e.g., solar photovoltaic systems), climate resiliency and adaptation measures, water conservation upgrades, and environmental health and safety upgrades to commercial properties.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to commercial properties located in Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must own a commercial property in Montgomery County
Property must be eligible for a C-PACE surcharge on the property tax bill
Projects must involve energy efficiency, renewable energy, resiliency, climate adaptation, water conservation, or environmental health and safety improvements
Properties must qualify under Building Energy Performance Standards (BEPS) where applicable
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Montgomery County Green Bank, which serves as the Program Administrator as of April 2021, for information on how to apply. The Green Bank manages day-to-day administration and loan processing. Additional information is available at the Montgomery County Green Bank C-PACE Program webpage (mcgreenbank.org/c-pace/). The Montgomery County Department of Environmental Protection program page is also available for further details.

structured_extraction.program_name: Commercial Property Assessed Clean Energy (C-PACE) Program – New Construction
structured_extraction.program_description: An expansion of the Commercial Property Assessed Clean Energy Program to include new construction. The program allows commercial property owners to finance clean energy, renewable energy, and energy efficiency improvements through a property assessment.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property-assessed financing for clean energy, renewable energy, and energy efficiency improvements on commercial properties, now expanded to include new construction projects.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Commercial property owners in Montgomery County seeking to finance clean energy or energy efficiency improvements, including new construction
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Clean energy technologies, renewable energy, and energy efficiency improvements in commercial properties
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a commercial property in Montgomery County
Program expanded to new construction projects

structured_extraction.program_name: Commission for Women Internship Program (Montgomery County)
structured_extraction.program_description: A paid internship program hosted by the Montgomery County Commission for Women. High school, college, and graduate students work with Commission staff on projects related to women's issues, legislation and policy, program planning, communications, research, and general office work. Interns can receive academic credit or student service-learning hours.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Paid internship positions available during fall, spring, and summer terms on a rolling admission basis. Interns work in a hybrid format (remote and in-office). Full-day hours are 10:00am–4:00pm; part-time hours vary. Academic credit and service-learning hours are available.
structured_extraction.program_audience: High school, college, and graduate students interested in women's issues, social justice, and civic engagement in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Internship compensation (paid positions); academic credit or service-learning hours for eligible students.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is based in Montgomery County, MD. Open to students affiliated with institutions or schools in the area.
requirements_list: Must be a high school, college, or graduate student
Strong writing and organizational skills
Interest in women's issues, social justice, and civic engagement
Must be motivated, proactive, and have a positive attitude
Submit a résumé and cover letter
Submit dates and hours of availability
Submit a list of goals for the internship
Submit a writing sample of no more than 2–3 paragraphs
Participate in an in-person interview
Email the Commission before applying to confirm space availability
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Email the Commission to confirm space is available, then submit a résumé, cover letter, availability dates and hours, a list of internship goals, and a short writing sample (2–3 paragraphs) to Carmen Kaarid at Carmen.Kaarid@montgomerycountymd.gov. Applicants will be invited to an in-person interview.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Access Program (CAP) provides funding assistance to nonprofit and community organizations so they can use the Silver Spring Civic Building and Veterans Plaza for their programs and events. Since its launch over a decade ago, CAP has supported more than 600 organizations, helping them spend more resources on their programs rather than on facility costs. Harvard University has recognized the program for its positive community impact.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: CAP provides funding to offset facility rental costs at the Silver Spring Civic Building and Veterans Plaza. Priority is given to applicants with demonstrated financial need. A review committee evaluates applications to ensure alignment with the program's community benefit mission.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Events scheduled between July 2025 and June 2026; applications available starting July 1, 2025
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit and community organizations including youth groups, faith-based organizations, arts and cultural programs, and civic groups, especially those with demonstrated financial need.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Offsetting facility rental costs for events held at the Silver Spring Civic Building and Veterans Plaza
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Events must be held at the Silver Spring Civic Building and Veterans Plaza in Silver Spring, MD
requirements_list: Applicant must be a nonprofit or community organization
Must demonstrate financial need (priority consideration)
Events must be scheduled between July 2025 and June 2026
Application must align with the program's mission of community benefit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply for CAP funding starting July 1, 2025. A review committee evaluates applications for alignment with community benefit goals and financial need. Contact Miguel Lozada by email or phone for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free eight-month advocacy training program that teaches advocacy skills to economically disadvantaged Montgomery County residents with lived experience of poverty. Created by the Community Action Board in 2016, monthly workshops run October through May and cover topics such as working with elected officials, storytelling, research, developing testimony, and key county advocacy issues. The program is fully bilingual in English and Spanish.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free eight-month advocacy training program consisting of monthly workshops running October through May. Topics include working with elected officials, storytelling, research, developing testimony, and key county advocacy issues. The program is fully bilingual in English and Spanish and is open to economically disadvantaged community members with modest incomes.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Economically disadvantaged Montgomery County residents with lived experience of poverty and modest incomes
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Building advocacy skills to engage in local policy and community issues
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be an economically disadvantaged resident with lived experience
Must have modest income
Must apply during summer recruitment period
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Recruitment for the program takes place each summer. Check the program page for the latest information on how to apply.

structured_extraction.program_description: A paid internship program at Montgomery County's Pre-Release and Reentry Services (PRRS) facility. Interns assist with supervising residents, organizing activities, mentoring, case management, security operations, resident orientation, adjustment hearings, recreational trip coordination, on-site verifications, community release activities monitoring, resident transportation, and treatment team meetings. The program runs up to 24 hours per week for a minimum of four months, with interviews scheduled approximately four times per year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Paid internship providing approximately $300 every two weeks via direct deposit, weekly individual and group training, Montgomery County Government training, and eligibility for a free Ride-On bus pass. Interns work a maximum of 24 hours per week for a minimum of four months. Benefits eligibility, paid time off considerations, and compensatory leave at supervisor discretion may apply.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Interviews scheduled as positions become available, approximately 4 times per year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals at least 21 years old who have completed at least two years of college, including one year in criminal justice, behavioral science, or a human services-related field, with a valid driver's license and ability to pass a background investigation and physical exam. Also open to students enrolled in local colleges and universities pursuing careers in corrections or criminal justice.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Paid work experience in community corrections and reentry services, including resident supervision, mentoring, case management, facility operations, recreational trip coordination, resident transportation, and professional development training.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Located in Rockville, Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: At least 21 years of age
Completion of at least two years of college, with one year in criminal justice, behavioral science, or human services related discipline
Valid Driver's License with no restrictions
Social Security card required
Must be able to pass a background investigation and physical exam including drug screening
Medical clearance required
OHR clearance required
Selection through an in-person interview
Maximum of 24 hours per week
Minimum four-month commitment
Flexible schedule availability including weekends required
Ability to work 4:00–9:00 PM or 5:00–10:00 PM shifts
Must wear staff ID at all times on PRRS grounds (visible, above waist)
Professional dress code required; jeans allowed on casual Fridays
Must obey all traffic laws; use seat belt; ensure passengers use seatbelts when transporting residents
Cannot handle resident checks/monies or dispense medications
Must maintain confidentiality; only authorized information may be released
Must carry cell phone during transports
Cannot allow residents into personal vehicles

Cannot loan money or offer rides to residents outside of official duties
Sign in/out on daily log
Complete timesheet via MC Time every two weeks
Attend bi-weekly intern meetings
Bring two recreation trip ideas to each meeting
Comply with PREA
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at www.montgomerycountymd.gov under Careers and Internships. The position is listed as Community Corrections Intern. Interviews are scheduled as positions become available, approximately four times per year.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) - Public Services Funding via CDAC
structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Development Advisory Committee (CDAC) reviews and recommends nonprofit grant applications to receive annual federal Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) funding for public services in Montgomery County. Each fall, the CDAC holds a public hearing, conducts applicant interviews, and makes funding recommendations to the County Executive for the following year's budget.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual federal CDBG grants for public services. Funding amounts are not specified on this page. Nonprofit applicants meet with the CDAC on three evenings in the fall to discuss their application, after which the CDAC makes funding recommendations to the County Executive for the following budget year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations seeking federal CDBG funding for public services in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Public services as defined under the CDBG program
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Applicant must be a nonprofit organization
Must submit a CDBG application for public services
Must meet with the CDAC during the fall review cycle (three evenings)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Nonprofits submit CDBG applications for public services. Each fall, the CDAC holds a public hearing and then conducts applicant interviews over three evenings. Based on the application and interview, the CDAC makes funding recommendations to the County Executive for the following year's budget.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Development Block Grant Program (Public Services Stream)
structured_extraction.program_description: Federal grant program administered by Montgomery County that funds public service projects for low- and moderate-income residents. Eligible nonprofit organizations and governmental agencies can apply for grants to support services such as eviction prevention, employment, youth development, education, health care, mental health, and other public service activities. Construction projects are not eligible. FY27 grants cover July 1, 2026 – June 30, 2027.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Public service grants up to $45,000 per organization to fund public service activities for low- and moderate-income Montgomery County residents. Funds support personnel costs, fringe benefits, consultants, and operating expenses (office rent, utilities, training, insurance, office supplies, telephone, and indirect/overhead up to 15%). Applicants are limited to two applications per organization. Multi-year funding of up to three years is possible for the same program/activity, though years 2–3 are not guaranteed. A recent cycle totaled $589,417 across 18 organizations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low- and moderate-income (LMI) Montgomery County residents (minimum 70% of beneficiaries must be LMI); specific populations may include homeless persons, persons with disabilities, the elderly, youth, and legal immigrants. Served by 501(c)(3) nonprofits, organizations with pending 501(c)(3) status (finalized by July 1, 2026), and governmental agencies.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Public service activities including eviction prevention, employment, youth development, education, welfare, housing-related supportive services, crime prevention, health care, mental health, and recreation. Eligible costs include personnel, fringe benefits, consultants, office rent, utilities, training, insurance, office supplies, telephone, audit and accounting, and indirect/overhead (maximum 15%). Ineligible uses include equipment purchases, entertainment, political activities, and income payments (except payments made directly to service providers for up to 3 consecutive months). Construction projects are not eligible. Funds may not be used to promote gender ideology (E.O. 14168) or elective abortions (E.O. 14182).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must serve Montgomery County, Maryland residents. Excludes cities of Rockville, Gaithersburg, and Takoma Park (which have their own CDBG programs) and certain non-participating jurisdictions (Town of Barnesville, Town of Chevy Chase View, Chevy Chase Village, Village of Chevy Chase Section 3, Town of Laytonsville, Village of Martin's Additions).
requirements_list: Must be a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization (or have pending 501(c)(3) status finalized by July 1, 2026), or be a governmental/quasi-governmental agency
Must directly serve low- and/or moderate-income Montgomery County residents (minimum 70% of beneficiaries must be LMI)
Construction projects are not eligible
Must submit IRS tax-exempt nonprofit status letter
Must submit Board of Directors listing with names, titles, terms, and addresses
Must submit organizational chart or structure
Must submit current fiscal year budget and most recent audit
Must submit resumes of chief administrative and fiscal officers and key project staff
Must submit two letters of community support
Must submit documentation of corporate good standing from the state of incorporation
Must provide federal tax ID (EIN) and UEI number
Must be a legally incorporated organization with state corporation number
Must meet federal audit requirements (Uniform Guidance 2 CFR Part 200, Subpart F)
Must comply with applicable Executive Orders including E.O. 14151 and E.O. 14173
Applicants limited to two applications per organization
Grant contracts start on or around July 1, 2026
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download the CDBG application and instructions from the DHCA website. Submit the completed application along with required attachments (listed and numbered in order) by Friday, September 19, 2025 at 4:00 P.M. The application cycle typically opens in August and closes in mid-September. DHCA staff screen applications for eligibility and send email receipts. Eligible applications are reviewed by the Community Development Advisory Committee (CDAC), which makes funding recommendations to the DHCA Director and County Executive. The County Executive submits recommendations to the County Council, which makes final funding selections, typically approving the budget in late May. Grant contracts start on or around July 1, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants to nonprofit 501(c)(3) organizations for food assistance services in Montgomery County. The program supports directly serving residents with regularly scheduled, no-cost food services at county-based sites at least once per month for a minimum of one year, as well as food recovery services involving recovering, handling, and redistributing surplus food. The program prioritizes under-resourced ZIP codes, home delivery models, services to immigrant and unhoused residents, food recovery operations, and high-performing returning grantees. A food recovery component serves as a dedicated funding source for organizations assisting community members experiencing food insecurity. Approximately $3.5 million is awarded to community-based organizations (56 active providers in FY26, up from 49 in FY25), including a food recovery component. Funding supports direct food purchases, Manna Food Center Food Staples Credits, operational expenses, and food recovery activities. Applications are submitted through the ecivis grants portal with details provided in the NOFO.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Approximately $3.5 million awarded to 56 active 501(c)(3) food assistance provider organizations overall, including $1.9M in expanded grants distributed across 53 nonprofit providers. A food recovery component provides $428,202 total to six organizations, of which $290,785 is renewable FY26 funding and $137,417 is supported through a FY26 Special Appropriation passed on November 18, 2025. Four funding options: Option 1 — direct grant funds for food purchasing and operational expenses (operational expenses capped at 15% of food purchase request); Option 2 — Manna Food Center Food Staples Credits with operational support (capped at 5%); Option 3 — food recovery operational expenses only (no cap); Option 4 — combined direct food purchase funds and food recovery operational expenses. Awards prioritize under-resourced ZIP codes, home delivery, immigrant and unhoused resident services, and food recovery operations. An expanded food recovery grant component is expected to launch fall 2026 as part of a three-part food recovery strategy.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Catherine Nardi, Program Manager II (OFSR - technical questions)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit 501(c)(3) food assistance and food recovery organizations serving Montgomery County residents, including those providing pantry services, prepared meals, home delivery, and food recovery operations; ultimately serving Montgomery County households experiencing or at risk of food insecurity, including low-income, immigrant, and unhoused residents
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Support regularly scheduled, no-cost food assistance services to Montgomery County residents at county-based sites; recovering, handling, and redistributing surplus food; food distribution including choice pantries, pre-packed distributions, prepared meals, home delivery, and food recovery operations. Eligible expenses include: food purchases from wholesalers, retailers, local farms, and Capital Area Food Bank; Manna Food Center Food Staples Credits; staffing (salaries, benefits, contract workers); supplies (boxes, bags, PPE, packaging); location costs (rent, utilities); transportation (gas, vehicle rental); indirect costs (legal, accounting, liability insurance, audits); and food recovery operational expenses. Funds cannot be used as lump sum distributions and require a Notice to Proceed before spending.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. Organizations must be based in Montgomery County and serve Montgomery County residents. Service Consolidation Hubs designated by the Department of Health and Human Services are NOT eligible.
requirements_list: Must be a currently active 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization
Must be based in Montgomery County
Must be registered and in Good Standing with Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
Must provide regularly scheduled, no-cost food assistance services
Must serve Montgomery County residents at county-based sites
Must have provided services at least once per month for a minimum of one year
Must provide IRS 990 Form or exemption explanation
Must demonstrate successful performance history with selected service format
Food recovery applicants (Options 3 & 4) must have 1-3 years significant food recovery experience in Montgomery County
Food recovery applicants must commit to regular Food Recovery Network participation (~2 hours/month)
Must comply with food safety standards and County/state food licensing requirements
Must remain in Good Standing throughout application review, grant agreement finalization, and payment
Proof of insurance required before fund distribution
Compliance with Title VII Civil Rights Act of 1964
Accessibility for persons with disabilities
Must track unduplicated households served, food quantities distributed, and client satisfaction
Realistic implementation timeline required
Alignment with OFSR core values (equity, systems-based, innovation, data-driven)
Service Consolidation Hubs designated by Department of Health and Human Services are NOT eligible
Prioritization given to providers serving under-resourced ZIP codes, immigrant and unhoused residents, and food recovery
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Program is not currently accepting new applications for the current FY26 cycle. Contract and grant amendments for existing grantees are in progress; contact OFSR for details. When open: complete certifications, acknowledgments, and assurances in the ecivis online grant application portal; submit proposal (non-revisable after submission); review committee scores applications on Criteria A-E plus added-value characteristics; funds require Notice to Proceed before spending; subject to audit within 3 years of final payment. Review the NOFO (https://assets.montgomerycountymd.gov/files/FY26-CFA-NOFO.pdf) for full details.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Montgomery County Commission on Common Ownership Communities (CCOC) provides a training program called 'Community Governance Fundamentals' for board members and residents of common ownership communities such as condominiums, cooperatives, and homeowners' associations. The training covers ethics, roles and responsibilities of board members and homeowners, governing documents, financial management, meeting rules, and general administration. It is required by county law for new board members and must be completed within 90 days of being elected or appointed.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free online or in-person training program lasting approximately 3 hours, including videos and quizzes. Upon successful completion, participants receive a certificate of completion that is valid for 3 years. Classroom sessions can be scheduled at the community's facility or at the CCOC's Rockville offices.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Board members and residents of common ownership communities (condominiums, cooperatives, and homeowners' associations) in Montgomery County, as well as members of the public interested in learning about common ownership community operations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training on community governance, ethics, roles and responsibilities, governing documents, financial management, meeting rules, and general administration.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: New board members must complete the training within 90 days of being elected or appointed on or after January 1, 2016.
Training must be completed through the CCOC or a CCOC-approved organization to receive valid certification.
Certificate of completion is valid for 3 years and must be retained by the governing body for inspection.
The governing body must register and pay an annual registration fee with DHCA's Licensing & Registration unit, reporting board membership and training completion dates.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register online at the COC Board Training portal (https://ex11.montgomerycountymd.gov/extranetportal/) or contact CCOC by email at CCOC@MontgomeryCountyMD.gov to schedule a classroom presentation.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides recently released inmates from the Montgomery County Correctional Facility with an official government-issued identification card that serves as a photo ID, a free Ride-On bus pass, and a library card for computer and services access at Montgomery County Public Library branches. The card is valid for 60 days after release and includes the person's photo and release address.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A Community Reentry Identification Card is issued upon release from the Montgomery County Correctional Facility. It is valid for 60 days and serves as: (1) an official government photo ID meeting federal I-9 guidelines, (2) a no-cost Ride-On bus pass throughout Montgomery County's transit system, and (3) a library card for computer and services access at all Montgomery County Public Library branches.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Inmates being released from the Montgomery County Correctional Facility who need identification and transportation assistance during reentry.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Photo identification, free bus transportation on Ride-On, and library computer access for up to 60 days following release.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to individuals released from the Montgomery County Correctional Facility (22880 Whelan Lane, Boyds, Maryland 20841). Bus pass valid on Ride-On transit throughout Montgomery County.
requirements_list: Must be a qualified offender being released from the Montgomery County Correctional Facility
Card is issued upon release
Card is active for the first 60 days following release
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The card is issued directly to qualified offenders upon release from the Montgomery County Correctional Facility by the Reentry Services Unit. No separate application process is described.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Support Network (CSN) - My Turn Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides resources, education, information, and short-term financial assistance to families and caregivers of children (ages 3–18) with an intellectual or developmental disability who are not connected with State of Maryland resources. Works with families to identify the child's needs and provide support for community integration, addressing needs outside of IDEA services. Services include outreach, assistance with community recreational activities, summer camp placements, limited medical supplies, augmentative devices, behavioral consultation, referrals to other resources, educational seminars, and linkages to community services. Funds can be used for community recreational activities (e.g., swimming, horseback riding) from July through January, and for summer camp from February through the first week of July. Funds cannot be used for therapeutic services such as occupational therapy, physical therapy, or speech therapy.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Short-term, limited financial assistance provided one request at a time. Funds can be used for community recreational activities (e.g., swimming, horseback riding) from July through January, and for summer camp from February through the first week of July. Also includes limited medical equipment, augmentative devices, behavioral consultation, outreach, referrals to other resources, educational seminars, and linkages to community services. Funds cannot be used for therapeutic services such as occupational therapy, physical therapy, or speech therapy.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families and caregivers of Montgomery County residents ages 3 to 18 with a diagnosed intellectual or developmental disability as defined by the Maryland Developmental Disability Administration (DDA) who are not currently receiving long-term funded programs through Montgomery County or the State of Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Recreational activities (e.g., swimming, horseback riding), summer camp, limited medical equipment, augmentative devices, behavioral consultation, and other identified needs related to community integration. Cannot be used for therapeutic services (OT, PT, Speech).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County residents only.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Montgomery County resident
Child must be between ages 3 and 18 (up to but not including age 19)
Child must have a diagnosed developmental disability meeting the Maryland DDA definition
Family must not be receiving any long-term funded programs through Montgomery County or State of Maryland
Must provide documentation of the child's developmental disability (school records, IEP, psychological evaluations)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 240-777-1216 (TTY: MD Relay 711) to schedule an intake interview with a My Turn Program staff member. Bring all documentation related to the child's developmental disability, including school records, IEP, and psychological evaluations. Referrals are also accepted from school personnel or professionals working with the family.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Support Network Respite Care Program (Respite Coordination - The Arc Montgomery County)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides short-term temporary relief (respite care) to primary unpaid full-time live-in caregivers and families who care for frail elderly adults, adults or children with functional or developmental disabilities (including Alzheimer's disease and other dementias), children with challenging behaviors, children with severe medical conditions, or frail seniors. Care is provided by trained, certified care workers and may be arranged in the family's home, adult medical day programs, or approved respite care facilities. Services are coordinated through The Arc Montgomery County under a county contract. The program may provide a financial subsidy to pay a Respite Care Provider (RCP) for short-term relief ranging from a few hours to a day, a weekend, or sometimes longer. Funding is limited and a subsidy is not guaranteed for every request. After application approval, the primary caregiver attends an orientation and staff help locate the most appropriate direct service provider.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Short-term temporary respite care provided by trained, certified care workers in the family's home, adult medical day programs, or approved respite care facilities. A financial subsidy may be provided to pay a Respite Care Provider for short-term relief ranging from a few hours to a day, a weekend, or sometimes longer. Funding is limited and a subsidy is not guaranteed for every request. Care is arranged at no cost to the caregiver through The Arc Montgomery County Respite Coordination program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Primary unpaid full-time live-in caregivers and families residing in Montgomery County, MD, who care for frail elderly adults, adults or children with functional or developmental disabilities (including Alzheimer's disease and other dementias), children with challenging behaviors, children with severe medical conditions, or frail seniors living in the same household.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment to a Respite Care Provider for short-term relief care in the family home, adult medical day programs, or approved respite facilities, giving the primary caregiver a temporary break from full-time caregiving duties.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be the primary full-time live-in unpaid caregiver or family member providing full-time care
Must reside in Montgomery County
Care recipient must reside in the same household as the caregiver
Care recipient must be a frail elderly adult/frail senior, a child or adult with a functional or developmental disability, a child with challenging behaviors, or a child with severe medical needs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call The Arc Montgomery County Respite Coordination program at (301) 984-5777 x1204 or visit their website to request an application. Submit the completed application with required documentation by email to Respite@arcmontmd.org or by US mail to The Arc Montgomery County. Applications take up to 30 business days to process. Once approved, the caregiver attends an orientation and staff help find an appropriate provider. You may also contact the Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services, Aging and Disability Services at 240-777-1216.

structured_extraction.program_name: Commuter Choice Mass Transit Flexible Spending Account
structured_extraction.program_description: A pre-tax benefit account that lets Montgomery County Government (MCG) employees set aside money from each paycheck before taxes to pay for eligible mass transit commuting and parking expenses. Employees can enroll, change, or stop their election at any time during the plan year, unlike other FSA types.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Employees elect monthly contributions — up to $230/month for MCGEO employees and up to $300/month for unrepresented employees — deducted pre-tax from paychecks to cover eligible transit expenses (Metro, MARC train, vanpool, ferry, Lyft Line, Uber Pool) and parking. The pre-tax deduction reduces federal, state, and FICA taxes. Funds are accessed via a FLEXEXPRESS debit card or submitted as reimbursement claims. WMATA users must purchase or reload fare cards, obtain receipts, and file a claim for reimbursement. Claims must be submitted within 180 days of the expense. Employees can enroll, increase, reduce, or stop contributions on a monthly basis without a qualifying life event.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Can enroll, change, or stop election at any time during the plan year on a monthly basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: MCGEO and unrepresented Montgomery County Government employees who use mass transit or parking for commuting to work. IAFF and FOP employees are not eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eligible work-related commuting expenses including mass transit (Metro, MARC train, bus, light or regional rail, streetcar, trolley, subway, ferry, UberPOOL, Vanpool, and Lyft Line passes, tokens, fare cards, or vouchers) and parking expenses used for commuting to work.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to benefit-eligible Montgomery County Government employees.
requirements_list: Must be a benefit-eligible Montgomery County Government employee
Only available to MCGEO and unrepresented employees (IAFF and FOP employees are not eligible)
Must be actively employed to participate
Only the employee's own commuting expenses are eligible (not dependents or spouses)
Claims must be submitted within 180 days of the expense incurred date
WMATA metro card purchases require a receipt and claim form — the FSA debit card cannot be used directly for WMATA fare cards
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Employees may opt in or out on a monthly basis without a qualifying life event; changes are effective on the 1st of the month. Elect a monthly contribution amount to be deducted pre-tax from each paycheck. Use the FLEXEXPRESS debit card to purchase eligible transit passes or parking, or submit a reimbursement claim form for WMATA fare cards and other eligible expenses.

structured_extraction.program_description: A composting education and training program that teaches residents, Master Gardeners, and farmers how to compost food scraps using best practices. The program demonstrates various composting methods, trains participants to become Extension Composters, and supports the county's goal of diverting waste and building local soil health.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free hands-on composting training for residents, Master Gardeners, and farmers. Participants are trained to become Extension Composters through a multi-level program. Farmers receive training on state and local rules for on-farm composting, system siting and design, and best management practices.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Composting education and hands-on training to learn best practices for composting food scraps at various scales.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact natalia.salazar@montgomerycountymd.gov to be added to the mailing list for program updates.

The team works with clients inside the jail to develop treatment plans addressing mental health, substance abuse, housing, vocational training, family reintegration, and education, then continues to support clients in the community for up to 12 months after release.

Funded by a 2-year BJA grant serving 120 clients.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free information and referral service that helps adults aged 50 and older and adults with disabilities find transportation options by connecting them with information about public and private transportation services. Trained staff can help people learn to use public buses and Metrorail, connect them with free or low-cost volunteer ride programs, and assist with transportation needs for medical services, errands, social activities, and more. Multilingual support is available.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free information and referral service where trained staff provide details about available public and private transportation options for eligible individuals. Staff can help people learn to use public buses and Metrorail and connect them with free or low-cost volunteer ride programs. Available Monday–Friday, 9 am–5 pm by phone or email. Multilingual support available.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Finding and accessing transportation options for medical services, errands, social activities, and other needs

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 301-738-3252 Monday–Friday, 9 am–5 pm, or email ConnectARide@AccessJCA.org to discuss your transportation needs.

structured_extraction.program_name: Coordinated Community Supports Partnership (CSP) Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A Montgomery County grant program supporting coordinated community behavioral health services and supports for students in Montgomery County Public Schools. The program builds a framework of Community Supports Partnerships to coordinate delivery of behavioral health services, supporting a continuum of holistic mental health and substance use support services from prevention through treatment and recovery, aligned with Multi-Tiered Systems of Support (MTSS).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant awards ranging from $50,000 to $3.5 million (average approximately $750,000) for behavioral health services and supports for Maryland students in Montgomery County. Grant term is 12 months: July 1, 2026 – June 30, 2027. Funds may be used for personnel, fringe benefits, travel, equipment, supplies, contractual services, training, indirect costs, school bus use (subcontract), stipends for school staff training outside contract hours, and behavioral health-related supplies. Funds cannot be used for direct family support for social determinants, student activity fees, field trips, somatic health services, or academic/vocational support. Funds must be spent after contract finalization and Notice to Proceed is secured.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Sara Rose, Director, Local Behavioral Health Authority; Ali Hoy, Program Manager II, Office of Grants Management
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students (pre-K through high school) in Montgomery County Public Schools, school staff, and families; priority given to unduplicated individuals and sub-groups with identified needs
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Behavioral health services and programming in schools including school bus use (subcontract), stipends for school staff training outside contract hours, behavioral health-related supplies, staff positions for program delivery, data collection and reporting, Evidence-Based Program implementation, and staff training

structured_extraction.program_description: The CCS Program helps individuals with developmental disabilities who have been found eligible by Maryland's Developmental Disabilities Administration (DDA) to find and access the best community services and supports. Case managers provide advocacy, care coordination, crisis management, and intervention to ensure individuals' health and safety needs are met so they can fully participate in their communities. The program also serves school-to-work transition students with developmental disabilities who qualify for Maryland DDA Home and Community Based Services (HCBS) Waiver services. CSN is one of six agencies in Montgomery County offering this program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Case management, advocacy, and coordination of community services and supports for individuals with developmental disabilities. Services include crisis management, intervention, school-to-work transition assistance, and help navigating community services to meet health and safety needs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: School-to-work transition students and adults with developmental disabilities who are determined eligible by Maryland's Developmental Disabilities Administration (DDA) for Home and Community Based Services (HCBS) Waiver services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Case management, advocacy, and coordination of community services and supports including crisis management, intervention, and school-to-work transition assistance for individuals with developmental disabilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
