Must be eligible for Maryland DDA Home and Community Based Services (HCBS) Waiver services
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Developmental Disabilities Administration (DDA). Call 301-362-5100 or 1-888-207-2479 to request an application, or apply online at the DDA website.

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County's Income Tax Offset Credit (ITOC) provides eligible owner-occupied principal residence homeowners a $692 credit on their annual property tax bill. The credit offsets increases in county property tax resulting from the county income tax rate being above 2.6%, with the credit amount established by County Council resolution. To receive the credit, homeowners must have a Homestead Tax Credit (HTC) application on file with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT). The HTC application is a one-time filing that automatically applies to future years once approved — no annual reapplication is needed. The credit appears as 'County Property Tax Credit' on tax bills.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A $692 annual tax credit applied to the property tax bill of eligible homeowners, offsetting increases in county property tax resulting from the county income tax rate being above 2.6%. The credit amount is established by County Council resolution. Once a Homestead Tax Credit application is on file with SDAT and approved, the credit is automatically applied each year — no annual reapplication is needed. The HTC application must be on file with SDAT by May 1, 2026 for the credit to appear on tax bills beginning July 1, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residential property owners who own and live in (occupy) their property as their primary residence (owner-occupied homeowners).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of property tax bill by $692 per year, offsetting increases in county real property tax liability.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residential property owners in Montgomery County, Maryland who occupy their property as their primary residence.
requirements_list: Must own and live in (occupy) the property as a principal residence in Montgomery County
Must have a Homestead Tax Credit (HTC) application on file with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
Property must be owner-occupied (principal residence) as determined by SDAT
HTC application must be filed by May 1st (May 1, 2026 for credit to appear on bills beginning July 1, 2026)
Property address must be where homeowner(s) file federal and Maryland income tax returns (if filing)
Married couples may only claim one principal residence
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Check if you already have a Homestead Application on file by searching your property at sdat.dat.maryland.gov/RealProperty. If the status shows 'Approved' or 'Application Received,' no further action is needed. Step 2: If the status shows 'No application,' apply online at Maryland OneStop (onestop.md.gov) or by mail using the SDAT paper application (dat.maryland.gov/realproperty). You only need to apply once — no separate application for the ITOC itself is required. Once approved, the credit is applied automatically each year.

structured_extraction.program_name: County Supplemental Homeowners' Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides additional Montgomery County property tax credits to homeowners who already qualify for the Maryland State Homeowners' Property Tax Credit (HOTC). Eligibility is based on the homeowner's household income compared to their property tax bill. The credit applies only against the General County and Special Service Area real property tax. Established and governed by Expedited Bill 15-04, which revised the County tax credit supplement to the state homeowners property tax credit program. For the July 1, 2026 tax billing, the assessed value on which the credit applies is $383,100; combined income eligibility limit is $76,620; and net worth limit is $255,400. The progressive income scale ranges from 0% allowable percentage at up to $25,540 combined gross income to 8% at up to $53,630. No separate application is required — homeowners simply apply for the State HOTC through SDAT to be automatically considered for the county supplement. Combined with the Senior Property Tax Credit, the benefit averaged $1,276 last year and benefited 4,486 County residents. Taxpayers age 70 or older may submit retroactive applications for the current and up to 3 prior levy years at any time.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A County-level property tax credit applied against the General County and Special Service Area real property tax, calculated on a progressive scale based on household income relative to property tax bill. For the July 1, 2026 tax billing: the assessed value on which the credit applies is $383,100; combined income eligibility limit is $76,620; net worth limit is $255,400. The progressive income scale ranges from 0% allowable percentage at up to $25,540 combined gross income to 8% at up to $53,630. Qualified retirement savings are excluded from the net worth calculation. No separate application is required — it is included when applying for the State Homeowners' Property Tax Credit. Combined with the Senior Property Tax Credit, averaged $1,276 last year and benefited 4,486 County residents. Taxpayers age 70+ may apply retroactively for the current and up to 3 prior levy years at any time.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: October 1st of the applicable tax year (taxpayers age 70+ may submit retroactive applications for the current and 3 prior levy years at any time)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners in Montgomery County who qualify for the Maryland State Homeowners' Property Tax Credit (HOTC), particularly those with household income relative to their property tax bill, including seniors age 70 or older who may apply retroactively.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of county real property tax liability (General County and Special Service Area taxes only).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland only.
requirements_list: Must be a homeowner in Montgomery County
Must qualify for the Maryland State Homeowners' Property Tax Credit (HOTC)
Household combined income must be at or below $76,620
Net worth must be at or below $255,400 (excluding principal property and qualified retirement savings)
Property assessed value eligible for the credit is up to $383,100
Must apply to SDAT by October 1st for the applicable tax year
Taxpayers age 70 or older may submit retroactive applications for the current and up to 3 prior levy years at any time
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: No additional application is needed beyond the State HOTC application. Apply for the Maryland State Homeowners' Property Tax Credit (HOTC) through the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) by October 1st of the applicable tax year. The county supplemental credit is automatically considered based on that application. Applications can be submitted online at the State's HOTC application portal. Copies of the governing bill are available from the Council Office in the Council Office Building, 100 Maryland Avenue, Rockville.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program helps property and business owners in Montgomery County improve the exteriors of their older commercial buildings. The county reimburses up to 50% of eligible costs for design and construction of approved facade improvements. Funding comes from the County's Capital Improvement Program (CIP) budget. In exchange, participants sign a facade easement agreement committing them to maintain the improvements for a set term. Eligible improvements include facade renovation, signage, LED lighting, streetscape elements, landscaping, murals, and other exterior amenities. Buildings must be 10 or more years old or not meet current commercial standards to qualify.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible property and business owners are reimbursed up to 50% of eligible costs for the design and construction of approved facade improvement projects, funded through the County's Capital Improvement Program (CIP) budget. After completion, participants must maintain improvements for a negotiated term through a facade easement agreement with the County. Technical support is also provided.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No full submission review until July 1, 2025, at the earliest
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners and business owners of older (10 or more years) commercial properties in Montgomery County seeking to improve their building exteriors, as well as community associations seeking facade improvements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Facade renovation and treatments, building and/or pylon signage, LED lighting, streetscape elements, landscape installation, art/mural installation, and other exterior amenities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to commercial property and business owners throughout Montgomery County, Maryland.

Applicant must be a property or business owner in Montgomery County
Participants must sign a facade easement agreement with the County to maintain improvements for a negotiated term after project completion

Due to funding limitations, the County was not reviewing projects for full submission and approval until July 1, 2025, at the earliest. Contact Kristina Ellis at Kristina.Ellis@montgomerycountymd.gov for more information.

Grants are prorated based on available funds and each business's share of total state tax credits received by all qualified businesses in the County.

structured_extraction.program_name: DC Central Kitchen Culinary Job Training
structured_extraction.program_description: A 14-week hands-on professional culinary training program designed to lead participants to full-time food service employment. The program provides practical skills, job placement support, and a 3-day evaluation period in various food-production stations followed by a probationary period.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 14-week hands-on culinary training program including a 3-day evaluation period in various food-production stations, job placement support, and preparation for full-time food service employment. Each enrollment cycle selects 20-25 candidates plus 5 waitlist candidates.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Culinary training, skill development, and job placement in the food service industry.

structured_extraction.program_name: DHCA Workforce Housing - Olney Springs (Project Site)
structured_extraction.program_description: A program that makes homes available at below-market prices to income-eligible households in Montgomery County. Homes are subject to a 20-year control period that limits resale prices, requires owner-occupancy, and restricts refinancing to protect long-term affordability. The program also allows workforce housing unit owners to receive credit for home improvements made to their properties for purposes of resale, refinance, home equity loan/line of credit, personal information, or foreclosure.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Homes are sold at below-market prices to income-eligible households. During the 20-year control period, the maximum resale price is calculated using the original base price plus a yearly CPI adjustment (based on the 10-year average percent change in CPI-U from date of purchase), plus the cost of options selected at purchase and allowable capital improvements. Refinancing is allowed but must not reduce the owner's equity below $10,000. Owners can also request credit for documented home improvements (permanent installations like appliances, flooring, decks, patios, heating/AC systems, accessibility improvements) to calculate adjusted resale prices or shared profit calculations; improvements must be permanent in nature with acceptable documentation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Income-eligible households seeking to purchase an affordable workforce housing home in the Olney Springs community in Montgomery County, MD, and existing Workforce Housing Unit (WFHU) owners seeking credit for home improvements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of a primary residence at a below-market price; home improvements (permanent installations like appliances, flooring, decks, patios, heating/AC systems, accessibility improvements) for credit toward resale price calculations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Limited to the Olney Springs development in Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must occupy the WFH home as your primary residence
Cannot rent out the home during the 20-year control period
Must sell the WFH home before purchasing other residential property in the Washington, DC Primary Metropolitan Statistical Area
Refinancing must not reduce owner's equity below $10,000
Must obtain written permission from DHCA before signing a listing agreement with a real estate agent
Must be income-eligible
Must provide receipts, cancelled checks, or other documentation verifying improvement costs
Must submit building permits for improvements requiring permits
Improvements must be permanent in nature
Documentation must be readable and show proof of payment
Receipts must detail work done and break out costs for each item
No credit for owner's labor
Physical deterioration or neglect may reduce improvement value
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To refinance or sell your WFH home, submit a written request for the current maximum control period resale price by email to WFH Intake, by fax to 240-777-3691, or by mail to WFH Program, DHCA, 1401 Rockville Pike, 4th Floor, Rockville, MD 20852. Include your name, email, phone number, an itemized list of allowable capital improvements, and invoices/receipts for those improvements. The WFH office has 21 days to respond by law but aims to respond within 10 days. To request credit for home improvements, submit a letter indicating the purpose (resale, refinance, home equity loan/line of credit, personal information, or foreclosure) along with supporting documentation including receipts, cancelled checks, and building permits where applicable.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Workforce Housing (WFH) Program helps families with incomes too high to qualify for the Moderately Priced Dwelling Unit (MPDU) Program find affordable homes in Montgomery County. It supports building and purchasing homes for households earning up to 120% of the area median income, with the goal of providing housing near jobs, reducing commutes, and helping employers attract workers who cannot afford to live close to where they work. The program sets income eligibility standards and maximum sale prices and rents by County Executive regulation, and defines where workforce housing must be located based on mandatory and optional zoning provisions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program makes homes available at below-market prices to eligible households. During a 20-year Control Period, owners must occupy the home as their primary residence and can only sell at prices set by DHCA to other qualified WFH buyers. Refinancing is limited to the DHCA-set resale price and must maintain at least $10,000 in equity. After the Control Period ends, owners who sell must pay half of any proceeds above the original WFH price to the County's Housing Initiative Fund. Rental Workforce Housing Units are also available through participating rental complexes. Maximum sale prices and rents are set by the County Executive by regulation.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Robert Love, Manager, Affordable Housing Programs Section
structured_extraction.program_audience: Households with incomes up to 120% of the area median income who do not qualify for the MPDU Program, including public workers and employees who cannot afford to live near their workplace in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase or rent a home at an affordable, below-market price in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Montgomery County, Maryland. Program encourages living near Metro Station Policy Areas. Housing must be located in areas defined by mandatory and optional zoning provisions.

Housing must be located in areas defined by mandatory and optional zoning provisions

structured_extraction.program_description: A Montgomery County real property tax credit for taxpayers who make improvements to real property used exclusively for day care services, including registered family day care homes, licensed childcare centers, licensed day care centers for the elderly, or licensed day care centers for the medically handicapped. The credit is limited to the lesser of $10,000 or the amount of General County and Special Area taxes attributable to the improvement, and is available to individual taxpayers as well as businesses with at least 25 employees.

The credit is limited to the lesser of $10,000 or the amount of General County and Special Area taxes attributable to the improvement. Available to individual taxpayers and businesses with at least 25 employees.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed or registered day care providers in Montgomery County; property owners whose improvements are used exclusively for qualifying day care services.

Apply with the Montgomery County Division of Treasury by April 1 to receive the credit in the following tax year

structured_extraction.program_description: Program to solve drainage problems where there is no storm drain system or the existing system is failing or is inadequate; addresses requests for assistance to correct drainage problems where runoff water originates from the public Right-of-Way on properties owned and maintained by Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: County staff investigate drainage problems, determine if the issue qualifies as a DAR project, calculate watershed size and water flow characteristics, and either implement a spot solution (design and schedule construction work) or recommend a comprehensive Capital Improvement Project (CIP) for County Executive and County Council approval. The county handles design, coordination, and construction through its own contractors. No direct financial payment is made to applicants. Requests in Gaithersburg and Rockville are referred to their respective DPWTs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners and communities in Montgomery County experiencing drainage problems caused by runoff from County-maintained properties and public Right-of-Way.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Drainage system improvements and repairs, including designing and constructing drainage improvements or spot solutions where runoff originates from the public right-of-way.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland only. The drainage problem must originate from the public Right-of-Way or County-owned/maintained properties. Requests in the municipalities of Gaithersburg and Rockville are referred to their respective DPWTs.
requirements_list: Drainage problem must be caused by runoff from the public Right-of-Way or County-owned/maintained property
No adequate storm drain system exists, or the existing system is failing or inadequate
Location of drainage problem
Description of problem, water origin, and destination
Photographs (helpful)
Requestor name, address, and phone number
Permission for County staff site visit
Availability to meet staff at site
Community or Homeowner Association information, if applicable
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a Drainage Request Form or contact the DTE Design Section by telephone, email, FAX, or letter. County staff will review the request, investigate the problem, and notify you of the findings and proposed action.

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County residents can replace deteriorated driveway aprons at the county's contract price when roadway or concrete rehabilitation projects are underway in their neighborhood. The county's contractor performs the work, and the cost is calculated per square foot based on unit prices set during the county's procurement process.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Residents can have their driveway apron replaced by the county's contractor at the county's contract price (priced per square foot) rather than paying full market rates. The program is available only when a roadway or concrete rehabilitation project is already underway in the neighborhood.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents with deteriorated driveway aprons located within the public right-of-way, in neighborhoods where county roadway or concrete rehabilitation projects are underway.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Replacement of the driveway apron — the portion of the driveway within the public right-of-way between the curb and the sidewalk or property line.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents in Montgomery County neighborhoods where active roadway or concrete rehabilitation projects are underway.
requirements_list: Driveway apron must be located in a neighborhood where a county roadway or concrete rehabilitation project is underway
A Highway Services inspector must determine the apron qualifies for replacement
Property owner is responsible for the cost of replacement at the county's contract unit price
Property owner is responsible for maintenance of the apron and any drainage pipe beneath it
Additional improvements outside the county right-of-way require permits from the Department of Permitting Services
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: A newsletter is sent to residents at the start of large-scale projects describing the program. A Highway Services inspector visits and leaves a notice on the door if the apron qualifies. If no notice is received but the resident believes their apron qualifies, they can contact the inspector working in the neighborhood or call 311 to request an inspection.

structured_extraction.program_name: Drop-In Conversation Classes – Gilchrist Immigrant Resource Center
structured_extraction.program_description: Free, no-registration-required conversation practice classes for intermediate and advanced English speakers living in Montgomery County. Offered year-round to help participants practice speaking English and learn new vocabulary.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free drop-in conversation classes offered year-round for intermediate and advanced English speakers. No registration required.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Intermediate and advanced English speakers living in Montgomery County, Maryland (age 18+)
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Practicing spoken English and building vocabulary through informal conversation classes
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must live in Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: No registration required
Intended for intermediate and advanced English speakers
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: No registration required. Simply drop in. Visit the Drop-In Conversation Classes page for schedule and location details.

structured_extraction.program_description: The ECOWISE program gives Montgomery County businesses that generate small amounts of hazardous waste an inexpensive and convenient way to dispose of hazardous materials. Businesses can drop off hazardous waste at the Shady Grove Processing Facility without complicated paperwork, and they save up to 75% compared to hiring a private hazardous waste pickup service. The program also provides guidance on federal, state, and county hazardous waste requirements, including waste reduction, storage, and disposal methods.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Businesses pay discounted per-pound fees (e.g. $0.58–$16.66/lb depending on material type) to dispose of hazardous waste at a county facility. This costs up to 75% less than using a private hazardous waste contractor. No pre-registration fee, no minimum quantity, and no contractual obligation. Payment is by credit card (with up to 3% surcharge) or business check made out to Clean Harbors Environmental Services. The program also accepts up to 100 kilograms (approximately 220 pounds) of acids, bases, pesticides, fuels, solvents, oil-based paints, photographic chemicals, oxidizers, reactive materials, and batteries. Does not accept acute hazardous wastes, radioactive materials, explosives, or medical waste. Additionally provides guidance on identifying, packaging, labeling, and transporting hazardous waste, emergency response procedures, and regulatory compliance information.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County businesses and non-profit organizations that generate less than 220 pounds (100 kg) of hazardous waste per calendar month (State of Maryland-defined Small Quantity Generators or SQGs), including industries such as print shops, service stations, dry cleaners, construction, equipment repair, furniture refinishing, landscaping, laboratories, auto body shops, and others.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Disposal of hazardous materials including acids, bases, batteries, fluorescent bulbs, fuels, mercury products, oxidizers, paints, pesticides, solvents, and other accepted hazardous waste categories. Also covers waste reduction strategies, proper storage, and regulatory compliance support.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to businesses located in Montgomery County, Maryland. Drop-off is at the Shady Grove Processing Facility and Transfer Station, 16101 Frederick Rd, Derwood, MD 20855 (near the intersection of Maryland Route 355 and Shady Grove Road in Derwood, Maryland).
requirements_list: Must be a non-residential entity (business or non-profit organization)
Must generate less than 220 pounds (100 kg) of hazardous waste per calendar month
Must generate less than 2.2 pounds (1 kg) of acute hazardous waste per month
Must register for the program (registration is free)
Cannot bring more than 220 pounds of hazardous waste per visit
Must not be a federally defined Small Quantity Generator (i.e., must not produce between 220 and 2,200 pounds per year)
Must comply with RCRA regulations
Must comply with Maryland COMAR 26.13 regulations
Must comply with Montgomery County Executive Regulation 19-93 AM
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register for free online at the ECOWISE registration form or by completing the PDF paper application and returning it signed to Mike Fisher by email or mail. Once registered, conduct a hazardous waste audit using the Ecowise Guide. If your audit confirms you generate less than 220 pounds per calendar month, you may begin using the program. Drop off is Monday–Friday, 8am–12pm at the Shady Grove HHW compound; no appointment needed. Annual hazardous waste report forms are mailed to generators by late January.

structured_extraction.program_name: ESOL English Classes – Gilchrist Immigrant Resource Center
structured_extraction.program_description: Free or low-cost English for Speakers of Other Languages (ESOL) classes offered to adult immigrants and non-native English speakers in Montgomery County. Classes are available in person and online via Zoom at multiple proficiency levels (Basic through Level 4) and meet for 8 weeks per session. Also offers Basic Computer Skills, English Conversation, and Citizenship Preparation classes. Registration is required and placement is first-come, first-served.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free or low-cost English language instruction at multiple proficiency levels (Basic through Level 4). Also offers Basic Computer Skills, English Conversation, and Citizenship Preparation classes. Online Saturday classes are free. In-person and online evening classes require a $35 textbook fee; no textbook required for Saturday online or Gaithersburg classes. Classes meet for 8 weeks per session beginning first week of May 2026. Most classes are taught online via Zoom; limited in-person options are available in Wheaton and Gaithersburg. Referrals to food assistance, health care/insurance, housing information, immigration legal services, and job training are also available. Space is limited and filled on a first-come, first-served basis.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on a first-come, first-served basis starting at 6:00 pm on April 2nd, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adult immigrants (age 18+) and non-native English speakers living in Montgomery County, Maryland seeking to improve their English language skills.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: English language instruction at multiple proficiency levels through structured ESOL classes, as well as basic computer skills training and citizenship preparation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must live in Montgomery County, Maryland. Classes are held at locations in Wheaton and Gaithersburg, and online via Zoom.
requirements_list: Must live in Montgomery County, Maryland
Must be 18 years old or older
Complete an online application
Take an online placement test
Placement is first-come, first-served; space is limited
Regular attendance is required
Students may not register for both Evening and Saturday classes
Some classes require a $35 textbook purchase; others (Saturday online and Gaithersburg classes) do not
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Registration is required online only. Complete the online application (available in English, Spanish, and French) and take a placement test. Test results determine the class level. Registration for Spring 2026 opened April 2, 2026 at 6:00 p.m. on a first-come, first-served basis. Visit the program page for registration instructions and information about local classes and independent study resources.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program through Montgomery County's Department of Health and Human Services that connects East County residents to county services and community resources, including help applying for state and federal benefits, referrals for clothing and employment, and emergency financial assistance requests.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free coordination services including help applying for state and federal benefits, referrals for clothing and employment, and submission of emergency financial assistance requests. Services provided on-site at the East County Regional Services Center, off-site in the community, or virtually.

structured_extraction.program_name: Eat Well Be Active Partnership (EWBA) / Transforming Communities Initiative (TCI)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Eat Well Be Active Partnership (EWBA) is a county-wide collaborative that implements chronic disease prevention strategies in Montgomery County. It provides funding through the Transforming Communities Initiative (TCI), a multi-year effort to reduce obesity, promote tobacco-free living, and address social factors that impact community health. TCI focuses on policy, systems, and environmental changes in specific communities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: TCI provides funding to implement and support community health improvement goals and objectives, with a focus on policy, systems, and environmental changes that reduce obesity, promote tobacco-free living, and address social determinants of health.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community organizations, government agencies, and partners working to improve health outcomes in Montgomery County, particularly in Gaithersburg, Germantown, Long Branch, and Takoma Park.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Implementing public health strategies to reduce obesity, promote tobacco-free living, and address social factors that impact community health through policy, systems, and environmental changes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Primarily focused on the communities of Gaithersburg, Germantown, Long Branch, and Takoma Park in Montgomery County, Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Montgomery County fund that provides financial assistance to support economic development. The regulation (Executive Regulation 9-14AM under Montgomery County Code Section 20-76) establishes the award criteria and process for administering the fund, governing how financial assistance is awarded to eligible businesses and organizations in the county.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance (including grants and loans) awarded through the Economic Development Fund based on criteria and processes established by Executive Regulation 9-14AM under Montgomery County Code Section 20-76. Specific amounts and terms are determined by the fund's award criteria.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses and organizations seeking economic development assistance in Montgomery County, MD
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Economic development activities in Montgomery County as determined by the fund's award criteria
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must meet award criteria established in Executive Regulation 9-14AM under Montgomery County Code Section 20-76
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Montgomery County Department of Economic Development for a copy of the regulation and application procedures. Written comments or requests for copies of the proposed regulation may also be submitted to Gene Smith at the Department of Economic Development, Finance and Administration, 111 Rockville Pike, Suite 800, Rockville, Maryland 20850.

structured_extraction.program_name: Economic Development Fund Grant & Loan Program (EDFGLP)
structured_extraction.program_description: The EDFGLP is a discretionary program for attracting and retaining businesses in targeted industry sectors that generate significant economic impact in Montgomery County, such as job growth and retention or capital investment. Priority is given to high technology companies, manufacturing companies, businesses in urban revitalization areas, and private employers providing the greatest public benefits. Awards include conditions for disbursement, minimum performance measures, and clawback provisions if a business fails to meet expected economic output. The program typically provides assistance from $5,000 to $100,000, though larger projects may receive more.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Discretionary grants and/or loans awarded to private employers who retain or create jobs and generate significant economic development impact in Montgomery County. The program typically provides assistance from $5,000 to $100,000, with larger projects potentially receiving more. Awards include conditions for disbursement, minimum performance measures, and clawback provisions if a business fails to meet expected economic output.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private employers and businesses in targeted industry sectors that generate significant economic development impact in Montgomery County, including high technology companies, manufacturers, and businesses in urban revitalization areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Job growth and retention, capital investment, and other economic development activities in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in Montgomery County, Maryland. Priority is given to businesses located in urban revitalization areas.
requirements_list: Must be a private employer
Must retain existing jobs or stimulate job creation in Montgomery County
Must be in a targeted industry sector
Must generate significant economic development impact such as job growth/retention or capital expenditure
Must show projected job growth or capital investment.
Must provide financial history and projections, including balance sheets, income statements, and cash flow statements.
Must provide company and management background.
Must provide a present and future market outlook.
Priority is given to projects that create significant new jobs within 1 to 3 years.
Priority is given to projects that result in significant capital investment.
Priority is given to projects that leverage existing state and private funding.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Montgomery County Business Portal at montgomerycountymd.gov/businesses/business-resources/business-funding-incentives.

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County issues tax-exempt Economic Development Revenue Bonds to help businesses and non-profit organizations finance capital projects such as constructing or acquiring facilities and equipment. The County acts as a conduit for the bond financing, meaning the debt is repaid by the borrower, not the County. Montgomery County participates in both the Maryland Industrial Development Financing Authority (MIDFA) and Economic Development Revenue Bond (EDRB) programs to help fund facilities, manufacturing, solid waste disposal, low-income housing, and other qualifying projects for non-profit organizations and selected for-profit businesses that want to locate or expand operations within the County.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax-exempt bond financing (Economic Development Revenue Bonds or Industrial Revenue Bonds) issued on a case-by-case basis as conduit bonds. Bonds are not backed by the full faith and credit or taxing power of Montgomery County. A non-refundable application fee of $5,000 is charged at filing. An annual administrative fee of 10 basis points of the original bond issue amount is due at closing and each year the bonds are outstanding. All legal and administrative costs are borne by the borrower regardless of whether financing is completed. The amount and term of financing are determined by the project needs as described in the application.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations (501(c)(3) entities) and selected for-profit businesses seeking to locate or expand in Montgomery County, including schools, medical/health organizations, manufacturers, and businesses with positive economic impact on the County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction or acquisition of facilities, purchase of equipment, rehabilitation of existing structures, small manufacturing, solid waste disposal, low-income housing, and other qualifying projects that comply with federal tax-exempt financing rules, as well as related project costs such as architectural, engineering, financing, and legal fees.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located within Montgomery County, Maryland. For-profit applicants must be located in or relocating to Montgomery County, or demonstrate economic benefit to the County.
requirements_list: Submit a $5,000 non-refundable application fee (check payable to Montgomery County, remitted to the Director of Finance)
Provide three years of financial statements (audited preferred) and interim statements
Submit a Letter of Good Standing from the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation at the time of application
Non-profits must be qualified under Section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code and provide a copy of their IRS Determination Letter prior to bond closing
Underwriter must provide a letter confirming the project is financially feasible
Non-collegiate educational institutions must hold a Certificate of Approval from the State Board of Education (or an exemption determination)
Medical or health service organizations must be properly licensed by applicable government authorities
Religious organizations must obtain a letter of preliminary advice from the County's bond counsel regarding constitutional limits on tax-exempt financing
For-profit businesses and/or their landlords must pay County property taxes and be current on all amounts owed to the County and State
Projects must be non-speculative (developed for a specific occupant)
Projects must comply with federally mandated tax legislation restricting use of tax-exempt financing
For-profit projects must have a positive economic and fiscal impact on the County
Provide background information on the organization, project description, employment data, and a statement of benefits to Montgomery County
Submit a proposed financing term sheet and financing structure
Disclose status of all government approvals (zoning, permits, land use) and any legal issues related to the project
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Borrower completes application and submits required materials plus the $5,000 non-refundable application fee to the Department of Finance; a copy goes to the County's bond counsel. 2. Department of Finance reviews the application against eligibility criteria on a case-by-case basis and requests a Letter of Intent from the borrower; bond counsel drafts a County Council Resolution. 3. Department of Finance holds a TEFRA/public hearing and forwards its recommendation to the County Executive. 4. If the County Executive accepts, the Resolution is forwarded to the County Council. 5. County Council acts on the Resolution. The entire process takes a minimum of approximately 6 weeks. All legal and administrative costs are borne by the applicant.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides GED and Pre-GED education classes, volunteer tutoring, and referrals to community literacy and English as a Second Language (ESL) programs for individuals in the Pre-Release and Reentry Services program. Classes are offered four nights per week through a partnership with Montgomery College.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive Pre-GED and GED classes four nights per week taught through Montgomery College, one-on-one volunteer tutoring for those below Pre-GED level, and referrals to community services such as the Montgomery County Literacy Council and ESL programs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals enrolled in the Pre-Release and Reentry Services program in Montgomery County who need GED preparation or basic literacy skills.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: GED and Pre-GED instruction, individual tutoring, and referrals to literacy and ESL programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a participant in the Pre-Release and Reentry Services (PRRS) program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Participants are referred to education services through the Pre-Release and Reentry Services program at 11651 Nebel Street, Rockville, Maryland 20852.

structured_extraction.program_name: Electric Leaf Blower Rebate Program (Incentive Program for Electric Leaf Removal Equipment)
structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County Department of Environmental Protection offers a time-limited rebate/reimbursement incentive program to help residents and businesses offset the cost of purchasing new electric leaf blowers and electric leaf removal equipment. The program is established under Montgomery County Executive Regulation No. 1-24 and supports the county's ban on gas-powered leaf blowers effective July 1, 2025. Rebate amounts: Residents up to $100; Revenue-qualifying businesses up to $1,500 per 12-month period; Non-revenue-qualifying businesses up to $1,000 per 12-month period. Applications are expected to open July 1, 2026 and close no later than December 31, 2026.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Partial reimbursement/rebate for the purchase of new electric leaf removal equipment (handheld, backpack, or walk-behind devices powered by battery or cord, as well as batteries, chargers, and leaf vacuums). Rebate amounts: Residents up to $100; Revenue-qualifying businesses (annual revenue <$250,000 or ≤5 employees) up to $1,500 per 12-month period; Non-revenue-qualifying businesses (annual revenue ≥$250,000 or ≥6 employees) up to $1,000 per 12-month period. Applications open July 1, 2026 and close no later than December 31, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents (individuals who own or rent and maintain their property) and leaf removal businesses operating in Montgomery County (individuals or entities earning income using leaf removal equipment for paid work with a business mailing address in Montgomery County).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of electric leaf removal equipment including battery-powered or corded handheld blowers, backpack blowers, walk-behind blowers, leaf vacuums, batteries, and chargers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must have a Montgomery County street mailing address. Available to residents and businesses in Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must have a Montgomery County street mailing address
Residents must own or rent and maintain their property in Montgomery County
Businesses must operate a leaf removal business with a Montgomery County business mailing address
Revenue-qualifying businesses must have annual revenue less than $250,000 or 5 or fewer employees
Non-revenue-qualifying businesses must have annual revenue of $250,000 or more or 6 or more employees
Must purchase new electric leaf removal equipment (handheld, backpack, or walk-behind devices powered by battery or cord)
Application must be submitted no later than December 31, 2026
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications open on July 1, 2026 and must be submitted no later than December 31, 2026. Check for updates in June 2026. Applications and inquiries may be submitted to LeafBlowerRebateProgram@montgomerycountymd.gov or to Mary Travaglini at the Department of Environmental Protection, 2425 Reedie Drive, 4th Floor, Wheaton, Maryland, 20902. The full regulation document is available at https://assets.montgomerycountymd.gov/files/1-24.pdf.

structured_extraction.program_description: A pilot program that helps Montgomery County residents switch from fossil fuels (oil, gas, and propane) to electric appliances in their homes. The program provides a one-stop option including energy audits, technical support, direct installation services, and financial incentives applied at the point of sale for qualifying electric appliances like heat pumps, water heaters, stoves, and dryers. It is designed to help residents reduce utility bills and carbon emissions while facilitating the transition away from fossil fuel heating and appliances.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Direct incentives applied at the point of sale toward the cost of electrification upgrades, plus technical assistance and energy audits. Incentive amounts vary by appliance: Ducted Heat Pump $1,000; Mini-Split Heat Pump $2,000; Cold-Climate Heat Pump $2,500; Geothermal Heat Pump $2,000; Heat Pump Water Heater $500; Electric Range/Cooktop $500; Electric Clothes Dryer $250; Whole House Surge Protector $200; Single-appliance surge protector (hardwired) $100; Natural gas line capping permit $165; Oil tank removal $500; Add-on incentive of $1,000 for electrifying two fossil fuel appliances that share a flue. Work must be completed by the County-selected contractor, Elysian Energy.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents who use fossil fuels (oil, gas, or propane) in their homes and want to switch to electric appliances to reduce utility bills and carbon emissions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of electric appliances replacing fossil-fuel equivalents, including heat pumps, heat pump water heaters, electric stoves/cooktops, electric dryers, surge protectors, natural gas line capping, and oil tank removal.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a residence located in Montgomery County, Maryland with individually metered utilities.
requirements_list: Must be a homeowner or resident in Montgomery County
Must currently use fossil fuels (oil, gas, or propane)
Must be a residence located in Montgomery County, Maryland
Must have individually metered utilities
Effective July 16, 2024: must replace a fossil-fueled equivalent appliance
Work must be coordinated and completed by Elysian Energy to qualify for Electrify MC incentives
Incentives cannot be received retroactively
Appliances must meet minimum efficiency standards (e.g., CEE Tier 1 or ENERGY STAR where specified)
For mini-split heat pumps, must cover 50% or more of total heating load
For heat pump or range incentives, fossil fuel heating/combustion appliances must be removed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Sign up by completing the Montgomery County Electrify Everything Pledge online form, or contact the Electrify MC Help Desk by phone at 301-830-5767 or email at electrifymc@elysianenergy.com. The Electrify MC team will call and email you to walk through the process. Next steps typically include scheduling an energy audit, reviewing electrification options, and having work completed by Elysian Energy. Incentives are applied directly on the invoice at the point of sale.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Grocery purchases

requirements_list: Must have experienced a sudden benefit disruption or have pending program enrollment
Must be referred through an NBO grantee partner organization

structured_extraction.program_name: Emergency Medical Transportation Insurance Reimbursement Act
structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County Fire and Rescue Service (MCFRS) bills private health insurance companies, Medicare, or Medicaid directly for ambulance transport services. Montgomery County residents are not required to pay any out-of-pocket expenses (co-payments, deductibles, or uninsured portions) for emergency medical services (EMS) transport provided by MCFRS. Revenue collected is used to fund equipment, enhancements, and training for MCFRS.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Montgomery County residents who receive ambulance transport from MCFRS pay no out-of-pocket costs (no co-payment, deductible, or uninsured portion). The county bills third-party payers (private insurance, Medicare, or Medicaid) directly. Residents must provide insurance information and sign an assignment of benefits allowing the county to submit claims on their behalf.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents who receive emergency medical services (ambulance) transport from MCFRS and have private health insurance, Medicare, or Medicaid coverage.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Covers the cost of emergency medical services ambulance transport; residents pay no out-of-pocket expenses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Montgomery County, Maryland residents only.
requirements_list: Must be a Montgomery County resident
Must have received ambulance transport from MCFRS
Must provide health insurance and/or other applicable insurance information to the county upon request
Must sign an assignment of benefits to allow the county to submit a claim to the applicable third-party payer
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: If asked to provide additional insurance information about your ambulance transport, call 888-874-0813. For further questions, contact MCFRS.EMSBilling@montgomerycountymd.gov or the Patient Advocate at 240-777-3636.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Emergency Solutions Grant (ESG) program provides federal funds to support emergency shelter and services for people experiencing homelessness. Montgomery County is the prime recipient of federal ESG funds through DHCA, and the program is administered by the Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services (MCDHHS) in coordination with DHCA.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Montgomery County received approximately $400,000 in ESG funds in fiscal year 2026 (July 2025–June 2026). Funds are integrated into the Montgomery County Continuum of Care (CoC) activities and administered by MCDHHS under a memorandum of understanding with DHCA.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations providing emergency shelter and services for people experiencing homelessness in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Emergency shelter, services for people experiencing homelessness, and related Continuum of Care activities
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Montgomery County, MD
requirements_list: Must align with the Montgomery County Continuum of Care (CoC) activities
ESG funds administered under a memorandum of understanding between MCDHHS and DHCA
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For more information, email housingforall@montgomerycountymd.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: Vision benefits program providing coverage for eye exams, eyeglass frames and lenses, contact lenses, progressive lenses, anti-reflective coatings, and related vision care services through a network of eye care providers. Includes tiered benefit structures for progressive lenses (Tiers 1-5) and anti-reflective coatings (Tiers 1-3), blue light filtering lens materials, and backside UV coating options. Employees can use the participating EyeMed provider network (nearly 82,000 in-network providers nationwide) for higher benefit levels or submit out-of-network claims within 15 months of the date of service.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement and coverage for routine eye exams, eyeglass frames, lenses, contact lenses, progressive lenses, anti-reflective coatings, blue light filtering lens materials, and backside UV coating. Members save an average of 72% off retail prices when combining eye exam and new glasses; additional discounts on multiple pairs (40% off), sunglasses (20% off), and frame allowances (up to 20% off). Using the EyeMed participating provider network provides higher benefits than the non-network schedule. Out-of-network claims must be submitted within 15 months of the date of service.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County government employees
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Vision care services including routine eye exams, eyeglass frames, lenses, contact lenses, progressive lenses, anti-reflective coatings, blue light filtering, and UV protection
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Montgomery County, MD government employees; access to nearly 82,000 in-network providers nationwide
requirements_list: Must be a Montgomery County employee
Must follow specific steps outlined in the benefit booklet to qualify for network benefit
Must submit out-of-network claims within 15 months of the date of service
Must have out-of-network benefits to submit an out-of-network claim
Driver's license or Social Security Number required at time of service
ID card not required but available upon request
Member must select from approved lens and coating product lists when applicable
Copays and amounts over allowances are member responsibility

structured_extraction.program_name: FY25 Food Recovery Network Infrastructure Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This grant program funds non-profit food recovery organizations to build capacity in Montgomery County's food recovery network. It supports collaborative and shared-use projects that expand food recovery operations—including transportation and cold storage capacity—to enable partners to recover, store, and distribute more fresh and perishable foods. The program focuses on diverting food from the waste stream through donation to community-based organizations, supporting food recovery runs, redistribution to partner organizations, and direct-to-resident food distribution. Goals include establishing new donor relationships, increasing access to higher-value food products, reducing climate impacts of food recovery, and leveraging external investment. $306,000 was awarded across four organizations: AfriThrive, Nourish Now, Rainbow Community Development Center, and So What Else.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: $306,000 total awarded to four organizations (AfriThrive, Nourish Now, Rainbow Community Development Center, and So What Else) for refrigerated vehicles and shared cold storage units to expand food recovery infrastructure across Montgomery County. Funds support infrastructure purchases (refrigeration, shelving, vehicles, pallet jacks, etc.), staff costs (program coordination, logistics, administration), and indirect/operational expenses for food recovery activities including transport, storage, and distribution of recovered food as part of a three-part food recovery strategy.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit food recovery and redistribution organizations, community-based organizations, and volunteer-based organizations operating in Montgomery County, Maryland, as well as Montgomery County residents receiving food assistance
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Infrastructure purchases (capital/durable goods for food recovery and distribution capacity including refrigerated vehicles, cold storage units, shelving, pallet jacks, etc.), staff costs (program coordination, logistics, administration), indirect costs (administrative expenses supporting operations), establishing new donor relationships, increasing access to higher-value and limited-availability food products, reducing climate impacts of the food recovery and assistance network, and leveraging external investment and resources.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland (primary focus); DMV-based organizations eligible for local sourcing metrics
requirements_list: Projects must reflect collaborative, shared-use approaches
Must support capacity building of the overall food recovery network

Must leverage external investment and/or resources

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides funding to one umbrella (lead) organization to design, implement, and manage a countywide collaborative initiative delivering comprehensive services to socioeconomically disadvantaged individuals and families navigating challenges related to immigration status in Montgomery County. Services include navigation, guidance, emergency support, and intensive case management to connect individuals and families to housing, healthcare, education, and immigration legal services. The program is a recurring annual grant competition, with FY26 and FY27 cycles, administered by Montgomery County's Department of Health and Human Services and Office of Grants Management. Organizations apply through the ecivis grants portal in response to a Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: $3,504,636.00 in County funds awarded to one umbrella (lead) organization to design, implement, and manage a countywide collaborative service initiative. Eligible costs include personnel, fringe benefits, travel and transportation stipends, equipment, supplies, contractual services/training/licenses, formalized partner organization costs, construction/renovation, indirect costs (up to 15% or approved federal NICRA rate), and sub-grants to community-based organizations. The project period runs October 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026, with a potential one-time no-cost extension until October 1, 2026. Specific amounts for future cycles are subject to the approved Operating Budget.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides subsidies to cover facility rental fees at county public schools and other county buildings for nonprofit organizations that offer direct services or benefits to vulnerable youth or low-income individuals in Montgomery County. The program encourages and helps underserved communities use public facilities at reduced or no cost. It is created by the County Executive and administered by the Director of the Office of Community Use of Public Facilities (CUPF). Also known as the Facility Fee Assistance Program (FFAP) and the Community Use of Public Facility Subsidy.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Subsidies cover facility use fees at eligible county spaces. The maximum annual award is $5,400 (as of FY18), enough to fund an afterschool program two or three times a week for a full school year or an ongoing Saturday program. Awards are contingent on available funding and are valid only for the fiscal year in which they are granted. Organizations may submit multiple applications per year up to the annual maximum.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted at any time until funds run out; allow minimum 30 days for processing
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland-based nonprofit 501(c)(3) organizations whose mission is to serve vulnerable youth (ages 12-18 at risk for a competent transition to adulthood) or low-income individuals in Montgomery County, as well as organizations and individuals serving underserved communities seeking to use public facilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Covers facility rental fees for programs providing direct services or benefits to vulnerable youth or low-income individuals. Cannot be used for fundraising, internal administrative or staff meetings, or activities that only benefit the organization or its membership (e.g., church services or lectures to club members).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Programs must serve vulnerable youth or low-income individuals in Montgomery County. Eligible spaces include county public schools (especially Title I or high-FARMS schools), public libraries, county office buildings (Executive and Council), Clarksburg Cottage, Regional Service Centers, and the District 3 Police Station. Does not cover gyms, stadium fields, auditoriums, kitchens, equipment, or MCPS support staff.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Maryland-based nonprofit 501(c)(3) organization or qualify as a nonprofit under IRS standards
Organization's mission must be to serve vulnerable youth or low-income individuals in Montgomery County
Program or activity must provide direct services or benefits to vulnerable youth or low-income individuals in Montgomery County
Program must serve underserved communities with a focus on vulnerable youth and low-income persons
Preferred: program provides direct service in a Title I or high-FARMS county school or economically disadvantaged area
Preferred: program is free or reduced cost to participants
Preferred: program is led by volunteers
Preferred: applicant is a first-time applicant
Organization must report back to CUPF after program completion on the number of individuals served
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Review subsidy criteria to confirm eligibility. 2. Complete the online Request Form. 3. Submit completed application online, by mail to 255 Rockville Pike Suite 201 Rockville MD 20850, or by email. 4. After a room use permit is approved via ActiveMONTGOMERY.org, contact CUPF to apply the subsidy. Applications are reviewed by staff and then forwarded to a review committee. The CUPF Director makes the final award decision.

structured_extraction.program_description: Allows landlords of rent-stabilized properties in Montgomery County experiencing financial hardship — such as reduced net operating income or increased operating expenses — to apply for a rent increase above the annual allowable limit.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: If approved, DHCA determines a Fair Return Increase amount that stays in effect for 12 months. If the approved increase is 15% or less, it may be implemented within 12 months of approval or at lease renewal, whichever is later. If greater than 15%, the increase must be phased in over consecutive years. For vacant units resulting from a voluntary move-out or just cause termination, the full increase may be applied in one year or upon re-rental. No additional annual rent increase is permitted during the 12-month period, but a capital improvement surcharge may be applied concurrently if applicable.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landlords of regulated rental properties in Montgomery County experiencing financial hardship due to reduced net operating income or increased operating expenses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Allows rent increases above the annual allowable limit to achieve a fair return on the rental property.

Any banked rent must be fully applied to the regulated units before applying
Property must be a regulated rental property
Applications and required documentation must be submitted via the Rental Housing Portal
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application and all required documentation through the Montgomery County Rental Housing Portal. Sample application forms are available on the Applications and Forms page.

structured_extraction.program_description: The FareShare Program promotes the use of public transit and vanpooling among employees working in Montgomery County by matching employer contributions toward commuting costs. Montgomery County reimburses participating private-sector and non-profit employers for the portion of the transit benefit above the minimum $25 per employee per month, up to $325 per month per employee (the federal maximum as of January 1, 2025), less the employer's own contribution. The maximum county reimbursement is $40,000 per year per employer. Employers can also earn a Maryland Commuter Choice Tax Credit of 50% of their contribution, up to $100 per employee per month, lowering their own taxes. The program encourages employers to provide transit subsidies for their workers, helping reduce single-occupancy vehicle trips, traffic congestion, and pollution across Montgomery County's Transportation Management Districts. Employees receive transit subsidies up to $325 per month tax-free. Pre-tax payroll deductions and SmartBenefits are also available. Public sector employers and employees, as well as federal workers who already receive transit benefits from their employer or agency, are not eligible. The program received $500,000 in funding in the FY20 budget.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Montgomery County reimburses participating private-sector and non-profit employers for transit and vanpool subsidies provided to employees. Reimbursement covers the portion of the transit benefit above the minimum $25 per employee per month, up to the federal maximum of $325 per month per employee, less the employer's own contribution. The maximum county reimbursement is $40,000 per year per employer. Employers can also earn a Maryland Commuter Choice Tax Credit of 50% of their contribution, up to $100 per employee per month. Employees receive transit subsidies up to $325 per month tax-free beginning January 1, 2025. Pre-tax payroll deductions and SmartBenefits are also available. Public sector employers/employees and federal workers already receiving transit benefits are not eligible. Program is contingent on availability of funds.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private-sector and non-profit employers with employees working in Montgomery County who want to offer or enhance transit and vanpool commuting benefits, as well as employees seeking to reduce commuting costs. Employees do not need to live in Montgomery County — only the employer must be located there. Public sector employers/employees are ineligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Employee transit and vanpool commuting subsidies. Funds reimburse the employer's contribution toward employees' monthly transit or vanpool costs, and employees receive tax-free transit subsidies to reduce single-occupancy vehicle commuting.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Employer must be located in or have employees working in Montgomery County, Maryland. Employees may live anywhere but must work for an employer located in Montgomery County. Public sector employers and employees are not eligible.

Employer must offer a minimum transit benefit of $25 per employee per month
Total benefit provided to any employee cannot exceed their actual commuting cost (federal law)
Employees must use transit or vanpool for commuting
Employee must not already receive transit benefits from an employer or agency (federal workers with existing transit benefits are ineligible)
Employer must complete the FareShare Employer Enrollment Form

Employer must conduct a pre-program employee survey before implementation
Employer must participate in Commuter Surveys every other year

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Employers contact Commuter Services by phone at 240-773-2989 or email at mcdot.commuterservices@montgomerycountymd.gov to receive the FareShare Employer Enrollment Form. Marketing specialists will visit the employer's office free of charge to help set up a commuting benefits program tailored to the company's needs. 2. After enrollment, submit the Employer Worksheet Invoice and WMATA SmartBenefits Order Confirmation Form. 5. Receive reimbursement from the county. Employees can also ask their employer to contact MCDOT to get started. A downloadable brochure is available at https://assets.montgomerycountymd.gov/files/BWTW_FareShareBrochure_June2024%281%29.pdf for additional details.

structured_extraction.program_description: The HOME Investment Partnership Program increases affordable housing choices for low-income households in Montgomery County by supporting the development of rental housing and homeownership opportunities. HOME funds support affordable housing production and preservation, including construction, acquisition, rehabilitation of housing units, and tenant-based rental assistance. The program targets deeply affordable units, requiring that 90% of rental units serve households at or below 60% of Area Median Income (AMI), with 20% at or below 50% AMI for projects with more than five units. Homeownership projects can assist persons earning up to 80% AMI. Montgomery County received approximately $2 million in HOME funds in fiscal year 2026 (July 2025–June 2026). Funds are loaned to non-profit and for-profit developers and may also be provided as grants or subsidies.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Montgomery County received approximately $2 million in HOME funds in fiscal year 2026 (July 2025–June 2026). Funds can be used for affordable housing construction, acquisition, rehabilitation, and tenant-based rental assistance. Funds may be provided as loans or grants/subsidies to eligible developers. Funds must be tied to individual units monitored for up to 20 years, and there is an annual maximum subsidy per unit. Funds must be proportional to the number of HOME units in a project. If other federal funds are in a project, a subsidy layering review must be completed before commitment of funds. Federal Davis-Bacon prevailing wage rates apply for projects with 12 or more units.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Focused Neighborhood Assistance (FNA) Program helps low- and moderate-income homeowner and condominium associations in Montgomery County improve common areas. Using Community Development Block Grant (CDBG), Capital Improvement Project (CIP), and Maryland Community Legacy Grant funds, the program provides financial and technical assistance for neighborhood improvement construction projects. Eligible projects include health and safety improvements, energy-efficient lighting, ADA compliance upgrades, neighborhood courtyard enhancements, and other common area repairs. DHCA covers 100% of architectural, engineering, and management service costs, plus up to 80% of construction costs, with participating associations contributing 20% of final construction costs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: DHCA covers 100% of architectural, engineering, and management service costs, plus 80% of construction costs using CDBG, CIP, and/or Maryland Community Legacy Grant funds. Participating community associations must contribute 20% of final construction costs upfront. The funding mix may vary year to year. For example, a $100,000 FY19 Community Legacy Grant supported balcony replacements for low-to-moderate income households at Kimberly Place Condominiums in Silver Spring.

structured_extraction.program_name: Food Aggregation Grant Program (FY26 Stage One & Stage Two)
structured_extraction.program_description: A Montgomery County grant program that provides funding to local food aggregation and distribution companies and organizations with experience in market development for small farmers to establish and maintain a facility in Montgomery County, with the goal of improving food access and distribution throughout the county. The facility will aggregate, distribute, and market food grown by regional farmers to wholesale markets including schools, senior centers, hospitals, food banks, and correctional facilities. The program operates in two stages: Stage One is an eligibility assessment submitted through the ecivis grants portal, and Stage Two is a fit and alignment assessment open on an invitation-only basis to applicants who complete Stage One. Stage Two awards $550,000 in year one for operating and build-out costs to establish a local food aggregation facility meeting current and future wholesale and institutional market demand.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Multi-year grant program with two stages. Stage One provides grant funding to food aggregation and distribution companies and organizations to establish, maintain, and operate food aggregation and distribution activities in Montgomery County. Stage Two, available on an invitation-only basis to Stage One applicants, awards $550,000 for the initial one-year program period (performance period June 30, 2026 - June 30, 2030) for operating and build-out/capital costs to establish a local food aggregation facility. Additional assistance includes guaranteed purchases of Montgomery County products by the County government pending performance. Funds are disbursed on a reimbursement basis or fixed schedule after documentation submission, and must be spent after contract finalization and Notice to Proceed.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Office of Food Systems Resilience (OFSR) awards funding to support the design, implementation, and ongoing coordination of a centralized Montgomery County Food Recovery Network (FRN). The grant funds a central coordinating organization to manage and coordinate the network, strengthen partnerships and collaboration across food recovery operators, convene food recovery organizations, facilitate data and resource sharing, identify efficiency opportunities, and manage the transport, storage, and distribution of recovered food to residents in Montgomery County. The program aims to improve operational efficiency at the organizational and network levels, leverage new resources, and boost collaboration across the food recovery ecosystem. Also referred to as the FY26 Food Recovery Network Coordination (FRNC) Grant, the program is expected to launch June 2025.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A grant (up to $30,000) awarded to serve as the primary coordinating organization for the Montgomery County Food Recovery Network/Collaborative, funding coordination and management activities including design, implementation, ongoing network coordination, convening food recovery partners, facilitating data and resource sharing, improving operational efficiency, leveraging new resources, and supporting transport, storage, and distribution of recovered food to residents.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Design, implementation, and ongoing coordination of a centralized food recovery network; convening food recovery partners; facilitating data and resource sharing; identifying collaboration and efficiency opportunities; improving operational efficiency; leveraging new resources; and managing transport, storage, and distribution of recovered food to residents.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program funds healthcare and clinic-led initiatives that screen pediatric patients for food insecurity and provide nutritious food and nutrition education services. It aims to address gaps in nutrition security and diet-related health challenges by increasing access to culturally diverse, medically relevant, nutritious, and locally produced food for children and families in underserved communities in Montgomery County. Programs must be anchored in healthcare/clinic settings and integrate clinical screening, referral, nutrition education, and recurring food access on a minimum biweekly basis, with a defined enrollment period targeting an average of 3-9 months per family. The FY26 cycle has $750,000 in total grant funding available to support qualifying organizations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: $750,000 in total grant funding is available for FY26 to support healthcare and clinic-led Food as Medicine programs. Individual awards vary; in FY25, grants ranged from $50,000 to $200,000 across six partnerships. Planning guidance suggests $100–$250 per family per month. Funds support programs that increase access to culturally diverse, medically relevant, nutritious, and locally produced food for Montgomery County households that screen positive for food insecurity, include at least one child aged 0–18, and include a parent or child with a current diagnosis of a diet-related disease. Allowable uses include medically relevant food purchases (produce, staples, proteins); food distribution (choice markets, pre-packaged boxes/bags, retail vouchers); staffing (care coordination, community health workers, nutrition educators); program operations (food handling supplies, translation, outreach materials, transportation/logistics); data collection and evaluation; limited equipment directly tied to food distribution; and indirect costs (up to 15% without a NICRA; NICRA rate if available). Grants are for a one-year period with potential renewal.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Friendship Heights TMD provides free commuter services to employers and employees in the Friendship Heights business district of Montgomery County. Employers with 25 or more employees are required by county law to submit a TDM Plan. The program also applies to nonresidential and multi-unit residential building owners, and new development projects.
