structured_extraction.program_name: Greater Shady Grove Transportation Management District (TMD)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Greater Shady Grove TMD is the largest of Montgomery County's six TMDs, spanning more than 6,400 acres and including parts of Rockville and Gaithersburg. It provides free commuter services to employers, employees, and residents to encourage use of transit and other commuting alternatives. Staff help employers create Transportation Demand Management (TDM) Plans, run commuter information fairs, conduct biennial commuter surveys, offer green business certification, and recognize employers who support alternative commuting. The TMD serves the Shady Grove Life Sciences Center area, which is the third largest biotech cluster in the United States. Services include transit subsidies and tax credits guidance, carpool/vanpool formation assistance, teleworking program design, Guaranteed Ride Home program, car sharing program access, and customized seminars and presentations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free services including commuter information fairs, biennial commuter surveys, green business certification, employer recognition, and help designing and carrying out a Transportation Benefits Program for the worksite. Services include: Transportation Benefits Plan design, transit subsidies and tax credits guidance, public transportation information, carpool/vanpool formation assistance, parking information, biking/walking amenities support, Guaranteed Ride Home program, teleworking/alternative work schedule design, car sharing program access, accessible transportation support, HOV lane information, customized seminars and presentations, and commuter information materials. Employers with 25 or more employees in the TMD are required by county law to submit a TDM Plan within 90 days of receiving written notice from the Director. TDM Plans must achieve Non-Auto Driver Mode Share (NADMS) goals. Residential buildings with 100+ dwelling units and new development projects may also be required to submit TDM Plans. Annual transportation demand management fees are charged to fund TDM administration and strategy implementation.

structured_extraction.program_name: HOC Housing Choice Voucher Program (HCV) – Including Mainstream Vouchers for People with Disabilities
structured_extraction.program_description: Rental assistance program administered by the Housing Opportunities Commission (HOC) of Montgomery County for very low and extremely low-income households, the elderly, and persons with disabilities. The program provides a rent subsidy (voucher) so that households pay no more than 30–40% of their total household income toward rent. Tenant-based vouchers can be used at any home, apartment, townhouse, or private market residence that meets program requirements, safety standards, and rent reasonableness; project-based vouchers are assigned to a specific building. A set-aside of Mainstream Vouchers is specifically designated for households with at least one disabled family member between the ages of 18 and 61, with incomes up to approximately $52,750 for one person. Tenant-based vouchers are portable throughout the United States, including Guam, Puerto Rico, Alaska, Hawaii, and the Virgin Islands.

Tenant-based vouchers can be used at any qualifying home, apartment, or private market residence meeting safety standards and rent reasonableness requirements. Project-based vouchers are tied to a specific building. Mainstream Vouchers are set aside for households with at least one disabled member between ages 18 and 61, with incomes of $0 to approximately $52,750 for one person. Tenant-based vouchers are portable anywhere in the United States, including Guam, Puerto Rico, Alaska, Hawaii, and the Virgin Islands.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental housing costs — participants can use the voucher for single-family homes, townhouses, apartments, or their current residence, as long as the unit meets program safety standards and rent reasonableness requirements.
