structured_extraction.program_description: A $50 million fund to accelerate the completion of mixed-income housing developments by the Housing Opportunities Commission (HOC). The fund helps create new housing units, with at least 20% affordable to households at or below 50% of area median income and another 10% affordable at or below the Moderately Priced Dwelling Unit (MPDU) income level.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A $50 million fund that provides financial assistance to the HOC to produce mixed-income housing developments. At least 20% of units created must be affordable to households at or below 50% of area median income, and at least 10% must be affordable at or below MPDU income levels. The fund is expected to help create nearly 8,800 new housing units.
structured_extraction.program_audience: The Housing Opportunities Commission (HOC) and housing developers seeking to create mixed-income affordable housing in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Development of mixed-income housing units, with affordability requirements for low- and moderate-income households.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: At least 20% of housing units must be affordable to households at or below 50% of area median income
At least 10% of units must be affordable at or below the MPDU income level

structured_extraction.program_name: HUD Continuum of Care (CoC) Funding Competition – Montgomery County MD-601
structured_extraction.program_description: The Montgomery County Continuum of Care (CoC) is a partnership of public and private organizations working to prevent and end homelessness in Montgomery County, Maryland. Designed to promote community-wide commitment to ending homelessness, the program funds projects aimed at quickly rehousing persons experiencing homelessness, reducing trauma and disruption caused by homelessness, promoting access to mainstream programs, and enhancing self-sufficiency. Each year, HUD (the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development) releases a Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) for CoC grants. Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services, as the CoC Lead, runs a local competition to select and rank projects for submission in HUD's national CoC competition. Selected projects may receive federal funding for housing and supportive services for people experiencing homelessness, including Permanent Supportive Housing (PSH), Transitional Housing, Supportive Services Only (SSO), Street Outreach, Coordinated Entry, and DV Bonus Projects.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal grant funding awarded through HUD's annual Continuum of Care competition. HUD is awarding more than $3.918 billion nationally in 2025. Montgomery County runs a local competition to rank and select projects, which are then submitted as part of a collaborative application to HUD. The Estimated Annual Renewal Demand (ARD) for MD-601 is $11,084,880; Tier 1 (30%) is $3,325,464; CoC Bonus is $2,216,976; DV Bonus is $726,527. Funding supports: Permanent Supportive Housing (PSH) renewals, Transitional Housing (TH), Supportive Services Only – Standalone (SSO-SS), Supportive Services Only – Street Outreach (SSO-SO), Supportive Services Only – Coordinated Entry (SSO-CE), and DV Bonus Projects. Eligible costs include leasing, operating expenses, supportive services, rental assistance, HMIS, and project administrative costs. The FY2025 NOFO had been withdrawn by HUD but local competition deadlines were set for December 2025.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: December 5, 2025, 5:00 PM – Letter of Intent; December 11, 2025, 5:00 PM – All applications, addenda, budgets, and supporting documents
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations, state and local government agencies, and instrumentalities of government providing housing and supportive services to people experiencing homelessness in Montgomery County, Maryland, including elderly individuals, persons with physical or developmental disabilities, survivors of domestic violence, and individuals with substance use disorders or mental health conditions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Housing and supportive services for people experiencing homelessness, including permanent supportive housing, rapid rehousing, transitional housing, street outreach, coordinated entry, and related services. Eligible costs include personnel/salaries, leasing/rental assistance, facility costs, operating expenses, administrative costs, case management, employment services, substance use disorder treatment, mental health services, benefits navigation (SSI, SSDI, SNAP, Medicaid), and HMIS costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland (CoC region MD-601).
requirements_list: Must serve people experiencing homelessness in Montgomery County
Must submit a letter of intent by December 5, 2025, 5:00 PM during the local competition process
Must submit completed Project Application Addendum with each application by December 11, 2025, 5:00 PM
Project must align with CoC priorities as outlined in the local scoring criteria
Projects must meet FY2025 NOFO funding objectives
Must comply with HUD CoC program regulations
Eligible applicants include private nonprofit organizations, state government, local government, and instrumentalities of state and local government
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Montgomery County DHHS runs a local competition when HUD releases its annual CoC NOFO. Interested organizations submit letters of intent by December 5, 2025 (5:00 PM), attend information sessions, and complete a Project Application Addendum with budgets and supporting documents by December 11, 2025 (5:00 PM). Projects are scored and ranked locally using the published scoring criteria before being submitted as part of a collaborative application to HUD. Applicants should monitor HUD and county updates for future opportunities.

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County requires anyone who collects or transports solid waste within the county to obtain a license. This program issues annual solid waste hauler and collector licenses and vehicle registrations to businesses and individuals engaged in waste collection or hauling. Independent collection contractors may also be authorized to collect non-recyclable solid waste on behalf of Montgomery County from residents in Subdistrict B (unincorporated areas).
eligible_industries: Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The county issues annual solid waste hauler and collector licenses (valid one year from date of issuance) and vehicle registration decals. License fee is $25.00 per license and $5.00 per vehicle or trailer registered. Government agencies, municipalities, and public sector entities are exempt from license and permit fees. Payment is accepted by credit card or Echeck payable to Montgomery County, Maryland. Independent collection contractors in Subdistrict B are authorized to collect non-recyclable solid waste from single- or two-family dwelling units (up to 6 units) under private contract with residents, billing residents for collection costs only (disposal charged through tax bill).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Renewal applications must be received at least 30 days prior to expiration date
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses and individuals who collect or transport solid waste within Montgomery County, Maryland, including private haulers, collectors, and collection contractors. Also includes independent collection contractors serving residential customers in Subdistrict B.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Obtaining a license and vehicle registration decals to legally collect or transport solid waste within Montgomery County. For contractors in Subdistrict B, authorization to provide collection service and deliver waste to the County Transfer Station.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicant must have an office business address in Montgomery County or provide a local or toll-free telephone number. Program is required for anyone collecting or transporting solid waste within Montgomery County. Independent contractor authorization applies specifically to Subdistrict B (unincorporated areas of the County, excluding Subdistrict A).
requirements_list: Must operate a commercial business or be engaged in an enterprise that involves collecting and hauling solid waste
Must have an office business address in Montgomery County or provide a local or toll-free telephone number
Must submit a completed application signed by owner or authorized agent
Must provide a copy of the State Vehicle Registration Card for each vehicle or trailer
Must submit $25.00 license fee and $5.00 per vehicle registration fee (waived for government/municipal entities)
Collectors must sign a Memorandum of Understanding (first and last pages completed, last page signed and witnessed)
Collectors must submit a County-approved Affidavit Form signed by an authorized company representative
Must follow Montgomery County Solid Wastes Law (Chapter 48)
Must submit semi-annual tonnage reports per Executive Regulation 5-13 AM
Personal Protective Equipment (high visibility vest, hard hat, closed toe shoes) required on transfer station tipping floor
Renewal applications must be submitted at least 30 days before expiration
Maintain valid Hauler/Collector License
Collect only non-recyclable solid waste; do not commingle with other waste sources
Bill residents for collection costs only (not disposal) in Subdistrict B
Provide regular collection between 7:00 a.m.–9:00 p.m. (9:00 a.m. start on Sundays/holidays)
Deliver all waste to County's Shady Grove Processing Facility/Transfer Station in Derwood
Comply with non-discrimination in employment policies (Section 118-3 and Section 27-19 of Montgomery County Code 2014)
No discrimination based on age, color, creed, national origin, race, religious belief, sexual preference, or handicap
Comply with applicable federal, state, and local laws and regulations
Include non-discrimination provisions in all subcontracts
Applicant must be over 18 years old
Company responsible for compliance with Chapter 48 provisions regarding collection and transportation of solid waste
Statement of service must be distributed to each existing customer at least once per calendar year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Collector/Hauler License Application online at the DEP Licensing portal. Submit a vehicle registration form for each vehicle or trailer, upload a copy of the State Vehicle Registration Card for each vehicle, and include all required documents (Memorandum of Understanding and Affidavit for collectors). The Memorandum of Understanding must be executed with signature by Owner, Corporate President, or Authorized Agent. The Affidavit requires a sworn statement from the company owner or employee responsible for compliance. Once the application is reviewed and approved by the License Program Specialist, a separate email with a payment link will be sent. Pay fees by credit card or Echeck. License certificates and decals will be mailed to the address on the application. For assistance, call 240-777-6566 Monday–Friday 7:00 am–3:30 pm or email DEP.Licensing@MontgomeryCountyMD.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: A pre-tax benefit account that lets Montgomery County Government (MCG) employees set aside money from each paycheck before taxes to pay for eligible health care expenses not covered by medical, prescription, dental, or vision benefits, including deductibles and copayments. Expenses can be for the employee or their qualifying dependents. Three FSA options are offered: Health Care FSA, Child Care FSA, and Commuter Choice Mass Transit FSA. Available even without MCG health plan enrollment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Employees elect an annual contribution amount that is deducted from each paycheck before federal, state, and FICA taxes are calculated. Three FSA options are available: (1) Health Care FSA: covers medical, OTC, prescription, dental, vision, and hearing expenses, up to $3,300 max annually; (2) Child Care FSA: covers day care, elder care, and before/after school care, up to $7,500 max annually; (3) Commuter Choice Mass Transit FSA (MCGEO and unrepresented employees only): covers parking and transit expenses, up to $230–$300 max monthly. After incurring eligible expenses, employees submit a claim with supporting documentation (bills or receipts) to Voya for reimbursement. Employees have until April 30 of the following year to submit claims, and until March 15 following the end of the calendar year to incur expenses. Unused funds are forfeited and cannot be carried over or returned.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Must enroll each year during open enrollment
structured_extraction.program_audience: All benefit-eligible Montgomery County Government (MCG) employees (Health Care FSA and Child Care FSA); MCGEO and unrepresented employees only (Commuter Choice Mass Transit FSA).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eligible medical, dental, vision, hearing, and prescription expenses including copays, coinsurance, and deductibles for the employee or qualifying dependents; dependent care expenses (day care, elder care, before/after school care); and work-related transit and parking expenses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Montgomery County Government employees in Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a benefit-eligible MCG employee
Must enroll each year to participate
Health Care FSA and Child Care FSA: full plan year participation (Jan 1 – Dec 31)
Commuter Choice Mass Transit FSA available to MCGEO and unrepresented employees only
Must submit claims by April 30 of the following year
Must incur expenses by March 15 following the end of the calendar year
Some expenses require a prescription or Letter of Medical Necessity from a qualified healthcare professional
Expenses must be IRS-qualified per IRS Publication 502
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Enroll each year during the open enrollment period. Elect a contribution amount to be deducted pre-tax from each paycheck. After incurring eligible expenses, submit a claim with supporting documentation to Voya for reimbursement via the Voya website or by phone.

structured_extraction.program_name: Health Care for the Homeless Program (HCHP)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Health Care for the Homeless Program improves health access, outcomes, and equity for single adults and families experiencing homelessness in Montgomery County. It provides integrated medical and psychiatric care with service coordination, hospital discharge planning, emergency room diversion, assistance with medical and social benefit enrollment, and prescription access. The program uses nurse-led case management in shelters, street medicine for unsheltered individuals, and close collaboration with local hospitals, behavioral health providers, and community clinics.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: No-fee services including medical and psychiatric care navigation and referrals, prescription medication access, assistance applying for public medical and social benefits, monthly nurse case management, hospital discharge planning, transportation assistance, primary care and intensive nurse case management at shelter locations, medical respite care, hospital-based diversion services, and mobile dental services. No payment is required and clients will not be denied care for lack of insurance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults age 18 and older experiencing homelessness or unstable housing in Montgomery County, including sheltered and unsheltered individuals with medical or psychiatric needs, regardless of health insurance status.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Medical and psychiatric care coordination, prescription access, benefit enrollment assistance, nurse case management, hospital discharge planning, transportation coordination, and mobile dental services for people experiencing homelessness.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Montgomery County resident experiencing homelessness or lacking stable housing.
requirements_list: Must be experiencing homelessness or lack stable housing
Must be a Montgomery County resident
Must have medical or psychiatric needs requiring coordination of care
Health insurance is not required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: No formal application form required. Referrals are made by shelter case managers and/or community partners such as hospitals, clinics, County-represented programs, and outreach agencies. Bring any available identification, health insurance cards (if available), and medical documents to appointments.

structured_extraction.program_name: Healthy, Efficient, Electrified, Climate-Adapted Pilot (HEECAP) Homes Grants Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This grant program provides funding competitively awarded to community partner organizations to help low- and moderate-income homeowners in Montgomery County reduce greenhouse gas emissions, address health and safety repairs, and adapt their homes to climate change through electrification and weatherization improvements. The program pilots strategies to repair health and safety issues, electrify homes by replacing fossil-fuel appliances, improve indoor air quality, and enhance climate resilience and durability. Funding covers three areas: pre-weatherization repairs, electrification, and climate resilience improvements. The pilot program began in June 2024, with FY26 funding anticipated to launch in mid-March 2026.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants competitively awarded to community partner organizations to fund pre-weatherization repairs, home electrification (replacing fossil-fuel appliances), indoor air quality improvements, weatherization, greenhouse gas emission reductions, and climate resilience enhancements for low- and moderate-income households in Montgomery County. Total program funding is $1.5 million.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community partner organizations and low- and moderate-income homeowners in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Pre-weatherization repairs, home electrification (replacing fossil-fuel appliances), weatherization, indoor air quality improvements, greenhouse gas emission reductions, and climate resilience and durability enhancements
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Grants are competitively awarded to community partners
Serves low- and moderate-income homes in Montgomery County
Household must be low- or moderate-income
Applicants must be income-eligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Grants are competitively awarded to community partners. Visit the HEECAP website for information on current grantees and resources. FY26 funding is anticipated to launch in mid-March 2026.

structured_extraction.program_name: Hiring Initiative for Displaced Federal Workers
structured_extraction.program_description: A hiring preference program for former federal employees who live in Montgomery County and were separated from federal employment due to a reduction in force or position elimination on or after January 1, 2025. Eligible applicants who meet minimum job qualifications are placed in the highest rating category on the eligible list, increasing their chances of being selected for a first-round interview for Montgomery County government positions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible displaced federal employees who meet minimum qualifications are placed in the highest rating category on the Montgomery County government job eligible list, improving their chances of receiving a first-round interview. This is a hiring preference, not a guarantee of employment or an interview.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Former federal employees who reside in Montgomery County and were separated from federal employment on or after January 1, 2025 due to a reduction in force or their position no longer being needed.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Hiring preference for Montgomery County government job applications.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must reside in Montgomery County, Maryland and must verify residency with a valid government-issued ID showing a Montgomery County address.
requirements_list: Must reside in Montgomery County
Must have been fully separated from federal employment on or after January 1, 2025
Reason for separation must be that the federal position was no longer needed or that the individual was subject to a federal reduction in force
Must not be a current or former Montgomery County government employee
Must meet minimum qualifications for the specific position applied for
Must answer supplemental eligibility questions on the job application
Must attach official federal separation notification document
Must attach proof of Montgomery County residency (e.g. driver's license or Maryland ID with Montgomery County address)
Federal contractors are not eligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply for a Montgomery County government position through the county careers website. During the application, answer supplemental online questions to claim displaced federal worker eligibility. Attach the official federal separation notice and a valid government-issued ID showing a Montgomery County address. If eligible and meeting minimum qualifications, you will be placed in the highest rating category. After the job posting closes, OHR reviews applications within two weeks and the hiring department then contacts selected candidates for interviews.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Montgomery County property tax credit program that encourages the restoration and preservation of privately owned historic properties, including properties designated historic by the City of Rockville or listed in the Montgomery County Master Plan for Historic Preservation, or within a designated historic district. Owners receive a credit equal to 25% of qualified costs for documented exterior maintenance, restoration, or preservation work. A minimum of $1,000 must be spent in a calendar year. The credit is applied against the following year's property taxes, up to the total amount of county real property taxes, and any unused portion may be carried forward for up to five tax years. Only exterior work is eligible; new construction does not qualify. Work must be certified eligible by the Historic District Commission (HDC).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A property tax credit equal to 25% of qualified costs spent on documented exterior maintenance, restoration, or preservation of historically designated properties. Owners must spend a minimum of $1,000 in a calendar year. The credit is applied against the following year's property taxes, up to the total county real property tax amount. Any unused portion may be carried forward for up to five tax years. Only exterior work is eligible; new construction does not qualify. Owner labor costs are not eligible, but material costs may qualify.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of historic properties in Montgomery County designated on the Montgomery County Master Plan for Historic Preservation, within a designated historic district, or designated historic by the City of Rockville, including businesses, non-profits, and individuals.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Exterior maintenance, restoration, or preservation work on historically designated properties, including approved storm windows and doors, chimney repairs, exterior painting, gutter replacement, roof repairs and replacement, window repairs, repointing brick or stone, restoring documented features, professional services (architects, engineers, color consultants), and similar eligible exterior work certified by the Historic District Commission. New construction is not eligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. Available to owners of properties listed in the Montgomery County Master Plan for Historic Preservation, within a designated historic district, or designated historic by the City of Rockville. Properties listed only in the National Register of Historic Places are not eligible.
requirements_list: Property must be listed in the Montgomery County Master Plan for Historic Preservation, within a designated historic district, or designated historic by the City of Rockville Mayor and Council
Work must be certified eligible by the Historic District Commission (HDC)
Work must be subject to an approved historic area work permit, OR be ordinary maintenance exceeding $1,000
Minimum expenditure of $1,000 in a calendar year
Credit applies to exterior work only
No credit for new construction
Application must include copies of receipts for materials, paid receipts from a licensed contractor, and before-and-after photographs
Owner labor costs are not eligible, but material costs may qualify
Work requiring a Certificate of Approval (COA) must have obtained one
Unused credit may be carried forward up to 5 tax years
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Montgomery County Planning Historic Preservation Tax Credit Program. The Historic District Commission (HDC) determines eligibility of expenditures and sends findings to the Montgomery County Department of Finance for processing. The director of finance may request additional documentation and will notify the applicant of approval or disapproval. Contact the Department of Finance at (240) 777-8931 for details.

structured_extraction.program_description: HARP is a free program designed to help people renovate their homes to make them more accessible for people with disabilities and older adults.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free home accessibility renovation assistance provided to eligible homeowners.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners with disabilities and older adults seeking to make their homes more accessible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home renovations and modifications to improve accessibility for people with disabilities and older adults.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides personal care services and light housekeeping to adults aged 18 and older in Montgomery County who have functional disabilities and need help with personal care, chores, and activities of daily living. The goal is to help people remain in their own homes and prevent or reduce the need for institutionalization, and to prevent or remedy abuse, neglect, self-neglect, or exploitation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Personal care services and light housekeeping provided to eligible adults. Hours are determined by individual assessment and a service plan. A sliding-scale fee may apply based on the applicant's income and family size, paid to the Department of Social Services.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults aged 18 and older residing in Montgomery County who have functional disabilities and need assistance with personal care, chores, or activities of daily living to remain in their own homes.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Personal care services and light housekeeping to help adults with functional disabilities live independently at home.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must reside in Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be 18 years of age or older
Must reside in Montgomery County
Must be receiving case management
Must require home care services as part of a treatment plan
Must be unable to obtain necessary paraprofessional services from another resource
Must be willing to accept home care services
Must agree to pay any required fee
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call the Aging and Disability Resource Unit at 240-777-3000 to get more information and discuss eligibility.

structured_extraction.program_name: Home Computer Telecommuting Incentive Personal Property Business Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A Montgomery County personal property tax credit for employers who purchase new home computers or laptops to create new off-site employee workstations for telecommuting purposes. The credit is equal to up to 50% of the cost of each qualifying computer purchased, with a maximum aggregate credit of $2,000 per taxpayer per year. Total annual credits are capped by the County Council (starting in 2009), and credits are granted in the order applications are received. The employee must work at home at least 78 days per calendar year (approximately 1.5 days per week). Application must be submitted within 12 months of purchase. Employees must certify that the computers are used for business purposes.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: An annual credit against the county personal property tax for up to 50% of the cost of each new home computer or laptop purchased to establish a new off-site employee workstation for telecommuting. Maximum credit per taxpayer per year is $2,000. Total annual credits are capped (set annually by the County Council starting in 2009). Credits are granted in the order applications are received. Employees must certify that computers are used for business purposes and that they work from home at least 78 days per year. Application must be submitted within 12 months of purchase.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Employers and businesses in Montgomery County who purchase new computers or laptops for employees to telecommute from home at least 78 days per year.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of new computers or laptops to establish off-site employee workstations for telecommuting; reduces county personal property tax liability.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Employer must purchase a new computer or new laptop computer
Purchase must establish a new off-site employee workstation
Computer must be purchased after December 31, 2005
Computer must be used for telecommuting
Employee must work at home at least 78 days per calendar year (approximately 1.5 days per week)
Employees must certify that computers are used for business purposes
Employer must document date of purchase and cost
Application must be submitted within 12 months of purchase
Credit capped at 50% of each computer's cost and $2,000 aggregate per taxpayer per year
Business must be located in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Telework Tax Credit Application form (PDF available on the program page) and submit to the Department of Finance within 12 months of purchasing the computer. The credit is applied in the tax year of purchase or the following tax year. Contact the Department of Finance, Division of Treasury for details.

structured_extraction.program_name: Home Energy Assistance Program (Utility Assistance Program)
structured_extraction.program_description: Helps low-income Montgomery County households pay past due and ongoing electric and heating bills. Eligibility is based on household size and gross monthly income at or below 200% of the Federal Poverty Guidelines. If a resident is at risk of a utility shut off, immediate assistance is available by calling the program hotline. Includes sub-programs: Electric Universal Service Program (EUSP), Maryland Energy Assistance Program (MEAP), Universal Service Protection Program (USPP), Arrearage Retirement Assistance (ARA), and Gas Arrearage Retirement Assistance (GARA).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance to help pay past due and ongoing electric and/or heating bills. Benefit amount is based on household income and size. Annual electric grants (EUSP) and heating/fuel grants (MEAP) are available. Arrearage (past-due bill) assistance up to $2,000 for electric (ARA) and up to $2,000 for gas (GARA), each available once every 5 years. Utility shut-off prevention through budget billing enrollment (USPP). Energy efficiency improvement referrals through DHCD. Applications are processed through the Maryland Department of Human Services Office of Home Energy Programs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income Montgomery County residents and households at risk of utility shut off or with past due electric or heating bills
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment of past due and ongoing electric and/or heating utility bills; arrearage assistance for electric and gas; utility shut-off prevention; energy efficiency improvement referrals
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Household gross monthly income within the last 30 days must be at or below 200% of the Federal Poverty Guidelines (e.g., $2,608/month for a household of 1; $3,525 for 2; $4,441 for 3; $5,358 for 4)
Completed Home Energy Program application
Proof of identity (photo ID)
Proof of citizenship for all household members
Social Security cards for all household members
Proof of gross monthly household income for last 30 days
Electric bill and/or heating bill
Living Arrangement Form or Mortgage Invoice/tax bill
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at MyDHR (mydhrbenefits.dhr.state.md.us), call 1-800-352-1446 to request a paper application, or submit a completed application by email to ohep@montgomerycountymd.gov. Paper applications and a document drop box are available at 1301 Piccard Drive, 4th Floor, Rockville, and at housing stabilization offices. Phone appointments may be requested by calling 240-777-4450. If you are at risk of a utility shut off, call immediately for emergency assistance.

structured_extraction.program_name: Home Fire Safety Visit Program (Smoke Alarm Program)
structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County Fire and Rescue Service (MCFRS) and the Department of Health and Human Services offer free in-person or virtual home safety visits and smoke alarm installation to residents of Montgomery County. During a visit, trained MCFRS staff check smoke alarms, replace backup batteries when needed, recommend replacement of outdated alarms, identify fire hazards, help households create home fire escape plans, and discuss fire safety topics. Free smoke alarm installation is targeted to high-risk individuals, including older adults, people with disabilities, mobility, vision, or hearing impairments, and economically challenged residents. Specially designed visual smoke alarms and alert devices (including strobe lights, pillow/bed shakers, and audio alert devices) are available in limited supply for residents who are deaf or hard of hearing. Free home safety evaluations are also available to all Montgomery County residents to identify fire hazards and reduce fire risk.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free home safety visits (in-person or virtual) that include smoke alarm checks, battery replacements, identification of fire hazards, assistance developing home fire escape plans, and fire safety education. For eligible high-risk residents, free smoke alarm installation is provided, including interconnected alarms installed in bedrooms, outside sleeping areas, and on every level of the home. Specialized visual alarms and alert devices for deaf and hearing-impaired residents are available in limited supply, including strobe lights, pillow/bed shakers, and audio alert devices. Free home safety evaluations are available to all Montgomery County residents to identify fire hazards and improve safety.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents of Montgomery County, Maryland, particularly high-risk individuals such as older adults, senior citizens, people with disabilities, mobility, vision, or hearing impairments, economically challenged or low-income residents, and people who are deaf or hard of hearing. Free home safety evaluations are available to all county residents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free home fire safety inspections, smoke alarm checks and battery replacements, free smoke alarm installation for high-risk residents, specialized visual alarms and alert devices (strobe lights, pillow/bed shakers, transmitters, receivers) for deaf or hard-of-hearing residents, home fire escape plan development, and fire safety education.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Montgomery County, Maryland only.
requirements_list: Must be a resident of Montgomery County, Maryland
A household member 18 years of age or older must be present during the visit
Household agrees to maintain and test smoke alarms monthly, develop a home fire escape plan, and practice escape routes regularly
Free alarm installation is prioritized for high-risk individuals (older adults, people with disabilities, mobility/hearing/vision impairments, or economically challenged residents)
Specially designed visual smoke alarms and alert devices available for residents who are deaf or hard of hearing
Landlords, not MCFRS, are responsible for installing or replacing smoke and carbon monoxide alarms in rental properties
Home safety evaluations are available to all Montgomery County residents
Select equipment with recognized testing laboratory labels
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Residents can request a home safety visit online through the MCFRS website at the link provided, or call 311 to schedule a free home safety visit, smoke alarm installation, or home safety evaluation. Choose in-person or virtual appointment. In emergencies, call 911; for urgent smoke alarm needs, call 301-279-8000.

structured_extraction.program_description: Matches renters seeking affordable housing with homeowners who have spare rooms available for long-term rental.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Matches renters seeking affordable housing options with homeowners who have spare rooms in their homes to rent long-term.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Renters seeking affordable housing and homeowners with spare rooms in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Affordable long-term room rental
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, MD
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call HIP at 301-857-4273 or visit the website to view available rooms and connect with the program.

structured_extraction.program_name: Home and Community Based Services and Supports
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides supports planning (case management) services to older adults and individuals with disabilities enrolled in Community Personal Assistance Services (CPAS), Community First Choice (CFC), and the Community Options (CO) Waiver. Support planners help participants access Medicaid and non-Medicaid funded home and community-based services such as personal care, nurse monitoring, and necessary medical supplies. Support planners also help participants maintain Medicaid eligibility. Eligible CO Waiver applicants in nursing homes can receive help transitioning back to the community.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Supports planning (case management) services include help accessing personal assistance, nurse monitoring, personal emergency response systems, environmental assessments, accessibility adaptations, medical day care, and assisted living (CO Waiver). Support planners also assist with maintaining Medicaid eligibility and transitioning out of nursing homes into community settings.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Older adults and individuals with disabilities who qualify for community Medicaid or a Medicaid waiver and need help with activities of daily living such as bathing, grooming, and dressing.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Personal assistance services, supports planning, nurse monitoring, personal emergency response systems, environmental assessments, accessibility adaptations, medical day care, and assisted living.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Montgomery County, Maryland through the Montgomery County DHHS Area Agency on Aging Supports Planning Agency.
requirements_list: Must qualify for community Medicaid or a Medicaid waiver
Must need help with activities of daily living such as bathing, grooming, and dressing
Must meet the program's medical level of care
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call the Aging and Disability Resource Unit (ADRU) at 240-777-3000 to apply.

structured_extraction.program_name: Home and Community-Based Services Waiver for Individuals with Brain Injury (Traumatic Brain Injury Waiver)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides home and community-based services to adults with brain injuries so they can live in the community rather than in a specialty hospital or nursing facility.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides residential habilitation, day habilitation, supported employment, individual support services, case management, and medical day care. Also includes standard Medicaid state plan services such as physician and hospital care, pharmacy, home health, laboratory, mental health services, durable medical equipment, and Medicare premium payments.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Maryland Department of Health, Behavioral Health Administration
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults with a brain injury that occurred after age 17 who require specialty hospital or nursing facility level of care and meet financial eligibility requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Community-based residential, day, employment, and support services for adults with brain injuries, enabling community living as an alternative to institutional care.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland residents.
requirements_list: Diagnosis of brain injury
Brain injury occurred after age 17

Currently inpatient in a State Behavioral Health Administration facility, state-owned nursing facility, Maryland licensed Special Hospital for Chronic Disease accredited by CARF for Brain Injury Inpatient Rehabilitation, or placed by Medicaid in an out-of-state facility
Must require specialty hospital or nursing facility level of care
Must meet financial eligibility requirements for Medicaid
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Maryland Department of Health, Behavioral Health Administration at 410-402-8476 or 1-877-463-3464 for information on eligibility and how to apply.

structured_extraction.program_description: A post-arrest diversion program for homeless individuals charged with specific nonviolent misdemeanors or who have outstanding warrants for misdemeanors and transit or traffic offenses. Participants can resolve their legal matters through the program instead of traditional court processes — charges are dropped and criminal records expunged upon successful 90-day service plan completion. Participation is voluntary — each person can choose to join HPCDP or pursue traditional legal options including a trial.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Post-arrest diversion with STET docket placement (up to 90 days); nolle prosequi (case dismissal) upon satisfactory service engagement; expungement of charges upon successful completion. Participants receive case management, legal representation (pro bono attorney or public defender), and support services including housing, healthcare, behavioral health, benefits enrollment, and employment assistance to resolve open misdemeanor criminal, traffic, and transit matters (including outstanding warrants) without going through traditional prosecution. Monthly meetings are held at Progress Place, 8106 Georgia Avenue, Silver Spring, with the program coordinator, participants, attorneys, and service providers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeless individuals who have been charged with nonviolent misdemeanors or have outstanding warrants for misdemeanors, transit, or traffic offenses. Eligible if currently on the street, in a shelter, doubled up in another person's household, in a motel, or living in places not meant for human habitation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Resolution of open misdemeanor criminal, traffic, and transit matters including outstanding warrants; case diversion; legal representation; record expungement; and support services including housing, healthcare, behavioral health, benefits, and employment assistance for persons who are homeless or have been homeless.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. Must have pending cases or warrants issued in Montgomery County District Court.
requirements_list: Must be experiencing homelessness (on the street, in a shelter, doubled up in another person's household, in a motel, or in places not meant for human habitation)
Must have a pending case or outstanding warrant in Montgomery County District Court

Must be charged with eligible nonviolent misdemeanors or transit/traffic offenses (including alcohol offenses, drug possession, disorderly conduct, panhandling, solicitation, traffic offenses, property destruction, indecent exposure, vagrancy, prostitution, theft, trespassing, Metro fines, etc.)
Must complete an approved service plan within 90 days
Participation is voluntary
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individuals can be referred to HPCDP by a case manager, court, attorney, or other sources, or can self-refer by contacting the program directly at hpcdp@montgomerycountymd.gov or 240.749.1844. Referral form is submitted with participant contact info and Maryland case details; internal processing includes HMIS verification and State's Attorney's Office (SAO) coordination. Participants meet with an attorney to develop a service plan, which is presented to the State's Attorney for approval. Monthly meetings are held at Progress Place. Referral and participant authorization forms are available in English and Spanish on the program's website.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides grants or loans to eligible homeowners for delinquent mortgage payments, past due association fees and real estate taxes, as well as for home repairs and energy efficiency improvements. Eligibility is based on income and COVID-19 impact, and owner occupancy is required.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants or loans for delinquent mortgage payments, past due association fees, past due real estate taxes, home repairs, and energy efficiency improvements. A $3,000,000 special appropriation was made for FY2023.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income homeowners in Montgomery County impacted by COVID-19
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Delinquent mortgage payments, past due association fees, past due real estate taxes, home repairs, and energy efficiency improvements
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must meet income eligibility requirements
Must demonstrate COVID-19 impact
Must be owner-occupant of the property

structured_extraction.program_description: A local property tax credit for eligible homeowners in Montgomery County, Maryland that reduces the amount of real property tax owed based on the homeowner's income and net worth. The Chief Administrative Officer adjusts the qualifying property tax values and income levels annually based on the Consumer Price Index (CPI-U) for the Washington-Arlington-Alexandria area. Effective July 1, 2026, updated income and property value thresholds apply, with allowable tax credit percentages varying by income bracket.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A property tax credit that reduces the real property tax bill for eligible homeowners. As of July 1, 2026, the eligibility thresholds are: gross income limit up to $76,620; net worth limit up to $255,400; and total real property tax multiplier up to $383,100. The allowable tax credit percentage varies by combined gross income bracket (0%, 2%, 5%, 6.5%, or 8%).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County homeowners who meet income and net worth eligibility thresholds
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of local real property tax liability
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a homeowner in Montgomery County
Gross income must not exceed $76,620 (effective July 1, 2026)
Net worth must not exceed $255,400 (effective July 1, 2026)
Property must meet the total real property tax multiplier threshold of $383,100 (effective July 1, 2026)

structured_extraction.program_name: Housing Initiative Program (formerly Supportive Housing Rental Assistance Program)
structured_extraction.program_description: A Montgomery County program that provides supportive housing rental assistance to eligible individuals with special housing needs, administered through the Department of Health and Human Services. Previously called the Supportive Housing Rental Assistance Program, the program establishes standards for eligibility and procedures for administering rental and housing assistance to individuals with special housing needs in Montgomery County. The program is governed by Executive Regulation 17-06AM (original), Executive Regulation 20-12 (updated), and Executive Regulation 7-17.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rental and housing assistance for individuals with special housing needs in supportive housing. Specific benefit amounts and terms are defined in the governing regulations (Executive Regulation 20-12, formerly Executive Regulation 17-06AM, and Executive Regulation 7-17).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and residents with special housing needs in Montgomery County, Maryland seeking supportive housing rental assistance.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental and housing assistance for supportive housing for eligible individuals with special needs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Eligibility standards defined in Executive Regulation 17-06AM (original regulation)
Must meet program requirements as defined in Executive Regulation 20-12 (current regulation)
Must meet eligibility criteria established under Executive Regulation 7-17
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Gloria Huggins at the Department of Health and Human Services, Director's Office, Special Needs Housing, 401 Hungerford Drive, 5th Floor, Rockville, MD 20850 for information on obtaining a copy of the regulation and applying.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides case management and limited financial grants to help Montgomery County residents at risk of homelessness keep or obtain housing. Services include emergency financial assistance for eviction prevention, utility shut-off prevention, utility reconnection, security deposits, first month's rent, and burial assistance grants. Also provides homelessness prevention services and financial help to prevent foreclosure and utility disconnection for residents in crisis.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Limited financial grants for eviction prevention, utility shut-off prevention, utility reconnection, security deposits, first month's rent, and burial assistance. Also provides case management to help households stabilize their housing. Eviction prevention grants are available to households that meet income guidelines (at or below 60% of area median income), have a court judgment or eviction notice, and have not received an eviction prevention grant in the past 12 months. Specific dollar amounts vary by need and circumstance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents at risk of homelessness or experiencing a housing emergency, including those facing eviction, foreclosure, or utility shutoff, with household income at or below 60% of area median income (AMI).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eviction prevention, utility shut-off prevention, utility reconnection, security deposits, first month's rent, burial assistance, foreclosure prevention, and homelessness prevention.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Montgomery County, Maryland resident. Residents of the City of Gaithersburg, City of Rockville, or City of Takoma Park may also be eligible for additional local support.
requirements_list: Must be a Montgomery County resident
Household income must be at or below 60% of area median income (AMI)
Must not have received an eviction prevention grant in the past 12 months (for eviction prevention grants)
Must have a court summons, judgment, red and white notice from the Sheriff's Office, or a landlord-issued put-out notice (for eviction prevention)
Photo identification for all adults in the household
Bank/financial statements for the last 30 days for all accounts
Income documentation for the last 30 days for all adults in the household
Proof of expenses (utility bills, rent, etc.)
Current rental ledger for eviction prevention cases
Welcome letter and lease for security deposit and first month's rent assistance
Signed Release of Information Form
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit one of three HSS offices in person (Germantown, Rockville, or Silver Spring) during lobby hours Monday–Friday 8:30 a.m.–5:00 p.m. (sign-in until 4:30 p.m.). Bring all required documentation at the time of application. For eviction emergencies, call 311 (or 240-777-0311 from outside Montgomery County) to be connected with HSS, or call to schedule a phone interview. Limited on-site services and document drop-off are available at all three office locations. Reasonable accommodations, including electronic document submission, are available upon request by contacting HSS.

structured_extraction.program_name: Housing at Metrorail Stations Act – Payment in Lieu of Taxes
structured_extraction.program_description: This regulation establishes the procedure to administer and implement the Housing at Metrorail Stations Act under Bill 29-20. It sets conditions for developers of qualifying housing projects near Metrorail stations to receive a payment in lieu of taxes (PILOT), including requirements related to contractor wage compliance and local workforce participation.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Developers of qualifying housing projects near Metrorail stations may receive a payment in lieu of taxes (PILOT). To qualify, developers must agree in writing that: (1) no contractor or subcontractor hired had three or more final, non-appealable penalties of $5,000 or more in the prior three years for wage and hour law violations; and (2) at least 25% of workers constructing the project were Montgomery County residents. Developers must also submit quarterly compliance reports to the County Executive during construction.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Developers of qualifying housing projects near Metrorail stations in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment in lieu of taxes for qualifying residential development near Metrorail stations
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland – projects at or near Metrorail stations
requirements_list: Developer must agree in writing that no contractor or subcontractor had 3 or more final, non-appealable penalties of $5,000 or more in the prior 3 years for wage and hour law violations
At least 25% of workers constructing the project must be Montgomery County residents while performing the work
Developer must submit quarterly compliance reports to the County Executive during construction
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Developer must agree in writing to the stated conditions as part of receiving PILOT and submit quarterly reports during construction. Written comments on the proposed regulation were due March 31, 2021 to the Department of Finance.

structured_extraction.program_description: A weekend camp program that brings together fifth grade students from Montgomery County to learn about civil and human rights topics, including fair housing, fair employment, voter's rights, and bullying prevention. Students come from diverse backgrounds to build interracial and intercultural understanding.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Students selected to attend a three-day residential camp experience at YMCA's Camp Letts in Edgewater, Maryland. A cash award and public recognition are given to the winner of a fair housing poster contest held during camp. Only 100 students (50 boys and 50 girls) are selected annually.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Fifth grade students attending Montgomery County Elementary Schools who have demonstrated acts of kindness, promoted diversity and tolerance, or have an interest in human rights issues.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational camp experience covering civil and human rights topics.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to fifth grade students attending Montgomery County Elementary Schools.
requirements_list: Must be a fifth grade student attending a Montgomery County Elementary School
Must have demonstrated acts of kindness, barrier-breaking, moral stances, or initiated programs related to diversity and tolerance; or have an interest in diversity, tolerance, or human rights
Selection may also be based on recommendation by teachers, counselors, or administrators
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Teachers, counselors, and administrators recommend students. Registration is open to eligible students with selection based on demonstrated actions and interest in diversity and human rights.

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County Recreation provides accommodations and inclusion support for individuals with disabilities so they can fully participate in recreation programs, classes, and camps alongside individuals without disabilities. Accommodations are tailored to each person's unique needs and may include interpreters, large print materials, auxiliary aids, or inclusion support partners who help participants engage in activities in a positive and welcoming environment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Individualized accommodations such as interpreters, large print materials, auxiliary aids, and inclusion support partners are provided to help individuals with disabilities participate in Montgomery County Recreation programs, classes, and camps.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Requests recommended 2-3 weeks in advance; no formal deadline
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with disabilities (including primary, secondary, and intellectual disabilities), children and youth, who want to participate in Montgomery County Recreation programs, classes, or camps
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Accommodations to support full participation in recreation programs, including interpreters, large print materials, auxiliary aids, and inclusion support partners
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents and participants in Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be registered in a Montgomery County Recreation program, class, or camp
Submit accommodation request at least 2-3 weeks in advance
Complete the Parent Participant Profile form
Provide participant information (name, birthdate, gender)
Provide parent/guardian contact information
Identify primary disability
Provide health information
Provide activity preferences and strengths
Provide behavior and communication details
Complete safety and independence assessment
Provide daily activity and physical capability information
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Register for any Montgomery County Recreation program, class, or camp on ActiveMONTGOMERY. 2. Email rec.inclusion@montgomerycountymd.gov to make your accommodation request. 3. Complete and submit the Parent Participant Profile form (fillable PDF).

structured_extraction.program_name: Infant and Early Childhood Mental Health Consultation Support Services
structured_extraction.program_description: This program connects mental health professionals with licensed early care and education providers and families in Montgomery County. Consultants observe children and classrooms, talk with parents and child care staff, and develop individualized strategies to support children's social and emotional development. The goal is to reduce challenging behaviors, prepare children for school, and prevent expulsions from child care settings.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free mental health consultation services provided by licensed mental health professionals to families and child care providers. Consultants observe children, gather information, and develop strategies for home and child care settings. Families also receive referrals to other resources and professionals such as pediatricians, occupational therapists, and speech therapists.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families of children ages birth to 5 years who are enrolled in licensed child care programs in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Mental health consultation and support to improve children's social-emotional development and school readiness.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. Services are available through licensed child care programs; not available in before- or after-school programs.
requirements_list: Child must be between birth and 5 years old
Child must be enrolled in a licensed child care program
Services are not provided in before and/or after school programs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call Montgomery County Child Care Support Services at 240-777-4769 (240-777-GROW) to apply.

structured_extraction.program_name: Infant at Risk Home Visiting Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program accepts referrals to case manage mothers and newborns who have medical or social problems that could affect their health, development, or well-being. A public health nurse makes home visits to support eligible mothers and infants. Common referral reasons include teen mothers, no prenatal care, substance use, mental health concerns, intimate partner violence, unstable housing, previous infant death, previous preterm birth, and very low birthweight.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Public health nurses conduct home visits to case manage mothers and newborns at risk. The service is free of charge. Once a referral is received, a public health nurse contacts the family to schedule home visits. Coordination of services includes health care, WIC, immunizations, mental health support, substance use treatment, and other maternal-infant support services.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Postpartum mothers and infants identified as at-risk based on medical, psychosocial, pregnancy-related, or infant risk factors, including teen mothers, those with no prenatal care, substance use issues, mental/behavioral health concerns, intimate partner violence, unstable housing, previous infant death, previous preterm birth, or very low birthweight infants.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home visiting and case management services for at-risk mothers and newborns, including coordination of health care, WIC, immunizations, mental health support, and substance use treatment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available through health centers in Silver Spring, Germantown, and Rockville in Montgomery County, MD.
requirements_list: Must be a mother or newborn with medical or social problems that could affect health, development, or well-being
Referrals typically received from hospitals via the Maryland Postpartum Infant and Maternal Referral Form
Identification of at least one risk factor from medical, psychosocial, pregnancy-related, or infant risk categories

Eligible conditions include: teen mothers, no prenatal care, substance use/misuse, mental/behavioral health issues, intimate partner violence, unstable housing/homelessness, previous infant death, previous preterm birth, very low birthweight (under 1,500 grams), or any other serious risk circumstance
Secure transmission of referral form via fax, encrypted email, or other secure means
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Fax the Maryland Postpartum Infant and Maternal Referral Form to either the Silver Spring Health Center (fax: 240-777-3054) or the Germantown Health Center (fax: 240-777-4648). The form may also be submitted via encrypted email or other secure means. After the referral is received, a public health nurse will contact the family to schedule home visits.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Accelerator is a structured problem-solving course and community for Montgomery County Government employees. Participants (called Accelerators) learn process improvement, human-centered design, and other change management methods through a three-day workshop intensive, then lead real improvement projects in their departments. The program includes peer mentoring, coaching, an online collaboration tool (Miro), and an online community, and concludes with an Innovation Showcase where participants present their results. After completing initial projects, Accelerators join ongoing chapter clubs, peer learning circles, and monthly work sprints. Participants work in cohorts with peers from across county government to solve real workplace problems, improve processes, and deliver innovations without needing new budget, staff, or technology. Projects range from improving constituent appointments to automating administrative processes.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive a three-day intensive workshop, coaching, peer mentoring, access to an online community and collaboration tool (Miro), regular coaching hours, Open Innovation events, and additional learning sessions. Civic Design Leads guide teams through human-centered design processes, including design skills coaching workshops on visual design, plain language, and government forms, and project-based support for service improvements. After completing initial projects, Accelerators join ongoing chapter clubs, peer learning circles, and monthly work sprints. No financial award is provided.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County Government employees across all departments and positions who want to create change in their departments, improve processes and systems within their teams, and improve outcomes for residents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Improving government processes, redesigning services, and delivering workplace innovations using existing resources, including cost savings through process automation and efficiency improvements. This is a training and technical assistance program, not a funding program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to employees of Montgomery County Government only.
requirements_list: Must be a Montgomery County Government employee
Must apply and be selected to participate in a cohort
Must be committed to making improvements
Must choose to participate voluntarily
Must have manager support and approval for the time commitment
Project must involve humans and their motivations, behaviors, and needs
Focus beyond efficiency to better experience
Complex challenge
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online via the provided application link (Microsoft Forms). Selected applicants form a cohort and begin with a three-day workshop intensive (e.g., January 14–16, 2026 and February 19, 20, and 23, 2026), then carry out change projects in their departments over the following months, culminating in an Innovation Showcase.

structured_extraction.program_name: Intervention Program for Substance Abusers (IPSA) Pre-Trial Services
structured_extraction.program_description: IPSA is a pre-trial diversion program for eligible individuals with substance abuse issues in Montgomery County. It diverts first-time offenders charged with misdemeanor drug crimes out of the court system and into programs that promote behavior change through drug testing, education, treatment, and community service. It also gives judges a sentencing option for offenders with mild to moderate substance abuse problems and limited criminal histories. Participants must complete four educational classes (each up to 1.5 hours, in any order), community service hours, and periodic check-ins with a case manager, in lieu of or as a condition of prosecution. The program is run in cooperation with the State's Attorney's Office, County Police Department, and County Department of Health and Human Services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive drug testing (twice per week for misdemeanor cases, or random/regular for citation cases), drug education classes (four 1.5-hour sessions covering drugs and the individual, drugs and the law, thinking for change, and treatment and recovery), a marijuana-specific education class (2.5 hours, offered monthly), referrals to treatment, substance abuse counseling, support group meetings, case management, and community service opportunities (24 hours required) through the Community Service Work Crew or an approved site. Classes can be taken in any order and more than one class per week is allowed. Participants may also receive home visits from a case manager. Successful completion helps participants avoid a criminal record.
structured_extraction.program_audience: First-time offenders charged with minor/misdemeanor drug crimes in Montgomery County, offenders with mild to moderate substance abuse problems and limited criminal histories referred by a judge, and individuals with substance abuse issues involved in the pre-trial process in Montgomery County, MD.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Drug testing, drug education classes, substance abuse treatment referrals, substance abuse counseling, support group meetings, case management, and community service to assist participants in completing pre-trial diversion requirements and maintaining a drug- and arrest-free lifestyle.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland (11651 Nebel Street, Rockville, Maryland 20852)
requirements_list: Must be charged with a minor/misdemeanor drug offense
No prior felony convictions within the past 10 years
No more than 30 days jail time in the past 10 years
No prior IPSA participation for the same charge type
No pending felony charges
For probation referrals: no prior violent offense conviction
Must be a first-time offender or have a limited criminal history with mild to moderate substance abuse problems
Referred through the court or Pre-Trial Services
Complete four required drug education classes (in any order)
Arrive on time for classes
Drug/alcohol testing twice per week (misdemeanor cases) or random/regular testing (citation cases)
Complete 24 hours of approved community service
May be subject to scheduled or unscheduled home visits by case manager
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Participants are referred through the court system or by a judge. Once enrolled, contact your caseworker to coordinate class enrollment and community service. Community service is coordinated through the Alternative Community Service Program Work Crew at 11651 Nebel Street, Rockville, MD 20852. Participants must complete required drug testing, drug education classes, community service hours, and any other program components assigned to them. Direct questions or comments to Diversion Unit Manager Frank Rini at Frank.Rini@montgomerycountymd.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: A residential electrical trainee program through the Joint Apprenticeship and Training Committee (JATC) for Local Union 26 IBEW. Accepted individuals sign an agreement and are placed with a signatory electrical contractor. Pay increases as trainees progress through the program, and trainees can advance to apprentice status.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Paid trainee-to-apprentice program requiring 10,000 hours of job training (about 2,000 hours per year), 8 modules, and 10 online classes. Pay increases with progress. Application requires a $50 fee. Online course access requires a $150 subscription for 12 months.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals seeking a career in residential electrical work, especially youth involved with the juvenile court system in the DC/Maryland area.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Electrical residential trainee and apprenticeship program with on-the-job training and online coursework.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Main location near Springdale, DC area; serves Washington DC and surrounding Maryland counties.
requirements_list: No GED or high school diploma required
Access to a computer and Wi-Fi required for online Computer Mediated Learning (CML) courses
$50 application fee
$150 subscription fee for 12 months of CML course access
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at https://www.jatc26.org/applications/residential-trainee/. A $50 application fee is required. CML courses available through a $150/12-month subscription to the PTSI system.

structured_extraction.program_description: Jail Addiction Services (JAS) is a comprehensive jail-based addiction treatment program for eligible inmates at the Montgomery County Correctional Facility (MCCF), operated through a collaboration between the Montgomery County Department of Correction and Rehabilitation and the Department of Health and Human Services. The program combines an eight-week education phase with ongoing aftercare, including community meetings, education and therapy groups, peer counseling, self-help meetings, cognitive behavioral skill-building, medication-assisted treatment, and naloxone training. Participants live in separate therapeutic housing units apart from the general population. As participants approach release, the program provides discharge planning and connections to community-based treatment services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides intensive in-custody addiction treatment including an eight-week education phase followed by an ongoing aftercare phase for the duration of incarceration. Participants live in therapeutic housing units separate from the general population. Services include community meetings, education and therapy groups, peer counseling, self-help meetings, cognitive behavioral skill-building, medication-assisted treatment, naloxone training, and discharge planning with linkages to community-based treatment services upon release.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible inmates at the Montgomery County Correctional Facility (MCCF) who have drug, alcohol, or substance use addiction issues.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Addiction treatment, education, therapeutic housing, peer counseling, cognitive behavioral skill-building, medication-assisted treatment, naloxone training, discharge planning, and linkage to community-based treatment services upon release.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to inmates housed at the Montgomery County Correctional Facility (MCCF), 22880 Whelan Lane, Boyds, Maryland 20841.
requirements_list: Must be an inmate at the Montgomery County Correctional Facility
Must be eligible for addiction treatment participation
Must meet eligibility criteria for addiction treatment services
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Jail Addiction Services at (240) 773-9991 or inquire through the facility's Inmate Services. Contact program manager Monir Khanjani, LCSW-C at MCCF for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A training program that teaches janitorial staff how to properly recycle and reduce waste in commercial settings. Sessions cover recycling regulations, recyclable materials, container types, roles and responsibilities, green cleaning practices, and how to troubleshoot common recycling challenges. Training is available in-person (45-minute sessions with Q&A) and online in English and Spanish.
eligible_industries: Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free in-person and online training sessions for janitorial staff. In-person sessions are 45 minutes long with 15 minutes of interactive Q&A. Online training is available in English and Spanish.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Janitorial service providers and their staff working in commercial settings in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training on recycling practices, waste reduction, and green cleaning in commercial buildings
