structured_extraction.program_name: Keeping it SAFE Student Video Contest
structured_extraction.program_description: Student teams from Montgomery County public and private high schools and middle schools create a 30-second public service announcement video about the risks and dangers of underage (under-21) alcohol use. Teams compete for cash prizes awarded to their affiliated school or organization. This is not an anti-drunk driving message contest. The Keeping it SAFE (KIS) Coalition is a multi-agency, public-private coalition established in 1992 with goals of deterring underage alcohol use and reducing youth access to alcohol.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Cash prizes awarded to the affiliated school or organization (not to individual students). High school prizes: 1st place $1,000, 2nd place $500, 3rd place $350, Honorable Mention $100. Middle school prizes: 1st place $500, 2nd place $300, 3rd place $250, Honorable Mention $100. The video with the most 'likes' receives an additional $150 prize. Each student in a qualifying submission also receives 5 SSL (Service Learning) hours. Winning entries may be submitted to media outlets.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Student teams of two or more enrolled in Montgomery County public or private schools, or faith-based or service-based organizations in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cash prizes are payable to affiliated schools or organizations only; prizes are not paid directly to individual students.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Open to students enrolled in Montgomery County public or private schools or in faith-based or service-based organizations in Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Teams must have two or more students
Students must be enrolled in a Montgomery County public or private school or a faith-based or service-based organization
Video must be exactly 30 seconds in length
Video must address one of the three specified topics about under-21 alcohol use risks and dangers
Video must not include copyrighted materials without documented permission
This is not an anti-drunk driving message contest
No clothing, language, or music glorifying alcohol, drugs, sex, violence, or gangs
No branded products featured
Public domain or royalty-free music only
Video must be 16x9 aspect ratio, 720p or higher resolution
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the online application form and submit a link to your video entry. Each participating student must also complete a consent and release form. Information sessions were held in January 2026.

structured_extraction.program_name: Kids Ride Free - Youth Cruiser SmarTrip Card (Ride On)
structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County youth ages 5 to 18 (or older if still in high school) can ride for free on all Montgomery County Department of Transportation (MCDOT) buses — including Ride On, Ride On extRa, Ride On Flex, and Flash — as well as most Metrobuses within the county, through the Kids Ride Free program. The Youth Cruiser SmarTrip Card is a free transit card issued to eligible Montgomery County youth that enables free Metrobus rides and can hold stored value for use on Metrorail, other Metrobuses, and additional SmarTrip-accepting transit agencies. Cards are distributed to eligible students through participating schools, making it easier for youth to access free transit. Starting June 29, 2025, zero fares apply to all riders on MCDOT buses. Starting February 1, 2026, a Youth Cruiser SmarTrip card is required for free Metrobus rides. Children under 5 must be accompanied by a parent or guardian and ride free on MCDOT buses.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free bus rides on all MCDOT buses (Ride On, Ride On extRa, Ride On Flex, and Flash) for youth ages 18 and under (or older if still in high school). Free rides on most Metrobuses within Montgomery County are available for residents ages 5 to 18 (or older if still in high school) using a Youth Cruiser SmarTrip card. The Youth Cruiser SmarTrip card is issued at no cost; first card and replacement cards are free. Cards are distributed through participating schools or can be obtained in person at county locations. The card enables free Metrobus rides (no fare deducted) and can hold stored value for Metrorail and other SmarTrip-accepting transit agencies. Children under 5 must be accompanied by a parent or guardian and ride free on MCDOT buses. Starting February 1, 2026, a Youth Cruiser SmarTrip card is required for free Metrobus rides.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free public bus transportation on MCDOT buses and Metrobuses within Montgomery County; stored-value transit use on Metrorail and other SmarTrip-accepting agencies.

Free Metrobus rides are available for Montgomery County residents ages 5 to 18. Students attending participating schools in Montgomery County are eligible. U.S. citizenship is not required.

structured_extraction.program_name: Landlord Risk Mitigation Fund (LRMF) – Services to End and Prevent Homelessness (SEPH) Landlord Supports
structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County's Services to End and Prevent Homelessness (SEPH) partners with landlords to quickly match them with potential tenants experiencing or at risk of homelessness. The Landlord Risk Mitigation Fund (LRMF) is a core component of this program, helping landlords reduce the financial risk of renting to tenants referred through SEPH. Landlords who partner with SEPH gain access to special incentives, supported tenants, resources, and networking opportunities to help keep their rental units consistently leased. Incentives include free unit marketing, financial bonuses for signing up ($500) and referring other landlords ($250), a risk mitigation fund to cover potential property damage (up to $5,000 annually per household, $10,000 lifetime limit) or unpaid rent, double security deposits where appropriate, consistent rent payments from housing providers, care coordination, conflict mediation, technical assistance, and networking opportunities with legal and regulatory updates.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Landlords who partner with SEPH and rent to referred tenants receive: (1) a Landlord Risk Mitigation Fund to cover property damage beyond normal wear and tear (up to $5,000 annually per household, $10,000 lifetime limit per household, minimum reimbursement $100) or unpaid rent at lease end; (2) vacancy loss reimbursement (up to 2 months); (3) free marketing of rental units; (4) double security deposit where appropriate; (5) financial sign-on bonus ($500 for new landlords, $250 for referrals); (6) consistent rent payments from housing providers; (7) care coordination and conflict mediation services; (8) access to technical assistance; and (9) networking opportunities and legal/regulatory updates. Claims require supporting documentation including lease terms, damage descriptions, repair receipts, insurance information, and evidence of collection attempts. Landlords must attempt collection from the tenant and wait 10 business days before submitting a claim.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landlords and property owners with licensed rental properties in Montgomery County who rent or are willing to rent to tenants referred through the county's Services to End and Prevent Homelessness (SEPH) program, including those seeking to keep their rental units consistently leased while serving tenants who need housing stability. Eligible tenants include participants in SHaRP, RRH, HIP, and PSH programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Covers financial risks associated with renting to referred tenants, including reimbursement for property damage beyond normal wear and tear, unpaid rent/rental arrears, and vacancy losses. Landlords also receive sign-on incentive payments, double security deposits, free unit marketing, care coordination, conflict mediation, technical assistance, and networking opportunities for partnering with the county's homelessness prevention program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to landlords with rental properties located in Montgomery County, Maryland.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Landlords interested in partnering with SEPH can contact the Department of Health and Human Services at LRMF@montgomerycountymd.gov to connect with available tenants and access incentives. Landlords must attempt collection from the tenant and wait 10 business days before submitting a claim. Program documents including the LRMF Claim Form, Brochure & FAQs, Inspection Checklist, and Program Agreement are available for download from the county website.

structured_extraction.program_name: Law Enforcement Officer Safety Act (LEOSA) Qualification Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Montgomery County Police Department offers a LEOSA (H.R. 218) qualification training and certification program for retired MCPD officers. Qualified retirees complete a firearms qualification course and receive a LEOSA card that allows them to carry a concealed firearm as permitted under federal law (18 U.S.C. 926C).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Retired MCPD officers attend a firearms qualification class at the Public Safety Training Academy (PSTA) indoor range in Gaithersburg, MD. Classes are offered monthly, limited to 13 students per session, with two time slots per session (0800 hrs and noon). Upon successful qualification, retirees receive a LEOSA certification card allowing them to carry concealed firearms under 18 U.S.C. 926C. Applicants must apply at least 30 days but no more than 60 days before their class date. Retirees must supply their own firearm, holster, and a minimum of 100 rounds of ammunition.

structured_extraction.program_description: Lead for Impact (LFI) is a six-month peer leadership development program for professionals working to end homelessness in Montgomery County. Participants build leadership skills, confidence, and peer community through group workshops, one-on-one coaching sessions, small group meetings, and a personal leadership project. Leadership is defined as "the ability to take responsibility for something that matters to you and then successfully engage others in bringing it to life."
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A six-month cohort-based leadership program that includes: a virtual orientation session, six group workshops (mix of in-person and virtual on May 1, May 15, June 17, July 17, August 21, September 18, October 16), three one-on-one virtual coaching sessions per participant, monthly small group peer meetings, monthly pre-work (recorded video lessons and reflection exercises, estimated 1 hour/month), completion of a 360-degree leadership profile, and development of a personal Leadership Project. Total time commitment is estimated at 2–4 hours per week.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Professionals at any level — from direct service providers to executive officers — working in organizations focused on ending homelessness in Montgomery County, across both the private sector and county government.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Leadership development, skill-building, peer community, and advancing a personal leadership project aimed at reducing homelessness in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to individuals working within Montgomery County, Maryland's homelessness-response ecosystem.
requirements_list: Must be contributing to or interested in expanding impact on ending homelessness in Montgomery County
Must be ready to step more fully into a leadership role
Must be available for all scheduled sessions (May 1, May 15, June 17, July 17, August 21, September 18, October 16)
Must submit both written and video application components
Space is limited; a selection process is used to choose participants who demonstrate good program fit and contribute to a diverse cohort
Participation confirmation communicated by April 17, 2025
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Google Form with personal information and written responses, then submit video responses to a separate form. structured_extraction.program_name: Live Healthy – Health, Dental and Prescription Discounts (Montgomery RX / Live Healthy)
structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County partners with the National Association of Counties (NACo) to offer residents free prescription discount cards and low-fee dental and health discount programs. The prescription discount card (Montgomery RX) is free and covers brand-name and generic drugs at participating pharmacies (68,000+ retail pharmacies nationwide) with no claim forms or annual fees, saving an average of 24% off retail price. The Dental Discount program provides discounts of 15% to 50% on dental procedures including check-ups, cleanings, fillings, crowns, and root canals, with no deductibles and no benefit maximums, and access to over 110,000 participating dental professionals nationwide. The Health Discount program offers savings of 15%–75% on vision services, hearing aids, diabetes supplies, lab work, screenings, and more. Prescription discounts also apply to pets of county residents. This is NOT insurance; members pay full cost minus applicable discount.

Health Discount program is $6.95/month per individual or $69/year, offering 15%–75% savings on vision, hearing aids, diabetes supplies, prepaid lab tests, screenings, and more. Combined Health + Dental plan is $13.90/month per individual or $138/year. This is NOT insurance; members pay full cost minus applicable discount.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program requires prime contractors on large Montgomery County government contracts (High Dollar Value Contracts with estimated value exceeding $10 million) to subcontract at least 10% of the contract value to certified local businesses. The goal is to increase local business participation in County procurement, ensuring that in aggregate at least 10% of the total dollar value of all High Dollar Value Contracts goes to local businesses. It establishes procedures to facilitate this local business participation goal. Businesses must be certified by the Montgomery County Office of Procurement, Division of Business Relations and Compliance, and may apply through the Montgomery County Central Vendor Registration System (CVRS).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Prime contractors on High Dollar Value Contracts (estimated value over $10 million) must award at least 10% of contract dollars to certified local business subcontractors. In aggregate, at least 10% of the total dollar value of all High Dollar Value Contracts must go to local businesses. The contractor must complete a PMMD-192 performance plan specifying the percentage of contract dollars going to local business subcontractors, attach certification letters, and obtain approval from the Director of the Office of Procurement. Subcontracts must include binding arbitration language for dispute resolution and the plan covers the entire contract life through final expiration. To qualify as a local business, the company must be certified by the Montgomery County Office of Procurement and have its principal place of business in Montgomery County — either with all locations in the county, or with the county location accounting for more than 50% of total employees or gross sales.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local businesses certified by Montgomery County Office of Procurement with a principal place of business in Montgomery County that want to participate as subcontractors on large County procurement contracts, and prime contractors holding High Dollar Value Contracts in Montgomery County.

structured_extraction.program_name: Low Income Household Water Assistance Program (LIHWAP)
structured_extraction.program_description: Federally-funded American Rescue Plan program that provides assistance to help low-income households pay water and wastewater bills. The program can restore disconnected services, prevent disconnection, and reduce outstanding past-due balances. Benefits are based on household income, household size, and the amount owed on the water or wastewater account.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging from $100 to $2,000 to pay down arrearages (balances 30 or more days past due) on water and/or wastewater accounts. Benefits can also cover standard billing and reconnection fees. Service address must have a minimum arrearage balance of $100 to qualify. Applications are processed first come, first served until funding is depleted. Household income must not exceed 60% of State Median Income (thresholds range $3,121–$8,283+ per month based on household size).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income renters, homeowners, and public housing residents in Montgomery County responsible for water or wastewater bill payment, with past-due balances, who live at the property receiving assistance
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Restoration of disconnected water or wastewater services; prevention of disconnection; payment of arrearages, standard billing fees, and reconnection fees on water or wastewater accounts
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. Applicant must be a Maryland resident and must live at the property for which assistance is provided.

structured_extraction.program_description: The MC Groceries Program helps Montgomery County families with children access fresh and shelf-stable food through an online shopping platform. Eligible households receive monthly grocery benefits loaded to an Instacart Fresh Funds account on the 15th of each month (or next business day) and can use them for grocery delivery or pickup at local retailers. Benefits cover eligible food and non-alcoholic beverage items including fresh/frozen produce, seafood, dairy, eggs, meat and meat alternatives, bakery, deli, and pantry staples; driver tips, delivery fees, and service fees can also be covered. Households may receive up to $100 per eligible child per month (ages 0–18 who are not eligible for SNAP), up to a maximum of $400 per month, with up to 700 families served. The program targets families who do not qualify for the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), helping to close the 'SNAP gap' and support food security for children in Montgomery County. The program is part of Montgomery County's Strategic Plan to End Childhood Hunger and is funded through Montgomery County Council Extraordinary Resolution No. 24-37 ($1.8 million, December 2023) and FY2025 Operating Budget allocations. The current benefits cycle runs from July 15, 2025 to July 15, 2026, with a new cycle (July 2026–July 2027) anticipated. The program is administered by the Office of Food Systems Resilience (OFSR) in partnership with Montgomery County DHHS.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible households receive $100 per month for each child under age 18 who is not eligible for SNAP, up to a maximum of $400 per month (up to 700 families served). Benefits are loaded as Instacart Fresh Funds credits on the 15th of each month (or next business day) and can be used to purchase eligible fresh and shelf-stable food and non-alcoholic beverage items — including fresh/frozen produce, seafood, dairy, eggs, meat and meat alternatives, bakery, deli, and pantry staples — through the Instacart platform for home delivery or store pickup. Driver tips, delivery fees, and service fees may also be covered. The current program is funded for one year, with benefits available from July 15, 2025 to July 15, 2026.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Program enrollment is not currently open to new participants for the current cycle (July 15, 2025 – July 15, 2026); waitlist available for the upcoming benefits cycle (July 2026 – July 2027)

structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with at least one child under 18 residing in Montgomery County who do not receive SNAP benefits and have post-tax household income below 400% of the Federal Poverty Level (e.g., $124,000/year for a family of 4). Seniors (age 60+) may access additional support through the Instacart Health Senior Support Line at (844) 981-3433, available daily 8 a.m. to 11 p.m. ET.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of eligible fresh and shelf-stable food and non-alcoholic beverage items (including fresh/frozen produce, seafood, dairy, eggs, meat and meat alternatives, bakery, deli, and pantry staples) through the Instacart platform for home delivery or store pickup. Driver tips, delivery fees, and service fees may also be covered.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must reside in Montgomery County, Maryland throughout the program period.
requirements_list: Must reside in Montgomery County throughout the program
Must have at least one child under age 18 who is not eligible for SNAP benefits
Post-tax household income must be below 400% of the Federal Poverty Level (e.g., $124,000/year for a family of 4)
Must upload proof of income (pay stubs from last 30 days or employer letter)
Must upload a valid photo ID for parent(s) or guardians
Must upload proof of address (lease, landlord letter, driver's license, or utility bill)
Must upload government-issued proof of identity for all children in the program (e.g., birth certificate or school documents)
Must be able to navigate an English-only platform to use benefits
Must have access to a backup electronic payment method (debit card, credit card, Google Pay, Apple Pay, PayPal, or Klarna)
Must consent to participate in a mid-year check-in
Orders must be placed, delivered, and/or picked up within the same benefit period
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Contact a Nutrition Benefits Navigator (Montgomery County Food Council at SNAP@mocofoodcouncil.org / 301-818-3614, or DHHS Navigation Line at 240-777-4141) for a brief eligibility pre-screening. 2. If pre-screening criteria are met, the Navigator helps you complete the waitlist form. 3. When an opening becomes available, you will be notified and asked to complete a full application and submit required documentation including proof of income, photo ID, proof of address, and proof of identity for children. 4. Once enrolled, participants receive instructions to create an Instacart Fresh Funds account and receive a unique code to access monthly benefits. Enrollment is first-come, first-served based on completed applications. The program is also conducting a limited enrollment expansion for new households; contact OFSR or NBO grantee partners for enrollment information. Seniors needing assistance with account setup or order placement may call the Instacart Health Senior Support Line at (844) 981-3433, available daily 8 a.m. to 11 p.m. ET.

structured_extraction.program_name: Make Office Vacancy Extinct (MOVE) Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The MOVE Grant Program is a business incentive grant program under Montgomery County's Economic Development Fund that provides one-time financial support to businesses to help reduce office vacancy in Montgomery County. It attracts new businesses and supports expanding businesses by offering grants to offset expenses related to their first commercial office space lease or an expansion lease of at least 500 square feet of Class A or B office or flex space in Montgomery County. Grants are awarded on a first-come, first-served basis based on the eligible square footage of the signed lease. The program is not available to retail, restaurant, independent financial, or insurance agent/broker establishments. The program's policies and procedures are governed by Executive Regulation MCER NO. 12-24.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time grant to help businesses offset expenses related to their first commercial office lease or an expansion lease of at least 500 square feet in Montgomery County. Grants are based on eligible square footage of the signed lease: less than 7,500 SF receives $8/SF (max $60,000); 7,501–10,000 SF receives $10/SF (max $100,000); more than 10,000 SF receives $12.50/SF (max $150,000); strategic industry businesses receive $15/SF (max $150,000). Leased space must be Class A or B office or flex space. Grant is disbursed after a site visit confirms occupancy. Not available to retail, restaurant, independent financial, or insurance agent/broker establishments.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Completed application must be submitted on or before 180 days of the lease execution date; subject to availability of funding
structured_extraction.program_audience: New businesses locating in Montgomery County, existing businesses relocating within Montgomery County, and existing businesses expanding in Montgomery County. Eligible businesses must be in good standing with Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) and sign their first commercial office lease or expand an existing commercial office lease by at least 500 square feet of Class A or B office or flex space in Montgomery County, MD.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Offsetting expenses related to a first commercial office lease or expansion lease of at least 500 square feet in Montgomery County; support for businesses locating, relocating, or expanding office space in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Office space must be located in Montgomery County, Maryland. Space must be Class A or B office or flex space.
requirements_list: Must be signing first commercial lease for office space OR expanding existing office lease by at least 500 square feet
Lease term must be 36 months or greater
Lease must be for Class A or B office or flex space in Montgomery County
Must submit an executed inaugural commercial lease or expanded commercial lease
Business must be in good standing with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation
Must submit signed Articles of Incorporation or equivalent documents
Must submit a utility bill or equivalent document as proof of occupancy
Must submit a complete business plan with type, purpose, and financial projections
Completed application must be submitted within 180 days of the lease execution date
Lease premises must be labeled as Office Space by third-party software and have a real property address
Lease cannot be between the business and its subsidiary
Business purpose cannot be retail, restaurant, or independent financial or insurance agent/broker
Lease must be a direct lease for at least three years
Business must be locating, relocating, or expanding office space in Montgomery County
Must meet eligibility criteria established in the bill
Business must not be owned, primarily funded, or controlled by a government agency
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review all eligibility criteria and Executive Regulation 12-24, then apply through the online portal at montgomerycountymd.seamlessdocs.com. Submit all required supporting documents including articles of incorporation, signed lease, proof of occupancy, and a business plan. Applications are reviewed in the order received (first-come, first-served). A site visit will be scheduled to verify occupancy before grant disbursement. A copy of the full regulation can be obtained from the Department of Finance, 101 Monroe Street, Rockville, Maryland, 20850.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Health Connection – Health Insurance Enrollment Assistance (Health Connect Assistance)
structured_extraction.program_description: Helps Montgomery County residents apply for and enroll in health insurance through Maryland's official health insurance marketplace (Maryland Health Connection). Free in-person, phone, and virtual enrollment assistance is available from trained, certified staff to help individuals and families find and sign up for a health plan. Assistance is available in more than 200 languages, including Relay services for the deaf and hard of hearing, and interpreter services at no cost. Licensed insurance brokers are also available to help choose a private health plan.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free, personalized enrollment assistance to help residents apply for health insurance through Maryland Health Connection. Help is available in person at four locations (Germantown, Rockville, and two Silver Spring sites) without an appointment, by phone at 240-777-1815 (Monday–Friday 8 a.m.–4 p.m.) or the Maryland Health Connection Call Center at 1-855-642-8572 (Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–6 p.m.), or through a virtual callback queue. Free language assistance and interpretation services are available in multiple languages including Spanish, Amharic, Arabic, Chinese, Farsi, French, Gujarati, Haitian Creole, Igbo, Korean, Portuguese, Russian, Tagalog, Urdu, Vietnamese, and Yoruba; relay services are available for deaf and hard of hearing individuals at no cost. Licensed insurance brokers are also available to help choose a private health plan via a broker connect form for a callback within 30 minutes.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents who need help enrolling in or applying for health insurance through Maryland Health Connection; non-English speakers; deaf and hard of hearing individuals
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Health insurance enrollment and application assistance through Maryland Health Connection
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a resident of Montgomery County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at MarylandHealthConnection.gov, call the Maryland Health Connection Call Center at 1-855-642-8572, call the Montgomery County Call Center at 240-777-1815 (Monday–Friday 8 a.m.–4 p.m.), scan the QR code to join a virtual callback queue, visit one of four in-person locations without an appointment (bring required documents listed on the application checklist), or complete the broker connect form to speak with a licensed insurance agent within 30 minutes. To request interpreter services, call 1-855-642-8572.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides on-site and in-home Community Health Nurse Case Management services to uninsured pregnant women and children up to age two. Services include health education, assessment and referral, and help accessing health, economic, and self-sufficiency programs. Program includes Nurse Home Visiting for first-time moms, teens, and high-risk individuals; Community Health Worker Home Visiting for pregnant persons with low health literacy or social concerns; and the Babies Born Healthy Program for African American pregnant persons in the Silver Spring region.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Nurse case management services delivered in the home or at a health center, including individual health education, care coordination, and referrals to health and social services. Services include nurse home visits, community health worker home visits, and specialized care coordination for high-risk pregnant persons and first-time mothers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Uninsured pregnant women enrolled in the Montgomery County Maternity Partnership program and their infants up to age two who need nurse case management services. Also includes first-time mothers, teens, pregnant persons with high-risk conditions (diabetes, hypertension, history of loss, preterm/low birth weight, substance abuse/behavioral health concerns), low health literacy, and African American pregnant persons in the Silver Spring region.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Health education during pregnancy and after birth, care coordination, referrals to health, economic, and self-sufficiency services, and home visiting services for high-risk pregnant persons and first-time mothers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland; Silver Spring region specifically for the Babies Born Healthy Program
requirements_list: Must be uninsured
Must be pregnant and enrolled in the Montgomery County Maternity Partnership program, or an infant of an enrolled woman
Must need nurse case management services

Qualifying social/medical risk factors may include: low health literacy, unsafe living environment, history of preterm birth, chronic medical conditions (e.g., diabetes, hypertension), depression/behavioral health concerns, history of prior pregnancy loss, close child spacing, low birth weight history, substance abuse concerns
First-time mothers and teens are eligible for Nurse Home Visiting
Pregnant persons with low health literacy or first birth in the U.S. are eligible for Community Health Worker Home Visiting
African American pregnant persons in the Silver Spring region are eligible for the Babies Born Healthy Program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: No application is required. Women enrolled in the County Maternity Partnership program for prenatal services and their infants are assessed and provided nurse case management if needed. Referrals can be submitted via the Montgomery Perinatal Program Referral Form.

structured_extraction.program_name: Medical Assistance (MA) for Aged, Blind, or Disabled and Medicare Savings Programs
structured_extraction.program_description: Medical Assistance for the Aged, Blind, and Disabled (MA-ABD) and Medicare Savings Programs (MSPs) are Medicaid-administered programs that help low-income residents cover healthcare costs. MA-ABD provides full Medicaid health coverage for those with very low income. Medicare Savings Programs help Medicare beneficiaries by paying for Medicare premiums and out-of-pocket costs such as deductibles and co-pays.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MA-ABD provides full Medicaid health coverage for low-income aged (65+), blind, or disabled individuals. Medicare Savings Programs cover Medicare premiums through the Special Low Income Medicare Beneficiary Program (SLMB) and Medicare deductibles and co-pays through the Qualified Medicare Beneficiary Program (QMB). There are no fees or payments required from recipients.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income Montgomery County residents who are aged (65 or older), blind, or disabled, as well as Medicare beneficiaries with income within specific limits.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Healthcare coverage including medical services, Medicare premiums, Medicare deductibles, and co-pays.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Montgomery County, Maryland. Applications can be filed in person at offices in Silver Spring, Rockville, or Germantown.
requirements_list: Must be aged (65+), blind, or disabled, OR a Medicare beneficiary
Income and assets must be within program limits
Must provide proof of identity
Must provide Social Security number
Must provide proof of income
Must provide proof of citizenship or immigration status (for non-U.S. born applicants)
Those receiving Supplemental Security Income (SSI) automatically qualify for MA-ABD
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at the Maryland Benefits Programs & Services Portal (benefits.maryland.gov), by mail, by fax, or in person at a regional office in Silver Spring, Rockville, or Germantown. Interpreter services are available. Processing takes approximately 30 days.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant-funded program that provides 'last resort' non-emergency transportation for Montgomery County residents who receive Medicaid (Medical Assistance) and have no other means of getting to medically necessary appointments. The program serves ambulatory, wheelchair, and stretcher-bound recipients. Transportation modes include ambulance (BLS, ALS, SCT/P, SCT/N, Neo-natal), wheelchair van, paratransit vehicle, public transit system, or sedan/cab based on clinical necessity and medical condition. Rides can be scheduled up to 7 days in advance; next-day service requires a request by noon the prior business day. Trip scheduling is available Monday–Friday (except holidays) between 8:30 a.m. and 12:00 noon.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free non-emergency transportation to and from medical appointments covered by Medical Assistance (Medicaid) for eligible Montgomery County residents who have no other available transportation. Transportation modes include ambulance, wheelchair van, paratransit vehicle, public transit, or sedan/cab based on clinical necessity. Certification is valid for one year from the certification date. Transportation can be scheduled up to 7 days in advance; next-day service requires a request by noon the prior business day. The office schedules trips Monday–Friday (except holidays) between 8:30 a.m. and 12:00 noon.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents who have eligible, non-restrictive Medical Assistance (Medicaid) and need transportation to medically necessary services covered by Medical Assistance with no other available means of transport. Also serves seniors and individuals with medical conditions or disabilities that prevent use of public transportation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Transportation to and from medical appointments and medically necessary services covered by Medical Assistance (Medicaid). Not for hospital discharges or transfers (a separate Transfer and Discharge form applies for those).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Montgomery County, Maryland residents only. Must provide proof of Montgomery County residency (utility bill, mortgage/lease, state ID, driver's license, or phone bill).
requirements_list: Must be a Montgomery County resident
Must have eligible, non-restrictive Medical Assistance (Medicaid)
Must have a valid 11-digit Medical Assistance number or Social Security number
Must need transportation to medically necessary services covered by Medical Assistance
Must have exhausted all alternative transportation resources, or be physically unable to use other existing transportation
Physician Certification Form must be completed by a health care provider (Physician, Physician Assistant, CRNP, or Dentist) with legible diagnosis and explanation of medical necessity
Medical necessity documentation with underlying diagnosis and clinical justification required
Certification is valid for one year from the certification date; periodic recertification required
Must notify office of address or medical condition changes
Must sign and return Authorization for Release of Information form
Medicare reimbursement status must be verified where applicable
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit completed Physician Certification Form and proof of Montgomery County residency by mail to the Medicaid and Senior Transportation Section. Applicants are notified in writing of eligibility status (determinations are not provided by phone). Once certified, call the Trip Scheduling Line at 240-777-5899 during scheduling hours (Monday–Friday, 8:30 a.m.–12:00 noon, except holidays) to schedule rides. Authorization numbers for specific trips are typically provided within 24 hours of request.

structured_extraction.program_description: A monthly injectable medication program (VIVITROL) offered to eligible individuals in the custody of Montgomery County's Department of Correction and Rehabilitation. VIVITROL is a nonaddictive opioid antagonist that blocks the effects of opioids and supports recovery from alcohol or opioid dependence. Jail Addiction Services staff run a weekly group for interested individuals to discuss VIVITROL and other medication-assisted treatment options to support their recovery after release.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Once-monthly VIVITROL (naltrexone) injection provided to eligible individuals in custody who meet medical criteria and release considerations. Includes a weekly group session with Jail Addiction Services staff to discuss medication-assisted treatment options before release.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals currently incarcerated at the Montgomery County Correctional Facility who are opioid- or alcohol-dependent and meet medical criteria for VIVITROL treatment.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Medication-assisted treatment with VIVITROL injections and related recovery support services to prevent relapse to opioid or alcohol dependence upon release.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only to individuals in custody at the Montgomery County Correctional Facility.
requirements_list: Must be in the custody of the Montgomery County Department of Correction and Rehabilitation
Must meet medical criteria for VIVITROL
Must be opioid-free at the time of initial VIVITROL administration
Alcohol-dependent patients must be able to abstain from alcohol in an outpatient setting prior to treatment initiation
Must not be actively drinking at time of first administration
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individuals in custody at the Montgomery County Correctional Facility can express interest through Jail Addiction Services staff. Eligibility is reviewed with all interested candidates. A weekly group is offered to those considering VIVITROL and other medication-assisted treatment.

structured_extraction.program_description: A problem-solving court program in Montgomery County's Circuit and District Courts that diverts adults with severe, persistent mental illness who have been charged with or are on probation for offenses related to their mental illness away from incarceration and into community-based treatment and services. The program aims to reduce repeat arrests by addressing the root cause of criminal behavior. Participants follow an individualized treatment plan (Care Plan) over a minimum of 18 months across three phases (4 months, 6 months, 8 months), meeting goals such as medication compliance, therapy engagement, stable housing, employment, and sobriety to graduate. All court costs and fees are waived upon admission to the program. Participants who successfully complete the program have their criminal charges reduced or dropped. Eligible mental illnesses include schizophrenia, clinical depression, bipolar disorder, PTSD, and Traumatic Brain Injury. Veterans with mental health conditions and/or substance abuse issues and individuals with developmental disabilities who also have mental illness may also be eligible.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive court-supervised, community-based mental health treatment and services instead of incarceration, including an individualized Care Plan covering medication management, therapy, substance abuse treatment, stable housing, employment support, and case management. Services may also include psychiatric rehabilitation, vocational rehabilitation, education assistance, housing assistance (including transitional and permanent housing), intensive case management, individual therapy, job training, medical/dental care, support groups, cognitive behavioral therapy, day treatment, residential services, and crisis intervention. All court costs and fines are waived upon admission to the program (per Administrative Order dated November 15, 2016), and any prior judgments for costs/fines are vacated. The program runs for a minimum of 18 months across three phases (4 months, 6 months, 8 months). Participants who successfully complete the program have their criminal charges reduced or dropped.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults age 18 or older who are Montgomery County residents, diagnosed with a severe persistent mental illness (including schizophrenia, clinical depression, bipolar disorder, PTSD, Traumatic Brain Injury, or other serious mental illness), deemed legally competent, and charged with or on probation for offenses related to their mental health diagnosis. Veterans with mental health conditions and/or substance abuse issues and individuals with developmental disabilities who also have mental illness may also be eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Community-based mental health treatment, supervision, therapy, medication management, stable housing support, employment assistance, substance abuse treatment, case management, psychiatric rehabilitation, vocational rehabilitation, education assistance, medical/dental care, support groups, cognitive behavioral therapy, day treatment, residential services, crisis intervention, and other support services as outlined in an individualized Care Plan.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be residents of Montgomery County, Maryland, and must reside in court-approved housing within Montgomery County during program participation.
requirements_list: Must be age 18 or older
Must be a resident of Montgomery County
Must reside in court-approved housing within Montgomery County
Must be diagnosed with a severe, persistent mental illness
Must be deemed legally competent
Must be charged with, or on probation for, offenses related to their mental health diagnosis
Participation is voluntary
Must receive approval from the State's Attorney's Office given current charges and criminal history
Must have a documented history of hospitalizations and/or services related to mental illness
Must complete diagnostic evaluation and comply with care plan
Must follow prescribed medication regimen
Must sign medical/treatment records authorization
Must abstain from controlled substances and illegal drugs
Must submit to drug/alcohol testing at any time
Must report all new law enforcement contact within 24 hours
Must report changes in housing, employment, medication, or treatment within 24 hours
Must appear for all court dates
Must accept potential probation extension and court sanctions/termination for non-compliance
Must waive right to speedy trial
Cannot have been convicted of a violent crime (within previous five years per similar program standards)
Must not be charged with a domestic violence crime
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Anyone (judge, prosecutor, defense attorney, law enforcement, Department of Correction and Rehabilitation, Parole and Probation, state hospital, private mental health provider, family member, or any person) can refer a defendant by contacting the Problem Solving Court Coordinator. Step 1: Submit referral and a signed limited release of information to the Coordinator. Step 2: Coordinator contacts the candidate's attorney, the State's Attorney's Office, and the clinical team from Montgomery County Health and Human Services to assess willingness, approval, and documented mental health history. Step 3: Case is presented to the Mental Health Court Team for judge approval. Step 4: Upon approval, the plea or violation of probation is set before the Mental Health Court judges; the candidate is sentenced and placed on probation with a special condition of completing Mental Health Court. Step 5: Defendant petitions for acceptance into program, acknowledges receipt of program documents, and signs the MHC Agreement including a sworn statement of eligibility.

Case managers act as brokers to link clients to services on a short-term basis, typically lasting three to six months. No direct medical, dental, or psychiatric treatment is provided.

structured_extraction.program_name: Minority, Female and Disabled-Owned Businesses Program (MFD)
structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County's MFD Program helps state- and agency-certified minority, female, service-disabled veteran-owned, and disabled-owned businesses gain access to prime contractor and subcontractor opportunities with Montgomery County government agencies. Certified firms (at least 51% owned, controlled, and managed by a minority person, woman, or disabled person) are classified in the Central Vendor Registration System. The program sets participation goals for each purchasing category: Construction 22%, Professional Services 25%, Non-Professional Services 24%, and Goods 10% (effective January 1, 2025). It also conducts outreach activities, workshops, and forums where businesses can explore individual and joint contracting opportunities. The program applies to contracts with estimated dollar value of $50,000 or more and includes non-profit entities where at least 51% of service providers are persons with disabilities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program connects certified MFD businesses (at least 51% owned, controlled, and managed by a minority person, woman, or disabled person) with prime and subcontractor opportunities with Montgomery County government agencies. Participation goals are set for each purchasing category: Construction 22%, Professional Services 25%, Non-Professional Services 24%, and Goods 10% (effective January 1, 2025). Certified firms are classified in the Central Vendor Registration System. The program conducts outreach activities, workshops, and forums to support MFD firms in pursuing individual and joint contracting opportunities. Applies to contracts with estimated dollar value of $50,000 or more. Prime contractors must subcontract a specified percentage of total contract dollar value to certified MFD businesses; failure to comply results in liquidated damages and potential contract termination. Business owners must provide proof of existing state or agency certification.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Minority, female, service-disabled veteran-owned, and disabled-owned businesses (at least 51% owned, controlled, and managed by an African American, Hispanic American, Asian American, Native American, disabled person, or woman) seeking prime contractor and subcontractor opportunities with Montgomery County government agencies. Also includes non-profit entities where at least 51% of service providers are persons with disabilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participation as prime contractors or subcontractors on Montgomery County government contracts in construction, professional services, non-professional services, and goods categories, as well as participation in outreach activities and workshops to explore individual and joint contracting opportunities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to businesses seeking to contract with Montgomery County, Maryland government agencies. Businesses based inside or outside Montgomery County may participate.
requirements_list: Business must be at least 51% owned, controlled, and managed daily by a minority person(s), woman, or disabled person
Eligible categories: African American, Hispanic American, Asian American, Native American, Disabled Persons, and Women
Must hold a certification from an accepted certifying agency (e.g., MDOT-MBE, SBA 8(a), SBA Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business, WBENC, MSDC, MWBOO, or City of Baltimore)
Must provide proof of certification to obtain classification in the Central Vendor Registration System
As of October 1, 2021, U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs 'Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business' certification qualifies under the disabled category
Must be seeking contracting opportunities with Montgomery County government agencies
Applies to contracts with estimated dollar value of $50,000 or more
Prime contractors must submit MFD Subcontractor Performance Plan for Director approval
Prime contractors must include binding arbitration provision in subcontracts with MFD subcontractors
Must comply with wage requirements under Montgomery County Code § 11B-33A
Must maintain payroll records and submit required reports
Contractors must conspicuously post wage requirement notices to employees
For non-profits: 51% of personnel must be persons with disabilities
Must be designated as subcontractor in contract Performance Plan (if applicable)
Must submit MFD Report of Payments Received monthly during service period (if applicable)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Businesses must obtain certification from one of the accepted certifying agencies listed by the program (e.g., MDOT-MBE, SBA 8(a), SBA Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business, WBENC, MSDC, MWBOO, or City of Baltimore). Once certified, provide proof of certification when registering in the Montgomery County Central Vendor Registration System, then participate in outreach activities and pursue contracting opportunities with Montgomery County government agencies. Prime contractors must complete the PMMD-65 Subcontractor Performance Plan form with contractor and subcontractor details, submit with certification letters, and obtain approval from the Office of Procurement. Designated MFD subcontractors must submit completed MFD Report of Payments Received monthly to the Office of Business Relations and Compliance during the contract period.

structured_extraction.program_description: A shared cold storage unit (20'x10') that gives small Montgomery County farms access to refrigerated space for aggregating, co-packing, and storing produce after harvest and before distribution to food assistance providers, schools, food pantries, and businesses. The program helps reduce food waste and supports the county's food system resiliency goals, while also supporting broader agricultural micro-hub operations in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Farmers receive access to a shared cold storage unit capable of holding approximately 10 standard pallets (average 8,750 lbs of product at a time). During peak growing and harvest seasons (mid-March through mid-November), the unit can distribute an estimated 303,300 lbs of produce annually, valued at approximately $853,000. Farmers must complete a brief training and request space through the Food Corridor App.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small farms and agricultural businesses located in Montgomery County, Maryland that need shared cold storage space for aggregating and distributing produce, as well as farmers interested in micro-hub operations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cold storage space for farm produce after harvest and before distribution to food pantries, schools, food assistance providers, and businesses; support for micro-hub agricultural operations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to county farmers and agricultural businesses in Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a small county farm
Must complete a brief training
Must request space through the Food Corridor App
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Farmers complete a brief training and then request storage space through the Food Corridor App at app.thefoodcorridor.com.

It delivers 300 Mbps symmetrical internet access at no cost, along with free access to Plume's smart home Wi-Fi system including hardware, parental controls, and cybersecurity features.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free 300 Mbps/300 Mbps symmetrical internet service provided at no charge to eligible residents. Also includes free access to Plume HomePass smart home system with SuperPod hardware, adaptive Wi-Fi, parental controls, advanced cybersecurity, and 24/7 customer support.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income and special needs residents living in selected Montgomery County affordable housing developments.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free home broadband internet access and smart home Wi-Fi services for personal and family use.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of specific affordable housing properties in Montgomery County, Maryland, including locations in Silver Spring, Bethesda, Rockville, Takoma Park, and Gaithersburg.

Must be low-income or have special needs
Must reside in an active MoCoNet-enabled building
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Residents of active MoCoNet buildings can apply by scanning the QR code on the program page or visiting the linked sign-up form. For questions, call 240-773-8017.

The clinic operates on a walk-in, first-come, first-served basis with no appointments required.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Access to medical, dental, and behavioral health services.

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County's MPDU Program provides affordable rental apartments and for-sale homes to income-eligible residents, and requires developers of new residential developments with 20 or more units to include a percentage of MPDUs priced or rented at affordable rates for eligible lower-income households. The program establishes policies, procedures, and pricing standards for administering Montgomery County's Moderately Priced Housing law, including income limits for eligibility (up to 70% of the Washington Metro Area Median Income), maximum rental rates for garden apartments and high-rise apartments, regulated sales prices for affordable dwelling units, alternative methods of meeting MPDU requirements, and a priority system for the sale of MPDUs. It applies to residential subdivisions that have an MPDU requirement, to MPDUs that are sold, resold, or rented through the program, and to individuals or households applying to purchase or rent an MPDU. Unit prices range from approximately $150,000 for a 2-bedroom condominium to approximately $220,000 for a 3-bedroom townhouse with a garage. Resale price controls apply during the control period (30 years for for-sale units purchased after April 1, 2005; 10 years for units first purchased before April 1, 2005; 99 years for rental units). During the control period for for-sale units, the home must be sold at a County-calculated maximum resale price to another MPDU-certified household; the owner may not rent the property without written permission, may not obtain a reverse mortgage, and must submit annual certification of residency (effective 2025). After the control period expires, the seller may sell at market value but must pay the County 50% of the excess profit above the MPDU resale value; the County uses those shared profit funds to finance new affordable housing for low- and moderate-income families. Renters apply directly to MPDU apartment communities throughout the county; first-time homebuyers with moderate household income (minimum $40,000; maximum varies by household size, up to $133,000 for a household of 6 as of April 2025) can purchase new or resale MPDU homes at affordable prices through a lottery selection process. Applicants must complete three required classes — an MPDU Orientation Seminar, a HUD-approved First-Time Homebuyer class, and an online Application Tutorial — before submitting a purchase application and must obtain a mortgage pre-qualification letter for at least $150,000 from a licensed lender. Developers who build MPDUs receive waivers of certain fees and expedited permitting assistance from DHCA. Priority is given to people who live or work in Montgomery County. The rental program does not apply to the City of Rockville or City of Gaithersburg, which have separate MPDU programs. The MPDU office also oversees refinancing and home equity lines of credit (HELOCs) for homes under the MPDU program, calculating Maximum Resale Price and Shared Profit amounts and managing the right-of-first-refusal process with the County and Housing Opportunities Commission (HOC).
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: For residents (rentals): Below-market-rate apartments are available in MPDU apartment communities throughout Montgomery County, with rents set by county Executive Regulation and recalculated annually. Rent increases are limited to once per 12-month period and cannot exceed the county Voluntary Rent Guideline. For garden apartments, income limits are set at 65% of AMI for new tenants; for high-rise apartments (5+ stories), the limit is 70% AMI. Renewing tenants may have incomes up to 130% of the new-tenant maximum. Application fees are capped at $25, and no amenities fees or non-structured parking fees may be charged. Applicants apply directly to individual MPDU apartment properties, which verify income and credit history to determine eligibility. For residents (purchases): Affordable for-sale homes (new and resale) are offered to first-time homebuyers with moderate household income (minimum $40,000 per year; maximum up to 70% of Washington Metro AMI — approximately $80,500 for a single person, up to $133,000 for a household of 6 as of April 2025). Unit prices range from approximately $150,000 for a 2-bedroom condominium to approximately $220,000 for a 3-bedroom townhouse with a garage. Homes are subject to a 30-year (or 10-year for MPDUs first purchased before April 1, 2005) control period during which the owner must occupy the home as their primary residence and may only sell at the MPDU-controlled resale price. No direct financial subsidy is provided to buyers or renters — the affordability comes from the developer requirement to offer units at controlled prices. The program does not provide financing; buyers must obtain their own mortgage. Applicants must obtain a mortgage pre-qualification letter from a licensed lender for at least $150,000, issued within the last three months; applications are reviewed within 30 days of submission. During the control period, the home must be sold at a County-calculated maximum resale price to another MPDU-certified household. After the control period expires, the seller may sell at market value but must pay the County 50% of the excess profit above the MPDU resale value, which the County uses to finance new affordable housing. For current MPDU homeowners: The MPDU office calculates the Maximum Resale Price and Shared Profit amounts, manages the right-of-first-refusal process with the County and HOC, and coordinates the Random Selection Drawing (RSD) for eligible buyers. Refinancing or obtaining a HELOC requires prior contact with the MPDU Office. After the control period, the County takes 50% of the excess profit and then terminates the MPDU covenants. Improvement credits of up to 10% of the original purchase price may be applied toward the resale price calculation for permanent improvements that add market value (supported by receipts, cancelled checks, paid invoices, or credit card statements and any required building permits; no credit for owner labor or tools). For developers: Developers who build MPDUs receive a waiver of the Systems Development Charge (SDC) imposed by WSSC and the development impact tax collected by DPS. MPDUs also qualify for 'green tape' expedited processing at DPS. DHCA staff assists developers in calculating sales prices and rents and guides them through the Agreement to Build and Offering Agreement process. Alternative methods of meeting MPDU requirements are also available.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Income-eligible individuals and households seeking affordable rental or for-sale housing in Montgomery County, including first-time homebuyers with moderate income (minimum $40,000; maximum varies by household size up to 70% of Washington Metro AMI) who have completed required classes, income-eligible renters who do not own residential property, current MPDU homeowners who are under or have completed their MPDU control period and want to refinance, obtain a HELOC, or sell their home, developers and builders of new residential developments with 20 or more units who are required to provide MPDUs, as well as real estate agents, lenders, and title companies involved in MPDU transactions. structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Affordable housing — renting or purchasing a moderately priced dwelling unit at regulated sales prices or rents; or, for developers, fee waivers (impact tax and SDC) and expedited permitting for MPDU units built within qualifying developments. Shared profit funds collected after the control period are used by the County to finance new affordable housing for low- and moderate-income families.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For residents (rentals): Apply directly to an MPDU apartment community of your choice. Review the list of apartment communities with MPDU units at https://apps.montgomerycountymd.gov/dhca-mpdu/Rental/List, contact one or more communities, and submit an application to the property management company. The management company verifies income and credit history and determines eligibility. The DHCA MPDU office does not accept applications or issue Certificates of Eligibility for rentals. For residents (purchases): 1. Complete and submit a pre-screening intake form to the Greater Washington Urban League (GWUL) at MPDU@GWUL.org to register for the MPDU Orientation Seminar (held virtually on the 2nd and 4th Thursdays of each month). 2. After passing the Orientation Seminar post-test, register for and complete the First-Time Homebuyer Class (held virtually on the 2nd Saturday of each month). 3. Receive instructions from the MPDU office and complete the online Application Tutorial via the MPDU Application Portal, passing all tests with a score of 80% or better. 4. Gather all required documents (pay stubs, tax returns, photo ID, mortgage pre-qualification letter, etc.) and submit application with all required documents through the MPDU Application Portal. 5. Await email confirmation and review (processing takes up to 30 days). If approved, receive a Certificate of Eligibility valid for one year; certificates must be renewed within 60 days of expiration. 6. Use your certificate number to enter online Random Selection Drawings for available MPDU units. If selected, the builder or selling agent will contact you to offer the unit. For resale during control period: (1) Request Maximum Resale Price from MPDU Office using the Resale and Refinance Price Request Form; list all permanent improvements with documentation (receipts, cancelled checks, paid invoices, or credit card statements) and building permits; improvement credits are limited to 10% of original purchase price. (2) Complete and return the MPDU Marketing Form. (3) Offer the MPDU to the County and HOC (right of first refusal). (4) If County/HOC declines, offer to MPDU certificate holders via Random Selection Drawing using a trained real estate agent. (5) If no certificate holders are interested, request written permission to sell to the general public. (6) After a contract is ratified, submit required documents to MPDU Office within 14 days. For refinancing/HELOC: (1) Submit Resale Price Request Form to MPDU Office. (2) Receive refinance/HELOC value letter. (3) Share letter with lender. (4) Send lender and settlement details to MPDU Office before closing. (5) MPDU Office sends official refinance/HELOC letter to lender and settlement company. For post-control period sale: (1) Submit Shared Profit Calculation Request Form (at least 21 days before settlement) and, if applicable, Calculation of Improvements Credit Request Form plus the first page of the signed Sales Contract and listing agreement. (2) Receive Shared Profit Calculation from MPDU Office. (3) Settlement company sends Shared Profit payment check to Montgomery County DHCA. For annual residency certification: Complete the 2025 Certification form with owner information, property details, and residency attestation; submit with valid Driver's License/REAL ID and two acceptable proof-of-residency documents to MPDU.Cert@montgomerycountymd.gov by October 30, 2025. For developers: 1. Obtain MPDU requirement from Montgomery County Planning Board during development review. 2. Execute an Agreement to Build MPDUs with DHCA before building permits are issued by DPS. 3. When MPDUs are ready for occupancy, submit an Offering Agreement to DHCA for approval (including all required schedules, signed and notarized covenants, and completion of sales training for onsite and settlement staff). 4. DHCA notifies the Housing Opportunities Commission (HOC) and certain nonprofits, who have 21 days to select units. 5. DHCA schedules a Random Selection Drawing (RSD) for eligible MPDU certificate holders and provides the sales agent with a prioritized list of buyers. 6. Developer/builder completes sale or lease transactions with eligible certificate holders and submits required forms to DHCA. For general inquiries, contact the Department of Housing and Community Affairs, 1401 Rockville Pike, 4th Floor, Rockville, Maryland 20850. For MPDU resale inquiries, email MPDU.Resales@montgomerycountymd.gov.

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery Cares - Medical Care for Uninsured Adults
structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery Cares is a network of community-based health care providers and geographically distributed health centers and clinics that deliver free primary and specialty medical care to low-income, uninsured adults living in Montgomery County. The program has no immigration status requirement. Services include doctor and nurse visits, medications, lab tests, x-rays, specialist referrals, oral health care, mental health services, women's health services, and access to other health programs. Multilingual support is available at participating locations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free medical services through participating community health centers, including check-ups, sick visits, medications, lab tests, x-rays, specialist referrals, oral health care, mental health services, women's health services, and other clinical services. No fees or payments are required. Montgomery Cares is accepted as insurance coverage at participating clinics, regardless of immigration status.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income, uninsured adults aged 18 or older who live in Montgomery County and are not enrolled in any health insurance plan, regardless of immigration status.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Primary and specialty health care services including doctor/nurse visits, medications, lab tests, x-rays, specialist referrals, oral health care, mental health services, women's health services, and other health programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a resident of Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be age 18 or older
Must be uninsured
Must have income at or below 250% of the Federal Poverty Level
Must be a resident of Montgomery County
Must not be enrolled in any health insurance including Medicaid, Medicare, commercial insurance, or employer-sponsored coverage

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact a Montgomery Cares health center of your choice to enroll. Bring proof of income (such as pay stubs, tax returns, or a letter from an employer) and proof of Montgomery County residency (such as a lease, utility bill, or driver's license) to your first appointment. Call 311 or 240-777-0311 to find a health center near you. You may also contact individual clinics by phone to schedule an appointment or inquire about walk-in availability, or visit a participating clinic listed on the Primary Care Coalition website.

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County Agricultural Land Preservation Easement Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County purchases agricultural land preservation easements to permanently protect farmland from commercial, residential, or industrial development. The program includes both direct county easement purchases and supplemental payments toward Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation purchases. The county uses a formula-based system (Agricultural Value Formula) to determine easement values based on farm size, soil quality, road frontage, land tenure, and farm location. Offers to sell are ranked by a defined process, and payments follow specified terms. Because the county program is not dependent on State approval, applications are typically processed in 6–12 months.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The County purchases agricultural preservation easements directly and provides supplemental payments toward Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation easement purchases. Easement values are calculated using the Agricultural Value Formula (AVF), which considers farm size, soil quality, land tenure, road frontage, and proximity to the edge of an agricultural zone. Offers to sell are ranked by a set process, and payments follow specified terms. One Transferable Development Right (TDR) per 25 acres must be retained with the property to be eligible for maximum easement value.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmland owners in Montgomery County's Agricultural Reserve, Rural Cluster Zone, or Rural Zone with at least 50 acres (or 10+ acres of cropland adjacent to protected land)
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Compensation to landowners in exchange for permanently restricting development on their agricultural land; purchase of agricultural land preservation easements
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Land must be located in the Agricultural Reserve (AR), Rural Cluster Zone (RC), Rural Zone (RZ), or other zones with significant agricultural value in Montgomery County, MD. Land must lie outside water and sewer categories 1, 2, and 3.
requirements_list: Farm must be located in the Agricultural Reserve (AR), Rural Cluster Zone (RC), Rural Zone (RZ), or other zones with significant agricultural value
Minimum property size of 50 acres, or 10 or more acres of cropland adjacent to other protected land
One Transferable Development Right (TDR) for every 25 acres must be retained with the property prior to easement application to be eligible for maximum easement value
At least 50 percent of the land must meet USDA Soil Classification Standards I–III or Woodland Classifications 1 and 2
Land must lie outside water and sewer categories 1, 2, and 3
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Mike Weyand at michael.weyand@montgomerycountymd.gov with questions about preservation easements or to explore preservation options for your property.

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County Bar Foundation Pro Bono Legal Clinics – TESS Center
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides free legal services to low-income Montgomery County residents in civil cases. Offers two service options: legal advice clinics on a walk-in basis and a client intake line for referral to an attorney volunteer for direct representation. Supported by Maryland Legal Services Corporation and Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services.

Practice areas include divorce, separation agreements, custody, adoption/guardianship, name changes, bankruptcy, debt defense (limited), landlord-tenant issues (deposits only), limited immigration services, wills, and powers of attorney. Registration for clinics is available from 6 p.m. to 6:30 p.m. on clinic days. A $25.00 non-refundable processing fee (Cashier's Check or Money Order only) is required for formal representation.

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County Community Reinvestment and Repair Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: A county fund that provides grants to community-based organizations serving communities most impacted by disproportionate enforcement of cannabis prohibition laws before July 1, 2022. Funded through a portion of cannabis tax revenue as established by Bill 4-24, the program supports community-based initiatives that benefit low-income communities and areas of Montgomery County disproportionately impacted by the War on Drugs. Total awards are estimated at $1 million annually, subject to appropriation of funds and execution of grant agreements between the county and awardees.

Funds must be used for community-based initiatives benefiting low-income communities or disproportionately impacted areas. Funds cannot be used for law enforcement agencies or activities.

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County Dental Health Services Sliding Fee Discount Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) offers affordable dental health services on a sliding fee scale to low-income, uninsured or underinsured residents of all ages, regardless of immigration status. Services are delivered at reduced fees through local participating dentists and county dental clinics (Dental Connections Program) as well as directly at county dental clinic locations. The sliding fee discount reduces the cost of dental care based on family income, family size, insurance coverage, and the number of visits needed. The program covers oral exams, x-rays, cleanings, fillings, extractions, root canals, crowns, dentures, fluoride applications, sealants, and oral health education. School-based dental services are also available for children enrolled in eligible schools, including free dental screenings, cleanings, fluoride varnish, dental sealants, and Silver Diamine Fluoride (SDF) treatment to stop tooth decay. A referral from the county dental program is required before services are provided. Fees are adjusted according to ability to pay using a county sliding fee scale based on the Maryland Department of Health scale. The Adult Dental Program component provides uninsured adults ages 19-59 low-cost dental care at county clinics for a flat fee of $20 per regular visit or $30 per emergency visit, including non-surgical extractions and limited oral surgery. Patients needing specialty dental care are given information for appropriate resources. Patients who still need help after the discount is applied can request an interest-free payment plan for up to 12 months or a hardship fee reduction or waiver considered case-by-case every 6 months, covering all dental expenses within a 6-month window from the date of hardship determination. The Dental Connections component connects residents to community dental offices through partnerships with local dentists and dental organizations, with program availability depending on funding.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Dental services are provided at reduced fees through participating local dentists and county dental clinics using a sliding fee scale set by the Maryland Department of Health, with costs adjusted based on family income, family size, insurance coverage, and number of visits. The Adult Dental Program provides low-cost dental care at county clinics for $20 per regular visit or $30 per emergency visit, including non-surgical extractions and limited oral surgery, for adults ages 19-59 with income at or below 250% of the Federal Poverty Level. Services include oral exams, x-rays, cleanings, fillings, extractions, root canal therapy, crowns, dentures, fluoride applications, sealants, and oral health education. The Dental Connections Program connects residents to community dental offices through partnerships with local dentists and dental organizations; program availability depends on funding. Patients can also request: (1) an interest-free payment plan for up to 12 months with no additional application required, or (2) a dental hardship fee reduction or waiver considered case-by-case every 6 months, covering all dental expenses within a 6-month window from the date of hardship determination.
