structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County Design for Life Property Tax Credit Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Design for Life (DFL) Property Tax Credit Program encourages development of housing that accommodates a wider range of accessibility needs, helping Montgomery County residents remain in their homes as physical needs change. As authorized by County Council Bill 5-13 (effective July 1, 2014), it offers property tax credits for homeowners, builders, and developers in Montgomery County who incorporate accessibility features into their homes, including no-step entrances, wider doorways, accessible bathrooms, ramps, elevators or lifts, grab bars, lever door handles, chair lifts, sensory alarms, and other mobility-friendly upgrades. Three tracks are available for homeowners: (1) Individual Accessibility Features — up to $2,500 (50% of eligible costs, minus other subsidies) for installing one or more of 15 listed features when spending more than $500; (2) Level I (VISITable) standards — up to $3,000 (100% of reasonable costs, minus other subsidies); and (3) Level II (LIVEable) standards — up to $10,000 (100% of reasonable costs, minus other subsidies). Credits are applied at up to $2,000 per tax year, with any remaining balance carrying over to future years and transferring with the property on sale. Builders and developers can receive variable credits against the Development Impact Tax for Public School Improvements ($500–$2,000 per qualifying house depending on the percentage of homes meeting Level I or Level II standards). The program also includes a Design for Life Builder/Homeowner and Project Certification Program that certifies properties meeting Visit-Ability and Live-Ability accessibility design standards. Builders also benefit from fast-track permitting and community recognition. The program is open to homeowners of all ages and life stages, including people with temporary or permanent disabilities. Properties located in the City of Rockville or City of Gaithersburg must also submit a signed affidavit from their respective city confirming all inspections were completed. Property owners apply for a building permit, complete the required construction and inspection, then submit a tax credit application. The county Department of Finance assesses the appropriate credit, which appears as a line item on the next property tax bill. Annual county-wide limits apply: $100,000 for individual accessibility features and $500,000 for Level I/II accessibility standards.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two types of tax credits are available. (1) Homeowner Property Tax Credits with three tiers: (a) Individual Accessibility Features — a credit equal to the lesser of 50% of eligible costs or $2,500, minus any subsidies received, when eligible expenditures exceed $500 and are incurred within 12 months of application; (b) Level I (VISITable) — up to $3,000 (100% of reasonable costs, minus subsidies including school impact tax credit) for a single-family home meeting Level I accessibility standards; (c) Level II (LIVEable) — up to $10,000 (100% of reasonable costs, minus subsidies including school impact tax credit) for a single-family home meeting Level II accessibility standards. Credits are applied at a maximum of $2,000 per tax year; excess credit carries forward to future years and transfers with the property on sale. Only one application per property per tax year is accepted. Annual county-wide limits: $100,000 for individual accessibility features; $500,000 for Level I/II accessibility standards. (2) Development Impact Tax for School Improvements credit for new single-family developments: $500 per residence if 5% meet Level I; $1,000 per residence if 10% meet Level I; $1,500 per residence if 20% meet Level I; $2,000 per residence if 30% meet Level I. Requires an Impact Tax Credit Certification Agreement signed before building permits are issued. For phased developments, a Master Agreement and separate agreements for each phase are required. The credit is assessed by the Montgomery County Department of Finance after construction is completed and a final inspection is passed, appearing as a line item on the property owner's next property tax bill. A full tax credit incentive table is available at https://assets.montgomerycountymd.gov/files/2026-04/DFLTaxCreditIncentiveTable.pdf.

Includes first-time homebuyers, families, active adults, people with temporary or permanent disabilities, home care facility owners, as well as builders and developers constructing new single-family homes seeking property tax or school impact tax credits for incorporating accessibility features. Also covers property owners making accessible (Design For Life) improvements to residential or commercial buildings.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and installation of accessibility features such as no-step entrances, ramps, 32-inch or wider doorways, elevators or lifts, accessible or maneuverable bathrooms and kitchens, reinforced walls with grab bars, accessible showers or tubs, lever door handles, chair lifts, chair-height toilets, relocated switches, thermostats and outlets, closet renovations, alternative sensory alarms, and other features that improve home accessibility and universal accessibility. Expenditures must exceed $500 and be incurred within 12 months of application. Also covers new construction or renovation of single-family homes to meet Visit-Ability and Live-Ability standards. Tax credits offset property taxes or Development Impact Tax for School Improvements for qualifying accessible home design features.

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County EV Purchasing Cooperative Pilot (EVPC)
structured_extraction.program_description: A cooperative program that uses the combined purchasing power of Montgomery County residents and businesses to secure discounts and incentives on new and pre-owned electric vehicles from local dealerships. The program connects members with community partners, participating organizations, and 'Electrified Dealers' to answer questions, organize events, and make EV ownership more affordable and convenient. Participating dealerships post rotating monthly incentives and discounts each month. Members gain access to new purchase incentives, group discounts, educational events, and resources to support EV adoption. Current examples of dealership offers include 0% financing for 72 months or $4,000 customer cash plus home charger installation on a 2025 Ford Mach-E (Koons Ford Silver Spring), $10,000 bonus cash for competitive owners/lessees purchasing a 2026 Chevrolet Equinox EV RS (Sport Chevrolet), and 0.99% financing for up to 60 months on a 2026 Honda Prologue EV Touring AWD (Sport Honda). Customers must confirm all offers directly with the dealership.

Rotating monthly incentives from participating dealerships include financing deals, cash bonuses, and other promotions. Some offers require approved credit or competitive owner/lessee status. The program also provides educational resources and connects members with community partners. Offers vary by dealership and are available at the dealership's discretion. Customers must confirm current offers directly with the participating dealership.

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County Energy-Efficient Buildings Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A two-tiered property tax credit program for owners of commercial and multi-family buildings in Montgomery County that make significant energy efficiency improvements or exceed current building code energy requirements, supporting the county's climate goals of 80% greenhouse gas emissions reduction by 2027 and zero emissions by 2035. For existing buildings, Tier 1 rewards measurable reductions in ENERGY STAR scores, with credits calculated based on improvement in ENERGY STAR score multiplied by a tier-based multiplier (1.0 to 2.5), and credits can reach up to 100% of County property taxes for two years. For newly constructed buildings, Tier 1 rewards buildings that perform at least 10% above code (demonstrated via the performance pathway), with credits calculated by multiplying the building's percentage above code by a multiplier (0.5 to 2.0), and credits can reach up to 100% of County property taxes for four years (or five years for Living Building Certification). Buildings that demonstrated code compliance via the prescriptive pathway are not eligible for new construction. Tier 2 (Building Sustainability Tax Credit) adds credit for achieving recognized green building certifications: for existing buildings, LEED O+M or BREEAM In-Use; for new construction, LEED, NGBS, BREEAM, PHIUS+, or Living Building Challenge. Tier 2 adds 25% or 50%/75% depending on certification level and building type. Buildings in Equity Emphasis Areas (MWCOG) receive an additional 10% credit. For existing buildings, up to three total applications (one initial plus two reapplications) are allowed per building. For newly constructed buildings, only one application per building is permitted. The program also sets annual limits on total credits granted and altered eligibility criteria, amounts, and durations by building type.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to 100% property tax credit against Montgomery County taxes. For existing buildings: credit applies for two years; Tier 1 credit is based on improvement in ENERGY STAR score multiplied by a tier-based multiplier (1.0 to 2.5); Tier 2 adds 25% (LEED O+M Gold or BREEAM In-Use Excellent) or 50% (LEED O+M Platinum or BREEAM In-Use Outstanding). For newly constructed buildings: credit applies for four years (five years for Living Building Certification sustainability credit); Tier 1 credit is based on percentage above code multiplied by a multiplier (0.5 to 2.0); buildings that demonstrated code compliance via the prescriptive pathway are not eligible; Tier 2 adds 25% (LEED Gold, NGBS Gold, PHIUS+/Passive House, BREEAM-NC Excellent or equivalent) or 75% (LEED Platinum, NGBS Emerald, BREEAM-NC Outstanding, LBC Petal Certification or equivalent). Buildings in MWCOG Equity Emphasis Areas receive an additional 10% credit. Maximum credit in any fiscal year cannot exceed 100% of the building's annual County property tax liability. Annual limits apply to total credits granted for existing buildings. Each building may apply up to 3 times for existing buildings (one initial application plus two reapplications); only one application per building is permitted for newly constructed buildings.

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County Government Tuition Assistance Program (TAP)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides tuition assistance funding and employee development support to eligible Montgomery County Government employees and active volunteers to support their professional development through education. Funding helps pay for education or training directly related to current job functions, career ladder, or career change within the County. Covers certificates, associate degrees, baccalaureate degrees, and graduate degrees, as well as credit courses, non-credit courses, and seminars. Funds are available on a first-come, first-served basis until the fiscal year budget is exhausted. The program is administered through the Office of Human Resources and includes ongoing updates to improve administration, increase accountability, and add better safeguards.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tuition assistance funds are provided to eligible county government employees with merit system status and active volunteers. Funding levels vary by employee bargaining unit (FOP, IAFF, MCGEO, UNREP, MCVFRA). For MCGEO and UNREP employees: tuition costs only (up to $2,300 for full-time, $1,150 for part-time per fiscal year). For IAFF and FOP employees: tuition plus direct/compulsory costs (lab fees, library services fees, registration fees, technology fees). For MCVFRA volunteers: tuition costs only, up to $1,830 per active volunteer per fiscal year. Does not cover books, supplies, application fees, parking, travel, food, lodging, audit courses, exam fees, courses outside USA, or recreational/faith-based courses. Funds are awarded on a first-come, first-served basis until the fiscal year budget is fully obligated. The program begins July 1st of each new fiscal year.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: June 18, 2026; applications must be submitted within fiscal year (July 1 – June 30); submit at least 2–4 weeks prior to course registration depending on bargaining unit
structured_extraction.contact_name: Dr. Rochelle Plummer, Manager, Professional Learning Training & Organizational Development; Teddy Ramet, Tuition Assistance Program SME; Anithia Rhodes, Tuition Assistance Program Manager
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County Government employees with merit system status (full-time and part-time year-round merit employees), including those affiliated with FOP, IAFF, MCGEO, UNREP bargaining units, as well as active volunteer firefighters and rescue personnel affiliated with MCVFRA, seeking tuition assistance or employee development support. Probationary employees are also eligible (reimbursed after achieving merit status).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition costs for educational courses or programs at accredited institutions recognized by the U.S. Department of Education or Higher Education Accreditation Commission, including certificates, associate degrees, baccalaureate degrees, graduate degrees, credit courses, non-credit courses, and seminars. For IAFF and FOP employees, also covers compulsory direct costs such as matriculation, registration, laboratory fees, and library services. Training must be directly related to current County job functions, career ladder positions, or approved career change within the County. Courses must be taken in the United States.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to employees of Montgomery County Government and active MCVFRA volunteers only. Courses must be taken at accredited colleges/universities recognized by the U.S. Department of Education or Higher Education Accreditation Commission, and must be held within the United States.

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County Green Bank Technical Assistance Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Montgomery County Green Bank provides technical assistance to commercial and other building owners and operators in Montgomery County to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, comply with Montgomery County's Energy Benchmarking Law, and generate jobs for contractors. Assistance includes ASHRAE Level I, II, and III/Investment Grade energy audits and targeted analyses into benchmarking, energy efficiency, solar PV, electrification, EV charging infrastructure, and resiliency measures. The program also connects building owners to qualified benchmarking vendors and can help offset the cost of benchmarking for first-time benchmarkers.

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County Head Start / Early Head Start (Birth to Five Community Based Model)
structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County Head Start provides early childhood education and family support services for children ages birth to 5 in Montgomery County. The Early Head Start component operates through a community-based model where registered family child care homes and licensed center-based programs partner as Early Head Start childcare hubs. Partners receive funding per child as well as wrap-around services including training, technical assistance, coaching, mental health consultation, and family engagement support. The program is a federal Head Start program with 5-year project periods, offering comprehensive services including health, nutrition, and family support.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible childcare programs receive $17,965 per child per year (monthly payments of $1,497 over 12 months) for providing a full-year (1,380 annual hours), full-day (9-hour) Early Head Start program. Partners also receive administrative support, training, technical assistance, ECE coaching support, family engagement services, health services for children, and education supplies and equipment from the County's Early Childhood Services program.

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County Prevailing Wage Law Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Requires that construction workers employed on Montgomery County-financed construction contracts of $250,000 or more are paid the prevailing wage — the going rate for comparable work in the private sector within the County. The law is modeled after the federal Davis-Bacon Act and the State of Maryland prevailing wage law. It prohibits misclassification of workers, requires certified payroll reporting, apprenticeship compliance, and allows the County to withhold payments or assess liquidated damages if violations are found. Enforced through Contractor Compliance and Monitoring, Inc. (CCMI).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Construction workers on qualifying County-financed contracts must be paid the prevailing wage rate (hourly rate plus fringe benefits) set by the Maryland Commissioner of Labor and Industry. Contractors must post wage rates at worksites, submit certified payroll records and fringe benefit statements within 14 days after each payroll period via LCPTracker, and provide proof of apprentice registration. Only actively enrolled apprentices may work at apprentice rates. Overtime must be paid for hours over 10 in a single day, over 40 in a workweek, or on Sundays and legal holidays. Monthly jobsite employee interviews are conducted. Liquidated damages of $20 per day per worker apply for underpayment or misclassification, and $10 per calendar day for late payroll submission.

structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. Applies to County-financed construction contracts of $250,000 or more. Does not apply if the Federal or State prevailing wage law already applies to the project.

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County Public Campaign Financing Program (Public Election Fund)
structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County's Public Election Fund (PEF) provides public matching funds to qualifying candidates running for County Executive or County Council. The program is designed to encourage greater voter participation, increase opportunities for residents to run for office, and reduce the influence of large private donations and contributions from businesses and political action groups. Montgomery County was the first county in the United States to have a public campaign finance program for local elections. Matching funds are provided to eligible candidates at tiered ratios — up to 7-to-1 on the first $50 — making it easier for a broader range of candidates to run for office. The program has been offered across multiple election cycles (2018, 2022, 2026). For the 2026 cycle, funds are governed by Council Bill 20-24 and Executive Regulation #10-25, with distribution reports issued monthly throughout the 2025–2026 election cycle. For the 2022 cycle, funds were governed by County Code and Executive Regulation 2-21, with distribution reports issued monthly during both primary and general election periods. For the 2018 cycle, compliance seminars were held and a Summary Guide Book was provided to assist candidates; 23 qualifying candidates received approximately $5.25 million in total matching public funds. In the 2022 cycle, approximately $3.7 million was distributed to 20 qualifying candidates. The program is administered by the Maryland State Board of Elections, the Montgomery County Department of Finance, and the Office of Consumer Protection.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Public matching funds are distributed based on a tiered matching ratio applied to qualifying contributions from Montgomery County residents. For the 2026 cycle, County Executive candidates can receive up to $870,170 per election; Council-at-Large candidates up to $290,060 per election; District Council candidates up to $145,030 per election. Matching ratios for County Executive: 7-to-1 (first $50), 4-to-1 (second $50), 2-to-1 (third $50), no match above $150. Matching ratios for County Council: 5-to-1 (first $50), 3-to-1 (second $50), 2-to-1 (third $50), no match above $150. For prior cycles (e.g., 2022, per Bill 31-20): County Executive candidates received $6 per dollar of the first $50, $4 per dollar of the second $50, and $2 per dollar of the third $50; County Council candidates received $4 per dollar of the first $50, $3 per dollar of the second $50, and $2 per dollar of the third $50, with maximums of $750,000 for County Executive, $250,000 for at-large Council, and $125,000 for district Council per election. Qualifying contributions must be from Montgomery County residents and range from $5 to $150 per contributor per 4-year election cycle. Distribution period for the 2026 cycle runs June 23, 2025 through December 3, 2026. Funds are distributed via ACH direct deposit within 3 business days of Board authorization on a regular reporting schedule throughout each election cycle. Unspent funds must be returned to the Fund within 90 days after the general election, except up to $10,000 may be retained for post-election expenses if the candidate commits to the next election cycle.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Notice of Intent (register with MDCRIS): April 15, 2026; Certificate of Candidacy: February 26, 2026; Qualifying Period closes: May 9, 2026 (45 days before primary); Primary Election: June 30, 2026; General Election: November 3, 2026

Post-election expenses up to $10,000 are permitted if the candidate retains funds for the next election cycle.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Submit your Certificate of Candidacy in person at the Montgomery County Board of Elections by February 26, 2026. 2. structured_extraction.program_description: A county law that limits how much landlords can raise rent each year on most residential rental units that are at least 23 years old. The annual rent increase allowance is based on the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U) for the Washington-Arlington-Alexandria area plus 3%, but cannot exceed 6%. The program also regulates fees landlords can charge tenants and allows landlords to petition for additional rent increases for capital improvements, fair return, or substantial renovations.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Limits annual rent increases to CPI-U + 3% or 6%, whichever is lower (5.7% for July 2025 through June 2026). Rent may only be increased once per 12-month period. Landlords may bank unused allowable increases (capped at 10%) for future use. Landlords may petition DHCA for additional rent increases through Capital Improvement Petitions (surcharge capped at 20% of base rent for all units, 15% for a subset of units) or Fair Return Petitions based on net operating income analysis. A 23-year exemption may be granted for buildings that undergo substantial renovations costing at least 40% of the assessed value. The program also regulates permissible fees landlords may charge tenants, including application fees, pet deposits (max $300, adjusted annually by CPI-U), late fees, lost key fees, lockout fees, parking fees, storage fees, and internet/cable fees, with increases limited to once per 12-month period and requiring 90 days written notice.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Tenants living in Montgomery County residential rental units that are at least 23 years old, and landlords who own and manage such units.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Protects tenants from excessive rent increases. Allows landlords to petition for higher increases to cover capital improvement costs (permanent structural alterations that enhance habitability, protect health/safety, or provide energy savings), ensure a fair return on investment, or obtain exemptions for substantial renovations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland only. Applies to all County-licensed residential rental units that are at least 23 years old, with certain exemptions. DHCA Office of Rent Stabilization is located at 1401 Rockville Pike, 4th Floor, Rockville, MD 20852.
requirements_list: Unit must be a County-licensed residential rental unit that is at least 23 years old (based on SDAT 'Year Built' record)

Unit must not fall under an exempt category (e.g., newly constructed units less than 23 years old, owner-occupied duplexes, accessory dwelling units, assisted living facilities, nursing homes, school dormitories, religious facilities, units subject to income-restricted regulatory agreements, units with substantial renovations within the prior 23 years, or units owned by landlords who own 2 or fewer rental units and are natural persons or trusts/estates)
Landlords must comply with annual data reporting requirements under County Code Section 29-51
Landlords in Troubled or At-Risk properties may not increase rents without DHCA approval
Rent increases require at least 90 days advance written notice to tenants
Landlord must not increase base rent more than once in a 12-month period
All regulated units in a rental housing must receive the same percentage rent increase
Capital Improvement Petitions must certify improvements are capital improvements and not ordinary maintenance; must be permanent structural alterations intended to enhance value
Capital improvements must be completed before surcharge implementation
Capital Improvement Petition must be filed with supporting documentation including comprehensive cost calculations per COMCOR 29.58.01.04(f)
Landlord must notify affected tenants of capital improvement petitions within 5 business days of filing by first-class mail and email

For Capital Improvement Certificate of Continuation: must be filed at least 90 days before original surcharge expires; proof that full cost has not been recovered within original surcharge period required

Fair Return Applications must include detailed financial documentation, gross income, operating and maintenance expenses, net operating income calculation, and fair return calculation using 3% + 10-year Treasury Note Yield benchmark; all Banked Amounts must be applied before consideration

Substantial Renovation Applications must include detailed plans, specifications, permits, building assessments, unit schedules; renovation costs must equal at least 40% of building value (exclusive of land); renovations must be completed within the past 23 years
Landlords must notify tenants of all petition/application filings within 5 business days
All regulated units must be properly registered and licensed with DHCA prior to any petition submission
Compliance required within 90 days of Executive Regulation 2-24 effective date (6/13/24)
Fees may only be increased once per 12-month period; 90-day written notice required for fee increases; documentation of actual costs must be provided to tenants
Compliance with Chapters 8, 26, and 29 of Montgomery County Code required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The program applies automatically to all qualifying units. Tenants who believe a landlord is violating rent stabilization rules can file a complaint with DHCA's Rent Stabilization Office by calling MC311 at 240-777-0311 or emailing dhca.ors.intake@montgomerycountymd.gov. Landlords who wish to petition for a Capital Improvement surcharge, Fair Return increase, or Substantial Renovation exemption must submit the relevant petition form with all required supporting documentation to the DHCA Office of Rent Stabilization. The Director reviews applications for completeness within 30 days and issues a preliminary decision within 60 days of receiving a complete application. Landlords must notify affected tenants within 5 business days of filing and distribute the Director's decision to tenants within 10 business days of approval.

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County Working Families Income Supplement (Refundable Earned Income Credit)
structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County provides a supplement to the Maryland State Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) for low-income working residents. Eligible county residents receive a tax credit equal to 56% of their State EITC. The program includes both a non-refundable tax credit component and a refundable Earned Income Credit (EIC) component. The refundable portion is administered in partnership with the Maryland Office of the Comptroller, which verifies eligibility and mails separate checks to qualifying residents on behalf of the County. ITIN (Individual Taxpayer Identification Number) filers are also eligible for the credit. State and County checks are mailed separately based on when the tax return is filed.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible residents receive a tax credit equal to 56% of the Maryland State Earned Income Tax Credit. The refundable portion is paid via a check from the Maryland Office of the Comptroller on behalf of Montgomery County. State and County checks are mailed separately. Checks are mailed based on filing date: returns filed through June result in checks mailed by end of July; July through September filings result in checks by end of October; returns filed through December result in checks by end of January. ITIN filers are eligible.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low- to moderate-income Montgomery County residents who worked during the tax year and are eligible for the Maryland State Earned Income Tax Credit, including ITIN filers. Eligibility for the refundable portion requires at least one dependent and having filed as a Montgomery County resident for the applicable tax year.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Refundable or non-refundable tax credit applied to reduce state and local tax liability or increase refund; direct financial assistance to low-income working residents in the form of a refundable tax credit check.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents who reside in and filed as a Montgomery County, Maryland resident for the applicable tax year.
requirements_list: Must file a Maryland tax return
Must be eligible for the Maryland State Earned Income Tax Credit
Must reside in Montgomery County
ITIN filers are eligible
Must be eligible for the federal Earned Income Credit
Must claim the Maryland EIC on state income tax return
Must have earned income in the tax year claimed
Must have at least one dependent (for refundable portion)
Must have filed as a Montgomery County resident for the tax year in which the credit is claimed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: No separate application is needed. Eligibility is determined when the resident files their Maryland income tax return. Residents can get assistance filing through the Community Action Agency's Volunteer Income Tax Assistance (VITA) program, including at VITA sites that serve ITIN taxpayers. For the refundable EIC, the Maryland Office of the Comptroller verifies eligibility and mails the County Refundable EIC check on behalf of Montgomery County. Questions about eligibility for the refundable portion should be directed to the Maryland Office of the Comptroller at (800) MDTAXES or (410) 260-7980.

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County – Local Business Preference Program (LBPP)
structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County's Local Business Preference Program gives local businesses a competitive advantage when bidding on county contracts. Businesses with a principal place of business in Montgomery County receive a 10% price reduction (up to $200,000) on Invitations for Bids (IFBs) for evaluation purposes only, or an evaluation factor worth 10% of total points on Requests for Proposals (RFPs). The program does not provide direct funding but improves competitiveness in county procurement.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Local businesses receive a 10% price preference reduction (capped at $200,000) on IFB bids for evaluation and award purposes only, or a 10% evaluation factor on RFP scoring. This is a preference points program — it does not provide direct funding but improves competitiveness in county procurement. Businesses apply through the Montgomery County Central Vendor Registration System (CVRS).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses with their principal place of business in Montgomery County that bid on county contracts through IFBs or RFPs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable — this is a bid preference program, not a direct funding program. The preference is applied during contract evaluation to improve a local business's chance of winning a county contract.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Business must have its principal place of business in Montgomery County: either (1) all physical locations are in the county, or (2) the county location(s) account for more than 50% of total employees or more than 50% of gross sales.
requirements_list: Business must have its principal place of business in Montgomery County
Must be independently owned — brokers and subsidiary businesses are not eligible
Must have a federal tax number or W-9 in the name of the business
Must be certified as a local business before submitting a bid or proposal (or apply before the bid/proposal deadline)
Preference does not apply to LSBRP IFBs or RFPs, contracts with State or Federal funding that prohibit it, or awards by discount or line item
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register or update your vendor profile at https://azex32.montgomerycountymd.gov/cvrs/ and follow the prompts. During registration, you will be given the option to enroll in the LBPP if you meet the criteria. You must be certified before submitting a bid or proposal, or at minimum apply before the submission deadline.

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County – Local Small Business Reserve Program (LSBRP)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Local Small Business Reserve Program (LSBRP) is a Montgomery County procurement program established by Bill 23-04 (effective July 25, 2005) that requires county departments to award at least 25% of the combined value of their procurement contracts for goods, services, and construction to registered and certified local small businesses. The program helps local small businesses compete for county contracts by reserving solicitations specifically for businesses of similar size and resources, and requires internet posting for certain purchases. Montgomery County-based retailers, construction and trades companies, wholesalers, service firms, manufacturers, and non-profits are encouraged to participate. The program establishes contract value thresholds specific to local small business participation and sets minimum percentage requirements for the combined value of contracts that county departments must award to local small businesses. A Veteran-Owned Business Preference Program (VBPP) launched January 2, 2025 gives verified veteran-owned local small businesses an additional 5% evaluation points on LSBRP proposals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: County departments reserve at least 25% of their procurement contracts for registered LSBRP vendors. Eligible businesses compete only against other local small businesses of similar size for county contracts for goods, services, and construction. Veteran-owned local small businesses receive an additional 5% evaluation points on LSBRP proposals through the VBPP. Registration is free through the County Vendor Registration System (CVRS).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Independently owned small businesses and non-profits with a principal place of business in Montgomery County, including retailers, wholesalers, service firms, construction and trades companies, and manufacturers that meet employee and revenue thresholds, seeking to participate in Montgomery County government contracting opportunities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Access to reserved county procurement opportunities for goods, services, and construction contracts designated for local small businesses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Business must have its principal place of business in Montgomery County. This means either all physical locations are in Montgomery County, or the Montgomery County location(s) account for more than 50% of total employees or gross sales.
requirements_list: Must be a registered and certified local small business
Must be an independently owned business (brokers and subsidiaries are not eligible)
Must have a federal tax number or W-9 in the name of the business
Principal place of business must be in Montgomery County

Must meet size thresholds by business type: Retail — 30 employees or $5M average sales; Wholesale — 30 employees or $5M average sales; Services — 100 employees or $10M average sales; Construction — 50 employees or $14M average sales; Manufacturing — 40 employees or $14M average sales
Must register through the County Vendor Registration System (CVRS) at no cost

For VBPP: must hold both LSBRP and VBPP certifications, and have a valid Veteran-Owned Small Business (VOSB) or Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) certificate from the U.S. SBA or VA's Center for Verification and Evaluation
Must be a local small business as defined by program criteria
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Businesses register and apply for LSBRP or VBPP certifications through the County Vendor Registration System (CVRS) at no cost. Vendors create and maintain a profile, upload required certification documents, and can then be identified for reserved procurement opportunities. The program was established by Bill 23-04, effective July 25, 2005. For additional information about the regulation and program details, contact the Office of Business Relations & Compliance, Department of General Services, 255 Rockville Pike, Rockville, Maryland 20850.

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery Parks Fee Reduction Program (parks facilities, no public assistance requirement)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides financial assistance to Montgomery County residents to reduce fees for parks programs operated by Montgomery Parks, part of the Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reduced fees for campsites, playgrounds, courts, parks, and other Montgomery Parks facilities and programs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents who need financial assistance to access parks programs
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Parks program and facility fees
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County residents

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides prenatal care and home-based case management services to at-risk pregnant and parenting families in Montgomery County. Services include prenatal care, home visiting, nurse case management or Community Health Worker services, health education, care coordination, and referrals to other resources during pregnancy and up to one year after birth (postpartum). Clients may be uninsured or enrolled in Medicaid; no immigration status is required.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: No-cost home visiting, nurse case management or Community Health Worker services, health education, care coordination, and referrals to other resources for eligible pregnant and postpartum women. Prenatal care services are provided regardless of immigration status. Services are delivered in the home; prenatal classes are offered at health centers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income, uninsured, or Medicaid-enrolled pregnant women or women who recently gave birth residing in Montgomery County, regardless of immigration status.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Prenatal care services, home visiting, nurse case management, health education during pregnancy, preparation for delivery, infant care support, and care coordination.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must reside in Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be pregnant or recently delivered
Must be low-income, uninsured, or enrolled in Medicaid
Must live in Montgomery County
No immigration status required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: No formal application is required. Contact the Silver Spring Health Center at 240-777-3160 or the Germantown Health Center at 240-777-3380 to enroll. Bring your Medicaid or Managed Care Organization insurance card if applicable. Visit the Montgomery Perinatal Program page on the Montgomery County website for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Multi-Family Food Scraps Recycling Technical Assistance Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County's Department of Environmental Protection provides free technical assistance and education to multi-family residential properties to help them set up and run a food scraps recycling collection program. County staff offer training, containers, compostable bags, and educational materials to support Zero Waste goals.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free technical assistance and education for multi-family property managers and residents. Assistance includes kick-off training sessions, in-unit food scraps recycling containers, certified compostable bags, labels, posters, and other educational materials. Staff also provide resident interest surveys and help properties track and report their recycling results.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Multi-family residential property managers, boards, and residents in Montgomery County who want to start a food scraps recycling program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Setting up and expanding food scraps recycling collection programs at multi-family properties, including resident training and educational outreach.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to multi-family properties located within Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Property must be a multi-family residential building
Property must be located in Montgomery County, Maryland
Board or management approval required
Property must engage residents and management to gauge interest before starting
Must sign a food scraps recycling collection contract with a licensed private hauler
Resident training must be provided
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Get informed about food scraps recycling options. Measure resident interest via survey. Present benefits to management, board, and residents. Request quotes from local licensed collectors. Review and sign a collection contract. Conduct resident training. Contact Multi-Family Recycling Program Manager Ruth Carbonell at Ruth.Carbonell@MontgomeryCountyMD.gov to express interest and schedule a kick-off training with DEP staff.

structured_extraction.program_description: The TRRAC (Think, Reduce and Recycle at Apartments and Condominiums) program provides education, outreach, training, and technical assistance to multi-family property owners, managers, staff, green team members, haulers/collectors, and residents to reduce waste and recycle more at apartments and condominiums, aiming for Zero Waste. Properties with seven or more dwelling units must also report their recycling activities to Montgomery County each year.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Program offers education, outreach, training, and technical assistance to help multi-family properties implement recycling programs and reduce waste. Resources include recycling bins, property manager guides, seminars, and webinars.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Multi-family property owners, managers, staff, green team members, haulers/collectors, and residents of apartments and condominiums in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Implementing recycling programs, reducing waste, and meeting annual recycling reporting requirements at apartments and condominiums
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: All multi-family properties (apartments and condominiums) are required to recycle
Properties with seven or more dwelling units must report recycling activities to Montgomery County each year
Annual recycling reports are due February 1 each year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Montgomery County Department of Environmental Protection. Property managers can order recycling bins, access guides, attend seminars and webinars, and file annual recycling reports through the county's online portal.

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County provides flexible loan financing to support the development and preservation of affordable housing, including new construction, acquisition, and rehabilitation of affordable multifamily rental and homeownership housing. Funding comes from the Housing Initiative Fund (HIF), which has been active since 1989, and other county resources. The county also administers Rental Agreements and Payment in Lieu of Taxes (PILOT) agreements as additional financial incentives for affordable housing development. DHCA evaluates applications based on County priorities including income levels served, preservation, production, family-sized units, mixed-income housing, senior housing, transit proximity, green building standards, permanent supportive housing, racial equity, readiness to proceed, community benefits, and homeownership. Large projects are defined as those with 10 or more county-funded units and $500,000 or more in county funds; smaller projects may use a simplified application.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: DHCA provides flexible loans from the Housing Initiative Fund (HIF) for acquiring, constructing, and rehabilitating multifamily affordable housing developments. The target interest rate is 3%, though the rate may vary based on project purpose and other financing partners. Loan repayment is structured to meet the project's financial needs and senior lender requirements. An equity contribution of 10% (excluding deferred developer fee) is an expected goal. Funds are disbursed during construction in coordination with senior lenders. DHCA is generally not a resource for predevelopment costs. The county also provides Rental Agreements and Payment in Lieu of Taxes (PILOT) tax incentive agreements as additional financial tools. Large projects are defined as those with 10 or more county-funded units and $500,000 or more in county funds; smaller projects may use a simplified application.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit and nonprofit affordable housing developers seeking to acquire, construct, or rehabilitate multifamily affordable rental and homeownership housing in Montgomery County, MD.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: New construction, acquisition, or rehabilitation of affordable multifamily rental and homeownership housing. Not available for predevelopment costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available for affordable housing development projects located in Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a for-profit or nonprofit affordable housing developer
Project must involve multifamily rental housing
Housing must be affordable rental housing for Montgomery County residents
Projects must serve households at or below Area Median Income (AMI) thresholds
Preference given to projects serving households at 50% AMI or below, including those at 30% AMI or below
Must demonstrate financial feasibility through a 20-year pro forma analysis
Must demonstrate that County financing is necessary for the project
Debt Service Coverage (DSC) of 1.0 required; loan-to-value ratio should not exceed 100% based on market-rate valuation
Targeting a 3:1 leverage ratio of other resources to County funds
Three years of independently audited financials required from the applicant
Site control and necessary plan approvals with Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission required
Preference given to projects that can close within 12 months of funding commitment or tax credit award
Projects receiving over $5 million must provide community benefits at no additional cost to the County
Properties must give the County right of first refusal if the property is sold
Properties must give preference to Montgomery County residents or workers for vacant units
Projects receiving federal funding must comply with applicable federal program requirements
County-funded projects must meet affordability requirements and maintain tenant income eligibility documentation
Property owners/managers must perform annual tenant income recertification for assisted units
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Developers submit either a small project application (for projects with fewer than 10 county-funded units or less than $500,000 in county funds) or a large project application (for projects with 10 or more county-funded units and $500,000 or more in county funds). Application forms including loan request summary forms, financial forms, and cost estimate forms are available on the DHCA website. DHCA evaluates applications based on how well projects meet County priorities including income levels served, preservation, production, family-sized units, mixed-income housing, senior housing, transit proximity, green building standards, permanent supportive housing, racial equity, readiness to proceed, community benefits, and homeownership. Projects are underwritten for financial feasibility. Contact Lawrence Cager at Lawrence.Cager@montgomerycountymd.gov for additional information.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides gap financing to experienced rental housing developers for multifamily rental housing projects with more than four units. The program aims to increase or preserve affordable rental housing in Montgomery County. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Gap financing for multifamily rental housing developments with more than four units. No maximum number of units. Funding amount is determined through underwriting and review by DHCA staff, the Selection Advisory Committee (SAC), and the DHCA Director. A conditional commitment letter details the final terms and conditions.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Experienced rental housing developers seeking gap financing for multifamily affordable rental housing projects in Montgomery County with more than four units.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Development or redevelopment of multifamily rental housing that increases or preserves affordable rental units.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Project must have more than four (4) units
Applicant must be an experienced rental housing developer
Project must comply with DHCA development and applicant requirements
Project must meet one or more County and DHCA preferred criteria to increase or preserve affordable rental housing
Applicants must complete an Inquiry or Intake Form before applying
Land use approvals, entitlements, and financing must be finalized before final application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Complete an Inquiry Form (for future projects) or an Intake Form (with detailed project information). 2. DHCA staff contacts the applicant to schedule a meeting with the Multifamily Section Manager and Chief of Housing. 3. Staff reviews the application, requests additional information as needed, and processes applications in the year funding is required. 4. Provide quarterly project updates to DHCA. 5. Receive a general support letter from DHCA if needed. 6. Finalize development plans (land use approvals, entitlements, financing). 7. Submit the final application to the Multifamily team for underwriting. 8. Project is reviewed by the DHCA Selection Advisory Committee (SAC). 9. SAC recommends the project to the DHCA Director for approval. 10. DHCA Director approves, modifies, or rejects the SAC recommendation. 11. Final approval is issued via a conditional commitment letter.

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County Government employees who are fluent in English and a second language can become certified in that language and receive a pay differential for all hours worked. The program certifies employees to provide language services to County residents with Limited English Proficiency (LEP), ensuring quality of language services. It is one of several channels to provide multilingual services to County residents. Certified employees may be called upon to provide language skills outside their service area or department.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Certified employees receive a multilingual pay differential for all hours worked and are registered in the Language Certified Employees Database. MCGEO and non-represented employees: Basic $1.00/hour, Advanced $1.50/hour. IAFF employees: Basic $1.00/hour. FOP employees: Basic $1.00/hour, Advanced $2.00/hour, Expert $3.00/hour. Certification levels: Basic (Listening/Speaking for front-facing positions serving LEP residents), Advanced (written translation of official County documents), Expert (FOP only, mastery for interrogations, investigations, and legal proceedings). Departments are responsible for funding the differential for all hours worked, including overtime.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County Government employees who are fluent in English and an approved second language and work in a front-facing position that interacts with County residents on a daily basis. Eligible departments include Police (FOP and Non-FOP), Fire, Sheriff, Corrections, and all County departments and offices providing services to residents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Multilingual pay differential compensates certified employees for providing multilingual interpretation or translation services to County residents with Limited English Proficiency. Departments are responsible for funding the differential for all hours worked, including overtime.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Montgomery County Government employees only. Program operates within Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a Montgomery County Government employee fluent in English and an approved target language
Approved languages include: American Sign Language, Amharic, Chinese, French, Korean, Spanish, Vietnamese
Basic level: must work in a front-facing position that interacts with County residents daily and provide multilingual interpretation at least weekly to residents with Limited English Proficiency

Advanced level: must provide written translation of official government documents at least weekly into the target language; translation work cannot be serviced by the Office of Community Partnership's Translations Unit
Expert level (FOP members only): must have mastery in the target language for use in interrogations, investigations, and legal proceedings
Must pass a language certification exam
Must receive approval from supervisor and director/designee before testing
IAFF members are eligible for Basic Level only
Must complete multilingual certification request through the eMultilingual system
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Employee logs in and submits a request via the online eMultilingual system. 2. Request is routed to supervisor for review and approval (FOP requests go directly to OHR). 3. Supervisor approves, denies, or returns for corrections. 4. If approved, request is routed to the department director or designee for approval. 5. OHR coordinates scheduling, testing, and rating. 6. Employee takes the language certification exam. 7. Employee and supervisor are notified of results and effective date. 8. Employees who pass receive a multilingual pay differential and are registered in the Language Certified Employees Database.

structured_extraction.program_name: Neighborhood Events Matching Funds Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Neighborhood Events Matching Funds (NEMF) program promotes community engagement, capacity building, networking, and local economic activity in Montgomery County. Neighborhood organizations, block groups, tenant associations, and civic clubs can apply for matching grants of up to $1,000 to hold community events and activities that are open to the public and have a lasting positive effect on the neighborhood. The program also supports educational community gatherings. Funds are awarded on a first-come, first-served basis, with priority given to first-time applicants. The program is managed by five Regional Service Offices: Bethesda-Chevy Chase, East County, Mid-County, Silver Spring, and UpCounty.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Matching grants of up to $1,000 per applicant per funding cycle, matched dollar for dollar (1:1) with cash or in-kind donations from the applicant. Funds are distributed on a first-come, first-served basis, with priority given to first-time applicants. Applicants must submit receipts for all expenses and a final report before receiving payment, and must be registered in the County Central Vendor System. Supports neighborhood events, educational community gatherings, and activities that promote community engagement and build community capacity. Eligible expenses include food, paper products, printing, and other event-related expenses.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Events must occur between July 1, 2025, and June 30, 2026; funds available on a first-come, first-served basis
structured_extraction.contact_name: Thomas C. Dant (Bethesda/Chevy Chase); Ayanna King (East County); Talia Beaulieu-Hains (Mid-County); Jacob Newman (Silver Spring); Jake Adler (UpCounty)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Neighborhood organizations, block groups, tenant associations, civic clubs, and eligible community residents that are active and in good standing in Montgomery County, including those served by the Bethesda-Chevy Chase, East County, Mid-County, Silver Spring, and UpCounty Regional Service Offices.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Hosting community events, educational community gatherings, and activities that are open to residents and the public and create sustainable, lasting impacts for the neighborhood, promoting community engagement and capacity building. Eligible expenses include food, paper products, printing, and other event-related expenses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. Managed by five Regional Service Offices: Bethesda-Chevy Chase, East County, Mid-County, Silver Spring, and UpCounty.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a neighborhood organization, block group, tenant association, civic club, or eligible community resident
Organization must be active and in good standing
Events must be open to everyone in the community
Events must take place between July 1, 2025, and June 30, 2026
Events must comply with Montgomery County law
Applicant must provide matching funds (cash or in-kind donations) at a 1:1 ratio
Applicant must submit receipts for all expenses before receiving grant funds
Applicant must submit a final report before payment is sent
Applicant group must be registered in the County Central Vendor System
Application must be submitted to the correct Regional Service Office
Events must create sustainable and lasting impacts for the neighborhood
Approved applicants must agree to grant conditions prior to payment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Submit an online application or request a PDF from your Regional Service Office. 2. Your local Regional Service Office reviews your application to check eligibility. 3. You receive a decision; if approved, you get a notice with the grant amount (up to $1,000). 4. Agree to program rules, provide receipts for all spending, and submit a final report. 5. Register in the County Central Vendor System to receive payment. Processing takes 1–2 weeks.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides mentoring, business training (marketing, accounting, business planning), and access to sustainable farming resources for new farmers in Montgomery County. Instead of placing farmers on shared incubator space, the program matches them directly with private landowners in the Agricultural Reserve for long-term leases, so they can focus on growing their business from day one. Currently not fully active due to budgetary and staffing reductions affecting mentorship and land matching components.

Also includes equipment training as weather permits and business consulting services. Note: as of 2017, the land matching and mentorship components are not fully active due to budget and staffing reductions, but other program areas remain available.

structured_extraction.program_name: New Jobs Tax Credit & Enhanced New Jobs Tax Credit (Montgomery County)
structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit program under §9-230 of the Tax-Property Article of the Annotated Code of Maryland and Chapter 52, Article X of the Montgomery County Code that benefits businesses planning to increase both their space and their staff in Montgomery County. The standard New Jobs Tax Credit is a six-year credit against local real and personal property taxes; the Enhanced New Jobs Tax Credit runs for 24 years for very large expansion projects. Recipients also qualify for an additional State tax credit against income, franchise, or insurance premiums taxes. Both credits include a recapture provision if job and space requirements are not maintained for three years.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The New Jobs Tax Credit is a six-year credit against local real and personal property taxes. The credit rate decreases over time: 52% in years 1–2, 39% in years 3–4, and 26% in years 5–6, applied to the increase in property tax assessments resulting from expansion. An additional State tax credit of 28%/21%/14% is available over the same six years against corporate or personal income taxes, the financial institutions franchise tax, or the insurance premiums tax. The Enhanced New Jobs Tax Credit is a 24-year credit at a flat rate of 58.5% of additional local tax liability, plus a State credit of 31.5% for each of the 24 years. Both credits include a recapture provision if job and space requirements are not maintained for three years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses already located in Montgomery County or relocating from outside Maryland that plan to expand their space and increase their workforce, including businesses establishing or expanding operations in Montgomery County. Retailers and businesses relocating from another Maryland county or Baltimore City are not eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Offsets local real and personal property tax liability resulting from business expansion (new space and new jobs), and provides a tax credit against state income taxes, financial institution franchise taxes, or insurance premium taxes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to businesses located or expanding in Montgomery County, MD. New or expanded premises must be consistent with applicable land use master plans. Businesses may be existing county residents or relocating from outside Maryland. Not available to businesses relocating from another Maryland county or Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Must increase commercial space by at least 5,000 sq ft (New Jobs) or 250,000–700,000 sq ft (Enhanced)
Must create at least 25 new permanent full-time employees within 24 months (New Jobs)
Enhanced Credit requires 500–1,250 new full-time positions depending on the qualifying pathway

Business must notify the County of intent before expanding space and staff
Not available to retailers (new positions cannot be solely or primarily involved in retail sales of goods or services)
Not available to businesses relocating from another Maryland county or from Baltimore City
Enhanced Credit limited to businesses in qualified industries
New jobs must last at least 24 months
Enhanced credit requires business to operate in specific qualifying industries
New or expanded premises must not have been previously occupied
Business must pay state/county income, franchise, or insurance premium taxes
Cannot have received other tax credit or exemption for same premises in same taxable year
Must submit payroll records, employee time sheets, and supporting documentation for current year and three years following last credit grant
Submit quarterly Maryland withholding tax or unemployment insurance tax filing
Provide copy of current lease or documentation detailing occupied space
State number of permanent full-time employees (current and planned)
Specify square footage (current and planned)
Include expansion timeline (target month/year)
For Enhanced credit with job retention provision: state number of jobs to retain
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Businesses must notify the Montgomery County Department of Finance of their intent to seek the credit before expanding space and staff by submitting a notification letter to the Director of Finance with business details and expansion plans, including quarterly tax filings and lease documentation when available. After meeting job and space requirements, the business submits a completed application form with required documentation to begin receiving the credit. Application forms are available on the County website.

structured_extraction.program_name: Nonprofit Properties Water Quality Protection Charge (WQPC) Credit Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County nonprofit (IRS 501(c)(3)) property owners can reduce their annual Water Quality Protection Charge (WQPC) — a stormwater fee based on impervious surface area on their property — by installing and maintaining qualifying stormwater management practices such as rain gardens, green roofs, permeable pavement, or rain barrels. Credits are calculated based on the volume of stormwater treated by eligible practices relative to the required water quality volume (WQv) or environmental site design volume (ESDv). Credits are also available for properties that qualify for a hardship reduction if the charge exceeds 0.2% of the property's total revenues.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Nonprofit 501(c)(3) property owners can receive a credit (reduction) off their annual WQPC of up to 60% based on the volume of stormwater treated by a combination of environmental site design and stormwater management systems, or up to 80% if the property is completely treated by environmental site design (ESD) practices. For pre-ESD era practices (permitted 1935–2003), maximum credit is 45% for treatment up to 1-inch depth. Credits up to 100% are available when treating offsite areas, provided a minimum 60% onsite credit is first achieved. Credits are valid for 3 years and must be renewed. A separate hardship partial exemption is available for 501(c)(3) organizations exempt from property taxes if the WQPC exceeds 0.2% of the property's total revenues from the subject property.
structured_extraction.program_audience: IRS-designated 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations that own property in Montgomery County, Maryland and are subject to the Water Quality Protection Charge.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of the annual Water Quality Protection Charge (stormwater fee) through credits for qualifying on-site stormwater management practices (including green roofs, conservation landscaping, bioretention, rain gardens, permeable pavements, rainwater harvesting, and sheet flow to conservation areas), or a partial exemption for organizations facing financial hardship.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to nonprofit property owners in Montgomery County, Maryland. Properties must have impervious area on private property parcels within Montgomery County.
requirements_list: Property must be owned by an IRS-designated 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization.

For the Stormwater Management Credit: property must have a qualifying stormwater management practice registered with Montgomery County DEP (e.g., rain garden, green roof, permeable pavement, rain barrel/cistern, stormwater pond, conservation landscaping, dry well, grass swale, bioretention, submerged gravel wetland).
Stormwater management practices must be maintained in accordance with DEP maintenance requirements and Montgomery County Code Section 19-28.
Must submit evidence that practices are installed properly and not removed or altered (typically photographic evidence).

Credit application must include Account ID, owner name, property address, mailing address, telephone number, email, and relevant design data (impervious area, year of installation, facility size, impervious area treated).
Stormwater practices must meet Maryland Department of Environment (MDE) Stormwater Design Manual requirements.
Site-specific impervious/pervious data and hydrologic soil group data required; documentation of facility type, drainage area, and treatment volumes required.
For offsite treatment: minimum 60% onsite credit must be achieved first; provide total offsite impervious and drainage areas.
Credits must be renewed every 3 years.

For the Hardship Reduction: organization must be a 501(c)(3) exempt from real property taxes under State law; the WQPC must exceed 0.2% of the organization's total revenues from the subject property; must submit most recent federal tax return or other revenue verification.
Applications, submissions, and appeal requests are due September 30.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Use the online WQPC forms portal (requires login) to apply for a credit, submit an appeal, or request to combine adjoining property accounts. Applications and requests are due September 30. For stormwater credit applications, provide required property and design information including facility type, drainage area, and design documentation; if design data is unavailable, a calculator auto-generates required WQv and ESDv based on permit approval era. DEP may conduct a site visit. For offsite treatment credits, provide total offsite impervious and drainage areas; the calculator back-calculates incremental offsite treatment volume. For appeals, submit a written request with a detailed basis statement and supporting documents to the Director of DEP. The Director will respond in writing within 60 days.

structured_extraction.program_name: North Bethesda Transportation Center (North Bethesda TMD)
structured_extraction.program_description: The North Bethesda Transportation Center (NBTC), operated by the Transportation Action Partnership, provides free commuter services to employers, employees, residents, and visitors in the North Bethesda area including Grosvenor, White Flint, Twinbrook, Executive Boulevard, and Rock Spring Park. NBTC helps employers create Transportation Demand Management (TDM) Plans, runs commuter information fairs, conducts biennial commuter surveys, offers green business certification, and recognizes employers who support alternative commuting. The program also provides guidance on transportation benefits, transit options, carpooling, biking, and alternative work arrangements. Residential building owners with 100+ dwelling units and new development projects are also required to submit TDM Plans to achieve Non-Auto Driver Mode Share (NADMS) goals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free services including commuter information fairs, biennial commuter surveys, green business certification, employer recognition, and help designing and carrying out a Transportation Benefits Program for the worksite. Specific services include: Transportation Benefits Plan design, transit subsidies and tax credit information, public transportation information and routing, carpool/vanpool formation assistance, parking information for carpools/vanpools, biking/walking amenities assistance, Guaranteed Ride Home program, teleworking and alternative work schedule design, car sharing program information, accessible transportation information, HOV lane guidance, customized seminars and presentations, and commuter information materials. Employers with 25 or more employees in the TMD are required by county law to submit a TDM Plan within 90 days of receiving written notice from the Director (extendable for good cause). Building owners of residential complexes with 100+ dwelling units and new development projects must also submit TDM Plans. An annual transportation demand management fee applies to fund district administration and TDM strategy coordination.
