structured_extraction.program_name: PILOT Program (Payment in Lieu of Taxes for Affordable Housing)
structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County negotiates agreements with rental property owners to reduce or eliminate County real property and special area taxes in exchange for commitments to provide affordable housing to low-income residents. The County negotiates an exemption from County real property taxes and accepts a payment in lieu of those taxes from the property owner, as authorized under Montgomery County Code Section 52-18M and Maryland state law (Section 7-503 of the Tax-Property Article of the Maryland Annotated Code). The Director of Finance is authorized to approve PILOT arrangements for qualifying affordable housing. Standard PILOTs are reviewed case-by-case; by-right PILOTs are available automatically in certain circumstances, including projects owned or controlled by the Housing Opportunities Commission of Montgomery County or non-profit-owned projects meeting AMI restrictions. A 100 percent PILOT exemption is available for housing developments owned or controlled by the Housing Opportunities Commission (HOC) or a nonprofit housing developer where at least 50 percent of units are affordable to households earning 60 percent or less of area median income. Established under Bill 26-21. The by-right PILOT program became available on March 28, 2022. The annual maximum aggregate amount of all PILOTs previously capped by Council resolution has been repealed. A 2022 temporary regulation update revised the criteria the Director of Finance uses to authorize PILOTs under Montgomery County Code Section 52-24. The County Council sets the maximum annual funding for PILOT programs for 10-year periods for properties not owned or controlled by the Housing Opportunities Commission. The abatement amount is typically based on each affordable unit and equals the average county homeowner tax credit (adjusted annually), and the term of the PILOT is tied to the affordability period required by Montgomery County. PILOTs are not transferable under the Standard program, but may be transferable under the By-Right program if the transferee meets all State and County PILOT requirements.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: County real property and special area taxes are abated based on the PILOT agreement. Owners of qualifying affordable housing may make payments in lieu of property taxes rather than paying standard property taxes, as authorized by the Director of Finance. The Finance Department calculates the abatement annually and credits it against County property tax bills. The abatement amount is typically based on each affordable unit and equals the average county homeowner tax credit (adjusted annually). The term of the PILOT is tied to the affordability period required by Montgomery County. A monitoring fee of $40 per unit per year applies. By-right PILOTs — including a 100 percent PILOT — are available to projects owned or controlled by the Housing Opportunities Commission of Montgomery County, or to non-profit-owned projects where at least 50% of units are reserved for households earning 60% or less of Area Median Income (AMI) for at least 15 years; such by-right PILOTs abate 100% of county real property taxes for a term of at least 15 years and may be transferable if the transferee meets all State and County PILOT requirements. The County Council sets the maximum annual funding for PILOT programs for 10-year periods for properties not owned or controlled by the Housing Opportunities Commission. DHCA recommends PILOT agreements to the Director of Finance, who approves or denies based on guidelines and applicable funding limits. PILOTs are not transferable under the Standard program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Affordable housing developers, rental property owners, and managers seeking real property tax relief in exchange for maintaining affordable units in Montgomery County, including the Housing Opportunities Commission, nonprofit housing developers with at least 50% affordable units rented to households at or below 60% AMI, and for-profit developers qualifying under Maryland state law.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax abatement to support development and preservation of affordable housing by reducing or eliminating property tax burden on projects with income-restricted units, including reduction of County real property and special area tax costs for affordable rental housing developments.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland only. Projects must be located within Montgomery County.
requirements_list: Affordable housing must qualify under Maryland state law (Section 7-503 of the Tax-Property Article of the Maryland Annotated Code)
Must meet criteria established by Montgomery County Code Section 52-24 and applicable temporary regulations
Authorization must be granted by the Director of Finance
Units must be occupied by income-eligible tenants charged affordable rents as specified in the PILOT agreement
Property owners/managers must file annual financial reports and compliance certificates
Monitoring fee of $40 per unit per year must be paid by September 30 each year

By-right eligibility: project must be owned/controlled by the Housing Opportunities Commission of Montgomery County, OR owned/controlled by a non-profit with at least 50% of units reserved for households at 60% AMI or below for 15 years
Rent levels must be limited in accordance with AMI restrictions
Property must qualify as affordable housing under state law
Rental property owner must commit to providing affordable housing to low-income residents
Agreement must be negotiated and approved through DHCA and the Director of Finance
Subject to annual county funding limits
10-year funding limit applies to properties not owned or controlled by the Housing Opportunities Commission
Legal description of the property
Project financial pro forma including evidence of financial commitments for total project costs and financial need for the PILOT
Project description including total number of units and number of affordable units, with documentation of affordability (e.g. rent rolls or LIHTC Covenants)
Demonstrate site control equivalent to fee simple title, 99-year lease, or option to purchase with no contingencies except financing
Any other information or documentation reasonably required by the County to determine eligibility
Property owner must pay all State real property taxes, municipal taxes, front foot benefit charges, and other applicable fees unless waived

For by-right PILOT: property must be owned or controlled by a non-profit organization with at least 50% of units leased to households with incomes no greater than 60% of AMI for the Washington Metropolitan Statistical Area
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Standard PILOTs are underwritten and approved by the County on a case-by-case basis through the Multifamily Section. Submit required information electronically to DHCA.Multifamily@montgomerymd.gov or by mail to Department of Housing and Community Affairs, 1401 Rockville Pike, 4th Floor, Attn: PILOT Request, Rockville, MD 20852. The County analyzes the request using financial information provided by the property owner to define the level of PILOT required. A Regulatory Agreement is then signed and recorded among land records. By-right PILOTs are granted automatically when eligibility criteria are met — a Regulatory Agreement is signed by the property owner and the County and recorded among land records for the term of the PILOT. Applicants negotiate a PILOT agreement with DHCA, which then recommends the agreement to the Director of Finance for approval. The Asset Management team monitors compliance after the agreement is negotiated. Applicants may also contact Stephanie Killian, Multifamily Housing Manager, DHCA, Council Office Building, 100 Maryland Avenue, 4th Floor, Rockville, Maryland 20850.

structured_extraction.program_name: Partnership Fund for Victims of Hate/Violence
structured_extraction.program_description: A fund administered by the Committee on Hate and Violence (COHV) under Montgomery County that provides partial reimbursement to victims of hate crimes or hate violence acts in Montgomery County. It covers property damage and medical expenses resulting from physical injury caused by hate or violence acts based on race, ethnicity, religion, sexual orientation, or disability. The program aims to demonstrate community support for victims and ease the financial burden caused by hate-motivated acts.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement of up to $2,000 per hate/violence act for property damage, and up to $4,000 for medical expenses from physical injury. Total compensation cannot exceed $8,000 to any one victim within a 12-month period.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and private institutions in Montgomery County who are victims of hate crimes or hate violence acts and have suffered property damage or physical injury based on race, ethnicity, religion, sexual orientation, or disability.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reimbursement for property damage caused by hate/violence acts, and medical expenses resulting from physical injury from hate/violence acts.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The hate/violence incident must have occurred in Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a victim of a hate/violence act occurring in Montgomery County
Property was damaged by a hate/violence act based on race, ethnicity, religion, sexual orientation, or disability
Must be an individual or private institution eligible under County law
Property damage reimbursement capped at $2,000 per hate/violence act
Medical expense reimbursement capped at $4,000 per incident
Total compensation cannot exceed $8,000 to any one victim within a 12-month period
Prompt application must be made to the Montgomery County Office of Human Rights
Must have suffered property damage as a result of the hate/violence incident
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 240-777-8450 or email [email protected] for information about the fund. Victims may also contact or visit the Montgomery County Office of Human Rights to report the incident and apply for compensation, or file a complaint via the Montgomery County Hate/Bias Incident Complaint Portal. Visit the Partnership Fund for Victims of Hate/Violence web page for more details.

structured_extraction.program_name: Payment in Lieu of Taxes (PILOT) Program – WMATA PILOT
structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County's WMATA Payment in Lieu of Taxes (PILOT) program provides a 100% exemption of county real property taxes for 15 years for new high-rise residential developments built on property leased from the Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority (WMATA) at a Metro station in Montgomery County. The exemption begins in the year a use and occupancy permit is issued. The project must include at least 50% residential rental housing (high-rise, more than 8 stories), and at least 25% of required MPDUs must be affordable to households at or below 50% AMI. The program aims to accelerate housing development near transit, create affordable housing, and support new businesses and jobs around metro stations. Enacted under Bill 29-20, it is administered through the MPDU Declaration of Covenants under Chapter 25A of the County Code.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Exempts 100% of Montgomery County real property taxes for 15 years beginning in the year a use and occupancy permit is issued, for new high-rise residential construction (more than 8 stories) on WMATA-leased land at a Metro station. Project must be a 'qualifying development': at least 50% high-rise residential apartments, located on WMATA-leased land at a Metro station, and at least 25% of required MPDUs must be affordable to households at or below 50% AMI. At least 25% of construction workers must be Montgomery County residents.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Developers of new high-rise residential projects on WMATA-leased land at Metro stations in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Elimination of county real property taxes to support transit-oriented affordable rental housing development near metro stations
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located on land leased from WMATA at a Metro station in Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: At least 50% of the project must consist of high-rise residential apartment buildings (more than 8 stories above ground)
Project land must be located at a Metro station on land leased from WMATA
Must include at least 50% rental housing
At least 25% of the MPDUs required for the project must be affordable to households at or below 50% AMI
At least 25% of rental units must be moderately priced dwelling units (MPDUs) reserved for individuals earning 50% or less of area median income
Applicant and project must meet requirements of Maryland law governing PILOTs
At least 25% of workers constructing the project must be residents of Montgomery County
Must meet specific quarterly reporting requirements
Legal description of the property
Agreement to Build MPDUs describing total units and number of MPDUs at required affordability levels
Copy of the WMATA lease
Documentation concerning workers constructing the project
100% property tax exemption applies for 15 years from issuance of use and occupancy permit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit required information electronically to DHCA.Multifamily@MontgomeryCountyMD.gov or by mail to Department of Housing and Community Affairs, 1401 Rockville Pike, 4th Floor, Attn: PILOT Request, Rockville, MD 20852. The PILOT is administered under the MPDU Declaration of Covenants required under Chapter 25A of the County Code, signed by the property owner and recorded among land records.

structured_extraction.program_name: Permanent Supportive Housing (PSH) & Housing Initiative Program (HIP)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides long-term rental subsidies, application fees, security deposits, and supportive services to individuals and families exiting homelessness or in shelter placement. Participants pay 30% of their household's adjusted gross income to the landlord, and the housing provider covers the remainder. A utility allowance is also provided, along with case management and in-home visits 3-4 times per month.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants pay 30% of their household's adjusted gross income directly to the landlord; HIP pays the remaining 70% directly to the landlord. Program also covers application fees and security deposit (up to 2 months rent), provides a utility allowance, and includes monthly case management and supportive services with in-home visits 3-4 times per month.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeless or shelter-residing Montgomery County residents with disabilities, chronic mental illness, substance abuse issues, or elderly persons needing permanent supportive housing
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental assistance (70% of rent), application fees, security deposits, utility allowance, case management and supportive services
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Montgomery County resident
Homeless or residing in shelter placement
Combined household income ≤30% of area median income
Household assets ≤$10,000

Member of special population (sensory/cognitive/mobile impairment, developmental disability, chronic mental disorder, co-occurring disability, chronic substance abuse, or elderly needing supportive housing)
Referred through Coordinated Entry System (CES)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: All referrals through Montgomery County Coordinated Entry System (CES); participants assessed for Permanent Supportive Housing placement.

structured_extraction.program_description: Personify Health (formerly Virgin Pulse) is a free wellness program for eligible Montgomery County Government employees. Members can earn up to $350 per year for making healthy choices, receive a free fitness tracker, participate in step challenges, and access a personalized health and fitness portal supporting physical, mental, social, and financial well-being.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible employees can earn up to $350 per year in rewards cash ($85/quarter) through a tiered reward system (Levels 1-4) based on point accumulation. A free Max GO activity tracker is provided or existing trackers can be connected. Rewards cash can be donated, used in store, or converted to gift cards. Access is also provided to partner programs: Foodsmart, RethinkCare, and Wellbeats, along with a personalized health and fitness portal and countywide step challenges.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Insurance-eligible Montgomery County Government and participating agency employees
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Health and wellness activities, fitness tracking, and healthy lifestyle choices. Rewards cash can be donated, used in store, or converted to gift cards.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Montgomery County Government and participating agency employees
requirements_list: Must be insurance-eligible as a Montgomery County Government or participating agency employee
Not required to be enrolled in a health plan, only eligible to enroll
Activate account at join.personifyhealth.com/livewell
Download the Personify Health app
Connect activity tracker or receive FREE Max GO device
Upload profile picture and add friends
Complete Health Check survey and at least 2 preventative screenings to reach Level 1
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: New employees receive a registration email from Personify Health within 3-4 weeks of hire date. Current employees enrolling for the first time should email LiveWell@montgomerycountymd.gov to request registration details. Once registered, activate account at join.personifyhealth.com/livewell, download the Personify Health app, and earn points through daily activities.

structured_extraction.program_name: Planning Your Path to Retirement Seminar
structured_extraction.program_description: A retirement planning seminar for Montgomery County employees who are eligible to retire or within five years of normal retirement. The seminar covers county retirement benefits, Social Security and Medicare, deferred compensation, financial planning, and estate planning.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Retirement planning seminar providing guidance, tools, and information to help employees prepare for retirement. Topics include county retirement benefits (ERS, RSP, GRIP plans), Social Security and Medicare, deferred compensation (County 457 plan), financial planning, and estate planning. Video recordings of each topic are available online.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County government employees who are eligible to retire or within five years of normal retirement age as defined by their retirement plan.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable — this is an informational/training seminar, not a funding program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Montgomery County government employees.
requirements_list: Must be a Montgomery County employee
Must be eligible to retire or within five years of normal retirement as defined by the employee's retirement plan
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible employees may attend the seminar. Video recordings of each topic are available online.

structured_extraction.program_description: A collaborative program between Pre-Release Services and Drug Court that places individuals who are coming out of jail, or in lieu of going to jail, at the Pre-Release Center to gain stability. Participants receive addiction treatment, case management, and reentry support while maintaining Drug Court responsibilities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants live at the Pre-Release Center and receive substance abuse therapy through Outpatient Addiction Services, three Twelve-Step meetings per week, weekly appearances before a Drug Court judge, weekly case management meetings, reentry planning, and support securing employment and sober housing.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals referred by Drug Court who are transitioning out of jail or as an alternative to incarceration, requiring substance abuse treatment and reentry support.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Residential stabilization, outpatient addiction therapy, case management, reentry planning, employment support, and sober housing search.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Located at 11651 Nebel Street, Rockville, Maryland 20852; serves Montgomery County Drug Court participants.
requirements_list: Must be a Drug Court client placed at the Pre-Release Center by Drug Court
Must attend Outpatient Addiction Services therapy groups
Must attend three Twelve-Step meetings per week
Must appear before a Drug Court judge weekly
Must meet weekly with a case manager at the Pre-Release Center
Must maintain full-time employment
Must seek sober housing
Must follow all rules and responsibilities of the reentry plan and contract at the Center
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Placement is arranged through Drug Court in collaboration with Pre-Release Services. Clients are referred directly by Drug Court rather than applying independently.

structured_extraction.program_description: PRRS evaluates and places eligible offenders into pre-release and home confinement programs designed to support community reintegration. The program offers a residential facility (Pre-Release Center) providing work-release opportunities, education, counseling, community involvement, and home visitation, as well as a Home Confinement program that extends services under electronic monitoring to participants living in the community. Both programs are voluntary and help participants build stable community support through employment, counseling, 12-step programs, family activities, and community services while under structured supervision.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants are placed in either the Pre-Release Center (residential work-release) or Home Confinement (non-residential electronic monitoring). Both programs provide work opportunities, education programs, counseling, community involvement, home visitation, mental health services, substance abuse treatment, employment assistance, housing referrals, health insurance navigation, public benefits assistance, and transportation guidance. Home Confinement allows offenders to live at home under program supervision while building employment, counseling, and community support systems. Electronic monitoring ensures community accountability. Weekend turnaround transfers are available to facilitate employment continuity. Virginia and Washington DC addresses are prohibited for home confinement; Maryland addresses within approximately 50 miles of PRRS staff are required.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Sentenced offenders within 12 months of release, including local incarcerates, federal offenders returning to the Washington metropolitan area, and state inmates returning to Montgomery County; incarcerated individuals preparing for release and reentrants.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supports community reintegration through work-release, education, employment, counseling, 12-step programs, family activities, community services, mental health treatment, substance abuse treatment, housing referrals, health insurance navigation, public benefits assistance, and transportation guidance while under supervision.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to offenders returning to Montgomery County, Maryland. Maryland addresses within approximately 50 miles of PRRS staff are required for home confinement; Virginia and Washington DC addresses are prohibited for home confinement.
requirements_list: Must be fully sentenced with no serious pending charges or detainers
Must be within 12 months of an established release date
Must have no prior escapes
If not a U.S. citizen, must possess a valid green card, employment authorization, or permanent residency status
Must be medically cleared for work-release and psychologically capable of functioning in a community correctional setting
Participation is voluntary — offenders must volunteer for the program
Final approval required from the Chief of Pre-Release and Reentry Services and the sentencing judge
Must complete application (Self Report Personal History form)
Must complete assessment process with PRRS staff
Must be willing to share personal/criminal history information
Must authorize information sharing with potential employers, community resources, and program sponsors
Must have stable housing and employment/education plans (for home confinement)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested offenders must volunteer for the program. Applicants complete the Self Report Personal History form covering general information, legal information, education, military service, employment/vocational history, finances, family background, relationships and children, medical history, sexual orientation, and alcohol/drug use history. Eligibility is evaluated using established criteria by the screening section. Assessment is conducted with PRRS staff and authorization for information sharing is obtained. Final approval lies with the Chief of PRRS and the sentencing judge. Applicants can also review the Assessment and Screening Eligibility document.

structured_extraction.program_name: Pre-Release and Reentry Services (PRRS) Case Management and Re-entry Planning
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides individualized case management to people nearing release from incarceration. A case manager works with each resident to assess reentry risks and needs, create a reentry plan with goals and strategies, monitor progress, and make referrals to community resources including housing, counseling, mental health services, substance abuse treatment, and social services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Case managers assess each resident's reentry needs and develop a personalized reentry plan. They refer residents to community agencies for housing, counseling (substance abuse, anger management, domestic violence, mental health), and social services. Residents also receive help finding transportation to religious services and connecting with support groups. Ten percent of a resident's take-home pay is set aside in a savings account for housing costs upon release.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents of the Pre-Release and Reentry Services program who are preparing for release from incarceration in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Case management, reentry planning, referrals to housing, mental health, counseling, substance abuse treatment, and social services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland residents in the Pre-Release and Reentry Services program at 11651 Nebel Street, Rockville, MD 20852.
requirements_list: Must be a resident of the Pre-Release and Reentry Services (PRRS) program
Must participate in reentry risk and needs assessment
Must develop and follow a program contract and reentry plan
Must save 10% of take-home pay in a savings account for housing
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Residents are assessed upon entry to the PRRS program. Case managers use assessment results to develop a program contract and reentry plan with the resident. Progress is monitored through a structured level system.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Montgomery County Department of Police offers rebates to property owners and tenants — including residents, businesses, and nonprofits — who install qualifying exterior security cameras in Montgomery County. The program aims to deter and solve crime by encouraging more security camera installations throughout the county, enabling voluntary co-production of public safety between community members and police. Eligible locations are designated priority areas determined by current crime data and public safety indicators, evaluated annually by the Police Chief.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rebates of up to $250 per qualifying security camera, covering only the cost of the camera itself (not to exceed actual purchase cost). Residents may receive a rebate for up to 1 camera per qualifying residence (max $250). Businesses and nonprofits may receive rebates for up to 5 cameras per location (max $1,250), with a separate application required for each camera. Rebates are paid by the Montgomery County Department of Finance, subject to availability of funds/appropriation.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Lt. Dan Helton, Management Services Bureau
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners or tenants of residences, businesses, or nonprofit organizations located in designated priority areas within Montgomery County, MD, as determined by the Police Chief based on public safety indicators and crime levels.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and installation of qualifying exterior security cameras (purchased on or after November 15, 2023). Cameras must be outdoor/weatherproof, have functioning digital video recording capability, meet minimum technical and video specifications, and retain footage for at least 7 days.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties located within Montgomery County, MD, specifically within Priority Areas designated by the Police Chief based on public safety indicators and crime levels. Priority areas are evaluated annually. Applicants can determine eligibility through the Department's online camera application website.
requirements_list: Applicant must be an owner or tenant of a property used as a residence, business, or nonprofit organization in Montgomery County, MD
Property must be located within a Priority Area designated by the Police Chief based on public safety indicators and crime levels
Security camera must be purchased and installed on or after November 15, 2023
Camera must meet minimum technical and video specifications published by the Police Department
Camera must be installed on the exterior of a building and be weatherproof
Camera must retain video footage for at least 7 days
Camera must have functioning digital video recording capability
Applicant must register the camera with the Montgomery County Police Department (MCPD)
Proof of purchase (receipt/invoice) must be submitted
Make, model, and serial number of the camera must be provided

Verification of installation is required (either by a licensed security installation business with photographic evidence, or by an on-site visit from a police officer if installed by the owner or another unlicensed person)
Tenants must comply with applicable building and lease requirements
Written agreement that camera will not record private property not owned or leased by applicant
Businesses and nonprofits must post notice alerting visitors of the existence of security cameras
Compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local laws and regulations including electrical code
Compliance with regulations regarding image collection, dissemination, use, and disposal
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an online application form available on the Police Department's website. Include proof of purchase, camera make/model/serial number, and verification of installation. Applications are submitted according to the form and manner prescribed by the Police Chief. Upon approval and confirmation that all requirements are met, the rebate is paid by the Montgomery County Department of Finance, subject to availability of funds. If denied, applicants must submit a new application. For additional details, contact the Management Services Bureau, Montgomery County Department of Police.

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County's Productivity Housing program allows affordable rental and for-sale housing to be built in commercial and industrial zones where residential use is not normally permitted. Housing units are priced to be affordable to households earning at or below 75% of the County median income, adjusted for family size.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Developers may receive approval through a Special Exception from the Board of Appeals to build residential units in commercial and industrial zones (C-1, C-2, C-3, C-4, O-M, I-1, I-3, I-4). Base density is 6 units per acre, increasing to 21.5 units per acre if at least 35% of units are affordable. No more than 25% of land in each master plan area zoned commercial or industrial can be used for multifamily housing. For-sale Productivity Housing Units (PHUs) are price-controlled for 10 years; rental PHUs for 20 years. Maximum rents may not exceed 30% of gross household income at 75% of area median income, adjusted for family size.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Developers seeking to build affordable housing in commercial and industrial zones in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction of affordable rental and for-sale multifamily or single-family housing in eligible commercial and industrial zones
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Montgomery County, Maryland, in commercial and industrial zones as defined by the County zoning ordinance
requirements_list: Developer must apply for and receive a Special Exception from the Montgomery County Board of Appeals
Developer must execute a written Productivity Housing agreement with the DHCA Director before a building permit is issued
Agreement must be recorded in County Land Records
At least 35% of units must be affordable to households at or below County median income to qualify for increased density (up to 21.5 units per acre)
PHUs must include at least two bedrooms in single-family units
Rental PHU rates set at 75% of area median income adjusted for family size; rents must not exceed 30% of gross household income
Maximum sales price for PHUs must not exceed 175% of the comparable Moderately Priced Dwelling Unit (MPDU) sale price
For-sale PHUs must be owner-occupied as primary residence during 10-year control period
Rental PHUs subject to 20-year control period; no subletting unless approved by Department
Owner selling PHU on open market after control period must pay one-half of excess profit into the County's Housing Initiative Fund
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Apply for a Special Exception with the Montgomery County Board of Appeals per zoning ordinance Section G-2.36.2. 2. Execute a written Productivity Housing agreement with the DHCA Director before obtaining a building permit. 3. Record the agreement in County Land Records and provide a copy to the County. 4. Submit a copy of the executed agreement to the Department of Permitting Services with the first building permit application.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides education and workforce training to young adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities through internships at Montgomery County government worksites. Interns rotate through three 10-week intensive worksite placements supported by job coaches, combined with daily classroom instruction.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Unpaid internship program running September to June. Interns work approximately 25 hours per week across three 10-week worksite rotations and receive one hour of daily classroom instruction. Program hours are 8:30 am to 2:30 pm.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Young adults ages 18-30 with intellectual and/or developmental disabilities who are eligible for DDA (Developmental Disabilities Administration) funding or can pay privately.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Career development, job skills training, and worksite internship experience.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Between the ages of 18 and 30
Have an intellectual and/or developmental disability
Eligible for DDA funding or able to use private pay
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete SEEC's Project SEARCH Montgomery Application form. Follow the instructions in the application to mail or email the completed application for review. Contact PSRecruitment@seeconline.org for alternate application formats.

structured_extraction.program_name: Property Tax Credit for Disabled Veterans
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides a partial credit against Montgomery County property tax for qualified disabled veterans or their surviving spouses. The credit amount depends on the veteran's service-connected disability rating: veterans with a rating of 75% or more receive a credit equal to 50% of the County property tax, while veterans with a rating between 50% and 74% receive a credit equal to 25% of the County property tax. The credit also continues for qualified surviving spouses of eligible disabled veterans. Veterans who already qualify for a property tax exemption under Section 7-208 of the Maryland Tax Property Article are not eligible. The veteran must have an honorable discharge and a federal adjusted gross income not exceeding $100,000.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Veterans with a service-connected disability rating of 75% or more receive a credit equal to 50% of the County property tax. Veterans with a rating between 50% and 74% receive a credit equal to 25% of the County property tax. Qualified surviving spouses are also eligible. Veterans who already qualify for a property tax exemption under Section 7-208 of the Maryland Tax Property Article are not eligible. Credit applies to the veteran's principal residence (dwelling house occupied by no more than two families).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: On or before April 1 before the tax year for which credit is sought
structured_extraction.program_audience: Disabled veterans with honorable discharge and a permanent service-connected disability rating of at least 50% (or 100% non-permanent service-connected disability), and their qualifying surviving spouses, who own a principal residence in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of Montgomery County property tax liability — tax credit applied against property tax owed on the veteran's principal residence.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Principal residence (dwelling house) must be located in Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be honorably discharged or released under honorable circumstances from active military, naval, or air service.
Must have a permanent service-connected disability of at least 50%, or a 100% non-permanent service-connected disability.
Disability must have resulted from blindness or other disabling cause, and must not be caused by misconduct.
Federal adjusted gross income (prior tax year) must not exceed $100,000.
Property must be the veteran's principal residence (dwelling house).
Property must be occupied by no more than two families.
Must not already qualify for a property tax exemption under Section 7-208 of the Maryland Tax Property Article.
Must apply on or before April 1 before the tax year for which credit is sought.
Must submit DD-214 discharge document, VA disability certification with percentage rating, and prior year federal income tax return.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Disabled Veteran Tax Credit Application form and submit it by April 1 along with three required documents: DD-214 discharge certificate, VA disability certification with percentage rating, and prior year federal income tax return.

structured_extraction.program_name: Property Tax Credit for Elderly Individuals and for Military Retirees (Bill 42-16)
structured_extraction.program_description: A Montgomery County property tax credit for homeowners aged 65 and above who have either lived in and owned their home for at least 40 consecutive years (maximum assessed property value $700,000) or are retired from the U.S. armed forces or qualifying uniformed services, or are surviving spouses of deceased qualifying retirees (maximum assessed property value $550,000). The credit reduces County property taxes by 20% for 7 consecutive years on owner-occupied homes and cannot be renewed after that period. The program is designed to reduce the real estate property tax burden for long-term senior residents and retired military service members in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides a 20% credit on Montgomery County property taxes only, for owner-occupied dwellings. The credit is granted for 7 consecutive years and cannot be renewed after that period. For 40-year homeowners (owned and lived in the same dwelling for at least 40 consecutive years), the property assessment must be $700,000 or less. For retired military service members (U.S. Air Force, Army, Coast Guard, Marine Corps, Navy, NOAA uniformed services, Public Health Service uniformed corps, military reserves, or National Guard), the assessment must be $550,000 or less. Surviving spouses of eligible military retirees aged 65+ who have not remarried may also qualify. Applications approved by April 1 will appear as a credit on the July property tax bill.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County homeowners aged 65 or older who have either owned and lived in their home for 40+ consecutive years (deed dated June 30, 1986 or earlier, max assessed value $700,000), or are retired from the U.S. armed forces including military reserves, National Guard, uniformed corps of the Public Health Service, or uniformed corps of NOAA (max assessed value $550,000), or are surviving spouses of deceased qualifying retirees aged 65+ who have not remarried.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of Montgomery County real estate property taxes on owner-occupied dwellings.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only in Montgomery County, Maryland. Property must be the applicant's owner-occupied dwelling.
requirements_list: Applicant must be 65 years of age or older (born on or before June 30, 1961 to receive credit beginning July 1, 2025)
Applicant must be listed on the deed for the property
Property must be owner-occupied primary residence

Must meet one of two criteria: (1) 40-Year Homeowner — owned and lived in the dwelling for at least 40 consecutive years (deed dated June 30, 1986 or earlier), with property assessment of $700,000 or less; OR (2) Retired Military — retired from U.S. Air Force, Army, Coast Guard, Marine Corps, Navy, NOAA uniformed services, Public Health Service uniformed corps, military reserves, or National Guard, with property assessment of $550,000 or less
Proof of age required (driver's license or certificate of live birth)
40-year homeowners must provide original deed; military retirees must provide retired military ID (e.g., DD-214)
Veteran status alone does not qualify — applicant must have retired status

Properties titled in a trust must include a completed Affidavit Re Trust Ownership; applicant must be settler, grantor, or beneficiary of the trust and must not pay rent or other remuneration to reside in the property

Surviving spouses of military retirees must provide: death certificate, DD-214 or retired military ID, signed affidavit of non-remarriage, and proof of age (driver's license or certificate of live birth); the retiree must have been at least 65 and retired at time of death; surviving spouse must not have remarried after marriage to deceased military retiree
Application must be received on or before April 1 of each year
The 20% credit is granted for 7 consecutive years and cannot be renewed

structured_extraction.program_name: Property Tax Credit for Public Safety Officers and Emergency Communications Specialists
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides a property tax credit on the county property tax bill for eligible public safety officers, including full-time sworn police officers, firefighters, emergency medical technicians, public safety emergency communications specialists, deputy sheriffs, correctional officers, and active fire and rescue volunteers, who own and live in their principal residence in Montgomery County. The program aims to increase the number of these employees who reside in the County and to help recruit and retain them. The credit was expanded in 2025 (Bill 15-24) to include officers employed by certain regional commissions (M-NCPPC, WSSC, WSTC) and county municipalities (Gaithersburg, Rockville, Takoma Park, Chevy Chase Village), as well as full-time county employees assigned to the DHHS Crisis Center providing emergency response services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The credit equals the lesser of $2,500 or the total county property tax due on the applicant's principal residence, applied annually to the county property tax bill. Eligible recipients include active public safety officers, public safety communications specialists, deputy sheriffs, correctional officers, active fire and rescue volunteers, and qualifying full-time officers/employees as defined by Bill 15-24, all of whom must own and live in a principal residence in Montgomery County.

structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicant must be the legal owner of a principal residence in Montgomery County, Maryland.

Must be the legal owner of a principal residence in Montgomery County

structured_extraction.program_name: Property Tax Credit – Fire Sprinkler Systems
structured_extraction.program_description: A Montgomery County real property tax credit for property owners who voluntarily install an approved complete automatic fire sprinkler system for fire protection in a detached single-family home, attached dwelling unit, multi-family building, or commercial building where installation was not legally required. For residential properties, the credit equals the lesser of: (1) the total cost of installing the sprinkler system, or (2) 50% of the General County real property tax attributable to the dwelling. The system must have been installed on or after July 1, 2000. The credit is meant to encourage homeowners, residential property owners, and commercial building owners to add fire sprinklers to improve life safety.

System must have been installed on or after July 1, 2000 for residential properties. For residential properties, application must be submitted in the year of installation to receive the credit in that tax year or the following tax year.

structured_extraction.program_name: Property Tax Credit – Renewable Energy (Energy Conservation Devices) (Residential)
structured_extraction.program_description: A Montgomery County real property tax credit for owners of owner-occupied residential properties who install qualifying energy conservation devices or renewable energy systems that reduce demand for conventional fuels or increase their efficiency. Credits of up to $250 per property per fiscal year are available, subject to a countywide annual cap of $100,000. Applications are processed in the order received, and applications received after the cap is reached roll over to the next fiscal year.

Total annual county funding for this credit is capped at $100,000. Credits are granted in the order applications are received; applications received after the cap is reached roll over to the next fiscal year.

structured_extraction.program_name: Property Tax Deferral Program – Residential Real Property (Expedited Bill 10-05)
structured_extraction.program_description: Allows eligible Montgomery County homeowners to defer payment of a portion of their county property taxes on their primary residence. The program modifies the amount of residential real property taxes that may be deferred, revises income limits (household gross income must not exceed $120,000 for the preceding calendar year), and sets interest rates that apply to deferred taxes. Deferral applies to the amount by which current county property taxes exceed the prior year's county taxes (provided the increase is not due to substantial property improvements), covering General County tax and Special Service Area taxes. Interest accrues at a rate set annually by the county, not to exceed the prime lending rate. Total accumulated deferred taxes and interest cannot exceed 50% of the full cash value of the property. Deferred taxes and interest become a first lien on the property. The owner must have resided in the dwelling as their principal residence for at least 5 years.

Applies to General County tax and Special Service Area taxes. Interest accrues at a rate set annually by the county, not exceeding the prime lending rate. Deferred taxes and interest become a first lien on the property. Total accumulated deferred taxes and interest cannot exceed 50% of the full cash value of the property. Eligible homeowners must have household gross income at or below $120,000 for the preceding calendar year and must have resided in the dwelling as their principal residence for at least 5 years.

structured_extraction.program_description: The PATC program deploys trauma care kits in public spaces (schools and government buildings) and provides training to help bystanders address life-threatening injuries before emergency medical professionals arrive. Kits include supplies for severe bleeding control, penetrating trauma, and hypothermia. Training is available in person, via video, and through a mobile app.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides trauma care kits placed in county government buildings, public schools, and Montgomery College facilities, along with free in-person training sessions (subject to availability), instructional videos, and a mobile app. Montgomery County Government departments can request a kit evaluation for their facility or a replacement kit if an existing kit is missing, damaged, or has been used.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County and Prince George's County residents, Montgomery County Government employees, Montgomery County Public Schools staff, and Montgomery College community members who want to learn trauma care skills or request kit deployment at their facility.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Trauma care kit deployment in eligible facilities; in-person training for residents and county employees on how to use kit supplies to treat severe injuries before emergency responders arrive.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Montgomery County and Prince George's County, Maryland. Kit deployment is currently limited to Montgomery County Government facilities, Montgomery County Public Schools, and Montgomery College.

Training requests are subject to resource availability.
Kit replacement requests apply only when an existing kit is missing, damaged, or has been used, or a facility does not yet have a kit and wants a site evaluation.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To request in-person PATC training, submit a request via the online form at the OEMHS website. To request a PATC kit evaluation or replacement, Montgomery County Government departments can submit a request through the OEMHS online form. structured_extraction.program_description: A conditional grant program under the Economic Development Fund that helps local for-profit small businesses and non-profit organizations in Montgomery County continue operating when they have been significantly harmed by the spread of a communicable disease that led to a Federal, State, or County Public Health Emergency order restricting business operations in the County. Grants or conditional grants are awarded based on criteria established by Temporary Executive Regulation 9-20T (MCER No. 9-20T) under the Economic Development Fund, administered by the Montgomery County Department of Finance. The program was established as a sub-program of the Economic Development Fund to support businesses and organizations during a public health emergency.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants or conditional grants provided through the Montgomery County Economic Development Fund to help eligible businesses and non-profits continue operating during a public health emergency. Initial disbursement of up to $10,000 for businesses demonstrating significant financial loss (50% or greater adjusted revenue loss); up to $75,000 maximum for documented revenue losses with multiple disbursements available subject to fund availability. Additionally, up to $2,500 for purchasing technology equipment and software to facilitate employee teleworking. Restaurants and retail storefront establishments are prioritized with one-quarter of funds reserved for these industries. Funds cannot reimburse losses already covered by federal/state assistance or insurance, nor wages for periods covered by unemployment insurance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local for-profit businesses with 100 or fewer full-time equivalent employees and non-profit organizations with 100 or fewer full-time equivalent employees located in Montgomery County that have experienced significant adverse impact due to a communicable disease-related public health emergency.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Offset actual lost revenue caused by a public health emergency; purchase technology equipment and software for employee teleworking. Cannot reimburse losses already covered by federal/state assistance or insurance, nor wages for periods covered by unemployment insurance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Business must have its principal place of business in Montgomery County, Maryland. For multi-location businesses, either all physical locations must be in the County, or County-based location(s) must account for over 50% of total employees or gross sales.

Must be located in Montgomery County with principal place of business in the County
Must employ 100 or fewer full-time or full-time equivalent employees
Must have been in existence prior to March 5, 2020
Must demonstrate Significant Financial Loss (50% or greater adjusted revenue loss) for a financial period attributable to the Public Health Emergency
Must be in Good Standing with the State of Maryland at time of application

Students propagate native plants during the second semester for use in watershed restoration projects. A portion of the plants grown are returned to the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) and Pope Farm for stormwater management and county projects, and schools can use the remaining plants for a native plant sale or other environmental project.

In return, at least 33% of the plants produced must be returned to RainScapes by mid-spring, and schools must complete a one-page assessment survey. Schools keep the remaining plants for community projects or native plant sales.

structured_extraction.program_description: RainScapes Rewards is a rebate program administered by Montgomery County that encourages property owners to install stormwater management practices on their property, including rain barrels, rain gardens, conservation landscapes, permeable pavement, pavement removal, green roofs, water harvesting systems, and cisterns. The program is part of Clean Water Montgomery and aims to reduce stormwater runoff, keep pollution out of storm drains and local streams, and improve local water quality. Rebates are funded by the Water Quality Protection Charge (WQPC) and are issued after installation and a passing final inspection. Applications are accepted on a first come, first served basis. The program serves residential, commercial, HOA, multifamily, and institutional property owners including community pools, homeowner associations, private schools, congregations, and other institutional properties. Rebate amounts vary by project type and size: rain barrels are rebated at $1 per gallon of capacity (up to $250 for residential or commercial/institutional properties, minimum project size 200 gallons or 100 gallons for townhomes); cisterns are rebated at $1 per gallon of capacity (up to $500 for residential and $2,000 for commercial/institutional, minimum 250 gallons, exceptions considered case by case); if both rain barrels and cisterns are installed on the same property, the total maximum rebate is $750; permeable pavement retrofit is rebated at $14 per square foot; other approved stormwater practices may receive up to $7,500 per parcel for residential properties and up to $20,000 per parcel for commercial, HOA, multifamily, or institutional properties. Property owners pay all upfront costs and are reimbursed based on itemized receipts, excluding sales tax. Rebates are typically issued within 8–12 weeks after final inspection. Properties in the municipalities of Rockville, Gaithersburg, and Takoma Park are not eligible, as those cities run their own programs.
eligible_municipalities: Unincorporated Montgomery County (excluding Rockville, Gaithersburg, and Takoma Park)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Cost-share rebate for on-site stormwater management retrofits. Applications are accepted on a first come, first served basis. Property owners pay all upfront costs and receive a rebate after installation and a passing final inspection. Rebate amounts vary by project type: rain barrels are rebated at $1 per gallon of capacity (maximum $250 for residential; $250 for commercial/institutional; minimum project size 200 gallons, or 100 gallons for townhomes; minimum individual barrel size 50 gallons); cisterns are rebated at $1 per gallon of capacity (maximum $500 for residential; $2,000 for commercial/institutional; minimum size 250 gallons; exceptions to the maximum may be considered case by case); if both rain barrels and cisterns are installed on the same property, the total maximum rebate is $750; permeable pavement retrofit is rebated at $14 per square foot; other approved stormwater practices may receive up to $7,500 per parcel for residential and up to $20,000 per parcel (lifetime maximum per parcel based on tax ID number) for commercial, HOA, multifamily, or institutional properties (including community pools, congregations, and private schools). The final rebate amount is based on total acceptable receipts up to the approved amount. Rebate calculations are based on itemized paid receipts with sales tax excluded. Rebates are typically issued within 8–12 weeks after final inspection. Properties in Rockville, Gaithersburg, and Takoma Park are not eligible.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential, commercial, HOA, multifamily, and institutional property owners, communities, schools, congregations, community pools, and individual residents in Montgomery County (outside the municipalities of Rockville, Gaithersburg, and Takoma Park) interested in installing stormwater management practices such as rain barrels, rain gardens, conservation landscapes, permeable pavement, pavement removal, green roofs, water harvesting systems, or cisterns on their property. Also includes property managers and board members of qualifying community properties such as HOAs, private schools, and congregations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rebate covers costs of approved stormwater management installations including rain barrels, rain gardens, conservation landscapes, permeable pavement, pavement removal, green roofs, water harvesting systems, and cisterns. Eligible expenses include approved plants, materials (mulch, compost, stone), hardware (pipe and connectors), equipment rental, design fees, and labor directly related to the approved project. Tools and general equipment (e.g., shovels, wheelbarrows) are not eligible. Taxes are excluded from rebate calculations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to properties in Montgomery County, Maryland, excluding the municipalities of Rockville, Gaithersburg, and Takoma Park. Residents of those municipalities should check with their respective jurisdictions, which collect the Water Quality Protection Charge separately and may offer their own rebate programs.
requirements_list: Property must be located in Montgomery County outside the municipalities of Rockville, Gaithersburg, and Takoma Park
Must install one of the eligible project types: rain barrel, rain garden, conservation landscape, water harvesting system, green roof, permeable pavement, pavement removal, or cistern
Submit a project application through the RainScapes Rewards portal before beginning work
Project must be approved by RainScapes before installation begins
Project must receive runoff from an impervious surface
At least 75% of plants used must be native to the mid-Atlantic region
Invasive plants and sterile cultivars of native plants are not permitted
Project must not be located within a right-of-way or easement
Project must not require a stormwater permit or have been installed because of a permit requirement
Project must not have previously received a RainScapes rebate
Project must not be grant-funded
Project must not consist of re-landscaping current, healthy, non-invasive landscaping
Receive a site assessment from an assigned planner
Submit required plan documents (including location plan and HOA approval letter if applicable) within 3 months of receiving the site assessment report
Installation must be completed within 6 months of project approval
Call MISS Utility (811) before installation
Meet minimum installation standards for the chosen project type
All payments to contractors must be made in full before a rebate can be issued
Property owner must electronically sign the Property Owner Agreement
Property owner must allow County inspections of the project every three years

Rain barrels and cisterns must attach to roof downspouts
Must provide location plan with graphic scale indicating foundation area
HOA approval letter required if applicable

Must schedule and pass a final inspection
Only new projects are eligible; cannot be used to fulfill a county-required stormwater permit

Sufficient space on property to accommodate overflow
Residential: $7,500 lifetime rebate maximum per property

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Review the application guide and Water Harvesting Project Manual on the program website. 2. Submit a project application through the RainScapes Rewards online portal (apps.montgomerycountymd.gov/Rainscapes/). Applications are accepted on a first come, first served basis; no paper application is available (contact the program for help). Community property applicants may also contact RainScapes staff directly to schedule a site assessment. 3. A planner is assigned within 2 to 4 weeks and conducts a site assessment (in person or virtually). 4. Submit required plan documents (including location plan and HOA approval letter if applicable) within 3 months of receiving the site assessment report. 5. For cisterns, a preliminary inspection will be conducted to confirm site suitability. 6. Receive official project approval and electronically sign the Property Owner Agreement. 7. Call MISS Utility (811) before installation. 8. Install the approved project within 6 months of approval, meeting all design and location requirements. 9. Contact your planner to schedule a final inspection. 10. Submit itemized receipts, photos, and measurements as requested. 11. Receive rebate, typically within 8–12 weeks after final inspection. Applicants can also check the status of a current application online.

structured_extraction.program_name: RainScapes Stormwater Garden: Conservation Landscapes Rebate
structured_extraction.program_description: The RainScapes Conservation Landscapes rebate rewards property owners in Montgomery County who replace lawn, invasive plants, or eroded areas with native plants and improved soil. Conservation landscapes act as simplified rain gardens — they slow down and soak up stormwater runoff and provide habitat for pollinators. The program is funded by the Water Quality Protection Charge (WQPC) and supports three types of stormwater gardens: Rain Gardens, 3" Ponding Conservation Landscapes, and Conservation Landscapes.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rebates are $5 per square foot for conservation landscapes without ponding, or $6 per square foot for landscapes with at least 3 inches of ponding (minimum 250 square feet for residential, 350 square feet for commercial/institutional). Maximum rebate is $7,500 for residential and $20,000 for commercial/institutional properties. Applications are accepted on a first come, first served basis.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners in Montgomery County (outside the municipalities of Rockville, Gaithersburg, and Takoma Park) who want to replace lawn or invasive plants with native plants to manage stormwater runoff. Includes residential, commercial, institutional property owners, congregations, and schools.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installing conservation landscapes using native plants to replace lawn, invasive plants, or eroded areas on the applicant's property. Eligible costs include native plant planting, soil amendments, mulch, excavation, materials, and labor.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland private properties, excluding properties within the municipalities of Rockville, Gaithersburg, and Takoma Park (which collect the Water Quality Protection Charge separately). Cannot be in County right-of-way.
requirements_list: Must replace lawn, invasive plants, or erosion-prone areas with native plants and improved soil
Minimum 250 square feet for residential projects (no individual garden smaller than 75 sq ft); minimum 350 square feet for commercial/institutional
At least 75% native Piedmont plants by quantity and coverage
Ponding gardens must drain within 24 hours
Ponding gardens must be at least 10 feet from basements and 5 feet from built structures
Gardens should not be placed in soggy areas or near large tree roots
Water must drain away from foundations and not toward neighbors' properties
Planting plan required with title, north arrow, accurate scale, species labels, and quantities
Proper weir notch installation for overflow management
Deer-resistant plants recommended for wooded areas
Proper maintenance required (weeding, watering)
Must meet qualification requirements outlined in the Conservation Landscaping requirements document
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Develop a scaled planting plan with native species. Submit a plant list spreadsheet with required information. RainScapes staff review and apply calculations for approval. Review the application guide on the RainScapes Rewards Rebate Application Guide page, then submit an application. Applicants can hire a RainScapes professional or DIY install. Applications are accepted on a first come, first served basis. Applicants can also check the status of a current application online.

structured_extraction.program_name: RainScapes Stormwater Garden: Rain Garden Rebate
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides a rebate to property owners who install a rain garden to capture and absorb stormwater runoff from hard surfaces like roofs, driveways, and patios. Supports three types of gardens: Rain Gardens, 3" Ponding Conservation Landscapes, and Conservation Landscapes. Rain gardens are depressed landscape areas filled with spongy soil and at least 75% native plants that clean and soak up rainwater, reducing runoff into local waterways. Promotes native plants, pollinators, soil health, and watershed protection.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: $10 per square foot of total rain garden area. A minimum garden size of 75 square feet is required. Applications are accepted on a first come, first served basis.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County property owners (residential and commercial), schools, and congregations who want to install a stormwater garden to manage stormwater runoff on their property.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of stormwater gardens including Rain Gardens, 3" Ponding Conservation Landscapes, and Conservation Landscapes that capture stormwater runoff from hard surfaces, using native plants and appropriate soils.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to properties in Montgomery County, Maryland, including areas in the Piedmont region.
requirements_list: Minimum rain garden size of 75 square feet
Garden surface must be depressed 6 inches
Must include at least 75% native plants (native to Piedmont region in both plant quantity and coverage)
Garden must capture stormwater runoff from hard surfaces such as roofs, driveways, patios, or sidewalks
Final garden sizing must be verified by a RainScapes planner after application
Ponding gardens must be placed at least 10 feet from basements and 5 feet from built slabs
Rain gardens must pass a percolation test (soil must drain within 36 hours)
Ponding gardens should be placed between hard surfaces and property exit points
Utilities must be marked before excavation (call 811-257-7777)
Planting plan with title, north arrow, accurate scale, species labels, and quantities required
Hard edging installed lower than existing edge
3" of natural hardwood mulch (non-dyed)
Deer-resistant plants if deer present in area
Balance of shrubs and perennials in design
Weekly watering during first year after planting
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Develop a scaled planting plan with measurements and create a plant list spreadsheet with required information. Submit plan for RainScapes staff review. RainScapes staff apply calculations to evaluate coverage and effectiveness. Choose DIY installation or hire a RainScapes contractor. Applications are accepted on a first come, first served basis. A RainScapes planner will verify the final garden sizing for rebate eligibility.

structured_extraction.program_description: A referral program run by the Montgomery County Commission for Women to help women re-enter the workforce or community. Individuals fill out an online form to be connected with relevant resources or services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Referral assistance connecting participants to relevant resources and services through an online referral form.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Women seeking to re-enter the workforce or community in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Fill out the online referral form at the link provided on the page.

structured_extraction.program_description: A custom after-school recreation program created in partnership with school Parent Teacher Associations (PTAs). Montgomery County Recreation works with PTAs to design and deliver fun, skill-building programs for students, faculty, and staff. Program ideas can cover a wide range of categories including arts, sports, fitness, cooking, and more.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Montgomery County Recreation creates a custom recreation program based on your idea. A Recreation Specialist schedules the program and works with contracted instructors. Programs require at least 8 registered participants within 72 hours of the program start. Fees are set per program at $8–$15 per participant. There is no charge to submit an initial request; fees apply only after the program is created and confirmed.
structured_extraction.program_audience: School Parent Teacher Associations (PTAs), students, faculty, and staff at Montgomery County schools
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Creating and delivering custom after-school recreation programs for students and school communities
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to schools and PTAs in Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be associated with a school PTA or school community
Program must have at least 8 participants registered within 72 hours of the program start date
Fees of $8–$15 per participant apply after the program is confirmed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Email rec.classes@montgomerycountymd.gov with your program idea. No commitment or payment is required at this stage. You will receive a response within two business days. A Recreation Specialist will work with you to schedule the program. Once the program is created in ActiveMONTGOMERY, you will receive a registration link for participants.

structured_extraction.program_description: An after-school program for Montgomery County middle school students offering engaging activities tailored to each school to support personal growth, social interaction, and skill-building.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: School-tailored after-school activities for middle school students focused on skill-building, personal growth, and social connection.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: After-school program offering sports, creative arts, and mentoring open to all youth in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.program_audience: All youth in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Sports, creative arts, mentoring, and social activities after school
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County

structured_extraction.program_description: REDE provides pre-employment training to incarcerated individuals at the Montgomery County Correctional Facility. Participants receive soft skills training, workplace survival techniques, and hands-on work experience in the Job Shop (assembly and bulk mail) and the Digital Imaging Shop. The program also trains inmates to repair damaged library books in partnership with Montgomery County Public Libraries. Participants may earn industrial time credit toward sentence reduction while gaining work skills.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive soft skills training and hands-on work experience for six hours each weekday in the Job Shop and Digital Imaging Shop. Selected participants may earn industrial time credit toward reducing their sentence. Training is conducted in a simulated workplace environment emphasizing work habits, etiquette, and performance expectations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Sentenced and unsentenced inmates at the Montgomery County Correctional Facility seeking pre-employment skills and work experience to support employment after release.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Pre-employment soft skills training, workplace habit development, and hands-on work experience to prepare participants for employment after release.

Selection criteria for book repair program not specified
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: No formal application process described on the page. Program participation appears to be available to eligible inmates at the Montgomery County Correctional Facility.

structured_extraction.program_description: A county property tax credit for landlords who provide reduced rent to eligible elderly (age 65 or older) or disabled tenants who meet income and asset requirements. The credit encourages landlords to offer below-market rents to qualifying tenants.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Landlords receive a county property tax credit equal to 50% of the reduced rent charged to eligible elderly or disabled tenants. The reduced rent must be at least 15% below market rent as determined by the Department of Housing and Community Affairs (DHCA). The credit cannot exceed the county property tax paid by the landlord in the same year (non-refundable). Total credits are capped at $250,000 per fiscal year, granted in the order received.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landlords in Montgomery County who provide reduced rent to elderly (65+) or disabled tenants meeting income and asset eligibility requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Offsets county property tax liability for landlords who charge reduced rent to qualifying elderly or disabled tenants.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to landlords in Montgomery County, MD.
