Tenant must meet income and asset eligibility requirements
Reduced rent must be at least 15% below market rent as determined by DHCA
Credit cannot exceed county property tax paid by the landlord in the credit year
Program is capped at $250,000 per fiscal year; credits granted in order received
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Michael Parent in the Montgomery County Department of Finance for details on applying.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides rental assistance to low-income Montgomery County residents. Preference is given to households where at least one member is over age 62, has a documented disability, is fleeing or a survivor of domestic violence, or is homeless or at risk of homelessness.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rental assistance to low-income residents. Preference given to households with a member over 62, with a documented disability, fleeing domestic violence, or experiencing or at risk of homelessness.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income Montgomery County residents, with preference for elderly, disabled, domestic violence survivors, or those at risk of homelessness
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental housing costs
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, MD
requirements_list: Low income
Preference for households with member over age 62, documented disability, domestic violence survivor, or homeless/at risk of homelessness
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the HOC Housing Path Portal online application.

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County uses Rental Agreements to preserve affordable housing by restricting a set number of units in multifamily properties to income and rent limits. In exchange, the County pays a per-unit subsidy to the property owner equal to the difference between the affordable rent and the market rate rent for a comparable unit.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Per-unit subsidy paid by the County, calculated as the difference between the stipulated affordable rent and the average market rate rent for a comparable unit in the same or adjacent property. Any rent increases on subsidized units must follow the County's Voluntary Rent Guideline (VRG). Monitoring fee of $40 per unit per year applies.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Multifamily property owners and managers willing to restrict a portion of units to affordable rent and income limits in exchange for a County subsidy.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Subsidy payments to offset the difference between affordable rents and market rents on restricted units, supporting preservation of affordable housing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland only.
requirements_list: Follow the income and rent restrictions specified in the regulatory agreement.
Provide regular compliance reports including each tenant's name, household size, household income, and lease information.
Register with the County's Central Vendor Registration System (CVRS).
Select ACH payment method in CVRS to receive electronic subsidy payments.
Submit invoices with detailed backup documentation supporting the requested subsidy.
Payee name on invoice must match the owner's name in the rental agreement (or have written approval from the owner).
Invoice must include date, invoice number, and total amount requested.
Pay monitoring fee of $40 per unit per year by September 30 each year.
Rent increases on subsidized units must comply with the County's Voluntary Rent Guideline.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The Multifamily Section underwrites and negotiates rental agreements. Agreements typically arise from expiring Moderately Priced Dwelling Unit (MPDU) agreements, Right of First Refusal opportunities, or affordable housing development/preservation projects. The Asset Management team monitors compliance after execution.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides monthly rental assistance to Montgomery County residents who are homeless or at imminent risk of homelessness and have a household member with a documented disability or who is at least 55 years old. The program helps eligible households afford rent by subsidizing a portion of their monthly rental costs. Benefits are calculated as the amount by which monthly rent exceeds income-based thresholds (40% of gross income for households of 1–3 members; 35% for households of 4+ members), minus other housing subsidies. Payments are made via two-party check mailed to the applicant at the end of each month for the following month's rent. A related component, the Handicapped Rental Assistance program, helps low-income disabled individuals with rental expenses in licensed care facilities. Eligibility is based on age, income, disability, need, or other requirements. This is a referral-only program administered by Montgomery County's Office of Health and Human Services; benefit amounts were updated by an August 2021 regulation superseding Executive Regulation 18-20AM in part.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible households can receive between $100 and $503 per month. Benefits are calculated as the amount by which monthly rent (less other housing subsidies) exceeds 40% of combined monthly gross income for households of 1–3 members, or 35% for households with 4+ members. The maximum monthly benefit is $400 per the regulation; the FAQ notes benefits up to $503 based on household income and rental amount. Checks are mailed to the applicant's address at the end of each month for the following month's rent, made payable to both the tenant and landlord (two-party check). Benefits are approved for a maximum of 12 months, after which a new application is required. A separate component (Handicapped Rental Assistance) helps disabled individuals with costs at licensed care facilities. Benefit payments are subject to available appropriated funds and waiting lists may be implemented at the Director's discretion.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County renters who are currently homeless or at imminent threat of homelessness, have a household member with a documented disability or age 55+, and meet income and asset limits. Also includes low-income disabled individuals seeking assistance with licensed care facility rental expenses. Broadly serves county residents exiting homelessness who need rental assistance.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Monthly rental payments to help eligible households afford housing in Montgomery County; rental expenses in licensed care facilities for disabled individuals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicant must be a renter in Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be currently homeless (living in a car, on the street, or in a shelter) or at imminent threat of homelessness (eviction notice or lack of resources to maintain housing)
A member of the household must have a documented disability OR be at least 55 years old
Must be a renter in Montgomery County and rent cannot exceed 120% of average suitable-sized unit in Montgomery County
Monthly gross income cannot exceed program limits (e.g., $4,783/month for a 1-person household, up to $8,471/month for a 7-person household as of September 2025)
Household assets must be less than $10,000
Must not receive a Housing Choice Voucher or live in Public Housing
Must not rent from a relative
Rental unit must be appropriately sized for household composition
Household income thresholds: 40% of combined monthly gross income for households of 1–3 members; 35% for households of 4+ members
Minimum monthly benefit of $100; maximum of $400 per regulation
Only one household per eligible rental unit may receive benefits
Benefit payments subject to available appropriated funds; waiting lists may be implemented
Must be a Montgomery County resident
Referral required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: RAP is a referral-only program. All new applications must be submitted by a Montgomery County Health and Human Services social worker or case manager working within the Montgomery County Homeless Continuum of Care (e.g., Housing Stabilization Services). Renewal applications are mailed two months before benefits expire; applicants can also request a renewal by calling 240-777-4400. Renewals require proof of income, bank statements, most recent federal tax return, and proof of child care or medical expenses. Landlords must register with Montgomery County's Client Vendor Registration System (CVRS). Tenants receive recertification packets several months before subsidy expiration.

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County supplements the State of Maryland's Renters' Tax Credit by providing an additional payment equal to 50% of the State credit. Renters who qualify for and receive the State Renters' Tax Credit automatically receive this County Supplement — no separate application is required.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The County Supplement equals 50% of the State Renters' Tax Credit (which is up to $1,000). The County calculates the supplement automatically once it receives information from the State and sends a check directly to the renter. There is no separate application process.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Renters in Montgomery County who qualify for and receive the Maryland State Renters' Tax Credit, including those who are 60 or older, under 60 with at least one dependent child, or 100% disabled.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Direct payment to renters to help offset property tax costs passed through to renters.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to renters residing in Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must qualify for and receive the Maryland State Renters' Tax Credit
Must be 60 years of age or older, under 60 with at least one dependent child, or 100% disabled (per State requirements)
Must reside in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply for the State Renters' Tax Credit through the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) website. No separate application is needed for the County Supplement — the State sends credit information to the County, which then calculates and mails a check to the renter.

structured_extraction.program_name: Resident and Community Gardening Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program awards grants to eligible organizations to expand residents' access to yard, patio, and community gardening supplies, space, and education. It supports community health, food security, equity, climate goals, and food production resilience within Montgomery County. The program also provides access to land, nutrition education, cooking, and healthy eating resources. It funds proven, scalable food gardening initiatives that measurably increase the volume of fresh, edible food available to Montgomery County residents experiencing food insecurity. In FY24, $210,559 was awarded across seven grantees; FY26 funding totals $100,000 (performance period anticipated June 30, 2026 to August 31, 2027), and FY27 funding is expected to total $250,000, reaching approximately 4,000 residents.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are awarded to support resident and community food gardening initiatives, gardening education, nutrition education, cooking, and healthy eating programming. FY26 funding totals $100,000, with a performance period anticipated from on/about June 30, 2026 to August 31, 2027. In FY24, $210,559 was awarded across seven grantees, with individual awards ranging from approximately $17,856 to $43,242. FY27 funding is expected to total $250,000, reaching approximately 4,000 residents.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations, for-profit entities, individuals, and government entities in Montgomery County that provide residents with access to gardening supplies, land, space, and education to support food security, community health, and nutrition, particularly for food-insecure residents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Expanding resident and community food production capacity, providing gardening supplies and space, delivering gardening and nutrition education, cooking instruction, culturally appropriate healthy eating programming, and proven scalable food gardening initiatives that increase fresh edible food available to food-insecure residents.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to organizations and individuals operating within Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be an eligible organization (nonprofit, for-profit, individual, or government)
Program activities must expand resident and community food production capacity within Montgomery County
Programs must support community gardening, nutrition, cooking, or healthy eating education
Initiatives must be proven and scalable
Must measurably increase the volume of fresh, edible food available to food-insecure residents
Expected to leverage existing SNAP-Ed materials where applicable
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Office of Grants Management; FY26 grant anticipated to launch in mid-March 2026. Contact ofsr@montgomerycountymd.gov for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides major rehabilitation of residential roadways in older communities. Work includes pavement rehabilitation and reconstruction, under drains, subgrade drains, and curbs and gutters. Pavement reconstruction involves removing and replacing the entire existing pavement structure where there is widespread fatigue-related distress, base failures, or subgrade failures.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: County-funded pavement rehabilitation and reconstruction of residential roadways in older communities, including repair of under drains, subgrade drains, curbs, and gutters. Seasonal activity suspended November through April.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential communities in older neighborhoods in Montgomery County, MD
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rehabilitation and reconstruction of residential roadway pavement, including ancillary elements such as under drains, subgrade drains, and curbs and gutters
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Residential roadways in older communities
Pavement must exhibit widespread fatigue-related distress, base failures, subgrade failures, or conditions where other restoration approaches are impractical

structured_extraction.program_description: RBSP is a comprehensive alcohol awareness training program for Montgomery County government personnel. It covers the history and current conditions of the alcohol industry, intoxication rate factors, visible signs of intoxication, effective intervention strategies, and Montgomery County-specific alcohol policies and practices.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Virtual training session lasting 3–4 hours including an exam. Currently only available to Montgomery County government agency personnel who have been invited to take the course.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County government agency employees
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Alcohol awareness and policy education for government personnel
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland — limited to Montgomery County government agency personnel
requirements_list: Must be a Montgomery County government agency employee
Must be invited to participate; not open to the general public
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact ABS via email to express interest if you have not been invited. Participation is by invitation to Montgomery County government agencies.

structured_extraction.program_name: Retiree Dental - CIGNA PPO Dental Plan
structured_extraction.program_description: A dental insurance plan for Montgomery County government retirees, administered by CIGNA Health and Life Insurance Company. The plan covers preventive, basic restorative, major restorative, orthodontic, and implant services on a cost-sharing basis. Includes the WellnessPlusSM Progressive Maximum Benefit feature that increases the annual dollar maximum when preventive care is received. Retirees may use any licensed dentist, but using a PPO network dentist typically results in lower out-of-pocket costs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The plan pays 100% of reasonable and customary charges for Class I (diagnostic and preventive) services; 80% for Class II (basic restorative, endodontics, periodontics, oral surgery); 60% for Class III (major restorative, prosthodontics); 60% for Class IV (orthodontics); and 60% for Class IX (implants). The annual maximum benefit (excluding orthodontics) is $2,000–$2,300 per person depending on year of enrollment, with the WellnessPlusSM feature allowing the maximum to increase when preventive care is received. The lifetime orthodontic maximum is $1,000 per person. A deductible of $50 per person or $150 per family applies each year (not applicable to Class I or Class IV services). Service frequency limitations apply (e.g., 2 cleanings per year, 2 exams per year).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County government retirees and their eligible dependents (spouses, domestic partners, and children under 26) seeking dental coverage.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Dental care expenses including preventive visits, basic and major restorative work, endodontics, periodontics, oral surgery, prosthodontics, orthodontics, and implants.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Montgomery County, MD government retirees. A separate summary exists for Texas residents, indicating some retirees may reside out of state. Services must generally be received within the United States.
requirements_list: Must be a retiree of Montgomery County government who has attained Normal Retirement Age as determined by the employer
Must be enrolled in the CIGNA PPO Dental Plan during an eligible enrollment period
Must pay required contributions/premiums
Dependents must meet eligibility criteria (age limits, legal relationship)
Must enroll within specified timeframes or be considered a Late Entrant
Services must be Medically Necessary and/or Dentally Necessary and provided by a licensed dentist
Calendar year deductible: $50 individual / $150 family (not applicable to Class I preventive or Class IV orthodontic services)
Annual benefits maximum: $2,000–$2,300 depending on year of enrollment
Class I preventive services required in prior calendar year to advance WellnessPlusSM wellness incentive levels
Service frequency limitations apply (e.g., 2 cleanings per year, 2 exams per year)
Out-of-network claims must be submitted within 365 days of the date of service
Coordination of benefits rules apply if covered under multiple plans
Coverage limited to services meeting plan guidelines and commonly accepted dental standards
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Enroll through the Montgomery County Office of Human Resources by signing an approved payroll deduction or enrollment form. No waiting period; coverage is effective upon election and eligibility. Use in-network CIGNA DPPO providers to receive in-network benefits. Submit out-of-network claims using the ADA Dental Claim Form to CIGNA P.O. Box 188037, Chattanooga, TN 37422-8037 within 365 days of service. For appeals or grievances, submit in writing within 180 days of denial.

structured_extraction.program_description: A license agreement program administered by the Montgomery County Department of Transportation (MCDOT) that allows developers to use Ride On transit service branding, data, or infrastructure in connection with development projects in Montgomery County.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A license agreement granting developers access to use Ride On transit resources, branding, or data as part of development projects in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Developers seeking to use Ride On transit service branding or resources in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Licensing access to Ride On transit branding, data, or infrastructure for development projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County's Right of First Refusal (ROFR) program requires that before an owner sells a multifamily rental property with 4 or more units, they must first offer the County, the Housing Opportunities Commission (HOC), or a certified tenant organization the chance to purchase it. The program preserves affordable housing and prevents tenant displacement. The County may also assign its right to purchase to qualified affordable housing developers. Qualified entities must demonstrate expertise in acquiring, maintaining, and managing affordable rental housing.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The County, HOC, or a certified tenant organization receives the right to purchase multifamily rental properties (4+ units) at the same price and terms as the pending third-party contract. The County may assign its purchase right to a qualified entity. Qualified entities must limit rent increases to no more than Voluntary Rent Guidelines for 15 years, protect tenants from eviction without cause, and guarantee tenants the right to return after rehabilitation. Down payment required is no more than 5% of the contract price. The sale must be completed within 180 days of DHCA receiving the ROFR packet. Qualified entities must demonstrate expertise in acquiring, maintaining, and managing affordable rental housing.
structured_extraction.program_audience: The County, Housing Opportunities Commission, certified tenant organizations, and qualified affordable housing developers (including non-profits, for-profits, partnerships, LLCs, corporations, and other organizational structures) seeking to purchase multifamily rental housing (4+ units) in Montgomery County before it is sold to a third party. Organizations must be experienced in affordable rental housing acquisition, maintenance, and management.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchasing multifamily rental housing developments of 4 or more units to preserve affordability and prevent tenant displacement, including acquisition, renovation, and new construction of affordable rental housing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland only.
requirements_list: Property must be multifamily rental housing with 4 or more units
Owner must submit a complete ROFR packet to DHCA within 5 days of executing a purchase contract
ROFR packet must include copy of pending purchase and sale contract, architectural and engineering plans, specifications, and operating data
Organizations wishing to become a qualified entity for ROFR assignment must apply to DHCA and submit supporting documents
Qualified entities must remain in good standing — not violating 53A provisions or failing to complete purchases without good cause
Assignees must limit rent increases to Voluntary Rent Guidelines for 15 years
Assignees must protect tenants from eviction without cause
Assignees must provide tenants the right to return to their unit after rehabilitation or redevelopment
ROFR must be exercised within 60 days of DHCA receiving the packet
Sale must be completed within 180 days of DHCA receiving the ROFR packet
Down payment may not exceed 5% of the contract price
All ROFR submissions must be submitted by email to DHCA.ROFR@montgomerycountymd.gov
Maryland business registration and license
Maryland Certificate of Good Standing
Documentation of prior affordable housing project experience
List of lenders and equity sources
Copies of affordability covenants
Certified list of code citations (5-year history)
Certified list of landlord/tenant judgments (5-year history)
Management company references
Resident counseling or neighborhood organization experience
10-year compliance with housing-related laws
No financial defaults as borrower or guarantor
Confidentiality agreement regarding Department information
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Owner sends DHCA a complete ROFR packet within 5 days of executing a purchase contract. Step 2: DHCA forwards the packet to approved qualified entities. Step 3: DHCA and qualified entities inspect the property. Step 4A: If the County wants to assign its ROFR, qualified entities have 45 days to notify DHCA of their interest. Step 4B: If not assigning, DHCA issues a certificate of compliance. Step 5: If proceeding, the County executes an assignment agreement with a qualified entity before the 60-day exercise period expires. Organizations wanting to become a qualified entity must apply to DHCA using the application form provided and submit all required supporting documents, including certifications regarding truthfulness, legal compliance, financial standing, and confidentiality. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides free or reduced-cost general dental care — including preventive, restorative, and emergency dental services — to uninsured or underinsured people living with HIV who are enrolled in HIV case management or medical case management services under the Ryan White Regional Services Network. Services are provided at the Dennis Avenue Health Center in Silver Spring, MD. Income eligibility is up to 500% of the Federal Poverty Level. Specialty care such as dentures is not included.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free or reduced-cost general dental care including preventive, restorative, and emergency dental services provided at the Dennis Avenue Health Center in Silver Spring, MD. Income eligibility is up to 500% of the Federal Poverty Level. Clients sign an eligibility form valid for 6 months and must provide income updates every 6 months. Specialty care such as dentures is not included.
structured_extraction.program_audience: HIV-positive individuals enrolled in Ryan White Part A or Part B services living in the Ryan White DC Eligible Metropolitan Area (District of Columbia, Montgomery County, Prince GeorgeS County, Frederick County, Charles County, and Calvert County) or the broader Ryan White Regional Services Network area.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Preventive, restorative, and emergency dental care services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Ryan White Regional Services Network area covering Montgomery County, Prince GeorgeS County, Frederick County, Charles County, Calvert County, Baltimore County, and the District of Columbia.
requirements_list: Must be eligible for Ryan White Part A and Part B services
Must be HIV-positive
Must reside in the Ryan White DC Eligible Metropolitan Area or Ryan White Regional Services Network service region
Income up to 500% of the Federal Poverty Level
Proof of income required at each dental visit
Eligibility form must be updated every 6 months
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 240-777-1737 to schedule an appointment at the Dennis Avenue Health Center. Bring a completed registration packet and proof of income to your first visit.

structured_extraction.program_description: A 5-year apprenticeship training program combining 40 hours of on-the-job training with classroom learning every two weeks to build sheet metal skills. The program is technically and professionally oriented.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 5-year apprenticeship combining on-the-job training and classroom instruction held once every two weeks.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications taken Monday through Friday, 8:00am to 3:30pm. New classes start every 3 months.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals seeking a career in sheet metal trades, especially youth involved with the juvenile court system in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Apprenticeship training in sheet metal work combining hands-on job experience and classroom learning.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Located in Suitland, Maryland; serves Montgomery County area youth.
requirements_list: No GED or high school diploma required
Ability to obtain a driver's license
Ability to arrive at the selected location by 7:00am, Monday through Friday
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications accepted Monday through Friday, 8:00am to 3:30pm. New classes start every 3 months. Contact TrainingCenter@Smart100.org or call 301-568-8655 ext. 3.

structured_extraction.program_name: SORRT (Smart Organizations Reduce and Recycle Tons) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A non-residential recycling program that educates businesses, organizations, and government facilities in Montgomery County about recycling requirements and best practices. The program provides recycling materials, on-site technical assistance, workshops, and outreach to help workplaces meet the county's mandatory recycling requirements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides free deskside recycling bins, literature, decals, posters, and educational videos. It also offers on-site technical assistance and site visits, presentations on waste reduction and recycling, business recycling seminars, and webinars on filing annual recycling reports.
structured_extraction.program_audience: All businesses, organizations, and local, state, and federal government facilities in Montgomery County that are required to recycle.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable — this is a technical assistance and education program, not a funding program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a business, organization, or government facility located in Montgomery County
All such entities are required by county law to recycle
Some businesses are required to file an Annual Recycling Report with Montgomery County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Businesses can order recycling bins and materials online, request a speaker presentation, or contact Sarah Mueller directly to request an on-site site visit. Webinars and seminars are available to attend for further guidance.

structured_extraction.program_description: Low-cost treatment for sexually transmitted infections (STIs) such as syphilis, chlamydia, and gonorrhea, provided on a sliding fee scale based on income. Referrals to other care providers for hepatitis B vaccination and hepatitis C treatment are also available.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: STI treatment provided on a sliding fee scale based on income. No one is turned away based on ability to pay. Available at Silver Spring and Germantown locations. Referrals for hepatitis B vaccine and hepatitis C treatment are also available.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents diagnosed with STIs such as syphilis, chlamydia, or gonorrhea.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Treatment for sexually transmitted infections (STIs). Referrals for hepatitis B vaccine and hepatitis C treatment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Services available at Dennis Avenue Health Center in Silver Spring and a Germantown location.
requirements_list: Must have been diagnosed with an STI such as syphilis, chlamydia, or gonorrhea
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 240-777-1760 (Silver Spring) or 240-777-1609 (Germantown) to access treatment services.

structured_extraction.program_name: Safe Routes to School (SRTS) for Schools
structured_extraction.program_description: Safe Routes to School (SRTS) is a nationwide program run locally by Montgomery County that works with schools and communities to make walking and biking to school safer and more appealing for students, including those with disabilities. The program uses six elements — engagement, equity, engineering, encouragement, education, and evaluation — to help schools create safer walking and biking environments. It combines education (promoting traffic safety, enforcing rules, encouraging participation) and engineering (improving sidewalks, crosswalks, curb extensions, ADA-compliant ramps, and traffic signs near schools) to reduce traffic, fuel use, and air pollution while promoting healthy, active lifestyles among students. Schools can also become SRTS Ambassadors.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides free resources, education, and infrastructure improvements to help students walk and bike to school safely. Schools that join receive support focused on student pedestrian and cyclist safety, including educational content, safety tips, and access to program guides. Available activities include bicycle and pedestrian safety education classes or assemblies, bicycle safety rodeos, crosswalk simulation activities, training for volunteers or staff on Walking School Bus/Bicycle Train development, Crossing Guard Appreciation, International Walk to School Day participation, and Walking Wednesdays. Infrastructure improvements include new sidewalks, crosswalk markings, ADA-compliant ramps, curb extensions, crossing islands with midblock flashing beacons, and traffic calming measures near schools. Schools can also become SRTS Ambassadors.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County Public School students (kindergarten to 8th grade), parents, teachers, educators, drivers, and communities seeking safer walking and biking routes to school, as well as schools wanting to improve student safety traveling to and from school.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Education and outreach activities, traffic safety programs, assessment of school travel route safety, walking and bicycling promotion and events, infrastructure improvements (sidewalks, crosswalks, pedestrian ramps, traffic signs, curb extensions, crossing islands) near schools, and supporting student pedestrian and cycling safety through encouragement and community engagement.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Montgomery County, Maryland, near public schools (kindergarten through 8th grade).
requirements_list: School must commit to the safety of students traveling to and from school and while on school property
Must be a Montgomery County Public School student, parent, or educator to participate in school-based programs
Schools must sign up to become a Safe Routes to School partner school
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Schools and community members can sign up online to become a Safe Routes to School partner school, request a bike rodeo, request resources or outreach, plan a Walking Wednesday, or take the Safety Pledge using the forms linked on the program website. Schools can also contact the program directly to find out how to start a Safe Routes to School initiative. Schools can apply to become an SRTS school by completing the online form provided on the page.

structured_extraction.program_description: The SafeKeep Program provides temporary care (up to 30 days) for owned pets while their owners are unable to care for them due to illness, homelessness, or other emergencies. Pets may be housed at the shelter, placed in a foster home, or placed at a partner boarding facility, with the goal of reuniting owners with their pets.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Temporary housing and care for eligible pets (all species except dogs with bite histories or aggression toward people) for up to 30 days. Spay/neuter services are provided at no stated cost if the pet is not already altered. Pets may be housed at the shelter, in a foster home, or at a partner boarding facility.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents who are temporarily unable to care for their pets due to illness, homelessness, or other emergencies, and who are working with (or will establish a relationship with) a Montgomery County social worker, case manager, or allied agency.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Temporary boarding, foster placement, and spay/neuter services for owned pets while the owner resolves a temporary crisis.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Owner must be working with a Montgomery County social worker, case manager, or allied agency, or must establish such a relationship while the animal is in OAS care.
Owner must be available for regular (every other week) check-in calls with OAS.
Owner must plan to take their pet home within 30 days.
Pet must be used to living indoors.
Pet must be overall healthy or currently maintained on medication.
Pet must be friendly toward strangers.
Owner must consent to spay/neuter of their pet if not already altered.
Dogs with a bite history are not eligible.
Dogs aggressive toward people are not eligible.
All dogs must pass a behavior evaluation for foster placement.
Pets must complete a full intake including heartworm or FELV/FIV testing if not up to date on required vaccinations.
Participation is subject to available space.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the SafeKeep application (available through OAS). All dogs undergo a behavior evaluation. A full intake with an OAS staff member is required.

structured_extraction.program_description: Same Day Access (SDA) is a subsidized taxi transportation program for Montgomery County residents who hold a current MetroAccess identification card. Unlike the main Call-N-Ride program, there is no income requirement. Participants pay $30 and receive $60 in value on their SDA swipe card each month. All trips must begin and end in Montgomery County, with special exceptions for transportation to approved medical facilities in Designated Service Areas.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants pay $30 and receive $60 in value on their SDA swipe card, once per month. No income requirement. All trips must begin and end in Montgomery County, with special exceptions for approved medical facilities in Designated Service Areas (including Baltimore, Prince George's County, Northern Virginia, and Washington D.C.). Must hold a current MetroAccess identification card and reside in Montgomery County. Recertification required upon Metro Access card expiration; recertification must be submitted within 30 days of recertification notice.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Recertification required within 30 days from date of recertification letter
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents who hold a current MetroAccess identification card (people with disabilities or seniors who qualify for paratransit service)
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Taxi transportation to medical and personal appointments via participating taxi companies within Montgomery County and approved Designated Service Areas (Baltimore, Prince George's County, Northern Virginia, and Washington D.C. for approved medical facilities only).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a resident of Montgomery County, Maryland, and hold a current MetroAccess identification card. All trips must begin and end in Montgomery County, with special exceptions for transportation to approved medical facilities in Designated Service Areas.
requirements_list: Must be a Montgomery County, Maryland resident
Must hold a current MetroAccess identification card (photocopy required)
No income requirement
Proof of current residence in Montgomery County (within last 6 months): SSI statement, utility bill, W-2, property tax bill, insurance bill, mortgage statement, or lease agreement
Completed application form with signature
Recent photograph recommended but not required
All trips must begin and end in Montgomery County (exceptions for approved Designated Service Areas)
Recertification required upon Metro Access card expiration; must recertify within 30 days of recertification notice
Valid photo ID required if swipe card lacks photograph
Advance notice required for wheelchair accessible vehicle requests
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the SDA Application Form (PDF) and submit with a photocopy of your current Metro Access ID and proof of Montgomery County residence (within last 6 months). Submit by fax to 240-556-0999, email to cnrorder@montgomerycountymd.gov, or by mail/hand-delivery to Call-n-Ride Program, 101 Monroe Street, 5th Floor, Rockville, MD 20850. For recertification, complete the SDA Recertification Form and submit required documentation within 30 days of your recertification notice. For questions, call 301-948-5409 (Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.), Connect-A-Ride at 301-738-3252, or dial 311 for the MC 311 Call Center.

structured_extraction.program_name: School Based Health and Wellness Centers (SBHWCs)
structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County operates 16 School Based Health and Wellness Centers located in schools across the county. These centers provide comprehensive health services to students including preventive medical care, sick care, mental health support, social services, immunizations, reproductive health care, dental screenings, and health education. Services are designed to help students stay healthy and succeed in school.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free or low-cost health and wellness services provided on-site at schools. Services include well-child and sports physicals, sick care, immunizations, prescriptions, lab testing, dental varnish, reproductive health care, STI/HIV prevention and testing, mental health therapy, case management, and health education. Only Maryland Children's Health Insurance Program (MCHP/HealthChoice) is billed; no student is billed or denied care.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students enrolled in schools that have a SBHWC, uninsured siblings of enrolled students, and children in the Care for Kids Program assigned to the SBHWC.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Health and wellness services including medical care, mental health, social services, dental screenings, immunizations, prescriptions, and health education for students and eligible siblings.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at 16 school locations across Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a student enrolled in a school that has a SBHWC, an uninsured sibling of a student enrolled in a school with a SBHWC, or a Care for Kids Program client assigned to the SBHWC
Parent or guardian must sign written consent for child to receive services
No insurance requirement — all students are eligible regardless of insurance status
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the SBHWC at your child's school to obtain an enrollment packet. Complete the packet with written parental permission and return it to SBHWC staff at your child's school. Bring the child's insurance card if they have one; staff can assist uninsured families in obtaining coverage.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides free or low-cost dental services to students at select Montgomery County Public Schools on school premises during normal school hours, in partnership with Montgomery County Public Schools. Services include screenings, exams, cleanings, fluoride treatments, and sealants.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free or low-cost dental services including screenings, exams, cleanings, fluoride treatments, and sealants provided on school premises during normal school hours at select Montgomery County Public Schools.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students enrolled at select Montgomery County Public Schools.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Dental care services including screenings, exams, cleanings, fluoride treatments, and sealants for school-age children.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Select Montgomery County Public Schools.
requirements_list: Must be a student enrolled at a participating Montgomery County Public School
Registration form required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Email the Dental Kids program at hhsdentalkids@montgomerycountymd.gov or call 240-777-4238 for more information. Registration forms are available on the Dental Application Forms page.

structured_extraction.program_description: This grant program supports non-profit organizations that address gaps in healthy food access for children and families by co-locating food assistance programs at Montgomery County Public Schools (MCPS) school sites. Funded organizations establish, expand, or maintain school-based food pantries, produce distributions, snack bag programs, prepared meal programs, and related food assistance initiatives in partnership with MCPS. In FY26, the program expanded to 80+ MCPS school sites, representing a 30%+ expansion over the prior year, supported by $300,000 in new budget funds, with a total of $2,303,775 awarded to 13 organizations serving more than 50,000 children. Applications are submitted through the ecivis grants portal, and the Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) is available for review.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants awarded annually to non-profit organizations to support food assistance programs co-located at MCPS school sites. In FY26, 13 organizations received a total of $2,303,775 (approximately $2.3 million), supporting 80+ school sites and serving more than 50,000 children. In FY25, 11 organizations shared $1,250,274. In FY24, eight organizations shared $480,452. Individual awards have ranged from approximately $15,750 to $146,250. FY26 included $300,000 in new budget funds representing a 30%+ expansion over the prior year. Funds may be used for new activities or expansion of existing activities. Cannot be used for purchases already made, lobbying, alcoholic beverages, or supplanting other funds. FY26 grant period runs 08/25/2025 - 06/30/2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit 501(c)(3) food assistance provider organizations based in Montgomery County that operate food assistance programs at or in partnership with Montgomery County Public Schools, serving students and families experiencing food insecurity.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Establishing, expanding, or maintaining school-based food pantries, produce distributions, snack bag programs, prepared meal programs, and other food assistance services at MCPS school sites for families experiencing food insecurity. Eligible costs include staffing, food purchases (with preference for sourcing from Montgomery County and Washington Metropolitan/DMV region farms), operating costs, and indirect costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland — programs must operate at Montgomery County Public School sites. Preference for sourcing food from Montgomery County and Washington Metropolitan/DMV region farms and underserved communities.
requirements_list: Must be an IRS-designated 501(c)(3) organization
Must be based in Montgomery County
Must be registered with Maryland State Department of Assessment and Taxation (SDAT) and maintain Good Standing status
Must have provided food assistance services over the past calendar year at one or more MCPS site(s)
Must partner with MCPS to deliver food assistance at school sites
Must address food resource needs identified by school personnel
Must develop a program model for services at new or existing school sites
Mid-cycle and end-cycle programmatic and financial reports required per school matched
Memoranda of Understanding (MOU) with assigned schools
Documentation photos of food distribution
Satisfaction survey distribution to participants
Photo releases for public use
Sound fiscal management practices and financial reporting capability
Experience collaborating with MCPS partners
Demonstrated performance history serving Montgomery County children and families
Strong evaluation and data collection capacity
Culturally relevant and inclusive service delivery
Nutrition quality control measures
Technical, cultural, and linguistic proficiency
Board conflict-of-interest disclosures
Proof of insurance before fund distribution
Compliance with Title VII Civil Rights Act
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations apply competitively through the Office of Food Systems Resilience via the ecivis grants portal. Review the NOFO (available at https://assets.montgomerycountymd.gov/files/FY26-SFBA-Grant-NOFO.pdf) for full details. The program runs on an annual (fiscal year) cycle. Resources for current grantees including program requirements and school matches are posted on the program page. For technical questions contact Catherine Nardi at OFSR; for ADA accommodations contact Greg Weissman at OGM (grants@montgomerycountymd.gov, (240) 773-3344).

structured_extraction.program_name: Securing Houses of Worship Preparedness Training
structured_extraction.program_description: A preparedness training program for faith leaders in Montgomery County, delivered by the Office of Emergency Management and Homeland Security, Fire and Rescue Services, Police, and the Faith Community Working Group, covering how to secure houses of worship against threats and emergencies.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free in-person preparedness training provided to faith leaders and houses of worship in Montgomery County. County staff visit the requesting organization to deliver the training.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Faith leaders and houses of worship in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Emergency preparedness and security planning for houses of worship.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a house of worship located in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Fill out the Request a Speaker form on the Montgomery County website. Staff will follow up with more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: Allows participants in Montgomery County's Retirement Savings Plan, Deferred Compensation Plan, and Police Deferred Retirement Savings Plan to invest in a wider range of options — including mutual funds, ETFs, equities, stocks, bonds, CDs, and other securities — through Fidelity BrokerageLink, beyond the standard investment options offered by the Board of Investment Trustees.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants can open a self-directed brokerage account through Fidelity BrokerageLink to invest retirement plan funds in mutual funds, ETFs, equities, stocks, bonds, CDs, REITs, foreign securities, Treasury securities, and other eligible securities not otherwise prohibited. The Board does not monitor or evaluate investments made through this account. SIPC and excess SIPC protection apply. Minimum initial investment of $2,499 for RSP/EOP participants; $999 for subsequent transfers; no minimum for payroll contributions.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County employees participating in eligible retirement plans including the Retirement Savings Plan (RSP), Employee Option Plan (EOP), Deferred Compensation Plan (DCP), Police Deferred Retirement Savings Plan (DRSP), Sworn Deputy Sheriffs and Uniformed Correctional Officers DROP; intended for hands-on investors willing to actively monitor their portfolio and assume responsibility for personal investment decisions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Self-directed investment in mutual funds, ETFs, stocks, bonds, CDs, REITs, foreign securities, Treasury securities, options, and other eligible securities through a Fidelity BrokerageLink brokerage account.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Montgomery County government employees enrolled in eligible retirement plans.
requirements_list: Must be a participant in the Retirement Savings Plan (RSP), Employee Option Plan (EOP), Deferred Compensation Plan (DCP), Police Deferred Retirement Savings Plan (DRSP), or Sworn Deputy Sheriffs and Uniformed Correctional Officers DROP
Must complete and submit the SDBA Enrollment Form and Fidelity BrokerageLink Participant Acknowledgment Form with original signatures
Minimum initial investment of $2,499 for RSP/EOP; $999 for subsequent transfers; no minimum for payroll contributions
Minimum $500 recommended to remain in standard plan options to cover fees
Active monitoring and management of portfolio required
Participant is responsible for determining investment suitability
Compliance with plan guidelines and restrictions required
Options trading requires separate application and approval
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Fidelity BrokerageLink Application and the SDBA Enrollment Form, then return original signed copies to Montgomery County Employee Retirement Plans, 101 Monroe Street, 6th Floor, Rockville, MD 20850. Once enrolled, account can be accessed through Fidelity.com, Fidelity Mobile, or the FAST telephone system (1-800-544-5555). Fund the account through payroll contributions or exchanges from standard plan options.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state-mandated program that allows eligible owner-occupied residential property owners in Montgomery County to pay their real property taxes in two installments rather than one lump sum. The first payment is due September 30th and the second is due December 31st. The program was designed to reduce closing costs for new homebuyers by spreading out tax payments.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Taxpayers pay half of their annual real property tax bill by September 30th and the remaining half by December 31st, instead of the full amount at once. Taxpayers who escrow their payments may elect to pay annually by notifying their lender by May 1st. Personal property taxes, residential rental property taxes, and commercial real property taxes are not eligible.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owner-occupied residential property owners in Montgomery County who pay real property taxes
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Spreading real property tax payments into two semi-annual installments
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to owner-occupied residential property owners in Montgomery County, MD
requirements_list: Must own owner-occupied residential property in Montgomery County
Property must be principal residence
Personal property taxes, residential rental property, and commercial real property are not eligible
Taxpayers who escrow must notify their lender by May 1st to elect annual payment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: No action is required to enroll — eligible taxpayers are automatically placed on the semi-annual schedule. Tax bills will show both semi-annual and annual payment options. Taxpayers who escrow and wish to pay annually must notify their lender by May 1st.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that helps qualified Montgomery County residents pay for care in licensed assisted living facilities. Service operates Monday through Friday. Vehicles are wheelchair and electric scooter accessible, with loading and unloading assistance available upon request.

structured_extraction.program_name: Senior Citizens Real Property Tax Deferral Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Allows eligible senior homeowners in Montgomery County to defer the portion of their County residential real property tax that exceeds the prior year's County tax bill. The deferred amount carries no interest during the deferral period and is secured by a lien on the property. The total accumulated deferred taxes cannot exceed 50% of the property's fair market value. Deferred taxes become due when the owner sells, stops occupying the property as their principal residence, the property goes to tax sale, or its use changes. A new application must be filed each year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible homeowners may defer the amount by which their current County property tax exceeds their prior year's County property tax. No interest is charged during the deferral period. The total accumulated deferred taxes cannot exceed 50% of the property's fair market value. The deferred taxes become a lien on the property and a personal liability of the applicant, secured by a Tax Deferral and Lien Agreement filed in the county land records at the owner's expense. Once approved, the deferral is applied to the second installment or refunded if the bill was already paid in full. Homeowners remain liable for non-deferred taxes and may end the deferral at any time by written notice and payment.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: September 1 of the current taxable year
structured_extraction.contact_name: Michael J. Coveyou, Director of Finance
structured_extraction.program_audience: Senior homeowners age 65 or older who have lived in their principal residence in Montgomery County for at least five consecutive years, whose combined household gross income does not exceed $80,000 in the prior calendar year, and who continue to occupy the property as their principal residence.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Deferral of the annual increase in County residential real property taxes for eligible senior homeowners.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only in Montgomery County, Maryland, for residential real property occupied as the owner's principal residence.
requirements_list: At least one homeowner must be 65 years of age or older (proof of age required)
At least one homeowner must have resided in the property as their principal residence for five consecutive years and must continue to do so
Combined gross income of all household members (excluding dependents and those paying reasonable rent or room and board) must not exceed $80,000 in the previous calendar year
Property must be residential real property occupied as the owner's principal residence
The accumulated deferred taxes cannot exceed 50% of the fair market value of the property
Application must be received by September 1 of the current taxable year with all required documentation
Must submit copies (not originals) of supporting documents including W-2s, federal income tax return with all schedules, and benefit statements
Must sign a Tax Deferral and Lien Agreement, which must be notarized by both the homeowner and the county director
Applicant pays all costs of recording the lien in Montgomery County land records
Authorization required for verification through Social Security Administration, IRS, and other agencies
A new application must be filed each year
Incomplete applications will be returned
Property must not become subject to tax sale
Property use must not change
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Pick up a printed application at the Division of Treasury (27 Courthouse Square, Suite 200, Rockville, MD 20850) or download the Senior Citizens Tax Deferral Application (PDF) online. Complete the application using the provided instructions, attach proof of age, copies (not originals) of supporting income documents (W-2s, federal income tax return with all required schedules, benefit statements), and the signed and notarized Tax Deferral and Lien Agreement. Submit all materials to the Montgomery County Department of Finance, Division of Treasury, Attn: Tax Deferral, 27 Courthouse Square Suite 200, Rockville MD 20850 by September 1 of the tax year for which deferral is requested. The agreement is recorded in Montgomery County Land Records. Incomplete applications will be returned. A new application must be filed each year.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Senior Dental Program provides dental health services to eligible low-income, uninsured seniors age 60 and older in Montgomery County who are not eligible for Medicaid. The program offers free or low-cost dental benefits to residents who meet income requirements at or below 250% of the Federal Poverty Level. Services are provided at county dental clinics, with visits available for $20 per regular visit or $30 per emergency visit. Applications can be submitted online through the Community Connect Portal.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free or low-cost dental care at county clinics for eligible seniors. Regular visits are $20 and emergency visits are $30. There are no fees or costs associated with most County health programs. Applications can be submitted online through the Community Connect Portal starting January 1, 2025.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Uninsured seniors age 60 and older who are Montgomery County residents with family income at or below 250% of the federal poverty level, no dental insurance, and who are not eligible for Medicaid (Medical Assistance).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Dental health services including routine and emergency dental care at county clinics for eligible seniors.

Must be a Montgomery County resident
Must be uninsured or have no dental insurance
Must not be eligible for Medicaid (Medical Assistance)
Must meet financial eligibility requirements (family income at or below 250% of the Federal Poverty Level)
Must provide proof of income, proof of identity, and proof of Montgomery County residence
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online through the Community Connect Portal at https://communityconnect.montgomerycountymd.gov/, apply in person at an Office of Eligibility and Support Services (OESS) location, or complete the fillable application form, print it, and return it to OESS. OESS will confirm eligibility. Once enrolled, call the county dental clinic closest to your home to schedule an appointment.

structured_extraction.program_description: Drop-in social and activity programs for adults age 55 and older, offered at 13 locations across Montgomery County. Participants can connect with others, have coffee, and take part in activities such as fitness classes, arts, games, and more. Some locations include a nutrition lunch program and limited transportation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free or low-cost drop-in programming including fitness classes, social activities, games, arts, and nutrition lunch at select locations. Some sites offer limited transportation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults age 55 and older in Montgomery County, Maryland
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at 13 recreation center locations across Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be age 55 or older
Some programs require registration; others are drop-in
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Drop-in programs require no registration. Programs that require registration can be registered for through ActiveMONTGOMERY online or by contacting the individual recreation center.

structured_extraction.program_description: Funded under Public Law 109-365, the Older Americans Act (OAA), Montgomery County's Senior Nutrition Program provides hot, cold, and vegetarian lunches in congregate (group) settings for seniors at multiple senior program locations across the county, operated in partnership with the Department of Health & Human Services, Aging and Disability Services. The program promotes better health through improved nutrition, helps older adults remain healthy, independent, and active, and encourages fellowship and socialization to reduce isolation. Meals meet federal nutrition standards and are suitable for people with diabetes, heart disease, and hypertension. Menus are available in multiple languages including Chinese, English, French, Korean, Spanish, and Vietnamese. Kosher, Chinese, Korean, and Vietnamese meals are available at certain sites. The program also offers nutrition education, screening, and counseling, as well as lectures and food demonstrations. It serves as a central referral contact for home-delivered meals (Meals on Wheels). Seniors aged 60 and over are asked for a voluntary donation; those under 60 pay the full meal price. Advanced registration is required at least one week in advance. Participating locations include Damascus, Silver Spring, Rockville, Germantown, Wheaton, Gaithersburg, and Montgomery Village, among others.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Subsidized hot, cold, and vegetarian lunch meals are provided at congregate senior center and recreation center locations across Montgomery County. Seniors age 60 and over pay only a voluntary donation; those under 60 pay the full meal price. All meals include whole grain rolls or pasta (unless otherwise stated), milk or yogurt, and 100% fruit juice. Nutrition education, screening, and counseling are also available. Referrals to Meals on Wheels programs for home-delivered meals are provided. Advanced reservation is required at least one week before the meal date.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults age 60 and over in Montgomery County; spouses of any age of a registered 60+ participant; SNP volunteers of any age (for up to two hours per month); persons with disabilities under 60 living with a registered parent/grandparent participant; persons with disabilities under 60 living in a building where a nutrition site is located; and adults under 60 who pay the full meal price.

structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at multiple senior center and recreation center locations in Montgomery County, Maryland, including Damascus, Silver Spring, Rockville, Germantown, Wheaton, Gaithersburg, and Montgomery Village.
requirements_list: Age 60 or older, OR spouse of any age of an active registered participant, OR disabled adult child/grandchild living with an active registered participant, OR person with disabilities under 60 living in a building where a nutrition site is located, OR SNP volunteer (any age, up to two hours per month)
Participants under age 60 (other than those meeting exemption criteria) must pay the full meal price
Complete SNP registration form annually
Receive SNP meal card
Valid Maryland ID required
Must reserve a meal at least one week in advance by calling the participating center
Some centers offer a stand-by or waiting list for last-minute meals if extras are available

Contact the nutrition site manager at the desired site to make a reservation at least one week in advance. Some centers also offer a stand-by or waiting list for last-minute availability if extra meals are available.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Montgomery County property tax credit for homeowners who are at least 65 years old and use the property as their principal residence. The credit equals 50% of the combined Maryland State Homeowners' Tax Credit and the Montgomery County Supplement, further reducing the taxpayer's county property tax bill. The credit amount may be based on the Maryland State Homeowners' Tax Credit, the Montgomery County Supplement, or a combination of both, depending on eligibility. Introduced in levy year 2007. No separate application is required — homeowners who have already applied for the State Homeowners' Property Tax Credit (HOTC) through SDAT are automatically considered, as SDAT uses age information on file to determine eligibility.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A property tax credit equal to 50% of the combined State Homeowners' Tax Credit and Montgomery County Supplement, applied against the county property tax bill. The credit amount may be based on the Maryland State Homeowners' Tax Credit, the Montgomery County Supplement, or a combination of both, depending on eligibility. Introduced in levy year 2007. No separate application is needed for the Senior Credit if the homeowner has already applied for the State Homeowners' Property Tax Credit — SDAT uses age information on file to determine eligibility automatically.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residential property owners who are at least 65 years old and use the property as their principal residence, and who qualify for the Maryland State Homeowners' Tax Credit.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of property tax liability on a principal residence in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to homeowners in Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: At least one property owner must be at least 65 years of age or older.
The home must be the applicant's principal residence.
Must apply for or qualify for the Maryland State Homeowners' Property Tax Credit (HOTC) or the Montgomery County Supplement to be considered.
SDAT uses age information on file to determine eligibility automatically — no separate application needed if already applied for the State Homeowners' Property Tax Credit.
Applications for 2026 can be submitted online through the One Stop portal.

No separate application is needed for the Senior Credit — SDAT uses age information on file to automatically consider eligibility. Applications for 2026 can be submitted online through the One Stop portal. Call SDAT at 800-944-7403 for questions.

Participation in recertification process

structured_extraction.program_description: Award-winning incubator program offering turnkey office space and comprehensive business support services for advanced technology companies. structured_extraction.program_description: The Silver Spring TMD provides free commuter services to employers and employees in downtown Silver Spring. Established in 1987, it helps employers set up Transportation Demand Management (TDM) Plans, runs commuter information fairs, conducts biennial commuter surveys, offers green business certification, and recognizes employers who support alternative commuting. The goal is to reduce traffic congestion by encouraging employees to use transit, carpools, vanpools, biking, walking, and telework instead of driving alone.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free services including commuter information fairs, biennial commuter surveys, green business certification, employer recognition, and help designing and carrying out a Transportation Benefits Program for the worksite. Employers with 25 or more employees in the TMD are required by county law to submit a Traffic Demand Management Plan within 90 days of receiving written notice from the Director. TDM Plans must include strategies to achieve Non-Auto Driver Mode Share (NADMS) goals and may include alternative work hours, carpool/vanpool programs, transit subsidies, parking management, and improved bicycle/pedestrian access. Plans are reviewed by a TMD representative and committee before final approval. Revenue from TDM fees must be used within the District for administering TDM strategies, coordinating with projects and occupants, reviewing and monitoring TDM Plans, and funding District programs.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Within 90 days after receiving written notice from the Director
structured_extraction.program_audience: Employers with 25+ employees and building owners (nonresidential and multi-unit residential) located in the Silver Spring Transportation Management District in Montgomery County; also applicable to development applicants, building/project managers, and employees and residents within the District
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reducing solo driving by helping employees learn about and use transit, carpool, vanpool, biking, walking, and telework options; planning and implementation of employer-based transportation demand management initiatives; funding commitments for on-site commuting programs and performance incentives
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Silver Spring Transportation Management District in Montgomery County, Maryland (Red, Orange, or Yellow Policy Areas as defined in the Subdivision Staging Policy)

Must comply with all approved TDM Plan provisions and provide survey data
