structured_extraction.program_name: Small Business Assistance Program (SBAP) / Impact Assistance Fund (IAF)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Montgomery County Small Business Assistance Program (SBAP) provides loans, grants, and/or technical assistance to small businesses through the County's Economic Development Fund. Created by Montgomery County Council under Bill 6-12 in April 2012, the program specifically helps financially healthy small businesses that are negatively affected by a County-funded redevelopment project or a redevelopment project on County-owned property, helping these businesses remain viable during the project. Executive Regulation 24-12AM governs the award process and criteria, and the maximum financial assistance a small business can receive is $125,000 (raised from $75,000 in June 2019). The program is currently focused on the Wheaton Revitalization Project (a public-private partnership between Montgomery County and Stonebridge-Carras). An associated component, the Impact Assistance Fund (IAF), provides one-time financial and/or technical assistance up to $25,000 to financially healthy small businesses in currently designated geographic areas — including Silver Spring, Bethesda, and Clarksburg — that are negatively affected by a County-initiated redevelopment project.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Under the SBAP, financial assistance of up to $125,000 (increased from a previous $75,000 maximum, raised in June 2019 per Executive Regulation 24-12AM) and/or technical assistance may be provided periodically over the duration of the County-related redevelopment project, awarded through the Economic Development Fund as loans, grants, and/or technical assistance. Businesses may receive multiple disbursements. Under the IAF component, one-time financial assistance (grants) of up to $25,000 and/or technical assistance is available to businesses in currently designated geographic areas adversely impacted by a County-initiated redevelopment project, including areas around the Studio Plaza Project in Silver Spring, the Bethesda Metro Station South Entrance CIP Project in Bethesda, and the Clarksburg Square Road Extension Project in Clarksburg.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Financially healthy small businesses located within an identified geographic area adversely impacted by a County-funded or County-related redevelopment project in Montgomery County, including designated areas such as Silver Spring, Bethesda, Clarksburg, and Wheaton.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Maintaining small business viability and offsetting adverse impacts during a County-related or County-initiated redevelopment project, as defined by the Economic Development Fund guidelines and program criteria.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must be located within an identified geographic area affected by a County-funded redevelopment project or a redevelopment project on County-owned property in Montgomery County, Maryland. Currently designated areas under the IAF include Silver Spring (Studio Plaza Project area), Bethesda (Bethesda Metro Station South Entrance CIP Project area), and Clarksburg (Clarksburg Square Road Extension Project area). The SBAP is currently focused on the Wheaton Revitalization Project area.
requirements_list: Business must be financially healthy
Business must be located within an identified geographic area adversely impacted by a County-funded or County-related redevelopment project
Business must meet eligibility requirements and criteria in Executive Regulation 24-12AM
Business must be currently experiencing adverse impact due to a County redevelopment project in a designated area (for IAF component)
Business must be located in a designated geographic area adversely impacted by a County-initiated redevelopment project (for IAF component)
Business must be located in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Montgomery County Business Portal at montgomerycountymd.gov/businesses/business-resources/business-funding-incentives. For award process and criteria details, contact the Department of Finance or refer to Executive Regulation 24-12AM.

structured_extraction.program_name: Small Business Innovation Research and Small Business Technology Transfer (SBIR/STTR) Matching Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County's SBIR/STTR Matching Grant Program provides non-dilutive matching grants to small biotech, medical, and life sciences companies in Montgomery County that are applying for or have received federal SBIR/STTR awards. Established under the Montgomery County Economic Development Fund (MCER No. 2-23) and administered by the Montgomery County Department of Finance, the program offers three tiers: Phase 0 (up to $5,000 to reimburse technical assistance costs for companies applying for their first SBIR/STTR award), Phase 1 (up to $25,000 matching grant for Phase 1 awardees), and Phase 2 (up to $50,000 matching grant for Phase 2 awardees). The program supports small businesses in the early stages of competing for federal research and development funding and helps them prepare, apply for, and commercialize federal SBIR/STTR grants. Companies must conduct at least 51% of their research and development in Montgomery County. The regulation establishing policies and procedures for administering the program was adopted in August 2023. Note: the program expired as of July 1, 2025 and is no longer accepting applications.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Three grant tiers are available: Phase 0 reimburses up to $5,000 in technical assistance costs for applying for a first SBIR/STTR award. Phase 1 provides a matching grant of 25% of the federal SBIR/STTR Phase 1 award, up to $25,000. Phase 2 provides a matching grant of 25% of the federal SBIR/STTR Phase 2 award, up to $50,000. For Phase 1 and Phase 2 grants, up to 50% of the matching grant may be used for technical assistance, investment assistance, or commercialization assistance. Funds cannot be used for expenses already reimbursed by other federal or state sources. Specific match amounts and terms are also defined in the full regulation (MCER No. 2-23).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Program expired as of July 1, 2025; no longer accepting applications. Previously, two application periods per calendar year: August 11 and February 15 (subject to change at Director's discretion).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses (up to 20 employees) in Montgomery County conducting research in biotechnology, medicine, or life sciences that are applying for or have received a federal SBIR or STTR award. Businesses must be in operation for 5 years or less (Phase 0 and Phase 1) or 7 years or less (Phase 2).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Phase 0: reimbursement of technical assistance costs related to writing an SBIR/STTR application. Phase 1 and 2: advancing technologies toward commercialization, with up to 50% usable for technical assistance, investment assistance (fundraising, business planning, pitch decks), or commercialization assistance (product development, regulatory planning, market strategy). Funds may not duplicate other federal or state reimbursements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Business must conduct at least 51% of its research and development in Montgomery County, Maryland. Company must maintain 51% of operations in the County for a minimum of 2 years from the date of the grant award.
requirements_list: Business must be in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
At least 51% of the research and development must be conducted in Montgomery County
Company must maintain 51% of operations in the County for a minimum of 2 years from the date of the grant award
Business must have a maximum of 20 employees at time of application
Research must be in medicine, biotechnology, or life sciences
Must have received a federal SBIR or STTR award
Must meet county eligibility criteria for local small businesses
Must be a small business
Must participate in the federal SBIR or STTR program

Phase 0: business must have no prior SBIR/STTR awards, be in operation 5 years or less, and have submitted an SBIR/STTR Phase 1 proposal with qualifying technical assistance costs incurred after December 27, 2022

Phase 1: business must have received an SBIR/STTR Phase 1 award in the current fiscal year, be in operation 5 years or less, and have received no more than 2 prior Phase 1 awards and 0 prior Phase 2 awards

Phase 2: business must have received an SBIR/STTR Phase 2 award in the current fiscal year, be in operation 7 years or less, and have received no more than 4 prior Phase 1 awards and 1 prior Phase 2 award
Phase 0 applicants must be pursuing their first Phase I grant and meet additional stated criteria
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted on a first-come, first-served basis through the application portal on the County Business Center website (MontgomeryCountyMD.gov). There are two application periods per calendar year: August 11 and February 15 (dates subject to change at the Director's discretion). Separate application links exist for Phase 0 and for Phase 1/Phase 2. The full regulation (MCER No. 2-23) contains complete policies and procedures. For additional information, contact the Department of Finance, Fiscal Management at 101 Monroe Street, 15th Floor, Rockville, Maryland 20850. Note: the program has expired as of July 1, 2025 and is not currently accepting applications.

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County invests $50 million in county funds in participating community banks headquartered in the county. Those banks commit an equal amount of their own funds, resulting in $100 million in loans to local small businesses to promote job creation and economic growth. The county places deposits with participating local community banks at competitive rates of return, with deposits secured by FDIC insurance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: $100 million in total small business lending is made available through participating community banks. Montgomery County deposits $50 million in county funds into qualifying community banks, which must match that amount with their own lending. Banks must originate loans within 12 calendar months of the county's commitment to deposit. All deposited funds are covered by FDIC insurance. Banks must be headquartered in Montgomery County, have assets between $200 million and $10 billion, meet county safety and soundness standards, and maintain a minimum Green/Veribanc safety rating. Banks must maintain loans of at least 200% of county deposits placed.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small business owners in Montgomery County seeking loans through community banks participating in the program; county residents who benefit from job creation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Small business lending to promote job creation and business growth in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to small businesses in Montgomery County, Maryland. Participating banks must be headquartered in Montgomery County.
requirements_list: Loans must be originated through a community bank headquartered in Montgomery County
Participating banks must have assets greater than $200 million and no more than $10 billion
Participating banks must meet safety and soundness standards established by the county
Participating banks must meet minimum Green/Veribanc safety rating
Banks must originate loans within 12 calendar months of the county's deposit commitment
Banks must maintain loans of at least 200% of county deposits placed
Deposits secured by FDIC insurance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Small businesses apply for loans through participating community banks that are enrolled in the program. Banks that wish to participate must meet eligibility criteria and enter into an agreement with Montgomery County.

structured_extraction.program_name: Small Business Rental Assistance Program (Latino Economic Development Center Partnership)
structured_extraction.program_description: A one million dollar rental assistance program for small businesses in Montgomery County, created in partnership with the Latino Economic Development Center. Small businesses can apply for grants to help pay their rent.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants to small businesses to cover rent costs. Total program funding is $1 million.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment of business rent

Located in Montgomery County

structured_extraction.program_description: Soccer4Change is a free, year-round outdoor soccer program for middle and high school students in Montgomery County. It uses soccer to connect young people to developmental assets, reduce risky behaviors, and build emotional skills like problem solving and self-efficacy. The program reinforces positive character development through the four characteristics of Accountability, Respect, Trustworthiness, and Teamwork (A.R.T.T.).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free participation in a competitive soccer league with after-school programming, skill development, enrichment activities, and experiential learning. There is no cost to participate.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Middle and high school students in Montgomery County, particularly in the Germantown, Watkins Mill, Gaithersburg, Wheaton, and Silver Spring areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free after-school soccer programming including competitive league play, skill development, enrichment activities, and experiential learning.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Countywide program targeting specific areas: Germantown, Watkins Mill, Gaithersburg, Wheaton, and Silver Spring in Montgomery County.
requirements_list: Must be a middle or high school student
Must be enrolled in a partnering agency's program (City of Gaithersburg Recreation Department, Identity Inc., Street Outreach Network, RecXtra, Excel Beyond the Bell Middle, or RecZone)
Space is limited — students are encouraged to get on a waitlist through a partnering agency
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact one of the partnering agencies (City of Gaithersburg Recreation Department, Identity Inc., Street Outreach Network, or a Youth Development program such as RecXtra, Excel Beyond the Bell Middle, or RecZone) to get on the waitlist. For program registration, email Carlos Castro at Carlos.Castro@montgomerycountymd.gov or call 240-777-6925.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program helps food-producing farmers in Montgomery County improve soil quality by delivering one 40 cubic yard load of Leafgro organic compost to their farm each year. Assistance is provided on a first-come, first-served basis and is subject to available funding.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One 40 cubic yard load of Leafgro organic compost delivered to the farm annually. Assistance is provided on a first-come, first-served basis and is subject to funding availability.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Food-producing farmers operating on agriculturally assessed property in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Improving soil quality on food-producing farms using organic compost
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to farms located in Montgomery County, Maryland, on agriculturally assessed property
requirements_list: Must be a for-profit agricultural business in good standing with the state, if registered
If not registered, must have a federal Employee Identification Number (EIN) or Farm Service Agency (FSA) number
Must be operating on agriculturally assessed property
Must have a current nutrient management plan
Not available to landscape contractors
Farm delivery location must be accessible to a 40 cubic yard dump truck
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Email a request to Jacqueline.Arnold@montgomerycountymd.gov with your farm name, farmer/contact name, contact phone number, farm address for delivery, and any specific delivery instructions.

structured_extraction.program_name: South Village/Montgomery Village Focused Neighborhood Assistance Project
structured_extraction.program_description: A neighborhood improvement project that installs new energy-efficient LED street lights and makes site improvements for 482 households in the South Village section of Montgomery Village. Communities served include Walker's Choice, Center Stage, Grover's Forge, and The Hamptons.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) funds are used to construct street light and site improvements, with a 20% cost contribution from the homeowners association (HOA).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Households in the South Village section of Montgomery Village, specifically in Walker's Choice, Center Stage, Grover's Forge, and The Hamptons communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of energy-efficient LED street lights and site improvements in the South Village area of Montgomery Village.

requirements_list: 20% contribution from the homeowners association (HOA)

structured_extraction.program_description: A discounted parking permit program for licensed childcare providers located within the Bethesda, Silver Spring, or Wheaton Parking Lot Districts. Providers must receive or accept state or county subsidies or subsidized placements to qualify.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A limited number of discounted parking permits are available for eligible childcare providers. The Division of Parking Management reviews eligibility criteria before issuing permits.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed childcare providers located within the Bethesda, Silver Spring, or Wheaton Parking Lot Districts that receive or accept state or county subsidies or subsidized placements
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Discounted parking permits for eligible childcare providers
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be located within the Parking Lot Districts of Bethesda, Silver Spring, or Wheaton in Montgomery County
requirements_list: Must be a licensed childcare provider
Must receive or accept State or County subsidies or accept subsidized placement
Must be located within the Bethesda, Silver Spring, or Wheaton Parking Lot Districts
Application must be printed and emailed with copies of corresponding documents

structured_extraction.program_description: A free County-supported fall prevention program led by a trained professional. Participants learn to manage health behaviors to reduce the risk of falls.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free fall prevention classes led by a trained professional. Participants learn strategies to manage health behaviors and reduce fall risk.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Older adults at risk of falling
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participation in free fall prevention classes
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 240-773-8290 for information.

structured_extraction.program_description: Allows homeowners' associations (HOAs) and community associations (CAs) that own residential stormwater facilities on common areas to transfer structural maintenance responsibility for those facilities to Montgomery County. Once the transfer is complete, the County takes over structural maintenance (such as repairing leaks, replacing stone, concrete, and pipes), while the property owner retains ownership and responsibility for non-structural upkeep like trash removal and landscaping.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The County assumes responsibility for structural maintenance of transferred stormwater facilities, including repairs to leaks, stone replacement, and replacement of concrete and pipes. Property owners retain ownership and continue to handle non-structural maintenance. No financial payment is made to the applicant — the benefit is relief from structural maintenance obligations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners' associations (HOAs) and community associations (CAs) in Montgomery County that own residential stormwater facilities on common area property and wish to transfer structural maintenance responsibility to the County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Transfer of structural maintenance responsibility for stormwater facilities to Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residential stormwater facilities located on HOA/CA common areas within Montgomery County, MD.
requirements_list: Facility must be a residential stormwater facility located on HOA/CA common area property
Facility must have an approved final inspection and be in proper working condition as determined by DEP before transfer documents are forwarded to the County Administrative Officer
Applicant must provide a deed showing transfer of the parcel from the developer to the property owner
Applicant must provide appropriate easements and covenants for the stormwater facility
Applicant must provide a current property tax bill
All transaction documents (easements, covenants, or amendments) must be completed, signed, and notarized
Storm drains are not eligible for transfer
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Stage 1: Gather documents including list of facilities and parcel numbers, a deed, appropriate easements and covenants, and the most recent tax bill. Contact DEP at SWMF.Transfer@montgomerycountymd.gov or call 311 before submitting. Stage 2: Complete the Stormwater Facility Maintenance Transfer Application form, sign and notarize all transaction documents, and submit drafts in Word format to DEP and the Montgomery County Office of the County Attorney for legal review. Do not execute documents until DEP approves the drafts. Stage 3: Once DEP returns fully executed documents, record them at County Land Records and notify DEP. DEP will then send an official approval letter confirming the County's maintenance responsibility.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides street outreach, gang intervention, and trauma-informed activities for at-promise youth in communities and schools. Services include resolving gang-related conflicts, recreational and life skills activities (music production, boxing, photography, sports, art), and referrals to resources for newcomer families.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free street outreach, gang intervention, trauma-informed programming, recreational activities, life skills training, and referrals to community resources. No fees charged.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Youth ages 12 to 24, particularly at-promise or gang-involved youth in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Gang prevention and intervention, recreational and life skills activities, referrals to community services
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be between the ages of 12 and 24
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 240-773-1229 or get a referral from a partner organization. No documents are required.

structured_extraction.program_description: Each spring and fall, the Department of Transportation plants hundreds of new street trees in public rights-of-way throughout Montgomery County. Trees are planted in communities with low tree canopy coverage, prioritizing areas in watersheds identified for water and air quality protection.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free street tree planting in public rights-of-way adjacent to streets and roads. Residents can request a new street tree or maintenance of an existing street tree by contacting MC311.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents and property owners who want a street tree planted or maintained in the public right-of-way near their property.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planting and maintaining street trees in public rights-of-way.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout Montgomery County, with emphasis on communities with low tree canopy coverage in priority watersheds.
requirements_list: Request must be for a tree in a public right-of-way adjacent to a street or road
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact MC311 at mc311.com or by calling 3-1-1 to request a new street tree or maintenance of an existing street tree.

structured_extraction.program_description: Allows landlords of existing rent-stabilized buildings in Montgomery County to apply for a 23-year exemption from rent stabilization after completing substantial, permanent renovations that cost at least 40% of the building's assessed value.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A 23-year exemption from rent stabilization requirements for an existing building. The exemption requires completed substantial permanent renovations costing at least 40% of the building's assessed value. The exemption must be implemented within 12 months of approval. It cannot begin if the landlord has unresolved violations under Chapters 8, 26, or 29 of the Montgomery County Code, and cannot be applied to occupied units until the current lease term ends.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landlords of existing rent-stabilized buildings in Montgomery County who complete substantial permanent renovations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Exemption from rent stabilization for 23 years following qualifying substantial renovation of an existing building.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland only.
requirements_list: Must be an existing building subject to rent stabilization
Renovations must be substantial, permanent, and enhance the building
Renovation cost must be at least 40% of the building's assessed value
No unresolved violations under Chapters 8, 26, or 29 of the Montgomery County Code
Exemption must be implemented within 12 months of approval
Cannot be applied to occupied units until the current lease term ends
Applications and required documentation must be submitted via the Rental Housing Portal
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application and all required documentation through the Montgomery County Rental Housing Portal. Sample application forms are available on the Applications and Forms page.

structured_extraction.program_description: A paid ten-week fellowship run by the Montgomery County Council that places graduate students in local government roles across the County Council, Executive Branch, Office of Legislative Oversight, and Montgomery County Economic Development Corporation. Fellows work on policy analysis, research projects, and independent research that they present to the full Council.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Fellows receive an $8,000 stipend for the ten-week program running June 1 to August 7, 2026. The program provides hands-on local government work experience, mentorship from elected officials and senior staff, weekly field trips, and the opportunity to present independent policy research to the full County Council.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Stage 1 application is now closed; selected applicants notified by end of March 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Current graduate students (Masters or PhD) in public policy, public administration, public health, planning, law, or related fields who will have completed at least their first year of graduate study by summer 2026 and have a GPA of at least 3.0
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Stipend to support participation in the fellowship; transportation and relocation costs are not covered beyond the stipend
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Fellows must live in the Washington, D.C. region during the fellowship period; the program is located in Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a current graduate student (Masters or PhD) and cannot have graduated before the program start date
Must have completed at least the first year of graduate study by the program start date
Must study public policy, public administration/affairs, public health, planning, law, or a related field
Must have a cumulative GPA of at least 3.0 on a 4.0 scale
Must live in the Washington, D.C. region during the fellowship period
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Stage 1: Written application (now closed). Stage 2: Selected applicants submit two reference letters, a graduate transcript, a 5-10 page writing sample, and four short answer responses. Stage 3: Selected applicants participate in an interview. Applicants selected for the program are notified by end of March 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: Property owners seeking to conduct a timber harvest in Montgomery County can apply for an exemption from certain provisions of the County's Forest Conservation Law. The County Arborist reviews logging and harvesting plans to ensure they follow sustainable forest management practices before granting approval for the exemption.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The County Arborist reviews timber harvesting plans and, if the plan is consistent with sustainable forest management practices, approves an exemption from certain requirements of the Montgomery County Forest Conservation Law. This allows qualifying landowners to proceed with a timber harvest without fulfilling all standard Forest Conservation Law requirements.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Forest/timber owners and operators, and property owners with forest land in Montgomery County who wish to conduct a sustainable timber harvest and seek an exemption from certain Forest Conservation Law requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable — this is a regulatory exemption, not a financial assistance program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to property owners with forest properties located within Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Submit general information (owner name, address, contact details, location, acreage, preparer info)
Obtain a Sediment Control/Forest Harvest Permit from the Montgomery County Department of Permitting Services
Submit the Information for Sustainable Timber Harvest form to the County Arborist

Obtain an Environmental Review from the Maryland Department of Natural Resources Natural Heritage Program documenting presence or absence of threatened or endangered species on-site (free of charge, approximately 30 days)
Provide forest stand harvest operation details (cutting type, regeneration method, stand composition, age distribution, damage assessment, species lists)
Document existing and anticipated post-harvest conditions using standardized diameter classes
Submit forest harvest map with plot locations, stand boundaries, interior forest, slopes, streams, wetlands, buffers, skid trails, and landings
Receive approval from the County Arborist following a site visit
Complete and submit the Natural Resources Inventory/Forest Conservation Plan Exemption application to Montgomery Planning, Environmental Planning Division via ePlans
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Obtain a Forest Harvest Sediment Control Permit from Montgomery County Department of Permitting Services. 2. Submit the Sustainable Timber Harvest information form and a DNR Environmental Review letter to the County Arborist and schedule a site visit for approval. 3. Complete the NRI/Forest Conservation Plan Exemption application forms. 4. Submit application electronically to askdep@montgomerycountymd.gov or by mail to the County Arborist address, and upload required documents (sediment control permit, DNR letter, Arborist approval) into the ePlans system. Contact the County Arborist for guidance.

structured_extraction.program_name: Taber Financial Advisers One-on-One (2-hour) Investment Counseling Session
structured_extraction.program_description: A free two-hour one-on-one financial planning and investment counseling session offered to Montgomery County employee retirement plan participants, including those enrolled in the Retirement Savings Plan (RSP) and Deferred Compensation Plan (DCP). A registered financial adviser (Paul Taber of Taber Financial Advisers, a registered representative with Cambridge Investment Research) provides customized, confidential, and independent guidance to help participants build a diversified portfolio and deepen their understanding of investments to meet their retirement savings goals. Sessions are available in-person or virtually.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free 2-hour one-on-one financial planning and investment counseling sessions provided by Paul Taber of Taber Financial Advisers, a registered representative with Cambridge Investment Research. Sessions are confidential, professional, and independent, covering retirement savings planning, portfolio diversification, and investment education. Available to participants in the Retirement Savings Plan (RSP) and Deferred Compensation Plan (DCP). Sessions available in-person or virtually.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County government employees enrolled in the Retirement Savings Plan (RSP) or Deferred Compensation Plan (DCP) seeking personalized retirement savings and investment guidance.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Retirement savings planning, portfolio diversification, and building understanding of investments.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Montgomery County government employee retirement plan participants enrolled in the RSP or DCP.
requirements_list: Must be a participant in a Montgomery County Employee Retirement Plan
Must be enrolled in the Retirement Savings Plan (RSP) or Deferred Compensation Plan (DCP)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Book a one-on-one session online through the county's scheduling tool on the program page. You will receive a confirmation email a few days before your session. For questions, call 410-557-7300.

structured_extraction.program_name: Takoma-East Silver Spring (TESS) Community Action Center and Navigation Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A walk-in community action center and navigation program serving Montgomery County residents with modest incomes. Part of Montgomery County's Department of Health and Human Services' 'no wrong door' service integration model, ensuring community members can access all department and community resources. Staff connect individuals and families to essential services including information and referrals, social service assistance, interpretation and translation, education, free tax help (VITA), and legal services. Navigators help people apply for over 30 programs to ensure every person gets holistic, coordinated support.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free walk-in and appointment-based services including application assistance for over 30 programs such as SNAP, Temporary Cash Assistance, Housing Voucher Program, Child Care Grants, Eviction Prevention Referrals, Utility Assistance, and Food Referrals. Also includes information and referrals, interpretation and translation (Spanish, Amharic, and other languages via Language Line), free legal services through the Montgomery County Bar Foundation's Pro Bono Program, and free tax preparation through the Volunteer Income Tax Assistance (VITA) program. Navigators help connect families to food, housing, clothing, utility bill assistance, healthcare, and other services. Services available at multiple community locations including Manna Choice Pantry, WUMCO, Gilchrist Immigrant Resource Center, Clifton Park Hub, Nourishing Bethesda, and the TESS Center.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents with modest or low incomes seeking social services, referrals, legal help, tax assistance, or help navigating government and nonprofit programs. Multilingual services available in English, Spanish, and Amharic.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Assistance connecting individuals and families to food, housing, clothing, utility bill support, healthcare, immigration referrals, legal aid, tax filing, SNAP, cash assistance, housing vouchers, child care grants, eviction prevention, and other social services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Serves Montgomery County, Maryland residents. Walk-in site located at 8703 Flower Avenue, Silver Spring, MD 20901. Navigation services also available at several other community sites throughout Montgomery County including Manna Choice Pantry, WUMCO, Gilchrist Immigrant Resource Center, Clifton Park Hub, Nourishing Bethesda, and the TESS Center.
requirements_list: Must be a Montgomery County resident
Low or modest income preferred
TESS Center services by appointment only
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 240-777-4141 (English), 240-777-1587 (Spanish), or 240-777-1590 (Amharic) to request assistance or self-refer via QR code. Walk in during open hours (Tuesday–Friday 9–11:30 a.m.) or call 240-773-8260 to schedule an appointment (1–4 p.m. Tuesday–Thursday). In-person navigation available at multiple community locations throughout Montgomery County.

structured_extraction.program_name: Tax Credit for Property Leased by Religious Organizations
structured_extraction.program_description: A Montgomery County property tax credit for property owners whose property is leased, occupied, and used by a religious organization exclusively for public religious worship, educational purposes, or related office space.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A credit against county real property tax for the portion of a property leased and exclusively used by a religious organization for public worship, educational purposes, or supporting office space.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners in Montgomery County whose property is leased to and used exclusively by a religious organization for qualifying purposes.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of county real property tax liability.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Property must be leased, occupied, and used by a religious organization
Use must be exclusively for public religious worship, educational purposes, or supporting office space
Application must be filed with the Montgomery County Division of Treasury by April 1 of the preceding tax year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: File an application with the Montgomery County Division of Treasury by April 1 before the tax year in which the credit is to be used.

structured_extraction.program_name: Tax Credit for Spouse of Fallen Law Enforcement Officer or Rescue Worker
structured_extraction.program_description: A Montgomery County real property tax credit covering 100% of county property taxes on the primary home of a surviving spouse of a fallen law enforcement officer or rescue worker. The credit applies to the dwelling owned at the time of death, a dwelling acquired by the surviving spouse within 2 years of the officer/worker's death (if they were domiciled in Maryland at the time of death), or a subsequent dwelling to the extent of the prior credit.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A 100% county real property tax credit on the dwelling of a surviving spouse (who has not remarried) of a fallen law enforcement officer or rescue worker. Applies to the dwelling owned at the time of death, a dwelling acquired by the surviving spouse within 2 years of the officer/worker's death (if they were domiciled in Maryland at the time of death), or a subsequent dwelling to the extent of the prior credit.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Surviving spouses (who have not remarried) of fallen law enforcement officers or rescue workers who own property in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Elimination (100%) of county real property tax on the surviving spouse's dwelling.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a surviving spouse of a fallen law enforcement officer or rescue worker
Surviving spouse must not have remarried

Dwelling must have been owned by the fallen officer/worker at time of death, OR acquired by the surviving spouse within 2 years of death (if domiciled in Maryland at time of death), OR be a subsequent dwelling to the extent of the prior credit
Application must be submitted to the Division of Treasury by April 1 for the following tax year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application to the Division of Treasury by April 1 to receive the credit for the next taxable year. Applications can also be submitted online via the Montgomery County application portal at http://montgomerycountymd.seamlessdocs.com/f/FallenOfficerSpouseApp.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides peer group education to pregnant and parenting teens on raising children, healthy relationships, and prevention of repeat teenage pregnancy. Support groups are led by school nurses and assisted by Montgomery County Public Schools staff and community partners. Groups meet during the school day and give teens a chance to share experiences, learn from peers, and gain knowledge through presentations and discussions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free facilitated peer support groups held during the school day at Montgomery County high schools (depending on need). Groups cover raising children, healthy relationships, and preventing repeat teenage pregnancy. Attendance is voluntary.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Pregnant and/or parenting Montgomery County Public School students (both teen mothers and teen fathers).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participation in peer support group education on parenting, healthy relationships, and pregnancy prevention.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at high schools in Montgomery County, Maryland, depending on need.
requirements_list: Must be a pregnant and/or parenting Montgomery County Public School student
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: See your School Nurse for information about joining a group.

structured_extraction.program_description: Specially designed day camps for individuals with disabilities. Trained staff lead structured, adapted activities tailored to each camper's unique strengths and abilities, with a 1:4 staff-to-participant ratio. Program includes TR Summer Fun Zones (youth and young adults ages 6–21), After ESY afternoon camps, and Splash Camps with sports, arts and crafts, games, and swim activities.

Camps are grouped by age (Youth 6–10, Mid 11–14, Teen 15–21) with a 1:4 staff-to-participant ratio. Multiple session types available: year-round TR Camps, TR Summer Fun Zones, After ESY afternoon camps, and Splash Camps.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Youth and young adults ages 6–21 with disabilities who can follow one- to two-step directions, make simple choices, and perform basic self-care tasks with minimal assistance. All campers must be toilet trained.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participation in structured recreational camp activities including crafts, sports, games, music, and swimming.

Ages 6–21 (for Summer Fun Zones and After ESY camps)
Must be able to follow one- to two-step directions
Must be able to make simple choices
Must be able to perform basic self-care tasks with minimal assistance
Must be toilet trained
Personal care assistance is not provided

structured_extraction.program_description: Thinking for a Change (T4C) is a cognitive behavioral program for residents at the Pre-Release and Reentry Services facility. Participants identify and examine thinking and decision-making patterns that contributed to their contact with the criminal justice system. They learn pro-social communication and problem-solving skills. All new residents receive a 5-hour introductory module on Cognitive Behavioral Change, and high-risk residents continue the program over four weeks covering social skills and problem solving.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive a 5-hour introductory cognitive behavioral change module. High-risk residents are referred to a continuing four-week T4C program covering social skills and problem solving. Thinking Reports are used within the disciplinary process to help residents reflect on thoughts, feelings, attitudes, and beliefs that affect behavior.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents at the Pre-Release and Reentry Services facility, particularly those assessed as high risk, who are involved with the criminal justice system.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cognitive behavioral training to develop pro-social communication and problem-solving skills and reduce recidivism.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents at the Pre-Release and Reentry Services facility located at 11651 Nebel Street, Rockville, Maryland 20852 in Montgomery County.
requirements_list: Must be a resident at the Pre-Release and Reentry Services facility
All new residents receive the introductory module
High-risk residents are referred for the full four-week continuing program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Residents are assessed upon entry; all new residents automatically receive the 5-hour introductory module. High-risk residents are referred to the continuing four-week program.

structured_extraction.program_name: Tobacco Prevention, Cessation and Enforcement Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Helps Montgomery County residents quit smoking and vaping, reduces secondhand smoke exposure, and provides training and educational materials to local organizations. Includes community outreach, cessation treatment connections, retailer education and compliance visits, and information about current tobacco cessation classes at local hospitals and other venues. Nicotine replacement therapy (NRT) products are available free through the 1-800-Quit Now program. Also includes Freedom From Smoking, America's gold standard smoking cessation program — a 7-week live instruction course with a trained coach to help participants quit smoking for good, administered through Suburban Hospital.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free quit resources, community health education, cessation treatment referrals, and training and materials for local organizations. Residents can call 1-800-QUIT-NOW (1-800-784-8669) for free quitting help. Some hospital-based tobacco cessation classes may charge a fee. Nicotine replacement therapy (NRT) products are available free through the 1-800-Quit Now program. The Freedom From Smoking program offers 7 weeks of live instruction with a trained coach, support from a quit-smoking specialist at the Lung HelpLine, access to program materials including relaxation exercises, and referral to free nicotine patches and/or gum via MD QUIT NOW.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents who use tobacco or want to quit smoking or vaping, including patients, family, friends, and area community members, as well as local organizations and tobacco retailers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tobacco cessation support, community education, retailer compliance activities, cessation classes and support services, smoking cessation instruction, coaching, support services, materials, and nicotine replacement therapy.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland residents and organizations.
requirements_list: Must be a Montgomery County resident (for individual cessation services)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 240-777-3848 or 1-800-QUIT-NOW (1-800-784-8669) for free quitting help. Call 240-777-1222 for information about current cessation classes and locations. Contact the program office for organizational training or retailer education services. For Freedom From Smoking classes, register online at events.suburbanhospital.org or call 301-896-3844 to reserve a seat.

structured_extraction.program_description: Landowners in Montgomery County's Agricultural Reserve can sell development rights — called Transferable Development Rights (TDRs) — to developers in designated growth areas. When TDRs are created and sold, a TDR easement is placed on the property permanently restricting future development to a maximum of 1 unit per 25 acres. This allows rural landowners to recapture equity lost from the 1980 down-zoning while directing growth to areas with existing infrastructure.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Landowners generate TDRs from their Agricultural Reserve land and sell them to developers in designated receiving areas, generating private funds. Over 52,000 acres have been preserved through this program, generating $117 million in private TDR purchase funds. A TDR easement is placed on the property permanently restricting development to 1 unit per 25 acres.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners in Montgomery County's Agricultural Reserve interested in selling development rights from their land
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Proceeds from TDR sales go to the landowner as compensation for permanently restricting development on the property
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Land must be located in Montgomery County's Agricultural Reserve (AR) Zone, established in 1980 and covering more than 93,000 acres.
requirements_list: Land must be located in the Agricultural Reserve (AR) zone
Landowners may retain TDRs at a rate based on previous zoning (1 unit per 5 acres) relative to the current Agricultural Reserve density (1 unit per 25 acres)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a letter of intent at https://montgomerycountymd.seamlessdocs.com/ng/fa/fnvem23kcp1b to notify the Office of Agriculture of your interest in creating TDRs from your land.

structured_extraction.program_description: An early intervention program run by the State's Attorney's Office for Montgomery County that works with middle school (and some high school) students who have excessive absences. The program discovers the root causes of truancy and helps students and families address issues that affect school attendance, using mentoring, goal setting, and individualized support. Participation is voluntary and students are referred by school administrators.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Volunteers meet weekly with students for 10 weeks per semester (about 3 hours per week) to provide mentoring, goal setting, and individualized support. Students who reduce truancy by 60% or more can graduate from the program and are honored at a ceremony at the Montgomery County Circuit Courthouse.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Middle school and some high school students in Montgomery County Public Schools who have excessive absences and are referred by school administrators. Also seeks community volunteers to serve as mentors.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Addressing barriers to school attendance, providing mentoring and goal setting support, and improving student attendance, academics, and attitudes toward school.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County Public Schools — currently serving 25 middle schools and 2 high schools, with plans to expand to all 40 public middle schools.
requirements_list: Students must be enrolled in a participating Montgomery County Public School
Students are referred by school administrators
Participation is voluntary
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Students are recommended to the program by school administrators. Community members wishing to volunteer can complete the TPP Volunteer Application (PDF available on the program page) and contact Rebecca Marcolini for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: Establishes a tax credit against real property tax for urban agricultural properties in Montgomery County, Maryland. Promotes urban agricultural purposes including cultivation of fruits, vegetables, flowers, ornamental plants, keeping of fowl or bees, and aquaculture. The credit is calculated and applied as a line item deduction on a revised property tax bill, separate from the annual July tax bill.

The credit is not included in the annual July tax bill but appears on a subsequent bill revision, reducing property tax liability for eligible urban agricultural properties.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners engaged in urban agricultural purposes in Montgomery County, Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credit applied to real property tax liability for urban agricultural properties and activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties must be in residential zones, at least 0.5 acres and not more than 1 acre, located within 1000 feet of or in designated Metro Station Policy Areas in Montgomery County, Maryland.

Located within 1000 feet of or in designated Metro Station Policy Area
Used for urban agricultural purposes
Property owner must have more than $1,000 in gross income from sale of products grown or produced on the property

structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Action Agency's VITA program provides free in-person and virtual tax preparation help to Montgomery County residents who earned less than $69,000 per year. Trained, IRS-certified volunteers prepare federal, Maryland, and Montgomery County tax returns at no cost. The program helps individuals and families file their income tax returns, claim tax credits including the Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC, up to $8,046 federally), Maryland EITC, and Working Families Income Supplement, and connects them with financial education resources and guidance on opening bank accounts and saving with U.S. Savings Bonds. All VITA sites serve taxpayers filing with ITINs (Individual Taxpayer Identification Numbers). ITIN application and renewal assistance is also available on Wednesdays by appointment. Services are available at multiple locations throughout Montgomery County, including Gaithersburg, Silver Spring, Rockville, East County, Germantown, Wheaton, and the TESS Community Action Center in the Takoma/East Silver Spring area (Tuesdays during tax season). Tax season runs mid-January through mid-April; post-tax season appointments are available mid-June through October.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free in-person and virtual tax preparation and filing assistance provided by IRS-certified volunteers. Services cover federal, Maryland, and Montgomery County tax returns. Helps eligible residents claim tax credits including the federal EITC (up to $8,046), Maryland EITC, and Working Families Income Supplement. Also provides financial education resources and guidance on opening bank accounts and saving with U.S. Savings Bonds. Services are offered at multiple Montgomery County locations including the TESS Community Action Center (Tuesdays during tax season). Tax season appointments run mid-January through mid-April; post-tax season appointments are available mid-June through October. ITIN application and renewal assistance is also available on Wednesdays by appointment. All sites serve ITIN filers.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Wage Requirement Law Program requires contractors and subcontractors on qualifying Montgomery County service contracts to pay their employees a minimum hourly wage set by the county. The rate is adjusted annually each July 1 based on changes in the Consumer Price Index for the Washington-Baltimore metropolitan area. The program ensures workers on county-funded service contracts receive livable wages. It also includes compliance and reporting requirements: contractors must submit quarterly payroll reports documenting wage rates, hours worked, and employee demographic information, and must properly classify and document workers as either employees or independent contractors.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Contractors and subcontractors performing work on qualifying Montgomery County service contracts must pay employees at least $18.15 per hour (rate effective July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026). The county conducts random audits to verify compliance. Contractors who violate the law may face liquidated damages including unpaid wages and audit costs. Contractors must submit certified quarterly payroll reports within 14 days after each quarter ends, documenting employee wages, hours, and benefits, as well as employee demographic data (race and gender). Contractors must also declare whether they use independent contractors and submit required documentation verifying proper worker classification. Late or non-submission may result in contract payment withholding, liquidated damages, or contract termination. Employees may file complaints and recover unpaid wages, interest, and attorney fees.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Quarterly submissions due 14 days after each quarter ends
structured_extraction.program_audience: Contractors and subcontractors performing work on qualifying Montgomery County service contracts, and their employees. Prime contractors awarded County contracts who use independent contractors.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable — this is a wage compliance requirement, not a direct financial assistance program. Workers receive minimum wage protections under county service contracts.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. Applies to county service contracts entered into on or after July 1, 2003.
requirements_list: Vendor must receive $50,000 or more from the County in the most recent 12-month period, or will receive $50,000 or more under the contract in the next 12 months
Contract must be a county service contract (not a goods or construction contract)
Contract must not be with a public entity or a 501(c)(3) nonprofit
Contract must not be awarded on a noncompetitive basis where wage requirements would significantly impair performance (as determined by the Chief Administrative Officer)
Contract must not be for regulated utility services
Contract must not be an emergency contract to prevent or respond to an imminent threat to public health or safety
Contract must not be a bridge or cooperative procurement contract
Employees must perform direct and measurable work on the qualified county service contract
Employer must post county-provided WRL notices in the workplace
Employer must submit certified quarterly payroll reports within 14 days after each quarter ends (end of January, April, July, and October)
Employer must retain payroll records for 2 years after contract end
Report all employees' hours worked, pay rates, and gross wages
Include employee demographic data (race and gender for statistical reporting)
Attest under penalty of perjury to accuracy and compliance
All offerors must indicate independent contractor (IC) usage intent and submit Wage Requirements Law Independent Contractor Declaration Form

If using independent contractors, provide documentation: business license, insurance certificates, sole proprietor status forms, contracts, 1099s, invoices, SDAT information, federal tax returns, proof of public availability of services
Must comply with IRS and court standards for worker classification
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: This is a compliance program, not an application-based assistance program. Contractors with qualifying county service contracts must certify compliance with the WRL, post required notices, keep records, and submit quarterly payroll reports (PMMD-183 form) to the Office of Procurement at wrl@montgomerycountymd.gov within 14 days after each quarter ends. Reports must include an attestation statement signed by an authorized company representative. Prime contractors must also submit a signed Independent Contractor Declaration Form (PMMD-193) with supporting documentation for all independent contractors on bid/offer.

structured_extraction.program_name: Water Quality Protection Charge (WQPC) Hardship Reduction

structured_extraction.program_name: Water Quality Protection Charge (WQPC) Stormwater Management Credit Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Property owners in Montgomery County who own and maintain on-site stormwater management practices (such as rain gardens, rain barrels, permeable pavement, green roofs, bioretention, swales, cisterns, dry wells, or stormwater ponds) can receive a credit of up to 80% off their annual Water Quality Protection Charge, which appears on their yearly property tax bill. Credits of up to 80% are available for single-family residential (SFR) properties and up to 60-80% for non-residential/multi-family residential (NR/MFR) properties. The credit is calculated based on the volume of stormwater captured and treated by the on-site practice relative to the required Environmental Site Design Volume (ESDv). Credits must be renewed every 3 years, and eligibility requires that the property owner has consistently maintained their stormwater management infrastructure in accordance with DEP requirements and Montgomery County Code Section 19-28.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Credits of up to 80% off the annual Water Quality Protection Charge (a fee included in the yearly property tax bill) are available to property owners who own and maintain qualifying on-site stormwater management practices. For single-family residential (SFR) properties, credits up to 80% are available. For non-residential/multi-family residential (NR/MFR) properties, credits up to 60-80% are available based on treatment volume. Approved practices include bioretention, rain gardens, swales, green roofs, pervious pavement, rain barrels, cisterns, disconnections to pervious areas, conservation landscaping, dry wells, and micro-infiltration. Treatment is credited up to the first 1 inch (45% credit potential) and additional volume 1–2.2 inches (15% credit potential). An additional offsite treatment credit is available up to a 100% maximum, provided a minimum 60% onsite WQPC credit is first achieved. The credit is calculated based on the volume of stormwater captured by the on-site practice. Property owners must renew the credit every 3 years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential, agricultural, and commercial property owners in Montgomery County who own and are responsible for the structural maintenance of on-site stormwater management practices registered with the County, including stormwater ponds, rain gardens, rain barrels, permeable pavement, and green roofs. Also includes Home Owner Associations, non-profit organizations, and government-owned properties subject to the Charge.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of up to 80% off the annual Water Quality Protection Charge on the property tax bill for owning and maintaining qualifying on-site stormwater management practices.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland only.
requirements_list: Must own property in Montgomery County
Must own and maintain on-site stormwater management practices registered with Montgomery County
Must be responsible for the structural maintenance of the stormwater management practice
Must have consistently maintained the stormwater infrastructure
Practice must be maintained in accordance with DEP maintenance requirements and Montgomery County Code Section 19-28
Credit application must be submitted by September 30
Credit must be renewed every 3 years
Submit evidence of proper installation through photographic evidence
For SFR properties: self-inspection and maintenance checklist completion required
For NR/MFR properties: property owner-maintained systems only (unless part of County-approved participation project)
May require technical documentation submission if practices not permitted through Department of Permitting Services
Practices must comply with MDE Stormwater Design Manual
For offsite treatment credit: minimum 60% onsite WQPC credit must be achieved first
Offsite treatment limited to non-ESD practices only
Site-specific impervious/pervious data and hydrologic soil group data required for NR/MFR applications
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a credit application using the WQPC online form by September 30. Indicate whether this is a new or renewal application. A site visit may be coordinated to verify the stormwater practice.

structured_extraction.program_name: Water Quality Protection Charge (WQPC) Stormwater Management Credit for Multi-Family and Non-Residential Properties
structured_extraction.program_description: Property owners of multi-family residential and non-residential properties in Montgomery County can apply for a credit to reduce their annual Water Quality Protection Charge (WQPC). The WQPC is a fee based on the amount of impervious surface (pavement, rooftops, etc.) on a property. Property owners who install or maintain stormwater management practices — such as rain gardens, permeable pavement, or green roofs — can receive a reduction of up to 60% or up to 80% of their annual charge, depending on how much stormwater runoff is treated. Properties can achieve up to 100% credit by treating both onsite and offsite stormwater runoff. Credits must be renewed every 3 years.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A credit (reduction) off the annual Water Quality Protection Charge based on the volume of stormwater treated by stormwater management practices: up to 60% credit for non-ESD (Environmental Site Design) practices; up to 80% for ESD practices; and up to 100% total credit possible when treating both onsite and offsite stormwater runoff. Eligible practices include green roofs, conservation landscaping, micro-bioretention, rain gardens, permeable pavements, rainwater harvesting (rain barrels/cisterns), sheet flow to conservation areas, wet ponds, and bioretention systems. Credits must be renewed every 3 years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of multi-family residential and non-residential properties (including commercial, industrial, nonprofit-owned, and government-owned) in Montgomery County who pay the Water Quality Protection Charge and have or plan to install stormwater management practices on their property.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of the annual Water Quality Protection Charge fee assessed on impervious surface area. Eligible stormwater management practices include swales, roof leader disconnection, dry wells, green roofs, rain gardens, permeable pavements, rainwater harvesting, conservation landscaping, micro-bioretention, sheet flow to conservation areas, wet ponds, and bioretention systems.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to property owners of private property parcels within Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must own a multi-family residential or non-residential property subject to the WQPC in Montgomery County
Stormwater management practice must be registered with the County and permitted through the Department of Permitting Services
Property owner must maintain stormwater management practices in accordance with DEP maintenance requirements and Montgomery County Code Section 19-28
Must provide Account ID (8-digit number) from property tax bill
Must submit application for new credit or renewal every 3 years
Engineer-certified plans must include total impervious area, year of installation, facility size, impervious area treated, and a photograph of the stormwater management system
Stormwater management system must be documented; treatment volume must be calculated per MDE Stormwater Design Manual or auto-calculated by County calculator
Implementation of Maryland Department of Environment (MDE) recognized stormwater treatment practices per MDE Stormwater Design Manual
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application using the online WQPC form, available at the County's WQPC portal. Indicate whether applying for a new credit or renewal. Provide property and owner information, stormwater system design data, and supporting documentation. DEP will coordinate a site visit as needed. Applications and renewal requests are due by September 30.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Biotechnology Investor Incentive Program (BIIP) provides supplemental grants to qualified investors who have received a final tax credit certificate from the State of Maryland's Biotechnology Investor Incentive Tax Credit Program and have invested in Montgomery County biotechnology businesses. Investors approved for the state tax credit automatically receive the County supplemental grant. Grant amounts are prorated based on the amount appropriated for the program and each investor's share of total state tax credits received by all investors in County biotechnology businesses. The county typically pays out the grants between March and May for investments made in the previous calendar year.

Grant amounts are prorated based on the amount appropriated for the program and each investor's share of total state tax credits received by all investors in County biotechnology businesses. Exact amounts vary. The county typically pays out grants between March and May for investments made in the previous calendar year.

structured_extraction.program_name: J.O.B.S. (Jobs, Opportunities and Business Support) Initiative – Job Creation Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: A $20 million economic development initiative from Montgomery County that creates three complementary funds: a $10 million Job Creation Fund, a $7 million Innovation Fund, and a $3 million Equity Fund. The Job Creation Fund offers grants to employers in Montgomery County to help companies grow and expand by hiring new workers. Eligible companies can receive $10,000 per new job created, or $12,000 per job if the business is in a designated Community Equity Index disadvantaged area, with a maximum award of $500,000 per company.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Three funds totaling $20 million: a $10 million Job Creation Fund, a $7 million Innovation Fund, and a $3 million Equity Fund. Under the Job Creation Fund, eligible companies receive $10,000 per new qualifying job created, or $12,000 per job if located in a Community Equity Index disadvantaged area. The total award per company cannot exceed $500,000.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Employers located in Montgomery County, including company headquarters, national nonprofit organizations, and businesses in target industries such as Life Sciences, Advanced Technology, Cybersecurity, Quantum Computing, and Hospitality seeking job creation and innovation support.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Job creation, innovation, and equity-focused economic development activities. Grant funds support business growth and expansion connected to hiring new employees.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. Companies located in Community Equity Index disadvantaged areas receive a higher award amount per job.
requirements_list: Must be a company headquarters, a national nonprofit organization, or operate in a target industry (Life Sciences, Advanced Technology, Cybersecurity, Quantum Computing, Hospitality).
Must create at least five new full-time, permanent jobs within twelve months of applying.
Each new job must have a base annual salary of $100,000, not including benefits.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application to the Montgomery County Department of Finance, stating the number of qualifying jobs you plan to create and the hiring schedule. The submission date starts a 12-month period during which you must hire at least 5 qualifying employees. An additional 6 months is available to hire positions beyond the initial five.

structured_extraction.program_description: The HUD-VASH program combines Housing Choice Voucher rental assistance for homeless veterans with case management and clinical services provided by the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA). The VA provides services at VA medical centers and community-based outreach clinics, and screens and refers veterans to the Housing Authority. The program is available in both Montgomery County (administered through the Housing Opportunities Commission) and Prince George's County (administered through the Prince George's County Housing Authority), helping homeless veterans with severe psychiatric or substance abuse disorders obtain and maintain stable housing.

The VA screens and refers veterans to the local Housing Authority, which administers the vouchers. Services are delivered at VA medical centers and community-based outreach clinics.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental assistance for housing, combined with case management and clinical services provided by the VA.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County and Prince George's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a veteran
Must be homeless
Must have severe psychiatric or substance abuse disorder (Montgomery County)
Must be screened and referred by the VA
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The VA screens veterans and makes referrals to the local Housing Authority (Housing Opportunities Commission in Montgomery County or Prince George's County Housing Authority). Veterans do not apply directly; they must be referred through the VA. Montgomery County applicants may also apply through the HOC Housing Path Portal or contact HOC directly.

structured_extraction.program_description: NHS Baltimore offers one-on-one financial coaching to help Baltimore City residents strengthen their finances and build long-term financial stability. structured_extraction.program_description: Neighborhood Housing Services (NHS) of Baltimore offers affordable, flexible in-house mortgage programs to help Baltimore City residents purchase homes. The NHS Mortgage Plus program provides fixed-rate mortgages with no mortgage insurance required, low down payment options, competitive interest rates, reduced or eliminated private mortgage insurance (PMI), lower closing costs, and access to grants and deferred loans. The program is available to buyers earning under 80% of Area Median Income (AMI) or those purchasing in a low-to-moderate income census tract. Applicants work with licensed NHS mortgage loan originators with local expertise who can connect borrowers with down payment assistance and other resources to make homeownership more accessible and affordable. The loan is paired with a full suite of homebuying support services, including educational workshops, financial coaching, and access to NHS-rehabbed homes in the community, providing a seamless, one-stop homebuying experience. Borrowers must complete pre-purchase homebuyer education and counseling. Personalized, one-on-one guidance from certified mortgage professionals is available throughout the process.

The loan is paired with comprehensive support services including homebuyer education workshops, financial coaching, and access to NHS-rehabbed homes for sale throughout the community. Borrowers must complete pre-purchase homebuyer education and counseling. One-on-one support from certified mortgage professionals helps lower monthly costs.
