structured_extraction.program_name: NHS of Baltimore HUD-Certified Homebuyer Education and Counseling
structured_extraction.program_description: Neighborhood Housing Services of Baltimore (NHS) offers a HUD-certified homebuyer education workshop and one-on-one counseling to help residents — including first-time homebuyers, self-employed individuals, freelancers, gig workers, and small business owners — prepare for homeownership. The program teaches participants everything they need to know about the home buying process, including how to qualify for down payment assistance, how to find a home within their budget, mortgage and real estate terms, how to choose a lender, loan documentation requirements, budgeting, credit, debt management, home maintenance, protecting your home investment, and what to expect at closing. Participants can choose from multiple formats: a one-day six-hour virtual or in-person Saturday session (9:00 AM–3:00 PM), two three-hour virtual Thursday evening sessions (5:00 PM–8:00 PM), or a self-paced online course. Upon completion, participants earn a HUD-certified Homebuyer Education Certificate required by most down payment and closing cost assistance programs at the city and state level. NHS also provides free one-on-one counseling with a HUD-certified and NeighborWorks-certified NHS Homeownership Advisor who creates a personalized homebuying action plan, reviews mortgage options, financing choices, document preparation, credit, budgeting, closing costs, loan estimates, and long-term homeownership planning, and connects clients with trusted lenders and realtors. Completing the workshop and a counseling session is required before putting a contract on a property to remain eligible for most down payment and closing cost assistance programs. The program also connects participants with local resources and special incentive programs to support homeownership.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: HUD-certified homebuyer education workshops available in multiple formats: a one-day six-hour Saturday session (virtual or in-person, 9:00 AM–3:00 PM), two-part Thursday evening sessions (5:00 PM–8:00 PM), or a self-paced online course. Participants also have access to free one-on-one counseling sessions with a HUD-certified and NeighborWorks-certified NHS Homeownership Advisor covering mortgage options, financing choices, document preparation, credit review, budgeting, closing costs, loan estimates, closing disclosures, and long-term homeownership planning, as well as connections to trusted lenders and realtors. Graduates receive a HUD-certified Homebuyer Education Certificate required by most down payment and closing cost assistance programs at the city and state level. Completing both the workshop and a counseling session is required before placing a contract on a property. The program also provides access to special incentive programs and local resources to help people buy a home.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City residents — especially first-time homebuyers, self-employed individuals, freelancers, gig workers, and small business owners — preparing to buy a home and qualify for down payment and closing cost assistance programs. One-on-one counseling is designed for homebuyers who have completed a HUD-certified homebuyer education workshop, have at least $3,000 in savings, and a credit score of 640 or higher.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Homebuyer education and counseling to prepare for mortgage application and homeownership, including understanding closing costs, loan estimates, budgeting, credit and debt management, home maintenance, and protecting your home investment, and to earn the certificate required for down payment and closing cost assistance programs. One-on-one counseling provides guidance on financing options, lender and realtor connections, personalized homebuying action planning, and access to special incentive programs and local resources.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Primarily serving Baltimore City residents and prospective homebuyers in Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Must be a prospective homebuyer or Baltimore City resident preparing to purchase a home
Must complete a homebuyer education workshop
Must complete a counseling session
Both must be completed before placing a contract on a property to remain eligible for most down payment and closing cost assistance programs
Completion of HUD-approved course required to access certain down payment assistance programs
Enrollment in a scheduled workshop session required
For one-on-one counseling: must have completed a HUD-certified homebuyer education workshop (through NHS Baltimore or a partner organization)
For one-on-one counseling: at least $3,000 in savings
For one-on-one counseling: credit score of 640 or higher
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the online registration form on the NHS Baltimore website at https://www.nhsbaltimore.org/homebuyers-education-workshop/ or visit https://www.nhsbaltimore.org/become-a-homeowner/ to find your starting point. Alternatively, create an account and sign up for services online at nhsbaltimore.force.com/nhsbaltimorecft. Choose a session format that fits your schedule (Saturday 9 AM–3 PM, two-part Thursday evenings 5–8 PM, or self-paced online). Gather financial documents ahead of time. After submitting registration, NHS intake staff will contact you to confirm. One-on-one counseling is available alongside or after the workshop — complete the online Homebuyer Counseling Registration Form at https://www.nhsbaltimore.org/homebuyers-counseling/ to schedule a one-on-one appointment with an NHS Homeownership Advisor. After submission, an intake team member will contact you with next steps.

structured_extraction.program_name: NHS of Baltimore Home Repair and Renovation Assistance
structured_extraction.program_description: NHS of Baltimore partners with the Baltimore City Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) and other community organizations to help homeowners fund major home repairs and renovations. The program targets homeowners facing financial hardship, including those on fixed incomes, helping them restore and remain in their homes.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: NHS coordinates multiple funding sources to cover major home repair costs. Documented cases include over $100,000 invested to fully renovate a fire-damaged home and approximately $150,000 in repairs for another property, with NHS and partners covering the majority of costs and the family financing the remaining balance over time.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore homeowners facing significant repair needs, particularly those on fixed incomes, the disabled, or those without insurance coverage
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Major home repairs and renovations, including fire damage restoration, roof repair, and bringing properties back to habitable condition
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City
requirements_list: Must be a homeowner in Baltimore City
Home must require significant repair or rehabilitation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Homeowners contact NHS Baltimore for an assessment of repair needs. NHS then works with city agencies and community partners to identify and assemble funding sources for the necessary repairs.

structured_extraction.program_name: NHS of Baltimore Homeownership Assistance Program
structured_extraction.program_description: NHS of Baltimore helps Baltimore residents become first-time homeowners by providing homebuyer education workshops, financial coaching, one-on-one housing counseling, mortgage products, and access to down payment assistance programs. The program helps people improve their credit, build savings, and secure affordable home financing.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: NHS provides first mortgage products combined with local and federal down payment assistance (DPA) programs. In at least one documented case, a homebuyer received over $70,000 in down payment assistance. Services include homebuyer education workshops, financial coaching, and one-on-one counseling.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home purchase, down payment, and closing costs

Participate in financial coaching
Complete one-on-one housing counseling
Obtain mortgage pre-approval

structured_extraction.program_description: Helps existing NHS of Baltimore borrowers manage their home improvement or mortgage loans. Borrowers can view loan details, check payment history, and request assistance online or by phone.

NHS first mortgage customers can receive up to $15,000, while lender partner customers receive $5,000. The loan carries 0% interest and is repayable upon sale or refinance of the home.

Complete one-on-one homebuyer counseling
Have a signed purchase contract
Have a pre-approval letter from a lender
Purchase must be in Baltimore City

structured_extraction.program_name: Rehab Home Improvement Loan (including Rapid Rehab / RHIP)
structured_extraction.program_description: A loan program offered by Neighborhood Housing Services (NHS) of Baltimore providing affordable financing for home repair and renovation projects for Baltimore City homeowners. The program includes two primary options: (1) The Rapid Rehab / Rapid Home Improvement Program (RHIP) provides up to $20,000 at a fixed 6% interest rate for up to 10 years for any home renovation or energy-efficient repair project — including leaking roofs, aging systems, urgent safety issues, or essential systems failures — with funds available within approximately 30 days, no home equity or appraisal required, no income limit, and a minimum credit score of 680. Homeowners manage their own contractors and project timelines under this option. This option is especially designed for new homeowners facing urgent, time-sensitive repairs in the early years of ownership. Monthly ACH payment is optional. (2) The standard Rehab Home Improvement Loan offers up to $30,000 at 0%–6% interest for larger, more complex home repair and rehabilitation projects — such as roofing, heating, plumbing, or electrical work — for homeowners earning up to 120% of Area Median Income (AMI), repayable over up to 20 years. Repayment schedule is based on ability to repay; payments may be deferred until sale of home. Funds are released in stages as work is completed and inspected, and NHS counselors provide hands-on support throughout the project, including help reviewing contractor bids, selecting contractors, and managing project timelines. Both new and long-time homeowners can apply, including those with limited or non-traditional credit history.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans up to $20,000 (Rapid Rehab/RHIP: fixed 6% interest rate, repayable over up to 10 years, no home equity or appraisal required, funds available within approximately 30 days, no income limit, minimum credit score of 680, must have a bank account, must be continuously employed for at least 1 year, monthly ACH payment optional; homeowners manage their own contractors and project from start to finish; designed for urgent, time-sensitive repairs affecting safety, habitability, or essential home systems) or up to $30,000 (Rehab Home Improvement Loan: 0%–6% interest, repayable over up to 20 years, for larger or more complex projects, for homeowners earning up to 120% AMI; repayment schedule based on ability to repay, payments may be deferred until sale of home; no banking requirement; no minimum credit score but credit is reviewed; funds released in stages as work is inspected). Eligible uses include kitchen or bathroom upgrades, roof or window replacements, plumbing or electrical fixes, accessibility modifications, structural improvements, whole-home energy efficiency upgrades, and other major home improvement projects. The standard loan option includes personalized support from NHS Rehab Specialists to review bids, select contractors, and manage project timelines.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City homeowners — both new homeowners (especially those facing urgent repair needs in the early years of ownership) and long-time ('seasoned') homeowners — including those earning up to 120% of Area Median Income (AMI) and those needing urgent, time-sensitive repairs to safety, habitability, or essential home systems. Also includes homeowners seeking quick financing for smaller repairs and upgrades, including those with limited or non-traditional credit history and new homeowners without equity.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Any home renovation project or energy-efficient repairs, including roof or foundation repairs, full kitchen or bath renovations, structural improvements, whole-home energy efficiency upgrades, major repairs such as roofing, heating, plumbing, or electrical work, aging systems, urgent safety-related updates, window replacements, accessibility modifications, and other major home improvement projects. Also covers urgent, time-sensitive repairs that affect safety, habitability, or essential home systems (e.g., structural concerns or failures in systems needed for daily living). Not for purely cosmetic upgrades or elective renovations under the RHIP option.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must reside in and own property in Baltimore City, Maryland, and use the property as primary residence.
requirements_list: Must be a Baltimore City homeowner and use property as primary residence
Minimum credit score of 680 (Rapid Rehab/RHIP)
Continuously employed for at least one year (Rapid Rehab)
Property taxes, water bill, and mortgage (if any) must be current
No home equity or appraisal required (Rapid Rehab)
No income limits apply (Rapid Rehab)
Repairs must be time-sensitive and affect safety, habitability, or essential home systems (RHIP)
Must have a bank account (Rapid Rehab)
Must demonstrate ability to repay the loan
Must provide proof of income for all household members (most recent paystub with year-to-date income or award letters)
Self-employed applicants must provide federal tax returns from the last 2 years
Must provide bank statements (last 3 months)
Must provide copy of homeowner's insurance declarations page
Must provide copy of photo ID (e.g., driver's license)
Must provide proof of homeownership (recorded deed, property tax bill, or mortgage statement)
Must provide written estimates from licensed contractors
Must earn no more than 120% of Area Median Income (AMI) (Rehab Home Improvement Loan)
Must work with a licensed contractor (Rehab Home Improvement Loan)
Credit reviewed (no minimum score required for standard Rehab Home Improvement Loan)
No medical collections over $1,000 (standard Rehab Home Improvement Loan)
No judgments or liens (standard Rehab Home Improvement Loan)
Must provide recent mortgage statement
U.S. citizenship required
Credit report authorization required
NHS reserves the right to inspect work
Specific eligibility requirements available at https://www.nhsbaltimore.org/eligibility-rehab-loans/
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at NHSbaltimore.org through the NHS customer portal or loan application portal by submitting details about your home, the repairs needed, and your goals. A paper application may also be downloaded and submitted. You may also complete the inquiry form on the program page or contact NHS of Baltimore to review repair needs and eligibility. Applications may also be submitted by email at lendingadvisor@nhsbaltimore.com or intake@nhsbaltimore.com, or by mail to 25 E. 20th Street, Suite 170, Baltimore, MD 21218. To request a mailed application, email intake@nhsbaltimore.com or call 410-327-1200 ext. 104. Applicants may also pay for a credit report online through the NHS portal. Complete application form with all supporting documents including required documentation checklist items; authorization for credit checks and income verification is required. For the Rapid Rehab/RHIP option: (1) Confirm you are a Baltimore City homeowner and that your repairs are time-sensitive and affect safety or habitability. (2) Gather required documents: proof of income, proof of homeownership, bank statements, homeowner's insurance declarations page, photo ID, and written contractor estimates. (3) Apply through the NHS customer portal and receive approval with funds available within approximately 30 days; homeowners then manage their own contractors and project timelines. (4) Stay engaged and responsive during the loan review process. For the standard Rehab Home Improvement Loan, after applying, work with an NHS Rehab Specialist who will help review contractor bids and manage the project. Full eligibility details are available at nhsbaltimore.org/eligibility-rehab-loans/.

structured_extraction.program_name: Reinvest Baltimore Down Payment Assistance (DPA) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A down payment assistance program designed to increase homeownership opportunities in Baltimore City neighborhoods that are part of the Baltimore Vacants Reinvestment Initiative (BVRI) and UPLIFT redevelopment efforts. NHS Baltimore administers the program on behalf of the Maryland Community Investment Corporation (MCIC), providing forgivable loans to qualified homebuyers purchasing redeveloped properties in designated BVRI areas.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $20,000 per homebuyer as a five-year forgivable loan at 0% interest, with 20% of the principal forgiven annually over five years. The borrower must occupy the home as their primary residence. Only fixed-rate mortgages are permitted (cash sales and owner financing are not allowed). There are no household income restrictions and the program is not limited to first-time homebuyers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualified homebuyers purchasing properties that are part of BVRI-funded or UPLIFT-funded redevelopment efforts within designated BVRI areas in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment assistance for the purchase of a home located within a BVRI-funded or UPLIFT-funded project in designated BVRI areas in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties must be located within BVRI-funded or UPLIFT-funded project areas in designated BVRI neighborhoods in Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Borrower must occupy the home as their primary residence
Property must be located within a BVRI-funded or UPLIFT-funded project in designated BVRI areas
Pre-purchase housing counseling is required
Fixed-rate mortgage only — cash sales and owner financing are not permitted
No household income restrictions
Not limited to first-time homebuyers
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact NHS Baltimore for more information and eligibility requirements at www.nhsbaltimore.org/nhs-dpa. Pre-purchase housing counseling is required as part of participation.

Homeowners on three blocks in the Walbrook and Panway neighborhoods received grants for exterior home improvements to stimulate block-wide enhancements and build a stronger community.

structured_extraction.program_name: Neighborhood Impact Investment Fund (NIIF) Direct Loans
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides direct loans for development projects in Baltimore City. It helps fund projects at any stage, including buying property, planning, construction, and long-term financing. The program supports housing, commercial development, community facilities, and mixed-use projects.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers several types of loans up to $3 million, including acquisition, construction, bridge, and term loans. Predevelopment loans are available for up to $100,000. Interest rates begin at 5.0% and are subject to review. Loan terms vary by type, ranging from 18 months to 7 years. The program may provide subordinate debt to fill funding gaps.
structured_extraction.program_audience: This program is for developers, including small businesses and non-profits, working on real estate projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can pay for various project costs. These include buying vacant land or buildings. You can also use funds for predevelopment costs like engineering and design. The loans also cover construction, adaptive reuse, and major renovations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in specific, pre-defined Eligible Neighborhoods within Baltimore City. An interactive map on the program website shows these areas.
requirements_list: Commitment fee of $5,000
Origination fee up to 1.50% of the loan amount
Loans generally require a first or second lien on the property as collateral
Loan-to-value (LTV) ratios apply and vary by loan type, typically up to 90-95%
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, use the program's interactive map to confirm your project is in an eligible neighborhood. Next, decide which financing option fits your needs. Finally, complete and submit the online intake form.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing

structured_extraction.program_description: A financial rewards program that provides monthly subsidies to commuters who form new carpools or vanpools. New carpool arrangements (2–4 people) earn $130 per month for the first three months, and new vanpool arrangements (5–12 people) earn $200 per month for the entire length of the vehicle lease. The program is administered through Commuter Connections in the Washington D.C. region and is available to commuters in Prince George's County.

Must enroll in the 'Pool Rewards program through commuterconnections.org
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Find co-commuters using the Commuter Connections ridematching site or app, then enroll in the 'Pool Rewards program at commuterconnections.org.

structured_extraction.program_description: The ACCU program helps HealthChoice (Medicaid managed care) members understand their benefits, choose a Managed Care Organization (MCO), find doctors and dentists, access transportation and community resources, resolve complaints, billing issues, and navigate the Medicaid renewal process. Staff act as advocates for health care needs and coordinate care with MCOs, including explaining appeal and grievance rights.

Services include: help understanding HealthChoice benefits and MCO choices; finding primary care doctors, specialists, and dentists; linking to transportation services; prescription assistance; explaining out-of-network services and referral requirements; Medicaid renewal assistance; billing issue resolution; and appeal and grievance support. No cost to participants.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Care coordination, benefits navigation, provider location, complaint and billing resolution, appeal and grievance support, and advocacy for HealthChoice members

structured_extraction.program_description: AERS provides free comprehensive evaluations to county residents who are functionally or chronically ill and at risk of being placed in an institution. A nurse or social worker visits the client at home or their current location to assess health history, mental health, family support, and financial situation, then develops an individualized Plan of Care with service and resource recommendations to help the person stay independent in the least restrictive environment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free in-home or on-site comprehensive evaluations conducted by a nurse or social worker. The evaluation results in an individualized Plan of Care with recommendations for home and community-based services to help avoid institutionalization. There is no cost to the client.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Comprehensive evaluation to identify home and community-based services that allow individuals to remain independent and avoid institutionalization.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Prince George's County, Maryland.

Must be at risk of institutionalization
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Referrals can be made by physicians, other county agencies, religious organizations, or any concerned individual by phone, fax, or email. Call 301-856-4730 Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Housing Authority of Prince George's County (HAPGC) provides tax-exempt bond financing that generates 4% Federal Low-Income Housing Tax Credits (LIHTC) for multifamily rental housing projects. The program supports for-profit and non-profit developers building or preserving affordable rental housing for low-to-moderate income individuals, families, and seniors across Prince George's County, including new construction, adaptive reuse, and preservation of existing units. The program seeks to finance higher density, multifamily housing in transit-oriented, mixed-use communities with easy access to jobs.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax-exempt and/or taxable bond financing for acquisition, rehabilitation, or new construction of affordable multifamily rental housing (5+ units). Eligible projects may qualify for 4% Low Income Housing Tax Credits. Includes construction and permanent financing, conduit financing (limited liability, non-recourse obligations), as well as refinancing and refunding options. Projects rated AA or higher by major rating agencies are eligible; unrated privately-placed transactions are also financed.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit and non-profit developers, governmental entities, and owners of multifamily rental housing serving low-to-moderate income individuals, families, and seniors in Prince George's County, as well as project owners seeking refinancing or ownership transfers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: New construction of multifamily developments; acquisition and substantial rehabilitation of existing multifamily developments; development costs including professional fees, architect fees, and builder fees; refinancing and refunding of existing projects; compliance monitoring and administrative expenses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in Prince George's County, Maryland. Priority areas include Inner Beltway Communities, Regional Transit Districts (areas around Metro stops at Largo Town Center, New Carrollton, Prince George's Plaza, Branch Avenue, Suitland), Opportunity Zones, and Designated Development Areas such as Westphalia.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a private for-profit or non-profit developer/owner, or governmental entity
Project must be a multifamily rental housing development (minimum 5 units)
Project must serve low-to-moderate income individuals, families, or seniors
At least 20% of units rented to households at or below 50% AMI OR 40% of units at or below 60% AMI
Maximum rent capped at 30% of Area Median Income (utilities included)
Property must remain in affordable rental use for minimum 15 years
Non-transient use only (minimum 1-year leases)
No discrimination in tenant selection based on protected class status
Units must be proportionally representative of bedroom mix; no clustering
Annual audited financial statements required
Monthly occupancy and compliance reports required
Prior HAPGC approval required for ownership transfers
New owners must assume all prior obligations
Payment of assumption fees and professional fees required
Compliance monitoring fee payment required until expiration of Qualified Project Period
Deed restrictions must remain in force for at least 15 years
Developer fee limits per Exhibit D guidelines
QAP requirements compliance (rents, vacancy, operating expenses, reserves, debt service coverage ratios)
Capital needs assessment required for replacement reserves
Operating reserve requirements (3-6 months of expenses)
Project must be located in Prince George's County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact HAPGC for more information. Tax-exempt bond authority is allocated on a first-come-first-served basis. Application materials include Form 202 (Multifamily Rental Financing Application) and Form 203 (Developer's and Sponsor's/Owner's Qualifications). Refer to the Rental Housing Guide and Term Sheet and Financing Guide for program details.

Annual application and proof of claim must be filed with the Director of Finance

structured_extraction.program_description: This program helps Prince George's County residents understand the risks of alcohol and drug use. It offers free education and outreach services to residents, schools, and community groups, including prescription drug take-back events, family strengthening initiatives, naloxone training, tobacco youth ambassador training, and public awareness campaigns.

All services are free of charge.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Prince George's County residents, including youth and families, seeking education and support around alcohol, drug, and tobacco use prevention.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Education, outreach, and prevention services related to alcohol, drug, and tobacco use.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Prince George's County resident.
requirements_list: Must be a Prince George's County resident
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 301-883-7828 to schedule an appointment. Services are available Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

structured_extraction.program_description: An elective partnership between Prince George's County and qualified tax-exempt faith-based organizations or 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations to improve water quality by treating and reducing polluted stormwater runoff. Participating organizations can qualify for a reduction in a portion of their Clean Water Act Fee (the impervious area fee) by choosing one or more of three options: providing a property easement for stormwater best management practices (50% fee reduction), participating in outreach and education activities (25% fee reduction), or adopting green care and good housekeeping practices (25% fee reduction).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Qualified organizations can receive a reduction on the impervious area portion of their Clean Water Act Fee. Option 1 (Easement) provides a 50% fee reduction; Option 2 (Outreach & Education) provides a 25% fee reduction; Option 3 (Green Care & Good Housekeeping) provides a 25% fee reduction. Options can be combined. The administrative fee ($20.58 per tax account annually) cannot be waived.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Tax-exempt faith-based organizations and 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations located in Prince George's County that pay the Clean Water Act Fee.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Fee reduction on the impervious area portion of the Clean Water Act Fee in exchange for stormwater runoff reduction activities, education outreach, or good housekeeping practices.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to property owners in Prince George's County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a tax-exempt faith-based organization or a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization
Must agree to participate in at least one of three program options

Option 1: Provide a Temporary Right-of-Entry Agreement and Temporary Construction Easement to the County; sign a Maintenance Agreement and maintain installed BMPs; subject to triennial inspection by the Department of the Environment

Option 2: Participate in the County's education and outreach campaign and/or host one annual activity such as a Rain Check Rebate Program, recycling event, trash pick-up event, or planting at least 5 trees on-site

Option 3: Use lawn and landscaping companies certified in fertilizer application (listed in Maryland Department of Agriculture's pesticide database) and/or commit to at least 3 good housekeeping practices
Must submit CWAF Reduction Request Form for Alternative Compliance Application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Select the option(s) you wish to participate in, complete and digitally sign the application form, then submit online and mail it to the Prince George's County Department of the Environment, Stormwater Management Division, 1801 McCormick Drive, Suite 500, Largo, MD 20774. Step 2: Meet with the County's agent to develop an alternative compliance plan and finalize which options are feasible. Step 3: Submit the written alternative compliance plan to the Department of the Environment (DoE). DoE reviews the plan and determines the fee credit amount. Additionally, submit the CWAF Reduction Request Form for Alternative Compliance Application.

structured_extraction.program_name: Alternative Energy/Energy Conservation Tax Credit (Prince George's County Solar and Geothermal Residential Property Tax Credit)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides a property tax credit for residential structures in Prince George's County that utilize solar energy or geothermal energy devices. Residential property owners who install solar or geothermal systems may apply for a reduction in County property taxes by filing an application and proof of claim with the Director of Finance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property tax credit for residential structures in Prince George's County that utilize solar energy or geothermal energy devices. Application and proof of claim must be filed with the Director of Finance to claim the credit.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of residential structures that use solar energy or geothermal energy devices in Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of County property taxes for residential properties with solar or geothermal energy installations, including installation of solar energy systems and geothermal energy systems.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Property must be a residential structure in Prince George's County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a residential structure
Must utilize solar energy or geothermal energy devices
Must file application and proof of claim with the Director of Finance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: File an application and proof of claim with the Director of Finance. Visit the Prince George's County Finance Department property tax credits page or the Sustainable Energy Resources page for details.

structured_extraction.program_name: American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) - Coronavirus Local Fiscal Recovery Fund (CLFRF) for Prince George's County
structured_extraction.program_description: Prince George's County received $176,626,110 from the federal Coronavirus Local Fiscal Recovery Fund (CLFRF) under the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021. These funds help the county respond to the COVID-19 public health emergency, address its economic impacts, support essential workers, replace lost government revenue, and invest in water, sewer, and broadband infrastructure.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Prince George's County received $176,626,110 in two equal tranches from the federal CLFRF. Funds must be obligated by December 31, 2024 and spent by December 31, 2026. Eligible uses include COVID-19 response, premium pay or grants for essential workers, government services to offset revenue loss, and infrastructure investments in water, sewer, or broadband.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Funds must be obligated by December 31, 2024 and spent by December 31, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Prince George's County government and community stakeholders responding to COVID-19 impacts
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: COVID-19 public health emergency response; economic impact assistance; premium pay or grants for essential workers; government services to offset revenue reduction; water, sewer, or broadband infrastructure investments
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Funds may not be used to offset a reduction in net tax revenue due to a change in law from March 3, 2021 through the last day of the fiscal year in which funds are spent
Funds may not be deposited into a pension fund
Funds may not be used for debt service costs, legal settlements, or judgments
Funds may not be deposited into a rainy day fund or financial reserves
Expenditures must be obligated by December 31, 2024
Expenditures must be spent by December 31, 2026
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Community members and stakeholders can provide feedback and recommendations by completing the online ARPA feedback form on the county website or emailing ARPAFeedback@co.pg.md.us. The County Council reviews and approves the spending plan.

structured_extraction.program_name: Andrews Federal Credit Union Furlough Relief Programs
structured_extraction.program_description: Andrews Federal Credit Union offers several financial assistance programs to help federal employees cope with furloughs or other employment disruptions, including short-term loans, payment deferrals, emergency counseling, and personal consumer loans.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Furlough Relief Loans: short-term, low-interest loans for essential expenses. Loan Payment Deferrals: defer payments on existing Andrews Federal loans without penalty. Emergency Relief Assistance: personalized financial counseling and hardship support. Personal Consumer Loans: competitive rates and flexible terms for affected federal employees.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Federal employees impacted by furloughs or employment disruptions
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Essential expenses during missed pay periods; existing loan payments
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to members of Andrews Federal Credit Union
requirements_list: Must be a federal employee affected by furlough or employment disruption
Must be an Andrews Federal Credit Union member or eligible to join
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Andrews Federal at 1-800-487-5500, visit www.andrewsfcu.org, or stop by a branch location to discuss available options and eligibility requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program seeks to increase the number of native trees and shrubs planted in Prince George's County by providing free native trees and shrubs to schools to plant and maintain on school grounds. It educates students about the everyday importance of native trees, empowers them to improve their community, and provides funds for planting projects on schoolyards.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free program for participating schools. Assistance includes selecting tree planting locations on school campus, developing a tree planting plan, creating a post-planting maintenance schedule, purchasing and arranging delivery of trees and materials, and providing technical and design assistance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public schools and their staff and students in Prince George's County interested in planting native trees on their grounds.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchasing and arranging delivery of trees and materials, plant care and storage, and supporting tree planting projects on school grounds.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to public schools located in Prince George's County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Submit an Intent to Apply Form
Schedule a consultation with the Program Coordinator
Submit a Program Application
Tree planting must occur in spring or fall (not summer)
School principal approval required
Facility manager approval required
Project organizer must commit to 2-year maintenance plan following tree planting
Staff or volunteers must participate in planting
Maintenance tasks include: watering trees every 7 days during dry periods, weeding and mulching up to 2 times per year, pruning
Utility line marking by MISS Utility required
PGCPS Request for Building approval required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Submit the Intent to Apply Form (PDF). 2. The Program Coordinator will contact you to schedule a required consultation. 3. During the consultation, you will receive guidance on completing the Program Application, developing a tree planting plan, and creating a post-planting maintenance plan. 4. Submit the Program Application.

structured_extraction.program_description: Prince George's County's Art in Public Places (AIPP) program dedicates at least 1% of construction costs for new or significantly renovated County civic buildings to acquiring and installing public artwork. The program creates opportunities for artists, promotes art and culture in the county, and visually enhances public spaces for residents.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: At least 1% of construction costs of eligible County civic building projects is allocated to the acquisition and installation of artwork. Artists are selected through a formal selection process.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Artists seeking opportunities to create and install public artwork in Prince George's County civic buildings and public spaces.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition and installation of public artwork in County civic buildings and public spaces.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available for projects located in Prince George's County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Artwork must be intended for installation in new County civic buildings or major renovations of County civic buildings.
Artists are selected through the AIPP selection process.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Artwork selection is conducted through a formal selection process. Visit the Art Selection Process page for details.

structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore Gas and Electric (BGE) provides expanded bill payment support options to customers impacted by the federal government shutdown to help manage energy costs and avoid service disconnection.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Multiple payment arrangements, budget billing plans, 30-day late payment charge waivers (granted in increments), due-date extensions, and connections to state assistance programs and the Fuel Fund of Maryland.
structured_extraction.program_audience: BGE customers impacted by the federal government shutdown, including federal workers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy bill payment relief and management.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: BGE service territory in Maryland

No government ID required to access support measures
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact BGE's Customer Care team at 1-800-685-0123 or visit bge.com/heretohelp for information on available support measures.

structured_extraction.program_name: BGE Electric Vehicle Charging Pilot Program
structured_extraction.program_description: BGE offers rebates and incentives to residential and multifamily property customers to help offset the cost of adopting electric vehicles and installing electric vehicle charging stations. Residential customers can receive up to $300, and multifamily property managers, owners, and homeowners associations can receive up to $25,000 for installing Level 2 smart chargers or DC fast chargers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Residential customers can receive rebates and incentives up to $300 for adopting an electric vehicle and installing a charger. Multifamily property managers, owners, and homeowners associations may be eligible for incentives up to $25,000 for installing Level 2 smart chargers or DC fast chargers on their properties.
structured_extraction.program_audience: BGE residential customers and multifamily property managers, owners, and homeowners associations in Prince George's County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Adoption of electric vehicles and installation of Level 2 smart chargers or DC fast chargers at residential or multifamily properties
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to BGE customers, including those in Prince George's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a BGE customer
Multifamily: must be a property manager, owner, or homeowners association installing Level 2 smart chargers or DC fast chargers
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the BGE EVsmart page to learn more and apply for rebates and incentives.

structured_extraction.program_description: Back on Track is a Problem-Solving Court in Prince George's County that helps first-time, low-level felony offenders avoid future criminal behavior. Participants plead guilty and complete a 12-to-18-month program that includes community service, mental health support, education, career training, and leadership development. Those who successfully complete the program may have their records expunged.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive a structured 12-to-18-month program including community service, mental health support, education, industry-recognized certifications, career training, employment placement, and leadership development. Successful completion makes participants eligible for record expungement.
structured_extraction.program_audience: First-time, low-level felony offenders who are verified residents of Prince George's County with no prior felony or violent convictions and not currently under community supervision.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Program services include community service, mental health support, education and certifications, career training, employment placement, and leadership development leading to potential record expungement.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a verified resident of Prince George's County, Maryland.
requirements_list: No prior felony or violent convictions
No prior felony convictions for drug or gun offenses
No prior violent misdemeanor convictions
Not currently under community supervision in any jurisdiction
Not found to be drug dependent
Verified resident of Prince George's County, Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligibility is determined through a structured screening and review process. Contact the Program Coordinator for information about eligibility and referrals.

structured_extraction.program_description: The BRAC Zone program focuses residential population growth from military base realignment in designated growth areas and provides local governments with financial assistance for public infrastructure. It aligns state resources and programs to local governments and businesses located in BRAC Zones to coordinate state support for growth in those areas following the 2005 Base Realignment and Closure (BRAC) process. The program pays a portion of real property tax increments on qualified properties within defined BRAC Zones and supports repayment of bonds, including Tax Increment Financing bonds, issued for infrastructure improvements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Local jurisdictions receive: (1) payment of 100% of the state real property tax increment on qualified properties, and (2) payment equal to 50% of the local jurisdiction's real property tax increment on qualified properties. Benefits are available for 10 years from the time the first project in the zone is designated as a qualified property. Funds must be used for infrastructure improvements and can be used to pay back bonds, including Tax Increment Financing (TIF) bonds issued for infrastructure improvements.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments and jurisdictions within designated BRAC Zones in Prince George's County that are accommodating growth from U.S. military installation expansions following the 2005 Base Realignment and Closure process.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Public infrastructure improvements, including repayment of bonds and Tax Increment Financing (TIF) bonds issued for infrastructure projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available within designated BRAC Zones in Prince George's County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local jurisdiction within a designated BRAC Zone.
Properties must be designated as qualified properties under the program.
Funds must be used for infrastructure improvements.
Benefits are available for 10 years from the time the first project in the zone is designated as a qualified property.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Economic Development Corporation at 301-583-4650 and ask to speak with a Business Development Specialist. Additional details are available through the Maryland Department of Commerce or the Maryland Department of Business and Economic Development.

structured_extraction.program_name: Best Friends Grant – Remaining County Zip Codes
structured_extraction.program_description: Grant funding through Best Friends Animal Society to cover the cost of spaying and neutering feral cats in Prince George's County zip codes not covered by other TNVR grants. Residents contact The Spay Spot clinic and charge the cost to the grant.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free or subsidized spay/neuter services for feral cats in Prince George's County zip codes not covered by other grants, charged to 'The Best Friends Grant' at The Spay Spot clinic.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents of Prince George's County zip codes not covered by other TNVR grants who wish to spay/neuter feral cats.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Spay/neuter services for feral cats in Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Prince George's County residents in zip codes not covered by other TNVR grants listed on this page.
requirements_list: Cats must be feral
Zip code must not be covered by another TNVR grant on this page
Must mention 'The Best Friends Grant' when scheduling at The Spay Spot
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call The Spay Spot at 301-254-8151 to make a vet appointment and request that feral cat costs be charged to 'The Best Friends Grant.'

structured_extraction.program_name: Boys and Girls Club Property Tax Exemption
structured_extraction.program_description: A real property tax exemption for property owned by a Boys and Girls Club chartered by the Prince George's County Boys and Girls Club, Incorporated.

Annual application and proof of claim must be filed with the Director of Finance by October 1 of the tax year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: File annual application and proof of claim with the Director of Finance by October 1 of the tax year the exemption is sought.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free one-stop center in Prince George's County that connects returning citizens, transitional-aged youth (ages 18–25), and veterans to services and support for a successful transition into the community. Originally supported by a three-year Maryland Department of Health grant (Grant 11-009, $210,000) to the Prince George's Health Department, the program has continued as a county-administered initiative. Services include behavioral health screenings and assessments, case management and referrals, peer support, job training and employment assistance, addiction services, life skills education, parenting development, transportation support, benefits enrollment, Veterans Affairs and claims assistance, anger management courses, child support assistance, mentoring programs, legal help, and vital documents assistance (IDs and birth certificates). The program also connects clients to partner organizations for mental health and substance use treatment, GED and college enrollment, medical care, and family reunification services. The program previously served 82 individuals through 984 visits under the original grant period. There is no cost for any services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free services including behavioral health screenings and assessments, case management and referrals, peer support, job training and employment assistance, transportation support, benefits enrollment, VA and claims assistance, anger management courses, child support assistance, mentoring programs, legal help, and vital documents assistance (IDs and birth certificates). Partner organizations provide mental health and substance use treatment, GED/college enrollment help, medical care, and family reunification services. The program was originally funded by a $210,000 Maryland Department of Health grant (Grant 11-009) supporting staff salaries for behavioral health care, addiction services, life skills education, parenting, employment, and transportation assistance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Prince George's County residents ages 18 and older who are returning citizens, transitional-aged youth (ages 18–25), or veterans; previously also served ex-offenders transitioning back to the community under the original grant program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services are provided directly — not cash or financial assistance. Supports case management, job training, behavioral health services, addiction services, life skills education, parenting development, transportation, benefits enrollment, legal help, and other reentry and community transition services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Prince George's County, Maryland residents only.
requirements_list: Must be a Prince George's County resident
Must be age 18 or older
Must be a returning citizen, transitional-aged youth (ages 18–25), or a veteran
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the Bridge Center at Adam's House at 5001 Silver Hill Road, Suite 300, Suitland, MD 20746, Monday through Friday from 9:00 AM to 4:30 PM. Contact by phone at 301-817-1900 or email at bridgecenter@co.pg.md.us.

structured_extraction.program_description: Bridges2Success is a community-based program that helps young people in Prince George's County who have been referred by the Department of Juvenile Services (DJS). Case managers work with youth to reduce risk factors, strengthen protective factors, connect them to community services, and provide referrals for vocational training and employment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Case managers provide screening, referrals to community-based services, and referrals for vocational training and/or employment. Services are available Monday through Friday, 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM at the Leonard Dyer Health Center in Clinton, Maryland.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Youth residents of Prince George's County who have been referred by the Department of Juvenile Services
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reducing risk factors, enhancing protective factors, linkage to community-based services, and referrals for vocational training and/or employment
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Prince George's County resident
requirements_list: Must be a Prince George's County resident
Must have a referral from the Department of Juvenile Services
Must complete the DJS Intake Information Form
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Referral must come from the Department of Juvenile Services. Applicants complete the DJS Intake Information Form. Contact the D. Leonard Dyer Regional Health Center at 301-856-9400 for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: Helps offset burial expenses for low-income families.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides financial assistance to help low-income families cover burial expenses.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income families needing burial assistance
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Burial expenses
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a low-income family

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides paratransit (door-to-door transit) service to visitors with disabilities who are unable to use accessible fixed-route bus or rail services in Prince George's County. Eligible visitors may use the service for up to 21 days in any rolling 365-day period.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Paratransit transportation service available to visitors with disabilities for up to 21 days in a rolling 365-day period. Visitors apply by having their current paratransit provider or healthcare provider submit verification of disability to the County. Once approved, an authorization letter and service instructions are mailed or emailed to the applicant.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No deadline; rolling applications recommended at least 3 weeks before visit
structured_extraction.program_audience: Visitors to Prince George's County, Maryland who have a disability that prevents them from using accessible fixed-route bus or rail transit, and who hold paratransit eligibility in their home area (or can provide healthcare provider certification of disability).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Paratransit transportation within Prince George's County during the visitor's stay.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to visitors traveling to Prince George's County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a visitor to Prince George's County (not a resident)
Must be unable to use accessible fixed-route bus or rail service due to a disability
Must provide applicant's full name, address, and phone number
Must provide paratransit ID number and expiration date from home area provider (if applicable)
Must provide type of disability
Must provide type of mobility aid used, if applicable
Must indicate if a Personal Care Assistant (PCA) is authorized
Must indicate if a service animal is used
If no home-area paratransit exists, must provide healthcare provider certification of disability
Current paratransit provider or healthcare provider must mail, fax, or email verification to the County office
Recommended to apply at least 3 weeks before the visit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Have your current paratransit provider (or healthcare provider if you have no home-area paratransit) send verification of your disability and required personal information to the Prince George's County Call-A-Bus office by mail, fax, or email. The County will enter you into the system and mail or email an authorization letter with instructions for using the service.

structured_extraction.program_description: Call-A-Cab provides reduced-cost taxi transportation for Prince George's County seniors (age 60+) and people with disabilities. Eligible residents buy coupon books at half price and use them to pay cab fares when Metrobus, Metrorail, or Call-A-Bus service is not available.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible residents may purchase up to fourteen $20 coupon books per six-month period at $10 per book (50% discount). Coupons can be used with any participating taxi company and combined with cash to pay fares.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Prince George's County residents who are age 60 or older, or who have a disability
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Pay for taxi rides with participating cab companies when fixed-route transit is not available
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Prince George's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a Prince George's County resident
Must be age 60 or older and/or have a qualifying disability
Must provide proof of age or disability (e.g., driver's license, Metro Senior/Disability Card, or MetroAccess card)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at the Call-A-Cab portal, or download and print the application form. Submit the completed form with a check or money order for $10 per coupon book (payable to Prince George's County) and proof of age or disability by mail to: Office of Transportation, 9400 Peppercorn Place, Suite 320, Largo, MD 20774. Call 301-499-8603 or Maryland Relay 800-735-2258 for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Care for Uninsured Residents (Cheverly Health Center and MCH @ Laurel)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Prince George's County Health Department provides basic primary care, childhood immunizations, reproductive health, sexual health, STI testing and treatment, dental, and behavioral health services on a sliding fee schedule for residents who have lost or lack health insurance. structured_extraction.assistance_description: Sliding fee scale health care services at Cheverly Health Center and Maternal and Child Health Center (MCH @ Laurel). Services include primary care, immunizations, reproductive and sexual health, dental, behavioral health, and TB treatment. No one turned away for inability to pay.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Health care services including primary care, dental, immunizations, sexual health, behavioral health, TB treatment
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County

Sliding fee based on ability to pay
No one turned away for inability to pay

structured_extraction.program_name: Chesapeake Bay Restoration Fund (Bay Restoration Funds)

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funds to cover the cost of installing BAT nitrogen-reducing septic tanks or connecting to public sewer. Applications are processed through the Momentum online portal at momentum.princegeorgescountymd.gov.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners in Prince George's County who have an existing septic system and want to upgrade to nitrogen-reducing technology or connect to public sewer.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of BAT nitrogen-reducing septic tanks or connection to public sewer.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be seeking to install a BAT nitrogen-reducing septic system or connect to public sewer
Property must have an existing septic system
System must be eligible for nitrogen-reducing upgrade or public sewer connection
Application must be submitted through the Momentum system
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application through the Prince George's County Momentum online portal at momentum.princegeorgescountymd.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides subsidized child care assistance to eligible families in Prince George's County, helping cover the cost of child care services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Subsidized child care payments to help eligible families afford child care. Specific benefit amounts and terms are not described on this page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families in Prince George's County who need financial assistance with child care costs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Child care expenses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Child Care Subsidy Program application listed on this page.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Prince George's County Health Department program supports children with elevated blood lead levels and children diagnosed with asthma. It works to reduce environmental lead hazards and asthma triggers in the home, encourages ongoing medical care, and provides environmental case management in partnership with families and healthcare providers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Services include case management for children with elevated blood lead levels, home environmental assessments following confirmed elevated blood lead reports, educational programs on lead exposure prevention and safe lead paint reduction, telephone consultations on asthma triggers and indoor air quality, and up to six home visits for eligible children with asthma to help manage triggers and receive home items to control asthma triggers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with children who have elevated blood lead levels or who have been diagnosed with asthma (under age 19 with Medicaid or Medicaid-eligible) in Prince George's County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home environmental assessments, case management, educational services, and home items to reduce asthma triggers
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Child must have an elevated blood lead level (for lead services) or be diagnosed with asthma (for asthma services)
For asthma program: child must be under age 19
For asthma program: child must have Medicaid or be eligible for Medicaid
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For lead services, the Health Department receives a report from the state and contacts families directly. For asthma services, families can call 301-883-7662 or email leadandasthmaprogram@co.pg.md.us to inquire about eligibility and enrollment.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Children & Families Information Center (CFIC) provides 24/7 information and referral services and systems navigation to help children and families in Prince George's County find and connect to community resources and care coordination. Callers to the referral line can get help identifying services for their families. For those needing multiple services, a CFIC worker helps connect them to the right agencies and coordinates resources.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free 24/7 phone-based information and referral service (call 866-533-0680). Residents can get help finding community resources and services. For those with complex needs, a CFIC worker provides systems navigation — helping callers connect to multiple agencies and coordinating the resources needed.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Children and families residing in Prince George's County who need help finding community resources and services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Connecting families to community resources, care coordination, and agency referrals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Prince George's County residents.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call the CFIC referral line at 866-533-0680. The service is available 24/7.

structured_extraction.program_name: Children in Need of Support (CINS) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A juvenile justice diversion program for youth ages 13-18 in Prince George's County. The program works to interrupt pre-delinquent behavior and redirect youth to prevent them from entering or progressing further into the juvenile justice system. It uses an evidence-based assessment to identify family strengths and needs, develops a Family Service Plan, assigns a case manager, and connects families to community-based services. The program also includes an 8-week component for both parents and youth covering parenting skills, brain development, communication, conflict resolution, and positive youth development.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Case management services connecting families to community-based resources, an evidence-based family assessment (Child and Family Adolescent Functional Assessment Survey), a comprehensive Family Service Plan, and an 8-week educational component for both parents and youth.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Youth ages 13-18 and their families in Prince George's County who are at risk of entering or have entered the juvenile justice system.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Case management, family assessments, connection to community-based services, and educational programming for parents and youth.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Prince George's County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Youth must be between ages 13 and 18
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 301-265-8446 for assistance or more information about the CINS Program.

structured_extraction.program_name: Clean Energy Program – ENERGY STAR Certification and Green Leasing Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: This grant program encourages owners of existing commercial office and multifamily buildings in Prince George's County to install energy conservation measures (ECMs) that help achieve ENERGY STAR® certification, perform energy and water efficiency retrofits, and adopt green leasing best practices. The goal is to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, lower energy costs, and attract and retain high-value tenants while supporting the County's Climate Action Plan and greenhouse gas reduction goals. The program provides reimbursement grants to building owners who are PEPCO and/or Washington Gas customers for energy audits, electric and natural gas efficiency measures, water efficiency retrofits, and licensed professional fees to verify and stamp ENERGY STAR certification applications. The program also supports compliance with Maryland Building Energy Performance Standards (BEPS) regulation.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement grants up to $150,000 per location address: up to $50,000 for auditing, energy assessments, ENERGY STAR certification, and validation; up to $50,000 for electric energy conservation measures; up to $50,000 for natural gas conservation measures; and up to $1,500 for a licensed professional to verify and stamp the ENERGY STAR certification application. Green leasing measures are eligible but cannot exceed 20% of total funding. Projects must show at least 20% reduction in total energy costs, kWh, and therms. Buildings must maintain ENERGY STAR certification for at least three years and adopt green leasing practices. Payment structure: up to 80% of pre-qualified amount upon receipt of complete request for payment; remaining balance paid upon proof of ENERGY STAR certification. Funding also supports energy and water efficiency retrofits and adoption of Green Leasing best practices. Eligible measures include HVAC, lighting, windows, insulation, air sealing, hot water heaters, appliances, commercial kitchen equipment, full building tune-up, operations and maintenance training, and variable frequency drives.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on a rolling basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of existing multifamily (2+ units per building, 20+ units per property) and commercial office buildings (10,000+ sq ft) in Prince George's County who are PEPCO and/or Washington Gas customers, with buildings built before March 23, 2016, seeking ENERGY STAR certification and green leasing adoption
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Costs for electric and natural gas energy conservation measures prescribed in an energy audit, including HVAC, lighting, windows, insulation, air sealing, hot water heaters, appliances, commercial kitchen equipment, full building tune-up, operations and maintenance training, and variable frequency drives; water efficiency retrofits; hiring an EmPOWER-approved auditor to conduct benchmarking and an Investment Grade Audit (ASHRAE Level 2 or 3); licensed professional fees to verify and stamp the ENERGY STAR certification application; and green leasing measures (up to 20% of total grant).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Buildings must be located within Prince George's County, Maryland, and within the service territories of PEPCO and/or Washington Gas, as verified by utility bills.

structured_extraction.program_name: Clean Energy Program – Energy Efficiency Grant (Prince George's County)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides supplemental grant funding to eligible Prince George's County homeowners living in designated Energy Resiliency Communities (ERCs) to offset the cost of home energy efficiency improvements and retrofits, combined with existing EmPOWER Maryland utility incentives. The program supports energy efficiency upgrades—including air sealing, duct sealing, insulation, HVAC systems, water heating, lighting, ENERGY STAR certified appliances, solar PV, and solar water heaters—to help residents lower energy costs and reduce greenhouse gas emissions. Participants must also apply to the applicable EmPOWER Maryland incentive program. Natural Gas incentives are currently available for Washington Gas customers in the nine designated ERC neighborhoods, aimed at reducing energy injustice and barriers while supporting Maryland and the County's energy efficiency and carbon reduction goals. Electric incentives are no longer funded; all-electric homes do not qualify. As of February 2024, over 2,000 applications have been processed across nine designated ERC neighborhoods.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $6,250 for residential energy efficiency improvements. Up to $2,500 can be allocated toward natural gas incentives. Up to 60% of the total grant award ($3,750) can be allocated toward air sealing and insulation. The $100 home energy assessment cost is included in the total $6,250. Electric incentives are no longer funded; all-electric homes do not qualify. Additional solar incentives are available: up to $10,000 for homeowner-owned solar PV systems (up to $2,000 for third-party owned); up to $7,500 for homeowner-owned solar water heaters (up to $2,000 for third-party owned); and up to $2,000 for solar power outlets. Grants are combined with EmPOWER Maryland energy incentives (Washington Gas). Work must be completed within 90 days of prequalification approval.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners and residents in Prince George's County who live within one of the nine designated Energy Resiliency Communities (ERCs) in single-family homes, townhouses, or individually metered condominiums, and are customers of Washington Gas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home energy efficiency improvements and retrofits recommended by a whole-house energy assessment, including air sealing, duct sealing, insulation, HVAC service/repair/upgrades, water heating, lighting, ENERGY STAR certified appliances, solar PV systems, and solar water heaters. Up to 15% can cover health and safety improvements identified during the audit that must be addressed before energy work can begin.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only to residents in nine designated Energy Resiliency Communities (ERCs) within Prince George's County, Maryland: Bladensburg - East Riverdale; Forestville; Hillcrest Heights - Marlow Heights; Kentland - Palmer Park; Oxon Hill - Glassmanor; Silver Hill; Suitland - Coral Hills; Langley Park; Woodlawn - West Lanham. ERC eligibility can be confirmed using the ERC Address Locator tool.
requirements_list: Must be a homeowner or resident in Prince George's County
Must reside in a designated Energy Resiliency Community (ERC)
Must live in a single-family home, townhouse, or individually metered condominium
Must be a Washington Gas utility customer (electric-only/all-electric homes do not qualify)
