structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Confirm your address is within an ERC using the ERC Address Locator. 2. Select a certified contractor from the pre-approved list. 3. Schedule and complete a whole-house energy audit/home energy assessment. 4. Apply to the applicable EmPOWER Maryland program. 5. Receive grant pre-qualification. 6. Complete work within 90 days of prequalification approval. 7. Submit invoice for reimbursement after work is completed. A fillable grant application form is available for download on the County website. Applications can also be submitted through the Prince George's County Department of the Environment or via DoE Sustainable Energy.

structured_extraction.program_name: Clean Energy Program – Solar Energy Grant (Solarize Prince George's)
structured_extraction.program_description: A county-led program that makes going solar easier and more affordable for Prince George's County homeowners. Provides grant funding to eligible homeowners to offset the cost of installing rooftop solar photovoltaic (PV) systems. The program connects residents with financial incentives, vetted solar installers, and expert guidance covering home assessment, permitting, and installation. Option A: Up to $10,000 for Pepco customers located in a designated Energy Resiliency Community (ERC) — for income-qualified applicants (household gross income below 60% of Prince George's County median income), the grant covers 100% of cost up to $10,000. Option B: Up to $5,000 for all other homeowner-owned rooftop solar PV systems in the county. For homeowner-owned systems, an additional up to $2,000 is available for a solar power outlet for grid outage resilience. For third-party owned systems (leased or power purchase agreement), up to $2,000 for solar PV installation and up to $2,000 for a solar power outlet. Up to 20% of the grant can cover ancillary measures facilitating installation (e.g., tree trimming, roof repairs, service panel upgrades, mold remediation). The grant requires a Prequalification Notice before installation begins and is disbursed after installation is complete and all required close-out documents are submitted. Grants are awarded on a first-come, first-served basis. The program also requires completion of energy efficiency upgrades prior to solar grant eligibility for ERC participants. The grant is combined with state energy incentives. The program is funded in part through the U.S. Department of Energy's Energy Efficiency and Conservation Block Grant (EECBG) Program under the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are awarded on a first-come, first-served basis. Option A: Up to $10,000 for Pepco customers located in an Energy Resiliency Community (ERC) — income-qualified applicants (household gross income below 60% of Prince George's County median income) receive up to 100% of cost up to $10,000; market-rate applicants receive up to $5,000. Option B: Up to $5,000 for all other homeowner-owned rooftop solar PV systems in the county. For homeowner-owned systems, an additional up to $2,000 is available for a solar power outlet for grid outage resilience. For third-party owned systems (leased or power purchase agreement): up to $2,000 for solar PV installation and up to $2,000 for a solar power outlet. Up to 20% of the grant can cover ancillary measures facilitating installation (e.g., tree trimming, roof repairs, service panel upgrades, mold remediation). Minimum system size of 2.0 kW DC; no maximum size. Minimum 70% average Total Solar Resource Fraction across array. All equipment must be new (not rebuilt, refurbished, or relocated). Funds are disbursed after installation is complete and all required close-out documents are submitted. The grant is combined with state energy incentives. The program also connects residents with vetted solar installers and expert guidance. Systems must remain in Prince George's County for 10 years following installation. Federal Period of Performance: work must be complete no later than April 30, 2026.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications are accepted on a rolling basis from November 10, 2025, to February 27, 2026. The deadline may be extended, but awards are limited, so early submission is strongly encouraged. All project work must be complete no later than April 30, 2026 (Federal Period of Performance).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Prince George's County homeowners who have not previously received a Solar Energy Grant from the county and want to install a new rooftop solar PV system. Income-qualified residents (household gross income below 60% of Prince George's County median income) in designated Energy Resiliency Communities may receive enhanced grant amounts. ERC participants must also have Pepco and/or Washington Gas as their utility provider and have completed energy efficiency upgrades through the Clean Energy Program. Program prioritizes low and moderate income residents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of a new rooftop solar photovoltaic (PV) system on a single-family residence, including parts, components, and accessory equipment. The system must be installed on the roof of the home. Up to 20% of the grant may be used for ancillary measures facilitating installation such as tree trimming, roof repairs, service panel upgrades, and mold remediation. May also cover a solar power outlet for grid outage resilience. Does not fund battery/energy storage components. Materials and products must comply with Buy America requirements for federally funded iron, steel, manufactured products, and construction materials.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Prince George's County, Maryland. Enhanced grants are available to residents in designated Energy Resiliency Communities (ERCs) within the Pepco and/or Washington Gas service territory. ERC eligibility can be confirmed using the ERC Address Locator tool. The program is limited to nine designated ERC neighborhoods for the enhanced grant tier. Properties may be served by Pepco, BGE, Smeco, or other utilities for the standard grant tier. The standard grant (Option B) is also available to households outside an ERC zone, or inside an ERC zone but outside of Pepco's service area.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications accepted on a rolling, first-come, first-served basis from November 10, 2025 to February 27, 2026 (deadline subject to extension). All work must be completed by April 30, 2026. Step 1: Check eligibility — confirm your address is within an ERC (if applicable) using the ERC Address Locator. Step 2: Select a qualified contractor from the Maryland Solar Access Program's Participating Contractor List and obtain at least two quotes. Step 3: Submit a prequalification application (including the grant application, invoice template, recent electricity bill, contractor qualifications, solar PV analysis/proposal/pre-install photos, and the contractual agreement) before installation begins. Applications can be submitted by email, hand delivery, or mail. Step 4: Receive a Prequalification Notice. Step 5: Install the solar system within 4 months of prequalification approval. Step 6: Submit close-out documents (final invoice, utility Authorization to Operate letter, interconnection agreement, permits, inspection sticker, installation photos, proof of solar array registration with the Maryland Public Service Commission, and proof of one month of solar generation) to receive grant funds. For ERC participants: complete energy efficiency upgrades through the Clean Energy Program and confirm eligibility with DoE Sustainable Energy staff before applying. Applicant must sign affidavit witnessed by contractor.

structured_extraction.program_name: Clean Energy Program – Solar Water Heater Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grant funding to Prince George's County residents within Energy Resiliency Communities (ERCs) to help cover costs of installing a solar water heating system and other energy efficiency measures. The program also supports solar PV installations. Grants supplement Pepco and Washington Gas incentives and operate on a first-come, first-served basis. Designed to assist residents with becoming more energy efficient and supports the county's energy resilience and carbon reduction goals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Energy Efficiency Grant: up to $7,500 total ($5,000 maximum for electric incentives, $2,500 maximum for natural gas incentives); up to 50% of total grant ($3,750) for air sealing and insulation; up to $100 for home energy assessment. Solar PV (homeowner-owned): up to $10,000 for system costs; up to $2,000 for solar power outlet. Solar PV (third-party owned): up to $2,000 for system costs; up to $2,000 for solar power outlet. Solar Water Heater (homeowner-owned): up to $7,500 for eligible costs including parts, components, and accessory equipment. Solar Water Heater (third-party owned): up to $2,000. Up to 15% of the solar water heater grant can cover installation facilitation measures.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Prince George's County single-family homeowners, townhouse, or condominium owners who are Pepco and/or Washington Gas customers residing in one of the nine designated Energy Resiliency Communities (ERCs). Prioritizes low- and moderate-income residents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency home improvements including HVAC systems, water heaters, insulation, air sealing, duct sealing, lighting upgrades, and appliances. Solar PV system installation. Solar water heater system installation including parts, components, and accessory equipment. Home energy assessment costs. Health and safety measures.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must reside in one of nine designated Energy Resiliency Communities (ERCs) within Prince George's County: Bladensburg - East Riverdale; Forestville; Hillcrest Heights - Marlow Heights; Kentland - Palmer Park; Oxon Hill - Glassmanor; Silver Hill; Suitland - Coral Hills; Langley Park; and Woodlawn - West Lanham. Address eligibility can be verified using the ERC Address Locator tool.

Must be a Pepco customer (electric) and/or Washington Gas customer (gas)
Must provide a recent utility bill (within 3 months) proving Pepco/Washington Gas customer status
Must obtain a home energy audit report (Home Performance with ENERGY STAR or QHEC audit)
Must apply to the EmPOWER Maryland incentive program
Contractor must be registered as a County vendor
Must complete IRS Form W-9

Contact DoE Sustainable Energy staff to confirm that measures qualify
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Residents in ERC communities may apply for the Solar Water Heater Grant upon successful completion of energy efficiency upgrades. Verify address eligibility using the ERC Address Locator tool. Obtain a home energy assessment and apply to EmPOWER Maryland incentives. Ensure contractor is a registered County vendor. Contact DoE Sustainable Energy staff to confirm eligibility of proposed measures. Program operates on a first-come, first-served basis.

structured_extraction.program_name: Clean Water Act Fee Hardship Exemption
structured_extraction.program_description: Residential property owners in Prince George's County who face substantial financial hardship may qualify for a full suspension of their Clean Water Act Fee for the applicable tax year if they have received the Maryland State Homeowners' Property Tax Credit.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Qualified residential property owners receive a full suspension of the Clean Water Act Fee for the eligible tax year. Eligibility requires having received the Homeowners' Property Tax Credit from the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation. The exemption must be applied for annually.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential property owners in Prince George's County with demonstrated substantial financial hardship
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Full suspension of the Clean Water Act Fee for the tax year
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a residential property owner in Prince George's County
Must demonstrate substantial financial hardship
Must have received the Homeowners' Property Tax Credit from the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation for the tax year in which the CWAF is billed
Must apply annually to the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation to continue receiving the Homeowners' Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply annually to the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation for the Homeowners' Property Tax Credit. Upon determination of homeowner eligibility, the County's Office of Finance will suspend the fee entirely for the eligible tax year.

structured_extraction.program_name: Clean Water Act Fee Reduction Credits
structured_extraction.program_description: Property owners in Prince George's County who install or maintain stormwater Best Management Practices (BMPs) or Environmental Site Design (ESD) techniques that reduce stormwater runoff quantity or improve its quality may qualify for a reduction of up to 100% of their Clean Water Act Fee (CWAF) impervious area fee. Credits are available for residential, multi-family, condominium, and non-residential properties. Specific credit amounts vary by property type and type of stormwater practice installed: residential properties can receive up to 40% for roof treatment, 50% for driveways/parking lots, and 10% for other impervious areas; non-residential properties with ESDs can receive up to 45% for roof and parking areas, plus additional credits for green lawn care and reforestation. Properties with legacy stormwater ponds built after 2002 can receive up to 100% reduction (up to 50% for ponds built 1985-2002, and no reduction for ponds built before 1985 unless an easement is provided for retrofit). Alternative compliance options (easements, outreach, green care) are available for qualified tax-exempt nonprofits and faith-based organizations, providing up to 100% combined reduction. The $20.58 per tax account administrative fee is not reduced. Credits are valid for three years and must be renewed by reapplying.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible property owners can receive up to 100% reduction in the impervious area portion of the annual Clean Water Act Fee. Credits vary by property type and stormwater practice: residential properties can receive up to 40% for roof treatment, 50% for driveways/parking lots, and 10% for other impervious areas; non-residential properties with ESDs can receive up to 45% for roof or parking lot areas, plus 5% for green lawn care and 5% for reforestation. Properties with legacy stormwater ponds built after 2002 can receive up to 100% reduction; ponds built 1985-2002 receive up to 50%; ponds built before 1985 receive no reduction unless an easement is provided for retrofit. Alternative compliance options for tax-exempt religious organizations and 501(c) nonprofits: 50% for providing easements, 25% for outreach/education, 25% for green care/good housekeeping, up to 100% combined. The $20.58 per tax account per year administrative fee is never reduced. Impact fee basis is $20.90 per account per ESU (1 ESU = 2,465 sq. ft. untreated impervious surface). Credits are valid for three years and require annual inspection and good maintenance of BMPs.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications submitted prior to October 1 are eligible for credit in the current taxable year (ending June 30); all other requests are eligible for credit in the following taxable year. Alternative compliance applications must be submitted by March 31 to be eligible for a fee reduction credit in the next taxable year (July 1–June 30).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential, multi-family, condominium, commercial, industrial, institutional, and agricultural property owners, as well as tax-exempt religious organizations and 501(c) nonprofit organizations in Prince George's County that install or maintain stormwater management practices.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of the annual Clean Water Act impervious area fee charged to property owners.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only to property owners within Prince George's County, Maryland (excluding properties within the City of Bowie municipal limits).
requirements_list: Property must be located in Prince George's County
Stormwater BMPs or ESD practices must be installed and in use on the property
BMPs must be functioning correctly and maintained in good condition
BMPs must pass an inspection by the Department of the Environment (DoE)
Access to BMPs must be granted to the DoE
Off-site BMP credit requires same owner and same drainage area as the BMP property
Structural BMPs for non-residential properties must be approved and certified by the County
Legacy stormwater ponds for non-residential properties must have passed the County's triennial inspection
Alternative compliance applicants must be a qualified tax-exempt faith-based organization or 501(c)(3) nonprofit
Applicants must complete and submit the appropriate reduction credit request form for their property type
Credit must be renewed every three years by reapplying
For green lawn care credit: business must be listed in Maryland Department of Agriculture's pesticide database
Alternative compliance Option 1: Provide temporary easements and maintain BMPs with tri-annual inspections
Alternative compliance Option 2: Participate in outreach/education and host annual activities (trash pick-up, recycling, rain check rebate, or tree planting)
Alternative compliance Option 3: Implement green care and good housekeeping practices
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and submit the appropriate application form for your property type (Detached Single-Family Residential, Condominium/Multi-Family Residential, Non-Residential with ESDs, Non-Residential with Legacy Ponds, or Alternative Compliance for nonprofits). Forms may be submitted via email to CleanWaterActFee@co.pg.md.us or by mail to: Prince George's County Department of the Environment, Stormwater Management Division, 1801 McCormick Drive, Suite 500, Largo, Maryland 20774. The Prince George's County Department of the Environment inspects and field-verifies BMPs, then determines the amount of fee reduction credit to award. Credits appear on the following year's annual property tax bill.

structured_extraction.program_description: A 30-year public-private partnership between Corvias and Prince George's County to improve stormwater infrastructure and support local economic development. The program creates procurement opportunities for local, small, minority, and women-owned business enterprises, particularly Prince George's County business enterprises, through contractor development, community outreach, and compliance programs.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides procurement opportunities (subcontracting, consulting, and supply contracts) for target class businesses, along with contractor development support and community outreach. It targets local, small, minority, and women-owned business enterprises in Prince George's County. Specific financial amounts are not stated on this page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local, small, minority, and women-owned business enterprises, particularly Prince George's County business enterprises seeking subcontracting and procurement opportunities in stormwater green infrastructure projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Subcontracting, consulting, and supply work related to stormwater green infrastructure design, construction, operation, and maintenance.

Preference for Prince George's County business enterprises
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit thecleanwaterpartnership.com for more information on how to get involved.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Commercial Property Improvement Program (CPIP) provides grant funding to support the revitalization of underperforming retail centers and main street storefronts in targeted areas of Prince George's County. Funding helps owners of smaller neighborhood retail centers, strip malls, main street retail space, and stand-alone retail storefronts make exterior facade improvements, placemaking, lighting, and major building systems upgrades. The goal is to boost the economic performance of older or underperforming retail centers by improving their appearance and enhancing the retail experience for Prince George's County residents, with a focus on properties within the Central Avenue Blue Line Corridor and Suitland-Naylor Road Metro Sustainable Community areas.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants totaling $250,000 in available funding for the 2025/2026 cycle. CPIP reimburses up to 50% of approved construction costs after the awardee pays in full. Applicants must provide a 50% match (at least half of total project cost). Minimum grant award is $25,000 (requiring at least $50,000 in total project costs); maximum grant award is $125,000 (requiring at least $250,000 in total project costs). Eligible improvements include storefront facade redesign, building system upgrades, architectural feature repairs, window/door replacement, lighting, signage, awnings, painting, landscaping, parking lot improvements, and roof replacement. Architectural design and permit costs are not reimbursed until construction is complete. Construction must begin within 90 days of grant approval and be completed within 270 days of approval.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of commercial retail centers, strip malls, main street storefronts, and stand-alone retail storefronts located within the Central Avenue Blue Line Corridor or Suitland-Naylor Road Metro Sustainable Community areas in Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Exterior facade enhancements including storefront facade redesign, architectural feature repairs, window and door replacement, lighting, signage, awnings, and painting; placemaking; landscaping; parking lot improvements; roof replacement; and major building systems improvements. Applicants must select a minimum of 3 improvement types. Architectural design and permit costs are reimbursable only after construction is complete.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties must be located within the Central Avenue Blue Line Corridor or the Suitland-Naylor Road Metro Sustainable Community areas in Prince George's County, Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) Program – Prince George's County
structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) Program is a federally funded entitlement program administered by Prince George's County Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD). It provides annual competitive grant funding to municipalities, local government agencies, and nonprofit 501(c)(3) organizations to carry out community development activities that benefit low- and moderate-income residents of Prince George's County. Funded projects must provide decent housing, a suitable living environment, or expanded economic opportunities. Eligible activities include rehabilitation and improvement of public facilities and infrastructure (streets, sidewalks, parks, health facilities), affordable housing acquisition and rehabilitation, demolition, economic development assistance to micro and small for-profit businesses, and targeted public services such as senior programs, youth services, job training, and healthcare. The program accepts applications on an annual basis for each program year, with proposal application packets typically becoming available in October. The most recent cycle covered Program Year 52 (July 1, 2026 – June 30, 2027). Public service projects are limited to 15% of available CDBG funds. Funding is provided on a reimbursement basis—agencies pay expenses first, then submit requests with proof of payment. Large projects should be broken into annual phases.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual competitive federal CDBG block grant funding allocated by HUD and administered by Prince George's County DHCD. Grants are awarded to municipalities, local government agencies, and nonprofit 501(c)(3) organizations for one-year project periods beginning July 1. Funds can support affordable housing acquisition and rehabilitation, demolition, economic development assistance to micro and small for-profit businesses, public facility and infrastructure improvements, and public services such as senior services, youth services, job training, and healthcare. At least 51% of persons or households served must be low- and moderate-income, or the project must serve a HUD-designated low- and moderate-income area, address slum or blight, or meet an urgent community need. Public service projects are limited to 15% of available CDBG funds. Funding is provided on a reimbursement basis—agencies pay expenses first, then submit requests with proof of payment. Grant amounts may be less than requested. Large projects should be broken into annual phases.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Not accepting applications for Program Year 52 (July 1, 2026 – June 30, 2027); proposal application packets typically available in October
structured_extraction.program_audience: Municipalities, local government agencies, and nonprofit 501(c)(3) organizations in Prince George's County seeking funding for community development projects that benefit low- and moderate-income residents
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Affordable housing acquisition and rehabilitation; demolition; economic development assistance to micro and small for-profit businesses; rehabilitation and improvement of public facilities and infrastructure (streets, sidewalks, parks, health facilities); public services including senior programs, youth services, job development/training, and healthcare; housing and community development activities benefiting low-to-moderate income residents as defined under the CDBG program

Applicant agency must serve low- and moderate-income Prince George's County residents. Eligibility areas are based on HUD census data.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Proposal application packets become available in October. Submit proposals to the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD), Community Planning and Development division. A Proposal Advisory Group reviews submitted proposals. DHCD compiles and summarizes proposals and submits them to the County Executive, who makes recommendations to the County Council. The County Council holds public hearings in April and adopts the Annual Action Plan by early May. The County submits the adopted plan to HUD by May each year. Projects begin July 1. Applications for Program Year 52 (July 1, 2026 – June 30, 2027) are no longer being accepted. Sign up for Subscribe MyPGC notifications or call 301-883-5540 to be notified when funding becomes available. Monitor the county's Notice of Funding Availability page for future program year announcements.

Advanced training courses are also available in areas such as CPR, shelter management, and amateur radio.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Redevelopment Authority of Prince George's County awards small capital grants to civic and neighborhood associations and community-based nonprofit organizations to help implement innovative projects within Prince George's County. The goal is to strengthen communities and build organizational capacity through neighborhood beautification and environmental sustainability projects. Grants support two categories: Neighborhood Beautification (e.g., streetscaping, signage, façade improvements, public art) and Environment/Natural Resources and Sustainability (e.g., park restoration, urban agriculture, stormwater management, historic preservation). Funds can only be used for capital expenses such as equipment and materials — not operations, salaries, or program costs. Total program funding is $250,000, with awards up to $50,000 per project.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Small capital grants up to $50,000 per award for the purchase of equipment and materials. Total program funding is $250,000, split into two tracks: $100,000 designated for National Capital Strategic Economic Development Areas (inside the Beltway, within sustainable communities' boundaries) and $150,000 available for county-wide projects. Grants are provided on a reimbursable basis or as traditional grants (funds provided before expenses incurred). One-year grant performance period from execution of grant agreement. Projects must fall under Neighborhood Beautification (e.g., streetscaping, signage, façade improvements, public art) or Environment/Natural Resources/Sustainability (e.g., park restoration, urban agriculture, green roofs, stormwater management, historic preservation). Funds cannot be used for operating costs, program costs, salaries, or personnel.

Also includes condominium associations, recreation associations, community development corporations, arts/cultural organizations, and religious institutions/houses of worship.

Also includes memorial gardens and landscaping, facility renovations and upgrades, security system installation, and architectural and engineering services. Cannot be used for operations, program costs, salaries, or personnel.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Partnership Grant (CPG) Program is the main discretionary grant initiative offered by the Prince George's County Executive's Office. It provides funding to eligible private 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations that deliver services or activities within Prince George's County. Grants support projects and programs that serve the community, particularly underserved populations, and align with the County Executive's strategic priorities. Awards are based on criteria including community value added, overall program costs, organizational stability, and adequacy of other funding sources. Approximately $1.5 million is available through the FY 2026 CPG Program, with grants up to $100,000 per organization per fiscal year. Awards are for one year only and are determined by an Executive Review Panel. The full award amount is disbursed in a single payment, and grantees must submit final financial and programmatic reports.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $100,000 per organization per fiscal year. Approximately $1.5 million is available through the FY 2026 CPG Program. Previous awards ranged from $1,000 to $125,000. Awards are for one year only. The full award amount is disbursed in a single payment. Funding is subject to availability and determined by an Executive Review Panel. Only one proposal per organization is accepted per fiscal year. Fiscal sponsorship is not accepted. Awards are based on criteria including community value added, overall program costs, organizational stability, and adequacy of other funding sources. Grantees must submit a final financial expenditure report and a final programmatic summary report.

structured_extraction.program_name: Coordinated Specialty Care for First Episode Psychosis (FEP) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: An evidence-based, multidisciplinary treatment team-based intervention providing community-based, person-centered, recovery-oriented coordinated specialty care services for individuals experiencing a first episode of psychosis. Services include psychiatry, peer support, recovery coaching, employment/education support, and case management. The program improves quality of life for participants and families, increases engagement in education and employment, improves psychosocial functioning, reduces severity of symptoms, hospitalization admissions, and overnight stays, and provides family education to decrease stigma and support for caregivers. Prince George's County's Local Behavioral Health Authority (LBHA) invites qualified behavioral health providers to apply for funding to support this program.

structured_extraction.program_name: County Right of First Refusal Program: Multifamily Rental Properties
structured_extraction.program_description: This program gives Prince George's County the right to purchase multifamily rental properties (20 or more units) before they are sold on the open market. The county can buy the property directly or assign its purchase rights to a third party in order to preserve and expand affordable rental housing for low- to moderate-income households. A companion Preservation Fund provides flexible financing (subordinate loans) for acquisition, rehabilitation, and stabilization of rental apartment complexes subject to the ROFR Program, funded through ARPA and other County-secured funds.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The county exercises a right of first refusal (ROFR) to purchase multifamily rental properties of 20 or more units when a property owner enters into a contract of sale. DHCD may purchase the property directly or assign its purchase rights to a third-party developer or buyer. The county has a 60-day evaluation period from receipt of a complete ROFR offer and up to 180 days to complete the purchase, with up to 180-day financing contingency available. Property owners and prospective buyers may also request an exception to the ROFR by executing a Written Agreement with DHCD before entering into a contract of sale. A companion Preservation Fund offers subordinate loans up to $3,000,000 (exceptions may be approved) at 0% interest, with loan terms up to 40 years, amortization up to 40 years, no payments due prior to December 31, 2026, LTV up to 110% (120% for high public purpose properties), and no origination, legal, or other fees.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of multifamily rental properties with 20 or more units in Prince George's County who are seeking to sell, as well as prospective buyers, third-party developers, and approved borrowers interested in acquiring, rehabilitating, and preserving affordable housing.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Preservation of affordable rental housing for low- to moderate-income households in Prince George's County, including acquisition, rehabilitation, and typical transaction costs of properties acquired under ROFR Program terms.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All areas of Prince George's County, Maryland, as established by CR-51-2015. Properties within municipal boundaries must comply with municipal approval requirements of the ROFR Code. Preservation Fund loans are limited to properties within Qualified Census Tracts (QCTs) as defined by HUD per 26 U.S.C. 42(d)(5)(B)(ii)(I).
requirements_list: Property must be a multifamily rental facility with 20 or more dwelling rental units.
Property owner must provide written notice of the sale to the DHCD Director after entering into a bona fide contract of sale.
Prospective buyers seeking an exception to the ROFR must execute a Written Agreement with DHCD before the property owner and buyer enter into a bona fide contract of sale.
All ROFR offers must be submitted electronically by email to designated DHCD staff.
Preservation Fund borrowers must be approved by the Department as eligible participants in the ROFR Program.
Developers seeking to be listed on the ROFR Developer Roster must be approved by the Department.
Property owners must offer the County the right of first refusal on the same terms and conditions as offered to the original purchaser.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Property owners notify DHCD in writing after entering a bona fide contract of sale. DHCD reviews the notice and decides whether to exercise its right of first refusal to purchase the property or assign that right to a third party. The county has a 60-day evaluation period from receipt of a complete ROFR offer and up to 180 days to complete the purchase. To request an exception to the ROFR, prospective buyers must contact DHCD and execute a Written Agreement before the sale contract is signed. All ROFR offers and submissions should be sent electronically to the designated DHCD staff members listed on the program page. Eligible developers may apply to be listed on the ROFR Developer Roster to receive first opportunity consideration for property acquisitions.

structured_extraction.program_name: Deferred Retirement Option Program (DROP) — Police, Fire, and Deputy Sheriff
structured_extraction.program_description: Prince George's County offers Deferred Retirement Option Programs (DROP) for eligible county public safety employees across three variants: the Police DROP for members of the Prince George's County Police Pension Plan covered under the F.O.P. Lodge 89 Collective Bargaining Agreement; the Fire DROP for members of the Prince George's County Fire Service Pension Plan covered under the IAFF Local No. 1619 Collective Bargaining Agreement; and the Deputy Sheriff's DROP for members of the Deputy Sheriff's Pension Plan covered under the F.O.P. Lodge 112 Collective Bargaining Agreement. All programs allow eligible members to voluntarily 'retire' while continuing to work for an additional three years, accumulating monthly pension benefits in a DROP account along with bi-weekly payroll pension contributions, monthly compounded interest, and annual cost-of-living adjustments. The Fire DROP also includes an annual fire bonus. Upon retirement, participants receive the accumulated DROP account balance as a lump-sum benefit and begin receiving their monthly pension. Enrollment is limited each calendar month and selection is based on seniority. Police and Fire Service eligibility requires at least 22 years of actual service; Deputy Sheriff eligibility requires at least 22 or 27 years of actual service depending on date of hire, or attainment of age 57 with at least 5 years of service. Leave and purchased prior military service do not count toward eligibility.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants accumulate a DROP account funded by monthly pension benefit amounts (calculated at DROP entry date), bi-weekly payroll pension contributions, monthly compounded interest, and annual retiree cost-of-living adjustments. The Fire DROP additionally includes an annual fire bonus. For the Police DROP, a maximum of 8 employees may enter per calendar month (no more than 2 Lieutenants and 2 Sergeants). For the Fire DROP and Deputy Sheriff's DROP, a maximum of 4 employees may enter per calendar month. Selection in all programs is by greatest seniority. The DROP period lasts three years, after which employment ends and participants receive their monthly pension benefit plus the accumulated DROP account balance as a lump-sum benefit.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Police DROP and Deputy Sheriff's DROP: Interest of Participation form must be submitted no later than 30 days prior to anticipated entry date. Fire DROP: Interest of Participation form must be submitted during the announced enrollment period.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Members of the Prince George's County Police Pension Plan (F.O.P. Lodge 89), members of the Prince George's County Fire Service Pension Plan (IAFF Local No. 1619), and members of the Deputy Sheriff's Pension Plan (F.O.P. Lodge 112) in Prince George's County who are eligible county public safety employees with sufficient years of service.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Accumulation of deferred retirement benefits in a DROP account during continued active public safety service, resulting in a lump-sum benefit upon retirement in addition to monthly pension payments.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Prince George's County police, fire service, and deputy sheriff employees covered under their respective collective bargaining agreements (F.O.P. Lodge 89 for police; IAFF Local No. 1619 for fire; F.O.P. Lodge 112 for deputy sheriffs).
requirements_list: Must be a member of the applicable pension plan (Police Pension Plan, Fire Service Pension Plan, or Deputy Sheriff's Pension Plan)
Must be covered under the applicable Collective Bargaining Agreement (F.O.P. Lodge 89 for police; IAFF Local No. 1619 for fire; F.O.P. Lodge 112 for deputy sheriffs) at the time of election
Police/Fire Service: must have at least 22 years of actual service
Deputy Sheriff's: must have at least 22 or 27 years of actual service depending on date of hire, or attain age 57 with at least 5 years of service
Leave and purchased prior military service do not count toward eligibility
Police DROP and Deputy Sheriff's DROP: Must submit an Interest of Participation form no later than 30 days prior to the anticipated entry date
Fire DROP: Must submit an Interest of Participation form during the announced enrollment period
Participation is based on seniority and is not guaranteed
Entry date is always effective the first day of a month
Police DROP: A maximum of 8 employees may enter per calendar month (no more than 2 Lieutenants and 2 Sergeants)
Fire DROP: A maximum of 4 employees may enter per calendar month
Deputy Sheriff's DROP: A maximum of 4 employees may enter per calendar month
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Interest of Participation form and submit it to the appropriate DROP contact (pgcpolicedrop@co.pg.md.us for police; pgfddrop@co.pg.md.us for fire; pensions@co.pg.md.us for deputy sheriffs) within the required timeframe. A Retirement Analyst will notify employees of their standing. If selected, complete an Application for Enrollment and any other required forms (including Beneficiary Designation/Change form for deputy sheriffs). Entry date is always the first day of a month. For general inquiries, contact the Office of Human Resources Management.

structured_extraction.program_description: Federal program providing direct assistance for rental payments and utilities to eligible renters experiencing housing instability due to COVID-19. Provides emergency rental assistance to eligible tenants and residents in Prince George's County who are facing eviction or financial hardship due to unpaid rent and utility costs. The program supports both tenant-initiated and landlord-initiated applications. Tenants with household income below 80% of AMI who have a court summons, court judgment, Warrant of Restitution, or Warrant for Possession may apply directly; tenants at or below 50% AMI do not require eviction paperwork. Landlords and property owners may apply on behalf of their tenants for units located in qualifying census tracts or for landlords who previously applied in Fall 2020 and did not receive assistance. Rental and utility assistance payments are made directly to landlords on behalf of eligible tenants via Electronic Funds Transfer (ACH), subject to funding availability and DHCD review.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Direct rental and utility assistance payments made to eligible tenants or on behalf of tenants to landlords via Electronic Funds Transfer (ACH). Up to 18 months cumulative rental and utility payment assistance for eligible households. The exact amount is determined by DHCD after application review and is subject to funding availability. Landlords receive a Rental Assistance Agreement and tenants receive an affidavit; both must accept the approved amount to receive payment.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Portal is closed; applications no longer being accepted
structured_extraction.program_audience: Prince George's County renters with household income below 80% of the Area Median Income (AMI) who are experiencing financial hardship related to COVID-19 and are at risk of eviction, as well as landlords and property owners whose tenants meet income and hardship eligibility requirements, specifically for units in qualifying census tracts or landlords who applied in Fall 2020 without receiving assistance.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Past-due rent and utility bills, as well as ongoing rental costs for eligible tenant households to prevent eviction.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Rental property must be located in Prince George's County, Maryland. Units must be within census tracts that meet risk factors such as housing stress, social factors, and pandemic effects, or the landlord must have applied in Fall 2020 and not received assistance. Properties may also need to be in HUD Qualified Census Tracts (QCT) for income self-certification.
requirements_list: Household income must be below 80% of the Area Median Income (AMI)
Rental property must be located in Prince George's County, Maryland

If household income is above 50% AMI: must be facing eviction due to delinquent rent and have a court summons, court judgment, Warrant of Restitution, Warrant for Possession, or a scheduled eviction by the Sheriff
If household income is at or below 50% AMI: eviction paperwork is not required; priority given to households at or below 50% AMI
Court documentation requirements vary by income level: 30% AMI and below: none required; 31%-50% AMI: court summons; 51%-80% AMI: court judgment
One or more household members must have qualified for unemployment, experienced income reduction, or incurred financial hardship due directly or indirectly to COVID-19
Tenant must have a signed lease or acceptable alternative documentation (utility payment evidence, landlord attestation, or other reasonable documentation)
Rental unit must be in a qualifying census tract based on housing stress, social factors, and pandemic effects, OR landlord applied in Fall 2020 and did not receive assistance
Property must be in a HUD Qualified Census Tract (QCT) to use income self-certification
Landlord must provide: name, address, SSN or Tax ID, Unique ID Number, Property Deed, W-9 Form, and PGC EFT/ACH Enrollment Form
Tenant income documentation required for all adults over 18 who are not full-time students (tax forms, W-2, 1099, pay stubs, or bank statements)
Evidence of housing instability (past due bills, rent notices, or failure to pay notices)
Documentation of financial hardship due to COVID-19 (written attestation or unemployment documentation)
Self-certification letter acceptable as last resort when documentation unavailable due to COVID-19 impact
Must verify residency and income
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call ERAP Hotline at (301) 883-6504, Press 9 for access code. Tenants may apply online at erentalassistance.princegeorgescountymd.gov. Submit required documentation including residency verification (current lease or signed approval letter) and income verification (W-2s, tax filings, paystubs, or other income documents). Landlords must gather required documentation including property deed, W-9, EFT enrollment form, rent ledger, tenant lease, and income verification documents, and coordinate with tenants to collect tenant-specific documents. Applications are submitted through DHCD's portal. After submission, applicants are screened for prioritization, assigned to a reviewer, and undergo review and quality control. DHCD contacts applicants by email about discrepancies or missing information. If approved, landlords receive a Rental Assistance Agreement and tenants receive an affidavit; both must accept the approved amount to receive payment. Finance/DHCD approval is obtained and sent to County Finance for payment processing. Note: the application portal is currently closed.

structured_extraction.program_description: Enterprise zones are state-designated areas where state and local governments offer tax credits on income and property taxes to encourage businesses to expand or relocate. Businesses that create jobs or invest in real property within designated enterprise zones and focus areas in Prince George's County can receive multi-year state income tax credits and local property tax credits. The program aims to encourage business growth and job creation in targeted areas.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two tiers of tax credits are available depending on whether the business is in a standard Enterprise Zone or a Focus Area. In a standard (Non-Focus) Enterprise Zone: State income tax credit of $3,000 in Year 1, $2,000 in Year 2, and $1,000 in Year 3 per disadvantaged employee ($6,000 total), and a one-time $1,000 credit per non-disadvantaged employee. Local property tax credit of 80% of the eligible real property assessment in each of the first 5 years, decreasing by 10% per year (to 70%, 60%, 50%, 40%, 30%) in years 6–10. In a Focus Area Enterprise Zone: State income tax credit of $4,500 in Year 1, $3,000 in Year 2, and $1,500 in Year 3 per disadvantaged employee ($9,000 total), and a one-time $1,500 credit per non-disadvantaged employee. Local property tax credit of 80% of the eligible real property assessment for all 10 years, plus a 10-year 80% credit on new personal property investments.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses expanding or locating within designated Enterprise Zone areas or Focus Areas in Prince George's County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credits applied against state income taxes for new employees hired and against local property taxes on real property expansion, renovation, or capital improvements (and personal property in Focus Areas).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only within designated Enterprise Zone and Enterprise Zone Focus Area locations in Prince George's County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Business must be located in a designated Enterprise Zone or Focus Area in Prince George's County
Credits are tied to creation of new jobs (income tax credit) or investment in real/personal property expansion, renovation, or capital improvements (property tax credit)
Employees must be classified as either disadvantaged or non-disadvantaged to determine credit amount
Property tax credits apply to real property expansion, renovation, or capital improvement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Prince George's County Economic Development Corporation at 301-583-4650 and ask to speak with a Business Development Specialist. Additional details are available through the Maryland Department of Commerce.

structured_extraction.program_name: FY 2025 HUD Continuum of Care (CoC) Local Competition
structured_extraction.program_description: The Continuum of Care (CoC) is the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development's (HUD) primary funding source for homeless services. It provides competitive grants for housing and supportive services to address homelessness in Prince George's County. The program promotes community-wide commitment to ending homelessness by funding nonprofit providers, states, and local governments to rapidly re-house homeless individuals, families, persons fleeing domestic violence, and youth. The FY2025 Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) was withdrawn by HUD on December 8, 2025, for revision, and a modified NOFO is expected to be reissued. Local competition materials including applications and scoring tools are delayed pending further HUD guidance. Letters of Intent were due December 10, 2025, with the full application delayed pending the revised HUD NOFO. Three application tracks are available: Renewal Projects, New Projects - CoC Bonus, and New Projects - DV Bonus. Supports six pillars: equity, data and evidence, collaboration (foundations) and housing and supports, crisis response, and prevention (solutions). Emphasizes Housing First approach, racial equity, LGBTQ+ inclusion, and system performance improvement. Includes project types: permanent supportive housing (PSH), permanent housing-rapid rehousing (PH-RRH), transitional housing (TH), joint TH/PH-RRH, supportive services only (SSO), coordinated entry, HMIS, Youth Homelessness Demonstration Program (YHDP), and Domestic Violence (DV) Bonus funding. Also includes CoCBuilds funding for new construction, acquisition, or rehabilitation of PSH units, with up to 20% of award for other eligible CoC Program activities and up to 10% for project administration.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal HUD Continuum of Care program grants awarded through an annual competitive application process to fund homeless services and housing programs in Prince George's County. Includes funding for permanent supportive housing (PSH), transitional housing (TH), rapid rehousing (RRH), HMIS operations, supportive services, and project administration. Total estimated funding includes approximately $11,287,526 for renewal/reallocation projects, $564,376 for planning, $1,354,503 for new permanent housing bonus projects, $1,038,306 for new DV housing bonus projects, and $1,754,287 in YHDP renewal projects. Requires minimum 25% local match (except leasing funds; YHDP projects may be waived if applicant demonstrates reasonable steps to maximize resources). RRH subsidies provided on a declining basis up to 12 months maximum. CoC Bonus projects up to 12% of Final Pro Rata Need; DV Bonus projects up to 15% of Preliminary Pro Rata Need, minimum $50,000 or maximum $5 million. $52,000,000 specifically available for DV Bonus projects nationally. YHDP special activities include host home/kinship care payments, supportive services extensions, moving expenses, security deposits, rental arrears, and utility assistance. CoCBuilds awards provide one-time capital funding for new construction, acquisition, or rehabilitation of PSH units; up to 20% of award may fund other eligible CoC Program activities (supportive services, operating costs); up to 10% of award may be used for project administration. Project-based rental assistance, supportive services, and operating costs also eligible under CoCBuilds. Grant agreement execution required by September 1, 2025.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Letters of Intent due Wednesday, December 10, 2025 at 5:00 PM; full application delayed pending revised HUD NOFO; FY 2025 HUD submission deadline 8:00 PM EDT on August 29, 2025
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations, government entities, and service providers offering housing and homeless services in Prince George's County seeking HUD CoC program funding. Ultimate beneficiaries include chronically homeless individuals, families experiencing homelessness, unaccompanied youth (ages 24 and younger, including pregnant/parenting youth), domestic violence survivors, veterans, returning citizens, elderly/aging populations, BIPOC and LGBTQ+ individuals, persons with severe behavioral, developmental, or somatic health barriers, and unsheltered persons in encampments. Also includes developers, housing providers, and social service organizations with experience in permanent supportive housing development.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Permanent supportive housing development and operations, transitional housing, rapid rehousing, emergency shelter, street outreach, case management, behavioral health services, employment assistance, HMIS operations, coordinated entry systems, rental assistance, supportive services, program administration, construction and rehabilitation activities, VAWA-related emergency transfer facilitation, host home/kinship care payments, security deposits, rental arrears, utility assistance, and training and technical assistance for CoC staff and providers. CoCBuilds-specific uses include acquisition of property, rehabilitation of property, new construction, project-based rental assistance, supportive services (case management, life skills, healthcare, etc.), operating costs, and administrative costs. Also includes housing assistance, operations, acquisition, rehabilitation, demolition, construction, lease, repair, lead-based paint hazard reduction, and relocation assistance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland. CoC geographic service areas as designated by HUD, which may include tribal areas and reservations. Projects must be located within FY 2024 CoC Program Registration geographic areas; exception for Tribal reservations and trust lands which may be temporarily added.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a Letter of Intent by the deadline to receive competition updates. structured_extraction.program_description: A public campaign financing program for Prince George's County that provides matching funds to candidates running for county office (County Executive, At-Large County Councilmember, or District Councilmember). The program promotes broader access to elected office and reduces the influence of large donations by supporting candidates who raise small donations from ordinary residents and receive matching funds from the Fair Election Fund.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Matching public contributions for qualified campaign contributions from Prince George's County residents. Contributions must be $1–$250 per donor. Maximum public contributions are $750,000 (County Executive), $200,000 (At-Large Council Member), and $75,000 (District Council Member). Funds are distributed during the distribution period, which begins 365 days before the primary election and ends 15 days after the general election (for the November 2026 election: June 30, 2025 through November 18, 2026).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Last Tuesday in February of the election year (9pm) to file Notice of Intent and Certificate of Candidacy; 45 calendar days before primary election ends the Qualifying Period; primary or general election date (11:59 PM) for receipt submission. For the 2026 election cycle: February 24, 2026 for filing Notice of Intent and candidacy.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Prince George's County residents running for covered county elective offices: County Executive, At-Large County Councilmember, or District Councilmember.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Campaign expenses directly related to election campaign activities for candidates running for covered county elective office in Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to candidates running for elected office in Prince George's County, Maryland. Qualifying contributions must come from Prince George's County residents; contributions from non-residents are permitted but do not qualify for the public match.
requirements_list: Must be a candidate for County Executive, At-Large County Councilmember, or District Councilmember in Prince George's County
File Notice of Intent before accepting contributions (or 24 months prior to primary election if pre-existing campaign account has activity)
Collect required number of qualifying contributions (specific amounts vary by office)
Register committee through MDCRIS
Open a citizen-funded campaign bank account with EIN
Obtain EIN (Form SS-4) from IRS
Contributions must be $1–$250 per donor aggregate
All contributions must have signed receipts with contributor name, residential address, and date
Candidate/spouse may contribute or loan up to $6,000 total (does not qualify for match)
Must certify candidate with State Board of Elections before receiving public funds
File campaign finance reports through MDCRIS
Cannot accept contributions from organizations, PACs, corporations, or non-residents
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: File a Notice of Intent and Certificate of Candidacy by the last Tuesday in February of the election year. Register a campaign committee through MDCRIS, open a citizen-funded campaign bank account, and collect qualifying contributions during the Qualifying Period (which ends 45 calendar days before the primary election). Submit receipts and apply for certification with the Maryland State Board of Elections to receive matching public funds. Contact the Fair Election Fund Commission at fairelections@co.pg.md.us or visit the commission's webpage for a Program Summary Guide.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides support to caregivers — including family members, friends, and community members — who care for adults age 60 and older. The program helps caregivers make decisions, identify benefits, and solve problems for individuals who may be losing their ability to live independently. It also connects caregivers with support groups, problem-solving resources, education, and respite care, and provides information on programs, services, and benefits for both the caregiver and the person receiving care.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides information and assistance to family caregivers, including help with decision-making, identifying benefits, and problem-solving. Also connects caregivers with support groups, education, and respite care related to caring for older adults.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Family caregivers, friends, and community members who provide care to individuals age 60 and older in Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Caregiver support, decision-making assistance, benefits identification, program navigation, support groups, problem-solving resources, education, and respite care.

requirements_list: Caregiver must be providing care to an individual age 60 or older
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Aging and Disabilities Services Division by phone at 301-265-8450.

structured_extraction.program_description: Family Preservation is an intensive home-based service for families in Prince George's County whose children are at imminent risk of being placed outside the home. A team of a social worker and a case associate works with the family to build on its strengths. The program serves families in crisis due to physical or mental illness, environmental issues, high risk of child maltreatment, or court orders related to neglect or abuse, as well as families reunifying with children after foster care.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Intensive home-based services delivered by a team of a social worker and a case associate. Services focus on building family strengths and preventing out-of-home placement of children. Referrals are made through the Abuse, Neglect and Services Intake line.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families in Prince George's County whose children are at imminent risk of out-of-home placement, families reunifying after foster care, and families under court order due to neglect or abuse.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Intensive home-based support services to keep families together and prevent children from being placed outside the home.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Prince George's County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Children must be at imminent risk of out-of-home placement, OR family is reunifying after foster care, OR family is under court order due to neglect or abuse
Referral required through the Abuse, Neglect and Services Intake number (301-909-2450)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Abuse, Neglect and Services Intake line at 301-909-2450 to request a referral to the Family Preservation program. Interpretation services are available for non-English speakers and deaf or hard-of-hearing individuals.

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary program for Housing Choice Voucher and Public Housing participants in Prince George's County. Participants sign a 5-year contract with the Housing Authority and receive supportive services such as education and job training to help them become economically independent and increase their earned income while reducing reliance on welfare assistance and rental subsidies. When a family's income rises and they pay higher rent, the difference between the old and new rent is credited to a personal escrow account that participants can access upon successful completion of the contract.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive supportive services including education and job training over a 5-year contract period. A personal escrow account is built up as the family's income increases and their rent payment rises — the difference between the old and new rent amount is credited to this escrow account, which participants can access upon successful completion of the 5-year contract.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Housing Choice Voucher Program and Public Housing participants in Prince George's County, including residents of public housing developments such as Cottage City Towers, Kimberly Gardens, Marlborough Towne, Rollingcrest Village, and Owens Road.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Escrow savings can be used by participants upon successful completion of the 5-year contract. Training and supportive services help participants gain employment and economic independence, increasing earned income and reducing dependency on welfare and rental subsidies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Housing Choice Voucher and Public Housing participants in Prince George's County, Maryland, including residents of public housing developments: Cottage City Towers, Kimberly Gardens, Marlborough Towne, Rollingcrest Village, and Owens Road.
requirements_list: Must be a Housing Choice Voucher Program or Public Housing participant
Must be a HUD-assisted family
Head of household must enter a 5-year contract with the Housing Authority
Participation is voluntary
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible Housing Choice Voucher or Public Housing participants contact the Prince George's County Housing Authority to enroll and sign a 5-year self-sufficiency contract.

structured_extraction.program_description: A 12-month program for families with children ages 6 to 18 who are overweight or obese. The program focuses on healthy eating, physical activity, and positive parenting to help families make lasting healthy lifestyle changes. Participants attend two 1-hour virtual group classes per month led by an FBT interventionist, plus individualized sessions with a dietitian and follow-up with a primary care provider.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Families receive 4 hours of individual family assessment, 22 hours of group-based behavioral treatment, and 2 hours of individualized medical nutrition therapy (1 hour in each 6-month period). A primary care provider follows up every 6 months to track weight status. Group cohorts consist of 2 to 10 families. Enrollment is rolling.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with children ages 6 to 18 who are overweight or obese living in Prince George's County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participation in behavioral health and nutrition support services aimed at improving healthy eating, physical activity, metabolic health, self-esteem, and parenting skills
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a family with at least one child between ages 6 and 18
Child must be overweight or obese
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Participation Interest Form available on the county website to express interest in joining a cohort. Enrollment is rolling and cohorts consist of 2 to 10 families.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Financial reimbursement for adjusting commute timing to reduce peak congestion.

Must delay trip during peak congestion times to qualify
