structured_extraction.program_name: Flexible Spending Account (FSA) - Health Care and Dependent Care
structured_extraction.program_description: Prince George's County offers benefits-eligible county employees two pre-tax flexible spending accounts (FSAs): a Health Care FSA and a Dependent Care FSA. These accounts let employees set aside pre-tax dollars to pay for eligible out-of-pocket health care and dependent care expenses. Accounts are administered by Voya Financial and must be renewed annually during open enrollment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Employees can contribute up to $3,050 per year to the Health Care FSA (with up to $610 rollover of unused funds) and up to $5,000 per year to the Dependent Care FSA. Contributions are deducted from gross pay pre-tax, reducing federal and Social Security tax liability. The full annual Health Care FSA election is available for reimbursement before all contributions are collected. All expense receipts must be submitted by March 31 of each calendar year.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Must renew each year during open enrollment for the following plan year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Benefits-eligible Prince George's County government employees
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Health Care FSA: eligible health care expenses including deductibles, copayments, coinsurance, eye exams, glasses, contact lenses, prescription drugs, dental care, orthodontia, and OTC products. Dependent Care FSA: eligible dependent care expenses such as licensed day care, in-home care, elder care, day camp, and nursery school for dependents under age 13.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Prince George's County government employees.
requirements_list: Must be a benefits-eligible Prince George's County government employee
Must enroll or re-enroll each year during open enrollment
Health Care FSA: contribute up to $3,050 per year
Dependent Care FSA: contribute up to $5,000 per year (single or married filing jointly)
All expense receipts must be submitted by March 31 of each calendar year
You do not need to enroll in a County medical plan to participate in the Health Care FSA
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Enroll during the annual open enrollment period each year. If enrollment is not completed, the FSA will be canceled. Accounts are administered through Voya Financial (1-888-401-3539).

structured_extraction.program_name: Flood Control Program – Endangered Structures Acquisition
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides funding to acquire residential properties located within the 100-year floodplain that are vulnerable to natural hazards such as slope failure or stream erosion. Properties are evaluated and prioritized based on flood risk severity and availability of state and federal grant funding.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Funding may be available to acquire residential properties in the 100-year floodplain that are at risk from flood-related natural hazards. Funding availability depends on state and federal grant opportunities. Acquisitions are prioritized by the severity of flood risk.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential property owners in Prince George's County whose properties lie within the 100-year floodplain and are at risk from slope failure or stream erosion.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition of at-risk residential properties in the 100-year floodplain.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Limited to Prince George's County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Property must be located within the 100-year floodplain
Property must be vulnerable to slope failure or stream erosion
Acquisition eligibility is based on severity of flood risk and availability of grant funding
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Properties are evaluated and prioritized based on flood risk severity and availability of state and federal grant funding. No formal application process described on this page.

structured_extraction.program_name: Flood Protection & Drainage Improvement Capital Improvements Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Plans, designs, and constructs flood protection and drainage improvement projects that address severe threats to residential structures in Prince George's County. Projects focus on frequent home flooding, severe road flooding, and erosion problems, and are prioritized using a three-tier system based on severity and proximity to homes.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The county funds planning, design, and construction of flood protection and drainage improvement projects. Eligible projects include frequent home flooding (water entering the living area), severe road flooding not under the Department of Public Works and Transportation, flood control system certification, municipal participation, storm drain acceptance, and flood warning systems. Water quality improvements are incorporated where possible. Property owners benefiting from projects must provide a right of entry and easement to the county at no cost.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential property owners in Prince George's County experiencing flooding or erosion problems that threaten habitable structures.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planning, design, and construction of flood protection and drainage improvement infrastructure projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Limited to Prince George's County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Projects must address severe threats to residential, habitable structures
Eligible projects include frequent home flooding (water entering the habitable structure) or severe road flooding not under county Public Works jurisdiction
Property owners must provide right of entry and easement to the county at no cost
Projects are prioritized by a 3-tier system based on severity and proximity to residential structures
Priority I: frequent damage to habitable residential structures or severe rare damage, or erosion threatening structural integrity
Priority II: rare damage to habitable structures, high dangerous flow near habitable areas, severe erosion safety hazards, or serious street flooding
Priority III: frequent excessive stormwater flows, severe channel or property erosion, or protection of stream ecosystems
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Problems are categorized and prioritized using a three-tier system. All sites are evaluated for cost versus benefit. No formal application process is described on this page.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Foster Grandparents Program places volunteers aged 55 and older with at-risk children and youth throughout Prince George's County in community settings such as schools, hospitals, drug treatment centers, jails, and day care centers. Participants volunteer a minimum of 15 hours per week, providing one-on-one daily attention to help young people grow, build self-confidence, and become productive members of society. Eligible participants may receive a stipend if they meet income eligibility requirements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible participants may receive a small stipend for volunteering a minimum of 15 hours per week with at-risk children and youth, subject to income eligibility requirements.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults aged 55 and older who want to volunteer with at-risk children and youth in Prince George's County. Stipend available for income-eligible participants.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Stipend provided to eligible volunteers serving at-risk children and youth.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be at least 55 years old
Must volunteer a minimum of 15 hours per week
Must meet income eligibility requirements to receive a stipend
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Foster Grandparent Program at 301-265-8450 for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Free Smoke Alarm and Fire Safety Advisory Inspection
structured_extraction.program_description: The Prince George's County Fire/EMS Department visits eligible homeowners' residences to conduct a free fire safety advisory inspection and install free battery-operated smoke and carbon monoxide alarms. The program aims to improve home fire safety for county residents, protect them from fire and carbon monoxide hazards, and reduce fire-related 911 calls. Also includes community education on smoke alarm safety and operation, and distribution of free smoke and/or CO alarms as a public service to encourage fire and life safety and prevent injury, death, and property loss. Note: hard-wired smoke alarms are not replaced or installed by the department; homeowners with hard-wired smoke alarms are responsible for their own replacement and installation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A free in-home fire safety advisory inspection and installation of free battery-operated smoke and carbon monoxide alarms (one alarm per household) by Fire/EMS personnel. Also includes distribution of free smoke alarms, CO alarms, or combination smoke/CO alarms, and educational information on smoke alarm safety. Hard-wired smoke alarms are not replaced or installed by the department.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Prince George's County homeowners and residents seeking free fire safety inspection and smoke alarm or carbon monoxide alarm installation. Applicants must be homeowners of single-family dwellings in Prince George's County. Applicants must not have hard-wired smoke detectors, or must understand the department will not replace hard-wired units.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: In-home fire safety advisory inspection and installation of free battery-operated smoke and carbon monoxide alarms in the qualifying owner-occupied residence. Alarms may also be distributed (not installed) to eligible residents.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of single-family dwellings in Prince George's County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a resident of Prince George's County
Must be a homeowner of the residence
Single-family dwelling
Only one free smoke alarm issued per household
Residence must have no working smoke alarms
Residence must have no hardwired alarms; homeowners with hard-wired smoke alarms are responsible for their own replacement and installation
Recipient must sign liability release form (Smoke and/or Carbon Monoxide Alarm Distribution Liability Release Form)
Monthly checking/maintenance of alarms required for effectiveness
Must complete the Free Smoke Alarm and Fire Safety Advisory Inspection form
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Free Smoke Alarm and Fire Safety Advisory Inspection form to request a visit from the Fire/EMS Department, or call the Prince George's County Fire/EMS Watch Office at 301-583-2200 (available 24/7) or 301-883-5250 (Mon-Fri) to arrange a smoke alarm installation and fire safety advisory inspection visit. For alarm distribution, recipient completes and signs the Smoke and/or Carbon Monoxide Alarm Distribution Liability Release Form.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides retirement benefits to General Service Employees of Prince George's County Government who participate in the Maryland State Retirement and Pension System or the Prince George's Supplemental Pension Plans. Employees can apply for service retirement by submitting a completed retirement application packet to the Retirement Services Division.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Monthly pension payments through the Maryland State Retirement and Pension System or the Prince George's County Supplemental Pension Plans (General Schedule, Police Civilian, Fire Civilian, AFSCME, or Crossing Guards). Payment options include survivor benefit options and a 50% survivor option for eligible spouse. Benefits are paid via direct deposit (electronic funds transfer) starting on the first day of the month following separation from employment. Employees may also elect federal and state income tax withholding from pension/annuity payments. Upon separation, accrued unused annual and sick leave may be disposed of via cash payment, rollover to financial institution, conversion for retirement credit, or retention on leave record.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No later than 60 days prior to desired retirement date
structured_extraction.program_audience: General Service Employees of Prince George's County Government enrolled in the Maryland State Retirement and Pension System or a Supplemental Pension Plan, as well as retirees, beneficiaries, and alternate payees receiving pension or annuity payments
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Retirement income for eligible county employees; disposition of accrued unused annual and sick leave upon separation from service
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland government employees only
requirements_list: Must be a General Service Employee of Prince George's County Government
Must be enrolled in the Maryland State Retirement and Pension System or a Prince George's County Supplemental Pension Plan
Must submit completed retirement packet at least 60 days before desired retirement date
Retirement date must be the first day of the month following separation from employment
Application must be signed and dated in the presence of a notary
Employee ID number (EID) and Social Security number required
Selection of retirement type (Normal or Vested) and retirement allowance option (Unreduced or 50% Option)
Proof of contingent annuitant's date of birth (if applicable)

For electronic funds transfer: account must be held in payee's name only; voided personal check, deposit slip, or bank statement required for verification; must notify Benefits and Pensions Division of any account changes; separate form required for each type of request
Benefits cannot be assigned to another person
Must have federal and state tax withholding (W-4P) form on file; subject to IRS penalties for insufficient tax payment
Leave Disposition Authorization form must be completed with separation date; authorization becomes irrevocable 10 working days after effective separation date
For rollover of leave balance: separate fund transfer application required and certified by accepting financial institution
For retirement credit option (civilians): only sick leave can be applied to Maryland State Pension Plan
For leave donation option: leave donation form must be completed prior to separation date
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Service Retirement Application Packet including all required forms for your plan type. Submit completed forms and supporting documentation by email to pensions@co.pg.md.us or by fax to 301-883-6360 at least 60 days before your desired retirement date. Additionally, complete an Authorization Agreement for Electronic Funds Transfer with bank verification document for direct deposit of benefits, a W-4P Tax Withholding Form to elect federal and state income tax withholding, and a Leave Disposition Authorization Form to specify disposition of accrued unused leave upon separation.

structured_extraction.program_description: A scholarship awarded in memory of Congresswoman Gladys Noon Spellman, presented by Prince George's County Office of the County Executive during Women's History Month. The scholarship recognizes 12th grade residents of Prince George's County who demonstrate academic achievement, community service, and extracurricular involvement.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Scholarship award presented at the Annual Women's International History Month Luncheon. Specific dollar amount not stated on this page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: 12th grade students who are residents of Prince George's County, Maryland, accepted into a college, university, or accredited vocational institution.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational expenses (scholarship for post-secondary education or accredited vocational training).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicant must be a resident of Prince George's County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a resident of Prince George's County, Maryland
Must be in the 12th grade and accepted into a college, university, or accredited alternative vocational institution
Must be involved in extracurricular school activities and non-school activities
Must provide examples of community service
Must have a GPA of 2.5 or above
Must be able to attend the Annual Women's International History Month Luncheon on March 26, 2026, in person
Must submit an unofficial copy of high school transcript
Must submit a copy of most current report card
Must submit two letters of reference (from a School Counselor/Teacher/Administrator and a non-family member)
Must submit an original essay of at least 1,500 words in Times New Roman, 12 pt., double-spaced, responding to one of two provided prompts
Must create a 30-second YouTube Unlisted video and submit the link
Application must be submitted via the WHML Portal by March 11, 2026, at 11:59 pm

Include an unofficial high school transcript, most recent report card, two letters of reference, and an original essay responding to one of two provided prompts. Also create and submit a link to a 30-second unlisted YouTube video. References are submitted separately via the Submit References link.

structured_extraction.program_description: A structured seven-week training program that helps small businesses and entrepreneurs understand and navigate government contracting. Sessions cover foundational knowledge, marketing strategies, proposal development techniques, and compliance guidance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Seven-week virtual training program (with an in-person graduation) held every Tuesday from 9 AM to 12 PM. Class size is limited to 25-30 individuals. Topics include government contracting basics, marketing strategies, proposal development, and compliance guidance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses and entrepreneurs seeking to understand and participate in government contracting.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and education on government contracting processes, marketing, proposal development, and compliance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program offered through Prince George's County Economic Development Corporation; primarily serves Prince George's County.
requirements_list: Application must be submitted between March 26, 2025 and April 9, 2025
Registration does not guarantee successful enrollment
Class size limited to 25-30 individuals
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application through the PGCEDC events calendar registration link between March 26 and April 9, 2025. Registration does not guarantee enrollment.

structured_extraction.program_description: An 'economic gardening' business development initiative funded by the American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) that offers comprehensive training and technical support programs to help local businesses grow and compete. The initiative focuses on empowering BIPOC women, Latino, and women entrepreneurs with equitable access to skills and growth opportunities. Programs cover topics such as business finance, podcast media, website essentials, business valuation, AI adoption for business operations, government contracting and procurement (CertifyPG & Prosper Certification Training), and a Spanish-language small business accelerator (0 to 100 Accelerator Program, in partnership with M&T Bank). The initiative has impacted over 1,050 businesses and helped create an estimated 115 jobs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free training programs delivered through multiple tracks including: AI for Small Business (hands-on AI training for business operations), CertifyPG & Prosper Certification Training (government contracting and procurement expertise), 0 to 100 Accelerator Program (Spanish-language small business training in partnership with M&T Bank), and a broader training series covering business finance, podcast media, website essentials, business valuation, and small business development. All programs are offered at no cost to remove barriers related to access to technical support and technology tools.
structured_extraction.program_audience: BIPOC women, Latino, and women-owned small to mid-sized businesses in Prince George's County that have surpassed the startup phase and are seeking growth strategies, as well as Latino small business owners seeking Spanish-language programming.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business training and technical assistance, including AI adoption, government contracting certification, financial literacy, media, digital presence, business valuation, and business growth strategies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to businesses located in Prince George's County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Business owner must be BIPOC, Latino, or a woman
Business must be an established small to mid-sized firm that has surpassed the startup phase
Business must be located in Prince George's County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individual program events are listed on the PGCEDC events calendar. Interested participants can register through the links provided for each specific program. Visit www.PGCEDC.com for information on future programming cohorts.

structured_extraction.program_name: HOME Investment Partnership Program (HOME) Multi-Family Development Program (Prince George's County)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides gap financing for real estate developers to build affordable housing developments for families and individuals with income below 80% of the Area Median Income (AMI).
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Gap financing for real estate developers to construct affordable housing developments.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Real estate developers building affordable housing for low- to moderate-income families and individuals.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction of affordable housing developments for households earning below 80% of Area Median Income.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Project must serve households with income below 80% of Area Median Income

structured_extraction.program_description: Federal block grant program under HUD designed to create affordable housing for low-income households. Prince George's County is a Participating Jurisdiction (PJ) receiving HOME funds from HUD. The Department of Housing and Community Development utilizes the allocation to provide gap financing for building, buying, and/or rehabilitating affordable rental and homeowner housing, supports nonprofit and for-profit developers to produce and rehabilitate housing, assists first-time homebuyers to purchase homes, acquires or improves group homes for special populations, and supports Community Housing Development Organizations (CHDOs) to create housing opportunities for households with limited income. Includes a special additional allocation through the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021 (HOME-ARP).
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance is provided primarily as subordinate loans (gap financing) for affordable multifamily rental housing projects. Standard HOME loans: up to $2,500,000 (exceptions at Director's discretion), 2% simple interest during permanent loan period, 0% during construction, 40-year amortization, generally coterminous with Senior Loan(s), secured by subordinate lien Deed of Trust, prepayment allowed without penalty if affordability requirements are met. HOME-ARP loans: up to 100% of Total Development Costs for HOME-ARP Assisted Units plus up to $45,000 per unit operating cost assistance reserve, 2% simple interest during permanent loan period, 0% during construction, up to 40-year term and amortization, annual payments due by April 30, $50,000 legal fee due at closing. County receives approximately $3.5 million annually from HUD. Requires 25-cent County match per dollar of HOME funds spent and a minimum 10:1 leverage ratio. Assistance amount subject to HOME Subsidy Limits set by HUD. Additional forms of assistance include grants, real estate tax abatement or PILOT, waiver of local fees, and land donation or long-term leasing.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis or via NOFA as determined by the Director; PILOT requests must be submitted no later than four months in advance of anticipated close of construction financing.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit and for-profit housing developers, first-time homebuyers, Community Housing Development Organizations (CHDOs), developers of group homes for special populations, and developers/sponsors of affordable multifamily rental housing (including senior housing) in Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Production and rehabilitation of affordable housing, first-time homebuyer assistance, acquisition or improvement of group homes for special populations, support for CHDOs, acquisition costs, site preparation and infrastructure, construction and rehabilitation costs, financing costs, professional fees, developer fees, operating and replacement reserves, syndication costs for LIHTC projects, green building/energy-efficiency improvements, supportive services for residents, and operating cost assistance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland. Priority given to projects within one mile of the Blue Line transit corridor, within one mile of the Purple Line transit corridor, and within one mile of existing and planned MDOT Metro Stations throughout the County. Projects must conform to the Prince George's County 2035 General Plan.
requirements_list: Projects must comply with Federal lead-based paint regulations under the Housing and Community Development Act of 1992
Projects must meet the minimum affordability period for each type of eligible activity
Beneficiaries must meet HUD HOME income limits (published annually)
Assistance amount is subject to HOME Subsidy Limits
Compliance with 24 CFR Part 92 and HOME regulations
Affirmative Fair Housing Marketing Plan (HUD Form 935) required
Davis-Bacon Fair Labor Standards apply for projects with 12 or more units
Section 3 compliance required (35% Section 3 workers; 5% Targeted Section 3 workers)
30% of development costs to County-Based Small Businesses
Developers/Sponsors must have demonstrated experience in successful development and completion of affordable housing projects in the immediate past five years
Borrowers must have business registrations in good standing
Development team members must not be suspended, debarred, or ineligible for federal funds
Firm financing commitments from all sources required
Detailed project budget with itemized costs required
Third-party appraisal required
Projects must demonstrate long-term financial viability and self-sustaining operations
Projects must maintain adequate operating and capital reserve funds
Sufficient debt service coverage required
All PILOT allocations must be approved by resolution of Prince George's County Council
Minimum HOME subsidy: $1,000 per unit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Projects are evaluated on a project-by-project basis throughout the fiscal year. The Director may accept applications on a rolling basis or issue a Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA). Interested applicants should contact the DHCD Housing Development Division. Loan terms are outlined in the HOME Loan Term Sheet and HOME ARP Loan Term Sheet. Underwriting follows the HOME Underwriting Guidelines Policies and Procedures Manual.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Healthy Beginnings Program promotes healthy pregnancy outcomes and early health care practices for infants and children. Nurses and support staff provide case management through assessments, interventions, and referrals to help clients address psychosocial and behavioral risk factors associated with poor health and developmental outcomes. The program serves pregnant women, women of childbearing age, women who have experienced pregnancy loss, and caregivers of infants up to 24 months of age who reside in Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free telephonic and home-visiting case management services including teaching preventive health practices and self-care, counseling on healthy behaviors, and helping clients access community resources. Services promote healthy pregnancy outcomes and early health care practices for infants and children. No fees are charged.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Pregnant women with risk factors associated with poor pregnancy outcomes; women of childbearing age who desire to become pregnant in the next 12–18 months; women who have experienced a miscarriage, stillbirth, or infant loss; infants and children up to age 2 with risk factors associated with poor health and developmental outcomes; and caregivers of new infants (e.g., grandparents, childcare providers, family members) — all residing in Prince George's County, Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Case management services including health education, counseling on healthy behaviors, referrals to community resources, and promotion of healthy pregnancy outcomes and early health care for infants and children.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a resident of Prince George's County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a Prince George's County, Maryland resident
Pregnant women must have a risk factor associated with poor pregnancy outcomes
Women of childbearing age who desire to become pregnant in the next 12–18 months
Women who have an infant under 24 months of age
Women who have experienced a miscarriage, stillbirth, or infant loss
Infants and children must be up to age 2 and have risk factors associated with poor health and developmental outcomes
Any resident involved in the care of a new infant (e.g., grandparents, childcare providers, family members)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Referrals are accepted from individuals, family members, physicians, managed care organizations, health care workers, hospitals, and government and community agencies. Contact the program at 3003 Hospital Drive, Suite 2061, Cheverly, MD 20785, Monday through Friday 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., excluding holidays. Phone: 301-583-3384.

structured_extraction.program_description: A 4-month program that offers self-monitoring, lifestyle coaching, and nutrition education classes to help adults with high blood pressure (hypertension) achieve and maintain healthy blood pressure levels. Participants receive tools to measure blood pressure at home, monthly nutrition education seminars, and two consultations per month.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A 4-month program providing personalized guidance, blood pressure monitoring tools, monthly 60-minute nutrition education seminars, and two 10-to-15-minute consultations per month.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults (18+) diagnosed with high blood pressure or on anti-hypertensive medication, who have not had a recent cardiac event and do not have certain heart conditions or lymphedema.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Managing high blood pressure through lifestyle coaching, nutrition education, and self-monitoring.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be at least 18 years old
Must have been diagnosed with high blood pressure and/or be on anti-hypertensive medication
Must not have experienced a cardiac event within the last 12 months
Must not have atrial fibrillation or other arrhythmias
Must not have or be at risk for lymphedema
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Email wellnessinfo@co.pg.md.us, call (301) 856-9465, or text (240) 990-7563 to register. Registration deadline was February 28, 2026, and registration is currently closed.

structured_extraction.program_description: Uses SAMHSA funding to provide mental health and supportive services for Prince George's County young adult residents aged 16 to 25 who are diagnosed with or at risk of developing serious mental health conditions. The program specifically supports those entering or aging out of foster care and those entering or transitioning out of the juvenile justice system, as well as unhoused youth. It connects young adults to mental health resources, makes services easier to access, and supports approximately 275 participants through coordinated, individualized care plans and community-based mental health services. Services include needs-based assessments, strength-based individualized care planning, educational and enrichment activities, employment assistance, peer support, behavioral health services, and youth advocacy opportunities through a partnership-based approach.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Comprehensive support services for transition-age youth including needs-based assessments, strength-based individualized care planning, referrals to behavioral health treatment, supported employment, educational and enrichment activities, peer support, crisis prevention, trauma- and grief-informed therapy, life skills training (soft skills, cooking, budgeting, apartment hunting, cleaning), group peer-to-peer sessions, and care coordination for housing and employment. Services are provided through contracted providers including Maryland Family Resource Inc., iMind Behavioral Health, Maryland Coalition of Families, and Pathways. The program is part of Prince George's County's Project Live initiative and is connected to the Youth Move national initiative.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Prince George's County young adult residents aged 16 to 25 who are diagnosed with or at risk of developing serious mental health conditions, particularly those entering or aging out of foster care, entering or transitioning out of the juvenile justice system, or who are unhoused. Also serves families of individuals with mental health, substance use, or problem gambling challenges.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Behavioral health and mental health services, supported employment, educational and enrichment activities, care coordination, crisis prevention, trauma- and grief-informed treatment, life skills development, peer support, and referrals to community resources.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Prince George's County resident aged 16 to 25.
requirements_list: Must be a Prince George's County resident
Aged 16 to 25 (some provider services available up to age 26)
Diagnosed with or at risk of developing serious mental health conditions
May be entering or aging out of foster care, or entering or transitioning out of juvenile justice care and custody
Unhoused youth are also eligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Referrals can come from the Department of Social Services, Department of Juvenile Services, Prince George's County Public Schools, or through self-referral. Once submitted, the Department of Family Services receives the referral for further action. Complete the SOC and Healthy Transitions Referral Form at sochtreferral.princegeorgescountymd.gov. A Transition Specialist then meets with the participant to complete a needs-based assessment and collaborates to create a strength-based individualized care plan, followed by referrals to appropriate services.

structured_extraction.program_name: High Technology Facilities Real Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A real property tax credit for businesses in high technology industries — such as biotechnology, information technology, defense, aerospace, engineering, life sciences, and energy — that construct or expand facilities and create new jobs in Prince George's County. The credit applies to the increased value of the property for five years: 100% in year one, decreasing by 20% each year to 20% in year five.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Real property tax credit against county property taxes for high technology manufacturing, fabrication, assembling, or research and development facilities that construct or expand in Prince George's County. The credit applies to the increased assessed value of the property for five years: 100% in year one, 80% in year two, 60% in year three, 40% in year four, and 20% in year five. Businesses must invest at least $500,000 in construction or expansion, add at least 5,000 square feet of gross floor area, and create at least 10 new permanent full-time positions within three years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: High technology businesses in manufacturing, fabrication, assembling, or research and development (including engineering, life sciences, and computer sciences) that are constructing or expanding facilities in Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Credit against county real property taxes on the increased assessed value of qualifying high technology facilities for up to five years.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Business must be primarily involved in high technology manufacturing, fabrication, assembling, or R&D (including engineering, life sciences, and computer sciences) as determined by the County Executive
Must construct or expand a building within the County with at least 5,000 square feet of gross floor area
Must invest at least $500,000 in the construction or expansion
Must create at least 10 new permanent full-time positions in the new or expanded building within three years
Relocation of existing positions or reclassification of existing positions does not count as new positions

Application must include legal description of property, written description of business activity, floor plans, documentation of minimum investment, copy of valid Use and Occupancy permit, and any other information required by the Director of Finance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: An eligible business first applies for the tax credit through the Economic Development Corporation (EDC). The EDC reviews the application, and then the County's Finance Department must approve the project. The application must include a legal description of the property, a written description of the company's business activity, floor plans, proof of minimum investment, a valid Use and Occupancy permit, and any other required information. Submit to the Director of Finance.

structured_extraction.program_description: A workforce program that connects local job seekers (dislocated workers) with employment and training opportunities in Prince George's County. The program helps employers develop training programs tailored to their needs and reimburses a portion of training and on-the-job training salary costs when they hire local dislocated workers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Employers can receive reimbursement of up to 50% of training costs and up to 90% of on-the-job training salary costs for up to six months when they hire local dislocated workers. The program also provides employment-related services and job placement assistance to dislocated workers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local dislocated workers seeking employment and companies in Prince George's County looking to hire and train local talent.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training cost reimbursement for employers; employment and training services for dislocated workers including on-the-job training salary reimbursement.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Employers must hire local dislocated workers
Training programs must be developed around skills employers are seeking
Salary reimbursement available for up to six months of on-the-job training
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Jeffrey Swilley at jswilley@co.pg.md.us or call 301-618-8400 for information about employment, training, and recruiting opportunities through the program.

structured_extraction.program_description: A home rehabilitation program that provides grants and financial assistance to low- and moderate-income owner-occupied homeowners in Prince George's County to repair and upgrade deteriorated single-family homes. The program addresses health, safety, energy efficiency, and accessibility needs, bringing homes up to contemporary minimum property standards and eliminating housing code violations. Administered in partnership with Habitat for Humanity of Metro Maryland, a nonprofit partner of the Prince George's County Department of Housing and Community Development.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $30,000 for eligible homeowners. Households under 50% of the area median income (AMI) can receive up to $50,000 in services. Services may include roofing and gutters, electrical repair, plumbing repair, tree removal, stairlift and accessibility equipment, HVAC replacement and repair, and water heater replacement/repair. Financial assistance is also available for rehabilitation of single-family homes to bring them up to contemporary minimum property standards, including elimination of housing code violations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owner-occupied homeowners of limited financial means in Prince George's County, particularly those with household income under 50% of the area median income, with deteriorated single-family homes in need of repair or rehabilitation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Health, safety, energy efficiency, and accessibility repairs and home rehabilitation including roofing, gutters, electrical, plumbing, tree removal, stairlifts, HVAC, water heater work, and elimination of housing code violations to meet minimum property standards.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must own and occupy a home in Prince George's County
Household income must meet program eligibility limits (limited financial means)
Must own a single-family home
Home must need rehabilitation to meet minimum property standards or address health, safety, energy efficiency, or accessibility issues
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an inquiry via Habitat for Humanity of Metro Maryland's website or by mail (call 301-990-0014 x 19). Applications are only forwarded to those recorded on the inquiry list. Visit the Habitat for Humanity Metro Maryland website for full application details.

structured_extraction.program_description: Helps Prince George's County residents who are at immediate risk of losing their housing by stabilizing their situation before a crisis occurs. Support includes short-term rental assistance, landlord mediation, case management, and referrals to community resources to prevent eviction and promote long-term housing stability.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Short-term rental assistance, landlord mediation, case management, and referrals to community resources to prevent eviction and stabilize housing.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Prince George's County residents at imminent risk of homelessness
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental assistance and housing stabilization services
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a Prince George's County resident
Must be at imminent risk of homelessness

structured_extraction.program_name: Housing Authority of Prince George's County - Public Housing Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Federally funded public housing program that provides affordable rental housing to eligible low-income residents of Prince George's County. The Housing Authority of Prince George's County owns and manages approximately 392 units of public and assisted housing, including 376 public housing units (296 for elderly and disabled residents and 80 family units) and 16 assisted housing units at Coral Gardens, across five properties. Units are funded by HUD operating subsidies and tenant rental revenues, and must meet rigorous housing quality standards. The program provides housing assistance to eligible low-income families, individuals, elderly persons, and disabled persons who meet HUD income limits and additional Housing Authority standards.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Subsidized affordable rental housing units available to eligible low-income individuals and families. The program includes approximately 376 public housing units funded by HUD operating subsidies and tenant rental revenues, including 296 units for elderly and disabled residents and 80 family units, plus 16 assisted housing units at Coral Gardens, across five properties in Prince George's County. All units must meet rigorous housing quality standards.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income individuals and families, elderly residents, and people with disabilities in Prince George's County. The head of household or spouse must be at least 18 years old or an emancipated minor.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Affordable rental housing assistance provided at subsidized rates to eligible families and individuals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents and applicants in Prince George's County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must qualify as a 'family' as defined in the Housing Authority's Administrative Plan (can be a single individual or group of persons, with or without children)
Applicant must be within the appropriate income limits set by HUD
Head of household or spouse must be at least 18 years of age or an emancipated minor under State law
All family members aged six and older must provide a Social Security number
Applicant must furnish a declaration of Citizenship or Eligible Immigrant Status and verification where required
At least one family member must be a U.S. citizen or have eligible immigration status
Must meet federal eligibility requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Housing Assistance Division (HAD) of the Housing Authority of Prince George's County. Applicants must submit required documentation including Social Security numbers for all family members aged 6 and older and proof of citizenship or eligible immigration status.

structured_extraction.program_description: Converts a Housing Choice Voucher (HCV) rental subsidy into a homeownership subsidy, helping first-time homebuyers in Prince George's County purchase their own home instead of using the voucher to pay rent to a landlord.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A monthly voucher subsidy previously used for rental payments is redirected to help cover homeownership costs for eligible first-time homebuyers. Financial and programmatic support is provided for Housing Choice Voucher holders to purchase homes.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Current Housing Choice Voucher (HCV) Program participants in good standing who are first-time homebuyers in Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchasing a home — the voucher subsidy is applied toward homeownership costs instead of rental payments.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Prince George's County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a current participant of the Housing Choice Voucher Program in good standing
Must be a Housing Choice Voucher holder for at least 1 year
Must be a first-time homebuyer who has not owned a home in the last 3 years
Must have a good rental payment history for the last 12 months
Must have consistent full-time employment history during the last 12 months (waived for disabled/elderly)
Must have a minimum annual income of $30,000 (waived for disabled/elderly)
Must have a minimum credit score of 620
No fraud or compliance reviews in the last 3 years
No prior mortgage loan defaults
Must complete a homebuyer education workshop
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and submit the Homeownership Program Application to hcvhomeownership@co.pg.md.us. Applications are processed within a 60-day period.

structured_extraction.program_description: Free online training sessions that educate rental property owners and managers about how the Housing Choice Voucher (Section 8) Program works, including program rules, regulations, and requirements for participating landlords.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free monthly online briefing sessions held from 9:30 AM to 12:00 PM. Sessions are designed to help landlords understand how to participate in the Housing Choice Voucher Program, including rules and regulations for contracting with the local housing agency.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Rental property owners and managers interested in participating in the Housing Choice Voucher (Section 8) Program in Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Education and guidance on participating in the Housing Choice Voucher Program.

The receiving housing authority takes over administration of the voucher. Voucher payment and occupancy standards apply. Participants must find a qualifying unit within the voucher search period.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental housing assistance (subsidy paid on behalf of tenant) in the new jurisdiction of residence.

Participants who are residents of or employed in Prince George's County at the time of their initial interview qualify for portability immediately; others must wait one year (unless initial PHA allows early portability).

To port into Prince George's County, contact your current housing authority caseworker, who will mail, fax, or email the portability packet to the Housing Authority of Prince George's County at 9200 Basil Court, Largo, MD 20774.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Housing Choice Voucher Program (also called Section 8) is a federal tenant-based rental assistance program administered by the Housing Authority of Prince George's County (HAPGC) that helps low-income families, elderly individuals, and people with disabilities afford safe, decent housing of their choice in the private market. HAPGC issues vouchers that cover a portion of rent and utilities up to maximum payment standards set by zip code. HAPGC pays the landlord the difference between 30% of the family's adjusted income and the determined payment standard or actual gross rent, whichever is lower. Families may choose a unit with higher rent and pay the difference, up to 40% of adjusted income. Payment standards (maximum limits including rent and utilities) vary by zip code and unit size, ranging from efficiency up to 7-bedroom units. For example, a 2-bedroom unit in zip code 20720 has a maximum of $3,597 per month, while a 2-bedroom in zip code 20712 has a maximum of $1,804 per month (effective January 1, 2026). In certain circumstances, families may also use their voucher to purchase a modest home. Applicants are placed on a waitlist through a lottery system that randomly selects 5,000 applicants; current Emergency Housing Voucher (EHV) participants are automatically added to the waitlist without going through the lottery and receive the highest preference ranking, but must verify current EHV participation. Current voucher holders use their voucher to rent a unit from a participating landlord, and the Housing Authority pays a portion of the rent directly to the landlord on the tenant's behalf. Vouchers are valid for an initial 60-day period from issuance; families must submit a Request for Tenancy and unsigned lease within that period unless an extension is granted. The Housing Authority encourages voucher holders to search in specific higher-opportunity zip codes and also maintains listings of accessible units. Landlords who participate receive housing assistance payments directly from HAPGC on behalf of eligible tenants, and can receive payments via direct deposit. In Fiscal Year 2026, 5,986 vouchers were administered.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Monthly rental subsidy paid directly to landlords on behalf of eligible families. HAPGC pays the landlord the difference between 30% of the family's adjusted income and the payment standard or gross rent (whichever is lower). Families may pay up to 40% of adjusted income if they choose a unit with rent above the payment standard. Payment standards (maximum limits including rent and utilities) vary by zip code and unit size, ranging from efficiency up to 7-bedroom units. For example, a 2-bedroom unit in zip code 20720 has a maximum of $3,597 per month, while a 2-bedroom in zip code 20712 has a maximum of $1,804 per month (effective January 1, 2026). The Housing Authority must approve contract rent based on Rent Reasonableness criteria, and the unit must pass a Housing Quality Standards inspection. Vouchers are valid for an initial 60-day period from issuance; families must submit a Request for Tenancy and unsigned lease within that period unless an extension is granted. In certain circumstances, the voucher may also be used toward a home purchase. Landlords can receive housing assistance payments via direct deposit. Eligible applicants are placed on a waitlist through a lottery that randomly selects 5,000 applicants; current Emergency Housing Voucher (EHV) participants are automatically added to the waitlist without going through the lottery. In Fiscal Year 2026, 5,986 vouchers were administered.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Waiting list closed Friday, December 5, 2025 at 11:59 p.m. EST
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income families, elderly individuals, and people with disabilities seeking rental assistance in Prince George's County, including current Housing Choice Voucher holders searching for a rental unit; and landlords and property owners in Prince George's County who want to rent to low-income households using Housing Choice Vouchers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental assistance — subsidizes the cost of renting housing of the tenant's choice in Prince George's County, including rent and utility payments for privately owned housing units that meet Housing Quality Standards, units in higher-opportunity areas, and units with accessible features. May also be used toward home purchase in certain circumstances. For landlords, covers the gap between the tenant's share of rent and the total rental amount.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Prince George's County, Maryland. Payment standards vary by zip code. The Housing Authority encourages voucher holders to search in specific higher-opportunity zip codes: 20601, 20613, 20623, 20715, 20716, 20720, 20721, 20735, 20772, 20774.
requirements_list: Must meet federal eligibility requirements for low-income households
Must be a U.S. citizen or eligible non-citizen
Must apply during an open waitlist period
Applicants are selected through a lottery system (5,000 spots available)

Current Emergency Housing Voucher (EHV) participants are automatically added to the waitlist without going through the lottery and receive the highest preference ranking, but must verify current EHV participation
Must complete eligibility verification and provide required documentation if selected

Must keep contact information current (notify HAPGC in writing of any changes to address, phone number, or email) if selected for the waitlist; changes may be submitted to hcvwaitlist@co.pg.md.us or through the Applicant Portal
Must be a current Housing Choice Voucher holder to use the voucher for a rental unit
Families must report all income and all household members to determine subsidy level and bedroom size
Voucher is valid for an initial 60 calendar days from date of issuance
Family must submit a Request for Tenancy and unsigned lease within the 60-day period unless an extension is granted
Written extension requests must be received before the voucher expiration date
Unit must be located within the Housing Authority of Prince George's County jurisdiction
Unit must pass a Housing Quality Standards inspection to meet quality standards
Contract rent must be approved based on Rent Reasonableness criteria
Landlord must obtain a Rental License in Prince George's County
Landlord must list the property with the Housing Authority

For landlord direct deposit: voided check (for checking account) or bank direct deposit form (for savings account) required; bank documentation confirming account number, routing number, and account holder name; account name must match landlord's name; email address required for direct deposit stubs; signed authorization form with printed name, signature, date, and SSN/EIN
Reasonable accommodations available for individuals with disabilities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Tenants: Submit a preliminary application through the online portal during the open application window (December 1–5, 2025). A lottery randomly selects 5,000 applicants for the waitlist. Selected applicants are notified by email and mail at least 45 days after the waitlist closes, then must complete eligibility verification and submit required documents. Once a voucher is issued, the family has 60 days to find a qualifying unit, submit a Request for Tenancy and unsigned lease, and have the unit pass inspection. Written requests for extensions must be submitted before the voucher expires. Current voucher holders search available unit listings by bedroom size on the Housing Authority website (including general units, units in higher-opportunity areas, and units with accessible features). Once a unit is selected, it must be inspected by the Housing Authority before move-in. In certain circumstances, vouchers may be used toward a home purchase. Landlords: List the property with the Housing Authority and complete a New Landlord Packet. Apply for a Rental License and ensure the property meets housing quality standards. Payments can be received via direct deposit by completing the HAPGC Landlord HAP Direct Deposit Authorization form and mailing it with supporting documentation to HAPGC, Attn: FAS. Rent increase requests can be submitted by landlords via email to HCVRentincreases@co.pg.md.us. Applications are processed through the Housing Choice Voucher Division (HCVD) of the Housing Authority of Prince George's County.

structured_extraction.program_name: Housing Choice Voucher Program – Moving Process
structured_extraction.program_description: Helps current Housing Choice Voucher (Section 8) participants move to a new rental unit. The Housing Authority reviews the new unit for approval, conducts a Housing Quality Standards inspection, and sets up a Housing Assistance Payments contract with the new landlord so the participant can use their voucher at the new address.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rental assistance provided through the Housing Choice Voucher Program. The Housing Authority makes Housing Assistance Payments (HAP) on behalf of the tenant to the owner of a privately-owned rental unit after the unit passes a Housing Quality Standards inspection and the contract rent is approved. Participants are assigned a Move Specialist who issues the voucher and move packet and provides ongoing support. Portability to other housing authorities is available after one year. No security deposit assistance is provided.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: 60 calendar days from voucher issuance (initial term)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Current Housing Choice Voucher Program participants in Prince George's County who want to move to a new rental unit.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental assistance payments (Housing Assistance Payments) to a new landlord for an approved privately-owned unit. Move expenses including security deposit, movers, and truck rental are the participant's responsibility.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Housing Choice Voucher participants in Prince George's County, Maryland. Portability/transfer to other housing authorities is available after residing in the county for one year.
requirements_list: Submit a signed Request for Tenancy Approval
Provide a copy of the unsigned lease from the prospective owner
Provide proof of paid utility bills on the current unit
Provide a copy of your written 30-day notice to vacate
New unit must pass a Housing Quality Standards (HQS) inspection
Contract rent must be approved including lease dates and terms
Owner must provide a Rental License issued by Prince George's County Department of Permitting, Inspections and Enforcement (DPIE)
Participants are responsible for their own security deposit, moving expenses, and screening fees
Must be in good standing with current landlord and Housing Authority
Attend virtual voucher issuance briefing within 10 days of move request form submission
Must report household composition, income, or asset changes within 10 days
Must complete recertification if notice received during or after move process
Move-out date must be the last day of the month (not the first)
Tenant must return keys to landlord on vacate date
Both tenant and landlord must sign the Notice of Intent to Vacate form and original must be returned to the PHA
Reside in current unit one year or be 90 days from lease end before moving
Complete move package in its entirety
Neither tenant nor household members can be related to the unit owner
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Read the moving guide. Step 2: Complete the Request to Move/Transfer form and submit to the Leasing Department. Step 3: Attend virtual voucher issuance briefing within 10 days of form submission; a Move Specialist is assigned and issues the voucher and move packet. Step 4: Return completed move package in its entirety, including signed Request for Tenancy Approval, unsigned lease, proof of paid utility bills, and 30-day notice to vacate. Step 5: Complete the contracting process — Housing Authority schedules an HQS inspection and performs a rent reasonableness review; if deficiencies are found, the owner must repair them before re-inspection; once the unit passes and rent is approved, tenant and owner sign the lease and the owner signs the Housing Assistance Payments Contract. Step 6: Follow ongoing requirements including reporting changes in household composition, income, or assets within 10 days. Also complete the Notice of Intent to Vacate form, obtain signatures from both tenant and landlord, and return the original to the PHA.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Housing Investment Trust Fund (HITF) provides flexible gap financing for acquisition, rehabilitation, and new construction of affordable and workforce multifamily rental housing in Prince George's County. Established in 2012 to address foreclosure-related challenges and amended in 2017 to include gap financing for workforce and affordable housing development, it targets households earning up to 120% of the area median income (AMI). The fund is supported by at least 20% of the county's collected recordation taxes (minimum $10 million annually as of 2021), and is authorized under Section 10-296 et seq. of the Prince George's County Code.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Subordinate loan financing up to $2,500,000 (exceptions may be approved by the Director). Interest rate is 0% during construction and 2% simple interest during the permanent loan period. Loan term is generally up to 40 years, coterminous with Senior Loan(s), with up to 40-year amortization from the beginning of the permanent loan period. No repayments are due during construction; during the permanent period, repayment comes from surplus cash flow after Senior Loan debt service (lesser of 75% of surplus cash flow or the full amortization amount). Prepayable without penalty. A legal fee of $50,000 is due at closing. Collateral is a subordinate lien Deed of Trust. Grants for predevelopment costs may also be available at the Director's discretion. Funded from the County's collected property recordation tax and other designated County funds. Projects are reviewed on a project-by-project basis throughout the fiscal year.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Jonathan R. Butler, Director; Ashley P. Johnson-Hare, Deputy Director
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit and for-profit developers, Community Housing Development Organizations (CHDOs), faith-based organizations, and community development corporations producing or rehabilitating affordable and workforce multifamily rental housing for households earning up to 120% of the area median income, including low-income homeowners, seniors, families, households with disabilities, and people experiencing homelessness.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: New construction, rehabilitation, and preservation of workforce and affordable multifamily rental housing; home repairs and rehabilitation; energy efficiency upgrades; accessibility improvements; roof and window replacements; health and safety improvements; homeownership preservation; training and technical assistance for faith-based housing development.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland. Funding priorities include areas within one mile of the Blue Line transit corridor, within one mile of the Purple Line transit corridor, and within one mile of existing and planned MDOT Metro Stations throughout the County.
requirements_list: Developers/Sponsors must have demonstrated experience in successful development and completion of affordable housing projects in the immediate past five years
Borrower and managing entities must have business registrations in good standing
Development team members cannot be suspended, debarred, or otherwise ineligible
Projects must incorporate a minimum affordability period for each type of eligible activity (generally 40-year affordability restrictions)
DHCD applies HOME program underwriting guidelines and procedures to HITF; exceptions may be applied at the DHCD Director's discretion
HOME and HITF funds may not be used for the same unit within a project
Income and rent limits set by HUD apply
Income restrictions of 30%–120% AMI depending on program
Legal fee of $50,000 due at closing
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Projects are reviewed and funded on a project-by-project basis throughout the fiscal year. Applicants should refer to the HITF Term Sheet for financing terms. The development team must be approved by the Department.

structured_extraction.program_name: Housing Opportunities for Persons With AIDS (HOPWA)
structured_extraction.program_description: HOPWA is a federal entitlement program that provides funding to address the housing needs of people living with HIV/AIDS and their families. In the Washington, D.C. region, including Prince George's, Charles, and Calvert counties in Maryland, the program is administered through the District of Columbia's HIV/AIDS Hepatitis/STD/TB Administration (HAHSTA). HOPWA funds are distributed by HUD using a formula based on AIDS case statistics from the CDC. Local housing services and information are delivered through the Metropolitan Housing Access Program (MHAP), run by Housing Counseling Services, Inc. The program provides voucher-based rental assistance, emergency housing assistance, and supportive services to individuals and families living with HIV/AIDS. Three quarters of formula funding goes to states and metropolitan areas with the highest number of AIDS cases; one quarter goes to areas with above-average per capita incidence of AIDS.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal grant funding allocated annually by HUD to provide housing assistance and supportive services for persons with HIV/AIDS and their families. HOPWA funds are distributed by HUD using a formula based on AIDS case statistics from the CDC. Three quarters of formula funding goes to states and metropolitan areas with the highest number of AIDS cases; one quarter goes to areas with above-average per capita incidence of AIDS. Assistance includes voucher-based rental assistance, emergency housing assistance, housing services, and housing information for people living with HIV/AIDS, delivered locally through the Metropolitan Housing Access Program (MHAP).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Persons living with HIV/AIDS and their families in Prince George's County, Charles County, and Calvert County, Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Housing assistance, rental costs, emergency housing assistance, housing services, and housing information for persons living with HIV/AIDS and their families.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Charles County, and Calvert County, Maryland, as part of the Washington, D.C. Eligible Metropolitan Area.
requirements_list: Must be a person living with HIV/AIDS or their family member
Must reside in Prince George's County, Charles County, or Calvert County, Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Housing Counseling Services, Inc. (HCS) at 202-667-7006 or visit http://housingetc.org/metropolitan-housing-access-program-mhap-prince-georges-county-md/ to learn about available MHAP services in Prince George's County.

structured_extraction.program_name: Improvements to Historic Resources Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides a property tax credit for expenses incurred in restoring or preserving structures with historic, architectural, or cultural value that are classified as Historic Sites or Historic Districts in Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax credit for restoration, preservation, or new construction on qualifying historic structures. The credit applies for the tax year immediately following the year work (or any portion thereof) is completed. Claims may be filed within 5 years of completion. If taxes were paid during the credit period, a refund is issued. Unused portions of the credit can be carried over within the same 5-year period.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of structures classified as Historic Sites or Historic Districts on the Adopted and Approved Historic Sites and Districts Plan of Prince George's County, or structures recommended for such classification by the Historic Preservation Commission.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Offset of expenses for restoration, preservation, or new construction on qualifying historic structures.

requirements_list: Structure must be classified as a Historic Site or Historic District on the Adopted and Approved Historic Sites and Districts Plan of Prince George's County, or recommended for such classification by the Historic Preservation Commission
Expenses must be for restoration, preservation, or new construction
Application must be filed within 5 years of completion of work
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit applications and receipts to the Historic Preservation Commission.

structured_extraction.program_description: A CDC-recognized 26-week lifestyle change program for people at high risk for type 2 diabetes. structured_extraction.program_audience: Southern Maryland residents aged 18 or older who are at high risk for type 2 diabetes (prediabetes blood test results, prior gestational diabetes, or a high-risk score on the CDC Prediabetes Risk Test) and not previously diagnosed with type 1 or type 2 diabetes.

structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Serves Southern Maryland residents.

structured_extraction.program_name: Pathway to Purchase Home Buyer Assistance Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A first-time homebuyer assistance program administered by the Prince George's County Department of Housing and Community Development that helps eligible residents purchase a home in the county. The program provides up to $50,000 in financial assistance, including down payment, mortgage principal reduction, and/or closing cost support, for the purchase of for-sale, foreclosed, or owner-occupied short-sale residential properties. Funded by the HOME Investment Partnerships Program (HOME) established under Title II of the Cranston-Gonzalez National Affordable Housing Act. Assistance is provided as a 0% interest deferred payment loan secured by a promissory note and deed of trust, forgiven after 10 years if the home remains the borrower's primary residence. A graduated recapture schedule applies if the property is sold or transferred before the 10-year period ends. Income limits (up to 80% of Area Median Income), housing counseling requirements, and property quality standards apply. Applicants must use a participating lender and an approved title company, and the property must pass a Housing Quality Standards (HQS) inspection.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $50,000 in down payment, mortgage principal reduction, and/or closing cost assistance for eligible first-time homebuyers purchasing residential properties in Prince George's County. Assistance is provided as a 0% interest deferred payment loan secured as a second trust on the property. The loan is forgiven after 10 years if the home remains the borrower's primary residence; a graduated recapture schedule applies if the property is sold or transferred before the 10-year affordability period ends. Income limits apply: household income must not exceed 80% AMI ($91,800–$173,100 depending on household size). Purchase price limits: $448,000 for resale properties, $485,000 for new construction. Eligible property types include single-family homes, townhouses, and condominiums (new construction, resales, foreclosures, or short sales). Funds must be used for acquisition of the property only and are disbursed at settlement.
structured_extraction.program_audience: First-time homebuyers who have not owned a home in the past 3 years, are at least 18 years old, and have household incomes at or below 80% of Area Median Income, purchasing residential properties in Prince George's County, Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment assistance, mortgage principal reduction, and/or closing cost assistance for the purchase of single-family homes, townhouses, or condominiums (new construction, resales, foreclosures, or short sales) in Prince George's County. Funds must be used for acquisition of the property only and are disbursed at settlement. Funds cannot be used for repairs, reimbursements to buyer, cash back at closing, or tenant relocation activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available for home purchases within Prince George's County, Maryland. All zip codes within Prince George's County are eligible. Property cannot be located in FEMA-identified special flood hazard areas unless the property participates in the National Flood Insurance Program.
requirements_list: Must be a first-time homebuyer (no residential property ownership in the past 3 years)
Must meet program income limits: gross annual household income not to exceed 80% AMI for Prince George's County ($91,800–$173,100 depending on household size)
Must be at least 18 years old
Debt-to-income ratios: estimated mortgage payment must not exceed 35% of monthly income; total monthly debt must not exceed 47% of monthly income
Must use a Certified Participating Lender
Must complete a minimum 8-hour HUD-certified housing counseling course
Must use an approved housing counseling agency
Must use an approved title company
Property must pass a Housing Quality Standards (HQS) inspection by American Property Consultants, Inc.

All utilities must be operational; smoke/CO detectors installed; no paint chipping/peeling; appliances clean and working; permanent heating system; hot/cold water; working toilet/shower; no plumbing leaks; windows/doors operational with locks; electrical outlets/switches functional with cover plates; roof must not leak; proper handrails/guardrails; unit free from roaches/rodents
All deficiencies identified in HQS Inspection and FHA Appraisal must be corrected prior to closing
Imminent threats to life, health, or safety must be corrected prior to occupancy
Independent home inspection required (unless newly constructed with use and occupancy certificate)
Executed sales contract with at least 21 business days remaining at time of application (60 days to settlement per homebuyer kit)
Property purchase price must not exceed $448,000 (resale) or $485,000 (new construction)
Property must be a single-family home, townhouse, or condominium located in Prince George's County
Property must become and remain borrower's primary residence for 10-year affordability period
Not available for investors, rental properties, or second homes
Annual certification and proof of residency required
First mortgage loan cannot be adjustable rate or subprime
No current ownership or co-ownership of any property
No other liens, security interests, or encumbrances on borrower's right/title/interest except purchase money financing
Must not refinance senior mortgage, sell, transfer, lease, or cease using property as primary residence during loan term
Must comply with HOME Investment Partnerships Program requirements (24 CFR Part 570)
Must sign borrower and seller affidavits and other required forms including EEOC form and lead disclosure
Property cannot be acquired through tax foreclosure or eminent domain
Must provide income verification for all household members 18 and older
Must provide bank statements (60 days), W2s, tax transcripts, and federal tax returns (2 years)
Cannot receive cash back at closing
Certain fees must be paid outside of closing (earnest money, appraisal, credit report, hazard insurance, home inspection, termite report, HQS inspection)
Borrower must maintain liability and property hazard insurance
Multiple borrowers have joint and several liability
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Obtain pre-approval from a Certified Participating Lender (see 2026 Participating Lenders list). 2. Complete a minimum 8-hour HUD-certified housing counseling course through an approved housing counseling agency. 3. Obtain an executed sales contract with at least 21 business days remaining (60 days to settlement). 4. Submit a complete application package via email to Sandy Dixon (SVDixon@co.pg.md.us) including all required documentation: Program Loan Application, borrower and seller affidavits, EEOC form, lead disclosure, HUD Income Calculation Worksheet, property appraisal (within 60 days of contract), termite inspection report, passed HQS inspection, income verification for all household members 18+, identification documents, bank statements, W2s, tax transcripts, and federal tax returns. 5. Property must pass HQS inspection (submit HQS Inspection Request form and payment); submit HQS Move-in Inspection Checklist verifying all items are operational. 6. Upon approval, funds are disbursed at closing as a deferred payment second trust loan. Contact the Department of Housing and Community Development at 301-883-7327 or SVDixon@co.pg.md.us for more information.
