It offers education, clinical services, lab work, risk reduction counseling, and referrals to eligible HIV-negative individuals who are at risk of getting HIV through sex or injection drug use. PrEP is a daily pill that, when taken as prescribed, is highly effective at preventing HIV.

The program is delivered online in three phases: weekly sessions for the first phase, bi-weekly for the second, and monthly for the third.

structured_extraction.program_description: PreventionLink is a free program that connects primary care providers and patients to a network integrating clinical practice with evidence-based public health programs to prevent and manage chronic diseases such as diabetes, hypertension, heart disease, and stroke. The program serves both providers and patients in underserved areas of Prince George's, Charles, Calvert, and St. Mary's counties, with a noted five-year plan for broader Southern Maryland expansion. Participating providers receive technical assistance, care coordination support, access to a community of practice, and a bi-directional electronic referral system through the Chesapeake Regional Information System for our Patients (CRISP). Community Health Workers help patients address social barriers to care—including transportation, affordability, and social support—and PreventionLink advisors support practices with care planning, workflows, and quality improvement. For individual residents, PreventionLink connects participants with lifestyle coaches, certified health educators, and community health workers through online and in-person peer-supported programs to prevent chronic diseases and better manage diabetes, high blood pressure, or high cholesterol. The program uses health information technology to reduce hospitalizations and improve health outcomes for chronic disease patients, offering free or low-cost healthcare services including the National Diabetes Prevention Program (in-person and virtual) and Telehealth Diabetes Self-Management Education and Support.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Providers receive free technical assistance and practice coaching, access to a bi-directional electronic referral system through CRISP, Community Health Worker support for patients, care plan and workflow development, quality improvement coaching (including PDSA cycles), and participation in a quarterly Community of Practice for sharing best practices. For individual residents, the program provides free or low-cost access to lifestyle coaches, certified health educators, and community health workers through online and in-person sessions, including the National Diabetes Prevention Program (in-person and virtual, featuring 16 weekly sessions followed by monthly maintenance sessions, with a trained lifestyle coach, group support, and a goal of at least 5% weight loss) and Telehealth Diabetes Self-Management Education and Support. Participants can be referred by their doctor or fill out an interest form to be connected with program staff. The program integrates clinical and community-based chronic disease prevention and management programs to reduce hospitalizations and improve health outcomes.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Primary care practices in Prince George's, Charles, Calvert, or St. Mary's counties that serve patients with or at risk for diabetes, hypertension, or heart disease, as well as individual residents of Southern Maryland—particularly those in underserved communities—who want to prevent chronic disease or better manage diabetes, high blood pressure, or high cholesterol, and high-system utilizers with frequent hospitalizations. Also includes adults with prediabetes interested in lifestyle change programs to prevent or delay type 2 diabetes, and the general public interested in lowering cholesterol and improving heart health.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Technical assistance and support for chronic disease prevention and management, including access to clinical and community-based programs, lifestyle coaching, health education sessions, chronic disease management programs, diabetes prevention education, self-management support, and connection to medical professionals and community health workers. Not a traditional cash grant or loan program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must operate a primary care practice or reside in Prince George's, Charles, Calvert, or St. Mary's counties in Maryland, particularly in underserved areas of Southern Maryland. The program notes a five-year plan for broader Southern Maryland expansion.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For providers: Submit an interest form online at preventionlinkmd.com, call (301)-883-7220, or email PreventionLink@co.pg.md.us. Once enrolled, sign required agreements including a Business Associate Agreement, Data Exchange Agreement, Memorandum of Understanding, and Commitment Form. For individual residents: Ask your doctor for a referral to PreventionLink or complete the Participant Interest form online. Your doctor will determine your eligibility and refer you to the appropriate program. If you do not have a primary care doctor or your provider does not yet participate, fill out an interest form on the Prince George's County website or email PreventionLink@co.pg.md.us and a representative will follow up to speak with PreventionLink staff or community health workers to determine eligibility. For the National Diabetes Prevention Program specifically, ask your physician for a referral to a CDC-recognized program.

structured_extraction.program_name: Prince George's County COVID-19 Business Relief Fund / Business Recovery Initiative (BRI)
structured_extraction.program_description: A county-funded relief program created to provide financial assistance to businesses in Prince George's County affected by the COVID-19 pandemic. Originally structured as low-cost loans (up to $100,000) and grants (up to $10,000), the program was modified in May 2020 to convert all assistance to grants using federal CARES Act funding and renamed the Business Recovery Initiative (BRI). The expanded $20 million program (supplemented by an additional $315,000 from Pepco Holdings and BGE) increased grant amounts up to $100,000 and broadened eligibility to include sole proprietors, 1099 contractors, and co-ops who were previously ineligible. Grants were distributed weekly to approved applicants, and supplemental wrap-around technical assistance to help businesses pivot to sustainable models was also planned.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Originally offered low-cost loans of up to $100,000 and grants of up to $10,000 to cover cash operating expenses. Following program modifications in May 2020, all assistance was converted to grants ranging from $5,000 to $100,000 from a $20 million fund (supplemented by $315,000 from Pepco Holdings and BGE), with previously approved loans up to $100,000 plus $10,000 grants converted to a maximum of $110,000 total in forgivable loans or grants. Award amounts are based on financial statement analysis, needs assessment, number of jobs affected, and documented losses caused by COVID-19. Grants were wired directly to approved businesses on a weekly basis. Complimentary wrap-around technical assistance to help businesses pivot to sustainable models was also being developed.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Small, local, and minority-owned businesses, sole proprietors, 1099 independent contractors, and co-ops in Prince George's County adversely affected by the COVID-19 pandemic

structured_extraction.program_name: Prince George's County Climate-Smart Local Producers Pilot Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A pilot program to develop and evaluate a Climate-Smart Local Producers Program that supports farmers and food producers — especially those from historically underserved communities — in adopting climate-smart practices in organic farming. The program addresses marketing of products grown using climate-smart practices, reduces barriers to practice implementation on existing and new farms, and promotes minority- and woman-owned farms in Prince George's County. The marketing strategy combines values of eating local, on-farm climate-smart practices, and woman/minority-owned farms. The program includes greenhouse gas reduction monitoring and analysis in partnership with Bowie State University, and aims to contribute to the availability of healthy food throughout the county. Funded by a $3.25 million USDA Partnerships for Climate-Smart Commodities grant, the program is currently under development.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program is funded by a $3.25 million USDA Partnerships for Climate-Smart Commodities grant awarded to Prince George's County. Funding supports farmers and producers in implementing climate-smart agricultural practices, with emphasis on historically underserved producers including beginning farmers, socially disadvantaged farmers, veteran farmers, limited resource farmers, women farmers, and specialty crop producers. Assistance includes climate-smart practice implementation support, marketing strategy development, greenhouse gas reduction measurement and monitoring (in partnership with Bowie State University), and technical assistance to reduce barriers to farm ownership and operation and expand access to green markets for local producers. The county plans to scale up and institutionalize pilot successes after the initial five-year USDA-funded project period.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers and food producers in Prince George's County, with a focus on historically underserved producers including beginning farmers, socially disadvantaged farmers, veteran farmers, limited resource farmers, women farmers, minority-owned farms, and specialty crop producers, as well as county residents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Implementing climate-smart and climate-centric farming practices, marketing strategy implementation for products grown using climate-smart practices, expanding access to green markets for local producers, reducing barriers for farm owners and operators, monitoring methodology development, greenhouse gas reduction analysis, and supporting healthy food availability throughout the county.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a farmer or food producer operating in Prince George's County
Must use or adopt climate-smart practices on farms

Priority given to historically underserved producers including beginning farmers, socially disadvantaged farmers, veteran farmers, limited resource farmers, women farmers, and specialty crop producers
Priority given to minority- and woman-owned farms
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The program is currently under development. The webpage asks visitors to monitor it for more information as it becomes available. No formal application process has been described yet.

structured_extraction.program_name: Prince George's County Comprehensive Pension Plan – Sworn Public Safety Employees
structured_extraction.program_description: A defined-benefit pension plan for sworn public safety employees of Prince George's County Government, including correctional officers, deputy sheriffs, firefighters, and police officers. Eligible employees can apply for service retirement by submitting a retirement application packet at least 60 days before their desired retirement date.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Monthly pension benefit paid to eligible sworn public safety employees (correctional officers, deputy sheriffs, firefighters, and police officers) upon retirement. Retirement begins on the first day of a month. Benefits are paid by direct deposit. Employees may also choose a survivor option for a beneficiary and may cash out, apply for additional pension credit, or donate unused leave.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No later than 60 days prior to desired retirement date
structured_extraction.program_audience: Sworn public safety employees of Prince George's County Government enrolled in the Correctional Officer Comprehensive Pension Plan, Deputy Sheriffs' Comprehensive Pension Plan, Fire Service Pension Plan, or Police Pension Plan.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Retirement income for eligible sworn public safety employees.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only to sworn public safety employees of Prince George's County Government.
requirements_list: Must be a sworn public safety employee of Prince George's County Government enrolled in one of the Comprehensive Pension Plans
Must submit completed retirement application packet to Retirement Services Division no later than 60 days before desired retirement date
Application for Retirement must be signed and dated before a notary
If a survivor option is chosen, proof of birth must be included for the beneficiary (only one beneficiary allowed)
Must provide direct deposit information with voided check or bank statement
Must complete tax withholding election form
Must complete leave disposition form
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the four required forms: (1) Application for Retirement specific to your pension plan, (2) Authorization Agreement for Electronic Funds Transfer (direct deposit), (3) Tax Withholding Election Form, and (4) Leave Disposition Form. Submit all completed forms and supporting documentation to Retirement Services Division by email at pensions@co.pg.md.us or fax at 301-883-6360 at least 60 days before the desired retirement date. Retirements take effect on the first day of each month.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Prince George's County procurement and business development program that pairs established large businesses (Mentors) with county-based certified small or minority-owned businesses (Protégés) to help Protégés grow their capacity to compete for government contracts. Protégés receive technical assistance, management assistance, financial assistance, business development support, and trade education through a formal 24-month Mentor-Protégé Team Agreement and Business Plan. Mentors and Protégés may also form joint ventures and pursue minority/small business set-aside contracts.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Protégés receive technical assistance, management assistance, financial assistance, business development support, and trade education from Mentors through a formal 24-month agreement. Mentors and Protégés may also form joint ventures and pursue minority/small business set-aside contracts at the prime level.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Established businesses seeking to serve as Mentors, and Prince George's County-certified small or minority-owned businesses (including certified Minority Business Enterprises) seeking to serve as Protégés to improve their ability to compete for government contracting opportunities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business development, technical and management capacity building, financial assistance, trade education, and preparation to compete for government contracts at the prime level.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to businesses operating in Prince George's County, Maryland. Protégés must be certified county-based small businesses or certified county-based Minority Business Enterprises (MBEs).
requirements_list: Mentors must meet the County's Responsibility criteria under Section XII of the County's Procurement Regulations
Mentors must be in good standing with local and state agencies
Mentors must have been in business for five or more years
Mentors must have successfully completed a minimum of 10 projects/contracts within the same NAICS code
Mentors must designate a senior-level officer committed to a 24-month agreement
Protégés must be a certified county-based small business or certified county-based Minority Business Enterprise
Protégés must designate a senior-level officer as company representative committed to a 24-month agreement with a mentor
Protégés must be willing to enter into a Team Agreement and Business Plan with their Mentor
Protégés must have a positive attitude and be receptive to information exchange with the assigned mentor
Mentor and Protégé must enter into a formal Mentor-Protégé Team Agreement and Business Plan after approval
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application to the Mentor-Protégé Committee. The Committee reviews applications within 14 business days of receipt. Approved Mentors and Protégés are notified and listed on the Business Highway website so firms can identify and contact each other. Once a pair is formed, they submit applications (or form a relationship and then apply), and upon approval, execute a formal Mentor-Protégé Team Agreement and Business Plan.

structured_extraction.program_name: Prince George's County Rain Check Rebate Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A partnership program between Prince George's County and the Chesapeake Bay Trust that provides rebates to property owners in Prince George's County who install approved stormwater management practices on their residential, commercial, or public properties. The program helps reduce stormwater runoff and improve water quality in local streams and rivers, and helps Prince George's County meet its Clean Water Act obligations. Eligible installations include rain barrels, cisterns, rain gardens, green roofs, permeable pavement, pavement removal, urban tree canopy plantings, and conservation landscaping. Rebate amounts vary by project type: cisterns ($2/gallon stored, 250-gallon minimum), conservation landscaping ($5/sq ft, 250 sq ft minimum), green roofs ($10–$20/sq ft, minimum 1/4 roof retrofit), pavement removal ($6/sq ft), permeable pavement ($12/sq ft), rain barrels ($2/gallon stored), rain gardens ($10/sq ft, 100 sq ft minimum), and urban tree canopy ($150/tree, minimum 5-foot height). The maximum lifetime rebate per residential property is $6,000; for commercial, multi-family, homeowner associations, condominium associations, civic associations, non-profit, and not-for-profit properties the maximum is $20,000. Properties within the City of Bowie are not eligible. Properties in Cheverly, University Park, and College Park are eligible only for cistern, green roof, pavement removal, permeable pavement, rain barrel, and rain garden projects (not urban tree canopy).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rebates are available for approved stormwater management practices installed on residential, commercial, and public properties. Rebate amounts vary by project type: cisterns ($2/gallon stored, 250-gallon minimum), conservation landscaping ($5/sq ft, 250 sq ft minimum), green roofs ($10–$20/sq ft, minimum 1/4 roof retrofit), pavement removal ($6/sq ft), permeable pavement ($12/sq ft), rain barrels ($2/gallon stored, minimum 50 gallons for residential or 100 gallons for commercial/organizational), rain gardens ($10/sq ft, 100 sq ft minimum), and urban tree canopy ($150/tree, minimum 5-foot height and 1/2-inch caliper, planted between October 1 and May 1 on private property). The maximum lifetime rebate per residential property is $6,000; for commercial, multi-family, homeowner associations, condominium associations, civic associations, non-profit, and not-for-profit properties the maximum is $20,000. Rebates are awarded on a first-come, first-served basis and cannot exceed the project's total cost. Applications must be submitted and approved within 12 months of the project completion date. Contractor training courses on rain check rebate practices are also available for landscape professionals.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Application must be approved within 12 months of the project completion date
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential property owners (including housing cooperatives), commercial property owners, homeowner associations, condominium associations, civic associations, multi-family dwellings, nonprofit organizations, not-for-profit organizations, and public property owners in Prince George's County. Also landscape professionals seeking contractor training. Excludes properties in the City of Bowie. Properties in Cheverly, University Park, and College Park are eligible only for cistern, green roof, pavement removal, permeable pavement, rain barrel, and rain garden projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of approved stormwater management practices including rain barrels, cisterns, rain gardens, green roofs, permeable pavement, pavement removal, urban tree canopy plantings (native trees on private property), and conservation landscaping on residential, commercial, or public property in Prince George's County. Contractor training on rain gardens, permeable paving, pavement removal, tree planting, rain barrels, and green roofs is also available.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to property owners within Prince George's County, Maryland. Properties within the City of Bowie are not eligible. Properties in the Town of Cheverly, Town of University Park, and City of College Park are eligible only for cistern, green roof, pavement removal, permeable pavement, rain barrel, and rain garden projects (urban tree canopy and conservation landscaping projects are not eligible in these municipalities). Properties within municipalities that have their own similar stormwater rebate programs are not eligible. Urban tree canopy projects must be on private property (not in public right-of-way).
requirements_list: Applicant must own the property, or be a non-profit organization with an agreement to complete a project on private or public land
Must install an eligible stormwater management practice on the property following DoE/CBT best practice guidelines and criteria
Property must be located in Prince George's County (City of Bowie properties are not eligible)
Property must not be located within a municipality that has its own similar stormwater management rebate program
Projects must be completed within 12 months of receiving pre-approval from the Chesapeake Bay Trust (CBT)
For rain barrels, receipt or invoice must be submitted within 12 months of application approval
Application must be approved within 12 months of the project completion date
CBT must inspect the completed project and confirm it complies with the approved application and County best practice guidelines
If the property is part of an HOA, applicant must provide documentation of HOA approval
Projects associated with permit requirements for new building construction, additions, or renovations are not eligible
All applicants must sign a property owner agreement; commercial and public project applicants must also sign an operations and maintenance agreement
Urban tree canopy projects are not eligible for properties in Cheverly, University Park, or College Park
Contractors must complete the Rain Check Rebate Contractor Training Course to be listed on the Contractor Training Completion List
Rebate amount cannot exceed the total project cost
For cisterns: minimum capacity of 250 gallons; cistern must be watertight with smooth interior surfaces and watertight lid; placed at least 10 feet from existing trees

For green roofs: must cover at least one-quarter of roof area; must replace existing roof area (not expand footprint); structural load analysis report from licensed structural engineer required; must be installed by certified green roof contractor
For pavement removal: minimum 400 square feet for commercial/organizational projects; no minimum for residential
For permeable pavement: no minimum for residential; minimum 400 square feet for commercial/organizational; professional licensed contractor installation required; slope must be less than 5%

For rain barrels: minimum storage capacity of 50 gallons for residential properties or 100 gallons for commercial/organizational properties; base must be level and stable; overflow outlet must direct away from building foundation; no permit required

For rain gardens: minimum 100 square feet; must be located at least 10 feet from home and neighboring home foundations; at least 25 feet from septic field or well head; gently sloped location receiving regular runoff; full or partial sun exposure; soil must drain within 24–36 hours (standing water drains within 4 hours per maintenance guidelines); bedrock and groundwater at least 2 feet below surface; must use native plant species; permit required if project exceeds 5,000 square feet and/or 100 cubic yards of earth movement

For urban tree canopy: trees must be native species; minimum tree height of 5 feet at planting; minimum caliper of 1/2 inch (at 6 inches above soil); planted in 5-gallon or larger biodegradable container or balled and burlapped; planting must occur between October 1 and May 1; trees must be planted on private property, not in public right-of-way; must be at least 3 feet from utilities, fences, walkways, driveways, decks, and patios; ash species (Fraxinus) not recommended due to emerald ash borer
Professional registration and MHIC certification required for contractors installing work
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Chesapeake Bay Trust (CBT) website at cbtrust.org/grants/prince-georges-county-rain-check-rebate. CBT pre-approves all applications before work begins (except rain barrels). After completing the project, submit all invoices and receipts to CBT for review. CBT conducts pre- and post-installation inspections. Rebates are awarded on a first-come, first-served basis. Additional information is available by calling 301-883-5810 or 410-974-2941. Landscape professionals interested in contractor training should contact dmpringle@co.pg.md.us to receive announcements of future training courses.

structured_extraction.program_name: Prince George's County Senior Nutrition Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides nutritious meals and related social, recreational, and educational opportunities to older adults in Prince George's County. The program has two parts: home-delivered meals for homebound seniors (hot meal delivered five days a week) and congregate meals served at senior centers, religious facilities, senior housing, and community centers. Transportation to congregate meal sites may also be available.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free or subsidized hot meals delivered to homebound older adults five days a week (Home-Delivered Meal program), and hot nutritious meals served at congregate sites such as senior centers and community centers (Congregate Meal program). Transportation to congregate meal sites may be provided. Each meal meets at least one-third of the Recommended Dietary Allowances for older adults.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Prince George's County residents who are at least 60 years of age, or who have a spouse who is 60 years of age and attends the program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Meals and nutrition support for eligible older adults.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Prince George's County, Maryland resident.
requirements_list: Must be a Prince George's County resident
Must be at least 60 years of age, OR have a spouse who is at least 60 years of age and attends the Senior Nutrition Program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Aging & Disabilities Services Division at 301-265-8450 or reach out to the specific nutrition site location nearest to you to make reservations.

structured_extraction.program_name: Prince George's County Small Business Support Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides grants and technical assistance to small businesses operating along the Blue and Purple Line transit corridors in Prince George's County. Businesses can apply for up to $20,000 in grant funding to support operations and growth.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Awards 25 grants of $20,000 each plus technical assistance. Total program funding is $500,000. Funds can be used for payroll, rent, utilities, marketing, technology, relocation services, capital improvements, and more.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payroll, rent, utilities, marketing, technology, relocation services, and capital improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must be operating along the Blue and Purple Line corridors in Prince George's County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Ten or fewer employees
Operating in the target corridor areas for at least three years
Demonstrate financial need
Compliance with applicable regulations
Show prospects for growth
Demonstrate positive community impact
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications were accepted between April 15 and May 13, 2024. Applicants apply through the Greater Washington Community Foundation (GWCF), which administers the grant program.

structured_extraction.program_name: Prince George's County Stormwater Stewardship Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Funds on-the-ground restoration and program activities that improve communities and water quality, and engages Prince George's County residents in the restoration and protection of local waterways. Established in 2012 as Stormwater Management Retrofit Program and expanded in 2013 with Local Watershed Protection and Restoration Fund. Eligible activities include water quality improvement, citizen awareness and engagement, technical assistance, tree planting, environmental education, and trash reduction in the Anacostia.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants awarded to eligible organizations for stormwater restoration and water quality improvement projects in Prince George's County. Eligible activities include stormwater management capital improvement projects, public education and outreach related to stormwater management or stream and wetland restoration, on-the-ground restoration and program activities, tree planting, environmental education, and trash reduction in the Anacostia watershed. Matching funds or in-kind services are not required but are preferred and considered during review. Specific grant amounts are not stated on this page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations, municipalities, faith-based organizations, educational institutions, community associations, civic groups, homeowners, businesses, county residents, and property owners in Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Stormwater management capital improvement projects, public education and outreach related to stormwater management or stream and wetland restoration, on-the-ground restoration and program activities, citizen awareness and engagement, technical assistance to churches, tree planting, environmental education, and trash reduction in the Anacostia watershed.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be implemented in Prince George's County, Maryland.

Projects must be implemented in Prince George's County
Applications are evaluated on quality, justification, partnerships, cost-effectiveness, likelihood of success, and demonstration value
Matching funds or in-kind services are preferred but not required
Likelihood of project success
Cost-effectiveness and appropriate budget items
Consistency with the request for proposals (application)
Sustainability
Justification
Partnerships
Demonstration

structured_extraction.program_name: Prince George's County Volunteer Internship Program
structured_extraction.program_description: An experiential learning program that gives students hands-on work experience in a Prince George's County government agency. Interns apply classroom knowledge to real work settings over a six-month period, gaining practical experience under professional supervision. Placements are unpaid.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Six-month unpaid internship placement in a county agency. Interns complete an orientation and sign a liability waiver. No financial compensation is provided; the benefit is practical work experience and professional development.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students currently enrolled in a trade school, community college, four-year college or university, or graduate program (including Master's, Doctoral, Law Degree, or Graduate Certificate programs).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Hands-on work experience in county government across interest areas including Customer Service, IT, Public Safety, Homeland Security/Emergency Management, Environmental Science, Public Administration, Trades, Engineering, Accounting, Human Resources, Criminal Justice, and more.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Internship placements are within Prince George's County government agencies located in the county.
requirements_list: Must be enrolled in a trade school, community college, four-year college/university, or graduate program
Graduate interns must be enrolled in a Master's, Doctoral, Law Degree, or Graduate Certificate program
Must submit a resume
Must submit official transcripts reflecting current level of education
Must submit three references, at least one of whom must be a faculty member or academic instructor (references must include full name, title, address, phone number, and email)
Must submit a double-spaced one- to three-page essay detailing interest area, academic study, and career objectives
Must complete an orientation upon acceptance
Must sign a waiver of liability upon acceptance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a resume, official transcripts, three references (at least one faculty member or academic instructor with full contact details), and a double-spaced one- to three-page essay about your interest area, academic study, and career goals. Applications are reviewed for placement in available interest areas.

structured_extraction.program_name: Prince George's County Youth CareerConnect Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A four-year STEM demonstration grant program that connects high school students in Prince George's County with workforce training, mentoring, and internship opportunities in healthcare and information technology. The program prepares students for employment immediately following high school graduation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides program participants with mentoring, skills training, paid summer internship and Capstone experiences, college entrance exam preparation, and college tours. Funded by a $7 million grant from the U.S. Department of Labor. A competitive scholarship is also available for YCC seniors heading to college.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Job readiness training, paid summer internships, mentoring, college exam preparation, and college tours
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to students at participating high schools in Prince George's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a high school student at a participating YCC school in Prince George's County

structured_extraction.program_name: Prince George's Federal Credit Union Government Shutdown Loan
structured_extraction.program_description: Prince George's Federal Credit Union offers a Government Shutdown Loan and related relief options to provide short-term financial relief to members affected by the federal government shutdown.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Government Shutdown Loan: up to $5,000 (max 2x member's monthly income), terms up to 24 months, flat rate 7.49% APR, no payments for up to 60 days, member must qualify under normal lending guidelines. Payment Deferrals: skip up to 2 months on qualified loans (excludes real estate, mobile home, and revolving loans). Waived Early-Withdrawal Penalty on CDs: no penalty on withdrawals up to $10,000.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Members of Prince George's Federal Credit Union affected by the federal government shutdown
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Essential expenses during the federal government shutdown; existing loan payments; short-term financial flexibility
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to members of Prince George's Federal Credit Union
requirements_list: Must be a member of Prince George's Federal Credit Union
Must qualify under normal lending guidelines for the Government Shutdown Loan
Loan amount cannot exceed 2x member's monthly income
Payment deferrals exclude real estate loans, mobile home loans, and revolving loans including credit cards
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply for the Government Shutdown Loan online via the link provided, or contact Prince George's Federal Credit Union at 301.627.2666, email Inquiries@PrinceGeorgesCFCU.org, or visit a branch.

structured_extraction.program_description: A bi-monthly event series that connects local businesses directly with public sector procurement opportunities. Each session focuses on one government agency or organization, giving attendees face-to-face access to procurement officers and contracting leads, sector-specific contract opportunities, and guidance on agency needs, timelines, and qualifications.

Each session provides direct access to procurement officers, real-time sector-specific contract opportunities, and targeted information about a specific agency's needs, timelines, and qualifications. The series launches July 22, 2025.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Project Based Voucher (PBV) Program provides affordable rental housing assistance at specific properties throughout Prince George's County. Unlike tenant-based vouchers, PBV assistance is tied to designated units at approved privately owned properties across 11 designated properties with 1–3 bedroom units. If a family moves out, the rental assistance stays with the unit, not the tenant. Eligible applicants are placed on a waitlist through a lottery process and, if selected, receive assistance to live in designated housing units.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rental assistance subsidy attached to specific affordable housing units at approved properties in Prince George's County. Assistance remains with the unit if the tenant moves out. Available at 11 designated properties with 1–3 bedroom units. Applicants are selected via lottery for placement on the waitlist, then must complete eligibility verification and provide required documentation before receiving assistance.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Tuesday, March 17, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. EST (waitlist now closed)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income households seeking affordable rental housing at specific properties in Prince George's County. Eligibility is based on household income, family size, and available unit size. Households cannot be enrolled in any other federally funded housing subsidy program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental assistance for housing at designated PBV properties in Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only at specific properties located throughout Prince George's County, Maryland, including Fort Washington, Capitol Heights, Upper Marlboro, Lanham, Glenarden, Bladensburg, Riverdale, Hyattsville, District Heights, and Clinton.
requirements_list: Must apply during the open waitlist period
Must be selected through the lottery process
Must complete eligibility verification if selected
Must provide required documentation if selected
Must notify HAPGC in writing of any changes to contact information if selected for the waitlist
Meet income eligibility requirements based on household income and family size
Household size must be appropriate for the available unit size
Cannot be currently enrolled in any other federally funded housing subsidy program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: When the waitlist opens, apply online through a Rent Café account (or create one). Applicants are randomly selected through a lottery. All applicants are notified of their status within 45 days of the application closing. Selected applicants are referred to an available PBV unit and must complete the property's screening process. Once the landlord approves the application, HAPGC reviews it for program eligibility.

structured_extraction.program_name: Project Based Voucher Accessibility Waiting List
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides accessible rental housing units to participants, residents, and applicants of HAPGC programs who have accessibility needs due to a disability. Government-funded program providing rental housing in privately owned and managed rental units (single-family homes, townhomes, or apartments). Rental cost is typically 30% of household adjusted gross income.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Placement on a separate waiting list for accessible rental units under the Project Based Voucher program. Units are in privately owned and managed properties with rental subsidy. Rental cost is typically 30% of household adjusted gross income. Accessible units are matched to the applicant's disability-related accessibility needs (physical, developmental, intellectual, emotional, or mental health disabilities). Only the Head of Household or Co-head may apply.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Current HAPGC Housing Choice Voucher participants, Public Housing residents, Project Based Voucher participants, Moderate Rehabilitation Program participants, and current applicants on any HAPGC waiting list who need an accessible unit due to a disability. Persons who are homeless and low-income households with disabilities are also served. Head of Household or Co-head must apply.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental housing assistance for accessible units meeting the applicant's disability-related accessibility needs. Accommodations for individuals with physical, developmental, intellectual, emotional, or mental health disabilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland. Preference for current residents and workers in Prince George's County. Program is administered by the Housing Authority of Prince George's County (HAPGC), 9200 Basil Court, Rm 500, Largo, MD 20774.
requirements_list: Must be a current participant of the HAPGC Housing Choice Voucher Program, OR a current resident of the HAPGC Public Housing Program, OR a current participant of the HAPGC Project Based Voucher Program, OR a current participant of the HAPGC Moderate Rehabilitation Program, OR a current applicant on a HAPGC waiting list
Must have a disability (physical, developmental, intellectual, emotional, or mental health)
Only the Head of Household or Co-head may apply; other household members cannot apply separately
Must provide household composition and income information on the preliminary application
Must complete the preliminary application with truthful and accurate information
Must notify the agency of any changes in address, status, or family composition
Cannot have outstanding debts from previous federally-funded housing programs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a completed PBVAWL preliminary application form with personal, household, income, and disability accommodation information to the 504 Coordinator at HAPGC's office (9200 Basil Court, Rm 500, Largo, MD 20774) by mail or in person. Applications can also be obtained online. Applicant must verify accuracy and sign the application. The agency will refer the applicant to the first available unit matching bedroom size and waiting list priority. Applications are accepted at any time; the waiting list remains open.

structured_extraction.program_description: Project HIRE is an apprenticeship program that provides individuals with developmental and/or intellectual disabilities between the ages of 18 and 25 a meaningful paid job training experience with a Prince George's County Government agency. Participants are placed within a host county agency for one year, where they can enhance current skills, learn new skills, and gain on-the-job work experience.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive a paid job training placement with a Prince George's County Government agency for one year. Participants work Monday through Friday for a maximum of 8 hours per day. Additionally, employers who hire program participants may be eligible for the Maryland Disability Employment Tax Credit (MDETC).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Prince George's County residents with intellectual or developmental disabilities between the ages of 18 and 25 who are associated with a supportive Employment Provider Agency.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Paid on-the-job training and work experience within a Prince George's County Government agency.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Prince George's County resident.
requirements_list: Must be a Prince George's County resident with an intellectual or developmental disability
Must be between 18 and 25 years of age
Must be available to work Monday through Friday for a maximum of 8 hours per day
Must be associated with a supportive Employment Provider Agency
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your supportive Employment Provider Agency, who will assist you in completing the Project HIRE application online. Employers or partners interested in participating should call (301) 265-8450.

structured_extraction.program_name: Public Safety Officer Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides a property tax credit of up to $2,500 against Prince George's County property taxes for qualified homeowners who are public safety officers, including firefighters, EMTs, correctional officers, police officers, dispatchers, deputy sheriffs, and eligible volunteer firefighters or EMTs employed by or serving Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $2,500 property tax credit against the County portion of property taxes. The credit cannot exceed the total County taxes due.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Vanessa Surles (for volunteer firefighters/EMTs); Donna Truitt (for M-NCPPC officers)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Prince George's County homeowners who are currently employed full-time as public safety officers by Prince George's County Government or a bi-county agency, or who are eligible volunteer firefighters/EMTs for the County Fire/EMS Department.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of County property taxes for eligible public safety officer homeowners.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Prince George's County homeowner.
requirements_list: Must be a qualified Prince George's County homeowner

Must meet the definition of Public Safety Officer: firefighter, EMT, correctional officer, police officer, dispatcher, deputy sheriff currently employed full-time by Prince George's County Government, an eligible volunteer firefighter or EMT, or a public safety officer employed full-time by a bi-county agency (e.g., M-NCPPC) predominantly in Prince George's County
Property must be applicant's principal residence
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: County employees apply through the credit application portal at https://propertytaxcredit.princegeorgescountymd.gov/. Volunteer firefighters/EMTs should contact Vanessa Surles. M-NCPPC officers should contact Donna Truitt. You will need your property tax account number. Applicants already determined eligible do not need to reapply.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF) Program forgives the remaining balance on Direct federal student loans for borrowers who work full-time for a qualifying government or not-for-profit employer and make 120 qualifying monthly payments under an accepted repayment plan. Created by Congress in October 2007 to encourage employment in the public service sector. A Temporary Expansion (TEPSLF) was authorized in March 2018 for borrowers ineligible for PSLF only due to ineligible repayment plans.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Forgiveness of remaining principal and interest on eligible Direct Loans after a borrower makes the equivalent of 120 qualifying monthly payments while employed full-time by a qualifying public service employer. Loans must not be in default and payments must be made under an eligible repayment plan.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Full-time employees of government agencies and qualifying not-for-profit organizations who have federal Direct Loans and are seeking forgiveness of remaining student loan debt after 120 qualifying payments
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Forgiveness of remaining federal student loan (Direct Loan) principal and interest balance after 120 qualifying payments
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to employees of qualifying U.S.-based public service employers; Prince George's County employees can submit their PSLF form through OHRM.
requirements_list: Be employed full-time (30+ hours/week average) by a U.S. federal, state, local, or tribal government agency, qualifying not-for-profit organization, AmeriCorps position, or Peace Corps full-time position
Have Direct Loans or consolidate other federal student loans into a Direct Loan
Repay loans under an income-driven repayment plan or a 10-year Standard Repayment Plan
Make a total of 120 qualifying monthly payments (need not be consecutive)
Loans must not be in default
Must be employed full-time by a qualifying employer at the time of application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a PSLF form using the PSLF Help Tool at studentaid.gov/pslf. You can complete and sign the form digitally, send it to your employer for digital certification, and submit electronically to MOHELA (the PSLF servicer). Alternatively, print and sign the form, submit to HRService@co.pg.md.us with a signed OHRM Employee Information Authorization Form, and then send the employer-signed form to MOHELA by mail, fax, or upload.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Adolescent Recovery Clubhouse of Prince George's County supports youth aged 12 to 17 with a history of substance use or at risk of substance use. The program offers a strengths-focused, talent-focused, and skills-based approach in a non-clinical, non-treatment setting. It provides empowering experiences through programs and activities to reduce substance use, prevent substance abuse, decrease juvenile delinquency, and develop age-appropriate life skills for healthy transition to adulthood. The program connects youth and families to resources for informed recovery decisions and has been shown to improve academic performance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free non-clinical support services including case management and advocacy, recovery support groups, educational tutoring and computer labs, GED and college preparation, vocational and skills training, job readiness and coaching, evidence-based life skills programs, and enriching field trips. Additional support is provided through referrals to treatment programs and community support systems. Intake includes assessment of presenting problem, mental health status, legal status, school status, family assessment, and identification of strengths, weaknesses, and high-risk behaviors.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Prince George's County residents aged 12 to 17 with a history of substance use or at risk of substance use, and their families. Includes those referred for counseling related to substance use or mental health concerns.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services support recovery, daily living skills, education, vocational readiness, and substance use prevention for adolescents. Includes intake assessments, case management, recovery support specialist appointments, and referrals to treatment and community support systems.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a resident of Prince George's County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a resident of Prince George's County
Ages 12 to 17
History of substance use or at risk of substance use
Strong desire to begin the recovery process
Must be referred to treatment before attending Clubhouse
May be referred for counseling services related to substance use or mental health concerns
Referral submission with completed referral form required for intake
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Recovery Clubhouse directly by phone or email, or submit a referral using the Recovery Clubhouse Referral Form. The intake process includes two appointments with a Recovery Support Specialist and assessments of presenting problem, mental health, legal status, school status, and family situation.

structured_extraction.program_description: A real property tax credit that encourages revitalization and redevelopment in existing communities in Prince George's County. Eligible property owners in County-established Revitalization Tax Credit Districts receive relief from taxes on the incremental value added by qualifying real property improvements. The increase in property taxes caused by a higher assessed value after qualifying improvements is phased in over time rather than applied all at once. The credit applies to both non-residential and residential improvements, including construction, reconstruction, or extension of structures. Eligible improvements must require a County building permit and be located within a designated Revitalization Tax Credit District.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax credit on eligible county real property taxes based on the value of eligible improvements within a designated Revitalization Tax Credit District. Non-residential properties receive a credit of 100% of county property tax on the increased assessment in year 1, then 80% in year 2, 60% in year 3, 40% in year 4, and 20% in year 5. Residential properties receive a credit of 100% in year 1, 66% in year 2, and 33% in year 3. The maximum eligible residential improvement is $200,000 per dwelling unit. Developments of 10 or more single-family dwellings or multifamily units require County Council approval. Eligible improvements include construction or reconstruction of non-residential structures, reconstruction or extension of residential structures, new single-family construction on previously razed lots or vacant infill lots, and new construction in small residential developments.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No later than October 1 of the tax year the property becomes eligible
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners and developers in designated Revitalization Tax Credit Districts in Prince George's County making qualifying real property improvements, including both non-residential and residential projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Credit against county real property taxes for qualifying construction or reconstruction improvements within a Revitalization Tax Credit District. Taxes on the added assessed value are phased in over multiple years rather than charged immediately.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Property must be located within a designated Revitalization Tax Credit District in Prince George's County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Property must be located within a County-established Revitalization Tax Credit District
Improvements must require a County building permit

Eligible improvements include: construction, reconstruction, or extension of non-residential structures; reconstruction or extension of existing residential structures; new single-family construction on lots where a residential structure was razed within the prior 5 years or vacant infill lots; and new construction in developments of fewer than 10 one-family dwellings
County Council approval required for developments of 10 or more single-family dwellings or multifamily units
Maximum eligible residential improvement value is $200,000 per dwelling unit
Application must be made under oath on the form provided by the Director of Finance
Application must be filed with the Director of Finance by October 1 of the tax year the property becomes eligible
Application must include a legal description of the property, proof of a valid Use and Occupancy permit for the eligible improvements, and any other required documentation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the application form provided by the Director of Finance, made under oath. File with the Director of Finance by October 1 of the tax year the property becomes eligible. Include a legal description of the property, proof of a valid Use and Occupancy permit, and any other documentation required by the Director. For additional information, contact the Economic Development Corporation at 301-952-4030 and ask to speak with a Business Development Specialist.

structured_extraction.program_name: Religious Organizations Leased Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A real property tax credit for the portion of commercial property leased to a qualifying tax-exempt religious organization and used exclusively for religious worship, education, or related office space in Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax credit against county real property tax for the portion of a commercially zoned property leased and used exclusively by a qualifying tax-exempt religious organization for worship, education, or necessary office support.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No later than September 1 of the tax year for which the credit is being requested
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of commercial property leased to tax-exempt religious organizations in Prince George's County, and the religious organizations themselves.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction in county real property taxes for qualifying leased portions of commercial property used for religious or educational purposes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Property must be located in a commercial zone in Prince George's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Religious group or organization must qualify for property tax exemption under Section 7-204 of the Tax-Property Article
Religious group or organization must have verifiable IRS tax-exempt nonprofit status
The credit applies only to the portion of property used exclusively for public religious worship, educational purposes, or necessary supporting office space
Property upon which the credit is based may not be used for profit-making purposes
Religious group or organization must be contractually liable to the owner for property taxes
Owner must be contractually obligated to reduce the tenant's tax liability by the amount of the credit
Property must be located in a commercial zone
Application must be submitted by September 1 of the tax year and signed under oath by both the property owner and the lessee
A copy of the executed lease must be submitted with the application
Owner must notify the Supervisor of Assessments and Taxation within 30 days of lease termination or end of possession
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application to the Supervisor of Assessments and Taxation in Prince George's County by September 1 of the applicable tax year. Application must be signed under oath by both the property owner and the lessee. Attach a copy of the executed lease.

Appointment required — call 301-583-3340 to schedule

structured_extraction.program_name: Restaurant Temporary Outdoor Seating Area (RTOSA) Permit
structured_extraction.program_description: Prince George's County allows qualified restaurants and bars to set up temporary outdoor table service by obtaining an RTOSA Permit. The program expedites approvals through a multi-agency workgroup to help restaurants reopen and expand seating outdoors.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The county expedites review and issues a permit allowing restaurants and bars to temporarily operate outdoor seating areas. Tables must be spaced six feet apart, and the seating area must be separated from the sidewalk or street by a three-foot barrier. Wheelchair access and restroom facilities must be provided.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Restaurants and bars in Prince George's County seeking to add or expand temporary outdoor seating
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Establishing temporary outdoor table service areas, including seating, barriers, and optional tents or heating elements (with revision permit)
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to restaurants and bars operating in Prince George's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a restaurant or bar located in Prince George's County
Must complete an online permit application
Must provide a brief description of the restaurant
Must provide a copy of current Use and Occupancy Permit (U&O); if U&O already permits outdoor seating, RTOSA Permit is not required
Must provide a seating chart of the outdoor area showing chairs, tables, open tents, and barriers
Canopies, awnings, and enclosed tents require a separate Building Permit/U&O application
Must provide a signed and dated Letter of Authorization from the property owner on owner's letterhead
If seating is in a right-of-way controlled by SHA or a municipality, approval from that entity is required
Tenant's and owner's businesses must be registered and in good standing with the State of Maryland
Tables must be spaced six feet apart
Seating area must be separated from sidewalk or street by a three-foot barrier
Wheelchair access and restroom facilities must be provided
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Gather required documents including application, restaurant description, current U&O Permit, seating chart, and Letter of Authorization from property owner. Step 2: Complete the permit application online through the Momentum portal at https://momentumhome.princegeorgescountymd.gov/. After review, you will receive an email invitation to upload your seating plan to the online portal. Once approved, download the JobCard and related plans, then schedule an inspection by calling 301-755-9000 or via the online scheduling link.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Mileage reimbursement and insurance coverage for volunteers serving in community roles.

requirements_list: Must be 55 years of age or older
Willing to help people of all ages and ethnicities
Must serve in the communities of Prince George's County
Willing to use their gifts and talents to help others
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete the RSVP Registration Form (PDF) to get started. Call 301-265-8450 for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: Prince George's County provides employer-paid basic life insurance to eligible county retirees. Coverage equals two times the employee's annual base salary at retirement (up to schedule-specific maximums), and reduces gradually starting at age 60. The program is administered through MetLife and includes options for accelerated benefits, conversion to individual whole life policies, and supplementary services such as grief counseling, funeral planning, will preparation, and estate resolution services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Employer-paid basic life insurance equal to 2 times the retiree's base annual salary at retirement, rounded to the nearest thousand dollars. Maximum benefit varies by employee group (ranging from $100,000 to $225,000; for correctional officers, maximum is $150,000). Beginning the first day of the birth month in which the retiree turns 60, coverage reduces by 15%, with further equal reductions on each of the next four birth anniversaries, but never below 25% of the original retirement amount. Amounts over $50,000 are treated as taxable (imputed) income. An Accelerated Benefit Option is available (up to 80% of basic life amount, not to exceed $120,000 for correctional officers). Conversion to an individual whole life policy is available upon retirement, employment termination, or change in employee class. Premium payments are continued for up to 12 months during total disability. Supplementary services include grief counseling (up to 5 face-to-face sessions), funeral discounts through Dignity Memorial Network (up to 10% off), beneficiary claim assistance, will preparation, and estate resolution services. Coverage is administered through MetLife (Group Policy No. 229162-1-G).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible retirees of Prince George's County, including correctional officers, crossing guards, exempt and general schedule employees, AFSCME employees, police civilians, fire civilians, firefighters, paramedics, sheriff's civilians, police officers, deputy sheriffs, orphan's court judges, and certain judges and assessors enrolled in county benefits. Also includes dependents and beneficiaries of insured employees.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Employer-paid life insurance benefit for retirees; death benefits payable to designated beneficiaries. Also includes supplementary services such as grief counseling, funeral planning, legal services (will preparation, estate resolution), and beneficiary financial guidance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Prince George's County government retirees. Supplementary services vary by state; grief counseling not available in NY; funeral discounts not available in AK, FL, KY, MT, ND, NY, and WA.
requirements_list: Must be a retired Prince George's County employee enrolled in the county benefits program
Coverage level and maximum benefit depend on the employee's salary schedule/group at time of retirement
Amounts over $50,000 treated as imputed (taxable) income
Age-based reductions apply beginning the first day of the birth month in which the retiree turns 60
For conversion to individual policy: coverage must terminate due to retirement, employment termination, or change in employee class
For disability premium continuation: total disability status must be determined by employer
Signed application/enrollment form required; 2-year contestability period applies
Proof of death required to file a claim
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To update beneficiaries, complete a Beneficiary Change Form and submit to the Benefits Division. To obtain the value of your policy, complete a Life Insurance Verification Form and submit to the Benefits Division. To file a claim upon a retiree's death, notify the Benefits Division; a Human Resource Analyst will be assigned to process the claim. To convert group life coverage to an individual whole life policy upon a qualifying event, call MetLife at 1-877-275-6387. For portability inquiries, call 1-888-252-3607. For grief counseling services, call 1-888-319-7819. For funeral planning, call 1-866-853-0954. Contact the Benefits Division at 301-883-6380 or Benefits@co.pg.md.us for additional information.
