Services include job search assistance, resume workshops, Job Club, Federal Bonding letters, and customized WIOA (Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act) training — all at no cost.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free services including Job Club, resume workshops, Federal Bonding letters, job search assistance, and customized WIOA training. The One-Stop Career System serves over 700 people weekly.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Prince George's County residents who have been incarcerated and are ready to re-enter the workforce.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Job search assistance, resume development, job training, and employment placement support.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a returning citizen (previously incarcerated)
Must be a Prince George's County resident
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Pete Goodson at the Prince George's One-Stop Career Center at (301) 618-8425 to access services.

structured_extraction.program_description: RideSmart Commuter Solutions is a Prince George's County program that provides free information, technical assistance, and support to help commuters and employers find alternatives to driving alone, such as walking, biking, carpooling, vanpooling, transit, telework, and flexible schedules. The program provides free technical assistance to employers to develop and implement alternative transportation and commuter benefit programs for employees, helping reduce taxes for both businesses and employees. Services include virtual or on-site meetings, transportation fairs, customized commute program planning based on data analysis and surveys, customizable printed and digital materials, trip-planning tools, park-and-ride lots, Guaranteed Ride Home services, rewards for commuting, and connections to transit/vanpool/bike agencies and incentives like the Maryland Commuter Tax Credit (up to 50% of the cost of providing a transit subsidy) and pre-tax transit benefits up to $280/month. Employers can earn recognition for their programs. For example, a company with 50 participating employees could save $20,900 per year in taxes, cut up to $89,250 from employees' collective tax bills, and convert $78,000 of benefits budgeted into untaxed business costs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free technical assistance, information, and program development support to help employers create alternative commuting and commuter benefit programs for their employees. Services include review of commuter benefit materials, customizable printed and digital content, on-site or virtual commuter events, transportation fairs, customized commute program design based on data analysis and surveys, connections to transit/vanpool/bike agencies, and support for earning employer recognition. Employers may also access pre-tax transit benefits up to $280/month and the Maryland Commuter Tax Credit (up to 50% of the cost of providing a transit subsidy). Employers and employees can achieve significant tax savings — a company with 50 participating employees could save $20,900 per year in taxes and cut up to $89,250 from employees' collective tax bills. Commuters can also access trip-planning tools, park-and-ride lots, Guaranteed Ride Home services, rewards for commuting, carpool/vanpool matching, telework programs, and flexible work schedule support.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Commuters, business owners, and Human Resources managers in or near Prince George's County seeking to reduce commuting costs, develop alternative transportation programs, and build commuter benefit programs for employees.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Developing and implementing employee alternative commuting programs, commuter benefit programs including transit subsidies, carpooling/vanpooling/biking/walking/telecommute/flexible schedule arrangements, and rewards, to reduce traffic congestion, lower parking costs, achieve tax savings for employers and employees, and improve employee morale and productivity.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Serves commuters and employers in and around Prince George's County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a business owner or HR manager in Prince George's County to access employer program services
Employers or employees must be located in or commuting to/from Prince George's County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the RideSmart Commuter Solutions team by emailing info.pgcridesmartsolutions@co.pg.md.us or calling 301-883-5656 to schedule a virtual or on-site meeting, or fill out the contact form on the RideSmart Employer Programs page to get in touch with the team for guidance or to build an employer program.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tree removal and replacement program that removes hazardous, dead, or significantly decayed street trees (including Bradford Pear trees) and replants them with species suited to the built environment. The program also removes stumps and prunes trees. It aims to expand the urban tree canopy, reduce air temperature, manage stormwater runoff, increase wildlife habitat and biodiversity, and beautify Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free removal of hazardous, dead, or significantly decayed street trees (including Bradford Pear trees), stump removal, tree pruning, and planting of replacement trees suited to the built environment. Services are provided to homeowners and community civic associations in the public right-of-way.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners and community civic associations in Prince George's County with street trees in the public right-of-way.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tree removal, stump removal, tree pruning, and replacement tree planting in the public right-of-way.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Trees must be located in the public right-of-way (street trees)
Trees must be high-risk, dead, or significantly decayed (e.g., Bradford Pear or other hazardous species)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Program Coordinator Collin Breidenbach at trees@ndc-md.org for more information. The program collaborates with community members to develop designs tailored to each community using resident input.

structured_extraction.program_description: A four-day intensive training program designed to equip Latino entrepreneurs with the knowledge and tools to launch or grow their businesses, at no cost to participants. The program aims to break down financial barriers and build a more inclusive business community in Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free four-day intensive business training for Latino entrepreneurs covering the knowledge and tools needed to start or grow a business.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Latino entrepreneurs in Prince George's County looking to launch or grow a business
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business training and education to support starting or growing a business
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland

structured_extraction.program_description: The Ryan White HIV/AIDS Program (HAP), administered by Prince George's County Health Department, provides comprehensive HIV medical care, case management, counseling, testing, and support services to people living with HIV/AIDS who are uninsured or underinsured. Funded through the federal Ryan White Comprehensive AIDS Resources Emergency (CARE) Act, the program serves as a payer of last resort when no other resources are available. Services include free HIV counseling and testing, health assessments (physical exams, lab tests, personal medical treatment plans), outpatient ambulatory medical care, dental care, medical nutrition therapy, substance use counseling, women's health services, mental health treatment, early intervention services, emergency financial assistance, health insurance premium and cost sharing assistance, medical transportation, HIV medication assistance, housing referrals, and outreach services. Services are available Monday through Friday by appointment at two locations: Cheverly Health Center (3003 Hospital Drive, Suite 1055, Cheverly, MD 20785) and D. Leonard Dyer Regional Health Center (9314 Piscataway Road, Clinton, MD 20735). Core services are available to residents of Prince George's, Montgomery, Charles, Calvert, and Frederick Counties in Maryland, with some services accessible to individuals outside these counties.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free HIV counseling and testing services. Low-cost and some free medical, dental, nutrition, and counseling services for eligible clients. Services include health assessments (physical exams, lab tests, personal medical treatment plans), dental care, early intervention services, emergency financial assistance, health insurance premium and cost sharing, medical case management (health education, linkage to insurance, HIV medication assistance, linkage to supportive services), medical nutrition therapy, medical transportation, mental health and substance abuse treatment, outpatient ambulatory services, outreach services, women's health services, HIV medication assistance, and referrals for housing and other social services. Fees for services are based on current financial status for confirmed HIV-positive clients. Services available Monday through Friday by appointment at Cheverly Health Center (3003 Hospital Drive, Suite 1055, Cheverly, MD 20785) and D. Leonard Dyer Regional Health Center (9314 Piscataway Road, Clinton, MD 20735).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents who are HIV positive and are uninsured or underinsured, primarily living in Prince George's, Montgomery, Charles, Calvert, or Frederick County. Some services may be accessible to individuals living outside these counties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: HIV medical care, dental services, health assessments, nutrition counseling, substance use counseling, mental health treatment, emergency financial assistance, health insurance premium and cost sharing, transportation to medical appointments, HIV medication assistance, case management, and referrals for housing and social services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Prince George's, Montgomery, Charles, Calvert, or Frederick County in Maryland who are HIV positive and uninsured or underinsured under the Federal Ryan White HIV/AIDS Treatment Modernization Act. Some services (dental, outpatient ambulatory, mental health/substance abuse) may be accessible to individuals living outside these counties. Services are provided at Cheverly Health Center and D. Leonard Dyer Regional Health Center.
requirements_list: Must be HIV positive
Must be uninsured or underinsured based on criteria set by the Federal Ryan White HIV/AIDS Treatment Modernization Act
Must be a resident of Maryland in Prince George's, Montgomery, Charles, Calvert, or Frederick County (some services may be available to those outside these counties)
Appointment required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 301-583-3700 for more information and to schedule an appointment. Services are available Monday through Friday (excluding holidays). You may also call 301-883-7879 to access services. Visit one of two service locations: Cheverly Health Center (3003 Hospital Drive, Suite 1055, Cheverly, MD 20785) or D. Leonard Dyer Regional Health Center (9314 Piscataway Road, Clinton, MD 20735).

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal training program for executives of small businesses poised for growth in historically underserved urban communities. Participants spend seven months learning business strategy, growth planning, marketing, hiring, and financing, and must present a final growth plan to a panel of industry experts to graduate.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A seven-month executive training program covering business planning, marketing, sales, hiring, and financing. Participants develop and present a growth plan to industry experts. The program is delivered through local co-sponsors and host sites such as the Prince George's County Economic Development Corporation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small business executives in historically underserved urban communities, particularly those in the Washington DC Metro Area including Prince George's County, MD
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business training — not a cash award; assistance is in the form of education, mentorship, and networking to support business growth
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington DC Metro Area, including Prince George's County and Montgomery County in Maryland
requirements_list: Business executive or CEO of a small business
Business must be poised for growth in a historically challenged or urban community
Must complete a final growth plan to graduate
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the EDC Small Business Development Manager for information on participating. Classes are offered through local co-sponsors such as the Prince George's County EDC.

structured_extraction.program_description: Southern Maryland Electric Cooperative (SMECO) offers extended payment arrangements and fee waivers to customers, including federal employees, facing difficulty paying their electric bills.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Extended payment arrangements, waiver of good-faith payment requirement, waiver of late payment fees, prevention of disconnection for identified federal employees, reconnection without payment for disconnected federal employees with waived collection and reconnect fees and no deposit required.
structured_extraction.program_audience: SMECO customers, especially federal employees, facing challenges paying their electric bills due to the federal government shutdown.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Electric bill payment relief and service reconnection.

structured_extraction.program_description: Safe Sleep training for organizations, child care centers, or community groups that interact with pregnant women, mothers with infants under 1 year of age, or care for infants under 1 year of age.

Evening services for children ages pre-kindergarten through grade 12 are also offered at Oxon Hill High School.

Evening pediatric services for pre-K through grade 12 are available at the Oxon Hill High School Evening Community Pediatric Center.

Children ages pre-K through grade 12 eligible for evening services at Oxon Hill

structured_extraction.program_name: School Facilities Surcharge Exemption for Studio and Efficiency Apartments
structured_extraction.program_description: Prince George's County fully exempts studio and efficiency apartment units from the school facilities surcharge when they are located near transit or in designated transit zones, recognizing that these unit types are less likely to generate increased school enrollment.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Dwelling units that are studio or efficiency apartments located within ¼ mile of a metro station, in an approved Transit District Overlay Zone (TDOZ), or in other limited qualifying circumstances are fully exempt from the school facilities surcharge (which otherwise ranges from $9,035 to $15,489 per unit as of FY 2015).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential developers building studio or efficiency apartment units near transit in Prince George's County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Full exemption from school facilities surcharge fees owed at time of development
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be located within ¼ mile of a metro station, in an approved Transit District Overlay Zone (TDOZ), or other limited circumstances in Prince George's County
requirements_list: Dwelling unit must be a studio apartment or efficiency apartment
Must be located within ¼ mile of a metro station, in an approved Transit District Overlay Zone (TDOZ), or meet other limited qualifying circumstances
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Economic Development Corporation at 301-583-4650 and ask to speak with a Business Development Specialist for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: Prince George's County applies a school facilities surcharge to new residential developments or redevelopments to cover anticipated increases in public educational services required to accommodate new residents. This program offers reductions or exemptions from that surcharge for qualifying multifamily housing projects located near transit or in designated overlay zones. A 50% reduction is available for multifamily residential developments within ¼ mile of a metro station, in the Bowie MARC Station Community Center Designation Area, or in an approved Transit District Overlay Zone (TDOZ). Studio and efficiency apartments located within ¼ mile of a Metro station, an approved TDOZ, or other limited circumstances are fully exempt from the surcharge entirely.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Qualifying multifamily properties receive a 50% reduction in the school facilities surcharge — from $15,489 to $7,745 per unit (outside the Capital Beltway) or from $9,035 to $4,518 per unit (inside the Capital Beltway or near a WMATA rail station), based on proximity to a Metro station, the Bowie MARC Station Community Center Designation Area, or an approved Transit District Overlay Zone (TDOZ), as of Fiscal Year 2015. Additionally, studio and efficiency apartments located within ¼ mile of a Metro station, within an approved TDOZ, or meeting other limited circumstances are fully exempt from the surcharge.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Developers of new multifamily residential developments or redevelopments in Prince George's County, particularly those located near transit infrastructure such as Metro stations or within designated overlay zones.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction or elimination of the school facilities surcharge costs on new residential development units.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland. For the transit-related 50% reduction or full exemption, property must be located within ¼ mile of a Metro station, in the Bowie MARC Station Community Center Designation Area, or in an approved Transit District Overlay Zone (TDOZ).
requirements_list: Must be a multifamily residential development or redevelopment in Prince George's County
For reductions: property must be within ¼ mile of a Metro station, within the Bowie MARC Station Community Center Designation Area, or within an approved Transit District Overlay Zone (TDOZ)
For exemptions: dwelling units must be studio or efficiency apartments and located within ¼ mile of a Metro station, within an approved TDOZ, or meet other limited circumstances
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Economic Development Corporation at 301-583-4650 and ask to speak with a Business Development Specialist for more information on eligibility and how to apply.

structured_extraction.program_name: Senior Assisted Living Group Home Subsidy Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides funding for low- to moderate-income older adults who need financial assistance to afford placement in an assisted living facility, enabling them to continue living in the community. Assisted living facilities offer congregate meals, housekeeping, personal services, and 24-hour supervision. The program subsidizes the cost of care for eligible residents of Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial subsidy to help low- to moderate-income older adults afford placement in an assisted living group home facility that provides congregate meals, housekeeping, personal services, and 24-hour supervision.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low- to moderate-income older adults age 62 and older who are Prince George's County residents needing financial assistance for assisted living placement.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Placement in an assisted living facility that provides congregate meals, housekeeping, personal services, and 24-hour supervision.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Prince George's County resident.
requirements_list: Be at least 62 years old
Be a Prince George's County resident
Must be a low- to moderate-income older adult
Meet income guidelines not to exceed $4,350 per month (individual)
Meet asset guidelines not to exceed $20,064 (individual) or $24,400 (couple)
Must reside in an assisted living facility
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Aging & Disabilities Services Division at 301-265-8450 for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: SCSEP, also known as Title V, is a federally funded program that provides part-time work-based training and employment assistance to low-income, unemployed older adults in Prince George's County who have poor employment prospects. The program helps participants find jobs through counseling, job training, and job referrals, while also offering civic engagement opportunities. It educates employers about the value of hiring older workers. Participants are placed at local community service host agencies, which must be nonprofit 501(c)(3) or governmental organizations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive part-time, paid work placement at a local community service host agency, along with personal counseling, job-related counseling, job training, and job referrals. The program focuses on helping low-income older adults secure employment and engage civically. Host agencies must be nonprofit 501(c)(3) or governmental organizations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income, unemployed older adults aged 55 and older who are residents of Prince George's County with poor employment prospects, including veterans and their eligible spouses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Part-time work-based training and supportive services to help older adults find employment in the community, including counseling, job training, and job referrals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a resident of Prince George's County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be at least 55 years old
Must be a resident of Prince George's County
Must be legally eligible to work in the U.S.
Must be unemployed
Must be low-income
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Prince George's County Department of Family Services at 301-265-8450 for more information. Veterans and their eligible spouses are encouraged to apply.

structured_extraction.program_description: Senior Transportation Service (STS) is a curb-to-curb transportation service for Prince George's County seniors aged 60 and older and persons with disabilities. It provides scheduled rides for nutrition programs, medical appointments (including dialysis), and general trips to senior activity centers and shopping. The service is a special program under Call-a-Bus.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free or reduced-cost curb-to-curb transportation throughout Prince George's County. Includes rides to nutrition lunch sites (Monday–Friday, 10 a.m.–2 p.m.), medical appointments (schedulable up to 7 days in advance by calling 301-499-8603), dialysis treatment (requires written request), senior activity centers, shopping trips, and recreational purposes. Free transportation to nutrition sites is provided for eligible seniors.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Prince George's County residents aged 60 and older, and persons with disabilities. Spouses of any age are eligible when accompanying an age-eligible spouse for nutrition programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Transportation to nutrition sites, medical appointments, dialysis treatment, senior activity centers, shopping trips, and recreational activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout Prince George's County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a Prince George's County resident
Must be aged 60 or older, OR a person with a disability, OR a spouse of any age accompanying an age-eligible spouse (for nutrition program)
Routine medical rides must be scheduled up to 7 days in advance
Ongoing medical transportation (e.g., dialysis) requires a written request to the Office of Transportation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For nutrition and general transportation, call 301-699-2696 to enroll. For medical appointments, call 301-499-8603 up to 7 days in advance. For ongoing medical transportation such as dialysis, submit a written request to: Prince George's County Office of Transportation, Attention: Transit Division, 9400 Peppercorn Place, Suite 320, Largo, MD 20774.

structured_extraction.program_description: Short Term Disability insurance through MetLife protects a portion of your income if you cannot work due to a covered injury or illness. It replaces up to 60% of your salary (maximum $3,000 per week) for up to 26 weeks.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides income replacement of up to 60% of salary, with a maximum weekly benefit of $3,000, for up to 26 weeks. Benefits begin after a 7-day elimination period for both sickness (including pregnancy) and injury. Premiums are deducted on an after-tax basis. Rates are age-based, ranging from $0.62 to $1.72 per $10 of covered weekly benefit.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Prince George's County employees seeking voluntary short-term disability income protection.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Income replacement during a covered disability period when the employee is unable to work due to injury or illness.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to employees of Prince George's County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a Prince George's County employee
7-day elimination period before benefits begin
Pre-existing conditions (treatment received within 3 months before coverage takes effect) are excluded for 12 months after coverage begins
No benefits for elective procedures, acts of war, self-inflicted injury, commission of a felony, or active participation in a riot
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Enroll through the Prince George's County Human Resources Management benefits enrollment process. Former UNUM participants who switch to MetLife may count prior UNUM coverage time toward the one-year pre-existing condition waiting period if there is no break in coverage.

structured_extraction.program_description: Prince George's County homeowners can get a Short-Term Rental License to legally rent their primary residence to guests through online platforms like Airbnb. Online platforms that facilitate short-term rentals can also apply for a Platform License. The program ensures compliance with county code, life safety requirements, and local regulations.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The county issues Short-Term Rental Host Licenses (valid for one year from issuance) and Short-Term Rental Platform Licenses to qualifying applicants. Applicants receive a temporary license upon application submission and fee payment — 90 days for hosts and 30 days for platforms — which converts to a permanent license if no issues are found. Licenses are issued and printed online through the Momentum portal. Host license fee: $198 (includes administrative fee + 10% technology fee). Platform license fee: $3,300 (includes administrative fee + 10% technology fee). A second application review fee of $132 applies after a 2nd incomplete application. Enforcement civil citations of $1,200 apply for hosts and platforms operating without a license. Fees are per the DPIE Fee Schedule (effective March 2, 2025).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Prince George's County homeowners who want to rent their primary residence as a short-term rental, and online platforms (e.g., Airbnb) that facilitate short-term rental bookings in the county.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Obtaining a license to legally operate a short-term rental in Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties must be located in Prince George's County, Maryland. The property must be the host's permanent residence (verified via Homestead Tax Credit).
requirements_list: Property must be the host's permanent residence with a valid Maryland Homestead Tax Credit
Smoke and carbon monoxide detectors installed in all bedrooms or hallway outside bedrooms
Properly charged fire extinguisher (minimum 2A:10BC) hung or mounted in a fixed location on travel path to exit
Floor plan showing fire exits and escape routes conspicuously posted inside the rental
Current and valid liability insurance of at least $1,000,000
HOA must allow short-term rentals
Emergency contact information conspicuously posted inside the rental
Updates to contact information provided within five business days of any change
Off-street parking availability (one parking space per every 3 overnight guests)
Neighbor notification forms submitted to adjacent neighbors (left, right, front, and behind)
Proof of intent to apply submitted to HOA
List of all platforms to be used provided
Rules for short-term rental guests posted at main entrance
Completion of Human Trafficking Training videos and quiz
Compliance with all applicable laws and codes
No outstanding taxes, liens, or code violations on the property
Two outdoor trash receptacles and one recycling receptacle
All life safety devices up to date and in good working order
Basements used as habitable space must be authorized by DPIE Enforcement Division
Attest to ownership of the short-term rental property
Maximum 8 renters at one time; maximum 3 guests per bedroom
Maximum 30 consecutive rental days
Maximum 90 days per calendar year if owner unoccupied; 180 days if owner occupied
Pay applicable license fees plus 10% Technology Fee
Program established by Prince George's County through CB-11-2018
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online through the Momentum portal at momentumhome.princegeorgescountymd.gov. Create an account, select the appropriate application type (host or platform), complete and submit the application, and pay the required fees. A temporary license is issued upon payment. DPIE staff reviews the application and may contact you if there are issues. The temporary license converts to a permanent license at the end of the temporary period if no issues remain. Print the permanent license from the My Permits/Licenses dashboard. Applicants must also notify abutting neighbors using the Proof of Intent to Apply/Neighbor Notification form and submit attestation of compliance with regulations to DPIE prior to application.

structured_extraction.program_name: Single Family Homeowner Occupied Housing Rehabilitation Assistance Program (Housing Rehabilitation Assistance Program - HRAP)
structured_extraction.program_description: A home improvement loan program to help eligible Prince George's County homeowners with health and safety home repairs, including roof replacement, electrical work, plumbing improvements, energy efficiency upgrades, and ADA-related improvements. Administered in partnership with the Redevelopment Authority of Prince George's County and Housing Initiative Partnership (HIP).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 0% interest rate loans with no monthly payment for up to $60,000 to eligible homeowners for health, safety, energy efficiency, and accessibility repairs including roof replacement, electrical, plumbing, lead/mold/asbestos abatement, insulation, windows, and ADA improvements such as ramps, grab bars, and railings.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owner-occupied homeowners in Prince George's County who need health and safety home repairs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Health hazard remediation (lead, mold, asbestos abatement), safety and code compliance repairs (roof, electrical, plumbing, flooring), energy efficiency upgrades (windows, insulation, air sealing, siding), and ADA-related improvements (ramps, grab bars, railings).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must own and occupy a home in Prince George's County
Must be current on mortgage payments, property taxes, and property insurance
Cannot have any current liens, judgments, or recent bankruptcy
Cannot have an underwater mortgage
Total household income may not exceed program limits
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit HIP's HRAP website at hiphomes.org for more information and to apply.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides financial support to help lower energy costs and reduce greenhouse gas emissions through solar installations and energy efficiency upgrades.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial grants to support solar and energy efficiency upgrades. Specific amounts and terms are not stated on this page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Prince George's County residents, particularly those in historically underserved and overburdened communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Solar energy installations and energy efficiency upgrades.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides free spay and neuter surgeries for dogs and cats owned by Prince George's County residents who cannot afford these services. Funded through a grant from the Maryland Department of Agriculture (not county general funds), so availability is limited and may vary.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free spay and neuter surgical services for dogs and cats. Services are funded by a grant from the Maryland Department of Agriculture and available in limited quantities to Prince George's County residents who cannot afford the cost of surgery.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Grant funding is currently closed; check back for when applications will be accepted. Note: approved vouchers must be used within 30 days of authorization.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Prince George's County residents who cannot afford spay or neuter services for their pets, including low-income individuals and those on fixed incomes or receiving public assistance.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free spay and neuter surgical services for pets (dogs and cats).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a resident of Prince George's County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a Prince George's County resident
Must be unable to afford the full cost of spay/neuter surgery without assistance
Application must be filled out correctly and completely
Pet must be current on rabies vaccination (preferred)
Applicant may need to provide proof of public assistance or fixed income
Approved service voucher must be used within 30 days of authorization
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the application form (available in English or Spanish). Submit via email to MPPerez@co.pg.md.us or drop off in person at the Animal Services Center (3750 Brown Station Rd, Upper Marlboro, MD 20772). The coordinator reviews the application and contacts the applicant with a decision. Approved applicants receive a numbered voucher to Spay Spot, valid for 30 days.

structured_extraction.program_description: Step Forward is an intensive six-month cohort-based loan readiness program for minority women entrepreneurs in Prince George's County, designed to improve financial literacy, build loan readiness skills, and accelerate business growth by making the right connections. Sponsored by Wells Fargo, participants receive one-on-one counseling with business and banking advisors, attend monthly training sessions and workshops with industry experts and guest speakers, and work toward identifying loan package deficiencies, completing a lender-ready loan application package, and obtaining lender pre-qualification. Workshops cover business planning, marketing, legal formation, and financial training. A cohort of 10 competitively selected women-owned businesses participates per annual cycle, with future cycles anticipated.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A six-month intensive loan readiness program sponsored by Wells Fargo featuring workshops on business planning, marketing, legal formation, and financial literacy, plus one-on-one business and banking counseling. Participants receive monthly group training sessions with industry experts and guest speakers, support in identifying loan package deficiencies, preparing a complete loan application package, and getting applications pre-reviewed and pre-qualified by lenders. A select cohort of 10 businesses is competitively selected on an annual basis, with future cycles planned by PGCEDC.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Current cycle has passed; future cycles anticipated
structured_extraction.program_audience: Minority women-owned small businesses located in Prince George's County, Maryland seeking access to capital and loan readiness skills
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Building financial literacy, strengthening loan packages, identifying loan deficiencies, completing loan applications, obtaining lender pre-qualification, and accessing capital for business growth; includes training on business planning, marketing, and legal formation
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to women-owned businesses based in Prince George's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a minority women-owned business
Must be located in Prince George's County
Must be an established business seeking access to capital
Competitively selected; cohort limited to 10 businesses per annual cycle
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Businesses are competitively selected on an annual basis. The current cycle has closed; future cycles will be announced by PGCEDC. Participants apply to join a six-month cohort program facilitated by the EDC Business Development team. Visit www.pgcedc.com/stepforward or follow PGCEDC on social media for updates on the selection process.

structured_extraction.program_name: Stormwater Stewardship Grant Program – Community Stormwater Management Blitz (Pilot Project)
structured_extraction.program_description: A pilot project that builds community-wide climate resilience and addresses local flooding through focused outreach, community engagement, and installation of small to medium-scale green infrastructure practices such as cisterns, rain gardens, conservation landscaping, and pavement removal.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Supports installation of green infrastructure practices including cisterns, rain gardens, conservation landscaping, and pavement removal, similar to those supported under the County's Rain Check Rebate Program. The pilot is being led by Alliance for the Chesapeake in the Tantallon area of Fort Washington.

structured_extraction.program_name: Summer Youth Enrichment Program (SYEP) – Host/Sponsor Partnership
structured_extraction.program_description: The Summer Youth Enrichment Program (SYEP) connects Prince George's County youth and young adults (ages 14–24) with enriching and constructive summer work experiences at host organizations in community organizations, private sector companies, and government agencies. The program focuses on job skills training, professional development, career exposure, job readiness training, networking, and paid work experience. Businesses, nonprofits, and government entities can participate as host employers or worksite partners. Organizations that do not have open positions can instead become Sponsorship Partners through two models: Capstone Sponsorships (funding program curriculum, workforce training, and transportation) or Student Sponsorships (funding individual youth employment at nonprofit locations).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Host organizations can hire county-funded youth workers as designated worksites (nonprofits and government entities) or hire youth directly (corporate partners). Youth participants earn hourly pay: ages 16–17 earn $13/hour (max 32 hrs/week); ages 18–24 earn $15/hour (max 40 hrs/week). Stipends are also provided upon 75% program completion: ages 14–15 receive $300; ages 16–17 receive $400; ages 18–24 receive $500. Sponsorship Partners can contribute through Capstone Sponsorships (funding curriculum, workforce training, and transportation costs) or Student Sponsorships with three tiers: $5,000 (ages 16–22), $3,500 (ages 14–15), or $1,500 (transportation only). Sponsors are recognized on SYEP marketing materials and social media and receive program communications and event invitations. Industry-specific training is available in Aviation, Electrical, Help Desk Technology/IT, Hospitality Services and Culinary, Digital Marketing, Administrative Support, and Energy Conservation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses, nonprofits, and government organizations in Prince George's County interested in hosting or sponsoring youth employment opportunities for county youth and young adults ages 14–24.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Sponsorship contributions support program curriculum, workforce training, transportation costs, and youth employment salaries. Student Sponsorships directly fund individual youth employment at nonprofit locations. Participant wages are paid hourly or via stipend depending on age and program completion.

structured_extraction.program_description: Prince George's County makes county-owned surplus real property available for sale, lease, or other disposition to eligible parties through the Redevelopment Authority of Prince George's County (RDA). Properties are declared surplus when no longer needed for county use or when the transfer serves a public purpose, governed by County Code Section 2-111.01 (as updated by CB-061-2023) and County Council Resolution CR-41-2025. The RDA administers the disposition process to eliminate county maintenance costs, generate sales revenue, increase the tax base, and identify sites for strategic development. Available parcels are sold at appraised fair market value through a public bid process: interested buyers submit an Expression of Interest (EOI) bid proposal with a 10% earnest money deposit in certified funds payable to Prince George's County. Properties are sold 'as-is' with no warranties. If more than one party bids on a property, a sealed Best and Final Offer process is used; unsuccessful bidders receive their deposit back. The program aims to encourage community and economic development, support job creation, and promote affordable housing.

Interested buyers must submit an Expression of Interest (EOI) bid proposal with a 10% earnest money deposit in certified funds payable to Prince George's County, Maryland. Properties are sold 'as-is' with no warranties. If more than one party bids on a property, a sealed Best and Final Offer process is used. Unsuccessful bidders receive their deposit back. Properties may be acquired via fee simple purchase or ground lease.

Services include outpatient mental health clinic (OMHC) services, individualized care plans, referrals, and connections to community-based mental health resources, delivered through contracted providers including Maryland Family Resource Inc., Synergy Family Services, NAMI of Prince George's County, and Maryland Coalition of Families.

structured_extraction.program_description: Tax Increment Financing (TIF) is a tool that helps fund public improvements tied to economic development, such as parking facilities, roads, and stormwater management. When a development or redevelopment project generates additional tax revenue, the county can issue bonds to pay for related public infrastructure. Those bonds are repaid using the incremental increase in property tax revenue the project creates above a designated base-year assessed value. Prince George's County has pre-designated certain areas as TIF Districts, giving projects in those areas increased certainty of approval for TIF bond financing, though exact terms must still be negotiated with the county.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The county issues bonds to finance public infrastructure improvements (such as roads, parking, and stormwater management) for qualifying development projects. The bonds are repaid using the incremental increase in property tax revenue generated by the project above the designated base-year assessed value. Projects located within pre-designated TIF Districts have increased certainty of approval, though exact terms are negotiated individually with the county.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Developers and businesses undertaking development or redevelopment projects in Prince George's County, particularly within pre-designated TIF Districts.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Public infrastructure improvements related to economic development, including parking facilities, roadways, and stormwater management.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available within Prince George's County, Maryland. Pre-designated TIF Districts within the county offer increased certainty of approval for TIF bond financing.
requirements_list: Project must be located within Prince George's County
Project must generate incremental increase in assessed property value above the base-year assessed value
Projects in pre-designated TIF Districts have pre-qualified eligibility, though exact terms must be negotiated with the county
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Prince George's County Economic Development Corporation at 301-583-4650 and ask to speak with a Business Development Specialist to discuss eligibility and negotiate terms.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free, virtual program that helps people living with Type 2 diabetes learn to manage their condition. structured_extraction.program_name: Third-Party Plan Review and Peer Review Programs (TPPRP / PRP)
structured_extraction.program_description: Prince George's County offers two distinct plan review programs administered by DPIE. The Third-Party Plan Review Program (TPPRP) requires certain building projects to use a county-authorized Third-Party Plan Review Agency (TPPRA) — a private firm hired by the applicant at their own cost — to review and approve building plans instead of county staff. It is mandatory for large commercial buildings over $50 million, multifamily residential buildings over $50 million, pools, spas (non-residential), design-build commercial projects, government buildings, and fire protection systems. Reviews cover Structural/Non-Structural and Fire and Life Safety disciplines, including sprinkler systems, fire alarm systems, smoke control, fire resistance rated construction, means of egress, and building services. The optional Peer Review Program (PRP) allows any applicant to hire DPIE-certified peer reviewers at their own cost to expedite plan review and approval for building and site development projects, potentially reducing review and approval time by up to 50%. Peer reviewers conduct reviews across multiple disciplines including architectural, structural, mechanical, electrical, fire protection, site/civil, floodplain, traffic, and geotechnical. In the PRP, peer reviewer findings are submitted to DPIE staff for final approval, whereas in the TPPRP the third-party reviewer has full approval authority.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two programs are available: (1) TPPRP (mandatory for qualifying projects): Applicants hire a DPIE-authorized third-party plan review firm at their own expense to review and approve building plans in place of county staff. Required for commercial buildings over $50 million, swimming pools and spas (except one- and two-family dwellings), all design-build commercial buildings, all government buildings, all fire protection systems, and multifamily residential buildings over $50 million. Reviews cover multiple disciplines including structural, mechanical, electrical, fire protection, and non-structural, certifying compliance with applicable Construction Codes and Prince George's County Code. (2) PRP (optional): Applicants hire DPIE-certified peer reviewers at their own expense to review construction and site development plans across disciplines including building/architectural, structural, electrical, mechanical, fire protection, site/civil, floodplain, traffic, road/bridge, geotechnical, and utility; peer reviewer results are then reviewed and approved by county staff. This can reduce plan review and approval time by up to 50%. Both programs require all revisions to go through the respective reviewer, and all projects must also go through DPIE's Third-Party Inspections Program (TPIP). Electronic plan submissions are processed through ePlan (ProjectDox).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners and applicants seeking building permits or expedited plan review for large commercial, multifamily residential, government, and other qualifying construction or site development projects in Prince George's County, including builders, developers, design professionals (Professional Engineers, Architects), and general contractors.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Review and approval of building and site development plans for qualifying construction projects, either through mandatory third-party review (TPPRP) or optional peer review (PRP) to expedite approval timeframes. Covers code compliance certification across multiple disciplines including structural, mechanical, electrical, fire protection, site/civil, floodplain, and traffic engineering.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Economic Development Incentive (EDI) Fund is a Prince George's County program administered through FSC First in partnership with the Prince George's County Economic Development Corporation and the Maryland Department of Commerce. Established in 2011 to stimulate the county's economy following the recession, it provides grants and conditional/low-interest loans to eligible businesses and organizations to support expansion of the county's commercial tax base, job retention and attraction, small and local businesses, development and redevelopment opportunities, transit-oriented development, and growth of key industry sectors aligned with the county's Economic Development Strategic Action Plan. The fund has a total multi-year commitment of $50 million, with approximately $7 million to $11 million available each fiscal year. Most awards are made as loans to small and medium-sized businesses; grants may be considered in extraordinary circumstances involving large numbers of jobs. Loans are offered at a minimum of $250,000 with a maximum term of 10 years (amortization not to exceed 25 years), at competitive market rates or slightly below based on individual credit and financial history (county prime rate: 4%). Collateral (business and personal assets) and personal guarantees are required. An application fee of 1% of the loan amount applies. The loan process takes approximately 90 days from application to funding. As of June 2018, $36 million in awards had been made across 44 approved projects, generating $1 billion in private investment and creating or retaining over 12,000 jobs. Priority is given to projects in the county's developed tier, transit-oriented development areas, Transforming Neighborhoods Initiative areas, and other focus areas. The fund also sets aside $1 million to help small businesses get lines of credit from traditional banks. Examples of funded projects include a $400,000 loan to a sheet metal fabrication business for expansion and job creation, a $250,000 grant toward a $31 million expansion project, and a $480,000 conditional loan to Vegetable and Butcher for relocation of headquarters to the county.

structured_extraction.program_description: CatalystQ is a six-month business accelerator program administered by Queen Anne's County Economic & Tourism Development for minority entrepreneurs and minority-owned businesses in Queen Anne's County. It provides intensive training, mentoring, and professional support to help minority-owned businesses start, grow, and succeed by addressing barriers such as access to capital, business knowledge, legal and regulatory compliance, and professional networking. Ten selected businesses receive hands-on coaching and mentoring, help drafting a business plan, creating marketing materials, introductions to local banks, accountants, insurance providers, and attorneys, plus a microgrant for strategic growth initiatives. Participants engage in bi-weekly in-person sessions at Chesapeake College, Mentoring Mondays, and one-on-one support from experienced professionals including SBDC consultants. Technical assistance covers accounting, legal services, marketing, business planning, HR, IT, grant writing, supply chain, and e-commerce. Graduates receive a certificate of completion from the County Commissioners and continuing education credits from Chesapeake College. The program is an expanded continuation of a pilot launched in 2023, previously funded through the Rural Maryland Economic Development Fund. Queen Anne's County also issues an RFP for qualified organizations to deliver accelerator services for the program, with up to $100,000 in total funding available.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Each of the ten selected minority-owned businesses receives a hands-on business coach and mentor, help with business planning and marketing collateral, introductions to local banks, accountants, insurance providers, and attorneys, plus a microgrant (mini-grant) for strategic growth initiatives including professional assistance such as accounting, legal, and certifications. Mini-grants are restricted from working capital or equipment purchases. The six-month accelerator includes bi-weekly in-person sessions at Chesapeake College (with potential virtual component), Mentoring Mondays, and one-on-one support from SBDC consultants, accountants, lawyers, and other subject matter experts. Technical assistance covers accounting and bookkeeping, legal advice, marketing, HR, business planning, financial management, IT, grant writing, supply chain, e-commerce, and networking. Subcontracting for licensed services (accounting, legal) is permitted. Co-working/programming space may also be provided. Graduates receive a certificate of completion from the County Commissioners and continuing education credits from Chesapeake College. Queen Anne's County also issues an RFP for qualified vendors to implement the full suite of accelerator services, with up to $100,000 in total program funding.

structured_extraction.program_name: Enterprise Zone Tax Credits (Queen Anne's County)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides real property tax credits and income tax credits to businesses that invest in commercial properties, commercial development, redevelopment, or create jobs within the Queen Anne's County Enterprise Zone, which covers parts of Grasonville, Chester, and Stevensville.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two types of credits: (1) Real Property Tax Credit: 10-year credit against local property taxes. Credit is 80% of the increase in assessed value for the first 5 years, then declines by 10% annually (70%, 60%, 50%, 40%, 30%) in years 6–10. (2) Income Tax Credit for job creation: $1,000 per new non-disadvantaged employee (one-time); up to $3,000/$2,000/$1,000 over 3 years for economically disadvantaged employees as certified by DLLR.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Certification must be submitted to SDAT by December 31 of the preceding calendar year to receive credit beginning July 1 of the next tax year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses locating, expanding, or substantially improving commercial properties within the Queen Anne's County Enterprise Zone, and businesses creating new full-time jobs in the Zone
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Real property improvements, commercial development, redevelopment, and job creation within the Enterprise Zone
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties and businesses must be located within the Queen Anne's County Enterprise Zone (covers Grasonville, Chester, Stevensville including Chesapeake Bay Business Park, Matapeake Professional Park, and Thompson Creek area)
requirements_list: Investment must occur within the designated Enterprise Zone area
Property must be commercial (mixed-use: only commercial portion qualifies)
Capital investment in property required for real property credit (no minimum investment)
Base assessment must be completed before construction begins
Application must be submitted after receiving all required building permits, before or at the beginning of construction
Certification to SDAT must occur by December 31 for the credit to apply in the following tax year
For income tax credit: new employees must be hired after Enterprise Zone designation date or business relocation date
Employees must work at least 35 hours per week for at least 6 months
Employees must be paid at least 150% of federal minimum wage
Employees must spend at least half their working hours in the Enterprise Zone
Employees must fill new positions or replace economically disadvantaged employees
For disadvantaged worker credit: DLLR must certify employee status; voucher must be submitted within 28–30 days of hiring
Ineligible businesses: fast-food restaurants, convenience stores, stand-alone gas stations, adult entertainment, and gambling facilities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the application for either the real property or income tax credit. Submit certification to the Queen Anne's County Department of Economic Development (Zone Administrator), who certifies eligibility to SDAT. For income tax credits, submit vouchers to DLLR for economically disadvantaged workers, then claim credits on tax return using Form 500CR.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Treatment costs for age-related diseases in pets.

Applicant must be facing financial hardship covering treatment costs

structured_extraction.program_description: An 8-week business accelerator program for entrepreneurs in the early stages of business development or those thinking about starting a business in Queen Anne's County. Expert-led weekly sessions guide participants through developing an entrepreneurial vision into a launch plan, drafting a financing proposal, and creating a 4-minute funding pitch to secure capital through loans, grants, or investors. The program is led by internationally certified business coach Russell Teeter and includes group coaching, peer-to-peer advising, one-on-one mentoring, and access to exclusive resources.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Structured coaching, mentorship, and networking over 8 weekly Tuesday evening sessions (5:30 PM–8:30 PM) at the Queen Anne's County Family YMCA, running April 1 – May 20, 2025. Participants pay $45 per person. Includes group coaching, peer-to-peer advising, one-on-one mentoring, and access to exclusive resources.

structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses based in Queen Anne's County receive priority. Businesses outside the county that are interested in relocating or expanding to Queen Anne's County are also eligible.

Business based in Queen Anne's County (priority) or interested in relocating/expanding there
Committed to active participation and program completion
Selected by committee based on business stage, industry type, and program fit
Applications considered on a competitive basis
Space is limited
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application online via the HubSpot form at choosequeenannes.com/accelerators. Applications are reviewed by a selection committee on a competitive basis. Deadline is March 10, 2025.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Queen Anne's County program that provides funding assistance to residents who have broadband internet service available at or near the end of their driveway (within approximately 1,500 feet) but need help covering the cost of extending that connection down a long driveway to their home. The county covers 90% of the build cost, up to a maximum of $13,500 per household. The program was approved by the County Commissioners in June 2023. Eligible addresses must have broadband available at the end of or within approximately 1,500 feet of their driveway and must not fall within another existing grant-funded broadband build area.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The county covers 90% of the cost to extend broadband service (fiber, cable, or other connection) down a long driveway to a residential property, with a maximum grant amount of $13,500 per household. Applicants must have internet service available at the end of their driveway or within approximately 1,500 feet of their driveway and must not fall within another existing grant-funded broadband build area.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Queen Anne's County residents with long driveways whose properties have broadband available at or near the end of their driveway (within approximately 1,500 feet) but lack a connection to the home, and are not served by existing grant-funded broadband build areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Extending broadband internet infrastructure (fiber, cable, or other connection) from the road or nearby connection point down a long driveway to connect a residential property to available internet service.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Queen Anne's County, Maryland, in areas not covered by other grant-funded broadband build programs. Applicant's driveway must be within approximately 1,500 feet of an existing broadband connection.
requirements_list: Must be a Queen Anne's County resident
Internet service must be available at the end of the driveway or within approximately 1,500 feet of the driveway
Property must not fall within another existing grant-funded broadband build area
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Residents meeting the eligibility criteria can apply for county funds through the Long Driveway Grant Program. Details and the application form are available via the program document linked on the county website (https://www.qac.org/DocumentCenter/View/25023/Long-Driveway-Grant-Program--Revised_01302026). An earlier version of the program document is also available at https://www.qac.org/DocumentCenter/View/18280/Long-Driveway-Grant-Program-for-QAC_v1. The program was approved by the County Commissioners in June 2023. Contact the county for specific application steps.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Firefighter and EMT training and certification.

Program is offered through the Board of Education in conjunction with MFRI
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the MFRI Upper Eastern Shore Regional Training Center at 410-758-2112 or visit www.mfri.org for more information.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal USDA-VAPG grants of up to $75,000 for planning activities or up to $250,000 for working capital expenses. Approximately $30 million is available nationally in 2025.

structured_extraction.program_description: Queen Anne's County is soliciting proposals from qualified organizations to build and outfit a mobile visitors center trailer for use as a tourism ambassador at various events and festivals. All proposals must be sealed and clearly marked 'QAC Mobile Visitors Center Trailer'
Proposals evaluated on cost, design, specs, and experience as outlined in the RFP

Landowners are billed for hourly labor plus herbicide costs.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Spot spraying and herbicide treatment to eradicate or control noxious weeds on private or public land
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout Queen Anne's County

Failure to pay for services can result in a lien against the property

structured_extraction.program_description: Queen Anne's County offers a set of incentives to recruit and retain volunteer firefighters and EMS personnel. Volunteers receive training, gear, tax breaks, life insurance, and other benefits in exchange for their service to the community.

structured_extraction.program_name: Queen Anne's County Youth Career Development Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A county-run program that connects local youth with internship and apprenticeship opportunities at local businesses, especially in technology and trade industries. A dedicated Career Technology Liaison helps businesses set up youth apprenticeships and internships, and helps students and schools access information about available opportunities in Queen Anne's and Kent Counties.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A Career Technology Liaison connects local businesses with youth workers through two pathways: (1) Youth Apprenticeships — requiring Maryland Department of Labor approval, 450 hours of employment, and 141 hours of related instruction; and (2) Youth Internships — where students earn 1 graduation credit per internship and complete 7.5 hours of work per week. The Liaison helps businesses navigate Maryland Department of Labor requirements and connects them with the state's Youth Apprenticeship Navigator.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local businesses in Queen Anne's and Kent Counties interested in hiring youth interns or apprentices, and students seeking on-the-job training and work experience.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Developing internship and apprenticeship positions for youth, particularly in technology and trade industries.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Serves Queen Anne's County and Kent County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Youth Apprenticeships require Maryland Department of Labor approval for both the business and the youth employee
Apprenticeships require 450 hours of employment and 141 hours of related instruction
Employer must offer advancement opportunities after apprenticeship completion
Youth Internships require the student's graduation requirements and school schedule to accommodate the internship
Student earns 1 credit toward graduation per internship
An agreement must be signed by the employer, school counselor, and parent
Student must complete 7.5 hours of work per week at the local business
Employer must complete online application
Employer must meet DLLR eligibility requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Businesses interested in establishing a youth apprenticeship should contact the Career Technology Liaison Connie Dean. Businesses can also apply directly through the Maryland Department of Labor Youth Apprenticeship Employer Application. The Maryland Department of Labor Youth Apprenticeship Navigator (Bob Zimberoff) will contact the employer directly after the initial application.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Rental Allowance Program (RAP) is a grant from the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development to Queen Anne's County that provides rent subsidies and monthly rent assistance to low-income residents who are homeless or have an emergency housing need. The goal is to help people move from homelessness or temporary emergency housing into permanent housing and return to self-sufficiency. Payments are fixed amounts based on family size and location of the rental unit in Maryland, and can be received for up to 12 months, with possible extensions under special circumstances. Funding is limited and may run out.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rent subsidies provided to eligible low-income residents in fixed monthly amounts based on family size and location of the rental housing unit in Maryland. Payments can be received for up to 12 months and may be extended under special circumstances. Helps residents transition from homelessness or temporary emergency housing into permanent housing and return to self-sufficiency. Funding is limited and may run out.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income residents of Queen Anne's County who are homeless or have an emergency housing need.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rent assistance to transition from homelessness or temporary emergency housing into permanent housing and achieve self-sufficiency.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Queen Anne's County residents. Payment amounts vary by location within the state of Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a low-income resident
Must be homeless or have an emergency housing need
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call the Division of Housing at 410-758-3977 to make an appointment with a Housing Program Administrator to determine which resources best suit your circumstances.

structured_extraction.program_name: Retired or Disabled Veterans' Tax Credit

structured_extraction.assistance_description: A credit equal to 20% of the Queen Anne's County property tax on the principal dwelling. The credit continues without further application after approval, but an Annual Eligibility Certification must be filed each subsequent year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Retired or disabled veterans age 65 or older, and surviving spouses of eligible veterans who have not remarried.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of county property tax liability.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Queen Anne's County, Maryland only.
requirements_list: Must be a retired or disabled veteran, or surviving spouse of either who has not remarried
Must be at least 65 years of age
Qualified veteran must be named on the property deed
Property must have been owned by and served as the principal residence of the applicant for at least two years prior to application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application by June 15 to the Queen Anne's County Department of Budget and Finance. Annual Eligibility Certification must be filed each subsequent year to continue the credit.

structured_extraction.program_description: Queen Anne's County Animal Services offers a free Trap-Neuter-Release (TNR) service to help residents deal with stray and feral cats. Each cat is spayed or neutered, vaccinated, and ear-tipped for identification, then returned to its original location. The program aims to humanely reduce stray cat populations and prevent unwanted litters without placing cats in shelters.

structured_extraction.program_description: A no-cost home repair program for long-term (legacy) homeowners in the Johnston Square neighborhood of East Baltimore City. The program provides major repairs and façade improvements to help legacy residents stay in their homes as the neighborhood undergoes revitalization. It addresses safety issues and aging systems such as roofs and electrical systems, helping residents build home equity. The program serves as an anti-displacement strategy to ensure existing homeowners can remain and benefit alongside new development. The first phase invested $2.4 million in repairs for 33 homeowners, with repairs carried out by Rebuilding Together Baltimore (RTB). The program is currently at capacity with a waiting list as it seeks resources to expand.

structured_extraction.program_description: ReBUILD Metro's Path to Own Program is a free initiative that helps first-time and prospective homebuyers in East Baltimore assess their financial readiness, access homebuyer education workshops, connect with HUD-certified housing counselors, find favorable mortgage products, and identify down payment assistance programs to achieve sustainable homeownership and build generational wealth. The program provides access to up to $50,000 in combined homeownership programs and incentives, including property tax discounts, grants, and employer-based assistance. Program managers guide participants through the entire homebuying process — from viewing homes in ReBUILD Metro's portfolio to mortgage prequalification and closing. Participants attend homebuyer education workshops (held bimonthly at The Hammond, 1100 Greenmount Avenue, Baltimore), receive one-on-one counseling referrals to HUD-certified housing counselors, and get connected to down payment assistance programs that can reduce down payment costs close to zero. One featured offering is the Mura Street Homes in Baltimore's Johnston Square neighborhood, where buyers can access financial incentives to make purchasing a restored rowhome more affordable. The program particularly serves African American Baltimoreans and current ReBUILD Metro residents who have faced systemic barriers to homeownership.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore Energy Initiative Loan Program provides low-interest financing to Baltimore City nonprofit organizations and for-profit small businesses to fund energy-saving building improvements such as lighting, HVAC upgrades, building envelope improvements, domestic hot water systems, and other efficiency measures. The goal is to lower utility bills, improve building comfort, and reduce energy waste so organizations can reinvest savings back into their communities. The program is funded by the City of Baltimore using Customer Investment Funds from the Maryland Public Service Commission (utility merger of Baltimore Gas & Electric Company and Exelon) and is managed by the Baltimore City Energy Office, with lending originated and serviced by Healthy Neighborhoods Inc. (HNI) and The Reinvestment Fund (TRF). The program covers limited retrofits, whole-building retrofits, gut rehabs, substantial rehabilitation/reconstruction, and new construction with energy measures. Loans under $150,000 are referred to Healthy Neighborhoods Inc.; loans of $150,000 and above are handled by The Reinvestment Fund.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest loans up to $2,000,000 per project, financing up to 90% of eligible energy project costs. Loans of $150,000–$2,000,000 are handled by The Reinvestment Fund; the BEI component is priced at 4.0% and blended with other Reinvestment Fund capital into a single loan at a blended rate. Loan terms are typically up to 7 years (up to 15 years per program guidelines). Loans under $150,000 are referred to Healthy Neighborhoods Inc. at rates from 3.0%–4.0% with terms up to 15 years. Nonprofits may use up to 20% of the loan amount (capped at $50,000) for non-energy improvements that enable the energy upgrades. Eligible measures include building envelope improvements, HVAC systems and controls, lighting fixtures and controls, domestic hot water heaters, low-flow plumbing fixtures, ENERGY STAR appliances, distributed generation systems (solar PV, combined heat-and-power), and energy storage/demand response systems.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Anne Draddy (General questions); Rahn Barnes (Small projects <$150,000); Dana Johnson (Large projects ≥$150,000); Roger Clark (Technical energy questions)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations and for-profit small businesses located in Baltimore City within New Markets Tax Credit-eligible census tracts or Baltimore Main Streets Districts, as well as nonprofit or for-profit small-business real estate developers meeting affordability or neighborhood improvement criteria in eligible geographies. Nonprofits must provide at least 50% of services to families with incomes at or below 80% of area median income. For-profit small businesses must meet the SBA definition of 'small business' (tangible net worth <$15 million and average net income <$5 million after taxes for preceding two years).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy-saving building improvements including building envelope upgrades, HVAC and controls, lighting and controls, domestic hot water systems, low-flow plumbing fixtures, ENERGY STAR equipment, distributed generation (e.g., solar PV, combined heat-and-power) when part of a broader energy project, energy storage and demand response systems, and other measures that reduce building energy use. Nonprofits may use up to 20% of the loan (capped at $50,000) for non-energy improvements (health, safety, aesthetic issues) that enable the energy upgrades. Project soft costs/pre-development costs and hard costs for energy and eligible non-energy measures are covered.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located within Baltimore City and in an eligible area — specifically in New Markets Tax Credit-eligible census tracts or Baltimore Main Streets Districts. A mapping tool is available on the BEI website to confirm eligibility.
requirements_list: Must be a nonprofit organization, for-profit small business, or real estate project developer
Project must be located in Baltimore City within a New Markets Tax Credit-eligible census tract or a Baltimore Main Streets District
Tier 1 nonprofits must provide at least 50% of services to families with incomes at or below 80% of area median income

Tier 1 for-profit businesses must meet the SBA definition of 'small business' (tangible net worth <$15 million and average net income <$5 million after taxes for preceding two years) and be located in an eligible geography

Tier 2 real estate developers must provide new neighborhood amenities, address widespread vacancy, or include affordability commitments (at least 50% of housing serving residents at or below 80% of area median income)

Retrofit projects must achieve at least a 15% energy improvement (BTU basis); new construction Tier 1 must achieve 10% energy savings below applicable code; new construction Tier 2 must achieve 15% energy savings below applicable code
Gut rehab projects must meet International Residential Code or International Green Construction Code
Energy audits must be ASHRAE Level II or comparable by BPI-certified auditor for retrofits
Energy modeling must use approved software (DOE-2.2, EnergyPlus, eQuest, HAP, Trace, or RESNET HERS) for gut rehabs or new construction
Individual homeowners are NOT eligible
BGE Energy Solutions rebate required
Projects must involve retrofits of existing buildings, gut rehab projects, substantial rehabilitation/reconstruction, or new construction with energy measures

Loan recipients must participate in ongoing impact tracking including benchmarking via ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager and providing building energy consumption data for a defined period before and after project completion
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review the Program Guidelines and Instructions, then complete and submit the Initial Financing Request Form (as a Word document with a unique filename) by email to BEI@reinvestment.com or LoanRequests@EnergyLoansBEI.org. The program website also has available documents including the two-page Initial Financing Request Form.
