The initiative aims to help HBCUs overcome financial barriers, strengthen their institutional capacity, and deepen their role as community anchors and centers of academic excellence. Since 2018, Reinvestment Fund has loaned more than $50 million to HBCUs through this initiative, funding capital projects, infrastructure improvements, balance sheet restructuring, and new real estate development.

Since 2018, Reinvestment Fund has loaned more than $50 million to HBCUs. Credit enhancement and network-building support are also available. Grants fund developmental projects such as campus infrastructure improvements, predevelopment and planning, and sustainability and environmental initiatives. Technical assistance is provided through a curriculum administered by Reinvestment Fund and a council of HBCU leaders, advocates, and financial experts.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Campus infrastructure improvements, predevelopment and planning, sustainability and environmental initiatives, and institutional development activities.

structured_extraction.program_description: Invest Health is a national cross-sector initiative that brings together diverse leaders from small to mid-sized U.S. cities to develop new strategies for increasing public and private investment and accelerating improvements in neighborhoods facing the biggest barriers to better health. The program supports new partnerships in 50 cities, addressing social determinants of health such as jobs, housing, education, community safety, and environmental conditions in low-income communities. It provides small grants, peer learning exchanges, convenings, access to skilled faculty advisors and coaches, and a learning community to support pipeline development for financeable built environment projects, improve community development investment systems, and prioritize community engagement, data, and equity.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Each selected city team receives a $60,000 grant. Teams also participate in a learning community, have access to skilled faculty advisors and coaches, and engage local stakeholders to encourage knowledge sharing. Additional support includes peer learning exchanges and convenings to develop financeable built environment projects and improve community development investment systems.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Diverse cross-sector city leaders and teams in small to mid-sized U.S. cities working to improve health outcomes in low-income neighborhoods through community development and investment.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Developing strategies to increase public and private investment and accelerate health improvements in low-income neighborhoods; addressing social determinants of health including jobs, housing, education, community safety, and environmental conditions; supporting community engagement, data, and equity work; and developing financeable built environment projects.

Focus must be on improving health outcomes in low-income neighborhoods

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County Early Childhood Education (ECE) Facility Loan Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A loan program that helps licensed child care providers in Montgomery County, Maryland grow, improve, and serve more families. The program offers forgivable loans and zero-interest loans to expand or upgrade child care facilities, with the goal of giving children across the county — especially those in underserved and low-income communities — equitable access to safe, high-quality child care. Montgomery County funds the program, which is administered by Reinvestment Fund in partnership with the Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services. Three loan types are available: forgivable loans for both home-based and center-based providers (up to $74,000, forgiven 20% per year over five years); pre-development loans (a special type of forgivable loan, fully forgiven after one year) covering planning costs ($1,000–$10,000 for homes; $5,000–$50,000 for centers); and zero-interest loans for center-based providers only (up to $200,000 for quality improvements or $300,000 for facility expansion). Loans can cover expanding child care capacity, renovating or upgrading spaces, pre-development costs, and purchasing equipment and materials. The program also includes technical assistance and professional development support. Religious-affiliated programs must be organized as independent business entities to be eligible.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Three loan types are available: (1) Forgivable Loans for both home-based and center-based providers — up to $74,000, 0% interest, forgiven 20% per year over five years (no repayment required if the borrower remains open and licensed for five years and completes 12 hours of business training per year); can be used for facility expansion or improvement. (2) Pre-Development Loans (a special type of forgivable loan) — $1,000–$10,000 for homes; $5,000–$50,000 for centers; fully forgiven after one year if requirements are met; covers planning costs such as zoning contracts, architect contracts, and building permits. (3) Zero-Interest (0%) Loans for center-based providers only — up to $200,000 for quality improvements or $300,000 for expansion; must be repaid but with no interest charged; flexible repayment schedule based on business plan and ability to pay. All loan types can cover expanding child care capacity, renovating or upgrading spaces, pre-development costs (architect fees, permits, zoning approvals), and purchasing equipment, furniture, fixtures, and educational/learning materials. The program also provides technical assistance and professional development, including required annual business training covering loan terms/forgiveness, budgeting/sustainability, tax management, time management, grants/financing opportunities, and HR/hiring.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications are closed. Decisions were communicated in April 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: The New Markets Tax Credit (NMTC) program attracts private investment into low-income and severely distressed communities by leveraging federal tax credits. Investors receive tax credits equal to 39% of their qualified equity investment, spread over a seven-year compliance period, in exchange for financing community development projects in qualifying census tracts. Reinvestment Fund and Enterprise Community Partners are among the allocatees that channel NMTC financing to projects in distressed communities. Reinvestment Fund prioritizes projects in severely distressed census tracts that provide essential services such as health care, education, and access to healthy food, as well as projects that anchor community revitalization. Since 2004, Reinvestment Fund alone has received $663.4 million in NMTC allocations supporting close to $1.7 billion in total investments.
eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Investors receive federal tax credits equal to 39% of their qualified equity investment, claimed over a seven-year compliance period (5% per year for the first three years, then 6% per year for the remaining four years). Reinvestment Fund provides NMTC financing with flexible features including subordinated debt, below-market interest rates, lower-than-standard origination fees, longer interest-only payment periods, higher-than-standard loan-to-value ratios, longer amortization periods, more flexible borrower credit standards, and lower debt service coverage ratio requirements. Reinvestment Fund can serve as a bridge lender, leverage lender, direct lender, allocatee, or co-lender. Enterprise Community Partners also allocates NMTC financing to qualifying community development projects. Eligible use of funds includes working capital, equipment purchases, inventory purchases, construction of new buildings, rehabilitation of existing buildings, and expense reimbursement.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community and economic development projects in severely distressed, low-income communities seeking flexible financing for health care, education, food access, housing, commercial revitalization, business expansion, and community facilities. Projects serving underserved people and communities, advancing racial equity, and providing low-income community benefits.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Community revitalization, economic opportunity, and community services projects including healthcare facilities, education, workforce development, affordable housing, commercial development, real estate development, business expansion, and community facilities in low-income communities. Eligible uses include working capital, equipment purchases, inventory purchases, construction of new buildings, rehabilitation of existing buildings, and expense reimbursement.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in qualifying low-income census tracts (2010 Census) and severely distressed census tracts that qualify as low-income communities under NMTC eligibility criteria, including qualifying census tracts nationwide and in Maryland.
requirements_list: Project must be located in a qualifying low-income census tract
Project must be located in a severely distressed census tract (Reinvestment Fund priority)
Project must provide essential services (health care, education, food access) or serve as a community revitalization anchor
Projects should demonstrate meaningful input from low-income community residents
Projects should prioritize services for the most impacted communities
Must demonstrate community impact and benefit to low-income residents
Must meet the allocatee's investment and underwriting criteria
Project must fit Reinvestment Fund's mission and NMTC priorities
Must expand economic opportunity for underserved people and communities
Must meet federal NMTC program requirements
Housing projects: minimum 25% of units reserved for households earning ≤80% AMFI
Projects prioritized on quantitative and qualitative impact

For Enterprise Community Partners: Contact Enterprise to discuss project eligibility and financing needs; Enterprise reviews applications and allocates NMTC financing to qualifying projects.

structured_extraction.program_description: Pay for Success (PfS) financing, sometimes called a social impact bond, is an innovative financing mechanism that helps governments test and scale promising policy programs while reducing financial risk. A government agency contracts with a private service provider to deliver a program and only pays when the provider meets specific performance targets. The service provider gets working capital through private financing, which is repaid with a modest return only when goals are achieved. Reinvestment Fund acts as a senior lender in PfS transactions, with deep experience in housing, social services, and early childhood intervention.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reinvestment Fund provides senior lending (working capital loans) to service providers participating in Pay for Success transactions. The loan is repaid with a modest return only when the service provider meets its performance targets under the government contract. Loan amounts and terms vary by transaction.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private service providers and government agencies engaged in Pay for Success transactions, particularly in housing, social services, juvenile justice, and early childhood education.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Working capital to fund operations while awaiting performance-based payments from a government payer.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: No explicit geographic restriction stated; Reinvestment Fund operates nationally with examples in Cuyahoga County (Ohio) and Santa Clara County (California).
requirements_list: Applicant must be a service provider in a Pay for Success contract with a government agency
Payments from government are contingent on meeting defined performance targets
Contracts typically run several years or more
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Reinvestment Fund to learn more about Pay for Success financing opportunities. No formal application process is described on the page.

structured_extraction.program_description: Reinvestment Fund offers promissory notes as a direct investment opportunity in its diversified loan fund. Investors earn a modest financial return while their capital supports socially and environmentally responsible development projects that benefit low-income communities, including affordable housing, health, education, and food access. The fund has operated since 1985 and has made over $3 billion in loans to community businesses across 17 jurisdictions including Maryland. Reinvestment Fund, Inc. is a federally certified Community Development Financial Institution (CDFI) and 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Promissory notes (impact investments) starting at $1,000 and up to $5 million. Interest rates are: 3.75% for 3–4 year terms; 4.50% for 5, 7, or 10 year terms; and 5.00% for a 15-year term. Fixed interest rates are set at time of issuance with annual interest payments. Notes are unsecured obligations with no restrictive covenants and auto-reinvest at maturity unless the investor elects repayment. No early redemption without mutual written consent. The program has maintained a 100% repayment rate since 1985. Investments are not government-insured and are not tax-deductible charitable gifts. Proceeds are used to make loans and equity investments in organizations and businesses serving low-wealth communities, including housing, education, food access, commercial real estate, health care, and clean energy sectors.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individual investors (including school teachers and CEOs), faith-based organizations, family foundations, banks, civic organizations, higher education institutions, and others in 17 jurisdictions including Maryland who want to earn a financial return while supporting community development projects. Also serves low-wealth communities, low- and moderate-income individuals, underserved communities, and minority and women entrepreneurs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital is deployed as loans to community businesses and development projects supporting low-income communities, including affordable housing, health care, education, and food access. Funds may also be used for equity investments, loans to affiliates (including TRF Enterprise Fund, Inc. for re-lending to urban-based small businesses and PolicyMap up to $1,250,000), capital contributions to affiliate RFIA, and to refinance existing obligations. Some interest earnings may offset Fund operating expenses and fund the loan loss reserve.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to investors in 17 jurisdictions: PA, MD, DC, NJ, VA, GA, CT, HI, IL, IA, ME, MA, MS, NM, RI, SD, and TX. Fund conducts lending and investment activities nationally with a focus on low-income and distressed communities.
requirements_list: Investor must be located in one of the 17 eligible jurisdictions: PA, MD, DC, NJ, VA, GA, CT, HI, IL, IA, ME, MA, MS, NM, RI, SD, or TX
Minimum investment of $1,000
Maximum investment of $5 million
Investors must have no need for liquidity in their investment
Investors must understand significant risk of total loss, as investments are unsecured and not government-insured
Investments funded via wire transfer, automated clearing house (ACH), or check
Audited financial statements provided annually within 120 days of fiscal year-end
Withdrawal right available within two business days of receiving prospectus
Backup withholding of 24% may apply if investor fails to provide proper tax documentation (TIN)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download a copy of the prospectus from the Reinvestment Fund website. Use the investor toolkit available on the website to open a new promissory note. Investor remits funds to Reinvestment Fund, Inc. via wire transfer, ACH, or check. A written notice is required if the investor wishes to withdraw within the two business day withdrawal period after receiving the prospectus. For questions, contact Reinvestment Fund by phone at 215.574.5819 or email invest@reinvestment.com.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Agricultural Education and Rural Development Assistance Fund (MAERDAF) / Rural Maryland Prosperity Investment Fund (RMPIF)
structured_extraction.program_description: MAERDAF/RMPIF is a competitive grant program administered by the Rural Maryland Council that invests in rural-serving nonprofit organizations, community colleges, for-profit entities, and government bodies to promote statewide and regional planning, economic and community development, and agricultural and forestry education. The program aims to raise the overall standard of living in rural areas to meet or exceed statewide benchmark averages by 2030, while preserving cultural heritage and the rural way of life. It supports targeted investments in economic and community development programs, promotes regional and intergovernmental cooperation, increases organizational capacity to address rural development challenges, supports small and agricultural businesses through enhanced training and technical assistance, and builds public/private partnerships to leverage non-state funding. Specific areas include regional infrastructure, rural entrepreneurship, agricultural development, workforce development, cooperative development, and rural health care. The FY2027 appropriation is $6,047,464. Grants are awarded up to $25,000 per award, with an average grant of approximately $18,000. Priority is given to applicants with matching funds from non-state sources, though matching is not required. The program operates through a two-phase application process including a Letter of Intent (Phase I) followed by a full application.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants awarded to eligible organizations through a two-phase application process. Grants are up to $25,000 per award, with an average grant of approximately $18,000 over the life of the program. The FY2027 rural Maryland appropriation is $6,047,464. Priority is given to applicants with non-state matching funds, though matching is not required; federal funds count as matching. Phase I (Letter of Intent) is due May 15, 2026, followed by a full application due July 10, 2026. Awards are announced the week of August 17, 2026.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Phase 1 Letter of Intent: Friday, May 15, 2026; Phase 2 Full Application: Friday, July 10, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Rural-serving nonprofit organizations (501(c)(3) or similar), rural community colleges, for-profit businesses, and government entities in Maryland focused on statewide and regional planning, economic and community development, agricultural and forestry education, and rural prosperity initiatives. Applicants do not need to be located in a rural area but must serve a regional or statewide rural constituency.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Statewide and regional planning, economic and community development, agricultural and forestry education, training and technical assistance for small and agricultural businesses, building public/private partnerships to leverage non-state funding, facilitating targeted investments in economic and community development programs, promoting regional and intergovernmental cooperation, and improving quality of life in rural Maryland. Specific areas include regional infrastructure, rural entrepreneurship, agricultural development, workforce development, cooperative development, and rural health care. Projects must serve more than one rural county and be completed within the grant period. Additional eligible uses include capital items, job creation initiatives, grant-writing skill development, volunteer board and staff development, and institutional capacity building.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide, with a focus on rural areas of Maryland including the Eastern Shore, Western Maryland, and Southern Maryland. Projects must serve more than one rural county. State-designated rural counties include: Allegany, Calvert, Caroline, Carroll, Cecil, Charles, Dorchester, Frederick, Garrett, Harford, Kent, Queen Anne's, St. Mary's, Somerset, Talbot, Washington, Wicomico, and Worcester.
requirements_list: Must be a rural-serving nonprofit organization, rural community college, for-profit business, or government entity
Applicant must be a 501(c)(3) or similar tax-exempt organization serving a regional or statewide rural constituency (for nonprofit applicants)
Trade associations are not eligible
Applicant does not need to be located in a rural area
Must promote statewide or regional planning, economic and community development, or agricultural and forestry education
Community colleges must support small and agricultural businesses through enhanced training and technical assistance
Project must serve more than one rural county
Project must be completed within the applicable grant period
Maximum grant is $25,000
Priority given to applicants with non-state matching funds, though not required; federal funds count as matching
Only minor changes in project scope are allowed after award
Unused funds must be returned by the end of the grant period
Past and current grantees are eligible if they have met all prior grant agreement requirements including reporting deadlines
Must submit a Letter of Intent (Phase I) as part of the two-phase application process
Submit reports through RMC Grant Portal
Interim and final reports required with original documentation of expenditures (Interim Report due January 31; Final Report due July 15)
Acknowledge RMC funding with RMC logo in promotional materials
Complete Managing for Results (MFR) metrics as applicable
Provide evidence of project success and measurable outcomes
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The program operates on an annual cycle with a two-phase process. Phase 1: Submit Letter of Intent by May 15, 2026. Applicants notified of Phase 1 decision the week of June 18, 2026. Phase 2: Submit full application by July 10, 2026. Awards announced the week of August 17, 2026. The full application package must be submitted by email only (no paper applications accepted) and must include: (1) a completed MAERDAF application form, (2) a project narrative of no more than 5 pages, and (3) Appendix Attachments A-E, all combined into one Word or PDF file. Applications are reviewed by the MAERDAF Grant Review Board and the Rural Maryland Council. After award, grantees must execute a grant agreement and submit reports through the RMC Grant Portal. Visit Rural.Maryland.gov for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Rural Health Transformation (RHT) - Rural Maryland Council Food Access Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Supports initiatives that improve access to healthy, locally sourced food across rural communities. Funds projects that expand post-harvest infrastructure for small farms, enhance food distribution through food hubs and mobile markets, increase procurement of local foods by institutions such as schools, hospitals, and community organizations, and advance nutrition education and regional coordination to address food insecurity in rural areas.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants to support rural food access and health initiatives. Specific award amounts are not stated on the page.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Phase 1 Letter of Intent: Friday, May 15, 2026; Phase 2 Full Application: Friday, July 10, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations working to improve food access and address food insecurity in rural Maryland communities, including those operating small farms, food hubs, mobile markets, and institutions such as schools and hospitals.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Expanding post-harvest infrastructure for small farms, enhancing food distribution through food hubs and mobile markets, increasing local food procurement by institutions, advancing nutrition education, and supporting regional coordination to address food insecurity.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to organizations serving rural areas of Maryland, with priority for rural 'hot spot' communities facing food insecurity.
requirements_list: Projects must serve rural communities in Maryland
Must focus on improving access to healthy, locally sourced food
Eligible activities include post-harvest infrastructure, food distribution, institutional food procurement, nutrition education, or regional food system coordination
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Phase 1: Submit Letter of Intent by May 15, 2026. Applicants notified of Phase 1 decision the week of June 18, 2026. Phase 2: Submit full application by July 10, 2026. Awards announced the week of August 17, 2026. An information session was held April 30, 2026 via Zoom.

structured_extraction.program_description: This fund provides grants to improve the standard of living in Maryland's rural areas. It supports key economic and community development projects. The program also encourages cooperation between regions and governments.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers grants for economic and community development. The Fiscal Year 2026 grant cycle made $6,000,000 in funding available for projects in rural Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Fiscal Year 2026 Grant Process Is Now Closed
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local and regional public organizations and nonprofit organizations serving rural areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support economic and community development projects. Specific areas include regional infrastructure, rural entrepreneurship, agricultural development, workforce development, cooperative development, and rural health care.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is for projects that benefit rural areas in Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The application process has two phases. First, applicants submit a Letter of Intent. If approved, they then submit a full application.

structured_extraction.program_description: ShoreCorps is a service program where members work for one year with a nonprofit or government agency on Maryland's Eastern Shore. Members help meet community needs in areas like environmental education, youth development, senior care, and financial literacy.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Members who complete a year of service can receive a Segal Education Award.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals who want to serve their community for one year. Members do not have to be students.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program serves communities on Maryland's Eastern Shore.
requirements_list: Must commit to one year of service.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To apply, interested individuals should visit the program website to learn more about the requirements, benefits, and application process.

structured_extraction.program_description: The SWED Ag Grant Fund fosters growth in Wicomico County's emerging agriculture and resource-based industries by providing grant funding through a partnership between Wicomico County, PNC Bank, and the Maryland Agricultural & Resource Based Industry Development Corporation (MARBIDCO). The fund provides grants to new and existing agriculture and resource-based businesses for startup and growth needs, including equipment and infrastructure purchases for agricultural production, as well as projects supporting farming, forestry, seafood, agritourism, and the production, packaging, processing, or marketing of agricultural products. It operates as a cost-share program, requiring the applicant to contribute at least 50% of the total project cost.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides one-time reimbursable grants to agriculture and resource-based businesses in Wicomico County. Targeted grant amounts are $2,500 or less per applicant, matched by MARBIDCO, with a maximum of $25,000 total. FSMA matching grants are capped at $5,000; deer fences and farm operation solar/generators are capped at $3,000. The MARBIDCO grant cannot exceed the local government's investment. It operates as a cost-share program, requiring the applicant to contribute at least 50% of the total project cost. Funds are distributed on a reimbursement basis.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit agricultural and resource-based businesses headquartered and located in Wicomico County, Maryland, including minority-owned, women-owned, disabled-owned, and veteran-owned businesses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Equipment and infrastructure purchases, agri-tourism (new or expansion of current initiatives), agricultural business diversification (new or expansion of current initiatives), deer fencing (specifications determined by MARBIDCO), value-added food processing infrastructure, timber processing equipment, and other agriculture and resource-based industry project costs including projects supporting farming, forestry, seafood, agritourism, and the production, packaging, processing, or marketing of agricultural products, subject to MARBIDCO approval.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must have their headquarters and main operations in Wicomico County, Maryland, and must be in Good Standing with the State of Maryland and Wicomico County.
requirements_list: Must operate in agriculture or resource-based industry in Wicomico County.
The applicant must contribute at least 50% of the total project cost.
The business must be registered and in good standing with the State of Maryland and Wicomico County.
The project must help Wicomico County's farming, forestry, or seafood industries.
Businesses that package, process, or market agricultural products are also eligible.
Business must be currently in operation.
Nonprofits are not eligible.
Must maintain records on fund expenditures.
Funds are distributed on a reimbursement basis.
Subject to audit with documentation requirements (tax returns, financial statements, receipts, payroll records, etc.).
Must provide correct Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) via IRS Form W-9.
Must certify U.S. person status and compliance with federal, state, and local laws.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants download and complete the fillable PDF application and submit it along with a signed grant agreement and IRS W-9 form to Salisbury-Wicomico Economic Development (SWED). SWED then submits the application to the Maryland Agricultural & Resource Based Industry Development Corporation (MARBIDCO). Both SWED and MARBIDCO must approve the application. See the FAQ and grant agreement documents for details.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants for weatherization and related repairs for qualifying members of Choptank Electric Cooperative.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants for weatherization and related home repairs for eligible Choptank Electric Cooperative members.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Choptank Electric Cooperative members who qualify for weatherization assistance.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Weatherization and related home repairs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to members of Choptank Electric Cooperative in its service territory.
requirements_list: Must be a member of Choptank Electric Cooperative
Must qualify based on program criteria
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: See linked program document for details on how to apply.

structured_extraction.program_name: FEMA National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) Community Rating System (CRS) - Somerset County
structured_extraction.program_description: Somerset County participates in FEMA's National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) Community Rating System (CRS), a program that rewards communities that go beyond minimum floodplain management standards. Because Somerset County has achieved Class 7 CRS status (effective April 1, 2025), county residents can receive a discount on their NFIP flood insurance policy premiums when those policies come up for renewal. No separate application is required — the discount is applied automatically at renewal.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible Somerset County residents can receive up to a 15% reduction on their NFIP flood insurance policy premiums at renewal, as Somerset County is a CRS Class 7 community. This discount takes effect April 1, 2025, and is applied automatically when an NFIP policy renews for properties located in Somerset County.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Somerset County residents who hold National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) flood insurance policies.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of flood insurance policy premiums at renewal — discount applied automatically at policy renewal as a result of Somerset County's Class 7 CRS participation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Somerset County, Maryland, which is a CRS Class 7 community.
requirements_list: Must be a Somerset County resident
Must hold an NFIP flood insurance policy
Discount applies when the policy comes up for renewal
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: No separate application is required. The discount is automatically applied to eligible NFIP policies at renewal because Somerset County participates in the CRS program at Class 7 level. The property must be located in Somerset County.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides complementary door-to-door paratransit transportation for people with disabilities who are unable to use the regular STS public bus service and live within three-quarters of a mile of a fixed public transportation route in St. Mary's County, as required by the Americans with Disabilities Act. Service is available on-call during normal public transit hours (Monday–Saturday 6am–10pm; Sunday 6am–8pm on California/Great Mills route), and all buses are wheelchair accessible. The program aims to provide at least 6,000 trips per year. Discount fare identification cards are available from the STS Transit office. Out-of-town visitors with ADA Paratransit certification from their home transit system may use the service for up to 21 days per year. The fare is $2.00 per one-way trip or $4.00 round trip ($20.00 for a sheet of 10 tickets).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Door-to-door paratransit transportation for certified riders with disabilities. Service is available on-call during normal public transit hours (Monday–Saturday 6am–10pm; Sunday 6am–8pm on California/Great Mills route) within three-quarters of a mile of all fixed STS public transportation routes in St. Mary's County. Next-day service is required by law, and the program aims to provide at least 6,000 trips per year. Fare is $2.00 per one-way trip or $4.00 round trip ($20.00 for a sheet of 10 tickets). Discount fare identification cards are available from the STS Transit office. Vehicles include wheelchair lifts/ramps, driver assistance with boarding/disembarking, accommodations for service animals and portable oxygen, and wheelchair securement.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Persons with disabilities who are unable to use the regular STS public bus service and live within three-quarters of a mile of a fixed public transportation route in St. Mary's County, including seniors age 60 and above, and out-of-town visitors with ADA Paratransit certification from their home transit system (limited to 21 days per year for visitors).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Transportation services (door-to-door rides) for persons with disabilities to destinations of the rider's choice within the eligible service area.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of St. Mary's County, Maryland whose origin to destination is within three-quarters of a mile of a fixed STS public transportation route, and out-of-town visitors with ADA Paratransit certification from their home transit system (limited to 21 days per year for visitors).
requirements_list: Must be a person with a disability unable to use regular STS public bus service (including inability to board, ride, or disembark from accessible vehicles; needing a wheelchair/mobility device; or having impairment-related conditions preventing travel to/from bus stops)
Must live within three-quarters of a mile of a fixed STS public transportation route
Must complete and submit an Application for Paratransit Transportation to the STS Office with required documentation (disability certification from doctor, SSI/SSDI, VA, TDAP, or other entity)
Must be determined eligible through the application process
Reservations required by 5pm the day before travel
Exact fare payment required at pickup ($2.00 one-way or $4.00 round trip)
Home/building pick-up locations must have a wheelchair ramp or an assistant available
Accessible driveway with safe turnaround for bus access required
One stop per round trip (additional stops charged $2.00 or require rescheduling)
Passengers must be prepared to board 10 minutes prior to scheduled pickup time
Children under 12 years must be accompanied by an adult
Must comply with health and cleanliness standards and control service animals
Out-of-town visitors must provide proof of residence outside St. Mary's County and ADA Paratransit certification from their home system
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Application for Paratransit Transportation (including appropriate sections for paratransit, disability discount fare card, or senior discount fare card) and submit it with required documentation to the STS Office by mail or fax at (301) 866-6797. Allow 1–2 weeks for processing. Once approved, call the STS Office at (301) 475-4200 ext. 1120 by 5pm the day before your trip or email SDispatchers@stmaryscountymd.gov to make a reservation. You may also contact Mary Ann Blankenship by email or phone for assistance with the application.

structured_extraction.program_name: Accessible Homes for Seniors Program (St. Mary's County)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides 0% interest loans to help homeowners make accessibility improvements to their homes, such as wheelchair ramps, bathroom modifications, and grab bars.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 0% interest loan for home accessibility modifications including wheelchair ramps, bathroom modifications, and grab bars.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners who want to make accessibility improvements to their homes.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home accessibility improvements such as wheelchair ramps, bathroom modifications, and grab bars.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_description: A judicially supervised treatment program for St. Mary's County residents with substance abuse-driven criminal histories. Instead of incarceration, eligible participants complete a structured four-phase program of addiction treatment, drug testing, case management, employment, and housing stability to achieve sustained sobriety and avoid future criminal behavior. The program lasts a minimum of 12–18 months, possibly longer.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive judicially supervised addiction treatment, case management, drug and alcohol testing (random and scheduled), recovery support, mental health services, employment/job training and education support, self-help groups, and self-improvement courses (anger management, parenting, relationship counseling). The program costs approximately $19 per day ($7,105 per year) compared to $99–$105 per day for incarceration. Participants may owe fees for treatment, drug testing, and alcohol monitoring (SCRAM bracelet) in addition to probation and parole fees.
structured_extraction.program_audience: St. Mary's County residents with substance abuse-driven criminal histories, including repeat DUI offenders, who would otherwise face incarceration or a probation violation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Addiction treatment (inpatient and outpatient), drug and alcohol testing, mental health services, case management, recovery support meetings, employment/job training and education assistance, housing stability support, and self-improvement courses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a full-time resident of St. Mary's County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must enter the program after a guilty plea or admission of probation violation (post-plea)
Must waive right to speedy trial and preliminary hearing
Must have a determination of drug abuse or dependency / current substance abuse assessment required
Must voluntarily enter the program
Must be a full-time resident of St. Mary's County
All active criminal/jailable traffic cases must be resolved prior to entry
Home study must be completed
No serious disqualifying mental or physical health issues (reviewed case by case)
Not a gang member
Not a violent offender (prior violent crime convictions generally disqualifying; exceptions possible)
Not a sex offender (prior sexual offense convictions generally disqualifying; exceptions possible)
No drug distribution charges (generally disqualifying; exceptions possible)
No assault or weapons offenses unless unanimously approved by the ARC team
Must remain clean, sober, and law-abiding throughout the program
Must comply with all supervision requirements
Must not possess alcohol, cannabis, illicit drugs, or drug paraphernalia
Must not associate with drug/alcohol users
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete the application (PDF available on the program page) and submit to Linda Spates (Recovery Court Coordinator). Applicants are placed on a candidate list and reviewed by the Recovery Court team. The candidate is notified of the review date; if accepted, they are notified of the court entry date (a waiting list is possible). If accepted, sign the participant agreement (contract). Progress through four program phases, each with specific requirements, before becoming eligible for graduation.

structured_extraction.program_description: St. Mary's County Public Schools offers an after-school mentoring program for Community Schools in Lexington Park. The program works to combat poverty by providing students with individual and small group interactions with caring adults and lessons focusing on social skills and healthy lifestyles, using the MindUp Curriculum.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Students receive after-school mentoring with individual and small group interactions with caring adults focused on social skills and healthy lifestyles.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students at Community Schools in Lexington Park
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Lexington Park, St. Mary's County, MD

structured_extraction.program_name: Aging and Disability Resource Center / Maryland Access Point (ADRC/MAP)
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Access Point (MAP) is a free information and referral service that connects older adults, people with disabilities, and caregivers to health and support services. It provides a single point of entry to access information, individualized person-centered counseling and support for benefits and long-term care planning, and connections to community service providers. It helps individuals navigate the complex system of long-term support services and community resources.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free information, referral, and options counseling services. Staff connect individuals to community resources, benefits programs, and long-term care planning assistance. Services include assistance accessing in-home care options, healthcare, transportation, financial assistance programs, senior centers, nutrition and meals, pharmacy assistance, housing, volunteer opportunities, assistive technology, home-delivered meals, home modifications, home health aides, chore services, adult medical day care, and assisted living facilities. All services are confidential and open to all income levels.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Older adults, individuals age 18 and older with a disability, caregivers, healthcare providers, and aging professionals.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Information and referral to services, options counseling on benefits and long-term care, connection to partner agency services, and application assistance for public and private programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Maryland residents statewide, across all 23 counties and Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Open to adults 50 and over
Open to individuals 18 and older experiencing a disability
Open to caregivers
Open to anyone with concerns about a person in need
No income requirement for information and referral services; income guidelines may apply for some programs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact MAP by phone or walk in. Work with a certified Options Counselor to learn about available services, identify options, apply for programs, and access services. Services are available 24/7 via the statewide line.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grassroots nonprofit program designed to support at-risk youth socially and academically in St. Mary's County. The program assesses students' academic needs and provides group activities and one-on-one tutoring to foster independent thinking and improve future success.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Students referred to the program receive academic needs assessment, group activities, and one-on-one tutoring.
structured_extraction.program_audience: At-risk youth in St. Mary's County
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: St. Mary's County, MD
requirements_list: Referral to the program required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Referrals can be made to the program coordinator.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Christmas Caring Program connects families in need with community partners — including agencies, organizations, businesses, churches, schools, and individuals — who provide gifts of toys, clothing, and food during the holiday season. Sponsors are matched with specific children to give gifts based on each child's request. The program also partners with the U.S. Marine Corps' Toys for Tots Program to collect and distribute toys locally.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Families identified as needing help receive gifts (toys, educational items, or clothing) and food basket items (such as turkeys) donated by community sponsors. Monetary donations are tax-deductible.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families in St. Mary's County identified as needing assistance during the holiday season, as well as community members, businesses, churches, and schools interested in sponsoring families or donating.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Toys, educational items, clothing, and food for families in need during the holiday season.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of St. Mary's County, Maryland. Toys collected through Toys for Tots collection points remain in St. Mary's County.
requirements_list: Families must be identified in the database maintained in partnership with the Department of Social Services

Churches, businesses, or schools helping families specific to their organization should contact the Human Services Division to check if those families are already in the database to prevent duplication of service
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Families in need are identified through a database created in partnership with the Department of Social Services. Community members, businesses, churches, or schools wishing to sponsor a family or donate should contact the Human Services Division. Toys for Tots donations can be dropped at collection boxes at stores and establishments county-wide.

structured_extraction.program_name: Christmas In April, St. Mary's County
structured_extraction.program_description: A non-profit organization that helps low-to-moderate income homeowners with needed home repair projects at no charge. Homes are selected by a committee and repairs are made on the last Saturday in April.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free home repairs at no charge to the homeowner, completed on the last Saturday in April each year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-to-moderate income homeowners in St. Mary's County needing home repairs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Needed home repair projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: St. Mary's County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a low-to-moderate income homeowner
Must apply between May and October each year
Home selection made by committee
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply between May and October each year. A committee selects homes based on varying factors. Repairs are made at no charge on the last Saturday in April.

structured_extraction.program_description: A local chapter of a national mentoring program offering a multi-generational approach to poverty reduction. Weekly dinner meetings support Circle Leaders in all areas of life, including transportation, job training, financial literacy, physical health, emotional wellness, and community connection. Childcare with educational programming for children is provided during meetings.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Weekly dinner meetings provide support in transportation, job training, financial literacy, health, emotional wellness, and community, plus childcare with educational programming for children.

structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: St. Mary's County, MD

structured_extraction.program_description: A volunteer-led neighborhood program that helps St. Mary's County residents reduce litter, address junk-filled yards, and improve community appearance. The county provides support through its Department of Public Works and Transportation (DPW&T), including waste containers, safety supplies, and trash hauling services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The county provides waste collection containers, safety vests, trash bags, safety signage, and free litter pickup by county highway crews. Multiple sub-programs are available: the Neighborhood Litter Critter Program (containers dropped off Friday and hauled away Monday), Fall Clean-up Campaign, Adopt-A-County-Road, Litter Pick-up Program, and the CLEAN Team litter reporting program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: St. Mary's County residents, community groups, schools, and businesses wanting to improve neighborhood cleanliness and reduce litter
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Neighborhood litter cleanup, waste removal, community beautification efforts
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: St. Mary's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a resident or community group in St. Mary's County
Program is volunteer-led and requires neighborhood leadership for implementation
Containers may not be filled with appliances, tires, or large amounts of commercial construction materials
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Solid Waste Manager at (301) 475-4200 or email John.Curtis@stmaryscountymd.gov to set up a program or request services. For litter pickup requests, residents can also submit a Maintenance Request Form online.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides fresh, hot meals Monday through Friday at noontime to seniors at senior activity centers and one nutrition site in St. Mary's County. Meals are served at three senior activity centers and include protein, vegetables, starches, fruits, beverages, condiments, and 1% milk. Meals are available for a minimal cost or by donation depending on age.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Hot meals served at three senior activity centers and one nutrition site. Cost is $7.00 for individuals under age 60; free by donation for seniors age 60 and older. Meal reservations must be made by noon the business day before the meal date by calling the respective senior activity center.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Reservations must be made by noon the business day before meal date
structured_extraction.contact_phone: Garvey Senior Activity Center: 301-475-4200, ext. 1065; Loffler Senior Activity Center: 301-475-4200, ext. 1657; Northern Senior Activity Center: 301-475-4200, ext. 3105
structured_extraction.program_audience: Seniors in St. Mary's County, particularly those age 60 and older (donation appreciated); individuals under 60 years of age ($7.00 cost).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Daily hot lunch meals served at county senior activity centers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to seniors in St. Mary's County, Maryland at three senior activity centers and one nutrition site.
requirements_list: Must be age 50 or older
Meal reservation required by noon the business day before the meal date
Must contact respective senior activity center to reserve or cancel
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call the senior activity center of your choice (Garvey, Loffler, or Northern) to make a meal reservation by noon the business day before the desired meal date.

structured_extraction.program_name: Disability and Senior Discount Fare Cards
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides discounted fare cards to seniors and persons with disabilities for use on St. Mary's County public transit buses. Additional transportation assistance is available for seniors, persons with disabilities, and low-income residents including medical transportation, paratransit services, and wheelchair accessible options.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Discount fare cards reduce the cost of public transit to $0.50 for a one-way trip and $0.75 with a transfer for eligible seniors and persons with disabilities. Public Transportation operates Monday through Sunday.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Seniors and persons with disabilities who ride St. Mary's County public transportation buses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduced-cost bus fares on public transportation routes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: St. Mary's County public transportation routes.
requirements_list: Must be a senior or person with a disability
Must qualify through the application process
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Mary Ann Blankenship by email or phone to learn how to qualify for the discount fare program.

structured_extraction.program_description: An annual program that distributes free farm fresh produce from local farmers to community members in St. Mary's County. Residents can pick up a box of fresh vegetables such as corn, tomatoes, and squash at designated distribution events.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free boxes of farm fresh produce distributed at two events per year. Each family unit is limited to one box per event, available until the event end time or until supplies run out.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community members in St. Mary's County seeking free fresh produce
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free farm fresh produce for household consumption
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: St. Mary's County, Maryland — distribution at Bay District Fire Department and Feed St. Mary's Food Bank in Lexington Park
requirements_list: Limited to one box of produce per family unit per event
Must attend during scheduled distribution hours
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: No application required. Attend one of the scheduled distribution events at the listed locations during the designated hours while supplies last.

structured_extraction.program_description: Fast TRAC is a St. Mary's County initiative to help residents get connected to the internet. It bundles digital skills training, connected device distribution (free HP Chromebooks to eligible households), internet affordability support, and broadband infrastructure expansion to help all county residents make full use of online resources. The Chromebook distribution component is grant-funded by the Maryland Office of Statewide Broadband.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides multiple forms of assistance: (1) digital skills training through a partnership with the University of Maryland Extension Office; (2) one free HP Chromebook per eligible household distributed through a Connected Devices Grant (4,500+ devices); (3) referrals to the Federal Affordable Connectivity Program (ACP) through Breezeline and Comcast for reduced-cost internet service; and (4) grants to expand last-mile and middle-mile broadband infrastructure in the county. Chromebook eligibility requires household income at or below 200% of Federal Poverty Guidelines or participation in qualifying assistance programs.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Bob Kelly (IT Department) / Jenna Guzman (Communications Director)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Southern Maryland residents (St. Mary's, Calvert, and Charles Counties) who lack internet access, digital skills, or affordable connectivity options; Chromebook distribution targets low-income households meeting eligibility criteria
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Internet access, digital devices (free HP Chromebooks), digital literacy training, broadband infrastructure expansion, and support for education, work, and everyday connectivity
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of St. Mary's, Calvert, and Charles Counties in Southern Maryland. Proof of address required for Chromebook distribution. Distribution events held in St. Mary's County (Lexington Park, District 4 Station, 21633 Great Mills Rd).
requirements_list: Household income at or below 200% of Federal Poverty Guidelines, OR participation in SNAP, Medicaid, WIC, SSI, FPHA, Veterans Pension and Survivors Benefit, Free/Reduced-Price School Lunch/Breakfast Programs, or current Federal Pell Grant recipient
Proof of eligibility and proof of address required
One device per household
Households cannot have received a Chromebook from prior distributions
While supplies last
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Attend a distribution event (e.g., December 14, 2024 at District 4 Station, 21633 Great Mills Rd, Lexington Park). Bring proof of eligibility and proof of address. Eligibility is verified on-site. Eligible households receive one free HP Chromebook along with tech support. Residents can also sign up for the Affordable Connectivity Program through Breezeline or Comcast and access training resources through the University of Maryland Extension Office and the county library.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federally funded, competitive grant program that helps homeowners reduce flood damage risk, including elevation of structures and other hazard mitigation measures. St. Mary's County Department of Emergency Services applies on behalf of eligible homeowners as a subrecipient of funding from FEMA through the Maryland Department of Emergency Management (MDEM). Projects are ranked by MDEM and FEMA based on eligibility, cost-effectiveness, and ranking before funding is awarded. The program is offered on an annual basis with due dates set each year based on FEMA fund availability.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: FEMA provides grants covering 75% of the total project cost for eligible flood mitigation measures (90% for Repetitive Loss properties; 100% for Severe Repetitive Loss properties), including home elevation, acquisition, and other flood risk reduction projects. Eligible costs include detachment, raising, and re-attachment of structure to foundation, and directly related structural or utility work. New construction, upgrades, and additions are not eligible. The homeowner must contribute 25% of the total project cost held in escrow (for standard properties). The grant is offered on an annual basis; due dates are set each year based on FEMA fund availability. Specific amounts and terms are also detailed in the MEMA Hazard Mitigation Grants for Homeowners PDF guide.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annual; due dates communicated each year based on fund availability from FEMA
structured_extraction.program_audience: St. Mary's County homeowners whose homes are at high risk for flood damage and are insured through the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP), seeking to reduce flood risk through hazard mitigation measures such as home elevation. Also applies to property owners in Special Flood Hazard Areas (SFHA) with flood-prone properties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Flood hazard mitigation measures that reduce flood damage to the home, including elevation of structures so the lowest occupied floor is above Base Flood Elevation (BFE), acquisition, or other flood risk reduction projects. Eligible costs include detachment, raising, and re-attachment of structure to foundation and directly related structural or utility work.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Home must be located within a flood zone in St. Mary's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Home must be actively insured through the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP)
Home must be located within a flood zone

Homeowner must be willing and able to commit to providing 25% of the total project cost in an escrow account upon project approval (standard properties; reduced or no match required for Repetitive Loss or Severe Repetitive Loss properties)
Must provide an Elevation Certificate
Must provide a copy of the NFIP Declaration
Must provide documentation of previous losses due to flooding (if applicable)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Email EMA@stmaryscountymd.gov with required documents (Elevation Certificate, NFIP Declaration, flood loss documentation) and express interest in applying. 2. Emergency Management staff will contact you about the next available application cycle and any additional requirements. 3. Staff will work with you to gather project proposals and additional required documentation, then submit the application on your behalf. The process may take several months to submit, approximately a year for approval, and an additional year for funding release if approved. Additional guidance is available in the MEMA Hazard Mitigation Grants for Homeowners PDF guide at https://www.stmaryscountymd.gov/docs/HomeownerHMAElevationGuide.pdf.

structured_extraction.program_name: Historic Preservation Real Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A real property tax credit available to owners of historic landmarks and properties in local historic districts in St. Mary's County. Property owners who rehabilitate or maintain qualifying historic properties may receive a credit against their county real property taxes. The credit applies to St. Mary's County real estate taxes commencing with the tax year immediately subsequent to completion of work, with unused portions carried forward up to four subsequent tax years.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A credit against St. Mary's County real property taxes for owners of historic landmarks and properties located within local historic districts who undertake qualifying rehabilitation or maintenance work. The credit commences with the tax year immediately subsequent to completion of work, and any unused portion may be carried forward up to four subsequent tax years.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Application must be submitted prior to the start of work
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of historic landmarks and properties within local historic districts in St. Mary's County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Historic preservation improvements and rehabilitation of qualifying historic properties
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: St. Mary's County, Maryland — properties must be located within a local historic district or designated as a historic landmark
requirements_list: Property must be a designated historic landmark or located within a local historic district
Application must be submitted before work begins
Work permit may be required (must contact Inspection and Permits)
Photographs of existing conditions required
Estimated cost proposal required
Work must comply with building permit requirements
Work must comply with Historic Preservation Commission standards
Receipts for actual expenditures required for final approval
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application with property details, work description, estimated costs, and photos before work begins; receive preliminary approval; complete work per specifications; submit receipts for final approval by Historic Preservation Commission; forwarded to County Commissioners for final approval.

structured_extraction.program_description: Delivers well-balanced meals and a friendly visit to homebound seniors in St. Mary's County who cannot shop or cook for themselves. Fresh meals are delivered by volunteers around noon Monday through Friday, and frozen meals are delivered once a week in sets of five.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free meals delivered to eligible homebound seniors. No charge to recipients, though donations are accepted. Funded through the federal Older Americans Act, state funds, county funds, and donations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homebound seniors age 60 or older in St. Mary's County who are unable to shop or cook for themselves
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Provision of nutritious meals delivered to the homes of eligible seniors
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: St. Mary's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be age 60 or older
Must be homebound (unable to leave home without assistance)
Must be unable to shop or cook for themselves
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Home-Delivered Meals Program Coordinator Danielle Manalansan at (301) 475-4200 ext. 1060 for more information or to apply.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Human Services Division collaborates with partner agencies to alleviate poverty and homelessness by building a coordinated system of care for individuals and families in St. Mary's County. Staff serve as liaisons to federal, state, and local grantors, monitor associated programs and services, and represent the county in homelessness prevention efforts including the WARM (Wrapping Arms 'Round Many) program and regional/statewide coalitions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Division coordinates a system of care for individuals and families facing poverty and homelessness. It acts as the required county government contact for Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) funding, monitors associated programs, and provides transportation support for the WARM homelessness prevention program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and families in St. Mary's County facing poverty or homelessness, as well as partner agencies providing related services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Coordination of services to prevent homelessness and alleviate poverty, including transportation for the WARM program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: St. Mary's County, Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Cynthia Brown, Human Services Division Manager, for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Housing Authority Home Repair Loan Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides low interest loans to homeowners who need major home repairs such as roofing, wells, and windows.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low interest loan for major home repairs such as roofing, wells, and windows.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners in St. Mary's County who need major home repairs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Major home repairs such as roofing, wells, and windows.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: St. Mary's County, Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Housing Authority, St. Mary's County, Maryland for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant-funded transit program that provides evening, Saturday, and Sunday bus service to unemployed and underemployed individuals as part of statewide Welfare-to-Work initiatives in St. Mary's County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides evening and weekend bus service (Saturday and Sunday) for unemployed and underemployed individuals, including reverse commute service. Hours range from 6am to 9pm. Funded by a combination of federal, Transit Administration, St. Mary's County Department of Social Services, and County Commissioner funds, plus passenger fares.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Unemployed and underemployed individuals, particularly those participating in Welfare-to-Work initiatives in St. Mary's County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Transportation to employment, serving California, Great Mills, Lexington Park, Leonardtown, Loveville, Mechanicsville, and Charlotte Hall.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Operates in California, Great Mills, Lexington Park, Leonardtown, Loveville, Mechanicsville, and Charlotte Hall in St. Mary's County.
requirements_list: Must be unemployed or underemployed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: No application process described on this page. Contact STS or the Tri-County Council of Southern Maryland for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: St. Mary's County uses American Rescue Plan funds to extend wired broadband (cable) service to residential and other addresses that currently lack access. The county works with existing cable providers to bring last-mile connections to unserved locations. Eligible participants are identified through a countywide address review, and the county initiates the grant process once participants are confirmed.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding covers the cost of extending wired broadband infrastructure to unserved Last Mile addresses. The county has allocated a total of approximately $6.2 million in American Rescue Plan funds for this effort. Government grant funding offsets capital improvement costs for broadband expansion without assuming maintenance/support costs. Eligible participants are identified by the county and then contacted to initiate the grant process. Addresses beyond maximum BUS Grant distance may be eligible for cost sharing agreements.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents and address holders in St. Mary's County who do not have access to wired broadband service, including students, tele-work, tele-health, and tele-school users.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Extending wired broadband (cable) infrastructure to unserved Last Mile addresses, including broadband cable construction, installation, and plant expansions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Limited to addresses in St. Mary's County, Maryland that are unserved or underserved by wired broadband and return 'Last Mile' status on the Broadband Availability Check.
requirements_list: Address must be located in St. Mary's County
Address must lack access to wired broadband service
Address must be identified as an unserved Last Mile location through the county's review process
Address must qualify as 'Last Mile' on broadband availability mapping
Must register contact information with the county
Must complete and submit Grant Application digitally
Must respond to county communications regarding construction and documentation
Must contact cable provider to establish service after construction completion
Addresses beyond maximum BUS Grant distance may require a cost sharing agreement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Confirm eligibility via the Broadband Availability Check webpage and register contact information. The county will identify eligible participants and initiate the Last Mile Grant Process. Undergo vendor assessment; complete and submit grant application; coordinate construction scheduling; confirm completion; sign up for service with cable provider; payment processed by county. Updates are sent automatically by email as projects progress.

structured_extraction.program_description: L.I.F.E. (Learning Is ForEver) provides educational and enrichment classes, tours, and presentations for adults aged 50 and older. Based on the concept of peer teaching, most instructors are older adults who share their knowledge and experience. Classes are held in spring and fall at various locations in the tri-county area. Volunteers plan and lead trips Monday-Friday, 8 a.m. - 5 p.m. The program also includes a volunteer driver component providing transportation for older adults on educational trips and tours using St. Mary's County Government 15-passenger vans.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Educational and enrichment classes, tours, and presentations offered in spring and fall at minimal cost to participants aged 50 and older. Classes are held at various locations in the tri-county area. Volunteer opportunities include planning and leading educational/enrichment tours or presentations and providing van transportation for older adults on educational trips. AARP Defensive Driving Course registration fees are covered by the department for volunteer drivers.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Candice Nelson, Division Manager, Senior Center Operations

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participation in educational and enrichment learning opportunities; volunteer trip leadership and transportation services
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in St. Mary's County and Southern Maryland area, with trips traveling to Charles County, Calvert County, Prince George's County, Annapolis, Washington DC, Baltimore, and Northern Virginia

Must register with the Department of Aging & Human Services

Volunteers must complete an application, health statement, interview, and orientation. Volunteer driver applicants must also pass a criminal background check, complete AARP Defensive Driving Course, and complete L.I.F.E. Volunteer Driver training.

structured_extraction.program_name: Legal Assistance for Seniors (Maryland Legal Aid)
structured_extraction.program_description: Free legal services for St. Mary's County residents age 60 and over, provided through a contract between the Department of Aging & Human Services and Maryland Legal Aid. Cases cover denial of public benefits, Social Security and SSI overpayments, advance directives, credit problems, landlord/tenant disputes, consumer problems, Medicare, Medicaid, Supplemental Security Income, food stamps, and subsidized housing.

Services are limited to specific case types including public benefits denials, Social Security issues, advance directives, credit problems, landlord/tenant disputes, consumer problems, Medicare, Medicaid, SSI, food stamps, and subsidized housing. Appointments are made by calling (301) 475-4200 ext. 1064.
structured_extraction.program_audience: St. Mary's County residents age 60 and over who need legal assistance with specific civil legal matters.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free legal representation and advice in areas including public benefits, Social Security, advance directives, credit, housing, and consumer issues.

Must be age 60 or older

structured_extraction.program_description: Links pro-bono (no-cost) attorneys with individuals who meet the program's eligibility criteria. Provides free legal representation in areas including adult guardianship, income tax disputes, bankruptcy chapter 7, simple divorce, and estate administration.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free legal representation provided by volunteer attorneys. Service areas include adult guardianship, income tax disputes, bankruptcy chapter 7, simple divorce, and estate administration, among others. No charge to eligible participants.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals who meet the program's eligibility criteria and need pro-bono legal representation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Legal representation in civil matters including guardianship, tax disputes, bankruptcy, divorce, and estate administration.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must meet program's eligibility criteria (specific criteria not listed on this page)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the Maryland Volunteer Lawyer Service website at mvlslaw.org for more information on how to apply.

structured_extraction.program_name: National Family Caregivers Support Program and County In-Home Services Program Respite Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides small, one-time grants to family members caring for an aging relative or a person with a disability. Families use the grant to help pay for a caregiver of their choosing so they can take a short break from caregiving duties.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time grants of an unspecified amount (contingent on available funds) to offset the cost of hiring a private caregiver. Grants are not awarded on a monthly or yearly basis.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Family caregivers caring for an aging family member; seniors caring for a grandchild under age 18; parents caring for an adult child with a disability age 18 or older.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Hiring a caregiver to provide a temporary break (respite) for the family caregiver.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: St. Mary's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be caring for an aging family member, OR be a senior caring for a grandchild under 18, OR be a parent caring for an adult child with a disability age 18 or older
Grant is a one-time-only award
Award amount depends on availability of funds
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the St. Mary's County Department of Aging & Human Services for information on how to apply.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that helps neighborhood residents address speeding, excessive traffic volumes, and safety concerns on local residential streets in St. Mary's County. Residents can apply to have physical traffic calming devices installed, such as speed humps, traffic circles, chokers, and other measures, based on a point system and eligibility criteria.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The county evaluates and installs traffic calming devices on eligible residential streets at county expense, subject to available budget resources. Devices include speed humps (3½ inches high, 22 feet travel length, slows vehicles to 15-20 mph; available as permanent bituminous or portable rubber) and speed bumps (3-6 inches high, 6 inches to 3 feet travel length, slows vehicles to 5 mph or less), as well as traffic circles, roundabouts, chokers, striping, and intersection modifications.
