Residents submit applications and the county conducts traffic studies and designs custom solutions for each location.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Neighborhood residents in St. Mary's County experiencing traffic-related problems such as speeding or excessive traffic volumes on local residential streets.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation and maintenance of traffic calming devices on residential streets, including speed humps, speed bumps, traffic circles, striping, chokers, intersection modifications, and other physical measures.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available on local and neighborhood collector streets within St. Mary's County with a speed limit of 25 mph, at least 750 feet in uninterrupted length, and not a cul-de-sac.
requirements_list: Petition signed by at least 65% of residents on the street in question
At least 55% of average daily traffic (ADT) must exceed the posted speed limit
Street must have a speed limit of 25 mph
Street must be classified as a local or neighborhood collector
Street must not be a cul-de-sac
Installation must not impair safety or drainage
Street must be 750 feet or more in uninterrupted length (excluding intersections)
Street must already have posted speed limit signs
Traffic calming devices must be properly designed, marked, and signed according to MUTCD standards
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Neighborhood residents submit a written application or request to the Department of Public Works & Transportation by June 1 each year. The department reviews the request using a point system based on road classification, traffic volume, speed, accident rate, proximity to schools/playgrounds, pedestrian generators, sidewalk availability, sight distance, and non-local traffic. High-scoring requests proceed to traffic studies, community consultation, and implementation based on available funding.

structured_extraction.program_name: New and Expanding Business (NEXB) Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: St. Mary's County offers property tax credits to new and expanding businesses that create at least ten full-time jobs locally or are new to the county and in targeted industries. Credits are provided on both existing and new structures (real and personal property) for up to ten years, based on the number of jobs created, with a maximum benefit of $100,000. Targeted industries include defense, cyber security, aerospace, manufacturing, agriculture, and aquaculture, among others. The program also supports capital investment through an additional 50% reduction on county property taxes for new capital investment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property tax credits (real and personal) are awarded based on jobs created: 10–15 jobs = $5,000/year for 5 years ($25,000 total); 16–25 jobs = $8,000/year for 8 years ($64,000 total); 26+ jobs = $10,000/year for 10 years ($100,000 total), for a maximum benefit of $100,000. An additional credit equal to a 50% reduction on county property taxes is available for new capital investment. Businesses have three years to reach the 10-job minimum.
structured_extraction.program_audience: New and expanding businesses in St. Mary's County in targeted industries (defense, cyber security, aerospace, manufacturing, agriculture, aquaculture, and others), as well as any business creating at least 10 new full-time jobs in the county, including firms relocating to or expanding existing operations within the county.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credits on real and personal property taxes to offset costs associated with job creation and capital investment in St. Mary's County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to businesses located in or relocating to St. Mary's County, MD. Additional consideration given to businesses in the Lexington Park or Leonardtown Development District and/or the Town of Leonardtown or a town center.
requirements_list: Must create a minimum of 10 new full-time jobs (or full-time equivalents) in St. Mary's County, OR be new to the county and in a targeted industry
Jobs must be new to the county, not relocated from another St. Mary's County location
Business must be in a targeted industry or creating at least 10 local full-time jobs
Businesses have three years to reach the 10-job minimum
Only taxable capital investments are eligible for the capital investment credit
Businesses that export services or products out of the county are targeted
Must be a private venture
Projects with new capital investment receive an additional property tax credit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Submit a completed application (available via the online form or with assistance from the Department of Economic Development). 2. DED reviews the application and the Director recommends applicants for approval. 3. Recommended requests are forwarded to the Commissioners of St. Mary's County. 4. If approved, the applicant signs a contract outlining benefits and obligations. 5. DED presents the signed contract to the Commissioners for final approval. Submitting an application does not guarantee an award.

structured_extraction.program_description: An evidence-based community health program where specially trained nurses regularly visit first-time, low-income mothers starting early in pregnancy and continuing through the child's second birthday. Nurses help mothers have healthy pregnancies, safely care for their children, and build a stable future for their families.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Trained nurses make regular home visits to first-time mothers from early pregnancy through the child's second birthday, providing health guidance, parenting support, and resources.
structured_extraction.program_audience: First-time, low-income mothers-to-be in St. Mary's County
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: St. Mary's County, MD
requirements_list: First-time mothers
Living in poverty

structured_extraction.program_name: Opportunity Zone Investment Program (St. Mary's County)
structured_extraction.program_description: Federal Opportunity Zones (O-Zones) are designated areas that offer special tax benefits to investors who invest capital gains in those zones. Investors in St. Mary's County's Opportunity Zone (centered on the Lexington Park Redevelopment District) can defer, reduce, or eliminate capital gains taxes depending on how long they hold their investment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Three potential tax advantages: (1) Immediate deferral of capital gains tax payments until December 31, 2026. (2) After a 5-year investment, reduce capital gains tax owed by up to 10%; after a 7-year investment, reduce by up to 15%. (3) After a 10-year investment, receive a permanent exemption from capital gains tax on gains accrued after investing in an Opportunity Fund. Eligible investments include single-asset real estate, company stock, and Opportunity Funds (privately managed funds with at least 90% of assets in O-Zones). Investors must invest within 180 days of the capital gain event.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Investors with capital gains looking to invest in real estate, company stock, or opportunity funds in St. Mary's County's designated Opportunity Zone in Lexington Park, MD.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Investment in single-asset real estate, company stock, or Opportunity Funds (O-Funds) located within the St. Mary's County Opportunity Zone.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The Opportunity Zone is located in Lexington Park, St. Mary's County, Maryland, coinciding with the Lexington Park Redevelopment District Master Plan area. St. Mary's County is located on the Southern Maryland peninsula, within a 2-hour drive of Washington D.C., Baltimore, MD, and Richmond, VA.
requirements_list: Investment must be made with funds triggered by a capital gain.
Investor must invest in the O-Zone within 180 days of the capital gain event.
For Opportunity Fund investments, the fund must hold at least 90% of its assets in O-Zones.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the St. Mary's County Department of Economic Development for guidance. Investors typically form an LLC or invest through an Opportunity Fund to participate.

structured_extraction.program_description: St. Mary's County offers a free prescription discount card to help residents save money on prescription medications. Residents can save an average of $21.41 per prescription or about 30% off the retail price. The card is accepted at participating pharmacies and can be used for prescriptions not covered by insurance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free discount card that saves an average of $21.41 per prescription or 30% off the retail price. No enrollment forms, no membership fees, and no limits on frequency of use. Cards are available at all St. Mary's County libraries, Senior Activity Centers, and the Division of Human Services.
structured_extraction.program_audience: St. Mary's County residents who need help covering the cost of prescription medications not covered by insurance
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Discount on prescription medications at participating pharmacies
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of St. Mary's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a St. Mary's County resident
Card is for prescriptions not covered by insurance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: No enrollment is required. Pick up a free card at any St. Mary's County library, Senior Activity Center, or Division of Human Services location. Present the card at a participating pharmacy when filling a prescription.

structured_extraction.program_description: St. Mary's County's Property Tax Challenge encourages investment in commercial real property in designated challenged areas by freezing county property taxes for 7 or 10 years after qualifying renovations, rehabilitation, or upgrades. Commercial property owners who invest at least 10% of the property's assessed value (minimum $25,000) in a single 12-month period are eligible. If taxes would otherwise increase during the incentive period, the owner pays the pre-improvement tax amount instead. The incentive is subject to approval by the Commissioners of St. Mary's County, and if approved, a Developer's Rights and Responsibilities Agreement is prepared and signed by both parties outlining project terms.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: County property taxes are frozen (held constant) for either 7 years (investment of 10%–15% of assessed value) or 10 years (investment of 16% or more of assessed value). The total value of the tax reduction may not exceed 25% of the property's assessed value at the time of award. The minimum investment is $25,000 and must represent at least 10% of the property's assessed value, made within a single 12-month period. The incentive is not guaranteed and is subject to approval by the Commissioners of St. Mary's County. If approved, a Developer's Rights and Responsibilities Agreement is executed.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Commercial property owners in designated challenged areas of St. Mary's County, including the Lexington Park Development District, Charlotte Hall Town Center, and Leonardtown Downtown area, who plan to invest in renovations, rehabilitation, or upgrades to their properties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eligible improvements include renovations, rehabilitation, and upgrades to commercial real property, including exterior façade improvements and painting, structural improvements, building-mounted signage, canopies, shutters, awnings, utility/trash/storage screening, enhanced exterior lighting, streetscape amenities (walkways, landscaping, bike racks), sidewalks, and new construction that enhances the building or property.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be located in a designated challenged area in St. Mary's County, Maryland. The Lexington Park Development District is the primary target area; projects in the Charlotte Hall Town Center and Leonardtown Downtown area will also be considered.
requirements_list: Must own commercial real property in a challenged area of St. Mary's County
Property must be located in the Lexington Park Development District, Charlotte Hall Town Center, or Leonardtown Downtown area
Project must align with the Lexington Park Development District Master Plan and the St. Mary's County Comprehensive Zoning Ordinance
Must invest at least 10% of the property's assessed value
Minimum investment of $25,000
Investment must be a one-time investment occurring within a single 12-month period
Must submit a completed Property Tax Challenge application
Incentive is not guaranteed; subject to approval by the Commissioners of St. Mary's County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a completed Property Tax Challenge application (available online) including business name, property address, contact information, total investment amount, assessed property value, project description, implementation timeline, and economic benefit statement. The application also requires a signed acknowledgment that submission does not guarantee an incentive. If approved by the Commissioners of St. Mary's County, a Developer's Rights and Responsibilities Agreement is executed.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides qualified individual applicants the opportunity to participate in recreation activities (camp and one sport/leisure program) at a prorated amount off the registration fee. Funded through contributions from local civic organizations, net proceeds from the department's Scholarship Fund Golf Tournament, and other special events.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Prorated amount off registration fees for camp and one sport/leisure program; maximum amount per family each calendar year.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Prior to designated deadline each year prior to open camp registration on March 1st
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students ages 5-20 who are St. Mary's County residents; Adults 18+ with MD Independence Card.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Recreation activities including camps and sport/leisure programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be current St. Mary's County residents.
requirements_list: Ages 5-20 OR 18+ with MD Independence Card
Receive Free or Reduced Lunch from SMCPS (or proof of enrollment at Community Eligibility Provision school)
Do not receive Purchase of Care for summer programs or other DSS/County/State funding for summer camp
Current St. Mary's County residence
Submit completed application through CivicPlus with proof of eligibility
Indicate requested weeks of assistance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete scholarship application through CivicPlus with proof of eligibility prior to the designated deadline before open camp registration on March 1st each year.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides housing subsidies to individuals who need help paying rent. Administered locally by the Housing Authority, St. Mary's County, Maryland under the US Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Housing rental subsidies to help individuals cover rental costs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals who need financial assistance with rental housing costs in St. Mary's County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental cost assistance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: St. Mary's County, Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Housing Authority, St. Mary's County, Maryland directly for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: Helps seniors live with dignity in their own homes at lower cost than nursing facility care. Provides comprehensive needs assessment by registered nurse, case management, financial assistance, and access to gap-filling funds to help seniors remain in their homes and communities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Services may include case management, durable medical equipment, emergency response systems, loaned equipment, incontinence supplies, nutritional supplements, financial assistance for prescriptions, home safety modifications, vision and dental care, personal care assistance, and gap-filling monies to enable aging in place rather than nursing facility placement.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Seniors age 65 or older who are current residents of St. Mary's County and are at risk of nursing home placement.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services and equipment to enable aging in place and prevent nursing facility placement, including durable medical equipment, emergency response systems, incontinence supplies, nutritional supplements, and financial assistance for prescriptions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a current resident of St. Mary's County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Age 65 or older
Meet income and asset guidelines
Severely or moderately disabled (per nursing assessment)
Current St. Mary's County resident
At risk of entering nursing facility (per nursing assessment)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Maryland Access Point at (301) 475-4200 ext. 1057 for referral and screening. A Local Health Department nurse then conducts an in-home assessment. The assessment is presented to a team to determine eligibility and develop a care plan.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides older adults aged 60 and up with door-to-door transportation to medical appointments, social engagements, shopping, and other destinations. Volunteer drivers use their personal vehicles to transport eligible riders within and outside St. Mary's County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free or low-cost door-to-door transportation provided by volunteer drivers using their personal vehicles. Fees are charged using a radius method based on the rider's pick-up address. Riders are limited to 4 transportation trips per month. Out-of-county rides are for medical purposes only (to destinations such as Annapolis, Baltimore, and Washington D.C.) and require 5 business days advance notice; in-county rides require 3 business days advance notice.
structured_extraction.program_audience: St. Mary's County residents aged 60 or older, including veterans, who cannot use other public transportation options and lack reliable transportation, with low to moderate income not exceeding $5,216/month for an individual or $7,050/month for a couple.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Transportation to medical appointments, social engagements, shopping, and other destinations. Also supports volunteer drivers through mileage reimbursement, training, and insurance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of St. Mary's County, Maryland. Out-of-county rides are for medical purposes only, serving destinations such as Annapolis, Baltimore, and Washington D.C.
requirements_list: Be 60 years of age or older
Be a St. Mary's County resident
Have a low to moderate income not exceeding $5,216 per month for an individual or $7,050 per month for a couple
Be able to walk using a cane or walker (wheelchairs cannot be accommodated)
Maintain cognitive awareness and ability to maintain independence
Lack access to reasonable, affordable transportation
Use other forms of public transportation when available and appropriate
Complete a Rider Application
Request transportation at least 3 business days in advance for in-county and 5 business days for out-of-county destinations
Sign a release/waiver form
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Rider Application form by phone, in-person, or by mail and sign the Ridership Release/Waiver. Submit to the Department of Aging & Human Services. Once accepted, schedule rides at least 3 business days in advance for in-county trips or 5 business days for out-of-county medical trips. Transportation is subject to driver availability.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that allows property owners to transfer inactive sewer Equivalent Dwelling Units (EDUs) — the measure of sewer capacity allocation — from one property or owner to another within the same wastewater treatment plant service area in St. Mary's County. This enables unused sewer capacity to be reallocated to support new development or redevelopment projects. Participation is voluntary and allows property owners to recover value from inactive EDUs on residential or commercial property.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Allows the transfer of inactive sewer EDUs (Equivalent Dwelling Units — units of sewer capacity) from a Sending Property to a Receiving Property within the same wastewater treatment plant service area. Applicants submit a Notice of Intent to Transfer and an Application to Receive Sewer EDUs. A $20 application fee is required. A 30-day public notice period applies (with exemptions for family/related ownership). Pricing for the EDU transfer is negotiated between parties. A Standard Operating Procedure document (LUGM SOP24-0002) guides the process.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Minimum 30 days after Notice publication before Application to Receive Sewer EDUs can be filed
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners with inactive sewer EDUs (Sending Properties), property owners needing sewer capacity (Receiving Properties), and properties with failing onsite septic systems in St. Mary's County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Transfer of sewer EDU capacity allocations (infrastructure capacity rights) to enable sewerage service connection and support development or redevelopment projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Sending and Receiving Properties must be within the same wastewater treatment plant service area in St. Mary's County, Maryland. Receiving Property must be in the correct sewerage Service Category (S-1 or S-3D) per the Comprehensive Water & Sewerage Plan (CWSP). Properties must be served by MetCom sewer facilities.
requirements_list: Sending Property must have inactive EDUs available
Completion of Notice of Intent to Transfer Sewer EDU(s) form
Publication notice requirement — 30-day waiting period before Application to Receive can be filed (with exemptions for family/related ownership per LUGM SOP24-0002 § 2.1.3.1)
Up to 5 business days for notice publication
Completion of Application to Transfer Sewer EDUs form with signatures from both Sending and Receiving Property owners
Provide property information (address, tax map/parcel, property tax ID, sewer facility name)
Confirmation of sewer facility with MetCom
Submit affidavit under penalties of perjury
$20 application fee payable to Commissioners of St. Mary's County
Must comply with the Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) LUGM SOP24-0002 dated 9-19-2025
Certificate of Transfer form required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Submit Notice of Intent to Transfer Sewer EDUs form to the St. Mary's County Department of Land Use & Growth Management (LUGM). 2. Confirm sewer facility with MetCom at (301) 737-7400. 3. Allow up to 5 business days for notice publication and wait the required 30-day notice period (exemptions may apply). 4. Submit the completed Application to Transfer Sewer EDUs with owner signatures, property details, and affidavit. 5. Pay the $20 application fee payable to the Commissioners of St. Mary's County. 6. Follow the Standard Operating Procedure (LUGM SOP24-0002) for full guidance.

structured_extraction.program_name: Shore Erosion Control Program (St. Mary's County)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides technical and financial assistance to public and private property owners experiencing shore erosion problems. The program funds non-structural (vegetative/living shoreline) projects using sand fill and marsh grasses to create stable shoreline buffers. Structural projects are available for public lands and roads. Property owners form a Special Taxing District to access funding, with future maintenance their responsibility. DNR prepares need and feasibility reports; the county conducts informational meetings; the district assumes responsibility for erosion control project costs through special benefit tax assessments.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 45/55 matching grants for private landowners (property owner pays 45%, program covers 55%) and 75/25 grants for eligible public land protection projects (program covers 75%). Funding covers design, construction, and project management for living shoreline and non-structural erosion control projects. Project costs are financed through annual special benefit assessments levied on properties within the established shore erosion control taxing district.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public and private property owners (including groups and communities of property owners) experiencing shoreline erosion problems in St. Mary's County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Design and construction of living shorelines and vegetative/non-structural shoreline erosion control projects; sand fill, marsh grass planting, and small stone structures to protect shorelines; construction costs for shore erosion control projects
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties within established shore erosion control taxing district boundaries in St. Mary's County, Maryland; properties along the Chesapeake and coastal bays
requirements_list: Submit a Letter of Interest (petition) and an Exhibit showing the boundary of lots to be included in the proposed Shore Erosion Control District
Exhibit must show a bold boundary matching the letter of interest
75% of property owners must return confirming petitions in support of the district
Property owners assume responsibility for annual special benefit assessments following project completion
Structural projects limited to public lands and facilities (e.g., roadways) and private property eligible since 2002
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a Letter of Interest (petition) and an Exhibit indicating district boundaries to initiate the process. DNR prepares a need and feasibility report. The county conducts an informational meeting and issues confirming petitions to owners (75% must confirm support). A public hearing is held to establish the district by ordinance. Complete construction plans are prepared, followed by a second public hearing for final plans. A construction bid process is conducted; an escrow account is established if a cash contribution is required. Construction is awarded. A final public hearing is held to set the annual assessment charge. Contact DNR's Shoreline Conservation Section or the Department of Public Works for guidance. Refer to the Procedures for Establishing a Shore Erosion Control Taxing District document.

structured_extraction.program_description: Allows landowners in St. Mary's County to establish a Special Drainage District to fund the correction and improvement of recurring drainage problems in subdivisions and neighborhoods. Costs are assessed equitably across all benefited properties over time, and the County may maintain the system with ongoing maintenance costs allocated to the district.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Design, construction, and interest costs are assessed to all benefited properties over a period not to exceed 15 years. The County may maintain the system and allocate ongoing maintenance costs to the district as a perpetual annual assessment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners in St. Mary's County subdivisions and neighborhoods with recurring drainage problems
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Design and construction of storm drainage improvements to correct or improve recurring drainage problems
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: St. Mary's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Petition with signatures of more than 50% of property owners within the proposed drainage district must be submitted
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a petition signed by more than 50% of property owners within the proposed drainage district. Contact the Department of Public Works & Transportation at (301) 475-4200 for procedures.

structured_extraction.program_description: Mechanism to upgrade substandard subdivision roads and make them suitable for acceptance into the County Highway Maintenance System. Established in 1976 with legislative authority from the Maryland General Assembly, the program addresses roads constructed prior to January 1, 1977. The County borrows the funds for construction, and the benefited lot owners repay the principal and interest over time through special tax assessments.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The County finances road improvements and property owners repay through special tax assessments over an amortization period not to exceed 20 years. The County covers administrative, preliminary engineering, and inspection costs, as well as additional costs to meet current standards beyond original subdivision approval standards. Property owners cover design engineering, construction, and utility costs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners in residential subdivisions with substandard roads in St. Mary's County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Road construction and improvement, design engineering, utility costs, and street/drainage system upgrades to meet County Highway Maintenance System standards
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Substandard subdivision roads in St. Mary's County that connect to existing streets or roads in the County Highway Maintenance System or maintained by the State
requirements_list: Roads must have been constructed prior to January 1, 1977
Roads must connect to an existing street or road in the County Highway Maintenance System or a State-maintained road
Requires a petition from two-thirds (2/3) of benefited lot owners
Process includes public informational meeting, ordinance preparation, public hearing, budget request, construction, and acceptance phases
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Department of Public Works and Transportation at (301) 475-4200 or refer to the Special Taxing District Procedures document. Submit a petition signed by two-thirds of benefited lot owners to begin the process of establishing a Special Road Taxing District.

structured_extraction.program_name: St. Mary's County Agricultural Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit available to landowners in St. Mary's County who participate in agricultural preservation districts, helping to keep farmland in active agricultural use.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A tax credit for landowners in agricultural preservation districts in St. Mary's County. Applicants must complete and submit the Agricultural Tax Credit Agreement Form and Application.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners in St. Mary's County with agricultural preservation districts
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax relief for agricultural landowners participating in preservation districts
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: St. Mary's County, Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and submit the St. Mary's County Agricultural Tax Credit Agreement Form and the Agricultural Preservation District Tax Credit Application.

structured_extraction.program_name: St. Mary's County FIRE/EMS Scholarship Program Year 2025-2026 (SMC FY2026)
structured_extraction.program_description: A scholarship program for individuals interested in fire and EMS (emergency medical services) careers in St. Mary's County. Applicants submit an application to the Department of Emergency Services for consideration.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Scholarship funding for individuals pursuing fire and EMS training or education. Specific award amounts are not stated on the page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals interested in fire and EMS careers in St. Mary's County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Fire and EMS education or training
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: St. Mary's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Application must be received on or before August 31, 2025
Submit application to St. Mary's County Emergency Services, Attention: Angel Clem, PO Box 653, Leonardtown, MD 20650-0653
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download the application form and mail it to St. Mary's County Emergency Services, Attention: Angel Clem, Post Office Box 653, Leonardtown, MD 20650-0653. Applications must be received by August 31, 2025.

structured_extraction.program_name: St. Mary's County Façade and Streetscape Improvement Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program reimburses commercial property and business owners for costs to rehabilitate their buildings, storefronts, and adjacent streetscapes in the historic commercial core of Lexington Park and Charlotte Hall. It aims to improve the visual appearance of commercial areas, stimulate private investment, and support community revitalization in designated grant areas. Applicants receive 50% reimbursement of eligible project costs, up to $6,000 per address per calendar year, with applications ranked using a points-based scoring system.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimburses up to 50% of eligible project costs, with a maximum reimbursement of $6,000 per address per calendar year. There is no minimum award, though projects must provide meaningful improvement. Funding covers cleaning and repair of building exteriors, masonry, paint, replacement of deteriorated windows/doors/siding/framing visible from the public right-of-way, and restoration of exteriors within the designated grant area. Applications are ranked using a points-based scoring system.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-residential property owners and business owners (tenants with written authorization from property owner) located within the Façade and Streetscape Grant Area in Lexington Park or Charlotte Hall, St. Mary's County. Eligible for existing structures legally used for commercial, mixed-use, industrial, or office uses, and vacant structures zoned in those districts.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rehabilitation of commercial building exteriors, storefronts, and adjacent streetscapes, including: cleaning and repair of building exteriors, cleaning/re-pointing of brick and masonry, exterior paint or like finishes, replacement of deteriorated or damaged windows, doors, siding, and framing visible from the public right-of-way, and restoration of exteriors.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties must be located within the designated Façade and Streetscape Grant Area in Lexington Park (Downtown and Great Mills Corridor per the Lexington Park Master Plan) or the Charlotte Hall footprint of the Sustainable Communities designation.
requirements_list: Property must be located within the Façade and Streetscape Grant Area
Proposed work must align with eligible reimbursement projects per Program Guidelines
Cost estimates must be obtained from licensed and insured contractors
Business owner/tenant applicants must have written property/building owner authorization
Limited to one application per address per calendar year
Application must be complete and accurate
Must be a non-residential property owner or business owner/tenant in Lexington Park or Charlotte Hall
Eligible structures must be used for commercial, mixed-use, industrial, or office uses, or be vacant and zoned in those districts
Must complete a project that rehabilitates buildings, storefronts, and/or adjacent streetscapes
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Confirm the property is in the grant area. 2. Verify the proposed work matches eligible projects in the Program Guidelines. 3. Obtain cost estimates from licensed and insured contractors. 4. Identify the reimbursement amount requested (50% of project cost, max $6,000). 5. Gather all required documents. 6. Submit the online application via the provided HubSpot form. Note: the application cannot be saved and resumed, so have all documents ready before starting.

structured_extraction.program_name: St. Mary's County Senior Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides a property tax credit on the primary dwelling of qualifying senior citizens with limited income in St. Mary's County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A property tax credit on the qualifying senior's dwelling. Applicants must be age 70 or older as of July 1 of the tax year in which they apply and have a household taxable net income of $80,000 or less.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Senior citizens age 70 or older with limited income who own property in St. Mary's County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of property tax bill on primary dwelling
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: St. Mary's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a senior citizen age 70 or older as of July 1 of the tax year
Must have a household taxable net income of $80,000 or less
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are available at all senior activity centers in St. Mary's County.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state-funded paratransit transportation program that provides door-to-door and curb-to-curb, demand-responsive transit services to elderly residents and persons with disabilities in St. Mary's County who do not have sufficient access to public transportation routes or ADA paratransit. The program provides general-purpose transportation on a first-come, first-served basis, with preference given to individuals with scheduled medical appointments. Planned demand routes operate in rural areas on rotating schedules to maximize coverage. Riders are transported to medical appointments, senior nutrition centers, shopping, employment, and other destinations within designated service zones.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides subsidized curb-to-curb or door-to-door transportation services using wheelchair accessible vehicles, buses, and county cars. The fare is $6.00 round trip (or $3.00 one-way) per ride within St. Mary's County, with exact change required at time of pickup. An additional $3.00 charge applies for each additional stop. No-shows are charged $6.00 if the bus arrives at the home. Between $130,000 and $175,000 in annual state grant funding supports the program, with a required local match. Service is available between 10:00 AM and 2:00 PM (appointments scheduled between 10:00 AM and 1:00 PM) on a first-come, first-served basis, providing approximately 17,000 trips per year. Planned demand routes run in rural areas on rotating days (Monday through Friday) to increase coverage. ADA Paratransit fares are $4.00 round trip; discount fares on public transportation are $0.50 one-way or $0.75 with transfer.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Elderly residents (senior citizens) and persons with disabilities in St. Mary's County, particularly those not sufficiently close to public transportation routes or ADA paratransit, including those in rural areas who can plan their transportation in advance.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Transportation to medical appointments, senior nutrition centers, shopping centers, employment sites, businesses, personal errands, and other destinations within designated service zones throughout St. Mary's County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Service is available in five zones covering communities throughout St. Mary's County, including Charlotte Hall, Leonardtown, California, Lexington Park, Ridge, Great Mills, Callaway, Piney Point, Tall Timbers, St. Inigoes, Mechanicsville, Golden Beach, Hollywood, Breton Bay, Compton, Chaptico, Wicomico Shores, Wildewood, Oakville, and Avenue. Each zone is served on specific days of the week (Monday through Friday). Available to all qualifying residents of St. Mary's County.
requirements_list: Must be elderly (senior citizen) or a person with a disability
Must not have sufficient access to public transportation routes or ADA paratransit
Must complete a paratransit application to qualify
Must pay $3.00 one-way or $6.00 round trip at time of pickup (exact change required)
Must be ready at scheduled pickup time
Must return at designated time
Seniors must present proof of age to receive discount fares
Appointments must be scheduled in advance (up to 30 days)
Appointments should be scheduled between 10:00 a.m. and 1:00 p.m.
First-come, first-served basis; preference given to those with scheduled medical appointments
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete a paratransit application to establish eligibility. Call (301) 475-4200 ext. 1120 or 1121 (or 301-863-8400 ext. 1120) to discuss eligibility and schedule rides up to 30 days in advance. Riders can also obtain identification cards from the STS Transit office at 44829 St. Andrews Church Road, California, MD 20619. Confirm pick-up times by calling in the morning of the scheduled ride. Riders may also contact the office by email at SDispatchers@stmaryscountymd.gov. Refer to the SSTAP Rider's Guide for detailed information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Street Lighting Special Taxing District Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Allows property owners in St. Mary's County subdivisions and neighborhoods to establish a Special Taxing District to fund the installation and ongoing maintenance of street lights. Only those properties that benefit from the service pay the associated costs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Installation and energy costs for street lights are paid only by benefiting property owners through a special tax district assessment. Costs are distributed equitably among benefited property owners.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners in St. Mary's County subdivisions and neighborhoods that want street lighting installed
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation and ongoing energy and maintenance costs for street lighting in subdivisions and neighborhoods
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: St. Mary's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Petition from at least 60% of property owners must be received by the Department of Public Works
Established homeowners associations are encouraged to contract directly with SMECO at (301) 475-5631
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a petition signed by at least 60% of property owners in the area to the Department of Public Works. Contact the Department for current installation costs and monthly charges.

structured_extraction.program_name: The Boys & Girls Club of Southern Maryland – Lexington Park
structured_extraction.program_description: An afterschool program in Lexington Park that helps children excel academically, socially, and emotionally. Trained staff work with children daily, and nationally recognized programs such as Positive Action, Smart Girls, and Passport to Manhood are offered to help students make good decisions and live healthy lifestyles.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Daily afterschool programming from 2–6pm (with extended hours on early-dismissal days) providing academic help, social-emotional learning, and health and wellness programming.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Children in Lexington Park, St. Mary's County
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Lexington Park, St. Mary's County, MD

structured_extraction.program_name: The Patuxent Partnership Youth Workforce Readiness Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A nonprofit initiative committed to enhancing career awareness and workforce readiness for young people and their parents in the Great Mills area. The program provides career exposure, security clearance education, durable skills training, and hands-on work experience to prepare students for high-demand careers, especially in Navy and Department of Defense industries.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Career exposure, security clearance education, durable skills training, and hands-on work experience for students and their parents in the Great Mills area.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Young people and their parents in the Great Mills area of St. Mary's County
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Great Mills area, St. Mary's County, MD

structured_extraction.program_name: Volunteer Fire & EMS Recruitment and Retention Incentives
structured_extraction.program_description: St. Mary's County offers incentives to encourage residents to volunteer at local fire departments and rescue squads. The program is a partnership between St. Mary's County Volunteer Fire & Rescue Services, St. Mary's County Board of Education, and Maryland Fire and Rescue Institute (MFRI). Benefits include free firefighter and EMT training (including Firefighter 1 & 2, Vehicle Machinery and Extrication, Hazardous Materials Operations, Rescue Technician Site Operations, and EMT courses), college scholarships, a length of service award, dependent care reimbursement, and a Maryland State tax incentive after three years of service. High school juniors and seniors may earn Firefighter and EMT state and national certifications through a one-year program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Volunteers receive free certified firefighter or EMT training (Firefighter 1 & 2, Vehicle Machinery and Extrication, Hazardous Materials Operations, Rescue Technician Site Operations, and EMT/Paramedic courses), college scholarships, a length of service award program, dependent care reimbursement, community service credit hours for students, and a Maryland State income tax deduction after completing minimum service requirements.
structured_extraction.program_audience: St. Mary's County residents interested in volunteering at local fire departments or rescue squads, including high school juniors and seniors seeking certifications, and those seeking non-emergency administrative or fundraising roles.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: College scholarships, length of service awards, dependent care reimbursement, free training and certifications, and Maryland State tax incentives for volunteer service.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to volunteers serving at fire departments and rescue squads in St. Mary's County, Maryland. The county has six fire departments, six rescue squads, one combination fire department/rescue squad, and one advanced life support unit.
requirements_list: Must volunteer at a St. Mary's County fire department or rescue squad
Maryland State tax incentive requires at least three years of service
College scholarship and length of service award programs have minimum service requirements
High school juniors and seniors are eligible for the one-year training/certification program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Emergency Services Recruitment & Retention Coordinator at 301-475-4200 ext. 2114 or FireEMSRecruitment@stmaryscountymd.gov for more information on joining.

structured_extraction.program_description: State of Maryland program for marking channels and harbors, clearing waterway debris, dredging channels, constructing jetties and marine facilities beneficial to the boating public. Projects are funded through the Maryland Waterway Improvement Fund and managed through a Special Taxing District (Waterway Improvement District). The State may finance projects completely or partially through interest-free long-term loans or 50/50 matching grants. Governed by Natural Resources Article, Section 8-707 of the Annotated Code of Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The State may fund waterway improvement projects completely or partially. 100% grants are available for projects that significantly benefit the general boating public (e.g., harbors of refuge, anchorage, water access, fueling/repair facilities). 50/50 matching grants are available when general boating public benefit is limited. Interest-free long-term loans are also available, with repayment terms not to exceed 25 years or the estimated service life of the improvement (whichever is less). The County repays through a special assessment district. Maximum State allocation is $25,000 per year per project. The County handles engineering, bid documents, and construction inspection. Property owners are responsible for identifying spoil sites for dredging projects.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners with waterway problems or concerns, including real property owners abutting natural or artificial bodies of water within St. Mary's County, and public and private waterway property owners and communities seeking waterway improvements
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Marking channels and harbors, clearing debris from waterways, dredging channels, constructing jetties and marine facilities, engineering, design, permitting, construction services, project management, and future maintenance and improvements
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: St. Mary's County, Maryland; specifically real property abutting natural or artificial bodies of water within St. Mary's County
requirements_list: 75% of property owners must submit a Letter of Interest indicating proposed district boundaries
Preparation of a Need and Feasibility Report by the Department of Natural Resources
Identification of dredge material placement sites (for dredging projects)
75% of benefiting property owners must submit a formal Petition with project details and assessment method
Benefit value must equal or exceed assessment costs
Ordinance establishment by County Commissioners
Full project funding approval in County budget required
Annual assessment payment as county taxes
Project must meet eligibility criteria under Natural Resources Article Section 8-707
Maximum State funding is $25,000 per year per project
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: A 20-step process beginning with a Letter of Interest signed by at least 75% of benefited property owners to initiate a formal DNR Need and Feasibility review, followed by petition submission, ordinance establishment by County Commissioners, budget approval, and post-construction maintenance responsibility. Refer to the Special Taxing District Policy and Procedures documents available online or from the Department of Public Works.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides qualified individual applicants the opportunity to participate in recreation activities (camp and one sport/leisure program) at a prorated amount off the registration fee. Scholarships are funded through contributions from local civic organizations, net proceeds from the department's Scholarship Fund Golf Tournament, and other special events.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Prorated discount off registration fees for camp and one sport/leisure recreation program; maximum amount per family each calendar year.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Prior to designated deadline each year prior to open camp registration on March 1st
structured_extraction.program_audience: Youth ages 5-20 who are students, and adults 18 years or older, who are St. Mary's County residents seeking financial assistance to participate in youth and adult sports and recreation programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Summer camps and one sport/leisure recreation program offered by St. Mary's County Recreation & Parks.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Current St. Mary's County, Maryland residents only.
requirements_list: Must be a current St. Mary's County resident
Students ages 5-20 receiving Free or Reduced lunch from SMCPS OR adults 18+ with MD Independence Card
No Purchase of Care assistance for summer programs
Submit completed scholarship request through CivicPlus
Provide proof of eligibility (Free/Reduced Lunch Approval Form, proof of enrollment, or Independence Card)
Indicate which weeks assistance is requested (if applicable)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete scholarship application through CivicPlus online registration platform and provide required proof of eligibility documentation.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program offers a property tax credit. It encourages new and existing businesses to move to or expand in state-designated enterprise zones. These zones are in economically distressed areas.
structured_extraction.agency: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a property tax credit to eligible businesses.
structured_extraction.program_audience: New and existing businesses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The business must be located in a state-designated enterprise zone.

structured_extraction.program_description: Talbot County provides Alcohol Awareness Training classes to help employees involved in the sale of alcoholic beverages meet the state-required training requirement. Employees must complete the training within 180 days of their hire date. Training covers either on-sale (bars, restaurants, hotels) or off-sale (liquor stores, distilleries) alcohol sales.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: In-person classroom training sessions for employees who sell alcohol. On-sale license training is approximately 4 hours and costs $35 per person. Off-sale license training is approximately 3 hours and costs $35 per person. Upon passing the exam, participants receive a certification.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Employees involved in the sale of alcoholic beverages at licensed establishments in Talbot County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Satisfying the state-required alcohol awareness training certification for alcohol sales employees
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Talbot County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be an employee involved in the sale of alcoholic beverages
Must complete training within 180 days of date of hire
Must pre-register for class
Must take an approved course online but test must be proctored (in person); fully online certification is not allowed in Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Pre-register online at the Talbot County JotForm registration link, or email Nickole Whitmer at NWhitmer@talbotcountymd.gov with your requested class date, legal name, email, phone number, and employer/business name. A confirmation email with class time, location, and payment requirements will be sent.

structured_extraction.program_name: Bay Restoration Fund (BRF) Program - Talbot County
structured_extraction.program_description: A state-supported grant program locally administered by Talbot County that provides funding to replace conventional septic tanks with nitrogen-reducing Best Available Technology (BAT) units, or to connect existing dwellings to public sewer where available. The goal is to reduce harmful nutrients like nitrogen that septic systems discharge into the Chesapeake Bay and its tributaries. Funding levels vary by income and property ownership type, and priority is given to failing systems within the Chesapeake Bay Critical Area.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant covers the cost and installation of a BAT septic system plus a two-year Operations and Maintenance (O&M) package. Funding levels vary by income: up to 100% of BAT unit cost for households with income under $300,000; 50% for households over $300,000; 50% for business-owned properties (up to 75% for small businesses); 100% for non-profits (tank only). Low-income applicants may also receive funding for non-BAT components like drain fields. New construction projects have a $1,200 deductible. Applicants are prioritized by failing systems in the Chesapeake Bay Critical Area first.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners in Talbot County with conventional septic systems, including individuals, businesses, and non-profits seeking to upgrade to nitrogen-reducing BAT septic systems or connect to public sewer.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and installation of a BAT nitrogen-reducing septic unit, two-year O&M package, and for low-income applicants, repair or replacement of non-BAT components such as drain fields. Also funds sewer connections for existing dwellings where public sewer is available.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to property owners in Talbot County, Maryland. Priority given to properties within the Chesapeake Bay Critical Area (land within 1,000 feet of tidal waters).
requirements_list: Must be an existing dwelling or new construction in Talbot County
Public sewer must be available at the property (for sewer connection funding)
Must obtain a SB554 Letter of Determination from the Office of Environmental Health (OEH)
Must obtain an approved Sanitary Construction Permit from OEH
Must submit a completed application including a signed Public Works Agreement (PWA) notarized by all property owners listed on the deed
Must provide current year Federal Tax Return (1040 Form) for all property owners (income under $300,000 qualifies for up to 100% funding; over $300,000 qualifies for 50%)
Non-profits must submit federal income tax form 990 as verification
Low-income applicants must provide IRS verification transcript or non-filing status letter for 100% funding
Low-income applicants must submit three contractor bids for non-BAT components; lowest bid is awarded
New construction owners are responsible for a $1,200 deductible from the grant amount
A Three-Way Agreement signed by BAT unit vendor, property owner, and septic contractor is required
If any property owner listed on the deed is deceased, a copy of the death certificate is required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a complete application package to the Talbot County Department of Public Works including: a notarized Public Works Agreement signed by all property owners, current Federal Tax Return, SB554 Letter of Determination from OEH, approved Sanitary Construction Permit, and a Three-Way Agreement. Applicants are placed on a funding list upon receipt of complete documentation. For low-income applicants, three contractor bids must be submitted and DPW awards the contract to the lowest bidder with MDE approval. Contact the Talbot County Public Works Department for more information.
attachment_urls: https://www.talbotcountymd.gov/departments/publicworks/resources-4/uploads/File/publicworks/Bay%20Restoration Fund/OSDS BRF BAT Funding Summary FY2026.pdf

structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) program provides federal funds, administered through Maryland's Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) and distributed by Talbot County, to support community development projects. In Talbot County, funds have supported renovation and construction projects for non-profits, food pantries, shelters, and community service organizations serving low- and moderate-income residents. The program supports public facilities, housing, infrastructure, economic development, and public services with a 24-month implementation period for funded activities.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal block grant funds distributed by Talbot County to eligible subrecipients for construction, renovation, services, staffing, food supplies, equipment, and facility improvements. Recent awards have ranged up to $150,000 per subrecipient (e.g., $75,000 each for two food pantries) and larger construction grants for building renovation projects. Funding is provided on a first come, first serve basis for special projects. Projects include site acquisition, construction, professional services, environmental review, permitting, elevator/lift installation, and project administration. Letters of interest are currently being sought for State Fiscal Year 2027 (SFY2027).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Letters of Interest for SFY2027 — deadline not stated
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations and government entities serving low- and moderate-income residents of Talbot County, including homeless individuals and families, persons with disabilities, and communities experiencing slum/blight
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction, renovation, rehabilitation, services, staffing, food supplies, equipment, and facility improvements for community-serving organizations; site acquisition; professional services (engineering, planning); environmental review; permitting and bidding costs; project administration staffing and expenses; elevator/lift installation; accessibility improvements such as wheelchair lifts
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Talbot County, Maryland. Projects outside special flood hazard areas preferred; projects not in 100-year floodplain or regulatory floodway preferred.
requirements_list: Applicants must serve low- and moderate-income persons
Projects must comply with HUD requirements including Davis-Bacon wage rules, Section 3, and BABA (Build America Buy America) certification
Subrecipients must be able to meet grant expenditure deadlines
Environmental review mandatory as first step after award
Public hearing and notice requirements must be satisfied before application submission
Citizen participation plan required
Fair housing and equal opportunity compliance
Americans with Disabilities Act compliance
Applicant responsible for completion of grant activities and corrective actions
Applicant may be required to repay funds if necessary
Davis-Bacon prevailing wage and fringe benefit payments required for construction
Weekly certified payrolls must be submitted
Records must be maintained for 3 years after project completion
Davis-Bacon poster (WH-1321) must be posted at job site
Equal employment opportunity compliance (Executive Order 11246)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a Letter of Interest to Talbot County Grants Administrator. County Manager is authorized to execute required documents for application submission. Environmental review is the mandatory first step after award. More information is available through the Maryland DHCD CDBG program page. Questions can be directed to Mary Kay Verdery at the Talbot County Courthouse.

structured_extraction.program_name: FY 2025 Opioid Restitution Fund Community Micro Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides one-time micro grants to non-profit organizations to fund initiatives that address opioid use, prevention, and treatment in Talbot County, Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time grants ranging from $1,000 to $20,000, to be used by June 30, 2026.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Portal for this round of funding has now closed.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations with active 501(c)3 status and in good financial standing seeking funding to address opioid use, prevention, and treatment in Talbot County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: School education campaigns to prevent opioid use; evidence-based overdose prevention and substance use treatment; crisis response systems, safe stations, and stabilization centers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Talbot County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a non-profit organization with active 501(c)3 status
Must be in good financial standing

Must submit a formal letter of interest identifying the amount requested, justification and beneficiaries, scope of work, how funds will address identified objectives, and how grant success will be quantified
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a formal letter of interest through the application portal. The portal for this round of funding has closed.

structured_extraction.program_name: Talbot County Community Repair and Reinvestment Fund (CRRF)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grant funding to community-based organizations that benefit disproportionately impacted and low-income communities in Talbot County. Grounded in a restorative justice approach to public investment, the fund directs cannabis tax revenue into community-based initiatives addressing harms from disparate cannabis law enforcement, strengthening community well-being, expanding service access, building community capacity, and enabling sustainable change. It is supported by revenue from Maryland's adult-use cannabis tax and overseen by the Maryland Office of Social Equity.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funds awarded through two pathways: Pathway 1 - Small Community Grants ($10,000 or less; $50,000 total available); Pathway 2 - Community Impact Grants (minimum $25,000; $150,000 total available). Grant period runs 5/1/26 – 6/30/27. Applicants must review the Notice of Funding Opportunity and submit a signed application and budget form electronically. The inaugural funding round opened January 27, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community-based organizations, nonprofits, and for-profit organizations serving disproportionately impacted and low-income communities in Talbot County, particularly those in the 21601 zip code area (Easton). Funding is not awarded to individuals.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Community-based services and supports including reentry, legal, and stabilization supports; economic opportunity and workforce development initiatives; and programs addressing harms from disparate cannabis law enforcement and related social and economic disparities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Talbot County, Maryland. The disproportionately impacted area identified by the Maryland Office of Social Equity for Talbot County is zip code 21601 (Easton). Funding may be awarded elsewhere in Talbot County when work demonstrates addressing similar harms.
requirements_list: Applicants must serve disproportionately impacted and/or low-income communities in Talbot County
Must select one grant pathway: Small Community Grant or Community Impact Grant
Projects must align with the purposes of the Community Repair and Reinvestment Fund
Must describe community focus, lived experience involvement, and outcomes
Must demonstrate data collection capacity (or willingness to develop it), including disaggregation by race and ethnicity
Must address disproportionately impacted and/or low-income communities
Must include collaboration details if applicable
Must track participation data including race and ethnicity
Must describe program/strategy with key activities and timeline
Must explain how work helps improve conditions CRRF is intended to address
Must describe organizational readiness and capacity to carry out work
Must describe sustainability beyond grant period (if applicable)
Must provide signature and date from Authorized Official
Must review the Notice of Funding Opportunity before applying
Must submit signed application and completed budget form electronically using the submission link in the NOFO
Funding not awarded to individuals
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review the Notice of Funding Opportunity, then complete and submit a signed application form and budget form electronically using the submission link provided in the NOFO. A pre-application meeting was held on February 10, 2026 (slide deck and recording available). Contact Nancy Andrew at director@talbotfamilynetwork.org for additional information.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Appalachian Regional Commission (ARC) program merges local, state, and federal funds to support economic and social development projects in the Appalachian region of Western Maryland. The program focuses on job-creating infrastructure improvements and economic development for the six-county area, helping package multiple funding sources for single projects.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: ARC combines local, state, and federal funds to support infrastructure and economic development projects in Western Maryland. Funding is competitive due to reduced federal and state resources.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, businesses, and organizations in the six-county Western Maryland Appalachian region seeking funding for infrastructure and economic development projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Municipal infrastructure improvements and economic development projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in the six-county Appalachian region of Western Maryland served by the Tri-County Council for Western Maryland.
requirements_list: Project must be located in the Appalachian region of Western Maryland
Funding is competitive and subject to availability
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Tri-County Council for Western Maryland for guidance on applying. Planning documents and ARC-specific forms and guidelines are available on the organization's website.

structured_extraction.program_description: The EDA program helps economically distressed rural and urban communities generate jobs, retain existing jobs, and stimulate industrial and commercial growth. It builds local capacity through strategic investment planning to help communities plan for new technologies, job creation, and enterprise development. The Tri-County Council for Western Maryland (TCCWMD) administers EDA assistance in the Western Maryland region. The Comprehensive Economic Development Strategy (CEDS) 2023-2027 serves as the regional planning document, identifying three priority areas: Economic Development, Workforce Development and Training, and Infrastructure, with five investment goals: Building Appalachian Businesses, Building Appalachia's Workforce Ecosystem, Building Appalachia's Infrastructure, Building Regional Culture and Tourism, and Building Community Leaders and Capacity.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: EDA provides strategic investments in physical, financial, and human capital to distressed communities. Assistance includes Revolving Loan Funds (through Summit Financing Solutions for new and expanding businesses), grant programs, tax incentive programs (including Biotechnology Investment Incentive, Brownfields Tax Incentive, Cybersecurity Investment Incentive, Enterprise Zone, Job Creation Tax Credit, More Jobs for Marylanders-Manufacturing Tax Credit, One Maryland program, RISE Zone Program, Research & Development incentives), technical assistance, GIS assistance, business coaching, workforce training and development, broadband infrastructure development, infrastructure improvements (water, wastewater, roads, bridges), education coordination, and regional strategic planning. Specific funding amounts and terms vary by program component.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Economically distressed rural and urban communities experiencing high unemployment, low income, or other severe economic distress in Western Maryland, including existing and expanding businesses, startup businesses, job seekers, workforce participants, students, educational institutions, local governments, veterans, displaced workers, and community organizations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Infrastructure improvements (broadband, water, wastewater, roads, bridges), local capital market development, strategic planning, job creation and retention, workforce development and training, entrepreneurship and business support, tourism marketing and development, historic and cultural preservation, downtown revitalization, education program development, broadband expansion, and economic recovery and resilience planning.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to economically distressed rural and urban areas in Western Maryland (Allegany, Garrett, and Washington counties), encompassing twenty-four municipalities across the three-county Appalachian Maryland region.
requirements_list: Must be located in an economically distressed area experiencing high unemployment, low income, or other severe economic distress
Must be in the Tri-County Western Maryland region (Allegany, Garrett, or Washington County)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Tri-County Council for Western Maryland for information on applying for EDA assistance. Application forms may be available at https://www.tccwmd.org/apply-online/forms-and-applications/.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program uses funds from video lottery terminals to provide loans to small, minority-owned, and women-owned businesses. It helps these businesses with financing for various needs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers loans from $10,000 to $1,000,000. Interest rates are set at the Prime Rate plus 1%. Loan terms can be up to 5 years for working capital and up to 15 years for fixed assets like property or equipment.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: State Lottery Terminal (SLoT) Fund applications accepted on a continual basis.
structured_extraction.program_audience: This program is for small, minority-owned, and women-owned businesses in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used for business acquisition and expansion, owner-occupied commercial real estate, lease-hold improvements, equipment purchases, start-up costs, working capital, professional and technical assistance, and, in some cases, refinancing existing debt.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is available to businesses throughout Maryland. Businesses in Garrett, Allegany, and Washington counties are in the primary target area.
requirements_list: A business plan is required.
A personal credit score of 650 is generally required, though lower scores may be considered.
Personal guarantees are required from all owners with 20% or more interest in the business.
A minimum equity injection of 10% is generally required for start-up businesses.
A non-refundable application fee of $250 is required, or $25 for loans between $10,000 and $25,000.
Approved borrowers must pay a 1% loan origination fee at closing.
Collateral is required and may include deeds of trust, liens on machinery and equipment, personal guarantees, and key person life insurance.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To apply, first complete and submit an inquiry form available on the program website. Applications are reviewed using standard underwriting practices, which consider repayment capacity, financial strength, industry experience, and collateral.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Western Maryland Revolving Loan Fund (RLF) provides gap financing loans to small businesses and organizations looking to locate or expand in Garrett, Allegany, and Washington counties in Maryland. The program participates alongside banks and other lenders to help finance business projects that create or save jobs. Money repaid by borrowers is recycled back into the fund to make new loans, creating an ongoing source of financing for job creation and retention in the Appalachian region. Loans range from $10,000 to $500,000 with interest rates tied to the prime rate (currently prime plus 1% with a floor of 5%), and maximum terms of 5 years for working capital and up to 15 years for fixed assets.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Gap financing loans ranging from $10,000 to $500,000. Interest rates are tied to the prime rate, currently prime plus 1% with a floor of 5%. Maximum terms are 5 years for working capital and up to 15 years for fixed assets. A $250 non-refundable application fee applies (or $25 for loans between $10,000–$25,000). Approved borrowers pay a 1.5% loan origination fee at closing (no origination fee for loans $10,000–$25,000). The project must create or retain at least one job for every $30,000 of RLF funds requested. Collateral required includes Deeds of Trust, machinery and equipment liens, personal guaranties, and key man life insurance. Loan proceeds are repaid and returned to the fund to make additional loans.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Revolving Loan Fund loan applications accepted on a continual basis.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Ms. Chris Funk, Business Development Loan Officer, Tri County Council for Western Maryland
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit corporations, non-profit organizations, partnerships, or sole proprietorships located in Garrett, Allegany, or Washington County in western Maryland seeking to start, expand, or relocate a business and create or retain jobs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business acquisition, commercial real estate acquisition, building improvements, equipment purchase, leasehold improvements, business start-up costs, and working capital. Not eligible for real estate speculation, projects that do not create or retain permanent jobs, or projects that qualify for traditional financing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Western Maryland region — Garrett, Allegany, and Washington counties in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a for-profit corporation, non-profit organization, partnership, or sole proprietorship
Must be located or expanding in Garrett, Allegany, or Washington County
Project must create or retain at least one job for every $30,000 of RLF funds requested
Standard underwriting applies: repayment capacity, financial strength, industry/management experience, and collateral
Collateral required: Deeds of Trust, machinery/equipment liens, personal guaranties, key man life insurance
Non-refundable application fee of $250 (or $25 for loans $10,000–$25,000)
A 1.5% loan origination fee is charged at closing (waived for loans between $10,000–$25,000)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete the Western Maryland Revolving Loan Fund (RLF) Inquiry Form and Application from the Tri-County Council for Western Maryland forms and applications page (https://www.tccwmd.org/apply-online/forms-and-applications), then submit to Tri-County Council for Western Maryland (Summit Financing Solutions). A $250 non-refundable application fee (or $25 for loans $10,000–$25,000) is required for loan processing. Applications are accepted on a continual basis.

structured_extraction.program_name: Senator George C. Edwards Fund (Western Maryland Economic Future Investment Board)
structured_extraction.program_description: A regional economic development fund established in 2022, also known as the Western Maryland Economic Future Investment Board, to drive economic growth in Western Maryland. The fund supports qualifying economic development projects — including capital infrastructure and business development — that create significant job opportunities or increase the local tax base in Allegany, Garrett, and Washington counties.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers grants and loans for two types of projects: infrastructure and business development. The minimum award amount is typically $150,000, but the board may consider smaller projects on a case-by-case basis.
