Infrastructure uses can include broadband connectivity, road access improvements, utility connections, property purchases, and building construction.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses, non-profits, or local governments with qualifying economic development projects that will have a major economic impact in Western Maryland, particularly in Allegany, Garrett, or Washington County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support capital infrastructure and business development. Infrastructure uses can include broadband connectivity, road access improvements, utility connections, property purchases, and building construction. Business development projects must create new jobs or significantly increase the local tax base.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in Allegany, Garrett, or Washington County in Western Maryland.
requirements_list: Project must qualify under the fund's economic development criteria
Projects must create new jobs that pay at least 120% of the State Minimum Wage.
Infrastructure projects require a minimum 20% match from the local government, the business, or another approved source.
Business development projects require a minimum 10% match from the local government, the business, or another approved source.
Projects must create significant jobs or provide a significant increase to the tax base.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To apply, first make an inquiry to the Executive Director, a Member of the Board, or the Economic Development Director in the county where the project is located. You may also contact the Allegany Works team for help determining if your project qualifies and for assistance applying.

structured_extraction.program_name: Economic Injury Disaster Loans (EIDLs) for Francis Scott Key Bridge Collapse
structured_extraction.program_description: The U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) offers low-interest, long-term Economic Injury Disaster Loans (EIDLs) of up to $2 million to small businesses, small agricultural cooperatives, aquaculture businesses, and most private nonprofits in Maryland and the broader mid-Atlantic region affected by the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse on March 26, 2024, and the resulting Port of Baltimore closure. The loans help cover working capital needs and ongoing operating expenses—including payroll, accounts payable, fixed debts, and other bills—during the disaster recovery period that could have been met if not for the disaster. Business Recovery Centers were established in Baltimore City (CareFirst Engagement Center, 1501 S Clinton St), Baltimore County (Community College of Baltimore County-Dundalk / Dundalk Renaissance Center), and Anne Arundel County (Arundel Christian Church, 710 Aquahart Rd, Glen Burnie) to assist applicants in person, staffed by SBA customer service representatives and representatives from federal, state, and county agencies. Centers were open Monday to Friday 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. and Saturdays 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. The application deadline was December 30, 2024.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest, long-term Economic Injury Disaster Loans of up to $2 million to help eligible small businesses, small agricultural cooperatives, aquaculture businesses, and most private nonprofits overcome temporary loss of revenue and meet financial obligations during the disaster recovery period caused by the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse and Port of Baltimore closure. Funds may be used for normal operating expenses such as payroll, accounts payable, fixed debts, and other bills. Interest rates are fixed at 3.25% for non-profits and 4% for businesses, with loan terms up to 30 years and a 12-month deferment on payments and interest from first disbursement. Loans up to $25,000 are unsecured. In-person Business Recovery Centers with SBA customer service representatives were available in Baltimore City (CareFirst Engagement Center, 1501 S Clinton St), Baltimore County (Community College of Baltimore County-Dundalk / Dundalk Renaissance Center), and Anne Arundel County (Arundel Christian Church, 710 Aquahart Rd, Glen Burnie). Contact SBA at (800) 659-2955 for details on interest rates and loan terms.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses, small agricultural cooperatives, aquaculture businesses, most private nonprofit organizations, and impacted workers in Maryland and the mid-Atlantic region that suffered economic injury due to the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse and Port of Baltimore closure on and after March 26, 2024.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Working capital needs caused by the disaster, including financial obligations and ongoing operating expenses such as payroll, accounts payable, fixed debts, and other bills during the disaster recovery period that could have been met if not for the bridge collapse and Port of Baltimore closure.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland and surrounding Mid-Atlantic states affected by the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse (Disaster Declaration #20258; Maryland Disaster Number MD-20001). Eligible Maryland counties include all 24 jurisdictions. Contiguous eligible counties also include Delaware (Kent, New Castle, Sussex), Pennsylvania (Adams, Bedford, Chester, Fayette, Franklin, Fulton, Lancaster, Somerset, York), Virginia (Accomack, Alexandria, Arlington, Fairfax, Loudoun), West Virginia (Berkeley, Grant, Hampshire, Jefferson, Mineral, Morgan, Preston), and the District of Columbia. Business Recovery Centers serving applicants in person were located in Baltimore City (CareFirst Engagement Center, 1501 S Clinton St), Baltimore County (Dundalk Renaissance Center / CCBC), and Anne Arundel County (Arundel Christian Church, 710 Aquahart Rd, Glen Burnie).
requirements_list: Must be a small business, small agricultural cooperative, aquaculture business, or private nonprofit organization
Must have suffered economic injury as a result of the Francis Scott Key Bridge Collapse on March 26, 2024 and/or the Port of Baltimore closure
Must demonstrate economic injury (temporary loss of revenue)
Eligibility is based on the financial impact of the disaster only
Maryland Governor Wes Moore disaster declaration enables eligibility
Application deadline was December 30, 2024
Business must have been impacted by the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse
Must visit a Business Recovery Center in person or apply online at sba.gov/disaster
Must complete a Disaster Loan application
Cell phone, email address, and contact information required for all applicants
Social Security numbers and EINs required for all applicants/owners
Financial information required (income, account balances, monthly expenses)
Complete copy of most recent Federal income tax return required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at sba.gov/disaster or through the SBA disaster loan portal at lending.sba.gov. Call SBA's Customer Service Center at (800) 659-2955 or email disastercustomerservice@sba.gov for assistance. In-person Business Recovery Centers were available in Baltimore City (CareFirst Engagement Center, 1501 S Clinton St), Baltimore County (Community College of Baltimore County-Dundalk / Dundalk Renaissance Center), and Anne Arundel County (Arundel Christian Church, 710 Aquahart Rd, Glen Burnie). Centers were open Monday to Friday 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. and Saturdays 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. Application deadline was December 30, 2024.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Historically Underutilized Business Zones (HUBZone) Program, run by the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA), certifies small businesses located in designated underutilized areas for preferential treatment when competing for federal government contracts. It helps small businesses in urban and rural communities gain preferential access to federal government contracting opportunities, including set-aside contracts, sole source awards, and a 10% price evaluation preference in full and open competitions. The federal government targets 3% of all prime contract dollars to HUBZone businesses; in Fiscal Year 2022, HUBZone contracting was valued at $16.3 billion government-wide. In Maryland, areas including all of Garrett County and portions of Hagerstown and Washington County have been designated as HUBZones, meaning eligible businesses there can qualify for these federal contracting preferences.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Certified HUBZone businesses receive preferential status in federal contracting, including: set-aside awards, sole source awards, a 10% price evaluation preference (PEP) in full and open competitions, and subcontracting opportunities. The federal government targets 3% of all prime contract dollars to HUBZone businesses; in Fiscal Year 2022, HUBZone contracting was valued at $16.3 billion government-wide.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses located in HUBZone-designated areas, including all of Garrett County and designated areas in and around Hagerstown, Maryland, that are at least 51% owned and controlled by U.S. citizens or qualifying entities and meet SBA size standards.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Federal contracting preferences — businesses use the certification to compete for federal contracts and subcontracts on preferential terms, including set-aside awards, sole source awards, and a 10% price evaluation preference.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All of Garrett County, Maryland is designated as a HUBZone. Designated HUBZone areas also exist in and around Hagerstown in Washington County. At least 35% of the business's employees must also reside in a HUBZone area.
requirements_list: Be a small business as defined by SBA Size Standards
Have principal office located in a HUBZone
At least 35% of employees must reside in a HUBZone

Be at least 51% owned and controlled by U.S. citizens, a Community Development Corporation, an agricultural cooperative, an Alaska Native corporation, a Native Hawaiian organization, or an Indian tribe
Must be certified by the SBA before participating
Must recertify annually
Program examination required at least every three years
Must notify SBA of mergers, acquisitions, or if HUBZone employee residency drops below 20% while performing on a HUBZone contract
Must be located in a designated HUBZone area
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply for HUBZone certification through the SBA at sba.gov. The SBA offers a tip sheet outlining the steps to get certified. An eligibility workbook tool is available to help applicants organize and present information about their principal office and employee residency; uploading this workbook with the application can speed up SBA's review. The SBA determines eligibility, maintains a listing of qualified HUBZone businesses, and adjudicates eligibility protests. After certification, businesses must recertify annually.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal loan program administered by the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) providing forgivable loans to help small businesses keep their workforce employed during the COVID-19 crisis. The SBA recommends applying through approved online lenders (FinTechs) that do not require prior customer or account status, making it easier to access funding. Borrowers can set the loan covered period between 8 and 24 weeks, with loans covering payroll, operations, property damage, supplier costs, and worker protection expenditures. Forgiveness is available through the SBA direct forgiveness portal or through the borrower's lender.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Forgivable SBA-backed loans available through approved lenders including FinTechs (Funding Circle, OnDeck, Kabbage, LoanBuilder, BlueVine, Lendistry, and Lendio) as well as traditional participating PPP lenders. Borrowers can set the loan covered period between 8 and 24 weeks. Loans cover payroll, operations, property damage, supplier costs, and worker protection expenditures. Borrowers can apply for forgiveness through the SBA direct forgiveness portal or through their lender.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses, nonprofits, sole proprietors, independent contractors, and self-employed individuals, including those who have been unable to access PPP through traditional lenders due to prior customer or account requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payroll, operations, property damage, supplier costs, and worker protection expenditures.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Nationwide
requirements_list: Must be a small business, nonprofit, sole proprietor, independent contractor, or self-employed individual
Eligible entities include 501(c)(6)s, housing cooperatives, and direct marketing organizations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download the First Draw or Second Draw PPP Loan Application from the SBA and work with a participating PPP lender through the SBA Lender Match tool, or apply through one of the SBA-approved FinTech lenders (Funding Circle, OnDeck, Kabbage, LoanBuilder, BlueVine, Lendistry, or Lendio), which do not require prior customer or account status. Apply for forgiveness through the SBA direct forgiveness portal if your lender participates, or through your lender directly.

structured_extraction.program_name: SBA COVID-19 Economic Injury Disaster Loan (EIDL) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal disaster loan program administered by the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) providing low-interest loans to small businesses and private nonprofits that suffered financial losses due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Loans help cover working capital and operating expenses including health care benefits, rent, utilities, fixed debt payments, payroll, and accounts payable. Loans are available at 3.75% interest for small businesses and 2.75% for nonprofits, with repayment terms up to 30 years and an automatic one-year deferment before repayment begins.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest federal disaster loans available at 3.75% for small businesses and 2.75% for nonprofits. Loan limits cover up to 24 months of economic injury with a maximum of $500,000. Repayment terms up to 30 years with an automatic one-year deferment before repayment begins. Collateral required for loans over $25,000.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted through December 2021, pending availability of funds
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses and private nonprofit organizations impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic, available nationwide including all Maryland counties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Working capital and operating expenses including health care benefits, rent, utilities, fixed debt payments, payroll, and accounts payable.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available nationwide, including all counties in Maryland following the state's official SBA disaster designation.
requirements_list: Must be a small business or private non-profit organization
Must have suffered significant economic injury due to COVID-19
Collateral required for loans over $25,000
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply directly to the SBA online at www.sba.gov/funding-programs/loans/coronavirus-relief-options/economic-injury-disaster-loans.

structured_extraction.program_description: The U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) offers low-interest disaster loans to small businesses, non-profits, and other eligible entities affected by declared disasters. This program provides step-by-step guidance for registering and applying for disaster assistance through the SBA's Disaster Loan Application Portal. Businesses can apply online after a disaster declaration is approved. Funding is described as being in the billions, with an anticipated turnaround time of 21 days for small business applications.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest economic injury disaster loans provided by the SBA to help small businesses, non-profits, and other eligible entities recover from declared disasters. Eligible business types include sole proprietorships, corporations, partnerships, limited partnerships, trusts, LLCs, and private non-profit organizations. Funding is described as being in the billions, with an anticipated turnaround time of 21 days for small business applications.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses, non-profit organizations, and other eligible entities (including sole proprietorships, home-based businesses, self-employed individuals, and rental property owners) experiencing economic injury from declared disasters
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Disaster recovery and economic injury relief for small businesses following a disaster declaration
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to businesses located in areas covered by individual disaster declarations. Applicants must select the state and county where the loss occurred and identify the corresponding disaster declaration during the application process.
requirements_list: Must be a small business, non-profit, or other eligible entity (sole proprietorship, corporation, partnership, LLC, trust, etc.)
Disaster declaration must be approved prior to applying
Must be located in a declared disaster area
SBA Form 5 or Form 5C (depending on business type)
Tax Authorization Form 4506-T (for 20% owners, general partners, 50% affiliates)
Most recent business tax return
Personal Financial Statement (Form 413) for 20% owners and general partners
Schedule of Liabilities (SBA Form 2202)
Monthly Sales information (SBA Form 1368)
Statement of Loss
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online through the SBA Disaster Loan Application Portal (DLAP) at disasterloan.sba.gov after the disaster declaration is approved. Applicants select the state and county where the loss occurred and the corresponding disaster declaration. A step-by-step guide is available as a PDF download.

structured_extraction.program_name: SBA Physical Damage and Economic Injury Disaster Loans — Maryland Severe Flooding (May 2018)
structured_extraction.program_description: The U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) offers low-interest disaster loans to businesses, nonprofits, homeowners, and renters in declared Maryland counties who suffered physical damage or economic losses from the severe flooding events in May 2018. Loans can be used to repair or replace damaged real estate, equipment, inventory, and personal property. Economic Injury Disaster Loans (working capital loans) are also available for businesses that did not suffer physical damage but experienced economic losses, including businesses in Howard County affected by the May 15–20, 2018 flooding.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Businesses and nonprofits can borrow up to $2 million to repair or replace disaster-damaged real estate, machinery, equipment, and inventory, or for working capital (Economic Injury Disaster Loans). Homeowners can borrow up to $200,000 to repair or replace damaged real estate. Homeowners and renters can borrow up to $40,000 to repair or replace damaged personal property including automobiles. Interest rates are as low as 3.61% for businesses, 2.5% for nonprofits, and 1.938% for homeowners and renters, with terms up to 30 years. Applicants may also be eligible for a loan increase of up to 20% of physical damages for mitigation improvements such as storm shelters. Working capital loans are also available to businesses in Howard County affected by the May 15–20, 2018 flooding to help recover from economic losses.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Sept. 24, 2018 for physical property damage; April 25, 2019 for economic injury
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses of all sizes, private nonprofit organizations, homeowners, and renters in declared disaster counties in Maryland who experienced damage or economic losses from the May 2018 severe flooding events, including Howard County businesses affected by the May 15–20, 2018 flooding.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Repair or replace disaster-damaged real estate, machinery, equipment, inventory, personal property (including automobiles), or working capital needs. Mitigation improvements such as safe rooms or storm shelters are also eligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City and Howard counties, and the adjacent counties of Anne Arundel, Baltimore County, Carroll, Frederick, Montgomery, and Prince George's in Maryland. Howard County businesses affected by the May 15–20, 2018 flooding are also eligible for working capital loans.
requirements_list: Located in a declared disaster county in Maryland
Sustained damage or economic loss caused by the severe flooding in May 2018
Businesses, nonprofits, homeowners, or renters as applicable
Economic Injury Disaster Loans available even if no physical damage occurred
Business must have been affected by the May 15–20, 2018 flooding in Howard County (for working capital loans)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online through the Electronic Loan Application (ELA) at DisasterLoan.sba.gov. Applications can also be downloaded at www.sba.gov and mailed or returned to a recovery center. Call the SBA Customer Service Center at 800-659-2955 (or 800-877-8339 for deaf/hard-of-hearing) or email disastercustomerservice@sba.gov for assistance.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Technology Internship Program (MTIP) helps Maryland keep top technology talent in the state by increasing the number of paid technical internships. Administered by UMBC and funded by the State of Maryland, the program offers financial assistance to technology-based businesses and state and local agencies to hire more interns.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance to technology-based businesses and state and local government agencies to hire paid technical interns.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Technology-based businesses and state and local government agencies in Maryland looking to hire technical interns.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding paid technical internships at technology-based businesses and government agencies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a technology-based business or state/local government agency
Must use funds to hire paid technical interns
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact UMBC's Maryland Technology Internship Program or attend the Queen Anne's County Workforce Development Showcase for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A paid internship program that matches University of Baltimore students with community-based organizations in Baltimore to gain hands-on community development experience while supporting neighborhood improvement efforts. Interns work 10–20 hours per week for 15 weeks and may earn academic credit.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Interns earn $15.00 per hour, working 10–20 hours per week over a 15-week semester. Funding comes from sources including BGE, Wells Fargo, Whiting-Turner, and UB alumni. Interns may also earn academic course credit with approval from their program director.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Current juniors, seniors, or graduate students at the University of Baltimore with a strong interest in community development and creating positive change in urban areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Paid student internships working on community outreach, special events, grant writing, economic development, and other community development projects at Baltimore-based host organizations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Baltimore City only. Interns are matched with community-based organizations operating in Baltimore neighborhoods.
requirements_list: Must be a current junior, senior, or graduate student at the University of Baltimore
Must be in good academic standing (3.0 GPA or better)
Must be enrolled at least part-time (6 credits per semester for graduate students; 9 credits per semester for undergraduates)
Must be available to work a minimum of 10 hours per week at the host organization
Must have a strong interest in community development and creating positive change in urban areas
Must have community development experience and/or knowledge of Baltimore's neighborhoods
Must be able to work independently and take initiative
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Students apply online through the program's application form. Applicants go through an interview process to be matched with a community-based host organization. Host sites also apply separately to participate as partners.

structured_extraction.program_description: A fellowship program for graduate students at Maryland institutions with master's degree programs in public policy or a related field. Fellows gain hands-on experience in the legislative process by working alongside nonpartisan staff in the Department of Legislative Services (DLS) during the Maryland General Assembly's annual 90-day session (January through April).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Fellows work alongside nonpartisan staff in the Maryland Department of Legislative Services for a 90-day legislative session, gaining immersive, hands-on experience in the state legislative process.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Graduate students enrolled in master's degree programs in public policy or related fields at Maryland institutions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participation in Maryland General Assembly legislative session activities through the Department of Legislative Services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Open to graduate students at Maryland institutions that offer master's degrees in public policy or a related field.
requirements_list: Must be a graduate student at a Maryland institution
Must be enrolled in a master's degree program in public policy or a related field
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit http://dls.maryland.gov/careers/legislative-fellows to learn more and apply.

structured_extraction.program_name: NextGen Leaders for Public Service Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A University of Baltimore initiative that prepares students from any major to explore careers in public service through paid internships at state, county, and local government agencies and nonprofits in Maryland. Interns work 10–20 hours per week, earn $15 per hour, and can earn academic credit. Internships generally last 15 weeks.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Paid internships at $15 per hour for 10–20 hours per week over approximately 15 weeks. Interns may also earn academic credit with prior approval from their internship coordinator. Students can also earn a NextGen Leadership credential and digital badges upon completing a set of program activities.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications for the 2026 Summer Term are now OPEN
structured_extraction.program_audience: University of Baltimore undergraduate and graduate students from any major interested in careers in government and nonprofit public service
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Paid internship experience in Maryland state, local, or municipal government agencies or nonprofit organizations
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Internship host sites are located in Maryland state, local, and municipal government agencies, Maryland nonprofits, and Baltimore community development organizations
requirements_list: Must be an enrolled University of Baltimore student (undergraduate or graduate)
Apply and designate top choices for interviewing with host sites
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Students apply online through the NextGen Leaders application form, designate their top host site choices, and interview with selected host sites.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Rosencrantz Local Government Fellowship places University of Baltimore College of Public Affairs students into paid fellowship positions in Maryland counties and municipalities. Fellows work 10-15 hours per week during fall, spring, or summer semesters, assisting local government offices with special projects, research, social media, administrative work, and community outreach. The program gives students real-world experience in local government while supplementing their coursework.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Paid fellowship positions for students placed in Maryland local government offices. Fellows work 10-15 hours per week and may receive academic credit if approved as an internship. Specific pay rates and amounts are not stated on the page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: University of Baltimore College of Public Affairs students from the Schools of Public and International Affairs, Criminal Justice, or Health and Human Services (undergraduate and graduate programs).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Paid work for students placed in Maryland county and municipal government offices, including work on special events, social media, administrative tasks, research, and community outreach.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Maryland counties and municipalities that partner with the University of Baltimore College of Public Affairs.
requirements_list: Must be a student at the University of Baltimore College of Public Affairs
Applicants predominantly come from the Schools of Public and International Affairs, Criminal Justice, or Health and Human Services
Represents one of 14 undergraduate or graduate programs
Fellows work 10-15 hours per week balanced with coursework
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The position description is negotiated with the site sponsor (local government partner) and advertised as a call for student applicants. Students apply through the College program; positions may be approved as internships for academic credit.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Schaefer Center offers a limited number of fellowships for full-time University of Baltimore graduate students. Fellows work 20 hours per week at the Center while attending graduate school full-time, assisting with research projects, data collection and analysis, training programs, and strategic planning activities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Fellows receive full tuition remission up to 9 credit hours per semester and a $6,000 per semester stipend for Master's level students, or 6 credit hours of tuition remission and an $8,000 per semester stipend for Doctoral students. Awards are generally made on an academic year basis, with the opportunity to continue working at the Center during the summer.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: November 15th for Spring 2026; April 15th for Fall 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Full-time University of Baltimore graduate students (Master's or Doctoral level) interested in public policy research, program evaluation, or related areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition remission and living stipend to support graduate education while working at the Schaefer Center.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be enrolled or planning to enroll at the University of Baltimore.
requirements_list: Enrolled or planning to enroll at the University of Baltimore with at least 9 credits per semester (Master's) or 6 credits per semester (Doctoral)
Minimum undergraduate or graduate GPA of 3.0
Experience with math/statistical software (e.g., Excel, SPSS, R) or data analysis and reporting tools (e.g., NVivo, PowerBI, Qualtrics)
Experience or interest in public policy research, program evaluation, survey research, strategic planning, or other policy-related areas
Must work all fellowship hours on-campus during standard business hours
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a completed application via Qualtrics online form, along with a professional resume, two letters of recommendation, unofficial transcripts, and a 3–5 page essay. Applications are screened for completeness, then reviewed by staff; top applicants are invited for virtual or in-person interviews. Fellowships are awarded competitively based on GPA, work experience, educational goals, research interests, references, and fit with the Center's work.

structured_extraction.program_description: A University of Maryland program that promotes development and commercialization of products and processes through industry-university research partnerships. Provides matching funds to help Maryland companies pay for university research initiated by the companies to meet their own R&D goals, covering projects in engineering, computer science, physical sciences, life sciences, and industrial training programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Matching funds awarded on a competitive basis: up to $100,000 per year for large and small companies, and up to $90,000 per year for start-up firms. Funds are used to support university research partnerships based on joint proposals submitted by Maryland companies and researchers from University System of Maryland institutions. Projects are initiated by companies to meet their own R&D and commercialization goals.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland companies seeking to commercialize products and processes through research partnerships with the University of Maryland and University System of Maryland institutions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: University research costs related to company R&D and commercialization goals, including projects in engineering, computer science, physical sciences, life sciences, and industrial training programs for employees.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Maryland company; research conducted at University System of Maryland institutions.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland company
Project must be initiated by the company
Proposal must be submitted jointly with a University System of Maryland researcher
Research must be in engineering, computer science, physical sciences, life sciences, or related to industrial training programs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Companies and university researchers submit joint proposals on a competitive basis through the MIPS website at the University of Maryland (https://mips.umd.edu/).

structured_extraction.program_description: The Upper Shore Regional Council (USRC) Business Mentoring Program connects small business owners and aspiring entrepreneurs in Cecil, Kent, and Queen Anne's Counties with free, volunteer business mentors. Experienced volunteer mentors have professional experience across many fields and provide free, confidential, personalized one-on-one guidance and coaching tailored to the business owner's unique goals, whether they are just starting out or looking to grow. Services include help with business planning, financial planning, marketing plan development, identifying funding and financing sources, preparing financial documents, registering a business, licensing and permits, marketing and sales, customer relations, ongoing operations, and long-range planning. All services are free and confidential.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free and confidential one-on-one business mentoring provided by experienced volunteer professionals with experience across many fields. Services include guidance on business planning, financial planning, marketing plan development, identifying funding and financing sources, preparing financial documents, registering a business, licensing and permits, marketing and sales, customer relations, ongoing operations, and long-range planning. There is no cost to participants.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Aspiring entrepreneurs, new business owners, and existing small business owners who own or want to start a small business in Cecil, Kent, or Queen Anne's Counties in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Technical assistance and mentoring — not a cash grant or loan program. Program provides free mentoring and coaching services to help with business planning, finance, marketing, licensing, and ongoing operations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to small business owners and aspiring entrepreneurs located in Cecil, Kent, or Queen Anne's Counties, Maryland (Upper Shore region).
requirements_list: Must own or want to start a small business in Cecil, Kent, or Queen Anne's County
Must complete the Business Mentor Request Form
Must sign a Mentee Agreement with the Upper Shore Regional Council outlining terms and conditions of the service
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Business Mentor Request Form by clicking the 'Request a Business Mentor' button on the program page. The USRC team will review your request, match you with an appropriate mentor, and send you a Mentee Agreement to sign. Once the agreement is received and a mentor is assigned, the USRC team will connect you with your mentor.

structured_extraction.program_name: Upper Shore Workforce Investment Board Incumbent Worker Training Fund (IWT)
structured_extraction.program_description: This program helps businesses in Kent and Queen Anne's counties pay for training for their current (non-contractual) employees. The training should help workers improve their skills, get new career opportunities, or earn higher wages. All training must result in a credential confirming completion. Training expenses are covered up to a maximum of $5,000 per company, with a targeted rate of $1,500 per individual (negotiable).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program reimburses businesses for training costs. A company can receive a maximum of $5,000. The program targets a training cost of $1,500 per person, but this amount is negotiable. Eligible training types include classroom training for new skills and certifications, on-the-job training, in-house training programs, and training from outside providers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses in Kent and Queen Anne's counties that want to train their current (non-contractual) employees.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used to pay for different types of training, including classroom training for new skills and certifications, on-the-job training, in-house training programs, and training from outside providers. All training must result in a credential confirming completion.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is available to businesses located in Kent and Queen Anne's counties, Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicants must be businesses located in Kent or Queen Anne's County
Applicants must have a plan to train current, non-contractual employees
Employees being trained must not be contractual employees
All trainings must result in a credential confirming completion
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To apply, download and complete the application form available via the program flier or application PDF. For more information, contact Debbie Bowden at envistrallc@gmail.com.

structured_extraction.program_description: A business accelerator program launched in 2017 that helps underinvested, growth-stage small business owners build resilience and grow their businesses. It provides financial and management training, mentorship, networking, and access to affordable loan capital through an eight-week workshop series combined with small group and individualized support.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free eight-week virtual workshop series covering financial and management training, marketing, risk mitigation, and business performance. Participants receive an individualized growth plan, access to WACIF small business advisers, a capstone presentation opportunity, and eligibility for WACIF grant and debt (loan) capital. Twelve months of continued accountability and engagement opportunities are included after graduation. Up to 15 businesses are accepted per cohort.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications are now open for the 2026 cohort
structured_extraction.program_audience: Growth-stage small business owners in Washington D.C., Prince George's County (MD), Montgomery County (MD), Howard County (MD), Arlington County (VA), or Alexandria (VA) whose businesses have operated for at least two years and generate at least $50,000 in annual revenue.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business growth, financial management, marketing, customer relationship building, risk mitigation, and business performance improvement. Grant and loan capital may be accessed after program completion.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The principal office of the business must be in Washington, D.C., Prince George's County (MD), Montgomery County (MD), Howard County (MD), Arlington County (VA), or Alexandria (VA).
requirements_list: Business must have operated for at least two years
Business must generate at least $50,000 in annual sales
Business must have an operational website
Business must be registered and in good standing
Business owner must be running the business full-time
Owner must be available for virtual workshops on Tuesdays from 10:00 am to 1:30 pm EST
Commit up to 10 hours per week for workshops, research, and assignments
Attend all training sessions (absences limited to one session)
Create a 12-month growth plan
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application through the online application form (HubSpot form linked on the page). Applications are reviewed holistically based on overall business strength, financial sustainability, growth potential, expressed challenges, and potential to increase revenue and profitability. All applicants are notified before the program start date if they are accepted. An information session is also available to register for via Eventbrite.

structured_extraction.program_description: Certified Up helps small businesses grow through expert-led certification training and hands-on technical assistance. The program offers workshops, bootcamps, expert consultations, and personalized support to help businesses obtain key certifications and use them to win public and private contracts.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides HIVE Workshops hosted at the Anacostia Arts Center (AAC) covering certification types and requirements, intensive Certification Bootcamps to prepare for certification applications and compliance, Expert Open Hours (1–2 hour drop-in sessions for one-on-one consultations), and group Technical Assistance sessions with coaches and instructors to navigate certification processes.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small business owners, particularly those operating in the D.C. region and businesses at The HIVE, who are seeking to obtain or better leverage business certifications to access local, state, and federal contract opportunities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable — program provides training and technical assistance rather than funds.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses operating throughout the D.C. region.
requirements_list: Must be a small business
Must operate in the D.C. region
Owner seeking to expand through public and/or private contract opportunities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Participants can attend events; see the WACIF events page for upcoming workshops and sessions.

structured_extraction.program_description: Loan program supporting small businesses making sustainable upgrades or operating in an environmentally responsible way, with an added bonus grant component.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loan for sustainable business upgrades or green operations, paired with a bonus grant component.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses seeking to grow sustainably or make green upgrades.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Sustainable upgrades or green business operations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Serves the Washington, DC metropolitan region.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Share business info and financial needs, check eligibility (no credit score required to prequalify), then complete the application with support from the WACIF team.

structured_extraction.program_description: OWI empowers entrepreneurs in the Greater Washington DC region by providing equitable access to capital, education, and professional business networks. It offers small business loans, grants, technical assistance, one-on-one advisory and coaching, workshops and training on capital readiness and leadership, networking events, and referrals to coworking space.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: OWI provides small business loans, grants, and technical assistance. It also offers one-on-one advisory coaching with access to legal, marketing, certification, and financial experts, plus group training workshops and referrals to coworking space at the Anacostia Arts Center's HIVE.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Women entrepreneurs and small business owners in the Greater Washington DC region
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital access, business development, training, and professional networking
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Greater Washington DC region
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Speak with an advisor by visiting the WACIF website to become a client.

structured_extraction.program_description: Loan program providing capital to small businesses navigating recovery or seeking long-term growth and stability, with an added bonus grant component.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loan for businesses in recovery or pursuing growth and stability, paired with a bonus grant component.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses needing to strengthen operations, recover from setbacks, or build long-term stability.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business recovery, resilience, or growth activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Serves the Washington, DC metropolitan region.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Share business info and financial needs, check eligibility (no credit score required to prequalify), then complete the application with support from the WACIF team.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program through the Washington Area Community Investment Fund (WACIF) that allows organizations or individuals to become Growth Partners, supporting economic development in the Washington DC area.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Growth Partners partner with WACIF to support community investment and economic development. Specific assistance terms and amounts are not detailed on this page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations and individuals interested in partnering with WACIF to support economic development in the Washington DC area.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington DC metro area, including Maryland counties of Montgomery and Prince George's.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the online application form on the WACIF Growth Partners Application page.

structured_extraction.program_name: WACIF Small Business Lending and Advising (Small Business Loan Program)
structured_extraction.program_description: WACIF (Washington Area Community Investment Fund) provides flexible loans and personalized small business advising to low- and moderate-income entrepreneurs and small businesses in underserved communities in the Washington, DC metro area, including Montgomery and Prince George's counties in Maryland and select Northern Virginia jurisdictions. Businesses can apply for loans to fund working capital, equipment purchases, renovations, and other business needs. WACIF takes a flexible, character-based approach to lending, including for applicants with limited or poor credit. Clients receive both financial capital (loans) and knowledge and technical support from in-house small business advisors.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: WACIF offers flexible business loans for purposes such as working capital, equipment purchases, and renovations. Loan size is not specified; a personal guarantee and business assets as collateral may be required depending on loan size. In addition to financial capital, clients receive personalized support and local expertise from in-house small business advisors.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low- and moderate-income entrepreneurs and small businesses located in DC, Montgomery or Prince George's County MD, or select Northern Virginia jurisdictions (Arlington County, Alexandria, Fairfax County, or City of Fairfax) that have been operating for at least one full year and generated at least $50,000 in revenue in the last fiscal year.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Working capital, equipment purchases, renovations, and other stated business purposes as determined through consultation with a small business advisor.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Business must be located in DC, Montgomery or Prince George's County (MD), or Arlington County, Alexandria, Fairfax County, or City of Fairfax (VA).
requirements_list: Must be a low- or moderate-income entrepreneur or small business owner located in the Washington, DC metro area
Business must be located in DC, Montgomery or Prince George's County MD, or select Northern Virginia areas (Arlington County, Alexandria, Fairfax County, or City of Fairfax)
Business must have been operating for at least one full year
Business must have generated at least $50,000 in revenue in the last fiscal year

Must provide business and personal tax returns (last 2 years), business bank statements, interim Profit & Loss Statement and Balance Sheet, personal financial statement, articles of incorporation and business licenses, and quotes/invoices for project costs if applicable
Must consent to a soft credit check
Must be willing to provide a personal guarantee and business assets as collateral depending on loan size
Must have a clear purpose and estimated amount for the loan
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the online prequalification self-assessment on the WACIF website to check loan readiness. If ready, start the loan application via the online application form. Applicants can also complete an intake form to connect with a small business advisor for one-on-one support or technical assistance; the advisor will contact you to discuss your needs and develop goals for your consultation.

structured_extraction.program_description: Flexible term loans for small business owners to access capital for growth, operations, inventory, working capital, or equipment purchases. Loans range from $10,000 to $250,000 with competitive interest rates, no minimum credit score requirement, and no prepayment penalties. Available to businesses in the Washington, DC metropolitan region including Montgomery County and Prince George's County in Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Term loans from $10,000 to $250,000 with competitive interest rates, no minimum credit score requirement, and no prepayment penalties. Funds can be used for equipment purchases, inventory, working capital, and day-to-day business operations. Loan amounts can be less than $75,000 or $75,000 or greater, with documentation requirements varying accordingly.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small business owners located in the DC metro area including Montgomery County and Prince George's County in Maryland, the District of Columbia, and select Virginia jurisdictions who have been in business at least 1 year with at least $50,000 in annual revenue. Minority-owned, women-owned, and certified businesses preferred.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Equipment purchases, inventory, working capital (day-to-day cash flow needs), and business operations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must be located in DC, Montgomery County MD, Prince George's County MD, Arlington County VA, City of Alexandria VA, Fairfax County VA, or City of Fairfax VA. Serves the broader Washington, DC metropolitan region (DMV region).
requirements_list: Business must be located in DC, Montgomery County MD, Prince George's County MD, Arlington County VA, City of Alexandria VA, Fairfax County VA, or City of Fairfax VA
Business owner must be a U.S. citizen, legal permanent resident, or have a valid work visa
Must have filed federal income taxes for the most recent filing deadline (business and/or personal) or have filed an extension
Business must have a business bank account
Must have been in business for a minimum of 1 year
Must have had business revenue at or above $50,000 during the previous fiscal year
Cannot be a non-profit (except child care centers), an unregistered business, or a Limited Cooperative Association

Cannot operate in restricted industries including lobbying, speculative businesses, prurient entertainment, religion-focused counseling, pyramid sales, gambling, financial businesses primarily engaged in lending, life insurance, illegal activity, tanning salons, cannabis, pawn shops, or astrology/palm reading
Personal tax returns (1-2 years required)
Business tax returns (1-2 years required)
Business bank statements (1-2 years depending on loan amount)
CPA-compiled financials (required if loan $75,000 or greater; optional if less than $75,000)
Business insurance proof (if required for business)
Active business license (if required for business)
IRS Installment Agreement proof (if applicable)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Speak with a Small Business Advisor by visiting the WACIF client intake page. Share business info and financial needs, check eligibility (no credit score required to prequalify), compile required and optional documents including tax returns, bank statements, and CPA-compiled financials as applicable, and submit a loan application with support from the WACIF team. Underwriting process reviews documents; additional documentation may be requested.

structured_extraction.program_description: Washington County Transit (WCT) offers ADA Complementary Paratransit service — a demand-response, shared-ride transportation service — for people who are certified as unable to use fixed-route public buses. The service complies with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990 and runs curb-to-curb within three-quarters of a mile of WCT's fixed-route system, covering most of Hagerstown and surrounding areas in Washington County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-way paratransit fare is $2.00 per person. Personal Care Assistants (PCAs) ride free at no additional cost. Trips can be made for any purpose with no trip-purpose restrictions. Service operates Monday–Friday 6:15 a.m.–9:45 p.m. and Saturday 7:45 a.m.–9:45 p.m. (no Sunday or holiday service).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local residents and long-term visitors (staying 21+ days) who are certified as unable to use fixed-route public transportation due to a physical or mental impairment, as well as ADA-certified eligible individuals visiting from other localities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Door-to-door shared-ride transportation for trips of any purpose within the paratransit service area.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Service area covers origin and destination points within three-quarters of a mile on either side of WCT's fixed-route system — primarily Hagerstown, Williamsport, Smithsburg, Funkstown, and surrounding areas in Washington County.
requirements_list: Must complete an ADA Complementary Paratransit Eligibility Determination process
Condition must be certified on the application by a healthcare professional
Must be a local resident or long-term visitor (21+ days), or ADA-certified eligible visitor from another locality
Pick-up and drop-off must be within the paratransit service area
Must be unable to board, ride, or disembark from accessible vehicles without assistance (except operator assistance)
OR cannot use the system with a mobility device lift because the route is not 100% ADA accessible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact WCT at 240-313-2750 (menu option 2) or email paratransit@washco-md.net to request an eligibility application. A healthcare professional must certify your condition on the application. Applicants are notified of eligibility status by U.S. mail.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program run by Washington County's Department of Business and Economic Development to support agricultural innovation and equipment purchases for agricultural producers and businesses in Washington County, Maryland. The program is part of a broader suite of agriculture incentives and financial programs including loans, grants, and facilitation programs for agricultural enterprises.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding for agricultural innovation and equipment purchases. The broader program suite also includes low-interest loans (e.g., MRBIFF at 4.75% up to $300,000–$1,000,000 for equipment, real estate, food/fiber processing; Agribusiness Equipment & Working Capital at 6.75% up to $100,000), matching grants, down-payment assistance, loan guarantees, and technical assistance and training.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Closed; check back in 2026 for the next round
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural producers, agribusiness enterprises, farmers (including beginning and young farmers), forest products businesses, urban farmers, rural small businesses, and nonprofit organizations in Washington County, Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Agricultural innovation initiatives, equipment purchases, value-added agricultural processing, food production and processing, specialty crops, renewable energy, and direct-to-consumer marketing
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland (primary focus); rural Maryland counties for certain programs
requirements_list: Applicants must be agricultural producers or agribusinesses located in Washington County, Maryland
Rural area designation (outside cities with 50,000+ population) may apply for certain USDA-related programs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The current round is closed. Check back in 2026 for updates on the next round.

structured_extraction.program_description: Voluntary ten-year restriction on development of eligible farming property in Washington County in return for property tax credits and ability to apply for easement sales to the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation (MALPF). Helps the County control development location and ensures program participation eligibility. Landowners also receive protection from nuisance complaints under the Right to Farm Ordinance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: County property tax credits for farmland, farm buildings, and a partial tax credit for the home. Landowners also receive protection from nuisance complaints, eligibility to apply for permanent agricultural preservation easement sales to the State of Maryland, and eligibility retention for family/owner/child lot releases. Easement purchase is subject to availability of government funds and is not guaranteed.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural landowners in Washington County who wish to voluntarily restrict development on their land for ten years in exchange for property tax credits and eligibility for agricultural easement programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax credit on farmland, farm buildings, and partial home credit; eligibility to sell development rights easements through MALPF; preservation of agricultural land and restriction of commercial, industrial, and residential development.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland. Property must be outside water and sewer service areas and outside designated growth areas.
requirements_list: Minimum 50 acres (standalone) or 20 acres (contiguous to other districts)
Minimum 50% soil classes I, II, and III
Must be outside water and sewer service areas
Must be outside growth areas
Must implement an approved soil conservation plan within 10 years
Ten-year agreement restricting development, subdivision, or use of land for industrial, commercial, or residential purposes
No subdivision, off-conveyance, or boundary line movement without County written approval
No non-agricultural building or structure construction without County approval
Agreement runs with the land and must be recorded in County Land Records
Landowner must sign a notarized district agreement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Landowner submits a written application (Ag District Intake Form) with parcel information, ownership details, and farming operation description to the Land Preservation Office in the County's Department of Planning & Zoning. A district agreement is then executed between the County and the landowner, notarized, and recorded in County land records.

structured_extraction.program_description: A real property tax credit for Washington County property owners who commit to agricultural use for ten years within a designated agricultural preservation district.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax credit applied against Washington County real property taxes based on the assessed value of qualified agricultural land and improvements. The credit is allowed for the tax year immediately following application and approval.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners within a designated agricultural preservation district who commit to agricultural pursuits for 10 years.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of county real property taxes on qualified agricultural land and improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Property must be located within a designated agricultural preservation district in Washington County, MD.
requirements_list: Property must be located within a designated agricultural preservation district
Owner must commit to remaining in agricultural related pursuits for a period of ten years
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Washington County Planning Department at (240) 313-2430 for information and to apply.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides a property tax credit on agricultural real property in Washington County. Details are contained in the Agricultural Real Property Tax Credit Ordinance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A property tax credit for agricultural real property owners in Washington County, as defined by the county ordinance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural real property owners in Washington County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of property tax obligations on qualifying agricultural land.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: See the Agricultural Real Property Tax Credit Ordinance for details.

structured_extraction.program_description: A collection of incentives and financial programs available to agricultural businesses and landowners in Washington County, including low-interest loans for land and equipment, working capital loans, and other financial support for agricultural and resource-based industry enterprises.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Various incentives and financial programs supporting agriculture in Washington County, including: low-interest loans (2.25% initially) for land acquisition, capital equipment, and building construction (up to $750,000); moderate-cost loans (5.25%) for working capital and equipment ($15,000–$100,000 range); and other financial programs. Details available in the linked program guide.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural businesses, resource-based industry enterprises, farmers, producers, and landowners in Washington County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Support for agricultural operations and investments including land acquisition, capital equipment purchases, working capital, production and processing activities, and building construction in Washington County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland
requirements_list: MRBIFF maximum loan: $250,000 for equipment/fixed assets; $500,000 for real estate; $750,000 for large-scale food/fiber processing
Rural Business Equipment and Working Capital Loan Fund: minimum loan $15,000, maximum loan $100,000
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review the Agriculture Incentives and Financial Programs guide for details on available programs and how to apply.

structured_extraction.program_description: Washington County issues annual and temporary tip jar licenses to organizations that want to operate tip jar games as part of the county's charitable gaming program. Organizations can apply for an annual operator's license or a temporary license depending on their situation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The county issues tip jar operator licenses — annual or temporary — allowing eligible organizations to legally run tip jar games in Washington County. A full temporary application is required for new applicants, organizations with changed officers, or those whose last full application was more than two years ago. A short form is available for returning applicants with current information on file.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations seeking to operate tip jar games in Washington County, Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Charitable gaming operations via tip jar games
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a qualifying organization under Washington County tip jar regulations
Full application required for new applicants, organizations with changed officers, or those whose last full application was more than two years ago
Short form available if organization information on file is current and full application was completed within the past two years
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the appropriate application form to the Washington County Office of Grant Management. Use the full temporary tip jar application if you are a new applicant, your officers have changed, or it has been two or more years since your last full application. Use the short form if your information is current and less than two years have passed since the last full application.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federally funded grant program that provides grants to eligible entities in Washington County for projects supporting economic opportunities, workforce development, critical infrastructure, natural and cultural assets, and leadership and community capacity in the Appalachian region.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal grants requiring a 50% match from the applicant. Matching funds must be identified and committed at the time of application, with commitment letters required for all matching funds with committed status. Projects must demonstrate measurable outcomes and/or economic impact. Applicants should identify the minimum ARC funding amount needed for project viability. Review committee may reduce funding requests to maximize the number of projects funded.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations with capacity to administer federal grants in Washington County seeking funding for projects related to economic development, workforce readiness, critical infrastructure, natural and cultural assets, or community leadership capacity.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects supporting entrepreneurial and small business development, education and workforce training, critical infrastructure (broadband, transportation, water/wastewater, clean energy), natural and cultural heritage assets, downtown revitalization, heritage and cultural preservation, technology development, tourism and outdoor recreation, recovery ecosystems, and community/leadership capacity building. Must align with ARC Investment Goals and State Strategic Objectives/Strategies (2024-2028).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to eligible entities in Washington County, Maryland, within the Appalachian region.
requirements_list: Projects must relate to ARC goals: economic opportunities, ready workforce, critical infrastructure, natural/cultural assets, or leadership and community capacity
Projects must align with ARC 2024 Strategy Statement and Strategic Goals and Objectives (2024-2028)
50% matching funds required and must be identified and committed at time of application
Commitment letters required for all matching funds with committed status
Must identify minimum ARC funding amount needed for project viability
Projects must demonstrate measurable outcomes and/or economic impact with defined outputs and achievement timeframes using ARC acceptable performance measures
Organizational capacity to administer federal grants and recent awards documentation required
Project should be part of an overall economic development plan
Submit Preliminary Project Description and ARC Project Budget and Funding Sources forms to the Office of Grant Management
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Submit the Preliminary Project Description (PPD) form (including project details, organizational capacity, goals/objectives, performance measures, and funding sources) and ARC Project Budget and Funding Sources worksheet (with matching fund documentation) to the Office of Grant Management (email to Maria Kramer). 2. Projects are reviewed and ranked by the Washington County Commissioners. 3. County-ranked projects are submitted to Tri-County Council for Western Maryland for regional ranking. 4. Top-ranked projects receive a letter in early Fall inviting them to submit a formal grant application to ARC, due in November.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Washington County Office of Grant Management recognizes outstanding young people in the community through the Commissioners' Youth Meritorious Award (YMA). Nominees are evaluated on scholastic achievement, leadership qualities, community service, and other positive characteristics. Selected winners are recognized at a meeting of the County Commissioners.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Recipients are recognized publicly at a meeting of the Washington County Board of County Commissioners. This is an award/recognition program, not a financial assistance program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Middle school and high school youth in Washington County who demonstrate scholastic achievement, leadership, community service, and other positive qualities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Public recognition at a County Commissioners meeting.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland
requirements_list: Nominee must be a young person from middle school through high school
Nominee should be well-rounded, demonstrating scholastic achievement, leadership qualities, community service, and other positive characteristics
Nominations accepted from public schools, private schools, youth-serving organizations, and family and friends
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the online nomination form available at the Youth Meritorious Award Nomination Form page. Nominators who know the candidate in only one area of achievement should coordinate with others familiar with the candidate to address all required criteria.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides financial support to charitable (non-profit) organizations in Washington County that offer services improving the community and quality of life for county residents. Each year, the Board of County Commissioners sets aside a funding allocation, and the Office of Grant Management administers the application, award, and oversight process. The program uses a prioritized, results-based approach to ensure accountability and efficient use of funds.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual grant funding for non-profit organizations. The Board of County Commissioners determines the total allocation each funding cycle. Grants are awarded through a competitive application process with defined opening and closing dates announced via a Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: FY 27 cycle is closed and not accepting applications
structured_extraction.program_audience: Charitable non-profit 501(c)(3) organizations on the Washington County Board of County Commissioners' Recognized Non-Profit List (Section 1-108 of the Code of Public Local Laws) that provide services benefiting Washington County residents. Eligible organizations include libraries, museums, medical centers, family services, volunteer fire companies, ambulance units, historical societies, health services, arts organizations, youth organizations, community development organizations, and other social service nonprofits.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Programs and services that improve the community and quality of life for Washington County citizens, with emphasis on results-based programmatic outcomes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must serve Washington County, Maryland residents. Organization must be on the Board of County Commissioners' Recognized Non-Profit List (1-108 List).
requirements_list: Organization must be included on the Board of County Commissioners' Recognized Non-Profit List (Section 1-108 of the Code of Public Local Laws)
Must be a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization
Must be active and in good standing with Maryland Business Express
Applications are only accepted during the published application window announced in the Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA)
Must demonstrate programmatic and fiscal accountability
Must achieve results-based programmatic outcomes that positively impact the community
Written letter of request from organization
Copy of IRS 501(c)(3) determination letter
Proof that organization is active and in good standing with Maryland Business Express
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: A Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) is sent to all organizations on the Recognized Non-Profit List, with instructions on how to apply and the application window dates. Organizations not yet on the 1-108 list must apply to be added before they can apply for funding. To be added to the 1-108 list, submit a completed application packet (including a written letter of request, IRS 501(c)(3) determination letter, and proof of good standing with Maryland Business Express) by mail or email to Kimberly Jacobson, Legal Assistant, at kjacobson@washco-md.net or countyattorneyoffice@washco-md.net. Contact the Office of Grant Management at 240-313-2040 for questions about the COF program.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program created to assist eligible local nonprofit organizations in Washington County that were negatively impacted by the COVID-19 health emergency. Funded with $1,500,000 in American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funds, the program provides awards of up to $40,000 to eligible nonprofits that experienced decreased revenue, financial insecurity, increased costs, or other hardships due to COVID-19. Designed to support nonprofits serving Washington County citizens, including those contributing to disproportionate pandemic impact in Qualified Census Tracts.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Awards of up to $40,000 per eligible organization, funded through $1,500,000 in ARPA funds allocated by Washington County. Funds may be used for replacement of lost revenue/increased costs caused by the pandemic (salary and wages, inventory, rent, utilities, technology, contracted services), provision of increased services, or a combination of both. Not eligible: indirect/administrative costs or capital expenses.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local nonprofit organizations (501c3 or 501c19) based in Washington County that serve a majority of Washington County citizens and were impacted by COVID-19, including those serving vulnerable populations such as low-income households, seniors, and pandemic-impacted children.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Replacement of lost revenue/increased costs (salary and wages, inventory, rent, utilities, technology, contracted services); provision of increased services addressing public health, mental health/substance abuse, seniors services, low-income household assistance; service expansion or new programs addressing community needs. Indirect/administrative costs and capital expenses are not eligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Organization must have a physical location/address in Washington County, Maryland, and provide more than 50% of services to Washington County citizens.
requirements_list: Must have a valid 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(19) designation from the IRS
Must have a physical location/address in Washington County and serve a majority (>50%) of Washington County citizens
Must be in good standing with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation's Personal Property Tax Division
Must be in compliance with Federal, State, and local human rights laws
Must have been established before March 1, 2019
Must have been adversely impacted by the COVID-19 public health emergency
Organizations operating under a fiscal sponsor are ineligible
Churches and religious organizations are ineligible unless they have a separate non-profit status and provide services to the public regardless of faith (e.g., food banks, shelters)
Fraternal organizations or social clubs are ineligible
Homeowner's Associations are ineligible
Labor Unions are ineligible
Private, political, or public foundations are ineligible
Required documents: Completed Community Recovery Nonprofit Grant Application (all fields completed, signed by applicant and Authorized Signatory)
Required documents: Copy of IRS Determination Letter
Required documents: Completed Financial Budget Template (Excel Spreadsheet)
Required documents: Most recent audit/financial statement
Required documents: W-9 form (if organization has never received funds from Washington County or has an address change)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit completed application and all required attachments via email to CommunityRecovery@washco-md.net by October 19, 2022 at 3:00 pm. Each application and attachment must be submitted as individual electronic files with appropriate labels including the organization name. Hard copy applications are not accepted. Applicants are encouraged to submit questions prior to the week before the deadline.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides qualifying businesses with Maryland state income tax credits and local real property tax credits in return for job creation and capital investments made within designated Enterprise Zones in Washington County.
