Approximately 5,500 acres in Washington County are designated as Enterprise Zones across three state-approved zones, including the Hagerstown-Washington County Enterprise Zone (approximately 4,000 acres) and the Town of Hancock Enterprise Zone (approximately 1,500 acres). Local real property tax credits are available for up to 10 years on capital investments, with credits of 80% on the increased assessed value of real property for the first five years, decreasing by 10% in each of the remaining five years. State income tax credits are also available for qualifying job creation. Exemptions from commercial building excise tax are also available for new construction in Enterprise Zones.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Local real property tax credits for up to 10 years on capital investments: 80% credit on the increased assessed value of real property for the first five years, decreasing to 70%-30% in years 6-10. State income tax credits for job creation: $1,000 maximum (one-time) for most new jobs; up to $3,000 first year, $2,000 second year, $1,000 third year for 'economically disadvantaged' certified employees. Personal property tax credits available in Enterprise Zone Focus Areas. Exemption from commercial building excise tax for new construction in Enterprise Zones. Three state-designated Enterprise Zones: Hagerstown-Washington County (~4,000 acres, including Hopewell Valley Industrial Park, Washington County Business Park, CSX Valley Park, City of Hagerstown Business Park, and Central Business District) and Town of Hancock (~1,500 acres).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Property tax credits must be applied for prior to project completion and issuance of User/Occupancy Permits
structured_extraction.program_audience: New or expanding businesses and developers locating, relocating, or expanding within designated Enterprise Zones in Washington County, MD, seeking to create jobs and make capital investments.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credits to offset real property taxes on capital investments, state income tax credits for job creation, personal property tax credits in Focus Areas, and exemptions from commercial building excise tax for new construction, rehabilitation, and new machinery and equipment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be located within a designated Enterprise Zone in Washington County, MD — either the Hagerstown-Washington County Enterprise Zone or the Town of Hancock Enterprise Zone. Personal property tax credits require location within a Focus Area within the Enterprise Zone.
requirements_list: Must locate or expand within a designated Enterprise Zone
Must create jobs or make capital investments
Application for property tax credits must be submitted prior to project completion and issuance of User/Occupancy Permits
Qualified employees must meet Maryland Department of Commerce requirements
Property owner must co-sign application if developer/company is applying on behalf of owner
Applicants must agree to provide all data required by Enterprise Zone
Each Enterprise Zone is approved by the State for a ten-year period
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Washington County Department of Business Development for application details. Application packet available at the provided link. Property tax credit applications must be submitted prior to project completion and issuance of User/Occupancy Permits.

structured_extraction.program_description: A real property tax credit for Washington County residents who qualify as fallen heroes or their surviving family members. The credit reduces the county real property tax owed on the applicant's property.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A real property tax credit applied to Washington County property taxes for qualifying fallen heroes or their survivors. The specific credit amount and terms are defined in the county ordinance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Fallen heroes (military, law enforcement, or other qualifying public safety personnel) and their surviving family members who own real property in Washington County, Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of Washington County real property taxes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to real property owners in Washington County, Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Washington County Real Property Tax Credit for Fallen Heroes Application and submit it to the Washington County Treasurer's Office at 35 West Washington Street, Suite 102, Hagerstown, MD 21740.

structured_extraction.program_description: Foreign Trade Zone #255 in Washington County, Maryland allows businesses to minimize customs duties and taxes on imported and exported goods. The zone covers nearly 1,800 acres of industrial and commercial properties along the I-81 and I-70 corridor, providing access to two-thirds of the U.S. population within one day and a major port within one hour. Businesses operating within the zone may import goods without paying customs duties until those goods enter U.S. Customs territory, and tangible personal property held in the FTZ for export is exempt from state and local taxes and ad valorem taxes. No duty applies to re-exported merchandise, labor, overhead, or profit from FTZ production, and businesses can choose the lower duty rate on component materials or finished products. The zone supports reduced costs, streamlined import/export processes, and improved supply chain efficiency.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Businesses in FTZ #255 may import goods without paying customs duties until those goods enter U.S. Customs territory. Tangible personal property held in the FTZ for export is exempt from state and local taxes and ad valorem taxes. No duty applies to re-exported merchandise, labor, overhead, or profit from FTZ production. Businesses can choose the lower duty rate on component materials or finished products, reducing overall import/export costs and improving supply chain competitiveness.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Industrial and commercial businesses engaged in importing or exporting goods that want to reduce customs duties and taxes and improve supply chain efficiency within Washington County's Foreign Trade Zone #255.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction and deferral of U.S. customs duties on imported goods, exemption from state and local taxes and ad valorem taxes on tangible personal property held for export, and elimination of duties on re-exported merchandise.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be located within Washington County, MD Foreign Trade Zone #255 (approximately 1,800 acres of industrial and commercial properties along the I-81 and I-70 corridor).
requirements_list: Must operate within the boundaries of FTZ #255 in Washington County, MD
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Washington County Department of Business and Economic Development to learn more about participating in Foreign Trade Zone #255. Additional resources are available through the National Association of Foreign Trade Zones, U.S. Department of Commerce, and U.S. Customs and Border Protection.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides one-time grant funding to organizations operating in Washington County for unanticipated projects or events that were not budgeted. The goal is to address current financial issues or situations that need a prompt response and are not eligible for Community Organization Funding or Hotel Rental Tax Funding.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time grant funding for unanticipated projects or events. Maximum award of $2,000 per grant. Funds are paid directly to the applicant (not vendors). The amount available may be adjusted annually at the discretion of the Board of County Commissioners.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted throughout the fiscal year (contingent on available funding)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations operating within Washington County with unexpected circumstances or critical community needs requiring prompt financial support.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: One-time projects or events addressing unexpected circumstances or critical community needs, including personnel costs, operating expenses, equipment, and other project-related expenditures.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to organizations operating within Washington County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be an organization operating within Washington County
Project or event must be one-time and unanticipated (not previously budgeted)
Must not qualify for Community Organization Funding or Hotel Rental Tax Funding
Must meet the Board of County Commissioners' funding goals
Have an unexpected circumstance requiring prompt resolution
Provide evidence that request meets a critical need in the community
Not have an alternative source of funding
Have proven to be a valuable community resource
Submit completed Grant Report Form with supporting documentation within 60 days of event/project completion
Return unused funds within 30 days of completion
Submission of receipts and supporting documentation for all expenditures
Certification that expenses align with approved funding application
Report on community impact and economic benefits
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete the General Fund Contingency Funding Grant Application. Applications are accessible and processed via the county website (www.washco-md.net), or can be printed and mailed/emailed. The Office of Grant Management (OGM) receives applications and determines applicant qualification and project/event eligibility. Submit completed Grant Report Form to Washington County Office of Grant Management, 100 W. Washington St. Rm. 2200, Hagerstown, MD 21740.

structured_extraction.program_name: Hagerstown Community College Technical Innovation Center (TIC) / David W. Fletcher Incubator + Labs
structured_extraction.program_description: A technology-focused business incubator located on the Hagerstown Community College campus in Washington County, Maryland. The facility helps entrepreneurs, tech startups, small businesses, researchers, and independent workers grow by providing affordable workspace and lab space, business development support, and access to a network of contacts and resources. Tenants can access private office suites, wet labs, virtual offices, dedicated desks, co-working space, conference rooms, 4,000 square feet of biotech research labs, and hourly commercial kitchen access. Business support services include concept review, bookkeeping setup, clerical support, cash-flow planning, HR planning, market evaluations, manufacturing assistance, presentation development, and SBIR/STTR application support.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides affordable facilities including private office suites, wet labs, virtual offices, dedicated desks, co-working space, conference rooms, and 4,000 square feet of biotech research labs, as well as hourly commercial kitchen access. Business development and support services include business concept review, bookkeeping setup, clerical support, cash-flow planning, HR planning, market evaluations, manufacturing assistance, presentation development, and SBIR/STTR application support. Spaces can be combined.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Entrepreneurs, tech startups, small businesses, researchers, independent contractors, catering chefs, and companies moving into Maryland or seeking lab space and business support services in Western Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Workspace and lab space (private offices, wet labs, virtual offices, dedicated desks, co-working space, commercial kitchen), business development support, and access to incubator resources.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Located in Hagerstown, Maryland on the Hagerstown Community College campus, serving Washington County and entrepreneurs from the surrounding region.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit www.incubatorhcc.com or hagerstowncc.edu/technical-innovation-center, or call 240-500-2479 for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Washington County real property tax credit program for owners of historic properties who rehabilitate, restore, or preserve designated historic structures. Applicants may receive a tax credit equal to 25% of qualifying restoration and preservation expenses on an existing historic structure, or an additional 5% for new construction exterior work attached to an existing historic structure, up to the total amount of county real estate property taxes owed. Unused credits may be carried forward for up to 5 tax years. The credit is allowed for the tax year immediately following completion of the work. The program can be stacked with state and federal credits for up to 70% total credit. The program covers properties designated on Washington County's master plan for historic preservation, including Historic Preservation (HP) Overlay zoned properties, the Antietam Overlay (AO1 or AO2) districts, Historic Rural Villages, and contributing structures in Towns on the National Register of Historic Places with appropriate zoning and design guidelines.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax credit equal to 25% of the owner's qualified restoration and preservation expenses on an existing historic structure, up to the total amount of county real estate property taxes owed. An additional 5% credit is allowed for new construction exterior work attached to an existing historic structure. Unused credits may be carried forward for up to 5 tax years. The credit is allowed for the tax year immediately following completion of the work. Qualified rehabilitation expenses include roof repair/replacement, chimney repair/replacement, window restoration, storm doors/windows, masonry re-pointing, structural repairs, and architectural/engineering/consulting fees. The program can be stacked with state and federal credits for up to 70% total credit. Applicants submit a three-part application (Part 1, Part 2, and Part 3 including an expense sheet) documenting the project and qualifying expenses.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential and commercial historic property owners in qualifying areas of Washington County, including properties with HP Overlay zoning, properties in Antietam Overlay districts, Historic Rural Villages, and contributing structures in eligible municipalities on the National Register of Historic Places.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rehabilitation, restoration, and preservation of historic structures; qualifying expenses include roof repair/replacement, chimney repair/replacement, window restoration, storm doors/windows, masonry re-pointing, structural repairs, architectural/engineering/consulting fees, and tool/equipment rental. Credits offset county real property taxes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available within Washington County, Maryland. Property must be documented on the Maryland Inventory of Historic Properties and located in a qualifying overlay district or historic village, including Historic Preservation (HP) Overlay zoned properties, Antietam Overlay (AO1 or AO2) districts, Historic Rural Villages, structures under MHT Easement, or contributing structures in eligible municipalities on the National Register of Historic Places.
requirements_list: Property must be located within Washington County
Property must be documented on the Maryland Inventory of Historic Properties
Property must be located in a qualifying overlay district or historic area (HP Overlay, Antietam Overlay, Historic Rural Village, MHT Easement, or eligible municipality)
Work must comply with the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation
Work must comply with Washington County's Design Guidelines for Historic Structures
Compliance with Federal, State, and local laws (zoning, building, safety codes)
Part I must be submitted first (unless HP Overlay applies)
Part II must be approved BEFORE rehabilitation work begins
Complete Part III after project completion with itemized expenses and proof of payment
Provide ownership documentation (if not fee-simple owner, must provide written consent from owner)
Attach exterior photographs of all sides of structure and documentation of work completed
Itemized expense spreadsheet with eligible/ineligible expenses clearly delineated with invoices/receipts and proof of payment
HDC reserves the right to inspect up to 5 years after completion
Unused credit may be carried forward for up to 5 tax years
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a three-part application to the Washington County Historic District Commission (HDC) at 747 Northern Avenue, Hagerstown, MD 21742 or by email. Part I: Submit application to qualify the structure, including property information, significance statement, exterior photographs, and supporting documentation for HDC review and determination. Part II: Submit application describing all proposed rehabilitation work with photographs and supporting documentation (site plans, architectural plans, specifications) BEFORE work begins; HDC reviews for consistency with standards. Part III: Submit after project completion with itemized expense sheet, invoices/receipts, proof of payment, and photographs documenting completed work. Review the Tax Credit Brochure and Historic Tax Credit Directions for guidance before applying. Contact the Washington County Department of Planning and Zoning at (240) 313-2430 or email askplanning@washco-md.net for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state and local program that limits the annual increase in taxable assessed value for owner-occupied residential properties to protect homeowners from large assessment increases.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Limits the annual taxable assessment increase for owner-occupied residential properties. Rates: State of Maryland limits increases to 10%; Washington County limits increases to 5%; municipalities limit increases to 5%. The credit is automatically applied to all properties listed as 'Principal Residence.'
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owner-occupants of residential properties in Maryland, particularly those affected by large property assessment increases.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Limits annual growth in taxable property assessment, reducing real property tax liability.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to owner-occupied residential properties throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Property must be owner-occupied and listed as 'Principal Residence'
Credit is automatically applied; contact SDAT if not received
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Credit is automatically applied to eligible properties. If not received, contact the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation at 301-791-3050 or visit www.dat.state.md.us.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides grants funded by Washington County's 6% hotel rental tax to help local organizations, agencies, businesses, and municipalities develop tourism attractions, support economic development, and fund cultural and recreational projects. It is designed to help applicants launch activities and events that can eventually grow and sustain themselves without ongoing financial support.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants funded from 6% County Hotel Rental Tax revenue. Funds are invested back into the community through the Convention and Visitors Bureau, local municipalities, and designated local projects. Grant categories include: Develop Tourism/Attraction, Economic Development, Cultural, or Recreational projects. Eligible expenses include personnel, operating costs, equipment, advertising, facility rental, contracted services, and other approved expenses. Individuals, for-profit ventures, and organizations supporting political candidates are not eligible.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Requests can be made throughout the fiscal year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local municipalities, businesses, organizations, and agencies in Washington County, Maryland that want to develop tourism attractions, support economic development, or fund cultural and recreational projects. Also serves visitors to Washington County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Developing tourism attractions, advertising and marketing, economic development and job creation projects, cultural and history-related projects, recreational activities and events, tourism-related facilities, strategic planning and research for tourism development. Personnel, operating costs, equipment, facility rental, contracted services, and other approved expenses. Not for routine operating expenses, administrative costs, endowments, or organizations with budget deficits.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to organizations, agencies, and businesses in Washington County, Maryland only.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local municipality, business organization, non-profit, or agency in Washington County (not individuals, for-profit ventures, or organizations supporting political candidates)
Project must support tourism, economic development, or cultural/recreational activities in Washington County
Must generate overnight stays in the County
Must encourage support of County businesses, restaurants, and attractions
Must reach a broad segment
Event/project must generate hotel/motel room nights
Expenses must align with approved event or project proposal
Expenses must meet intent of Hotel Rental Tax Funding requirements
Copies of all receipts and supporting documentation required
Certification of billed costs and expenses accuracy required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and save the Hotel Rental Tax Funding Application PDF to your computer before completing it. Review the Guidelines and Instructions document. Submit the completed application. After receiving funding, complete a grant report form including organization details, project information, expense breakdown, and impact assessment, along with all receipts and supporting documentation. Submit by mail to: Washington County Office of Grant Management, 100 W. Washington St., Hagerstown, MD 21740, or by email.

structured_extraction.program_description: Washington County's Department of Business Development provides a whole-team consultation service to help businesses start, grow, or relocate in Washington County, Maryland. The team connects businesses with workforce resources, demographic data, tax incentives, financing programs, and location information.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free business consultation and referral service connecting businesses with workforce data, demographic research, tax incentives, financing programs, and site location support.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses looking to start, grow, or relocate in Washington County, Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business development support including workforce data, demographic research, tax and incentive information, and financing program referrals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a contact form on the program page with your name, email, and message to connect with the Washington County Department of Business Development team.

structured_extraction.program_description: Accelerates agricultural land preservation easement purchases by allowing landowners to sell development rights to Washington County in exchange for installment payments over ten years at a fixed interest rate.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Landowners sell an agricultural preservation easement to the County and receive payment through an Installment Purchase Agreement (IPA) over 10 years. Ten percent of the principal is paid at settlement along with interest, and 10% of the principal plus interest is paid annually for the remaining 9 years. The fixed interest rate is set in the agreement. The program is competitive and depends on economic conditions.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural landowners in Washington County who meet minimum qualifications and want to sell development rights to the County on an installment basis.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment to landowners for permanent restriction of development rights on agricultural land, paid over 10 years.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland
requirements_list: Property must meet minimum qualifications for agricultural land
Easement covers entire contiguous acreage minus one acre per existing dwelling
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply to the County's Land Preservation Office. If the County accepts, an Installment Purchase Agreement is drafted specifying total payment and terms.

structured_extraction.program_name: LMB ENOUGH Capacity Building Fiscal Year 2026
structured_extraction.program_description: Grant funding to support innovative programs that bridge the gap between transportation and healthcare access in underserved communities in Washington County. Funded through the Governor's Office for Children (GOC) and the ENOUGH Initiative, the program targets greater healthcare access for seniors, individuals with disabilities, and low-income households with children who face significant mobility barriers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $40,000 per award. Total funding pool is $74,000. Washington County intends to award 1–3 grants with individual awards ranging from $10,000 to $40,000. Grants may fund operating costs, capital investments, or a combination of both. The performance period runs from May 15, 2026 through September 30, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit 501(c)(3) organizations and local governments providing transportation and healthcare access services to Washington County residents, especially seniors, individuals with disabilities, and low-income households with children.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Programs addressing non-emergency medical transportation (including direct transport to primary care, dialysis, mental health services, and pharmacy pickups), expansion of existing volunteer driver or specialized transit networks, or last-mile solutions for underserved areas not reached by public transit. Funds may cover operating costs, capital investments, or a combination of both.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Services must be provided exclusively to residents of Washington County, Maryland. Organization must be located in Washington County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Be a registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization or a local government entity
Be in 'Good Standing' with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
Provide services exclusively to residents of Washington County, Maryland
Demonstrate a proven track record of fiscal responsibility and programmatic performance
Have no unpaid obligations to any government entity
Must not discriminate based on race, creed, sex, age, color, national origin, physical or mental disabilities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the completed application electronically with all required documents (Application Submission Form including organizational information, statement of need, organizational capacity description, program plan, and collaborations/partnerships details; program budget; letters of support; 501(c)(3) determination letter; and SDAT Good Standing proof) to cahrens@washco-md.net by March 6, 2026 at 3:00pm.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Commuter and Shuttle Bus COVID RELIEF Grant Program

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Relief from continued financial impacts of COVID-19.

structured_extraction.program_description: A range of Maryland state property tax exemptions available for qualifying properties including those owned by charitable, educational, religious, government, and other eligible organizations, as well as certain individuals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Full or partial exemption from Maryland real and personal property taxes for qualifying property types, including charitable/educational properties, religious organizations, government properties, blind or disabled veteran homeowners, fire companies, housing authorities, and various personal property categories (farm implements, livestock, manufacturing equipment, vehicles, etc.).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners whose properties qualify under Maryland Tax Property Article Title 7 exemptions, including non-profits, governments, religious organizations, and qualifying individuals.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Elimination or reduction of Maryland real and/or personal property tax liability.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Property must qualify under one of the categories listed in Maryland Tax Property Article Title 7, Subtitle 2 or Subtitle 3
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Refer to the Annotated Code of Maryland Tax Property Article Title 7 for the full list of exemptions. Contact the Washington County Treasurer's Office or Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation for guidance.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides emergency assistance for eligible restaurants, bars, and other qualifying businesses impacted by COVID-19.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Emergency financial assistance for restaurants, bars, and other qualifying food and beverage businesses impacted by COVID-19.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Restaurants, bars, and other eligible food and beverage businesses impacted by COVID-19.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business expenses impacted by COVID-19.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Ride Assist Program provides subsidized transportation vouchers to elderly residents and people with disabilities who cannot use Washington County Transit's fixed-route buses. Participants purchase vouchers at a reduced rate and use them to pay registered taxi or ride providers, saving at least 50% on transportation costs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants purchase a set number of transportation vouchers per month at a reduced rate, saving at least 50% on taxi fares. Vouchers come in various denominations and expire June 30 each year. Vouchers cannot be used for tipping.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications expire June 30 of every year; annual renewal required.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents age 60 or older, and individuals with disabilities who cannot use Washington County Transit fixed-route buses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment for transportation services through registered ride providers using discounted vouchers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to eligible residents of Washington County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be age 60 or older, OR have a qualifying disability that prevents use of fixed-route buses
If under age 60, application must be certified by a healthcare professional acknowledging the disability
Must have an annually updated application on file
Applications expire June 30 each year and must be renewed annually
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call the WCT office at 240-313-2750 to have an application mailed, or pick one up in person at 1000 West Washington Street, Hagerstown, MD. Complete the application (have it certified by a healthcare professional if under age 60). Mail or drop off the completed application at the WCT office (faxes not accepted). Applicants are notified by mail of their eligibility. Vouchers may then be purchased at the WCT office or by mail using check, money order, or credit card.

structured_extraction.program_name: Rural Maryland Economic Development Fund Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: Funds public infrastructure projects that support economic development activity, stimulate private investment, and grow jobs in Maryland's rural counties. Eligible projects include utilities, transportation, broadband, commercial or industrial property acquisition for business parks, workforce development, entrepreneurship and innovation, and planning and feasibility studies.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funds are provided for public infrastructure projects such as utilities, transportation, and broadband; purchase of commercial or industrial properties for business parks; workforce development; entrepreneurship and innovation stimulation; planning and feasibility studies; capital and operational expenses. Up to 3% of total award may be used for administrative costs. No matching funds are required. All grant funds must be expended within 24 months of award date. Direct private-sector incentives, subsidies, grants, loans, and residential or housing projects are not eligible. Granting land or buildings purchased with these funds to private entities is prohibited, but sale or lease is permitted.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: August 31 (hard deadline set by Maryland Department of Commerce)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local government entities, institutions of higher education, workforce development organizations, and not-for-profit entities in rural Maryland counties seeking to fund public infrastructure and economic development projects
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Public infrastructure (utilities, transportation, broadband), commercial/industrial property acquisition for business parks, workforce development, entrepreneurship and innovation initiatives, planning and feasibility studies, capital and operational expenses, and administrative costs (up to 3% of award)
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to rural counties in Maryland served by the state's five tri-county councils, including Allegany, Garrett, and Washington Counties (Western Maryland), as well as Eastern Shore and Southern Maryland rural counties
requirements_list: Projects must be proposed through one of Maryland's five tri-county regional councils
Projects must support economic development, attract or retain businesses, or grow jobs
Project must demonstrate significant economic development impact
Eligible uses are limited to public infrastructure, property acquisition for business parks, workforce development, or planning studies
Capital and operational expenses are eligible
Up to 3% of total award may be used for administrative costs
No matching funds are required
All grant funds must be expended within 24 months of award date
Interim reports due at 6-month intervals
Direct private-sector incentives, subsidies, grants, or loans are not eligible
Residential or housing projects are not eligible
Granting land or buildings purchased with these funds to private entities is prohibited (sale or lease is permitted)
Budget must include funding sources and amounts
Project summary required (250 words or less)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a completed Project Summary Application including contact information, project details, budget with funding sources and amounts, and an economic impact description (250 words or less) to the Washington County Office of Grant Management by the deadline. Application materials are available on the program page. The hard deadline of August 31 is set by the Maryland Department of Commerce.

structured_extraction.program_name: Senior Citizen Supplement – Homeowners Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A Washington County supplemental property tax credit for homeowners age 65 and older who meet income qualifications, added on top of the Maryland State Homeowners' Property Tax Credit.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Supplements the State Homeowners' Property Tax Credit for eligible senior homeowners. The credit is based on the amount by which state and county real property taxes exceed a percentage of the homeowner's combined income. The county supplement may significantly increase the total credit received. Under the State formula, the first $8,000 of income is excluded. Effective July 1, 2012.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: September 1 of each year (State HTC-60 form deadline)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Washington County homeowners age 65 and older who meet income qualifications.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of real property taxes for qualifying senior homeowners.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, MD. Property must be owner-occupied residential.
requirements_list: Must be a homeowner age 65 or older
Must meet income qualifications
Property must be owner-occupied residential
Must apply using State Homeowners' Property Tax Credit Application Form HTC-60
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply using the State's Homeowners' Property Tax Credit Application Form HTC-60. Eligibility for both the Washington County and State credits is determined by the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Washington County real estate property tax credit for homeowners who are service-connected disabled American veterans or their surviving spouses.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Real estate property tax credit for Washington County homeowners classified as 1% to 100% service-connected disabled American veterans and their surviving spouses.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Washington County homeowners who are service-connected disabled American veterans (1%-100%) or surviving spouses of such veterans.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of Washington County real estate property taxes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, MD.
requirements_list: Must be a homeowner in Washington County
Must be classified as a 1%-100% service-connected disabled American veteran, or the surviving spouse of such a veteran
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Application Form (available as a PDF) and contact the Maryland State Department of Veterans Affairs at 301-791-0356 for additional information.

structured_extraction.program_description: Comprehensive suite of incentives including tax credits, workforce training, utility incentives, and connectivity support designed to attract and support business expansion, relocation, and job creation in Washington County. Programs include the Job Creation & Capital Investment Real Property Tax Credit Program, New Jobs Tax Credit Program, Brownfield Revitalization Incentive Program (BRIP), C-PACE Program, Pad-Ready Site Commercial Stimulus Program, and more.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Multiple incentive programs including: real property tax credits (e.g., 52% credit years 1-2, 39% years 3-4, 26% years 5-6 for qualifying businesses under Section 4(a)); personal property and business property tax exemptions; capital investment incentives; energy efficiency/renewable energy financing (C-PACE); workforce training grants; utility incentives; infrastructure/broadband connectivity support; microenterprise grants for businesses with 5 or fewer employees; revolving loan fund for small business growth, expansion, rehabilitation, and facade enhancement; and Foreign Trade Zone (#255) access.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses looking to open, expand, or relocate in Washington County, including manufacturers, technology companies, small businesses, and nonprofits (for C-PACE)
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business development, expansion, or relocation costs; capital investment; job creation; workforce training; energy efficiency improvements; broadband/connectivity infrastructure; rehabilitation and facade enhancement
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland; City of Hagerstown and other municipalities throughout Washington County
requirements_list: Section 4(a): Minimum 1,500 sq ft, 1 new full-time employee for real property tax credit
Section 4(b): Minimum 2,500 sq ft, 5 new full-time employees for real property tax credit
Microenterprise grants limited to businesses with 5 or fewer employees in Hagerstown
C-PACE program open to nonprofits in addition to for-profit businesses
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Programs are tailored to individual business needs and developed in partnership with local and state partners. Contact the Washington County Department of Business and Economic Development or the City of Hagerstown Community and Economic Development Department for program-specific application guidance.

structured_extraction.program_name: Washington County FY23 Surplus Funding Nonprofit Assistance Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program distributes surplus county funds to local nonprofits serving Washington County residents. It provides an objective, systematic approach to reviewing and awarding funding, emphasizing efficient use of funds and achieving measurable program outcomes that positively impact Washington County citizens.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $100,000 per organization from a total pool of $1,831,447 in county surplus funds. Organizations must expend awarded funds within one year of receipt or return the funds to the county. Capital and operating expenses are eligible (not indirect costs, endowments, or individual benefits), but this is a one-time program, not an annual grant. Organizations should plan to sustain operating costs in future years without relying on these funds.

Not eligible: indirect costs, endowments, or individual benefits.

structured_extraction.program_name: Washington County Forest Conservation Payment-in-Lieu Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A program where developers and property owners subject to forest conservation requirements may pay a fee into the local Forest Conservation Fund instead of planting or retaining forest on-site. The county uses these funds to purchase conservation easements, plant trees, and conduct reforestation/afforestation in sensitive environmental areas, protecting large contiguous forest areas to benefit water quality and the environment. Requires forest stand delineations, forest conservation plans, maintenance agreements, and sureties for regulated development activities on parcels of 20,000 square feet or greater.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Developers and property owners who must remove forest during subdivision or development may pay a payment-in-lieu fee into the Washington County Forest Conservation Fund instead of completing on-site retention, afforestation, or reforestation when requirements cannot be reasonably accomplished on-site. The county pools these fees to fund reforestation/afforestation within 2-3 years of receipt, including site identification and acquisition, site preparation, acquisition of planting stock, compensation for planting activities, and maintenance of previously planted/protected forests. Funds remain in a dedicated account and do not revert to the general fund. Applicants may also purchase credits from approved Forest Mitigation Banks (one credit per tenth acre of required mitigation) as an alternative compliance pathway.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners, developers, subdividers, and property owners in Washington County proposing regulated development activities (subdivision, site plan, grading, sediment control permits) on parcels of 20,000 sq. ft. or greater, as well as public utilities and agricultural operators subject to forest conservation requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment-in-lieu fees are deposited into the Washington County Forest Conservation Fund and used for: site identification and acquisition, site preparation, acquisition of planting stock, compensation for planting activities, maintenance of previously planted/protected forests, and administration of the forest conservation program. Funds cannot be utilized outside county boundaries and do not revert to the general fund.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland, including Special Planning Areas, Urban Growth Areas, and Town Growth Areas as designated in the Comprehensive Plan. Funds cannot be utilized outside county boundaries.
requirements_list: Forest stand delineation required for sites 20,000 sq. ft. or greater, prepared by a licensed forester, landscape architect, or qualified professional.
Forest Conservation Plan (Preliminary and/or Final depending on project type) must be submitted and approved before regulated activities commence.
Priority given to retention of existing forest on-site before payment-in-lieu is allowed.
Minimum forest cover requirements by land use category (e.g., 20% for agricultural/resource use).
Protection of priority forests and priority areas required.
Long-term protective agreements (Installation and Maintenance Agreement) required for forest conservation areas.
Surety/bonding requirements must be met.

Payment-in-lieu fee must be paid prior to permit issuance for construction activity; rate determined by square footage applied to required planting area and periodically established by County Commissioners by resolution.
Native plant species required unless inappropriate; minimum 100 live trees per acre for forest definition (50% with potential to reach 2-inch diameter within 7 years).
Stream buffers minimum 50 feet wide; forest corridors minimum 100-300 feet wide.
Compliance with approved forest conservation plan is mandatory.
Express Procedures available for eligible smaller developments.

For Forest Mitigation Bank credits: submit completed application with Forest Mitigation Bank Plan including vicinity map, forest stand delineation, detailed planting plan, maintenance agreement, and notarized property owner authorization if using an agent.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit forest stand delineation and forest conservation plan to the Washington County Planning Commission for approval before regulated activities begin. If using payment-in-lieu, pay the fee (rate set by County Commissioners) prior to permit issuance. If using a Forest Mitigation Bank, submit a completed application with the Mitigation Bank Plan. Contact Planning and Zoning at 240-313-2430 for details.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Washington County Gaming Commission distributes funds from the Washington County Charitable Gaming Fund to eligible organizations in Washington County. The seven-member commission reviews applications and awards annual grants using revenue generated from charitable gaming activities such as tip jar sales and bingo. Approximately 50% of Gaming Funds are allocated to the Washington County Volunteer Fire & Rescue Association; the remainder is allocated to eligible local charitable organizations. Since inception in 1995, the program has provided over $60 million to charities and fire and rescue companies. Applications are scored using a rubric and the commission publishes annual award lists and reports documenting historical grant awards.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual grants distributed from the Washington County Gaming Fund, funded by revenues from tip jar sales and charitable gaming activities. Maximum grant award is $100,000 per application. Funds must be used exclusively within Washington County and cannot be distributed outside the county. Grant funds must be spent within one year of award; unspent funds must be returned for reallocation. Applications are scored using a rubric. Award amounts vary by year and are listed in the annual award documents published on the Gaming Fund Awards & Reports page.
structured_extraction.contact_name: C. Ahrens; Jill Mackereth; Maria Kramer (Director)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local 501(c)(3) charitable organizations and the Washington County Volunteer Fire and Rescue Association serving Washington County residents, seeking grant funding derived from the county's charitable gaming revenues.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds must be used exclusively within Washington County for eligible charitable purposes including health and human services, emergency services, animal welfare, civic and community activities, athletic/recreational activities, educational and cultural activities. May be used for operating expenses, equipment, or capital projects. Indirect costs capped at 15% of direct costs. Cannot be used for real property, goods, or materials that become property of Washington County Board of Education or Public Schools (unless organization retains ownership with superintendent approval). Funds must be spent within one year of award.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Organization must be located in Washington County, Maryland and provide services that benefit residents within Washington County.
requirements_list: Must be a 501(c)(3) charitable organization with valid status, or a corporation, LLC, or unincorporated association located in Washington County
Must provide services without discrimination based on race, creed, sex, age, color, national origin, marital status, or familial status
Complete application packet must be submitted by April 30, 2026 at 3:00 p.m.

Application packet must include: Notice of Funding Letter, Grant Application Guidelines, Instructions and Checklist, Application for Gaming Funds, Budget Narrative Worksheet, SDAT Information, Notice of Responsible Person, and W9 Form
Must use current (2026) version of application; previous versions not accepted
501(c)(3) determination letter from IRS required
Current annual financial statements and Form 990 (if applicable)
SDAT proof of good standing with the State of Maryland
Supporting documentation (permits, estimates, quotes, partnership letters) for requested project
Budget narrative spreadsheet with line-item justifications
Must designate a responsible person (Notice of Responsible Person form required for unincorporated associations)
Must submit a W-9 form (and Washington County vendor form if new or address changed)
If previously awarded a grant, must submit a prior-year grant report by June 30, 2026
Grant funds must be spent within one year of award; unspent funds must be returned
Incomplete applications will not be reviewed
Applications submitted after the deadline will not be reviewed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications available online starting April 1, 2026. Download and save the application packet from the Washington County website to your computer before completing it. Gather all required documents listed in the checklist. Attend the optional informational workshop (April 6, via Zoom or limited in-person). Complete the Application for Gaming Funds along with all required attachments (Notice of Responsible Person, W-9, Budget Narrative Worksheet, SDAT Information, and prior-year grant report if applicable). Submit the complete application electronically to cahrens@washco-md.net (copy to jmackereth@washco-md.net) or deliver a hard copy to the Office of Grant Management at 100 West Washington Street, Suite 1601, Hagerstown, MD 21740 by April 30, 2026 at 3:00 p.m. Applications are scored using a scoring rubric. Contact the Washington County Grant Management office for current application information.

structured_extraction.program_name: High Performance Commercial Building Tax Incentive Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides a three-year real property tax credit to owners of commercial buildings in Washington County that achieve LEED Platinum, Gold, or Silver certification through new construction or renovation. The credit applies to the increased assessed value of the property as determined by the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation. Credit amounts are 30% of the increase for LEED Platinum, 25% for LEED Gold, and 20% for LEED Silver certification. Owners must apply within one year of receiving LEED certification and maintain the certification level throughout the three-year credit period.
structured_extraction.agency: Washington County Department of Business Development
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Three-year tax credit applied against the increased assessed value of a commercial property as determined by the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation. Credit amounts: 30% of the increase for LEED Platinum, 25% for LEED Gold, and 20% for LEED Silver certification. Eligible property types include office, industrial/commercial, and warehouse buildings.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Within 1 year after building is certified as a high performance building
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of new or renovated commercial buildings in Washington County that achieve LEED certification, including commercial building owners and developers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of county real property taxes on the increased assessed value of LEED-certified commercial properties.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, MD.
requirements_list: Must be new construction or renovated commercial space
Must achieve LEED Platinum, Gold, or Silver certification (LEED-NC, LEED-EB, or LEED-CS systems)
Credit applies only to the increase in assessed value of the property
The application must be submitted within one year of the building receiving its LEED certification
The building must maintain its certification level for the three-year credit period
Applicants must submit an annual letter of compliance attesting conditions remain unchanged
Report anticipated changes impacting certification in a timely manner
Retain all drawings, specifications, and as-built documents during the creditable period
Obtain use and occupancy certificate
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, the building owner submits a complete application form, including a copy of their LEED certification request. After the project is finished, the owner must provide a use and occupancy certificate and proof of the final LEED certification. The Department of Business Development then reviews the materials to approve the tax credit. Application packet available through Washington County Department of Business Development at the provided link.

structured_extraction.program_name: Job Creation and Capital Investment Real Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A Washington County program offering multi-year real property tax credits on the county portion of real estate taxes to businesses that expand or relocate to Washington County and increase employment. The program attracts new companies and supports existing companies that expand in Washington County. Credits range from 6 to 15 years depending on the qualifying section, with tiered percentages based on investment amount and number of new full-time jobs created. The property must be located in a Priority Funding Area; businesses located in an Enterprise Zone are not eligible.
structured_extraction.agency: Washington County Department of Business Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax credits on the county portion of real estate taxes ranging from 6 to 15 years depending on the qualifying section: Section 4(a) — requires at least 1,500 sq ft of new/expanded space and 1 new full-time job; credits of 52% (years 1-2), 39% (years 3-4), 26% (years 5-6). Section 4(b) — requires at least 2,500 sq ft and 5 new full-time employees within 24 months; credits of 30% (years 1-2), 20% (years 3-4), 10% (years 5-6). Section 4(c) — requires $10M capital investment and 100 new full-time jobs; credits of 100% (years 1-5), 75% (years 6-10), 50% (years 11-15). The credit applies to the increased value of real property after expansion or new construction.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling, before project construction is complete
structured_extraction.program_audience: Existing businesses expanding or new businesses locating in Washington County that create jobs and meet specific investment and job creation thresholds.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of the county portion of real estate property taxes for qualifying businesses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland. The business property must be located in a Priority Funding Area. Businesses located in an Enterprise Zone are not eligible for this program.
requirements_list: Must expand or locate in Washington County
Must be located in a Priority Funding Area
Cannot be located in an Enterprise Zone
Submit an application before construction is complete
Section 4(a): Must obtain at least 1,500 sq ft of new or expanded premises and employ at least 1 new permanent full-time employee within a 12-month period
Section 4(b): Must obtain at least 2,500 sq ft and employ at least 5 additional new permanent full-time employees within a 24-month period; new jobs must pay at least 150% of the federal minimum wage
Section 4(c): Must invest $10,000,000 in capital improvements and create 100 new permanent full-time employees
Must provide annual employment reports to maintain the credit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, a business must notify the county of its intent to apply for the credit. Then, it submits an application to the Department of Business Development before finishing construction. The department will certify the business if it is eligible. After certification and project completion, the business must create the required number of new jobs. The business must submit yearly reports on employment to maintain the credit. Complete the Job Creation and Capital Investment Real Property Tax Credit Application Packet available at https://www.washco-md.net/wp-content/uploads/JCRP-2025-Info_Fillable-Form-1.pdf or https://www.washco-md.net/wp-content/uploads/Job-Creations-and-Capital-Investment-Packet.pdf.

structured_extraction.program_description: Project Lifesaver is a search and rescue and monitoring program for individuals who are prone to wandering due to a diagnosed cognitive condition such as autism, dementia, Alzheimer's, Down syndrome, or other neurological disorders. Participants wear a small radio transmitter that emits a silent radio signal, allowing trained first responders and emergency personnel to locate and recover them quickly when they go missing. The program operates as a 24/7 last-resort safety measure for enrolled clients and their caregivers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Enrolled participants receive a wearable radio transmitter (worn on the wrist) that emits a silent radio signal and are monitored 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. Trained emergency personnel use a tracking receiver with a ground range of up to one mile (and up to 5–7 miles when deployed from a helicopter) to locate wandering individuals. The program provides proactive monitoring and specialized rescue operations as a last-resort safety measure at no stated cost to participants.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults and children with a diagnosed cognitive condition such as autism, dementia, Alzheimer's, Down syndrome, or other neurological disorders who have a tendency or history of wandering, their caregivers, and individuals who have a 24-hour caregiver and do not live alone.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Enrollment in the tracking and search-and-rescue program, including receiving a wearable radio transmitter, 24/7 monitoring, and access to trained recovery personnel for locating individuals who wander.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Washington County and Baltimore County, Maryland. Washington County program is located at 16232 Elliott Parkway, Williamsport, MD 21795.
requirements_list: Participant must have a diagnosed cognitive condition that causes a tendency to wander (e.g., autism, dementia, Alzheimer's, Down syndrome, or related neurological disorder)
Participant must have a history of wandering or be at risk of wandering
Client must have a 24-hour caregiver
Client must not live alone
Specific eligibility criteria must be met as determined by the program
Must complete application profile (Step 1) and caregiver tip sheet (Step 2) where applicable
Comprehensive client profile completion including personal data, medical history, physical description, and caregiver information
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For Washington County: Complete the Application Profile (Step 1) and Caregiver Tip Sheet (Step 2) available for download on the program page; the client profile form requires detailed personal, medical, psychological, and behavioral information. Call (240) 313-4368 or contact the PLS Coordinator at shoover@washco-md.net for questions. For Baltimore County: Complete the online application form with information about the potential client and their caregiver; a response will be provided within 48 hours of submission.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program that helps households struggling to afford internet service during the COVID-19 pandemic by providing monthly discounts on broadband service and a one-time discount toward purchasing a computing device.

structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available nationwide to eligible households.
requirements_list: Household income at or below 135% of the Federal Poverty Guidelines, OR participation in SNAP, Medicaid, or Lifeline

Received a Federal Pell Grant during the current award year
Experienced a substantial loss of income due to job loss or furlough since February 29, 2020, with total 2020 household income at or below $99,000 (single filers) or $198,000 (joint filers)
Meets eligibility criteria for a participating provider's existing low-income or COVID-19 program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply in one of three ways: (1) Contact a participating broadband provider directly; (2) Apply online at GetEmergencyBroadband.org; or (3) Call 833-511-0311 to request a mail-in application and return it with proof-of-eligibility documents to the Emergency Broadband Support Center, P.O. Box 7081, London, KY 40742. After receiving an eligibility determination, contact a participating provider to select an eligible service plan.
