structured_extraction.program_description: The SWED Shovel Ready Site program helps Wicomico County better compete for large-scale economic development projects by encouraging and supporting shovel-ready industrial sites through upfront and creative financing. The program targets sites suitable for manufacturing, logistics, or other industrial users that can support significant job creation, preparing industrial sites for immediate development and lease or sale.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Upfront and creative financing to prepare industrial or commercial sites for immediate development. Sites must meet minimum criteria: at least 10 acres or ability to support 100,000 sq ft facility (expandable to 200,000 sq ft), all utilities in place and with sufficient capacity, adequate transportation network, and appropriate industrial zoning. Specific loan and financing terms are available in the program information sheet.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners and developers with industrial sites seeking to attract large-scale economic development projects in the Wicomico County area, targeting manufacturing, logistics, or other industrial uses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Site improvements and preparation to achieve shovel-ready status for industrial land offered for lease or sale, targeting manufacturing, logistics, or other industrial uses with a minimum of 100 jobs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Wicomico County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Minimum of 10 acres or ability to support a minimum 100,000 sq ft facility (ideally expandable to 200,000 sq ft)
All utilities (electric, natural gas, municipal water/sewer, fiber/internet) must exist and be at the site
All utilities must have capacity to accommodate significant new development
Transportation network must exist with capacity for significant new development
Zoning must be light industrial, heavy industrial, industrial park, or planned development district
Applicant must demonstrate legal site control
Proposed site improvements must be offered for lease or sale
Targeted economic sectors: manufacturing, logistics, or other industrial
Targeted minimum number of jobs: 100
Targeted number of users: 1
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact SWED at 410-749-1251 or info@swed.org to discuss specific projects and opportunities. Visit the SWED Shovel Ready page at https://www.swed.org/shovel-ready or download the Program Information Sheet for full details.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Special Loan Program provides grant and loan funding to owner-occupied properties in Wicomico County for general rehabilitation, home replacement, and lead abatement services. It is administered by the Wicomico County Department of Planning, Zoning and Community Development.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants and loans for general home rehabilitation, home replacement, and lead abatement on owner-occupied properties.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owner-occupants of residential properties in Wicomico County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: General rehabilitation, home replacement, and lead abatement services
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Wicomico County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must own and occupy the property
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download the application packet from the program page or contact the Community Development Division by email or phone for assistance with application forms.

structured_extraction.program_name: USDA Rural Development Housing Rehabilitation Program (Section 504 Home Repair)
structured_extraction.program_description: The USDA Section 504 Home Repair program provides loans to very-low-income homeowners to repair, improve, or modernize their homes, and grants to elderly very-low-income homeowners to remove health and safety hazards. It is administered by the USDA Rural Development office.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans for very-low-income homeowners to repair, improve, or modernize their homes. Grants for homeowners age 62 or older who cannot repay a loan, specifically to remove health and safety hazards.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Very-low-income rural homeowners; grants specifically for homeowners age 62 or older
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home repair, improvement, or modernization; removal of health and safety hazards
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Rural designated areas in Wicomico County, Maryland (USDA Hagerstown Office serves all Maryland counties; eligibility determined by USDA Rural Development rural area definitions)
requirements_list: Must be the homeowner and occupy the home
Must be unable to obtain affordable credit elsewhere
Household income must not exceed very low income limits
Income limits apply
For grants: must be age 62 or older and unable to repay a repair loan
Residential property must be in an eligible rural area
Application must be accompanied by checklist of required supporting documentation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call the USDA Hagerstown Office at (301) 797-0500 and dial extension 4 for more information and to apply. Applicants must submit a completed Uniform Residential Loan Application (Form RD 410-4) along with a checklist of required items to accompany the application for home repair loan or grant funds.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides mentoring and comprehensive career planning support, education resources, and budgeting education for youth ages 14-24 who have not completed high school, are at risk for homelessness, or are currently homeless.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Mentoring, career planning support, education resources, and budgeting education for eligible youth ages 14-24.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Youth ages 14-24 in Wicomico County who have not completed high school, are at risk for homelessness, or are currently homeless.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Career planning, education resources, and budgeting education for youth.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Wicomico County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be ages 14-24
Must reside in Wicomico County
Must have not completed high school, be at risk for homelessness, or be currently homeless

structured_extraction.program_description: This program uses Bay Restoration Fund (BRF) money collected from septic system users to upgrade onsite septic systems with Best Available Technology (BAT) for nitrogen removal. The goal is to reduce nutrients flowing into the Chesapeake Bay. Worcester County property owners can apply for grant money to cover the cost and installation of a BAT unit plus two years of maintenance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant money covers the cost and installation of a BAT nitrogen-removal unit plus two years of maintenance. Up to 100% grant for households with income under $300,000 and non-profits; up to 50% grant for property owners with income over $300,000 and businesses. Does not cover drainfield costs (except for qualifying low-income owners), pump systems, electrical upgrades, grading, or permit/recordation fees. Funding can also pay for abandoning an existing septic system and connecting to a public sewer system that achieves enhanced nutrient removal (ENR). Funding priority is based on system condition, location relative to the Critical Area, and homeowner income.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Worcester County individual residential property owners with septic systems, including owners of full-time principal residences, seasonal/weekend properties, and rentals; especially those with failing systems in the Chesapeake Bay Critical Area or Maryland Coastal Bays Critical Area
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase, cost and installation of a Best Available Technology (BAT) nitrogen-removal unit, two years of system operation and maintenance, or connecting to a qualifying public sewer system
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Worcester County property owners. Highest priority goes to properties within 1,000 feet of mean high tide in the Chesapeake Bay Critical Area (CBCA) or Maryland Coastal Bays Critical Area (MCBCA), and properties within Priority Funding Areas (PFA).
requirements_list: Must be a Worcester County property owner
Must submit application form and proof of income
Must allow access for an initial site inspection by the Department of Environmental Programs
If approved, must sign and record an agreement to maintain the BAT system with a qualified operator for as long as the system is in use
Must allow periodic county inspections to verify the BAT unit is operating properly
Properties with access to public sewer may be denied grant funding and required to connect to the public system instead
Sites with holding tanks are only considered if a viable soil-based disposal area can be identified
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download the application form (PDF) from the county website. Complete the form and submit it along with proof of income to the Department of Environmental Programs by mail, fax, or email. The department will review the application, assess public sewer availability, conduct a site inspection, and determine funding priority.

structured_extraction.program_name: FY 2026 Amended Worcester County Reinvestment and Repair Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Worcester County Local Management Board is accepting applications for the FY26 Amended Worcester County Reinvestment and Repair Grant Program. The Community Reinvestment and Repair Fund (CRRF), created by Maryland's Cannabis Reform Act of 2023, directs 35% of adult-use cannabis tax revenue to local jurisdictions to support community initiatives that benefit low-income and disproportionately impacted communities. The Maryland Office of Social Equity guides how the state spends CRRF funds.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding from the Community Reinvestment and Repair Fund, sourced from 35% of adult-use cannabis tax revenue, to support community initiatives benefiting low-income and disproportionately impacted communities in Worcester County.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations and entities serving low-income and disproportionately impacted communities in Worcester County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Community initiatives benefiting low-income and disproportionately impacted communities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Worcester County, Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a proposal/application in response to the solicitation issued by the Worcester County Local Management Board.

structured_extraction.program_description: Worcester County local fire departments provide and install smoke alarms at no cost to residents who cannot afford them. Smoke alarms are installed outside each sleeping area, on each level of multi-level homes (including basements), and inside each sleeping room where feasible. Strobe smoke alarms are also available free of charge for hearing-impaired residents on a first-come, first-served basis.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free smoke alarms provided and installed by local fire and rescue personnel for residents who cannot afford them. Alarms are installed outside each sleeping area, on every level (including basements), and inside each sleeping room where feasible. Battery-operated alarms must be sealed, tamper-resistant with silence/hush button and long-life batteries. Strobe smoke alarms are available free of charge for hearing-impaired residents on a first-come, first-served basis.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Worcester County residents who cannot afford smoke alarms, residential property owners and occupants, and hearing-impaired residents in need of strobe smoke alarms.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of battery-operated and hardwired smoke alarms meeting Maryland safety standards in residential dwellings.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Worcester County, Maryland residential dwellings
requirements_list: Must be unable to afford smoke alarms (for standard alarm program)
Hearing-impaired status required for strobe smoke alarm program
Strobe alarms available on a first-come, first-served basis
Smoke alarms must meet Maryland Public Safety Article requirements
By 1/1/2018: battery-operated alarms must be sealed, tamper-resistant with silence/hush button and long-life batteries
Minimum locations: outside each sleeping area, on every level (including basements), and inside each sleeping room
Monthly testing and replacement every 10 years required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local Fire Department to request smoke alarms. Fire and rescue personnel will provide and install them at no cost.

structured_extraction.program_description: A credit granted to owner-occupied residential properties that limits the annual increase in assessed value used to calculate property taxes to a certain percentage. If eligible, the credit is automatically reflected on the tax bill.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A credit that limits the taxable assessment increase for owner-occupied residential properties to a set annual percentage. The credit is automatically applied to the tax bill if the homeowner qualifies.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owner-occupants of residential properties in Worcester County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of real property tax liability by capping annual assessment increases
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to owner-occupied residential properties in Worcester County, Maryland
requirements_list: Property must be owner-occupied and residential
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligibility is determined automatically; the credit is reflected on the tax bill if applicable.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants and loans to owner-occupied homes in Worcester County for general rehabilitation (bringing homes up to the county's Minimum Livability Code) and lead abatement services. Priority is given to senior citizens, people with disabilities, extremely low-income families, and homes with safety or health hazards.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants for general rehabilitation and lead abatement are available to eligible homeowners. Grant terms are 5–15 years with no repayment required unless the property is sold or refinanced during the grant period; grants are secured with a recorded property lien. Lead abatement grants have no minimum term and no repayment if the home is sold or refinanced (a 10% match is required if family income exceeds 80% of the area median income). Loans are also available at interest rates between 0% and 7%, scaled to the family's ability to repay; payments may be fully deferred, with the full loan balance due when the property is sold or otherwise transferred.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low- to moderate-income homeowners in Worcester County who occupy their home as their principal residence, including senior citizens, people with disabilities, and families with extremely low income.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: General home rehabilitation to meet the county's Minimum Livability Code and lead abatement services, including mold remediation, roof repair/replacement, asbestos abatement, lead abatement, electrical hazards, plumbing issues, septic/sewer, foundation waterproofing, radon mitigation, structural repairs, accessibility improvements, pest treatments, and more.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to homeowners in rural areas or any incorporated township of Worcester County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Homeowner must occupy the dwelling as their principal residence and may not own other houses or properties
Home must have conditions that do not meet the County's Minimum Livability Code (for general rehab grant and loan)
Homeowner must have acceptable credit or be willing to set up payment plans on non-medical accounts in collections; judgments must be paid in full
Property taxes must be paid in full at time of application
Mobile homes are not eligible unless secured on a permanent block or brick foundation and not in a mobile home park
Current or retired Worcester County employees, their immediate families, or individuals holding contracts with the county are generally ineligible for grant assistance (general rehab grants only)

For lead abatement grants: family must be of extremely low income or have insufficient funds to make loan payments, or the cost of lead abatement must exceed the assessed value of the dwelling; home must be in an eligible census tract and structurally sound
For loans: family must be of low to moderate income
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete the Special Loans Rehabilitation Application from the program page and submit it to the Worcester County Department of Development, Review and Permitting. Contact Davida Washington for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Zanvyl and Isabelle Krieger Fund Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: The Krieger Fund awards grants twice a year to nonprofit organizations working in Baltimore on affordable housing, community development, behavioral health and healing, environmental justice, and support for families with children from birth to three years old. Both direct service and advocacy (non-lobbying) work are eligible. Most grants range from $2,500 to $25,000 per year, with some exceptions. The fund does not make multi-year commitments, but organizations may reapply each year.
structured_extraction.agency: Zanvyl & Isabelle Krieger Fund / Middendorf / Robert W. Deutsch Foundations
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are awarded twice a year at the June and December board meetings. Application deadlines are March 1 and September 1. Most grants range from $2,500 to $25,000 per year, with some exceptions. The fund does not make multi-year commitments, but organizations may reapply each year. All grant funds must be used for direct program expenses — overhead and indirect costs are not covered. First-time applicants must submit a Letter of Intent (LOI) before being invited to apply. Renewal applicants apply via Google form.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations doing direct service and/or advocacy (non-lobbying) work in Baltimore focused on affordable housing and community development, behavioral health and healing, environmental justice, or families with children from birth to three years old.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Direct program expenses for affordable housing and community development work, behavioral health and healing, environmental justice, and services and advocacy for families with children from birth to three years old. Cannot be used for endowments, indirect costs, capital or annual campaigns, special events, or publications.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Work must address community issues in Baltimore.
requirements_list: Work must focus on at least one of the fund's priority areas: affordable housing and community development, behavioral health and healing, environmental justice, or families with young children (birth to three)
Work must be direct service and/or advocacy (non-lobbying)
Grant funds must be used for direct program expenses only — not overhead or indirect costs
Organizations may apply once per year and not in back-to-back grant cycles
First-time applicants must submit a Letter of Intent (LOI) before a full proposal

LOI must describe mission, community issue addressed, approach, partnerships, fit in Baltimore ecosystem, evidence of impact, dollar amount requested, organizational budget with current funding sources, and current board member list
Renewal applicants apply via Google form combining cover letter, final report, and proposal narrative
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First-time applicants submit a brief Letter of Intent (LOI) by email to Jen Eames at jeames@associated.org. If outside the stated focus areas, contact Jen before submitting anything in writing. Renewal applicants submit via Google form (Krieger Fund only, or combined Krieger Fund and Fund for Change form). Full applications are due March 1 (for June board meeting) or September 1 (for December board meeting).
